r7.04.03 Post-processing according to the RCC-M r7.04.03 Post-processing according to the RCC-M Summary: The operator POST_RCCM u4.83.11 makes it possible to check the level-0 criteria and certain level-A criteria of chapter B3200 of the RCC‑M, for modellings of 2D or 3D continuous media. The level-0 criteria aim to protect the equipment against the damage of excessive strain, of plastic instability, and of elastic and elastoplastic instability. The level-A criteria aim, for their part, to protect the equipment against the damage of progressive strain and of fatigue. It also makes it possible to compute the level-A criteria of chapters B3600 and ZE200 in post-processing of piping analyses. Finally, it makes it possible to evaluate the environmental-fatigue resistance for chapters B3200 and ZE200. Furthermore, the operator POST_RCCM makes it possible to compute the crack-initiation factor at a singular zone, in the sense of appendix ZD of the RCC-M. 1 Introduction The RCC-M describes the general rules for the analysis of the behaviour of the equipment of nuclear power plants. These rules aim to ensure for the equipment of PWR plants safety margins sufficient with respect to the various types of damage to which they could be exposed as a result of the loadings applied to them: excessive strain and plastic instability, elastic or elastoplastic instability, progressive strain under the effect of repeated loadings, fatigue (progressive cracking), sudden fracture… In code_aster , it is possible to carry out four types of analysis: - computation of the level-0 and level-A criteria of chapter B3200 in post-processing of analyses on 2D or 3D structures; - computation of the fatigue criteria of chapter B3600 in post-processing of piping analyses; - computation of the fatigue criteria of appendix ZE200 in post-processing of piping analyses. The method according to appendix ZE200 is a mixed method which combines simplified equations of B3600 and a detailed analysis of B3200. - computation of environmental fatigue compatible with chapters B3200 and appendix ZE200 of the RCC-M. The environmental-fatigue resistance was integrated into the RCC-M, 2016 edition, in the form of a Rule in Probationary Phase (RPP). r7.04.03-generalites recalls general points on chapter B3200 and appendix ZE200 of the RCC-M. The criteria of B3200 correspond in the operator POST_RCCM to the methods (TYPE_RESU_MECA) ‘B3200’ and 'EVOLUTION'. Their computation is detailed in r7.04.03-type-b3200 and r7.04.03-type-evolution. 'EVOLUTION' makes it possible to compute an initiation factor for geometric singularities and is well suited to cases where there are few situations. Conversely, 'B3200' is well suited to computations for numerous situations, which may be distributed over several operating groups. The earthquake, the passage situations and the environmental fatigue can be taken into account with this TYPE_RESU_MECA. The criteria of ZE200 correspond in the operator POST_RCCM to the methods ‘ZE200a' and 'ZE200b'. Their computation is detailed in r7.04.03-types-ze200a-ze200b. The computation of the environmental-fatigue resistance is described in r7.04.03-fatigue-environnementale. The fatigue criterion of B3600 corresponds in the operator POST_RCCM to the method ‘B3600’. Their computation is detailed in r7.04.03-type-b3600. 2 General points This chapter aims to recall a few basic definitions associated with chapter B3200 and with appendix ZE200 of the RCC-M. It does not concern chapter B3600. This chapter also makes it possible to describe the necessary adaptations carried out in code_aster , which are motivated in and . The criteria of chapter B3200 correspond in the operator POST_RCCM to the methods TYPE_RESU_MECA=‘EVOLUTION’ and TYPE_RESU_MECA=‘B3200’. The criteria of appendix ZE200 correspond in the operator POST_RCCM to the methods TYPE_RESU_MECA=‘ZE200a’ and TYPE_RESU_MECA=‘ZE200b’. 2.1 Geometric data The user of the RCC-M must distinguish in his structure the zones of major discontinuity, the zones of minor discontinuity and the zones comprising geometric singularities. The latter require a specific treatment (described in part 6.5). Current zone (outside a geometric singularity): The RCC-M defines “support segments” which serve to linearise the stresses. These segments are, outside the discontinuity zones, segments generally normal to the mean surface of the wall, and in the discontinuity zones, the shortest segments making it possible to join the 2 faces of the wall. The user of code_aster must therefore define the set of the sections of the structure where the post-processing computations will be done (it is he who knows whether these sections pass through current zones, or zones of geometric discontinuity). In practice, one works: - either on a segment existing in the mesh; - or on a segment defined in MACR_LIGN_COUPE. One computes all the criteria systematically at the two ends of the segment (computation of Pm, of the usage factor...). Geometric singularity: The zones of local discontinuities whose geometric contour presents abrupt variations are the seat of sharp stress concentrations. In this case, the classical methods associated with the current zones are unsuitable and one introduces the notion of initiation factor. This parameter must be computed on a circle (of imposed radius, depending on the material) around the singularity. The initiation factor can be computed only with the type 'EVOLUTION'. The user must therefore define this cutting line. In practice, one works: - either on a circular cutting line existing in the mesh; - or on a circular cutting line defined in MACR_LIGN_COUPE. 2.2 Material data The material data necessary for the computation are the following: - S_m : allowable value (tabulated in the RCC-M Appendix ZI). - S_y : conventional elastic limit (tabulated in the RCC-M Appendix ZI 2.1). - m , n : material constants for the computation of K_e (defined in the RCC-M B3234.6). - E_c , E : elastic moduli (for the correction of the fatigue curve, appendix ZI). - Fatigue curves of the material: according to the RCC-M appendix ZI. - Distance d to the geometric singularity and initiation law of the material (as defined and tabulated in appendix ZD2200 of the RCC-M) for the computation of the initiation factor. 2.3 Simplifying hypotheses In the RCC-M, the user must be able to say, after analysis of the results of the computation, whether the principal directions at a given point are fixed or whether they rotate in the course of time. In the command POST_RCCM, one need not make any hypothesis. One will consider only the case where the principal directions are arbitrary. Moreover, the user must be able to classify the stresses in the following categories: - General primary membrane: P_m - Local membrane primary: P_l - Primary bending: P_b - Thermal expansion: P_e - Secondary: Q - Peak: F This choice cannot be made by POST_RCCM. Only the user can qualify a stress field (“primary”, “secondary”, or the sum of the two). The criteria which are to be checked are computed from stress fields (constant or a function of time) supplied by the user. It is he who ensures the consistency between the computation of these fields and the criteria applied. However, to fix ideas, the classification is simpler in the following cases: - a constant or variable loading with imposed force or pressure is primary, except for certain very particular structures, - a constant or variable loading with imposed displacement is in principle secondary (except in the case of the “spring effect”), - a permanent or transient thermal loading is in principle secondary. On the other hand, the combination of these types of loadings leads to a result which can no longer be qualified as primary or secondary. According to the criteria, the user may therefore be led to decompose his loadings. 2.4 Computations carried out by POST_RCCM One describes in what follows the operation of the command POST_RCCM making it possible to carry out the computation of certain level-0 and level-A criteria of the RCC-M B3200 and of the level-A criteria of appendix ZE200. The implementation described here does not take into account all the criteria of B3200 and may be completed. The principal datum is the (support) segment where the computations will be carried out. It is the user who chooses the segment and who has the responsibility of finding the one for which the quantities appearing in the criteria are maximal. The automatic search for this segment is a difficult problem, and is not programmed. After having computed one or more results by MECA_STATIQUE or STAT_NON_LINE, the user must extract the stresses on the analysis segment by POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE. Finally, the user requests the computation of the criterion or criteria by the operator POST_RCCM. Four types of criteria are accessible, each by the factor keyword 'OPTION': - level-0 criteria by the keyword PM_PB, - level-A criteria (excluding fatigue) by the keyword SN, - level-A fatigue criteria by the keywords FATIGUE (for the types 'B3200', 'ZE200a' and 'ZE200b') or FATIGUE_ZH210 (for the type ‘EVOLUTION’), - an environmental-fatigue criterion by the keyword EFAT. This criterion is compatible with the options 'B3200', 'ZE200a' and 'ZE200b'. Furthermore, with the method ‘EVOLUTION’ only, it is possible to check the initiation criterion (level-A criterion) in a singular zone (keyword AMORCAGE). 2.5 Level-0 criteria specified by the RCC-M (keyword PM_PB) The level-0 criteria aim to protect the equipment against the damage of excessive strain, of plastic instability and of elastic and elastoplastic instability. They must be checked for the reference situation (see B3121 and B3151). These criteria require the computation of the equivalent stresses P_m , P_l , P_b which are defined below and are available for the types 'B3200' and 'EVOLUTION'. 2.5.1 General primary membrane equivalent stress Given the primary stress of the reference situation (1st category) and a segment situated outside a zone of major discontinuity. At each end point of this segment of length l , one computes P_m and the criterion is written (B3233.1): P_m \leq S_m S_m is the allowable equivalent stress, tabulated in appendix ZI of the RCC-M. S_m is defined in the computation by the operand SM of the factor keyword RCCM (or RCCM_FO) of DEFI_MATERIAU. It may be a function of the temperature. 2.5.2 Local membrane primary equivalent stress Given the primary stress of the reference situation (1st category) and a segment situated in a zone of major discontinuity , the definition of P_l is identical to that of P_m on this segment. The criterion is written (B3233.2): P_l \leq 1.5\, S_m 2.5.3 Primary membrane+bending equivalent stress Given the primary stress of the reference situation (1st category) and a (oriented) segment. At each end point of this segment of length l (ends corresponding to the external and internal skins), one computes P_{mb} and P_{lb} and the criteria are written (B3233.3): P_{mb} \leq 1.5\, S_m P_{lb} \leq 1.5\, S_m 2.6 Level-A criteria specified by the RCC-M (keywords SN and FATIGUE/FATIGUE_ZH210) The level-A criteria aim to protect the equipment against the damage of progressive strain and of progressive cracking. With the methods 'EVOLUTION', ‘B3200’, 'ZE200a' and 'ZE200b', four types of criteria can be checked: - Amplitude of variation of the linearised stresses S_n (option ‘SN’); - Amplitude of variation of S_n (option ‘SN’); - Computation of the thermal ratchet (option ‘SN’); - Computation of the fatigue usage factor (options ‘FATIGUE’/‘FATIGUE_ZH210’) These various parameters and the associated criteria are described below as defined in the RCC-M. In r7.04.03-Hypotheses-simplificatrices, one introduces a simplifying hypothesis before detailing their computation in code_aster in chapters 3, 4 and 6. 2.6.1 Computation of Sn and Sn One takes into account the primary plus secondary stresses and the stresses resulting from the constrained thermal expansions: P_l + P_b + P_e + Q , which therefore represents the linearised stresses associated with the whole loading (mechanical and thermal). The computation points are the two ends of the segment. At each end point of this segment of length l , one computes S_n according to paragraph B3232.6 and the global shakedown criterion is written (B3234.2): S_n \leq 3\, S_m S_m being the allowable stress, a function of the material and of the temperature, given by the operand SM of the factor keyword RCCM (or RCCM_FO) of DEFI_MATERIAU. If this criterion is not satisfied, one can carry out the simplified elastoplastic analysis of B3234.3. One must carry out the following three operations: - one computes S_n the amplitude S_n computed without taking into account the bending stresses of thermal origin and one must check the criterion: S_n \leq 3\, S_m - make an elastoplastic correction ( K_e > 1 ) in the fatigue analysis, - check the thermal-ratchet criterion (B3234.8) in the current parts of the cylindrical shells (and pipes) subjected to a pressure and a cyclic temperature gradient. 2.6.2 Computation of the thermal ratchet The wall of an apparatus subjected simultaneously to a constant pressure and to cyclic variations of temperature can undergo large strains under thermal ratchet. This is a particular mechanism of progressive strain in which the strain increases by approximately the same quantity at each cycle. The condition to be respected is written below and concerns the maximum allowable value of the amplitude of variation of the stress of thermal origin, cf. B3234.8. If the value S'_{alt} computed for a combination (i,j) of stabilised state is less than this minimum amplitude, the usage factor is equal to 0 for the combination (i,j) considered. 4 Types 'ZE200a' and 'ZE200b' 4.1 Loading data The types ‘ZE200a’ and 'ZE200b' are well suited to computations on a piping line or a branch connection subjected to numerous situations. Several operating groups can also be defined, with possibly passage situations between these groups. Sharing groups and an earthquake can also be taken into account. Each situation is described by two stabilised states and a thermal transient. The stabilised states describe the loadings due to the moments via a resultant \left\{M_X, M_Y, M_Z \right\} . The pressure can be described in two different ways: - 'ZE200a': it is associated with the stabilised states, which are then defined by a pressure p - 'ZE200b': it is in the form of a transient under the keyword 'RESU_PRES'. The use of these options requires the prior computation of the stress fields for each of the thermal transients; these fields are to be supplied on the analysis segment at the time instants of the discretisation of the computation by means of tables. Additional data are necessary for the computation according to Appendix ZE200 of the RCC-M. These data enter into the simplified equations taken from chapter B3600. They are the following: - Geometric characteristics of the piping: thickness EP, radius R and moment of inertia I under the keyword TUYAU. - Stress indices of paragraph B3680 of the RCC-M: C1, C2, C3, K1, K2, K3 under the keyword INDI_SIGM - For the branch connections, it is also possible to use the types ZE200a and ZE200b by defining two moment resultants associated respectively with the body and with the nozzle. One must also define the radii of the body and of the nozzle under 'TUYAU' as well as their stress indices under 'INDI_SIGM'. Appendix 3 summarises the equations in this case. - The forces are not taken into account in ZE200. - In 'ZE200b', the user must also supply the stress fields for each of the pressure transients and they must be defined at the same time instants as the thermal transients. - The two methods of selection of the time instants 'TRESCA' and 'TOUT_INST' are available (cf. r7.04.03-methode-selection-instants ) Notes 4.2 Computations carried out with the option ‘SN’ 4.2.1 Type ’ZE200a’ One denotes by \sigma_{ther} the stress tensor of the thermal transient associated with the situation and by t^{maxSn} and t^{minSn} the extremal time instants of this transient as defined in r7.04.03-methode-selection-instants. If S_{p^{1}}'=\left\lVert\sigma_{tran,q}(t_{q^{maxSp}})-\sigma_{tran,p}(t_{p^{minSp}})\right\rVert , then S_{p^{meca,1}}'(p,q)=\left\lVert\sigma_{pression,q}(t_{q^{maxSp}})-\sigma_{pression,p}(t_{p^{minSp}})\right\rVert and S_{p^{meca,2}}'(p,q)=\left\lVert\sigma_{pression,p}(t_{p^{maxSp}})-\sigma_{pression,q}(t_{q^{minSp}})\right\rVert . With 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST' , one does not carry out a new search for time instants with respect to the KE_MECA method (cf. r7.04.03-calcul-sp ). Let t_{1^{p}} and t_{1^{q}} be the time instants of fictitious transient 1 S_{p^{1}}' , and t_{2^{p}} and t_{2^{q}} the time instants of fictitious transient 2 S_{p^{2}}' . Then, the parameters S_{p^{meca,1}}' and S_{p^{meca,2}}' for the combination of situations p and q are defined by: S_{p^{meca,1}}=\left\lVert\sigma_{pres,p}(t_{1^{p}})-\sigma_{pres,q}(t_{1^{q}})\right\rVert S_{p^{meca,2}}=\left\lVert\sigma_{pres,p}(t_{2^{p}})-\sigma_{pres,q}(t_{2^{q}})\right\rVert 4.3.2 Computation of the total usage factor The taking into account of the earthquake, the sharing groups, the sub-cycles, the management of the passage situations, the storage of the elementary usage factors and the computation of the total usage factor are the same as for the method 'B3200' (see r7.04.03-situations-passage to r7.04.03-calcul-facteur-usage-total ). 5 Environmental fatigue The taking into account of the environmental effects on the fatigue resistance in code_aster is available for the types B3200, ZE200a and ZE200b. This taking into account is carried out after the combination of the situations and the computation of the usual usage factor described in r7.04.03-calcul-facteur-usage-total . 5.1 Computation of the FEN The environmental factor for the combination of the situations p and q is expressed as a function of \Delta\varepsilon the strain increment, of F the partial environmental factor and of the time instants t_k and t_l . The index k runs over the time instants of the transient of p and the index l runs over the time instants of the transient of q . FEN_{comb}(p,q)=\frac{\sum_k ?\,\Delta\varepsilon(t_k)+\sum_l ?\,\Delta\varepsilon(t_l)}{\sum_k F(t_k)\Delta\varepsilon(t_k)+\sum_l F(t_l)\Delta\varepsilon(t_l)} Whatever the material studied, the general form of the partial environmental factor F is the following: F(t_k)=\exp\left[\left(A+B\,\dot{\varepsilon}^{ }(t_k)\right)S^{ }O^{ }T^{ }+C\right] - A, B and C are constants which depend on the nature of the material: ferritic, austenitic, nickel-base (keywords A_ENV, B_ENV and C_ENV), - S^ is the sulphur content of the metal analysed, therefore common to all the situations (keyword S_ETOILE), - O^ is the degree of dissolved oxygen in the water in contact with the section analysed. This quantity can be different for each situation (keyword O_ETOILE), - T^ is a function which depends on the mean temperature T. The user must therefore supply a table which contains the evolution of the temperature in the course of the transient (keyword TABL_TEMP). T=\frac{T(t_k)+T(t_{k-1})}{2} The function T^ is described below and depends on the thresholds T_{seuil,sup} and T_{seuil,inf} (keywords SEUIL_T_SUP and SEUIL_T_INF) and on the threshold values T_{sup} , T_{inf} , T_{moy,num} and T_{moy,den} (keywords VALE_T_SUP, VALE_T_INF, VALE_T_MOY_NUM and VALE_T_MOY_DEN): \begin{aligned} T^{ }=\begin{cases}T_{inf} & \text{si } T>T_{seuil,sup} \\ \frac{T-T_{moy,num}}{T_{moy,den}} & \text{si } T_{seuil,inf}\le T\le T_{seuil,sup} \\ T_{sup} & \text{si } T \varepsilon_{seuil,sup} \\ \ln\left(\frac{\dot{\varepsilon}}{\varepsilon_{seuil,sup}}\right) & \text{si } \varepsilon_{seuil,inf}\le\dot{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon_{seuil,sup} \\ \ln\left(\frac{\varepsilon_{seuil,inf}}{\varepsilon_{seuil,sup}}\right) & \text{si } \dot{\varepsilon} \sigma_2>\sigma_3 \end{aligned} \begin{split}\Delta\sigma(t_k)=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma_1(t_k)&0&0\\0&\sigma_2(t_k)&0\\0&0&\sigma_3(t_k)\end{pmatrix}\qquad\text{avec}\qquad\sigma_1>\sigma_2>\sigma_3\end{split} One can then compute \Delta\varepsilon which is a function of the principal stresses, of the Ke of the combination of situations and of Young's modulus E taken at the mean temperature of the time step T . Ke was stored during the computation of the usual usage factor (cf. r7.04.03-calcul-salt ) and E is computed by linear interpolation on the curve E(T) given under the keyword TABL_YOUNG. \begin{aligned} \Delta\varepsilon(t_k)=\begin{cases}0 & \text{si } \sigma_1\le 0 \\ K_e\cdot\frac{\sigma_1(t_k)-\sigma_3(t_k)}{E(T)} & \text{si } \sigma_1>0\end{cases} \end{aligned} Note The temperature table entered under the keyword TABL_TEMP must be defined at the same time instants as the tables which contain the stresses in transient form (thermal, pressure, mechanical depending on the computation method). 5.2 Computation of the usage factor with environmental effect For the computation of the usage factor with environmental effect, two quantities still enter at this stage: a criterion on the strain (keyword CRIT_EPSI) and the integrated FEN (keyword FEN_INTEGRE). These two quantities do not depend on the combination of situations; one therefore enters only one value for all combinations of situations. 5.2.1 Criterion on the minimum strain During the computation of FEN_{comb(p,q)} , if the sum of the strain increments due to situations p and q is less than CRIT_EPSI then the environmental effect is not taken into account for this combination. More precisely, \text{si }\sum_k ?\,\Delta\varepsilon_p(t_k)+\sum_k ?\,\Delta\varepsilon_q(t_k)\le\varepsilon_{limite} \quad\text{alors}\quad FEN_{comb}(p,q)=1 Finally, in order to obtain the elementary usage factor with environmental effect, one multiplies the elementary usage factor {U}^{elem}(p,q) (cf. r7.04.03-calcul-facteur-usage-fatigue ) by the FEN of the combination of situations p and q: U_{env}^{elem}(p,q)=U^{elem}(p,q)\cdot FEN_{comb}(p,q) The total usage factor with environmental effect {U}_{env}^{TOT} is computed by taking into account {U}_{env}^{elem}(p,q) in place of {U}^{elem}(p,q) but without going again through the algorithm of r7.04.03-Algorithme-calcul-facteur-usage-total . 5.2.2 Global FEN and integrated FEN A last check is then made: one defines the global FEN such that: FEN_{global}=\frac{U_{env}^{TOT}}{U^{TOT}} If {FEN}_{global}>{FEN}_{integre} then the total usage factor with environmental effect {U}_{env}^{TOT} is updated by dividing it by FEN_INTEGRE. 6 Type ‘EVOLUTION’ 6.1 Loading data ‘EVOLUTION’ is well suited to computations on a component subjected to few loading situations and no earthquake. The user of the RCC-M must give the number of occurrences of each operating situation (for example: heating of the boiler, hot shutdown, etc.). An operating situation can be decomposed into transients, that is evolutions of the global operating parameters (pressure, temperature) as a function of time. In code_aster , one deals with mechanical results (produced by MECA_STATIQUE or STAT_NON_LINE), therefore with transients. For each transient, the stress fields are to be supplied on the analysis segment at the time instants of the discretisation of the computation by means of tables created by a call to POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE. Several types of results may be necessary for each transient: stresses for the thermomechanical loadings (TABL_RESU_MECA), stresses for the thermal loading alone (TABL_SIGM_THER), stresses for the pressure loading alone (TABL_RESU_PRES) and stresses for the singular zones (TABL_SIGM_THETA). This TYPE_RESU_MECA is the one which leads to the most precise results. It does not indeed require the introduction of any simplifying hypothesis, either on the definition of the loadings, or on the computation of the various level-0 or level-A criteria. Furthermore, it makes it possible to compute the initiation factor at a singular zone, in the sense of appendix ZD of the RCC-M. 6.2 Computations carried out with the option ‘AXIS’ and ‘RAYON_MOYEN’ The treatment of the linearisation of the stresses by means of the 3D method can lead to an erroneous result because of the inhomogeneous radial mass distribution under the axisymmetric hypothesis. For an axisymmetric model, the median axis must be offset outwards by a distance such that the resulting bending moment vanishes on the offset axis. Axisymmetric model and variables involved in the stress-linearisation method. Left: model without curvature; Right: model with a curvature in the XOY plane. (Ref. ANSYS APDL Theory Reference) By convention, the model is axisymmetric about the Y axis. The stress tensor having been converted into the local 2D frame, according to the physical design, one can quantify the offset distance in order to linearise the normal stress: x_f=\frac{M_z}{F_y}=\frac{t^2\cos(\phi)}{12R_c} Where M_z is the total bending moment in the circumferential direction induced by the normal stress and F_y is the total normal force. The other variables are shown in r7.04.03-fig-modele-axisymetrique. Likewise, the offset distance for linearising the circumferential stress is expressed as: the offset distance for linearising the circumferential stress is expressed: x_h=\frac{M_y}{F_z}=\frac{t^2}{12\,\rho} The main idea of the computation of the membrane stress {\sigma}_{ij}^{m} is to average the total force by the elementary area in the plane which is orthogonal to the stress component. The computation of the bending stress uses the equation in section 3.2 when in the 3D cases. The only difference with the 3D models is the taking into account of the offset axis. Here, the detailed computation is presented as an example for the circumferential stress component, whose formulation is the most complicated. \sigma_z^m=\frac{F_z}{A_z}=\frac{\int_{-t/2}^{t/2}\sigma_z(\rho+x)\Delta\phi\,dx}{\rho\Delta\phi\,t}=\frac{\int_{-t/2}^{t/2}\sigma_z\left(1+\frac{x}{\rho}\right)\,dx}{t} \sigma_z^b=\frac{M_z(x-x_h)}{I_y}=\frac{(x-x_h)\int_{-t/2}^{t/2}\sigma_z(\rho+x)\Delta\phi(x-x_h)\,dx}{\rho t\Delta\phi\left(\frac{t^2}{12}-x_h^2\right)}=\frac{x-x_h}{t\left(\frac{t^2}{12}-x_h^2\right)}\int_{-t/2}^{t/2}\sigma_z\left(1+\frac{x}{\rho}\right)(x-x_h)\,dx The simplified expression of the other linearised stress components can be found in ANSYS APDL Theory Reference. The code newly developed within the code_aster command POST_RCCM makes it possible for the users to switch to the optimised computation routine if an axisymmetric model is declared, without the original functionalities of the command being disturbed. Furthermore, it has been possible to indicate the curvature of the axis \rho in the XOY plane if necessary, by referring to r7.04.03-fig-modele-axisymetrique. The default value \rho has been set to -1, representing a perfectly straight axis. 6.3 Computations carried out with the option ‘PM_PB’ The stress table comprises either a single time step, or a complete transient ( nb_inst time steps). In this latter case, one will look for the maximum, with respect to the list of the order numbers, of the various terms entering into the criteria. It is for the user to know whether one computes Pm (general membrane stress: outside the zones of geometric singularity) or else Pl (local membrane stress: in the singularities). From the stress readings supplied, one therefore computes a membrane stress. The algorithm is the following. Over the set of the order numbers n=1,\text{nb\_inst} : - extraction of the stresses at the time instant t - On each end of the segment: > computation of P_m(t) , P_b(t) , P_{mb}(t,s=0) and P_{mb}(t,s=l) by integration over the segment \sigma_{ij}^{moy}(t)=\frac{1}{l}\int_0^l\sigma_{ij}(t)\,ds P_m(t)=\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{moy}(t)\right\rVert \sigma_{ij}^{fle}(t)=\frac{6}{l^2}\int_0^l\left(s-\frac{l}{2}\right)\sigma_{ij}(t)\,ds P_b(t)=\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{fle}(t)\right\rVert P_{mb}(t,s=0)=\max_t\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{moy}(t)-\sigma_{ij}^{fle}(t)\right\rVert P_{mb}(t,s=l)=\max_t\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{moy}(t)+\sigma_{ij}^{fle}(t)\right\rVert - Search for the maximum of P_m(t) , P_{mb}(t,s=0) and P_{mb}(t,s=l) - Output and storage in the result table. Note The thermal stresses are of secondary type and must therefore not be taken into account in the computation of the level-0 criteria. In POST_RCCM, if TABL_RESU_MECA and TABL_SIGM_THER are present simultaneously, one supposes that the result TABL_RESU_MECA corresponds to the complete thermomechanical loading, and one therefore subtracts from it the stresses of thermal origin. 6.4 Computations carried out with the option ‘SN’ 6.4.1 Computation of Sn One denotes by nb_inst the number of time instants selected in the transient considered. The algorithm for the computation of S_n is the following: - over the set of the order numbers, n_1 = 1,\mathrm{nb\_inst} - Extraction of the time instant t_1 - Computation of \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1,s=0) and \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1,s=l) - For n_2 varying from n_1+1 to \mathrm{nb\_inst} - Extraction of the time instant t_2 - computation of \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2,s=0) and \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2,s=l) and \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2,s=0)-\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1,s=0) and \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2,s=l)-\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1,s=l) - computation of the principal directions and of the Tresca criterion: \left(\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2,s=0)-\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1,s=0)\right)_{Eq.Tresca} and \left(\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2,s=l)-\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1,s=l)\right)_{Eq.Tresca} - search for the maximum, therefore for S_n , at each end - Output and storage in the result table. Note The quantity S_n computed here corresponds to an amplitude. It is therefore indispensable that all the states of the system be considered, including the states with zero stress (for example cold shutdown: zero applied pressure and moments and ambient temperature). 6.4.2 Computation of Sn This computation is carried out if the operand TABL_SIGM_THER is present. Only the user ensures the consistency of the data, that is to say that this result must be produced by a thermomechanical computation under thermal loading alone, given that the result given by TABL_RESU_MECA may be due to a combination of this thermal loading with other loadings. One must therefore in particular ensure that the time instants of the tables TABL_RESU_MECA and TABL_SIGM_THER correspond. The algorithm is identical to the preceding one but bears on two stress fields. 6.4.3 Computation of the thermal ratchet The computation is carried out if the operands TABL_SIGM_THER and TABL_RESU_PRES are present. One must also have previously defined the conventional elastic limit for the maximum temperature reached in the course of the cycle, either by the operand SY_MAX of POST_RCCM, or by the operand SY_02 of the keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. If no elastic limit is defined, the computation of the thermal ratchet is impossible. In the result table appear, for each end of each analysis segment, the elastic limit SY, the amplitude of variation of the stress of thermal origin SP_THER, the maximum of the general membrane stress due to the pressure SIGM_M_PRES and two maximum allowable values of the amplitude of variation of the thermal stress computed either by supposing a linear temperature variation in the wall (VALE_MAXI_LINE), or by supposing a parabolic temperature variation in the wall (VALE_MAXI_PARAB). 6.5 Fatigue computations with the option ‘FATIGUE_ZH210’ The requirements relating to the computation of the usage factor are defined in §2.6.3. The method ‘‘EVOLUTION’’ corresponds to appendix ZH210 of the RCC-M. It consists in “forgetting” the notion of situation and in combining directly loading states , which are the significant time instants of all the transients where the stresses pass through a local extremum. By default, in code_aster , all the computation time instants are used. One associates with each of them the number of occurrences N_{occ} of the transient. The definition is therefore: Loading state = {time instant, stress tensor, number of occurrences}. Next, one constructs the set of all the loading states by sweeping all the transients. In the end, the notion of transient is forgotten: one works only on a set of loading states. One then computes the elementary usage factors associated with all the combinations taken two by two. One then uses a method of cumulation of the elementary usage factors, based on the hypothesis of the linear cumulation of damage, in order to obtain the global usage factor. The main advantage of this method is to consider automatically all the possible sub-cycles: it is not necessary to identify the fictitious transients combining the situations with one another. Its drawback is the number of computations to be carried out if one does not restrict the set of the time instants used in the computation. Note The algorithm described here is similar to that of POST_FATIGUE. More precisely, the algorithm used in POST_FATIGUE is a restriction to the uniaxial case of the ZH210 method. Indeed, the datum of the command POST_FATIGUE is a scalar function of time, whereas POST_RCCM deals with stress tensors functions of time. 6.5.1 Computation of the elementary usage factors At each end of the segment, for every pair of loading states k and l , one computes the quantities S_p(k,l) and S_n(k,l) defined by: S_p(k,l)=\left(\sigma_{ij}(k)-\sigma_{ij}(l)\right)_{Eq.Tresca} For the computation of S_{alt} , two formulae are proposed (cf. r7.04.03-calcul-salt ): - the original method (KE_MECA) which makes no distinction between the mechanical part and the thermal part: - the KE_MIXTE method introduced in the 1997 modification of the RCC-M, which is based on a decomposition of S_{alt} between the mechanical part and the thermal part. The fatigue curve N_{adm}=f(S_{alt}) is a function defined by DEFI_FONCTION, and introduced into DEFI_MATERIAU by the keyword WOHLER of the factor keyword FATIGUE. It makes it possible to compute the number of allowable cycles N_{adm}(k,l) associated with S_{alt}(k,l) , then the elementary usage factor: u(k,l)=\frac{1}{N_{adm}(k,l)} This computation is carried out for each combination of two loading states. One therefore obtains (still for each end of the segment) a symmetric matrix u(k,l) , of order the number of loading states N_{tot} . 6.5.2 Computation of the total usage factor The algorithm for the computation of the total usage factor, for each of the ends of the cutting line, is the following: 1. u^{tot}=0 2. u^{max}=0 3. Loop i=1\ldots N_{tot} (search for the maximum in the table) If Nocc(i)>0 : > Loop j=i+1\ldots N_{tot} > If Nocc(j)>0 and u(i,j)>u^{max} : > u^{max}=u(i,j),\; m=i,\; n=j 4. Nocc(m,n)=\min\left(Nocc(m),Nocc(n)\right) 5. u^{tot}=u^{tot}+Nocc(m,n) u(m,n) 6. Updating of the number of occurrences: Nocc(m)=Nocc(m)-Nocc(m,n) 7. Nocc(n)=Nocc(n)-Nocc(m,n) 8. Return to the beginning of the procedure until elimination of all the occurrences. - If the number of time instants defined for each transient is large, the computation time can be prohibitive. One must therefore be able to restrict it. This is what is done in POST_FATIGUE, by a preliminary sorting of the time instants. One eliminates the time instants such that the scalar function is linear, in order to keep only the ends of the straight-line segments. One also eliminates the very small variations. Here, in a multiaxial situation, the sorting is more delicate. The notion of proportional stresses could be used, but in practice the user can define himself the list of the time instants (keyword NUME_ORDRE). - By this method, one is sure not to forget any sub-cycle. On the other hand, it is desirable to eliminate the time instants which do not correspond to local extrema, because they could generate spurious sub-cycles, increasing the usage factor (these time instants are used only for the numerical discretisation of the mechanical or thermal problem). - With the option ‘FATIGUE_ZH210’, the combinations of transients are taken into account in the computation of S_n and of S_n . In this case, the notion of usage factor defined previously is no longer suitable and it must be replaced by the notion of initiation factor (B3234.7). The initiation factor is computed from the amplitude of variation of the stress in the structure at a distance d from the singularity, and from an initiation law. The analysis procedure is defined in appendix ZD2200. The distance d and the initiation laws are material characteristics and are tabulated in table ZD2300. The initiation law defined in the RCC-M is of the form: \Delta\sigma_{\theta\theta}(d)=A_{AMORC}\cdot(N_a)^{B_{AMORC}} with N_a the number of acceptable cycles and \Delta\sigma_{\theta\theta} the amplitude of variation of the tangential stresses, in the local frame, at the distance d from the singularity. The initiation law developed in the operator POST_RCCM takes into account the load ratio R of the loading, as recommended in the RSE-M (ref 15): \Delta\sigma_{eff}(d)=A_{AMORC}\cdot(N_a)^{B_{AMORC}} with the following relation between the real amplitude of variation of the stresses \Delta\sigma_{\theta\theta} and the effective one \Delta\sigma_{eff} : \Delta\sigma_{eff}=\frac{\Delta\sigma_{\theta\theta}}{1-?} Note In order to use an initiation law such as defined in the RCC-M, that is without taking the load ratio into account, it is sufficient to define a large R_AMORC (1000 for example). 6.6.2 Computation in code_aster The parameters of the initiation law (A_AMORC, B_AMORC, R_AMORC) and the distance to the singularity D_AMORC are to be defined under the factor keyword RCCM of DEFI_MATERIAU. The table expected as input, under the keyword TABL_SIGM_THETA, corresponds to the reading of the stresses on a circular cutting line (of radius D_AMORC) around the singularity. The stresses must be expressed in the local frame . definition of the local frame Such a table can be created by means of the command MACR_LIGN_COUPE. As in the fatigue computation (cf. §6.4), one considers that all the time instants supplied correspond to extrema of the transient. Furthermore, the notion of transient is forgotten and one works only on a set of loading states. One denotes by N_{occ}(i) the number of occurrences associated with the loading state i and by N_{tot} the total number of loading states. The computation algorithm is then the following: Loop over the points of the cutting line - Check that the point is at the distance d from the singularity - Loop over the points of the cutting line - Check that the point is at the distance d from the singularity - Loop i=1\ldots N_{tot} - Extraction of \sigma_{\theta\theta}(i) - Loop j=i+1\ldots N_{tot} - Extraction of \sigma_{\theta\theta}(j) - Computation of \Delta\sigma_{\theta\theta}(i,j)=\left|\sigma_{\theta\theta}(j)-\sigma_{\theta\theta}(i)\right| - Computation of R(i,j)=? - Computation of \Delta\sigma_{eff}(i,j)=\frac{\Delta\sigma_{\theta\theta}(i,j)}{1-?} - Computation of the number of allowable cycles and of the elementary initiation factor N_a(i,j)=(?)^{1/B_{AMORC}} FA(i,j)=? At the end of this first part, one therefore has a matrix of the initiation factors of the set of the combinations of loading states. The size of the matrix is N_{tot} x N_{tot} but only the part above the diagonal is filled in. The algorithm for the computation of the total initiation factor, for a given point on the cutting line, is then the following: 1. FA^{max}=0 2. FA^{tot}=0 3. Loop i=1\ldots N_{tot} (search for the maximum in the table) If Nocc(i)>0 : > Loop j=i+1\ldots N_{tot} > If Nocc(j)>0 and FA(i,j)>FA^{max} : FA^{max}=FA(i,j),\quad m=i,\quad n=j Nocc(m,n)=\min\left(Nocc(m),Nocc(n)\right) FA^{tot}=FA^{tot}+Nocc(m,n)\times FA(m,n) 6. Updating of the number of occurrences: Nocc(m)=Nocc(m)-Nocc(m,n) Nocc(n)=Nocc(n)-Nocc(m,n) 7. Return to the beginning of the procedure until elimination of all the occurrences. At the end of this algorithm, one thus has the initiation factor for each of the points (i.e. for each of the angles) of the cutting line. 7 Type 'B3600' In code_aster, it is possible to evaluate level-A criteria (fatigue) according to chapter B3600 of the RCC-M. It is customary in B3600 to define each situation as the passage from a stabilised state A (corresponding to a given internal pressure in the piping line, a given uniform temperature, and fixed mechanical loadings) to a stabilised state B (with constant loadings different from the preceding ones). One associates with this situation a thermal transient. Loadings of thermal origin can also be taken into account in the computation. The treatment which is described here is carried out for each node of each mesh cell of the piping line considered. The result obtained will therefore be a usage factor (total or partial) for each node of each mesh cell requested by the user. 7.1 Prior computation of all the loading states For each node of each mesh cell, the present step consists in computing, for all the situations, the moments relating to each stabilised state (by cumulating the various loadings which enter). 7.1.1 Computations of the static loading states One processes the results of the static analyses (field EFGE_ELNO or SIEF_ELNO) for the stabilised states of the list of the situations undergone by the line. A stabilised state can be defined by a list of load cases, each load being signed. In this case, the resultants of the stabilised state are obtained by algebraic summation of the resultants of each of the load cases: M_i=M_{i_{{CHAR}^1}}+M_{i_{{CHAR}^2}}+\cdots\qquad i\in(z) The loadings are for example the constrained thermal expansion, the anchor displacement. 7.1.2 Computation of the seismic loadings The seismic loading is decomposed into two parts: - An inertial part It is computed by imposing on the set of the anchors the same motion characterised by the envelope spectrum of the various floor spectra, in the horizontal directions X and Y on the one hand, and vertical Z on the other hand (in the global frame). To this end, one uses the command COMB_SISM_MODAL, which produces generalised forces which correspond to each earthquake direction as well as the quadratic combination of these forces. The inertial contribution of the earthquake to the component i of the moment is written: M_{i_{S\_DYN}}=\sqrt{\sum_j\left(M_{i_{S\_DYN}}\left(spectre_j\right)\right)^2}\qquad i,j\in((x;y;z);(X;Y;Z)) with M_{i_{S\_DYN}}(spectrej) the moment in the direction i resulting from the dynamic loading in the direction j . This combination is done directly by COMB_SISM_MODAL. - A quasi-static part It is estimated by imposing static differential displacements corresponding to the maxima of the differences of the seismic motions of the anchor points in the course of time. The computations are therefore carried out for each unit loading (one computation per displacement in a given direction for one end of the line). One denotes by N_{ANC} the number of anchor points of the structure. The quasi-static contribution of the differential anchor displacements to the component i of the moment is written: M_{i_{S\_ANC}}=\sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{N_{ANC}}\left(M_{i_{S\_ANC}}^{k}\right)^2} with M_{i_{S\_ANC}}^{k} the i -th component of the moment corresponding to the k -th anchor displacement. 7.1.2.1 Combination of the inertial and differential components due to the earthquake The i -th resulting component is obtained by the root-mean-square of the i -th inertial and differential components: M_{i_S}=\sqrt{\left(M_{i_{S\_ANC}}\right)^2+\left(M_{i_{S\_DYN}}\right)^2}\qquad i\in(x;y;z) which in fact amounts to carrying out the root-mean-square of all the inertial and differential moments, M_{i_S}=\sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^{N_{ANC}}\left(M_{i_{S\_ANC}}^{k}\right)^2+\left(M_{i_{S\_DYN}}\right)^2} \qquad i\in(x;y;z) For the user, the earthquake situation is defined by the list of the results corresponding to the inertial response and to the responses to the displacement of the N_{ANC} successive anchor points. The recombination by root-mean-square is done directly by the operator POST_RCCM. 7.1.3 Computation of the thermal transients The loadings of the type "thermal gradient through the thickness" are decomposed into three parts, cf. r7.04.03-fig-decomposition-distribution : - a constant value which is the mean value of the temperature: T_{moy}=\frac{1}{t}\int_{-t/2}^{t/2}T(y)\,dy where t corresponds to the nominal thickness of the wall. - a linear distribution of zero mean (moment of order 1): V=\frac{12}{t^2}\int_{-t/2}^{t/2}y\cdot T(y)\,dy - a non-linear distribution of zero mean and of zero moment with respect to the mean fibre. For each of the transients and each piping section of the line (and each junction), one therefore carries out beforehand, depending on the geometric complexity of the problem studied, a 2D or 3D thermal analysis. Each analysis is then post-processed so as to extract, for each time instant of the transient, the temperature on the chosen section and the mean values (moments of order 0 and 1). This operation can be done for example by means of two calls to POST_RELEVE_T (OPERATION=‘EXTRACTION’ and OPERATION = ‘MOYENNE’). In the case of a material discontinuity or of a junction, one computes the mean temperature (denoted T_a and T_b ) on the two sides of the junction. In practice, the zones a and b will correspond to segments chosen by the user in POST_RELEVE_T, and the tables produced will be associated with the two adjacent mesh cells having in common the node which corresponds to the junction. Decomposition of the temperature distribution through the thickness of the wall (figure taken from the RCC-M, §B3653.4) 7.2 Computations of the amplitudes of variation of the stresses 7.2.1 Principle of the method The amplitudes of variation of the stresses are defined in paragraph B3653 of the RCC-M for combinations between two time instants or two loading states. Denoting by t_i and t_j these two time instants, one has schematically for the amplitude of variation of a quantity S : S(t_i,t_j)=S^{mecanique}(t_i)-S^{mecanique}(t_j)+S^{thermique}(t_i)-S^{thermique}(t_j) In the method as developed in code_aster , the situations are defined in a simplified way by two stabilised states and a thermal transient: it is then not possible to work directly on each of the time instants of the situations and hypotheses must be introduced. One therefore considers the set of the combinations (i,j) with (i,j)\in(1,2,..,N,1,2,..,N) , N being the number of stabilised states excluding the earthquake (that is 2 times the number of situations of the group). Let two stabilised states, i and j , belonging respectively to the situations p and q . The amplitude of variation S will then be computed in the following way: S(i,j)=S^{mecanique}(i)-S^{mecanique}(j)+\max\left(\Delta S^{thermique}(p),\Delta S^{thermique}(q)\right) denoting by S^{thermique}(p) the amplitude of variation of the thermal stress of the transient p . 1. It is important to note that the amplitude of variation of the stresses is obtained by maximising the amplitude of the thermal stresses for each thermal transient independently of one another. The computation method for the case ‘B3600’ is therefore different from that adopted for the case ‘B3200_UNIT’. 2. As indicated in paragraph B3653.2, all the states of the system must be considered, including the states with zero stress (for example cold shutdown: zero applied pressure and moments and ambient temperature). The stress tensors are reconstructed by linear combination from the stress tensors associated with each of the unit loadings. For example, one denotes by sigma^{F_x} the stress tensor associated with the unit force loading in the direction X . The computation of the stress tensor corresponding to a mechanical loading belonging to a stabilised state is then obtained in the following way: \sigma=F_X\cdot\sigma^{F_X}+F_Y\cdot\sigma^{F_Y}+F_Z\cdot\sigma^{F_Z}+M_X\cdot\sigma^{M_X}+M_Y\cdot\sigma^{M_Y}+M_Z\cdot\sigma^{M_Z}+P\cdot\sigma^{P} The use of this option requires the prior computation of the stress fields for the 7 unit loadings and of the stress fields for each of the thermal transients; the unit fields are to be supplied on the analysis segment by means of tables under the keyword 'RESU_MECA_UNIT'. Note For the branch connections, it is also possible to define two force tensors associated respectively with the body and with the nozzle. The force resultant goes from 6 to 12 components and one goes from 7 to 13 unit loadings. Appendix 5 summarises the equations in this case. 8.1 Computations carried out with the option 'PM_PB' For the moment, this option is available if the data of the situations are in unit form only, not in instantaneous form. Given the primary stress of the reference situation (1st category) and a segment situated outside a zone of major discontinuity. At each end point of this segment of length l , one computes for a situation: P_m=\max_t\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{moy}\right\rVert_{TRESCA}\quad\text{avec}\quad\sigma_{ij}^{moy}=\frac{1}{l}\int_0^l\sigma_{ij}\,ds\quad\text{et}\quad\left\lVert\tau_{ij}\right\rVert_{TRESCA}=\max_{I,J}\left|\tau_I-\tau_J\right| P_b=\max_t\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{fle}\right\rVert_{TRESCA}\quad\text{avec}\quad\sigma_{ij}^{fle}=\frac{6}{l^2}\int_0^l\left(s-\frac{l}{2}\right)\sigma_{ij}\,ds P_{mb}=\max_t\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{lin}\right\rVert_{TRESCA}\quad\text{avec}\quad\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(s=0)=\sigma_{ij}^{moy}-\sigma_{ij}^{fle} \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(s=l)=\sigma_{ij}^{moy}+\sigma_{ij}^{fle} Denoting by A and B the two stabilised mechanical states of the situation, one has: P_m=\max\left\{\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{moy}\right\rVert^{A},\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{moy}\right\rVert^{B}\right\} and P_b=\max\left\{\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{fle}\right\rVert^{A},\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{fle}\right\rVert^{B}\right\} P_{mb}=\max\left\{\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{lin}\right\rVert^{A},\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{lin}\right\rVert^{B}\right\} . 8.2 Computations carried out with the option ‘SN’ 8.2.1 Computation of Sn The computation points are the two ends of the segment. For a given situation , at each end point of this segment of length l , one computes S_n according to paragraph B3232.6: S_n=\max_{t_1,t_2}\left\lVert\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_1)-\sigma_{ij}^{lin}(t_2)\right\rVert_{TRESCA} \quad\text{avec}\quad \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(s=0)=\sigma_{ij}^{moy}-\sigma_{ij}^{fle} \sigma_{ij}^{lin}(s=l)=\sigma_{ij}^{moy}+\sigma_{ij}^{fle} One denotes by \sigma_A and \sigma_B the mechanical stresses associated with the two stabilised states of the situation and by \sigma_{ther}(t) the thermal transient associated with this situation. One then has, \sigma_{A^{lin}}-\sigma_{B^{lin}}=(F_{XA}-F_{XB})\,\sigma^{F_X}+(F_{YA}-F_{YB})\,\sigma^{F_Y}+\ldots+(M_{ZA}-M_{ZB})\,\sigma^{M_Z}+(P_A-P_B)\,\sigma^{P} Depending on the method of selection of the time instants chosen (see r7.04.03-methode-selection-instants), one obtains the amplitude Sn. With 'METHODE' = 'TRESCA', t^{maxSn} and t^{minSn} being the extremal time instants of this transient as defined in r7.04.03-methode-selection-instants, the parameter S_n for the situation is defined by: S_n=\max\left(\left\lVert\sigma_{A^{lin}}-\sigma_{B^{lin}}+\sigma_{tran}^{lin}(t^{maxSn})-\sigma_{tran}^{lin}(t^{minSn})\right\rVert,\left\lVert\sigma_{B^{lin}}-\sigma_{A^{lin}}+\sigma_{tran}^{lin}(t^{maxSn})-\sigma_{tran}^{lin}(t^{minSn})\right\rVert\right) With 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST', the parameter S_n for the situation is defined by: S_n=\max\left(S_{n1},S_{n2}\right) , with S_{n1}=\max_{t_1,t_2}\left\lVert\sigma_{A^{lin}}-\sigma_{B^{lin}}+\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_1)-\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_2)\right\rVert and S_{n2}=\max_{t_1,t_2}\left\lVert\sigma_{B^{lin}}-\sigma_{A^{lin}}+\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_1)-\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_2)\right\rVert . 8.2.2 Computation of Sn One denotes by S_n the amplitude S_n computed without taking into account the bending stresses of thermal origin. If a thermal transient is defined (i.e. the keyword NUME_RESU_THER is filled in), the computation of S_n for a situation is done in a manner similar to that of S_n : S_n =\max\left(\left\lVert\sigma_{A^{lin}}-\sigma_{B^{lin}}+\sigma_{ther}^{moy}(t^{maxSn})-\sigma_{ther}^{moy}(t^{minSn})\right\rVert,\left\lVert\sigma_{B^{lin}}-\sigma_{A^{lin}}+\sigma_{ther}^{moy}(t^{maxSn})-\sigma_{ther}^{moy}(t^{minSn})\right\rVert\right) 8.2.3 Thermal ratchet See r7.04.03-calcul-rochet-thermique . 8.3 Computations carried out with the option ‘FATIGUE’ 8.3.1 Computation of Sn One denotes by \sigma_p (respectively \sigma_q ) the mechanical stresses associated with a stabilised state of situation p (respectively of situation q). One denotes by \sigma_{tran,p}(t) the transient tensor associated with the situation p and by \sigma_{tran,q}(t) the transient tensor associated with the situation q . t_{p^{maxSn}} and t_{p^{minSn}} the extremal time instants of the transient of the situation p and t_{q^{maxSn}} and t_{q^{minSn}} the extremal time instants of the transient of the situation q as defined in r7.04.03-methode-selection-instants . One denotes by \sigma_{tran,p}(t) the transient tensor associated with situation p and by \sigma_{tran,q}(t) the transient tensor associated with situation q. t_{p^{maxSn}} and t_{p^{minSn}} the extremal time instants of the transient of situation p and t_{q^{maxSn}} and t_{q^{minSn}} the extremal time instants of the transient of situation q as defined in r7.04.03-methode-selection-instants . With 'METHODE' = 'TRESCA', the parameters S_{p^1} and S_{p^2} for the combination of situations p and q are defined by: S_{p^{1}}(p,q)=\max\left(S_{pA},S_{pB}\right) S_{p^{2}}(p,q)=\min\left(S_{pA},S_{pB}\right) By maximising over the four possible combinations of stabilised states (\sigma_p,\sigma_q) , S_{pA}=\max\left(\left\lVert\sigma_p-\sigma_q+\sigma_{tran,p}(t_{p^{maxSp})-\sigma_{tran,q}(t_q^{minSp}})\right\rVert,\left\lVert\sigma_q-\sigma_p+\sigma_{tran,p}(t_{p^{maxSp}})-\sigma_{tran,q}(t_q^{minSp})\right\rVert\right) that is 8 possibilities. With 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST', the parameter S_{p^1} for the combination of situations p and q is defined by: S_{p^{1}}(p,q)=\max\left(S_{pA},S_{pB}\right) with S_{pA}=\max_{t_1,t_2}\left\lVert\sigma_p-\sigma_q+\sigma_{tran,p}(t_1)-\sigma_{tran,q}(t_2)\right\rVert S_{pB}=\max_{t_1,t_2}\left\lVert\sigma_q-\sigma_p+\sigma_{tran,p}(t_1)-\sigma_{tran,q}(t_2)\right\rVert If t_{1^p} and t_{1^q} are the time instants of fictitious transient 1 S_{p^1}(p,q) , then one determines the time instants of fictitious transient 2 t_{2^p} and t_{2^q} according to the method described in Appendix 2 and the quantity S_{p^2}(p,q) is equal, by maximising over the four possible combinations of stabilised states (\sigma_p,\sigma_q) , to: S_{p^{2}}(p,q)=\max\left(\left\lVert\sigma_q-\sigma_p+\sigma_{tran,p}(t_{2^{p}})-\sigma_{tran,q}(t_{2^{q}})\right\rVert,\left\lVert\sigma_p-\sigma_q+\sigma_{tran,p}(t_{2^{p}})-\sigma_{tran,q}(t_{2^{q}})\right\rVert\right) Note In this part, \sigma_{tran}(t)=\sigma_{ther}(t) . 8.3.3 Computation of Sp^{meca} One denotes by \sigma_{p1} (respectively \sigma_{q1} ) the mechanical stresses associated with the stabilised states of situation p and of situation q which have maximised the quantity S_{p^1} . One denotes by \sigma_{p^2} (respectively \sigma_{q^2} ) the mechanical stresses associated with the stabilised states which have maximised the quantity S_{p^2} . With 'METHODE' = 'TRESCA' and 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST' : S_{p^{meca,1}}(p,q)=\left\lVert\sigma_{p1}-\sigma_{q1}\right\rVert \quad\text{et}\quad S_{p^{meca,2}}(p,q)=\left\lVert\sigma_{p2}-\sigma_{q2}\right\rVert 9 Appendix 2: B3200 equations for situations in unit form with interpolation on the temperature Each situation is defined by two stabilised mechanical states A and B. Each state is described from a pressure p and a force resultant \left\{F_X,F_Y,F_Z,M_X,M_Y,M_Z\right\} defined under the keyword 'CHAR_MECA' and corresponds to a temperature (TEMP_A or TEMP_B). In this example, the situations have no pressure loading. The user must also enter the temperature profile as a function of time in the course of the situation (keyword 'TABL_TEMP' under the factor keyword ' SITUATION' ) The stress tensors are then reconstructed by linear interpolation from this temperature as a function of time and from the two resultants. The use of this option requires the prior computation of the stress fields for the 6 unit loadings ('RESU_MECA_UNIT') and of the stress fields for each of the thermal transients ('RESU_THER'). For the moment, the computation of PM_PB is not available if the data of the situations are in unit form with interpolation on the temperature. 9.1 Computation of Sn for a situation One denotes by \sigma_{A^{mom,lin}} and \sigma_{B^{mom,lin}} the linearised mechanical stresses associated with the moments of the two stabilised states of the situation and by \sigma_{ther}(t) the thermal transient associated with this situation. One then has, \sigma_{A^{mom,lin}}(T=TEMP_A)=F_{XA}\,\sigma^{lin,F_X}+F_{YA}\,\sigma^{lin,F_Y}+F_{ZA}\,\sigma^{lin,F_Z}+M_{XA}\,\sigma^{M_X,lin}+M_{YA}\,\sigma^{M_Y,lin}+M_{ZA}\,\sigma^{M_Z,lin} \sigma_{B^{mom,lin}}(T=TEMP_B)=F_{XB}\,\sigma^{lin,F_X}+F_{YB}\,\sigma^{lin,F_Y}+F_{ZB}\,\sigma^{lin,F_Z}+M_{XB}\,\sigma^{M_X,lin}+M_{YB}\,\sigma^{M_Y,lin}+M_{ZB}\,\sigma^{M_Z,lin} At the time instants t_1 and t_2 , one has T(t_1)=TEMP_1 and T(t_2)=TEMP_2 . If TEMP_A < TEMP_B , by interpolation one has F_X(t_1)=\frac{F_{XB}-F_{XA}}{TEMP_B-TEMP_A}\cdot TEMP_1+\frac{F_{XA}TEMP_B-F_{XB}TEMP_A}{TEMP_B-TEMP_A} F_X(t_2)=\frac{F_{XB}-F_{XA}}{TEMP_B-TEMP_A}\cdot TEMP_2+\frac{F_{XA}TEMP_B-F_{XB}TEMP_A}{TEMP_B-TEMP_A} The equations are similar for the five other components. One deduces from them the expression of the linearised mechanical stresses due to the moments at the time instants t_1 and t_2 . \sigma^{mom,lin}(t_1)=F_X(t_1)\sigma^{lin,F_X}+F_Y(t_1)\sigma^{lin,F_Y}+\ldots+M_Z(t_1)\sigma^{M_Z,lin} \sigma^{mom,lin}(t_2)=F_X(t_2)\sigma^{lin,F_X}+F_Y(t_2)\sigma^{lin,F_Y}+\ldots+M_Z(t_2)\sigma^{M_Z,lin} With 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST', the parameter S_n for the situation is defined by: S_n=\max_{t_1,t_2}\left\lVert\sigma^{mom,lin}(t_1)-\sigma^{mom,lin}(t_2)+\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_1)-\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_2)\right\rVert With 'METHODE' = 'TRESCA', the parameter S_n for the situation is defined by: S_n=\left\lVert\sigma^{mom,lin}(t_{maxSn})-\sigma^{mom,lin}(t_{minSn})+\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_{maxSn})-\sigma_{ther}^{lin}(t_{minSn})\right\rVert 9.2 Computations carried out with the option ‘FATIGUE’ 9.2.1 Computation of Sn for a combination of situations p and q One denotes by \sigma_{Ap}^{mom,lin} and \sigma_{Bp}^{mom,lin} the linearised mechanical stresses associated with the moments of the two stabilised states of situation p and by \sigma_{ther,p} the thermal transient associated with this situation. One denotes by \sigma_{Aq}^{mom,lin} and \sigma_{Bq}^{mom,lin} the linearised mechanical stresses associated with the moments of the two stabilised states of situation q and by \sigma_{ther,q} the thermal transient associated with this situation. For the time instant t_p belonging to \sigma_{ther,p} , one has T(t_p)=TEMP_p and if TEMP_{Ap}<TEMP_{Bp} , by interpolation one has F_X(t_p)=\frac{F_{XBp}-F_{XAp}}{TEMP_{Bp}-TEMP_{Ap}}\cdot TEMP_p+\frac{F_{XAp}TEMP_{Bp}-F_{XBp}TEMP_{Ap}}{TEMP_{Bp}-TEMP_{Ap}} For the time instant t_q belonging to \sigma_{ther,q} , one has T(t_q)=TEMP_q and if TEMP_{Aq}<TEMP_{Bq} , by interpolation one has F_X(t_q)=\frac{F_{XBq}-F_{XAq}}{TEMP_{Bq}-TEMP_{Aq}}\cdot TEMP_q+\frac{F_{XAq}TEMP_{Bq}-F_{XBq}TEMP_{Aq}}{TEMP_{Bq}-TEMP_{Aq}} The equations are similar for the five other components. One deduces from them the expression of the linearised mechanical stresses due to the moments at the time instants t_p and t_q . \sigma^{mom,lin}(t_p)=F_X(t_p)\sigma^{lin,F_X}+F_Y(t_p)\sigma^{lin,F_Y}+\ldots+M_Z(t_p)\sigma^{M_Z,lin} \sigma^{mom,lin}(t_q)=F_X(t_q)\sigma^{lin,F_X}+F_Y(t_q)\sigma^{lin,F_Y}+\ldots+M_Z(t_q)\sigma^{M_Z,lin} With 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST', the parameter S_n for the combination of situations p and q is: S_n=\max_{t_p,t_q}\left\lVert\sigma^{mom,lin}(t_p)-\sigma^{mom,lin}(t_q)+\sigma_{ther,p}^{lin}(t_p)-\sigma_{ther,q}^{lin}(t_q)\right\rVert 9.2.2 Computation of Sp for a combination of situations p and q One denotes by \sigma_{Ap}^{mom,lin} and \sigma_{Bp}^{mom,lin} the mechanical stresses associated with the moments of the two stabilised states of situation p and by \sigma_{ther,p} the thermal transient associated with this situation. One denotes by \sigma_{Aq}^{mom,lin} and \sigma_{Bq}^{mom,lin} the mechanical stresses associated with the moments of the two stabilised states of situation p and by \sigma_{ther,q} the thermal transient associated with this situation. For the time instant t_p belonging to \sigma_{ther,p} , one has T(t_p)=TEMP_p and if TEMP_{Ap}<TEMP_{Bp} , by interpolation one has F_X(t_p)=\frac{F_{XBp}-F_{XAp}}{TEMP_{Bp}-TEMP_{Ap}}\cdot TEMP_p+\frac{F_{XAp}TEMP_{Bp}-F_{XBp}TEMP_{Ap}}{TEMP_{Bp}-TEMP_{Ap}} For the time instant t_q belonging to \sigma_{ther,q} , one has T(t_q)=TEMP_q and if TEMP_{Aq}<TEMP_{Bq} , by interpolation one has F_X(t_q)=\frac{F_{XBq}-F_{XAq}}{TEMP_{Bq}-TEMP_{Aq}}\cdot TEMP_q+\frac{F_{XAq}TEMP_{Bq}-F_{XBq}TEMP_{Aq}}{TEMP_{Bq}-TEMP_{Aq}} The equations are similar for the five other components. One deduces from them the expression of the mechanical stresses due to the moments at the time instants tp and tq. \sigma^{mom}(t_p)=F_X(t_p)\sigma^{F_X}+F_Y(t_p)\sigma^{F_Y}+\ldots+M_Z(t_p)\sigma^{M_Z} \sigma^{mom}(t_q)=F_X(t_q)\sigma^{F_X}+F_Y(t_q)\sigma^{F_Y}+\ldots+M_Z(t_q)\sigma^{M_Z} With 'METHODE' = 'TOUT_INST', the parameter S_{p^1} for the combination of situations p and q is: S_{p^{1}}=\max_{t_p,t_q}\left\lVert\sigma^{mom}(t_p)-\sigma^{mom}(t_q)+\sigma_{ther,p}(t_p)-\sigma_{ther,q}(t_q)\right\rVert The time instants of S_{p^2} are determined according to Appendix 5. 10 Appendix 3: Equations for a piping junction (branch connection) 10.1 Type ’B3200’ Situation of unit type One denotes by \sigma_1 and \sigma_2 the mechanical stresses associated with the two stabilised states of the situation. r7.04.04 Multiaxial fatigue-initiation criteria r7.04.04 Multiaxial fatigue-initiation criteria Summary: In this note we propose a formulation of the MATAKE, DANG VAN and FATEMI-SOCIE criteria and of the formula criteria adapted to the framework of damage accumulation under multiaxial periodic and non-periodic loading. These criteria can be used in the command CALC_FATIGUE. The first part of this document is devoted to the MATAKE and DANG VAN criteria adapted to periodic multiaxial loadings. In this part, after having addressed the notions of endurance and of damage accumulation and the general form of the fatigue criteria, we describe the two models of DANG VAN and of MATAKE (critical plane) intended to carry out damage-accumulation analyses under multiaxial loading. One details there the definition of the various shear planes associated with the Gauss points or with the nodes, as well as the definition of a loading amplitude through the circle circumscribed about the loading path in the shear plane. Finally the criteria available in Code_Aster are presented. In the second part we propose a formulation of the MATAKE, DANG VAN and FATEMI-SOCIE criteria within the framework of damage accumulation under non-periodic multiaxial loading. In order to define a cycle in the variable-amplitude case, we reduce the loading history to a one-dimensional function of time by projecting the tip of the shear vector onto an axis, and we use a cycle-counting method. Here we choose the RAINFLOW method. The MATAKE, DANG VAN and FATEMI-SOCIE criteria adapted to damage accumulation under non-periodic loading are implemented in Code_Aster . In addition to the well-established criteria, one has available in Code_Aster formula criteria allowing the user to construct new criteria as functions of the predefined quantities. This type of criterion is detailed in the third part of this document. Finally, the option VMIS_TRESCA makes it possible to compute the maximum variation, over time, of a stress tensor according to the Von Mises and Tresca criteria. 1 Introduction The multiaxial fatigue
