u2.01.09 Definition of an initial stress field and of an initial field of internal variables u2.01.09 Definition of an initial stress field and of an initial field of internal variables > Summary. It is explained how to build two of the fields which make up the initial state of a non-linear analysis (STAT_NON_LINE): the stress field and the field of internal variables. - the components of the stress field have an "analytical" form (for example: state of a soil subjected to the "weight of the earth"), - the components of the field of internal variables are non-zero constants. In both cases, the solution consists in chaining a certain number of CREA_CHAMP commands. For the stress field, the difficulty consists in evaluating the "analytical formulae" (OPERATION='EVAL'). For the field of internal variables, the difficulty comes from the fact that the quantity associated with the internal variables (VARI_R) has an a priori undetermined number of components: 'V1', 'V2', ... The solutions proposed are implemented in the test zzzz130A. The test zzzz130b shows how to use the Python field API to build the same stress field and field of internal variables. 1 Definition of the analytical stress field It is assumed that the model contains continuum finite elements (MODELISATION='3D'). One wants the stress components to have the following expressions at each Gauss point: - SIZZ = RHO G Z - SIXX = SIYY = KP SIZZ where: - RHO: density - G: acceleration due to gravity - Z: 3rd space coordinate - KP: coefficient of soil "thrust" The solution proposed consists in: 1. defining three "formula" functions corresponding to SIXX, SIYY and SIZZ, 2. building a field whose components are the previous functions, 3. evaluating the formulae of the field by supplying it with the geometry field required for their evaluation. 1.1 Step 1: defining the formulae RHO = 1000.0 G = 10.0 KP = 3.0 SIZZ = FORMULE(REEL="""(REEL:Z) = RHO G Z """) SIXX = FORMULE(REEL="""(REEL:Z) = KP SIZZ(Z) """) SIYY = FORMULE(REEL="""(REEL:Z) = KP SIZZ(Z) """) 1.2 Step 2: creating the field of formulae SIG1 SIG1 = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="AFFE", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_NEUT_F", MODELE=MO, PROL_ZERO="OUI", AFFE=_F(TOUT="OUI", NOM_CMP=("X1", "X2", "X3"), VALE_F=(SIXX, SIYY, SIZZ)), ) - the field SIG1 which one creates is a cham_elem at the Gauss points (ELGA), - the only fields which can have components of "function" type are the fields of the quantity NEUT_F. One must therefore remember that the component 'X1' of SIG1 is in reality 'SIXX', etc., - the keyword PROL_ZERO='OUI' is mandatory because, for every finite-element type, the NEUT_R cham_elem currently have 6 components: 'X1', 'X2', ..., 'X6'. One must therefore accept "extending" the field by zero over the 3 components which are not assigned. Extension by "zero" for a field whose components are texts (names of the functions) consists in assigning the string " " to each component absent from the field. Caution, therefore: this is not a zero function. This can be seen by using INFO=2 to print the field SIG1. > Notes. 1.3 Step 3: evaluating the formulae of the field SIG1 The field SIG1 is a field known at the Gauss points of the finite elements of the model. At each point, one will want to evaluate the functions SIXX, SIYY and SIZZ. For that, the values of all the variables appearing in the functions (here Z) must be available. These variables must be known at the same points as the field of functions. One must therefore have a field containing the geometry of the Gauss points (cham_elem_GEOM_R / ELGA). This field of the geometry of the Gauss points (CHXG) is obtained from the mesh (MA) by the following 2 commands: CHXN = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="EXTR", TYPE_CHAM="NOEU_GEOM_R", NOM_CHAM="GEOMETRIE", MAILLAGE=MA, INFO=1 ) CHXG = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION="DISC", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_GEOM_R", MODELE=MO, CHAM_GD=CHXN, INFO=1) The first command extracts the geometry field (at the nodes) from the mesh. The second transforms the geometry field at the nodes into a geometry field at the Gauss points by using the shape functions of the finite elements of the model. The functions can then be evaluated by means of the operator CREA_CHAMP / OPERATION='EVAL': SIG2 = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION="EVAL", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_NEUT_R", INFO=1, CHAM_F=SIG1, CHAM_PARA=(CHXG,)) The field (SIG2) obtained by evaluation of a field of the quantity NEUT_F is a field of the quantity NEUT_R whose components have the same names as the components of NEUT_F: 'X1', 'X2', ..., 'X6'. Caution The components 'X4', 'X5', 'X6' are undefined (in reality they contain the largest possible real number), because they correspond to a non-existent function. It remains to change the quantity of the field SIG2 (NEUT_R into SIEF_R) in order to finish building our analytical stress field: SIGINI = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="ASSE", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_SIEF_R", MODELE=MO, PROL_ZERO="OUI", ASSE=_F( TOUT="OUI", CHAM_GD=SIG2, NOM_CMP=("X1", "X2", "X3"), NOM_CMP_RESU=("SIXX", "SIYY", "SIZZ") ), ) - only the components 'X1', 'X2' and 'X3' of the field SIG2 are copied in this operation, to give the components 'SIXX', 'SIYY', 'SIZZ' of the field SIGINI. This stress field must also contain the components related to the shears ('SIXY', 'SIYZ', 'SIXZ'). To obtain them (with a zero value), extension by zero must be used, with PROL_ZERO='OUI'. - the operations carried out in order to obtain the zero shear components would have been simpler if a zero function had been assigned explicitly to these 3 components. One would not have had to "play" with the extensions. But one would have benefited from the coincidence that the quantities SIEF_R and NEUT_R both have 6 components for the cham_elem (ELGA) on the finite elements of the model. > Notes. 2 Definition of the non-zero field of internal variables 2.1 Problem One wants to create a field of initial internal variables for the command STAT_NON_LINE. This field must not be zero everywhere. More precisely, one wants: STAT_NON_LINE( COMPORTEMENT=( _F(GROUP_MA='MASSIF', RELATION = 'CJS'), _F(GROUP_MA='BETON', RELATION = 'ENDO_LOCAL'),), for the constitutive relation 'CJS' (16 internal variables), one wants to assign: V1 = 1.0 and V9 = 9.0 for the constitutive relation 'ENDO_LOCAL' (2 internal variables), one wants to assign: V2 = 2.0 2.2 First method The operator to use is CREA_CHAMP / OPERATION='AFFE'. It makes it possible to assign (by mesh cell or GROUP_MA) the values one wishes. The difficulty comes from the fact that the quantity associated with the internal variables (VARI_R) is different from the others: one does not know a priori what its components are. Indeed, the name of its components reflects this ignorance: 'V1', 'V2', ... Depending on the constitutive behaviour chosen by the user in STAT_NON_LINE, the number of internal variables changes. In our example, the constitutive behaviour 'CJS' requires 16 variables, whereas 'ENDO_LOCAL' uses only 2. The assignment operation is carried out as follows: VAIN1 = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="AFFE", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_VARI_R", MODELE=MO, PROL_ZERO="OUI", AFFE=( _F(GROUP_MA="BETON", NOM_CMP="V2", VALE=2.0), _F(GROUP_MA="MASSIF", NOM_CMP=("V1", "V9", "V16"), VALE=(1.0, 9.0, 0.0)), ), ) - The keyword PROL_ZERO='OUI' makes it possible to assign only the non-zero components. But, as the command does not know the number of internal variables carried by the mesh cells, it relies on the highest number assigned. In the example above, on the group 'MASSIF', it is important to assign 'V16' (here to 0.) so that the field has 16 components. - It is important, for the non-linear analysis which follows, that the field of internal variables be consistent with the constitutive behaviours that one will choose. Here, the mesh cells of the group 'BETON' must have 2 internal variables (and only 2), and those of the group 'MASSIF' must have 16. Important notes Caution If the model includes other types of constitutive behaviour (for which one does not wish to initialise the field with non-zero values), zero values must also be assigned to them explicitly. This drawback (having to know ALL the constitutive behaviours used and their number of internal variables) can be removed with the 2nd method below (but it is more complicated). 2.3 Second method This method (more complicated) makes it possible to assign explicitly only the mesh cells which possess non-zero components. The problem is to obtain a field containing the correct number of internal variables for each mesh cell, as a function of the constitutive behaviour which will be assigned to it in STAT_NON_LINE. To solve this problem, a fictitious non-linear analysis will be carried out (with the real constitutive behaviours). The field of internal variables produced will then be a good "model" of a field. One will therefore proceed as follows: 1. fictitious non-linear analysis: UBID 2. extraction of the field of internal variables (VBID) from the result UBID 3. assignment of the non-zero values in the field VAIN2 4. setting VBID to zero + overloading of the values of VAIN2 in order to produce the result VAIN22 2.3.1 Fictitious non-linear analysis BETON = DEFI_MATERIAU(ELAS=_F(E=20000.0, NU=0.0), ECRO_LINE=_F(SY=6.0, D_SIGM_EPSI=-10000.0)) MASSIF = DEFI_MATERIAU( ELAS=_F(E=35.0e3, NU=0.15), CJS=_F( BETA_CJS=-0.55, GAMMA_CJS=0.82, PA=-100.0, RM=0.289, N_CJS=0.6, KP=25.5e3, RC=0.265, A_CJS=0.25, ), ) CHMAT = AFFE_MATERIAU( MAILLAGE=MA, AFFE=(_F(GROUP_MA="MASSIF", MATER=MASSIF), _F(GROUP_MA="BETON", MATER=BETON)) ) TEMPS1 = DEFI_LIST_REEL(VALE=(0.0, 1.0)) CHAR_U1 = AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MO, DDL_IMPO=_F(NOEUD=("N1", "N2", "N3"), DX=0.0, DY=0.0, DZ=0.0)) UBID = STAT_NON_LINE( MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CHMAT, EXCIT=_F(CHARGE=CHAR_U1), COMPORTEMENT=( _F(GROUP_MA="MASSIF", RELATION="CJS"), _F(GROUP_MA="BETON", RELATION="ENDO_LOCAL"), ), NEWTON=_F(MATRICE="ELASTIQUE"), CONVERGENCE=_F( ARRET="NON", ITER_GLOB_MAXI=1, ITER_INTE_MAXI=1 # pour continuer sans convergence ), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=TEMPS1), ) 2.3.2 Recovery of the "model" field of internal variables VABID = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="EXTR", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_VARI_R", INFO=1, NOM_CHAM="VARI_ELGA", RESULTAT=UBID, NUME_ORDRE=1, ) > Note. VABID is not zero. 2.3.3 Assignment of the non-zero values in a NEUT_R map VAIN2 = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="AFFE", TYPE_CHAM="CART_NEUT_R", MODELE=MO, AFFE=( _F(GROUP_MA="BETON", NOM_CMP=("X2",), VALE=(2.0,)), _F(GROUP_MA="MASSIF", NOM_CMP=("X1", "X9"), VALE=(1.0, 9.0)), ), ) 2.3.4 Setting the "model" field of internal variables to zero and overloading the non-zero values VAIN22 = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION="ASSE", TYPE_CHAM="ELGA_VARI_R", MODELE=MO, # mise à zéro: ASSE=( _F(TOUT="OUI", CHAM_GD=VABID, CUMUL="OUI", COEF_R=0.0), # surcharge des valeurs non nulles: _F( GROUP_MA="BETON", CHAM_GD=VAIN2, CUMUL="OUI", COEF_R=1.0, NOM_CMP=("X2",), NOM_CMP_RESU=("V2",), ), _F( GROUP_MA="MASSIF", CHAM_GD=VAIN2, CUMUL="OUI", COEF_R=1.0, NOM_CMP=("X1", "X3"), NOM_CMP_RESU=("V1", "V9"), ), ), ) > Note. For setting to zero and for overloading the non-zero values, the keywords CUMUL='OUI' and COEF_R=0. are used.

u2.01.10 User's guide on the choice of finite elements u2.01.10 User's guide on the choice of finite elements > Summary. This document aims to give some information on the choice of finite elements and of their associated modelling in the case of thermal, thermomechanical or non-linear mechanical studies. It amounts, in a sense, to proposing to the user an a priori choice, making it possible to avoid certain common errors. In the event of particular difficulties, other choices may be made. 1 Introduction This document gives the a priori choices which may be made concerning the finite elements. The case considered is that of a thermomechanical chaining, but the advice remains valid for thermal or mechanical analyses which are not chained (linear or otherwise). A brief justification is given. For more details on the justification of these choices, the user may refer to the reference documents of Code_Aster as well as to the note [bib1]. 2 A priori choices 2.1 The mesh The elements may equally well be: - triangular elements or quadrangles in 2D, - tetrahedra or hexahedra in 3D. Indeed, contrary to a widespread idea, elements of triangle or tetrahedron type give good results, even in plasticity, provided of course that one does not use a mesh that is too coarse . One may also use the HOMARD software, which carries out the adaptation of 2D/3D meshes for finite elements of triangular, quadrangular, tetrahedral or hexahedral type by refinement and unrefinement. One can thus obtain the optimum mesh as a function of an error indicator (cf. R4.10.01, R4.10.02, R4.10.03, or the test case TPLL01j V4.02.01 for a demonstration) by calling the command MACR_ADAP_MAIL in the Code_Aster command file. On the other hand, it is recommended to use: - linear elements in thermal analysis for chained analyses and for rapid transient thermal analyses. For the other cases, one may also opt for quadratic elements, - quadratic elements in mechanics. This choice is all the more important when one carries out chained thermal then mechanical analyses. One must then use two different meshes for the thermal analysis and for the mechanical analysis. Two strategies are then possible: - either mesh the structure independently for the thermal analysis and for the mechanical analysis - or build a mesh with linear elements and then transform it into a quadratic mesh by means of the command CREA_MAILLAGE, factor keyword LINE_QUAD. Whatever method is chosen, one can optimise each mesh separately with Homard by means of the thermal and mechanical error indicators available in Aster (cf. test case forma05b V6.03.120). > Note. | It is recalled here that all quantities of stress or strain type are computed at the Gauss points, and that any transfer to the nodes introduces a bias. This is all the more true when one then seeks to compute norms; we have thus observed that the tetrahedra were more sensitive than the hexahedra to the method of computation of the equivalent stresses, for example. One must therefore look even more critically at the results computed at the nodes. | | --- | 2.2 The modelling Whether for the solution of thermal or mechanical problems, several modellings are available in Code_Aster . These different modellings may be distinguished by the number or the type of degrees of freedom, the number of integration points, particular treatments… Depending on the analysis carried out, some are of course better suited than others. 2.2.1 In thermal analysis To carry out a thermal analysis with Code_Aster , two types of modelling are available (U3.23.01, U3.24.01, R3.06.02, R3.06.07): - classical finite elements: modelling 3D, AXIS or PLAN - lumped or diagonalised finite elements: modelling 3D_DIAG, AXIS_DIAG or PLAN_DIAG We propose as the default choice: modelling XXXX_DIAG with linear elements Justification In thermal analysis, the time step \Delta t cannot be arbitrary; it must satisfy a condition \Delta {t}_{\min} 0.45 ) | | --- | --- | --- | | triangles/tetrahedra | standard | INCO | | quadrilaterals/hexahedra | SI | SI or INCO | Justifications and precautions: - If the material is quasi-incompressible ( \nu >0,45 ), it is preferable to use one of the INCO formulations, because the standard displacement formulation does not give good results. - Plastic flow takes place at constant volume. This incompressibility condition may cause difficulties with the classical modelling, namely an overly stiff behaviour and, above all, the appearance of oscillations in the stresses. Under-integration makes it possible to improve these problems, because one then checks the incompressibility condition at fewer Gauss points. However, only the QUAD8 and HEXA20 elements are truly under-integrated; for the other mesh cells, it is the classical integration which is retained. Consequently, when oscillation phenomena are observed for a mesh composed of triangles or tetrahedra, it is preferable to use one of the INCO formulations. This markedly improves the results, but the analyses will take longer. - In the general case, the under-integrated modelling gives results as good as those of the classical finite elements, and this for a shorter run time, since fewer Gauss points are used. Furthermore, in the case of thermomechanical analyses, this makes it possible to limit the difficulties when passing from the strain of thermal origin to the mechanical analysis when the refinements of the thermal and mechanical meshes differ. However, under-integration may sometimes lead to the appearance of spurious modes. If, at the end of the analysis, the deformed shape exhibits this kind of non-physical deformation mode, it is better to carry out the analysis with the classical modelling, or with the quasi-incompressible modelling if the levels of plasticity are very high. 3 Implementation in Code_Aster The main stages of the Aster analysis are recalled here in the case of a plane-strain analysis, stating explicitly where the specifications discussed above come into play. For the mechanical part, what is specific to the case of a thermomechanical analysis has been written in bold. 3.1 Thermal study - Reading of the thermal mesh | MA=LIRE_MAILLAGE(UNITE=20,) | | --- | - Choice of the thermal model MOTH2D=AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=MA, VERIF='MAILLE', AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA= (‘GMA1’,’GMA2’,…), PHENOMENE='THERMIQUE', MODELISATION='PLAN_DIAG',),) - Thermal properties of the material - Thermal loading - THER_LINEAIRE or THER_NON_LINE THER = … - Possible post-processings 3.2 Mechanical study - Reading of the mechanical mesh | MAME=LIRE_MAILLAGE() | MAME=CREA_MAILLAGE( MAILLAGE = MA, LINE_QUAD=_F(TOUT=’OUI’)) | | --- | --- | - Definition of the mechanical model MOME=AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=MAME, VERIF='MAILLE', AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA= (‘GMA1’,’GMA2’,…), PHENOMENE='MECANIQUE', MODELISATION='D_PLAN_SI',),); - Projection of the thermal analysis if the analysis is chained onto 2 different meshes CHTHER=PROJ_CHAMP( METHODE='COLLOCATION', RESULTAT=THER, MODELE_1=MOTH2D, MODELE_2=MOME,); - Characteristics of the material CHMAT = AFFE_MATERIAU(MAILLAGE = MAME, AFFE_VARC = _F( NOM_VARC='TEMP', TEMP_REF = 20., EVOL=CHTER ou THER si pas de projection …) - Mechanical loadings - STAT_NON_LINE - Post-processings 4 Bibliography 1. MICHEL-PONNELLE, A. RAZAKANAIVO: Quality of Studies in Solid Mechanics: study of the finite elements. Note EDF HT-64/02/007/B

u2.01.11 User's guide for the handling of fields and tables u2.01.11 User's guide for the handling of fields and tables Summary: The aim of this document is to provide the user with a few recipes related to the handling of fields or tables. This document describes the following cases of field handling: - Continuing a STAT_NON_LINE analysis after having removed or added elements in the model (e.g.: excavation of a tunnel, placing of the layers of a dam); - Defining an initial stress state (or of internal variables) from "analytical formulae"; - Applying a pressure on a part (not provided for in the mesh) of the boundary of a 3D structure; - Computing the integral of the stresses or of a derived quantity on the boundary of a 3D structure; - Reading back a field that is constant per element and projecting it onto the nodes of the mesh. And for the tables: - Evaluating a damping on the computed eigenfrequencies. 1 How to continue a STAT_NON_LINE analysis after having removed or added elements in the model 1.1 Problem statement The restart of an analysis with a model made up of additional elements, or conversely of a model restricted to certain elements, requires certain precautions. Indeed, the analysis is no longer carried out on the same number of elements, which means that the fields defining the initial state for the restart of the analysis (displacement, stress and internal-variable fields) must undergo a few adjustments in order to be taken into account in the solution operator. When one removes finite elements from the model, the problem is a priori fairly simple: it is enough to "forget" information. On the other hand, when one wants to add elements, one must "invent" some. That is why, in the remainder of this document, we shall treat the case of the addition of elements. 1.2 Addition of elements in the model 1.2.1 Objective We shall present a methodology which makes it possible to carry out this kind of analysis, starting from an example. Step 0 Step 1 Step 2 Step 3 In this example one wishes to simulate the progressive addition of elements in the study, for example to simulate the construction of a dam by successively adding layers of elements. Four steps will be necessary to carry out these analyses: at the first step, the analysis will be carried out on a model made up of the mesh-cell group \mathrm{E1} , at the second on a model made up of the mesh-cell groups \mathrm{E1}+\mathrm{E2} , and so on up to step 4. The user will have taken care, when building the mesh, to define explicitly the mesh-cell groups \mathrm{E1} , \mathrm{E2} , \mathrm{E3} and \mathrm{E4} . The user will begin by carrying out step 0, which consists in performing the analysis on the mesh restricted to the group \mathrm{E1} . For the following steps, which consist in continuing the analysis carried out previously, several "forms" of implementation can be envisaged: - either one carries out a restart (new command file): this choice is not relevant if the number of layers of elements is large, - or one enriches the command file: the size of the command file is a function of the number of restarts, and therefore of the number of layers; this choice is not necessarily judicious. - or one uses a Python loop: we favour this choice because it has the advantage of being easily extensible in order to take into account the addition of further layers. In substance, the procedure is the same: with the aim of supplying an initial state to the analysis, it calls the operator CREA_CHAMP: - to extract the displacement, stress and internal-variable fields, - to extend these fields to the new model. The following diagram illustrates the simplified structure of the command file: Initialisation of the Python lists for storing the Aster concepts Step 0: - creation of the GROUP_MA 'ELEM': ELEM = E1 - creation of the model MOD[0], of the material field MAT[0], of the loading CHA[0]. - carrying out of the analysis U[0] - extraction of the fields of U[0], useful for the initial state of the following analysis Python loop on i (i=1,3) to treat steps 1, 2 and 3: Update of the GROUP_MA 'ELEM': ELEM = E1+…+E(i+1) Creation of the model MOD[i], of the material field MAT[i] and of the loading CHA[i]. Creation of the fields on the new model from the fields extracted at step i-1 Carrying out of the analysis U[i] having specified an initial state Extraction of the fields of U[i] for step i+1 In the table below we present the commands executed as well as the concepts produced. One will notice how the concepts pass from one step to the next. | | | Step 0 | Step 1 | Step 2 | Step 3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mesh | LIRE_MAILLAGE DEFI_GROUP | E1 | E1+E2 | E1+E2+E3 | E1+E2+E3+E4 | | Model | AFFE_MODELE | MOD_0 | MOD_1 | MOD_2 | MOD_3 | | Material | AFFE_MATERIAU | MAT_0 | MAT_1 | MAT_2 | MAT_3 | | Load | AFFE_CHAR_MECA | CHA_0 | CHA_1 | CHA_2 | CHA_3 | | Initial state | CREA_CHAMP/ASSE | | DEP_0 SIG_0 VARI_0 | DEP_1 SIG_1 VARI_1 | DEP_2 SIG_2 VARI_2 | | Solution | STAT_NON_LINE | U_0 | U_1 | U_2 | U_3 | | Extraction | CREA_CHAMP/EXTR | DEP_0 SIG_0 VARI_0 | DEP_1 SIG_1 VARI_1 | DEP_2 SIG_2 VARI_2 | DEP_3 SIG_3 VARI_3 | Table 1.1: concepts produced ( : field computed at step i , expected at step i+1 ) The various steps and their implementations in the command file are presented in what follows. 1.2.2 Implementation 1.2.2.1 Initialisation Each concept produced by these operators will be stored in a Python list. These lists must therefore be allocated. Let n be the number of layers of elements: in this example, n=4 . One will write in the command file: - MOD=[None] n, - MAT=[None] n, - CHA=[None] n, - U=[None] n, - DEP=[None] n, - SIG=[None] n, - VARI=[None] n. Note: It is enough to modify the value of n in order to take into account new layers of elements. 1.2.2.2 Step 0: layer \mathit{E1} - one defines the group 'ELEM' which will evolve according to the various steps: DEFI_GROUP(MAILLAGE=MA, CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='ELEM',GROUP_MA='E1'),) - Creation of the new model, assignment of the material and of the loading: MOD[0]=AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=MA,AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA='ELEM',...) MAT[0]=AFFE_MATERIAU(MODELE=MOD[0], AFFE=_F(TOUT='OUI',MATE=...),...) CHA[0]=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MOD[0], …) - Analysis: U[0]=STAT_NON_LINE(MODELE=MOD[0],CHAM_MATER=MAT[0], EXCIT=_F(CHARGE=CHA[0]),...) - Extraction of the displacement, stress and internal-variable fields: DEP[0]=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', OPERATION='EXTR', RESULTAT=U[0], NOM_CHAM='DEPL', ...); SIG[0]=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', OPERATION='EXTR', RESULTAT=U[0], NOM_CHAM='SIEF_ELGA', ...); VAR[0]=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R', OPERATION='EXTR', RESULTAT=U[0], NOM_CHAM='VARI_ELGA', ...); 1.2.2.3 Step i : layers \mathit{E1}+\mathrm{...}+\mathit{Ei} At this stage, the analyses have already been carried out at steps 0 to i-1. We are in the Python loop "for i in range(1,n):" at index i: - Update of the mesh-cell group 'ELEM' of the mesh MA DEFI_GROUP(MAILLAGE=MA, CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='ELEM0',GROUP_MA='ELEM'),...) DEFI_GROUP(MAILLAGE=MA, DETR_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='ELEM'),...) DEFI_GROUP(MAILLAGE=MA, CREA_GROUP_MA=(_F(NOM='ELEM', OPTION='UNION', GROUP_MA=('ELEM0','E'+str(i+1)),),...) - Creation of the new model, assignment of the material and of the loading MOD[i]=AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=MA,AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA='ELEM',...) MAT[i]=AFFE_MATERIAU(MODELE=MOD[i], AFFE=_F(TOUT='OUI',MATE=...),...) CHA[i]=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MOD[i], ...) - Creation of the displacement, stress and internal-variable fields for the initial state of step i DEPBID=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', OPERATION='AFFE', MODELE=MOD[i], AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA='ELEM', NOM_CMP=('DX','DY','DZ',...), VALE=(1.0,1.0,1.0,...),),...) INIDEP=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', OPERATION='ASSE', MODELE=MOD[i], OPTION='DEPL', PROL_ZERO='OUI', ASSE=(_F(GROUP_MA='ELEM', CHAM_GD=DEPBID, CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R=0.0), _F(GROUP_MA='ELEM0', CHAM_GD=DEP[i-1], CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R=1.0,),),); SIEBID=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', OPERATION='AFFE', MODELE=MOD[i], AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA='ELEM', NOM_CMP=('SIXX','SIYY','SIZZ',...), VALE=(1.0,1.0,1.0,...),),...) INISIG=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', OPERATION='ASSE', MODELE=MOD[i], PROL_ZERO='OUI', ASSE=(_F(GROUP_MA=ELEM, CHAM_GD=SIEBID, CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R=0.0), _F(GROUP_MA='ELEM0', CHAM_GD=SIG[i-1], CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R=1.0,),),); CART = CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_NEUT_R', OPERATION='AFFE', MODELE=MOD[i], PROL_ZERO='OUI', AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA=ELEM, NOM_CMP =('X1','X2','X3', ...), VALE =(0.0,0.0,0.0,...),),) INIVAR=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R', OPERATION='ASSE', MODELE=MOD[i], PROL_ZERO='OUI', ASSE=(_F(GROUP_MA=ELEM, CHAM_GD=CART, NOM_CMP =('X1','X2','X3',...), NOM_CMP_RESU=('V1','V2','V3',...), CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R=0.0), _F(GROUP_MA=ELEM0, CHAM_GD=VAR[i-1], CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R=1.0),)) U[i]=STAT_NON_LINE(MODELE=MOD[i], CHAM_MATER=MAT[i], ETAT_INIT=_F(SIGM=INISIG,VARI=INIVAR,DEPL=INIDEP), EXCIT=_F(CHARGE=CHA[i]),...) DEP[i]=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', OPERATION='EXTR', RESULTAT=U[i], NOM_CHAM='DEPL',); SIG[i]=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', OPERATION='EXTR', RESULTAT=U[i], NOM_CHAM='SIEF_ELGA',); VAR[i]=CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R', OPERATION='EXTR', RESULTAT=U[i], NOM_CHAM='VARI_ELGA',); - Deletion of the concepts INIVAR,INIDEP,INISIG,CART DETRUIRE(CONCEPT=(_F(NOM=INIDEP), _F(NOM=INISIG), _F(NOM=INIVAR), _F(NOM=CART),),) 2 How to define an initial stress state (or of internal variables) with analytical formulae 2.1 Objective The objective is to be able to build two of the fields making up the initial state of a non-linear analysis: the stress field and the field of internal variables. In both cases, the solution consists in chaining a certain number of CREA_CHAMP commands. The reader is invited to consult the documentation U2.01.09 ("Analytical definition of an initial stress field and of an initial field of internal variables") which answers this problem explicitly. The reader may also look at the command file of the test case zzzz130a which illustrates this implementation. We present below a "concise" recipe for each of the cases. 2.2 Building an analytical stress field 2.2.1 Recipe - Defining the formulae: from the analytical expression of each stress, one builds the corresponding Aster concept by means of the operator FORMULE. Example: SIZZ = FORMULE (REEL='''(REEL:Z) = RHO G Z'''). (the formula thus defined depends on the variable Z (geometric coordinate)). - Creation of the field of formulae: one builds a neutral field (without a particular quantity) in order to associate, with each previously defined formula, a component of this field. Exemple : SIZF=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE',TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_NEUT_F', AFFE=_F(TOUT=(OUI','NOM_CMP'='X1',VALE_F=SIZZ),...); - Creation of the parameter field: We must have available a field whose components are among the variables of the formulae of the evaluation field. In this example, we must have available the geometry field (component Z) at the Gauss points. One proceeds in two steps: - extraction of the geometry field at the nodes: CHXN = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_GEOM_R',NOM_CHAM='GEOMETRIE',...) - transformation of the field at the nodes into a geometry field at the Gauss points: CHXG = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='DISC', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_GEOM_R',...) - Creation of the field by evaluation of the functions: One can now evaluate the field: one uses the operation EVAL: SIGZ2=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EVAL', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_NEUT_R', CHAM_F=SIZF, CHAM_PARA=CHXG, …) - Creation of the stress field: in order to obtain our analytical stress field, the quantity SIEF_R must be assigned to the evaluation field. SIGZ=CREA_CHAM(OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', ASSE=_F(CHAM_GD=SIGZ2, NOM_CMP='X1',NOM_CMP_RESU='SIZZ'),...). 2.2.2 Commands used | Commands | Functionality | | --- | --- | | FORMULE | Creation of the formulae | | CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='AFFE' | Creation of the field of formulae | | CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='EXTR' | Creation of the parameter field | | CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='EVAL' | Creation of the evaluation field | | CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='DISC' | Creation of the desired stress field after change of quantity | Table 2.1 2.3 Building a non-zero field of internal variables Two methods can be envisaged for creating a non-zero field of internal variables. 2.3.1 First method 2.3.1.1 Recipe This method requires knowledge of the number of internal variables of each constitutive law of your STAT_NON_LINE. Document U4.51.11 makes it possible to obtain this information. This method relies on the assignment of all the internal variables of the laws supplied to your STAT_NON_LINE. One uses the assignment operator AFFE of CREA_CHAMP for this purpose. This operation is carried out in two steps: - one first creates a NEUT_R map Example: VAIN = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE',,TYPE_CHAM='CART_NEUT_R', AFFE=(_F(GROUP_MA ='GM1', NOM_CMP=('X1','X2'),VALE=(0,,2,)), _F(GROUP_MA ='GM2', NOM_CMP=('X1','X2','X3',X4','X5'), VALE=(0,0,0,9,2,1)),...) - one transforms the NEUT_R map into a field at the Gauss points of VARI_R via the operation 'ASSE': VARI=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R', ASSE=(_F(CHAM_GD=VAIN, GROUP_MA='GM1',NOM_CMP=('X1','X2'), NOM_CMP_RESU=('V1','V2')) _F(CHAM_GD=VAIN, GROUP_MA='GM2', NOM_CMP=('X1','X2','X3','X4','X5'), NOM_CMP_RESU=('V1','V2','V3','V4','V5'),),), ...) The field of internal variables VARI contains 2 internal variables for the elements of the group \mathrm{GM1} and 5 for \mathrm{GM2} . Thus the constitutive law to be applied on the group \mathrm{GM1} of the model in the solution operator will have to comprise exactly 2 internal variables. 2.3.1.2 Commands used | Commands | Functionality | | --- | --- | | CREA_CHAMP/AFFE | Creation of a map in which all the components are assigned. | | CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='ASSE' | Transformation of the map into a field of internal variables. | 2.3.2 Second method 2.3.2.1 Recipe This method makes it possible to assign explicitly only the mesh cells which possess non-zero components. One proceeds as follows: - One carries out a first dummy analysis (in order to have available a posteriori a "model" field of internal variables): UBID=STAT_NON_LINE(COMPORTEMENT=(_F(GROUP_MA='GM1',RELATION=...), _F(GROUP_MA='GM2',RELATION=...),), …) - One extracts the field of internal variables VBID from the result UBID: VBID=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR',RESULTAT=UBID, TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R',NOM_CHAM='VARI_ELGA',...) - This time one assigns the non-zero values: VAIN1 = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE',,TYPE_CHAM='CART_NEUT_R', AFFE=(_F(GROUP_MA='GM1', NOM_CMP=('X2'),VALE=(2,)), _F(GROUP_MA ='GM2', NOM_CMP=('X3',X4','X5'),VALE=(9,2,1)),), ...) - One sets to zero the "model" field of internal variables and one overloads it with the non-zero values: VAIN2 = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE',TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R' ASSE=(_F(TOUT='OUI',CHAM_GD=VBID, CUMUL='OUI',COEF_R=0.), _F(GROUP_MA='GM1',CHAM_GD=VAIN1, CUMUL='OUI',COEF_R=1., NOM_CMP=('X2'),NOM_CMP_RESU=('V2'),), _F(GROUP_MA='GM2',CHAM_GD=VAIN1, CUMUL='OUI',COEF_R=1., NOM_CMP=('X3','X4','X5'), NOM_CMP_RESU=('V3','V4','V5'),),),...) 2.3.2.2 Commands used | Commands | Functionality | | --- | --- | | STAT_NON_LINE | Creation of a dummy result | | CREA_CHAMP/EXTR | Extraction of the field of internal variables. | | CREA_CHAMP/AFFE | Creation of a map in which only the non-zero components are assigned. | | CREA_CHAMP/ASSE | Transformation of the map into a field of internal variables in order to assemble it with the field extracted from the result (previously reset to zero). | 3 How to apply a pressure on a restricted part (not meshed exactly) of the boundary of a 3D structure It is possible with Code_Aster to assign a pressure field on a geometric zone of the part to be analysed which is not necessarily meshed. Indeed, it is enough to create the skin mesh supporting the pressure zone, to create on it a pressure field which one projects onto the mesh of the part. The data setup is then similar to the recovery / projection of a pressure field computed by a CFD code. In the example below, one wants to assign a pressure on a circular zone centred on a face of a cube, uniformly meshed with HEXA8. The mesh of the disc is produced separately. Note: One checks the value of the total force resultant by a computation of the integral of the pressure over the assigned zones. Indeed, the projection operation induces a loss (proportional to the coarseness of the mesh) which it is advisable to measure. We shall concern ourselves with the creation of the load CHA_PROJ. The various steps are the following: - reading of the mesh (disc) carrying the pressure force; - creation of the pressure field on the disc; - projection of the pressure field from the disc onto the structure being analysed; - creation of the load. We shall detail each of these steps. 3.1 Step 1: creation of the pressure field on the disc - Creation of a pressure field constant per element VAL =CREA_CHAMP( TYPE_CHAM = 'ELEM_PRES_R', OPERATION = 'AFFE', MODELE = modele2, PROL_ZERO = 'OUI', AFFE =_F( GROUP_MA = 'disque', NOM_CMP = 'PRES', VALE = 100000000. ), ...) - Creation of a result of type EVOL_CHAR from this field RES_PRES=CREA_RESU(OPERATION = 'AFFE', TYPE_RESU = 'EVOL_CHAR', NOM_CHAM = 'PRES', AFFE = _F(CHAM_GD = VAL , MODELE = modele2, INST = 0. ), ) 3.2 Step 2: projection of the pressure field from the disc onto the structure being analysed RES_PROJ=PROJ_CHAMP(METHODE='COLLOCATION', RESULTAT=RES_PRES, MODELE_1=modele2, MODELE_2=MODE, DISTANCE_MAX=1., CAS_FIGURE='2.5D', PROL_ZERO='OUI', VIS_A_VIS=_F(GROUP_MA_1='disque', GROUP_MA_2='Group_1',), TOUT_ORDRE='OUI',); 3.3 Step 3: creation of the load For the creation of the loading, one uses the loadings that evolve in time, of type evol_char, produced by LIRE_RESU U7.02.01 (or CREA_RESU), and containing pressure fields, volume force densities in 2D or 3D and surface force densities in 2D or 3D. CHA_PROJ=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MODE, EVOL_CHAR=RES_PROJ,) 3.4 Command file DEBUT() MAIL=LIRE_MAILLAGE(FORMAT='MED',); MAIL=MODI_MAILLAGE(reuse =MAIL, MAILLAGE=MAIL, ORIE_PEAU_3D=_F(GROUP_MA='Group_1',),) MAIL=DEFI_GROUP(reuse =MAIL, MAILLAGE=MAIL, CREA_GROUP_NO=_F(NOM='Group_3', GROUP_MA='Group_3' ) ) MA=DEFI_MATERIAU(ELAS=_F( E = 2.E11, NU = 0.3, ALPHA = 1.E-5, RHO=1. ), ECRO_LINE=_F( D_SIGM_EPSI = 2.E9, SY = 2.E8 ) ) MODE=AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=MAIL, AFFE=_F(TOUT='OUI', PHENOMENE='MECANIQUE', MODELISATION='3D',),); MATE=AFFE_MATERIAU(MAILLAGE=MAIL, AFFE=_F(TOUT='OUI', MATER=MA,),); ########################################## ##### création de la charge CHA_PROJ ##### ########################################## # lecture du maillage (disque) porteur de l effort de pression mail2=LIRE_MAILLAGE(UNITE=21, FORMAT='MED',); mail2=MODI_MAILLAGE(reuse =mail2, MAILLAGE=mail2, ORIE_PEAU_2D=_F(GROUP_MA='disque',),); modele2=AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=mail2, AFFE=_F(TOUT='OUI', PHENOMENE='MECANIQUE', MODELISATION='3D',),) # création du champ de pression sur le disque VAL =CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM='ELEM_PRES_R', OPERATION='AFFE', MODELE=modele2, PROL_ZERO='OUI', AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA = 'disque', NOM_CMP = 'PRES', VALE = 100000000. ), INFO=1,) RES_PRES=CREA_RESU(OPERATION = 'AFFE', TYPE_RESU = 'EVOL_CHAR', NOM_CHAM = 'PRES', AFFE = _F(CHAM_GD = VAL , MODELE = modele2, INST = 0. ), ) # calcul de la force de pression résultante sur le disque du premier maillage tab1=POST_ELEM(INTEGRALE = _F(GROUP_MA = 'disque', DEJA_INTEGRE = 'NON', NOM_CHAM = 'PRES', NOM_CMP = 'PRES' ), RESULTAT = RES_PRES , MODELE = modele2 ) IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=tab1) # projection du champ de pression depuis le disque vers la structure calculee RES_PROJ=PROJ_CHAMP(METHODE='COLLOCATION', RESULTAT=RES_PRES, MODELE_1=modele2, MODELE_2=MODE, DISTANCE_MAX=1., CAS_FIGURE='2.5D', PROL_ZERO='OUI', VIS_A_VIS=_F(GROUP_MA_1='disque', GROUP_MA_2='Group_1',), TOUT_ORDRE='OUI',); # calcul de la force de pression résultante après projection tab2=POST_ELEM(INTEGRALE = _F(GROUP_MA = 'Group_1', 'PRES', DEJA_INTEGRE = 'NON', NOM_CMP = 'PRES' ), RESULTAT = RES_PROJ , MODELE = MODE ) IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=tab2) # création de la charge CHA_PROJ=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MODE, EVOL_CHAR=RES_PROJ,) ################################################## ##### fin de creation de la charge CHA_PROJ ##### ################################################## BLOQ=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MODE, DDL_IMPO=_F(GROUP_MA='Group_3', DX=0.0, DY=0.0, DZ=0.0,),) RESU=MECA_STATIQUE(MODELE = MODE, CHAM_MATER = MATE, EXCIT=(_F(CHARGE=BLOQ,), _F(CHARGE=CHA_PROJ,),) ) RESU=CALC_CHAMP(reuse =RESU, FORCE='REAC_NODA', RESULTAT=RESU,) STANLEY() FIN() 4 How to compute the integral of the stresses or of a derived quantity on the boundary of a 3D structure 4.1 Objective The user has a stress field (at the Gauss points). He wishes to integrate each component on the boundary of his model or to compute a derived quantity such as an axial moment. | {\int}_{S}{\sigma}_{xx}\mathit{ds} {\int}_{S}{\sigma}_{xx}.y\mathit{ds} | | --- | The computation of the integral is done by the command POST_ELEM. When one wishes to integrate a quantity derived from a field, it must be defined (FORMULE) and evaluated (CREA_CHAMP) beforehand. The stresses at the Gauss points are not computed directly on the faces, so the user is faced with a few difficulties. A recipe has been established in order to be able to carry out this computation. It is presented below. For more details, one will consult the test case tplv07a which implements this recipe in a thermal setting in order to compute the outgoing flux on a boundary. 4.2 Recipe 4.2.1 Step 1: computation of the 3D stress field at the nodes First of all, the stress fields at the nodes must be computed. CALC_CHAMP(CONTRAINTE='SIGM_NOEU',RESULTAT=...,) The following step consists in building a neutral field whose values: - are located at the Gauss points of the mesh cells (2D and 3D), and - correspond to the values of the stresses. 4.2.2 Step 2: computation of a neutral field corresponding to the stresses It is assumed that the 3D model (MO3D) which was used to carry out the analysis contains, in addition to the "3D" elements, boundary elements (facets) on all its boundaries. 4.2.2.1 Case of the integration of an existing field 1. Extraction of the stress field at the nodes: SIGNO=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_SIEF_R', NOM_CHAM='SIEF_NOEU',RESULTAT=...,INST=...) 1. Transformation of the field SIGNO into a neutral field: NEUTNO=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_NEUT_R',MODELE=MO3D, PROL_ZERO='OUI',ASSE=_F(TOUT='OUI',CHAM_GD=SIGNO, NOM_CMP=('SIXX','SIYY','SIZZ'), NOM_CMP_RESU=('X1','X2','X3'),) 4.2.2.2 Case of the integration of a derived field (for example for the computation of an axial moment or of a thermal flux) When the quantity to be integrated does not exist directly, it must be built. The approach is then exactly the same as that described in § 2.2.1. One will begin by defining the integrand with the operator FORMULE, then a field of functions of type NEUT (CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='ASSE') and finally one will evaluate it (CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='EVAL'). One will also refer to the test case tplv07a for an example in thermal analysis. 4.2.3 Step 3: computation of the integral on the boundary It is enough to integrate the field NEUTNO on the boundary mesh cells. For example, for the face 'HAUT', the command is the following: INT=POST_ELEM(CHAM_GD=NEUTNO, MODELE=MOD3D, INTEGRALE=_F(GROUP_MA='HAUT', NOM_CMP=('X1','X2','X3'),),) 4.3 Commands used | Commands | Functionality | | --- | --- | | CALC_CHAMP | Creation of the stress fields at the nodes by element at the various time instants. | | CALC_CHAMP | Creation of the stress fields at the nodes at the various time instants. | | AFFE_MODELE | Creation of a 3D model. | | CREA_CHAMP/EXTR | Extraction of the stress field at the nodes at the time instant INST. | | (FORMULE) | Definition of the integrand where applicable. | | CREA_CHAMP/ASSE (CREA_CHAMP/AFFE) | Transformation of the stress field into a neutral field. Creation of a neutral field of functions. | | (CREA_CHAMP/EVAL) | Evaluation of the field of functions where applicable. | | POST_ELEM | Computation of the integral by specifying the mesh-cell groups of the face. | 5 How to read back a field constant per element and project it onto the nodes of the mesh 5.1 Objective The user has a field with 3 components, constant per element, in MED format. He wishes to be able to project it onto the nodes of another mesh. More precisely, one considers 2 meshes. The first is a mesh made up of surface mesh cells on which a field constant per mesh cell has been computed (coming, for example, from a fluid analysis). The second is a line mesh (representing, for example, a piping line onto which one wishes to project the field computed on the first mesh). The aim is therefore to read the field back on mesh 1 and to transfer it to the nodes of mesh 2. For the technique presented here to work, it is enough simply that the meshes be parallel to one another (for example, they must both lie along the z axis) and that they have a range of coordinates in common along the axis along which they are parallel. 5.2 Method 5.2.1 Reading back the MED file The reading back is done in two steps: 1. Reading back of mesh 1: - MAIL1 = LIRE_MAILLAGE(FORMAT = 'MED',); - Reading back of the field with LIRE_CHAMP. Indeed, it is LIRE_CHAMP which most simply makes it possible to read back fields that are constant per element, via the production of the map (in the sense of Code_Aster ). The field to be read back is called here 'ForceLineique'; one stores it in a map with 3 components of error-indicator type (this last point is incidental, because one uses it only as a container): CH1=LIRE_CHAMP(FORMAT = 'MED', MAILLAGE = MAIL1, UNITE = 20, NOM_MED = 'ForceLineique', INST = 0.0001, TYPE_CHAM = 'CART_ERRE_R', NOM_CMP = ('ERREST','NUEST','SIGCAL',), NOM_CMP_MED = ('FX','FY','FZ',),); 5.2.2 Creation of the result and projection of the field In order to be able to project the field by means of PROJ_CHAMP, it must first be stored in a result data structure by using the command CREA_RESU: 1. Creation of the result: EVOL1=CREA_RESU(OPERATION = 'AFFE', TYPE_RESU = 'EVOL_NOLI', NOM_CHAM = 'ERME_ELEM', AFFE = (_F(CHAM_GD = CH1, INST = 0.0001,),),); 1. Projection: EVOL2=PROJ_CHAMP(RESULTAT = EVOL1, NOM_CHAM = 'ERME_ELEM', MODELE_1 = MO1, MODELE_2 = MO2, TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU',); where MO1 and MO2 are models resting respectively on mesh 1 and on mesh 2 (the reading back of which is not set out here). These models must be consistent with one another and, of course, with the subsequent use that one wishes to make of the field. Consequently, their creation is not part of this explanation, because it depends on the application sought. In the end, one now obtains a new result data structure containing a nodal field defined on mesh 2. A last (optional) step consists in modifying the name and the type of the field in order to obtain a true nodal field. In what follows, this is what one will seek to obtain by converting the error field obtained into a displacement field (nodal field with 3 components). 5.2.3 Modification of the type of the field The last step breaks down into two sub-steps: 1. Extraction of the field: CHTMP1 = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION = 'EXTR', NOM_CHAM = 'ERME_ELEM', TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_ERRE_R', RESULTAT = EVOL2, INST = 0.0001,); 1. Conversion of the field: CHNOFIN = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION = 'ASSE', TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_DEPL_R', MODELE = MO2, ASSE = (_F(CHAM_GD = CHTMP1, COEF_R = 1.0, TOUT = 'OUI', NOM_CMP = ('ERREST', 'NUEST', 'SIGCAL'), NOM_CMP_RESU = ('DX', 'DY', 'DZ'),),),); 6 How to use the value of the computed eigenfrequencies to evaluate the damping One wishes to interpolate a damping function F(\mathit{FREQ})=\text{f\_amor} on the eigenfrequencies of a model. The eigenfrequencies and eigenmodes are obtained by CALC_MODES. modes = CALC_MODES(…) One extracts only the list of the computed frequencies by doing the following (one obtains a table made up of a column with the order numbers and a column with the frequencies): tab = RECU_TABLE(RESU=modes, NOM_PARA='FREQ') The trick consists in creating an identity function on the list of frequencies G(\mathit{FREQ})=\mathit{FREQ} by recovering the values from the table: g_freq = RECU_FONCTION(TABLE=tab, PARA_X='FREQ', PARA_Y='FREQ') The damping evaluated on the eigenfrequencies is therefore f_amor = F(G(FREQ)), that is: amor = CALC_FONCTION(COMPOSE=_F(FONC_PARA=g_freq, FONC_RESU=f_amor)) This example is available in sdld22a.com1.

u2.02.01 User's guide for the plate, shell, grid and membrane elements u2.02.01 User's guide for the plate, shell, grid and membrane elements > Summary. This document is a user's guide for the plate, shell, grid and membrane modellings. Shell and plate elements are used in the numerical modelling of thin structures with a middle surface that is plane (plate modelling) or curved (shell modelling). Grid modellings are used for the numerical modelling of reinforcement and prestressing cables in reinforced-concrete structures. Membrane modelling makes it possible to model thin structures whose bending stiffness is negligible. Mechanics : The DKT models are the most complete, because, for thin or slightly thick structures ( h/L {10}^{6.}h/L ) one approaches the LOVE-KIRCHHOFF theory. In practice it is recommended not to change this coefficient. Indeed, these elements provide a physically correct solution, whether the shell is thick or thin, with the coefficient k=5/6 . All the shell elements present in Code_Aster are protected against shear locking, like the plate elements (see § 2.1.3.2 ). Selective integration is used for this purpose R3.07.03. However, this property is lost if a displacement field is projected onto a shell element from an analysis on a plate element (with the PROJ_CHAMP command). One should not be surprised by the shear stresses subsequently obtained by a linear analysis from the displacements (for small thicknesses). 2.2 Commands to use 2.2.1 Spatial discretisation and assignment of a modelling: operator AFFE_MODELE In this part, the choice and the assignment of a plate or shell modelling are described, together with the associated degrees of freedom and mesh cells. Most of the information described is taken from the user's guides for the modellings (U3.12.01: DKT - DST - Q4G modelling, U3.12.02: COQUE_AXIS modellings). 2.2.1.1 Degrees of freedom The The local frame is built either using the two "nautical" angles \alpha and \beta (supplied in degrees), which define a vector v whose projection onto the plane tangent to the shell fixes the direction {x}_{l} . or, if the VECTEUR keyword is present, by the 3 components of the vector v One may define a single vector V for the whole structure, or one per zone (keywords GROUP_MA / MAILLE). The construction of the local frame is defined in AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01. This local frame will be called the user frame hereafter. The definition of this reference axis is also useful for defining the orientation of the fibres of a multilayer or orthotropic shell (see the DEFI_COMPOSITE operator U4.42.03). - The number of layers COQUE_NCOU used for the integration through the thickness of the shell, in the STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE operators (DKT, COQUE_3D, COQUE_AXIS modellings). - A feature of DEFI_GROUP makes it possible to create automatically a mesh-cell group whose normal lies within a given solid angle, of axis the reference direction. This command can be used in pre-processing to assign non-isotropic material data, or in post-processing after a shell analysis. - The offset (constant for all the nodes of the mesh cell) EXCENTREMENT of each of them relative to the support mesh cell. This distance is measured along the normal to the support mesh cell. In the offset case, the rotary inertias are necessarily taken into account and INER_ROTA is set to OUI. - COEF_RIGI_DRZ defines a fictitious stiffness coefficient (necessarily small) on the degree of freedom of rotation about the normal to the shell. It is necessary in order to prevent the stiffness matrix from being singular, but it must be chosen as small as possible. For the DKT, if one chooses COEF_RIGI_DRZ negative, one reinforces, by a variational statement, the rotation kinematics of the plate element about its normal. A value of {10}^{-8} is recommended. Figure 2.2.2-a: Global frame and tangent plane For the GRILLE_EXCENTRE and GRILLE_MEMBRANE modellings, The following geometric data are necessary to model the reinforcement layer: - SECTION= {S}_{1} : section of the reinforcement in direction 1. The section is given per linear metre. It therefore corresponds to the cumulative section over a width of 1 metre. If there is a section s every \mathrm{20.0cm} , the cumulative section is \mathrm{5.s} . - The orientation of the reinforcement is defined either by - ANGL_REP, to define a vector projected onto the element - or, in the case of a cylindrical shell, by ORIG_AXE, AXE to define the angle of the reinforcement, constant in a cylindrical frame. - The offset (constant for all the nodes of the mesh cell) of the reinforcement layer relative to the support mesh cell (distance measured along the normal to the support mesh cell), (GRILLE_EXCENTRE modelling only). To define a grid, or if the reinforcement section in the longitudinal direction and in the transverse direction are different, two layers of elements must be created (command crea_maillage, keyword crea_group_ma), one layer of elements for the longitudinal direction and a second layer of elements for the transverse direction: For the MEMBRANE modelling in linear analysis, only the orientation of the constitutive behaviour of the membrane is necessary. It is defined either by: - ANGL_REP, to define a vector projected onto the element - in the case of a cylindrical shell, by ORIG_AXE, to define the angle of the reinforcement, constant in a cylindrical frame. > If the MEMBRANE modelling is used in non-linear analysis, the following must then be supplied: - EPAIS, the thickness of the membrane. - ANGL_REP, the frame in which the stresses are expressed (only an isotropic constitutive behaviour is possible). - N_INIT, an initial pretension, of dimension force per unit length, which disappears after the Newton iterations of the first time step. This pretension is useful only for the convergence of the first time step. Important note: The direction of the normals to each element is a recurrent problem concerning the use of this type of element, for example when pressure-type loadings are applied, or when defining an offset or a local frame. By default, for the surface elements, the orientation is given by the vector product 12^13 for a triangle numbered 123 (DKT, ...) or 1234567 (COQUE_3D), and 12^14 for a quadrangle numbered 1234 (DKQ, ...) or 123456789 (COQUE_3D). For the line shells, n is given by the formula of paragraph Error: Reference source not found, with t oriented in the traversal direction of the mesh cell in the mesh. In general, these data are accessible by looking in the mesh file, which is not very practical for the user. Furthermore, the user must check the consistency of the mesh and make sure that all the mesh cells do indeed have the same orientation. The user can modify automatically the orientation of the elements of the mesh by imposing a normal direction, for a mesh or a part of a mesh using shell modellings, and whatever the type of modelling. The reorientation of the elements is done by means of the ORIE_NORM_COQU operator of the MODI_MAILLAGE command U4.12.05. The principle is as follows: under ORIE_NORM_COQU one defines a direction by means of a vector and a node belonging to the mesh-cell group to be reoriented. If the vector introduced is not in the plane of the mesh cell selected by MODI_MAILLAGE, a normal direction is deduced automatically, obtained as the given vector minus its projection onto the plane of the mesh cell. All the mesh cells of the group connected to the one initially selected will then automatically have the same normal orientation. Furthermore, an automatic check of the same orientation of the connected mesh cells is carried out by means of the VERI_NORM operator of the AFFE_CHAR_MECA command U4.25.01. 2.2.3 Materials: DEFI_MATERIAU The definition of the constitutive behaviour of a material is carried out using the DEFI_MATERIAU operator U4.43.01. | DEFI_MATERIAU | COQUE_3D | DKT, DST, Q4G | DKTG, Q4GG | COQUE_AXIS | GRILLE_EXCENTRE, GRILLE_MEMBRANE | MEMBRANE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | LINEAR ELASTICITY | | | | | | | | ELAS | | | | | | | | ELAS_ORTH ELAS_ISTR | | | | | | | | ELAS_COQUE | | | | | | | | ELAS_MEMBRANE | | | | | | | | DEFI_MATERIAU | COQUE_3D | DKT | DST Q4G | DKTG | Q4GG | COQUE_AXIS | GRILLE_EXCENTRE GRILLE_MEMBRANE | MEMBRANE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | PER LAYER | | | | | | | | | | constitutive behaviours available in C_PLAN | | | | | | | | | | constitutive behaviours available in 1D | | | | | | | | | | GLRC_DAMAGE | | | | | | | | | | GLRC_DM, KIT_DDI | | | | | | | | | The MEMBRANE in linear analysis is used with ELAS_MEMBRANE and in non-linear analysis with ELAS. The connections available with the plate and shell elements are the following: - Beam–shell connection: this consists in establishing the link between an end node of a beam element and a group of edge mesh cells of shell elements. Beam and plate theories only know of cuts normal to the fibre or to the middle surface. The connections can take place only along these fibres or middle surfaces. The beam–shell connection is feasible for beams whose neutral fibre is orthogonal to the normals to the facets of the plates or of the shells. Extending it to other configurations (a beam arriving perpendicular to the plane of a plate, for example) requires a feasibility study, because the plate or shell elements have no stiffness associated with a rotation in the plane perpendicular to the normal to the middle surface. The connection is usable by using the keyword LIAISON_ELEM: (OPTION: ‘COQ_POU’) of AFFE_CHAR_MECA. - Shell–pipe connection: this consists in establishing the link between an end node of a pipe element and a group of edge mesh cells of shell elements. The formulation of the shell–pipe connection is presented in the reference document R3.08.06. Pipe and plate theories only know of cuts normal to the fibre or to the middle surface. The connections can take place only along these fibres or middle surfaces. The shell–pipe connection is feasible for pipes whose neutral fibre is orthogonal to the normals to the facets of the plates or of the shells. The connection is usable by using the keyword LIAISON_ELEM: (OPTION: ‘COQ_TUYAU’) of AFFE_CHAR_MECA. Figure 2.2.4.5-a: Shell connections with other mechanical elements - Shell – solid 3D connection: the shell–3D solid connection is under study, but it will be limited at first to the cases where the normal to the solid is orthogonal to the normal to one of the facets of the plate or shell element (see [bib4]). - Connection between shell elements : to connect two shell elements to one another, one uses the LIAISON_COQUE keyword of AFFE_CHAR_MECA(_F) (documentation U4.44.01). This connection is made by means of linear relations. The classical approach assumes that 2 planes meshed with shells intersect along a straight line that belongs to the mesh of the structure. In order to avoid the volume that is the intersection of the two shells being counted twice, one stops the mesh of a shell perpendicular to a given shell at the level of the upper or lower skin of the latter. In [Figure 2.2.4.5-b], the link between the 2 shells is made by rigid-body links between the facing nodes of the segments {A}_{1}{A}_{2} and {B}_{1}{B}_{2} . Figure 2.2.4.5-b: Connection between shell elements Test cases making it possible to validate these connections are available in the examples section. 2.2.4.6 Command variables The command variables taken into account by the various modellings are listed here: | Command variables | COQUE_3D | DKT, DST, Q4G | DKTG | Q4GG | COQUE_AXIS | GRILLE_MEMBRANE GRILLE_EXCENTRE MEMBRANE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TEMP | | | | | | | | others: SECH, HYDR, etc. | | | | | | | 2.3 Solution 2.3.1 Linear analyses: MECA_STATIQUE and the other linear operators Linear analyses are carried out in small strains. The 3D constitutive behaviours can also be used by means of the De Borst method R5.03.09. When plate-type or shell elements become coplanar, the stiffness problem about the normal should be kept under control. Indeed, by construction, these elements have no stiffness in this direction: DRZ is a fictitious degree of freedom which avoids the singularity of the DKT matrices in the global frame. The COEF_RIGI_DRZ coefficient in the AFFE_CARA_ELEM operator makes it possible to modify this value. The default value is sufficient in most cases, but, in certain situations such as: - thin plate elements used with a large thickness (DKT, for example); - a non-linear analysis (STAT_NON_LINE or DYNA_NON_LINE); - DKT-type elements on warped quadrangles in general; - COQUE_3D with large-transformation kinematics; - a plate subjected to a rotation about its normal. Advice for the DKT on COEF_RIGI_DRZ: a poor value penalises the convergence of the analyses. The result, if it has converged, remains correct , but the rate of convergence is reduced. For example, a linear elastic analysis requires more than one Newton iteration to converge. The value of COEF_RIGI_DRZ must then be changed and reduced. Nevertheless, care is needed in the choice of this coefficient, because a value that is too small can make the matrix singular. It is also possible to enrich the DKT models by taking the stiffness along DRZ into account. To do this, it is enough to take COEF_RIGI_DRZ negative. In this latter case, one notes that one does not quite have a DKT model as it is formulated in the literature, but a DKT model enriched by a kinematics in DRZ: DRZ becomes a physical degree of freedom. Advice for COQUE_3D: conversely, for COQUE_3D, it is better to favour an ever larger COEF_RIGI_DRZ in order to avoid singular matrices. The RESULTAT concept of STAT_NON_LINE/DYNA_NON_LINE contains displacement, stress and internal-variable fields at the integration points, always computed at the Gauss points: - DEPL: displacement fields. - SIEF_ELGA: stress tensor per element at the integration points (COQUE_3D and DKT) in the user frame. For each layer, one stores through the thickness, and for each thickness at the surface integration points. Thus, if one wants information on a stress for layer NC, at level NCN (NCN = -1 if lower, NCN = 0 if middle, NCN = +1 if upper) for the surface integration point NG, one must look at the value given by the point defined in the POINT option such that: NP = 3 (NC-1) NPG+(NCN+1) NPG+NG where NPG is the total number of surface integration points of the COQUE_3D element (7 for the triangle and 9 for the quadrangle) and of the DKT element. For the GRILLE_EXCENTRE and GRILLE_MEMBRANE modellings, one simply stores one value per integration point: the SIXX component in the direction of the reinforcement. For the DKTG and Q4GG modellings, SIEF_ELGA contains the 6 generalised forces (membrane forces, bending moments, shear forces) per Gauss point. In the general case, SIEF_ELGA is a Cauchy stress field, but for COQUE_3D it is a stress field of the second Piola-Kirchoff type. - VARI_ELGA: field of internal variables (DKT and COQUE_3D) per element at the surface integration points. For each surface integration point, the information on the layers is stored starting with the first, level ‘INF’. The number of variables represented is therefore 2 NCOU NBVARI, where NBVARI represents the number of internal variables. It can be enriched with the following fields, computed in post-processing by the CALC_CHAMP operator: - EFGE_ELNO: activates the computation of the tensor of generalised forces per element at the nodes (membrane forces, bending moments, shear forces), in the user frame (defined in paragraph [§2.2.2]). - VARI_ELNO: activates the computation of the internal-variable field per element at the nodes through the thickness (by layer SUP/MOY/INF through the thickness, unless otherwise stated). 2.3.2.2 Detail on the integration points The numbering of the surface Gauss points for the COQUE_3D elements is given in R3.07.04 §4.7.1. Take care with the order of the Gauss points for the 9-point formula, which is not the same as that adopted for the isoparametric elements. For the DKT, COQUE_3D and COQUE_AXIS modellings, in the case of non-linear analyses, the integration method for the plate and shell elements is an integration method by layers , the number of which is defined by the user. For each layer, except for the GRILLE modelling, a three-point Simpson method is used, at the middle of the layer and on the upper and lower skins of the layer. For N layers, the number of integration points through the thickness is \mathrm{2N}+1 . To treat the material non-linearities, it is recommended to use 3 to 5 layers through the thickness, for a number of integration points equal to 7, 9 and 11 respectively. For the tangent stiffness, one computes for each layer, in plane stress, the contribution to the membrane, bending and membrane–bending coupling stiffness matrices. These contributions are added and assembled to obtain the total tangent stiffness matrix. For each layer, one computes the stress state and the set of internal variables, at the middle of the layer and on the upper and lower skins of the layer. This information is available in VARI_ELGA and SIEF_ELGA. In post-processing one can access the transverse shear stress and strain values obtained from the derivative of the moments. To do this, even in non-linear analysis, an elastic relation is assumed for the transverse constitutive behaviour. For the GRILLE_EXCENTRE and GRILLE_MEMBRANE modellings of reinforced-concrete structures, there is only one integration point per layer. 2.3.2.3 Geometric non-linear behaviour The geometrically non-linear analyses (large displacements and large rotations), available with the COQUE_3D modelling, are carried out using the STAT_NON_LINE operator, using, under the COMPORTEMENT keyword, DEFORMATION = 'GROT_GDEP'. The geometrically non-linear analyses (large displacements and large rotations), available with the MEMBRANE modelling, are carried out using the STAT_NON_LINE operator, using, under the COMPORTEMENT keyword, DEFORMATION = 'GROT_GDEP'. The geometrically non-linear analyses (large displacements and small strains), available with the exce modelling, are carried out using the STAT_NON_LINE operator, using, under the COMPORTEMENT keyword, DEFORMATION = 'GROT_GDEP'. It is possible to apply follower pressures on the COQUE_3D elements. This loading has the particular feature of following the geometry of the structure during its deformation (for example: the hydrostatic pressure always remains perpendicular to the deformed geometry). To take this type of loading into account, the following information must be specified in the STAT_NON_LINE operator: STAT_NON_LINE ( EXCIT =_F( CHARGE = pres TYPE_CHARGE = 'SUIV' ) ) The geometric non-linear behaviour of structures may present instabilities (buckling, snap‑through/snap-back...). The determination and the crossing of these limit points cannot be obtained by imposing the loading; however, the load-control options ‘DDL_IMPO’ or ‘LONG_ARC’ of the STAT_NON_LINE operator make it possible to pass these critical points. The use of the MEMBRANE element in geometrically non-linear analysis can be delicate because of the strong non-linearities and of its lack of bending stiffness. The following points should be borne in mind: - Use of the pretension: the use of an initial pretension via N_INIT in the AFFE_CARA_ELEM operator U4.42.01 is a particular feature of structural elements with no resistance to bending; it is found in code_aster for the cable elements. Indeed, a membrane subjected to a force perpendicular to its initial surface, as is the case with a pressure, undergoes a rigid-body motion, which causes the analysis to stop. One way of getting round this problem is to create an initial stiffness, called "geometric", in order to allow the convergence of the first increment. It is then normal for the convergence time of this first time step to be rather long, so one should not hesitate to allow a high number of Newton iterations (>100) and to adjust the value of the initial tension N_INIT. The pretension is a generalised force and is written in the form {N}_{\mathit{init}}={h\sigma }_{0} with h the thickness and {\sigma}_{0} the prestress; it is recommended to start by taking a small prestress value (for example 1.E-3 ) and then to increase this value by multiplying it by 10 until convergence is obtained. It is moreover preferable to take h and as independent parameters and then to enter {h\sigma }_{0} as the argument under the N_INIT keyword. The value {\sigma}_{0} is sometimes difficult to find, but it is useful only for the first time step, so it can be tested quickly. - Initial force and stiffness: the very strong non-linearity of the element implies that convergence may be poor when the applied force is too small relative to the stiffness of the material. This ratio is difficult to quantify, but the user should not hesitate to set a high force at the first time step, even if this means activating time-step splitting via the DEFI_LIST_INST command. This remark is particularly true when a pressure is applied. - Line search (and contact): one way of improving convergence noticeably is to activate the line search (keyword RECH_LINEAIRE in the STAT_NON_LINE command U4.51.03). This is sometimes indispensable for the convergence of the analyses, in particular during the first time steps. The line search is unfortunately not compatible with contact problems in code_aster; this may lead one to have to split the problems into two parts: a first part without contact, with the line search, and a second part with the contact only. - Load control: if, after varying the value of the initial tension and the value of the initial force, one cannot make the analysis converge at the first increment, it is also possible to use load control (keyword PILOTAGE in STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03). Load control is also incompatible with contact. 2.3.2.4 Linear buckling Linear buckling analyses are similar to the search for natural frequencies and vibration modes. The problem to be solved is expressed in the form: Find (\lambda ,X)\in (\mathrm{ℝ},{\mathrm{ℝ}}^{N}) such that \mathit{AX}=\lambda \mathit{BX} | where | A | is the stiffness matrix | | --- | --- | --- | | | B | is the geometric stiffness matrix (computed with the RIGI_GEOM option of CALC_MATR_ELEM), available for the DKT, DKTG and COQUE_3D modellings | | | \lambda | is the critical load | | | X | is the buckling mode associated with the critical load | The CALC_MODES operator [U4.52.02] is used to determine the critical load and the associated buckling mode. 2.4 Additional computations and post-processings 2.4.1 Computations of elementary matrices: operator CALC_MATR_ELEM The CALC_MATR_ELEM operator (documentation U4.61.01) makes it possible to compute elementary matrices, which can then be assembled by the ASSE_MATRICE command (documentation U4.61.22). These elements are plate elements, or line elements in the case of structures of revolution or of structures invariant along an axis. The curvature of the structure is not taken into account in itself. The metric of the tangent plane of each element is computed assuming that all the vertices are coplanar. These elements assume an a priori parabolic distribution of temperature through the thickness, which results from an asymptotic expansion in linear thermal analysis for a small shell thickness, when the temperature variations are not too large. It should be noted that a model based on a richer expansion of the temperature field through the thickness sees its terms of order higher than two converge towards zero when the shell is thin. One therefore cannot treat thermal-shock problems with a strong variation of the temperature profile through the thickness with these shells. The instructions for use of these elements are presented in U1.22.01. 3.1 Definition of the problem 3.1.1 Spatial discretisation and assignment of a modelling: operator AFFE_MODELE 3.1.1.1 Degrees of freedom The degrees of freedom are the temperatures TEMP_MIL (temperature on the middle surface of the shell), TEMP_INF (temperature on the lower surface of the shell) and TEMP_SUP (temperature on the upper surface of the shell). 3.1.1.2 Support mesh cells of the stiffness matrices | Modelling | Mesh cell | Nature of the mesh cell | Finite element | Remarks | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE | QUAD9 QUAD8 QUAD4 TRIA7 TRIA6 TRIA3 | plane plane plane plane plane plane | THCOQU9 THCOQU8 THCOQU4 THCOTR7 THCOTR6 THCOTR3 | nodes with 3 coordinates x, y, z | | COQUE_PLAN | SEG3 | not assumed plane | THCPSE3 | nodes with 2 coordinates x, y | | COQUE_AXIS | SEG3 | not assumed plane | THCASE3 | nodes with 2 coordinates x, y | For the THCOTRi, only the three vertices are used to define the local geometry (tangent plane, normal). For the chaining of analyses with curved mechanical elements, it is therefore necessary that the geometry of the plate not be too far from that of the shell. When the structure is curved, the thermal analysis must therefore be meshed sufficiently finely in order to have correct results in anticipation of the mechanical part. Only the line thermal elements are perfectly associated with the corresponding line elements in mechanics, because they take into account the curvature of the meshed structure. - Chaining with multilayer materials is not available at present. - Thermo-mechanical chaining is also possible if one knows, analytically or from experimental measurements, the variation of the temperature field through the thickness of the structure or of certain parts of the structure. In this case one works with a temperature map defined a priori; the temperature field is no longer given by the three values TEMP_INF, TEMP_MIL and TEMP_SUP of the thermal analysis obtained by EVOL_THER. The DEFI_NAPPE operator makes it possible to create such temperature profiles from the data supplied by the user. These profiles are assigned by the CREA_CHAMP and CREA_RESU commands (see test case hsns100b). It will be noted that it is not necessary, for the mechanical analysis, that the number of integration points through the thickness be equal to the number of discretisation points of the temperature field through the thickness. The temperature field is automatically interpolated at the integration points through the thickness of the plate or shell elements. - The thermal evolution that can be associated with the material field by AFFE_MATERIAU/AFFE_VARC must be ready to be used by the finite elements of the mechanical model. A problem arises for shell-type or pipe elements, which use a temperature varying through the thickness on the different layers. For these elements, it is necessary to prepare the computation of the temperature on the layers upstream of the AFFE_MATERIAU command. To do this, the user must use the CREA_RESU command with the PREP_VARC operation (PREparation of the Command VaRiables") which makes it possible to compute the temperature in the layers of a shell, starting either from a temperature defined by a map of functions or from a temperature computed by Code_Aster with a shell model (TEMP_MIL/TEMP_INF/TEMP_SUP) . | HPLA100 The aim is to study a thermal expansion phenomenon in which the temperature fields are computed with THER_LINEAIRE by a steady-state analysis: thermal expansion: T(\rho )-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho )=0.5({T}_{s}+{T}_{i})+2.({T}_{s}+\mathrm{Ti})(r-R)/h with: {T}_{s}=0.5°C,{T}_{i}=-0.5°C,{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}=0°C {T}_{s}=0.1°C,{T}_{i}=0.1°C,{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}=0°C The stresses, the forces and the bending moments are tested at L and M . The reference results are analytical. For the COQUE_3D modellings one takes into account the metric variation with the thickness of the shell. Figure 5-a: Fields of use of plates and shells A few recommendations concerning the field of use of these elements: - Thin structures : for these structures, whose h/L ratio is less than 1/20, the transverse shear effects can be neglected and Kirchhoff theory applies. It is recommended to use, for this type of structure, DKT-DKQ plate elements or curved shell elements (COQUE_3D, _AXIS). It is recommended to use preferably the DKT and DKQ elements , which give very good results on the displacements and more approximate results on the stresses (to be recommended for vibration analyses). Even if a large number of these elements must be used, the execution times remain reasonable compared with those of the curved elements. It is recommended not to exceed a ratio h/L=1/500 in order to avoid problems linked to numerical locking. - Thick structures: for these structures, one will use DST, DSQ and Q4G plate elements, which take transverse shear into account with a shear correction factor k=5/6 (Reissner theory), or preferably curved shell elements . The shear correction factor makes it possible to pass from a Hencky-Mindlin-Naghdi theory for k=1 , to a Reissner theory for k=5/6 . The shear coefficient is adjustable only for the curved shell elements, but it is recommended not to modify its default value. When the Q4G modelling has been preferred, a small mesh-sensitivity study must be carried out . The tests show, indeed, that this modelling requires a mesh that is sufficiently fine in the directions loaded in bending in order to obtain small errors. The DKT, DKQ, DST, DSQ and Q4G elements are plane elements; they do not take the curvature of the structures into account, so it is necessary to refine the mesh where the curvature is significant if one wants to avoid spurious bending. The variation of the metric of the geometry (that is, its radius of curvature) as a function of its thickness is taken into account: - automatically for the COQUE_3D modelling. - defined by the user for the COQUE_AXIS modelling. The optimal mechanical element in statics, according to all the test cases of paragraph [§2.5], is the 9-node shell element MEC3QU9H , which makes it possible to obtain good displacements and good stresses thanks to its P2 interpolation in membrane. It is a versatile element which can be used both to represent very thin structures ( h/L\le 1/100 ) and thicker ones. As, moreover, the 7-node shell element MEC3TR7H is less efficient , the user is advised to mesh the shell structure with as many quadrangles as possible . - Material non-linearity: the non-linear constitutive behaviours (plasticity, etc.) in plane stress are available for the curved shell elements (COQUE_3D, COQUE_AXIS) and the DKT-DKQ plate elements only. The plastic constitutive behaviour does not include the transverse shear terms, which are treated elastically, because the transverse shear is decoupled from the plastic constitutive behaviour. For a good representation of the progression of plasticity through the thickness, it is recommended to use, for the numerical integration, 3 to 5 layers through the thickness, for a number of Gauss points equal to 3, 5 and 11 respectively. - Geometric non-linearity : the geometric non-linearities (large displacements, large rotations) in plane stress are available for the curved shell elements COQUE_3D only. - Euler buckling : this type of analysis is available with the curved shell elements COQUE_3D and the plate elements DKT and DKTG. Elements corresponding to the mechanical elements exist in thermal analysis; the thermo-mechanical couplings are therefore available both for the plate elements and for the shell elements. At present these couplings are not possible for multilayer materials. 6 Bibliography 1. J.L. Batoz, G. Dhatt "Modelling of structures by finite elements: beams and plates" Hermès, Paris (1990). 2.
