u2.02.02 User's guide for the TUYAU_* elements u2.02.02 User's guide for the TUYAU_ elements Summary: This document is a user's guide for the TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M modellings. The TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M finite elements correspond to line elements for straight or curved piping. The kinematics of the TUYAU elements combines both a beam kinematics, which describes the overall motion of the piping line, and a shell kinematics, which provides the description of the swelling, of the ovalisation and of the warping of the cross-section. These modellings can be used for problems of relatively thick three-dimensional piping, in linear or non-linear mechanical analysis and in small displacements. 1 Introduction The TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M finite elements correspond to line elements for straight or curved piping. They rely on a Timoshenko beam kinematics for the displacements and the rotations of the mean fibre and on a shell kinematics for the strains of the cross-section (ovalisation, warping, swelling). These transverse strains are decomposed into Fourier series. The TUYAU_3M modelling takes into account 3 modes at most, whereas the TUYAU_6M modelling takes into account 6 Fourier modes. These modellings can be used for problems of relatively thick three-dimensional piping, only in linear or non-linear mechanical analysis and in small displacements. At present, no thermal or acoustic analysis is possible. This document presents the capabilities of the TUYAU modelling available since version 6 of Code_Aster . The capabilities of this type of modelling are presented first; the formulation of the finite elements and their differences with respect to the beam modellings are then briefly recalled. The list of the options available for each of the elements is also given. The document ends with the presentation of a few academic test cases and, finally, with a few recommendations for use. The straight or curved pipe elements are grouped under the modellings TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M. The computation options are defined in this document. The present capabilities of these pipe elements are the following: | straight or curved piping lines, | | --- | | line element with 3 nodes (SEG3) or with 4 nodes (SEG4), | | relatively thick pipe: e/R One can use the operator MODI_MAILLAGE to build SEG4 mesh cells from SEG3 mesh cells. Note: > The TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M elements are under-integrated in stiffness. The full integration of the stiffness matrices raised problems in the computation of the internal forces (non-physical oscillations), in particular for the shear forces. > The TUYAU_3M elements on the SEG4 support mesh cells are also under-integrated in mass. Full integration can cause the appearance of non-physical eigenmodes on the degrees of freedom not associated with a beam kinematics. 3.1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings All the loadings applicable to the elements used are treated by direct discretisation on the support mesh cell of the element in a displacement formulation. The pressure and the other line forces, as well as gravity, are examples of loadings applied directly on the element. No special loading mesh cell is therefore necessary. 3.1.4 Model: AFFE_MODELE The assignment of the modelling is carried out by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01. It is recalled that only the mechanical phenomenon is available with the TUYAU element. | AFFE_MODELE | | TUYAU_3M TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AFFE | | | | | PHENOMENE | 'MECANIQUE' | | | | MODELISATION | 'TUYAU_3M' | | | | MODELISATION | 'TUYAU_6M' | | | Regarding the choice of the TUYAU modelling, it can be noted that the use of a Fourier-series decomposition to order 6 (TUYAU_6M element) improves the approximation of the behaviour of the cross-section in the presence of local modes, in the case where the latter deforms according to a high-order mode, for example in the case of thin tubes where the ratio of the thickness to the radius of the cross-section is The option MODI_METRIQUE='OUI' has been deactivated following the observation of incorrect results when it was used. For the moment, only the option MODI_METRIQUE='NON' is allowed. 3.2.2 Generatrix and notion of local frame: keyword ORIENTATION The generatrix drawn all along the piping makes it possible to define the origin of the angles \Phi [Figure]. This is used: - to interpret the ovalisation degrees of freedom; Figure 3.2.2-a: Representation of two non-coplanar elbows connected by a straight pipe. For an end cross-section of the piping line [Figure], the user defines in AFFE_CARA_ELEM under the keyword ORIENTATION a vector whose projection onto the end cross-section defines a unit origin vector {z}_{1} . The syntax is as follows: AFFE_CARA_ELEM( # ... ORIENTATION= _F( GROUP_NO= 'EXTREMITE', CARA= ’GENE_TUYAU’, VALE = (x,y,z), ) ) where: EXTREMITE is the centre node of the end cross-section. (x,y,z) contains the 3 components of the vector orienting the generatrix of the pipe, to be projected onto the end cross-section. This vector must be defined at an end node or an end group_no of the pipe. The geometry is then built automatically for all the connected TUYAU elements. The intersection between the direction of this vector and the mean surface of the elbow determines the trace of the generatrix on this section. {x}_{1,}{y}_{1,}{z}_{1} denotes the right-handed triad associated with this section, where {x}_{1} is the unit vector perpendicular to the cross-section. The intersection between the cross-section and the straight line issuing from the centre of this section and directed by {z}_{k} is the trace of a generatrix represented below. For all the other cross-sections, the triad {x}_{k},{y}_{k},{z}_{k} is obtained either by rotation of the triad {x}_{k-1},{y}_{k-1},{z}_{k-1} in the case of the elbowed parts, or by translation of the triad {x}_{k-1},{y}_{k-1},{z}_{k-1} for the straight parts of the piping. Figure 3.2.2-b: Representation of the reference generatrix. The origin of the \Phi common to all the elements is defined with respect to the trace of this generatrix on the cross-section. The angle between the trace of the generatrix and the current position on the cross-section is located by the angle \Phi . The local frame of the straight and elbowed pipe is thus defined by the option ORIENTATION ('GENE_TUYAU') of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, which makes it possible to define the first vector {z}_{k} at one end. Note : Pipe–beam connections. The aim is to establish a connection between an end node of a pipe element and an end node of a beam element. The pipe formulation includes a beam-type kinematics identical to the kinematics of the beam elements. There is therefore no discontinuity between the beam-type displacements (3 displacements and 3 rotations). The mean fibre of the beam and of the pipe are the same. On the other hand, the kinematics of the beam elements does not include a shell kinematics (the section is non-deformable) as in the case of the pipe elements; there is therefore a discontinuity at the level of the strain of the cross-section. There is no specific pipe–beam connection in Code_Aster; the connection between these two elements is ensured automatically, without any action by the user, by the node common to the pipe element and to the beam element. Nevertheless, certain precautions must be taken: the transition between the pipe and beam elements must be sufficiently far from any "pipe" zones where the strain of the cross-section is significant, that is to say one must connect only when the ovalisation has died out. To model T-junctions, preference will be given to modellings with shell or 3D elements and, consequently, to the use of connections of type COQ_TUYAU or 3D_TUYAU respectively. Regarding the shell/pipe connection, preference will be given to applying it in the straight sections rather than in the curved sections (it is recommended to move the connections out into regular, hence straight, zones). 3.4.6 Boundary conditions: keywords DDL_IMPO and LIAISON_ The factor keyword DDL_IMPO makes it possible to impose, on nodes introduced by one (at least) of the keywords: TOUT, NOEUD, GROUP_NO, MAILLE, GROUP_MA, one or more displacement values (or of certain associated quantities). Depending on the name of the operator called, the values are supplied directly (AFFE_CHAR_MECA) or by means of a function concept (AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F). The operands available for DDL_IMPO are listed below: - DX DY DZ: Fixing of the displacement component in translation - DRX DRY DRZ: Fixing of the displacement component in rotation If the specified nodes belong to 'TUYAU_3M' elements (these elements have 15 shell degrees of freedom): | U: warping | V , W : ovalisation | | --- | --- | | I : 'in plane' | O : 'out of plane' | That is: - UI2 VI2 WI2 UO2 VO2 WO2: degrees of freedom associated with mode 2. - UI3 VI3 WI3 UO3 VO3 WO3: degrees of freedom associated with mode 3. - WO WI1 WO1: degrees of freedom of swelling and mode 1 on W . If the specified nodes belong to 'TUYAU_6M' elements (these elements have 33 shell degrees of freedom), the following degrees of freedom are added: - UI4 VI4 WI4 UO4 VO4 WO4: degrees of freedom associated with mode 4. - UI5 VI5 WI5 UO5 VO5 WO5: degrees of freedom associated with mode 5. - UI6 VI6 WI6 UO6 VO6 WO6: degrees of freedom associated with mode 6. 3.5 Application of a thermal expansion. No thermal analysis is available with the TUYAU modelling; it is nevertheless possible to apply an expansion (loading of thermal origin), in the form of a temperature field at the nodes, defined by the 3 components TEMP, TEMP_INF, TEMP_SUP, from which the mean temperature is deduced. This field will have been created beforehand by means of the operator CREA_CHAMP (documentation U4.72.04). | CREA_CHAMP | | TUYAU_3M TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TYPE_CHAM | 'NOEU_TEMP_R' 'NOEU_TEMP_F' | | Result field of temperature type | | OPERATION | | | | | MAILLAGE | | | | | MODELE | | | | | AFFE | TOUT: 'OUI' GROUP_MA MAILLE NOEUD GROUP_NO | | The field is built by assignment of values on nodes or mesh cells | | NOM_CMP | 'TEMP' | | The names of the components which one wants to assign: temperature | | | 'TEMP_INF' | | Internal temperature | | | 'TEMP_SUP' | | External temperature | The assignment of the thermal expansion is carried out by means of the operator AFFE_MATERIAU (documentation U4.43.03). | AFFE_MATERIAU | | TUYAU_3M TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AFFE_VARC | | | | | NOM_VARC | ‘TEMP’ | | Name of the command variable | | NOM_CHAM | ‘TEMP’ | | | | EVOL | tempe | | tempe is the field or the evolution created by CREA_CHAMP and then possibly by CREA_RESU. | | VALE_REF | | | reference temperature | Note: In the case where one wants to apply a temperature defined by a function, one can use the operator CREA_RESU(TYPE_RESU='EVOL_THER', …), document U4.44.12 in order to create a concept of type EVOL_THER usable in AFFE_MATERIAU. Examples of use are available in the test base: the test cases ELSA01B, SSLL106A, SSNL117A and SSNL503A. The following example is taken from the test case SSLL101C. TEMP= CREA_CHAMP( MAILLAGE = MAILLAGE , TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_TEMP_R' , OPERATION = 'AFFE' , AFFE=( _F(TOUT = 'OUI' , NOM_CMP = 'TEMP' , VALE = 472.22 ) , ) , ) TEMPER= CREA_RESU( OPERATION='AFFE' , TYPE_RESU='EVOL_THER' , NOM_CHAM='TEMP' , AFFE=_F(INST = 0.0, CHAM_GD = TEMP) ) AFF_MAT1 = AFFE_MATERIAU( MAILLAGE = MAILLAGE , AFFE=_F(TOUT = 'OUI' , MATER = MATER) , AFFE_VARC=_F(TOUT = 'OUI' , EVOL = TEMPER , NOM_VARC = 'TEMP' , NOM_CHAM = 'TEMP' , VALE_REF = 0.0 ) , ) 4 Solution 4.1 Linear analyses: MECA_STATIQUE and the other linear operators The linear analyses are carried out in small strains. Several linear solution operators are available: - MECA_STATIQUE: solution of a linear static mechanics problem U4.51.01, - MACRO_ELAS_MULT: computes the linear static responses for different load cases or Fourier modes U4.51.02, - CALC_MODES: computation of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors by subspace methods or inverse iterations U4.52.02, - MODE_ITER_CYCL: computation of the eigenmodes of a structure with cyclic symmetry U4.52.05, - DYNA_VIBRA: computation of the transient dynamic response to an arbitrary time excitation U4.53.03. By default, the only fields computed are the displacement fields DEPL and the stress fields SIEF_ELGA. Other fields are available through the operand OPTION (see the options available in paragraph [§5.2] dealing with the use of CALC_CHAMP). 4.2 Non-linear analyses: STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE 4.2.1 Available constitutive behaviours and strain assumptions The following information is taken from the User documentation of the operator STAT_NON_LINE: U4.51.03. | STAT_NON_LINE DYNA_NON_LINE | | | TUYAU_3M TUYAU_6M | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COMPORTEMENT | RELATION | | | all the constitutive behaviours available in C_PLAN | | | DEFORMATION | PETIT | | | The incremental constitutive relations (factor keyword COMPORTEMENT) under the assumption of small displacements and small strains (keyword DEFORMATION= ‘PETIT’) are the only non-linear mechanical constitutive relations available for the TUYAU modelling. These constitutive relations relate the strain rates to the stress rates. The non-linear constitutive behaviours supported are those already existing in plane stress defined in the operators STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE. Furthermore, with the De Borst method R5.03.03, all the 2D constitutive behaviours (D_PLAN, AXIS) in small strains can be used. The RESULTAT concept of STAT_NON_LINE contains stress fields, a displacement field and internal-variable fields at the integration points, always computed at the Gauss points: - SIEF_ELGA: Stress tensor per element at the integration points in the local frame of the element, - VARI_ELGA: Internal-variable field per element at the integration points in the local frame of the element, - DEPL: displacement fields. Furthermore, a call to the operator CALC_CHAMP makes it possible to access other fields. In particular, one can transfer the stresses and internal variables from the Gauss points to the nodes in order to form the fields SIEF_ELNO and VARI_ELNO (see paragraph [§5.2]). A VARI_… field can have several types of component. For example, the components of the field VARI_ELNO are, for the TUYAU elements: K times: (\mathrm{V1},\mathrm{V2},\dots \mathrm{..}\mathrm{Vn}) | Where: | K is the total number of integration points K=(2\times \mathrm{NCOU}+1)\times (2\times \mathrm{NSEC}+1) N is the number of internal variables and depends on the constitutive behaviour. | | --- | --- | 4.2.2 Details on the integration points For the linear and non-linear analyses, the numerical integration is carried out with a method of: - Gauss along the mean fibre. The stiffness matrices are under-integrated, bringing the number of integration points to 2 for the elements on SEG3 mesh cells, and to 3 for the elements on SEG4 mesh cells. Furthermore, the mass matrices of the elements supported by SEG4 are also under-integrated (3 integration points). For a mesh cell whose vertices are 1 and 2 and which is numbered from 1 to 2, the 3 Gauss points are such that the first is close to 1, the second is equidistant from 1 and 2 and the third is closer to 2. One must therefore pay attention to the orientation of the mesh cells when looking at the results at Gauss points 1 and 3. Indeed, if one changes the orientation of the mesh cell and numbers it from 2 to 1, the first Gauss point is closer to 2. - Simpson through the thickness and over the circumference: - The integration through the thickness is a Simpson integration with 3 points per layer. The number of integration points per layer is fixed at 3, at the middle of the layer, on the upper skin and on the lower skin of the layer, the two end points being common with the neighbouring layers. - The integration along the circumference is a Simpson integration by sector, each sector having an angle 2\pi /\mathrm{NSEC} . \Phi is the angle between the generatrix and the centre of the sector. The number of integration points per sector is fixed at 3, at the middle of the sector, on the upper part ( \Phi +2\pi /\mathrm{NSEC} ) and the lower part ( \Phi -2\pi /\mathit{NSEC} ) of the sector, the two end points being common with the neighbouring sectors. The number of layers and the number of sectors must be defined by the user from the keywords: TUYAU_NCOU, TUYAU_NSEC of the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. For example, with 3 layers and 16 sectors, the number of integration points per element is (2\times \mathrm{NCOU}+1)\times (2\times \mathrm{NSEC}+1)\times \mathrm{NPG} which gives 693 integration points. For each Gauss point along the length of the element, the information on the layers is stored and, for each layer, on all the sectors. If one wants information at the Gauss point \mathrm{NG} , on the layer \mathrm{NC} level \mathrm{NCN} ( \mathrm{NCN}=–1 if lower, \mathrm{NCN}=0 if middle, \mathrm{NCN}=+1 if upper), on the sector \mathrm{NS} , level \mathrm{NSN} ( \mathrm{NSN}=–1 if lower, \mathrm{NSN}=0 if middle, \mathrm{NSN}=+1 if upper), then one looks at the required values at the integration point: \begin{array}{cc}\mathrm{NP}=& (\mathrm{NG}-1)\times (2\mathrm{NCOU}+1)\times (2\mathrm{NSEC}+1)\\ & +(2\times \mathrm{NC}+\mathrm{NCN}-1)\times (2\mathrm{NSEC}+1)+(2\times \mathrm{NS}+\mathrm{NSN})\end{array} . 4.3 Dynamic analyses Regarding the dynamic analyses, there is no specific feature due to the TUYAU finite element. 5 Additional computations and post-processings 5.1 Computation of elementary matrices: operator CALC_MATR_ELEM The operator CALC_MATR_ELEM (documentation U4.61.01) makes it possible to compute elementary matrices assembled by the command ASSE_MATRICE (documentation U4.61.22). The only matrices which can be computed with the pipe elements are the stiffness and mass matrices of the elements of the model: | CALC_MATR_ELEM | | TUYAU_3M | TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 'rigi_meca' | | | | | | 'MASS_MECA' | | | | | These computations of elementary matrices are used, for example, for the determination of the eigenfrequencies of a thick cylindrical ring, in the test case SDLS109G. 5.2 Computations by element: operator CALC_CHAMP The operator CALC_CHAMP (documentation U4.81.04) carries out the computation of the fields on the elements: - stresses, strains, internal variables at the nodes; - equivalent values (not available for the TUYAU modelling). The post-processing options for the pipe elements are presented below. For structures modelled by pipe elements, it is particularly important to know how the stress results are presented: the approach adopted in Code_Aster consists in observing the stresses in a particular frame linked to the element, whose reference axis was defined in paragraph [§3.2.2]. This approach seems the most physical because, for a cylindrical structure, the stresses which are easiest to interpret are not the stresses in a Cartesian frame but the stresses in cylindrical coordinates. Furthermore, this approach allows greater flexibility of use. | CALC_CHAMP | | TUYAU_3M | TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 'SIEF_ELGA' | | | | | | 'SIEF_ELNO' | | | | | | 'SIGM_ELGA' | | | | | | 'SIGM_ELNO' | | | | | | 'EFGE_ELGA' | | | | | | 'EFGE_ELNO' | | | | | | 'EPSI_ELGA' | | | | | | 'EPSI_ELNO' | | | | | | 'VARI_ELNO' | | | | | - SIEF_ELGA: computation of the stresses per element at the integration points of the element from the displacements (Use in elasticity only), in the local frame of the element. - SIEF_ELNO: computation of the stresses per element at the nodes of the element from the stresses at the Gauss points, in the local frame of the element. - SIGM_ELGA: computation of the stresses per element at the integration points of the element from SIEF_ELGA in the local frame of the element. - SIGM_ELNO: computation of the stresses per element at the nodes of the element from SIGM_ELNO, in the local frame of the element. - EFGE_ELGA: computation of the generalised forces per element at the Gauss points from the displacements, by integration from SIEF_ELGA, in the local frame of the element. - EFGE_ELNO: computation of the generalised forces per element at the nodes from the displacements in linear analysis and computed by integration from SIEF_ELGA in non-linear analysis, in the local frame of the element. - EPSI_ELGA: computation of the strains per element at the integration points of the element from the displacements, in the local frame of the element (small strains). - EPSI_ELNO: computation of the strains per element at the nodes of the element from the strains at the Gauss points, in the local frame of the element (small strains). - VARI_ELNO: computation of the internal-variable field per element at the nodes from the Gauss points, for all the layers (in the thickness SUP/MOY/INF) and for all the sectors in the local frame of the element. One then obtains, per node of each element, a single stress tensor (or a single set of internal variables), which allows graphical post-processing (evolution of a component, …). 5.3 Computations at the nodes: operator CALC_CHAMP | CALC_CHAMP | | TUYAU_3M | TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 'FORC_NODA' | | | | | | 'REAC_NODA' | | | | | | 'EFGE_NOEU' | | | | | | 'SIEF_NOEU' | | | | | | 'SIGM_NOEU' | | | | | | 'VARI_NOEU' | | | | | The operator CALC_CHAMP (documentation U4.81.04) carries out the computation of the fields at the nodes by averaging and the computation of the forces and reactions: - fields at the nodes: stresses, strains, internal variables, equivalent values; - Option name: replace _ELNO_ by _NOEU_ - The fields at the nodes can be computed by CALC_CHAMP SIEF_NOEU, VARI_NOEU - forces and reactions: - from the stresses, the equilibrium: FORC_NODA (computation of the nodal forces from the stresses at the integration points, element by element), - then by removing the applied loading: REAC_NODA (computation of the nodal reaction forces at the nodes, from the stresses at the integration points, element by element): REAC_NODA = FORC_NODA - applied loadings, - useful for checking the loading and for computations of resultants, moments, etc. 5.4 Computations of quantities over the whole or part of the structure: operator POST_ELEM The operator POST_ELEM (documentation U4.81.22) makes it possible to compute quantities over the whole or part of the structure. The quantities computed correspond to particular computation options of the assigned modelling. | | | TUYAU_3M | TUYAU_6M | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 'MASS_INER' | | | | | For the TUYAU modellings, the only option available at present is the computation, on each element, of the mass, of the inertias and of the position of the centre of gravity (option 'MASS_INER'). 5.5 Values of components of fields of quantities: operator POST_RELEVE_T For the TUYAU modellings, the operator POST_RELEVE_T (documentation U4.81.21) can be used to extract, on a line, values (for example SIEF_ELNO). The nodes must be reordered along the post-processing line. The solution is to use the operator DEFI_GROUP with the option NOEU_ORDO. This option makes it possible to create an ordered GROUP_NO containing the nodes of a set of mesh cells made up of segments (SEG2, SEG3 or SEG4). An example of extraction of a component is given in the test case SSNL503 (see the description in paragraph [§6.2]): TAB_DRZ=POST_RELEVE_T( ACTION=_F( > GROUP_NO = 'D', > INTITULE = 'TB_DRZ', > RESULTAT = RESUL, > NOM_CHAM = 'DEPL', > NOM_CMP = 'DRZ', > TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', > OPERATION = 'EXTRACTION' > ) > ) The purpose of this syntax is: | to extract: | OPERATION = 'EXTRACTION' | | --- | --- | | on the line (the node group) D: | GROUP_NO = 'D' | | the component DRZ of the displacement: | NOM_CHAM = 'DEPL', NOM_CMP = 'DRZ', | | for all the computation time instants: | TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' | 6 Examples The following tables describe a few test cases using the TUYAU element. 6.1 Linear static analysis | SSLL101 | Title: Hovgaard problem. u2.02.03 User's guide for the discrete elements u2.02.03 User's guide for the discrete elements Summary: This document is a user's guide for the modellings of the discrete elements. The discrete elements are used in the numerical modelling of stiffnesses, dampings or masses localised on a node ( POI1 mesh cell) or between two nodes ( SEG2 mesh cell). Their degrees of freedom are generalised displacements. They can be used in linear or non-linear mechanics. 1 Introduction The discrete elements are used to model, very simply, masses, springs or dampers. They are used to assign point properties to nodes of the mesh and to define point masses, stiffnesses and support damping. These modellings can be used in linear and non-linear mechanics, under the assumption of small displacements. Three categories of discrete elements are described in this document: - mass, - stiffness, - damper, In a first part, the data setup of the properties of the discrete elements is presented, with the various options available. In the second and third parts, the computation and post-processing operators for the discrete elements are given. The last part gives a list of test cases, examples of use of the discrete elements. 2 Assignment of the properties of the discrete elements 2.1 Support mesh cells of the discrete elements The support mesh cells of the discrete elements are POI1 (mesh cell with one node) or SEG2 (segment with two nodes). 2.2 Spatial discretisation and assignment of a modelling In this part, the choice and the assignment of one of the discrete modellings are described, together with the degrees of freedom and the associated mesh cells. Most of the information described is taken from the user documentation of the modellings: - U3.11.02: modellings DIS_T and DIS_TR . - U3.13.09: modellings 2D_DIS_T and 2D_DIS_TR . 2.3 Degrees of freedom The discretisation degrees of freedom are defined at each node of the support mesh cell. The components, depending on the modelling chosen, are given in the following table. | Modelling | Degrees of freedom (at each node) | | --- | --- | | 2D_DIS_T | DX, DY | | 2D_DIS_TR | DX, DY, DRZ | | DIS_T | DX, DY, DZ | | DIS_TR | DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ | 2.3.1 Support mesh cells of the matrices | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | | --- | --- | --- | | 2D_DIS_T | POI1, SEG2 | MECA_2D_DIS_T_N, MECA_2D_DIS_T_L | | 2D_DIS_TR | POI1, SEG2 | MECA_2D_DIS_TR_N, MECA_2D_DIS_TR_L | | DIS_T | POI1, SEG2 | MECA_DIS_T_N, MECA_DIS_T_L | | DIS_TR | POI1, SEG2 | MECA_DIS_TR_N, MECA_DIS_TR_L | Note: In a mesh, in order to transform a node into a POI1 mesh cell, one can use the command CREA_MAILLAGE with the keyword CREA_POI1. 2.3.2 Model: AFFE_MODELE The assignment of the modelling is done by means of the operator AFFE_MODELE. | AFFE_MODELE | | | --- | --- | | AFFE | | | PHENOMENE | MECANIQUE | | MODELISATION | 2D_DIS_T, 2D_DIS_TR, DIS_T, DIS_TR | 2.4 Elementary characteristics, operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM In this part, the characteristic operands of the discrete elements are described. See the user documentation of the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. These keywords make it possible to assign directly, to entities (mesh cells or nodes) which support elements of type DIS_T , DIS_TR (DISCRET 3D) or 2D_DIS_T , 2D_DIS_TR (DISCRET_2D), matrices of stiffness , of mass or of damping . The characteristics can be defined by one of the following four keywords and govern the linear elastic constitutive behaviour. 2.4.1 Keyword: DISCRET or DISCRET_2D The characteristics of the discrete elements are described by the following nomenclature: with \begin{cases}M & Masse\\K & Rigidité\\A & Amortissement\end{cases} \begin{cases}T & Translations\\TR & Translations~et~rotations\end{cases} \large \left[~M~|~K~|~A~\right] \underline{} \left~T~|~TR~\right \underline{} \left[~N~|~L~\right] D if present, the matrix is diagonal \begin{cases}N & support~nœud~ou~POI1\\L & support~SEG2\end{cases} The possibilities for assigning the matrices are: - Stiffness matrices: K_T_D_N, K_TR_D_N, K_T_D_L, K_TR_D_L, K_T_N, K_TR_N, K_T_L, K_TR_L - Mass matrices: M_T_D_N, M_TR_D_N, M_T_D_L, M_TR_D_L, M_T_N, M_TR_N, M_T_L, M_TR_L - Damping matrices: A_T_D_N, A_TR_D_N, A_T_D_L, A_TR_D_L, A_T_N, A_TR_N, A_T_L, A_TR_L The number of values required to define the matrices is a function of the characteristic chosen in U4.42.01. By default, the characteristics are given in the global frame. The local frame can be defined for a node, a POI1 mesh cell or an SEG2 mesh cell by means of the keyword ORIENTATION of AFFE_CARA_ELEM and by specifying REPERE=’LOCAL’. - The index T or \mathit{TR} must be compatible with the definition of the models in AFFE_MODELE, DIS_T or DIS_TR - One can apply mass and stiffness characteristics on the same mesh cell. If one assigns only a mass on a discrete element, one obtains the alarm DISCRETS_27 to indicate that a zero stiffness is considered. The alarm DISCRETS_26 is emitted in the case where one assigns only a stiffness. To suppress these alarms, the various matrices must be supplied. - The keyword AMOR_HYST= {\mathit{amor}}_{h} makes it possible to build a complex stiffness matrix (modelling of hysteretic damping); the matrix built is: \left(1+i.{\mathit{amor}}_{h}\right).\mathrm{K} where \mathrm{K} is the matrix K_ whose values are supplied in the same occurrence of the keyword DISCRET. The complex stiffness matrix will be built during a call to CALC_MATR_ELEM U4.61.01 with the option AMOR_HYST (see test SDLD313 and R5.05.04). - The complete definition of the stiffness, mass or damping matrices makes it possible to define eccentric elements. The test case SDNL113 gives the example of eccentric masses (V5.02.113). Notes 2.4.2 Keyword: RIGI_PARASOL This functionality corresponds to a methodology used to determine the characteristics of discrete elements (translation and/or rotation springs) to be applied to the nodes of a raft from global stiffnesses. This option is available in 3D and in 2D. In the 3D case, the raft will be modelled by a surface. In the 2D case, it will be modelled by a line (test SSNL130 V6.02.130). In the 2D case, the discrete elements are 2D_DIS_TR or 2D_DIS_T. The factor keyword RIGI_PARASOL distributes 6 global stiffnesses in proportion to the areas of the elements surrounding its nodes. - SSLS118 C and D V2.03.118 - SSNL130 A and B V6.02.130 Test cases: 2.4.3 Keyword: RIGI_MISS_3D This keyword assigns the exact terms of an impedance matrix computed by MISS3D for all the interface degrees of freedom (3 times the number of nodes) and for a given extraction frequency. The assignment of these terms (modelling DIS_T) is then made to the point mesh cells POI1 of the nodes of the surface foundation. - SDNX101A V5.05.101. u2.03.04 User's guide for thermo-metallurgical-mechanical analyses on steels u2.03.04 User's guide for thermo-metallurgical-mechanical analyses on steels Summary The objective of this note is to give the information necessary for a user to be able to carry out easily a thermo-metallurgical-mechanical analysis in Code_Aster . This type of analysis concerns steels which undergo structural transformations in the course of a heating or of a cooling. 1 The main lines of the thermo-metallurgical-mechanical analysis In Code_Aster , the thermal, metallurgical and mechanical analyses are uncoupled. The successive stages of a complete analysis are as follows: 1. A thermal analysis is carried out, which makes it possible to obtain the temperature field at each node. 2. As a post-processing of the thermal analysis, the metallurgical analysis is carried out, which makes it possible to obtain the proportion of the different metallurgical phases at each node and possibly the associated hardness. In Code_Aster, two different types of material can be treated, which undergo metallurgical transformations: steels or ZIRCALOY. Only materials of steel type are of interest here. For a steel, five different metallurgical phases can be taken into account: ferrite, pearlite, bainite and martensite, called the \alpha phase, and austenite, called the gamma phase. 3. From the temperature field and the metallurgical phases, the mechanical analysis is carried out by choosing a constitutive model which takes into account the various possible effects of the metallurgical transformations. The fields of stresses, of strains and of internal variables are thus obtained at each Gauss point. 2 What to do in order to carry out a thermo-metallurgical-mechanical analysis? 2.1 Stage 1: which documents to read – summary 2.1.1 For the thermal part The document R5.02.02 contains the information necessary for the understanding of a non-linear thermal analysis. In Code_Aster , for a non-linear analysis, heat diffusion is treated with an enthalpy formulation. One can supply either the conductivity and the enthalpy as a function of the temperature, or the conductivity and the specific heat \rho {C}_{p} as a function of the temperature. 2.1.2 For the metallurgical constitutive-model part The document R4.04.01 of Code_Aster describes the various metallurgical models. Brief summary: When a material is heated, the \alpha phases transform into the \gamma phase. When the material is cooled, the austenite transforms, depending on the cooling rate, into ferrite and/or pearlite and/or bainite and/or martensite. One must therefore define, for the heating, the kinetics of the transformation \alpha \to \gamma and, for the cooling, the nature and the kinetics of the possible transformations \gamma \to \alpha . Transformation kinetics on heating: The evolution law of the austenite is given by the equation: \dot{{Z}_{\gamma}}=\frac{{Z}_{\mathrm{eq}}-{Z}_{\gamma}}{\tau} with {Z}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\lbrace \begin{array}{ccc}0& \text{si}& T\le \mathrm{Ac1}\\ \frac{T-\mathrm{Ac1}}{\mathrm{Ac3}-\mathrm{Ac1}}& \text{si}& \mathrm{Ac1}\le T\le \mathrm{Ac3}\\ 1& \text{si}& T\ge \mathrm{Ac3}\end{array} and \tau =\lbrace \begin{array}{ccc}{\tau}_{1}& \text{si}& T\le \mathrm{Ac1}\\ {\tau}_{1}+\frac{T-\mathrm{Ac1}}{\mathrm{Ac3}-\mathrm{Ac1}}({\tau}_{3}-{\tau}_{1})& \text{si}& \mathrm{Ac1}\le T\le \mathrm{Ac3}\\ {\tau}_{3}& \text{si}& T\ge \mathrm{Ac3}\end{array} where {Z}_{\gamma} is the proportion of phase \gamma , \mathrm{Ac1} the quasi-static temperature of the start of transformation of the phases, \mathrm{Ac3} \alpha the quasi-static temperature of the end of transformation of the phases \alpha and {\tau}_{1} , {\tau}_{3} two coefficients of the material. {Z}_{\mathrm{eq}} corresponds to the evolution of the transformed austenite fraction during quasi-static evolutions. The temperatures of the start \mathrm{Ac1} and of the end \mathrm{Ac3} of the austenitic transformation and the parameters {\tau}_{1} and {\tau}_{3} can be identified from experimental data supplying, for different heating rates, the proportion of austenite formed as a function of the temperature. Details on the method of identification of the coefficients will be found in [bib1]. Example: For a 16MND5 steel, the coefficients are \mathit{Ac1}=716°C , \mathit{Ac3}=802°C , {\tau}_{1}=12\text{s} and {\tau}_{3}=0.5\text{s} . Transformation kinetics on cooling: For the ferritic, pearlitic and bainitic transformations, the kinetics is given by the following relation: \dot{Z}=f(T,\dot{T},Z,{M}_{s},{d}^{c})\frac{{(T-{M}_{s})}^{+}}{(T-{M}_{s})} with Z=\lbrace {Z}_{F},{Z}_{P},{Z}_{B}\rbrace where {M}_{s} represents the temperature of the start of the martensitic transformation, {d}^{c} the austenitic grain size and {(X)}^{+} the positive part of X . For the evolution functions f , no particular forms are imposed and the identification of f reduces to the definition of diagrams of TRC type (transformation on Continuous Cooling). This diagram makes it possible to define the evolutions of ferrite, pearlite and bainite associated with a thermal history on cooling and with given austenitisation conditions (for a given grain size {d}^{c} ). For the martensitic transformation, the Koistinen-Marburger kinetics given by the equation is used: {Z}_{M}=(1-{Z}_{F}-{Z}_{P}-{Z}_{B})\left[1-\exp(\alpha ({M}_{s}-{T}^{+}))\right] {M}_{s}=\lbrace \begin{array}{ccc}{M}_{\mathrm{s0}}& \text{si}& {Z}_{F}+{Z}_{P}+{Z}_{B}\le \mathrm{seuil}\\ {M}_{\mathrm{s0}}+\mathrm{Akm}({Z}_{F}+{Z}_{P}+{Z}_{B})+\mathrm{Bkm}& \text{si}& {Z}_{F}+{Z}_{P}+{Z}_{B}>\mathrm{seuil}\end{array} where {M}_{\mathrm{s0}} represents the temperature of the start of the martensitic transformation when the latter is total, and \alpha , \mathrm{Akm} , \mathrm{Bkm} and \mathrm{seuil} are material parameters. In the simplest case, the temperature {M}_{s} can be taken constant and therefore equal to {M}_{\mathrm{s0}} . For a 16MND6 steel, {M}_{\mathrm{s0}} is equal to 365°C . Note: The TRC diagrams relate to given austenitisation conditions, to which a value of the grain size d corresponds. This grain size results from the thermal history undergone on heating and no longer evolves on cooling. In Code_Aster, it is possible to compute, from the thermal history on heating, the evolution of the grain size and to take its effect on the metallurgical behaviour on cooling into account (see the reference test cases hsnv126a.comm, hsnv126b.comm and mtlp102a.comm for the use). Note: It is possible in Code_Aster to compute the hardness \mathrm{Hv} of the multiphase mixture given by the relation \mathrm{Hv}=\sum_{k=1}^{5}{Z}_{k}{\mathrm{Hv}}_{k} where {\mathrm{Hv}}_{k} is the hardness associated with the phase k and supplied under the operator DEFI_MATERIAU under the keyword ’DURT_META’. The hardness of the multiphase mixture is obtained by the operator CALC_META with the option ’DURT_ELNO’ (hardness at the nodes per element). 2.1.3 For the mechanical constitutive-model part with effects of the metallurgical transformations The reference document of Code_Aster is the note R4.04.02. Several constitutive models are available in the code. They make it possible to model the following different phenomena: plastic behaviour or viscous behaviour, linear or non-linear isotropic hardening or linear kinematic hardening, transformation plasticity, restoration of hardening of metallurgical origin, restoration of hardening of viscous origin. An analysis can be carried out in small strains but also in large strains (beware: the large strains for a model with kinematic hardening are not activated). For an understanding of the large-strain aspect, read the reference documents R5.03.21 (large strains without metallurgical effect) and R4.04.03 (large strains with metallurgical effects). Brief summary: The effects of the structural transformations on the mechanical behaviour are of 4 types: - the mechanical characteristics of the material which undergoes transformations are modified. In particular, the plastic characteristics (yield stresses in particular) and the thermal expansion coefficient are strongly affected. For the yield stress of the multiphase point, a non-linear law of mixtures is used, given by: {\sigma}_{y}=\left[1-g(\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i})\right]{\sigma}_{y\gamma }+g(\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i}){\sigma}_{y\alpha } , {\sigma}_{\mathrm{ya}}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i}{\sigma}_{y\alpha i}}{\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i}} where {Z}_{i} is the proportion of each \alpha phase and g a function of the {Z}_{i} . - the volume expansion or contraction which accompanies the structural transformations results in a spherical "transformation" strain which is superimposed on the thermal strain. In general, this effect is grouped with that due to the modification of the thermal expansion coefficient. The thermal strain is given by: {\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}={Z}_{\gamma}\left[{\alpha}_{\gamma}(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}})-(1-{Z}_{\gamma}^{r})\Delta {\varepsilon}_{f\gamma }^{{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right]+\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i}\left[{\alpha}_{f}(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}})+{Z}_{\gamma}^{r}\Delta {\varepsilon}_{f\gamma }^{{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right] where {\alpha}_{\gamma} and {\alpha}_{f} are the expansion coefficients of the austenitic and ferritic phases, respectively. \Delta {\varepsilon}_{f\gamma }^{{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}} represents the difference in compactness between the two phases at the reference temperature. One has {Z}_{\gamma}^{r}=1 when the reference phase is the austenitic phase and {Z}_{\gamma}^{r}=0 when the reference phase is the ferritic phase. - a transformation taking place under stresses can give rise to an irreversible strain, even for stress levels very much lower than the yield stress of the material. This phenomenon is called transformation plasticity. In small strains, this additional term appears in the expression of the total strain. The evolution law of the strain which accompanies this phenomenon is written: {\dot{\varepsilon}}^{\mathit{pt}}=\frac{3}{2}\tilde{\sigma}\sum_{i=1}^{4}{K}_{i}F{'}_{i}({Z}_{\gamma})\cdot \langle \dot{{Z}_{i}}\rangle where \tilde{\sigma} is the deviator of the stress tensor, \langle X\rangle the positive part of X , {K}_{i} and {F}_{i} , coefficients of the 4 ferritic phases. It is considered that this phenomenon does not exist during austenitic transformations. - finally, during the transformation one can have a phenomenon of restoration of hardening: the hardening of the parent phase is not (or not totally) transmitted to the newly created phases. The newly created phases can either be born with a virgin hardening state, or inherit only part of the hardening of the parent phase, or inherit the whole of the hardening of the parent phase. In the case of isotropic hardening, the plastic strain p is no longer characteristic of the hardening state and other variables must be defined for each phase, denoted {r}_{k} . The isotropic hardening is then written: R=(1-\bar{f}(Z)){R}_{\gamma}+\frac{\bar{f}(Z)}{Z}\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i}\cdot {R}_{i} , Z=\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i} where {R}_{k} is the hardening variable of the phase k , which can be linear or non-linear with respect to {r}_{k} , and \bar{f}(Z) a function depending on Z such that \bar{f}(Z)\in [0,1] . The evolution laws of the variables {r}_{i} are given by: \begin{array}{ccc}{\dot{r}}_{\gamma}=\dot{p}+\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{4}\langle -\dot{{Z}_{i}}\rangle ({\theta}_{i\gamma }{r}_{i}-{r}_{\gamma})}{{Z}_{\gamma}}-\underset{\text{uniquement en viscosité}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{(C{r}_{\mathrm{moy}})}^{m}}}& \text{si}& {Z}_{\gamma}>0\\ \dot{{r}_{i}}=\dot{p}+\frac{\langle {Z}_{i}\rangle ({\theta}_{\gamma i}{r}_{\gamma}-{r}_{i})}{{Z}_{\gamma}}-\underset{\text{uniquement en viscosité}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{(C{r}_{\mathrm{moy}})}^{m}}}& \text{si}& {Z}_{i}>0\end{array} {r}_{\mathrm{moy}}=\sum_{k=1}^{5}{Z}_{k}{r}_{k} C=\sum_{k=1}^{5}{Z}_{k}{C}_{k} m=\sum_{k=1}^{5}{Z}_{k}{m}_{k} {C}_{k} and {m}_{k} are the viscous-restoration coefficients associated with the phase k , {\theta}_{i\gamma } and {\theta}_{\gamma i} characterise the proportion of hardening transmitted during the transformation \alpha \to \gamma and during the transformation \gamma \to \alpha , respectively. The memory is non-existent if \theta =0 , complete if \theta =1 . In an equivalent manner, one writes in the case of kinematic hardening: X=(1-\bar{f}(Z))+\frac{\bar{f}(Z)}{Z}\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i}\cdot {X}_{i} , Z=\sum_{i=1}^{4}{Z}_{i} where {X}_{k} is the kinematic hardening variable of the phase k , which is linear with respect to the variable {\alpha}_{k} : {X}_{k}=\frac{2}{3}{H}_{k}{\alpha}_{k} The evolution laws of the kinematic variables {\alpha}_{k} are given by: \begin{array}{ccc}{\dot{\alpha}}_{\gamma}={\dot{\varepsilon}}^{p}+\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{4}\langle \dot{{Z}_{i}}\rangle ({\theta}_{i\gamma }{\alpha}_{i}-{\alpha}_{\gamma})}{{Z}_{\gamma}}+\underset{\text{uniquement en viscosité}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{\frac{3}{2}{(C{\alpha}_{\mathrm{eq}})}^{m}\frac{\alpha}{{\alpha}_{\mathrm{eq}}}}}& \text{si}& {Z}_{\gamma}>0\\ {\dot{\alpha}}_{i}={\dot{\varepsilon}}^{p}+\frac{\langle \dot{{Z}_{i}}\rangle ({\theta}_{\gamma i}{\alpha}_{\gamma}-{\alpha}_{i})}{{Z}_{i}}+\underset{\text{uniquement en viscosité}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{\frac{3}{2}{(C{\alpha}_{\mathrm{eq}})}^{m}\frac{\alpha}{{\alpha}_{\mathrm{eq}}}}}& \text{si}& {Z}_{i}>0\end{array} {\dot{\varepsilon}}^{p}=\frac{3}{2}\dot{p}\frac{(\tilde{\sigma}-X)}{{(\sigma -X)}_{\mathrm{eq}}} where {H}_{k} are the hardening slopes associated with each phase k . For a plasticity model, the plastic multiplier is obtained by writing the consistency condition \dot{f}=0 and one has: \dot{p}\ge 0 , f\le 0 and \dot{p}f=0 In the viscous case, \dot{p} is written: \dot{p}={(\frac{\langle f\rangle }{\eta})}^{n} where f is the plasticity threshold given by: f={\sigma}_{\mathrm{eq}}-R-{\sigma}_{y} in the case of isotropic hardening f={(\sigma -X)}_{\mathrm{eq}}-{\sigma}_{y} in the case of kinematic hardening 2.2 Stage 2: construction of the command file 2.2.1 Thermal and metallurgical parts | 1) | Definition of the TRC diagram: see the command DEFI_TRC in the document [U4.43.04]. u2.03.05 User's guide for the numerical simulation of welding u2.03.05 User's guide for the numerical simulation of welding > Summary. The aim of this document is to give the information needed for a user to carry out multipass welding analyses with Code_Aster . It constitutes a methodological guide to the tools available and to the good practice to put in place in order to conduct a quality study in the numerical simulation of welding. The various pieces of advice given to the user come essentially from the feedback of three studies: - A bevelled 316L pipe welded by the TIG process, with filler metal, in thirteen passes (CEA/EDF sheet 3488); the first 2 passes of this example constitute a Code_Aster test case V7.42.100; - A bevelled 316L plate welded by the TIG process, with filler metal, in two welding passes (CEA/EDF sheet 2425); the various command files attached to this study are stored in the Code_Aster study database (SERVICE/BDD Etudes); - An unbevelled 316L plate, with creation of a fusion line by the TIG process, but without filler metal (INSA Lyon thesis of L.
