u3.12.02 Modellings COQUE_AXIS u3.12.02 Modellings COQUE_AXIS Summary: This document describes, for the modelling COQUE_AXIS: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the related support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. The thermo-elasto-plastic modelling COQUE_AXIS corresponds to a formulation derived from the 3D models with a shell kinematics R3.07.02. It can be used to model structures whose middle surface has a particular geometry: - shells with rotational symmetry about the axis \mathit{OY} , The thermomechanical analyses are chained from the thermal shell finite elements (see U3.22.01). 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom For the three shell modellings, the discretisation degrees of freedom are, at each node of the support mesh cell, the three displacement components (two translations and one rotation). The nodes are assumed to belong to the middle surface of the shell. | Finite element | Degrees of freedom (at each vertex node) | | --- | --- | | MECXSE3 | DX | DY | DRZ | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices The support mesh cells of the finite elements, in displacement formulation, are three-node segments: | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE_AXIS | SEG3 | MECXSE3 | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings All the loadings applicable on the middle surface of the shell elements are treated by direct discretisation on the support mesh cell of the element in displacement formulation. No loading support mesh cell is therefore necessary for the faces of the shell elements. For the imposed displacements, the support mesh cells are mesh cells reduced to a point. 2 Assignment of the characteristics For these 2D structural elements, it is necessary to assign geometrical characteristics which are complementary to the mesh data. The definition of these data is carried out with the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM associated with the following factor keyword: - COQUE Makes it possible to define and assign to the mesh cells the thickness, the shear coefficient, the eccentricity, ... 3 Supported loadings The available loadings are the following: - 'FORCE_COQUE' Makes it possible to apply surface forces. - 'PRES_REP' Makes it possible to apply a pressure to a continuum domain. - 'ROTATION' Makes it possible to define the rotation speed and the rotation vector. - 'PESANTEUR' Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. - The application of a thermal expansion loading is carried out by defining the factor keyword AFFE_VARC under AFFE_MATERIAU[U4.43.03]. 4 Non-linear possibilities 4.1 Constitutive laws The constitutive laws specific to these modellings, usable under COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, are the plane-stress constitutive relations available with the modelling 'AXIS' ( cf. U4.51.11). 4.2 Strains Only the linearised strains, keyword 'PETIT' under DEFORMATION, are available in the constitutive relations ( cf. U4.51.11). 5 Examples of implementation: test cases - COQUE_AXIS - Linear statics SSLS114I V3.03.114 : Quasi-static analysis of a quarter of a cylindrical shell subjected to a pressure.

u3.12.03 Modelling COQUE_3D u3.12.03 Modelling COQUE_3D Summary: The COQUE_3D modelling presented here corresponds to a general shell and plate kinematics formulation, of Naghdi-Reissner type, in which the generalised stresses are obtained from the three-dimensional constitutive laws of the constituent materials R3.07.04. Unlike the modellings DKT-DST, Q4G corresponding to the plate-element formulations developed by J.L. BATOZ [bib1]_ which use plane finite elements, the COQUE_3D modelling makes it possible to carry out analyses of shell structures of arbitrary shapes, with a good approximation of the geometry. Furthermore, this modelling is capable of representing the large rotations of the structures R3.07.05 under the assumption of small strains. The degrees of freedom are the displacements and the rotations, taken at the nodes of the elements. The non-linear constitutive behaviour is discretised by polynomials \mathit{P2} , which allows a precise analysis of the stresses. It can be used for problems of three-dimensional shell structures in linear and non-linear mechanical analysis. This formulation also exists for slice problems, or problems of revolution. It is based on 1D elements: (see [U3.12.02]). The thermomechanical analyses are chained from the thermal shell finite elements (see U3.22.01). 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom For the three-dimensional shell modelling, the discretisation degrees of freedom are, at each node of the support mesh cell, the six displacement components (three translations and three rotations) at the vertex nodes and at the mid-side nodes of the support mesh cell. At the central node of the support mesh cell, the degrees of freedom are reduced to the rotations only. These nodes belong to the middle surface of the shell. | Modelling | Degrees of freedom (at each node) | | --- | --- | | COQUE_3D | DX DY DZ DRX DRY DRZ DRX DRY DRZ only at the central node | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices, mass matrices ... The support mesh cells of the finite elements, in displacement formulation, may be 7-node triangles or 9-node quadrilaterals. These mesh cells are not assumed to be plane; they are created from meshes in TRIA6 and QUAD8 by the command CREA_MAILLAGE (see U4.23.02). | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE_3D | TRIA7 QUAD9 | MEC3TR7H MEC3QU9H | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings All the loadings applicable to the facets of the shell elements are treated by direct discretisation on the support mesh cell of the element in displacement formulation. No loading support mesh cell is therefore necessary for the faces of the shell elements. For the loadings applicable on the edges of the shell elements, a support mesh cell of type SEG3 can be used: | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE_3D | SEG3 | MEBOCQ3 | 2 Assignment of the characteristics For these \mathrm{2D}1/2 structural elements, it is necessary to assign geometrical characteristics which are complementary to the mesh data. The definition of these data is carried out with the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM associated with the following factor keyword: - COQUE Makes it possible to define and assign to the mesh cells the thickness, the shear coefficient, the eccentricity, ... 3 Supported loadings The available mechanical loadings are the following: - 'FORCE_ARETE' Makes it possible to apply linear forces, to an edge of a volume element. - 'FORCE_COQUE' Makes it possible to apply surface forces. - 'PESANTEUR' Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. - 'PRES_REP' Makes it possible to apply a pressure to a continuum domain. - 'ROTATION' Makes it possible to define the rotation speed and the rotation vector. The application of a thermal expansion loading is carried out by defining the factor keyword AFFE_VARC under AFFE_MATERIAU U4.43.03. 4 Non-linear possibilities 4.1 Constitutive laws All the plane-stress relations, usable under COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, are available ( cf. U4.51.11). 4.2 Strains The available strains, used in the constitutive relations under the keyword DEFORMATION for the operators STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, are (Cf. U4.51.11): / 'PETIT' The strains used for the constitutive relation are the linearised strains. / 'PETIT_REAC' The strain increments used in the incremental constitutive relation are the linearised strains of the displacement increment in the updated geometry. / 'GROT_GDEP' Makes it possible to carry out analyses in large displacements and in large rotations. The strains used in the constitutive relation are the GREEN‑LAGRANGE strains. Note: 1. Warning: the analysis of the strains using 'PETIT_REAC' is only an approximation of the large-displacement assumptions. It requires very small loading increments to be performed. In order to take large displacements, and especially large rotations, into account correctly, it is recommended to use DEFORMATION='GROT_GDEP'. 2. It is possible, by using under the factor keyword EXCIT(TYPE_CHARGE='SUIV') to take a follower pressure into account. 5 Examples of implementation: test cases - Linear statics SSLP304C V3.02.304: Analysis of an orthotropic square plate subjected to a uniaxial tension outside the axes of orthotropy - Non-linear statics HPLA100C V7.01.100 : Thermoelastic analysis of a heavy hollow cylinder in uniform rotation. - Linear dynamics SDLS01E V2.03.01: Analysis of the frequencies and of the associated bending modes of a thin square plate in free-free conditions and clamped on one edge. 6 Bibliography J.L. BATOZ, G. DHATT: Modelling of structures by finite elements. Vol.2 - beams and plates - HERMES, PARIS, 1990.

u3.12.04 Modelling GRILLE_EXCENTRE, GRILLE_MEMBRANE and MEMBRANE u3.12.04 Modelling GRILLE_EXCENTRE, GRILLE_MEMBRANE and MEMBRANE Summary: This document describes, for the modellings GRILLE_EXCENTRE, GRILLE_MEMBRANE and MEMBRANE: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the related support mesh cells, - the supported materials and loadings, - the analysis options for the elementary matrices and the post-processings, - the non-linear possibilities as well as the fracture-mechanics options if they exist. The modelling GRILLE_EXCENTRE (Phenomenon: MECANIQUE) corresponds to finite elements whose support mesh cells are three-node triangles and is used to represent the reinforcements for reinforced-concrete modellings of shell type. Indeed, it makes it possible to take into account the eccentricity of the reinforcement layers relative to the middle surface. The modelling GRILLE_MEMBRANE (phenomenon: MECANIQUE) corresponds to finite elements whose support mesh cells are three- or six-node triangles and four- or eight-node quadrilaterals and is used to represent the reinforcements for reinforced-concrete modellings of 3D solid type. Indeed, it does not make it possible to take the eccentricity into account and therefore does not require a rotation degree of freedom, which is unnecessary in 3D modelling. The modelling MEMBRANE (phenomenon: MECANIQUE) corresponds to finite elements whose support mesh cells are three-, six- or seven-node triangles and four-, eight- or nine-node quadrilaterals and is used to represent an arbitrary linear membrane behaviour or a non-linear isotropic membrane behaviour. It does not make it possible to take the eccentricity into account and has only displacement degrees of freedom. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degrees of freedom (at each vertex node) | | --- | --- | | GRILLE_EXCENTRE | \mathit{DX} : displacement along X | | --- | --- | | | \mathit{DY} : displacement along Y | | | \mathit{DZ} : displacement along Z | | | \mathit{DRX} : rotation about X | | | \mathit{DRY} : rotation about Y | | | \mathit{DRZ} : rotation about Z | | GRILLE_MEMBRANE and MEMBRANE | \mathit{DX} : displacement along X | | --- | --- | | | \mathit{DY} : displacement along Y | | | \mathit{DZ} : displacement along Z | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices The support mesh cells of the finite elements, in displacement formulation, are triangles. | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | | --- | --- | --- | | GRILLE_EXCENTRE | TRIA3 | MEGCTR3 | | --- | --- | --- | | | QUAD4 | MEGCQU4 | | GRILLE_MEMBRANE | TRIA3 | MEGMTR3 | | | QUAD4 | MEGMQU4 | | | TRIA6 | MEGMTR6 | | | QUAD8 | MEGMQU8 | | MEMBRANE | TRIA3 | MEMBTR3 | | | QUAD4 | MEMBQU4 | | | TRIA6 | MEMBTR6 | | | QUAD8 | MEMBQU8 | | | TRIA7 | MEMBTR7 | | | QUAD9 | MEMBQU9 | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings All the loadings applicable to the facets of the grid and membrane elements are treated by direct discretisation on the support mesh cell of the element in displacement formulation. u3.13.01 Modellings AXIS, D_PLAN, C_PLAN u3.13.01 Modellings AXIS, D_PLAN, C_PLAN Summary: The modellings AXIS, D_PLAN, C_PLAN (Phenomenon: mechanical) correspond to finite elements whose support mesh cells are surface mesh cells. The modelling assumptions are the following: - AXIS for axisymmetry (Fourier mode 0) about the Y axis, - D_PLAN for the plane strains, - C_PLAN for the plane stresses. This document describes: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the related support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degrees of freedom (at each vertex node) | | --- | --- | | AXIS | DX: corresponds to the radial displacement DY: corresponds to the longitudinal displacement | | D_PLAN | DX: displacement along X DY: displacement along Y | | C_PLAN | DX: displacement along X DY: displacement along Y | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices The support mesh cells of the finite elements may be triangles or quadrilaterals. The elements are isoparametric. | Modellings | Mesh cell | Interpolation | | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS D_PLAN C_PLAN | TRIA3 QUAD4 TRIA6 TRIA10 QUAD8 QUAD9 QUAD12 | Linear Bi-linear Quadratic Serendipity Bi-quadratic Cubic | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings | Modellings | Mesh cell | Interpolation | | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS D_PLAN | SEG2 | Linear or | | C_PLAN | SEG3 | Quadratic | 2 Supported loadings The available loadings are the following: - CONTACT Makes it possible to define the zones subjected to contact conditions. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN - EPSI_INIT Makes it possible to apply an initial strain loading. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN - FORCE_CONTOUR Makes it possible to define linear forces on the edge of a domain. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN - FORCE_INTERNE Makes it possible to define body forces. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN - PESANTEUR Makes it possible to define the acceleration and the direction of gravity. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN In axisymmetric modelling, gravity is applied only parallel to the axis of revolution Y. - PRES_REP Makes it possible to apply a pressure. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN - ROTATION Makes it possible to define a rotation speed and the direction of the rotation vector. Supported modellings: AXIS, C_PLAN, D_PLAN 3 Non-linear possibilities 3.1 Constitutive laws The constitutive laws (classical models, local models with damage, models for concrete, …), usable under COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, under the keyword RELATION, are described in detail in the document 'Non-linear constitutive behaviours' U4.51.11. 3.2 Strains The strains usable under COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, under the keyword DEFORMATION, are described in detail in the document «Non-linear constitutive behaviours» U4.51.11. 4 Examples of implementation: test cases - AXIS - Linear statics FORMA09B V7.20.101 : Thermoelastic analysis of a straight tube subjected to a cold shock. SSLS07A V3.03.007 : Linear static analysis of a thin cylinder subjected to a uniform axial load. - Non-linear statics SSNL129C V6.02.129: Simulation of a tensile test: validation of the constitutive laws 'VISC_ISOT_TRAC' and 'VISC_ISOT_LINE'. - Linear dynamics SDLS07B V2.03.007: Determination of the eigenfrequencies and of the associated modes of a thin spherical shell. - Non-linear dynamics SDNV103B V5.03.103: Impact of a TAYLOR bar: analysis of the frictional impact of an elastoplastic bar on a rigid solid. The modelling includes: contact, friction, elastoplasticity, large strains. - D_PLAN - Linear statics SSLV100H V3.04.100: Analysis of a hollow cylinder subjected to an internal pressure, in plane strains. - Non-linear statics SSNL129B V6.02.129: Simulation of a tensile test: validation of the constitutive laws 'VISC_ISOT_TRAC' and 'VISC_ISOT_LINE'. - Linear dynamics SDLS501A V2.03.501: Determination of the eigenfrequencies and of the associated modes of a corrugated sheet in free-free conditions. - Non-linear dynamics SDNV104A: Dynamic response of a rigid frictional pad subjected to a pressure and a restoring force. - C_PLAN - Linear statics SSLP101B V3.02.101: Analysis of a cracked plate in tension, analysis of the energy release rate in plane stresses. - Linear dynamics SDLL11G : Determination of the eigenfrequencies and of the associated modes of a thin circular ring in free-free conditions. - Non-linear statics HSNV100B V7.22.100: Analysis of a cylinder in thermo-plasticity subjected to a simple tensile force. - Non-linear dynamics DEMO002A : Non-linear dynamic analysis of a cracked blade with contact.

u3.13.02 Mechanical modelling AXIS_FOURIER u3.13.02 Mechanical modelling AXIS_FOURIER Summary: This document describes, for the mechanical modelling AXIS_FOURIER: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the related support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modelling. The modelling AXIS_FOURIER (Phenomenon: mechanical) corresponds to finite elements whose support mesh cells are plane and make it possible to model the longitudinal section of solids of revolution about the axis \mathit{OY} , (in cylindrical coordinates (r,z,\theta ) ) and subjected to loadings whose spatial distribution is decomposed into a Fourier series about this axis. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degrees of freedom (at each vertex node) | | --- | --- | | AXIS_FOURIER | \mathit{DX} : corresponds to the radial displacement | | --- | --- | | | \mathit{DY} : corresponds to the longitudinal displacement | | | \mathit{DZ} : corresponds to the ortho-radial displacement | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS_FOURIER | TRIA3 | Linear | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | QUAD4 | Bi-linear | | | | TRIA6 | Quadratic | | | | QUAD8 | Serendipity | | | | QUAD9 | Bi-quadratic | | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings The mesh must have been produced in the half-plane (X>0,Y) . | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS_FOURIER | SEG2 | Linear or | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | Bi-linear | | | | SEG3 | Quadratic, | | | | | Serendipity or | | | | | Bi-quadratic | | 2 Supported loadings The available loadings are the following: - 'FORCE_CONTOUR' Makes it possible to apply linear forces on the edge of a 2D domain. - 'FORCE_INTERNE' Makes it possible to apply body forces. - 'PESANTEUR' Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. - 'PRES_REP' Makes it possible to apply a pressure to a continuum domain. - 'ROTATION' Makes it possible to define a rotation speed and the direction of the rotation vector. 3 Non-linear possibilities No non-linear possibility exists; this modelling can be used only with MECA_STATIQUE or by a manual assembly. 4 Examples of implementation: test cases Linear statics - HSLV304A V7.14.304: Static analysis of a cylinder subjected to a thermal loading decomposable into 2 harmonics. - SSLV303A V3.04.303: Static analysis of a clamped cylinder under its self-weight and subjected to an internal pressure. - SSLV139A V3.04.139: Buckling of a circular plate subjected to a compressive force uniformly distributed on its contour.

u3.13.03 Modellings 2D_FLUIDE, 2D_FLUI_STRU, AXIS_FLUIDE, AXIS_FLUI_STRU u3.13.03 Modellings 2D_FLUIDE, 2D_FLUI_STRU, AXIS_FLUIDE, AXIS_FLUI_STRU Summary: This document describes, for the modellings 2D_FLUIDE, 2D_FLUI_STRU, AXIS_FLUIDE, AXIS_FLUI_STRU: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the related support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. At present, taking the free surface into account is not developed. The modellings AXIS_FLUIDE (elements in a plane) and AXIS_FLUI_STRU (1D fluid-structure interaction elements) correspond to the axisymmetric formulation, under the linear assumption, of the coupled problem allowing the study of the vibratory behaviour of a structure in the presence of a non-viscous, compressible fluid R4.02.01. U4.51.11). 4 Examples of implementation: test cases 1. 2D_FLUIDE FDLV111B V8.01.111 : Analysis of the absorption of a pressure wave created by a piston, in a fluid column. 1. u3.13.05 Modellings AXIS_SI, D_PLAN_SI, C_PLAN_SI u3.13.05 Modellings AXIS_SI, D_PLAN_SI, C_PLAN_SI Summary: The modellings AXIS_SI, D_PLAN_SI, C_PLAN_SI (Phenomenon: mechanical) correspond to finite elements whose support mesh cells are surface mesh cells. The suffix _SI means: Under-integrated: the integration of the terms relating to the constitutive laws is carried out in a reduced manner (Gauss-point scheme of lower order than the modelling with full integration). The modelling assumptions are the following: - AXIS_SI for axisymmetry (Fourier mode 0) about the Y axis, - D_PLAN_SI for the plane strains, - C_PLAN_SI for the plane stresses. u3.13.07 Modellings AXIS_INCO_UPG, D_PLAN_INCO_UPG u3.13.07 Modellings AXIS_INCO_UPG, D_PLAN_INCO_UPG Summary: This document describes, for the modellings AXIS_INCO_UPG, D_PLAN_INCO_UPG: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear capabilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. This modelling is based on finite elements adapted to the treatment of quasi-incompressible problems. It is indispensable in order to carry out limit analyses with the Norton-Hoff law and is also useful for studies presenting large plastic strains for which the classical displacement formulation proves insufficient (stress oscillation). The formulation used is a 3-field formulation: displacement-pressure-swelling R6.03.05, usable with all constitutive behaviours written in incremental form. The modellings are supported by plane mesh cells of degree 2 (TRIA6 and QUAD8). 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degrees of freedom at all the nodes | Degrees of freedom only at the vertex nodes | | --- | --- | --- | | D_PLAN_INCO_UPG | DX, DY | PRES( ), GONF | | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS_INCO_UPG | DX, DY | PRES( ), GONF | - no kinematic condition can be imposed on the degree of freedom PRES. 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices The support mesh cells of the finite elements may be triangles, or quadrangles (degree 2), for the modellings D_PLAN_INCO_UPG and AXIS_INCO_UPG. | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation in displacement | Interpolation in pressure and swelling | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | D_PLAN_INCO_UPG | TRIA6 | Quadratic | Linear | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | QUAD8 | Quadratic | Linear | | AXIS_INCO_UPG | TRIA6 | Quadratic | Linear | | | QUAD8 | Quadratic | Linear | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the surface loadings | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation in displacements | | --- | --- | --- | | D_PLAN_INCO_UPG and AXIS_INCO_UPG | SEG3 | Quadratic | | --- | --- | --- | 2 Supported loadings The available loadings are the following: - 'CONTACT' Makes it possible to define the zones subjected to contact conditions. Supported modellings: D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, AXIS_INCO_UPG - 'FORCE_CONTOUR' Makes it possible to apply line forces on the edge of a 2D domain. Supported modellings: D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, AXIS_INCO_UPG - 'FORCE_INTERNE' Makes it possible to apply volume forces. Supported modellings: D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, AXIS_INCO_UPG - 'PESANTEUR' Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. Supported modellings: D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, AXIS_INCO_UPG - 'PRES_REP' Makes it possible to apply a pressure to a continuum domain. Supported modellings: D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, AXIS_INCO_UPG 3 Non-linear capabilities Note that this modelling is accessible only from STAT_NON_LINE. It cannot be used with MECA_STATIQUE or by a manual assembly. 3.1 Constitutive laws All the constitutive laws usable on continuum mesh cells have a physical meaning for these modellings and can be assigned provided that they are accessible from COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE (see U4.51.11). One constitutive law is specific to this modelling (dedicated to the limit-load analysis, cf. [R7.07.01]): / 'NORTON_HOFF' Supported modellings: D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, AXIS_INCO_UPG 3.2 Strains The available strains, used in the constitutive relations under the keyword DEFORMATION for the operators STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, are (see U4.51.11): / 'PETIT' The strains used for the constitutive relation are the linearised strains. / 'SIMO_MIEHE' / 'GDEF_LOG' Makes it possible to carry out analyses in large plastic strains. 3.3 Newton method For the solution of the problem by the Newton-Raphson method, the elastic matrix is not available. One must therefore use, under the keyword NEWTON for the operators STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE (see U4.51.11): / PREDICTION = ‘TANGENTE’ The prediction phase is carried out with the tangent matrix. / MATRICE = ‘TANGENTE’ The matrix used for the global iterations is the tangent matrix. Note: The formulation used leads to non-positive matrices and the current solvers cannot always solve the linear systems associated with them satisfactorily. In the event of a convergence difficulty, it may therefore be useful to test the other solvers available in the code or the other renumbering methods (cf. U4.50.01). 4 Implementation examples: test cases - AXIS_INCO_UPG - Incompressible elasticity: SSLV130D V3.04.130: analysis of a hollow cylinder subjected to an internal pressure. The material has a Poisson's ratio equal to 0.4999. - Example of limit analysis: SSNV146A V6.04.146: tank with a torispherical head - D_PLAN_INCO_UPG - Elastoplastic material: SSNP123B V6.03.123: Analysis of a notched rectangular plate made of an elastoplastic material with isotropic hardening which is subjected to tension at its ends. - Example of limit analysis: SSNV124A V6.04.146: limit-load analysis of a rectangular plate

u3.13.09 Modellings 2D_DIS_T and 2D_DIS_TR u3.13.09 Modellings 2D_DIS_T and 2D_DIS_TR Summary: This document describes, for the modellings 2D_DIS_T, 2D_DIS_TR (see R5.03.17): - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear capabilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. The modelling 2D_DIS_T allows the representation of discrete translation elements with one or two nodes. The modelling 2D_DIS_TR allows the representation of discrete translation and rotation elements with one or two nodes. They are usable for two-dimensional problems in linear or non-linear mechanical analysis. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom The discretisation degrees of freedom are, at each node of the support mesh cell, the two translational displacement components and the rotation. | Finite element | Degrees of freedom (at each vertex node) | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2D_DIS_T | DX | DY | | | | | | 2D_DIS_TR | DX | DY | DRZ | | | | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices The support mesh cells of the discrete elements, in displacement formulation, are two-node segments SEG2 or point mesh cells POI1 coincident with a node: | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2D_DIS_T | POI1 | MECA_2D_DIS_T_N | | | | SEG2 | MECA_2D_DIS_T_L | | | 2D_DIS_TR | POI1 | MECA_2D_DIS_TR_N | | | | SEG2 | MECA_2D_DIS_TR_L | | As regards the POI1 mesh cells, the internal forces are computed from the differences between the degrees of freedom of the mesh cell and the fixed frame (as if this discrete node were attached to a fixed frame). For the SEG2 mesh cells, the forces are computed from the differences between the degrees of freedom carried by each of the 2 nodes. 2 Assignment of the characteristics For these discrete elements, it is necessary to assign geometrical characteristics which are complementary to the mesh data. The definition of these data is carried out with the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM associated with the following factor keywords: - DISCRET Makes it possible to define and assign the values of the stiffness, mass or damping matrices. Supported modellings: 2D_DIS_T, 2D_DIS_TR - ORIENTATION Makes it possible to define and assign a local frame. Supported modellings: 2D_DIS_T, 2D_DIS_TR 3 Supported loadings The supported loading is the following: - 'PESANTEUR' Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. Supported modellings: 2D_DIS_T, 2D_DIS_TR 4 Non-linear capabilities All the modellings 2D_DIS_ are usable with STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE. In this case one must define a material with DEFI_MATERIAU. 4.1 Constitutive law The constitutive laws specific to these modellings, usable under COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, are the following (see U4.51.11): / 'DIS_GOUJ2E_ELAS' Supported modelling: All / 'DIS_GOUJ2E_PLAS' Supported modelling: All / 'ELAS' Supported modellings: All In addition to the assignment of the characteristics (AFFE_CARA_ELEM), the use of the modellings DIS_T and DIS_TR with STAT_NON_LINE/DYNA_NON_LINE requires material characteristics to be defined (AFFE_MATERIAU). 4.2 Strains The available strains, used in the constitutive relations under the keyword DEFORMATION for the operators STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, are (see U4.51.11): / 'PETIT' The strains used for the constitutive relation are the linearised strains computed on the initial geometry. Supported modelling: All / 'PETIT_REAC' The strains used in the incremental constitutive relation are the linearised strains computed on the updated geometry. Supported modelling: All 5 Implementation examples: test cases - 2D_DIS_T - Linear statics - SSLL108A V3.01.108: Analysis of the response of a bar, modelled by 10 discrete elements (SEG2 mesh cells) subjected to a tensile loading. - Non-linear statics - ZZZZ120A: Analysis of a stud-flange assembly without the upper flange, with an elastoplastic Von Mises constitutive law representing the local behaviour of a thread of a stud in a threaded assembly. - Linear dynamics - SDLD02E V2.01.002: Computation of the vibration frequencies and of the associated modes of a mechanical structure composed of masses and springs. - Non-linear dynamics - SDNV104A: Dynamic response of a rigid friction pad subjected to a pressure and to a restoring force. - 2D_DIS_TR - Linear dynamics - SDLD02F V2.01.002: Computation of the vibration frequencies and of the associated modes of a mechanical structure composed of masses and springs.

u3.13.14 Modellings x_JOINT, x_ELDI, x_INTERFACE and x_INTERFACE_S u3.13.14 Modellings x_JOINT, x_ELDI, x_INTERFACE and x_INTERFACE_S Summary: This document describes, for the modellings PLAN_JOINT, AXIS_JOINT, 3D_JOINT, PLAN_ELDI, AXIS_ELDI, PLAN_INTERFACE, AXIS_INTERFACE, 3D_INTERFACE, PLAN_INTERFACE_S, AXIS_INTERFACE_S and 3D_INTERFACE_S, the following points: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the non-linear capabilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. The modellings of JOINT type (Phenomenon: mechanics) correspond to joint finite elements. They are based on a penalty formulation, and make it possible to model the opening of a crack. Their geometrical supports are degenerate finite elements, whose nodes are coincident in pairs (QUAD4, HEXA8 and PENTA6). These finite elements can support the constitutive laws CZM_EXP_REG and CZM_LIN_REG (cohesive laws: doc [R7.02.11]). In addition, the elements PLAN_JOINT, AXIS_JOINT support the constitutive law JOINT_BA (steel–concrete bond: doc [R7.01.21]). The modellings PLAN_ELDI and AXIS_ELDI (Phenomenon: mechanics) correspond to elements with an internal discontinuity. Their geometrical supports are volume elements (QUAD4) crossed by a discontinuity. They also make it possible to model the opening of a crack. Such finite elements can support the constitutive law: CZM_EXP (cohesive law: see doc R7.02.14). The modellings PLAN_INTERFACE, AXIS_INTERFACE, 3D_INTERFACE, PLAN_INTERFACE_S, AXIS_INTERFACE_S and 3D_INTERFACE_S (Phenomenon: mechanics) correspond to mixed interface finite elements, based on an augmented-Lagrangian type formulation. Their geometrical supports are degenerate finite elements (QUAD8, HEXA20 and PENTA15). Such elements can support the cohesive laws CZM_OUV_MIX, CZM_EXP_MIX, CZM_TAC_MIX, CZM_FAT_MIX, CZM_TRA_MIX and CZM_LAB_MIX (see doc [R7.02.11] and R3.06.13). In what follows, the characters 'XXX' may be replaced by 'PLAN’ or 'AXIS’. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degrees of freedom on each node | | --- | --- | | XXX_JOINT | DX: displacement along X | | --- | --- | | | DY: displacement along Y | | 3D_JOINT | DX: displacement along X | | | DY: displacement along Y | | | DZ: displacement along Z | | XXX_ELDI | DX: displacement along X | | | DY: displacement along Y | | XXX_INTERFACE and XXX_INTERFACE_S | DX: displacement along X or SIGN Lagrange multiplier | | --- | --- | | | DY: displacement along Y or SITX: Lagrange multiplier | | 3D_INTERFACE and 3D_INTERFACE_S | DX: displacement along X or SIGN Lagrange multiplier | | | DY: displacement along Y or SITX: Lagrange multiplier | | | DZ: displacement along Z or SITY: Lagrange multiplier | For the location of the displacement and Lagrange degrees of freedom for the modellings of INTERFACE type, see doc R3.06.13. 1.2 Support mesh cell The support mesh cells of the finite elements are quadrangles, hexahedra or pentahedra. u3.14.02 Modellings 3D_FLUIDE, FLUI_STRU, 2D_FLUI_PESA u3.14.02 Modellings 3D_FLUIDE, FLUI_STRU, 2D_FLUI_PESA Summary: This document describes, for the modellings 3D_FLUIDE, FLUI_STRU, 2D_FLUI_PESA: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear capabilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. The modellings 3D_FLUIDE (volume elements) and FLUI_STRU (2D fluid-structure interaction elements) correspond to the linear formulation of the coupled problem allowing the study of the vibratory behaviour of a structure in the presence of an inviscid, compressible fluid R4.04.01. At the nodes there will therefore be continuity of the fluid displacement potential PHI on the surface and in the fluid volume. 1.2 Support mesh cells of the stiffness matrices | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 3D_FLUIDE | TETRA4 | MEFL_TETRA4 | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | TETRA10 | MEFL_TETRA10 | | | | PENTA6 | MEFL_PENTA6 | | | | PENTA15 | MEFL_PENTA15 | | | | HEXA8 | MEFL_HEXA8 | | | | HEXA20 | MEFL_HEXA20 | | | | HEXA27 | MEFL_HEXA27 | | | FLUI_STRU | TRIA3 | MEFS_FACE3 | | | | TRIA6 | MEFS_FACE6 | | | | QUAD4 | MEFS_FACE4 | | | | QUAD8 | MEFS_FACE8 | | | | QUAD9 | MEFS_FACE9 | | | 2D_FLUI_PESA | TRIA3 | MEFP_FACE3 | | | | TRIA6 | MEFP_FACE6 | | | | QUAD4 | MEFP_FACE4 | | | | QUAD8 | MEFP_FACE8 | | | | QUAD9 | MEFP_FACE9 | | Note 1: Coupling with a structure meshed with elements COQUE_3D requires the fluid-structure interface to be meshed with elements QUAD8 (and not QUAD9 ). The bulk fluid domain is therefore meshed with HEXA20 (and not HEXA27 ). Indeed, the fluid-structure coupling is carried out on the displacement degrees of freedom only, for the solid. > Note 2: It is imperative that the outward normal to the fluid domain always be oriented from the fluid towards the structure, for all fluid-structure interface modellings, in particular FLUI_STRU . 1.3 Support mesh cells of the loadings | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 3D_FLUIDE | TRIA3 | MEFL_FACE3 | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | TRIA6 | MEFL_FACE6 | | | | QUAD4 | MEFL_FACE4 | | | | QUAD8 | MEFL_FACE8 | | | | QUAD9 | MEFL_FACE9 | | | 2D_FLUI_PESA | TRIA3 | MEFP_FACE3 | | | | TRIA6 | MEFP_FACE6 | | | | QUAD4 | MEFP_FACE4 | | | | QUAD8 | MEFP_FACE8 | | | | QUAD9 | MEFP_FACE9 | | 2 Supported loadings The available loadings are the following: PESANTEUR Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. u3.14.06 Modelling 3D_INCO_UPG u3.14.06 Modelling 3D_INCO_UPG Summary: This document describes, for the modelling 3D_INCO_UPG: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the supported constitutive laws and loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modelling. This modelling is based on finite elements suited to the treatment of quasi-incompressible problems. It is indispensable for carrying out limit analyses with the Norton-Hoff law and is also useful for studies presenting high plastic strains for which the classical displacement formulation proves insufficient (oscillation of the stresses). The formulation used is a 3-field formulation: displacement-pressure-swelling R6.03.05, usable with all the constitutive behaviours written in incremental form and in elasticity. The modelling 3D_INCO_UPG has volume support mesh cells and accepts the TETRA10, the HEXA20, and the PENTA15. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degree of freedom at all the nodes | Degree of freedom only at the vertex nodes | | --- | --- | --- | | 3D | DX, DY, DZ | PRES( ), GONF | | --- | --- | --- | - No kinematic condition can be imposed on the degree of freedom PRES. 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices For the modelling 3D, the support mesh cells of the finite elements may be tetrahedra, hexahedra or prisms. | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation in displacements | Interpolation in pressure and swelling | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 3D | TETRA10 | Quadratic | Linear | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | HEXA20 | Quadratic | Linear | | | PENTA15 | Quadratic | Linear | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the surface loadings | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation in displacements | | --- | --- | --- | | 3D | TRIA6 | Quadratic | | --- | --- | --- | | | QUAD8 | Quadratic | 2 Supported loadings The loadings available under AFFE_CHAR_MECA are the following: - 'FORCE_ARETE' Makes it possible to apply line forces to an edge of a volume element. - 'FORCE_FACE' Makes it possible to apply surface forces on a face of a volume element. - 'FORCE_INTERNE' Makes it possible to apply body forces. - 'PESANTEUR' Makes it possible to apply a gravity-type loading. - 'PRES_REP' Makes it possible to apply a pressure to a domain of a continuous medium. 3 Non-linear possibilities 3.1 Constitutive laws All the constitutive laws usable on mesh cells of continuous media have a physical meaning for these modellings and can be assigned from the moment when they are accessible from COMPORTEMENT in STAT_NON_LINE (Cf. U4.51.11). Or in MECA_STATIQUE (linear elastic in small strains). Let us point out that one constitutive law is specific to this modelling (dedicated to the limit-load analysis, cf. R7.07.01): / 'NORTON_HOFF' 3.2 Strains The strains available, used in the constitutive relations under the keyword DEFORMATION for the operators STAT_NON_LINE, DYNA_NON_LINE and CALCUL, are (Cf. U4.51.11): / 'PETIT' The strains used for the constitutive relation are the linearised strains. / 'SIMO_MIEHE' 'GDEF_LOG' Makes it possible to carry out analyses in large plastic strains. In MECA_STATIQUE, one is in small-strain elasticity. 3.3 Newton method For the solution of the problem by the Newton-Raphson method in the non-linear operators, the elastic matrix is not available. One must therefore use, under the keyword NEWTON for the operators STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE (Cf. U4.51.11): / PREDICTION = ‘TANGENTE’ The prediction phase is carried out with the tangent matrix. / MATRICE = ‘TANGENTE’ The matrix used for the global iterations is the tangent matrix. Note: The formulation used leads to non-positive matrices and the current solvers are not always able to solve properly the linear systems which are associated with them. In the event of a convergence difficulty, it may therefore be useful to test the other solvers available in the code or the other renumbering methods (cf. U4.50.01). 4 Examples of implementation: test cases - Small strains: - SSLV130A V3.04.130: Analysis of an incompressible hollow cylinder, subjected to an internal pressure. - Large strains: - SSNV112A V6.04.112: Analysis of an incompressible hollow cylinder in large strains, subjected to an internal radial displacement. - Limit analysis: - SSNV124B V6.04.124: Determination of the limit load of a cube subjected to loadings on its edges.

The modelling 3D_ABSO (Phenomenon: mechanics) corresponds to finite elements whose support mesh cells are surface mesh cells. u3.22.01 Modellings COQUE, COQUE_PLAN, COQUE_AXIS - Phenomenon THERMIQUE u3.22.01 Modellings COQUE, COQUE_PLAN, COQUE_AXIS - Phenomenon THERMIQUE Summary: This document describes, for the thermal modellings of the axisymmetric and plane elements: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the supported loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. The COQUE modelling of the Phenomenon THERMIQUE R3.11.01 can be used to treat the heat equations in media with a middle surface in linear thermal analysis. One can use it as the first analysis of a thermomechanical chaining with the corresponding mechanical elements. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom The degrees of freedom are the temperatures TEMP (temperature on the middle surface of the shell), TEMP_INF (temperature on the lower surface of the shell), and TEMP_SUP (temperature on the upper surface of the shell). 1.2 Support mesh cells of the stiffness matrices | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | Remarks | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE | TRIA3 | THCOTR3 | nodes with 3 coordinates x , y , z | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | TRIA6 | THCOTR6 | | | | TRIA7 | THCOTR7 | | | | QUAD4 | THCOQU4 | | | | QUAD8 | THCOQU8 | | | | QUAD9 | THCOQU9 | | | COQUE_PLAN | SEG3 | THCPSE3 | nodes with 2 coordinates x , y | | COQUE_AXIS | SEG3 | THCASE3 | | For the THCOTRi, only the 3 vertices are used to define the local geometry (tangent plane, normal). For the THCOQUi, one considers that the element is plane and that its tangent plane is defined by default by 3 of the 4 vertices of the element. 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings All the loadings applicable to the facets of the shell elements are treated by direct discretisation on the support mesh cell of the element in temperature formulation. No loading support mesh cell is therefore necessary for the faces of the shell elements. For the loadings applicable on the edges of the shell or plate elements of the -shell- modelling, a support mesh cell of type SEG2 or SEG3 must be used. | Modelling | Mesh cell | Finite element | Remarks | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE | SEG2 | THCOSE2 | with TRIA3 and QUAD4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COQUE | SEG3 | THCOSE3 | with TRIA6 or TRIA7 and QUAD8 or QUAD9 | For the imposed temperatures, the support mesh cells are mesh cells reduced to a point. 2 Assignment of the characteristics For these thermal structural elements, it is necessary to assign geometric characteristics which are complementary to the mesh data. The definition of these data is carried out with the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM associated with the following factor keyword: - COQUE Makes it possible to define and to assign the thickness on the mesh cells. 3 Supported loadings The loadings available are the following: - FLUX_REP Makes it possible to apply normal fluxes to faces of shell elements on the faces ±. Supported modellings: COQUE, COQUE_PLAN, COQUE_AXIS - ECHANGE Makes it possible to apply exchange conditions with an external temperature to shell faces on the upper and lower faces. Supported modellings: COQUE, COQUE_PLAN, COQUE_AXIS 4 Non-linear possibilities None. 5 Transient possibilities Only the COQUE modelling makes it possible to treat transient thermal problems. 6 Examples of implementation: test case - COQUE - Linear steady thermal analysis HPLA100C V7.01.100: Analysis of a heavy thermoelastic hollow cylinder in uniform rotation. In this modelling, one carries out a chained thermoelastic analysis and a thermoelastoplastic analysis without plastic evolution. TPLS100A V4.03.100: Steady thermal analysis of an infinite plate subjected to a pair of antisymmetric heat fluxes on its two half-faces. - Linear transient thermal analysis TTLL01M V4.21.001: Linear transient thermal analysis of an infinite wall subjected to a thermal shock. - COQUE_PLAN - Linear steady thermal analysis HPLA100B V7.01.100: Analysis of a heavy thermoelastic hollow cylinder in uniform rotation. In this modelling, one carries out a chained thermoelastic analysis and a thermoelastoplastic analysis without plastic evolution. TPLS100B V4.03.100: Steady thermal analysis of an infinite plate subjected to a pair of antisymmetric heat fluxes on its two half-faces.

u3.23.01 Modellings AXIS, PLAN, AXIS_DIAG and PLAN_DIAG - Phenomenon THERMIQUE u3.23.01 Modellings AXIS, PLAN, AXIS_DIAG and PLAN_DIAG - Phenomenon THERMIQUE Summary: This document describes, for the thermal modellings of the axisymmetric and plane elements: - the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements which support the modelling, - the associated support mesh cells, - the supported materials and loadings, - the non-linear possibilities, - the test cases implementing the modellings. The axisymmetric and plane modellings (Phenomenon: THERMIQUE) correspond to finite elements whose support mesh cells are surface mesh cells. The modellings AXIS_DIAG and PLAN_DIAG cover the same possibilities as AXIS and PLAN and differ from them only for a thermal analysis in which the thermal mass matrix is then diagonalised. 1 Discretisation 1.1 Degrees of freedom | Modelling | Degrees of freedom (at each vertex node) | | --- | --- | | AXIS, AXIS_DIAG, PLAN, PLAN_DIAG | TEMP: corresponds to the temperature | | --- | --- | 1.2 Support mesh cell of the stiffness matrices The support mesh cells of the finite elements may be triangles or quadrilaterals. The elements are isoparametric. | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation | Remarks | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS(_DIAG) - PLAN(_DIAG) | TRIA3 | Linear | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS(_DIAG) - PLAN(_DIAG) | QUAD4 | Linear | | | AXIS - PLAN | TRIA6 | Quadratic | | | AXIS - PLAN | TRIA10 | Cubic | | | AXIS - PLAN | QUAD8 | Serendip | | | AXIS - PLAN | QUAD9 | Quadratic | | | AXIS - PLAN | QUAD12 | Cubic Serendip | | 1.3 Support mesh cell of the loadings | Modelling | Mesh cell | Interpolation | Remarks | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS(_DIAG) - PLAN(_DIAG) | SEG2 | Linear | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AXIS - PLAN | SEG3 | Quadratic | | | AXIS - PLAN | SEG4 | Cubic | | 2 Supported loadings The loadings available are the following: - SOURCE Makes it possible to apply volumetric sources to a 2D domain. Supported modellings: AXIS(_DIAG), PLAN(_DIAG) - FLUX_REP Makes it possible to apply normal fluxes to edges of 2D elements. Supported modellings: AXIS(_DIAG), PLAN(_DIAG) - ECHANGE Makes it possible to apply exchange conditions with an external temperature to edges of 2D elements. Supported modellings: AXIS(_DIAG), PLAN(_DIAG) - ECHANGE_PAROI Makes it possible to apply exchange conditions between two walls. Supported modellings: AXIS(_DIAG), PLAN(_DIAG) - GRAD_TEMP_EPSI Makes it possible to apply an "initial" temperature gradient assumed to be uniform in the element. Supported modellings: AXIS(_DIAG), PLAN(_DIAG) - CONVECTION Makes it possible to take into account the heat-transport terms by convection, for THER_NON_LINE_MO only. Supported modellings: AXIS, PLAN - RAYONNEMENT Makes it possible to take into account the flux radiated to infinity. Supported modellings: AXIS(_DIAG), PLAN(_DIAG) 3 Non-linear possibilities Two operators are available for the study of non-linear behaviours: - THER_NON_LINE U4.54.02: this operator makes it possible, in steady state or in transient regime, to solve the problems of: - Standard non-linear thermal analysis: material depending on the temperature, boundary conditions (radiation and non-linear imposed flux), - Non-linear thermal analysis with analysis of the hydration of the concrete, - Drying of the concrete. - THER_NON_LINE_MO U4.54.03: this operator makes it possible to solve the steady heat equation in a moving reference frame linked to a loading and moving in a given direction and at a given speed. 4 Examples of implementation: test cases 4.1 Thermal - AXIS - Linear steady thermal analysis TPLA07A V4.01.007: Thermal analysis of an orthotropic hollow cylinder subjected to various boundary conditions (imposed flux, convection, linear variation of the external temperatures). - Non-linear steady thermal analysis TPNA01A V4.41.001: Thermal analysis of a hollow cylinder subjected to a convective exchange on the inner wall and to radiation to infinity on the outer wall. - Linear transient thermal analysis TTLV01B V4.25.001: Linear transient thermal analysis of a solid sphere subjected to a heat exchange by convection. - Non-linear transient thermal analysis TTNA200A: non-regression test case - PLAN - Linear steady thermal analysis TPLL100B V4.02.100: Thermal analysis of an anisotropic plane wall subjected to an imposed temperature and to a flux. - Non-linear steady thermal analysis TPNL300A V4.42.300: One-dimensional thermal analysis of a wall subjected to an imposed temperature on the inner wall and to an exchange by radiation on the outer wall (NAFEMS test). - Linear transient thermal analysis TTLP100B V4.23.100: Computation of the linear transient thermal response of two plates separated by a gap in which a heat transfer takes place between the walls. - Non-linear transient thermal analysis TTNL02A V4.22.002: Simulation of a liquid/solid phase change by introducing, by means of the volumetric enthalpy, the latent heat of fusion. - Non-linear steady thermal analysis with a moving load TPLV102A V4.04.102: Heat transport by convection and by conduction in a square cavity. - AXIS_DIAG - Linear transient thermal analysis TTLV100A V4.25.100: Linear transient thermal analysis of a pipe assumed to be infinite, in which one imposes a cold thermal shock by means of an exchange boundary condition. - PLAN_DIAG - Linear transient thermal analysis TTLL100A V4.21.100: Linear transient thermal analysis of an infinite plane wall on which one imposes a cold thermal shock by means of an exchange boundary condition. - Non-linear transient thermal analysis TTNL02C V4.22.002: Simulation of a liquid/solid phase change by introducing, by means of the volumetric enthalpy, the latent heat of fusion. 4.2 Hydration - AXIS TTNL03B V4.22.003: simulation of an adiabatic test: analysis of the thermo-hydrating behaviour of a sample of fresh concrete immersed in a calorimeter, the setting taking place with release of heat. 4.3 Drying - AXIS HSNA102A V7.20.102: Validation of the analysis of the drying of concrete; this is an axisymmetric test case in which the water concentration is applied directly on the outer wall. - AXIS_DIAG HSNA102D V7.20.102: Validation of the analysis of the drying of concrete; this is an axisymmetric test case in which the water concentration is applied directly on the outer wall.
