u4.01.00 How to read the command documentation u4.01.00 How to read the command documentation Summary: This note is a reading guide for booklets U4 and U7 of the User's manual. It explains in particular the meaning of the meta-characters and of the typographical conventions used to describe the syntax of the commands. All the examples given here are given for illustration and do not replace the complete description of the commands given in booklets U4 and U7. Table of contents 1 Reminders on the syntax of the Code_Aster commands The command language and its supervisor are completely described in document U1.03.01. A few points on the syntax of the Code_Aster commands are recalled here. In Code_Aster , the generic term commands covers both the operators , the procedures and the macro-commands of the command language. An operator supplies a typed produced concept (typed by the operator) and named by the user. A procedure does not generate a produced concept; it carries out actions such as printouts or resource allocations. In the example below, the vocabulary used in the description of the commands is recalled. Terminology Aster An operand is therefore the whole formed by a keyword and its argument. However, in the command documentation, the operands of an operator or of a procedure are often designated by the name of their keyword. For example: RHO, a simple keyword, or ELAS, a factor keyword. The term produced concept is generic for all the operators; it is the result of the work of the operator. Here, in the DEFI_MATERIAU example, the data structure of type mater (material), named beton by the user, has been created. It groups the names (keywords E, NU, RHO) and the values (arguments 3.4E10, 0.25, 2500.) of the elastic mechanical characteristics (factor keyword ELAS) of the material. The term concept of result type applies to the outputs of the analysis operators, that is to say fields of physical quantities (displacements, temperatures, stresses, forces, modes, etc.) on the nodes or on the mesh cells at different time instants or for different frequencies. The result concept generally has subtypes . 2 Standard layout of the user's documents for the commands Each document presenting a command contains the following chapters: - Purpose, - Syntax, - Operands, - Examples (where applicable). This presentation allows the user to find in a single document all the knowledge required to use a command. 3 Purpose paragraph The functionality fulfilled by the command (actions carried out) is stated. The types of the concepts expected on input and of the produced concept are also specified, together with the particular features of the command. This paragraph is also displayed by the search engines; it therefore contains only text, without equations or formulae. Example: operator STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03 Purpose : Compute the quasi-static mechanical evolution of a structure in the non-linear regime. The non-linearity is related either to the constitutive behaviour of the material (for example plastic), or to the geometry (for example in large displacements). For details on the solution method used, refer to the reference documentation R5.03.01. The evolution can be studied in several successive jobs (re-entrant concept), either as a continuation (the last computed time instant is the initial time instant of the next analysis), or as a recovery starting from an earlier time instant. If the time required to carry out the run is not sufficient, the program stops, but the results already computed are saved if a database has been defined in the user's study profile. It produces a data structure of type evol_noli. 4 Syntax paragraph This paragraph gives the full set of operands of the command. For each operand, meta-characters and indentations specific to the typographical presentation of the commands are used to specify (see the example of the operator AFFE_MATERIAU): - the name of the operator, - the names of the keywords, - the symbolic user names of the produced concept and of the arguments of the keywords, - whether the operands are mandatory or optional (status), - the alternatives in the choice of the operands, - the types of the arguments expected by the keywords, - the default values taken by the arguments in the case of optional operands, - the type of the produced concept, when it is an operator. Symbolic name of the produced concept Type of the produced concept Name of the operator Symbolic name of the argument _mater] = AFFE_MATERIAU cham [ chm Imposed argument of text type [maillage] MAILLAGE = ma, ♦ ( ♦ ♦ Meta-character "mandatory" / TOUT= ‘OUI’, AFFE =_F ( , [l_maille] lma / MAILLE= / GROUP_MA= [l_gr_maille] , lgma Expected user concept type [mater] MATER = mat, ♦ Meta-character "optional" ◊ TEMP_REF = / 0., [DEFAUT] / [R] , tref Default argument Expected argument type ) Meta-character "alternative" ) ; Presentation of the (partial) syntax of the operator AFFE_MATERIAU 4.1 Meta-characters for the status of operands ( ♦ ◊ / | ) Four meta-characters are used to indicate the status of the operands. Status of the operands means here whether they are declared as mandatory or optional, and the nature of the alternatives in the choice of the operands. These meta-characters are not part of the command language. They have only a documentary presentation function and must therefore not be used when writing the command file. 4.1.1 Mandatory or optional operands They are identified by a black or white lozenge at the head. | ♦ | black lozenge: it is mandatory to declare in the command the operand or operands which follow this sign. | | --- | --- | | ◊ | white lozenge: the declaration of the operand or operands which follow this sign is optional. If the operand is absent, the command will where appropriate assign one or more default values. | | Example : operator DEFI_LIST_ENTI | (definition of a list of strictly increasing integers whose values are evenly spaced) | | --- | --- | li = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( ♦ DEBUT = deb , ◊ INTERVALLE = _F ( ♦ JUSQU_A = if , ♦ PAS = ipas, ) ) - It is mandatory to declare the operand identified by the keyword DEBUT and to supply deb, which is the first integer of the list to be built. - It is not mandatory to declare the operand identified by the factor keyword INTERVALLE. In that case the list of integers will consist of a single integer of value deb (this is stated in the description of the operands). - If the operand INTERVALLE is declared, then it is mandatory to declare the operand JUSQU_A, which specifies the integer end if of the interval to be subdivided with a constant step, and the operand PAS, which indicates the step ipas used to subdivide the interval. 4.1.2 Alternatives in the choice of the operands They are identified by the presence, at the head of each choice of the alternative, of: - a / (slash): exclusive alternative, a single choice among those proposed, - a | (pipe, semicolon): non-exclusive alternative, one or more choices among those proposed. | Example of an exclusive alternative: operator AFFE_MODELE | (assignment of the finite-element type over all or part of a mesh). | | --- | --- | mo = AFFE_MODELE ( ♦ MAILLAGE = ma ♦ AFFE = _F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / MAILLE = mail , [l_maille] / NOEUD = noeu , [l_noeud] / GROUP_MA = g_mail , [l_gr_maille] / GROUP_NO = g_noeu , [l_gr_noeud] ............... ) ) ; In the operand AFFE (mandatory) one must indicate where, on the mesh, the finite-element type specified in the operands PHENOMENE and MODELISATION of the same command will be assigned: - either over the whole mesh (TOUT), - or on certain mesh cells (MAILLE), - or on certain nodes (NOEUD), - or on certain mesh-cell groups (GROUP_MA), - or on certain node groups (GROUP_NO). Example of a non-exclusive alternative: | operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA operand DDL_IMPO | (assignment of imposed displacements on degrees of freedom). | | --- | --- | DDL_IMPO = _F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / NOEUD = lno , [l_noeud] / GROUP_NO= lgno, [l_gr_noeud] / MAILLE = lma , [l_maille] / GROUP_MA= lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ | DX = ux , [R] | DY = uy , [R] | DZ = uz , [R] | DRX = x , [R] | DRY = y , [R] | DRZ = z , [R] | GRX = g , [R] | PRES= p , [R] | PHI = , [R] | TEMP= T , [R] | PRE1= pr1 , [R] | PRE2= pr2 , [R] ) In this operator, one must specify, as a mandatory item: - the domain of application on the mesh: everywhere (TOUT), on certain nodes (NOEUD) or on certain node groups (GROUP_NO), - on which degrees of freedom, with which values imposed by the user. The meta-character | indicates that the user may impose a displacement value on one (the symbol ♦ indicates that at least one is required) or several of the degrees of freedom (DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ, GRX, PRES, PHI, TEMP, PRE1, PRE2) of the nodes designated beforehand. 4.1.3 Combinations of the meta-characters for the choice of the operands These meta-characters can be combined to illustrate the multiplicity of choices in certain commands. Example : command DEFI_MATERIAU (definition of a material by its constitutive behaviour properties) For a thermomechanical study, one needs to define a material which has both mechanical characteristics (ELAS) and thermal characteristics (THER), hence the use of the pipe: | But within each choice, one is obliged to choose whether the material properties are dependent (_FO) or not on the temperature, hence the use of the slash: / ; see below: ma = DEFI_MATERIAU ( | /ELAS = _F ( ♦ E = yg, ♦ NU = nu, ◊ RHO = rho, ◊ ALPHA = dil, ) …… /ELAS_FO =_F( ♦ E = f1, ♦ NU = f2, ◊ RHO = f3, ◊ ALPHA = f4, ) | /THER = _F ( ♦ RHO_CP = cp, ♦ LAMBDA = la, ) …… /THER_FO =_F( ♦ RHO_CP = g1, ♦ LAMBDA = g2, ) …… ); 4.2 Meta-characters for the type of a concept or of an argument Like the meta-characters for the status of operands, the brackets [ ] and the asterisk are not part of the command language. They have only a documentary presentation function. 4.2.1 Types of concepts or of arguments [ ] They enclose the type of the produced concepts as well as the type of the arguments. Example : command AFFE_MODELE (assignment of the finite elements on the mesh cells of a mesh) mo [modele] = AFFE_MODELE ( ♦ MAILLAGE = ma, [maillage] ♦ AFFE =_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / MAILLE = mail, [l_maille] .................... ) In the example above, it is therefore specified that the concept produced by AFFE_MODELE is of type modele and that the concept expected as the argument of the keyword MAILLE must be of type l_maille (i.e. a list of mesh cells). 4.2.2 Type of the produced concept [ ] This meta-character indicates that the type of the produced concept, or the subtype of the produced concept of result type, depends on the types of the arguments of certain operands. In this case the various possibilities are written after the syntax of the command. Example: command CREA_CHAMP In this example, ch2 will be a field at the nodes, a map or a field by element according to the value of TYPE_CHAM. ch2 [ ] = CREA_CHAMP ( ♦ TYPE_CHAM = / ‘NOEU_xxxx’, [Kn] / ‘CART_xxxx’, / ‘ELGA_xxxx’, / ‘ELNO_xxxx’, / ‘ELEM_xxxx’, ) Si TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_TEMP_R' alors [ ] = CHAM_NO_TEMP_R 'NOEU_DEPL_R' CHAM_NO_DEPL_R ... 'CART_TEMP_R' CARTE_TEMP_R 'CART_DEPL_R' CARTE_DEPL_R ... 4.3 Comments For certain complex commands such as AFFE_CARA_ELEM or DEFI_MATERIAU, for example, the comment character is used to comment on the alternatives of the operands. It has the same meaning as in the command language and is interpreted as such by the supervisor. Example for AFFE_CARA_ELEM: POUTRE=_F(♦ / MAILLE= lma, [l_maille] / GROUP_MA= lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ / SECTION= 'GENERALE', / # section constante ◊ CARA= | 'A' | 'IY' | 'IZ' liste des choix | 'AY' | 'AZ' possibles pour une | 'EY' | 'EZ' section constante | 'JX' | 'RY' | 'RZ' | 'RT', / # section variable ◊ CARA= | 'A1' | 'A2' | 'IY1' | 'IY2' | 'IZ1' | 'IZ2' liste des choix | 'AY1' | 'AY2' | 'AZ1' | 'AZ2' possibles pour une | 'EY1' | 'EY2' | 'EZ1' | 'EZ2' section variable | 'JX1' | 'JX2' | 'RY1' | 'RY2' | 'RZ1' | 'RZ2' | 'RT1' | 'RT2', ..... ) 4.4 Types of the arguments expected by the keywords The keywords of the operands expect arguments which, in general, fall into four classes: - values; a symbolic name then specifies the accepted computer type (real, integer, character string, etc.), - imposed texts; the text or texts ('OUI', 'HY1') are then indicated between quotes, - names of simple topological entities (node name, mesh-cell names, or lists of names), declared in the mesh file, or names of node groups or of mesh-cell groups, or lists of names of node groups or of mesh-cell groups, - names and lists of names of concepts produced by the operators. The table below gathers all the main types of arguments expected by the keywords: | [R] | real | 3 | | --- | --- | --- | | [l_R] | list of reals | (1., 3., 7.) | | [I] | integer | 7 | | [l_I] | list of integers | (9, 6, 1, 9) | | [C] | complex | RI 1.1, 7.8 or MP 10.,1.57 | | [l_C] | list of complexes | (RI 1.1, 7.), (RI 4.7, 9.) | | [TXM] | unconstrained text (TITRE name...) | ‘mon titre’ | | [Kn] | text of length less than or equal to n characters | ’INST’ | | [l_Kn] | list of texts of length less than or equal to n characters | (‘SIXX’, ‘SIYY’, ‘SIXY’) | | [noeud] | node name | N23 | | [l_noeud] | list of node names | (N23, N24, N25) | | [gr_noeud] | name of a node group | NBORD6 | | [l_gr_noeud] | list of names of node groups | (NBORD, NBASE, NBORD) | | [maille] | mesh-cell name | M34 | | [l_maille] | list of mesh-cell names | (M34, M35) | | [gr_maille] | name of a mesh-cell group | MPIQUAGE | | [l_gr_maille] | list of names of mesh-cell groups | (MSOM, MDROI, MGA) | | [type_concept] | type of concept (or of field) produced beforehand, generally with automatic checking of the type | monresu | | [l_type_concept] | list of user concept types | (resu1, resu2) | 4.5 Types of the concepts produced in Aster The meta-character for the choice of an exclusive alternative / is used to indicate the plurality of concepts expected behind a keyword. | Example: operator ASSE_MATRICE | (assembly of the elementary matrices contained in a list of concepts of type matr_elem_ .) | | --- | --- | ma [matr_asse_ ] = ASSE_MATRICE ( ♦ MATR_ELEM = lmel, / [l_matr_elem_DEPL_R] / [l_matr_elem_DEPL_C] / [l_matr_elem_TEMP_R] / [l_matr_elem_TEMP_C] / [l_matr_elem_PRES_R] / [l_matr_elem_PRES_C] ... ); simatr_elem [matr_elem_DEPL_R] alors [ ] DEPL_R [matr_elem_DEPL_C] DEPL_C [matr_elem_TEMP_R] TEMP_R [matr_elem_TEMP_C] TEMP_C [matr_elem_PRES_R] PRES_R [matr_elem_PRES_C] PRES_C In the example above, the concept expected as the argument of MATR_ELEM may be of different types, and the typing of the concept produced by the operator ASSE_MATRICE will depend (according to the rules stated above) on the type of the concept passed as an argument by the user. 5 Operands paragraph For each operand, the meaning of the operand for this command is described, together with the nature and the type of the arguments expected by the keywords, and the restrictions and difficulties of use. For example, in the documentation of the operator AFFE_MATERIAU, for the operand AFFE, an operand intended to specify on which topological entity or entities of the mesh named ma the material named mat produced by the operator DEFI_MATERIAU will be assigned, one will read: ♦ AFFE Factor keyword which makes it possible to assign different materials on “pieces” of the mesh. / TOUT= ‘OUI’, This keyword makes it possible to assign on all the mesh cells of the mesh. / GROUP_MA= lgma, This keyword makes it possible to assign on a list of mesh-cell groups of the mesh. / MAILLE= lma, This keyword makes it possible to assign on a list of mesh cells of the mesh. To each mesh-cell group (keyword GROUP_MA) or each list of mesh cells (keyword MAILLE), or again to the whole mesh (keyword TOUT), a material mat is assigned, which is a concept produced by one of the operators DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 or DEFI_COMPOSITE U4.42.03. If a mesh cell appears explicitly (or implicitly) in several occurrences of the factor keyword AFFE, the overloading rule is applied: it is the last assignment which prevails U2.01.08. 6 Verification / execution phases The Syntax paragraph of the user's documentation is the exact reflection of the catalogue of the command. This catalogue is a file which contains, written in the language of the supervisor, all the rules on the keywords: presence, exclusion, implication, content … The EFICAS editor uses this command catalogue and allows the user, if in the end the composed file is valid, to obtain a correct command set. On execution of the study, the Code_Aster supervisor reproduces the same task of syntactic verification: either globally for the whole file, or alternating with execution, command by command. In addition, during the actual execution of the commands (entered in the FORTRAN part of the source code), further checks may be made. These are constraints which cannot be managed at the level of the command language (equality of the cardinals of different lists …). 7 Typography and indentations For the readability of the documents relating to the commands, everything which relates to the syntax is printed in Courier 10-point type. The different types of functional elements (produced concept, keyword, factor keyword, argument) are distinguished by the use of upper case and lower case. In upper case: - names of the operators and of the procedures, - names of the keywords and of the factor keywords, - imposed arguments of text type (these are between 'quotes', as in the syntax of the commands). In lower case: - names of the produced concepts, - symbolic names of the arguments, - types of the produced concepts and of the arguments. In mixed lower case – upper case when the produced concept admits a subtype. The subtype appears in upper case, as does the FORTRAN type of the quantity of the subtype. The readability of the syntax is reinforced by the use of indentations. They are used to identify blocks of operands and to set off a group of operands under a factor keyword. They are also used to place the parentheses of one and the same block in vertical alignment. Example: ma [matr_asse_ ] = ASSE_MATRICE ( ♦ MATR_ELEM = lmel, / [l_matr_elem_DEPL_R] / [l_matr_elem_DEPL_C] / [l_matr_elem_TEMP_R] / [l_matr_elem_PRES_C] ♦ NUME_DDL = nu, [nume_ddl] ◊ CHAR_CINE = lcha, / [l_char_cine_meca] / [l_char_cine_ther] / [l_char_cine_acou] ◊ INFO = / 1, [DEFAUT] / 2, ); > if matr_elem [matr_elem_DEPL_R] then [ ] DEPL_R [matr_elem_DEPL_C] DEPL_C [matr_elem_TEMP_R] TEMP_R [matr_elem_PRES_C] PRES_C

u4.01.02 1 u4.01.02 New features and changes in the commands Organisation(s): EDF-R&D/AMA User's manual Booklet U4.0-: Use of the commands Document: U4.01.02 1 u4.01.02 New features and changes in the commands Summary: The purpose of this document is to give an overall view of the syntax changes and of the new possibilities of the Code_Aster commands between two stabilised versions. This update thus reports the changes introduced since version 6.3 of April 2002 and valid for version 6.4 of November 2002. For further details, consult the command documentation and the histor file of the corresponding sub-version (e.g.: [6.3.12], Development section of the site www.code-aster.org). The commands affected are listed in alphabetical order. 1 New features between versions 6.3 and 6.4 1.1 New commands 1.1.1 GENE_MATR_ALEA This command makes it possible to produce random symmetric positive-definite matrices from a mean matrix and an uncertainty level. Three probability distributions are available (cf. [6.3.12]). 1.1.2 GENE_VARI_ALEA Same purpose as the previous command, for real variables (cf. [6.3.12]). 1.1.3 LIRE_TABLE This new command makes it possible to re-read a table which has been printed by IMPR_TABLE (cf. [6.3.13]). 1.1.4 MACR_LIGN_COUPE This macro facilitates the post-processing of mechanical and thermal results by extracting the values of a field at the nodes on a cutting line (mesh of segments) (cf. [6.3.14]). 1.1.5 MACR_RECAL This macro makes it possible to carry out recalibration in Code_Aster : the macro determines the parameters of an analysis which best describe the tests (cf. [6.3.18]). 1.2 Modified commands 1.2.1 AFFE_CHAR_MECA LIAISON_UNIL_NO removed: - The functionalities are now available under the keyword CONTACT, with the exception of TRESCA friction, which is no longer available (cf. [6.3.17]). REAC_GEOM new, REAC_GEOM_INTE removed: - The keyword REAC_GEOM makes it possible to control the geometric updating of the contact algorithm; it takes the value SANS, AUTOMATIQUE or CONTROLE. In the latter case, the imposed number of updates NB_REAC_GEOM must be specified (cf. [6.3.10]). STOP_SINGULIER new: - This offers the possibility of continuing the solution even if a singular matrix is detected (the validity of the solution being conditional on the check of equilibrium) (cf. [6.3.16]). PROJECTION=’QUADRATIQUE’ new: - When the elements in contact are quadratic, this projection makes it possible to compute the gap exactly (cf. [6.3.12]). DIRE_APPA new: - For the continuous method, the user thus imposes the search direction for the pairing (cf. [6.3.14]). INTEGRATION=(’SIMPSON’,’SIMPSON1’,’SIMPSON2’) new possible values: - For the continuous method, this makes it possible to specify the type of integration required (cf. [6.3.14]). 1.2.2 AFFE_MODELE Modellings 2D_CONTACT, 3D_CONTACT removed: - These modellings were applied on the contact elements, which have been withdrawn (see also AFFE_CHAR_MECA, cf. [6.3.17]). Modellings CONT_DVP_2D, CONT_DVP_3D removed: - The user is no longer obliged to assign the modellings related to the contact algorithm he has chosen; the code does it itself (these modellings relate to the continuous method). Modellings 3D_THVD, AXIS_THVD, D_PLAN_THVD new: - New thermo-hydraulic modellings (without mechanics) for storage studies (cf. STAT_NON_LINE and [6.3.15]). Modellings _HMD, _HHHD, _THHD, _THHMD, _THMD new: - New diagonal THM modellings (cf. [6.3.15]). 1.2.3 CALC_ELEM VARI_ELNO_COQU new option: - The option VARI_ELNO_COQU computes the internal variables in a layer of COQUE, GRILLE or DKT elements (keyword NIVE_COUCHE) from the internal variables computed during a non-linear analysis (cf. [6.3.2]). VALE_NCOU_MAXI new option, keywords NOM_CHAM and NOM_CMP associated: - This option makes it possible to extract the extreme values of the component of a field defined on pipe elements, as well as their location (cf. [6.3.19]). CRIT_ELNO_RUPT new option: - This option computes 6 failure criteria in orthotropic materials (cf. [6.3.7]). ETOT_ELGA, ETOT_ELNO_ELGA, ETOT_ELEM new options: - These options compute the total energy density at the integration points (ETOT_ELGA), at the nodes (ETOT_ELNO_ELGA) and the total energy density integrated over the elements (ETOT_ELEM) (cf. [6.3.17]). TEMP_INIT removed: - This keyword was not used (cf. [6.3.3]). 1.2.4 CALC_FATIGUE TYPE_CALCUL new: - Makes it possible to choose the type of fatigue analysis requested; it takes the value CUMUL_DOMMAGE or FATIGUE_MULTI. Keywords RESULTAT, CHAM_MATER, CRITERE, METHODE new: - To determine the plane in which the shear is maximum in a multiaxial fatigue analysis (FATIGUE_MULTI, cf. [6.3.9]). 1.2.5 CALC_FONCTION PUISSANCE new: - Makes it possible to compute the n-th power of a function (cf. [6.3.12]). NORME new: - Computes the L2 norm of a function (cf. [6.3.12]). CORR_ACCE new: - Makes it possible to correct a real accelerogram (cf. [6.3.2]). LISS_ENVELOP new: - Computes the smoothed envelope spectrum from a raw spectrum (cf. [6.3.16]). 1.2.6 CALC_G_THETA_T FOND_FISS new: - Formerly FOND, in order to standardise the vocabulary with the other CALC_G_ commands (cf. [6.3.10]). 1.2.7 CALC_META ETAT_INIT / INST_INIT new: - On a restart, this keyword makes it possible to define the time instant from which the analysis will be continued (cf. [6.3.19]). 1.2.8 CALC_THETA FOND_FISS new: - Same as CALC_G_THETA_T. 1.2.9 COMB_MATR_ASSE CALC_AMOR_GENE new: - This builds an object MATR_ASSE_GENE corresponding to the BASILE damping matrix from a list of reduced dampings (cf. [6.3.19]). 1.2.10 COMB_SISM_MODAL COMB_DEPL_APPUI new: - This keyword makes it possible to compute the responses to the primary loadings (seismic excitation) and to the secondary loadings (due to differential anchorage displacements). NUME_CAS must be defined under DEPL_MULT_APPUI (cf. [6.3.8]). 1.2.11 DEBUT CODE / NIV_PUB_WEB new: - Under the keyword CODE (for the test cases), NIV_PUB_WEB defines the dissemination level of the test on the Code_Aster website (cf. [6.3.6]). 1.2.12 DEFI_MATERIAU TEMP_DEF_ALPHA mandatory: - The presence of this keyword is now mandatory if the expansion coefficient ALPHA depends on the temperature (cf. [6.3.3]). Constitutive laws removed: - The following constitutive laws have been removed from the code because of their lack of qualification (cf. [6.3.25]): OHNO, VISCOCHAB, VENDOCHAB, LMARC, NADAI_B, SURF_ETAT_SATU, SURF_ETAT_NSAT, CAM_CLAY_THM, LIQU_SATU_GAT, LIQU_NSAT_GAT. EFFO_N_INIT modified: - This parameter, used with the discrete elements, may now depend on the temperature (cf. [6.3.19]). BAZANT_FD new: - Bazant desiccation-creep model (creep due to the drying of concrete under mechanical loading) (cf. [6.3.13]). MAZARS_FO new: - Mazars model making it possible to take into account the variation of the coefficients with respect to temperature (cf. [6.3.18]). 1.2.13 DYNA_NON_LINE and STAT_NON_LINE See DEFI_MATERIAU for the constitutive laws removed and added. KIT_THV new: - New relation, without mechanics, for storage studies. The degrees of freedom are the temperature and the water pressure; the vapour pressure is an internal variable (cf. [6.3.15]). 1.2.14 EXTR_RESU SENSIBILITE new: - This makes it possible to exploit the derived quantities when extracting a result (cf. [6.3.1]). 1.2.15 IMPR_TABLE FORMAT=’ASTER’ new: - This keyword makes it possible to print a table in Aster format; see also LIRE_TABLE (cf. [6.3.13]). 1.2.16 LIRE_MAILLAGE VERI_MAIL by default: - By default, the mesh check is activated (orphan nodes, duplicate mesh cells, flattened mesh cells…) (cf. [6.3.3]). 1.2.17 LIRE_MISS_3D NOM new: - This makes it possible to define the name of the file to be read (cf. [6.3.12]). 1.2.18 LIRE_RESU MATR_A, MATR_B new: - Behind these keywords one supplies the stiffness and mass matrices in order to be able to re-read (and test) a mode obtained by DYNA_TRAN_MODAL (cf. [6.3.19]). FORMAT=’MED’ new: - This makes it possible to re-read results in MED format (recommended for exchanges between EDF/CEA analysis codes). For the moment, only fields at the nodes are processed (cf. [6.3.2]). Associated simple keywords: NOM_MED, NOM_CMP, NOM_CMP_MED, NOM_CMP_IDEM, NOM_MAIL_MED, UNITE. DATASET_58 new: - This format makes it possible to re-read the data supplied by experimental measurement software (cf. [6.3.8]). 1.2.19 MACR_ADAP_MAIL and MACR_INFO_CALC VERSION_HOMARD new default value: - The default version of HOMARD is now V5_5. 1.2.20 MACR_ASCOUF_CALC and MACR_ASPIC_CALC PRESS_LEVRE new: - This keyword makes it possible to apply or not the internal pressure on the lips of a surface-breaking crack on the inner skin (cf. [6.3.19]). 1.2.21 MECA_STATIQUE SIEF_ELGA_DEPL by default: - This option is now computed by default. One may specify OPTION=’SANS’ if one does not wish it (cf. [6.3.19]). 1.2.22 MODI_MAILLAGE MODI_BASE new: - Makes it possible to impose a change of frame (cf. [6.3.18]). TRANSLATION, ROTATION, ECHELLE new: - These keywords make it possible to carry out translations, rotations and scaling of a mesh (cf. [6.3.18]). 1.2.23 POST_K1_K2_K3 FOND_FISS new: - See CALC_G_THETA_T. TOUT_ORDRE, NUME_ORDRE, LIST_ORDRE new: - The data setup is modified; the command itself will explore the result data structure (cf. [6.3.4]). 1.2.24 POST_RCCM OPTION=’FATIGUE_B3200’ new: - Fatigue analysis of a sound piping line according to the RCCM code §B3200 (cf. [6.3.19]). OPTION=’FATIGUE_B3600’ new: - Fatigue analysis of a sound piping line according to the RCCM code §B3600 (cf. [6.3.16]). 1.2.25 PRE_GMSH MODI_QUAD new: - Produces quadratic mesh cells before converting the GMSH mesh to ASTER format (cf. [6.3.7]). 1.2.26 PROJ_MESU_MODAL The syntax has been thoroughly reworked and its possibilities extended. - See the documentation of the command and the test cases sdld104 and sdlv122 (cf. [6.3.18]). 2 New features between versions 6.2 and 6.3 2.1 Changes common to several commands TAILLE_BLOC removed: - Functionality taken over by DEBUT and POURSUITE; TAILLE_BLOC is no longer available in the following commands: | AFFE_CHAR_ACOU | AFFE_CHAR_MECA | AFFE_CHAR_MECA_C | | --- | --- | --- | | AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F | AFFE_CHAR_OPS011 | AFFE_CHAR_THER | | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | AFFE_MODELE | CALC_CHAM_ELEM | | CALC_ELEM | CALC_FORC_AJOU | CALC_MATR_AJOU | | CALC_NO | DYNA_NON_LINE | MACR_ASCOUF_CALC | | MACR_ASPIC_CALC | MACR_ELEM_STAT | MACRO_ELAS_MULT | | MACRO_MATR_AJOU | MACRO_MATR_ASSE | MACRO_PROJ_BASE | | MECA_STATIQUE | NUME_DDL | NUME_DLL_GENE | | POST_ELEM | RECA_WEIBULL | STAT_NON_LINE | | THER_LINEAIRE | THER_NON_LINE | THER_NON_LINE_MO | 2.2 Withdrawn command MACRO_CHAR_F_U is removed. The functionality is covered by the piloting specific to the limit analysis ANA_LIM of STAT_NON_LINE (cf. [6.2.17]). 2.3 Changes of convention - ANGL_REP under the factor keyword COQUE in AFFE_CARA_ELEM: change of sign of the angle (see AFFE_CARA_ELEM) (cf. [6.2.14]), - NU_LT becomes NU_TL and conversely (see DEFI_MATERIAU) in ELAS_ORTH, - Coefficient ½ in the computation of the thermal contribution of ENER_POT (see CALC_ELEM and POST_ELEM, cf. [6.2.13]). 2.4 Modified commands 2.4.1 AFFE_CARA_ELEM AFFE_SECT, AFFE_FIBRE new: - Make it possible to describe the section of a multi-fibre beam element from a 2D mesh (factor keyword AFFE_SECT) or directly by defining the fibres one by one (keyword AFFE_FIBRE, cf. [6.2.6]). COQUE / ANGL_REP modified: - The convention used here was contrary to those adopted for the beams and for the definition of the orthotropy frames. The sign of the second angle defined by ANGL_REP is therefore reversed; it is the nautical-angle convention (cf. [6.2.14]). COQUE_NCOU, GRILLE_NCOU, TUYAU_NSEC and TUYAU_NCOU new: - Under the factor keywords COQUE, GRILLE and POUTRE, to describe the subdivision of a shell/plate into layers, and of a pipe into layers and angular sectors. They were previously supplied under STAT_NON_LINE (cf. [6.2.6]). DIST_N removed: - Replaced by EXCENTREMENT (cf. [6.2.30]). 2.4.2 AFFE_CHAR_MECA ARLEQUIN / CARA_ELEM new: - To supply the characteristics of the shell in the case of a junction between a 3D model and a shell model (cf. [6.2.28]). GONF new: - Makes it possible to impose incompressibility on the new incompressible elements (cf. [6.2.17]). 2.4.3 AFFE_MODELE AFFE / PHENOMENE and AFFE / MODELISATION new possibilities: - Removal of the phenomenon NON_LOCAL, and addition, in the phenomenon MECANIQUE, of the non-local constitutive laws regularised on the strain, and of the associated modellings: 3D_GRAD_EPSI, D_PLAN_GRAD_EPSI, C_PLAN_GRAD_EPSI, AXIS_GRAD_EPSI, and of the modellings associated with the formulation with gradients of internal variables 3D_GRAD_VARI, D_PLAN_GRAD_VARI, C_PLAN_GRAD_VARI, AXIS_GRAD_VARI (cf. [6.2.20]). - New modelling PLAN_FISSURE associated with the finite elements of CZM type (joints), making it possible to treat crack propagation with a constitutive law of Barenblatt type (cf. [6.2.26]). - New modellings 3D_INCO, D_PLAN_INCO (replaces PLAN_INCO), C_PLAN_INCO associated with the three-field formulation of the new incompressible element (displacement, pressure, swelling, cf. [6.2.17]). - New lumped modellings in THM: 3D_HHMD, 3D_HMD, 3D_THHD, 3D_THHMD, 3D_THMD, AXIS_HHMD, AXIS_HMD, AXIS_THHD, AXIS_THHMD, AXIS_THMD, D_PLAN_HHMD, D_PLAN_HMD, D_PLAN_THHD, D_PLAN_THHMD, D_PLAN_THMD (integration points brought back to the vertices of the elements, cf. [6.2.25]). - New modellings POU_D_EM (straight Euler beam) and POU_D_TGM (straight Timoshenko beam with warping) associated with multi-fibre beams (cf. [6.2.6]). AFFE / MODELISATION change of name: - The modelling TUYAU is no longer accessible; it is replaced by TUYAU_3M (cf. [6.2.30]). 2.4.4 AIDE COMMANDE removed: - This functionality is no longer available (it had no longer worked since version 6.0). 2.4.5 CALC_ELEM EPOT_ELEM_DEPL modified: - Standardisation of the computation of the potential energy (removal of the ½ for the thermal contribution to the strain-energy term) and addition of the thermal-expansion term for the structural elements (cf. [6.2.22]). SENSIBILITE / THETA removed: - SENSIBILITE is now a simple keyword which receives the list of the sensitive parameters; THETA is replaced by PARM_THETA (cf. [6.2.1]). PARM_THETA new: - Recalls the value of the parameter of the theta-method used to solve the transient thermal analysis; default value: 0.57. ERTH_ELEM_TEMP and ERTH_ELNO_ELEM new: - Options associated with the residual error estimator in thermal analysis (cf. [6.2.1]). INFO new: - Makes it possible to obtain details on the analyses carried out (in particular for sensitivity, cf. [6.2.1]). DLSI_ELGA_DEPL removed: - This option is removed. The computation of the Lagrangian derivative is now activated by the analysis operator (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, THER_LINEAIRE) when the keyword SENSIBILITE is activated. 2.4.6 CALC_MATR_ELEM MASS_ID_MDEP_R, MASS_ID_MTEM_R, MASS_ID_MDNS_R, MASS_ID_MTNS_R new: - Options making it possible to compute an identity matrix (of the displacements or temperatures, symmetric or non-symmetric) on finite elements in order to compute the eigenvalues of a stiffness matrix or other matrix (cf. [6.2.9]). 2.4.7 CALC_NO SENSIBILITE new: - List of the sensitive parameters (cf. [6.2.1]). DLDE_NOEU, DLSI_NOEU_DLDE, DLTE_NOEU removed: - The computation of these options is no longer available. The computation of the Lagrangian derivative is now supplied by the analysis operator (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, THER_LINEAIRE) when the keyword SENSIBILITE is activated. 2.4.8 COMB_SISM_MODAL TYPE_COMBI replacement: - This keyword replaces TYPE, which was removed in version 6.4; possible values: QUAD, LINE, ABS (cf. [6.2.26]). 2.4.9 CREA_RESU OPERATION new: - Defines the operation to be carried out, among AFFE, ECLA_PG, PERM_CHAM, PROL_RTZ (cf. [6.2.12]). NUME_ORDRE_INIT removed: PRECISION, CRITERE new: - The user no longer supplies a sequence number; access is made directly from the value of the time instant, possibly supplying a PRECISION and a CRITERE (cf. [6.2.21]). 2.4.10 DEFI_BASE_MODALE DIAG_MASS new: - This option makes it possible to create a modal basis containing the static modes and the dynamic modes; the static modes are such that the mass matrix projected onto this basis is diagonal (cf. [6.2.11]). 2.4.11 DEFI_FONC_ELEC INST_CC_INIT mandatory: - This keyword is now mandatory (cf. [6.2.14]). 2.4.12 DEFI_GROUP CRIT_NOEUD new: - Makes it possible to define, from a mesh-cell group, a node group consisting only of the SOMMET nodes, the MILIEU nodes, or the CENTRE nodes (cf. [6.2.17]). 2.4.13 DEFI_MATERIAU NU_LT modified: - In ELAS_ORTH, the Batoz convention is adopted, namely: NU_LT / E_L = NU_TL / E_T, as in DEFI_COQU_MULT (cf. [6.2.13]). ROUSS_VISC new: - Rousselier model extended to viscoplasticity; parameters SIGM_0, EPSI_0 and M (cf. [6.2.10]). FLU_IRRA new: - Modification of the law ASSE_COMBU in order to take into account a dependence of creep with respect to fluence. Keywords: QSR_K, BETA, PHI_ZERO and L (cf. [6.2.9] and [6.2.13]). LABORD_1D new: - New damageable 1D constitutive law for concrete (cf. [6.2.6]). MAZARS new: - New damageable constitutive law for concrete (cf. [6.2.25]). CAM_CLAY new: - New elastoplastic constitutive law for porous media (soils, porous joints, cf. [6.2.25]). LAIGLE new: - New constitutive law in rock mechanics (cf. [6.2.25]). RUPT_FRAG modification: - New keywords SIGM_C and SAUT_C to treat crack propagation with the CZM elements (cf. [6.2.26]). NORTON_HOFF removed: - The new incompressible finite elements offer the same functionality by using only the yield limit (cf. [6.2.17]). 2.4.14 DYNA_LINE_HARM SENSIBILITE new: - List of the sensitive parameters (cf. [6.2.1]). 2.4.15 DYNA_NON_LINE and STAT_NON_LINE ENDO_ISOT_BETON new: - Replaces the behaviours BETON_ENDO_LOCAL and BETON_GRAD_EPSI, which are removed (cf. [6.2.25]). ENDO_FRAGILE new: - Replaces the behaviour ENDO_LOCAL and ENDO_GRAD_EPSI (cf. [6.2.25]). PLAS_GRAD_LINE, PLAS_GRAD_TRAC removed: - The laws specific to non-local behaviour are removed; in the present cases one uses respectively VMIS_ISOT_LINE and VMIS_ISOT_TRAC. Associated with a modelling _GRAD_EPSI or _GRAD_VARI in AFFE_MODELE (cf. [6.2.22]). LABORD_1D, MAZARS, BARENBLATT, ROUSS_VISC, CAM_CLAY, LAIGLE new: - New behaviours (see DEFI_MATERIAU). SENSIBILITE new: - List of the sensitive parameters (cf. [6.2.1]). INCREMENT / OPTI_LIST_INST, NOM_CHAM, NOM_CMP, VALE new: - Under the factor keyword INCREMENT, these new keywords define the options of the automatic subdivision of the time step (cf. [6.2.21]). RHO replaced: - The penalty coefficient of the augmented Lagrangian is now supplied under the keyword R (cf. [6.2.22]). MODELE_NON_LOCAL removed: - This keyword no longer exists; non-local behaviour is activated directly from the choice of the elements in AFFE_MODELE (cf. [6.2.22]). TUYAU_NCOU, TUYAU_NSEC, COQUE_NCOU removed: - These characteristics are now supplied in AFFE_CARA_ELEM (cf. [6.2.6]). HYDR removed: - To use the behaviour HYDR, one must override the code in development mode with the routines PERMEA and SATURA, or use HYDR_UTIL with the definition of the material parameters in DEFI_MATERIAU (cf. [6.2.19]). 2.4.16 EXTR_RESU NOM_CHAMP new: - As opposed to CHAMP_EXCLU, the user may select either the fields he wishes to keep, or those he wishes to exclude (cf. [6.2.14]). 2.4.17 IMPR_COURBE EXCEL new: - To print one or more curves in columns (cf. [6.2.4]). 2.4.18 IMPR_FICO_HOMA NUMORD_INDICA, NUMPT_INDICA, NOM_RESU_INDICA, NOM_CHAM_INDICA new: - Information on the error indicator: sequence number, time step and name of the indicator field in the result data structure (cf. [6.2.16] and [6.2.22]). NOM_MED_SUPPOR removed: - The MED name of the input mesh is now used. 2.4.19 IMPR_MACR_ELEM FORMAT ‘PLEXUS’ new: - Makes it possible to print in IDEAS version 5 format: the mass and stiffness matrices generalised by block, the dynamic eigenmodes, the static modes of the modal basis (cf. COMP_INCR new: - Factor keyword grouping RELATION and VMIS_ISOT_TRAC. 2.4.25 MACRO_MODE_MECA COEF_DIM_ESPACE new: - See MODE_ITER_SIMULT. 2.4.26 MECA_STATIQUE SENSIBILITE / THETA removed: - SENSIBILITE is now a simple keyword which receives the list of the sensitive parameters; THETA is removed (cf. u4.01.03 1 u4.01.03 New features and changes of version 7 Organisation(s): EDF-R&D/AMA User's manual Booklet U4.0-: Use of the commands Document: U4.01.03 1 u4.01.03 New features and changes of version 7 Summary: The purpose of this document is to give an overall view of the syntax changes and of the new possibilities of the Code_Aster commands which have occurred between each version since version 7.0. Index A of this document thus reports the changes introduced since version 7.3 of April 2004 and valid for version 7.4 of December 2004. For further details, consult the command documentation and the histor file of the corresponding sub-version (e.g.: [7.3.12], Development section of the site www.code-aster.org). The commands affected are listed in alphabetical order. 1 New features between 7.3 and 7.4 1.1 Changes to the environment 1.1.1 Med Code_Aster now relies on the MED 2.2 library. To read files in med 2.1.5 format, they must be converted with the med_import tool (there is no tool in the opposite direction). 1.1.2 Homard Following the change of version of med, homard has also evolved in order to support the same library level. homard 7.1 also brings other new features (cf. [U7.03.xx]). 1.2 New commands 1.2.1 CREA_TABLE This command makes it possible to create a table from a function or from several lists of integers, of reals or of character strings. One can create a full table or a table with gaps by indicating the rows one wishes to fill in. 1.2.2 DEFI_COMPOR This command makes it possible to define a monocrystalline or polycrystalline behaviour. 1.2.3 DEFI_PART_FETI This command makes it possible to create a partitioning into subdomains with a view to a solution by the Feti method. 1.2.4 IMPR_FONCTION This new command replaces IMPR_COURBE, and it handles only functions (hence the change of name); tables are handled by IMPR_TABLE (cf. [7.3.13]). 1.2.5 MACR_ECLA_PG This macro-command replaces the ECLA_PG options of the two commands CREA_MAILLAGE and CREA_RESU. Consistency between the two commands is thus ensured. 1.2.6 MODI_MODELE_XFEM This command makes it possible to create finite elements with enriched degrees of freedom required for the XFEM method. 1.3 Withdrawn commands 1.3.1 DEFI_VALEUR Since the content of the Python objects is saved (in the file pick.1) “alongside” the Aster database (file glob.1), it is no longer necessary to have a specific command to define a parameter. For example (see also [U3.01.0x]): deuxpi = 2. pi 1.3.2 IMPR_COURBE Replaced by IMPR_FONCTION (cf. [7.3.13]). 1.3.3 POST_GOUJ2E This command had not been withdrawn at the same time as the associated macros MACR_GOUJ2E_MAIL/CALC. The analysis methodology is kept in the test cases zzzz120a and zzzz120b (cf. [7.2.14]). 1.4 Changes common to several commands 1.4.1 Keywords FICHIER and UNITE Depending on the type of command, one had to use either UNITE (reading commands), where a logical unit number was expected, or FICHIER (post-processing commands), behind which one expected not a file name but a “label” (ddname) which was associated with a logical unit by default or assigned via the command DEFI_FICHIER (formerly DEFUFI). The notion of a label disappears; the commands all work with UNITE and those which know how to use a genuine file name also accept the keyword FICHIER. The risk of confusion is reduced: one supplies to UNITE the logical unit entered in astk and to FICHIER a complete unix file name (see also the use of REPE_IN/REPE_OUT in the astk documentation U1.04.00). 1.4.2 Post-processing commands CALC_ELEM, CALC_NO, CALC_G_LOCAL_T, CALC_G_THETA_T, POST_ELEM MODELE, CHAM_MATER, CARA_ELEM, EXCIT become optional: - The result data structure (coming from STAT_NON_LINE, THER_LINEAIRE…) keeps these 4 parameters in memory; it therefore becomes optional to supply them to these post-processing operators. One may however enter these keywords in certain particular cases; one then checks that they are the same ones which were used for the analysis; if this is not the case, an alarm is issued or one stops in error (case of MODELE) (cf. [7.3.7], [7.3.24]). 1.5 Modified commands 1.5.1 AFFE_CARA_ELEM ANGL_L, POUR_CENT_L, POUR_CENT_T removed, SECTION_L renamed to SECTION: - These keywords are no longer of interest since the introduction of new membrane grid elements, which make it possible to model the reinforcement grids in a given direction, and which can be used together with a 3D modelling of the concrete. Likewise the grid elements (usable with "shell") now work in a single direction. The orientation of the reinforcements is defined under ANGL_REP (cf. [7.3.10]). POUTRE/VARI_SECT modified: - To guide the user among the possible choices, one now chooses a value for SECTION, then for VARI_SECT (new choice: CONSTANT by default), which makes it possible to limit the list of what is possible for CARA (cf. [7.3.23]). PREC_AIRE, PREC_INERTIE new: - The consistency of the information (area and inertia of the multi-fibre beams) supplied under the keywords POUTRE and AFFE_SECT is checked to the accuracy indicated by these keywords (cf. [7.3.28]). 1.5.2 AFFE_CHAR_MECA / AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F FORMULATION new: - When solving a contact problem with the continuous method, one has the choice between a displacement formulation (value DEPL) or a velocity formulation (value VITE, numerically well suited to the treatment of impacts) (cf. [7.3.18]). TOLE_PROJ replaced by TOLE_PROJ_EXT, TOLE_PROJ_INT new: - In the case of the symmetric pairing MAIT_ESCL_SYME, it is necessary to have a projection tolerance for the detection of zero pivots (cf. [7.3.23]). ITER_MULT_MAXI new: - ITER_MULT_MAXI multiplied by the number of slave nodes gives the maximum number of contact iterations (cf. [7.3.23]). COEF_MULT_2, VECT_NORM_2, DIST_1, DIST_2 replaced by COEF_MULT_ESCL, VECT_NORM_ESCL, DIST_MAIT and DIST_ESCL: - Standardisation of the vocabulary following the renaming of GROUP_MA_1/2 to GROUP_MA_MAIT/ESCL (cf. [7.3.24]). GRAPPE_FLUIDE new keywords: - Several keywords making it possible to locate the forces according to their type and their zone of application have been added (APPL_FORC_xxxx, DIRE_FORC_FPLAQ, UNITE_IMPR_xxxx) (cf. [7.3.23]). ARLEQUIN changes: - Improvement of the Arlequin method (cf. reference document) and addition of the keywords COND_LIM, COLLAGE, POIDS_GROSSIER, POIDS_FIN (cf. [7.3.28]). 1.5.3 AFFE_MATERIAU SECH_REF new: - Makes it possible to enter the value of the reference drying; at this concentration, the desiccation shrinkage is zero. The user must remember to enter K_DESSIC if his drying field is variable (cf. [7.3.2]). 1.5.4 CALC_FATIGUE MODELE removed: - The keyword was not used (cf. [7.3.2]). 1.5.5 CALC_FONCTION METHODE new: - Improvement of the computation of the FFT by adding the method PROL_ZERO, in which the signal is padded with zeros (cf. [7.3.14]). 1.5.6 CALC_G_LOCAL_T and CALC_G_THETA_T EXCIT replaces CHARGE: - The multiplicative coefficient of the loads was not taken into account. This is now the case; CHARGE, FONC_MULT and TYPE_CHARGE are added under EXCIT. Same change in CALC_G_THETA_T (cf. [7.3.6]). By default, it is in fact not necessary to supply EXCIT, which is stored in the result data structure (cf. [§1.4.2]). VITE, ACCE new: - Make it possible to take the inertia terms into account in the computation of G (cf. [7.3.4]). 1.5.7 CREA_MAILLAGE NOM_CHAM new: - In order to explode the elements (ECLA_PG), one needs to know the Gauss-point family used. For this, one must supply the name of the field (cf. [7.3.19]). 1.5.8 CREA_RESU MODELE, CHAM_MATER, CARA_ELEM new: - Make it possible to create a result of type elas_mult (MACRO_ELAS_MULT) (cf. [7.3.7]). 1.5.9 DEBUT FORMAT_HDF=’OUI’/’NON’ replaces the factor keyword HDF: - Databases in HDF format (portable binary format between machines of different architectures) are now supported by astk; it is therefore enough to specify whether or not one wishes to read a database in this format (cf. [7.3.22]). 2 New features between 7.2 and 7.3 2.1 New commands 2.1.1 MACR_FIABILITE This macro-command computes the probability that a physical variable (displacement, stress, ...) exceeds a threshold defined by the user as a function of a certain number of parameters which will have been defined as sensitive by the user. These sensitive parameters may be Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, a pressure, etc. The macro-command calls the MEFISTO software, which is external to Code_Aster , and which implements the FORM method (cf. [7.2.11]). 2.1.2 STANLEY Stanley, an interactive post-processing tool, was already present in version 7; this macro-command simplifies calling it, since it is now launched as an ordinary command (cf. [7.2.25]). 2.1.3 TEST_FICHIER This macro-command makes it possible to test the non-regression of the commands which produce files, intended for developers (cf. [7.2.25]). 2.2 Withdrawn commands 2.2.1 FACT_INTE_SPEC This command has been merged with GENE_FONC_ALEA (cf. [7.2.3]). 2.2.2 MACR_GOUJ2E_MAIL and MACR_GOUJ2E_CALC These two macro-commands are withdrawn. The analysis methodology is kept in the command files zzzz120a and zzzz120b which validated these functionalities (cf. [7.2.14]). 2.3 Modified commands 2.3.1 AFFE_CARA_ELEM RIGI_MISS_3D new: - Makes it possible to assign the terms of a soil impedance matrix computed by MISS3D for a given extraction frequency (cf. [7.2.2]). 2.3.2 AFFE_MODELE _HH2D new modellings: - These modellings make it possible to take into account two phases in the two constituents; the dissolved-air pressure is related to the dry-air pressure by Henry's law (cf. [7.2.7]). GRILLE_MEMBRANE new modelling: - This is a new reinforcement-layer element which works only in membrane, with no rotation degree of freedom (cf. [7.2.21]). 2.3.3 AFFE_CHAR_MECA / AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F GRAPPE_FLUIDE new: - Makes it possible to take into account the fluid forces due to the displacement of the cluster in the fluid which bathes the internal elements of the core (cf. [7.2.2]). TOLE_PROJ new: - Makes it possible to adjust the projection of the slave nodes onto the master mesh cells (cf. [7.2.1]). CONTACT keywords renamed: - GROUP_MA_MAIT, MAILLE_MAIT, GROUP_MA_ESCL, MAILLE_ESCL respectively replace GROUP_MA_1, MAILLE_1, GROUP_MA_2, MAILLE_2 (cf. [7.2.4]). 2.3.4 ASSE_MAILLAGE OPERATION, MAILLAGE_1, MAILLAGE new: - Three types of operation are now available: SOUS_STR, SUPERPOSE, COLLAGE (cf. [7.2.4]). 2.3.5 CALC_CHAM_ELEM / CALC_ELEM Duplication: - These two commands duplicated each other on most of the options computed; only a few options remain in CALC_CHAM_ELEM (cf. [7.2.17]). 2.3.6 CALC_FATIGUE TYPE_CHARGE new: - Defines the type of loading (periodic or not); under the keyword CRITERE, the choice is thus restricted according to the type of loading (cf. [7.2.5]). CRITERE=’DOMM_MAXI’, PROJECTION, DELTA_OSCI new: - These keywords are associated with the new criterion suited to non-periodic loadings; it is a variable-amplitude criterion based on a critical plane selected according to the maximum induced damage (cf. [7.2.5]). CRITERE=’DANG_VAN__MODI_AC’ / ‘DANG_VAN_MODI_AV’ new: - This is a variable-amplitude criterion based on a critical plane selected from the maximum damage. This criterion, which is suited to the case in which the loading is non-periodic, is an evolution of the original DANG VAN criterion. ‘AC’ for constant amplitude, ‘AV’ for variable amplitude (cf. [7.2.11]). 2.3.7 CALC_G_THETA_T New type for the field: - One can now supply a field of type cham_no_depl_r (and build it to suit!) instead of the one supplied by CALC_THETA (cf. [7.2.8]). 2.3.8 CALC_NO GROUP_MA_RESU, GROUP_NO_RESU, MAILLE_RESU, NOEU_RESU new: - Make it possible to specify the zone on which the field by element will be reduced before computing the values at the nodes, because incorrect results could be obtained when a node is on the boundary of two modellings (cf. [7.2.7]). 2.3.9 CREA_MAILLAGE / CREA_RESU ECLA_PG new possibilities: - One can now explode a mesh (by creating one element per Gauss point) over only part of a mesh; and, in 2D, give a fictitious thickness to flat elements. Warning: The parameters supplied to CREA_MAILLAGE and CREA_RESU must be consistent: the same mesh-cell groups given in the same order (cf. [7.2.8]). 2.3.12 DEFI_MATERIAU BARCELONE new behaviour for KIT_HHM and KIT_THHM: - Mechanical and hydraulic constitutive law of unsaturated soils. This model involves two criteria, a mechanical plasticity criterion which is that of CAM_CLAY and another, hydraulic, criterion controlled by the suction (cf. [7.2.21]). GLRC / GLRC_FO new behaviour: - Constitutive law of reinforced-concrete plates written in generalised forces; associated finite element DKTG (on TRIA3 and QUAD4 mesh cells) (cf. [7.2.4]). CORR_ACIER new: - Damageable elastoplastic model of a steel in which the plastic strain at rupture depends on the corrosion rate (cf. [7.2.23]). VISC_IRRA_LOG new behaviour: - Viscoelastic constitutive law for the axial creep of the guide tubes under irradiation (cf. [7.2.1]). DRUCKER_PRAGER new behaviour: - Constitutive law for soil mechanics (cf. [7.2.7]). LIQU_AD_GAZ_VAPE new: - Coupling law for dissolved air for THM (Henry's law), which relates the dissolved-air pressure to the dry-air pressure (cf. [7.2.7]). DOMM_A, DOMM_B, COEF_CISA_TRAC new: - Associated with the fatigue criterion DOMM_MAXI of CALC_FATIGUE (cf. [7.2.5]). EPSP_SEUIL, EXP_S new: - Associated with the fatigue criterion DOMMA_LEMAITRE of CALC_FATIGUE (cf. [7.2.19]). LAMBDA and D_LAMBDA_TEMP removed under THM_ : - The thermal conductivity is now defined as the product of three functions of the temperature (LAMB_T), of the saturation (LAMB_S) and of the porosity (LAMB_PHI) plus a constant (LAMB_CT), as well as the three derivatives of the functions (D_LB_T, D_LB_S, D_LB_PHI) (cf. [7.2.10]). In the thermal case, only LAMB_T is mandatory, the other functions then being taken equal to one and their derivatives zero. 2.3.13 GENE_FONC_ALEA / GENE_MATR_ALEA / GENE_VARI_ALEA - These commands have been completely reworked; FACT_GENE_ALEA has been withdrawn in favour of GENE_FONC_ALEA. [7.2.3]). 2.3.14 IMPR_RESU FORMAT=’GMSH’ / VERSION new default: - The default version of the GMSH file is now 1.2 (in which GMSH knows how to post-process quadrangles): the quadrangles are not cut into triangles (cf. [7.2.10], see on the Code_Aster intranet under Utilisation/Matériaux). 2.3.16 MACR_RECAL POIDS new: - One can weight the various curves on which the recalibration is carried out (cf. [7.2.4]). 2.3.17 MODI_MAILLAGE SYMETRIE new: - Makes it possible to take the symmetric of a mesh with respect to a straight line or a plane according to the dimension (cf. [7.2.16]). 2.3.18 POST_ELEM New: - One can now use POST_ELEM after a multiple solution with MACRO_ELAS_MULT (cf. [7.2.22]). 2.3.19 POST_K1_K2_K3 TOUT new: - Makes it possible to compute the stress intensity factors on all the nodes of the mesh cells making up the crack front (cf. [7.2.4]). 2.3.20 PROJ_CHAMP DISTANCE_MAX new: - Makes it possible to project judiciously fields from a model A onto a model B. When nodes of mesh B are not in an element of mesh A and are beyond a certain distance, the field is not projected (cf. [7.2.16]). NUAG_DEG_ methods removed: - These field-projection methods have been removed; inaccurate results (cf. [7.2.22]). 2.3.21 POST_RCCM TYPE_RESU_MECA new, modification of the options: - This keyword may take the values ‘UNITAIRE’ or ‘TUYAUTERIE’; OPTION=’FATIGUE’ replaces B3200 and B3600… (cf. [7.2.17]). 2.3.22 MACRO_CARA_POUTRE RT new result: - One can obtain under this keyword the torsion radius of the section of a beam (cf. [7.2.2]). 2.3.23 STAT_NON_LINE / DYNA_NON_LINE ALGO_1D new: - One can thus use all the (small-strain) 3D behaviours in the bar elements, the grid elements and the multi-fibre beam elements; the method proposed by R. De Borst for plane stresses has been extended to 1D behaviours. This results, as for plane stresses, in 4 internal variables (cf. [7.2.18]). ETAT_INIT mandatory in re-entrant mode (when the result is enriched) (cf. [7.2.1]). BARCELONE new: - Behaviour of soils in an unsaturated medium (cf. [7.2.21]). GLRC new: - Behaviour of reinforced-concrete plates written in generalised forces (cf. [7.2.4]). CORR_ACIER, CORROSION new: - Make it possible to supply the parameters required for the damageable elastoplastic model of a steel in which the plastic strain at rupture depends on the corrosion rate (cf. [7.2.23]). SOUS_STRUC new: - Integration of static macro-elements. The intended application is to optimise the solution of large-sized problems in which only a restricted part has a non-linear behaviour (cf. [7.2.23]). THER_HOMO, THER_POLY removed: - Removal of the thermal constitutive law under RELATION_KIT in THM (cf. [7.2.16]). 2.3.24 THER_NON_LINE_MO The command is no longer re-entrant because only one time instant is computed (steady analysis in a moving frame). 3 New features between 7.0 and 7.2 One finds here the syntax changes consequent on the developments introduced in versions 7.1 and 7.2 (version 7.0 being similar to 6.4). 3.1 New commands 3.1.1 CALC_PRECONT This command makes it possible to define and apply the prestressing of the cables of a reinforced-concrete structure, taking into account different types of anchorage, and making it possible to tension each cable individually while complying with the BPEL standards (cf. [7.0.14]). 3.1.2 CREA_TABLE This command makes it possible to create a table from a function or from two lists (cf. [7.1.17]). 3.1.3 DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI This is the first version of the explicit dynamics operator, in which not all the possibilities have yet been introduced (master–slave contact, for example) (cf. [7.1.16]). 3.1.4 EXTR_TABLE This command makes it possible to recover the content of a cell of a table; only the type MATR_ASSE_GENE_R is handled for the moment (cf. [7.1.17]). 3.1.5 MACR_CABRI_MAIL – MACR_CABRI_CALC These commands make it possible to mesh flanges automatically, and to launch analyses on these meshes (cf. [7.1.5]). 3.2 Withdrawn commands The commands MACRO_CHAR_F_U and MACRO_MADMACS have been removed in version 7.1. 3.3 Renamed commands - MACR_CARA_POUTRE replaces MACRO_CARA_POUTRE. - DEFI_FICHIER replaces DEFUFI and FERMER (the latter will be withdrawn in version 7.3). In addition, DEFI_FICHIER makes it possible to access a file by indicating its system name (and not only with its fortran logical unit number) (cf. [7.1.16]). 3.4 Changes common to several commands 3.4.1 FOND_FISS replaces FOND, FOND_3D In the commands CALC_G_LOCAL_T, CALC_G_THETA_T, CALC_THETA, POST_K1_K2_K3 - Standardisation of the vocabulary in fracture mechanics (cf. [7.0.9]). 3.4.2 Solver preconditioning options – keyword PRE_COND In the commands CALC_FORC_AJOU, CALC_MATR_AJOU, DYNA_NON_LINE, MACR_ASCOUF_CALC, MACR_ASPIC_CALC, MACRO_MATR_AJOU, MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, THER_LINEAIRE, THER_NON_LINE, THER_NON_LINE_MO - The option PRE_COND=’DIAG’ is removed; only the option LDLT_INC (incomplete) remains (cf. [7.0.14]). 3.5 Modified commands 3.5.1 AFFE_CARA_ELEM GROUP_MA_POI1 new: - Keyword introduced in order to assign RIGI_PARASOL characteristics on elements of type POI1 (cf. [7.0.14]). 3.5.2 AFFE_CHAR_MECA DDL_POUTRE new: - Makes it possible to impose boundary conditions in the local frame of a beam (cf. [7.0.10]). LIAISON new: - Under DDL_IMPO, to block all the displacements at once (cf. [7.1.5]). SIGM_BPEL default value: - The default value is now ‘NON’; the value ‘OUI’ is usually used only for the prestressing of the cables (cf. [7.0.13]). 3.5.3 AFFE_CHAR_MECA_C LIAISON new: - Under DDL_IMPO, to block all the displacements at once (cf. [7.1.5]). 3.5.4 AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F LIAISON new: - Under DDL_IMPO, to block all the displacements at once (cf. [7.1.5]). EFFET_FOND new: - Allows the closed-end effect to be taken into account as a function of time (cf. [7.0.1]). 3.5.5 AFFE_MATERIAU GROUP_NO, NOEUD removed: - Assignment is possible only on mesh cells (cf. [7.1.8]). 3.5.6 AFFE_MODELE SHB8 new modelling: - New under-integrated shell element without a locking mode (cf. [7.1.18]). AFFE modification: - possibility of supplying a list under AFFE, with the overloading rule (cf. [7.1.18]). 3.5.7 CALC_ELEM EQUI_ELNO_SIGM different computation method: The equivalent stresses (Von Mises, Tresca, ...) were computed from the stresses extrapolated to the nodes. The equivalent stresses are now computed by extrapolation of the equivalent stresses computed at the Gauss points (as for the internal variables). The only stress fields supplied are therefore SIEF_ELGA_DEPL in linear analysis and SIEF_ELGA in non-linear analysis. On the other hand, for shell elements, the way of computing the equivalent stresses has not changed: the user must compute the stress field at a point through the thickness (SIGM_ELNO_DEPL in linear analysis and SIGM_ELNO_COQU in non-linear analysis), and the option EQUI_ELNO_SIGM computes the invariants of this field at the nodes. 3.5.8 CALC_FATIGUE CRITERE new possibility: - Addition of the DANG_VAN criterion (cf. [7.0.17]). BETON_UMLV_FP new: - Addition of a constitutive relation for taking into account the basic creep of concrete (cf. [7.0.4]). BPEL_ACIER /SY becomes F_PRG: - F_PRG is the guaranteed stress of the maximum load at rupture (cf. [7.1.17]). COMP_THM new: - Grouping of the parameters to be supplied for a THM analysis according to the coupling law used (cf. [7.1.18]). DIS_CONTACT/ ANGLE_i and MOMENT_i: - For the grid–rod connection, the angles and moments as a function of temperature and fluence are introduced (cf. [7.1.7]). In fatigue: - Addition of the DANG_VAN CRITERE (cf. [7.0.7]). - For the MATAKE criterion, ENDU_FT is replaced by COEF_FLEX_TORS. 3.5.19 DETRUIRE OBJET new: - Possibility of destroying objects associated with concepts inaccessible to the user (cf. [7.1.9]). 3.5.20 DYNA_LINE_TRAN and DYNA_NON_LINE SENSIBILITE new: - Addition of the computation of the derivatives of the result fields with respect to the material data or the boundary conditions (cf. [7.1.5] for DYNA_LINE_TRAN, [7.1.3] for DYNA_NON_LINE). 3.5.21 FIN HDF new: - Define the parameters for writing a database in HDF format (portable between machines) (cf. [7.1.16]). 3.5.22 FORMULE ENTIER removed: - Integer formulae are henceforth forbidden (cf. [7.0.17]). 3.5.23 IMPR_FICO_HOMA There are syntax changes in this procedure, called by MACR_ADAP_MAIL, which are therefore not described here. 3.5.24 IMPR_RESU VERSION new: - Makes it possible to specify the version level of the files in GMSH format. With version 1.2 (available in recent versions of GMSH), the quadrangles are no longer cut into triangles, GMSH being able to handle all the linear elements (cf. [7.0.3]). 3.5.25 IMPR_TABLE TITRE_TABLE new: - Possibility of defining a title when printing a table (cf. [7.0.16]). 3.5.26 INCLUDE_MATERIAU UNITE_LONGUEUR new: - Makes it possible to use the data of the material catalogue with the millimetre as the unit of length (cf. [7.0.14]). 3.5.27 LIRE_CHAMP INST new: - One can now locate the field or fields to be read by the time instant in a file in MED format (cf. [7.1.10]). 3.5.28 LIRE_RESU FORMAT replaces FORMAT_IDEAS: - Behind this keyword one specifies the reading format: IDEAS or IDEAS_DS58 (cf. [7.0.13]). 3.5.29 MACR_ADAP_MAIL NON_SIMPLEXE new: - Allows acceptance of quadrangular, hexahedral and pentahedral elements (which are not refined) in a mesh submitted to Homard (cf. [7.1.10]). MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE new: - Possibility of supplying a mesh for boundary tracking (cf. [7.1.10]). TYPE_CHAM modification: - One now expects the same thing as in the command CREA_CHAMP (cf. [7.0.12]). 3.5.30 MACR_INFO_MAIL NON_SIMPLEXE and MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE new: - See MACR_ADAP_MAIL. 3.5.31 MECA_STATIQUE INST_FIN new: - The operator is now re-entrant in order to be able to treat long transients (cf. [7.1.8]). 3.5.32 MODE_ITER_SIMULT APPROCHE new possibility: - Addition of the ‘COMPLEXE’ approach in order to treat the quadratic eigenvalue problem, for strongly damped cases for example (cf. [7.0.12]). 3.5.33 MODI_MAILLAGE ORIE_SHB8 new: - Makes it possible to orient the SHB8 shell elements (cf. [7.1.18]). 3.5.34 MODI_OBSTACLE TUBE_NEUF removed: - The keyword has been moved into the command POST_USURE (cf. [7.0.2]). 3.5.35 MODI_REPERE GROUP_MA, MAILLE, GROUP_NO, NOEUD new: - Makes it possible to restrict the change of frame to part of the mesh (cf. [7.0.9]). 3.5.36 PROJ_CHAMP SENSIBILITE new: - Makes it possible to project derived fields from one mesh onto another (cf. [7.1.10]). 3.5.37 POST_USURE TUBE_NEUF new: - Makes it possible to supply new wear values (cf. [7.0.2]). 3.5.38 POST_RCCM TYPE_KE new - Offers two methods of computing Ke. 3.5.39 PRE_GMSH MODI_QUAD removed: - This functionality is taken over in CREA_MAILLAGE and applies to an Aster mesh whatever its origin (cf. [7.0.6]). Note: | PRE_GMSH is once again a procedure. | | --- | 3.5.40 PRE_IDEAS CREA_GROUP_COUL new: - Makes it possible to create or not the groups associated with the IDEAS colours (cf. [7.0.2]). 3.5.41 STAT_NON_LINE RESI_REFE_RELA, SIGM_REFE, EPSI_REFE, FLUX_THER_REFE, FLUX_HYD1_REFE, FLUX_HYD2_REFE new: - New method for the convergence test with respect to a reference value defined for each quantity (grandeur) (cf. [7.0.16]). SELECTION new: - Choice of the piloting parameter: NORM_INCR_DEPL, ANGL_INCR_DEPL, RESIDU: one minimises respectively the displacement increment (default), the angle between u+ and u-, the residual (cf. [7.0.9]). ETA_PILO_R_MAX, ETA_PILO_R_MIN, PROJ_BORNES new: - Make it possible to define the bounds of the search interval (cf. [7.0.9]). PAS_MIN_CRIT, ITER_LINE_CRIT, RHO_MAX, RHO_MIN, RHO_EXCL new: - Bounds of the line search in the case of piloting (cf. [7.0.9]). CRIT_FLAMB new: - Search for the buckling modes of a structure (cf. [7.1.17]). SENSIBILITE new: - Introduction of sensitivity analyses in the non-linear regime (cf. [7.1.3]). 3.5.42 TEST_TABLE SENSIBILITE new: - Makes it possible to test the derived tables (cf. [7.1.12]). Page intentionally left blank.

u4.01.04 1 u4.01.04 New features and changes of version 8 Organisation(s): EDF-R&D/AMA User's manual Booklet U4.0-: Use of the commands Document: U4.01.04 1 u4.01.04 New features and changes of version 8 Summary: The purpose of this document is to give an overall view of the syntax changes and of the new possibilities of the Code_Aster commands which have occurred in the course of the development of version 8, that is to say since version 7.4. Index B of this document thus reports the changes introduced since version 8.4 of June 2006 and valid for version 8.4 of December 2006. Paragraphs 2 and, respectively, 3 deal with the syntactic developments between version 8.2 (December 2005) and 8.3 (June 2006) and, respectively, between versions 8.0 (December 2004) and 8.2. For further details, consult the command documentation and the histor file of the corresponding sub-version (e.g.: [8.3.7], Development section of the site www.code-aster.org). The commands affected are listed in alphabetical order. 1 New features between 8.3 and 8.4 1.1 New commands 1.1.1 MACR_SPECTRE This is a macro-command for computing floor spectra at several nodes, as a post-processing of a seismic analysis. It chains the following stages (cf. [8.3.21], documentation U4.32.11): - recovery of the relative acceleration of the various nodes, - combination with the entrainment acceleration in order to obtain the absolute acceleration, - computation of response spectra for several dampings, - envelope of the nappes corresponding to the same floor in order to obtain the floor spectrum. 1.1.2 POST_GP The purpose of this command is to group the various stages of a post-processing whose aim is to compute the energy criterion Gp at the end of a thermomechanical analysis. Either one identifies the critical values of the parameter Gp as a function of given critical fracture toughnesses at a fixed temperature (typically on a CT-specimen analysis), or one estimates the instants of rupture on a transient from the critical values of Gp identified previously (cf. [8.3.14], documentation U4.82.31). 1.1.3 POST_K_TRANS This command chains the computation of the modal stress intensity factors (option K_G_MODA of CALC_G) and the computation of K(t) as a post-processing of a transient mechanical analysis on a modal basis of the cracked structure (cf. [8.3.10], documentation U4.82.30). 1.1.4 SIMU_POINT_MAT Makes it possible to carry out simply quasi-static non-linear mechanical analyses on a material point. The analysis is in fact carried out on a tetrahedron. On input one defines the loading history, the material and the behaviour, and the analysis time instants (cf. [8.3.11], documentation U4.51.12). 1.1.5 Versions of the tools The version of the mesh refinement/coarsening tool homard used is 8.5. The version of the med library used for data exchange is 2.3.1. 1.2 General changes The command variables (field of parameters of the mechanical analysis) of corrosion, hydration and irradiation type have been supplied in AFFE_MATERIAU under the keyword AFFE_VARC since version 8.3 (cf. general changes in 8.3). Drying, anelastic strains and metallurgy join the same logic (cf. [8.3.10]). Temperature remains… The keywords SECH_CALCULEE and EPSA_CALCULEE therefore disappear from AFFE_CHAR_MECA. 1.3 Removals The commands COMB_CHAM_NO and COMB_CHAM_ELEM dealt with the combination of fields and with Fourier recombination. They are removed in favour of CREA_CHAMP and CREA_RESU (cf. [8.3.12]). The modelling 3D_JOINT_CT has been withdrawn. The constitutive law POLY_CFC is removed, replaced by POLYCRISTAL, which is richer. The command DEFI_TEXTURE is removed. The obstacle type disappears; the command DEFI_OBSTACLE produces an object of type table_fonction which one can handle with the classical operators dealing with tables. 1.4 Modified commands 1.4.1 Behaviour of the non-linear operators For the constitutive laws, a similar keyword is, in general, added/modified in the command DEFI_MATERIAU. Automatic subdivision of the time steps: - New keywords beginning with SUBD_xxx, making it possible to choose the subdivision method used and to define its arguments. The method which existed previously is called UNIFORME; the automatic method is EXTRAPOLE. The latter attempts to determine by extrapolation the number of subdivisions and the ratio to be applied in order to converge with the number of iterations requested. - The commands concerned are STAT_NON_LINE, DYNA_NON_LINE, DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI, CALC_PRECONT, MACR_ASCOUF_CALC, MACR_ASPIC_CALC, MACR_CABRI_CALC, SIMU_POINT_MAT. New behaviour GLRC_DAMAGE and GLRC_DM: - GLRC_DAMAGE is a constitutive model of reinforced-concrete plates written in generalised forces, with damage in bending. It replaces the GLRC model present previously. The formulation of the model is the same as in Europlexus. - GLRC_DM is also a global damage model. It takes into account the membrane/bending coupling for damage, but damage and plasticity are not coupled. The intended applications are the seismic analyses of reinforced-concrete structures. New behaviour VMIS_ISOT_PUIS: - This is the elastoplastic behaviour with a Von Mises criterion and isotropic hardening following a power law. Post-processing of structural analyses in civil engineering: - New options have been introduced in CALC_ELEM: EPVC_ELNO/ELGA, whose components are the thermal strains, the desiccation shrinkage and the endogenous shrinkage. - The new options EPFP_ELNO/ELGA compute the basic-creep strain for the models BETON_UMLV and GRANGER. - The options EPFD_ELNO/ELGA compute the desiccation-creep strain. - The options EPGR_xxxx are removed. DEFORMATION='REAC_GEOM' new: - Treatment of multi-fibre beams (element POU_D_TGM) in large displacements and large rotations with geometric updating and a small-strain assumption, without neglecting the geometric stiffness (cf. [8.3.4]). Parameter PARM_THETA: - This parameter, specific to the behaviour, is moved under COMP_INCR, in the spirit of what was done for the local convergence criteria (cf. § changes in version 8.2). 1.4.2 Keyword SUIVI_DDL This new keyword, available under STAT_NON_LINE / DYNA_NON_LINE, makes it possible to follow, in the course of the analysis, the value at a point or an extremum of a component of a field (cf. [8.3.3]). 1.4.3 Keyword SOLVEUR This keyword is common to the operators DYNA_LINE_TRAN, DYNA_NON_LINE, MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, THER_LINEAIRE, THER_NON_LINE. METHODE='MUMPS' / SCALING and RENUM new: - SCALING controls the type of pre-processing to be applied to the system in order to “balance it”. RENUM makes it possible to choose the type of renumbering (cf. [8.3.1]). 1.4.4 AFFE_CARA_ELEM COQUE / VECTEUR new: - Makes it possible to define the vector orienting the local frame of the shells by its coordinates, without going through ANGL_REP (cf. [8.3.5]). MASSIF / ANGL_EULER new: - Makes it possible to define the vector orienting the local frame of the orthotropic solid elements by giving the Euler angles instead of the nautical angles (ANGL_REP) (cf. [8.3.11]). DISCRET / VALE_F new (for the elementary characteristics of the discrete elements): - Makes it possible to carry out a sensitivity analysis with respect to a term of the elementary matrix of the DISCRET and DISCRET_2D elements, limited to the stiffness and mass matrices (cf. [8.3.13]). 1.4.5 AFFE_CHAR_MECA / AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F NOM_CHAM, COEF_IMPO, COEF_MULT_ESCL removed: - These keywords were used to define unilateral conditions in THM in particular. One must now use the keyword LIAISON_UNILATER (cf. [8.3.3]). FOND_FISSURE new (continuous-method contact): - Makes it possible to treat contact correctly at the crack front if one uses Barsoum elements (cf. [8.3.3]). RACCORD_SURF new (continuous-method contact): - Makes it possible to treat contact correctly in the presence of a connection by LIAISON_MAIL (cf. [8.3.3]). COEF_MULT_FONC new: - Makes it possible to define coefficient functions in a LIAISON_DDL (cf. [8.3.18]). 1.4.6 AFFE_MATERIAU AFFE_NOEUD new: - Development in progress for the assignment of material properties to the nodes of the elements for THM (cf. [8.3.2]). LIST_NOM_VARC new possibilities: - The new command variables are SECH for drying, EPSA for the anelastic strains, M_ACIER and M_ZIRC for the metallurgical phases (cf. § general changes and [8.3.10]). 1.4.7 AFFE_MODELE SUPER_MAILLE replaces MAILLE: - Standardisation of the vocabulary; one now uses the keyword SUPER_MAILLE when it is a matter of substructuring (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.8 CALC_ELEM REPE_COQUE new: - Under this factor keyword one finds the parameters for defining the local post-processing frame of the shell elements, similar to those of AFFE_CARA_ELEM. The post-processing can thus be carried out in different frames by mesh-cell groups (cf. [8.3.21]). New options ARCO_ELNO_SIGM/ARCO_NOEU_SIGM - These options compute the arch and cantilever stresses useful for post-processing in a local frame on the faces of a 3D structure. This is used in particular for the stress analysis on the skin of dams (cf. [8.3.21]). INDI_ERRE renamed to INDI_ERREUR - In order to be consistent with CALC_NO (cf. [8.3.5]). 1.4.9 CALC_FATIGUE New criterion VMIS_TRESCA: - Computes the maximum amplitude of variation of a stress tensor (cf. [8.3.18]). Changes to the criterion names: - MATAKE becomes MATAKE_MODI_AC, DOMM_MAXI becomes MATAKE_MODI_AV and FATEMI_SOCIE becomes FATESOCI_MODI_AV (cf. [8.3.18]). 1.4.10 CALC_FONCTION NORME default value removed: - In order to avoid any risk of error, there is no longer a default value for this keyword for the operation SPEC_OSCI (cf. [8.3.21]). 1.4.11 CALC_G NUME_FOND new: - In the case of multiple crack fronts with X-FEM, makes it possible to choose the crack front which one post-processes (cf. [8.3.4]). New option: CALC_K_MAX - Makes it possible to distinguish the opening from the closing of cracks, which CALC_G_MAX does not allow (cf. [8.3.10]). New smoothing method: LAGRANGE_REGU - Overcomes the drawbacks of the LAGRANGE smoothing method for closed crack fronts, for which the LEGENDRE method is not applicable, or for unmeshed cracks (X-FEM) (cf. [8.3.11]). Removal of MODELE, CHAM_MATER, DEPL, VITE, ACCE - The information is extracted directly from the RESULTAT concept on input to the command, in order to avoid any risk of error (same logic as CALC_ELEM/CALC_NO) (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.12 CREA_CHAMP OPERATION, new possibilities: R2C, C2R - The R2C option makes it possible respectively to produce a complex field from a real field with a zero imaginary part. The C2R option makes it possible to extract the real or imaginary part of a complex field (cf. [8.3.12]). COEF_C new - For the operation ASSE, makes it possible to apply a complex coefficient to the values of a field (cf. [8.3.12]). 1.4.13 CREA_TABLE TYPE_TABLE new - In order to identify the tables which contain names of functions, the type table_fonction has been introduced (cf. [8.3.17]). Note: one can extract these functions with the command RECU_FONCTION, and print them directly with the command IMPR_TABLE, option IMPR_FONCTION=’OUI’. 1.4.14 DEFI_COMPOR FAMI_SYS_GLIS, new possibility: BCC24 - Family of slip systems specific to bainitic steels (cf. [8.3.11]). The parameters H1 to H6 have been introduced under DEFI_MATERIAU under ECRO_ISOT1 in order to define the interaction matrix between the slip systems. ANGL_EULER new: - See AFFE_CARA_ELEM (cf. [8.3.11]). 1.4.15 DEFI_INTERF_DYNA DDL_ACTIF removed: - Only the MASQUE option can be used (cf. [8.3.3]). 1.4.16 DEFI_MAILLAGE SUPER_MAILLE and DEFI_SUPER_MAILLE replace MAILLE and DEFI_MAILLE: - See AFFE_MODELE (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.17 DEBUT / POURSUITE SD_VERI new: - Intended for developers: triggers the checking of the data structures in the course of the analysis (cf. [8.3.2]). 1.4.18 DEPL_INTERNE SUPER_MAILLE replaces MAILLE: - See AFFE_MODELE (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.19 EXEC_LOGICIEL MAILLAGE new: - Makes it possible to execute a geometric data set in order to produce the mesh by calling the mesher directly from the Aster command set (cf. [8.3.10]). If this may be of interest in certain studies, parametric ones in particular, it is more prudent to produce the mesh, and to check it, before launching the Aster study. 1.4.20 IMPR_RESU UNITE by default in GMSH format - The default unit in GMSH format is now 37, which corresponds to the pos type in astk (cf. [8.3.21]). 1.4.21 LIRE_IMPE_MISS / MACRO_MISS_3D TYPE = ‘BINAIRE’ new: - In order to improve the performance of reading the impedances coming from Miss3D, one can use a binary format (cf. [8.3.13]). 1.4.22 LIRE_MAILLAGE RENOMME new: - Makes it possible, when reading a mesh with FORMAT=’MED’, to rename certain names of mesh-cell groups or of node groups. One can thus remove possible conflicts between the MED group names, which may be written on 32 characters, whereas in Code_Aster they are limited to 8 characters (cf. [8.3.22]). 1.4.23 MACRO_MATR_ASSE CHAR_CINE new: - Taking into account of boundary conditions of kinematic-load type (cf. [8.3.1]). 1.4.24 MACR_ADAP_MAIL SENSIBILITE new: - It is now possible to adapt a mesh according to the derivative of a field (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.25 MACR_ELEM_STAT PROJ_MESU, MODE_MESURE new: - Make it possible, from the measured information, to estimate the eigenmodes of a structure following a structural modification (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.26 MACR_RECAL LIST_DERIV new: - Makes it possible to use the derivatives coming from the SENSIBILITE analysis; it is possible to mix finite differences and sensitivity (cf. [8.3.8]). METHODE / GRADIENT / FONCTIONNELLE / INTER_FONC_MAXI new: - These keywords make it possible to parameterise the new recalibration algorithms available (cf. [8.3.20]). AFFICHAGE new: - Makes it possible to choose when the graphs are displayed (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.27 MODI_MAILLAGE MODELE removed: - It is no longer necessary to give the model in order to orient mesh cells; the keyword has been removed (cf. [8.3.6]). 1.4.28 NORM_MODE MASSE, RAIDE, AMOR new: - Makes it possible to renormalise the modes of a base_modale concept, a Ritz basis for example (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.29 POST_RCCM TABL_RESU_PRES new: - Together with the presence of TABL_RESU_THER, activates the computation of the thermal-ratcheting criterion for the EVOLUTION option (cf. [8.3.16]). For the UNITAIRE option, the thermal-ratcheting criterion is computed on the presence of RESU_THER. SY_MAX new: - Conventional yield limit, an alternative to the value SY_02 present in the RCCM material (cf. [8.3.16]). 1.4.30 PROJ_CHAMP NOM_PARA new: - see PROJ_MESU_MODAL (cf. [8.3.2]). TRANSF_GEOM_2 new: - To define 2 or 3 functions (fx, fy, fz) of the geometric transformation applied to MODELE_2 before the projection (cf. [8.3.2]). 1.4.31 PROJ_MESU_MODAL NOM_PARA new: - Makes it possible to select the data which will be kept in the result data structure (cf. [8.3.2]).
