TRANSF_GEOM_2 new: - To define 2 or 3 functions (fx, fy, fz) of the geometric transformation applied to MODELE_2 before the projection (cf. [8.3.2]). 1.4.32 PROJ_SPEC_BASE TOUT_CMP new: - Makes it possible to take into account the total dimensionless spectrum and not only one component of the mode shape (cf. [8.3.8]). 1.4.33 PROPA_XFEM METHODE and RAYON new: - The domain of application of the command is extended to the 3D propagation of cracks in mixed mode on arbitrary tetrahedral meshes or on hexahedral meshes with parallel opposite faces (cf. [8.3.9]). 1.4.34 RECU_FONCTION NAPPE new: - Makes it possible to extract a function from a nappe for a given VALE_PARA_FONC (cf. [8.3.21]). 1.4.35 REST_BASE_PHYS GROUP_NO, NOEUD, GROUP_MA, MAILLE new: - Make it possible to carry out a recovery of a generalised concept onto the physical basis at certain nodes only (cf. [8.3.20]). 1.4.36 TEST_RESU VALE, VALE_I, VALE_R new behaviour: - One can validate a result if it corresponds to one of the values supplied (cf. [8.3.17]). 2 New features between 8.2 and 8.3 2.1 General changes The command variables corrosion, hydration and irradiation are no longer supplied in AFFE_CHAR_MECA but in AFFE_MATERIAU under the keyword AFFE_VARC. This will make it possible to extend the number and the type of the command variables. Eventually, temperature, drying and the anelastic strains should merge into this mould (cf. [8.1.4, 8.2.18]). 2.2 New commands 2.2.1 CALC_G The commands CALC_G_THETA_T and CALC_G_LOCAL_T have been merged into a single command CALC_G. 2.2.2 POST_MAIL_XFEM / POST_CHAM_XFEM The command POST_MAIL_XFEM makes it possible to generate a cracked mesh from a sound mesh and from the X-FEM crack. This mesh is produced only for visualisation purposes and must not be used for an analysis. The command POST_CHAM_XFEM uses this cracked mesh and makes it possible to create a displacement field associated with the cracked mesh. This displacement field can then be viewed (IDEAS, GMSH…). 2.3 Removals The following functionalities have been withdrawn in version 8.3: - Constitutive law CHABOCHE: the model VISC_CIN2_CHAB makes it possible, among other things, to do the same thing, - OHNO law: to treat progressive-strain problems, it is recommended to use the elastoplastic or elastoviscoplastic model of TAHERI, - THM constitutive laws: ELAS_THM, SURF_ETAT_SATU, SURF_ETAT_NSAT, CAM_CLAY_THM, LIQU_SATU_GAT, LIQU_NSAT_GAT, - Modellings APPUI_REP and ASSE_GRIL, - Commands POST_SIMPLIFIE, DIST_LIGN_3D, DEFI_THER_JOULE, - Computation option INDU_MUTU. 2.4 Modified commands 2.4.1 Constitutive laws of the non-linear operators In general, a similar keyword is added/modified in the command DEFI_MATERIAU. HOEK_BROWN modified: - In THM, one now distinguishes HOEK_BROWN_EFF (the plasticity criterion being formulated in effective stresses) and HOEK_BROWN_TOT (the same criterion formulated in total stresses). No change in pure mechanics (cf. [8.2.1]). ELAS_HYPER new: - Hyperelastic constitutive law of Signorini (Mooney-Rivlin) (cf. [8.2.8]). IRRAD3M new: - Constitutive law of steels under irradiation (cf. [8.2.9]). DIS_GRICRA modified: - The parameters of the grid–rod connection have been extensively modified in order to be more easily identifiable and to improve the integration of the law itself (cf. [8.2.17]). DEFORMATION=’COROTATIONNEL’ new: - Large strains in a corotational formulation for the Aster–Zmat coupling (cf. [8.2.12]). 2.4.2 AFFE_CARA_ELEM NOEUD, MAILLE, GROUP_NO, GROUP_MA moved - These keywords are accessible according to whether the characteristic of the discrete elements is “_N” or “_L” (cf. [8.2.16]). 2.4.3 AFFE_CHAR_MECA / AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F DIST_POUTRE/DIST_COQUE and CARA_ELEM new: - Allows, during the treatment of contact, a gap corresponding to the radius of the beam (circular section) or to the thickness of the shell to be taken into account (cf. [8.2.6, 8.2.16]). METHODE = ‘GPC’ new: - The projected conjugate-gradient method for contact is the iterative version of the active-constraint method, which comes into its own (performance in terms of memory space and of solution time) when the number of contact constraints is large (cf. [8.2.9]). LIAISON_UNILATER new: - Makes it possible to impose a unilateral condition on any degree of freedom (cf. [8.2.12]). VECT_ORIE_POU new: - Makes it possible to define the orientation of the beams in the case of beam–beam contact (cf. [8.2.19]). FACE_IMPO / SANS_GROUP_MA, SANS_MAILLE new: - Makes it possible to exclude the nodes of certain mesh cells from the imposed condition in order to avoid redundant relations (cf. [8.2.17]). 2.4.4 AFFE_MODELE Modelling: C_PLAN_X, D_PLAN_X - XFEM modelling in plane stresses and plane strains (cf. [8.2.1, 8.2.14]). Modellings: 3D_THH2MD, 3D_THH2MS… - Extension to 3D of the HH2 modellings (cf. [8.2.9]). 2.4.5 CALC_ELEM QIRE_EL.._SIGM, QIZ2_EL.._SIGM new options associated with the keyword RESU_DUAL: - Error indicators in quantity of interest (cf. [8.2.16]). 2.4.6 CALC_G LISSAGE = ‘LAGRANGE_NO_NO’ new: - Value at the nodes of the error indicator in quantity of interest (cf. [8.2.16]). 2.4.7 CALC_NO QIRE_NOEU_ELEM new option: - Error indicators in quantity of interest (cf. [8.2.16]). 2.4.8 CALC_TABLE ACTION new: - This factor keyword makes it possible to apply several operations in their order of appearance (cf. [8.2.11]). REGEXP new: - Makes it possible to filter the rows of a table by applying a regular expression to a column of text type (cf. [8.2.16]). SENSIBILITE new: - Makes it possible to access a derived table (for example coming from a post-processing of the derivatives of a result) (cf. [8.2.16]). 2.4.9 CREA_CHAMP OPERATION=’NORMALE’ new: - Produces a field at the nodes of the normals to the elements (cf. [8.2.13]). 2.4.10 CREA_TABLE SENSIBILITE new: - Makes it possible to produce a table with the sensitive label (that is to say as if it were the derivative of another table with respect to a parameter) (cf. [8.2.5]). 2.4.11 DEFI_FOND_FISS FOND_SUP, FOND_INF new: - Makes it possible to define the crack front by two lists of nodes, each referring to one lip (cf. [8.2.1]). PREC_NORM new: - Defines the accuracy with which one searches for the nodes belonging to the normal to the crack front. This operation was previously done in POST_K1_K2_K3 (cf. [8.2.20]). 2.4.12 DETRUIRE SENSIBILITE new: - Makes it possible to destroy a sensitive concept (cf. [8.2.16]). 2.4.13 DYNA_LINE_HARM - The command is now re-entrant (cf. [8.2.1]). 2.4.14 DYNA_LINE_TRAN ACCE_INIT new: - Makes it possible to supply an initial acceleration field (cf. [8.2.3]). SOLVEUR modified: - Standardisation with the other commands (cf. [8.2.11]). 2.4.15 DYNA_NON_LINE ETAT_INIT/ACCE new: - Makes it possible to supply an initial acceleration field (cf. [8.2.3]). LIST_AMOR new: - Makes it possible to give a damping list coming from DEFI_LIST_REEL (cf. [8.2.1]). MODI_EQUI new: - Specifies whether or not one modifies the equilibrium equation. If MODI_EQUI=’OUI’, one uses a complete HHT scheme; if MODI_EQUI=’NON’, one uses the HHT scheme as it was until now (cf. [8.2.7]). CRIT_FLAMB new: - Makes it possible to carry out a stability analysis on the updated stiffness matrix (cf. [8.2.11]). MODE_VIBR new: - Vibratory modal analysis on the global matrices (cf. [8.2.11]). DIFF_CENT replaces NEWMARK: - The central-difference scheme no longer requires parameters (cf. [8.2.11]). TCHAMWA new: - Dissipative time-integration scheme (cf. [8.2.11]). 2.4.16 DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI ETAT_INIT/ACCE new: - Makes it possible to supply an initial acceleration field (cf. [8.2.3]). MASS_DIAG new: - Makes it possible to use the diagonal mass matrix (cf. [8.2.12]). MASS_GENE, RIGI_GENE, AMOR_GENE new under PROJ_MODAL EXCIT_GENE new: - Explicit solution from matrices projected onto a Ritz basis (cf. [8.2.13]). STOP_CFL new: - This keyword, introduced at the same time as the check of the stability condition on the time step (known as the CFL condition), makes it possible to turn a possible error message into a mere warning, if it is judged unjustified (case of elements for which Code_Aster does not know how to compute the condition, or a stabilising phenomenon in the modelling) (cf. [8.2.15]). 2.4.17 DYNA_TRAN_MODAL Definition of the impact nodes: - This can be done by giving a mesh cell of type SEG2 (keyword MAILLE), or else a group of one (single) mesh cell of type SEG2 (keyword GROUP_MA) (cf. [8.2.1]). 2.4.18 IMPR_CO CONCEPT new: - This factor keyword is created in order to be able to associate the name of a sensitive parameter with a concept (cf. [8.2.13]). 2.4.19 LIRE_TABLE TYPE_TABLE removed: - Tables are no longer “sub-typed”; only one type, “table”, remains. This is transparent in the other commands (cf. [8.2.2]). 2.4.20 MACR_LIGN_COUPE GROUP_MA, MAILLE new: - Limits the extraction of the values to the mesh cells specified (cf. [8.2.20]). 2.4.21 MACRO_MISS_3D New parameters: - About fifteen keywords correspond to the OPTIMISS file and make it possible to define the data describing the soil in MISS3D (cf. [8.2.13]). 2.4.22 POST_K1_K2_K3 TYPE_MAILLAGE, NB_NOEUD_COUPE new: - Allows post-processing on free meshes (only mapped meshes were supported previously), for which one specifies the number of nodes to be built in the direction normal to the crack front (cf. [8.2.20]). 2.4.23 POST_RELEVE_T OPERATION = ’EXTREMA’ new: - Post-processing making it possible to extract the min and max values of a field as well as their location (cf. [8.2.7]). 2.4.24 PROJ_CHAMP Accepts result concepts of type dyna_trans (produced by DYNA_LINE_TRAN) (cf. [8.2.1]). NUME_DDL new, RIGI_MECA, MASS_MECA, AMOR_MECA removed: - Makes it possible to impose the numbering of the degrees of freedom for any type of data structure and not only mode_meca, with the old method using xxxx_MECA (cf. [8.2.4]). 2.4.25 POST_ELEM INTEGRALE new: - Makes it possible to compute the mean and the integral of the component of a field (cf. [8.2.12]). 2.4.26 POST_RCCM MX, MX_TUBU new: - Makes it possible to carry out an RCCM analysis with the unit method by defining two force torsors: one for the branch connection, one for the nozzle (cf. [8.2.12]). 2.4.27 REST_BASE_PHYS CYCLIQUE new: - Makes it possible to recover, onto the complete mesh of a structure with cyclic symmetry, an analysis carried out on a single sector (cf. [8.2.4]). RESU_PHYS new: - Recovery of an analysis carried out on a Ritz basis in DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI (cf. [8.2.13]). 2.4.28 STAT_NON_LINE METHODE = ‘FETI’ new: - Functionality under development; the domain of application is limited (cf. [8.2.12]). 3 New features between 7.4/8.0 and 8.2 3.1 General changes 3.1.1 Local convergence criteria The local convergence criteria are by nature relevant only for a given behaviour; the accepted residual, the integration scheme or the number of iterations can now be defined differently for each behaviour of the model. From the point of view of the syntax, the keywords RESI_INTE_RELA, INTER_INTE_REAL, INTER_INTE_MAXI, RESO_INTE are moved from CONVERGENCE to COMP_INCR/COMP_ELAS (an occurrence of which defines each behaviour). The commands concerned are DYNA_NON_LINE, DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI, STAT_NON_LINE and, in cascade, the macro-commands CALC_PRECONT, MACR_ASCOUF_CALC, MACR_ASPIC_CALC, MACR_CABRI_CALC. 3.1.2 MUMPS solver A new direct solver is available in Code_Aster : MUMPS. It makes it possible to solve problems known with the classical solvers when the matrix is not positive (XFEM case, incompressible elements, …). It can be used by the commands DYNA_NON_LINE, MECA_STATIQUE, RESO_LDLT, STAT_NON_LINE, THER_LINEAIRE and THER_NON_LINE (cf. [8.0.14]). Note for the local versions This solver is not part of the Code_Aster sources; it is an external package. 3.1.3 FETI solver The FETI solver is a parallel solver by domain decomposition. It is under development; its field of application is therefore limited in version 8.2. 3.2 New commands 3.2.1 CALC_TABLE This command makes it possible to handle the data of the tables in the manner of a spreadsheet. The command makes it possible to carry out operations on the data of the tables. The operations currently available are: - concatenate / combine two tables having common parameters, - apply a formula, - rename parameters, - filter the rows according to certain criteria, - extract columns from a table, - order the rows. 3.2.2 INFO_FONCTION / CALC_FONCTION The command CALC_FONCTION has been thoroughly rewritten so that it is simple and quick to introduce new generic processings into it at the request of users. Thus, only the operations which compute a function (or a nappe) from other functions have been kept in CALC_FONCTION. It should be noted that the envelope-smoothing operation of the floor spectra (SRO), LISS_ENVELOP, has been revised according to the recommendations of EDF Septen. All the operations on functions which produce something else (today this is only a table) are now available in the command INFO_FONCTION: - MAX, RMS, NOCI_SEISME, NORME and ECART_TYPE. 3.2.3 LIRE_FORC_MISS / LIRE_IMPE_MISS LIRE_IMPE_MISS and LIRE_FORC_MISS make it possible to create respectively a generalised matrix and a generalised seismic-force vector from the soil impedance matrix or from the seismic soil forces created by MISS3D for a given extraction frequency. 3.2.4 POST_MAIL_XFEM / POST_CHAM_XFEM 3.2.5 MAC_MODES This command makes it possible to compute an orthogonality criterion, the Modal Assurance Criterion, between two modal bases (in general, one experimental and one computed) (cf. [8.1.14]). 3.3 Modified commands 3.3.1 AFFE_CARA_ELEM CARA_SECT removed: - Unused keyword (cf. [8.0.6]). RIGI_PARASOL / GROUP_MA_POI1 and GROUP_MA_SEG2 new: - Make it possible to define a spring mat in order to model a foundation displacement, a ground slip, and to apply force boundary conditions (cf. [8.0.17]). 3.3.2 AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F can be used with STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE. GROUP_MA, MAILLE new: - Definition of the zones to be constrained (cf. [8.0.6]). 3.3.3 AFFE_CHAR_MECA CONTACT / METHODE=’VERIF’ new: - Makes it possible to check whether or not there is material interpenetration a posteriori without paying the extra cost of the solution with contact (cf. [8.0.7]). CONTACT / GLISSIERE, ALARME_JEU new: - Makes it possible to carry out, with the active-constraint method, “sticking” contact: the facing surfaces cannot separate, an alarm being issued in the case where the gap becomes excessive (value defined by the user) (cf. [8.0.7], [8.1.11]). CONTACT_INIT new: - This keyword makes it possible to do without artificial stiffnesses blocking the motions of rigid bodies (cf. [8.0.8], [8.0.11]). CONTACT / COMPLIANCE new: - Introduction of a micro–macro model for the contact interface (effect of roughness at the microscopic scale) (cf. [8.1.13]). CHAMNO_IMPO new: - Makes it possible to take the content of a CHAM_NO as the right-hand side of the linear relation (cf. [8.0.8]). ELIM_MULT new: - In the case where one wishes to tie several meshes together (keyword LIAISON_MAIL), the redundant conditions are now eliminated in order to avoid obtaining zero pivots at the moment of the solution (ELIM_MULT=’NON’). If, in certain particular cases, one does not wish to eliminate these conditions, one can modify the default value (cf. [8.0.3]). LIAISON_CYCL new: - Application of a cyclic-symmetry condition with a phase shift (cf. [8.0.8]). PRESSION_CALCULE removed: - EVOL_CHAR does the same thing and accepts other types of fields (cf. [8.1.19]). VERI_DDL removed: - The inexpensive check is now systematic (cf. [8.1.19]). 3.3.4 AFFE_MATERIAU AFFE_VARC new: - The command variables are now supplied in AFFE_MATERIAU and no longer in the solution operators DYNA_NON_LINE/STAT_NON_LINE (cf. [8.1.4]). 3.3.5 AFFE_MODELE New modellings PLAN_ELDI, PLAN_JOINT, AXIS_ELDI, AXIS_JOINT: - XXX_JOINT replace XXXX_FISSURE in order to distinguish the JOINT elements from the elements with internal discontinuity ELDI (cf. [8.0.18]). New modellings XXXX_THMS: - These so-called “selective” modellings rely on an integration scheme at the vertices for the terms of capacitive type, and at the Gauss points for the terms of diffusive type (cf. [8.1.10]). 3.3.6 CALC_ELEM DURT_ELGA_TEMP removed: - The computations are now carried out at the nodes (DURT_ELNO_TEMP) (cf. [8.0.14]). 3.3.7 CALC_FATIGUE COEFF_PREECROU new: - This parameter makes it possible to take a pre-hardening into account in the criteria of MATAKE, DANG_VAN_MODI_AC/AV and DOMM_MAXI (cf. [8.0.3]). 3.3.8 CREA_MAILLAGE CREA_FISS new: - Makes it possible to generate QUAD4 mesh cells (in order to associate finite elements with a discontinuity with them) from node groups (cf. [8.0.13], [8.0.18]). QUAD_LINE new: - Transformation of quadratic mesh cells into linear mesh cells (cf. [8.0.13]). 3.3.9 CALC_FATIGUE CRITERE = ’FATEMI_SOCIE’ new: - Addition of the criterion of Fatemi and Socie in elasticity and plasticity (cf. [8.1.5]). 3.3.10 CALC_FLUI_STRU AMOR_REDUIT_CONN new: - Connors method for the analysis of the vibratory behaviour of steam-generator tubes (cf. [8.1.1]). 3.3.11 CALC_G_LOCAL_T / CALC_G_THETA_T OPTION = ’K_G_MODA’ new: - Computation of the modal stress intensity factors (cf. [8.1.17]). 3.3.12 CALC_META META_INIT, META_ELGA_TEMP removed: - Assuming that the integration-point families are the same for the metallurgical analysis and the mechanical analysis was not very sound. The computations are now done at the nodes. META_INIT is therefore replaced by META_INIT_ELNO and META_ELGA_TEMP is removed; META_ELNO_TEMP is computed by default (cf. [8.0.14]). 3.3.13 CREA_CHAMP EXTR / TABLE new: - Makes it possible to create a field from data contained in a table (cf. [8.1.17]). 3.3.14 DEBUT / POURSUITE ERREUR new: - Makes it possible to raise a Python exception instead of stopping at the fortran level (useful only for particular macro-commands) (cf. [8.1.20]). IMPR_MACRO new: - Makes it possible to choose the display mode of the commands launched by a macro-command, which is now deactivated by default (cf. [8.1.13]). RESERVE_CPU new: - Makes it possible to ensure that one has a minimum of time for the last stages of the analysis (closing of the database, transfer of the results) (cf. [8.0.13]). 3.3.15 DEFI_BASE_MODALE ORTHO_BASE new: - Makes it possible to re-orthogonalise a modal basis obtained by concatenation of several bases; the collinear modes can be eliminated by EXTR_MODES (cf. [8.1.7]). 3.3.16 DEFI_FISS_XFEM CONTACT, INTEGRATION new: - Modelling of contact on the crack lips with the continuous method (cf. [8.0.6]) and choice of the integration method at the nodes on the contact facets (cf. [8.1.7]). RAYON_ENRI new: - Makes it possible to define a radius bounding the enrichment zone of the nodes at the crack front (cf. [8.1.19]). ALGO_LAGR new: - Selection of the algorithm for choosing the Lagrange multiplier space for contact with X-FEM (cf. [8.1.19]). 3.3.17 DEFI_FLUI_STRU CSTE_CONNORS, RHO_TUBE, NB_CONNORS new: - Connors method for the analysis of the vibratory behaviour of steam-generator tubes (cf. [8.1.1]). 3.3.18 DEFI_GROUP DETR_GROUP_MA / DETR_GROUP_NO new: - Make it possible to destroy existing groups; one can if need be create groups of the same names (cf. [8.1.6]). 3.3.19 DEFI_MATERIAU RUPT_FRAG, RUPT_FRAG_FO new: - Definition of the parameters of the Barenblatt law (fracture toughness, critical stress and displacement jump) as a function of temperature (cf. [8.0.1]). LEMAITE_IRRA, LMARC_IRRA, GRAN_IRRA_LOG replace GRAN_IRRA, FLU_IRRA: - Definition of the parameters of the various laws which one previously found under the name ASSE_COMBU (cf. [8.0.8]). GATT_MONERIE new: - New thermomechanical elastoviscoplastic law of the fuel (cf. [8.0.16]). BETON_REGLE_PR new: - Regulatory concrete law known as the “parabola-rectangle” (cf. [8.0.17]). HOEK_BROWN new: - Modified Hoek-Brown constitutive law for the mechanical analysis of rocks (cf. [8.1.1]). CABLE modification: - The elastic parameters must be supplied under the keyword ELAS (cf. [8.1.17]). 3.3.20 DYNA_NON_LINE See STAT_NON_LINE. 3.3.21 EXTR_MODES SEUIL_X/_Y/_Z new: - Makes it possible to select the modes on a directional criterion (cf. [8.1.17]). 3.3.22 GENE_MATR_ALEA MATR_MOYEN new: - Makes it possible to generate a random macr_elem_dyna from a mean value (cf. [8.1.8]). 3.3.23 IMPR_GENE FORMAT, UNITE moved: - Were previously under the factor keyword GENE (cf. [8.0.21]). 3.3.24 IMPR_RESU PARTIE new: - Makes it possible to select the real or imaginary part when printing complex fields (cf. [8.1.1]). GROUP_MA, MAILLE, GROUP_NO, NOEUD new: - Selection of topological entities added for the MED format (cf. [8.1.13]). 3.3.25 LIRE_RESU POSI_AMOR new: - In IDEAS (unv) format, makes it possible to recover the reduced damping (cf. [8.1.17]). 3.3.26 MACR_CABRI_MAIL FICHIER removed: - Was no longer used (cf. [8.0.6]). 3.3.27 MACR_LIGN_COUPE LIGNE_COUPE / VECT_Y new: - Makes it possible to define a local frame for the post-processing (cf. [8.1.6]). 3.3.28 MACR_RECAL GRAPHIQUE / FORMAT new: - Makes it possible to produce the curves in Xmgrace or Gnuplot format (cf. [8.1.22]). 3.3.29 MECA_STATIQUE NUME_COUCHE, NIVE_COUCHE, ANGLE and PLAN removed: - These keywords were used for the computation of certain options which are no longer computed by MECA_STATIQUE but by CALC_ELEM/CALC_NO (cf. [8.0.5]). 3.3.30 MODI_MODELE_XFEM CRITERE new: - Makes it possible to remove the jump degrees of freedom in order to avoid an ill-conditioning of the matrix (cf. [8.1.7]). 3.3.31 POST_K1_K2_K3 SYME_CHAR new: - Makes it possible to take into account the symmetry of the modelling in the computation of the stress intensity factors (cf. [8.0.6]). 3.3.32 PROJ_CHAMP PROL_ZERO new: - Makes it possible to extend the projected fields by zero where the initial field is not defined (cf. [8.1.4]). 3.3.33 STAT_NON_LINE VARI_COMM removed: - The command variables are supplied in AFFE_MATERIAU (cf. [8.1.4]). AFFICHAGE new: - Customisation of the display of the convergence table (cf. [8.1.11]). 3.3.34 TEST_FONCTION VALE_ABS new: - To test the absolute value of a result (cf. [8.1.1]). 3.3.35 TEST_RESU RESU_GENE new: - To test the resu_gene concepts (cf. [8.0.19]). VALE_ABS new: - To test the absolute value of a result (cf. [8.1.1]). 3.3.36 TEST_TABLE VALE_ABS new: - To test the absolute value of a result (cf. [8.1.1]). Page intentionally left blank.

u4.01.05 1 u4.01.05 New features and modifications of version 9 Organisation(s): EDF-R&D/AMA User's manual Booklet U4.0-: Use of the commands Document: U4.01.05 1 u4.01.05 New features and modifications of version 9 Summary: The purpose of this document is to provide an overall view of the syntax modifications and of the new possibilities of the Code_Aster commands introduced during the development of version 9, that is, since version 8.4. Revision index B of this document thus reports the changes introduced since version 9.1 of June 2007 and valid for version 9.2 of December 2007. Paragraph 2 deals with the syntactic changes which occurred between version 8.4 (December 2006) and version 9.1 (June 2007). For further details, one should consult the documentation of the commands and the histor file of the corresponding sub-version (e.g.: [9.1.7], section Support/Histor of the site www.code-aster.org). The commands affected are listed in alphabetical order. 1 New features between 9.1 and 9.2 1.1 New commands 1.1.1 CALCUL The purpose of this new command is to compute the elementary tangent matrices and the elementary internal forces, and to integrate the constitutive law (cf. [9.1.7]). Its principle is: knowing U-, SIGMA-, VARI- and dU, one computes: - SIGMA+, VARI+, the elementary tangent matrices, the elementary residual vectors if OPTION=('COMPORTEMENT', 'FORC_INT_ELEM', 'MATR_TANG_ELEM') - SIGMA+, VARI+, the elementary residual vectors if OPTION=('COMPORTEMENT', 'FORC_INT_ELEM') 1.1.2 FACTORISER and RESOUDRE replace FACT_GRAD/FACT_LDLT and RESO_GRAD/RESO_LDLT The commands FACT_GRAD and FACT_LDLT have been merged into a single one: FACTORISER. Likewise for RESO_GRAD and RESO_LDLT, which have been merged into RESOUDRE (cf. [9.1.14]). The keyword MATR_FACT of RESO_LDLT becomes MATR. The keyword MATR_ASSE of RESO_GRAD becomes MATR, and MATR_FACT becomes MATR_PREC. 1.2 General modifications 1.2.1 Command variables The use of temperature as a command variable in mechanics must now be done using AFFE_MATERIAU / AFFE_VARC / NOM_VARC=’TEMP’ instead of AFFE_CHAR_MECA / TEMP_CALCULEE. The former syntax TEMP_CALCULE will have disappeared in the next version. See the note concerning the reference temperature, § AFFE_MATERIAU/TEMP_REF. 1.2.2 Constitutive behaviour ELAS_VMIS_PUIS This constitutive behaviour, equivalent to VMIS_ISOT_PUIS in linear elasticity, has been available since 9.1.15. The keyword ELAS_VMIS_PUIS (analogue of ELAS_VMIS_TRAC) appears in the commands STAT_NON_LINE, DYNA_NON_LINE and CALC_G. 1.2.3 Distributed parallel MUMPS solver This change consists in calling the MUMPS solver in distributed parallel version, as opposed to the centralised parallel version. In both cases, the solution of the linear system is performed in parallel on several nodes and processors of the machine. In the distributed version, the computation of the elementary matrices is distributed over the various processors, then the assembly, and finally the solution of the system. The distribution mode is chosen via the keyword PARALLELISME. The operators concerned are DYNA_LINE_TRAN, DYNA_NON_LINE, MECA_STATIQUE, THER_LINEAIRE, THER_NON_LINE, STAT_NON_LINE. Friction is excluded from the scope of use. The development is still undergoing validation The solver is available only on the centralised server for the moment (cf. [9.1.16]). 1.3 Removals 1.3.1 FACT_GRAD/FACT_LDLT and RESO_GRAD/RESO_LDLT Replaced by FACTORISER and RESOUDRE (cf. [9.1.14]). 1.4 Modified commands 1.4.1 AFFE_CHAR_CINE EVOL_IMPO new: - Makes it possible to define the result of a previous analysis as a kinematic loading. The intended application is the structural zoom, in which the displacements obtained during the first analysis are imposed on the boundary of the zoom (cf. [9.1.14]). 1.4.2 AFFE_CHAR_MECA / AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F PRES_REP / FISSURE new: - Makes it possible to apply a pressure on an unmeshed crack, defined by DEFI_FISS_XFEM (cf. [9.1.8]). CONTACT / GROUP_MA_FOND new: - Together with the use of METHODE=’VERIF’, this keyword makes it possible to define the crack tip on which it is unnecessary to check interpenetration (cf. [9.1.11]). LIAISON_SOLIDE / TRAN, ANGL_NAUT, CENTRE new: - These keywords make it possible to impose the displacement of a non-deformable part of the model (cf. [9.1.13]). APPL_FORC_xxxx removed: - These keywords were used for the loading GRAPPE_FLUIDE (cf. [9.1.22]). 1.4.3 AFFE_MATERIAU AFFE_VARC / FONC_INST new: - This keyword has been added in order to apply a loading, thermal for example, whose time evolution is different from that of the mechanical analysis. For example, the mechanical analysis can cycle over a thermal evolution. The function supplied then makes it possible to pass from the time of the loading to the time of the mechanical analysis (cf. [9.1.5]). TEMP_REF no longer has a default value: In order to avoid the risk of wrong results with an incorrect account taken of the reference temperature, an analysis is considered as thermo-mechanical if a temperature field exists on the finite element in question. In that case it is compulsory to supply both the reference temperature AND the thermal expansion coefficient. If one of these two values is absent, the code will stop in fatal error with a warning message for the user (cf. [9.1.15]). 1.4.4 AFFE_MODELE MODELISATION: GRILLE_EXCENTRE replaces GRILLE: - Account taken of the offset (cf. [9.1.4]). MODELISATION: xx_XFEM_CONT new: - The finite elements xx_XFEM no longer have a degree of freedom for contact, in order to treat efficiently the problems without contact. The finite elements xx_XFEM_CONT are added for that purpose (cf. [9.1.11]). 1.4.5 CALC_FONCTION FRACTILE new: - Computation of the fractile of nappes or of functions (cf. [9.1.8]). PUISSANCE / EXPOSANT real: - It is now possible to take the real power of a function (cf. [9.1.9]). 1.4.6 CALC_MATR_ELEM MECA_GYRO new: - Computation of the gyroscopic damping matrix for the analysis of shaft lines (cf. [9.1.16]). 1.4.7 CALC_TABLE VALE_xxx modified: - In IMPR_TABLE and CALC_TABLE, it is possible to filter the rows of a table. By repeating the factor keyword FILTRE, one applies an AND between the filters. One can now apply an OR by giving several values to the keywords VALE_xxx (cf. [9.1.3]). 1.4.8 COMB_SISM_MODAL MULTI_APPUI new: - Allows account to be taken of correlated excitations in the multi-support case. The user now has the choice between MONO_APPUI=’OUI’, MULTI_APPUI=’CORRELE’ (new option) or ’DECORRELE’, which corresponds to the option available previously (cf. [9.1.18]). 1.4.9 CREA_MAILLAGE HEXA20_27 new: - Makes it possible to transform the HEXA20 elements of a mesh into HEXA27 elements (cf. [9.1.6]). 1.4.10 CREA_RESU OPERATION=’ASSE’ new: - Makes it possible to assemble several thermal analysis results, possibly translating them. This operation can also be supplemented with AFFE_MATERIAU/AFFE_VARC, FONC_INST in order to repeat a thermal loading (cf. [9.1.5]). 1.4.11 DEBUT and POURSUITE RESERVE_CPU new default value: - This keyword makes it possible to reserve a fraction of the total time of a study (requested in astk) at the end of the run for the system tasks (compression, file copy…). The value is set by default to 10% of the time requested, with a limit of 900 seconds (cf. [9.1.20). 1.4.12 DEFI_FONCTION ABSCISSE / ORDONNEE new: - Equivalents of the keywords LIST_PARA and LIST_RESU, except that one passes lists of values instead of list_r8 concepts (cf. [9.1.9]). 1.4.13 DEFI_LIST_ENTI OPERATION = ‘NUME_ORDRE’ new: - This makes it possible to extract the order numbers of a resultat concept in a given interval. One can then use this list in all the commands which accept the keyword LIST_ORDRE (cf. [9.1.16]). 1.4.14 DEFI_MATERIAU RELATION_KIT / THM_DIFFU new: - For unsaturated models and the coupling laws LIQU_xxx_GAZ, the user can define the law by choosing either HYDR_UTIL as before, or HYDR_VGM: Mualem–Van Genuchten law. In the latter case, five parameters must be defined (cf. [9.1.4]). LETK new: - This is a viscoplastic law of Laigle and Klein for modelling the constitutive behaviour of argillite, the host rock of a storage site (cf. [9.1.17]). HUJEUX new parameters: - This is the extension of the Hujeux law to the cyclic case (cf. [9.1.18]). 1.4.15 DYNA_TRAN_MODAL NB_MODE_DIAG removed: - This keyword was not used (cf. [9.1.11]). 1.4.16 FORMULE VALE_C new: - Offers the possibility of defining a formula with a complex value (cf. [9.1.1]). 1.4.17 IMPR_RESU PARTIE extended: - Makes it possible to select the real or imaginary part which will be printed (cf. [9.1.2]). GMSH / TYPE_CHAMP new: - Makes it possible to choose the type of field and the components to be printed in GMSH format: scalar (the default), vector (VECT_2D, VECT_3D) or tensor (TENS_2D, TENS_3D) (cf. [9.1.10]). 1.4.18 IMPR_TABLE Cf. CALC_TABLE. 1.4.19 LIRE_RESU TYPE_RESU=’EVOL_VARC’ new: - Makes it possible to read, in MED format, fields which will then be used as command variables: temperature, irradiation… (cf. [9.1.17]). COMP_INCR new: - When one reads a result, the keyword COMP_INCR makes it possible to recreate the constitutive-behaviour information which cannot be stored in MED format (cf. [9.1.18]). 1.4.20 MACRO_MODE_MECA and NORM_MODE MASS_INER removed: - In order to facilitate the use of the command and avoid the risks of error, the mass is computed by NORM_MODE (cf. [9.1.18]). 1.4.21 MACR_CARA_POUTRE GROUP_NO new: - Same operation as the existing keyword NOEUD (cf. [9.1.9]). 1.4.22 POST_CHAM_XFEM NOM_CHAM extended: - Possibility of post-processing the internal-variable fields (cf. [9.1.4]). 1.4.23 POST_ELEM MINMAX new: - Makes it possible to extract the extrema of a component of a field into a table, possibly in the course of time. The table contains the location (mesh cell or node) of the extrema (cf. [9.1.18]). 1.4.24 POST_MAIL_XFEM PREF_NŒUD_X/M/P, PREF_MAILLE_X new: - Makes it possible to impose the prefix of the names of the nodes created by the command (cf. [9.1.5]). 1.4.25 POST_RCCM NUME_PASSAGE removed: - The use of NUME_PASSAGE is no longer possible for the type TUYAUTERIE. In Code_Aster , only simple passage paths are treated for the moment (cf. [9.1.22]). 1.4.26 TEST_FICHIER (developer command) NB_CHIFFRE, EPSILON removed, TYPE_TEST, NB_VALE, VALE new: - See the documentation of the command (cf. [9.1.21]). 1.4.27 THER_LINEAIRE, THER_NON_LINE, THER_NON_LINE_MO Alignment of the syntax with STAT_NON_LINE (cf. [9.1.19]): - TEMP_INIT/NUME_INIT becomes ETAT_INIT/NUME_ORDRE. - Under INCREMENT, NUME_INIT and NUME_FIN become NUME_INST_INIT and NUME_INST_FIN. Time-step subdivision is available and works under the same conditions as STAT_NON_LINE (cf. SUBD_METHODE ). For THER_NON_LINE only, OBSERVATION is available with the same syntax and the same operation as in STAT_NON_LINE. In THER_NON_LINE_MO, the only modification concerns ETAT_INIT/NUME_ORDRE (because there is no list of time steps). 2 New features between 8.4 and 9.1 2.1 New commands 2.1.1 DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE Within the framework of multi-fibre beam modellings, this operator defines fibre groups making up the cross-section of the beams. A material and a constitutive behaviour are then assigned to each fibre group via DEFI_COMPOR (cf. [9.0.10]). 2.1.2 MACRO_EXPANS The aim of this macro-command is to perform an expansion of experimental data onto a numerical model. For that purpose, it chains the commands PROJ_MESU_MODAL, REST_BASE_PHYS and PROJ_CHAMP (cf. [9.0.4]). 2.1.3 MACRO_VISU_MEIDEE This macro-command takes up the features of the MEIDEE tool developed by EDF R&D/MF2E, which performs identification of fluid forces. The macro-command is composed of a GUI with which the user interacts in order to adjust the analysis/test correlation (cf. [9.0.4]). 2.1.4 OBSERVATION This is a macro-command which facilitates the projection of the results between the numerical model and the experimental model, taking into account assumptions on the sensors (single-axis, for example), and managing the changes of frame (cf. [9.0.23]). 2.2 General modifications 2.2.1 Command variables The use of temperature as a command variable in mechanics must now be done using AFFE_MATERIAU / AFFE_VARC / NOM_VARC=’TEMP’ instead of AFFE_CHAR_MECA / TEMP_CALCULEE. 2.2.2 Substructuring Homogenisation of the vocabulary for substructuring: MAILLE is replaced by SUPER_MAILLE in CALC_VECT_ELEM, DYNA_NON_LINE, STAT_NON_LINE in order to be consistent with DEFI_MAILLAGE. 2.2.3 Keyword SOLVEUR ELIM_LAGR2 new - Within the framework of the use of the MUMPS solver, this keyword makes it possible to eliminate the 2nd Lagrange degree of freedom. This is the new default behaviour (cf. [9.0.2]). REAC_RESI new - For the FETI method, this keyword determines the frequency of updating of the computation of the residual of the GCPC of FETI (cf. [9.0.17]). 2.2.4 Version of homard The version of homard compatible with Code_Aster 9.1 is version 8.7. 2.3 Removals 2.3.1 DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI The command DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI has been removed. The explicit transient analysis is available in DYNA_NON_LINE. 2.3.2 IMPR_CLASSI The command made it possible to print the results of a modal analysis for the code CLASSI. 2.4 Modified commands 2.4.1 AFFE_CARA_ELEM AFFE_SECT, AFFE_FIBRE replaced by MULTIFIBRE, GEOM_FIBRE: - These new keywords make it possible to assign fibre groups (coming from DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE, from the mesh of the beam cross-section) to the beam elements (cf. [9.0.10]). 2.4.2 AFFE_CHAR_MECA / AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F PRE_COND, COEF_RESI new - Make it possible to choose the preconditioner and its convergence criterion for the Projected Conjugate Gradient algorithm of contact, method GCP (cf. [9.0.4]). RECH_LINEAIRE new (experimental) - This keyword has an effect on the way of moving along the search direction: does one remain inside the convex set of admissible stresses, or not? (cf. [9.0.4]). ALGO_CONT/ALGO_FROT new - Makes it possible to choose (finely!) the formulation of the continuous contact/friction method (Lagrangian, stabilised Lagrangian or augmented Lagrangian) (cf. [9.0.9]). USURE new - Makes it possible to take into account an Archard-type wear model of the slave surface (cf. [9.0.9]). MODL_AXIS removed - The axisymmetric modelling is checked from the model and not from this keyword (cf. [9.0.17]). CONTACT_XFEM / METHODE=’XFEM’ new - Definition of contact on the lips of cracks (unmeshed) modelled with the XFEM method. Note that the contact GLISSIERE is now available with X-FEM (cf. [9.0.21]). 2.4.3 AFFE_MATERIAU AFFE_COMPOR new - Makes it possible to assign a multi-fibre beam constitutive behaviour (cf. [9.0.10]). NOM_VARC / LIST_NOM_VARC addition of ‘TEMP’ - Addition of temperature as a command variable under AFFE_VARC (cf. [9.0.15]). 2.4.4 AFFE_MODELE C_PLAN_XFEM, D_PLAN_XFEM replace C_PLAN_X, D_PLAN_X - Homogenisation of the names of the modellings (cf. [9.0.11]). 3D_INCO_GD, AXIS_INCO_GD, D_PLAN_INCO_GD new modellings - New nearly incompressible modellings in large strains (cf. [9.0.11]). 3D_JOINT new modelling - Extension to 3D of the joint elements and of the constitutive law CZM_EXP_REG (cf. [9.0.13]). New HH and HH2 modellings - Unsaturated hydraulic modellings of HH and HH2 type (cf. [9.0.26]). Exhaustive list: 3D_HHS, 3D_HHD, 3D_HH2S, 3D_HH2D, AXIS_HHS, AXIS_HHD, AXIS_HH2S, AXIS_HH2D, D_PLAN_HHS, D_PLAN_HHD, D_PLAN_HH2S, D_PLAN_HH2D 2.4.5 CALC_ELEM ERRE_THM / LONGUEUR, PRESSION, TEMPERATURE new - Characteristic values making it possible to non-dimensionalise the computation of the error indicator in THM (cf. [9.0.20]). 2.4.6 CALC_FONCTION METHODE=’COMPLET’ for the FFT - Activates the algorithm which accepts an arbitrary number of samples for the computation of the FFT (cf. [9.0.9]). 2.4.7 CALC_NO OPTION=’ARCO_NOEU_SIGM’ - Computation of the arch and cantilever stresses (cf. [9.0.10]). 2.4.8 CREA_RESU OPERATION=’PREP_VRC1’/’PREP_VRC2’ - Make it possible to compute the temperature in the layers of multi-layer shells, either from a field of functions of time and of space (PREP_VRC1), or from a temperature computed on a shell model containing TEMP/TEMP_INF/TEMP_SUP (cf. [9.0.15]). 2.4.9 DEBUT and POURSUITE DYNAMIQUE new (experimental) - Objects of a size greater than that specified are not allocated in the jeveux common, but dynamically in an independent memory area. Experimental, because the release of the memory is not yet managed ideally (cf. [9.0.11]). 2.4.10 DEFI_CABLE_BP MAILLAGE removed - The mesh is recovered by the command from the MODELE supplied (cf. [9.0.15]). 2.4.11 DEFI_COMPOR GEOM_FIBRE, MATER_SECT, MULTIFIBRE new - Make it possible to define the constitutive behaviour by fibre group and the material of the section to be homogenised. One can thus take several materials into account (one per fibre group) on a multi-fibre beam element (POU_D_EM, POU_D_TGM) (cf. [9.0.10]). 2.4.12 DEFI_FISS_XFEM CONTACT removed - The definition of contact on the crack lips is done in AFFE_CHAR_MECA, keyword CONTACT, METHODE=’XFEM’ (cf. [9.0.21]). FORM_FISS new - Makes it possible to define simply the shape of the crack, elliptical only for the moment, by giving a few geometrical parameters (cf. [9.0.23]). 2.4.13 DEFI_FOND_FISS NOEUD_EXTR, GROU_NO_EXTR replace MAILLE_ORIG,GROU_MA_ORIG - Definition of the crack-tip node (cf. [9.0.12]). 2.4.14 DEFI_MAILLAGE MACR_ELEM replaces MACR_ELEM_STAT - Static macro-elements and dynamic macro-elements are now accepted (cf. [9.0.13]). 2.4.15 DEFI_MATERIAU Becomes re-entrant - One can now enrich a material (for example, add mechanical parameters to an initially thermal material). On the other hand, one cannot replace a constitutive behaviour which is already present (cf. [9.0.1]). DIS_ECRO_LINE new - Parameters for the viscoelastic constitutive law with mixed hardening on discrete elements (cf. [9.0.3]). DIS_VISC new - Parameters for the viscous-damper type law on discrete elements (cf. [9.0.3]). HUJEUX new - Parameters for the Hujeux THM law (cf. [9.0.10]). Constitutive behaviours ROUSS_PR, ROUSS_VISC: VISC_SINH_FO, BETA, DP_MAXI new - Variation of the parameters as a function of a command variable for the constitutive behaviours ROUSS_PR and ROUSS_VISC, fraction of plastic energy transformed into heat, plastic-strain threshold beyond which time-step subdivision is triggered (cf. [9.0.11]). KOCKS_RAUCH new - Parameters for the viscoplastic constitutive law of Kocks & Rauch for the single crystal (cf. [9.0.12]). A_AMORC, B_AMORC, D_AMORC, R_AMORC new - Coefficients required for the computation of the initiation factor according to the RCCM (cf. [9.0.16]). ZETA_F, RG0, TOLER_ET, ZETA_G new - Parameters for the integration of swelling and of creep under irradiation for the constitutive law IRRAD3M (cf. [9.0.20]). NON_LOCAL/PENA_LAGR new - Penalty coefficient for the new algorithm concerning models with a gradient of internal variables (cf. [9.0.23]). ELAS_2NDG new - Parameters of second-gradient elasticity, modelling with a gradient of volumetric strain (cf. [9.0.26]). 2.4.16 DYNA_NON_LINE and STAT_NON_LINE SUIVI_DDL integrated into OBSERVATION - The monitoring of a degree of freedom is now offered under the factor keyword OBSERVATION with SUIVI_DDL=’OUI’ (cf. [9.0.10]). FONCT_MULT new - Introduction of a multiplying function for the loading of the macro-elements (cf. [9.0.13]). Only in DYNA_NON_LINE: NEWMARK, TETA_METHODE, HHT removed. SCHEMA_TEMPS new - With the merging of DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI into DYNA_NON_LINE, a new factor keyword appears in order to define the time scheme used and its parameters (cf. [9.0.17]). EXCIT_GENE, PROJ_MODAL new - These two features come from DYNA_TRAN_EXPLI (cf. [9.0.17]). 2.4.17 GENE_VARI_ALEA COEF_VAR removed - Unused keyword (cf. [9.0.8]). 2.4.18 IMPR_MACR_ELEM GROUP_MA_CONTROL new - Point mesh cells on which one can recover the evolution of the quantities after a MISS3D analysis (cf. [9.0.15]). FORMAT_R new - Makes it possible to choose the print format and therefore the precision of the reals transmitted to ProMISS3D 1.4 (cf. [9.0.28]). 2.4.19 IMPR_RESU INFO_MAILLAGE only in MED format - This keyword is active only in MED format (cf. [9.0.22]). 2.4.20 INFO_FONCTION PESANTEUR: no longer a default value - In order to limit the risk of error, there is no longer a default value, because it depends on the dimensions of the problem (cf. [9.0.28]). 2.4.21 LIRE_RESU CHAM_MATER, CARA_ELEM, EXCIT new - These keywords may optionally be supplied in order to build a complete result which one will in particular be able to process in STANLEY (cf. [9.0.10]). 2.4.22 MACR_ELEM_DYNA MATR_IMPE, CAS_CHARGE new - Make it possible to create the loads on a dynamic macro-element from generalised vectors (cf. [9.0.13]). 2.4.23 MACR_LIGN_COUPE TYPE new, with the choices GROUP_NO, SEGMENT, ARC - The possibility is introduced of extracting values along a circular arc (cf. [9.0.12]). Iso-functionality with POST_RELEVE_T (cf. [9.0.22]): - The extraction can be performed on a CHAM_GD. - One can select the time instants extracted from the RESULTAT with the keywords NUME/LIST_ORDRE, INST/LIST_INST… - One can supply a line mesh-cell group on which to extract the values, - VIS_A_VIS is used for the option of the same name of PROJ_CHAMP. - OPERATION=’EXTRACTION’, ‘MOYENNE’ - INVARIANT, ELEM_PRINCIPAUX... 2.4.24 MACR_RECAL GRAPHIQUE / INTERACTIF replaced by PILOTE - Makes it possible to benefit from all the possibilities of IMPR_FONCTION (cf. [9.0.23]). 2.4.25 MACR_SPECTRE NORME: no longer a default value - In order to limit the risk of error, there is no longer a default value, because it depends on the dimensions of the problem (cf. [9.0.5]). 2.4.26 MACRO_MISS_3D Versions of ProMISS3D - The default version is version 1.3. Version 1.4 is allowed by the macro (cf. [9.0.28]). 2.4.27 MEMO_NOM_SENSI NOM_ZERO, NOM_UN removed - Were not used (cf. [9.0.23]). 2.4.28 MODI_MODELE_XFEM CONTACT new - Makes it possible to transmit the contact load to the X-FEM model (cf. [9.0.21]). 2.4.29 POST_CHAM_XFEM NOM_CHAM new - Possibility of processing the stress fields ‘SIEF_ELGA’ (cf. [9.0.20]). MAILLAGE_SAIN, MAILLAGE_FISS, MODELE_VISU new - In order to visualise the X-FEM results, POST_MAIL_XFEM generates the cracked mesh, which must be supplied under MAILLAGE_FISS. The sound mesh is the initial mesh. In order to visualise the fields at the Gauss points, one must first define a model solely for visualisation on the cracked mesh, to be supplied under MODELE_VISU (cf. [9.0.23]). 2.4.30 POST_K1_K2_K3 FISSURE new - Makes it possible to compute the stress intensity factors in post-processing of an X-FEM analysis by interpolation of the displacement jumps (cf. [9.0.12]). 2.4.31 POST_MAIL_XFEM MAILLAGE_SAIN new - Initial mesh into which the crack must be introduced (cf. [9.0.23]). 2.4.32 POST_RCCM TABL_SIGM_THETA new - Table containing the stresses in order to compute the initiation factor (cf. [9.0.16]). 2.4.33 REST_BASE_PHYS MACR_ELEM_DYNA new - Makes it possible to perform the recovery in physical space on a macro-element (cf. [9.0.13]). 2.4.34 SIMU_POINT_MAT ARCHIVAGE, MODELISATION, SIGM_IMPOSE, EPSI_IMPOSE new - For the analysis at a material point, these keywords make it possible to archive only part of the results, to apply loading paths in 2D, and to define the loading path in imposed stresses or strains (cf. [9.0.5]). COMP_ELAS, RECH_LINEAIRE, SIGM_INIT, EPSI_INIT, VARI_INIT new - Make it possible to extend the use to non-linear elastic constitutive behaviours, to activate the line search and to define a non-zero initial state (cf. [9.0.20]). 2.4.35 STAT_NON_LINE See DYNA_NON_LINE. Only in STAT_NON_LINE: VARI_REFE new - This is the reference value for the internal variables, used to estimate the convergence of the Newton algorithm in the presence of RESI_REFE_RELA (cf. [9.0.23]). This page is intentionally left blank

u4.01.06 New features and modifications of version 10 u4.01.06 New features and modifications of version 10 Summary: The purpose of this document is to provide an overall view of the syntax modifications and of the new possibilities of the Code_Aster commands introduced during the development of version 10, that is, since version 9.4.10. For further details, one should consult the documentation of the commands and the histor file of the corresponding sub-version (e.g.: [10.1.7], section Support/Histor of the site www.code-aster.org). 1 Fracture mechanics 1.1 XFEM Formulations: - Frictional contact in small/large sliding - Without contact - Axisymmetry - Large rotations Features: - Multiple cracking - Junctions - Boundary conditions on XFEM nodes - Prescribed pressure on an XFEM boundary Scope of use: - Non-linear constitutive behaviours - Thermo-mechanics Crack propagation: Possibility of multiple cracks, including in 3D: PROPA_FISS Post-processings: principle of iso-functionality between FEM and XFEM Standard FE post-processings: - Cleavage failure probability: POST_BORDET - Extension to the free mesh: POST_K1_K2_K3 - Improvement of the performance of POST_RCCM Post-processings exploiting the XFEM framework: - Plane and non-plane cracks POST_K1_K2_K3 - Extension to the non-linear case CALC_G 1.2 Cohesive models Features: - Crack initiation and propagation - Fatigue - Frictional contact - Hydro-mechanical coupling Fields of application: - Statics and dynamics - Linear and non-linear - Brittle and ductile fracture Family of modellings: - Joint elements - Elements with a discontinuity - Interface elements 2 Linear and non-linear dynamics 2.1 Analysis–test dialogue Exploitation of experimental measurements: - Interactive graphical feature - Identification of forces, structural modification, …: new operator CALC_ESSAI Updating in dynamics: - Updating on the basis of eigenmodes - Genetic algorithm MACR_RECAL 2.2 Couplings Implicit–explicit: - Implicit–explicit non-linear dynamics: MACR_BASCULE_SCHEMA - Single Code_Aster–Europlexus data setup: CALC_EUROPLEXUS Soil–structure - Extension to a non-linear structure: CALC_MISS - Response to a seismic motion varying in space: DYNA_ISS_VARI 2.3 Modal analysis Rotating machines: - Modal analysis of shaft lines - Gyroscopic effect for all beam types - Campbell diagram Cracked structures: - Extension to XFEM - Computation of the modal G by K_G_MODA 2.4 Ergonomics Modal analysis: - Complete simulation in one command: CALC_MODAL Dynamic substructuring: - Production of macro-elements CREA_ELEM_SSD, ASSE_ELEM_SSD Soil–structure interaction: - Pre-processing, analysis and post-processing CALC_MISS Constitutive behaviour: - Determination of the homogenised material parameters GLRC_DM by the command DEFI_GLRC Recovery of the results in physical coordinates: - Clarification of the features - Splitting of the command REST_BASE_PHYS into three commands: REST_GENE_PHYS, REST_SOUS_STRUC, REST_COND_TRAN 3 Thermo-hydro-mechanics 3.1 Formulations: HH and HH2 modellings: - Pure hydraulics, without thermal, without mechanics - HH: 2 phases, 1 constituent per phase - HH2: 2 phases, 2 constituents per phase Two-phase flows in a porous medium - SUSHI (Scheme Using Stabilisation and Hybrid Interfaces), finite-volume formulation Flows in a crack / propagation under fluid pressure - Joint with hydro-mechanical coupling - Selective integration _JHMS Regularisation suited to porous media - Modelling with a gradient of volumetric strain in order to avoid localisation problems Damage model dedicated to heterogeneous materials - Random distribution of micro-defects (Weibull) D_PLAN_GRAD_SIGM + ENDO_HETEROGENE - Fracturing of rocks due to gas injection 3.2 Constitutive laws Mechanics - Cyclic Hujeux law: multi-mechanism law for sands and clays, earth dykes - Laws of Laigle and Kleine, and viscous Drucker–Prager: viscoplastic laws for rocks (in particular argillites); rocks of storage sites Hydraulics - Mualem–Van Genuchten law: hydrodynamic law of unsaturated soils. Account taken of the disappearance/appearance of phases. Rocks of storage sites 4 Numerical methods 4.1 Non-linear methods Newton method - Adaptive time steps, event-driven DEFI_LIST_INST - Mixed line search: extension to mechanics, thermal, THM Alternative to Newton: IMPLEX - Robust for softening problems: approximate solutions, dependence on the time step - Supports automatic management of the time step Large strains [Miehe et al. ] - Isotropic and kinematic hardening, anisotropy - Any constitutive law written under the HPP assumption - Symmetric matrix, quadratic convergence GDEF_LOG Mixed formulation u-p - Treatment of incompressibility - Linear and quadratic elements _INCO_UP 4.2 Contact New operator dedicated to contact DEFI_CONTACT - Data setup common to all the methods - Better readability - Significant gains in performance New methodological documentation to help the user: - User's guide for contact U2.04.04 5 Architecture, ergonomics, performance 5.1 Ergonomics Easy programming of constitutive laws: - No knowledge of the software architecture required: 1 file to create, 2 files to modify - See the document D5.04.01 “Introducing a new constitutive law” - Exhaustive description via catalogues of constitutive laws External programming of constitutive laws by UMAT interfacing - User constitutive-law definition format of Abaqus - Ease of compilation thanks to the as_run tool - Small/large strains Simplification of the field names - From 3 items, one goes to 2: SIEF_ELNO_ELGA becomes SIEF_ELNO - A translator is available 5.2 Performance More efficient and measurable management of memory by display of the consumption Generalisation of the parallel analysis - Change one keyword ( SOLVEUR ) + specify the number of processors - Distribution of the elementary computations - Parallel solution of linear systems - Iso-functionality with the sequential version

u4.01.09 New features and modifications of version 13 u4.01.09 New features and modifications of version 13 Summary: The purpose of this document is to provide an overall view of the syntax modifications and of the new possibilities of the code_aster commands introduced during the development of version 13, that is, since version 12.3.24. For further details, one should consult the documentation of the commands and the histor files of the sub-versions. 1 Linear and non-linear dynamics 1.1 Operator DYNA_VIBRA > The overhaul of the operator DYNA_VIBRA gave rise to the following changes: - Reprogramming of the DEVOGE integration scheme and generalisation to all analyses. - Availability of the ITMI integration scheme for any transient analysis and not only IFS. - Introduction of a new method for the treatment of shocks, drawing on the particular features of IFS, with the keyword TRAITEMENT_NONL = 'EXPLICITE'/'IMPLICITE'. - Change to archiving in order to allow the user to force the computation and the archiving of the time instants of interest. - Treatment of localised non-linear forces (options TRAN / GENE). - Introduction of unidirectional friction for the constitutive law DIS_CHOC via the keyword UNIDIRECTIONNEL=/'OUI'/'NON'. 1.2 MISS3D coupling - Improvement of CALC_MISS / DEFI_SOL_MISS with more extensive automation of the generation of the MISS3D data - Improvements of DEFI_SOL_EQUI, including the introduction of an ONDE_PLANE loading of several types, with or without periodicity boundary conditions - Modification of CALC_MISS / IMPEDANCE_TEMPORELLE for the output of a binary file 1.3 Tools Dynamic analysis on a modal basis: - Check of the physical meaning of the damping computed by the macro-command CALC_AMOR_MODAL > Post-processings of signals: - Computation of coherence functions from time signals via CALC_FONCTION/COHERENCE - Interpolation of accelerograms via CALC_FONCTION/INTERPOL_FFT - Introduction of the macro-command CALC_SPECTRE_IPM for the modelling of floor–equipment interaction - Introduction of the macro-command LISS_SPECTRE in order to automate the smoothing of spectra. 2 Thermo-hydro-mechanics 2.1 Modellings Membrane, plate and shell modelling: - Introduction of a membrane modelling in large transformations - Improvement of the DKT element with account taken of the third rotation in the plate elements - Refactoring of the SHB elements 2.2 Loadings > Improvements: - Account taken of large displacements in the rigid links AFFE_CHAR_MECA/LIAISON_SOLIDE - Account taken of the reflected wave in the plane-wave loading AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F/ONDE_PLANE/DIST_REFLECHI 2.3 Constitutive laws - Improvement of the constitutive law ENDO_FISS_EXP with the modelling of crack closure. - Introduction of the Iwan law for the modelling of the cyclic behaviour of soils - Introduction of a Rankine model for the modelling of the behaviour of joints. - Introduction of the LKR law (improvement of LETK by modifications of the hardening functions and introduction of the thermal part) for thermo-elasto(-visco)-plastic modelling applicable to rocks and to soils (dilatant materials). - Modification of the constitutive law GRAN_IRRA_LOG for the modellings of guide tubes. 2.4 Post-processings Engineering post-processings: - Introduction of the macro-command POST_LIQUEFACTION for the post-processing of a criterion for detection of soil liquefaction. - Changes to the operator POST_RCCM. Visualisations: - Addition of features for the visualisation of the generalised forces of structural elements in the form of diagrams on the mesh. - Addition of features for the visualisation of the parameters of ELAS_FO. 3 Fracture mechanics > X-FEM elements: - Optimisation of the cutting into sub-elements in the quadratic case for the X-FEM elements. - Introduction of Lagrange multipliers for the X-FEM hydro-mechanical models. 4 Numerical methods 4.1 Model reduction (ROM) - Introduction of the ROM ( Reduced Order Model ) - Introduction of the post-processing operator for the ROM: REST_REDUIT_COMPLET - Application of model reduction in vibro-acoustics 4.2 Contact New contact method: - Introduction of the LAC method and improvement of segment–segment pairing; - Parallelisation of the “loop” over the slave mesh cells. 5 Architecture, ergonomics, performance 5.1 Ergonomics Simplified programming - Factorisation of the finite-element catalogues - Improvement of the performance of reading the mesh in .med format > Simplification of the post-processings: - Naming of the internal variables according to the mechanical terminology Removal: - Removal of the command DEFI_PARTITION - Removal of printout in CASTEM format - Removal of direct access to the keywords NOEUD and MAILLE 5.2 Performance Version upgrade for the tools: - MUMPS version 5.1 - Version of the METIS renumberer: from 4.0 (Sept 1998) to 5.1.0 (March 2013). - Version of PETSc (3.7.3) - MED version 3.2.1 > Addition of new features related to the MUMPS and PETSc solvers: - Introduction of a new value of the keyword SOLVEUR/POSTTRAITEMENTS='MINI' - Introduction of the LowRank method via the new keywords SOLVEUR/LOW_RANK_TAILLE and SOLVEUR/LOW_RANK_SEUIL. - Automatic activation of threads - Parallel analysis phase in MUMPS - Second-level preconditioner LMP. Improvement of parallelism: - Authorisation of the parallelism of elementary computations for macro-elements - Introduction of a hybrid distribution mode for elementary computations (SOUS_DOMAINE)

u4.01.13 New features and modifications of version 17 u4.01.13 New features and modifications of version 17 Summary: The purpose of this document is to provide an overall view of the syntax modifications and of the new possibilities of the code_aster commands introduced during the development of version 17, that is, since version 16.5. For further details, one should consult the documentation of the commands and the histor files of the sub-versions. 1 Mechanics - Output of the fields RESI_GLOB_RELA via MECA_NON_LINE (#26870 - 17.1) For the command MECA_NON_LINE, the residual fields at the nodes are stored during the analysis and can be printed at the end. - Follower loading FORCE_FACE . (#34164 - 17.3) The possibility is added of making FORCE_FACE a follower load via TYPE_CHARGE='SUIV' . The tangent matrix is modified accordingly. - Addition of the option SIMY_ELGA for the elements GRAD_INCO / GRAD_VARI (#34478 - 17.3) The option SIMY_ELGA, which makes it possible to compute a mean stress per finite element, is added for the elements GRAD_INCO or GRAD_VARI. - Non-symmetric tangent matrix for the interface elements (#34573 - 17.3) This development includes several improvements: introduction of a distinction between the constitutive laws of JOINT and the laws of INTERFACE, change over to generalised strains and stresses for the INTERFACE elements in order to systematise the programming, and treatment of symmetric or non-symmetric matrices with the use of the generic routines. - New shell/3D connection based on a variational formulation (#29018 - 17.3) A first version (intended to be improved later) of a new COQUE/3D link is introduced, based on a variational formulation. - New command REST_HOMO_LOCAL for the reconstruction of the local fields (#34321 #34671 #34682 - 17.3) This command takes as input the thermal and/or mechanical correctors and a thermoelastic (or elastic or thermal) result on a homogeneous global mesh. It returns a result concept of the same type as the global input result, which contains the reconstructed local solution on the mesh of the VER (Representative Elementary Volume). Optionally, the local solution can be reconstructed on the complete mesh (CALC_MATE_HOMO works on 1/8 of the geometry). The command REST_HOMO_LOCAL can be used with parallel meshes. - Operator CALC_MATE_HOMO — addition of a new TYPE_HOMO = 'PLAQUE_CT_MINDLIN' (#34899-35094 - 17.4) The purpose of this development is the addition of a new option to CALC_MATE_HOMO : TYPE_HOMO = 'PLAQUE_CT_MINDLIN' in order to define the homogenisation of plates with transverse shear. This will produce a table of orthotropic characteristics (but with isotropic expansion) for ELAS_COQUE and finite-element modelling DST. - Operator CALC_MATE_HOMO — new formulation for transverse shear TYPE_HOMO="PLAQUE_CT_TOURATIER" (#35094 - 17.4) The purpose of this development is the addition of a new TYPE_HOMO="PLAQUE_CT_TOURATIER" to the command CALC_MATE_HOMO . It is a new kinematic formulation for plates, for taking transverse shear into account without the introduction of correction coefficients. - Introduction of a new macro-command THERMECA_MULT (#33809 - 17.4) A new macro-command THERMECA_MULT is introduced, making it possible to obtain the mechanical responses corresponding to thermal fields applied to one and the same mechanical model. This command THERMECA_MULT is distinguished from MACR_ELAS_MULT by the fact that it is possible to supply a temperature field as a loading. - Simultaneous HHO and FE analysis (#35004 - 17.4) This development makes possible the simultaneous analysis of HHO elements and finite elements. - HHO elements: order higher than 2 (#34395 -17.4) The purpose of this development is the addition of HHO elements for the following orders: k=0: CONSTANTE, k=1: LINEAIRE, k=2: QUADRATIQUE, k=3: CUBIQUE, k=4: QUARTIQUE. - Detection of the plane of the discrete element when DIS_CONTACT / DIS_CHOC and COIN_2D (#34860 - 17.4) This development concerns a change to the constitutive law COIN_2D, so as to supply compulsorily 3 values under the keyword PRECISION . These values govern the flatness tests in the planes YZ, XZ and XY respectively. - Addition of the option EVOL_IMPO to CHAR_MECA or of DIDI to CHAR_CINE (#28597 -17.4) This development makes it possible to make the loading type DIDI compatible with CHAR_CINE loadings. 2 Thermal - Operator THER_NON_LINE - TRANSITOIRE (#33079 - 17.1) The command THER_NON_LINE is now implemented on the Python side. Some keywords are not yet supported (drying, model reduction); in that case the Fortran operator is called. - Computation of the temperature gradient GRAT (#33934 - 17.2) One wishes to have the temperature gradient in the form of a field at the nodes. This field is necessary in order to compute the “relocalised” stresses at the end of a homogenised analysis. The temperature-gradient field is called GRAT. - Extension of the analyses available for HHO (#33950/#33946/#33966/#34394 - 17.2 to 17.3) The HHO elements are made compatible with orthotropic thermal analyses and with a transient THER_NON_LINE analysis. The possibility is added of supplying command variables VARC for HHO in thermal analysis. The HHO elements in thermal analysis are available at order 0 in thermal analysis. - Introduction of a new macro-command CALC_THER_MULT (#33806 - 17.4) This new macro-command CALC_THER_MULT makes it possible to carry out thermal analyses with linearisation of the mesh and an automated time step. This command computes the evolution of the temperature in the structure under multiple transient thermal loadings. Two thermal responses can be taken into account: thermal response to a unit shock, or thermal response to an arbitrary loading coming from an AFFE_CHAR_THER. - Correction of the tangent matrices in non-linear thermal analysis: thermal conduction (#34600 - 17.4) The tangent matrices of non-linear thermal analysis do not lead to quadratic convergence, even on very simple cases. In this development, account is taken of the dependence of thermal conduction on temperature. - New operator SECH_NON_LINE (#33112 -17.4) Until now, drying analyses were carried out with the command THER_NON_LINE . This development creates a new command specific to drying analyses, SECH_NON_LINE , associated with the drying laws, and produces a new result EVOL_SECH possessing a field SECH with a component "SECH". 3 Fluid–structure interaction - Change to DEFI_SPEC_TURB (SPEC_CORR_CONV_1-2)/PROJ_SPEC_BASE (#32094 - 17.1) The operators DEFI_SPEC_TURB/ PROJ_SPEC_BASE did not make it possible to carry out, in a suitable way, an analysis of the response of a structure to turbulence. The options available were too restrictive concerning the spectra and the correlation lengths. The changes concern: - the possibility of defining correlation lengths and convective velocities. - the possibility of integrating a transverse correlation length for Au-Yang and Corcos. - the possibility of defining correlation lengths depending on the angular frequency. - the removal of the Au-Yang correlation, because it is wrong. - Relax the check of consistency of the IFS formulations (#35153 - 17.4) In order to lift in part the restriction on the possibility of mixing several FORMULATION values in IFS in the same mesh, the keyword VERI_FORMULATION_IFS is added in AFFE_MODELE . 4 Constitutive laws 4.1 New laws or improvements: - Introduction of a quasi-brittle constitutive law with a cap in compression: ENDO_LOCA_TC (#32232 -17.1) Introduction of a new constitutive law for concrete which covers the following phenomenology: - Damage in tension / shear and a dedicated threshold - Hardening in tension identical to ENDO_LOCA_EXP - Damage in compression and a dedicated threshold - Hardening in compression of perfect-plasticity type, asymptotic after a first linear phase - The thresholds have an analytical expression (robustness, efficiency) - The stress is bounded whatever the loading direction - Regularisation of the angular points for the tangent matrix (as for ENDO_LOCA_EXP) - Viscous regularisation of the damage The vocabulary in DEFI_MATER_GC and DEFI_MATERIAU has been revised. (#34613 -17.3) - Constitutive law ENDO_LOCA_TC : modification of the numerical regularisations (#34393 - 17.3) The two regularisation parameters are evaluated (one in order to “round off” the shape of the damage threshold, the other in order to round off the tension–compression transition) so that the impact on the stresses is of the same order of magnitude as the precision requested for the integration of the constitutive behaviour (via RESI_INTE_RELA). - Constitutive law ENDO_LOCA_TC — Estimation of the influence of viscosity (#34611 - 17.3) The internal variable SIGMVISC is introduced, which evaluates the difference from the stress which one would have for the same strain in the absence of viscosity. Another internal variable, ENDOTOT, is also introduced, which measures the maximum damage which can be observed in the current state by scanning all the possible loading directions. - Integration of the modified Cam-Clay constitutive model via Mfront (#33516 - 17.1) Integration of the modified Cam-Clay constitutive model (named MCC) via MFront. It will eventually replace the constitutive law CAM_CLAY in order to gain in robustness and in performance for carrying out non-linear analyses. This update will make it possible to produce, progressively, variations of MCC, thus allowing increasingly realistic predictions with respect to experimental tests on soils. - Integration of the Barcelona constitutive model via MFront (#33678 - 17.2) The purpose of this issue is the integration of the Barcelona constitutive model with MFront, while at the same time deactivating the existing Fortran version. In time, this new integration will make it possible to develop more sophisticated variations of the Barcelona model suited to materials of bentonite type. - Integration of the CSSM constitutive model via MFront (#33712 - 17.2) The purpose of this issue is the integration of the CSSM constitutive model (Critical State Soil Model) via MFront in Code_Aster. CSSM relies on the combination of two models, close to modified Cam-Clay and to Iwan, in order to represent the phenomenology of soils, both under monotonic and under cyclic loadings (which neither modified Cam-Clay nor Iwan manages to do on its own). - Change to the constitutive law DIS_GRICRA (#33519 - 17.2) In the material DIS_GRICRA, KP is added, which is the elastic stiffness in parallel (identical for the 3 directions). This discrete element is placed in parallel in order to avoid null pivots, because DIS_GRICRA can return a null tangent matrix. - For the discrete constitutive law DIS_CHOC , account taken of an elastic spring in parallel (#34730 - 17.3) The use of a shock discrete element can lead to singular-matrix configurations. In order to work around this case, the practice is to duplicate the support element in order to add an elastic spring with a low stiffness. This spring in parallel can now be taken into account directly in the constitutive behaviour DIS_CHOC. - For the discrete constitutive law DIS_CHOC with friction and a non-symmetric tangent matrix (#35026 - 17.4) The objective of this development is to move to a formulation involving a true non-symmetric tangent matrix for the constitutive law DIS_CHOC in the presence of Coulomb friction, in statics and in dynamics. This issue gave rise to an update of the affected test cases, and to the addition of new tests. - For the discrete constitutive laws, addition of an elastic spring in parallel (#35027 -17.4) This development consists in adding an elastic spring in parallel for all the constitutive laws of discrete elements (when this is possible). - Enrichment of the constitutive law DIS_ECRO_TRAC (#32285 -17.4) One wishes to model a non-linear spring in the axial direction and in the tangential direction. The constitutive law 'DIS_ECRO_TRAC' makes it possible to model an elastoplastic spring with a tension curve. The objective of this development is to enrich this constitutive law in order to extend it to both directions at the same time: axial or tangential. - Replacement of FONC_DESORP for the definition of the desorption isotherms in BETON_DESORP HR = f(C,T) (#33617 - 17.2) The keyword ELAS_FO/FONC_DESORP becomes BETON_DESORP/FONC_DESORP, with BETON_DESORP a new keyword of DEFI_MATERIAU. Other parameters are introduced under BETON_DESORP, making it possible to evaluate the hygrometry from the Leverett isotherm. - Development of a new constitutive law for drying SECH_RFT (#33618 -17.2) A new constitutive law relating to drying has been developed and validated on the experimental data of the VeRCoRs concrete. The model is RICHARD_FICK_TEMPERATURE (Adia et al., 2020). This model is to be introduced in the form of a new option known as ’SECH_RFT’ of the keyword RELATION in the operator THER_NON_LINE , and in the form of a new keyword of the operator DEFI_MATERIAU. - Supplements to the developments of SECH_RFT and BETON_DESORP (#34147- 33620 - 17.4) The keyword UNITE_PRESSION is added to DEFI_MATERIAU/BETON_DESORP: it makes it possible to choose the desired unit for the capillary pressure PCAP. The keywords UNITE_TEMPS and UNITE_LONGUEUR are added to SECH_RFT. For the 4 drying modellings (3D_SECH, 3D_SECH_DIAG, AXIS_SECH and AXIS_SECH_DIAG), two options are created for the computation of fields at the Gauss points: DIFF_ELGA for the diffusion coefficient and HYGR_ELGA for the hygrometry. - Visco-hyperelastic constitutive law ELAS_HYPER_VISC (#34083 - 17.2) Introduction of a visco-hyperelastic MFront constitutive law ELAS_HYPER_VISC. This model is adopted for elastomers. It is compared and validated with Abaqus simulations. - Modification of the formulation of desiccation creep in the constitutive law BETON_BURGER_FP (#25328 - 17.3) In the constitutive law BETON_BURGER, the computation of desiccation creep was overestimated (Bazant model) when there are cycles of large humidity variations. The Mfront file of this constitutive law has been modified in order to correct this point and, at the same time, an implicit solution scheme has been adopted in this new formulation. - Integration of the BURGER_AGEING constitutive model in a THM framework (#33999 - 17.3) The constitutive model BURGER_AGEING is available in an MFront version. The BURGER_AGEING model is designed to predict a basic creep which is linear in stress and includes an ageing effect, unlike the BETON_BURGER model. The BURGER_AGEING model is furthermore developed within the framework of a THHM modelling, because of the influence of the capillary pressure and of the temperature on the creep behaviour which it predicts. - Hill constitutive law in Mfront (#34665 - 17.3) Introduction of a hyperelastic MFront constitutive law adopted for compressible foams. This is the Hill law, whose potential is expressed as a function of the principal stretches and of the variation of the volume. - MFront constitutive law for vessel steel VISC_ISOT_PLAS (#31499 - 17.4) One wishes to capitalise an isotropic elastoviscoplastic MFront constitutive law named VISC_ISOT_PLAS. This model is adopted for irradiated vessel steel (bainitic). It is multi-scale, takes into account the properties of the microstructure, static and dynamic ageing, and large strains. 4.2 Improvements of the Mfront/code_aster interface: - Account taken of the keywords and of the command variables by Mfront (#24065/23957 -17.1) The keywords RESI_INTE_MAXI and ITER_INTE_MAXI of COMPORTEMENT had default values which are now removed. Thus, the parameters Epsilon and IterMax of the Mfront file are no longer systematically overwritten. The values of the MFront file are overloaded only if the keyword is present. RESI_INTE_MAXI and RESI_INTE_RELA are renamed RESI_INTE. For the management of the command variables, a correspondence is created in Behaviour_module between the established MFront name for each component of a command variable and the aster component name in the external-variable field generated by code_aster. This facilitates the ergonomics of the use of the command variables transmitted to Mfront via the MGIS interface. - Large strains GREEN_LAGRANGE with MGIS (#33782 - 17.2) This development consists in connecting large strains GREEN_LAGRANGE with MGIS. In aster, one uses DEFORMATION="GREEN_LAGRANGE" and in MFront, one uses: @DSL DefaultFiniteStrain. The Cauchy stress sig is returned. - Use of Mfront possible for the interface constitutive laws CZM (#34369 -17.3) - Improvement of the MFront/MGIS interface: error codes (#34642 17.3) The management of the error codes of MGIS/MFront was incorrect and may wrongly suggest that a constitutive law has not converged. The three possible return codes of Mfront are taken into account in order to convert them in code_aster. - Use of the GRAD_VARI modellings with MFront constitutive laws (#34627 - 17.3) This use is now possible and tested on a von Mises constitutive law with linear isotropic hardening with an AXIS_GRAD_VARI modelling 4.3 General points: - Definition of AFFE_MATERIAU in several pieces (#33342 - 17.1) One can split into two distinct calls the assignment of AFFE_MATERIAU: on the one hand, the assignment of the materials (AFFE), and on the other hand, the assignment of the command variables (AFFE_VARC), by calling the material field already defined. - Check of consistency of the elastic parameters for geomechanics (#33602 - 17.1) In DEFI_MATERIAU, with the keywords ELAS and ELAS_FO, one could enter only E and nu. For many materials (soils, rocks, etc.), one “knows” K and G better (bulk and shear moduli), or the two wave speeds of the P and S waves: Vp and Vs. Under ELAS (this is not done for the functions for the moment), one can now supply either (E, NU), or (K, MU), or (CELE_P, CELE_S, RHO). - Introduction of a vapour-density exchange term ECHANGE_THM_HR in THM (#33856 - 17.2) One wishes to introduce a mass-exchange condition (water and vapour) at the interface in order to model ventilated media in a more realistic way. The vapour density being directly related to the relative humidity, this amounts to writing a condition in relative humidity (which is generally the information available to the user). In the end, it is a non-linear mixed condition on the wall. A new keyword ECHANGE_THM_HR is therefore introduced here in AFFE_CHAR_MECA , with GROUP_MA and 3 keywords in order to define coefficients: HR_EXT (for the external relative humidity), ALPHA (for the value of the exchange coefficient) and PVAP_SAT for the value of the saturating vapour pressure. A version in AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F exists in order to be able to vary PVAP_SAT with the temperature and the other coefficients with time. - Introduce piloting PRED_ELAS for the interface constitutive law CZM_LAB_MIX (#34485 - 17.3) The piloting in question is introduced, on the basis of a control of the increment of the maximum sliding variable. The piloting increment is normalised by the critical sliding delta_c, which is a material parameter (a piloting increment of 1 corresponds to a sliding increment of delta_c). - Introduction of piloting PRED_ELAS for the constitutive law VMIS_ISOT_NL (#34190 - 17.3), with the aim of facilitating limit-analysis computations and of ensuring more robust analyses when this piloting is already used elsewhere in the structure (reinforced concrete) 5 Linear and non-linear dynamics - Reduction of the memory consumption of DYNA_VIBRA (#31151 - 17.1) In DYNA_VIBRA, a large block of memory was allocated at the start of the analysis. Memory consumption has been improved by cutting the jeveux objects into several blocks, so as to be able to allocate / unload them as the analysis proceeds. - Modification of the computation of the irreversible displacements of the command POST_NEWMARK (#33544 - 17.1) Update of the way in which the command POST_NEWMARK computes the irreversible displacements from the mean acceleration. The method implemented (construction of a fictitious acceleration signal, clipped at the critical-acceleration value before double integration) gave less satisfaction and seemed less robust than obtaining the velocity signal from the integration of the mean acceleration and clipping for the velocities lower than zero before integration in order to obtain the displacements. The algorithm is replaced by a simple time integration of the mean acceleration, with clipping at zero if the values are lower than 0 before time integration in order to obtain the displacements. - Improvement of the performance of the projection stage for the computation of the factor of safety with POST_NEWMARK (#33542 - 17.1) The mesh used for the projection of the stresses is restricted to the 2D finite elements adjacent to the slip line (a stage necessary for the computation of skin stresses SIRO_ELEM on the slip line). The user is allowed to carry out a projection by COLLOCATION of the operator PROJ_CHAMP (in that case, SIEF_NOEU must be precomputed by the user). The projection is carried out for the NOEU field, then the ELGA stress field is computed time instant by time instant. - Procedure for automatic cutting of frequency bands upstream of a CALC_MODES (#33821 - 17.2) A new command is introduced allowing an automatic cutting into balanced frequency bands (i.e., each having a comparable number of eigenfrequencies), upstream of a multi-band modal analysis via CALC_MODES. This is an iterative method based on an eigenvalue-counting procedure (Sturm test available in INFO_MODE), which it is proposed to implement. Because of its non-intrusive character, this method simply takes the form of a Python function which will return to the user the “optimal” frequency bands, which can then be entered in a CALC_MODES. - Implementation of the HHT scheme without overshooting in DYNA_NON_LINE (#33909 - 17.2) The “No Overshooting” version of the HHT scheme is implemented in DYNA_NON_LINE.
