This consists in adapting the formulation proposed by Kaiping (2008) to the non-linear case in order to implement it in DYNA_NON_LINE, then in studying the presence of overshooting via several elementary test cases (by comparing the results obtained with those coming from the HHT scheme currently present in DYNA_NON_LINE). The NOHHT scheme is thus available in DYNA_NON_LINE, for the formulations in displacement and in acceleration. - Seismic analysis of tanks: equivalent pressure EC8/DERESMA (#31186 - 17.2) The usual approach for the analysis of the seismic resistance of tanks is based on Eurocode 8 part 4 (EC8, standard NF EN 1998-4). The effects of the fluid under earthquake on the wall of the tank are represented by an equivalent pressure field defined by the superposition of several functions in cylindrical coordinates (for vertical cylindrical tanks). These fields are then imposed on the wall in order to allow an equivalent static seismic analysis of push-over type. A macro-command carrying out this analysis is developed. The macro-command DEFI_PRES_EC8 produces a formula usable in AFFE_CHAR_MECA/FORCE_COQUE_FO (#33522). - Output of the macro-command MACR_SPECTRE (#33961 - 17.2) The default behaviour of MACR_SPECTRE is changed so as not to print by default the envelope of the horizontal directions of the spectra (denoted H). - Addition of a refined mesh output for the option VERI_MASSE of POST_NEWMARK (#33996 - 17.2) The mesh used for the computation of the sliding mass in the command POST_NEWMARK is made available to the user, in the case of use of the option VERI_MASSE . - Addition of the possibility of taking into account the regression scatter for the estimation of ky in POST_NEWMARK (#33997 - 17.2) The computation option for ky developed in issue32770 considers a linear regression between the factor of safety and the mean acceleration for a range lying between 0.8 and 1.2 of the factor of safety. The critical-acceleration value retained is that at 3σ of the regression. The user is given the possibility of choosing another multiplicative factor between 0 and 6 (0 = not taken into account, 6 = conservative estimate at −6σ). - Addition of the name for GROUP_MA during the computation of the mean acceleration in POST_NEWMARK (#34011 - 17.2) At the output of the macro-command POST_NEWMARK , a new mesh is supplied — identical to the mesh used for the dynamic analysis — containing the mesh-cell group used for the computation of the resultant and of the sliding mass (if VERI_MASSE is activated). - Optimisation of the macro-command DYNA_ISS_VARI (#34287 -17.3) The optimisation of the command was carried out along 2 lines of improvement: optimisation of the computation of the coherence matrix and optimisation of the computation of the eigenvalues and of the energy. A gain by a factor of 10 is noted on a test case. - Operator GENE_ACCE_SEISME : ZPA correction (#30484 - 17.3) In the simulation of accelerograms with gene_acce_seisme, one wishes to generate signals which possess exactly the right PGA (the ZPA on the spectrum). The keyword is added: CORR_ZPA = 'OUI' or 'NON' (default) - Shock law with buckling DYNA_VIBRA (#34294 17.3) The operator DYNA_VIBRA is modified so as to make the relation FLAMBAGE usable with a generic buckling law, given in the form of three functions, namely the buckling threshold, the stiffness and the damping as a function of the total indentation. Thus, the input data of DYNA_VIBRA/FLAMBAGE are now identical to those of the constitutive law CHOC_ENDO_PENA usable in DYNA_NON_LINE. - Operator COMB_SISM_MODAL : Addition of the method ENVELOPPE (#34351 - 17.3) Addition of the option ENVELOPPE to the keyword ANALYSE . This “Envelope” analysis option makes it possible to compute the spectral response of a system in the multi-support case with an envelope spectrum of all the input spectra, for each direction. The multi-support system is considered as a MONO_APPUI system. - Operator COMB_SISM_MODAL : New combination methods (#33545 #34054 - 17.3) The following combination methods are added in COMB_SISM_MODAL under the keyword COMB_MODE/TYPE "NRC_GROUPING", "NRC_DSA" and "NRC_TEN_PERCENT" . - Operator COMB_SISM_MODAL : Programming optimisation, memory consumption and performance (#34465-34698-34677 -17.3 - 17.4) Improvement of the operator in order to reduce the run time The programming of the macro COMB_SISM_MODAL is revised in order to remove duplicates, improve the readability of the blocks, improve the use of the variables and the pythonisation of the scripting. The excess memory consumption appears in the case of the treatment of the option ELNO in COMB_SISM_MODAL: the script is optimised in order to improve the consumption. - Operator CALC_FONCTION / SPEC_OSCI HARMO : addition of a direct-computation option (#34798 -17.4) The operator CALC_FONCTION makes it possible to compute response spectra in pseudo-acceleration by the NIGAM method (time solution) or HARMO (filtering in the frequency domain). For the keyword SPEC_OSCI , a new keyword PSEUDO = 'OUI' or 'NON' is added (default = 'OUI'), so as to be able to compute the absolute acceleration. The computation of the absolute acceleration and of the relative velocity will be possible only with the method HARMO . - Change to the operator MODE_STATIQUE by grouping the supports (#34760 - 17.4) At present the operator MODE_STATIQUE makes it possible to compute, in MULTI_APPUI, the pseudo-modes by blocked degree of freedom, that is: support by support, direction by direction. In certain industrial cases with a very large number of supports, one wishes to group the supports. The objective of this development is to compute the static modes by support group in MODE_STATIQUE. In MODE_STATIQUE, a keyword CORRELE="OUI"/"NON" is added under the factor keyword PSEUDO_MODE. If CORRELE="OUI", then a single mode is created per active direction. The user must specify NOM_APPUI (of length 0. - Rewriting of the command POST_KCP for the computation of the plastic correction Kcp (#34099 #34311 - 17.3) The new macro-command POST_KCP will integrate the "beta" correction for the DSR (case of the semi-elliptical defect) in accordance with the RSE-M 2022. The compulsory keyword UNITE_LONGUEUR is added to POST_KCP when the user wishes to work in millimetres (mm). - Make the INCO_UPG elements compatible with the operator CALC_G (#33972 - 17.2) The computation of the free-energy density is corrected for the incompressible elements, and the computation of the stress in the case of G_EPSI. Henceforth, the operator CALC_G is compatible only with the INCO_UPG elements (the most generic). An error will be issued for the other modellings such as INCO_UP and INCO_UPO. - Operator CALC_G : Addition of the curvature terms for the computation of the SIFs, option 'K' (#34348 - 17.3) In order to improve the computation of the SIFs in the case of a plane crack with a curved front, new auxiliary fields are introduced for modes 1, 2 and 3 (Thesis of Le Cren and C. Stolz). These new fields take into account the local curvature of the crack, thus allowing a more precise evaluation of the SIFs. The keyword added is FORM_FISS = "ELLIPSE" or "CERCLE". - Operator POST_RCCM — addition of the peak stress F in the output table of POST_RCCM (#34800 - 17.4) The peak stress F is added in the output table of POST_RCCM for the option Pm + Pb. 9 THM models (Thermo-Hydro-Mechanical) - Modification of the formulation of the Fick laws in THHM (#32248 - 17.3) It is therefore proposed to rewrite the diffusive fluxes in the gas mixture in mass form (models HH : LIQU_VAPE_GAZ and LIQU_AD_GAZ_VAPE ) with a much simpler writing, consistent with the literature. - Integration of the BURGER_AGEING model in a THM framework (#33999 -17.3) The purpose of this issue is the integration of the BURGER_AGEING constitutive model in MFront. 10 Contact - Formulation DIS_CONTACT / DIS_CHOC : Contact in the global frame (#33438 - 17.1) When one wishes to carry out contact with discrete elements (material DIS_CONTACT, constitutive behaviour DIS_CHOC), contact is established in the direction of the discrete element, with or without friction in the perpendicular plane. One therefore has contact which is treated in the LOCAL frame of the discrete element. The change makes it possible to solve the contact in the global frame of the mesh and no longer in the local frame of the discrete element. The addition of a keyword in the material DIS_CONTACT makes it possible to define the type of contact which one wishes, CONTACT='COIN_2D' . This keyword is optional and its default value corresponds to the case of the discrete element with contact in the LOCAL frame: - For DIS_CONTACT with CONTACT='COIN_2D' , addition of the keyword PRECISION (#34590 - 17.3) This keyword PRECISION makes it possible to specify the tolerance so that the DISCRET in COIN_2D remains in a plane. - Removal of the option GAP_GEOM (#33728 - 17.1) The option GAP_GEOM has no practical usefulness in the contact analysis. This option was used only to test the pairing in the test cases. The option and all its dependencies are removed. - Update and improvement of the pairing of the Python methods for contact (#33736,34349 - 17.3) In the operator DEFI_CONT, a new architecture/development of the contact-pairing part is carried out: - Rewriting of the PANG algorithm - Refactoring of the objects and of the Python methods which are linked to them This development makes it possible to carry out additional post-processings on the pairing for the debugging of studies. - Introduction of contact/friction in augmented Lagrangian (#34372 - 17.3) . The possibility is introduced of carrying out frictional-contact analyses in large sliding, relying on: - a mortar approach with use of a sub-mesh for the numerical integration, representing the intersection of the master and slave mesh cells - a formulation of augmented-Lagrangian type - a solution by a generalised Newton method It is a mixed formulation in which the multipliers are carried by the nodes of the slave elements, in P2P1 in 3D and P2P2 in 2D. Two formulations are introduced: a so-called classical formulation, of Alart & Curnier type, activated by ALGO_CONT='LAGRANGIEN' and VARIANTE='CLASSIQUE' (the multipliers there are expressed in the local basis of the element), and a so-called robust formulation (the default), proposed by Poulios & Renard, activated by ALGO_CONT='LAGRANGIEN' and VARIANTE='ROBUSTE' . The multipliers there are expressed in the global frame. - Addition of a penalisation method (#34603 - 17.3) The formulation is degraded by removing the multipliers, which leads naturally to a penalised approach. It therefore inherits the characteristics of the original formulation, namely that a single penalisation coefficient is used for the contact and for the friction. The quadratic convergence observed on the augmented-Lagrangian formulation is observed. The formulation is activated by ALGO_CONT="PENALISATION". - Make the contact zones communicate in HPC (#30552 - 17.3) The aim of this development is to make contact in MECA_NON_LINE compatible with mesh partitioning. 11 Post-processings - Possibility of restricting MODI_REPERE by the keyword GROUP_MA (#31636 - 17.1) The keyword GROUP_MA has been added under MODI_CHAM in MODI_REPERE (by default TOUT="OUI") in order to restrict the computation to the zones where the frame has been changed. Only the following frames are affected: COQUE_ . - Operator PROJ_CHAMP: PROL_VALE replaces PROL_ZERO (#33278 - 17.2) For all the methods for which the keyword PROL_ZERO exists, it is replaced by PROL_VALE . With the new operation, on the components of the nodes of the mesh cells not concerned by the projection if PROL_VALE = xxx ==> one extends by xxx, if PROL_VALE is not supplied ==> a NaN value is set. - Operator CALC_CHAMP option VARC_ELNO and VARC_NOEU (#33830 - 17.2) An option VARC_ELNO is added for the most classical modellings (3D, 3D_SI, D_PLAN, D_PLAN_SI, C_PLAN, C_PLAN_SI) and a few structural elements (DKT, BARRE, GRILLE_MEMBRANE, DIS_T). In the documentation of the option VARC_ of CALC_CHAMP, the precautions for use of this option are specified accordingly. - Access to the values of generalised coordinates from a dynamics result (#33734 - 17.2) Add one (or several) method(s) making it possible to access the values of generalised coordinates (in Python) from a dynamics result (e.g., the generalised displacements/velocities/accelerations from a TransientGeneralizedResult). Such a method could take the form of a getValues() or toNumpy() which can be called from a Python class of “generalised result” type. - Interpolation of the fields of a result (#32348 - 17.2) The objective is to make available, in Python and in C++, methods allowing linear interpolation between fields. Interpolation between fields is carried out with a wrap of the Fortran routine rsinch provided for this purpose; and this in order to have a single programming for use in C++ and in Python. The name of the new method is interpolateField in Python and interpolateFieldOnNodesReal + interpolateFieldOnCellsReal in C++. - Change of the quantity of a field in Python (#33968 - 17.2) The method is named setPhysicalQuantity() , as there is getPhysicalQuantity changeLocalization is also renamed setLocalization . The development is done for FieldOnNodes, FieldOnCells, SimpleFieldOnNodes, SimpleFieldOnCells. - Ease of handling of the fields (#16019 - 17.1) One can handle the fields with the elementary operations +, − , . (See for example in zzzz505a) - Handling of the components of the fields by elements (#34339,34354 - 17.3) This development makes it possible to write simply operations on the values of the fields in the macro-commands via the object ComponentOnCells . Operations on the values at the nodes are also allowed via the object 'ComponentOnNodes'. - Account taken of DISTANCE_ALARME in MACR_LIGN_COUPE (#34460/34536 - 17.3) Addition of one PROJ_CHAMP per cut line, so as to be able to parameterise the PROJ_CHAMP correctly as a function of the DISTANCE_ALARME and DISTANCE_MAX of each cut line. For performance reasons, the minimum of DISTANCE_ALARME (respectively DISTANCE_MAX) is taken for the whole of LIGN_COUPE. - Operator CALC_PRESSION (#32185 17.3) In the result at the output of CALC_PRESSION , the component CISA has been completed in the field PRES_NOEU, representing the amplitude of the tangential force density. The components of the tangential-force vector are stored in the components VX, VY and VZ of the field PRES_NOEU. This post-processing is available only on the 2D models. - New operator VERI_FERRAILLAGE and macro-command POST_VERI_FERRAILLAGE (#34004 #34705 - 17.3) The command VERI_FERRAILLAGE makes it possible to automate the computation of the mechanical reinforcement margins on plate elements. A new Python macro-command POST_VERI_FERRAILLAGE is added for the computation of the critical interaction diagrams on plate elements. The underlying algorithm is the CAPRA_MAURY method for the identification of the critical facet for each mesh cell. The design codes are Eurocode 2 and BAEL91. - Addition of the minimum reinforcement for crack control in CALC_FERRAILLAGE (#35148 -17.4) One wishes to take into account the minimum reinforcement for crack control in CALC_FERRAILLAGE : computation of the minimum reinforcement with respect to crack control for the plate elements with the formulae (7.1) of EN1992-1-1 and DCONC 4110-1/DN 2200-1 of the RCC-CW. The keywords FERR_MIN_FISS and EFFET_ECHELLE are added to the command CALC_FERRAILLAGE. New outputs of the command CALC_FERRAILLAGE are added, with the quantities ASMINXI, ASMINXS, ASMINYI, ASMINYS. - Introduction of a new macro-command CREA_COUPE (#33807 - 17.4) A new macro-command CREA_COUPE is introduced, making it possible to adjust the data supplied by the user in order to create one-dimensional cuts. The creation of cuts is sometimes complicated with MARC_LIGN_COUPE if a large number of cuts is necessary. This new macro-command makes it possible to take as input a table, which is updated so that the nodes are correctly positioned on the skin of the mesh. Via the keyword REVOLUTION, one can create additional cuts by multi-rotation. - Creation of the command EXTR_COUPE , which takes as input the output table of CREA_COUPE (#33810 - 17.4) The objective of this new command EXTR_COUPE is to extract the results on these cuts as result fields. - Allow IMPR_RESU to keep NOM_CAS in the name of the MED fields (#33808 - 17.4) A keyword TYPE_RESU is added, with two choices "NUME_ORDRE" (by default) and "NOM_CAS" . The first makes it possible to keep the current behaviour of IMPR_RESU, while the second makes it possible to print the name of the case at the beginning of the name of the MED field and thus to replace the default name given by code_aster. - Addition of the option FORC_VARC_ELEM_P to CALC_VECT_ELEM (#349125 - 17.4) A new option FORC_VARC is added in CALC_VECT_ELEM in order to obtain the forces generated by the command variables. - Addition of an extraction option with NUME_ORDRE in CREA_CHAMP (#34932 - 17.4) The value NUME_ORDRE is added to the keyword TYPE_RESU of CREA_CHAMP/EXTR, so as to be able to build a field indicating the order number rather than the time instant at which the extremum is reached for each entity. - Account taken of NUME_DDL in LIRE_RESU (#34518 - 17.4) The keyword NUME_DDL is added to LIRE_RESU and LIRE_CHAMP , in order to reconstruct a field with the desired components. - Changes to the macro-command POST_ROCHE (#35056 - 17.4) In order to be able to supply a tension curve other than that of Ramberg–Osgood at the true-stress computation stage, the keyword TRAC_EPSI is added (strain curve as a function of the stress). The keyword RCCM_RX is renamed SIGM_LIM . The keywords VARIANTE and SIGM_ABAT are added, which make it possible to compute the criteria of the following new formulations. The abated moments are computed. These developments are accompanied by a change of type of the output object and of the components of the fields. - Development of new modal parameters and a new macro-command POST_MODE (#33662 - 17.4). - output the unitary effective modal inertias in rotation - output unitary effective modal inertias in translation or in rotation, but only on a mesh-cell group (“local”) - be able to sort the modes according to a criterion on these new quantities This development makes it possible to: In the operator CALC_MODES , the computation of the effective modal inertias and of the unitary effective modal inertias in rotation with respect to the centre of gravity is added. A new macro-command POST_MODE is added. This macro-command computes the effective masses and inertias in an “approximate” way by putting zeros on the global mass matrix for the nodes not contained in the mesh-cell group supplied. The approximation lies in the fact that the contribution of the nodes on the boundary of the group also includes what comes from the mesh cells outside the group connected to that same node. 12 HPC version - Rebalance a mesh by exploiting the loadings (#33789 - 17.2) When one distributes a mesh for the first time, at read time therefore, one has no choice other than to do so on the basis of the connectivity. Nevertheless, in the cases where linear relations are applied between degrees of freedom, this information is relevant and would make it possible to guide the distribution. The possibility is added of asking the partitioner to group node groups on a single processor, with an argument to splitMeshAndFieldsFromMedFile: nodeGrpToGather. - Line search for MECA_NON_LINE (#33469 - 17.2) The behaviour of MECA_NON_LINE is made uniform between thermal and mechanics. The case of the mixed line search MIXTE is added. - Stop the MECA_NON_LINE analysis by a number of time steps (#34072 - 17.2) The request is to stop without error an analysis after N computed time instants, whether or not these time instants are in the initial list. - Addition of the loading type TYPE_CHARGE="DIDI" in MECA_NON_LINE (#31797 - 17.3) - Addition of account taken of maps for ETAT_INIT/SIGM (#34418 - 17.3) - Addition of the criterion RESI_REFE_RELA for MECA_NON_LINE (#33172 - 17.3) - Extend certain features of PROJ_CHAMP to HPC (#34537 17.3) Only the projection of fields at the nodes is supported. - Choose the value of the overlap (#33695 - 17.3) In the HPC context, the overlap is fixed at 1. In connection with the work on non-linear preconditioning, it is necessary to be able to choose a different value. An optional argument is added to the function ParallelMesh.readMedFile: ghost=1. - Loading EFFE_FOND in HPC (#34910 - 17.4) The loading EFFE_FOND evaluates geometrical quantities (size of the opening of the pipe) on the basis of the mesh. This feature is made compatible with the distributed HPC mesh. - Command COPIER (#35035 - 17.4) The command COPIER is now available for HPC. 13 Performance - Performance of GDEF_LOG (#33694 - 17.1) A great deal of time was spent in “integration of the constitutive law” in the GDEF_LOG case, even with a linear constitutive behaviour, in particular in the computation of the logarithmic strains. The factorisation of the code allows a gain of: - ~20% in “integration of the constitutive law” (ex perf02a) - 7% on average over all the GDEF_LOG tests - Reduce the disk footprint of the outputs of DEFI_SOL_EQUI (#33639 - 17.1) Reduction of the disk footprint of the output files of the macro-command DEFI_SOL_EQUI by offering the user the possibility of recording, in the table recorded in the logical unit UNITE_RESU_TRAN, only: - acceleration at the free field - acceleration at the outcropping bedrock - acceleration at the borehole - acceleration on the lower nodes of the layers of the soil column (defined either via column 'M' of the soil table, or via the keyword COUCHE) For this last point, the user will be able to supply a list with the names of the layers where the accelerations are desired (this can be useful for comparisons with the seismic motion "within"). The keywords TOUT_ACCE and LIST_COUCHE_ACCE are added. - Optimisation of the performance of REST_GENE_PHYS (#33336 - 17.1) In the studies, the time costs of this operator REST_GENE_PHYS (and of DEFI_BASE_MODALE) were disproportionate with respect to those of CALC_MODES (which itself benefits from 3 levels of parallelism and from long-standing optimisations in the modal analysis and in MUMPS). Now that the latter are optimised. Accelerations of up to a factor of 30 are observed. - Simplification of the nodal pairing for LIAISON_GROUP (#33763 - 17.1) The nodal pairing carried out in LIAISON_GROUP was not optimal. There are far too many checks of no usefulness, and the order of the loops has been reversed in order to gain in efficiency. - Mesh reading time (#34447 - 17.3) The naming of the nodes and of the mesh cells in aster is removed. The reading of the mesh LIRE_MAILLAGE in MED format is rewritten in C++ with the med interface which is already available. One can therefore make the best use of the improvements of the collections in C++ with direct accesses in memory. In the example treated, one goes from 5 h to 7 min. 14 Solution and solvers - Industrialisation of MUMPS 5.6.2.2c (#33202 - 17.1) Version upgrade of MUMPS, of its prerequisites (PARMETIS, METIS, SCOTCH, PT-SCOTCH) and of other dependencies: - METIS 5.1.0 ==> identical version but supplied by ParMETIS - MFront 4.1.0 ==> 4.2.0 - MGIS 2.1-dev ==> 2.2 - Scotch 7.0.1 ==> 7.0.4 - Scalapack 2.1.0 ==> 2.2.0 + correction for use of the MKL scalapack if available - Mumps 5.5.1_consortium_aster1 ==> 5.6.2.2c - PETSc 3.17.1_aster ==> PETSc 3.19.5 - mpi4py 3.1.3 ==> 3.1.5 - medcoupling V9_10_0 ==> V9_11_0 Impact on the studies: an improvement of the performance of all the code_aster simulations is noted (when coupled with a related modification of the slurm parameters: between X1.6 and X3 This version allows the correction of several bugs/malfunctions in MUMPS reported by the tests. - Use of “simple Lagrange multipliers” (#33452/33510 - 17.1) In order to limit the number of degrees of freedom, one would like to be able to make do with simple Lagrange multipliers. This is done for the commands STAT_NON_LINE and CALC_PRECONT. For the cases of the macro-command CALC_PRECONT, the keyword DOUBLE_LAGRANGE='OUI' or 'NON' is introduced in order to ensure the homogeneity of the choices with the loadings. - Export the local portion of a matrix or of a vector to petsc4py (#33690 - 17.1) Within the framework of the thesis work on non-linear preconditioning, one wishes to be able to solve a non-linear problem on each sub-domain. To this end, one wishes to export the local portion of a matrix or of a vector to petsc4py. On this basis, one will be able to build a non-linear solver on each sub-domain. - Stop the STAT_NON_LINE analysis by a number of time steps (#34051 - 17.2) The idea is to be able to control more finely the list of time instants of a static analysis in order to limit the memory footprint. The user is left the possibility of controlling the number of time steps in STAT_NON_LINE, whatever the initial length of the list of time instants. The keyword NB_PAS_MAXI is used in DEFI_LIST_INST. If NB_PAS_MAXI is reached, even if one is not at the end of the list of time steps given by the user, the analysis stops cleanly and archives the data. - Develop the non-linear solver RASPEN (#33849 - 17.2) Within the framework of the thesis of Mehdi ETTAOUCHI, work is carried out on non-linear solvers based on domain decomposition. One is interested specifically in the Restrictive Additive Schwarz Preconditioned Exact Newton (RASPEN) approach, which has good robustness properties. It is implemented in MECA_NON_LINE. - Introduction of a second-level preconditioner in RASPEN (#34401 - 17.4) Within the framework of a thesis, work is carried out on non-linear solvers based on domain decomposition. One is interested specifically in the Restrictive Additive Schwarz Preconditioned Exact Newton (RASPEN) approach, which has good robustness properties; introduced in 17.2, it is now proposed to add the possibility of using a 2nd-level preconditioner. Its objective is to improve the scalability of the method in the presence of numerous sub-domains. - Allow time-step cutting with RASPEN (#35109 - 17.4) In order to make RASPEN usable in studies, the possibility of time-step cutting is added. - Add options in PETSC/HPDDM (#34931 - 17.4) The aim of this development is to add keywords under the option SOLVEUR for HPDDM. Another construction of the coarse problem is added, with harmonic_overlap HARMO in addition to geneo GENEO . It is suited to the non-symmetric problem. By default, the solver operates with mode AUTO (default): GENEO if the matrix is SYME, otherwise HARMO. One is also allowed to give the number of modes which one wants to compute for the coarse problem ( NB_MODE , default=30), and a threshold in order to eliminate the useless MODES in relative terms with respect to the most important one (SEUIL, default=0.0, all the modes are kept). 15 Software - The operator STAT_NON_LINE becomes a macro-command (#33752 - 17.3) Be able simply to launch the tests which use STAT_NON_LINE with MECA_NON_LINE in order to draw up the assessments for updating the validation scope of MECA_NON_LINE. STAT_NON_LINE becomes a macro-command which calls the “real” STAT_NON_LINE, renamed STAT_NON_LINE_FORT. The call to MECA_NON_LINE is also added to this macro. Following this integration, it will suffice to change the value of a Boolean in the macro so that STAT_NON_LINE calls MECA_NON_LINE. - Operators DEBUT/POURSUITE (#33431 - 17.1) There is now only the command DEBUT which, in automatic mode (MODE="AUTO", which is the default), initialises the analysis if there is no database and re-reads a database if it exists. With MODE="DEBUT" , a new analysis is initialised even if a database exists. With MODE="POURSUITE" , the database is re-read if it exists, otherwise one stops in error. For compatibility, POURSUITE is retained, equivalent to DEBUT(MODE="POURSUITE"). - Operator FIN : Optimise the tasks (#34113 - 17.2) In FIN, closing the database can take a little time. Yet this is not necessary if one has not planned to recover the database. Objective: a gain in time when the file system is not among the fastest, or when one launches many analyses. - Add dynamic balancing (#33609 - 17.1) Within the framework of studies in which non-linearities are very localised and then propagate, it is necessary to balance the load during the analysis. One can imagine supplying a scalar field at the nodes which will be used as a weight by the partitioner. Addition of the test zzzz155h, which carries out a MECA_STATIQUE analysis and re-cuts the result according to a command given by the user. The analysis uses an AFFE_CHAR_CINE and an AFFE_CHAR_MECA. - New meshes in mesh_builder (#33948 - 17.2) For the needs of field projection, be able to create easily the meshes of a point cloud or else of a 1d spline. Addition of 2 new meshes in mesh_builder.py: buildPointCloud(coordlist, groups=False, info=1) and buildSpline1D(coordlist, groups=False, info=1) - Coupling aster/aster (#34103 - 17.2) Addition of the possibility of carrying out ASTER/ASTER coupling in MPI. For this purpose, an ExternalCoupling object is added which makes it possible to do this. The exchange of the data and the interpolation are done with ParaMEDMEM. The coupling of fields and the conversions are done with MEDCoupler. There are in particular simple Python conversion methods. PLE is necessary in order to split the communicator into two sub-communicators (one per application). If PLE is absent, an emulation is used which merely splits the communicator into two equal parts. This furthermore makes it possible to launch the tests easily. - aster/saturne coupling (#34081 - 17.2) Several issues have been dealt with for the aster/saturne coupling. An object SaturneCoupling is added, which inherits from ExternalCoupling. Only the methods set_parameters and run have been overloaded. Addition of methods on the simple fields in order to carry out Import/Export to MedCouplingField (#34128 - 17.3) - Porting under windows mingw32 (#33476 - 17.2) The modifications necessary for the porting under windows using mingw are capitalised. The platform is identified with the define ASTER_PLATFORM_MINGW (the former ASTER_PLATFORM_WINDOWS, which was not maintained, has been removed). - Facilitate the use of DDT (#33932 - 17.2) The use of DDT in parallel with code_aster, which is a Python module, is complicated. It is proposed to wrap the launching in order to encourage this use. - New module for integration of the constitutive laws (#33770 - 17.2) The renovation of the supervisor of the constitutive laws is undertaken. Observation: the constitutive laws need information in order to work, but this information is often disparate and incomplete. Furthermore, the generalisation of the new procedures (such as the efficient prediction, issue33631) is difficult because of the multiplicity of particular cases and of the considerable volume of source (more than 200 laws). Method: several years ago, a module and derived types had been introduced in order to manage the things in common in nmcomp/lcxxxx. - Make explicit the type integer(kind=8) (#33331 - 17.3) Compilation in integer(kind=8) is no longer forced. This makes it possible to use, for example, the includes of Mumps without having to modify them at installation, and therefore makes it possible to use versions of Mumps which come from packages (conda, for example). The same applies to Med and PETSc. - Extension of run_sbatch and run_aster (#34641 - 17.3) Addition of the options --run_aster_option='--save_db' in order to force the closing of the database, even if there is none as a result in the '.export' file The option '--run_aster_option' is added to run_sbatch in order to pass options to run_aster. The options --time_limit and --memory_limit are also added, which overload the values of the '.export' in order to create the sbatch script and in order to be passed to run_aster. - Pixi configuration in pyproject.toml (#35160 - 17.4) The pixi configuration is available in the file pixi.toml. - Improve the fix method of the mesh (#35044 - 17.4) The fix routine for the mesh (Mesh) is improved, which makes it possible to - check the outward normal for the boundary faces - check the positive volume of the cells - merge duplicate nodes - merge duplicate mesh cells - optimisation of the performance (without degrading the reading and refinement part) - memory optimisation: use of short integers as far as possible. Potential gain of 40% - Reprogramming of the computation of the strains (#35080 - 17.4) The programming of the option EPSP_ELGA is revised in order to avoid duplications at several levels: computation of the total strains and computation of the anelastic strains coming from the command variables. - Extension of the computation of the inelastic strains (#35101 - 17.4) The reprogramming of the computation of the strains is extended to the options: EPSP_ELGA (plastic strains), EPM_ELGA (mechanical strains), EPVC_ELGA (anelastic strains) and ENER / ETOT / INDI_ERRE: energies and error indicators. - Switch of the base OS to debian 12 (#35068 - 17.4) - Version upgrade of the prerequisites : 20251026 (#34454 - 17.4) The new prerequisites are: - medcoupling c3928d335 (9.15 modified) - asrun 7d7eafcd (future 2025) - mfront 5.0.1 - mgis 3.0.1 - med 4.2.0 - petsc 3.24.0 - python 3.11 with numpy, scipy, sympy, pandas. - Addition of documentation on the launching of code_aster, u1.04.00 (#34576 - 17.4) 16 Syntax modifications and removals - The command POURSUITE may be replaced by DEBUT(MODE="POURSUITE") (#33431 - 17.1) - In the command CREA_RESU , the keyword NOM_CHAM is moved into the factor keyword AFFE (#33432 - 17.1) - In the command DYNA_NON_LINE , the default value of AMOR_RAYL_RIGI is changed to the value 'ELASTIQUE' (#33825 - 17.1) - The keyword ELAS_FO/FONC_DESORP becomes BETON_DESORP/FONC_DESORP with BETON_DESORP (#33617 - 17.2) - The default behaviour of MACR_SPECTRE is changed so as not to print by default the envelope of the horizontal directions of the spectra, denoted H (#33961 - 17.2) - In AFFE_CARA_ELEM , a single occurrence possible for MASS_AJOU & RIGI_MISS_3D (#34507 17.3) - Prohibition of MODI_METRIQUE=OUI for the pipes (#34450 17.3) - Removal in CREA_MAILLAGE of the keywords: PREF_MAILLE , PREF_NOEUD and PREF_NUM (#34447 17.3) - Removal of the keyword NIV_PUB_WEB in DEBUT (#34633 17.3) - Removal of the harmfulness index “destructive power” POUV_DEST from INFO_FONCTION (#34175 -17.3) - Removal of the operator CALC_IFS_DNL (Calcium coupling) #32446 17.3 - Removal of the operator THER_NON_LINE_MO (#33520 -17.3) - Operator POST_BEREMIN — moving of the keyword GROUP_MA under WEIBULL(_FO) (#34565 - 17.4) - Operator POST_BEREMIN : improvement of the ergonomics and update of numerous keywords (#34979 #34981 - 17.4) - Operator CALC_MATE_HOMO : removal of VECT_NORM (#34898 - 17.4) In the operator CALC_MATE_HOMO, the keyword VECT_NORM is removed and the Z axis is used by default. The material THER is also made compulsory for TYPE_HOMO="PLAQUE" (#34565 - 17.4) - Clarification of the treatment of REPERE in MACR_LIGN_COUPE (#35098 - 17.4) Addition of an optional keyword REPERE_INIT = "GLOBAL" or "LOCAL". This keyword is necessary when one requests a change of frame on an ELGA, ELNO or ELEM field (liable to be expressed in the LOCAL frame) in order to raise an error if the base field was not expressed in the GLOBAL frame - Removal of the event COLLISION in DEFI_LIST_INST (#35029 - 17.4) - Operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM: Modification of the keyword VERIF =[OUI | NON] (#34561 - 17.4) - Operator POST_ROCHE (#35056 - 17.4) RESU_MECA_TRAN is removed and RCCM_RX is renamed SIGM_LIM.

u4.01.14 New features and modifications of version 18 u4.01.14 New features and modifications of version 18 Summary: The purpose of this document is to provide an overall view of the syntax modifications and of the new possibilities of the code_aster commands introduced during the development of version 18, that is, since version 17.4. For further details, one should consult the documentation of the commands and the histor files of the sub-versions. 1 Mechanics - New stabilised mixed finite elements (#35072 - 18.1) A new type of stabilised mixed linear elements is introduced (formulation u, epsilon). These are the modellings 3D_MIX_STA and D_PLAN_MIX_STA . The additional degrees of freedom are the strain components (EPXX, EPYY ... etc). The detail of the formulations is given in R3.06.15. - New isoparametric cubic element in 2D (#35515 - 18.1) The following isoparametric cubic elements are added: TRIA10, QUAD12 and TETRA20 - New pile-foundation finite element 3D_INTERF_POU (#33213 - 18.1) A new finite element is added representing a non-linear phenomenological interaction between a pile segment (model POU_D_T) and a small volume of soil around it (3D model — HEXA8). It may be described as an “interface” element. This new finite element must be associated with the material INTERF_POU_ELAS or INTERF_POU_CINE . The detail of the formulations is given in R3.06.15. - Improvement of the HHO elements and extension of the features. Several issues deal with these improvements: - Addition of the modelling AXIS_HHO. (#32760 - 18.1) - Addition of the use of the line search in statics (#35433 - 18.1) - Addition of the use of piloting (#35432 - 18.1) - Addition of the prism and penta geometric supports (#35409 - 18.1) - Addition of post-processings (#35293 - 18.1) - Addition of static condensation (#35447 - 18.1) - Addition of the modellings AXIS_HHO_GRAD_VARI (#35287 - 18.1) - Addition of the VARC stresses for HHO (#35438 - 18.1) - Addition of the HHO elements with MECA_STATIQUE (#35439 - 18.1) 2 Constitutive laws - Constitutive law BETON_BURGER (#35484 - 18.1) The names of the internal variables are renamed (in order to shorten them) in the MFRONT file. - Addition of hardening recovery for the constitutive law VMIS_ISOT_NL (#35545 - 18.1) The hardening-recovery feature REST_ECRO is added for the constitutive law VMIS_ISOT_NL. - Cohesive law equivalent to JOINT_MECA_FROT (#35543 - 18.1) A cohesive law equivalent to JOINT_MECA_FROT is added, based on a mixed formulation carried by the interface elements. - Modification of the creep law in the constitutive law BETON_RAG (#35499 - 18.1) This development concerns the rewriting of the creep part with a formulation of BURGER type _R7.01.35. As in the former formulation, the creep law involves spherical and deviatoric creep strains. The essential difference between the new law and the former one comes from the description of reversible and irreversible creep. - Implementation of the constitutive law DIS_ECRO_CINE in DYNA_VIBRA (#35738 - 18.1) The possibility is added of using the constitutive law DIS_ECRO_CINE in the operator DYNA_VIBRA, so that this law can be used in the framework of dynamic analyses on a modal basis. 3 Contact - So-called “element-based” method (#35413 - 18.1) Implementation of an alternative method for numerical integration in frictional contact with a mortar approach (with ray casting/raytracing). In this classical so-called “element-based” method, all the integration points of the slave mesh cell are projected. This method is developed for the operator DEFI_CONT usable with MECA_NON_LINE. 4 Loadings and pre-processing - New linear relation on a generalised modal basis AFFE_CHAR_GENE . (#34773 - 18.1) A new operator is added in order to define loadings on the modellings on a modal basis. Via the factor keyword LIAISON , one can impose a non-homogeneous linear relation between degrees of freedom of the problem in a context of solution on a modal basis. - New computation for RIGI_PARASOL via the keyword METHODE (#35216 - 18.1) For AFFE_CARA_ELEM, options RIGI_PARASOL and RIGI_GRILLE, the computation of the area assigned to the node has until now been carried out by dividing the area of the mesh cell by the number of nodes of the mesh cell. This computation is exact for all the TR3 and for the QU4 whose angles are right angles (comparison PRES_REP), but not for the other supports. A new method is proposed, based on the same methodology as PRES_REP and FORCE_COQUE. A new keyword METHODE='UNIFORME'/'DIAG' is introduced for the choice of the distribution method, with METHODE = 'DIAG' by default (new distribution method; the former method remains accessible via 'UNIFORME'). 5 Post-processings - Computation of SIEF_ELGA and STRX_ELGA (#35440 - 18.1) The computation of SIEF_ELGA and STRX_ELGA is added in MECA_STATIQUE . - Addition of account taken of complex matrices for PROJ_BASE (#35707 - 18.1) The operator PROJ_BASE can carry out projections with complex matrices, as was already possible with PROJ_MATR_BASE. - Med output for checking the cut lines (#35079 - 18.1) In the command MACR_LIGN_COUPE, the output of a med file is allowed, presenting the results obtained at each node of the cut, in order to facilitate the checking and the exploitation of the results produced during the cut. In addition, a paravis/paraview macro has been developed in order to automate the visualisation of this med file in paravis. This macro is present in the code_aster sources (repo src->data->paraview->macros). - Addition of a MED attribute for the description of the fields (#34432 - 18.1) This description is used in the aster to medcoupling conversion and in IMPR_RESU. - code-aster / code-saturne coupling (#35741 , #35740 - 18.1) The possibility is added of projecting the P0 fluid-force field with the nodal projection. 6 Performance - Improvement of the command CALC_FERRAILLAGE (#35021 - 18.1) Thanks to a refactoring of the code, the performance of the reinforcement computation at ELS_QP is improved. A speed-up by a factor of 8 is observed on certain runs. 7 Solution and solvers - Change to DEFI_LIST_INST and addition of the first time step PAS_INIT (#34657 -18.1) The keyword PAS_INIT is added, alongside PAS_MINI and PAS_MAXI. It makes it possible to set the starting value of the time step. This change is available only in MECA_NON_LINE. - Optimise the acceleration of the time step (#35652 - 18.1) In the case of automatic adaptation of the time step, one may be obliged to take a very small time step in order to pass over the points of the list of time instants. The optimum consists in keeping the time step as large as possible before the compulsory passage instant, so that the time step following that instant is itself also as large as possible. This change is available only in MECA_NON_LINE. 8 Syntax modifications and removals - Removal of the command CALC_BT (#32638 - 18.1) - Removal of the constitutive laws PINTO_MENEGOTTO and GRILLE_PINTO_MEM (#33840 - 18.1) - Removal of the option PETIT_REAC for DKT and COQUE_3D (#35530 - 18.1) - Removal of FORCE_ELEC and DEFI_FONC_ELEC (#32742 - 18.1) - Modification of the computation mode of RIGI_PARASOL and RIGI_GRILLE with the use of a new keyword METHODE='UNIFORME'/'DIAG' ('DIAG' by default). - Renaming of the internal variables of the constitutive law BETON_BURGER (#35484 - 18.1)

u4.03.01 Title and subtitle of a produced concept u4.03.01 Title and subtitle of a produced concept 1 Purpose Define a title or a subtitle during the execution of an Aster command. The title and the subtitle, when they are provided for by the command, are: - either defined by default, - or supplied by the user. The title is attached to the data structure produced by an operator. The titles of the modified concepts are stacked. The choice of a title is possible as soon as the operator has a simple keyword TITRE. The expected argument is a list of texts (l_Kn). The text supplied by the user is used as it stands; in particular, there is no implicit lower-case/upper-case conversion. The subtitle makes it possible to add comments on the occasion of a printout by a procedure. The subtitle exists only for the duration of the procedure and must therefore be rebuilt at each call to the procedure, in particular if the latter is reused in POURSUITE. It is therefore not attached to a concept. The choice of a subtitle is possible as soon as the procedure has the simple keyword SOUS_TITRE (possibly under a factor keyword). It is therefore not attached to a concept. The expected argument is a list of texts (l_Kn).

u4.11.01 Procedure DEBUT u4.11.01 Procedure DEBUT 1 Purpose Assign the memory, disk and file resources. The execution consists of a set of commands beginning with DEBUT and ending with FIN. See also the procedure POURSUITE. The command DEBUT carries out the following tasks: - Definition of the characteristics of the databases (managed by JEVEUX) and allocation of the associated files, - Reading of the catalogues of the elements and of the commands. The apparently complex syntax of this procedure should not worry the user; calling it with the default operands, sufficient in most cases, is: DEBUT(). 2 Syntax DEBUT( ◇ IMPR_MACRO = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ BASE = _F( ◆ FICHIER = / "GLOBALE", / "VOLATILE", ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ CAS = text, ◇ NMAX_ENRE = int, ◇ LONG_ENRE = int, ◇ LONG_REPE = int, ), ◇ CATALOGUE = _F( ◆ FICHIER = text, ◇ UNITE = unit, ), ◇ CODE = / "NON", / "OUI", ◇ ERREUR = _F( ◇ ERREUR_F = / "ABORT", / "EXCEPTION", ◇ ALARME = / "ALARME", / "EXCEPTION", ), ⟐ DEBUG = _F( ◇ JXVERI = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ SDVERI = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ JEVEUX = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ ENVIMA = "TEST" (ou non renseigné), ◇ VERI_BASE = / "GLOBALE", / "VOLATILE", ◇ VERI_BASE_NB = int (défaut: 125), ), ⟐ MESURE_TEMPS = _F( ◇ NIVE_DETAIL = / 0, / 1 (par défaut), / 2, / 3, ◇ MOYENNE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ), ⟐ MEMOIRE = _F( ◇ TAILLE_BLOC = float (défaut: 800.0), ◇ TAILLE_GROUP_ELEM = int (défaut: 1000), ), ⟐ RESERVE_CPU = _F( ◇ / VALE = int, / POURCENTAGE = float, ), ⟐ RESERVE_MEMOIRE = _F( ◇ / VALE = int, / POURCENTAGE = float, ), ◇ IGNORE_ALARM = list[text], ◇ LANG = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ MODE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "DEBUT", / "POURSUITE", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Displays At the start of the execution, a header is displayed. It contains: - The precise identification of the version used: version number, date of the latest modifications, - The date and time of the start of the execution, - The name, the architecture and the operating system of the machine, - The language used for the display of the messages, - The type of parallelism available (MPI/OpenMP), the number of processors allocated, - The version of the libraries used (when it is available) for hdf5, med, mumps, scotch, - Then several pieces of information on the distribution of the memory. For example: Mémoire limite pour l'allocation dynamique : 1894.40 Mo ajouté à l'initialisation du processus : 1125.45 Mo Limite cible du processus : 3019.85 Mo This means: - 1894.40 Mo is the quantity of memory reserved for the internal objects. In detail: the user requested 1536.00 Mo. 10% was removed (default value of RESERVE_MEMOIRE/POURCENTAGE), leaving 1382.40 Mo. 512.00 Mo is always added for the internal Jeveux objects, giving 1894.40 Mo. - 1125.45 Mo is consumed simply by starting the execution (loading of the executable, of the associated dynamic libraries, and so on). It is a measured value. - 3019.85 Mo is the sum of the two previous values. It is the total quantity of memory that must not be exceeded. During the execution, depending on the dynamic allocations carried out, when this value varies by more than 10% (upwards or downwards), a message of this type informs the user: La mémoire consommée actuellement hors JEVEUX est de 214.08 Mo. La limite de l'allocation dynamique JEVEUX est fixée à 41.92 Mo. En fin d'exécution, un bilan indique si le même calcul peut être relancé avec moins de mémoire: La mémoire demandée au lancement est surestimée, elle est de 256 Mo. Le pic mémoire utilisée est de 216.02 Mo. or if more memory is necessary (indeed, depending on the platforms, the maximum limit may be exceeded without the system having interrupted the analysis): La mémoire demandée au lancement est sous-estimée, elle est de 256 Mo. Le pic mémoire utilisée est de 273.22 Mo. 4 Operands 4.1 Keyword IMPR_MACRO Allows or disallows the displays produced by the macros in the message file. Reading the message files can be tedious when they contain all of the echoes of the sub-commands generated by the macro itself. By default, only the echo of the commands explicitly called by the user in the command set will appear. 4.2 Keyword LANG It makes it possible to choose the display language of the messages issued by the code. If the keyword is not set, it is the environment variables that determine the language of the messages (reference: gettext manual). One may for example define in the file ~/.bashrc: export LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8. The encoding (UTF-8 or ISO-8859-1) makes it possible to display accented characters correctly. The keyword LANG expects a two-letter value, for example 'FR' (for French) or 'EN' (for English). When a language is chosen (whether by the environment or by LANG), the translated message file (.mo file) must still be available. This file is expected under this name: :file: ASTER_ROOT/share/locale/ /LC_MESSAGES/aster_ .mo where ASTER_ROOT is the main directory of the installation (e.g.: /aster or /opt/aster), lang is the lower-case name of the language (e.g. en, fr, de...) and version is the name of the version used (e.g. stable, testing, unstable). If the translation file cannot be read, French is used. Note Even if the translation file exists, when a message has not been translated, it is displayed in French (the language in which the messages are written in the source code). 4.3 Keyword BASE The purpose of this keyword is to redefine the values of the parameters of the direct-access files associated with the "databases" in the case where one does not wish to use those set by default. Default values of the parameters associated with the databases. | GLOBALE | | | --- | --- | | NMAX_ENRE | 62914 | | LONG_ENRE | 100 Kwords | | LONG_REPE | 2000 | | VOLATILE | | | NMAX_ENRE | 62914 | | LONG_ENRE | 100 Kwords | | LONG_REPE | 2000 | The word is worth 8 bytes on a 64-bit platform, 4 bytes on a 32-bit platform. Under 64-bit Linux, with the default values, the procedure DEBUT will allocate a direct-access file of at most 62914 records of 100 Kwords (K is worth 1024) for the 'GLOBALE' database. Note The real size of the file is dynamic; it depends on the volume of information actually to be stored. The information is stored in files not exceeding 12 Go each. This value can be modified by passing an argument on the command line of the executable after the keyword --max_base=taille , where taille is a real value measured in Mo. For the Globale database, which can be saved and reused as input to an analysis, the initial maximum size in POURSUITE is kept as it is if the parameter --max_base is not used, but it may be redefined if needed in this way. In practice, this option is not useful, the maximum size being 2 To. 4.3.1 Operand FICHIER Symbolic name of the database concerned. 4.3.2 Operands LONG_ENRE / NMAX_ENRE / LONG_REPE Definition of the parameters of the database (direct-access files). LONG_ENRE is the length of the records, in Kwords, of the direct-access files used. Note The JEVEUX memory manager uses this parameter to determine two types of object: the large objects, which will be split into as many records as necessary, and the small objects, which will be accumulated in a buffer the size of one record before being unloaded. NMAX_ENRE is the default number of records; this value is determined from LONG_ENRE and from an operational parameter on the Linux 64 reference platform, set to 2 To for the maximum total size of a database, if this value has not been modified by the use of the keyword --max_base on the command line of the executable. Note The two operands LONG_ENRE and NMAX_ENRE must be used with care, incorrect use being able to lead to an abrupt stop of the program by saturation of the direct-access files. Consistency between the maximum size of the file and the value resulting from the product of the two parameters LONG_ENRE and NMAX_ENRE is checked at the start of the execution. LONG_REPE is the initial length of the directory (maximum number of objects addressable by JEVEUX); it is managed dynamically by the memory manager, which extends the size of the directory and of all the associated system objects as needs arise. Note The user's choice to modify these various parameters definitively determines certain characteristics of the GLOBALE database, which can no longer be modified in POURSUITE. 4.4 Keyword CODE This keyword is intended only for the command files of the test cases. It modifies the behaviour in the event of an error or an exception, and activates the coverage of the keywords... 4.5 Keyword ERREUR Makes it possible to modify the behaviour of the code in the event of an error. 4.5.1 Operand ERREUR_F In the event of an error, the code interrupts the normal execution of the command set. By default, an exception is then raised (for the detailed definition of a Python exception, one should refer to the Python documentation or to that of the supervisor, cf. U1.03.01). In this case, the code executes the command FIN (cf. U4.11.02), which then closes the database so as to allow a possible restart of the analysis. It will be noted that, although the initial error is said to be "fatal" ( ), the diagnosis is _ERROR because the exception is "caught" by FIN. This database will then be copied by the study manager. This is the behaviour when ERREUR_F='EXCEPTION'. If ERREUR_F='ABORT', this means that one explicitly asks the code to interrupt definitively the execution of the command set in the event of a fatal error ( ). The command FIN is not executed, the database is therefore not closed correctly, it is not copied and no restart of the analysis is possible. Notes For the execution of the test cases by the developers, stopping by ABORT is automatic and is the default. This is activated by the presence of the factor keyword CODE (unless ERREUR_F specifies something else). In the event of a lack of CPU time or of memory, for all errors of type and for exceptions, the behaviour is that described when ERREUR_F='EXCEPTION'. 4.6 Keyword IGNORE_ALARM Allows the user to suppress the display of certain alarms (whose origin is known) in order to identify more easily the other alarms that might appear. During the execution of the command FIN, a summary table of the alarms issued during the execution (and the number of occurrences) is systematically displayed. The alarms ignored by the user are preceded by ' ' to distinguish them (and they appear even if they have not been issued). The alarms are designated from the nomenclature appearing between the characters , for example: IGNORE_ALARME = ('MED_2', 'SUPERVIS_40',...). 4.7 Keyword DEBUG Debugging option (reserved for developers and for maintenance of the code). 4.7.1 Operand JXVERI Makes it possible to check the integrity of the memory segments between two consecutive command executions. By default the execution is carried out without "DEBUG". This option is systematically activated in the presence of the keyword CODE. 4.7.2 Operand ENVIMA Makes it possible to display the values of the parameters defined in the routine ENVIMA characterising the machine D6.01.01. 4.7.3 Operand JEVEUX Makes it possible to activate the debug operating mode of the JEVEUX memory manager: non-deferred unloading to disk and assignment of the value segments to an undefined value D6.02.01. 4.7.4 Operand SDVERI Use of this keyword is intended for developers. Warning: this functionality can cause a non-negligible extra cost during the execution. This keyword triggers the checking of the data structures produced by the operators. It is used within the code development procedures in the non-regression tests. If the keyword CODE is present, this keyword takes the default value 'OUI'. 4.8 Keyword MESURE_TEMPS The keyword MESURE_TEMPS makes it possible to choose the level of detail of the CPU time printouts that will be displayed in the message file by the commands carrying out elementary computations, resolutions of linear systems, unloading of objects to disk or MPI communications. 4.8.1 Operand NIVE_DETAIL ◊ NIVE_DETAIL = 0 aucune impression. = 1 impressions par défaut. = 2 impressions plus détaillées: = 3 impressions plus détaillées et impression incrémentale pour chaque pas de temps. By default, at the end of each command, a line of the following type will be printed: #1.Resolution.des.systemes.lineaires CPU.(USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 7.52 0.79 11.22 #2.Calculs.elementaires.et.assemblages CPU.(USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 15.07 0.70 15.77 #1.Resolution.des.systemes.lineaires CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 7.72 0.82 8.72 #1.1.Numerotation,.connectivité.de.la.matrice CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.21 0.02 0.31 #1.2.Factorisation.symbolique CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.58 0.05 1.28 #1.3.Factorisation.numerique.(ou.precond.) CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 6.78 0.73 7.71 #1.4.Resolution CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.15 0.02 0.35 #2.Calculs.elementaires.et.assemblages CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS) : 28.87 0.64 29.47 #2.1.Routine.calcul CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 26.61 0.56 26.61 #2.1.1.Routines.te00ij CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 24.58 0.07 25.78 #2.2.Assemblages CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 2.26 0.08 3.36 #2.2.1.Assemblage.matrices CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 2.02 0.06 3.12 #2.2.2.Assemblage.seconds.membres CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.24 0.02 0.37 During parallel analyses (MPI), the time spent in communications is also displayed: #4 Communications MPI CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 12.67 0.50 12.68 4.8.2 Operand MOYENNE The keyword MOYENNE makes it possible to control the display of additional statistics exclusively for parallel analyses. These are the mean of the measurements over all the processors and the standard deviation of these measurements. Each displayed time is then completed as follows: #1 Résolution.des.systèmes.linéaires CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.29 0.00 0.35 (moyenne....diff..procs) CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.30 0.00 0.47 (écart-type.diff..procs) CPU (USER+SYST/SYST/ELAPS): 0.01 0.00 0.05 4.9 Keyword MEMOIRE The allocation of the various data structures is a dynamic allocation; the user indicates the resource limits when launching the executable in the access interface. 4.9.1 Operand TAILLE_GROUP_ELEM This parameter gives the maximum number of finite elements of the same type that will be grouped in a group of elements. This parameter influences the memory and CPU performance of the elementary computations and of the assemblies. When tgrel is increased, one should in general gain CPU time. On the other hand, the JEVEUX objects are larger, which may require more memory. 4.9.2 Operand TAILLE_BLOC This parameter gives the size of the blocks of the factorised matrices for the LDLT solver. This size is given in kiloR8 (1 kiloR8 = 1024 reals). This parameter affects the number of input/output operations and therefore the assembly and resolution time. By default this value is set to 800 kiloR8, that is 8 records by default on the direct-access file associated with the JEVEUX database. 4.10 Keyword CATALOGUE This keyword is reserved for developers; it is used during the operation of compiling the element catalogues in order to obtain the file in the form of a JEVEUX database. 4.10.1 Operand FICHIER Can only take the value 'CATAELEM'. 4.10.2 Operand UNITE Number of the logical unit associated with the element catalogues. In the procedures for building the element catalogue, the value 4 is used. The file fort.4 is obtained from the content of the source directory by means of a Python procedure. 4.11 Keyword RESERVE_CPU Makes it possible to reserve a share of the CPU time allocated to the job in order to terminate the execution cleanly in the event of a stop for lack of CPU time detected by a command. This mechanism is useful only in the case of a batch execution. The value of this reserve may be given as an absolute value or else in the form of a percentage of the total CPU time. When the keyword CODE is present, that is for all the tests, a CPU time reserve of 10 seconds is systematically imposed if the keyword VALE is absent. At the end of the execution, it may be necessary to carry out compression operations before transfer of the result files or of the Globale database, which are sometimes very costly. 4.11.1 Operand VALE This is the value, expressed in seconds, subtracted from the total CPU time, on which certain global commands rely in order to stop the execution cleanly. 4.11.2 Operand POURCENTAGE Percentage subtracted from the total CPU time, on which certain global commands rely in order to stop the execution cleanly. 4.12 Keyword RESERVE_MEMOIRE Makes it possible to reserve a share of the memory allocated to the job for the objects other than the internal Jeveux objects (those whose size cannot be measured precisely). This mechanism is useful only in the case of a batch execution. The value of this reserve may be given as an absolute value or else in the form of a percentage of the memory requested initially. 4.12.1 Operand VALE This is the value expressed in Mo (1024 ko, that is 1024 x 1024 bytes) that will be subtracted from the quantity of memory requested initially. 4.12.2 Operand POURCENTAGE Percentage of the memory requested initially that will be allocated to the reserve and therefore not available for the Jeveux objects.

u4.11.02 Command FIN u4.11.02 Command FIN 1 Purpose This command terminates the execution of an analysis cleanly. In this way, one tells the memory manager that the objects may be released and written to disk in the global database (and a restart, POURSUITE, made possible). The call to this procedure is mandatory for the execution to finish correctly, which requires every command file to end with: FIN() 2 Syntax FIN( ◇ RETASSAGE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ INFO_BASE = / "NON", / "OUI", ◇ INFO_RESU = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands The command FIN saves all the concepts computed during the execution in the file glob.1 (and possibly glob.2 , ... if necessary), as well as all the Python objects of the execution context in pickle files. These objects will be available for a restart (POURSUITE) of the analysis. If the user has not asked for the database to be copied after the analysis (there is no database in the .export file of the study), FIN will do nothing. Note Python objects of class, function and type kinds are not saved in the file :file: pick.codeaster.objects . When FIN has finished its work, Python continues to analyse the instructions that follow, and these will certainly fail if they call code_aster objects. The developer may use FIN(exit=True) to force an exit from the Python interpreter. 3.1 Keyword RETASSAGE Causes the 'GLOBALE' database to be repacked before it is written to the associated file. This makes it possible to keep smaller databases (cleared of the objects associated with the concepts destroyed by the user). This repacking is carried out by the command as follows: - closure of the databases, - opening of the 'GLOBALE' database, - opening of a 'VOLATILE' database, - copy, non-empty record by non-empty record, of the 'GLOBALE' database onto the 'VOLATILE' database, - renaming by the code of this 'VOLATILE' database so that it is saved as if it were the standard 'GLOBALE' database. The GLOBALE database consists of one or more binary files organised as fixed-length records. During destruction operations, the associated records are declared free and may possibly be reused during the run. At the end of the run, unoccupied records may remain and contribute to the final size of the file. The repacking operation therefore consists in reusing this space by reorganising the records. It is an operation that can lead to a large number of disk reads and writes. In a standard parallel run (MPI), in "centralised" mode, each instance of the GLOBALE database is processed, which multiplies the input/output. In distributed mode, each instance manages its own input/output according to its needs. 3.2 Keyword INFO_RESU Causes information relating to the content of all the result data structures stored in the GLOBALE database to be printed in the MESSAGE file. Note: Use of this keyword can considerably increase the execution time of the command FIN and produce very large output files. For this reason, it is not activated by default. 3.3 Keyword INFO_BASE This keyword makes it possible to print, in the MESSAGE file, the list of objects present in the global database together with their size. When the database is saved, the printout is produced automatically. Otherwise, this keyword can be activated in order to display the list.

u4.11.03 Procedure POURSUITE u4.11.03 Procedure POURSUITE 1 Purpose Restart a study from the database save carried out by FIN. This command is retained for compatibility reasons. Indeed, one may simply use DEBUT(), whether to start a study or to resume the execution. In the presence of the database, the restart of the previous analysis is performed automatically. New since version 17 . The syntax is therefore identical to that of the command DEBUT, even if some keywords have no effect in POURSUITE. 2 Syntax The syntax is identical to that of the command DEBUT, even if some keywords have no effect in POURSUITE. 3 Operating principle The restart carries out the following tasks: - definition of the logical units of the files used for printout, - allocation of the files associated with the databases managed by JEVEUX, - reading of the command catalogues but not of the element catalogues, which were copied onto the database during the first execution. The simple Python concepts (of variable type) created during a previous execution are kept in a file associated with the JEVEUX database (pick. ). During the execution of the procedure POURSUITE these concepts are regenerated and can therefore be used under the name with which they were created. Note Objects of class, function and type kinds are not saved by Python when FIN is called and will therefore not be available in a restart. See paragraph u4.11.03-exemples. 4 Operands For the Globale database, which can be saved and reused as input to an analysis, the initial maximum size in POURSUITE is kept as it is if the argument --max_base is not used, but it may be redefined if needed in this way. 5 Examples of use The standard use of this procedure is: POURSUITE() Python does not save the functions and classes defined in the main file (it merely remembers in which Python module they were defined). This is therefore the case for the code_aster command file. To use functions or classes and recover them in a restart, they must be defined in an external module: - Either the module userpkg/usermod.py: def pyfunc(x): return x 2 - One would do, in the first command set: DEBUT() from userpkg import usermod form = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X', VALE='pyfunc(X)', pyfunc=usermod.pyfunc) assert form(2) == 4 FIN() - Then: POURSUITE() assert form(2) == 4 FIN() For this, it is enough to add to the study the directory userpkg of type nom . One must understand that, on re-reading, Python will try to import the module userpkg.usermod . It must therefore find it in the same place. Moreover, by importing this module, Python executes the instructions it finds there. For this reason, it is not recommended to create concepts in the main body of an imported module (because they will be created on every import and will clutter the database). This must be done in functions that will be executed only on request.

u4.12.03 Procedure DEFI_FICHIER u4.12.03 Procedure DEFI_FICHIER 1 Purpose Open or close a file associated with a logical-unit number. This number may be indicated in the procedure or else obtained in return from the latter. This action may be carried out at any moment during the work. This procedure makes it possible to associate a logical-unit number with a FORTRAN file of ASCII type, but this notion may also apply, with certain restrictions, to files of binary type. 2 Syntax entier = DEFI_FICHIER( ◇ ACTION = / "ASSOCIER" (par défaut), / "LIBERER", / "RESERVER", # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'ASSOCIER') ◆ | UNITE = unit, | FICHIER = text, ◇ TYPE = / "ASCII" (par défaut), / "BINARY", / "LIBRE", # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'ASCII') ◇ ACCES = / "NEW" (par défaut), / "APPEND", / "OLD", # Si: not equal_to("TYPE", 'ASCII') ◇ ACCES = / "NEW" (par défaut), / "OLD", # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'RESERVER') ◆ | UNITE = unit, | FICHIER = text, ◇ TYPE = "ASCII", ◇ ACCES = "APPEND", # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'LIBERER') ◆ / UNITE = unit, / FICHIER = text, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Behaviour of DEFI_FICHIER Input/output on ASCII files from Code_Aster is carried out, for the most part, by means of FORTRAN instructions using the notion of a logical unit ; it is an integer varying from 1 to 99 associated, by means of an instruction of "open" type, with a file. By default this number xx is associated with the name fort.xx, but it is possible to associate it with any file name. The logical-unit number is used in the astk access interface to the code in order to copy the input and output files. In the Aster command file the various operators carrying out reads or writes accept the keyword UNITE as an argument. Logical unit 6 is reserved by the code during the initialisation phase. It is not permitted to modify this logical-unit number 6, which makes it possible to trace the progress of an execution. | logical unit | file name | modification allowed | | --- | --- | --- | | 6 | MESSAGE | no | The user may wish to add or modify associations by means of the procedure DEFI_FICHIER in order, for example, to use new file names, to print certain results or to group them differently in files. The procedure DEFI_FICHIER also makes it possible to designate directly the file of ASCII type that will be associated with the specified logical unit. It may be specified either by an absolute name (limited to 255 characters) if the file is located on the machine, or by a relative name in an agreed directory (./REPE_IN or ./REPE_OUT) when the interface is responsible for the remote and global transfer of all the files located under the directory (type repe in astk). A named Fortran OPEN is then carried out on the files of ASCII type. The command also makes it possible to position oneself either at the head of the file or at the end of the file. The code manages internally a data structure gathering all the associations logical unit – file name – file type – access type. 4 Operands The modification or modifications of the logical-unit–file-name association concern the output files and the input files. 4.1 Operand ACTION ◊ ACTION= 'ASSOCIER' The logical-unit number is associated, when this is permitted, with the name defined after the keyword FICHIER if it is filled in, and with the name fort.xx otherwise. It is not possible to redefine the associations of the logical numbers 6 and 9. ◊ ACTION= 'LIBERER' The logical-unit number is released; it is no longer valid to use this unit number. The associated file, when it is of ASCII type, is the subject of a close order by means of the Fortran CLOSE instruction. It then becomes possible to reuse the logical-unit number with an action of type ‘LIBERER’. This mechanism is essential if one wishes to be able to reuse immediately the content of the associated file in the command file in progress; indeed the buffers must have been completely flushed and the file must be accessible, possibly during a call to a piece of software from a Python command of type os.system. ◊ ACTION= 'RESERVER' This type of action is used in the macro-commands and makes it possible to avoid conflicts of logical-unit number between Fortran and Python. The logical-unit number is associated, when this is permitted, with the name defined after the keyword FICHIER if it is filled in, and with the name fort.xx otherwise. There is no instruction of OPEN type executed; it is up to the macro-command to carry out the various necessary actions. 4.2 Operand FICHIER ◊ FICHIER= nomfic Physical name of the file (< 255 characters) that one wishes to associate with a logical unit. This file will be created under the execution directory of the code, but one may indicate directly a file name (complying with UNIX conventions) in the user's directory. Under the execution directory, it is possible to use an additional level of directory tree of conventional name REPE_IN (data files) or REPE_OUT (result files) recognised by the astk access interface to the code. This name must be placed between quotes. Although they are not associated with a logical unit by a Fortran OPEN order, binary files (for example MED) may be treated with this mechanism; one must nevertheless specify the access type NEW or OLD in order to activate the copy (by a system call from the code) from the data directory or towards the result directory. When the operand is absent, it is by default the file name fort.ul, where ul is the unit number, that is associated with the logical unit defined after UNITE. For files of ASCII type, a Fortran OPEN instruction is executed on the name associated with the logical unit. 4.3 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE= numul Associated logical-unit number; its value for the ASCII files opened by instructions lies between 1 and 99 inclusive. It is possible to reuse a number already assigned, but in this case one must take the precaution of releasing the latter beforehand. Certain logical-unit numbers cannot be redefined from the Aster commands; these are the numbers 6 and 9, which are allocated respectively to the files MESSAGE and ERREUR. This number may then be used in all the Aster commands that have the operand UNITE (IMPR_RESU, IMPR_TABLE, IMPR_FONCTION, etc.). The operand UNITE may sometimes be omitted; it is then the code that will choose to assign a number, according to availability. One must then necessarily specify the operand FICHIER; the code then takes care internally of associating the logical-unit number and the associated file. It is then possible to recover an integer value on output from the operator. 4.4 Operand TYPE ◊ TYPE= 'ASCII' The file associated with the logical unit is of ASCII type. ◊ TYPE= 'LIBRE' The file associated with the logical unit is of a type undetermined in the Fortran sense; this makes it possible to manage access to the file more flexibly. This type is used essentially for access to MED files. The logical unit is not really used in this case, but this makes it possible to have the naming convention fort.ul on the file and to be able to transmit it easily through the access interface to the code. ◊ TYPE= 'BINARY' The file associated with the logical unit is of BINARY type. 4.5 Operand ACCES ◊ ACCES= 'NEW' The file of "ASCII" type is opened and one positions oneself at the head; a Fortran instruction of REWIND type is executed. If it exists, the file is overwritten. To be used for a result file. ◊ ACCES= 'OLD' The file of "ASCII" type is opened and one positions oneself as it is, that is to say possibly at the position at which one was during the last access. To be used for a data file. ◊ ACCES= 'APPEND' The file is opened and one positions oneself at the end of the file. Used only in the case of files of ASCII type. To be used for a data file that one wishes to complete (which will therefore a priori be a result file). 4.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= inf Makes it possible to print in the MESSAGE file the list of the logical units opened with the command DEFI_FICHIER together with the associated parameters. If INFO = 1, there is no printout. 5 Declaration in the access interface to the code of the logical unit used in DEFI_FICHIER Generally the user will call DEFI_FICHIER with a view to carrying out post-processings when the need is felt to create physically several result files according to the load cases, the quantities, the steps or time instants of the evolution of the analysis. The user must declare the physical names of the files and the associated logical units. This declaration is made, in the astk interface, before the launching of the execution of the work. The files must be added to the study profile by selecting the type libr and associating with them the chosen logical-unit number. The type repe is used in the astk interface to transmit or receive the whole content of a file directory; it is up to the user to call DEFI_FICHIER in the command file in order to carry out the association with the logical-unit number. By convention the data files are transmitted in the local directory named REPE_IN, and the result files are transmitted in the local directory named REPE_OUT. In the command DEFI_FICHIER, the name passed after FICHIER is of the form: ./REPE_IN/mon_fichier. For a data file, one will for example do: DEFI_FICHIER(FICHIER='./REPE_IN/file.data', ACCES='OLD', UNITE=11) LIRE_FONCTION(UNITE=11, ...) Note INCLUDE cannot be used with a logical unit associated with a particular file name.

u4.13.01 Procedure INCLUDE u4.13.01 Procedure INCLUDE 1 Purpose This inserts a sequence of commands that will be executed almost as they are written. There is no possibility of passing arguments. The results of the commands are exported into the main command set. The other objects are normally usable in the command file but will not be available in a POURSUITE. For example, a Python function or class defined in an INCLUDE may be used in a FORMULE in the command file and evaluated there, but not in a POURSUITE. It is therefore advisable to limit the use of INCLUDE to these simple cases (a set of commands defined in another file). If one wishes to execute more Python instructions, it is preferable to use import (use the type 'nom' to copy a file into the execution directory without renaming it). 2 Syntax INCLUDE( ◆ / UNITE = unit, / DONNEE = text, ◇ ALARME = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ INFO = / 0, / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands Apart from the location of the included file, the behaviour is strictly identical with UNITE or DONNEE. 3.1 Operand UNITE Logical unit of the file to include. This number must correspond to the file to include, defined in the launching interface or in the .export file. This file is copied into the execution directory under the name fort.NN . Note One cannot use INCLUDE with a logical unit associated with a file name by DEFI_FICHIER. If necessary, one may use DONNEE=fichier. 3.2 Operand DONNEE This keyword, intended to be used in the test cases, makes it possible to include a file stored in the tests_data directory, whose distribution is restricted. This makes it possible to distribute a test case except for a small part that must remain confidential. This directory is by default located in the share/aster directory of the installation. The command-line option --rcdir makes it possible to override this location. The included file will therefore be xxx/share/aster/tests_data/fichier .
