One may also supply the absolute path to the path to include. 3.3 Operand ALARME This keyword makes it possible to suppress the message warning about the precautions for use of INCLUDE. 3.4 Operand INFO | 0 | no printout of the content of the included file. | | --- | --- | | 1 | printout of the content of the included file, in the 'MESSAGE' file | | 2 | identical to 1 (this value exists by convention) | 4 Example of use - Main command file: DEBUT() INCLUDE(UNITE=91, INFO=1) mo = AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=ma, AFFE=_F(TOUT="OUI", PHENOMENE="MECANIQUE", MODELISATION="3D")) INCLUDE(UNITE=92, INFO=1) FIN() - Command file attached to unit 91 ma = LIRE_MAILLAGE() - Command file attached to unit 92 lbew = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA="INST", VALE=( 0.0, -0.19949, 0.01000, -0.25487, # etc. ), )

u4.13.04 Operator INFO_EXEC_ASTER u4.13.04 Operator INFO_EXEC_ASTER 1 Purpose Create a table containing information specific to the execution in progress, which can be consulted from the command file. This command, intended to be extended, makes it possible for the moment to recover the time remaining and the first free logical-unit number. Recovering the time thus offers the possibility of stopping or of leaving a Python control structure conditionally. 2 Syntax table = INFO_EXEC_ASTER( ◆ LISTE_INFO = / "TEMPS_RESTANT", / "UNITE_LIBRE", / "ETAT_UNITE", # Si: is_in('LISTE_INFO', 'ETAT_UNITE') ◆ / UNITE = unit, / FICHIER = text, ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand LISTE_INFO ◊ LISTE_INFO = ‘TEMPS_RESTANT’ Makes it possible to recover the time remaining during the execution: it is the difference between the maximum time allocated to the analysis and the value of the time already elapsed. ◊ LISTE_INFO = ‘UNITE_LIBRE’ Returns the first logical-unit number available (in decreasing order from 99) at the moment of the call. This value, recovered in a Python variable, can then be passed as an argument of an Aster command. The logical-unit numbers are managed from the command DEFI_FICHIER U4.12.03 and are stored in a data structure internal to the code that links the files and the unit numbers. ◊ LISTE_INFO = ‘ETAT_UNITE’ Returns, according to the presence of the keyword UNITE or FICHIER, the state of the logical unit: free, reserved, or else the name of the associated file. 3.2 Operands UNITE/FICHIER ◊ UNITE Number of the logical unit whose state one wishes to query ◊ FICHIER Name of the file whose associated logical-unit number one wishes to obtain 3.3 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title assigned to the associated table data structure. For more details see U4.03.01. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = 1 Operand unused for the moment. 4 Example A loop from 1 to 10 is carried out for k in range(1,10): # # on appelle une ou plusieurs commandes (AFFE_CHAR_MECA, STAT_NON_LINE, etc.) … # on récupère le temps restant dans la table TAB TAB=INFO_EXEC_ASTER(LISTE_INFO='TEMPS_RESTANT') # on récupère la valeur du temps dans une variable python valcpu=TAB['TEMPS_RESTANT',1] # cette instruction nécessite # d'être en mode PAR_LOT='NON' # on teste cette variable python, s’il reste moins de 5 s, on sort de la boucle if valcpu< 5.0: break # on détruit le concept de type table, pour pouvoir le récréer à l’itération suivante. DETRUIRE(CONCEPT=(_F(NOM=TAB),))

u4.14.01 Operator DETRUIRE u4.14.01 Operator DETRUIRE 1 Purpose Destroy user concepts. After destruction, the concept can therefore naturally no longer be used in the following commands. The destruction of an object is not as natural as it may appear. It is important to understand fully its behaviour, described in this documentation. The destruction of unused objects makes it possible to reduce the size of the files associated with the 'GLOBALE' database. The repacking mechanism is handled by the memory manager during the work. However, another repacking mechanism can be triggered by the user by means of the keyword RETASSAGE= 'OUI' within the procedure FIN U4.11.02. 2 Syntax DETRUIRE( ◆ NOM = datastructure, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword NOM ♦ NOM = lco List of the objects to destroy. All the direct references to the objects supplied are removed in the context where DETRUIRE is invoked. See below for the detailed behaviour. 3.2 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = info In the case where INFO=2, the list of the objects destroyed is printed in the MESSAGE file. 4 How does destruction work? 4.1 Example One creates a list of reals named listr listr = DEFI_LIST_REEL( … ) One destroys the concept named listr DETRUIRE(NOM=listr) Note that reusing the same Python variable listr has the same effect as DETRUIRE. 4.2 In detail The objects created by code_aster (a mesh, a result) are Python objects. DETRUIRE removes the references to the object in the command set. Python actually deletes this object when there is no longer any reference to this object. Take the example: > mesh = LIRE_MAILLAGE() > alias = mesh > lst = [mesh] One has created a mesh object; mesh is a variable that references (or "that gives access to", or again "that points to") this object. alias is a variable that references the same object. lst is a list, created with the operator [ ], which contains a single entry, and this entry also references the same mesh object. If one does: > DETRUIRE(NOM=mesh) All the direct references to the mesh object are removed from the command set. Thus, the variables mesh and alias are removed. Indeed, during the execution, one sees: > Deletion of the reference: ‘mesh’ > Deletion of the reference: ‘alias’ On the other hand, the reference via the list is not seen (one would have to walk through all types of object!) and therefore, in accordance with the way Python works, the mesh object is not actually destroyed, since there is still a reference to this object. If one deletes the list: > del lst or the entry of the list: > del lst[0] Then there is no longer any reference to the object, which is then actually destroyed. One can see: > Deleting 00000004 mesh Note that: > DETRUIRE(NOM=lst[0]) would have had exactly the same behaviour (deletion of mesh and alias but not of lst[0]), because one passes the object to DETRUIRE and not the list lst or the index 0. One would also have the same behaviour with a dictionary containing a mesh object or any object referencing the mesh. Indeed, only the container (the list object, dictionary or other) knows how to delete one of its entries. 4.3 Dependency between objects The data structures (field at the nodes–numbering, field by element–model, and so on) rely on one another. Destroying a data structure that is used by another therefore has no immediate effect. On the other hand, when all the references to a data structure are removed, it is then actually removed.

u4.14.02 Operator COPIER u4.14.02 Operator COPIER 1 Purpose Duplicate a user concept under another name. This command is rarely useful and it has the disadvantage of doubling the "disk" space of the concept in the user's global database. The concept produced can be destroyed (command DETRUIRE) in order to recover the disk space. Only certain types of concept are accepted. 2 Syntax / cabl_precont / evol_elas / evol_noli / evol_ther / fonction / listis / listr8 / maillage / modele / nappe / table = COPIER( ◇ reuse = , ◆ CONCEPT = cabl_precont / evol_elas / evol_noli / evol_ther / fonction / listis / listr8 / maillage / modele / nappe / table, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword CONCEPT ♦ CONCEPT = co1 Name of the concept that one wishes to duplicate. The result of the command is of the same type as the duplicated concept. 3.2 Types of CONCEPT allowed On ne peut dupliquer tous les types de concepts. Seuls sont traités actuellement : | cabl_precont, | | | --- | --- | | listr8_sdaster, | | | listis_sdaster, | | | fonction_sdaster, | | | nappe_sdaster, | | | table_sdaster, | | | maillage_sdaster, | | | modele_sdaster, | | | evol_elas, | | | evol_noli, | | | evol_ther, | | | | | | | | | | | | If the type of the concept that you wish to duplicate does not appear in this list | an enhancement request must be submitted. | 3.3 Notes The need to duplicate a concept is rare because it is in principle useless to have the same object under two different names. The concept produced (co2) corresponds to a "deep" copy of the initial concept (co1), that is to say that ALL the JEVEUX objects of co1 have been duplicated. The "volume" of co2 in the global database is identical to that of co1. Use of the command therefore always leads to a loss of disk space. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = info This keyword has no influence. 4 Example Lr1 = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( … ) Lr2 = COPIER (CONCEPT = Lr1)

u4.15.01 Procedure MAJ_CATA u4.15.01 Procedure MAJ_CATA 1 Purpose Compilation of the element catalogue (associated AGLA scripts: ccat92-py and ccat‑ele.csh). This procedure is of no interest to the user. If necessary, one may refer to the AGLA User's manual D1.02.01. 2 Syntax MAJ_CATA( ◆ / ELEMENT = _F( ), / TYPE_ELEM = _F( ), ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword ELEMENT This operand causes compilation of the element catalogue. Note: Management of logical units by name in JEVEUX has led to the removal of the simple keywords under this factor keyword. The calling syntax is therefore of the form: MAJ_CATA ( ELEMENT = _F() , ) 3.2 Keyword TYPE_ELEM This operand causes the printout of all the (element_type, option) pairs available in the version called; this information can then be used for the analysis of code coverage. 3.2.1 Keyword UNITE ◊ UNITE = num Number of the logical unit associated with a file to which the printouts will be directed. One should refer to the command DEFI_FICHIER U4.12.03. By default, the printouts are made in the file associated with logical unit 8.

u4.15.12 Operator DEBUG u4.15.12 Operator DEBUG 1 Purpose Makes it possible to activate or deactivate the debugging functionalities between the various commands. Some keywords are accessible in the commands DEBUT and POURSUITE. This is a functionality intended for developers. 2 Syntax DEBUG( ◇ SDVERI = / "OUI", / "NON", ◇ JXVERI = / "OUI", / "NON", ◇ JEVEUX = / "OUI", / "NON", ◇ IMPR_MACRO = / "OUI", / "NON", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand SDVERI Warning: this functionality can cause a non-negligible extra cost during the execution. This keyword triggers the checking of the data structures produced by the operators. It is used within the code development procedures in the non-regression tests. 3.2 Operand JXVERI Makes it possible to check the integrity of the memory segments between two consecutive command executions. This functionality concerns only the so-called static memory-management mode, when a memory area allocated at the start of the execution is managed by JEVEUX by chaining the various objects allocated during the execution. In the so-called dynamic memory-management mode the various objects are allocated directly by the system and no chaining exists. 3.3 Operand JEVEUX Makes it possible to activate the debug operating mode of the JEVEUX memory manager: non-deferred unloading to disk and assignment of the value segments to an undefined value D6.02.01. 3.4 Keyword IMPR_MACRO Allows or disallows the displays produced by the macros in the message file. Reading the message files can be tedious when they contain all of the echoes of the sub-commands generated by the macro itself. By default, only the echo of the commands explicitly called by the user in the command set will appear.

u4.21.01 Operator LIRE_MAILLAGE u4.21.01 Operator LIRE_MAILLAGE 1 Purpose Create a mesh by reading from a file. The supported file formats are: ASTER, MED, GIBI, GMSH and IDEAS. Produces a data structure of type maillage. Important note: One can check the quality of the mesh read by using (following LIRE_MAILLAGE, the command MACR_INFO_MAIL U7.03.02. 2 Syntax maillage = LIRE_MAILLAGE( ◇ FORMAT = / "ASTER", / "GIBI", / "GMSH", / "IDEAS", / "MED" (par défaut), ⟐ VERI_MAIL = _F( ◇ VERIF = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ APLAT = float (défaut: 0.001), ), # Si: ( not equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ) ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 20), # Si: ( equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ) ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 20), ◇ NOM_MED = text, ◇ INFO_MED = / 0 (par défaut), / 1, ◇ PARTITIONNEUR = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "PTSCOTCH", # Si: ( equal_to("FORMAT", 'IDEAS') ) ◇ CREA_GROUP_COUL = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ INFO = / 0, / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = i Logical-unit number of the mesh file. Unit 20 by default. 3.2 Operand FORMAT ◊ FORMAT = / 'MED' [DEFAUT] / 'ASTER' / 'GMSH' This keyword is used to specify the format of the file to be read. Today three formats are supported: 'MED', 'ASTER' and 'GMSH'. The format 'ASTER' is described in U3.01.00. The format 'MED', which means "Modelling and Exchange of Data", is a neutral data format developed by EDF R&D and the CEA for the exchange of data between analysis codes. The data that one can exchange according to this format are the meshes and the result fields: fields at the nodes, fields by element. MED files are binary and portable files (relying on the HDF library, Hierarchical Data Format). Reading a MED file with LIRE_MAILLAGE makes it possible to recover a mesh produced by any other code capable of creating a MED file. It is the format recommended in code_aster and the default one. Whatever the format, the data read are: | the list of nodes | number, name, coordinates, | | --- | --- | | the list of mesh cells | number, name, type, name of the nodes, | | the list of node groups | number, name, number of nodes, names of the nodes, | | the list of mesh-cell groups | number, name, number of mesh cells, names of the mesh cells. | Note: In a MED file, there is a partition of the nodes and of the mesh cells according to the groups. A partition corresponds to a MED family. In a MED file, the groups are distributed within the families: one therefore finds families of nodes and families of mesh cells. When a MED file is read, the lists of the node groups and of the mesh-cell groups are built on the fly by decomposition of the families. Concerning GMSH, files in ASCII formats 1.0 and 2.0 are read. In GMSH, the groups are always numbered. They are also sometimes named in version 2.0. For GMSH format version 1, the node and mesh-cell groups are read in the following way: - all the element groups numbered 1, 2, ... of GMSH are transformed into mesh-cell groups (GROUP_MA) bearing the name GM1, GM2, - the groups are mutually exclusive: a mesh cell cannot belong to several groups. For GMSH format version 2, the node and mesh-cell groups are read in the following way: - only the groups named in GMSH (section PhysicalNames of the msh format) are imported; - the groups may overlap: a mesh cell may belong to several groups; - the GMSH type of the mesh cell must be consistent with the GMSH dimension of the group in order to be able to belong to this group (for example a 2-node segment for a 1D group) 3.3 Operand VERI_MAIL The keyword VERI_MAIL triggers 4 checks on the mesh: - absence of orphan nodes, - absence of "duplicate" mesh cells, - absence of quadratic mesh cells having the same vertex nodes but not the same mid-side nodes, - absence of mesh cells that are too flat. If these checks are not satisfied, the code issues an alarm. By default (that is to say in the absence of the keyword VERI_MAIL), the checks are carried out. If the user wishes to avoid these checks, the following will be written: VERI_MAIL = _F (VERIF = 'NON',) A node is declared orphan if it does not form part of the connectivity of any mesh cell. A mesh cell is declared "duplicate" if 2 mesh cells (or more) have connectivities formed by the same list of nodes. The keyword APLAT= ap makes it possible to issue alarms when the mesh contains mesh cells that are too flat. The flatness of a mesh cell is defined as the ratio Amin/Amax where Amin and Amax are the lengths of the shortest and the longest edges of the mesh cell. The name of the mesh cells whose flatness is lower than ap will be printed on the 'MESSAGE' file. Other quality criteria for the mesh are available via the command MACR_INFO_MAIL U7.03.02. In the case of the issue of an error or alarm message, it is possible to try to create a repaired mesh with the following function fix_mesh = mesh.fix() 3.4 Operands for the format 'MED' ◊ NOM_MED = mamed A MED file may contain several meshes. Each mesh is identified by its name. To read one mesh in particular, its name must be supplied as the argument of this keyword NOM_MED. In the absence of the keyword, the first mesh found in the file will be read. When the file contains only one mesh, there is therefore nothing to specify. Notes: - In a mesh, a mesh-cell group may be composed of elements of different dimensions (edges, faces or volumes). - This kind of group is displayed in Salome (Mesh module) as several groups bearing the same name under different categories, but in fact it is a single group in code_aster. ◊ INFO_MED= / 1, [DEFAUT] / 2, / 3 Prints information specific to the progress of the re-reading of the MED mesh file (number of nodes and of mesh cells re-read, information on the MED families, …): - INFO_MED = 1 : no printout, - INFO_MED = 2 : only printouts relating to the family / group correspondence, - INFO_MED = 3: all the information is printed. ◊ PARTITIONNEUR= / ‘SANS’, : [DEFAUT] / ‘PTSCOTCH’ By default (SANS), the mesh is not partitioned (sequential and former parallelism). With PTSCOTCH, this makes it possible to partition a mesh contained in a file in order to distribute it among the various sub-domains during a parallel analysis. The mesh is cut into as many sub-domains as there are MPI processes. In sequential mode, the keyword is ignored. Warning: for the moment, certain POI1 mesh cells are not copied. 3.5 Operands for the format 'IDEAS' ◊ CREA_GROUP_COUL The user may request the creation of mesh-cell groups and of node groups gathering all the mesh cells and nodes of the same colour by indicating CREA_GROUP_COUL = 'OUI'. These groups are named COUL_n where n is the colour number in IDEAS. By default this is not done, so as not to increase unnecessarily the number of mesh-cell groups and of node groups. Notes: - Only Cartesian coordinate systems are treated. - Only a single Cartesian coordinate system is handled. - During the conversion of the IDEAS universal file, a check is made as to whether the user has defined several coordinate systems. If this is the case, an alarm message warns the user, asking that it be checked that all the coordinate systems are identical. 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 , [DEFAUT] / 2 Print level. If: INFO= 1 - title of the mesh, - number of nodes, - number of mesh cells of each type, - number of node groups and, for each of them, its name and the number of nodes of the group - number of mesh-cell groups and, for each of them, its name and the number of mesh cells of the group. If: INFO= 2 one prints, in addition to the information of INFO= 1: | list of the nodes | number, name, coordinates, | | --- | --- | | list of the mesh cells | number, name, type, name of the nodes, | | list of the node groups | number, name, number of nodes, names of the nodes, | | list of the mesh-cell groups | number, name, number of mesh cells, names of the mesh cells. |

u4.22.01 Operator DEFI_GROUP u4.22.01 Operator DEFI_GROUP 1 Purpose Define, in an existing mesh, new node groups or mesh-cell groups. This can make it easier to define new geometric loci for data input or for post-processings. To create new groups, one uses topological, logical or geometric criteria. In what follows one will use the vocabulary "mesh". This command makes it possible to define new mesh-cell groups (or node groups) in an existing mesh: one enriches the mesh ma. No new mesh cell and no new node are created. They must already be present in the mesh in order to be able to be used. The definition of a new group can be done in several ways: - by a Boolean operation on existing groups: intersection (INTERSEC), union (UNION) or difference (DIFFE), - according to a geometric criterion: mesh cells of which a node belongs to a given sphere, … - for the node groups, by referring to existing mesh-cell groups. The node group thus defined contains all the nodes of the mesh cells of the original mesh-cell group (keywords TOUT_GROUP_MA and GROUP_MA). The operator treats first the keyword CREA_GROUP_MA so that one can use the mesh-cell groups thus defined in the keyword CREA_GROUP_NO. At each occurrence of a keyword CREA_GROUP_MA(_NO) one defines a new named group (keyword NOM). This new group can then be reused in the following occurrences to define new groups by intersection, union, ... The keywords DETR_GROUP_MA and DETR_GROUP_NO make it possible to "destroy" mesh-cell groups or node groups. The mesh cells and the nodes of these groups are not removed; it is only the definitions of the groups that are erased. These keywords are useful for example in Python loops when one wishes to create a group at each iteration of the loop: one begins by destroying this group then one recreates it under the same name. This avoids changing the group name at each iteration. One may note that most of the functionalities of DEFI_GROUP can be done directly in the SMESH module of SALOME, namely: - Boolean operation on existing groups, - creation of a group by mesh-cell type (SMESH filter Type), - according to a geometric criterion (SMESH filter LyingOn), - according to a normal-angle criterion for surface mesh cells (SMESH filter Coplanar), - for the mesh-cell groups resting on node groups (SMESH function 'Group based on nodes of other groups'), - for the node groups, by referring to existing mesh-cell groups (SMESH function 'Group based on nodes of other groups'), - deletion of groups. 3.2 Operands MAILLAGE and GRILLE | MAILLAGE= ma ma is the name of the mesh that one wishes to "enrich". gr is the name of the auxiliary grid that one wishes to "enrich". 3.3 Keywords DETR_GROUP_MA and DETR_GROUP_NO These two factor keywords make it possible to remove the definition of mesh-cell groups or of node groups. These keywords are sometimes necessary because the code stops with a fatal error if one attempts to create a group whose name is already used. The group must be destroyed before its name can be reused. The behaviour of the two keywords is similar and we shall speak here only of DETR_GROUP_MA. DETR_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM=(gm1,gm2, ...)), The factor keyword DETR_GROUP_MA is in principle repeatable but this is never necessary because the keyword NOM makes it possible to indicate a list of names of groups to destroy (gm1, gm2, …). It is important to know that all the occurrences of the keyword DETR_GROUP_MA are treated before those of the keyword CREA_GROUP_NO, because the aim of this keyword is to be able to reuse the destroyed name. One must also know that the destruction of a non-existent group does not lead to any alarm message. These choices make it possible for example to do, in a Python loop: for i in range(n) : DEFI_GROUPE(reuse=MA, MAILLAGE=MA, DETR_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM('GM1',), CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='GM1', ... During the first iteration, the group 'GM1' does not exist; one requests its destruction but no alarm message is issued. Note: | As the destructions take place at the start of the command, it is impossible to modify a group by making a single call to DEFI_GROUP . For example, one cannot make a group 'grow' (in a loop) by adding a small group ( b1 ) to it: for i in range(n): b1=new group ... DEFI_GROUP(reuse=MA,MAILLAGE=MA, CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='tout', UNION=('tout','b1'),),) To do this, one must call DEFI_GROUP twice: for i in range(n): b1=new group ... DEFI_GROUP(reuse=MA,MAILLAGE=MA, DETR_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='tout2'), CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='tout2', UNION=('tout','b1'),),) DEFI_GROUP(reuse=MA,MAILLAGE=MA, DETR_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='tout'), CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='tout', UNION=('tout2','b1'),),) | | --- | 3.4 Keyword CREA_GROUP_MA | CREA_GROUP_MA One occurrence of this factor keyword makes it possible to define a new mesh-cell group. 3.4.1 Operand NOM NOM= gma One gives here the name (with "quotes") of the new mesh-cell group. 3.4.2 Operand TYPE_MAILLE TYPE_MAILLE= /'TOUT'/'3D'/'2D'/'1D' (DEFAUT='TOUT') /'SEG2'/'TRIA3'/'QUAD4'/.../'PYRAM13' This keyword makes it possible to filter the mesh cells that one will put into the new mesh-cell group. By default, there is no filter, but if the user writes for example: TYPE_MAILLE='2D', the group created will contain only surface mesh cells. The user may also filter the group to be created for a particular mesh-cell type (TRIA3, HEXA27, …). All the mesh-cell types (POI1, SEG2, SEG3, SEG4, …, PYRAM13) are allowed. Examples: CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='VOLUM', 'TOUT='OUI', TYPE_MAILLE='3D') makes it possible to create the group of all the volume mesh cells (HEXA, PENTA, ...) of the mesh. CREA_GROUP_MA=_F(NOM='VOLH27', 'GROUP_MA='GMA1', TYPE_MAILLE='HEXA27') makes it possible to create the group of all the mesh cells of type 'HEXA27' contained in the GROUP_MA. GMA1. 3.4.3 Operand TOUT TOUT= 'OUI' This keyword makes it possible to define a group containing all the mesh cells of the mesh. 3.4.4 Operand INTERSEC INTERSEC= (gma1, gma2, gma3,...), The new mesh-cell group will be obtained by taking all the mesh cells of gma1 that also belong to gma2, gma3,.... The order of the mesh cells remains that of gma1. 3.4.5 Operand UNION UNION= (gma1, gma2, gma3,...) The new mesh-cell group will be obtained by taking all the mesh cells of gma1, then by adding the mesh cells of gma2 that do not belong to gma1, then those of gma3 that belong neither to gma1 nor to gma2, and so on. 3.4.6 Operand DIFFE DIFFE = (gma1, gma2, gma3,...) The new mesh-cell group will be obtained by taking all the mesh cells of gma1 that do not belong to the other groups of the list. The order of the mesh cells remains that of gma1. 3.4.7 Sub-group of an existing group: keywords GROUP_MA / POSITION / NUME_INIT / NUME_FIN One can create a new mesh-cell group by selecting certain mesh cells of an existing group. 1st possibility: One creates a group of a single mesh cell by specifying, with the keyword POSITION, the mesh cell sought. Example: CREA_GROUP_MA= _F ( GROUP_MA= G1 , POSITION= 'INIT' , NOM= G1I ) The group G1I contains the 1st mesh cell of the group G1. 2nd possibility: One creates a group containing the mesh cells lying between the ranks nuini and nufin (inclusive) in an existing group. Example: CREA_GROUP_MA=_F (GROUP_MA= G1, NUME_INIT= 3 , NUME_FIN = 7, NOM = G1P) The group G1P contains mesh cells 3, 4, 5, ..., 7 of G1. Warning: These keywords use the notion of the order of the mesh cells in a mesh-cell group. This order is often unknown to the user. It may depend on the pre-processor. It is the order of the mesh cells at the time of the definition of the GROUP_MA in the Aster mesh file. 3.4.8 Operand OPTION = 'FACE_NORMALE' OPTION = 'FACE_NORMALE' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_MA made up of surface mesh cells whose normal is parallel to the direction of the vector defined by its components if one uses the keyword VECT_NORMALE, or to that of the first vector of the new basis defined by the change of frame due to the nautical angles. In 3D, one assumes that the surface mesh cells are plane facets. They are of type TRIA3, TRIA6, QUAD4, QUAD8 or QUAD9. If one calls {X}_{1} , {X}_{2} , and {X}_{3} the position vectors of the first three vertex nodes of the element, the normal is determined by the vector product: ({X}_{2}-{X}_{1})\mathrm{\wedge }({X}_{3}-{X}_{1}) . In 2D, one assumes that the surface mesh cells are straight segments. They are of type SEG2 or SEG3. If one calls {X}_{1} and {X}_{2} the position vectors of the two end nodes of the element, the normal is defined by ({X}_{2}-{X}_{1})\mathrm{\wedge }z where z is the unit vector perpendicular to the plane and where 0. has been assigned as the third component of ({X}_{2}-{X}_{1}) . Note: A "facet" mesh cell will be retained if its normal is collinear with the normal vector defined by VECT_NORMALE. This condition must be satisfied to within a certain precision (keyword ANGL_PREC). When one chooses an ANGL_PREC (for example 30. degrees), one in fact defines the group of the mesh cells whose normal belongs to the cone of axis VECT_NORMALE and of apex angle ANGL_PREC. This can be used (for example) to group the mesh cells of a half spherical envelope (ANGL_PREC= 90.). 3.4.8.1 Operand ANGL_NAUT ANGL_NAUT = a en 2D (a,b) en 3D The nautical angles (a, b), defined in degrees, are the angles making it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the coordinates of the nodes to a frame whose first vector designates the direction along which the normal of the surface mesh cells that one wishes to recover is oriented. For the definition of the nautical angles, see the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, operand ORIENTATION. 3.4.8.2 Operand VECT_NORMALE VECT_NORMALE = (x, y) en 2D (x, y, z) en 3D The coordinates x, y, z are those giving the direction along which the normal of the surface mesh cells that one wishes to recover is oriented. 3.4.8.3 Operand ANGL_PREC ANGL_PREC = a It is the tolerance, in degrees, that one accepts on the angle formed by the vector supplied by the user and the vector normal to the surface element in order to assert that these two vectors have the same direction. The default value of a is 0.5 degree. 3.4.8.4 Operand VERI_SIGNE VERI_SIGNE = 'NON' , 'OUI' , [DEFAUT] If one assigns the value 'NON' to VERI_SIGNE, the GROUP_MA will be made up of the surface mesh cells whose normal is parallel to the vector given by the user. If one assigns the value 'OUI', the GROUP_MA will be made up of the surface mesh cells whose normal is parallel and has the same orientation as the vector given by the user. The default value is 'OUI'. 3.4.9 Operand OPTION = 'SPHERE' OPTION = 'SPHERE' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_MA made up of the mesh cells of which at least one node belongs to a sphere (a circle in 2D) defined by its centre and its radius. 3.4.9.1 Operand POINT POINT = (x, y) en 2D (x, y, z) en 3D x y z are the coordinates of the centre of the sphere. 3.4.9.2 Operand GROUP_NO_CENTRE GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno This keyword makes it possible to indicate which is the node coinciding with the centre of the sphere. 3.4.9.3 Operand RAYON RAYON = r r is the radius of the sphere (of the circle in 2D). 3.4.10 Operand OPTION = 'CYLINDRE' OPTION = 'CYLINDRE' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_MA made up of the mesh cells of which at least one node belongs to a cylinder defined by its axis and its radius. The axis is defined by a vector and a point belonging to this axis. This option has meaning only in 3D. 3.4.10.1 Operand POINT POINT = (x, y, z) x y z are the coordinates of a point situated on the axis of the cylinder. 3.4.10.2 Operand GROUP_NO_CENTRE GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno This keyword makes it possible to indicate a node situated on the axis of the cylinder. 3.4.10.3 Operand RAYON RAYON = r r is the radius of the cylinder. 3.4.10.4 Operand ANGL_NAUT ANGL_NAUT = (a, b) The nautical angles a, b, defined in degrees, are the angles making it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the coordinates of the nodes to a frame whose first vector designates the direction of the axis of the cylinder. For the definition of the nautical angles see the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, operand ORIENTATION. 3.4.10.5 Operand VECT_NORMALE VECT_NORMALE = (x, y, z) x y z are the coordinates of a vector orienting the axis of the cylinder. 3.4.11 Operand OPTION = 'BANDE' OPTION = 'BANDE' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_MA made up of the mesh cells of which at least one node belongs to a "band" defined by a "mid" plane (a straight line in 2D) and the half-width on either side of this plane. The plane is defined by a vector normal to this plane and a point belonging to it. 3.4.11.1 Operand POINT POINT = (x, y) en 2D (x, y, z) en 3D x y z are the coordinates of a point belonging to the "mid" plane of the band. 3.4.11.2 Operand GROUP_NO_CENTRE GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno This keyword makes it possible to define one belonging to the "mid" plane of the band. 3.4.11.3 Operand ANGL_NAUT ANGL_NAUT = a en 2D (a,b) en 3D The nautical angles a, b, defined in degrees, are the angles making it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the coordinates of the nodes to a frame whose first vector is orthogonal to the "mid" plane of the band. For the definition of the nautical angles, see the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, operand ORIENTATION. 3.4.11.4 Operand VECT_NORMALE VECT_NORMALE = (x, y) en 2D (x, y, z) en 3D x y and z are the components of a vector perpendicular to the "mid" plane of the band. 3.4.11.5 Operand DIST DIST = d d is the half-width of the band. 3.4.12 Operand OPTION = 'APPUI' This option makes it possible to recover the group of the mesh cells of which certain nodes belong to the set of the nodes specified by the keyword GROUP_NO. GROUP_NO = l_gno This keyword makes it possible to define the list of the nodes that will serve as support for the mesh cells. Let us call this list lno1. TYPE_APPUI = / 'TOUT' : la maille sera retenue si tous ses nœuds appartiennent à lno1 / 'SOMMET' : la maille sera retenue si tous ses nœuds «sommet» appartiennent à lno1 / 'AU_MOINS_UN' : la maille sera retenue au moins un de ses nœuds appartient à lno1 / 'MAJORITE' : la maille sera retenue si plus de la moitié deses nœuds appartiennent à lno1 3.4.13 Operand OPTION = 'FISS_XFEM' This option makes it possible to recover the group of the mesh cells of X-FEM type specified by the keywords TYPE_GROUP. FISSURE = (fiss1, fiss2, ...) TYPE_GROUP = / 'HEAVISIDE' : la maille sera retenue si elle est de type Heaviside / 'CRACKTIP' : la maille sera retenue si elle est de type Crack-tip / 'MIXTE' : la maille sera retenue si elle est de type Mixte (Heaviside et Crack-tip) / 'XFEM':la maille sera retenue si elle est de type Heaviside, Crack-tip ou Mixte / 'FISSUREE' : la maille sera retenue si tous ses nœuds sont enrichis For a precise definition of the notions of Heaviside mesh cell and Crack-tip mesh cell, see R7.02.12, §3.2.5. 3.5 Keyword CREA_GROUP_NO | CREA_GROUP_NO One occurrence of this factor keyword makes it possible to define a new node group (for the keywords GROUP_MA and TOUT_GROUP_MA, one creates several node groups "at one go"). 3.5.1 Operand NOM NOM= gno One gives here the name (with "quotes") of the new node group. 3.5.2 Operand INTERSEC INTERSEC= (gno1, gno2, gno3,...) The new node group will be obtained by taking all the nodes of gno1 that also belong to gno2, gno3,.... The order of the nodes remains that of gno1. 3.5.3 Operand UNION UNION= (gno1, gno2, gno3,...) The new node group will be obtained by taking all the nodes of gno1, then by adding the nodes of gno2 that do not belong to gno1, then those of gno3 that belong neither to gno1 nor to gno2, and so on. 3.5.4 Operand DIFFE DIFFE= (gno1, gno2, gno3,...) The new node group will be obtained by taking all the nodes of gno1 that do not belong to the other groups of the list. The order of the nodes remains that of gno1. 3.5.5 Sub-group of an existing group: keywords GROUP_NO / POSITION / NUME_INIT / NUME_FIN One can create a new node group by selecting certain nodes of an existing group. 1st possibility: One creates a group of a single node by specifying, with the keyword POSITION, the node sought. Example: CREA_GROUP_NO= _F ( GROUP_NO= G1 , POSITION= 'INIT' , NOM= G1I ) The group G1I contains the 1st node of the group G1. 2nd possibility: One creates a group containing the nodes lying between the ranks nuini and nufin (inclusive) in an existing group. Example: CREA_GROUP_NO=_F(GROUP_NO= G1, NUME_INIT= 3 NUME_FIN = 7 , NOM = G1P) The group G1P contains nodes 3, 4, 5, ..., 7 of G1. Warning: These keywords use the notion of the order of the nodes in a node group. This order is often unknown to the user. It may depend on the pre-processor. It is the order of the nodes at the time of the definition of the GROUP_NO in the Aster mesh file. 3.5.6 Operand OPTION = 'ENV_SPHERE' OPTION = 'ENV_SPHERE' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_NO made up of the nodes situated on the envelope of a sphere, to within a given precision. 3.5.6.1 Operand POINT POINT = (x, y) , en 2D (x, y, z), en 3D x y z are the coordinates of the centre of the sphere. 3.5.6.2 Operand GROUP_NO_CENTRE GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno This keyword makes it possible to define the node coinciding with the centre of the sphere. 3.5.6.3 Operand RAYON RAYON = r r is the radius of the sphere. 3.5.6.4 Operand PRECISION PRECISION = eps eps is the tolerance with which one defines the belonging of a node to the envelope of the sphere. This tolerance is to be taken in the following sense: if d is the distance from a node to the centre of the sphere, one says that this node belongs to the group if: ∣d-r∣\le \text{eps} 3.5.7 Operand OPTION = 'ENV_CYLINDRE' OPTION = 'ENV_CYLINDRE' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_NO made up of nodes situated on the envelope of a cylinder, to within a given precision. This option has meaning only in 3D. 3.5.7.1 Operand POINT POINT = (x, y, z) x y z are the coordinates of a point belonging to the axis of the cylinder. 3.5.7.2 Operand GROUP_NO_CENTRE GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno This keyword makes it possible to define a node belonging to the axis of the cylinder. 3.5.7.3 Operand RAYON RAYON = r r is the radius of the cylinder. 3.5.7.4 Operand ANGL_NAUT ANGL_NAUT = (ab) The nautical angles a, b, defined in degrees, are the angles making it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the coordinates of the nodes to a frame whose first vector designates the direction of the axis of the cylinder. For the definition of the nautical angles, see the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, operand ORIENTATION. 3.5.7.5 Operand VECT_NORMALE VECT_NORMALE = (x, y, z) x y z are the coordinates of a vector orienting the axis of the cylinder. 3.5.7.6 Operand PRECISION PRECISION = eps eps is the tolerance with which one defines the belonging of a node to the envelope of the cylinder. This tolerance is to be taken in the following sense: if d denotes the distance from the current point to the axis of the cylinder, one says that the current point belongs to the envelope of the cylinder if: ∣d-r∣\le \text{eps} 3.5.8 Operand OPTION = 'PLAN' This option makes it possible to define a GROUP_NO made up of nodes situated on a straight line (in 2D) or in a plane (in 3D), to within a given precision. 3.5.8.1 Operand POINT POINT = (x, y) , en 2D (x, y, z), en 3D x y z are the coordinates of a point belonging to the plane (to the straight line). 3.5.8.2 Operand GROUP_NO_CENTRE GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno This keyword makes it possible to define a node belonging to the plane (to the straight line). 3.5.8.3 Operand ANGL_NAUT ANGL_NAUT = a , en 2D (a, b), en 3D The nautical angles a, b, defined in degrees, are the angles making it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the coordinates of the nodes to a frame whose first vector is orthogonal to the 'mid' plane of the band. For the definition of the nautical angles, see the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, operand ORIENTATION. 3.5.8.4 Operand VECT_NORMALE VECT_NORMALE = (x, y) , en 2D (x, y, z), en 3D x y and z are the components of a vector perpendicular to the plane (to the straight line). 3.5.8.5 Operand PRECISION PRECISION = eps eps is the tolerance with which one defines the belonging of a node to the plane (or to the straight line). This tolerance is to be taken in the following sense: if d denotes the distance from the node to the plane (or to the straight line), one says that this node belongs to this plane (or to this straight line) if: ∣d∣\le \text{eps} 3.5.9 Operand OPTION = 'SEGM_DROI_ORDO' This option is used to order a set of nodes situated approximately on a straight-line segment AB. GROUP_NO = gno2, One defines the set of the nodes that one wishes to order. GROUP_NO_ORIG = gnoA , GROUP_NO_EXTR = gnoB , One defines the nodes A and B , origin and end of the segment \mathrm{AB} . PRECISION = prec, CRITERE = 'RELATIF' , 'ABSOLU' , These two arguments are safeguards; they are used to check that the nodes that one is seeking to order (lno2 or gno2) do indeed lie on the segment \mathrm{AB} . If the deviation of a node from \mathrm{AB} is greater than prec the code stops with a fatal error. If the criterion chosen is 'RELATIF', the distance of a node from \mathrm{AB} will be divided by the length of \mathrm{AB} . 3.5.10 Operand OPTION = 'NOEUD_ORDO' This option is used to create an ordered group_no containing the nodes of a set of mesh cells formed of segments (SEG2, SEG3 or SEG4). The set of these mesh cells must form a continuous line. The line may be "open" (with 2 ends) or "closed" (it is then a simple loop). GROUP_MA= gmaAB Name of the group_ma whose nodes one wishes to order. The mesh cells of gmaAB must form an open line. GROUP_NO_ORIG = gnoA , GROUP_NO_EXTR = gnoB , The keywords make it possible to define the nodes A and B , origin and end of the line \mathrm{AB} . The node A will be numbered first, then one uses the topology of the mesh cells of gmaAB to number the nodes step by step. If the node A is not supplied by the user, the program will choose as "origin" node the first node of gmaAB that belongs to only a single segment mesh cell. The origin is therefore arbitrary: the program could just as well have fallen upon the other end. One checks that the last numbered node is indeed B (if the latter is given). 3.5.10.1 Case of closed lines If the line is a loop, one cannot determine its ends automatically. To define the origin of the curvilinear abscissae, the user may fill in the origin and end nodes. These 2 nodes must be identical. But one may also write: ORIGINE='SANS'. The "origin" node will then be taken at random on the closed line. To orient a closed line, one cannot use the knowledge of the origin and end nodes. If so wished, the user may then fill in the keyword VECT_ORIE (2 or 3 coordinates according to the dimension of the space). One will choose, as the direction of travel of the loop, the mesh cell of gmaAB that touches the origin node and that minimises the angle with the vector supplied by VECT_ORIE. 3.5.11 Operand OPTION = 'TUNNEL' This option is used to create the group_no formed of the nodes situated inside a "tunnel" whose axis and radius one supplies. The nodes retained will be those whose distance to the axis is less than the radius. The axis of the "tunnel" is defined by the linear mesh cells supplied via the keyword GROUP_MA_AXE. The axis of the tunnel must have an "origin" defined by the keyword GROUP_NO_ORIG. The keyword RAYON is used to define the "radius" of the tunnel. One can limit the tunnel by giving its length with the keyword LONGUEUR. This length is measured from the origin of the tunnel. The nodes that are candidates to form part of the tunnel are those carried by the mesh cells defined by the keywords: TOUT='OUI' and GROUP_MA. 3.5.12 Operand OPTION = 'INCLUSION' OPTION = 'INCLUSION' , GROUP_MA = lgma , [l_group_ma] CAS_FIGURE = / '2D' / '3D' / '2.5D' DISTANCE_MAX = distma GROUP_MA_INCL = lgma_inc , [l_group_ma] MAILLAGE_INCL = ma_inc , [maillage] This option makes it possible to create the group of the nodes of the mesh cells of lgma that are geometrically inside the mesh cells of lgma_inc. If MAILLAGE_INCL is not supplied, lgma_inc is a list of GROUP_MA of the mesh that one is enriching (ma). Otherwise they are GROUP_MA of ma_inc. The keyword CAS_FIGURE is mandatory; it is used to determine which are the mesh cells of lgma_inc that must be used to determine the inclusion: '2D': one is interested only in the surface mesh cells (TRIA and QUAD) of a 2D mesh (plane \mathrm{XOY} ). '3D': one is interested only in the volume mesh cells (TETRA, PENTA, …) '2.5D': one is interested only in the surface mesh cells (TRIA and QUAD) of a 3D mesh (shell). The keyword DISTANCE_MAX is optional. It is used to give a small tolerance in order to define whether a node is included in a mesh cell. Indeed, a node situated "just" on an interface between 2 mesh cells risks being considered as "outside" the 2 mesh cells and therefore as not forming part of the inclusion. This is why a default value of distma is taken by the code. One has chosen 1% of the length of the smallest edge of the mesh ma_inc. In the case of a mesh of "shell" type (2.5D), if the surface is not plane, it is virtually impossible for a facet element to be geometrically included in other mesh cells: there is almost always a gap in the direction "normal" to the surface. One will therefore in general, in this case, have to supply a value of distma greater than the default value. 3.5.13 Operand OPTION = 'INTERVALLE_VALE' This option is used to create the group_no formed of the nodes whose value of a component (cmp) of a field at the nodes (cham_no) lies between two values (vmin and vmax). The field and the component that will be used to select the nodes are given by the keywords CHAM_GD and NOM_CMP. The values vmin and vmax are supplied via the keyword VALE. Example: DEFI_GROUP( reuse = MAIL, MAILLAGE = MAIL, CREA_GROUP_NO = _F(NOM='GN700', OPTION='INTERVALLE_VALE', CHAM_GD=TEMPER, NOM_CMP='TEMP', VALE=(700., 800.),),); The GROUP_NO 'GN700' will be formed of all the nodes of the mesh MAIL whose temperature in the field TEMPER lies between 700. and 800. 3.5.14 Operand OPTION = 'FISS_XFEM' This option makes it possible to recover the group of the nodes of XFEM type specified by the keywords TYPE_GROUP. FISSURE = (fiss1, fiss2, ...) TYPE_GROUP = / 'XFEM' : le nœud sera retenu si c'est un nœud enrichi / 'HEAVISIDE' : le nœud sera retenu si c'est un nœud enrichi de type Heaviside / 'CRACKTIP' : le nœud sera retenu si c'est un nœud enrichi de type Cracktip / 'MIXTE' : le nœud sera retenu si c'est un nœud enrichi de type Mixte (Heaviside et Cracktip) :ref: 3.2 / 'ZONE_MAJ' : le nœud sera retenu si il est contenu dans la zone de mise à jour des level sets. Dans le cas où le maillage de la fissure est passé par le mot-clé MAILLAGE(§), la zone de mise à jour coïncide: en l'absence d'une grille auxiliaire associée à la fissure, avec le domaine de calcul autour du fond, en présence d'une grille auxiliaire associée à la fissure, avec le domaine de projection entre grille et maillage, indépendamment du domaine de calcul utilisé sur la grille. 3.2 In the case where a grid is passed by the keyword GRILLE(§), the update zone always coincides with the analysis domain used on the grid. / 'TORE': the node will be retained if it is contained in a torus built around the crack front, of radius given by the keyword RAYON_TORE. If localisation of the domain has been used for the analysis of the crack, this option cannot be selected. In this case, the node group is created using the update zone (one automatically selects the option TYPE_GROUP='ZONE_MAJ') and the user's choice is ignored. For a precise definition of the notions of enriched node, Heaviside node, Crack-tip node, auxiliary grid, analysis domain and its localisation, see R7.02.12, §3.2.5. 3.5.15 Operand RAYON_TORE If TYPE_GROUP='TORE' > RAYON_TORE= r, One specifies the radius r of the torus to be used for the selection of the nodes. 3.5.16 Operand OPTION = 'RELA_CINE_BP' For each triplet of connections (3 directions of space) contained in the list of kinematic relations of a cable_precont concept coming from DEFI_CABLE_BP, this option creates a node group containing the cable node and the concrete nodes concerned. The name of this group is the value given to PREF_GRNO followed by the name of the cable node. CABLE_BP = cable_bp Nom du concept cable_precont. PREF_GRNO = pref Préfixe donné aux groupes de nœudscréés. 3.5.17 Operands GROUP_MA and NOM GROUP_MA= lgma For each mesh-cell group of the list lgma, one creates a node group formed of the nodes carried by the mesh cells of this mesh-cell group. NOM = lgno If lgno is supplied by the user, this list must be of the same length as lgma. These are the names that one wishes to give to the new node groups. If lgno is not supplied, the node groups will bear the same names as the mesh-cell groups that gave rise to them. CRIT_NOEUD = /'TOUS' [DEFAUT] : on prend tous les nœuds de chaque maille. | /'SOMMET': | one takes only the 'vertex' nodes of the mesh cells (that is to say the ends of the edges). | | --- | --- | | /'MILIEU': | one takes only the 'mid-side' nodes of the edges of the mesh cells. | | /'CENTRE': | one takes only the nodes that are neither 'vertex' nor 'mid-side', that is to say the nodes at the centre of the facets or of the volume mesh cells. | 3.5.18 Operand TOUT_GROUP_MA TOUT_GROUP_MA= 'OUI' This keyword has the same meaning as the previous one, except that one creates node groups for all the existing mesh-cell groups of the mesh. 3.5.19 Operand ALARME = 'OUI' [DEFAULT] / 'NON' if ALARME= 'NON', the code does not issue an alarm; for example when it is asked to create a GROUP_NO and this group is empty. The default value of this keyword is 'OUI'. 3.5.20 Operand INFO if INFO= 1, one prints in the 'MESSAGE' file the number of groups created and, for each group, the name of the group and the number of entities constituting it. if INFO= 2, one prints in the 'MESSAGE' file the number of groups created and, for each group, the name of the group, the number of entities constituting it, then the list of the entities constituting the group or groups. 4 Examples Example 1 (topological and logical criteria): Let ma be a mesh already containing the mesh-cell groups: M1 M2 M3 and the node groups: N1 N2 N3 ma = DEFI_GROUP (reuse = ma, MAILLAGE= ma, CREA_GROUP_MA= ( _F ( NOM= NM1, GROUP_MA= (GMA7, GMA9,...) ), _F ( NOM= NM2, UNION= (M1, NM1) ), _F ( NOM= NM3, DIFFE= (NM2, M2) ),), CREA_GROUP_NO= _F ( TOUT_GROUP_MA= 'OUI'), ) ma = DEFI_GROUP (reuse = ma, MAILLAGE= ma, CREA_GROUP_MA= _F ( NOM= NM4, GROUP_MA= (GMA7, GMA11, GMA13)) CREA_GROUP_NO= (_F ( NOM= NN1, INTERSEC= (NM1, N1)), _F( GROUP_MA= NM4))) After these two calls to the command DEFI_GROUP, the mesh then contains: - the mesh-cell groups: - M1, M2, M3 (initial) - NM1 = (mesh cells: MA7, MA9, ...) - NM2 = M1 "union" NM1 - NM3 = NM2 "minus" M2 - NM4 = (MESH CELLS: MA7, MA11, MA13) - the node groups: - N1, N2, N3 (initial) - M1, M2, M3, NM1, NM2, NM3: group_no containing the nodes of the group_ma of the same names . These group_no are created by the 1st command DEFI_GROUP. - NN1 = NM1 "intersection" N1 - NM4 = (nodes of the group_ma NM4) Example 2 (geometric criteria): ma = DEFI_GROUP (reuse = ma, MAILLAGE= ma, CREA_GROUP_MA= (_F ( NOM= facesup , OPTION = 'FACE_NORMALE' , VECT_NORMALE = (0., 0., 1.)), _F ( NOM= S01 , OPTION = 'SPHERE' , POINT = (0., 0., 0.), RAYON = 1.),), CREA_GROUP_NO=(_F ( NOM = BO_S01 , OPTION = 'ENV_SPHERE' , POINT=(0.,0.,0.),RAYON=1.,PRECISION=0.01), _F ( NOM = S01_1 , GROUP_MA = S01), _F ( NOM = S01_2 , OPTION = 'ENV_SPHERE' , POINT=(0.,0.,0.),RAYON=0.5,PRECISION=0.5),), ) After DEFI_GROUP the mesh ma will contain 2 new GROUP_MA and 3 new GROUP_NO: - facesup contains the facets whose normal is oriented along \mathrm{OZ} (towards Z>0 ), - S01 contains all the mesh cells of which one of the nodes belongs to the sphere of radius 1. centred at O (origin of the axes), - B0_S01 is the group of the nodes that are found in the neighbourhood of the envelope of the previous sphere (S01), - S01_1 is the group of all the nodes of the mesh cells of the mesh-cell group S01; warning: certain nodes of this group may be outside the sphere! - S01_2 is the group of the nodes included in the sphere S01: ∣d(M,O)-0.5∣\le 0.5

u4.23.01 Operator DEFI_MAILLAGE u4.23.01 Operator DEFI_MAILLAGE 1 Purpose Define a mesh with the help of macro-elements. This command makes it possible to define a new mesh from static or dynamic macro-elements. This new mesh (containing only the geometric supports of the macro-elements) can then be "assembled" with another mesh (containing for example "classical" mesh cells) thanks to the command ASSE_MAILLAGE U4.23.03 and the option specific to substructuring. Produces a data structure of type maillage. 2 Syntax super_mesh = DEFI_MAILLAGE( ◆ DEFI_SUPER_MAILLE = _F( ◆ MACR_ELEM = macr_elem_dyna / macr_elem_stat, ◇ SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◇ TRAN = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, # Si: exists("ANGL_NAUT") ◇ CENTRE = float, ), ◇ RECO_GLOBAL = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ), ◇ RECO_SUPER_MAILLE = _F( ◆ SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ OPTION = / "GEOMETRIQUE" (par défaut), / "NOEUD_A_NOEUD", / "INVERSE", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'GEOMETRIQUE') ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ), DEFI_NOEUD = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NOEUD_INIT = no, # Si: exists("TOUT") ◇ PREFIXE = text, ◆ INDEX = int, # Si: exists("NOEUD_INIT") ◆ SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◆ NOEUD_FIN = no, ), ◇ DEFI_GROUP_NO = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◇ & GROUP_NO_INIT = grno, ◆ | GROUP_NO_FIN = grno, ◇ PREFIXE = text, | INDEX = int, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General points In the documentation of this command, one will speak of: - macro-element: object of type macr_elem_stat or macr_elem_dyna, - super mesh cell: geometric entity supporting a macro-element, - initial mesh when one designates the mesh that was used to generate a macro-element, - final mesh to designate the mesh produced by this command. By extension these adjectives initial/final will apply to the entities attached to the meshes: node, mesh cell, node group. In practice, to build the final mesh: - one defines super mesh cells by positioning in space (2D or 3D) existing macro-elements (one and the same macro-element may generate several super mesh cells), - one joins the super mesh cells to one another, - one renames, if one wishes, certain nodes, - one creates, if one wishes, certain node groups. Notes: One can observe that the mesh created by this command is formed only of super mesh cells. One therefore cannot (for example) draw it with the usual post-processors. Possibilities of remedying this may exist with the command DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01. To mix "classical" finite elements and substructures, one must use the operator for "concatenation" of meshes U4.23.03: mag = ASSE_MAILLAGE ( MAILLAGE= (m1, m2)) A mesh resulting from the operator DEFI_MAILLAGE contains: - super mesh cells, - nodes, - node groups. The super mesh cells are defined by translation/rotation of macro-elements. Like a "classical" mesh cell, a super mesh cell is entirely defined by the list of its nodes. The coordinates of the nodes of the mesh cells are those of the external nodes of the macro-elements transformed by the geometric transformation: translation, rotation... If one does not carry out any joining (cf. RECO_GLOBAL / RECO_SUPER_MAILLE), the mesh has as many nodes as the sum of the nodes of the super mesh cells. Convention C1: When one "joins" the super mesh cells, one eliminates certain nodes. By convention, when coincident nodes are eliminated, one keeps the node (and therefore its coordinates) that comes from the first mesh cell of the list l_mail (cf. RECO_GLOBAL / RECO_SUPER_MAILLE). As in any Aster mesh, the nodes are named . By default, the names of the nodes are given by the program in the form: Nijk where ijk is a number between 1 and 999999.9. The keyword DEFI_GROUP_NO allows the user to rename certain nodes and to define node groups. 4 Operands 4.1 Keyword DEFI_SUPER_MAILLE ♦ DEFI_SUPER_MAILLE= This factor keyword makes it possible to define the super mesh cells of the mesh with the help of the macro-elements. 4.1.1 Operand MACR_ELEM ♦ MACR_ELEM = l_se l_se is the list of the names of the macro-elements that will generate the mesh cells. 4.1.2 Operand SUPER_MAILLE ◊ SUPER_MAILLE = l_mail l_mail is the list of the names that one wishes to give to the mesh cells. This argument is optional. In its absence, the mesh cells will be given the names of the macro-elements (this is obviously impossible if one wishes to use the same macro-element several times). 4.1.3 Operands for geometric transformations ◊ | ◊ TRAN= This keyword defines the translation to apply to the macro-element: - if one is in 2D , one expects 2 reals: (tx, ty), - if one is in 3D , one expects 3 reals: (tx, ty, tz). | ◊ ANGL_NAUT= ◊ CENTRE= These keywords define the rotation to apply to the macro-element. If one is in 2D , one expects 3 reals: - a is the angle (in degrees) of rotation in the plane for ANGL_NAUT, - px and py are the coordinates of the centre of rotation for CENTRE. If one is in 3D , one expects 6 reals: - a, b, c are the nautical angles (\alpha ,\beta ,\gamma ) of the rotation (in degrees). (Cf. the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01) for ANGL_NAUT, - px, py and pz are the coordinates of the centre of rotation for CENTRE. Important note: One knows that the order of the keywords is not significant for Aster. The translation/rotation operation is conventionally carried out in the order rotation then translation. These two operations do not commute in general. 4.2 Keyword RECO_GLOBAL ◊ | RECO_GLOBAL= ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' , / SUPER_MAILLE= l_maille, ◊ | CRITERE = / 'ABSOLU' , / 'RELATIF' , [DEFAUT] | PRECISION = / prec, / 1.D-3, [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to join automatically a set of super mesh cells (designated by the keyword SUPER_MAILLE or the keyword TOUT) with a criterion of geometric proximity: 2 nodes of 2 different super mesh cells m1 and m2 will be merged if the distance separating them is: < prec (CRITERE = 'ABSOLU'), < prec min(d(m1),d(m2)) (CRITERE = 'RELATIF'). where d(mi) denotes the smallest distance between 2 nodes of the super mesh cell mi. Notes: Two nodes of one and the same mesh cell will never be joined. If a mesh cell contains only a single node, one must use CRITERE='ABSOLU'. 4.3 Keyword RECO_SUPER_MAILLE ◊ RECO_SUPER_MAILLE = This factor keyword makes it possible to join " by hand " certain super mesh cells designated by the user. The super mesh cells that one can join are those that have been defined by the keyword DEFI_SUPER_MAILLE. One then joins the super mesh cells via node groups. To say what one wishes to join one must therefore give pairs (mesh cell, node group (of the initial mesh)). Notes: When one gives a pair (mesh cell, node group), one designates the list of the nodes of the node group that are external for the macro-element that defines the super mesh cell. It is in fact the intersection of the node group and of the boundary of the substructure. This list is ordered like the initial node group. In principle, when one joins 2 mesh cells via 2 node groups, the set of the designated nodes must be joined (cf. the convention chosen by the keyword OPTION). An alarm message will be issued if this is not the case. 4.3.1 Operands SUPER_MAILLE/GROUP_NO ◊ SUPER_MAILLE= One gives here the list of the mesh cells to join. In general, one joins the mesh cells 2 by 2. For the "corners", it may be convenient to join all the concurrent mesh cells in a single operation (for example the 4 super-cubes that share the same edge). ◊ GROUP_NO= One gives here the list of the node groups to join. This list is of the same length as the list of the mesh cells. 4.3.2 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION= This keyword makes it possible to choose the convention for joining the lists of nodes defined by the node groups. - 'GEOMETRIQUE': The program will make the nodes coincide by considerations of geometric proximity. (Cf. keyword: RECO_GLOBAL) - 'NOEUD_A_NOEUD' / 'INVERSE': Si OPTION = 'NOEUD_A_NOEUD' , GROUP_NO = (G1, G2, G3) Si OPTION = 'INVERSE' , GROUP_NO = (G1, G2, G3) Warning: For the option 'INVERSE', only the first node group of the list of GROUP_NO is "turned over". 4.4 Keyword DEFI_GROUP_NO ◊ DEFI_GROUP_NO= This factor keyword makes it possible to define node groups from groups existing in the initial meshes of the macro-elements. Note: An initial node group may contain nodes that do not belong to the boundaries of the macro-elements. These internal nodes therefore do not exist in the final mesh. For convenience, one adopts the convention of creating the group anyway, reduced to its intersection with the boundary of the macro-element. 4.4.1 Operands TOUT/SUPER_MAILLE/PREFIXE/INDEX | ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' , / SUPER_MAILLE = mail, ◊ PREFIXE = pref, ♦ INDEX = (dm, fm, dn, fn), These keywords make it possible to create all the node groups corresponding to the groups of the initial mesh associated with the mesh cell mail, or with all the mesh cells if: TOUT= 'OUI'. The renaming convention is the following (in pseudo FORTRAN): gno_fin(k8) = pref//no_mail(dm:fm)//gno_ini(dn:fn) Which means that the name of a node group will be formed by concatenating: - the prefix possibly given by the user, - a sub-string of characters extracted from the name of the mesh cell, - a sub-string of characters extracted from the name of the group_no of the initial mesh. It is therefore necessary that: ltot = length(prefix) + (fm-dm+1) + (fn-dn+1) ≤ 8 A frequent case is the following: the meshes that gave rise to the macro-elements come from a pre-processor that generates names of the form GRNOijkl. If the user gives the super mesh cells names of 2 characters: SA, SB,...., the sequence: DEFI_GROUP_NO=_F(TOUT= 'OUI' , PREFIXE='GN' , INDEX=(1,2,5,8)) will generate node groups with the names: GNSA0001, GNSA0002,... , GNSB0001. 4.4.2 Operands GROUP_NO_FIN/SUPER_MAILLE/GROUP_NO_INIT | ♦ GROUP_NO_FIN = gno_fin, ♦ SUPER_MAILLE = mail, ♦ GROUP_NO_INIT= gno_ini, These keywords make it possible to create node groups one by one : - gno_fin is the name that one wishes to give to the GROUP_NO, - mail and gno_ini identify the initial GROUP_NO: - mail is the name of the super mesh cell that carries the GROUP_NO, - gno_ini is the name of the GROUP_NO of the initial mesh. 5 Example Let the mesh be m1: GROUP_NO : GROUP_MA : AB = (N1 N2 N3) grma1 BC = (N3 N4 N5) grma2 CD = ..... ...... On this mesh m1 one defines 2 macr_elem_stat. mo1 = AFFE_MODELE ( AFFE = _F (GROUP_MA = grma1)...) mo2 = AFFE_MODELE ( AFFE = _F (GROUP_MA = grma2)...) S1 = MACR_ELEM_STAT ( DEFINITION = _F (MODELE = mo1...) EXTERIEUR = _F (GROUP_NO = (AB,BC,CD,DE,EA)) ...) S2 = MACR_ELEM_STAT ( DEFINITION = _F (MODELE = mo2...) EXTERIEUR = _F (GROUP_NO = (BC,BG,FG,CF)) ...)
