u4.23.02 Operator CREA_MAILLAGE u4.23.02 Operator CREA_MAILLAGE 1 Purpose Create a data structure of type maillage from another mesh. The new mesh is created from an existing mesh by duplicating, destroying, transforming or exploding mesh cells, or by copying a mesh (the case of geom_fibre). Produces a data structure maillage. 2 Syntax maillage = CREA_MAILLAGE( ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, / GEOM_FIBRE = gfibre, ◆ / COQU_VOLU = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ EPAIS = float, ◆ PLAN = / "INF", / "MOY", / "SUP", # Si: equal_to("PLAN", 'MOY') ◆ TRANSLATION = / "INF", / "SUP", ), / CREA_FISS = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ GROUP_NO_1 = grno, ◆ GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ), / CREA_MAILLE = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / CREA_POI1 = _F( ◇ NOM_GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = list[grma], | GROUP_NO = list[grno], ), / ECLA_PG = _F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ SHRINK = float (défaut: 0.9), ◇ TAILLE_MIN = float (défaut: 0.0), ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEGE_ELGA", / "DEPL_ELGA", / "DERA_ELGA", / "DIFF_ELGA", / "DISS_ELGA", / "EFGE_ELGA", / "ENDO_ELGA", / "ENEL_ELGA", / "EPEQ_ELGA", / "EPFD_ELGA", / "EPFP_ELGA", / "EPGQ_ELGA", / "EPME_ELGA", / "EPMG_ELGA", / "EPMQ_ELGA", / "EPSG_ELGA", / "EPSI_ELGA", / "EPSL_ELGA", / "EPSP_ELGA", / "EPVC_ELGA", / "ETOT_ELGA", / "FLHN_ELGA", / "FLUX_ELGA", / "FLUX_ELGA", / "GRAT_ELGA", / "GRAT_ELGA", / "HYDR_ELGA", / "HYGR_ELGA", / "INDL_ELGA", / "MATE_ELGA", / "PDIL_ELGA", / "SIEF_ELGA", / "SIEQ_ELGA", / "SIGM_ELGA", / "SIMY_ELGA", / "SOUR_ELGA", / "STRX_ELGA", / "TEMP_ELGA", / "UT01_ELGA", / "UT02_ELGA", / "UT03_ELGA", / "UT04_ELGA", / "UT05_ELGA", / "UT06_ELGA", / "UT07_ELGA", / "UT08_ELGA", / "UT09_ELGA", / "UT10_ELGA", / "VARC_ELGA", / "VARI_ELGA", ), / HEXA20_27 = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / LINE_QUAD = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / LINE_CUBI = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / MODI_MAILLE = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ OPTION = / "QUAD8_9", / "QUAD_TRIA3", / "SEG3_4", / "TRIA6_7", ), / QUAD_LINE = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / REPERE = _F( ◆ TABLE = table, ◇ NOM_ORIG = / "CDG", / "TORSION", ◇ NOM_ROTA = "INERTIE" (ou non renseigné), # Si: equal_to("NOM_ORIG", 'CDG') ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ), / RESTREINT = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ TOUT_GROUP_MA = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◇ TOUT_GROUP_NO = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ), / PENTA15_18 = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / DECOUPE_LAC = _F( ◆ | GROUP_MA_ESCL = list[grma], ◇ DECOUPE_HEXA = / "HEXA", / "PYRA" (par défaut), ), / MODI_HHO = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), / COQUE_SOLIDE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ GROUP_MA_SURF = list[grma], ), / RAFFINEMENT = _F( ◇ TOUT = "OUI", ◇ NIVEAU = int (défaut: 1), ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Risk of producing a non-conforming mesh A certain number of functionalities of the command CREA_MAILLAGE can lead to the production of a non-conforming mesh. For this reason, the user must be particularly vigilant when using CREA_MAILLAGE to transform mesh cells. A mesh is non-conforming when the shape functions of 2 adjacent elements do not have the same trace on their common boundary. For example: - 2 pentahedra assembled to form a hexahedron and placed on another hexahedron (1 quadrangle facing 2 triangles). - 1 QUAD8 sharing an edge with 1 QUAD4 or 1 TRIA3 - 1 TRIA6 sharing an edge with 2 TRIA3 Non-conforming meshes lead in general to incorrect results (at least locally). Among the possibilities of CREA_MAILLAGE, several situations are potentially dangerous: - Use of one of the keywords QUAD_TRIA3 (u4.23.02-QUADTRIA3), LINE_QUAD (u4.23.02-LINEQUAD), LINE_CUBI (u4.23.02-LINECUBI) , QUAD_LINE (u4.23.02-QUADLINE), HEXA20_27 (u4.23.02-HEXA2027), PENTA15_18 (u4.23.02-PENTA1518) with the keyword GROUP_MA. If, for example, one partially transforms a linear mesh into a quadratic mesh, the mesh will be non-conforming on the boundary between the linear elements and the quadratic elements. When the keyword GROUP_MA is used, the skin mesh cells will be added automatically. - Use of the keyword HEXA20_27 or PENTA15_18 if there exist in the mesh volume elements with quadrangular faces of a type different from the elements that one is modifying. For example, if there exist pentahedra or pyramids when one modifies hexahedra. The risk is that, for example, a quadrangular face of an HEXA27 (9 nodes) is placed against a quadrangular face with 8 nodes of an adjacent PENTA15. - Use of the keyword QUAD_TRIA3 if there exist TRIA6 elements in the mesh. In this case, the quadrangles transformed into TRIA3 will be incompatible with the TRIA6. 4 Operands 4.1 Keyword MAILLAGE The keyword MAILLAGE gives the name of the initial mesh that one wishes to reproduce before modifying it by adding or deleting new mesh cells or nodes. Note The keyword is mandatory except when the keywords ECLA_PG and GEOM_FIBRE are used. 4.2 Factor keyword CREA_MAILLE One occurrence of the factor keyword CREA_MAILLE makes it possible to define a new mesh-cell group made up of new mesh cells, themselves supported on existing nodes. To duplicate several mesh-cell groups, one repeats the factor keyword CREA_MAILLE. Unlike the command DEFI_GROUP, for which the mesh concept always retains the same number of mesh cells and of nodes, here the number of mesh cells of the new mesh is increased (the number of nodes remains identical because the new mesh cells are supported on already existing nodes). This can facilitate the creation of new geometrical locations in order to be able to apply different modellings to the same mesh-cell group. 4.2.1 Keyword NOM The name of the new mesh-cell group which will be created is given by the keyword NOM. 4.2.2 Keywords GROUP_MA and TOUT The set of mesh cells supplied by the user with these two keywords will be duplicated and the new mesh cells will be gathered in a mesh-cell group bearing the name stipulated by the keyword NOM. If the set of mesh cells to be duplicated contains duplicate mesh cells, they are eliminated. 4.3 Factor keyword CREA_POI1 One occurrence of the factor keyword CREA_POI1 makes it possible to define mesh cells of type 'POI1' (mesh cell with a single node) from nodes or from nodes of mesh cells. 4.3.1 Keywords TOUT/GROUP_MA/GROUP_NO All the nodes which belong to entities stipulated by the user with these keywords generate a mesh cell of type POI1. The mesh cell created will have the same name as the node which supports it. 4.3.2 Keyword NOM_GROUP_MA All the POI1 mesh cells created may be grouped in one and the same mesh-cell group named by the keyword NOM_GROUP_MA. 4.3.3 How to create several POI1 mesh cells on each node? The POI1 mesh cells created by CREA_POI1 have the same names as the nodes from which they were created. It is therefore not possible to create several POI1 mesh cells on one and the same node by using several occurrences of the keyword CREA_POI1. A possible workaround is to combine the use of CREA_MAILLAGE / CREA_POI1 with CREA_MAILLAGE / CREA_MAILLE. For example, to create 2 POI1 mesh cells on each node of the group 'GNO1', one may do: MA2=CREA_MAILLAGE(MAILLAGE=MA1, CREA_POI1 = _F(NOM_GROUP_MA='GM1', GROUP_NO='GNO1')) MA3=CREA_MAILLAGE(MAILLAGE=MA2, CREA_MAILLE =_F(NOM_GROUP_MA='GM2', GROUP_MA='GM1')) 4.4 Factor keyword MODI_MAILLE One occurrence of the factor keyword MODI_MAILLE makes it possible to transform a set of mesh cells according to what is indicated by the keyword OPTION: 1. OPTION='SEG3_4': transformation of three-node segments into four-node segments (usable for example for the modelling 'TUYAU' 2. OPTION='TRIA6_7': transformation of six-node triangles into seven-node triangles, 3. OPTION='QUAD8_9': transformation of eight-node quadrangles into nine-node quadrangles, 1. OPTION='QUAD_TRIA3': transformation of quadrangles into 3-node triangles: - transformation of mesh cells of type QUAD4 into two mesh cells of type TRIA3 - transformation of mesh cells of type QUAD8 into six mesh cells of type TRIA3 - transformation of mesh cells of type QUAD9 into eight mesh cells of type TRIA3 - An automatic procedure for cutting quadrangular mesh cells into triangles can generate a kind of "polarisation" of the mesh: starting from a given QUAD mesh, all the diagonals end up oriented in the same direction. Note Caution: use of the option 'QUAD_TRIA3' can lead to a non-conforming mesh. See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. 4.5 Factor keyword LINE_QUAD This functionality makes it possible to create a quadratic mesh from a linear mesh. One may apply it only to part of the mesh (keyword GROUP_MA), but this is not recommended. See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. The mesh-cell groups are retained, as are the node groups (without change). As when refining a mesh, the nodes created are not introduced into the existing node groups. If a node group corresponds to a boundary, after LINE_QUAD this group does not contain the mid-edge nodes. In order to obtain a complete GROUP_NO, one may use for example the command DEFI_GROUP (OPTION = 'APPUI'). The set of mesh cells stipulated by the user with the two keywords GROUP_MA or TOUT will be transformed into quadratic mesh cells. Caution: use of the keyword GROUP_MA is not recommended. See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. 4.6 Factor keyword LINE_CUBI This functionality makes it possible to create a cubic mesh from a linear mesh. One may apply it only to part of the mesh (keyword GROUP_MA), but this is not recommended. See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. The mesh-cell groups are retained, as are the node groups (without change). As when refining a mesh, the nodes created are not introduced into the existing node groups. If a node group corresponds to a boundary, after LINE_CUBI this group does not contain the vertex nodes of the edges. In order to obtain a complete GROUP_NO, one may use for example the command DEFI_GROUP (OPTION = 'APPUI'). The set of mesh cells stipulated by the user with the two keywords GROUP_MA or TOUT will be transformed into quadratic mesh cells. 4.7 Factor keyword PENTA15_18 This factor keyword works like the factor keyword LINE_QUAD (same syntax). It is used to transform PENTA15 into PENTA18 by adding nodes at the centres of the quadrangular faces. Caution: use of this keyword is not recommended if the mesh contains other types of volume mesh cells (HEXA and PYRAM). See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. 4.8 Factor keyword HEXA20_27 This factor keyword works like the factor keyword PENTA15_18 with the hexahedra. It is used to transform HEXA20 into HEXA27 by adding nodes at the centres of the faces and at the centre of each hexahedron. Caution: use of this keyword is not recommended if the mesh contains other types of volume mesh cells (PENTA and PYRAM). See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. 4.9 Factor keyword MODI_HHO This option makes it possible to create a mesh compatible with the HHO elements from any mesh. This option is indispensable in order to use the HHO method on tetrahedra, prisms and pyramids. The mesh created is composed of SEG3, QUAD9, TRIA7, HEXA27, TETRA15, PENTA21 and PYRAM19. Caution: use of this keyword is not recommended if it is applied only to part of the mesh, because that can generate non-conforming meshes. See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. 4.10 Factor keyword COQUE_SOLIDE This option makes it possible to create a mesh compatible with the COQUE_SOLIDE elements from a mesh of HEXA8 or PENTA6 elements. This option is indispensable in order to use the COQUE_SOLIDE modelling; the new HEXA9 and PENTA7 mesh cells contain a node in the middle of the support, which makes it possible to take the pinching degree of freedom into account. The mesh created is therefore composed of SEG2, QUAD4, HEXA9, PENTA7 and TRIA3. In the case of hexahedral elements, it is necessary to supply the keyword GROUP_MA_SURF which identifies the surface used to orient the mesh cells. This surface may be the upper one or the lower one. This is not necessary for the prisms, since in that configuration it is the fact of having TRIA3 which identifies the upper and lower surfaces of the shell. 4.11 Factor keyword RAFFINEMENT This option makes it possible to create a uniformly refined mesh from a given mesh. The option is applied to the whole mesh in order to avoid any conformity problem. The principle of uniform refinement is to cut each edge in two and then to propagate the cut to the other mesh cells. It is equivalent to the 'RAFFINEMENT_UNIFORME' adaptation of MACR_ADAP_MAIL. Caution: the size of the mesh increases very rapidly and its quality may decrease if the starting mesh is not of sufficient quality. It is recommended to start from a mesh which already represents the geometry well, in particular if it is curved, before refining. The refinement is applied to the whole mesh. The keyword NIVEAU makes it possible to specify the number of successive refinements required. 4.12 Factor keyword QUAD_LINE This functionality makes it possible to create a linear mesh from a quadratic mesh; one may apply it only to part of the mesh (caution in that case regarding the junction of the linear and quadratic zones). See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. The set of mesh cells stipulated by the user with the two keywords GROUP_MA or TOUT will be transformed into linear mesh cells. Caution: use of the keyword GROUP_MA is not recommended. See u4.23.02-risqueNonConformite. 4.13 Factor keyword REPERE One occurrence of the factor keyword REPERE makes it possible to define a new mesh from the old mesh by carrying out a change of frame. This functionality is used in particular in the command MACR_CARA_POUTRE for the computation of the warping constant. The keyword TABLE gives the name of the concept table "geometrical characteristics", which contains in particular the coordinates of the centre of inertia and of the centre of torsion, the nautical angles defining the principal frame of inertia, etc. This table may be obtained by the command POST_ELEM with the factor keywords CARA_GEOM or CARA_POUTRE. The centre of the new frame is indicated by the keyword NOM_ORIG: the centre of gravity ('CDG') or the centre of torsion ('TORSION'). If NOM_ORIG= 'CDG', one may indicate by the keyword GROUP_MA the name of the mesh-cell group whose centre of gravity will be the origin of the new frame. If one does not use GROUP_MA, the centre of gravity of the whole model will be the origin of the new frame. If NOM_ORIG= 'TORSION', the keyword GROUP_MA has no effect. The direction of the new frame is indicated by the keyword NOM_ROTA. Only one solution is possible: the directions are those of the principal frame of inertia. 4.14 Factor keyword COQU_VOLU From the data of a group of surface mesh cells (QUAD, TRIA3), the volume mesh (HEXA8, PENTA6) is built by extrusion along the normal to the elements (at a node, one takes the average of the normals of the elements meeting there). Only one layer of elements is created. The operation applies only to linear meshes; if one wishes to create a quadratic mesh, it is enough to use LINE_QUAD afterwards. The name of the mesh-cell group made up of the volume mesh cells created during this operation is indicated by the keyword NOM. The keyword GROUP_MA gives the mesh-cell groups constituting the surface mesh to be extruded. The thickness of the layer of elements created (thickness of the shell) is given by the keyword EPAIS. The keyword PLAN specifies that the surface mesh to be extruded, given by GROUP_MA, will be the upper ('SUP'), lower ('INF') or middle ('MOY') plane of the shell. In the case where PLAN='MOY', the keyword TRANSLATION specifies whether the initial surface to be extruded is translated to the upper skin ('SUP') or to the lower skin ('INF'). 4.15 Factor keyword CREA_FISS The factor keyword CREA_FISS makes it possible to create a crack with joint elements R3.06.09 or elements with a discontinuity R7.02.12 along a line defined by two node groups placed facing one another. The two node groups must have the same number of nodes and must have been ordered beforehand (for example with DEFI_GROUP and OPTION='NOEUD_ORDO') so that their numbering "starts" from the same side. One may then assign a modelling of "joint" type to these new QUAD4 mesh cells (for example 'PLAN_JOINT'). A new GROUP_MA containing all the QUAD4 mesh cells created will also be created. The keyword NOM gives the name of the mesh-cell group made up of the volume mesh cells created during this operation. The node groups constituting the lips of the crack are given by the keywords GROUP_NO_1 and GROUP_NO_2. The node group GROUP_NO_1 carries the local nodes 1 and 2 (the first node of the group has a local numbering equal to 1), and GROUP_NO_2 carries the local nodes 3 and 4 (the first node of the group has a local numbering equal to 4). These node groups must be chosen according to the geometry so that the local numbering of the elements is carried out in the anticlockwise direction. Ordering of the segments 4.16 Factor keyword ECLA_PG Factor keyword to be removed. .. The factor keyword ECLA_PG is not to be used directly. It is used by the command MACR_ECLA_PG. 4.17 Factor keyword GEOM_FIBRE The factor keyword GEOM_FIBRE makes it possible to obtain the mesh created by DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE. This mesh contains all the fibre groups of the study as well as the mesh containing all the fibres. 4.18 Factor keyword RESTREINT This factor keyword (non-repeatable) makes it possible to generate a "sub"-mesh extracted from an existing mesh. The extracted (or "restricted") mesh is formed from a list of mesh cells supplied by the keyword GROUP_MA. The nodes retained are those of the mesh cells retained. Moreover, if the keyword GROUP_NO is used, the nodes of these groups are added The mesh will contain all the mesh-cell groups of the keyword GROUP_MA. Moreover, if the keyword TOUT_GROUP_MA='OUI' is used, the non-empty mesh-cell groups of the initial mesh are added. The mesh will contain all the node groups of the keyword GROUP_NO. Moreover, if the keyword TOUT_GROUP_NO='OUI' is used, the non-empty node groups of ma_1 are added. 4.19 Factor keyword DECOUPE_LAC The factor keyword DECOUPE_LAC makes it possible to obtain a mesh containing "patches" created on the mesh-cell group specified in GROUP_MA_ESCL. It is a pre-processing operation on the slave mesh cells for the treatment of contact by the mortar LAC method. Note that the mesh cells underlying the mesh cells of GROUP_MA_ESCL are also cut. The cuts of the elements PYRA5 PYRA13, PENTA6, PENTA15 and HEXA8 HEXA20 in the case DECOUPE_HEXA='PYRA' are "non-conforming" cuts in the sense that they introduce elements different from the element being cut (pyramids and/or tetrahedra) so as to add only one node per cut element in the mesh. Cutting of PENTA18 is not supported. DECOUPE_LAC must be the last command to act on the mesh. The MODI_MAILLAGE operations must be carried out beforehand. DECOUPE_LAC on the 3D mesh cells DECOUPE_LAC on the 2D mesh cells The keyword DECOUPE_HEXA makes it possible to define the type of cut used on the HEXA8 and the HEXA20. By default, these elements are cut into pyramids in order to limit the number of nodes added. However, by using the value HEXA, they are cut into HEXA, which can be useful if the introduction of pyramids into the mesh poses a problem. 4.20 Keyword INFO The keyword INFO specifies the information printed in the message file (1: no printout, 2: details on the number of mesh cells created, modified…). 4.21 Keyword TITRE The keyword TITRE makes it possible to specify a title. 5 Examples 5.1 Duplication of mesh cells Let there be a mesh already containing the mesh cells: M1 M2 M3 and the shell mesh-cell group: coque : M1 M2 Each mesh cell is supported on the following nodes: M1 : N1 N2 N3 M2 : N3 N4 N5 M3 : N4 N5 N6 If one calls the following command: ma_2 = CREA_MAILLAGE(MAILLAGE = ma_1, CREA_MAILLE = _F(NOM = 'sol', GROUP_MA = 'coque', ),) After the call to the command CREA_MAILLAGE, the new mesh then contains: - the mesh-cell groups: - coque (initial) - sol containing the mesh cells M4 and M5 - the mesh cells are supported on the following nodes: - M1 : N1 N2 N3 - M2 : N3 N4 N5 - M3 : N4 N5 N6 - M4 : N1 N2 N3 - M5 : N3 N4 N5 5.2 Transformation of 6-node triangles into 7-node triangles ma_2 = CREA_MAILLAGE(MAILLAGE = ma_1, MODI_MAILLE = _F(GROUP_MA = 'triangle', OPTION = 'TRIA6_7', ),) Suppose that in ma_1 the GROUP_MA triangle is composed of two mesh cells M1, M2 having the following nodes: M1: N1 N2 N3 N4 N5 N6 M2: N1 N2 N7 N4 N8 N9 In the mesh ma_2, the two mesh cells M1, M2 will have the following nodes: M1: N1 N2 N3 N4 N5 N6 N10 M2: N1 N2 N7 N4 N8 N9 N11 5.3 Example of use of DECOUPE_LAC Cutting of the surface with the option DECOUPE_LAC (test cases zzzz383)

u4.23.03 Operator ASSE_MAILLAGE u4.23.03 Operator ASSE_MAILLAGE 1 Purpose Assemble two meshes to form a new one. The two meshes to be assembled may come from the operators: LIRE_MAILLAGE U4.21.01, DEFI_MAILLAGE U4.23.01, ASSE_MAILLAGE U4.23.03, ... That is to say that they may contain ordinary mesh cells or super mesh cells carrying macro-elements. Produces a data structure of type maillage. 2 Syntax / super_mesh / maillage = ASSE_MAILLAGE( ◆ MAILLAGE_1 = maillage, ◆ MAILLAGE_2 = maillage, ◆ OPERATION = / "SOUS_STR", / "SUPERPOSE", / "COLLAGE", # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'COLLAGE') ◆ COLLAGE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA_1 = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_2 = grma, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands MAILLAGE_1 and MAILLAGE_2 ♦ MAILLAGE_1 = ma1, MAILLAGE_2 = ma2, ma1 and ma2 are the names of the two meshes to be assembled. 4 Operand OPERATION = 'SUPERPOSE' With the choice 'SUPERPOSE', all the entities (mesh cells, nodes, mesh-cell groups and node groups) of the two meshes are retained. The only problem to be settled concerns the name of these entities (a name conflict is possible because the two meshes may contain, for example, nodes of the same name). To resolve these possible name problems: 1. The nodes and the mesh cells are always renamed. This means that the user cannot know the name of the nodes and mesh cells of the result mesh. In general the user will have to use (which is always recommended) the names of mesh-cell groups and node groups. Or else the user will have to print the mesh in order to know the names that were chosen. 2. The names of the node groups and of the mesh-cell groups are retained as far as possible. If two mesh-cell groups (or two node groups) have the same name in the two meshes, the group coming from the 2nd mesh is renamed automatically and the name change is indicated in the message file. 5 Operand OPERATION = 'COLLAGE' The operation 'COLLAGE' is used to connect two meshes which would have been meshed independently in two distinct files (for example by two different teams). If the two meshes are not consistent on their interface (different discretisation), the user will have no choice other than to use the functionality AFFE_CHAR_ /LIAISON_MAIL in order to link the degrees of freedom of the two meshes, which will remain topologically disjoint. The user must then use the operation 'SUPERPOSE'. If, on the other hand, the two meshes have been designed to be joined back together, the user will use the operation 'COLLAGE'. For that, the user will have had to take the precaution of naming the two mesh-cell groups (of the interface) which will make it possible to join the two meshes. Moreover these two mesh-cell groups must be geometrically coincident. The user will then write: OPERATION='COLLAGE', COLLAGE= _F(GROUP_MA_1='gma1', GROUP_MA_2='gma2',), The mesh-cell groups gma1 and gma2 will then be merged. More precisely: 1. the mesh cells of gma1 and gma2 will be deleted, 2. the nodes of gma2 will remain (but will be orphans), 3. the nodes of gma1 will connect the two meshes. Before merging the two mesh-cell groups gma1 and gma2, the code will check that the nodes of these two mesh-cell groups are indeed coincident (with a tolerance of 0,001 times the length of the shortest edge of the two meshes). The name conflicts of the entities of the two meshes are settled in the same way as for the operation 'SUPERPOSE' (see above). 6 Operand OPERATION = 'SOUS_STR' In order to mix ordinary finite elements and macro-elements (or substructures) in one and the same model, one must have a mesh containing both ordinary mesh cells and super mesh cells. The operator ASSE_MAILLAGE / OPERATION = 'SOUS_STR' makes it possible to constitute this "mixed" mesh by assembling an ordinary (or mixed) mesh and a mesh containing super mesh cells (coming from DEFI_MAILLAGE). This procedure uses the names of the nodes and of the mesh cells of the meshes; it is therefore applicable only for meshes in the "ASTER" format. The meaning of the assembly is as follows: - All the entities of the two argument meshes ma1 and ma2 (mesh cells, super mesh cells, nodes, mesh-cell group and node group) are copied into the result mesh: mac. - The only shared entities are the nodes of the same names . It is these nodes which make it possible to assemble the two meshes. - Treatment of the entities bearing the same name: - nodes: the nodes of the second mesh bearing a name which exists in the first mesh are not added: it is assumed that they are the same. The coordinates of the retained node are those of the node of the first mesh. An alarm is emitted when the distance between the two coincident nodes is greater than: {10}^{-6}.\text{d\_refe} where \text{d\_refe} is a characteristic length of the mesh: \text{d\_refe}=\max(d(O,N)) where d(O,N) is the distance of the node N from the origin of the global frame. - mesh cells (or super mesh cells): if the mesh ma2 contains mesh cells of the same name as mesh cells of the first mesh ma1, the code stops in fatal error. - mesh-cell group (or node groups): if the mesh ma2 contains a mesh-cell group of the same name as a mesh-cell group of ma1, the latter is ignored and the code emits an alarm message.

u4.23.04 Operator MODI_MAILLAGE u4.23.04 Operator MODI_MAILLAGE 1 Purpose Carry out modifications on an existing mesh. The possible modifications are: - reorient boundary mesh cells used to apply a pressure, - check the orientation of the normals on the shell elements, - reorient the mesh cells of a single layer of joint elements, - reorient the x-axis in the parametric space of the biquadratic hexahedral elements, - update the mesh from a deformed shape computed previously, - in a mesh with a crack front, move the mid-edge nodes of the edges touching the crack front to a quarter of these edges, - translate a mesh, - impose one or more rotations about arbitrary axes on a mesh, - generate a mesh symmetric with respect to a plane in 3D or a straight line in 2D. - compute the curvilinear abscissa along a line formed of line elements (SEG) - modify the coordinates of the nodes randomly Produces a data structure of type maillage or modifies the data structure (re-entrant operator). 2 Syntax maillage = MODI_MAILLAGE( ◆ reuse = , ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◆ | ORIE_FISSURE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ), | DEFORME = _F( ◆ OPTION = "TRAN" (ou non renseigné), ◆ / DEPL = cham_no, / ALEA = float, ), | ORIE_PEAU = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA_PEAU = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_INTERNE = grma, ), | ORIE_NORM_COQUE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ VECT_NORM = float, # Si: exists("VECT_NORM") ◇ GROUP_NO = grno, ), | ORIE_INTERF_POU = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ VECT_ORIE = float, ), | MODI_MAILLE = _F( ◆ OPTION = "NOEUD_QUART" (ou non renseigné), ◆ | GROUP_MA_FOND = grma, | GROUP_NO_FOND = grno, ), | TRANSLATION = float, | ROTATION = _F( ◆ POIN_1 = float, ◇ ANGLE = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ / POIN_2 = float, / DIR = float, ), | MODI_BASE = _F( ◆ VECT_X = float, ◇ VECT_Y = float, ), | ECHELLE = float, | SYMETRIE = _F( ◆ POINT = float, ◆ AXE_1 = float, ◇ AXE_2 = float, ), | ORIE_LIGNE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ VECT_TANG = float, # Si: exists("VECT_TANG") ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ), | ABSC_CURV = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ GROUP_NO_ORIG = grno, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE > ♦ MAILLAGE = ma, Mesh of type [maillage] to which the modifications and/or checks will apply. Note: It is possible to apply a 3D modification to an initially two-dimensional mesh. 3.2 Operand INFO > ◊ INFO = Indicates the printout level of the results of the operator, | 1 = | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2 = | printout of the mesh cells whose connectivity has been modified, including the printout of the old and new connectivities. | The printouts are made in the file 'MESSAGE'. 3.3 Keyword ORIE_FISSURE > ◊ ORIE_FISSURE = This keyword is used to reorient (if necessary) the mesh cells of a group forming a "single layer" of elements. It works in 2D or in 3D, with a linear or quadratic mesh [Figure 3.4-a]. Figure 3.4-a At present, this keyword is used to reorient the joint elements and the interface elements (modellings AXIS_xxx, PLAN_xxx and 3D_xxx with xxx=JOINT or INTERFACE). The user specifies (with the keyword GROUP_MA) which mesh cells are candidates for reorientation (the "single layer"). These mesh cells must be "prisms" (QUAD in 2D, HEXA and PENTA in 3D). The direction "transverse" to the layer is determined topologically (and not according to a flatness criterion). In order to be able to be reoriented, the elements of the layer must be supported (via the bases of the prisms) on other mesh cells of the same dimension (2D or 3D) which do not belong to the group of mesh cells to be reoriented. Consider the (2D) mesh opposite. One wishes to reorient the group of the 3 mesh cells A, B and C. For the mesh cells A and B, the support mesh cells (above and below) determine an unambiguous transverse orientation (vertical). On the other hand, mesh cell C has 3 support mesh cells (top, bottom, right) and one cannot determine the transverse direction. The reorientation algorithm will fail. Note: The "reorientation" referred to here consists in reality in modifying the definition of the connectivity of the mesh cells. For example, in 2D, the convention is that sides 2 and 4 of the quadrangles are transverse to the layer. ♦ GROUP_MA= l_gm, List of the mesh-cell groups whose orientation one wishes to check (and possibly modify). 3.4 Keyword DEFORMEE ♦ DEFORME / OPTION='TRAN' Option making it possible to add to the initial geometry of the mesh ma: - the values of TRANslation (dx, dy (+ dz in 3D)) of the displacement field depl given by the keyword DEPL; - Or a random quantity. / DEPL= depl , Displacement field used to update the geometry / ALEA= epsi , One adds to each coordinate of each node of the mesh a random quantity (delta). This quantity is obtained by the formula: delta=epsi dim alea() Where: - epsi is a number supplied by the user (1.e-8 for example) - dim is the dimension of the mesh in the direction concerned by the component (X, Y or Z) - alea() is a function returning a pseudo-random number in the interval - [-1,1]. Note: The possibility of modifying the coordinates of a mesh randomly is, a priori, a "developer" functionality. It is dangerous in certain situations: very flat mesh cells (joints, ...) 3.5 Keyword ORIE_PEAU > ◊ ORIE_PEAU= This keyword is used to reorient boundary mesh cells so that their normals are consistent (towards the outside of the material). This keyword is valid for a two-dimensional (2D) or three-dimensional (3D) study. It is an indispensable preliminary if, for example, one wishes to apply a pressure loading on this "skin". > ♦ GROUP_MA_PEAU= lgrma, [l_gr_ma] Mesh-cell groups to be reoriented. The mesh cells are oriented in such a way that the normal is outward. For each boundary mesh cell (edge or face), one looks for the "volume" mesh cell which it "borders". One orients it in such a way that its normal is in the opposite direction to the vector joining its first node to the barycentre of the volume mesh cell. It sometimes happens that the "skin" one wishes to orient is inserted in the material (for example, when one carries out an analysis for which mesh cells are progressively added to or removed from the model: modelling of an excavation, or of a construction by layers). The orientation algorithm described above then fails, because one generally finds 2 volume mesh cells on either side of the skin mesh cell. One does not then know which one to use to orient the skin mesh cell. For this purpose, the optional keyword GROUP_MA_INTERNE has been introduced. This keyword allows the user to specify which "internal" mesh cells are to be used to orient the skin mesh cells. Example: Let there be 1 skin mesh-cell group (GPEAU) which one wishes to orient with a normal directed outwards. One must indicate that it is the skin of the "volume" mesh-cell group GV2. One will write: ORIE_PEAU=_F(GROUP_MA_PEAU='GPEAU', GROUP_MA_INTERNE='GV2'), 3.6 Keyword ORIE_NORM_COQUE > ◊ ORIE_NORM_COQUE= _F( This keyword is used to check that, in a list of surface mesh cells (shells), the normals are consistent with one another. Otherwise, certain mesh cells are reoriented. > ♦ GROUP_MA= lgrma, [l_gr_ma] Groups of surface mesh cells to be reoriented. The mesh cells of lgrma must form a "connected" group in order that one may reorient them by continuity. One may impose the sense of the orientation by means of the keywords GROUP_NO/VECT_NORM. If one does not do so, the orientation retained will be that of the 1st mesh cell of lgrma, but this is not necessarily the 1st mesh cell of the 1st GROUP_MA! It is therefore recommended always to use the keyword VECT_NORM. > ◊ VECT_NORM= (n1, n2, [n3]), [l_R] ni: 2 or 3 components (according to the dimension) of the normal vector. One must also specify the support node of this normal: > ◊ GROUP_NO = grno, [gr_no] > grno must be a GROUP_NO containing only one node. > The normal chosen will be the one which makes an acute angle with the vector given by VECT_NORM. Note: if GROUP_NO is not given by the user, the code will automatically choose one of the nodes of GROUP_MA. One must therefore be careful in the definition of the latter, so that the normal is well defined over the whole set of mesh cells. In particular, one must avoid cases where the group does not define an almost plane topological zone. 3.7 Keyword ORIE_INTERF_POU > ◊ ORIE_INTERF_POU= _F( This keyword is used to check that, in a list of biquadratic volume mesh cells (HEXA27), the vector x in its parametric space is oriented along the direction and the sense of the axis passing through the nodes in positions 25 and 27 in the connectivity table of the element and forming an acute angle with the orientation vector VECT_ORIE. Otherwise, certain mesh cells are reoriented. > ♦ GROUP_MA= lgrma, [l_gr_ma] Groups of biquadratic volume mesh cells (HEXA27) to be reoriented. The mesh cells are not reoriented by continuity, each one being oriented individually. It is therefore not necessary that the mesh cells of lgrma form a "connected" group. The sense of the orientation is imposed by means of the keyword VECT_ORIE. > ♦ VECT_ORIE= (n1, n2, n3), [l_R] The axis chosen for the orientation is the one which makes an acute angle with the vector given by VECT_ORIE. 3.8 Keyword ORIE_LIGNE > ◊ ORIE_LIGNE= _F( This keyword is used to check that, in a list of line mesh cells (beams), the tangents are consistent with one another. Otherwise, certain mesh cells are reoriented. > ♦ GROUP_MA= lgrma, [l_gr_ma] Groups of line mesh cells to be reoriented. The mesh cells of lgrma must form a "connected" group in order that one may reorient them by continuity. One may impose the sense of the orientation by means of the keywords GROUP_NO/VECT_TANG. If one does not do so, the orientation retained will be that of the 1st mesh cell of lgrma, but this is not necessarily the first mesh cell of the first GROUP_MA! It is therefore recommended always to use the keyword VECT_TANG. > ◊ VECT_TANG= (n1, n2, [n3]), [l_R] ni: 2 or 3 components (according to the dimension) of the tangent vector. One must also specify the support node of this normal: > ◊ GROUP_NO = grno, [gr_no] > grno must be a GROUP_NO containing only one node. > The tangent chosen will be the one which makes an acute angle with the vector given by VECT_TANG. 3.9 Keyword MODI_MAILLE > ♦ OPTION= 'NOEUD_QUART' , Activates the displacement of the mid-edge nodes of the edges touching the crack front to a quarter of these edges (towards the crack front). > ♦ / GROUP_MA_FOND= lgma_fo, [l_gr_ma] / GROUP_NO_FOND= lgno_fo, [l_gr_no] In 2D, one enters the node of the crack front (by GROUP_NO_FOND). In 3D, one enters either the nodes of the crack front, or the SEG3 mesh cells of the crack front (and not the mesh cells of the lips of the crack or the material mesh cells backed against the front). 3.10 Keyword TRANSLATION Caution One may combine this functionality with ROTATION, but these operations are not commutative. The translation is always executed before the rotation. One cannot combine this functionality with SYMETRIE. ◊ TRANSLATION= (n1, n2, [:ref: n3 ]), [l_R] Simple keyword for the translation of a mesh along a vector. 3.11 Keyword ROTATION Caution One may combine this functionality with TRANSLATION, but these operations are not commutative. On the other hand, it is not allowed to use ROTATION, MODI_BASE and SYMETRIE at the same time. The translation is always executed before the rotation. ◊ ROTATION= Factor keyword for the rotation of a mesh about an arbitrary axis. > ♦ POIN_1 = (ni, n2, [n3]), [l_R] Coordinates of the first point used to define the axis of rotation. > ♦ / POIN_2 = (ni, n2, [n3]), [l_R] / DIR = (ni, n2, [:ref: n3 ]), [l_R] Coordinates of the second point or direction used to define the axis of rotation completely. ♦ ANGLE = a, [R] Angle of rotation expressed in degrees. The rotation is carried out in the positive direction, with respect to its oriented axis. This axis passes through the point POIN_1 and its orientation is given either by the vector DIR, or by the vector with origin POIN_1 and end POIN_2. The rotation is defined by: Let \text{M}(x,y,z) be a point in space; one imposes on it a rotation of angle \alpha (in radians) whose axis passes through \text{P}(\mathit{px},\mathit{py},\mathit{pz}) and has for direction \text{D}(\mathit{dx},\mathit{dy},\mathit{dz}) . Then \text{M} becomes \text{M}’ after the rotation: \text{M'}=\text{P}+\cos\alpha .\text{PM}+(1-\cos\alpha ).(\text{PM}.\text{D}).\text{D}+\sin\alpha (\text{D}\mathrm{\wedge }\text{PM}) 3.12 Keyword ECHELLE Caution This functionality may be used with TRANSLATION and ROTATION. The scaling, when it is requested, is always done after TRANSLATION and ROTATION. One cannot combine this functionality with SYMETRIE. ◊ ECHELLE= n1, [R] Simple keyword for the scaling of a mesh according to a real number. Let \text{M}(x,y,z) be a point of the mesh, it will become, by this transformation of ratio \mathit{n1} : \text{M}’(\mathit{n1}\cdot x,\mathit{n1}\cdot y,\mathit{n1}\cdot z) . 3.13 Keyword MODI_BASE Caution This functionality is not allowed with ROTATION and SYMETRIE. ◊ MODI_BASE= Factor keyword for the change of basis in which the coordinates of a mesh are expressed. The change of frame always takes place between 2 orthonormal bases. > ♦ VECT_X = (n1, n2, [n3]), [l_R] Coordinates of the first vector of the new basis, of arbitrary norm. > ◊ VECT_Y = (n1, n2, [n3]), [l_R] Coordinates of the second vector of the new basis (not used in 2D), also of arbitrary norm. In 2D, it is enough to give the axis VECT_X, and Code_Aster automatically constructs the second vector in order to define a direct orthogonal basis. A test checks whether VECT_X has a non-zero norm. In 3D, one checks that VECT_X and VECT_Y have a non-zero norm and one checks that they are orthogonal. The third vector which completes the basis is constructed as the cross product of VECT_X with VECT_Y. One thus ensures the construction of a direct orthogonal basis. Then, in all cases (2D and 3D), the vectors of the basis are normalised to 1; the user therefore does not have to worry about it. One therefore finally has a direct orthonormal basis. In 3D, one therefore expects the data of VECT_X and VECT_Y , the first two vectors of the new basis. The change of basis is then defined as: 3.14 Keyword SYMETRIE Caution One cannot combine this functionality with TRANSLATION, ROTATION, ECHELLE and MODI_BASE. ♦ POINT = (n1, n2, [:ref: n3 ]) [l_R] Coordinates of a point belonging to the straight line in 2D or to the plane in 3D. ♦ AXE_1 = (n1, n2, [:ref: n3 ]) [l_R] Direction vector of the straight line in 2D or 1st vector making it possible to describe the plane. ◊ AXE_2 = (n1, n2, n3) [l_R] 2nd vector making it possible to describe the plane. In 2D, the symmetry is carried out with respect to a straight line, which is in the plane \mathit{OXY} . In order to define this straight line one must give the direction vector of the straight line (AXE_1) and a point (POINT) belonging to this straight line. In 3D, the symmetry is carried out with respect to a plane. In order to define this plane, one must give 2 vectors of the plane (AXE_1, AXE_2) and a point (POINT) belonging to this plane. In all cases (2D or 3D), the symmetry is carried out with respect to a plane. In 2D, the second vector necessary for the definition of the plane is fixed at AXE_2 = (0.0, 0.0, -1.0). The algebraic distance \delta between a point \text{M}(x,y,z) and a plane passing through the point \text{Mo}(\mathit{xo},\mathit{yo},\mathit{zo}) with perpendicular vector \text{V}=\text{AXE\_1}\mathrm{\wedge }\text{AXE\_2}=(a,b,c) is: \delta =\frac{a(x-{x}_{0})+b(y-{y}_{0})+c(z-{z}_{0})}{\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+{c}^{2}}} The coordinates of the point \text{M}' symmetric to the point \text{M} with respect to the plane are given by: \mathit{OM}'=-2\delta .\frac{V}{\mathrm{\parallel }V\mathrm{\parallel }}+\mathit{OM} 3.15 Keyword ABSC_CURV ◊ ABSC_CURV = _F (...), Computes the curvilinear abscissa for the set of SEG mesh cells supplied via the keywords GROUP_MA or TOUT='OUI'. For each of the nodes of the mesh cells concerned, one computes its curvilinear abscissa taking account of its possible curvature. The keyword GROUP_NO_ORIG allows the user to choose the origin of the curvilinear abscissae (the node where the abscissa is zero). The origin must be one of the ends of the line on which one wishes to compute the curvilinear abscissa. This option is necessary, for example, in order to carry out a modal analysis for a tube with external and internal fluid, when the density of the external fluid is defined as a function of the curvilinear abscissa. Notes: - All the mesh cells concerned must be of type SEG2, SEG3 or SEG4. - Mesh cells of type SEG2 are considered to be straight and the mesh cells SEG3 and SEG4 are assumed to be in the shape of an arc of a circle.

u4.24.01 Operator DEFI_SQUELETTE u4.24.01 Operator DEFI_SQUELETTE 1 Purpose Define the visualisation mesh of the results of a dynamic substructuring. In the case of cyclic dynamic substructuring, the mesh is created by using all or part of the mesh cells (visualisation mesh) of the sector structure and then repeating it cyclically in order to reconstitute the global structure. In the case of general dynamic substructuring, the mesh is created by using all or part of the mesh cells (visualisation mesh) of the various substructures and then associating them so as to reconstitute the global structure. The mesh cells used (called visualisation mesh cells) are not necessarily the support of a finite element. This makes it possible to use a reduced number of visualisation mesh cells, different from the analysis mesh cells, and representing roughly the shape of the structure (skeleton). One may also create a skeleton from another skeleton, some nodes of the interfaces of which will be merged according to a proximity criterion. Restriction: the visualisation mesh cells must be defined from nodes supporting degrees of freedom of the analysis (there is no interpolation of the results). Warning: Use of the operand TOUT='OUI' can lead to serious performance problems. Always prefer the call that specifies the mesh-cell groups involved in the skeleton, particularly when the meshes of the substructures constitute only a small part of the complete mesh. This operator creates a data structure of type squelette. 2 Syntax squelette = DEFI_SQUELETTE( ◆ / CYCLIQUE = _F( ◆ / MODE_CYCL = mode_cycl, / MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ & NB_SECTEUR = int, ), / MODELE_GENE = modele_gene, / MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ / SECTEUR = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ), ◇ SQUELETTE = squelette, ◇ RECO_GLOBAL = _F( ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_NO_1 = grno, ◇ & SOUS_STRUC_1 = text, ◇ & SOUS_STRUC_2 = text, ◇ & GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ DIST_REFE = float, ), ◇ & NOM_GROUP_MA = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ SOUS_STRUC = text, ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ), / SOUS_STRUC = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ / GROUP_MA = grma, / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ), ◇ EXCLUSIF = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ TRANS = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Cyclic substructuring (factor keyword CYCLIQUE) 3.1.1 Operand MODE_CYCL ♦ MODE_CYCL = mocy Concept mode_cycl resulting from an analysis in cyclic substructuring. 3.1.2 Operand MAILLAGE/NB_SECTEUR ♦ MAILLAGE = mail Concept maillage_sdaster used to define the skeleton. It is accompanied by the keyword NB_SECTEUR, an integer which gives the number of repetitions of this mesh in order to obtain the complete structure of the skeleton. 3.1.3 Keyword SECTEUR ♦ SECTEUR Factor keyword for the creation of a skeleton from a result of type mode_cycl produced by MODE_ITER_CYCL U4.52.05. Makes it possible to define, on the base sector, the list of visualisation mesh cells which will be repeated cyclically. 3.1.3.1 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA ◊ / TOUT All the mesh cells of the mesh of the base sector will be visualisation mesh cells. ◊ / GROUP_MA = grma List of the visualisation mesh-cell groups of the base sector. 3.2 Classical substructuring 3.2.1 Operand MODELE_GENE ♦ MODELE_GENE = mogene Name of the modele_gene concept coming from DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02 defining the global structure on which one wishes to define the skeleton. 3.2.2 Keyword SOUS_STRUC ♦ SOUS_STRUC Factor keyword for the creation of a skeleton following an analysis by classical dynamic substructuring. Makes it possible to define, on each substructure of the generalised model, the list of visualisation mesh cells. 3.2.2.1 Operand NOM ◊ NOM = nom_struc Name of the substructure. It must be identical to one of the names of the substructures defining the generalised model (see DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02). 3.2.2.2 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA ◊ / TOUT All the mesh cells of the mesh of the substructure will be visualisation mesh cells. ◊ / GROUP_MA= grma List of the visualisation mesh-cell groups of the substructure. 3.3 Keywords SQUELETTE and RECO_GLOBAL The keyword SQUELETTE defines an initial concept of type squelette in which the nodes of the interfaces will be merged by the keyword RECO_GLOBAL, either all these nodes (TOUT= 'OUI'), or selectively a node group grno1 (operand GROUP_NO_1) of the substructure nom_sstru1 (operand SOUS_STRUC_1) with a node group grno2 (operand GROUP_NO_2) of the substructure nom_sstru2 (operand SOUS_STRUC_2). These substructures must belong to the concept of type modele_gene supplied by the operand MODELE_GENE. The skeleton modified by the merging will be the result of the operator DEFI_SQUELETTE. 3.3.1 Operands DIST_REFE / CRITERE / PRECISION The merging will be done according to a proximity criterion, either absolute (with respect to dist_ref) or relative (with respect to dist_ref prec). 3.4 Keyword NOM_GROUP_MA In the case where one modifies an initial concept of type squelette (entered by the keyword SQUELETTE) by a merging of the nodes of the interfaces (by means of the keyword RECO_GLOBAL), one may then recover mesh-cell groups (entered by the operand GROUP_MA) in the substructure nomsst (entered by the operand SOUS_STRUC) by assigning them a new mesh-cell group name (operand NOM) in the result skeleton. 3.5 Keyword EXCLUSIF In the case of an analysis by classical substructuring, only. By setting EXCLUSIF='OUI', one deletes from the final skeleton the mesh-cell groups coming from the initial meshes. 4 Example The command file which follows computes, by two substructuring methods, the bending modes of a plate clamped at its centre: - cyclic method, - classical method. Then, by the command DEFI_SQUELETTE, a visualisation mesh is created ( skeleton mesh). After the results have been expressed in physical space, the visualisation mesh and the results are written to a RESULTAT file in IDEAS format. 4.1 Command file # # CALCUL PAR SOUS-STRUCTURATION CYCLIQUE # # CALCUL DES MODES PROPRES CYCLIQUES # mod_cy = MODE_ITER_CYCL (BASE_MODALE= bamo, NB_MODE = 5, NB_SECTEUR = 4, LIAISON = _F(DROITE ='DROITE', GAUCHE ='GAUCHE'), CALCUL = _F(TOUT_DIAM ='OUI', NMAX_FREQ = 2), INFO = 1) # # CREATION DU MAILLAGE DE CALCUL # squel1 = DEFI_SQUELETTE (MODE_CYCL= mod_cy, SECTEUR = _F(GROUP_MA= ’CALCUL’)) # # CREATION DU MAILLAGE DE VISUALISATION # squel2 = DEFI_SQUELETTE (MODE_CYCL= mod_cy, SECTEUR = _F(GROUP_MA= ’VISUAL’)) # # RESTITUTION DES RESULTATS SUR LES MAILLAGES SQUELETTES # modgl1 = REST_SOUS_STRUC (RESU_GENE= mod_cy,SQUELETTE= squel1) modgl2 = REST_SOUS_STRUC (RESU_GENE= mod_cy,SQUELETTE= squel2) # … # CALCUL PAR SOUS-STRUCTURATION CLASSIQUE # # CALCUL DU MACRO-ELEMENT # macele = MACR_ELEM_DYNA (BASE_MODALE= bamo) # # CALCUL DU MODELE GENERALISE # modege = DEFI_MODELE_GENE ( SOUS_STRUC=_F(NOM='CARRE1', MACR_ELEM_DYNA= macele), SOUS_STRUC=_F(NOM='CARRE2', MACR_ELEM_DYNA= macele, ANGL_NAUT=(90., 0., 0.)), SOUS_STRUC=(NOM='CARRE3', MACR_ELEM_DYNA= macele, ANGL_NAUT=(180.,0.,0.)), SOUS_STRUC=(NOM='CARRE4', MACR_ELEM_DYNA= macele, ANGL_NAUT=(270., 0., 0.)), LIAISON=_F(SOUS_STRUC_1='CARRE1', SOUS_STRUC_2='CARRE2', INTERFACE_1 ='GAUCHE', INTERFACE_2 ='DROITE'), LIAISON=_F(SOUS_STRUC_1='CARRE2', SOUS_STRUC_2='CARRE3', INTERFACE_1 ='GAUCHE', INTERFACE_2 ='DROITE'), LIAISON=_F(SOUS_STRUC_1='CARRE3', SOUS_STRUC_2='CARRE4', INTERFACE_1 ='GAUCHE', INTERFACE_2 ='DROITE'), LIAISON=_F(SOUS_STRUC_1='CARRE4', SOUS_STRUC_2='CARRE1', INTERFACE_1 ='GAUCHE', INTERFACE_2='DROITE')) # … # CREATION DU MAILLAGE DE VISUALISATION squel = DEFI_SQUELETTE (MODELE_GENE=MODEGE SOUS_STRUC=_F(NOM ='CARRE1', GROUP_MA= ’VISUAL’), SOUS_STRUC=_F(NOM ='CARRE2', GROUP_MA= ’VISUAL’), SOUS_STRUC=_F(NOM ='CARRE3', GROUP_MA= ’VISUAL’), SOUS_STRUC=_F(NOM ='CARRE4', GROUP_MA= ’VISUAL’)) # # RESTITUTION DES RESULTATS SUR LE MAILLAGE SQUELETTE # modglo = REST_SOUS_STRUC ( RESU_GENE= resgen, SQUELETTE= squel) # 4.2 Graphical results Shown above are the analysis meshes and the skeleton of the clamped plate, with respectively the modal deformed shapes of the second mode.

u4.24.02 Operator DEFI_GRILLE u4.24.02 Operator DEFI_GRILLE 1 Purpose Define a grid from a mesh. A grid is a particular type of mesh for which the nodes are all aligned along the directions of a local basis. The operator produces a concept of type grille. 2 Syntax grille = DEFI_GRILLE( ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ INFO = / 0 (par défaut), / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE ♦ MAILLAGE = ma ma: mesh to be used for the definition of the grid The mesh ma must be regular, such that all its nodes are aligned along the directions of a local basis. This imposes restrictions on the type and the shape of the elements which may be used to define the mesh ma: one may use only QUAD4 elements of square or rectangular shape in 2D and HEXA8 elements of cubic or elongated shape in 3D. No restriction is imposed on the shape of the domain defined by the mesh ma, that is to say that the domain does not necessarily have to be a square or a rectangle in 2D and a cube or a parallelepiped in 3D. However, all the elements must be connected to one another and the domain cannot be formed by several parts which are not connected. The local basis of the grid, along which the nodes are aligned, is computed automatically. 3.2 Operand INFO | / 0 : | no printout in the file 'MESSAGE' | | --- | --- | | / 1 : | printout in the file 'MESSAGE': of the length of the shortest edge of the mesh ma of the computed local basis | | / 2 : | printout in the file 'MESSAGE': of the same information as for INFO=2 of the connection table and of the distances of the nodes of the grid |

u4.25.01 Operator DEFI_FLUI_STRU u4.25.01 Operator DEFI_FLUI_STRU 1 Purpose Define the characteristics necessary for the dynamic study of a structure under flow. By the choice of one of the factor keywords, the user specifies the type of "structure-flow" configuration studied: tube bundle under cross-flow or axial flow, control-rod cluster, coaxial shells. Depending on the type of configuration, the data supplied make it possible to carry out downstream: - a fluid/structure coupling study: estimation of the fluid-elastic force coefficients and computation of the new modal parameters of the structure by means of the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02, - the projection onto the modal basis under flow of one or more turbulent excitations defined by their spectral density (densities): operators DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31 and PROJ_SPEC_BASE U4.63.14. One may then compute the response of the structure to the turbulent excitation, in time and in frequency. The operator "DEFI_FLUI_STRU" produces a concept of type type_flui_stru intended to be used downstream by the operators FONC_FLUI_STRU U4.35.02, CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02 or, indirectly, PROJ_SPEC_BASE U4.63.14. 2 Syntax type_flui_stru = DEFI_FLUI_STRU( ◆ / FAISCEAU_TRANS = _F( ◇ COUPLAGE = / "OUI", / "NON", ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ PROF_VITE_FLUI = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ PROF_RHO_F_INT = défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS ♦ / FAISCEAU_TRANS Factor keyword making it possible to characterise a configuration of the type "tube bundle under cross-flow". If the study is based on the definition of several excitation zones, there must be as many occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS as there are zones. ◊ COUPLAGE = 'OUI' ou 'NON' Text-type indicator specifying whether or not the fluid-elastic forces are taken into account. This operand must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. ◊ CARA_ELEM = cara Concept of type [cara_elem] making it possible to supply all the data relating to the geometry of the elements of the structure: useful for the estimation of the hydraulic diameter. This operand must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. ♦ PROF_VITE_FLUI = profv Concept of type [fonction] making it possible to supply the non-dimensional profile of transverse velocity along the tube. The parameter of the function is the curvilinear abscissa. This operand must appear in all the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS. ◊ PROF_RHO_F_INT = profrhoi Concept of type [fonction] making it possible to supply the density profile of the fluid internal to the tube, along the tube. The parameter of the function is the curvilinear abscissa. This operand must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. ◊ PROF_RHO_F_EXT = profrhoe Concept of type [fonction] making it possible to supply the density profile of the fluid external to the tube, along the tube. The parameter of the function is the curvilinear abscissa. This operand must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. ◊ NOM_CMP = 'DX' ou 'DY' ou 'DZ' Text-type indicator [TXM] specifying the direction along which the fluid-elastic forces and/or the turbulent forces act. This operand must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. ◊ COEF_MASS_AJOU = cm Value of the added-mass coefficient cm. This operand, if it is used, may be defined in only one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. ◊ CSTE_CONNORS = cste List of two reals defining the interval of the Connors constants for the method of the same name (see R4.07.04). ◊ RHO_TUBE = rho Density of the tube for the Connors method ◊ NB_CONNORS = nb , [I] Number of discretisation points inside the interval defined by the keyword CSTE_CONNORS presented above. ◊ / ◊ TYPE_PAS = 'CARRE_LIGN' ou 'TRIA_LIGN' Text-type indicator [TXM] making it possible to specify the type of pitch of the bundle, defined by the arrangement of the tubes with respect to one another and by the direction of the flow with respect to the bundle. This operand may appear in only one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. 'CARRE_LIGN' = pas carré ligne. 'TRIA_LIGN' = pas triangulaire ligne. ♦ TYPE_RESEAU = tr Integer indicator, strictly less than 1000 and positive, defining the experimental configuration for which the coupling coefficients used for the study were obtained [bib1]. This operand must appear in all the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS. Note: "tr" must appear in two files «cd.70» and «ck.71» which make it possible to describe the evolution of the damping and of the stiffness added by the flow as a function of the reduced velocity {V}_{r} , the latter being computed from the inter-tube velocity. The files «cd.70» and «ck.71» are read on logical units 70 and 71. They both have the following structure: Line 1 of the file : number of correlations present in the whole file (integer) then, for each of these correlations, a block composed of Line 1 of the block : type of pitch of the array associated with the correlation (1 if TYPE_PAS=«CARRE_LIGN» , 2 if TYPE_PAS=«TRIA_LIGN») Line 2 of the block : tr (integer supplied for the operand «TYPE_RESEAU») Line 3 of the block : nbplages (number of contiguous ranges of reduced velocity over which the added damping and stiffness have been interpolated by the user in polynomial form) Line 4 of the block : nbplages reals, followed by two reals A and B; the first nbplages reals correspond to the reduced-velocity values — ordered by increasing order — of the lower bounds of the contiguous nbplages; the two reals A and B are respectively the smallest and the largest values of reduced velocity for which the added damping and stiffness have been determined experimentally on a test rig in thermohydraulic similarity; they therefore bound the range of reduced velocities inside which the correlation may be interpolated from the values identified on the test rig. In general, one therefore chooses the first of the nbplages reals equal to A and the last of the nbplages reals equal to B . Following Nbplages lines : each line corresponds to the polynomial interpolation of the damping correlation or of the added stiffness in the range considered, the first range of reduced velocities extending between the first and the second of the nbplages reals. On each line, 11 coefficients are to be supplied. These coefficients are the {({\alpha}_{i})}_{1\le i\le 11} defining the polynomial used for the interpolation in the range considered. Thus, for example, {C}_{d} denoting the damping added by the flow. The expression which will be taken into account as a function of the reduced velocity is the following {V}_{r} (the expression for the added stiffness is analogous): {C}_{d}({V}_{r})=\sum_{i=1}^{11}{\alpha}_{i}{V}_{r}^{(i-4)} Following line: a line making it possible to delimit the blocks associated with each correlation, in general of the form: « » end of the block If there are other correlations, Line 1 of the block corresponding to the next correlation. On the basis of a certain number of tests, EDF has developed and validated a set of fluid-elastic correlations making it possible to simulate the damping and the stiffness added to a structure by a flow. The supply of these correlations in the form of two files of a format consistent with that specified above will be studied case by case according to the request. ◊ UNITE_CA = iu1 Number of the logical unit in which the file «cd.70» of the dampings added by the flow is written. ◊ UNITE_KA = iu2 Number of the logical unit in which the file «cd.71» of the stiffnesses added by the flow is written. ◊ PAS = pas Value of the reduced pitch of the bundle: ratio between, on the one hand, the centre-to-centre distance between 2 neighbouring tubes, and on the other hand the outside diameter of the tubes. This operand may appear in only one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS, and may be omitted in the others. 3.2 Keyword GRAPPE ♦ / GRAPPE Factor keyword making it possible to characterise a configuration of the type "control-rod cluster". ♦ COUPLAGE = 'OUI' ou 'NON' Text-type indicator [TXM] specifying the taking into account of the fluid-elastic forces. The fluid-elastic coupling, if it is taken into account, involves the non-dimensional fluid-elastic force coefficients identified on the GRAPPE2 mock-up, which are used to represent a resultant force and a resultant moment [bib2]. If COUPLAGE = 'OUI', the following operands must obligatorily be supplied, with the exception of COEF_MASS_AJOU which remains optional. ◊ / ♦ GRAPPE_2 = 'ASC_CEN' ou 'ASC_EXC' ou 'DES_CEN' ou 'DES_EXC' Four possible choices corresponding to the various experimental configurations for which the fluid-elastic force coefficients have been identified: - AScending flow, control rod CENtred; - AScending flow, control rod off-centre (EXCentred); - DEScending flow, control rod CENtred; - DEScending flow, control rod off-centre (EXCentred). ♦ GROUP_NO = grno Identifier of the node where the resultant force and the resultant moment representing the action of the fluid-elastic forces are applied. ♦ CARA_ELEM = cara Concept of type [cara_elem] supplying all the data relating to the geometry of the elements of the structure: useful for the estimation of the diameter of the control rod. This concept provides, among other things, the information relating to the orientations of the elements. ♦ MODELE = modele Concept of type [modele] supplying the information relating to the types of the elements of the structure. ◊ COEF_MASS_AJOU = cm1 Value of the added-mass coefficient due to the local confinement of the control rod at the housing plate. If the modal characteristics in water at rest of the structure have been computed with the equivalent density. {\rho}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\alpha \frac{\pi {D}^{2}}{\mathrm{4S}}{\rho}_{\mathrm{eau}}+{\rho}_{\mathrm{poutre}} The coefficient cm1 of added mass due to the local confinement at the housing plate is given by the relation: \text{cm1}=\frac{\pi (-\alpha )}{2} where D denotes the outside diameter of the rod; S is the area of the straight section of the tube and H represents the thickness of the fluid film at the confinement. Note: When the user does not supply the operand COEF_MASS_AJOU, cm1 is estimated automatically by means of this expression with \alpha =1 . ♦ RHO_FLUI = rho_f Value of the density of the fluid surrounding the structure. 3.3 Keyword FAISCEAU_AXIAL ♦ / FAISCEAU_AXIAL Factor keyword making it possible to characterise a configuration of the type "tube bundle under axial flow" [bib2]. Note: In the case where the study is carried out by means of a representation of the complete bundle, only one occurrence is allowed for this factor keyword. If the study is based on a simplified representation, there must be as many occurrences as there are tubes in the simplified bundle. Each tube of the simplified bundle defines an equivalence class for the tubes of the real bundle. The characteristics of the tubes of the real bundle for one and the same equivalence class (common radius, positions) are the subject of one occurrence of the factor keyword. In order to be able to use a simplified representation of the bundle, the modal basis computed in air must be equivalent to the complete modal basis in air of the real bundle; each tube of the simplified bundle must therefore be a tube equivalent to each class of real tubes. For example, for a class of N real tubes, of Young's modulus E and of density \rho , a possible equivalent tube is characterised by a Young's modulus \mathit{NE} and a density N\rho . ♦ / GROUP_MA = l_grma In the case where the study concerns the complete bundle: list of the mesh-cell groups corresponding to the tubes of the bundle (concepts of type [group_ma]). In the case where the study is based on a simplified representation: the use of this operand is mandatory and excludes recourse to TRI_GROUP_MA. One expects a concept of type [group_ma] corresponding to one of the equivalent tubes of the simplified bundle. / TRI_GROUP_MA = 'racine ' ou ' racine ' ou ' racine' Text-type argument [TXM] defining the root of the names of the mesh-cell groups corresponding to the tubes of the bundle. The use of this operand is licit only in the case where the study is carried out by means of a representation of the complete bundle. The root may be a prefix, an intermediate character string or a suffix. ♦ VECT_X = l_comp List of three reals giving the components of the direction vector of the bundle in the global frame. The bundle having to be oriented along one of the axes of the global frame, only three sets of components are acceptable: (1.,0.,0.) , (0.,1.,0.) or (0.,0.,1.) . This operand is mandatory if the study concerns the complete bundle, and must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword if the study is based on a simplified representation. ♦ PROF_RHO_FLUI = profrho Concept of type [fonction] defining the density profile of the fluid surrounding the tubes. The parameter of the function is the space coordinate corresponding to the axis of the global frame directing the tube bundle. This operand is mandatory if the study concerns the complete bundle, and must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword if the study is based on a simplified representation. ♦ PROF_VISC_CINE = profvisc Concept of type [fonction] defining the kinematic-viscosity profile of the fluid surrounding the tubes. The parameter of the function is the space coordinate corresponding to the axis of the global frame directing the tube bundle. This operand is mandatory if the study concerns the complete bundle, and must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword if the study is based on a simplified representation. ♦ / CARA_ELEM = cara Concept of type [cara_elem] supplying all the data relating to the geometry of the elements of the structure: radius of each of the tubes. This concept is to be supplied only in the case where the study concerns the complete bundle. / ♦ RAYON_TUBE = rayon Radius of the tubes of the real bundle for one and the same equivalence class. This operand is used only in the case where the study is based on a simplified representation. ♦ COOR_TUBE = l_coor List of the coordinates of the centres of the tubes of the real bundle belonging to one and the same equivalence class. This operand is used only in the case where the study is based on a simplified representation. ◊ PESANTEUR = l_g List of four reals defining the norm and the orientation of the gravity vector g in the global frame. One must supply, in order, the data (g,{a}_{p},{b}_{p},{c}_{p}) such that: g=g\frac{{a}_{p}X+{b}_{p}Y+{c}_{p}Z}{\sqrt{{a}_{p}^{2}+{b}_{p}^{2}+{c}_{p}^{2}}} The default values are: g=9.81 ; {a}_{p}=0. ; {b}_{p}=0. ; {c}_{p}=–1. ♦ RUGO_TUBE = rug Value of the absolute roughness of the walls of the tubes, used for the estimation of the axial friction coefficient. This operand is mandatory if the study concerns the complete bundle, and must appear in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword if the study is based on a simplified representation. A characteristic value for a smooth steel is 10–5 metre. ♦ CARA_PAROI = l_cara List of text-type arguments [TXM] giving the names of the geometrical characteristics of the enclosure surrounding the bundle. The licit arguments are the following: - 'YC' , 'ZC' and 'R' in the case of a circular enclosure: 'YC' , 'ZC' coordinates of the centre in any plane x={x}_{0} along the axes of the global frame perpendicular to the bundle and ordered so that (X, Y, Z) is direct if X is the axis of the global frame oriented along the bundle. 'R' radius. 'YC' , 'ZC' , 'HY' and 'HZ' in the case of a rectangular enclosure: 'YC' , 'ZC' coordinates of the centre in any plane x={x}_{0} . 'HY' , 'HZ' dimensions of the sides of the enclosure parallel respectively to the directions Y and Z. ♦ VALE_PAROI = l_vale List of reals giving the values of the geometrical characteristics, in correspondence with the list of names received for CARA_PAROI. ◊ ANGL_VRIL = alpha Angle of rotation (in degrees) about the direction axis of the bundle for a rectangular enclosure. This operand is mandatory if one defines a rectangular enclosure by CARA_PAROI and VALE_PAROI. It is forbidden in the case of a circular enclosure. Note: The operands CARA_PAROI and VALE_PAROI are mandatory when the study concerns the complete bundle. When the study is based on a simplified representation, these operands must appear together in at least one of the occurrences of the factor keyword FAISCEAU_AXIAL. The operand ANGL_VRIL must also be present under the same occurrence if one defines a rectangular enclosure. Example: Global frame (x,y,z) axis of the bundle y Note: In the case where the study is carried out taking into account the grids of the tube bundle, the user must supply each of the eight operands which follow. Recall that the geometry of a grid is a prismatic array with a square base. There may exist several types of grid; for example, the end grids and the mixing grids in the fuel assemblies. The grids of one and the same type are characterised by identical dimensions and coefficients. ◊ LONG_TYPG= l_hg List of reals giving the lengths of each type of grid of the tube bundle. The length of a grid is its dimension along the direction of the bundle. ◊ LARG_TYPG= l_dg List of reals giving the widths of each type of grid. The width of a grid is its dimension in the plane perpendicular to the axis of the bundle (that is to say the length of the side of the array). ◊ EPAIS_TYPG= l_tg List of reals giving the thicknesses of each type of grid. What is called the thickness of a grid is the thickness of the array constituting the grid in a section perpendicular to the axis of the bundle. Example of a grid: Global frame (x,y,z) axis of the bundle y ◊ RUGO_TYPG= l_rugg List of reals giving the roughness height of each type of grid. These roughnesses are used for the estimation of the axial friction coefficient of each grid. ◊ COEF_TRAI_TYPG= l_cdg List of reals giving the drag coefficient of each type of grid. These drag coefficients make it possible to compute the drag forces exerted by each grid on the axial flow of the fluid. ◊ COEF_DPOR_TYPG= l_cpg List of reals giving the slope (at zero incidence) of the lift coefficient of each type of grid, which is assumed to be slightly inclined. These coefficients make it possible to compute the lift forces exerted by each grid on the flow of the fluid. ◊ COOR_GRILLE= l_zg List of the coordinates y (along the axis of the bundle) of the discretisation points of each of the grids. These coordinates correspond to the mid-points (at mid-length) of the grids. ◊ TYPE_GRILLE= l_itypg List of integers defining the type of each of the grids. 3.4 Keyword COQUE_COAX ♦ / COQUE_COAX Factor keyword making it possible to characterise a configuration made up of two coaxial cylindrical shells separated by an annular gap in which a fluid flows [bib2]. ◊ MASS_AJOU = 'OUI' ou 'NON' Text-type indicator [TXM] by which the user specifies whether or not the added-mass effects are taken into account, in addition to the added damping and stiffness effects. ♦ GROUP_MA_INT = gr_ma_i Identifier of the mesh-cell group (concept of type [group_ma]) corresponding to the internal shell. ♦ GROUP_MA_EXT = gr_ma_e Identifier of the mesh-cell group (concept of type [group_ma]) corresponding to the external shell. ♦ VECT_X = l_comp List of three reals giving the components of the direction vector of the axis of revolution of the two shells in the global frame. The axis of revolution of the shells having to be one of the axes of the global frame, only three sets of components are acceptable: (1.,0.,0.) , (0.,1.,0.) or (0.,0.,1.) . ♦ CARA_ELEM = cara Concept of type [cara_elem] providing all the geometrical characteristics of the elements. ♦ MATER_INT = mater_i Concept of type [mater] providing all the physical quantities (grandeurs) characteristic of the constituent material of the internal structure. ♦ MATER_EXT = mater_e Concept of type [mater] providing all the physical quantities (grandeurs) characteristic of the constituent material of the external structure. ♦ RHO_FLUI = rho_f Density of the fluid. ♦ VISC_CINE = visco Kinematic viscosity of the fluid. ♦ RUGOSITE = rug Absolute wall roughness of the shells. A characteristic value for a smooth steel is 10–5 metre. ♦ PDC_MOY_1 = cde Steady (mean) part of the coefficient of singular inlet head losses. ♦ PDC_DYN_1 = cdep Unsteady (dynamic) part of the coefficient of singular inlet head losses. ♦ PDC_MOY_2 = cds Steady (mean) part of the coefficient of singular outlet head losses. ♦ PDC_DYN_2 = cdsp Unsteady (dynamic) part of the coefficient of singular outlet head losses. Notes: | | The values of the various mean and dynamic singular head-loss coefficients are given, as further information, for various usual geometrical inlet and outlet configurations (see below [§6]). | | --- | --- | | | By convention, a positive mean flow velocity means that the flow is in the direction of increasing space parameter along the axis of revolution of the structures. Conversely, a negative mean flow velocity means that the flow is in the direction of decreasing space parameter. The sign of the mean flow velocity therefore fixes the inlet and outlet positions. So that there is no ambiguity about these positions, one will take care in CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.80.03 to define a range of velocities of the same sign. | | | The model MOCCA_COQUE used for the resolution of the fluid-structure coupling requires, for each mode retained, identification of the shell order on the deformed shape. The identifiable shell orders {k}_{i} are such that: {k}_{i}\le \frac{N}{2} where N denotes the number of nodes of the mesh on a circumference, i.e. at a fixed elevation. The shell orders {k}_{i} precisely identified are such that {k}_{i}\le \frac{N}{4} , with the same definition for N . It is recommended to use a mesh with at least 20 nodes on the circumferences of the shells. A minimum number of 8 nodes is required. | 3.5 Keyword INFO ◊ INFO = 1 ou 2 Printout level. If INFO = 2 one prints the characteristics of the configuration in the file MESSAGE. If INFO = 1 there is no printout. 4 Further information concerning configurations of the type "tube bundles under cross-flow" The four operands TYPE_PAS, TYPE_RESEAU, PAS and COEF_MASS_AJOU are optional. No value is taken by default. When these characteristics are defined, three possibilities of use are offered: - TYPE_PAS , TYPE_RESEAU and PAS are present. COUPLAGE = 'OUI' The fluid-elastic forces will be taken into account during a dynamic analysis. The added-mass coefficient is computed as a function of the pitch and of the type of pitch. - TYPE_PAS , TYPE_RESEAU , PAS and COEF_MASS_AJOU are present. COUPLAGE = 'OUI' The fluid-elastic forces will be taken into account during a dynamic analysis. The added-mass coefficient is defined by the user. - COEF_MASS_AJOU is present. COUPLAGE = 'NON' Only the added mass due to the fluid is taken into account (no coupling). 5 Further information concerning the configurations "coaxial cylindrical shells" The values of the singular head-loss coefficients are supplied below for a few particular inlet-outlet geometrical configurations. 5.1 Coefficients of singular inlet head losses Configuration (1) \mathrm{cde}=0,5 \mathrm{cdep}=0 Configuration (2) \mathrm{cde}=0,5(1-\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{1}{H}_{1}}) \mathrm{cdep}=0 Configuration (3) \mathrm{cde}=0 \mathrm{cdep}=0 Configuration (4) \mathrm{cde}={(1-\frac{{R}_{1}{H}_{1}}{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}})}^{2}{(\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{1}{H}_{1}})}^{2}={(\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{1}{H}_{1}}-1)}^{2} \mathrm{cdep}=0 Configuration (5) \mathrm{cde}=0,5(1-\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{1}{H}_{1}}) \mathrm{cdep}=\frac{\mathrm{cde}}{{H}_{1}} 5.2 Coefficients of singular outlet head losses Configuration (1) \mathrm{cds}=1 \mathrm{cdsp}=0 Configuration (2) \mathrm{cds}={(1-\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{3}{H}_{3}})}^{2} \mathrm{cdsp}=0 Configuration (3) \mathrm{cds}=0 \mathrm{cdsp}=0 Configuration (4) \mathrm{cds}=0,5(1-\frac{{R}_{3}{H}_{3}}{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}){(\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{3}{H}_{3}})}^{2} \mathrm{cdsp}=0 Configuration (5) \mathrm{cds}=0,5{(1-\frac{{R}_{2}{H}_{2}}{{R}_{3}{H}_{3}})}^{2} \mathrm{cdsp}=\frac{-2\mathrm{cds}}{{H}_{3}} 6 Bibliography 1.
