LAINET: Integration of various models of fluid-elastic excitations into Code_Aster : specifications HT-32/96/014/A.

u4.26.01 Operator DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE u4.26.01 Operator DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE 1 Purpose Within the framework of a multifibre modelling, there are two "levels" of modelling: - the so-called "longitudinal" modelling represented by a beam (with geometrical support SEG2) - the plane modelling of the section (perpendicularly to the SEG2). The operator DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE makes it possible to define the geometry of the fibre groups which will be used in the definition of the cross-section by means of the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. The fibres may be described either by means of a plane mesh previously read by the operator LIRE_MAILLAGE (keyword SECTION) and/or in the form of "point" surfaces (keyword FIBRE or ASSEMBLAGE_FIBRE). Each occurrence of SECTION, FIBRE or ASSEMBLAGE_FIBRE defines a set of fibres which must be named in a unique way. A set of fibres will have the same constitutive behaviour for all its fibres, defined by means of DEFI_COMPOR. The command creates a data structure of type geom_fibre. Caution: With the information given in SECTION or FIBRE, it is possible to compute the majority of the integrated characteristics of the straight sections (area, static and quadratic moments). However, it is not possible to compute the torsional and warping inertias, nor the position of the centre of torsion. These quantities (grandeurs) must be given to the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. If the fibres are defined from a mesh, the operator MACR_CARA_POUTRE makes it possible to read this mesh and to compute all the characteristics. The result of this operator is a table which may be used as input to the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 2 Syntax gfibre = DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE( ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◆ | SECTION = _F( ◆ GROUP_FIBRE = text, ◆ | TOUT_SECT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA_SECT = grma, ◆ MAILLAGE_SECT = maillage, ◆ COOR_AXE_POUTRE = float, ◇ ANGLE = float, ), | FIBRE = _F( ◆ GROUP_FIBRE = text, ◇ CARA = / "SURFACE" (par défaut), / "DIAMETRE", ◆ VALE = float, ◆ COOR_AXE_POUTRE = float, ◇ ANGLE = float, ), ◇ ASSEMBLAGE_FIBRE = _F( ◆ GROUP_ASSE_FIBRE = text, ◆ GROUP_FIBRE = text, ◆ COOR_GROUP_FIBRE = float, ◆ GX_GROUP_FIBRE = float, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand INFO ◊INFO If the value of INFO is 2, the operator prints in the file 'MESSAGE', for each occurrence of the keywords SECTION or FIBRE, the characteristics of each fibre (position and area). Note: All the characteristics are given with respect to the axis defined in the operand COOR_AXE_POUTRE, calling the coordinates of the section x (horizontal) and y (vertical). 3.2 Keywords SECTION and FIBRE ♦|SECTION |FIBRE Define the entities of the beam mesh concerned and the sections which are assigned to them. The keyword SECTION makes it possible to assign a section defined by a plane mesh (the elements of this mesh are the sections of the fibres). The numbering of the fibres depends entirely on the mesh and on the type of mesh cells (quadrangle or triangle). The keyword FIBRE makes it possible to assign a section in which the fibres are defined by "points". The fibres are numbered from 1 to n in the order in which they were defined. In the presence of both keywords, the numbering of the fibres will begin with the fibres defined under the keyword SECTION and then those defined under the keyword FIBRE. In order to obtain it, it is possible to set INFO=2 in DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE. Note: At present the number of fibre groups on a beam element is limited to 10. 3.2.1 Operands common to SECTION and FIBRE ♦GROUP_FIBRE This operand makes it possible to define a name for the fibre group (24 characters). This name will be used in the operator DEFI_COMPOR to assign a material and a constitutive behaviour to this fibre group. Recall that all the fibres defined by one occurrence of SECTION or FIBRE will have the same constitutive behaviour. ◊COOR_AXE_POUTRE=(xg,yg) This operand makes it possible to define the coordinates of the axis of the beam in the frame of the straight section. The integrations (static moments or moments of inertia) will be carried out with respect to this axis. The default position is (\mathrm{0.0,}0.0) . ◊ANGLE=angle This operand makes it possible to define the angle of rotation of the frame in which the mesh is defined, in order to make it correspond to the principal frame of the beam. This rotation is always carried out after COOR_AXE_POUTRE. The default angle is 0.0 . When the coordinates of the fibres are given either by a mesh (keyword SECTION) or by triplets of values (keyword FIBRE), they are in a frame which is not linked to the beam. This makes it possible to define complex sections without being obliged to define them in the principal frame of inertia of the beam. It is easier to parameterise the mesh of an angle section (figure) in the frame ({x}_{1,}{y}_{1}) than in the frame ({x}_{2,}{y}_{2}) . The mesh of the section is in the plane \mathit{XY} . Figure 3.2.1-a: Angle section. The characteristics of the beams (section, inertias, ...) are defined in the principal frame of inertia; it is therefore necessary to establish the relation between the frame in which the fibres are defined and the principal frame of inertia of the beam. The keyword COOR_AXE_POUTRE makes it possible to define the translation of the frame linked to the mesh of the section in order to make it correspond to that of the beam. The keyword ANGLE makes it possible to rotate the mesh of the section in order to make it correspond to that of the beam. In the example of the angle section (figure), in order to make the mesh correspond to the principal frame of the beam section, both keywords must be supplied: - COOR_AXE_POUTRE = ( xg , yg ) - ANGLE= -90 3.2.2 Operands specific to SECTION The fibre group is defined by a set of "surface" fibres. ♦MAILLAGE_SECT Name of the plane "mesh" which contains the "description of the section". By "mesh", one means a set of 3-node triangular mesh cells and/or 4-node quadrilateral mesh cells. By "description of the section", one means a part of this "mesh" specified by one of the operands TOUT_SECT or GROUP_MA_SECT. Each mesh cell represents the section of a fibre. ♦/TOUT_SECT /GROUP_MA_SECT | Operands | Contents / Meaning | | --- | --- | | TOUT_SECT | The section is defined by all the mesh cells of the mesh defined under MAILLAGE_SECT | | GROUP_MA_SECT | The section is defined by a list of mesh-cell groups | Notes: Since it does not serve as a support for finite elements, the "mesh" does not necessarily have to have a connectivity; it may be composed of a set of mesh cells placed side by side or not. The coordinates x and y of the plane mesh of the section ( x horizontal, y vertical) are defined in a plane perpendicular to the axis of the beam. In order to define the twist angle, that is to say the angle between the axis x of the plane mesh of the section and the axis Y of the beam element, one must use the keyword ORIENTATION of the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 3.2.3 Operands specific to FIBRE The fibre group is defined by a set of "point" fibres. ◊CARA = 'SURFACE' | 'DIAMETRE' Makes it possible to specify whether the third value given for each fibre is the area or the diameter (see VALE). ♦VALE Each fibre is described by a triplet of values: (x,y,\mathit{val}) It is necessary to give the values in this sequence, as many triplets as there are fibres. - x and y are the coordinates of the centre of the fibre in a plane perpendicular to the axis of the beam. - \mathrm{val} is either the area of a fibre, or the diameter of a cylindrical fibre. The position of the frame may be modified by means of COOR_AXE_POUTRE. In order to give a twist angle, one must use the keyword ORIENTATION of the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 3.3 Keyword ASSEMBLAGE_FIBRE This keyword makes it possible to define an assembly of fibre groups. The kinematics linking the various fibre groups is particular and is used to account for phenomena specific to the modelling of fuel assemblies, cf. R3.08.08 Multifibre beam element (straight). ♦GROUP_ASSE_FIBRE This operand makes it possible to define a name for the fibre-assembly group (24 characters). This name will be used in the operator DEFI_COMPOR to assign a material and a constitutive behaviour to this fibre-assembly group. Recall that all the fibres defined by one occurrence of GROUP_ASSE_FIBRE will have the same constitutive behaviour. ♦GROUP_FIBRE This operand makes it possible to define the list of the names of the fibre groups which will constitute the fibre assembly. The names of the groups are defined either by SECTION/GROUP_FIBRE or by FIBRE/GROUP_FIBRE. ♦COOR_GROUP_FIBRE This operand makes it possible to define the coordinates of the centre of gravity of the fibre groups defined under the keyword GROUP_FIBRE. It is a list of reals (x1, y1, …, xn, yn) which is twice as long as the list given under GROUP_FIBRE. The coordinates of the fibre groups are translated by (xi, yi). ♦GX_GROUP_FIBRE This operand makes it possible to define the torsion coefficient of the fibre groups defined under the keyword GROUP_FIBRE. It is a list of reals (gx1, …, gxn) which has the same length as the list given under GROUP_FIBRE. 4 Example One wishes to build a reinforced-concrete beam section, with two cylindrical steel reinforcements, of diameter 32. One creates a data structure named GF comprising two fibre groups: - one is named SBET, and is created with a plane mesh, - the other is named SACI, and is created with two point fibres for the steels. MASEC1 = LIRE_MAILLAGE(UNITE = 21) GF=DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE( SECTION=_F(GROUP_FIBRE=’SBET’, MAILLAGE_SECT=MASEC1, TOUT_SECT=’OUI’, COOR_AXE_POUTRE=(0., 0.),), FIBRE=_F(GROUP_FIBRE=’SACI’, CARA=’DIAMETRE’, VALE=( 0.05, -0.2, 32.E-3, -0.05, -0.2, 32.E-3), COOR_AXE_POUTRE=(0., 0.),), )

u4.31.01 Operator DEFI_CONSTANTE u4.31.01 Operator DEFI_CONSTANTE 1 Purpose Define the value of an invariant quantity (grandeur). This operator is a convenience offered whenever a concept of type fonction is expected and the datum to be introduced is constant. This makes it possible to define, for example, materials with characteristics independent of the temperature, for commands which make it possible to treat materials with characteristics that vary with the temperature. Take care not to confuse this with the definition of a real parameter (e.g.: a = 3.). 2 Syntax fonction = DEFI_CONSTANTE( ◇ NOM_RESU = text (défaut: "TOUTRESU"), ◆ VALE = float, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NOM_RESU ◊ NOM_RESU = nr Designates the name of the result; the function thus created is a function whose value has the name nr (8 characters maximum). Note: Some commands (CALC_FONCTION, DEFI_MATERIAU…) check the consistency of the names of the parameter and of the result according to their context. 3.2 Operand VALE ♦ VALE = v Value of the constant (real number). 3.3 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = ti Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 4 Examples - Define the constant function "1.": F_UN = DEFI_CONSTANTE ( VALE = 1. ) The function F_UN represents "any kind of result" (TOUTRESU) by default - Define a constant function representing a constant Young's modulus F_YOUNG = DEFI_CONSTANTE ( VALE = 2.1E11 , NOM_RESU = 'E' )

u4.31.02 Operator DEFI_FONCTION u4.31.02 Operator DEFI_FONCTION 1 Purpose Define a real or complex function of a real variable. This operator makes it possible to define, for example, material characteristics as a function of temperature, or boundary conditions which depend on a space variable or on time. The concept produced by this operator is of type fonction. 2 Syntax / fonction_c / fonction = DEFI_FONCTION( ◆ NOM_PARA = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", / "DTAN", / "TEMP", / "TSEC", / "INST", / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "EPSI", / "META", / "FREQ", / "PULS", / "DSP", / "AMOR", / "ABSC", / "SIGM", / "HYDR", / "SECH", / "PORO", / "SAT", / "IRRA", / "PGAZ", / "PCAP", / "PLIQ", / "PVAP", / "PAD", / "VITE", / "ENDO", / "NORM", / "EPAIS", / "EXCENT", / "NEUT1", / "NEUT2", / "NEUT3", / "NEUT4", / "XF", / "YF", / "ZF", / "NUME_ORDRE", ◇ NOM_RESU = text (défaut: "TOUTRESU"), ◆ / VALE = float, / VALE_C = float, / VALE_PARA = listr8, / NOEUD_PARA = no, / ABSCISSE = float, # Si: exists("VALE_PARA") ◆ VALE_FONC = listr8, # Si: exists("ABSCISSE") ◆ ORDONNEE = float, # Si: exists("NOEUD_PARA") ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◆ VALE_Y = float, ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ VERIF = / "CROISSANT" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = np Designates the name of the parameter (variable or abscissa) of the function. The possible values for np are: | ’ABSC’: | Curvilinear abscissa | | --- | --- | | ’AMOR’: | Damping | | ’DRX’: | Rotation about the x-axis | | ’DRY’: | Rotation about the y-axis | | ’DRZ’: | Rotation about the z-axis | | ’DSP’: | | | ’DX’: | Displacement along the x-axis | | ’DY’: | Displacement along the x-axis | | ’DZ’: | Displacement along the x-axis | | ’ENDO’: | Damage | | ’EPAIS’: | Thickness | | ’EPSI’: | Strain | | ’FREQ’: | Frequency | | ’HYDR’: | Hydration | | ’INST’: | Time instant | | ’META’: | | | ’NEUT1’: | Neutral parameter 1 | | ’NEUT2’: | Neutral parameter 2 | | ’NEUT3’: | Neutral parameter 3 | | ’NORM’: | | | ’NUME_ORDRE’: | Order number | | ’PAD’: | | | ’PCAP’: | Capillary pressure | | ’PGAZ’: | Gas pressure | | ’PLIQ’: | Liquid pressure | | ’PORO’: | Porosity | | ’PULS’: | Pulsation | | ’PVAP’: | Vapour pressure | | ’SAT’: | Saturation | | ’SECH’: | Drying | | ’SIGM’: | Stress | | ’TEMP’: | Temperature | | ’TSEC’: | | | ’VITE’: | Velocity | | ’X’: | x-coordinate | | ’Y’: | y-coordinate | | ’Z’: | z-coordinate | | ’XF’: | Final x-coordinate, in the case of a follower loading. | | ’YF’: | Final y-coordinate, in the case of a follower loading. | | ’ZF’: | Final z-coordinate, in the case of a follower loading. | | VITE_[X\|Y\|Z] | Velocity of the structure, in the case of a follower loading. | | ACCE_[X\|Y\|Z] | Acceleration of the structure, in the case of a follower loading. | 3.2 Operand NOM_RESU ◊ NOM_RESU = nr Designates the name of the result (8 characters). The function thus created is nr = f(np). Note: Some commands (CALC_FONCTION, DEFI_MATERIAU…) check the consistency of the names of the parameter and of the result according to their context. For example, one expects a tension curve defined by a function for which NOM_PARA=’EPSI’ and NOM_RESU=’SIGM’. 3.3 Operand VALE / VALE = lv lv is the list of values (x1, y1, …, xn, yn) with, in order: - x1, y1 (the first value of the parameter and the corresponding value of the result), - ... , - xn, yn (the last value of the parameter and the corresponding value of the result). Note: The list lv of values must be described in the order of increasing abscissae (x). 3.4 Operand VALE_C / VALE_C = lv lv is the list of values (x, y, z, …, xn, yn, zn) with: - xi values of the parameter - ... , - yi, zi the real part and the imaginary part of the complex function for this parameter. 3.5 Operands ABSCISSE / ORDONNEE / ABSCISSE = labs / ORDONNEE = lord The values of the abscissae and of the ordinates of the function are supplied separately in the form of lists of real values (x1, x2, …, xn) for ABSCISSE and (y1, y2, …, yn) for ORDONNEE. The two lists must have the same cardinality. 3.6 Operand VALE_PARA / VALE_FONC / VALE_PARA = la / VALE_FONC = lo nom [:ref: ref 1 ] Same operation as ABSCISSE, ORDONNEE except that the lists are supplied in the form of a listr8 concept produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. VALE_PARA and VALE_FONC must have identical cardinalities, otherwise the command stops in error. 3.7 Operand NOEUD_PARA / NOEUD_PARA = lno lno list of nodes making it possible to define the values of the abscissae of the function to be defined. The abscissae will be equal to the curvilinear abscissae of the nodes on the curve which they define. 3.8 Operands PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE = Define the type of extension to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable: | ’CONSTANT’ | for an extension with the last (or first) value of the function, | | --- | --- | | ’LINEAIRE’ | for an extension along the first segment defined (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last segment defined (PROL_DROITE), | | ’EXCLU’ | if the extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden (in this case if an analysis requests a value of the function outside the domain of definition, the code will stop in fatal error). | For example: - PROL_DROITE = ’CONSTANT’ , PROL_GAUCHE = ’CONSTANT’ - PROL_DROITE = ’LINEAIRE’, PROL_GAUCHE = ’EXCLU’ Note: The type of extension and of interpolation are independent of one another. 3.9 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL= Type of interpolation of the function between the values of the domain of definition of the function: one type for the interpolation of the parameter and one for the interpolation of the function. This is obtained by supplying a list of texts among: INTERPOL = (’LIN’, ’LOG’) | ’LIN’: | linear, | | --- | --- | | ’LOG’: | logarithmic, | Note: If only one value is specified, it is taken into account both for the interpolation of the parameter and for that of the function. INTERPOL = ’LOG’ is equivalent to (’LOG’, ’LOG’). 3.10 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= Précise les options d’impression sur le fichier MESSAGE. | 1: | no printout (default option) | | --- | --- | | 2: | printout of the parameters plus the list of the first 10 values in increasing order of the parameter | 3.11 Operand VERIF ◊ VERIF= The operator DEFI_Fonction checks that the values of the abscissae are strictly increasing. If this is not the case, an error is triggered. This is the default behaviour, VERIF is equal to ’Croissant’. The user has the possibility of not carrying out this check by indicating VERIF=’NON’. In this case, the function is reordered by increasing abscissae. An alarm is emitted if the abscissae of the function were not increasing. On the other hand, the abscissae must imperatively be strictly monotonic. 3.12 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = ti Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.13 Operands MAILLAGE and VALE_Y These two keywords must be supplied if one defines the function from NOEUD_PARA. MAILLAGE = ma Name of the mesh associated with the node list lno. VALE_Y = lv List of the values of the ordinates of the function to be defined. 4 Definition of a function depending on time 4.1 The function and the variables are entered in the form of reals Definition of a function (piecewise linear) which depends on time (parameter INST). 4.2 The function and the variables are entered in the form of listr8 concepts It is possible to define this function by means of concepts of type listr8 created through the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01: ABSCISSE = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( DEBUT = 0. , INTERVALLE = ( _F ( JUSQU_A = 1., NOMBRE = 1,), _F ( JUSQU_A = 3., NOMBRE = 1,), _F ( JUSQU_A = 6., NOMBRE = 1,),) ) ORDONNEE = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( DEBUT = -1. , INTERVALLE = ( _F (JUSQU_A = 0., NOMBRE = 1,), _F (JUSQU_A = 1., NOMBRE = 1,), _F (JUSQU_A = 2., NOMBRE = 1,),) ) EX_2 = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = ’INST’, VALE_PARA = ABSCISSE, VALE_FONC = ORDONNEE, PROL_DROITE = ’CONSTANT’, PROL_GAUCHE = ’LINEAIRE’, ) Note: This example is obviously very complicated for defining the function proposed. We only wished to highlight the principle of use of the possibility offered. This becomes interesting when one uses functions defined at a large number of points. Another reason for using the definition by DEFI_LIST_REEL is when the lists are necessary as an argument for another operator: (list of the time instants of a transient analysis THER_LINEAIRE, DYNA_VIBRA, …); this then avoids the duplication of information.

u4.31.03 Operator DEFI_NAPPE u4.31.03 Operator DEFI_NAPPE 1 Purpose Define a real function of two real variables. A nappe defines N functions for N values of a parameter. This operator makes it possible to define, for example, boundary conditions depending on a space variable and on time, or on two space variables, or material data (for example traction curves as a function of temperature). The concept produced by this operator is of type nappe. 2 Syntax nappe = DEFI_NAPPE( ◆ NOM_PARA = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", / "DTAN", / "TEMP", / "TSEC", / "INST", / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "EPSI", / "META", / "FREQ", / "PULS", / "DSP", / "AMOR", / "ABSC", / "SIGM", / "HYDR", / "SECH", / "PORO", / "SAT", / "IRRA", / "PGAZ", / "PCAP", / "PLIQ", / "PVAP", / "PAD", / "VITE", / "ENDO", / "NORM", / "EPAIS", / "EXCENT", / "NEUT1", / "NEUT2", / "NEUT3", / "NEUT4", / "XF", / "YF", / "ZF", / "NUME_ORDRE", ◇ NOM_RESU = text (défaut: "TOUTRESU"), ◆ PARA = float, / FONCTION = fonction, ◆ / DEFI_FONCTION = _F( ◆ VALE = float, ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ), ◇ / NOM_PARA_FONC = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", / "DTAN", / "TEMP", / "TSEC", / "INST", / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "EPSI", / "META", / "FREQ", / "PULS", / "DSP", / "AMOR", / "ABSC", / "SIGM", / "HYDR", / "SECH", / "PORO", / "SAT", / "IRRA", / "PGAZ", / "PCAP", / "PLIQ", / "PVAP", / "PAD", / "VITE", / "ENDO", / "NORM", / "EPAIS", / "EXCENT", / "NEUT1", / "NEUT2", / "NEUT3", / "NEUT4", / "XF", / "YF", / "ZF", / "NUME_ORDRE", ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ VERIF = "CROISSANT" (ou non renseigné), ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = np Designates the name of the parameter of the nappe (second variable); cf. the example in [§4.1]. The allowed values listed are the same as in DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02. 3.2 Operand NOM_RESU ◊ NOM_RESU = nr Name of the result, of the values of the nappe. It must be identical to the NOM_RESU of each of the functions making up the nappe. In fact, this operand is not systematically used for consistency checks, in the execution of the code. These consistency checks are made by the command CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04. 3.3 Operand PARA ♦ PARA = lp List of the values of the parameter characteristic of the nappe: para1, para2, ... The cardinality of this list must be equal to the number of functions defined afterwards. 3.4 Operands PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE = Define the type of extension to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable: | 'CONSTANT' | for an extension with the last (or first) value of the nappe, | | --- | --- | | 'LINEAIRE' | for an extension along the first segment defined (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last segment defined (PROL_DROITE); this extension does not take account of a possible logarithmic interpolation, | | 'EXCLU' | if the extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter np is forbidden (in this case if an analysis requests a value of the function outside the domain of definition, the code will stop in fatal error). | 3.5 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL= Type of interpolation of the nappe: one type for the interpolation of the second variable and one for the interpolation between two functions. This is obtained by supplying a list of 2 texts among: INTERPOL = ('LIN', 'LOG') | 'LIN': | linear, | | --- | --- | | 'LOG': | logarithmic, | Note: If only one value is specified, it is taken into account both for the interpolation of the parameter and for that of the function. INTERPOL = 'LOG' is equivalent to ('LOG', 'LOG'). 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Specifies the printout options in the message file (unit 6). | 1 : | no printout (default option) | | --- | --- | | 2 : | printout of the parameters plus the list of the first 10 values of each function in increasing order of the first 10 parameters | 3.7 Operand VERIF ◊ VERIF = The operator DEFI_NAPPE reorders the values of the parameters np in increasing order. If VERIF is equal to 'Croissant' the operator stops the execution if the values of the parameter np have not been given in this order. 3.8 Definition of the functions of the nappe Two modes of definition of the nappe are possible: - from a list of existing functions [§3.8.1], - by defining directly the various functions of the nappe [§3.8.2]. 3.8.1 Operand FONCTION FONCTION = lf List of concepts of type fonction created by the commands DEFI_Fonction U4.31.02, DEFI_CONSTANTE U4.31.01, CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01, … lf is the list of the names of concepts of type fonction corresponding to the values of the parameter. All the functions of the list must have the same variable name (NOM_PARA of DEFI_FONCTION, which we shall call npf) and have the same name nr as the result name. nf is a nappe of the variable of name np and of the variable of name npf and whose value has the name nr. 3.8.2 Direct definition of the functions 3.8.2.1 Operand NOM_PARA_FONC ♦ NOM_PARA_FONC = npf Name of the parameter characteristic of the functions constituting the nappe. The allowed values listed are the same as for NOM_PARA. 3.8.2.2 Keyword DEFI_FONCTION DEFI_FONCTION = Direct definition of the functions constituting the nappe. 3.8.2.3 Operand VALE ♦ VALE =lv lv is the list of values (x1, y1, …, xn, yn) with, in order: x1, y1 (the first value of the parameter and the corresponding value of the result), ... xn, yn (the last value of the parameter and the corresponding value of the result). 3.8.2.4 Operands PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE= Define the type of extension to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable: | 'CONSTANT' | for an extension with the last (or first) value of the function, | | --- | --- | | 'LINEAIRE' | for an extension along the first segment defined (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last segment defined (PROL_DROITE), | | 'EXCLU' | if the extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter npf is forbidden (in this case if an analysis requests a value of the function outside the domain of definition, the code will stop in fatal error). | 3.8.2.5 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL= Type of interpolation of the function between the values of the domain of definition of the function: one type for the interpolation of the abscissae and one for the interpolation of the ordinates of the function. This is obtained by supplying a list of texts among: INTERPOL = ('LIN', 'LOG') | 'LIN': | linear, | | --- | --- | | 'LOG': | logarithmic, | | 'NON': | one does not interpolate (and therefore the program will stop if one requests the value of the function for a value of the parameter for which it has not been defined). | Note: If only one value is specified, it is taken into account both for the interpolation of the parameter and for that of the function. INTERPOL = 'LOG' is equivalent to ('LOG', 'LOG'). 3.9 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = ti Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.10 Evaluation of a nappe Let there be a nappe N whose parameter is NOM_PARA= y and which is composed of functions whose NOM_PARA_FONC= x , with values NOM_RESU= z=f(x) . To evaluate N(x,y) : - One looks for i such that {y}_{i}\le y NOM_RESU = 'z', > NOM_PARA_FONC = 'x', > INTERPOL = (a, b), > DEFI_FONCTION = (_F( VALE=..., > INTERPOL = (c, d),), > other functions... ),) The types of interpolation used are: - c between two values of x, - d when one evaluates the functions at x, - a between two values of y, - b between two different functions (evaluated at x). 4 Examples 4.1 Definition of the nappe after definition of the function FCT2 = DEFI_FONCTION (NOM_PARA = 'EPSI', PROL_DROITE = 'LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE = 'LINEAIRE', VALE = (1.25E-5, 3.75, 3.75E-5, 7.5,), ) FCT3 = DEFI_FONCTION (NOM_PARA = 'EPSI', PROL_DROITE = 'LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE = 'LINEAIRE', VALE = (1.25E-5, 2.50, 3.75E-5, 5.0,), ) SIG = DEFI_NAPPE (NOM_PARA = 'TEMP', PROL_DROITE = 'CONSTANT', PROL_GAUCHE = 'CONSTANT', PARA = (20.0, 30.0,), FONCTION = (FCT3, FCT2,) , ) 4.2 Direct definition of the nappe and of the constituent functions FCT2 = DEFI_NAPPE ( NOM_PARA = 'TEMP', PROL_DROITE = 'CONSTANT', PROL_GAUCHE = 'CONSTANT', PARA = (20.0, 30.0,), NOM_PARA_FONC = 'EPSI', DEFI_FONCTION = ( _F( PROL_DROITE = 'LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE = 'LINEAIRE', VALE =(1.25E-5, 3.75, 3.75E-5, 7.5,), ), _F( PROL_DROITE = 'LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE = 'LINEAIRE', VALE =(1.25E-5, 2.5, 3.75E-5, 5.0,), ), ), )

u4.31.05 Operator FORMULE u4.31.05 Operator FORMULE 1 Purpose Define a real-valued or complex-valued formula from its mathematical expression. The formula will be usable in a later command as an argument of type fonction/formule, or evaluated with particular values of the variables. In many applications, one may tabulate this formula for particular values by the command CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01, which produces a concept of type fonction or fonction_c, as do DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02 or DEFI_NAPPE U4.31.03. 2 Syntax / formule / formule_c = FORMULE( ◆ / VALE = text, / VALE_C = text, ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Definition of the function The body of the function is a Python algebraic expression represented by a character string. It must be evaluable: that is to say, it must respect the Python syntax, and the functions, constants or other objects necessary for its evaluation must be defined as arguments. Example: alpha = 1.23 form = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X', VALE='sin(X) alpha', alpha=alpha) The expression of the formula is 'sin(X) alpha'. In order to evaluate it, X is the variable of the formula. The function sin is supplied by the math module (see below). The constant alpha is defined in the command file. It is therefore necessary to define it as an argument and to supply its value. Thus, the formula may be evaluated anywhere. Caution The functions, classes (and other Python objects) defined in the command file are not available in POURSUITE (Python cannot "pickle" them). In order that formulae using this type of complementary argument may be evaluated again in POURSUITE, one must redefine the functions, classes (and other Python objects) in POURSUITE and declare them to the formulae by setContext. If one uses VALE, the formula produced is real-valued (concept of type formule). If one uses VALE_C, the formula is complex-valued (concept of type formule_c). In both cases, the parameters are real. The names of the parameters necessary for the evaluation of the formula are supplied under the keyword NOM_PARA. In the event of a syntax error, it is the Python language which emits the error message and not Code_Aster itself. Note The order of the parameters (keyword NOM_PARA ) is important. If one creates a formula with two parameters in order to produce a nappe, the first parameter is the parameter of the nappe, the second is the parameter of the functions making up the nappe. 3.2 Standard functions Besides the ordinary algebraic signs + - / , standard functions (builtins) are also available: min, max, abs, float … Caution: the division sign here denotes real division: 1 / 2 = 0.5 If one wishes to carry out an operation in integer division, one must use the operator //: 1 // 2 = 0 3.3 Mathematical functions All the functions of the Python math module are imported by default. They are therefore directly usable in the body of the formulae. http://docs.python.org/lib/module-math.html | sin | sinh | | --- | --- | | cos | cosh | | tan | tanh | | atan | sqrt | | atan2 | log | | asin | log10 | | acos | exp | Moreover, the constant pi, from the same module, is also available. Caution: The trigonometric functions are therefore those of Python and expect angles expressed in radians. One must be vigilant about consistency with the simple keywords ANGL_ of the command language, which in general require angles in degrees. 4 Examples of use For various examples one will refer to the test case ZZZZ100A. 4.1 A formula is used like a tabulated function Definition of the formula Sia: SIa = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X',VALE='sin(X)') Equivalent tabulated function SI: LR = DEFI_LIST_REEL( DEBUT = 0., INTERVALLE = _F( JUSQU_A = pi , PAS = 0.01 ) SI = CALC_FONC_INTERP( FONCTION = SIa, LIST_PARA = LR, NOM_PARA = 'X', NOM_RESU = 'DEPL', ) In order to define a tabulated function in this way from an interpretable formula, see CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01. Use of SI or of SIa in a simple keyword expecting a function or a formula: champ=CREA_CHAMP( ... AFFE = _F( ... VALE_F = SI or SIa, ) ) 4.2 A formula may be evaluated as a real In the body of the command file: SIa = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X',VALE='sin(X)') X = SIa(1.57) print SIa(1.57) Behind a simple keyword expecting a real: LR = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT=SIa(0.), INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A=SIa(pi/2.), PAS=0.01)) In another formula: SIb = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X', VALE='X SIa(5.)', SIa=SIa) 4.3 Calling a formula or a function in another formula SIa = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X',VALE='sin(X)') Take care to remember to put the argument (X here) in the call to the function SIa: SIb = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='X', VALE='X SIa(X)', SIa=SIa) 4.4 Formula with several parameters NAP = FORMULE(NOM_PARA=('AMOR','FREQ'), VALE='''(1./((2. pi FREQ) 2 - OMEGA 2 ) 2 +(2. AMOR 2. pi FREQ OMEGA) 2)''', OMEGA=OMEGA) In this example, one defines a formula with 2 parameters. Given the length of the expression, it is written for convenience on several lines with triple quotes to delimit it. The constant pi is a standard constant (cf. paragraph [§3.2]), the constant OMEGA must be supplied explicitly. In the present state, only formulae from \mathrm{ℝ} into \mathrm{ℝ} or \mathrm{ℂ} are possible: a single scalar is produced. 4.5 Formula coming from the programming of a Python function One may refer in a formula to functions programmed in Python, which allows formulae much more complex than simple algebraic expressions. For example a Heaviside function: \mathrm{HEAVYSIDE}(x)=\lbrace \begin{array}{c}0.\mathrm{si}x<0.\\ 1.\mathrm{si}x\ge 0.\end{array} The Python function is programmed as follows: def heaviside(x): if x < 0.: return 0. else: return 1. F_HVS = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='INST', VALE='heaviside(INST)', heaviside=heaviside) Caution: The use of Python programming in the command file (here the method heaviside ) is incompatible with editing this file in graphical mode with AsterStudy. In order that the formula F_HVS may be evaluated in POURSUITE, one must redefine the Heaviside function and declare it to the formula: def heaviside(x): if x < 0.: return 0. else: return 1. F_HVS.setContext( dict(heaviside=heaviside) ) 4.6 Example of the definition of formulae in a Python loop When one defines, in a loop, formulae whose expression depends on the index of the loop, one sees the full benefit of passing the constants explicitly. Example: for i in range(3): FO[i] = FORMULE(VALE='cos(i INST)', NOM_PARA='INST', i=i) CH[i] = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE', ..., VALE_F=FO[i]) With these instructions, one has defined 3 formulae which all have the same expression. At each iteration, a different value is stored for the argument i. When the formula is evaluated in order then to assign the values of the field, there is no ambiguity about the value of i. It is the value attached to the formula when it was created, and not the current value of i. Indeed, in mode PAR_LOT='OUI', all the commands are created, and only afterwards executed. In this mode, i is equal to 2 during the actual execution of the commands.

u4.32.01 Operator CALC_FONC_INTERP u4.32.01 Operator CALC_FONC_INTERP 1 Purpose Build a concept of type fonction or fonction_c from a FORMULE function with 1 or 2 variables. Real functions of real variables, complex functions of real variables, and nappes may be defined. One can also produce a new real or complex function, or a nappe, by interpolating another function of the same type (real, complex, or a nappe). The use of CALC_FONC_INTERP allows a tabulation of the formula prior to the analysis. Its use is recommended before any transient and/or non-linear analysis, for performance reasons. The operator is not re-entrant; it produces a new function or a nappe. 2 Syntax / formule / nappe / fonction / fonction_c = CALC_FONC_INTERP( ◆ FONCTION = formule / nappe / fonction / fonction_c, ◆ / VALE_PARA = float, / LIST_PARA = listr8, ◇ NOM_RESU = text, ◇ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN", / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "EXCLU", / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "EXCLU", / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", ◇ NOM_PARA_FONC = text, # Si: exists("NOM_PARA_FONC") ◆ / VALE_PARA_FONC = float, / LIST_PARA_FONC = listr8, ◇ INTERPOL_FONC = / "LIN", / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE_FONC = / "EXCLU", / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", ◇ PROL_GAUCHE_FONC = / "EXCLU", / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand FONCTION ♦ FONCTION = f Name of the FORMULE (interpretable function (FORMULE, cf. U4.31.05)). This function may have one or two variables in the case of real formulae, and one variable only in the case of complex formulae. One may nevertheless create a new function (respectively fonction_c, nappe) from a function (respectively fonction_c, nappe) by interpolating the first on a different list of parameters. This possibility is used essentially in the macro-commands. When the input type is a formula and NOM_PARA_FONC is supplied, the data structure produced is a nappe. Note When interpolating a formula with two parameters, one checks the consistency between the parameters of the formula and the keywords NOM_PARA and NOM_PARA_FONC . See the example in paragraph 4.2 . 3.2 Operand NOM_RESU ◊ NOM_RESU = nr Designates the name of the result; the function thus created is a function whose value has the name nr (8 characters). 3.3 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA = nr Designates the name of the parameter of the function or of the nappe. By default, the name of the parameter of the formula or function supplied is used. 3.4 Operands VALE_PARA/LIST_PARA ◊ / VALE_PARA = lvale, lvale is the list of values of the parameter. / LIST_PARA = lpara, lpara is the list of values of the parameter: it is a concept of type listr8 created beforehand by the command DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. 3.5 Operands PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE = Define the type of prolongation to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the parameter of the function or of the nappe | 'CONSTANT' | for a prolongation with the last (or first) value of the function, | | --- | --- | | 'LINEAIRE' | for a prolongation along the first defined segment (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last defined segment (PROL_DROITE), | | 'EXCLU' | extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden (in this case, if an analysis requests a value of the function outside the domain of definition, the code will stop with a fatal error), | 3.6 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL= Type of interpolation of the function between the values of the variable, or type of interpolation of the nappe between the values of the parameter. After this keyword one expects a list of parameters (two at most). | 'LIN': | linear, | | --- | --- | | 'LOG': | logarithmic, | If a single value is given, the interpolation will be the same for the abscissae and the ordinates. If two values are given, the first corresponds to the interpolation of the abscissae and the second to the interpolation of the ordinates. 3.7 Operand NOM_PARA_FONC ◊ NOM_PARA_FONC = nr Designates the name of the variable of the functions defining the nappe. When the input type is a formula and this keyword is filled in, the data structure produced is a nappe. 3.8 Operands VALE_PARA_FONC/LIST_PARA_FONC ◊ / VALE_PARA_FONC = lvale, lvale is the list of values of the variable of the functions defining the nappe. / LIST_PARA_FONC = lpara, lpara is the list of values of the variable of the functions defining the nappe: it is a concept of type listr8 created beforehand by the command DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. 3.9 Operands PROL_DROITE_FONC and PROL_GAUCHE_FONC ◊ PROL_DROITE_FONC et PROL_GAUCHE_FONC = Define the type of prolongation to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable of the functions of the nappe: 'CONSTANT', 'LINEAIRE', 'EXCLU' have the same meaning as previously. 3.10 Operand INTERPOL_FONC ◊ INTERPOL_FONC= Type of interpolation of the functions between the values of the variable of the functions defining the nappe. After this keyword one expects a list of parameters (two at most). The behaviour is identical to that of INTERPOL. 3.11 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= Specifies the printout options in the MESSAGE file. | 1 : | no printout (default option) | | --- | --- | | 2 : | printout of the parameters plus the list of the first 10 values in increasing order of the parameter | 3.12 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = ti Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 4 Examples 4.1 Case of a function 4.1.1 Define the FORMULE function sin(t) SI = FORMULE ( NOM_PARA = 'INST', VALE = 'sin(INST)' ) 4.1.2 Tabulate sin(t) from a list of reals DEPI = 2. pi PAS0 = DEPI/200. LI1 = DEFI_LIST_REEL (DEBUT = 0, INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A=DEPI, PAS=PAS0),) SI1 = CALC_FONC_INTERP (FONCTION= SI, LIST_PARA = LI1, NOM_RESU = 'DEPL', PROL_GAUCHE='EXCLU', PROL_DROITE='CONSTANT', INTERPOL='LIN', TITRE='FONCTION SINUS' ) 4.1.3 Tabulate sin(t) from a list of values LI2 = ( 0.,0.01,0.03,0.04,0.05,0.06,0.07,0.08,0.09,0.10) SI2 = CALC_FONC_INTERP ( FONCTION = SI, VALE_PARA = LI2, NOM_PARA =’INST’, PROL_GAUCHE = 'EXCLU', PROL_DROITE = 'EXCLU', INTERPOL = 'LIN', TITRE = 'FONCTION SINUS') 4.2 Case of a nappe 4.2.1 Define the FORMULE function sin(omega t) SI = FORMULE ( NOM_PARA = ('FREQ', 'INST'), VALE = 'sin(2 pi FREQ INST)') 4.2.2 Tabulate sin(omega t) from a list of time instants The parameter of the nappe is 'FREQ'; the variable of the functions defining the nappe is 'INST'. One checks in CALC_FONC_INTERP that the first parameter of the formula is the same as NOM_PARA, and that the second parameter of the formula is identical to NOM_PARA_FONC. LI_FREQ = DEFI_LIST_REEL (DEBUT = 10, INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A=100, PAS=10),) LI_INST = DEFI_LIST_REEL (DEBUT = 0, INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A=100, PAS=1),) SI1 = CALC_FONC_INTERP ( FONCTION= SI, NOM_RESU = 'DEPL', NOM_PARA_FONC='INST', LIST_PARA_FONC = LI_INST PROL_GAUCHE_FONC='EXCLU', PROL_DROITE_FONC='CONSTANT', INTERPOL_FONC='LIN', NOM_PARA='FREQ', LIST_PARA = LI_FREQ PROL_GAUCHE='LINEAIRE', PROL_DROITE='LINEAIRE', INTERPOL='LIN', TITRE='FONCTION SINUS',)

u4.32.02 Operator LIRE_FONCTION u4.32.02 Operator LIRE_FONCTION 1 Purpose Read a data file containing real values representing a function. Produces a concept of type fonction U4.31.02 or nappe U4.31.03. 2 Syntax / fonction_c / fonction / nappe = LIRE_FONCTION( ◇ FORMAT = / "LIBRE" (par défaut), / "NUMPY", ◇ TYPE = / "FONCTION" (par défaut), / "FONCTION_C", / "NAPPE", ◇ SEPARATEUR = text (défaut: "None"), ◇ INDIC_PARA = int (défaut: [1, 1]), # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'FONCTION') ◇ INDIC_RESU = int (défaut: [1, 2]), # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'FONCTION_C') ◇ FORMAT_C = / "REEL_IMAG" (par défaut), / "MODULE_PHASE", # Si: equal_to("FORMAT_C", 'REEL_IMAG') ◇ INDIC_REEL = int (défaut: [1, 2]), ◇ INDIC_IMAG = int (défaut: [1, 3]), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT_C", 'MODULE_PHASE') ◇ INDIC_MODU = int (défaut: [1, 2]), ◇ INDIC_PHAS = int (défaut: [1, 3]), # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'NAPPE') ◆ NOM_PARA_FONC = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", / "DTAN", / "TEMP", / "TSEC", / "INST", / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "EPSI", / "META", / "FREQ", / "PULS", / "DSP", / "AMOR", / "ABSC", / "SIGM", / "HYDR", / "SECH", / "PORO", / "SAT", / "IRRA", / "PGAZ", / "PCAP", / "PLIQ", / "PVAP", / "PAD", / "VITE", / "ENDO", / "NORM", / "EPAIS", / "EXCENT", / "NEUT1", / "NEUT2", / "NEUT3", / "NEUT4", / "XF", / "YF", / "ZF", / "NUME_ORDRE", ◆ INDIC_ABSCISSE = int, ◇ INTERPOL_FONC = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE_FONC = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE_FONC = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ DEFI_FONCTION = _F( ◆ INDIC_RESU = int, ), ◆ UNITE = unit, ◆ NOM_PARA = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", / "DTAN", / "TEMP", / "TSEC", / "INST", / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "EPSI", / "META", / "FREQ", / "PULS", / "DSP", / "AMOR", / "ABSC", / "SIGM", / "HYDR", / "SECH", / "PORO", / "SAT", / "IRRA", / "PGAZ", / "PCAP", / "PLIQ", / "PVAP", / "PAD", / "VITE", / "ENDO", / "NORM", / "EPAIS", / "EXCENT", / "NEUT1", / "NEUT2", / "NEUT3", / "NEUT4", / "XF", / "YF", / "ZF", / "NUME_ORDRE", ◇ NOM_RESU = text (défaut: "TOUTRESU"), ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ VERIF = / "CROISSANT" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand UNITE ♦ UNITE = u Integer, logical unit number for reading, defining the file in which the data are read. 3.2 Operand FORMAT ◊ FORMAT = 'LIBRE' ou 'NUMPY', Indicates the format of the file to be read. The NUMPY format indicates that the file was produced by numpy.save; in LIBRE format, it is a simple text file. 3.3 Operand SEPARATEUR ◊ SEPARATEUR = 'None'ousep Character separating the columns of numbers in the file to be read. The default value 'None' means one or more blank characters. For the other separators, blank characters are tolerated between the numbers and the separator sep itself. It is not used in NUMPY format. 3.4 Operands PROL_DROITE/PROL_GAUCHE / NOM_PARA / NOM_RESU / INTERPOL / VERIF / TITRE / INFO The numerical values are read in the file indicated, then the function is actually created by lire_fonction by calling DEFI_FONCTION or DEFI_NAPPE. Thus, these keywords are taken over unchanged from DEFI_FONCTION or DEFI_NAPPE and make it possible to specify the characteristics of the function produced: interpolation, prolongations, names of the access parameters. 3.5 Operand INDIC_PARA ◊ INDIC_PARA = / [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] This keyword is identical in principle to the keyword VALE_PARA of the command DEFI_FONCTION. It makes it possible to choose the column of numbers in the file read which will define the abscissae of the function, that is the values of the parameter. One necessarily expects a list of two integers: the first designating the number of the 'block' in the file (cf. paragraph [§4] Examples), the second designating the column number. To identify the blocks of the file, any line which would not contain exclusively numbers and column separators is considered as a block separator. The columns are defined by the presence of the column separators which bound them (keyword SEPARATEUR). The default value is [1,1]: one reads the first column of the first block. In NUMPY format, there is only one "block", so the first index is always 1. 3.6 Operand TYPE ◊ TYPE = / 'FONCTION' , [DEFAUT] / 'FONCTION_C' , / 'NAPPE' , Specifies the type of function read and created: 'FONCTION', 'FONCTION_C' (call, in the macro-command, to DEFI_FONCTION) or 'NAPPE' (call to DEFI_NAPPE). 3.7 Case of a real function: TYPE='FONCTION' ◊ INDIC_RESU = / [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] Operating in the same way as INDIC_PARA, this keyword makes it possible to choose the column of numbers in the file read defining the ordinates of the function, that is the values of the result. The default value is [1,2]: one reads the second column of the first block. In NUMPY format, there is only one "block". 3.8 Case of a complex function: TYPE='FONCTION_C' ◊ FORMAT_C = 'REEL_IMAG' ♦ INDIC_REEL = / [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] ♦ INDIC_IMAG = / [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] ◊ FORMAT_C = 'MODULE_PHASE' ♦ INDIC_MODU = / [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] ♦ INDIC_PHAS = / [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] In the case of a complex function, two columns of numbers (real values) are to be identified in the file read in order to define the list of complex values of the result. One may thus read, as one chooses, real part/imaginary part or modulus/phase. The phase is expressed in radians. The default values are respectively [1,2] and [1,3]: one reads the second and third columns of the first block. The first column read by default having been the value of the parameter (INDIC_PARA). 3.9 Case of a nappe: TYPE='NAPPE' ♦ NOM_PARA_FONC = cf mot clé NOM_PARA ♦ INDIC_ABSCISSE = [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] , ◊ INTERPOL_FONC = cf mot clé INTERPOL ◊ PROL_DROITE_FONC = cf mot clé PROL_DROITE ◊ PROL_GAUCHE_FONC = cf mot clé PROL_GAUCHE ◊ DEFI_FONCTION = _F( ♦ INDIC_RESU = [:ref: indice1,indice2 ] , The principle is the same as that of DEFI_NAPPE[U4.31.03]: the list of possible values of the parameter (second variable) having been defined by INDIC_PARA, it remains to identify the functions in the file read by the factor keyword DEFI_FONCTION (analogous to the factor keyword FONCTION of DEFI_NAPPE). Caution: the number of functions identified (occurrences of the factor keyword) must be identical to the cardinality of the values read by INDIC_PARA. Unlike nappes in general, one imposes that the functions share the same list of abscissa values INDIC_ABSCISSE, which is why only INDIC_RESU is present under the factor keyword DEFI_FONCTION. The '_FONC' keywords apply to the functions of the nappe (cf. DEFI_NAPPE, factor keyword DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.03). 4 Examples of use Consider the following text file, containing the information to be read. It is composed of columns of numbers, here separated by blank characters, defining blocks, themselves delimited by free text. Any line comprising characters other than numbers and the predefined separator is considered as delimiting free text. There are therefore 4 blocks in the following file: aaa bbb ccc ddd eee fff 0. 0. 0. 0.1 1. 10. 0.2 2. 20. 0.3 3. 30. xxx yyy www zzz 0.4 4. 40. 400. 0.5 5. 50. 500. 0.6 6. 60. 600. xxx 70. 700. 80. 800. 90. 900. ppp qqq 8.8 9.9 4.1 Reading of a simple function Using the default values for the choice of columns: F=LIRE_FONCTION( UNITE = 38, NOM_PARA = ‘INST’, ) The function thus created is: Abscisses = [:ref: 0., 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 ] Ordonnées = [:ref: 0., 1. , 2. , 3. ] By associating, for the abscissae and the ordinates, columns taken from different blocks: F=LIRE_FONCTION( UNITE = 38, NOM_PARA = ‘INST’, INDIC_PARA = [:ref: 2,4 ], INDIC_RESU = [:ref: 3,1 ], The function thus created is: Abscisses = [:ref: 400., 500., 600. ] Ordonnées = [:ref: 70., 80., 90. ] Caution: the command then checks that the cardinalities of the columns defined by INDIC_PARA and INDIC_RESU are indeed identical. This would not have been the case here with, for example, INDIC_PARA = [1,3]. 4.2 Reading of a complex function Using the default values for the choice of columns: F=LIRE_FONCTION( UNITE = 38, NOM_PARA = ‘INST’, TYPE = ‘FONCTION_C’, FORMAT_C = ‘REEL_IMAG’, ) The function thus created is: Abscisses = [:ref: 0., 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 ] Ordonnées = [:external:ref: (0.,0.) , (1.,10.) , (2.,20.) , (3.,30.) ] One could of course have specified columns for INDIC_REEL and INDIC_IMAG other than the default ones. Take care, however, to point to columns of the same cardinality. 4.3 Reading of a nappe Using the default values for the choice of columns: F=LIRE_FONCTION( UNITE = 38, NOM_PARA = ‘INST’, INDIC_PARA = [:ref: 4,1 ], NOM_PARA_FONC = ‘FREQ’, INDIC_ABSCISSE = [:ref: 2,2 ], DEFI_FONCTION = ( F( INDIC_RESU = [:ref: 3,1 ], ), F( INDIC_RESU = [:ref: 2,3 ], ), ) ) The nappe thus created is: For the parameter value INST=8.8, the function: Abscisses = [:ref: 4. , 5. , 6. ] Ordonnées = [:ref: 70. , 80. , 90. ] For the parameter value INST=9.9, the function: Abscisses = [:ref: 4. , 5. , 6. ] Ordonnées = [:ref: 40. , 50. , 60. ] The consistency checks on the cardinalities of the columns of abscissae and of ordinates are carried out by the command.

u4.32.03 Operator RECU_FONCTION u4.32.03 Operator RECU_FONCTION 1 Purpose Extract, in the form of a function, the evolution of one quantity as a function of another. If the extraction is carried out from a data structure resultat, or from a field of a quantity (grandeur) cham_gd, or from a resu_gene, the function produced corresponds to the time evolution of a component at a node or at a Gauss point of the mesh. From a data structure tran_gene, one can also extract the evolution of two parameters at a shock node. From a table, one can extract the evolution of 2 parameters in the columns of the table, or a function contained in a cell of the table. From a nappe, one can extract the function corresponding to a given value of the parameter. From a data structure melasflu one can extract the evolution of modal parameters as a function of the flow velocity of the fluid, or the evolution of the critical velocity as a function of the Connors number. From a data structure interspectre one can extract the frequency evolution of the interspectrum associated with the i -th row and the j -th column of the interspectral matrix, or the time evolution of the interspectrum at the n -th component of the diagonal. Produces a data structure of type fonction or fonction_c. On exit from the command, the function is reordered by increasing abscissae. On the other hand, it is forbidden to have several identical abscissae (it would no longer be a function). 2 Syntax / fonction_c / fonction = RECU_FONCTION( ◆ / CHAM_GD = cham_elem / cham_no, / ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT= resu Name of the concept of type resultat on which the extraction bears. For the operands making it possible to extract the field, refer to [§3.7]. For the operands making it possible to locate the field, refer to [§3.8]. 3.2 Operand CHAM_GD ♦ CHAM_GD= ch_gd Name of the concept of a field on which the extraction bears. For the operands making it possible to locate the field, refer to [§3.7]. The field supplied to the keyword CHAM_GD is: - either a field at the nodes of quantity (grandeur): DEPL_R, TEMP_R or PRES_R; - or a field by elements (at the nodes or at the Gauss points) of quantity (grandeur): VARI_R, EPSI_R, FLUX_R, or PRES_R. 3.3 Operand RESU_GENE 3.3.1 Time evolution of a physical or generalised component, type tran_gene ♦ RESU_GENE= gene Name of the concept of type resu_gene produced by DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 on which the extraction bears. The function recovered is expressed - in terms of the physical variables: one has specified GROUP_NO = grno. - in terms of the generalised variables: one has specified NUME_CMP_GENE = n_val . NOM_CHAM gives the name of the field which one wants to recover ('DEPL', 'VITE', 'ACCE', or 'PTEM'). The option 'PTEM' makes it possible to extract, for each time instant (or order number) of recovery, the values of the analysis time step. Note: Carrying out this recovery on the physical basis is the role of the command REST_GENE_PHYS. In later versions, this functionality will be removed from RECU_FONCTION; one will have to carry out the recovery and then extract the function. 3.3.1.1 Operands MULT_APPUI and ACCE_MONO_APPUI ◊ MULT_APPUI If this keyword is 'OUI', one recovers the evolution of the variables in the physical space by treating the problem in absolute motion in the case of a multi-support excitation. Otherwise, the recovery in the physical space is carried out by assuming that the problem is treated in relative motion. This keyword cannot be used if the keyword CORR_STAT is used. ◊ ACCE_MONO_APPUI In the case of a single-support acceleration, one must indicate here the acceleration imposed on all the supports in the direction considered, in order to calculate the absolute acceleration of the point. If the keyword is not filled in, one obtains the relative acceleration as the result of the command. Note: The name of the concept must be the same as that entered under FONC_MULT of DYNA_VIBRA. 3.3.1.2 Operands CORR_STAT ◊ CORR_STAT If this keyword is 'OUI', the evolution of the variables in the physical space is obtained by taking into account the correction due to the consideration of static modes (cf. [R4.05.03]). This keyword cannot be used if the keyword MULT_APPUI is used. 3.3.1.3 Information concerning the shock nodes ♦ RESU_GENE= gene Concept of type tran_gene containing, for the various shock nodes: the local displacements, the normal and tangential velocities, and the normal and tangential shock forces. ♦ GROUP_NO_CHOC= no_choc, Node group (which contains only a single node) of the shock, where one recovers the function. This shock node is defined in the command DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. ♦ PARA_X= nparax Name of the parameter defining the abscissae (argument taken from the list: 'INST', 'FN', 'FT1, 'FT2', 'VN', 'VT1', 'VT2', 'DXLOC', 'DYLOC', 'DZLOC', 'VINT1', 'VINT2', 'VINT3', 'VINT4', 'VINT5', 'VINT6', 'VINT7', 'VINT8', 'VINT9', 'VINT10', 'VINT11', 'VINT12', 'VINT13', 'VINT14', 'VINT15', 'VINT16', 'VINT17', 'VINT18', 'VINT19', 'VINT20', 'VINT21'). ♦ PARA_Y= nparay Name of the parameter defining the ordinates (argument taken from the list: 'INST', 'FN', 'FT1, 'FT2', 'VN', 'VT1', 'VT2', 'DXLOC', 'DYLOC', 'DZLOC', 'VINT1', 'VINT2', 'VINT3', 'VINT4', 'VINT5', 'VINT6', 'VINT7', 'VINT8', 'VINT9', 'VINT10', 'VINT11', 'VINT12', 'VINT13', 'VINT14', 'VINT15', 'VINT16', 'VINT17', 'VINT18', 'VINT19', 'VINT20', 'VINT21'). ◊ LIST_PARA= li_para List of the values of the parameter on the abscissa defining the function. Caution: it is possible to have problems of interpolation of the result on this list of parameters (because, to within machine precision, the values may lie slightly outside the bounds of the functions produced). In this case, it is enough not to use this keyword here. The function will then be created at all the time instants of the analysis. One can then interpolate this function with CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01 on the list of parameters of one's choice, while controlling the prolongations to the left and to the right. ◊ INTITULE = nom This name defines the shock link (this name, if it is used, is defined in the command DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03). ◊ SOUS_STRUC = nom_str In an analysis with dynamic substructuring, name of the substructure which contains the shock node (cf. command DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02). In this case the keyword INTITULE must also be filled in. 3.3.2 Frequency evolution of a generalised or physical component, type harm_gene ♦ RESU_GENE= gene Name of the concept of type harm_gene produced by DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. > The function recovered is expressed - in terms of the physical variables: one has specified GROUP_NO = grno. - in terms of the generalised variables: one has specified NUME_CMP_GENE = n_val . NOM_CHAM gives the name of the field which one wants to recover ('DEPL', 'VITE' or 'ACCE'). Note: Carrying out this recovery on the physical basis is the role of the command REST_GENE_PHYS. In later versions, this functionality will be removed from RECU_FONCTION; one will have to carry out the recovery and then extract the function. 3.3.3 Frequency evolution of a generalised or physical component, type mode_gene ♦ RESU_GENE= gene Name of the concept of type mode_gene produced by CALC_MODES U4.52.02. The function recovered is expressed with the physical variables if NOM_CMP is present, with the generalised variables if NUME_CMP_GENE is present. > ♦ NOM_PARA_RESU / NOM_CHAMP See paragraph 3.8 . > ♦ NOM_CMP / GROUP_NO See paragraph 3.9 . > ♦ SQUELETTE Name of the skeleton mesh of the global structure on which the result will be recovered: see the operator DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01. > ♦ SOUS_STRUC See above. 3.4 Operand TABLE One can recover: 1. either a function defined from two columns of the table, 2. or a function whose name is indicated in a cell of the table. > ♦ TABLE= tabl Name of the result table in which an extraction is carried out. 3.4.1 Function defined from two columns of the table 3.4.1.1 Operands PARA_X/ PARA_Y ♦ PARA_X= nparax Name of the column of the table defining the abscissae. ♦ PARA_Y= nparay Name of the column of the table defining the ordinates. 3.4.2 Function whose name is indicated in a cell of the table 3.4.2.1 Operand NOM_PARA_TABL ♦ NOM_PARA_TABL= 'FONCTION' ou ‘FONCTION_C’ The presence of this keyword indicates that one recovers a function whose name is stored in a cell of the table. The real functions are stored in the column ‘FONCTION’, the complex functions in the column ‘FONCTION_C’. 3.4.2.2 Keyword FILTRE ◊FILTRE The extraction operands are different from those used for the previous cases. To carry out the extraction, one must use the keyword FILTRE and the operands NOM_PARA, CRIT_COMP, VALE_X, CRITERE, PRECISION. This factor keyword makes it possible to filter the information stored in the table. For the use of this keyword see the command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. To recover a function whose name is indicated in a cell of the table, one must use the factor keyword FILTRE at least twice in order to select only the relevant cell. 3.5 Operand BASE_ELAS_FLUI One recovers, in a data structure of type melasflu produced by the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02, the evolutions of the frequency or of the damping, for a given mode, as a function of the various excitation velocities of the fluid. ♦ BASE_ELAS_FLUI = flui Concept of type melasflu produced by the command CALC_FLUI_STRU. 3.5.1 Operand NUME_MODE ♦ NUME_MODE = im Number of the mode for which the extraction of the frequency or of the damping as a function of the fluid velocity is carried out. 3.5.2 Operands PARA_X / PARA_Y/NUME_ORDRE/TOUT_ORDRE ♦ PARA_X = /'VITE_FLU' /'NB_CONNORS' On the abscissa, the parameter is the excitation velocity of the fluid, of name 'VITE_FLU', or else the Connors number, of name 'NB_CONNORS'. If one has chosen as abscissa the excitation velocity of the fluid 'VITE_FLU', then: ♦ PARA_Y = / 'FREQ', / 'AMOR'. On the ordinate, one has the choice between the frequency (parameter name 'FREQ') or the damping (parameter name 'AMOR'). ♦ / NUME_ORDRE = is, / TOUT_ORDRE= 'OUI', The evolution of the frequency or that of the damping is given for all the fluid velocities (TOUT_ORDRE) or for some order numbers of the fluid velocities (NUME_ORDRE). If one has chosen as abscissa the Connors number 'NB_CONNORS', then there are three possibilities for the ordinate: ♦ PARA_Y = /'VITE_CRIT', [Kn] /'INSTAB_EDF', /'INSTAB_TOUT_CMP', VITE_CRIT permetde tracer la vitesse critique en fonction du nombre de Connors. Pour accéder aux rapports d'instabilité (vitesse efficaces divisées par la vitesse critique), les choix de PARA_Y entre INSTAB_EDF et INSTAB_TOUT_CMP permettent de tracer le rapport calculé avec la méthode Gevibus (méthode EDF) et la méthode conservative (dite toutes composantes) respectivement [:ref: R4.07.04 ]. 3.6 Operand INTE_SPEC One extracts, in a data structure of type interspectre, the frequency evolution of the interspectrum associated with row i and column j of the interspectral matrix intespec. One can also extract the time evolution of one of the functions generated by GENE_FONC_ALEA U4.36.05 by specifying its order number. ♦ INTE_SPEC = intespec 3.6.1 Operand NOM_CHAM ◊ NOM_CHAM= nomsymb Symbolic name of the field on which the extraction bears. 3.6.2 Operands NUME_ORDRE_I, NUME_ORDRE_J ♦ NUME_ORDRE_I = numei ◊ NUME_ORDRE_J = numej Indication of the pair of indices (row i , column j ) to be extracted from the interspectral matrix intespec. These operands are mutually exclusive with the operands NUME_ORDRE NOEUD_I NOM_CMP_I NOEUD_J NOM_CMP_J. Note: It is not compulsory to fill in NUME_ORDRE_J if one wants to extract a term of the diagonal of the matrix. 3.6.3 Operands NUME_ORDRE ♦ NUME_ORDRE = nume Indication of the order number of the time function generated by the operator GENE_FONC_ALEA U4.36.05. These operands are mutually exclusive with the operands NUME_ORDRE_I NUME_ORDRE_J NOEUD_I NOM_CMP_I NOEUD_J NOM_CMP_J. 3.6.4 Operands NOEUD_I, NOM_CMP_I, NOEUD_J, NOM_CMP_J ♦ NOEUD_I = noei ♦ NOM_CMP_I = cmpi ◊ NOEUD_J = noej ◊ NOM_CMP_J = cmpj These operands correspond to the names of the nodes and of the components (row i, column j) of the matrix of the interspectral matrix intespec. These operands are mutually exclusive with the operands NUME_ORDRE_I NUME_ORDRE_J NUME_ORDRE. Note: It is not compulsory to fill in NOEUD_J and NOM_CMP_J if one wants to extract a term of the diagonal of the matrix. 3.7 Operand NAPPE One recovers, in a data structure of type nappe, the function corresponding to a given value of the parameter of the nappe. ♦ VALE_PARA_FONC = np \mathit{np} is the value of the parameter of the nappe for which one wishes to extract the function. There is no interpolation on the parameter of the nappe. CRITERE and PRECISION make it possible to supply \mathit{np} with a given precision. 3.8 Operands for extraction of the field or of the parameter 3.8.1 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM= nomsymb Symbolic name of the field on which the extraction bears. 3.8.2 Operand NOM_PARA_RESU ♦ NOM_PARA_RESU= parametre Symbolic name of the parameter of the data structure which one wants to extract (for example: ETA_PILOTAGE, MASSE_EFFE_DX, MASSE_GENE ...). The extracted function will then have as abscissa the access variable (INST, FREQ...) and as ordinate the value of parametre. 3.8.3 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / TOUT_INST / LIST_ORDRE ♦ / TOUT_ORDRE= 'OUI' (valeur par défaut) This keyword indicates that one wants to extract for all the order numbers already computed. Example: all the time instants for a result of type evol_ . / NUME_ORDRE= l_nume The extraction will be carried out for the order-number values l_nume supplied. / TOUT_INST = 'OUI' This keyword indicates that one wants to extract for all the time instants. > / LIST_ORDRE= l_ord This keyword indicates that one wants to extract at the order numbers described in the concept l_ord of type listis. 3.8.4 Operands INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ ◊ / INST= l_inst This keyword indicates that one wants to extract at the time instants l_inst. / LIST_INST= li_inst This keyword indicates that one wants to extract at the time instants described in the concept li_inst of type listr8. / FREQ = l_freq This keyword indicates that one wants to extract at the frequencies l_freq. / LIST_FREQ= li_freq This keyword indicates that one wants to extract at the frequencies described in the concept li_freq of type listr8. 3.8.5 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ PRECISION= prec This operand makes it possible to indicate that one is looking for the value of the field whose time instant or frequency lies in an interval defined by the absolute or relative position: "inst \pm prec" (cf. CRITERE). By default prec = 1.0D-3 ◊ CRITERE= 'RELATIF': the search interval is [inst(1-prec),inst(1+prec)] 'ABSOLU': the search interval is [inst-prec,inst+prec] 3.8.6 Operand INTERP_NUME ◊ INTER_NUME This keyword defines the type of interpolation between two order numbers. It is valid only in the case where the user has defined a list of time instants or of frequencies. It is possible to forbid interpolation 'NON' or to allow a linear interpolation 'LIN'. Interpolation cannot be used when one extracts the value of a parameter (keyword NOM_PARA_RESU). 3.9 Operands for localisation of the field 3.9.1 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO= grno Name of the node group, containing a single node, on which the extraction bears. 3.9.2 Operands GROUP_MA / GROUP_NO / POINT ♦ GROUP_MA= grma Name of a mesh-cell group (grma), containing a single mesh cell, on which the extraction bears. These keywords concern only the cham_elem. ♦ / GROUP_NO= grno Designates the name of the node group, containing a single node name, on which the extraction bears (case of the cham_elem at the nodes). / POINT= nupoint The integer nupoint specifies the local number, in the element, of the Gauss point from which one wishes to obtain the value (case of the cham_elem at the Gauss points). ◊ SOUS_POINT= nusp The integer nusp specifies the number of the sub-point from which one wishes to obtain the value (case of the cham_elem with sub-points, used by the structural elements: beams, pipes, shells). In the case of multi-layer plates and shells, the sub-point number corresponds to the level in the set of layers. Each layer is described by a lower, middle and upper skin. By convention, for N layers, this number varies between 1 and 3N , where the first point lies at the level of the lower skin of the first layer and the 3N -th point at the level of the upper skin of the last layer (cf. R3.07.03 and R3.07.04 for the numbering of the layers). In the case of multi-fibre beams, this integer is the number of the fibre whose numbering is described in the documentation U4.26.01 and R3.08.08. In the case of pipes, one must refer to the description given in the document R3.08.06. 3.9.3 Operands NOM_CMP/NOM_VARI > ◊ NOM_CMP = nocmp, [Kn] > Name of the component on which the extraction bears. > ◊ NOM_VARI= novari, [Kn] For the fields of internal variables (VARI_ ), one may give the name of the internal variable on which the extraction bears (see U4.51.11 for the naming rules of the internal variables). 3.10 Attributes of the fonction concept created by RECU_FONCTION 3.10.1 Default values By default the attributes of the fonction concept created by the command RECU_FONCTION are: Left prolongation: 'EXCLU' Right prolongation: 'EXCLU' NOM_PARA: given on input NOM_RESU: given on input 3.10.2 Overloading of the attributes The user may overload the attributes given by default by using the following keywords: 3.10.2.1 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA = para It designates the name of the parameter (variable or abscissa) of the function. The values currently allowed for lpara are: / 'TEMP' / 'INST' / 'EPSI' / 'X' / 'Y' / 'Z' / 'FREQ' / 'PULS' / 'AMOR' / 'DX' / 'DY' / 'DZ' / 'DRX' / 'DRY' / 'DRZ' plus those specific to the shock nodes (cf. [§3.3.2.2]). 3.10.2.2 Operand NOM_RESU ◊ NOM_RESU = resu It designates the name of the result; the function thus created is a function whose value has the name lresu (8 characters). 3.10.2.3 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL Type of interpolation of the function between the values of the parameter of the domain of definition. After this keyword one expects a list of parameters (two at most) among 'LIN', 'LOG'. If a single value is given, the interpolation will be the same for the abscissae and the ordinates. If two values are given, the first corresponds to the interpolation of the abscissae and the second to the interpolation of the ordinates. 3.10.2.4 Operands PROL_DROITE /PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE They define the type of prolongation to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable: - 'CONSTANT' for a prolongation with the last (or first) value of the function, - 'LINEAIRE' for a prolongation along the first defined segment (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last defined segment (PROL_DROITE), - 'EXCLU' if the extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden. 3.11 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.12 Operand INFO ◊ INFO Specifies the printout options in the MESSAGE file. | 1 | no printout (by default) | | --- | --- | | 2 | printout of the descriptor of the function and of the list of the first 10 values of the function in increasing order of the first 10 parameters | 4 Examples 4.1 Extractions of a function on the dynamic response of a piping network tran_gen = DYNA_VIBRA( ... ) l_inst = DEFI_LIST_REEL( DEBUT= 0., INTERVALLE= _F( JUSQU_A= 3., PAS= 0.005 ) ) dyn_tran = REST_GENE_PHYS( RESU_GENE= tran_gen, NOM_CHAM= 'DEPL', LIST_INST= l_inst, INTERPOL= 'LIN' ) dyn_tran = CALC_CHAMP( ... , CONTRAINTE = 'SIEF_ELGA' ) tab_rele = POST_RELEVE_T( ACTION=_F( INTITULE = 'sixx_254', CHEMIN = ligne, RESULTAT = dyn_tran, NOM_CHAM = 'SIEF_ELGA', INST = 2.54, TOUT_CMP = 'OUI', OPERATION = 'EXTRACTION' ) ) 4.1.1 Evolution of the displacement of the node NO01, component 'DX', at all the time instants of the analysis f1 = RECU_FONCTION( RESU_GENE= tran_gen, NOM_CHAM= 'DEPL', GROUP_NO= 'GNO01' , NOM_CMP = 'DX' ) 4.1.2 Evolution of the quantity 'SIXX' on the mesh cell MA01 at the node NO01 at all the time instants of the analysis f2 = RECU_FONCTION( RESULTAT= dyn_tran, NOM_CHAM= 'SIEF_ELGA', GROUP_MA= 'GMA01' , GROUP_NO= 'NO01', NOM_CMP='SIXX') 4.1.3 'SIXX' along the piping line (curvilinear abscissa greater than 10) at the analysis time instant 2.54 s f4 = RECU_FONCTION( TABLE= tab_rele, FILTRE= _F( NOM_PARA = 'ABSC_CURV', CRIT_COMP= 'GE', VALE = 10. , ), PARA_X= 'ABSC_CURV', PARA_Y= 'SIXX' ) 4.2 Extraction of a function in a data structure melasflu meles1 = CALC_FLUI_STRU ( ... ) f_freq = RECU_FONCTION ( BASE_ELAS_FLUI = meles1, PARA_X = 'VITE_FLU', PARA_Y = 'FREQ', TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', NUME_MODE = 2 ) 4.3 Extraction of a function in a data structure interspectre reppx_ac = REST_SPEC_PHYS ( ... ) statx_ac = POST_DYNA_ALEA ( INTERSPECTRE = _F( INTE_SPEC = reppx_ac, OPTION = 'DIAG', > ) > ) f_freq = RECU_FONCTION ( INTE_SPEC = statx_ac, NOEUD_I = 'N_TUB_01', NOM_CMP_I = 'DX', )

u4.32.04 Operator CALC_FONCTION u4.32.04 Operator CALC_FONCTION 1 Purpose Carry out mathematical operations on data structures of type fonction. The operator makes it possible to carry out general operations on functions (integration, derivative, absolute value, combination, polynomial regression…) and operations dedicated to signal processing and to the earthquake (calculation of the FFT, envelope smoothing, correction of accelerograms...). Produces a data structure fonction, fonction_c or nappe, according to the factor keyword used.
