It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. The only method (given by METHODE) currently available is DIFF_CENTREE (by default). Note See keyword INTEGRE 3.2 Factor keyword INTEGRE This keyword makes it possible to integrate the function (with respect to its parameter) given by FONCTION. The constant of integration is given by COEF; by default it is 0. It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. Two methods (entered via METHODE) are available: the method of the 'TRAPEZE' (by default) and the 'SIMPSON' method. The integral is exact for the piecewise-linear functions such as those supplied on input. The error committed with respect to the integral of the function which one has discretised is in o(\frac{1}{{n}^{2}}) for functions of class \mathcal{C}^{2} . Simpson's method is exact for polynomials of degree less than or equal to 3. The error is in o(\frac{1}{{n}^{4}}) for functions of class \mathcal{C}^{4} . For arbitrary functions, very irregular, such as accelerograms, it is recommended to use the trapezoidal method. On the other hand, when the function (before discretisation) is sufficiently regular, Simpson's method is much more precise. - For INTEGRE as for DERIVE, the NOM_PARA of the function produced is unchanged. On the other hand, the NOM_RESU may be modified in the following cases: for differentiation, DEPL becomes VITE, VITE becomes ACCE; for integration, ACCE becomes VITE, VITE becomes DEPL. The user always has the possibility of modifying it by the keyword of the same name NOM_RESU in the command. - Concerning the prolongations, the function produced has, by default, EXCLU prolongations to the left and to the right, whatever those of the starting function may be. One should not therefore expect a linear prolongation to become constant in the differentiated function. Here again, the user is in control of the prolongations for the function produced, through the keywords PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE. Notes 3.3 Factor keyword INVERSE This keyword makes it possible to invert the function given by FONCTION. It is necessary that the latter be bijective (strictly increasing or strictly decreasing). It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. - The labels of the parameters are not inverted! It is left to the user to assign the correct values through the keywords NOM_PARA and NOM_RESU. By default, the NOM_PARA is unchanged and NOM_RESU is assigned to TOUTRESU. - The interpolation modes are swapped: for example (LIN, LOG) becomes (LOG,LIN). - The prolongations EXCLU and LINEAIRE are unchanged. On the other hand, a CONSTANT prolongation is changed to EXCLU. Note 3.4 Factor keyword ABS This keyword makes it possible to create a function or a nappe containing the absolute value of a function or of a nappe given by FONCTION. - The parameters (prolongations, interpolations, NOM_PARA and NOM_RESU) of the function produced are the same as those of the starting function. - Except for the LINEAIRE prolongation, it is systematically changed to EXCLU as a precaution. Indeed, the linear prolongation to the right of a decreasing function leads, for sufficiently large abscissae, to negative values: the responsibility is therefore left to the user to assign PROL_DROITE=’LINEAIRE’ himself (and respectively for PROL_GAUCHE). Note 3.5 Factor keyword ENVELOPPE This keyword makes it possible to calculate the envelope of several functions. This operation is available on operands of nature fonction or nappe. The list of functions or nappes whose envelope one seeks is given by the keyword FONCTION. The keyword CRITERE='SUP' seeks the upper envelope and the keyword CRITERE='INF' seeks the lower envelope. - The functions must all be of the same nature (fonction or nappe) - Case of simple functions: for the prolongations, interpolations, NOM_PARA and NOM_RESU, it is the parameters of the first of the functions in the list which are retained. The abscissa support of the envelope function will be the union of the lists of abscissae of all the functions. - Case of nappes: the parameters (prolongations, interpolations, NOM_PARA, NOM_RESU and NOM_PARA_FONC) must necessarily be identical between the nappes supplied. The abscissa supports (values of the parameters and abscissae of the functions of the nappes) are homogenised so that the envelope can be calculated. The nappe produced will have this discretisation as abscissae. Notes 3.6 Factor keyword FRACTILE This keyword makes it possible to calculate the fractile of several functions. This operation is available on operands of nature fonction or nappe. The list of functions or nappes for which one seeks to calculate the fractile is given by FONCTION. FRACT is the value of the quantile to be calculated. By default FRACT = 1; the fractile is then the upper envelope. 3.7 Factor keyword MOYENNE This keyword makes it possible to calculate the mean of several functions given by FONCTION. This operation is available on operands of nature fonction or nappe. 3.8 Factor keyword COHERENCE This keyword makes it possible to calculate the coherence function of time signals. The coherence function depends on the distance between two measurement points and on the frequency. It expresses the correlation between the two signals, measured at a distance d , as a function of the frequency. The complex coherence function is evaluated in the frequency domain, by way of the spectral densities (DSP). The operator returns the real part of the complex coherence, which corresponds to the unlagged coherency or to the plane wave coherency in the case of a plane wave. The time signals must have the same discretisation (same time step {dt} and same duration T ). The user must supply two nappes which contain respectively the signals at stations 1 and 2, a distance d apart. The signals in each nappe are parameterised by NUME_ORDRE (1,2,3,..) and then paired in order to calculate the coherences and to take their mean. 3.8.1 Keywords NAPPE_1 and NAPPE_2 NAPPE_1 contains N functions measured at station 1. The functions of the nappe must be numbered from 1 to N by NOM_PARA = 'NUME_ORDRE'. NAPPE_2 contains N functions measured at station 2. The functions of the nappe must be numbered from 1 to N by NOM_PARA = 'NUME_ORDRE'. 3.8.2 Keyword FREQ_COUP FREQ_COUP is the cut-off frequency for the plotting of the coherence functions. The cut-off frequency must be less than \frac{1}{2 \, dt} , where dt is the time step of the time signals. For the evaluation of the coherence functions, the cut-off frequency is always determined by the time step of the time signals. If FREQ_COUP is filled in, then the coherence function is cut off at this frequency before recovery. 3.8.3 Keyword NB_FREQ_LISS NB_FREQ_LISS is the number of frequency steps used for the smoothing of the DSPs by a Hamming window. The Hamming window obtained with NB_FREQ_LISS = 12 is shown in the figure below. Hamming window for the calculation of the coherence of two functions NOM_PARA is not a keyword of the factor keyword COHERENCE. 3.8.4 Keyword OPTION The keyword OPTION makes it possible to define whether the entire signal or only the strong phase is used for the calculation of the coherence function: - If OPTION='TOUT', one uses the time signals as they are. - If OPTION='DUREE_PHASE_FORTE', one evaluates the coherence function for the duration of the strong phase only. The start and end time instants of the strong phase are calculated for the first signal only. One then uses the same time interval for the other signals. In the case of an earthquake, this assumes that all the records come from the same event. To evaluate the duration of the strong phase, one uses the notion of Arias intensity. One must then fill in the lower and upper bounds (see INFO_FONCTION). 3.8.5 Keywords BORNE_INF and BORNE_SUP The keywords BORNE_INF and BORNE_SUP give the bounds limiting the share of Arias intensity defining the initial and final time instants of the strong phase (they are given as a percentage of the Arias intensity) of the earthquake — the same meaning as for INFO_FONCTION. By default, one takes 5% and 95%. 3.9 Factor keyword COMB This keyword makes it possible to calculate the function giving the real linear combination of several concepts of nature fonction or nappe. The name of the function to be combined is given by FONCTION and the value of the coefficient is given by COEF. One may use the keyword LIST_PARA to give the list of the values of the parameters for which the combination of functions will be discretised. If this keyword is not filled in, a default list is built by taking the union of the lists of the values of the parameters of each function. LIST_PARA is not a keyword of the factor keyword COMB. Note See the notes for the keyword ENVELOPPE 3.10 Factor keyword COMB_C This keyword makes it possible to calculate the function giving the complex linear combination of several concepts of nature fonction_c. The name of the function to be combined is given by FONCTION. The value of the coefficient is given by COEF_C (complex) or COEF_R (real). One may use the keyword LIST_PARA to give the list of the values of the parameters for which the combination of functions will be discretised. If this keyword is not filled in, a default list is built by taking the union of the lists of the values of the parameters of each function. LIST_PARA is not a keyword of the factor keyword COMB_C. Note See the notes for the keyword ENVELOPPE 3.11 Factor keyword MULT This factor keyword makes it possible to multiply several fonction, fonction_c or nappe. It produces a concept of the same nature, fonction, fonction_c or nappe. FONCTION gives the name of the function to be multiplied with the others. LIST_PARA makes it possible to discretise the result function as for COMB. LIST_PARA is not a keyword of the factor keyword MULT. 3.12 Factor keyword COMPOSE This factor keyword makes it possible to calculate the composed function of two functions F(G( \cdot )) . The function F(\cdot) is given by FONC_RESU and G( \cdot ) is given by FONC_PARA. It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. One checks that the NOM_PARA of F(\cdot) does indeed correspond to the NOM_RESU of G( \cdot ) . 3.13 Factor keyword ASSE This factor keyword makes it possible to create a real function by concatenating two tabulated real functions. It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. The functions to be concatenated are given by FONCTION. One expects exactly two functions. The discretisation points of the function created are those of the set of the two functions, modulo the effects of overloading. If the domains of definition of the functions overlap, one of the functions imposes its points on the overlap zone and, for the prolongations, one uses the keyword SURCHARGE: - SURCHARGE= 'DROITE': it is the function which has the largest abscissa which is chosen, - SURCHARGE= 'GAUCHE': it is the function which has the smallest abscissa which is chosen. One checks that all the functions have the same NOM_PARA, as well as the same interpolations. 3.14 Factor keyword EXTRACTION This factor keyword makes it possible to build, from a complex function (type fonct_c), a real function representing either the real part, or the imaginary part, or the modulus, or the phase of the complex function. The (complex) function to be treated is given by the keyword FONCTION. The keyword PARTIE makes it possible to choose which extraction operation to carry out | Value of PARTIE | Operation | | --- | --- | | REEL | extraction of the real part of the function | | IMAG | extraction of the imaginary part of the function | | MODULE | calculation of the modulus of the function | | PHASE | calculation of the phase (in degrees) of the function | 3.15 Factor keyword PUISSANCE The factor keyword PUISSANCE makes it possible to build the n-th power of a function or of a set of functions supplied in the form of a nappe. The result function calculated will be f{(\cdot)}^{n} . The function to be treated f{(\cdot)} is given by the keyword FONCTION and the exponent n will be given by EXPOSANT. By default, n=1 . 3.16 Factor keyword REGR_POLYNOMIALE The factor keyword REGR_POLYNOMIALE calculates the polynomial regression of a function by the least-squares method (using the function polyfit of numpy ). The function to be treated f{(\cdot)} is given by the keyword FONCTION and the degree of the polynomial sought is given by DEGRE. One may use the keyword LIST_PARA to tabulate the polynomial calculated. Otherwise, it is tabulated on the list of the abscissae of the function f{(\cdot)} . LIST_PARA is not a keyword of the factor keyword REGR_POLYNOMIALE. 3.17 Factor keyword FFT The factor keyword FFT calculates the direct or inverse Fourier transform of a function (hence by the FFT algorithm). The name of the function on which the operation is carried out is given by FONCTION. If the NOM_PARA of the function is INST, then the direct FFT is calculated. If the NOM_PARA of the function is FREQ, then the inverse FFT is calculated. It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. The FFT algorithm is faster for samples whose length is a power of 2. 3.17.1 Keyword METHODE The keyword METHODE makes it possible to choose the way of treating the cases where the sample is not a power of two: - The method 'PROL_ZERO' (by default) proposes to extend the input signal with zeros until one has a total number of samples which is the first power of 2 whose value is greater than the initial number of samples. - The method 'TRONCATURE' will consider only the first samples whose total number is the greatest power of two whose value is less than the initial number of samples. - The method 'COMPLET' makes it possible to take into account the whole of the input signal, whatever the number of samples. For example, on a signal of 601 values, the method 'PROL_ZERO' will complete the signal so as to have 1024 samples, whereas the method 'TRONCATURE' will consider only the first 512 time instants. If the input signal has a number of samples which is a power of two, the two methods are of course equivalent: one takes the signal into account without modifying it. Note In the case of a sample of length N , whose time step would be dt , the sampling frequency of the FFT is \frac{1}{N \, dt} . On the other hand, the last frequency for which the discrete transform is calculated is not \frac{1}{dt} , but \frac{N-1}{N \, dt} . 3.17.2 Keyword SYME The keyword SYME applies only to the inverse Fourier transform. In the case where one were to supply the complete spectrum, the inverse transform is calculated directly by using SYME = 'OUI'. The methods 'TRONCATURE' and 'PROL_ZERO' are then not active. If the (complex) spectrum supplied on input to the inverse FFT does not contain the folded part (associated with the negative frequencies of the spectrum), one can nevertheless estimate a time signal having the same spectral content on the part associated with the positive frequencies. If one denotes by {X}_{k} the k -th sample of the Fourier transform of a sample of length N , then one has {X}_{k}={X}_{(N-k)}^{\text{ }} , where {(\cdot)}^{\text{ }} corresponds to the complex conjugate. This information can be exploited to reconstruct a time signal while knowing only half of the spectrum. This operation is carried out when one chooses SYME = 'NON'. The time signal is then reconstructed so as to obtain a time sample of even length. In theory, in order to reconstruct a time signal of length 2 \times M , the spectrum must satisfy certain conditions: - The spectrum must be of length M+1 , - The first point of the spectrum must be real, - The last point of the spectrum must be real. If these conditions are not satisfied, then one builds an approximate spectrum of odd length satisfying these conditions. If the initial spectrum is of even length, the last point is then reconstructed by carrying out a prolongation by interpolation of the initial spectrum. This reconstruction may introduce a slight bias when the spectral content of the sample is very significant on the last points of the spectrum. The methods 'TRONCATURE' and 'PROL_ZERO' are still available for the inverse FFT. Take care, however, with the use of the method 'TRONCATURE'. If the number of truncated points is significant, then the results may be very appreciably different. 3.18 Factor keyword INTERPOL_FFT The factor keyword INTERPOL_FFT carries out the interpolation of an accelerogram by the "zero padding" method. This method consists in calculating the Fourier transform of the initial signal, in completing the frequency signal obtained with new frequencies of zero value, then in calculating the inverse Fourier transform of this modified frequency signal. This functionality uses the same algorithms as the keyword FFT. The method is necessarily 'COMPLET' and SYME = 'NON'. It makes it possible not to add frequency content to the interpolated function. The name of the function on which the operation is carried out is given by FONCTION. The NOM_PARA of the function is necessarily the time INST. The keyword PAS_INST makes it possible to give the time increment desired for the interpolated signal. It must be smaller than the time increment of the function supplied. The time step actually obtained is often slightly different from that indicated via PAS_INST. The keyword PRECISION defines the maximum difference desired between these two values; if it is exceeded, an alarm message is issued in order to warn the user. 3.19 Factor keyword CORR_ACCE The factor keyword CORR_ACCE makes it possible to correct an accelerogram (seismic signal in acceleration) so that the displacement signal does not possess a drift. One returns on output the corrected accelerogram. The signal may then be integrated by the standard methods (keyword INTEGRE of CALC_FONCTION). It is advisable to check the quality of the result by checking the absence of drift of the displacement signal and by comparing the response spectra before and after modification. The name of the function on which the operation is carried out is given by FONCTION. This is the real accelerogram measured. It does not apply to concepts of type nappe. 3.19.1 Keyword METHODE The keyword METHODE makes it possible to designate the method which one wishes to use in order to correct the signals: correction by polynomials or by filtering in the frequency domain. For the correction by polynomials (METHODE='POLYNOME'), one removes the drift of the signal, calculated by linear smoothing in the least-squares sense over the whole of the signal. The drift of the corresponding relative velocity is also removed, unless CORR_DEPL='NON'. In this latter case, one does not correct the drift of the relative displacement; this is the default value. If CORR_DEPL='OUI', one also removes the drift of the relative displacement. This option is to be used with caution, because one does not know a priori the value of the final displacement after the earthquake. For the correction by filtering (METHODE='FILTRAGE'), one removes the drift by filtering ("passe_haut") of the signal in the frequency domain. This filter is described in the documentation R4.05.05. The frequency of the filter is given by the keyword FREQ_FILTRE. One must choose the smallest frequency which makes it possible to obtain the desired effect, namely to remove the drift, without (too greatly) altering the other properties of the signal. By default, the frequency of the filter is 0.05Hz. This value is generally well suited to seismic signals. This value may be decreased if the signal allows it, or increased if a drift persists. 3.20 Factor keyword LISS_ENVELOP The name of the input nappe or nappes formed of the raw spectra associated with each damping level is given by the keyword NAPPE. The nappe therefore depends on the parameters frequency and damping. The name of the input table or tables formed of the raw spectra associated with each damping level is given by the keyword TABLE. In the expected format, the first column contains the values of the frequencies; each of the following columns contains the value of the acceleration associated with the frequency for a given damping level. The values of the dampings are given by LIST_AMOR. The name of the function formed of the raw spectrum associated with a damping level is given by the keyword FONCTION. The keyword OPTION makes it possible to choose the method associated with the smoothing of the envelopes. - Option CONCEPTION: the first step consists in producing an envelope of the spectra supplied. In a second step, one carries out the smoothing of the spectrum obtained as a function of the number of smoothed points requested by the keyword NB_FREQ_LISS. - Option VERIFICATION: the first step consists in carrying out a smoothing of each spectrum supplied according to the number of points requested. Then, one carries out a broadening of each spectrum according to the coefficients supplied in ELARG. In a third step, the envelope of the broadened spectra is calculated. Finally the last step carries out the smoothing of the spectrum obtained as a function of the number of smoothed points requested. NB_FREQ_LISS gives the number of frequencies desired for the smoothed spectrum. In the case of the option 'CONCEPTION', one supplies only one value. For the option 'VERIFICATION', one may supply two values which will be applied to the first step and to the fourth step. The frequency range of definition of the smoothed spectrum is given by FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX. The frequencies mentioned under FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX must be chosen from among the discretisation frequencies of the raw spectrum. By default, one considers the complete spectrum. The broadening is activated by the keyword ELARG; it bears on the whole of a spectrum for the option VERIFICATION. One must supply as many values with ELARG as there are numbers of nappes or tables. For each frequency {F}_{i} : of the raw spectrum, one defines two new frequency values such that: {F}^{-} = {F}_{i}(1-{\tau}_{g}) \text{ avec } 0 INTERVALLE=_F( JUSQU_A = DEPI, PAS = PAS0) ) COa = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='INST',VALE='cos(INST)') SIa = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='INST',VALE='sin(INST)') CO = CALC_FONC_INTERP( FONCTION=COa, LIST_PARA=LI1, NOM_PARA='INST', NOM_RESU='DEPL', PROL_GAUCHE='EXCLU', PROL_DROITE='LINEAIRE', INTERPOL='LIN', TITRE=' FONCTION COSINUS' ) SI = CALC_FONC_INTERP( FONCTION=SIa, LIST_PARA=LI1, NOM_PARA='INST', NOM_RESU='DEPLACEMENT', PROL_GAUCHE='EXCLU', PROL_DROITE='CONSTANT', INTERPOL='LIN', TITRE=' FONCTION SINUS ' ) ENV1=CALC_FONCTION( ENVELOPPE=_F( FONCTION = ( SI, CO, ), CRITERE = 'SUP') ) 4.2 Calculation of the derivative of the function si The commands which follow der1 = CALC_FONCTION( DERIVE=_F( FONCTION= si ),) inst1 = 20. pas TEST_FONCTION( VALEUR= _F( FONCTION = der1, NOM_PARA = 'inst', VALE_PARA= inst1, VALE_REFE= COa(inst1),) ) produce on the file 'RESULTAT': ---- FONCTION : DER1 OK INST RELA -0.016 % VALE: 8.0888392298046D-01 6.28319E-01 TOLE 0.100 % REFE: 8.0901699437495D-01 4.3 Concatenation of two functions DFC1=DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA='X', NOM_RESU='Y', VALE=( 0., 10., 4., 14., 6., 16.,), PROL_DROITE='LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE='LINEAIRE' ) # DFC2=DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA='X', NOM_RESU='Y', VALE=( 5., 25., 7., 27., 8., 28.,), PROL_DROITE='LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE='LINEAIRE' ) # DFC3=CALC_FONCTION( ASSE=_F( FONCTION = ( DFC2, DFC1, ), SURCHARGE = 'DROITE') ) DFC4=CALC_FONCTION( ASSE=_F( FONCTION = ( DFC1, DFC2, ), SURCHARGE = 'GAUCHE') ) The values of the function dfc3 are: x = 0. 4. 5. 7. 8. y = 10. 14. 25. 27. 28.
