u4.32.05 Operator INFO_FONCTION u4.32.05 Operator INFO_FONCTION 1 Purpose Carry out mathematical operations on data structures of type fonction. The following operations are currently available: - the search for the maxima of a function, - the calculation of the {L}_{2} norm of a function, - the standard deviation of a function, - the RMS value of a function, - the value of the earthquake harmfulness indicator. Produces a data structure table. 2 Syntax table = INFO_FONCTION( ◆ / RMS = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "SIMPSON", / "TRAPEZE" (par défaut), ◆ FONCTION = fonction, ◇ INST_INIT = float, ◇ INST_FIN = float, ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), / MAX = _F( ◆ FONCTION = nappe / fonction, ◇ INTERVALLE = float, ), / NOCI_SEISME = _F( ◆ / FONCTION = fonction, / SPEC_OSCI = nappe, # Si: exists("FONCTION") ◇ OPTION = / "INTE_ARIAS", / "INTE_SPEC", / "VITE_ABSO_CUMU", / "DUREE_PHAS_FORT", / "MAXI", / "ACCE_SUR_VITE", / "ASA", / "TOUT" (par défaut), # Si: is_in('OPTION', ("TOUT", "ASA")) ◆ FREQ_FOND = float, ◇ FREQ_PAS = float (défaut: 0.01), ◇ NORME = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ RATIO = float (défaut: 0.4), # Si: is_in('OPTION', ("TOUT", "INTE_SPEC","ASA" )) ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, # Si: is_in('OPTION', ("TOUT", "INTE_ARIAS", "DUREE_PHAS_FORT")) ◆ PESANTEUR = float, # Si: exists("SPEC_OSCI") ◇ OPTION = "INTE_SPEC", ◆ NATURE = / "DEPL", / "VITE", / "ACCE", ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ INST_INIT = float, ◇ INST_FIN = float, ◇ COEF = float, ◇ FREQ_INIT = float (défaut: 0.4), ◇ FREQ_FIN = float (défaut: 10.0), ◇ LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ FREQ = float, ◇ NORME = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ BORNE_INF = float (défaut: 0.05), ◇ BORNE_SUP = float (défaut: 0.95), # Si: (exists("INST_INIT"))or(exists("INST_FIN"))or(exists("FREQ_INIT"))or(exists("FREQ_FIN")) ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), / NORME = _F( ◆ FONCTION = nappe, ), / ECART_TYPE = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "SIMPSON", / "TRAPEZE" (par défaut), ◆ FONCTION = fonction, ◇ INST_INIT = float, ◇ INST_FIN = float, ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword MAX / MAX = Search for the abscissae where the maximum and the minimum are reached. This operation is available on functions of nature fonction or nappe. ♦ FONCTION = f Name of the function or of the functions whose maxima are sought. If f is a fonction, the concept produced is a table whose access parameters are: > FONCTION, TYPE, the NOM_PARA of the function, the NOM_RESU of the function. where one finds respectively the name of the function, MAXI or MINI, the abscissa of the maximum/minimum, the value of the maximum/minimum. When several factors are supplied, the table contains the max or the maxima of the maxima, and the min or the minima of the minima. If f is a nappe, the concept produced is a table whose access parameters are: > FONCTION, TYPE, the NOM_PARA of the nappe, the name of the parameter of the functions (NOM_PARA_FONC), the NOM_RESU of the functions. ◊ INTERVALLE = inter List of reals defining the bounds of the intervals over which the minima and the maxima of the functions will be sought. inter is composed of pairs of reals of which the first corresponds to the lower bound of the first interval, the second corresponds to the upper bound of the first interval, and so on for the other intervals. inter is therefore composed of an even number of elements. This keyword is not taken into account for nappes. 3.2 Keyword NORME This keyword makes it possible to monitor the convergence according to the {L}_{2} norm of a sequence of functions {f}_{N} given in the form of a nappe. The result table has one line per function; the input parameters are NORME and FONCTION. ♦ FONCTION = f Name of the nappe whose norm is to be evaluated. 3.3 Keyword ECART_TYPE / ECART_TYPE = One calculates the standard deviation of the function f(t) which is defined by: \sigma =\sqrt{\frac{1}{({t}_{\mathit{fin}}-{t}_{\mathit{deb}})}{\int}_{{t}_{\mathit{deb}}}^{{t}_{\mathit{fin}}}{(f(t)-\bar{f})}^{2}\mathit{dt}} where \bar{f} is the mean over [{t}_{\mathrm{deb}},{t}_{\mathrm{fin}}] The keywords are identical to those supplied under the factor keyword RMS. The concept produced is a table whose access parameters are: FONCTION, METHODE, MOYENNE, INST_INIT, INST_FIN, ECART_TYPE. 3.4 Keyword RMS / RMS = One calculates the RMS value of the function f(t) which is defined by: \mathrm{RMS}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{({t}_{\mathrm{fin}}-{t}_{\mathrm{deb}})}{\int}_{{t}_{\mathrm{deb}}}^{{t}_{\mathrm{fin}}}{f}^{2}(t)\mathrm{dt}} ♦ FONCTION = f Name of the function whose RMS value is calculated. Does not apply to concepts of type nappe. ◊ METHODE = Name of the METHODE used to calculate the integral. Two methods are available: the 'TRAPEZE' method (by default) and the 'SIMPSON' method. ◊ INST_INIT = tdeb, ◊ INST_FIN = tfin, Lower and upper bounds of the integration interval. If these values are not supplied, the lower and upper discretisation points (the order relation being defined with respect to the abscissa parameter) are taken as the bounds of the integration interval. ◊ PRECISION = / 0.001, / prec, ◊ CRITERE = / 'ABSOLU', / 'RELATIF', [DEFAUT] One looks for a discretisation point of the function in an interval defined by the absolute or relative position around a value of the abscissa parameter for which the function is to be estimated: | [inst (1-prec) , inst (1+prec)] | if CRITERE= 'RELATIF' | | --- | --- | | [inst - prec , inst + prec] | if CRITERE= 'ABSOLU' | The concept produced is a table whose access parameters are: FONCTION, METHODE, INST_INIT, INST_FIN, RMS. 3.5 Keyword NOCI_SEISME / NOCI_SEISME = ♦ / FONCTION = f, / SPEC_OSCI= sro, Name of the function (acceleration signal a(t) ) or of the nappe considered, which must be defined in DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02 with NOM_RESU=’ACCE’. If a nappe is considered, only the calculation of the spectral intensity is available. ◊ / OPTION= Makes it possible to choose one or more of the following six harmfulness indices: | 'TOUT' gives the set of the six harmfulness indices, | 'MAXI' gives the maximum of the acceleration a(t) , of the velocity v(t) and of the displacement (obtained by integration) \mathit{PGA}=\underset{t\in [{t}_{i},{t}_{f}]}{max}\left\lbrace ∣a(t)∣\right\rbrace , \mathrm{PGV}=\underset{t\in [{t}_{i},{t}_{f}]}{\max}\left\lbrace ∣v(t)∣\right\rbrace , \mathrm{PGD}=\underset{t\in [{t}_{i},{t}_{f}]}{\max}\left\lbrace ∣x(t)∣\right\rbrace | 'INTE_ARIAS' gives the Arias intensity {I}_{A}=\frac{\pi}{2g}{\int}_{{t}_{i}}^{{t}_{f}}{a}^{2}(t)\mathit{dt} where g is the acceleration of gravity. This value must be supplied via the keyword PESANTEUR. | 'VITE_ABSO_CUMU' gives the cumulative absolute velocity \mathit{CAV}={\int}_{{t}_{i}}^{{t}_{f}}∣a(t)∣\mathit{dt} | 'DUREE_PHAS_FORT' strong-phase duration (the Arias intensity being a monotonically increasing function): Minimum duration {t}_{\sup}-{t}_{\inf} such that, for the bounds {b}_{\inf},{b}_{\sup} : {b}_{\inf}\times {I}_{A}⩽\frac{\pi}{2g}{\int}_{{t}_{inf}}^{{t}_{\sup}}{a}^{2}(f)\mathit{dt}⩽{b}_{\sup}\times {I}_{A} where g must be supplied by the keyword PESANTEUR. The table produced contains {t}_{inf} under DEBUT_PHAS_FORT. | 'ASA'(Average Spectral Acceleration) This indicator is based on the spectral pseudo-acceleration of the structure and depends on its fundamental frequency. Damage, characterised by a drop in this natural frequency, is taken into account by integrating the spectral pseudo-accelerations {S}_{a}(f,\eta ) over a frequency range: > {\mathit{ASA}}_{R}=\frac{1}{R{f}_{0}}{\int}_{(1-R){f}_{0}}^{{f}_{0}}{S}_{a}(f,\eta )\mathit{df} where R denotes the ratio defining the integration domain and \eta is the reduced damping. The value of the ratio may be supplied by the user via the keyword RATIO. By default, one determines {\mathit{ASA}}_{40} with R=0.4 and reduced damping \eta =0.05 . The keyword FREQ_PAS makes it possible to define the integration step. The spectral pseudo-acceleration will be normalised to the NORME supplied (by default 1.0). Housner spectral intensity, between the frequencies {f}_{\mathrm{deb}},{f}_{\mathrm{fin}} , {S}_{V}(f,\eta ) denoting the oscillator response spectrum in pseudo-velocities for the reduced damping \eta : {I}_{H}={\int}_{{f}_{\mathit{deb}}}^{{f}_{\mathit{fin}}}\frac{{S}_{V}(f,\eta )}{{f}^{2}}\mathit{df} \text{ACCE\_SUR\_VITE}=\frac{\underset{t\in [{t}_{i},{t}_{f}]}{max}\left\lbrace ∣a(t)∣\right\rbrace }{\underset{t\in [{t}_{i},{t}_{f}]}{max}\left\lbrace ∣\nu (t)∣\right\rbrace } Depending on the option, certain parameters must be supplied; if no option is indicated, by default all the indices are calculated and therefore everything must be supplied. The integration method is the 'TRAPEZE' method. INST_INIT = tdeb, INST_FIN = tfin, Lower and upper bounds of the time interval considered. If these values are not supplied, the lower and upper discretisation points (the order relation being defined with respect to the abscissa parameter) are taken as the bounds of the interval. PRECISION = / 0.001, / prec, CRITERE = / 'ABSOLU', / 'RELATIF', [DEFAUT] One looks for a discretisation point of the function in an interval defined by the absolute or relative position around a value of the abscissa parameter for which the function is to be estimated: | [inst (1-prec) , inst (1+prec)] | if CRITERE= 'RELATIF' | | --- | --- | | [inst - prec , inst + prec] | if CRITERE= 'ABSOLU' | | [freq (1-prec) , freq (1+prec)] | if CRITERE= 'RELATIF' | | [freq - prec , freq + prec] | if CRITERE= 'ABSOLU' | COEF = r1 Integration constant, 0 by default. In the option 'MAXI', the velocity and the displacement are calculated by two successive integrations of the damping; COEF must therefore be supplied if one does not wish to take it by default. FREQ_INIT = fdeb, FREQ_FIN = ffin, Frequencies representing the two integration bounds for the calculation of the Housner spectral intensity. These must lie between the extrema of the frequency base defining the SRO nappe, otherwise an interpolation problem arises. By default, these two frequencies are equal to 0,4\mathrm{Hz} and \mathrm{10Hz} . AMOR_REDUIT= am Reduced damping, for the calculation of the oscillator response spectrum within that of the Housner spectral intensity. FREQ = lfre fre = ({\Phi}_{1,}\mathrm{...},{\Phi}_{i},\mathrm{...}) . List of frequencies. LIST_FREQ = lfreq List of the frequencies supplied under a listr8 concept. NORME = r2 The oscillator spectrum will be normalised to the value r2 (value of the pseudo-acceleration). BORNE_INF = binf, BORNE_SUP = bsup, Bounds limiting the share of Arias intensity defining the initial and final time instants of the strong phase (between ({b}_{\inf})\text{\%} and ({b}_{\sup})\text{\%} of {({I}_{A})}_{\max} ) of the earthquake (one often takes 5% and 95%). > PESANTEUR Acceleration of gravity. Its value depending on the units of the model, this keyword is mandatory for the indices INTE_ARIAS, DUREE_PHAS_FORT. 3.6 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = t Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.7 Operand INFO ◊ INFO If INFO=2, the function is printed (IMPR_FONCTION format TABLEAU) in the MESSAGE file. 4 Examples 4.1 Without an interval A5=DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_RESU='SIGM', NOM_PARA='EPSI', VALE=( 0.002, 400.0, 0.003, 500.0, 0.0045, 550.0, 0.0065, 580.0, 0.008, 590.0, 0.01, 600.0, 0.02, 600.0, ), PROL_DROITE='CONSTANT', PROL_GAUCHE='LINEAIRE', ) tab = INFO_FONCTION(MAX=_F(FONCTION=A5),) IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=tab) gives, in the 'RESULTAT' file. # #ASTER 8.02.00 CONCEPT tab CALCULE LE 24/01/2006 A 16:14:04 DE TYPE #TABLE_SDASTER FONCTION TYPE EPSI SIGM A5 MINI 2.00000E-03 4.00000E+02 A5 MAXI 1.00000E-02 6.00000E+02 A5 MAXI 2.00000E-02 6.00000E+02 4.2 With intervals tab2 = INFO_FONCTION(MAX = _F(FONCTION=A5), INTERVALLE=(0.002, 0.005, 0.006, 0,02),),) IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=tab2) gives, in the 'RESULTAT' file. # #ASTER 8.02.00 CONCEPT tab2 CALCULE LE 24/01/2006 A 16:14:04 DE TYPE #TABLE_SDASTER #Calcul des extremas sur fonction A5 sur chaque intervalle FONCTION TYPE INTERVALLE EPSI_MIN EPSI_MAX EPSI SIGM A5 MINI 1 2.00000E-03 5.00000E-032.00000E-03 4.00000E+02 A5 MAXI 1 2.00000E-03 5.00000E-03 2.00000E-03 5.50000E+02 A5 MINI 2 6.00000E-03 2.00000E-036.00000E-03 5.80000E+02 A5 MAXI 2 6.00000E-03 2.00000E-03 1.00000E-02 6.00000E+02 A5 MAXI 2 6.00000E-03 2.00000E-03 2.00000E-02 6.00000E+02

u4.32.11 Macro-command MACR_SPECTRE u4.32.11 Macro-command MACR_SPECTRE 1 Purpose This macro-command makes it possible to carry out a fast and efficient post-processing analysis in order to determine the floor spectra of any building after a seismic dynamic analysis. It may for example be used after a transient dynamic analysis of a building under earthquake loading, in which the connections between the soil and the raft in single-support or multi-support conditions are simulated by a soil stiffness (DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03, transient dynamic analysis on a reduced modal basis, calculated in the relative reference frame, concept produced: resu_gene) or after analyses coming from the Code_Aster – ProMiss3D coupling (CALC_MISS U7.03.12, concept produced: tran_gene or harm_gene) or else following a non-linear transient dynamic solution (DYNA_NON_LINE, concept evol_noli, and on the observation table coming from an analysis of this type). This macro-command executes successively: - the extraction of the relative acceleration at one or more nodes of the mesh in the result concept (RECU_FONCTION U4.32.03); - the combination with the ground acceleration in order to obtain the absolute acceleration (CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04); - the calculation of the acceleration response spectrum with several damping coefficients (CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04); - the envelope function of the relative displacement or of the acceleration corresponding to a given floor. - the printout of the envelope spectra by floor and by direction. - the creation of a table for the envelope spectra of all the floors. For practical examples of implementation, the reader may refer to the test cases SDNL131 (post-processing of a piping analysis), SDNV112 (civil-engineering building under multi-support seismic loading) or to the tests SDLX101, SDLX101, MISS01, MISS05 with a Code_Aster – Miss3D coupling analysis. The macro-command produces a concept of type table_sdaster. 2 Syntax table = MACR_SPECTRE( ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: exists("MAILLAGE") ◆ PLANCHER = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◇ BATIMENT = text, ◇ COMMENTAIRE = text, ◆ | GROUP_NO = grno, ), # Si: not exists("MAILLAGE") ◆ PLANCHER = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◇ BATIMENT = text, ◇ COMMENTAIRE = text, ◆ NOEUD = no, ), ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "ACCE", / "DEPL", ◆ CALCUL = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF", ◇ ENVELOPPE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("NOM_CHAM", 'ACCE') and equal_to("CALCUL", 'RELATIF') ◆ AMOR_SPEC = float, ◇ LIST_INST = listr8, ◆ / LIST_FREQ = listr8, / FREQ = float, ◆ NORME = float, ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / RESU_GENE = tran_gene, / RESULTAT = dyna_trans / evol_noli, ◆ ACCE_X = fonction, ◆ ACCE_Y = fonction, ◆ ACCE_Z = fonction, ), # Si: equal_to("NOM_CHAM", 'ACCE') and equal_to("CALCUL", 'ABSOLU') ◆ AMOR_SPEC = float, ◇ LIST_INST = listr8, ◆ / LIST_FREQ = listr8, / FREQ = float, ◆ NORME = float, ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / RESU_GENE = tran_gene, / RESULTAT = dyna_trans / evol_noli, ), ◇ MULT_APPUI = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), # Si: equal_to("NOM_CHAM", 'ACCE') ◇ IMPRESSION = _F( ◇ TRI = / "AMOR_SPEC" (par défaut), / "DIRECTION", ◇ FORMAT = / "TABLEAU" (par défaut), / "XMGRACE", ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 29), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'XMGRACE') ◇ PILOTE = / "" (par défaut), / "EPS", / "INTERACTIF", / "JPEG", / "MIF", / "PDF", / "PNG", / "PNM", / "POSTSCRIPT", / "SVG", ◇ TOUT = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ), # Si: equal_to("NOM_CHAM", 'DEPL') and equal_to("CALCUL", 'RELATIF') ◇ LIST_INST = listr8, ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / RESU_GENE = tran_gene, / RESULTAT = dyna_trans / evol_noli, ), # Si: equal_to("NOM_CHAM", 'DEPL') and equal_to("CALCUL", 'ABSOLU') ◇ LIST_INST = listr8, ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / RESU_GENE = tran_gene, / RESULTAT = dyna_trans / evol_noli, ◆ DEPL_X = fonction, ◆ DEPL_Y = fonction, ◆ DEPL_Z = fonction, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands The classical post-processing of a seismic analysis in transient dynamics consists in carrying out the following calculations: - The floor spectrum obtained from the absolute accelerations, for each direction \text{X},\text{Y},\text{Z} , calculated at a specified node of the mesh (for example in the case of a «stick» model); - The envelope of the floor spectrum, calculated at a few nodes of the same floor, for each direction \text{X} , \text{Y} , \text{Z} and \text{H} (maximum between \text{X} and \text{Y} ), (for example in the case of a 3D building structure); - The envelope displacements of the structure relative to the ground motions. - Three operators of Code_Aster can produce result concepts corresponding to transient dynamic analyses: - DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 produces a resu_gene concept, including the relative acceleration and displacement fields. In this case, the ground accelerations must be added in order to obtain the absolute accelerations, which are necessary for the calculation of the floor spectrum. - CALC_MISS U7.03.12 produces a tran_gene or harm_gene concept, including the absolute acceleration and displacement fields. In this case, the accelerations are used directly for the calculation of the floor spectrum; conversely, subtraction of the ground displacements is mandatory (to be read with the command LIRE_FONCTION U4.32.02 from a specific file given by its logical unit) in order to obtain the relative displacements. - DYNA_NON_LINE U4.53.01. The treatment is then the same as for the previous point. Here is a schematic of the calculation algorithm of this macro-command: Loop #1 over the floors Loop #2 over the floor nodes Loop #3 over the 3 directions > Loop #4 over the results • Recovery of the relative acceleration functions at the nodes: RECU_FONCTION • If acceleration calculation: ◦ Combination or not with the ground acceleration function: CALC_FONCTION/COMB ◦ Calculation of the response spectrum, with specified values of frequencies and of damping with CALC_FONCTION/SPEC_OSCI • If displacement calculation (absolute displacements): ◦ The ground displacements are subtracted in order to obtain the relative displacements: CALC_FONCTION/COMB . End of loop #4 • In the case of the acceleration calculation: ◦ calculation of the mean value for a given node and a given direction: CALC_FONCTION/COMB • In the case of the displacement calculation: ◦ recovery of the maxima End of loop #3 • Printout of the acceleration spectrum for each node and each direction > : IMPR_FONCTION End of loop #2 • Envelopes of the acceleration spectrum for a given floor, or maximum displacements CALC_FONCTION/ENVELOPPE • Envelopes of the acceleration spectrum for each floor, for each direction > IMPR_FONCTION End of loop #1 The table produced by the macro-command contains 3 types of entries: - the calculated spectra: - in the case of a displacement calculation: the envelope spectra on each floor; - in the case of an acceleration calculation: the envelope spectra by floor and by specified damping values. - the correspondence between the damping indices and the values of these dampings; - the information (name, building, details) on the floors. 3.1 Keyword MAILLAGE This keyword corresponds to the mesh read by the operator LIRE_MAILLAGE U4.21.01. This keyword is optional. Knowledge of the mesh is necessary only in the case where the user uses the simple keyword GROUP_NO of the factor keyword PLANCHER. Indeed, as described in the previous algorithm, the treatment is carried out on the nodes and, if the user gives directly the name of the nodes present in the table, the mesh is not necessary. 3.2 Keyword PLANCHER This keyword is mandatory in order to define the names of the floors, where the spectra will be calculated. These names will be used to select or filter the display parameters in the table structure produced by the macro-command table_sdaster. 3.2.1 Operand NOM This mandatory operand makes it possible to name the floor considered. 3.2.2 Operand BATIMENT This optional operand makes it possible to supply the name of the building to which the floor belongs. This information will then appear in the output table. 3.2.3 Operand COMMENTAIRE This optional operand makes it possible to give a comment. This information will then appear in the output table. It must not exceed 24 characters. 3.2.4 Operand GROUP_NO This operand makes it possible to define the nodes making up the floor where the spectra will be calculated. It is available only if the mesh has been supplied. 3.3 Keyword CALCUL This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define the nature of the transient dynamic analysis used for the post-processing: in the absolute reference frame ('ABSOLU') or the relative reference frame ('RELATIF'). 3.4 Keyword ENVELOPPE This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define whether the output spectra must be edited with or without (respectively ENVELOPPE = 'OUI' or ENVELOPPE = 'NON' ) the envelope of the two horizontal directions. The two horizontal directions are commonly denoted X and Y and their envelope is denoted H . 3.5 Keyword NOM_CHAM This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define the nature of the field used: accelerations ('ACCE') or displacements ('DEPL'). 3.6 Case NOM_CHAM ='ACCE' In this case, the user must supply the following data required for the calculation of the acceleration response spectrum: in the 3 directions \text{X} , \text{Y} , \text{Z} (vertical) and \text{H} (maximum horizontal value between the values along \text{X} and \text{Y} ). 3.6.1 Operand AMOR_SPEC This mandatory operand makes it possible to define the values of the reduced damping coefficient used in the calculation of the spectral response. See also CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04, keyword SPEC_OSCI. 3.6.2 Operand LIST_INST This optional operand makes it possible to specify the list, produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01, defining all the time steps for the transient dynamic analysis. 3.6.3 Operand FREQ / LIST_FREQ / ◊ FREQ = L_FR L_FR = (f1,f2, f3, ...) fi. frequencies. / ◊ LIST_FREQ = LFREQ List of frequencies previously defined by a listr8 concept. This optional operand makes it possible to define the frequency values; see also CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04, keyword SPEC_OSCI. 3.6.4 Operand NORME ♦ NORME = r The response spectrum will be normalised by the value \text{r} (pseudo-acceleration value). The analyses are carried out in most cases in units of the International System (USI) and the acceleration histories are often given in units . The response spectra are generally given with . Thus, this mandatory operand NORME may be used as a unit-conversion factor between the calculated accelerations and the response spectrum; see also CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04, keyword SPEC_OSCI. 3.6.5 Keyword RESU This mandatory keyword makes it possible to specify the names of the result concepts in which the nodal accelerations are considered. The possible values are: > / 'RESU_GENE' = TG [TRAN_GENE] if the post-processing is carried out from a DYNA_VIBRA concept U4.53.03 (transient dynamics on a reduced modal basis). However, this result must be calculated in the relative reference frame or: > / 'RESULTAT' = RESU [DYNA_TRANS] [EVOL_NOLI] if the post-processing is carried out from a transient-dynamics result (coming for example from CALC_MISS U7.03.12, concept produced: tran_gene or harm_gene, or from DYNA_NON_LINE, concept produced: evol_noli). or: > / 'TABLE' = TAB [TABLE_SDASTER] if the post-processing is carried out from a table containing the results to be read. Typically, an observation table derived from a transient dynamic analysis. 3.6.6 Case CALCUL ='RELATIF' ♦ ACCE_X = /AC_X [FONCTION] ♦ ACCE_Y = /AC_Y [FONCTION] ♦ ACCE_Z = /AC_Z [FONCTION] In this case, the user must supply the ground-acceleration functions, defined on the same list of time instants, in each spatial direction, in order to combine them with the relative accelerations so as to calculate the absolute accelerations. 3.6.7 Case CALCUL ='ABSOLU' ◊ MULT_APPUI = 'OUI' In this case, the user may specify whether it is a multi-support modelling. By default, it is a single-support modelling. Multi-support modelling is possible only when the result concept is of type resu_gene. 3.7 Keyword IMPRESSION This optional keyword makes it possible to specify the nature of the results to be printed (spectra, envelopes). The outputs will be according to the directions 'X', 'Y', 'Z', 'H' and the damping values. 3.7.1 Operand TRI This optional keyword makes it possible to specify the nature of the curves to be printed, sorted according to: the value of the damping coefficient ('AMOR_SPEC') or the spatial direction ('DIRECTION'). 3.7.2 Operand FORMAT This optional keyword makes it possible to specify the printout format of the curves: by printout in table format ('TABLEAU') or in a form readable by the Xmgrace software ('XMGRACE'). The scale of the abscissae (frequencies) is logarithmic. 3.7.3 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = U Logical unit of the file in which the results are written (integer between 10 and 90). The default unit is 29. This unit number must be consistent with the declaration made in the astk interface for the file in question. 3.7.4 Case FORMAT ='XMGRACE' For more details, see the documentation of the command IMPR_FONCTION U4.33.01. 3.7.5 Operand TOUT This optional operand TOUT='OUI' may be used to print the whole spectrum calculated at the end of loop #4: the mean values at each node, for all the directions and all the damping values. 3.8 Case NOM_CHAM ='DEPL' In this case, the user must give the following data required for the calculation of the displacement envelope: in the 3 directions \text{X} , \text{Y} , \text{Z} (vertical) and \text{H} (maximum horizontal value along \text{X} and \text{Y} ). 3.8.1 Operand LIST_INST This operand makes it possible to specify the list, coming from DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01, defining all the time steps of the dynamic transient for the calculation of the envelope displacement. 3.8.2 Keyword RESU This mandatory keyword makes it possible to specify the names of the result concept from which the nodal accelerations are extracted. The associated operand may be: > / 'RESU_GENE' = TG [TRAN_GENE] if the post-processing is carried out from a DYNA_VIBRA concept U4.53.03 (transient dynamics on a reduced modal basis). However, this result must be calculated in the relative reference frame. or: > / 'RESULTAT' = RESU [DYNA_TRANS] [EVOL_NOLI] if the post-processing is carried out from a transient-dynamics result (coming for example from LIRE_MISS3D U7.02.31, concept produced: DYNA_TRANS, or from DYNA_NON_LINE, concept produced: evol_noli). or: > / 'TABLE' = TAB [TABLE_SDASTER] if the post-processing is carried out from a table containing the results to be read. The table may be produced by: - a transient dynamic analysis, and come from an observation table. In this case the names of the columns of the table are ('INST', 'NOEUD', 'NOM_CHAM', 'NOM_CMP', 'VALE') with 'NOM_CHAM'='ACCE'. - any command producing a table. In this case the names of the columns of the table are necessarily ('INST', 'NOEUD', 'NOM_CHAM', 'DX', 'DY', 'DZ') with 'NOM_CHAM'='ACCE'. 3.8.3 Case CALCUL ='ABSOLU' ♦DEPL_X = /DE_X [FONCTION] ♦DEPL_Y = /DE_Y [FONCTION] ♦DEPL_Z = /DE_Z [FONCTION] In this case, one must introduce the ground entrainment-displacement functions, for each result concept, defined on the same list of time instants, in each spatial direction, which must be subtracted from the absolute displacements in order to obtain the relative displacements. 4 Examples The following examples illustrate the calculation of an acceleration spectrum, as well as the calculation of the displacement envelope: TAB=MACR_SPECTRE( MAILLAGE = MAIL, PLANCHER = _F(NOM = 'SOMMET', GROUP_NO = ('GTOP1',),), NOM_CHAM = 'ACCE', CALCUL = 'ABSOLU', AMOR_SPEC = L_AMOR_S, FREQ = L_FREQ, NORME = 9.81, RESU=(_F(RESU_GENE = RESUGENE,),), ) TAB2=MACR_SPECTRE( MAILLAGE = MA1, PLANCHER = ( _F(NOM = 'NIV1', GROUP_NO = ('N4_NIV1','N5_NIV1','N6_NIV1','N7_NIV1',),), _F(NOM = 'NIV8', GROUP_NO = ('N4_NIV8','N5_NIV8','N6_NIV8','N7_NIV8',),), ), NOM_CHAM = 'DEPL', CALCUL = 'RELATIF', LIST_INST = LISTE, RESU=( _F(RESU_GENE = TRAN_GE1,), _F(RESU_GENE = TRAN_GE2,), _F(RESU_GENE = TRAN_GE3,), ), ), TAB3=MACR_SPECTRE( MAILLAGE = MA1, PLANCHER = ( _F(NOM = 'NIV1',GROUP_NO = ('N4_NIV1',), ), _F(NOM = 'NIV8',GROUP_NO = ('N4_NIV8','N5_NIV8',), ), ), NOM_CHAM = 'ACCE', CALCUL = 'ABSOLU', AMOR_SPEC = L_AMOR_S, LIST_FREQ = L_FREQ, RESU=(_F(RESULTAT = DYNAT_K1,), _F(RESULTAT = DYNAT_K2,), _F(RESULTAT = DYNAT_K3,),), IMPRESSION =_F(FORMAT ='TABLEAU', UNITE = 16,), ) One may also refer to the test case SDNV112A for another example of use.

u4.32.12 Macro-command CALC_SPECTRE_IPM u4.32.12 Macro-command CALC_SPECTRE_IPM 1 Purpose This macro-command makes it possible to carry out a fast and efficient post-processing analysis in order to determine the floor spectra of any building after a seismic dynamic analysis, taking into account the interaction of the floor with the masses of the equipment ( cf. document R4.05.08). It may for example be used after a transient dynamic analysis of a building under earthquake loading, a transient dynamic analysis on a reduced modal basis, calculated in the relative reference frame, or else following a non-linear transient dynamic solution. This macro-command executes successively: 1. the extraction of the relative acceleration at one or more nodes of the mesh in the result concept (RECU_FONCTION U4.32.03); 2. the combination with the ground acceleration in order to obtain the absolute acceleration (CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04); 3. calculation of the transfer function which takes into account the interaction of the floor and of the masses 4. the calculation of the acceleration response spectrum with several damping coefficients (CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04); 5. the printout of the floor spectra. For practical examples of implementation, the reader may refer to the test case sdld109 V2.01.109. The macro-command produces a concept of type table_sdaster. 2 Syntax table = CALC_SPECTRE_IPM( ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: exists("MAILLAGE") ◆ EQUIPEMENT = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ RAPPORT_MASSE_TOTALE = float, ◆ COEF_MASS_EQUIP = float, ◆ FREQ_SUPPORT = float, ◆ AMOR_SUPPORT = float, ◆ AMOR_EQUIP = float, ◆ FREQ_EQUIP = float, ), # Si: not exists("MAILLAGE") ◆ EQUIPEMENT = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ NOEUD = no, ◆ RAPPORT_MASSE_TOTALE = float, ◆ COEF_MASS_EQUIP = float, ◆ FREQ_SUPPORT = float, ◆ AMOR_SUPPORT = float, ◆ AMOR_EQUIP = float, ◆ FREQ_EQUIP = float, ), ◆ CALCUL = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF", ◆ AMOR_SPEC = float, ◇ LIST_INST = listr8, ◇ LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ FREQ = float, ◆ NORME = float, # Si: equal_to("CALCUL", 'RELATIF') ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / FONCTION = fonction, ◆ ACCE_Z = fonction, ), # Si: equal_to("CALCUL", 'ABSOLU') ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / FONCTION = fonction, ), ◇ TOLE_INIT = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CORR_INIT = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands The classical post-processing of a seismic analysis in transient dynamics consists in carrying out the following calculations: - The floor spectrum obtained from the absolute accelerations, for the direction Z , calculated at a specified node of the mesh (for example in the case of a «stick» model); - Three operators of Code_Aster can produce result concepts corresponding to transient dynamic analyses: - DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 produces a resu_gene concept, including the relative acceleration and displacement fields. In this case, the ground accelerations must be added in order to obtain the absolute accelerations, which are necessary for the calculation of the floor spectrum. - CALC_MISS U7.03.12 produces a dyna_trans concept, including the absolute acceleration and displacement fields. In this case, the accelerations are used directly for the calculation of the floor spectrum; conversely, subtraction of the ground displacements is mandatory (to be read with the command LIRE_FONCTION U4.32.02 from a specific file given by its logical unit) in order to obtain the relative displacements. - DYNA_NON_LINE U4.53.01. The treatment is then the same as for the previous point. Here is a schematic of the calculation algorithm of this macro-command: Loop #1 on the floors - Recovery of the properties of the support and of the equipment Loop #2 over the floor nodes > • Recovery of the relative acceleration functions at the nodes: RECU_FONCTION > • If relative calculation Combination or not with the ground acceleration function: CALC_FONCTION/COMB > • Calculation of the transfer function > • Calculation of the response spectrum, with specified values of frequencies and of damping with CALC_FONCTION/SPEC_OSCI > • Printout of the acceleration spectrum for each node : IMPR_FONCTION End of loop #2 End of loop #1 Floor–mass interaction is taken into account by transforming the acceleration measured at node N by means of a transfer function. This transfer function converts the response of a model A into a model B, as illustrated in the figure below. Document R4.07.05 gives more complete explanations of the method and of the assumptions. 3.1 Keyword MAILLAGE This keyword corresponds to the mesh read by the operator LIRE_MAILLAGE U4.21.01. This keyword is optional. Knowledge of the mesh is necessary only in the case where the user uses the simple keyword GROUP_NO of the factor keyword PLANCHER. Indeed, as described in the previous algorithm, the treatment is carried out on the nodes and, if the user gives directly the name of the nodes present in the table, the mesh is not necessary. 3.2 Keyword PLANCHER This keyword is mandatory in order to define the names of the floors, where the spectra will be calculated. These names will be used to select or filter the display parameters in the table structure produced by the macro-command table_sdaster. 3.2.1 Operand NOM This mandatory operand makes it possible to name the floor considered. 3.2.2 Operands NOEUD / GROUP_NO These operands make it possible to define the nodes (individually or by groups) making up the floor where the spectra will be calculated. It is possible to supply GROUP_NO if the mesh has been supplied. 3.2.3 Keyword RAP_MASS This is the ratio of the masses of the equipment to the mass of the floor \lambda =\frac{{m}_{2}}{{m}_{1}} . It lies between 0 and 1. 3.2.4 Keyword RAP_MASS_COEFF This is the list of the ratios of the individual masses {\alpha}_{i} of each piece of equipment to the total mass of the equipment {m}_{i}={\alpha}_{i}{m}_{2} . The sum of the coefficients must be equal to 1. 3.2.5 Keyword FREQ_SUPP This keyword defines the frequency of the support {f}_{1} of model A. 3.2.6 Keyword FREQ_EQUI This keyword defines the list of the frequencies of the equipment. {f}_{i} . 3.2.7 Keyword AMOR_SUPP This keyword defines the damping of the support {\xi}_{1} . 3.2.8 Keyword AMOR_EQUI This keyword defines the list of the dampings of the equipment {\xi}_{i} . 3.3 Keyword CALCUL This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define the nature of the transient dynamic analysis used for the post-processing: in the absolute reference frame ('ABSOLU') or the relative reference frame ('RELATIF'). 3.4 Operand AMOR_SPEC This mandatory operand makes it possible to define the values of the reduced damping coefficient used in the calculation of the spectral response. See also CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04, keyword SPEC_OSCI. 3.5 Operand LIST_INST This optional operand makes it possible to specify the list, produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01, defining all the time steps for the transient dynamic analysis. 3.6 Operand FREQ / LIST_FREQ / ◊ FREQ = L_FR / ◊ LIST_FREQ = LFREQ List of frequencies previously defined by a listr8 concept. This optional operand makes it possible to define the frequency values; see also CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04, keyword SPEC_OSCI. 3.7 Operand NORME ♦ NORME = r The response spectrum will be normalised by the value r (pseudo-acceleration value). The analyses are carried out in most cases in units of the International System (USI) and the acceleration histories are often given in the unit m/{s}^{2} . The response spectra are generally given with g=\mathrm{9.81m}/{s}^{2} . Thus, this mandatory operand NORME may be used as a unit-conversion factor between the calculated accelerations and the response spectrum; see also CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04, keyword SPEC_OSCI. 3.8 Keyword RESU This mandatory keyword makes it possible to specify the input data from which the nodal accelerations are extracted. ♦ / 'TABLE' = TAB [TABLE_SDASTER] > / 'FONCTION' = FCT [FONCTION_SDASTER] The post-processing is carried out from a table or from a function containing the results to be read. Typically, an observation table or function derived from a transient dynamic analysis. The table supplied has two possible formats: - Either it has (at least) the columns INST, NOEUD, NOM_CHAM, NOM_CMP and VALE. In this case, only the lines which have both the value ACCE in the column NOM_CHAM and the value DZ in the column NOM_CMP are taken into account. The analysis stops if the table does not contain such lines. - Or it has (at least) the columns INST, NOEUD, NOM_CHAM and DZ. In this case, only the lines which have the value ACCE in the column NOM_CHAM are taken into account. The analysis stops if the table does not contain such lines. 3.8.1 Keyword ACCE_Z ♦ ACCE_Z = /AC_Z [FONCTION] In this case CALCUL ='RELATIF', the user must supply the ground-acceleration function, defined on the same list of time instants, in each spatial direction, in order to combine it with the relative accelerations so as to calculate the absolute accelerations. 3.9 Operand TOLE_INIT ◊ TOLE_INIT = 1e-3 This optional operand makes it possible to specify a limit criterion for the initial value of the initial accelerations of the signals. One checks that the ratio between the initial value of the signal and the maximum of the signal is less than the tolerance defined. 3.10 Operand CORR_INIT ◊ CORR_INIT = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] > / 'OUI' This optional operand makes it possible to correct the initial value of the signal if it is greater than the tolerance given. 4 Examples The following example is taken from the test case sdld109 V2.01.109: tabl_spe = CALC_SPECTRE_IPM(MAILLAGE = MAILLAGE, AMOR_SPEC = 0.05, EQUIPEMENT =(_F(NOM='NOEUD2', GROUP_NO='N02', RAPPORT_MASSE_TOTALE = lbd, COEF_MASS_EQUIP = (m2_1/m2,m2_2/m2,m2_3/m2), FREQ_EQUIP = (f2_1,f2_2,f2_3), FREQ_SUPPORT = f1, AMOR_SUPPORT = amor_supp, AMOR_EQUIP = (amor_equi,amor_equi,amor_equi) ),), LIST_INST = L_INST, CALCUL ='RELATIF', LIST_FREQ = L_FREQ, NORME = 1., RESU = (_F(TABLE = TAB, ACCE_Z = ACCE,),), ) In this test case, an input result obtained in the relative reference frame (single-support) is used; the entrainment signal, named here ACCE, must therefore be given.

u4.32.13 Macro-command LISS_SPECTRE u4.32.13 Macro-command LISS_SPECTRE 1 Purpose This macro-command makes it possible to smooth spectra from tables coming from MACR_SPECTRE or from nappes defined by the user, by means of calls to CALC_FONCTION/LISS_ENVELOPPE. The tables coming from MACR_SPECTRE are transformed into nappes (frequency, damping) before grouping and smoothing. The spectra supplied are grouped by direction and by floor before the smoothing is carried out. Finally, four files are created for a given floor and a given direction: - printout of the smoothed spectra in TABLEAU format - printout of the smoothed spectra in graphical format - printout of the envelope of the raw spectra, possibly broadened, in TABLEAU format - printout of the envelope of the raw spectra, possibly broadened, and of the smoothed spectra in graphical format These files are created in REPE_OUT. 2 Syntax LISS_SPECTRE( ◆ SPECTRE = _F( ◆ / TABLE = table, / NAPPE = nappe, ◇ ELARG = float, # Si: exists("NAPPE") ◆ DIRECTION = / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "H", ◆ NOM = text, ◇ BATIMENT = text, ◇ COMMENTAIRE = text, ), ◆ OPTION = / "VERIFICATION", / "CONCEPTION", ◇ FREQ_MIN = float, ◇ FREQ_MAX = float, ◇ NB_FREQ_LISS = int (défaut: 10), ◇ ZPA = float, ◇ BORNE_X = float, ◇ BORNE_Y = float, ◇ ECHELLE_X = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ ECHELLE_Y = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ LEGENDE_X = text, ◇ LEGENDE_Y = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword SPECTRE This keyword is mandatory in order to supply the various spectra to be processed. 3.1.1 Operand TABLE This operand makes it possible to supply spectra in the form of a table coming from the macro-command MACR_SPECTRE. In this case, the macro-command builds nappes from the table supplied (with parameters FREQ and AMOR). One nappe is built for a given floor name and a given direction. In addition to the floor name, the building name and a comment are recovered if they are present (see U4.32.11). 3.1.2 Operand NAPPE This operand allows the user to supply spectra directly in the form of nappes whose parameters are the frequency and the damping. Additional information must then be supplied in order to proceed to the stage of grouping the nappes by direction and by floor. These are the operands DIRECTION and NOM. The operands BATIMENT and COMMENTAIRE may also be supplied in order to fill the title blocks of the graphical outputs. 3.1.3 Operand DIRECTION This keyword, mandatory if the spectra are defined by the keyword NAPPE, makes it possible to supply the direction of the spectra. It takes one of the following 4 values: ‘X’, ‘Y’, ‘Z’, ‘H’. 3.1.4 Operand NOM This keyword makes it possible to define the name of the floor from which the spectrum defined by the keyword NAPPE comes. It is mandatory if NAPPE is present. 3.1.5 Operand BATIMENT This keyword makes it possible to define the name of the building in which the floor from which the spectrum defined by the keyword NAPPE comes is located. This keyword is optional. If it is supplied, it is used in particular for the naming of the “tables” and “figures” files created. 3.1.6 Operand COMMENTAIRE This keyword makes it possible to give a comment related to the spectrum defined by the keyword NAPPE. This keyword is optional. If it is supplied, it will appear in the subtitles of the figures created. 3.1.7 Operand ELARG This keyword makes it possible to define the broadening which will be applied to the spectrum during the smoothing stage (call to CALC_FONCTION/LISS_ENVELOPPE). The effect of this broadening value is explained in U4.32.04 (see ELARG in LISS_ENVELOPPE). Note: this keyword has an effect only for OPTION=’VERIFICATION’. 3.2 Keyword OPTION This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define the smoothing option of CALC_FONCTION/LISS_ENVELOPPE. > / 'CONCEPTION' La première étape consiste à réaliser une enveloppe sur les spectres fournis. Dans une seconde étape, on réalise le lissage du spectre obtenu en fonction du nombre de points lissés demandés NB_FREQ_LISS. / 'VERIFICATION' La première étape consiste à réaliser un lissage de chaque spectre fourni. Puis, on réalise un élargissement de chaque spectre suivant les coefficients fournis dans ELARG. Dans une troisième étape, on calcule l’enveloppe des spectres élargis. Enfin, on réalise le lissage du spectre obtenu en fonction du nombre de points lissés demandés. 3.3 Keyword NB_FREQ_LISS Number of frequencies required for the smoothed spectra. In the case of the option ' CONCEPTION ', only one value is supplied. For the option ' VERIFICATION ', two values may be supplied in the form of a pair, which will be applied respectively to the first and to the second smoothing. 3.4 Keywords FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX Frequency range of definition of the smoothed spectrum. The frequencies given under FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX must be chosen from among the discretisation frequencies of the raw spectrum. By default, the complete spectrum is considered. 3.5 Keyword ZPA Value of the high-frequency acceleration which one wishes to impose for the smoothed spectra. This keyword is optional. By default, it is the ZPA value of the spectrum with the least damping which is retained. 3.6 Keywords BORNE_X, BORNE_Y, ECHELLE_X, ECHELLE_Y, LEGENDE_X, LEGENDE_Y These keywords are used when printing the figures. They are passed to IMPR_FONCTION. The details are given in U4.33.01.

u4.32.21 Operator CALC_SPEC u4.32.21 Operator CALC_SPEC 1 Purpose Build all or part of a cross-spectral or transfer matrix from functions or from a table of functions. When the user chooses to enter a series of functions, these are used in full. When the user chooses to enter a table_fonction, the stored functions may be cut up, averaged and windowed, with a given overlap. To clarify the point, suppose that the user has 2 functions A and B . If the user chooses to use the operator from functions, the definition of the cross-spectrum {G}_{\mathrm{AB}} which will be calculated will necessarily be {G}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{1}{{N}_{A}}\mathrm{FFT}(A)\ast \mathrm{FFT}{(B)}^{\mathrm{H.}} . Where {N}_{A} is the number of points contained in the vector A . If the user chooses to build a table_fonction with the functions A and B , it will be possible to extract N sub-vectors {A}_{1,}\mathrm{...},{A}_{N} from the vector A (resp. {B}_{1,}\dots ,{B}_{N} from the vector B ), and to calculate an averaged cross-spectrum {G}_{\mathrm{AB}} such that {G}_{\mathrm{AB}}=\frac{1}{{N}_{A}}(\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\mathrm{FFT}({A}_{k})\ast \mathrm{FFT}{({B}_{k})}^{\mathrm{H.}}) . The functions read are of type sd_fonction. The concept produced is of type interspectre. It is possible to use this operator in a Code_Aster command file, but also interactively by means of the operator CALC_ESSAI (U4.90.01). 2 Syntax interspectre = CALC_SPEC( ◆ / TAB_ECHANT = _F( ◆ NOM_TAB = table, ◇ LONGUEUR_DUREE = float, ◇ LONGUEUR_POURCENT = float, ◇ LONGUEUR_NB_PTS = int, ◇ RECOUVREMENT_DUREE = float, ◇ RECOUVREMENT_POURCENT = float, ◇ RECOUVREMENT_NB_PTS = int, ), / ECHANT = _F( ◆ NUME_ORDRE_I = int, ◆ NUME_MES = int, ◆ FONCTION = fonction, ), ◆ / INTERSPE = _F( ◇ FENETRE = / "RECT" (par défaut), / "HAMM", / "HANN", / "EXPO", / "PART", # Si: FENETRE == 'EXPO' or FENETRE == 'PART' ◇ DEFI_FENE = float, ), / TRANSFERT = _F( ◇ ESTIM = / "H1" (par défaut), / "H2", / "CO", ◆ REFER = int, ◇ FENETRE = / "RECT" (par défaut), / "HAMM", / "HANN", / "EXPO", / "PART", # Si: FENETRE == 'EXPO' or FENETRE == 'PART' ◇ DEFI_FENE = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Keywords 3.1 Keyword TAB_ECHANT Defines the table_fonction of the time samples and the associated signal-processing parameters. It cannot be combined with the keyword ECHANT. 3.1.1 Keyword NOM_TAB Name of the table_fonction in which the samples are stored. Only one table_fonction name may be specified as input in order to carry out the calculations. The functions stored in the table_fonction correspond to the results of measurements, real or simulated, which serve as the basis for the calculation of the spectral-density matrix. All the functions stored in the table_fonction must be defined with the same sampling frequency. NB: the table_fonction must associate an order number and a measurement number with each function (see sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.3 for the meaning of these parameters) 3.1.2 Keywords LONGUEUR_DUREE / LONGUEUR_POURCENT / LONGUEUR_NB_PTS Defines the length of the sub-samples which will be retained for the signal processing. If the keyword is not supplied, the length of the smallest available sample is assigned by default. If the specified length is shorter than the length of the smallest sample, the total sample is cut into as many lengths as the specified length. This length may be specified in three different ways: - LONGUEUR_DUREE: one defines the length of the samples by their duration, expressed in the same unit as that used for the vector defining the time instants. - LONGUEUR_POURCENT: one defines the length of the samples as a percentage of the total length. - LONGUEUR_NB_PTS: one defines the length of the samples from the number of points which one wishes to retain. 3.1.3 Keyword RECOUVREMENT_DUREE / RECOUVREMENT_POURCENT / RECOUVREMENT_NB_PTS Defines the overlap length between two sub-samples which will be retained for the signal processing. If the keyword is not supplied, there is no overlap; the initial sample corresponds to the juxtaposition of the sub-samples. This length may be specified in three different ways: - RECOUVREMENT_DUREE: one defines the length of the samples by their duration, expressed in the same unit as that used for the vector defining the time instants. - RECOUVREMENT_POURCENT: one defines the length of the samples as a percentage of the total length. - RECOUVREMENT_NB_PTS: one defines the length of the samples from the number of points which one wishes to retain. The figure illustrates the cutting and the windowing of an initial sample into windowed sub-samples. Figure 3.1.3-1 : illustration of the cutting and of the windowing of an initial sample. The window applied is of Hanning type, with an overlap of 50% between the sub-samples. 3.2 Keyword ECHANT Factor keyword in which the functions used for the signal processing are defined. It cannot be used together with the keyword TAB_ECH. 3.2.1 Keyword FONCTION Name of the function containing the time sample. 3.2.2 Keyword NUME_ORDRE_I Defines the order number of the time sample (for example, a sensor number, a measurement-channel number, or a point on a mesh). This mandatory keyword is used to locate the cross-spectra or the transfers in the resulting interspectre concept. 3.2.3 Keyword NUME_MES Defines the measurement number of the sample. This mandatory keyword is used to identify the measurements which would be carried out simultaneously, or with the same phase reference, so that averaging of the spectra is valid. If two samples have the same measurement number, this means that they were acquired simultaneously. It is then possible to compute cross-spectra and transfer functions of one with respect to the other. Otherwise, this is impossible, because of the absence of a phase reference between the two signals. 3.3 Keyword INTERSPEC Calculates the spectral-density (or cross-spectral) matrix from the time samples supplied. 3.3.1 Keyword FENETRE Defines the type of window to be applied to the time sample. The size of the window is adapted to the length of the sample or of the sub-samples, depending on the case treated. Keyword to be chosen from among: - RECT: defines a rectangular window on the sample. - HAMM: defines a Hamming window. - HANN: defines a Hanning window. - EXPO: defines a decreasing exponential window. The keyword DEFI_FENE must then be supplied. - PART: allows the user to define a window from a list of reals given in the keyword DEFI_FENE. The list must be of the same length as the samples or sub-samples considered. 3.3.2 Keyword DEFI_FENE Allows the user to supply the necessary information when the keyword FENETRE takes the values ‘EXPO’ or ‘PART’. - ‘EXPO’: the list consists of exactly two values. The first corresponds to the number of points for which the window takes the value 1. The second corresponds to the slope of the exponential at the origin. These two quantities are illustrated in the figure. - ‘PART’: the window is defined by a list of reals entered by the user. Figure 3.3.2-1 : Definition of the parameters of DEFI_FENE: width (in number of points) of the initial plateau, and slope at the origin of the exponential. 3.4 Keyword TRANSFERT Calculates the transfer functions from the time samples supplied. 3.4.1 Keyword ESTIM Defines the estimator to be used for the calculation of the transfer functions. To be chosen from among: - H1: uses the estimator \mathrm{H1} - H2: uses the estimator \mathrm{H2} . - CO: calculates the coherence between the estimators \mathrm{H1} and \mathrm{H2} . For the record, if one has two signals A and B , the estimator \mathrm{H1} of the transfer function A/B is defined by: \mathrm{H1}(A/B)={G}_{\mathrm{AB}}/{G}_{\mathrm{BB}} , And the estimator \mathrm{H2} by: \mathrm{H2}(A/B)={G}_{\mathrm{AA}}/{G}_{\mathrm{AB}} , Where {G}_{\mathrm{AB}} is the cross-spectrum between the signals A and B . The coherence is defined by: \mathrm{CO}(A/B)=\mid \mathrm{H1}/\mathrm{H2}\mid . The estimator \mathrm{H1} minimises the influence of noise on the measured outputs, and \mathrm{H2} minimises the influence of the noise liable to appear on the measurements of the inputs. 3.4.2 Keyword REFER List of integers which define the reference measurements for the calculation of the transfers. The integers used correspond to the order numbers of the time samples. 3.4.3 Keyword FENETRE Defines the type of window to be applied to the time sample. See section 3.3.1. 3.4.4 Keyword DEFI_FENE Allows the user to supply the necessary information when the keyword FENETRE takes the values ‘EXPO’ or ‘PART’. See section 3.3.2. 3.5 Keyword TITRE Defines the title associated with the interspectre data structure in which the results are stored. 4 Examples These examples are taken from the test case zzzz241a. 4.1 Calculation of a cross-spectral matrix from a table_fonction The time responses may be stored in the form of lists in a separate file, or built on the basis of an analysis. Suppose here that four responses are available, with the respective names REP_1, REP_2, REP_3 and REP_4. Suppose that all these measurements were carried out simultaneously. Otherwise, a measurement number would have to be defined for each batch of simultaneous acquisitions. These four responses are first stored in a table_fonction: tab_rep=CREA_TABLE(LISTE=(_F(PARA='NOM_CHAM',LISTE_K='Rep_Temp',), One defines the various measurement numbers, associated with sensors, or with particular degrees of freedom > _F(PARA='NUME_ORDRE_I',LISTE_I=(1,2,3,4),), One defines the measurement numbers. Here, the 4 measurements are simultaneous, they therefore have the same number: > _F(PARA='NUME_MES',LISTE_I=(1,1,1,1),), One defines the functions from the time samples. > _F(PARA='FONCTION', > LISTE_K=('REP_1','REP_2','REP_3','REP_4'),), > ), > TITRE='', > TYPE_TABLE='table_fonction', > ) One then chooses to calculate the cross-spectral matrix by cutting each sample into sub-samples 1201 points long, with an overlap of 6 seconds, each weighted by a Hanning window SPEC=CALC_SPEC(TAB_ECHANT=_F(NOM_TAB=tab_rep, > LONGUEUR_NB_PTS=1201, > RECOUVREMENT_DUREE=6,), > INTERSPE=(_F(FENETRE='HANN',),), > ) 4.2 Calculation of transfer functions from functions The time responses may be stored in the form of lists in a separate file, or built on the basis of an analysis. Suppose here that two measurements carried out at different time instants are available. On the one hand, an excitation signal EXC_1 and a response REP_1 are acquired simultaneously. This may be the response to an impact, or to an excitation by a shaking table. On the other hand, an excitation signal EXC_2 and the associated response REP_2 are also acquired simultaneously. In both cases, the excitation signal was applied at the same point. The responses are measured at two different locations. The excitation point has order number 1, the point associated with the first measurement has number 2, and the point associated with the second measurement has number 3. The calculation of the transfer functions 2/1 and 3/1 is carried out as follows: Calculation of the transfer from the impulse response: FRF1_IMP=CALC_SPEC(ECHANT=( Definition of the various time samples > _F(NUME_ORDRE_I = 1, > NUME_MES=1, > FONCTION=REP_1,), > _F(NUME_ORDRE_I = 2, > NUME_MES=1, > FONCTION=REP_1,), > _F(NUME_ORDRE_I = 1, > NUME_MES=2, > FONCTION=EXC_2,), > _F(NUME_ORDRE_I = 3, > NUME_MES=2, > FONCTION=REP_2,), > ), Definition of the parameters for the calculation of the transfers: Choice of the estimator: > TRANSFERT=(_F(ESTIM='H1', Choice of the window to be applied: > FENETRE='EXPO', Complementary definition of the window: > DEFI_FENE=(10,-0.02), Definition of the order numbers associated with the reference points: > REFER=1,), > ), > ) By using the functions directly, rather than going through data setup in a table_fonction, the user does not have access to the possibilities of averaging over the length of the signal. In order to do so, either the user defines the sub-functions, keeping this same input formalism, or the user fills a table_fonction and uses the formalism presented in section 4.1.

u4.33.01 Operator IMPR_FONCTION u4.33.01 Operator IMPR_FONCTION 1 Purpose Print the content of objects of type fonction or list of reals in a file intended for a curve plotter. Note: Tables, for their part, are printed with the command IMPR_TABLE . 2 Syntax IMPR_FONCTION( ◇ FORMAT = / "TABLEAU" (par défaut), / "AGRAF", / "XMGRACE", / "LISS_ENVELOP", # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'XMGRACE') ◇ PILOTE = / "" (par défaut), / "POSTSCRIPT", / "EPS", / "MIF", / "SVG", / "PNM", / "PNG", / "JPEG", / "PDF", / "INTERACTIF", / "INTERACTIF_BG", ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 29), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'AGRAF') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 25), ◇ UNITE_DIGR = unit (défaut: 26), # Si: not equal_to("FORMAT", 'LISS_ENVELOP') ◆ COURBE = _F( ◆ / FONCTION = formule / fonction_c / fonction / nappe, / LIST_RESU = listr8, / FONC_X = formule / fonction, / ABSCISSE = float, # Si: exists("FONCTION") ◇ LIST_PARA = listr8, # Si: is_type("FONCTION") in (fonction_c, formule_c) ◇ PARTIE = / "REEL", / "IMAG", # Si: exists("LIST_RESU") ◆ LIST_PARA = listr8, # Si: exists("FONC_X") ◆ FONC_Y = formule / fonction, ◇ LIST_PARA = listr8, # Si: exists("ABSCISSE") ◆ ORDONNEE = float, ◇ LEGENDE = text, ◇ STYLE = int, ◇ COULEUR = int, ◇ MARQUEUR = int, ◇ FREQ_MARQUEUR = int, ◇ TRI = / "N" (par défaut), / "X", / "Y", / "XY", / "YX", ), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'LISS_ENVELOP') ◆ COURBE = _F( ◆ / NAPPE = nappe, / NAPPE_LISSEE = nappe, ), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'TABLEAU') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ SOUS_TITRE = text, ◇ SEPARATEUR = text (défaut: " "), ◇ COMMENTAIRE = text (défaut: "#"), ◇ COMM_PARA = text, ◇ DEBUT_LIGNE = text, ◇ FIN_LIGNE = text (défaut: " "), ◇ FORMAT_R = text (défaut: "E12.5"), # Si: not equal_to("FORMAT", 'TABLEAU') ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ SOUS_TITRE = text, ◇ BORNE_X = float, ◇ BORNE_Y = float, ◇ ECHELLE_X = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ ECHELLE_Y = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ GRILLE_X = float, ◇ GRILLE_Y = float, ◇ LEGENDE_X = text, ◇ LEGENDE_Y = text, # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'LISS_ENVELOP') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 25), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Presentation of the curves A set of optional operands makes it possible to define the presentation of the curve. All have a default value. 3.1.1 Operand FORMAT ◊ FORMAT= Printout format of the function | 'AGRAF' | printout intended for the agraf software, which also makes it possible to adjust the presentation parameters interactively, | | --- | --- | | 'TABLEAU' | the column printout makes it easy to import the data into a spreadsheet; if several curves are given, it is the list of abscissae of the first function which is used to interpolate the values of the other functions, | | 'XMGRACE' | printout intended for the xmgrace software. One can also adjust the presentation parameters interactively. The use of the keyword PILOTE makes it possible to produce an image or postscript file directly. | | 'LISS_ENVELOP' | printout intended for the spectra coming from CALC_FONCTION/LISS_ENVELOP. The curves are plotted using the Python Matplotlib libraries available in the Salomé-Méca distribution. | Note The format XMGRACE is intended for version 5 of grace and is not compatible with grace6 (version 5.99). 3.1.2 Operand PILOTE By choosing FORMAT = 'XMGRACE', one has the output drivers used by xmgrace by using the keyword PILOTE. This amounts to using the export functions of xmgrace via its menu "File/Print Setup …". The exact list of the drivers available on your server is supplied by the "-version" option of xmgrace. Possible values of PILOTE: | '' | : | in this case, no driver is used, the file obtained is the .agr or .dat of xmgrace (file containing the data and the graphic directives). | | --- | --- | --- | | 'POSTSCRIPT', 'EPS' | : | full-page or encapsulated postscript file, | | 'PNG', 'JPEG', 'PNM' | : | image-type file, | | 'PDF', 'MIF', 'SVG' | : | particular formats, | | 'INTERACTIF' | : | no file is returned if xmgrace can be opened on the screen. | | 'INTERACTIF_BG' | : | As for INTERACTIF but xmgrace is launched in the background, the analysis continues. | 3.1.3 Graph layout common to XMGRACE, AGRAF and LISS_ENVELOP 3.1.3.1 Operands BORNE_X/BORNE_Y ◊ BORNE_X= Plotting of the function over a given abscissa interval. ◊ BORNE_Y= Plotting of the function over a given ordinate interval. 3.1.3.2 Operands ECHELLE_X/ECHELLE_Y ◊ ECHELLE_X= Type of scale required for the abscissae, LINear or LOGarithmic. ◊ ECHELLE_Y= Type of scale required for the ordinates, LINear or LOGarithmic. 3.1.3.3 Operands LEGENDE_X/LEGENDE_Y ◊ LEGENDE_X= Legend associated with the abscissa axis. ◊ LEGENDE_Y= Legend associated with the ordinate axis. 3.1.3.4 Operands GRILLE_X/GRILLE_Y ◊ GRILLE_X= nx For xmgrace, nx is the distance between two successive vertical grid lines. For agraf, nx is the integer defining the plotting frequency of these lines. ◊ GRILLE_Y= ny The same for the horizontal lines of the grid. 3.1.4 Layout in TABLEAU format See IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03 for the description of the formatting keywords (DEBUT_LIGNE, COMMENTAIRE...). Note: The column labels are suffixed by «_ + column number» (starting at 0) in order to avoid repetition, because the column names must all be different. 3.1.5 Keywords common to all the formats ◊ TITRE ◊ SOUS_TITRE Make it possible to define the main and secondary titles of the graph or of the table. If FORMAT=LISS_ENVELOP then the titles and subtitles are used to fill the title blocks of the graph. The subtitle must follow the nomenclature «Storey, Details» so that the two boxes are filled correctly. If the subtitle contains more than one comma, the elements contained after the second comma will not be taken into account in the title block. Note The value of the TITRE stored by certain commands (example RECU_FONCTION ) in the function objects is not used by IMPR_FONCTION . 3.2 Keyword COURBE ♦ COURBE Factor keyword making it possible to print the defined functions or to plot one or more functions in the same graph (one function per occurrence of the factor keyword). 3.2.1 Additional attributes for the plotting of each function by the xmgrace or agraf software ◊ STYLE= sty This keyword defines the line style of the curve. For xmgrace , the correspondence is as follows: | 0 no line | 1 continuous line | 2 dotted | 3 short dashes | 4 long dashes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 5, 6, 7, 8 alternating dotted dashes For agraf , the styles are: | 0 line | 1 dotted | 2 point | | --- | --- | --- | ◊ MARQUEUR= marq This keyword defines the type of marker or symbol of the points of the curve. For xmgrace : | 0 no marker | 1 circle | 2 square | 3 diamond | 4 up triangle | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 5 left triangle | 6 down triangle | 7 right triangle | 8 plus | 9 cross | | 10 star | | | | | For agraf , the markers are: | 0 circle | 1 square | 2 plus | 3 diamond | 4 filled circle | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 5 filled square | 6 filled diamond | 7 circle+cross | 8 diamond+cross | | ◊ COULEUR= coul This keyword defines the colour of the curve. For xmgrace , the colours are: | 0 white | 1 black | 2 red | 3 green | 4 blue | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 5 yellow | 6 brown | 7 grey | 8 purple | 9 cyan | | 10 magenta | 11 orange | 12 maroon | 13 indigo | 14 turquoise | | 15 dark green | | | | | For agraf , the colours are: | 0 black | 1 red | 2 dark green | 3 blue | 4 magenta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 5 cyan | 6 green | 7 maroon | 8 orange | 9 mauve | | 10 yellow | 11 light brown | | | | ◊ LEGENDE = legende Legend given to the function (by default the name of the function is recovered). ◊ FREQ_MARQUEUR= freqmarq Integer indicating the print frequency of the marker associated with a function. Every freqmarq discretisation points of the function, a marker is printed (by default every point). 3.2.2 Additional attributes for plotting by the agraf software ◊ TRI= tr This keyword makes it possible to sort in ascending order the parameters defining the function: - tr = ‘N’, no sorting, - tr = ‘X’, sorting of the points of the function in ascending order of the abscissae x, - tr = ‘Y’, sorting of the points of the function in ascending order of the ordinates y, - tr = ‘XY’, sorting of the points of the function in ascending order of the abscissae x and, in the event of equality, in ascending order of the ordinates, - tr = ‘YX’, sorting of the points of the function in ascending order of the ordinates y and, in the event of equality, in ascending order of the abscissae, 3.2.3 Printout or plotting of a real function / ♦ FONCTION= fr Name of the real function to be printed or plotted. ◊ LIST_PARA= lr Printout or plotting of the function according to the list of parameters given. 3.2.4 Printout or plotting of a complex function One plots either the real part or the imaginary part. If one wishes to plot the real part and the imaginary part in the same graph, the factor keyword COURBE must be repeated. / FONCTION= fc Name of the complex function to be printed or plotted. ◊ PARTIE= Printout or plotting of the REEL part or of the IMAG part. ◊ LIST_PARA= lr Printout or plotting of the function according to the list of parameters given. No effect during a column printout (format 'TABLEAU'). 3.2.5 Printout or plotting of a function defined by 2 lists of reals / ♦ LIST_PARA= lpara Name of the list of abscissae. ♦ LIST_RESU= lresu Name of the list of ordinates. Or else: / ♦ ABSCISSE = labs Python list of the abscissae. ♦ ORDONNEE = lordo Python list of the ordinates. 3.2.6 Printout or plotting of a parametric function / ♦ FONC_X= fx Name of the parametric function x=f(t) to be printed or plotted. ♦ FONC_Y= fy Name of the parametric function y=g(t) to be printed or plotted. ◊ LIST_PARA= lr Printout or plotting of the function according to the list of parameters given. 3.2.7 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE= unit ◊ UNITE_DIGR = unit_digr si FORMAT = 'AGRAF' Make it possible to choose on which logical unit the functions are printed. If one plots numerous curves, it is more flexible to use the repe type combined with the command DEFI_FICHIER; the files will be in the directory ./REPE_OUT. In AGRAF format, the data are written to UNITE whereas the directives are written to UNITE_DIGR (equal to 26 by default). The default value of unit is: - 8 in TABLEAU format, - 25 in AGRAF format, - 29 in XMGRACE format (optional if PILOTE = 'INTERACTIF/_BG'), - 25 in LISS_ENVELOP format. 3.2.8 Plotting of a nappe or of a smoothed nappe / ♦ NAPPE= nappe Name of the raw nappe to be plotted. The plot will be drawn as dashes. ♦ NAPPE_LISSEE= nappe Name of the smoothed nappe to be plotted. The plot will be drawn as a solid line. The values of the smoothed nappe will be entered in a table under the curve. If several smoothed nappes are supplied, the last one entered will be taken into account for the table. 3.2.9 Functionalities which existed in IMPR_COURBE The formatting of graphs from a table is now handled by IMPR_TABLE. The plotting of a resu_gene at a shock node must be done in two stages: recover a function with RECU_FONCTION, keyword RESU_GENE, then print the graph with IMPR_FONCTION. 4 Examples 4.1 Curve representing a complex function fc = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA='INST', NOM_RESU='DX', VALE_C=(0., 0., 0., 1., 2., 3., 2., 3., 4., 3., 4., 5., 4., 5., 6., 5., 6., 7. ),) IMPR_FONCTION( UNITE = 24, FORMAT = 'XMGRACE', PILOTE = 'POSTSCRIPT', LEGENDE_X = 'Temps (s)', LEGENDE_Y = 'DX (mm)', COURBE = ( _F(FONCTION = fc, PARTIE = 'REEL', COULEUR = 4, STYLE = 2, MARQUEUR = 5, LEGENDE = 'partie réelle',), _F(FONCTION = fc, PARTIE = 'IMAG', COULEUR = 2, STYLE = 5, MARQUEUR = 8, LEGENDE = 'partie imaginaire',), ), TITRE = "Tracé d'une fonction complexe", ) 4.2 Parametric curve lt = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT = 0., INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A=10., PAS=0.01),) fx = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='t', VALE="""2. cos(t) - cos(2. t)""",) cardioX=CALC_FONC_INTERP( FONCTION = fx, LIST_PARA = lt,) fy = FORMULE(NOM_PARA='t', VALE="""2. sin(t) - sin(2. t)""",) cardioY=CALC_FONC_INTERP( FONCTION = fy, LIST_PARA = lt,) IMPR_FONCTION( UNITE = 27, FORMAT = 'XMGRACE', TITRE = 'Cardioide', COURBE = ( _F(FONC_X = cardioX, FONC_Y = cardioY,), ), ) One thus obtains a file which can be viewed in xmgrace: Additional formatting in xmgrace: menu Plot/Graph appearance , type fixed (square grid), and remove the legend by unchecking the box Display legend . 4.3 Nappe and smoothed nappe One thus obtains the following .png file.
