"TABLE_CONTAINER", ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword FONCTION 3.1.1 Operand FONCTION The table is created from a function. The first column of the table contains the abscissae of the function and the second the values of the function at the corresponding abscissae. 3.1.2 Operand PARA Names of the parameters of the table. This keyword is optional: the names of the parameters are then identical to the NOM_PARA and NOM_RESU of the function. If it is supplied, its cardinality must be equal to 2: parameter name for the column associated with the abscissae, parameter name for the column associated with the ordinates. 3.2 Keyword LISTE This keyword must be supplied at least twice: each occurrence makes it possible to define a column of the table. The lists do not necessarily have the same cardinality; the keyword NUME_LIGN is used to indicate which lines must be filled. 3.2.1 Operand LISTE_R A column is created in the table from a list of reals. 3.2.2 Operand LISTE_I A column is created in the table from a list of integers. 3.2.3 Operand LISTE_K A column is created in the table from a list of character strings. 3.2.4 Operand TYPE_K Length of the character strings for the case LISTE_K. 3.2.5 Operand LISTE_CO This operand makes it possible to define a list of concepts. The table created from a list of concepts is necessarily a table of type TABLE_CONTENEUR. The list of concepts is used to create two columns of the table: a column with parameter NOM_SD and a column with parameter TYPE_OBJET. If the operand LISTE_CO is supplied, the user must also define a column with parameter NOM_OBJET containing a unique key for each concept of the list of concepts. 3.2.6 Operand NUME_LIGN When the lists do not all have the same cardinality, or in order to build a table with holes, this keyword is used to specify which lines are filled. 3.2.7 Operand PARA Name of the parameter of the table associated with the list supplied. 3.3 Keyword RESU This keyword must be used only once. It makes it possible to create a table from the components of an isolated field (keyword CHAM_GD) or from the fields of a result data structure (keyword RESULTAT). The fields processed must have real values. 3.3.1 Operand CHAM_GD This operand makes it possible to collect the name of the field which will be read in order to create the table. This field may come for example from the command CREA_CHAMP. 3.3.2 Operands RESULTAT/NOM_CHAM/TOUT_ORDRE/NUME_ORDRE/LIST_ORDRE /INST/LIST_INST/MODE/LIST_MODE/FREQ/LIST_FREQ/CRITERE/PRECISION These operands make it possible to choose the fields of the result data structure to be processed. One may limit the order numbers with the keywords INST, LIST_INST, … as well as the names of the fields ('DEPL', 'SIEF_ELGA', …) with the keyword NOM_CHAM. For more information concerning these keywords, please consult the document U4.71.00 3.3.3 Operand INTITULE This operand makes it possible to overload the name of the RESULTAT or of the CHAM_GD in the table. By default, the name of the user variable is taken. 3.3.4 Operands TOUT_CMP/NOM_CMP/NOM_VARI These operands make it possible to choose the components which one wishes to see in the table. Either one uses TOUT_CMP='OUI' in order to choose all the components of the field, or one uses NOM_CMP or NOM_VARI in order to retain only some of them. > ◊ NOM_CMP = nocmp, [Kn] > Name of the component which one wishes to see in the table. > ◊ NOM_VARI= novari, [Kn] For the fields of internal variables (VARI_ ), one may give the name of the internal variable which one wishes to see in the table (see U4.51.11 for the rules for naming the internal variables). 3.3.5 Operands TOUT/GROUP_MA/GROUP_NO These operands make it possible to choose the entities of the mesh on which the values of the components of the field will be recovered. The operand TOUT ='OUI' makes it possible to consider the whole mesh. In order to restrict a part of the mesh, the remaining operands must be used. For a field of type: - NOEU: one may choose GROUP_MA and/or GROUP_NO. - ELNO/ELGA: one may choose GROUP_MA. 3.4 Operand TYPE_TABLE Determines the type of the table produced. The choices are: - TABLE: an ordinary table - TABLE_FONCTION: a table which contains a column whose parameter is FONCTION or FONCTION_C, in which one finds names of fonction concepts. 3.5 Operand TITRE Title which will be given to the table produced. 4 Examples 4.1 Creation of a table from a function FCT=DEFI_FONCTION(NOM_PARA='X', VALE=(0.0,5.0,4.0,17.5)) ; T_FCT=CREA_TABLE(FONCTION=_F(FONCTION=FCT)); IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=T_FCT) ; The printout of the table created is as follows: X TOUTRESU 0.00000E+00 5.00000E+00 4.00000E+00 1.75000E+01 4.2 Creation of a table from three lists, of heterogeneous types T_LST=CREA_TABLE(LISTE=( _F(LISTE_R=(0.0,4.0),PARA='X'), _F(LISTE_R =(5.0,17.5),PARA='Y') ,); _F(LISTE_I =(6.7),PARA='K') IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=T_LST) ; The printout of the table created is as follows: X Y K 0.00000E+00 5.00000E+00 6 4.00000E+00 1.75000E+01 7 4.3 Creation of a table with holes TAB=CREA_TABLE( LISTE=( _F( PARA='NUME_ORDRE', LISTE_I=(8,15,156,67), ), _F( PARA='VAR', LISTE_R=(2.,15.,18), NUME_LIGN=(1,3,4), ), _F( PARA='COMMENT', LISTE_K=('VALEUR',), TYPE_K='K24', NUME_LIGNE=1, ), ), L'impression de la table créée est la suivante: NUME_ORDRE VAR COMMENT 8 2.00000E+00 VALEUR 15 – - 156 1.50000E+01 - 67 1.80000E+01 - 4.4 Creation of a table from a field > TB01=CREA_TABLE(RESU=_F(RESULTAT=TEMP0, > TOUT='OUI', > NUME_ORDRE=4, > TOUT_CMP='OUI', > NOM_CHAM='TEMP',),) L'impression de la table créée est la suivante: #TABLE_SDASTER RESULTAT NOM_CHAM NUME_ORDRE NOEUD COOR_X COOR_Y TEMP TEMP0 TEMP 4 N1 1.0 0.0 85.0 TEMP0 TEMP 4 N2 2.0 0.0 85.0 TEMP0 TEMP 4 N3 2.0 4.0 85.0 TEMP0 TEMP 4 N4 1.0 4.0 85.0

u4.33.03 Procedure CALC_TABLE u4.33.03 Procedure CALC_TABLE 1 Purpose Manipulate the data of tables in the manner of a spreadsheet. The command makes it possible to carry out operations on the data of the tables. The following operations are currently available: - Concatenate / Combine two tables, - Apply a formula, - Rename parameters, - Filter the lines according to certain criteria, - Extract certain columns of a table, - Order the lines, - Add lines or columns, - Add information on the table itself. Produces a data structure table. 2 Syntax / table / table_container / table_fonction = CALC_TABLE( ◇ reuse = , ◆ TABLE = table, ◆ ACTION = _F( ◆ OPERATION = / "AJOUT_COLONNE", / "AJOUT_LIGNE", / "CALCUL", / "COMB", / "EXTR", / "FILTRE", / "OPER", / "RENOMME", / "STATISTIQUES", / "SUPPRIME", / "TRI", / "UNIQUE", # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'FILTRE') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ CRIT_COMP = / "EQ" (par défaut), / "GE", / "GT", / "LE", / "LT", / "MAXI", / "MAXI_ABS", / "MINI", / "MINI_ABS", / "NE", / "NON_VIDE", / "REGEXP", / "VIDE", # Si: (is_in("CRIT_COMP", ('EQ','NE','GT','LT','GE','LE'))) ◆ / VALE = float, / VALE_I = int, / VALE_K = text, / VALE_C = complex, # Si: equal_to("CRIT_COMP", 'REGEXP') ◆ VALE_K = text, # Si: is_in("CRIT_COMP", ('EQ','NE')) ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'EXTR') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'SUPPRIME') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'UNIQUE') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ FORMAT_R = text, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'RENOMME') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'TRI') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ ORDRE = / "CROISSANT" (par défaut), / "DECROISSANT", # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'COMB') ◆ TABLE = table, ◇ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ RESTREINT = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ FORMAT_R = text, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'AJOUT_LIGNE') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◆ VALE = not_checked, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'AJOUT_COLONNE') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◆ / VALE = not_checked, / VALE_COLONNE = not_checked, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'OPER') ◆ FORMULE = formule, ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ NOM_COLONNE = text, # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'CALCUL') ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◆ TYPE_CALCUL = / "MAXI", / "MAXI_ABS", / "MINI", / "MINI_ABS", / "MOY", / "SOMM", / "SOMM_ABS", ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TABLE ♦ TABLE = matable Name of the initial table on which the manipulations will be carried out. 3.2 Operand ACTION ♦ ACTION = ( _F(OPERATION='xxx', ...), _F(OPERATION='yyy',...), ...) The “actions” are carried out one after the other. The operation 'yyy' takes the table in the state in which the operation 'xxx' left it. It is distinctly more efficient to repeat the factor keyword ACTION than to make as many successive calls to the command CALC_TABLE. 3.3 OPERATION = 'COMB': concatenate/combine two tables L'opération COMBpermet de concaténer, de combiner deux tables entre elles, avec couture sur une liste de paramètres communs. 3.3.1 Operand TABLE ♦ TABLE = table Name of the table whose values are to overload and/or enrich the initial table. 3.3.2 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA = l_para Name of the parameters whose values must be identical in the two tables. 3.3.3 Operand FORMAT_R This is a format which will be used before comparing two real numbers in order to determine whether they are identical or not. Note that, in the table, one recovers the unrounded value (from the second table). 3.3.4 Operand RESTREINT ◊ RESTREINT = 'OUI' ou 'NON' Example of the combination of two tables: tab_resu=CALC_TABLE(TABLE=tab1, ACTION=_F(OPERATION='COMB', TABLE=tab2, NOM_PARA=('ABSC_CURV','NOEUD'), RESTREINT='NON' ) ) When ABSC_CURV and NŒUD are identical between tab1 and tab2, the values of tab2 are inserted on the line of tab1 (for the other parameters common to the 2 tables, it is therefore the value of tab2 which overwrites that of tab1). If ABSC_CURV and/or NŒUD differ between tab1 and tab2, the line of tab2 is added at the end of tab1. NOM_PARA acts as a primary key: if the pair (ABSC_CURV, NOEUD) is not found more than once, the line is added. The same operation with RESTREINT='OUI' produces the same lines when ABSC_CURV and NŒUD are identical. On the other hand, no line is added when the parameters differ. 3.4 OPERATION = 'OPER': Apply a formula Permet d'appliquer une formule dont les variables sont les paramètres de la table et d'insérer le résultat dans une nouvelle colonne. 3.4.1 Operand FORMULE Name of the formula to be applied 3.4.2 Operand NOM_PARA Name of the new column. 3.4.3 Operand NOM_COLONNE This keyword makes it possible to use a formula whose parameters are not parameters of the table. For example, one has a formula which depends on INST. If one wishes to evaluate this formula using the column INST_FIN of the table, it is sufficient to specify NOM_COLONNE='INST_FIN'. 3.5 OPERATION = 'RENOMME': Rename parameters of a table The operation RENOMME makes it possible to rename one or more parameters of a table. 3.5.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = l_para Name of the parameters: pair of values (old name of the parameter, new name of the parameter) 3.6 OPERATION = 'FILTRE': Filter the lines according to certain criteria This factor keyword makes it possible to filter the lines of the table. For the use of this keyword see the command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. 3.7 OPERATION = 'EXTR': Extract certain columns of a table L'opération EXTRpermet d'extraire certaines colonnes d'une table. 3.7.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = l_para Name of the parameters which one wishes to extract. 3.8 OPERATION = 'TRI': Order the lines L'opération TRI permet d'ordonner les lignes selon les valeurs des paramètres. 3.8.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = l_para Names of the parameters on which the sorting bears. 3.8.2 Operand ORDRE ♦ ORDRE = / 'CROISSANT' / 'DECROISSANT' This keyword serves to specify whether an ascending or descending order must be used. By default, one sorts in ascending order. The order relations used are: - the natural order for the integers and the reals, - the alphabetical order for the texts and the names of concepts. Notes: One cannot use a complex parameter to rank the lines of a table. For parameters of type NŒUD (or MAILLE), the order is alphabetical because these parameters contain the names of the nodes (or of the mesh cells). If one specifies: TRI=_F (NOM_PARA= ('NOEUD','INST'), ORDRE= 'CROISSANT'), The lines of the table will be sorted in the alphabetical order of the nodes. If several lines corresponding to a given node exist, the second sorting criterion (INST) will be used to rank these lines. 3.9 OPERATION = 'AJOUT_LIGNE': add a line L'opération AJOUT_LIGNE permet d'ajouter une ligne à une table existante. 3.9.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = lpara Names of the parameters (names of the columns of the table) of the added line. One may very well define values only for certain columns of the table. If a parameter name does not exist in the table, it is added. Its type is determined from the value supplied. 3.9.2 Operand VALE ♦ VALE = lvale List of the values for each parameter of NOM_PARA. The type of the values must be compatible with the types of the columns of the table. VALE may contain heterogeneous values among integer, real, character string. The type must conform to the type of the parameter of the table. The first value corresponds to the first parameter given in NOM_PARA, the second value to the second parameter, etc. The lists NOM_PARA and VALE therefore have the same cardinality. 3.10 OPERATION = 'AJOUT_COLONNE': add a column L'opération AJOUT_COLONNE permet d'ajouter une ou plusieurs colonnes constantes (valeur identique pour toutes les lignes, en utilisant le mot-clé VALE), ou bien, une seule colonne avec des valeurs distinctes (en utilisant le mot-clé VALE_COLONNE). 3.10.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = lpara Names of the parameters, names of the columns added to the table. None of these parameters must already be present in the table. Only one parameter must be supplied if VALE_COLONNE is used. 3.10.2 Operand VALE ♦ VALE = lvale List of the values of each column. VALE may contain heterogeneous values among integer, real, character string. The type associated with the parameter is determined from this value. The first value corresponds to the first parameter given in NOM_PARA, the second value to the second parameter, etc. The lists NOM_PARA and VALE therefore have the same cardinality. 3.10.3 Operand VALE_COLONNE ♦ VALE_COLONNE = lval_col List of the values of the lines of the added column. The type of the values supplied may be integer, real, character string. All the values must be of the same type. The values are added on the lines as they are ordered at the time of the addition. There may be more or fewer values added than there are lines in the table. Either the column will be longer than the initial table, or it will contain empty values. 3.11 OPERATION = 'SUPPRIME': delete columns L'opération SUPPRIME permet de supprimer une ou plusieurs colonnes d'une table existante. 3.11.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = lpara Names of the parameters, names of the columns to be deleted in the table. 3.12 OPERATION = 'UNIQUE': deletion of duplicates L'opération UNIQUE permet de supprimer les lignes en doublon dans une table. 3.12.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = lpara Names of the columns in which the duplicates are sought. Two lines are said to be duplicates if all these parameters are identical (to within the format of the reals where applicable, see FORMAT_R). 3.13 OPERATION = 'STATISTIQUES' L'opération STATISTIQUES permet d'ajouter des informations sur la table elle-même. Les colonnes ajoutées sont nommées STAT_NOM et STAT_VALE. Elles contiennent respectivement le nom du paramètre et sa valeur. Les statistiques élémentaires ajoutées sont: le nombre de lignes (nommé NB_LIGNES), le nombre de colonnes (NB_COLONNES) et le nombre de cellules vides (NB_VIDE). 3.13.1 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = tit Title of the table produced. When it is not supplied, the title of the input table is, depending on the operations, completed. 3.13.2 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = inf Prints, in the "message" file, additional information if inf=2. Nothing happens if inf=1. 3.14 OPERATION = 'CALCUL' L'opération CALCUL permet des calculs simples pour des colonnes avec des variables réelles ou entières dans une table. En présence de reuse, une colonne avec le nom TYPE_CALCUL est ajoutée dans la table. Pour chaque TYPE_CALCUL, une ligne est ajoutée avec des valeurs calculées aux colonnes demandées. En absence dereuse, une nouvelle table est créée uniquement avec les colonnes à calculer ainsi que une colonne de TYPE_CALCUL. Chaque ligne correspond à un type de calcul. 3.14.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = lpara Names of the parameters, names of the columns to which the calculations are to be applied in the table. 3.14.2 Operand TYPE_CALCUL ♦ TYPE_CALCUL = / 'MAXI', / 'MINI', / 'SOMM', / 'MOY', / 'MAXI_ABS', / 'MINI_ABS', / 'SOMM_ABS', Type of calculation to be applied to the columns. It is possible to choose several types of calculation. Choice of the types of calculation: 'MAXI' for the maximum in the column, 'MINI' for the minimum in the column, 'SOMM' for the sum in the column, 'MOY' for the mean in the column, 'MAXI_ABS' for the maximum of the absolute values in the column, 'MINI_ABS' for the minimum of the absolute values in the column, 'SOMM_ABS' for the sum of the absolute values in the column. 4 Examples | Table 'TB1' | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | N | Y | Z | NOEUD | | 0 | 2.0 | 4.5 | NO1 | | 1 | 4.0 | 17.5 | N03 | | 2 | 17.5 | 9.0 | N06 | | Table 'TB2' | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | N | X | Z | NOEUD | | 1 | 2.0 | 2.5 | NO1 | | 3 | 4.0 | 5.5 | N031 | | 4 | 17.5 | 20.5 | N062 | | 6 | 5.0 | 8.0 | N013 | #--- COMBINAISON TB3=CALC_TABLE(TABLE=TB1, ACTION =_F(OPERATION='COMB', TABLE = TB2, NOM_PARA='NOEUD')) The content of the table TB3 is: N Y Z NOEUD X 1 2.00000E+00 2.50000E+00 N01 2.00000E+00 1 4.00000E+00 1.75000E+01 N03 - 2 1.75000E+01 9.00000E+00 N06 - 3 - 5.50000E+00 N031 4.00000E+00 4 - 2.05000E+01 N062 1.75000E+01 6 - 8.00000E+00 N013 5.00000E+00 #--- Formule DNOR=FORMULE(NOM_PARA = ('X','Z'), VALE = 'sqrt(X X+Z Z)') TB3=CALC_TABLE(TABLE = TB3, reuse = TB3, ACTION =_F(OPERATION='OPER', FORMULE=dnor , NOM_PARA='NOR_COOR')) Le contenu de la table TB3est : N Y Z NOEUD X NOR_COOR 1 2.00000E+00 2.50000E+00 N01 2.00000E+00 3.20156E+00 1 4.00000E+00 1.75000E+01 N03 - u4.34.01 Operator DEFI_LIST_REEL u4.34.01 Operator DEFI_LIST_REEL 1 Purpose Create a strictly increasing list of reals. The list may be given “in extenso” by the user, or else it may be formed from sub-lists defined at “constant step”. Produces a data structure of type listr8. 2 Syntax listr8 = DEFI_LIST_REEL( ◆ / VALE = float, / DEBUT = float, ◇ / INTERVALLE = _F( ◆ JUSQU_A = float, ◆ / NOMBRE = int, / PAS = float, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand VALE VALE= lr8 List of the reals which will form the resulting listr8 data structure. This list may be built from a Python list. 3.2 Operand DEBUT ♦ DEBUT = It is the first real of the list of reals which one wishes to build. 3.3 Operand INTERVALLE ♦ INTERVALLE = ♦ JUSQU_A = r1 It is the end of the interval which will be subdivided with a constant step. ♦ / NOMBRE = n1 It is the number of steps required in the interval which ends at r1. / PAS = r2 It is the subdivision step of the interval. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = i Indicates the printout level of the results of the operator. | 1: | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2: | printout of the list of reals created | 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title which the user wishes to give to the list of reals. 4 Notes - when the keyword PAS is used, it may be that the number of steps calculated is not strictly an integer. The last interval will then be “adapted” so as to fall exactly on the final value (JUSQU_A). If, in order to do so, the value of the step is modified by more than 1/1000, an alarm is issued, - caution: this command produces a listr8 data structure which can be used only in the commands expecting such data structures, and not in those which expect lists of reals (notation: l_R). 5 Examples Example 1: Suppose that one wishes to create the list: 1. 3. 5. 10. 15. 20. 25. 26. 27. 28. which is such that the step is: 2. from 1. to 5. 5. from 5. to 25. 1. from 25. to 28. One may write: lr = DEFI_LIST_REEL (DEBUT = 1., INTERVALLE =( _F (JUSQU_A= 5. , NOMBRE= 2, ), _F (JUSQU_A= 25., NOMBRE= 4, ), _F (JUSQU_A= 28., PAS= 1.,),), ) Example 2: Pour créer la liste: 1. 3. 12. 13. One may write: lr = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( VALE= (1., 3., 12., 13.), ) Example 3: On peut construire une liste Python de cette manière. lr = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( VALE= [:ref: sqrt(i) for i in range(5) ], )

u4.34.02 Operator DEFI_LIST_ENTI u4.34.02 Operator DEFI_LIST_ENTI 1 Purpose Create a strictly increasing list of integers. The list may be given “in extenso” by the user, or else it may be formed from sub-lists defined at “constant step”. The list may be built by extraction of the order numbers of a result data structure. Produces a data structure of type listis. 2 Syntax listis = DEFI_LIST_ENTI( ◇ OPERATION = / "DEFI" (par défaut), / "NUME_ORDRE", # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'DEFI') ◆ / VALE = int, / DEBUT = int, ◇ / INTERVALLE = _F( ◆ JUSQU_A = int, ◆ / NOMBRE = int, / PAS = int, ), # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'NUME_ORDRE') ◆ RESULTAT = resultat, ◆ PARAMETRE = text, ◆ INTERVALLE = _F( ◆ VALE = float, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Definition of a list of integers 3.1.1 Operand VALE ◊ VALE= lis List of the integers which will form the resulting listis data structure; any Python list may be supplied. 3.1.2 Operand DEBUT ♦ DEBUT = deb: first integer of the list to be built. 3.1.3 Keyword INTERVALLE ◊ INTERVALLE Factor keyword, each occurrence of which makes it possible to define an interval at constant step. 3.1.3.1 Operand JUSQU_A ♦ JUSQU_A = if if is the integer end of the interval to be subdivided with a constant step. 3.1.3.2 Operand PAS ♦ / PAS = ipas Subdivision step of the interval. 3.1.3.3 Operand NOMBRE / NOMBRE = in Number of steps required in the interval. 3.2 Extraction of order numbers This operation makes it possible to recover, in a result data structure (evol_noli coming from STAT/DYNA_NON_LINE for example), the order numbers corresponding to certain criteria. The list of order numbers thus obtained may then be used in all the commands which have the keyword LIST_ORDRE. For the moment, the only criterion programmed is the extraction of a parameter in a given interval. 3.2.1 Operand PARAMETRE Name of the parameter of the result data structure whose value one wishes to extract. 3.2.1.1 Factor keyword INTERVALLE One defines as many occurrences of the factor keyword INTERVALLE as one wishes search intervals. The search is carried out on the union of these intervals. > VALE= (val1, val2) Definition of the bounds of each interval to which the parameter to be extracted must belong (bounds included). 3.3 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = i Indicates the printout level of the results of the operator: 1: no printout, 2: printout of the list of integers created. 3.4 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 4 Notes - one checks that the list is increasing, - caution: the data structure of type listis cannot be used after a keyword expecting an l_I (sequence of integers written between parentheses). 5 Examples 5.1 Case OPERATION = 'DEFI' To build the list of integers at constant step: listi = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( DEBUT = 1, INTERVALLE = (_F ( JUSQU_A = 16, PAS = 3 ),), ) To build the list of integers with two different values of the step: listi = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( DEBUT = 1, INTERVALLE = (_F ( JUSQU_A = 5, PAS = 1, ), _F ( JUSQU_A = 15, PAS = 5, ),) ) or listi = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( DEBUT = 1, INTERVALLE = (_F ( JUSQU_A = 5, NOMBRE = 4, ), _F ( JUSQU_A = 15, NOMBRE = 2, ),), ) or, from any Python list object: listi = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( VALE = range(10) ,) 5.2 Case OPERATION = 'NUME_ORDRE' lnuor = DEFI_LIST_ENTI(OPERATION='NUME_ORDRE', RESULTAT=DEPLTRAN, PARAMETRE='INST', INTERVALLE=( _F(VALE=(1.36, 1.37)), _F(VALE=(1.45, 1.46)), ),) lnuor will contain the list of the order numbers whose time-instant value (parameter INST) lies in the intervals given.

u4.34.03 Operator DEFI_LIST_INST u4.34.03 Operator DEFI_LIST_INST To define the list of analysis time instants, as well as its management for the iterative solution algorithms (commands STAT_NON_LINE, DYNA_NON_LINE, MECA_NON_LINE and THER_NON_LINE) - possibilities of recutting the time step in the event of failure, - possibilities of adapting the time step. Produces a data structure list_inst. 1 Syntax list_inst = DEFI_LIST_INST( ◇ MODELE = modele, ◇ METHODE = / "AUTO", / "MANUEL" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MANUEL') ◆ DEFI_LIST = _F( ◆ / VALE = list[float], / LIST_INST = listr8, / RESULTAT = resultat, ◇ & SUBD_PAS = int, ), # Si: (equal_to("METHODE", 'AUTO')) ◆ DEFI_LIST = _F( ◆ / VALE = list[float], / LIST_INST = listr8, ◇ PAS_INIT = float, ◇ PAS_MINI = float, ◇ PAS_MAXI = float, ◇ NB_PAS_MAXI = int (défaut: 1000000), ), ⟐ ECHEC = _F( ◇ EVENEMENT = / "DELTA_GRANDEUR", / "DIVE_RESI", / "ERREUR" (par défaut), / "INSTABILITE", / "INTERPENETRATION", / "RESI_MAXI", # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'ERREUR') # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'DECOUPE') # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'AUTO') ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'MANUEL') ◇ SUBD_PAS = int (défaut: 4), ◇ SUBD_NIVEAU = int (défaut: 3), ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ SUBD_METHODE = / "AUTO", / "MANUEL" (par défaut), ◇ ACTION = / "ARRET", / "DECOUPE" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'DELTA_GRANDEUR') # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'DECOUPE') # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'AUTO') ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'MANUEL') ◇ SUBD_PAS = int (défaut: 4), ◇ SUBD_NIVEAU = int (défaut: 3), ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ SUBD_METHODE = / "AUTO", / "MANUEL" (par défaut), ◇ / GROUP_MA = list[grma], / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◆ VALE_REF = float, ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "SIEF_ELGA", / "VARI_ELGA", ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ ACTION = / "ARCHIVAGE", / "ARRET", / "DECOUPE" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'INTERPENETRATION') ◆ PENE_MAXI = float, ◇ ACTION = "ARRET", # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'DIVE_RESI') # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'DECOUPE') # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'AUTO') ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'MANUEL') ◇ SUBD_PAS = int (défaut: 4), ◇ SUBD_NIVEAU = int (défaut: 3), ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ SUBD_METHODE = / "AUTO", / "MANUEL" (par défaut), ◇ ACTION = "DECOUPE", # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'RESI_MAXI') # Si: equal_to("ACTION", 'DECOUPE') # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'AUTO') ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("SUBD_METHODE", 'MANUEL') ◇ SUBD_PAS = int (défaut: 4), ◇ SUBD_NIVEAU = int (défaut: 3), ◇ SUBD_PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ SUBD_METHODE = / "AUTO", / "MANUEL" (par défaut), ◆ RESI_GLOB_MAXI = float, ◇ ACTION = "DECOUPE", # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'INSTABILITE') ◇ ACTION = / "ARRET", / "CONTINUE" (par défaut), ), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'AUTO') ⟐ ADAPTATION = _F( ◇ EVENEMENT = / "AUCUN", / "SEUIL" (par défaut), / "TOUT_INST", # Si: equal_to("EVENEMENT", 'SEUIL') ◇ NB_INCR_SEUIL = int (défaut: 2), ◇ NOM_PARA = "NB_ITER_NEWTON", ◇ CRIT_COMP = / "GE", / "GT", / "LE" (par défaut), / "LT", # Si: equal_to("NOM_PARA", 'NB_ITER_NEWTON') ◇ VALE_I = int, ◇ MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS = / "DELTA_GRANDEUR", / "FIXE" (par défaut), / "IMPLEX", / "ITER_NEWTON", # Si: equal_to("MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS", 'FIXE') ◇ PCENT_AUGM = float (défaut: 100.0), # Si: equal_to("MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS", 'DELTA_GRANDEUR') ◇ / GROUP_MA = list[grma], / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◆ VALE_REF = float, ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "SIEF_ELGA", / "VARI_ELGA", ◆ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: equal_to("MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS", 'ITER_NEWTON') ◆ NB_ITER_NEWTON_REF = int, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 General parameters 2.1 Operand METHODE This keyword makes it possible to choose the mode of management of the list of time instants. By default, management is manual (METHODE='MANUEL'), which means that one will go through exactly the list of time instants defined by the user. In the event of subdivision, new time instants may be inserted. In automatic management (METHODE='AUTO'), the code automatically computes the new analysis time instants. The modes of computation of the new time steps are defined under the keyword ADAPTATION. The analysis time instants defined by the user are nevertheless respected. 2.2 Operand MODELE This keyword makes it possible to define the model in the case where one filters the field used by DELTA_GRANDEUR (see below) via a list of mesh-cell groups or of nodes. In this case, the model is mandatory. Otherwise, it is unnecessary. 3 Definition of the list of time instants - keyword DEFI_LIST 3.1 Operands LIST_INST and VALE The analysis time instants can be defined in 3 different ways: - either by supplying the keyword LIST_INST with a concept defined beforehand by the command DEFI_LIST_REEL, - or by supplying the keyword VALE with a list of reals, - or by supplying the keyword RESULTAT with a concept produced by STAT_NON_LINE or DYNA_NON_LINE. This keyword makes it possible to refine an already existing list of time instants. Indeed, one then defines a list of time instants SUBD_PAS times finer than the list of the time instants actually computed in STAT_NON_LINE or DYNA_NON_LINE. It should be noted that this list of actually computed time instants may differ from the list of time instants given as input to STAT_NON_LINE or DYNA_NON_LINE (for example because of the subdivision) and from the list of archived time instants (if one does not archive every time instant). This functionality is useful for checking the independence of the results with respect to the time discretisation. For example, to obtain a list of time instants 2 times finer, one chooses SUBD_PAS=2. Caution If the result data structure comes from an analysis with restart, it is not possible to reuse it in the command because one cannot extract a list of unique time instants (some time instants will be duplicated). 3.2 Operands PAS_MINI, PAS_MAXI, NB_PAS_MAXI These operands are to be supplied only in the case of automatic management of the list of time instants (METHODE='AUTO'). Automatic adaptation of the time step The operand PAS_MINI makes it possible to specify the minimum time step. If, in the course of adapting the time step, one is led to process a time step smaller than PAS_MINI, then the analysis stops. If this operand is not supplied, in the general case PAS_MINI is then equal to {10}^{-12} (this is moreover the minimum permitted value); if it is not supplied and MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='IMPLEX', then PAS_MINI is equal to 1/1000th of the first analysis time step (necessarily entered by the user via LIST_INST). If \Delta {t}_{i} \text{PAS\_MAXI} then \Delta {t}_{i} = \text{PAS\_MAXI} The operand NB_PAS_MAXI makes it possible to specify the number of time steps beyond which the analysis stops. The default value is one million (it is also the maximum permitted value). 3.3 Operand PAS_INIT Warning This keyword is taken into account by MECA_NON_LINE but is not used by STAT_NON_LINE. This keyword makes it possible to define the initial time step of the analysis. It has no effect if PAS_INIT is larger than the first time step computed from the list of time instants. An analysis time instant at PAS_INIT from the initial time instant is inserted. In the event of failure, of cutting and of automatic adaptation, it is possible that this precise time instant is not computed. 4 Keyword ECHEC This repeatable factor keyword makes it possible to manage the list of time instants in the event of failure of convergence. At each occurrence of the keyword ECHEC, one defines a cause of failure (see u4.34.03-echec_events ) and an action to be carried out if this cause is satisfied (see u4.34.03-echec_actions ). The actions may differ between each occurrence of the keyword ECHEC. If several causes of failure are satisfied simultaneously, the order of triggering of these failures is predetermined; in particular, 'ERREUR' always has priority over 'DELTA_GRANDEUR'. 4.1 Definition of the causes of failure The operand EVENEMENT makes it possible to define the causes of failure. 4.1.1 Event 'ERREUR' By default, the cause of failure is ERREUR. This cause groups the following reasons: - Exceeding the maximum permitted number of Newton iterations. - Failure during the local integration of the constitutive law. The local parameters of the algorithm used for the integration of the constitutive law are found in COMPORTEMENT. - Failure of the Deborst algorithm for plane stresses or 1D models. More details will be found in COMPORTEMENT. - Failure during the solution of the discrete contact problem (see R5.03.50). There is failure when the maximum number of contact iterations is exceeded or when the contact matrix is singular. - The system matrix is singular. Singularity detection relies on the parameter NPREC of the factor keyword SOLVEUR (see SOLVEUR). - The iterative linear solver has reached the maximum number of Krylov iterations set by NMAX_ITER in the factor keyword SOLVEUR (see SOLVEUR). - At convergence, physical criteria are not satisfied during the integration of the constitutive law (notion of “event-driven”). Even if one finds no occurrence of ECHEC / EVENEMENT = 'ERREUR', the code automatically adds one with the default parameters (that is, the action 'DECOUPE' in mode 'MANUEL' with SUBD_NIVEAU=4). 4.1.2 Event 'DIVE_RESI' The choice of the event 'DIVE_RESI' makes it possible to specify another possible cause of failure (“event-driven”). There will be failure if the residual does not decrease sufficiently in the course of the Newton iterations. More precisely, there will be failure if: min[R_{i}, R_{i-1}] > R_{i-2} for i \ge 3 , where R_{j} is the residual (RESI_GLOB_MAXI) at Newton iteration j . If there is failure, then the time step is subdivided (there are no other possibilities). The interest of this functionality is that it is not necessary to wait until one reaches the end of the permitted Newton iterations in order to recut the time step in the event of “notable” non-convergence. Non-convergence is detected sooner, so a saving of time is expected. Note Activation of this functionality with discrete contact is not advised because, in this type of analysis, the residual does not in general decrease monotonically. 4.1.3 Event 'DELTA_GRANDEUR' The choice of the event 'DELTA_GRANDEUR' makes it possible to specify another possible cause of failure (“event-driven”). There will be failure if the increment of a component of a field exceeds a fixed threshold, at convergence . One must then define the name of the field by the operand NOM_CHAM (displacement, stress or internal-variable field), the name of the component by the operand NOM_CMP and the value of the reference threshold by the operand VALE_REF. More precisely, let v be the component NOM_CMP of the field NOM_CHAM and valref the reference value VALE_REF. If the field NOM_CHAM is a field at the nodes and {N}_{no} is the set of all the nodes of the mesh, then there will be failure if, at convergence: max(\Delta \vert{v}^{i}\vert, \forall i\in {N}_{no}) > valref If the field NOM_CHAM is a field at the Gauss points, {N}_{sp,pg,el} is the set of all the sub-points of all the Gauss points of all the elements of the model, then there will be failure if, at convergence: max(\Delta \vert{v}^{i}\vert, \forall i\in {N}_{sp,pg,el}) > valref The increment \Delta is to be understood as the increment between two time instants. By default, the maximum is taken over the whole field. However, one can filter the location by using the keywords GROUP_MA (for the fields SIEF_ELGA and VARI_ELGA) or GROUP_NO (for the field DEPL). In this case, the maximum is taken respectively over the list of mesh-cell groups or the list of node groups. Example no. 1 with a law VMIS_ISOT_LINE: ECHEC = ( _F( EVENEMENT="DELTA_GRANDEUR", VALE_REF=0.1e-2, NOM_CHAM="VARI_ELGA", NOM_CMP="V1", ), ) There will be failure if the increment of the cumulative plasticity between two time steps exceeds 10^{-3} . Example no. 2: ECHEC = ( _F( EVENEMENT="DELTA_GRANDEUR", VALE_REF=5.0e-2, NOM_CHAM="DEPL", NOM_CMP="DX", ), _F(EVENEMENT="DELTA_GRANDEUR", VALE_REF=5.0e-2, NOM_CHAM="DEPL", NOM_CMP="DY"), ) There will be failure if the norm (sup norm) of the displacement (in 2D) varies by more than 0.05 between two time steps. Note In the two preceding examples, although EVENEMENT='ERREUR' is not present, it will still be activated by default. 4.1.4 Event 'INTERPENETRATION' This event detects the interpenetration of a node into a surface when regularised unilateral contact (penalisation) is activated. The user gives a value of the maximum penetration that he or she wants to obtain (parameter PENE_MAXI) and the code then adapts the penalisation coefficient (ACTION='ADAPT_COEF_PENA') or stops (ACTION='ARRET') in order to satisfy this constraint. This functionality is available only for contact with FORMULATION='DISCRETE' (see DEFI_CONTACT). 4.1.5 Event 'INSTABILITE' This event makes it possible to manage the course of a non-linear analysis when an instability is detected during the call to CRIT_STAB (cf. STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE). If this keyword CRIT_STAB is not used then this event cannot occur. If an instability is detected, an action will then be triggered, according to two possibilities: - ACTION='CONTINUE': this is the default value and the analysis will be continued, even in the event of instability, - ACTION='ARRET': if an instability is captured, then the non-linear solution will be stopped cleanly. More details on the instability criterion and its use are given in the documents R7.05.01 and U2.08.04. 4.1.6 Event 'RESI_MAXI' This event makes it possible to avoid the equilibrium residual “exploding”. Indeed, in certain situations, integration of the constitutive law over time steps that are too large increases the equilibrium residual. It is then in general no longer possible for the residual to decrease afterwards, which leads to failure of the analysis. By activating this event, one sets a maximum value on RESI_GLOB_MAXI during the Newton iterations, which makes it possible to cut the time step or to stop the analysis. 4.2 Definition of the actions to be carried out in the event of failure Depending on the event, only certain actions are possible; see the table below: | ACTION EVENEMENT | ARRET | DECOUPE | CONTINUE | ARCHIVAGE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ERREUR | YES | YES | | | | DIVE_RESI | | YES | | | | DELTA_GRANDEUR | YES | YES | | YES | | COLLISION | YES | YES | | | | INTERPENETRATION | YES | | | | | INSTABILITE | YES | | YES | | | RESI_MAXI | YES | YES | | | For example, in the most general case (EVENEMENT='ERREUR'), there are these possibilities: - Cut the time step (ACTION='DECOUPE'); - Stop (ACTION='ARRET'). 4.2.1 Action 'ARRET' If one chooses ACTION= 'ARRET', the analysis stops cleanly. 4.2.2 Action 'DECOUPE' This action consists in redoing the time step by cutting it. There are two methods of cutting the time step: AUTO mode and MANUEL mode. Note In MECA_NON_LINE, the time instants inserted by the cutting are not compulsory passage points. Thus if one uses time-step adaptation (acceleration) at the same time, it may be that some of the cutting time instants are ignored. 4.2.2.1 Cutting in mode MANUEL In MANUEL mode, the time step is cut uniformly. One must therefore specify the number of cuts using the keyword SUBD_PAS. Cutting in mode MANUEL with SUBD_PAS=2 The event ERREUR is triggered during time step 1, initially of length \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{1}} . This time step is then cut into two time steps (SUBD_PAS = 2) of equal lengths such that \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{2}} = \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{2}} = \frac{\Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{1}}}{2} . The next time step (number 2 in the initial configuration) then becomes time step 3; its length remains unchanged \Delta {t}_{3}^{{N}_{2}} = \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{1}} . | Time step | 1 | 2 | 3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Initial – 1 | \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{1}} | \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{1}} | | | Cutting – 2 | \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{2}} | \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{2}} | \Delta {t}_{3}^{{N}_{2}} | 4.2.2.2 The notion of cutting level Cutting of the time step is recursive: if the event ERREUR is triggered during an already cut time step, one cuts again. An example is shown in the following figure. Recursive cutting in mode MANUEL with SUBD_PAS=2 After the first cutting, the failure occurs in the (new) second time step. One cuts it again with \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{3}} = \Delta {t}_{3}^{{N}_{3}} = \frac{\Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{2}}}{2} . The following time step remains unchanged \Delta {t}_{4}^{{N}_{3}} = \Delta {t}_{3}^{{N}_{2}} , the first time step has converged and therefore also remains unchanged \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{3}} = \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{2}} . Which gives: | Time step | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Initial – 1 | \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{1}} | \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{1}} | | | | Cutting – 2 | \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{2}} | \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{2}} | \Delta {t}_{3}^{{N}_{2}} | | | Cutting – 3 | \Delta {t}_{1}^{{N}_{3}} | \Delta {t}_{2}^{{N}_{3}} | \Delta {t}_{3}^{{N}_{3}} | \Delta {t}_{4}^{{N}_{3}} | There cannot be a difference of more than one level between two time steps. 4.2.2.3 Cutting in mode AUTO The automatic cutting mode attempts a linear extrapolation of the value of the residuals. If one denotes by iter the Newton iteration and by {resi}^{\text{ext}} the value of the extrapolated residual (RESI_GLOB_RELA and/or RESI_GLOB_MAXI), then one seeks {a}_{1} , {a}_{2} and b such that: {resi}^{\text{ext}} = \frac{({a}_{1} \cdot iter + {a}_{2})}{b} Here is the algorithm used: > For iter = deb,fin > xx = log({resi}_{iter+1}) > If iter > fin -3 > poids = 2 > Otherwise > poids = 1 > One computes > xn = xn+poids > sx = sx+poids.xx > sy = sy+poids.iter > sxx = sxx+poids.({xx}^{2}) > syx = syx+poids.xx.iter > End For > {a}_{1} = sxx.sy–sx.syx > {a}_{2} = -(sx.sy)+syx.xn > b = -{sx}^{2}+sxx.xn To perform this extrapolation, a minimum of three Newton iterations is required and the last two iterations are considered to have twice the weight of the first ones; if this is not possible (or if the extrapolation fails for another reason), one automatically switches to MANUEL cutting mode (SUBD_PAS=4). 4.2.2.4 Control of the cutting If convergence is difficult and the event is triggered several times in a row, leading to recursive cutting of the time step, one can stop the process in two ways in MANUEL mode: - Cutting will stop as soon as cutting has been done more than SUBD_NIVEAU times. - Cutting will stop as soon as the time step is smaller than SUBD_PAS_MINI. In AUTO mode, only the keyword SUBD_PAS_MINI is available. Note concerning the buckling analysis During an elastoplastic buckling analysis, it may happen that the tangent matrix of the system is singular in the course of the Newton iterations. By recutting the time step, one can get past these difficult points. Particularities of the operand SUBD_NIVEAU The operand SUBD_NIVEAU is a notion which ought to be global to all the occurrences of the keyword ECHEC. Thus, this operand ought to be defined only once. In practice, this is not the case and nothing prevents one from defining a different value of SUBD_NIVEAU at each occurrence of the keyword ECHEC. To guard against that case, the algorithm will ultimately retain as the single global value of SUBD_NIVEAU the maximum of the SUBD_NIVEAU values defined by the user. 4.2.3 Action 'CONTINUE' If the event INSTABILITE is triggered, this action consists in attempting to continue the non-linear analysis. It is the default value for this event, which is the only one that can be combined with this action. 4.2.4 Action 'ARCHIVAGE' If the event DELTA_GRANDEUR is triggered, this action stops the analysis without error. In STAT_NON_LINE, the final time instant of the time step which led to the triggering of the event will be archived in the result. In MECA_NON_LINE, the initial and final time instants of the time step which led to the triggering of the event will be archived in the result. 5.1 Keyword ADAPTATION Time-step adaptation consists in computing a new time step \Delta {t}_{i+1} , from the information of the current time step \Delta {t}_{i} (and of the previous time steps \Delta {t}_{i-1} , \Delta {t}_{i-2} , ...). The aim is therefore to compute \Delta {t}_{i+1} = c \cdot \Delta {t}_{i} , where c is a real coefficient. The procedure is as follows: For occurrence k of the keyword ADAPTATION, one defines an event and a mode of computation of \Delta {t}_{i+1} . If the event is satisfied, then one computes {c}^{k} with the chosen mode of computation. One obtains a summary table of this type: | Occurrence no. 1 | {c}^{1} = 4.2 | | --- | --- | | Occurrence no. 2 | event not satisfied | | Occurrence no. 3 | {c}^{3} = 1.7 | | Occurrence no. 4 | {c}^{4} = 3.9 | Then, one chooses c=min({c}^{k}) among the occurrences whose event is satisfied. In this example, the new time step will be equal to \Delta {t}_{i+1} = 1.7 \cdot \Delta {t}_{i} . To use MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='IMPLEX', this keyword must be used only once. 5.1.1 Operand EVENEMENT This operand makes it possible to specify the triggering criterion for adaptation of the time step. If EVENEMENT='SEUIL', then the event is satisfied only if the threshold is crossed. If EVENEMENT='TOUT_INST', then the event is satisfied at every time instant; this case is mandatory with the IMPLEX method. If EVENEMENT='AUCUN', then the event is never satisfied. 5.1.2 Operands NB_INCR_SEUIL, NOM_PARA, CRIT_COMP, VALE_I These operands are to be supplied only in the case of a threshold-type event (EVENEMENT='SEUIL'). The event is satisfied if one has a “green light” NB_INCR_SEUIL times in a row, a green light being characterised by the condition defined by NOM_PARA, CRIT_COMP and VALE_I. For example if NB_INCR_SEUIL=2, NOM_PARA='NB_ITER_NEWTON', CRIT_COMP='LE' and VALE_I=5, then the event is satisfied if one has performed fewer than 5 Newton iterations twice in a row. Note There is no default value for VALE_I in the catalogue of the operator DEFI_LIST_INST. However, if its value is not supplied, VALE_I will be taken as half the maximum number of Newton iterations (declared in the options of the non-linear operator). 5.1.3 Operand MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS This operand is used to specify the mode of computation of the new time step (in fact, of the coefficient c ). If MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='FIXE', then the coefficient c is fixed. Its value is determined by the keyword PCENT_AUGM. The new time step is then equal to: \Delta {t}_{i+1} = \left( 1+\frac{\text{PCENT\_AUGM}}{100.} \right) \Delta {t}_{i} If the following time step \Delta {t}_{i+2} led to exceeding the next time instant of the list of time instants, it would automatically be reduced and the next increase would not be optimal. In this case, one limits \Delta {t}_{i+1} so that \Delta {t}_{i+2} = c \Delta {t}_{i+1} makes it possible to reach exactly the next time instant. Thus \Delta {t}_{i+3} (after the compulsory time instant) will be optimised, and so on. If MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='DELTA_GRANDEUR', then the coefficient c is linked to the variation, over the time step, of a chosen quantity. The following formula is used: c = \underset{i \in N}{min}\left( \frac{{V}_{ref}}{\vert \Delta {V}_{i} \vert} \right) with N the set of nodes or of Gauss points for which \Delta {V}_{i} is not zero. The reference value {V}_{ref} is chosen by the user. If the field \Delta V is identically zero, then one considers that the criterion (the event) is not satisfied. By default, all the values of the component are examined. However, one can filter the location by using the keywords GROUP_MA (for the fields SIEF_ELGA and VARI_ELGA) or GROUP_NO (for the field DEPL). In this case, the evaluation concerns only the list of mesh-cell groups or the list of node groups. If MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='ITER_NEWTON', then the coefficient c is linked to the variation, over the time step, of the number of Newton iterations. The following formula is used: c = \sqrt{\frac{{N}_{ref}}{{N}_{it}+1}} where {N}_{it} is the number of Newton iterations performed and {N}_{ref} a reference value chosen by the user. Recall that the prediction is considered to be Newton iteration no. 0, which means that if one converges as early as the prediction then c=\sqrt{{N}_{ref}} . If MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='IMPLEX', then the coefficient c is linked to the increments of internal variables (cumulative plastic strain or damage) of the previous time step (see R5.03.81). In this case, the keyword ADAPTATION must be used only once. The coefficient c will necessarily lie between 0.5 and 1.2. Moreover, by definition of the IMPLEX method there will be no cause of failure. 5.1.4 Operand PCENT_AUGM This operand is used to specify the percentage increase of the time step if MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS = 'FIXE'. By default, one increases by 100%, that is, one doubles the value of the time step. The value may be negative and must be strictly greater than -100. 5.1.5 Operands VALE_REF, NOM_CHAM, NOM_CMP These operands are used to specify the computation of the increase coefficient c of the time step if MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS='DELTA_GRANDEUR' (cf. u4.34.03-delta_grandeur) with VALE_REF the reference value {V}_{ref} and NOM_CHAM the name of the quantity field considered. 5.1.6 Operand NB_ITER_NEWTON_REF This operand is used to supply the reference number of Newton iterations, denoted {N}_{ref} (cf. u4.34.03-mode_calc_tplus) in the case where MODE_CALCUL_TPLUS = 'ITER_NEWTON'. 5.2 Operand INFO For the moment, this operand is not used.

u4.34.04 Operator DEFI_LIST_FREQ u4.34.04 Operator DEFI_LIST_FREQ 1 Purpose To create a list of reals, possibly refining around frequency values supplied by the user. It produces a data structure of type listr8. 2 Syntax DEFI_LIST_FREQ( ◇ / VALE = float, / DEBUT = float, ◇ / INTERVALLE = _F( ◆ JUSQU_A = float, ◆ / NOMBRE = int, / PAS = float, ), ◇ RAFFINEMENT = _F( ◆ LIST_RAFFINE = float, ◇ NB_POINTS = int (défaut: 5), ◇ PAS_MINI = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", / "LARGEUR_3DB", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF') or equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◇ DISPERSION = float (défaut: 0.01), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'LARGEUR_3DB')) ◆ / AMOR_REDUIT = float, / LIST_AMOR = listr8, ), ◇ EQUI_MODES = _F( ◇ TYPE_SAISIE = / "LISTE" (par défaut), / "MATR_ASSE", ◆ FREQ_MIN = float, ◆ FREQ_MAX = float, # Si: (equal_to("TYPE_SAISIE", 'LISTE')) ◇ LIST_FREQ = listr8, # Si: (equal_to("TYPE_SAISIE", 'MATR_ASSE')) ◇ MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ MATR_MASS = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ NB_MODES = int (défaut: 40), ◇ NB_POINTS_INIT = int (défaut: 10), ◇ NB_POINTS_SUPP = int (défaut: 1), ◇ ITER_MAXI = int (défaut: 20), ◇ TOLERANCE = float (défaut: 0.01), ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands VALE, DEBUT, INTERVALLE, JUSQU_A, TITRE, INFO These keywords are used directly by DEFI_LIST_REEL to define the initial list of frequencies. Note All the values requested in the base list are automatically in the final list at the output of DEFI_LIST_FREQ. 3.2 Keyword RAFFINEMENT 3.2.1 Operand LIST_RAFFINE List of the frequencies around which one wishes to refine. This list can be built from a Python list. This keyword is particularly useful in the case of a harmonic analysis of a structure (operator DYNA_VIBRA), because it will make it possible to compute the harmonic response around the eigenfrequencies of the structure and thus to recover the local extrema. It is possible to recover the eigenfrequencies directly in a data structure of type mode_XXX coming from a modal analysis carried out for example with the command CALC_MODES. To do this, it is enough to use the method LIST_VARI_ACCES(). Example: modes = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=matassr, MATR_MASS=matassm, OPTION="AJUSTE", CALC_FREQ=_F(FREQ=(5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 24.0, 27.0)), ) list_freq = modes.LIST_VARI_ACCES()['FREQ'] list_freq is thus a Python list containing the list of the eigenfrequencies present in the result modes. 3.2.2 Operand PAS_MINI If the gap between two values is smaller than PAS_MINI then one of them is removed. With this rule, the removed value may be a value present in the initial list (VALE) or in the list of refinement points (LIST_RAFFINE). 3.2.3 Operand DISPERSION DISPERSION is the width of the interval surrounding each frequency of LIST_RAFFINE where one wants to refine. 3.2.4 Operand CRITERE The width of the interval df surrounding each frequency freq_{i} of LIST_RAFFINE where one wants to refine is determined from the value of DISPERSION and is equal to: - If CRITERE='RELATIF': df = disp . freq_{i} - If CRITERE='ABSOLU': df = disp If CRITERE='LARGEUR_3DB', one supplies the list of damping values with the keywords AMOR_REDUIT or LIST_AMOR. This is the list of reduced dampings ( \eta_{1} , \eta_{2} , ..., \eta_{n} ) corresponding to each eigenmode of the system in the form of a list of reals. Name of the concept of type listr8 containing the list of reduced dampings ( \eta_{1} , \eta_{2} , ..., \eta_{n} ). Note If the number of reduced dampings given is smaller than the number of basis vectors used in the modal basis, the dampings of the additional vectors are taken equal to the last damping of the list. If the damping \eta_{i} is non-zero, the frequency freq_{i} used to compute the length of the interval df is the frequency freq_{i} of LIST_RAFFINE shifted to the resonance frequency of a forced system, that is freq_{i} = freq_{i} \sqrt{(1-2{\eta}_{i}^{2})} . The length of the interval df surrounding each frequency freq_{i} where one wants to refine is equal to: - If \eta_{i} \ne 0 : df = 2{\eta}_{i} freq_{i} - If \eta_{i} \ne 0 : df = 0.01 freq_{i} 3.2.5 Operand NB_POINTS NB_POINTS is the number of points that one wants to add around the frequencies of the list LIST_RAFFINE. The added points are uniformly distributed in the interval df . Therefore if NB_POINTS is an odd number, the frequencies of LIST_RAFFINE will be in the final list. If CRITERE='LARGEUR_3DB' and NB_POINTS is an even number, one keeps the frequency freq_{i} of LIST_RAFFINE and one adds the resonance frequency of a forced system such that freq_{i} = freq_{i} \sqrt{(1-2{\eta}_{i}^{2})} . 3.3 Keyword EQUI_MODES This keyword concerns the parameterisation of an algorithm for balancing frequency bands, upstream of a multi-band modal analysis via the operator CALC_MODES. This algorithm aims to determine the ends of frequency bands, so that the latter contain a comparable, and limited, number of eigenfrequencies ( i.e. , of the order of \mathcal{O}(10^{1}) ). This makes it possible in particular to improve the robustness and the performance of a multi-band modal analysis (see R5.01.04). To do this, the aforementioned algorithm relies on an iterative procedure, aiming to carry out several calls to an eigenvalue-counting procedure, so as to “discover” sufficiently the distribution of the eigenvalues of the problem and thus propose a cutting into balanced frequency bands. When the keyword EQUI_MODES is used, the operator DEFI_LIST_FREQ returns a list of reals comprising the ends of the optimised frequency bands. This list can then be supplied to the operator CALC_MODES, via the operand FREQ of the keyword CALC_FREQ with OPTION = 'BANDE' . The aforementioned algorithm takes into account two types of input data: - a list of reals comprising eigenfrequencies computed beforehand, - stiffness and mass matrices. In such a case, the aforementioned algorithm is based on the eigenvalue-counting procedure of the operator INFO_MODE. 3.3.1 Operands FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX The operands FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX make it possible to define the ends of the interval in which the procedure of balancing frequency bands is carried out. 3.3.2 Operand TYPE_SAISIE The mode of use of the frequency-band balancing algorithm is defined via TYPE_SAISIE. The case TYPE_SAISIE = 'LISTE' corresponds to the specification of a list of precomputed eigenfrequencies. The specification of assembled stiffness and mass matrices can be done by supplying TYPE_SAISIE = 'MATR_ASSE' . 3.3.3 Operand LIST_FREQ The operand LIST_FREQ makes it possible to specify a list of reals corresponding to precomputed eigenfrequencies, in the case TYPE_SAISIE = 'LISTE' . 3.3.4 Operands MATR_RIGI and MATR_MASS In the case of the specification of assembled matrices ( TYPE_SAISIE = 'MATR_ASSE' ), the stiffness and mass matrices are supplied via the operands MATR_RIGI and MATR_MASS. It is important to note that the frequency-band balancing algorithm is implemented only in the case of standard real symmetric generalised eigenvalue problems (see R5.01.01). Consequently, only real symmetric assembled matrices can be used. 3.3.5 Parameters of the balancing algorithm The keyword EQUI_MODES also makes it possible to specify (optional) parameters relating to the algorithm for balancing frequency bands, namely: - NB_MODES, corresponding to the desired number of eigenfrequencies per band. It is set by default to 40, based on the recommendations stated in the reference document R5.01.04. - ITER_MAXI, making it possible to set the maximum number of iterations of the algorithm, - NB_POINTS_INIT, making it possible to set the initial number of eigenfrequency search intervals used by the algorithm, - NB_POINTS_SUPP, making it possible to define the number of additional search intervals in the course of an iteration of the algorithm. - TOLERANCE, making it possible to define the stopping criterion of the algorithm. In the case of the balancing of B frequency bands, the latter are considered to be sufficiently balanced if the following condition is satisfied: where \varepsilon_i denotes the error defined as follows: N_i denoting the number of eigenfrequencies in band i , N_b the desired number of eigenfrequencies per band (NB_MODES), and N the total number of eigenfrequencies lying in the interval [FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX]. 3.3.6 Description of the result and use in a modal analysis In the case where the frequency-band balancing algorithm is used, the data structure produced by the operator DEFI_LIST_FREQ is a table ( table_sdaster ), whose columns gather information relating to the results of the algorithm, namely: - NUME_BANDE, corresponding to the numbers of each frequency band obtained, - FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX, corresponding respectively to the minimum and maximum ends of each band, - NB_MODES, corresponding to the number of eigenfrequencies contained in each band, - NB_CIBLE, corresponding to the desired number of eigenfrequencies per band ( i.e. NB_MODES in EQUI_MODES), - ERR_REL, corresponding to the relative error \left|\varepsilon_i\right| associated with each band, - NB_ITER, corresponding to the number of iterations carried out, - ITER_MAXI, corresponding to the maximum number of iterations permitted ( i.e. ITER_MAXI in EQUI_MODES). This table can then be used to carry out a multi-band modal analysis with the operator CALC_MODES, via the extraction of the frequency bands in Python . An example of use is given below: table = DEFI_LIST_FREQ( EQUI_MODES=_F(TYPE_SAISIE="MATR_ASSE", FREQ_MIN=0.0, FREQ_MAX=500.0, MATR_RIGI=matassr, MATR_MASS=matassm, ), ) list_freq = [table.EXTR_TABLE().values()["FREQ_MIN"][0]] + table.EXTR_TABLE().values()["FREQ_MAX"] modes = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=matassr, MATR_MASS=matassm, OPTION="BANDE", CALC_FREQ=_F(FREQ=list_freq), ) 4 Examples Let us imagine that one wants to create the base list: (1., 3., 5., 10., 15.) And that one wants to refine around the frequency 3.5 with the criterion 'ABSOLU'. One writes: lr = DEFI_LIST_FREQ( DEBUT=1.0, INTERVALLE=(_F(JUSQU_A=5.0, NOMBRE=2), _F(JUSQU_A=15.0, PAS=5)), RAFFINEMENT=( _F(LIST_RAFFINE=3.5, PAS_MINI=0.001, NB_POINTS=5, CRITERE="ABSOLU", DISPERSION=0.02), ), ) One then obtains a list containing the values: (1.0, 3.0, 3.49, 3.495, 3.5, 3.505, 3.51, 5.0, 10.0, 15.0) Using the criterion 'RELATIF' for the refinement, one can write: lr = DEFI_LIST_FREQ( VALE=(1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 10.0, 15.0), RAFFINEMENT=_F( LIST_RAFFINE=(3.5,), PAS_MINI=0.001, NB_POINTS=6, CRITERE="RELATIF", DISPERSION=0.03 ), ) One then obtains a listr8 list containing the values: (1., 3., 3.4475, 3.4685, 3.4895, 3.5105, 3.5315, 3.5525, 5., 10., 15.) The test case sdld21b presents other examples of use.

u4.35.01 Operator DEFI_FONC_FLUI u4.35.01 Operator DEFI_FONC_FLUI 1 Purpose To define a fluid flow-velocity profile along a beam. Profiles corresponding to “standard” profiles coming from experimental results and used within a dynamic analysis taking fluid-elastic forces into account. The velocities are computed at the nodes for which one looks up, in the mesh concept, the value of the associated curvilinear abscissa. At present, it is possible to apply a velocity profile defined by DEFI_FONC_FLUI only on a structure whose mesh cells are of type 'SEG2'. The concept produced is of type fonction (parameter 'ABSC', curvilinear abscissa) 2 Syntax fonction = DEFI_FONC_FLUI( ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◆ / GROUP_NO_INIT = grno, ◆ / GROUP_NO_FIN = grno, ◆ VITE = _F( ◇ VALE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◆ PROFIL = / "UNIFORME", / "LEONARD", ◇ NB_BAV = / 0 (par défaut), / 2, / 3, ), ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE ♦ MAILLAGE = ma Name of the mesh for which the curvilinear abscissa is defined. 3.2 Operands GROUP_NO_INIT and GROUP_NO_FIN ♦ GROUP_NO_INIT = gni, [grno] ♦ GROUP_NO_FIN = gnf, [grno] The function is defined over the whole mesh. The operands 'GROUP_NO_INIT' and 'GROUP_NO_FIN' make it possible to define the zone of application of the velocity profile. Outside this zone, the value of the function is zero. 3.3 Keyword VITE ♦ VITE Factor keyword; it makes it possible to define the velocity profile. ♦ PROFIL This operand, associated with the operands VALE and NB_BAV, makes it possible to define a “standard” profile: 'UNIFORME' or 'LEONARD'. / ◊ VALE = vale Makes it possible to define the level of the function, if the standard profile is 'UNIFORME'. / ◊ NB_BAV If the profile is of type 'LEONARD', NB_BAV defines a “standard” profile stored in a catalogue. Note: BAV (Anti-Vibration Bar) is terminology linked to steam-generator tubes. NB_BAV corresponds to the number of anti-vibration bars located in the zone where the profile is obtained. 3.4 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL Type of interpolation of the function between the parameter values of the domain of definition. | 'LIN': | linear, | | --- | --- | | 'LOG': | logarithmic, | 3.5 Operands PROL_GAUCHE and PROL_DROITE ◊ PROL_GAUCHE / PROL_DROITE Define the type of extension to the left (respectively to the right) of the domain of definition of the parameter. | 'LINEAIRE': | the function is extended to the left (to the right) by a straight-line segment with the same slope as at the lower (upper) bound of the domain of definition of the parameter, | | --- | --- | | 'EXCLU': | extrapolation of the function outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden, | | 'CONSTANT': | the function is extended to the left (to the right) by the value that it takes at the lower (upper) bound of the domain of definition of the parameter. | 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO Printout level. | INFO = 1: | no printout, | | --- | --- | | INFO = 2: | one prints in the MESSAGE file the name of the function, the number of definition points, the name of the parameter, the name of the result, the extension and interpolation options and the first 10 values of the function, in increasing order of the parameter. | 3.7 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Text argument defining the title attached to the output fonction concept. 4 Presentation of the standard velocity profiles They are defined in a form discretised in \theta (angle in degrees varying from 0. to 180.) - [Figure 4-a], [Figure 4-b] and [Figure 4-c]. Thus, it is possible from equation [eq. 4-1] to apply these profiles over a domain defined in curvilinear abscissa. > v({s}_{i})=\frac{{\alpha}_{i}\cdot {\gamma}_{i}+{\beta}_{i}}{{v}_{\mathrm{moy}}} eq. 4-1 with \lbrace \begin{array}{}{\alpha}_{i}=\frac{{v}_{k+1}-{v}_{k}}{{\theta}_{k+1}-{\theta}_{k}}\\ {\gamma}_{i}=180(\frac{{s}_{i}-{s}_{ni}}{{s}_{\mathrm{nf}}-{s}_{ni}})\\ {\beta}_{i}=\frac{{v}_{k}{\theta}_{k+1}-{v}_{k+1}{\theta}_{k}}{{\theta}_{k+1}-{\theta}_{k}}\end{array} {s}_{i},{s}_{ni},{s}_{\mathrm{nf}} are respectively the curvilinear abscissa of the current point, of the initial node and of the final node which define the zone of application. k: index in the table of the discretised function. {v}_{\mathrm{moy}}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}({\alpha}_{i}\cdot {\gamma}_{i}+{\beta}_{i})}{N} N: number of discretisation points of the zone of application. Figure 4-a: Velocity profile - NB_BAV = 0 Figure 4-b: Velocity profile - NB_BAV = 2 Figure 4-c: Velocity profile - NB_BAV = 3 5 Bibliography 1. GAY: Flustru Version 2.0 - General presentation. User's guide - Fortran source of the software. Technical note EDF/DER HT-32/93.05A.

u4.35.02 Operator FONC_FLUI_STRU u4.35.02 Operator FONC_FLUI_STRU 1 Purpose To create a constant function parameterised by the curvilinear abscissa. This function gives the value of the added-mass coefficient for a configuration of the type “tube bundle under transverse flow”. This function is used downstream by the operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01, factor keyword ELAS_FLUI. It produces a concept of type fonction. 2 Syntax fonction = FONC_FLUI_STRU( ◆ TYPE_FLUI_STRU = type_flui_stru, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands ♦ TYPE_FLUI_STRU = typeflui Concept of type [type_flui_stru] produced by the operator DEFI_FLUI_STRU [U4.25.01], providing the value of the added-mass coefficient Cm. Notes: The value of Cm can be imposed by means of the keyword COEF_MASS_AJOU appearing in the command DEFI_FLUI_STRU. If fluid-elastic coupling is taken into account, the added-mass coefficient can be computed by the operator as a function of the other characteristics of the bundle. The operator FONC_FLUI_STRU creates a concept of type [fonction] which is then directly usable by DEFI_MATERIAU [U4.43.01], keyword ELAS_FLUI. The function is constant, parameterised by the curvilinear abscissa, and gives the value of Cm. The combined use of the operators FONC_FLUI_STRU and then DEFI_MATERIAU, option ELAS_FLUI, is necessary when one studies a configuration of the type “tube bundle under transverse flow”, and it is permitted only for this type of configuration.

u4.36.01 Operator LIRE_INTE_SPEC u4.36.01 Operator LIRE_INTE_SPEC 1 Purpose To read complex functions from an external file in order to create an interspectral matrix. The user file is coded in Ascii. The functions read are of type fonction_C. The concept produced is of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = LIRE_INTE_SPEC( ◆ UNITE = unit, ◇ FORMAT_C = / "REEL_IMAG", / "MODULE_PHASE" (par défaut), ◇ FORMAT = / "ASTER" (par défaut), / "IDEAS", ◇ NOM_PARA = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", / "TEMP", / "INST", / "X", / "Y", / "Z", / "EPSI", / "FREQ" (par défaut), / "PULS", / "AMOR", / "ABSC", ◇ NOM_RESU = text (défaut: "DSP"), ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN", / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU", ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU", ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand UNITE ♦ UNITE= u Logical unit number of the external file on which the reading is done. 3.2 Operand FORMAT Defines the reading format: - 'ASTER' by default, - 'IDEAS' if one reads results obtained with IDEAS 3.3 Operand FORMAT_C Defines the reading format for complex functions: - 'MODULE_PHASE' by default, - 'REEL_IMAG' real part and imaginary part. 3.4 Operand NOM_PARA Defines the name of the parameter of the function (abscissa). By default one takes 'FREQ'. 3.5 Operand NOM_RESU Defines the name of the result of the function (ordinate) 3.6 Operands PROL_DROITE / PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE= Defines the extension of the function to the right of the domain of definition of the variable. ◊ PROL_GAUCHE= Defines the extension of the function to the left of the domain of definition of the variable: | 'CONSTANT' | | | --- | --- | | 'LINEAIRE' | for an extension along the first segment defined (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last segment defined (PROL_DROITE). | | 'EXCLU' | if extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden. | 3.7 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL= - 'LOG' logarithmic interpolation between two values of the domain of definition. - 'LIN' linear interpolation between two values of the domain of definition. 3.8 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= Specifies the printout options on the message file. | 1 | printing of the attributes of the functions: number of definition points, names of the parameter and of the result, as well as the extension and checking options | | --- | --- | | 2 | like 1, plus the list of the first 10 values of each function in increasing order of the parameter | For example: - PROL_DROITE = 'CONSTANT', PROL_GAUCHE = 'CONSTANT' - PROL_DROITE = 'LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE = 'EXCLU' 4 Verification stage Checking of the number of values read per function. Checking of the number of functions read. 5 Notes on use The functions associated with the interspectral matrix are accessible to the user by means of the command RECU_FONCTION U4.32.03 using the keyword INTE_SPEC. 5.1 File syntax The information read on the file is composed of three parts: - a mandatory chapter-heading keyword: INTERSPECTRE. - the keyword DIM, dimension of the matrix. - 'n' sub-files defining 'n' complex functions. Each sub-file begins with the keyword FONCTION_C and ends with FINSF. - the file must end with FIN. 5.2 Descriptor 5.2.1 Keyword describing the characteristics of the matrix ♦ DIM = dim An integer makes it possible to define the dimension of the matrix. Note: The sign '=' is mandatory. 5.2.2 Keyword describing a fonction_C Preliminary note: 'n', the number of functions to be defined, is equal to: n = (dim (dim+1))/2, since the matrix under consideration is 'HERMITIAN'. The n functions are defined by their indices I and J in the matrix. Only the upper triangular part of the matrix is defined, (indices (1,1); (1,2); (2,2); (1,3); ... (n,n)). ♦ FONCTION_C ♦ I = entier indice ligne de la fonction dans la matrice. ♦ J = entier indice colonne de la fonction dans la matrice. ♦ NB_POIN = entier nombre de points de la FONCTION ♦ VALEUR = 3 NB_POINréels doivent être présents. La lecture des valeurs s'effectue ligne à ligne. On each line the following are defined, in the following order: - the value of the parameter, the real part of the result, the imaginary part of the result (FORMAT= 'REEL_IMAG'), or - the value of the parameter, the modulus of the result, the phase of the result (FORMAT='MODULE_PHASE') Note: For the format MODULE_PHASE, the phase is given in degrees. 6 Example Example of user-file syntax: INTERSPECTRE DIM = 2 FONCTION_C I = 1 J = 1 NB_POIN = 4 VALEUR = | 0 | 10 | 0.1 | | --- | --- | --- | | 10 | 10 | 0.1 | | 10.01 | 0 | 0 | | 100 | 0 | 0 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | FINSF | | | | | | | | FONCTION_C | | | | | | | | I = 1 | | | | | | | | J = 2 | | | | | | | | NB_POIN = 4 | | | | | | | | VALEUR = | | | | 0 | 2 | 0.5 | | --- | --- | --- | | 10 | 2 | 0.5 | | 10.01 | 0 | 0 | | 100 | 0 | 0 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | FINSF | | | | | | | | FONCTION_C | | | | | | | | I = 2 | | | | | | | | J = 2 | | | | | | | | NB_POIN =4 | | | | | | | | VALEUR = | | | | 0 | 20 | 0.1 | | --- | --- | --- | | 10 | 20 | 0.1 | | 10.01 | 0 | 0 | | 100 | 0 | 0 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | FINSF | | | | | | | | FIN | | | Example of command syntax: AUTOSPC=LIRE_INTE_SPEC( UNITE=19, FORMAT='MODULE_PHASE', PROL_DROITE='EXCLU', PROL_GAUCHE='EXCLU', INTERPOL='LIN' )

u4.36.02 Operator DEFI_INTE_SPEC u4.36.02 Operator DEFI_INTE_SPEC 1 Purpose To define a spectral density matrix (one also says: interspectral matrix). The terms of the matrix are defined by: - constants (white noise), - existing complex functions, - the analytical formula of KANAI-TAJIMI. It produces a data structure of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = DEFI_INTE_SPEC( ◇ DIMENSION = int (défaut: 1), ◆ / PAR_FONCTION = _F( ◆ / NOEUD_I = no, / NUME_ORDRE_I = int, # Si: exists("NUME_ORDRE_I") ◆ NUME_ORDRE_J = int, # Si: exists("NOEUD_I") ◆ NOEUD_J = no, ◆ NOM_CMP_I = text, ◆ NOM_CMP_J = text, ◆ FONCTION = fonction_c / fonction, ), / KANAI_TAJIMI = _F( ◆ / NUME_ORDRE_I = int, / NOEUD_I = no, # Si: exists("NUME_ORDRE_I") ◆ NUME_ORDRE_J = int, # Si: exists("NOEUD_I") ◆ NOEUD_J = no, ◆ NOM_CMP_I = text, ◆ NOM_CMP_J = text, ◇ FREQ_MIN = float, ◇ FREQ_MAX = float (défaut: 100.0), ◇ PAS = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ AMOR_REDUIT = float (défaut: 0.6), ◇ FREQ_MOY = float (défaut: 5.0), ◇ / VALE_R = float, / VALE_C = complex, ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ), / CONSTANT = _F( ◆ / NUME_ORDRE_I = int, / NOEUD_I = no, # Si: exists("NUME_ORDRE_I") ◆ NUME_ORDRE_J = int, # Si: exists("NOEUD_I") ◆ NOEUD_J = no, ◆ NOM_CMP_I = text, ◆ NOM_CMP_J = text, ◇ FREQ_MIN = float, ◇ FREQ_MAX = float (défaut: 100.0), ◇ PAS = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ / VALE_R = float, / VALE_C = complex, ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ PROL_DROITE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ◇ PROL_GAUCHE = / "CONSTANT", / "LINEAIRE", / "EXCLU" (par défaut), ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand DIMENSION ◊ DIMENSION = n Dimension of the spectral density matrix, stored in a table of interspectra (tabl_intsp). 3.2 Keyword PAR_FONCTION ♦ PAR_FONCTION= Factor keyword; it makes it possible to define a term (i, j) of the interspectral matrix from concepts of type fonction_c already defined. 3.2.1 Operands NUME_ORDRE_I, NUME_ORDRE_J NUME_ORDRE_I = i NUME_ORDRE_J = j Pair of indices (row, column) of the matrix on which one will assign a function. These operands are excluded with the operands NOEUD_I NOEUD_J NOM_CMP_I NOM_CMP_J. 3.2.2 Operands NOEUD_I, NOEUD_J, NOM_CMP_I, NOM_CMP_J NOEUD_I = nd_i [noeud] NOEUD_J = nd_j [noeud] NOM_CMP_I = ncmp_i [Kn] NOM_CMP_J = ncmp_j [Kn] These operands correspond to the names of the nodes and of the components (row, column) of the matrix where one will assign a function. These operands are excluded with the operands NUME_ORDRE_I NUME_ORDRE_J. 3.2.3 Operand FONCTION ♦ FONCTION : fonct fonct is a concept of type fonction_c. 3.3 Keyword KANAI_KAJIMI KANAI_TAJIMI= Factor keyword; it makes it possible to define a spectral density function using the model of Kanai and Tajimi. This spectral density function corresponds to that of a filtered white noise [bib2]. One gives the three parameters of the spectral density of the KANAI_TAJIMI model: damping, frequency and level. 3.3.1 Operands NUME_ORDRE_I, NUME_ORDRE_J NUME_ORDRE_I = i NUME_ORDRE_J = j Pair of indices (row, column) of the interspectral matrix. Having no model of spectral coherence, the Kanai-Tajimi model makes it possible only to create auto-spectra. One must therefore choose i = j (in general, one will choose here n=1 and i=j=1). These operands are excluded with the operands NOEUD_I NOEUD_J NOM_CMP_I NOM_CMP_J. 3.3.2 Operands NOEUD_I, NOEUD_J, NOM_CMP_I, NOM_CMP_J NOEUD_I = nd_i [noeud] NOEUD_J = nd_j [noeud] NOM_CMP_I = ncmp_i [Kn] NOM_CMP_J = ncmp_j [Kn] These operands correspond to the names of the nodes and of the components (row, column) of the matrix where one will assign a function. In the case of the Kanai-Tajimi model, one chooses NOEUD_I = NOEUD_J and NOM_CMP_I = NOM_CMP_J. These operands are excluded with the operands NUME_ORDRE_I NUME_ORDRE_J. 3.3.3 Operands AMOR_REDUIT/FREQ_MOY/VALE_R / VALE_C ◊ AMOR_REDUIT = amor ◊ FREQ_MOY = fmoy ◊ / VALE_R = valr / VALE_C = valc fmoy and amor are the natural frequency and the reduced damping of the filter. The level may be given in complex or real form. 3.3.4 Operands INTERPOL/PROL_GAUCHE/PROL_DROITE For each function one gives the classical parameters which govern the interpolation and the extrapolation of the function produced. The possibilities as well as the default values are recalled on page 2. ◊ INTERPOL ◊ PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE Pour plus de détails voir les [:ref: §3.4 ] et [:ref: §3.5 ]. 3.3.5 Operands FREQ_MIN/FREQ_MAX/PAS One gives the parameters of the frequency discretisation. ◊ FREQ_MIN = fmin ◊ FREQ_MAX = fmax ◊ PAS = pas 3.3.6 Operands PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE = Define the type of extension to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable: | 'CONSTANT' | for an extension with the last (or first) value of the function, | | --- | --- | | 'LINEAIRE' | for an extension along the first segment defined (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last segment defined (PROL_DROITE), | | 'EXCLU' | if extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden (in this case if an analysis requests a value of the function outside the domain of definition, the code will stop in fatal error). | For example: - PROL_DROITE = 'CONSTANT' , PROL_GAUCHE = 'CONSTANT' - PROL_DROITE = 'LINEAIRE', PROL_GAUCHE = 'EXCLU' Note: The type of extension and of interpolation are independent of one another. 3.3.7 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL= Type of interpolation of the function between the values of the domain of definition of the function: one type for the interpolation of the parameter and one for the interpolation of the function. This is obtained by supplying a list of texts among: INTERPOL = ('LIN', 'LOG') | 'LIN': | linear, | | --- | --- | | 'LOG': | logarithmic, | Note: If only one value is specified, it is taken into account both for the interpolation of the parameter and for that of the function. INTERPOL = 'LOG' is equivalent to ('LOG', 'LOG'). 3.4 Keyword CONSTANT ◊ CONSTANT= Factor keyword which makes it possible to define a spectral density function corresponding to a band-limited white noise (constant spectral density over the frequency band considered). All the keywords under this factor keyword have the same meaning as for the factor keyword KANAI_TAJIMI except AMOR and FREQ_MOY, which have no meaning here. 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre titre is the title of the analysis to be printed at the head of the results.
