See U4.03.01. 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= | 1: | no printout. | | --- | --- | | 2: | printing of the characteristics of the interspectral matrix defined. | 4 Example In the example below one defines a spectral density function (in interspectrum terms it is a 1 x 1 matrix) with a constant value: INTEREXC = DEFI_INTE_SPEC ( DIMENSION=1, INFO=2, CONSTANT=_F( NUME_ORDRE_I=1, NUME_ORDRE_J=1, FREQ_MIN=0., FREQ_MAX=100., PAS=1., PROL_GAUCHE='CONSTANT', PROL_DROITE='CONSTANT', INTERPOL='LIN', VALE_C=(‘RI’,1.,0.), ), ) ; To define the interspectrum of a white noise filtered by an oscillator represented by the KANAI‑TAJIMI filter: INTKTJ1 = DEFI_INTE_SPEC ( DIMENSION=1, INFO=2, KANAI_TAJIMI=_F( NUME_ORDRE_I=1, NUME_ORDRE_J=1, FREQ_MOY=15., AMOR=0.05, VALE_R=1., INTERPOL='LIN', PROL_GAUCHE='CONSTANT', PROL_DROITE='CONSTANT', FREQ_MIN=0., FREQ_MAX=30., PAS=5., ), ) ; The 3 parameters of the filter have been given: 1. damping = 0.05, 2. frequency = 15. Hz, 3. level = 1. 5 Bibliography 1. J.S. BENDAT, J.WILEGSON: "Engineering application of correlation and spectral analysis". 1. DUVAL "Dynamic response under random excitations in Code_Aster : theoretical principles and examples of use". Note DER HP-61/92-148

u4.36.03 Operator CALC_INTE_SPEC u4.36.03 Operator CALC_INTE_SPEC 1 Purpose To compute a spectral density function from a time signal (function of time). The spectral density (or auto-spectrum) is the arithmetic mean of a certain number of spectra computed on different time blocks of the signal. If several signals are given, one obtains a spectral density matrix (or interspectrum). It produces a concept of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = CALC_INTE_SPEC( ◇ INST_INIT = float, ◆ INST_FIN = float, ◇ DUREE_ANALYSE = float, ◇ DUREE_DECALAGE = float, ◆ NB_POIN = int, ◆ FONCTION = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands INST_INIT / INST_FIN ◊ INST_INIT= ii First value of the parameter for which the signals will be used for the computation of the interspectral matrix (initial time instant). ♦ INST_FIN= if Last value of the parameter for which the signals will be used for the computation of the interspectral matrix (final time instant). Note: The functions will be computed with the interpolation mode which has been associated with them. It is advised, in order not to have a discretisation problem, that the functions have an authorised linear interpolation. Figure 3.1-a: Analysis and computation on 3 windows with overlap 3.2 Operands DUREE_ANALYSE / DUREE_DECALAGE ◊ DUREE_ANALYSE= da The functions will be cut into several windows of analysis duration da. For each of these windows an interspectral matrix is computed. The interspectral matrix resulting from the operator will be the arithmetic mean of the matrices computed. ◊ DUREE_DECALAGE= dd Makes it possible, when cutting the functions into windows according to the analysis duration, to shift each window with respect to the others by a duration dd. If {t}_{k} is the initial time instant of the {k}^{\text{ième}} window, the initial time instant of the {(k+1)}^{\text{ième}} window will be {t}_{k} +dd. Let x[k] and y[k] be two discrete time signals and {x}_{p}[k] and {y}_{p}[k] the respective time windows obtained by cutting. If X[k] and Y[k] denote their discrete FOURIER transforms, then the interspectral matrix is written[bib1]: S[k]\text{vaut}(\begin{array}{cc}{S}_{xx}[k]& {S}_{xy}[k]\\ {S}_{xy}^{\text{ }}[k]& {S}_{yy}[k]\end{array}) where {S}_{xx}[k]=\frac{1}{\mathrm{p.n}\Delta t}\sum_{i=1}^{p}{X}_{p}[k].{X}_{p}^{\text{ }}[k] {S}_{xy}[k]=\frac{1}{\mathrm{p.n}\Delta t}\sum_{i=1}^{p}{X}_{p}[k].{Y}_{p}^{\text{ }}[k] where n is the number of points per block, p is the number of blocks. Caution: This averaging, perfectly suited to “real” signals resulting from a measurement, is not suitable without care for functions close to a sine (the averaging frequency must be much higher than the frequency of the signal. Note: If the signals processed come from the operator GENE_FONC_ALEA, possibly via the computation of a dynamic response (operator DYNA_VIBRA for example), then it is advised to process each of the draws of GENE_FONC_ALEA independently. In this case, one must choose analysis and shift durations equal to the duration of each of the draws of GENE_FONC_ALEA (cf. GENE_FONC_ALEA U4.36.05). 3.3 Operand NB_POIN ♦ NB_POIN= np Number of points of the parameter for an analysis duration. For each point the functions will be computed according to the type of interpolation and of extension defined. The number of points must be a power of 2 (fast Fourier transform computation). Note: If the signals consist of a sufficient number (a power of two) of points with a constant step, it is preferable to choose this number in order to avoid interpolations which can generate artefacts. In particular, if the signals processed come from the operator GENE_FONC_ALEA, possibly via the computation of a dynamic response (operator DYNA_VIBRA for example), this number will correspond to twice the number of points supplied in GENE_FONC_ALEA, keyword NB_POIN, or obtained by INFO=2 in GENE_FONC_ALEA (cf. GENE_FONC_ALEA U4.36.05). 3.4 Operand FONCTION ♦ FONCTION= List of the names of the functions (time signals) of concept type fonction, whose interspectral matrix one wishes to compute. 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre is the title of the interspectre concept to be printed at the head of the results U4.03.01. 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= Specifies the printout options on the MESSAGE file. | 1 | prints the initial frequency, the final frequency and the frequency step. | | --- | --- | | 2 | like 1, plus, for each auto-spectrum and interspectrum, a convergence criterion as a function of the number of random draws. (one random draw corresponds to an analysis window). | 4 Verification stage One checks whether the number of points np is a power of 2. 5 Notes on use The operator creates a concept of type interspectre which constitutes the interspectral matrix. This matrix being Hermitian and positive definite, the functions are of real type for the diagonal terms and of complex type for the off-diagonal terms. Only the upper triangular part of the matrix is stored. These functions can be extracted by means of the operator RECU_FONCTION U4.32.03. 6 Example FONC1=RECU_FONCTION( RESU_GENE=DYNAMODE, NOM_CHAM='DEPL', NOEUD='N51', NOM_CMP='DY', INTERPOL='LIN' ) FONC2=RECU_FONCTION( RESU_GENE=DYNAMODE, NOM_CHAM='DEPL', NOEUD='N52', NOM_CMP='DY', INTERPOL='LIN' ) INTERS=CALC_INTE_SPEC( INST_INIT=0., INST_FIN=10.24, DUREE_ANALYSE=1.024, DUREE_DECALAGE=1.024, NB_POIN=1024, FONCTION=( FONCT1, FONCT2, ) ) REP1=RECU_FONCTION( INTE_SPEC=INTERS, NUME_ORDRE_I = 1, ) 7 Bibliography [bib1] Note DER HP-61/93-067 - Generation of random signals of given spectral density - G.JACQUART

u4.36.04 Operator GENE_ACCE_SEISME u4.36.04 Operator GENE_ACCE_SEISME 1 Purpose This operator makes it possible to generate artificial seismic accelerograms for transient dynamic analyses. It makes it possible to generate two types of signals: 1. Non-stationary seismic signals according to the evolutionary Kanai-Tajimi power spectral density (DSP) model, option DSP; 2. Seismic signals compatible with a target oscillator response spectrum (SRO), option SPEC_MEDIAN, SPEC_MOYENNE, SPEC_UNIQUE or SPEC_FRACTILE. In both cases, one must associate with them a modulation function which determines the time evolution of the seismic signals, by the factor keyword MODULATION. If one does not wish to apply a time modulation, one must choose a “constant” modulation over the time interval. One should consult the document R4.05.05 for a detailed description of the modellings and of the parameters to be supplied. It produces a concept of type table_fonction. 2 Syntax table_fonction = GENE_ACCE_SEISME( ◇ INIT_ALEA = int, ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◆ PAS_INST = float, ◇ NB_POIN = int, ◆ PESANTEUR = float, ◆ DUREE_PHASE_FORTE = float, ◇ NB_TIRAGE = int (défaut: 1), ◇ FREQ_CORNER = float, ◇ FREQ_FILTRE = float, ◇ FREQ_FILTRE_ZPA = float, ◇ FREQ_PENTE = float, / COEF_CORR = float, ◇ / MATR_COHE = _F( ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◆ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, ◆ TYPE = / "MITA_LUCO", / "ABRAHAMSON", / "ABRA_ROCHER", / "ABRA_SOLMOYEN", # Si: equal_to('TYPE', 'MITA_LUCO') ◆ VITE_ONDE = float, ◇ PARA_ALPHA = float (défaut: 0.1), ), / PHASE = _F( ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◆ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, ◆ DIRECTION = float, ◆ VITE_ONDE = float, ◇ COOR_REFE = float, ), # Si: exists('COEF_CORR') and exists('SPEC_FRACTILE') ◇ RATIO_HV = float, ◆ / DSP = _F( ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◆ FREQ_FOND = float, ), / SPEC_MEDIANE = _F( ◆ SPEC_OSCI = fonction, ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ / FREQ_PAS = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ NB_ITER = int, ◇ ERRE_ZPA = float (défaut: (1.0, 0.2)), ◇ ERRE_MAX = float (défaut: (0.5, 0.2)), ◇ ERRE_RMS = float (défaut: (0.5, 0.2)), ◇ METHODE = / "NIGAM", / "HARMO" (par défaut), ), / SPEC_MOYENNE = _F( ◆ SPEC_OSCI = fonction, ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ / FREQ_PAS = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ NB_ITER = int, ◇ ERRE_ZPA = float (défaut: (1.0, 0.2)), ◇ ERRE_MAX = float (défaut: (0.5, 0.2)), ◇ ERRE_RMS = float (défaut: (0.5, 0.2)), ◇ METHODE = / "NIGAM", / "HARMO" (par défaut), ), / SPEC_UNIQUE = _F( ◇ ERRE_ZPA = float (défaut: (1.0, 0.2)), ◇ ERRE_MAX = float (défaut: (0.5, 0.2)), ◇ ERRE_RMS = float (défaut: (0.5, 0.2)), ◆ SPEC_OSCI = fonction, ◇ CORR_ZPA = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ / FREQ_PAS = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ NB_ITER = int, ◇ METHODE = / "NIGAM", / "HARMO" (par défaut), ), / SPEC_FRACTILE = _F( ◆ SPEC_OSCI = fonction, ◆ SPEC_1_SIGMA = fonction, ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ / FREQ_PAS = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, ), # Si: exists('DSP') ◆ MODULATION = _F( ◆ TYPE = / "GAMMA", / "JENNINGS_HOUSNER", / "CONSTANT", ◇ / ACCE_MAX = float, / INTE_ARIAS = float, / ECART_TYPE = float, # Si: equal_to('TYPE', 'GAMMA') ◆ INST_INI = float, ), # Si: not exists('DSP') ◆ MODULATION = _F( ◆ TYPE = / "GAMMA", / "JENNINGS_HOUSNER", / "CONSTANT", # Si: equal_to('TYPE', 'GAMMA') ◆ INST_INI = float, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword DUREE_PHAS_FORT > ♦ DUREE_PHAS_FORT = TSM [R] Duration of the strong phase of the signal to be generated (R4.05.05). The parameters of the modulation functions GAMMA and of Jennings & Housner (JENNINGS_HOUSNER) are identified so that the mean strong phase of the signals corresponds to the one given. In the case of a constant modulation, the total duration of the signal corresponds to the strong-phase duration supplied. 3.2 Keyword NB_POIN > ◊ NB_POIN = nb_poin [I] Number of discretisation points of the interspectrum to be used in the generation algorithm. nb_poin must be an even number. If NB_POIN is supplied, then the duration of the simulation is determined by this value: T=\mathit{dt}(N-1) and the time-discretisation points are: {t}_{j}=j \mathit{dt},j=0,\mathrm{...},N-1 . If the keyword NB_POIN is not supplied, the simulation duration is taken equal to three times the duration of the strong phase plus {t}_{\mathit{ini}} : T=\mathrm{3 TSM}+{t}_{\mathit{ini}} . This makes it possible to simulate the accelerogram over its whole length if the variation of the signal is defined by a Gamma or Jennings & Housner modulation function. The number of points NB_POIN is then computed from this value. In the case of a constant modulation (TYPE=CONSTANT), one takes T=\mathit{TSM} and NB_POIN is not requested. 3.3 Keyword FREQ_FILTRE > ◊ FREQ_FILTRE = ff [R] Optional keyword used to supply a frequency (in \mathit{Hz} ) in order to filter the low frequencies of the seismic signals (accelerograms) in the time domain. It is therefore a high-pass filter. This filter makes it possible to remove a possible drift of the displacement signals obtained by integration of the accelerograms. By default, no time filtering is applied (ff=0.0). Note: One must take care not to choose ff too large (ff=0.05Hz constitutes a reasonable reference value). If ff is too large, then one does not only remove the drift but one also removes a large part of the low-frequency content of the signals. 3.4 Keyword FREQ_CORNER ◊ FREQ_CORNER = fc [R] This frequency is known in the seismological community by the term corner frequency . One can observe that the frequency content of natural seismic signals tends towards 0 very rapidly from a certain minimum frequency, namely for frequencies lower than the corner frequency . In the case of the generation of signals compatible with an SRO, one can use this command to optimise the adjustment of the low-frequency content of the signals. In the case of the generation of signals by the Kanai-Tajimi DSP, this filter must be applied in order to obtain a physical model in agreement with the seismological data, in particular the property that the spectral content must tend towards zero beyond the “ corner frequency ” (without a filter, the Kanai-Tajimi DSP is not zero at the origin). By default, one uses a filter with \mathit{fc}=0.05\times \text{FREQ\_FOND} for the Kanai-Tajimi DSP. 3.5 Keyword FREQ_FILTRE_ZPA ◊ FREQ_FILTRE_ZPA =fz [R] Optional keyword used to supply a frequency (in \mathit{Hz} ) in order to filter the high frequencies beyond the ZPA frequency. It is therefore a low-pass filter. This filter is applied to the DSP in the frequency domain. This filter makes it possible to remove residual frequency content beyond the ZPA value, which can produce erroneous asymptotic values if one computes the SRO for dampings lower than the value used to identify the DSP (SPEC_MOYENNE, SPEC_UNIQUE, SPEC_MEDIANE). By default, no low-pass filter is applied. Note One must take care not to choose fz too small; the cut-off frequency fz of the low-pass Butterworth filter is not the frequency at which filtering begins but the central point of the transition zone. Figure 1: illustration of the shape of the Butterworth filter for different cut-off frequencies 3.6 Keyword PAS_INST ♦ PAS_INST = dt [R] Time step of the seismic signals. This value is used to determine the cut-off frequency for the simulations by the formula F=1/(2\mathit{dt}) (Shannon). One must ensure that the cut-off frequency is large enough to model the phenomenon well. 3.7 Keyword FREQ_PENTE ◊ FREQ_PENTE = fp [R] Slope for the evolution of the central frequency [ \mathit{Hz}/s ]: f(t)={f}_{0}+{f}_{p}({t}_{0}-t) , where {t}_{0} is the reference time instant and {f}_{0} the central frequency at that time instant. In GENE_ACCE_SEISME, the reference time instant is chosen as the time instant in the middle of the strong phase: {t}_{0}=\mathrm{0.5 TSM}+{t}_{\mathit{ini}} . Constant values are taken before and after the strong phase (it is advised to consult R4.05.05 for more details). One observes that, generally, the fundamental frequency decreases with time. In that case one must give a negative slope: {f}_{p} ♦ MAILLAGE = mail [maillage_sdaster] Mesh of the modelling. 3.12.2 Operand GROUP_NO_INTERF ♦ GROUP_NO_INTERF = gni [grno] With this keyword, one defines the node group for which one wishes to generate a space-time seismic field. 3.12.3 Operand TYPE > ♦ TYPE = coherence model [txt] One can choose between the coherence function of Mita & Luco (MITA_LUCO) or those of Abrahamson (ABRAHAMSON, ABRA_ROCHER, ABRA_SOLMOYEN). If one chooses MITA_LUCO, then one must in addition supply VITE_ONDE. The parameter PARA_ALPHA is optional; by default one takes alpha = 0.1. 3.12.4 Operands VITE_ONDE and PARA_ALPHA ♦ VITE_ONDE = vite_onde, [R] ◊ PARA_ALPHA = / 0,1 [DEFAUT] / alpha, [R] A detailed description of these parameters is found in U4.53.31. 3.13 Factor keyword PHASE This factor keyword must be supplied if one wishes to generate a set of seismic signals taking into account the phase shift due to wave propagation. The arrival times of the signals are computed as a function of the coordinates of the nodes of the mesh, and with respect to a reference point. In the TABLE_FONCTION at the output of the operator, the signals are listed by their node name, for example NOEUD = N1. 3.13.1 Operand MAILLAGE > ♦ MAILLAGE = mail [maillage_sdaster] Mesh of the modelling. 3.13.2 Operand GROUP_NO_INTERF ♦ GROUP_NO_INTERF = gni [grno] With this keyword, one defines the node group for which one wishes to generate a space-time seismic field. 3.13.3 Operand VITE_ONDE ♦ VITE_ONDE = vite_onde, [R] The propagation speed of the wave. 3.13.4 Operand DIRECTION ♦ DIRECTION = dir, [R] The direction of propagation of the wave (direction vector: 3 values). 3.13.5 Operand COOR_REFE ◊ COOR_REFE = crefe [R] This keyword is optional. It makes it possible to supply the (3D) coordinates of a reference point for the computation of the phase shift (arrival time of the wave). By default, one identifies the node of the mesh which sees the wave first. 3.14 Keyword PESANTEUR ♦ PESANTEUR = g [R] In general, one takes PESANTEUR=9.81 ( m/{s}^{2} ). In this case, one must supply ACCE_MAX (PGA), and ECART_TYPE or, where applicable, the target spectrum (SPEC_OSCI) in g . This normalisation quantity is also used for the computation of the Arias intensity. As an example, giving ACCE_MAX= 0.2 corresponds to a PGA of \mathrm{0.2g} with g=\mathrm{9.81m}/{s}^{2} . The accelerograms generated will then be accelerations in m/{s}^{2} . 3.15 Factor keyword DSP The earthquake is modelled by a non-stationary stochastic process. Evolutionary power spectral densities (DSP) make it possible to take into account a phenomenon that is non-stationary in amplitude and in frequency content, such as the earthquake. The variation of the amplitude is taken into account by a modulation function, whereas the evolution of the frequency content is modelled by the evolutionary Kanai-Tajimi DSP. The Kanai-Tajimi DSP is furthermore filtered in order to remove the very low-frequency content, which can lead to numerical problems (non-zero drifts for the integrated signals). The parameters linked to the variation of the amplitude are the Arias intensity, the duration of the strong phase and the instant of the start of the strong phase. The parameters linked to the DSP and to the evolution of the frequency content are the damping and the fundamental frequency of the Kanai-Tajimi DSP as well as the slope describing the evolution of the latter in the course of time. These parameters can be determined from a given accelerogram, from an SRO (oscillator response spectrum) or by calling on the data available in the literature. Furthermore, the model being parameterised, it is possible to take into account the variability and the uncertainty of these parameters by means of random draws. The simulation algorithm and the model are described in more detail in the reference document R4.06.04. 3.15.1 Operands AMOR_REDUIT, FREQ_FOND ♦ AMOR_REDUIT = amo [R] Value of the critical damping ratio of the Kanai-Tajimi DSP. ♦ FREQ_FOND = f0 [R] Central frequency of the Kanai-Tajimi DSP; it is the frequency at which the most energy is concentrated. 3.16 Factor keywords SPEC_MEDIANE, SPEC_MOYENNE, SPEC_UNIQUE and SPEC_FRACTILE This factor keyword makes it possible to supply the data of a target SRO in order to generate seismic signals in agreement with the target SRO. One must then determine a DSP “compatible” with the data of the target SRO. There are several options: - SPEC_UNIQUE: Generation of a seismic signal whose SRO is very close to the target SRO: one must proceed by iterations in order to adjust the spectral content of the signal as well as possible. If several signals are requested (NB_TIRAGE), then the adjustment is done signal by signal. - SPEC_MOYENNE, SPEC_MEDIANE: Generation of \mathrm{Nbt} signals whose median/mean spectrum satisfies the target. If the target SRO is a physical spectrum, then the set of signals generated generally has a median SRO close to the target. One can however carry out iterations in order to improve the adjustment of the SRO, either in the median (SPEC_MEDIANE) or in the mean (SPEC_MOYENNE). If one does not carry out iterations (NB_ITER not supplied) in order to improve the adjustment, then the two options produce the same result. - SPEC_FRACTILE: Generation of \mathit{Nbt} signals whose median spectrum and one-sigma spectrum satisfy the target. This is a method for “ best-estimate ” studies. The signals generated have a variability close to that of the real signals available in the databases, in particular as regards the variability between realisations ( record-to-record variability ). For this, one must supply the median spectrum as well as the one-sigma spectrum. The median spectrum as well as the one-sigma spectrum are generally provided by the attenuation laws. 3.16.1 Operand SPEC_OSCI > ♦ SPEC_OSCI = spec_cible One supplies here the target SRO in the form of a function with the frequencies on the abscissa and the spectral accelerations on the ordinate (the latter must be normalised according to PESANTEUR). One can use DEFI_FONCTION to build it. If one has chosen the option SPECTRE_FRACTILE, then this spectrum must correspond to the median spectrum (as defined by the attenuation laws). 3.16.2 Operand SPEC_1_SIGMA > ♦ SPEC_1_SIGMA = spec_cible_1s Mandatory keyword for the option SPEC_FRACTILE. One supplies here the target one-sigma SRO in the form of a function with the frequencies on the abscissa and the spectral accelerations on the ordinate (the latter must be normalised according to PESANTEUR). One can use DEFI_FONCTION to build it. The one-sigma spectrum is, for example, provided by the attenuation laws, which assume a log-normal distribution of the spectral accelerations and therefore of the SRO values. This implies that the one-sigma SRO corresponds to the 84% fractile of the SRO. It is advised to consult the reference document R4.05.05 for more details on this modelling. 3.16.3 Operand AMOR_REDUIT > ♦ AMOR_REDUIT = amo [R] Value of the reduced damping of the SRO supplied under SPEC_OSCI. 3.16.4 Operand CORR_ZPA ◊ CORR_ZPA = /'NON' [DEFAUT] /'OUI' [TXM] This keyword is optional and can be used only with the option SPEC_UNIQUE. If CORR_ZPA = 'OUI' then the time signals will be modified by a correction function so that they have the right PGA value, namely the ZPA value which corresponds to the asymptote of the target spectrum for the high frequencies. 3.16.5 Operands ERRE_ZPA, ERRE_RMS and ERRE_MAX ◊ ERRE_MAX = (cmax,emax) [R] ◊ ERRE_ZPA = (czpa,ezpa) [R] ◊ ERRE_RMS = (crms,erms) [R] These keywords are optional; one can supply the weighting coefficients as well as the maximum error desired by the user for the three adjustment criteria: maximum error over the frequency band, error on the ZPA (zero period acceleration) and RMS error. It is possible to supply a weighting coefficient (cmax, czpa, crms) and a target maximum error (emax, ezpa, erms). The three weightings must be supplied together. The error computed is the relative error, namely the difference between the value of the spectrum obtained and the value of the target spectrum divided by the value of the target spectrum: \text{erri}_i = \frac{\text{vale}_i - \text{target}_i}{\text{target}_i} , \quad i=1,2,3 where: - \mathrm{vale}_i is the value of the spectrum obtained for criterion i - \mathrm{target}_i is the value of the target spectrum for criterion i - i=1 corresponds to ERRE_MAX, i=2 to ERRE_ZPA, and i=3 to ERRE_RMS The weighting coefficients are used to determine a weighted multi-objective error for each iteration: \text{error} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{3} \left( c_1^2 , \text{err}_1^2 + c_2^2 , \text{err}_2^2 + c_3^2 , \text{err}_3^2 \right)} where: - c_i is the weighting coefficient associated with criterion i - \mathrm{err}_i is the relative error computed for criterion i (expressed as a percentage) - i=1,2,3 represent respectively ERRE_MAX, ERRE_ZPA, and ERRE_RMS This criterion is used to choose, among the results of the iterations, the accelerogram (or the accelerograms) at the output of the analysis which best satisfy the criterion (it is not always the last iteration). If one of the errors computed is greater than the value supplied (emax, ezpa, erms), an alarm is emitted. 3.16.6 Operand NB_ITER > ◊ NB_ITER = nbiter [I] One supplies the number of iterations in order to improve the adjustment of the accelerogram to the target spectrum (SRO). This keyword is optional: by default, no iterations are carried out. With the option SPEC_FRACTILE, one cannot iterate. 3.16.7 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE = /'HARMO' [DEFAUT] /'NIGAM' [TXM] This optional keyword makes it possible to choose the method for the computation of the response spectra. These are the same methods as those available for the computation of an SRO with CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04. By default, one uses the method HARMO. The response spectrum is then obtained by successive harmonic analyses (for different oscillator eigenfrequencies) by way of an FFT/IFFT of the input signal. The method NIGAM is detailed in the document R5.05.01. 3.16.8 Operand FREQ_PAS > ◊ FREQ_PAS = fpas [R] With this optional keyword, one can choose the discretisation step of the SRO used to determine the compatible DSP. The SRO values supplied via SPEC_OSCI are then interpolated in order to obtain the desired discretisation step fpas. By default, one takes the same frequency step as the one used for the generation of the signals. The latter is deduced from the cut-off frequency and from the number of points NB_POIN. 3.17 Factor keyword MODULATION The parameters of the modulation functions GAMMA and of Jennings & Housner (JENNINGS_HOUSNER) are identified so that the mean strong phase TSM of the signals corresponds to the one given. For a CONSTANT modulation (no modulation), the duration of the simulated signals corresponds to TSM. One uses the definition based on the Arias intensity. One writes \mathit{TSM}={T}_{2}-{T}_{1} where {T}_{1} and {T}_{2} are respectively the time instants at which 5% and 95% of the Arias intensity (the total energy) are reached. The time instant {T}_{1} corresponds to the start of the strong phase {t}_{\mathit{ini}} . If NB_POIN is given for the Gamma and Jennings & Housner modulations, then the total duration of the signals corresponds to (NB_POIN-1) PAS_INST. 3.17.1 Operand TYPE ♦ TYPE = / 'JENNINGS_HOUSNER' [TXM] / 'GAMMA' / 'CONSTANT' Definition of the type of modulation (cf. also R4.05.05). The modulation of type CONSTANT corresponds to a signal without modulation of the amplitude. If one furthermore assumes that the fundamental frequency of the DSP is constant, then one comes back to a stationary process. 3.17.2 Operands INT_ARIAS, ACCE_MAX, ECART_TYPE If one has chosen the option DSP, then one must supply one of the three parameters Arias intensity, PGA (peak ground acceleration) or standard deviation in order to define the energy contained in the signals. If one has chosen one of the three factor keywords SPEC_UNIQUE, SPEC_MEDIANE or SPEC_FRACTILE, then this information is already contained in the target spectrum. > ◊ INT_ARIAS = arias [R] Mean Arias intensity: \mathit{Arias}=E(\frac{\pi}{2g}{\int}_{0}^{\infty}{X}^{2}(t)\mathit{dt}) with X the process modelling the seismic motion (acce) and g the gravity. > ◊ ACCE_MAX = pga [R] Peak ground acceleration (PGA). One associates this value with the median maximum of the signals to be generated. The corresponding standard deviation is determined from the peak factor and for the strong phase TSM. One must supply ACCE_MAX (PGA) in g . The value of g is to be supplied by the keyword PESANTEUR. Thus, ACCE_MAX= 0.2 corresponds to a PGA of \mathrm{0.2 g} with g=\mathrm{9.81m}/{s}^{2} . The accelerograms generated will then be accelerations in m/{s}^{2} . > ◊ ECART_TYPE = ect [R] Standard deviation of the underlying stationary stochastic process. One then applies the modulation of the amplitude (GAMMA or JENNINGS_HOUSNER). One must supply ECART_TYPE in g (see also above). The value of g is to be supplied by the keyword PESANTEUR. One must take PESANTEUR=9.81 ( m/{s}^{2} ) in order to obtain accelerations in m/{s}^{2} . 3.17.3 Operand INST_INIT > ♦/◊ INST_INIT = t_ini [R] Instant of the start of the strong phase in the case of the GAMMA modulation function. The parameters of the GAMMA modulation function are identified (by least squares) so that \mathit{TSM} and {t}_{\mathit{ini}} are satisfied. 3.18 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 : pas d'impression / 2 : impression des informations relatives au modèle et la discrétisation (traitement du signal). 3.19 Operand TITRE > ◊ TITRE = titre titre is the title of the analysis to be printed at the head of the results U4.03.01. 4 Table produced > The parameters of the table produced are as follows: | PARAMETER | TYPE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | --- | | NUME_ORDRE | I | order numbers (NB_TIRAGE) | | FONCTION | K24 | name of the generated functions | | NOM_PARA | K24 | ACCE1 and ACCE2 (if COEF_CORR) ACCE1, ACCE2 and ACCE3 (if RATIO_HV) | | NOEUD | K24 | Name of the node (if MATR_COHE) | 5 Examples On peut consulter le cas test zzzz317 [:external:ref: V1.01.317 ].

u4.36.05 Operator GENE_FONC_ALEA u4.36.05 Operator GENE_FONC_ALEA 1 Purpose To generate a trajectory of a multivariate one-dimensional stochastic process (i.e. with several components and indexed on a single variable), stationary, with zero mean, from its spectral density matrix (interspectral matrix). The trajectories of the stochastic process are time functions which then make it possible to carry out a transient dynamic analysis. The trajectories obtained have an interspectral matrix which converges on average towards the target interspectral matrix and are the realisations of an asymptotically Gaussian process (i.e. when the number of draws tends to infinity). The algorithm used is a simulation algorithm by trigonometric series with random phase and an inverse fast Fourier transform. The time functions produced are stored in an interspectre data structure. Each function is identified by its order number. It can be extracted by using the operator RECU_FONCTION [U4.32.03]. 2 Syntax interspectre = GENE_FONC_ALEA( ◆ INTE_SPEC = interspectre, ◇ NUME_VITE_FLUI = int, ◇ INTERPOL = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("INTERPOL", 'OUI') ◇ DUREE_TIRAGE = float, ◇ FREQ_INIT = float, ◇ FREQ_FIN = float, ◇ NB_POIN = int, ◇ NB_TIRAGE = int (défaut: 1), ◇ INIT_ALEA = int, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand INTE_SPEC ♦ INTE_SPEC = intf [interspectre] Name of the interspectral matrix towards which the interspectral matrix of the generated signals must tend. The interspectral matrix is a complex matrix, each term of which is written {S}_{\mathit{XY}}(f)={\int}_{-\infty }^{+\infty }E[X(t)Y(t-\tau )]{e}^{-\mathrm{2i}\pi f\tau }d\tau where E[\text{}\cdot \text{}] is the mathematical expectation, and where X and Y are two stationary random processes (for example two components of a loading at two distinct points of a mesh). Note: To be physical, the interspectral matrix must be a positive-definite Hermitian matrix. This interspectral matrix is generated mainly by the operators: > DEFI_INTE_SPEC, LIRE_INTE_SPEC and CALC_INTE_SPEC. For further information on the meaning of the parameters, the reader is invited to consult the documentation of the command DEFI_INTE_SPEC U4.36.02. 3.2 Operand NUME_VITE_FLUI ◊ NUME_VITE_FLUI= nk [I] This order number corresponds to a flow velocity if the interspectra model, via the operators CALC_FLUI_STRU and DEFI_SPEC_TURB, a turbulent excitation induced by a fluid flow. 3.3 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL = / 'OUI' [DEFAUT] One allows interpolation of the frequency functions constituting the terms of the interspectral matrix. In particular, the new discretisation will depend on the duration of the signal to be generated (keyword DUREE_TIRAGE) and on the number of points of the FFT (keyword NB_POIN). / 'NON' The values of the interspectrum used are only the existing values (no interpolation used). Caution: If INTERPOL='NON', it is necessary that: - the different terms of the interspectral matrix have exactly the same discretisation and a constant frequency step. If the number of discretisation points of the interspectrum is not a power of 2, and/or is not compatible with the interspectrum, one or more alarms are emitted and an ad hoc power of 2 is chosen, - the interspectra are discretised finely enough to allow generation of time histories with enough time instants. 3.4 Operand DUREE_TIRAGE ◊ DUREE_TIRAGE = durée [R] Duration of the signal to be generated, for each draw (the total duration will therefore be nt \text{}\times \text{} durée). If the keyword DUREE_TIRAGE is not present, the duration of the signal to be generated is computed by \text{durée}=\frac{1}{\Delta f} where \Delta f is the frequency step of the interspectrum (original minimum step of the interspectrum, or step computed from the keywords FREQ_INIT, FREQ_FIN and NB_POIN). Note: The generated signals start at time instant 0. with a zero value. Note: To obtain the desired duration, the generation algorithm adjusts the number of points used in the FFT (cf. [§3.6] Operand NB_POIN) and, if needed, extends the interspectrum beyond the min and max frequencies with null values. 3.5 Operands FREQ_INIT / FREQ_FIN ◊ FREQ_INIT = fi [R] ◊ FREQ_FIN = ff [R] First and last frequency values for which the interspectrum will be taken into account. The presence of these keywords has the effect of truncating the interspectrum. If the keywords are not present, it is the minimum and maximum frequency values of the interspectrum which are used. 3.6 Operand NB_POIN ◊ NB_POIN = nb_poin [I] Number of discretisation points of the interspectrum to be used in the generation algorithm. This number must be a power of 2 because it corresponds to the number of points of the inverse fast Fourier transform used by the generation algorithm. If this is not the case, it is the power of 2 immediately greater than nb_poin which is retained. If the keyword NB_POIN is not present, the number of points is computed so that Shannon's theorem is satisfied, that is \frac{1}{\Delta t}>2\cdot {f}_{\max} , where \Delta t is the time step of the signal to be generated (which depends on NB_POIN and on DUREE_TIRAGE) and where {f}_{\max} is the maximum frequency retained from the interspectrum. Suggestion: It is advised not to specify the number of points; the coded algorithm in that case automatically chooses the optimal value. In particular, if the keywords DUREE_TIRAGE and NB_POIN are not present, then one is assured that the generated signal is consistent both with the discretisation step of the interspectrum and with the maximum frequency. However, if the user wants to specify NB_POIN, the two notes which follow should help. Note: If the keywords DUREE_TIRAGE and NB_POIN are present then one has: \Delta t=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{\text{durée}}{\text{nb\_poin}} In this case, if nb_poin is too small with respect to durée for Shannon's theorem to be satisfied, then an alarm is emitted and it is the minimum number of points allowing Shannon's theorem to be satisfied which is retained. The value specified by NB_POIN is therefore taken into account only when it is greater than the minimum value. By imposing a high number of points, one can force the signal to have a time-discretisation step smaller than the default one. One must then be aware that the discretisation of the time history is finer than is theoretically allowed by the maximum frequency of the interspectrum. Note: If INTERPOL='NON' and if nb_poin is not compatible with the interspectrum, an alarm is emitted and an ad hoc power of 2 is chosen. Note: The number of points making up the generated signals is equal to twice the number of discretisation points of the interspectrum, and therefore to twice nb_poin when the keyword is supplied. This number of points is useful to know for later use in CALC_INTE_SPEC U4.36.03 (cf. [§ 3.9] "Operand INFO" and [§ 6] "Examples"). 3.7 Operand NB_TIRAGE ◊ NB_TIRAGE = nt [I] Number of draws which the generated time signals must contain. The resulting signals will contain nt statistically independent draws placed end to end. One can then post-process the results obtained from these generated signals with the operator CALC_INTE_SPEC U4.36.03, cf. [§ 6] "Examples". Caution: If the keyword DUREE_TIRAGE is present, the total duration of the signal will be nt \text{}\times \text{} durée. However, it is of course not equivalent to generate 1 draw of duration nt \text{}\times \text{} durée_tirage and nt draws of duration durée_tirage placed end to end. There is statistical independence between the different segments of duration d in the second case and not in the first. 3.8 Operand INIT_ALEA ◊ INIT_ALEA = ni [I] Causes initialisation at its ni-th term of the sequence of pseudo-random numbers used for the generation of the signals. If the keyword INIT_ALEA is absent, the terms of the sequence used are those immediately following those already used. If no term has yet been used, the sequence is initialised at its first term. Suggestion: Unless there is a particular use, it is advised not to supply the keyword INIT_ALEA in the following operators: GENE_FONC_ALEA, GENE_VARI_ALEA and GENE_MATR_ALEA. In this case, at the first call to one of these operators, the sequence of pseudo-random numbers is initialised at its first term. Omitting the keyword INIT_ALEA at each call of these operators in the command file guarantees the statistical independence of the pseudo-random numbers used. Note: The seed of the sequence remains identical from one execution of Code_Aster to another; the results therefore remain strictly identical (one can thus test the non-regression of statistical results which have not converged). If one wishes to generate results which are statistically independent from one execution to another, then one must use the keyword INIT_ALEA with values greater than the number of terms used in the previous executions. Caution: The random-variable generator used is that of the Python module "random". It depends on the version of Python used by Code_Aster. Results which have not converged statistically may therefore vary from one version of Code_Aster to another or from one platform to another, if the version of Python is not the same and if between the two versions the module random has changed (the case between Python 2.1 and 2.3). Note: In Python version 2.3, the period of the generator is 2 19937-1. 3.9 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 : pas d'impression. / 2 : impression du pas de temps, du temps initial, du temps final des signaux générés, et du nombre de points utilisés dans la transformée de Fourier rapide inverse. Note: INFO=2 makes it possible to know the number of points making up the generated signals (it is twice the number of points used in the inverse fast Fourier transform). It is better to use this number of points afterwards in the operator CALC_INTE_SPEC, keyword NB_POIN (cf. [§ 6] "Examples"). 3.10 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre titre is the title of the analysis to be printed at the head of the results U4.03.01. 4 Verification stage Various checks are carried out to ensure that the data are consistent (nb_poin large enough with respect to the maximum frequency and the duration to be generated, duration large enough with respect to the discretisation of the interspectrum, and so on). Alarms are emitted where applicable. If the keyword NB_POIN is present, then one checks that the value given is a power of 2. Otherwise, an alarm is emitted and the value is modified. If INTERPOL='NON', one checks that the different terms of the interspectral matrix have the same discretisation with a constant frequency step. 5 Concept produced The time functions produced are stored in an interspectre data structure. Each function is identified by its order number. It can be extracted by using the operator RECU_FONCTION U4.32.03. 6 Examples # Cet exemple n'a pour but que de donner une idée de la syntaxe et # des opérateurs associés utiles (pour la récupération des fonctions # générées et leur éventuelle vérification). # L'interspectre utilisée n'a pas de signification. Il n'y a pas # d'utilisation des fonctions générées (avec un dyna_tran_modal par # exemple). # Les cas test zzzz180a et sdll107a fournissent des exemples plus complets # Définition de l'interspectre spect11 = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA = 'FREQ', VALE_C = ( 0. , 10. , 0., 50.0 , 10. , 0., 150. , 0.1 , 0., ) ) spect12 = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA = 'FREQ', VALE_C = ( 0. , 0.5 , 0.8, 150. , 0.5 , 0.8, ) ) spect22 = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA = 'FREQ' VALE_C = ( 0. , 1. , 0., 150. , 1.. , 0., ) ) mat_int = DEFI_INTE_SPEC( DIMENSION = 2, PAR_FONCTION = ( _F( NUME_ORDRE_I = 1, NUME_ORDRE_J = 1, FONCTION = sp11), _F( NUME_ORDRE_I = 1, NUME_ORDRE_J = 2, FONCTION = sp12), _F( NUME_ORDRE_I = 2, NUME_ORDRE_J = 2, FONCTION = sp22) ) ) # Génération des deux fonctions temporelles via la structure de données # interspectre vect = GENE_FONC_ALEA(INTE_SPEC = mat_int, DUREE_TIRAGE = 5., NB_TIRAGE = 10, ) # Récupération des deux fonctions par exemple pour un IMPR_FONCTION FONC1 = RECU_FONCTION( INTE_SPEC = vect, NUME_ORDRE = 1) FONC2 = RECU_FONCTION( INTE_SPEC = VECT1, NUME_ORDRE = 2) # Vérification : Calcul de l'interspectre des fonctions générées # Attention : la valeur donnée à NB_POIN est importante. Il est # souhaitable de la prendre égale au nombre de points constituant # les fonctions (2 nb_fft si provenant de GENE_FONC_ALEA). INTERS=CALC_INTE_SPEC( INST_INIT=0., INST_FIN=50., DUREE_ANALYSE=5., DUREE_DECALAGE=5., NB_POIN=2048, FONCTION=( FONC1, FONC2, )) # Récupération de l'auto-spectre de FONC1 pour comparaison à spetc11 F11 =RECU_FONCTION(INTE_SPEC=INTERS, NUME_ORDRE_I=1, )

u4.36.08 Macro-command IMPR_ACCE_SEISME u4.36.08 Macro-command IMPR_ACCE_SEISME 1 Purpose This macro-command aims to automate the post-processing of the data coming from the command GENE_ACCE_SEISME. It carries out the following tasks: - printing of one figure per accelerogram, that is, per direction and per draw; - printing of one figure of all the accelerograms for each direction; - computation of the velocities and then of the displacements of the signals; - printing of one figure of all the displacements for each direction; - printing of one figure containing the severity indicators for each direction; - printing of a statistics table on the severity indicators; - computation of the spectra of the signals and computation of the mean spectrum per direction; - printing of one figure with the target spectrum and the mean spectrum per direction; - printing of one figure containing all the spectra as well as the target spectrum and the mean spectrum per direction; - computation of the plus and minus \sigma spectra; - printing of one figure with the plus and minus \sigma spectra as well as the target \sigma spectrum for each direction; - correction of the mean spectrum (by a multiplicative factor) so that it is not lower than the target spectrum over a given frequency band for each direction; - computation and printing, on a figure, of the geometric mean of the mean spectra in the vertical directions if the dimension of the problem is greater than or equal to 2. The figures and tables are created in the REPE_OUT directory of the temporary execution directory U4.12.03. 2 Syntax IMPR_ACCE_SEISME( ◆ TABLE = table, ◆ TITRE = text, ◇ NOCI_REFE = _F( ◆ | AMAX = float, | VMAX = float, | DMAX = float, | INTE_ARIAS = float, | DUREE_PHASE_FORTE = float, | VITE_ABSO_CUMU = float, | ACCE_SUR_VITE = float, ), ◇ DUREE = float, ◆ SPEC_OSCI = fonction, ◇ SPEC_1_SIGMA = fonction, ◇ LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ & FREQ_MIN = float, & FREQ_MAX = float, ◇ RATIO_HV = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands This command uses XMGRACE, but this utility is not available in salome_meca; it must therefore be added on the execution machine. 3.1 Keyword TABLE This mandatory keyword makes it possible to provide the table coming from the operator GENE_ACCE_SEISME to be post-processed. 3.2 Keyword TITRE This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define a title used in the various figures created. 3.3 Factor keyword NOCI_REFE This factor keyword makes it possible to give reference values for the severity indicators. For each operand (AMAX, VMAX, DMAX, INTE_ARIAS, DUREE_PHASE_FORTE, VITE_ASBO_CUMU, ACCE_SUR_VITE), three values are to be supplied; they correspond to the mean and to the lower and upper bounds of the confidence interval. 3.4 Keyword DUREE This optional keyword makes it possible to display the accelerograms over a duration shorter than the one computed. The value supplied must therefore be smaller than the total duration of the accelerograms. 3.5 Keyword SPEC_OSCI This mandatory keyword makes it possible to provide the target spectrum. It appears on certain figures in order to be compared with the computed spectra. For more details, see U4.36.04. 3.6 Keyword SPEC_1_SIGMA This optional keyword makes it possible to provide the target \sigma spectrum. If it is supplied, the plus and minus one \sigma spectra are computed and printed with this target spectrum on a figure. For more details, see U4.36.04. 3.7 Keyword LIST_FREQ This optional keyword makes it possible to give the list of frequencies to be taken into account for the computation of the spectra. 3.8 Keywords FREQ_MIN and FREQ_MAX These two optional keywords are to be supplied together. If they are present, one computes the multiplication factor required so that the mean spectrum of the accelerograms is not lower than the target spectrum, in the frequency range going from FREQ_MIN to FREQ_MAX. 3.9 Keyword RATIO_HV In the case of a table containing data in the vertical direction (and therefore with three components), this keyword makes it possible to weight the various target spectra so that they are consistent with the data supplied.

u4.36.09 Operator DEFI_PROP_ALEA u4.36.09 Operator DEFI_PROP_ALEA 1 Purpose This operator makes it possible to define random fields in order to take into account the spatial variability of mechanical properties such as Young's modulus (for example of the soil or of the concrete). The operator builds analytical expressions of the random fields by a Karhunen-Loeve decomposition. The fields follow a log-normal law and are defined by the correlation lengths in the 1, 2 or 3 directions of space, the median and the coefficient of variation. In addition, one must supply the size of the domain ( bounding volume ) and the number of terms to be retained. One can generate 1D fields (processes), 2D fields or 3D fields. DEFI_PROP_ALEA produces a formula whose parameters are X and/or Y and/or Z depending on the data, which can be passed as material parameters to DEFI_MATERIAU. It produces a concept of type formule. 2 Syntax formule = DEFI_PROP_ALEA( ◆ INIT_ALEA = int, ◆ MEDIANE = float, ◆ COEF_VARI = float, ◆ | LONG_CORR_X = float, | LONG_CORR_Y = float, | LONG_CORR_Z = float, ◇ / PRECISION = float, / NB_TERM = int, # Si: exists('LONG_CORR_X') ◆ X_MINI = float, ◆ X_MAXI = float, ◆ NB_TERM_X = int, # Si: exists('LONG_CORR_Y') ◆ Y_MINI = float, ◆ Y_MAXI = float, ◆ NB_TERM_Y = int, # Si: exists('LONG_CORR_Z') ◆ Z_MINI = float, ◆ Z_MAXI = float, ◆ NB_TERM_Z = int, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword INIT_ALEA ♦ INIT_ALEA = ni [I] The keyword INIT_ALEA initialises the seed of the random sequences used to define the random fields. Two consecutive analyses with the same initialisation then produce the same result. 3.2 Keyword MEDIANE Keyword used to define the median value of the log-normal random field. In general, the median value is associated with the best-estimate value. 3.3 Keyword COEF_VARI ♦ COEF_VARI = cov [R] Keyword used to define the coefficient of variation of the random fields. The coefficient of variation is defined as the ratio between the standard deviation and the mean of the random field. In the case of fields with log-normal laws, the logarithmic standard deviation \beta is linked to the coefficient of variation by the formula \mathit{cov}=\sqrt{({\exp}^{({\beta}^{2})}-1)} . 3.4 Keywords LONG_CORR_X, LONG_CORR_Y and LONG_CORR_Z ♦| LONG_CORR_X = LcX [R] | LONG_CORR_Y = LcY [R] | LONG_CORR_Z = LcZ [R] Keyword used to define the correlation length of the random fields along the direction X (if supplied). The definition of the correlation lengths is that of Vanmarcke: {L}_{c}={\int}_{-\infty }^{+\infty }R(u)\mathit{du} where R(u) is the correlation function for the variable u (here: the distance along the direction X ). The correlation function is a simple exponential R(u)={\exp}^{(-u/(0.5{L}_{c}))} along each direction. LONG_CORR_Y and LONG_CORR_Z are analogous to those of LONG_CORR_X for the directions Y and Z . 3.5 Keywords NB_TERM_X, X_MINI and X_MAXI > These keywords are mandatory if LONG_CORR_X is supplied. ♦ NB_TERM_X = Nx [I] The number of terms to be retained for the Karhunen-Loève decomposition along the direction X . The number of terms defines the number of eigenfunctions and therefore the small fluctuations of the variable parameter. As the random field is generated on unit domains [0,1] , the number of terms must be chosen relative to the size of the domain and the discretisation. Failing that, it is recommended to take Nbt equal to the extent of the domain divided by the mesh-cell size (here (xmax-xmin)/dx). ♦ X_MINI = xmin [I] The minimum coordinate according to the extent of the domain in the direction X . ♦ X_MAXI = xmax [I] The maximum coordinate according to the extent of the domain in the direction X . The last two keywords make it possible to define the extent of the domain over which the random fields must be generated ( bounding volume ). 3.6 Keywords NB_TERM_Y, Y_MINI and Y_MAXI > These keywords are mandatory if LONG_CORR_Y is supplied. 3.7 Keywords NB_TERM_Z, Z_MINI and Z_MAXI > These keywords are mandatory if LONG_CORR_Z is supplied. 3.8 Keywords NB_TERM or PRECISION to reduce the model These optional keywords can be used to reduce the model in the case of 2D or 3D fields. The mandatory keywords NB_TERM_X, NB_TERM_Y and NB_TERM_Z make it possible to define the number of terms for the Karhunen-Loève (KL) representation to be computed for each component (X and/or Y and/or Z). In the case of a 2D random field, there are two components, and for 3D there are 3 components. The total energy for this KL representation is computed as the sum of all the combinations of products of eigenvalues. For example, in the case of a 2D field along the directions X and Y with Nx and Ny eigenfunctions respectively, the KL representation comprises Nxy=Nx Ny terms. In order to retain a reduced number of terms, while preserving a good representation of the fields, the cross terms are ranked according to their contribution to the total energy of the decomposition. One can then reduce the model by retaining the Nbt most energetic terms. For the example above, it is necessary that Nbt ].

equal_to("METHODE",'SOUS_DOMAINE' ) ◇ NB_SOUS_DOMAINE = int, ◇ PARTITIONNEUR = / "METIS" (par défaut), / "SCOTCH", ), ◇ VERI_JACOBIEN = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ VERI_NORM_IFS = / "NON", / parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Choice of the mesh The keyword MAILLAGE gives the mesh associated with the study, on which one assigns the finite elements. Note For the axisymmetric modellings, the axis of revolution is the axis Y of the mesh. The whole structure must be meshed in X\ge 0 . The axis {Ox} therefore designates the radial direction. The components of the computed fields will therefore be: X for the radial direction, Y for the axial direction and Z for the orthoradial (circumferential) direction. 3.2 Assignment of the finite elements The keyword AFFE defines the types of finite elements which will be assigned on the chosen mesh entities. For each occurrence, one specifies a modelling. - the assignments are made by superposing the effects of the different keywords - in the event of a conflict, the last keyword specified prevails over the previous ones. Note One recalls that the overloading rule is applied (see U1.03.00): The mesh entities are specified by the keyword TOUT = 'OUI' , which assigns all the mesh cells of the mesh, and GROUP_MA = g_mail , which assigns a list of mesh-cell groups. The type of finite element is specified by the following keywords: - PHENOMENE : physical phenomenon modelled (associated conservation equation) - MODELISATION : type of interpolation and of discretisation - FORMULATION : type of formulation in certain cases The first two keywords PHENOMENE and MODELISATION are mandatory for each occurrence of the factor keyword AFFE . This pair of keywords defines in a one-to-one way the type of element assigned to a type of mesh cell. In certain cases, it may be necessary to specify the FORMULATION used: - For the discretisation of HHO type ( 3D_HHO , AXIS_HHO or D_PLAN_HHO ), one can specify whether it is a constant ( CONSTANTE ), linear ( LINEAIRE ), quadratic ( QUADRATIQUE ), cubic ( CUBIQUE ) or quartic ( QUARTIQUE ) approach; see the documentation R3.06.14. There may exist limitations depending on the physics. For example, the constant approach is available only in thermal analysis; - For the discretisations in fluid or in fluid–structure interaction, one can specify whether it is a formulation with three variables (U,P,\varphi ) , with two variables (U,P) or (U,\psi ) ; see the documentation R4.02.02. - For the second-gradient modellings in mechanics, one can specify whether it is the historical formulation of the second-gradient model that must be used ( DIL ) or the incompressible formulation ( DIL_INCO ). - For the stabilised mixed modellings, one can specify whether it is the standard formulation of the model that must be used ( STA ) or the incompressible formulation ( STA_INCO ). - the keyword PHENOMENE must have the same value for all the occurrences of the factor keyword AFFE . - by assigning the finite elements on the volume mesh cells (and/or surface mesh cells) of the mesh-cell group g_mail , if this mesh-cell group also contains the boundary mesh cells (and/or edge mesh cells) of the volume mesh cells (and/or surface mesh cells), then one also automatically assigns on the latter the finite elements necessary for certain analysis options (assignment of external loadings, for example). If one needs to assign additional modellings on these interfaces, one must then provide duplicated mesh cells in the mesh: this is for example the case in fluid–structure interaction. SUPER_MAILLE is the list of the super-mesh cells that one wants to assign in the model. As for the finite elements, it is not mandatory to assign all the mesh cells of the mesh. It is AFFE_MODELE which confirms which substructures will be used in the model. The difference with the classical finite elements is that, on the super-mesh cells, one chooses neither the MODELISATION nor the PHENOMENE , because the macro-element (built by the operator MACR_ELEM_STAT) which will be assigned on the super-mesh cell has its own modelling and its own phenomenon (those which served to compute it). If TOUT = 'OUI' , all the (super) mesh cells are assigned. 3.5 Checks The keyword VERI_JACOBIEN serves to check that the mesh cells of the model are not too distorted. One computes the Jacobian of the geometric transformation which transforms the reference element into each real mesh cell of the model. If, at the different integration points of a mesh cell, the Jacobian changes sign, this means that this mesh cell is very “badly shaped”. An alarm is then emitted. The keyword VERI_NORM_IFS serves to check that all the normals on the fluid–structure interfaces (modelling of type FLUI_STRU ) are indeed oriented in the same direction. If this is not the case, an alarm is emitted and the user is invited to reorient these normals either directly in the mesh, or via the command MODI_MAILLAGE. The keyword VERI_PLAN serves to check that the mesh cells of type QUAD4 used in the plate formulations ( DKT , DST , etc.) are indeed plane. One builds a plane on the first three nodes of the element, then one computes the distance of the fourth point with respect to this plane. If the distance is greater than 1,0 \times 10^{-4} , then the alarm is emitted with the list of the mesh cells concerned. The keyword VERI_FORMULATION_IFS serves to check that one uses the same FORMULATION for the fluid mesh cells and FLUI_STRU . Nevertheless, one can lift this check in certain situations. Typically, if the mesh cells assigned by the fluid (or the interface) are not connected to one another (by their nodes), one can assign different formulations. 3.6 Factor keyword GRANDEUR_CARA The factor keyword GRANDEUR_CARA serves to define a few physical quantities characteristic of the problem treated. These quantities are currently used to “non-dimensionalise” certain terms of the error estimators in HM. See R4.10.05. 3.7 Distribution of the mesh cells 3.7.1 Principles The factor keyword DISTRIBUTION makes it possible to distribute the finite elements of the model for the parallelism of the elementary analyses, of the assemblies and of certain linear solvers; see User's guide to parallelism. It defines how the mesh cells/elements will be distributed (or not) for the parallelised phases. The user therefore has the possibility of driving this distribution among the processors. The parallelism operates: - on the elementary analyses and on the assemblies of matrices and vectors (this is what the factor keyword DISTRIBUTION makes it possible to control), - at the solution of the linear system if the solver is parallelised (Keyword SOLVEUR). Note In the case of the parallelism mode (parallel mesh of type maillage_p ), the distribution mode is necessarily CENTRALISE , because the mesh has already been distributed and it is not possible to redistribute the analyses again. If another distribution mode is chosen for this parallelism mode, it will automatically be switched to mode CENTRALISE without warning the user. It is possible to modify the distribution mode in the course of one's study. It is sufficient to use the command MODI_MODELE. It can be convenient to restart a parallel analysis with a number of processors different from that used for the initial analysis. In particular, one may want to carry out certain post-processings in sequential mode. It is recommended to use the command MODI_MODELE to define the distribution to be used on restart. More precisely, when the initial analysis has used parallelism by groups of elements ( GROUP_ELEM or SOUS_DOMAINE ), the command MODI_MODELE is useless. On the other hand, when the initial analysis has used parallelism “by elements” ( MAIL_CONTIGU or MAIL_DISPERSE ), the command MODI_MODELE is mandatory. If one forgets it, one is stopped during the analysis by an error message. 3.7.2 Choice of the method There exist different modes of distribution of the mesh cells, controlled by the keyword METHODE . When one chooses the method METHODE='CENTRALISE' , the parallelism begins only at the level of the linear solver. Each processor builds and supplies to the solver the whole of the system to be solved. The elementary analyses are not parallelised. This is the mandatory distribution method in the case of a parallel mesh of type maillage_p . The distribution method METHODE='GROUP_ELEM' allows a perfect load balancing (in terms of numbers of elementary analyses) a priori , that is to say that each processor will carry out, for a given element type, the same number of elementary analyses (to within one). Obviously this in no way prejudges the final load balancing, in particular in non-linear analyses where the cost of an elementary analysis depends on parameters other than the element type. In this mode, the elements of the model are grouped by “group” in order to pool certain analyses, which makes it possible to gain in efficiency. The number of elements per group can be chosen in the command DEBUT. Furthermore, this is the only mode able to distribute the elementary analyses induced by the late elements, that is to say by the loadings such as the dualised boundary conditions or the contact. The distribution by METHODE='MAIL_DISPERSE' operates on the mesh cells. They are distributed evenly over the different processors available. The mesh cells are distributed over the different processors as one does when one deals cards to several players. One also speaks of a “cyclic” distribution. For example, with a model comprising 8 mesh cells, run on 4 processors, one obtains the following distribution: | Distribution mode | Mesh cell 1 | Mesh cell 2 | Mesh cell 3 | Mesh cell 4 | Mesh cell 5 | Mesh cell 6 | Mesh cell 7 | Mesh cell 8 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | MAIL_DISPERSE | Proc. 0 | Proc. 1 | Proc. 2 | Proc. 3 | Proc. 0 | Proc. 1 | Proc. 2 | Proc. 3 | One sees that, with this distribution mode, a processor will treat mesh cells regularly spaced in the order of the mesh cells of the mesh. The advantage of this distribution is that, “statistically”, each processor will treat as many hexahedra, pentahedra, …, and triangles. The workload for the elementary analyses will in general be well distributed. On the other hand, the matrix assembled on a processor will be very “scattered”, unlike what happens for the following mode MAIL_CONTIGU . The distribution by METHODE='MAIL_CONTIGU' operates on the mesh cells. They are distributed in packets of contiguous mesh cells over the different processors available. For example, with a model comprising 8 mesh cells, a machine with 4 processors available, one obtains the following distribution: | Distribution mode | Mesh cell 1 | Mesh cell 2 | Mesh cell 3 | Mesh cell 4 | Mesh cell 5 | Mesh cell 6 | Mesh cell 7 | Mesh cell 8 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | MAIL_CONTIGU | Proc. 0 | Proc. 0 | Proc. 1 | Proc. 1 | Proc. 2 | Proc. 2 | Proc. 3 | Proc. 3 | 3.7.3 Control of the load For the distribution modes by elements, the workload for the elementary analyses may be less balanced. For example, a processor may have to treat only “easy” boundary mesh cells. On the other hand, the matrix assembled on a processor is in general more compact. The keyword CHARGE_PROC0_MA is accessible only for the distribution modes MAIL_DISPERSE and MAIL_CONTIGU . Indeed these distribution modes do not in general share the analysis load fairly, because of the dualised boundary conditions, whose elementary analyses are treated by processor 0. If one wishes to relieve processor 0 (or on the contrary to overload it), one can use the keyword CHARGE_PROC0_MA . It allows the user to choose the percentage of load that one wishes to assign to processor 0. For example, if the user chooses CHARGE_PROC0_MA=80 , processor 0 will treat 20% fewer elements than the other processors, that is 80% of the load that it should bear if the sharing were fair among the processors. 3.7.4 Decomposition of the mesh The distribution by the method METHODE='SOUS_DOMAINE' of the mesh cells is based on a decomposition of the mesh into subdomains, built by an external partitioning tool defined by the keyword PARTITIONNEUR . The number of subdomains can be determined by the user, via the keyword NB_SOUS_DOMAINE . By default, the number of subdomains is taken equal to the number of processors involved in the analysis. The finite-element model elements carried by the mesh cells of each subdomain are then distributed by groups of similar elements (as in the distribution corresponding to the method GROUP_ELEM ), in order to balance the elementary analyses as well as possible. The prior partitioning of the mesh into subdomains makes it possible to ensure that all the elements of a group of finite elements belong to a single subdomain. 4 Execution phase From the keywords PHENOMENE , MODELISATION and FORMULATION , one creates a data structure specifying the type of element attached to each mesh cell. A brief reminder of the assignments is printed systematically ( INFO=1 ) in the message file. 5 Example For a modelling of the phenomenon 'MECANIQUE', one assigns on the mesh-cell group gma of the mesh ma isoparametric 3D finite elements. If the mesh-cell group gma also contains the boundary mesh cells and/or the edge mesh cells of the volume mesh cells, then one also assigns on them the isoparametric finite elements necessary for certain analysis options (assignment of external loadings for example, cf. AFFE_CHAR_MECA). mo = AFFE_MODELE(MAILLAGE=ma, AFFE=(_F(GROUP_MA=gma, PHENOMENE="MECANIQUE", MODELISATION="3D")))

The partition of the finite elements is stored in the SD_MODELE (kept on the global database). When one is in restart, this implies continuing with the same number of processors. This is not necessarily desirable. To work around this difficulty, the command MODI_MODELE makes it possible to redefine the partition of the model. Modifies the data structure of type modele (re-entrant operator). 2 Syntax modele = MODI_MODELE( ◆ reuse = , ◆ MODELE = modele, ⟐ DISTRIBUTION = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "CENTRALISE", / "GROUP_ELEM", / "MAIL_CONTIGU", / "MAIL_DISPERSE", / "SOUS_DOMAINE" (par défaut), # Si: is_in("METHODE", ('MAIL_DISPERSE','MAIL_CONTIGU')) ◇ CHARGE_PROC0_MA = int (défaut: 100), ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE ♦ reuse = mo, ♦ MODELE = mo Name of the model that one seeks to modify (re-entrant operator). 3.2 Keyword DISTRIBUTION ◊ DISTRIBUTION This keyword as well as the operand METHODE are described in the documentation of AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01. Important note: It is recommended to begin command files of type POURSUITE with MODI_MODELE (reuse=MO,MODELE=MO). This command will create a new partition suited to the number of available processors. 4 Example This example illustrates several modifications of the partition mode of the model (extract from mumps05a): DEBUT() … # PARALLELISME CENTRALISE (seul le solveur Mumps sera traité en parallèle) MODI_MODELE(reuse=MO, MODELE=MO, DISTRIBUTION=_F(METHODE='CENTRALISE')) MECAC=MECA_STATIQUE(MODELE=MO, SOLVEUR=_F(METHODE='MUMPS', … ) … ) … # DISTRIBUTION DE MAILLES DISPERSEES, EQUILIBRAGE DE CHARGE AUTOMATIQUE MODI_MODELE(reuse=MO, MODELE=MO, DISTRIBUTION=_F(METHODE='MAIL_DISPERSE', CHARGE_PROC0_MA=0)) MECAD1=MECA_STATIQUE(MODELE=MO, SOLVEUR=_F(METHODE='MUMPS', … ) … ) … # DISTRIBUTION DE MAILLES DISPERSEES, EQUILIBRAGE DE CHARGE FORCé POUR # SOULAGER LE PROCESSEUR 0 MODI_MODELE(reuse=MO, MODELE=MO, DISTRIBUTION=_F(METHODE='MAIL_DISPERSE', CHARGE_PROC0_MA=70)) MECAD2=MECA_STATIQUE(MODELE=MO, SOLVEUR=_F(METHODE='MUMPS', … ) … ) FIN()

u4.41.11 Operator MODI_MODELE_XFEM u4.41.11 Operator MODI_MODELE_XFEM 1 Purpose Create a new model by introducing specific finite elements which can be crossed by a crack of X-FEM type, starting from an existing model. This operator makes it possible to modify certain classical finite elements into enriched finite elements; the elements to be modified have been determined beforehand by the operator DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08. The new model thus defined may be used in the rest of the analyses as input data: - to the operators MECA_STATIQUE U4.51.01 or STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03 if the initial model is a mechanical model; - to the operator THER_LINEAIRE U4.54.01 if the initial model is a thermal model. The operator produces a concept of type modele. 2 Syntax modele = MODI_MODELE_XFEM( ◆ MODELE_IN = modele, ◆ / FISSURE = fiss_xfem, / MODELE_THER = modele, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ CONTACT = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "STANDARD", / "MORTAR", ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "SANS", / "FORCE", ◇ DECOUPE_FACETTE = / "DEFAUT" (par défaut), / "SOUS_ELEMENTS", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE_IN ♦ MODELE_IN = mo mo: name of the initial model (also called the “sound model”) built on the mesh which served to define the crack beforehand by the operator DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08. This initial model, built with the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01, serves as the basis for the creation of the new model. It is necessary to choose a different name for the new model; modification of an existing model is not allowed, and the check is carried out during the syntax analysis of the command file. 3.2 Operand FISSURE ♦ / FISSURE = (fiss1, ...) (fiss1,...): list of the names of the cracks defined beforehand by the operator DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08. The number of cracks in a model is not limited. 3.3 Operand MODELE_THER / MODELE_THER = modxth The use of this keyword is of interest only in the particular case of chained thermo-mechanical analyses with X-FEM. In this case the following checks will be carried out by the operator: - modxth must be the thermal X-FEM model (already produced by the operator MODI_MODELE_XFEM, with the keyword FISSURE) with which the linear thermal problem is solved by the operator THER_LINEAIRE U4.54.01; - the sound model mo must be a mechanical model, and must have been defined on the same mesh as the enriched thermal model modxth The model produced by the operator is a mechanical model. 3.4 Operand CRITERE ♦ CRITERE = crit crit: real value of the criterion making it possible to cancel the enriched degrees of freedom when the crack passes close to a node. When the crack cuts a 3D finite element into two volumes, the ratio between the smallest volume and the largest volume must not exceed this criterion; otherwise, this can cause conditioning problems in the stiffness matrix, and lead to zero pivots. Thus, if the criterion is exceeded, the degrees of freedom liable to lead to zero pivots are eliminated automatically. The default value of the criterion is based on simple tests R7.02.12. 3.5 Operand CONTACT ♦ CONTACT = / ‘SANS’ / ‘STANDARD’ / ‘MORTAR’ This operand makes it possible to indicate whether interface forces exist between the lips of the crack: these may be contact, or cohesive forces. If this is the case, a contact load or cohesive forces must then be introduced by the command DEFI_CONTACT. For all the formulations, it is the value STANDARD which must be specified, except for the cohesive law CZM_LIN_MIX, which is a mixed cohesive law suited to linear finite elements (see R5.03.55]), for which one specifies the value MORTAR. Indeed, the latter requires the addition of several multiplier fields, which must therefore be specified when modifying the model in order to create the appropriate finite elements. 3.6 Operand PRETRAITEMENT ♦ PRETRAITEMENT S = / ‘AUTO’ / ‘SANS’ / ‘FORCE’ This operand makes it possible to indicate whether the algebraic preconditioning algorithms must be activated (modification of the stiffness matrix). By default, the choice is automatic ('AUTO'). One can either deactivate them ('SANS'), or force them ('FORCE'). Note : if there are quadratic finite elements in the model, the preconditioning algorithms will be activated. 3.7 Operand DECOUPE_FACETTE ♦ DECOUPE_FACETTE = / ‘DEFAUT’ / ‘SOUS_ELEMENTS’ This operand makes it possible to activate an alternative procedure ('SOUS_ELEMENTS') for constructing the contact facets, other than the default one ('DEFAUT'). The alternative procedure makes it possible in particular to treat the case of quadratic facets. 3.8 Operand INFO | / 1: | printout on the 'MESSAGE' file of 1. The stages of the analysis 2. The choice of the factor keyword defining the type of elements (POUTRE, DISCRET, ...) implies that the appropriate element types exist in the model (check carried out systematically). Examples: COQUE = _F(EPAIS = 1.E-2, GROUP_MA = ’G1’), COQUE = _F(ANGL_REP = (0., 90.), GROUP_MA = ’G2’), - for the assignments concerning BARRE, POUTRE and DISCRET, as well as ORIENTATION for the beam elements and the discrete elements, the large number of characteristics that can be assigned has led to a better adapted syntax: CARA= (…) # list of names of characteristics VALE= (…) # list of the values corresponding to the characteristics An example is given below to illustrate this case. : Assignment of the values. Three types of cross-section, defined by the operand SECTION , can be treated. For each type of section, it is possible to assign different characteristics identified by one or more names (operand CARA ) to which as many values are associated (operand VALE ). It is also possible to give the characteristics by means of a table in the case of the general section; see the documentation of the command MACR_CARA_POUTRE. 6.2 Syntax BARRE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ SECTION = / "CERCLE", / "GENERALE", / "RECTANGLE", # Si: equal_to("SECTION", 'GENERALE') ◇ / TABLE_CARA = table, & NOM_SEC = text, ◇ / AIRE = float, ◇ / CARA = "A" (ou non renseigné), & VALE = float, # Si: equal_to("SECTION", 'RECTANGLE') ◆ CARA = / "EP", / "EPY", / "EPZ", / "H", / "HY", / "HZ", ◆ VALE = list[float], de 1 à 4 valeurs attendues, # Si: equal_to("SECTION", 'CERCLE') ◆ CARA = / "EP", / "R", ◆ VALE = list[float], de 1 à 2 valeurs attendues, ◇ FCX = fonction / formule / nappe, ), Rule of use: One cannot overload one type of section (CERCLE, RECTANGLE, GENERALE) by another. 6.3 Operands 6.3.1 Operand SECTION = 'GENERALE' The only characteristic to be supplied in this case is the area of the cross-section of the bar 'A'.
