Rules of use: > For a given mesh cell - H is incompatible with HZ and HY - EP is incompatible with EPY and EPZ . 6.4 Operand 'FCX' 7 Keyword CABLE 7.1 Assignable characteristics Makes it possible to assign a constant section to elements of cable or cable-pulley type. 7.2 Syntax CABLE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ N_INIT = float, ◆ / AIRE = float, / RAYON = float, / DIAMETRE = float, ◇ FCX = fonction / formule / nappe, ), 7.3 Operands 8 Keyword COQUE 8.1 Assignable characteristics The characteristics that one can assign to the plate or shell elements are: - for all the elements of this type, a thickness constant on each mesh cell, since the mesh represents only the middle surface (or the reference surface for the offset ones), - for all the elements of this type, the number of layers used for the integration through the thickness, - for all the elements of this type, the orientation of the local frame specific to each mesh cell, - for certain shell models, particular characteristics: shear coefficient, metric, offset, etc. 8.2 Syntax COQUE = _F( ♦ GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ / EPAIS = ep, [real] / EPAIS_FO = epfct [function] ◊ / ANGL_REP = / (0.0, 0.0), [default] / ( \alpha , \beta ), [l_real] / VECTEUR = (vx ,vy ,vz), [l_real] ◊ MODI_METRIQUE = [’NON’|’OUI’], [default)] ◊ COEF_RIGI_DRZ = KRZ (1.E-5), [real (default)] ◊ EXCENTREMENT = e (0.0), [real (default)] EXCENTREMENT_FO = efct [function] ◊ INER_ROTA = ’OUI’, ◊ A_CIS = kappa (0.8333333), [real (default)] ◊ COQUE_NCOU = n (1), [integer (default)] ) 8.3 Operands 8.3.1 Operand EPAIS ♦ / EPAIS = ep / EPAIS_FO = epfct EPAIS represents the thickness of the shell, which must be expressed in the same units as the coordinates of the nodes of the mesh. EPAIS_FO is a function which gives the thickness of the shell, in the same units as the coordinates of the nodes of the mesh. This function depends on the geometry (X,Y,Z) and is evaluated at the centre of gravity of the mesh cell. 8.3.2 Operands EXCENTREMENT / EXCENTREMENT_FO ◊ excentrement = / e (0.0), [real (default)] excentrement_F0 = efct [function] excentrement: define the distance between the meshed surface and the mean surface, in the direction of the normal (modellings DKT, DST, GRILLE_EXCENTRE). excentrement_FO: Function which gives the distance between the meshed surface and the mean surface, in the direction of the normal (modellings DKT, DST, GRILLE_EXCENTRE). This function depends on the geometry (X,Y,Z) and is evaluated at the centre of gravity of the mesh cell. Taking the offset into account influences the bending behaviour and possibly the membrane behaviour in the presence of coupling (there is no effect on the shear). 8.3.3 Operands MODI_METRIQUE / COEF_RIGI_DRZ / INER_ROTA ◊ modi_metrique = ’non’ Makes the assumption that the thickness of the element is small. During the integrations through the thickness, the variation of the radius of curvature is not taken into account (default option for all shells). ◊ modi_metrique = ’oui’ For the modelling: COQUE_AXIS, the integrations are performed taking into account the variations of the radius of curvature as a function of the thickness; see for example R3.07.02 ◊ iner_rota = ’oui’ Account is taken of the rotary inertia for the modellings DKT, DST and Q4G. It is mandatory in the case of an offset. This keyword may be omitted for thin shells, where the rotary-inertia terms are negligible compared with the others in the mass matrix R3.07.03. ◊ coef_rigi_drz = krz, KRZ is a fictitious stiffness coefficient (necessarily small) on the rotational degree of freedom about the normal to the shell. It is necessary in order to prevent the stiffness matrix from being singular, but it must be chosen as small as possible. The default value of {10}^{-5} is suitable for most situations (it is a relative value: the stiffness about the normal is equal to KRZ times the smallest diagonal term of the stiffness matrix of the element). For the DKT, there are two modes of operation. COEF_RIGI_DRZ negative and COEF_RIGI_DRZ positive. In the case of COEF_RIGI_DRZ positive, the degree of freedom DRZ always has the meaning of a fictitious rotation which prevents the matrix from being singular in the global frame. In the case of a negative COEF_RIGI_DRZ, the rotational kinematics of the plate element about its normal is reinforced by a variational formulation. The degree of freedom DRZ therefore has a physical meaning. A value of {10}^{-8} is recommended. Note: Caution: in STAT/DYNA_NON_LINE, this coefficient may lead to additional Newton iterations (more than one iteration for a linear problem, for example). 8.3.4 Operand ANGL_REP / VECTEUR The keywords ANGL_REP or VECTEUR make it possible to specify the “user” frame in each shell element. It is in this frame that, for example, the stresses in the shell or the generalised forces are expressed U2.01.05. By means of these keywords, the user supplies a vector V which will make it possible to define the frame completely. The construction of this “user” frame from V is carried out at every point P in the following way (cf. Figure ): - the projection of V onto the tangent plane supplies the axis {x}_{l} , - the vector {z}_{l} is collinear with the normal n to the plane of the shell, which is known for each element; its orientation can be changed by MODI_MAILLAGE/ORIE_NORM_COQUE[U4.23.04], - the vector {y}_{l} is constructed so as to obtain an orthonormal frame. The “user” frame is therefore: (P,{x}_{l},{y}_{l},{z}_{l}) with: {z}_{l}=n and {y}_{l}={z}_{l}{x}_{l} : Definition of the user frame of a shell. The keywords ANGL_REP and VECTEUR are mutually exclusive; the vector V is defined by means of one or the other. ◊ ANGL_REP= ( \alpha , \beta ) The keyword ANGL_REP defines the vector V in the global frame (O,X,Y,Z) from two nautical angles \alpha and \beta as explained in Figure and Figure . | : Representation of the angle \alpha The rotation \alpha about \mathrm{OZ} transforms (\mathrm{OXYZ}) into ({\mathrm{OX}}_{1}{Y}_{1}Z) with {Z}_{1}\equiv Z . | : Representation of the angle \beta The rotation \beta about {\mathrm{OY}}_{1} transforms {\mathrm{OX}}_{1} into {\mathrm{OX}}_{2} . In the figure the angle \beta is negative. | | --- | --- | In a three-dimensional representation, the vector is obtained as follows [Figure]. : Three-dimensional representation of the vector V defined by ANGL_REP. ◊ VECTEUR = (\mathrm{vx},\mathrm{vy},\mathrm{vz}) The vector V is defined by its coordinates in the global frame (O,X,Y,Z) . Notes: • If none of the keywords above is supplied, it is therefore the global axis X which determines, by projection onto the tangent plane of the shell, the “user” frame of each mesh cell. • The “user” frame is also used for the definition of the orientation of the fibres in composite shells (DEFI_COMPOSITE, U4.42.03 ). 8.3.5 Operand COQUE_NCOU ◊ COQUE_NCOU = / n (1), [integer, default] This is the number of layers used for the integration through the thickness of the shell. The number of layers also determines the number of sub-points of the stress field: 2n+1 . In the non-linear case, it is necessary to use more than one layer in order to integrate the stresses through the thickness correctly, cf. U2.02.01. 8.3.6 Operand A_CIS ◊ A_CIS = / kappa (0.8333333), [real, default] This parameter is to be used if one wishes, for a thick shell, to place oneself within the framework of the Love-Kirchhoff model. It is applicable only for the modellings COQUE_C_PLAN, COQUE_D_PLAN, COQUE_AXIS and COQUE_3D. For more detail the user should refer to the guide U2.02.01. 8.3.7 Note on the use of ELAS_COQUE When ELAS_COQUE is used, the bending and membrane stiffnesses are entered by hand by the user in DEFI_MATERIAU. In this case, the thickness supplied in AFFE_CARA_ELEM serves only to compute the mass in dynamics and does not contribute to the stiffness. 9 Keyword POUTRE 9.1 Assignable characteristics This keyword makes it possible to assign the characteristics of the cross-sections of beam -type elements (modellings POU_D_E, pou_d_em, POU_D_T, POU_D_TG, POU_D_TGM, POU_D_T_GD, TUYAU_3M, TUYAU_6M). Several types of section, defined by the operand SECTION, can be treated: - GENERALE: The mechanical characteristics are given. - RECTANGLE: The dimensions of the section are given. Code_Aster computes the necessary mechanical characteristics: area, inertias, ... - CERCLE: The dimensions of the section are given. Code_Aster computes the necessary mechanical characteristics: area, inertias, ... - COUDE: Used to define the correction coefficients of the inertias and the amplification coefficients of the stresses in the case where one wishes to take into account the ovalisation of the section, which cannot be taken into account by beam theory. The mechanical characteristics are given by SECTION, which may take the value GENERALE or RECTANGLE or CERCLE. For each type of section, it is possible to assign different characteristics identified by one or more names (operand CARA) to which as many values are associated (operand VALE). It is also possible to give the characteristics by means of a table in the case of the general section; see the documentation of the command macr_cara_poutre. It is possible to treat beams of constant section (characteristic name without a suffix) or of variable section (characteristic name with suffix 1 or 2). The mode of variation of the section is defined by the keyword VARI_SECT (cf. [§ 9.4.1 ]). The characteristics of the section are then given at the initial node (name with suffix 1) and at the final node (name with suffix 2) (“initial” and “final” relative to the numbering of the support mesh cell). This keyword must also be used to define the torsion constant for the modelling (POU_D_EM). 9.2 Syntax POUTRE = _F( ◆ SECTION = / "CERCLE", / "COUDE", / "GENERALE", / "RECTANGLE", # Si: equal_to("SECTION", 'GENERALE') ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ VARI_SECT = / "CONSTANT" (par défaut), / "HOMOTHETIQUE", # The twist angle (which makes it possible to orient the cross-section of the beam about its neutral fibre) is always given in order to orient the principal axes of the section, which is rather impractical, because these axes are in general unknown before the computation of the geometric characteristics of the section, cf. MACR_CARA_POUTRE[U4.42.02] . • It is possible to supply, via Python variables, the characteristics of the (general) sections coming from an analysis with MACR_CARA_POUTRE (Cf. the test SSLL107F). • The various names of characteristics of the arguments of the operand CARA are described further on for each argument of the operand SECTION . - For a given mesh cell: ◦ One cannot overload one type of section variation (constant or variable) by another. ◦ One cannot overload one type of section ( CERCLE , RECTANGLE , GENERALE ) by another. ◦ For beams of variable section, the names with suffix 1 or 2 are incompatible with the names without a suffix. Example: A is incompatible with \mathit{A1} and \mathit{A2} . ◦ H is incompatible with \mathit{HZ} and \mathit{HY} (as well as \mathit{H1} , \mathit{H2} , …) ◦ \mathit{EP} is incompatible with \mathit{EPY} and \mathit{EPZ} (as well as \mathit{EP1} , \mathit{EP2} , …). ◦ \mathit{RY} , \mathit{RZ} and \mathit{RT} come into play only for the computation of the stresses. 9.4 Operands 9.4.1 Operand VARI_SECT Makes it possible to define the type of section variation between the two end nodes of the beam element, elements POU_D_E and POU_D_T R3.08.01. The possibilities are: | Section | Affine | Homothetic | | --- | --- | --- | | circle | no | yes | | rectangle | yes (along y ) | yes | | general | no | yes | - “Affine” means that the area of the section varies linearly between the two nodes. The dimensions in the direction y are constant ( \mathit{HY} , \mathit{EPY} ) and those in the direction z vary linearly ( \mathit{HZ1} , \mathit{HZ2} , \mathit{EPZ1} , \mathit{EPZ2} ). - “Homothetic” means that the dimensions of the section vary linearly between the values given at the two end nodes. In this case, the area of the section evolves quadratically. In the case of circular hollow sections, for the section to be considered homothetic, it is necessary that {\mathit{EP}}_{\mathit{DEBUT}}/{R}_{\mathit{DEBUT}}={\mathit{EP}}_{\mathit{FIN}}/{R}_{\mathit{FIN}} . If the homothety is not respected, the solution given by Code_Aster is approximate R3.08.01. 9.4.2 Operand MODI_METRIQUE Makes it possible to define, for the TUYAU elements, the type of integration through the thickness (modellings TUYAU_3M, TUYAU_6M): - MODI_METRIQUE= 'NON' leads to assimilating, in the integrations, the radius to the mean radius. This is therefore valid for pipes of small thickness (relative to the radius), - MODI_METRIQUE= 'OUI' implies a complete integration, more accurate for thick piping, but which may in certain cases lead to oscillations of the solution. Note > The option MODI_METRIQUE='OUI' has been deactivated following the observation of incorrect results when it is used. The flexibility coefficient corrects the geometric data (geometric moments of inertia) in accordance with the construction rules. Certain rules lead to performing the bending-stiffness computation with a corrected geometric moment of inertia: {I}_{y,z}=\frac{{I}_{y,z}(\mathrm{tube})}{\mathrm{cflex}} with \mathrm{cflex}>1.0 A classical value of \mathrm{cflex} , for a piping of thickness e and of mean radius {R}_{\mathrm{moy}} , is given by: \mathrm{cflex}=\frac{1.65}{\lambda} with \lambda =\frac{e{R}_{\mathrm{courb}}}{{R}_{\mathrm{moy}}^{2}} This value can be computed directly in the command file; see for example the test FORMA01A[V7.15.100]. In the case where 2 coefficients are given, one obtains: {I}_{y}=\frac{{I}_{y}(\mathit{tube})}{{\mathit{cflex}}_{xy}},{I}_{z}=\frac{{I}_{z}(\mathit{tube})}{{\mathit{cflex}}_{xz}} By default, \mathit{cflex}={\mathit{cflex}}_{xz}={\mathit{cflex}}_{xy}=1 (no modification of the geometric inertias). The stresses are then written: {\sigma}_{xx}=\frac{{M}_{y}.R}{{I}_{y}}\times \mathit{isigm} or {\sigma}_{xx}=\frac{{M}_{z}.R}{{I}_{z}}\times \mathit{isigm} with \mathit{isgim}\ge 1 In the case where 2 indices are given, one has: {\sigma}_{xx}=\frac{{M}_{y}.R}{{I}_{y}}\times {\mathit{isigm}}_{xy} or {\sigma}_{xx}=\frac{{M}_{z}.R}{{I}_{z}}\times {\mathit{isigm}}_{xz} By default, \mathit{isigm}={\mathit{isigm}}_{xz}={\mathit{isigm}}_{xy}=1 (no modification of the geometric inertias). The axis {z}_{3} (also a principal axis of inertia) is such that \left(P,{x}_{3},{y}_{3},{z}_{3}\right) is right-handed. VECT_Z makes it possible to define the orientation of the principal vector corresponding to the principal axis of inertia Z. {z}_{1}^{d},{z}_{2}^{d},{z}_{3}^{d} are the 3 components of a vector {Z}^{d} whose projection onto the plane orthogonal to {x}_{3} will supply the principal axis of inertia {z}_{3} . The axis {y}_{3} (also a principal axis of inertia) is such that \left(P,{x}_{3},{y}_{3},{z}_{3}\right) is right-handed. 10.8 Operand CARA = ’VECT_MAIL_Y’ | ’VECT_MAIL_Z’ VECT_MAIL_Y makes it possible, in the case of the use of a mesh to define the cross-section, to define the orientation of the section, by making the axis {y} of the mesh of the section correspond to the axis {y}_{3} obtained by the projection of {y}_{1}^{d},{y}_{2}^{d},{y}_{3}^{d} onto the plane orthogonal to {x}_{3} . The axis {z}_{3} is such that \left(P,{x}_{3},{y}_{3},{z}_{3}\right) is right-handed. VECT_MAIL_Z makes it possible, in the case of the use of a mesh to define the cross-section, to define the orientation of the section, by making the axis {z} of the mesh of the section correspond to the axis {z}_{3} obtained by the projection of {z}_{1}^{d},{z}_{2}^{d},{z}_{3}^{d} onto the plane orthogonal to {x}_{3} . The axis {y}_{3} is such that \left(P,{x}_{3},{y}_{3},{z}_{3}\right) is right-handed. In order to carry out this operation, it is necessary to know the angle \alpha giving the orientation of the principal frame of inertia with respect to the axes of the mesh of the section. This computation is carried out by the command MACR_CARA_POUTRE. The table produced contains all the necessary quantities. It must therefore be supplied by the keywords: TABLE_CARA = 'name of the table' and NOM_SEC = 'name of the section'. 10.9 Operand CARA = ’GENE_TUYAU’ This vector must be defined at a GROUP_NO (containing only one node) at the end of the pipe. There is the so-called “longitudinal” modelling, which will be represented by a beam (of geometric support SEG2), and a plane modelling of the section (perpendicularly to the SEG2). The keyword MULTIFIBRE makes it possible to associate groups of fibres (previously defined by the operator DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE) with a beam element. GEOM_FIBRE makes it possible to give the name of the concept created by DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE containing the description of all the groups of fibres. Caution: The information contained in the groups of fibres makes it possible to compute certain of the integrated characteristics of the cross-sections (area, static and quadratic moments). For the elements POU_D_TGM and POU_D_EM , it is necessary to give consistent values for the operands A,\mathrm{IY},\mathrm{IZ} under the keyword POUTRE . A check is carried out on the consistency of these quantities. On all the entities one can assign matrices corresponding to the translational degrees of freedom (T) only or to the translational and rotational degrees of freedom (\mathrm{TR}) . The matrices may be diagonal (D) or full (symmetric or non-symmetric). In all cases (symmetric, diagonal, full matrices) the numbering convention of the terms is imposed : - for symmetric matrices, only the upper triangle will be supplied, with an imposed convention for the numbering of the terms (see examples). - for diagonal matrices, only the terms of the diagonal will be supplied, with an imposed convention for the numbering of the terms (see examples). - for non-symmetric matrices, all the terms will be supplied, with an imposed convention for the numbering of the terms (see examples). The matrices may be assigned: - to nodes or to mesh cells of type POI1; they are then called nodal matrices (N) , - to mesh cells of type SEG2; they are then called connection matrices (L) . In the case of assignment of matrices to mesh cells or to nodes, the element type DISCRET must be assigned, beforehand, to these mesh cells or to these nodes by the operator AFFE_MODELE[U4.41.01]. 12.2 Syntax DISCRET and DISCRET_2D = _F( ♦ GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ◊ SYME = [’OUI’| ’NON’] [default] stiffness matrices ♦ / CARA = | ’K_T_D_N’| ’K_TR_D_N’| ’K_T_D_L’|’K_TR_D_L’, mass matrices / CARA = | ’M_T_D_N’| ’M_TR_D_N’,| ’M_T_D_L’,| ’M_TR_D_L’ damping matrices / CARA = | ’A_T_D_N’| ’A_TR_D_N’| ’A_T_D_L’|’A_TR_D_L’, ♦ / VALE = lva, [l_real] ◊ REPERE = [’LOCAL’,’GLOBAL’] [default] ◊ AMOR_HYST = amnh (0.0), [real (default)] ) 12.3 Operands 12.3.1 Rules of use - The complex stiffness matrix will actually be built during a call to CALC_MATR_ELEM[U4.61.01] with the option AMOR_HYST (see test SDLD313) and R5.05.04. 12.3.6 Operand REPERE ◊ REPERE = / ’LOCAL’, / ’GLOBAL’, By default the values of the matrices supplied for the discrete elements are used to express the corresponding quantities in the REPERE=’GLOBAL’. If one wishes to define a particular frame at a node (or mesh cell of type POI1) one will specify REPERE=’LOCAL’ by defining this frame by the keyword ORIENTATION [§ 10 ]. For a matrix defined on a mesh cell of type SEG2 the operand REPERE=’LOCAL’ makes it possible to refer to the local frame attached to the mesh cell (initial node, final node), completed if necessary by a twist angle defined by the keyword ORIENTATION [§ 10 ]. 13 Keyword MASSIF 13.1 Assignable characteristics Makes it possible to assign to 3D or 2D elements local axes (which may for example be used to define directions of orthotropy (cf. DEFI_MATERIAU[U4.43.01], DEFI_COMPOR[U4.43.06]. - ANGL_REP (3 nautical angles) - ORIG_AXE and ANGL_AXE (origin and axis of the cylindrical frame) - ANGL_EULER (3 angles) In 3D, these local axes can be defined by the keywords: - ANGL_REP (a single nautical angle) - ORIG_AXE (origin of the cylindrical frame) In 2D, these local axes can be defined by: One specifies that: - ANGL_REP or ANGL_EULER is used for an orthotropic or transversely isotropic material with fixed axes. - ORIG_AXE and ANGL_AXE are used for an orthotropic or transversely isotropic material whose axes follow a cylindrical frame, and only in this case. - CHAM_ORIE makes it possible to give a field (a map, in fact) of variable axes per element, precomputed in advance. 13.2 Syntax MASSIF = _F( ♦ / GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] > / TOUT = ‘OUI’, [only if keyword CHAM_ORIE] ♦ / ANGL_REP = ( \alpha , \beta , \gamma ), [l_real] > / ANGL_EULER = ( \Psi , \theta , \phi ), [l_real] / ORIG_AXE = (x1, x2, x3), [l_real] ◊ ANGL_AXE = ( \alpha , \beta ), [l_real] > / CHAM_ORIE , [sd_cara_elem.carmassi] ) 13.3 Operand ANGL_REP \alpha , \beta , \gamma are the 3 nautical angles (as for the keyword ORIENTATION, cf [§ 10 ]) defining the local axes (x,y,z) , which correspond to the frame of orthotropy (N,L,T) . In 2D, only \alpha must be given, which defines the frame (\text{LT}) in the plane. 13.4 Operand ANGL_EULER Definition of the 3 Euler angles which make it possible to orient the local frame of the element. The passage from the fixed frame OXYZ to the frame attached to the solid \textcolor{#0000ff}{O{x}_{3}{y}_{3}{z}_{3}} is made by three successive rotations: | The precession \textcolor{#ff0000}{\Psi} , about the axis OZ , passes from OXYZ to the frame \textcolor{#ff0000}{O{x}_{1}{y}_{1}{z}_{1}} .The nutation \textcolor{#008000}{\theta} , about the axis \textcolor{#ff0000}{O{x}_{1}} , passes from \textcolor{#ff0000}{O{x}_{1}{y}_{1}{z}_{1}} to \textcolor{#008000}{O{x}_{2}{y}_{2}{z}_{2}} .The proper rotation \textcolor{#0000ff}{\phi} , about the axis \textcolor{#008000}{O{z}_{2}} , passes from \textcolor{#008000}{O{x}_{2}{y}_{2}{z}_{2}} to the frame attached to the solid \textcolor{#0000ff}{O{x}_{3}{y}_{3}{z}_{3}} .In 2D, only one rotation angle must be given. | : Euler angles | | --- | --- | This operand is not available in 2D. 13.5 Operands ORIG_AXE/ANGL_AXE These keywords are to be given in order to define local axes for which a property of rotational symmetry, or of transverse isotropy, will be used (for example: a structure with orthotropic cylindrical symmetry). In 3D, ANGL_AXE = ( \alpha , \beta ) defines the axis of revolution \mathrm{x1} , (\alpha ,\beta ) being the first two nautical angles, ORIG_AXE = (x1 , x2 , x3) defines a point \mathrm{O1} of the axis. In 2D, the axis of revolution is necessarily oriented along Z. One therefore supplies only the point of the XY plane through which the axis of revolution passes. ORIG_AXE = (x1 , x2). : Definition of the axis for the MASSIF. 13.6 Operand CHAM_ORIE The keyword CHAM_ORIE makes it possible to define the orientations from an orientation field whose support is the mesh. As input to this keyword, one expects a field (a map) of the quantity CAMA_R which has 7 components: a scalar (of no importance for the user), the 3 nautical angles and the 3 Euler angles. It should be noted that this keyword was introduced in order to exploit orientation fields generated automatically from the topology of the mesh by a utility called “Local Frames Generator” available in the Salome platform (from version 9.11). This utility produces a MED file containing the mesh and the orientation field with 7 components. The object expected as input to the keyword CHAM_ORIE is therefore this orientation field read from the MED file with a LIRE_CHAMP / TYPE_CHAM = CART_CAMA_R. An example of use is given in the test case SSLV002. It will be noted that if the keyword CHAM_ORIE is called, then one can have only a single occurrence of the keyword AFFE_CARA_ELEM/MASSIF, and one must have the operand TOUT=’OUI’. The orientation field must have the complete mesh as its support. 13.7 Example of use One seeks to model a cylinder made of a transversely isotropic elastic material of type ELAS_ISTR, such that the axis of orthotropy of the material is in the direction of the cylinder. The characteristics of such a material are to be defined in the local frames of the elements, with the convention that the axis of orthotropy must be carried by N (cf. DEFI_MATERIAU[U4.43.01] [§3.5]). One can imagine two cases: - the axis of the cylinder has been defined along Z in the global frame. In this case, without performing a rotation of the local frames, one has by default (X,Y,Z)=(L,T,N) and N // Z as desired. - the axis of the cylinder has been defined along Y in the global frame. It is then necessary to perform a rotation of the local frames in order to bring N along Y as desired. One uses AFFE_CARA_ELEM(MASSIF=_F(ANGLE_REP=(0.,0.,-90.),),) which produces the transformation (L,T,N)=(X,-Z,Y) , and one then indeed has N // Y . In two dimensions, ELAS_ORTH will be used because ELAS_ISTR is forbidden. If the axis of anisotropy is not parallel to X or Y , the local frame will be rotated as in the 3D example by means of the keyword ANGLE_REP (which this time contains only a single angle) so as to bring L or T into the desired direction. 14 Keyword POUTRE_FLUI 14.1 Syntax POUTRE_FLUI = _F( ♦ GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ B_T = bt, [real] ♦ B_N = bn, [real] ♦ B_TN = btn, [real] ♦ A_FLUI = aflui, [real] ♦ A_CELL = acell, [real] ♦ COEF_ECHELLE = ech, [real] ) 14.2 Assignable characteristics This factor keyword makes it possible to define the characteristics of the finite elements (hexahedron with 8 or 20 nodes) associated with the modelling ’3D_FAISCEAU’, cf. the command AFFE_MODELE[U4.41.01]. This modelling concerns the representation of a periodic array of tubes bathed by an incompressible fluid R4.07.05. An example is given in the test SDLV111[V2.04.111]. 14.3 Operand GROUP_MA Place of assignment of the elementary characteristics: - list of mesh-cell groups (keyword GROUP_MA). 14.4 Operands A_FLUI/ A_CELL/ COEF_ECHELLE | The periodic cell of the medium to be homogenised is two-dimensional.The basic periodic cell which serves to compute the homogenised coefficients is obtained by homothety from the real periodic cell of the medium | : Fluid beam. | | --- | --- | ♦ A_FLUI: Area of the part occupied by the fluid in the basic periodic cell ♦ A_CELL: Area of the basic periodic cell ♦ COEF_ECHELLE: Homothety coefficient making it possible to transform the real periodic cell into the basic periodic cell 14.5 Operands B_T/ B_N/ B_TN Homogenised coefficients of the fluid-structure problem computed in the frame (T,N) R4.07.05. The orientation of this frame is fixed by the factor keyword ORIENTATION. The direction L is necessarily parallel to the axis of the bundle of tubes. 15 Keyword GRILLE 15.1 Syntax GRILLE = _F( ♦ GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ / SECTION = S1, [réel] / SECTION_FO = S1fct [fonction] ♦ / ANGL_REP_1= (:math: \alpha , :math: \beta ) [l_réel] / ANGL_REP_2= (:math: \alpha , :math: \beta ) [l_réel] / VECT_1= (vx, vy, vz) [l_réel] / VECT_2= (vx, vy, vz) [l_réel] ◊ / EXCENTREMENT = ez, [réel] / EXCENTREMENT_FO = ezfct [fonction] ◊ / REPERE = / "CYLINDRIQUE", / "GLOBAL" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("REPERE", "CYLINDRIQUE")) ♦ / ORIGINE = l_origine, [l_réel] ♦ / AXE_Z = l_axe, [l_réel] ◊ COEF_RIGI_DRZ = kz (1.E-10), [réel (défaut)] ) 15.2 Assignable characteristics : Replacement of the reinforcements by an equivalent layer. Makes it possible to define characteristics of a layer characterised by a stiffness in a single direction, used in particular to model reinforcement layers in reinforced-concrete shells (see for example the test SSNS100[V6.05.100]), assigned to the modellings GRILLE_EXCENTRE or GRILLE_MEMBRANE. To describe a reinforcement “lattice”, it is sufficient to superimpose two grille_excentre or grille_membrane elements whose orientations (and therefore the stiffnesses) are orthogonal (see the example in the following paragraph). 15.3 Description of the operands The following geometric data are necessary to model the reinforcement layer: ♦ / SECTION = {S}_{1} / SECTION_F0 = \mathit{S1fct} SECTION: section of the reinforcements in direction 1, per unit length. It therefore corresponds to the cumulative section over a unit width. If there is a section s every 1/\mathrm{5ème} of a unit, the cumulative section is 5\times s . SECTION_FO: function giving the section of the reinforcements in direction 1, per unit length. It therefore corresponds to the cumulative section over a unit width. This function depends on the geometry (X,Y,Z) and is evaluated at the centre of gravity of the mesh cell. ◊ / EXCENTREMENT = {e}_{z} / EXCENTREMENT_F0 = \mathit{ezfct} EXCENTREMENT: value of the offset {e}_{z} (constant for all the nodes of the mesh cell) of the reinforcement layer relative to the support mesh cell (distance measured along the normal to the support mesh cell), (modelling GRILLE_EXCENTRE only). EXCENTREMENT_F0: function which gives the offset (constant for all the nodes of the mesh cell) of the reinforcement layer relative to the support mesh cell (distance measured along the normal to the support mesh cell), (modelling GRILLE_EXCENTRE only). This function depends on the geometry (X,Y,Z) and is evaluated at the centre of gravity of the mesh cell. ◊ COEF_RIGI_DRZ = see keyword COQUE [§8]. ◊ / REPERE = / "CYLINDRIQUE", / "GLOBAL" (by default), The use of VECT_1/VECT_2 is simple and practical. However, it is not always possible to use them, as in the case of a polar frame in a horizontal plane. The option REPERE is by default equal to "GLOBAL", but the user can specify a "CYLINDRIQUE" frame by giving ORIGINE and AXE_Z. In this case, VECT_1 and VECT_2 (but also ANGL_REP_1 and ANGL-REP_2) will be expressed in this cylindrical frame. If: (equal_to("REPERE", "CYLINDRIQUE")) > ♦ / ORIGINE = (x, y, z), > ORIGINE defines the coordinates in the global frame of the centre of the "CYLINDRIQUE" frame. > ♦ / AXE_Z = (vx, vy, vz), > AXE_Z defines in the global frame the vector along the height of the "CYLINDRIQUE" frame. ♦ / ANGL_REP_1 = see ANGL_REP of the keyword coque [§8]. This keyword makes it possible to define the reference axis x of the local frame from two nautical angles. It also defines the frame in which the strains, stresses, curvatures, etc. are computed. / ANGL_REP_2 = see ANGL_REP of the keyword coque [§8]. This keyword makes it possible to define the reference axis y of the local frame from two nautical angles. It also defines the frame in which the strains, stresses, curvatures, etc. are computed. / VECT_1= (vx, vy, vz) This keyword also makes it possible to fix the local frame of the element. The projection of the vector supplied via the keyword VECT_1 defines the local vector x . / VECT_2 = (vx, vy, vz) This keyword also makes it possible to fix the local frame of the element. The projection of the vector supplied via the keyword VECT_2 defines the local vector y . For example, in the case of a cylindrical geometry, it makes it possible to define the directions of the circumferential reinforcements. To define a grid containing reinforcements in the longitudinal direction and in the transverse direction, two layers of elements must be created (command crea_maillage, keyword crea_group_ma), one layer of elements for the longitudinal direction and a second layer of elements for the transverse direction: GRILLE=( _F(GROUP_MA = ’GEOL’, SECTION = 0.02, ANGL_REP_1 = (0.0, 0.0,), EXCENTREMENT = 0.0, ), _F(GROUP_MA = ’GEOT’, SECTION = 0.01, ANGL_REP_1 = (90.0, 0.0,), EXCENTREMENT = 0.01, ), ) 16 Keyword MEMBRANE 16.1 Syntax MEMBRANE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ EPAIS = float, dans [0.0, ∞[, ◇ / ANGL_REP_1 = float, 2 valeurs attendues, / ANGL_REP_2 = float, 2 valeurs attendues, / VECT_1 = float, 3 valeurs attendues, / VECT_2 = float, 3 valeurs attendues, ◇ N_INIT = float, dans [0.0, ∞[ (défaut: 0.0), ), 16.2 Assignable characteristics One distinguishes two constitutive behaviours for the membrane. One has available a linear constitutive behaviour for small strains and a non-linear constitutive behaviour for large strains. 16.2.1 For the linear constitutive behaviour: : replacement of the reinforcements by a membrane The keyword MEMBRANE makes it possible to define characteristics of an anisotropic layer when the modelling MEMBRANE is used (see for example the test SSLS138. It can in particular be used to model elastic reinforcement layers in reinforced-concrete shells. This modelling can be associated with interface elements in order to model the decohesion of this layer. The stiffness of this membrane is supplied under DEFI_MATERIAU / ELAS_MEMBRANE. 16.2.2 For the non-linear constitutive behaviour: The keyword MEMBRANE makes it possible to define characteristics of an isotropic membrane when the modelling MEMBRANE is used (see for example the test SSNS115. The stiffness and the Poisson's ratio of this membrane are supplied under DEFI_MATERIAU/ELAS and the constitutive law under STAT_NON_LINE/RELATION/ELAS_MEMBRANE_SV or ELAS_MEMBRANE_NH COMPORTEMENT. One has available only two hyperelastic constitutive laws: the Saint-Venant–Kirchhoff law and the neo-Hookean law. 16.3 Description of the operands 17 Keyword RIGI_PARASOL 17.1 Syntax RIGI_PARASOL = _F( # Mailles servant à répartir les caractéristiques des discrets ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, # Mailles de type POI1 correspondant aux discrets ◆ / GROUP_MA_POI1 = grma, / GROUP_MA_SEG2 = grma, # Fonctions de répartition ◆ / FONC_GROUP = formule / nappe / fonction, / COEF_GROUP = float, ◇ REPERE = / "LOCAL", / "GLOBAL" (par défaut), # Raideurs et Amortissements à répartir ◆ CARA = / "K_TR_D_N", / "K_T_D_N", / "K_TR_D_L", / "K_T_D_L", / "A_TR_D_N", / "A_T_D_N", / "A_TR_D_L", / "A_T_D_L", # Si: exists("CARA") and (len(CARA)==1 or (len(CARA)==2 and CARA[0][2:]==CARA[1][2:])) ◆ VALE = float, # Méthode de calcul des surfaces afférentes aux noeuds du radier ◇ METHODE = / "UNIFORME", / "DIAG" (par défaut), # Centre de gravite ◆ / GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno, / COOR_CENTRE = float, ◇ UNITE = unit, ), 17.2 Assignable characteristics This functionality corresponds to a methodology used to determine the characteristics of discrete elements (translation and/or rotation springs) to be applied to the nodes of a raft from a global stiffness. This option is available in 3D and in 2D. In the 3D case the raft will be modelled by a surface; in the 2D case it will be modelled by a line SSNL130. In the 2D case the discrete elements are 2D_DIS_TR or 2D_DIS_T . One must assign the modelling DIS_TR | DIS_T in 3D or 2D_DIS_TR | 2D_DIS_T in 2D, on the node group which makes up the raft. The mesh cells which make up the raft carry a plate modelling (DKT, DST) or a 3D face modelling SDLS108. One must distinguish a mesh-cell group for the raft, to be declared after the keyword GROUP_MA of the factor keyword RIGI_PARASOL , and a mesh-cell group with 1 node resting on the nodes of this raft, which must be modelled and declared in AFFE_MODELE in the form of point mesh cells of type POI1 . If the mesh cells are of type POI1 , this must be indicated by means of the keyword GROUP_MA_POI1 of the factor keyword RIGI_PARASOL . The overloading rule applies The main operating principles of Code_Aster. If a mesh cell is present in several occurrences, it is the last assignment which is taken into account. 17.3 Description of the operands - in 3D, to give 3 values for VALE = ({k}_{x},{k}_{y},{k}_{z}) - in 2D, to give 2 values for VALE = ({k}_{x},{k}_{y}) 17.4 Principle of the determination of the characteristics of the discrete elements The document Seismic response by transient analysis gives theoretical information on the method used. 17.4.1 Discrete elements in translation In 3D, the raft is represented by a set of surface elements of centre of gravity O . One therefore has 3 global quantities which characterise the coupling between the soil and the raft: 3 translational stiffnesses {K}_{x},{K}_{y},{K}_{z} . In 2D, the raft is represented by a set of line elements of centre of gravity O . One therefore has 2 global quantities which characterise the coupling between the soil and the raft: 2 translational stiffnesses {K}_{x},{K}_{y} . Note: It is the same reasoning for the discrete elements of “damping” type. 17.4.2 Discrete elements in translation and rotation In 3D, the raft is represented by a set of surface elements of centre of gravity O . One therefore has 6 global quantities which characterise the coupling between the soil and the raft: 3 translational stiffnesses {K}_{x},{K}_{y},{K}_{z} , 3 rotational stiffnesses {Kr}_{x},{Kr}_{y},{Kr}_{z} . In 2D, the raft is represented by a set of line elements of centre of gravity O . One therefore has 3 global quantities which characterise the coupling between the soil and the raft: 2 translational stiffnesses {K}_{x},{K}_{y} , 1 rotational stiffness {Kr}_{z} . Note: It is the same reasoning for the discrete elements of “damping” type. 17.4.3 Distribution of discrete elements in stiffness and in damping If one wishes to distribute both stiffnesses and dampings, this must be specified under the keyword CARA, for example: CARA = (‘K_T_D_N', ‘A_T_D_N'), both in 2D and in 3D. The values to be distributed will be given under VALE. For example: Note: 17.4.4 Distribution method At each node of the mesh of the raft, one seeks the stiffness characteristics of a discrete element of type \text{K\_TR\_D\_N} = \left( {k}_{x}, {k}_{y}, {k}_{z}, {kr}_{x}, {kr}_{y}, {kr}_{z} \right) cf. Seismic response by transient analysis. To determine the translational stiffnesses, one imposes that they be proportional to the area represented by the node and to a distribution function depending on the distance to the centre of gravity of the raft. Let S(P) be the area attached to the node P and f(r) the distribution function where r is the distance from the node P to the node O . For the rotational stiffnesses, one distributes the remainder (what remains after having removed the contributions due to the translations) in the same way as the translations. If one computes the forces and the resulting moments at the point O due to the distribution of the springs at each node of the mesh of the raft and if one identifies them with the global values, one obtains the following formulae: \begin{array}{ccc}{k}_{x}={K}_{x}/\left(\sum_{p}S(p)f({op})\right)& ;& {k}_{x}(p)={k}_{x}S(p)f({op})\\ {k}_{y}={K}_{y}/\left(\sum_{p}S(p)f({op})\right)& ;& {k}_{y}(p)={k}_{y}S(p)f({op})\\ {k}_{z}={K}_{z}/\left(\sum_{p}S(p)f({op})\right)& ;& {k}_{z}(p)={k}_{z}S(p)f({op})\end{array} \begin{array}{ccc}{k}_{rx}=\left({K}_{rx}-\sum_{p}\left({k}_{z}(p){y}_{op}^{2}+{k}_{y}(p){z}_{op}^{2}\right)\right)/\left(\sum_{p}S(p)f({op})\right)& ;& {k}_{rx}(p)={k}_{rx}S(p)f({op})\\ {k}_{ry}=\left({K}_{ry}-\sum_{p}\left({k}_{x}(p){z}_{op}^{2}+{k}_{z}(p){x}_{op}^{2}\right)\right)/\left(\sum_{p}S(p)f({op})\right)& ;& {k}_{ry}(p)={k}_{ry}S(p)f({op})\\ {k}_{rz}=\left({K}_{rz}-\sum_{p}\left({k}_{x}(p){y}_{op}^{2}+{k}_{y}(p){x}_{op}^{2}\right)\right)/\left(\sum_{p}S(p)f({op})\right)& ;& {k}_{rz}(p)={k}_{rz}S(p)f({op})\end{array} Note 1: Note 2: One considers that the same formulae can be applied in order to carry out a distribution of discrete damping elements. 17.5 Examples of use Example no. 1: RIGI_PARASOL = _F(GROUP_MA = radier, COEF_GROUP = 2.0, GROUP_NO_CENTRE = 'P1', CARA = ( 'K_TR_D_N' , 'A_TR_D_N' ), VALE = ( 6 réels , 6 réels ), ) Example no. 2: RIGI_PARASOL = _F(GROUP_MA='DALLE', COEF_GROUP=1.0, GROUP_NO_CENTRE='PCDG', GROUP_MA_POI1='RESSORT', REPERE='GLOBAL', CARA='K_T_D_N', VALE=( 3 réels ), ) 18 Keyword RIGI_MISS_3D 18.1 Syntax ◇ RIGI_MISS_3D = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA_POI1 = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_SEG2 = grma, ◆ FREQ_EXTR = float, ◇ UNITE_RESU_IMPE = unit (défaut: 30), ), 18.2 Assignable characteristics The use of this keyword is dedicated to problems of uplift of the foundation in order to take better account of the soil spring mat than is done by RIGI_PARASOL, which distributes 6 global stiffnesses under a foundation in proportion to the areas of the elements surrounding its nodes. This keyword will assign the exact terms of an impedance matrix computed by MISS3D for all the interface degrees of freedom (3 times the number of nodes) and for a given extraction frequency. The assignment of these terms (modelling DIS_T ) is then made to the point mesh cells POI1 of the nodes of the surface foundation and possibly to the lines of the network of SEG2 superimposed on the foundation in order to represent the transverse connections between nodes. 18.3 Description of the operands 19 Keyword RIGI_GRILLE 19.1 Syntax RIGI_GRILLE = _F( # Mailles servant à répartir les caractéristiques des discrets ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, # Mailles de type SEG2 correspondant aux discrets (pour les directions X, Y, Z, RX, RY) ◆ GROUP_MA_SEG2 = grma, 5 valeurs attendues, # Raideurs ou Amortissements à répartir ◆ VALE = float, 5 valeurs attendues, # Centres de gravité ◆ GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno, 5 valeurs attendues, # Option ◇ OPTION = "RIGI" (par défaut), # Méthode de calcul des surfaces afférentes aux noeuds du radier ◇ METHODE = / "UNIFORME", / "DIAG" (par défaut), ), 19.2 Assignable characteristics This functionality corresponds to a methodology used to determine the characteristics of discrete elements to be applied to the raft from global stiffnesses. This option is available in 3D. The raft will be modelled by a surface; the discrete elements are DIS_TR . One must distinguish a mesh-cell group for the raft, to be declared after the keyword GROUP_MA , and the 5 mesh-cell groups of type SEG2 to be declared after the keyword GROUP_MA_SEG2 . These mesh cells SEG2 must be assigned by DIS_TR in AFFE_MODELE . These mesh cells each have one node in common with the raft, and one node on which a LIAISON_SOLIDE will be applied separately. 19.3 Description of the operands 19.3.1 Distribution method One denotes by S(p) the area pertaining to the node p of the raft, G(x_G,y_G) its geometric centre. One sets: - S_{tot} = \sum S(p) , - I_x = \sum S(p) (y_p − y_G )^2 , - I_y = \sum S(p) (x_p − x_G )^2 . The equivalent distribution laws are then: - k_x(p) = k_x {S(p) \over S_{tot}} - k_y(p) = k_y {S(p) \over S_{tot}} - k_z(p) = k_z {S(p) \over S_{tot}} - k_{rx}(p) = k_{rx} {S(p) \over I_x} - k_{ry}(p) = k_{ry} {S(p) \over I_y} 20 Keyword MASS_AJOU 20.1 Syntax ◇ MASS_AJOU = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_POI1 = grma, ◆ FONC_GROUP = fonction / formule / nappe, ), 20.2 Assignable characteristics The objective of this keyword is to take into account simply the added mass of fluid without having to model the fluid as in MACRO_MATR_AJOU and to keep only the structure for non-linear dynamic studies. The idea is therefore, in a new option of AFFE_CARA_ELEM , to distribute point-mass characteristics to the nodes of the fluid-structure interface without adding degrees of freedom. One draws inspiration from the distribution of the global stiffness or damping characteristics carried out by the option RIGI_PARASOL of AFFE_CARA_ELEM . The option MASS_AJOU makes it possible to distribute to the nodes of the fluid-structure interface characteristics M_T_N with elementary values of directional mass. These values are obtained by integration of the normal pressure on the elements from distribution functions which may depend on the coordinates, in particular on the altitude, in order to express Westergaard relations or, more simply, the expression of the hydrostatic pressure. The assignment of these terms (modelling to be declared in AFFE_MODELE: DIS_T for a surface fluid-structure interface in 3D and 2D_DIS_T for a line fluid-structure interface in 2D) is made to the point mesh cells POI1 of the nodes of the fluid-structure interface by means of the keyword GROUP_MA_POI1 of the factor keyword MASS_AJOU . These point mesh cells must be distinguished from the surface or line mesh-cell groups for the fluid-structure interface, to be declared after the keyword GROUP_MA . In the case where the result of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM with the keyword MASS_AJOU is used to carry out an analysis with results coming from an analogous model without MASS_AJOU , for example within the framework of an analysis with an initial state coming from a model without added mass, it is necessary to extend the result over the whole of the new model, in order to initialise the fields correctly. This can be done via the command PROJ_CHAMP with PROL_VALE = 0.0 . 20.3 Description of the operands 21 Keyword MASS_REP 21.1 Syntax MASS_REP = _F( # Surface ou ligne servant à répartir la masse ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, # Mailles de type POI1 correspondant aux masses ◆ GROUP_MA_POI1 = grma, # Masse à répartir sur les mailles de GROUP_MA ◆ VALE = float, ◆ TYPE = / "LINEIQUE", / "SURFACIQUE", / "TOTALE", # Fonction de répartition de la masse ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ), 21.2 Assignable characteristics The objective of this keyword is to take into account simply a mass and to distribute it over a surface. The option MASS_REP makes it possible to distribute to the nodes of the discrete elements of characteristic M_T_D_N mass values obtained in proportion to the area of the surface mesh cells or to the length of the line mesh cells. The assignment (modelling DIS_T to be declared in AFFE_MODELE) is made to the point mesh cells POI1 given to GROUP_MA_POI1 . The point mesh cells and the surface mesh cells to be declared after the keyword GROUP_MA must be distinguished. The overloading rule applies The main operating principles of Code_Aster. If a mesh cell POI1 is present in several occurrences of MASS_REP, it is the last assignment which is taken into account. In the case of overloading, a piece of information is written in the ‘message’ file, indicating the number of overloadings carried out. 21.3 Description of the operands

u4.42.02 Macro-command MACR_CARA_POUTRE u4.42.02 Macro-command MACR_CARA_POUTRE This macro-command makes it possible to compute the characteristics of a beam cross-section from a 2D mesh of its cross-section. It makes it possible to build a table of values, usable by the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01 in order to assign straight-section characteristics to all the beam finite elements (modellings POU_D_E, POU_D_T, POU_D_TG, pou_d_em, pou_d_tgm) or bar finite elements (modelling BARRE) of arbitrary section. The necessary characteristics are defined in the reference note R3.08.03. They are: - the geometric characteristics, which can be computed on a complete mesh, a half-mesh with symmetry with respect to Y or to Z , a quarter-mesh with two symmetries with respect to Y and to Z . - the torsion characteristics: torsion radius, torsional stiffness constant, position and eccentricity of the centre of torsion for bending–torsion coupling. - the shear characteristics for the models with shear-force strains. - the warping characteristics for the torsion models of non-symmetric open sections. The macro-command produces a concept of type table_sdaster containing the characteristics of the section. The values contained in this table can be used, via Python, in the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01 for an analysis of beam type, or by supplying the table produced in AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01 via the keyword table_cara . 1 Syntax table = MACR_CARA_POUTRE( ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: not exists("MAILLAGE") ◇ FORMAT = / "ASTER", / "MED" (par défaut), # Si: ( equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ) ◇ UNITE = unit, # Si: ( not equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ) ◇ UNITE = unit, ◇ ORIG_INER = float (défaut: (0.0, 0.0)), ◇ QUADRANT = / 1, / 2, / 3, / 4, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TABLE_CARA = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ / SYME_Y = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA_BORD = grma, ◇ / SYME_Z = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, # Si: not (equal_to("TABLE_CARA", 'OUI') and exists("GROUP_MA")) ◆ NOM = text, # Si: exists("GROUP_MA_BORD") ◇ GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ GROUP_MA_INTE = grma, # Si: (exists("GROUP_MA_BORD")) and (exists("GROUP_MA")) ◇ & LONGUEUR = float, & LIAISON = / "ROTULE", / "ENCASTREMENT", & MATERIAU = mater, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands 2.1 Operand MAILLAGE Name of the 2D mesh of the beam section whose characteristics one is going to compute. If the name of the mesh is not given, the following keywords must be supplied so that the macro-command carries out the reading by the command LIRE_MAILLAGE. Note: When the section is made up of elements of small thickness (tubes, built-up sections, ...), it is necessary to have several mesh cells through this thickness in order to compute correctly the characteristics linked to torsion. 2.2 Operands UNITE and FORMAT If MAILLAGE is not present, one must give the logical unit for reading the file as well as its format. Logical unit number for reading the 2D mesh of the beam section whose characteristics one is going to compute. Note: If one must make several calls to MACR_CARA_POUTRE in the same command file, on the same mesh or on different meshes, one must then change UNITE. 2.3 Operand TABLE_CARA When this option is present, the table produced contains only the parameters useful to AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 2.4 Operand NOM The operand NOM must be given (except if TABLE_CARA=’OUI’ and GROUP_MA is specified, because it is useless in that case). This value is found in the column LIEU of the table. This allows the user to give a name to the section, which can be used in AFFE_CARA_ELEM. Note: If GROUP_MA is specified (and TABLE_CARA=’OUI’), the names of the mesh-cell groups can be used directly in AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 2.5 Operands SYME_Y / SYME_Z If SYME_Y: Indicates that the mesh corresponds to a half-mesh. The computation of the characteristics of the cross-section takes account of a symmetry with respect to Y\mathrm{=}0 . If SYME_Z: Indicates that the mesh corresponds to a half-mesh. The computation of the characteristics of the cross-section takes account of a symmetry with respect to Z\mathrm{=}0 . The simultaneous use of the two options makes it possible to supply only a quarter of the mesh. The symmetry properties are used to speed up the computation of the geometric characteristics. Note: The keywords SYME_Y and SYME_Z are used only for the computation of the geometric characteristics. The mechanical characteristics (torsion constant, warping constant, shear coefficients) do not take them into account. In order to compute them, one must therefore mesh the section in full. This is why SYME_Y and SYME_Z cannot be specified when GROUP_MA_BORD is used. 2.6 Operand QUADRANT Makes it possible to define the quadrant in which one wants to obtain the mechanical characteristics linked to the principal inertia frame, and therefore linked to the definition of the angle \alpha . The quantities concerned are: ALPHA, IY, IZ, EY, EZ, AY, AZ, IYR2, IZR2. If QUADRANT is not given, no modification is carried out. When QUADRANT is [1, 2, 3, 4], the change of quadrant consists of a permutation of the quantities, with a change of sign if necessary. | Definition of the quadrants: I : \alpha is in [ 0°, 90°[ II : \alpha is in [ 90°, 180°[ III : \alpha is in [180°, 270°[ IV : \alpha is in [270°, 360°[ | : Definitions of the quadrants. | | --- | --- | 2.7 Computation of the mechanical characteristics 2.8 Case of a network of beams 3 Definition of the quantities produced 3.1 Frame of the structural element Figure u4.42.02-fig-repere_element_poutre indicates the frame linked to the structural element. The axis X represents the neutral axis of the structural element. The mechanical characteristics must be given in the principal axes of the cross-section R3.08.01 of the element: {Y}_{principal} and {Z}_{principal} . : Frame of the structural element 3.2 Frames used for the geometric characteristics Two frames are used: - the frame OYZ of description of the 2D mesh; - the principal inertia frame Gyz of the cross-section, whose naming corresponds to that used in the description of the beam elements of neutral fibre Gx AFFE_CARA_ELEM. Note: The mesh which is input to the command is in 2D and must therefore be given in the axes oxy . The coordinates z must all be identical. The command MACR_CARA_POUTRE makes the correspondence between the axes x and Y , y and Z . : Definition of the geometric quantities relating to a beam section. 3.3 Quantities available in the table produced 3.3.1 Geometric characteristics These characteristics are given in the table for the whole mesh and for each group of the list lgm , which may correspond to a half or a quarter of the section if the keywords SYME_Y or SYME_Z are present. 3.3.1.1 Characteristics of the mesh read - area: A_M - position of the centre of gravity: CDG_Y_M,CDG_Z_M - area moments of inertia, at the centre of gravity G in the frame GYZ : IY_G_M, IZ_G_M, IYZ_G_M 3.3.1.2 Characteristics of the beam section - area: A. - position of the centre of gravity: CDG_Y,CDG_Z. - area moments and product of inertia, at the centre of gravity G in the frame GYZ : IY_G, IZ_G, IYZ_G. - principal area moments of inertia in the frame Gyz , usable for the computation of the bending stiffness of the beam: IY and IZ. - ALPHA: angle of passage from the frame GYZ to the principal inertia frame Gyz . - characteristic distances, with respect to the centre of gravity G of the section, for the computations of maximum stresses: Y_MAX, Y_MIN, Z_MAX, Z_MIN and R_MAX. - RY and RZ: maximum of Y_MIN and Y_MAX and of Z_MIN and Z_MAX. - Y_P, Z_P: point of computation of the geometric moments of inertia. - IY_P, IZ_P, IYZ_P: geometric moments of inertia in the frame PYZ . - IY_P, IZ_P: moments of inertia in the frame Pyz . - IYR2_G, IZR2_G, IYR2, IZR2, IXR2_P, IYR2_P: characteristics useful for the geometric stiffness matrix of the elements POU_D_TG and POU_D_TGM. For more detail on the definition of the quantities see R3.08.04: {I}_{yr}^{2} = \int_{S} y \left(y^2+z^2 \right) dS {I}_{zr}^{2} = \int_{S} z \left(y^2+z^2 \right) dS 3.3.2 “Mechanical” characteristics These characteristics are supplied in the table for the whole mesh and for each mesh-cell group of the list lgm . 3.3.2.1 Torsion characteristics - torsion constant: JX The solution of a steady thermal problem of unknown \varphi makes it possible to determine the torsion constant and the shear stresses. Note: When the section is made up of elements of small thickness (tubes, built-up sections, ...), it is necessary to have several mesh cells through this thickness in order to compute correctly the characteristics linked to torsion. The torsion characteristics are obtained by the solution of \Delta \varphi on the section; the mesh must therefore make it possible to solve this equation. It is necessary to have more than three linear mesh cells or two quadratic mesh cells through the thickness in order to solve \Delta \varphi correctly. If there is doubt about the value found, it is possible to obtain an approximate value by applying the formula given in [bib1]_ (page 200, table 3.6.5). - torsion radius: RT The torsion radius Rt may vary along the external contour. Indeed, for an arbitrary section, the shears due to torsion vary on the edge. One chooses to take the value of Rt leading to the maximum shears on the external edge, that is to say the maximum value of Rt (in absolute value) on the external contour. Moreover, if the section is cellular, one has several “several torsion radii”: Rt = 2 A(k)/L(k) , where A(k) represents the area of cell k and L(k) its perimeter. If one is content to look for the maximum value of the shear, one must take the maximum of the values Rt obtained on the external edge and on the cells. - Position of the centre of torsion (point C ) in the frame GYZ: PCTY and PCTZ. One deduces from it the eccentricity of the centre of torsion CG in the principal inertia frame Gyz: EY and EZ. - Position of the centre of torsion (point C ) in the frame of the initial mesh: PCT_M_Y and PCT_M_Z. - Warping constant (usable for the modellings POU_D_TG and POU_D_TGM with 7 degrees of freedom): JG. 3.3.2.2 Shear characteristics The coefficients {A}_{y} and {A}_{z} are given, in the principal inertia frame Gyz , in the form of the ratio >1 of the total area to the area effectively sheared. 3.4 Assignment of the quantities in AFFE_CARA_ELEM The characteristics contained in this table and which can be used in AFFE_CARA_ELEM have the same names as the characteristics expected under the keyword CARA of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM. The results computed by MACR_CARA_POUTRE can be transmitted simply to AFFE_CARA_ELEM via the keyword TABLE_CARA. 4 Examples of use 4.1 Characteristic of an equal-leg angle section Angle 50x50x8 treated by the test SSLL107. 4.1.1 Section studied : Equal-leg angle 50x50x8. 4.1.2 Command file TCARA = MACR_CARA_POUTRE( GROUP_MA_BORD = ’LSURF’, GROUP_NO= ’GN1’, INFO = 2 ) where LSURF is the group of the line mesh cells of the contour of the section. 4.1.3 Geometric characteristics obtained The characteristics of the mesh are identical to those of the section.
