u4.42.03 Operator DEFI_COMPOSITE u4.42.03 Operator DEFI_COMPOSITE 1 Purpose Determine the homogenised material characteristics of a multilayer shell from the characteristics of each layer. The following characteristics are taken into account: - thickness, - type of the constituent material, - orientation of the fibres with respect to a reference axis. This command produces a data structure of type mater. It cannot be used in non-linear mechanics (STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE). 2 Syntax mater = DEFI_COMPOSITE( ◆ COUCHE = _F( ◆ EPAIS = float, ◆ MATER = mater, ◇ ORIENTATION = float, ), ◇ IMPRESSION = _F( ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword COUCHE ♦ COUCHE = _F Factor keyword for the definition of a layer of the multilayer composite, starting from the lower layer up to the upper layer. 3.1.1 Operand EPAIS ♦ EPAIS = EP Thickness of the layer. 3.1.2 Operand MATER ♦ MATER = MA The concept MA contains the constituent material of the layer and is produced by the operator DEFI_MATERIAU under the factor keyword ELAS_ORTH. The damping parameters AMOR_ALPHA, AMOR_BETA and AMOR_HYST available in ELAS_ORTH are not taken into account by DEFI_COMPOSITE. 3.1.3 Operand ORIENTATION ◊ ORIENTATION = orien Angle of the 1st direction of orthotropy (longitudinal direction or fibre direction) in the plane tangent to the element with respect to the 1st direction of the reference frame defined in the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM by the factor keyword COQUE and the keyword ANGL_REP U4.42.01. By default orien is zero; otherwise it must be supplied in degrees and must lie between –90° and +90° . 3.2 Operand IMPRESSION ◊ IMPRESSION = _F ( ◊ UNITE = / unit , [I] / 8 , [DEFAUT] This integer makes it possible to choose the logical unit of the file on which the printout, in RESULTAT format, of the list of homogenised coefficients will be made. By default, the printout will be carried out on the logical unit associated with the file of logical unit 8. 4 Example MULTI = DEFI_COMPOSITE( COUCHE =(_F(EPAIS = 1.E-3, MATER = MAT1, ORIENTATION = - 20.), _F(EPAIS = 2.E-3, MATER = MAT2, ORIENTATION = 10.), _F(EPAIS = 2.E-3, MATER = MAT2, ORIENTATION = - 10.), _F(EPAIS = 1.E-3, MATER = MAT1, ORIENTATION = 20.),), ) corresponds to the multilayer:

u4.42.04 Macro-command DEFI_CABLE_BP u4.42.04 Macro-command DEFI_CABLE_BP > Summary The objective of this command is to compute the initial tension profiles along the prestressing cables of a concrete structure. The data of the analysis are the tension applied at the ends and other parameters characteristic of the anchorages and of the materials. The relations used are those prescribed by the BPEL 91 or by the ETCC. It also makes it possible to create kinematic relations between the nodes of the cable and the nodes of the concrete in which it is embedded. The concept cabl_precont produced can then be used: - either by the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01, operand RELA_CINE_BP, to define the mechanical loadings linked to the presence of the cable (kinematic relations and/or tension in the cables). These loadings will be taken into account by the operator STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03; - or by the operator CALC_PRECONT U4.42.05 for a progressive tensioning of the cables and the possibility of carrying out phasing; - or by the operator DEFI_GROUP (CREA_GROUP_NO/OPTION = ’RELA_CINE_BP’) to create node groups corresponding to the links created and to allow a visual check of these kinematic relations. Produces a data structure of type cabl_precont. 1 Syntax cabl_precont = DEFI_CABLE_BP( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ GROUP_MA_BETON = grma, ◆ TYPE_ANCRAGE = / "ACTIF", / "PASSIF", ◇ ADHERENT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: (equal_to("ADHERENT", 'OUI')) ◆ / DEFI_CABLE = _F( ◇ / GROUP_MA = grma, / | TABL_CABLE = table, | GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = grno, ), / MODI_CABLE_RUPT = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = grno, ◆ TENSION = table, ), ◇ TYPE_RELAX = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "BPEL", / "ETCC_DIRECT", / "ETCC_REPRISE", # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RELAX", 'BPEL') ◆ R_J = float, # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RELAX", 'ETCC_DIRECT') ◆ NBH_RELAX = float, # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RELAX", 'ETCC_REPRISE') ◇ MODI_CABLE_ETCC = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = grno, ◆ TENSION = table, ), ◆ NBH_RELAX = float, ◇ CONE = _F( ◆ RAYON = float, ◆ LONGUEUR = float, ◆ PRESENT = / "OUI", / "NON", ), # Si: (not exists("MODI_CABLE_RUPT")) ◆ TENSION_INIT = float, ◆ RECUL_ANCRAGE = float, # Si: (equal_to("ADHERENT", 'NON')) ◆ DEFI_CABLE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = grno, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands 2.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = modèle Concept produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01 making it possible to define the types of finite elements assigned to the mesh cells of the mesh. 2.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER = chmat Concept produced by the operator AFFE_MATERIAU U4.43.02 making it possible to assign materials to the mesh cells of the mesh. 2.3 Operand CARA_ELEM ♦ CARA_ELEM = caelem Concept produced by the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01 making it possible to assign mechanical and geometric characteristics to the elements of the structure studied. 2.4 Operand GROUP_MA_BETON ♦ GROUP_MA_BETON = grmabe Name of the mesh-cell group (or groups) of the mesh representing the concrete structure. One thus defines precisely the geometric locus of projection of the cables, a preliminary step to the determination of the kinematic relations between the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the cables and the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the concrete structure. Notes: 1- It is possible to supply here a list of mesh-cell groups, in particular for the case in which all the concrete mesh cells surrounding the cable do not have the same constitutive behaviour. However, it is indispensable that all the concrete mesh cells concerned have the same characteristics BPEL_BETON . 2- The mesh cells modelling the concrete can only be 3D mesh cells or 2D mesh cells in the case of a plate modelling ( DKT,Q4GG) . 2.5 Definition of the cable 2.5.1 Keyword DEFI_CABLE [DEFAUT] DEFI_CABLE Factor keyword making it possible to define a cable by designating the topological entities of the mesh which represent it. Multiple occurrences are allowed, in order to be able to define several cables. The cables can be defined individually or via the supply of a table (see test SSNV229a) / ♦ GROUP_MA = grmaca Name of the mesh-cell group of the mesh representing the cable. ♦ GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = l_gnoa List of node groups defining the anchorages. The cardinal of this list must be less than or equal to 2. In each node group, one will retain as anchorage only the first node of the group. / ♦ TABL_CABLE = table When the number of cables is large, it may be easier to have defined them via a table containing 3 columns, defining the mesh-cell group of the cables and the name of the 2 node groups defining the anchorages. The columns must be named GROUP_MA, GROUP_NO1, GROUP_NO2. This table can be defined outside Code_Aster (Excel, python) and read with the command LIRE_TABLE. Example: #LISTE CABLE GROUP_MA GROUP_NO1 GROUP_NO2 CAB1 CAB1_I CAB1_F CAB3 CAB3_I CAB3_F 2.5.2 Keyword MODI_CABLE_ETCC ◊ MODI_CABLE_ETCC Factor keyword making it possible to define a cable by designating the topological entities of the mesh which represent it and supplying, for each of the cables, the short-term initial tension in order to make it possible to compute the losses by relaxation of the steel according to the ETCC ( bonded cable only ). Multiple occurrences are allowed, in order to be able to define several cables. In order to use it, one must have specified TYPE_RELAX=’ETCC_REPRISE’. ♦ GROUP_MA = grmaca Name of the mesh-cell group of the mesh representing the cable. ♦ GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = l_gnoa List of node groups defining the anchorages. The cardinal of this list must be less than or equal to 2. In each node group, one will retain as anchorage only the first node of the group. ♦ TENSION = table Table containing the tension in the cable for all the curvilinear abscissae (table with 2 columns). This table is used to compute the losses by relaxation of the steel in the case where the user has opted for the option TYPE_RELAX = ’ETCC_REPRISE’. This table is obtained via a POST_RELEVE_T on the nodes of the cable studied, after a first static analysis. 2.5.3 Keyword MODI_CABLE_RUPT ◊ MODI_CABLE_RUPT Factor keyword making it possible to define a cable by designating the topological entities of the mesh which represent it. This keyword makes it possible to bypass the tension computation by recovering the table supplied under the keyword TENSION. The technique makes it possible to simulate the failure of a cable with re-anchoring ( bonded cable only ). Multiple occurrences are allowed, in order to be able to define several cables. ♦ GROUP_MA = grmaca Name of the mesh-cell group of the mesh representing the cable. ♦ GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE = l_gnoa List of node groups defining the anchorages. The cardinal of this list must be less than or equal to 2. In each node group, one will retain as anchorage only the first node of the group. ♦ TENSION = table Table containing the tension in the cable for all the curvilinear abscissae (table with 2 columns) and which will become the reference tension. This table is obtained via a POST_RELEVE_T on the nodes of the cable studied after a first analysis, then modified as the user wishes. 2.6 Operand ADHERENT ♦ ADHERENT = / ’OUI’ [DEFAUT] / ’NON’ This keyword makes it possible to indicate whether one wishes to model cables bonded to the concrete (ADHERENT = ’OUI’) or sliding or frictional cables (ADHERENT = ’NON’). For the non-bonded cases, one must use, in order to represent the steel, the modelling CABLE_GAINE and the constitutive law CABLE_GAINE_FROT. The bonded case can be simulated with the modellings BARRE or CABLE_GAINE. Note: In the case ADHERENT = ’NON’, the tension profile is computed even if it is not used afterwards (neither in AFFE_CHAR_MECA/RELA_CINE_BP, nor in CALC_PRECONT). 2.7 Operand TYPE_ANCRAGE ♦ TYPE_ANCRAGE = l_tya List of arguments of text type characterising the anchorages of the cable: ‘ACTIF’ or ‘PASSIF’ (the only admissible arguments). This list must contain 2 arguments, no more and no less, and must be ordered with respect to the list of the nodes defining the anchorages (operand GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE above). Note that if several cables are defined in DEFI_CABLE then the first argument of TYPE_ANCRAGE applies to all the first nodes which define the anchorages. Likewise for the second argument. Notes: 1- The operator reconstructs the connected path leading from the first to the second anchorage of the cable by traversing the mesh cells which represent it. The non-existence of a connected path between the two anchorages causes the program to stop in fatal error. 2- The active anchorages are those at which one applies an initial tension. 2.8 Operand TENSION_INIT ♦ TENSION_INIT = f0 Value of the initial force applied to the active anchorages of the cables. This value must be positive. 2.9 Operand RECUL_ANCRAGE ♦ RECUL_ANCRAGE = delta Value of the anchorage slip at the active anchorages of the cables. This value must be positive. 2.10 Choice of the type of analysis for taking into account the relaxation of the steels ◊ TYPE_RELAX = /'SANS', [DEFAUT] /'BPEL', /'ETCC_DIRECT', /'ETCC_REPRISE', Keyword making it possible to define whether or not one takes into account the tension losses by relaxation of the steel by the regulatory method, and if so which one (ETCC or BPEL). This factor keyword being optional, by default the tension losses by relaxation of the steel are not taken into account. 2.10.1 TYPE_RELAX='SANS' This is the default value. In this case, one does not take this type of loss into account by a regulatory method. On the other hand, one can take it into account by using the viscoelastic constitutive law RELAX_ACIER for the cable (cf. R5.03.09). 2.10.2 TYPE_RELAX=’BPEL’ In this case, the BPEL formula is applied, and the keyword R_J must be specified (cf. § 2.11 for the detail). 2.10.3 TYPE_RELAX=’ETCC_DIRECT’ In this case, the ETCC formula is applied, but the force used takes into account only the losses by friction and by anchorage slip (cf. § 4). It is necessary to specify the keyword NBH_RELAX (cf. § 2.12). 2.10.4 TYPE_RELAX=’ETCC_REPRISE’ In this case, the exact formula of the ETCC is applied. This implies carrying out a first analysis without relaxation and recovering the tension in the cable. Then one should define the cable as a function of MODI_CABLE_ETCC instead of DEFI_CABLE. It is necessary to specify the keyword NBH_RELAX (cf. § 2.12). 2.11 Operand R_J ◊ R_J = \mathit{rj} Parameter to be specified only if TYPE_RELAX=’BPEL’. Value of the dimensionless function r(j) characterising the evolution of the relaxation of the steel in time and of the steel only (this coefficient does not apply to the losses by creep or shrinkage of the concrete specified under BPEL_BETON in DEFI_MATERIAU); for example the BPEL 91 recommends: r(j)=\frac{j}{j+9\times {r}_{m}} with j in days and {r}_{m}=\frac{\text{aire de la section de béton}}{\text{périmètre de la section de béton}}\equiv \text{rayon moyen} This value must be positive or zero. j corresponds to the date (in days) for which one wants to estimate the stress state in the structure. For the case in which, in the structural analysis, the bars would be modelled with a constitutive behaviour of creep type, this keyword must not be specified in DEFI_CABLE_BP. 2.12 Operand NBH_RELAX ◊ NBH_RELAX = \mathit{nh} Parameter to be specified only if TYPE_RELAX=’ETCC_DIRECT’ or ’ETCC_REPRISE’. Time considered for taking into account the losses by relaxation of the steel in the ETCC, expressed as a number of hours. The formula applied is the following: \Delta {F}_{\mathit{pr}}=0,66.{\rho}_{1000}.{e}^{9,1\frac{\tilde{F}(s)}{{P}_{\mathit{pk}}}}.{\left(\frac{\mathit{nh}}{1000}\right)}^{0,75(1-\tilde{F}(s)/{P}_{\mathit{pk}})}.{10}^{-5}\tilde{F}(s) where: {\rho}_{1000} is the value of the relaxation coefficient of the steel at 1000 hours in %, specified under ETCC_ACIER. {P}_{\mathit{pk}} is the maximum tension of the steel at failure, computed from the datum F_PRG under ETCC_ACIER. \tilde{F} is equal to the tension computed according to the ETCC taking into account the losses by friction and by anchorage slip if TYPE_RELAX=’ETCC_DIRECT’, or the tension supplied by the user under MODI_CABLE_ETCC/TENSION in the other case. 2.13 Keyword CONE ♦ CONE This factor keyword makes it possible to define a geometric volume around the anchorages, and to assign, on output from AFFE_CHAR_MECA keyword RELA_CINE_BP, to all the nodes (concrete and cable) contained in this volume, a kinematic relation of type LIAISON_SOLIDE (rigid body). The definition of this volume makes it possible to attenuate the stresses which the tensions at the ends of the cables produce on the concrete. In reality, this phenomenon is avoided thanks to the installation of a stress-diffusion cone (material harder than the concrete) which distributes the prestressing force over a large area of the concrete. In practice, the cone being practically straight, one defines a cylindrical volume. | Real situation | Finite-element modelling | | --- | --- | Figure 1: use of a diffusion cone: real situation and modelling Note that several cones, and therefore several rigid blocks, are defined if the keyword PRESENT contains two ‘OUI’ (one block per end of the cable) or if several cables are defined under DEFI_CABLE. Note: In practice, the cylinder is defined by the command DEFI_GROUP option TUNNEL. The methodology for extracting the nodes contained in the cone is described in document U4.22.01 (command DEFI_GROUP). ♦ RAYON = rayon Radius of the cone. ♦ LONGUEUR = longueur Length of the cone, in the sense of the curvilinear abscissa on the cable. One defines the cone as a succession of cylinders, stopping when the total length of the cylinders is equal to the parameter longueur. ♦ PRESENT = l_pre This list must contain 2 arguments, no more and no less, and must be ordered with respect to the list of the nodes defining the anchorages (operand GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE above). The only valid arguments are ‘OUI’ or ‘NON’; they make it possible to define the cone on the two anchorages (PRESENT=(‘OUI’,‘OUI’,)), on the first anchorage (PRESENT=(‘OUI’,‘NON’,)) or on the second anchorage (PRESENT=(‘NON’,‘OUI’,)). Note that if several cables are defined in DEFI_CABLE then the first argument of PRESENT applies to all the first nodes which define the anchorages. Likewise for the second argument. 2.14 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = l_titr List of arguments of text type defining a title attached to the concept [cabl_precont]. 3 Theoretical complement: estimation of the tension losses in a prestressing cable according to the prescriptions of the BPEL In the case where the user has defined the material characteristics BPEL_BETON and BPEL_ACIER, the evolution of the tension (in newtons) along a prestressing cable is computed using the relations prescribed by the BPEL. These relations are the following. 3.1 Evolution of the tension in the vicinity of the anchorage The tension is written: F(s)=\tilde{F}(s)-\lbrace {x}_{\mathit{flu}}\times {F}_{0}+{x}_{\mathit{ret}}\times {F}_{0}+r(j)\times \frac{5}{100}\times {\rho}_{1000}\left[\frac{\tilde{F}(s)}{{S}_{a}\times {\sigma}_{y}}-{\mu}_{0}\right]\times \tilde{F}(s)\rbrace where s designates the curvilinear abscissa along the cable. The parameters introduced in this expression are: | {F}_{0} | initial tension (N); | | --- | --- | | {x}_{\mathrm{flu}} | lump-sum rate of tension loss by creep of the concrete, with respect to the initial tension; | | {x}_{\mathrm{ret}} | lump-sum rate of tension loss by shrinkage of the concrete, with respect to the initial tension; | | {\rho}_{1000} | relaxation of the steel at 1000 hours, expressed in %; | | {S}_{a} | area of the cross-section of the cable defined in AFFE_CARA_ELEM; | | {\sigma}_{y} | elastic limit stress of the steel; | | {\mu}_{0} | dimensionless relaxation coefficient of the prestressed steel. | r(j) is a dimensionless function characterising the evolution of the relaxation in time: r(j)=\frac{j}{j+9\times {r}_{m}} with j in days and {r}_{m}=\frac{\text{aire de la section de béton}}{\text{périmètre de la section de béton}}\equiv \text{rayon moyen} The function r(j) depending on the geometry of the structure, the value used is defined in the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP. \tilde{F}(s) is the evolution of the tension in the vicinity of the anchorage after taking into account the loss by anchorage slip and the losses by contact between the cable and the concrete. \tilde{F}(s) is defined by the relation: {F}_{c}(s)\times \tilde{F}(s)={\left[{F}_{c}(d)\right]}^{2} {F}_{c}(s) designates the evolution of the tension along the cable after taking into account the losses by contact between the cable and the concrete: {F}_{c}(s)={F}_{0}\exp\left(-f\alpha -\varphi s\right) \alpha designates the cumulative angular deviation and the parameters introduced in the expression of its {F}_{c}(s) t: f coefficient of friction between the cable and the sheath in the curved part, in rad–1; \varphi coefficient of friction between the cable and the sheath in m-1. Notes: - The coefficients f,\varphi ,{\rho}_{1000,}{\sigma}_{y},{\mu}_{0} are to be specified in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU under the keyword BPEL_ACIER, - {x}_{\mathit{flu}} and {x}_{\mathit{ret}} are to be specified in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU under the keyword BPEL_BETON. The length d appearing in the expression of \tilde{F}(s) is the length over which the tension loss by anchorage slip applies. This length is estimated with the help of the relation: {E}_{a}{S}_{a}\Delta ={\int}_{0}^{d}\left({F}_{c}(s)-\tilde{F}(s)\right)\mathit{ds} where {E}_{a} is the Young's modulus of the steel and \Delta the value of the anchorage slip. Thus {E}_{a}{S}_{a}\Delta represents the strain energy (of the cable) due to the anchorage slip. 3.2 Evolution of the tension beyond the length over which the tension losses by anchorage slip apply This tension is written: F(s)={F}_{c}(s)-\lbrace {x}_{\mathit{flu}}\times {F}_{0}+{x}_{\mathit{ret}}\times {F}_{0}+r(j)\times \frac{5}{100}\times {\rho}_{1000}\left[\frac{\tilde{F}(s)}{{S}_{a}\times {\sigma}_{y}}-{\mu}_{0}\right]\times \tilde{F}(s)\rbrace with the same notations as those introduced in the previous paragraph. 4 Theoretical complement: estimation of the tension losses in a prestressing cable according to the prescriptions of the ETCC In the case where the user has defined the material characteristics ETCC_BETON and ETCC_ACIER, the evolution of the tension (in newtons) along a prestressing cable is computed using the relations prescribed by the ETCC. However, the losses due to the elastic strain of the concrete and to the strains due to the shrinkage and to the creep of the concrete are not taken into account in the analysis. If one wants to take them into account, one should: - tension the cables in 2 families in order to recover the losses due to the elastic strain of the concrete - impose on the concrete the shrinkage and creep strains, after the tensioning of the cables. The relations implemented are the following. 4.1 Evolution of the tension in the vicinity of the anchorage It is written: F(s)=\tilde{F}(s)-0,8\Delta {F}_{\mathit{pr}}(s) with \tilde{F}(s) is the evolution of the tension in the vicinity of the anchorage after taking into account the loss by anchorage slip and the losses by contact between the cable and the concrete. \tilde{F}(s) is defined by the relation: {F}_{c}(s)\times \tilde{F}(s)={\left[{F}_{c}(d)\right]}^{2} {F}_{c}(s) designates the evolution of the tension along the cable after taking into account the losses by contact between the cable and the concrete: {F}_{c}(s)={F}_{0}{\exp}^{-\mu (\alpha +ks)} \alpha designates the cumulative angular deviation and the parameters introduced in the expression of its {F}_{c}(s) are: - \mu [:ref: {\mathit{rad}}^{-1} ] the coefficient of friction between the cable and the sheath; k[{\mathit{rad}}^{-1}.{m}^{-1}] the coefficient of loss per unit length. The length d appearing in the expression of \tilde{F}(s) is the length over which the tension loss by anchorage slip applies. This length is estimated with the help of the relation: {E}_{a}{S}_{a}\Delta ={\int}_{0}^{d}({F}_{c}(s)-\tilde{F}(s))\mathrm{ds} where {E}_{a} is the Young's modulus of the steel and \Delta the value of the anchorage slip. Thus {E}_{a}{S}_{a}\Delta represents the strain energy (of the cable) due to the anchorage slip. \Delta {F}_{\mathit{pr}} are the losses due to the relaxation of the cables, estimated by the following formula \Delta {F}_{\mathit{pr}}(s)=0,66.{\rho}_{1000}.{e}^{9,1\frac{\tilde{F}(s)}{{P}_{\mathit{pk}}}}.{\left(\frac{\mathit{nh}}{1000}\right)}^{0,75(1-\tilde{F}(s)/{P}_{\mathit{pk}})}.{10}^{-5}\tilde{{F}_{(s)}} s designates the curvilinear abscissa along the cable. The parameters introduced in this expression are: | {\rho}_{1000} | Relaxation of the steel at 1000 hours, expressed in %. | | --- | --- | | {P}_{\mathit{pk}} | Force at failure in the steel (computed from the parameter F_PRG specified in DEFI_MATERIAU/ETCC_ACIER) | | \mathit{nh} | The number of hours after the prestressing at which the losses are computed. | Notes: - The coefficients \mu ,k,{\rho}_{1000,}{F}_{\mathit{prg}} are to be specified in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU under the keyword BPEL_ACIER, - \mathit{nh} is to be specified in the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP. 4.2 Evolution of the tension beyond the length over which the tension losses by anchorage slip apply One writes the following relation: F(s)={F}_{c}(s)-0,8\ast 0,66{\rho}_{1000}.{\exp}^{9,1{F}_{c}(s)/{F}_{\mathit{prg}}}.{\left(\frac{\mathit{nh}}{1000}\right)}^{0,75(1-{F}_{c}(s))/{F}_{\mathit{prg}}}.{10}^{-5}{F}_{c}(s) With the same notations as those introduced in the previous paragraph. 5 Example See the test SSNV164 for an application, and documents U2.03.06 and U4.42.05 in order to know more precisely how to tension the prestressing cables. See the test SSNV229 for an example of taking into account the relaxation of the steel according to the ETCC, according to the 2 possible methods, but also for the definition of the cables via a table. Modelling C makes it possible to validate the procedure for simulating the failure of a cable with re-anchoring. See the test ZZZZ347 for an example of use with the modelling CABLE_GAINE.

u4.42.05 Macro-command CALC_PRECONT u4.42.05 Macro-command CALC_PRECONT Summary This macro-command makes it possible to tension the cables in a structure, in such a way that, at the end of this analysis, the structure is in equilibrium and the tension is equal to the tension given by the BPEL91 rules, computed by the command DEFI_CABLE_BP. It also makes it possible: - to apply the prestressing progressively, so as to be able to treat the case in which the concrete will plasticise or be damaged according to the constitutive model adopted, - to carry out the phasing of the prestressing, that is to say the tensioning of the cables in a sequential way. In this tensioning phase, the constitutive behaviour of the steel is considered as purely elastic. choix possibles 2 Operands 2.1 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM ♦ MODELE = mo Name of the model whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. ♦ CHAM_MATER = chmat Name of the material field assigned on the mesh. Warning: all the mesh cells of the model must be associated with a material. ♦ CARA_ELEM = carac Name of the characteristics of the shell, beam, pipe, bar, cable and discrete elements assigned on the model mo. 2.2 Operand DOUBLE_LAGRANGE This keyword makes it possible to say whether or not the user wishes to double the Lagrange multipliers used in order to define the dualisation of the boundary conditions in the assembled matrix. Concretely, doubling the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to use linear solvers which do not allow pivoting. Not doubling the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the problem (and therefore the size of the problem to be solved), but its use is limited to the solvers MUMPS and Petsc. Note that the two Lagrange multipliers associated with the relation will be such that the first will be located before all the terms involved in the relation and the second after, in the assembled matrix. This choice has the advantage of having an assembled matrix whose storage size is smaller, but has the disadvantage of being able to make a singularity appear in the matrix. The numbering being in any case liable to be modified by the renumberer of the external solver chosen, this detail therefore remains purely technical. 2.3 Keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT = This factor keyword makes it possible to describe, at each occurrence, a load. One must supply the boundary conditions for the structure, possibly instantaneous loadings such as gravity, as well as the kinematic links linked to the cables which have already been tensioned by a previous call to CALC_PRECONT. In no case must one include the loading of the cable (or cables) that one wants to tension by the call to this macro-command, nor the loadings linked to the cable (or cables) declared inactive. 2.3.1 Operands CHARGE ♦ CHARGE = chi chi is the mechanical loading specified at the i -th occurrence of EXCIT. 2.4 Keyword COMPORTEMENT The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.11. 2.5 Keyword INCREMENT ♦ INCREMENT = Defines the time intervals taken in the incremental method. 2.5.1 Operands LIST_INST ♦LIST_INST = /litpsr8, listr8 /litps, [list_inst] ♦ Si LIST_INST = litpsr8 listr8 The analysis time instants are those defined in the concept litpsr8 by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. > ♦ If LIST_INST = litps [list_inst] The analysis time instants are those defined in the concept litps by the operator DEFI_LIST_INST [U4.34.03]. Remarque: In the case of bonded cables (ADHERENT=’OUI’ in DEFI_CABLE_BP), even if the analysis is carried out with several time steps, only the last time step is stored in the result concept. In the course of the process of tensioning the cables, time instants are generated automatically in addition to those supplied by the user. It is therefore entirely normal to see appear, in the message file, analyses with STAT_NON_LINE at time instants that the user has not specified. These time instants are also stored in the result concept. 2.5.2 Operands INST_INIT / INST_FIN ◊ INST_INIT = instini The initial time instant of the analysis (which therefore is not (re)computed) must be designated by its value. If this initial time instant is not specified, the default is computed in the following way: - if an initial state is specified (operand ETAT_INIT) and if it defines a corresponding time instant (by EVOL_NOLI or INST_ETAT_INIT), then the initial time instant is that defined by the initial state, - if there is no initial state, or if it does not define a corresponding time instant (the fields are given in ETAT_INIT without specifying INST_ETAT_INIT), then one takes the first time instant of the list of time instants litps (NUME_INST_INIT =0). ◊ INST_FIN = instfin The final time instant (last step computed) is designated in the same way as the initial time instant, except that it is not possible to refer to the time instant of the initial state. 2.5.3 Operand PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = prec 2.6 Keyword CABLE_BP ♦ CABLE_BP = cabl_pr Here one must supply a list of the concepts of type cabl_precont produced by the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP U4.42.04. All the cables concerned will be tensioned at the end of this analysis. 2.7 Keyword CABLE_BP_INACTIF ◊ CABLE_BP_INACTIF = cabl_pr Here one must supply a list of the concepts of type cabl_precont produced by the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP U4.42.04. The macro-command takes care of generating the kinematic links linked to these inactive cables, and does not take into account the stiffness of these cables. 2.8 Keyword METHODE ◊ METHODE = /NEWTON , [DEFAUT] /IMPLEX , This keyword makes it possible to define the method of solution of the problem. By default, it is the exact iterative Newton method which is used. If the user so wishes, the robust but approximate method IMPLEX can be used. 2.9 Keyword NEWTON The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.03. It can be used only if the method requested is NEWTON. 2.10 Keyword ETAT_INIT The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.03. 2.11 Keyword RECH_LINEAIRE The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.03. 2.12 Keyword SOLVEUR The syntax of this keyword, common to several commands, is described in document U4.50.01. 2.13 Keyword CONVERGENCE The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.03. 2.14 Keyword ARCHIVAGE The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.03. 2.15 Keyword ENERGIE This keyword makes it possible to activate the computation of the energy balance and its display in the course of the analysis of the stages of prestressing of the concrete and of the switch-over of the external forces into internal forces (see document R4.09.01). This balance is stored in the table of name PARA_CALC, from which it can be extracted with the help of the command RECU_TABLE [U4.71.02]. The balance at the last time instant corresponds only to the energy balance of the stage of the switch-over of the external forces into internal forces. As mentioned in the doc [R7.01,02], this stage is a numerical device serving to make it possible to continue the analysis afterwards, and therefore the energy balance there is negligible. The energy balance at the end of the prestressing phase is that observed at the previous time instant. 2.16 Operand INFO The syntax of this keyword, common to the command STAT_NON_LINE, is described in document U4.51.03. 2.17 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = tx tx is the title of the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results. See U4.03.01. 3 Example The principal stages of an analysis of a structure containing prestressing cables are detailed here (test case SSNV164) 3.1 Before using the macro-command - Definition of the cables In the event of non-simultaneous tensioning of all the cables, it is necessary to make (at least) as many DEFI_CABLE_BP as there are loading stages. CAB_BP1=DEFI_CABLE_BP(MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, GROUP_MA_BETON='VOLTOT', DEFI_CABLE=(_F(GROUP_MA='CAB1', GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE=('PC1D','PC1F',), TYPE_ANCRAGE=('ACTIF','PASSIF',),), _F(GROUP_MA='CAB2', GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE=('PC2D','PC2F',), TYPE_ANCRAGE=('ACTIF','PASSIF',),),), TENSION_INIT=3.750000E6, RECUL_ANCRAGE=0.001,) CAB_BP3=DEFI_CABLE_BP( MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, GROUP_MA_BETON='VOLTOT', DEFI_CABLE=(_F(GROUP_MA='CAB3', GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE=('PC3D','PC3F',), TYPE_ANCRAGE=('ACTIF','PASSIF',),), _F(GROUP_MA='CAB4', GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE=('PC4D','PC4F',), TYPE_ANCRAGE=('ACTIF','PASSIF',),),), TENSION_INIT=3.750000E6, RECUL_ANCRAGE=0.001,) CAB_BP5=DEFI_CABLE_BP(MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, GROUP_MA_BETON='VOLTOT', DEFI_CABLE=_F(GROUP_MA='CAB5', GROUP_NO_ANCRAGE=('PC5D','PC5F',), TYPE_ANCRAGE=('ACTIF','ACTIF',),), TENSION_INIT=3.750000E6, RECUL_ANCRAGE=0.001, ) - Definition of the loadings One must distinguish: - the loadings linked to the boundary conditions plus any instantaneous loadings, - the loadings linked to the cables containing only the kinematic links, - the non-instantaneous loadings subsequent to the tensioning of the cables. CLIM =AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MO, DDL_IMPO=( _F(GROUP_NO='PP', DX=0.0,DY=0.0,), _F(GROUP_NO='PX', DY=0.0,), _F(GROUP_NO='PY', DX=0.0,), _F(GROUP_NO='SU3', DZ=0.0,), ), PESANTEUR=(9.81,0.0,0.0,-1.0,), ) CMCAB1=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MO, RELA_CINE_BP=_F(CABLE_BP=CAB_BP1, SIGM_BPEL='NON', RELA_CINE='OUI',),) CMCAB3=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MO, RELA_CINE_BP=_F(CABLE_BP=CAB_BP3, SIGM_BPEL='NON', RELA_CINE='OUI',),) CMCAB5=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MO, RELA_CINE_BP=_F(CABLE_BP=CAB_BP5, SIGM_BPEL='NON', RELA_CINE='OUI',),) CHMECA =AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MO, DDL_IMPO=_F(GROUP_NO='SU2', DZ=1.0,), ) - Preliminary analysis before tensioning of the cables (optional) Here one takes into account the loadings which apply to the structure before the tensioning of the cables. In order not to take into account the stiffness of the cables, and not to introduce a loading on the cables, one must carry out the analysis either on a model which does not contain the cables, or by assigning to them a constitutive law SANS, which imposes that the stress remains zero in these elements. RES1 = STAT_NON_LINE(MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, COMPORTEMENT=(_F( RELATION = 'ELAS',), _F( RELATION = 'SANS', GROUP_MA= ('CAB1' ,'CAB3', 'CAB5'),),), EXCIT =(_F(CHARGE = CLIM,), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB1), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB3), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB5),), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST = LINST, INST_FIN = 150.),) 3.2 Use of the macro-command: successive tensioning of the 5 cables One calls upon the macro-command as many times as necessary. RES1 = CALC_PRECONT ( reuse=RES1, ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=RES1), MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, COMPORTEMENT=(_F( RELATION = 'ELAS',),), EXCIT =(_F(CHARGE = CLIM,),), CABLE_BP =(CAB_BP1,), CABLE_BP_INACTIF = (CAB_BP3, CAB_BP5,), INCREMENT=_F( LIST_INST = LINST, INST_FIN = 300., ),) RES1 = CALC_PRECONT ( reuse=RES1, ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=RES1), MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, COMPORTEMENT=(_F(RELATION = 'ELAS',),), EXCIT =(_F(CHARGE = CLIM,), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB1,), CABLE_BP =(CAB_BP3,), CABLE_BP_INACTIF = (CAB_BP5,), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST = LINST, INST_FIN = 450., ),) RES1 = CALC_PRECONT ( reuse=RES1, ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=RES1), MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, COMPORTEMENT=(_F( RELATION = 'ELAS',),), EXCIT =(_F(CHARGE = CLIM,), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB1,), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB3,), CABLE_BP =(CAB_BP5,), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST = LINST, INST_FIN = 600., ),) 3.3 Continuation of the loading after tensioning of the cables The cables being tensioned, one has only to continue the analysis, always including the kinematic links binding the nodes of the cable to the concrete. RES1 = STAT_NON_LINE(reuse = RES1, ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=RES1), MODELE=MO, CHAM_MATER=CMAT, CARA_ELEM=CE, COMPORTEMENT=_F( RELATION = 'ELAS'), EXCIT =(_F(CHARGE = CLIM,), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB1), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB3), _F(CHARGE = CMCAB5), _F(CHARGE=CHMECA, FONC_MULT = FCT,), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST = LINST,),)

u4.42.08 Macro-command CALC_ENDO u4.42.08 Macro-command CALC_ENDO Summary: This macro-command makes it possible to facilitate the data setup of a viscous-damage analysis. As for any non-linear mechanical analysis, the loading is discretised into physical time instants supplied by the user. For each of these physical time instants, CALC_ENDO calls STAT_NON_LINE in order to compute a fictitious loading sequence, composed of a loading ramp and a stabilisation phase. This stabilisation phase ends when a stabilisation criterion is satisfied. CALC_ENDO produces a result concept in which these stabilised time instants are saved. optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Principle This macro-command aims to simplify the data setup of viscous-damage analyses. In such an analysis, the viscosity refers to: - the viscous damage. It makes it possible to pass through instabilities linked to the sudden propagation of the damage, and is available only for certain constitutive laws ( ENDO_LOCA_TC and ENDO_FISS_TC ). - the viscous regularisation (see REGU_VISC). It makes it possible to stabilise the fully damaged elements. Note that, in order to be able to use CALC_ENDO , the characteristic viscosity times of these two phenomena must necessarily be set to 0 (no viscosity) or to 1. The introduction of these numerical viscosities into the model leads to a delay in the propagation of the damage. In the case of a loading which is a function of time, it is necessary to let the damage stabilise before applying the next loading increment. Thus, the loading transient is divided into several fictitious loading sequences. A fictitious loading sequence corresponds to a ramp phase in which one applies the loading increment. There then follows a stabilisation phase, in which the loading is frozen until the stabilisation criterion is reached. This principle is illustrated in Figure 1. The stabilisation criterion is checked by means of OBSERVATION carried out in the course of the fictitious non-linear analysis. Figure 1: Discretisation of the loading. On the left, as a function of physical time. On the right, for a fictitious loading sequence. Once the analysis has stabilised, one saves the last time instant in the output result concept of the macro-command, and one moves on to the next fictitious loading sequence. The macro-command CALC_ENDO makes it possible to greatly facilitate the implementation of such an analysis, by carrying out all the operations described previously and by calling STAT_NON_LINE as many times as necessary, automatically. The syntax of CALC_ENDO is therefore very similar to that of STAT_NON_LINE . Note Piloting of the loading is incompatible with the use of a numerical viscosity and is therefore not available in CALC_ENDO . Note For the moment, it is not possible to use a loading which is a function of time by means of the commands AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F or AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F . One must necessarily use FONC_MULT in the definition of the loading (see STAT_NON_LINE) Note Any command variables which are a function of time are treated as a loading which is a function of time. In a fictitious loading sequence, these command variables evolve during the ramp phase, and are frozen during the stabilisation phase. - a list of physical time instants. For each physical time instant, CALC_ENDO will compute a fictitious loading sequence. This list of time instants is defined by means of the factor keyword INCREMENT (see STAT_NON_LINE). Any parameterisation of this list of time instants by means of DEFI_LIST_INST is not taken into account. - a list of fictitious time instants, which describes the fictitious loading sequence. This list of time instants is defined by the keyword LIST_INST under the factor keyword ENDO_VISC . Any parameterisation of this list of time instants by means of DEFI_LIST_INST is taken into account. Note It can be seen that the user must define two lists of time instants: 3 Operands For the most part, the syntax of CALC_ENDO is identical to that of STAT_NON_LINE (see STAT_NON_LINE). Only the specific features of CALC_ENDO are described below. 3.1 Keyword INCREMENT This keyword makes it possible to describe the time discretisation of the physical time instants, for which a fictitious loading sequence will be computed. Its syntax is identical to that of STAT_NON_LINE (see STAT_NON_LINE). Note that any parameterisation of the list of time instants by means of the command DEFI_LIST_INST is not taken into account. 3.2 Keyword ARCHIVAGE This keyword makes it possible to describe the archiving of the physical time instants. Its syntax is identical to that of STAT_NON_LINE . (see STAT_NON_LINE). 3.3 Keyword OBSERVATION This keyword makes it possible to describe the observations carried out for each fictitious analysis time instant. The syntax is identical to that of STAT_NON_LINE . (see STAT_NON_LINE). Some of these observations may be used to evaluate a stabilisation criterion after each stabilisation phase. In this case, the titles of these observations must be declared in the keyword OBSERVATION under the factor keyword ENDO_VISC. Note that it must be a scalar (the maximum, the minimum or the mean of a field, for example). 3.4 Keyword ENDO_VISC ◆ ENDO_VISC = _F( ◆ LIST_INST = list_inst / listr8, ◇ & OBSERVATION = list[text], & PREC_STAB = list[float], ◇ ARRET = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ TABLE = co, ◇ RESULTAT = co, ), 3.4.1 Keyword LIST_INST This mandatory keyword makes it possible to define the time discretisation of a fictitious loading sequence. This list must necessarily contain three reals: - the duration of a fictitious loading ramp. - the duration of a fictitious ramp added to that of a unit stabilisation phase. The stabilisation criterion will be evaluated after each unit stabilisation phase. If the analysis is not stabilised, another stabilisation phase will be computed. - the maximum total duration that a fictitious loading sequence may last. This list is therefore necessarily increasing. This list of time instants may come from the commands (either one): - DEFI_LIST_INST . In this case, CALC_ENDO will use, in the calls to STAT_NON_LINE , the parameterisation of the list of time instants supplied by the user. - DEFI_LIST_REEL . In this case, CALC_ENDO will use a default parameterisation of the subdivision of the time step, suited to the constitutive laws ENDO_LOCA_TC and ENDO_FISS_TC , in order to guarantee a continuous evolution of the damage. 3.4.2 Keyword OBSERVATION This optional keyword makes it possible to define the list of observation titles used for the evaluation of the stabilisation criterion. In the absence of this keyword, the stabilisation criterion is evaluated from the viscous stresses, on the basis of two observations: - the maximum of the difference between the internal variable SIGMVISC (laws ENDO_LOCA_TC and ENDO_FISS_TC ) and the stress which would have been computed in the absence of viscosity. This observation is named VISCENDO . - the maximum of the viscous stress of REGU_VISC . This observation is named VISCELAS . By default, these two observations are compared with 1% of the parameter f_t . If the user supplies additional observations whose title is VISCELAS or VISCENDO , then these default observations are overwritten. If the titles differ from VISCELAS or VISCENDO , then these additional observations are added to the default observations. 3.4.3 Keyword PREC_STAB This optional keyword makes it possible to supply the list of real values with which the observations will be compared for the stabilisation criterion. This list must necessarily be supplied if OBSERVATION is present. It must be of the same length as that supplied in OBSERVATION . 3.4.4 Keyword RESULTAT This optional keyword makes it possible to create a dictionary-of-results concept ( evol_noli concepts) containing the fictitious time instants of each loading sequence. The dictionary is indexed by the number of the loading sequence. This keyword is mandatory if one wishes to archive these fictitious time instants (see ARCHIVAGE_VISC ). 3.4.5 Keyword ARRET This optional keyword makes it possible to continue or to stop the analysis if the stabilisation criteria are not satisfied at the end of the fictitious loading sequence. By default, this parameter is equal to OUI and the analysis stops in error. If this parameter is equal to NON , one moves on to the next loading sequence even if the criterion is not satisfied. 3.4.6 Keyword TABLE This optional keyword makes it possible to recover, in the form of a table, all the observations (the default ones and those defined by the user). This table is indexed, among other things, by two parameters INST and INST_VISC . The first corresponds to the physical time instants, the second to the fictitious time instants. 3.5 Keyword ARCHIVAGE_VISC This optional keyword makes it possible to describe the archiving of the fictitious time instants for each loading sequence. Its syntax is identical to that of ARCHIVAGE in STAT_NON_LINE . (see STAT_NON_LINE). By default, these fictitious time instants are not archived. If one wishes to archive them, then the keyword RESULTAT under ENDO_VISC is mandatory. 4 Examples of use 4.1 Default parameters evol_me = CALC_ENDO( MODELE=mo_me, CHAM_MATER=mate_me, CARA_ELEM=cara_me, EXCIT=_F(CHARGE=liaison_me, FONC_MULT=fonction_charge), COMPORTEMENT=( _F(GROUP_MA="massif", RELATION="ENDO_LOCA_TC", REGU_VISC="OUI"), _F(GROUP_MA="coque", RELATION="VMIS_ISOT_LINE", RESI_CPLAN_MAXI=r_conv / 100), _F(GROUP_MA="grille", RELATION="GRILLE_ISOT_LINE"), _F(GROUP_MA="grille_excentree", RELATION="GRILLE_ISOT_LINE"), _F(GROUP_MA="barre", RELATION="VMIS_ISOT_LINE"), _F(GROUP_MA="ressort", RELATION="ELAS"), ), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=inst_me), NEWTON=_F(MATRICE="TANGENTE"), SOLVEUR=_F(ELIM_LAGR="NON"), CONVERGENCE=_F( RESI_REFE_RELA=r_conv, EPSI_REFE=1.0e-3, SIGM_REFE=b_ft, EFFORT_REFE=700, MOMENT_REFE=4900, ITER_GLOB_MAXI=10, ), ENDO_VISC=_F(LIST_INST=inst_visc, TABLE=CO("tab_obs")), ) The syntax is identical to that of STAT_NON_LINE , with the exception of the keyword ENDO_VISC . The physical time discretisation is described under the keyword INCREMENT , by the list inst_me . All the physical time instants are archived by default. The discretisation of a loading sequence is described under the keyword ENDO_VISC , by the list inst_visc . The default parameters are those used for the evaluation of the stabilisation criteria and the parameterisation of the time step. The variable tab_obs will contain a concept of type TABLE containing all the observations of the analysis. 4.2 Advanced parameters evol_me = CALC_ENDO( MODELE=mo_me, CHAM_MATER=mate_me, CARA_ELEM=cara_me, EXCIT=_F(CHARGE=liaison_me, FONC_MULT=fonction_charge), COMPORTEMENT=( _F(GROUP_MA="massif", RELATION="ENDO_LOCA_TC", REGU_VISC="OUI"), _F(GROUP_MA="coque", RELATION="VMIS_ISOT_LINE", RESI_CPLAN_MAXI=r_conv / 100), _F(GROUP_MA="grille", RELATION="GRILLE_ISOT_LINE"), _F(GROUP_MA="grille_excentree", RELATION="GRILLE_ISOT_LINE"), _F(GROUP_MA="barre", RELATION="VMIS_ISOT_LINE"), _F(GROUP_MA="ressort", RELATION="ELAS"), ), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=inst_me), NEWTON=_F(MATRICE="TANGENTE"), SOLVEUR=_F(ELIM_LAGR="NON"), CONVERGENCE=_F( RESI_REFE_RELA=r_conv, EPSI_REFE=1.0e-3, SIGM_REFE=b_ft, EFFORT_REFE=700, MOMENT_REFE=4900, ITER_GLOB_MAXI=10, ), OBSERVATION=( _F( TITRE="ENDO_MOY", PAS_OBSE=1, NOM_CHAM="VARI_ELGA", NOM_CMP=(vari_trac, vari_comp), GROUP_MA="massif", EVAL_CMP="FORMULE", FORMULE=f_endo, EVAL_ELGA="MAX", EVAL_CHAM="MOY", ), _F( TITRE="VISCENDO", PAS_OBSE=1, NOM_CHAM="VARI_ELGA", NOM_CMP=vari_visc, GROUP_MA="massif", EVAL_ELGA="MAX", EVAL_CHAM="MAX", ), _F( TITRE="VISCELAS", PAS_OBSE=1, NOM_CHAM="VARI_ELGA", NOM_CMP=vari_ener_visc_elas, GROUP_MA="massif", EVAL_CMP="FORMULE", FORMULE=f_sigm_visc, EVAL_ELGA="MAX", EVAL_CHAM="MAX", ), ), ENDO_VISC=_F( LIST_INST=inst_visc, OBSERVATION=["VISCENDO", "VISCELAS"], PREC_STAB=[r_stab b_ft] 2, TABLE=CO("tab_obs"), RESULTAT=CO("d_evol"), ), ARCHIVAGE_VISC=_F(PAS_ARCH=1), ) Here, one defines two observations VISCENDO and VISCELAS for the evaluation of the stabilisation criterion. The observation ENDO_MOY will be present in the output table, but will not be used for the evaluation of the criterion. One furthermore requests the archiving of all the fictitious analysis time instants, contained in a results dictionary d_evol .

Characteristics from a table Definition of the constant or function linear elastic characteristics. The keyword TABLE simplifies the writing of DEFI_MATERIAU for certain constitutive behaviours (COMPOR) by reading the data from a table. The TABLE is used to create functions. The parameters are stored in columns, with an additional column giving the abscissa of the functions that are created (NOM_PARA). For example, the following table makes it possible to define an elastic constitutive behaviour. | TEMP | E | NU | RHO | ALPHA | TEMP_DEF_ALPHA | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 20 | 200 | 0,3 | 1000 | 1,E-5 | 20,0 | | 50 | 190 | 0,3 | 1000 | 1,E-5 | 20,0 | 4 General elastic characteristics 4.1 Factor keywords ELAS, ELAS_FO Definition of the constant or function linear elastic characteristics. Most of the functions may depend on the command variables (see U4.43.03) or on other parameters such as time ('INST' or the geometry 'X', 'Y', 'Z') 'TEMP', 'HYDR', 'SECH', 'NEUT1', 'NEUT2', 'X', 'Y', 'Z',… Warning! For the geometry, there are two cases: - The direct variables 'X', 'Y', 'Z', which work only in a few particular cases; - The command variable 'GEOM', which is more general; 4.1.1 Operands E/NU, K/MU, CELE_P/CELE_S One of the three pairs (E, NU), (K, MU) or (CELE_P, CELE_S) must be supplied. E is Young's modulus. One checks that E \ge 0 . NU is Poisson's ratio. One checks that -1. \le \nu \le 0.5 . If one supplies (K, MU= \mu ), one assigns instead: \begin{split}\begin{array}{l} E = \frac{9 K \mu}{3 K + \mu} \\ \nu = \frac{3 K - 2 \mu}{6 K + 2 \mu} \end{array}\end{split} If one supplies (CELE_P= V_P , CELE_S= V_S ) then RHO is necessary and one assigns instead: \begin{split}\begin{array}{l} E = \frac{\rho {V_S}^2 ( 3 {V_P}^2 - 4 {V_S}^2)} {{V_P}^2 - {V_S}^2} \\ \nu = \frac{{V_P}^2 - 2 {V_S}^2}{2 ({V_P}^2 - {V_S}^2)} \end{array}\end{split} 4.1.2 Operand RHO Density. No check of the order of magnitude. Warning: for THM modellings in statics, only the homogenised density entered under THM_DIFFU (cf. section 10.7.2 ) will be taken into account. For THM modellings in dynamics, this value must on the contrary be entered here and be consistent with that indicated under THM_DIFFU. This keyword can be a function only of the geometry via the command variable 'GEOM'. 4.1.3 Operands ALPHA/TEMP_DEF_ALPHA/PRECISION Isotropic thermal expansion coefficient. The thermal expansion coefficient is a mean expansion coefficient which may depend on the temperature T . The values of the expansion coefficients are determined by dilatometry tests which take place at ambient temperature ( 0°C or more generally 20°C ). As a result, one generally has available the values of the expansion coefficient defined with respect to 20°C (the temperature at which the thermal strain is assumed to be zero). Certain studies require a reference temperature different from the ambient temperature (thermal strain zero for a temperature other than the ambient temperature). One must then carry out a change of reference frame in the computation of the thermal strain R4.08.01. TEMP_DEF_ALPHA is the value of the temperature at which the values of the thermal expansion coefficient were determined, and were entered under the keyword ALPHA. This keyword becomes mandatory as soon as one has entered ALPHA. For non-THM constitutive behaviours, the thermal strain is computed by the formula R4.08.01: {e}^{\mathit{th}}\left(T\right)=\widehat{\alpha}\left(T\right)\left(T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}}\right) with \widehat{\alpha}\left(T\right)=\frac{\alpha \left(T\right)\left(T-{T}_{\text{def}}\right)-\alpha \left({T}_{\mathit{ref}}\right)\left({T}_{\mathit{ref}}-{T}_{\text{def}}\right)}{T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}}} and {e}^{\mathit{th}}\left({T}_{\mathit{ref}}\right)=0 Note It is not possible to use a formula or a nappe for ALPHA, because of the modifications to be taken into account described above. The parameter ALPHA can depend ONLY on the temperature and provided that it is a function. The user, if wishing to use a formula, must first tabulate it by means of the command CALC_FONC_INTERP. This keyword is used when the keyword TEMP_DEF_ALPHA is specified. It is a real which indicates with what precision a temperature {T}_{i} (from the list of temperatures used to define \alpha {\left({T}_{i}\right)}_{i=1,N} ) is close to the reference temperature {T}_{\text{ref}} . This real is used for the computation of the function \widehat{\alpha}\left({T}_{i}\right) . The mathematical formula allowing the computation of \widehat{\alpha}\left({T}_{i}\right) differs according to whether {T}_{i}\ne {T}_{\text{ref}} or {T}_{i}={T}_{\text{ref}} . In THM, the computation of the thermal strain is different (see R4.08.01). The thermal strain is evaluated by the following formula: {e}^{\mathit{th}}\left(T\right)=\alpha \left(T-{T}_{\mathit{ini}}\right) In particular, one does not use TEMP_DEF_ALPHA (but one must enter it) and ALPHA cannot be a function; it is necessarily a constant. Moreover, the reference temperature is given by THM_INIT/TEMP. 4.1.4 Operands AMOR_ALPHA/AMOR_BETA/AMOR_HYST AMOR_ALPHA = a_alpha AMOR_BETA = a_beta Coefficients \alpha and \beta making it possible to build a viscous damping matrix proportional to the stiffness and/or to the mass [C]=\alpha [K]+\beta [M] . One will refer to the documents on the modelling of mechanical damping [U2.06.03] and R5.05.04. AMOR_HYST = eta Hysteretic damping coefficient \eta making it possible to define the complex Young's modulus (viscoelastic material) from which the complex stiffness matrix will be created, allowing the computation of the harmonic response U2.06.03 and R5.05.04. - The presence of the keywords AMOR_ALPHA and AMOR_BETA associated with a zero value may lead, in certain algorithms, to assembling a damping matrix and thus generates additional computation costs. - These keywords may depend on the geometry via the direct variables 'X', 'Y' and 'Z' but not on the command variable 'GEOM'. Notes: 4.1.5 Operands COEF_AMOR /LONG_CARA For the justification of the use of these operands, one will refer to the documents on the modelling of absorbing boundary elements R4.02.05. COEF_AMOR = coeam Coefficient appearing in the expression of the stress vector integrated along the absorbing boundary of the finite-element domain and which corresponds to viscous dampers distributed along this boundary: {\mathrm{t}}_{0}=\mathit{coeam}(\rho {c}_{P}\frac{\partial {u}_{3}}{\partial t}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}+\rho {c}_{S}\frac{\partial {\mathrm{u}}^{'}}{\partial t}) This term is assigned to the constitutive material of the absorbing-boundary element. LONG_CARA = lcara Coefficient corresponding to a characteristic dimension L . Associated with the Lamé coefficients \lambda and \mu , this coefficient appears in the expression of the added term of the stress vector integrated along the absorbing boundary of the finite-element domain, which corresponds to stiffnesses distributed along this boundary of the finite-element domain: {\mathrm{t}}_{1}=\frac{\lambda +2\mu }{L}{u}_{3}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}+\frac{\mu}{L}{\mathrm{u}}^{'} This term is assigned to the constitutive material of the absorbing-boundary element. Note The absence of the keyword LONG_CARA has the effect that no added stiffness is assigned on the absorbing boundary. 4.1.6 Operands K_DESSIC/B_ENDOGE K_DESSIC = k Desiccation shrinkage coefficient. K_ENDOGE = e Autogenous shrinkage coefficient. These characteristics are used with the constitutive behaviours of concrete (see ref. [R7.01.12]). 4.2 Keyword ELAS_VISCO The keyword ELAS_VISCO makes it possible to define isotropic viscoelastic materials for a given frequency. It is simply the definition of an elastic material whose elastic moduli are complex. 4.2.1 Operands G/NU G = g Complex shear modulus. NU = nu Complex Poisson's ratio. Note In the command file one must necessarily enter complex numbers even if the imaginary part is zero; for example if nu is real, one must enter complex(nu, 0). 4.2.2 Operand RHO RHO = rho Density. No check of the order of magnitude. 4.3 Factor keyword ELAS_FLUI The keyword ELAS_FLUI makes it possible to define the equivalent density of a tubular structure with internal and external fluid, taking the confinement effect into account. This operation falls within the study of the dynamic behaviour of a configuration of the type "tube bundle under cross-flow". The study of the behaviour of the bundle is reduced to the study of a single tube representative of the whole bundle. Cf. U4.35.02. The equivalent density of the structure {\rho}_{\mathit{eq}} is defined by: \begin{array}{cc}{\rho}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{1}{({d}_{e}^{2}-{d}_{i}^{2})}\left[{\rho}_{\mathrm{i.}}{d}_{i}^{2}+{\rho}_{\mathrm{t.}}({d}_{e}^{2}-{d}_{i}^{2})+{\rho}_{e}.{d}_{e}^{2}\right]& \\ {d}_{\mathrm{eq}}^{2}=\frac{2.{C}_{m}.{d}_{e}^{2}}{\pi}& \end{array} {\rho}_{i} , {\rho}_{e} , {\rho}_{t} are respectively the density of the fluid, of the external fluid and of the structure. {d}_{e} , {d}_{i} are respectively the external and internal diameter of the tube. {C}_{m} is an added-mass coefficient (which defines the confinement). 4.3.1 Operands RHO/E/NU RHO = rho Density of the material. E = yg Young's modulus. NU = nu Poisson's ratio. 4.3.2 Operands PROF_RHO_F_INT/PROF_RHO_F_EXIT/COEF_MASS_AJOU PROF_RHO_F_INT = rhoi Concept of type [fonction] defining the density profile of the internal fluid along the tube. This function is parameterised by the curvilinear abscissa. PROF_RHO_F_EXT = rhoe Concept of type [fonction] defining the density profile of the external fluid along the tube. This function is parameterised by the curvilinear abscissa, 'ABSC'. COEF_MASS_AJOU = fonc_cm Concept of type [fonction] produced by the operator FONC_FLUI_STRU [U4.35.02]. This constant function, parameterised by the curvilinear abscissa, supplies the value of the added-mass coefficient {C}_{m} . 4.4 Factor keyword CABLE Definition of the constant non-linear elastic characteristic for cables: two different elastic constitutive behaviours in tension and in compression, defined by Young's moduli E and EC (modulus in compression). The standard characteristics of the elastic material are to be entered under the factor keyword ELAS. 4.4.1 Elasticity operands ◊ EC_SUR_E = ecse Ratio of the moduli in compression and in tension. If the compression modulus is zero, the global linear system in the displacements may become singular. This is the case when a node is connected only to cables and all of them go into compression. 4.5 Factor keywords ELAS_ORTH, ELAS_ORTH_FO, ELAS_VISCO_ORTH Definition of the orthotropic elastic characteristics, constant or functions of the temperature, for the isoparametric continuum elements or the constituent layers of a composite R4.01.02. It is possible to define constant orthotropic viscoelastic characteristics (ELAS_VISCO_ORTH) at a given frequency; the moduli to be entered are then complex. 4.5.1 Elasticity operands To define the orthotropy frame (\text{L},\text{T},\text{N}) attached to the elements, the reader will refer: - for the isoparametric continuum elements, to the documentation U4.42.01 AFFE_CARA_ELEM keyword MASSIF, - for the composite shell elements, to the documentation U4.42.01 AFFE_CARA_ELEM keyword COQUE as well as to the documentation U4.42.03 DEFI_COMPOSITE keyword ORIENTATION. E_L = ygl Longitudinal Young's modulus. E_T = ygt Transverse Young's modulus. E_N = ygn Normal Young's modulus. GL_T = glt Shear modulus in the plane \text{LT} . G_TN = gtn Shear modulus in the plane \text{TN} . G_LN = gln Shear modulus in the plane \text{LN} . Note: For shells, the transverse shear moduli are not mandatory; in this case, one computes with a thin shell by assigning an infinite stiffness to the transverse shear (elements DST, DSQ and Q4G). NU_LT = nult Poisson's ratio in the plane \text{LT} . Important notes: \mathit{nult} is not equal to \mathit{nutl} . In fact, one has the relation: \mathit{nutl}=\frac{\mathit{ygt}}{\mathit{ygl}}.\mathit{nult} \mathit{nult} must be interpreted in the following way: if one applies a tension along the axis L giving rise to a strain along this axis equal to {\epsilon}_{L}=\frac{{\sigma}_{L}}{\mathit{ygl}} , one has a strain along the axis T equal to: {\epsilon}_{T}=-\mathit{nult}.\frac{{\sigma}_{L}}{\mathit{ygl}} . The various elasticity coefficients E_L, G_LN and NU_LN cannot be chosen arbitrarily: physically, a non-zero strain must always produce a strictly positive strain energy. This is expressed by the fact that the Hooke matrix must be positive definite. The operator DEFI_MATERIAU computes the eigenvalues of this matrix and emits an alarm if this property is not satisfied. For 2D models, as the user has not yet chosen the MODELISATION (D_PLAN, C_PLAN, ...), one checks the positivity of the matrix in the various cases. The first two, SIGC and PRAGER, refer to the elastoplastic branch of the model. They characterise respectively the elastic limit and the Prager constant which relates the back-stress to the plastic strain according to X=C{\epsilon}^{p} . Young's modulus {E}^{p} and Poisson's ratio {\nu}^{p} specific to the elastoplastic branch are for their part defined under the factor keyword ELAS, via the keywords E and NU. The same applies to the thermal expansion coefficient ALPHA where appropriate. Thus E_VISC and NU_VISC characterise respectively Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio of the viscoelastic branch. Note carefully that the elastic characteristics of the elastoplastic branch are defined under ELAS whereas the elastic characteristics of the viscoelastic branch are defined under KICHENIN_NL. And this even if the global stiffness of the constitutive model takes all of these values into account. 5.22 Factor keywords VISC_ISOT_PLAS, VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO | VISC_ISOT_PLAS = _F( ◆ YoungModulus = float, ◆ PoissonRatio = float, ◆ TAILLE_GRAIN = float, ◆ D_DISLOC = float, ◆ C_AMAS = float, ◆ TAILLE_AMAS = float, ◇ UNITE_LONGUEUR = / "M" (par défaut), / "MM", ◇ UNITE_CONTRAINTE = / "Pa" (par défaut), / "MPa", ), | VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO = _F( ◆ YoungModulus = fonction / formule / nappe, ◆ PoissonRatio = fonction / formule / nappe, ◆ TAILLE_GRAIN = fonction / formule / nappe, ◆ D_DISLOC = fonction / formule / nappe, ◆ C_AMAS = fonction / formule / nappe, ◆ TAILLE_AMAS = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ UNITE_LONGUEUR = / "M" (par défaut), / "MM", ◇ UNITE_CONTRAINTE = / "Pa" (par défaut), / "MPa", ), ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles The constitutive law VISC_ISOT_PLAS is an isotropic elasto-viscoplastic flow model described in R5.03.38, which models the multi-scale effects of plasticity as well as those of irradiation. This modelling is mainly adopted to describe the mechanical constitutive behaviour of the steels of the vessels (bainitic) in the non-irradiated and irradiated states. The parameters of the model comprise the elastic mechanical characteristics of the material, i.e. Young's modulus (YoungModulus) and Poisson's ratio (PoissonRatio), as well as the mechanical characteristics of the microstructure of the material, generally obtained experimentally: grain size (TAILLE_GRAIN) for the non-irradiated state, initial dislocation density (D_DISLOC), concentration (C_AMAS) and size (TAILLE_AMAS) of the solute clusters for the irradiated state. These material parameters may be constant (VISC_ISOT_PLAS) or functions of the temperature (VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO) or of any other command variable such as creep. The unit of length considered is the metre by default. It is possible to choose the millimetre by means of the simple keyword UNITE_LONGUEUR. Likewise, the unit of stress considered is the pascal by default, possibly modifiable to the megapascal via the operand UNITE_CONTRAINTE. 5.22.1 Operand YoungModulus | VISC_ISOT_PLAS = _F( ◆ YoungModulus = float, | VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO = _F( ◆ YoungModulus = fonction / formule / nappe, This is the Young's modulus considered. The value entered must be strictly positive. Moreover, it must also be entered via the operand E under the factor keyword ELAS, ELAS_FO. In the scalar case only, a check is carried out and a fatal error will be emitted if the values entered are different. The default unit considered for Young's modulus is that prescribed via the operand UNITE_CONTRAINTE. By default, if nothing is specified, it is the pascal. It is also possible to choose the megapascal by means of the operand UNITE_CONTRAINTE. In all cases, a check is carried out and a fatal error will be emitted if the value entered is negative or zero, whatever the unit chosen. 5.22.2 Operand PoissonRatio | VISC_ISOT_PLAS = _F( ◆ PoissonRatio = float, | VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO = _F( ◆ PoissonRatio = fonction / formule / nappe, This is the Poisson's ratio considered. The value entered must be strictly greater than -1,0 and strictly less than 0,5 . Moreover, it must also be entered via the operand NU under the factor keyword ELAS, ELAS_FO. In the scalar case only, a check is carried out and a fatal error will be emitted if the values entered are different. One recalls that Poisson's ratio has no unit. 5.22.3 Operand TAILLE_GRAIN | VISC_ISOT_PLAS = _F( ◆ TAILLE_GRAIN = float, | VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO = _F( ◆ TAILLE_GRAIN = fonction / formule / nappe, This is the mean size of the grains (lath packets) of the microstructure considered for the non-irradiated state. The value entered must be positive or zero. It corresponds to a length of dislocation line per unit volume. It is expressed by default in m^{-2} but possibly in mm^{-2} if the unit of length set by UNITE_LONGUEUR is the millimetre. For the vessel steels, the value entered is generally between 10^{12} \, m^{-2} and 10^{20} \, m^{-2} (or equivalently between 10^{6} \, mm^{-2} and 10^{14} \, mm^{-2} ). In all cases, a check is carried out and a fatal error will be emitted if the value entered is strictly negative, whatever the unit chosen. 5.22.5 Operand C_AMAS | VISC_ISOT_PLAS = _F( ◆ C_AMAS = float, | VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO = _F( ◆ C_AMAS = fonction / formule / nappe, This is the concentration of the solute clusters for the irradiated state of the microstructure considered. The value entered must be positive or zero. It corresponds to a number of clusters per unit volume. It is expressed by default in m^{-3} but possibly in mm^{-3} if the unit of length set by UNITE_LONGUEUR is the millimetre. For the vessel steels, the value entered is generally less than 10^{25} \, m^{-3} (or equivalently less than 10^{16} \, mm^{-3} ). In all cases, a check is carried out and a fatal error will be emitted if the value entered is strictly negative, whatever the unit chosen. 5.22.6 Operand TAILLE_AMAS | VISC_ISOT_PLAS = _F( ◆ TAILLE_AMAS = float, | VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO = _F( ◆ TAILLE_AMAS = fonction / formule / nappe, This is the size of the solute clusters for the irradiated state of the microstructure considered. The value entered must be positive or zero. The default unit considered for the size of the solute clusters is that prescribed via the operand UNITE_LONGUEUR. By default, if nothing is specified, it is the metre. It is also possible to select the millimetre via the operand UNITE_LONGUEUR. For the vessel steels, the value entered is generally between 10^{-9} \, m and 10^{-8} \, m (or equivalently between 10^{-6} \, mm and 10^{-5} \, mm ). In all cases, a check is carried out and a fatal error will be emitted if the value entered is strictly negative, whatever the unit chosen. 5.22.7 Operand UNITE_LONGUEUR (optional) ◇ UNITE_LONGUEUR = / "M" (par défaut), / "MM", This is to specify the unit of length chosen to express the mechanical characteristics of the microstructure of the material considered. The expected value is a character string which may be 'M' to designate the metre or 'MM' to designate the millimetre ( i.e. one thousandth of a metre). Any other textual value entered will lead to a fatal error. This operand is optional and its default value is 'M', meaning that the metre is the unit of length used by default. 5.22.8 Operand UNITE_CONTRAINTE (optional) ◇ UNITE_CONTRAINTE = / "Pa" (par défaut), / "MPa", This is to specify the unit of stress chosen to express the elastic mechanical characteristics of the material considered. The expected value is a character string which may be 'Pa' to designate the pascal or 'MPa' to designate the megapascal ( i.e. one million pascals). Any other textual value entered will lead to a fatal error. This operand is optional and its default value is 'Pa', meaning that the pascal is the unit of stress used by default. 6 Constitutive behaviours related to damage and fracture 6.1 Factor keywords ROUSSELIER,ROUSSELIER_FO Definition of the coefficients of the ductile-fracture constitutive model of Rousselier (cf. [R5.03.06] and R5.03.07). This model may be used in small strains, in large strains and in viscoplasticity (keyword VISC_SINH) Briefly, one solves for an elastoplastic increment: \lbrace \begin{array}{cc}\frac{{\sigma}_{\mathit{eq}}}{\rho}-R\left(p\right)+D{\sigma}_{1}f\exp\left(\frac{{\sigma}_{H}}{{\sigma}_{1}}\rho \right)=0& \text{éq 5.1-1}\\ \sigma =\rho \Lambda \left(\epsilon -{\epsilon}^{p}\right)\hfill & \phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\\ \dot{{\epsilon}_{p}}=\dot{p}\rho \frac{\partial f}{\partial \sigma }\hfill & \phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\\ \dot{f}=3\left(1-f\right){\epsilon}_{H}^{p}\hfill & \phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\end{array} with \lbrace \begin{array}{cc}\frac{\partial f}{\partial \sigma }=\frac{1}{\rho}\left(\frac{3}{2}\frac{\tilde{\sigma}}{{\sigma}_{\mathit{eq}}}+\frac{\mathit{Df}}{3}\exp\left(\frac{{\sigma}_{H}}{{\sigma}_{1}\rho }\right)\right)& \phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\\ \rho =\frac{1-f}{1-{f}_{0}}\hfill & \text{éq 5.1-2}\end{array} R(p) entered by means of the traction curve (keyword TRACTION). With the material coefficients D,{\sigma}_{1,}{f}_{0} specific to the ROUSSELIER model. These various parameters may depend on the temperature; in this case one will use the keyword ROUSSELIER_FO. It is possible to complete the model by bringing in the following quantities: - the critical porosity {f}_{c} beyond which the growth of the cavities is accelerated: \dot{f}=3A(1-f){\epsilon}_{H}^{p}\text{}\mathit{si}f>{f}_{c} two additional characteristics are then necessary: {f}_{c} and A . - the limit porosity {f}_{l} beyond which the material is considered broken. The constitutive behaviour is then replaced by an imposed drop of the stresses: \dot{\sigma}=-\lambda E\frac{\sigma}{\mid \sigma \mid }\mid \dot{\varepsilon}\mid \text{}\mathrm{si}f={f}_{l} (with E defined under ELAS). two additional characteristics are then necessary: {f}_{1} and \lambda . - the volumetric nucleation rate of cleavage cracks {A}_{n} , modifying as follows equations [éq 5.1-1] and [éq 5.1-2]. \lbrace \begin{array}{c}\frac{{\sigma}_{\mathit{eq}}}{\rho}-R(p)+D{\sigma}_{1}(f+{A}_{n}p)\exp(\frac{{\sigma}_{H}}{{\sigma}_{1}\rho })=0\\ \rho =\frac{1-f-{A}_{n}p}{1-{f}_{0}}\end{array} These last five parameters are independent of the temperature. The following correspondence table must be used: | Modelling | Keywords | | --- | --- | | D | D | | {\sigma}_{1} | SIGM_1 | | {f}_{0} | PORO_INIT | | {f}_{c} | PORO_CRIT dp | | A | PORO_ACCE | | {A}_{n} | AN | | {f}_{l} | PORO_LIMI | | \lambda | D_SIGM_EPSI_NORM | In the SIMO_MIEHE version the constitutive law requests a sub-stepping when the plastic-strain increment is greater than the value \mathit{dp} supplied after the keyword DP_MAXI. The keyword BETA is to be entered with the constitutive behaviours ROUSS_PR or ROUSS_VISC in order to take adiabatic heating into account: it sets the proportion of plastic energy which is actually transformed into heat. The choice is given to the user, by means of the keyword PORO_TYPE, of changing the formulation of the porosity as a function of the plastic strain or of the total strain. It has been observed that for a low initial porosity {f}_{0} , the behaviour at the beginning of the evolution changes strongly as a function of this parameter. Thus PORO_TYPE is assigned 1 (porosity in plastic strain), 2 (porosity in total strain). 6.1.1 Help with use The Rousselier model has been the subject of numerous developments and has several variants named ROUSSELIER, ROUSS_PR and ROUSS_VISC (these models are available in the command STAT_NON_LINE by means of the keyword RELATION). Thus each of these models requires a particular knowledge from the "user" point of view. Moreover, the user must be warned that it is advisable to consider, as convergence criterion, a convergence criterion by reference stress under the keyword RESI_REFE_RELA. 6.2 Factor keyword GTN This keyword makes it possible to define the coefficients of the GTN model (constitutive relations GTN and VISC_GTN) for the part related to the evolution of the porosity, cf. R5.03.29. It covers the three aspects of ductile fracture, namely the phases of nucleation, growth and coalescence of cavities. 6.2.1 Operands The cavity-nucleation phase ( nucleation in English, hence the prefix NUCL in the keywords) is modelled by a contribution to the porosity, denoted {f}^{\mathit{nuc}} , the other contribution being related to the growth of the cavities {f}^{\mathit{growth}} : > \dot{f}={\dot{f}}^{\mathit{growth}}+{\dot{f}}^{\mathit{nuc}};{\dot{f}}^{\mathit{growth}}=\left(1-f\right)\mathrm{tr}{\dot{\mathrm{E}}}^{\mathrm{p}}\text{avec}f(0)={f}_{0} The evolution of the nucleation porosity is a function of the hardening variable \kappa and of the cumulated plastic strain according to the following incremental model: {\dot{f}}^{\mathit{nuc}}={B}_{n}\left(\kappa \right)\dot{\kappa}+{b}_{0}{\dot{E}}_{\mathit{eq}}^{p}H({E}_{\mathit{eq}}^{p}-{E}_{c}^{p});{B}_{n}(\kappa )=\frac{{f}_{N}}{{s}_{N}\sqrt{2\pi }}\exp\left[-\frac{1}{2}{\left(\frac{\kappa -{\kappa}_{N}}{{s}_{N}}\right)}^{2}\right]+\frac{{c}_{0}}{{\kappa}_{f}-{\kappa}_{i}}{\mathrm{\chi }}_{[{\kappa}_{i};{\kappa}_{f}]} where H denotes the Heaviside function (zero for a strictly negative argument, equal to 1 for a positive argument) and {\chi }_{I} the characteristic function of a set I (equal to 1 in I , zero elsewhere). In the absence of a declaration of the nucleation parameters, the function B and {b}_{0} are zero, so that there is then no nucleation. Cavity growth is described by the evolution of the plasticity, governed by a threshold function which relies on an equivalent stress {T}_{\text{ }} . The latter is defined implicitly by the following equation, in which \mathrm{T} denotes the stress tensor specific to the GDEF_LOG kinematics: {\left(\frac{{T}_{\mathit{eq}}}{{T}_{\text{ }}}\right)}^{2}+2{q}_{1}{f}_{\text{ }}\cosh\left({q}_{2}\frac{3}{2}\frac{{T}_{H}}{{T}_{\text{ }}}\right)-1-{q}_{1}{f}_{\text{ }}=0 where {T}_{\mathit{eq}} denotes the von Mises equivalent stress and {T}_{H} one third of the trace of T . Coalescence is expressed (in loading) by an acceleration of the evolution of the effective porosity {f}_{\text{ }} according to the following relation: \lbrace \begin{array}{cc}\mathrm{si}\phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}f\le {f}_{c}& {f}_{\text{ }}=f\hfill \\ \mathrm{si}\phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}f>{f}_{c}& {f}_{\text{ }}={f}_{c}+{\delta}_{c}(f-{f}_{c})\end{array} Here again, there will be no coalescence mechanism ( {f}_{\text{ }}=f ) if the corresponding parameters are not entered. The slope {\delta}_{c} may be supplied directly or recomputed if one prefers to enter the fracture porosity {f}_{r} such that {q}_{1}{f}_{\text{ }}({f}_{r})=1 . Finally, two additional parameters activate regularisation techniques of the model in order to reinforce its robustness: ENDO_CRIT_VISC and ENDO_CRIT_RUPT. Denoting by "damage" the value {q}_{1}{f}_{\text{ }} , one introduces for the model VISC_GTN the viscosity-threshold damage {d}_{v} beyond which one limits the loss of viscosity which results from the damage, which makes it possible to maintain a certain degree of viscous regularisation in order to absorb stress shocks. Moreover, in order to avoid seeking to solve the equations of the model for a damage too close to 1 (they degenerate for d=1 ), one may force prematurely the fracture of the point considered beyond a damage {d}_{r} . By default, it is computed as a function of the numerical precision requested by the user (RESI_INTE_RELA) but this may prove too constraining and lead to an excessive cutting of the time steps. 6.3 Keywords VENDOCHAB/ VENDOCHAB_FO Definition of the coefficients of the viscoplastic model with scalar damage of Chaboche, see R5.03.15).
