RUPT_FRAG_FO The fracture theory of Francfort and Marigo makes it possible to model the appearance and the propagation of cracks in brittle fracture. It relies on the Griffith criterion which compares the release of elastic energy and the energy dissipated during the creation of a cracked surface, supplied by the keyword GC. These are the notions which are used to describe fracture in the cohesive-zone models, subject to the definition of other notions specific to certain laws. RUPT_FRAG is the keyword used to define the material parameters of the cohesive constitutive laws, CZM_xxx (with the exception of CZM_TRA_MIX and CZM_LAB_MIX) (see R7.02.11). 6.6.1 Operand G_C The dissipated energy is proportional to the crack surface created, the coefficient of proportionality being the critical energy density of the material {G}_{c} . 6.6.2 Operand SIGM_C Critical stress at the origin from which the crack will open and the stress between the lips will decrease. 6.6.3 Operand PENA_ADHERENCE Small regularisation parameter of the stress at zero (for further details see R7.02.11). Note The parameters SIGM_C and PENA_ADHERENCE are mandatory only in the case of the modellings xxx_JOINT. They are not used for the Griffith criterion, which is why they appear as optional at catalogue level. 6.6.4 Operand PENA_CONTACT Small regularisation parameter of the contact. 6.6.5 Operands PENA_LAGR and RIGI_GLIS Penalisation parameter of the Lagrangian ( \mathit{pla}\ge 1.01 ) and stiffness in slip mode. Operand CINEMATIQUE Determines the opening modes authorised by the interface law for the law CZM_TAC_MIX. 'UNILATER' means that the two volumes on either side of the interface cannot interpenetrate, 'GLIS_2D' that the two volumes can only slide in the plane tangent to the interface, and 'GLIS_1D' that they can slide only in a single direction. The tangent frame considered is defined via the factor keyword MASSIF of AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01. In the case of a one-dimensional slip, the only possible slip direction is defined by the second vector of the rotated frame ( \mathit{Oy} ). 6.7 Factor keyword NON_LOCAL This factor keyword makes it possible to enter the characteristics necessary for the use of non-local constitutive models for which the response of the material is no longer defined at the scale of the material point but at that of the structure; see also AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01 and R5.04. 6.7.1 Operands LONG_CARA/C_GRAD_VARI/COEF_RIGI_MINI/C_GONF/PENA_LAGR/TAU_EPSI LONG_CARA = long Determines the characteristic length or internal length scale of the material. Not to be used with the non-local damage laws with damage gradient GRAD_VARI. C_GRAD_VARI = long Non-locality parameter for the internal-variable gradient formulation, present in the free energy in the form c/2{\left(\nabla a\right)}^{2} . It determines the characteristic length of the damage zone. To be used exclusively with the non-local damage laws with damage gradient GRAD_VARI. COEF_RIGI_MINI = coef For its part it has an algorithmic role since it sets, for the damage models which degrade the stiffness of the material, the proportion of the initial stiffness (Young's modulus) defined under ELAS (0.1% for example) below which one stops the damage mechanism: this residual stiffness makes it possible to preserve the well-posed character of the elastic problem. C_GONF = gonf In the Rousselier model, the softening character is carried by the porosity which has a purely hydrostatic effect. In order to control the localisation, the idea is to regularise the problem only on this part and therefore to regularise the swelling variable if one uses the INCO_UPG modelling. PENA_LAGR = pena Penalisation parameter used for the modellings with internal-variable gradients ( _GRAD_VARI ) and second gradient ( _DIL ), which makes it possible to control the coincidence between a nodal field (degrees of freedom specific to the non-local formulation) and a field at the Gauss points (internal variable or strain). A default value of 1000 is implemented. For the modelling _DIL it is inadvisable to decrease this value (loss of precision for the solution). For the modelling GRAD_VARI this parameter corresponds to the multiplier r of the quadratic penalisation term in the free energy: r/2{\left(\alpha -a\right)}^{2} . It is up to the user to adjust its value as a function of the law used. PENA_LAGR_INCO = pena_inco Penalisation parameter used for the modellings with internal-variable gradients in large strains ( _GRAD_INCO), which makes it possible to reinforce the kinematic relation between the swelling degree of freedom and the volume change seen from the strain. Numerical tests in the case of a ductile-fracture problem lead to recommending a value of the order of ten times the initial elastic limit. Too low a value (or zero) may lead to the appearance of plastic localisation bands. Too high a value leads to numerical locking in incompressibility which this enriched kinematics precisely seeks to limit. TAU_EPSI = tau_epsi Stabilisation parameter of the stabilised mixed modellings (MIX_STA). Its value lies between 0 and 1. For a value of 1, one recovers a standard linear finite element. For a value of 0, one recovers a non-stabilised mixed formulation. In practice, it is recommended to use \tau_{\varepsilon} = \frac{h}{L} where L represents the characteristic length of the problem, and h the size of the mesh cells. 6.8 Factor keyword CZM_LAB_MIX This factor keyword makes it possible to specify the parameters of the steel–concrete interface law CZM_LAB_MIX (see R7.02.11). 6.8.1 Operand SIGM_C Maximum stress that can be supported by the steel–concrete interface. 6.8.2 Operand GLIS_C Slip for which the stress at the interface is maximum. 6.8.3 Operands ALPHA and BETA Shape parameters of the steel–concrete bond law. alpha typically varies between 0 and 1, whereas beta is positive. 6.8.4 Operands PENA_LAGR Penalisation parameter of the Lagrangian ( \mathit{pla}\ge 1.01 ). 6.8.5 Operand CINEMATIQUE Determines the slip modes authorised by the interface law. 'UNILATER' means that the two volumes on either side of the interface cannot interpenetrate, 'GLIS_2D' that the two volumes can only slide in the plane tangent to the interface, and 'GLIS_1D' that they can slide only in a single direction. The tangent frame considered is defined via the factor keyword MASSIF of AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01. In the case of a one-dimensional slip, the only possible slip direction is defined by the second vector of the rotated frame ( \mathit{Oy} ). 6.9 Factor keyword RUPT_DUCT These material characteristics are intended to define the constitutive behaviour of a ductile cohesive crack with the constitutive law CZM_TRA_MIX, see R7.02.11. 6.9.1 Operand G_C The dissipated energy is proportional to the crack surface created, the coefficient of proportionality being the critical energy density of the material {G}_{c} . 6.9.2 Operand SIGM_C Critical stress at the origin from which the crack will open. 6.9.3 Operands COEF_EXTR and COEF_PLAS Shape parameters of the cohesive law CZM_TRA_MIX, see R7.02.11. 6.9.4 Operands PENA_LAGR and RIGI_GLIS Penalisation parameter of the Lagrangian ( \mathit{pla}\ge .01 ) and stiffness in slip mode. 6.10 Factor keyword RANKINE The simplified modelling of the joints of concrete dams relies on this material R7.01.39. It is a perfect-plasticity criterion in tension bearing on the components of the principal stresses: {\sigma}_{i=\mathrm{1,2,3}}\le {\sigma}_{t} . When a principal stress reaches the threshold value {\sigma}_{t} , the joint opens in this direction. It should be noted that the plastic strain thus created is not reversible; the model therefore does not make it possible to represent the reclosing of the joint and is valid only on a monotonic loading path. 6.10.1 Operand SIGMA_T Threshold in tension (positive value). 6.11 Factor keyword JOINT_MECA_RUPT The modelling of the joints of dams relies on these material characteristics, cf. R7.01.25. The hydrostatic pressure due to the possible presence of fluid in the joint is taken into account. Two industrial procedures are also implemented: keying — the injection of concrete under pressure between the blocks of the structure — and sawing — the sawing of the dam in order to release the compressive stresses. This material keyword is used by the constitutive law of the same name: JOINT_MECA_RUPT. 6.11.1 Operand K_N Normal stiffness in tension. 6.11.2 Operand K_T Tangential stiffness. 6.11.3 Operand SIGM_MAX Maximum critical stress from which the crack opens and the stress between the lips decreases. This stress is often called the tensile strength. 6.11.4 Operand ALPHA Regularisation parameter of the tangential damage. The critical opening length from which the tangential stiffness falls towards zero is defined thus: {L}_{\mathit{CT}}={L}_{C}\tan(\mathit{ALPHA}\pi /4) Operand PENA_RUPTURE Brittle-fracture smoothing parameter. The maximum opening before complete fracture is given by {L}_{C}=\mathrm{SIGM}\text{\_}\mathrm{MAX}(1+\mathrm{PENA}\text{\_}\mathrm{RUPTURE})/K\text{\_}N 6.11.5 Operand PENA_CONTACT Ratio between the normal stiffness in compression and in tension. 6.11.6 Operand PRES_FLUIDE Pressure on the lips of the crack due to the presence of fluid (function which may depend on geometric coordinates or on the time instant). Valid only with the mechanical-joint modellings: xxx_JOINT, and incompatible with RHO_FLUIDE, VISC_FLUIDE and OUV_MIN. 6.11.7 Operand PRES_CLAVAGE Pressure of concrete injected into the joint during the keying phase (function which may depend on geometric coordinates or on the time instant). Valid only with the mechanical-joint modellings: xxx_JOINT, and incompatible with RHO_FLUIDE, VISC_FLUIDE and OUV_MIN. 6.11.8 Operand SCIAGE The saw size used during the sawing phase. Valid only with the mechanical-joint modellings: xxx_JOINT, and incompatible with RHO_FLUIDE, VISC_FLUIDE and OUV_MIN. 6.11.9 Operand RHO_FLUIDE Density of the fluid (positive real [mass]/[volume]), valid only for the coupled hydro-mechanical modellings: xxx_JOINT_HYME and incompatible with PRES_FLUIDE and PRES_CLAVAGE 6.11.10 Operand VISC_FLUIDE Dynamic viscosity of the fluid (strictly positive real [pressure].[time]), valid only for the coupled hydro-mechanical modellings: xxx_JOINT_HYME and incompatible with PRES_FLUIDE and PRES_CLAVAGE. 6.11.11 Operand OUV_MIN Regularisation opening at the crack tip (strictly positive real [length]), valid only for the coupled hydro-mechanical modellings: xxx_JOINT_HYME and incompatible with PRES_FLUIDE and PRES_CLAVAGE. 6.12 Factor keyword JOINT_MECA_FROT The modelling of friction between the joints of dams relies on this material R7.01.25. The hydrostatic pressure due to the possible presence of fluid in the joint is taken into account. It is an elastoplastic version of the Mohr–Coulomb law, which depends on five parameters. Two elastic parameters: the tangential stiffness and the normal stiffness. Two parameters characterising the threshold function: adhesion and the friction coefficient. Plus a regularisation parameter of the tangent matrix in slip. An industrial procedure is also implemented: the sawing of the dam in order to release the compressive stresses. This material keyword is used by the constitutive law of the same name: JOINT_MECA_FROT. 6.12.1 Operand K_N Normal stiffness. 6.12.2 Operand K_T Tangential stiffness in the elastic domain. 6.12.3 Operand MU Friction coefficient. 6.12.4 Operand ADHESION Friction stress at zero normal stress. The tensile strength is then given by: {R}_{T}=C/\mu 6.12.5 Operand AMOR_NOR Surface density of normal damping integrated over the surface of a face of a 3D_JOINT element then distributed as a discrete characteristic on each segment joining each pair of vertex nodes facing each other from one face of the element to the other. The characteristic length computed automatically makes it possible, when the fineness of the mesh changes from one analysis to another, to keep stable results by avoiding localisation phenomena. This length, computed automatically or given by the user, leads to the value of the ultimate hardening in tension according to the formula (for a linear post-peak hardening): {\kappa}_{u}\left(\theta \right)=\frac{2.{G}_{t}\left(\theta \right)}{{l}_{c}.{f}_{t}^{\prime }\left(\theta \right)} In the particular case of a mesh containing adjacent mesh cells whose dimensions are very different, the ultimate hardenings of the model BETON_DOUBLE_DP computed from the characteristic length of the mesh cells are consequently very different, which may generate convergence problems or lead to a rather unphysical stress state. (This characteristic length is computed from the volume of the current mesh cell). For this reason, one proposes to give the user the possibility of defining a mean length which overloads the characteristic length computed for each mesh cell. The default value of Code_Aster is the characteristic length computed for each mesh cell. Choosing an arbitrary length identical for all the mesh cells may also generate convergence difficulties. The best solution consists in creating a mesh whose variations of the dimensions of the mesh cells respect the sense of variation of the stress field, and in using the characteristic length computed automatically as a function of the size of the mesh cells. The overloading by LONG_CARA must be reserved for particular cases, when the user cannot freely intervene on the mesh. In the case where the user defines the characteristic length in the material, he or she will choose a pair ({G}_{t},\text{LONG\_CARA}) such that \frac{2.{G}_{t}\left(\theta \right)}{{l}_{c}.{f}_{t}^{\prime }\left(\theta \right)} is worth the value that he or she wishes for the ultimate hardening in tension {\kappa}_{u} . Moreover, the basic-creep strain is assumed proportional to the internal relative humidity: Spherical part: {\epsilon}^{s}=h\cdot f\left({\sigma}^{s}\right) and, deviatoric part: \underline{\underline{{\epsilon}^{d}}}=h\cdot f\left(\tilde{\underline{\underline{\sigma}}}\right) where h denotes the internal relative humidity. The constitutive model BETON_UMLV is a non-ageing viscoelastic model developed in partnership with the Université de Marne-la-Vallée in order to describe the basic creep of concretes. It is particularly suited to multiaxial configurations by not presupposing the value of the creep Poisson's ratio. The spherical stresses are at the origin of the migration of the water absorbed at the interfaces between the hydrates at the scale of the macro-porosity and absorbed within the micro-porosity into the capillary porosity. The diffusion of the inter-lamellar water from the hydrate pores towards the capillary porosity takes place in an irreversible manner. The total spherical creep strain is therefore written as the sum of a reversible part and of an irreversible part: {\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{fs}}=\underset{\begin{array}{}\mathrm{partie}\\ \mathrm{réversible}\end{array}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{\varepsilon}_{r}^{\mathrm{fs}}}}+\underset{\begin{array}{}\mathrm{partie}\\ \mathrm{irréversible}\end{array}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{\varepsilon}_{i}^{\mathrm{fs}}}} The process of spherical creep strain is governed by the following system of coupled equations: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{\dot{\varepsilon}}^{\mathrm{fs}}=\frac{1}{{\eta}_{r}^{s}}\cdot \left[h\cdot {\sigma}^{s}-{k}_{r}^{s}\cdot {\varepsilon}_{r}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right]-{\dot{\varepsilon}}_{i}^{\mathrm{fs}}\\ {\dot{\varepsilon}}_{i}^{\mathrm{fs}}=\frac{1}{{\eta}_{i}^{s}}{\langle \left[{k}_{r}^{s}\cdot {\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{fs}}-({k}_{r}^{s}+{k}_{i}^{s})\cdot {\varepsilon}_{i}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right]-\left[h{\sigma}^{s}-{k}_{r}^{s}\cdot {\varepsilon}_{r}^{\mathrm{fs}}\right]\rangle }^{+}\end{array} where {k}_{r}^{s} denotes the apparent stiffness associated with the skeleton formed by blocks of hydrates at the mesoscopic scale; {\eta}_{r}^{s} the apparent viscosity associated with the diffusion mechanism within the capillary porosity; {k}_{i}^{s} denotes the apparent stiffness associated intrinsically with the hydrates at the microscopic scale and {\eta}_{i}^{s} the apparent viscosity associated with the interfoliar diffusion mechanism. (The brackets {⟨⟩}^{+} denote the MacCauley operator: {⟨x⟩}^{+}=\frac{1}{2}\left(x+|x|\right) ) The deviatoric stresses are at the origin of a sliding mechanism (or quasi-dislocation mechanism) of the CSH sheets in the nano-porosity. Under deviatoric stress, the creep takes place at constant volume. Moreover, the UMLV creep law assumes the isotropy of the deviatoric creep. Phenomenologically, the sliding mechanism comprises a reversible viscoelastic contribution of the water strongly adsorbed on the CSH sheets and an irreversible viscous contribution of the free water: \underset{\begin{array}{c}\mathit{déformation}\\ \mathit{déviatorique}\\ \mathit{totale}\end{array}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{\underline{\underline{\varepsilon}}}^{\mathit{fd}}}}=\underset{\begin{array}{c}\mathit{contribution}\\ \mathit{eau}\\ \mathit{absorbée}\end{array}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{\underline{\underline{\varepsilon}}}_{\text{}r}^{\mathit{fd}}}}+\underset{\begin{array}{c}\mathit{contribution}\\ \mathit{eau}\\ \mathit{libre}\end{array}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{{\underline{\underline{\varepsilon}}}_{\text{}i}^{\mathit{fd}}}} The jth principal component of the total deviatoric strain is governed by the following system of equations: {\tilde{\dot{\sigma}}}^{j}(1+\frac{{\eta}_{r}^{d}}{{\eta}_{i}^{d}})+\frac{{k}_{r}^{d}}{{\eta}_{i}^{d}}{\tilde{\sigma}}^{j}={\eta}_{r}^{d}{\ddot{\varepsilon}}^{d,j}+{k}_{r}^{d}{\dot{\varepsilon}}^{d,j} where {k}_{r}^{d} denotes the stiffness associated with the capacity of the absorbed water to transmit loads ( load bearing water ); {\eta}_{r}^{d} the viscosity associated with the water adsorbed by the hydrate sheets and {\eta}_{i}^{d} denotes the viscosity associated with the free water. 8.13.1 Operand K_RS = K_RS {k}_{r}^{s} apparent stiffness associated with the skeleton formed by blocks of hydrates at the mesoscopic scale. It relies on the Von Mises stress and the exponential of the stress tensor and compares well with experimental results on concrete in biaxial loading. The parameter BETA0 is of a more numerical nature and its only interest is to make the elasticity domain bounded, including for hydrostatic compressions; the default value fulfils this role well, with no effect on the shape of the domain in the zones of interest. In order to avoid an abrupt change of regime on passing from tension to compression, a function S' regularises the jump in stiffness, see R7.01.42. The parameter REST_RIGIDITE, positive, controls this regularisation; it corresponds to the coefficient γ of the function S'. A value of 0 leads to not restoring the stiffness (i.e. the model is without stiffness restoration) whereas a very large value amounts to practically dispensing with the regularisation. The command DEFI_MATER_GC U4.42.07 facilitates the quantification of this parameter by stipulating what proportion of the stiffness is restored for a strain level corresponding to the initial threshold in compression. 8.31 Factor keyword ENDO_LOCA_TC / ENDO_LOCA_TC_FO Definition of the parameters of the constitutive law ENDO_LOCA_TC R7.01.47. The threshold stress in compression tends monotonically towards a limit, the compressive strength. which describes the homogeneous cracking of a concrete structure via a local quasi-brittle isotropic damage model. 8.31.1 Operands ENER_TRAC_RUPT_N and COEF_ECRO_TRAC These are the internal parameters of the model which define the hardening (see R7.01.47 ). The GonfElas law is a constitutive model for swelling clays (bentonite type); it is defined by the relation: d\tilde{\sigma}={K}_{0}d{\varepsilon}_{V}+b(1+\frac{s}{A}){e}^{-{\beta}_{m}{(\frac{s}{A})}^{2}}\mathrm{ds} with \tilde{\sigma} : net stress (trace) \sigma =\tilde{\sigma}-{p}_{g} . | In the saturated domain: | d\tilde{\sigma}={K}_{0}d{\varepsilon}_{V}-{\mathrm{bdp}}_{w}+{\mathrm{dp}}_{g} | | --- | --- | | Or alternatively: | d\tilde{\sigma}={K}_{0}d{\varepsilon}_{V}-{\mathrm{bdp}}_{c}+(1-b){\mathrm{dp}}_{g} | {K}_{0} is the bulk modulus of the material b is the Biot coefficient A is a parameter homogeneous to a pressure {\beta}_{m} is a dimensionless parameter s the suction (or capillary pressure) From there, the identification is carried out by seeking the swelling pressure. Let {P}_{\mathrm{gf}} be the expected swelling pressure and let {P}_{\mathrm{gf}}({s}_{0}) be the swelling pressure found by the model when one re-saturates a specimen in a test at blocked strain and starting from a suction {s}_{0} . It is easy to see that: \frac{{P}_{\mathit{gf}}({s}_{0})}{A}=\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2\sqrt{{\beta}_{m}}}\mathit{Erf}\left(\frac{{s}_{0}}{A}\sqrt{{\beta}_{m}}\right)+\frac{1}{2{\beta}_{m}}\left(\begin{array}{c}1-{e}^{-{\beta}_{m}{\left(\frac{{s}_{0}}{A}\right)}^{2}}\\ \phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\end{array}\right) One must have {P}_{\mathrm{gf}}={P}_{\mathrm{gf}}^{\infty} . One knows that \mathrm{Erf}(\infty )=1 and therefore: \frac{{P}_{\mathit{gf}}({s}_{0})}{A}=\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2\sqrt{{\beta}_{m}}}+\frac{1}{2{\beta}_{m}} For more details, one will refer to R7.01.41. 10.18.1 Operand YoungModulus and PoissonRatio Classical elasticity parameters (Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio). 10.18.2 Operand BiotCoef Biot coefficient. It will eventually replace the laws LETK and LKR. The scope of use of the model NLH_CSRM is for the moment limited to the isotropic mechanical constitutive behaviour. Taking structural anisotropy into account and the dependence of the hardenings on temperature — effective in the latest version of the LKR model — will be the subject of forthcoming updates; likewise the dependence of the criteria on the third invariant of the stress deviator (Lode angle). The model NLH_CSRM falls within the thermodynamic framework of generalised standard materials with two irreversible mechanisms, - Plastic mechanism — instantaneous irreversible constitutive behaviour: hardening and/or softening, contracting or dilating volumetric constitutive behaviour, influence of the mean stress on the brittle character of the response in compression,…; - Viscoplastic mechanism — delayed irreversible constitutive behaviour (of Perzyna type): primary, secondary and tertiary creep (failure). A coupling between these two mechanisms makes it possible — among other things — to represent the dependence of the maximum strength of certain geomaterials on the loading rate. This law has been integrated implicitly via the Mfront tool. Its reference documentation bears the key r7.01.46. YoungModulus and PoissonRatio are also to be supplied in the factor keyword ELAS. 10.25 Factor keyword MCC The constitutive model MCC makes it possible to represent qualitatively the phenomenology of granular soils under monotonic loadings, taking into account the effects of dilatancy/contractancy, of softening/hardening, and of the critical state. The MCC model falls within the framework of generalised standard materials. It updates the formulation and the numerical solution method of the law CAM_CLAY R7.01.14, while remaining faithful to the elements of phenomenology predicted by the latter, in order, eventually, to replace it. The parameters of the MCC model are seven in total. Three define the isotropic non-linear elastic constitutive behaviour; three represent the initial reversibility domain. A combined kinematic-isotropic hardening carried by the volumetric plastic strain is governed by a last parameter. The constitutive equations are solved using a direct implicit time-integration method, implemented in MFront. The reference documentation of the MCC model bears the key R7.01.48. 10.26 Factor keyword CSSM The constitutive model CSSM ("Critical State Soil Model") is a combination of two models aimed at representing respectively the monotonic and the cyclic drained constitutive behaviour of soils. The first component relies on the modified Cam-Clay model, which describes the phenomena of dilatancy or contractancy as well as confinement effects under monotonic and drained loadings. The second component is a multi-mechanism model of Iwan type, designed to represent the cyclic non-linear constitutive behaviour of soils at low strain levels. The model complies with the framework of generalised standard materials. The constitutive model CSSM comprises a total of eleven parameters: two to describe the reversible (elastic) constitutive behaviour, five for the irreversible constitutive behaviour linked to the modified Cam-Clay component, and three for the irreversible constitutive behaviour linked to the Iwan component. A last parameter weights the contributions of the two components to the shear constitutive behaviour of the CSSM model. The constitutive equations are solved using a direct implicit time-integration method, implemented in MFront. The reference documentation of the CSSM model bears the key R7.01.49. 11 Constitutive behaviours specific to 1D elements It makes it possible to model a constitutive behaviour with linear isotropic hardening, but with different elastic limits and hardening moduli in tension and in compression. The main regulations are: BPEL83, NF-EN-1992-1-1 October 2005, AFCEN-ETCC-2010, One wishes to be able to model strains which will vary slowly in the course of time, in particular in order to take into account the creep of the concrete and the variations of temperature. One also wishes to take into account the influence of temperature on the relaxation phenomena. In regulatory terms, it would be possible to take into account the effect of the creep of the concrete and of the thermal strain by making a linear combination of the various phenomena (cf. the regulations for more details). This approach is incompatible with a finite-element analysis. In order for the relaxation law to be usable in a finite-element code for structural analyses with variations of loadings such as: creep of the concrete, re-tensioning of the cables, taking into account of the influence of temperature, … it must be incremental and thermodynamically correct. The formulation adopted is based on that proposed by J. Lemaitre: \sigma =E.{\epsilon}^{e} \epsilon ={\epsilon}^{e}+{\epsilon}^{\mathit{an}} {\dot{\varepsilon}}^{\mathrm{an}}=\langle \frac{\sigma –R({\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{an}})}{{f}_{\mathrm{prg}}.k} \rangle^{n} with R \left( {\epsilon}^{an} \right)= \large {\frac{{f}_{prg}.c.{\epsilon}^{an}}{ {\left(1+{\left(b.{\epsilon}^{an} \right)}^{nr}\right)}^{\frac{1}{nr}}}} The constitutive law is 1D, and available only for modellings of bar type, which are used to model the prestressing cables in the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP. In order to take into account the influence of temperature on the relaxation, all the coefficients of the law may be functions of the temperature. Note: The parameters c , b , n and \mathit{nr} are dimensionless, and therefore independent of the units used during the study. k is made dimensionless with respect to {f}_{\mathit{prg}} and therefore with respect to the stresses, but not with respect to time. Indeed {\dot{\epsilon}}^{\mathit{an}} is homogeneous to {[s]}^{-1} , if the unit of time is the second. Therefore if one knows k for a rate in a given unit of time, it is necessary to convert its value with respect to the unit of time used during the study. 12.12.1 Operands \bf f_{prg} Failure stress of the cable. RAID_CP_[X|Y|RX|RY] = rcp[x|y|rx|ry] Stiffness of the kinematic hardening in translation or in rotation along x or y of the bearing-capacity criterion (homogeneous to a translational stiffness, optional). Equal to 0 by default. GAMMA_CP_[X|Y|RX|RY]= gcp[x|y|rx|ry] Parameter of the kinematic hardening in translation or in rotation along x or y of the bearing-capacity criterion (homogeneous to the inverse of a distance, optional). Equal to 0 by default. DECOLLEMENT Parameter for activation of the uplift mechanism if equal to 'OUI'. (Optional and equal to 'NON' by default). KP = kp Normal stiffness (that is, along the axis x of the local frame of the element) of an elastic spring placed in parallel with the discrete element (optional parameter). R5.03.17, the non-linear constitutive behaviour of a connection in out-of-plane bending, of the junction between a wall and a floor or a raft, in reinforced concrete, cf. The moments M , just like the stiffnesses, are therefore understood in units of torque (length force). 12.15.1 Operands KE Elastic rotational stiffness {K}_{e}>0 . One will take the same value as that supplied in AFFE_CARA_ELEM (DISCRET=(_F(CARA='K_TR_D_ ',REPERE='LOCAL',...),),). KP Plastic hardening slope {K}_{p}\le {K}_{e} . RDM Damage-threshold rotation {\theta}_{d}^{-} COEF_AMOR= alpha, This parameter is defined as the reflection coefficient (amplitude ratio of a reflected P wave). This coefficient is involved exclusively if one defines an absorbing fluid boundary. In fact, the impedance of an absorbing fluid boundary is defined as {Z}_{C}=\rho c{q}_{\alpha} , where \rho is the density of the fluid defined with the operand RHO, c is the celerity of propagation of the acoustic waves defined by the operands CELE_R and CELE_I and {q}_{\alpha}=(1+\alpha )/(1-\alpha ) where \alpha is defined with the operand COEF_AMOR. By default this value is 0 . When \alpha =0 one has {q}_{\alpha}=1 , that is one is in the presence of a perfectly absorbing boundary. In order to approximate asymptotically the constitutive behaviour of a wave by a cylindrical (spherical) wave propagating towards infinity, one generally truncates the fluid domain at a cylinder or half-cylinder (sphere or half-sphere) of radius R . One notes that the first-order radiation condition is equivalent to the exact radiation condition for the propagation of a spherical wave. This function gives the number of cycles to failure {N}_{\mathit{rupt}} as a function of the half-amplitude of stress \frac{\Delta \sigma }{2}. . The Wöhler curve is a function for which the user chooses the interpolation mode: - LOG LOG: logarithmic interpolation on the number of cycles to failure and on the half-amplitude of the stress (Basquin formula piecewise), - LIN LIN: linear interpolation on the number of cycles to failure and on the half-amplitude of the stress (this interpolation is not recommended because the Wöhler curve is absolutely not linear in this frame), - LIN LOG: linear interpolation on the half-amplitude of stress, and logarithmic on the number of cycles to failure, which corresponds to the expression given by Wöhler. If it is not given, an automatic coefficient is determined as a function of the physics of the problem. 14.5 Factor keyword WEIBULL,WEIBULL_FO Definition of the coefficients of the Weibull model R7.02.06. Briefly, the cumulative probability of failure P_r of a structure is written, in the case of a monotonic loading: {P}_{r}=1-\exp\left[-\sum_{{V}_{p}}({(\frac{max({\sigma}_{I}-\sigma_{th},0)}{{\sigma}_{u}})}^{m}\frac{{V}_{p}}{{V}_{0}})\right] where the summation is carried over the mesh cells {V}_{p} which have plastified (that is, cumulative plastic strain greater than a value chosen arbitrarily {p}_{s} ) and m,s_u,V_0,\sigma_{th} are the parameters of the Weibull model.
