In the axisymmetric case, the forces to be supplied are reduced to a sector of 1 radian (divide the real loading by 2\pi ). 3.6 Case of large transformations 3.6.1 The problem When one applies a Dirichlet loading on a structure in large transformations (large displacements, large rotations), one must take care that this loading remains applicable when the assumption of small perturbations is no longer satisfied. This is naturally the case for the following loadings: - DDL_IMPO but if one uses AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F, one must do so with functions that represent the true imposed displacement (curvilinear in general). If one does not, the interpolation in time takes one through “false” intermediate states; - LIAISON_MAIL + TYPE_RACCORD=’MASSIF’; - LIAISON_UNIF; - LIAISON_OBLIQUE; - LIAISON_DDL; - LIAISON_CHAM_NO; - CHAMNO_IMPO; - LIAISON_SOLIDE provided that one applies the assumption of a follower loading. On the other hand, for the following loadings, the assumption of large transformations is not applicable and will produce wrong results: - FACE_IMPO with DNOR=f(t): the “normal” changes under large rotations; - LIAISON_MAIL + TYPE_RACCORD=’COQUE_MASSIF’ and LIAISON_MAIL + 'MASSIF_COQUE'; - LIAISON_ELEM; - LIAISON_RBE3. 3.6.2 Follower loadings For the non-linear operators (STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE), some loadings may be “follower” loadings, that is their application depends on the displacement and therefore changes at each Newton iteration. It is then necessary for the user to state this by the operand TYPE_CHARGE in the factor keyword EXCIT of these commands (see U4.51.03). Stating that the loading is a follower loading sometimes adds a contribution to the stiffness matrix (see for example R3.03.04) and may make it non-symmetric. For the loading EVOL_CHAR, it is not necessary to state that the loadings are follower loadings; they are so automatically by default. Stating it simply activates the additional matrix contribution and therefore acts on the rate of convergence (and not on the accuracy of the result). The loading EFFE_FOND in follower mode is an approximation of reality. It is activated because it depends simultaneously on a loading of type PRES_REP. On the other hand, if, in the zone where the loading EFFE_FOND is applied, the motions are not negligible (variation of the cross-section such as ovalisation or a non-negligible rotation which modifies the normal), an error is made. 3.7 Designation of the topological entities for assignment of the loadings In general, when the entities on which values must be assigned are defined: - On a single node: one uses the operand GROUP_NO which must obviously contain only one node; - On a list of nodes: one may use the operand GROUP_NO but also the operand GROUP_MA or TOUT=’OUI’ to assign over the whole mesh; - On a single mesh cell: one uses the operand GROUP_MA which must obviously contain only one mesh cell; - On a list of mesh cells: one may use the operand GROUP_MA or TOUT=’OUI’ to assign over the whole mesh; Some keywords need to define several topological entities (groups of nodes facing each other for example); in this case, the names may vary slightly (GROUP_NO_2, GROUP_MA_ESCL, etc.). It is possible in most keywords to exclude nodes or mesh cells by means of keywords of type SANS_ . This feature avoids redefining groups in the mesh or in the command DEFI_GROUPs. 3.8 Overloading rule and persistence rule To define the assignment domain as simply as possible, one uses the overloading rule defined in the document U1.03.00, the principles of which are recalled: - Assignments are made by superposing the effects of the different loadings; - In the event of conflict, the last loading prevails over the previous ones; If, for example, the user writes: FORCE_FACE=_F(GROUP_MA=’G1’,FX= 12 ), PRES_REP=_F(GROUP_MA=’G1’,PRES= 13 ) And if the normal for {G1} is oriented along X , then everything will happen as if one had written: FORCE_FACE=_F(GROUP_MA=’G1’, FX= 25) The preceding overloading rule must be completed by another rule in order to specify what happens when several quantities can be assigned for each occurrence of a loading. Take for example: FORCE_INTERNE=( _F(TOUT = ’OUI’, FX = 1. ), _F(GROUP_MA = ’GM1’, FY = 2. ), ) The overloading rule tells us that the second occurrence of FORCE_INTERNE overloads the first. But what is the value of FX on a mesh cell belonging to GM1? Has it been erased by the second occurrence? If only the overloading rule is applied, FX is not defined on GM1. One therefore uses a second rule, called the persistence rule, which specifies that when applying the overloading rule to occurrences, one keeps the components that are not overloaded. Applying the persistence rule to the example, FX keeps the value assigned beforehand. All the elements of the model therefore have a value for FX and the elements of GM1 have a value both for FX and for FY 3.9 Definition of the reference frames Most loadings are defined in the global reference frame of the mesh, except: - For structural elements; - For the keywords DNOR, DTAN and pressure-type loadings. In this case, it is necessary to define normals and tangents, or possibly to use the command MODI_MAILLAGE; - When the keyword ANGL_NAUT can be used; In the other cases, it is generally possible to define functions of space. 3.9.1 Normals and tangents to the mesh cells The standard definition of the normals and of the tangents according to the type of boundary mesh cell is given here: - For segment elements in 2D, the tangent is that defined by the segment oriented by its two first nodes; the normal \underline{n} is then such that (\underline{n},\underline{t}) form a right-handed frame Definition of the normal in the two-dimensional case Definition of the tangent in the two-dimensional case - For triangle or quadrangle elements in 3D, the orientation of the normal \underline{n} is that corresponding to the right-handed sense of the description of the mesh cell. Definition of the normal in the three-dimensional case If DNOR (or DTAN) is specified, the normal (or the tangent) on a node is the average of the normals or of the tangents of the mesh cells on which the boundary conditions are assigned and which have this node in common (except for curved quadratic elements, where the normal is correctly computed at every point). Smoothing of the normals The operator MODI_MAILLAGE makes it possible to ensure the continuity of the orientation of the normal to the boundaries of solid continuum elements. 3.9.2 Case of structural elements Structural elements (beams, plates and shells) have their own local reference frame, the definition of which is given in the documentation of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 3.9.3 Definition of a reference frame by the nautical angles Some loadings offer the possibility of giving their direction of application by using nautical angles, the definition of which is recalled here. The nautical angles \alpha , \beta , \gamma supplied in degrees, are the angles making it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the node coordinates (P,X,Y,Z) to the local frame (P,{X}_{3},{Y}_{3},{Z}_{3}) . The latter is obtained by three rotations: - A rotation of angle \alpha about Z , transforming (XYZ) into ({X}_{1}{Y}_{1}{Z}_{1}) with {Z}_{1}\equiv Z ; Definition of the angle \alpha - A rotation of angle \beta about {Y}_{1} , transforming ({X}_{1}{Y}_{1}{Z}_{1}) into ({X}_{2}{Y}_{2}{Z}_{2}) with {Y}_{2}\equiv {Y}_{1} ; Definition of the angle \beta ( the rotation angle \beta is negative) - A rotation of angle \gamma about {X}_{2} , transforming ({X}_{2}{Y}_{2}{Z}_{2}) into ({X}_{3}{Y}_{3}{Z}_{3}) with {X}_{3}\equiv {X}_{2} ; Definition of the angle \gamma The local frame is: ({X}_{3}{Y}_{3}{Z}_{3}) . Representation of the global and local frames 4 General operands 4.1 Keyword MODELE The keyword MODELE expects a concept produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE in which are defined the types of finite elements assigned on the mesh. The model is necessarily of type MECANIQUE. 4.2 Keywords CHAM_MATER and CARA_ELEM The keyword CHAM_MATER must be supplied when one gives a function that depends on the density (parameter RHO). The keyword CARA_ELEM must be supplied when one gives a function that depends on the thickness of the shell mesh cell (parameter EP). 4.3 Keyword DOUBLE_LAGRANGE This keyword makes it possible to say whether or not the user wishes to duplicate the Lagrange multipliers used to define and dualise the boundary conditions in the assembled matrix. In concrete terms, duplicating the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to use linear solvers that do not allow pivoting. Not duplicating the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the problem (and therefore the size of the problem to be solved) but its use is limited to the solvers MUMPS and Petsc. Note that the two Lagrange multipliers associated with the relation will be such that the first will be located before all the terms involved in the relation and the second after them, in the assembled matrix. This choice has the advantage of giving an assembled matrix whose storage requirement is smaller but has the disadvantage of being able to introduce a singularity into the matrix. Since the numbering is in any case liable to be modified by the renumberer of the external solver chosen, this detail therefore remains purely technical. 4.4 Keyword VERI_NORM The keyword VERI_NORM checks the orientation of the normals to the surface mesh cells in 3D (skin mesh cells TRIA or QUAD) and the line mesh cells in 2D (skin mesh cells SEG). If a normal is not outward, a fatal error message is issued. To reorient the mesh cells so as to have outward normals, one must use the command MODI_MAILLAGE, keyword ORIE_PEAU. No check is possible on shells or plates. To check their orientation, one is also referred to the command MODI_MAILLAGE, keyword ORIE_NORM_COQUE. 4.5 Keyword VERI_AFFE The keyword VERI_AFFE checks the relevance of the requested assignments according to the types of finite elements. For example, one checks that a pressure imposed by PRES_REP is not assigned on volume elements or point elements. It is possible to deactivate these checks, on large models, if they take too much time. 4.6 Keyword INFO The keyword INFO controls the level of the printouts on the message file. 4.7 Keywords ANGL_NAUT/CENTRE/TRAN ANGL_NAUT makes it possible to define a reference frame by the nautical angles in degrees. CENTRE gives the coordinates of the centre of rotation (in the global frame). TRAN gives the components of the translation vector (in the global frame). 5 Dirichlet-type loadings 5.1 Degrees of freedom Dirichlet loadings are imposed on the degrees of freedom of the quantity DEPL_R (or DEPL_C or DEPL_F ) , representing the degrees of freedom of the mechanical problem (or of the thermo-hydro-mechanical problem or of hydraulics). including between the different occurrences, one checks that there is no redundancy between the boundary conditions by application of the overloading and persistence rules. Indeed, such a situation would lead to a singular matrix during the analysis. However, if the same boundary condition is specified twice by two different calls to AFFE_CHAR_MECA (for example, with two values of imposed displacement), this leads to a singular matrix. The kinematic boundary conditions are always imposed on the nodes , not on the mesh cells. 5.3 Pairing operations Pairing is an operation aimed at giving the relation between two meshes. 5.3.1 Node-to-node pairing (compatible meshes) This type of pairing (used for example in LIAISON_GROUP or LIAISON_COQUE) makes it possible to establish pairs of nodes two by two. It is done in the same way as in AFFE_CHAR_THER. First, one establishes the two lists of nodes {\Gamma}_{1} and {\Gamma}_{2} to be placed facing each other (i.e. to be paired), for each occurrence of the factor keyword. Redundancies being eliminated, the two lists of nodes obtained must have the same length . Determination of the pairs of facing nodes is done in several steps: - For each node {N1} of the first list, one looks for the image node {N2}=f({N1}) of the second list. If f is not injective (a node {N2} is the image of two distinct nodes {N1} and {N3} ), the following error message is issued: There is a conflict in the facing of the nodes. The node {N2} is at the same time the facing node of node {N1} and of node {N3} . - For each node {N2} of the second list, one looks for the image node {N1}=g({N2}) of the first list. If g is not injective (a node {N1} is the image of two distinct nodes {N2} and {N3} ), the following error message is issued: There is a conflict in the facing of the nodes. The node {N1} is at the same time the facing node of node {N2} and of node {N3} . - One checks that g={f}^{-1} , that is that the pairs obtained by the first two steps are the same (one wants a bijection f between the two lists of nodes). If f is not surjective, the following error message is issued: There is a conflict in the facing of the nodes. The node {N1} is the image of no node by the inverse correspondence. For a given node N , one calls image node f(N) the node of the other list of nodes which realises the minimum of the distance to N . To facilitate pairing, in particular in the case of particular geometries (where the boundaries {\Gamma}_{1} and {\Gamma}_{2} could “almost” be deduced from one another by the composition of a translation and a rotation), the possibility is offered of making a virtual geometric transformation of the first node group (translation and rotation) before computing the distances (keywords TRAN, CENTRE and ANGL_NAUT). In the pairs of facing nodes, the order of the nodes matters. If for the first occurrence of the factor keyword, a node N belongs to the first node group and a node M to the second node group, and if for the second occurrence of the same factor keyword it is the reverse, one will obtain at the end of pairing the pairs (N,M) and (M,N) . They will not be eliminated during the detection of redundancies; on the other hand, the matrix obtained will be singular. Thus, one is advised to keep the same logic when describing the facing edges. 5.3.2 Mesh-cell-to-node pairing (incompatible meshes) In the remainder of this paragraph, one will speak of the “slave” face (FACE2) and of the “master” face (FACE1). The “tying” of two faces will be done by writing linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the two faces. The displacements of the nodes of the slave face will be linked to the displacements of their projections on the master face. For each node of the slave face, one will write 2 (in 2D) or 3 (in 3D) linear relations (see the operator PROJ_CHAMP for more details). The principle of the relation is to eliminate the slave degrees of freedom by writing them as linear relations of the master degrees of freedom. There is a certain symmetry in the problem and one might believe that one can choose at random which will be the master and which will be the slave. In reality, one must be careful on two particular points: - The syntax is not symmetric: on the slave side, the user must specify the nodes to “weld”, whereas on the master side, the user must give mesh cells. Moreover, the master mesh cells are (for the moment) of a topological dimension to what would be natural. For example, for a 2D mesh, the surfaces to be tied are lines, and one might expect the master mesh cells to be segments. The code expects surface mesh cells (quadrangles and triangles). - It is preferable (from a mechanical point of view) to choose as slave surface the surface meshed most finely. In the same way as when one welds two sheets, it is better to multiply the weld points. Notes - In 3D, one must not give surface master mesh cells, but the volume mesh cells adjacent to the face. The mesh cells specified are “candidates” for the search for facing points. One may give too many; that is not a problem. In the same way, in 2D, the “master” mesh cells must be surface mesh cells (QUAD, TRIA) and not line mesh cells. - When one ties a mesh formed of linear elements ({P1}) onto another quadratic mesh ({P2}) , it is rather advised to choose as “slave” face the quadratic face. 5.4 Keyword DDL_IMPO The keyword DDL_IMPO can be used to impose on nodes one or more values of a degree of freedom. If one wants to impose a degree of freedom in another direction, it is possible to use the keyword DTAN. DTAN makes it possible to apply a boundary condition in the direction tangent to the edge. One thus modifies the values of the displacement degrees of freedom DX, DY and DZ. Topological assignment: GROUP_MA, SANS_GROUP_MA, SANS_GROUP_NO The kinematic conditions are imposed on the nodes belonging to the mesh cells given by the keywords TOUT, GROUP_MA while possibly excluding some by means of the keywords SANS_ . The mesh cells are necessarily triangles or quadrangles in 3D and segments in 2D. Components: DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ, GRX, PRE1, PRE2, PRES, PHI, TEMP Note The imposed degrees of freedom are defined in the global frame of definition of the mesh. If one wants to impose a degree of freedom in another direction, it is possible to use the keyword DTAN. DTAN makes it possible to apply a boundary condition in the direction tangent to the face. One thus modifies the values of the displacement degrees of freedom DX, DY and DZ. This condition can work only in 2D, not in 3D. DNOR makes it possible to apply a boundary condition in the direction normal to the face. One thus modifies the values of the displacement degrees of freedom DX, DY and DZ. DNOR blocks the displacement along the normal of the element. Note If the geometry of the selected (skin) mesh cells is not of good quality, the computation of the normals may be disturbed and this may lead to “rough” results. If the zone concerned is plane, one can then replace the keyword FACE_IMPO / DNOR (or DTAN) by the keyword LIAISON_OBLIQUE. One is then sure that the nodes will move strictly in the same direction. DRNOR makes it possible to apply a boundary condition in the direction normal to the face. One thus modifies the values of the displacement degrees of freedom DRX, DRY and DRZ. DRNOR blocks the rotation along the normal of the element. 5.7 Keyword LIAISON_DDL The keyword LIAISON_DDL makes it possible to define a linear relation between degrees of freedom of two or more nodes. The following kinematic condition will be applied: {\sum}_{i=1}^{r}{\alpha}_{i}{U}_{i}=\beta With {U}_{i} the list of the r degrees of freedom, {\alpha}_{i} the coefficients and \beta the right-hand side. Topological assignment: GROUP_NO gives the list of nodes {N}_{i} ordered in the natural way, that is in the order of the list of node groups, and for each node group, in the order of definition of the group by GROUP_NO, Warning! The order of the nodes matters (see the examples). DDL gives the ordered list of the r degrees of freedom {U}_{i} . Warning! The order of the degrees of freedom matters (see the examples). COEF_MULT gives the ordered list of the r real coefficients {\alpha}_{i} . Warning! The order of the coefficients matters (see the examples). COEF_MULT_FONC gives the ordered list of the r function coefficients {\alpha}_{i} ( AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F ). The functions can depend only on the initial geometry. Warning! The order of the coefficients matters (see the examples). COEF_IMPO is the value of the linear relation \beta . If it is a function (AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F), it may depend on time or on the initial geometry . Example 1: one wants to impose a linear relation between the degrees of freedom of one and the same node. In this particular case, one will repeat after the keyword GROUP_NO the name (of the group) of the node as many times as there are degrees of freedom in the relation. To impose {U}_{x}={U}_{y} on the node of name (of group) {GN}1 , one will write: LIAISON_DDL =_F(GROUP_NO = (’GN1’, ’GN1’), DDL = (’DX’, ’DY’), COEF_MULT = (1., -1.), COEF_IMPO = 0.,) Example 2: one wants to impose a linear relation between node groups It is important to note that to one occurrence of the factor keyword LIAISON_DDL there corresponds one and only one linear relation. If one wants to impose the same relation between two node groups GRN01 and GRN02 (the same displacement {U}_{x} node to node for example) one cannot write : LIAISON_DDL = _F(GROUP_NO = (’GRNO1’ , ’GRNO2’), DDL = (’DX’, ’DX’), COEF_MULT = (1. , -1.), COEF_IMPO = 0.,) This writing makes sense only if {GRNO1} and {GRNO2} each contain only one node. Topological assignment: GROUP_NO, the loading is assigned on the nodes. Components: DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ, values of the components. The linear relation that one is going to impose is: 2. DX(N01) + 1. DY(N01) + 3. DZ(N01) + 1. DX(N02) + 4. DY(N02) + 2. DZ(N02) + 3. DRX(N02) + 5. DRY(N02) + 2. DRZ(N02) = b Example 2: equality of components of displacements averaged on two pieces of boundary of a solid One wants to impose an equality of a mean-displacement component on a piece of boundary of a solid with another mean-displacement component on another piece of boundary: \int_{S_1}{u_i dS}-\int_{S_2}{u_j dS}=0 \Leftrightarrow \int_{S_1}{F_{1i}. u_i dS}-\int_{S_2}{F_{2j}. u_j dS}=0 with distributed force components F_{1i}=1 and F_{2j}=-1 on each respective piece of boundary. To realise this relation condition above, one will use: - the command AFFE_CHAR_MECA producing the loadings F_{1i}=1 and F_{2j}=-1 on each mesh-cell group describing the respective piece of boundary, for example at the edge of a 2D domain: - FORCE_CONTOUR specifying the respective component i or j of the forces on the mesh-cell group concerned, or - PRES_REP if the mean displacement to be imposed is expressed in a frame local to the boundary: normal component PRES_REP =_F(PRES=-1.) or tangential in 2D PRES_REP =_F(CISA_2D =1.)...). - or on a face of a 3D domain: - FORCE_FACE specifying the respective component i or j of the forces on the mesh-cell group concerned, - then, to obtain the cham_no concept used in LIAISON_CHAMNO, one must compute: - with the command CALC_VECT_ELEM the elementary vector (with the OPTION 'CHAR_MECA'), - which one will assemble with ASSE_VECTEUR (having beforehand a numbering concept for the degrees of freedom obtained with the command NUME_DDL), - the result obtained will be the cham_no concept wanted in LIAISON_CHAMNO and one will specify COEF_IMPO=0.0. Example 3: control of the work of a mechanical response on a boundary One wants to impose that the work of a mechanical response in a distributed force field applied on a boundary of a solid be equal to a unit value. \int_{S}{\overrightarrow{F}. \overrightarrow{u} ~dS}=1 One will use an approach similar to the preceding example to produce the wanted cham_no concept with the distributed force loading on the boundary (with FORCE_CONTOUR, not forgetting to define all the components of this force vector). And in LIAISON_CHAMNO one will specify: COEF_IMPO=1.0. 5.11 Keyword CHAMNO_IMPO CHAMNO_IMPO = _F( ◆ CHAM_NO = cham_no, ◆ COEF_IMPO = float, ) It is in fact a slight adaptation of the keyword LIAISON_CHAMNO (see § 5.10 ). The latter makes it possible to apply as coefficients of the linear relation the content of a cham_no. In the case of the keyword CHAMNO_IMPO, one takes the content of a cham_no as the right-hand side of the linear relation. It is therefore strictly equivalent to a manual procedure in which one recovers the values of the cham_no by hand and then imposes them via DDL_IMPO. If the field cham_no contains the value 2 for DX, one imposes the relation: DX = COEF_IMPO 2. The coefficient {\alpha} is fixed at 1. ◆ CHAM_NO Name of the cham_no which serves to define the right-hand sides of the linear relation. ◆ COEF_IMPO = b Multiplier coefficient of the cham_no. 5.12 Keyword LIAISON_GROUP LIAISON_GROUP = _F( ◆ / GROUP_MA_1 = grma, / GROUP_NO_1 = grno, ◆ / GROUP_NO_2 = grno, / GROUP_MA_2 = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ DDL_1 = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", ... liste_dof ◆ COEF_MULT_1 = float, ◆ DDL_2 = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", ... liste_dof ◆ COEF_MULT_2 = float, ◆ COEF_IMPO = float ou fonction, ◇ TRAN = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ CENTRE = float, ) The keyword LIAISON_GROUP makes it possible to define the same linear relation between certain degrees of freedom of pairs of nodes, these pairs of nodes being obtained by placing facing each other two lists of mesh cells or of nodes (see § 5.3.1 ). The total number of relations imposed is equal to the number of pairs of nodes. Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_MA_1, GROUP_NO_1: First list of nodes to be put in relation (denoted {\Gamma}_{1} ). ◆ GROUP_MA_2, GROUP_NO_2: Second list of nodes to be put in relation (denoted {\Gamma}_{2} ). ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO This operand makes it possible to remove from the list of pairs of facing nodes all the pairs of which at least one of the nodes belongs to the list of nodes described by this operand. This makes it possible to avoid the accumulation of linear relations on one and the same node over different repetitions of the factor keyword LIAISON_GROUP, which most of the time leads to a singular matrix. ◆ DDL_1 Gives the list of the degrees of freedom for the edge {\Gamma}_{1} (see § 5.1 for the possible degrees of freedom). If DDL_1 = ’DNOR’, one links the displacement degrees of freedom along the normal to the surface of the element (see § 3.9.1 ). ◆ DDL_2 Gives the list of the degrees of freedom for the edge {\Gamma}_{2} (see § 5.1 for the possible degrees of freedom). If DDL_2 = ’DNOR’, one links the displacement degrees of freedom along the normal to the surface of the element (see § 3.9.1 ). ◆ COEF_MULT_1 List of reals exactly sized to the number of degrees of freedom declared in DDL_1 corresponding to the multiplier coefficients of the linear relation. ◆ COEF_MULT_2 List of reals exactly sized to the number of degrees of freedom declared in DDL_2 corresponding to the multiplier coefficients of the linear relation. ◆ COEF_IMPO Blocking coefficient of the linear relation. ◇ CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/TRAN The operands CENTRE / ANGL_NAUT / TRAN (see § 4.6 ) make it possible to define an approximate virtual transformation (rotation and/or translation) of \Gamma_1 into {\Gamma}_{2} in order to ensure the bijectivity of the facing function [§ 5.3.1 ]. The command first carries out the rotation, then the translation. Example : One wants to impose a cyclic repetition condition (same normal displacement) between face 1 and face 2 of the geometry below: Suppose that FACE1 (respectively FACE2) is composed of the list of mesh cells lma1 (respectively lma2). Since the relation must be bijective, the two faces necessarily have the same number of nodes {nbno} . One wants to write the following linear relations: \forall {N}_{i}^{1} nœud de la FACE1 de vis-à-vis {N}_{i}^{2} \forall i = 1...{nbno} {u.n}({N}_{i}^{1})={u.n}({N}_{i}^{2}) The data of LIAISON_GROUP will be written: LIAISON_GROUP = _F( GROUP_MA_1 = lma1, GROUP_MA_2 = lma2, DDL_1 = ’DNOR’, DDL_2 = ’DNOR’, COEF_MULT_1 = 1., COEF_MULT_2 = -1., COEF_IMPO = 0, CENTRE = (X0,Y0,Z0), ANGL_NAUT = (:math: \alpha ,0.,0.), ) In the case where FACE2 is perpendicular to the X axis, the preceding example can also be written: LIAISON_GROUP=_F ( GROUP_MA_1 = lma1, GROUP_MA_2 = lma2, DDL_1 = ('DX', 'DY'), DDL_2 = 'DY', COEF_MULT_1 = (-sin(:math: \alpha ), cos(:math: \alpha )), COEF_MULT_2 = -1., COEF_IMPO = 0 ) Note: The total number of relations imposed by one occurrence does not depend on the number of arguments of DDL_1 or of DDL_2, which serve only to enrich the relation. In the following case, one imposes {nbno} relations: LIAISON_GROUP=_F ( GROUP_MA_1 = lma1, GROUP_MA_2 = lma2, DDL_1 = ('DX', 'DY'), DDL_2 = ('DX', 'DY'), COEF_MULT_1 = (1, 1), COEF_MULT_2 = (-1, -1), COEF_IMPO = 0 ) In the following case, one imposes 2\cdot {nbno} relations: LIAISON_GROUP=(_F( GROUP_MA_1 = lma1, GROUP_MA_2 = lma2, DDL_1 = 'DX', DDL_2 = 'DX', COEF_MULT_1 = 1, COEF_MULT_2 = -1., COEF_IMPO = 0) _F ( GROUP_MA_1 = lma1, GROUP_MA_2 = lma2, DDL_1 = 'DY', DDL_2 = 'DY', COEF_MULT_1 = 1, COEF_MULT_2 = -1., COEF_IMPO = 0 ) ) It must be carefully noted that these last two examples are not equivalent. 5.13 Keyword LIAISON_MAIL LIAISON_MAIL = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA_MAIT = grma, ◆ | GROUP_MA_ESCL = grma, | GROUP_NO_ESCL = grno, ◇ DISTANCE_MAX = float, ◇ DISTANCE_ALARME = float, ◇ TYPE_RACCORD = / "MASSIF" (par défaut), / "COQUE", / "COQUE_MASSIF", / "MASSIF_COQUE", # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RACCORD", 'COQUE') ◇ TRANSF_GEOM_MAIT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TRANSF_GEOM_ESCL = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ DDL = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RACCORD", 'MASSIF') ◇ TRAN = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ CENTRE = float, ◇ DDL = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", ... liste_dof # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RACCORD", 'COQUE_MASSIF') ◆ EPAIS = float, ◆ CHAM_NORMALE = cham_no, ◇ ELIM_MULT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ) 5.13.1 Use and examples The keyword LIAISON_MAIL makes it possible to define linear relations in order to “tie” two “edges” of a structure. The particular feature of this keyword (compared with LIAISON_GROUP for example) is to make it possible to link the displacements of nodes without a constraint on the mesh. The meshes of FACE1 and FACE2 may be incompatible. Note (cf. § 5.3.2 ): In 3D, one must not give surface master mesh cells, but the volume mesh cells adjacent to the face to be linked. The mesh cells specified are “candidates” for the search for facing points. One may give too many; that is not a problem. In the same way, in 2D, the “master” mesh cells must be surface mesh cells (QUAD, TRIA) and not line mesh cells . Examples : 1. a periodicity condition (study of a homogenisation cell) Experience has shown that for periodic homogenisation computations, the results are much more accurate if the two faces have compatible meshes (that is the meshes of FACE1 and FACE2 can be superimposed modulo an isometry). 1. a cyclic repetition condition 1. a simple tying condition In the remainder of this paragraph, one will speak of the “slave” face (FACE2) and of the “master” face (FACE1). The “tying” of the two faces will be done by writing linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the two faces, see § 5.3.2 . The displacements of the nodes of the slave face will be linked to the displacements of their projections on the master face. For each node of the slave face, one will write two (in 2D) or three (in 3D) linear relations. 5.13.2 A few notes and precautions of use - If FACE1 and FACE2 are not geometrically coincident but there exists an isometry (rotation and translation) between the two, the user must define this isometry (the one which transforms FACE2 into FACE1), by means of the keywords CENTRE / ANGL_NAUT / TRAN. - A “classical” use of this feature is for example the tying of a mesh formed of linear elements ({P1}) onto another quadratic mesh ({P2}) . In this case it is rather advised to choose as “slave” face the quadratic face. - The keyword LIAISON_MAIL is in principle made to link two surfaces which are a priori disjoint. Sometimes this is not the case and a slave node may belong to one of the master mesh cells. The linear relation that the problem seeks to write becomes a tautology ( X{=}X ), which leads to a zero pivot during factorisation. To avoid this problem, one does not write the relations linking a slave node to its master mesh cell if: ◦ This node belongs to the connectivity of the mesh cell; ◦ And if the keywords CENTRE / ANGL_NAUT / TRAN have not been used. - One must be aware that for each occurrence of LIAISON_MAIL, one links a priori all the slave nodes to the master mesh cells even if the projection distances are large (alarms are however issued in this case). One can change this behaviour by using the keyword DISTANCE_MAX. - If one writes: LIAISON_MAIL = ( _F(GROUP_MA_ESCL=’GE’, GROUP_MA_MAIT =’GM1’), _F(GROUP_MA_ESCL=’GE’, GROUP_MA_MAIT =’GM2’) ) It would be a mistake to think that the program will sort in \text{GE} the nodes close to \text{GM1} and those close to \text{GM2} . In this example, the nodes of \text{GE} will be eliminated twice and one can expect a zero-pivot problem during factorisation. The user must write: LIAISON_MAIL = _F(GROUP_MA_ESCL=’GE’, GROUP_MA_MAIT=(’GM1’,’GM2’) ) 5.13.3 Keywords ◆ GROUP_MA_ESCL, GROUP_NO_ESCL: List of the slave nodes to be put in relation. When one wants to tie only the normal displacements of the faces (cf. keywords DDL_MAIT and DDL_ESCL), one must be able to determine the normal direction of the faces. The normal direction is computed on the slave face. One must therefore in this case use the keyword GROUP_MA_ESCL with mesh cells of “facet” type. ◆ GROUP_MA_MAIT List of the master mesh cells to be put in relation. ◇ DISTANCE_MAX When a slave node is not found (geometrically) in any master mesh cell, the program puts in relation the node and the point (of the boundary) of the nearest mesh cell. If one wishes a slave node “far” from the master mesh cells not to be concerned by the relation, one must use the operand DISTANCE_MAX. This operand makes it possible to give the maximum distance beyond which one will not make a relation. There is no default value for DISTANCE_MAX. Which means that by default, the relation will concern all the slave nodes. ◇ DISTANCE_ALARME = d_ala The keyword DISTANCE_ALARME = d_ala makes it possible to be warned if a slave node is at a distance d > d_ala from the nearest master mesh cell. There is no default value for DISTANCE_ALARME. By default, an alarm is issued if the distance d is greater than 1/10 of the size of the nearest mesh cell (relative criterion). ◇ TYPE_RACCORD This keyword makes it possible to choose the type of the linear relations that one is going to write in order to eliminate the degrees of freedom of the slave nodes. - If TYPE_RACCORD = ’MASSIF’, the nodes are assumed to carry translation degrees of freedom (DX, DY, DZ). If the user does not specify DDL_MAIT='DNOR', one will write (for example in 2D) two linear relations for each slave node: one to eliminate its 'DX', the other to eliminate its 'DY'. - If TYPE_RACCORD = ’COQUE’, the nodes are assumed to carry translation degrees of freedom (DX, DY, DZ) and rotation degrees of freedom (DRX, DRY, DRZ). One will write six linear relations to eliminate the six degrees of freedom of each slave node. - If TYPE_RACCORD = ’MASSIF_COQUE’, the slave nodes are assumed to be of “solid” type (translations: DX, DY, DZ) and the master nodes are assumed to be of “shell” type (three translations and three rotations). The translation degrees of freedom of the slave nodes are eliminated by writing that they are equal to the translations of the facing “master” point. The translations of the master point are computed as if the small segment normal to the shell remained rigid. The figure below shows a “touching” situation in section of a solid and of a shell with the nodes put in relation: the translation kinematics of the point A of the shell is parametrised by the degrees of freedom of the shell ({U},{\Theta}) and its position on the finite element considered, obtained by the projection coming from the slave node A' of the MASSIF mesh. In this figure, one has arranged that only the nodes of the boundary of the MASSIF mesh are considered by the relation with the value of DISTANCE_MAX. - If TYPE_RACCORD = ’COQUE_MASSIF’, the slave nodes are assumed to be of “shell” type (six degrees of freedom: DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ) and the master nodes are assumed to be of “solid” type (DX, DY, DZ). The translation degrees of freedom of the slave nodes are eliminated by writing that they are equal to the translations of the facing “master” point. The rotation degrees of freedom of the slave nodes are eliminated by writing that they are equal to the rotations of the facing “master” point (A) . These rotations of the point A are computed from the translations, parametrised by the degrees of freedom of the master nodes, of two other points A1 and A2 located at +h/2\vec{n} and -h/2\vec{n} , if \vec{n} is a vector normal to the shell and whose length is the thickness h of the shell (see the mandatory keywords in this case EPAIS and CHAM_NORMALE). The figure below shows a “touching” situation in section of a solid and of a shell with the nodes put in relation: the translation kinematics of the point A' of the COQUE mesh is parametrised by the degrees of freedom of the solid ({U}) and its position A on the finite element considered, obtained by the projection coming from the slave node A' of the COQUE mesh. The figure below shows a situation of “abutment” of a solid (master nodes) and of a shell (slave nodes) with the nodes put in relation (see for example the test case SSLS101). ◇ DDL List of the degrees of freedom to which one imposes the relations. The existence of the degrees of freedom is not checked (see § 5.1 for the name of the degrees of freedom). If TYPE_RACCORD=’COQUE’ then the degrees of freedom allowed are: [’DX’|’DY’|’DZ’|’DRX’|’DRY’|’DRZ’] ◇ CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/TRAN The operands CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/TRAN (see § 4.6 ) make it possible to pass from the slave face to the master face. The command first carries out the rotation, then the translation. If these keywords are absent, it is because the geometric transformation is “the identity”, that is the master and slave faces are geometrically coincident. Warning! The sense of the transformation is slave towards master . ◆ EPAIS/CHAM_NORMALE These two keywords are mandatory if TYPE_RACCORD = ’COQUE_MASSIF’: EPAIS gives the thickness of the shell at the level of the relation (assumed constant) and CHAM_NORMALE gives a field at the nodes which contains the direction of the normal to the shell on the nodes of the “slave” mesh cells. The field can be obtained by the command: CHNOR = CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM = ’NOEU_GEOM_R’, OPERATION = ’NORMALE’, MODELE = MODEL, GROUP_MA = ’GMCOQU’) ◇ ELIM_MULT This keyword serves to solve the problem which may arise when one ties several adjacent slave surfaces (that is which have one or more nodes in common). Imagine for example that one writes (in 2D): LIAISON_MAIL=(_F(GROUP_MA_ESCL=’LIGNE_AB’, GROUP_MAIT= ...) _F(GROUP_MA_ESCL=’LIGNE_BC’, GROUP_MAIT= ...)) If the user forces ELIM_MULT=’NON’, the program will treat each occurrence of LIAISON_MAIL independently. The node B , belonging to LIGNE_AB and LIGNE_BC, will therefore be taken into account in two different relations and it is probable that the computation will stop during factorisation of the matrix with the message “Almost zero pivot” if the linear relations generated by LIAISON_MAIL are redundant. Most of the time, the default value ELIM_MULT=’OUI’ is the right choice. The only case where the user might use ELIM_MULT=’NON’ is that of the use of the keyword DDL_ESCL=’DNOR’. If the “slave” normals are not collinear, the linear relations generated will not be redundant. ◇ TRANSF_GEOM_MAIT ◇ TRANSF_GEOM_ESCL The 2 keywords TRANSF_GEOM_[MAIT|ESCL] = (fx, fy, fz) make it possible to carry out one (or two) geometric transformations on the coordinates of the nodes of the master and slave meshes before doing the projection. This geometric transformation is temporary (for the duration of the pairing phase): the meshes are not modified. 5.14 Keyword LIAISON_PROJ LIAISON_PROJ = _F( ◆ MATR_PROJECTION = corresp_2_mailla, ◆ DDL = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", ... liste_dof, ◇ TYPE = / "IDENTITE" (par défaut), / "EXCENTREMENT", ) Factor keyword which makes it possible to define linear relations between the nodes of one and the same model. The coefficients of the linear relations are determined with the help of the command PROJ_CHAMP which makes it possible to have as result concept the matrix of the influence coefficients determined from the shape functions of the elements. It is the same algorithm which is used with the keyword LIAISON_MAIL, where one finds the notion of master and slave mesh cell which one also finds in the command PROJ_CHAMP. 5.14.1 Operands ◆ MATR_PROJECTION Name of the concept coming from the command PROJ_CHAMP. The concept corresponds to the matrix of the coefficients obtained by the option PROJECTION = ’NON’ of the command PROJ_CHAMP. Example: matcoeff = PROJ_CHAMP(PROJECTION = ’NON’, METHODE = ’COLLOCATION’, MAILLAGE_1 = mail, MAILLAGE_2 = mail, VIS_A_VIS = _F(GROUP_MA_2 = ’ARMAT’, GROUP_MA_1 = ’SDALLE’,), ) MAILLAGE_1 and MAILLAGE_2 must correspond to the same mesh. The command AFFE_CHAR_MECA requires the model to be supplied, and the model rests on a mesh. Since one is going to write relations between degrees of freedom of a model, it is mandatory that the meshes be identical. Consistency is checked when LIAISON_PROJ is used. VIS_A_VIS: under this factor keyword the groups make it possible to define the master and slave mesh cells: - GROUP_MA_1 corresponds to the master mesh cells. - GROUP_MA_2 corresponds to the slave mesh cells. ◆ DDL List of the degrees of freedom of the slave nodes to which one imposes the relations. The existence of the degrees of freedom on the slave and master nodes is checked. All the degrees of freedom are allowed. ◇ TYPE = ‘EXCENTREMENT’ Makes it possible, in the case where rotation degrees of freedom exist on the master mesh cells, to impose on the slave nodes displacements which take these rotations into account. The relations are of the following form: - For the degrees of freedom of the slave nodes given under DDL. {DDL}({N}_{{escl}})={\sum}_{i}{{Coeff}}_{i}\ast {DDL}({N}_{{maître}}^{i}) with i: node of the master mesh cell containing the slave node. - In the case where TYPE=’EXCENTREMENT’, the relation on the translation degrees of freedom of the slave nodes becomes: {DDL}({N}_{{escl}})={\sum}_{i}{{Coeff}}_{i}\ast ({DDL}({N}_{{maître}}^{i})+\overrightarrow{\omega ({N}_{{maître}}^{i})}\wedge \overrightarrow{{N}_{{maître}}^{i}{N}_{{escl}}}) The existence of the degrees of freedom on the master and slave nodes is checked. 5.15 Keyword LIAISON_CYCL LIAISON_CYCL = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA_MAIT1 = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_MAIT2 = grma, ◆ | GROUP_MA_ESCL = grma, | GROUP_NO_ESCL = grno, ◇ TRAN = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ CENTRE = float, ◇ COEF_MAIT1 = float, ◇ COEF_MAIT2 = float, ◇ COEF_ESCL = float, ◇ & DDL_MAIT = "DNOR" (ou non renseigné), & DDL_ESCL = "DNOR" (ou non renseigné), ) The keyword LIAISON_CYCL makes it possible to define the linear relations in order to impose cyclic symmetry conditions taking a phase shift into account. It is mainly intended to be used within the restrictive framework of dynamic analysis with cyclic symmetry. The particular feature of this keyword (in the image of LIAISON_MAIL) is to make it possible to link the displacements of nodes without a constraint on the mesh. The meshes of {FACEG} and {FACED} may be incompatible. The cyclic repetition condition applied within the framework of dynamics is based on the mesh-duplication method. The operator therefore starts from the postulate that the initial mesh of a sector is duplicated into two identical meshes in the image of the following figure. In the remainder of this paragraph, one will speak of the “slave” face and of the “master” face. The “tying” of the two faces will be done by writing linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the two faces. The displacements of the nodes of the slave face will be linked to the displacements of their projections on the master face. For each node of the slave face, one will write two (in 2D) or three (in 3D) linear relations. If {FACEG} and {FACED} are not geometrically coincident but there exists an isometry (rotation + translation) between the two, the user must define this isometry (the one which transforms {FACEG} into {FACED} ) by means of the keywords CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/TRAN. The expression of the cyclic symmetry condition for a given inter-sector phase shift \beta and considering G as the slave interface is the following: \left[\begin{array}{c}{q}_{g}^{1}\\ {q}_{g}^{2}\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{cc}{cos}\beta & {sin}\beta \\ -{sin}\beta & {cos}\beta \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}{q}_{d}^{1}\\ {q}_{d}^{2}\end{array}\right] In order to write the linear relations making it possible to take this condition into account, it is necessary to give two occurrences of the factor keyword LIAISON_CYCL: - The first makes it possible to link the degrees of freedom of face G of mesh 1 with face D of the same mesh and face D of mesh 2. The coefficients ( {cos}\beta and {sin}\beta ) must be supplied by the keywords COEF_MAIT1, COEF_MAIT2. - The second makes it possible to link the degrees of freedom of face G of mesh 2 with face D of the same mesh and face D of mesh 1. The coefficients ( -{sin}\beta and {cos}\beta ) must be supplied by the keywords COEF_MAIT1, COEF_MAIT2. Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_NO_ESCL/GROUP_MA_ESCL: These keywords make it possible to define the set of nodes of the slave face. One takes all the nodes specified by the keyword GROUP_NO_ESCL plus all the nodes carried by the mesh cells specified by the keyword GROUP_MA_ESCL. ◇ GROUP_MA_MAIT_1: This keyword makes it possible to define the set of master mesh cells of mesh 1 (or 2) where one will look for the facing nodes of the slave face of mesh 1 or 2. ◇ GROUP_MA_MAIT_2: This keyword makes it possible to define the set of master mesh cells of mesh 1 (or 2) where one will look for the facing nodes of the slave face of mesh 1 or 2. ◇ COEF_MAIT_1/COEF_MAIT_2/COEF_ESCL These keywords make it possible to define the coefficients of the linear relation to be applied; in the case of cyclic symmetry these are the cosines and sines of the inter-sector phase-shift angle considered. These coefficients must therefore be consistent with the definition of the master and slave interfaces. The coefficient COEF_ESCL makes it possible to put a coefficient in front of the slave degrees of freedom. For example: {COEF}\text{\_}{ESCL}({q}_{g}^{1}){=}\left[{COEF}\text{\_}{MAIT1}{\times}{COEF}\text{\_}{MAIT2}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}{q}_{d}^{1}\\ {q}_{d}^{2}\end{array}\right]{=}\left[{cos}\beta {\cdot}{sin}\beta \right]\left[\begin{array}{c}{q}_{d}^{1}\\ {q}_{d}^{2}\end{array}\right] ◇ DDL_MAIT/DDL_ESCL If one wants to tie only the displacements normal to the faces, one must specify DDL_MAIT= ’DNOR’ and DDL_ESCL=’DNOR’. The normal direction being computed on the slave face, one must give facet mesh cells (see GROUP_MA_ESCL). This normal direction is transformed by the possible rotation of the geometric transformation (see CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/ TRAN) in order to determine the normal direction on the master face. ◇ CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/TRAN The operands CENTRE/ANGL_NAUT/TRAN (see § 4.6 ) make it possible to pass from the slave face to the master face. The command first carries out the rotation, then the translation. If these keywords are absent, it is because the geometric transformation is “the identity”, that is the master and slave faces are geometrically coincident. Warning! The sense of the transformation is slave towards master . 5.16 Keyword LIAISON_SOLIDE LIAISON_SOLIDE = _F( ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ DIST_MIN = float, ) The keyword LIAISON_SOLIDE makes it possible to model a non-deformable part of a structure. One imposes linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the nodes of this non-deformable part such that the relative displacements between these nodes are zero, and one possibly imposes the displacements at the values resulting from the translation and/or the rotation. These nodes are defined by the mesh-cell groups and the node groups to which they belong. For the restrictions of use, see § 3.2.1 . In small perturbations, one imposes in 2D ({{nb}}_{{ddl}}{\times}{{nb}}_{{noeud}}–3) relations and in 3D ({{nb}}_{{ddl}}{\times}{{nb}}_{{noeud}}–6) relations, where {{nb}}_{{ddl}} is the number of degrees of freedom per node and {{nb}}_{{noeud}} is the number of nodes of the list given after LIAISON_SOLIDE. A solid is determined by the position of one of its points and of a frame at that point. Relations are written by taking the vector formula expressing a rigid-body motion in small rotations: \overrightarrow{u}(M)=\overrightarrow{u}(A)+\overrightarrow{\Omega}(A)\wedge \overrightarrow{{AM}} where A is an arbitrary node of the solid. For more details, see the document R3.03.02. It is possible to use LIAISON_SOLIDE in large transformations in STAT_NON_LINE (since the problem becomes non-linear) only by imposing that the loading be a follower loading (TYPE_CHARGE=’SUIV’, see U4.51.03). Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_MA, SANS_GROUP_MA, SANS_GROUP_NO The rigid-body kinematic conditions are imposed on the nodes belonging to the mesh cells given by the keywords TOUT, GROUP_MA while possibly excluding some by means of the keywords SANS_ . ◇ DIST_MIN This keyword serves to define a distance (in the units of the mesh) below which one considers that the points of the mesh are coincident. This distance also serves to determine whether points are aligned, that is whether they lie in a cylinder of diameter smaller than {dmin} . By default, {dmin}{=}0.001{\times}{armin} , where {armin} is the smallest edge of the mesh. Notes: If an element has all its nodes in a zone “solidified” by LIAISON_SOLIDE , its strain is zero. The stress state is then also zero, as are the generalised forces if it is a structural element. If the list of nodes to be linked contains only aligned nodes carrying no rotation degree of freedom, then, if the system is to be subjected to a rotation, one must add a fictitious non-aligned node to the list. The other solution is to place oneself under the assumption of large rotations and large displacements (TYPE_CHARGE='SUIV'); one then explicitly imposes on the solid relation that the distances be constant. 5.17 Keyword LIAISON_ELEM | LIAISON_ELEM = _F( ◆ OPTION = / "2D_POU", / "3D_POU", / "3D_POU_ARLEQUIN", / "3D_TUYAU", / "COQ_3D", / "COQ_POU", / "COQ_TUYAU", / "PLAQ_POUT_ORTH", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", '3D_POU') ◇ GROUP_MA_1 = list[grma], ◆ / GROUP_NO_2 = grno, / GROUP_MA_2 = grma, ◇ ANGL_MAX = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'COQ_3D') ◆ GROUP_MA_COQUE = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_MASSIF = grma, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ COEF_RIGI_DRZ = float (défaut: 1e-05), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", '3D_POU_ARLEQUIN') ◇ GROUP_MA_1 = list[grma], ◇ GROUP_MA_2 = list[grma], ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", '2D_POU') ◇ GROUP_MA_1 = list[grma], ◆ / GROUP_NO_2 = grno, / GROUP_MA_2 = grma, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'COQ_POU') or equal_to("OPTION", 'COQ_TUYAU') ◇ GROUP_MA_1 = list[grma], ◇ GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ AXE_POUTRE = list[float], # Si: equal_to("OPTION", '3D_TUYAU') ◇ GROUP_MA_1 = list[grma], ◇ GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ AXE_POUTRE = list[float], ◇ ANGL_MAX = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'PLAQ_POUT_ORTH') ◇ GROUP_MA_1 = list[grma], ◇ GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ◇ ANGL_MAX = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ VERIF_EXCENT = / "NON", ) The keyword LIAISON_ELEM makes it possible to link the kinematics of the interfaces between two different modellings of a structure, taking into account the shape and the degree of approximation of the finite elements on the interface, and without creating artefacts of localised stresses. One can thus transmit the generalised forces or the kinematic conditions without generating “parasitic” stresses. It is advised to place the junction sufficiently far from the zone to be analysed finely, far from a strong geometric singularity (a strong curvature, a corner, a hole…) or from material heterogeneities, or from strong variations of loading, of temperatures... This solution makes it possible to treat situations of “generalised plane strain” type, without being affected by the limitations inherent in this approximation, which is not recommended. Calling “solid part” the piece of structure modelled with 3D isoparametric elements, which may be a particular zone, “zoomed” from a slender structure, this factor keyword makes it possible to model the junction: - Of a solid part with a shell part; - Of a solid part with a beam part R3.03.03 or a pipe element R3.08.06 or a discrete element; - Of a shell part with a beam part R3.03.06 or a pipe element R3.08.06 or a discrete element; The beam (or shell) part is dedicated to the global idealisation of the structure studied, in its part where the geometry is relatively regular. To ensure consistency, it is desirable that the constitutive relations of the constituent materials of the beam (or of the shell) correspond to those modelled in the refined zone in the neighbourhood of the junction. This factor keyword also makes it possible to connect the edge of a 2D structure with a beam or a discrete element. The aim of this feature is not to account for the length scales between the parts to be connected but to allow a simplification of the modelling by replacing a solid or surface part by a beam part for example. The junction is treated by imposing linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the junction of the two parts to be connected, without imposing superfluous relations. The kinematic relations thus created are defined on the geometry of the mesh, and are not updated in a large-displacement situation. One may consult the document: “Modellings of particular zones of slender solids”, EDF/DER CR-MMN 98/099, and also the report “3D beam junctions, 3D shell junctions and generalisations” EDF/DER HI-70/97/001/0. 5.17.1 Option ’COQ_3D’ This option makes it possible to connect a 3D solid part with a part modelled with shell or plate elements. It makes it possible to ensure mechanical continuity between a volume modelling and a surface modelling at the interface. This kinematic relation does indeed let the shell/plate “breathe” through its thickness at the interface: the pinching strain remains free. It is based on a variational formulation, unlike the LIAISON_MAIL relations of TYPE_RACCORD MASSIF_COQUE and COQUE_MASSIF. All the pairs of supports of the finite elements respectively considered {SEG2, SEG3} {TRIA3, TRIA6, QUA4, QUA8} are supported at the interface, the mesh cells having to be compatible between the modelled parts. One will note that Code_Aster does not check the consistency at the interface between the thickness of the solid part and the thickness of the shell or plate part. One can consult an example in the test case v3.03.124. Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_MA_COQUE Mesh-cell group corresponding to the boundary of the domain discretised with shell- or plate-type elements to be connected to the solid part. ◆ GROUP_MA_MASSIF Mesh-cell group corresponding to the boundary of the domain discretised with volume elements to be connected to the shell or plate part. ◆ CARA_ELEM Concept created by the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, containing the geometric characteristics of the shell and plate elements, in particular the thickness. ◇ COEF_RIGI_DRZ A fictitious coefficient which plays a role similar to a rotational stiffness coefficient for the shell and plate elements. This coefficient comes into play when the shell or plate elements present geometric discontinuities (in particular of tangent) — for example in branching zones or zones of strong curvature. 5.17.2 Option ’3D_POU’ This option makes it possible to connect a 3D solid part with a part modelled with Euler or Timoshenko beams. A junction between a 3D solid part and a beam part requires six linear relations. This kinematic relation can also be used to connect a 3D solid part with a discrete element DIS_TR, which makes it possible to control the displacements and the rotations of the interface of the 3D solid part considered, without introducing parasitic stresses (by Poisson effect) or a variational crime , that is without exerting localised forces producing a singularity. The part modelled with beams must have, at the level of the junction, a neutral line perpendicular to the plane of the cross-section connected to the 3D solid part, arriving at its centre of gravity, in order to be able to interpret the generalised forces correctly. One notes that this relation treats only the six translation and rotation degrees of freedom (Euler or Timoshenko), but not the warping of the POU_D_TG elements. One can use the command POST_ELEM, keyword MASS_INER u4.25.01, to compute the position of the centre of inertia of the cross-section of the solid part that is connected. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: This operand defines the surface mesh cells of the solid part modelling the trace of the beam cross-section on this solid part. These mesh cells must have been assigned finite elements of faces of 3D elements beforehand. The solid part must be meshed with quadratic elements because the coefficients of the relations to be imposed are geometric quantities integrated numerically. For these integrals to be evaluated correctly, it is necessary to have quadratic elements. ◆ GROUP_NO_2, GROUP_MA_2: These operands define the node of the beam (or of the discrete element DIS_TR assigned to a mesh cell of type SEG2) to be connected to the solid part. Therefore if one uses GROUP_NO_2, one must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node. If one uses GROUP_MA_2, the mesh cell must be unique and of type POI1, support of a discrete element DIS_TR. ◇ ANGL_MAX Gives the angle (in degrees) making it possible to check whether the mesh cells of the list GROUP_MA_1 have normals making an angle greater than ANGL_MAX between them. If this is the case, an alarm message is issued. 5.17.3 Option ’3D_POU_ARLEQUIN’ This option makes it possible to connect a 3D solid part with a part modelled with Timoshenko beams within the Arlequin framework. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: These operands define the volume mesh cells of the solid part included in the overlap zone. These mesh cells must have been assigned 3D volume elements beforehand. The solid part may be meshed with linear or quadratic elements. HEXA27 mesh cells are however not allowed. ◇ GROUP_MA_2: These operands define the beam -type mesh cells to be connected to the solid part. These mesh cells must have been assigned 1D Timoshenko beam elements beforehand. ◆ CARA_ELEM Concept created by the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, containing the geometric characteristics of the beam, used for the construction of the Arlequin coupling matrices. ◆ CHAM_MATER Concept created by the command AFFE_MATERIAU, containing the characteristics of the materials of the beam, used for the construction of the Arlequin coupling matrices. These characteristics are supposed to be weighted by the user, in the sense of the partition of unity necessary to the Arlequin framework. 5.17.4 Option ’2D_POU’ This option makes it possible to connect a boundary of a 2D surface domain to the end of a part modelled with a beam or a discrete element 2D_DIS_TR. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: This operand defines the boundary mesh cells of the 2D part to be connected to the 1D element. The surface part must be meshed with quadratic elements because the coefficients of the relations to be imposed are geometric quantities integrated numerically. For these integrals to be evaluated correctly, it is necessary to have quadratic elements. ◆ GROUP_NO_2, GROUP_MA_2: These operands define the node of the beam to be connected to the 2D surface domain. If one uses GROUP_NO_2, one must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node; if one uses GROUP_MA_2, the mesh cell must be unique and of type POI1, support of the discrete element 2D_DIS_TR. 5.17.5 Option ’COQ_POU’ This option makes it possible to connect a part modelled with shells or plates with a beam part or a discrete element DIS_TR. The trace of the beam cross-section on the shell part must correspond exactly to the boundary mesh cells defined by GROUP_MA_1. This implies the identity of the centres of inertia and of the areas of the facing shell and beam cross-sections. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: This operand defines the boundary mesh cells of the part meshed with shells or plates (the boundary mesh cells are therefore SEG2 or SEG3 according to the modelling chosen). These mesh cells must have been assigned shell-boundary finite elements beforehand. ◇ GROUP_NO_2: This operand defines the node of the beam (or of the discrete element) to be connected to the shell part. One must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node. ◆ AXE_POUTRE Makes it possible to define the axis of the beam to be connected, whose end is lno2 or lgno2 (1 single node). It is desirable that it be orthogonal to the plane containing the boundary of the shell domain. ◆ CARA_ELEM Concept created by the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, containing the geometric characteristics of the shell (in particular the thickness). 5.17.6 Option ’3D_TUYAU’ This option makes it possible to connect a 3D solid part with a part modelled with pipe elements. A junction between a 3D solid part and a pipe part requires six linear relations for the beam degrees of freedom, plus one relation on the swelling mode, plus twelve relations corresponding to the transmission of Fourier modes two and three of ovalisation of the pipe. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: This operand defines the surface mesh cells of the solid part modelling the trace of the pipe cross-section on this solid part. These mesh cells must have been assigned finite elements of faces of 3D elements beforehand. ◇ GROUP_NO_2: This operand defines the node of the pipe to be connected to the solid part. One must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node. ◆ AXE_POUTRE Defines the axis of the pipe to be connected, whose end is a single node (lgno2). ◆ CARA_ELEM Concept created by the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, containing the geometric characteristics of the pipe. ◇ ANGL_MAX Gives the angle (in degrees) making it possible to check whether the mesh cells of the list GROUP_MA_1 have normals making an angle greater than ANGL_MAX between them. If this is the case, an alarm message is issued. 5.17.7 Option ’COQ_TUYAU’ This option makes it possible to connect a part meshed with shells to a part meshed with pipe elements. The trace of the pipe cross-section on the shell part must correspond exactly to the boundary mesh cells defined by GROUP_MA_1. This implies the identity of the centres of inertia and of the areas of the facing shell and pipe cross-sections. Consequently, junctions of “branch connection” type are impossible . A junction between a shell part and a pipe part requires the same linear relations as the option COQ_POU on the beam degrees of freedom of the pipe element, in addition to the relations on the degrees of freedom of ovalisation, warping and swelling. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: This operand defines the boundary mesh cells of the part meshed with shells (the boundary mesh cells are therefore SEG2 or SEG3 according to the modelling chosen). These mesh cells must have been assigned shell-boundary finite elements beforehand. ◇ GROUP_NO_2: This operand defines the node of the pipe to be connected to the solid part. One must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node. ◆ AXE_POUTRE Defines the axis of the pipe to be connected, whose end is a single node (lgno2). ◆ CARA_ELEM Concept created by the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, containing the geometric characteristics of the pipe and of the shell. 5.17.8 Option ’PLAQ_POUT_ORTH’ This option makes it possible to connect a part meshed with TRI3 and QUA4 elements (modellings DKT, DST and DKTG) with a part modelled by a beam element or a discrete element. This relation makes it possible to avoid introducing a spurious singularity into the response of the shell, by transmitting the forces and moments correctly. Thus, one does not impose a kinematic relation at a single point but one represents this relation by approaching the three-dimensional reality. A typical example is that of a slab supported by pillars. In order to simplify the data input the following checks are not carried out 2: - There is no check that the axis of the beam is perpendicular to the plate; - There is no check between the computation of the mechanical characteristics (S, I, ...) carried out on the mesh cells of the trace of the beam cross-section and the mechanical characteristics assigned to the beam by means of CARA_ELEM. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA_1: This operand defines the mesh cells of the plate which model the trace of the beam cross-section on this part. These mesh cells must have been assigned plate finite elements, modellings DKT, DST and DKTG. ◇ GROUP_NO_2: This operand defines the node of the beam to be connected to the plate. One must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node. ◇ ANGL_MAX Gives the angle (in degrees) making it possible to check whether the mesh cells of the list GROUP_MA_1 have normals making an angle greater than ANGL_MAX between them. If this is the case, an alarm message is issued. ◇ VERIF_EXCENT = ’NON’/’OUI’ The node of the beam must coincide, to within a tolerance, with the centre of gravity of the mesh cells which model the trace of this beam on the slab. If this rule is not respected, two behaviours are possible: - If VERIF_EXCENT=’OUI’, the default behaviour, an error message is issued and the code stops in fatal error; - If VERIF_EXCENT=’NON’, an information message is issued. This operand makes it possible not to be obliged to position the beams exactly at the centre of gravity of the trace of the cross-section, which is not necessarily known when the mesh is built. In the case where this rule is not respected, the user is informed of the distance between the beam node and this centre of gravity either by a fatal error (VERIF_EXCENT=’OUI’) or by the issue of an information message (VERIF_EXCENT=’NON’). 5.18 Keyword LIAISON_MASSIF LIAISON_MASSIF = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA_ESCL = list[grma], ◆ GROUP_MA_MAIT = list[grma], ◆ METHODE = / "LAGRANGIEN", / "NITSCHE", / "PENALISATION", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LAGRANGIEN') ◇ COEF_PENA = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'PENALISATION') or equal_to("METHODE", 'NITSCHE') ◆ COEF_PENA = float, ◇ APPARIEMENT = "MORTAR", # Si: equal_to("APPARIEMENT", "MORTAR") ◇ APPA_TOLE = float (défaut: 1e-08), ◇ AIRE_TOLE = float (défaut: 1e-08), ◇ TYPE_APPA = / "FORCEBRUTE" (par défaut), / "PANG", / "RAPIDE", ), The keyword LIAISON_MASSIF makes it possible to connect the solution of two meshes which are potentially non-conforming at the interface by using a variational formulation R3.03.03 ◆ GROUP_MA_ESCL: List of the slave mesh-cell groups at the interface. ◆ GROUP_MA_MAIT List of the master mesh-cell groups at the interface. ◆ METHODE = / "LAGRANGIEN", / "NITSCHE", / "PENALISATION", Choice of the method used for the junction. See R3.03.03 for the advantages and disadvantages of each. ◆ COEF_PENA Penalisation parameter. The larger it is, the stronger the junction, but this deteriorates the conditioning of the matrix. This parameter is homogeneous to a stress. It must typically be chosen of the order of the local stiffness. The following parameters are identical to those of contact and must be used in the same way. ◆ APPARIEMENT = "MORTAR" The pairing used to compute the junction integrals is based on the mortar method. ◇ APPA_TOLE Tolerance used for the various projection algorithms used during pairing. ◇ AIRE_TOLE If the intersection area between the slave mesh cell and the master mesh cell is smaller than AIRE_TOLE then it will not be retained. This makes it possible to avoid numerical artefacts linked to small variations of intersection. ◇ TYPE_APPA = / "FORCEBRUTE" (par défaut), / "PANG", / "RAPIDE", Choice of the algorithm for determining the intersections of mesh cells. FORCEBRUTE is the most robust but is very costly. The others are faster but may miss intersections in the case of concave geometries. 5.19 Keyword LIAISON_RBE3 LIAISON_RBE3 = _F( ◇ GROUP_NO_MAIT = grno, ◆ DDL_MAIT = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", ◇ GROUP_NO_ESCL = grno, ◆ DDL_ESCL = text, ◇ COEF_ESCL = float (défaut: 1.0), ) The keyword LIAISON_RBE3 makes it possible to define in a general way linear relations of RBE3 type between the degrees of freedom of a master node and of slave nodes, while ensuring transmission of the force torsor. These are relations making it possible to specify the value of certain degrees of freedom of a master node as being the weighted average of certain displacements and of certain rotations of slave nodes. The linear relations produced are such that the forces seen by the master node are distributed to the slave nodes in proportion to their distance to the centre of gravity of the slave nodes. Possible additional weightings supplied by the user can be taken into account. For more details, one may refer to the reference documentation R3.03.08. This option makes it possible to connect a 3D solid part with a part modelled with Euler or Timoshenko beams. A junction between a 3D solid part and a beam part requires six linear relations. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_NO_MAIT: Identifies the master node of the linear relation. One must give only one group, and this group must contain only one node. ◇ GROUP_NO_ESCL: Identification of the slave nodes of the linear relation. ◆ DDL_MAIT Identification of the degrees of freedom of the master node involved in the linear relation. One expects a list comprising at most six entries among ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’, ’DRY’, ’DRZ’. ◆ DDL_ESCL Identification of the degrees of freedom of the slave nodes involved in the linear relation. Either the list has a length equal to the number of slave nodes, or there is only one term. In the latter case, one assumes that this same term corresponds to all the DDL_MAIT. Each term of the list must be a combination of the entries ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’, ’DRY’, ’DRZ’, separated by a hyphen ’-’. ◇ COEF_ESCL List of weighting coefficients of the terms of the linear relation for each slave node. The list must: - Either have the same length as the number of slave nodes; - Or be of length 1 , in which case this coefficient is used for all the slave nodes Example : If one wants to create a relation of RBE3 type between: - The degrees of freedom ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’ of the master node ’NO1’; And: - The degrees of freedom ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’ of the slave node ’NO2’ with the weighting coefficient 0.1 ; - The degrees of freedom ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’ of the slave node ’NO3’ with the weighting coefficient 0.2 ; - The degrees of freedom ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’ of the slave node ’NO4’ with the weighting coefficient 0.3 ; One must write the command: LIAISON_RBE3 = _F( GROUP_NO_MAIT = ’NO1’, DDL_MAIT = (’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’), GROUP_NO_ESCL = (’NO2’, ’NO3’, ’NO4’), DDL_ESCL = (’DX-DY-DZ’, ’DX-DY-DZ-DRX’, ’DX-DY-DZ-DRX’), COEF_ESCL =(0.1, 0.2, 0.3), ) x takes the values 2 and 3 for TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M, and 4, 5 and 6 only for TUYAU_6M To carry out these checks, the user would have to give, in addition to the beam node, the name of the mesh cell assigned by the CARA_ELEM which has as end the junction node. In the great majority of cases, this mesh cell is unknown to the user; it is the meshing software which defines its name. 6 Dirichlet-type loadings for structural elements 6.1 Keyword DDL_POUTRE DDL_POUTRE = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = grma, | GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ | DX = float, | DY = float, | DZ = float, | DRX = float, | DRY = float, | DRZ = float, ◆ / VECT_Y = float, / ANGL_VRIL = float, ◇ GROUP_MA_REPE = grma, ) The keyword DDL_POUTRE makes it possible to block degrees of freedom in a local frame of a beam. The local frame of a beam is defined: - By the axis X determined by the mesh cell to which the node belongs. The mesh cell is oriented towards the specified node. To avoid indeterminacy, the node on which the condition bears must belong to a single SEG. In the case where it belongs to several mesh cells, the user defines the mesh cell giving the local orientation. - By VECT_Y, a vector whose projection on the plane orthogonal to the axis X defines the axis Y . The axis Z is determined with the help of X and Y - By ANGL_VRIL, the twist angle, given in degrees, which makes it possible to orient a local frame about the axis X . Topological assignment: ◆ TOUT, GROUP_MA, GROUP_NO, SANS_GROUP_MA, SANS_GROUP_NO The kinematic conditions are imposed on the nodes given by the keywords TOUT , GROUP_MA , GROUP_NO while possibly excluding some by means of the keywords SANS_ . Components: ◆ DX , DY , DZ , DRX , DRY , DRZ See their meaning in § 5.1 . ◇ GROUP_MA_REPE Definition of the frame of the beam on the last mesh cell. ◇ ANGL_VRIL Twist angle, given in degrees, which makes it possible to orient a local frame about the axis X . ◇ VECT_Y Vector whose projection on the plane orthogonal to the axis X defines the axis Y . The axis Z is determined with the help of X and Y . 6.2 Keyword LIAISON_COQUE LIAISON_COQUE = _F( ◆ | GROUP_MA_1 = grma, | GROUP_MA_2 = grma, | GROUP_NO_1 = grno, | GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA_1 = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO_1 = grno, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA_2 = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO_2 = grno, ) The keyword LIAISON_COQUE makes it possible to represent the junction between shells by means of linear relations. The classical approach assumes that two planes meshed with shells intersect along a straight line which belongs to the mesh of the structure. The pairs of nodes are obtained by placing facing each other two lists of nodes (see § 5.3.1 ). This has the disadvantage of counting twice the volume which is the intersection of the two shells. The idea is therefore to stop the mesh of a shell perpendicular to a given shell at the level of the upper or lower skin of the latter. The volume of the shells has been drawn in solid lines and the mean planes of these shells (which come from the mesh) in dotted lines. The horizontal shell stops at {A}_{1}{A}_{2} and the projection of {A}_{1}{A}_{2} on the mean plane of the vertical shell is {B}_{1}{B}_{2} (which has been drawn in solid lines). The link between the two shells is made by rigid-body relations (see § 5.16 ) between the facing nodes of the segments {A}_{1}{A}_{2} and {B}_{1}{B}_{2} . For example for the nodes {A}_{1} and {B}_{1} , one will write the formula (valid in small rotations): U({B}_{1})=U({A}_{1})+\Omega ({A}_{1})\wedge {A}_{1}{B}_{1} And the equality of the rotations: \Omega ({B}_{1})=\Omega ({A}_{1}) Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_MA_1, GROUP_NO_1: First list of nodes to be put in relation. The nodes are given by the keywords GROUP_MA_1, GROUP_NO_1 while possibly excluding some by means of the keywords SANS_ . These nodes represent the trace of the perpendicular shell on the current shell. In our example, these would be the nodes of the segment {B}_{1}{B}_{2} or of the segment {A}_{1}{A}_{2} . ◆ GROUP_MA_2, GROUP_NO_2: Second list of nodes to be put in relation. The nodes are given by the keywords GROUP_MA_2, GROUP_NO_2 while possibly excluding some by means of the keywords SANS_ . These nodes belong to the perpendicular shell and face the nodes of the first list. The facing is adjusted by the program according to the criterion of smallest distance. In our example if the first list consists of the nodes of {A}_{1}{A}_{2} , the second list consists of the nodes of {B}_{1}{B}_{2} . 7 Neumann-type loadings 7.1 Keyword FORCE_NODALE FORCE_NODALE = _F( ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ | FX = float ou fonction, | FY = float ou fonction, | FZ = float ou fonction, | MX = float ou fonction, | MY = float ou fonction, | MZ = float ou fonction, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ) The factor keyword FORCE_NODALE can be used to apply, to nodes or node groups, nodal forces, defined component by component in the global frame or in an oblique frame defined by three nautical angles. Strictly speaking, the application of a nodal loading is physically incorrect and can cause stress concentrations. It is preferable to use distributed loadings. Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_NO The loading is assigned on the nodes. Components: ◆ FX, FY, FZ, MX, MY, MZ Values of the components of the nodal forces and of the nodal moments applied to the specified nodes. These nodal forces will be superposed on the nodal forces coming, possibly, from other loadings. In axisymmetry, the values correspond to a sector of one radian (divide the real loading by 2\pi ). ◇ ANGL_NAUT List of the three angles, in degrees, which define the oblique frame of application of the nodal forces (the last angles of the list may be omitted if they are zero). The nautical angles make it possible to pass from the global frame of definition of the coordinates of the mesh to any oblique frame (see § 3.9.3 ). By default the angles are identically zero and therefore the force components are defined in the global frame. 7.2 Keyword FORCE_ARETE FORCE_ARETE = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FX = float ou fonction, | FY = float ou fonction, | FZ = float ou fonction, | MX = float ou fonction, | MY = float ou fonction, | MZ = float ou fonction, ) The factor keyword FORCE_ARETE can be used to apply line forces, to an edge of a volume element or of a shell, defined component by component in the global frame. This edge is defined by one or more mesh cells or mesh-cell groups of segment type. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on the mesh cells which are necessarily segments. Components: ◆ FX, FY, FZ, MX, MY, MZ Values of the components of the line forces and of the line moments applied to the specified mesh cells. This loading applies to the following modellings: DKT, DST, Q4G, 3D and COQUE_3D. 7.3 Keyword FORCE_CONTOUR FORCE_CONTOUR = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FX = float ou fonction, | FY = float ou fonction, | FZ = float ou fonction, ), The factor keyword FORCE_CONTOUR can be used to apply line forces to the edge of a 2D domain , defined component by component in the global frame. This contour is defined by one or more mesh cells of segment type. Note: fundamentally it is a line force but the unit is a surface force because one reasons for a unit thickness (plane stresses, plane strains) or divided by 2\pi for the axisymmetric modellings (see § 3.5 ). Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on the mesh cells which are necessarily segments. Components: ◆ FX, FY, FZ Values of the components of the line forces applied to the specified mesh cells. This loading applies to the following modellings: D_PLAN, AXIS and AXIS_FOURIER, including XFEM. 7.4 Keyword FORCE_FACE FORCE_FACE = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FX = float ou fonction, | FY = float ou fonction, | FZ = float ou fonction, ) The factor keyword FORCE_FACE can be used to apply surface forces (therefore of the dimension of a pressure) on a face of a 3D element , defined component by component in the global frame. This face is defined by one or more mesh cells of triangle or quadrangle type. Topological assignment: ◆ GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on the mesh cells which are necessarily triangles or quadrangles. Components: > ◆ FX, FY, FZ Values of the components of the surface forces applied to the specified mesh cells. This loading applies to the following modellings: 3D, 3D_HHM, 3D_HM, 3D_THHM, 3D_THM, 3D_HH2, 3D_THH2M and XFEM.
