This loading may be a follower loading. 7.5 Keyword FORCE_INTERNE FORCE_INTERNE = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FX = float ou fonction, | FY = float ou fonction, | FZ = float ou fonction, ) The factor keyword FORCE_INTERNE can be used in two cases: - To apply volume forces on a 3D domain , defined component by component in the global frame. This domain is defined by one or more mesh cells of hexahedron , tetrahedron , pyramid or pentahedron type. - To apply volume forces on a 2D domain , defined component by component in the global frame. This domain is defined by one or more mesh cells of triangle or quadrangle type. Topological assignment: ◆ TOUT, GROUP_MA Components: The loading is assigned on the mesh cells which are necessarily triangles or quadrangles in 2D and hexahedra, tetrahedra, pyramids or pentahedra in 3D. ◆ FX, FY, FZ Values of the components of the volume forces applied to the specified mesh cells. For the 3D case, this loading applies to the following modellings: 3D , 3D_SI , 3D_INCO , 3D_HHMD , 3D_HMD , 3D_THHD , 3D_THHMD , 3D_THMD , 3D_THHM , 3D_THM , 3D_HM , 3D_THH , 3D_HHM. For the 2D case, this loading applies to the following modellings: C_PLAN , D_PLAN , AXIS , AXIS_FOURIER , AXIS_SI , AXIS_INCO , AXIS_THHM , AXIS_HM , AXIS_THH , AXIS_HHM, AXIS_THM , D_PLAN_THHM , D_PLAN_HM , D_PLAN_THH , D_PLAN_HHM , D_PLAN_THM . 7.6 Keyword PRES_REP PRES_REP = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = grma, | FISSURE = fiss_xfem, ◆ | PRES = float ou fonction, | CISA_2D = float ou fonction, ) The factor keyword PRES_REP can be used to apply: - a pressure to a continuum domain in 2D or 3D or to fluid/structure interface elements ( _FLUI_STRU); - a pressure on a shell of type COQUE_3D; - a shear to a 2D continuum domain; - a pressure on the lips of an XFEM crack. Topological assignment: ◆ |TOUT, GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on the mesh cells which are necessarily segments in 2D and triangles or quadrangles in 3D. ◆ | FISSURE The imposition of a pressure on the lips of an X-FEM crack is done by the specific keyword FISSURE, since no mesh-cell group corresponds to the lips. One then supplies the name or names of the cracks (coming from the command DEFI_FISS_XFEM[U4.82.08]) on which one wishes to apply the pressure. Warning: it is not possible to apply a pressure loading on the lips of an XFEM model of cohesive type. ◆ | PRES Value of the imposed pressure. For the isoparametric elements (2D or 3D), the pressure is positive in the sense opposite to the normal to the element. Let \sigma be the stress tensor; the imposed loading is: {\sigma}_{ij}{n}_{i}{n}_{j}=-p{n}_{i}{n}_{j} . This loading applies to the following modellings: AXIS, D_PLAN, C_PLAN, AXIS_FOURIER, D_PLAN_HHM, D_PLAN_HM, D_PLAN_THHM, D_PLAN_THM, AXIS_HHM, AXIS_HM, AXIS_THHM, AXIS_THM, TUYAU_3M, TUYAU_6M, 3D_HHM, 3D_HM, 3D_THHM, 3D_THM, 3D and COQUE_3D. For the fluid-structure interface elements, this loading applies to FLUI_STRU, 2D_FLUI_STRU and AXIS_FLUI_STRU. In the case of a “function” pressure, the dependence on the geometry may be made with respect to the initial geometry with the parameters X, Y and Z or with respect to the updated geometry (only if TYPE_CHAR = ’SUIV’) with the parameters XF, YF and ZF. Notes: - Pressures of “function” type are for the moment not compatible with the modelling COQUE_3D and COQUE_SOLIDE - For elements of type COQUE_SOLIDE, a volume pinching contribution is added to the loadings assigned on the skin elements. The process is automatic when the loading is assigned ◆ | CISA_2D Value of the imposed shear. The shear is positive along the tangent to the element. This loading applies to the following modellings: AXIS, D_PLAN, C_PLAN and AXIS_FOURIER. 7.7 Keyword EVOL_CHAR EVOL_CHAR = evol_char The factor keyword EVOL_CHAR can be used to apply loadings evolving in time of type evol_char produced by LIRE_RESU and containing pressure fields (corresponding to a loading of type PRES_REP), volume force densities in 2D or 3D (corresponding to a loading of type FORCE_INTERNE) and surface force densities in 2D or 3D (corresponding to a loading of type FORCE_FACE and FORCE_CONTOUR). Some of these loadings may be follower loadings (see § 3.6.2 ), but since it is the loading identified by EVOL_CHAR which is declared potentially as a follower loading, if the latter contains a single loading which cannot be one, then an error message is issued. 7.8 Keyword EFFE_FOND EFFE_FOND = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA_INT = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ PRES = float ou fonction, ) The factor keyword EFFE_FOND can be used to compute the end effect on a piping branch (3D modelling exclusively) subjected to an internal pressure P . The cross-section of the piping must be modelled in full, without symmetry . Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_ MA Set of the surface mesh cells (triangles or quadrangles) modelling the material cross-section of the piping (gmat in the figure) where the pressure will be applied. This surface must have been oriented according to the same convention as for the loading PRES_REP (cf. § 7.6 ). ◆ GROUP_MA_INT Set of the line mesh cells (segments) modelling the contour of the hole (gtrou in the figure). Knowledge of these mesh cells is necessary because one needs to compute the area of the hole. Indeed, the resultant force (or end effect) due to the plugging of the hole at the end is: {F}_{b}=\pi {R}_{i}^{2}P This force or end effect is applied on the wall of the tube (gmat). The corresponding distributed force is then: {F}_{p}=\frac{\pi {R}_{i}^{2}}{\pi \left({R}_{e}^{2}-{R}_{i}^{i}\right)}P=P\frac{{S}_{\mathit{trou}}}{{S}_{\mathit{mat}}} ◆ PRES Internal pressure of the piping. One will in practice apply {F}_{p} to gmat (a positive value corresponding to a force oriented in the sense opposite to the outward normal and an end effect inducing a tension on the piping). 7.9 Keyword PESANTEUR PESANTEUR = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ GRAVITE = float, ◆ DIRECTION = float, ) The factor keyword PESANTEUR can be used to apply a gravity field on the model. g represents the intensity of the gravity field and ({a}_{p},{b}_{p},{c}_{p}) specifies the direction and the sense of application of the field. The loading which results from it is of the form: \rho g\frac{({a}_{p}i+{b}_{p}j+{c}_{p}k)}{\sqrt{{a}_{p}^{2}+{b}_{p}^{2}+{c}_{p}^{2}}} where (i,j,k) is the global Cartesian frame, and \rho is the density defined as a characteristic of the material (see the operators DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 and AFFE_MATERIAU U4.43.03). There can be only one occurrence of this keyword in AFFE_CHAR_MECA . Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA By default, this field applies to the whole model. It is possible to restrict it to a part of the model by means of the keyword GROUP_MA, which specifies the mesh cells on which the field applies (this possibility, which has no physical meaning, is nevertheless very useful for applying a gravity field progressively). ◆ GRAVITE Acceleration of gravity. ◆ DIRECTION Direction of gravity. 7.10 Keyword ROTATION ROTATION = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ VITESSE = float, ◆ AXE = float, ◇ CENTRE = float, ) The factor keyword ROTATION can be used to apply a force field equivalent to the centrifugal force applied to a rotating structure. Let \omega be the rotation speed and ({a}_{r},{b}_{r},{c}_{r}) the axis of rotation. \omega =\omega \frac{({a}_{r}i+{b}_{r}j+{c}_{r}k)}{\sqrt{{a}_{r}^{2}+{b}_{r}^{2}+{c}_{r}^{2}}} \omega =\omega \frac{({a}_{r}i+{b}_{r}j+{c}_{r}k)}{\sqrt{{a}_{r}^{2}+{b}_{r}^{2}+{c}_{r}^{2}}} The loading which results from it is of the form: f=\rho (\omega \mathrm{\wedge }\mathit{OM})\mathrm{\wedge }\omega Where O is the origin of the coordinates and M a current point of the structure, with \rho the density defined as a characteristic of the material (see the operators DEFI_MATERIAU[U4.43.01] and AFFE_MATERIAU[U4.43.03]). There can be only one occurrence of this keyword in AFFE_CHAR_MECA . Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA By default, this field applies to the whole model. It is possible to restrict it to a part of the model by means of the keyword GROUP_MA, which specifies the mesh cells on which the field applies. ◆ VITESSE Rotation speed. ◆ AXE Axis of rotation. For plane modellings, the axis of rotation must be in the direction Oz and for axisymmetric and Fourier modellings, it must be in the direction Oy . ◇ CENTRE If the centre of rotation is not the origin (default), one can specify its coordinates (x, y, z). For axisymmetric and Fourier modellings, the centre must be the origin. One can vary the rotation speed in time by decomposing the rotation in a multiplicative way between spatial loading and evolution in time \omega (t)={\omega}_{0}f(t) , then by multiplying the load by a multiplier function (keyword FONC_MULT) in the transient analysis. However, care must be taken: the loading \rho (\omega \wedge \mathrm{OM})\wedge \omega being proportional to the square of the rotation speed, \omega {(t)}^{2} , one must assign the square of the evolution in time, f{(t)}^{2} , after FONC_MULT. 7.11 Keyword PRE_SIGM PRE_SIGM = _F( ◆ SIGM = cham_elem / carte, ) The factor keyword PRE_SIGM can be used to apply a prestress {\sigma}_{\mathit{pre}} . This loading makes it possible to apply mean volume stresses, globally uniform (2D or 3D), to a volume domain. The elementary right-hand side computed will be: {\int}_{\mathit{Ve}}{\sigma}_{\mathit{pre}}:\varepsilon (v\text{ }){\mathit{dV}}_{e} This loading is known under the option FORC_NODA which one finds in the command CALC_CHAMP or during the Newton prediction phase of the operator STAT_NON_LINE. The stress field sigm is of type carte or cham_elga. It may come from CREA_CHAMP or have been computed elsewhere. One must not confuse this prestress with the initial stress {\sigma}_{\mathit{ini}} used in non-linear analysis, because this prestress does not intervene directly in the expression of the constitutive law. This prestress field is used as a right-hand side in the resolutions of MECA_STATIQUE and STAT_NON_LINE. 7.12 Keyword PRE_EPSI PRE_EPSI = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = grma, | EPSI = cham_elem / carte, ◆ | EPXX = float ou fonction, | EPYY = float ou fonction, | EPZZ = float ou fonction, | EPXY = float ou fonction, | EPXZ = float ou fonction, | EPYZ = float ou fonction, | EPX = float ou fonction, | KY = float ou fonction, | KZ = float ou fonction, | EXX = float, | EYY = float, | EXY = float, | KXX = float, | KYY = float, | KXY = float, | VECT_N = float, # Si: exists("VECT_N") ◆ | KN1 = float ou fonction, | KN2 = float ou fonction, ) The factor keyword PRE_EPSI can be used to apply a prestrain {\varepsilon}_{\mathit{pre}} . It is a strain loading applied to a 2D, 3D or structural element. The elementary right-hand side computed will be: {\int}_{\mathit{Ve}}A{\varepsilon}_{\mathit{pre}}:\varepsilon (v\text{ }){\mathit{dV}}_{e} where A denotes the elasticity tensor (recovered in the material field for all the laws for which the elastic characteristics are defined). One must not confuse this prestrain with the initial strain {\varepsilon}_{\mathit{ini}} used in non-linear analysis, because this prestrain does not intervene directly in the expression of the constitutive law. This prestrain can be used for example to solve the elementary problems determining the elastic correctors in the basic cell (2D, 3D), in periodic homogenisation. The homogenised elasticity coefficients are obtained by computing with the operator POST_ELEM U4.81.22 the keyword ENER_POT, that is the potential energy of elastic strain at equilibrium from the correctors. But it can serve for other applications. 7.12.1 Direct assignment of a map or of a strain field ◆ EPSI The maps come from CREA_CHAMP/AFFE and the fields of type ELGA come from another analysis. 7.12.2 Topological assignment ◆ TOUT, GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on these mesh cells. 7.12.3 Components for the isoparametric elements ◆ EPXX, EPYY, EPZZ, EPXY, EPXZ, EPYZ Values of the components of the initial strain tensor in the global frame for the 2D or 3D isoparametric elements (C_PLAN, AXIS, D_PLAN, 3D, 3D_SI, AXIS_SI, D_PLAN_SI) 7.12.4 Components for the beam elements The modellings compatible with the features described here are: POU_D_E, POU_D_T, POU_D_TG, POU_D_EM, POU_D_TGM. With homothetic beams, this loading is allowed only if the cross-section characteristics are such that: A1 = A2, IY1 = IY2 and IZ1 = IZ2. These conditions are imposed because it is for the moment not possible to obtain different forces at the two nodes of one and the same element. ◆ EPX Constant value per element of the elongation along the local axis of the beam. ◆ KY Constant value per element of the curvature variation along the local axis y , -\frac{d{\theta}_{y}}{\mathit{dx}} , of the beam. ◆ KZ Constant value per element of the curvature variation along the local axis z , \frac{d{\theta}_{z}}{\mathit{dx}} , of the beam. ◆ VECT_N (Three-dimensional) direction v_n making it possible to define the curvature variations in a frame different from the local y and the local z . Let x be the first vector of the local basis (axis of the beam); one then defines y_n = \frac{v_n \wedge x}{\lVert v_n \wedge x \rVert} and z_n = x \wedge y_n . One cannot use this operand with KY and KZ. ◆ KN1 Constant value per element of the curvature variation along the local axis y_n , -\frac{d{\theta}_{y_n}}{\mathit{dx}} , of the beam. ◆ KN2 Constant value per element of the curvature variation along the local axis z_n , \frac{d{\theta}_{z_n}}{\mathit{dx}} , of the beam. Case of functions The operands EPX, KY, KZ, KN1 and KN2 may be functions. For this one must use the command AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F. The functions supplied may depend on the parameters: - X, Y and Z (coordinates of the nodes) - INST (values of the analysis time instant) - ABSC (values of the curvilinear abscissa) In the case ABSC, it is necessary to have built the curvilinear abscissae by using the command MODI_MAILLAGE, keyword ABSC_CURV. The functions supplied are evaluated at the middle of the beam elements. 7.12.5 Components for the shell elements (DKT, DST, Q4G) ◆ EXX, EYY, EZZ Constant values per element of the membrane strains in the local frame of the shell. ◆ KXX, KYY, KZZ Constant values per element of the curvature variations in the local frame of the shell. 7.13 Keyword VECT_ASSE VECT_ASSE = cham_no The factor keyword VECT_ASSE can be used to apply a right-hand side in the form of a CHAM_NO. This CHAM_NO is transmitted to these commands via the name of the loading. The displacement field chamno is of type cham_no. It may come from CREA_CHAMP or have been computed elsewhere. 8 Neumann-type loadings for structural elements 8.1 Keyword FORCE_POUTRE FORCE_POUTRE = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = / "VENT", / "FORCE" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("TYPE_CHARGE", 'FORCE') ◆ | FX = float, | FY = float, | FZ = float, | MX = float, | MY = float, | MZ = float, | N = float, | VY = float, | VZ = float, | MT = float, | MFY = float, | MFZ = float, | MGX = float, | MGY = float, | MGZ = float, # Si: equal_to("TYPE_CHARGE", 'VENT') ◆ | FX = formule / nappe / fonction, | FY = formule / nappe / fonction, | FZ = formule / nappe / fonction, | N = formule / nappe / fonction, | VY = formule / nappe / fonction, | VZ = formule / nappe / fonction, ) The factor keyword FORCE_POUTRE can be used to apply line forces, on beam-type elements defined on the whole mesh or on one or more mesh cells. The forces are defined component by component, either in the global frame, or in the local frame of the element defined by the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01. One thus defines the force of type VENT. If p is the pressure exerted by the wind on a plane surface normal to its direction, \nu =({\nu}_{x},{\nu}_{y},{\nu}_{z}) the unit vector having the direction and the sense of the wind velocity, and d the diameter of the cable on which the wind is exerted, then: \mathit{Fx}=pd{\nu}_{x} \mathit{Fy}=pd{\nu}_{y} \mathit{Fz}=pd{\nu}_{z} Note that one must remain consistent in each occurrence of the factor keyword FORCE_POUTRE: either all the components are defined in the global frame or all the components are defined in the local frame of definition of the beam. Topological assignment: .. code-block:: text > ◆ TOUT, GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on these mesh cells which are necessarily segments. ◆ TYPE_CHARGE = ’FORCE’/’VENT’ Specifies the type of load. - For TYPE_CHARGE = ’FORCE’ Components: ◆ FX, FY, FZ, MX, MY, MZ Values of the components of the forces or of the line moments (in the global frame) applied to the specified mesh cells, with: - \mathit{fx} , \mathit{fy} , \mathit{fz} : forces along x , y and z - \mathit{mx} , \mathit{my} , \mathit{mz} : moments along x , y and z This loading applies to the following modellings: POU_D_T, POU_D_E, POU_D_TGM and POU_D_TG. Distributed moments can be applied only on straight beams of constant cross-section. ◆ N, VY, VZ, MT, MFY, MFZ, MGX, MGY, MGZ Values of the components of the generalised forces (in the local frame of the beam) which are line forces applied to the specified mesh cells, with: - n : tension/compression force - \mathit{vy} : shear force along y - \mathit{vz} : shear force along z - \mathit{mt} : torsion moment - \mathit{mfy} : bending moment along y - \mathit{mfz} : bending moment along z - \mathit{mgx} : moment of the assembly grid along x - \mathit{mgy} : moment of the assembly grid along y - \mathit{mgz} : moment of the assembly grid along z This loading applies to the following modellings: POU_D_T, POU_D_E, POU_D_TGM, POU_D_TG and POU_D_EM. Distributed moments can be applied only on straight beams of constant cross-section. In the case where the force is given by a function, therefore by AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F, the parameters of the function may be: 'INST': the time 'X', 'Y', 'Z': the position of the node where the force is computed 'DX', 'DY', 'DZ': the direction vector of the structural element 'VITE_X', 'VITE_Y', 'VITE_Z': the structural velocity of the node 'ACCE_X’, ’ACCE_Y’, ’ACCE_Z’: the structural acceleration of the node - For TYPE_CHARGE = ’VENT’ Components: ◆ FX, FY, FZ Values of the components of the forces or of the line moments (in the global frame) applied to the specified mesh cells, with: - \mathit{fx} , \mathit{fy} , \mathit{fz} : forces along x , y and z This loading applies to the following modellings: POU_D_T, POU_D_E, POU_D_TGM and POU_D_TG. ◆ N, VY, VZ Values of the components of the generalised forces (in the local frame of the beam) which are line forces applied to the specified mesh cells, with: - n : tension/compression force - \mathit{vy} : shear force along y - \mathit{vz} : shear force along z This loading applies to the following modellings: POU_D_T, POU_D_E , POU_D_TGM and POU_D_TG. 8.2 Keyword FORCE_TUYAU FORCE_TUYAU = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ PRES = float, ) The factor keyword FORCE_TUYAU can be used to apply a pressure on pipe elements, defined by one or more mesh cells or mesh-cell groups. ◆ TOUT, GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on these mesh cells which are necessarily segments. ◆ PRES Value of the imposed pressure (real or function). The pressure is positive when the pressure is internal to the piping. This loading applies to the modellings TUYAU_3M and TUYAU_6M. 8.3 Keyword FORCE_COQUE | FORCE_COQUE = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FX = float, | FY = float, | FZ = float, | MX = float, | MY = float, | MZ = float, | PRES = float, | F1 = float, | F2 = float, | F3 = float, | MF1 = float, | MF2 = float, ◇ PLAN = / "SUP", / "INF", / "MOY", / "MAIL" (par défaut), ), The factor keyword FORCE_COQUE can be used to apply surface forces on shell-type elements (DKT, DST, Q4G, COQUE_3D…). The operands of FORCE_COQUE may be defined: - In the global frame with the keywords FX, FY, FZ, MX, MY and MZ if one wants to impose a torsor of surface forces by component. - The component PRES imposes a pressure normal to the surface; - In a reference frame defined on each mesh cell with the keywords F1, F2, F3, MF1 and MF2 if one wants to impose a torsor of surface forces by component; the frame is built around the normal to the shell element ({z}_{\mathit{ref}}) and a fixed direction ({x}_{\mathit{ref}}) (for the mesh-cell group) defined by the keyword ANGL_REP at the same time as the thickness of the shell (see the factor keyword COQUE of the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01). If it is applied on COQUE_3D elements, this loading may be of follower type but only if it is a pressure (operand PRES). It is also possible to define a torsor of surface forces on the middle, lower or upper plane, or on the plane of the mesh. If one denotes by d the offset, h the thickness of the shell, (\mathit{F2X},\mathit{F2Y},\mathit{F2Z},\mathit{M2X},\mathit{M2Y},\mathit{M2Z}) the force torsor on the plane defined by the user (possibly offset) and (\mathit{F1X},\mathit{F1Y},\mathit{F1Z},\mathit{M1X},\mathit{M1Y},\mathit{M1Z}) the force torsor in the plane of the mesh. The transformation formulae are the following: - If the computation plane is the plane of the mesh: \mathit{F2}=\mathit{F1} \mathit{M2}=\mathit{M1} - If the computation plane is the offset middle sheet: \mathit{F2}=\mathit{F1} \mathit{M2X}=\mathit{M1X}–\mathit{dx}\mathit{F1Y} \mathit{M2Y}=\mathit{M1Y}+\mathit{dx}\mathit{F1X} - If the computation plane is the offset upper sheet: \mathit{F2}=\mathit{F1} \mathit{M2X}=\mathit{M1X}–d+\frac{h}{2}.\mathit{F1Y} \mathit{M2Y}=\mathit{M1Y}+d+\frac{h}{2}.\mathit{F1X} - If the computation plane is the offset lower sheet: \mathit{F2}=\mathit{F1} \mathit{M2X}=\mathit{M1X}–d-\frac{h}{2}.\mathit{F1Y} \mathit{M2Y}=\mathit{M1Y}+d-\frac{h}{2}.\mathit{F1X} Note that one must remain consistent in each occurrence of the factor keyword FORCE_COQUE: either everything in force component in the global frame or everything in force component in the frame of definition of the shell. The applied pressure is positive in the sense opposite to the normal to the element (defined by the orientation of each mesh cell (cf. [§ 3.9.1 ]). The loading is assigned on these mesh cells which are necessarily triangles or quadrangles. ◆ PRES Value of the imposed pressure (real or function), normal to the shell. Components: ◆ FX, FY, FZ, MX, MY, MZ Value of the forces and of the moments in the global frame. Components: ◆ F1, F2 Membrane forces along {x}_{\mathit{ref}} and {y}_{\mathit{ref}} . Components: ◆ F3 Normal force along {z}_{\mathit{ref}} . Components: ◆ MF1, MF2 Bending moments of axis X and Y Definition of PLAN for writing the force torsor: - ’MOY’: one applies the force torsor on the offset middle sheet; - ’INF’: one applies the force torsor on the lower skin; - ’SUP’: one applies the force torsor on the upper skin; - ’MAIL’: one applies the force torsor at the level of the plane of the mesh. 8.4 Keyword FORCE_COQUE_FO FORCE_COQUE_FO = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ PRES = formule / nappe / fonction, ) The factor keyword FORCE_COQUE_FO makes it possible to assign pressures (only PRES is available) in the form of functions which do not depend on time. It is in a way equivalent to AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F/FORCE_COQUE but makes it possible, when the function does not depend on time, to evaluate this function only once and not at each analysis time instant. The functions or formulae supplied may depend on the parameters X, Y, Z, EP and RHO. Where EP is the thickness of the mesh cell (in this case, one must supply the keyword CARA_ELEM), and where RHO is the density of the mesh cell (in this case, one must supply the keyword CHAM_MATER). 9 Other loadings 9.1 Keyword LIAISON_INTERF LIAISON_INTERF = _F( ◆ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macr_elem_dyna, ◇ TYPE_LIAISON = / "RIGIDE" (par défaut), / "SOUPLE", ) The factor keyword LIAISON_INTERF makes it possible to define linear relations between the physical degrees of freedom of the interfaces of the part of the model in finite elements and the generalised coordinates of modes of reduced representation of the interface motions contained in certain macro-elements of static condensation. It can be used with a model containing both finite elements and static macro-elements condensing certain subdomains. ◆ MACR_ELEM_DYNA Name of the macr_elem_dyna which serves to define the linear relations between the physical degrees of freedom of the interface between the non-condensed domain modelled in finite elements and a domain condensed by the macro-element, and the components of the nodes assimilated to generalised coordinates of interface-motion modes. This is necessary only when the interface-motion modes are a reduced basis of all the constrained modes, each corresponding to a displacement mode for each physical degree of freedom of the interface. One thus generates relations of type LIAISON_DDL whose coefficients are computed in a way that is transparent for the user, between the nodes of the dynamic interface of the macro-element and those associated with the reduction basis which served to build the macro-element. ◇ TYPE_LIAISON = ’RIGIDE’/’SOUPLE’ - If ’RIGIDE’, one writes the relation between the physical degrees of freedom of the interface {U}_{\Sigma} and the components of the nodes assimilated to generalised coordinates q of interface-motion modes \Phi in the form of a single product: {U}_{\Sigma}={\Phi}_{q} . This choice makes it possible to have a relation more rigid than by taking into account all the constrained modes, each corresponding to a displacement mode for each physical degree of freedom of the interface. - If ’SOUPLE’, one writes the relation between the physical degrees of freedom of the interface {U}_{\Sigma} and the components of the nodes assimilated to generalised coordinates q of interface-motion modes \Phi in the form of a double product: {\Phi}^{T}{U}_{\Sigma}={\Phi}^{T}\Phi q . This choice makes it possible to have a relation more flexible than by taking into account all the constrained modes, each corresponding to a displacement mode for each physical degree of freedom of the interface. 9.2 Keyword RELA_CINE_BP RELA_CINE_BP = _F( ◆ CABLE_BP = cabl_precont, ◇ RELA_CINE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("RELA_CINE", 'OUI') ◇ SIGM_BPEL = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("RELA_CINE", 'NON') ◇ SIGM_BPEL = "OUI", ◇ TYPE_EPX = / "ADHE" (par défaut), / "GLIS", / "FROT", ◇ DIST_MIN = float, ) This type of loading can be defined for a mechanical system comprising a concrete structure and its prestressing cables. The initial tension profiles in the cables, as well as the coefficients of the kinematic relations between the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the cables and the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the concrete structure, are determined beforehand by the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP U4.42.04. The cabl_precont concepts produced by this operator supply all the information necessary for the definition of the loading. Multiple occurrences are allowed for the factor keyword RELA_CINE_BP, in order to make it possible, in one and the same call to the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA, to define the contributions of each of the groups of cables which have been the subject of distinct calls to the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP U4.42.04. With each group of cables considered, defined by a cabl_precont concept, is associated one occurrence of the factor keyword RELA_CINE_BP. The loading thus defined then serves to compute the equilibrium state of the whole concrete structure / prestressing cables. However, taking this type of loading into account is not effective in all the resolution operators. The loading of type RELA_CINE_BP is for the moment recognised only by the operator STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03, incremental constitutive behaviours exclusively. ◆ CABLE_BP Concept of type cabl_precont produced by the operator DEFI_CABLE_BP U4.42.04. This concept supplies on the one hand the map of the initial stresses in the elements of the cables of one and the same group, and on the other hand the lists of the kinematic relations between the degrees of freedom of the nodes of these cables and the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the concrete structure. ◇ SIGM_BPEL = ’OUI’/’NON’ Text-type indicator by which one specifies whether the initial stresses in the cables are taken into account; the default value is ’NON’. In the case ’NON’, only the kinematic linking is taken into account. This is useful if one chains STAT_NON_LINE analyses when one has prestressing cables. For the first STAT_NON_LINE one must have set ’OUI’, so that the tension is set up in the cables. On the other hand, for the following STAT_NON_LINE, one must consider as loading only the kinematic relations and therefore define the loading with SIGM_BPEL = ’NON’, otherwise the tension is counted twice. Since the restitution of the macro-command for tensioning the cables, the user should no longer need to do an AFFE_CHAR_MECA with SIGM_BPEL = ’OUI’; this should thus avoid the risks of error. ◇ RELA_CINE = ’OUI’/’NON’ Text-type indicator by which one specifies whether the kinematic relations between the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the cables and the degrees of freedom of the nodes of the concrete structure are taken into account; default value ’OUI’. ◇ DIST_MIN = float See LIAISON_SOLIDE §:ref:5.16 . ◇ TYPE_EPX = ’ADHE’/’GLIS’/’FROT’ This keyword has an effect only in CALC_EUROPLEXUS. It makes it possible to indicate whether one wishes total cable-concrete relations (that is in the 3 directions of space, corresponding to this Aster loading), sliding relations or frictional relations. 9.3 Keyword VITE_FACE VITE_FACE = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ / VNOR = float, / DIRECTION = float, # Si: exists("DIRECTION") ◆ VITE = float, ) The factor keyword VITE_FACE makes it possible to apply velocities to a face in the case of the modelling 2D_FLUIDE, AXIS_FLUIDE, 3D_FLUIDE or fluid/structure interface elements ( _FLUI_STRU). Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on the mesh cells which are necessarily segments in 2D and triangles or quadrangles in 3D. There are two ways of assigning a velocity: 1. If one supplies VNOR, then the velocity (of norm VNOR) will be normal to the face on which it is applied (defined by GROUP_MA); 2. If one supplies DIRECTION which gives the direction of the velocity then VITE will be the norm of this velocity. This method can be used only if one has chosen a formulation of type U_PHI (keyword in AFFE_MODELE). The direction and the norm (VNOR or VITE) may be reals or functions. 9.4 Keyword ONDE_PLANE ONDE_PLANE =_F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ TYPE_ONDE = / "S", / "P", / "SV", / "SH", ◆ DIRECTION = (kx,ky,kz), ◆ FONC_SIGNAL = f, ◇ DEPL_IMPO = fd, ◇ COOR_SOURCE = (x0, y0, z0), # Si: exists("COOR_SOURCE") ◇ COOR_REFLECHI = (x1, y1, z1), ) The factor keyword ONDE_PLANE (only one occurrence is allowed) makes it possible to impose a seismic loading by plane wave, corresponding to the loadings classically encountered during soil-structure interaction analyses by the integral equations (see R4.05.01). In harmonic regime, an elastic plane wave is characterised by its direction, its angular frequency and its type (wave P for the compression waves, waves S , \mathit{SV} or \mathit{SH} for the shear waves). In transient regime, the datum of the angular frequency, corresponding to a wave stationary in time, must be replaced by the datum of a displacement profile whose propagation in the course of time in the direction of the wave will be taken into account. More precisely, one characterises: - A wave P by the function u(x,t)=f\left(k\cdot x-{C}_{p}t\right) ; - A wave S by the function u(x,t)=f\left(k\cdot x-{C}_{s}t\right)\wedge k ; With: - k the unit direction vector; - f the profile of the wave given along the direction k ; There can be only one occurrence of this keyword in AFFE_CHAR_MECA . Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA The loading is assigned on the mesh cells of absorbing boundaries concerned by the introduction of the incident wave. If nothing is given, by default, all the mesh cells of the modelling ABSO are concerned. ◇ COOR_SOURCE This list of real parameters makes it possible to determine the phase shift in time due to the passage of the wave, by indicating the coordinates of the entry point {\mathrm{x}}_{0} of the plane-wave loading into the structure. If this parameter is not present, then one will supply the operand FONC_SIGNAL with a nappe of time signals. ◇ COOR_REFLECHI This list of real parameters makes it possible to take the reflected wave into account, activated if one gives the coordinates of the exit point {\mathrm{x}}_{1} . In this case, the expression of the profile of the wave taking into account the spatial phase shift linked to the passage of the wave \dot{f}\left(k.(\mathrm{x}-{\mathrm{x}}_{0})-{C}_{m}t\right) then becomes \dot{f}\left(k.(\mathrm{x}-{\mathrm{x}}_{0})-{C}_{m}t\right)+\dot{f}\left(k.(2{\mathrm{x}}_{1}-{\mathrm{x}}_{0}-\mathrm{x})-{C}_{m}t\right) with m=S or P . Figure 9.4-1: Diagram of the propagation of an inclined plane wave in a 2D model To clarify the use of the operands COOR_SOURCE and COOR_REFLECHI one refers to the diagram in the figure. If one considers a plane wave inclined by an angle \alpha to the vertical, one identifies in an obvious way the first point which comes into contact with the domain of study, that is the point {\mathrm{x}}_{0} . This point is considered as the source point of the incident wave and its coordinates represent the input datum of the operand COOR_SOURCE. With the same reasoning, if one wishes to add the taking into account of the reflected wave, one can clearly identify the first point of the free surface which generates the reflected wave, that is the point {\mathrm{x}}_{1} . This point is considered as the source point of the reflected wave and its coordinates represent the input datum of the operand COOR_REFLECHI. Notes concerning the use of the operands COOR_SOURCE and COOR_REFLECHI: - In the case of a 2D modelling (D_PLAN, for example) one works in the XY frame. In this case one will simply have to enter the X and Y coordinates of the source point of the incident wave (COOR_SOURCE) and, possibly, of the reflected wave (COOR_REFLECHI). The third coordinate, even if it is entered, will not be considered; - In the case of a vertical propagation, the phase shift of the wave is independent of the coordinates X and Y in 3D (X in 2D). Indeed, the wave front is perfectly horizontal and it is phase-shifted exclusively with respect to the vertical level (Z in 3D and Y in 2D). Consequently, one can enter any coordinate X and Y in 3D (X in 2D) for the source points of the incident wave and of the reflected wave. What matters is to enter correctly the coordinate Z in 3D (Y in 2D) in order to compute correctly the phase shift linked to the vertical propagation. ◆ TYPE_ONDE = ’P’/’S’/’SV’/’SH’ Type of the wave (compression or shear). | P | compression wave | | --- | --- | | \mathit{SV} | shear wave (only in 3D) | | \mathit{SH} | shear wave (only in 3D) | | S | shear wave (only in 2D) | The directions of the waves P , \mathit{SV} and \mathit{SH} are determined from the vector V supplied by DIRECTION. Namely: - P is collinear with V and normalised to 1, - \mathit{SH} is the intersection of the horizontal plane and of the plane normal to V , and normalised to 1, - \mathit{SV} is the vector product of \mathit{SH} and of P . There is a case of indeterminacy with this rule when the horizontal plane and the normal plane coincide. In this case, if V = :math: Z purely vertical, one imposes \mathit{SH} = Y , and \mathit{SV} = X . ◆ DIRECTION Direction of propagation of the wave. ◆ FONC_SIGNAL Derivative of the profile of the wave f(t) for t\in [0,+\infty [ . Warning: it is the function corresponding to the velocity v(t)=\dot{u}(t) that the user gives in FONC_SIGNAL. If the operand COOR_SOURCE is absent, one gives a nappe of time signals in velocity parametrised by values of propagation coordinates k.\mathrm{x} for the variable X . ◇ DEPL_IMPO Profile of the wave \mathit{fd}(t) for t\in [0,+\infty [ . Warning: it is the function corresponding to the integral of the velocity v(t)=\dot{u}(t) that the user mandatorily gives in DEPL_IMPO. This optional datum is activated only if one has stiffnesses added on the absorbing boundary, activated by the datum of a non-zero value of the operand LONG_CARA of the keyword ELAS of DEFI_MATERIAU. If the operand COOR_SOURCE is absent, one gives a nappe of time signals in displacement parametrised by values of propagation coordinates k.\mathrm{x} for the variable X . Note concerning the use of this load: It is strongly advised to orient, by means of the keywords ORIE_PEAU_2D or ORIE_PEAU_3D of MODI_MAILLAGE, the skin mesh cells assigned a modelling of absorbing boundary towards the outside of the domain that they bound. 9.5 Keyword ONDE_FLUI ONDE_FLUI = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ PRES = float, ) The factor keyword ONDE_FLUI makes it possible to apply a pressure amplitude of a sinusoidal incident wave arriving normally to a face on the modellings 3D_FLUIDE, 2D_FLUIDE and AXIS_FLUIDE. Topological assignment: ◇ GROUP_MA The wave is applied on these mesh cells. They are necessarily boundary mesh cells (segments in 2D and triangles/quadrangles in 3D). > ◆ PRES Amplitude of pressure of a sinusoidal incident wave arriving normally to the face. 9.6 Keyword FLUX_THM_REP FLUX_THM_REP = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FLUN = float, | FLUN_HYDR1 = float, | FLUN_HYDR2 = float, | FLUN_FRAC = fonction / formule / nappe, ) The factor keyword FLUX_THM_REP makes it possible to apply to a 2D or 3D continuum domain a heat flux and/or a fluid mass supply (hydraulic flux). The hydraulic fluxes (water and vapour) are defined by: \begin{array}{c}{\varphi}^{e}={\rho}_{e}\left(\nabla {P}_{e}-{\rho}_{e}g\right)\cdot n\\ {\varphi}^{v}={\rho}_{v}\left(\nabla {P}_{v}-{\rho}_{v}g\right)\cdot n\end{array} With the density of the water {\rho}_{e} , the density of the vapour {\rho}_{\nu} , the pressure of the water {P}_{e} (degree of freedom PRE1 ) and the pressure of the vapour {P}_{v} (degree of freedom PRE2 ). The heat flux is defined by: {\varphi}_{T}={\lambda}_{T}\frac{\partial T}{\partial n}+{h}_{m}^{e}{\varphi}^{e}+{h}_{m}^{v}{\varphi}^{v}+{h}_{m}^{a}{\varphi}^{a} With the mass enthalpies of the water {h}_{m}^{l} , of the vapour {h}_{m}^{v} , of the air {h}_{m}^{a} and the air flux {\varphi}^{a} . Topological assignment: ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, The loading is assigned on these mesh cells. They are necessarily boundary mesh cells (segments in 2D and triangles/quadrangles in 3D). This loading can be used only in (thermo)-hydraulics or in pure hydraulics (THM, THH, THHM, HM or HHM). ◆ | FLUN Value of the heat flux. ◆ | FLUN_HYDR1 Value of the hydraulic flux associated with the water constituent. ◆ | FLUN_HYDR2 Value of the hydraulic flux associated with the vapour constituent. ◆ | FLUN_FRAC Value of the hydraulic flux injected into a cohesive interface for the HM-XFEM models. This loading is imposed exclusively by means of a function of space on the main elements and not on the boundary elements. For more details concerning the use of this keyword, refer to the documents R7.02.18 and U2.05.02. 9.7 Keyword ECHANGE_THM ECHANGE_THM = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ COEF_11 = float, ◇ COEF_12 = float, ◇ COEF_21 = float, ◇ COEF_22 = float, ◆ PRE1_EXT = float, ◇ PRE2_EXT = float, ) The factor keyword ECHANGE_THM makes it possible, for an unsaturated modelling, to apply to a 2D or 3D continuum domain an exchange condition on the external hydraulic pressures. The hydraulic fluxes (water and air) which result from it are defined by: \begin{array}{c}\left({M}_{w}+{M}_{\text{vp}}\right).n=C11({p}_{1}-{p}_{{}_{1}}^{\text{ext}})-C12({p}_{2}-{p}_{{}_{2}}^{\text{ext}})\\ \left({M}_{\text{ad}}+{M}_{\text{as}}\right).n=C21({p}_{1}-{p}_{{}_{1}}^{\text{ext}})-C22({p}_{2}-{p}_{{}_{2}}^{\text{ext}})\end{array} With the capillary pressure {p}_{1} (degree of freedom PRE1 ) and the gas pressure {p}_{2} (degree of freedom PRE2 ). {M}_{w}+{M}_{\text{vp}} corresponds to the water flux (sum of the liquid-water flux {M}_{w} and of the vapour flux {M}_{\text{vp}} ) and {M}_{\text{ad}}+{M}_{\text{as}} corresponds to the air flux (sum of the dissolved-air flux {M}_{\mathit{ad}} and of the dry-air flux {M}_{\text{as}} ). Topological assignment: ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, The loading is assigned on these mesh cells. They are necessarily boundary mesh cells (segments in 2D and triangles/quadrangles in 3D). This loading can be used only for the unsaturated modellings of type THH2MS, THH2S, HH2MS or HH2S. > ◆ PRE1_EXT Value of the external capillary pressure. ◇ PRE2_EXT Value of the external gas pressure (0 by default). ◆ COEF_11 exchange coefficient C11 (cf. eq. ) linking the water flux to the capillary pressure. ◇ COEF_12 exchange coefficient C12 (cf. eq. ) linking the water flux to the gas pressure (0 by default). ◇ COEF_21 exchange coefficient C21 (cf. eq. ) linking the air flux to the capillary pressure (0 by default). ◇ COEF_22 exchange coefficient C22 (cf. eq. ) linking the air flux to the gas pressure (0 by default). 9.8 Keyword ECHANGE_THM_HR ECHANGE_THM_HR = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ HR_EXT = float, ◆ ALPHA = float, ◆ PVAP_SAT = float, ) The factor keyword ECHANGE_THM_HR makes it possible, for an unsaturated modelling, to apply to a 2D or 3D continuum domain a mixed exchange condition on the vapour density (proportional to the relative humidity). The water flux is then written: \left({M}_{w}+{M}_{\text{vp}}\right).n= \alpha.\left( \rho_{vp} -{\rho_{vp}}^{ext} \right) with \rho_{vp} the vapour density. Knowing that the relative humidity HR is a function of the density via the saturating vapour density \rho_{vp}^{sat} : \rho_{vp} = HR.\rho_{vp}^{sat} The flux is then expressed \left({M}_{w}+{M}_{\text{vp}}\right).n= \alpha.\rho_{vp}^{sat}\left( HR -{HR}^{ext} \right) One can express this equation as a function of the capillary pressure (Pc which is an unknown of the model) thanks to the Kelvin relation, that is: HR = exp\left[ \frac{Pc.M_{H2O}}{\rho_{l}.R.T}\right] with {M}_{H2O} the molar mass of water, R the perfect-gas constant and T the temperature. Ultimately the expression of the flux becomes: \left({M}_{w}+{M}_{\text{vp}}\right).n= \alpha.\rho_{vp}.\left( exp\left[ \frac{Pc.M_{H2O}}{\rho_{l}.R.T}\right] -{HR}^{ext} \right) Topological assignment: ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ HR_EXT External relative humidity. ◆ ALPHA Exchange coefficient > ◆ PVAP_SAT Saturating vapour pressure 9.9 Keyword FORCE_SOL FORCE_SOL = _F( ◆ / GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, / SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◆ | UNITE_RESU_MASS = unit, | UNITE_RESU_RIGI = unit, | UNITE_RESU_AMOR = unit, ◇ UNITE_RESU_FORC = unit, ◇ NB_PAS_TRONCATURE = int, ◇ TYPE = / "BINAIRE", / "ASCII" (par défaut), ) The factor keyword FORCE_SOL makes it possible to take into account the internal force of a soil domain by using the time evolutions of the contributions in stiffness, mass and damping of the soil impedance. The soil impedance extracted at the initial time instant makes it possible to build, by MACR_ELEM_DYNA, a macro-element representing the behaviour of the soil domain which one adds to the structural model. The dynamic interface of the macro-element is described either by a super-mesh-cell of the model containing both the structure and this macro-element, or by a node group if the physical interface coincides with the modal dynamic interface. One can also take into account, if it exists, the time evolution of the seismic forces, assigned to this same dynamic interface in the form of a logical unit. This type of load is taken into account in the command DYNA_NON_LINE. An example of use is supplied in the test case MISS03B V1.10.122. There can be only one occurrence of this keyword in AFFE_CHAR_MECA . Topological assignment: ◆ / GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, / SUPER_MAILLE = ma, These operands make it possible to describe the dynamic interface of the macro-element representing the behaviour of the soil domain which one adds to the structural model, either by a super-mesh-cell of the model containing both the structure and this macro-element by the keyword SUPER_MAILLE, or by a node group by the keyword GROUP_NO_INTERF if the physical interface coincides with the modal dynamic interface. ◆ | UNITE_RESU_MASS = unit, | UNITE_RESU_RIGI = unit, | UNITE_RESU_AMOR = unit, These operands make it possible to introduce the time evolutions of the contributions in stiffness, mass and damping of the soil impedance in the form of logical units. ◇ TYPE = / "BINAIRE", / "ASCII" (par défaut) This operand makes it possible to introduce the common writing format ('ASCII' or 'BINAIRE') of the time evolutions of the contributions in stiffness, mass and damping of the soil impedance supplied in the form of logical units by the preceding operands UNITE_RESU_ . The value of the operand must be consistent with the value entered in the operand TYPE_FICHIER_TEMPS during the computation of the option TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS' by CALC_MISS. ◇ UNITE_RESU_FORC This operand makes it possible to introduce, if it exists and in the form of a logical unit, the time evolution of the seismic forces, assigned to the dynamic interface of the macro-element representing the behaviour of the soil domain which one adds to the structural model. ◇ NB_PAS_TRONCATURE = int, This operand makes it possible to introduce (if it is present) a truncation of the computation of the contribution to the right-hand side of the soil force in DYNA_NON_LINE. This truncation operates on the summation from the displacement fields stored at the preceding time instants. Following tests, one realises that it is often sufficient to truncate the sum over the last 50 to 100 time steps instead of doing the complete sum over all the preceding stored time instants, which is the default option. It is therefore advised to use as a practical value the integer value of the maximum between 50 and one tenth of the total number of stored time steps.

u4.44.02 Operators AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F u4.44.02 Operators AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F 1 Purpose Assign thermal loadings and boundary conditions on a model. For the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER, the assigned values do not depend on any parameter and are defined by real values. For the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER_F, the values are functions of one or more parameters to be chosen from the set (INST, X, Y, Z). For the loadings used in non-linear thermal analysis, the functions depend solely on the temperature (TEMP) and must be tabulated. Moreover, for certain loadings (for example SOURCE), the values may depend on the command variables. These functions must previously be defined by calling one of the operators: - DEFI_CONSTANTE[U4.31.01]; - DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02; - DEFI_NAPPE[U4.31.03]; - FORMULE[U4.31.05]; - CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01. The concept produced is of type char_ther. Table of Contents 2 Syntax char_ther = AFFE_CHAR_THER( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ DOUBLE_LAGRANGE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", | EVOL_CHAR = evol_char, ◆ | TEMP_IMPO = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = grma, | GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ | TEMP = float, | TEMP_MIL = float, | TEMP_SUP = float, | TEMP_INF = float, ), | SOURCE = _F( ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ / SOUR_CALCULEE = cham_elem / cham_no, / SOUR = float, ), | FLUX_REP = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FLUN = float, | FLUN_INF = float, | FLUN_SUP = float, | CARA_TORSION = table, ), | ECHANGE = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | COEF_H = float, | COEF_H_INF = float, | COEF_H_SUP = float, ◇ & TEMP_EXT = float, ◇ & TEMP_EXT_INF = float, ◇ & TEMP_EXT_SUP = float, ), | ECHANGE_PAROI = _F( ◆ / GROUP_MA_1 = grma, / FISSURE = fiss_xfem, ◆ / GROUP_MA_2 = grma, # Si: not exists("FISSURE") ◆ COEF_H = float, ◇ TRAN = float, # Si: exists("FISSURE") ◆ / COEF_H = float, / TEMP_CONTINUE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ), | PRE_GRAD_TEMP = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ | FLUX_X = float, | FLUX_Y = float, | FLUX_Z = float, ), | LIAISON_DDL = _F( ◇ GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ DDL = / "TEMP", / "TEMP_MIL", / "TEMP_INF", / "TEMP_SUP", / "H1", ◆ COEF_MULT = float, ◆ COEF_IMPO = float, ), | LIAISON_GROUP = _F( ◆ / GROUP_MA_1 = grma, / GROUP_NO_1 = grno, ◆ / GROUP_NO_2 = grno, / GROUP_MA_2 = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ DDL_1 = / "TEMP" (par défaut), / "TEMP_MIL", / "TEMP_INF", / "TEMP_SUP", / "H1", ◆ COEF_MULT_1 = float, ◇ DDL_2 = / "TEMP" (par défaut), / "TEMP_MIL", / "TEMP_INF", / "TEMP_SUP", / "H1", ◆ COEF_MULT_2 = float, ◆ COEF_IMPO = float, ◇ TRAN = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ CENTRE = float, ), | LIAISON_UNIF = _F( ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ DDL = / "TEMP" (par défaut), / "TEMP_MIL", / "TEMP_INF", / "TEMP_SUP", / "H1", ), | LIAISON_CHAMNO = _F( ◆ CHAM_NO = cham_no, ◆ COEF_IMPO = float, ), | RAYONNEMENT = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ SIGMA = float, ◆ EPSILON = float, ◆ TEMP_EXT = float, ), | LIAISON_MAIL = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA_MAIT = grma, ◆ | GROUP_MA_ESCL = grma, | GROUP_NO_ESCL = grno, ◇ TRAN = float, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ CENTRE = float, ◇ ELIM_MULT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ DISTANCE_MAX = float, ◇ DISTANCE_ALARME = float, ), | CONVECTION = _F( ◆ VITESSE = cham_no, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General remarks Possible error messages related to the command AFFE_CHAR_THER It sometimes happens that a thermal analysis command (THER_LINEAIRE, THER_NON_LINE, ...) stops with a fatal error during the computation of the elementary right-hand sides due to the loadings defined in the commands AFFE_CHAR_THER_ . When the code stops during these elementary computations, an important piece of information in the error message is the name of the computation option requested by the code. The name of this option is in general unknown to the user, and it is therefore difficult for the user to understand the message. In the table below, the names of the computation options are given side by side with the name of the command and of the factor keyword which make it possible to activate this option. | Elementary computation option | Command | Factor keyword | | --- | --- | --- | | CHAR_THER_FLUNL | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | FLUX_NL | | CHAR_THER_FLUN_F | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | FLUX_REP | | CHAR_THER_FLUN_R | AFFE_CHAR_THER | FLUX_REP | | CHAR_THER_FLUTNL | AFFE_CHAR_THER | CONVECTION | | CHAR_THER_FLUTNL | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | CONVECTION | | CHAR_THER_FLUX_F | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | FLUX_REP | | CHAR_THER_FLUX_R | AFFE_CHAR_THER | FLUX_REP | | CHAR_THER_GRAI_F | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | PRE_GRAD_TEMP | | CHAR_THER_GRAI_R | AFFE_CHAR_THER | PRE_GRAD_TEMP | | CHAR_THER_PARO_F | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | ECHANGE_PAROI | | CHAR_THER_PARO_R | AFFE_CHAR_THER | ECHANGE_PAROI | | CHAR_THER_SOUR_F | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | SOURCE | | CHAR_THER_SOUR_R | AFFE_CHAR_THER | SOURCE | | CHAR_THER_TEXT_F | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | ECHANGE | | CHAR_THER_TEXT_R | AFFE_CHAR_THER | ECHANGE | | CHAR_THER_SOURNL | AFFE_CHAR_THER_F | SOUR_NL | 4 Operands 4.1 General remarks on the operands 4.1.1 The two forms of operands under a factor keyword The operands under a factor keyword are of two forms: - the operands specifying the topological entities on which the loadings are assigned (keywords GROUP_NO and GROUP_MA, etc.). The arguments of these operands are identical for the two operators. - the operand or operands specifying the assigned values ( TEMP , COEF_H , etc.). The meaning of these operands is the same for the two operators, but the arguments of these operands are all of type real for the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER and of type fonction (created by one of the operators DEFI_FONCTION, DEFI_NAPPE, DEFI_CONSTANTE, FORMULE or CALC_FONC_INTERP) for the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER_F. We shall therefore not distinguish, in this document, except where expressly stated otherwise, between the two operators AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F. 4.1.2 Topological entities for the assignment of the loadings In general, the topological entities on which values are to be assigned are defined: - by nodes, using the operand GROUP_NO, which makes it possible to introduce a list of node groups, - by mesh cell, using the operand GROUP_MA, which makes it possible to introduce a list of mesh-cell groups, Rule: In order to define the assignment domain as simply as possible, the overloading rule is used: it is the last assignment which takes precedence. 4.2 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo, Concept produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01, in which the types of finite elements assigned on the mesh are defined. 4.3 Operand DOUBLE_LAGRANGE ◊ DOUBLE_LAGRANGE = ’OUI’/’NON’ This keyword makes it possible to state whether or not the user wishes to duplicate the Lagrange multipliers used to define and dualise the boundary conditions in the assembled matrix. Concretely, duplicating the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to use linear solvers which do not allow pivoting. Not duplicating the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the problem (and therefore the size of the problem to be solved), but its use is limited to the solvers MUMPS and Petsc. Note that the two Lagrange multipliers associated with the relation will be such that the first will be located before all the terms involved in the relation and the second after them, in the assembled matrix. This choice has the advantage of producing an assembled matrix whose storage requirement is smaller, but has the disadvantage of being able to give rise to a singularity in the matrix. Since the numbering is in any case liable to be modified by the renumberer of the chosen external solver, this detail therefore remains purely technical. 4.4 Keyword TEMP_IMPO 4.4.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to impose, on nodes or node groups, a temperature. Depending on the name of the operator called, the values are supplied directly (AFFE_CHAR_THER) or by means of a concept of type fonction (AFFE_CHAR_THER_F). 4.4.2 Syntax - for AFFE_CHAR_THER TEMP_IMPO = _F( ♦ | TOUT = 'OUI', | GROUP_NO = lgno, [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA= lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ / TEMP = t, [R] / | TEMP_MIL = tinf, [R] | TEMP_INF = tinf, [R] | TEMP_SUP = tsup, [R] ) - for AFFE_CHAR_THER_F TEMP_IMPO = _F( ♦ | TOUT = 'OUI', | GROUP_NO = lgno, [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA= lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ / TEMP = tf, [fonction] / | TEMP_MIL = tf, [fonction] | TEMP_INF = tinf, [fonction] | TEMP_SUP = tsupf, [fonction] ) 4.4.3 Operands / TEMP = Value of the temperature imposed on the specified node(s). / Pour les éléments de coque thermique uniquement (Modélisation : 'COQUE'): | TEMP_MIL Temperature on the middle surface imposed on the specified node(s). | TEMP_INF Temperature imposed on the lower wall of the shell. | TEMP_SUP Temperature imposed on the upper wall of the shell. This “initial” temperature gradient can be used, for example, to solve the elementary problems determining the correctors of stationary linear thermal analysis in the basic cell (2D, 3D), in periodic homogenisation. The homogenised conductivity coefficients are obtained by computing, with the operator POST_ELEM U4.81.22, keyword ENER_POT, the thermally dissipated energy at equilibrium in linear thermal analysis from the correctors. Because of the thermal analogy, this approach can be used to obtain the correctors in anti-plane elasticity in the 2D basic cell, as well as in electrical conduction. The analysis uses the conductivity of the material. The latter is assumed to be isotropic and independent of the temperature. The assignment can be made on one or more mesh cells or on all the elements of the model. 4.10.2 Syntax - for AFFE_CHAR_THER PRE_GRAD_TEMP = _F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ | FLUX_X = flx, [R] | FLUX_Y = fly, [R] | FLUX_Z = flz, [R] ) 4.10.3 Operands This loading applies to the following mesh-cell types and modellings: | Mesh cell | Modelling | | --- | --- | | TRIA3, TRIA6, QUAD4, QUAD8, QUAD9 | PLAN, AXIS, PLAN_DIAG, AXIS_DIAG | | HEXA8, HEXA20, HEXA27 PENTA6, PENTA15, TETRA4, TETRA10 PYRA5, PYRA13 | 3D, 3D_DIAG | ♦ | FLUX_X = flx (flxf) | FLUX_Y = fly (flyf) | FLUX_Z = flz (flzf) (en 3D seulement) Components of the temperature gradient \mathrm{grad}{T}_{\mathrm{ini}} in the global frame. The elementary right-hand side computed is: {\int}_{{V}_{e}}\mathrm{grad}{T}_{\mathrm{ini}}K\mathrm{grad}{T}^{\text{ }}{\mathrm{dV}}_{e} where K is the tensor of the thermal conductivities. The gradients may be functions of the geometry and/or of time. - for AFFE_CHAR_THER_F PRE_GRAD_TEMP = _F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ | FLUX_X = flxf, [fonction] | FLUX_Y = flyf, [fonction] | FLUX_Z = flzf, [fonction] ) 4.11 Keyword LIAISON_DDL 4.11.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to define a linear relation between degrees of freedom of two or more nodes. Depending on the name of the operator called, the values are supplied directly (AFFE_CHAR_THER) or by means of a fonction concept (AFFE_CHAR_THER_F). 4.11.2 Syntax - for AFFE_CHAR_THER LIAISON_DDL = _F ( ♦ GROUP_NO = lgno, [l_gr_noeud] ◊ DDL = | 'TEMP', [DEFAUT] | 'TEMP_MIL', | 'TEMP_INF', | 'TEMP_SUP', | 'H1', ♦ COEF_MULT = ai , [l_R] ♦ COEF_IMPO = b , [R] ) - for AFFE_CHAR_THER_F LIAISON_DDL = _F ( ♦ GROUP_NO = lgno, [l_gr_noeud] ◊ DDL = | 'TEMP', [DEFAUT] | 'TEMP_MIL', | 'TEMP_INF', | 'TEMP_SUP', | 'H1', ♦ COEF_MULT = ai , [l_R] ♦ COEF_IMPO = bf , [fonction] ) 4.11.3 Operands The list of nodes {N}_{i} ( i=1,r ) defined by GROUP_NO is ordered in the natural way, that is, in the order of the list of node groups, and, for each node group, in the order of definition of the group by GROUP_NO. The argument of DDL must be a list of degrees of freedom {T}_{i} ( i=1,r ) of r texts taken from among: TEMP , TEMP_MIL , TEMP_SUP , TEMP_INF , H1 If the keyword DDL is omitted, by default the linear relation will bear on the degrees of freedom 'TEMP'. The argument of COEF_MULT must be a list {a}_{i} ( i=1,r ) of coefficients (of type real for AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F). The argument of COEF_IMPO is a coefficient \beta for AFFE_CHAR_THER, a function of space for AFFE_CHAR_THER_F. The following kinematic condition is applied: \sum_{i=1}^{r}{\alpha}_{i}{T}_{i}=\beta Notes: The components 'TEMP_MIL', 'TEMP_SUP' and 'TEMP_INF' can appear only in combinations assigned solely to nodes which belong to shell elements (modelling 'COQUE'). The component 'H1' can appear only in combinations assigned solely to nodes which belong to X-FEM elements. In this case, only the degrees of freedom 'TEMP' and 'H1' may appear in the linear relation. In the case of a linear relation between the degrees of freedom of one and the same node, one will repeat, after the keyword GROUPE_NO , the name of the group defining the node as many times as there are degrees of freedom in the relation. Example: to impose {T}_{\sup}={T}_{\inf} on the node of group \mathit{GN}1 , one will write: LIAISON_DDL = _F ( GROUP_NO = (GN1,GN1), DDL = ('TEMP_SUP', 'TEMP_INF'), COEF_MULT = (1.,-1.), COEF_IMPO = 0., ) It is important to note that to one occurrence of the factor keyword LIAISON_DDL there corresponds one and only one linear relation. If one wishes to impose the same relation between 2 node groups GRN01 and GRN02 (the same temperature, node to node, for example), one cannot write: LIAISON_DDL = _F ( GROUP_NO = (GRN01, GRN02), DDL = ('TEMP', 'TEMP'), COEF_MULT = (1.,-1.), COEF_IMPO = 0., ) This form of writing makes sense only if GRN01 and GRN02 each contain only one node. In the case above, each linear relation will have to be written out explicitly, node by node. The keyword LIAISON_GROUP, on the other hand, makes it possible to condense the writing of the linear relations between 2 node groups facing each other. 4.12 Keyword LIAISON_GROUP 4.12.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to define linear relations between pairs of nodes, these pairs of nodes being obtained by placing two lists of mesh cells or of nodes face to face. DDL_2) : List of texts taken from among: 'TEMP', 'TEMP_MIL', 'TEMP_INF', 'TEMP_SUP', 'H1' 'TEMP_MIL', 'TEMP_INF' and 'TEMP_SUP' can be used only for thermal shell elements (modelling: 'COQUE'). 'H1' can be used only for X-FEM elements. In this case, only the degrees of freedom 'TEMP' and 'H1' may appear in the linear relations. By default, the degree of freedom considered for all the nodes of the linear relations is 'TEMP'. 4.12.4 Use of LIAISON_GROUP - LIAISON_GROUP generates linear relations only between 2 nodes (one on {\Gamma}_{1} , one on {\Gamma}_{2} ) To generate linear relations on more than 2 nodes, use the keyword LIAISON_DDL. - determination of the pairs of nodes facing each other: first, the two lists of nodes to be placed face to face (i.e. to be paired) are established, for each occurrence of the factor keyword LIAISON_GROUP: - for the keywords GROUP_NO_1 and GROUP_NO_2, these are the nodes constituting the node groups, - for the keywords GROUP_MA_1 and GROUP_MA_2, these are the nodes of the mesh cells constituting the mesh-cell groups. Redundancies having been eliminated, the two lists of nodes obtained must have the same length. The determination of the pairs of nodes facing each other is carried out in several stages: - for each node \mathit{N1} of the first list, one looks for the image node \mathit{N2}=f(\mathit{N1}) of the second list. If f is not injective (a node \mathit{N2} is the image of two distinct nodes \mathit{N1} and \mathit{N1}' ), the following error message is issued: CONFLIT DANS LES VIS-A-VIS DES NOEUDS LE NOEUD N2 EST LE VIS-A-VIS DES NOEUDS N1 ET N1' - for each node \mathit{N2} of the second list, one looks for the image node \mathit{N1}=g(\mathit{N2}) of the first list. If g is not injective (a node \mathit{N1} is the image of two distinct nodes \mathit{N2} and \mathit{N2}' ), the following error message is issued: CONFLIT DANS LES VIS-A-VIS DES NOEUDS LE NOEUD N1 EST LE VIS-A-VIS DES NOEUDS N2 ET N2' - one checks that g={f}^{-1} , that is, that the pairs obtained by stages a) and b) are the same (one wishes to have a bijection f between the two lists of nodes). If f is not surjective, the following error message is issued: CONFLIT DANS LES VIS-A-VIS GENERES SUCCESSIVEMENT A PARTIR DES LISTES LIST1 ET LIST2 LE NOEUD DE LA PREMIERE LISTE N1 N'EST L'IMAGE D'AUCUN NOEUD PAR LA CORRESPONDANCE INVERSE For a given node N , one calls image node f(N) the node of the other list of nodes which achieves the minimum of the distance to N . To facilitate the pairing, in particular in the case of particular geometries (where the boundaries {\Gamma}_{1} and {\Gamma}_{2} could “almost” be deduced from one another by the composition of a translation and a rotation), the possibility is offered of performing a virtual geometric transformation of the first group of nodes (translation and rotation (cf. [Figure 4.11.3-a]) before computing the distances (keywords TRAN, CENTRE and ANGL_NAUT). For each occurrence of the factor keyword LIAISON_GROUP, the list of the new pairs facing each other is thus constructed. When all the occurrences have been scanned, the duplicate pairs are removed from the list. Note: In the pairs of nodes facing each other, the order of the nodes is important. If, for the first occurrence of LIAISON_GROUP, a node N belonged to the first group of nodes and a node M to the second group of nodes, and if, for the second occurrence of LIAISON_GROUP, it is the reverse, one will obtain at the end of the pairing the pairs (N,M) and (M,N) . They will not be eliminated during the detection of redundancies; on the other hand, the matrix obtained will be singular. Thus, one is advised to keep the same logic when describing the edges facing each other. 4.13 Keyword LIAISON_MAIL 4.13.1 Purpose Factor keyword making it possible to “tie thermally” two edges of a structure. These edges may be meshed differently (incompatible meshes) but must be deducible from one another by rotation and/or translation. 4.13.2 Syntax - in AFFE_CHAR_THER only LIAISON_MAIL = _F ( ♦ GROUP_MA_MAIT = lgma_mait, ♦ | GROUP_MA_ESCL = lgma_escl, | GROUP_NO_ESCL = lgno_escl, ◊ DISTANCE_MAX = d_max, [R] ◊ | ♦ TRAN = (tx, ty, [tz]), [l_R] | ♦ CENTRE = (xc, yc, [zc]), [l_R] ♦ ANGL_NAUT = (alpha, [beta, gamma]), [l_R] ) Face 1 is called the “master” face; face 2 is called the “slave” face. 4.13.3 Operands 4.13.3.1 GROUP_MA_ESCL / GROUP_NO_ESCL These keywords make it possible to define the set of nodes of the slave face. One takes all the nodes specified by the keyword GROUP_NO_ESCL plus, possibly, the nodes carried by the mesh cells specified by the keyword GROUP_MA_ESCL. 4.13.3.2 GROUP_MA_MAIT This keyword makes it possible to define the set of mesh cells in which one will look for the counterparts of the nodes of the slave face. One must not give the surface mesh cells (in 3D) making up the master face, but the volume mesh cells adjacent to the master face. The mesh cells specified are candidates for the search for counterparts. One may give too many of them. 4.13.3.3 DISTANCE_MAX To project the mesh \mathit{MA1} onto the mesh \mathit{MA2} , the method looks for the element of the mesh \mathit{MA1} in which each node of \mathit{MA2} lies, then interpolates the value by means of the shape functions of the element. When a node of \mathit{MA2} lies in no element of the mesh \mathit{MA1} , the method relates the node to the (boundary) point of the nearest element. It interpolates the value by means of the shape functions of the element, even if the node is “far” from this element. If one wishes a node which lies in none of the elements of the mesh \mathit{MA1} not to be concerned by the projection, one uses the operand DISTANCE_MAX. This operand makes it possible to give the maximum distance that one authorises between the node and the nearest element. If the node does not satisfy the proximity criterion, the field will not be projected onto this node (i.e. the node will carry no component). There is no default value for DISTANCE_MAX. This means that, by default, the field will be extended outside the material as far as necessary. 4.13.3.4 DISTANCE_ALARME = d_ala The code issues an alarm when a node of \mathit{MA2} is judged “distant” from the mesh cells of \mathit{MA1} . Let d be the distance separating a node of \mathit{MA2} from the nearest mesh cell of \mathit{MA1} . By default, the criterion for judging whether a node is distant is relative: d > 1/10th of the size of the nearest mesh cell. But if the user uses DISTANCE_ALARME = d_ala, the alarm message is issued if d > d_ala (absolute criterion). 4.13.3.5 CENTRE / ANGL_NAUT / TRAN These operands make it possible to define the geometric transformation (rotation and/or translation) making it possible to pass from the slave face to the master face. The command first performs the rotation, then the translation. Caution: the transformation is in the slave-to-master direction. This boundary condition applies to plane modellings ('PLAN' or 'AXIS') or volume modellings ('3D'). 4.14 Keyword ECHANGE_PAROI 4.14.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to apply thermal exchange conditions between 2 walls. These walls may be defined in two ways: - each separately, by one or more mesh cells (case of meshed walls); - from a list of X-FEM cracks, the two walls then corresponding to the two lips of each crack. In this case it is also possible to impose the continuity of the temperature field across the lips of each crack. 4.14.2 Syntax - for AFFE_CHAR_THER ECHANGE_PAROI = _F ( # si la paroi est maillée ♦ GROUP_MA_1 = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ GROUP_MA_2 = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ COEF_H = h, [R] ◊ TRAN = lr, [l_R] # si la paroi est définie avec des fissures X-FEM ♦ FISSURE = lfiss, [l_fiss_xfem] ♦ / COEF_H = h, [R] / TEMP_CONTINUE = 'OUI' ) - for AFFE_CHAR_THER_F ECHANGE_PAROI = _F ( # si la paroi est maillée ♦ GROUP_MA_1 = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ GROUP_MA_2 = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ COEF_H = h, [fonction] ◊ TRAN = lr, [l_R] # si la paroi est définie avec des fissures X-FEM ♦ FISSURE = lfiss, [l_fiss_xfem] ♦ / COEF_H = h, [fonction] / TEMP_CONTINUE = 'OUI' ) 4.14.3 Operands 4.14.3.1 Case of meshed walls ♦ COEF_H Exchange coefficient between the 2 walls. Real for the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER, function for the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER_F. ♦ GROUP_MA_1 ♦ GROUP_MA_2 Figure 4.13.3-a These operands make it possible to define the 2 lists of mesh cells representing, for the list indexed “_1”, the wall {\Gamma}_{1} and, for the list indexed “_2”, the wall {\Gamma}_{2} . For each crack given in this list, the two walls facing each other are defined as the upper lip and the lower lip of the crack. There are therefore as many pairs of walls facing each other as there are cracks present in this list. ♦ / COEF_H Exchange coefficient between the lips of the crack. If this keyword is present, the exchange condition imposed between the lips of each crack given under the keyword FISSURE is the same as in the case of a meshed wall (see the previous section), taking the identity for the bijection f since the upper and lower lips of each crack are geometrically coincident. / TEMP_CONTINUE This keyword can be supplied only with the value 'OUI'. If this keyword is present, one imposes the continuity of the temperature field across the lips of each crack given under the keyword FISSURE, by cancelling the enrichment degrees of freedom (“Heaviside” and “crack-tip”). 4.14.4 Use of ECHANGE_PAROI > In the case of a meshed wall: The user gives two lists of mesh cells from which the pairs of paired nodes will be taken. These lists are first sorted by mesh-cell type: the paired nodes will come from mesh cells of identical type. For each mesh cell of the first list, one determines the nearest mesh cell in the second list by computing all the distances of the nodes taken two by two (one runs through all the possible permutations). The minimum distance obtained defines both the mesh cell facing it and the pairs of paired nodes for the two mesh cells concerned. As in LIAISON_GROUP [§4.11], it is possible to perform a virtual geometric transformation (rotation and/or translation) before computing the distances. > In the case of one or more X-FEM cracks: One defines as many pairs of walls facing each other as there are cracks in the list supplied for the keyword FISSURE. - If the keyword COEF_H is present, all the cracks contained in this list will be assigned the same exchange coefficient (real or function). To assign a value of the exchange coefficient specific to each crack, one must use the repeatable character of the factor keyword ECHANGE_PAROI. - If the keyword TEMP_CONTINUE is present, one imposes the continuity of the temperature field across all the cracks contained in this list. 4.14.5 Mesh cells and modellings supporting this loading: > In the case of meshed walls: The lists of mesh cells given by the user must be made up of boundary mesh cells; coupling mesh cells are then generated automatically.
