These nodes are defined by the mesh-cell groups or the node groups to which they belong. 4.15.2 Syntax - for AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F LIAISON_UNIF = _F ( ♦ / GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] / GROUP_NO = lgno, [l_gr_noeud] ♦ DDL = | 'TEMP' , [DEFAUT] | 'TEMP_MIL', | 'TEMP_INF', | 'TEMP_SUP', ) 4.15.3 Operands ♦ / GROUP_MA / GROUP_NO These operands make it possible to define a list of n nodes {N}_{i} from which redundancies have been eliminated (for GROUP_MA, these are the connectivities of the mesh cells). ♦ DDL This operand makes it possible to define a list of degrees of freedom {T}_{i}(i=1,r) of r texts taken from among: 'TEMP', 'TEMP_MIL', 'TEMP_INF', 'TEMP_SUP'. The r\times (n-1) resulting ‘kinematic’ conditions are: {T}_{i}({N}_{1})={T}_{i}({N}_{k}) for k\in (2,\mathrm{...},n) , i\in (1,\mathrm{...},r) Note: The components 'TEMP_MIL', 'TEMP_SUP', 'TEMP_INF' can appear only for nodes of shell elements. 4.16 Keyword LIAISON_CHAMNO 4.16.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to define a linear relation between all the temperatures present in a CHAM_NO concept. 4.16.2 Syntax LIAISON_CHAMNO = _F ( ♦ CHAM_NO = chamno, [cham_no] ♦ COEF_IMPO= b, [R] ) 4.16.3 Operands CHAM_NO= Name of the chamno which is used to define the linear relation. The temperatures that are related are all those present in the chamno. The coefficients to be applied to the temperatures are the values of these temperatures in the chamno. Example: Suppose that one has a chamno bearing on 3 nodes of names \mathit{N01} , \mathit{N02} and \mathit{N03} . Suppose that the values of the temperatures at these 3 nodes in the chamno are respectively 2., 5.4 and 9.1. The linear relation that one will impose is: 2.T(\mathit{NO1})+5.4T(\mathit{NO2})+9.1T(\mathit{NO3})=\beta COEF_IMPO= This is the value of the real coefficient \beta on the right-hand side of the linear relation. 4.17 Keyword CONVECTION 4.17.1 Purpose Keyword usable to take into account the term of heat transport by convection, whose expression is \rho {C}_{p}.V\mathit{grad}T , appearing in the expression of the material derivative \rho {C}_{p}\frac{\mathit{dT}}{\mathit{dt}}:\rho {C}_{p}\frac{\mathit{dT}}{\mathit{dt}}=\rho {C}_{p}\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}+\rho {C}_{p}V\mathit{grad}T . In the case of a liquid medium, V denotes the imposed velocity of the fluid particle at the current point. In the case of a moving solid medium, V denotes the velocity of the solid. In all cases, one assumes that the velocity field is known a priori. The case of a moving solid is fairly frequent in practice. It concerns in particular welding or surface-treatment applications, which involve a heat source moving in a given direction and at a given velocity. The thermal problem is then studied in a reference frame attached to the source (cf. THER_NON_LINE_MO U4.54.03). 4.17.2 Syntax CONVECTION = _F ( ♦ VITESSE = v [cham_no_sdaster]) 4.17.3 Operand For AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F, VITESSE = Name of the velocity field at the time instant at which one performs the analysis. This field is a cham_no concept of type cham_no_depl_r. It must have been defined on the whole model for which one performs the analysis. 4.18 Keyword SOUR_NL 4.18.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to apply volumetric sources depending on the temperature (2D or 3D) to a domain defined by one or more mesh cells of volume type. This type of flux is available only in the command AFFE_CHAR_THER_F and is used only by the commands THER_NON_LINE U4.54.02 and THER_NON_LINE_MO U4.54.03. The values are supplied by a concept of type fonction. The function depends on the temperature, to the exclusion of any other parameter. Moreover, it must necessarily be a tabulated function and not a formula. 4.18.2 Syntax SOUR_NL = _F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgma, [l_gr_maille] ♦ SOUR = sf, [fonction] ) 4.18.3 Operands This loading applies to the following mesh-cell types and modellings: | Mesh cell | Modelling | | --- | --- | | HEXA8, HEXA20, HEXA27 PYRA5, PYRA13, PENTA6, PENTA15 TETRA4, TETRA10 | 3D | | TRIA3, TRIA6, QUAD4, QUAD8, QUAD9 | PLAN, AXIS | | HEXA8, PYRA5, PENTA6, TETRA4 | 3D_DIAG | | TRIA3, QUAD4 | PLAN_DIAG, AXIS_DIAG | / ♦ SOUR = s, Value of the source depending on the temperature and assumed constant on the element. 4.19 Keyword EVOL_CHAR EVOL_CHAR = evch The factor keyword EVOL_CHAR is usable to apply loadings that evolve in time, of type evol_char, produced by LIRE_RESU U7.02.01 or CREA_RESU U4.44.12 and containing fields of coefficients corresponding either: - to a loading of type ECHANGE (see § 4.8): the field T_EXT corresponds to the parameter TEMP_EXT and the field COEF_H corresponds to the parameter COEF_H. - to a loading of type FLUX_REP (see § 4.5): the field FLUN corresponds to the parameter of the same name.

u4.44.03 Operators AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F u4.44.03 Operators AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F 1 Purpose Define a loading of type “imposed degrees of freedom”. This command can be used with a mechanical, thermal or acoustic model. The treatment of these “kinematic” conditions will be carried out without dualisation and therefore without the addition of Lagrange degrees of freedom. 1. For AFFE_CHAR_CINE (except for the case EVOL_IMPO), the assigned values do not depend on any parameter and are defined by real values (mechanical or thermal) or by complex values (acoustic). These values may be zero (restraint). 2. For AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F, the assigned values are functions of one (or several) parameters to be chosen from the set (\mathrm{INST},X,Y,Z) . Produces a data structure of type char_cine_ . 2 Syntax / char_cine_acou / char_cine_meca / char_cine_ther = AFFE_CHAR_CINE( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ / MECA_IMPO = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◆ | DX = float, | DY = float, | DZ = float, | DRX = float, | DRY = float, | DRZ = float, | GRX = float, | PRES = float, | PHI = float, | TEMP = float, | PRE1 = float, | PRE2 = float, | UI2 = float, | UI3 = float, | VI2 = float, | VI3 = float, | WI2 = float, | WI3 = float, | UO2 = float, | UO3 = float, | VO2 = float, | VO3 = float, | WO2 = float, | WO3 = float, | UI4 = float, | UI5 = float, | VI4 = float, | VI5 = float, | WI4 = float, | WI5 = float, | UO4 = float, | UO5 = float, | VO4 = float, | VO5 = float, | WO4 = float, | WO5 = float, | UI6 = float, | UO6 = float, | VI6 = float, | VO6 = float, | WI6 = float, | WO6 = float, | WO = float, | WI1 = float, | WO1 = float, | GONF = float, | H1X = float, | H1Y = float, | H1Z = float, | H1PRE1 = float, | K1 = float, | K2 = float, | K3 = float, | V11 = float, | V12 = float, | V13 = float, | V21 = float, | V22 = float, | V23 = float, | V31 = float, | V32 = float, | V33 = float, | PRES11 = float, | PRES12 = float, | PRES13 = float, | PRES21 = float, | PRES22 = float, | PRES23 = float, | PRES31 = float, | PRES32 = float, | PRES33 = float, | LH1 = float, | GLIS = float, | PSI = float, | LAG_GV = float, | EPXX = float, | EPYY = float, | EPZZ = float, | EPXY = float, | EPXZ = float, | EPYZ = float, ), / THER_IMPO = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◆ | TEMP = float, | TEMP_MIL = float, | TEMP_INF = float, | TEMP_SUP = float, ), / ACOU_IMPO = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◆ PRES = complex, ), / EVOL_IMPO = evol_elas / evol_noli / evol_ther, # Si: exists("EVOL_IMPO") ◇ NOM_CMP = list[text], ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General remarks These two commands create concepts of type char_cine_ (_meca/_ther). The command AFFE_CHAR_CINE can also create concepts of type char_cine_acou. These types are different from the type charge created by the commands AFFE_CHAR_MECA[U4.44.01], AFFE_CHAR_THER[U4.44.02] or AFFE_CHAR_ACOU[U4.44.04]). The objects created are therefore not interchangeable. The advantage of “kinematic” loads is that they do not increase the number of unknowns of the systems to be solved, unlike the method of dualisation by LAGRANGE multipliers, used in the commands producing a concept of type charge. On the other hand, the use of these loads has the following limitations: - they can be used only in the case of a relation of type “imposed degree of freedom” (and not for linear relations), - these loads are not yet accepted in all the global commands. Today the possible commands are: - MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, DYNA_NON_LINE - THER_LINEAIRE - for an analysis that does not use the global commands: assembly of a matrix, then solution, the sequence of commands to be used is more complicated than with “ordinary” loads, as can be seen in example 2 [§ 5.2]. 4 Operands 4.1 General remarks on the operands The operands under the factor keywords MECA_IMPO, THER_IMPO and ACOU_IMPO are of two forms: - the operands specifying the geometric entities on which the loadings are assigned (keywords GROUP_MA, GROUP_NO…). The arguments of these operands are identical for the two operators. - the operands specifying the assigned values (DX, DY, DZ, etc.). The meaning of these operands is the same for the two operators. The arguments of these operands are all of type real for the operator AFFE_CHAR_CINE and of type fonction (or formula) for the operator AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F. This is true with one exception: the factor keyword ACOU_IMPO (which does not exist in the command AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F) is always of type complex. We shall therefore not distinguish, in this document, except where expressly stated otherwise, between the two operators AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F. In general, the entities on which values are to be assigned are defined by nodes: 1. either by the operand TOUT = 'OUI', which makes it possible to designate all the nodes of the mesh, 2. or by the operand GROUP_NO, which makes it possible to designate a list of node groups, 3. or by the operand GROUP_MA, which makes it possible to designate all the nodes carried by the mesh cells designated by the lists of GROUP_MA. 4.2 Behaviour in the case of overloading: 4.2.1 Overloading within a single command AFFE_CHAR_CINE When, within one and the same command, one uses several occurrences of MECA_IMPO (or THER_IMPO, ...) and certain nodes are assigned several times, it is the last occurrence which takes precedence. For example: chcine= AFFE_CHAR_CINE( MECA_IMPO=( _F( TOUT='OUI', DX= 1., ...) _F( GROUP_NO='GN3', DX= 3., ...) In this case, the imposed displacement DX for the node GN3 is: 3. 4.2.2 Overloading between several commands AFFE_CHAR_CINE If one uses several different commands, the behaviour is different. For example: chcin1= AFFE_CHAR_CINE( MECA_IMPO= _F( TOUT='OUI', DX= 1., ...) chcin2= AFFE_CHAR_CINE( MECA_IMPO= _F( GROUP_NO='GN3', DX= 3., ...) In this case, the imposed displacement DX for the node GN3 is: 4 (because 1+3) 4.2.3 Overloading between AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_MECA If one “mixes” the commands AFFE_CHAR_MECA and AFFE_CHAR_CINE, the code will stop with a fatal error (FACTOR_41), explaining that there is an over-abundant restraint relation (NOEUDN3 / DX). 4.3 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo Concept produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE[U4.41.01], in which the types of finite elements assigned on the mesh are defined. 4.4 Keyword MECA_IMPO 4.4.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to impose, at nodes, a displacement value, defined component by component in the global frame. (voir la liste complète ci-dessous) ),), AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F / MECA_IMPO = (_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' , | GROUP_NO = lgno , [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA = lgma , [l_gr_maille] ♦ | DX = uxf , [fonction( )] | DY = uyf , [fonction( )] | ... (voir la liste complète ci-dessous) ),), fonction( ) : fonction ou formule List of the keywords available under MECA_IMPO in AFFE_CHAR_CINE: List of the keywords available under MECA_IMPO in AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F: These are the names of the degrees of freedom carried by the finite elements of the model. The meaning of these names is to be found in the documentation of AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01. 4.4.3 Operands / MECA_IMPO | DX = ux or uxf DY = uy or uyf DZ = uz or uzf | Value of the translational displacement component imposed on the specified nodes | | --- | --- | Only for the nodes of a 3D model comprising beam, plate, shell or discrete elements: | DRX = drx or drxf DRY = dry or dryf DRZ = drz or drzf | Value of the rotational displacement component imposed on the specified nodes | | --- | --- | For the more “exotic” degrees of freedom: GRX, TEMP, PRES and PHI, one should refer to the documentation of the command AFFE_CHAR_MECA[U4.44.01 §3.9]. Caution: One checks that the specified degree of freedom exists at this node for at least one of the elements of the model (keyword MODELE) which are supported on this node. Moreover, the overloading rule is applied when the same degree of freedom of the same node is imposed several times: only the last value is retained. 4.5 Keyword THER_IMPO 4.5.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to impose, at nodes, a nodal temperature value. These boundary conditions will subsequently be treated by the method known as elimination of the imposed degrees of freedom (that is: without dualisation, unlike the treatment of the same type of boundary condition by the use of the operators AFFE_CHAR_THER or AFFE_CHAR_THER_F[U4.44.02]) 4.5.2 Syntax for AFFE_CHAR_CINE / THER_IMPO = (_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' , | GROUP_NO = lgno , [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA = lgma , [l_gr_maille] ♦ | TEMP = t , [R] | TEMP_SUP = tsup , [R] | TEMP_INF = tinf , [R] ), ), for AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F / THER_IMPO = (_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' , | GROUP_NO = lgno , [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA = lgma , [l_gr_maille] ♦ | TEMP = ft , [fonction( )] | TEMP_SUP = ftsup , [fonction( )] | TEMP_INF = ftinf , [fonction( )] ), ), fonction( ) : fonction ou formule 4.5.3 Operands | TEMP Temperature imposed on the nodes (or on the middle surface for thermal shells) | TEMP_INF Temperature imposed on the lower face for thermal shell elements. | TEMP_SUP Temperature imposed on the upper face for thermal shell elements. For shells, the lower and upper faces are defined, mesh cell by mesh cell, by the direction of the outward normal deduced from the numbering of the nodes: see FACE_IMPO of AFFE_CHAR_MECA[U4.44.01]. 4.6 Keyword ACOU_IMPO 4.6.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to impose, at nodes, an acoustic pressure value. These boundary conditions will subsequently be treated by the method known as elimination of the imposed degrees of freedom (that is: without dualisation, unlike the treatment of the same type of boundary condition by the use of the operator AFFE_CHAR_ACOU[U4.44.04]). 4.6.2 Syntax For AFFE_CHAR_CINE / ACOU_IMPO = (_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' , | GROUP_NO = lgno , [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA = lgma , [l_gr_maille] ♦ PRES = p , [C] ), ), For AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F: No keyword ACOU_IMPO, because there is not yet a complex function. 4.6.3 Operands PRES Value of the complex acoustic pressure imposed on the specified node(s). 4.7 Keyword EVOL_IMPO / EVOL_IMPO = evoimp / [evol_ther] / [evol_elas] / [evol_noli] ◊ NOM_CMP = lcmp [l_TXM] This keyword makes possible the “structural zoom” (see for example the test zzzz230a). The effect of this keyword is to impose all the degrees of freedom of the evolution evoimp as if they were functions of time. This possibility is offered for the data structures evol_elas, evol_noli and evol_ther. To perform a “structural zoom”, the degrees of freedom must be imposed only on the nodes of the boundary of the “zoom” model. This means that, in general, the “coarse” analysis must be projected onto the mesh cells of the boundary of the “zoom” model. If, moreover, one does not wish to impose all the components, the keyword NOM_CMP must be used to choose the components to be imposed (by default: all). Notes: - Take care not to use several EVOL_IMPO on common zones (otherwise there will be accumulation of the imposed values) - Take care with the use of FONC_MULT with EVOL_IMPO : the result may not be what one expects! - The EVOL_IMPO will be used for any value of time lying between \mathit{tmin} and \mathit{tmax} (extreme values of the time instants of the transient EVOL_IMPO ). Outside this interval, a fatal error is issued (extrapolation forbidden). - If the EVOl_IMPO has only one time instant, “constant” extension is allowed and an alarm is issued. 5 Examples 5.1 Degrees of freedom imposed in mechanics chcine = AFFE_CHAR_CINE (MODELE = mo, MECA_IMPO=( _F (TOUT = 'OUI' , DRZ = 0.), _F (GROUP_NO = 'bord1', DX = 0., DY = 0., DZ = 0., DRX = 0., DRY = 0.,))) For this plate problem in the plane \mathrm{XY} , all the rotational degrees of freedom about Z are restrained and the plate is clamped on its edge \mathrm{bord1} . 5.2 Compared use of kinematic loads and “ordinary” loads 5.2.1 Global commands ch1 = AFFE_CHAR_THER ( ... ) ch2 = AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F ( TEMP_IMPO = _F ( ... )) evoth = THER_LINEAIRE ( ... EXCIT = ( _F (CHARGE = ch1), _F (CHARGE = ch2),) ...) There is no difference. 5.2.2 “Step-by-step” analysis Ordinary loads ch1 = AFFE_CHAR_MECA ( ... ) mel = CALC_MATR_ELEM ( ... OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA' , CHARGE = ch1) matas = ASSE_MATRICE ( MATR_ELEM = mel ...) matas = FACTORISER ( reuse = matas, MATR_ASSE = matas ) U = RESOUDRE ( MATR = matas , CHAM_NO = F ) Kinematic loads ch1 = AFFE_CHAR_CINE ( ... ) mel = CALC_MATR_ELEM ( ... OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA' ) matas = ASSE_MATRICE ( MATR_ELEM = mel, ..., CHAR_CINE = ch1 ) matas = FACTORISER ( reuse = matas, MATR_ASSE = matas, ) vcine = CALC_CHAR_CINE ( ..., CHAR_CINE = ch2, ) U = RESOUDRE ( MATR = matas , CHAM_NO = F, CHAM_CINE = vcine) The terms induced by the kinematic loads are transferred to the right-hand side, which requires the computation of an additional nodal field vcine by the command CALC_CHAR_CINE[U4.61.03].

u4.44.04 Operator AFFE_CHAR_ACOU u4.44.04 Operator AFFE_CHAR_ACOU 1 Purpose Assign constant acoustic boundary conditions. The assigned values do not depend on any parameter and are complex values. Produces a data structure of type char_acou. 2 Syntax char_acou = AFFE_CHAR_ACOU( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ DOUBLE_LAGRANGE = "OUI", ◆ | PRES_IMPO = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = grma, | GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ PRES = complex, ), | VITE_FACE = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ / VNOR = complex, ), | LIAISON_UNIF = _F( ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ DDL = "PRES" (ou non renseigné), ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo Name of the model whose mesh supports the acoustic computational elements. 3.2 Operand DOUBLE_LAGRANGE ◊ DOUBLE_LAGRANGE = ’OUI’/’NON’ This keyword makes it possible to state whether or not the user wishes to duplicate the Lagrange multipliers used to define and dualise the boundary conditions in the assembled matrix. Concretely, duplicating the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to use linear solvers which do not allow pivoting. Not duplicating the Lagrange multipliers makes it possible to reduce the number of degrees of freedom of the problem (and therefore the size of the problem to be solved), but its use is limited to the solvers MUMPS and Petsc. 3.3 Keywords PRES_IMPO 3.3.1 Purpose Factor keywords giving the nature of the conditions imposed on the specified entities (nodes or mesh cells). ♦ | PRES_IMPO Makes it possible to impose the pressure degree of freedom. | VITE_FACE Makes it possible to specify the vibratory velocity field imposed as a loading on boundary elements. 3.3.2 Operands TOUT / GROUP_NO / GROUP_MA / SANS_GROUP_NO / SANS_GROUP_MA Declaration of the topological entities on which the loadings and boundary conditions are applied. These are imposed on the nodes or mesh cells given by the keywords TOUT, GROUP_MA, GROUP_NO, while possibly excluding some by means of the keywords SANS_ . Caution: the keywords SANS_ are available only for the keyword PRES_IMPO. 3.3.3 Operands PRES / IMPE PRES = pre Complex value of the acoustic pressure degree of freedom (the only degree of freedom in acoustic modelling) imposed on the specified nodes. IMPE = z Complex value of the acoustic impedance imposed on the specified mesh cells. 3.4 Keyword LIAISON_UNIF 3.4.1 Purpose Factor keyword making it possible to impose one and the same (unknown) value on degrees of freedom of a set of nodes. 3.4.2 Operands GROUP_MA / GROUP_NO These operands make it possible to define a list of n nodes {N}_{i} from which redundancies have been eliminated (for GROUP_MA, these are the connectivities of the mesh cells). 3.4.3 Keyword DDL This operand can, in acoustic modelling, take only the text 'PRES', defining the only permitted degree of freedom, the acoustic pressure p . The resulting imposed conditions are: p({N}_{1})=p({N}_{i}) for i\in \lbrace 2,\mathrm{...},n\rbrace 4 Example cha = AFFE_CHAR_ACOU( MODELE = mo , VITE_FACE = _F( GROUP_MA = gm4 , VNOR = ( 'RI' , 0.0135 , 0. ) ) , ) Note: The complex values are supplied in one of the two forms RI (real part, imaginary part) or MP (modulus, phase in degrees).

u4.44.05 Operators AFFE_CHAR_SECH and AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F u4.44.05 Operators AFFE_CHAR_SECH and AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F 1 Purpose Assign loadings and boundary conditions on a drying analysis model. For the operator AFFE_CHAR_SECH, the assigned values do not depend on any parameter and are defined by real values. For the operator AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F, the values are functions of one or more parameters to be chosen from the set (INST, X, Y, Z). The functions depend solely on the water concentration (SECH) and must be tabulated. Moreover, for certain loadings the values may depend on the command variables. These functions must previously be defined by calling one of the operators: - DEFI_CONSTANTE[U4.31.01]; - DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02; - DEFI_NAPPE[U4.31.03]; - FORMULE[U4.31.05]; - CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01. The concept produced is of type char_ther, as for the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER. The loadings can be applied only on elements to which a drying modelling is assigned. 2 Syntax char_ther = AFFE_CHAR_SECH( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ DOUBLE_LAGRANGE = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◆ | SECH_IMPO = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = list[grma], | GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◆ SECH = float, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) char_ther = AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ DOUBLE_LAGRANGE = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◆ | SECH_IMPO = _F( ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = list[grma], | GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◇ SECH = fonction / formule / nappe, ), | FLUX_NL = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ FLUN = fonction, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 General remarks on the operands 3.1.1 The two forms of operands under a factor keyword The operands under a factor keyword are of two forms: - the operands specifying the topological entities on which the loadings are assigned (keywords GROUP_NO and GROUP_MA, etc.). The arguments of these operands are identical for the two operators. - the operand or operands specifying the assigned values (SECH, etc.). The meaning of these operands is the same for the two operators, but the arguments of these operands are all of type real for the operator AFFE_CHAR_SECH and of type fonction (created by one of the operators DEFI_FONCTION, DEFI_NAPPE, DEFI_CONSTANTE, FORMULE or CALC_FONC_INTERP) for the operator AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F. We shall therefore not distinguish, in this document, except where expressly stated otherwise, between the two operators AFFE_CHAR_SECH and AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F. 3.1.2 Topological entities for the assignment of the loadings In general, the topological entities on which values are to be assigned are defined: - by nodes, using the operand GROUP_NO, which makes it possible to introduce a list of node groups, - by mesh cell, using the operand GROUP_MA, which makes it possible to introduce a list of mesh-cell groups, Rule: In order to define the assignment domain as simply as possible, the overloading rule is used: it is the last assignment which takes precedence. 3.2 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo, Concept produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01, in which the types of finite elements assigned on the mesh are defined. Only a model containing solely drying modellings is accepted in these operators. These modellings are: 3D_SECH, 3D_SECH_DIAG, AXIS_SECH and AXIS_SECH_DIAG. 3.3 Keyword SECH_IMPO 3.3.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to impose, on nodes or node groups, a water concentration. Depending on the name of the operator called, the values are supplied directly (AFFE_CHAR_SECH) or by means of a concept of type fonction (AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F). 3.3.2 Operand SECH Value of the water concentration imposed on the specified node(s). 3.4 Keyword FLUX_NL 3.4.1 Purpose Factor keyword usable to apply normal fluxes that are functions of the water concentration (SECH), to a face of a volume element defined by one or more mesh cells of type triangle or quadrangle . This keyword also makes it possible to apply a normal flux to an edge (in AXIS) on mesh cells of type segment. One can thus model a radiation condition of Stefan-law type. This type of flux is available only in the command AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F. The values are supplied by a concept of type fonction. The function depends on the water concentration, to the exclusion of any other parameter. Moreover, it must necessarily be a tabulated function and not a formula. 3.4.2 Syntax - For AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F FLUX_NL = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ FLUN = fonction, ), 3.4.3 Operand FLUN : flux imposé normal à la maille. This loading applies to the following mesh-cell types and modellings: | Mesh cell | Modelling | | --- | --- | | TRIA3, TRIA6, QUAD4, QUAD8, QUAD9 | 3D_SECH, 3D_SECH_DIAG | | SEG2, SEG3 | AXIS_SECH, AXIS_SECH_DIAG | More precisely, the boundary condition applied is: \lambda (\mathrm{grad}C\cdot n) = fl where n is the normal oriented in the direction of the numbering of the nodes of the mesh cell. Orientation described in AFFE_CHAR_MECA, document U4.44.01.

u4.44.06 AFFE_CHAR_GENE u4.44.06 AFFE_CHAR_GENE 1 Purpose Assign boundary conditions on a generalised model. Produces a data structure of type char_gene. 2 Syntax char_gene = AFFE_CHAR_GENE( ◆ NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_gene, ◆ LIAISON_DDL = _F( ◆ NUME_MODE = list[int], ◆ COEF_MULT = list[float], ◆ COEF_IMPO = float, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword NUME_DDL_GENE Numbering associated with the generalised model. 3.2 Keyword LIAISON The keyword LIAISON makes it possible to define a linear relation between modes. The following condition will be applied: {\sum}_{i=1}^{N}{\alpha}_{i}{M}_{i}=\beta With {M}_{i} the list of the N generalised degrees of freedom (each corresponding to a mode), {\alpha}_{i} the coefficients and \beta the right-hand side. NUME_MODE gives the ordered list of the N generalised degrees of freedom {M}_{i} . COEF_MULT gives the ordered list of the N real coefficients {\alpha}_{i} . COEF_IMPO is the value of the linear relation \beta .
