possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand OPERATION ♦ OPERATION= définit le type d’opération à effectuer avec cet opérateur : ’AFFE’ : creation of a result data structure from fields. It is up to the user to ensure the consistency of the fields supplied in order to create the data structure and to check that they rest on the same model. ’PERM_CHAM’ : reorganisation of the fuel assemblies, ’PROL_RTZ’ : extension of a \mathrm{1D} field onto an axisymmetric structure, ’PREP_VARC’ : computation of the temperature in the layers of a shell, starting either: - from a map of functions created from a temperature given by a NAPPE or a FORMULE of the type: \mathit{temp}=f(\mathit{inst},\mathit{epais}) ; \mathit{temp}=f(\mathit{inst},\mathit{excent}) ; \mathit{temp}=f(\mathit{inst},x,y,z) where: ◦ \mathit{inst} is the time, ◦ \mathit{epais} is the thickness of the shell in [-h/2,h/2] , ◦ \mathit{excent} is the position in the layer, taking account of the offset of the shell, in [\mathit{excent}-h/2,\mathit{excent}+h/2] . ◦ x,y,z coordinates of the centre of gravity of the layer. - from a temperature computed by aster with a shell model (TEMP_MIL / TEMP_INF / TEMP_SUP), ’ASSE’ : creation of a result data structure from several result data structures placed end to end. ’KUCV’ : creation of right-hand-side loading transients of type evol_char or dyna_trans by product of assembled matrices with kinematic fields of velocities and/or displacements. ’CONV_RESU’ : creation of right-hand-side loading transients of type evol_char or dyna_trans by conversion and combination of transient results. ’CONV_CHAR’ : creation of right-hand-side loading transients of type dyna_trans by assembly of space-time loads of plane-wave or nodal-force type. La structure de données résultat peut-êtreréentrante pour le opération AFFE. Elle l’est toujours pour PERM_CHAM Pour OPERATION = ’AFFE’, les champs existants peuvent être remplacés suivant la valeur de la variable d’accès INST en utilisant les valeurs renseignées derrière les mots clés PRECISIONet CRITERE. Quand il y a remplacement d’un champ existant, le code émet un message d’alarme, sinon les champs sont stockés à la fin de la structure de données. 3.2 Operand TYPE_RESU ♦ TYPE_RESU Type de la structure de données résultat créée. In the case of a result of type evol_varc and of an evaluation of a field of functions (time and space), the consistency between the nature of the field of functions and the name of the field given under NOM_CHAM is checked. If, for example, the field of functions is of type NOEU_NEUT_F, the name of the field must be NEUT. 3.3 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM Nom symbolique du champ à affecter. Ce nom doit être cohérent avec la structure de données modifiée ou créée. Il peut prendre par exemple la valeur ’DEPL’, ’VARI_ELGA’, ’TEMP’, ’FLUX_ELNO’, ’IRRA’, etc . In the case of a result of type evol_varc and of an evaluation of a field of functions (time and space), Code_Aster checks the consistency between the nature of the field of functions and the name of the field given under nom_cham. If, for example, the field of functions is of type NOEU_NEUT_F, the name of the field must be NEUT. In the case of a result of type ’EVOL_CHAR’, the fields that one can create are: | PRES | Pressure fields (N/{m}^{2}) , component \mathit{PRES} | | --- | --- | | FVOL_3D | Volumetric force fields (N/m\mathrm{³}) , components \mathit{FX} , \mathit{FY} , \mathit{FZ} | | FVOL_2D | Volumetric force fields (N/m\mathrm{³}) , components \mathit{FX} , \mathit{FY} | | FSUR_3D | Surface force fields (N/{m}^{2}) , components \mathit{FX} , \mathit{FY} , \mathit{FZ} | | FSUR_2D | Surface force fields (N/{m}^{2}) , components \mathit{FX} , \mathit{FY} | | VITE_VENT | Fields at the nodes of wind velocity (m/s) , components \mathit{DX} , \mathit{DY} , \mathit{DZ} | | T_EXT | Map of exterior temperature, component \mathit{TEMP} | | COEF_H | Map of the heat-exchange coefficient, component H | | FLUN | Map of normal fluxes, component \mathit{FLUN} | | FORC_NODA | Fields at the nodes, components \mathit{FX} , \mathit{FY} , \mathit{FZ} | 3.4 Operand COMPORTEMENT The syntax of this keyword, common to several commands, is described in the document U4.51.11. This keyword must be supplied in the case of non-linear mechanics, because it is used on restart of the analysis in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE in order to check the compatibility of the constitutive behaviours (the number of internal variables in particular). During the operation AFFE in the case of non-linear mechanics, - without reuse, a new result data structure will be created with the constitutive behaviour supplied. If COMPORTEMENT is not supplied, the constitutive behaviour taken by default is elastic (COMPORTEMENT=’ELAS’) in small strains (RELATION=’PETIT’). - One uses reuse in order to add or replace fields in the result. If COMPORTEMENT is supplied, its behaviour map is replaced for all the time instants; otherwise, the constitutive behaviour is kept for the existing time instant and that of the previous time instant is recovered for the non-existent time instant (elastic in small strains if there is no previous time instant). At the end of the operation AFFE, for each time instant, the consistency between its behaviour map and the number of internal variables is checked (see keyword VERI_VARI). Despite the inconsistencies, some authorised cases allow this field (VARI_ELGA) to be taken up again in a non-linear analysis, and the analysis should proceed correctly (automatic correction in the operator). 3.5 Operand VERI_VARI > ◊ VERI_VARI = /’OUI’ [DEFAUT] /’NON’ This keyword is used to check the consistency between the size of the fields of type VARI_ELGA and the definition of the non-linear constitutive behaviour. If there are differences, alarms are emitted. 3.6 Operands EXCIT For a result coming from the command CREA_RESU to be usable by other commands, it is necessary to build and to fill in the data structure by specifying the associated loads. The factor keyword EXCIT is used for the TYPE_RESU: EVOL_ELAS, EVOL_NOLI, EVOL_THER and EVOL_SECH. One will refer to the respective documents U4.51.01, U4.51.03 and U4.54.01. 3.7 Keyword CHAM_GD 3.7.1 Operand CHAM_GD ♦ CHAM_GD= chno chno is: 1. either a cham_no of functions created by the command crea_champ U4.72.04 and, in this case, one evaluates the function for each node and, for each time instant defined under list_inst or inst, one creates a cham_no of reals, 2. or a cham_no or a cham_elem of reals created by the command crea_champ (keyword AFFE or EXTR) and this field is duplicated as many times as the list of time instants defined under LIST_INST or INST requires. 3.7.2 Operands MODELE, CHAM_MATER, CARA_ELEM,CHARGE These optional operands are used to allow the result data structures to be filled in. This filling-in is essential in the case where the command CREA_RESU is called by MACRO_ELAS_MULT, in order then to use the post-processing commands which will look for this information in the data structure. ◊ MODELE = mo, Name of the model whose elements are the subject of the analysis. ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmat, Name of the material field. ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, Name of the characteristics of the structural elements (beam, shell, discrete, …) if they are used in the model. When OPERATION takes the value PREP_VARC, the components EPAIS and COQU_NCOU are recovered from it. ◊ CHARGE = char, Name of a concept of type char_meca produced by AFFE_CHAR_MECA or by AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01 from the model mo. One may also give the name of a “kinematic load” (type char_cine_meca), the result of the operators AFFE_CHAR_CINE or AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F U4.44.03. 3.7.3 Operands LIST_INST/ LIST_FREQ /NUME_INIT / NUME_FIN ♦ LIST_INST= litps List of reals produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. ♦ LIST_FREQ= lifreq List of reals produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. ◊ NUME_INIT= nuini ◊ NUME_FIN= nufin The analysis time instants are those defined in the concept litps, taken between the nuini and the nufin time-instant number. In the absence of the keyword NUME_FIN, it is the size of the list of reals that is taken into account. 3.7.4 Operands INST ♦ INST= linst List of reals: list of the time instants for which the cham_no of functions will be evaluated, or else the cham_no of reals will be assigned. Note: The order number created in the concept resultat is either recovered from the value of the access variable INST when it is present, or assigned to the immediately higher maximum value. 3.7.5 Operands FREQ Dans le cas MODE_MECA/MODE_MECA_C: ◊ FREQ = freq Value of the frequency. This operand is optional; it makes it possible, in the case of a re-entrant concept, to declare another field for one and the same mode number (NUME_MODE) without having to supply the frequency. Note that if the user declares a field (for example EFGE_ELNO) for a NUME_MODE for which another field already exists with an associated frequency (for example DEPL) and supplies the operand FREQ with a different value, the concept will not be able to be processed by COMB_SISM_MODAL. Dans les autres cas: ♦ FREQ= lfreq List of reals: list of the frequencies for which the cham_no of functions will be evaluated, or else the cham_no of reals will be assigned. Note: The order number created in the concept resultat is either recovered from the value of the access variable FREQ when it is present, or assigned to the immediately higher maximum value. 3.7.6 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE These operands make it possible to refine the access by real access variables of time or of frequency. I PRECISION = / prec [R] / 0.0 ou 1.0D-3 ou 1.0D-6 [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to indicate that one searches for all the fields whose time instant (respectively the frequency) lies in the interval "inst ± prec" (cf. CRITERE). In the case where OPERATION = ’AFFE’, the default value prec is set to 0.0 in order to avoid overwriting a field whose time-instant value is close to the one being processed. The time instant supplied is not used to recover a field in the data structure; it is an attribute which must be associated with the field that one stores. In general, the fields that one stores all correspond to different time instants. In the very rare case where the user would wish to overwrite one of the fields contained in the data structure, the keyword PRECISION will have to be used. An alarm message then indicates the name of the fields concerned, together with their storage time instants, and the precision supplied by the user: I CRITERE = / ’RELATIF’ [DEFAUT] / ’ABSOLU’ ’RELATIF’: the search interval is: [inst (1 - prec), inst (1 + prec)] ’ABSOLU’ : the search interval is: [inst - prec, inst + prec]. 3.7.7 Operands NUME_MODE / TYPE_MODE Dans le cas MODE_MECA/MODE_MECA_C: ♦ NUME_MODE = num Integer designating the mode number in the case TYPE_RESU=’MODE_MECA’. Dans le cas FOURIER_ELAS: ◊ NUME_MODE = num Integer designating the number of the Fourier harmonic of the field stored in a concept of type fourier_elas. ◊ TYPE_MODE= / ’SYME’ / ’ANTI’ / ’TOUS’ Defines the type of the Fourier mode stored. | ’SYME’: | symmetric harmonic | | --- | --- | | ’ANTI’: | antisymmetric harmonic | | ’TOUS’: | symmetric and antisymmetric harmonic | 3.7.8 Operand AXE Disponible dans le cas MODE_MECA/MODE_MECA_C uniquement: ◊ AXE = / ’X’ / ’Y’ / ’Z’ Makes it possible to define a direction for a given order number so that the output concept can be supplied to the operand MODE_CORR of COMB_SISM_MODAL[U4.84.01]. 3.7.9 Operand NOM_CAS ♦ NOM_CAS = nomc Character string defining the access variable of the field stored in a concept of type mult_elas. 3.7.10 Operands MATR_RIGI/MATR_MASS In the case where TYPE_RESU=’MODE_MECA’, ’DYNA_HARMO’ or ’DYNA_TRANS’: ◊ MATR_RIGI= matr_k Stiffness matrix corresponding to the stored fields. ◊ MATR_MASS= matr_m Mass matrix corresponding to the stored fields. 4 Operands associated with the fuel assemblies 4.1 Operands RESU_INIT ♦ RESU_INIT= rinit Nom de la SD evol_noli contenant les champs à transférer sur le nouveau maillage. 4.2 Operands INST_INIT / PRECISION/CRITERE ♦ INST_INIT = iinit Time instant characterising, in the evol_noli data structure indicated under RESU_INIT, the fields to be transferred onto the other mesh. By default, the last archived time instant is selected ♦ PRECISION = prec Précision utilisée pour rechercher l’instant spécifié par INST_INIT dans la structure de données evol_noli associée à RESU_INIT. ♦ CRITERE = / ’RELATIF’ [DEFAUT] / ’ABSOLU’ Critère utilisé pour rechercher l’instant spécifié par INST_INIT dans la structure de données evol_noli associée à RESU_INIT. 4.3 Operands MAILLAGE_INIT ♦ MAILLAGE_INIT= maillagei Nom du maillage sur lequel a été définie la SD evol_noli indiquée sous RESU_INIT. 4.4 Operands RESU_FINAL ♦ RESU_FINAL=resu Name of the evol_noli data structure defined on the new mesh onto which the fields will be transferred. The data structure resu must exist (it will have been created, for example, by the command STAT_NON_LINE) and must contain only one order number. 4.5 Operands MAILLAGE_FINAL ♦ MAILLAGE_FINAL = mailfin Nom de la structure de données maillagecréée sur le nouveau maillage sur lequel seront transférés les champs. 4.6 Keyword PERM_CHAM 4.6.1 Operands GROUP_MA_FINAL ♦ GROUP_MA_FINAL = gma_2 Name of the mesh-cell group of MAILLAGE_FINAL, the place where the fields are transferred into RESU_FINAL. 4.6.2 Operands GROUP_MA_INIT ♦ GROUP_MA_INIT = gma_1 Name of the mesh on which the evol_noli data structure indicated under RESU_INIT was defined. 4.6.3 Operand TRAN ♦ TRAN = (tx,ty,tz) Translation vector making it possible to obtain GROUP_MA_FINAL geometrically from GROUP_MA_INIT. It is necessary to supply exactly 3 values. 4.6.4 Operand PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = prec Absolute precision making it possible to check the proper correspondence between the initial mesh cells and the final mesh cells; by default the value is set to {10}^{-3} . 5 Operands associated with the projection onto an axisymmetric mesh Construction of a thermal transient on an axisymmetric mesh (3D) from the data of a thermal transient computed on a 1D mesh. The 1D transient is given in the form of a TABLE data structure coming from the command POST_RELEVE_T and possessing the following parameters: - the definition of the time instants (’INST’), - the coordinates of the nodes of the 1D mesh (’COOR_X’) - the value of the temperatures at the nodes (’TEMP’). The coordinates of the table must necessarily have as their origin the node of coordinate 0. The temperature values may optionally be extended in a constant manner or else interpolated linearly as a function of the coordinate ’COOR_X’. 5.1 Operands MAILLAGE_FINAL ♦ MAILLAGE_FINAL= mailfin Nom du maillage sur lequel on effectue la projection, l’opérateur vérifie que le maillage est tridimensionnel. 5.2 Operands TABLE ♦ TABLE= table Nom d’une structure de données TABLEissue de la commande POST_RELEVE_Tcontenant le transitoire thermique 1D. Les paramètres de cette table sont obligatoirement: ’INST’, ’COOR_X’et ’TEMP’. 5.3 Operands INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ INST= litps List of real values. ◊ LIST_INST= litps List of reals produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. ◊ PRECISION = / prec [R] /1-0D-6 [DEFAUT] Précision utilisée pour rechercher l’instant spécifié dans la TABLE post_1D. ◊ CRITERE = / ’RELATIF’, / ’ABSOLU,’ Critère utilisé pour rechercher l’instant spécifié dans la TABLE post_1D. 5.4 Operands PROL_DROITE and PROL_GAUCHE The projection of the transient is carried out along the coordinate COOR_X, considered as the coordinate r in the cylindrical frame of the 3D mesh. With the aid of these two operands, one can define the way of extending the field beyond the bounds defined by the range of variation of the parameter ’COOR_X’ in the table. ◊ PROL_DROITE et PROL_GAUCHE = Define the type of extension to the right (to the left) of the domain of definition of the variable: | ’CONSTANT’ | for an extension with the last (or first) value of the function, | | --- | --- | | ’LINEAIRE’ | for an extension along the first segment defined (PROL_GAUCHE) or the last segment defined (PROL_DROITE), | | ’EXCLU’ | if the extrapolation of the values outside the domain of definition of the parameter is forbidden (in this case if an analysis requests a value of the function outside the domain of definition, the code will stop in fatal error). | 5.5 Operand REPERE/ORIGINE/AXE_Z ♦ REPERE = ’CYLINDRIQUE’ The working frame for projecting the transient is assumed to be cylindrical, the 1D transient being considered as the radial variation of the temperature field. The following two operands make it possible to carry out a change of frame. ♦ ORIGINE = (ori1,ori2,ori3) Corresponds to the position of the origin of the 1D mesh with respect to the origin of the 3D mesh. ♦ AXE_Z = (axe1,axe2,axe3) Definition of the axis of the cylindrical frame. 6 Operands associated with the preparation of the command variables 6.1 Keyword PREP_VARC The thermal evolution that one can associate with the material field by AFFE_MATERIAU/AFFE_VARC must be ready to be used by the finite elements of the mechanical model. A problem arises for shell-type elements which use a temperature varying through the thickness over the different layers. For these elements, it is necessary to prepare the computation of the temperature on the layers upstream of the command AFFE_MATERIAU. To do this, the user must use the command CREA_RESU with the operation PREP_VARC (PREParation of the Command VaRiables). 6.1.1 Operand CHAM_GD ♦ CHAM_GD = chgd chgd is a map of functions created from a temperature given by a NAPPE or a FORMULE of the type: \mathit{temp}=f(\mathit{inst},\mathit{epais}) ; \mathit{temp}=f(\mathit{inst},\mathit{zexcen}) ; \mathit{temp}=f(\mathit{inst},x,y,z) where: ◦ \mathit{inst} is the time, ◦ \mathit{epais} is the thickness of the shell in [-h/2,h/2] , ◦ \mathit{excent} is the position in the layer, taking account of the offset of the shell, in [\mathit{excent}-h/2,\mathit{excent}+h/2] . ◦ x,y,z coordinates, in the frame of the mesh, of the centre of gravity of the layer. 6.1.2 Operand EVOL_THER ♦ EVOL_THER = evol evo is an EVOL_THER data structure of “shell” type, that is to say containing the components TEMP_MIL/TEMP_INF/TEMP_SUP. 6.2 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA Only in the case EVOL_THER. ◊ / TOUT= ‘OUI’ , [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to carry out the operation on all the mesh cells of the mesh. / GROUP_MA= lgma, This keyword makes it possible to carry out the operation on a list of mesh-cell groups of the mesh. 7 Operands associated with the assembly of result-type data structures Makes it possible to assemble several evol_ther data structures by placing them end to end while translating the value of the time parameter. 7.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT= resu resu is an evol_ther data structure. All the fields present in the data structure are processed; this concerns ’TEMP’,’FLUX_ELGA’,’FLUX_ELNO’,’FLUX_NOEU’,’META_ELNO’,’META_NOEU’, ’DURT_ELNO’,’DURT_NOEU’,’HYDR_ELNO’,’HYDR_NOEU’,’DETE_ELNO’, ’DETE_NOEU’,’SOUR_ELGA’,’COMPORTHER’,’ERTH_ELEM’,’ERTH_ELNO’, ’ERTH_NOEU’. 7.2 Operand TRANSLATION ◊ TRANSLATION = / tr, [R] / 0. [DEFAUT] tr is the real value which will be added to the value of the attribute INST for each field of the data structure resu before insertion into the result data structure. 8 Operands associated with the building of right-hand-side time evolutions 8.1 Keyword KUCV Building of a right-hand-side result of type evol_char or dyna_trans, to be assigned afterwards as a load in DYNA_VIBRA or DYNA_NON_LINE, from products of assembled damping and stiffness matrices with kinematic fields of velocities and displacements extracted from an evolution already computed. This makes it possible to carry out the products KU+CV , which one usually accesses by successive calls to PROD_MATR_CHAM in a time loop. 8.1.1 Operand RESU_INIT ♦ RESU_INIT= resui Nom du résultat d’évolution calculée de type dyna_trans, evol_char ou evol_noli à partir de laquelle on extrait des champs cinématiques de vitesses et déplacements utilisés dans les produits par des matrices assemblées. 8.1.2 Operands MATR_AMOR / MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_AMOR= matr_a ◊ MATR_RIGI= matr_k, Names of the assembled damping and stiffness matrices (the stiffness matrix being optional) that one uses in the products KU+CV constituting the evolution produced. 8.2 Keyword CONV_RESU Building of a result of type evol_char or dyna_trans (right-hand side), to be assigned afterwards as a load in DYNA_VIBRA or DYNA_NON_LINE, from an evolution already computed. This makes it possible to change, where applicable, the type of the result as well as the field produced. Thus, depending on the type of input to be supplied in the dynamic operators, one may have to change an evolution of type evol_char and of field ’FORC_NODA’ into an evolution of type ’dyna_trans’ and of field ’DEPL’, or the converse. Or else to change an evolution of type dyna_trans and of field ’FORC_NODA’ into another evolution of type dyna_trans but of field ’DEPL’. 8.2.1 Operand RESU_INIT ♦ RESU_INIT= resui Name of the computed evolution result of type evol_char, dyna_trans or evol_noli which one then converts into another result of type evol_char or dyna_trans, possibly changing the field name. 8.2.2 Operand NOM_CHAM_INIT ◊ NOM_CHAM_INIT= / ’DEPL’, / ’ACCE’, / ’FORC_NODA’ / ’REAC_NODA’, Name of the field of the result of the starting evolution computed, of type evol_char or dyna_trans, which one then converts into the field of the result of the evolution produced: necessarily ’FORC_NODA’ for the type evol_char, or ’DEPL’ for the dyna_trans. 8.2.3 Operands NUME_DDL / MATR_RIGI ♦ / MATR_RIGI= matr_k / NUME_DDL = nume Inputs from which one can obtain the reference numbering, or the conversion, of the evolution produced. Supplying the operand MATR_RIGI is recommended if one produces an evolution of type dyna_trans. 8.2.4 Operand COEF ◊ COEF = / coef [R] /1.0 [DEFAUT] Real combination coefficient of the evolution produced. 8.2.5 Operand DDL_EXCLUS ◊ DDL_EXCLUS = nom_cmp [TXM] Name of the component to be excluded on the field of the initial result that one converts. It applies in general to a field ’FORC_NODA’. The whole field is taken if the keyword is not supplied. 8.2.6 Operand GROUP_NO_INTERF ♦ GROUP_NO_INTERF = gni [grno] With this keyword, one defines the node group for which one wishes to generate a space-time seismic field by phase shift due to the passage of a wave. 8.2.7 Operand VITE_ONDE ♦ VITE_ONDE = vite_onde, [R] The propagation velocity of the wave. 8.2.8 Operand DIRECTION ♦ DIRECTION = dir, [R] The direction of propagation of the wave (directional vector: 3 values). 8.2.9 Operand COOR_REFE ♦ COOR_REFE = crefe [R] This keyword makes it possible to supply the coordinates (3D) of a reference point for the computation of the phase shift (arrival time of the wave). 8.2.10 Operands FONC_DX / FONC_DY /FONC_DZ / FONC_DRX / FONC_DRY / FONC_DRZ ♦ FONC_DX = fx [fonction] ◊ FONC_DY = fy [fonction] ◊ FONC_DZ = fz [fonction] ◊ FONC_DRX = frx [fonction] ◊ FONC_DRY = fry [fonction] ◊ FONC_DRZ = fry [fonction] These keywords make it possible to define, for each of the components ’DX’, ’DY’, ’DZ’, ’DRX’, ’DRY’, ’DRZ’, and only if necessary, functions or nappes or formulae depending on some of these components, as well as possibly on the parameter ’INST’, for fields of the evolution entered by RESU_INIT. This makes it possible in particular to rotate an evolution or else to obtain a differential evolution with respect to a point motion. 8.3 Keyword CONV_CHAR Building of a right-hand-side result of type dyna_trans, to be assigned afterwards as a load in DYNA_VIBRA or DYNA_NON_LINE, from the assembly, for a list of time instants, of a list of loads defined by AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F varying both in space and in time, such as plane waves or force nappes. 8.3.1 Operand CHAR ♦ CHARGE = lchar, Donnée d’une suite de nomsdeconceptsde type char_mecadéfinies par AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F etcorrespondant à des charges variant à la fois dans l’espace et dans le temps comme des ondes planes ou des forces de type FORCE_NODALE ou FORCE_ARETE constituées de l’application de nappes. Dans la suite donnée, on peut mélanger des charges de type différent, soit des ondes planes, soit des nappes de forces. Le coefficient à appliquer à l’évolution produite via COEF_MULT dans une charge EXCIT_RESU devra valoir 1.0 dans tous les cas. 8.3.2 Operand MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_RIGI= matr_k Input of a stiffness matrix serving as a reference object, and from which one can obtain the material field as well as the reference numbering of the evolution produced, of type dyna_trans. 8.4 Operands INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ INST= litps List of real values of the computation time instants of the evolutions produced. ◊ LIST_INST= litps List of reals produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01 of the computation time instants of the evolutions produced. ◊ PRECISION = / prec [R] /1.0D-6 [DEFAUT] Precision used to search for the time instant specified in the original result. ◊ CRITERE = / ’RELATIF’, / ’ABSOLU,’ Criterion used to search for the time instant specified in the original result. 9 Example of use Construction of a thermal transient from a function: The main commands used to build a result concept of type evol_ther have been defined below. Definition of a list of time instants. lr8 = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( DEBUT = 0.E0, INTERVALLE=(_F(JUSQU_A=5.e-3,NOMBRE=10 ), _F(JUSQU_A=5.e-2,NOMBRE= 9 ), _F(JUSQU_A=4.e-0,NOMBRE=79 ), _F(JUSQU_A=6.e-0,NOMBRE=20 ),) ) Definition of a function of the parameter ’INST’. fct1 = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = ’INST’ VALE= ( 0.0, 20.0, 0.5, 25.0, 2.0, 54.0, 10.0, 134.0,) PROL_DROIT = ’LINEAIRE’, PROL_GAUCHE= ’LINEAIRE’, ) Construction of a field at the nodes of functions; the same function fct1 is assigned to all the nodes of the mesh. ch = CREA_CHAMP ( TYPE_CHAM=’NOEU_TEMP_F’, OPERATION= ’AFFE’, MAILLAGE=ma , AFFE=_F(TOUT=’OUI’, NOM_CMP=’TEMP’, VALE_F=fct1,), ) ... Creation of the result concept TEMPE, built from the field at the nodes of functions ch. One limits oneself to order number 20, corresponding to the value 0.1. The data structure will comprise 20 order numbers from 1 to 20. TEMPE = CREA_RESU( OPERATION= ’AFFE’, TYPE_RESU= ’EVOL_THER’, AFFE= ( _F( CHAM_NO = ch , NOM_CHAM= ’TEMP’, LIST_INST= lr8, NUME_FIN = 20 , ), ) ) ... FIN()

u4.44.13 Operator DEFI_CONT u4.44.13 Operator DEFI_CONT Summary: One defines in this operator the unilateral contact and friction conditions for its (exclusive) use in the operator MECA_NON_LINE For contact in STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE, refer to the documentation of DEFI_CONTACT. This documentation is provisional, the operator cannot be used in the AIP studies and it is outside the scope of qualification. 1 Purpose Assign unilateral contact and friction conditions in mechanics. The following points are detailed: - control of the pairing for the facing boundaries; - the physical and numerical parameters, useful for the various formulations available. 2 Syntax / char_cont / char_frot = DEFI_CONT( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◆ ZONE = _F( ◇ VERI_NORM = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ ALGO_CONT = / "LAGRANGIEN" (par défaut), / "NITSCHE", / "PENALISATION", # Si: is_in("ALGO_CONT", ("NITSCHE")) ◇ SYME = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("SYME", "NON") ◇ VARIANTE = / "RAPIDE", / "ROBUSTE" (par défaut), # Si: is_in("ALGO_CONT", ("LAGRANGIEN")) ◇ VARIANTE = / "CLASSIQUE", / "ROBUSTE" (par défaut), ◇ COEF_CONT = float (défaut: 100.0), ◇ TYPE_INTE = / "ELEM_BASE", / "SEG_BASE" (par défaut), ◇ APPARIEMENT = "MORTAR", # Si: is_in("APPARIEMENT", ("MORTAR")) ◇ APPA_TOLE = float (défaut: 1e-8), ◇ AIRE_TOLE = float (défaut: 1e-8), ◇ TYPE_APPA = / "PANG", / "FORCEBRUTE", / "RAPIDE" (par défaut), ◇ COEF_MULT_APPA = float (défaut: -1.0), ◆ GROUP_MA_MAIT = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_ESCL = grma, # Si: is_in("ALGO_CONT", ("LAGRANGIEN","LAGRANGIEN_STD")) ◇ SANS_GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, # Si: is_in("ALGO_CONT", ("LAGRANGIEN",)) ◇ TYPE_MATR_TANG = / "ANALYTIQUE" (par défaut), / "PERTURBATION", # Si: is_in("ALGO_CONT", ("PENALISATION",)) ◇ TYPE_MATR_TANG = / "ANALYTIQUE" (par défaut), / "PERTURBATION", # Si: is_in("ALGO_CONT", ("LAGRANGIEN_STD",)) ◇ TYPE_MATR_TANG = "PERTURBATION", ◇ CONTACT_INIT = / "INTERPENETRE" (par défaut), / "NON", / "OUI", ◇ DIST_SUPP = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, # Si: exists("CARA_ELEM") ◇ DIST_POUTRE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ DIST_COQUE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ FROTTEMENT = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("FROTTEMENT", "OUI") # Si: equal_to("ALGO_CONT", "LAGRANGIEN") ◇ ALGO_FROT = "LAGRANGIEN", # Si: equal_to("ALGO_CONT", "PENALISATION") ◇ ALGO_FROT = "PENALISATION", # Si: equal_to("ALGO_CONT", "LAGRANGIEN_STD") ◇ ALGO_FROT = "LAGRANGIEN_STD", ◇ COEF_FROT = float (défaut: 100.0), # Si: equal_to("TYPE_FROT", "COULOMB") ◆ COULOMB = float, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Data setup 3.1 Principles The command makes it possible to describe the zones subjected to unilateral contact conditions with or without friction. The description is made at two levels: - The global parameters, such as the parameters for controlling the non-linear solution algorithm (fixed-point or Newton loops, parameters specific to the solver), are to be supplied in the command MECA_NON_LINE - The local parameters specific to each contact zone. The concept produced by DEFI_CONT is then supplied as a parameter in the simple keyword CONTACT of the command MECA_NON_LINE. Each zone comprises two surfaces which may come into contact, and which are described by the data of the mesh-cell groups which constitute them. The sets of mesh cells potentially in contact are skin mesh cells: surface and linear in dimension 3 (QUAD9, QUAD8, QUAD4, TRIA7, TRIA6, TRIA3, SEG3, SEG2), linear and point in dimension two (SEG3, SEG2 and POI1). The structures studied may undergo large sliding relative to one another. 3.2 General parameters 3.2.1 Keyword MODELE The keyword MODELE expects a concept produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE in which are defined the types of finite elements assigned on the mesh. The model is necessarily of type MECANIQUE. 3.2.2 Keyword INFO The keyword INFO manages the level of the printouts in the message file. This printout can produce very large text files; it should therefore be used with caution on large-sized studies. 3.3 Zonal parameters 3.3.1 Definition of a zone A contact zone is defined by two groups: a group of slave mesh cells and a group of master mesh cells given by the keywords GROUP_MA_MAIT and GROUP_MA_ESCL . In order to facilitate the compatibility of the methods using Lagrange multipliers, it is possible to exclude contact nodes by the keywords SANS_GROUP_MA and SANS_GROUP_NO . In this case it is a matter of excluding the nodes carrying Lagrange multipliers. These keywords therefore concern the slave surfaces. 3.3.2 Pairing The first phase of carrying out contact-friction is the pairing phase. The pairing operation consists in finding which mesh cells and which nodes are potentially in a contact situation. When APPARIEMENT="MORTAR" must be used, several pairing methods are available: - if TYPE_APPA="PANG" , one uses the PANG method implemented in DEFI_CONTACT , which is based on a traversal of the mesh cells by the neighbours (in the sense of the edges); - if TYPE_APPA="RAPIDE" , one uses a method inspired by the historical PANG method. This approach is used by default; - if TYPE_APPA="FORCEBRUTE" , one uses a brute-force type algorithm, in which one performs a double loop over the slave and master mesh cells. This algorithm is sub-optimal in terms of computational cost, but it is the most numerically robust. Two additional parameters may be supplied by the user in the case of this pairing, APPA_TOLE and AIRE_TOLE . These two quantities correspond to numerical tolerances used in all of the pairing algorithms mentioned above. APPA_TOLE is a tolerance used in the Newton algorithms, whereas AIRE_TOLE is a criterion on the computed intersection area. For this latter criterion, one allows oneself not to consider intersection areas that are "too small". Mathematically, this amounts to keeping only mesh cells satisfying: |\Omega_{inter}| > \delta_{area} |\texttt{F}^s| where \Omega_{inter} is the intersection obtained, \delta_{area} the tolerance given by AIRE_TOLE , and \texttt{F}^s the initial slave mesh cell considered. 3.3.3 Additional parameters related to pairing The parameter COEF_MULT_APPA makes it possible to improve the pairing phase by pre-detecting whether two mesh cells are potentially in contact. One defines the distance d_{\text{cell}} between two cells defined by d_{\text{cell}} = \Vert \vector{X}_b^{\text{s}} - \vector{X}_b^{\text{m}} \Vert with \vector{X}_b^{\text{s}} , (respectively \vector{X}_b^{\text{m}} ) is the vector of the coordinates of the barycentre of the slave mesh cell (respectively master). The mesh cells are potentially paired if, and only if: d_{\text{cell}} \le 2 \, d_{r} \, \max \left( d^{\text{s}} - d^{\text{m}} \right ) with d^{\text{s}} (respectively d^{\text{m}} ) the diameter of the slave mesh cell (respectively master) and d_{r} the coefficient given by COEF_MULT_APPA . If COEF_MULT_APPA is negative, this preliminary sorting is deactivated. The keyword VERI_NORM checks the orientation of the normals to the surface mesh cells in 3D (skin mesh cells TRIA or QUAD) and to the linear mesh cells in 2D (skin mesh cells SEG). If a normal is not outward, a fatal error message is emitted. In order to reorient the mesh cells so as to have outward normals, one must use the command MODI_MAILLAGE, keyword ORIE_PEAU . No check is possible on the shells or the plates. In order to check their orientation, one also refers to the command MODI_MAILLAGE, keyword ORIE_NORM_COQUE. The keyword CONTACT_INIT makes it possible to set the contact status at the initial state. By default, only the links with zero gap, or which are interpenetrated, are activated by the algorithm ( CONTACT_INIT="INTERPENETRE" ). It is nevertheless possible to force the algorithm to activate all the links without exception ( CONTACT_INIT="OUI" ). The value CONTACT_INIT="INTERPENETRE" is mandatory in the case of a restart of the analysis with an initial state. It is also possible to deactivate any initial contact by CONTACT_INIT="NON" . - It is important to check that the connectivity of these mesh cells is such that the normal to the structure is outward (to do this, use MODI_MAILLAGE - The intersection between the slave surface and the master surface of one and the same zone must be disjoint, or else the common nodes must be excluded - The slave surfaces must imperatively be pairwise disjoint in the continuous formulation Notes 3.3.4 Integration method In the case of a pairing of type MORTAR , once it has been carried out, several integration methods are available. The keyword TYPE_INTE makes it possible to choose the integration method to be used for the integration over the contact integrals. The case TYPE_INTE="SEG_BASE" consists in intersecting the slave and master mesh cells, and in remeshing the intersection area obtained from the barycentre. This option is the one chosen by default. The case TYPE_INTE="ELEM_BASE" consists in retaining only the intersection points of the slave mesh cell which are projected into the intersection computed beforehand. 3.3.5 Modifications of the gap The gap is always computed as being the minimum distance between the slave node and the projection onto the nearest master mesh cell. It is however possible to define gap values “hard-coded”, for example in order to simulate the presence of a hole or of a bump not represented by the mesh, or in order to take account of the geometric characteristics of the structural elements which use the notion of neutral fibre or of mean surface. The keyword DIST_SUPP makes it possible to modify the gap between the two surfaces. The keyword accepts functions or formulae. A negative value makes it possible to “hollow out” a surface virtually (master as well as slave). Conversely, a positive value makes it possible to “thicken” a surface. The quantities supplied are necessarily functions of the space variables or of time ( \left( X, Y, Z,\text{INST} \right) ). If the user desires a fixed value, a constant function must be defined (see DEFI_CONSTANTE). The keywords DIST_POUTRE and DIST_COQUE make it possible to introduce a fictitious gap which rests on the description of the structural elements in the concept produced by AFFE_CARA_ELEM, which the user has mandatorily supplied: - for the beam elements (modelling POU_ ), the keyword DIST_POUTRE stipulates that the code must take account of an additional gap corresponding to the radius of the circular section of the beam. - for the plate or shell elements (modelling DKT or COQUE_3 for example), the keyword DIST_COQUE stipulates that the code must take account of an additional gap corresponding to the half-thickness about the mean sheet of a shell. Caution: when one uses these keywords, the fictitious gap is added only on the slave surface. If one models a contact between two structural elements, one will therefore also have to use DIST_MAIT . When one uses one of these keywords, it is necessary to supply CARA_ELEM . 3.3.6 Contact algorithms The contact method is chosen by the keyword ALGO_CONT . There are two possibilities: - Augmented Lagrangian methods ( LAGRANGIEN ), which solve the problem by dualisation and introduction of Lagrange multipliers (on the nodes of the slave surface) - Penalisation method ( PENALISATION ), which is a method that solves the problem by regularisation (and therefore in an approximate manner). It is a non-consistent penalisation method, that is to say that it introduces an error on the solution which does not fade when one refines the mesh. One must then adapt the penalisation coefficient in order to improve the accuracy of the resolution - Nitsche method ( NITSCHE ), which is a method that solves the problem by regularisation (and therefore in an approximate manner). The Nitsche method is a consistent penalisation method, that is to say it converges towards the solution when one refines the mesh. It is available only in 2D and for isotropic elastic constitutive behaviours There exist variants. For the augmented Lagrangian method, the keyword VARIANTE makes it possible to choose between the classical method of Alart and Curnier (CLASSIQUE) and the method developed by Poulios and Renard (ROBUSTE). In both cases, the keyword COEF_CONT makes it possible to set the augmentation parameter, which acts on the speed of convergence but not on the quality of the result (the method is exact and respects the unilateral condition). For the Nitsche method, there exist three variants according to the choice of a coefficient which one generally denotes \theta . The keyword SYME makes it possible to choose between the variant producing a symmetric matrix (case \theta=1 ) and a non-symmetric matrix (cases \theta=0 and \theta=-1 ). In this latter situation, the keyword VARIANTE makes it possible to choose the value of the coefficient \theta . The case \theta=0 corresponds to the value RAPIDE of this keyword and the case \theta=-1 corresponds to the value ROBUSTE . It should be noted that the coefficient \theta makes it possible to bring out several variants, but that it is independent of the penalisation coefficient necessary for Nitsche and given by the keyword COEF_CONT . For the augmented Lagrangian method, the keyword variante makes it possible to choose between the formulation of Alart and Curnier ( VARIANTE="CLASSIQUE" ) or the formulation of Poulios and Renard ( VARIANTE="ROBUSTE" ). The classical method uses an approximation of the tangent matrix by perturbation. The keyword TYPE_MATR_TANG makes it possible, on the other hand, to choose between an approximation of the matrix by PERTURBATION or ANALYTIQUE for the Poulios-Renard formulation. 3.3.7 Friction algorithms In order to assign Coulomb friction to the contact zones, use the keyword FROTTEMENT="OUI" . The parameter COULOMB makes it possible to set the friction coefficient. In this case, the formulations by augmented Lagrangian and by penalisation are available, that is ALGO_FROT="LAGRANGIEN" or ALGO_FROT="PENALISATION" . For the formulation by augmented Lagrangian, one has the choice between the classical formulation ( VARIANTE="CLASSIQUE" ) or the Poulios-Renard formulation ( VARIANTE="ROBUSTE" ). The parameter COEF_FROT makes it possible to set the augmentation coefficient only in the classical case, because the Poulios-Renard formulation uses the same augmentation coefficient for the contact and for the friction. For the formulation by penalisation, the same augmentation coefficient is used for the contact and for the friction. 3.3.8 Parameters and algorithms used When using the penalisation algorithms ( ALGO_CONT="PENALISATION" ) or the augmented Lagrangian ( ALGO_CONT="LAGRANGIEN" ), it is necessary to define the penalisation or augmentation coefficients. The number of parameters to be supplied depends on the formulation chosen: - Formulations with a single parameter (coming from the formalism of Poulios & Renard): A single coefficient (common to the contact and to the friction) must be supplied via the keyword COEF_CONT . This case concerns the following configurations: - ALGO_CONT="LAGRANGIEN" associated with VARIANTE="ROBUSTE" , - ALGO_CONT="PENALISATION" . - Other formulations : Two distinct keywords must be supplied: - COEF_CONT for the parameter related to the contact. - COEF_FROT for the parameter related to the friction (if the latter is taken into account).

u4.44.21 Operator DEFI_OBSTACLE u4.44.21 Operator DEFI_OBSTACLE 1 Purpose Define the geometry of the shock locations of a slender structure. These locations are defined in a plane perpendicular to the structure modelled by POU_D_T and POU_D_E beams. It is then used by DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for the study of the response of a structure whose displacements are limited by the presence of this obstacle. One may also define the initial cross-section of a structure whose progressive wear will be studied. In this latter case, the concept will be used by MODI_OBSTACLE U4.44.22. Produces a concept of type table_fonction. 2 Syntax table_fonction = DEFI_OBSTACLE( ◇ TYPE = / "CERCLE" (par défaut), / "PLAN_Y", / "PLAN_Z", / "DISCRET", / "BI_CERCLE", / "BI_PLAN_Y", / "BI_PLAN_Z", / "BI_CERC_INT", ◇ VALE = float, ◇ VERIF = text (défaut: "FERME"), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TYPE The operand TYPE makes it possible to give the envelope shape of the clearance in the shock connection by a text chosen from the following: PLAN_Y, PLAN_Z, CERCLE, DISCRET, BI_PLAN_Y, BI_PLAN_Z, BI_CERCLE and BI_CERC_INT; Obstacles of type PLAN_Y, PLAN_Z, CERCLE and DISCRET define the geometry of the shock locations between a moving structure and a non-deformable obstacle. They are plotted below [Figure 3.1-a] according to the type chosen. Figure 3.1-a The value of the clearance and the local coordinate system (\mathit{Xloc},\mathit{Yloc},\mathit{Zloc}) will be defined at the time the obstacle is used (see operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03). The origin of this coordinate system is the location of the slender structure under consideration. In the case of the obstacle TYPE = ‘DISCRET’, the curve defining the contour and the clearance simultaneously must be specified, using the keyword VALE. The types BI_PLAN_Y, BI_PLAN_Z, BI_CERCLE and BI_CERC_INT make it possible to define the possible contact locations of the slender structure between two nodes \mathit{NO1} and \mathit{NO2} each belonging to a moving structure. The geometries of the plane-on-plane (or circle-on-circle) contact connections are described in the figure [Figure 3.1-b] below. Figure 3.1-b The value of the thicknesses of material surrounding the shock nodes ( \mathit{D1} and \mathit{D2} for an obstacle of type BI_PLAN_ , \mathit{R1} and \mathit{R2} for an obstacle of type BI_CERCLE or BI_CERC_INT) as well as the local coordinate system (\mathit{Xloc},\mathit{Yloc},\mathit{Zloc}) are defined at the time the obstacle is used, that is to say in the operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. Several initial shapes, in particular for the study of the vibrations of control-rod clusters, are defined. They correspond to the rod of the various control-rod clusters and to their guides. 3.2 Operands VALE/VERIF ◊ VALE = thetar In the case of the DISCRET obstacle the curve defining the contour and the clearance simultaneously must be specified, using the keyword VALE. thetar is the list of reals making it possible to describe the contour of the obstacle of type DISCRET in polar coordinates. The obstacle is described as a plane curve in polar coordinates by giving pairs of values, the first being the angle in degrees from 0 to 360°, the second the radius [Figure3.2-a]. When defining the obstacle, it must be considered that the y-axis corresponds to an angle of 0°. VALE = ( 0.0, 0.00086, 30.0, 0.001, 90.0, 0.001, 150.0, 0.001, 210.0, 0.001, 270.0, 0.001, 330.0, 0.001, 360.0, 0.00086,) Figure 3.2-a ◊ VERIF= 'FERME' Keyword making it possible to check whether the curve given in polar coordinates is indeed closed.

u4.44.31 Operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB u4.44.31 Operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB 1 Purpose Define a turbulent excitation spectrum. Various types of spectrum are available: - for “tube bundles under cross-flow”, spectra of “correlation length” type, - for established uniform flows, parallel to plane structures or to circular cylindrical structures, boundary-layer turbulence spectra, - an excitation spectrum defined by its decomposition on a family of shape functions, by supplying a cross-spectral matrix and a list of associated shape functions. The concepts tabl_intsp and fonction must then have been generated beforehand, - a predefined turbulence spectrum, identified on the GRAPPE1 or GRAPPE2 mock-up, - an excitation spectrum associated with one or more point forces and moments, by supplying a cross-spectral matrix of excitations (concept tabl_intsp which must have been generated beforehand), the list of the nodes of application of these excitations, the nature of the excitation applied at each of these nodes (force or moment) and the directions of application of the excitations thus defined. - an excitation spectrum defined by a set of complex analytical functions. Produces a concept of type spectre. 2 Syntax spectre = DEFI_SPEC_TURB( ◆ / SPEC_LONG_COR_1 = _F( ◆ LONG_COR = float, ◆ PROF_VITE_FLUI = formule / nappe / fonction, ◆ VISC_CINE = float, ), / SPEC_LONG_COR_2 = _F( ◆ LONG_COR = float, ◆ PROF_VITE_FLUI = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ FREQ_COUP = float (défaut: 0.1), ◇ PHI0 = float (défaut: 0.0015), ◇ BETA = float (défaut: 2.7), ), / SPEC_LONG_COR_3 = _F( ◆ LONG_COR = float, ◆ PROF_VITE_FLUI = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ FREQ_COUP = float (défaut: 0.2), ◇ PHI0_1 = float (défaut: 0.005), ◇ BETA_1 = float (défaut: 0.5), ◇ PHI0_2 = float (défaut: 4e-05), ◇ BETA_2 = float (défaut: 3.5), ), / SPEC_LONG_COR_4 = _F( ◆ LONG_COR = float, ◆ PROF_VITE_FLUI = formule / nappe / fonction, ◆ TAUX_VIDE = float, ◇ BETA = float (défaut: 2.0), ◇ GAMMA = float (défaut: 4.0), ), / SPEC_CORR_CONV_1 = _F( ◆ LONG_COR_1 = float, ◇ LONG_COR_2 = float, ◆ VITE_FLUI = float, ◆ RHO_FLUI = float, ◇ FREQ_COUP = float, ◇ K = float (défaut: 0.0058), ◆ D_FLUI = float, ◇ COEF_VITE_FLUI_A = float, ◇ COEF_VITE_FLUI_O = float, ◇ METHODE = / "AU_YANG", / "GENERALE" (par défaut), / "CORCOS", ), / SPEC_CORR_CONV_2 = _F( ◆ FONCTION = formule / nappe / fonction, ◆ LONG1_F = formule / nappe / fonction, ◆ LONG2_F = formule / nappe / fonction, ◆ VITE_FLUI = float, ◇ FREQ_COUP = float, ◇ METHODE = / "AU_YANG", / "CORCOS", ◇ COEF_VITE_FLUI_A = float, ◇ COEF_VITE_FLUI_O = float, ), / SPEC_CORR_CONV_3 = _F( ◆ TABLE_FONCTION = table_fonction, ), / SPEC_FONC_FORME = _F( ◆ / INTE_SPEC = interspectre, / GRAPPE_1 = / "DEBIT_180", / "DEBIT_300", ◇ & FONCTION = table_fonction, ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ MODELE = modele, ), / SPEC_EXCI_POINT = _F( ◆ / INTE_SPEC = interspectre, / GRAPPE_2 = / "ASC_CEN", / "ASC_EXC", / "DES_CEN", / "DES_EXC", # Si: exists("INTE_SPEC") ◆ NATURE = / "FORCE", / "MOMENT", ◆ ANGLE = float, ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, # Si: exists("GRAPPE_2") ◆ RHO_FLUI = float, ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ MODELE = modele, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keywords SPEC_LONG_COR_n The definition of an excitation spectrum of “correlation length” type can be made only by a single occurrence of one of the factor keywords SPEC_LONG_COR_n, corresponding to a zone of the tube defined beforehand by the function entered under the operand PROF_VITE_FLUI of the command DEFI_FLUI_STRU U4.25.01. The velocity profile associated with this zone, recalled here under the operand PROF_VITE_FLUI, must be identical to the one entered in DEFI_FLUI_STRU U4.25.01. The use of excitation spectra of “correlation length” type is limited to the configuration “tube bundle under cross-flow” (factor keyword FAISCEAU_TRANS of the operator DEFI_FLUI_STRU U4.25.01). To carry out an analysis with several excitation zones, as many spectra as there are zones must be defined. The contributions of the various spectra may then be added when the excitation is projected onto the modal basis by the command PROJ_SPEC_BASE U4.63.14. However, it is not possible in this command to combine spectra of “correlation length” type with spectra of another type (SPEC_CORR_CONV_n, SPEC_FONC_FORME or SPEC_EXCI_POINT). The four spectra of “correlation length” type have values defined by default. The definition of new coefficients is delicate, in particular as regards model 3, for which there are continuity conditions between the straight lines determined by the coefficients. The general analytical form of models 1 to 4 is as follows: S({s}_{1,}{s}_{2,}{f}_{r})=S({f}_{r})\cdot \exp(\frac{-∣{s}_{2}-{s}_{1}∣}{{\lambda}_{c}}) with: | S({s}_{1,}{s}_{2,}{f}_{r}) | dimensionless turbulence cross-spectrum between two points of curvilinear abscissae ({s}_{1,}{s}_{2}) ; | | --- | --- | | | | | S({f}_{r}) | turbulence autospectrum; | | | | | \exp(\frac{-∣{s}_{2}-{s}_{1}∣}{{\lambda}_{c}}) | spatial correlation function and {\lambda}_{c} correlation length. | The spectrum is defined as a function of a reduced frequency {f}_{r} (Strouhal number). For a tube under cross-flow, the expression for {f}_{r} is as follows: {f}_{r}=\frac{f\cdot \mathrm{de}}{{V}_{g}} f is the dimensional frequency, \mathrm{de} the external diameter of the tube {V}_{g} and the mean transverse velocity of the fluid along the structure, which will be recovered in the operator PROJ_SPEC_BASE U4.63.14 via the concept [melasflu] produced by the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU [U4.66.02]. 3.1.1 Analytical expression of the spectra of type SPEC_LONG_COR_1 ♦ / SPEC_LONG_COR_1 Factor keyword corresponding to the first spectrum model with correlation length. ♦ LONG_COR= lc Correlation length. ♦ PROF_VITE_FLUI= profv Name of the velocity profile corresponding to the zone where the turbulent excitation is applied. ♦ VISC_CINE= eps Kinematic viscosity of the fluid. S({f}_{r})=\frac{{\Phi}_{0}}{{\left[1-{\left[\frac{{f}_{r}}{{f}_{\mathit{rc}}}\right]}^{\beta /2}\right]}^{2}+4{e}^{2}{\left[\frac{{f}_{r}}{{f}_{\mathit{rc}}}\right]}^{\beta /2}} with: {\Phi}_{0}={\Phi}_{0}({R}_{e}) polynomial of the fifth degree. \begin{array}{}\beta =\beta ({R}_{e})\\ \varepsilon =\varepsilon ({R}_{e})\\ {f}_{\mathrm{rc}}=0,2\end{array} If 1,5{.10}^{4} {5.10}^{4} : {\Phi}_{0}=38,6075 | If {R}_{e}\le 3,5{.10}^{4} | | \varepsilon =0,7 \beta =3 | | --- | --- | --- | | Else if 3,5{.10}^{4} {f}_{c} . K denotes the constant of the model, entered under the operand K . For the CORCOS model, K is determined experimentally and is equal to K=5,8{.10}^{-3}{s}^{1/2}{m}^{-3/2} ; \rho is the mass density of the fluid, entered under the operand RHO_FLUI ; U is the fluid velocity, entered under the operand VITE_FLUI ; d is the hydraulic diameter, entered under the operand D_FLUI. 3.2.2 Definition of a turbulence spectrum given by an arbitrary function of frequency / SPEC_CORR_CONV_2 Factor keyword making it possible to define a pressure spectrum and correlation lengths that are functions of the angular frequency ♦ FONCTION= fonc Concept of type fonction defining the pressure spectrum as a function of the angular frequency, produced by one of the operators DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02, CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04 or CALC_FONC_INTERP U4.32.01. ♦ LONG1_F= lc1 Concept of type fonction defining the correlation length along the axis of the flow for any method. ♦ LONG2_F= lc2 Concept of type fonction defining the correlation length along the axis perpendicular to the flow for any method. ♦ VITE_FLUI= vflui Velocity of the fluid flowing along the structure under study. ◊ FREQ_COUP= fc Cut-off frequency beyond which the function defining the pressure spectrum is considered to be zero. ♦ METHODE= ’CORCOS’ ou ’AU_YANG’ Correlation method determined by the type of structure whose vibrations generated by the turbulence one wishes to study. ◊ COEF_VITE_FLUI_A= alpha Coefficient of the convective velocity of the eddies in the axial direction (direction of the flow) for the CORCOS and AU_YANG methods. ◊ COEF_VITE_FLUI_O= beta Coefficient of the convective velocity of the eddies in the direction orthoradial to the cylinder. By default, this parameter takes the value 999 and is thus not considered for the analysis. 3.2.3 SPEC_CORR_CONV_3: arbitrary spectrum defined analytically / SPEC_CORR_CONV_3 Factor keyword making it possible to define a spectrum on the basis of analytical functions. ♦ TABLE_FONCTION= table Concept of type table of functions containing the analytical formulae defining the spectrum. Example of use: one wishes to describe the pressure forces induced by an axial flow along a fuel rod in the form of a spectrum of “correlation length” type, describing: - on the one hand the decay of the turbulent energy downstream of the grid, - on the other hand the phase shift due to the convection of the turbulence with the flow. The correlation length, and the autospectrum, depend on the frequency. The analytical formulation proposed is as follows: {S}_{f}(\underline{{r}_{1}},\underline{{r}_{2}},\omega )=\lbrace \begin{array}{c}{S}_{x}=\exp(-\frac{\mid \underline{{r}_{2}}-\underline{{r}_{1}}\mid }{{\lambda}_{\text{cx}}(\omega )}).\exp(\mathit{j\omega }\frac{{z}_{2}-{z}_{1}}{{U}_{c}}){S}_{f}(\underline{{r}_{1}},\underline{{r}_{1}},\omega )\\ {S}_{y}=\exp(-\frac{\mid \underline{{r}_{2}}-\underline{{r}_{1}}\mid }{{\lambda}_{\text{cy}}(\omega )}).\exp(\mathit{j\omega }\frac{{z}_{2}-{z}_{1}}{{U}_{c}}){S}_{f}(\underline{{r}_{1}},\underline{{r}_{1}},\omega )\end{array} \underline{{r}_{1}} and \underline{{r}_{2}} are the vectors locating the positions of the two points to be correlated, z is the direction parallel to the axis of the rod. One may also add, if one wishes, a correlation term between the forces along x and y . The spectrum above is defined in the test case sdll148b with correlated forces. The modelling with uncorrelated forces is proposed here (no cross terms SXY and SYX). In this test case the rod is oriented along the Y direction. SXX = FORMULE(NOM_PARA=('X1','Y1','Z1','X2','Y2','Z2','FREQ'), VALE_C='exp(-FREQ/freq0) exp(distance(X1,Y1,Z1,X2,Y2,Z2)/correl(FREQ)) complex(cos(2 pi FREQ (Y2-Y1)/Uc), sin(2 pi FREQ (Y2-Y1)/Uc))',) SYY = ... # INTER-SPECTRE AVEC EFFORTS X ET Y DECORRELES INTESPEC = CREA_TABLE( LISTE=( _F(LISTE_K=("SXX", "SYY"), PARA="FONCTION_C"), _F(LISTE_K=("DX", "DY"), PARA="NUME_ORDRE_I"), _F(LISTE_K=("DX", "DY"), PARA="NUME_ORDRE_J"), ), TYPE_TABLE="TABLE_FONCTION", TITRE="EXCITATION FLUIDE TURBULENTE", ) SPECTRE1 = DEFI_SPEC_TURB(SPEC_CORR_CONV_3=_F(TABLE_FONCTION=INTESPEC)) The function distance has been defined in Python and gives the distance between two points of respective coordinates ({x}_{1,}{y}_{1,}{z}_{1}) and ({x}_{2,}{y}_{2,}{z}_{2}) . The function correl depends exponentially on the frequency. 3.3 Keyword SPEC_FONC_FORME / SPEC_FONC_FORME Factor keyword making it possible to define an excitation spectrum by its decomposition on a family of shape functions. ♦ / INTE_SPEC= int_spec Concept of type interspectre defining a cross-spectral excitation matrix. This concept may be produced by the operator LIRE_INTE_SPEC U4.36.01 after reading the cross-spectral matrix from an external file. FONCTION= l_tab_fonc List of concepts of type table_fonction defining the family of shape functions associated with each mode. For each mode, a table containing 2 shape functions in the 2 directions orthogonal to the axis of the slender structure is entered. / GRAPPE_1= ’DEBIT_180’ ou ’DEBIT_300’ Two possible choices corresponding to the flow rates for which the GRAPPE1 excitation was identified. ♦ GROUP_NO= gno Groupe contenant le noeud d’application de l’excitation. ♦ CARA_ELEM= cara Concept of type cara_elem produced by the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01; it defines the geometric characteristics assigned to the elements of the structure. The geometric characteristics are necessary for the estimation of the hydraulic diameter. In addition, the concept of type cara_elem provides the information relating to the orientations of the elements. ♦ MODELE= modele Concept of type modele produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01; it defines the types of elements assigned to the mesh cells of the structure. Notes The application length L is characterised in an intrinsic manner by the domain of definition of the shape functions associated with the excitation. The application zone is centred about the application node. The turbulent excitation being liable to be developed in a correlated manner in the two directions orthogonal to the axis of the slender structure (axis x ), the shape functions are a priori vectors with two components (along y and z ). One therefore defines, for each mode, two shape functions (one along y and one along z ) over the interval (0;L) . The functions are then passed in a table_fonction to the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB. (cf. test case sdll116a). 3.4 Keyword SPEC_EXCI_POINT / SPEC_EXCI_POINT Factor keyword making it possible to define an excitation spectrum associated with one or more point forces and moments. ♦ / INTE_SPEC= int_spec Concept of type interspectre defining a cross-spectral matrix of point excitations. This concept may be produced by the operator LIRE_INTE_SPEC U4.56.01 after reading the cross-spectral matrix from an external file. NATURE= l_nat List of arguments of text type defining the nature of the excitation at each of the application nodes. The admissible arguments are ’FORCE’ or ’MOMENT’. ANGLE= l_theta List of the angles defining the directions of the force and moment vectors at each of the application nodes (see the diagram). The force vector is directed in the plane P orthogonal to the neutral fibre. In this plane, the azimuth \theta gives the direction of the vector. The angles must be given in degrees . / GROUP_NO= l_gno List of the groups containing the nodes of application of the excitation. Note The cross-spectral matrix has as its dimension the number of point forces and moments applied. The diagonal terms of this matrix characterise the autospectra of these excitations. The lists defining the application nodes, the nature and the direction of the imposed excitations must therefore be ordered in accordance with the structure of the cross-spectral matrix of excitations. / GRAPPE_2= ’ASC_CEN’ ou ’ASC_EXC’ ou ’DES_CEN’ ou ’DES_EXC’ Four possible choices corresponding to the various experimental configurations for which the GRAPPE2 excitation was identified: - AScending flow, CENtred control rod, - AScending flow, EXCentred control rod, - DEScending flow, CENtred control rod, - DEScending flow, EXCentred control rod. The GRAPPE2 excitation is characterised by a point force and a point moment applied at one and the same node, in a homogeneous manner in the two directions orthogonal to the axis of the slender structure. RHO_FLUI= rho_f Mass density of the fluid surrounding the structure. GROUP_NO= gno Group containing the node of application of the GRAPPE2 excitation. Note: When a predefined GRAPPE2 spectrum is used, the list of nodes expected under the operand GROUP_NO is reduced to a single element (a single application node). ♦ CARA_ELEM= cara Concept of type cara_elem produced by the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01; it defines the geometric characteristics assigned to the elements of the structure. The geometric characteristics are necessary for the estimation of the hydraulic diameter. In addition, the concept of type cara_elem provides the information relating to the orientations of the elements. ♦ MODELE= modele Concept of type modele produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01; it defines the types of elements assigned to the mesh cells of the structure. 4 Bibliography 1. u4.50.01 Keyword SOLVEUR u4.50.01 Keyword SOLVEUR 1 Purpose The factor keyword SOLVEUR is common to all the commands which solve systems of linear equations (STAT_NON_LINE, CALC_MODES, ...). To solve these systems of equations, particular algorithms called “linear solvers” are used. The keyword SOLVEUR makes it possible to choose the linear solver to be used from among two categories: the direct solvers and the iterative solvers. Among the direct solvers, one has the classical “Gauss” algorithm (METHODE='LDLT'), a multifrontal factorisation ('MULT_FRONT') and the MUMPS library ('MUMPS'). For the iterative solvers, it is possible to call a conjugate gradient ('GCPC') or certain algorithms of the PETSc library ('PETSC'). Only MULT_FRONT, MUMPS and PETSC are parallelised . The first in shared memory (OpenMP), the other two mainly in distributed memory (MPI). Their parallel schemes can even be chained (PETSc + MUMPS as a preconditioner) or take advantage of a second level of parallelism (OpenMP in MUMPS and the BLAS library). On the other hand, whatever their level of parallelism, all the solvers remain compatible with a parallel processing of the elementary analyses and of the assemblies. Furthermore, only the three direct solvers are compatible with the modal analysis, the buckling studies and certain time-step refinement procedures in non-linear analysis. For further details and advice on the use of the linear solvers one may consult the specific user's guides U2.08.03/[U2.08.06]. 2 Syntax ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "MULT_FRONT", / "LDLT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "GCPC", / "PETSC", #
