Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), 3 Operands 3.1 Operand METHODE This keyword makes it possible to choose the method for solving the linear systems: | #Direct solvers | | | --- | --- | | /'MULT_FRONT' | Direct solver of multifrontal type (without pivoting during the factorisation). This method is parallelised in shared memory (OpenMP) and can be executed on several processors ( via the Astk interface, menu Options / Launching options / ncpus). | | | | | /'LDLT' | Direct solver with Crout factorisation by blocks (without pivoting). This solver is paged, so it can run with little memory. | | | | | /'MUMPS' [ DEFAUT ] | Direct solver of multifrontal type with pivoting. This solver calls the MUMPS library developed by CERFACS/CNRS/ENS Lyon/INPT/INRIA/University of Bordeaux. It makes it possible to treat models leading to non-positive-definite matrices (apart from the boundary conditions). For example, the ‘mixed’ elements having degrees of freedom of ‘Lagrange’ type (incompressible elements, etc.). This method is parallelised mainly in distributed memory (MPI) but some of its steps can also benefit from shared-memory parallelism (OpenMP). It can be executed on several cores, themselves possibly distributed over several nodes. MUMPS is supplied with external 64-bit renumberers. This makes it possible to extend the scope of use of code_aster to very large finite-element models (> 107 degrees of freedom). Note, however, that solving the linear systems associated with these models requires large computing resources and the activation of the various levels of parallelism or even one of the acceleration options. | | #Iterative solvers | | | /'GCPC' | Iterative solver of conjugate-gradient type with preconditioning by an incomplete factorisation to k levels or else a complete factorisation in single precision. | | | | | /'PETSC' | Iterative solvers from the PETSc library ( Argonne National Laboratory ) with various preconditioners. This method is parallelised in distributed memory (MPI) and can be executed on several processors. Warning: the solvers PETSC and MUMPS being incompatible in sequential mode, PETSC is not available in the sequential versions of code_aster. To use PETSC, one must therefore launch a parallel version of code_aster (even if only one processor is requested). | | | | | | | Advice: The default method is MUMPS . It makes it possible, at the same time, to take full advantage of the gains in time and memory provided by parallelism , and to solve numerically difficult problems (X-FEM, incompressibility, THM...). To solve more efficiently a problem of large size (> 106 degrees of freedom), one may resort to the ‘low-rank’ compressions of MUMPS (cf. keywords ACCELERATION/LOW_RANK_SEUIL) or, if the functional scope allows it, to the iterative solvers PETSC or GCPC. For further details and advice on the use of the linear solvers one may consult the specific user's guides U2.08.03 and U2.08.06. 3.2 Parameters common to several solvers ◊ NPREC = / nprec / 8 [DEFAUT] ◊ STOP_SINGULIER = / 'OUI' [DEFAUT] / 'NON' These two parameters are common to all the direct linear solvers (LDLT, MULT_FRONT, MUMPS). They are used to control the course of the numerical factorisation and the quality of the solution of the linear system. The numerical factorisation of a matrix can fail in two situations: a problem in constructing the factorised matrix (a structurally or numerically singular matrix) and the numerical detection of a singularity (unstable solution of the linear system). The keywords NPREC and STOP_SINGULIER make it possible to set the singularity-detection threshold and the behaviour to adopt in the event of failure during the factorisation. nprec is used to calibrate the singularity-detection process for the matrix of the system to be solved. With LDLT and MULT_FRONT, the absolute value of nprec is taken; with MUMPS, nprec is taken because its sign matters: if \text{nprec} \text{nprec} , the matrix is considered to be singular. If the user has indicated: | STOP_SINGULIER='OUI' | The code then stops in error. | | --- | --- | | STOP_SINGULIER='NON' | Execution continues after an ALARME has been issued. The quality of the solution is then not guaranteed. This setting is not recommended. In non-linear analysis, it is not necessarily too detrimental to the quality of the results because they are “corrected” by the Newton process. | Pour MUMPS: If, for at least one pivot, the infinity norm of the row (or of the column) is lower than the threshold {10}^{-\text{nprec}} then the matrix is considered to be singular. Some aspects of the two types of singularity-detection criterion are compared in the documentation U2.08.03. Notes: - Any significant loss of significant digits during a factorisation is an indicator of an ill-posed problem. Several causes are possible (non-exhaustive list): insufficient restraint boundary conditions on the structure, redundant linear relations, very heterogeneous numerical data (penalty terms that are too large)... - For LDLT and MULT_FRONT , singularity detection is performed all the time because it is very inexpensive. - As regards MUMPS , a mechanism makes it possible to check the quality of the solution by another means ( RESI_RELA ). The freedom to disable this criterion has therefore been left (by choosing a negative nprec ). - By default, with the direct solver MUMPS , there is therefore a double check on the quality of the solution: in linear analysis, RESI_RELA and NPREC ; in non-linear analysis, the Newton criterion and NPREC . It is possible to switch them off, but this is not recommended without a valid reason. ◊ ELIM_LAGR = 'NON'/'OUI'/'LAGR2' Ce mot clé permet d'éliminer les équations de Lagrange correspondant aux conditions cinématiques dualisées. Par défaut (sauf pour MUMPS), ces équations ne sont pas éliminées ('NON'). La technique d'élimination utilisée pour ELIM_LAGR='OUI' est décrite dans [:ref: R3.03.05 ]. Pour utiliser ELIM_LAGR='OUI' sur plusieurs processeurs, il est impératif d'avoir au préalable choisi DISTRIBUTION='CENTRALISE'dans AFFE_MODELE.La phase d'élimination est alors répliquée sur tous les processeurs (sans entraîner de gain en temps). La résolution du système linéaire résultant s'effectue ensuite en parallèle sur tous les processeurs (cette fois avec un gain en temps, qui dépend du solveur linéaire choisi). On ne peut pas utiliser ELIM_LAGR='OUI' avec le solveur linéaire direct 'MULT_FRONT'. Dans le cas du solveur MUMPS, une troisième valeur est possible: 'LAGR2'. L'objectif est alors de supprimer la deuxième équation de Lagrange, mais de conserver la première. La valeur 'LAGR2' est le défaut pour le solveur MUMPS. This parameter may be temporarily disabled by the code so as not to distort the computation of the determinant of the matrix. This feature is mainly required by the operators CALC_MODES with OPTION among ['PROCHE','AJUSTE','SEPARE'] and INFO_MODE. The user is then warned of this automatic change of setting via a dedicated message (only with INFO=2). 3 3.3 METHODE='MULT_FRONT' Scope of use: > Robust solver, not recommended however for modellings requiring pivoting (mixed finite elements, incompressible…), for generalised matrices with links (operators ASSE_ELEM/MATR_SSD…) as well as on large finite-element models (> 106 degrees of freedom). In these situations, rather use the MUMPS method (cf. §3.5) or, in non-linear analysis, PETSC + PRE_COND='LDLT_SP' (cf. § 3.7). ◊ RENUM = This argument makes it possible to number the nodes of the model in order to reduce the size of the factorised matrix (and therefore the CPU and memory consumption of the solution): | /'METIS' [ DEFAUT ] | Numbering method based on a nested dissection. The external product of the same name is used; it is a worldwide standard in the field. It is, in general, the most efficient method (in CPU time and in memory). | | --- | --- | | /'MD' | (‘Minimum Degree’) this numbering of the nodes minimises the fill-in of the matrix during its factorisation. | | /'MDA' | (‘Approximate Minimum Degree’) this numbering is in principle less optimal than 'MD' as regards fill-in but it is cheaper to compute. It is nevertheless preferable to 'MD' for large models ( \ge 50000 degrees of freedom). | Note: - In the case of generalised matrices 1 comprising link constraints, MULT_FRONT does not apply any renumbering. This strategy is not detrimental because these matrices are often nearly full and of small size. The choice of renumberer made by the user is therefore ignored. An information message reports this situation in the message file. 3.4 METHODE='LDLT' Scope of use: > Universal solver but only on small finite-element models ( Universal solver, efficient and robust. To be used on all types of problem and in particular large finite-element models (>106 degrees of freedom), or even very large models (>107 degrees of freedom). Especially if they mix modellings, types of finite element, or if the associated linear systems require pivoting (mixed finite elements, incompressible, X-FEM modelling, dualised boundary condition, links between mesh-cell groups, etc.). In non-linear analysis, it is often preferable to use MUMPS as a preconditioner, via the option PETSC + PRE_COND='LDLT_SP'/'LDLT_DP' (cf. §3.7). The MUMPS solver, currently developed by CERFACS/CNRS/ENS Lyon/INPT/INRIA/University of Bordeaux, is a direct solver of parallelised multifrontal type (in MPI and in OpenMP). It is robust because it makes it possible to pivot the rows and columns of the matrix during the numerical factorisation. Only the public version of MUMPS 5.5.1 is accepted in the coupling with code_aster . Furthermore, their restricted-access versions MUMPS v5.5.5 consortium are also accepted but only for EDF use. They provide access, ahead of the public version, to exploratory features. All are now compiled with external 64-bit renumberers ((PAR)METIS, (PT)SCOTCH and PORD), which allows MUMPS, by activating them (cf. keyword RENUM), to treat very large finite-element models (millions of mesh cells). Note, however, that solving the linear systems associated with these models requires large computing resources and the activation of the various levels of parallelism or even one of the acceleration options (cf. keyword ACCELERATION). For further information one may consult §4 of U2.08.03 and U2.08.06. 3.5.1 Functional parameters ◊ TYPE_RESOL = This keyword makes it possible to choose the type of MUMPS solution: | /'NONSYM' | Must be chosen for non-symmetric matrices. | | --- | --- | | /'SYMGEN' | Must be chosen for symmetric non-positive-definite matrices. This is the most general case in code_aster because of the dualisation of the boundary conditions by Lagrange multipliers. | | /'SYMDEF' | May be chosen for symmetric positive-definite matrices. There is no pivoting. The algorithm is faster and less costly in memory. | | /'AUTO' [ DEFAUT ] | The code will choose 'NONSYM' for non-symmetric matrices and 'SYMGEN' for symmetric matrices. | It is not forbidden to choose 'NONSYM' for a symmetric matrix. This will probably double the computing cost but this option gives MUMPS more algorithmic possibilities (pivoting, scaling …). Conversely , it can be worthwhile, in non-linear analysis, to symmetrise one's non-symmetric problem (cf. U4.51.03, keyword MATR_RIGI_SYME). It is the same kind of device as for the relaxation parameters FILTRAGE_MATRICE and MIXER_PRECISION. ◊ RESI_RELA = / resi / 1.d-6 [DEFAUT] en linéaire / -1.d0 [DEFAUT] en non linéaire et en calcul modal. Ce paramètre est désactivé par une valeur négative. Il est appelable dans les opérateurs qui peuvent avoir besoin de contrôler la qualité d'une résolution complète de système linéaire (donc pas les opérateurs éclatés effectuant juste des factorisations ; Par exemple FACTORISER et INFO_MODE). By specifying a strictly positive value for this keyword (for example {10}^{-6} ), the user indicates that he or she wishes to test the validity of the solution of each linear system solved by MUMPS (relative to the exact solution). This cautious approach is recommended when the solution is not itself corrected by another algorithmic process (Newton algorithm, singularity detection…), in short in the linear operators THER_LINEAIRE and MECA_STATIQUE. In non-linear analysis or in modal analysis, the singularity-detection criterion and the correction of the enclosing algorithm (Newton or modal solver) are sufficient safeguards. One can therefore switch off this checking process (this is what is done by default via the value -1), all the more so as it has a non-negligible cost in time and as this cost is greater (in relative terms) in parallel and/or with memory management that offloads large objects to disk (cf. keyword GESTION_MEMOIRE). It is an additional feature that the other direct solvers of code_aster do not offer. If the relative error (based on the condition numbers and the backward errors of the linear system treated) on the solution estimated by MUMPS is greater than resi, the code stops in ERREUR_FATALE, stating the nature of the problem and the values concerned. Activating this keyword also initiates an iterative refinement process (unless POSTTRAITEMENTS='SANS') whose objective is to improve the solution obtained. This post-processing has a particular setting (keyword POSTTRAITEMENTS). It is the solution resulting from this iterative improvement process that is tested by RESI_RELA. Note: - In the particular case where POSTTRAITEMENTS='MINI' and RESI_RELA>0, the quality estimate made by MUMPS is only partial (based solely on the backward errors) and therefore code_aster does not stop the analysis if this value is greater than resi. This combination of keywords is of interest only with INFO=2 in order to assess the qualities of the solutions. 3.5.2 Relaxation parameters ◊ FILTRAGE_MATRICE = / filtma / -1.d0 [DEFAUT] ◊ MIXER_PRECISION = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT] These parameters are reserved for quasi-static non-linear analysis. A negative value of filtma disables the feature. These features make it possible to “relax” the solutions carried out with MUMPS in order to gain in performance. The idea is simple. In non-linear analysis, the computation of the tangent matrix may be affected by error. This will probably slow down the Newton process (in number of iterations), but if handling this approximate matrix is less costly, one can globally gain in time (fewer floating-point operations), in memory consumption (RAM or even disk if OOC is activated) and in bandwidth (cache effect, volume of I/O). Thus, activating the feature FILTRAGE_MATRICE, with a value of filtma>0, leads code_aster to supply MUMPS only with the matrix terms satisfying ∣{\mathrm{K}}_{ij}∣>\mathrm{filtma}\cdot \left(∣{\mathrm{K}}_{ii}∣+∣{\mathrm{K}}_{jj}∣\right) The filter is therefore based on a threshold relative to the absolute values of the corresponding diagonal terms. By initialising MIXER_PRECISION to 'OUI', one uses the single-precision version of MUMPS while supplying it with a double-precision Aster matrix (possibly filtered via FILTRAGE_MATRICE). Hence potentially gains in memory (often 50%) and in time at the solution stage. However, this device is really worthwhile only if the tangent matrix is well conditioned ( \eta \left(\mathrm{K}\right) 0 (useful only for assessment). | Notes: - This process mainly consumes forward and backward substitutions, whose extra cost in time is still reasonable in sequential In-Core. On the other hand, it can be significant in Out-Of-Core and in parallel, or even of little use in non-linear analysis (the Newton algorithm corrects). - To limit any counter-productive drift, with the values ' AUTO ' and ' FORCE ' the iterative refinement procedure is capped internally in MUMPS: as soon as an iteration does not provide a gain of at least a factor of 5, the process stops. The number of iterations generally observed (by setting INFO=2 ) is 1 or 2. - On certain ill-conditioned test cases (for example perf001e), forcing this process made it possible to reach the desired accuracy (via the values ' FORCE ' or ' MINI' ). 3.5.4 Parameters for memory management To gain RAM without changing linear solver (and modelling or computer platform), several strategies are available (and often combinable). They are listed here in order of importance. - At constant numerical accuracy and with gains in computing time: Parallelism (Options/mpi_ menu of Astk) coupled, or not, with the activation of the keyword MATR_DISTRIBUEE in distributed parallelism mode (default mode); Activation of the pre-processings (done by default, cf. PRETRAITEMENTS); Redistribution of the parallelism between the MPI level and the OpenMP level (cf. REDUCTION_MPI). - At constant numerical accuracy but with, potentially, losses in computing time: Explicit activation of the disk-offloading capabilities of MUMPS (cf. GESTION_MEMOIRE), Change of renumberer (cf. keyword RENUM seen previously). One must also take care to provide an additional space reserved for pivoting of reasonable size: keyword PCENT_PIVOT. Often the default values of these parameters (GESTION_MEMOIRE='AUTO', RENUM='AUTO' and PCENT_PIVOT=20) provide the best compromises for adapting this part of the setting to the situation. - By accepting a loss of accuracy within a non-linear process (e.g. STAT or DYNA_NON_LINE, CALC_MODES, ...): all the relaxation parameters linked to the solver (FILTRAGE_MATRICE, MIXER_PRECISION seen previously) or even those linked to the non-linear process proper (elastic tangent matrix, projection space in modal analysis...). - By no longer using MUMPS as a direct solver but as a preconditioner (cf. GCPC or PETSC with REAC_PRECOND='LDLT_SP/DP' cf. §3.6/3.7). For further information one may consult the documents U2.08.03 (User's guide of the linear solvers) and U2.08.06 (User's guide of parallelism). ◊ PCENT_PIVOT = / pcent [I] / 20% [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to choose a percentage of memory that MUMPS will reserve at the start of the analysis for pivoting. Indeed, in order to factorise an Aster matrix, it is often preferable to permute two of its rows and/or of its columns (cf. R6.02.03 §2.3.1). Now the data objects managing this pivoting are difficult to size a priori . This is why the tool asks the user for a prior and arbitrary estimate of this additional space. The default value is 20%. It corresponds to a reasonable number of pivotings which is sufficient for most Aster analyses. If for example MUMPS estimates at 100 the space necessary for a factorisation without pivoting, it will ultimately allocate 120 to manage the analysis with pivoting. A value exceeding 50% must remain exceptional. Subsequently, if the memory space required by the pivotings proves larger, the space allocated will be insufficient and the code will ask for this criterion to be increased. Two situations will then arise according to the type of memory management chosen ( via the keyword GESTION_MEMOIRE): - If it is a precise mode, 'IN-CORE' or 'OUT_OF_CORE', the analysis stops in ERREUR_FATALE and proposes various remedial solutions. - If it is the automatic mode, 'AUTO', the analysis will continue and try again to factorise with a doubled value of PCENT_PIVOT. Up to three attempts of this type will be made before, in the event of repeated failures, a stop in ERREUR_FATALE + proposal of various remedial solutions. Notes: - For small problems ( 100) is then not surprising. - Self-learning process: if, in the process described previously, one is led to modify automatically the value of PCENT_PIVOT, it is this new value which is used until the end of the operator. It is assumed that the numerical difficulty will not decrease and this pivoting value is therefore kept so as not to waste any more time on aborted factorisation attempts. - In 'AUTO' mode, together with the doubling of the additional pivoting space, one may also be led to switch automatically to MUMPS Out-Of-Core memory management (as if one had explicitly set GESTION_MEMOIRE='OUT_OF_CORE'). This occurs according to certain MUMPS return codes or at the third (and last) attempt. ◊ GESTION_MEMOIRE= This keyword makes it possible to choose the memory-management mode of the external product MUMPS, or even, as a last resort, of certain objects managed directly by code_aster . The first two modes are “without a safety net”: no correction of the setting will be made “on the fly” in the event of a problem. Unlike the 3rd mode, the automatic mode, which will do everything (within certain limits!) so that the analysis does not fail for reasons of memory space. In particular, according to the memory that it manages to free elsewhere, it will play on the In-Core and Out-Of-Core modes of MUMPS or even on the space required for its pivoting (cf. keyword PCENT_PIVOT). | /'IN_CORE' | Speed of the analysis is favoured as much as possible. This is the option which requires the most memory, because here MUMPS is allowed to keep in RAM all the objects it needs. | | --- | --- | | /'OUT_OF_CORE' | Savings in memory consumption are favoured as much as possible. Activating Out-Of-Core helps to reduce the RAM required per processor, but it can slow down the analysis (cost of the RAM/disk I/O). This extra cost can be significant when many forward and backward substitutions are performed (e.g. non-linear analysis with many time steps or Newton iterations, search for many eigenmodes in a modal analysis...). Because in these algorithmic steps, as much time is spent handling the data (in RAM) as fetching them (from disk). This is all the more true when the disk is shared by several computing cores. For this reason, the In-Core mode is favoured as much as possible (especially in parallel). In 'EVAL' mode, the pre-estimates of the memory consumptions are much faster and less costly in memory than the complete analysis. They can make it possible to calibrate one's study on a local machine or on an interactive node of a centralised machine before launching the study proper in batch mode. Anecdotally, this mode can also be used to test roughly the data setup and/or the executable used. If everything works up to this evaluation, that is rather a good sign for the subsequent analysis! In 'AUTO' mode, MUMPS is allowed to “spread out in RAM” in order to gain time and to limit the late memory needs linked to pivoting. MUMPS will thus be able to take all the memory it deems necessary, even possibly beyond its initial estimates. This allows it to cope with possible future needs. To this end, code_aster supplies it with an estimate of the available RAM. These pre-allocations often make it possible to no longer have to adjust, often “by rule of thumb”, the parameter 'PCENT_PIVOT'. Hence a definite saving of time in setting up the studies. Furthermore, in 'AUTO' mode, a code_aster + MUMPS analysis thus really takes advantage of all the available memory: the Vmpeak is close to the figure set in Astk. On the other hand, in the other two modes ('IN_CORE' and 'OUT_OF_CORE'), MUMPS is not allowed to “spread out” in RAM. It pre-allocates no additional space beyond its initial memory estimates. This makes it possible to keep a safe mode of operation in the event of a poor evaluation of the available memory 4 . Another mechanism also makes it possible to remedy this kind of inconvenience: if MUMPS tries to allocate an object of size greater than the memory space actually available, a new factorisation is attempted, no longer allowing it to pre-allocate additional space. This corrective strategy, similar to that used for the parameter PCENT_PIVOT, is activated only with the 'AUTO' mode. Notes: - In the standard modes ('IN_CORE' and 'OUT_OF_CORE') code_aster offloads to disk the largest objects 5 linked to the linear system. This is in order to leave MUMPS a maximum of room in RAM. If subsequently MUMPS does not have enough room to allocate its data, an alarm is issued and the analysis continues. Depending on the cases, the analysis may finish without mishap but at the price of a large extra cost in time (system swap) or stop in ERREUR_FATALE. The user is then offered various alternatives, including the setting in 'AUTO' mode. - In 'AUTO' mode, if this freed space is insufficient to allow MUMPS to operate fully in In-Core, the whole remainder of unloadable JEVEUX objects is offloaded to disk. Then, according to the memory space thus freed, the In-Core or Out-Of-Core mode of MUMPS is activated or one stops in ERREUR_FATALE (+ advice). - The massive offloading of JEVEUX objects mentioned previously can, in exceptional cases, greatly slow down the execution. This can happen for example in the event of congestion of the disk accesses in parallel mode or when a great deal of data is offloaded (fields at the various time steps, projected fields...). The solution may then be to occupy fewer processors per node, to consume less memory (increase the number of processors, Out-Of-Core mode..) or to split one's analysis into several steps. - In 'EVAL' mode, the evaluation and then the stop are carried out at the first matrix factorisation via MUMPS. That is, for example, in the prediction phase for STAT_NON_LINE, or in the Sturm test for CALC_MODES. This is often sufficient to have a good order of magnitude of the memory requirements. To possibly postpone this evaluation, one must split one's analysis and use another linear solver (for example 'MULT_FRONT') for the operators that one wishes to preserve. ◊ MATR_DISTRIBUEE = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT] This parameter is for the moment limited to the operators MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE and it is active only in distributed parallel mode (AFFE_MODELE/PARTITION/PARALLELISME!='CENTRALISE'). By activating this keyword, the storage of the assembled matrix is done in a distributed manner on all the processors (values belonging to the other processors, which are useless, are no longer stored). This makes it possible to save memory in parallel with no extra cost in time, and no loss of accuracy (this keyword has no influence in sequential mode or in centralised parallel mode). 3.5.5 Parameters for reducing the computing time To reduce the computing time without changing linear solver (and modelling or computer platform), several strategies are available (and combinable). They are listed here in order of importance. - At constant numerical accuracy: - MPI and/or OpenMP parallelism or, possibly, an optimised combination of the two (cf. keyword REDUCTION_MPI); - activation of various accelerations and/or compressions (cf. keyword ACCELERATION); - change of renumberer (keyword RENUM seen previously; often the choice made by default is optimal); - activation of the pre-processings (done by default, keyword PRETRAITEMENTS); - the use of MUMPS, not as a direct solver but as a preconditioner. Can be very efficient, especially in non-linear analysis, with the reuse over several Newton steps of the same preconditioner (cf. PETSC or GCPC with PRE_COND='LDLT_SP/DP' §3.6/3.7) - By accepting a loss of accuracy, which is often not detrimental (the accuracy is sufficient) or is compensated by an enclosing non-linear process (e.g. STAT or DYNA_NON_LINE, CALC_MODES...): - for large-size problems ( N at least > 2.106 degrees of freedom), activation of the low-rank compressions (cf. keywords ACCELERATION/LOW_RANK_SEUIL below); - the relaxation parameters linked to the solver (FILTRAGE_MATRICE, MIXER_PRECISION seen previously) or even those linked to the non-linear process proper (elastic tangent matrix, projection space in modal analysis...); - the reduction of the post-processings (keyword POSTTRAITEMENTS). These keywords define the type of acceleration implemented in order to reduce the computing time. These accelerations can significantly reduce the computing time of large studies, and this without restriction of the scope of use and with little or no impact on the accuracy, the robustness and the overall behaviour of the simulation. Their availability depends on the versions of MUMPS coupled with code_aster. They are especially worthwhile on large-size problems (N at least > 2.10 6 degrees of freedom). The gains observed on a few code_aster studies vary from 20% to 80%. They increase with the size of the problem and with its massive character, and they are complementary to those provided by parallelism and by the renumberer. The various values of the parameter ACCELERATION are: - The value 'AUTO' (taken by default) chooses the best setting according to the version of MUMPS available, the case treated and the computing configuration. For the public version ‘AUTO’=’FR’ and, for the consortium version, ‘AUTO’=’FR+’ (except in modal analysis where AUTO=’FR’). - The value 'FR' allows a standard MUMPS solution (known as 'Full-Rank') to be implemented, that is to say without 'low-rank' compression and without “aggressive optimisations” of the options internal to MUMPS. - The value 'FR+' allows a solution without 'low-rank' compression to be implemented but activating “aggressive optimisations” of options internal to MUMPS. In particular one activates the analysis by blocks, which appreciably accelerates this first, often costly, step of MUMPS. - The value 'FR++ ' adds to ‘ FR+ ' particular options of MUMPS which accelerate the 2nd and 3rd steps of MUMPS (numerical factorisation and forward and backward substitutions): extended OpenMP scope, relaxed pivoting, accelerated symbolic factorisation… However, in particular cases, these aggressive options can disturb singularity detection (increase the value of NPREC) or the memory estimates (set GESTION_MEMOIRE='IN_CORE'/'OUT_OF_CORE'). - The value 'LR' activates a MUMPS solution with 'Low-Rank' compression. The compression rate is fixed by the parameter supplied by the keyword LOW_RANK_SEUIL. Roughly speaking , the larger this figure is (relative to the default precision, 10-15), for example 10-12 or 10-9, the greater the compression will be and therefore the more interesting the gains in performance can be. From a certain compression threshold (therefore “of approximation”), it is advisable to activate, in addition, the iterative refinement procedure (for example via POSTTRAITEMENTS='MINI'). This makes it possible to recover, often at a low extra cost, an error on the solution close to that which would have been obtained with the standard analysis, 'FR'. - The values 'LR+'/ 'LR++' activate the same option as previously ('LR') but adding the “aggressive optimisations” of 'FR++'. If the compression rate is positive (LOW_RANK_SEUIL >0), the standard BLR compression algorithm of MUMPS is used (known as ‘UFSC’); otherwise, it is its exploratory version (known as ‘UCFS’), potentially faster, because the compression is done earlier in the algorithmic process of MUMPS, but therefore less numerically stable. Depending on the options, one then rather targets the computing-time criterion or the memory consumption. - The value ' L R+' favours the gain in time. - The value ' L R+ + ' favours the gain in memory (additional compressions and use of mixed precisions). This value is reduced to 100 if the preconditioner LDLT_SP is used. ◊ RESI_RELA = / resi / 10-6 [DEFAUT] Convergence criterion of the algorithm. It is a relative criterion on the preconditioned residual: \frac{\parallel {M}^{-1}.{\text{r}}_{m}\parallel }{\parallel {M}^{-1}.\text{f}\parallel }\le \mathit{resi} {M}^{-1} is the preconditioner {\text{r}}_{m} is the residual at iteration m \text{f} is the right-hand side and the norm \parallel \parallel is the usual Euclidean norm. Notes: 1. The convergence criterion for PETSC is evaluated differently from GCPC; 2. When the preconditioner is of poor quality (for example because of a poor conditioning of the problem), the convergence criterion used by PETSC can give rise to poor solutions; this is why, in the linear analysis operators, an additional check on the non-preconditioned residual is carried out. The tolerance chosen for this additional criterion is \sqrt{\mathit{resi}} ; 3. The algorithm 'GCR' relies on right preconditioning and therefore checks the convergence criterion in the non-preconditioned norm. 4. When the preconditioner LDLT_INC is used, the matrix is systematically renumbered using the Reverse-Cuthill-Mackee algorithm. The user cannot modify this choice. 5. The preconditioner LDLT_INC is incompatible with MATR_DISTRIBUEE='OUI'. 3.7.1 Keywords specific to the preconditioner FIELDSPLIT ◊ NOM_CMP List of the components of the fields which appear in the modelling, for example NOM_CMP=('DX','DY','DZ','PRES') for a mixed displacement-and-pressure modelling for an incompressible elasticity problem. ◊ PARTITION_CMP The way in which the components of the fields will be grouped. In the example NOM_CMP=('DX','DY','DZ','PRES'), one uses PARTITION_CMP=(3,1), which means that the three displacement components and the pressure component will be treated separately. ◊ OPTION_PETSC Character string which defines the block preconditioner. This string must be on a single line (without a line break). 3.7.2 Keywords specific to the preconditioner HPDDM ◊ TYPE_RESOL = This keyword makes it possible to choose the type of construction and solution of the coarse problem: | /'GENEO' | is based on the GENEO approach | | --- | --- | | /'HARMO' | is based on the harmonic overlap approach | | /'AUTO' [ DEFAUT ] | The code will choose 'HARMO' for non-symmetric matrices and 'GENEO' for symmetric matrices. | ◊ NB_MODE = / nbmode / 30 [DEFAUT] Number of modes to be computed and used to build the coarse problem per subdomain. ◊ SEUIL = / seuil / 0.0 [DEFAUT] The threshold makes it possible not to take into account the modes whose frequency is smaller than it. 3.7.3 Keywords specific to the preconditioner UTILISATEUR ◊ KSP_UTIL Function written by the user which describes the solution algorithm. It is written in Python and uses the PETSc interface for this language, called petsc4py. This is an advanced use of PETSc, to be reserved exclusively for the expert, for research purposes. 3.7.4 Keyword OPTION_PETSC Outre définir précisément le préconditionneur FIELDSPLIT (comme évoqué ci-dessus), le mot-clé OPTION_PETSC permet également de passer à PETSc des options supplémentaires, non-prises en charge par l’interface décrite ici. Cette librairie est en effet conçue pour être hautement configurable à l’exécution ce que permet de réaliser ce mot-clé. Il s’agit d’une utilisation avancée de PETSc, à réserver exclusivement au fin connaisseur à fin de recherche. ◊ OPTION_PETSC Character string which makes it possible to pass a set of additional options to PETSc It is important to note that the additional options passed to PETSc are kept from its initialisation until its closure, generally at the execution of the command FIN(). So if a user passes additional options in STAT_NON_LINE, they will be used for all the subsequent solutions even with other solution operators such as DYNA_VIBRA. To work around this, it is possible to stop PETSc, which has the effect of resetting all the options. This is done using the commands: from code_aster import LinearAlgebra # import of the LinearAlgebra module LinearAlgebra.petscInitialize() # call to the method which initialises PETSc. It > # can take as arguments new > # options LinearAlgebra.petscFinalize() # call to the method which closes PETSc and resets > # the options Generated by the operator NUME_DDL_GENE. The blocks of factorised matrices (real or complex) managed by the current processor. The index vectors (integers) describing these blocks remain in RAM. The MUMPS estimates may be slightly overestimated. They summarise the figures required for a “stand-alone” use of the MUMPS product on the problem coming from code_aster. These estimates therefore include not only the objects that MUMPS will need in order to build its factorised matrix, but also the prior data-storage objects (matrix, RHS) and a flat 30 MB for the MUMPS executable. This can happen on certain platforms (e.g. clpaster-Rocks). Matrix (MATR_ASSE), description of the unknowns (NUME_DDL)... Parameter mpi_nbcpu of the launching tool. Resp. ncpus. This setting is normally determined automatically by the launching tool.

u4.51.01 Operator MECA_STATIQUE u4.51.01 Operator MECA_STATIQUE 1 Purpose Solve a linear static mechanical problem. This operator makes it possible to solve either: - a linear static mechanical problem with superposition of different boundary conditions and different loadings, - a thermo-mechanical analysis for a given list of time instants. - in this case the mechanical characteristics of the materials may depend on the temperature: the concept of type cham_mater must then be defined from functions (cf. operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 operand ELAS_FO), - the expansion loading can be determined only if the expansion coefficient and the reference temperature have been defined (cf. operators DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 and AFFE_MATERIAU U4.43.03). The concept produced by this operator is of type evol_elas containing one or more displacement fields at the various analysis time instants. 2 Syntax evol_elas = MECA_STATIQUE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ & RESULTAT = evol_elas, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ | CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, | CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, # Si: exists("CARA_ELEM") ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_meca / char_meca, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), # Si: not exists("CARA_ELEM") ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_meca / char_meca, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), ◆ / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, # Si: exists("LIST_INST") ◇ INST_INIT = float, ◇ INST_FIN = float, ◇ OPTION = / "SANS", / "SIEF_ELGA" (par défaut), ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "GCPC", / "LDLT", / "MULT_FRONT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "PETSC", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "METIS", / "PARMETIS", / "PORD", / "PTSCOTCH", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "LAGR2" (par défaut), / "NON", / "OUI", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "NONSYM", / "SYMDEF", / "SYMGEN", ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FR", / "FR+", / "FR++", / "LR", / "LR+", / "LR++", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", / "SANS", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 35), ◇ REDUCTION_MPI = int (défaut: 0), ◇ NB_RHS = int (défaut: 1), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "EVAL", / "IN_CORE", / "OUT_OF_CORE", ◇ MATR_DISTRIBUEE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'GCPC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ PRE_COND = / "LDLT_DP", / "LDLT_INC" (par défaut), / "LDLT_SP", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int (défaut: 0), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int (défaut: 0), # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "IN_CORE", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'PETSC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ MATR_DISTRIBUEE = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ ALGORITHME = / "CG", / "CR", / "FGMRES" (par défaut), / "GCR", / "GMRES", / "GMRES_LMP", ◇ OPTION_PETSC = text (défaut: ""), ◇ PRE_COND = / "BLOC_LAGR", / "BOOMER", / "FIELDSPLIT", / "GAMG", / "HPDDM", / "JACOBI", / "LDLT_DP", / "LDLT_INC", / "LDLT_SP" (par défaut), / "ML", / "SANS", / "SOR", / "UTILISATEUR", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int (défaut: 0), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int (défaut: 0), ◇ REMPLISSAGE = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "IN_CORE", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = int, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "RCMK", / "SANS" (par défaut), ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM The arguments making it possible to compute the stiffness matrix (and the right-hand side) are supplied: ♦ MODELE= mo, Name of the model whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. ♦ CHAM_MATER= chmat, Name of the material field. ◊ CARA_ELEM= carac, Name of the characteristics of the structural elements (beam, shell, discrete elements, ...) if they are used in the model. 3.2 Keyword EXCIT The boundary conditions and the loadings are defined here. ◊ EXCIT= This factor keyword makes it possible to define several concepts of type load, one per occurrence; the solution is computed by superposing the effects of the various applied loads. 3.2.1 Operands CHARGE / FONC_MULT ♦ CHARGE= char, Name of a concept of type char_meca produced by AFFE_CHAR_MECA or AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01 from the model mo. One may also give the name of a “kinematic load” (type char_cine_meca), the result of the operators AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F U4.44.03. ◊ FONC_MULT= fmult, Name of a concept of type fonction (or formula) which makes it possible to define, for each analysis time instant, a multiplying coefficient applied to the load char. fmult is a function of time: by default it is a constant function equal to 1. 3.3 Keywords INST / LIST_INST ◊ / INST= tps, Keyword used to carry out the analysis at a single time instant tps with the temperature corresponding to that time instant. / LIST_INST= litps, ◊ INST_FIN= tf, The list litps produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01 defines the time instants for which the analysis of a thermo-mechanical evolution is requested. The keyword INST_FIN makes it possible to compute only the time instants earlier than or equal to tf. This keyword (INST_FIN), combined with the keyword "RESULTAT" (re-entrant command), makes it possible to split a long thermo-mechanical transient. One will, for example, write: resu = MECA_STATIQUE (... LIST_INST = linst, INST_FIN = 10., ...) MECA_STATIQUE (RESULTAT = resu, LIST_INST = linst, INST_FIN = 20., ...) MECA_STATIQUE (RESULTAT = resu, LIST_INST = linst, INST_FIN = 30., …) 3.4 Keyword RESULTAT In the case where one wishes to continue an analysis that has already been run, RESULTAT indicates which object is enriched. In this case, the command simply does not recompute the previous time instants already computed. 3.5 Factor keyword SOLVEUR See U4.50.01. 3.6 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION = / 'SANS' / 'SIEF_ELGA' By default the command MECA_STATIQUE computes the stresses at the Gauss points (or the generalised forces for the structural elements). The other post-processing options will be computed a posteriori by the command CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04. If the user indicates OPTION = 'SANS', these stresses will not be computed and the data structure produced will be less bulky. 3.7 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= 1, Prints the main characteristics of the linear systems to be solved: number of unknowns, size of the matrix. 3.8 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titr, Title that one wishes to give to the result U4.03.01. 4 Examples of analyses 4.1 Static analysis with superposition of 2 load cases mest1 = MECA_STATIQUE ( MODELE= mo, CHAM_MATER= chmat, CARA_ELEM= carac, EXCIT= ( _F( CHARGE= ch1 , FONC_MULT= COS ), _F( CHARGE= ch2 ),),) 4.2 Thermoelastic analysis at various time instants chmat = AFFE_MATERIAU ( ..., AFFE_VARC=_F(... EVOL=evoth ...) ); mest2 = MECA_STATIQUE ( MODELE= mo , CHAM_MATER= chmat , EXCIT= _F( CHARGE= bloq ), LIST_INST= litps ) 5 Note For certain studies in linear elasticity for which the stiffness characteristics of the structure are independent of the thermal history and the kinematic boundary conditions are independent of the other loads, the deformed shapes for several loading cases can be determined by using MACRO_ELAS_MULT U4.51.02.

u4.51.02 Macro-command MACRO_ELAS_MULT u4.51.02 Macro-command MACRO_ELAS_MULT 1 Purpose The role of the command is to compute linear static responses for different load cases or Fourier modes. It is assumed that the kinematic conditions (restraints of the structure) and the material characteristics are invariant for all the load cases, which makes it possible to have the same stiffness matrix. The data structure produced is of type mult_elas for the multiple load case or fourier_elas for the Fourier analyses. 2 Syntax / fourier_elas / mult_elas / nume_ddl = MACRO_ELAS_MULT( ◇ reuse = , ◇ RESULTAT = fourier_elas / mult_elas, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ NUME_DDL = co / nume_ddl, ◆ / CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL = char_meca, / LIAISON_DISCRET = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◆ CAS_CHARGE = _F( ◆ / NOM_CAS = text, / MODE_FOURIER = int, ◇ TYPE_MODE = / "ANTI", / "SYME" (par défaut), / "TOUS", ◆ / CHAR_MECA = char_meca, / VECT_ASSE = cham_no, ◇ OPTION = / "SANS", / "SIEF_ELGA" (par défaut), ◇ SOUS_TITRE = text, ), ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "LDLT", / "MULT_FRONT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "METIS", / "PARMETIS", / "PORD", / "PTSCOTCH", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "NONSYM", / "SYMDEF", / "SYMGEN", ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "LAGR2" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "EVAL", / "IN_CORE" (par défaut), / "OUT_OF_CORE", ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FR", / "FR+", / "LR", / "LR+", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", / "SANS", ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands MACRO_ELAS_MULT is a macro-command which calls elementary operators liable to create concepts temporarily on the global database; it is therefore possible that the file associated with the latter contains superfluous records marked as destroyed. To reduce the final size of the file, when one wishes to keep it, one may use the procedure FIN and the keyword RETASSAGE='OUI' in the command file. 3.1 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM The arguments making it possible to compute the stiffness matrix (and the right-hand sides) are supplied. ♦ MODELE = mo, Name of the model whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmat, Name of the material field. ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, Name of the characteristics of the structural elements (beam, shell, discrete elements, ...) if they are used in the model. 3.2 Operand NUME_DDL ◊ NUME_DDL = nu, Keyword used to name the numbering for later use or to use an existing numbering. If no name is supplied, a numbering is created temporarily for each call to MACRO_ELAS_MULT. 3.3 Operands CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL / LIAISON_DISCRET ♦ / CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL = lchmg, Keyword defining the mechanical boundary conditions restraining the structure. These conditions are the same for all the load cases. They are defined by AFFE_CHAR_MECA or AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01. / LIAISON_DISCRET= 'OUI', This keyword simply states that there are no mechanical or kinematic restraint conditions on the structure. 3.4 Keyword CAS_CHARGE Factor keyword making it possible to define a load case. For each occurrence of the factor keyword, a right-hand side is built (unless VECT_ASSE is used (in which case the right-hand side is already assembled)) and the linear system is solved. 3.4.1 Operand NOM_CAS ♦ NOM_CAS = moncas, Character string, used as the access variable to the result data structure. Note: Each case is named by the user and the notion of sequence number does not exist. 3.4.2 Operands MODE_FOURIER / TYPE_MODE ◊ MODE_FOURIER = mode, Positive or zero integer indicating the Fourier harmonic on which the elementary stiffness matrix and the elementary vector are computed. ◊ TYPE_MODE = type, The type of the harmonic will be symmetric ('SYME'), or antisymmetric ('ANTI'), or symmetric and antisymmetric ('TOUS') (cf. the Fourier user's guide U2.01.07). 3.4.3 Operands CHAR_MECA / VECT_ASSE ◊ CHAR_MECA = lcharm, List of concepts of type char_meca produced by AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01 or AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01 from the model mo. Note for defining a load case of "thermal expansion alone": - taking thermal expansion into account in a load case is systematic if the material field "contains" temperature (AFFE_VARC/NOM_VARC='TEMP'). - for this loading to be the only one taken into account, lcharm must contain a "null" mechanical load (for example a zero nodal force on a node). ◊ VECT_ASSE = chdep, Concept of type cham_no_depl_r representing the right-hand side of the linear system to be solved. 3.4.4 Operands OPTION ◊ OPTION = / 'SANS', / 'SIEF_ELGA', [DEFAUT] By default the command MACRO_ELAS_MULT computes the stresses at the Gauss points (or the generalised forces for the structural elements). The other post-processing options will be computed a posteriori by the command CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04. If the user indicates OPTION = 'SANS', these stresses will not be computed and the data structure produced will be less bulky. 3.4.5 Operand SOUS_TITRE ♦ SOUS_TITRE = soustitre, Subtitle that one wishes to give to the resulting displacement field. 3.5 Keyword SOLVEUR U4.50.01 This keyword makes it possible to choose the method for solving the linear systems. Recall that, in the case of the multiple load case, a single factorisation is performed for each call to MACRO_ELAS_MULT and one solution for each load case. 3.6 Operand TITRE See U4.03.01. 4 Examples One may refer to the test SSLL14 A V3.01.014. # définition des conditions aux limites de blocage bloqu = AFFE_CHAR_MECA( MODELE= modele, DDL_IMPO=(_F(TOUT='OUI' , DZ=0. ), _F(GROUP_NO=('A','B'),DX=0.,DY=0.,),)) # définition de 4 chargements charg1 = AFFE_CHAR_MECA( MODELE= modele, FORCE_POUTRE=_F( GROUP_MA= 'D2' , FY= P ) ) charg2 = AFFE_CHAR_MECA( MODELE= modele, FORCE_NODALE=_F( GROUP_NO= 'C' , FY= F1 ) ) charg3 = AFFE_CHAR_MECA( MODELE= modele, FORCE_NODALE=_F( GROUP_NO= 'D' , FX= F2 ) ) charg4 = AFFE_CHAR_MECA( MODELE= modele, FORCE_NODALE=_F( GROUP_NO= 'D' , MZ= M ) ) statique = MACRO_ELAS_MULT ( MODELE = modele, CHAM_MATER = ch_mater, CARA_ELEM = cara_ele, CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL = bloqu, # on donne un nom afin de recupérer le concept NUME_DDL NUME_DDL = nu_ddl, CAS_CHARGE=_F ( NOM_CAS = 'charge numero 1', CHAR_MECA = charg1, OPTION = 'SIEF_ELGA', SOUS_TITRE='charge repartie verticale sur DC', ), ) # deuxième série de cas de charge statique= MACRO_ELAS_MULT ( reuse = statique, MODELE = modele, CHAM_MATER = ch_mater, CARA_ELEM = cara_ele, CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL = bloqu, # on donne le concept NUME_DDL calculé précédemment NUME_DDL = nu_ddl, CAS_CHARGE=(_F( NOM_CAS = 'charge numero 2', CHAR_MECA = charg2, OPTION = ( 'SIEF_ELGA','REAC_NODA' ), SOUS_TITRE= 'force ponctuelle verticale en C', ), _F ( NOM_CAS ='charge numero 3', CHAR_MECA =charg3, OPTION =( 'SIEF_ELGA','REAC_NODA' ), SOUS_TITRE='force ponctuelle horizontale en C', ), _F ( NOM_CAS = 'charge numero 4', CHAR_MECA = charg4, OPTION = ( 'SIEF_ELGA','REAC_NODA' ), SOUS_TITRE= 'moment en C', ),), )

u4.51.03 Operator STAT_NON_LINE u4.51.03 Operator STAT_NON_LINE Summary: Compute the coupled mechanical or thermo-hydro-mechanical evolution, in quasi-statics or in dynamics, of a structure in the non-linear regime. The non-linearity is related either to the constitutive behaviour of the material (for example plastic), or to the geometry (for example in large displacements), or to frictional contact. For details on the solution method used, one should refer to the reference documentation Quasi-static non-linear algorithm The evolution can be studied in several successive jobs (re-entrant concept), either as a continuation (the last computed time instant is the initial time instant of the following analysis), or as a recovery starting from an earlier time instant. Produces a data structure of type evol_noli. 1 Syntax evol_noli = STAT_NON_LINE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ RESULTAT = evol_noli, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ EXCIT =
