equal_to("INFO", 2) ◇ INFO_DBG = / "APPARIEMENT", / "CONTACT", / "FACTOR", / "MECANONLINE", / "PILOTAGE", / "SOLVEUR", ◇ TITRE = text, The general parameters describe the model, the field of the materials and the elementary characteristics (in particular for the structural elements). MODELE is the name of the model whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. The data structure comes from the command U4.41.01. It is always mandatory. CHAM_MATER is the name of the material field assigned on the model. The data structure comes from the command U4.43.01. All the main mesh cells of the model must be associated with a material. CARA_ELEM is the name of the characteristics of the shell, beam, pipe, bar and cable elements, and of the discrete elements assigned on the model. The data structure comes from the command U4.42.01. Obviously, this keyword is optional: if the model does not contain such elements, it is not useful; on the other hand, if the model contains such elements, it is mandatory. 3.1 Title The keyword TITRE makes it possible to give a title to the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results. See [ref:U4.03.01 ]. 3.2 Management of the verbosity The keyword INFO makes it possible to carry out various intermediate printouts in the message file. Other printouts are made systematically during the non-linear analysis, independently of the value assigned to the keyword INFO: these are the printouts of the residuals and of the relative displacement increments in the course of the Newton iterations. Warning: the output files can become very large with INFO greater than 2. The keyword INFO_DBG makes it possible to limit the output to certain functionalities in order to control the size of the output file. 4 Parameterisation of the analysis ◆ INCREMENT = _F( # Si: exists("INST_INIT") or exists("INST_FIN") ◇ CRITERE = "RELATIF", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◆ LIST_INST = list_inst / listr8, ◇ / NUME_INST_INIT = int, / INST_INIT = float, ◇ / NUME_INST_FIN = int, / INST_FIN = float, ), The non-linear analysis is solved by an incremental method, so it is necessary to parameterise the analysis. One uses for this the time variable (denoted INST), even if it has no physical meaning in statics. The (pseudo)-temporal discretisation is managed by the factor keyword INCREMENT, which defines the time intervals taken in the incremental method. Note The time instants thus defined have a physical meaning only for constitutive relations in which time enters explicitly (viscoelastic or viscoplastic, for example). In the other cases, they only make it possible to index the load increments and to parameterise the evolution of a possible temperature field. 4.1 General definition of the list of time instants To supply the list of time instants, there are two ways of proceeding. The first is direct: one gives the list of time instants by the keyword LIST_INST. This list is given by the operator U4.34.01. This way of proceeding does not give access to the advanced functionalities for the automatic management of the list of time instants. It is therefore not recommended. One can define the analysis time instants by the operator DEFI_LIST_INST and manage at the same time the automatic subdivision of the time step and other advanced functionalities. This is the recommended way of proceeding. It should also be recalled that, by convention, the initial time instant of the analysis of a virgin analysis (without recovery) is designated by the order number 0. Furthermore, the order numbers are necessarily increasing and without "gaps". 4.2 Management of the recoveries If one specifies nothing, the analysis will be carried out over all the time instants defined by LIST_INST. It is possible to manage this list more finely. The initial time instant of the analysis (which is therefore not (re)computed) is designated either by its value (INST_INIT), or by its order number in the list of time instants litps (NUME_INST_INIT). In the absence of the keywords INST_INIT or NUME_INST_INIT, the default is NUME_INST_INIT=0. The final time instant (last computed step) is designated in the same way as the initial time instant (either NUME_INST_FIN, or INST_FIN), except that it is not possible to refer to the time instant of the initial state. - If the automatic subdivision of the time step is activated, NUME_INST_FIN does not take it into account and always works on the initial list of time instants. NUME_INST_INIT and NUME_INST_FIN are active only at initialisation. - The list of time instants being strictly increasing, it can happen that certain time steps are not archived although they were requested. For example, in the case of a recovery of an analysis. If the analysis in recovery of a previous analysis has no time instant greater than the first phase of the analysis, no time step will be archived. - If INST_INIT does not exist in the list of time instants, one takes the immediately greater time step Notes A - Simple example (default behaviour) listInst = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT=0., INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A= 10.,NOMBRE=10)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst, INST_FIN=4.)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(reuse=evolNoli, INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst), ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=evolNoli)) The first MECA_NON_LINE carries out the analysis for the time instants 1, 2, 3 and 4. The second MECA_NON_LINE: carries out the analysis for the time instants 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, the initial state corresponding to time 4. B - Example to show the interest of INST_INIT listInst = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT=0., INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A= 10.,NOMBRE=10)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst, INST_FIN=4.)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(reuse=evolNoli, INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst, INST_INIT=8.), ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=evolNoli)) First MECA_NON_LINE: carries out the analysis of the time instants 1 to 4. Second MECA_NON_LINE: carries out the analysis for the time instants 9 and 10 (one does nothing for t=5,6,7 and 8), the initial state corresponding to time 4. 4.3 Selection of the time instants The time instants in MECA_NON_LINE are located by an order number (an integer). If the user wants to use a time instant (a real) and not an order number for the selection, the keywords PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to identify this order number (see U4.71.00 for the detailed syntax) These parameters are used to locate the correct order number (NUME_INST_FIN/NUME_INST_INIT) when the user supplies the time instant (INST_FIN/INST_INIT). Consider the following list of time instants: | NUME | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | INST | 0.0010 | 0.0020 | 0.0030 | 0.0040 | 0.0050 | 0.0060 | 0.0070 | If the user wants to select the time instant corresponding to NUME=4, it is enough to say INST=0.0040. Let us take another example | NUME | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | INST | 0.10000001 | 0.10000002 | 0.10000003 | 0.10000004 | 0.10000005 | 0.10000006 | 0.10000007 | If the user wants to select the time instant corresponding to NUME=4, it is not enough to say INST=0.10000004, because the relative gap between the time instants is \frac{0,10000005-0,10000004}{0,10000004}=1,0\times 10^{-7} which is smaller than the default precision value ( 1,0\times 10^{-6} ). One will therefore not be able to distinguish NUME=3, 4 and 5 (the code then stops in fatal error). It is then enough to change the parameter PRECISION in order to be able to select the time instant (in our example, PRECISION=1E-8 will do). 5 Settings of the non-linear solvers 5.1 Choice of the method ◇ METHODE = / "IMPLEX", / "MODELE_REDUIT", / "NEWTON" (par défaut), / "NEWTON_KRYLOV", There exist several categories of accessible non-linear solvers: the Newton method (and its variants), the Newton-Krylov method, the IMPLEX method, access to the non-linear solver SNES of the PETSc library, and the use of model-reduction methods (ROM). The solver is selected by the keyword METHODE. 5.2 Newton method ⟐ NEWTON = _F( ◇ REAC_INCR = int (défaut: 1), ◇ PREDICTION = / "DEPL_CALCULE", / "ELASTIQUE", / "EXTRAPOLE", / "TANGENTE", ◇ MATRICE = / "ELASTIQUE", / "TANGENTE" (par défaut), ◇ PAS_MINI_ELAS = float, ◇ REAC_ITER = int (défaut: 1), ◇ REAC_ITER_ELAS = int (défaut: 0), ◇ EVOL_NOLI = evol_noli, ◇ MATR_RIGI_SYME = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ), When METHODE="NEWTON", one uses the Newton-Raphson algorithm to solve the problem (see R5.03.01). It is the factor keyword NEWTON (a single occurrence) which makes it possible to set the various parameters. The keyword MATR_RIGI_SYME is used to force the symmetry of the stiffness matrix. It is useful when one simultaneously uses a functionality which uses a non-symmetric matrix (Simo-Miehe formalism, loadings of follower-pressure type, etc.) and the contact formulation of type DISCRETE or LIAISON_UNIL (cf. U4.44.11). Indeed, the latter can work only with a symmetric stiffness matrix. Making the stiffness matrix symmetric has consequences on the rate of convergence, which can go as far as its failure, but will never produce incorrect results. If making the stiffness matrix symmetric makes the convergence of Newton's algorithm impossible, the user is invited to use a contact formulation of type CONTINUE, which works with a non-symmetric stiffness matrix. 5.2.1 Prediction phase The prediction phase (Cf. R5.03.01) aims to compute an estimate of the displacement field so as to allow Newton's method to converge more quickly. When the keyword is absent, it is the rate tangent matrix (option RIGI_MECA_TANG) which is used if one has chosen for Newton's method a PREDICTION='TANGENTE', and it is the elastic matrix (option RIGI_MECA) which is used if one has chosen PREDICTION='ELASTIQUE'. It is also possible to make a prediction by using preliminary results coming from another analysis. For PREDICTION='EXTRAPOLE', one computes the estimate of the displacement increment from the total increment obtained as the solution at the previous time step (weighted by the ratio of the time steps). One projects this estimate onto the set of kinematically admissible fields (i.e. satisfying the Dirichlet boundary conditions) according to the norm given by the elastic matrix, which must therefore be computed. This functionality is of interest in the case of the use of explicit local integration schemes of Runge-Kutta type, which do not supply a tangent matrix: in this case Newton's method uses an elastic matrix, but the number of iterations required can be high. The use of the extrapolation can improve the performance. For PREDICTION='DEPL_CALCULE' it proposes, as the displacement for the prediction at each time step, the displacement given by a mechanical history specified under the keyword EVOL_NOLI (by the keyword EVOL_NOLI). The displacement is projected onto the set of kinematically admissible fields, as for the EXTRAPOLE method. - The methods 'EXTRAPOLE' and 'DEPL_CALCULE' carry out a projection of the solution onto the set of kinematically admissible fields. One uses for this the Dirichlet boundary conditions given in the keyword EXCIT. In this case, it is not possible to use Dirichlet loadings of "kinematic" type (operand AFFE_CHAR_CINE) but only Dirichlet loadings by dualisation (operand AFFE_CHAR_MECA). The analysis works, but the risk in this case being that the displacement field is not kinematically admissible, the user must be attentive to it. - The methods 'EXTRAPOLE' and 'DEPL_CALCULE' do not take into account the contact terms at the prediction phase. Consequently, it is advisable to choose the methods 'ELASTIQUE' or 'TANGENTE' in prediction for contact analyses. - It is necessary that the displacements used in 'EXTRAPOLE' and 'DEPL_CALCULE' come from an analysis using the same mesh, because the boundary conditions must be consistent. - Because of this projection onto the boundary conditions, these two options are incompatible with the functionalities of PILOTAGE. Notes: These two methods have other uses. For example, if one has obtained a first solution on the same mesh with other material parameters or another constitutive behaviour, the displacement fields can be reused in the analysis. Likewise, this makes it possible to reduce the memory space and to keep these results with a view to a later continuation. For a large analysis, one can store only the displacements at all the time instants in IMPR_RESU. If one wants to recompute the stresses and the internal variables, one does a LIRE_RESU in the appropriate format and then one uses DEPL_CALCULE with ITER_GLOB_MAXI=0 (one carries out a single iteration) and ARRET='NON' (there is no convergence, one does not check equilibrium). It is however necessary, for reasons of syntax, to give a loading (avoid the Dirichlet loadings, which impose a linear solution) as well as a convergence criterion, even if this information is not taken into account. Because of the impossibility of correctly "projecting" the boundary conditions from one mesh onto the other, it is now strongly inadvisable to use EXTRAPOLE and DEPL_CALCULE from a mesh different from that of the current analysis. 5.2.2 Correction phase The matrix used for the global iterations of the method is the (consistent) tangent matrix R5.03.01 if MATRICE='TANGENTE', or the elastic matrix if MATRICE='ELASTIQUE'. The keyword REAC_INCR makes it possible to control the update frequency of the matrix with respect to the time steps. - If the matrix used in prediction corresponds to the elastic analysis, it is evaluated only once at the initial time instant, at the beginning of the algorithm, unless the elastic characteristics depend on time or on a command variable such as the temperature, which depends on time - This "elastic" matrix is computed by using Young's modulus given under the keyword ELAS of the operator DEFI_MATERIAU, and not the slope at the origin of the traction curve given under the keyword TRACTION (and which is used, for its part, in the expression of the constitutive relations VMIS_ISOT_TRAC, VMIS_ECMI_TRAC and VISC_ISOT_TRAC) Notes: The keyword REAC_ITER makes it possible to control the update frequency of the matrix with respect to the Newton iterations. Thus, at the first Newton iteration, one reassembles the tangent matrix only if it is equal to 1: otherwise one keeps the matrix used in the prediction phase. By convention, if it is equal to 0 the matrix is not re-evaluated during the whole time step. 5.2.3 Switch of the matrix in correction The options PAS_MINI_ELAS and REAC_ITER_ELAS make it possible to pass from the tangent matrix to the unloading matrix (i.e. considering that the non-linearities do not evolve) when the time step is smaller than PAS_MINI_ELAS. This unloading matrix is the elastic matrix for constitutive models of plastic type; for damage models it is identified with the secant matrix. As convergence with the elastic matrix is slower than that with the tangent matrix, the keyword ITER_GLOB_ELAS under the factor keyword CONVERGENCE makes it possible to define a maximum number of iterations specific to the use of the elastic matrix and different from that associated with the use of the tangent matrix. One can define an update frequency of the unloading matrix with the keyword REAC_ITER_ELAS (analogue of REAC_ITER). If the unloading matrix does not depend on the state of strain (which is the case for plastic materials but not for damage models), take REAC_ITER_ELAS = 0 (since it will be the same in the course of the iterations). These options can be useful when the automatic subdivision of the time step is not enough to make an analysis converge. For example, in the case of softening laws, the tangent matrix can become singular and it is therefore better to use the elastic matrix in order to converge. 5.3 Newton-Krylov method If one chooses METHODE='NEWTON_KRYLOV', one uses an inexact version of the Newton-Raphson algorithm; the accuracy of the solutions of the linear systems by an iterative method is adapted in the course of each loading step (see R5.03.01). All the options described for Newton's method (management of the matrices, of the updating, etc.) can be used by the Newton-Krylov method. 5.4 IMPLEX method When METHODE='IMPLEX', one uses the IMPLEX algorithm to solve the problem (see [ref:R5.03.81 ]). This method can be used only with a limited number of: constitutive behaviours. 5.5 Model-reduction method (ROM) ◆ MODELE_REDUIT = _F( ◇ REAC_INCR = int (défaut: 1), ◇ PREDICTION = / "DEPL_CALCULE", / "ELASTIQUE", / "EXTRAPOLE", / "TANGENTE" (par défaut), ◇ MATRICE = / "ELASTIQUE", / "TANGENTE" (par défaut), ◇ REAC_ITER = int (défaut: 1), ◆ BASE_PRIMAL = mode_empi, ◇ DOMAINE_REDUIT = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ EVOL_NOLI = evol_noli, # Si: (equal_to("DOMAINE_REDUIT", 'OUI')) ◆ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, ◇ CORR_COMPLET = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: (equal_to("CORR_COMPLET", 'OUI')) ◇ COEF_PENA = float (défaut: 1000000.0), ◆ GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE = grno, ), When METHODE='MODELE_REDUIT', one uses a model-reduction method to carry out the non-linear analysis (see R5.01.05). It is necessary to have built a reduced basis beforehand (command DEFI_BASE_REDUITE). - contact and friction (all methods) - piloting, - the line search, - dualised boundary conditions (AFFE_CHAR_MECA): one must use AFFE_CHAR_CINE, - mixed models: model reduction is compatible only with displacement finite elements (nor with structural models either) Model reduction is not compatible with the following functionalities: One can specify the characteristics of the method of solution of the non-linear incremental problem by a model-reduction method. The prediction strategy can be set as in the case of Newton with the keyword PREDICTION. One can set the updating of the matrices with the keywords REAC_INCR and REAC_ITER. The reduced basis is given by the keyword BASE_PRIMAL. This basis must have been built on the same model and the same mesh as the analysis (but the loadings, the materials and the constitutive behaviour can be different). It is possible to activate hyper-reduction, which uses a method of dEIM type (discrete Empirical Interpolation Method) by DOMAINE_REDUIT='OUI'. In this case, the analysis is reduced to a restricted zone of the mesh (called RID) and built with the help of the operator DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT. One must give the node group on which the interface between the RID and the rest of the domain is defined, with the help of the keyword GROUP_NO_INTERF. To improve the quality of the results in hyper-reduction, it is possible to make a correction of the hyper-reduced analysis by a detailed finite-element analysis with CORR_COMPLET='OUI'. For this, it is necessary to define a node group used to make the connection between the RID and the rest of the model with the keyword GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE (defined for example in the command DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT). This node group makes it possible to impose the Dirichlet boundary conditions necessary for the corrected problem to be well defined. These boundary conditions being defined by penalisation, the penalisation coefficient can be changed by the keyword COEF_PENA. This correction always being carried out on the reduced domain, it will not be as accurate as a true detailed analysis (complete domain). Nevertheless, it is very useful when one changes the boundary conditions significantly between the definition of the reduced basis (off-line phase in DEFI_BASE_REDUITE) and the analysis using this reduced basis (on-line phase in STAT_NON_LINE). 5.6 Line search ◇ RECH_LINEAIRE = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "CORDE" (par défaut), / "MIXTE", / "PILOTAGE", ◇ RESI_LINE_RELA = float (défaut: 0.1), ◇ ITER_LINE_MAXI = int (défaut: 3), ◇ RHO_MIN = float (défaut: 0.01), ◇ RHO_MAX = float (défaut: 10.0), ◇ RHO_EXCL = float (défaut: 0.009), ), The line search can make it possible to improve the convergence of Newton's method (Cf.:ref:R5.03.01 for more details). Note: It is inadvisable to use the line search with the GROT_GDEP strains, for the COQUE_3D modellings and in the presence of contact. This factor keyword RECH_LINEAIRE makes it possible to activate the line search (see R5.03.01). The keyword METHODE makes it possible to choose the line-search method, that is to say the algorithm for searching for the zero of the functional. The CORDE method (by default) is the simplest method; it is a one-dimensional secant method. The MIXTE method is more elaborate and uses a secant method with variable bounds. It is more effective when the functional is not strictly concave (problems with damage or THM, for example). The PILOTAGE method is reserved for piloting of type DEFORMATION, PRED_ELAS and LONG_ARC (see the paragraph on piloting). It is the only method usable with this type of piloting. For piloting of type DDL_IMPO, one can use CORDE or MIXTE. One gives the maximum number of iterations to be carried out by ITER_LINE_MAXI and the precision to be reached by RESI_LINE_RELA in order to achieve convergence of the line search. For the CORDE method, it is not necessary to specify a very high precision or a very high number of iterations, practice showing that two or three line-search iterations are sufficient. One can therefore be content with requesting three iterations with the default precision. The user cannot put more than 999 line-search iterations for the CORDE method. On the other hand, for the MIXTE method, on problems with damage, several tens of iterations are often effective. The keywords RHO_MIN, RHO_MAX and RHO_EXCL fix the interval I in which one computes the coefficient \rho : of the line search, in the form I=[\rho_{min},\rho_{max}]-[-\rho_{exc},\rho_{exc}] 5.7 Control of the THM ◇ SCHEMA_THM = _F( ◇ PARM_THETA = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ PARM_ALPHA = float (défaut: 1.0), ), The keyword SCHEMA_THM makes it possible to manage the parameters of the THM schemes for the hydraulics (PARM_THETA, see R7.01.10) and for the finite volumes of SUSHI type (PARM_ALPHA, see R7.01.34). This parameter PARM_THETA is quite distinct from the one defined in the keyword COMPORTEMENT. 6 Loadings ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_meca / char_meca, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = / "DIDI", / "FIXE_CSTE" (par défaut), / "FIXE_PILO", / "SUIV", / "SUIV_PILO", ), 6.1 General principles The factor keyword EXCIT makes it possible to describe at each occurrence a load (loads and boundary conditions), and possibly a multiplying coefficient and/or a type of load. The non-linear analysis is solved by an incremental method, so it is necessary to parameterise the analysis. One therefore also applies the loadings in an incremental manner, for example by applying the force progressively (a ramp). The basic principle is to separate the spatial part of the loading and the (pseudo)-temporal part. \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( {\underline{u}, t} \right ) = g \left ( t \right ) \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( \underline{u} \right ) The spatial part of the loading \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( \underline{u} \right ) is given by the keyword CHARGE (possibly including the evolution of a temperature field). - In a thermo-mechanical analysis, if the initial temperature is different from the reference temperature (given in AFFE_MATERIAU), the associated strain field at the initial time instant can be incompatible and therefore lead to an associated state of stresses and of internal variables which is non-zero. If one uses an incremental constitutive relation and if one does not explicitly define an initial state of stresses and of internal variables (associated with an initial temperature field different from the reference temperature), the field of stresses and of internal variables computed at the first increment will take into account only the variation of temperature between the initial time instant and the first time instant, and not the possible compatibility stresses associated with the initial temperature. To take this initial state into account, one must give it explicitly, for example by means of the keywords in ETAT_INIT. To avoid such situations, which can lead to analysis errors, it is better to start an analysis by considering that one must start from a virgin state. - If one carries out an analysis in axisymmetry and one imposes nodal forces, these forces must be divided by 2\pi (one works on a sector of one radian) with respect to the real loadings. Likewise, if one wishes to compute the resultant of the forces, the result is to be multiplied by 2\pi in order to have the total resultant on the complete structure. Likewise, in plane stresses or in plane strains, one works on a unit thickness: the forces (over the thickness) applied must be divided by the thickness, and the real forces are obtained by multiplying the forces of the analysis by the thickness. Notes: The temporal part of the loading g \left ( t \right ) is given by the keyword FONC_MULT. If one does not specify the multiplying function, one applies a step function. It is possible to define directly \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( {\underline{u}, t} \right ) in the keyword CHARGE if one uses the command AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F (function of time). In this case, one must be careful: indeed, if one uses FONC_MULT at the same time, one multiplies the loading again by a function of time. By default, TYPE_CHARGE is equal to 'FIXE_CSTE': this corresponds to a loading applied on the initial geometry and not piloted. It can however be a function, and, in particular, depend on time. A fixed loading is re-evaluated only at each new time instant, and only if it depends on time (defined in AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F and parameterised by the time instant, or else affected by FONC_MULT). 6.2 Follower loadings If TYPE_CHARGE='SUIV', the loading is said to be a "follower", that is to say that it depends on the value of the unknowns: for example, the pressure, being a loading applied in the normal direction to a structure, depends on the updated geometry of the latter, and therefore on the displacements. A follower loading is re-evaluated at each iteration of the solution algorithm. At present the loadings which can be qualified as followers are the gravity loading for the CABLE_POULIE element, the pressure for the modellings 3D, 3D_SI, D_PLAN, D_PLAN_SI, AXIS, AXIS_SI, C_PLAN, C_PLAN_SI, COQUE_3D and for all the THM modellings, and the centrifugal force in large displacements (keyword ROTATION in AFFE_CHAR_MECA). There is also the surface force FORCE_FACE for the 3D elements. One can also impose that a Dirichlet loading be a follower in the case of the rigidification of a part of the structure by the use of LIAISON_SOLIDE (see AFFE_CHAR_MECA) in large transformations. - The pressure can be defined by a function depending on the geometry. In the follower case, one can choose whether this dependence is with respect to the initial geometry with the parameters X, Y and Z of DEFI_FONCTION or with respect to the updated geometry with the parameters XF, YF and ZF. - The follower loading of type LIAISON_SOLIDE is strictly incompatible with piloting and the line search. It can be used only with 2D and 3D isoparametric finite elements (not with structural elements such as beams, plates and shells). - In the case of COQUE_3D, the pressure loading can be created by the keywords PRES_REP/PRES or FORCE_COQUE/PRES of AFFE_CHAR_MECA. The other operands of FORCE_COQUE (FX, FY…, F1, F2, ...) are not compatible with follower loadings. Notes: 6.3 Piloted loadings If TYPE_CHARGE is equal to 'FIXE_PILO', the loading is still fixed (independent of the geometry) but it will be piloted by means of the factor keyword PILOTAGE. The pilotable loads must come from the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA or AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F (if it is not a function depending on time) and must not be affected by the keyword FONC_MULT. One cannot pilot the gravity loadings, the centrifugal force, the Laplace forces, the thermal loadings or those of initial or anelastic strains, and the connection conditions. To have piloted loads depending on the geometry (so-called "follower" loads), one uses TYPE_CHARGE='SUIV_PILO'. 6.4 Incremental loadings If TYPE_CHARGE='DIDI' then the Dirichlet conditions (imposed displacements, linear conditions) will apply to the displacement increment from the time instant given under ETAT_INIT/NUME_DIDI (by default the recovery time instant of the analysis) and not to the total displacement. For example, for an imposed displacement (keyword DDL_IMPO of AFFE_CHAR_MECA) the condition will be of the form u-{u}_{0}=d where {u}_{0} is the displacement defined by NUME_DIDI and not u=d . The differential Dirichlet option is available both for mechanical loadings (CHAR_MECA) and for kinematic loadings (CHAR_CINE). 7 Piloting Piloting is sometimes known under the name of continuation method . ◇ PILOTAGE = _F( ◆ TYPE = / "ANA_LIM", / "DDL_IMPO", / "DEFORMATION", / "LONG_ARC", / "PRED_ELAS", ◇ COEF_MULT = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ EVOL_PARA = / "CROISSANT", / "DECROISSANT", / "SANS" (par défaut), ◇ ETA_PILO_MAX = float, ◇ ETA_PILO_MIN = float, ◇ ETA_PILO_R_MAX = float, ◇ ETA_PILO_R_MIN = float, ◇ PROJ_BORNES = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'LONG_ARC') or equal_to("TYPE", ) ◇ SELECTION = / "ANGL_INCR_DEPL", / "MIXTE", / "NORM_INCR_DEPL" (par défaut), / "RESIDU", # Si: not equal_to("TYPE", 'LONG_ARC') ◇ SELECTION = / "MIXTE", / "NORM_INCR_DEPL" (par défaut), / "RESIDU", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ / NOEUD = list[no], / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◇ NOM_CMP = list[text], ), 7.1 General principles When the intensity \eta of a part of the loading is not known a priori (so-called reference loading defined in AFFE_CHAR_MECA with a load of type FIXE_PILO), the keyword PILOTAGE makes it possible to pilot this loading by means of a node (or node group) on which one can impose various piloting modes (keyword TYPE). - With FIXE_PILO, one cannot use the keyword FONC_MULT for the reference loading. - When the reference loading is defined by AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F, this loading can be a function of the space variables but not of time. Likewise, the changes coming from command variables (such as the temperature) which depend on time cannot be used with piloting. - Piloting is forbidden with contact. - It is not possible to do piloting with PREDICTION='DEPL_CALCULE' or PREDICTION='EXTRAPOLE' Notes: 7.2 The types of piloting The type of piloting carried out is given by the keyword TYPE. Seven piloting modes are available (Confer R5.03.80 for more details). 7.2.1 Piloting for the displacements Piloting for the displacements will control the intensity of the loading in order to control a displacement or equivalent. TYPE='DDL_IMPO' makes it possible to impose a given value of displacement increment (a single component i possible) at a single node (or of a node group comprising only one node) given by the keywords NOEUD or GROUP_NO. At each time increment, one seeks the amplitude \eta of the reference loading which will make it possible to satisfy the following incremental relation C \, \Delta {u}_{i} (\text{noeud}) = \Delta t TYPE='LONG_ARC' makes it possible to pilot the intensity \eta of the reference loading by the length (curvilinear abscissa) of the displacement response of a node group (to be used for example when one wants to control the buckling of a specimen). One checks the following relation: C \, \parallel \Delta u\parallel =\Delta t with \parallel (\Delta u)\parallel =(\sqrt{\sum_{n}\sum_{c}({\Delta u}_{n,c}^{2})}) where n are the piloting nodes and c the components of the displacement of the nodes considered. Even if the piloting node group is reduced to a single node, one must still use GROUP_NO. For both types, C is given by the keyword COEF_MULT and NOM_CMP gives the name of the component (corresponding to the degree of freedom i ) used for the piloting ('DX' for example). 7.2.2 Piloting for the limit analysis The piloting TYPE='ANA_LIM' is specific to the limit-load analysis (law NORTON_HOFF) by the kinematic approach (cf. [ref:R7.07.01 ] for more details). If F denotes the piloted assembled loading (indicated by TYPE_CHARGE='FIXE_PILO'), then the piloting function is written simply: P(u)=F \cdot u = 1 Except for the limit-load analysis, this functionality is of no interest a priori . For this piloting mode, no other keyword is to be specified. 7.2.3 Piloting for the softening constitutive behaviours The use of softening constitutive laws can lead to sudden snap-backs which make the course of the analysis delicate. The following two piloting modes remedy this: (Cf. R5.03.80 for more details). The piloting TYPE='DEFORMATION' guarantees that at least one Gauss point of the structure sees its strain evolve in a monotonic way. One checks the relation: C \,\underset{\mathrm{Pg}}{\max} \left( \frac{\dot{\varepsilon}}{\parallel \dot{\varepsilon}\parallel } \cdot \Delta \varepsilon \right) =\Delta t This piloting mode is valid for all the constitutive laws, including in large strains SIMO_MIEHE. When one wants to use this piloting mode, it is indispensable to carry out a first analysis without the keyword PILOTAGE in order to prime the problem and obtain an initial state {\varepsilon}^{-} different from zero (otherwise division by zero). One then carries out a recovery from this non-zero initial state and one uses the piloting. The piloting TYPE='PRED_ELAS' ensures that at least one Gauss point of the structure leaves the linearised elasticity threshold {f}_{\text{pred-elas}} by a quantity \frac{\Delta t}{C} . One checks the relation: C \, \underset{\mathrm{Pg}}{\max} \left( {f}_{\mathrm{PRED\_ELAS}} \right) =\Delta t This piloting mode is valid only for the laws ENDO_SCALAIRE (with the non-local version), VMIS_ISOT_NL (with the local version only), ENDO_FISS_EXP (non-local only), ENDO_ISOT_BETON and ENDO_ORTH_BETON (with the local version and the non-local version), BARENBLATT, BETON_DOUBLE_DP, CZM_EXP (with the elements with internal discontinuity _ELDI), CZM_OUV_MIX, CZM_TAC_MIX and CZM_LAB_MIX (interface elements _INTERFACE), CZM_EXP_REG (joint elements _JOINT or X-FEM modelling) and CZM_LIN_REG (joint elements). C is given by the keyword COEF_MULT but fixing this parameter is difficult to define at the first attempt because the notion of departure from the criterion \frac{\Delta t}{C} is not intuitive and varies according to the constitutive laws. For the laws ENDO_SCALAIRE, ENDO_FISS_EXP and ENDO_ISOT_BETON, a different version of the definition of \frac{\Delta t}{C} is used, in which this parameter is linked to the damage increment (see R7.01.04). The solution of the two previous equations makes it possible to obtain the unknown intensity of the loading. In certain cases, the solution of these equations can lead to several solutions for the intensity. One then always chooses the solution which is the closest to {\varepsilon}^{-} . This is why, when one wants to impose an alternating loading, one is obliged, at each change of sign of the loading, to carry out a first analysis without the keyword PILOTAGE in order to obtain an initial state {\varepsilon}^{-} of tension or of compression. One then carries out a second analysis in continuation from the previous initial state with the keyword PILOTAGE. These two types of piloting are not available for the structural elements. One gives the mesh cells or mesh-cell groups used to pilot the analysis by the keywords GROUP_MA, MAILLE or TOUT. This is of interest in order to lighten the solution of the equations of these piloting modes. 7.3 Control of the bounds These keywords ETA_PILO_R_MAX and ETA_PILO_R_MIN make it possible to define the search interval of the piloting values. At each Newton iteration all the piloting values outside [\eta^{R}_{min}, \eta^{R}_{max}] are ignored. This can lead to a "piloting failure" if this interval is too restrictive. If one does not specify any values, one has \eta^{R}_{min}=-\infty and \eta^{R}_{max}=+\infty . A possible use of this interval is the following. One wishes, for example, to pilot a pressure imposed on the structure and one expects to keep this pressure positive. By setting \eta^{R}_{min}=-0 , this makes it possible to impose positive piloting values. The keywords ETA_PILO_MAX and ETA_PILO_MIN make it possible to specify the interval of piloting values desired. One uses it to stop the analysis cleanly when ETA_PILOTAGE reaches the bounds of this interval. This interval must be more restrictive than the search interval defined previously, because the latter is applied in every case. The principle of operation is the following: at convergence of the Newton iterations, if one of the bounds has been reached, the analysis stops. A possible use of this interval is the following. In the case of the presence of snap-back, by setting \eta_{min} to a small value, this makes it possible to stop the analysis before a complete tearing/damage of the specimen and thus to avoid the divergence at the last time step. The other possible use is that of \eta_{max} as a maximum limit load. With the law ENDO_ISOT_BETON, these two keywords are mandatory, because they are used to fix the piloting bounds at element level. In the event of overshoot of the interval [\eta_{min}, \eta_{max}] , the user can indicate whether one wants to project the piloting value onto [\eta_{min}, \eta_{max}] with PROJ_BORNES='OUI'. With PROJ_BORNE='OUI', the projection will be carried out (if \eta>\eta_{max} then \eta=\eta_{max} ; if \etaw\eta_{min} then \eta=\eta_{min} ), which makes it possible, in the event of convergence, to stop the analysis precisely on \eta_{min} or \eta_{max} . With PROJ_BORNE='NON', one does not modify the values of eta, even if during the Newton iterations the latter has a value greater than \eta_{max} or smaller than \eta_{min} . On the other hand the analysis is stopped if, at convergence, \eta exceeds the bounds. A possible use of the interval [\eta_{min}, \eta_{max}] with the option PROJ_BORNE='OUI' is the following. One wishes, for example, to compare several analyses for a softening model, which are piloted in displacement. These piloting parameters make it possible to stop the analyses at the same loading when the structure is sufficiently softened. This strategy makes the comparison easier, thanks to the control of the last piloting point. It is strongly recommended to call on the option PROJ_BORNE='OUI' when setting up test cases involving piloting of the loading. This indeed makes it possible to stop the analysis at precise points where one comes to test the values, which improves the robustness of the test and facilitates its maintenance. An example of this data setup is proposed in the tests ssnp133a and ssnp133d. With PROJ_BORNE='NON' one can in certain cases unblock the analyses, which otherwise do not converge with the too restrictive conditions imposed via the interval [\eta^{R}_{min}, \eta^{R}_{max}] . Suppose one pilots a pressure imposed on the structure and one expects to keep this pressure positive. By setting \eta^{R}_{min}=0 , the analysis stops in piloting failure. On the other hand, by imposing \eta^{R}_{min} slightly negative, one authorises de facto the passage through a "non-physical" state during the Newton iterations, which facilitates convergence. The converged state in this case can just as well be physical (positive pressure) or non-physical. It is the value of \eta^{R}_{min}=0 , which will govern the behaviour in the event of convergence outside the bounds. This strategy makes it possible to keep only the positive piloting values, if one finds at least one positive piloting value. 7.4 Control of the multiple solutions The keyword SELECTION makes it possible to select the method making it possible to choose the piloting value in the case where several solutions are supplied by the piloting solution. SELECTION='NORM_INCR_DEPL' makes it possible to select the piloting value by the smallest norm of the displacement increment over the time step considered. SELECTION='ANGL_INCR_DEPL' makes it possible to select the piloting value by the smallest angle between the displacement obtained for the current time step and the displacement obtained for the previous time step. This choice is available only with TYPE=LONG_ARC. SELECTION='RESIDU' makes it possible to select the piloting value leading to the smallest residual. SELECTION='MIXTE' makes it possible to select the piloting value by relying on several strategies. One starts with the NORM_INCR_DEPL strategy above. If the results of the objective function (the norm of the displacement increment) are too close, one switches for this iteration to the RESIDU strategy. There again, if the residuals are too close, one returns to the NORM_INCR_DEPL strategy and one examines whether the list of the residuals RESI_GLOB_MAXI of the current time step presents cycles. If this is the case, it is the worst solution of NORM_INCR_DEPL which is chosen for this iteration. Otherwise, one simply chooses the better of the two, even if they are not sufficiently contrasted. - If one does a recovery of an analysis (reuse) with the keyword SELECTION='ANGL_INCR_DEPL', it is important to bear in mind that this criterion requires the two previous time steps. One will therefore have to take care to archive correctly the results of the previous analysis, at the risk of obtaining incorrect results. An alarm warns the user in this situation. Note: The keyword EVOL_PARA makes it possible to impose the growth or the decrease of the piloting parameter. 8 Settings of the convergence ⟐ CONVERGENCE = _F( ◆ | RESI_REFE_RELA = float, | RESI_GLOB_MAXI = float, | RESI_GLOB_RELA = float, ◇ / RESI_COMP_RELA = float, ◇ ITER_GLOB_MAXI = int (défaut: 10), ◇ ITER_GLOB_ELAS = int (défaut: 25), ◇ ARRET = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ VERIF = / "AU_MOINS_UN", / "TOUT" (par défaut), ), ⟐ CONVERGENCE_REFE = _F( # Si RESI_REFE_RELA est présent dans CONVERGENCE (inutile sinon) ◆ | EFFORT = float, | SIGM = float, | EPSI = float, | FLUXTHER = float, | MOMENT = float, | FLUXHYD1 = float, | FLUXHYD2 = float, | VARI = float, | DEPL = float, | LAGR = float, | PI = float, ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), The factor keyword CONVERGENCE makes it possible to control the convergence parameters of the analysis. When VERIF= "TOUT", all the activated convergence criteria (RESI_GLOB_RELA, RESI_GLOB_MAXI, RESI_REFE_RELA and RESI_COMP_RELA) are checked simultaneously; when VERIF="AU_MOINS_UN", a single one of the activated criteria is enough to establish convergence. One must be very cautious in the use of VERIF = "AU_MOINS_UN" because if one of the criteria is very loose, this can lead to incorrect results . 8.1 Standard convergence criteria There exist several convergence criteria: the two most common are RESI_GLOB_RELA in relative form and RESI_GLOB_MAXI in absolute form. If one supplies nothing, then everything proceeds as if RESI_GLOB_RELA = 1.E-6. For RESI_GLOB_MAXI= \varepsilon_{max} , the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as where {F}^{n} is the residual of iteration {n} (Cf. R5.03.01 for more details). If this operand is absent, the test is not carried out. For RESI_GLOB_RELA= \varepsilon_{rel} , the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as \underset{i=1, \dots , \mathrm{nbddl}}{\max} {F}^{n} > \varepsilon_{rel} . {\max} L where L is the vector of the imposed loading and of the support reactions (Cf. R5.03.01 for more details). When the loading and the support reactions become zero, that is to say when L is zero (for example in the case of a total unloading), RESI_GLOB_RELA is displayed as -1, and one tries to pass from the relative convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_RELA to the absolute convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_MAXI. This operation is transparent for the user (alarm message issued in the .mess file). When the vector L becomes different from zero again, one automatically returns to the relative convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_RELA. However, this switching mechanism cannot work at the first time step. Indeed, in order to find a reasonable value of RESI_GLOB_MAXI automatically (since the user has not supplied it), one needs to have had at least one converged step on a RESI_GLOB_RELA mode. Hence, if the loading is zero from the first time instant, the analysis stops. The user must then already check that the zero loading is normal from the point of view of the modelling which one is carrying out, and if such is the case, find another convergence criterion (RESI_GLOB_MAXI for example). If RESI_GLOB_RELA and RESI_GLOB_MAXI are both present, both tests are carried out. 8.2 Advanced convergence criteria The criterion RESI_COMP_RELA= \varepsilon_{cmp} leads one to estimate the convergence of Newton's algorithm by reasoning component by component. For this, one distinguishes in the residual vector the sub-vectors corresponding to each component \mathrm{cmp} (for example in THM, \mathrm{cmp}=\left\lbrace \mathrm{DX},\mathrm{DY},\mathrm{DZ},\mathrm{PRE1},\mathrm{PRE2},\mathrm{TEMP}\right\rbrace ). One then normalises these sub-vectors by the corresponding internal force. Thus, the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as \underset{c=1, \dots ,\mathit{nbcmp}}{max}(\frac{\underset{i=1, \dots ,\mathit{nbddl}}{max}\mid {F}_{i}^{c,n}\mid }{\underset{i=1, \dots ,\mathit{nbddl}}{max}\mid {L}_{i}^{int,c,n}\mid })>\varepsilon_{cmp} where {F}^{c,n} is the part of the residual {F}^{n} corresponding to the component c and {L}^{int,c,n} the vector of the internal forces at time n corresponding to this same component c (Cf. R5.03.01 for more details). The internal forces at time n are computed at the beginning of the time step from the result coming from the previous time step. For the first time step, one automatically passes to a relative criterion of type RESI_GLOB_RELA, or even to an absolute criterion for the cases where the loading is zero. This criterion is of interest only for problems of evolutionary type (THM) in which there reside strong contrasts between the various unknowns. The criterion RESI_REFE_RELA= \varepsilon_{refe} leads one to estimate the convergence of Newton's algorithm in the following way. From one or more reference quantities, defined by zones (mesh-cell groups): - A stress SIGM for standard finite elements or for grid and membrane elements; - A strain EPSI for incompressible elements or for second-gradient elements; - An internal variable VARI if one uses non-local laws with gradient of internal variables; - A Lagrange multiplier LAGR if one uses mixed elements; - A thermal flux FLUXTHER in a THM case; - Two hydraulic fluxes FLUXHYD1 and FLUXHYD2 in an HHM case; - A displacement DEPL if one uses joint or interface elements with a constitutive behaviour of CZM type; - A force EFFORT and a moment MOMENT if one uses structural elements (discrete elements, bars, beams or cables); - A line force EFFORT and a line moment MOMENT if one uses 2D structural elements (plates and shells); One computes a residual reference {F}^{\mathit{ref}} (a vector of the same length as the residual vector). défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Contents of the data structure EVOL_NOLI The data structure EVOL_NOLI contains the list of the fields archived during the analysis (according to the various options of the keyword ARCHIVAGE). By default, it contains, for each time instant, the list of the following fields: - DEPL: field (at the nodes) of the displacements; - SIEF_ELGA: field (at the Gauss points) of the stresses; - VARI_ELGA: field (at the Gauss points) of the internal variables; - COMPORTEMENT: map of the constitutive behaviour. This map contains information on the non-linear constitutive behaviour used; it is not readable when one prints it in MED format. In addition to these fields, the data structure also contains parameters. At each time instant, one stores at least: | Name | Origin keyword | Description | Type | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | INST | | Value of the analysis time instant | R | | EXCIT | EXCIT | Information on the loadings | K24 | | MODELE | MODELE | Model | K8 | | CARAELEM | CARA_ELEM | Elementary characteristics | K8 | | CHAMPMAT | CHAM_MATER | Material field | K8 | 3 General parameters The general parameters describe the model, the material field and the elementary characteristics (in particular for the structural elements). MODELE is the name of the model whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. The data structure comes from the command U4.41.01. It is always mandatory. CHAM_MATER is the name of the material field assigned on the model. The data structure comes from the command U4.43.01. All the main mesh cells of the model must be associated with a material. CARA_ELEM is the name of the characteristics of the shell, beam, pipe, bar, cable and discrete elements assigned on the model. The data structure comes from the command U4.42.01. Obviously, this keyword is optional: if the model does not contain such elements, it is not useful; on the other hand, if the model contains such elements, it is mandatory. 4 Parameterisation of the analysis The non-linear analysis is solved by an incremental method, so it is necessary to parameterise the analysis. One uses for this the time variable (denoted INST), even if it has no physical meaning in statics. The (pseudo)-temporal discretisation is managed by the factor keyword INCREMENT, which will define the time intervals taken in the incremental method. Note The time instants thus defined have a physical meaning only for constitutive relations in which time appears explicitly (viscoelastic or viscoplastic, for example). In the other cases, they only make it possible to index the load increments and to parameterise the evolution of a possible temperature field. 4.1 General definition of the list of time instants To supply the list of time instants, there are two ways of proceeding. 1/ One gives the list of time instants by the keyword LIST_INST. This list is given by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01. By default the operator will impose an automatic cutting of the time step. 2/ One may define the analysis time instants by the operator DEFI_LIST_INST U4.34.03 and manage simultaneously the automatic cutting of the time step and other advanced functionalities. To deactivate the automatic cutting, it is enough to impose the action ARRET in ECHEC: inst = DEFI_LIST_INST(DEFI_LIST=_F(LIST_INST=listr8), ECHEC=_F(EVENEMENT="ERREUR", ACTION="ARRET")) One must also recall that, by convention, the initial time instant of the analysis of a virgin analysis (without restart) is designated by the order number 0. Furthermore, the order numbers are necessarily increasing and without "gaps". 4.2 Management of restarts If one specifies nothing, the analysis will be carried out over all the time instants defined by LIST_INST. It is possible to manage this list more finely. The initial time instant of the analysis (which therefore is not (re)computed) is designated either by its value (INST_INIT), or by its order number in the list of time instants (NUME_INST_INIT). In the absence of the keywords INST_INIT or NUME_INST_INIT, the default is NUME_INST_INIT=0. The final time instant (last computed step) is designated in the same manner as the initial time instant (either NUME_INST_FIN, or INST_FIN), except that it is not possible to refer to the time instant of the initial state. - If the automatic recutting of the time step is activated, NUME_INST_FIN does not take it into account and always works on the initial list of time instants. NUME_INST_INIT and NUME_INST_FIN are active only at initialisation. - The list of time instants being strictly increasing, it may happen that certain time steps are not archived although they were requested. For example, in the case of a restart of an analysis. If the analysis in restart of a previous analysis has no time instant greater than the first phase of the analysis, no time step will be archived. Notes A - Simple example (default behaviour) listInst = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT=0., INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A= 10.,NOMBRE=10)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst, INST_FIN=4.)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(reuse=evolNoli, INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst), ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=evolNoli)) The first MECA_NON_LINE carries out the analysis for the time instants 1, 2, 3 and 4. The second MECA_NON_LINE: carries out the analysis for the time instants 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, the initial state corresponding to time 4. B - Example to show the interest of INST_INIT listInst = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT=0., INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A= 10.,NOMBRE=10)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst, INST_FIN=4.)), evolNoli = MECA_NON_LINE(reuse=evolNoli, INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=listInst, INST_INIT=8.), ETAT_INIT=_F(EVOL_NOLI=evolNoli)) First MECA_NON_LINE: carries out the analysis of the time instants 1 to 4. Second MECA_NON_LINE: carries out the analysis for the time instants 9 and 10 (one does nothing for t=5,6,7 and 8), the initial state corresponding to time 4. 4.3 Selection of the time instants The time instants in MECA_NON_LINE are located by an order number (an integer). If the user wants to use a time instant (a real) and not an order number for the selection, the keywords PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to identify this order number (see U4.71.00 for the detailed syntax). These parameters serve to locate the right order number (NUME_INST_FIN/NUME_INST_INIT) when the user supplies the time instant (INST_FIN/INST_INIT). Let the following list of time instants be: | NUME | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | INST | 0.0010 | 0.0020 | 0.0030 | 0.0040 | 0.0050 | 0.0060 | 0.0070 | If the user wants to select the time instant corresponding to NUME=4, it is enough to say INST=0.0040. Let us take another example | NUME | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | INST | 0.10000001 | 0.10000002 | 0.10000003 | 0.10000004 | 0.10000005 | 0.10000006 | 0.10000007 | If the user wants to select the time instant corresponding to NUME=4, it is not enough to say INST=0.10000004, because the relative gap between the time instants is \frac{0,10000005-0,10000004}{0,10000004}=1,0\times 10^{-7} which is smaller than the default precision value ( 1,0\times 10^{-6} ). One will therefore not be able to distinguish NUME=3, 4 and 5 (the code then stops in fatal error). It is then enough to change the parameter PRECISION in order to be able to select the time instant (in our example, PRECISION=1E-8 will be suitable). 5 Settings of the non-linear solvers 5.1 Choice of the method There exist three broad categories of accessible non-linear solvers: - the Newton method (and its variants); - the non-linear solvers called SNES (Scalable Nonlinear Equations Solvers) of the PETSC library; - the solver RASPEN (Restricted Additive Schwarz Preconditioned Exact Newton), which is based on a non-linear domain-decomposition approach. The solver is selected by the keyword METHODE. 5.2 Newton method and its variants When METHODE="NEWTON", one uses the Newton-Raphson algorithm to solve the problem (see R5.03.01). It is the factor keyword NEWTON (a single occurrence) which makes it possible to set the various parameters. The prediction phase (Cf. R5.03.01) aims to compute an estimate of the displacement field in order to allow Newton's method to converge more rapidly. When the keyword is absent, it is the rate tangent matrix (option RIGI_MECA_TANG) which is used if one has chosen for Newton's method a PREDICTION='TANGENTE', and it is the elastic matrix (option RIGI_MECA) which is used if one has chosen PREDICTION='ELASTIQUE'. The keyword REAC_INCR=mf makes it possible to control the frequency of updating of the matrix with respect to the time steps. - If the matrix used in prediction corresponds to the elastic computation, it is evaluated only once at the initial time instant, at the start of the algorithm, unless the elastic characteristics depend on time or on a command variable such as the temperature, which depends on time - This "elastic" matrix is computed using the Young's modulus given under the keyword ELAS of the operator U4.43.01, and not the slope at the origin of the tensile curve given under the keyword TRACTION (and which, for its part, serves in the expression of the constitutive relations VMIS_ISOT_TRAC, VMIS_ECMI_TRAC and VISC_ISOT_TRAC) Notes The matrix used for the global iterations of the method is the (consistent) tangent matrix R5.03.01 if MATRICE='TANGENTE' or the elastic matrix if MATRICE='ELASTIQUE'. The keyword REAC_ITER=it makes it possible to control the frequency of updating of the matrix with respect to the Newton iterations. Thus at the first Newton iteration, one reassembles the tangent matrix only if it equals 1: otherwise one keeps the matrix used in the prediction phase. By convention, if it equals 0 the matrix is not re-evaluated during the whole time step. 5.3 Method SNES When METHODE="SNES", one calls the non-linear solver SNES of the PETSC library. It is a very generic implementation of numerous different solvers, ranging from the classical Newton method to the BFGS method or the Picard method, as well as all the possible combinations of the latter (see [bib1]_). The parameterisation is done by a list of options transmitted in the form of character strings by the keyword OPTION_PETSC of the factor keyword SOLVEUR (see U4.50.01). Its use is reserved for advanced users. 5.4 Method RASPEN The method RASPEN is based on a non-linear domain-decomposition method. It is usable only in the HPC context. It relies on 2 levels of non-linear solvers: - a local level, where a non-linear problem is solved on each subdomain, without communication with its neighbours and therefore in a parallel and asynchronous manner; - a global level, which exploits the previous local solutions in order to facilitate the solution of the problem considered. As for the method SNES , the parameterisation is done by a list of options transmitted in the form of character strings by the keyword OPTION_PETSC of the factor keyword SOLVEUR. The options which concern the local solver are prefixed by lsnes_ whereas the options which concern the global solver are prefixed by gsnes_ . One may conveniently define these options as follows: myOptions = ( # local snes "-prefix_push lsnes_ " + "-snes_monitor -snes_linesearch_type basic -snes_rtol 1.e-8 -snes_atol 1.e-50 -snes_max_it 5 " + "-ksp_type preonly -pc_type lu -pc_factor_mat_solver_type mumps " + "-prefix_pop " # global snes + "-prefix_push gsnes_ " + "-snes_linesearch_type basic -ksp_monitor -ksp_rtol 1.e-7 -ksp_atol 1.e-50 -snes_max_it 20 " + "-prefix_pop " ) The first line expresses the fact that one is going to parameterise the non-linear solver local to each subdomain, called "lsnes" ("l" for local, "snes" for Scalable Nonlinear Equations Solvers). Next, one expresses that one wants to monitor the local non-linear solver, which by default is Newton's method; one specifies that the line search is not used (basic means that one uses a step of 1.) and one gives the relative and absolute convergence criteria as well as the maximum number of iterations. Next one expresses that one wishes to use the MUMPS solver to solve the linearised problems. One then does the same for the global non-linear solver called "gsnes". For any further detail, the reader is referred to [bib2]_. Its use is reserved for advanced users. 5.5 Line search The line search may make it possible to improve the convergence of Newton's method (Cf. [R5.03.01] for more details). Note: It is inadvisable to use the line search with the GROT_GDEP strains, for the modellings COQUE_3D and in the presence of contact. This keyword makes it possible to choose the line-search method, that is to say the algorithm for searching for the zero of the functional (see R5.03.01). The method is a one-dimensional secant method. The parameters ITER_LINE_MAXI=itelin and RESI_LINE_RELA=reslin are the parameters of the line search. One gives the maximum number of iterations itelin to be carried out and the precision reslin to be reached in order to achieve convergence of the line search. The keywords RHO_MIN, RHO_MAX and RHO_EXCL set the interval I in which one computes the coefficient \rho of the line search, in the form I=[\rho_{min},\rho_{max}]-[-\rho_{exc},\rho_{exc}] 6.1 Settings of the convergence The factor keyword CONVERGENCE makes it possible to control the convergence parameters of the analysis. The keyword ITER_GLOB_MAXI gives the maximum number of iterations carried out to solve the global problem at each time instant. An excessive increase of this parameter is generally the sign of a problem in the modelling or of an inadequate temporal discretisation. There exist two convergence criteria: RESI_GLOB_RELA in relative form and RESI_GLOB_MAXI in absolute form. If one supplies nothing, then everything proceeds as if RESI_GLOB_RELA = 1.E-6. For RESI_GLOB_MAXI=resmax, the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as where {F}^{n} is the residual of iteration n (Cf. R5.03.01 for more details). If this operand is absent, the test is not carried out. For RESI_GLOB_RELA=resrel, the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as: \underset{i=1, \dots , \mathrm{nbddl}}{\max} {F}^{n} > \text{resrel} . {\max} L where L is the vector of the imposed loading and of the support reactions (Cf. R5.03.01 for more details). When the loading and the support reactions become zero, that is to say when L is zero (for example in the case of a total unloading), RESI_GLOB_RELA is displayed as -1, and one tries to switch from the relative convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_RELA to the absolute convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_MAXI. This operation is transparent for the user (alarm message issued in the .mess file). When the vector L becomes non-zero again, one automatically switches back to the relative convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_RELA. However, this switching mechanism cannot work at the first time step. Indeed, in order to find a reasonable value of RESI_GLOB_MAXI automatically (since the user has not supplied it), one needs to have had at least one converged step on a RESI_GLOB_RELA mode. Consequently, if the loading is zero from the first time instant, the analysis stops. The user must then already check that the zero loading is normal from the point of view of the modelling being carried out, and if such is the case, find another convergence criterion (RESI_GLOB_MAXI for example). If RESI_GLOB_RELA and RESI_GLOB_MAXI are both present, both tests are carried out. 6.2 Advanced convergence criteria The criterion RESI_REFE_RELA \varepsilon_{refe} leads one to estimate the convergence of Newton's algorithm in the following manner. Starting from a reference, which may be: - A stress SIGM_REFE - A strain EPSI_REFE for incompressible elements, grid elements and membrane elements; - An internal variable VARI_REFE if one uses non-local laws with strain gradient; - A thermal flux FLUX_THER_REFE in a THM case; - Two hydraulic fluxes FLUX_HYD1_REFE and FLUX_HYD2_REFE in an HHM case; - A displacement DEPL_REFE if one uses joint elements with a constitutive behaviour of type CZM; - A force EFFORT_REFE and a moment MOMENT_REFE if one uses structural elements (discrete elements, bars, beams or cables); - A line force EFFORT_REFE and a line moment MOMENT_REFE if one uses 2D structural elements (plates and shells); One computes a residual reference {F}^{\mathit{ref}} (a vector of the same length as the residual vector). Convergence will be achieved if and only if: \forall i \in [1, \dots, \mathit{nbddl} ] \mid {F}_{i}^{n}\mid The table will contain at most 16 columns. | NOM_OBSERVATION | K80 | Name given automatically or by the keyword TITRE | | --- | --- | --- | | TYPE_OBJET | K16 | The table contains only real values, hence R | | NOM_SD | K24 | ' ' | | NUME_REUSE | I | Index of reuse of the table in the case of REUSE | | NUME_OBSE | I | Order number of the observation | | INST | R | Time instant of the observation | | NOM_CHAM | K16 | Name of the observed field | | EVAL_CHAM | K8 | Type of evaluation of the field | | NOM_CMP | K8 | Name of the observed component | | NOM_VARI | K16 | Name of the observed internal variable | | EVAL_CMP | K8 | Type of evaluation of the component | | NOEUD | K8 | Node at which the observation is carried out (field at the nodes) | | MAILLE | K8 | Mesh cell at which the observation is carried out (field at the mesh cells) | | EVAL_ELGA | K8 | Type of evaluation of the fields at the Gauss points | | POINT | I | Integration point at which the observation is carried out (fields at the mesh cells) | | SOUS_POINT | I | Integration sub-point at which the observation is carried out (fields at the mesh cells) | | VALE | R | Value | | NUME_GLOBAL_NOEUD | I | Number of the node at which the observation is carried out (field at the nodes) in the global numbering (caution: this numbering starts at zero). This column is added only in the case of the use of distributed parallelism, | The parameter NUME_REUSE serves in the case of enrichment of the result data structure. Indeed, if the restart overwrites old order numbers in the result data structure (see keyword ETAT_INIT), this is not the case for the values in the observation table, which is never modified retroactively. One may therefore have two different values for the same time instant in the table; the distinction will then be made on NUME_REUSE. 10 Loadings ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_meca / char_meca, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = / "DIDI", / "FIXE_CSTE" (par défaut), ), 10.1 General principles The factor keyword EXCIT makes it possible to describe at each occurrence a load (applied loads and boundary conditions), and possibly a multiplying coefficient and/or a type of load. The non-linear analysis is solved by an incremental method, so it is necessary to parameterise the analysis. One therefore also applies the loadings in an incremental manner, for example by applying the force progressively (a ramp). The basic principle is to separate the spatial part of the loading and the (pseudo)-temporal part. \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( {\underline{u}, t} \right ) = g \left ( t \right ) \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( \underline{u} \right ) The spatial part of the loading \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( \underline{u} \right ) is given by the keyword CHARGE (possibly comprising the evolution of a temperature field). - In a thermo-mechanical analysis, if the initial temperature is different from the reference temperature (given in U4.43.01), the associated strain field at the initial time instant may be incompatible and therefore lead to an associated non-zero state of stresses and of internal variables. If one uses an incremental constitutive relation and if one does not explicitly define an initial state of stresses and of internal variables (associated with an initial temperature field different from the reference temperature), the stress field and the field of internal variables computed at the first increment will take into account only the variation of temperature between the initial time instant and the first time instant, and not the possible compatibility stresses associated with the initial temperature. In order to take this initial state into account, one must give it explicitly, for example thanks to the keywords in ETAT_INIT. In order to avoid such situations, which may lead to analysis errors, it is better to start an analysis by considering that one must start from a virgin state. - If one carries out an analysis in axisymmetry and one imposes nodal forces, these forces must be divided by 2\pi (one works on a sector of one radian) with respect to the real loadings. Likewise, if one wishes to compute the resultant of the forces, the result is to be multiplied by 2\pi in order to have the total resultant on the complete structure. Likewise in plane stresses or in plane strain, one works on a unit thickness: the forces (over the thickness) applied must be divided by the thickness; the real forces are obtained by multiplying by the thickness the forces of the analysis. Notes The temporal part of the loading g \left ( t \right ) is given by the keyword FONC_MULT. If one does not specify the multiplying function, one applies a step function. It is possible to define directly \underline{L}_{ext} \left ( {\underline{u}, t} \right ) in the keyword CHARGE if one uses the command AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F (function of time). In this case, one must be careful: indeed, if one uses FONC_MULT at the same time, one multiplies the loading again by a function of time. By default, TYPE_CHARGE equals 'FIXE_CSTE': this corresponds to a loading applied on the initial geometry and not piloted. It may however be a function, and, in particular, depend on time. A fixed loading is re-evaluated only at each new time instant, and only if it depends on time (defined in AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F and parameterised by the time instant, or else assigned by FONC_MULT). 10.2 Incremental loadings If TYPE_CHARGE='DIDI' then the Dirichlet conditions (imposed displacements, linear conditions) will apply to the displacement increment from the time instant given under ETAT_INIT/NUME_DIDI (by default the time instant of restart of the analysis) and not to the total displacement. For example, for an imposed displacement (keyword DDL_IMPO of AFFE_CHAR_MECA) the condition will be of the form u-{u}_{0}=d where {u}_{0} is the displacement defined by NUME_DIDI and not u=d . The differential Dirichlet option is available both for mechanical loadings (CHAR_MECA) and for kinematic loadings (CHAR_CINE). 11 Contact The factor keyword CONTACT makes it possible to introduce the contact/friction conditions. 11.1 Passing of the parameters linked to the definition of the contact The user defines the contact (surfaces in contact, formulation used, etc.) by means of the operator DEFI_CONT. Then, this concept is supplied to the command MECA_NON_LINE by means of the keyword DEFINITION. 11.2 Choice and control of the global solution algorithm Within the framework of the simulation of frictional contact, it is necessary to treat the geometric non-linearity. The choice of the algorithm used is made using the keyword ALGO_RESO_GEOM. Two choices are possible: - a solution by a global Newton algorithm (ALGO_RESO_GEOM='NEWTON'): in this case, at each Newton iteration, one carries out the pairing on the current configuration, - a solution by a so-called fixed-point algorithm (ALGO_RESO_GEOM='POINT_FIXE'): in this case, one carries out a certain number of solutions for a given pairing, before pairing again. The management of the criterion used to manage the pairing is done in this case using REAC_GEOM. Indeed, the fixed-point algorithm requires one to specify the condition which will trigger a new pairing. This condition is managed by the keyword REAC_GEOM. Various options exist for the user: - REAC_GEOM=’AUTOMATIQUE’: the updating of the geometry (pairing) is controlled by a geometric convergence criterion (RESI_GEOM). This criterion controls the variation of the geometry between two iterates. When the criterion is reached, one updates the geometry. This is the recommended option. In this case, the user has a convergence criterion on this parameter, using a tolerance to be supplied (RESI_GEOM) and a maximum number of iterations (ITER_GEOM_MAXI). - REAC_GEOM='CONTROLE': the updating of the geometry is done after a certain fixed number of iterations. This number is supplied by the user using the parameter NB_ITER_GEOM. For example, if NB_ITER_GEOM=2, then one updates the geometry every two Newton iterations. - REAC_GEOM='SANS': in this case, one never updates the geometry, and one always works on the initial configuration. This option is valid only under the assumption of small perturbations or when the normal to the contact surfaces does not change during the analysis. Other printouts are made systematically during the non-linear analysis, independently of the value assigned to the keyword INFO: they are the printouts of the residuals and of the relative displacement increments during the Newton iterations. u4.51.05 Command CALC_MECA_MULT u4.51.05 Command CALC_MECA_MULT 1 Purpose The role of the command CALC_MECA_MULT is to compute the thermomechanical responses of a mechanical model for different cases of thermal loads. CHAM_MATER is the name of the material field assigned to the model supplied in MODELE. CARA_ELEM contains additional characteristics for the shell, beam, pipe, bar, cable and discrete elements. This keyword is optional. 3.2 Operand CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL Concept of type charge produced by the commands AFFE_CHAR_MECA, AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F, AFFE_CHAR_CINE or AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F. This keyword makes it possible to define the mechanical loading common to all the load cases defined by the user. 3.3 Operand LIST_INST This keyword serves to supply a list of the analysis time instants so that it is common to all the load cases. This list is defined in the concept of type litpsr8 by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL or in the concept litps by the operator DEFI_LIST_INST. When this keyword is not supplied, the temporal discretisation chosen for each load case is identical to the discretisation of the corresponding thermal field. The time instants are automatically recovered and may therefore be different for each load case. When this keyword is supplied, it is the time instants supplied in this keyword and only these time instants which are taken into account. 3.4 Operand CAS_CHARGE This factor keyword makes it possible to define each load case by supplying a result data structure coming from a thermal analysis, a name for the case, and possibly a reference value. 3.4.1 Operand EVOL_THER This keyword makes it possible to supply the thermal result to be used as loading. This may be a result data structure of type evol_ther or a composite data structure of type evol_ther_dict which may come from the command CALC_THER_MULT. 3.4.2 Operand NOM_CAS Character string serving as the access variable to the result data structure. This operand is useful only if the result supplied in the keyword EVOL_THER is not a result of type evol_ther_dict. 3.4.3 Operand VALE_REFE This keyword makes it possible to define the reference temperature for the load case considered, the temperature for which there is no thermal strain. By default this value is chosen as 0°C. Caution: in the case of the analysis of a response to a unit shock for numerical analysis methods, the choice of a temperature different from 0°C may lead to unexpected results. For the definition of this value, one may refer to the documentation concerning the materials; VALE_REFE in AFFE_MATERIAU. 3.5 Keyword CONVERGENCE See the keyword CONVERGENCE of STAT_NON_LINE. 3.6 Keyword SOLVEUR See the documentation of SOLVEUR. 3.7 Keyword NEWTON A Newton-Raphson algorithm is used; see the documentation of the Newton method.
