Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "RCMK", / "SANS" (par défaut), ), ◇ INFO = int (défaut: 1), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keywords MATR_MASS and MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_MASS Real, symmetric assembled matrix of type [matr_asse_depl_r]. ♦ MATR_RIGI Real, symmetric assembled matrix of type [matr_asse_depl_r]. 3.2 Keyword ETAT_INIT ◊ ETAT_INIT Under this factor keyword, one can supply a periodic solution in order to initialise the algorithm for computing the non-linear modes. 3.2.1 Operand MODE_LINE ◊ MODE_LINE Structure of type mode_meca produced by an analysis with the operator CALC_MODES. This keyword is not valid if the keyword MODE_NON_LINE is present. 3.2.2 Operand MODE_NON_LINE ◊ MODE_NON_LINE Structure of type table_container produced by an analysis with the operator MODE_NON_LINE. This keyword is not valid if the keyword MODE_LINE is present. 3.2.3 Operand NUME_ORDRE ◊ NUME_ORDRE If the keyword MODE_LINE is present then num_ordr indicates the order number of the linear eigenmode coming from mode_line chosen to initialise the algorithm. If the keyword MODE_NON_LINE is present then num_ordr indicates the order number of the periodic solution coming from resu_in chosen to initialise the algorithm. 3.2.4 Operand DIR_EVOLUTION ◊ DIR_EVOLUTION If 1 then one goes in the same direction as the first tangent vector computed. If -1 then one goes in the direction opposite to the first tangent vector computed. The default value is -1. 3.2.5 Operand COEF_AMPL ◊ COEF_AMPL ampl is the maximum amplitude given to the periodic solution chosen to initialise the algorithm. This value is useful when one initialises with a linear eigenmode, where the maximum amplitude must be small for the algorithm to converge. The default value is 1. 3.3 Keyword CHOC ◊ CHOC Under this factor keyword, one supplies the configuration and the physical parameters corresponding to the impact non-linearity that one wants to impose. 3.3.1 Operand JEU ♦ JEU jeu is the distance between the node and the elastic stop against which it can come into contact. 3.3.2 Operand RIGI_NOR ♦ RIGI_NOR alpha is the stiffness of the elastic stop. 3.3.3 Operand PARA_REGUL ◊ PARA_REGUL eta is the parameter making it possible to regularise the constitutive law that governs the relation between the node and the elastic stop. The default value is 0.005. 3.3.4 Operand GROUP_NO ◊ GROUP_NO grno is the name of the node group on which the non-linearity is located. Note that grno must contain only a single node. 3.3.5 Operand OBSTACLE ◊ OBSTACLE Three possibilities: 'PLAN', which corresponds to a unilateral elastic stop. 'BI_PLAN', which corresponds to a bilateral elastic stop. 'CERCLE', which corresponds to an elastic stop of circular shape. 3.3.6 Operand ORIG_OBST ◊ ORIG_OBST This keyword is available only in the case where OBSTACLE = 'CERCLE'. It defines the Cartesian coordinates of the centre of the circle in the local frame whose origin is the impact node. 3.3.7 Operand NOM_CMP ◊ NOM_CMP If OBSTACLE = 'PLAN', or OBSTACLE = 'BI_PLAN' then this keyword indicates on which axis, 'DX', 'DY' or 'DZ', the stop is located. If OBSTACLE = 'CERCLE', then this keyword indicates in which plane the stop is located. Plane Oxy: ('DX','DY'), Plane Oyz: ('DY','DZ'), Plane Oxz: ('DX','DZ') 3.4 Keyword RESOLUTION ♦ RESOLUTION Under this factor keyword, one supplies the type of algorithm and the associated parameters. The available methods are to be declared under the operand METHODE. 3.4.1 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE Choice of the algorithm for computing the non-linear modes. The only algorithm currently available is 'EHMAN', corresponding to the combination of the harmonic-balance method (EH) and the asymptotic numerical method (MAN), together with a Newton algorithm. The latter makes it possible to ensure the convergence of the algorithm. 3.4.2 Operand NB_HARM_LINE ♦ NB_HARM_LINE Hl is the number of harmonics used to expand, in the form of a Fourier series, the displacement variables. 3.4.3 Operand NB_HARM_NONL Hnl is the number of harmonics used to expand, in the form of a Fourier series, the functions representative of the constitutive laws that govern the relation between the node and the elastic stop. The following condition Hnl>Hl must be satisfied. The default value is 201. 3.4.4 Operand NB_BRANCHE nbra is the number of branches computed by the MAN. 3.4.5 Operand NB_PAS_MAN npas is the discretisation step of the branches computed by the MAN. 3.4.6 Operand NB_ORDRE_MAN nordre is the discretisation number of the branches computed by the MAN. The default value is 20. 3.4.7 Operand PREC_MAN eps_man is the tolerance of the MAN algorithm. The default value is 1.E-9. 3.4.8 Operand PREC_NEWTON eps_newt is the tolerance of the Newton algorithm. The default value is 1.E-8. 3.4.9 Operand ITER_NEWTON_MAXI iter_newt is the maximum number of iterations of the Newton algorithm. The default value is 15. 3.4.10 Operand CRIT_ORDR_BIFURCATION crit_bif is the number of coefficients of the power series coming from the MAN. The bifurcation analysis is performed on these points. The default value is 3. 3.4.11 Operand RESI_RELA_BIFURCATION ◊ RESI_RELA_BIFURCATION eps_bif is the tolerance of the criterion that makes it possible to decide whether or not a bifurcation is present. The default value is 1.E-4. 3.5 Keyword SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR The syntax of this keyword, common to several commands, is described in the document U4.50.01. 3.6 Keyword INFO ◊ INFO Integer making it possible to specify the print level in the MESSAGE file. If INFO=1, only the number of the branch computed is reported. If INFO=2, one also displays the relative error of the last point of the branch. As well as the error for each possible Newton iteration. And finally, the energy and the frequency of the first and of the last point of the branch.

u4.52.11 Operator NORM_MODE u4.52.11 Operator NORM_MODE 1 Purpose The role of the command is to normalise eigenmodes according to a criterion chosen by the user. The modal analysis operator CALC_MODES U4.52.02 produces a concept of type mode_meca or mode_meca_c whose real or complex eigenmodes are normalised in such a way that the largest of the components which is not a LAGRANGE multiplier is equal to 1. The operator NORM_MODE allows the user to choose another normalisation method, for example generalised mass, generalised stiffness ... Depending on the normalisation chosen, the modal parameters (participation factor, effective mass, ...) are updated. Re-entrant operator. 2 Syntax / mode_flamb / mode_meca / mode_meca_c = NORM_MODE( ◇ reuse = , ◆ MODE = mode_flamb / mode_meca, ◆ / NORME = / "EUCL", / "EUCL_TRAN", / "MASS_GENE", / "RIGI_GENE", / "TRAN", / "TRAN_ROTA", / GROUP_NO = grno, / AVEC_CMP = text, / SANS_CMP = text, # Si: exists("GROUP_NO") ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ MODE_SIGNE = _F( ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ SIGNE = / "NEGATIF", / "POSITIF" (par défaut), ), ◇ MASSE = matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_r, ◇ RAIDE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_r, ◇ AMOR = matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_r, ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODE ♦ MODE = m_in Name of the concept of type mode_ whose eigenmode normalisation one wants to change. If m_out is identical to m_in and if the keyword 'reuse' is activated with the value m_out, the renormalisation is done in place. 3.2 Operand NORME ◊ / NORME = Symbolic name of the chosen norm. - 'MASS_GENE' : The modes are normalised to unit generalised mass. - 'RIGI_GENE' : The modes are normalised to unit generalised stiffness. - 'TRAN' : The modes are normalised to 1. for the largest of the translation components (components: DX, DY, DZ). - 'TRAN_ROTA' : The modes are normalised to 1. for the largest of the translation and rotation components (components: DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ). - 'EUCL' : The modes are normalised to the Euclidean norm of the components which are not Lagrange multipliers (component: LAGR). - 'EUCL_TRAN' : The modes are normalised to the Euclidean norm of the translation components (components: DX, DY, DZ). 3.3 Operands GROUP_NO and NOM_CMP ◊ GROUP_NO = grno Name of the group of one node \mathit{grno} where one normalises. | Warning: the node group \mathit{grno} must contain a single node. ♦ NOM_CMP = cmp Name of the normalisation component at the node \mathit{no} or at the group of one node \mathit{grno} . This operand is mandatory if GROUP_NO is supplied. The modes are normalised to 1. for the component \mathit{cmp} of the node \mathit{no} or of the group of one node \mathit{grno} . 3.4 Operands AVEC_CMP/SANS_CMP ◊ / AVEC_CMP = a_cmp a_cmp list of the names of the components used for the normalisation. The modes are normalised to 1. for the largest of the components of the list a_cmp whatever the node. / SANS_CMP = s_cmp s_cmp list of the names of the components which are not used for the normalisation. The modes are normalised to 1. for the largest of the components which is not in the list s_cmp. 3.5 Factor keyword MODE_SIGNE This factor keyword makes it possible to impose, for all the modes, the sign of a component of a node stipulated by the user. This factor keyword can be used only for real modes (generalised problem). ♦ GROUP_NO = grnd Name of the group of one node where one imposes the sign of a component. | Warning: the node group \mathit{grnd} must contain a single node. ♦ NOM_CMP = cmp Name of the component of the group of one node \mathit{grnd} where the sign is imposed. ◊ SIGNE = / 'POSITIF' / 'NEGATIF' Imposed sign of the component: 'POSITIF' or 'NEGATIF'. 3.6 Case of the normalisation of a collection of modes coming from DEFI_BASE_MODALE If one wants to normalise a collection of modes (modal base) coming from DEFI_BASE_MODALE, one must supply the two matrices, of mass and of stiffness, making it possible to update the modal parameters: ◊ MASSE = masse [matr_asse_depl_r] ou [matr_asse_gene_r] ou [matr_asse_pres_r] ◊ RAIDE = masse [matr_asse_depl_r] ou [matr_asse_depl_c] ou [matr_asse_gene_r] ou [matr_asse_pres_r] Indeed, in this case, the information on the mass and stiffness matrices (and possibly the damping matrix) on which the modal base is based has been lost, or the modes may come from different sets of matrices. It is therefore necessary to recall them to the operator NORM_MODE. In the case of a base of complex modes, one must in addition give a damping matrix if one wants to normalise with respect to the generalised mass or to the generalised stiffness (cf paragraph 4.2). 3.7 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = t Title associated with the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.8 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = 1 ou 2 For each mode, the name of the old norm and the name of the new norm are indicated in the MESSAGE file. The printed names of the norms correspond to the keywords described in paragraphs 3.2, 3.3, 3.4. 4 Formulation of the normalisation rules The various norms used as well as the definition of the various modal parameters are listed in the reference documentation R5.01.03. 4.1 Real eigenmodes For modes of type mode_meca_r (real eigenmodes) the associated generalised eigenvalue problem is: (K-{\omega}^{2}M)x=(K-{(2\pi f)}^{2}M)x=0 where K,M are respectively the mass matrix and the stiffness matrix of the mechanical system. For the modellings ‘MECANIQUE’, one defines the components of the eigenvector: - translation components {u}^{T} - rotation components {u}^{R} - components of the LAGRANGE multipliers \lambda - other components (fluid pressure and potential) {p}_{f} One calls: - {u}^{\mathrm{TR}} the translation and rotation components, - u the components other than LAGRANGE multipliers. which leads to: {u}^{\text{ }}=\left[\begin{array}{}u\\ \lambda \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{}{u}^{T}\\ {u}^{R}\\ {p}_{f}\\ \lambda \end{array}\right] For models with translation and rotation components, the eigenmode {\phi }_{i} supplied by the modal-analysis algorithms is by default: {\Phi}_{i}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{maxu}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{max{u}^{\mathit{TR}}}={{\Phi}_{i}}^{\mathit{TR}} which is equivalent to the normalisation obtained by the keyword ‘TRAN_ROTA’. With the keyword ‘TRAN’ the mode obtained is defined by: {\Phi}_{i}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{max{u}^{T}}={{\Phi}_{i}}^{T} For models with translation components only, the normalisation is by default: {{\Phi}_{i}}^{T}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{maxu}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{max{u}^{T}} > which is equivalent to the normalisation obtained by the keyword ‘TRAN’. The default normalisation leads to the following generalised parameters: - generalised stiffness {}^{T}\Phi _{i}K{\Phi}_{i}={\gamma}_{i} - generalised mass {}^{T}\Phi _{i}M{\Phi}_{i}={\mu}_{i} - hence the eigen angular frequency {{\omega}_{i}}^{2}=\frac{{\gamma}_{i}}{{\mu}_{i}} The normalisation to unit generalised mass is obtained by the keyword ‘MASS_GENE’: {{\Phi}_{i}}^{M}=\frac{{\Phi}_{i}}{\sqrt{{\mu}_{i}}} hence {}^{T}{\Phi}_{i}^{M}M{{\Phi}_{i}}^{M}=1. and {}^{T}{\Phi}_{i}^{M}K{{\Phi}_{i}}^{M}={{\omega}_{i}}^{2} That to unit generalised stiffness is obtained by the keyword ‘RIGI_GENE’: {{\Phi}_{i}}^{K}=\frac{{\Phi}_{i}}{\sqrt{{\gamma}_{i}}} hence {}^{T}{\Phi}_{i}^{K}M{{\Phi}_{i}}^{K}=\frac{1}{{{\omega}_{i}}^{2}} and {}^{T}{\Phi}_{i}^{K}K{{\Phi}_{i}}^{K}=1. The normalisation of the eigenmode to the Euclidean norm ‘EUCL’ is obtained naturally by: {{\Phi}_{i}}^{\mathrm{\parallel }u\mathrm{\parallel }}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{\mathrm{\parallel }u\mathrm{\parallel }}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{\sqrt{\sum_{j}{({u}_{j})}^{2}}} The normalisation of the eigenmode to the Euclidean norm ‘EUCL_TRAN’ is: {{\Phi}_{i}}^{\mathrm{\parallel }{u}^{T}\mathrm{\parallel }}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{\mathrm{\parallel }{u}^{T}\mathrm{\parallel }}=\frac{{u}^{\text{ }}}{\sqrt{\sum_{j}{({u}_{j}^{T})}^{2}}} 4.2 Complex eigenmodes For modes of type mode_meca_c (complex eigenmodes) coming from the solution of a quadratic eigenvalue problem {\lambda}^{2}M+\lambda C+K=0 where C is the damping matrix of the mechanical system, one normalises the modes \Phi with respect to the associated linearised problem: (\lambda \left[\begin{array}{cc}0& M\\ M& C\end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{cc}-M& 0\\ 0& K\end{array}\right])(\begin{array}{c}\lambda \Phi \\ \Phi \end{array})=0 The eigenmode is normalised to unit generalised mass (‘MASS_GENE’), if {\Phi}_{i} satisfies: (\lambda {}^{T}\Phi _{i}{}^{T}\Phi _{i})\left\begin{array}{cc}0& M\\ M& C\end{array}\right=1. to unit generalised stiffness (‘RIGI_GENE’), if {\Phi}_{i} satisfies: (\lambda {}^{T}\Phi _{i}{}^{T}\Phi _{i})\left\begin{array}{cc}-M& 0\\ 0& K\end{array}\right=1. For the other norms, the definitions are equivalent to those defined for the real modes; it is sufficient to replace the scalar product by the Hermitian product. 5 Updated modal parameters A concept of type mode_meca can contain, for each mode, the following modal parameters (visible for example by printing the concept with the command IMPR_RESU in FORMAT='RESULTAT' with the option TOUT_PARA='OUI'): | Parameter heading in Code_Aster | Definition | | --- | --- | | FREQ | Eigenfrequency (damped, where applicable) | | AMOR_GENE | Generalised modal damping | | AMOR_REDUIT | Reduced modal damping | | FACT_PARTICI_D ( = X or Y or Z) | Participation factor of the mode in the direction D | | MASS_EFFE_D ( = X or Y or Z) | Effective modal mass in the direction D | | MASS_EFFE_UN_D ( = X or Y or Z) | Unit effective modal mass in the direction D | | MASS_GENE | Generalised mass of the mode | | OMEGA2 | Eigen angular frequency (damped, where applicable) squared | | RIGI_GENE | Generalised stiffness of the mode | Table 5.1: list of the modal parameters. These parameters are defined mathematically in the reference documentation R5.01.03. The operator NORM_MODE computes or updates the following modal parameters, which depend on the normalisation chosen: FACT_PARTICI_D , MASS_GENE and RIGI_GENE. It also enriches the data structure with the parameters MASS_EFFE_UN_D (independent of the normalisation). The other parameters are independent of the normalisation. 6 Examples for real modes For modes of type mode_meca (real eigenmodes) coming from the solution of a generalised eigenvalue problem (K-\lambda M)x=0 : - normalising an eigenvector x to unit generalised stiffness is equivalent to x satisfying {x}^{T}Kx=1 Normalisation with duplication of the mode_meca concept: mo_2 = NORM_MODE(MODE = mo_1, NORME='RIGI_GENE'); - normalising an eigenvector x to unit generalised mass is equivalent to x satisfying {x}^{T}Mx=1 Normalisation to unit generalised mass, with overwriting of the mode_meca concept: mo = NORM_MODE(reuse = mo, MODE = mo, NORME = 'MASS_GENE');

u4.52.12 Operator EXTR_MODE u4.52.12 Operator EXTR_MODE 1 Purpose Selectively extract modes from modal data structures. The modes are selected according to a criterion of a modal-parameter value greater than a certain threshold, then concatenated into a single final data structure. One can also print in the MESSAGE file a summary table of the cumulative sums of the unit effective modal masses or of the generalised masses of the modes retained. Produces a data structure of type mode_meca or mode_gene according to the type of the modes on input. 2 Syntax / mode_gene / mode_meca / mode_meca_c = EXTR_MODE( ◆ FILTRE_MODE = _F( ◆ MODE = mode_gene / mode_meca / mode_meca_c, ◆ / TOUT_ORDRE = / "NON", / "OUI", / NUME_ORDRE = int, / NUME_MODE = int, / NUME_MODE_EXCLU = int, / FREQ_MIN = float, / CRIT_EXTR = / "INER_EFFE", / "INER_EFFE_UN", / "MASS_EFFE", / "MASS_EFFE_UN", / "MASS_GENE", # Si: exists("FREQ_MIN") ◆ FREQ_MAX = float, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), # Si: exists("CRIT_EXTR") ◆ | SEUIL = float, | SEUIL_X = float, | SEUIL_Y = float, | SEUIL_Z = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ IMPRESSION = _F( ◇ CUMUL = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ CRIT_EXTR = / "INER_EFFE", / "INER_EFFE_UN", / "MASS_EFFE", / "MASS_EFFE_UN" (par défaut), / "MASS_GENE", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword FILTRE_MODE One repeats this keyword as many times as there are data structures of type mode_meca_ or mode_gene to filter and to concatenate. 3.2 Operand MODE Name of the mode_meca_ or mode_gene data structure to be sorted and concatenated with the others. 3.3 Filtering of the modes To filter the modes, three possibilities are offered to the user. 3.3.1 Operands NUME_MODE / NUME_ORDRE / TOUT_ORDRE List of the order numbers or of the modal positions of the modes that one wishes to keep. 3.3.2 Operand NUME_MODE_EXCLU List of the modal positions of the modes that one wishes to delete. 3.3.3 Operands FREQ_MIN / FREQ_MAX / PRECISION One keeps all the modes that correspond to frequencies lying between f_min and f_max to the relative precision prec. One must have f_min less than f_max. 3.3.4 Operand CRIT_EXTR Choice of the parameter that serves as the criterion for filtering the modes. The parameters are defined in the reference documentation R5.01.03. If the criterion is 'MASS_EFFE_UN' or 'MASS_EFFE' a mode will be retained as soon as one of its unit, or non-unit, directional effective modal masses is greater than a threshold set by the user. If the criterion is 'INER_EFFE_UN' or 'INER_EFFE' a mode will be retained as soon as one of its unit, or non-unit, directional effective modal inertias is greater than a threshold set by the user. If the criterion is 'MASS_GENE' a mode will be retained as soon as the ratio of the generalised mass to the sum of the generalised masses of the modes of the filtered structure is greater than a threshold set by the user. These criteria are meaningful only for data structures of type mode_meca_ . 3.3.5 Operands SEUIL, SEUIL_X, SEUIL_Y, SEUIL_Z Limit value of the criterion below which one considers that the mode can be filtered. This value, in the case of the parameters currently taken into account, is a dimensionless relative value. One can apply the same threshold in all directions (keyword SEUIL) or differentiate the thresholds according to the directions X , Y or Z (SEUIL_X, SEUIL_Y, SEUIL_Z) 3.4 Keyword IMPRESSION This keyword makes it possible to print a cumulative table of certain parameters. These parameters may be different from those chosen in the keywords FILTRE_MODE. 3.4.1 Operand CUMUL Printing or not printing the cumulative sums of the modal parameter retained by CRIT_EXTR for the result data structure resu_mod. 3.4.2 Operand CRIT_EXTR Choice of the print parameter for which one performs the cumulative operation. If the criterion is 'MASS_EFFE_UN' (unit effective mass), one cumulates separately the values of the parameters 'MASS_EFFE_UN_DX', 'MASS_EFFE_UN_DY', 'MASS_EFFE_UN_DZ' (unit effective modal mass in the direction D ) of the extracted modes. If the criterion is 'MASS_GENE' one cumulates the values of the parameter MASS_GENE (generalised mass) of the extracted modes. The parameters mentioned in this paragraph are defined more precisely in the reference documentation R5.01.03. 3.5 Keyword TITRE Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 4 Execution One checks that the parameter for which one performs the filtering does indeed exist in the input data structure mod. If this parameter is not supplied, one exits in fatal error. On the other hand, for the keyword IMPRESSION, if the parameters MASS_EFFE_UN_ are not supplied, one only issues an alarm. On output, the concept produced resu_mod must not be empty, otherwise one exits in fatal error. One also checks that all the mode_meca_ or mode_gene concepts are of the same type and that they come from the same initial problem (same matrices). After having filtered the modes of interest, one checks that they all have a different modal position. Otherwise, one issues an alarm message. To delete these duplicated modes, one must use the command EXTR_MODE again and activate the operand NUME_MODE_EXCLU. To date, one does not check that the data structures of type mode_meca_ correspond to one and the same norm. 5 Printout examples If the factor keyword IMPRESSION is present, the operator EXTR_MODE writes in the MESSAGE file a certain number of parameters on the extracted modes. Example of a printout, with the keywords CRIT_EXTR='MASS_EFFE_UN' and CUMUL='OUI': -------------------------------------------------------------------- CONCEPT MODESX DE TYPE MODE_MECA ISSU DE L OPERATEUR EXTR_MODE M A S S E E F NUME_ORDRE NUME_MODE FREQUENCE MASS_EFFE_UN_DX CUMUL_DX 1 1 2.66902D-01 4.12685D-02 4.12685D-02 2 11 6.49621D+01 1.18667D-01 1.59935D-01 3 19 2.56692D+02 1.02927D-02 1.70228D-01 -------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------- F E C T I V E U N I T A I R E MASS_EFFE_UN_DY CUMUL_DY MASS_EFFE_UN_DZ CUMUL_DZ 2.22156D-25 2.22156D-25 3.80903D-01 3.80903D-01 4.69363D-25 6.91519D-25 3.11195D-03 3.84015D-01 4.22168D-27 6.95741D-25 7.06977D-03 3.91085D-01 ---------------------------------------------------------- Le NUME_ORDRE est la position du mode dans la structure de donnée, le NUME_MODE est la position modale dans le spectre (cf. opérateur CALC_MODES [:external:ref: U4.52.02 ]). FREQUENCE est la fréquence propre du mode. MASS_EFFE_UN_D est la masse modale effective unitaire dans la direction ( = Xou You Z). Ces grandeurs sont définies dans la documentation de référence [:ref: R5.01.03 ]. CUMUL_ sont les sommes cumulées des masses effectives unitaires par direction. Exemple d'impression, avec les mot-clés CRIT_EXTR='MASS_GENE' et CUMUL='OUI': ------------------------------------------------------------------- CONCEPT MODESX DE TYPE MODE_MECA ISSU DE L OPERATEUR EXTR_MODE MASSE GENERALISEE NUME_ORDRE NUME_MODE FREQUENCE MASS_GENE CUMUL_MASS_GENE 1 1 2.66902D-01 1.00000D+00 1.00000D+00 2 11 6.49621D+01 1.00000D+00 2.00000D+00 3 19 2.56692D+02 1.00000D+00 3.00000D+00 ------------------------------------------------------------------- MASS_GENE est la masse généralisée du mode, définie dans la documentation de référence [:ref: R5.01.03 ]. CUMUL_MASS_GENE est la somme cumulée des masses généralisées. 6 Example of use Here is an example presenting the various possibilities of the command EXTR_MODE for a modal analysis carried out by 5 successive mode searches: Computation of the total mass of the structure (for checking) massestr = POST_ELEM (... MASS_INER = (...)); Computation of the first 17 frequencies (NUME_ORDRE from 1 to 17; NUME_MODE from 1 to 17) mode1 = CALC_MODES(MATR_RIGI = rigidité, MATR_MASS = masse, OPTION = 'PLUS_PETITE', CALC_FREQ = _F( NMAX_FREQ = 17 )) mode1 = NORM_MODE(MODE = mode1, reuse = mode1, NORME = 'TRAN_ROTA') Computation of other frequencies (NUME_ORDRE from 1 to 5; NUME_MODE from 18 to 22) mode2 = CALC_MODES(MATR_RIGI = rigidité, MATR_MASS = masse, OPTION = 'BANDE', CALC_FREQ =_F ( FREQ = (20. , 25.) ),) mode2 = NORM_MODE(MODE = mode2, reuse = mode2, NORME = 'TRAN_ROTA') Computation of other frequencies (NUME_ORDRE from 1 to 6; NUME_MODE from 23 to 28) mode3 = CALC_MODES (MATR_RIGI = rigidité, MATR_MASS = masse, OPTION = 'BANDE', CALC_FREQ =_F ( FREQ = (25. , 30.) ),) mode3 = NORM_MODE(MODE = mode3, reuse = mode3, NORME ='TRAN_ROTA',) Computation of other frequencies (NUME_ORDRE from 1 to 3; NUME_MODE from 28 to 30) mode4 = CALC_MODES(MATR_RIGI = rigidité, MATR_MASS = masse, OPTION = 'BANDE', CALC_FREQ =_F( FREQ = (29. , 32.) ),) mode4 = NORM_MODE(MODE = mode4, reuse = mode4, NORME ='TRAN_ROTA',) Computation of other frequencies (NUME_ORDRE from 1 to 6; NUME_MODE from 31 to 34) mode5 = CALC_MODES(MATR_RIGI = rigidité, MATR_MASS = masse, OPTION = 'BANDE', CALC_FREQ =_F ( FREQ = (32. , 35.) ),) mode5 = NORM_MODE(MODE = mode5, reuse = mode5, NORME = 'TRAN_ROTA') Extraction of the modes mode = EXTR_MODE(FILTRE_MODE =(_F(MODE = mode1, TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' ), _F(MODE = mode2, NUME_MODE = (18,19,20,21,22)), _F(MODE = mode3, FREQ_MIN = 25., FREQ_MAX = 30. ), _F(MODE = mode4, NUME_MODE_EXCLU = 28 ), _F(MODE = mode5, CRITERE = 'MASS_EFFE_UN', SEUIL = 0.005 ), ), IMPRESSION =_F ( CUMUL = 'OUI' ))

u4.52.13 Operator CALC_AMOR_MODAL u4.52.13 Operator CALC_AMOR_MODAL 1 Purpose Create a list of modal dampings computed according to the RCC-G rule. The analysis is performed in post-processing of the modal analysis of a building-type structure whose raft rests on a soil modelled by springs. The principle of the analysis is to weight, by the potential-energy ratios (with respect to the total energy), reduced dampings assigned by groups of mesh cells making up the structure (in fact input parameters of the potential-energy table created by POST_ELEM) and dampings radiated into the soil, by degree of freedom, as functions of the frequency [bib1] [bib2] R4.05.01. One also has the alternative possibility of directly creating a list of modal dampings by computed frequency of a concept of type mode_meca. This list depends both on the values of the frequencies of the mode and on the coefficients appearing in the expression of the Rayleigh damping. A mode of automatic correction of the computed dampings is also available. The list created can subsequently be used in the command DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 under the keyword LIST_AMOR. Produces a concept of type listr8. 2 Syntax listr8 = CALC_AMOR_MODAL( ◇ / AMOR_RAYLEIGH = _F( ◆ AMOR_ALPHA = float, ◆ AMOR_BETA = float, ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ), / ENER_SOL = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "RIGI_PARASOL", ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◆ / GROUP_NO_RADIER = grno, / GROUP_MA_RADIER = grma, ◇ / FONC_GROUP = formule / nappe / fonction, / COEF_GROUP = float, ◆ KX = float, ◆ KY = float, ◆ KZ = float, ◇ & KRX = float, & KRY = float, ◇ & KRZ = float, ◇ / GROUP_NO_CENTRE = grno, ◇ / COOR_CENTRE = float, ), ◇ / AMOR_INTERNE = _F( ◆ ENER_POT = table, ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ), ◇ / AMOR_SOL = _F( ◇ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◆ FONC_AMOR_GEO = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ HOMOGENE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.3), ), ◇ CORR_AMOR_NEGATIF = / "NON" (par défaut), / "IGNORE", / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("CORR_AMOR_NEGATIF", 'OUI') ◆ COEF_CORR_AMOR = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword ENER_SOL This factor keyword, used once only, is used to introduce the data required for the computation of the potential energy in the soil by degree of freedom for all the frequencies of a concept of type mode_meca. 3.1.1 Operand METHODE This operand makes it possible to define the method of computation of the energy in the soil by frequency. With the value 'DEPL', one computes the energy from the displacements averaged over the nodes of the raft for each mode: E=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1,6}{k}_{i}{U}_{i}^{2}{(\mathit{fr})}_{i} , where the {k}_{i} represent the 6 components KX, KY, KZ, KRX, KRY and KRZ of the global stiffness of the soil springs (cf. [§3.1.3]). With the value 'RIGI_PARASOL', one computes the energy from the forces averaged over the nodes of the raft for each mode: E=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1,6}\frac{{F}_{i}^{2}}{{k}_{i}}{(\mathit{fr})}_{i} . The nodal forces with this method are determined from the stiffness values distributed at the nodes under the raft as by the option RIGI_PARASOL of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01. 3.1.2 Operand MODE_MECA Makes it possible to introduce the concept of type mode_meca containing the frequencies of computation of the potential energy. 3.1.3 Operands KX / KY / KZ / KRX / KRY / KRZ Represent the values of the components of the global stiffness of the soil springs. They appear in the computation of the terms {k}_{i}.{U}_{i}^{2},i=1,\mathit{NCmp} , \mathrm{NCmp} is the number of components (3 or 6) determined by the presence or the absence of the operands KRX, KRY, KRZ, used (if they are) mandatorily together. \mathrm{NCmp} and the number of degrees of freedom carried by the nodes of the raft may be different. In the particular case of a clamped structure, the various components of the stiffness of the soil springs are indicated as being equal to zero so as to cancel the energy associated with the soil. These values are compatible with the default value ‘DEPL’ for the operand METHODE. 3.1.4 Operand GROUP_NO_RADIER This operand is linked to the value 'DEPL' of the operand METHODE. List of node groups constituting the raft of the structure resting on the soil. One then computes the averaged displacement at these nodes U of components {U}_{i} for each computed mode of frequency \mathrm{fr} in order to be able to determine the energy in the soil by degree of freedom and by frequency: \frac{1}{2}{k}_{i}.{U}_{i}^{2}(\mathrm{fr}) . 3.1.5 Operand GROUP_MA_RADIER This operand is linked to the value 'RIGI_PARASOL' of the operand METHODE. List of mesh-cell groups constituting the raft of the structure resting on the soil. Makes it possible to compute the averaged force at the nodes of these mesh cells F of components {F}_{i} for each computed mode of frequency \mathrm{fr} in order to determine the energy in the soil by degree of freedom and by frequency: \frac{1}{2}\frac{{F}_{i}^{2}}{{k}_{i}}(\mathrm{fr}) . 3.1.6 Operand FONC_GROUP / COEF_GROUP / GROUP_NO_CENTRE / COOR_CENTRE These operands are also linked to the value 'RIGI_PARASOL' of the operand METHODE. They are the same as in the option RIGI_PARASOL of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01. They also make it possible to obtain the stiffness values distributed at the nodes under the raft, used to determine the nodal forces by mode and then their average F of component {F}_{i} . An operand chosen from FONC_GROUP / COEF_GROUP makes it possible to determine weightings, functions of the abscissa or real, of each of the mesh-cell groups making up the raft. The formulae remain at the user's choice. By default, one considers that the distribution function is constant and equal to one, that is to say that each surface is assigned the same weight [bib2]. One must therefore have as many terms in the corresponding list as in the list of mesh-cell groups given by the operand GROUP_MA_RADIER. An operand chosen from GROUP_NO_CENTRE / COOR_CENTRE makes it possible to supply either the central node of the raft by a node group of a single node, or directly coordinates locating the central node. 3.2 Keyword AMOR_INTERNE Used once only at the same time as the keyword ENER_SOL. The contribution to the reduced damping of each mode is established from the distribution of the potential energy in the structure for the mode under consideration. This distribution is obtained using the command POST_ELEM U4.81.22 from the concept of type mode_meca (cf. [§3.1.1]) which produces a table. The input parameters of this table are names of mesh-cell groups, defined by the user according to the distributions of material damping in the structure. 3.2.1 Operand ENER_POT Name of the potential-energy table produced by the command POST_ELEM U4.81.22. The necessary parameters of the table are: | Parameters | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | NUME_ORDRE | I | Order number | | FREQ | R | Frequency at the order number NUME_ORDRE | | LIEU | K8 | Associated geometric entity: it may be the whole structure, a set of mesh cells or mesh-cell groups | | POUR_CENT | R | Potential-energy ratio with respect to the total energy | For further information on the meaning of the parameters, the reader is invited to consult the documentation of the command POST_ELEM U4.81.22. 3.2.2 Operand GROUP_MA The list of names of mesh-cell groups from which one will point into the table defined by ENER_POT (cf. [§3.2.1]). It is imperative that this list contain all the mesh-cell groups making up the structure and that their energy has indeed been computed in the table defined by ENER_POT. One will consider that for each mode the sum of the energies passing through the preceding mesh-cell groups will be equal to the total energy minus that passing through the soil springs and distributed from the keyword ENER_SOL. If the user indicates a mesh-cell group name whose energy has not been computed in the table defined by ENER_POT, there will be an alarm but no stop. It is therefore indeed up to the user to check the conformity of the mesh-cell groups of the table and of those of the list in the keyword AMOR_INTERNE. Finally, for the computation of the list of modal dampings according to the RCC-G rule to be meaningful, and in particular so that the energy passing through the soil springs is not negative (which would imply that the potential-energy ratio of the set of mesh-cell groups making up the structure could exceed 100%), it is strongly recommended to impose a rigid-link condition on the list of node groups constituting the raft of the structure resting on the soil. In order to compute correctly the potential-energy ratio of the constituent mesh-cell groups, it is imperative to have the total energy of the whole model. And for that, upstream, it is mandatory that in the table defined by ENER_POT one has computed the potential energy by the operator POST_ELEM for the entity TOUT=’OUI’. Otherwise, a stop message is issued. 3.2.3 Operand AMOR_REDUIT The list of the real values of material damping corresponding, term by term, to the list of mesh-cell group names defined by GROUP_MA (cf. [§3.2.2]). 3.3 Keyword AMOR_SOL Used once only at the same time as the keyword ENER_SOL. It makes it possible to determine the contribution of the geometric damping due to the reflection of the elastic waves. These directional damping values are obtained by interpolating, for each computed eigenfrequency, the geometric damping functions \frac{\text{Im}(K(\omega ))}{2\text{Re}(K(\omega ))} (cf. §[3.3.1]) where K(\omega ) is the complex impedance of the soil determined using one of the programs MISS3D, CLASSI or PARASOL: \mathrm{amor}({\omega}_{i})=\left[{\omega}_{i},\frac{\text{Im}(K({\omega}_{i}))}{2\text{Re}(K({\omega}_{i}))}\right] 3.3.1 Operand FONC_AMOR_GEO Defines the list of functions of frequency of the geometric dampings, one per degree of freedom (3 or 6). In the framework of a structure on a clamped base, this function must be supplied even if it has no particular meaning. One may take the constant function equal to zero, for example. 3.3.2 Operand AMOR_REDUIT Correction in the computation of the geometric damping due to the reduced material damping of the soil. Note: The reduced-damping value is necessary if the soil impedance is produced by PARASOL. One then assigns the complete value of the reduced material damping of the soil. If the soil impedance is produced by MISS3D, this value is necessary only if the soil is homogeneous (see operand HOMOGENE [§3.3.3] ) and in that case one introduces half the value of the reduced material damping of the soil. 3.3.3 Operand HOMOGENE If the soil is homogeneous ('OUI'), one weights the computation of the geometric damping by the factor 0.5. Then, in the case where the soil impedance is produced by MISS3D and only if the soil is homogeneous ('OUI'), one must introduce for the operand AMOR_REDUIT (cf. [§3.3.2]) half the value of the reduced material damping of the soil. One introduces nothing when the soil impedance is produced by MISS3D if the soil is not homogeneous ('NON'). 3.3.4 Operand SEUIL Value defined in the RCC-G [bib1] (0.3 by default) for the threshold beyond which one possibly truncates the modal damping. This threshold operates after the possible preceding corrections. 3.4 Keyword AMOR_RAYLEIGH Used once only to the exclusion of the keyword ENER_SOL. This keyword makes it possible to compute a list of modal dampings by computed frequency of a concept of type mode_meca. This list depends both on the values of the frequencies of the mode {\mathrm{freq}}_{i} and on the coefficients appearing in the expression of the Rayleigh damping. 3.4.1 Operand MODE_MECA Makes it possible to introduce the concept of type mode_meca containing the frequencies from which one will compute the modal damping. 3.4.2 Operands AMOR_ALPHA / AMOR_BETA Represent respectively the values of the components \alpha and \beta appearing in the expression of the Rayleigh damping from the stiffness and mass operators: C=\alpha K+\beta M . Then for each computed frequency {\mathrm{freq}}_{i} of the concept of type mode_meca \mathrm{mod} associated with an angular frequency {\omega}_{i}=2\pi {\mathrm{freq}}_{i} one obtains an equivalent modal damping: {\xi}_{i}=\frac{1}{2}(\alpha {\omega}_{i}+\frac{\beta}{{\omega}_{i}}) 3.4.3 Operands CORR_AMOR_NEGATIF / COEF_CORR_AMOR The keyword CORR_AMOR_NEGATIF makes it possible to check automatically whether there exist negative values in the list of damping coefficients generated by the operator. If this keyword is equal to 'NON' (default value), then if one detects a negative or zero damping, execution stops in error, with a message indicating the value in question. If the keyword is equal to 'IGNORE', one acts as previously except that the error is turned into a simple alarm. Finally, if the keyword is equal to 'OUI', then one replaces the negative or zero values by an arbitrary strictly positive value (and less than 1) defined by the user with the keyword COEF_CORR_AMOR. 4 Bibliography 1. RCC-G: Rules for the design and construction of PWR nuclear islands. EDF - Direction de l'Equipement, July 1988 edition 1. WAECKEL Seismic response by transient analysis R4.05.01 5 Example of use The use of CALC_AMOR_MODAL requires the computation of the eigenmodes of the structure on soil springs in the form of a concept of type mode_meca and of a concept of type table_sdaster of these modes computed by means of the command POST_ELEM U4.61.04. u4.52.14 Operator MODE_STATIQUE u4.52.14 Operator MODE_STATIQUE 1 Purpose Compute static modes for a unit imposed displacement, force or acceleration. One can also compute coupling modes (interface modes) in order to define a smaller generalised model. A static mode is the static deformed shape of an isostatic or hyperstatic structure on which one imposes: - at a blocked degree of freedom (node – component) a unit imposed displacement, - at a free degree of freedom (node – component) a unit nodal force, - in a direction , a unit imposed acceleration, - at a degree of freedom (node – component) a unit imposed acceleration. The coupling modes correspond to the modes of the substructure statically condensed onto the interface. These modes, defined only on the interface, are then statically expanded onto the whole of the substructure. The operator makes it possible to compute the set of static modes corresponding to several node–component pairs. The stiffness matrix must be assembled using a set of kinematic boundary conditions sufficient for all the rigid-body modes to be removed (operators AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01 or AFFE_CHAR_CINE U4.44.03). It is possible to request only part of the static modes corresponding to these kinematic conditions. The concept produced can be used to complete a modal base of vibration eigenmodes (operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02 or DYNA_ALEA_MODAL U4.53.22), to determine the loadings required for the computation of the entrainment motion under a seismic excitation (operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME U4.63.01) and to introduce the displacements at multi-support anchorages or the correction modes in a spectral analysis (operator COMB_SISM_MODAL U4.84.01). Produces a concept of type mode_meca. These modes are used to determine the loading due to the multi-support entrainment motion under a seismic excitation (operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME U4.63.01) (cf. reference R4.05.01) or to introduce the displacements at multi-support anchorages in a spectral analysis (operator COMB_SISM_MODAL U4.84.01) (cf. reference R4.05.03). See example §4.1. 3.5.1.1 Operands TOUT / GROUP_NO ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the nodes of the system that have blocked degrees of freedom. / GROUP_NO = g_noeu Computation of the modes on the node groups g_noeu (subset of the blocked nodes). 3.5.1.2 Operands TOUT_CMP / AVEC_CMP / SANS_CMP ♦ / TOUT_CMP = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the components blocked at the nodes defined previously. / AVEC_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes on the components cited only. / SANS_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes excluding the components cited. 3.5.2 keyword FORCE_NODALE / FORCE_NODALE factor keyword for the definition of the static modes with unit imposed force. These modes are used to complete a modal base of vibration eigenmodes (operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02 or DYNA_ALEA_MODAL U4.53.22). Cf. reference R5.06.01 and see example §4.2. 3.5.2.1 Operand TOUT / GROUP_NO ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the nodes of the system that have free degrees of freedom. / GROUP_NO = g_noeu Computation of the modes on the node groups g_noeu. 3.5.2.2 Operands TOUT_CMP / AVEC_CMP / SANS_CMP ♦ / TOUT_CMP = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the components free at the nodes defined previously. / AVEC_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes on the components cited only. / SANS_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes excluding the components cited. 3.5.3 keyword PSEUDO_MODE / PSEUDO_MODE factor keyword for the definition of the static modes (or pseudo-modes) with unit imposed acceleration. These modes are used to complete a modal base of vibration eigenmodes (operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02 or DYNA_ALEA_MODAL U4.53.22) (cf. reference R5.06.01, to determine the correction modes in a spectral analysis (operator COMB_SISM_MODAL U4.84.01, keyword MODE_CORR) (cf. reference R4.05.03). One treats the single-support case (operands AXE / DIRECTION, see example §4.3) or the multi-support case (operand GROUP_NO and CMP, see example §4.4). 3.5.3.1 Operands AXE / DIRECTION / NOM_DIR ♦ / AXE = l_axe Computes the modes along the axes of the global frame given (l_axe), these axes being 'X' , 'Y' and 'Z' . ♦ / DIRECTION = l_dir Computes the mode along the given direction (l_dir) (l_dir): direction vector with 3 components. ♦ NOM_DIR = n_dir User name that one wishes to give to the mode computed in the direction ( {n}_{\mathrm{dir}} ). By default the name is DIR_N, N being the number of the static mode. This name is mandatory. 3.5.3.2 Operands TOUT / GROUP_NO ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the nodes of the system. / GROUP_NO = g_noeu Computation of the modes on the node groups g_noeud. Note on use for the seismic analysis: In the framework of a static correction in spectral analysis ( COMB_SISM_MODAL ), the taking into account of the pseudo-mode depends on the type of analysis: - In single support ( TYPE_ANALYSE='MONO_APPUI' ), only the pseudo-modes defined by AXE or DIRECTION are used; - In multi-support ( TYPE_ANALYSE='MULT_APPUI' ), only the pseudo-modes defined by NOEUD or GROUP_NO are taken into account. It is strongly recommended to define distinct MODE_STATIQUE objects for each case of use in order to avoid ambiguities when calling COMB_SISM_MODAL . 3.5.3.3 Operands TOUT_CMP / AVEC_CMP / SANS_CMP ♦ / TOUT_CMP = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the components at the nodes defined previously. / AVEC_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes on the components cited only. / SANS_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes excluding the components cited. 3.5.3.4 Operands CORRELE / NOM_APPUI ◊ CORRELE = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT], The modes are correlated; one computes only a single mode per direction. This mode corresponds to the sum of the modes obtained by applying the acceleration at each node in this direction. # Si CORRELE = 'OUI' ◆ NOM_APPUI = text, One must give a support name that makes it possible to retrieve the mode corresponding to the support. 3.5.4 keyword MODE_INTERF / MODE_INTERF factor keyword for the definition of the coupling modes. These modes are used to complete a modal base of vibration eigenmodes (operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02 or DYNA_ALEA_MODAL U4.53.22). Cf. reference R5.06.01 and see example §4.2. 3.5.4.1 Operand TOUT / GROUP_NO ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the nodes of the system that have blocked degrees of freedom. / GROUP_NO = g_noeu Computation of the modes on the node groups g_noeu. 3.5.4.2 Operands TOUT_CMP / AVEC_CMP / SANS_CMP ♦ / TOUT_CMP = 'OUI' Computation of the modes on all the components blocked at the nodes defined previously. / AVEC_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes on the components cited only. / SANS_CMP = l_cmp Computation of the modes excluding the components cited. 3.5.4.3 Operand NB_MODE ♦ NB_MODE= nbmod Number of modes to be computed. It is, for the moment, not possible to specify a frequency band of interest, or the maximum frequency of the modes to be computed. The user must therefore estimate for himself the number of modes to be taken into account. The list of the frequencies associated with the interface modes makes it possible to determine the number of modes to be taken into account in the analysis for the reduced model. 3.5.4.4 Operand SHIFT ♦ SHIFT = shift Shift frequency (shift) used for the computation of the interface modes. The choice of this value makes it possible to improve the accuracy of the computation of the modes. One may choose a shift value corresponding to 10% of the first eigenfrequency expected for the coupling modes. The arbitrary default value is set to 1\mathit{Hz} . 3.6 keyword SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR = ... This factor keyword is optional: it makes it possible to choose the linear solver used in certain parts of the algorithm. The syntax being common to several commands, please consult the manual U4.50.01. Note: for the keyword MODE_INTERF, one must solve linear systems but for these, the solver is chosen “hard-coded” in the programming (LDLT if there are very few degrees of freedom and MUMPS if there are more). 3.7 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.8 Operand INFO ◊ INFO Indicates the level of printout of information in the “MESSAGE” file: 1: no printout 2: printout of the static modes computed. 4 Examples 4.1 Computation of the static modes with unit imposed displacement Calculdes modes statiques en déplacement imposé unitaire. | mode \Psi solution of \lbrace \begin{array}{c}\Psi =-{K}^{-1}\cdot {}^{t}B^{-1}\cdot {\lambda}_{i}\\ B\cdot \Psi ={V}_{i}\end{array} | with | K | :17: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. u4.52.15 Operator MAC_MODES u4.52.15 Operator MAC_MODES 1 Purpose The operator MAC_MODES makes it possible to compute a correlation matrix between two modal bases. The correlation coefficient between two vectors of this base is all the closer to 1 as these two vectors are collinear. It also makes it possible to compute the difference between two modal bases by using the IERI energy criterion (Energy Indicator of Interface Regularity). This criterion is all the closer to 0 as the two vectors are very close. It also makes it possible to compute the generalised matrix relative to the weighting matrix entered as input. Produces a concept of type table_sdaster. 2 Syntax table = MAC_MODES( ◆ BASE_1 = mode_meca_c / mode_flamb / mode_meca, ◆ BASE_2 = mode_meca_c / mode_flamb / mode_meca, ◇ & MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r, & IERI = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 General points The MAC matrix ( M odal A ssurance C riterion) indicates the correlation between two lists of vectors. It is often used to check the orthogonality of two modal bases (experimental or numerical). The i-th row, j-th column of the MAC matrix is defined by the following relation: {\mathit{MAC}}_{ij}=\frac{{\left({\Phi}_{i}^{H}W{\Phi}_{j}\right)}^{2}}{\left({\Phi}_{i}^{H}W{\Phi}_{i}\right)\left({\Phi}_{j}^{H}W{\Phi}_{j}\right)} Where: {\Phi}_{i} is the i-th vector of the first base, {\Phi}_{j} is the j-th vector of the second base, W is a weighting matrix, The superscript {}^{H} denotes the conjugate transpose. This MAC matrix is diagonal if the two bases are formed of the modal vectors coming from one and the same structure and if the weighting matrix is equal to the mass or stiffness matrix of the structure under consideration. One then speaks of the orthogonality of the eigenmodes with respect to the mass or stiffness matrix. The quantity {\Phi}_{i}^{H}W{\Phi}_{j} corresponds to the term of the generalised stiffness (or mass) matrix if the weighting matrix is equal to the stiffness (or mass) matrix. The IERI criterion ( I ndicator of E nergy of R egularity of the I nterface) is an energy indicator making it possible to compute the difference between two vectors. It is defined by the following relation: {\mathrm{IERI}}_{ij}=\frac{{({({\Phi}_{i}-{\Phi}_{j})}^{H}W({\Phi}_{i}-{\Phi}_{j}))}^{2}}{{({\Phi}_{i}^{H}W{\Phi}_{i})}^{2}+{({\Phi}_{j}^{H}W{\Phi}_{j})}^{2}} The weighting matrix is either the mass matrix or the stiffness matrix of the structure under consideration. This IERI criterion tends towards 0 if the two vectors are very close. 3.2 Operand BASE_1/BASE_2 ♦ BASE_1 = base_1 ♦ BASE_2 = base_2 Name of the modal concepts (mode_meca, mode_meca_c, mode_flamb) to be compared. In general, one compares a numerical modal base produced by an analysis (by CALC_MODES) and an experimental modal base, imported by LIRE_RESU. The two bases must be defined on the same model and have the same numbering. 3.3 Operand IERI ◊ IERI = ’OUI’ This operand is used to specify that one wants to compute the IERI criterion. In this case, the operand MATR_ASSE must be supplied. One must associate with it a mass matrix or a stiffness matrix. 3.4 Operand MATR_ASSE ◊ MATR_ASSE = matr Operand designating an assembled matrix used as a weighting. matr is the weighting matrix applied to the base vectors. It must have the same numbering as base1 and base2. One usually chooses the mass matrix or the stiffness matrix as the weighting matrix. If this operand is not supplied, the weighting matrix chosen is equal to the identity matrix. This weighting matrix is mandatory for the computation of the IERI criterion. 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = ’tit’ Optional name to be given to the table. 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = 1 ou 2 The MAC or IERI matrix and the generalised matrix are displayed in tabular form in the MESSAGE file if INFO=2. The name of the parameter of the output table associated with the generalised matrix is Y1_W_Y2. This generalised matrix is computed if the base vectors are of real type.

u4.52.16 Operator CALC_CORR_SSD u4.52.16 Operator CALC_CORR_SSD 1 Purpose Estimate the quality of the reduced models in the framework of the modal analysis. This command makes it possible to compute the works of the residual coupling forces at each of the interfaces, as well as the works of the residual forces on the internal parts of the substructures. Furthermore, on the basis of these works, the command computes enrichment terms, based on: - the works of the residual forces at the interfaces, for each substructure, - the works of the residual forces on the internal parts, for each substructure, - the differential displacements (separation) that may appear at the interfaces between the substructures. This is for example the case in the test SDLS122A, where one considers square macro-elements, clamped on the edge associated with the interface, and simply supported on the 2 other free corners. By releasing the clamping of the interface edge, the structure becomes hinged, and therefore presents rigid-body modes. In the absence of \mathit{SHIFT}>0 , the matrix is singular and the analysis cannot proceed correctly. 3.4 Keyword UNITE ◊ UNITE Specifies the unit of the file in which the results of the computations of the interface works will be printed. By default, the results are printed on unit 8. 3.5 Keyword VERIF ◊ VERIF Factor keyword inherited from the definition of the generalised model, in order to check its consistency. One determines whether the link is compatible or not. The nodes of the two interfaces do not a priori have to be ordered so that they coincide in pairs. If the nodes of the interfaces are not facing each other in pairs, the code detects this state and reorders the nodes so as to put them back facing each other. 3.5.1 Operand STOP_ERREUR Permet d'effectuer ou non la vérification de cohérence du modèle généralisé. 3.5.2 Operand PRECISION / CRITERE Indicates the precision threshold beyond which the links are incompatible. It is the distance (relative or absolute according to CRITERE) beyond which the link nodes are considered too far apart to be effectively connected.

u4.52.17 Macro-command POST_MODE u4.52.17 Macro-command POST_MODE Summary: The effective masses and inertias are parameters computed for each mode by the operator CALC_MODES. They can serve as criteria for selecting the modes of greatest interest. In that case, these parameters are computed by taking the whole model into account. It is however sometimes useful to be able to have these parameters on only part of the model. This macro-command makes it possible to compute the so-called local effective masses and inertias for each mode of a data structure of type mode_meca, that is to say by taking into account only a chosen part of the model. POST_MODE produces a table with the following parameters: NUME_ORDRE, NUME_MODE, FREQ, MASS_EFFE_DX, MASS_EFFE_DY, MASS_EFFE_DZ, INER_EFFE_DX, INER_EFFE_DY, INER_EFFE_DZ, MASS_EFFE_UN_DX, MASS_EFFE_UN_DY, MASS_EFFE_UN_DZ, INER_EFFE_UN_DX, INER_EFFE_UN_DY, INER_EFFE_UN_DZ 1 Purpose Compute the so-called local effective masses and inertias for each mode of a data structure of type mode_meca, that is to say by taking into account only a chosen part of the model. POST_MODE produces a table with the following parameters: NUME_ORDRE, NUME_MODE, FREQ, MASS_EFFE_DX, MASS_EFFE_DY, MASS_EFFE_DZ, INER_EFFE_DX, INER_EFFE_DY, INER_EFFE_DZ, MASS_EFFE_UN_DX, MASS_EFFE_UN_DY, MASS_EFFE_UN_DZ, INER_EFFE_UN_DX, INER_EFFE_UN_DY, INER_EFFE_UN_DZ 2 Syntax table = POST_MODE( ◆ MODE = mode_meca, ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ MATR_MASS = matr_asse_depl_r, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Principle The computation of these local effective masses and inertias is performed in an approximate manner. Indeed, in order to compute these quantities exactly, one would have to rebuild the mass matrix completely so as to take into account only the contributions of the selected mesh cells. POST_MODE does not compute the true “local” mass matrix. It transforms the global mass matrix (supplied to the operator CALC_MODES) by setting to zero the rows and columns corresponding to degrees of freedom that do not belong to the mesh-cell selection defined. By proceeding in this way, one retains, on the degrees of freedom of the nodes on the boundary of the selected domain and connected to other mesh cells of the model, contributions coming from mesh cells that were not selected. This approximation is accepted. With this tool one is not seeking perfect accuracy, but values that are accurate enough to provide good criteria for selecting the modes. The formulae for these various local criteria are the same as the formulae for these same global criteria (presented in R5.01.03) 4 Operands 4.1 Operand MODE ◆ MODE = mode Name of the mode_meca data structure for which one wishes to compute local criteria. 4.2 Operand GROUP_MA ◆ GROUP_MA = list[grma] List of the mesh-cell groups defining the sub-domain. 4.3 Operand CARA_ELEM ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem Name of the characteristics of the beam, shell, etc. elements. 4.4 Operand MATR_MASS ◆ MATR_MASS = matr_mass Assembled mass matrix that was used for the computation of the mode_meca mode . 5 Example of use One computes the effective-mass and effective-inertia criteria, unit and non-unit, on the desired part of the model: table_crit = POST_MODE( MODE=modes, GROUP_MA=("BATIMENT2",), CARA_ELEM=caraelem, MATR_MASS=masse, ) One modifies the table created by filtering on the chosen criterion, here local unit effective masses along X greater than 5%: table_crit = CALC_TABLE(reuse=table_crit, TABLE=table_crit, ACTION=_F(OPERATION="FILTRE", NOM_PARA="MASS_EFFE_UN_DX", CRIT_COMP="GT", VALE=0.05), ) One then recovers the list of the selected modes liste_modes = table_crit.EXTR_TABLE().values()["NUME_MODE"] and one builds a mode_meca object containing only these modes. EXTR = EXTR_MODE(FILTRE_MODE=_F(MODE=modes, NUME_MODE=liste_modes))

u4.52.51 Operator CALC_MODE_ROTATION u4.52.51 Operator CALC_MODE_ROTATION 1 Purpose Compute the modes and the frequencies of the following system as a function of the rotation speeds, M\ddot{\delta}+(C+\Omega G)\dot{\delta}+K\delta =0 Where M is the mass matrix of the system, C is a damping matrix, G is the gyroscopic matrix (antisymmetric), and K is the stiffness matrix of the system. \Omega represents the rotation speed. The data required for this macro are: 1. the matrices: K,C,G and M 2. A list of rotation speeds This operator returns a list of mode_meca_c concepts: one concept for each rotation speed. It calls the command CALC_MODES. 2 Syntax table_container = CALC_MODE_ROTATION( ◆ MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_depl_r, ◆ MATR_MASS = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ MATR_AMOR = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ MATR_GYRO = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ VITE_ROTA = float, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ METHODE = / "QZ" (par défaut), / "SORENSEN", ⟐ CALC_FREQ = _F( ◇ OPTION = / "PLUS_PETITE" (par défaut), / "CENTRE", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'PLUS_PETITE') ◇ NMAX_FREQ = int (défaut: 10), ◇ SEUIL_FREQ = float (défaut: 0.01), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CENTRE') ◆ FREQ = float, ◇ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ NMAX_FREQ = int (défaut: 10), ◇ SEUIL_FREQ = float (défaut: 0.01), ), ⟐ VERI_MODE = _F( ◇ STOP_ERREUR = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ SEUIL = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ PREC_SHIFT = float (défaut: 0.005), ◇ STURM = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands MATR_RIGI / MATR_MASS / MATR_AMOR / MATR_GYRO / INFO / METHODE / OPTION / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM They have the same meaning as in the command CALC_MODES U4.52.02. Note: > Because of the presence of the damping and gyroscopic matrices, only the methods QZ and SORENSEN can be used . 3.2 Keyword CALC_FREQ Plays the same role as in the command CALC_MODES U4.52.02, and has the same internal keywords with the same default values. Note: The number of modes \mathit{nbF} is the same for all the rotation speeds. 3.3 Operand VITE_ROTA List of the rotation speeds \Omega in \mathit{rad}/s . 3.4 Operand keyword VERI_MODE The internal operands have the same meaning as in the keyword of the same name of the command CALC_MODES U4.52.02. 4 Example Computation of the first 5 rotating modes using the QZ method: Lmod=CALC_MODE_ROTATION(MATR_RIGI = RIGIDITE, MATR_MASS = MASSE, MATR_AMOR=AMOR, MATR_GYRO =GYASS, VITE_ROTA=L_VITROT, METHODE = 'QZ', CALC_FREQ=_F(OPTION='PLUS_PETITE',NMAX_FREQ=5), VERI_MODE=_F(STOP_ERREUR='NON')); CALC_MODE_ROTATION returns a table (table_container) containing the modal bases computed for each rotation speed. The mode_meca_c produced are named as follows: mod_0,…mod_i..mod_nbV, i is the index of the rotation speed in VITE_ROTA.
