"PILOTAGE", ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword RESULTAT In the case where one wishes to continue an analysis which has already been run, RESULTAT indicates which object is enriched (see also ETAT_INIT). 3.2 Operands MODELE/CHAM_MATER/CARA_ELEM > These operands have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. 3.3 Operands MODE_STAT/MASS_DIAG ◊ MODE_STAT = modestat Name of the static mode required in the case of an analysis with multi-support excitations R4.05.01. They are computed beforehand by the operator MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14 with the option ‘MODE_STAT'. ◊ MASS_DIAG = / 'OUI', / 'NON', Option to be used with an explicit time scheme [bib2] and which makes it possible to solve with a lumped (diagonalised) mass matrix. This option is not available for all types of elements, in particular the discrete elements (in that case, one must solve with the consistent mass matrix). In the implicit case it is not possible to use a lumped matrix (a fatal error is emitted if the user is in that case). 3.4 Keyword EXCIT ◊ EXCIT =_F This factor keyword makes it possible to describe, at each occurrence, a load (excitations and boundary conditions), and possibly a multiplying coefficient and/or a type of load. The operands have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03, but there are a few specific features related to dynamics. Important note for the time schemes: If one imposes displacement boundary conditions which evolve in the course of time, one must take into account the primal unknown of the scheme used. These conditions are in fact imposed in acceleration in the explicit case (because that is the primal unknown). This means that one must enter in DYNA_NON_LINE the second derivative of the displacement signal which one wants to impose. This evolution of the imposed displacement must therefore be differentiable at least twice with respect to time. 3.4.1 Operands CHARGE/FONC_MULT > ♦ CHARGE = {\mathrm{ch}}_{i} ◊ FONC_MULT = :math: {f}_{i} The operands have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. 3.4.2 Operand TYPE_CHARGE ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = / 'FIXE_CSTE' , [DEFAUT] / 'SUIV', / 'DIDI', The operand has the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03, except that a loading cannot be piloted in dynamics, and therefore tchi cannot be FIXE_PILO. 3.4.3 Operands MULT_APPUI/ACCE/VITE/DEPL/DIRECTION/GROUP_NO ◊ MULT_APPUI= /'NON', [DEFAUT] /'OUI', ♦ ACCE = ac, [fonction] ♦ VITE = vi, [fonction] ♦ DEPL = dp, [fonction] ◊ DIRECTION = (dx,dy,dz,drx,dry,drz), [l_R] ◊ GROUP_NO = lgrno, [l_groupe_no] It is pointed out that the multi-support analysis rests fundamentally on the additive superposition of the motions, cf. [R5.05.05, §2.6]; therefore, if the static, elastic modes are solutions which generate strains in the structure, then for the superposition to be valid, the constitutive behaviour of the constituent materials must be linear, and the kinematics must be linear as well. The entrainment motions, which are functions of time, therefore produce inertia forces which are added to the other loads, and the solution produces a dynamic response under the assumption of fixed supports. These entrainment inertia forces are built with the operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME U4.63.01 from the static modes and the mass matrix. Only the entrainment acceleration at each support is therefore used for the solution, and the velocities and displacements at each support serve only to reconstruct, by additive superposition, the complete solution in velocities and displacements. One notes that the damping forces come only from the velocities solved under the assumption of fixed supports, and not from the complete velocities reconstructed by superposition with the velocities at each support. In the case of a multi-support excitation (MULT_APPUI= 'OUI'), the other operands have exactly the same meaning as in the factor keyword EXCIT of the operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. In this case, the fields ‘DEPL’, ‘VITE’, ‘ACCE’ correspond respectively to the displacements, velocities and accelerations, functions of time, of the entrainment motion on the supports specified in ‘GROUP_NO’ and for the direction ‘DIRECTION’. The new fields ‘DEPL_ABSOLU’, ‘VITE_ABSOLU’, ‘ACCE_ABSOLU’ are then created in the concept of type evol_noli produced by the operator DYNA_NON_LINE and correspond respectively to the displacements, velocities and accelerations of the absolute motion, sums of the entrainment motion on the supports and of the relative motion with respect to this multi-support entrainment motion. The linear elastic solutions associated with the unit entrainment motions on the supports, cf. [R5.05.05, §2.6], are described by the static modes MODE_STAT supplied under the corresponding keyword, see §3.3. If that is not the case, one must then describe the excitations by imposed displacements which are functions of time on all the supports, and the solution will be carried out in the absolute reference frame. 3.5 Keyword CONTACT > ♦ CONTACT = contact This simple keyword makes it possible to activate the solution of frictional contact or the taking into account of a unilateral constraint. contact is a concept produced by the operator DEFI_CONTACT U4.44.11. The operand has the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03 . 3.6 Keyword SOUS_STRUC ◊ SOUS_STRUC=_F This factor keyword makes it possible to specify which loadings are to be used for the static substructures, which then necessarily form part of the model. The operand has the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03 . 3.7 Keyword COMPORTEMENT The syntax of these keywords common to several commands is described in the document U4.51.11. All the constitutive relations supported by STAT_NON_LINE are also available in DYNA_NON_LINE, provided that the computation of the mass matrix of the elements concerned is provided for. 3.8 Keyword ETAT_INIT ◊ ETAT_INIT =_F Under this keyword are defined the initial conditions of the problem. The operands of the keyword ETAT_INIT have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. Note: In the case where the user has specified that the result concept is re-entrant, the keyword ETAT_INIT is mandatory. The enriched concept is supplied by the keyword RESULTAT. In dynamics, one can in addition define the initial velocity and acceleration fields. > ♦ / | VITE = vite > / | ACCE = acce If the keywords EVOL_NOLI, DEPL and VITE are absent, one assumes that the initial state is at zero displacements, velocities and stresses, and one computes the accelerations corresponding to the loading at the time instant instini defined by the operand INST. 3.9 Keyword INCREMENT ♦ INCREMENT =_F Defines the list of the analysis time instants. The operands of the keyword INCREMENT have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. 3.10 Keyword NEWTON ◊ NEWTON =_F Specifies the characteristics of the method of solution of the non-linear incremental problem (Newton-Raphson method). The operands of the keyword NEWTON have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. 3.11 Keyword RECH_LINEAIRE ◊ RECH_LINEAIRE =_F( ◊ METHODE = /'CORDE' [DEFAUT] /'MIXTE' ) Makes it possible to activate the line search. The operands of the keyword RECH_LINEAIRE have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03, except that the method PILOTAGE does not exist. 3.12 Keyword SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR =_F The syntax of this keyword common to several commands is described in the document U4.50.01. 3.13 Keyword CONVERGENCE ◊ CONVERGENCE =_F This keyword describes the parameters making it possible to assess the convergence of the NEWTON method used to solve the non-linear mechanical problem. The operands of the keyword CONVERGENCE have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. 3.14 Keyword ARCHIVAGE ◊ ARCHIVAGE =_F Makes it possible to archive some or certain results at all or at certain time instants of the analysis. In the absence of this keyword all the time steps are archived, including the analysis time instants newly created by automatic subdivision of the time step. The operands of the keyword ARCHIVAGE have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03, except for the keyword CHAM_EXCLU. 3.14.1 Operand CHAM_EXCLU ◊ CHAM_EXCLU = |'DEPL' |'VITE' |'ACCE' |'SIEF_ELGA' |'VARI_ELGA' Makes it possible to specify the fields which will not be archived, except at the last time step. 3.15 Keyword AMOR_RAYL_RIGI > ◊ AMOR_RAYL_RIGI = /'ELASTIQUE', [DEFAUT] /'TANGENTE' The operator evaluates, assembles and automatically brings into play, in the solution of the equations of motion, all the damping contributions defined in the material field, the characteristics of the elements of the model, and those possibly defined by the keyword AMOR_MODAL, cf. § 3.18. This keyword makes it possible to specify the stiffness matrix \mathrm{K} which will be used to build the Rayleigh damping \mathrm{C}=\alpha .\mathrm{K}+\beta .\mathrm{M} by means of the parameters available in the material field. With the default value ('ELASTIQUE'), one forces the computation of the Rayleigh damping with the elastic stiffness matrix. By choosing the value 'TANGENTE', the matrix \mathrm{K} will be the same as the one which is used for the computation of the internal forces. For softening constitutive models or models of GLRC type one is advised to use the elastic stiffness matrix. Note: If this keyword is absent, the computation of the Rayleigh damping is nevertheless carried out automatically with the elastic stiffness matrix. Note: The option AMOR_MECA, which carries out the computation of the Rayleigh damping, is not available for the THM finite elements. In order to carry out an analysis with these elements, one must leave the material parameters assigned to the mesh cells carrying THM finite elements, AMOR_ALPHA and AMOR_BETA, equal to 0. 3.16 Keyword VNOR ◊ VNOR = This option allows us to take into account the case of an emitting boundary. The most common case is the radiating one (or partially radiating if one defines a reflection coefficient \alpha \ne 0 ). In the case of a radiating boundary VNOR = 1 (option activated by default). In the case of an emitting boundary VNOR = -1. This coefficient is multiplied by the value of the impedance of the absorbing fluid boundaries ('3D_FLUI_ABSO', '2D_FLUI_ABSO' and 'AXIS_FLUI_ABSO'). If none of these elements is present in the model, this option will not be taken into account. 3.17 Keyword MATR_ELEM_AMOR ◊ MATR_ELEM_AMOR = matrAmor [matr_elem] Ce mot-clef permet d'ajouter des matrices élémentaires pour l'amortissement. Cet amortissement interviendra dans l'opérateur matriciel en plus des autres possibilités d'amortissement, par exemple, si on définit un amortissement de Rayleigh via les caractéristiques matériaux AMOR_ALPHA et AMOR_BETA. 3.18 Keyword AMOR_MODAL > ◊ AMOR_MODAL =_F This keyword makes it possible to take into account a damping equivalent to a modal damping decomposed on a basis of modes computed beforehand, in the form of a concept of type mode_meca. This damping is taken into account globally in the dynamic equilibrium equation as a corrective force on the right-hand side -\mathrm{C}.\dot{\mathrm{X}} . 3.18.1 Operands MODE_MECA / AMOR_REDUIT / LIST_AMOR / NB_MODE ♦ MODE_MECA = mode ♦ / AMOR_REDUIT = l_amor, / LIST_AMOR = lisamor ◊ NB_MODE = nbmode The concept mode of type mode_meca (entered by the operand MODE_MECA) represents the basis of modes computed beforehand on which one decomposes the modal damping. This basis must necessarily have the same numbering profile as that of the dynamic system defined by the parameters of the keyword SOLVEUR [§ 3.12]. It is possible to truncate the modal basis to a number of modes defined by NB_MODE. By default, one takes all the modes of the modal basis. The modal dampings in reduced form are given by a list of reals whose number of terms is less than or equal to the number of modes taken into account. If the number of terms of the list is strictly smaller, one extends this list with the value of its last term until its length reaches the number of modes computed. 3.18.2 Operand REAC_VITE ◊ REAC_VITE= /'OUI', [DEFAUT] /'NON', If its value is 'OUI', one modifies the modal-damping corrective force at each internal Newton iteration defined in the keyword NEWTON [§ 9]. If its value is 'NON', one updates this term only at the beginning of each time step. 3.19 Description of the time-integration scheme R5.05.05 ♦ SCHEMA_TEMPS =_F() ◊ STOP_CFL = /'OUI', [DEFAUT] /'NON', ◊ FORMULATION= /'DEPLACEMENT', /'VITESSE', /'ACCELERATION', One may use the implicit methods of Newmark (keyword SCHEMA='NEWMARK', or modified average acceleration: SCHEMA='HHT' with MODI_EQUI = 'NON'), or of Hilber-Hughes-Taylor (HHT) (SCHEMA='HHT' with MODI_EQUI = 'OUI'). It is also possible to use the version without overshooting of the complete HHT scheme (see R5.05.05 for further details), via the keyword SCHEMA='NOHHT' (see R5.05.05). Otherwise, one may choose an explicit method of central-difference type (keyword SCHEMA='DIFF_CENT') or a dissipative scheme of TCHAMWA type (keyword SCHEMA='TCHAMWA') With an implicit scheme, the solutions in displacement, velocity or acceleration are currently available (keyword FORMULATION = 'DEPLACEMENT', 'VITESSE' or 'ACCELERATION'). It should be noted that the solution in velocity is not available for the HHT schemes (keyword SCHEMA = 'HHT' or 'NOHHT'). Furthermore, with an explicit scheme, one can solve only in acceleration (keyword FORMULATION = 'ACCELERATION'). The explicit schemes being conditionally stable, it may be useful to check whether the time step given as input of the analysis does indeed comply with the stability condition (CFL condition). If STOP_CFL = 'OUI' (default), then if the list of time instants supplied by the user contains one or more time steps greater than the stability condition, the analysis stops in fatal error. If STOP_CFL = 'NON', one emits an alarm and continues the analysis. In every case, the critical time step is given in the message file for information. The computation of the CFL is not programmed for all the elements (in particular the discrete elements are ignored); the CFL estimated by Code_Aster may therefore be larger (less penalising) than the real CFL, with the risks of sudden divergence which follow from that. In the explicit case, it is also recommended to use a lumped (diagonalised) mass matrix: which one can obtain with the keyword MASS_DIAG = 'OUI' [§ 7]. Notes: - The choice MASS_DIAG='NON' is not recommended with the shells DKT. - With the elements DKT/DKTG it is necessary to specify in AFFE_CARA_ELEM, under the factor keyword COQUE, the simple keyword INER_ROTA = 'OUI'. Otherwise the mass matrix is singular and the explicit scheme is unusable. - In the explicit case, one does not recommend the use of quadratic finite elements (which can generate spurious oscillations on the solution fields). For the multi-step schemes (Newmark with MODI_EQUI='OUI' ), it is necessary to recompute the internal forces at the previous time instant. This mode of operation is problematic at the first time instant of a restart of an analysis. Indeed, if one has command variables (which therefore depend on the analysis time instant), it is necessary to recover the value at the previous time instant. This is not always possible, in particular if one is not in reuse and if ETAT_INIT is made from individual fields (no use of the keyword ETAT_INIT/EVOL_NOLI ). In that case, one does not compute this contribution at the previous step, which may possibly modify the convergence of the algorithm slightly. It is therefore strongly recommended to specify the initial state via the keyword ETAT_INIT/EVOL_NOLI, in order to allow the computation of the internal forces at the previous time instant. 3.19.1 Case SCHEMA = 'NEWMARK' > ◊ BETA = /0.25, [DEFAUT] > /beta, [R] > ◊ GAMMA = /0.5, [DEFAUT] > /gamm, [R] The time-integration method is that of NEWMARK, with the given values of the parameters beta and gamm. When one specifies neither beta nor gamm, one has the method known as the “trapezoidal rule” ( beta=0.25 ; \mathrm{gamm}=0.5 ) which, in the linear case, is unconditionally stable and introduces no spurious dissipation ( i.e. numerical damping), but which, in the non-linear case, may be unstable [bib1][bib2]. 3.19.2 Case SCHEMA = 'HHT' ◊ ALPHA = /-0.1, [DEFAUT] /alph, [R] ◊ MODI_EQUI = /'OUI', [DEFAUT] /'NON', For MODI_EQUI = ’NON’, the time-integration method (implicit integration scheme) is that of the modified average acceleration (of the Newmark family) ([bib1], [bib2]), with the given negative value of alph. The larger |alph| is, the larger the numerical damping introduced by the analysis. But this dissipation is sometimes necessary, in the non-linear case, in order to ensure stability (unless one assigns a damping by material to the structure). For MODI_EQUI = ’OUI’ (default value), the time-integration method (implicit integration scheme) is that of Hilber-Hughes-Taylor (HHT or \alpha -\text{méthode} ) [bib2], with the given negative value of alph. The larger |alph| is, the larger the numerical damping introduced by the analysis. Compared with the previous scheme (MODI_EQUI = ’NON’) of modified average acceleration, the numerical damping induced is more “selective”: it is weaker at low and medium frequencies (asymptotically zero at zero frequency) and it increases more quickly when the frequency becomes large. This second scheme is based on the first one with, in addition, a modification of the equilibrium equation (one shifts the internal and external forces in time) [bib2]. 3.19.3 Case SCHEMA = 'DIFF_CENT' The central-difference scheme is an explicit scheme of order two of the Newmark family, with parameters BETA = 0 and GAMMA = 0.5. It is a one-step scheme which presents no numerical dissipation. 3.19.4 Case SCHEMA = 'TCHAMWA' ◊ PHI = /1.05, [DEFAUT] /phi, [R] An alternative to the central-difference schemes is the scheme developed by Bertrand Tchamwa and Christian Wielgosz. This explicit scheme has several interesting particular features. It is not a derivative of Newmark, and the variation of its parameter PHI allows a controllable numerical dissipation of the high frequencies. When it is equal to 1, the dissipation is zero. In order not to degrade the Courant condition too much and to retain stability properties comparable to the central-difference scheme, it is recommended not to choose a PHI greater than 1.10. 1.05 is the value chosen by default. 3.19.5 Operand COEF_MASS_SHIFT ◊ COEF_MASS_SHIFT = /0. [DEFAUT] /coef The datum of the coefficient coef makes it possible to carry out a shift of the mass matrix M , which becomes: M'=M+\mathit{coef}K The value of this coefficient, zero by default, must be non-zero in order to be able to invert, in dynamics with an explicit scheme, the mass matrix when the latter has zero terms for certain specific degrees of freedom, for example the pressure for the elements of HM modelling. Entering this coefficient also makes it possible to improve greatly the convergence in dynamics with an implicit scheme in this same type of modelling, by imposing a cut-off frequency inversely proportional to the value of coef (at the price of a slight distortion of the whole set of eigenfrequencies of the system) 3.20 Keyword CRIT_STAB ◊ CRIT_STAB =_F This keyword makes it possible to trigger the computation, at the end of each time increment, of a stability criterion, identical to what is proposed in STAT_NON_LINE. This criterion is useful in order to detect, in the course of the loading, the point from which one loses stability (by buckling for example). It is not a stability criterion in the dynamic sense (negative damping). The operands of the keyword CRIT_STAB have the same meaning as in the document U4.51.03. It should however be pointed out that the use of CRIT_STAB on coupled fluid-structure models (formulation (u,p,\phi ) , cf. documentation R4.02.02, which are available with DYNA_NON_LINE but not STAT_NON_LINE) requires the fluid degrees of freedom to be excluded, because the global assembled stiffness matrix is singular for these degrees of freedom. To do this, one must combine the keywords DDL_EXCLUS (by excluding all the degrees of freedom specific to the fluid elements, such as 'PRES', 'PHI' and, in the cases with a free surface, 'DH') and MODI_RIGI = 'OUI'. Further details are given in the documentations U4.51.03, U2.06.11 and U2.08.04. The whole of the results is stored in a data structure of type table_container of name 'ANALYSE_MODALE' attached to the data structure evol_noli. The buckling modes (TYPE='FLAMBEMENT') are stored as TYPE_MODE='MODE_FLAMB' in the table, whereas the stability modes (TYPE='STABILITE') are stored there as TYPE_MODE='MODE_STAB' (see § 4). 3.21 Keyword MODE_VIBR ◊ MODE_VIBR =_F ( ◊ OPTION = /'PLUS_PETITE', [DEFAUT] /'BANDE', /'CALIBRATION', Si OPTION='PLUS_PETITE' { ◊ NMAX_FREQ = /3, [DEFAUT] /nbfreq, [I] } Si OPTION='BANDE' { ◊ FREQ = intba , listr8 } Si OPTION='CALIBRATION' { ◊ FREQ = intba , listr8 } ◊ MATR_RIGI = /'ELASTIQUE', [DEFAUT] /'TANGENTE', /'SECANTE', ◊ /LIST_INST = list_r8, listr8 /INST = l_r8, [R] /PAS_CALC = npas, [I] ◊ PRECISION = /1.e-6 [DEFAUT] /prec ◊ CRITERE = /'RELATIF', [DEFAUT] /'ABSOLU', ), This keyword makes it possible to trigger the computation, at the end of each time increment, of a search for vibration eigenmodes. This criterion is useful in order to follow, in the course of the transient analysis, the evolution of the vibratory response of the non-linear structure. This criterion is computed in the following way: at the end of a time step, one solves det(K-{\omega}^{2}.M)=0 . K may be either the elastic stiffness matrix, or the consistent tangent matrix at the current time instant, or the secant matrix. M is the mass matrix. This modal analysis is allowed only for symmetric matrices (mass and stiffness). The keyword OPTION makes it possible to choose the type of search: - OPTION='PLUS_PETITE': the NMAX_FREQ eigenvectors and eigenvalues corresponding to the smallest eigenvalues; - OPTION='BANDE': the eigenvectors and eigenvalues for the frequencies lying in the band FREQ; - OPTION='CALIBRATION', of which only the number of eigenvalues for the frequencies lying in the band FREQ. The whole of the results is stored in a data structure of type table_container of name 'ANALYSE_MODALE' attached to the data structure evol_noli. The vibration modes are stored as TYPE_MODE='DEPL_VIBR' in the table (see § 4). The time instants for which one wants to carry out a computation of a vibration mode are given by a list of time instants LIST_INST or INST (list_r8 or l_r8) or by a frequency PAS_CALC (every \mathit{npas} time steps). In the absence of these keywords the vibratory modal analysis is carried out at all the time steps. The keywords PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to select the time instants, cf. U4.71.00. Note on the list of time instants: If LIST_INST or INST of MODE_VIBR contains time instants equal to or earlier than the initial time instant of DYNA_NON_LINE, Code_Aster will ignore the computation of the vibration modes for these time instants. 3.22 Operand ENERGIE ◊ ENERGIE = _F() This keyword makes it possible to activate the computation of the energy balance, its display in the course of the analysis and its storage in the table of name PARA_CALC. The energy balance can be extracted from this table by means of the command RECU_TABLE U4.71.02. 3.23 Operand PROJ_MODAL ◊ PROJ_MODAL =_F This keyword makes it possible to carry out the analysis on a modal basis (or Ritz basis) computed beforehand. It is to be used with an explicit time-integration scheme. 3.23.1 Operands MODE_MECA, NB_MODE ♦ MODE_MECA = mode, [mode_meca] ◊ NB_MODE = nbmode, [I] One specifies the basis to be used (MODE_MECA) and the number of modes (NB_MODE). Important note: The modal basis must rest on a numbering consistent with that of the computed evolution (cf. [§ 11]): same numbering profile. 3.23.2 Operands MASS_GENE, RIGI_GENE, AMOR_GENE ◊ / MASS_GENE = massgen, [matr_asse_gene_R] RIGI_GENE = rigigen, [matr_asse_gene_R] AMOR_GENE = amorgen, [matr_asse_gene_R] These operands are used together in the case where one wants to condense dynamically a part of the model with linear behaviour, by computing strictly with DYNA_NON_LINE only domains with non-linear behaviour. This is in order to reduce the size of the analysis model. In this case, it is necessary to compute a modal Ritz basis on the whole set of domains: the non-linear domain modelled for the analysis calling DYNA_NON_LINE and the other, dynamically condensed, linear domains. This basis must be orthogonalised with respect to the mass and to a linear stiffness of the whole set of domains. It must simply be representative of the motions which activate the whole set of domains. On the other hand, one will supply under MODE_MECA only the modes obtained by reduction of the Ritz basis to the analysis model treated by DYNA_NON_LINE. An example of an analysis is provided by the test case SDNV107A V5.03.107. The operand MASS_GENE makes it possible to enter the projection of the mass matrix of the whole set of domains onto the Ritz basis with a diagonal storage. The operand RIGI_GENE makes it possible to enter the projection of the stiffness matrix of the condensed linear domains alone onto the Ritz basis with a full storage. The operand AMOR_GENE makes it possible optionally to enter the projection of a damping matrix (if it exists) of the condensed linear domains alone onto the Ritz basis with a full storage. 3.23.3 Operands DEPL_INIT_GENE, VITE_INIT_GENE, ACCE_INIT_GENE ◊ DEPL_INIT_GENE = deplgen, [vect_asse_gene] ◊ VITE_INIT_GENE = vitegen, [vect_asse_gene] ◊ ACCE_INIT_GENE = accegen, [vect_asse_gene] These operands are associated with the use of the operands MASS_GENE, RIGI_GENE and possibly AMOR_GENE in the keyword PROJ_MODAL. They serve to introduce a generalised vector coming from the projection, by PROJ_VECT_BASE (TYPE='DEPL'), of a displacement or velocity or acceleration field of the complete model (including the domain with linear behaviour) onto the modal basis of this complete model. This generalised vector will serve as the initial condition of the evolution of the generalised coordinates of the analysis on the model reduced to the non-linear domain. One will then also have to supply the operands of the keyword ETAT_INIT with the corresponding fields of displacement, velocity, acceleration, stress and internal variable of the reduced model. An example of an analysis is provided by the test case SDNV107C V5.03.107. 3.24 Keyword EXCIT_GENE > ◊ EXCIT_GENE =_F( ◊ FONC_MULT = fomult, [fonction_sdaster] ♦ VECT_GENE = vecgen, [vect_asse_gene] ) This repeatable keyword is associated with the use of the operands MASS_GENE, RIGI_GENE and possibly AMOR_GENE in the keyword PROJ_MODAL. It serves to introduce the forces applied on domains of linear behaviour which are dynamically condensed and not modelled in the analysis calling an explicit time-integration scheme. These forces are projected onto the Ritz basis computed on the whole set of domains. VECT_GENE serves to supply the force vectors projected onto the Ritz basis. FONC_MULT serves to supply the time-dependent multiplying function associated with each vector within an occurrence of the keyword EXCIT_GENE. 3.25 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = inf Makes it possible to carry out, in the message file, various intermediate printouts. Other printouts are made systematically during the non-linear analysis, independently of the value assigned to the keyword INFO: these are the printouts of the residuals and of the relative displacement increments in the course of the Newton iterations. Caution: the .mess files can become very large with INFO = 2. 3.26 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = tx tx is the title of the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results.
