The keywords specific to each type of analysis are described in the following paragraphs: - Transient response analysis on a modal basis (§ 5 ) - Transient response analysis on a physical basis (§ 6 ) - Harmonic response analysis on a physical basis and on a modal basis (§ 7 ) 4 Operands common to every type of analysis 4.1 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre Title of the result data structure U4.03.01. 4.2 Operand SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR This factor keyword is optional. It makes it possible to define the method of solution of the system. The syntax is described in document U4.50.01. Note : the method MULT_FRONT is not available for the solution of systems with generalised matrices. 5 Transient response analysis on a modal basis Let us consider the finite-element model of a linear structure, presenting internal dissipation mechanisms, subjected to external forces, which may equally well be known a priori (loadings) as have to be evaluated as the analysis proceeds (shock forces, contact, etc.). In the time domain, the equilibrium relation is written: \left[{\mathrm{K}}_{e}\right] \mathrm{x}(t) + \left[{\mathrm{D}}_{v}\right] \dot{\mathrm{x}}(t) + \left[\mathrm{M}\right] \ddot{\mathrm{x}}(t) = \left[\mathrm{B}\right]\mathrm{u}(t) where {\mathrm{K}}_{e} is the stiffness matrix of the structure, {\mathrm{D}}_{v} the matrix associated with the viscous dissipation, and \mathrm{M} the mass matrix. One also denotes by \mathrm{x} the vector of the degrees of freedom. The external-force term is defined by the product of a force-localisation matrix \mathrm{B} and of a vector \mathrm{u} specifying the time evolution of the excitation. This formulation makes it possible to separate the spatial and temporal components of a force often denoted \mathrm{f}(t) . One therefore has, in this case: \mathrm{f}(t)=\left[\mathrm{B}\right]\mathrm{u}(t) The solution of the problem on the basis of the complete model presented in the relation above can be prohibitive for models of industrial size. To get round this difficulty, one proposes to build a reduced model possessing the same spectral properties as the complete problem. One therefore postulates the existence of a reduction basis {\mathrm{T}}_{r} which allows a reasonable representation of the behaviour of the structure over the frequency band of interest. Under these conditions, one therefore has: \mathrm{x}\approx \left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}\right]{\mathrm{q}}_{r} The terms {\mathrm{q}}_{r} of the linear combination correspond to the generalised amplitudes of the complete problem projected onto the basis {\mathrm{T}}_{r} . These amplitudes therefore satisfy, in the general case: \left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}{\mathrm{K}}_{e}{\mathrm{T}}_{r}\right]{\mathrm{q}}_{r}(t)+\left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}{\mathrm{D}}_{v}{\mathrm{T}}_{r}\right]\dot{{\mathrm{q}}_{r}}(t)+\left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}\mathrm{M}{\mathrm{T}}_{r}\right]\ddot{{\mathrm{q}}_{r}}(t)={\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}\mathrm{B}\mathrm{u}(t) One therefore solves here a system of smaller size whose unknowns are the generalised amplitudes {\mathrm{q}}_{r} . \left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}{\mathrm{K}}_{e}{\mathrm{T}}_{r}\right] denotes the generalised stiffness matrix. \left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}{\mathrm{D}}_{v}{\mathrm{R}}_{r}\right] denotes the generalised damping matrix. \left[{\mathrm{T}}_{r}^{T}\mathrm{M}{\mathrm{T}}_{r}\right] denotes the generalised mass matrix. The basis {\mathrm{T}}_{r} is composed, in the majority of cases, of eigenmodes of the structure under study. This selection of modes may be enriched with particular responses, in order to represent the dynamics of the response better, while avoiding recourse to too large a number of eigenmodes U2.06.04. One may cite, for the usual cases: - The static corrections associated with a point of application of a force (external, or shock), computed by imposing either a unit force or a unit displacement; - The modes with imposed accelerations, in order to represent the seismic response, or the entrainment of an embedded substructure in translation through its interfaces; - Any other term necessary for a good representation of the quasi-static response of the structure or of each substructure. These corrective terms may be computed via the operator MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14 for the generic cases, or by direct analysis, via MECA_STATIQUE U4.51.01, or MACR_ELAS_MULT U4.51.02. All these vectors are then concatenated via the operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02. By an abuse of language, this family of vectors will hereafter be called the “modal basis”. 5.1 Generalised matrices In the case of an analysis by modal recombination, the generalised matrices must be established by the operator PROJ_MATR_BASE U4.63.12 or by the macro-command PROJ_BASE U4.63.11, from the same modal basis. In the case of an analysis by dynamic substructuring, the generalised matrices must be established by the operator ASSE_MATR_GENE from the same generalised numbering. ♦ MATR_MASS = ma Mass matrix \mathrm{M} of the generalised system. Concept of type matr_asse_gene_R. ♦ MATR_RIGI = ri Stiffness matrix of the generalised system. Concept of type matr_asse_gene_R. ◊ MATR_AMOR = am Damping matrix of the generalised system. Concept of type matr_asse_gene_R. This option is not available with the ‘DEVOGE’ method. 5.2 Keyword AMOR_MODAL This keyword makes it possible to take into account a damping equivalent to a modal damping decomposed on a basis of precomputed modes in the form of a concept of type mode_meca. This damping is taken into account globally in the dynamic equilibrium equation as a corrective force on the right-hand side -\mathrm{C}\dot{\mathrm{q}} . 5.2.1 Operands AMOR_REDUIT / LIST_AMOR ◊ /AMOR_REDUIT = la List of the reduced dampings ( {\eta}_{1,}{\eta}_{2,}\mathrm{...},{\eta}_{n} percentages of the critical damping) corresponding to each mode of the system, in the form of a list of reals. This option is not available in dynamic substructuring because the reduced dampings must be defined for each substructure separately (operator MACR_ELEM_DYNA U4.65.01). Note: if the number of reduced dampings given is lower than the number of basis vectors used in the modal basis, the dampings of the additional vectors are taken equal to the last damping in the list. /LIST_AMOR = l_amor Name of the concept of type listr8 containing the list of reduced dampings. 5.3 Integration schemes. Keyword SCHEMA_TEMPS Under this keyword one may supply an integration scheme together with, if need be, its parameters. The available schemes are to be declared under the operand SCHEMA. 5.3.1 Operand SCHEMA ◊ SCHEMA Choice of the numerical solution method. In the case of a classical analysis by modal recombination, the user has several methods of explicit type, an integral method and a method of implicit type. In the case of an analysis by dynamic substructuring R4.06.04, the method of transient analysis on a modal basis computed by substructuring supports all the integration schemes mentioned. On the other hand, the method of transient analysis on the “bases” of the substructures supports only the centred-difference scheme and the schemes with adaptive time step. 5.3.1.1 SCHEMA = 'NEWMARK': implicit scheme of order 2 This scheme supports the analysis taking into account all the localised non-linearities available. One may specify the time-integration parameters \beta and \gamma : ◊ BETA = beta Value of the parameter \beta for the NEWMARK method. By default \beta =0.25 . ◊ GAMMA = gamm Value of the parameter \gamma for the NEWMARK method. By default \gamma =0.5 . 5.3.1.2 SCHEMA = 'DIFF_CENTRE': explicit scheme of order 2 This scheme supports the analysis taking into account all the localised non-linearities available. Its formulation is a parameterisation in accelerations ( Code_Aster does not offer a parameterisation in displacements for this scheme). See R5.06.04 5.3.1.3 SCHEMA = 'DEVOGE': explicit scheme of order 4 The DEVOGELAERE scheme supports the analysis taking into account all the localised non-linearities available. 5.3.1.4 SCHEMA = 'ADAPT_ORDRE2': explicit scheme of order 2 This scheme (called 'ADAPT' in earlier versions of the code) supports the analysis taking into account all the localised non-linearities available. This method uses the centred-difference scheme; the time-step adaptation algorithm relies on the computation of an “apparent frequency”: {f}_{\mathit{APt}}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\sqrt{∣\frac{\ddot{{x}_{t}}-\ddot{{x}_{t-1}}}{{x}_{t}-{x}_{t-1}}∣} The operands specific to the method of integration by adaptive time steps are specified below. They are the following operands of the factor keyword INCREMENT: ◊ NB_POIN_PERIODE = N Number of points per apparent period. It is this parameter which sets the accuracy of the analysis. It must be at least equal to 20; its default value (50) guarantees a satisfactory accuracy (of the order of 1%) in most cases. ◊ VITE_MIN = Method of computation of the reference velocity used to evaluate the apparent frequency. When the denominator of the apparent frequency ( {x}_{n}-{x}_{n-1} ) becomes small, the latter may become very high, which leads to an unjustified refinement of the time step. To remedy this, the algorithm uses the following criterion: \frac{\mid {x}_{n}-{x}_{n-1}\mid }{\Delta t}\le {V}_{min}\mathrm{\Rightarrow }{f}_{\mathit{APn}}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\sqrt{∣\frac{\ddot{{x}_{n}}-\ddot{{x}_{n-1}}}{{V}_{min}\Delta t}∣} {V}_{min} may be computed in two different ways according to the value of VITE_MIN. If VITE_MIN = 'NORM': then {V}_{min}({t}_{n})=\frac{\parallel V({t}_{n})\parallel }{100} for all the degrees of freedom. This case may be used: - if the system has several degrees of freedom, - if the order of magnitude of the displacement is not too different from one degree of freedom to another. If VITE_MIN = 'MAXI': {V}_{min}^{i}({t}_{n})=\frac{\underset{0 1 ) when the error is greater than 1, the maximum number of iterations (N_MAX_ITER_PAS) has not been reached and the minimum time step has not been reached: \Delta {t}_{n} \text{plr}\Delta {t}_{\mathit{initial}} \mathrm{\Rightarrow }\Delta {t}_{n}=\frac{\Delta {t}_{n}}{\text{cdp}} The default value is 1.33333334 , that is a reduction by a factor 0.75 . ◊ PAS_LIMI_RELA = plr Coefficient applied to the initial time step in order to define the refinement limit and therefore the minimum time step: The default value is 1.33333334 , that is a reduction by a factor 0.75 . \Delta {T}_{min}=\text{plr}\Delta {t}_{\mathit{initial}} 5.3.1.5 SCHEMA = 'RUNGE_KUTTA_54': explicit scheme with adaptive step. This scheme belongs to the family of integration schemes of Runge-Kutta type. In particular, it is the explicit integration scheme of Dormand-Prince(54) R5.06.04 with adaptive time step. The scheme 'RUNGE_KUTTA_54' supports account being taken of all the non-linearities available in the operator. The computation of the optimal time step is carried out by controlling the error between the approximations of order 5 and 4 of the prediction of the state vector (concatenation of the displacement and velocity vectors). This scheme relies on the following relative-error control condition: \mathit{err}\le \mathit{tol} With: \mathit{err}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum}_{i}\sqrt{\text{}(\frac{{y}_{\mathit{i1}}-{\hat{y}}_{\mathit{i1}}}{{\mathit{sc}}_{i}})\mathrm{²}} \textrm{et} {\mathit{sc}}_{i}=\mathit{MAX}(\mid {y}_{\mathit{i0}}\mid ,\mid {y}_{\mathit{i1}}\mid )+\alpha Where: - {y}_{\mathit{i1}} is the value of the order-5 prediction of component i of the state vector y - {\hat{y}}_{\mathrm{1i}} is the value of the order-4 prediction of component i of the state vector y - n is the size of the state vector y - {y}_{\mathrm{0i}} is the value of component i of the state vector y at the current state ◊ TOLERANCE = tol Value of the relative-error control given by the user. By default it is equal to 1.E-3. ◊ ALPHA = alpha Value of the regularisation given by the user, entering into the expression for {\mathit{sc}}_{i} . By default it is equal to 1.E-3. 5.3.1.6 SCHEMA = 'RUNGE_KUTTA_32': explicit scheme with adaptive step. This is the default scheme for the transient analysis on a modal basis. Like the scheme 'RUNGE_KUTTA_54', the scheme 'RUNGE_KUTTA_32' belongs to the family of integration schemes of Runge-Kutta type. In this case, it is the explicit integration scheme of Bogacki-Shampine(32) R5.06.04 with adaptive time step. Like the previous scheme, it supports account being taken of all the non-linearities available in the operator. For this scheme, the computation of the optimal time step is carried out by controlling the error between the approximations of order 3 and 2 of the prediction of the state vector. The computation of the optimal time step itself is carried out in a manner analogous to the previous scheme. 5.3.1.7 SCHEMA = 'ADAPT_ORDRE1': explicit scheme of order 1 This scheme is a variant of the previous scheme 'ADAPT_ORDRE2'. It is in fact a version of the Euler scheme with adaptive time step. Apart from this difference, this scheme is used in the same way as the adaptive scheme of order 2: the syntax of the keywords is the same, and so are the methods for driving the time step. 5.3.1.8 SCHEMA = 'ITMI': integral scheme for the analysis of the response of very lightly damped mechanical systems This integration scheme by the integral method makes it possible, for lightly damped systems, to obtain an exact response provided that the dynamic matrices of mass, stiffness and damping are diagonal. 5.3.1.9 SCHEMA = 'TRBDF2': implicit scheme of order 2 This dissipative predictor-corrector scheme supports the analysis taking into account all the localised non-linearities available. It has very good stability properties, which make it a good candidate for stiff problems. 5.4 Keyword INCREMENT 5.4.1 Operands LIST_INST/PAS/VERI_PAS/PAS_MINI/PAS_MAXI ♦ / LIST_INST = l_temp Concept list of reals of type listr8. List of reals defining the time instants {t}_{i} of computation of the solution - Schemes 'RUNGE_KUTTA_54' and 'RUNGE_KUTTA32': For schemes of Runge-Kutta type, the keyword LIST_INST is not taken into account. / PAS = dt - Schemes 'DIFF_CENTRE', 'NEWMARK', 'ITMI': Time step of the transient analysis. - Schemes 'ADAPT_ORDRE1' and 'ADAPT_ORDRE2': Denotes the initial time step used by the algorithm. This parameter must be sufficiently small: - to allow the computation of the static phases (which always uses the maximum time step), - to start the algorithm correctly. It must however be sufficiently large so as not to penalise the analysis as a whole. - Schemes 'RUNGE_KUTTA_54', 'RUNGE_KUTTA32' and 'DEVOGE': Denotes the initial time step proposed by the user. If the prediction error between the control orders satisfies \mathit{err}\le 1 , then this is the first analysis step. Otherwise, the algorithm automatically chooses the time step required in order to satisfy this condition. Thereafter, the choice of the time step in the Runge-Kutta algorithms is managed automatically. ◊ VERI_PAS= rep Check of the analysis time step against the limiting time step determined as a function of the highest frequency of the modes of the modal basis considered, or of the bases of the substructures. Operands specific to an integration by adaptive time steps with the schemes 'ADAPT_ORDRE1', 'ADAPT_ORDRE2' as well as 'RUNGE_KUTTA_54' and 'RUNGE_KUTTA_32' and 'DEVOGE'. ◊ PAS_MAXI = dtmax Maximum value of the time step. If the conditions for increasing the time step are satisfied, the current time step may then increase up to this limiting value. If the user does not give a value to this optional parameter, the adaptive schemes of type ADAPT_ORDRE1/2 will estimate a value denoted \mathit{dts} from the cut-off frequency of the basis (possibly corrected by the shock stiffnesses). On the other hand, the other adaptive schemes (Runge-Kutta, De Vogelaere) will have no upper limitation in terms of time step. To recover the behaviour of earlier versions of the code, it is sufficient to impose: \mathit{dtmax}=\mathit{dt} , thus the same value for the parameter PAS as for PAS_MAXI. ◊ PAS_MINI = dtmin Minimum value of the time step. If the conditions for decreasing the time step are satisfied, the current time step may then decrease down to this limiting value. If the user does not give a value to this optional parameter, then the code will compute the minimum time step close to machine precision. To recover the behaviour of earlier versions of the code, it is therefore sufficient not to define PAS_MINI. Important note: in order to force an integration scheme to switch to constant-step mode, it is sufficient to choose PAS_MAXI= PAS_MINI=PAS=dt 5.4.2 Operands INST_INIT/INST_FIN/NUME_FIN ◊ INST_INIT= to Methods ‘DIFF_CENTRE’, ‘DEVOGE’, ‘NEWMARK’, ‘ADAPT_ORDRE1’ and ‘ADAPT_ORDRE2’: Time instant of the start of the transient analysis. In the event of a restart, one uses the keyword ETAT_INIT: under this keyword, the initial time instant is recovered with the operand INST_INIT or taken equal to the last archived time instant of the previous analysis. The operand INST_INIT must therefore be used only if there is no restart of a previous analysis. ◊ /INST_FIN= tf Time instant of the end of the simulation. /NUME_FIN= tf Number of the time instant of the end of the analysis in LIST_INST 5.5 Keyword ETAT_INIT Factor keyword which allows a restart of a transient analysis, taking as initial state: - either a result coming from a previous analysis by modal synthesis EXCIT(RESULTAT); - or displacements and velocities expressed in the form of generalised assembled vectors EXCIT(DEPL and VITE) Notes: - This functionality is not available for a transient analysis by substructuring without double projection. - The generalised displacements and velocities must be established by the operator PROJ_VECT_BASE U4.63.13 from the modal basis used for the generalised stiffness matrices, or by the operator RECU_GENE U4.71.03 applied to a previous analysis. 5.5.1 Operands RESU/DEPL/VITE ♦/ RESULTAT = tran Concept of type tran_gene coming from a previous analysis with DYNA_VIBRA. / I DEPL = do Concept of type vect_asse_gene, initial generalised displacements. I VITE = vo Concept of type vect_asse_gene, initial generalised velocities. 5.5.2 Operands INST_INIT / NUME_ORDRE ◊ /INST_INIT = to Time instant of the previous analysis to be extracted and taken as the initial state in the case of a restart. In the absence of this operand, the restart time instant is taken equal to the last archived time instant of the previous analysis. /NUME_ORDRE = nuord Designates the archiving number of the previous analysis to be extracted and taken as the initial state in the case of a restart. 5.5.3 Operand CRITERE ◊ CRITERE Indicates with what precision the search for the time instant must be carried out: 'RELATIF': search interval [(1-prec).instant, (1+prec).instant] 'ABSOLU': search interval [instant-prec, instant+prec] The criterion is 'RELATIF' by default. 5.5.4 Operand PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = / 1.E-06 [DEFAUT] / prec [:ref: R8 ] Indicates with what precision the search for the time instant must be carried out. 5.6 Description of the loading in separated variables: keyword EXCIT ◊ EXCIT Keyword defining the loading. This keyword must be repeated as many times as there are generalised loading vectors {f}_{i} . The total loading is the sum of these loading vectors. This keyword makes it possible to define the loading in the form of generalised vectors multiplied by multiplying functions. 5.6.1 Operands VECT_ASSE_GENE / NUME_ORDRE The loading is taken into account in the form of a vector projected onto the modal basis EXCIT=_F(VECT_ASSE_GENE), or in the form of a modal component EXCIT=_F(NUME_MODE), or both at once. VECT_ASSE_GENE= v Generalised vector making it possible to describe the spatial distribution of the loading. Concept of type vect_asse_gene. The generalised vectors must be established by the operator PROJ_VECT_BASE U4.63.13 from the modal basis used for the generalised matrices. In the case of an analysis by dynamic substructuring, the generalised vectors must be established by the operator ASSE_VECT_GENE U4.65.05 from the generalised numbering used for the generalised matrices. / NUME_ORDRE= nmordr Order number of the excitation mode of the structure (Warning! One must not confuse the order number of the mode — given by the modal analysis in the order in which they were computed — and the number of the mode, called NUME_MODE in Code_Aster ). 5.6.2 Operand FONC_MULT / COEF_MULT ♦ / FONC_MULT= f Function of time (fonction) making it possible to describe the time evolution of the loading vector. / COEF_MULT= a Multiplying coefficient of the generalised vector (real value constant with respect to time). 5.7 Keyword EXCIT_RESU Keyword making it possible to define a loading in the form of a generalised time evolution, without separation of variables (the most general case). This time evolution may have been computed from the operator PROJ_BASE, option RESU_GENE, which carries out the projection of a transient dynamic result (dyna_trans). 5.7.1 Keyword RESULTAT ♦ / RESULTAT= resu_gene Data structure resu_gene defining the generalised loading. 5.7.2 Operand COEF_MULT ◊ / COEF_MULT= f Multiplying coefficient; it is equal to 1.0 by default. 5.8 Particular case of the seismic analysis 5.8.1 Account taken of the neglected modes by static correction: keywords CORR_STAT, MODE_CORR and D_FONC_ During the seismic analysis of a singly excited structure, it is possible to take into account, a posteriori, the static effect of the neglected modes. In this case, on return to the physical basis, the relative displacements computed (respectively the relative velocities and accelerations) are corrected by a pseudo-mode. The details of this type of correction will be found in R4.05.01. Inside the factor keyword EXCIT, CORR_STAT='OUI' allows the neglected modes to be taken into account by static correction; it is then obligatory to supply the keywords MODE_CORR, D_FONC_DT and D_FONC_DT2. ◊ MODE_CORR = modcor Concept of type mult_elas produced by the macro-command MACRO_ELAS_MULT U4.51.02, or mode_meca, which corresponds to the linear static response of the structure to a unit loading of imposed-force type (uniform acceleration) in the earthquake direction considered. One notes that there are as many load cases as earthquake directions. ◊ EXCIT = _F( CORR_STAT ) If MODE_CORR is present, CORR_STAT='OUI' makes it possible to take into account the contribution of the modal correction a posteriori for each occurrence of the keyword EXCIT. ◊ EXCIT = _F( D_FONC_DTet D_FONC_DT2) D_FONC_DT and D_FONC_DT2 are respectively the first derivatives and the second derivatives with respect to time of the accelerogram defined, in each seismic direction considered, by the operand FONC_MULT. They weight the contribution of the modal correction a posteriori for each occurrence of the keyword EXCIT in order to obtain respectively the velocity and acceleration corrections on the physical basis. Notes: - Taking the static correction into account excludes that of multi-support excitation. - The concept mult_elas must be based on a numbering of the equations consistent (same profile and same renumbering option) with that of the system solved in the operator DYNA_VIBRA . - To the i th occurrence of the keyword EXCIT there corresponds the i th elastic solution of MODCOR . - For the static correction to be effectively taken into account on return to the physical coordinates in the operator REST_GENE_PHYS or RECU_FONCTION , one must specify CORR_STAT_='OUI'. 5.8.2 Account taken of multi-support excitation: keywords MODE_STAT, MULTI_APPUI and ACCE, VITE, DEPL In the case of a multi-supported structure, in order to recover the computed quantities in the absolute frame or to take localised non-linearities into account, one must compute the generalised response taking the entrainment component into account. For further details, one will refer to the reference R4.05.01. The keywords MODE_STAT, MULT_APPUI, ACCE, VITE, DEPL, DIRECTION and GROUP_NO) specific to taking the multi-supported character into account must be present simultaneously. A cham_no coming from the projection of a CALC_CHAR_SEISME represents the excitation vector on the support. It must not be forgotten, even if the information may appear redundant with the data of the support and of the earthquake direction. ◊ MODE_STAT = psi Concept of type mode_meca produced by the command MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14, which corresponds to the (3 or 6) nb_supports static modes (where nb_supports is the number of supports which undergo a different acceleration). ◊ EXCIT = _F( MULT_APPUI ) If one computes the seismic response of a multi-supported structure, MULT_APPUI= ’OUI’, one compares at each time instant the vector of the absolute displacements of each of the shock points considered, in order to determine whether there is a shock and to compute the corresponding shock forces. Otherwise, MULT_APPUI= ’NON’, one compares at each time instant the vector of the relative displacements of each of the nodes liable to come into shock. ◊ EXCIT = _F( / ◊ ACCE = ac, ◊ VITE = vi, ◊ DEPL = dp ) Names of the acceleration (ACCE), velocity (VITE) and displacement (DEPL) functions imposed during the analysis of the seismic response of multi-supported structures. Note: If the structure is singly excited, the accelerogram is defined by the keyword FONC_MULT. ◊ EXCIT = _F( DIRECTION =(dx, dy, dz, drx, dry, drz)) Components of the vector giving the direction of the earthquake in the global frame. ◊ EXCIT = _F( GROUP_NO = lgrno ) List of the names of the node groups corresponding to the supports concerned, where the earthquake is imposed. ◊ EXCIT = _F( VECT_ASSE_GENE = v ) Projected vector of the seismic excitation (coming from CALC_CHAR_SEISME U4.63.01) 5.9 Account taken of a rotational-speed transient 5.9.1 Operand VITESSE_VARIABLE Specifies whether the rotational speed of the rotor is variable as a function of time (VITESSE_VARIABLE = 'OUI' for speed transients) or constant (VITESSE_VARIABLE = 'NON'). 5.9.2 Operands VITE_ROTA, MATR_GYRO, ACCE_ROTA and MATR_RIGY These operands are the parameters defining the rotational-speed transient. If VITESSE_VARIABLE = 'OUI', then the following parameters must be supplied: ♦ VITE_ROTA = function giving the imposed angular-velocity law of the rotor ♦ MATR_GYRO = gyroscopic damping matrix ◊ ACCE_ROTA = function giving the imposed angular-acceleration law of the rotor ◊ MATR_RIGY = gyroscopic stiffness matrix Note: If ACCE_ROTA is not supplied, it is neglected (i.e. no numerical differentiation from VITE_ROTA). If VITESSE_VARIABLE = 'NON', the value of the constant rotational speed must be supplied. ◊ VITE_ROTA = rotational speed of the shaft [by default 0.0] 5.10 Keyword VERI_CHOC Keyword which makes it possible to evaluate a posteriori the ability of the modal basis to represent the impacts correctly. If VERI_CHOC is present, one computes at each shock node and for each mode the rate of reconstitution of the static solution: {t}_{s}={K}_{\mathit{statique}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{{({}^{T}{\Phi}_{i}.{F}_{\mathit{impo}})}^{2}}{{k}_{i}} and, for information, the rate of reconstitution of the shear force: {t}_{N}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{{}^{T}{\Phi}_{i}.{F}_{\mathit{impo}}}{{k}_{i}}.({}^{T}{F}_{\mathit{impo}}.K.{\Phi}_{i}) . One then computes the values cumulated over all the modes which constitute the modal basis used. One checks that the ratio of the neglected flexibility (static flexibility minus reconstituted static flexibility) to the shock flexibility remains lower than the value given by the operand SEUIL (SEUIL is equal to 0.5 by default); otherwise: - if STOP_CRITERE= ‘OUI’ one stops the execution of the program (this is the default case); - if STOP_CRITERE= ‘NON’ one continues the execution of the program with the issue of an alarm. Notes: - This functionality is available only for obstacles of type plan or bi_plan. - If the rate of reconstitution of the static solution is lower than the value of the threshold, the user is advised to complete the modal basis with the local modes at the shock points which have a large local flexibility. - The formula is not applicable in the case of static modes (stiffness matrix not invertible). The analysis then continues without checking of the shock criteria, and the user is warned of this. 5.11 Keyword COMPORTEMENT This factor keyword makes it possible to define a localised non-linear constitutive behaviour (applied on a node). Several types of constitutive behaviour are available. 5.11.1 Localised non-linearities of shock and friction type: DIS_CHOC ◊ RELATION = 'DIS_CHOC This keyword is used for the study of the response of structures (generally slender) whose displacements are limited at one (or several) point(s) — specified a priori by the user — by the presence of an obstacle (the various types of obstacles available are described in the documentation U4.44.21 of the operator DEFI_OBSTACLE), or of another opposing structure. 5.11.1.1 Operand INTITULE ◊ INTITULE= int Heading (eight characters at most) making it possible to name the non-linearity. If nothing is specified by the user, the heading is the name of the node of GROUP_NO_1. 5.11.1.2 Operands GROUP_NO_1 / GROUP_NO_2 . / GROUP_MA ♦ GROUP_NO_1 Name of the node group of the structure to which the non-linearity condition applies. In the case of a non-linear analysis by dynamic substructuring, one indicates under this keyword the shock node belonging to the first substructure (the various substructures do not belong to the same mesh). ◊ GROUP_NO_2 Name of the node group of the second structure to which the non-linearity condition applies. This operand is specific to the definition of a contact between two moving structures. In the case of a non-linear analysis by dynamic substructuring, one specifies the shock node coinciding with the node indicated in GROUP_NO_1, but belonging to the second substructure. Note: One checks that the node groups do indeed contain one and only one node. ♦ GROUP_MA One may also enter the facing shock nodes in the form of SEG2 mesh cells drawn in the mesh. In this way one keeps the same manner of describing the shocks as for DYNA_NON_LINE with the discrete shock elements (DIS_CHOC). One may enter a list of GROUP_MA. 5.11.1.3 Operand OBSTACLE ♦ OBSTACLE= obs Name of the concept of type obstacle defining the geometry of a non-deformable obstacle, or the envelope shape of the gap between two opposing structures. It is produced by the operator DEFI_OBSTACLE U4.44.21. 5.11.1.4 Operand NORM_OBST ♦ NORM_OBST= nor List of 3 reals defining the normal to the cutting plane of the obstacle, that is to say the vector {X}_{\mathit{loc}} as defined in the documentation of the operator DEFI_OBSTACLE U4.44.21. It is advised that {X}_{\mathit{loc}} be the direction of the neutral fibre or of a generatrix of the structure under study. Notes: - In spite of the name given to the operand, NORM_OBST is not a vector normal to the obstacle, but normal to the contact direction for the obstacles PLAN or BI_PLAN, or to the contact directions for the other types of obstacles; - In the case of an obstacle of type BI_PLAN_Y or BI_PLAN_Z, it is recommended to specify the twist angle (operand ANGL_VRIL), or to define the vector {X}_{\mathit{loc}} in the plane formed by the vector defined by the nodes of the groups GROUP_NO_1 and GROUP_NO_2 and the vector normal to the desired contact direction. cf. operand ANGL_VRIL. 5.11.1.5 Operand ORIG_OBST ◊ ORIG_OBST= ori List of 3 reals defining the position of the origin of the obstacle in the global frame (keyword obligatory in the case of shocks between a moving structure and a fixed wall). In the case of shocks between two moving structures, the code considers by default that the origin is situated midway between the two shock nodes GROUP_NO_1 and GROUP_NO_2. 5.11.1.6 Operand JEU ◊ JEU= jeu In the case of a shock between a moving structure and a non-deformable obstacle, the operand JEU represents: - the half-distance between planes for obstacles of type PLAN_Y and PLAN_Z - the radius of the circular obstacle for an obstacle of type CERCLE This keyword is unused in the case of obstacles discretised by segments of type DISCRET. Note: The obstacle of type PLAN_Y or PLAN_Z in fact comprises two plane obstacles. Thus, in the case where the user wishes to model the shock on a single plane, so as not to be hindered by the rebound of the structure under study on the symmetric plane, the user is advised to push it very far away (cf. figure below; one represents the real gap between the structure under study and the obstacle). Mass-spring system impacting a fixed wall Note: The keyword JEU is not used in the case of a shock between moving structures. The various cases of gaps are represented in the documentation of DEFI_OBSTACLE U4.44.21. 5.11.1.7 Operand ANGL_VRIL ◊ ANGL_VRIL= gamma \gamma , angle in degrees completing the definition of the angular position of the local frame in the global frame. By convention, the normal to the cutting plane of the obstacle, NORM_OBST, defines the axis {X}_{\mathit{loc}} of the local frame. For obstacles of type PLAN or BI_PLAN, this normal is not unique. Any vector lying in the plane of the obstacle is a vector normal to one of the cutting planes of the obstacle. For all the other obstacles, this orientation is unique. One passes from the global frame (X,Y,Z) to the local frame of the plane of the obstacle ({X}_{\mathit{loc}}, {Y}_{\mathit{loc}}, {Z}_{\mathit{loc}}) by a product of three rotations following the Euler angles: - A first rotation R_1(\alpha, Z) of angle \alpha about the axis Z of the global frame; - A second rotation R_2(\beta, Y_1) of angle \beta about the vector {Y}_{1} , the image of Y under R_1(\alpha, Z) ; - A third rotation R_3(\gamma, X_2) of angle \gamma about the vector {X}_{2} , the image of X_1 under R_2(\beta, Y_1) . The first figure below gives the position of the plane of an obstacle of type PLAN_Z (or BI_PLAN_Z) in the global frame (X, Y, Z) , and the associated local frame ({X}_{\mathit{loc}}, {Y}_{\mathit{loc}}, {Z}_{\mathit{loc}}) . The second figure below describes the set of rotations, with their parameters, allowing the passage from the global frame to the local frame. Position of the obstacle and of its local frame in the global frame, and view of the complete composition of the rotations. Decomposition of the complete motion into elementary rotations parameterised by the Euler angles. The angles \alpha and \beta are determined automatically from the normal to the obstacle {X}_{\mathit{loc}} . \alpha corresponds to the angle formed by X and X_1 , where X_1 is the projection of {X}_{\mathit{loc}} onto the plane (X, Y) . \beta is the angle formed by X_1 and X_{\mathit{loc}} . If X_{\mathit{loc}} is collinear with Z , then \alpha is taken equal to 0. The sole datum X_{\mathit{loc}} does not make it possible to position the local frame completely; one must then define \gamma , called the twist angle, in order to position the obstacle completely: - For all types of obstacles, with the exception of obstacles of type BI_PLAN, the default value of \gamma is zero. It is then essential to check that this value is indeed the one expected , or, otherwise, to indicate the desired value; - In the case of shocks between moving structures with obstacles of type BI_PLAN, if the user specifies nothing, the twist angle is computed by the code . The procedure for computing the twist angle for the case of obstacles of type BI_PLAN is detailed below. If one denotes by {N_1}{N_2} the vector defined by the nodes of GROUP_NO_1 and GROUP_NO_2, the twist angle is computed from the directions of the vectors {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} and {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} , where {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} is obtained by projection: - of the vector {N_1}{N_2} onto the plane normal to {X}_{\mathit{loc}} for the case of an obstacle BI_PLAN_Y; - of the vector {N_1}{N_2} \wedge {X}_{\mathit{loc}} onto the plane normal to {X}_{\mathit{loc}} for the case of an obstacle BI_PLAN_Z, and {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} completes the triad, so that ( {X}_{\mathit{loc}} , {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} , {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} ) is right-handed. If one does not pay attention to this point, and if one does not specify the operand ANGL_VRIL, it is possible to obtain results which are surprising at first sight. One solution making it possible to guard against the results of this computation consists in arranging that the direction normal to the contact ( {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} for an obstacle of type BI_PLAN_Y, or {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} for an obstacle of type BI_PLAN_Z) lies in the plane formed by the vectors {X}_{\mathit{loc}} and {N}_{1}{N}_{2} . This amounts to choosing {X}_{\mathit{loc}} such that: - {X}_{\mathit{loc}} lies in the plane of the obstacle; - {X}_{\mathit{loc}} lies in the plane formed by the vector {N_1}{N_2} and the vector normal to the contact direction ( {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} or {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} , according to the type of obstacle chosen). This choice of {X}_{\mathit{loc}} , given the procedure for computing the twist angle, guarantees the correct orientation of the vectors {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} and {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} , whatever the type of obstacle chosen. In all the other cases of choice of {X}_{\mathit{loc}} , it is strongly recommended to specify the twist angle, in order to avoid unexpected behaviours. This need is illustrated by means of the following simple case. The model consists of two beams, oriented by the axis Y of the global frame, which may strike one another at the nodes {N}_{1} and {N}_{2} along the direction carried by the axis Z of the global frame. These two beams lie in a plane parallel to the plane (Y, Z) , but the vector {N_1}{N_2} is not collinear with Z . The definition of an associated obstacle of type BI_PLAN is represented in the figure below. Representation of the desired contact case. To obtain this result, one wishes to use an obstacle of type BI_PLAN_Z. By definition, the direction {X}_{\mathit{loc}} must be normal to the cutting plane of the obstacle (and therefore, here, contained in the planes defining the obstacles). It is possible to choose {X}_{\mathit{loc}} as being the direction X of the global frame (case (a) in the figure below, with NORM_OBST = (1, 0, 0)), but also as being the direction {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} of the global frame (case (b) in this same figure, with NORM_OBST = (0, 1, 0)). Any other choice of vector in the plane ( {X} , {Y} ) is possible. On the other hand, only case (b) corresponds to the recommendation formulated. Representation of 2 possible choices for {X}_{\mathit{loc}} (operand NORM_OBST), and of the desired contact direction {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} . The figure below represents the planes associated with this obstacle in cases (a) and (b) when the operand ANGL_VRIL is not supplied , and when it is the code which computes it. It appears that case (a) does not correspond to what is desired (as in all the cases where {X}_{\mathit{loc}} is not collinear with Y ), since the vector {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} obtained is not collinear with the vector Z , which is desired in order to define the contact direction. {Y}_{\mathit{loc}} , on the other hand, does indeed correspond to the direction obtained by projection of the vector {N_1}{N_2} \wedge {X}_{\mathit{loc}} onto the plane normal to {X}_{\mathit{loc}} , and {Z}_{\mathit{loc}} completes the triad. To obtain the desired result, in this case, one must specify ANGL_VRIL = 0. In case (b), on the other hand, since the vector {X}_{\mathit{loc}} does indeed lie in the plane formed by the vector {N_1}{N_2} and the desired contact direction, one does obtain the desired result without needing to specify the operand ANGL_VRIL. Results obtained in the two cases if ANGL_VRIL is not supplied. 5.11.1.8 Operands DIST_1/DIST_2 ◊ DIST_1= dist1 Characteristic distance of material surrounding GROUP_NO_1: no1. Operand specific to contact between two moving structures. ◊ DIST_2= dist2 Characteristic distance of material surrounding GROUP_NO_2: no2. Operand specific to contact between two moving structures. Notes: - DIST_1 and DIST_2 are defined in the sense of the outward normals of the two solids facing each other (DIST_1 and DIST_2 are positive because they represent the thickness of the structures under study). - Because of the computation of the normal shock distance, the sum of DIST_1 and of DIST_2 must be sufficiently large with respect to the supposed amplitude of the relative displacement of the shock nodes (cf. R5.06.03). 5.11.1.9 Operands SOUS_STRUC_1 / SOUS_STRUC_2 ◊ SOUS_STRUC_1= ss1 Name of the substructure which contains the shock node supplying the keyword GROUP_NO_1. ◊ SOUS_STRUC_2= ss2 Name of the substructure which contains the shock node supplying the keyword GROUP_NO_2. 5.11.1.10 Operand REPERE ◊ REPERE = rep Specifies the frame in which the position of the obstacle is defined. / 'GLOBAL' The absolute position of the obstacle is defined independently of the rotations and translations to which the various substructures are subjected. / nom_sst Name of a substructure. The position and the normal of the obstacle are determined in the frame used to define the coordinates of the nodes of the substructure nom_sst, the final position and normal of the obstacle being the result of the rotation and of the translation to which the substructure is subjected. 5.11.1.11 Operand RIGI_NOR ♦ RIGI_NOR= kn Value of the normal shock stiffness (unit N/m in SI units). 5.11.1.12 Operand AMOR_NOR ◊ AMOR_NOR= cn Value of the normal shock damping (unit Nm/s in SI units). 5.11.1.13 Operand RIGI_TAN ♦ RIGI_TAN= kt Value of the tangential shock stiffness (unit N/m in SI units). 5.11.1.14 Operand AMOR_TAN ◊ AMOR_TAN= ct Value of the tangential shock damping (unit Nm/s in SI units). Note: If a stiffness {k}_{t} is specified and the keyword AMOR_TAN is absent, the code computes an optimised damping so as to minimise the residual oscillations in sticking, according to the formula: {c}_{t}=2\sqrt{({k}_{i}+{k}_{t}){m}_{i}}-2{\xi}_{i}\sqrt{{k}_{i}{m}_{i}} where i is the index of the predominant mode in the tangential direction in the response of the structure (the largest modal mass normalised by the tangential displacement). 5.11.1.15 Operand FROTTEMENT ◊ FROTTEMENT= / 'NON' The contact condition is frictionless. / 'COULOMB' ♦ COULOMB = mu Value of the coefficient of friction (dimensionless). / 'COULOMB_STAT_DYNA' ♦ COULOMB_STAT = mus Value of the coefficient of adhesion (dimensionless). > ♦ COULOMB_DYNA = mud Value of the coefficient of sliding (dimensionless). 5.11.1.16 Operand UNIDIRECTIONNEL ◊ UNIDIRECTIONNEL = / 'NON', [DEFAUT] / 'OUI', Activation of unidirectional friction, making it possible to define a non-isotropic coefficient of friction in the plane of the obstacle. This option may be used equally well with friction of type 'COULOMB' as with friction 'COULOMB_STAT_DYNA'. It is used to model the rolling and the friction of a roller on a rail, while still allowing lift-off. With a friction of type 'COULOMB': The coefficient of friction is equal to 0 along the axis supplied in NORM_OBST and mu in the perpendicular direction (cf. R5.06.03). With a friction of type 'COULOMB_STAT_DYNA': The coefficient of adhesion is equal to 0 along the axis supplied in NORM_OBST and mus in the perpendicular direction. The coefficient of sliding is equal to 0 along the axis supplied in NORM_OBST and mud in the perpendicular direction. 5.11.2 Localised non-linearities of a cracked rotor: ROTOR_FISS The following operands are specific to the transient analysis with a localised non-linearity of “cracked rotor” type for analyses of a shaft line modelled in 1D (beam). The crack is considered to be wholly contained in a cross-section of the rotor. It is bounded by two distinct nodes but with coincident coordinates, one connected to the left-hand part of the shaft line, the other to the right-hand part. They represent respectively the left lip and the right lip of the crack. The behaviour of the crack is given by a crack-stiffness law and its derivative. This law is determined elsewhere by 3D analyses in quasi-statics. It does not depend on the geometry of the rotor but only on the shape of the crack and on a dimensional coefficient. ◊ RELATION = 'ROTOR_FISS' > / ♦ GROUP_NO_G = node group naming the left lip of the crack > ♦ GROUP_NO_D = node group naming the right lip of the crack > ♦ ANGL_INIT = initial angle of the crack front with respect to its definition in the constitutive law of the crack [by default 0.0] > ◊ ANGL_ROTA = function giving the imposed law of angular position of the crack front with respect to its definition in the constitutive law of the crack (speed transients) > ♦ K_PHI = constitutive law in stiffness of the crack > ♦ DK_DPHI = derivative of the constitutive law in stiffness Orientation of the axis of the rotor: In order to respect the trigonometric sense of rotation, it is important to orient the rotor correctly: the axis of the rotor is automatically oriented by the crack, going from the left edge towards the right edge of the crack. 5.11.3 Localised non-linearity: ANTI_SISM ◊ RELATION = 'ANTI_SISM' This relation ANTI_SISM is incompatible with an analysis by dynamic substructuring. It makes it possible to compute the non-linear force which exists if an anti-seismic device is placed between the two opposing nodes whose names are specified by the keywords (GROUP_NO_1 and GROUP_NO_2): {F}_{D}={K}_{2}x+\frac{({K}_{1}-{K}_{2})x}{\sqrt{1+{({K}_{1}\frac{x}{{P}_{y}})}^{2}}}+C\mathit{sign}(\dot{x}){∣\dot{x}\frac{x}{{x}_{max}}∣}^{\alpha} {F}_{D}={K}_{2}x+\frac{({K}_{1}-{K}_{2})x}{\sqrt{1+{({K}_{1}\frac{x}{{P}_{y}})}^{2}}}+C\mathit{sign}(\dot{x}){∣\dot{x}\frac{x}{{x}_{max}}∣}^{\alpha} ◊ RIGI_K1, RIGI_K2, SEUIL_FX, C, PUIS_ALPHA et DX_MAX Parameters of the force due to the presence of an anti-seismic device. By way of example, the values of the parameters for an anti-seismic device of JARRET type are: \mathit{K1}=6.E+06N/m , \mathit{K2}=0.53E+06N/m , \mathit{Py}=1200. , C=0.07E+05\mathit{Nm}/s , alpha=0.2 and \mathit{xmax}=0.03m (if the problem is posed in SI units). 5.11.4 Non-linearity: DIS_VISC It is a non-linear viscoelastic constitutive behaviour between two nodes, cf. R5.03.17. This constitutive behaviour affects only the local degree of freedom \mathit{DX} of the element. The local direction x of the element goes from node 1 to node 2. Notes: - It is a non-linear viscoelastic constitutive behaviour between two nodes; there is therefore no finite element between the nodes concerned (only a constitutive relation). When computing the reduced modal basis, it may be judicious to define an element with an elastic stiffness corresponding to the tangent to the behaviour of the device R5.03.17 . - The results concerning the force, the viscous and relative displacements between the two nodes, as well as the dissipation of the non-linear device, may be saved in a file directly usable by the commands of Code_Aster. The definition of the file is made by the simple keyword UNITE_DIS_VISC , which is in the factor keyword IMPRESSION of the command. Diagram of the device. 5.11.4.1 Syntax ◊ RELATION = 'DIS_VISC' > ♦ GROUP_NO_1 =grno1, [group_no] > ♦ GROUP_NO_2 =grno2, [group_no] > ♦ /K1 =k1, [R] =usk1, [R] > ♦ /K2 =k2, [R] =usk2, [R] > ♦ /K3 =k3, [R] =usk3, [R] > ♦ C =c, [R] > ♦ PUIS_ALPHA =/0.5 [defaut] > /alpha, [R] > ♦ ITER_INTE_MAXI =/20 [defaut] [I] > ♦ RESI_INTE_RELA =/1.0E-06 [defaut] [R] 5.11.4.2 Operands related to the position of the device ♦ GROUP_NO_1 ♦ GROUP_NO_2 Names of the node groups of the structure between which the non-linear device is placed. The node group must contain only one node. During the analysis, it is necessary to know the direction of the non-linear device because it works only along its axis. The distance between the two nodes must therefore be non-zero. 5.11.4.3 Operands related to the constitutive behaviour The constitutive behaviour DIS_VISC is a non-linear viscoelastic rheological constitutive behaviour, of extended Zener type, making it possible to represent schematically the behaviour of a uniaxial damper, between two nodes. For the local direction x (and only that one) of the device, one supplies five coefficients. Their units must be consistent with the unit of the forces, the unit of the lengths and the unit of time of the problem: - K1: elastic stiffness of element 1 of the rheological model, - K2: elastic stiffness of element 2 of the rheological model, - K3: elastic stiffness of element 3 of the rheological model, - UNSUR_K1: elastic flexibility of element 1 of the rheological model, - UNSUR_K2: elastic flexibility of element 2 of the rheological model, - UNSUR_K3: elastic flexibility of element 3 of the rheological model, - PUIS_ALPHA: power of the viscous behaviour of the element \alpha , - C: coefficient of the viscous behaviour of the element. There are conditions to be respected on the values of the coefficients so that the tangent is always defined: \mathit{k1}\ge {10}^{-8} \mathit{usk1}\ge 0 \mathit{k3}\ge {10}^{-8} \mathit{usk3}\ge 0 \mathit{usk2}\ge {10}^{-8} \mathit{k2}\ge 0 C\ge {10}^{-8} {10}^{-8}\le \alpha \le 1 One therefore cannot have at the same time \mathit{usk1}=0 , \mathit{usk3}=0 and \mathit{k2}=0 , that is to say the case of the damper alone. 5.11.4.4 Operands related to the convergence of the constitutive behaviour of the device ♦ ITER_INTE_MAXI =/20 [defaut] [I] ♦ RESI_INTE_RELA =/1.0E-06 [defaut] [R] These operands have the same meaning as when they are used with the command STAT_NON_LINE/COMPORTEMENT U4.51.11. The constitutive relation DIS_VISC requires the solution of a non-linear system by a Runge-Kutta method of order 5 with adaptive step. The control of the algorithm (number of iterations and residual) is used to test the convergence and to adapt the step if need be. 5.11.5 Non-linearity: DIS_ECRO_TRAC The constitutive behaviour DIS_ECRO_TRAC is a non-linear constitutive behaviour, making it possible to represent schematically the behaviour of a uniaxial device, along the local axis x or in the tangent plane yz . Note: It is a non-linear constitutive behaviour between two nodes; there is therefore no finite element between the nodes concerned (only a constitutive relation). When computing the reduced modal basis, it may be judicious to define an element with an elastic stiffness corresponding to the tangent to the behaviour of the device R5.03.17 . The non-linear constitutive behaviour is given by a curve F=\mathit{fonction}(\Delta U) : - \Delta u represents the relative displacement of the 2 nodes in the local frame of the element. - F represents the force expressed in the local frame of the element. 5.11.5.1 Syntax ◊ RELATION = 'DIS_ECRO_TRAC' > ♦ GROUP_NO_1 =grno1, [group_no] > ♦ GROUP_NO_2 =grno2, [group_no] > ♦ / FX =fx, [fonction] > / FTAN =ftan, [fonction] > # if the function FTAN is given > ♦ ECROUISSAGE = | 'ISOTROPE', > ♦ ITER_INTE_MAXI =/20 [defaut] [I] > ♦ RESI_INTE_RELA =/1.0E-06 [defaut] [R] 5.11.5.2 Operands related to the position of the device ♦ GROUP_NO_1 ♦ GROUP_NO_2 Names of the node groups of the structure between which the non-linear device is placed. The node group must contain only one node. During the analysis, it is necessary to know the direction of the non-linear device because it works only along its axis. The distance between the two nodes must therefore be non-zero. 5.11.5.3 Operands related to the constitutive behaviour: FX or FTAN The only datum required is the function describing the non-linear constitutive behaviour. This function must satisfy the following criteria: - It is a function in the sense of code_aster: defined with the operator DEFI_FONCTION, - The interpolations on the axes of the abscissae and of the ordinates are linear, - The name of the abscissa when defining the function is DX or DTAN, - The extensions to the left and to the right of the function are excluded, - The function must be defined by at least 3 points, - The first point is (\mathrm{0.0,}0.0) and must be given, - The function must be strictly increasing. - The derivative of the function must be less than or equal to its derivative at the point (\mathrm{0.0,0}.0) . Examples of definition of the function FX: LesX = (0.0 , 0.2 , 0.3 , 0.50) LesY = (0.0 , 500.0 , 800.0 , 900.0) fctsy1 = DEFI_FONCTION(NOM_PARA='DX' , ABSCISSE = LesX, ORDONNEE = LesY, ) fctsy2 = DEFI_FONCTION(NOM_PARA='DX' , VALE = ( 0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 500.0, 0.3, 800.0, 0.50 , 900.0 ) , ) Examples of definition of the function FTAN: LesX = (0.0 , 0.2 , 0.3) LesY = (0.0 , 500.0 , 800.0) fctsy1 = DEFI_FONCTION(NOM_PARA='DTAN' , ABSCISSE = LesX, ORDONNEE = LesY, ) fctsy2 = DEFI_FONCTION(NOM_PARA='DTAN' , VALE = ( 0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 500.0, 0.3, 800.0 ) , ) The first two points of the function make it possible to define the elastic slope of the constitutive behaviour. The units of the abscissae and of the ordinates must be consistent with those of the problem: - The unit of the abscissae must be homogeneous with displacements, - The unit of the function must be homogeneous with forces. 5.11.5.4 Operands related to the convergence of the constitutive behaviour of the device ♦ ITER_INTE_MAXI = / 20 [defaut] / iter [I] ♦ RESI_INTE_RELA = / 1.0E-06 [defaut] / resi [R] These operands have the same meaning as when they are used with the command STAT_NON_LINE/COMPORTEMENT U4.51.11. The constitutive relation DIS_ECRO_TRAC requires the solution of a non-linear system by a Runge-Kutta method of order 5 with adaptive step. The control of the algorithm (number of iterations and residual) is used to test the convergence and to adapt the step if need be. 5.11.6 Non-linearity: DIS_ECRO_CINE The constitutive behaviour DIS_ECRO_CINE is an elastoplastic constitutive behaviour with non-linear kinematic hardening for discrete elements. This law is defined for each component of the torsor of the resultant forces (see R5.03.17). Note: This constitutive behaviour can be defined on mesh cells POI1 or SEG2. The detail of the parameters is given for DX. The node group must contain only one node. During the analysis, it is necessary to know the direction of the non-linear device because it works only along its axis. 5.11.7.3 Operands DIST_1/DIST_2 ◊ DIST_1 = dist1 Characteristic distance of material surrounding GROUP_NO_1: no1. Notes: DIST_1 and DIST_2 are defined in the sense of the outward normals of the two solids facing each other (DIST_1 and DIST_2 are positive because they represent the thickness of the structures under study). 5.11.7.4 Operand related to the constitutive behaviour: FX The only datum required is the function describing the non-linear constitutive behaviour. This function must satisfy the following criteria: - It is a function in the sense of code_aster: defined with the operator DEFI_FONCTION, - The interpolations on the axes of the abscissae and of the ordinates are linear, - The name of the abscissa when defining the function is DX. - The extension to the left of the function is excluded, - The extension to the right of the function is excluded or linear, - The function must be defined by at least 2 points, - The first point is (\mathrm{0.0,}0.0) and must be given, - The function must be strictly increasing. The reaction force during a shock with account taken of buckling is given by three functions of the penetration (defined by the user), namely the threshold force, the buckling stiffness and the buckling damping. One considers that there is buckling if the reaction force F reaches the limit value F_{\mathrm{seuil}} defined by the user. At each time instant, if the shock is detected, the force is given by: \begin{split}F = \left\{\begin{array}{ll} K(u_{\max})\times u + C(u_{\max})\times v \ \ \text{si} \ K(u_{\max})\times u {x}_{0} {F}_{c}(x)=0 \textrm{pour} ∣x∣\le {x}_{0} 5.11.10 Non-linearity: RELA_EFFO_VITE ◊ RELATION = 'RELA_EFFO_VITE' This relation makes it possible to define a force-velocity relation on a degree of freedom of a given node in the form of a non-linear function. The operands GROUP_NO, SOUS_STRUC, NOM_CMP and FONCTION have the same meaning for the relations RELA_EFFO_DEPL and RELA_EFFO_VITE. They are therefore not detailed in this paragraph. 5.12 Keyword ARCHIVAGE ◊ ARCHIVAGE Factor keyword defining the archiving. 5.12.1 Operand LIST_INST/INST ◊ / LIST_INST = l_arch List of reals defining the analysis time instants for which the solution must be archived in the result concept tran_gene. ◊ / INST Analysis time instants for which the solution must be archived in the result concept tran_gene. 5.12.2 Operand PAS_ARCH ◊ PAS_ARCH= ipa Integer defining the archiving periodicity of the solution of the transient analysis in the result concept tran_gene. If ipa = 5 one archives every 5 analysis steps. Whatever the archiving option chosen, one archives the first and the last time step and all the associated fields in order to allow a possible restart. Note: PAS_ARCH and LIST_INST/INST may both be present. In this case one archives the union of the time instants defined by these two criteria. 5.12.3 Operand CRITERE ◊ CRITERE = Indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be archived must be carried out: 'RELATIF': search interval [(1-prec).instant, (1+prec).instant] 'ABSOLU': search interval [instant-prec, instant+prec] The default value of the search criterion is 'RELATIF'. 5.12.4 Operand PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = / 1.E-06 [DEFAUT] / prec [R] Indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be archived must be carried out. 5.13 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = imp Integer making it possible to specify the level of printout in the message file. If INFO=1, one prints a summary of the dynamic analysis with the options chosen, the matrices and the number of non-linearities considered. The progress of the analysis is counted in slices of 5% of the total duration of the simulation. If INFO : 2, one prints, in addition to the information written in the case where INFO is equal to 1, the progress with shorter slices of 1%. In the presence of localised non-linearities, one prints for each obstacle the following additional information: - The number and type of the obstacle; - The name and the coordinates in the global frame of the shock node (of the shock nodes in the case of a shock between moving structures); - The orientation, in the global frame, of the normal to the obstacle; - The value of the twist angle; - The value of the initial gap; If the VERI_CHOC mode is activated, one also prints, for each shock node and for each mode, the values of the local shock stiffnesses and of the local flexibility rate and of the local flexibility. 5.14 Operand IMPRESSION ◊ IMPRESSION Factor keyword which makes it possible to print in the RESULTAT file quantities, not printable by a printing operator, such as the local displacement, the local velocity, the contact forces at the shock nodes and the value, cumulated over all the modes of the modal projection basis, of the rate of reconstitution of the static solution. 5.14.1 Operands TOUT / NIVEAU The keyword NIVEAU makes it possible to print one or several tables among 'DEPL_LOC', 'VITE_LOC', 'FORC_LOC' and ’TAUX_CHOC’. With TOUT = 'OUI' (default value), one prints the four tables. 5.14.2 Operands INST_INIT / INST_FIN These two keywords allow the user to filter the printouts in each loop over the time steps. 5.14.3 Operand UNITE_DIS_VISC ◊ UNITE_DIS_VISC= unit The results concerning the force, the viscous and relative displacements between the two nodes, as well as the dissipation of the non-linear device, may be saved in a file directly usable by the commands of code_aster . 5.15 Checking phase 5.15.1 Check on the matrices In the case of an analysis by modal recombination, one checks that the generalised matrices do indeed come from a projection onto a common basis and with the same number of basis vectors. In the case of an analysis by dynamic substructuring, one checks that the generalised matrices do indeed come from the same generalised numbering. 5.15.2 Check and advice on the choice of the time step for the schemes DIFF_CENTRE, DEVOGE and NEWMARK: One makes sure that the time step chosen satisfies the stability conditions of the numerical scheme (CFL criterion): - in the case of NEWMARK, stability is always ensured, but exceeding the criterion may induce a lack of accuracy on the result and is signalled by a message; the analysis continues (at the risk of producing a result of poor accuracy or a wrong result). - in the case of the schemes DIFF_CENTRE and DEVOGE, if the operand VERI_PAS is equal to 'OUI' (default value), the execution is stopped, and a minimum time step is proposed. If the operand VERI_PAS is equal to 'NON' or if it is an adaptive scheme, an alarm message is issued and the analysis continues (at the risk of producing a result of poor accuracy or a wrong result). When the denominator of the apparent frequency ({x}_{n}-{x}_{n-1}) becomes small, the apparent frequency may become very high, which leads to an unjustified refinement of the time step. To remedy this, the algorithm uses the following criterion for each degree of freedom i : \frac{∣{x}_{n}^{i}-{x}_{n-1}^{i}∣}{\Delta t}\le {v}_{min}^{i}\mathrm{\Rightarrow }{f}_{{\mathit{AP}}_{n}}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\sqrt{∣\frac{{\ddot{x}}_{n}^{i}-{\ddot{x}}_{n-1}^{i}}{{v}_{min}^{i}\Delta t}∣} {v}_{min}^{i} may be computed in two different ways according to the value of VITE_MIN: 'NORM' : {v}_{\min}^{i}({t}_{n})=\mathrm{Max}(\frac{\mathrm{Max}({\dot{x}}_{n+1/2}^{k},{\dot{x}}_{n+1/2}^{l})}{100},{10}^{-15}{\mathrm{ms}}^{-1}) where k and l are the degrees of freedom of the same nature as the degree of freedom i which are closest to i in the numbering ( \mathit{DX} or \mathit{DY} or \mathit{DZ} ...). 'MAXI' : {v}_{\min}^{i}({t}_{n})=\underset{0 1 ) when the error is sufficiently small: \Delta {t}_{n} 1 ) when the error is greater than 1, the maximum number of iterations (NMAX_ITER_PAS) has not been reached and the minimum time step has not been reached: \Delta {t}_{n}>\frac{1}{{\mathit{Nf}}_{{\mathit{AP}}_{n}}},\mathit{Niter} \mathit{plr}\mathrm{\ast }\Delta {t}_{\mathit{initial}}\mathrm{\Rightarrow }\Delta {t}_{n}=\frac{\Delta {t}_{n}}{\mathit{cdp}} Its default value is 1.3334 , that is a reduction by a factor 0,75 . ◊ PAS_LIMI_RELA = plr Coefficient applied to the initial time step in order to define the refinement limit and therefore the minimum time step: \Delta {t}_{min}=\mathit{plr}\mathrm{\ast }\Delta {t}_{\mathit{initial}} ◊ NB_POIN_PERIODE = N Number of points per apparent period. It is this parameter which sets the accuracy of the analysis. It must be at least equal to 20; its default value (50) guarantees a satisfactory accuracy (of the order of 1 to 2%) in most cases. ◊ NMAX_ITER_PAS Maximum number of reductions of the time step per analysis step: if \mathit{err}>1 and {N}_{\mathit{iter}} ◊ / INST Analysis time instants for which the solution must be archived in the result concept dyna_tran. 6.12.2 Operand PAS_ARCH / PAS_ARCH = ipa Integer defining the archiving periodicity of the solution of the transient analysis in the result concept dyna_trans. If ipa = 5 one archives every 5 analysis steps. Note: PAS_ARCH and LIST_INST/INST are both taken into account in the keyword ARCHIVAGE; one must take care to set PAS_ARCH to a value greater than the number of analysis steps if one wishes to drive the archiving solely by LIST_INST/INST. 6.12.3 Operand CRITERE ◊ CRITERE = Indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be archived must be carried out: 'RELATIF': search interval [(1-prec).instant, (1+prec).instant] 'ABSOLU': search interval [instant-prec, instant+prec] The default value of the search criterion is 'RELATIF'. 6.12.4 Operand PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = /1.E-06 [DEFAUT] /prec [R] Indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be archived must be carried out. 6.12.5 Operand CHAM_EXCLU ◊ CHAM_EXCLU = ( I 'DEPL', I 'VITE', I 'ACCE', ) Makes it possible to exclude the archiving of one or several fields among 'DEPL', 'VITE' and 'ACCE'. This exclusion is ignored for the last analysis time instant: the three fields are necessary for a restart (POURSUITE). 6.13 Keyword OBSERVATION ◊ OBSERVATION= _F() ◊ TITRE = titre This keyword makes it possible to post-process certain fields at the nodes (DEPL, VITE, ACCE) on parts of the model at time instants of a list (called the observation list), generally less refined than the list of archived time instants defined in the keyword ARCHIVAGE (where one stores all the fields over the whole model). It serves essentially to save storage, but also to evaluate fields on reduced parts of the mesh, without needing to post-process after the analysis. This keyword is repeatable and allows the creation of an observation table which one will be able to extract by means of the command RECU_TABLE. Cf. U4.51.03 (3.22.8) for the detailed table contents. One may use only 99 occurrences of the keyword OBSERVATION at most. It is possible to name an occurrence of the observation (column NOM_OBSERVATION) by using the keyword TITRE. If it is not used, the column NOM_OBSERVATION contains OBSERVATION_xx with xx varying from 1 to 99. 6.13.1 Operands LIST_INST/INST/PAS_OBSE/OBSE_ETAT_INIT ◊ /LIST_INST = list_r8 /INST = l_r8 /PAS_OBSE = npas /OBSE_ETAT_INIT = /'OUI', [DEFAUT] /'NON' Cf. U4.51.03 for the detailed syntax. 6.13.2 Operands PRECISION/CRITERE ◊ PRECISION = prec ◊ CRITERE = /'ABSOLU' /'RELATIF' Cf. U4.71.00 for the detailed syntax. 6.13.3 Operands NOM_CHAM/NOM_CMP ♦ NOM_CHAM = ( I 'DEPL', I 'VITE', I 'ACCE', ) ◊ NOM_CMP = nomcmp Cf. U4.51.03 for the detailed syntax. 6.13.4 Operands TOUT/NOEUD/GROUP_NOEUD/MAILLE/GROUP_MA ◊ /TOUT = 'NON' [DEFAUT] 'OUI' /NOEUD = no [no] /GROUP_NO = grno [grno] /MAILLE = lma [ma] /GROUP_MA = lgrma [grma] Cf. U4.51.03 for the detailed syntax. 6.13.5 Operands EVAL_CMP/FORMULE/EVAL_CHAM ◊ EVAL_CMP = /'VALE', [DEFAUT] /'FORMULE' ◊ FORMULE = form [ formule_aster ] ◊ EVAL_CHAM= /'VALE', [DEFAUT] /'MIN', /'MAX', /'MOY', Cf. U4.51.03 for the detailed syntax. 6.14 Checking phase The use of the centred-difference and adaptive schemes imposes certain restrictions of use: - these two schemes require the use of a diagonal mass matrix. A test checks that the mass matrix was created with the option 'MASS_MECA_DIAG' of CALC_MATR_ELEM. Moreover, the mass matrix must be stored in skyline form, - there must be no boundary conditions other than blocked degrees of freedom. A test checks that there are no boundary conditions of the type of links between degrees of freedom. It is not possible either to impose non-zero displacements by means of an assembled vector, - for the centred-difference scheme, one makes sure that the time step chosen satisfies the stability conditions: \mathit{dt}<0,05/{f}_{max} with {f}_{max}=\underset{1\le i\le \mathit{nddl}}{max}(\frac{1}{2\pi }\sqrt{\frac{{k}_{ii}}{{m}_{ii}}}) and {k}_{ii} and {m}_{ii} the diagonal terms of the stiffness and mass matrices. 7 Harmonic response analysis One solves the following equation in the frequency domain: (-j\omega \mathrm{³}.\mathrm{Q}-\omega \mathrm{²}.\mathrm{M}+j\omega .\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{K})\cdot \mathrm{x}=\left\lbrace \sum_{i=1}^{k}{h}_{i}(f).{\omega}^{{n}_{i}}.{\mathrm{e}}^{j\pi \frac{{\phi }_{j}}{180}}.{\mathrm{g}}_{i}(P)\right\rbrace Where: \mathrm{K} represents a real or complex stiffness matrix (case of hysteretic damping) \mathrm{M} represents a mass matrix \mathrm{C} represents a viscous damping matrix \mathrm{Q} represents an acoustic impedance matrix coming from a displacement-pressure-potential formulation (\mathrm{u},p,\varphi ) , cf. R4.02.02. P is a current point of the structure. \omega =2\pi f : excitation angular frequency {\mathrm{g}}_{i}(P) : spatial description of the excitation {h}_{i}(f) : frequency description of the excitation \mathrm{x} : complex response The damping of the structure may be viscous or hysteretic U2.06.03 R5.05.04. In the case of hysteretic damping, one has a complex stiffness matrix and one solves the following equation: (\mathrm{K}-\omega \mathrm{²}.\mathrm{M})\cdot \mathrm{x}=\left\lbrace \sum_{i=1}^{k}{h}_{i}(f).{\omega}^{{n}_{i}}.{\mathrm{e}}^{j\pi \frac{{\phi }_{j}}{180}}.{\mathrm{g}}_{i}(P)\right\rbrace with \mathrm{K} : complex stiffness matrix. This operator may be used with imposed force or with imposed displacement (solution in the absolute frame) or with imposed entrainment inertia force (solution in the relative frame). 7.1 Operand RESULTAT ◊ RESULTAT = harm Name of the result data structure to be enriched. This keyword is obligatory if one is in re-entrant concept mode (reuse). 7.2 Operand MODELE ◊ MODELE = mo Name of the concept defining the model whose elements are the subject of the harmonic analysis. 7.3 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmat Name of the concept defining the material field assigned to the model mo. 7.4 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac Name of the concept defining the characteristics of the beam, plate and shell elements, etc. 7.5 Operand MATR_MASS ♦ MATR_MASS = m Name of the assembled-matrix concept \mathrm{M} corresponding to the mass matrix of the system. 7.6 Operand MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_RIGI = k Name of the assembled-matrix concept \mathrm{K} corresponding to the stiffness matrix of the system. A hysteretic damping is obtained with a complex stiffness matrix. 7.7 Operand MATR_AMOR ◊ MATR_AMOR = c Name of the assembled-matrix concept \mathrm{C} corresponding to the viscous damping matrix of the system. 7.8 Keyword AMOR_MODAL Factor keyword for supplying the viscous damping in the form of lists of reduced modal damping (percentage of the critical damping) with the following operands; possible only in the case of a harmonic analysis on a modal basis. 7.8.1 Operands AMOR_REDUIT / LIST_AMOR / AMOR_REDUIT = la List of all the reduced modal viscous dampings: ({\eta}_{1},{\eta}_{2},\mathrm{...},{\eta}_{n}) . Note : if the number of reduced dampings given is lower than the number of basis vectors used in the modal basis, the dampings of the additional vectors are taken equal to the last damping in the list. / LIST_AMOR = l_amor Name of the concept of type listr8 containing the list of the reduced viscous modal dampings. 7.9 Operand MATR_IMPE_PHI ◊ MATR_IMPE_PHI = imp Name of the assembled-matrix concept \mathrm{Q} corresponding to the impedance matrix for a fluid-structure system whose formulation is in displacement-pressure-potential (\mathrm{u},p,\varphi ) R4.02.02. 7.10 Operands FREQ/LIST_FREQ ♦ / FREQ = lf List of all the analysis frequencies f : (f1, f2, ..., fn). / LIST_FREQ = cf Name of the concept of type listr8 containing the list of the analysis frequencies f . 7.11 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM ◊ / TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI' / NOM_CHAM = | 'DEPL' | 'VITE' | 'ACCE' Choice of the fields to be computed in order to represent the response: displacement, velocity, acceleration, or all three. 7.12 Keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT Factor keyword making it possible to define several types of excitations. Either by indicating an assembled vector corresponding to a loading, or loads which will lead to the computation and to the assembly of a right-hand side. For each occurrence of the factor keyword, one defines a component of the excitation in the form (h(f),\mathrm{g}(P),\phi ) , which one may also multiply by multiplying functions. This keyword must be repeated as many times as there are loading vectors. 7.12.1 Operands VECT_ASSE/VECT_ASSE_GENE/CHARGE Make it possible to define {\mathrm{g}}_{i}(P) , the spatial discretisation of the loading, in the form of a field at the nodes corresponding to one or several loads of imposed force or of imposed motion. ♦ / VECT_ASSE = vecti Name of the concept produced by: - the operator ASSE_VECTEUR, in imposed force or in entrainment inertia force under imposed acceleration in an absolute frame. The amplitudes of the excitation may be defined in the corresponding concepts of load type. The field expected is a field at the nodes of quantity DEPL_R, DEPL_C or PRES_C. / VECT_ASSE_GENE = vect_gene Name of the concept produced by: - the operator PROJ_VECT_BASE, which makes it possible to project an assembled vector (imposed force or entrainment force under imposed acceleration in an absolute frame) onto a modal basis or a Ritz basis. - the operator ASSE_VECT_GENE, which makes it possible to project a loading onto a basis defined on a generalised model for dynamic substructuring analyses. / CHARGE = chi chi, name of the loading concept created by a call to the command AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01. The keyword MODELE must be supplied if one uses the keyword CHARGE. 7.12.2 Operands FONC_MULT_C / COEF_MULT_C / FONC_MULT / COEF_MULT Make it possible to define {h}_{i}(f) , a complex or real function defining the dependence of the excitation as a function of the frequency, applied to all the components of the field at the node associated with this occurrence. Several possibilities are offered: ♦ / FONC_MULT_C = hci Name of the concept of type fonction_C or formule_C defining a complex function {h}_{i}(f) of the frequency f , / COEF_MULT_C = aci Complex multiplying coefficient of the loading, independent of the loading, / FONC_MULT = hi Concept of type fonction, formule or nappe defining a real function {h}_{i}(f) of the frequency f , / COEF_MULT = ai Real multiplying coefficient of the loading, independent of the loading. 7.12.3 Operand PUIS_PULS ◊ PUIS_PULS = ni Makes it possible to define the power of the angular frequency, cf. eq.(), when the loading is a function of the frequency; by default {n}_{i}=0 . For example, in order to take into account the time derivative of a loading; example: imposed displacement versus imposed velocity... 7.12.4 Operand PHAS_DEG ◊ PHAS_DEG = phi Makes it possible to define the phase of each component of the excitation in degrees with respect to a single phase reference for all the excitations {h}_{i}(f) ; by default {\varphi}_{i}=0 . 7.12.5 Note For a problem with motion imposed in displacement, one defines the blocked degrees of freedom (kinematic conditions prior to the construction of the cham_no); one may then choose an excitation: - in imposed displacement n=0 , \varphi =0 degree, - in imposed velocity n=1 , \varphi =90 degrees, - in imposed acceleration n=2 , \varphi =180 degrees. 7.13 Operand EXCIT_RESU ◊ EXCIT_RESU This factor keyword makes it possible to define several loadings in the form of a harmonic evolution of type dyna_harmo of assembled right-hand-side vectors, computed on the physical basis. This possibility is available on a physical basis and on a reduced modal basis or a Ritz basis. 7.14 Keyword CHAR_GENE ◊ CHAR_GENE This keyword makes it possible to define a loading of type char_gene (see U4.44.06) which imposes linear relations between generalised degrees of freedom. The problem to be solved is of the following form: \begin{aligned} \Biggl( \begin{bmatrix} K & B^T \\ B & 0 \end{bmatrix} -\omega^2 \begin{bmatrix} M & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \Biggr) \cdot \begin{bmatrix} x \\ \lambda \end{bmatrix} = \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ \beta \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned} Where: - \lambda represents the additional Lagrange degrees of freedom, - B represents the matrix of the coefficients to be imposed between the modes, - \beta represents the values of the linear relations to be applied. 7.14.1 Operand RESULTAT This keyword makes it possible to define the right-hand sides to be extracted for each analysis frequency from an already computed result containing nodal force fields. ♦ RESULTAT = resuforc Name of the concept of harmonic evolution of right-hand sides produced by the chaining of the operator CALC_FORC_NONL U4.84.21 and then of the operator REST_SPEC_TEMP U4.63.34. The operator CALC_FORC_NONL makes it possible to produce a transient evolution of right-hand sides. The operator REST_SPEC_TEMP transforms this transient evolution into a harmonic evolution. An example of use is provided in the test case SDLS119A. 7.14.2 Operand COEF_MULT_C ♦ COEF_MULT_C = aci Complex multiplying coefficient of the right-hand-side vector extracted from the result resuforc for each analysis frequency. 7.15 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = inf Makes it possible to carry out, in the message file, various intermediate printouts making it possible to follow the progress of the analysis. By default, if INFO=1, one prints the progress of the harmonic analysis with a step which corresponds at most to 5% of the total number of frequencies. The general rule is to print systematically the first and last frequencies as well as a maximum number of 20 frequencies in between. If INFO=2, a printout is made for each frequency and makes it possible to follow the progress of the analysis more precisely.
