Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "ACCE", ◇ MODE_MECA = co, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands MODELE / CARA_ELEM ♦ MODELE = modele, ◊ CARA_ELEM = caraelem, These keywords make it possible to supply: - the name of the model (modele) whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. - the name of the characteristics of the structural elements (plates, beams, discrete elements, …) if they are used in the model. 3.2 Factor keyword MATER_ELAS ◊ MATER_ELAS = _F( ♦ / MATER = mat / ♦ E = e ♦ AMOR_HYST = amorhyst ♦ RHO = rho ♦ NU = nu ♦ GROUP_MA = gma ) This keyword makes it possible to assign an elastic material with no frequency dependence to the elements belonging to GROUP_MA. The material may be defined before the macro-command by means of the operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01; in that case, this material is recalled with the keyword MATER. The material may also be defined here by its properties: Young's modulus E, mass density RHO, Poisson's ratio NU, and hysteretic damping AMOR_HYST. This factor keyword may be repeated as many times as there are elastic materials with no frequency dependence in the structure. 3.3 Factor keyword MATER_ELAS_FO ♦ MATER_ELAS_FO = _F( ♦ E = l_e ♦ AMOR_HYST = l_amor ♦ RHO = rho ♦ NU = nu ♦ GROUP_MA = gma ) This keyword makes it possible to assign a viscoelastic material with frequency dependence to the elements belonging to GROUP_MA. The mechanical properties of the viscoelastic material are of two kinds: - those which depend on frequency: Young's modulus E and the damping factor AMOR_HYST; they are supplied by functions indexed by frequency, produced by DEFI_FONCTION / NOM_PARA='FREQ' U4.31.02); - those which are constant: the mass density RHO and Poisson's ratio NU. This factor keyword may be repeated as many times as there are viscoelastic materials with frequency dependence in the structure. 3.4 Keyword TYPE_RESU ◊ TYPE_RESU = / ’HARM’ [DEFAUT] / ’MODE’ This keyword makes it possible to define the type of analysis to be carried out: - the choice 'MODE' makes it possible to compute the eigenmodes of the structure; - the analysis 'HARM' makes it possible to obtain the frequency response of the structure to a given excitation; one can also recover the eigenmodes computed, by means of the keyword MODE_MECA. 3.5 Keywords FREQ / LIST_FREQ ♦ / FREQ = l_f / LIST_FREQ = lfreq In the case of a modal analysis of the structure (TYPE_RESU='MODE'), this keyword makes it possible to define the frequency band in which the modes are sought. The list must then contain exactly 2 values (strictly increasing). In the case of a harmonic analysis of the structure (TYPE_RESU='HARM'), this keyword makes it possible to define the discrete frequencies for which the response of the structure is computed. The list must then contain at least 2 strictly increasing values. 3.6 Keywords TYPE_MODE / RESI_RELA ◊ TYPE_MODE = / ’REEL’ [DEFAUT] / ’BETA’ / ’COMPLEXE’ Several choices are possible for the computation of the eigenmodes: real modes, beta-modes (which are improved real modes giving a better accuracy of the results, cf. R5.05.09), as well as complex modes. The computation of the complex modes makes it possible to obtain the modal dampings. On the other hand, this type of mode cannot be used to carry out a harmonic analysis (TYPE_RESU='HARM'). Note: If one computes complex modes, one can recover the modal dampings in a Python list with this function: liste_python=modes.LIST_PARA()['AMOR_REDUIT'] (this requires using PAR_LOT='NON' in the command DEBUT). ◊ RESI_RELA = / 1.E-3 [DEFAUT] / eps The computation of the eigenmodes by the iterative method has a convergence criterion named RESI_RELA. An eigenmode is retained in the modal basis when the relative difference between the eigenfrequencies computed at two successive iterations is less than RESI_RELA. 3.7 Factor keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT =_F( ♦ CHARGE = charge ) This keyword makes it possible to assign loads (boundary conditions, excitation forces, ...) which have been defined beforehand by the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01. Note: At present, for external excitations, only excitations of type FORCE_NODALE are compatible with the command DYNA_VISCO . For the harmonic analysis, the basis of eigenmodes is enriched, transparently for the user, by the static modes associated with the excited nodes. 3.8 Keyword NOM_CHAM (if TYPE_RESU='HARM') ◊ NOM_CHAM = / ’DEPL’ [DEFAUT] / ’VITE’ / ’ACCE’ This keyword makes it possible to define which fields will be saved in the result concept (displacement, velocity or acceleration). It is possible to save several fields by giving a list, for example NOM_CHAM=('DEPL','ACCE'). 3.9 Keyword MODE_MECA (if TYPE_RESU='HARM') ◊ MODE_MECA = CO( 'modes' ) If this keyword is present, two concepts will be produced by the macro-command: - the concept modes of type mode_meca - the concept visco of type dyna_harmo The concept modes may for example be printed in the usual way with the command IMPR_RESU U4.91.01. 3.10 Keyword COEF_FREQ_MAX (if TYPE_RESU='HARM') ◊ COEF_FREQ_MAX = cfmax [R] During a harmonic analysis, the multiplying coefficient COEF_FREQ_MAX makes it possible to obtain more accurate frequency-response values, by multiplying by COEF_FREQ_MAX the value of the maximum frequency used to compute the modal basis of projection. The minimum value of this parameter is 1.5. 3.11 Keyword INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 [DEFAUT] / 2 Indique le niveau d’impression dans le fichier MESSAGE. 4 Examples 4.1 Definition of the frequency dependence of the properties of the viscoelastic materials frequencies for which the material parameters are given list_f=DEFI_LIST_REEL(VALE=(1,10,50,100,500,1000,1500,),); values (of the real part) of Young's modulus at the frequencies of list_f list_E=DEFI_LIST_REEL(VALE=(23.2E6,58.E6,145.E6,203.E6,348.E6,435.E6,464.E6,),); values of the loss factor at the frequencies of list_f list_eta=DEFI_LIST_REEL(VALE=(1.1,0.85,0.7,0.6,0.4,0.35,0.34,),); u4.53.05 Operator DYNA_LINE u4.53.05 Operator DYNA_LINE 1 Purpose DYNA_LINE is the unified operator making it possible to carry out a transient or harmonic response analysis on a physical or generalised basis. It can also treat localised non-linearities for transient response analyses, soil-structure interaction or fluid-structure interaction on a generalised basis. The advantage of the operator DYNA_LINE, compared with the operators DYNA_VIBRA or CALC_MISS, is that the user does not have to deal with the steps of assembly of the matrices. The construction of a relevant projection basis for the solution of the problem on a generalised basis is carried out automatically by the operator from the information supplied. The concept produced depends on the type of analysis carried out (dyna_trans, dyna_harmo). 2 Syntax / harm_gene / dyna_harmo / tran_gene / mode_meca / dyna_trans = DYNA_LINE( ◆ TYPE_CALCUL = / "HARM", / "TRAN", ◆ BASE_CALCUL = / "PHYS", / "GENE", ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ CHARGE = char_meca / char_cine_meca, ◇ BANDE_ANALYSE = float, ◇ PCENT_COUP = int (défaut: 90), # The user therefore in principle does not need to recover the basis or the generalised result which was used for the analysis. However, these objects may prove useful for certain advanced post-processings. 5.1 BASE_RESU ◊ BASE_RESU = base_resu, [mode_meca] Makes it possible optionally to recover the analysis basis built by the operator and which was used for the dynamic analysis on a generalised basis. The output concept is of type [mode_meca]. 5.2 RESU_GENE ◊ RESU_GENE = resu_gene, [tran_gene] The operand RESU_GENE makes it possible optionally to recover the result on a generalised basis. The output concept is of type [tran_gene, harm_gene] depending on the type of analysis (TYPE_CALCUL). 6 Computation of the static enrichment 6.1 ENRI_STAT ◊ ENRI_STAT = /'OUI', [DEFAUT] > /'NON', In the case of an analysis on a generalised basis, a static correction is set up by default via the computation of the static modes, which are added to the modal basis. Static modes are computed for each loading assigned under the factor keyword EXCIT (see § 9), according to strategies which depend on the types of loading. Static modes are also computed for the non-linear constitutive behaviours assigned under the factor keyword COMPORTEMENT (see § 11.1). The static modes are then assembled with the dynamic modes in order to form the generalised analysis basis. The keyword ENRI_STAT cannot be used in the case of an analysis with fluid-structure interaction (IFS='OUI') (see § 12). 6.2 ORTHO ◊ ORTHO = /'NON', [DEFAUT] > /'OUI', Makes it possible to orthogonalise the assembled basis of the dynamic modes and of the static modes. The orthogonalisation is carried out by means of an eigenvalue problem made up of the stiffness and mass matrices projected onto this assembled basis. 6.3 FREQ_COUP_STAT ◊ FREQ_COUP_STAT = fc_stat [R] Cut-off frequency (expressed in Hz) used for the modal analysis which makes the orthogonalisation possible. If the keyword FREQ_COUP_STAT is not defined by the user, no cut-off is taken into account. 7 Definition of the analysis range and of the increments 7.1 Operands BANDE_ANALYSE, PCENT_COUP 7.1.1 Keyword BANDE_ANALYSE ◊ BANDE_ANALYSE = [f_min, f_max], Makes it possible to define the frequency band in which one wishes to carry out the dynamic analysis. In the case of an analysis on a generalised basis, the values of the band are used for the computation of the dynamic modes. This keyword may contain only a single value; in that case this value will correspond to the maximum frequency f_max, the minimum frequency f_min being set to zero. If the keyword BANDE_ANALYSE is not supplied, in the case of a transient analysis, the minimum frequency f_min is set to zero, and the maximum frequency f_max will be computed automatically from the cut-off frequency of the input signals. 7.1.2 Keyword PCENT_COUP ◊ PCENT_COUP = / pcent_coup, [R] > / 90. The cut-off frequency of an input signal is computed so as to contain PCENT_COUP% of the energy of the input signal. The value of the keyword PCENT_COUP must lie between 80 and 100. The cut-off frequency corresponds to the maximum value of the cut-off frequencies of each of the signals. The maximum frequency f_max is then set to twice the cut-off frequency. 7.2 Operands FREQ, LIST_FREQ ◊ / FREQ = freq, [l_R] > / LIST_FREQ = list_freq , [:ref: listr8 ] In the harmonic case, these keywords make it possible to define the frequencies for which the dynamic response will be computed. 7.3 Operands SCHEMA_TEMPS, INCREMENT, ETAT_INIT, ARCHIVAGE The following keywords are useful in the case of a transient analysis. 7.3.1 Factor keyword SCHEMA_TEMPS ◊ SCHEMA_TEMPS = _F(...) This factor keyword makes it possible to define the parameters concerning the time-integration scheme in the case of a transient analysis. One may refer to the documentation of DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for further information on the meaning of the simple keywords used. Note that by default the operator DYNA_LINE uses the scheme DEVOGE, unlike DYNA_VIBRA, which uses the scheme DIFF_CENTRE by default. 7.3.2 Factor keyword INCREMENT ♦ INCREMENT =_F( > ◊ INST_INIT = ti, [R] > ◊ PAS = dt, [R] > ♦ INST_FIN= tf, [R] > ), This factor keyword makes it possible to define the analysis increments in the case of a transient analysis. One may refer to the documentation of DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for further information on the meaning of the simple keywords used. Note that, unlike the operator DYNA_VIBRA, it is not mandatory to specify the simple keyword PAS defining the analysis step. In that case, the analysis step is computed automatically. If the keyword BANDE_ANALYSE is present (see § 7.1.1), then the step is computed as follows: \Delta t=\frac{1}{5{f}_{max}} Otherwise, the step is computed directly from the cut-off frequency (see § 7.1.2), as follows: \Delta t=\frac{1}{5{f}_{c}} 7.3.3 Factor keyword ETAT_INIT ◊ ETAT_INIT = _F(...) This factor keyword makes it possible to define an initial state. One may refer to the documentation of DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for further information on the meaning of the simple keywords used. Note that, in the case of an analysis on a generalised basis, unlike what is provided for in the data setup of DYNA_VIBRA, the user cannot supply the vectors projected onto the generalised basis. One must then supply, in the same way as for an analysis on a physical basis, the fields at the nodes on the physical basis, which will automatically be projected by the operator onto the generalised basis if need be. 7.3.4 Factor keyword ARCHIVAGE ◊ ARCHIVAGE = _F(...) This factor keyword makes it possible to control the archiving time instants. One may refer to the documentation of DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for further information on the meaning of the simple keywords used. 8 Definition of the damping ◊ AMORTISSEMENT = _F(...) Factor keyword making it possible to introduce various types of damping. 8.1 TYPE_AMOR = 'RAYLEIGH' ♦ TYPE_AMOR = 'RAYLEIGH', This option makes it possible to compute the Rayleigh damping matrix on the basis of the parameters (AMOR_ALPHA, AMOR_BETA) of the materials assigned in CHAM_MATER (see § 4.2) and of the discrete elements of type (A_T ) defined in CARA_ELEM (see § 4.3). This option also makes it possible to compute the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries, in the case where they are present in the model. If one is in the presence of a harmonic analysis (TYPE_CALCUL = ‘HARMO’), one activates other options in order to handle the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries. 8.2 Operands VNOR and MATR_IMPE_PHI These operands are activated exclusively in the case where TYPE_CALCUL = ‘HARMO’ and TYPE_AMOR = ‘RAYLEIGH’. ◊ VNOR= This option allows us to take into account the case of an emitting boundary. The most common case is the radiating one (or partially radiating if one defines a reflection coefficient \alpha \ne 0 ). In the case of a radiating boundary VNOR = 1 (option activated by default). In the case of an emitting boundary VNOR = -1. This coefficient is multiplied by the value of the impedance of the absorbing fluid boundaries ('3D_FLUI_ABSO', '2D_FLUI_ABSO' and 'AXIS_FLUI_ABSO'). ◊ MATR_IMPE_PHI= If one uses the fluid formulation u-p-\phi in a harmonic analysis, one has the possibility of taking into account the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries via the computation of a third-order matrix (with the option IMPE_MECA). This third-order matrix can be used only in a harmonic analysis (operand MATR_IMPE_PHI in DYNA_VIBRA) and allows us to symmetrise the matrix (unlike the computation of this contribution via AMOR_MECA). If one wishes to use this third-order matrix in place of the first-order term (computed via AMOR_MECA), one must set MATR_IMPE_PHI = ‘OUI’ (by default MATR_IMPE_PHI = ‘OUI’). 8.3 TYPE_AMOR = 'HYST' ♦ TYPE_AMOR = 'HYST', This option is used in the case of a harmonic analysis (TYPE_CALCUL == 'HARM'). It makes it possible to compute the imaginary part of the stiffness matrix in the case: - of a material possessing a hysteretic damping supplied by the parameter (AMOR_HYST) assigned in CHAM_MATER (see § 4.2) and of the discrete elements of type (A_T ) defined in CARA_ELEM (see § 4.3). - of a viscoelastic material of type ELAS_VISCO_ assigned in CHAM_MATER (see § 4.2) 8.4 TYPE_AMOR = 'MODAL' ♦ TYPE_AMOR = 'MODAL', In the case of an analysis on a generalised basis, it is sometimes simpler and more relevant to define the modal dampings. In that case, one must specify in AMOR_REDUIT the reduced dampings (percentages of the critical damping) corresponding to each mode of the system, in the form of a list of reals. ♦ AMOR_REDUIT = l_amor , [l_R] If the number of reduced dampings given is less than the number of basis vectors used in the modal basis, the dampings of the additional vectors are taken equal to the last damping of the list l_amor. 9 Factor keyword EXCIT ◊ EXCIT = F(...) This factor keyword makes it possible to define a load at each occurrence. The operands have a meaning equivalent to those described in the document U4.54.03, with the difference that, for the operator DYNA_LINE, it is not necessary to supply all the information concerning the right-hand sides, which are computed automatically by the operator. 9.1 Keyword CHARGE Loading applied to the structure, defined beforehand by means of the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA. The keyword CHARGE must appear only in the occurrence of the factor keyword if the keyword TYPE_APPUI is not present. 9.2 Keywords TYPE_APPUI, DIRECTION, GROUP_NO Keywords used in the case of seismic loadings; one may refer to the document U4.63.01 for further details. The keyword TYPE_APPUI must appear only in the occurrence of the factor keyword if the keyword CHARGE is not present. 9.2.1 TYPE_APPUI = 'MONO' ◊ TYPE_APPUI = 'MONO' The structure is excited uniformly at all the supports. One must specify the direction of excitation via the keyword DIRECTION. 9.2.2 TYPE_APPUI = 'MULTI' ◊ TYPE_APPUI = 'MULTI' The excitation is applied on only part of the supports. One must specify the direction of excitation via the keyword DIRECTION as well as the nodes concerned via the keyword GROUP_NO. 9.2.3 Keyword DIRECTION ◊ DIRECTION = (dx, dy, dz, drx, dry, drz) Component of a vector giving the direction of the earthquake in the global reference frame. 9.2.4 Keyword GROUP_NO ◊ GROUP_NO = g_noeu List of the node groups of the structure subjected to the excitation in the case with TYPE_APPUI. If TYPE_APPUI = 'MULTI', one must necessarily specify the keyword GROUP_NO. If TYPE_APPUI = 'MONO', the keyword GROUP_NO is not mandatory. However, the occurrences of the keyword GROUP_NO must be the same for all the occurrences of the factor keyword EXCIT. 9.3 Operands FONC_MULT, COEF_MULT, FONC_MULT_C, COEF_MULT_C, ACCE, VITE, DEPL, PHAS_DEG, PUIS_PULS Coefficient or multiplying function of the assembled vector. In the transient case, one must necessarily supply a function of time. In the harmonic case, it is possible to supply a coefficient or a complex function depending on frequency. One should refer to the document U4.53.03 for further details on the use of these keywords. 10 Soil-structure interaction ◊ISS = 'OUI', Activation of the taking into account of soil-structure interaction. In the case with soil-structure interaction, the seismic analysis will use parameters computed by means of MISS3D ( via CALC_MISS). 10.1 Inputs and outputs of the soil analysis 10.1.1 Keyword CALC_IMPE_FORC ◊ CALC_IMPE_FORC = / 'OUI', [DEFAUT] > /'NON', By default, the operator CALC_MISS is called a first time using the option FICHIER, which makes it possible to launch an execution of MISS3D and to recover the results from it in files, defined on a logical unit. The user may deactivate this step by setting CALC_IMPE_MISS='NON'. One must then in that case define the logical units which correspond to files which already exist. 10.1.2 Keyword TYPE_EXCIT One must declare the nature of the loading supplied by the user. Two choices are possible: - 'INST' for a loading in the time domain - 'FREQ' for a loading in the frequency domain This information is necessary for the computation of the list of frequencies in the call to CALC_MISS. 10.1.3 Keywords UNITE_RESU_IMPE, UNITE_RESU_FORC ♦ UNITE_RESU_IMPE= uresimp [I] ♦ UNITE_RESU_FORC = uresfor [I] ◊ UNITE_RESU_FORC = uresfor [I] These keywords make it possible to define the logical units associated with the impedances and the equivalent seismic forces computed by MISS3D. In the case CALC_IMPE_FORC == 'NON', these keywords are mandatory and correspond to files which already exist and which were generated beforehand. In the case CALC_IMPE_FORC == 'OUI', these keywords are optional and make it possible to recover the impedances and the equivalent seismic forces computed by MISS3D. 10.1.4 Keywords TABLE_SOL / MATER_SOL ♦ / TABLE_SOL = tabsol [table] > / MATER_SOL = matsol These keywords make it possible to define the soil stratification used in the MISS3D analysis. One of these keywords must necessarily be defined if CALC_IMPE_FORC == 'OUI'. One may refer to the document U7.03.12 for further details concerning these keywords. 10.2 Soil-structure interface 10.2.1 Keyword VERSION_MISS ♦ VERSION_MISS = / 'V6.7', [DEFAUT] > 'V6.6', > 'V6.5', Number of the version of MISS3D. The default value corresponds to the production version of MISS3D (version d'exploitation). MISS3D analyses on large models (or with many frequencies) may be long and costly in memory. Fortunately they can be accelerated by activating one or two levels of parallelism. For further information one may consult the documentations U2.06.07 and U2.08.06. 10.2.2 Keywords GROUP_MA_INTERF, GROUP_NO_INTERF ♦ GROUP_MA_INTERF = grma, [grma] ♦ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, [grno] GROUP_MA_INTERF corresponds to the mesh-cell group constituting the soil-structure interface. GROUP_NO_INTERF corresponds to the node group at which the coupling conditions are imposed. This consists in automatically clamping the degrees of freedom of the nodes concerned in order to compute the eigenmodes of the structure. The user must not add boundary conditions on this group, as in the case of CALC_MISS. In the case of a rigid foundation, the user must define a LIAISON_SOLIDE via the keyword CHARGE and a GROUP_NO_INTERF containing a node corresponding to the centre of the foundation. In the case of a flexible foundation, no condition must be defined on the GROUP_NO_INTERF, which must contain all the nodes of the foundation. 10.2.3 Keywords TYPE_MODE / NB_MODE_INTERF TYPE_MODE = /'CRAIG_BAMPTON', [DEFAUT] > /'INTERF', > / 'PSEUDO', Makes it possible to define the method of computation of the interface modes associated with GROUP_MA_INTERF. If TYPE_MODE == 'CRAIG_BAMPTON', all the attachment modes or constrained modes associated with the soil-structure interface are computed. If TYPE_MODE == 'INTERF', the user must specify the number of static modes to be computed via the keyword NB_MODE_INTERF. If TYPE_MODE == 'PSEUDO', six rigid-body modes are computed. 10.3 Parameters of the soil analysis ◊ PARAMETRE= _F( This factor keyword makes it possible to enter the parameters of the MISS3D analysis. One should refer to the document U7.03.12 for further details. 10.4 Operands ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z, DEPL_X, DEPL_Y, DEPL_Z In the case of a transient analysis, these operands make it possible to supply the accelerograms by means of accelerations in one or several directions (ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z) or of imposed displacements in one or several directions (DEPL_X, DEPL_Y, DEPL_Z). 11 Non-linear behaviours ◊ COMPORTEMENT = _F(...) Keyword making it possible to define various types of localised non-linearities in the case of a transient analysis on a generalised basis. One should refer to the documentation U4.53.03 for further details. 12 Fluid-structure interaction ◊IFS = 'OUI', Activation de la prise en compte de l’interaction fluide-structure. Dans ce cas, l’interaction fluide-structure est prise en compte via des masses ajoutées avec un calcul dynamique sur base généralisée. 12.1 Taking the added force into account ◊ FORC_AJOU = 'OUI', This keyword handles the taking into account of the added forces due to the seismic entrainment motion. One may refer to the document U4.66.03 for further details. 12.2 Fluid-structure interface ♦ GROUP_MA_INTERF = interf, [gr_ma] Defines the mesh-cell group of the fluid-structure interface 12.3 Fluid model 12.3.1 MODELISATION_FLU ♦ MODELISATION_FLU = / '3D' > / 'COQUE' Type of modelling for the fluid model 12.3.2 GROUP_MA_FLUIDE ♦ GROUP_MA_FLUIDE = fluide, [gr_ma] Mesh-cell group on which the fluid model is supported. 12.4 Properties of the fluid ♦ RHO_FLUIDE = _F(...) Factor keyword under which one assigns the characteristics of the fluid material. If the density of the fluid varies over the fluid domain, one must specify these different densities by several occurrences of the factor keyword RHO_FLUIDE. 12.4.1 Operand RHO ♦ RHO = rho , [R] Density of the fluid. 12.4.2 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', > / GROUP_MA = grma, [gr_ma] Part of the fluid model on which the density rho is applied. 12.5 Boundary conditions for the fluid problem ♦ PRESSION_FLU_IMPO = _F(...) Factor keyword by which one specifies the boundary conditions of the fluid (of Dirichlet type). 12.5.1 Operand PRESS_FLUIDE ♦ PRESS_FLUIDE = pres [R] Keyword under which one specifies the value which one imposes on the hydrodynamic pressure (that is to say the pressure perturbation created by the vibration of the structure) on the topological entity determined below. 12.5.2 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO = grno [gr_no] Node groups at which one imposes the pressure pres on the fluid domain. 13 Factor keyword SOLVEUR One should refer to the document U4.50.01. The use of the keyword SOLVEUR is not possible in the case of an analysis with soil-structure interaction.

u4.53.22 Operator DYNA_ALEA_MODAL u4.53.22 Operator DYNA_ALEA_MODAL 1 Purpose This operator makes it possible to compute the spectral density matrix of the response of a linear structure under an excitation whose spectral density matrix is known (one also says excitation interspectrum). The operator then supplies the modal response in the form of its spectral density (the interspectrum of the response). The concept produced is of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = DYNA_ALEA_MODAL( ◆ BASE_MODALE = _F( ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◆ / BANDE = float, / NUME_ORDRE = int, # Si: exists("BANDE") ◆ AMOR_UNIF = float, # Si: exists("NUME_ORDRE") ◆ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ), ◇ MODE_STAT = mode_meca, ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ INTE_SPEC = interspectre, ◇ NUME_VITE_FLUI = int, ◇ OPTION = / "TOUT" (par défaut), / "DIAG", ◇ MODAL = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: (not exists("MODAL")) or (equal_to("MODAL", 'NON')) ◆ / NUME_ORDRE_I = int, / NOEUD_I = no, # Si: exists("NUME_ORDRE_I") ◇ / CHAM_NO = cham_no, / NOEUD = no, # Si: exists("NOEUD") ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ GRANDEUR = / "DEPL_R" (par défaut), / "EFFO", / "SOUR_DEBI_VOLU", / "SOUR_DEBI_MASS", / "SOUR_PRESS", / "SOUR_FORCE", ◇ DERIVATION = / 0 (par défaut), / 1, / 2, # Si: exists("NOEUD_I") ◆ NOM_CMP_I = text, ◆ NOEUD = no, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ GRANDEUR = / "DEPL_R" (par défaut), / "EFFO", / "SOUR_DEBI_VOLU", / "SOUR_DEBI_MASS", / "SOUR_PRESS", / "SOUR_FORCE", ◇ DERIVATION = / 0 (par défaut), / 1, / 2, # Si: (equal_to("MODAL", 'OUI')) ◆ NUME_ORDRE_I = int, ◇ GRANDEUR = / "DEPL_R" (par défaut), / "EFFO", / "SOUR_DEBI_VOLU", / "SOUR_DEBI_MASS", / "SOUR_PRESS", / "SOUR_FORCE", ◇ DERIVATION = / 0 (par défaut), / 1, / 2, ), ◇ REPONSE = _F( ◇ DERIVATION = / 0 (par défaut), / 1, / 2, ◇ OPTION = / "TOUT" (par défaut), / "DIAG", ◇ & FREQ_MIN = float, & FREQ_MAX = float, ◇ PAS = float, # Si: not exists("FREQ_MIN") ◇ FREQ_EXCIT = / "AVEC" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ NB_POIN_MODE = int (défaut: 50), ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Features The operator DYNA_ALEA_MODAL makes it possible to compute the response, in the frequency domain and on a modal basis, of a structure subjected to an excitation represented by an interspectral matrix (cf. DEFI_INTE_SPEC U4.36.02). The excitation quantity (grandeur) may be of the type imposed degree of freedom, or a force associated with a degree of freedom. It may also correspond to fluid excitation sources R4.05.02. The excitation may be given in derived form of order equal to 0, 1 or 2 (displacement, velocity or acceleration). The operator REST_SPEC_PHYS U4.63.22 makes it possible to restore the response in displacement or in force at the degrees of freedom “of observation” (node, component pair). The interspectral matrix of modal response thus computed may be reintroduced into a new analysis. 4 Operands 4.1 Keyword BASE_MODALE ♦ BASE_MODALE = _F ( Factor keyword for the definition of the parameters for selecting the modal basis of the analysis. 4.1.1 Operand MODE_MECA ♦ MODE_MECA = modemec modemec is the concept of type mode_meca containing the dynamic modes. 4.1.2 Operands NUME_ORDRE / AMOR_REDUIT / NUME_ORDRE = lordre lordre is the list of the order numbers of the modes of the concept modemec which are actually taken into account in the analysis. Example: (2,3,4) . AMOR_REDUIT = lamor lamor is the list of the reduced modal dampings corresponding to the modes retained. The number of elements of the list is equal to the number of elements of lordre. Example: (0.05,0.05,0.02) . This keyword can be used only with NUME_ORDRE. 4.1.3 Operands BANDE / AMOR_UNIF / BANDE = (f1 f2) The dynamic modes taken into account will be those of modemec whose frequency lies in the band (f1 f2) AMOR_UNIF = amor For each mode retained, the damping is equal to amor. This keyword can be used only with BANDE. 4.2 Operand MODE_STAT ◊ MODE_STAT = mosta Concept of type mode_meca containing the static modes required for the analysis. This keyword is necessary only in the case of a multi-support seismic analysis in which the excitation is applied on degrees of freedom (i.e. when the keyword GRANDEUR under the factor keyword EXCIT is equal to 'DEPL_R'). 4.3 Keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT = _F ( Factor keyword defining all the parameters concerning the excitation. The keywords DERIVATION, GRANDEUR and MODAL define the type of excitation. The keywords INTE_SPEC, NUME_VITE_FLUI, NUME_ORDRE_I, NUME_ORDRE_J, NOEUD_I, NOEUD_J, NOM_CMP_I and NOM_CMP_J define the excitation interspectrum. 4.3.1 Operand DERIVATION DERIVATION = When the excitation quantity (grandeur) is of the type imposed degree of freedom ('DEPL_R'), this keyword makes it possible to describe whether the excitation interspectrum must be considered as an imposed displacement, velocity or acceleration. The user then specifies 0, 1 or 2. This keyword is optional. By default, it is equal to 0. Note: In the case of a seismic analysis, the excitation is often an acceleration. This keyword must then be equal to 2. 4.3.2 Operand GRANDEUR ◊ GRANDEUR = This keyword makes it possible to state whether the excitation is of the type imposed degree of freedom ('DEPL_R'), imposed force ('EFFO'), volume flow-rate source ('SOUR_DEBI_VOLU'), mass flow-rate source ('SOUR_DEBI_MASS'), pressure source ('SOUR_PRESS') or fluid force source ('SOUR_FORCE'). This keyword is optional. By default, it is equal to 'DEPL_R' and the excitation is of the type imposed displacement degree of freedom in every case except in the case of supports represented by assembled vectors (keyword CHAM_NO). 4.3.3 Operands INTE_SPEC and NUME_VITE_FLUI These keywords define the excitation interspectrum (or interspectra). ♦ INTE_SPEC = interexc interexc is the concept of type interspectre containing the set of excitation interspectral matrices (spectral density matrices). It is taken into account as it is defined in the function associated with the concept, that is to say in particular that a possible folding of the spectrum is not interpreted. For a function defined by: f\in [{f}_{1,}{f}_{2}]:\tilde{S}(f) given One will interpret: \begin{array}{}f {f}_{2}:S(f)=0\end{array} If the frequency loop [{f}_{1,}{f}_{2}] must be reproduced for the negative frequencies, one must: - either give the whole of the spectrum on the real axis, - or apply a coefficient 2 to the value of the DSP, a possible workaround, since the spectral densities are assumed to be symmetric in the analyses carried out by the command DYNA_ALEA_MODAL. > The parameters required of the table are: 1. if one indexes the parameters of the table by order numbers: ‘NUME_ORDRE_I’[I], ‘NUME_ORDRE_J’[I], ‘FONCTION’[K24] 2. otherwise: ‘NŒUD_I’[K8], ‘NŒUD_J’[K8], ‘NOM_CMP_I’[K8], ‘NOM_CMP_J’[K8], ‘FONCTION’[K24]. 3. The table must be complete: presence of the auto-spectra (diagonal term of the matrix) and of the interspectra (off-diagonal term of the matrix). Cette table peut être générée par les opérateurs: DEFI_SPEC_MODAL, LIRE_INTE_SPEC ou CALC_INTE_SPEC. Le lecteur est invité à consulter la documentation de la commande TEST_FONCTION [:external:ref: U4.92.02 ] pour davantage d’informations sur le sens des paramètres. ◊ NUME_VITE_FLUI = nk nk est le numéro d’ordre de la vitesse du fluide associé à interexc. 4.3.4 Operands NUME_ORDRE_I, NOEUD, NOM_CMP, CHAM_NO and MODAL These keywords link the terms (line numbers in the matrix) of the excitation interspectrum and the excitation point (or points) for a modal excitation, or when the parameters of the table have been indexed by order numbers. ♦ / ♦ NUME_ORDRE_I = (noi1, noi2,..) This list of order numbers makes it possible to determine the term (line number) of the given interspectral matrix. The length of this list must correspond to the number of excitations imposed on the structure. ♦ / ♦ NOEUD = list_noe This keyword makes it possible to specify the nodes at which the multi-spectral excitation will be applied. Example ('N1', 'N5', 'N7'). For all types of excitation quantity (grandeur), except for pressure sources and force sources, list_noe contains as many terms as there are indices defining excitation interspectra. In the case of pressure sources or force sources, a dipole is associated with each source, that is to say two points of application. list_noe then has twice as many terms as there are indices defining interspectra. ♦ NOM_CMP = list_cmp This keyword makes it possible to specify the components on which the multi-spectral excitation will be applied. Example ('PRES' 'DRZ' 'PHI'). These components must of course correspond to degrees of freedom of the support nodes. In every case, list_cmp has the same number of elements as list_noe. For fluid sources, it is the degree of freedom 'PRES' which is excited. ◊ MODAL = 'NON' [DEFAUT] The excitation is not modal in this case. / ♦ cham_no= list_vass When this keyword is present, each excitation support is an assembled vector defined beforehand in the command file. list_vass contains the list of the assembled vectors standing in for supports. The associated exciting quantity (grandeur) is 'EFFO'. It is recommended that the intensity associated with the force which one imposes in this way be given by the interspectrum: the assembled vector serves essentially to define a shape function supporting a force power spectrum. It is therefore normalised. This option makes it possible to assign a force power spectrum on a shape function. In every case, list_vass contains as many terms as there are indices defining interspectra. / ♦ MODAL = 'OUI' The presence of 'OUI' under this keyword implies that the excitation interspectrum is considered as a modal excitation. 4.3.5 Operands NOEUD_I and NOM_CMP_I These keywords link the terms (line numbers in the matrix) of the excitation interspectrum (or interspectra) and the excitation points when the parameters of the table have been indexed by physical data consisting of the pair (Node-Component). ♦/ ♦ NOEUD_I = ndi1, ndi2,... ♦ NOM_CMP_I = cmpi1, cmpi2,... These lists are paired two by two in order to determine the term (line number) of the given interspectral matrix. The length of the preceding lists must correspond to the number of excitations imposed on the structure. ♦ NOEUD = list_noe [l_noeud] ♦ NOM_CMP = list_comp [l_cmp] These two keywords have the same meaning as in [§4.3.4]. ◊ MODAL = 'NON' [DEFAUT] L'excitation n'est pas modale dans ce cas. 4.4 Keyword REPONSE ♦ REPONSE = _F ( Factor keyword for the definition of all the parameters concerning the response. The following three keywords describe the type of the response. 4.4.1 Operand DERIVATION ◊ DERIVATION = Ce mot-clé a le même sens que pour le mot-clé facteur EXCIT [:ref: §4.3.1 ]. 4.4.2 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION = If this keyword is specified with 'DIAG', then all the off-diagonal functions of the response interspectrum are initialised to zero without being computed. Only the auto-spectra are computed. Otherwise ('TOUT'), all the functions of the response interspectrum are computed. 4.4.3 Operands FREQ_MIN / FREQ_MAX / PAS / FREQ_EXCIT / NB_POIN_MODE These keywords serve to describe the frequency discretisation in which the response will be given. ◊ ♦ FREQ_MIN = fmin ♦ FREQ_MAX = fmax fmin and fmax are the two bounds of the frequency interval. pas is the minimum discretisation step. ◊ PAS = pas If the values of fmin and fmax are given, pas is then by default equal to \frac{{f}_{\max}-{f}_{\min}}{100} . Otherwise one takes for fmax the largest eigenfrequency of the dynamic modes retained for the analysis. The discretisation then covers the domain [0;{\mathrm{2.f}}_{\max}] , \mathrm{pas}=\frac{{\mathrm{2.f}}_{\max}}{100} . On the other hand, if pas is present, one makes sure that the discretisation step of the response is everywhere less than pas. ◊ FREQ_EXCIT = / 'AVEC' / 'SANS' If the user gives the argument 'AVEC' under the keyword FREQ_EXCIT, then the frequencies of the excitation are included in the discretisation of the response (default option). If the user gives the argument 'SANS', they will be ignored. This keyword is set to 'SANS' if the keyword FREQ_MIN is present. ◊ NB_POIN_MODE = n [:ref: défaut = 50 ] The response is more refined at the eigenfrequencies in order to ensure a good description of the response at the peaks. The keyword NB_POIN_MODE makes it possible to define the number of frequency steps per eigenfrequency taken into account. By default, there are 50 steps per eigenfrequency. This keyword is not taken into account if FREQ_MIN is given. Each function of the interspectrum will by default have an interpolation mode of linear type and an extension mode outside the discretisation domain of type 'EXCLU'. 4.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre titre is the title of the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results. See U4.03.01. 4.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Specifies the printout options on the MESSAGE file. | 1 | no printout | | --- | --- | | 2 | recalls the analysis options chosen. | 5 Table produced > The parameters of the table produced are described in the table below: | PARAMETRE | TYPE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | --- | | NOM_CHAM | K16 | name of the field (=’DEPL_GENE’) | | OPTION | K16 | name of the option (‘TOUT’ or ‘DIAG’) | | DIMENSION | I | dimension | | NUME_VITE_FLUI | I | order number of the interspectral matrix of modal response | | VITE_FLUIDE | R | corresponding fluid velocity | | NUME_ORDRE_I NUME_ORDRE_J | K8 | Indices of the order numbers i and j making it possible to define a term of the interspectral matrix | | FONCTION | K24 | name of the modal-response function corresponding to the matrix term defined by NUME_ORDRE_x | 6 Useful notes for use - Need for a static mode and type of dynamic modes: In the case of an excitation by imposed displacement, the dynamic modes are computed with fixed supports and the presence of the static mode is mandatory. In the other cases, the dynamic modes are computed with free supports, and the presence of a static mode is no longer justified. The dimension of the interspectral matrix is given by the sum of the static modes and of the dynamic modes (if there are any) taken into account. Thus, for a structure with five dynamic modes, excited in displacement by two supports, the dimension of the interspectral matrix of modal response is 7. If the excitation is given as an imposed force, there are no static modes and the dimension of the interspectral matrix is 5. - Use of the keyword MODAL under the factor keyword EXCIT: In the case where the keyword MODAL is used under the factor keyword EXCIT in order to introduce directly the modal spectral density matrix as the excitation, one must give again, under the keywords EXCIT, BASE_MODALE and MODE_STAT, all the arguments which had been used to create this modal interspectral matrix (support nodes and degrees of freedom). 7 Verification stage One checks the consistency of the data: - number of modal dampings = number of modes retained. - number of support nodes equal to the number of components (for the excitation). - number of pairs of indices retained in the excitation interspectrum = number of supports or number of excitation points. - in the case of pressure sources: number of support nodes equal to twice the number of pairs of indices retained in the excitation interspectrum. - the presence of a mode_meca is checked in the cases of excitation by a quantity (grandeur) of type DEPL_R. - \mathrm{fmax}\ge \mathrm{fmin} 8 Example DYNALEA1=DYNA_ALEA_MODAL( BASE_MODALE=_F( MODE_MECA = FREQ1, NUME_ORDRE = 1, AMOR_REDUIT = 0.05), MODE_STAT=MODESTA1, EXCIT=_F( DERIVATION = 2, INTE_SPEC = INTEREXC, NUME_ORDRE_I = 1, NUME_ORDRE_J = 1, NOEUD = 'P1', NOM_CMP = 'DX'), REPONSE=_F( DERIVATION = 2), )

u4.53.23 Operator DYNA_SPEC_MODAL u4.53.23 Operator DYNA_SPEC_MODAL 1 Purpose Compute the response, by modal recombination, of a linear structure to a random excitation. This excitation is defined in the form of power interspectra of modal forces. The response is established in the form of power interspectra of the generalised displacements. Each interspectral matrix is associated with a modal basis for which the response is computed. The result produced is a concept of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = DYNA_SPEC_MODAL( ◆ BASE_ELAS_FLUI = melasflu, ◆ VITE_FLUI = float, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ INTE_SPEC_GENE = interspectre, ), ◇ OPTION = / "TOUT" (par défaut), / "DIAG", ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand BASE_ELAS_FLUI ♦ BASE_ELAS_FLUI = bef Concept of type melasflu; it defines a set of modal bases associated with the various flow velocities of the fluid. 3.2 Keyword VITE_FLUI ♦ VITE_FLUI = vitefl Flow velocity of the fluid for the response analysis. 3.3 Keyword PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = prec Accuracy on the flow velocity of the fluid (by default 1 E-3). 3.4 Keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT Factor keyword which defines the excitation. ♦ INTE_SPEC_GENE = exc Concept of type interspectre; it defines the excitation interspectra (modal forces). 3.5 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION = ’TOUT’ ou ’DIAG’ Text argument which indicates whether one wants to compute all the interspectra, 'TOUT', or the auto-spectra only, 'DIAG'. By default all the interspectra are computed. 3.6 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Text argument defining the title attached to the output concept of type interspectre.

u4.53.31 Operator DYNA_ISS_VARI u4.53.31 Operator DYNA_ISS_VARI 1 Purpose This operator makes it possible to compute the response of a structure subjected to a seismic motion which varies in space, from a coherence function, the impedance matrix and the seismic force. The latter may be computed by the PROMISS3D software. More precisely, one builds the spectral vectors of modal response (coming from a spectral decomposition of the coherence matrix) by means of a harmonic analysis in generalised components. As output, one obtains the power spectral density (DSP) of the modal response (for a unit excitation) or the time response in acceleration, from which response spectra can be deduced if accelerograms are given in one or several directions. Produces a concept of type interspectre or tran_gene. 2 Syntax / interspectre / tran_gene = DYNA_ISS_VARI( ◆ / EXCIT_SOL = _F( ◆ | ACCE_X = fonction, | ACCE_Y = fonction, | ACCE_Z = fonction, ), / NB_FREQ = int, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.999), ◇ ISSF = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◆ INTERF = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, ◆ MODE_INTERF = / "CORP_RIGI", / "TOUT", / "QUELCONQUE", ), ◆ MATR_COHE = _F( ◆ TYPE = / "MITA_LUCO", / "ABRAHAMSON", / "ABRA_ROCHER", / "ABRA_SOLMOYEN", # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'MITA_LUCO') ◆ VITE_ONDE = float, ◇ PARA_ALPHA = float (défaut: 0.1), ), ◇ UNITE_RESU_FORC = unit (défaut: 33), ◇ UNITE_RESU_IMPE = unit (défaut: 32), ◇ TYPE = / "BINAIRE", / "ASCII" (par défaut), ◆ MATR_GENE = _F( ◆ MATR_MASS = matr_asse_gene_r, ◆ MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_gene_c, ◇ MATR_AMOR = matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_gene_c, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, # Si: exists("EXCIT_SOL") ◇ & FREQ_MAX = float, & FREQ_PAS = float, # Si: exists("NB_FREQ") ◆ FREQ_INIT = float, ◆ FREQ_PAS = float, ◇ OPTION = / "TOUT" (par défaut), / "DIAG", ◆ NOM_CMP = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands UNITE_RESU_IMPE and UNITE_RESU_FORC ♦ UNITE_RESU_IMPE = / uresimp, [I] / 32, [DEFAUT] Logical unit of the file of the interface impedance matrix computed by CALC_MISS with option TYPE_RESU='FICHIER'. This matrix may either already have been computed and given as input in the study profile, or be the result of CALC_MISS in the same command file. ♦ UNITE_RESU_FORC = / uresfor, [I] / 33, [DEFAUT] Logical unit of the file of the interface seismic forces computed beforehand by MISS3D with CALC_MISS in post-processing and given as input in the study profile. 3.2 Operand TYPE ◊ TYPE= / 'BINAIRE' / 'ASCII' [DEFAUT] This operand makes it possible to read the impedances computed by the command CALC_MISS U7.03.12 in a file of binary format if necessary. 3.3 Factor keyword EXCIT_SOL If one wishes to obtain a time response , one must give one or several accelerograms via the keywords ACCE_X, ACCE_Y and ACCE_Z. Note: If EXCIT_SOL is not supplied, then DYNA_ISS_VARI gives as output the spectral densities of the response (for a unit excitation). 3.3.1 Operands ACCE_X, ACCE_Y and ACCE_Z > ◊ ACCE_X = accex [fonction_sdaster] ◊ ACCE_Y = accey [fonction_sdaster] ◊ ACCE_Z = accez [fonction_sdaster] Accelerograms, respectively in the directions X , Y and Z . If several operands are supplied then the signals must have the same abscissae. The frequency discretisation is determined from the time discretisation of the accelerograms: \mathit{FREQ}\text{\_}\mathit{INIT}=0.0,\mathit{PAS}=1./(\mathit{NB}\mathrm{\ast }\mathit{DT}) , where NB denotes the number of time steps of the accelerogram and DT is the time step. Note: The time step of the accelerogram must be constant. 3.4 Operands FREQ_MAX and FREQ_PAS If EXCIT_SOL is present, in order to reduce the computation time, it is possible to indicate the frequency step and the maximum frequency for the computation of the transfer function (recommended): ◊ FREQ_MAX = fmax ◊ FREQ_PAS = pas If FREQ_MAX and FREQ_PAS are supplied, then one determines the transfer function, taking spatial variability into account, only for a reduced number of frequencies. For the computation of the time response to the excitation by a seismic signal (accelerogram), one interpolates these values in order to arrive at the frequency discretisation required by Shannon's theorem. If FREQ_MAX is less than the cut-off frequency (\mathrm{NB}-1)\ast \mathrm{PAS} of the signal, then one completes the response with zeros up to the cut-off frequency. The last frequency of the analysis is consequently the cut-off frequency. One should check that the step FREQ_PAS is not too small in order to model the transfer function with spatial variability properly. 3.5 Operand NB_FREQ If one wishes to compute spectral densities , then one must indicate the parameters of the discretisation in the frequency domain (harmonic analysis) as follows: ♦ NB_FREQ = NF Number of frequency steps to be computed. ♦ FREQ_INIT = fini Starting frequency of the harmonic analysis. ♦ FREQ_PAS = pas Value of the frequency step for the harmonic analysis. ◊ OPTION = / 'TOUT', [DEFAUT] / 'DIAG', By default, one obtains as output the DSP matrix of the transfer function (or of the response for a unit excitation). If one chooses OPTION ='DIAG', then one recovers only the diagonal terms of this matrix. Note: This is the DSP in generalised coordinates. In most studies, one must first carry out the projection with the complete DSP matrix in order to retain only the diagonal terms of the response DSP in physical coordinates. 3.6 Operand NOM_CMP ♦ NOM_CMP = / 'DX', / 'DY', / 'DZ', Name of the component corresponding to a direction of the incident seismic field. This keyword is to be supplied only if NB_FREQ is present. 3.7 Operand ISSF ◊ ISSF = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT] Cet opérande indique si on a ou pas un domaine de fluide et donc aussi des interfaces fluide-structure et sol-fluide renseignées par les opérandes GROUP_MA_FLU_STRet GROUP_MA_FLU_SOLdans la commande IMPR_MACR_ELEM[U7.04.33]. 3.8 Keyword INTERF 3.8.1 Operand MODE_INTERF ♦ MODE_INTERF = / 'TOUT', / 'CORP_RIGI' / 'QUELCONQUE' This operand makes it possible to characterise the type of interface modes of the model. Three types of interface mode are possible: if one chooses a modelling based on the six rigid-body modes, one must supply 'CORP_RIGI'; if one works with all the interface modes (unit finite-element modes), one supplies 'TOUT'. For all the other foundation cases (embedded geometry, modes of arbitrary representation for a flexible foundation, the case ISSF='OUI'), one supplies 'QUELCONQUE'. 3.8.2 Operand GROUP_NO_INTERF ♦ GROUP_NO_INTERF = gr_inter With this keyword, one defines the node group supported by the surface mesh cells which make up the soil-structure interface. 3.9 Keyword MATR_COHE 3.9.1 Operands VITE_ONDE and PARA_ALPHA > ♦ TYPE = modele > One may choose between the coherence function of Mita & Luco (MITA_LUCO) and three empirical coherence functions established by Abrahamson (ABRAHAMSON, ABRA_ROCHER, ABRA_SOLMOYEN). > If one chooses MITA_LUCO, then one may supply: ♦ VITE_ONDE = :math: {V}_{s} ◊ PARA_ALPHA = :math: \alpha These are the parameters of the coherence function of Luco and Wong (pure incoherence without the wave-passage effect): \gamma (d)=\exp[-(\alpha .2\pi f.\frac{d}{{V}_{s}}{)}^{2}] where d denotes the distance between two points i and j on the foundation, f is the frequency and {V}_{s} the propagation velocity of the wave. The propagation velocity VITE_ONDE initially considered by Mita & Luco is equal to 600 m/s. The parameter \alpha is dimensionless; by default it is taken equal to 0.5. The three models of Abrahamson are - ABRAHAMSON: generic coherence model of Abrahamson (EPRI 1014101, 2006) - ABRA_ROCHER: model for a rock site established by Abrahamson from earthquakes recorded at Pinyon Flat, USA (EPRI 1015110, 2007). - ABRA_SOLMOYEN: model for a medium-soil site established by Abrahamson from various medium-soil sites in the USA (EPRI 1015110, 2007). 3.10 Keyword MATR_GENE 3.10.1 Operands MATR_MASS, MATR_RIGI, MATR_AMOR ♦ MATR_MASS = m Name of the assembled-matrix concept corresponding to the generalised mass matrix of the system. ♦ MATR_RIGI = rigigen Name of the assembled-matrix concept corresponding to the generalised stiffness matrix of the system. A hysteretic damping is obtained with a complex stiffness matrix. ◊ MATR_AMOR = amogen Name of the assembled generalised-matrix concept corresponding to the generalised damping matrix of the system. 3.11 Operand PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = prec This parameter is by default taken equal to 0.999. For the computation of the seismic forces with spatial variability of the incident field, one carries out the spectral decomposition of the coherence matrix [{\gamma}_{ij}] , i=\mathrm{1...},M . The parameter prec gives the share of the “energy” of the matrix which one retains by keeping only a reduced number of eigenvectors. If one denotes by K\ll M the number of eigenvalues retained (one retains the K largest eigenvalues), one has \text{prec}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{K}{\lambda}_{i}^{2}}{\sum_{i=1}^{M}{\lambda}_{i}^{2}} 3.12 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Indicates the level of printout of the results of the operator. | 1 = | no particular printout, | | --- | --- | | 2 = | printout of the eigenvalues retained from the spectral decomposition. | The printouts are made in the file 'MESSAGE'. 4 Examples of use Two examples of use of DYNA_ISS_VARI are presented here. The first example presents an analysis of the spectral density of the response. The second example presents an analysis of an oscillator response spectrum. The user must beforehand have carried out a ProMISS3D analysis (CALC_MISS U7.03.12 with TYPE_RESU='FICHIER'). 4.1 Example 1 An example of a set of commands is presented here for the computation of the spectral density of the response, taking into account the spatial variability of the incident seismic motion. RESU = DYNA_ISS_VARI( FREQ_INIT =fmin, NB_FREQ = NF, PAS = df , NOM_CMP = ‘DX’, PRECISION = 0.999 , INTERF =_F( GROUP_NO_INTERF='RADIER', MODE_INTERF ='CORP_RIGI',), MATR_COHE = _F( VITE_ONDE = 600. , PARA_ALPHA =0.5,), UNITE_RESU_IMPE = 32, UNITE_RESU_FORC = 33, MATR_GENE = _F( MATR_MASS = MASSGEN, MATR_RIGI = RIGIGEN, MATR_AMOR = AMORT, ), INFO =2 ,); One may also consult the test case SDLS118A for an implementation of the method. One can recover the spectral density of the response in physical coordinates by means of the operator REST_SPEC_PHYS. SPVX=REST_SPEC_PHYS( MODE_MECA=BAMO, TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', INTE_SPEC_GENE = RESU, NOM_CHAM='DEPL', NOEUD=( 'N77' ), NOM_CMP=('DX', ), OPTION='TOUT_TOUT' ); The transfer function is obtained for a unit seismic excitation and by plotting the square root of the values of the auto-spectrum. 4.2 Example 2 An example of a set of commands is presented here for the computation of the spectral density of the response, taking into account the spatial variability of the incident seismic motion. RESU = DYNA_ISS_VARI( EXCIT_SOL= _F(ACCE_X=ACCE_X), FREQ_MAX =50.0, FREQ_PAS = 0.5 , PRECISION = 0.99 , INTERF =_F( GROUP_NO_INTERF='RADIER', MODE_INTERF ='CORP_RIGI',), MATR_COHE = _F( VITE_ONDE = 600. , PARA_ALPHA =0.5,), UNITE_RESU_IMPE = 32, UNITE_RESU_FORC = 33, MATR_GENE = _F( MATR_MASS = MASSGEN, MATR_RIGI = RIGIGEN, MATR_AMOR = AMORT, ), INFO =2 ,); test_1=RECU_FONCTION(RESU_GENE=test_1_a, > NOM_CHAM='ACCE', > NOM_CMP='DX', > NOEUD=( 'N11' ), > INTERPOL='LIN', > TITRE='ACCELERATION AT THE LOWER CENTRE OF THE BASEMAT',); > SROX1=CALC_FONCTION(SPEC_OSCI=_F(FONCTION=test_1, > NORME=9.81, AMOR_REDUIT=0.05, ),); One may also consult the test case SDLS118B for an implementation of the method.

('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = int, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ◇ INFO = int (défaut: 1), ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Reminders 3.1 Optimisation problem associated with an energy functional This operator solves the following problem: Find the triplet of admissible fields (u,v,w)\text{} which minimises the functional: {e}_{\omega}^{2}(u,v,w)=\frac{\gamma}{2}{(u-v)}^{T}K+\frac{1-\gamma }{2}{(u-w)}^{T}{\omega}^{2}M+\frac{1-\alpha }{\alpha}{(\mathit{Hu}-\widehat{u})}^{T}\text{}\mathit{Gr} under the constraint: \left[K\right]v-{\omega}^{2}\left[M\right]\text{w=}0 Where: K represents a real stiffness matrix M represents a mass matrix H represents an observation matrix \mathit{Gr} represents a symmetric positive-definite matrix serving as the norm of the errors in the observation space \omega =2\pi f : excitation angular frequency \widehat{u} observation of the displacements at the angular frequency \omega \gamma weighting parameter of the errors (u-v) and (u-w) \alpha weighting parameter of the functional, which can be likened to a regularisation term 3.2 Equations for the solution of the problem Obtaining the triplet (u,v,w)\text{} associated with the constrained problem above leads, at each frequency considered, to the solution of the following system of linear equations: Al=b with, for each natural angular frequency {\omega}_{i} : {A}_{i}=\left(\begin{array}{cc}\gamma \left(\text{K+γ}/\left(1-\gamma \right){\omega}_{i}^{2}M\right)& -\gamma \left(K-{\omega}_{i}^{2}M\right)\\ -\gamma \left(K-{\omega}_{i}^{2}M\right)& \left(-\text{2α}/\left(1-\alpha \right)\right){H}^{T}{G}_{r}H\end{array}\right) ; and {b}_{i}=\left(\begin{array}{c}{0}_{n}\\ \left(-\text{2α}/\left(1-\alpha \right)\right){H}^{T}{G}_{r}{\widehat{u}}_{i}\end{array}\right) For further details on the formulation, one should refer to the document R4.10.07. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand MATR_MASS ♦ MATR_MASS = m Name of the assembled-matrix concept corresponding to the mass matrix of the system. 4.2 Operand MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_RIGI = k Name of the assembled-matrix concept corresponding to the stiffness matrix of the system. 4.3 Operand MATR_NORME ♦ MATR_NORME = g Name of the assembled generalised-matrix concept corresponding to the symmetric positive-definite matrix serving as the norm of the errors in the observation space. 4.4 Operand MATR_PROJECTION ♦ MATR_PROJECTION = h Name of the projection matrix making it possible to establish the geometric correspondence between the mesh associated with the mass and stiffness matrices on the one hand, and the mesh associated with the observations \widehat{u} on the other hand. The projection matrix h must come from an analysis with the operator PROJ_CHAMP U4.72.05 with the method 'COLLOCATION'. 4.5 Operand MESURE ♦ MESURE = me Name of the concept of type mode_meca or dyna_harmo containing the fields which will be used as the observation. This concept must contain as many order numbers as the number of frequencies which will be studied when the operator is called (operands FREQ/LIST_FREQ). Furthermore, the fields contained in me must not include degrees of freedom of Lagrange type. The dimension of the fields contained in this concept must be consistent with the dimension of the norm matrix g supplied under the operand MATR_NORME. The use of the operator OBSERVATION U4.90.03 may be an appropriate means of conditioning a concept of type mode_meca or dyna_harmo as the measurement me. 4.6 Operand CHAMP_MESURE > ◊ CHAMP_MESURE = | 'DEPL', [DEFAUT] | 'VITE', | 'ACCE', Choice of the fields determining the type of field contained in the measurement me. 4.7 Operands FREQ/LIST_FREQ ◊ / FREQ = lf List of all the analysis frequencies: (f1, f2, ..., fn). / LIST_FREQ = cf Name of the concept of type listr8 containing the list of the analysis frequencies. 4.8 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmat Nom du champ de matériau. Peut-être utile pour certains post-traitements. 4.9 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac Nom des caractéristiques des éléments de poutre, coque etc, nécessaire pour certains post-traitements. 4.10 Operand ALPHA ♦ ALPHA = al, Value of the weighting parameter of the functional, which can be likened to the regularisation term. 4.11 Operand GAMMA ♦ GAMMA = ga, Value of the weighting parameter of the errors (u-v) and (u-w) of the functional. 4.12 Operand EVAL_FONC > ◊ EVAL_FONC = | 'OUI', [DEFAUT] | 'NON', Choice determining whether the value of the functional for the optimal triplet of fields will be evaluated and stored in the result. If so, the operator will store the computed values under the dedicated parameter 'ERC_EVAL_FONC'. The value of 'ERC_EVAL_FONC' is stored in the following way in the output concept of type mode_meca: For the i-th analysis frequency, two values of 'ERC_EVAL_FONC' are stored: - in the (2 (i-1)+1)-th nume_ordre of the output concept one stores the value of {e}_{{\omega}_{i}}^{2}(u,v,w) - in the (2 (i-1)+2)-th nume_ordre of the output concept one stores the value associated with the term of the error fields (u-v) and (u-w) as follows: \frac{\gamma}{2}{(u-v)}^{T}K+\frac{1-\gamma }{2}{(u-w)}^{T}{\omega}^{2}M 4.13 Operands SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR This factor keyword is optional. It makes it possible to define the method of solution of the system. The syntax is described in the document U4.50.01. In the current version, the solvers available are MUMPS (default) and LDLT. 4.14 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = tx Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 5 Storage of the solution fields The operator CALC_ERC_DYN produces a result concept of type mode_meca. At each required frequency, it computes the solution fields u and (u-v) , which are stored in the following way: For the i-th analysis frequency, the following are stored: - in the (2 (i-1)+1)-th nume_ordre of the output concept the field u is stored - in the (2 (i-1)+2)-th nume_ordre of the output concept the field (u-v) is stored It is recalled that the field (u-w) is not computed directly, because it can be obtained by the scalar relation: (u-w)=\frac{-\gamma }{1-\gamma }(u-v) 6 Example of use # CONSTRUCTION DES MATRICES DU MODELE MECANIQUE ASSEMBLAGE(MODELE=MODNUM, CARA_ELEM=CARE, CHARGE=CHARGE_L, NUME_DDL=CO("NU"), SOLVEUR=_F( METHODE = 'MUMPS'), MATR_ASSE=(_F( MATRICE = CO("K"), OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA'), _F( MATRICE = CO("M"), OPTION = 'MASS_MECA'),), ); # CONSTRUCTION DE LA MATRICE REDUITE DE GUYAN SERVANT DE MATRICE_NORME # CL POUR LA CONSTRUCTION DE LA MATRICE REDUITE DE GUYAN CHAR_G=AFFE_CHAR_MECA(MODELE=MODNUM,DDL_IMPO=(_F( GROUP_NO = 'OBSPOINT', DX=0. ),),); ASSEMBLAGE(MODELE=MODNUM, CARA_ELEM=CARE, CHARGE=(CHAR_G,CHARGE_L), NUME_DDL=CO("NU_G"), SOLVEUR=_F( METHODE = 'MUMPS'), MATR_ASSE=(_F( MATRICE = CO("K1"), OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA'), _F( MATRICE = CO("M1"), OPTION = 'MASS_MECA'),), ); MOD_STA=MODE_STATIQUE(MATR_RIGI=K1, MATR_MASS=M1, MODE_STAT=(_F(GROUP_NO='OBSPOINT', AVEC_CMP=('DX',),),),); NUME_RED=NUME_DDL_GENE(BASE=MOD_STA,STOCKAGE='PLEIN'); MA_RE=PROJ_MATR_BASE(BASE=MOD_STA,NUME_DDL_GENE=NUME_RED,MATR_ASSE=M); K_RE=PROJ_MATR_BASE(BASE=MOD_STA,NUME_DDL_GENE=NUME_RED,MATR_ASSE=K); # ON CHOISIT (par exemple)LA MATRICE NORME COMME UNE COMBINAISON DES # MATRICES REDUITES DE MASSE ET RAIDEUR G_GUY=COMB_MATR_ASSE(COMB_R=(_F(MATR_ASSE = MA_RE,COEF_R = 1.), _F(MATR_ASSE = K_RE, COEF_R = 1.),),); ## CALCUL DE LA MATRICE DE PROJECTION ENTRE MODELE NUMERIQUE ET EXPERIMENTAL ## (concept corresp_2_mailla) ## METHODE COLLOCATION OBLIGATOIRE POUR CALC_ERC_DYN MATPROJ = PROJ_CHAMP(METHODE='COLLOCATION', PROJECTION='NON', MODELE_1=MODNUM, MODELE_2=MODEXP); ### CONDITIONNEMENET DES MESURES (concept MODES) SUR LES DDL QUI NOUS ### INTERESSENT OBS = OBSERVATION( RESULTAT = MODES, MODELE_1 = MODNUM, MODELE_2 = MODEXP, PROJECTION = 'OUI', TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', MATR_RIGI = KASEXP, MATR_MASS = MASEXP, NOM_CHAM = 'DEPL', FILTRE = _F( GROUP_MA = 'MESURE', NOM_CHAM = ('DEPL'), DDL_ACTIF = ('DX',),),); ### RESOLUTION DU PROBLEME DE L'ERC # CHOIX DES FREQUENCES SUR LESQUELLES ON VA RESOUDRE L'ERC: LFREQ=DEFI_LIST_REEL(VALE=[0.12181191980055407,1.25 0.22507907903927654],); # CHOIX DES FREQUENCES SUR LESQUELLES ERC=CALC_ERC_DYN( EVAL_FONCTIONNELLE='OUI', MATR_PROJECTION=MATPROJ, MESURE=OBS, CHAMP_MESURE='DEPL', MATR_MASS=M, MATR_RIGI=K, MATR_NORME=G_GUY, LIST_FREQ=LFREQ, GAMMA=0.5, ALPHA=0.5, INFO=1, SOLVEUR=_F(METHODE='MUMPS',),);

u4.53.51 Operator CALC_TRANSFERT u4.53.51 Operator CALC_TRANSFERT 1 Purpose This operator makes it possible to compute the matrix of dynamic transfer functions of a linear mechanical system between two points of the numerical model. The transfer functions may be in acceleration, velocity or displacement. One can treat the case of absolute or relative motions, under the action of an entrainment excitation. It is also possible to obtain the response at any point of the numerical model as a function of an output signal supplied by the user. This operator uses as input data the responses of the mechanical system to unidirectional excitations, preferably of white-noise type. It produces one or two data structures of type table, one for the matrix of transfer functions, the other for the possible computed signal. 2 Syntax table = CALC_TRANSFERT( ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "VITE", / "ACCE", ◆ ENTREE = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ), ◆ SORTIE = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ), ◇ REPERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: equal_to("REPERE", 'RELATIF') ◆ ENTRAINEMENT = _F( ◆ DX = fonction_c / fonction, ◆ DY = fonction_c / fonction, ◇ DZ = fonction_c / fonction, ), ◆ RESULTAT_X = dyna_trans / tran_gene / harm_gene / dyna_harmo, ◆ RESULTAT_Y = dyna_trans / tran_gene / harm_gene / dyna_harmo, ◇ RESULTAT_Z = dyna_trans / tran_gene / harm_gene / dyna_harmo, ◇ SIGNAL = _F( ◆ MESURE_X = fonction_c / fonction, ◆ MESURE_Y = fonction_c / fonction, ◇ MESURE_Z = fonction_c / fonction, ◆ TABLE_RESU = co, ◇ TYPE_RESU = / "HARMONIQUE" (par défaut), / "TEMPOREL", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Description of the macro-command and preliminary steps The operator CALC_TRANSFERT makes it possible to compute the dynamic transfer-function matrix between two points of the structure (input => output). It also allows the user to determine the signal at one point of the structure (at the input) knowing the signal at another point of the structure (at the output). Figure 1 – Schematic representation of the use of the macro-command Before using the command, the user must carry out several linear dynamic analyses under unidirectional excitation. For example, if the study is in 3D (respectively 2D), the user must carry out 3 analyses (respectively 2 analyses) exciting one of the three (respectively 2) directions. It is preferable to carry out these dynamic analyses by means of a unidirectional white noise. The dynamic analyses must be carried out with the same list of frequencies if the analysis is harmonic and with the same list of time instants if the analysis is transient. For a transient analysis, the user must take care to have a list of time instants with a constant step. Otherwise an error message will be issued, because the Fourier transform required by the various analyses requires a constant step. The dynamic analyses must be of the same type, either tran_gene, or harm_gene, or dyna_trans, or else dyna_harmo. When the user must supply the entrainment functions and/or the measured signals, it is preferable that the latter be discretised on the same list of frequencies (case of a harmonic analysis) or on the same list of times (case of a transient analysis). 4 Operands 4.1 Concepts created by the command This command creates as output a concept of type table. It is also possible to output a second table containing the signals corresponding to the dynamic excitation (at the input) computed from the measured signals (at the output). The first concept produced, whatever use the user makes of the macro-command, is a table which contains the data of the transfer-function matrix arranged as follows: - The first column corresponds to the frequencies (FREQ); - The following ones correspond to the components of the matrix arranged in order by rows {H}_{xx} , {H}_{xy} , {H}_{xz} , {H}_{yx} , {H}_{yy} , {H}_{yz} , {H}_{\mathrm{zx}} , {H}_{\mathrm{zy}} and {H}_{zz} . In the 2D case, one will have {H}_{xx} , {H}_{xy} , {H}_{yx} and {H}_{yy} . H(\omega )=(\begin{array}{ccc}{H}_{xx}& {H}_{xy}& {H}_{xz}\\ {H}_{yx}& {H}_{yy}& {H}_{yz}\\ {H}_{\mathrm{zx}}& {H}_{\mathrm{zy}}& {H}_{zz}\end{array}) 4.2 Operands RESULTAT_X, RESULTAT_Y and RESULTAT_Z ♦ RESULTAT_X = resu_x Name of the concept of type resultat for which the linear dynamic analysis was carried out with a unidirectional excitation along x . ♦ RESULTAT_Y = resu_y Name of the concept of type resultat for which the linear dynamic analysis was carried out with a unidirectional excitation along y . ◊ RESULTAT_Z = resu_z Name of the concept of type resultat for which the linear dynamic analysis was carried out with a unidirectional excitation along z . Notes: Only result data structures of type dyna_trans, dyna_harmo, tran_gene and harm_gene can be supplied in these operands. The analyses produced by the dynamic operators and which are to be supplied in the operands RESULTAT_X, RESULTAT_Y and RESULTAT_Z must be of the same type: dyna_trans, or dyna_harmo or tran_gene or harm_gene. 4.3 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM = nomcha Nom symbolique du champ que l'on souhaite extraire des calculs dynamiques linéaires réalisés au préalable par l'utilisateur et renseignés dans les opérandesRESULTAT_X, RESULTAT_Y et RESULTAT_Z. The possible names of the field are: 'DEPL', 'VITE' and 'ACCE'. Note: The various functions supplied by the user, such as the entrainment functions supplied under the keyword ENTRAINEMENT or the measured functions supplied under the keyword SIGNAL , must be of the same type as nomcha. 4.4 Operand REPERE ♦ REPERE = /'ABSOLU' /'RELATIF' This mandatory operand makes it possible to supply the type of response computed by the dynamic operators. If the reference frame is RELATIF (for a linear dynamic analysis in relative motion), then the user must supply the entrainment signal under the keyword ENTRAINEMENT (see paragraph 4.5). 4.5 Factor keyword ENTRAINEMENT The factor keyword ENTRAINEMENT makes it possible to supply the entrainment excitations which were used to carry out the various linear dynamic analyses in relative motion. Note: The various entrainment functions supplied under the keyword ENTRAINEMENT must be of the same type as nomcha ('DEPL', 'VITE' or 'ACCE') . 4.5.1 Operands DX, DY and DZ ♦ DX = entr_x This operand makes it possible to supply the unidirectional excitation (along the direction x ) used for the first dynamic analysis. ♦ DY = entr_y This operand makes it possible to supply the unidirectional excitation (along the direction y ) used for the second dynamic analysis. ◊ DZ = entr_z This operand makes it possible to supply the unidirectional excitation (along the direction z ) used for the third dynamic analysis. 4.6 Factor keywords ENTREE and SORTIE 4.6.1 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO = grno The mandatory factor keywords ENTREE and SORTIE make it possible to supply the name of a node group (grno, containing a single node) on which the extraction of the field 'DEPL' or 'VITE' or 'ACCE' is carried out. 4.7 Factor keyword SIGNAL This factor keyword (optional) makes it possible to determine the dynamic excitation (at the input) which led to the measured signals (at the output) supplied by the user under the factor keyword SIGNAL. 4.7.1 Operands MESURE_X, MESURE_Y and MESURE_Z ♦ MESURE_X = f_x This operand makes it possible to supply the signal measured along the direction x . ♦ MESURE_Y = f_y This operand makes it possible to supply the signal measured along the direction y . ◊ MESURE_Z = f_z This operand makes it possible to supply the signal measured along the direction z . Note: The signals must be of the same type as nomcha and must be discretised on one and the same list of frequencies or of times. 4.7.2 Operand TYPE_RESU ♦ TYPE_RESU = /'TEMPOREL', /'HARMONIQUE' This operand makes it possible to supply the type of results required as output of the table. 4.7.3 Operand TABLE_RESU ♦ TABLE_RESU = nom_table This operand makes it possible to supply the name of the table in which the signals computed from the measured signals will appear. The table will be composed of several columns arranged as follows: If TYPE_RESU = 'TEMPOREL': INST, FX, FY, FZ If TYPE_RESU = 'HARMONIQUE': FREQ, Re_FX, Im_FX, Re_FY,Im_FY, Re_FZ, Im_FZ

u4.54.01 Operator THER_LINEAIRE u4.54.01 Operator THER_LINEAIRE 1 Purpose Solve a linear thermal problem in the steady or evolutionary regime. The thermal loading is defined by the keyword EXCIT. The time discretisation is supplied by the list of time instants defined under the keyword LIST_INST. This evolutionary analysis can be initialised, at the first time instant, in three different ways (keyword ETAT_INIT): - by a constant temperature, - by a temperature field, defined beforehand, or extracted from a previous analysis, - by a preliminary steady analysis. The concept produced by this operator is of type evol_ther. 2 Syntax evol_ther = THER_LINEAIRE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ RESULTAT = evol_ther, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_ther / char_ther, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), ◇ TYPE_CALCUL = / "STAT", / "TRAN" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("TYPE_CALCUL", 'TRAN')) ◆ ETAT_INIT = _F( ◆ / STAT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / EVOL_THER = evol_ther, / CHAM_NO = cham_no, / VALE = float, # Si: exists("EVOL_THER") ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ INST = float, # Si: exists("INST") ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), ⟐ SCHEMA_TEMPS = _F( ◇ SCHEMA = "THETA", # Si: equal_to("SCHEMA", 'THETA') ◇ THETA = float (défaut: 0.57), ), ◆ INCREMENT = _F( # Si: exists("INST_INIT") or exists("INST_FIN") ◇ CRITERE = "RELATIF", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◆ LIST_INST = list_inst / listr8, ◇ / NUME_INST_INIT = int, / INST_INIT = float, ◇ / NUME_INST_FIN = int, / INST_FIN = float, ), ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "GCPC", / "LDLT", / "MULT_FRONT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "PETSC", #
