Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = list[int], ◇ NOM_CMP = list[text], # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "RCMK", / "SANS" (par défaut), ), ⟐ ARCHIVAGE = _F( ◆ / PAS_ARCH = int, / LIST_INST = listr8, / INST = list[float], # Si: exists("INST") or exists("LIST_INST") ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF') ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU') ◆ PRECISION = float, ◇ CHAM_EXCLU = list[text] (défaut: "('RESI_NOEU', 'RESI_RELA_NOEU')"), ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General parameters ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, The general parameters describe the model, the material field and the elementary characteristics (in particular for structural elements). MODELE is the name of the model whose elements are the subject of the thermal analysis. The data structure comes from the command AFFE_MODELE. It is always mandatory. Linear thermal problems can be treated with models using 3D, 2D, AXIS or COQUE finite elements. CHAM_MATER is the name of the material field assigned to the model. The data structure comes from the command AFFE_MATERIAU. All the main mesh cells of the model must be associated with a material. CARA_ELEM is the name of the characteristics of the shell elements assigned to the model. The data structure comes from the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM. Obviously, this keyword is optional: if the model does not contain thermal shells, it is not useful; on the other hand, if the model contains such elements, it is mandatory. 3.1 Title The keyword TITRE makes it possible to give a title to the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results. See [ref:U4.03.01 ]. 3.2 Management of verbosity The keyword INFO makes it possible to produce various intermediate printouts in the message file. Other printouts are made systematically during the non-linear analysis, independently of the value assigned to the keyword INFO: these are the printouts of the residuals in the course of the Newton iterations. Warning, the output files can become very large with INFO greater than 2. 4 Application of the loadings and of the boundary conditions The factor keyword EXCIT makes it possible to define several loadings or boundary conditions. For each occurrence of the factor keyword, one defines CHARGE, possibly multiplied by a time function FONC_MULT. The keyword CHARGE is a concept of type charge produced by AFFE_CHAR_THER. As for mechanics, it is also possible to define a load of the type “imposed degree of freedom”, here the temperature, by AFFE_CHAR_CINE. Note: For each occurrence of the factor keyword EXCIT, the various char concepts used must be built on the same model. The keyword FONC_MULT is a multiplicative coefficient which is a function of time (concept of type fonction, nappe or formule) applied to the load. Note: The concomitant use of FONC_MULT with a load containing temperature-dependent thermal loadings is forbidden. 5 Parametrisation of the analysis 5.1 Keyword TYPE_CALCUL The analysis is transient if TYPE_CALCUL = TRAN or steady if TYPE_CALCUL=’STAT’. In the case of a transient analysis, the computation of the initial state must be specified in ETAT_INIT. 5.2 Keyword INCREMENT The keyword INCREMENT makes it possible to define the analysis time instants which determine the time intervals taken in order to integrate the differential equation. The operands of the keyword INCREMENT have the same meaning as in the operator STAT_NON_LINE. Note: If the keyword INCREMENT is absent, one creates a list of time instants reduced to the single real 0 in the case of a steady analysis. 5.3 Keyword SCHEMA_TEMPS This keyword is available only in the case of a transient analysis (TYPE_CALCUL = ’TRAN’). The argument theta is the parameter theta of the theta-method applied to the transient problem. It must lie between 0 (explicit method) and 1 (fully implicit method). In the absence of the keyword, the value used is \theta =0.57 , slightly greater than \theta =0.5 corresponding to the Crank-Nicolson scheme. The effect of the choice of theta on the stability of the method is detailed in R5.02.02. 6 Restarts, archiving and management of the initial state ◇ RESULTAT = evol_ther, In the case where one wishes to continue an analysis already performed, the keyword RESULTAT indicates which object is enriched. 6.1 Definition of an initial state The keyword ETAT_INIT makes it possible to define a reference initial state in the case of a transient analysis. The initial field is assigned the order number 0 and the initial time instant takes as its value the first real of the list of time instants as defined by INCREMENT. Note: If the keyword ETAT_INIT is absent, one performs only the steady analysis at the first time instant defined under the keyword INCREMENT 6.1.1 Steady analysis If STAT = "OUI", then the initial value of the temperature field is the result of a preliminary steady analysis. This is the default mode. 6.1.2 Temperature field The keyword VALE makes it possible to define an initial value of the temperature constant over the whole structure, whereas the keyword CHAM_NO defines it by a nodal temperature field (result of the operator CREA_CHAMP) for example. One can also use the initial temperature field by extraction from an evol_ther result given by the keyword EVOL_THER. One can then give the order number NUME_ORDRE or the time instant INST of the field to be extracted from this data structure. If NUME_ORDRE or INST are not filled in, one takes the last existing archived number in evol_ther. Note: Warning, this is the order number in the data structure read on restart by the preceding keyword EVOL_THER. If this data structure was computed with a list of time instants different from that used under the factor keyword INCREMENT of the current solution, it is imperative to fill in NUME_INST_INIT under INCREMENT, the same order-number value corresponding to different physical time instants. In the case where the two lists of time instants are identical, one can dispense with filling in the same order number twice, under ETAT_INIT and under INCREMENT. The keywords PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to select the field finely from the value of the time instant given by INST. See U4.71.00. One can associate a time-instant value with this initial state by the keyword INST_ETAT_INIT. By default: - When the initial state is defined by the data of the fields, there is no associated time instant. - When the state is given by an evol_ther concept, it is the time instant in the previous analysis. 6.2 Archiving of the fields The keyword ARCHIVAGE is optional: by default, the set of fields computed for all the computed steps is archived in the resultat concept produced by the command. It is used to store certain order numbers in a resultat data structure and/or to exclude certain fields from storage. This keyword is identical to its equivalent for the operator STAT_NON_LINE. Note: In the event of the analysis stopping for lack of CPU time, the previously computed time steps are saved in the database. The command CALC_CHAMP makes it possible to compute the heat fluxes, at the integration points or at the nodes, from the nodal temperature field thus obtained by THER_LINEAIRE. 7 Settings of the linear solver The factor keyword SOLVEUR makes it possible to choose the options used by the linear solver. The syntax of this keyword, common to several commands, is described in the document U4.50.01.

u4.54.02 Operator THER_NON_LINE u4.54.02 Operator THER_NON_LINE 1 Purpose Compute the thermal response with non-linearities of constitutive behaviour and of boundary conditions. The heat equation is solved in the evolutionary regime (unless no list of time instants is supplied, in which case only the steady regime is computed). The non-linearities come either from the constitutive behaviour (material characteristics depending on the temperature), or from the boundary conditions (radiation in an infinite medium, non-linear flux, thermal source depending on the temperature). An enthalpy formulation has been chosen in order to take phase changes of the material into account more easily. The evolutionary analysis can be initialised, at the first time instant, in three different ways (factor keyword ETAT_INIT): - by a constant temperature, - by a temperature field, defined beforehand, or extracted from a previous analysis, - by a steady analysis. In order to model the hydration of concrete, the operator also makes it possible to add to the heat equation a source term which is a function of the hydration variable. This term is then given by an evolution equation in which the temperature appears. The concept produced by the operator THER_NON_LINE is of type evol_ther, as for a linear analysis by THER_LINEAIRE. 2 Syntax evol_ther = THER_NON_LINE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ & RESULTAT = evol_ther, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ⟐ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◇ RELATION = / "THER_HYDR", / "THER_NL" (par défaut), ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_ther / char_ther, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), ⟐ AFFICHAGE = _F( ◇ INFO_RESIDU = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ INFO_TEMPS = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ UNITE = unit, ◇ PAS = int, ), ◇ METHODE = / "MODELE_REDUIT", / "NEWTON" (par défaut), / "RASPEN", # Si: (equal_to("EVAL_CMP", 'FORMULE')) ◆ FORMULE = formule, # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General parameters ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, The general parameters describe the model, the material field and the elementary characteristics (in particular for structural elements). MODELE is the name of the model whose elements are the subject of the thermal analysis. The data structure comes from the command AFFE_MODELE. It is always mandatory. Linear thermal problems can be treated with models using 3D, 2D or AXIS finite elements. CHAM_MATER is the name of the material field assigned to the model. The data structure comes from the command AFFE_MATERIAU. All the main mesh cells of the model must be associated with a material. CARA_ELEM is necessary only in the case of a non-linear thermal solution with an orthotropic material (THER_NL_ORTH). It then makes it possible to transmit to the solution operator the definition of the local axes of the orthotropy reference frame in the 2D or 3D medium (command AFFE_CARA_ELEM, keyword MASSIF). 3.1 Title The keyword TITRE makes it possible to give a title which one wants to give to the result stored in temper, a data structure of type evol_ther U4.03.01. 3.2 Management of verbosity The keyword INFO makes it possible to produce various intermediate printouts in the message file. 4 Application of the loadings and of the boundary conditions The factor keyword EXCIT makes it possible to define several loadings or boundary conditions. For each occurrence of the factor keyword, one defines CHARGE, possibly multiplied by a time function FONC_MULT. The keyword CHARGE is a concept of type charge produced by AFFE_CHAR_THER. As for mechanics, it is also possible to define a load of the type “imposed degree of freedom”, here the temperature, by AFFE_CHAR_CINE. Note: For each occurrence of the factor keyword EXCIT the various char concepts used must be built on the same model. The keyword FONC_MULT is a multiplicative coefficient which is a function of time (concept of type fonction, nappe or formule) applied to the load. Note: The concomitant use of FONC_MULT with a load containing temperature-dependent thermal loadings (that is, for loadings of type ECHANGE, ECHANGE_PAROI, RAYONNEMENT, SOUR_NL or FLUNL) is forbidden. 5 Parametrisation of the analysis 5.1 Keyword TYPE_CALCUL The analysis is transient if TYPE_CALCUL = TRAN or steady if TYPE_CALCUL=’STAT’. In the case of a transient analysis, the computation of the initial state must be specified in ETAT_INIT. 5.2 Keyword INCREMENT The keyword INCREMENT makes it possible to define the analysis time instants which determine the time intervals taken in order to integrate the differential equation. The operands of the keyword INCREMENT have the same meaning as in the operator STAT_NON_LINE. Note: The list of time instants must contain at least two time instants, otherwise an error message appears. Nevertheless this requirement disappears when one performs a steady analysis (keyword STATIONNAIRE in ETAT_INIT). In this case the analysis result will contain only the initial time instant, computed under the stationarity assumption. 5.3 Keyword SCHEMA_TEMPS This keyword is available only in the case of a transient analysis (TYPE_CALCUL = ’TRAN’). The argument theta is the parameter theta of the theta-method applied to the transient problem. It must lie between 0 (explicit method) and 1 (fully implicit method). In the absence of the keyword, the value used is \theta =0.57 , slightly greater than \theta =0.5 corresponding to the Crank-Nicholson scheme. The effect of the choice of theta on the stability of the method is detailed in R5.02.02. 6 Settings of the non-linear solvers ◇ METHODE =/ "MODELE_REDUIT", / "NEWTON" (par défaut), / "NEWTON_KRYLOV", / "RASPEN", The keyword METHODE makes it possible to choose the method for solving the non-linear incremental problem. 6.1 Newton methods With METHODE='NEWTON', one uses the Newton-Raphson algorithm to solve the problem (see R5.03.01). 6.2 Reduced model With METHODE='MODELE_REDUIT', one uses a model-reduction method to perform the non-linear analysis (see R5.01.05). It is necessary to have built a reduced basis beforehand (command DEFI_BASE_REDUITE). The keywords MATRICE, PREDICTION, REAC_ITER and REAC_INCR have the same meaning and the same use as in the factor keyword NEWTON. It is necessary to supply an empirical basis in the keyword BASE_PRIMAL built on the temperatures (by means of the operator DEFI_BASE_REDUITE). This basis must have been built on the same model and the same mesh as the THER_NON_LINE analysis. Model reduction is not compatible with the following features: - The line search; - Dualised boundary conditions (AFFE_CHAR_THER; one must use AFFE_CHAR_CINE). It is possible to activate hyper-reduction, which uses a method of DEIM type, with DOMAINE_REDUIT = 'OUI'. In this case, the analysis is reduced to a restricted zone of the mesh (called the RID) and built with the help of the operator DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT. One must give the node group on which the interface is defined, by means of the keyword GROUP_NO_INTERF. 6.3 Method RASPEN The method RASPEN is based on a non-linear domain-decomposition method. It can be used only in the HPC context. It relies on 2 levels of non-linear solvers: - a local level, where a non-linear problem is solved on each subdomain, without communication with its neighbours and therefore in a parallel and asynchronous manner; - a global level, which exploits the previous local solutions in order to facilitate the solution of the problem under consideration. As for the method SNES , the parameters are set by a list of options transmitted in the form of character strings by the keyword OPTION_PETSC of the factor keyword SOLVEUR. The options which concern the local solver are prefixed by lsnes_ , whereas the options which concern the global solver are prefixed by gsnes_ . One can conveniently define these options as follows: myOptions = ( # local snes "-prefix_push lsnes_ " + "-snes_monitor -snes_linesearch_type basic -snes_rtol 1.e-8 -snes_atol 1.e-50 -snes_max_it 5 " + "-ksp_type preonly -pc_type lu -pc_factor_mat_solver_type mumps " + "-prefix_pop " # global snes + "-prefix_push gsnes_ " + "-snes_linesearch_type basic -ksp_monitor -ksp_rtol 1.e-7 -ksp_atol 1.e-50 -snes_max_it 20 " + "-prefix_pop " ) The first line expresses the fact that one is going to set the parameters of the non-linear solver local to each subdomain, called "lsnes" ("l" for local, "snes" for Scalable Nonlinear Equations Solvers). Next, one expresses that one wants to monitor the local non-linear solver, which by default is the Newton method; one specifies that the line search is not used (basic means that one uses a step of 1.) and one gives the relative and absolute convergence criteria as well as the maximum number of iterations. Next one expresses that one wishes to use the MUMPS solver to solve the linearised problems. One then does the same for the global non-linear solver, called "gsnes". For any further detail, the reader is referred to [bib2]_. Its use is reserved for advanced users. 7 Convergence settings 7.1 Convergence criterion The factor keyword CONVERGENCE makes it possible to control the convergence parameters of the analysis, either with RESI_GLOB_RELA or with RESi_GLOB_MAXI. Note: If neither of the two following operands is present, then everything proceeds as if RESI_GLOB_RELA = 1.E-6 For RESI_GLOB_MAXI= \varepsilon_{max} , the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as where {F}^{n} is the residual of iteration {n} (cf. R5.03.01 for more details). If this operand is absent, the test is not carried out. For RESI_GLOB_RELA= \varepsilon_{rel} , the algorithm continues the global iterations as long as \underset{i=1, \dots , \mathrm{nbddl}}{\max} {F}^{n} > \varepsilon_{rel} . {\max} L where L is the vector of the imposed loading. 7.2 Management of the iterations The keyword ITER_GLOB_MAXI gives the maximum number of iterations carried out in order to solve the global problem at each time instant. An excessive increase of this parameter is generally the sign of a problem in the modelling or of an inadequate time discretisation. 8 Restarts, archiving and management of the initial state ◇ RESULTAT = evol_ther, In the case where one wishes to continue an analysis already performed, the keyword RESULTAT indicates which object is enriched. 8.1 Definition of an initial state ◆ ETAT_INIT = _F( ◆ / STAT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / EVOL_THER = evol_ther, / CHAM_NO = cham_no, / VALE = float, # Si: exists("EVOL_THER") ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ INST = float, # Si: exists("INST") ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), The keyword ETAT_INIT makes it possible to define a reference initial state in the case of a transient analysis. Unlike the mechanical case, this initial state is mandatory; there is no default value. 8.1.1 Steady analysis If STAT = "OUI", then the initial value of the temperature field is then the result of a preliminary steady analysis. This is the default mode. 8.1.2 Temperature field The keyword VALE makes it possible to define an initial value of the temperature constant over the whole structure, whereas the keyword CHAM_NO defines it by a nodal temperature field (result of the operator CREA_CHAMP) for example. One can also use the initial temperature field by extraction from an evol_ther result given by the keyword EVOL_THER. One can then give the order number NUME_ORDRE or the time instant INST of the field to be extracted from this data structure. If NUME_ORDRE or INST are not filled in, one takes the last existing archived number in evol_ther. Note: Warning, this is the order number in the data structure read on restart by the preceding keyword EVOL_THER. If this data structure was computed with a list of time instants different from that used under the factor keyword INCREMENT of the current solution, it is imperative to fill in NUME_INST_INIT under INCREMENT, the same order-number value corresponding to different physical time instants. In the case where the two lists of time instants are identical, one can dispense with filling in the same order number twice, under ETAT_INIT and under INCREMENT. The keywords PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to select the field finely from the value of the time instant given by INST. See U4.71.00. 8.2 Archiving of the fields The keyword ARCHIVAGE is optional: by default, the set of fields computed for all the computed steps is archived in the resultat concept produced by the command. It is used to store certain order numbers in a resultat data structure and/or to exclude certain fields from storage. This keyword is identical to its equivalent for the operator STAT_NON_LINE. Note: In the event of the analysis stopping for lack of CPU time, the previously computed time steps are saved in the database. The command CALC_CHAMP makes it possible to compute the heat fluxes, at the integration points or at the nodes, from the nodal temperature field thus obtained by THER_LINEAIRE. 9 Settings of the linear solver The factor keyword SOLVEUR makes it possible to choose the options used by the linear solver. The syntax of this keyword, common to several commands, is described in the document U4.50.01. 10 Non-linear constitutive behaviours ⟐ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◇ RELATION = / "THER_HYDR", / "THER_NL" (par défaut), ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), The non-linear constitutive behaviours are described by the repeatable factor keyword COMPORTEMENT. The keyword GROUP_MA specifies the mesh cells on which the constitutive relation is applied. Unlike mechanics, the constitutive behaviour 'THER_NL' is necessarily applied to the whole mesh, option TOUT: 'OUI', the default option, which is in fact, in the general case, transparent for the user. There are three broad categories of non-linear constitutive behaviour: - Non-linear thermal analysis - The hydration analysis - The drying analysis (treated by the operator SECH_NON_LINE) Note: If the keyword COMPORTEMENT is absent, one performs a "standard" non-linear thermal analysis. 10.1 Non-linear thermal analysis When RELATION='THER_NL', this is the standard non-linear thermal solution. Supported modellings: - 3D continuous media: 3D - 2D continuous media: 2D and AXIS 10.2 Hydration analysis When RELATION='THER_HYDR', one solves the heat equation with an additional source term Q \dot{\xi} where Q is the heat of hydration, assumed constant. The hydration variable \xi is the solution of the non-linear evolution law, solved simultaneously with the thermal problem: \dot{\xi} = A(\xi ) \exp \left( -\frac{E}{RT} \right) One should refer to the documentation of the operator DEFI_MATERIAU for the meaning of the various parameters. At the initial time instant of the analysis, the hydration variable takes as its value the field found under the name 'HYDR_ELNO' in the evol_ther data structure defined under ETAT_INIT. By default, the initial hydration state is taken as virgin, \xi =0 . Supported modellings: - 3D continuous media: 3D - 2D continuous media: 2D and AXIS 11 Monitoring of the analysis This section groups the various tools making it possible to monitor an analysis: observation and display. 11.1 Observation The factor keyword OBSERVATION makes it possible to post-process certain fields at the nodes or at the elements on parts of the model at time instants of a list (known as the observation list), generally finer than the list of archived time instants defined in the keyword ARCHIVAGE (where one stores all the fields over the whole model). It is used essentially to save on storage. This keyword is repeatable and makes it possible to create an observation table with the same name as the result concept of THER_NON_LINE. For the description of the syntax of this factor keyword, refer to the documentation of the equivalent keyword of DYNA_NON_LINE. 11.2 Displays The factor keyword AFFICHAGE makes it possible to customise the display of the convergence table. If this keyword is not filled in, the table is built according to the various analysis options and with INFO_RESIDU='NON'. For the description of the syntax of this factor keyword, refer to the documentation of the equivalent keyword of STAT_NON_LINE.

u4.54.03 Operator THER_NON_LINE_MO u4.54.03 Operator THER_NON_LINE_MO 1 Purpose Compute the non-linear steady thermal response with a moving loading. This operator makes it possible to solve the steady heat equation in a moving reference frame attached to a loading and travelling in a given direction and at a given velocity R5.02.04. The non-linearities of the problem come both from the material characteristics, which depend on the temperature, and from boundary conditions of radiation type. Problems of this type can be treated with models using plane, axisymmetric and three-dimensional structural finite elements. The concept produced by this operator is of type evol_ther, as for an analysis by THER_LINEAIRE U4.54.01 or THER_NON_LINE U4.54.02, but it contains only a single order number, since one performs a steady analysis. 2 Syntax evol_ther = THER_NON_LINE_MO( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_ther, ), ◇ ETAT_INIT = _F( ◇ EVOL_THER = evol_ther, ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ), ⟐ CONVERGENCE = _F( ◇ CRIT_TEMP_RELA = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CRIT_ENTH_RELA = float (défaut: 0.01), ◇ ITER_GLOB_MAXI = int (défaut: 10), ), ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "MULT_FRONT", / "LDLT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "GCPC", / "PETSC", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = int, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE= mo Name of the model whose elements are the subject of the thermal analysis. 3.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER= chmat Name of the material field assigned to the model. 3.3 Keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT= Factor keyword which makes it possible to define several loadings. For each occurrence of the factor keyword, one defines a load which is constant in time. 3.3.1 Operand CHARGE ♦ CHARGE = char Concept of type charge produced by AFFE_CHAR_THER or by AFFE_CHAR_THER_F U4.44.02. Important notes: For each occurrence of the factor keyword EXCIT the various concepts char used must be built on the same model mo. Furthermore, the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER or AFFE_CHAR_THER_F must necessarily fill in, under the factor keyword CONVECTION, a concept of type cham_no_DEPL_R defining the displacement velocity of the domain and produced by CREA_CHAMP. Care must be taken to define boundary conditions consistent with the travel of the part (or of the loading, depending on the chosen reference frame) and the stationarity assumption: If the solid is animated by a uniform translational motion at constant velocity, it is equivalent to consider the computed temperature field: - as a snapshot at a given time instant, - or as a time sequence of the temperature map in a section of fixed abscissa, orthogonal to the direction of travel. Thus, downstream in space (early in time), the boundary condition on the edge of the part must impose the temperature of the part before the moving loading arrives. Upstream in space (or late in time), a zero heat flux (adiabaticity) guarantees the stationarity assumption. 3.4 Keyword ETAT_INIT ◊ ETAT_INIT Makes it possible to define the initial field from which the analysis in the moving reference frame under the stationarity condition is performed. 3.4.1 Operand EVOL_THER ♦ EVOL_THER = temp Name of the data structure of type evol_ther from which is extracted the temperature field from which the solution of the problem is computed. 3.4.2 Operand NUME_ORDRE ◊ NUME_ORDRE = / nuini_evol / 0 [DEFAUT] Order number of the field to be extracted from this data structure. Note: For this type of analysis, there is no initial condition to define (it is defined by a boundary condition on an edge of the domain defined by the model). Nevertheless, one can still perform the steady analysis starting from a temperature field already computed as the solution of the problem for only part of the load. This can be useful in the case where the application of the whole loading makes convergence difficult. One can then chain several solutions with a loading which evolves progressively and take as the first iterate of a current analysis the solution of the previous analysis. Concretely, one then uses the keyword ETAT_INIT to define the temperature field with which one wants to initialise the current analysis. 3.5 Keyword CONVERGENCE ◊ CONVERGENCE= Makes it possible to define the values associated with the convergence criteria: 3.5.1 Operand CRIT_TEMP_RELA ◊ CRIT_TEMP_RELA = / 1.e-3 / testr The algorithm continues the iterations as long as the relative variation of the iterate is greater than testr. {(\underset{i=1,\mathrm{...},\mathrm{nb}\mathrm{ddl}}{\Sigma}{({T}_{i}^{n}-{T}_{i}^{n-1})}^{2})}^{1/2}/{(\underset{i=1,\mathrm{...},\mathrm{nb}\mathrm{ddl}}{\Sigma}{({T}_{i}^{n})}^{2})}^{1/2}>\mathrm{testr} where {T}_{i}^{n} denotes the value of the temperature at node i for the n-th iteration. 3.5.2 Operand CRIT_ENTH_RELA ◊ CRIT_ENTH_RELA = / 1.e-2 / testl The algorithm continues the iterations as long as the relative variation of the iterate is greater than testl. {(\underset{i=1,\mathrm{...},N}{\Sigma}{({\beta}_{i}^{n}-{\beta}_{i}^{n-1})}^{2})}^{1/2}/{(\underset{i=1,\mathrm{...},N}{\Sigma}{({\beta}_{i}^{n})}^{2})}^{1/2}>\mathrm{test1} where {\beta}_{i}^{n} denotes the value of the enthalpy at the n-th iteration at the i-th Gauss point. 3.5.3 Operand ITER_GLOB_MAXI ◊ ITER_GLOB_MAXI = / 10 / iterl The algorithm continues the external iterations as long as the number of external iterations is less than iterl. 3.6 Keyword SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR = This factor keyword is optional: it makes it possible to choose another solver for the solution of the system. This operand is common to the whole set of global commands U4.50.01. 3.7 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title which one wants to give to the result stored in temp, a data structure of type evol_ther U4.03.01. 4 Modelling Non-linear thermal problems in a moving reference frame and under the stationarity condition can be treated with models using the 3D or 2D plane finite elements described in the documents U3.23.01 and U3.24.01. 5 Examples The main commands used to perform a non-linear thermal analysis in a moving reference frame and under the stationarity condition are presented below. conduc = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = 'TEMP', VALE = ... ) enthal = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = 'TEMP', VALE = ... ) mat = DEFI_MATERIAU ( THER_NL= _F( LAMBDA = conduc, BETA = enthal ),) ... chavi = CREA_CHAMP ( MAILLAGE = mail, TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', AFFE = _F( TOUT = 'OUI', NOM_CMP = ('DX','DY'), VALE_R = (1.0 , 0.0) ) char = AFFE_CHAR_THER ( MODELE = model, FLUX_REP =_F( GROUP_MA = sou, FLUN = 5.E6 ), CONVECTION=_F( VITESSE = chavi ) ) tempe = THER_NON_LINE_MO ( MODELE = model, CHAM_MATER = chmat, EXCIT =_F(CHARGE = char ), ) ...

u4.54.04 Command CALC_THER_MULT u4.54.04 Command CALC_THER_MULT 1 Purpose The role of the command is to compute the thermal responses of various load cases and to store them in one and the same result data structure. These loadings may be any thermal loadings (defined with the commands AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F) or unit shocks for which an automatic setup is used. The thermal boundary conditions and the material characteristics are invariant for the whole set of load cases called. Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = list[int], ◇ NOM_CMP = list[text], # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "RCMK", / "SANS" (par défaut), ), ⟐ NEWTON = _F( ◇ REAC_ITER = int (défaut: 0), ◇ REAC_INCR = int (défaut: 1), ◇ PREDICTION = "TANGENTE", ◇ MATRICE = "TANGENTE", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM MODELE is the name of the model whose elements are the subject of the thermal analysis. CHAM_MATER is the name of the material field assigned to the model given in MODELE. CARA_ELEM contains additional characteristics for the elements. This keyword is optional. 3.2 Operand CHAR_THER_GLOBAL Concept of type charge produced by the commands AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_F(u4.44.02). This keyword makes it possible to define the thermal loadings which are common to all the load cases (CAS_CHARGE) defined by the user. 3.3 Operand PARM_THETA The keyword PARM_THETA has the same meaning as in the documentation of THER_NON_LINE and applies to all the computed load cases. In the absence of the keyword, the value used is 1 (fully implicit method) 3.4 Operand CAS_CHARGE This factor keyword makes it possible to define the various load cases by choosing between the application of thermal loadings defined beforehand, or else by automatically generating a loading of unit thermal-shock type. Note: When the analysis of a load case of "unit shock" type is performed and other load cases of this type are also defined within the same command CALC_THER_MULT, exchange conditions with a temperature of 0°C are also applied on the mesh-cell groups given in the other occurrences of this type of load case. Function describing a shock of DUREE_CHOC d 3.4.1 Keyword NOM_CAS Character string used as the access variable to the result data structure. 3.4.2 Keyword EXCIT Keyword defining the thermal loading to be applied for the load case under consideration. It may be defined by the commands AFFE_CHAR_THER and AFFE_CHAR_THER_F. This factor keyword makes it possible to apply exchange conditions on a mesh-cell group with an external temperature whose value varies linearly from 0 to 1 over a time given by the user, as described in the u4.54.04-fig-choc . The applied loading uses the keyword ECHANGE defined in the documentation AFFE_CHAR_THER. 3.4.3 Keyword COEF_H Defines the exchange coefficient. 3.4.4 Keyword GROUP_MA List of the mesh cells defining the exchange surface subjected to the shock, for the assignment of the thermal loading. 3.4.5 Keyword DUREE_CHOC Value defining the duration of the applied unit shock, that is the time for the external temperature to vary linearly from 0 to 1. The value taken by default is 1\mathrm{e}{-6} . 3.4.6 Keyword LIST_INST List of time instants used for the analysis of the load case under consideration. Note: Within one and the same CAS_CHARGE , there cannot be both the keyword COEF_H and EXCIT . Moreover, the joint presence of the keywords COEF_H , GROUP_MA and DUREE_CHOC is mandatory if the keyword EXCIT is not present. 3.5 Operands SOLVEUR, CONVERGENCE and NEWTON These operands are the analysis options SOLVEUR, CONVERGENCE and NEWTON used in THER_NON_LINE.

u4.55.01 Operator FACTORISER u4.55.01 Operator FACTORISER 1 Purpose Factorise an assembled matrix or build a preconditioning matrix . The matrix produced by this operator is supplied to the operator RESOUDRE[U4.55.02] in order to solve the linear systems. This operator makes it possible: 1. Either to factorise the assembled matrix (into a product of two triangular matrices) for the direct methods, 2. Or to build a preconditioning matrix for the iterative methods, with the aim of accelerating convergence during the solution. This command is a mandatory preliminary step before calling the solution command RESOUDRE. Produces (or enriches) a data structure of type matr_asse. 2 Syntax / matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r = FACTORISER( ◇ reuse = , ◆ MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r, ◇ METHODE = / "GCPC", / "LDLT", / "MULT_FRONT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "PETSC", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ / BLOC_DEBUT = int, / DDL_DEBUT = int, ◇ / BLOC_FIN = int, / DDL_FIN = int, # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "METIS", / "PARMETIS", / "PORD", / "PTSCOTCH", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "NONSYM", / "SYMDEF", / "SYMGEN", ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "LAGR2" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "EVAL", / "IN_CORE" (par défaut), / "OUT_OF_CORE", ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FR", / "FR+", / "LR", / "LR+", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'GCPC') or equal_to("METHODE", 'PETSC') ◇ PRE_COND = / "JACOBI", / "LDLT_DP", / "LDLT_INC" (par défaut), / "LDLT_SP", / "SOR", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int (défaut: 0), ◇ REMPLISSAGE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "IN_CORE", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ RENUM = / "METIS", / "PARMETIS", / "SANS" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'JACOBI') or equal_to("PRE_COND", 'SOR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'PETSC') ◇ OPTION_PETSC = text (défaut: ""), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands The choice of the solution method is made beforehand in the command NUME_DDL (keyword METHODE). Five methods are possible: 'MULT_FRONT', 'MUMPS', 'GCPC', 'PETSC' and 'LDLT'. 3.1 Keyword reuse = matas For the sake of simplifying the programming and also in order to save disk space, the “in-place” factorisation of the matrix (use of reuse) is in general mandatory. The exception is the pair ('GCPC', 'LDLT_INC'). In this case, it is forbidden to use reuse. 3.2 Operand MATR_ASSE ♦ MATR_ASSE= mat Name of the assembled matrix to be factorised or to be preconditioned, depending on the method. For the methods 'LDLT', 'MULT_FRONT' and 'MUMPS', this matrix may be real or complex, symmetric or not. On the other hand, for the methods 'GCPC' and 'PETSC', this matrix must be real. For 'GCPC', the matrix must also be symmetric. 3.3 Operands STOP_SINGULIER, NPREC, TYPE_RESOL , PCENT_PIVOT, PRETRAITEMENTS, GESTION_MEMOIRE, ACCELERATION, LOW_RANK_SEUIL, PRE_COND, NIVE_REMPLISSAGE, REMPLISSAGE, RENUM, REAC_PRECOND and ELIM_LAGR These keywords are described in U4.50.01. 3.4 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre Title which one wants to give to the result U4.02.01. 3.5 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= 1: no printout 3.6 Partial factorisation (LDLT method) For the method 'LDLT', the operator makes it possible to factorise the matrix only partially. This possibility makes it possible to factorise the matrix in several goes (several jobs), or even to modify on the fly the last rows of this factorised matrix. Today, this feature is of little interest except for certain methods (known as discrete) of frictional contact, where one has, deliberately, placed in the last rows of the matrix the terms concerning the nodes liable to be in contact. Thus, as the pairing iterations proceed, the relations between these nodes changing, one deletes and then recomputes only these last contributions of the factorised matrix. It is a typical example where the clever use of a rather crude algorithm can bring major gains (in time). ◊ / BLOC_DEBUT= bd bd: partial factorisation from the bd-th block inclusive. / DDL_DEBUT= dd dd: partial factorisation from the dd-th equation inclusive (in the internal numbering established by the operator NUME_DDL U4.61.11). ◊ / BLOC_FIN= bf bf: partial factorisation up to the bf-th block inclusive. / DDL_FIN= df df: partial factorisation up to the df-th equation inclusive (in the internal numbering established by the operator NUME_DDL U4.61.11). BLOC_DEBUT and DDL_DEBUT - in the absence of the keywords BLOC_DEBUT and DDL_DEBUT, the matrix will be factorised starting from its first row. - if the argument bd of the keyword BLOC_DEBUT is negative or zero, the matrix will be factorised starting from the first block. Otherwise, one performs a partial factorisation starting from the bd-th block inclusive. - if the argument dd of the keyword DDL_DEBUT is negative or zero, the matrix will be factorised starting from the first equation. Otherwise, one performs a partial factorisation starting from the dd-th equation inclusive. 4 Examples See the examples in the documentation of the command RESOUDRE U4.55.02.

u4.55.02 Operator RESOUDRE u4.55.02 Operator RESOUDRE 1 Purpose Solve a system of linear equations (direct or iterative method) The solution methods implemented in Code_Aster and usable by this command are: 1. the MULT_FRONT method (direct method), 2. the LDLT method (direct method), 3. the MUMPS method (direct method), 4. the GCPC method (iterative method), 5. the PETSC method (iterative method). The effective choice of the method is made through the command FACTORISER U4.55.01. For the direct methods, the matrix must have been factorised beforehand by the command FACTORISER U4.55.01. In the case of the iterative methods with preconditioning, the preconditioning matrix is also supplied by the operator FACTORISER U4.55.01. The operator allows complex solutions for the "direct" methods (not for the iterative methods). Produces a data structure of type cham_no. 2 Syntax cham_no = RESOUDRE( ◇ reuse = , ◆ MATR = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r, ◆ CHAM_NO = cham_no, ◇ CHAM_CINE = cham_no, ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", / "SANS", ◇ NMAX_ITER = int (défaut: 0), ◇ MATR_PREC = matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_r, ◇ ALGORITHME = / "CG", / "CR", / "FGMRES" (par défaut), / "GCR", / "GMRES", ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General points This command makes it possible to solve: - by a direct method, the linear system \mathrm{AX}=B , where A is a matrix previously “factorised” by the command FACTORISER [U4.51.01.], - by an iterative method (GCPC or PETSC), the linear system {P}^{-1}\mathrm{AX}={P}^{-1}B , where {P}^{-1} is a preconditioning matrix determined by the command FACTORISER U4.51.01 and A the initial assembled matrix. The solution is possible for Dirichlet boundary conditions (kinematic boundary conditions), whether dualised or eliminated U2.01.02. In the latter case, if the loading \mathrm{X}={\mathrm{X}}_{0} on the “edge” {\Gamma}_{0} is applied with a kinematic load (operator AFFE_CHAR_CINE U4.44.03) taken into account in the assembled matrix (operator ASSE_MATRICE U4.61.22), the “value” of this loading ({X}_{0}) , computed by the operator CALC_CHAR_CINE U4.61.03, must be supplied by the keyword CHAM_CINE. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand MATR ♦ MATR = A, Name of the matrix of the system to be solved: - For the direct methods, one supplies to MATR the concept modified by the operator FACTORISER; this matrix may be real or complex, symmetric or not. - For the iterative methods, one supplies to MATR the initial matrix. The preconditioning matrix is to be supplied with the keyword MATR_PREC. 4.2 Operand CHAM_NO ♦ CHAM_NO = B, Name of the right-hand side vector (in general obtained by the command ASSE_VECTEUR). 4.3 Operand CHAM_CINE ◊ CHAM_CINE = vcine, Name of the vector representing the “value” of the eliminated Dirichlet boundary conditions (that is, applied with one of the commands AFFE_CHAR_CINE or AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F). This cham_no comes from the execution of the operator CALC_CHAR_CINE on the list of char_cine (kinematic loadings) associated with the assembled matrix A U2.01.02. 4.4 Operand ALGORITHME ◊ ALGORITHME = / 'GMRES' [DEFAUT] / 'CG' / 'CR' / 'GCR' Ce mot clé sert à choisir l'algorithme de la méthode itérative PETSC. Les différents algorithmes disponibles sont documentés dans le mot-clé SOLVEUR[U4.50.01]. 4.5 Operand MATR_PREC ◊ MATR_PREC = precond Preconditioning matrix, obtained by the operator FACTORISER U4.55.01. Preconditioning is necessary in the iterative methods in order to obtain good convergence with a minimum of iterations. With the GCPC method, the preconditioning matrix is a matrix distinct from the matrix of the problem (keyword MATR). On the other hand, with the PETSC method, one uses the same matrix for MATR_PREC and MATR, which means that the command FACTORISER must be done “in place” (with the keyword reuse). See the example below. 4.6 Operand RESI_RELA ◊ RESI_RELA = / 1.e-6, [DEFAUT] / eps , [R] This keyword is described in U4.50.01 For the iterative methods GCPC and PETSC, this is the convergence criterion of the algorithm. For the MUMPS method, this keyword makes it possible to check the quality of the solution. 4.7 Operand NMAX_ITER ◊ NMAX_ITER = niter Maximum number of iterations of the iterative algorithm. If niter = 0 then the algorithm chooses a default number of iterations. 4.8 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titr , Title which one wants to give to the result produced U4.03.01. 4.9 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = 1: no printout. 2: printouts 5 Examples 5.1 Solution by the direct method MULT_FRONT - Building of the assembled matrix and of the right-hand side: The elementary terms KEL, FEL have been computed beforehand. NU =NUME_DDL( MATR_RIGI=KEL ) K =ASSE_MATRICE( MATR_ELEM=KEL, NUME_DDL=NU, ) F =ASSE_VECTEUR( MATR_ELEM=FEL, NUME_DDL=NU, ) - Factorisation: K =FACTORISER( reuse=K, MATR_ASSE=K, METHODE='MULT_FRONT',) - Solution: U =RESOUDRE( MATR=K, CHAM_NO=F,) - for the use of kinematic loads (with elimination of the imposed degrees of freedom), see the example given in the command AFFE_CHAR_CINE U4.44.03. 5.2 Solution by the MUMPS method NU = NUME_DDL( MATR_RIGI= KEL) K = ASSE_MATRICE ( MATR_ELEM= KEL, NUME_DDL= NU) F = ASSE_VECTEUR ( VECT_ELEM= FEL, NUME_DDL= NU ) K = FACTORISER ( reuse= K, MATR_ASSE= K, METHODE= 'MUMPS' ) dep = RESOUDRE ( CHAM_NO = F , MATR= K) 5.3 Solution by the preconditioned conjugate gradient method NU = NUME_DDL( MATR_RIGI= KEL) K = ASSE_MATRICE ( MATR_ELEM= KEL, NUME_DDL= NU ) F = ASSE_VECTEUR ( VECT_ELEM= FEL, NUME_DDL= NU ) KPREC = FACTORISER ( MATR_ASSE= K, METHODE= 'GCPC', PRE_COND='LDLT_INC' ) dep = RESOUDRE ( CHAM_NO = F , MATR= K, MATR_PREC= KPREC, NMAX_ITER= 1000 , RESI_RELA= 1e-07 ) 5.4 Solution by the PETSC method NU = NUME_DDL( MATR_RIGI= KEL) K = ASSE_MATRICE ( MATR_ELEM= KEL, NUME_DDL= NU ) F = ASSE_VECTEUR ( VECT_ELEM= FEL, NUME_DDL= NU ) K = FACTORISER ( reuse=K, MATR_ASSE= K, METHODE= 'PETSC') dep = RESOUDRE ( CHAM_NO = F , MATR= K, MATR_PREC= K, ALGORITHME='GMRES', NMAX_ITER= 1000 , RESI_RELA= 1e-07)

u4.55.03 Operator ELIM_LAGR u4.55.03 Operator ELIM_LAGR 1 Purpose Remove the Lagrange equations from a matrix which contains them. This command is experimental. It is intended above all to produce matrices “without Lagrange” for the modal analysis operator (CALC_MODES). Notes: - In order to eliminate the Lagrange equations, one is led to eliminate certain physical degrees of freedom (one eliminates one physical degree of freedom for each linear relation if the relations are not redundant). - If one performs a modal analysis with “reduced” matrices, the computed modes must be restored onto the original degrees of freedom by means of the command REST_GENE_PHYS. Produces a data structure of type matr_asse_elim_r, usable only in CALC_MODES. 2 Syntax matr_asse_elim_r = ELIM_LAGR( ◆ MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_RIGI = K1, Name of the assembled stiffness matrix (with linear relations to be eliminated) If the keyword MATR_ASSE is not used, it is the matrix K1 which one “reduces” in order to create the result matrix (M2). 3.2 Operand MATR_ASSE ◊ MATR_ASSE = M1, Name of the assembled mass, damping, … matrix (not stiffness) which one wants to reduce. If this keyword is used, it is the matrix M1 which one “reduces” in order to create the result matrix (M2). 3.3 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titr , Title which one wants to give to the result produced U4.03.01. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = 1: no printout. 2: printouts 4 Analysis on several processors When one uses several processors, the data of the model must be replicated on all the processors taking part in the analysis, by using the keyword DISTRIBUTION of the command AFFE_MODELE MODEL=AFFE_MODELE(… DISTRIBUTION=_F(METHODE='CENTRALISE')) The analysis can then be performed on several processors. Warning: all the processors performing the same operations, there is no computational gain for the step of elimination of the Lagrange multipliers. The interest is then to perform a modal analysis on several processors. 5 Example K1 = ASSE_MATRICE(NUME_DDL=NU, MATR_ELEM=KEL,) M1 = ASSE_MATRICE(NUME_DDL=NU, MATR_ELEM=MEL,) # 1. calcul avec les matrices complètes : #------------------------------------------------------- mode1 = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=K1, MATR_MASS=M1, OPTION='BANDE', CALC_FREQ=_F( FREQ=(-2, 30),) ) # 2. calcul avec les matrices réduites par ELIM_LAGR : #------------------------------------------------------- K2=ELIM_LAGR(MATR_RIGI=K1, ) M2=ELIM_LAGR(MATR_RIGI=K1, MATR_ASSE=M1) mode2 = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=K2, MATR_MASS=M2, OPTION='BANDE', CALC_FREQ=_F( FREQ=(-2, 30),) ) mode3 = REST_GENE_PHYS(RESU_GENE=mode2)

u4.56.01 Operator SECH_NON_LINE u4.56.01 Operator SECH_NON_LINE 1 Purpose This operator makes it possible to solve (non-linear) drying problems by solving the heat equation in which the water concentration C is treated as a temperature. The thermal conductivity is in this case the diffusion coefficient, non-linear in C and a function, possibly, of a temperature computed beforehand and supplied as a command variable. The analysis can be initialised at the first time instant (factor keyword ETAT_INIT): - by a constant water concentration, - by a water-concentration field, defined beforehand, or extracted from a previous analysis, - by a steady analysis. The concept produced by the operator SECH_NON_LINE is of type evol_sech. This operator broadly shares the syntax of the operator THER_NON_LINE. 2 Syntax evol_sech = SECH_NON_LINE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ RESULTAT = evol_sech, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◆ RELATION = / "SECH_BAZANT", / "SECH_GRANGER", / "SECH_MENSI", / "SECH_NAPPE", / "SECH_RFT", ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_ther / char_ther, ◇ FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), ⟐ AFFICHAGE = _F( ◇ INFO_RESIDU = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ INFO_TEMPS = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ UNITE = unit, ◇ PAS = int, ), ◇ METHODE = "NEWTON", # Si: (equal_to("EVAL_CMP", 'FORMULE')) ◆ FORMULE = formule, # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General parameters ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ INFO = / 1, / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, The general parameters describe the model and the material field. 3.1 Model The keyword MODELE makes it possible to declare the model of the analysis, coming from the command AFFE_MODELE which assigns modellings to elements of the mesh. The only modellings allowed in SECH_NON_LINE are 3D_SECH, 3D_SECH_DIAG, AXIS_SECH and AXIS_SECH_DIAG. 3.2 Material field The keyword CHAM_MATER makes it possible to declare the name of the material field assigned to the model. The data structure comes from the command AFFE_MATERIAU. All the main mesh cells of the model must be associated with a material. 3.3 Title The keyword TITRE makes it possible to give a title which one wants to give to the result, a data structure of type evol_sech U4.03.01. 3.4 Management of verbosity The keyword INFO makes it possible to produce various intermediate printouts in the message file. 4 Application of the loadings and of the boundary conditions The factor keyword EXCIT makes it possible to define several loadings or boundary conditions. For each occurrence of the factor keyword, one defines CHARGE, possibly multiplied by a time function FONC_MULT. The keyword CHARGE is a concept of type charge produced by AFFE_CHAR_SECH. Note: For each occurrence of the factor keyword EXCIT the various char concepts used must be built on the same model. The keyword FONC_MULT is a multiplicative coefficient which is a function of time (concept of type fonction, nappe or formule) applied to the load. Note: The concomitant use of FONC_MULT with a load containing temperature-dependent loadings (that is, for the loading of type FLUX_NL) is forbidden. 5 Non-linear constitutive behaviours ◆ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◆ RELATION = / "SECH_BAZANT", / "SECH_GRANGER", / "SECH_MENSI", / "SECH_NAPPE", / "SECH_RFT", ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ), The drying constitutive behaviours are described by the repeatable and mandatory factor keyword COMPORTEMENT. The keyword GROUP_MA specifies the mesh cells on which the constitutive relation is applied. In a manner analogous to mechanics, one can use several different drying laws, applied to complementary mesh-cell groups. This factor keyword makes it possible to choose one of the drying models, defined by the expression of the diffusion coefficient. 5.1 Solution of the problem and description of the diffusion models The solution of drying is characterised by: \frac{\partial C}{\partial t} - Div \left( D(C,T) \vector{\nabla} C \right) = 0 This is the non-linear heat equation in which the drying variable C plays the role of the temperature. The choice of the constitutive relation makes it possible to define the diffusion coefficient D(C,T) according to various forms usual in the literature. In the general case, drying is solved after a preliminary thermal analysis (uncoupled but chained thermal/drying analysis). The temperature field, appearing as an auxiliary variable, is necessary in order to compute the diffusion coefficient of certain laws. The temperature is therefore an input datum of the drying analysis, which must necessarily be given as a command variable for the laws 'SECH_GRANGER', 'SECH_NAPPE' and 'SECH_RFT', in AFFE_MATERIAU. The thermal data given in AFFE_MATERIAU may be fields or, as is most often the case, results obtained by an execution of a thermal operator, linear or not. 5.1.1 Granger model For RELATION='SECH_GRANGER', the Granger formulation of the diffusion coefficient is given by the expression: D(C,T) = A \exp( BC ) \frac{T}{{T}_{0}} \, \exp \left( \frac{{Q}_{s}}{R}\, \left(\frac{1}{T}-\frac{1}{{T}_{0}} \right) \right) One should refer to the documentation of the operator DEFI_MATERIAU for the meaning of the various parameters. In the case of the use of the law SECH_GRANGER, it is necessary to make sure of the consistency between the material used and the constitutive law: that is, that the keyword SECH_GRANGER has indeed been filled in in DEFI_MATERIAU for the material used. 5.1.2 Mensi model For RELATION='SECH_MENSI', one applies the solution of drying characterised by the Mensi law. In the case of the use of this law SECH_MENSI, it is necessary to make sure of the consistency between the material used and the constitutive law: that is, that the keyword SECH_MENSI has indeed been filled in in DEFI_MATERIAU for the material used. 5.1.3 Bazant model For RELATION='SECH_BAZANT', one applies the solution of drying characterised by the Bazant law. In the case of the use of this law SECH_BAZANT, it is necessary to make sure of the consistency between the material used and the constitutive law: that is, that the keyword SECH_BAZANT has indeed been filled in in DEFI_MATERIAU for the material used. 5.1.4 General model For RELATION='SECH_NAPPE', one applies the solution of drying with a diffusion coefficient defined by a nappe defined by the command DEFI_NAPPE. In the case of the use of this law, it is necessary to make sure of the consistency between the material used and the constitutive law: that is, that the keyword SECH_NAPPE has indeed been filled in in DEFI_MATERIAU for the material used. 5.1.5 RFT model For RELATION='SECH_RFT', one applies the solution of drying characterised by the RFT law (RICHARD_FICK_TEMPERATURE). The expression of the diffusion coefficient of this law is presented in [R7.01.12]. In the case of the use of this law SECH_RFT, it is necessary to make sure of the consistency between the material used and the constitutive law: the keywords SECH_RFT and BETON_DESORP must be filled in in DEFI_MATERIAU for the material used. 6 Restarts, archiving and management of the initial state ◇ RESULTAT = evol_sech, In the case where one wishes to continue an analysis already performed, the keyword RESULTAT indicates which object is enriched. 6.1 Definition of an initial state ◆ ETAT_INIT = _F( ◆ / STAT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / EVOL_SECH = evol_sech, / CHAM_NO = cham_no, / VALE = float, # Si: exists("EVOL_SECH") ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ INST = float, # Si: exists("INST") ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), The keyword ETAT_INIT makes it possible to define a reference initial state in the case of a transient analysis. Unlike the mechanical case, this initial state is mandatory; there is no default value. 6.1.1 Steady analysis If STAT = "OUI", then the initial value of the water-concentration field is then the result of a preliminary steady analysis. This is the default mode. 6.1.2 Water-concentration or drying field The keyword VALE makes it possible to define an initial value of the water concentration constant over the whole structure, whereas the keyword CHAM_NO defines it by a nodal field (result of the operator CREA_CHAMP) for example. One can also use the initial water-concentration field by extraction from an evol_sech result given by the keyword EVOL_SECH. One can then give the order number NUME_ORDRE or the time instant INST of the field to be extracted from this data structure. If NUME_ORDRE or INST are not filled in, one takes the last existing archived number in the evol_sech object. Note: Warning, this is the order number in the data structure read on restart by the preceding keyword EVOL_SECH. If this data structure was computed with a list of time instants different from that used under the factor keyword INCREMENT of the current solution, it is imperative to fill in NUME_INST_INIT under INCREMENT, the same order-number value corresponding to different physical time instants. In the case where the two lists of time instants are identical, one can dispense with filling in the same order number twice, under ETAT_INIT and under INCREMENT. The keywords PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to select the field finely from the value of the time instant given by INST. See U4.71.00. 6.2 Archiving of the fields The keyword ARCHIVAGE is optional: by default, the set of fields computed for all the computed steps is archived in the resultat concept produced by the command. It is used to store certain order numbers in a resultat data structure and/or to exclude certain fields from storage. This keyword is identical to its equivalent for the operator STAT_NON_LINE. Note: In the event of the analysis stopping for lack of CPU time, the previously computed time steps are saved in the database. The command CALC_CHAMP makes it possible to compute the fluxes, at the integration points or at the nodes, from the nodal water-concentration field thus obtained by SECH_NON_LINE. 7 Parameters in common with THER_NON_LINE The following parameters are identical to those of the operator THER_NON_LINE. 7.1 Parametrisation of the analysis See u4.54.02-para-calc For the moment, the value "STAT" of the keyword TYPE_CALCUL is not available in SECH_NON_LINE. 7.2 Convergence settings See u4.54.02-reglage-conv 7.3 Settings of the linear solver See u4.54.02-reglage-solv 7.4 Monitoring of the analysis See u4.54.02-monitoring
