The constitutive relation of the material must be ELAS_FLU. 3.2 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM ♦ MODELE= mo This operand is used to indicate the elements for which the elementary analyses must be performed: one recalls that the finite elements are for the most part defined in the model. There are two exceptions: 1. The elements of dualisation of the DIRICHLET conditions, that is the elements making it possible to impose conditions on the displacement degrees of freedom in mechanics, the temperature degrees of freedom in thermal analysis and the pressure degrees of freedom in acoustics. 2. The elements of nodal loading. These elements are defined in the concepts of type char_meca, char_ther or char_acou. One must therefore supply the argument l_char for the computation of the elementary stiffness matrices: RIGI_MECA, RIGI_THER, RIGI_ACOU, RIGI_MECA_HYST. ◊ CHAM_MATER= chmat Name of the material field in which the material characteristics of the elements are defined. This argument is almost always necessary . In practice, one can do without it: - for the discrete elements whose elementary matrices are defined in the concept cara_elem. See AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, - for the computation of the stiffnesses due to the dualisation of the boundary conditions. ◊ INST= tps The argument tps is used when the material characteristics or the loadings depend on time. A fairly frequent case is that of a mechanical material depending on the temperature which itself depends on time. ◊ CARA_ELEM= carac The elementary characteristics carac are necessary if there exist in the model beam or shell elements or discrete elements, or if an anisotropy reference frame has been defined on solid elements (keyword MASSIF of the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM). 3.3 Operand CHARGE ◊ CHARGE = char This operand has several distinct functions: 1. Make possible the computation of the elementary stiffness matrices corresponding to the dualisation of certain Dirichlet boundary conditions, 2. For the option 'ONDE_FLUI': give the value of the pressure of the incident wave, 3. For the option 'RIGI_ROTA': give the value of the rotation imposed on the model. 3.4 Operand MODE_FOURIER ◊ MODE_FOURIER= / nh / 0 [DEFAUT] Positive or zero integer indicating the Fourier harmonic on which one computes the elementary matrices. 3.5 Operand CALC_ELEM_MODELE ◊ CALC_ELEM_MODELE= / 'OUI' [DEFAUT] / 'NON' This operand makes it possible to compute the elementary stiffness matrix associated only with the macro-elements of the model ('NON'). By default, the matrix is computed on the whole of the model ('OUI'). 3.6 Operand GROUP_MA ◊ GROUP_MA = lgma, This operand makes it possible to compute the elementary matrices only on the mesh cells of the groups lgma. The operand is allowed for the gyroscopy options, RIGI_MECA, RIGI_MECA_HYST, AMOR_MECA, MASS_MECA, IMPE_MECA, MASS_MECA_DIAG and MASS_FLUI_STRU. 3.7 Operand SIEF_ELGA (option 'RIGI_GEOM') ♦ SIEF_ELGA= sig The stress field sig given for the computation of the option 'RIGI_GEOM' must in principle have been computed with the option 'SIEF_ELGA' (stress field at the Gauss points of the elements) (cf. command CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04). The theory of linear buckling indeed assumes a theory of small elastic displacements. 3.8 Operands RIGI_MECA and MASS_MECA (options 'AMOR_MECA' and 'RIGI_MECA_HYST') ♦ RIGI_MECA= Real part of the elementary stiffness matrices ('RIGI_MECA') necessary for the computation of the matrices: - of damping ('AMOR_MECA') - of hysteretic stiffness by global hysteretic damping ('RIGI_MECA_HYST'), see "User's guide to damping and hysteretic stiffness" U2.06.03. - of complex stiffness for viscoelastic materials; the option 'RIGI_MECA_HYST' computes the imaginary part of the elementary stiffness matrix and assembles it with the real part passed as an argument of the option. ◊ MASS_MECA= Elementary mass matrices ('MASS_MECA' or 'MASS_MECA_DIAG') necessary for the computation of the damping matrices ('AMOR_MECA'). Note : For the option 'RIGI_MECA_HYST', the result of the analysis will contain, in addition to the hysteretic stiffness of the elements of the model, the matrix associated with the Lagrange multipliers induced by the dualisation of the loads supplied. Note : For a model containing only massless finite elements (for example '3D_ABSO' or 'D_PLAN_ABSO') , the user can build a damping matrix without having to build a mass matrix by going through the operator ASSEMBLAGE. 3.9 Operands AMOR_FLUI and VNOR > ◊ AMOR_FLUI = This option makes it possible for us to deactivate the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries ('3D_FLUI_ABSO', '2D_FLUI_ABSO' and 'AXIS_FLUI_ABSO'). In particular, if one uses the fluid formulation u-p-\phi in a harmonic analysis, one has the possibility of taking into account the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries via the computation of a third-order matrix (with the option IMPE_MECA). This third-order matrix is usable only in a harmonic analysis (operand MATR_IMPE_PHI in DYNA_VIBRA) and makes it possible for us to symmetrise the matrix (unlike the computation of this contribution via AMOR_MECA). The option AMOR_FLUI = ‘NON’ saves us from computing this contribution twice. By default, AMOR_FLUI = ‘OUI’. This operand is available exclusively for the option AMOR_MECA. ◊ VNOR= This option makes it possible for us to take into account the case of an emitting boundary. The most common case is the radiative one (or partially radiative if one defines a reflection coefficient \alpha \ne 0 ). In the case of a radiative boundary VNOR = 1. (option activated by default). In the case of an emitting boundary VNOR = -1. This coefficient is multiplied by the value of the impedance of the absorbing fluid boundaries ('3D_FLUI_ABSO', '2D_FLUI_ABSO' and 'AXIS_FLUI_ABSO'). This operand is available exclusively for the options AMOR_MECA, IMPE_MECA and AMOR_ACOU. 3.10 Operand TYPE_AMOR > ◊ TYPE_AMOR= This option makes it possible for us to compute all the sources of damping present in the model or only the source linked to the absorbing-boundary elements (fluid or not). The default option (TYPE_AMOR= ‘TOUT’) takes into account the possible Rayleigh damping, the damping coming from the discrete elements and that coming from the absorbing-boundary elements. In this case one is obliged to supply either the mass and stiffness matrices for the Rayleigh damping (and the material field), or the characteristics of the discrete elements. If one is in the presence of only the damping coming from the absorbing-boundary elements, one must specify TYPE_AMOR= ‘ABSO’ and supply as input only the material field. 4 Examples of analyses with CALC_MATR_ELEM 4.1 Geometric stiffness matrix for Euler buckling rigigeom = CALC_MATR_ELEM ( OPTION='RIGI_GEOM', MODELE= mo , CARA_ELEM= carac , SIEF_ELGA= chsig ) 4.2 “Mass” matrix in acoustics massacou = CALC_MATR_ELEM ( OPTION='MASS_ACOU', MODELE= mo , CHAM_MATER= chmat ) 4.3 Stiffness matrix in mechanics rigibloc = CALC_MATR_ELEM ( OPTION='RIGI_MECA', CHARGE= ch_bloc )

u4.61.02 Operator CALC_VECT_ELEM u4.61.02 Operator CALC_VECT_ELEM 1 Purpose Compute a set of elementary vectors which one will be able to assemble with ASSE_VECTEUR. The possible analysis options are: 'CHAR_MECA', 'CHAR_THER', 'CHAR_ACOU', 'FORC_NODA'. Produces a data structure of type vect_elem_ . 2 Syntax / vect_elem_depl_r / vect_elem_pres_c / vect_elem_temp_r = CALC_VECT_ELEM( ◆ OPTION = / "CHAR_ACOU", / "CHAR_MECA", / "CHAR_THER", / "FORC_VARC", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CHAR_MECA') ◆ | CHARGE = list[char_meca], | MODELE = modele, # Si: exists("CHARGE") ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ INST = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ MODE_FOURIER = int (défaut: 0), # Si: (exists("MODELE")) ◆ SOUS_STRUC = _F( ◆ CAS_CHARGE = text, ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / SUPER_MAILLE = list[ma], ), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'FORC_VARC') ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ INST = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CHAR_THER') ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◆ CHARGE = list[char_ther], ◇ INST = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CHAR_ACOU') ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ CHARGE = list[char_acou], ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General points This command is used to compute a set of elementary vectors (corresponding to a chosen option). The concept created, of type vect_elem_ , can then be assembled by the operator ASSE_VECTEUR U4.42.03 in order to give a right-hand side of type cham_no. The options available are: | 'CHAR_MECA' | in order to obtain the right-hand side of a mechanical problem | | --- | --- | | 'CHAR_THER' | in order to obtain the right-hand side of a thermal problem | | 'CHAR_ACOU' | in order to obtain the right-hand side of an acoustic problem | | 'FORC_VARC' | in order to obtain the forces generated by the command variables | 4 Operands 4.1 Operand CHARGE ♦ CHARGE= lchar The list of loads lchar must be consistent with the chosen option: - "mechanical" loads for the option 'CHAR_MECA', - "thermal" loads for the option 'CHAR_THER', - "acoustic" loads for the option 'CHAR_ACOU'. This argument is mandatory. It makes it possible to access all the data concerning the “loading” of the system. It is necessary that all the loads of the list be based on the same model. 4.2 Operand INST ◊ INST= tps The parameter tps (time instant of the analysis) is used as soon as the loading depends on time. 4.3 Operand MODELE ◊ MODELE= mo This keyword is mandatory in order to retrieve the substructures affected by the loading or for the command variables. mo is the name of the model. 4.4 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER Name of the material field in which the material characteristics of the elements are defined. This argument is necessary in mechanics for the gravity and rotation loadings and in acoustics. 4.5 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM= carac This concept of type cara_elem is necessary if there exist in the model structural elements (beam, plate, shell or discrete elements). 4.6 Operand MODE_FOURIER ◊ MODE_FOURIER= nh Positive or zero integer indicating the FOURIER harmonic on which one computes the elementary vector for an axisymmetric 2D model. By default, nh = 0. 4.7 Operands necessary for analyses with static substructuring ♦ SOUS_STRUC This factor keyword makes it possible to specify which loadings are to be used for the substructures. In its absence, the loadings on the substructures are zero. These loadings are added to the "finite element" loadings which can be applied on the rest of the model. ♦ CAS_CHARGE= nocas nocas is the name of the load case to be used. See the operator MACR_ELEM_STAT U4.62.01. ♦ / TOUT= 'OUI' This keyword makes it possible to assign the loading nocas to all the substructures of the model. ♦ / SUPER_MAILLE= l_mail This factor keyword makes it possible to assign the loading nocas only to certain substructures. 5 Examples - Computation of the right-hand side for a steady linear thermal problem: vect_elem = CALC_VECT_ELEM( OPTION= 'CHAR_THER', CHARGE= ch_ther ) - Computation of the mechanical loading of a structure containing static substructures: vect_elem = CALC_VECT_ELEM ( OPTION= 'CHAR_MECA', CHARGE= ch_meca, MODELE= mo, SOUS_STRUC= _F (CAS_CHARGE= 'ch_f1', TOUT= 'OUI')) - Computation of the forces generated by the command variables: vect_elem = CALC_VECT_ELEM ( OPTION= 'FORC_VARC', MODELE= mo, CHAM_MATER= mater)

u4.61.03 Operator CALC_CHAR_CINE u4.61.03 Operator CALC_CHAR_CINE 1 Purpose Compute the field at the nodes corresponding to the degrees of freedom imposed by AFFE_CHAR_CINE. This nodal field thus computed will have to be used when solving the linear system with the operator RESOUDRE U4.51.02. This operator is useful only for the “step-by-step” analyses in which one solves the linear systems by the command RESOUDRE. Produces a data structure of type cham_no. 2 Syntax cham_no = CALC_CHAR_CINE( ◆ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◆ CHAR_CINE = char_cine_acou / char_cine_ther / char_cine_meca, ◇ INST = float, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NUME_DDL ♦ NUME_DDL = nu Name of the numbering associated with the matrix which will be used for the solution. 3.2 Operand CHAR_CINE ♦ CHAR_CINE= l_chci List of the names of the kinematic loads to be evaluated. The computed cham_no will contain: - the value 0 on the degrees of freedom which are not imposed, - the value imposed by the kinematic loads on the degrees of freedom which are imposed. Warning: If a degree of freedom is imposed several times (if it appears in several kinematic loads of the list l_chci), the value imposed on this degree of freedom will be the sum of the imposed values, which is probably not what the user wants! This dangerous behaviour is unfortunately accompanied by no alarm. If the kinematic load is of function type, the value imposed on a degree of freedom is that obtained by evaluation of the function at the coordinates of the node carrying the degree of freedom and at the time instant t [§3.3]. 3.3 Operand INST ◊ INST= t Time instant used to evaluate any functions of time [§3.2]. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= impr Printout parameter: 1: (default) no printout, 2: printout of the resulting cham_no_ . 4 Examples An example of a sequence of commands using CALC_CHAR_CINE is given in the documentation of the command AFFE_CHAR_CINE U4.44.03.

u4.61.11 Operator NUME_DDL u4.61.11 Operator NUME_DDL 1 Purpose Number the unknowns of a system of linear equations. This operator also “prepares” the assembly of the matrix associated with this system of equations. It is in this operator that the method for solving the linear systems is chosen: LDLT, conjugate gradient, multifrontal… Produces a data structure of type nume_ddl. 2 Syntax nume_ddl = NUME_DDL( ◆ / MATR_RIGI = matr_elem_pres_c / matr_elem_depl_r / matr_elem_temp_r / matr_elem_depl_c, / MODELE = modele, # Si: exists("MODELE") ◇ CHARGE = char_ther / char_meca / char_acou, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General points This command makes it possible to number the equations (and the unknowns) of the linear systems to be solved. One also prepares the work of assembling the matrices, by establishing the pointer tables corresponding to the storage of these matrices. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand MODELE / CHARGE ♦ / MODELE = mo , CHARGE = lchar Le code numérotera les degrés de liberté des éléments du modèle mo ainsi que les degrés de liberté de dualisation des conditions cinématiques dualisées éventuellement présentes dans les charges de la liste lchar. 4.2 Operand MATR_RIGI ♦ / MATR_RIGI = lmel List of the matr_elem_ making it possible to establish the numbering of the unknowns of the problem. The aim of this operator is to number all the degrees of freedom of the problem. These degrees of freedom are those carried by the elementary matrices computed by the operator CALC_MATR_ELEM (lmel). Because of the dualisation of the “kinematic” conditions, the Lagrange degrees of freedom are carried by the matr_elem computed by the option 'RIGI_MECA' (or 'RIGI_THER', ...) on the loads where the kinematic conditions are defined. It is therefore important to give in lmel the list of all the “stiffness” matr_elem and not to forget the loads in the operator CALC_MATR_ELEM U4.61.01. 4.3 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 sur le fichier MESSAGE. - total number of degrees of freedom, number of nodes, - number of LAGRANGE degrees of freedom, - maximum height of a column (and mean height), - number of terms stored (for the storage 'MORSE'), 5 Examples Voir les exemples dans la commande RESOUDRE [:ref: U4.55.02 ]

u4.61.21 Macro-command ASSEMBLAGE u4.61.21 Macro-command ASSEMBLAGE 1 Purpose Compute one or more assembled matrices (stiffness, mass, damping …) as well as one or more assembled vectors. This command is recommended in order to create the concepts necessary for dynamic analyses, whether matrices or vectors. It avoids tedious calls to the “basic” commands: CALC_MATR_ELEM U4.41.01, NUME_DDL U4.61.01, ASSE_MATRICE U4.61.22, CALC_VECT_ELEM U4.61.02, ASSE_VECTEUR U4.61.23. Produces one or more data structures of type matr_asse_ and cham_no plus, possibly, a data structure of type nume_ddl. 2 Syntax / matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_c / cham_no / nume_ddl / matr_asse_temp_r = ASSEMBLAGE( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ INST = float, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ CHARGE = char_ther / char_meca / char_acou, ◇ CHAR_CINE = char_cine_acou / char_cine_ther / char_cine_meca, ◆ NUME_DDL = co / nume_ddl, ◆ | MATR_ASSE = _F( ◆ MATRICE = co, ◆ OPTION = / "RIGI_MECA", / "MASS_MECA", / "MASS_MECA_DIAG", / "AMOR_MECA", / "RIGI_MECA_HYST", / "IMPE_MECA", / "ONDE_FLUI", / "RIGI_FLUI_STRU", / "MASS_FLUI_STRU", / "RIGI_ROTA", / "RIGI_GEOM", / "MECA_GYRO", / "RIGI_GYRO", / "RIGI_THER", / "RIGI_ACOU", / "MASS_ACOU", / "AMOR_ACOU", # Si: is_in("OPTION", ('RIGI_GYRO', 'MECA_GYRO', 'IMPE_MECA', 'AMOR_MECA', 'MASS_MECA', 'RIGI_MECA', 'MASS_MECA_DIAG','MASS_FLUI_STRU')) ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'RIGI_MECA') ◇ MODE_FOURIER = int, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'RIGI_GEOM') ◆ SIEF_ELGA = cham_elem, ◇ MODE_FOURIER = int, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'RIGI_THER') ◇ MODE_FOURIER = int, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'AMOR_MECA') ◇ AMOR_FLUI = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ VNOR = / 1.0 (par défaut), / -1.0, ◇ TYPE_AMOR = / "TOUT" (par défaut), / "ABSO", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'IMPE_MECA') ◇ VNOR = / 1.0 (par défaut), / -1.0, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'AMOR_ACOU') ◇ VNOR = / 1.0 (par défaut), / -1.0, ), | VECT_ASSE = _F( ◆ VECTEUR = co, ◆ OPTION = / "CHAR_MECA", / "CHAR_ACOU", / "CHAR_THER", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CHAR_MECA') ◇ CHARGE = char_meca, ◇ MODE_FOURIER = int, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CHAR_THER') ◇ CHARGE = char_ther, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CHAR_ACOU') ◇ CHARGE = char_acou, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Concepts created by the macro-command This macro-command creates several typed concepts: - one matr_asse_ at each occurrence of the factor keyword MATR_ASSE (keyword MATRICE), - one cham_no at each occurrence of the factor keyword VECT_ASSE (keyword VECTEUR), - possibly a nume_ddl (keyword NUME_DDL) if it does not already exist. For example, the sequence: ... # nu n'est pas un concept encore existant. ASSEMBLAGE (MODELE = mo , ... NUME_DDL = CO("nu"), MATR_ASSE = ( _F( MATRICE= CO("K"), OPTION='RIGI_MECA'), VECT_ASSE = ( _F( VECTEUR= CO("F"), OPTION='CHAR_MECA')) ASSEMBLAGE (MODELE = mo , ... NUME_DDL = nu, MATR_ASSE = ( _F(MATRICE=CO("M"),OPTION='MASS_MECA'), _F(MATRICE=CO("A"),OPTION='AMOR_MECA'), ),) | the 1st call to ASSEMBLAGE creates | 1 MATR_ASSE: K | | --- | --- | | | 1 VECT_ASSE: F | | | 1 NUME_DDL: nu | | the 2nd call to ASSEMBLAGE creates | 2 MATR_ASSE: M and A | Note: On the 2nd call, the concept nume_ddl is supplied (it exists; it was created by the 1st call). In this case, it is assumed to be suitable for the 2 matr_asse to be created; it is therefore important that the nume_ddl be first computed for an option of type "RIGIDITE" in order to contain the Lagrange nodes of the fixing loads (cf. CALC_MATR_ELEM U4.61.01). In the previous example, the 3 matr_asse K, M and A and the vector F are based on the same numbering of the unknowns (nu). This is a necessary condition for the eigenmode search algorithms. 3.2 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM / INST ♦ MODELE = mo This operand is used to indicate the elements for which the elementary analyses must be performed: one recalls that the finite elements are for the most part defined in the model. There are a few exceptions: 1. The elements of dualisation of the DIRICHLET conditions, that is the elements making it possible to impose conditions on the displacement degrees of freedom in mechanics, the temperature degrees of freedom in thermal analysis and the pressure degrees of freedom in acoustics. 2. The elements of nodal loading, of thermal exchange between walls, ... These elements are defined in the concepts of type char_meca, char_ther or char_acou. One must therefore supply the argument l_char for the computation of the assembled stiffness matrices: RIGI_MECA, RIGI_THER, RIGI_ACOU, RIGI_MECA_HYST and RIGI_THER_CONV(_D). ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater Name of the material field in which the material characteristics of the elements are defined. This argument is almost always necessary. In practice, one can do without it: - for the discrete elements whose elementary matrices are defined in the concept cara_elem. See AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01, - for the computation of the stiffnesses due to the dualisation of the boundary conditions. ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac The elementary characteristics carac are necessary if there exist in the model structural elements (beam, shell or discrete elements) or non-isotropic continuous-medium elements. ◊ INST= tps The argument tps is used when the material characteristics or the loadings depend on time. A fairly frequent case is that of a mechanical material depending on the temperature which itself depends on time. 3.3 Operands CHARGE ◊ CHARGE = l_char This operand has several distinct functions: 1. specify the elements for which the elementary stiffness analyses are done (DIRICHLET conditions), 2. for the options 'RIGI_THER_CONV(_D)': give the value of the convection velocity, 3. for the option 'IMPE_MECA': give the value of the acoustic impedance of the mesh cells of the edge, 4. for the option 'ONDE_FLUI': give the value of the pressure of the incident wave, 5. for the option 'RIGI_ROTA': give the value of the rotation imposed on the model. Note: Warning for the two operands CHARGE : The one under VECT_ASSE cannot replace the one under ASSEMBLAGE . If one fills in CHARGE only under VECT_ASSE , the loadings are not taken into account in the functions below. When calling the macro-command for the assembly of the vectors in the case where the concept nume_ddl is an input (under the keyword NUME_DDL ), the value of the keyword CHARGE l_char must be identical to that used for the creation of the nume_ddl. For example, the following sequence: ... # nu n'est pas un concept encore existant. ASSEMBLAGE (MODELE = mo , CHARGE = (char_1,char_2),... NUME_DDL = CO("nu"), MATR_ASSE = ( _F( MATRICE= CO("K"), OPTION='RIGI_MECA')) # nu existe et est un concept entrant. ASSEMBLAGE (MODELE = mo , CHARGE = (char_1,char_2),... NUME_DDL = nu, VECT_ASSE = ( _F(VECTEUR=CO("F"),OPTION='CHAR_MECA', CHARGE=CHAR_F),),) 3.4 Operand CHAR_CINE ◊ CHAR_CINE = lchci This operand makes it possible not to “dualise” certain Dirichlet boundary conditions (fixings). These will be eliminated. 3.5 Operand NUME_DDL ♦ NUME_DDL = nu The user of the macro must always give a concept name after the keyword NUME_DDL. If the concept does not exist, it is created. If the concept exists, it is used to number the matrices. 3.6 Keyword MATR_ASSE This factor keyword makes it possible to request the computation of an assembled matrix (at each occurrence). The name of the assembled matrix is given by the operand MATRICE and the “nature” of the matrix is defined by the operand OPTION . The possible options: 'RIGI_MECA', 'MASS_MECA', … are described in U4.61.01. The choice of the option determines the type of the resulting matr_asse_ U4.61.01. 3.6.1 Operands specific to certain options 3.6.1.1 Operand MODE_FOURIER ◊ MODE_FOURIER = nh Positive or zero integer indicating the FOURIER harmonic on which one computes the matrices. By default: nh = 0 3.6.1.2 Operand SIEF_ELGA (option 'RIGI_GEOM') ♦ SIEF_ELGA = sig The stress field sig given for the computation of the option 'RIGI_GEOM' must have been computed with the option 'SIEF_ELGA' (stress field at the GAUSS points of the elements) (cf. commands CALC_CHAM_ELEM U4.81.03 or CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04). 3.6.1.3 Operand GROUP_MA (options 'MECA_GYRO' and 'RIGI_GYRO') ◊ GROUP_MA = grma On peut restreindre le calcul des options 'MECA_GYRO'et 'RIGI_GYRO'sur les mailles spécifiées par GROUP_MA. 3.6.1.4 Operands AMOR_FLUI, VNOR and TYPE_AMOR > ◊ AMOR_FLUI = This option makes it possible for us to deactivate the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries ('3D_FLUI_ABSO', '2D_FLUI_ABSO' and 'AXIS_FLUI_ABSO'). In particular, if one uses the fluid formulation u-p-\phi in a harmonic analysis, one has the possibility of taking into account the contribution of the absorbing fluid boundaries via the computation of a third-order matrix (with the option IMPE_MECA). This third-order matrix is usable only in a harmonic analysis (operand MATR_IMPE_PHI in DYNA_VIBRA) and makes it possible for us to symmetrise the matrix (unlike the computation of this contribution via AMOR_MECA). The option AMOR_FLUI = ‘NON’ saves us from computing this contribution twice. By default, AMOR_FLUI = ‘OUI’. This operand is available exclusively for the option AMOR_MECA. ◊ VNOR= This option makes it possible for us to take into account the case of an emitting boundary. The most common case is the radiative one (or partially radiative if one defines a reflection coefficient \alpha \ne 0 ). In the case of a radiative boundary VNOR= 1. (option activated by default). In the case of an emitting boundary VNOR= -1. This coefficient is multiplied by the value of the impedance of the absorbing fluid boundaries ('3D_FLUI_ABSO', '2D_FLUI_ABSO' and 'AXIS_FLUI_ABSO'). This operand is available exclusively for the options AMOR_MECA, IMPE_MECA and AMOR_ACOU. ◊ TYPE_AMOR= This option makes it possible for us to compute all the sources of damping present in the model or only the source linked to the absorbing-boundary elements (fluid or not). The default option (TYPE_AMOR= ‘TOUT’) takes into account the possible Rayleigh damping, the damping coming from the discrete elements and that coming from the absorbing-boundary elements. In this case one is obliged to supply either the mass and stiffness matrices for the Rayleigh damping (and the material field), or the characteristics of the discrete elements. If one is in the presence of only the damping coming from the absorbing-boundary elements, one must specify TYPE_AMOR= ‘ABSO’ and supply as input only the material field. This operand is available exclusively for the option AMOR_MECA. 3.7 Keyword VECT_ASSE This factor keyword makes it possible to request the computation of an assembled vector (at each occurrence). The name of the assembled vector is given by the operand VECTEUR. Among the possible options for elementary computation and assembly of vectors, only certain possibilities among all those proposed in the commands CALC_VECT_ELEM and ASSE_VECTEUR are proposed here: 'CHAR_MECA' for the mechanical phenomena, 'CHAR_THER' and 'CHAR_ACOU' for the thermal and acoustic phenomena respectively. The set of options and associated operands is described in u4.61.02 and u4.61.23. Note: The option 'FORC_NODA' and the taking into account of a model containing substructures under the option 'CHAR_MECA', often used in the case of statics, are not available in this macro-command. 3.7.1 Operands specific to certain options 3.7.1.1 Operand MODE_FOURIER ◊ MODE_FOURIER = nh Positive or zero integer indicating the FOURIER harmonic on which one computes the vectors in the case of the mechanical phenomena. By default: nh = 0 3.7.1.2 Operand CHARGE ◊ CHARGE = l_char_v Cette opérande permet d'accéder aux informations de chargement spécifiques à chaque vecteur. Les valeurs de l_char_v complètent ( par addition ) les charges l_char spécifiées sous le mot-clé CHARGE en dehors du mot clé VECT_ASSE. Note: Duplicates in the loads given in l_char and in l_char v are forbidden. Warning for the two operands of CHARGE : The one under VECT_ASSE cannot replace the one under ASSEMBLAGE . If one fills in CHARGE only under VECT_ASSE , the loadings are not taken into account in the functions mentioned in chapter 3.3. Example of the treatment of the loadings: ASSEMBLAGE (MODELE = mo , … CHARGE = (char_1,char_2), NUME_DDL = CO("nu"), MATR_ASSE = ( _F( MATRICE= CO("K"), OPTION='RIGI_MECA'), VECT_ASSE = ( _F( VECTEUR= CO("F1"), OPTION='CHAR_MECA',CHARGE=char_A ), _F( VECTEUR= CO("F2"), OPTION='CHAR_MECA',CHARGE=char_B ), _F( VECTEUR= CO("F3"), OPTION='CHAR_MECA'),) Dans l'exemple ci-dessus, les charges assemblées pour chaque vecteur sont: | Vector | Assembled loads | | --- | --- | | F1 | char_1, char_2, char_A | | F2 | char_1, char_2, char_B | | F3 | char_1, char_2 | 3.8 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE Title which one wants to give to the result U4.03.01. 4 Examples 4.1 Computation of mechanical eigenmodes ASSEMBLAGE ( MODELE = mo , CHARGE = ch_blocage , CHAM_MATER = chmat , CARA_ELEM = carac , NUME_DDL = CO("nu") , MATR_ASSE = (_F (MATRICE = CO("K"), OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA'), _F (MATRICE = CO("M"), OPTION = 'MASS_MECA'),),) modes = CALC_MODES ( MATR_RIGI = K, MATR_MASS = M, ...) 4.2 Computation of Euler buckling modes # chsief est le champ de contraintes lié au chargement ASSEMBLAGE ( MODELE = mo , CHARGE = ch_blocage , CHAM_MATER = chmat , CARA_ELEM = carac , NUME_DDL = CO("nu"), MATR_ASSE = ( _F(MATRICE= CO("K"), OPTION='RIGI_MECA'), _F(MATRICE= CO("KG"), OPTION='RIGI_GEOM', SIEF_ELGA=chsief),),) modflamb = CALC_MODES ( MATR_RIGI = K, MATR_MASS = KG, …) 4.3 Computation of a forced response ASSEMBLAGE ( MODELE = mo , CHARGE = ch_blocage , CHAM_MATER = chmat , CARA_ELEM = carac , NUME_DDL = CO("nu") , MATR_ASSE = (_F (MATRICE = CO("K"), OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA'), _F (MATRICE = CO("M"), OPTION = 'MASS_MECA'),), VECT_ASSE = ( _F( VECTEUR= CO("F"), OPTION='CHAR_MECA',CHARGE=char_A ),) reponse = DYNA_VIBRA ( MATR_RIGI = K, MATR_MASS = M, EXCIT = _F( VECT_ASSE = F, ...)...)

u4.61.22 Operator ASSE_MATRICE u4.61.22 Operator ASSE_MATRICE 1 Purpose Create a matrix by assembly of elementary matrices. The matrix produced is “sparse”; it is stored in “morse” form. Produces a data structure of type matr_asse_ . 2 Syntax / matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_temp_r / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_c = ASSE_MATRICE( ◆ MATR_ELEM = matr_elem_pres_c / matr_elem_depl_r / matr_elem_temp_r / matr_elem_depl_c, ◆ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◇ SYME = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ CHAR_CINE = char_cine_acou / char_cine_ther / char_cine_meca, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MATR_ELEM ♦ MATR_ELEM = mel, Name of the matr_elem_ concept to be assembled. 3.2 Numbering and storage ♦ NUME_DDL = nu, Specifies the numbering of the equations of the assembled system and the storage of the matrix. 3.3 Operand CHAR_CINE ◊ CHAR_CINE = cha, Name of the kinematic load to be taken into account in the assembled matrix for a treatment by elimination of the imposed degrees of freedom (see the command AFFE_CHAR_CINE U4.44.03). 3.4 Operand SYME > à SYME = 'OUI' This argument can take only the value 'OUI'. In this case, one forces the symmetrisation of the matrix after assembly. Thus, if the matrix K created by assembly is non-symmetric, the keyword SYME = 'OUI' makes it possible to symmetrise it and to replace it by: \mathrm{ma}=\frac{1}{2}(K+{K}^{T}) 3.5 Operand INFO ◊ INFO Allows the printout of information on the assembled matrix | 1: | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2: | printout of the number of stored terms and of the conditioning coefficient of the degrees of freedom of type 'LAGR', | 4 Example matas = ASSE_MATRICE ( NUME_DDL = nu , MATR_ELEM = mel, ) Note: The elementary matrices of mel will be assembled according to the numbering nu. This numbering must therefore take into account all the degrees of freedom of these elementary matrices (in particular the degrees of freedom corresponding to the dualisation of the boundary conditions). One will therefore do: mel = CALC_MATR_ELEM(OPTION = 'RIGI_MECA', MODELE = mo, CHARGE = condlim,) nu = NUME_DDL(MATR_RIGI = mel) matas = ASSE_MATRICE (NUME_DDL = nu, MATR_ELEM = mel,)

u4.61.23 Operator ASSE_VECTEUR u4.61.23 Operator ASSE_VECTEUR 1 Purpose Build a field at the nodes by assembly of elementary vectors. This field may, for example, be used as a right-hand side for the solution of a linear system. Produces a data structure cham_no. 2 Syntax cham_no = ASSE_VECTEUR( ◆ VECT_ELEM = vect_elem, ◆ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand VECT_ELEM ♦ VECT_ELEM = lvel List of the concepts of type vect_elem to be assembled. The various elementary vectors are summed in one and the same assembled vector (of type cham_no). The assembly is valid only if the various vect_elem concepts all correspond to one and the same quantity (grandeur) DEPL_R, TEMP_R, PRES_R or PRES_C. 3.2 Operand NUME_DDL ♦ NUME_DDL = nu Defines the numbering of the degrees of freedom to be used for the assembled vector.

u4.62.01 Operator MACR_ELEM_STAT u4.62.01 Operator MACR_ELEM_STAT 1 Purpose Create macro-elements for analyses of "static substructuring" or for analyses of "structural modification". In the case of analyses of "static substructuring", the macro-element is computed by assembly of ordinary finite elements and condensation of the matrices onto the "external" degrees of freedom. In the case of "structural modification", the macro-element is computed by expansion and condensation of the identified (measured) modal model onto the "external" degrees of freedom. Produces a data structure of type macr_elem_stat. 2 Syntax macr_elem_stat = MACR_ELEM_STAT( ◇ reuse = , ◇ MACR_ELEM = macr_elem_stat, ◆ | DEFINITION = _F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ CHAR_MACR_ELEM = char_meca, ◇ INST = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ NMAX_CAS = int (défaut: 10), ◇ NMAX_CHAR = int (défaut: 10), ◇ & PROJ_MESU = harm_gene / mode_gene / tran_gene, & MODE_MESURE = mode_meca, ), | RIGI_MECA = _F( ), | MASS_MECA = _F( ), | CAS_CHARGE = _F( ◆ NOM_CAS = text, ◇ SUIV = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ CHARGE = char_meca, ◇ INST = float (défaut: 0.0), ), ◇ & EXTERIEUR = _F( ◆ | GROUP_NO = grno, ), ◇ AMOR_MECA = _F( ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General points This operator is a mandatory step for static substructuring or for a structural-modification analysis by condensation of the measurement. For static substructuring, it is used: - to define a macro-element (keywords: DEFINITION and EXTERIEUR), - to request the condensation of the stiffness (or mass) matrix, - to define (and condense) the associated loadings; the user may on this occasion name one or more load cases. These 3 steps can be carried out in a single call to MACR_ELEM_STAT. But they can be carried out in several stages thanks to the use of the keyword "reuse" (enrichment of the macr_elem_stat). The definition step must be carried out first. The condensation of the mass must be done after the condensation of the stiffness. For structural modification, it is used: - to define a macro-element (keywords: DEFINITION and EXTERIEUR), - to request the expansion and the condensation of the measurement in order to arrive at condensed stiffness and mass matrices. The macr_elem_stat is a data structure which contains: - its references: modele, cara_elem, cham_mater, load, - its topological description: the external nodes, - its condensed matrices (stiffness, mass, ...), - a list of named condensed loadings (for static substructuring). The use of the full set of static-substructuring operators is described in the user's guide U2.07.02, and the structural-modification procedure is described in the user's guide U2.07.03. 4 Operands 4.1 Keyword DEFINITION ◊ DEFINITION This factor keyword (not repeatable) is used to define the macro-element. 4.1.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE= mo "Static substructuring" case: Name of the model that one wishes to condense. The matrices (and loadings) that one condenses are always computed on the model as a whole . When one wishes to condense several subsets of one and the same mesh, one must therefore create several models on different mesh-cell groups. "Structural modification" case: Name of the model given under the keyword MODELE_CALCUL of the command PROJ_MESU_MODAL associated with repgene of the keyword PROJ_MESU. This model serves as a support for the expansion of the measurement onto the "external" nodes. 4.1.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER= chmat Name of the material field associated with the model. This argument is unnecessary if the model contains only discrete elements and static substructures. It is mandatory otherwise. 4.1.3 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM= carac Name of the elementary characteristics if the model includes beam, plate or shell elements. 4.1.4 Operands CHAR_MACR_ELEM / INST ◊ CHAR_MACR_ELEM= lchar This argument is used to define: - the thermal loading which may modify the material characteristics, when these depend on the temperature; one will if necessary specify the time instant of the thermal evolution (keyword INST), - the kinematic conditions applied to the internal nodes (cf. keyword EXTERIEUR) of the macro-element. ◊ INST= inst During an analysis for which the material characteristics depend on the temperature, one specifies here the temperature field to be used. The field used is the one corresponding to the time instant inst of the thermal evolution referenced in the list of loads lchar (refer to the command CALC_MATR_ELEM('RIGI_MECA')) U4.61.01. Notes on the kinematic conditions: In the static-substructuring operators, kinematic conditions of "Dirichlet" type are always dualised, never eliminated. In general one will apply the kinematic conditions on the external nodes at the higher level of substructuring. They will therefore not appear in the loads of lchar. On the other hand, the kinematic conditions that must be given before condensation (lchar) are those that one will no longer be able to give afterwards: - the conditions involving internal nodes (imposed degrees of freedom or linear relations) because these nodes will be eliminated, - the conditions defined from the edges of the finite elements (FACE_IMPO) because these finite elements will no longer exist after condensation. Note on the argument lchar: The loads which appear in the list lchar are those which make it possible to compute the stiffness and mass matrices: - possible temperature load modifying the material characteristics, - kinematic conditions (dualisation). on the other hand, these loads play no part in the definition of the loadings (right-hand sides). For example, the expansions due to the temperature field will be taken into account in a load case only if the load containing this temperature field is explicitly given in the definition of this load case (keywords CAS_CHARGE and CHARGE). In the same way the non-zero kinematic conditions must be given again in the definition of the load cases. 4.1.5 Operands NMAX_CAS / NMAX_CHAR ◊ NMAX_CAS= nbcamx One gives here an upper bound on the number of load cases that the user will define on the macro-element (see argument CAS_CHARGE). This number is taken by default as 10. ◊ NMAX_CHAR= nbchmx One gives here an upper bound on the number of concepts of type load that one will assign to each load case (see argument CAS_CHARGE). This number is taken by default as 10. 4.1.6 Operand PROJ_MESU ♦ PROJ_MESU= repgene repgene denotes the name of the concept produced by the command PROJ_MESU_MODAL U4.73.01 which made it possible to define the measurement and the projection basis. 4.1.7 Operand MODE_MESURE ♦ MODE_MESURE= modemes One gives here the name of the concept containing the eigenmodes identified experimentally. These eigenmodes make it possible to build the modal model of the initial structure which will then be condensed onto the "external" nodes. 4.2 Keyword EXTERIEUR ♦ EXTERIEUR= This factor keyword (not repeatable) is used to define the set of "external" nodes onto which the matrices and the loadings will be condensed (the other nodes will be called "internal"). This keyword must appear in the first call to the command MACR_ELEM_STAT (one defines the exterior of a macro-element in a single step). Each external node carries the same degrees of freedom as the corresponding node of the model mo. A macro-element is topologically (and geometrically) entirely defined by the set of its external nodes. 4.2.1 Notes on the definition of the "exterior" of a macro-element - The exterior of a macro-element is the set of "external" nodes which define the topology and the geometry of the macro-element, - each "external" node carries all the degrees of freedom which exist on this node in the underlying model. The macro-elements produced by Aster can be used only by joining their external nodes and consequently all the degrees of freedom that they carry. Other analysis codes operate differently. For certain modellings (sliding, hinge, …), one will be led not to join certain nodes and to use, at the higher substructuring level, linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the external nodes of several macro-elements, - when defining the external nodes of a macro-element, if a node appears several times, it is counted only once, - for programming reasons, both external nodes and internal nodes must exist: neither family may be empty. 4.2.2 Operand GROUP_NO GROUP_NO= l_grno List of the names of the node groups that one wishes to be "external". 4.3 Keywords RIGI_MECA / MASS_MECA ♦ RIGI_MECA This keyword is used to specify that one wishes to condense the stiffness matrix. "Static substructuring" case: This matrix is computed on all the elements of the model as well as on the LAGRANGE elements of the kinematic conditions contained in the argument of CHAR_MACR_ELEM. "Structural modification" case: The condensed stiffness matrix is computed by expansion of the measured spectral matrix onto the "external" nodes. ◊ MASS_MECA This keyword is used to specify that one wishes to condense the mass matrix. "Static substructuring" case: This matrix is computed on all the elements of the model (GUYAN condensation). "Structural modification" case: The condensed mass matrix is obtained by expansion of the matrix of measured generalised masses onto the "external" nodes. ◊ AMOR_MECA This keyword is used to specify that one wishes to condense the damping matrix. This feature is not available in "static substructuring": "Structural modification" case: The condensed damping matrix is obtained by expansion of the matrix of measured generalised dampings onto the "external" nodes. 4.4 Keyword CAS_CHARGE. ◊ CAS_CHARGE This factor keyword makes it possible to define a set of named load cases (keyword NOM_CAS). These load cases may be applied to the higher-level model (CALC_VECT_ELEM U4.61.02). In general, one will seek to apply the nodal loadings (FORCE_NODALE) at the higher level of substructuring. On the other hand all the loadings defined on the finite elements must be applied before any condensation: (PESANTEUR, ROTATION, FORCE_FACE, FORCE_CONTOUR, FORCE_INTERNE, FORCE_COQUE, FORCE_POUTRE, PRES_REP, …) since these finite elements will have "disappeared" after condensation. Note that for a macro-element, there is no notion of contour, of orientation, of face, ... 4.4.1 Operand NOM_CAS ♦ NOM_CAS= nocas The loading condensed under the name nocas (between "quotes") corresponds to the loading defined by the arguments of CHARGE and INST to which one systematically adds the loadings of name nocas possibly present on the lower-level substructures contained in the model mo. 4.4.2 Operand SUIV ◊ SUIV= 'OUI'/'NON' This keyword states whether the load case "follows" the macro-element in its geometric transformations: translation, rotation, (cf. operator DEFI_MAILLAGE U4.23.01). For example, the loading due to a rotation (centrifugal force), a pressure (or a restrained expansion) is "follower" because its direction is linked to the position of the substructure. On the other hand, gravity is a "non-follower" loading (its direction is absolute). Warning: Kinematic loadings are always "follower" because their taking into account is done in the stiffness matrix (dualisation) and this matrix is "follower" by nature. 4.4.3 Operands CHARGE / INST ◊ CHARGE= lchar, ◊ INST= tps, The keywords CHARGE and INST have the same meaning as in the operator CALC_VECT_ELEM U4.61.02. 5 Examples of definition of a macro-element 5.1 Defining the exterior of a macro-element sup1 = MACR_ELEM_STAT ( DEFINITION= _F ( MODELE= mo, CHAM_MATER= chmat), EXTERIEUR= _F ( GROUP_NO= EXT ), ) > sup3 = MACR_ELEM_STAT ( DEFINITION= _F ( MODELE= mo , CHAM_MATER= chmat,), EXTERIEUR= _F ( GROUP_NO= ('L1','L3'),) 5.2 Condensing stiffness and mass matrices sup1 = MACR_ELEM_STAT (reuse = sup1, RIGI_MECA= _F (), MASSE_MECA= _F (), ) 5.3 Defining a loading on the macro-element sup1 = MACR_ELEM_STAT (reuse = sup1, CAS_CHARGE= ( NOM_CAS= 'ch1' , CHARGE= ch1,), ) 5.4 Defining the macro-element, its loadings, and requesting the condensation of the matrices sup2 = MACR_ELEM_STAT ( DEFINITION = _F ( MODELE= mo , CHAM_MATER= chmat), EXTERIEUR = _F ( GROUP_NO= EXT ), RIGI_MECA = _F (), MASSE_MECA = _F (), CAS_CHARGE = _F ( NOM_CAS= 'ch1' , CHARGE= ch1 ), ) 5.5 Defining a macro-element for a structural-modification analysis and requesting the condensation of the matrices Sup4 = MACR_ELEM_STAT ( DEFINITION = _F ( MODELE= mo , CHAM_MATER= chmat > PROJ_MESU=repgene, MODE_MESURE=modemes), EXTERIEUR = _F ( GROUP_NO= EXT ), RIGI_MECA = _F (), MASSE_MECA= _F (), )

u4.62.02 Operator DEPL_INTERNE u4.62.02 Operator DEPL_INTERNE 1 Purpose Compute the field inside a macro-element. Two situations may exist: the macro-element was obtained by static substructuring , or the macro-element was obtained by condensation of the measurement for a structural modification analysis (see U4.62.01). In the case of a static substructure: the result of the command is a displacement field (cham_no) on the mesh associated with the macro-element (that is, the lower-level mesh). One can repeat this operation down to the lowest-level meshes (those which contain the finite elements). This step may be regarded as a post-processing on the macro-element. It can be carried out only after the global solution. The field thus computed can then be used by the operator CALC_CHAMP (or other operators) to compute the stresses, .... When a macro-element has given rise to several substructures, the displacement fields in these substructures are recovered on the mesh underlying the macro-element. There is therefore a change of frame of the displacement field if the substructure has been rotated. If the substructure has been rotated by +\alpha , the displacement field is rotated by -\alpha . This displacement field is then consistent with the mesh and one can chain the post-processings: computation of the stresses, ... In the case where the macro-element is obtained by condensation of the measurement for a structural-modification analysis, the result of the command is a data structure of type resultat (evol_elas, dyna_trans, dyna_harmo, mode_meca) on the sensor mesh (measurement points). In this data structure the displacement fields corresponding to NOM_CHAM = ‘DEPL’ are computed. 2 Syntax / cham_no / mode_meca_c / dyna_trans / dyna_harmo / evol_elas / mode_meca = DEPL_INTERNE( ◆ DEPL_GLOBAL = cham_no / dyna_trans / mode_meca / dyna_harmo / evol_elas / mode_meca_c, ◆ SUPER_MAILLE = ma, ◇ NOM_CAS = text (défaut: " "), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand DEPL_GLOBAL ♦ DEPL_GLOBAL = ug In the case where the macro-element is obtained by static substructuring: ug is the name of the displacement field obtained during the solution at the global level on the macro-element. In the case where the macro-element is obtained by condensation of the measurement for a structural-modification analysis: ug is the name of the data structure of type resultat obtained during an analysis on the coupled model (global level). In this data structure, one uses, for each order number, the (displacement) field corresponding to NOM_CHAM=’DEPL’. 3.2 Operand SUPER_MAILLE ♦ SUPER_MAILLE = mail One gives here the name of the super-mesh cell which supports the substructure (cf. operator DEFI_MAILLAGE U4.23.01). 3.3 Operand NOM_CAS ◊ NOM_CAS = nocas nocas is the name of the load case corresponding to ug. This datum is indispensable if there exists a distributed loading on the substructure. It is up to the user to make sure that the field ug does indeed correspond to the load case nocas. The possible load-case names are those defined in the macro-element; that is, those given via the keyword CAS_CHARGE/NOM_CAS of the commands MACR_ELEM_STAT and MACR_ELEM_DYNA. If nocas = ' ', the displacement field was computed without distributed loading on the substructure. This operand is not used if the macro-element is obtained by condensation of the measurement. 4 Example - Level-1 mesh: ma, macro-element: S1 - Level-2 mesh: 2 substructures: S1 and S2 (obtained by rotation of S1). Displacement ug: - known on the external nodes of the substructures, - it is assumed to be radial (with respect to O). - u2 = DEPL_INTERNE ( DEPL_GLOBAL = ug , SUPER_MAILLE = S2 ) .. image:: images/100016200000110E00000C8120CACF2543F7545E.svg :width: 202 :height: 129 .. _RefImage_100016200000110E00000C8120CACF2543F7545E.svg: Displacement u2: - known on all the nodes of ma, - it remains radial because the field has been rotated by - 45° in order to be consistent with the mesh.

u4.63.01 Operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME u4.63.01 Operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME 1 Purpose Establish the seismic loading (unit entrainment inertia forces) for a response analysis in relative motion with respect to the motions of the supports. For a better theoretical understanding of this loading, one should refer to the document R4.05.01. The concept produced can be used directly during a direct transient analysis or a modal-synthesis analysis with DYNA_VIBRA[U4.53.03]. On the other hand, for a non-linear direct transient analysis with DYNA_NON_LINE[U4.53.01], this concept must be transformed into a load by means of the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA[U4.44.01]. Produces a field at the nodes of quantity DEPL_R. 2 Syntax cham_no = CALC_CHAR_SEISME( ◆ MATR_MASS = matr_asse_depl_r, ◆ DIRECTION = float, ◆ / MONO_APPUI = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / MODE_STAT = mode_meca, # Si: exists("MODE_STAT") ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MATR_MASS ♦ MATR_MASS = m Mass matrix M of the system, built with the boundary conditions of blocking of the supports. 3.2 Operand DIRECTION ♦ DIRECTION = (d1,d2,d3,r1,r2,r3) Components of the vector giving the direction of the entrainment motion of the earthquake in the global frame. It is a list of three reals if the imposed accelerograms are translations only. If infinitesimal rotational accelerations are also imposed, a list of six reals is expected (valid for modellings with discrete elements or structural finite elements having rotational degrees of freedom). This vector \Delta will be normalised automatically by the operator. For example, if one supplies: DIRECTION = (1., 2., 2.,), the result will be the same as for: DIRECTION = (0.333, 0.666, 0.666,). 3.3 Description of the entrainment motion 3.3.1 Operand MONO_APPUI ♦ / MONO_APPUI = 'OUI' La structure est excitée uniformément sur tous ses appuis: le mouvement d'entraînement est de corps rigide, dans la direction donnée par le mot-cléDIRECTION(en général de translation, mais on peut aussi considérer une rotation infinitésimale). In accordance with what is explained in the reference document R4.05.01 the operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME computes the following expression: -M.\Delta with \Delta the direction of the earthquake specified by the operand DIRECTION. 3.3.2 Multi-support excitation In this case, the accelerations undergone by all the support points of the structure under study are not necessarily identical or in phase. The entrainment motions are not rigid-body motions, but are described by linear elastic static modes. 3.3.2.1 Operand MODE_STAT / MODE_STAT = mode Static modes of the structure: concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator MODE_STATIQUE[U4.52.14] with the option MODE_STAT. They correspond to the 6\times {\mathrm{nb}}_{\mathrm{appuis}} linear elastic static modes with a unit degree of freedom imposed at the supports, where {\mathrm{nb}}_{\mathrm{appuis}} is the number of different accelerograms (translations, rotations) undergone by the structure and defined on each unit degree of freedom imposed on each support considered. Note: If the structure is loaded only by translational degrees of freedom, there are then 3{\mathrm{nb}}_{\mathrm{appuis}} static modes. 3.3.2.2 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO = g_noeu List of node groups (g_noeu) of the structure subjected to the seismic excitation: these nodes support the support degrees of freedom of the structure to which the imposed motions are applied. In accordance with what is explained in the reference document R4.05.01 the operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME computes the following expression: -M.{\Psi}_{Pj}.s with s the direction of the earthquake, specified by the operand DIRECTION, and {\Psi}_{Pj} the unit linear static modes, specified by the operand MODE_STAT, computed for each degree of freedom of the blocked supports listed in the node groups (g_noeu). 3.4 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.63.01. 4 Examples The two examples which follow illustrate the use of the operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME in the cases of a single-support seismic excitation and in the multi-support case (identical acceleration, then a different acceleration, on each support). 4.1 Computation of a right-hand side in the single-support case One considers the beam seismic modelling of the building represented in the test SDLL109B, as presented in the documentation of the operator POST_ELEM[U4.81.22]. One wishes to determine the forces during the transient dynamic response of the structure to an earthquake in the direction X . The transient response analysis is carried out here by modal recombination by DYNA_VIBRA[U4.53.03]. One computes the vibration modes of the structure of the model resting on a single elastic support (soil spring): # --- recherche des modes propres de vibration ------------------------- MODES = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI = RIGIDITE, MATR_MASS = MASSE, OPTION = 'PLUS_PETITE', CALC_FREQ =_F( NMAX_FREQ = 33 ), ) One defines the accelerogram of the earthquake: # --- excitation ------------------------------------------------------- LBNSNL1 = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_RESU = 'ACCE', NOM_PARA = 'INST', PROL_GAUCHE = 'EXCLU', PROL_DROIT = 'EXCLU', VALE =( 0.00000E+00 9.98700E-02 1.00000E-02 6.60700E-02 2.00000E-02 -5.65000E-03 3.00000E-02 -9.46800E-02 ----------------------------------------------------- 1.19800E+01 1.68110E-01 1.19900E+01 8.80300E-02 1.20000E+01 0.00000E+00 9.98700E-02 0.00000E+00 ) ) ; ACCELERO = CALC_FONCTION( COMB =_F(FONCTION= LBNSNL1, COEF= 1.47 ) ) ; One computes the right-hand side (field at the nodes of the entrainment inertia forces) and one defines the direction of the earthquake: DIRSEISM = CALC_CHAR_SEISME ( MATR_MASS = MASSE, MONO_APPUI = 'OUI', DIRECTION = ( -1., 0., 0. ) ) ; One proceeds to the computation of the transient response in the modal space # --- projection des matrices et vecteur assemblés sur les modes PROJ_BASE( BASE=MODE, NB_VECT=33,MATR_ASSE_GENE=( _F( MATRICE = CO("MASSGENE"), MATR_ASSE = MASSE), _F( MATRICE = CO("RIGIGENE"), MATR_ASSE = RIGIDITE)), VECT_ASSE_GENE=_F( VECTEUR = CO("VECTGENE"), VECT_ASSE = SEISME) ); # --- calcul par combinaison modale ------------------------------------ LISTAMOR=( 0.055, 0.055, 0.070, 0.070, 0.071, 0.072, 0.157, 0.085, 0.086, 0.070, 0.076, 0.074, 0.071, 0.072, 0.115, 0.073, 0.076, 0.086, 0.081, 0.070, 0.072, 0.075, 0.074, 0.070, 0.152, 0.148, 0.074, 0.297, 0.074, 0.075, 0.089, 0.138, 0.118, ) TRANGENE=DYNA_VIBRA(TYPE_CALCUL='TRAN',BASE_CALCUL='GENE', MATR_MASS=MASSGENE, MATR_RIGI=RIGIGENE, AMOR_MODAL=_F(AMOR_REDUIT=LISTAMOR,), SCHEMA_TEMPS=_F(SCHEMA=METHODE,), INCREMENT=_F(INST_INIT = 0., INST_FIN = 4., PAS = 0.002, VERI_PAS = 'NON'), EXCIT=_F(VECT_ASSE_GENE = VECTGENE, FONC_MULT = ACCELERO),) One has used here the accelerogram of the imposed motion. One returns to the physical space: # --- restitution en base physique ------------------------------------- LISTINST=DEFI_LIST_REEL( DEBUT=1.334, INTERVALLE=_F( JUSQU_A = 3.154, NOMBRE = 1) ) TRANPHYS=REST_GENE_PHYS( RESU_GENE=TRANGENE, CRITERE='RELATIF', PRECISION=1.E-06, LIST_INST=LISTINST, TOUT_CHAM='OUI' ) 4.2 Computation of a right-hand side in the multi-support case The example which follows shows the computation of the right-hand sides of entrainment inertia forces when the seismic signals are different on the supports. One considers the beam-element modelling of the following piping line on which an earthquake is applied in the direction X : One computes the unit linear static modes for each degree of freedom of the supports blocked in the direction X , in order then to express the vector of the entrainment inertia forces as a linear combination of these: MODST = MODE_STATIQUE ( MATR_RIGI = RG, MATR_MASS = MS, MODE_STAT =_F( GROUP_NO = ('GP1','GP2','GP3'), ) ( AVEC_CMP = 'DX'),) ) ; One must compute three different right-hand sides (field at the nodes of the entrainment inertia forces) for each node group subjected to the same seismic signal: SMP1 = CALC_CHAR_SEISME ( MATR_MASS = MS, DIRECTION =( 1., 0., 0.), MODE_STAT = MODST, GROUP_NO = 'GP1' ) ; SMP2 = CALC_CHAR_SEISME ( MATR_MASS = MS, DIRECTION =( 1., 0., 0.), MODE_STAT = MODST, GROUP_NO = 'GP2' ) ; SMP3 = CALC_CHAR_SEISME ( MATR_MASS = MS, DIRECTION =( 1., 0., 0.), MODE_STAT = MODST, GROUP_NO = 'GP3' ) ; In accordance with what is explained in the reference document R4.05.01 the operator CALC_CHAR_SEISME computes the following expression: -M.{\Psi}_{Pj,X}.s with s=(1,0,0) , the direction of the earthquake, specified by the operand DIRECTION, and {\Psi}_{Pj,X} the unit linear static modes, specified by the operand MODE_STAT, computed for each degree of freedom of the supports blocked in the direction X . Computation of the transient response (here without damping) with the accumulation of the contribution of the three different seismic signals ACCELP1, ACCELP2 and ACCELP3: TRANGENE = DYNA_VIBRA ( TYPE_CALCUL='TRAN', BASE_CALCUL='PHYS', MATR_MASS = MS, MATR_RIGI = RG, SCHEMA_TEMPS=_F(SCHEMA='NEWMARK',), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=LI), EXCIT =( _F(VECT_ASSE = SMP1, FONC_MULT = ACCELP1), _F(VECT_ASSE = SMP2, FONC_MULT = ACCELP2), _F(VECT_ASSE = SMP3, FONC_MULT = ACCELP3), ) ) ; Other examples of multi-supported structures subjected to seismic loadings can be found by consulting the tests SDLD103 and SDND102.

u4.63.02 Operator PRE_SEISME_NONL u4.63.02 Operator PRE_SEISME_NONL 1 Purpose The purpose of this operator is to simplify the implementation of the Laplace-Time method by making it possible to carry out non-linear analyses with impedances produced by MISS3D. The use of the Laplace-Time method ( cf . U2.06.05) requires several operations: 1. the computation of a basis of interface modes necessary for the projection of the impedances obtained with the operator CALC_MISS ( cf . U7.03.12); 2. the creation of a new model which assembles these impedance matrices, whether within the framework of a solution in the physical basis or with dynamic reduction techniques ( cf . U2.07.04); 3. possibly the static-dynamic transition when a state of prestress must be taken into account at the beginning of the transient analysis. These keywords make it possible to specify the names of the concepts that the user wishes to create: - the name of the model (mo) whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis, - the name of the mesh ( mail) possibly containing new nodes and mesh cells, - the name of the material field (chmat) assigned to the mesh mail, - the name of the characteristics ( carac ) of the shell, beam, pipe, bar, cable and discrete elements assigned to the model mo. In the case of a dynamic reduction ( cf. U2.07.04 and U4.44.01), these created concepts will contain the additional elements necessary for the subsequent analyses. 3.1.2 Operand BASE_MODALE / MACR_ELEM_DYNA ◊ / BASE_MODALE = CO('bamo'), [mode_meca] ◊ / MACR_ELEM_DYNA = CO('mael'), [macr_elem_dyna] These keywords cannot be used without supplying the factor keyword PRE_CALC_MISS ( cf . § 3.2 ). Indeed, they make it possible to specify the following output concepts: - the name of the modal basis (bamo) containing the interface modes used as the projection basis of the soil impedances, - the name of the macro-element ( mael) which points to bamo and which can be used directly in CALC_MISS ( cf . U7.03.12). 3.1.3 Operand CHARGE CHARGE = _F ( ♦ NOM = CO('l_char'), [l_char_meca] ♦ OPTION = / 'COND_LIM', [DEFAUT] / 'LAPL_TEMPS', [TXM] ), This keyword makes it possible to create a load linked to the boundary conditions (OPTION = 'COND_LIM'), mandatory when one seeks to carry out a dynamic reduction, or to the Laplace-Time method (OPTION = 'LAPL_TEMPS'), which requires the presence of the operands UNITE_RESU_RIGI, UNITE_RESU_AMOR or UNITE_RESU_MASS in the factor keyword POST_CALC_MISS ( cf . § 3.3 ). 3.2 Operand PRE_CALC_MISS ◊ / PRE_CALC_MISS = _F ( ♦ CALC_MISS_OPTION = / 'ISS', [TXM] / 'ISFS', [TXM] ♦ NMAX_MODE_ISS = nbiss, [I] # Si CALC_MISS_OPTION == 'ISFS' ♦ NMAX_MODE_IFS = nbifs, [I] ♦ GROUP_MA_INTERF = grma_int, [grma] ◊ GROUP_NO_CENT = grno_cent, [grno] ◊ REDUC_DYNA_ISS = / 'NON', [DEFAUT] / 'OUI', [TXM] ◊ REDUC_DYNA_IFS = / 'NON', [DEFAUT] / 'OUI', [TXM] ), 3.2.1 Operand REDUC_DYNA_ISS / REDUC_DYNA_IFS These operands indicate how to represent the kinematics of the ISS or IFS interfaces by means of a basis of static modes (REDUC_DYNA_ = 'NON') or of dynamic modes (REDUC_DYNA_ = 'OUI'). 3.2.2 Operand NMAX_MODE_ISS / NMAX_MODE_IFS These operands make it possible to specify the number of modes to be computed in the case of an ISS or ISFS analysis. If REDUC_DYNA_ = 'OUI', the corresponding value of the keyword NMAX_MODE_ must be a multiple of 6. 3.2.3 Operand GROUP_MA_INTERF This keyword, which is mandatory, makes it possible to specify the mesh-cell group corresponding to the dynamic interface to be considered (the whole of the ISFS interface, or that of the ISS, or that of the IFS) for the computation of the interface modes. 3.2.4 Operand GROUP_NO_CENT This keyword indicates the node group defined at the centre of an interface so as to consider a rigid behaviour of this interface. If this keyword is supplied, a condition of type LIAISON_SOLIDE ( cf. U4.42.01) must, a priori , be entered by means of the operand AFFE_CHAR_MECA ( cf. § 3.8 ). 3.2.5 Operand CALC_MISS_OPTION This keyword indicates whether the analysis to be carried out is of type 'ISS' or of type 'ISFS'. The value supplied must therefore be consistent with the other operands of PRE_CALC_MISS but also of the macro-command CALC_MISS ( cf . U7.03.12). 3.3 Operand POST_CALC_MISS 3.3.1 Operand MACR_ELEM_DYNA This keyword expects as input a concept of type macr_elem_dyna which corresponds essentially to the impedance (frequency-domain or time-domain) to be assembled to the numerical model and which is obtained beforehand by, for example, the sequence of the command LIRE_IMPE_MISS ( cf. U7.02.32) and MACR_ELEM_DYNA ( cf . U4.65.01). 3.3.2 Operand GROUP_MA_INTERF This keyword is the same as the one used in § 3.2.3 . 3.3.3 Operand GROUP_NO_CENT This operand is the same as the one used in § 3.2.4 . It is particularly important when an analysis with STAT_DYNA ( cf. § 3.4 ) must be carried out subsequently. 3.3.4 Operand UNITE_RESU_RIGI / UNITE_RESU_AMOR / UNITE_RESU_MASS Logical unit numbers of the files containing the time-domain soil impedances (or its decomposition in terms of inertia, damping and stiffness) for the Laplace-Time method. The operands UNITE_RESU_RIGI, UNITE_RESU_AMOR, UNITE_RESU_MASS, being of a use specific to the Laplace-Time method, are mandatory when a load concept of type LAPL_TEMPS ( cf. § 3.1.3 ) is requested as output of this macro-command. 3.4 Operand STAT_DYNA ◊ / STAT_DYNA = _F ( ♦ RESULTAT = resu, [evol_noli] ♦ EXCIT = _F( ♦ CHARGE = char, / [char_meca] / [char_cine_meca] ◊ FONC_MULT = fonct, /[fonction_sdaster] / [nappe_sdaster] / [formule] ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = / 'FIXE_CSTE', [DEFAUT] / 'FIXE_PILO', [TXM] / 'SUIV', [TXM] / 'DIDI', [TXM] ), ♦ COMPORTEMENT = _F( voir le document [:ref: U4.51.11 ] ), ♦ CONVERGENCE = _F( voir le document [:ref: U4.51.03 ] ), ♦ BASE_MODALE = bamo, [mode_meca] ♦ UNITE_IMPE_TEMPS = _F( ◊ UNITE_RESU_RIGI = uresrig, [I] ◊ UNITE_RESU_AMOR = uresamo, [I] ◊ UNITE_RESU_MASS = uresmas, [I] ), ♦ UNITE_IMPE_FREQ = uimpfr, [I] ♦ FORCE_SOL = fsol, [char_meca] ◊ COEF_AMOR = / 0.0, [DEFAUT] / coefamo, [R] ◊ NB_INST = / 100.0 [DEFAUT] / nbinst, [R] ), 3.4.1 Operand RESULTAT This operand expects as input a concept of type evol_noli corresponding to the result of a static analysis. In particular, within the framework of the Laplace-Time method, where one seeks to carry out a non-linear seismic analysis taking soil-structure interaction into account, the expected concept corresponds to that produced by the operator STAT_NON_LINE ( cf. U4.51.03). 3.4.2 Operand EXCIT Cf. U4.51.03. In practice and within the framework of the Laplace-Time method, the keyword EXCIT expects the set of loads used for the non-linear analysis whose result is entered in RESULTAT ( cf. § 3.4.1 ). 3.4.3 Operand COMPORTEMENT / CONVERGENCE Cf. U4.51.03. The syntax is the same as that of the factor keywords defined in the operator STAT_NON_LINE and it must be consistent with the result entered in RESULTAT ( cf. § 3.4.1 ). 3.4.4 Operand BASE_MODALE This keyword expects as input the modal basis serving to project the soil impedances. This basis must be the same as that used to project the soil impedances supplied in UNITE_IMPE_TEMPS ( cf. § 3.4.5 ) and UNITE_IMPE_FREQ ( cf. § 3.4.6 ) in the form of logical units. 3.4.5 Operand UNITE_IMPE_TEMPS The three keywords of this operand have the same meaning as in § 3.3.4 . 3.4.6 Operand UNITE_IMPE_FREQ This keyword expects as input the logical unit of the file containing the soil impedance computed in the frequency domain. 3.4.7 Operand FORCE_SOL This keyword expects as input a load concept of type 'LAPL_TEMPS' ( cf. § 3.1.3 ) as created beforehand by the use of the keyword POST_CALC_MISS ( cf. § 3.3 ). 3.4.8 Operand COEF_AMOR This keyword is a coefficient which makes it possible to control the value of viscous damping to be added at the soil-structure interface in the form of discrete elements of type DIS_TR. When COEF_AMOR is equal to 1.0, the damping value which is assigned to all the degrees of freedom of each discrete element is 1.E16 N.s.m-1. 3.4.9 Operand NB_INST This keyword expects as input the number of time steps necessary to stabilise the static-dynamic transition. The default value is often sufficient. 3.5 Operand AFFE_MODELE Makes it possible to define the physical phenomenon modelled (mechanical, thermal, acoustic) and the type of finite elements used. The syntax associated with the keyword AFFE_MODELE is the same as that of the operator of the same name U4.41.01. Only one occurrence of this keyword is allowed. 3.6 Operand AFFE_MATERIAU Makes it possible to assign materials to geometric zones of a mesh or of a model. The syntax associated with the keyword AFFE_MATERIAU is the same as that of the operator of the same name U4.43.03. The only difference concerns the operand MODELE, which is not mandatory when PRE_CALC_MISS ( cf. § 3.2 ) is present. Only one occurrence of this keyword is allowed. 3.7 Operand AFFE_CARA_ELEM Makes it possible to assign geometric and material characteristics to structural elements. The syntax associated with the keyword AFFE_CARA_ELEM is the same as that of the operator of the same name U4.42.01. The only difference concerns the operand MODELE, which is not mandatory when PRE_CALC_MISS ( cf. § 3.2 ) is present. Only one occurrence of this keyword is allowed. 3.8 Operand AFFE_CHAR_MECA Makes it possible to assign loadings and boundary conditions on a mechanical model. The syntax associated with the keyword AFFE_CHAR_MECA is the same as that of the operator of the same name U4.44.01. The only difference concerns the operand MODELE, which is not mandatory when PRE_CALC_MISS ( cf. § 3.2 ) is present. Only one occurrence of this keyword is allowed. 3.9 Operand INFO Makes it possible to control the message level of the macro-command.

u4.63.03 Macro-command DEFI_PRES_EC8 u4.63.03 Macro-command DEFI_PRES_EC8 Summary: This macro-command builds a formula making it possible to apply pressure fields to the walls of large tanks within the framework of a seismic verification by an equivalent mechanical analysis according to Eurocode 8. In order to apply this pressure field, this formula must be supplied to AFFE_CHAR_MECA/FORCE_COQUE_FO. 1 Purpose and description The objective of this macro-command is to build a formula making it possible to apply pressure fields to the walls of large tanks within the framework of a seismic verification by an equivalent mechanical analysis according to Eurocode 8. 1.1 Total pressure Equation :eq: eq-ptot gives the expression of this total pressure: P_{totale} = P_{hydro} + \text{sign}(\cos(\theta)) \sqrt{\bigl(\left(P_{ir}+P_{if}\right)^2+P_{c1}^2\bigr)} \pm 0.4 \left(P_{vr} + P_{vf} \right) + P_{slib} where \theta is the azimuth of the point of application of the pressure. According to the Newmark combination chosen, \pm becomes + , which is the combination "PC+", or - , which is the combination "PC-" of the keyword NEWMARK. 1.2 Hydrostatic pressure P_{hydro} The hydrostatic pressure is given by: P_{hydro} = \rho_l g \left( H-z\right) where \rho_l is the mass density of the water, g is the acceleration of gravity, H the height of water in the tank and z the distance from the point to the bottom of the tank. 1.3 Rigid impulsive pressure P_{ir} The rigid impulsive pressure is given by: P_{ir} = c_0(z)\rho_l H ZPA_h \cos(\theta) where ZPA_h is the zero-period acceleration read on the input spectrum in one of the horizontal directions and c_0(z) = \frac{8}{\pi^2} \sum^{\infty}_{n=0} \frac{(-1)^n}{(2n+1)^2} \varepsilon_n \cos \Bigl( (2n+1) \frac{\pi}{2} \frac{z}{H} \Bigr) with \varepsilon_n = \frac{I_1\biggl[(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{R}{H} \biggr]} { I'_1\biggl[(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{R}{H} \biggr] } I_1 denotes the modified Bessel function of the first order and I'_1 its first derivative. R is the radius of the tank. When building the formula one limits oneself to the first 20 terms in the expression of c_0 . 1.4 Flexible impulsive pressure P_{if} The flexible impulsive pressure is given by: P_{if} = \rho_l H \cos(\theta) \Psi(z) \sum^{\infty}_{n=0} d_n \cos\biggl((2n+1) \frac{\pi}{2} \frac{z}{H} \biggr) \left(Sa(f_{hfh})-ZPA_h\right) where Sa(f_{hfh}) is the acceleration read on the input spectrum in one of the horizontal directions at the impulsive frequency of mode n (spectrum at 4%) and \Psi(z) = \frac {\int_{0}^{H} \sin\biggl(\frac{z\pi}{2H}\biggr) \Biggl[\frac{\rho_s t(z)}{\rho_l H} + \sum^{\infty}_{n=0} b'_n \cos\biggl((2n+1) \frac{z\pi}{2H} \biggr) \Biggr]dz } {\int_{0}^{H} \sin\biggl(\frac{z\pi}{2H}\biggr) \Biggl[\frac{\rho_s t(z)}{\rho_l H} \sin\biggl(\frac{z\pi}{2H}\biggr) + \sum^{\infty}_{n=0} d_n \cos\biggl((2n+1) \frac{z\pi}{2H} \biggr) \Biggr]dz } with \rho_s the mass density of the steel, t the thickness of the shell wall at the point of application and b'_n = \frac{8}{\pi^2} \frac{(-1)^n}{(2n+1)^2} \varepsilon_n d_n = \frac{4}{\pi} \frac{ \frac{1}{H} \int_{0}^{H} \sin\biggl(\frac{z\pi}{2H}\biggr) \cos\biggl((2n+1) \frac{z\pi}{2H} \biggr) dz } {2n+1} \varepsilon_n For the infinite sum of :eq: eq-pif , one limits oneself to the first term (hence the first impulsive mode), which is predominant. 1.5 Convective pressure P_{c1} The convective pressure is given by: P_{c1} = 0.837 \rho_l R \cos(\theta) \frac{\cosh \biggl(\frac{1.841z}{R} \biggr) }{\cosh \biggl(\frac{1.841H}{R} \biggr) } Sa(f_{c1}) where Sa(f_{c1}) is the acceleration read on the input spectrum in one of the horizontal directions at the convective frequency of mode 1 (take the spectrum at 0.5%). 1.6 Rigid vertical pressure P_{vr} The rigid vertical pressure is given by: P_{vr} = \rho_l ZPA_v (H-z) where ZPA_v denotes the zero-period acceleration of the input spectrum in the vertical direction. 1.7 Flexible vertical pressure P_{vf} The rigid vertical pressure is given by: P_{vf} = 0.815 f \rho_l H \cos\biggl(\frac{z\pi}{2H}\biggr) \Bigl( Sa(f_{vf}) - ZPA_v \Bigr) ZPA_v with: f = 1.078 + 0.274 \ln \biggl(\frac{H}{R}\biggr) \text{ si } 0.8< \frac{H}{R} f = 1 \text{ sinon} Sa(f_{vf}) denotes the acceleration read on the input spectrum in the vertical direction at the vertical impulsive frequency (spectrum at 4%). 1.8 Free-surface pressure P_{slib} This pressure is supplied directly by the user and is added to the total pressure. It represents the pressure above the water height. For a point of the shell wall situated above the water height, the total pressure is equal to the free-surface pressure. 1.9 Computation of the pressures on the bottom of the tank Let r be the radius, in cylindrical coordinates, of the point of application of the pressure. The hydrostatic and vertical pressures have no dependence on r . 1.9.1 Adaptation of the rigid impulsive pressure In order to take into account the radius r smaller than the radius R of the tank on the bottom, one modifies the expression of \varepsilon_n (present in equation :eq: eq-c0 ) into \varepsilon_n(r) . :eq: eq-epsn then becomes: \varepsilon_n({\color{red}{r}}) = \frac{I_1\biggl[(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{\color{red}{r}}{H} \biggr]} { I'_1\biggl[(2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{R}{H} \biggr] } 1.9.2 Adaptation of the flexible impulsive pressure Taking the radius of the point of application into account is done by postulating a linear dependence. One therefore adds the factor r/R to equation :eq: eq-pif , which gives: P^{r}_{if}(r) = \frac{r}{R} P_{if} 1.9.3 Adaptation of the convective pressure Taking the radius of the point of application into account is done by adding a factor using the first Bessel function J_1 . Equation :eq: eq-pc1 becomes in this case: P_{c1} = 0.837 \rho_l R \cos(\theta) \frac{\cosh \biggl(\frac{1.841z}{R} \biggr) }{\cosh \biggl(\frac{1.841H}{R} \biggr) } Sa(f_{c1}) {\color{red}\frac{J_1 \bigl(1.841\frac{ r}{R} \bigr) }{J_1(1.841)}} 1.9.4 Non-flat bottoms The use of the formula created on a tank with a non-flat bottom is not forbidden, but no specific account has been taken of it and no validation of this type of use has been carried out. 1.10 Use of the formula produced The formula created is intended to be supplied to AFFE_CHAR_MECA/FORCE_COQUE_FO. One must then supply a CARA_ELEM for the thickness and a CHAM_MATER for the mass density of the material constituting the tank. This formula can also be evaluated directly for the purposes of tests or checks. One must then call the formula with 5 parameters: first the 3 coordinates of the point of application, then the thickness of the tank at that point and finally the mass density of the material at that point. The formula will produce an error message if: - the coordinate z of the point to be evaluated is less than Z_FOND (see Operands) - the radius r of the point to be evaluated exceeds RAYON by more than 1%. In the other cases, a result will be obtained; the user must therefore make sure that the mesh does indeed correspond to the geometry of the tank defined. In practice, one uses in every case the formulae adapted for the bottom, because one does not know a priori whether the point to be evaluated belongs to the shell walls or to the bottom of the tank. But this amounts to the same thing when r is equal to or very close to R . 2 Syntax formule = DEFI_PRES_EC8( ◆ Z_FOND = float, ◆ RAYON = float, ◆ HAUT_EAU = float, ◆ RHO_EAU = float, ◆ ACCE_SP_H = float, ◆ ACCE_FLEX_H_N = float, ◆ ACCE_FLEX_V = float, ◆ ACCE_SP_V = float, ◆ ACCE_CONV_H = float, ◇ GRAVITE = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ PRES_SURF_LIBR = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ NEWMARK = / "PC+" (par défaut), / "PC-", ◇ EVAL = _F( ◆ RHO = float, ◆ / LIST_H = float, / LIST_R_FOND = float, ◆ LIST_EPAIS = float, ◇ THETA = float (défaut: 0.0), ◆ TABLE = co, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands Z_FOND, RAYON, HAUT_EAU and RHO_EAU These four operands make it possible to define the parameters of the tank. The tank necessarily has the Z axis as axis of symmetry. ◆ Z_FOND Z coordinate of the bottom of the tank. ◆ RAYON Radius of the tank. R in the formulae of Purpose and description ◆ HAUT_EAU Height of water inside the tank. H in the formulae. It is indeed a height and not a coordinate. The Z coordinate of the points at the water surface is Z_FOND + HAUT_EAU. ◆ RHO_EAU Mass density of the water or of the liquid inside the tank. \rho_l in the formulae. 3.2 Operands ACCE_SP_H, ACCE_FLEX_H_N, ACCE_FLEX_V, ACCE_SP_V and ACCE_CONV_H These operands make it possible to define the various accelerations. ◆ ACCE_SP_H Zero-period acceleration read on the input spectrum in one of the horizontal directions. ZPA_h in the formulae. ◆ ACCE_FLEX_H_N Acceleration read on the input spectrum in one of the horizontal directions at the impulsive frequency of mode n (spectrum at 4%). Sa(f_{hfh}) in the formulae. ◆ ACCE_FLEX_V Acceleration read on the input spectrum in the vertical direction at the vertical impulsive frequency (spectrum at 4%). Sa(f_{vf}) in the formulae. ◆ ACCE_SP_V Zero-period acceleration read on the input spectrum in the vertical direction. ZPA_v denotes the ◆ ACCE_CONV_H Acceleration read on the input spectrum in one of the horizontal directions at the convective frequency of mode 1 (spectrum at 0.5%). Sa(f_{c1}) in the formulae. 3.3 Operands GRAVITE and PRES_SURF_LIBR ◇ GRAVITE Acceleration of gravity. Zero by default. Makes it possible to take the hydrostatic pressure into account. ◇ PRES_SURF_LIBR Value of the pressure on the free surface. Zero by default. It is added to the total pressure. The only pressure taken into account above the water height. 3.4 Operand NEWMARK ◇ NEWMARK = / "PC+" (par défaut), / "PC-", Makes it possible to choose the Newmark combination. In equation :eq: eq-ptot , \pm is + in the case "PC+" and - in the case "PC-". 3.5 Factor keyword EVAL Once the formula for the total pressure has been created, there is no longer access to the various pressures making up the total pressure. The keyword EVAL makes it possible to evaluate and to store the various pressures as well as the total pressure in a table for a certain number of points of the tank. The evaluation is always carried out on the points of one and the same line, either a vertical line of the shell wall, or a line of the bottom ( theta constant). ◇ EVAL = _F( ◆ RHO = float, ◆ / LIST_H = float, / LIST_R_FOND = float, ◆ LIST_EPAIS = float, ◇ THETA = float (défaut: 0.0), ◆ TABLE = co, ), ◆ RHO Mass density of the tank at the points to be evaluated.
