One does not allow it here to vary according to the points. ◆ / LIST_H List of heights on the vertical line of the shell wall to be evaluated. The bottom of the tank is at height 0. ◆ / LIST_R_FOND List of radii on the horizontal line going from the centre towards a low point of the shell wall. ◆ LIST_EPAIS List of the thicknesses corresponding to the points supplied by LIST_H or LIST_R_FOND ◇ THETA Azimuth of the line to which the evaluated points belong. Zero by default; the points then have for coordinates x and y respectively R and 0, and in the other cases \cos(theta) and \sin(theta) . ◆ TABLE Name of the table in which the various pressures will be stored for each evaluated point.

u4.63.11 Macro-command PROJ_BASE u4.63.11 Macro-command PROJ_BASE 1 Purpose Project assembled matrices and/or vectors onto a modal basis or onto a RITZ basis. The resulting projected matrices and vectors will be used by the analysis algorithms in generalised components (DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for example). This macro-command replaces the following successive commands: - NUME_DDL_GENE U4.65.03 which establishes the numbering of the generalised degrees of freedom, - one or more occurrences of PROJ_MATR_BASE U4.63.12 in order to project one or more assembled matrices, - one or more occurrences of PROJ_VECT_BASE U4.63.13 in order to project one or more assembled vectors. > Table of contents 2 Syntax / matr_asse_gene_c / matr_asse_gene_r / nume_ddl_gene / tran_gene / vect_asse_gene = PROJ_BASE( ◆ BASE = mode_gene / mode_meca, ◇ NB_VECT = int, ◇ STOCKAGE = / "DIAG", / "PLEIN" (par défaut), ◇ NUME_DDL_GENE = co / nume_ddl_gene, ◆ | MATR_ASSE_GENE = _F( ◆ MATRICE = co, ◆ / MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r, / MATR_ASSE_GENE = matr_asse_gene_c / matr_asse_gene_r, ), | VECT_ASSE_GENE = _F( ◆ VECTEUR = co, ◆ TYPE_VECT = / "ACCE", / "DEPL", / "FORC", / "VITE", ◆ / VECT_ASSE = cham_no, / VECT_ASSE_GENE = vect_asse_gene, ), | RESU_GENE = _F( ◆ RESULTAT = co, ◆ TYPE_VECT = / "ACCE", / "DEPL", / "FORC", / "VITE", ◆ RESU = dyna_trans, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand BASE ♦ BASE = ba Concept of type mode_meca or mode_gene (for substructuring), which contains the vectors defining the projection subspace. 3.2 Operand NB_VECT ◊ NB_VECT = nm Number of vectors used in the basis (one takes the first nm). One checks that the number nm is indeed less than the number of vectors of the basis; otherwise, all the vectors supplied are used. 3.3 Operand STOCKAGE ◊ STOCKAGE = /'PLEIN' [DEFAUT] /'DIAG' See NUME_DDL_GENE[U4.65.03]. If one matrix has a profile 'DIAG' and another a profile 'PLEIN', two numberings will be created with NUME_DDL_GENE. The use of the keyword STOCKAGE='DIAG' is legitimate when the basis onto which the matrices are projected is composed of eigenmodes. In this case, the projected matrices are indeed diagonal, and it is not necessary to save the other terms of the matrix, which are zero. Warning, if the basis is composed of other types of vectors (static modes for example), then the use of the keyword STOCKAGE='DIAG' leads to incorrect results. In the case of analyses using the fluid-structure operators, the analysis must be carried out with the diagonal storage option. 3.4 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ◊ NUME_DDL_GENE = /numgen [nume_ddl_gene] /CO('numgen'), [nume_ddl_gene] Numbering associated with the generalised model. This operand may be a concept that already exists or not (CO('numgen')). 3.5 Keyword MATR_ASSE_GENE ◊ MATR_ASSE_GENE Factor keyword defining the name of the resulting projected matrix and the name of the matrix to be projected. This keyword must be repeated as many times as there are matrices to project. 3.5.1 Operand MATRICE ♦ MATRICE = CO('mt') Concept of type matr_asse_gene_r or matr_asse_gene_c, real or complex resulting generalised matrix. 3.5.2 Operands MATR_ASSE / MATR_ASSE_GENE ♦ / MATR_ASSE = ma Concept of type matr_asse_depl_r or matr_asse_depl_c, real or complex assembled matrix that one wishes to project. / MATR_ASSE_GENE = ma Concept of type matr_asse_gene_r or matr_asse_gene_c, real or complex assembled matrix, coming from substructuring, that one wishes to project. 3.6 Keyword VECT_ASSE_GENE ◊ VECT_ASSE_GENE Factor keyword defining the name of the resulting projected vector and the name of the vector to be projected. This keyword must be repeated as many times as there are vectors to project. 3.6.1 Operand VECTEUR ♦ VECTEUR = CO('vt') Concept of type vect_asse_gene, resulting generalised vector. 3.6.2 Operand TYPE_VECT ♦ TYPE_VECT = typ Character string describing the type of the field represented by the assembled vector. The available values are 'FORC', 'DEPL', 'VITE' and 'ACCE'. The processing differs according to whether one uses the option FORC or the others. - With the option FORC, one carries out the simple projection {\Phi}^{T}f , where \Phi is the modal basis and f the force, - With the other options, one computes by an inverse problem the modal participation coefficients associated with a given displacement. One assumes that the displacement x can be written in the form x={\eta}^{T}\Phi . One then computes \eta ={\Phi}^{T}{({\Phi}^{T}\Phi )}^{-1}x (Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse). 3.6.3 Operands VECT_ASSE / VECT_ASSE_GENE ♦ / VECT_ASSE = va Concept of type cham_no_DEPL_R, assembled vector that one wishes to project. / VECT_ASSE_GENE = va Concept of type vect_asse_gene, assembled vector coming from substructuring, that one wishes to project. 3.7 Keyword RESU_GENE ◊ VECT_ASSE_GENE Makes it possible to project a result data structure of type dyna_trans (coming from a linear dynamic analysis, or from the reading of a data file). This keyword must be repeated as many times as there are vectors to project. 3.7.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = CO('res') Concept of type resu_gene, resulting generalised vector. 3.7.2 Operand TYPE_VECT ♦ TYPE_VECT = typ Character string describing the type of the field represented by the assembled vector. The available values are 'FORC', 'DEPL', 'VITE' and 'ACCE'. The processing differs according to whether one uses the option FORC or the others. - With the option FORC, one carries out the simple projection {\Phi}^{T}f , where \Phi is the modal basis and f the force, - With the other options, one computes by an inverse problem the modal participation coefficients associated with a given displacement. One assumes that the displacement x can be written in the form x={\eta}^{T}\Phi . One then computes \eta ={\Phi}^{T}{({\Phi}^{T}\Phi )}^{-1}x (Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse). 3.7.3 Operands RESU ♦ / RESU = res Concept of type dyna_trans, result data structure that one wishes to project. 3.8 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 [DEFAUT] / 2 Level of information printout for the command NUME_DDL_GENE (see U4.65.03). 4 Example of use # dynamique transitoire sur base modale système masse et ressort PROJ_BASE( BASE=MODES, MATR_ASSE_GENE=( _F(MATRICE = CO(’MASSEGEN’), MATR_ASSE = MATRMASS), _F(MATRICE = CO(’RIGIDGEN’), MATR_ASSE = MATRRIGI), _F(MATRICE = CO(’AMORTGEN’), MATR_ASSE = MATRAMOR, STOCKAGE = 'PLEIN')), VECT_ASSE_GENE= _F(VECTEUR = CO(’EFFOGENE’), VECT_ASSE = VECTASS) ) );

u4.63.12 Operator PROJ_MATR_BASE u4.63.12 Operator PROJ_MATR_BASE 1 Purpose Project an assembled matrix onto a basis of mechanical eigenmodes or a RITZ basis. The resulting projected matrix will be used by the analysis algorithms in generalised components (DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 for example). One may use PROJ_BASE U4.63.11 to process several matrices simultaneously. Produces a generalised-matrix concept of type matr_asse_gene_R if the assembled matrix to be projected is of type matr_asse_depl_R or of type matr_asse_gene_R. Produces a generalised-matrix concept of type matr_asse_gene_C if the assembled matrix to be projected is of type matr_asse_depl_C or of type matr_asse_gene_C. 2 Syntax / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_gene_c = PROJ_MATR_BASE( ◆ BASE = mode_gene / mode_meca, ◆ NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◆ / MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r, / MATR_ASSE_GENE = matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_gene_c, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand BASE ♦ BASE = ba Concept of type mode_meca or mode_gene (for substructuring) which contains the vectors defining the projection subspace. 3.2 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ♦ NUME_DDL_GENE = nu_gene Numbering associated with the generalised model. 3.3 Operands MATR_ASSE / MATR_ASSE_GENE ♦ / MATR_ASSE = ma Concept of type matr_asse_DEPL_R or matr_asse_DEPL_C, assembled matrix that one wishes to project. / MATR_ASSE_GENE = ma Concept of type matr_asse_gene_R or matr_asse_gene_C, assembled matrix coming from substructuring, that one wishes to project.

u4.63.13 Operator PROJ_VECT_BASE u4.63.13 Operator PROJ_VECT_BASE 1 Purpose Project an assembled vector onto a basis of mechanical eigenmodes or a Ritz basis. The projected vector may be used by the analysis algorithms in generalised components. One may use PROJ_BASE U4.63.11 for these projections. Produces a concept of type vect_asse_gene. 2 Syntax vect_asse_gene = PROJ_VECT_BASE( ◆ BASE = mode_gene / mode_meca, ◆ NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◆ TYPE_VECT = / "FORC", / "DEPL", / "VITE", / "ACCE", ◆ / VECT_ASSE = cham_no, / VECT_ASSE_GENE = vect_asse_gene, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand BASE ♦ BASE= ba Concept of type mode_meca or mode_gene for substructuring which contains the vectors defining the projection subspace. 3.2 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ♦ NUME_DDL_GENE = nu_gene Numbering associated with the generalised model. 3.3 Operands VECT_ASSE / VECT_ASSE_GENE ♦ / VECT_ASSE= va Concept of type cham_no_DEPL_R , assembled vector that one wishes to project. / VECT_ASSE_GENE = va Concept of type vect_asse_gene, assembled vector coming from substructuring, that one wishes to project. 3.4 Operand TYPE_VECT ♦ TYPE_VECT = /'FORC', /'DEPL', /'VITE', /'ACCE', Character string describing the type of the field represented by the assembled vector. The available values are 'FORC', 'DEPL', 'VITE' and 'ACCE'. The processing differs according to whether one uses the option FORC or the others. - With the option FORC, one carries out the simple projection {\Phi}^{T}f , where \Phi is the modal basis and f the force. - With the other options, one computes by an inverse problem the modal participation coefficients associated with a given displacement. One assumes that the displacement x can be written in the form x={\eta}^{T}\Phi . One then computes \eta ={\Phi}^{T}{({\Phi}^{T}\Phi )}^{-1}x (use of the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse).

u4.63.14 Operator PROJ_SPEC_BASE u4.63.14 Operator PROJ_SPEC_BASE 1 Purpose Project one or more turbulence spectra onto one (or more) modal basis (bases). The spectra are defined by the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31. The modal basis (or bases) may be defined by: - a concept of type melasflu produced by the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02, - a concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator CALC_MODES U4.52.02, - a list of concepts of type cham_no_depl_r corresponding to the mode shapes. Makes it possible to compute, for each modal basis defined, an interspectral matrix of generalised excitations. An option makes it possible, where applicable, to compute only the auto-spectra. The concept produced is of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = PROJ_SPEC_BASE( ◆ SPEC_TURB = spectre, ◇ TOUT_CMP = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◆ / BASE_ELAS_FLUI = melasflu, / MODE_MECA = mode_meca, / CHAM_NO = cham_no, # Si: exists("BASE_ELAS_FLUI") ◆ VITE_FLUI = float, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◆ FREQ_INIT = float, ◆ FREQ_FIN = float, ◆ NB_POIN = int, ◇ OPTION = / "TOUT" (par défaut), / "DIAG", ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ & MODELE_INTERFACE = modele, ◇ VECT_X = float, ◇ VECT_Y = float, ◇ ORIG_AXE = float, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand SPEC_TURB ♦ SPEC_TURB= l_spec List of concepts of type spectre produced by the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31 defining several turbulent excitation spectra. Notes: 1. The operand SPEC_TURB makes it possible to take into account several turbulent excitation spectra. The interspectra of generalised excitations are computed for each of the physical spectra supplied and are then added. 2. Turbulence spectra of "correlation length" type apply only to the tubes of steam generators. It is possible to project several turbulence spectra of "correlation length" type simultaneously, but the excitation zones of each spectrum must be strictly disjoint from one another. The zones over which these excitations apply are defined for each spectrum, with the command DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31. 3. Turbulence spectra of "correlation length" type cannot be combined with spectra of another type. 4. In the case of a spectrum of type SPEC_CORR_CONV_3 , the double projection is very resource-intensive, because one must loop over the directions, the mesh cells, their Gauss points and the modes (double loop), and each time evaluate the analytical function which defined the spectrum. It is advisable to use this type of spectrum on reduced meshes (fewer than 1000 degrees of freedom), starting with a small number of frequency-discretisation points in order to assess the analysis time. 3.2 Operand BASE_ELAS_FLUI The operand BASE_ELAS_FLUI is used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_LONG_COR_n, SPEC_FONC_FORME or SPEC_EXCI_POINT of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31. In this case, one must supply the fluid velocity vitefl. ♦ / BASE_ELAS_FLUI= baseflui Concept of type melasflu produced by the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02, which defines one modal basis or a set of modal bases onto which the spectra are projected, as well as the discretisation in velocity. The operator computes an interspectral matrix of generalised excitations {S}_{\mathrm{fifj}}^{k}(\omega ) corresponding to the fluid velocity vitefl which one must supply. The concept melasflu also supplies the name of the concept type_flui_stru produced at the beginning of the study by the command DEFI_FLUI_STRU U4.25.01. The concept type_flui_stru contains all the information characteristic of the configuration studied: one finds there, among other things, the data necessary for the dimensionalisation of the projected excitation. 3.3 Keyword VITE_FLUI The operand VITE_FLUI must be supplied if one uses a basis of type melasflu. ♦ VITE_FLUI = vitefl Fluid flow velocity for the response analysis. 3.4 Keyword PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = prec Precision on the fluid flow velocity (by default 1.E-3). 3.5 Operands MODE_MECA or CHAM_NO The operands MODE_MECA or CHAM_NO are used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a pressure spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_CORR_CONV_n of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31. / MODE_MECA= basemeca Concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator CALC_MODES U4.52.02, which defines the modal basis onto which the spectra are projected. This modal basis may have been computed taking into account an added fluid-mass effect, by recourse to the operator CALC_MATR_AJOU U4.66.01 or MACRO_MATR_AJOU U4.66.11. / CHAM_NO= l_cham List of concepts of type cham_no_depl_r, which define the mode shapes of the modal basis onto which the spectra are projected. This way of defining the modal basis makes it possible to impose on the structure a particular type of motion; a similar approach is adopted in the operator CALC_MATR_AJOU U4.66.01, where the operand CHAM_NO also appears. Note: | The operator determines the mutual-acceptance matrix relating the pressure spectrum to the interspectral matrix of generalised excitations acting on the structure: {S}_{\mathit{fifj}}(\omega )={S}_{p}(\omega )\times {J}_{\mathit{Aij}}(\omega ) where {S}_{p}(\omega ) is the pressure power spectral density, {J}_{\mathit{Aij}}(\omega ) is the mutual-acceptance matrix, {S}_{\mathit{fifj}}(\omega ) is the matrix of interspectra of generalised excitations. | | --- | Note: | In the case where the modal basis is defined by a list of fields at the nodes (keyword CHAM_NO ), it is imperative to supply the mechanical model associated with the elements on which the projection of the spectrum must be applied (by the keyword MODELE_INTERFACE ). If a modal basis of type mode_meca is given and if the structure is modelled with thin shells of type DKT , it is not mandatory to supply the keyword MODELE_INTERFACE . | | --- | The theoretical details are given in the internal report HP-51/97/027/B. 3.6 Operand MODELE_INTERFACE The operand MODELE_INTERFACE is used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a pressure spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_CORR_CONV_n of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31. ◊ MODELE_INTERFACE= modele Concept of type modele produced by the operator AFFE_MODELE U4.41.01, defining: 1. Either the (thermal) interface model between the structure and the fluid used beforehand for the computation of the added matrices by CALC_MATR_AJOU U4.66.01 or MACRO_MATR_AJOU U4.66.11. 2. Or the mechanical model of the structure if the latter is modelled by thin shell elements (DKT). Note: In the case where a thermal interface model is defined, the computation of the acceptance coefficients is carried out with the aid of this model, which characterises the wetted surface of the structure, under the assumption of a homogeneous turbulence over the whole fluid-structure interface. In the case where the model given is mechanical, the acceptance coefficients may be computed on the structure, provided that the latter is modelled with thin shells of type DKT. If the keyword MODELE_INTERFACE is not supplied, the mechanical model used is the one which is associated with the stiffness matrix, referenced in the modal projection basis. Note: In the case where the spectrum has been defined analytically with the option SPEC_CORR_CONV_3, the interface model must mandatorily be supplied, because the projection is carried out using the shape functions carried by the elements of the model. 3.7 Operand GROUP_MA / TOUT The operand GROUP_MA is used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a pressure spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_CORR_CONV_n of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31. ♦ GROUP_MA/TOUT List of mesh-cell groups or the whole of the mesh, on which the projection will be carried out. The mesh-cell groups must belong to the mesh associated with the model (thermal or mechanical) used for the computation of the acceptance coefficients. 3.8 Operand VECT_X The operand VECT_X is used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a pressure spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_CORR_CONV_n of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31, in the case where the CORCOS or AU_YANG correlations are used. ◊ VECT_X= l_cmpx List of three components of a unit vector x defining: - the direction of the flow on the surface of the plane structure, in the case of a CORCOS correlation, - the direction of the axis of revolution of the cylindrical structure of circular cross-section, in the case of an AU_YANG correlation. (see the diagrams below) 3.9 Operand VECT_Y The operand VECT_Y is used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a pressure spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_CORR_CONV_n of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31, in the case where the CORCOS correlation is used. ◊ VECT_Y= l_cmpy List of the three components of a unit vector y defining the direction orthogonal to the direction of the flow on the surface of the plane structure (see the diagrams below). 3.10 Operand ORIG_AXE The operand ORIG_AXE is used when one wishes to carry out the projection of a pressure spectrum defined by one of the factor keywords SPEC_CORR_CONV_n of the operator DEFI_SPEC_TURB U4.44.31, in the case where the AU_YANG correlation is used. ◊ ORIG_AXE= l_coor List of the three coordinates defining the position of an origin O on the axis of revolution of the cylindrical structure of circular cross-section (see the diagrams below). 3.11 Operands FREQ_INIT, FREQ_FIN and NB_POIN ♦ FREQ_INIT= fi ♦ FREQ_FIN= ff ♦ NB_POIN= np These operands define the frequency band and the number of frequency-discretisation points of the interspectra to be computed. The number of discretisation points must be equal to a power of 2, in order to allow post-processings of FFT type (Fast Fourier Transform). It is recommended to compute these three quantities according to the following method. If ({f}_{1}^{k},\mathrm{...},{f}_{N}^{k}) denote the frequencies of the modes of the k -th basis of the structure then: \text{FREQ\_INIT}=\underset{k}{\min}(\frac{{f}_{1}^{k}}{2}) \text{FREQ\_FIN}=\underset{k}{max}({f}_{N}^{k}+\frac{{f}_{1}^{k}}{2}) The number of discretisation points can then be deduced from the minimum frequency step defined by: \mathit{df}=\underset{i,k}{min}(2\times \pi \times {\mu}_{i}^{k}\times {f}_{i}^{k}) where {\mu}_{i}^{k} denotes the reduced damping of the i -th mode of the k -th modal basis. 3.12 Operand TOUT_CMP ◊ TOUT_CMP= ’OUI’ ou ’NON’ Indicator of the components of the modal mode shapes that one adopts in order to compute the excitation interspectra on a modal basis: | ’OUI’ | one uses the three translational components, | | --- | --- | | ’NON’ | one uses only the translational component which was defined beforehand by means of the operator DEFI_FLUI_STRU. | 3.13 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION= ’TOUT’ ou ’DIAG’ Indicator of the choice of the computation to be carried out: | ’TOUT’ | if one wishes to compute all the interspectra of generalised excitations (default option), | | --- | --- | | ’DIAG’ | if one wishes to compute only the auto-spectra of generalised excitations. | 3.14 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre Argument of text type defining the title attached to the output concept interspectre.

u4.63.22 Operator REST_SPEC_PHYS u4.63.22 Operator REST_SPEC_PHYS 1 Purpose Compute the response of a structure in the physical basis. The analysis is carried out from a modal-response interspectrum, at certain selected nodes of the mesh. The operator carries out the computation, with four variants, of the response spectra in the physical basis. The user may choose a response in displacements, velocities, accelerations and, under certain conditions, in generalised forces, stresses or nodal forces. The result produced is a concept of type interspectre. 2 Syntax interspectre = REST_SPEC_PHYS( ◆ | BASE_ELAS_FLUI = melasflu, | MODE_MECA = mode_meca, # Si: exists("BASE_ELAS_FLUI") ◆ VITE_FLUI = float, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ BANDE = float, ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ TOUT_ORDRE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◆ INTE_SPEC_GENE = interspectre, ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "VITE", / "ACCE", / "EFGE_ELNO", / "SIPO_ELNO", / "SIGM_ELNO", / "FORC_NODA", ◇ MODE_STAT = mode_meca, ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◆ | GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ), ◇ MOUVEMENT = / "RELATIF", / "ABSOLU" (par défaut), / "DIFFERENTIEL", ◇ OPTION = / "DIAG_TOUT", / "DIAG_DIAG" (par défaut), / "TOUT_TOUT", / "TOUT_DIAG", ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand BASE_ELAS_FLUI BASE_ELAS_FLUI = baseflui Concept of type melasflu produced by the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02, which defines a set of modal bases associated with the various flow velocities of the fluid. The modal response of the structure for a flow velocity considered is decomposed on the basis corresponding to this velocity. One must then specify the fluid velocity vitefl for which one wants to carry out the analysis. 3.1.1 Keyword VITE_FLUI The operand VITE_FLUI must be supplied if one uses a basis of type melasflu. ♦ VITE_FLUI = vitefl Fluid flow velocity for the response analysis. 3.1.2 Keyword PRECISION ◊ PRECISION = prec Precision on the fluid flow velocity (by default 1.E-3). 3.2 Operand MODE_MECA MODE_MECA = base This operand makes it possible to define the basis on which the modal response is decomposed. Concepts of type mode_meca produced by the operators CALC_MODES U4.52.02 or DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02 are accepted. Note: The operands BASE_ELAS_FLUI and MODE_MECA may be used simultaneously in the case where one wishes to compute a stress response of a beam structure subjected to the action of a flow. This analysis case is determined by the supply of a concept of type melasflu under the operand BASE_ELAS_FLUI, defining the modal bases of the structure at the various flow velocities, and the choice of the physical response field 'SIPO_ELNO' under the operand NOM_CHAM. The complementary supply of a concept of type mode_meca under the operand MODE_MECA then becomes mandatory, in order to define the field of the modal stresses at the nodes of the structure. The modal stresses are computed upstream by the operator CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04, option 'SIPO_ELNO', with the aid of the normalised modal mode shapes. The operator NORM_MODE U4.52.11 makes it possible to carry out beforehand the normalisation of the modal mode shapes. 3.3 Operands NUME_ORDRE, TOUT_ORDRE and BANDE These operands must be used only in the case where the basis on which the modal response is decomposed is defined by a concept of type mode_meca. ◊ / NUME_ORDRE = l_nuor List of the order numbers of the modes which are actually taken into account for the computation of the physical response. ◊ / TOUT_ORDRE = / ’NON’, [DEFAUT] / ’OUI’, If one wishes to take all the modes of the basis for the computation of the physical response, one may choose TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' instead of giving the list. / BANDE = (f1, f2) The modes which are taken into account for the computation of the physical response are the modes of the concept of type mode_meca whose frequency lies in the band defined by (f1 f2). 3.4 Operand INTE_SPEC_GENE ♦ INTE_SPEC_GENE = repmoda Concept of type interspectre produced by the operator DYNA_SPEC_MODAL U4.53.23 or DYNA_ALEA_MODAL U4.53.22, which defines the modal-response interspectra, i.e. the interspectra of generalised displacements. 3.5 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO = l_gr_no_rep, [l_gr_no] List of the node groups of the mesh where the physical-response interspectra are computed. If the keyword GROUP_NO is supplied, the length of the list of nodes must be equal to that of the list of components to be recovered (keyword NOM_CMP). If several components are to be recovered and the keyword GROUP_NO is supplied, it is imperative to have as many node groups as components; each group must contain a single node. If one component is to be recovered for several nodes, it is possible to supply under the keyword GROUP_NO one or more groups of as many nodes as required; it is therefore no longer required in this case that the groups contain a single node. 3.6 Operand GROUP_MA ◊ GROUP_MA = l_gr_ma_rep, [l_gr_ma] List of the mesh-cell groups of the mesh where the physical-response interspectra are computed, in the case where the response field is an element field (XXXX_ELNO). The list of mesh cells must be consistent, in length and in order, with respect to the list of node groups supplied by the user under the keyword GROUP_NO. Note: In the case of a fluid-structure interaction analysis, that is if the keyword BASE_ELAS_FLUI is supplied, the keyword GROUP_MA is not taken into account and the quantities recovered at a node from the element fields (type ELNO) are in reality only the arithmetic means of the field values on the mesh cells in the neighbourhood of this node. 3.7 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM = ’DEPL’ ou ’VITE’ ou ’ACCE’ ou ’EFGE_ELNO’ ou ’SIPO_ELNO’ ou ’SIGM_ELNO’ ou ’FORC_NODA’ Name of the physical response field to be computed. Note: The choice of the physical response field 'SIPO_ELNO' for a beam structure under flow requires the simultaneous use of the operands BASE_ELAS_FLUI and MODE_MECA (cf [§3.1]). 3.8 Operand NOM_CMP ♦ NOM_CMP = ’DX’ ou ’DY’ ou ’DZ’ ou ’SMFY’ ou ’SMFZ’ Names of the components of the physical response field which are actually to be computed. Note: The components 'DX', 'DY', and 'DZ' are valid for the fields 'DEPL', 'VITE' or 'ACCE'. The components 'SMFY' and 'SMFZ' are valid for the field 'SIPO_ELNO'. 3.9 Operand MODE_STAT ◊ MODE_STAT = modestat Concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14, which defines the static modes taken into account in the case of a multi-support seismic analysis where the excitation is applied on the degrees of freedom. 3.10 Keyword EXCIT ◊ EXCIT Factor keyword making it possible to define the degrees of freedom on which the excitation is applied, in the case of a multi-support seismic analysis. ♦ GROUP_NO = l_grno List of the node groups where the excitation is applied. ♦ NOM_CMP = l_ncmp List of the components on which the excitation is applied. Note: These components must correspond to degrees of freedom of the support nodes. Example: 'PRES', 'DRZ', 'PHI',... In every case, there must be as many arguments under the operand GROUP_NO as under the operand NOM_CMP. For fluid sources, it is the component 'PRES' which is excited. 3.11 Operand MOUVEMENT ◊ MOUVEMENT = 'ABSOLU' ou 'RELATIF' ou 'DIFFERENTIEL' Indicator characterising the physical response to be computed, in the case of a multi-support seismic analysis: absolute response ('ABSOLU') by default, dynamic contribution ('RELATIF') or differential contribution ('DIFFERENTIEL') of the response. 3.12 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION = 'DIAG_DIAG' ou 'DIAG_TOUT' ou 'TOUT_DIAG' ou 'TOUT_TOUT' Indicator specifying the choice of the computation to be carried out: - computation of the auto-spectra at the nodes by means of the modal auto-spectra; - computation of the auto-spectra at the nodes by means of all the modal interspectra; - computation of all the interspectra at the nodes by means of the modal auto-spectra; - computation of all the interspectra at the nodes by means of all the modal interspectra. Note: In the case where the modal response has been computed by DYNA_SPEC_MODAL U4.53.23, the choice of computation must be consistent with the one retained upstream in this operator. Indeed, the options 'DIAG_TOUT' or 'TOUT_TOUT' cannot be executed if one has chosen 'DIAG' in DYNA_SPEC_MODAL U4.53.23. The default choice is therefore 'DIAG_DIAG', which corresponds to the simplest analysis case that can be carried out whatever the choice retained upstream. 3.13 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Argument of text type defining the title attached to the output concept interspectre.

u4.63.31 Operator REST_GENE_PHYS u4.63.31 Operator REST_GENE_PHYS 1 Purpose Recover in the physical basis results in generalised coordinates. This operator makes it possible to recover in the physical space results obtained on a system in generalised coordinates by modal recombination methods. The concept produced is a concept of type: - dyna_trans if the generalised results come from an analysis by modal recombination or following the extrapolation of experimental measurement results onto a numerical model (the input concept is of type tran_gene), - mode_meca for the recovery following a modal analysis with projection onto a modal basis (the input concept is of type mode_gene), - dyna_harmo for the recovery following a harmonic analysis with projection onto a modal basis, without substructuring (the input concept is of type harm_gene). 2 Syntax / dyna_harmo / dyna_trans / mode_meca = REST_GENE_PHYS( ◆ RESU_GENE = harm_gene / mode_gene / mode_meca / tran_gene, ◇ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◇ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◇ / TOUT_INST = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / INST = list[float], / LIST_INST = listr8, / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = list[int], / NUME_MODE = list[int], ◇ / FREQ = list[float], / LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, # Si: exists("RESU_GENE") ◇ ENVELOPPE = / "NORME_MOMENT", / "VALE_ABS", ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ / MULT_APPUI = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / CORR_STAT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ / ACCE_MONO_APPUI = list[fonction / formule / nappe], ◇ / GROUP_NO = list[grno], ◇ / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◇ TOUT_CHAM = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), # Si: not exists("TOUT_CHAM") ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "ACCE" (par défaut), / "ACCE_ABSOLU", / "DEPL", / "EFGE_ELNO", / "FORC_NODA", / "SIGM_ELNO", / "SIPO_ELNO", / "VITE", ◇ & DIRECTION = list[float], ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESU_GENE ♦ RESU_GENE = tg | :14: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type tran_gene containing, for various time instants, generalised vectors of type displacement, velocity and acceleration. If the results come from the extrapolation of measurement results onto a numerical model (command PROJ_MESU_MODAL), the generalised vectors are of type displacement, strain and stress. In this case, the recombination basis is of type mode_meca. | | --- | --- | | :14: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type mode_gene containing the generalised vectors of the modes computed following a projection onto a modal basis. | | :14: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type harm_gene containing the generalised vectors of type displacement, velocity and acceleration of the harmonic response of a structure computed after a projection onto a modal basis | 3.2 Operand MODE_MECA ◊ MODE_MECA = mode Concept of type mode_meca containing a basis of eigenmodes obtained by dynamic substructuring. This operand is used in the case of a recovery in the physical system of a transient-analysis result carried out on a modal basis computed by dynamic substructuring. The modal basis contained in the concept mode_meca was obtained by the command REST_SOUS_STRUC U4.63.32. It is therefore a double recovery, after having carried out a double projection (cf. example in [§4]). 3.3 Operand NUME_DDL ◊ NUME_DDL = numeddl Concept of type nume_ddl containing a numbering corresponding to a reduced model in the case of an analysis with dynamic condensation when the user wishes a recovery on the degrees of freedom belonging to this reduced model. This operand thus makes it possible to obtain, following the recovery, a concept mode_meca which could be used subsequently for an analysis on the reduced model (see the test case SDNV107A for an example). 3.4 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / TOUT_INST / LIST_INST / INST ◊ / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' In order to recover on all the modes of the concept mode_gene. / NUME_ORDRE = num List of integers containing the order numbers of the modes on which the recovery is carried out. / NUME_MODE = num List of integers containing the numbers of the modes in the global spectrum on which the recovery is carried out. / TOUT_INST = 'OUI' If one wishes to recover on all the time instants contained in the generalised result (tran_gene). / LIST_INST = list List of increasing reals of type listr8 containing the time instants for which one wishes to carry out the recovery. / INST = inst List of reals containing the time instants on which the recovery is carried out. For a transient analysis, one checks that the time instants requested by the option LIST_INST do indeed lie in the domain of definition of the tran_gene. The results at an arbitrary time instant may be obtained by linear interpolation between the results at two analysis time instants actually contained in the tran_gene. 3.5 Operands FREQ / LIST_FREQ These operands are used in the case of a recovery on the physical basis of generalised harmonic analyses (harm_gene). / FREQ = freq Frequency at which one wishes to recover the harmonic analysis / LIST_FREQ = list List of reals containing the frequencies for which one wishes to carry out the recovery. For each frequency indicated, one recovers the fields obtained at the nearest analysis frequency. There is no interpolation. 3.6 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM ◊ / TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI' Makes it possible to recover the fields of symbolic name DEPL, VITE and ACCE contained in the generalised result (tran_gene, harm_gene). / NOM_CHAM = nomcha List of the symbolic names of the fields that one wishes to recover: 'DEPL', 'VITE', 'ACCE' and, if they have been computed, 'ACCE_ABSOLU', 'EFGE_ELNO', 'SIPO_ELNO', 'SIGM_ELNO' or 'FORC_NODA'. The recovery of the fields 'EFGE_ELNO', 'SIPO_ELNO', 'SIGM_ELNO' and 'FORC_NODA' is possible in the multi-support case. 3.7 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL = | 'LIN' | an interpolation is allowed between two time instants; this interpolation can be used only between two analysis time instants, but may lead to errors if the two archiving time instants U4.53.03 are separated by a time which is very long with respect to the periods of the phenomena studied. | | --- | --- | | 'NON' | the recovery must be carried out stricto sensu. | 3.8 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ PRECISION = prec ◊ CRITERE = When INTERPOL is 'NON', indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be recovered must be carried out | 'ABSOLU' | search interval [Inst - prec, Inst +prec], | | --- | --- | | 'RELATIF' | search interval [(1 - prec).Inst, (1 + prec) .Inst] Inst being the recovery time instant. | 3.9 Operand MULT_APPUI After the transient analysis of the generalised seismic response of a structure, the user must indicate 'OUI' under the keyword MULT_APPUI in order to recover the absolute displacements (and/or velocities and/or accelerations). If nothing is specified, the operator recovers the relative quantities. Note: If the transient analysis of the generalised seismic response of a structure is carried out in the TRAN_GENE option of CALC_MISS, the result is directly absolute without specifying MULT_APPUI='OUI', because the loading comes directly from the seismic soil forces computed by MISS. 3.10 Operands ACCE_MONO_APPUI and DIRECTION ◊ | ACCE_MONO_APPUI = (gamma1, gamma2, gamma3), [fonction] | DIRECTION = (dx1, dy1, dz1, dx2, dy2, dz2, dx3, dy3, dz3), [l_R] After the analysis of the generalised seismic response of a singly excited structure, the user indicates the name of the imposed accelerograms (keyword ACCE_MONO_APPUI) and the directions of the earthquake (keyword DIRECTION) in order to recover the absolute accelerations (accelerations only, which will be stored in the field ACCE_ABSOLU). If nothing is specified, the operator recovers the relative quantities. The field ACCE_ABSOLU will then be absent. Note: It is possible to impose up to 3 accelerograms under the keyword ACCE_MONO_APPUI. They must be the same as those imposed under the keyword FONC_MULT of the factor keyword EXCIT of the command DYNA_VIBRA. If the transient analysis of the generalised seismic response of a structure is carried out in the TRAN_GENE option of CALC_MISS, the result is directly absolute without specifying ACCE_MONO_APPUI and DIRECTION, because the loading comes directly from the seismic soil forces computed by MISS. 3.11 Operand CORR_STAT After the transient analysis of the generalised seismic response of a structure, provided that the user has requested 'CORR_STAT' = 'OUI' in DYNA_VIBRA, the displacements (and/or velocities and/or accelerations) can then be recovered with correction, by the static modes, of the truncation of the modal basis. The user must indicate 'OUI' under the keyword CORR_STAT. If nothing is specified, the operator recovers the quantities without static correction. 3.12 Operand GROUP_NO ◊ / GROUP_NO = lgrno / GROUP_MA = lgrma After a transient dynamic analysis on a modal basis, the user may recover kinematic fields on only part of the nodes or mesh cells of the mesh. List of the node/mesh-cell groups corresponding to the locations where the user wants to recover kinematic fields. 3.13 Operand ENVELOPPE ◊ ENVELOPPE = "VALE_ABS" / "MOMENT_NORM" This operand makes it possible to compute the envelopes of the various fields over time: ACCE , VITE , DEPL , EFGE_ELNO and REAC_NODA , using one of the following options: | Option | Description | | --- | --- | | VALE_ABS | Computes the maximum of the components from their absolute values: for each scalar component x_i(t) , one retains \max_t \|x_i(t)\| . | | | | | NORME_MOMENT | Similar to VALE_ABS , except for the computation of the envelope of the moment components. In this case, the envelope is determined from the resultant norm of the moment. Formally, if \mathbf{M}(t) = (M_x(t), M_y(t), M_z(t)) , one defines the norm of the moment as \\|\mathbf{M}(t)\\| = \sqrt{M_x(t)^2 + M_y(t)^2 + M_z(t)^2} . The time instant corresponding to the maximum norm is t^ = \arg\max_t \\|\mathbf{M}(t)\\| . The envelope values are then given by \mathbf{M}^ = \mathbf{M}(t^ ) . In other words, the envelope corresponds to the components of the moment at the time instant at which the resultant moment is the most intense. | 3.14 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 4 Example: Recovery of a transient-analysis result carried out on a modal basis computed by dynamic substructuring: double recovery Modal analysis on a generalised model: (\bar{\text{K}}-\bar{\text{M}}{\omega}^{2})\eta =0 with \bar{\text{K}}=(\begin{array}{ccc}{\bar{\text{K}}}_{1}& & \\ & {\bar{\text{K}}}_{2}& \\ & & \ddots \end{array}) and \bar{\text{M}}=(\begin{array}{ccc}{\bar{\text{M}}}_{1}& & \\ & {\bar{\text{M}}}_{2}& \\ & & \ddots \end{array}) and linking equations \text{L}\eta =0 modgene = CALC_MODES ( MATR_RIGI = :math: \bar{\text{K}} , MATR_MASS = :math: \bar{\text{M}} ) One obtains a generalised modal basis: the eigenmodes of the global structure are linear combinations of the eigenmodes of the substructures: it is onto this generalised modal basis \Phi that one projects the assembled generalised matrices (double projection). \begin{array}{cccc}\overline{\overline{\text{K}}}& =& {\Phi}^{T}\overline{\text{K}}\Phi & \text{opérateur}\text{PROJ\_MATR\_BASE}\\ \overline{\overline{\text{M}}}& =& {\Phi}^{T}\overline{\text{M}}\Phi & \\ \overline{\overline{\text{C}}}& =& {\Phi}^{T}\overline{\text{C}}\Phi & \\ {\overline{\overline{\text{F}}}}_{\mathrm{ext}}& =& {\Phi}^{T}{\overline{\text{F}}}_{\mathrm{ext}}& \text{opérateur}\text{PROJ\_VECT\_BASE}\end{array} Transient analysis on the modal basis \Phi obtained by dynamic substructuring. trangen = DYNA_VIBRA (BASE_CALCUL="GENE", MATR_MASS = :math: \overline{\overline{\text{M}}} , MATR_RIGI = :math: \overline{\overline{\text{K}}} , MATR_AMOR_GENE = :math: \overline{\overline{\text{C}}} , EXCIT = _F(VECT_ASSE_GENE = :math: {\overline{\overline{\text{F}}}}_{\mathrm{ext}} ) ) Recovery of the modal basis \Phi in the initial physical system: modmeca = REST_SOUS_STRUC ( RESU_GENE = modgene, SQUELETTE = squel ) Recovery of the transient analysis in the initial physical system: tran = REST_GENE_PHYS( RESU_GENE = trangen, MODE_MECA = modmeca )

u4.63.32 Operator REST_SOUS_STRUC u4.63.32 Operator REST_SOUS_STRUC 1 Purpose Recover in the physical basis results in generalised coordinates. This operator makes it possible, from results on a system in generalised coordinates obtained by modal recombination methods tran_gene, cyclic substructuring methods mode_cycl, dynamic substructuring mode_gene or harmonic substructuring harm_gene, to recover the results in the initial physical system. The concept produced is a concept of type: - dyna_trans if the generalised results come from an analysis by modal recombination or following the extrapolation of experimental measurement results onto a numerical model (the input concept is of type tran_gene) or following the recovery of a concept dyna_trans on a new visualisation mesh, - mode_meca following an analysis by cyclic substructuring (mode_cycl), by dynamic substructuring (mode_gene) or if the analysis corresponds to the recovery of a concept mode_meca on a new visualisation mesh, - dyna_harmo following an analysis by harmonic substructuring (harm_gene), - evol_noli following a non-linear analysis mixed with a modal analysis on its non-linear part 2 Syntax / dyna_trans / dyna_harmo / evol_noli / mode_meca = REST_SOUS_STRUC( ◆ / RESULTAT = evol_noli / dyna_trans / mode_meca, / RESU_GENE = mode_gene / tran_gene / harm_gene / mode_cycl, ◆ / SQUELETTE = squelette, ◇ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◇ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◇ / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = int, / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, / TOUT_INST = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_MODE = int, / FREQ = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ◇ INTERPOL = / "NON" (par défaut), / "LIN", ◇ TOUT_CHAM = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), # Si: not exists("TOUT_CHAM") ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "VITE", / "ACCE" (par défaut), / "ACCE_ABSOLU", / "EFGE_ELNO", / "SIPO_ELNO", / "SIGM_ELNO", / "FORC_NODA", ◇ / GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ CYCLIQUE = _F( ◇ NB_SECTEUR = int, ◇ NUME_DIAMETRE = int, ◇ RESULTAT2 = evol_char / dyna_trans / evol_noli / evol_elas / mode_meca, ), / SOUS_STRUC = text, / SECTEUR = int, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands RESU_GENE / RESULTAT / RESU_GENE = tg | :12: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type tran_gene containing, for various time instants, generalised vectors of type displacement, velocity and acceleration of the transient response computed by substructuring. | | --- | --- | | | | | :12: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type mode_cycl containing the generalised vectors of the modes computed by cyclic substructuring. | | | | | :12: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type mode_gene containing the generalised vectors of the modes computed by dynamic substructuring. | | | | | :12: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | concept of type harm_gene containing the generalised vectors of type displacement, velocity and acceleration of the harmonic response of a structure computed by substructuring. | / RESULTAT This keyword may be used when one first recovers a result coming from an analysis by dynamic substructuring on a first skeleton (visualisation mesh). One then defines an enriched skeleton in which one has merged the nodes at the interfaces of the substructures and recovered all or part of the node or mesh-cell groups of the initial mesh. The keyword RESULTAT then corresponds to the recovery of a concept mode_meca, dyna_trans, evol_noli on a new enriched skeleton (cf. example in [§4]). 3.2 Operand MODE_MECA ◊ MODE_MECA = mode Concept of type mode_meca containing a basis of eigenmodes obtained by dynamic substructuring. This operand is used in the case of a recovery in the physical system of a transient-analysis result carried out on a modal basis computed by dynamic substructuring. The modal basis contained in the concept mode_meca was obtained by a previous REST_SOUS_STRUC. In this case, one must supply the same recovery support (keyword SQUELETTE or SOUS-STRUC) used for the recovery of the modal basis. 3.3 Operand NUME_DDL ◊ NUME_DDL = numeddl Concept of type nume_ddl containing a numbering corresponding to a reduced model in the case of an analysis with dynamic condensation when the user wishes a recovery on the degrees of freedom belonging to this reduced model. This operand thus makes it possible to obtain, following the recovery, a concept mode_meca which could be used subsequently for an analysis on the model. 3.4 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / TOUT_INST / LIST_INST / INST ◊ / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' In order to recover on all the modes of the concept mode_cycl or mode_gene. / NUME_ORDRE = num List of integers containing the numbers of the modes on which the recovery is carried out. / NUME_MODE = num List of integers containing the numbers of the modes in the global spectrum on which the recovery is carried out. / TOUT_INST = 'OUI' If one wishes to recover on all the time instants contained in the generalised result (tran_gene). / LIST_INST = list List of increasing reals of type listr8 containing the time instants for which one wishes to carry out the recovery. / INST = inst List of reals containing the time instants on which the recovery is carried out. For a transient analysis, one checks that the time instants requested by the option LIST_INST do indeed lie in the domain of definition of the tran_gene. The results at an arbitrary time instant may be obtained by linear interpolation between the results at two analysis time instants actually contained in the tran_gene. 3.5 Operands FREQ / LIST_FREQ These operands are used in the case of a recovery of generalised harmonic analyses (harm_gene). / FREQ = freq Frequency at which one wishes to recover the harmonic analysis / LIST_FREQ = list List of reals containing the frequencies for which one wishes to carry out the recovery. For each frequency indicated, one recovers the fields obtained at the nearest analysis frequency. There is no interpolation. 3.6 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM ◊ / TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI' Makes it possible to recover the fields of symbolic name DEPL, VITE and ACCE contained in the generalised result (tran_gene, harm_gene). / NOM_CHAM = nomcha List of the symbolic names of the fields that one wishes to recover: 'DEPL', 'VITE', 'ACCE'. 3.7 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL = | 'LIN': | an interpolation is allowed between two time instants; this interpolation can be used only between two analysis time instants, but may lead to errors if the two archiving time instants U4.53.03 are separated by a time which is very long with respect to the periods of the phenomena studied. | | --- | --- | | 'NON' : | the recovery must be carried out stricto sensu. | 3.8 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ PRECISION = prec ◊ CRITERE = When INTERPOL is 'NON', indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be recovered must be carried out | 'ABSOLU': 'RELATIF': | search interval [Inst - prec, Inst +prec], search interval [(1 - prec).Inst, (1 + prec) .Inst] Inst being the recovery time instant. | | --- | --- | 3.9 Operand SECTEUR ◊ / SECTEUR Number of the sector of the cyclic structure on which the result (of type mode_cycl) will be recovered in the physical system in cyclic substructuring. 3.10 Operand SQUELETTE / SQUELETTE Name of the skeleton mesh of the global structure on which the result will be recovered: see the operator DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01. 3.11 Operand SOUS_STRUC / SOUS_STRUC = nom_sstruc Name of the substructure on which the result will be recovered: see the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. 3.12 Operand GROUP_NO ◊ / GROUP_NO = lgrno / GROUP_MA = lgrma After a transient dynamic analysis on a modal basis, the user may recover kinematic fields on only part of the nodes or mesh cells of the mesh. List of the node/mesh-cell groups corresponding to the locations where the user wants to recover kinematic fields. 3.13 Operand CYCLIQUE ◊ CYCLIQUE = _F( ◊NB_SECTEUR = ns [I] ◊NUME_DIAMETRE = nl [I] ◊RESULTAT2 = res [evol_elas] [evol_noli] [dyna_trans] [evol_char] [mode_meca] ) The operator DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01 makes it possible to regenerate the complete mesh of a structure with cyclic symmetry from the mesh of one sector of this structure. The option CYCLIQUE in REST_SOUS_STRUC makes it possible to recover on this new skeleton mesh the fields at the nodes computed on the model of the single sector and taking cyclic symmetry into account (with LIAISON_MAIL or LIAISON_CYCL for example). The action of this option of REST_SOUS_STRUC consists in: > 1/ in the static case (a single field at the nodes supplied) rotating this field at the nodes onto the skeleton mesh > 2/ in the dynamic case (2 fields at the nodes supplied, RESULTAT and RESULTAT2) combining the fields at the nodes and rotating them onto the new mesh. 3.14 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 4 Example: Recovery of a mode_meca on an enriched skeleton, use of the keyword RESULTAT An example of use of the keyword RESULTAT is given below. The complete command file corresponds to the test case SDLS106A. First step: computation of the generalised eigenmodes (obtained by dynamic substructuring) of the global structure resgen = CALC_MODES (MATR_RIGI = risgen, MATR_MASS = masgen, OPTION = 'PLUS_PETITE', CALC_FREQ = _F( NMAX_FREQ = 6 ) ) % definition of the first visualisation mesh of the computed quantities squel = DEFI_SQUELETTE (MODELE_GENE = modege, SOUS_STRUC = _F(NOM = 'carre1', TOUT ='OUI' ), SOUS_STRUC = _F(NOM = 'carre2', TOUT ='OUI' ) ) % recovery of the mode_gene on this first skeleton: modglo = REST_SOUS_STRUC (RESU_GENE = resgen, SQUELETTE = squel, TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI') % definition of the enriched skeleton in which one has merged the nodes at the interfaces of the substructures and recovered all or part of the node or mesh-cell groups of the initial mesh: squelbis = DEFI_SQUELETTE (MODELE_GENE = modege, SQUELETTE = squel, RECO_GLOBAL =_F ( TOUT='OUI', DIST_REFE = 0.1)) % recovery of the first mode_meca on the new skeleton: modglbis = REST_SOUS_STRUC (SQUELETTE = squelbis, RESULTAT = modglo)

u4.63.33 Operator REST_COND_TRAN u4.63.33 Operator REST_COND_TRAN 1 Purpose Recover in the physical basis of complete models the results of transient evolutions on condensed models. This operator makes it possible, from results of non-linear transient evolutions on condensed models, to obtain another transient-evolution result on a more complete model. The concept produced is a concept of type dyna_trans in every possible case: - following a non-linear transient analysis evol_noli with solution on a modal projection basis. One then recovers on the complete physical model from this modal basis entered by the keyword BASE_MODALE. - following a linear transient analysis dyna_trans or a non-linear one evol_noli on a mixed model composed of finite elements assigned a possibly non-linear constitutive behaviour and of macro-elements condensing models assigned a linear constitutive behaviour. One then recovers on one of the linear physical models entered by the keyword MACR_ELEM_DYNA. 2 Syntax / dyna_trans / evol_noli = REST_COND_TRAN( ◇ reuse = , ◇ RESULTAT = dyna_trans / evol_noli, ◇ TYPE_RESU = / "DYNA_TRANS" (par défaut), / "EVOL_NOLI", ◇ / BASE_MODALE = mode_meca, / MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macr_elem_dyna, ◇ / TOUT_INST = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = int, / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ◇ INTERPOL = / "LIN", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ TOUT_CHAM = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), # Si: not exists("TOUT_CHAM") ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "ACCE" (par défaut), / "DEPL", / "VITE", # Si: exists("BASE_MODALE") ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ RESU_FINAL = dyna_trans / evol_noli, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = evol Result of a non-linear transient evolution on models with modal condensation making it possible to obtain another transient-evolution result on a more complete model. Product of an analysis carried out by DYNA_VIBRA or DYNA_NON_LINE. 3.2 Operand RESU_FINAL ◊ RESU_FINAL = resphy If this operand is supplied, the evolution of the transient-evolution result on the complete model may be completed by the time instants of the concept entered by the operand RESULTAT and the result concept is then re-entrant. 3.3 Operands BASE_MODALE / MACR_ELEM_DYNA ♦ / BASE_MODALE Concept of type mode_meca containing a basis of projection modes for the solution of a non-linear transient analysis evol_noli with the keyword PROJ_MODAL in DYNA_NON_LINE. One then recovers on the complete physical model from this modal basis entered here by this keyword. An example of recovery of a result dyna_trans is given in the test SDNV107A. One may also complete the result recovered on the complete model in order to obtain a result of type evol_noli: an example is given in the test SDNV107C. / MACR_ELEM_DYNA This keyword makes it possible to introduce the name of a dynamic macro-element computed on a part of the model on which one will proceed to the recovery on the physical basis. Its supply is necessary when this macro-element is used as a super-mesh cell of substructures defined by the keyword AFFE_SOUS_STRUC in the mixed model, which also comprises classical finite elements, on which one has computed the linear or non-linear evolution entered under the keyword RESULTAT. An example is given in the tests MISS06B (non-linear) and MISS06C (iterative linear). 3.4 Operands TYPE_RESU / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM Dans le cas où l'opérande BASE_MODALE est renseigné, il est possible de compléter le résultat restitué sur le modèle complet afin d'obtenir un résultat de type evol_noli. Il faut alors préciser TYPE_RESU='EVOL_NOLI'. Pour calculer les champs 'SIEF_ELGA' et 'VARI_ELGA' sur la partie de modèle linéaire condensé, il est alors nécessaire de préciser les concepts renseignés par les opérandes CHAM_MATER et CARA_ELEM s'ils existent pour le modèle complet. 3.5 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / TOUT_INST / LIST_INST / INST ◊ / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' In order to recover on all the orders of the concept evol. / NUME_ORDRE = num List of integers containing the numbers of the orders on which the recovery is carried out. / TOUT_INST = 'OUI' If one wishes to recover on all the time instants contained in the result evol. > / LIST_INST = list List of increasing reals of type listr8 containing the time instants for which one wishes to carry out the recovery. > / INST = inst List of reals containing the time instants on which the recovery is carried out. For a transient analysis, one checks that the time instants requested by the option LIST_INST do indeed lie in the domain of definition of the result evol. The results at an arbitrary time instant may be obtained by linear interpolation between the results at two analysis time instants actually contained in the result evol. 3.6 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM ◊ / TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI' Makes it possible to recover the fields of symbolic name DEPL, VITE and ACCE contained in the result evol. / NOM_CHAM = nomcha List of the symbolic names of the fields that one wishes to recover: 'DEPL', 'VITE', 'ACCE'. 3.7 Operand INTERPOL ◊ INTERPOL = | 'LIN' : | an interpolation is allowed between two time instants; this interpolation can be used only between two analysis time instants, but may lead to errors if the two archiving time instants U4.53.03 are separated by a time which is very long with respect to the periods of the phenomena studied. | | --- | --- | | 'NON' : | the recovery must be carried out stricto sensu . | 3.8 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ PRECISION = prec ◊ CRITERE = When INTERPOL is 'NON', indicates with what precision the search for the time instant to be recovered must be carried out | 'ABSOLU': 'RELATIF': | search interval [Inst - prec, Inst +prec], search interval [(1 - prec).Inst, (1 + prec) .Inst] Inst being the recovery time instant. | | --- | --- |

u4.63.34 Operator REST_SPEC_TEMP u4.63.34 Operator REST_SPEC_TEMP 1 Purpose Return of result fields, in generalised coordinates or in the physical basis, from the frequency domain to the time domain and conversely, by fast Fourier transform (FFT). This operator makes it possible, from a transient-evolution result on a system in generalised coordinates or in the physical basis, to obtain a frequency-evolution result on the same basis by direct Fourier transformation of each of the transient-evolution functions at each point and each component of the selected kinematic fields (displacements, velocities or accelerations). And conversely, from a frequency-evolution result on a system in generalised coordinates or in the physical basis, one obtains a transient-evolution result on the same basis by inverse Fourier transformation of each of the harmonic-evolution functions at each point and each component of the selected kinematic fields. For each transformed evolution, the operation is analogous to that produced by the call to the operator CALC_FONCTION[U4.32.04] with the keyword FFT. The concept produced is a concept of type: · dyna_trans if the starting result transformed by FFT is of type dyna_harmo, · dyna_harmo if the starting result transformed by FFT is of type dyna_trans, · tran_gene if the starting result transformed by FFT is of type harm_gene, · harm_gene if the starting result transformed by FFT is of type tran_gene. 2 Syntax / tran_gene / dyna_trans / harm_gene / dyna_harmo = REST_SPEC_TEMP( ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◆ / RESU_GENE = tran_gene / harm_gene, / RESULTAT = dyna_trans / dyna_harmo, ◇ METHODE = / "PROL_ZERO" (par défaut), / "TRONCATURE", ◇ SYMETRIE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ TOUT_CHAM = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "VITE", / "ACCE", # Si: equal_to("METHODE",'PROL_ZERO' ) ◆ N_PUIS = int, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands RESU_GENE / RESULTAT ♦/ RESU_GENE= tg This keyword may be used if the concept to be transformed by direct or inverse FFT is a transient evolution result in generalised coordinates of type tran_gene or a frequency evolution result of type harm_gene. / RESULTAT = resu This keyword may be used if the concept to be transformed by direct or inverse FFT is a transient evolution result on the physical basis of type dyna_trans or a frequency evolution result of type dyna_harmo. 3.2 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM ◊/ TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI' Makes it possible to transform by direct or inverse FFT the fields of symbolic name DEPL, VITE and ACCE contained in the generalised result (tran_gene, harm_gene) or on the physical basis (dyna_trans, dyna_harmo). ◊/ NOM_CHAM = nomcha List of the symbolic names of the fields that one wishes to transform by direct or inverse FFT: 'DEPL', 'VITE', 'ACCE'. 3.3 Operand METHODE ◊METHODE = The FFT algorithm accepts as input only a signal whose number of samples, in time or in frequency according to the case, is a power of 2. The method 'PROL_ZERO' (by default) proposes to extend the input signal with zeros until one has a total number of samples which is the first power of 2 whose value is greater than the initial number of samples. The method 'TRONCATURE' will consider only the first samples whose total number is the greatest power of two whose value is less than the initial number of samples. For example, on a signal of 601 values, the method 'PROL_ZERO' will complete the signal in order to have 1024 samples, whereas the method 'TRONCATURE' will consider only the first 512 time instants. If the input signal has a number of samples which is a power of 2, the two methods are obviously equivalent: one takes the signal into account without modifying it. 3.3.1 Operand N_PUIS ◊N_PUIS = n, Keyword which must be specified only in the case where one applies METHODE = 'PROL_ZERO'. This option makes it possible to extend the input signal with zeros until one has a total number of samples which is the first power of 2 whose value is greater than the initial number of samples + N_PUIS. In practice, one may choose any power of 2 in order to complete the signal with zeros. At a minimum, if one wishes to use METHODE = 'PROL_ZERO' in its classical way, one must enter N_PUIS = 0. An example is given in order to show the use of N_PUIS: - One considers a time signal which goes up to {T}_{max}=20.475s with a time step \Delta t=0.005s ; - If one transforms this signal with, for example, CALC_FONCTION (option FFT, method PROL_ZERO) one ends up with a Fourier transform which has a frequency step \Delta f=1/(\Delta t+{T}_{max}) with a maximum frequency {f}_{max}=100\mathit{Hz} ; - Now, if one carries out, for example, a harmonic analysis on the physical basis (with the aid of DYNA_VIBRA) for a number of frequencies greater than 1024 but less than 2048 (while keeping the same frequency step of the Fourier transform), one would have a maximum analysis frequency greater than 50\mathit{Hz} . Then, if one returns to the time domain via the operator REST_SPEC_TEMP, with METHODE = 'PROL_ZERO', one completes up to 2048 frequencies (that is 100 Hz). The Fourier transforms (direct and inverse) therefore have the same normalisation and the analysis is correct; - If, on the other hand, one decides to truncate the harmonic analysis at 30\mathit{Hz} (entirely legitimate for a seismic analysis, for example) one would have a number of frequencies less than 1024 (but greater than 512) and with the PROL_ZERO of REST_SPEC_TEMP one will complete up to 50\mathit{Hz} . The signal at the output of REST_SPEC_TEMP would therefore have a factor of 2 with respect to the correctly normalised solution; - In order to output the correct solution (if one decides to truncate the analysis at 30\mathit{Hz} ) one would have to complete not only up to 1024 but reach 2048. For that, it is therefore enough to add one extra power of 2, that is simply to enter the option N_PUIS = 1. For a concrete example of the use of this keyword, one refers to modelling C of the test case sdls119. 3.4 Operand SYMETRIE ◊SYMETRIE = Keyword which applies only to the inverse Fourier transform (from the frequency domain to the time domain). The (complex) spectrum supplied as input to the inverse FFT must comply with certain rules (in particular in order to recover a real time function): with respect to its mid-point, its real part must be symmetric and its imaginary part antisymmetric. In general, if this spectrum comes from an FFT computation, then these symmetry conditions are satisfied (except for a voluntary truncation). On the other hand if one has only half of the spectrum, then this must be indicated to the FFT computation operator. This information on the symmetry of the spectrum is handled by the keyword SYMETRIE. If the spectrum is complete and therefore satisfies the symmetries, then the user must specify SYMETRIE = 'OUI'. Conversely, if the spectrum is truncated, then one should choose SYMETRIE = 'NON'. The spectrum is then symmetrised: this leads to a multiplication by 2 of its number of samples and therefore of its maximum frequency. Consequently, this operand applies only if the result to be transformed is a generalised frequency evolution (harm_gene) or one on the physical basis (dyna_harmo).

u4.63.35 Operator REST_MODE_NONL u4.63.35 Operator REST_MODE_NONL 1 Purpose The operator REST_MODE_NONL makes it possible to recover, in the time domain or in the Fourier domain, a periodic solution coming from an analysis with MODE_NON_LINE. This operator produces a concept of type dyna_trans (in the time domain) or mode_meca (in the Fourier domain). 2 Syntax / dyna_trans / mode_meca = REST_MODE_NONL( ◆ MODE_NON_LINE = table_container, ◇ TYPE_RESU = / "MODE_MECA", / "DYNA_TRANS" (par défaut), ◆ NUME_ORDRE = int, # Si: equal_to("TYPE_RESU", 'DYNA_TRANS') ◇ NB_INST = int (défaut: 512), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword MODE_NON_LINE ♦ MODE_NON_LINE resu_in is a concept of type table_container coming from an analysis with the operator MODE_NON_LINE. 3.2 Keyword NUME_ORDRE ♦ NUME_ORDRE num_ordr indicates the order number of the periodic solution coming from resu_in that one wishes to recover. 3.3 Keyword TYPE_RESU ◊ TYPE_RESU If TYPE_RESU = 'MODE_MECA' then resu_out is a periodic solution in the Fourier domain. If TYPE_RESU = 'DYNA_TRANS' then resu_out is a periodic solution in the time domain. By default, TYPE_RESU = 'DYNA_TRANS'. 3.4 Keyword NB_INST ◊ NB_INST nb_inst is the desired discretisation of the periodic solution, for a recovery in the time domain (i.e. TYPE_RESU = 'DYNA_TRANS'). Note that nb_inst must be a power of 2. By default, nb_inst = 512.

u4.63.36 Operator POST_GENE_PHYS u4.63.36 Operator POST_GENE_PHYS 1 Purpose Recover in the physical basis part of the results in generalised coordinates. This operator makes it possible to recover in the physical space results obtained on a system in generalised coordinates by modal recombination methods. Unlike the operator REST_GENE_PHYS, this operator makes it possible to limit the recovery by filtering on: - One or more groups/lists of nodes or of mesh cells - One or more fields at the nodes or at the elements, for all the components or only those of interest - A list of order numbers, frequencies, or time instants according to the type of generalised result In addition, the operator automatically takes the static correction into account during the recovery. It also makes it possible to extract absolute displacements and velocities for multi-support systems and to compute the absolute acceleration in the single-support case as well as in the multi-support case. The concept produced is of type table. It may be handled by the classical post-processing operators in Code_Aster (RECU_TABLE, RECU_FONCTION, IMPR_TABLE). 2 Syntax table = POST_GENE_PHYS( ◆ RESU_GENE = tran_gene / harm_gene, ◇ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◆ OBSERVATION = _F( ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "ACCE", / "DEPL_ABSOLU", / "VITE_ABSOLU", / "ACCE_ABSOLU", / "FORC_NODA", / "EFGE_ELNO", / "EGRU_ELNO", / "SIPO_ELNO", / "SIGM_ELNO", / "EFGE_ELGA", / "SIGM_ELGA", ◇ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, / TOUT_INST = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = int, / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / FREQ = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, # Si: (exists("INST")) or (exists("LIST_INST")) or (exists("FREQ")) or (exists("LIST_FREQ")) ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ◆ | GROUP_NO = grno, | GROUP_MA = grma, # Si: (equal_to("NOM_CHAM", 'ACCE_ABSOLU')) ◇ & ACCE_MONO_APPUI = formule / nappe / fonction, & DIRECTION = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESU_GENE ♦ RESU_GENE = res_gen | :14: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | Concept of type tran_gene containing, for various time instants, the generalised vectors of displacements, velocities and accelerations. | | --- | --- | | | | | :14: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short./ | Concept of type harm_gene containing the generalised vectors of displacements, velocities and accelerations of the harmonic response of a structure, computed after projection onto a modal basis. | Note : Recovery of the results by the operator POST_GENE_PHYS is not available for analyses in dynamic substructuring. 3.2 Operand MODE_MECA ◊ MODE_MECA = mode Concept of type mode_meca containing a basis of eigenmodes of the structure. In the absence of this operand, the recovery basis for the modal recombination is retrieved automatically from the generalised result res_gen at the input of the operator. 3.3 Keyword OBSERVATION This factor keyword may be repeated as many times as there are recoveries. For each of the observations, the user is free to choose the name of the field and its components, the order numbers, and the geometric support of the recovery. In the table produced, each occurrence of the keyword OBSERVATION is indexed by the parameter NUME_OBS of the table. 3.3.1 Filtering by the name of the field and its components ♦ NOM_CHAM = / 'DEPL', [DEFAUT] / 'VITE', / 'ACCE', / 'DEPL_ABSOLU', / 'VITE_ABSOLU', / 'ACCE_ABSOLU', / 'FORC_NODA', / 'EFGE_ELNO', / 'EGRU_ELNO', / 'SIPO_ELNO', / 'SIGM_ELNO', / 'EFGE_ELGA', / 'SIGM_ELGA', This keyword defines, for the observation in progress, the name of the field to be recovered. Note that for the force and stress fields, it is up to the user to make sure that these have indeed been computed on the modal projection basis with the operator CALC_CHAMP. Before the analysis, the operator POST_GENE_PHYS checks the existence of these fields in the projection basis. ◊ NOM_CMP = lcomp, [l_K] List of the names of the components of the field to be recovered. This keyword is optional. If it is absent, all the components of the field are retrieved and taken into account. If the user specifies a list of components, the operator POST_GENE_PHYS first checks the existence of these components in the requested field before carrying out the analysis. 3.3.2 Filtering by selection of the geometric support of the recovery ♦ / GROUP_NO = lgrno, [l_noeud] / GROUP_MA = lgrma, [l_gr_ma] It is mandatory to specify one of these 2 keywords. This makes it possible to define the geometric support for the recovery of the requested field (list of the node/mesh-cell groups). Note: For the recovery of an elementary field ( _EL ), it is indispensable to specify the keyword GROUP_MA in order to identify the groups of elements concerned. For a nodal field, the user may define the nodes directly via the keyword GROUP_NO , or specify the mesh cells carrying the nodes of interest for the recovery by means of the keyword GROUP_MA . 3.3.3 Filtering by the order numbers, time instants, or analysis frequencies ◊ / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', [DEFAUT] / NUME_ORDRE = num, [l_I] / TOUT_INST = 'OUI', / INST = inst, [l_R] / LIST_INST = list, listr8 / FREQ = freq, [l_R] / LIST_FREQ = list, listr8 By default, the recovery is carried out on all of the order numbers stored in the result: that is, on all the time instants for a transient analysis, and on all the frequencies for a harmonic analysis. It is possible for the user to limit the recovery to part of the analysis: a list of order numbers (NUME_ORDRE), of time instants (INST, LIST_INST), or of frequencies (FREQ, LIST_FREQ). It is important to note that no interpolation of the results is carried out. The time instants or frequencies requested must necessarily correspond to the time instants or frequencies present in the concept tran_gene or harm_gene supplied as input. The following operands make it possible to adjust the criteria for selecting the time instants or frequencies: ◊ CRITERE = / 'ABSOLU', / 'RELATIF', [DEFAUT] ◊ PRECISION = / prec, [R] / 1.E-06, [DEFAUT] 3.3.4 Taking into account an entrainment acceleration in the single-support case ◊ | ACCE_MONO_APPUI = (gamma1, gamma2, gamma3), [fonction] | DIRECTION = (dx1, dy1, dz1, dx2, dy2, dz2, dx3, dy3, dz3), [l_R] In the single-support case, in order to recover an acceleration in the absolute frame (ACCE_ABSOLU), it is necessary to specify the functions giving the magnitude of the acceleration of the supports as well as the directions of their motion. It is possible to supply up to three directions. Note 1: In the multi-support case, the computation of the absolute displacements, velocities and accelerations requires no additional information. It is enough to specify a NOM_CHAM among DEPL_ABSOLU, VITE_ABSOLU and ACCE_ABSOLU. The information relating to the absolute motions of the supports is already stored in the generalised concept. Note 2: If a static correction of the loadings has previously been taken into account during the analysis on the generalised basis (CORR_STAT = 'OUI' in DYNA_VIBRA), this correction is automatically included in the recoveries of POST_GENE_PHYS. 3.4 Operands TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01.

u4.64.01 Operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA u4.64.01 Operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA 1 Purpose Define the interfaces of a structure and assign a type to them. Used within modal recombination methods, or dynamic substructuring by modal synthesis. It also lists, without computing them (a task carried out by the operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02), the static deflected shapes corresponding to the defined interfaces. Produces a data structure of type interf_dyna_clas. 2 Syntax interf_dyna_clas = DEFI_INTERF_DYNA( ◆ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◆ INTERFACE = _F( ◇ & NOM = text, & TYPE = / "MNEAL", / "CRAIGB", / "CB_HARMO", / "AUCUN", ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ MASQUE = text, ), ◇ FREQ = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NUME_DDL ♦ NUME_DDL = nu Name of the nume_ddl concept of the structure. 3.2 Keyword INTERFACE ♦ INTERFACE Factor keyword for the definition of the interfaces. 3.2.1 Operand NOM ◊ NOM = ’nom_int’ Name of the interface. It is mandatory for each interface . If, for an occurrence of the factor keyword INTERFACE, no name is given, then this occurrence completes the definition of the previously named interface (concatenation of the list of nodes onto those already existing). This makes it possible to use the keyword GROUP_NO for one and the same interface, or else to give different arguments to the keywords MASQUE and DDL_ACTIF within the same interface. 3.2.2 Operand TYPE ◊ TYPE= It makes it possible to specify the kind of modal basis corresponding to the interface. 'MNEAL': Interface corresponding to a modal basis of MAC-NEAL type, which comprises eigenmodes and attachment modes. The attachment modes are counted, at the interface, only on the degrees of freedom that are neither fixed nor masked. 'CRAIGB': Interface corresponding to a modal basis of CRAIG-BAMPTON type, which comprises eigenmodes and constraint modes. The constraint modes are counted, at the interface, only on the degrees of freedom fixed by dualisation and not masked. 'CB_HARMO': Interface corresponding to a modal basis of harmonic CRAIG-BAMPTON type, which comprises eigenmodes and harmonic constraint modes (imposed harmonic unit displacement). The frequency used is that given as the argument of the frequency keyword 'FREQ'. The harmonic constraint modes are counted, at the interface, only on the degrees of freedom fixed by dualisation and not masked. 'AUCUN': Free interface. No static deflected shape will be computed; the modal basis will comprise only eigenmodes. 3.2.3 Operand GROUP_NO ◊ GROUP_NO= ’lgno’ Ordered list of the node groups of the mesh making up the interface.
