The final list of nodes is obtained by the union of the node groups in the order given by the user, when the groups are defined. 3.2.4 Operand MASQUE ◊ MASQUE= ’lddl’ List of the degrees of freedom, for the current nodes, which must not generate static deflected shapes (masked degrees of freedom). 3.3 Operand FREQ ◊ FREQ= val_freq Value of the frequency used for the computation of the harmonic constraint modes. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= Level of information supplied in the file 'MESSAGE': | 1 | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2 | writing of the definitions of the interfaces (kind, nodes), and of the static deflected shapes listed (makes it possible to check the list of the static deflected shapes before their actual computation). | 3.5 Case of a node common to several interfaces When a node is common to several interfaces (for example the centre of a circular structure), this often leads to a singular system in the computation of the eigenmodes of the complete structure. One gets around this problem by eliminating the common node. This of course leads to an error on the global modes, but if the mesh is fine enough it is not noticeable (see the test case SDLS01). 4 Example An example of the use of the command is given in the documentation of the operator DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01.

u4.64.02 Operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE u4.64.02 Operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE 1 Purpose The purpose of the operator is to define: - the basis of a dynamic substructure, when one has split the complete structure into substructures; - or the basis of a modal recombination, when one treats the complete structure directly. The modal basis obtained by this operator is of type: 'CLASSIQUE' if the modal basis is composed of dynamic eigenmodes and of the static deflected shapes computed by the operator from a concept of type interf_dyna_clas produced by DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01. The option DIAG_MASS makes it possible to recompute a numbering for the static modes such that the mass matrix is diagonal. The basis is of RITZ type in the other cases. The operator produces a concept of type mode_meca. 2 Syntax mode_meca = DEFI_BASE_MODALE( ◇ reuse = , ◆ / CLASSIQUE = _F( ◆ INTERF_DYNA = interf_dyna_clas, ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◇ NMAX_MODE = int, ), / RITZ = _F( ◆ / MODE_MECA = mode_meca, / BASE_MODALE = mode_meca, / MODE_INTF = mode_meca / mult_elas, ◇ NMAX_MODE = int, ), / DIAG_MASS = _F( ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◆ MODE_STAT = mode_meca, ), / ORTHO_BASE = _F( ◆ BASE = mode_meca / mult_elas, ◆ MATRICE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_r, ), # Si: exists("RITZ") ◇ INTERF_DYNA = interf_dyna_clas, ◇ NUME_REF = nume_ddl, ◇ ORTHO = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ LIST_AMOR = listr8, # Si: equal_to("ORTHO", 'OUI') ◆ MATRICE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_r, ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "LDLT", / "MULT_FRONT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "METIS", / "PARMETIS", / "PORD", / "PTSCOTCH", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "LAGR2" (par défaut), / "NON", / "OUI", ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "NONSYM", / "SYMDEF", / "SYMGEN", ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO", / "FR" (par défaut), / "FR+", / "FR++", / "LR", / "LR+", / "LR++", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", / "SANS", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 35), ◇ NB_RHS = int (défaut: 1), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: -1.0), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "EVAL", / "IN_CORE", / "OUT_OF_CORE", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'GCPC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ PRE_COND = / "LDLT_DP", / "LDLT_INC" (par défaut), / "LDLT_SP", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int (défaut: 0), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int (défaut: 0), # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "IN_CORE", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'PETSC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ ALGORITHME = / "CG", / "CR", / "FGMRES" (par défaut), / "GCR", / "GMRES", / "GMRES_LMP", ◇ OPTION_PETSC = text (défaut: ""), ◇ PRE_COND = / "BLOC_LAGR", / "BOOMER", / "FIELDSPLIT", / "GAMG", / "HPDDM", / "JACOBI", / "LDLT_DP", / "LDLT_INC", / "LDLT_SP" (par défaut), / "ML", / "SANS", / "SOR", / "UTILISATEUR", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int (défaut: 0), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int (défaut: 0), ◇ REMPLISSAGE = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), / "SANS", ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "IN_CORE", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float (défaut: 0.0), # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = int, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "RCMK", / "SANS" (par défaut), ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Factor keyword CLASSIQUE ♦ / CLASSIQUE = _F( Factor keyword for the definition of a modal basis of type 'CLASSIQUE', when one carries out an analysis by dynamic substructuring. 3.1.1 Operand INTERF_DYNA ♦ INTERF_DYNA = intdyn Name of the concept of type interf_dyna_clas produced by DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01. The operator computes the static deflected shapes corresponding to the various defined interfaces, relying on the numbering used for the computation of the eigenmodes. 3.1.2 Operands MODE_MECA / NMAX_MODE ◊ MODE_MECA = modes List of the concepts of type mode_meca containing the eigenmodes of the structure. ◊ NMAX_MODE = nbmodes List of integers giving, for each mode_meca concept, the maximum number of eigenmodes to retain. Starting from the i-th modal basis of the list modes, one then retains the modes corresponding to the nbmodes[i] lowest frequencies. In general, the length of the list of integers supplied under the keyword NMAX_MODE must correspond to that of the list of modal bases (keyword MODE_MECA). The only exception to this rule is when a single value is given in NMAX_MODE. In that case, the value of NMAX_MODE is used for each of the modal bases. If NMAX_MODE is not supplied, one takes by default all the modes of each of the modal bases given under the keyword MODE_MECA. 3.2 Factor keyword RITZ ♦ / RITZ = _F( Factor keyword making it possible: - in the case of an analysis by substructuring, to build a substructure modal basis of type 'RITZ'; - in the case of an analysis carried out directly on the complete structure, to build an enriched modal basis (for example: vibration eigenmodes, which one enriches with static modes associated with external forces). The basis is constituted in two different ways: either from two occurrences of the keyword RITZ (one with the keyword MODE_MECA or BASE_MODALE, and another necessarily with the keyword MODE_INTF; the other possibilities are not allowed); or from a single occurrence of the keyword RITZ, in which case only the keyword MODE_MECA is accepted (little used, except possibly to reduce the number of modes or to change the reference numbering). 3.2.1 Keyword MODE_MECA Name of the concept of type mode_meca containing the vibration eigenmodes of the structure, or of the substructure in the case of an analysis by substructuring. It may be used alone, or in the presence of a second occurrence of RITZ with the keyword MODE_INTF (if one wishes to add interface modes, for example). One may give a list of mode_meca obtained for the same structure (with different boundary conditions, for example). 3.2.2 Keyword MODE_INTF Name of the concept of type mode_meca (produced by CALC_MODES U4.52.02 or by MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14) or mult_elas (produced by MACRO_ELAS_MULT U4.51.02) containing: - in the case of an analysis by substructuring: the modes that one wants to use as interface modes of the substructure; - in the case of an analysis carried out directly on the complete structure: modes which enrich the basis of vibration eigenmodes given under the preceding keyword MODE_MECA. These may, for example, be static deflected shapes associated with external forces (a known imposed force; an impact force associated with an obstacle; etc.). It can be used only in the presence of a second occurrence of the keyword RITZ which will contain the keyword MODE_MECA or BASE_MODALE (even if one has to set NMAX_MODE to zero if, for example, one does not wish to take this keyword into account). 3.2.3 Keyword BASE_MODALE Name of the concept of type mode_meca produced by a previous call of the operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02. It can be entered only when the number of occurrences of the keyword RITZ is equal to two. The other occurrence of the keyword RITZ will then necessarily contain the keyword MODE_INTF (in order to enrich an existing basis). The name of the resulting mode_meca concept of the operator may be different from this one, or identical (it is then re-entrant). 3.2.4 Operand NMAX_MODE Number of modes to retain among the dynamic (or static) modes given by one of the preceding keywords under the occurrence of the keyword RITZ. If one supplies a list of mode_meca, one must give either a list of the same length for the numbers of modes to retain, or a single value (in that case, this value is applied to all the mode_meca concepts). If NMAX_MODE is not supplied, one takes by default all the modes. 3.2.5 Operand INTERF_DYNA Dynamic interface of the substructure (to be supplied if necessary, and only if one uses the factor keyword 'RITZ'). 3.2.6 Operand NUME_REF Reference numbering onto which all the displacement fields (dynamic and static modes) constituting the 'RITZ' basis will be reordered. 3.2.7 Operand LIST_AMOR List of the modal dampings that the user may supply in order to enrich the modes declared under the keyword MODE_MECA. This amounts to adding reduced dampings for these same modes even if, originally, they are real modes. This option is useful for simulating experimental results. 3.2.8 Operand ORTHO Operand making it possible to carry out an orthonormalisation of the Ritz basis (to be supplied if one wishes this re-orthonormalisation, and only if one uses the factor keyword 'RITZ'). This orthonormalisation is performed with an iterative Gram-Schmidt algorithm (IGS) following the Kahan-Parlett version. 3.2.9 Keyword MATRICE Name of the concept of type matr_asse_ which will be taken into account for the scalar products during the re-orthonormalisation of the RITZ basis. This keyword is mandatory if ORTHO='OUI'. 3.3 Factor keyword DIAG_MASS ♦ / DIAG_MASS = _F( Keyword making it possible to recompute the static modes by eliminating the dynamic contribution and by carrying out a Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation. 3.3.1 Keyword MODE_MECA Name of the concept of type mode_meca containing the dynamic eigenmodes of the substructure being treated. 3.3.2 Keyword MODE_STAT Name of the concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14 which contains the static modes. 3.4 Factor keyword ORTHO_BASE ♦ / ORTHO_BASE = _F( Keyword making it possible to orthonormalise the modes of a basis. This orthonormalisation is performed with an iterative Gram-Schmidt algorithm (IGS) following the Kahan-Parlett version. 3.4.1 Keyword BASE Name of the concept of type mode_meca or mult_elas containing dynamic eigenmodes. 3.4.2 Keyword MATRICE Name of the concept of type matr_asse_ which will be taken into account for the scalar products during the re-orthogonalisation. 3.5 Factor keyword SOLVEUR ◊ SOLVEUR = _F(...) This factor keyword is optional: it makes it possible to choose another solver for the solution of the system. In the case of this command, the syntax of the keyword is restricted to two methods: one may choose between the default method, MULT_FRONT, and the methods LDLT or MUMPS. The syntax being common to several commands, please consult the manual U4.50.01. 3.6 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Title of the concept created. 3.7 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Level of the information supplied in the file MESSAGE: | 1 | no printout; | | --- | --- | | 2 | writing of the general information (upstream concepts, type of basis). | 4 Examples 4.1 Dynamic substructuring The various modellings of the test case SDLS106 present the complete implementation of an analysis by substructuring, with various methods (Craig-Bampton, Mc Neal, compatible meshes or not, etc.). 4.2 Enrichment of a basis of eigenmodes with static modes # calcul des matrices assemblées et de la numérotation des DDL ... # calcul des modes propres de vibration modesvib = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=K_ASSE, MATR_MASS=M_ASSE, CALC_FREQ=_F( NMAX_FREQ = nb_freq) , ); # application d'une force extérieure force = AFFE_CHAR_MECA( MODELE=modele, FORCE_NODALE=_F( NOEUD = 'N11', FX=800., FY = -1000.)); # calcul de la déformée statique associée à cette force extérieure modestat = MODE_STATIQUE( MATR_RIGI=K_ASSE, MATR_MASS=M_ASSE, FORCE_NODALE=_F( NOEUD='N11', AVEC_CMP=('DX','DY') ), ); # construction de la base modale enrichie basemode = DEFI_BASE_MODALE( RITZ =(_F( MODE_MECA=modesvib ), _F( MODE_INTF=modestat ), ), NUME_REF=NUMDDL, ); The test case SDNL104c presents the complete implementation of this technique. Another example is given by the test case SDNL301a, in which the static deflected shapes that enrich the basis of eigenmodes are those linked to external forces generated by shocks.

u4.65.01 Operator MACR_ELEM_DYNA u4.65.01 Operator MACR_ELEM_DYNA 1 Purpose Define a macro-element for dynamic substructuring. Within a transient, modal or harmonic analysis with dynamic substructuring, the operator MACR_ELEM_DYNA projects the stiffness, mass and, possibly, damping matrices (harmonic analysis) onto the modal basis of the substructure defined by DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02, and extracts the connection matrices of the interfaces. The result consists of the projected matrices and of the connection matrices. It may be used several times, with different orientations, in the same model (cf. DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02). It may be printed to a file by the command IMPR_MACR_ELEM U7.04.33. Produces a concept of type macr_elem_dyna. 2 Syntax macr_elem_dyna = MACR_ELEM_DYNA( ◇ reuse = , ◇ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macr_elem_dyna, ◆ BASE_MODALE = mode_meca, / MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ / MODELE_MESURE = _F( ◆ FREQ = float, ◆ MASS_GENE = float, ◇ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ), ◇ / MATR_IMPE = matr_asse_gene_c, ◇ / MATR_MASS = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ / MATR_IMPE_MASS = matr_asse_gene_c, ◇ / MATR_IMPE_RIGI = matr_asse_gene_c, ◇ / MATR_IMPE_AMOR = matr_asse_gene_c, ◇ / MATR_AMOR = matr_asse_depl_r, / AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ / SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, / GROUP_NO = grno, # Si: exists("MATR_IMPE") ◆ FREQ_EXTR = float, ◇ AMOR_SOL = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ MATR_IMPE_INIT = matr_asse_gene_c, ◇ CAS_CHARGE = _F( ◆ NOM_CAS = text, ◆ / VECT_ASSE_GENE = vect_asse_gene, / RESU_GENE = tran_gene, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand BASE_MODALE ♦ BASE_MODALE = bamo Name of the mode_meca concept produced by the operator DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02. 3.2 Operand MACR_ELEM_DYNA ◊ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macro_dyna Name of the dynamic macro-element concept of type macr_elem_dyna, identical to the name of the concept produced. It is therefore re-entrant when it is present. The content of the concept is modified from the data of the operands MATR_IMPE that are present. 3.3 Operand MATR_RIGI ◊ MATR_RIGI = mr Name of the assembled-matrix concept of type matr_asse_DEPL_R or matr_asse_DEPL_C produced by the operator ASSE_MATRICE U4.61.22 or the macro-command ASSEMBLAGE U4.61.21 corresponding to the stiffness matrix of the substructure. 3.4 Operand MATR_MASS ◊ MATR_MASS = mm Name of the assembled-matrix concept of type matr_asse_DEPL_R produced by the operator ASSE_MATRICE U4.61.22 or the macro-command ASSEMBLAGE U4.61.21 corresponding to the mass matrix. These two operands are to be used if one uses the modal basis bamo of type 'RITZ'. 3.5 Operand MATR_AMOR / AMOR_REDUIT ◊ / MATR_AMOR = ma Name of the assembled-matrix concept of type matr_asse_DEPL_R produced by the operator ASSE_MATRICE U4.61.22 or the macro-command ASSEMBLAGE U4.61.21 corresponding to the viscous damping matrix, specific to the macro-element. This damping must be of RAYLEIGH type per element (linear combination of the stiffness and of the mass at the element level) and is therefore defined by the material properties (operator: DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01, operands AMOR_ALPHA and AMOR_BETA). / AMOR_REDUIT = la List of the reduced dampings (percentage of the critical damping) corresponding to each vibration mode of the macro-element. The length of the list is (at most) equal to the number of eigenmodes of the modal basis; if it is smaller, one completes the list with reduced dampings equal to the last term of the list entered by the user. No damping is associated with the static modes. The generalised damping matrix of the macro-element k is therefore an incomplete diagonal ( j index of the eigenmode): {\overline{\mathrm{C}}}^{k}=\left(\begin{array}{cc}\left({\xi}_{j}\right)& (0)\\ (0)& (0)\end{array}\right) 3.6 Operands MATR_IMPE / FREQ_EXTR / AMOR_SOL ◊ MATR_IMPE = mi Name of the assembled-matrix concept of type matr_asse_gene_C produced by the operator LIRE_IMPE_MISS U7.02.32 corresponding to the impedance matrix (dynamic stiffness, strictly speaking) of the soil interface {\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(\mathit{freq}) , which constitutes the macro-element. ♦ FREQ_EXTR = freq Frequency of extraction of the soil-interface impedance matrix \mathrm{mi} {\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(\mathit{freq}) , required for the computation of the radiative soil damping matrix from its imaginary part. ◊ AMOR_SOL = amosol Value of the material reduced damping of the soil, equal to half the hysteretic viscoelastic damping {\xi}_{\mathit{sol}}={\eta}_{\mathit{sol}}/2 , which was used for the computation of the matrix \mathrm{mi} . It serves to distinguish, in the damping coming from the soil domain, the strictly material (viscoelastic) part and the radiative part. If it is non-zero, the matrix corresponding to the radiative part {\mathrm{C}}_{\mathit{imp}} is then expressed such that: 2\pi .\mathit{freq}.{\mathrm{C}}_{\mathit{imp}}=\mathrm{\Im }\left({\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(\mathit{freq})\right)-2{\xi}_{\mathit{sol}.}\mathrm{\Re }\left({\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(\mathit{freq})\right) 3.7 Operand MATR_IMPE_INIT ◊ MATR_IMPE_INIT = mi0 Name of the assembled-matrix concept of type matr_asse_gene_C, {\mathrm{M}}_{i0} , of the same dimension as a mass matrix, produced by the operator LIRE_IMPE_MISS U7.02.32 corresponding to a soil impedance matrix which constitutes the macro-element, extracted at a quasi-zero frequency {\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(0) . In particular, in the cases of soil-structure-fluid interaction with the keyword ISSF='OUI' in the call to LIRE_IMPE_MISS, this makes it possible to extract a mass contribution M such that, in the low-frequency range: {(2\pi .\mathit{freq})}^{2}.{\mathrm{M}}_{i0}=\mathrm{\Re }\left({\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(0)\right)-\mathrm{\Re }\left({\mathrm{M}}_{\mathit{imp}}(\mathit{freq})\right) 3.8 Operands MATR_IMPE_RIGI/MATR_IMPE_AMOR/MATR_IMPE_MASS Names of the assembled-matrix concepts of type matr_asse_gene_C produced by successive calls to the operator LIRE_IMPE_MISS U7.02.32 in order to extract the respective contributions which constitute the macro-element, in stiffness, damping or mass, of a time-domain soil impedance matrix. If at least one of the operands is supplied, without the others being present, then the contributions of the latter to the terms of the macro-element will be filled in and set to 0. An example of use is provided by the test MISS03B V1.10.122. 3.9 Operands GROUP_NO / SANS_GROUP_NO ◊ GROUP_NO = grno Name of the node group comprising the list of the nodes attached to the degrees of freedom of the interface modes by a relation LIAISON_INTERF (or LIAISON_SOLIDE if the dynamic interface is reduced to one node) to the nodes of the physical interface of the part of the model on which one computes the dynamic macro-element. Supplying it is necessary only if this macro-element is used as a super-mesh cell of substructures defined by the keyword AFFE_SOUS_STRUC in a mixed model which also comprises classical finite elements, and in that case only when the nodes of the physical and dynamic interfaces (the latter defined by DEFI_INTERF_DYNA) do not coincide. For example, in the case of the dynamic interface reduced to one node connected by a rigid link to the physical interface. ◊ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno Name of the node group comprising the list of the nodes of the physical interface of the part of the model on which one computes the dynamic macro-element. These nodes are in a direct relation with the nodes attached to the degrees of freedom of the interface modes by a relation LIAISON_INTERF (or LIAISON_SOLIDE if the dynamic interface is reduced to one node). Supplying it is necessary only if this macro-element is used as a super-mesh cell of substructures defined by the keyword AFFE_SOUS_STRUC in a mixed model which also comprises classical finite elements, and in that case only when the nodes of the physical and dynamic interfaces (the latter defined by DEFI_INTERF_DYNA) do not coincide. For example, in the case of the dynamic interface reduced to one node connected by a rigid link to the physical interface. 3.10 Keyword CAS_CHARGE ◊ CAS_CHARGE This factor keyword makes it possible to define a set of named load cases (keyword NOM_CAS). These load cases serve to apply generalised load vectors applied on the part of the model on which one computes the dynamic macro-element, if this macro-element is subsequently used as a super-mesh cell of substructures in a mixed model which also comprises classical finite elements. 3.10.1 Operand NOM_CAS ♦ NOM_CAS = nocas The loading condensed under the name nocas (in quotes) corresponds to the loading defined by the argument VECT_ASSE_GENE or RESU_GENE on the part of the model on which one computes the dynamic macro-element. 3.10.2 Operands VECT_ASSE_GENE / RESU_GENE ♦ VECT_ASSE_GENE = vgen The loading condensed under the name nocas (in quotes) corresponds to the loading defined by the alternative arguments VECT_ASSE_GENE or RESU_GENE. It is obtained by the projection, onto the modal basis bamo defined above, either of an assembled load vector or of a transient right-hand-side force result, applied on the part of the model on which one computes the dynamic macro-element. These two options are tested simultaneously in the test SDNX101B. 3.11 Operand MODELE_MESURE ◊ MODELE_MESURE This factor keyword makes it possible to fill in manually the reduced matrices of the macro-element, using, for example, data coming from measurements (and imported with LIRE_RESU). One must, at a minimum, enter the generalised mass and the eigenfrequencies. One may also supply the list of reduced dampings. The number of data items supplied must be equal to the number of modes of the modal basis on which the macro-element is built. Methodological point: this type of use of MACR_ELEM_DYNA is justified for the use of the structural modification method starting from an experimental model. A presentation of the method is given in U2.07.03. The modal basis used to build the macro-element must be composed only of the eigenmodes of the measured structure , and must not include the static readings at the interface, because these are wrong (because they are not measured and, in the present state of knowledge, not measurable). The test case sdll137e is an example of the implementation of the methodology. 3.11.1 Operand FREQ ♦ FREQ = freq List of the identified eigenfrequencies. 3.11.2 Operand MASS_GENE ♦ MASS_GENE = mass List of the identified generalised masses. 3.11.3 Operand AMOR_REDUIT ♦ AMOR_REDUIT = xsi List of the identified reduced dampings. 4 Example An example of the use of this operator is given in the documentation of the operator DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01.

u4.65.02 Operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE u4.65.02 Operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE 1 Purpose Create the global structure from the substructures in dynamic substructuring (cf R4.06.02). Within an analysis using the dynamic substructuring methods (modal or harmonic analysis), the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE makes it possible to describe the global structure from the macro-elements coming from MACR_ELEM_DYNA U4.65.01 and from the various connections which link the substructures to one another. A macro-element may serve for the definition of several substructures, whatever their orientation in the physical frame, if the coupling is carried out by static modes (option ‘CLASSIQUE’). This possibility makes it possible to take into account the repetition of a component in the global structure. Produces a data structure of type modele_gene. 2 Syntax modele_gene = DEFI_MODELE_GENE( ◆ SOUS_STRUC = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macr_elem_dyna, ◆ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◆ TRANS = float, ), ◆ LIAISON = _F( ◆ SOUS_STRUC_1 = text, ◆ INTERFACE_1 = text, ◆ SOUS_STRUC_2 = text, ◆ INTERFACE_2 = text, ◇ / GROUP_MA_MAIT_1 = grma, / GROUP_MA_MAIT_2 = grma, ◇ OPTION = / "REDUIT", / "CLASSIQUE" (par défaut), ), ◇ VERIF = _F( ◇ STOP_ERREUR = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword SOUS_STRUC ♦ SOUS_STRUC Factor keyword making it possible to define all the substructures which make up the global structure. The definition of a substructure is made by giving its name, the macro-element associated with it, and its orientation in the physical frame. 3.1.1 Operand NOM ♦ NOM = ’nom_sstruc’ Name of 8 characters at most, which will subsequently make it possible to designate the substructure in: - operator: DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02, operands: LIAISON and SOUS_STRUC_1, - operator: DEFI_SQUELETTE U4.24.01, operand: SOUS_STRUC, - operator: ASSE_VECT_GENE U4.65.05, operand: SOUS_STRUC, - operator: REST_SOUS_STRUC U4.63.32, operand: SOUS_STRUC. 3.1.2 Operand MACR_ELEM_DYNA ♦ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macro_dyna Name of the macr_elem_dyna concept coming from the operator MACR_ELEM_DYNA U4.65.01 which designates the condensed model of the substructure. One recalls that a macro-element may serve for the definition of several substructures. 3.1.3 Operand ANGL_NAUT ◊ ANGL_NAUT = angl_naut List of the 3 nautical angles, in degrees, which make it possible to pass from the orientation of the model which gave rise to the macro-element to that of the substructure. One should refer to the operator AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01: Operand ORIENTATION for the definition and the use of the nautical angles. 3.1.4 Operand TRANS ◊ TRANS= trans List of 3 translation components which make it possible to build a new substructure from the model which gave rise to the macro-element, by applying an overall translation. 3.2 Keyword LIAISON ♦ LIAISON Factor keyword making it possible to define all the connection interfaces between substructures. A connection is defined by the names of the two substructures facing each other and, for each of them, the name of the corresponding interface. In the case of a mesh incompatibility between the two substructures facing each other, it is necessary to indicate which of the two will have its interface considered as master (keywords GROUP_MA_MAIT ). The slave nodes which are projected onto the master interface are defined beforehand by DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01. The "joining" of the 2 interfaces will be done by writing linear relations between the degrees of freedom of the 2 faces. Note: It is recommended that, in the case of incompatible interfaces, the master interface be the interface whose discretisation is the coarsest. In the case of the use of classical static modes (as many as there are degrees of freedom), one should therefore use the interface with the smallest number of degrees of freedom as the master interface. In the case of the use of coupling modes, this choice may be more delicate. The choice of the master interface may appreciably affect the quality of the result if the two models have very different discretisations. See the discussion of this subject in section 5.2 . The displacements of the nodes of the slave face will be linked to the displacements of their projections onto the master face. For each node of the slave face, one will write 2 (in 2D) or 3 (in 3D) linear relations. One application of this functionality is, for example, the joining of a mesh formed of linear elements (P1) onto another, quadratic, mesh (P2). In this case it is rather advisable to choose the quadratic face as the "slave" face. It is possible to define a connection by reduced modes (or interface modes) by means of the keyword OPTION. 3.2.1 Operand SOUS_STRUC_1 ♦ SOUS_STRUC_1 = ’nom_sstruc1’ Name of the first of the substructures involved on either side of the connection. It must have been defined beforehand by the keyword: SOUS_STRUC. 3.2.2 Operand INTERFACE_1 ♦ INTERFACE_1 = ’nom_int1’ Name of the interface of the first substructure involved in the connection. It must have been defined beforehand by the operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01 for the macro-element supporting the substructure. Note: In the case of the use of coupling modes (operator MODE_STATIQUE) with the keyword MODE_INTERF, it is indispensable that the dynamic interface be of type CRAIGB. 3.2.3 Operand GROUP_MA_MAIT_1 ◊ GROUP_MA_MAIT_1 = lgma1 This keyword makes it possible to designate the master substructure, independently of the mesh-cell group specified as input. The operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE takes charge of the search for the facing mesh cells in all cases, relying on the definition of the interfaces facing each other (operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA – U4.64.01). If the interface is incompatible, and the keyword is not supplied, it is substructure 1 which is defined as the master. 3.2.4 Operand SOUS_STRUC_2 ♦ SOUS_STRUC_2 = ’nom_sstruc2’ Name of the second of the substructures involved on either side of the connection. It must have been defined beforehand by the keyword SOUS_STRUC. 3.2.5 Operand INTERFACE_2 ♦ INTERFACE_2 = ’nom_int2’ Name of the interface of the second substructure involved in the connection. It must have been defined beforehand by the operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01 for the macro-element supporting the substructure. Note: In the case of the use of coupling modes (operator MODE_STATIQUE) with the keyword MODE_INTERF, it is indispensable that the dynamic interface be of type CRAIGB. 3.2.6 Operand GROUP_MA_MAIT_2 ◊ GROUP_MA_MAIT_2 = lgma2 This keyword makes it possible to designate the master substructure, independently of the mesh-cell group specified as input. The operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE takes charge of the search for the facing mesh cells in all cases, relying on the definition of the interfaces facing each other (operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA – U4.64.01). If the interface is incompatible, and the keyword is not supplied, it is substructure 1 which is defined as the master. 3.2.7 Operand OPTION ◊ OPTION = /'CLASSIQUE', /'REDUIT', Makes it possible to choose between a classical substructuring by static modes (Mac-Neal method, harmonic Craig-Bampton or not) or by interface modes. 3.3 Keyword VERIF ◊ VERIF Factor keyword making it possible to check the consistency of the generalised model: one checks that the connection is compatible with the orientations and the translations assigned to the substructures. The nodes of the two interfaces do not a priori have to be ordered so that they coincide in pairs. If the nodes of the interfaces are not facing each other in pairs, the code detects this state and reorders the nodes so as to put them back facing each other. 3.3.1 Operand STOP_ERREUR Makes it possible to carry out or not the consistency check of the generalised model. 3.3.2 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE Indicates the precision threshold beyond which the connections are incompatible. It is the distance (relative or absolute according to CRITERE) beyond which the connection nodes are considered too far apart to be effectively connected. 3.4 Keyword INFO > Keyword making it possible to specify the printout level. 4 Execution phase The operator carries out a certain number of checks on the consistency of the connections if the connection does not present a mesh incompatibility: - identical number of nodes on either side of the connection, - consistency, at each node, after orientation of the active degrees of freedom on either side of the connection. 5 Matrices and connection conditions computed by DEFI_MODELE_GENE 5.1 In the case of the option 'CLASSIQUE' The operator computes the oriented connection matrices involved in the generalised model: {{L}_{j}^{k}}_{\text{}\mathrm{orientee}}={B}_{j}^{k}{R}^{k}{\Phi}^{k} | where: | | the exponent characterises the substructure, | | --- | --- | --- | | | | the index characterises the connection interface, | | | {B}_{j}^{k} | is the matrix extracting the degrees of freedom of the connection :47: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short., | | | {R}^{k} | is the rotation matrix which makes it possible to pass from the orientation of the model which gave rise to the macro-element to that of the substructure, | | | {\Phi}^{k} | is the column matrix of the eigenvectors of the substructure :60: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short.. | The connection conditions between substructures 1 and 2 being written: {{q}_{j}^{1}}_{\mathrm{orientee}}={{q}_{j}^{2}}_{\mathrm{orientee}} , with {{q}_{j}^{k}}_{\mathrm{orientee}}={{L}_{j}^{k}}_{\mathrm{orientee}}{\eta}^{k} | where: | {q}_{j}^{k} | is the column vector of the physical coordinates of the connection of the substructure :88: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short., | | --- | --- | --- | | | {\eta}^{k} | is the column vector of the generalised coordinates of the substructure :99: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short.. | 5.2 In the case of the option 'REDUIT' The operator computes the oriented connection matrices involved in the generalised model: {{L}_{j}^{k}}_{\text{}\mathrm{orientee}}={B}_{j}^{k}{R}^{k}{\Phi}^{k} | where: | | the exponent characterises the substructure, | | --- | --- | --- | | | | the index characterises the connection interface, | | | {B}_{j}^{k} | is the matrix extracting the degrees of freedom of the connection :146: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short., | | | {R}^{k} | is the rotation matrix which makes it possible to pass from the orientation of the model which gave rise to the macro-element to that of the substructure, | | | {\Phi}^{k} | is the column matrix of the eigenvectors of the substructure :159: (INFO/1) Unexpected possible title overline or transition. Treating it as ordinary text because it's so short.. | In the case of the option ‘REDUIT’, one joins the generalised motions of the two interfaces. One ensures: {[{\Phi}_{\mathrm{esclave}}]}^{T}{{q}_{j}^{1}}_{\mathrm{orientee}}={[{\Phi}_{\mathrm{esclave}}]}^{T}{{q}_{j}^{2}}_{\mathrm{orientee}} , with {{q}_{j}^{k}}_{\mathrm{orientee}}={{L}_{j}^{k}}_{\mathrm{orientee}}{\eta}^{k} Indeed, in the case of the option «CLASSIQUE», the choice of the master and slave degrees of freedom amounts to writing the connection equation in the form {y}_{\mathrm{esclave}}-C{y}_{\mathrm{maître}}=0 , where y corresponds to the degrees of freedom. Now, the use of a space of reduced dimension in order to write the relation amounts to imposing the following constraints: {\Phi}_{\mathrm{esclave}}{q}_{\mathrm{esclave}}-C{\Phi}_{\mathrm{maître}}{q}_{\mathrm{maître}}=0 . One therefore has more equations than unknowns, the number of generalised degrees of freedom {q}_{\mathrm{esclave}} being distinctly smaller than the number of physical degrees of freedom of the interface {y}_{\mathrm{esclave}} . In order to ensure the proper conditioning of the joining conditions, one therefore projects this relation onto the restriction, to the interface, of the modes of the slave substructure, and the relation to be satisfied then becomes: {\Phi}_{\mathrm{esclave}}^{T}{\Phi}_{\mathrm{esclave}}{q}_{\mathrm{esclave}}-{\Phi}_{\mathrm{esclave}}^{T}C{\Phi}_{\mathrm{maître}}{q}_{\mathrm{maître}}=0 The choice of the master substructure therefore governs the quality of the joining in the case of strongly incompatible interfaces. Note: When using the option, particular care must be taken over the choice of the master and slave interfaces, inasmuch as the kinematic relation between the interfaces is written on the physical degrees of freedom, but the relation is then projected onto the modes of the slave interface. If the two modellings are identical (3D–3D, or 2D-2D) and the discretisations are equivalent, then the master interface will be the interface presenting the largest number of modes. In the case of different modellings, one must make sure that one has an equivalent number of interface modes for each of the substructures, ideally slightly fewer for the slave substructure, and choose as the master interface the one presenting the coarsest discretisation. In all cases, pending the development of tools making it possible to assess the quality of the joining, one will have to carry out a visual check of the results.

u4.65.03 Operator NUME_DDL_GENE u4.65.03 Operator NUME_DDL_GENE 1 Purpose Number the degrees of freedom of the global structure from the numbering of the substructures. Within an analysis using the dynamic substructuring methods (modal or harmonic analysis), the operator NUME_DDL_GENE defines the bijection between, on the one hand, the numbers of the generalised degrees of freedom of each substructure and the numbers of the connection degrees of freedom of each connection and, on the other hand, the numbers of the final degrees of freedom (that is, the row or column indices of the generalised matrices). Once the numbering has been carried out, the operator builds, according to the Morse storage mode, the addressing arrays necessary for the effective storage of the terms of the generalised matrices assembled with this numbering. A storage of full "skyline" type or diagonal "skyline" type is possible in order to compute a full added matrix or to solve a transient problem on a modal basis coming from a concept of type mode_meca. Produces a data structure of type nume_ddl_gene. 2 Syntax nume_ddl_gene = NUME_DDL_GENE( ◆ / MODELE_GENE = modele_gene, / BASE = mode_gene / mode_meca, # Si: exists("MODELE_GENE") ◇ STOCKAGE = / "LIGN_CIEL" (par défaut), / "PLEIN", ◇ METHODE = / "INITIAL", / "CLASSIQUE" (par défaut), / "ELIMINE", # Si: exists("BASE") ◇ STOCKAGE = / "DIAG", / "PLEIN" (par défaut), ◇ NB_VECT = int, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE_GENE ◊ MODELE_GENE = mo_gene Name of the concept of type modele_gene produced by the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02 from which the numbering is carried out. 3.2 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE = | /'CLASSIQUE' | Builds a generalised numbering making it possible to take the connection equations into account by the method of double Lagrange multipliers R4.06.02. | | --- | --- | | /'ELIMINE' | Builds a generalised numbering making it possible to take the connection equations into account by the constraint-elimination method R4.06.02. | | --- | --- | | /'INITIAL' | Initialises the numbering for the generalised operators in order to allow the construction of a numbering whose size can be driven from Python. The matrices (built with ASSE_MATR_GENE) and the vectors (built with ASSE_VECT_GENE) are of a suitable size, but initialised to zero. | | --- | --- | 3.3 Storage of the matrices ◊ STOCKAGE = Choice of a storage mode for the matrices that one is going to assemble with this numbering. 3 options are available: | /'LIGN_CIEL' | "skyline" storage by blocks; the assembled matrix will be stored block of columns by block of columns, starting from the 1st term liable to be non-zero for each column. | | --- | --- | In the assembled matrix, a term A(i,j) is liable to be non-zero if and only if the degree of freedom i and the degree of freedom j (respectively the i -th and j -th modes of the global structure) come from the same substructure or are linked by at least one LAGRANGE degree of freedom of two substructures connected by a connection. | /'PLEIN' | 'skyline' storage of the assembled generalised matrices by blocks, but with a full profile (one stores all the elements of the upper triangular part of the matrix). This type of storage must be used if one wants to compute the generalised added matrices (mass, stiffness, damping), which are full, as well as all the generalised matrices to which they are added. For the stiffness and damping matrices, the assembly is always done from a nume_ddl_gene coming from a mode_meca. | | --- | --- | | /'DIAG' | 'skyline' storage of the diagonal terms of the matrices projected onto a modal basis. This type of storage is to be used when the basis onto which one reduces the problem is orthogonal with respect to the matrices used (the mass, stiffness and damping matrices). This storage makes it possible to improve the performance of the computation operators (DYNA_VIBRA, for example). Warning: this can lead to incorrect results if the orthogonality is not satisfied, for example when one uses a modal basis composed of static modes. Indeed, the static modes are not orthogonal to one another. | | --- | --- | 3.4 Operand BASE This operand serves to identify the modal basis onto which one projects the matrices. 3.5 Operand NB_VECT Under this keyword, one expects the number of projection-basis vectors, possibly smaller than the number of modes defined in the basis specified by the keyword BASE. By default, this number is equal to the number of modes of the basis. 4 Execution phase No bandwidth optimisation is carried out during the numbering. The order of appearance of the substructures in the numbering corresponds to the order of their definition in the generalised model (operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE). The user can therefore limit the bandwidth by defining the substructures of the generalised model in a judicious order. The degrees of freedom coming from the double dualisation are then assembled on either side of the generalised degrees of freedom of the second substructure assembled (among the two substructures involved in the connection).

u4.65.04 Operator ASSE_MATR_GENE u4.65.04 Operator ASSE_MATR_GENE 1 Purpose Assemble the global stiffness or mass matrix from the substructures. Within an analysis using the dynamic substructuring methods (modal or harmonic analysis), this operator creates the generalised stiffness or mass matrix, or possibly the damping matrix (harmonic or transient analysis), by assembly of the corresponding generalised matrices of type macr_elem_dyna (cf. operator MACR_ELEM_DYNA U4.65.01) contained in a list defined when the generalised model is created (cf. operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02). The assembled generalised matrix is real, and may be symmetric or non-symmetric. It is built on a numbering of the generalised degrees of freedom and stored via the "skyline" or Morse formats. The addressing arrays are those computed beforehand by the operator NUME_DDL_GENE U4.65.03. The result concept produced by this operator is of type: matr_asse_gene_R. 2 Syntax / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_gene_c = ASSE_MATR_GENE( ◆ NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◇ METHODE = / "CLASSIQUE" (par défaut), / "INITIAL", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'CLASSIQUE') ◆ OPTION = / "RIGI_GENE", / "RIGI_GENE_C", / "MASS_GENE", / "AMOR_GENE", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ♦ NUME_DDL_GENE= nu_gene Name of the nume_ddl_gene concept coming from the operator NUME_DDL_GENE U4.65.03 which defines the numbering of the equations of the assembled generalised system, the storage mode of the coefficients of the assembled generalised matrix, and the generalised model on which the diagonal, or full, assembly operations are carried out. 3.2 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE= ‘CLASSIQUE’ Builds a generalised numbering making it possible to take the connection equations into account by the method of double Lagrange multipliers or by elimination (cf. R4.06.02). The method used is chosen consistently with the method supplied in the operator NUME_DDL_GENE U4.65.03 ◊ METHODE= ‘INITIAL’ Initialises a null matrix of type matr_asse_gene_R which one can fill using Python methods. This method was created for development. 3.3 Operand OPTION ♦ OPTION The option makes it possible to determine the list of macro-elements, contained in the modele_gene concept coming from DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02, to be assembled. It therefore defines the type of the assembled generalised matrix computed by the operator ASSE_MATR_GENE. | ‘RIGI_GENE’: 'RIGI_GENE_C' | computation of the assembled generalised stiffness matrix, including the terms associated with the LAGRANGE multipliers; computation of the complex generalised stiffness matrix, | | --- | --- | | ‘MASS_GENE’: | computation of the assembled generalised mass matrix, | | ‘AMOR_GENE’: | computation of the assembled generalised damping matrix. | 4 Execution phase The terms corresponding to the projected matrices are assembled without processing. On the other hand, the terms corresponding to the dualisation of the connections are the subject of a simple conditioning. They are multiplied by a factor, defined in a unique way, which is such that the maximum absolute value of the dualisation terms is equal to the maximum absolute value of the stiffness terms of the macro-elements (matrices of the projected substructures).

u4.65.05 Operator ASSE_VECT_GENE u4.65.05 Operator ASSE_VECT_GENE 1 Purpose Project the loadings onto the modal basis of a substructure. Within a harmonic analysis using the substructuring methods, the operator ASSE_VECT_GENE projects the loadings of type cham_no_DEPL_R coming from ASSE_VECTEUR U4.61.23 onto the modal basis of the substructure defined by DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02. The generalised vectors thus obtained are assembled from the definition of the generalised model coming from DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. The final assembled generalised vector is built on the numbering of the generalised degrees of freedom established beforehand by the operator NUME_DDL_GENE U4.65.03. The result concept produced by this operator is of type vect_asse_gene. 2 Syntax vect_asse_gene = ASSE_VECT_GENE( ◆ NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◇ METHODE = / "CLASSIQUE" (par défaut), / "INITIAL", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'CLASSIQUE') ◆ CHAR_SOUS_STRUC = _F( ◆ SOUS_STRUC = text, ◆ VECT_ASSE = cham_no, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ♦ NUME_DDL_GENE= nu_gene Name of the nume_ddl_gene concept coming from the operator NUME_DDL_GENE U4.65.03 which defines the numbering of the degrees of freedom to be used for the assembled generalised vector. 3.2 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE= ‘CLASSIQUE’, ‘INITIAL’ Type of method used for the assembly of the matrices. The method ‘INITIAL’ makes it possible to initialise a null vector of type vect_asse_gene which one can fill by Python methods. This method was created for development. 3.3 Keyword CHAR_SOUS_STRUC ♦ CHAR_SOUS_STRUC Factor keyword making it possible to define the loadings applied to the structure. The definition of the loading is made by giving the assembled vector associated with it and the name of the substructure to which it applies. 3.3.1 Operand SOUS_STRUC ♦ SOUS_STRUC= ’nom_sstruc’ Name of the substructure to which the loading is applied. It must have been defined beforehand by the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. 3.3.2 Operand VECT_ASSE ♦ VECT_ASSE= vecas Name of the cham_no_DEPL_R concept coming from ASSE_VECTEUR U4.61.23 which defines the spatial distribution of the loading applied to the substructure.

u4.65.11 Operator CREA_ELEM_SSD u4.65.11 Operator CREA_ELEM_SSD 1 Purpose The purpose of this operator is to make the user's task easier for the creation of a dynamic macro-element. CREA_ELEM_SSD computes the projection-basis vectors, defines the interfaces and creates the dynamic macro-element. It produces a concept of type macr_elem_dyna. The dynamic macro-element created is ready to be assembled with other dynamic macro-elements in order to obtain a generalised model. The creation of this generalised model can be done with the operator ASSE_ELEM_SSD. This operator is not intended to be able to create all the possible macro-elements. It makes it possible to create the standard real macro-elements which correspond to the majority of cases. The basis vectors of these macro-elements are of type CLASSIQUE, or else Ritz basis vectors with interface modes. For particular projection bases, the user is invited to create them manually with the help of the standard operators. 2 Syntax / macr_elem_dyna / nume_ddl = CREA_ELEM_SSD( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ NUME_DDL = co, ◇ CHARGE = char_ther / char_meca / char_acou, ◆ INTERFACE = _F( ◇ & NOM = text, & TYPE = / "MNEAL", / "CRAIGB", / "CB_HARMO", ◆ / GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ FREQ = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ MASQUE = text, ), ◆ BASE_MODALE = _F( ◆ TYPE = / "CLASSIQUE", / "RITZ", #
