Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ⟐ CALC_FREQ = _F( ◇ STOP_ERREUR = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ OPTION = / "PLUS_PETITE" (par défaut), / "BANDE", / "CENTRE", / "SANS", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'PLUS_PETITE') ◇ NMAX_FREQ = int (défaut: 10), # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'CENTRE') ◆ FREQ = float, ◇ AMOR_REDUIT = float, ◇ NMAX_FREQ = int (défaut: 10), # Si: (equal_to("OPTION", 'BANDE')) ◇ NMAX_FREQ = int (défaut: 9999), ◆ FREQ = float, ◇ APPROCHE = / "REEL" (par défaut), / "IMAG", / "COMPLEXE", ◇ DIM_SOUS_ESPACE = int, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Course of the analysis This operator makes it possible to create easily a real dynamic macro-element (without damping) by supplying only the mechanical characteristics of the model and the interfaces associated with the substructure. It chains the following operations: - creation of the stiffness and mass matrices of the substructure, - computation of the normal modes of the substructure, - definition of the interfaces associated with the substructure, - computation of the static modes or of the interface modes, - definition of the projection basis, - computation of the dynamic macro-element. For its implementation, the user may draw inspiration from the modellings «e» and «f» of the test case SDLD106. These modellings correspond respectively to the modellings «b» and «d» of the same test case. 3.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = modele modele: the model which contains the elements constituting the substructure. 3.2 Operand NUME_DDL ◊ NUME_DDL = nu nu: numbering of the degrees of freedom assigned to the substructure. Note: This numbering is necessary if one wants to compute the response of the assembled structure due, for example, to a loading applied to the substructure. One needs the numbering in order to be able to assemble the elementary vector according to the numbering of the degrees of freedom of the substructure. One then writes: NUME_DDL = CO('nume') , where nume designates the numbering that one wishes to give to the degrees of freedom of the substructure. 3.3 Operand CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER = chmat chmat: name of the material field in which the characteristics of the materials are defined. 3.4 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM = carele carele: elementary characteristics of the beam or shell elements, or of the discrete elements, if the substructure contains any. 3.5 Operand CHARGE ◊ CHARGE = chg chg: loading applied to the substructure. 3.6 Keyword INTERFACE The factor keyword INTERFACE makes it possible to define the interface or the interfaces associated with the substructure. The keywords associated with this factor keyword are identical to the factor keyword INTERFACE of the operator DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01. One also enters here the value of the frequency used for the computation of the harmonic constraint modes. The default value for this frequency is equal to 1. One applies the overloading rule. If the value of the frequency differs between the various interfaces, then one informs the user by means of an alarm which specifies the value of the frequency actually taken into account. 3.7 Keyword BASE_MODALE The factor keyword BASE_MODALE makes it possible to specify the type of basis onto which the substructure is projected. 3.7.1 Operand TYPE Cette opérande définit le type de la base de projection. ♦ TYPE= / 'CLASSIQUE' / 'RITZ' A basis of type CLASSIQUE is constituted of normal modes and of constraint modes or of attachment modes, depending on the type of the interface. The computation of the normal modes is done according to the indications supplied in the factor keyword CALC_FREQ. 3.7.2 Operand TYPE_MODE ◊ TYPE_MODE= / 'INTERFACE' [DEFAUT] / 'STATIQUE' The option TYPE = 'RITZ' makes it possible to specify the type of modes to add to the normal modes. The user may choose modes of type STATIQUE (static readings at the degrees of freedom of the interface nodes) or of type INTERFACE (interface modes). For the particular case in which one does not wish to use normal modes, one chooses OPTION = 'SANS' in the keyword CALC_FREQ. 3.7.3 Operand NMAX_MODE_INTF ◊ NMAX_MODE_INTF= / 10 [DEFAUT] > / nmintf NMAX_MODE_INTF corresponds to the number of interface modes to take into account. One considers here the first nmintf interface modes (nmintf > 0). 3.8 Keyword CALC_FREQ This factor keyword makes it possible to choose the frequency content of the normal modes. The operands associated with this factor keyword are identical to those defined for CALC_MODES U4.52.02. A particularity for the option BANDE: the operand FREQ makes it possible to enter a list of frequencies, and one carries out the modal computations on the various intervals of the list. One chooses OPTION = 'SANS' if one does not wish to compute normal modes. The keyword STOP_ERREUR makes it possible to indicate to the operator whether it must stop ('OUI') or continue ('NON') in the case where one of the criteria for checking the quality of the computed modes is not satisfied. This keyword is equivalent to the keyword STOP_ERREUR of the factor keyword VERI_MODE of CALC_MODES. Note: In order not to overload the command, this factor keyword does not make it possible to enter the parameters COEF_DIM_ESPACE , NMAX_ITER_SHIFT , PREC_SHIFT , SEUIL_FREQ and STOP FREQ_VIDE . On the other hand, the user may enter the dimension of the subspace ( DIM_SOUS_ESPACE ) if need be. The values chosen for the computation of the normal modes are the default values of these parameters in CALC_MODES . 3.9 Keyword SOLVEUR Optional keyword, see U4.50.01. 3.10 Operand INFO This operand makes it possible to print more or less information on the macro-element created in the file 'MESSAGE'. 4 Example of use This example is taken from the test case SDLS106e. MACEL1 = CREA_ELEM_SSD( MODELE = MODELE1, CHARGE = CHARGE_1, CHAM_MATER = CHAMAT1, CARA_ELEM = PARAM1, INTERFACE = _F( NOM = 'GAUCHE', TYPE = 'CRAIGB', GROUP_NO = 'GAUCHE', MASQUE = ('DX','DY'),), BASE_MODALE = _F( TYPE = 'RITZ', NMAX_MODE_INTF = 20,), CALC_FREQ = _F(NMAX_FREQ = 6,), )

u4.65.12 Operator ASSE_ELEM_SSD u4.65.12 Operator ASSE_ELEM_SSD 1 Purpose The purpose of this operator is to make the user's task easier for the assembly of the dynamic macro-elements. It chains the following commands: DEFI_MODELE_GENE, NUME_DDL_GENE and ASSE_MATR_GENE. It produces a concept of type modele_gene, and possibly a concept of type nume_ddl_gene and concepts of type matr_asse_gene_r. This operator is limited to the creation of the real generalised matrices. The generalised matrices obtained can be used directly to compute the eigenmodes of the generalised model. 2 Syntax / modele_gene / matr_asse_gene_r / nume_ddl_gene = ASSE_ELEM_SSD( ◆ RESU_ASSE_SSD = _F( ◆ MODELE = co, ◇ & NUME_DDL_GENE = co, & RIGI_GENE = co, ◇ & MASS_GENE = co, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◆ SOUS_STRUC = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macr_elem_dyna, ◇ ANGL_NAUT = float, ◇ TRANS = float, ), ◆ LIAISON = _F( ◆ SOUS_STRUC_1 = text, ◆ INTERFACE_1 = text, ◆ SOUS_STRUC_2 = text, ◆ INTERFACE_2 = text, ◇ / GROUP_MA_MAIT_1 = grma, / GROUP_MA_MAIT_2 = grma, ◇ OPTION = / "REDUIT", / "CLASSIQUE" (par défaut), ), ⟐ VERIF = _F( ◇ STOP_ERREUR = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ), ◇ METHODE = / "CLASSIQUE" (par défaut), / "ELIMINE", ◇ STOCKAGE = / "LIGN_CIEL" (par défaut), / "PLEIN", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Course of the analysis This operator chains the following operations: - definition of the generalised model (DEFI_MODELE_GENE), - numbering of the degrees of freedom of the generalised model (NUME_DDL_GENE), - assembly of the generalised matrices (ASSE_MATR_GENE), It is limited to the creation of the real generalised matrices. For its implementation, the user may draw inspiration from the modellings «e» and «f» of the test case sdls106. These modellings correspond respectively to the modellings «b» and «d» of the same test case. 3.1 Keyword RESU_ASSE_SSD This factor keyword defines the output concepts. 3.1.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = modele modele: generalised model which contains the elements constituting the global structure (assembled substructures). 3.1.2 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ◊ NUME_DDL_GENE = nugene nugene: numbering of the degrees of freedom of the global structure. 3.1.3 Operand RIGI_GENE ◊ RIGI_GENE = rigene rigene: generalised stiffness matrix of the global structure. 3.1.4 Operand MASS_GENE ◊ MASS_GENE = magene magene: generalised mass matrix of the global structure. 3.2 Keyword SOUS_STRUC Each occurrence of this factor keyword makes it possible to define the characteristics of a substructure. The description of the operands associated with this keyword is the same as that of the keyword SOUS_STRUC of the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. Note: By default, one considers that the substructure undergoes neither a translation nor a rotation: TRANS = (0., 0., 0.) and ANGL_NAUT = (0., 0., 0.). 3.3 Keyword LIAISON Each occurrence of this factor keyword makes it possible to define the connection between two substructures. The description of the operands associated with this keyword is the same as that of the keyword LIAISON of the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. Among the operands of this keyword, the operand OPTION makes it possible to choose the type of mode (static modes or interface modes) that one adds in addition to the normal modes. ◊ OPTION / 'CLASSIQUE' : à chaque ddl de l'interface correspond un mode statique de liaison / 'REDUIT' : utilisation des modes d'interface (préalablement calculés avec CREA_ELEM_SSD par exemple) 3.4 Keyword VERIF This keyword makes it possible to check the consistency of the generalised model. The description of the operands associated with this keyword is the same as that of the keyword VERIF of the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. 3.5 Operand METHODE This operand makes it possible to choose the way of numbering the degrees of freedom of the generalised model. Two choices are possible. ◊ METHODE / 'CLASSIQUE' : construit une numérotation des degrés de liberté généralisés permettant la prise en compte des équations de liaisons entre sous-structures par la méthode des doubles multiplicateurs de Lagrange. / 'ELIMINE': construit une numérotation des degrés de liberté généralisés permettant la prise en compte des équations de liaisons par la méthode d'élimination des contraintes sur les variables. 3.6 Operand STOCKAGE This operand makes it possible to choose the storage mode of the assembled matrix or matrices. ◊ STOCKAGE / 'LIGN_CIEL' : mode de stockage de type ligne de ciel / 'PLEIN': on stocke tous les éléments de la partie triangulaire supérieure de la matrice. 3.7 Operand INFO This operand makes it possible to print more or less information on the generalised model created in the file 'MESSAGE'. 4 Example of use This example is taken from the test case sdls106e ASSE_ELEM_SSD( RESU_ASSE_SSD = _F( MODELE = CO('MODEGE'), NUME_DDL_GENE = CO('NUMEGE'), RIGI_GENE = CO('RIGGEN'), MASS_GENE = CO('MASGEN'), ), SOUS_STRUC = ( _F(NOM = 'CARRE1', MACR_ELEM_DYNA = MACEL1,), _F(NOM = 'CARRE2', MACR_ELEM_DYNA = MACEL2, TRANS = (0.,0.5,0.), ANGL_NAUT = (-90.,0.,0.),), ), LIAISON = ( _F(SOUS_STRUC_1 = 'CARRE1', INTERFACE_1 = 'GAUCHE', GROUP_MA_MAIT_1 = 'CALCUL', OPTION = 'REDUIT', SOUS_STRUC_2 = 'CARRE2', INTERFACE_2 = 'BLOQUE',), ), VERIF = _F( STOP_ERREUR = 'OUI', PRECISION = 1.E-6, CRITERE = 'RELATIF'), METHODE = 'ELIMINE', ),

u4.66.01 Operator CALC_MATR_AJOU u4.66.01 Operator CALC_MATR_AJOU 1 Purpose Compute added mass R4.07.03, damping or stiffness matrices. The matrices are induced by a perfect, incompressible fluid, at rest or in potential flow, on a structure in 2D, axisymmetric 2D or in 3D. The terms of these matrices are computed on the modal basis of the structure in vacuum. The computation of the terms of the matrices is carried out by solving the LAPLACE equations within the framework of a thermal analogy . The computed temperature plays the role of a pressure in the fluid domain. One must therefore take care to define the fluid material by thermal characteristics, and to assign a thermal model to the part of the mesh which represents the fluid. Thanks to this operator, one can determine, for example, the added matrices of a bundle of tubes, considered as a single structure immersed in one and the same fluid. Within an analysis by dynamic substructuring, it is also possible to evaluate the added mass matrix on a generalised model. For systematic uses of this command, and in order to simplify the writing of the command file, one will efficiently use the macro-command MACRO_MATR_AJOU U4.66.11. Produces a data structure of type matr_asse_gene_R. The following test cases present examples of the use of this operator: - FDLV100 V8.01.100, - FDLV101 V8.01.101, - FDLV102 V8.01.102, - FDLV103 V8.01.103, - FDLV104 V8.01.104, - FDLV105 V8.01.105, - FDLV106 V8.01.106, - FDLV107 V8.01.107, - FDLV109 V8.01.109, - FDLV110 V8.01.110. 2 Syntax matr_asse_gene_r = CALC_MATR_AJOU( ◆ MODELE_FLUIDE = modele, ◆ MODELE_INTERFACE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ CHARGE = char_ther, ◇ / MODE_MECA = mode_meca, / CHAM_NO = cham_no, / MODELE_GENE = modele_gene, ◇ / NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◇ DIST_REFE = float (défaut: 0.01), ◇ AVEC_MODE_STAT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ NUME_MODE_MECA = int, ◆ OPTION = / "MASS_AJOU", / "AMOR_AJOU", / "RIGI_AJOU", ◇ POTENTIEL = evol_ther, ◇ NOEUD_DOUBLE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "MULT_FRONT", / "LDLT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "GCPC", / "PETSC", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "PORD", / "METIS", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "PARMETIS", / "PTSCOTCH", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON", / "LAGR2" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "NONSYM", / "SYMGEN", / "SYMDEF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FR", / "FR+", / "FR++", / "LR", / "LR+", / "LR++", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "SANS", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "SANS", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 35), ◇ REDUCTION_MPI = int, ◇ NB_RHS = int (défaut: 1), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "OUT_OF_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "EVAL", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'GCPC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ PRE_COND = / "LDLT_INC" (par défaut), / "LDLT_SP", / "LDLT_DP", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int, # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS", / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'PETSC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ ALGORITHME = / "CG", / "CR", / "GMRES", / "GCR", / "FGMRES" (par défaut), / "GMRES_LMP", ◇ OPTION_PETSC = text, ◇ PRE_COND = / "LDLT_INC", / "LDLT_SP" (par défaut), / "LDLT_DP", / "JACOBI", / "SOR", / "ML", / "BOOMER", / "GAMG", / "BLOC_LAGR", / "FIELDSPLIT", / "UTILISATEUR", / "HPDDM", / "SANS", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int, # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int, ◇ REMPLISSAGE = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS", / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = int, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE_FLUIDE ♦ MODELE_FLUIDE = fluide Thermal model that one assigns to the part of the mesh which corresponds to the fluid. The boundary elements at the fluid/structure interface must be present in the fluid model. It is on this model that one solves the Laplace equation with a boundary condition of "fluid flux" type, in order to have the pressure field throughout the fluid and a fortiori the pressure field at the fluid/structure interface. The nodes of the elements of the fluid mesh must all be numbered in such a way that the Jacobian of the element is of positive sign over the whole fluid mesh. 3.2 Operand MODELE_INTERFACE ♦ MODELE_INTERFACE = interf Thermal interface model gathering all the boundary elements defining the fluid/structure interface. It is on this model that one computes the terms of the added matrices. The computation depends on the orientation of the normal of these interface elements. One must take care that this normal is oriented, on all these elements, from the structure towards the fluid (adopted convention). If the fluids bathing the structure are of different densities, one must define the interface model by as many mesh-cell groups, not geometrically coincident, as there are fluids in contact with the structure. For example, a pipe may have its inner surface in contact with a fluid of density 1, and its outer surface in contact with a fluid of density 2. The interface model is therefore built on two mesh-cell groups that are not geometrically coincident, one in contact with the fluid of density 1 (interfa1) and the other in contact with the fluid of density 2 (interfa2). 3.3 Operands CHAM_MATER / CHARGE ♦ CHAM_MATER = matflui Material field defining the fluid immersing the structure. This material is defined by equivalent thermal characteristics in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. The thermal conductivity (keyword LAMBDA) is always taken equal to 1. The specific heat (keyword RHO_CP) plays the role of density of the fluid. ♦ CHARGE = charge Thermal load of type [char_ther] necessary for the solution of the linear system resulting from the Laplace equation in the fluid. One must impose an arbitrary temperature (which in fact plays the role of a pressure) on an arbitrary node of the fluid mesh, in order to make the system non-singular. This operation is carried out with the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER [U4.44.02]. 3.4 Operands MODE_MECA / CHAM_NO / MODELE_GENE ♦ / MODE_MECA = modes Dynamic modes computed on the structural model. If one has several non-connected structures immersed in one and the same fluid, for which one wants to determine the added matrices comprising the coupling terms through the fluid, the structural model that one defines gathers the whole of the immersed structures. The modes used by the operator are the modes computed for the global structure. / CHAM_NO = chamno Nodal field of displacements assigned on node groups defining the fluid/structure interface. By assigning such a displacement field on the interface node group(s) by means of the operator CREA_CHAMP, one can, for example, easily simulate rigid-body modes of the structures. This operand is to be used if one wants to estimate the terms of the added matrices and of the coupling matrices for a plane geometry without first carrying out a modal analysis of the structure in vacuum, and if one wants to assign these terms in discrete elements (modelling DIS_T). The operand INFO must imperatively be active in order to print the computed terms. Warning: The use of this operand excludes that of the operand NUME_DDL_GENE. One therefore cannot carry out a modal, transient or harmonic analysis using the operand CHAM_NO. Indeed, in order to carry out a modal analysis in water, one must have a generalised mass matrix and a generalised stiffness matrix of the structure. This supposes having carried out a modal analysis on the structure in vacuum (which is precisely what one wants to avoid). Ultimately, this operand is used only in order to evaluate the added mass matrix , the added stiffness and the added damping, and to use them in order to couple beam-type structures by discrete mass elements, for example. / MODELE_GENE = modgen Generalised model built by the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. This keyword is to be used when one carries out an analysis by dynamic substructuring, and one wants to compute the added mass matrix coupling the whole set of the substructures. In this case, the substructures may be in different mesh files, these files themselves possibly being distinct from the fluid mesh file. The substructures which present a repetitiveness within the fluid need be meshed only once, but one will take care, at the level of the fluid mesh, to mesh all the fluid/structure interfaces. Moreover, one must take care that the nodes of the fluid interface coincide as well as possible with the nodes of the structure interface, in order to be able to copy, on the basis of a geometric proximity criterion, the values of the structural displacement field onto the nodes of the fluid interface (see operand DIST_REFE). Warning: The use of this operand makes mandatory that of the operand NUME_DDL_GENE. 3.5 Operand OPTION This keyword specifies the added mass, stiffness or damping computation that one wants to carry out, using respectively 'MASS_AJOU', 'RIGI_AJOU', or 'AMOR_AJOU'. The last two computation options require the presence of a stationary (thermal) potential (see operand POTENTIEL). 3.6 Operand DIST_REFE Reference distance to be supplied when one carries out an added mass computation on a generalised model. This distance is an absolute geometric criterion intended for copying values of structural displacements into a thermal fluid model, in order to solve there the Laplace equation of the unsteady pressure field. By default, it is equal to 10–2 m. 3.7 Operand NOEUD_DOUBLE ◊ NOEUD_DOUBLE = 'OUI' This operand is to be used when one carries out an added mass computation from a generalised model which comprises a substructure meshed by a wireframe or surface mesh ( i.e. without thickness, such as a beam or a shell) and surrounded by two fluids. One must in this case, at the mesh level, duplicate the nodes of the fluid interfaces with respect to those of the structure, in order to be able to compute the jump in hydrodynamic pressure on either side of the structure ( cf. figure below). 3.8 Operand POTENTIEL ◊ POTENTIEL = phi Stationary (thermal) potential necessary for the computation of the added damping and of the added stiffness of the structure subjected to a potential flow. This potential is produced by the operator THER_LINEAIRE U4.54.01. 3.9 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ◊ NUME_DDL_GENE = numgen Generalised numbering based on the mechanical modes of the global structure. The presence of this operand makes it possible to compute an added mass matrix of type matr_asse_gene_R. It must necessarily be present if one subsequently wants to carry out a modal, harmonic or transient analysis. 3.10 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Indicates the level of printout of the results of the operator on the file MESSAGE. | 1 : | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2 : | printout of the upper triangular part of the added mass, added damping or added stiffness matrices. | Column presentation. 3.11 Factor keyword SOLVEUR See U4.50.01. 3.12 Operand AVEC_MODE_STAT Makes it possible to switch off the computation of the added-mass terms on the static modes contained in the modal basis of the substructures in the case of an analysis with a generalised model ( cf. [§3.4]). 3.13 Operand NUME_MODE_MECA Makes it possible to specify a list of numbers of modes retained for the computation. 4 Execution phase One checks that the fluid and interface models are indeed thermal. One checks that the storage of the added matrices is done on a full profile. One checks that the added self-mass coefficients (diagonal terms of the matrix) are indeed all positive. Otherwise, an alarm message is emitted so that the user checks the orientation of the normals. One checks that, for a computation of added damping or of added stiffness, the keyword POTENTIEL is indeed supplied. In the case of an added-mass computation on a generalised model, one informs the user about the copies of structural displacement fields into the fluid (number of values copied) and one indicates how to change the reference distance (DIST_REFE). 5 Example: Computation of the added mass matrix of a structure constituted of two concentric cylinders separated by an incompressible fluid The cylinders are each supported by springs. The added mass matrix is computed for the first two modes of the structure, namely the rigid-body modes of each of the cylinders in the direction Ox ( cf. diagram). One will present here only the steps of the command file, because this example is inspired by the test case FDLV101 V8.01.101. For the detail of the syntax of the other operators, the user may therefore refer to the command file of this test case. 1. Definition of the fluid material by equivalent thermal characteristics: 2. Assignment of this fluid material onto the fluid mesh, including the mesh-cell group defining the fluid/structure interface. 3. Assignment of the thermal fluid model (also comprising the interface) 4. Assignment of the thermal interface model 5. Assignment of the global structural model (comprising the two cylinders and their support springs) 6. Assignment of an imposed temperature in the fluid mesh 7. Computation of the eigenmodes of the structure in vacuum 8. Generalised numbering based on the computed mechanical modes 9. Computation of the added mass matrix of type matr_asse_gene_r (operand NUME_DDL_GENE present). As a result, one can then compute the eigenmodes of the "wetted" structure matraj = CALC_MATR_AJOU( MODELE_FLUIDE = fluide , MODELE_INTERFACE = interf , CHAM_MATER = chammat1 , CHARGE = charge , OPTION = 'MASS_AJOU' , MODE_MECA = modes , NUME_DDL_GENE = numgen , INFO =1 ) 1. Computation of the generalised mass and stiffness matrices on the generalised numbering based on the computed mechanical modes numgen. These matrices are of type [matr_asse_gene_r] 2. Computation of the total mass matrix of the structure (generalised mass matrix plus added mass matrix) 3. Computation of the modes of the immersed structure. 4. Recovery of the "wetted" modes onto the physical basis.

u4.66.02 Operator CALC_FLUI_STRU u4.66.02 Operator CALC_FLUI_STRU 1 Purpose Compute the modal parameters of a structure subjected to a flow. Makes it possible to take into account the fluid-elastic forces, which are represented by a complex transfer matrix relating them to the modal displacements. For certain configurations, the transfer matrix can be decomposed into three real matrices of added mass, damping and stiffness coefficients. The perturbations of the modal characteristics of the structure depend on the flow velocity. Thus the terms of the transfer matrix of the fluid-elastic forces depend on the fluid velocity and on the frequency of the motion, by means of the reduced-velocity parameter Vr = V/(f.D). The operator computes a modal basis modified by the coupling, for each mean fluid velocity studied. The concept produced is of type melasflu. 2 Syntax melasflu = CALC_FLUI_STRU( ◇ VITE_FLUI = _F( ◇ VITE_MIN = float, ◇ VITE_MAX = float, ◇ NB_POIN = int, ), ◆ BASE_MODALE = _F( ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◆ | AMOR_REDUIT = float, | AMOR_UNIF = float, | AMOR_REDUIT_CONN = float, ), ◆ TYPE_FLUI_STRU = type_flui_stru, ◇ IMPRESSION = _F( ◇ PARA_COUPLAGE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ DEFORMEE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ), ◇ STOP_ERREUR = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword VITE_FLUI ◊ VITE_FLUI Factor keyword which makes it possible to define the range of fluid velocities studied and the discretisation. ◊ VITE_MIN = vi First value of the velocity for which the coupling parameters are computed. ◊ VITE_MAX = vm Last value of the velocity for which the coupling parameters are computed. ◊ NB_POIN = np Defines the number of points in velocity (the discretisation step is constant). 3.2 Keyword BASE_MODALE ♦ BASE_MODALE Factor keyword which makes it possible to define the modal basis of concept mode_meca for which the coupling parameters are computed. The coupling modifies the eigenfrequencies and the values of the reduced-damping terms associated with each mode (keyword AMOR_REDUIT or AMOR_UNIF). ♦ MODE_MECA = mode Modal basis of concept type mode_meca. ◊ NUME_ORDRE = l_nuor Makes it possible to select the modes of the modal basis of type mode_meca to be taken into account for the computation of the coupling. ◊ / AMOR_REDUIT = l_amor List of the reduced dampings (percentage of the critical damping) corresponding to each mode of the structure. Note: They must be identical in number to the number of modes taken into account (these modes are defined by the keyword NUME_ORDRE). / AMOR_UNIF = amor One applies to all the modes of the modal basis the same reduced damping. ◊ AMOR_REDUIT_CONN = l_amor_c List of the reduced dampings (percentage of the critical damping) corresponding to each mode of the structure for the Connors method (see [R4.07.04]). In accordance with this reference documentation, one supplies two values of the Connors instability ratio (one of them said to be «All components»). Note: As for the keyword AMOR_REDUIT, they must be identical in number to the number of modes taken into account. 3.3 Keyword TYPE_FLUI_STRU ♦ TYPE_FLUI_STRU = typeflui Concept of type type_flui_stru. It makes it possible to define the configuration studied, that is the coupling coefficients used for the modelling of the fluid-elastic forces. Note: In the case of a configuration of the type «tube bundle under axial flow» (factor keyword FAISCEAU_AXIAL ), the computation of the coupling parameters of the structure with the fluid in the at-rest state is taken into account. This computation is carried out whatever the range of fluid velocities that the user has supplied by means of the keyword VITE_FLUI . In this case of a fluid at rest, the transfer matrix representing the fluid-elastic force exerted on the structure takes the form of an added-damping matrix. 3.4 Keyword IMPRESSION ◊ IMPRESSION Factor keyword making it possible for the user to choose the information which is to be written in the file RESULTAT. ◊ PARA_COUPLAGE = 'OUI' ou 'NON' By this keyword, the user may request the printout of tables of results giving, for each mode, the evolutions of the reduced velocity, of the frequency and of the modal reduced damping as a function of the flow velocity of the fluid. The default value is 'OUI'. ◊ DEFORMEE = 'OUI' ou 'NON' By this keyword the user may request the printout, in 'RESULTAT' format, of the displacement fields corresponding to the modal deflected shapes. The default value is 'NON'. 3.5 Operand STOP_ERREUR ◊ STOP_ERREUR = stop Keyword which makes it possible to define the behaviour of the code in the event of a convergence problem in the computation of the coupling coefficients for a given velocity and a deformation mode of the structure. If STOP_ERREUR='OUI', the code stops in fatal error in the event of a convergence problem, notifying the user of the velocity concerned. If STOP_ERREUR='NON', the code emits an alarm notifying the user of the convergence problem (velocity and mode number) and stores the last value computed for the coupling coefficients. 4 Notes In the case of a configuration of the type «tube bundles under transverse flow», it is possible to define several zones of interaction between the fluid and the structure, each of these zones being able to be modelled independently of the others. The computation of the modal parameters of the structure subjected to a flow then takes account of each of these zones, defined explicitly in the command DEFI_FLUI_STRU U4.25.01. The concept produced by CALC_FLUI_STRU contains, in the form of a table, the mass, damping and stiffness matrices for each fluid velocity. The table, representing the modified modal basis, can be recovered by RECU_TABLE in order to be injected into a DYNA_VIBRA analysis. This sequence of analysis is implemented in the test case SDLL118A.

u4.66.03 Operator CALC_FORC_AJOU u4.66.03 Operator CALC_FORC_AJOU 1 Purpose This command makes it possible to compute the effect of the hydrodynamic overpressure due to the entrainment motion of the structure in seismic analysis, in which one decomposes the total motion into an entrainment motion and a relative motion. The analysis of this force is carried out in the same way as that of the added mass by thermal analogy, but instead of taking into account only the relative motion, one obtains an added force on the right-hand side, also projected onto the modes of the structure without the fluid, in order to take the entrainment motion into account. The analysis of the added masses R4.07.03 by CALC_MATR_AJOU U4.66.01 and that of the added forces by CALC_FORC_AJOU can be launched simultaneously with the aid of the macro-command MACRO_MATR_AJOU U4.66.11. Produces a concept of type vect_asse_gene_R 2 Syntax vect_asse_gene = CALC_FORC_AJOU( ◆ MODELE_FLUIDE = modele, ◆ MODELE_INTERFACE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ CHARGE = char_ther, ◇ / MODE_MECA = mode_meca, / MODELE_GENE = modele_gene, ◇ & NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◇ DIST_REFE = float (défaut: 0.01), ◇ AVEC_MODE_STAT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ NUME_MODE_MECA = int, ◇ POTENTIEL = evol_ther, ◇ NOEUD_DOUBLE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◆ DIRECTION = float, ◆ / MONO_APPUI = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NOEUD = no, / GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ / MODE_STAT = mode_meca, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "MULT_FRONT", / "LDLT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "GCPC", / "PETSC", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "PORD", / "METIS", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "PARMETIS", / "PTSCOTCH", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON", / "LAGR2" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "NONSYM", / "SYMGEN", / "SYMDEF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FR", / "FR+", / "FR++", / "LR", / "LR+", / "LR++", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "SANS", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "SANS", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 35), ◇ REDUCTION_MPI = int, ◇ NB_RHS = int (défaut: 1), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "OUT_OF_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "EVAL", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'GCPC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ PRE_COND = / "LDLT_INC" (par défaut), / "LDLT_SP", / "LDLT_DP", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int, # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS", / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'PETSC') ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ ALGORITHME = / "CG", / "CR", / "GMRES", / "GCR", / "FGMRES" (par défaut), / "GMRES_LMP", ◇ OPTION_PETSC = text, ◇ PRE_COND = / "LDLT_INC", / "LDLT_SP" (par défaut), / "LDLT_DP", / "JACOBI", / "SOR", / "ML", / "BOOMER", / "GAMG", / "BLOC_LAGR", / "FIELDSPLIT", / "UTILISATEUR", / "HPDDM", / "SANS", ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int, # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int, ◇ REMPLISSAGE = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS", / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'ML') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BOOMER') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'GAMG') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'HPDDM') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = int, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE_FLUIDE ♦ MODELE_FLUIDE = fluide Thermal model which one assigns to the part of the mesh which corresponds to the fluid. The boundary elements at the fluid/structure interface must be present in the fluid model. It is on this model that one solves the Laplace equation with a boundary condition of "fluid flux" type, in order to have the pressure field throughout the fluid and a fortiori the pressure field at the fluid/structure interface. The nodes of the elements of the fluid mesh must all be numbered in such a way that the Jacobian of the element is of positive sign over the whole fluid mesh. 3.2 Operand MODELE_INTERFACE ♦ MODELE_INTERFACE = interf Thermal interface model gathering all the boundary elements defining the fluid/structure interface. It is on this model that one computes the terms of the added matrices. The analysis depends on the orientation of the normal of these interface elements. One must ensure that this normal is oriented, on all these elements, from the structure towards the fluid (adopted convention). If the fluids bathing the structure are of different densities, one must define the interface model by as many mesh-cell groups, geometrically non-coincident, as there are fluids in contact with the structure. For example, a pipe may have its inner surface in contact with a fluid of density 1, and its outer surface in contact with a fluid of density 2. The interface model is therefore built on two mesh-cell groups which are geometrically non-coincident, one in contact with the fluid of density 1 (interfa1) and the other in contact with the fluid of density 2 (interfa2). 3.3 Operands CHAM_MATER / CHARGE ♦ CHAM_MATER = matflui Material field defining the fluid immersing the structure. This material is defined by equivalent thermal characteristics in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. The thermal conductivity (keyword LAMBDA) is always taken equal to 1. The specific heat (keyword RHO_CP) plays the role of density of the fluid. ♦ CHARGE = charge Thermal load of type [char_ther] necessary for the solution of the linear system arising from the Laplace equation in the fluid. One must impose an arbitrary temperature (which in fact plays the role of a pressure) on an arbitrary node of the fluid mesh, in order to make the system non-singular. This operation is carried out with the operator AFFE_CHAR_THER [U4.44.02]. 3.4 Operands MODE_MECA / MODELE_GENE ♦ / MODE_MECA = modes Dynamic modes computed on the structural model. If one has several disconnected structures immersed in the same fluid, for which one wants to determine the added matrices including the coupling terms through the fluid, the structural model which one defines gathers all of the immersed structures. The modes used by the operator are the modes computed for the global structure. / MODELE_GENE = modgen Generalised model built by the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. This keyword is to be used when one carries out an analysis by dynamic substructuring, and when one wants to compute the added mass matrix coupling all of the substructures. In this case, the substructures may be in different mesh files, these files themselves possibly being distinct from the fluid mesh file. The substructures which exhibit a repetitiveness within the fluid need be meshed only once, but one will take care, at the level of the fluid mesh, to mesh all the fluid/structure interfaces. Moreover, one must ensure that the fluid interface nodes coincide as well as possible with the structure interface nodes, in order to be able to copy, on the basis of a geometric proximity criterion, the values of the structural displacement field onto the fluid interface nodes (see operand DIST_REFE). 3.5 Operand DIST_REFE Reference distance to be supplied when one carries out an analysis of added force on a generalised model. This distance is an absolute geometric criterion intended for copying values of structural displacements into a thermal fluid model, in order to solve there the Laplace equation of the unsteady pressure field. By default, it is equal to 10–2 m. 3.6 Operand NOEUD_DOUBLE ◊ NOEUD_DOUBLE = 'OUI' This operand is to be used when one carries out an analysis of added force from a generalised model which includes a substructure meshed by a wire or surface mesh ( i.e. without thickness, such as a beam or a shell) and surrounded by two fluids. In this case one must, at the mesh level, duplicate the nodes of the fluid interfaces with respect to those of the structure, in order to be able to compute the jump in hydrodynamic pressure on either side of the structure ( cf. figure below). 3.7 Operand POTENTIEL ◊ POTENTIEL = phi Steady (thermal) potential necessary for the analysis of the added damping and of the added stiffness of the structure subjected to a potential flow. This potential is produced by the operator THER_LINEAIRE U4.54.01. 3.8 Operand DIRECTION ♦ DIRECTION = (d1 , d2 , d3 , r1 , r2 , r3) Components of a vector giving the direction of the entrainment earthquake in the global frame. It is a list of three reals if the imposed accelerograms are only translations. If one also imposes rotational accelerations, a list of six reals is expected (valid for modellings with discrete elements). 3.9 Description of the entrainment motion 3.9.1 Operand MONO_APPUI ♦ / MONO_APPUI = 'OUI' The structure is excited uniformly at all the supports (rigid-body entrainment motion). 3.9.2 Multi-support excitation In this case, the accelerations undergone by all the anchor points of the structure studied are not necessarily identical and in phase. 3.9.2.1 Operand MODE_STAT / ♦ MODE_STAT = mode Static modes of the structure: concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14 with the option DDL_IMPO. They correspond to the 3 or 6 nb_supports static modes, where nb_supports is the number of different accelerograms undergone by the structure. Note: If the structure is subjected only to translations, there are then 3 nb_supports static modes. 3.9.2.2 Operands NOEUD / GROUP_NO ♦ / NOEUD = no / GROUP_NO = grno List of nodes (no) or node groups (grno) of the structure subjected to the seismic excitation: these nodes carry the degrees of freedom of the supports of the structure to which the imposed motions are applied. 3.10 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE > ◊ NUME_DDL_GENE = numgen Generalised numbering based on the mechanical modes of the global structure. The presence of this operand makes it possible to compute an added mass matrix of type matr_asse_gene_R. It must necessarily be present if one subsequently wants to carry out a modal, harmonic or transient analysis. 3.11 Factor keyword SOLVEUR See U4.50.01. 3.12 Operand AVEC_MODE_STAT Makes it possible to switch off the analysis of the added-mass terms on the static modes contained in the modal basis of the substructures in the case of an analysis with a generalised model ( cf. [§3.4]). 3.13 Operand NUME_MODE_MECA Makes it possible to specify a list of numbers of modes retained for the analysis. 3.14 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Indicates the printout level of the results of the operator on the MESSAGE file. 1: no printout 2: printout of the added-force terms.

u4.66.04 Operator CALC_CHAM_FLUI u4.66.04 Operator CALC_CHAM_FLUI 1 Purpose Compute fluid potential fields associated with the added-mass theory R4.07.03. The fields are induced by a perfect, incompressible fluid, at rest or in potential flow, on a 3D structure. The terms of these fields are computed on the modal basis of the structure in vacuum. The analysis of the terms of the matrices is carried out by solving the LAPLACE equations within the framework of a thermal analogy . The computed temperature plays the role of a pressure in the fluid domain. One must therefore take care to define the fluid material by thermal characteristics, and to assign a thermal model to the part of the mesh which represents the fluid. Thanks to this operator, one can determine, for example, the pressure created by the fluid on the structure vibrating according to one of its eigenmodes. The test FDLV114b provides an example of implementation on a case of a cylindrical tank. Produces a data structure of type evol_ther. 2 Syntax evol_ther = CALC_CHAM_FLUI( ◆ RIGI_THER = matr_asse_temp_r, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_ther, ◇ FONC_MULT = nappe / formule / fonction, ), ◇ POTENTIEL = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "PRES", ◇ DIST_REFE = float (défaut: 0.01), ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, # Si: exists("MODE_MECA") ◇ COEF_MULT = float (défaut: 1.0), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RIGI_THER ♦ RIGI_THER = rigi_ther Thermal stiffness matrix corresponding to the fluid potential. It is built by associating with the \rho {c}_{p} of the material assigned to the fluid model the density of the fluid. 3.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmat Name of the material field assigned on the model associated with the matrix rigi_ther. 3.3 Factor keyword EXCIT 3.3.1 Operand CHARGE ♦ CHARGE = ch Thermal loading corresponding to the boundary conditions on the fluid. For example in the case of an analysis of type POTENTIEL = «PRES»: > TEMP_IMPO(TEMP=0.0) corresponds to a zero pressure on this surface. 3.3.2 Operand FONCT_MULT ♦ FONC_MULT = fmult Multiplicative function or formula modulating the loading 3.4 Operand POTENTIEL ♦ POTENTIEL = / 'DEPL', / 'VITE', / 'PRES' [DEFAUT], Choice of the type of potential required, displacement potential, velocity potential, or a pressure field. 3.5 Operand DIST_REFE ◊ DIST_REFE = 1.E-2 [DEFAUT],, Reference distance to be supplied when one carries out an analysis on a generalised model. This distance is an absolute geometric criterion intended for copying values of structural displacements into a thermal fluid model, in order to solve there the Laplace equation of the unsteady pressure field. By default, it is equal to 10–2 m. 3.6 Operand MODE_MECA ♦ MODE_MECA = mode Modes on which one computes the fluid potential 3.6.1 Operand COEF_MULT ♦COEF_MULT = 1.0 [DEFAUT], Coefficient réel permettant, éventuellement, de mettre à l'échelle le potentiel résultat

u4.66.11 Macro-command MACRO_MATR_AJOU u4.66.11 Macro-command MACRO_MATR_AJOU 1 Purpose Compute, in a more condensed way than with CALC_MATR_AJOU, added mass, damping or stiffness matrices R4.07.03. The matrices are induced by a perfect, incompressible fluid, at rest or in potential flow, on a structure in 2D, axisymmetric 2D or 3D. The terms of these matrices are computed on the modal basis of the structure in vacuum. One can also compute, by launching CALC_FORC_AJOU U4.66.03, the vectors of the added forces induced by a seismic entrainment motion, also computed on the modal basis of the structure in vacuum. The advantage of this macro-command is essentially to hide the calls to the linear thermal operators which compute the hydrodynamic pressures caused by the vibration of the structure in the fluid. The user now only has to supply the characteristics of the fluid domain and the eigenmodes in air of the structure, the operator taking care of computing the added matrices. The possibilities of the command retain those of the operator CALC_MATR_AJOU U4.66.01. Examples of use of the macro-command MACRO_MATR_AJOU are presented in the test case: - FDLV101 V8.01.101, - FDLV102 V8.01.102, - FDLV106 V8.01.106, - FDLV108 V8.01.108, - FDLV109 V8.01.109, - FDLV112 V8.01.112. 2 Syntax / vect_asse_gene / matr_asse_gene_r = MACRO_MATR_AJOU( ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◆ GROUP_MA_FLUIDE = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_INTERF = grma, ◆ MODELISATION = / "PLAN", / "AXIS", / "3D", ◆ FLUIDE = _F( ◆ RHO = float, ◇ TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ), ◆ DDL_IMPO = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ / PRES_FLUIDE = float, / PRES_SORTIE = float, ), ◇ ECOULEMENT = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA_1 = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_2 = grma, ◆ VNOR_1 = float, ◇ VNOR_2 = float, ◇ POTENTIEL = evol_ther, ), ◆ | MODE_MECA = mode_meca, | DEPL_IMPO = cham_no, | MODELE_GENE = modele_gene, ◇ / NUME_DDL_GENE = nume_ddl_gene, ◇ DIST_REFE = float (défaut: 0.01), ◆ | MATR_MASS_AJOU = co, | MATR_AMOR_AJOU = co, | MATR_RIGI_AJOU = co, ◇ / MONO_APPUI = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / MODE_STAT = mode_meca, ◇ FORC_AJOU = _F( ◆ DIRECTION = float, ◇ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ VECTEUR = co, ), ⟐ SOLVEUR = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "MULT_FRONT", / "LDLT", / "MUMPS" (par défaut), / "GCPC", / "PETSC", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MULT_FRONT') ◇ RENUM = / "MD", / "MDA" (par défaut), ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LDLT') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'MUMPS') ◇ RENUM = / "AMD", / "AMF", / "PORD", / "METIS", / "QAMD", / "SCOTCH", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "PARMETIS", / "PTSCOTCH", ◇ NPREC = int (défaut: 8), ◇ ELIM_LAGR = / "OUI", / "NON", / "LAGR2" (par défaut), ◇ STOP_SINGULIER = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ TYPE_RESOL = / "NONSYM", / "SYMGEN", / "SYMDEF", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ ACCELERATION = / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FR", / "FR+", / "FR++", / "LR", / "LR+", / "LR++", ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, ◇ PRETRAITEMENTS = / "SANS", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ POSTTRAITEMENTS = / "SANS", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "FORCE", / "MINI", ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 35), ◇ REDUCTION_MPI = int, ◇ NB_RHS = int (défaut: 1), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "OUT_OF_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), / "EVAL", # Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'LDLT_INC') ◇ RENUM = "RCMK", ◇ NIVE_REMPLISSAGE = int, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('LDLT_SP', 'LDLT_DP')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS", / "METIS", / "PARMETIS" (par défaut), ◇ REAC_PRECOND = int (défaut: 30), ◇ PCENT_PIVOT = int (défaut: 20), ◇ GESTION_MEMOIRE = / "IN_CORE", / "AUTO" (par défaut), ◇ LOW_RANK_SEUIL = float, # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "SANS" (par défaut), / "RCMK", ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ NOEUD_DOUBLE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ AVEC_MODE_STAT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE Name of the mesh containing the fluid domain and the fluid/structure interface. This mesh may also include the structure. 3.2 Operand GROUP_MA_FLUIDE ♦ GROUP_MA_FLUIDE = fluide Mesh-cell groups (plane mesh cells in 2D and axisymmetric 2D, volume mesh cells in 3D) representing the fluid domain acting on the structure studied. 3.3 Operand GROUP_MA_INTERF ♦ GROUP_MA_INTERF = interf Mesh-cell groups representing the interface between the fluid and the structure (plane or line mesh cells). It must be emphasised that this mesh-cell group may be one of those used to model the surface of the structure, in particular if the latter is modelled by shell elements. It is not always necessary to create a specific interface mesh-cell group with mesh cells in their own right. 3.4 Operand MODELISATION Type of modelling to assign to the fluid domain and to the fluid/structure interface. At present, the modellings 'PLAN' (2D fluid domain), '3D' (volumetric fluid domain) and 'AXIS' (axisymmetric fluid domain) are the only ones allowed. 3.5 Keyword FLUIDE Factor keyword in which one assigns the characteristics of the fluid material. If the density of the fluid varies over the fluid domain, one must specify these different densities by several occurrences of the factor keyword FLUIDE. 3.5.1 Operand RHO ♦ RHO = rho Value of the density of the fluid to be assigned on the topological entities defined below. 3.5.2 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA Mesh-cell group or the whole of the fluid domain on which one assigns the density RHO. 3.6 Keyword DDL_IMPO Factor keyword by which one specifies the boundary conditions of the fluid (of Dirichlet type). 3.6.1 Operand GROUP_NO Node groups on which one imposes the boundary conditions on the fluid domain. 3.6.2 Operand PRES_FLUIDE Keyword under which one specifies the value which one imposes on the hydrodynamic pressure (that is to say the pressure perturbation created by the vibration of the structure) on the topological entity determined above. This keyword must appear at least once because it makes it possible to compute the unsteady pressure fields which generate the added mechanical quantities (grandeurs). 3.6.3 Operand PRES_SORTIE Outlet pressure to be imposed on a steady flow. Keyword to be used (in an occurrence of the factor keyword DDL_IMPO different from the one in which PRES_FLUIDE has been used) in order to specify the boundary conditions on the steady quantities to be computed (such as the potential of the steady fluid velocities characterising a steady flow disturbed by the vibrations). This keyword is to be used only if one wants to compute the added damping and stiffness matrices, which require the analysis of a steady flow assumed to be potential. 3.7 Keyword ECOULEMENT This factor keyword makes it possible to determine the boundary conditions of Neumann type when one wants to compute a steady flow assumed to be potential, in order to be able to compute the added damping and stiffness. 3.7.1 Operands GROUP_MA_1 / GROUP_MA_2 Names of the mesh-cell groups, respectively of inlet and of outlet of the fluid domain, on which one imposes conditions of normal velocity of inlet or of outlet of the fluid. 3.7.2 Operands VNOR_1 / VNOR_2 Real values of the normal velocities of the fluid, respectively at the inlet and at the outlet of the fluid domain. 3.7.3 Operand POTENTIEL Name given by the user to the potential of the steady fluid velocities if the user possibly wants to post-process it. 3.8 Operands MODE_MECA / DEPL_IMPO / MODELE_GENE ♦ / MODE_MECA = modes Dynamic modes computed on the structural model. If one has several disconnected structures immersed in the same fluid, for which one wants to determine the added matrices including the coupling terms through the fluid, the structural model which one defines gathers all of the immersed structures. The modes used by the operator are the modes computed for the global structure. / DEPL_IMPO = chamno Nodal displacement fields assigned on node groups defining the fluid/structure interface. By assigning such a displacement field on the interface node group(s) by means of the operator CREA_CHAMP, one can for example easily simulate rigid-body modes of the structures. This operand is to be used if one wants to estimate the terms of the added and coupling matrices for a plane geometry without first carrying out a modal analysis of the structure in vacuum, and if one wants to assign these terms in discrete elements (modelling DIS_T). The operand INFO must necessarily be active in order to display the computed terms. Caution: The use of this operand excludes that of the operand NUME_DDL_GENE. One therefore cannot carry out a modal, transient or harmonic analysis by using the operand CHAM_NO. Indeed, in order to carry out an analysis of modes in water, one must have a generalised mass matrix and a generalised stiffness matrix of the structure. This supposes that one has carried out a modal analysis on the structure in vacuum (which is precisely what one wants to avoid). Ultimately, this operand is used only to evaluate the added mass matrix , and the added stiffness and damping matrices, and to use them to couple beam-type structures by discrete mass elements, for example. / MODELE_GENE = modgen Generalised model built by the operator DEFI_MODELE_GENE U4.65.02. This keyword is to be used when one carries out an analysis by dynamic substructuring, and when one wants to compute the added mass matrix coupling all of the substructures. In this case, the substructures may be in different mesh files, these files themselves possibly being distinct from the fluid mesh file. The substructures which exhibit a repetitiveness within the fluid need be meshed only once, but one will take care, at the level of the fluid mesh, to mesh all the fluid/structure interfaces. Moreover, one must ensure that the fluid interface nodes coincide as well as possible with the structure interface nodes, in order to be able to copy, on the basis of a geometric proximity criterion, the values of the structural displacement field onto the fluid interface nodes (see operand DIST_REFE). 3.9 Operands MATR_MASS_AJOU / MATR_AMOR_AJOU / MATR_RIGI_AJOU These keywords specify the user name of the added mass, stiffness or damping matrices which one wants to compute. At least one of these keywords is required in order to carry out the analysis. The 3 keywords can be used simultaneously, but in the case of the use of MATR_AMOR_AJOU or MATR_RIGI_AJOU, one must supply the keywords ECOULEMENT and DDL_IMPO with PRES_SORTIE. 3.10 Operand DIST_REFE Reference distance to be supplied when one carries out an analysis of added mass on a generalised model. This distance is an absolute geometric proximity criterion intended for copying values of structural displacements into a fluid domain, in order to solve there the Laplace equation of the unsteady pressure field. By default, it is equal to 10–2. 3.11 Operand NOEUD_DOUBLE ◊ NOEUD_DOUBLE = 'OUI' This operand is to be used when one carries out an analysis of added mass from a generalised model which includes a substructure meshed by a wire or surface mesh ( i.e. without thickness, such as a beam or a shell) and surrounded by two fluids. In this case one must, at the mesh level, duplicate the nodes of the fluid interfaces with respect to those of the structure, in order to be able to compute the jump in hydrodynamic pressure on either side of the structure ( cf. figure below). 3.12 Operand AVEC_MODE_STAT ◊ AVEC_MODE_STAT = 'NON' This operand makes it possible to switch off the analysis of the added-mass terms on the static modes contained in the modal basis of the substructures in the case of an analysis with a generalised model ( cf. [§3.8]). 3.13 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE ◊ NUME_DDL_GENE = numgen Generalised numbering based on the mechanical modes of the global structure. The presence of this operand makes it possible to compute an added mass matrix of type matr_asse_gene_R. It must necessarily be present if one subsequently wants to carry out a modal, harmonic or transient analysis. 3.14 Description of the seismic entrainment motion 3.14.1 Operand MONO_APPUI ♦ / MONO_APPUI = 'OUI' The structure is excited uniformly at all the supports (rigid-body entrainment motion). 3.14.2 Multi-support excitation: operand MODE_STAT In this case, the accelerations undergone by all the anchor points of the structure studied are not necessarily identical and in phase. / ♦ MODE_STAT = mode Static modes of the structure: concept of type mode_meca produced by the operator MODE_STATIQUE U4.52.14 with the option DDL_IMPO. They correspond to the 3 or 6 nb_supports static modes, where nb_supports is the number of different accelerograms undergone by the structure. Note: If the structure is subjected only to translations, there are then 3 nb_supports static modes. 3.15 Added forces due to the seismic entrainment motion: keyword FORC_AJOU 3.15.1 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO = g_noeu Node groups (g_noeu) of the structure subjected to the seismic excitation: these nodes carry the degrees of freedom of the supports of the structure to which the imposed motions are applied. 3.15.2 Operand DIRECTION ♦ DIRECTION = ( d1 , d2 , d3 , r1 , r2 , r3 ) Components of a vector giving the direction of the entrainment earthquake in the global frame. It is a list of three reals if the imposed accelerograms are only translations. If one also imposes rotational accelerations, a list of six reals is expected (valid for modellings with discrete elements). 3.15.3 Operand VECTEUR ♦ VECTEUR = vecteur [vect_asse_gene] Nom du vecteur force ajoutée créé par le lancement de l'opérateur CALC_FORC_AJOU [:ref: U4.66.03 ]. Il y autant de vecteurs créés que d'occurrences du mot clé FORC_AJOU. 3.16 Keyword SOLVEUR Factor keyword specifying the technique for solving the linear system appearing here in the analysis of the unsteady pressure fields. See U4.50.01. 3.17 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Indicates the printout level of the results of the operator, | 1: | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2: | printout of the upper triangular part of the added mass, added damping or added stiffness matrices. | Presentation in columns. 4 Execution phase One checks that the storage of the added matrices is done on a full profile. One checks that the added self-mass coefficients (diagonal terms of the matrix) are indeed all positive. Otherwise, an alarm message is issued so that the user checks the orientation of the normals. In the case of an added-mass analysis on a generalised model, the user is informed about the copies of structural displacement fields into the fluid (number of values copied) and is told how to change the reference distance (DIST_REFE). 5 Example 5.1 Example 1: Analysis of the added mass matrix of a structure made up of two concentric cylinders separated by an incompressible fluid The cylinders are each supported by springs. The added mass matrix is computed for the first two modes of the structure, namely the rigid-body modes of each of the cylinders in the Ox direction ( cf. diagram). Only the stages of the command file will be presented here, because this example is inspired by the test case FDLV101 V8.01.101. For the detail of the syntax of the other operators, the user may therefore refer to the command file of this test case. 1. Assignment of the global structural model (comprising the two cylinders and their support springs). 1. Computation of the eigenmodes of the structure in vacuum 2. Generalised numbering based on the mechanical modes computed 3. Analysis of the added mass matrix of type matr_asse_gene_r (operand NUME_DDL_GENE present). As a result, one can then compute the eigenmodes of the "wet" structure MACRO_MATR_AJOU( MAILLAGE = maya , GROUP_MA_FLUIDE = 'grfluide' , GROUP_MA_INTERF = grinter, MODELISATION = ’PLAN’, FLUIDE = _F( RHO = rho , GROUP_MA = 'grtotal' ) , DDL_IMPO = _F( GROUP_NO = 'noflui' , PRES_FLUIDE = 0. ) , MATR_MASS_AJOU = massaj , MODE_MECA = modes , NUME_DDL_GENE= numgen , INFO =1 ) 1. Analysis of the generalised mass and stiffness matrices on the generalised numbering based on the computed mechanical modes numgen. These matrices are of type [matr_asse_gene_r] 2. Analysis of the total mass matrix of the structure (generalised mass matrix plus added mass matrix) 3. Analysis of the modes of the immersed structure. 4. Recovery of the "wet" modes on the physical basis. 5.2 Example 2: cylinder subjected to an annular flow This case (very close to the test case FDLV106 V8.01.106) implements the analysis of added mass, added damping, and added stiffness on a cylindrical structure subjected to an annular flow which one assumes to be potential. One computes, first, the mass and the damping added by the flow on the structure for different upstream velocities (4 m/s, 4.24 m/s and 6 m/s), this on a 3D model for the fluid and a shell model for the structure. The structure has a rotational displacement about a pivot located at the downstream end of the cylinder with respect to the flow. 1. After having modelled the cylindrical structure and computed its modes in air, the command MACRO_MATR_AJOU makes it possible to compute the mass, the stiffness and the damping added by the flowing fluid on this structure: MACRO_MATR_AJOU ( MAILLAGE = MAYA, GROUP_MA_FLUIDE = 'FLUIDE', GROUP_MA_INTERF = 'INTERFACE', FLUIDE = _F( RHO = 1000.), INFO = 2, MODELISATION = '3D', DDL_IMPO = ( _F( GROUP_NO = 'TEMPIMPO', PRES_FLUIDE = 0.), _F( GROUP_NO = 'NOSORT', PRES_SORTIE = 0.)), ECOULEMENT = _F( GROUP_MA_1 = 'ENTREE', GROUP_MA_2 = 'SORTIE', VNOR_1 = -4., VNOR_2 = 4. ), MATR_MASS_AJOU = CO("MASSAJ"), MATR_AMOR_AJOU = CO("AMORAJ"), MATR_RIGI_AJOU = CO("RIGIAJ"), MODE_MECA: = MODES , NUME_DDL_GENE= NUMGEN , )

u4.66.21 Operator MODI_BASE_MODALE u4.66.21 Operator MODI_BASE_MODALE 1 Purpose Define the modal basis of a structure under flow. This basis is obtained after an analysis of fluid-elastic coupling carried out with the aid of the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU U4.66.02. The concept produced is of type mode_meca. 2 Syntax mode_meca = MODI_BASE_MODALE( ◇ reuse = , ◆ BASE = mode_meca, ◆ BASE_ELAS_FLUI = melasflu, ◆ NUME_VITE_FLUI = int, ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ / AMOR_REDUIT = float, / AMOR_UNIF = float, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands ♦ BASE = mode Concept of type [mode_meca] which defines the modal characteristics before the fluid-elastic coupling is taken into account. According to the user's choice, the operator modifies this input concept or creates a new concept of type [mode_meca]. ♦ BASE_ELAS_FLUI = bef Concept of type [melasflu] which defines the new characteristics of the modes taken into account for the fluid-elastic coupling, for different flow velocities. ♦ NUME_VITE_FLUI = numv Makes it possible to point to the characteristics of the modes taken into account for the fluid-elastic coupling, for a given flow velocity. ◊ NUME_ORDRE = l_nuor If one modifies the input concept of type [mode_meca]: list of the order numbers of the unperturbed modes to which one wishes to assign a reduced damping. If one creates a new concept of type [mode_meca] on output: list of the order numbers of the unperturbed modes which are actually retained in order to rebuild the modal basis. The possibility of assigning a reduced damping to these modes is retained, by resorting to the operands AMOR_REDUIT or AMOR_UNIF below. Note: By default, one selects all the modes which have not been taken into account for the fluid-elastic coupling. Do not give in this list order numbers corresponding to the coupled modes. The constitution of the resulting [mode_meca] as a function of the choices for the operands NUME_ORDRE, AMOR_REDUIT and AMOR_UNIF is specified in paragraph [§ 1 ]. ◊ / AMOR_REDUIT = l_amor List of the reduced dampings assigned to the unperturbed modes. / AMOR_UNIF = amor Reduced damping assigned identically to the unperturbed modes. ◊ INFO = 1 ou 2 Inactive operand. In order to obtain the printout of the results, one must use the command IMPR_RESU U4.91.01. ◊ TITRE = titre Argument of text type [TXM] defining the title attached to the output concept [mode_meca]. 4 Details for use: content of the result concept [mode_meca]

u4.67.01 Operator DEFI_BASE_REDUITE u4.67.01 Operator DEFI_BASE_REDUITE The purpose of the operator is to build the reduced basis from a non-linear analysis (thermal or mechanical) or from a parametric linear analysis. There are two methods: - For non-linear problems, the operator relies on an sd_resultat of type evol_ther or evol_noli and carries out a singular value decomposition (SVD) on the transient or an incremental POD type strategy; - For parametric linear problems, one uses a greedy-type algorithm. In this case, one defines the linear system to be solved. The operator also makes it possible to truncate a basis (primal or dual) onto a reduced domain (for example produced by the command DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT). Two types of basis can be produced: - the so-called "primal" bases: they rely on the displacement fields for mechanics and on the temperature fields for thermal analysis; - the so-called "dual" bases: they rely on the stress fields for mechanics and on the flux fields for thermal analysis. The operator produces a concept of type mode_empi. 1 Syntax mode_empi = DEFI_BASE_REDUITE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ BASE = mode_empi, ◇ OPERATION = / "GLOUTON", / "ORTHO", / "POD" (par défaut), / "POD_INCR", / "TRONCATURE", #
