Si: equal_to("PRE_COND", 'BLOC_LAGR') ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('FIELDSPLIT')) ◇ RENUM = "SANS", ◇ PARTITION_CMP = list[int], ◇ NOM_CMP = list[text], # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('UTILISATEUR')) ◇ KSP_UTIL = not_checked, ◇ RENUM = "SANS", # Si: is_in("PRE_COND", ('JACOBI','SOR','SANS')) ◇ RENUM = / "RCMK", / "SANS" (par défaut), ), ◆ NB_MODE = int, ◇ TOLE_GLOUTON = float (défaut: 1e-10), # Si: (equal_to("OPERATION", 'TRONCATURE')) ◆ MODELE_REDUIT = modele, # Si: (equal_to("OPERATION", 'ORTHO')) ◇ ALPHA = float (défaut: 0.717), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands The operator returns a data structure of type mode_empi (empirical modes). 2.1 Operand BASE It is possible to enrich a basis of empirical modes by the following operations. In this case, one supplies it here. 2.2 Operand OPERATION This keyword makes it possible to choose the way of computing the empirical modes: - By a POD (OPERATION='POD'): one carries out an SVD on the snapshot matrix containing the results over a transient. This operation is exact (in the sense of the extraction of the empirical modes) but may potentially be costly (in CPU and in memory); - By an incremental POD (OPERATION='POD_INCR'): one builds the empirical basis in an incremental manner (see R5.01.50). This method is less accurate than the classical POD but much less costly. Moreover, it makes it possible to enrich an existing empirical basis with new results; - By a greedy method (OPERATION='GLOUTON', see R5.01.50) on parametric problems; It is also possible to truncate a basis (primal or dual) onto a reduced domain (for example produced by the command DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT) with OPERATION='TRONCATURE' or to re-orthogonalise an existing basis by the keyword OPERATION='ORTHO'. 2.3 Operands for the POD strategies 2.3.1 Operand RESULTAT Name of the result data structure to be analysed in order to generate the reduced basis. Two possible types of result: evol_noli or evol_ther. Limitations of use: - Works only in 3D (thermal and mechanical); - One cannot use Dirichlet boundary conditions by dualisation (AFFE_CHAR_MECA or AFFE_CHAR_THER). One must use Dirichlet boundary conditions by elimination (AFFE_CHAR_CINE). 2.3.2 Operand SNAPSHOT This keyword makes it possible to filter the time instants in the result given by the keyword RESULTAT in order to generate the snapshot matrix. The selected time instants are referenced by their order number. 2.3.3 Operand TABL_COOR_REDUIT When one computes an empirical basis by the incremental POD method in order to enrich an already existing basis, it is necessary to have the reduced coordinates of the previous analysis. These coordinates are stored in a data structure table named 'COOR_REDUIT' which is attached to the empirical basis. One can recover it via the operator RECU_TABLE. For example: coorredp = RECU_TABLE(CO=base, NOM_TABLE="COOR_REDUIT") But if you recover the previously computed empirical basis, by using an operator such as LIRE_RESU (in particular in MED format), this table is not available. The keyword TABL_COOR_REDUIT therefore makes it possible to give it to DEFI_BASE_REDUITE. It is therefore necessary beforehand to have saved this table at the same time as the empirical basis (by an IMPR_TABLE), then to recover it (by a LIRE_TABLE) in order to give it to DEFI_BASE_REDUITE. A typical succession of commands is therefore the following: 1. Creation of a first reduced basis - non-linear analysis - creation of the basis with DEFI_BASE_REDUITE - recovery of the table of reduced coordinates with RECU_TABLE - saving of the empirical basis by IMPR_RESU - saving of the table of reduced coordinates by IMPR_TABLE 2. Enrichment of the reduced basis - non-linear analysis - reading of the previous empirical basis by LIRE_RESU - reading of the previous table of reduced coordinates by LIRE_TABLE - enrichment of the reduced basis by DEFI_BASE_REDUITE by giving the previous basis (keyword BASE) and the previous table of reduced coordinates (keyword TABL_COOR_REDUIT) 2.3.4 Operand NOM_CHAM One specifies the type of field of the reduced basis. The possible fields are: - 'DEPL', 'SIEF_NOEU', 'SIEF_ELGA' or 'VARI_ELGA' if the data structure is of type evol_noli; - 'TEMP' or 'FLUX_NOEU' if the data structure is of type evol_ther. 2.3.5 Operands NOM_CMP and NOM_VARI It is possible to select the name of the component on which the empirical modes will be built. For the VARI_ELGA fields, it is strongly recommended to build one basis per component type. In this case, the use of NOM_VARI is possible and allows the user to give the name of the internal variable (e.g.: 'EPSEQ') rather than its order number (e.g.: 'V1'). In practice the modes will have the same number of components as the initial field but the components not selected by these keywords will have a zero value. 2.3.6 Operand TYPE_BASE One specifies the type of reduced basis. The line-type case is specific to the numerical simulation of welding. This case requires specifying the welding axis and information concerning the section of the welded zone, perpendicular to the welding axis. 2.3.7 Operands AXE and SECTION Operands used in the line-type case (specific to the numerical simulation of welding). AXE makes it possible to specify the welding axis. SECTION makes it possible to specify the node group contained in the first section of the mesh of the welded zone. Note These operands make it possible to define a local numbering used for the analysis of the reduced modes. 2.3.8 Operands NB_MODE / TOLE_SVD TOLE_SVD denotes the tolerance retained for the SVD. The default value is 1.0E-6. The selected modes are those whose singular value is greater than tole x sing_maxi where sing_maxi is the maximum singular value given by the SVD. Note The incremental POD (OPERATION='POD_INCR') also performs an SVD but not on the snapshot matrix. This parameter is therefore also useful in this case. NB_MODE is the number of modes retained for the construction of the reduced basis. The user must supply only one of the two operands in order to fix the number of modes retained for the construction of the reduced basis. 2.3.9 Operand TOLE This parameter makes it possible to adjust the accuracy of the incremental POD. 2.4 Operands for the GLOUTON strategies The method OPERATION='GLOUTON' makes it possible to build an empirical basis on a parameterised problem. The basic principle is to build the linear system which solves the targeted problem and to give the list of the parameters which vary. The empirical basis is then built by a greedy-type algorithm (greedy algorithm) to which one must supply the variation of the parameters. The linear system will thus be written: \sum_{i=1}^{{n}_{m}}{\alpha}_{i}\left({\gamma}_{j=1,{n}_{p}}\right){M}_{i}=\sum_{i=1}^{{n}_{v}}{\beta}_{i}\left({\gamma}_{j=1,{n}_{p}}\right){V}_{i} It contains {n}_{m} assembled matrices {M}_{i} (real or complex). These matrices can be built in the classical way in code_aster (CALC_MATR_ELEM and ASSE_MATRICE for example). In front of each matrix, there is a coefficient {\alpha}_{i=1,{n}_{m}} , which is either constant (real or complex), or a function or a formula (real or complex) which depends on at most {\gamma}_{j=1,{n}_{p}} parameters. Finally, the right-hand side V is also a linear combination of {n}_{v} vectors (real or complex) with a coefficient {\beta}_{i=1,{n}_{v}} , which is either constant (real or complex), or a function or a formula (real or complex) which depends on at most {\gamma}_{j=1,{n}_{p}} parameters. In order to build the empirical basis, one must traverse the space of the parameters, which the user defines by the parameter spaces. 2.4.1 Operands MATR_ASSE and VECT_ASSE These operands will build the linear system to be solved. One gives the list of the assembled matrices {M}_{i} by the factor keyword MATR_ASSE. The name of the matrix (coming for example from the command ASSE_MATRICE) is given in MATRICE. One then chooses the coefficient in front of each matrix. This coefficient is either constant (real by COEF_R or complex by COEF_C), or a function (real by FONC_R or complex by FONC_C). In the case of a function, it must depend on the parameters whose list (the variation) is given by the factor keyword VARI_PARA (see parameter space). The keywords define the right-hand side V by the keyword VECT_ASSE. One then chooses the coefficient in front of each vector. This coefficient is either constant (real by COEF_R or complex by COEF_C), or a function (real by FONC_R or complex by FONC_C). In the case of a function, it must depend on the parameters whose list (the variation) is given by the factor keyword VARI_PARA (see parameter space). 2.4.2 Operands VARI_PARA, NB_VARI_COEF and TYPE_VARI_COEF These operands define the parametric space traversed in order to build the empirical basis. NB_VARI_COEF gives the number of parameters when one traverses the parametric space. The keyword TYPE_VARI_COEF makes it possible to state that one is going to give explicitly the list of the values of the parameters (the only mode available for the moment). The factor keyword VARI_PARA gives the list of the parameters {\gamma}_{j=1,{n}_{p}} and their values. For each occurrence, one gives the name of the parameter in NOM_PARA. This parameter is necessarily used in the coefficients {\alpha}_{i=1,{n}_{m}} in front of the matrices. For each parameter, one gives the list of its values by VALE_PARA. The length of the vector VALE_PARA is necessarily equal to NB_VARI_COEF. One must also give an initial value VALE_INIT (which initialises the greedy algorithm). 2.4.3 Operand SOLVEUR This keyword gives the parameters of the solver used (see U4.50.01). Indeed the greedy algorithm will solve the defined linear system a large number of times. 2.4.4 Operand ORTHO_BASE This keyword makes it possible to carry out an orthonormalisation of the empirical basis when ORTHO_BASE='OUI'. This orthonormalisation is carried out with an iterative Gram-Schmidt type algorithm (IGS) following the Kahan-Parlett version. 2.4.5 Operand TYPE_BASE When TYPE_BASE='IFS_STAB', one creates an empirical basis which will be stable when it is used for fluid-structure interaction models (model \lbrace u,p,\varphi \rbrace see R4.02.02) in transient dynamics. The strategy consists in building an empirical basis by diagonalisation of three bases on each of the components (see R5.01.50). When one activates this keyword, a check of the components present is carried out on the components of the input result. 2.5 Other operations 2.5.1 Truncation of a basis The method OPERATION='TRONCATURE' makes it possible to truncate an empirical basis onto a model more restricted than the one which was used to build the basis. This operation is essential when one carries out model hyper-reduction (see keyword DOMAINE_REDUIT in STAT_NON_LINE and THER_NON_LINE). The input keyword BASE gives the empirical basis to be truncated. The keyword MODELE_REDUIT gives the model onto which the basis will be truncated. It is indeed the model and not the mesh. 2.5.2 Orthonormalisation of a basis The method OPERATION='ORTHO' makes it possible to orthonormalise an empirical basis. A standard POD procedure makes it possible to obtain an orthonormal basis. On the other hand, it may happen in certain cases that a basis is not orthonormal: - when one uses a greedy-type algorithm, - when one uses an incremental POD type algorithm with certain parameter values that are too "relaxed", - when the initial system to be solved is ill-conditioned. The input keyword BASE gives the empirical basis to be orthonormalised. This orthonormalisation is carried out with an iterative Gram-Schmidt type algorithm (IGS) following the Kahan-Parlett version. The parameter ALPHA makes it possible to adjust the algorithm. The larger it is, the less the algorithm will iterate but the more imperfect the orthonormalisation will be. 3 Examples of use Example of use of the incremental mode by enrichment (OPERATION='POD_INCR'): mat1 = AFFE_MATERIAU(AFFE=_F(TOUT="OUI", MATER=acier1)) resu1 = STAT_NON_LINE(CHAM_MATER=mat1, ...) mode1 = DEFI_BASE_REDUITE(RESULTAT=resu1, OPERATION="POD", NOM_CHAM="DEPL") mat2 = AFFE_MATERIAU(AFFE=_F(TOUT="OUI", MATER=acier2)) resu2 = STAT_NON_LINE(CHAM_MATER=mat2, ...) mode1 = DEFI_BASE_REDUITE(reuse=mode1, OPERATION="POD_INCR", RESULTAT=resu2, NOM_CHAM="DEPL") The empirical basis mode1 has been built on two sets of material parameters. - In the example above, the first DEFI_BASE_REDUITE could have been used in incremental mode (OPERATION='POD_INCR'); - With a very small tolerance (keyword TOLE), the incremental mode tends towards a classical SVD. Notes

u4.67.02 Operator DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT u4.67.02 Operator DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT The purpose of the operator is to enrich an existing mesh with groups (of mesh cells or of nodes) which define a subdomain called the reduced integration domain (RID). The operator relies on one or more result data structures of type mode_empi in order to determine specific nodes, called interpolation points, by applying the discrete empirical interpolation method (DEIM). The reduced integration domain is the set of mesh cells located in the neighbourhood of these interpolation points. The operator enriches the mesh data structure by creating two groups: - a mesh-cell group corresponding to the reduced domain; - a node group corresponding to the interface between the reduced domain and the rest of the initial domain. 1 Syntax maillage = DEFI_DOMAINE_REDUIT( ◆ reuse = , ◆ BASE_PRIMAL = mode_empi, ◆ BASE_DUAL = mode_empi, ◆ NOM_DOMAINE = text, ◇ NB_COUCHE_SUPPL = int (défaut: 0), ◆ GROUP_NO_INTERF = text, ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ DOMAINE_MINI = _F( ◇ GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ GROUP_MA = grma, ), ◇ DOMAINE_MAXI = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ), ◇ CORR_COMPLET = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: (equal_to("CORR_COMPLET", 'OUI')) ◆ GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE = text, ◇ NB_COUCHE_ENCASTRE = int (défaut: 0), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands 2.1 Operands BASE_PRIMAL and BASE_DUAL ♦ BASE_PRIMAL = base1, [mode_empi] ♦ BASE_DUAL = base2, [mode_empi] Nom desstructuresde données résultat de type mode_empi à analyser pour générer les points d'interpolation. Les deux bases base1 et base2 sont calculées à l'aide de l'opérateur DEFI_BASE_REDUITE [:ref: U4.67.01 ]. Le calcul de la base base1 s'appuie sur un champ de température ou un champ de déplacement. Le calcul de la base base2 s'appuie sur un champ de flux ou un champ de contrainte. 2.2 Operand MAILLAGE ♦ MAILLAGE = mail, [maillage] La commande va enrichir un concept maillage déjà existant avec les nouveaux groupes de nœuds et de mailles définis par DOMAINE_INCLUS, GROUP_NO_INTERFACEet GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE. Le mot-clef MAILLAGE est donc obligatoire. 2.3 Operand NOM_DOMAINE ♦ NOM_DOMAINE = nom_d On précise le nom du groupe de mailles correspondant au RID. 2.4 Operand GROUP_NO_INTERF ♦ GROUP_NO_INTERF = nom_i On précise le nom du groupe de nœuds contenus dans l'interface entre le RID et le reste du domaine. 2.5 Operand NB_COUCHE_SUPPL ◊ NB_COUCHE_SUPPL = nb_couche, [I] Par défaut, la commande construit le groupe RID en sélectionnant les mailles attachées aux points magiques (application de la dEIM, voir [:external:ref: R5.01.05 ]). Quand on utilise le mot-clef NB_COUCH_SUPPL, on peut agrandir le RID en prenant nb_couched'éléments supplémentaires autour du RID initial. Par défaut, nb_couche =0. 2.6 Operand DOMAINE_MINI / DOMAINE_MAXI > ◊ DOMAINE_MINI = _F( ◊ GROUP_MA = lgma1, [l_gr_maille] ◊ GROUP_NO = lgno1, [l_gr_noeud] ) Ce mot-clef facteur facultatif permet de mettre une partie du maillage dans le RID même si l''algorithme de recherche des points magiques par dEIM (voir [:external:ref: R5.01.05 ]) ne le permet pas. C'est très utile en particulier pour «forcer» l'intégration d'une partie des conditions limites dans le RID. On peut soit ajouter des nœuds, soit ajouter des mailles. ◊ DOMAINE_MAXI = _F( ◊ GROUP_MA = lgma1, [l_gr_maille] ) De manière symétrique, il est possible de restreindre la taille du domaine réduit RID par le mot-clef DOMAINE_MAXI. Cette option est utile lors de la réalisation de modèles incrémentaux comme le soudage multi-passe ou excavation. 2.7 Operands CORR_COMPLET / GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE / NB_COUCHE_ENCASTRE ◊ CORR_COMPLET = /'NON' [DEFAUT] /'OUI' Si CORR_COMPLET = 'OUI' { ♦ GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE = grno ◊ NB_COUCHE_ENCASTRE = /0 [DEFAUT] /nb_couche, [I] } Pour améliorer la qualité des résultats en hyper-réduction, il est possible de faire une correction du calcul hyper-réduit par un calcul élément fini détaillé avec CORR_COMPLET='OUI'. Pour celà, il est nécessaire de définir un groupe de noeuds servant à faire la liaison entre le RID et le reste du modèle avec le mot-clef GROUP_NO_ENCASTRE. Ce groupe de noeuds permet d'imposer les conditions limites de Dirichlet nécessaire à ce que le problème corrigé soit bien défini. Par défaut (NB_COUCHE_ENCASTRE=0), ce groupe de noeuds est défini à l'intérieur du domaine réduit (mot-clef NOM_DOMAINE) en prenant les premiers noeuds contenus dans le domaine et liés aux noeuds définis par GROUP_NO_INTERF. Il est possible de rendre le domaine plus grand en utilisant le mot-clef NB_COUCHE_ENCASTRE. De par la construction de ces groupes de noeuds, on a nécessairement NB_COUCHE_ENCASTRE inférieur ou égal à NB_COUCHE_SUPPL.

u4.67.03 Operator REST_REDUIT_COMPLET u4.67.03 Operator REST_REDUIT_COMPLET The purpose of the operator is to reconstruct the solutions on a complete model from a reduced model. The operator reconstructs an evol_ther or an evol_noli from an empirical basis (see U4.67.01, operator DEFI_BASE_REDUITE) and from the result of a reduced analysis. 1 Syntax / evol_noli / evol_ther = REST_REDUIT_COMPLET( ◆ CHAM_GD = _F( ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "TEMP", / "SIEF_NOEU", / "FLUX_NOEU", / "SIEF_ELGA", / "VARI_ELGA", ◆ BASE = mode_empi, ◆ OPERATION = / "GAPPY_POD", / "COMB", # Si: equal_to("OPERATION", 'GAPPY_POD') ◇ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, ), ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ RESULTAT_REDUIT = resultat, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TABL_COOR_REDUIT = table, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands 2.1 Operand RESULTAT_REDUIT ♦ RESULTAT_REDUIT = base2, [resultat_sdaster] This keyword gives the result data structure (evol_ther or evol_noli) which comes from the reduced analysis with THER_NON_LINE or STAT_NON_LINE. This data structure contains all the information necessary to reconstruct the results on the model given by the keyword MODELE. 2.2 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = modele [modele_sdaster] Nom du modèle sur lequel va être reconstruit la structure de données résultat. Il doit être différent du modèle sur lequel repose la structure de données résultat RESULTAT_REDUIT. 2.3 Factor keyword CHAM_GD ♦ CHAM_GD = _F( ♦ NOM_CHAM = /'DEPL', [TXM] /'TEMP', /'SIEF_NOEU', /'FLUX_NOEU', /'SIEF_ELGA', /'VARI_ELGA', ♦ BASE = base, [mode_empi] ♦ OPERATION = /'GAPPY_POD', [TXM] /'COMB', ◊ GROUP_NO_INTERF = grno, [grno]) Ce mot-clef facteur répétable permet de définir quels champs doivent être reconstruits et de quelle manière. NOM_CHAM donne le type de champ à reconstruire. La liste actuelle est exhaustive (on ne peut pas reconstruire un champ qui n'appartient pas à cette liste) La commande interdit de reconstruire un champ qui n'existe pas dans la structure de données initiale donnée par RESULTAT_REDUIT. Chaque champ reconstruit a besoin de sa base empirique donnée par le mot-clef BASE (calculée par DEFI_BASE_REDUITE). Des vérifications de cohérence sont faites entre la base donnée par l'utilisateur et le champ reconstruit. Un champ peut être reconstruit de deux manières par le mot-clef OPERATION: - Par recombinaison «modale»: il s'agit simplement de la somme pondérée des modes empiriques par les coordonnées réduites (voir TABL_COOR_REDUIT ). - Par Gappy-POD. L'opération consiste à reconstituer les coordonnées réduites en minimisant la différence entre le champ partiellement calculé sur le domaine réduit (voir commandes THER_NON_LINE et STAT_NON_LINE) et à recalculer ensuite le champ complet sur le domaine par combinaison linéaire. The keyword GROUP_NO_INTERF gives the node group defining the interface between the reduced domain and the rest of the model (see commands THER_NON_LINE and STAT_NON_LINE). 2.4 Operand TABL_COOR_REDUIT ◊ TABL_COOR_REDUIT = tabl_coor, Lorsqu'on recalcule un champ par combinaison modale, il est nécessaire de disposer des coordonnées réduites du calcul. Ces coordonnées sont stockées dans une structure de données tablede nom 'COOR_REDUIT'qui est attachée à la structure de données résultat. On peut la récupérer via l'opérateur RECU_TABLE. Par exemple: coorredp=RECU_TABLE(CO=resunl,NOM_TABLE='COOR_REDUIT') Mais si vous récupérez la base empirique précédemment calculée par un opérateur comme LIRE_RESU (en particulier au format MED), cette table n'est pas disponible. L'opérateur TABL_COOR_REDUIT permet donc de la donner à REST_REDUIT_COMPLET. Il est donc nécessaire en amont d'avoir sauvegardé cette table en même temps que le résultat non-linéaire (par un IMPR_TABLE), puis de la récupérer (par un LIRE_TABLE) pour la donner à REST_REDUIT_COMPLET. 2.5 Output data structure La structure de données de sortie est une sd_resultatstandard de code_aster.

u4.71.00 Selection of one or more fields in a RESULTAT data structure u4.71.00 Selection of one or more fields in a RESULTAT data structure 1 Purpose Description of the keywords for access to the fields of quantities (grandeurs) of a data structure of type resultat. In order to extract a field of quantities (grandeurs) in a result concept one has two types of indicators: the symbolic names and the access variables. This document describes all the keywords making it possible to access the fields of quantities (grandeurs) contained in a result data structure and used in the commands CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04, CALC_G U4.82.03, COMB_SISM_MODAL U4.84.01, EXTR_MODE U4.52.12, IMPR_GENE U4.91.02, IMPR_RESU U4.91.01, LIRE_RESU U7.02.01, POST_ELEM U4.81.22, POST_RCCM U4.83.11, POST_RELEVE_T U4.81.21, RECU_FONCTION U4.32.03, TEST_RESU U4.92.01. 2 Syntax # Extraction d’un champ de grandeur de resu ◇ / TOUT_CHAM = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NOM_CHAM = text, ◇ / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = int, / TOUT_INST = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / INST = float, / FREQ = float, / TOUT_MODE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_MODE = int, / NOEUD_CMP = text, / LIST_INST = listr8, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, / LIST_ORDRE = listis, / LIST_MODE = listis, / NOM_CAS = text, / ANGLE = float, ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, 3 Extraction of a field of a quantity (grandeur) 3.1 Choice of the symbolic names: Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM / TOUT_CHAM = /'OUI' [DEFAUT] This keyword indicates that one wants to access the field(s) of quantities (grandeurs) actually computed for the result concept RESU. If one does not use the operand NOM_CHAM, this operand is taken by default as 'OUI'. The possible fields are described in the specific documentations of the result concepts. Example: the possible fields are, for a result of type evol_elas U4.51.01: DEPL SIGM_ELNO EPSI_ELNO … … … / NOM_CHAM = L_NOMSYMB [:ref: l_K16 ] A result concept may be composed of several fields of quantities (grandeurs) of nodal-field type or field-by-element type. This keyword makes it possible to choose a list of symbolic field names from among all the possible ones (cf. TOUT_CHAM). Note: The keywords TOUT_CHAM and NOM_CHAM cannot be used simultaneously. 3.2 Choice of the order numbers: Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to access the field(s) for all the order numbers already computed. Example: - all the time instants for a result of type evol_... - all the eigenmodes for a result of type mode_meca. / NUME_ORDRE : LORDRE [l_I] This keyword makes it possible to access only the field(s) corresponding to a list of order numbers LORDRE (the plural is used here for the case where one has chosen TOUT_CHAM='OUI'). Exemple : RESU =(_F( RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM = ‘OUI’, NUME_ORDRE= (3,6)) One will access all the fields computed at the third and at the sixth order number. / LIST_ORDRE : LENTI [listis] The keyword LIST_ORDRE indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of order numbers LENTI, defined by the operator DEFI_LIST_ENTI U4.34.02 (LENTI is therefore a concept of type listis). Example: LISTE = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( VALE = (3,6)) RESU =(_F ( RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM = ‘OUI’, LIST_ORDRE= LISTE ) One will access all the fields computed at the third and at the sixth order number. 3.3 Other ways of choosing the order numbers: access variables 3.3.1 Operands TOUT_MODE / NUME_MODE / LIST_MODE / NOEUD_CMP / TOUT_MODE = 'OUI' This keyword indicates that one wants to access all the fields for all the mode numbers already computed. It is licit only for the types of result concept (static or dynamic modes) having NUME_MODE as access variable. / NUME_MODE = LMODE [l_I] This keyword indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of mode numbers LMODE. These numbers are those assigned by the analysis algorithm. It is licit only for the types of result concept (static or dynamic modes) having NUME_MODE as access variable. Exemple : RESU =(_F(RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM =‘OUI’, NUME_MODE= (3,6)) One will access all the fields corresponding to the third and to the sixth mode. / LIST_MODE = LENTI [listis] The keyword LIST_MODE indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of mode numbers LENTI, defined by the operator DEFI_LIST_ENTI U4.34.02 (LENTI is therefore a concept of type listis). It is valid only for the types of result concept having NUME_MODE as access variable. Example: LISTE = DEFI_LIST_ENTI ( VALE = (3,6)) RESU =(_F( RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM = ‘OUI’, LIST_MODE= LISTE ) One will access all the fields corresponding to the third and to the sixth mode. / NOEUD_CMP = LNOECMP [:ref: l_K16 ] Results of type base_modale or mode_stat have NOEUD_CMP as access variable. The value of these access variables is obtained by concatenating the name of the node and the name of the component. In order to specify a value of the access variable, the user will give two names, the name of the node followed by the name of the component. A list of n access variables will be introduced by the data of n pairs (name of the node, name of the component). A list of values of this access variable can be supplied by the list (\mathit{couple1},\mathit{couple2},\dots ) . 3.3.2 Operand NOM_CAS / NOM_CAS = NCAS [:ref: K16 ] The keyword NOM_CAS indicates that one wants to access the field corresponding to a loading case. It is licit only for result concepts of type mult_elas which have NOM_CAS as access variable and are produced by MACRO_ELAS_MULT U4.51.02. 3.3.3 Operand ANGLE / ANGLE = LANGL [l_R] The keyword ANGLE indicates that one wants to access the recombined field(s) for a list of angles. It is licit only for result concepts of type comb_fourier which have ANGLE as access variable and are produced by the operator COMB_FOURIER U4.83.31. 3.3.4 Operands FREQ / LIST_FREQ These operands are licit only for the types of result concept having FREQ as access variable (mode_meca, dyna_harm, …). / FREQ = LFREQ [l_R] The keyword FREQ indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of frequencies LFREQ. Exemple : RESU =(_F(RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM =‘OUI’, FREQ= (3.52,7.37)) One will access all the fields corresponding to the frequencies 3.52 and 7.37 . / LIST_FREQ = LREEL listr8 The keyword LIST_FREQ indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of frequencies LREEL, defined by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL (LREEL is therefore a concept of type listr8). Example: LISTE = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( VALE = (3.52,7.37)) RESU =(_F(RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM = ‘OUI’, LIST_FREQ = LISTE ) One will access all the fields corresponding to the frequencies 3.52 and 7.37 . 3.3.5 Operands TOUT_INST / INST / LIST_INST These operands are licit only for the types of result concept of time evolution having INST as access variables (evol_noli, evol_ther, dyna_trans, …). / TOUT_INST = 'OUI' This keyword indicates that one wants to access all the fields for all the time instants already computed. / INST = LINST [l_R] The keyword INST indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of time instants LINST. Exemple : RESU =(_F( RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM = ‘OUI’, INST= (3. , 7.)) One will access all the fields corresponding to the time instants 3. and 7. . / LIST_INST = LREEL listr8 The keyword LIST_INST indicates that one wants to access the field(s) corresponding to a list of time instants LREEL, defined by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL (LREEL is therefore a concept of type listr8). Example: LISTE = DEFI_LIST_REEL ( VALE = (3. , 7.)) RESU =(_F( RESULTAT= RESU, TOUT_CHAM = ‘OUI’, LIST_INST= LISTE ) One will access all the fields corresponding to the time instants 3. and 7. . 3.3.6 Operands PRECISION / CRITERE These operands make it possible to refine the access by real access variables of time or of frequency. PRECISION = / prec [R] / 1.0D-3 ou 1.0D-6 [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to indicate that one searches for all the fields whose time instant (respectively the frequency) lies in the interval "inst ± prec" (cf. CRITERE). By default prec = 1.0D-3 or prec = 1.0D-6 (according to the commands). If CRITERE='ABSOLU', there is no default value. CRITERE = / 'RELATIF' [DEFAUT] / 'ABSOLU' 'RELATIF': the search interval is: [inst (1 - prec), inst (1 + prec)] 'ABSOLU': the search interval is: [inst - prec, inst + prec].

u4.71.02 Operator RECU_TABLE u4.71.02 Operator RECU_TABLE 1 Purpose Permet de récupérer dans une table les valeurs d’un paramètre d’une structure de données résultat, ou bien, d’extraire une table contenue dans une autre structure de données pour celles qui le permettent. La table créée peut alors être utilisée dans d’autres commandes (IMPR_TABLE par exemple). Produit une structure de données de type table. 2 Syntax table = RECU_TABLE( ◆ CO = datastructure, ◆ / NOM_TABLE = text, / NOM_PARA = text, / TOUT_PARA = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands ♦ CO = nomsd , Name of the data structure from which one wants to extract a table. ♦ / NOM_TABLE = nomtab , Name of the table stored in the data structure. Today, the data structures containing a table which one can extract by RECU_TABLE / NOM_TABLE are the following: - a data structure of type evol_noli obtained by STAT_NON_LINE or DYNA_NON_LINE; the name of the table is then 'OBSERVATION', - a data structure of type maillage. The name of the table is then 'CARA_GEOM', - a data structure of type cabl_precont obtained by the command DEFI_CABLE_BP. The name of the table is then 'CABLE_BP', - a data structure of type melasflu obtained by the command CALC_FLUI_STRU; the name of the table is then 'MATR_GENE'. - the data structures of type evol_elas and evol_noli containing the global error estimators computed by CALC_ERREUR. The name of the table is then 'ESTI_GLOB'. - a data structure of type evol_noli obtained by STAT_NON_LINE or DYNA_NON_LINE, or of type evol_elas obtained by DYNA_VIBRA on a physical basis, contains a table named 'PARA_CALC' comprising the list of the time instants actually computed and, if the user activates the analysis, the energy balance. The table contains 7 columns: - INST: analysis time instant, - TRAV_EXT: work of the external forces, - ENER_CIN: kinetic energy, - ENER_TOT: total strain energy, - TRAV_AMOR: energy dissipated by damping, - TRAV_LIAI: energy dissipated and/or stored by the connections, - DISS_SCH: energy dissipated by the numerical scheme. ♦ / NOM_PARA = lpara , List of the names of the parameters to be extracted from the SD RESULTAT nomsd. This functionality makes it possible to extract, in the form of a table, the evolution of certain parameters of an SD RESULTAT, for example the piloting parameter ETA_PILOTAGE in the case of an SD of type evol_noli. The extracted parameters must be of integer, real or complex type, thereby excluding character strings. The first column of the table produced contains the order numbers (NUME_ORDRE) and the following ones contain the evolution of the parameters lpara. ♦ / TOUT_PARA = ‘OUI’ , This keyword makes it possible to extract all the parameters of the SD RESULTAT nomsd of integer, real or complex type. This produces the same table as if one gives all these parameters to NOM_PARA. ◊ TITRE = titr , Title which one wants to give to the result table. 4 Examples - recovery of a few geometric characteristics of a mesh: cargeo = RECU_TABLE ( CO= maillage , NOM_TABLE= 'CARA_GEOM' ,) - recovery of the values "observed" in the command DYNA_NON_LINE The command DYNA_NON_LINE U4.53.01 makes it possible to choose a set of mesh cells or of nodes for which one wishes to observe one or more components of certain fields (keyword OBSERVATION). dynl = DYNA_NON_LINE ( ... OBSERVATION= _F ( ... ) ... ) tabobs = RECU_TABLE ( CO= dynl , NOM_TABLE= 'OBSERVATION' , ) - recovery of the piloting parameter of an SD of type evol_noli stnl = STAT_NON_LINE ( ... PILOTAGE= _F ( ... ) ... ) etapilo = RECU_TABLE ( CO= stnl , NOM_PARA= 'ETA_PILOTAGE' ,)

u4.71.03 Operator RECU_GENE u4.71.03 Operator RECU_GENE 1 Purpose Extract a vector of generalised displacements, velocities or accelerations from a result which is itself in generalised coordinates. Their extraction takes place for given discretisations (time instants or frequencies). 2 Syntax vect_asse_gene = RECU_GENE( ◆ RESU_GENE = tran_gene / harm_gene, ◆ / INST = float, / FREQ = float, ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "ACCE", # Si: exists("INST") and not exists("FREQ") ◇ INTERPOL = / "NON" (par défaut), / "LIN", ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESU_GENE ♦ RESU_GENE = resgen Concept of type tran_gene or harm_gene which contains, for different discretisations (time instants or frequencies), generalised vectors of displacement, velocity or acceleration type. 3.2 Operand NOM_CHAM ◊ NOM_CHAM = nomcha Character string designating the symbolic name of the field which one wishes to extract: 'DEPL', 'VITE' or 'ACCE'. 3.3 Operand INST ♦ INST = instant For a transient result (tran_gene), the time instant for which one wishes to extract a generalised vector. 3.4 Operand INTERPOL For a transient result (tran_gene): ◊ INTERPOL = | 'NON': | the extraction must be carried out in the strict sense, | | --- | --- | | 'LIN': | an interpolation is authorised between two fields: this interpolation may be unacceptable between two archiving time instants which do not correspond to consecutive analysis time instants of DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. | 3.5 Operands CRITERE and PRECISION For a transient result (tran_gene): ◊ CRITERE = / 'ABSOLU' / 'RELATIF' - ◊ PRECISION = prec Indicate with what accuracy the search for the time instant must be carried out. | 'ABSOLU': | search interval | [instant-prec, instant+ prec]. | | --- | --- | --- | | 'RELATIF': | search interval | [(1-prec).instant, (1+prec).instant]. | | | | | | | | | | Note: If CRITERE='ABSOLU' | then the keyword PRECISION becomes mandatory. | | 3.6 Operand FREQ ♦ FREQ = freq For a harmonic result (harm_gene), the frequency for which one wishes to extract a generalised vector.

The reduction of the size of the result data structure is obtained by archiving part of the fields which it contains. One can choose the fields to be archived either by indicating the fields to be kept, or by indicating the fields to be excluded. The extraction can also be carried out on a part of the mesh or of the model on which the result data structure is based. One can reduce the quantity of memory used by the study by overwriting the result object, that is to say by reusing the same variable name. Example: result = EXTR_RESU(RESULTAT=result, ...) The memory will actually be recovered when the useless objects are automatically deleted. 2 Syntax / acou_harmo / dyna_harmo / dyna_trans / evol_elas / evol_noli / evol_sech / evol_ther / evol_varc / "VITE_ABSOLU", / "VITE_VENT", ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ◆ / LIST_ARCH = listis, / NUME_ORDRE = list[int], / INST = list[float], / FREQ = list[float], / NUME_MODE = list[int], / NOEUD_CMP = list[text], / LIST_INST = listr8, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, / LIST_ORDRE = listis, / NOM_CAS = text, / PAS_ARCH = int, ), ◇ RESTREINT = _F( ◆ / MAILLAGE = maillage, / MODELE = modele, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT Initial result data structure. - If the result contains one (or more) tables, for example: 'OBSERVATION', 'PARA_CALC', ..., these are ignored by the command. - Concepts of type FOURIER_THER are not processed by the operator EXTR_RESU. Notes 3.2 Factor keyword ARCHIVAGE Defines the fields to be saved. This keyword cannot be repeated more than once. 3.2.1 Operands LIST_ARCH and PAS_ARCH Define the order numbers to be saved. - LIST_ARCH: list of the order numbers obtained by the command DEFI_LIST_ENTI U4.34.02, - PAS_ARCH: saving of the results starting from the first, every n order numbers. 3.2.2 Operands CHAM_EXCLU and NOM_CHAM Defines the types of fields which one does not wish to save (SIEF_ELNO, ...) according to the type of the input result data structure. In order to specify the fields which one does not wish to save, one can: - either list the fields to be kept with the operand NOM_CHAM, - or list the fields to be excluded with the operand CHAM_EXCLU. If one of the fields to be retained is not part of the result data structure, the code stops in fatal error. 3.3 Factor keyword RESTREINT This keyword makes it possible to restrict the fields of the result onto a restricted mesh built with the aid of the command CREA_MAILLAGE, option RESTREINT. In the case where the restriction concerns only nodal fields, the user may supply only the restricted mesh by means of the keyword MAILLAGE. If the restriction also concerns fields by element, it is necessary to supply a restricted MODELE based on the restricted mesh. If the model contains structural elements (beams, plates, ...), it is in general necessary to supply a restricted CARA_ELEM. For certain post-processings, it may also be necessary to supply a restricted CHAM_MATER. 3.4 Operand TITRE Title given to the data structure RESUOUT created (cf. U4.03.01). 3.5 Operands NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / NUME_MODE / NOEUD_CMP / NOM_CAS / PRECISION / CRITERE Selection in a result data structure ( cf. U4.71.00). 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = info In the case where INFO=2, the parameters of each extracted field are displayed. 4 Examples Copy into the data structure FREQ2 of one mode out of 8 of the data structure FREQ. FREQ = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=MATASSR, MATR_MASS=MATASSM, OPTION="AJUSTE", CALC_FREQ=_F(FREQ=(5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 24.0, 27.0, 30.0, 32.0)), SOLVEUR_MODAL=_F(OPTION_INV="DIRECT"), ) FREQ2 = EXTR_RESU(RESULTAT=FREQ, ARCHIVAGE=_F(PAS_ARCH=8))

u4.71.05 1 u4.71.05 Procedure EXTR_TABLE Organisation(s): EDF-R&D/AMA 1 u4.71.05 Procedure EXTR_TABLE 1 Purpose Extract a concept from a table. The table may be a table_container coming from the command CALCUL. The extracted concepts are then elementary matrices, elementary vectors or fields. The table may have been obtained by the operator RECU_TABLE (NOM_TABLE = 'MATR_GENE' ...) from a result concept of the operator CALC_FLUI_STRU. 2 Syntax / cham_elem / vect_elem_depl_r / nappe / carte / table / cham_no / reel / matr_elem_temp_r / fonction / vect_elem_temp_r / matr_asse_gene_r / cham_gd / matr_elem_depl_r / fonction_c / entier / mode_meca = EXTR_TABLE( ◆ TYPE_RESU = / "MATR_ASSE_GENE_R", / "MATR_ELEM_DEPL_R", / "VECT_ELEM_DEPL_R", / "MATR_ELEM_TEMP_R", / "VECT_ELEM_TEMP_R", / "CHAM_GD_SDASTER", / "CHAM_NO_SDASTER", / "CARTE_SDASTER", / "CHAM_ELEM", / "MODE_MECA", / "TABLE_SDASTER", / "FONCTION_SDASTER", / "FONCTION_C", / "NAPPE_SDASTER", / "ENTIER", / "REEL", ◆ TABLE = table / table_container, ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ FILTRE = _F( ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ CRIT_COMP = / "EQ" (par défaut), / "LT", / "GT", / "NE", / "LE", / "GE", / "VIDE", / "NON_VIDE", / "MAXI", / "MAXI_ABS", / "MINI", / "MINI_ABS", # Si: (is_in("CRIT_COMP", ('EQ','NE','GT','LT','GE','LE'))) ◆ / VALE = float, / VALE_I = int, / VALE_K = text, / VALE_C = complex, ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ), ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TABLE ♦ TABLE= matable One gives the name of the table from which one wants to extract the value of a cell. 3.2 Operand TYPE_RESU ♦ TYPE_RESU: Type du résultat créé. La commande ne permet pas d'extraire tous les types de concept. Les types autorisés sont : 'MATR_ASSE_GENE_R', 'MATR_ELEM_DEPL_R', 'VECT_ELEM_DEPL_R', 'CHAM_GD_SDASTER', 'CHAM_NO_SDASTER', 'CARTE_SDASTER', 'CHAM_ELEM', 'MODE_MECA', 'FONCTION_SDASTER', 'FONCTION_C', 'NAPPE_SDASTER', 'ENTIER'. 3.3 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA= para One gives the name of the parameter identifying the column containing the cell to be extracted. 3.4 Extract a cell; keyword FILTRE This factor keyword (repeatable at will) serves to select the row containing the cell to be extracted. The use of this keyword is described in the command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre Title which one wants to give to the result of the command U4.02.01. 4 Examples Example taken from the test case sdll118a One wishes to extract from the table TT the generalised mass matrix for a given fluid velocity: MG = EXTR_TABLE ( TYPE_RESU = ‘MATR_ASSE_GENE_R’, TABLE = TT, NOM_PARA = ‘MATR_MASS’, FILTRE = _F( NOM_PARA = ‘NUME_VITE’, VALE_I = 2 ), ) #Exemple suite à CALCUL #Récupération du champ de contrainte: SIGM = EXTR_TABLE(TYPE_RESU='CHAM_GD_SDASTER', TABLE=CONT, NOM_PARA='SIEF_ELGA') #Récupération des matrices élémentaires: MATR = EXTR_TABLE(TYPE_RESU='MATR_ELEM_DEPL_R', TABLE=CONT, NOM_PARA='MATR_ELEM')

u4.71.06 Command EXTR_CONCEPT u4.71.06 Command EXTR_CONCEPT Summary: Makes it possible to extract a sub-object from a data structure of type dict . 1 Syntax evol_ther = EXTR_CONCEPT( ◆ DICT = ds_dict, ◆ NOM = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands Data structures of type dict are not Python dictionaries but their use is similar. The first data structure of this type is evol_ther_dict , in which one stores an object of type evol_ther associated with an access key. It is the only type currently supported. The command EXTR_CONCEPT returns the object stored for a given access key. 2.1 Keyword DICT Supplies the data structure of type dict . 2.2 Keyword NOM Value of the access key.

"NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("LINEARISATION", "NON") ◇ REPARTITION = / "GAUSSIENNE", / "UNIFORME" (par défaut), / "UTILISATEUR", # Si: equal_to("REPARTITION", 'UTILISATEUR') ◆ FORMULE = formule, # Si: equal_to("REPARTITION", 'GAUSSIENNE') ◆ MOYENNE = float, ◆ ECART_TYPE = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand COUPE Table containing the description of the sections. The table must have the format of the table coming from CREA_COUPE described in the paragraph COUPE of the user's manual of CREA_COUPE. Note 1: It must be noted that for each row of the table, the name of the section must be unique. Note 2: The support mesh of the newly generated fields contains mesh-cell groups and node groups for each section created as well as for each group of sections. These mesh-cell groups and node groups correspond to the names given in the table supplied Note 3: It is strongly recommended that this table be generated from the command CREA_COUPE. in order to ensure that the points at the ends are indeed on the skins of the mesh so that the sections are indeed inside the structure considered. 3.2 Operand RESULTAT Result from which the fields will be extracted on the created sections defined from the table described in paragraph u4.71.07-coupes. 3.3 Operand NOM_CHAM List of the fields to be extracted on the sections created. These fields must belong to the result concept supplied in the keyword RESULTAT. Only nodal fields can be extracted. If NOM_CHAM is not supplied, all the nodal fields are extracted on the sections. 3.4 Operand REPERE Makes it possible to determine the frame in which the values of the components of the fields will be expressed. If GLOBAL is supplied then the frame used is that of the result supplied. If LOCAL is supplied then the frame will be the local frame of each section defined as follows: - X axis: origin point → end point, - Y axis: origin point → 3rd point, then projected so that the vector is orthogonal to the X axis in the plane containing the three points (origin point, end point and 3rd point). - Z axis: orthogonal to the X and Y axes so that the frame is right-handed. 3.5 Operand LINEARISATION The operand LINEARISATION defines a section discretised by only 5 points presented in u4.71.07-fig-linearisation Diagram of the distribution of the quantity on a so-called "linearised" section The values MOMENT_0 and MOMENT_1 are those defined in §6.1 of the documentation of POST_RELEVE_T (u4.81.21). The values of the entry and exit points correspond to the value of the nodal field at these points. Any nodal field can be linearised. The selection is made with NOM_CHAM; otherwise all the nodal fields are linearised. The value of \varepsilon is 10^{-7} . 3.6 Operand REPARTITION This operand allows the user to determine the method of discretisation of the sections. The different options are: - UNIFORME : the discretisation is uniform over the whole of the section; this is the default option; - GAUSSIENNE : the distribution of the points along the section follows a normal distribution with the parameters supplied by the user in the operands MOYENNE and ECART_TYPE . These operands represent respectively the mean (lying between 0 and 1) and the standard deviation of the Gaussian distribution. - UTILISATEUR : the user supplies a formula by means of the operand FORMULE defining the distribution of the points. This formula must be defined with a single parameter defined between 0 and 1.

u4.72.01 Operator COMB_MATR_ASSE u4.72.01 Operator COMB_MATR_ASSE 1 Purpose Combine linearly, with real or complex coefficients, concepts of type matr_asse_ . This operator also makes it possible to carry out linear combinations by considering only the real or imaginary part of a matrix with complex coefficients (extraction of the real or imaginary part of a matrix). All the concepts of type matr_asse_ to be combined must share the same numbering , that is the two matrices will have been assembled by the operator ASSE_MATRICE with the same concept as argument of the keyword NUME_DDL (cf. U4.61.11). Produces a data structure of type matr_asse_ . 2 Syntax / matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_c / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r = COMB_MATR_ASSE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_c / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r, ◆ / COMB_R = _F( ◇ PARTIE = / "IMAG", / "REEL", ◆ MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_c / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r, ◆ COEF_R = float, ), / COMB_C = _F( ◆ MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_gene_c / matr_asse_gene_r / matr_asse_pres_c / matr_asse_pres_r / matr_asse_temp_c / matr_asse_temp_r, ◆ / COEF_R = float, / COEF_C = complex, ), / CALC_AMOR_GENE = _F( ◆ RIGI_GENE = matr_asse_gene_r, ◆ MASS_GENE = matr_asse_gene_r, ◆ / AMOR_REDUIT = float, / LIST_AMOR = listr8, ), ◇ SANS_CMP = "LAGR" (ou non renseigné), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword MATR_ASSE / MATR_ASSE It is possible to overwrite a matr_asse object with the result of the operation. In this case, it is mandatory to specify here which object is reused. 3.2 Keyword COMB_R / COMB_R Description of the terms of the linear combination producing a matrix with real coefficients . 3.2.1 Operand PARTIE ◊ PARTIE = / 'REEL' , / 'IMAG' , To carry out extractions or linear combinations of imaginary or real part(s) of complex matrices. 3.2.2 Operand MATR_ASSE ♦ MATR_ASSE = m Name of the concept matr_asse_ to be combined. 3.2.3 Operand COEF_R ♦ COEF_R = r Real coefficient to be applied to the concept that is the argument of MATR_ASSE. 3.3 Keyword COMB_C / COMB_C = Description of the terms of the linear combination producing a matrix with complex coefficients . 3.3.1 Reminder of the syntax of complex values Complex values may be declared in two different ways: - in the form a+\mathrm{ib} with the syntax “RI,a, b” where a and b are real numbers, - in the form (\mathrm{module},\mathrm{phase}) with “MPmod, ph” where mod and ph are real numbers (ph in degrees). 3.3.2 Operand MATR_ASSE ♦ MATR_ASSE = m Name of the concept matr_asse_ to be combined. 3.3.3 Operands COEF_R/COEF_C ♦ / COEF_R = r Real coefficient to be applied to the concept that is the argument of MATR_ASSE. / COEF_C = c Complex coefficient to be applied to the concept that is the argument of MATR_ASSE. 3.4 Keyword CALC_AMOR_GENE This keyword makes it possible to build an object of type matr_asse_gene_R corresponding to the Basile damping matrix from a list of reduced damping ratios (keyword AMOR_REDUIT or LIST_AMOR). MASS_GENE = masgen , RIGI_GENE = riggen, masgen and riggen are the 2 generalised mass and stiffness matrices. 3.5 Operand SANS_CMP = 'LAGR' This operand has the effect of setting to "zero" the terms of the resulting assembled matrix corresponding to the rows and the columns of the Lagrange degrees of freedom. 4 Examples of use 4.1 Classical linear combination mat_rs = COMB_MATR_ASSE(COMB_C = ( _F( MATR_ASSE = mat_1, COEF_R = 1.), _F( MATR_ASSE= mat_2, COEF_C= ('RI', 0.,1.,),) ,),) The concept produced mat_rs is of type matr_asse_ _C (complex): mat_rs = mat_1 + i mat_2 4.2 Copy of a concept of type matr_asse_ _R mat_sauv = COMB_MATR_ASSE( COMB_R = _F ( MATR_ASSE = mat_1, COEF_R = 1.)) 4.3 Difference between COMB_C and COMB_R : mat_R = COMB_MATR_ASSE( COMB_R = _F ( MATR_ASSE = mat_1, COEF_R = 1.)) # mat_R est à coefficients réels mat_R = mat_1 mat_C = COMB_MATR_ASSE( COMB_C = _F ( MATR_ASSE = mat_1, COEF_R = 1.)) # mat_C est à coefficients complexes, mais la partie imaginaire est nulle mat_C = mat_1 + i. [:ref: 0 ]. 4.4 Extraction of the real part of a matrix of type matr_asse_ _C mat_R = COMB_MATR_ASSE ( COMB_R = _F( PARTIE = 'REEL', MATR_ASSE = mat_C, COEF_R = 1. , ), )

u4.72.04 Operator CREA_CHAMP u4.72.04 Operator CREA_CHAMP 1 Purpose Create a field of type cham_no, carte or cham_elem. One can create a field: - by assigning values on nodes or mesh cells, - by assembling (and/or combining) pieces of existing fields, - by evaluating the functions of a field of functions in order to make a field of reals, - by modifying the geometric representation of a field (passage from nodes \iff Gauss points, for example), - by extracting a field from a data structure of type SD_RESULTAT (evol_ther, evol_noli, mode_meca, ...). - from the values contained in a data structure of type TABLE, - ... One can also use this command to combine several fields linearly, but one can make more “complicated” combinations: multiplication of fields ... to the result field This keyword (mandatory) serves first to type the result field of the command. It is formed of 2 “words” linked by an underscore (_): TYPE_CHAM= 'XXXX_GD' where: XXXX= / 'NOEU' Champ aux nœuds (cham_no) / 'CART' Champ constant par maille (carte) / 'ELNO' Champ par éléments aux nœuds (cham_elem) / 'ELGA' Champ par éléments aux points de Gauss (cham_elem) / 'ELEM' Champ constant par élément (cham_elem) GD= / 'DEPL_R' déplacement / 'SIEF_R' contrainte / 'TEMP_R' température / 'FLUX_R' flux / ... The type of the result field is deduced from this information given by the user. For example: TYPE_CHAM= 'NOEU_DEPL_R' -> cham_no (DEPL_R) TYPE_CHAM= 'CART_SIEF_R' -> carte (SIEF_R) TYPE_CHAM= 'ELNO_EPSI_R' -> cham_elem (EPSI_R) TYPE_CHAM= 'ELGA_VARI_R' -> cham_elem (VARI_R) This keyword also serves to specify (for the command) what the nature of the field wanted as a result must be. It is indispensable for the operations 'AFFE', 'ASSE' and 'DISC'. Examples: OPERATION= 'AFFE' + TYPE_CHAM= 'CART_DEPL_R' => une carte de DEPL_R. OPERATION= 'ASSE' + TYPE_CHAM= 'NOEU_EPSI_R' => un cham_no de EPSI_R. OPERATION= 'DISC' + TYPE_CHAM= 'NOEU_SIEF_R' => un cham_no de SIEF_R. There are only two operations for which this keyword is a useless (but mandatory!) constraint for the user (OPERATION='EVAL' and OPERATION='EXTR') because, for these two operations, the nature of the result field is imposed by the choice of the operation. Supplying the keyword TYPE_CHAM is (unfortunately) tedious for OPERATION='EXTR'. It is deduced from the keyword NOM_CHAM. The correspondence is given in [ 3.9.1 ]. Important note The possibility of creating cham_elem of any quantity is conditioned by the state of (software) development of the finite-element types of the model. Not everything is yet possible; for example, to create a cham_elem of FLUX_R on a model containing the elements DKT, this finite element must have provided for doing so (which is not the case today). One cannot give here the precise list of the quantities allowed for each finite-element type. One will content oneself with saying approximately: - for the isoparametric elements of mechanics, the quantities allowed are: GEOM_R, INST_R, NEUT_R, NEUT_F, EPSI_R, SIEF_R, VARI_R, DOMMAG and HYDR_R, - for the isoparametric elements of thermal analysis, the quantities allowed are: GEOM_R, INST_R, NEUT_R and NEUT_F. 3.1.2 Operand CHAM_GD With the operations ASSE and COMB, one can reuse an existing field. In this case, one must indicate here which field is reused. 3.1.3 Operand MAILLAGE = mailla When one creates a CHAM_NO or a CARTE, one must in general specify on which mesh this field will be supported. For that, one uses the keyword MAILLAGE. 3.1.4 Operand PROL_ZERO When one creates a CHAM_ELEM, the values existing in the field are determined by the finite elements of the model. For example, a field SIGM_ELGA on a 2D model must contain the 4 components SIXX, SIYY, SIZZ and SIXY. If the construction of the field does not make it possible to compute all the expected values, one is faced with a problem. If the keyword PROL_ZERO is 'OUI', the missing values will be set to zero. If the keyword PROL_ZERO is 'NON', the code will stop in error. This problem also concerns (but more rarely) the CHAM_NO when one wants to impose the numbering of their components (see the keywords NUME_DDL and CHAM_NO). 3.1.5 Operands MODELE, OPTION When one creates a CHAM_ELEM, one must specify on which finite elements the field will be defined. For that, one uses the keyword MODELE. To describe the structure of a CHAM_ELEM, it is not enough to give (via the MODELE) an element type for each mesh cell, because an element type may know several “forms” for a given quantity. To create the desired field, the user may use the keyword OPTION. If, for example, he or she writes: X= CREA_CHAMP(... MODELE=mo, OPTION='SIEF_ELGA', ...) , the field created by CREA_CHAMP will have the same form as if it had been computed by CALC_CHAMP / CONTRAINTE='SIEF_ELGA'. If the user does not use the keyword OPTION, CREA_CHAMP will choose (if it can) a default form. Note: for the operation 'ASSE', when one assembles cham_elem, it is in general better not to supply the keyword OPTION. The option that will be chosen will be that of the field supplied in the 1st occurrence of the factor keyword ASSE if the quantity associated with this field is the same as that of the result field. 3.1.6 Keywords AFFE_SP / CARA_ELEM The (non-repeatable) factor keyword AFFE_SP makes it possible to request the creation of a cham_elem with “sub-points” (for the structural elements: multilayer shells, multi-fibre beams, …). In the cham_elem produced, each point (node or Gauss point) will be represented by n sub-points (n being determined by the user's choices in the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM). The n sub-points of a point will carry the same components (with the same values). The keyword CARA_ELEM is mandatory: it is the name of the data structure of type cara_elem which makes it possible to determine the number of sub-points. 3.1.7 Keywords NUME_DDL and CHAM_NO These two keywords make it possible to impose a numbering for the result field (if the latter is a CHAM_NO). One gives via these keywords a numbering “model” for the result field. If one gives NUME_DDL= nu, one will take as numbering that of nu. This possibility is valid only for displacement fields (phenomenon 'MECANIQUE') or for temperature fields (phenomenon 'THERMIQUE') or acoustic pressure fields (phenomenon 'ACOUSTIQUE'). If one gives CHAM_NO= chno, one will take the numbering of chno. In this last case, the numbering supplied (object of type PROF_CHNO) is duplicated so that the field created is self-supporting. If Lagrange multipliers coming from dualised boundary conditions are present, a check is made by the operator. Indeed, if the fields considered do not satisfy the same boundary conditions, they are not compatible. An alarm is then issued: the Lagrange multipliers will be set to zero in the resulting field. 3.1.8 Operand TITRE = titr Title that one wishes to give to the result field U4.03.01. 3.1.9 Operand INFO = /1 /2 INFO = 1 No printout. INFO = 2 Printout on the 'MESSAGE' file of the result field. 3.2 Operand OPERATION = /'AFFE' / 'ASSE' / 'EVAL' / 'DISC' / 'EXTR' / 'R2C' / 'C2R' / 'COMB' This operand serves to choose the “mode” of manufacture of the result field. One can create a field: - by assigning values on nodes or mesh cells (OPERATION='AFFE'), - by assembling pieces of fields defined on pieces of meshes (OPERATION='ASSE'), - by modifying the geometric representation (discretisation) of a field (passage from nodes Gauss points, for example) (OPERATION='DISC'), - by extracting a field from an SD of type SD_RESULTAT (evol_ther, evol_noli, mode_meca, ...) (OPERATION='EXTR'). - by extracting numerical values from a table whose columns have predefined names: ‘MAILLE’, ‘NOEUD’… - by combining fields linearly (OPERATION='ASSE'), - by “combining” (multiplication, exponential, ...) fields (OPERATION='EVAL'), - by evaluating the functions of a field of functions in order to make a field of reals (OPERATION='EVAL'), - by transforming a real field at the nodes into a complex field (or conversely) (OPERATION='R2C'/'C2R'), - by making a linear combination of several cham_no having the same numbering (OPERATION='COMB'). Unlike the operation 'ASSE', the result field will keep the Lagrange degrees of freedom associated with the dualisation of the boundary conditions. 3.3 Operands for OPERATION = 'AFFE' This operation makes it possible to assign values (real, integer, complex or function) on geometric entities (nodes or mesh cells) of a mesh. The quantity associated with the field is implicitly given by the keyword TYPE_CHAM (above). 3.3.1 Factor keyword AFFE The operands are grouped under the factor keyword AFFE. This keyword is repeatable. The overloading principle is applied between the different occurrences of the keyword AFFE: if a geometric entity is assigned several times, the last assignment wins. 3.3.2 Operands TOUT='OUI', GROUP_MA and GROUP_NO The geometric entities that one wants to assign are given by the operands TOUT='OUI', GROUP_MA and GROUP_NO. If TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_xxx', one assigns nodes; the use of the operand GROUP_MA is possible and means that one assigns all the nodes of the specified mesh cells. If TYPE_CHAM:'EL.._xxx' (or 'CART_xxx'), one assigns mesh cells; the use of the operand GROUP_NO is then forbidden. Note: For the factor keyword AFFE, the keyword TOUT='OUI' means: - “all the nodes of the mesh” for the cham_no, - “all the mesh cells of the mesh” for the cartes, - “all the elements of the model” for the cham_elem, 3.3.3 Operand NOM_CMP The names of the components that one wants to assign are given by the operand NOM_CMP. If the quantity is 'VARI_R', the components must be named 'V1', 'v2', 'V3', … If the quantity is 'VARI_R', and if one chooses PROL_ZERO='OUI', the components whose number is lower than the highest number assigned are set to zero. For more details see the document U2.01.09. 3.3.4 Operands VALE, VALE_I, VALE_C or VALE_F The values to be assigned are given by the operands VALE, VALE_I, VALE_C or VALE_F according to the nature (real, integer, complex, function (or formula)) of the components of the quantity (DEPL_R: real, DEPL_C: complex, TEMP_F: function / formula, ....). 3.3.5 Note The persistence rule (see U1.03.00) applies to the different components that one may assign. 3.3.6 Examples Creation of a field at the nodes of displacement. One wants to impose the numbering of the field (that of cnomod): DEPL1 = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION= 'AFFE', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R' , MAILLAGE = MA , CHAM_NO= CNOMOD, AFFE= ( _F (TOUT='OUI', NOM_CMP=('DX','DY','DZ'), VALE=(0.,0.,0.),), _F (GROUP_MA=('GM1',’GM2’) , NOM_CMP= 'DX' , VALE= 3.5e-2), _F (GROUP_NO=('GN5',’GN7’,’GN9’) , NOM_CMP= 'DY' , VALE= 1.6e-2), ) ) Creation of a temperature map (functions): TEMPF = CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION= 'AFFE', TYPE_CHAM='CART_TEMP_F' , MAILLAGE = MA, AFFE=( _F( TOUT='OUI', NOM_CMP=('TEMP'),VALE_F= F1), _F( GROUP_MA=(‘GM1’,’GM2’),NOM_CMP=('TEMP' ),VALE_F= F2),) ) 3.4 Operands for OPERATION = 'ASSE' 3.4.1 General points This operator “assembles” “pieces of fields” in order to manufacture a new one. Each occurrence of the keyword ASSE defines a piece of field. One calls a piece of field the restriction of an existing field (carte, cham_no or cham_elem) to a set of geometric entities (mesh cells or nodes) and to a set of components. There is an overloading principle for the occurrences of the keyword ASSE if the pieces overlap one another. Currently, one can manufacture: - a cham_no by assembling pieces of cham_no. - a cham_elem by assembling pieces of cham_elem and/or of cartes. - a carte by assembling pieces of cartes and/or of cham_elem/ELEM. The operation 'ASSE' also makes it possible to change the quantity associated with a field; for example to transform a strain field (EPSI_R) into a stress field (SIEF_R). For that one must use the keywords NOM_CMP and NOM_CMP_RESU. The assembly of the pieces of fields can be done by accumulating the pieces (keywords CUMUL and COEF_R ). This makes it possible to use this command to make linear combinations of CHAM_NO or of CHAM_ELEM. 3.4.2 Operands MAILLAGE, MODELE Same use as for OPERATION= 'AFFE' [§3.3.1] and [§3.3.2]. 3.4.3 Operands for the factor keyword ASSE Each occurrence of the factor keyword ASSE makes it possible to define a piece of field which one assembles into the result field. 3.4.3.1 Operand CHAM_GD = ch1 ch1 is the (existing) field with which one wants to manufacture a piece of field. 3.4.3.2 Operands TOUT ='OUI', GROUP_MA and GROUP_NO These operands serve to define the geometric restriction of the field ch1. If ch1 is a CHAM_NO , one can use all these operands. If ch1 is a CHAM_ELEM (or a CARTE ), one cannot use the operand GROUP_NO . The keyword TOUT='OUI' means here: “all the nodes, mesh cells or elements which carry components (of the list NOM_CMP ) in the field ch1”. 3.4.3.3 Operands NOM_CMP and NOM_CMP_RESU The operand NOM_CMP serves to define the components on which one wants to restrict the field ch1. If NOM_CMP is absent, one takes all the components of ch1 . The operand NOM_CMP_RESU serves to rename (if one wishes) the components of ch1 . If NOM_CMP_RESU is supplied, NOM_CMP must be supplied as well and the two lists in correspondence must be of the same length. Example 1: transform a field of EPSI_R into a field of VARI_R CHVARI=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE',TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R', MODELE=MO, ASSE=_F( CHAM_GD=CHEPSI ,TOUT='OUI', NOM_CMP =('EPXX','EPYY'), NOM_CMP_RESU=('V3','V1'), ), ) Example 2: permute the cmps SIXX and SIYY of a field of SIEF_R CHS2=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE='NOEU_SIEF_R', MAILLAGE= MA , ASSE=_F( CHAM_GD=CHS1, TOUT='OUI', NOM_CMP =('SIXX','SIYY'), NOM_CMP_RESU=('SIYY','SIXX',) , ) ) 3.4.3.4 Operands CUMUL , COEF_R and COEF_C The operand CUMUL='OUI' means that the values of the occurrence concerned will be added to any values already existing. If CUMUL='NON' , the assigned value replaces the value possibly already present ( CUMUL='OUI' is invalid for “text” fields ( k8/k16 , ...) of course). The operand COEF_R = coefr makes it possible to multiply the piece of field by the real coefficient coefr before assembling it into the result field. Example: Manufacture the cham_elem: ch3 = 2. ch1 + 3. ch2 CH3= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION= 'ASSE', MODELE = MO, TYPE_CHAM ='ELGA_EPSI_R', ASSE = (_F( CHAM_GD = CH1 , TOUT ='OUI', CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R = 2.), _F( CHAM_GD = CH2 , TOUT ='OUI', CUMUL='OUI', COEF_R = 3.), ) ) Note concerning complex fields The keyword COEF_C is accepted only in the case where the result field ( CH3 ) and the argument fields ( CH1 and CH2 ) are all complex. To make a linear combination with complex coefficients of real fields, one must beforehand transform the real fields into complex fields. See OPERATION = 'R2C' . 3.4.4 Examples Example 1 Manufacture a cham_no of temperature by extracting an already computed field (from an evol_ther ) and by redefining it (at 25. degrees) on the mesh-cell group soudur1. CH1= CREA_CHAMP (OPERATION= 'EXTR' , TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_TEMP_R', RESULTAT= EVOTH , NOM_CHAM= 'TEMP', INST = 12. ) CH2= CREA_CHAMP (OPERATION = 'AFFE', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_TEMP_R', MAILLAGE =MA, AFFE=_F(TOUT =’OUI’ ,NOM_CMP =’TEMP’,VALE = 25.) ) CH3= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION = 'ASSE', MAILLAGE = MA, TYPE_CHAM ='NOEU_TEMP_R', ASSE = (_F(CHAM_GD = CH1 , TOUT ='OUI',), _F( CHAM_GD = CH2 ,GROUP_MA = SOUDUR1 ),) ) Example 2: Manufacture a cham_elem of VARI_R (in order to use it as an initial state for stat_non_line) by recovering the internal variables (6 and 8) of a constitutive law in order to make them the variables 1 and 2 of the (new) constitutive law which will be used in the forthcoming STAT_NON_LINE . CH1= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION= 'EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_VARI_R', RESULTAT= STNL, NOM_CHAM= 'VARI_ELGA', INST = 4. ) CH2= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION= 'ASSE', MODELE = MO, TYPE_CHAM ='ELGA_VARI_R', ASSE = _F(CHAM_GD = CH1 , TOUT ='OUI', NOM_CMP = ('V6', 'V8'), NOM_CMP_RESU =( 'V1', 'V2'), ) ) 3.5 Operands for the factor keyword COMB This keyword makes it possible to compute the linear combination of several cham_no having the same numbering. Unlike the operation 'ASSE', the result field will also contain the Lagrange coefficients corresponding to the dualisation of the boundary conditions. Each occurrence of the factor keyword COMB makes it possible to define one element of the linear combination. 3.5.1 Operand CHAM_GD = ch1 ch1 is the (existing) cham_no that one wants to combine linearly. 3.5.2 Operand COEF_R = coefr coefr is the real coefficient applied to ch1 for the combination. 3.5.3 Example To compute C = 1. A - 2. B, one writes: > TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', COMB=( _F(CHAM_GD=A, COEF_R= 1.), _F(CHAM_GD=B, COEF_R=-2.), ) C= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='COMB', ) 3.6 Operands for OPERATION = 'EVAL' This operation serves to transform a field of functions into fields of reals by evaluating the functions of the field of functions. The field of functions is necessarily a field of the quantity 'NEUT_F' and the result field will always be a field of 'NEUT_R' . This field may be transformed into a field of any other quantity by calling the command CREA_CHAMP / OPERATION='ASSE' a second time. An example of the use of the operation EVAL is given in the document U2.01.09 “Analytical definition of a stress field ...” 3.6.1 Operand CHAM_F= chf chf is the name of the field of functions to be evaluated ( CHAM_NO , CARTE or CHAM_ELEM ). 3.6.2 Operand CHAM_PARA= l_chpara l_chpara is the list of the “parameter” fields for the evaluation of the functions. All the fields of l_chpara must be discretised in the same way as chf . For example, if chf is a CHAM_ELEM/ELGA , all the fields of l_chpara must also be CHAM_ELEM/ELGA . The list of parameter fields must be sufficient to allow the evaluation of all the functions referenced in chf , and no component of a parameter field must be present in another parameter field of the list either. Note: Thus, for element fields, it is for example not possible to supply two fields of quantity NEUT even if it is not the same components that must be taken into account on the two fields, because each field has the components X1 to X30. 3.6.3 Examples 3.6.3.1 Example 1 One wants to create a cham_elem ( SIEF_R ) at the Gauss points whose components are analytical functions of the geometry and of time. For this example, one assumes that one has already manufactured two fields at the Gauss points, CHGEOMG : geometry field and CHINSTG : field of time instants. RHO=1000. G=10. KP=3. SIZZ = FORMULE (NOM_PARA = 'Z', VALE = 'RHO G Z') SIXX = FORMULE (NOM_PARA = ('Z','INST'), VALE = 'KP SIZZ(Z)+3. INST') # Affectation des fonctions : # ----------------------------------------------- SIG1=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_NEUT_F', MODELE=MO , PROL_ZERO='OUI', AFFE=_F(TOUT='OUI', NOM_CMP=('X1','X2'), VALE_F=('SIXX','SIZZ'), ) ) # Evaluation des fonctions : # ----------------------------------------------- SIG2= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EVAL' ,TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_NEUT_R', MODELE=MO ,CHAM_F=SIG1 , CHAM_PARA=( CHGEOMG,CHINSTG), ) # transformation du champ de NEUT_R en SIEF_R : # ----------------------------------------------- SIG3=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', MODELE=MO , PROL_ZERO='OUI', ASSE=_F(TOUT='OUI', CHAM_GD=SIG2, NOM_CMP= ('X1' ,'X2' ), NOM_CMP_RESU=('SIXX','SIZZ'), ) ) 3.6.3.2 Example 2 One wants to compute a temperature field at the nodes ( \mathrm{CH3} ) containing the product of 2 other temperature fields at the nodes ( \mathrm{CH1} and \mathrm{CH2} ) # 1) transformation des cham_no/TEMP_R (CH1 et CH2) en un cham_no/NEUT_R: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- CHN=CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_NEUT_R', MAILLAGE=MA, ASSE=(_F( TOUT = 'OUI', CHAM_GD = CH1, NOM_CMP = ('TEMP',), NOM_CMP_RESU = ('X1',), ), _F( TOUT = 'OUI', CHAM_GD = CH2, NOM_CMP = ('TEMP',), NOM_CMP_RESU = ('X2',)), ) ) # 2) multiplication CH3N = CHN/X1 CHN/X2 : # ------------------------------------------ FMULT = FORMULE(NOM_PARA = ('X1', 'X2'), VALE = 'X1 X2') CHFMU=CREA_CHAMP( OPERATION='AFFE', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_NEUT_F', MAILLAGE=MA, AFFE=_F( TOUT = 'OUI', NOM_CMP = 'X3', VALE_F = FMULT) ) # On a choisi ici la composante X3, mais on pourrait choisir n’importe quelle composante de X1 à X30. CH3N=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EVAL', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_NEUT_R', CHAM_F=CHFMU, CHAM_PARA=(CHN) ) # 3) transformation du cham_no/NEUT_R (CH3N) en cham_no/TEMP_R: # -------------------------------------------------------------------- CH3=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='ASSE', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_TEMP_R', MAILLAGE=MA, ASSE=_F( TOUT = 'OUI', CHAM_GD = CH3N, NOM_CMP = ('X3',), NOM_CMP_RESU = ('TEMP',) ), ) 3.7 Operands for OPERATION = 'DISC' This operation serves to modify the “discretisation” of an existing field. For example, to transform a field at the nodes into fields at the Gauss points. The two fields (input and result) are associated with the same quantity. There is one exception: the case of the operation DISC which makes it possible to transform a cham_no_VAR2_R (or a carte_VAR2_R ) into a cham_elem_VARI_R (see for example the test hplp100b). The discretisation wanted by the user for his or her result field is indicated by the keyword TYPE_CHAM . Only the following cases are currently processed by the command: | CARTE | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELNO | | --- | --- | | CARTE | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELGA | | CARTE | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELEM | | CARTE | -> CHAM_NO | | CHAM_NO | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELNO | | CHAM_NO | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELGA | | CHAM_NO | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELEM | | CHAM_ELEM / ELNO | -> CHAM_NO | | CHAM_ELEM / ELGA | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELNO | | CHAM_ELEM / ELGA | -> CHAM_NO | | CHAM_ELEM / ELEM | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELGA | | CHAM_ELEM / ELEM | -> CHAM_ELEM / ELNO | The ingredients of the processings are: CARTE / ELEM -> ELxx : - The (unique) value carried by a mesh cell is copied onto all the points of the mesh cell. NOEU -> ELxx : - the passage from the values at the nodes to the internal points of the mesh cell is done by using the shape functions of the finite elements of the model. ELGA -> ELNO : - the passage from the values at the internal points to the nodes of the mesh cell is done by using the Gauss->nodes extrapolation matrix. ELNO -> NOEU : - the passage to the values at the nodes of the mesh is done by arithmetic mean of the values carried by the nodes of the elements meeting there. 3.7.1 Operand CHAM_GD= ch1 ch1 is the field whose “discretisation” one wants to modify. 3.7.2 Keyword MODELE Same use as for OPERATION = 'AFFE' [3.3.2] 3.7.3 Example # CHXG = CHAMP DE GEOMETRIE AUX POINTS DE GAUSS : # --------------------------------------------------------- CHXN =CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_GEOM_R', NOM_CHAM='GEOMETRIE', MAILLAGE=MA ) CHXG= CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='DISC', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_GEOM_R', MODELE=MO , CHAM_GD= CHXN ) 3.8 Operands for OPERATION = 'NORMALE' This operation serves to compute the “normal” vectors to the facets of a model. The user must indicate, with the keywords MODELE and GROUP_MA , the name of the model concerned as well as the “facets” whose normals he or she wishes to compute. The “facets” may be “skin” elements of a 3D mesh or plate / shell elements. For 2D meshes, the “facets” are line elements. The field produced is a cham_no (quantity GEOM_R) whose components are named X, Y, Z. The normal carried by a node is obtained by averaging the normals of the facets meeting at that node. The “normal” vector has length 1. 3.9 Operands for OPERATION = 'EXTR' This operation generally serves to extract a field from an SD of type resultat_sdaster. There are 5 additional possibilities: - one can extract the geometry field of the nodes of a mesh. One must then use the keywords: MAILLAGE = ma, NOM_CHAM = 'GEOMETRIE' and TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_GEOM_R' . - one can extract the curvilinear-abscissa field of a mesh. One must then use the keywords: MAILLAGE = ma, NOM_CHAM = 'ABSC_CURV' and TYPE_CHAM = 'CART_ABSC_R' . - one can create a field by extracting from a table the values corresponding to parameters with pre-established names: MAILLE, NOEUD, POINT, SOUS_POINT , names of the components. - one can extract the “level sets” associated with an XFEM crack. One must then use the keywords: FISSURE = fiss_xfem, NOM_CHAM = / 'LTNO' / 'LNNO' / 'GRLTNO' / 'GRLNNO' / 'STNO' / 'STNOR' / 'BASLOC' and TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_NEUT_R' except for ‘ STNO ’, for which it will be ' NOEU_NEUT_I ' 'LTNO' level set tangente 'LNNO' level set normale 'GRLTNO' gradient de la level set tangente 'GRLNNO' gradient de la level set normale 'STNO' statut des nœuds, 1 valeur entière 'STNOR' statut des nœuds, 1 valeur réelle 'BASLOC' base locale en fond de fissure, avec 6/9 valeurs réelles, 2/3 coordonnées pour le point et 2/3 coordonnées pour chacun des vecteurs de la base locale en 2D/3D - one can extract the different fields contained in the data structures cara_elem and char_meca . This functionality is rather reserved for developers.
