The names of the parameters of the table must comply with certain rules. The names of the mesh cells and of the nodes must be coded on 8 characters; the tables printed in 'TABLEAU' format print the strings on 24 characters by default, so it is preferable to use the 'ASTER' format when re-reading the tables in order to specify the format of the character strings and to indicate K8 for the parameters NOEUD and MAILLE. The columns containing the values of the field (reals) must be identified by their component name in the quantity. For example: DX, DY, DZ for the displacement (DEPL_R). The other columns to be supplied depend on the type of field to be created: | Type of the field | Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | NOEUD_XXXX | NOEUD | | | | ELEM_XXXX | MAILLE | [SOUS-POINT] | | | ELNO_XXXX | MAILLE | NOEUD | [SOUS-POINT] | | ELGA_XXXX | MAILLE | POINT | [SOUS-POINT] | The parameter NOEUD contains the name of the node. The parameter MAILLE contains the name of the mesh cell. The parameter POINT contains the number of the Gauss point in the mesh cell. The parameter SOUS_POINT (necessary only for fields with “sub-points”) contains the number of the sub-point in the Gauss point (or the node). Warning: the table must not contain any column other than the expected columns (for example: NUME_ORDRE , INST , …). If the table contains useless columns, one must delete them by means of the command CALC_TABLE + OPERATION='EXTR' . 3.9.3 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = resu Name of the result concept in which one wants to recover a field. 3.9.4 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM This keyword specifies the symbolic name of the field to be extracted U4.71.00. 3.9.5 Operands NUME_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / NOM_MODE / ... / INTERPOL These keywords serve to specify the order number of the SD_RESULTAT that one wants to extract. The choice of the keywords to be used depends on the type of SD_RESULTAT U4.71.00. Notes When one uses INTERPOL = 'LIN', the extracted field will be an interpolation between two fields of the SD_RESULTAT. This interpolation does not always have a “physical” meaning; for example on eigenmodes. This keyword should be used only for SD_RESULTAT of type “evol_xxxx” When one uses an access of “real” type (INST or FREQ), one looks for a field in a given interval. If one finds several fields in the interval, the program stops in fatal error. 3.9.6 Computation of a field containing the “extrema” of an SD_RESULTAT The idea is to create a field containing, at each point of space, the extreme value encountered during a transient (or the time instant at which this value was encountered). Today this paragraph concerns only the results of type evol_ther , evol_elas , evol_noli and dyna_trans . The fields are always of “real” type. One must specify: - the order numbers defining the transient: TOUT_ORDRE , LIST_INST , - the type of extremum chosen: TYPE_MAXI = 'MAXI', ...,'MINI_ABS', 'NORM_TRAN' , - what one wants: the extreme value, the time instant or the order number at which this value is reached ( TYPE_RESU ). 3.9.6.1 Operand TYPE_MAXI | / 'MAXI' | one considers the maximum reached by the components during the transient, | | --- | --- | | / 'MAXI_ABS' | one considers the maximum reached by the absolute value of the components during the transient, | | / 'MINI' / 'MINI_ABS' | likewise for the minima, | | / 'NORM_TRAN' | one considers the maximum reached by the quantity: DX 2 + DY 2 + DZ 2. | - for the 4 values: 'MAXI' , ...,' MINI_ABS' , the components of the field are processed independently of one another: the extreme values may not be reached at the same time instant, - the fifth possible value: 'NORM_TRAN' is possible only for the fields of depl_R . At a given point, one looks for the time instant at which the norm of the translation vector is maximum and one copies into the result field all the components of the field at the time instant found. 3.9.6.2 Operand TYPE_RESU | / 'VALE' , | the result field contains the extreme values encountered during the transient, | | --- | --- | Note: Even if the extremum was obtained with an absolute value ('MAXI_ABS' or 'MINI_ABS'), the stored value is algebraic. One must use VALE_ABS in order to have the absolute value. | / 'INST' , | the result field contains the values of the time instants at which the extreme values were encountered. | | --- | --- | | / 'NUME_ORDRE' , | the result field contains the values of the order numbers at which the extreme values were encountered. | | --- | --- | Note: If, for example: - NOM_CHAM = 'FLUX_ELNO', - TYPE_RESU = 'INST', The result field is a field of type FLUX_R which contains values of time instants! | / 'VALE_ABS' , | available only with an absolute TYPE_MAXI ('MAXI_ABS' or 'MINI_ABS'), the result field then contains the extreme absolute values encountered during the transient. | | --- | --- | 3.9.6.3 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / LIST_INST / LIST_FREQ / PRECISION / CRITERE These keywords make it possible to specify the extent of the transient to be examined. If TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' one goes through all the order numbers. If LIST_INST = linst one considers only the time instants specified. 3.9.7 Examples 3.9.7.1 Extraction of a temperature field from a result concept of type evol_ther temp10 = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', NOM_CHAM = 'TEMP', TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_TEMP_R', RESULTAT = evoth, INST = 10. ) temp10 is the temperature field extracted from the result evoth (of type evol_ther) at time instant 10. 3.9.7.2 Extraction of a displacement field from a result concept of type mode_meca mode4 = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR' , NOM_CHAM = 'DEPL' , TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_DEPL_R', RESULTAT = modes, NUME_MODE = 4 ) mode4 is the 4th eigenmode of the result modes (of type mode_meca). 3.9.7.3 Extraction of the “temperature” field containing the time instants at which the maximum temperature was reached during a transient instmax = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', NOM_CHAM = 'TEMP', TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_TEMP_R', RESULTAT = evoth, TYPE_MAXI = 'MAXI', TYPE_RESU = 'INST' ) 3.9.7.4 Extraction of a stress field from a table Consider the file (fort.81) containing the image of the following table: #DEBUT_TABLE #TITRE CONTRAINTE ELNO' MAILLE POINT SIXX SIYY SIZZ K8 I R R R M1 1 -1.632E+03 -2.553E+02 6.788E-01 M1 2 -5.302E+03 -9.663E+01 6.018E+01 M1 3 -3.638E+03 -1.058E+02 5.669E+01 M2 1 5.632E+01 1.553E+02 3.788E-01 #FIN_TABLE One can extract a field of “stresses” at the nodes from this table by doing: # lecture de la table : TA=LIRE_TABLE(UNITE=81, TYPE_TABLE='TABLE', SEPARATEUR=' ') # extraction du champ dans la table : CH=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='ELNO_SIEF_R', TABLE='TA', MODELE=MO, PROL_ZERO='OUI', OPTION='SIEF_ELNO_DEPL') 3.9.7.5 Computation of the field of “normals” on a group of boundary mesh cells nor_DNOR = CREA_CHAMP(TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU_GEOM_R', OPERATION= 'NORMALE', MODELE= MO, GROUP_MA= 'FE' );

u4.72.05 Operator PROJ_CHAMP u4.72.05 Operator PROJ_CHAMP The purpose of the operator is to project the fields of a result data structure onto another mesh. This command can be used, for example, to transfer onto a “mechanical” mesh the result of a thermal analysis carried out on a different “thermal” mesh. One can also “continue” a thermal (or mechanical) analysis on another mesh (more or less refined). The command also makes it possible to define geometric “zones” which are projected onto one another, which makes it possible to solve the problem of a desired discontinuity of the projected field (for example along the faces of a crack). For reasons of CPU performance, one can first compute the geometric pairing of the two meshes and store the data structure produced in a concept which one will be able to reuse later in order to carry out the projections of the fields. It is possible to project an “isolated” field or a set of fields coming from an SD_RESULTAT. Produces a data structure SD_RESULTAT or an “isolated” field or a data structure CORRESP_2_MAILLA. 1 Contents

u4.72.06 Operator PROD_MATR_CHAM u4.72.06 Operator PROD_MATR_CHAM 1 Purpose Carry out the product of a matrix by a vector. The matrix is a data structure of type matr_asse: it has real or complex values, and is symmetric or non-symmetric. The vector is a data structure of type cham_no. It has real or complex values. One requires that the matrix and the vector both have real values or both have complex values (otherwise use beforehand the commands COMB_MATR_ASSE U4.72.01 or CREA_CHAMP U4.72.04) and that they share the same numbering (see the command NUME_DDL U4.61.11). Produces a concept of type cham_no. 2 Syntax cham_no = PROD_MATR_CHAM( ◆ MATR_ASSE = matr_asse_depl_c / matr_asse_temp_r / matr_asse_depl_r / matr_asse_pres_c, ◆ CHAM_NO = cham_no, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword MATR_ASSE ♦ MATR_ASSE = m Name of the matrix (concept matr_asse_ ) to be multiplied. 3.2 Keyword CHAM_NO ♦ CHAM_NO = u Name of the vector (concept cham_no) to be multiplied. 3.3 Keyword TITRE ◊ TITRE = titr Title that one wishes to give to the result. 4 Checks - Check that the matrix and the vector to be multiplied both have real values or both have complex values. - Consistency check: the operands of type matr_asse_ and of type cham_no must share the same numbering. 5 Example of use Matrix–vector product: u_mv_1 = PROD_MATR_CHAM ( MATR_ASSE = mat_1, CHAM_NO = u_1, ) For example, one can use this command to create a right-hand-side vector coming from the product of the mass matrix and an acceleration vector obtained by the command DYNA_VIBRA. This right-hand-side vector can be used as a loading for a static analysis.

u4.73.01 Operator PROJ_MESU_MODAL u4.73.01 Operator PROJ_MESU_MODAL 1 Purpose Extrapolate experimental measurements onto a numerical model in dynamics. The experimental data may be displacements, velocities, accelerations, strains or stresses. They are defined as a function of time or of frequency, or in the form of a list. The aim is to compute the generalised coordinates of the measurement relative to an expansion basis defined on the numerical model. This expansion basis (shapes, stresses or strains) is computed beforehand as a concept of type mode_meca. The basis vectors are then restricted to the measured degrees of freedom. The spatial association between the measurement points and the nodes of the numerical mesh can be carried out manually and/or automatically. The computation of the generalised coordinates is carried out by solving a least-squares minimisation problem, possibly regularised by the Tikhonov method. Applicable to any type of model (1D, 2D and 3D). Produces a data structure of type tran_gene, harm_gene or mode_gene. 2 Syntax / mode_gene / tran_gene / harm_gene = PROJ_MESU_MODAL( ◆ MODELE_CALCUL = _F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ BASE = mode_meca, ), ◆ MODELE_MESURE = _F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ MESURE = mode_meca_c / dyna_trans / dyna_harmo / mode_meca, ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "ACCE", / "SIEF_NOEU", / "EPSI_NOEU", ), ◇ CORR_MANU = _F( ◇ & NOEU_CALCUL = no, & NOEU_MESURE = no, ), ◇ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ RESOLUTION = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "LU" (par défaut), / "SVD", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'SVD') ◇ EPS = float, ◇ REGUL = / "NON" (par défaut), / "NORM_MIN", / "TIK_RELA", # Si: not equal_to("REGUL", 'NON') ◇ / COEF_PONDER = float, / COEF_PONDER_F = formule / nappe / fonction, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Factor keyword MODELE_CALCUL This factor keyword groups the characteristics of the numerical model onto which one wants to extrapolate the measurement. It must appear only once. 3.1.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mocalc Name of the numerical model on which the expansion basis is built. 3.1.2 Operand BASE ♦ BASE = base Name of the expansion basis. This basis is of type mode_meca. This concept has possibly been enriched, via the command CALC_CHAMP, by the modal strain and/or stress fields computed at the nodes. 3.2 Factor keyword MODELE_MESURE This factor keyword groups the information on the measured (observed) field that one wishes to extrapolate onto the numerical model. It must appear only once. 3.2.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mostru Name of the model associated with the observation. 3.2.2 Operand MESURE ♦ MESURE = mesure Name of the measured field. This keyword determines the type of concept produced by the operator PROJ_MESU_MODAL. If mesure is of type dyna_trans, the concept produced is of type tran_gene. If mesure is of type dyna_harmo, the concept produced is of type harm_gene. If mesure is of type mode_meca, or mode_meca_c, the concept produced is of type mode_gene. 3.2.3 Operand NOM_CHAM ◊ NOM_CHAM = | 'DEPL' [DEFAUT] | 'VITE' | 'ACCE' | 'SIEF_NOEU' | 'EPSI_NOEU' This keyword makes it possible to choose the field or fields to be read and extrapolated. The components of the field considered are those which have been measured (observed) and read in mesure. For the moment, one does not assign a weighting coefficient to the different components of the field: each component has the same weight during the inversion. 3.3 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA= lpara List of the symbolic names of the parameters of the measured data that one wishes to transmit to the generalised model. 3.4 Factor keyword CORR_MANU This factor keyword allows the user to define (overload) manually the correspondence between the observation node and the analogous node of the numerical model. This factor keyword is optional, but it may appear as many times as necessary. On the other hand, the operands under this factor keyword go in pairs: a NOEU_MESURE must have its associated NOEU_CALCUL. If this factor keyword is absent, the spatial association between the measurement points and the nodes of the numerical mesh is carried out automatically by using the shape function of the element of the numerical model in order to determine the value of the field at the measurement point. 3.4.1 Operand NOEU_MESURE ♦ NOEU_MESURE = no1 This keyword gives the name of the observation node that one wishes to associate with the node of the numerical model no2. In certain cases, the mesh file associated with the measurement is in universal format (Ideas format); one therefore cannot know a priori the Aster name associated with the node. It is therefore necessary, in this case, to read the mesh coming from PRE_IDEAS, by LIRE_MAILLAGE, in order to be able to assign the name of the node. 3.4.2 Operand NOEU_CALCUL ♦ NOEU_CALCUL = no2 This keyword gives the name of the node of the numerical model that one wishes to associate with the observation node no1. 3.5 Factor keyword RESOLUTION One defines here the solution method to be used and the parameters associated with this method. 3.5.1 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE = / 'LU' / 'SVD' One proposes the LU method (LU decomposition, Lower-Upper) and the SVD method (singular-value decomposition) for the computation of the inverse matrix. For the SVD method, the number of singular values to be taken into account depends on the value of eps that the user supplies under the operand EPS. By default, one adopts the LU method. 3.5.2 Operand EPS > This keyword is used if one chooses the SVD method. ◊ EPS = / 0. / eps This keyword gives the value from which a singular value is considered to be zero. It thus determines the number of singular values to be used during the solution. An eps equal to zero means that all the singular values are to be taken into account. An eps equal to 1 means that one considers only the largest singular value. By default, one chooses EPS = 0. 3.5.3 Operand REGUL ◊ REGUL = / 'NON' / 'NORME_MIN' / 'TIK_RELA' REGUL makes it possible to specify the regularisation method that one wants to use. By default, one does not add any regularisation (no additional constraint on the solution: REGUL = 'NON'). Currently, two types of regularisation are available (minimum norm: REGUL = 'NORM_MIN' or Tikhonov of order 0, and “relative” Tikhonov: REGUL = 'TIK_RELA'). One seeks to minimise, for each order number of the measured field, the following functional with respect to \eta : {\mid {q}_{\exp}-{\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}\eta \mid }^{2}+{\alpha \mid \eta -{\eta}_{\mathrm{priori}}\mid }^{2} with: - \eta : generalised coordinates relative to the expansion basis {\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}} . - {q}_{\exp} : measured field along the observation degrees of freedom. - {\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}} : expansion basis restricted to the observation degrees of freedom. - \alpha : weighting coefficients making it possible to specify the weight assigned to the a priori information on the solution. Depending on the method used, the parameters of the previous functional are set out as follows: Without regularisation: \alpha =0 Minimum norm (NORM_MIN): {\eta}_{\mathrm{priori}}=0 “Relative” Tikhonov (TIK_RELA): {\eta}_{\mathrm{priori}} : solution found at the previous order number It is not recommended to use this keyword when the measured field (mesure) is of type mode_meca. 3.5.4 Operands COEF_PONDER and COEF_PONDER_F This keyword corresponds to the weight assigned to the a priori information, \alpha . It is used if one applies a regularisation to the solution \eta . ◊ / COEF_PONDER = coef List of the weighting coefficients on the a priori solution (Tikhonov regularisation method) [bib3]. / COEF_PONDER_F = coef_f List of the weighting functions on the a priori solution (Tikhonov regularisation method). The variables of these functions are the same as those of the measured field (mesure). If the number of weighting coefficients or functions given is smaller than the number of basis vectors used in the expansion basis, the weighting coefficients or functions of the additional vectors are taken equal to the last coefficient or to the last function of the list. 4 Verification and execution phase 4.1 Computation of the expansion basis restricted to the measured degrees of freedom First, the mesh of the measurement is projected onto the mesh of the numerical model. One then determines the participation of the nodes of the numerical model for each measurement node via the shape function of the element which contains the measurement node. The correspondence obtained between the nodes is supplied in the MESSAGE file of the Aster study. The second processing consists in computing the component of the field (expansion basis) at the measurement node along the measured degrees of freedom. 4.2 Computation of the generalised coordinates The solution of the minimisation equation is given by: \begin{array}{ccc}\eta (0)& =& {\left[{\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}^{T}{\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}\right]}^{-1}{\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}^{T}{q}_{\exp}(0)\\ \eta (i)& =& {\left[{\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}^{T}{\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}+\alpha (i)\right]}^{-1}({\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}}^{T}{q}_{\exp}(i)+\alpha (i){\eta}_{\mathrm{priori}})\end{array} With: - \eta (i) : generalised coordinates for the order number i (ti or fi), - {q}_{\exp}(i) : measurement at the order number i, - {\bar{\Phi}}_{\mathrm{num}} : expansion basis restricted to the measurement degrees of freedom, - \alpha (i) : coefficients making it possible to specify the weight assigned to the a priori information at the order number i. These variables or functions are defined by the user in the operands COEF_PONDER or COEF_PONDER_F of the factor keyword RESOLUTION. They are introduced in the form of a list of reals or of functions and correspond, term by term, to each vector of the expansion basis retained. Depending on the method used, the previous parameters are set out as follows: Without regularisation: \alpha =0 Minimum norm (NORM_MIN): {\eta}_{\mathrm{priori}}=0 “Relative” Tikhonov (TIK_RELA): {\eta}_{\mathrm{priori}}={\eta}_{i-1} Note 1: If a weighting coefficient is negative, the processing stops in fatal error. Note 2: If all the weighting coefficients are zero for a given order number and the number of measurements is strictly smaller than the number of basis vectors, an alarm message is issued in order to warn of the risk of a singular matrix (indeed, in this case, the solution is not unique). At the end of the analysis, the identified generalised coordinates are differentiated in order to compute the corresponding velocities and accelerations. The result of the inversion is a concept of type tran_gene, harm_gene or mode_gene. 5 Example of use of PROJ_MESU_MODAL For the examples of use, it is strongly recommended to refer to the test cases SDLD104 and SDLV122. One presents in this paragraph the different steps for the expansion of the measurement onto the numerical model. - Reading of the mesh made up of the measurement points: The objective of this operation is to read the position of the measurement points in a file of mesh type. The format of this file must be readable by Code_Aster (GIBI format, universal (I-deas) format, or shortly MED). Mesh cells linking the measurement nodes may have been defined. They obviously have no physical meaning but will possibly make it possible to visualise the results during the post-processing phase. In the majority of cases, the mesh comes from an experimental measurement code which supplies a file in universal format (I-deas format). To transform it into Aster format, one uses the operator PRE_IDEAS. PRE_IDEAS(UNITE_IDEAS = 19, UNITE_MAILLAGE = 21,) mailmesu = LIRE_MAILLAGE ( UNITE = 21,) - Assignment of a mechanical model to the mesh: The objective of this operation is to define the model of the support of the nodes of the mesh made up of the measurement points. Two cases may be envisaged: assignment of a modelling DIS_T (discrete in translation => 3 degrees of freedom per node: DX, DY and DZ) or assignment of a modelling DIS_TR (discrete in translation–rotation => 6 degrees of freedom per node: DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY and DRZ) in the case where rotation measurements are carried out. modlmesu = AFFE_MODELE ( MAILLAGE = mailmesu, AFFE = _F( GROUP_NO = 'noeumesu', MODELISATION = ‘DIS_T’, PHENOMENE = ‘MECANIQUE’,), ) - Reading of the measurement: The measurement can be read via the operator LIRE_RESU. This operator makes it possible to read a file in universal format (dataset 58). It recovers the component of the observed field and assigns it to the corresponding model. mesure = LIRE_RESU ( FORMAT = 'IDEAS_DS58', UNITE = 33, MAILLAGE = mailmesu, TYPE_RESU = 'DYNA_TRANS', NOM_CHAM = 'SIEF_NOEU',) - Definition of the expansion basis: The expansion basis must be of type mode_meca. This concept may come from CALC_MODES or from DEFI_BASE_MODALE. If one wants to extrapolate a strain or stress field, the basis must be enriched, via the command CALC_CHAMP, by the strain or stress fields computed at the nodes. - Computation of the generalised coordinates: The computation of the generalised coordinates relative to the expansion basis is carried out by the operator PROJ_MESU_MODAL. repgene = PROJ_MESU_MODAL ( MODELE_CALCUL = _F( MODELE = modlcalc, BASE = base,), MODELE_MESURE = _F( MODELE = modlmesu, MESURE = mesure, NOM_CHAM = 'SIEF_NOEU',), CORR_MANU = _F( NOEU_MESURE = 'no1', NOEU_CALCUL = 'no2',), RESOLUTION = _F( METHODE = 'SVD', EPS = 1.E-4,), ) - Expansion onto the numerical model: This expansion consists in computing, on all the nodes of the numerical model, the field compatible with the field observed on the measured degrees of freedom. This expansion is carried out by the command REST_GENE_PHYS. reponse = REST_GENE_PHYS ( RESU_GENE = repgene, TOUT_CHAM = 'OUI',) 6 Bibliography 1. u4.73.02 Macro-command MACR_RECAL u4.73.02 Macro-command MACR_RECAL 1 Purpose Recalibrate analysis results on experimental results or on other analysis results. Consider, on the one hand, one or more test results and, on the other hand, one or more Code_Aster analyses modelling these tests. MACR_RECAL makes it possible to determine the parameters of these analyses (which may be parameters of a constitutive law, of a loading, etc.) describing the tests as well as possible. For more details on the algorithms implemented, refer to R4.03.06. 2 Syntax listr8 = MACR_RECAL( ◆ UNITE_ESCL = unit, ◇ & RESU_EXP = not_checked, / LIST_PARA = not_checked, ◇ / COURBE = _F( ◆ FONC_EXP = fonction, ◆ NOM_FONC_CALC = text, ◆ PARA_X = text, ◆ PARA_Y = text, ◇ POIDS = float, ), ◆ / PARA_OPTI = _F( ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◆ VALE_INI = float, ◆ VALE_MIN = float, ◆ VALE_MAX = float, ), / LIST_POIDS = not_checked, ◇ & RESU_CALC = not_checked, ◇ UNITE_RESU = unit (défaut: 91), ◇ PARA_DIFF_FINI = float (défaut: 1e-05), ◇ GRAPHIQUE = _F( ◇ FORMAT = / "XMGRACE" (par défaut), / "GNUPLOT", ◇ AFFICHAGE = / "TOUTE_ITERATION" (par défaut), / "ITERATION_FINALE", ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 29), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'XMGRACE') ◇ PILOTE = / "" (par défaut), / "POSTSCRIPT", / "EPS", / "MIF", / "SVG", / "PNM", / "PNG", / "JPEG", / "PDF", / "INTERACTIF", / "INTERACTIF_BG", ), ◇ METHODE = / "LEVENBERG" (par défaut), / "FMIN", / "FMINBFGS", / "FMINNCG", / "GENETIQUE", / "HYBRIDE", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'GENETIQUE') or equal_to("METHODE", 'HYBRIDE') ◇ NB_PARENTS = int (défaut: 10), ◇ NB_FILS = int (défaut: 5), ◇ ECART_TYPE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ GRAINE = int, ◇ ITER_ALGO_GENE = int (défaut: 10), ◇ RESI_ALGO_GENE = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ ITER_MAXI = int (défaut: 10), ◇ ITER_FONC_MAXI = int (défaut: 1000), ◇ RESI_GLOB_RELA = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ TOLE_PARA = float (défaut: 1e-08), ◇ TOLE_FONC = float (défaut: 1e-08), # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'FMINBFGS') ◇ GRADIENT = / "NON_CALCULE" (par défaut), / "NORMAL", / "ADIMENSIONNE", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'FMINNCG') ◆ GRADIENT = / "NORMAL", / "ADIMENSIONNE", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'LEVENBERG') ◇ GRADIENT = / "NORMAL" (par défaut), / "ADIMENSIONNE", ⟐ CALCUL_ESCLAVE = _F( ◇ LANCEMENT = / "DISTRIBUTION", / "INCLUSION" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("LANCEMENT", 'DISTRIBUTION') ◇ UNITE_SUIVI = unit (défaut: 29), ◇ MODE = / "INTERACTIF", / "BATCH", ◇ MEMOIRE = int, ◇ TEMPS = int, ◇ MPI_NBCPU = int, ◇ MPI_NBNOEUD = int, ◇ CLASSE = text, ◇ NMAX_SIMULT = int, ), ◇ DYNAMIQUE = _F( ◆ MODE_EXP = text, ◆ MODE_CALC = text, ◇ APPARIEMENT_MANUEL = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General presentation 3.1 Principle of the recalibration Consider the model problem of identification of the elastoplastic characteristics E , {\sigma}_{y} , {E}_{T} (respectively Young's modulus, yield stress and hardening modulus) of a material on a uniaxial tensile test. On the one hand one has the experimental tensile curve giving the evolution of the stress as a function of time, which is a datum: On the other hand one has a function of the 3 parameters which, for each value of the triplet E , {\sigma}_{y} , {E}_{T} , returns a computed tensile curve: The objective of the recalibration is then to answer the question: What are the values of (E,{\sigma}_{y},{E}_{T}) which describe my experiment as well as possible? 3.2 Organisation of the recalibration In order to carry out a recalibration successfully, it is necessary to have all of the following information: - the N experimental curves (an arbitrary weight may be assigned to each of these curves), - the P parameters to be recalibrated and, for each of them, an estimate of its initial value, its minimum value and its maximum value, - the command file modelling the N tests that one wants to recalibrate, - the names of the N quantities to be extracted from the command file above and which will be recalibrated on the N experimental curves. These quantities must be contained in a table coming from POST_RELEVE_T. The data setup of this information then requires the following organisation: - a command file called the master containing the N experimental curves, the P parameters, the names of the quantities to be recalibrated as well as other information specific to the recalibration, the whole being supplied in MACR_RECAL. The various formats used are specified in what follows, - a command file called the slave modelling the experimental tests. Indeed, the recalibration is an iterative process: the master file executes the slave file, it recovers the N curves computed with the current values of the P parameters, it compares the values of the computed curves with those of the experimental curves, it deduces new values for the P parameters and launches the slave file again. This process continues until convergence is obtained. N experimental curves Master file MACR_RECAL (.comm file of the study profile) P parameters Recalibration loops N computed curves Slave file Figure 3.2-a. Diagram of the operation of the recalibration procedure for the classical case In the following part the operands of MACR_RECAL are described. Reference is made there to a few notions of the Python language. It is however in no way necessary to know Python in order to use this macro-command. The part “Example of use” is there to enlighten the user. The data structure produced is a list of reals containing the values of the parameters at convergence in the event of convergence, or at the last iteration otherwise. 3.3 Particular case of use: mode EXTERNE In this mode of use, the optimisation algorithm is external to Code_Aster . Figure 3.3-a : MACR_RECAL method EXTERNE Code_Aster is only a black box which takes as input a text file containing the list of the parameter values, carries out the computation of the functional for this set of parameters, possibly carries out the computation of the gradients with respect to the parameters, and returns to the external algorithm, by means of a text file, the value of the functional and possibly of the gradients. In this mode of operation, paragraph 3.1 remains valid. 3.4 Particular case of the recalibration of a dynamic model In the case of the recalibration of the parameters of a dynamic model using experimental data coming from the dynamic analysis, there are a few particularities for the implementation. The experimental data are in this case natural frequencies and eigenvectors (mode shapes) contained in a mode_meca concept coming from the measurement. The user has this concept from a data-acquisition software, usually in “.unv” format, and must build a so-called “experimental” model in order to use it in the Code_Aster environment. This “experimental” model contains, among other things, the experimental mesh, that is the mesh of the sensors, coarser than the mesh of the numerical model, which must also be available for the recalibration study. The user therefore no longer has to supply the experimental curves in the master file, but will supply here the names of the concepts which contain them, concepts which will be extracted by a first slave analysis from the external “unv” file. The format used to transmit this information to MACR_RECAL is the same as that for RESU_CALC: a Python list of N Python lists containing the names of the tables and of the columns containing the experimental responses. Below one presents the diagram of the recalibration process in the case of dynamics: Figure 3.4-a. Diagram of the operation of the recalibration procedure in dynamics > Two other particularities concern the command file of the slave analysis: - it also contains the commands necessary for the construction of the experimental model. The mode_meca concept usable to extract RESU_EXP is supplied by LIRE_RESU; - The quantities corresponding to the experimental and numerical responses are always contained in tables but no longer necessarily coming from POST_RELEVE_T. The responses linked to the mode shapes come either from CREA_TABLE (for the experimental MAC criterion) or from MAC_MODES (for the numerical MAC criterion). One recalls that the MAC criterion U4.52.15 serves to compare two modal bases; here it is the experimental one and the numerical one. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand UNITE_ESCL ♦ UNITE_ESCL Logical unit number of the slave file, assigned in the Astk interface (column UL). The extension of this file may be arbitrary. 4.2 Operands RESU_EXP, RESU_CALC, FONC_EXP, NOM_FONC_CALC, PARA_X, PARA_Y, POIDS The user has 2 input modes for supplying the experimental data and the names of the tables and of the columns of the computed results. He or she has the choice of using: - RESU_EXP and RESU_CALC and possibly LIST_POIDS, which require the entry of Python lists, - the keywords FONC_EXP, NOM_FONC_CALC, PARA_X, PARA_Y, POIDS of the factor keyword COURBE, which have the advantage of using Aster concepts. ◊ RESU_EXP Name of the Python list of N numpy arrays containing the N experimental curves. For a static model the list is defined beforehand in the form: resu_exp=[ numpy.array([[x0,y0], [x1,y1], ... [xn,yn]]), ... numpy.array([[u0,v0], [u1,v1], ... [un,vn]]) ] For the recalibration of a dynamic model with experimental modal data (frequencies and eigenvectors), it will be the name of the Python list of N Python lists containing the names of the tables and of the columns containing the experimental responses. For example: resu_exp=[[‘REPEX1’,’NUM_ORDR’,’FREQ’],[‘REPEX2’,’NUM_ORDR’,’MAC_EXP’]] ◊ RESU_CALC Name of the list of N Python lists containing the names of the tables and of the columns containing the numerical responses corresponding to the experimental measurements on which the recalibration will be carried out. For example: resu_calc=[['TABLE1’,’INST’,’SIYY’], ['TABLE2’,’INST’,’V1’], ...] ◊ LIST_POIDS Name of the Numpy array containing the N weights to be assigned to the N experimental curves. If the keyword is not supplied, then each curve has the same weight. The list is defined beforehand in the form: LIST_POIDS= numpy.array([p1, p2, ...]) ◊ FONC_EXP Name of the function previously defined by the operator DEFI_FONCTION which corresponds to the experimental data. To make the link with RESU_EXP, the function supplied to this keyword at iteration i corresponds to the i th numerical array of RESU_EXP. ◊ NOM_FONC_CALC Chaîne de caractères correspondant au nom que l'on souhaite attribuer à la fonction après recalage des données expérimentales. ◊ POIDS Valeur du poids à affecter à la courbe expérimentale. Si non renseigné, alors la valeur est 1. ◊ PARA_X Name of the parameter X of the computed function. ◊ PARA_Y Name of the parameter Y of the computed function. For example: COURBE=( _F(FONC_EXP=fct1, NOM_FONC_CALC='TABLE1',PARA_X='INST',PARA_Y='SIYY',), _F(FONC_EXP=fct2, NOM_FONC_CALC='TABLE2',PARA_X='INST',PARA_Y='V1',),) 4.3 Operands LIST_PARA, PARA_OPTI, NOM_PARA, VALE_INI, VALE_MIN, VALE_MAX The user has 2 input modes for supplying the names and the values of the parameters. He or she has the choice of using: - LIST_PARA, which require the entry of Python lists, - the keywords NOM_PARA, VALE_INI, VALE_MIN, VALE_MAX of the factor keyword PARA_OPTI, which have the advantage of using Code_Aster concepts (numerical values or character strings). ◊ LIST_PARA Name of the Python list of P Python lists containing the names of the variables, their initial values, their minimum values and their maximum values. This list is defined beforehand in the form: List_para=[['PARA1__’, INI_1, MIN_1, MAX_1], [‘PARA2__’, INI_2, MIN_2, MAX_2], .... [‘PARAP__’, INI_P, MIN_P, MAX_P]] Warning: One requires that the names of the variables end with two underscores (for example: YOUN__). Note: The bounds are not handled by the algorithms FMIN, FMINBFGS and FMINNCG. ◊ NOM_PARA Name of the parameter. The character string supplied to NOM_PARA at iteration i corresponds to the first element of the i th Python list of the list supplied to LIST_PARA. ◊ VALE_INI Initial value of the parameter. The real supplied to NOM_PARA at iteration i corresponds to the second element of the i th Python list of the list supplied to LIST_PARA. ◊ VALE_MIN Minimum value of the parameter. The real supplied to NOM_PARA at iteration i corresponds to the third element of the i th Python list of the list supplied to LIST_PARA. ◊ VALE_MAX Maximum value of the parameter. The real supplied to NOM_PARA at iteration i corresponds to the fourth element of the i th Python list of the list supplied to LIST_PARA. 4.4 Operand UNITE_RESU ◊ UNITE_RESU Logical unit number of the result file of the recalibration (evolution of the parameters during the iterations, convergence criteria). 4.5 Operand ITER_MAXI ◊ ITER_MAXI Maximum number of recalibration iterations. 4.6 Operand ITER_FONC_MAXI ◊ ITER_FONC_MAXI Maximum number of evaluations of the functional. 4.7 Operand RESI_GLOB_RELA ◊ RESI_GLOB_RELA Global relative residual of the recalibration. This value is separate from that supplied for the non-linear solvers STAT_NON_LINE and DYNA_NON_LINE. 4.8 Operand TOLE_FONC ◊ TOLE_FONC Stopping criterion of the recalibration algorithm based on the variation of the functional from one iteration to the next. This criterion corresponds to the absolute value of the norm of the functional. 4.9 Operand TOLE_PARA ◊ TOLE_PARA Stopping criterion of the recalibration algorithm based on the variation of the parameters from one iteration to the next. This criterion corresponds to the \mathit{L2} norm: square root of the sum of the squares of the differences of each parameter. 4.10 Operand PARA_DIFF_FINI ◊ PARA_DIFF_FINI The recalibration requires the computation of the derivatives of the responses with respect to the parameters. This computation is carried out by finite differences. PARA_DIFF_FINI corresponds to \alpha in the following formula: \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}\approx \frac{f(x+\alpha x)-f(x)}{\alpha x} 4.11 Operand GRAPHIQUE ◊ UNITE Logical unit number of the plots produced during the recalibration. At each iteration, MACR_RECAL produces N graphic files (whose format is defined by the keyword PILOTE) representing the N experimental and computed curves. ◊ PILOTE Type of display of the plots. If PILOTE = 'INTERACTIF' or 'INTERACTIF_BG', xmgrace is opened interactively with the plot. With 'INTERACTIF_BG', xmgrace is called in the background and the analysis continues. If PILOTE is 'POSTSCRIPT', 'EPS', 'MIF', 'SVG', 'PNM', 'PNG', 'JPEG' or 'PDF' then xmgrace is used to generate the file of the corresponding format, in the logical unit defined by UNITE. Warning: The INTERACTIF mode is possible only when the recalibration runs interactively and not in batch. ◊ FORMAT Choice of the software for displaying the curves in interactive mode: xmgrace or gnuplot. The use of Xmgrace is blocking: one must close the Xmgrace window in order to continue the execution. ◊ AFFICHAGE Display of the curves at each iteration or only at the end. 4.12 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE Method or optimisation algorithm chosen: 1. LEVENBERG (default): Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. This algorithm is the one recommended for quadratic minimisation problems of least-squares type, such as problems of recalibration of material parameters. 2. FMIN: Nelder–Mead simplex algorithm (uses only estimates of the functional). 3. FMINBFGS: quasi-Newton method (uses the functional and the gradient of the functional). 4. FMINNCG: line-search Newton conjugate-gradient method (uses the functional, the gradient of the functional and its Hessian). 5. GENETIQUE: evolutionary algorithm based on the mechanism of selection and replacement. It is an algorithm which is expensive in CPU time; its use is advised only for a coarse exploration of the parameter space within the hybrid recalibration technique presented in the following point. 6. HYBRIDE: technique which combines the stochastic with the deterministic — the evolutionary algorithm with the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. 7. Mode EXTERNE: this method makes it possible to use an optimisation algorithm external to Code_Aster , for example Matlab or Scilab, and to use Code_Aster only for the estimation of the functional and possibly of the gradient by finite differences. This is not a keyword of MACR_RECAL, because mode EXTERNE is used directly by calling the file bibpyt/Macro/recal.py. Concerning the choice of the optimisation algorithm , it is strongly advised to opt for the default algorithm, Levenberg–Marquardt . The latter is very often superior to the FMIN algorithms for minimisation problems of least-squares type, such as the recalibration of parameters. Indeed, it uses the functional in its vector form whereas the other algorithms use a scalar functional, consequently less rich. Moreover, it uses an active-constraint method in order to handle bounds on the parameters, whereas the other algorithms do not handle the bounds. The other algorithms may nevertheless be useful in the cases where Levenberg–Marquardt is in difficulty. For example, the FMIN algorithm does not use gradients, whose evaluation may in certain very particular cases generate numerical problems (very sensitive parameters, too few experimental values, or others). The FMIN algorithm is distinctly slower, but will be able to reach convergence (to draw a parallel, the issue is similar to that of using the elastic matrix in place of the tangent matrix in STAT_NON_LINE). For the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, the document R4.03.06 describes more precisely the mathematical algorithms brought into play. The FMIN algorithms have been taken over in full from a Python module distributed on the Internet (http://pylab.sourceforge.net) under the GPL licence by Travis E. Oliphant, who is moreover the principal contributor to the Python-Scipy project and responsible for the optimisation module of Scipy. The details of the algorithms and of the implementation can be found on the page http://pylab.sourceforge.net. The HYBRIDE method is advised when one has a high degree of uncertainty on the optimal values of the parameters or when the functional presents numerous local minima. Thus, within this method, one first launches a coarse search with the evolutionary algorithm, which will make it possible to avoid the local minima, followed by a refinement of the optimisation with the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. 4.13 Keyword CALCUL_ESCLAVE 4.13.1 Operand LANCEMENT ◊ LANCEMENT Method of launching the slave files: inclusion or distribution. The two modes have advantages and disadvantages, and the choice of one or the other depends mainly on the run times of the slave files, as well as on their compatibility with Inclusion mode. 4.13.2 Operand INCLUSION ◊ INCLUSION In this mode, the slave file is included. There is therefore no loss of time for the generation of a new study, the creation of the temporary execution directory, etc. In return, only one slave study will be able to run at the same time on the machine. On the other hand, certain slave studies (for example those using included data files, or somewhat complex execution profiles) are not compatible. Note: In INCLUSION mode, the Aster command INCLUDE cannot be present in the slave file (incompatibility with the Aster supervisor). One must therefore replace the command: INCLUDE(UNITE=n) by the command: execfile(fort.n) where n is the logical unit of the file to be included. 4.13.3 Operands DISTRIBUTION, MODE, MEMOIRE, TEMPS, CLASSE, UNITE_SUIVI ◊ DISTRIBUTION In this mode, at each iteration of the optimisation algorithm, the N+1 slave analyses (for a recalibration of N parameters) are executed in parallel, in batch or interactively, using the distributed-analysis module of as_run. Compared with Inclusion mode, each study is slightly longer to execute, because one must regenerate a new Code_Aster study, create the temporary files, etc. On the other hand, as the studies are launched in parallel, depending on the characteristics of the slave studies (size and duration), the larger the number of parameters, the more Distributed mode becomes advantageous over Inclusion mode. In distributed mode, additional parameters are available in order to control the executions of the slave analyses: ◊ MODE : INTERACTIF ou BATCH ◊ MEMOIRE : mémoire en Mo ◊ TEMPS : temps en secondes ◊ CLASSE : classe de batch, permet de forcer les calculs à utiliser une classe spécifique, par exemple «distr» sur le serveur Code_Aster ◊ UNITE_SUIVI : si ce mot-clé est préciser, il défini l'unité logique du fichier du profil dans lequel seront stockés tous les fichiers output des jobs esclaves ◊ NMAX_SIMULT: nombre de calculs esclaves lancés en parallèle en mode distribution (si aucune valeur n'est renseigné, le code décide automatiquement de ce nombre) It is possible to use MPI parallelism for the slave studies. In this case, it is necessary to launch the master analysis with an MPI version and on a single processor (in interactive mode or in batch). The MPI characteristics of the slave analyses must be indicated by the following keywords: ◊ MPI_NBCPU: nombre de processeurs MPI pour chacun des calculs esclaves lancés en parallèle ◊ MPI_NBNOEUD: nombre de nœuds pour chaque calcul esclave lancé en parallèle One notes that operating problems may disturb the launching of the distributed slave analyses (for example, the batch classes are badly defined and the analyses cannot execute). In this case, the error obtained in the .mess of the master analysis may be rather terse (an error message of the kind “at least one of the slave analyses could not start”). In order to obtain additional information concerning the distributed module of as_run, one must set UNITE_SUIVI and INFO=2 simultaneously. 4.14 Operands NB_PARENTS and NB_FILS ◊ NB_PARENTS For the method GENETIQUE or HYBRIDE, this operand defines the size of the population of the parameter sets. Initially all the individuals are identical and initialised with the initial values of the parameters supplied by the user in LIST_PARA. During the optimisation the population evolves, the least “adapted” individuals being replaced by others which have supplied a better value of the functional. ◊ NB_FILS Represents the replacement rate of the population. More precisely, the best “parent” (the one for which the value of the functional is the smallest) is allowed to reproduce, thus generating NB_FILS “children”. At that moment the size of the population is NB_PARENTS+NB_FILS. According to the hierarchy of the values of the functional, only the best individuals of this whole population are retained and one returns to the initial size: NB_PARENTS. 4.15 Operand ECART_TYPE ◊ ECART_TYPE This is the value of the standard deviation that the user imposes for the quasi-random draws of the “children”. The more one wants to explore the topological space of the parameters, the more one must increase this value. Corroborated with the size of the population and the replacement rate, this operand makes it possible to drive the evolutionary algorithm according to the complexity of the model and the degree of uncertainty on the optimal values of the parameters. If one knows little about the values of the parameters to be recalibrated, it is advisable to use a large population size, a likewise high replacement rate and a large standard deviation. The counterpart will be a very high CPU time. 4.16 Operand ITER_ALGO_GENE ◊ ITER_ALGO_GENE Maximum number of iterations for the evolutionary algorithm. If one uses the HYBRIDE method, this value (or RESI_ALGO_GENE) will determine the switch to the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. 4.17 Operand RESI_ALGO_GENE ◊ RESI_ALGO_GENE Relative residual of the recalibration of the evolutionary algorithm. If one uses the HYBRIDE method, this value (or ITER_ALGO_GENE) will determine the switch to the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. 4.18 Operand GRAINE ◊ GRAINE Value imposed by the user for the seed of the generator of the random draws in the evolutionary algorithm. If one supplies a value for this keyword, one forces the random-number generator present in the evolutionary algorithm to generate always the same draws, and one will therefore have a repetition of the solution. Its use is reserved only for the test cases, for reasons of monitoring the non-regression of the code. 4.19 Operand DYNAMIQUE One supplies this operand for the recalibration of the parameters of a dynamic model by modal analysis. ◊ MODE_EXP Name of the mode_meca concept which contains the experimental modal data. This concept is extracted in the slave analysis by an LIRE_RESU. ◊ MODE_CALC Name of the mode_meca concept which contains the numerical modal data. This concept is computed in the slave file by a CALC_MODES. ◊ APPARIEMENT_MANUEL Choice of displaying, in interactive mode, a graphical window which will make it possible to pair the eigenmodes manually. One thus avoids, for example, the bad automatic pairing of crossed double eigenmodes. The screen capture presented in Figure 4.19-a illustrates this graphical window. Figure 4.19-a. Graphical window for the manual pairing of the MAC The user thus sees, at each generation of the evolutionary algorithm or at each iteration of the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, the MAC matrix, and he or she can decide to change the pairing by modifying the order of the modes in the lists located at the bottom of the window. This window is blocking for the execution of the Code_Aster commands, so one must close it in order for the recalibration process to continue. Closing the window by clicking on the Close button makes it possible to recover the new lists of modes whose order has possibly been modified by the user. 4.20 Operand GRADIENT ◊ GRADIENT For the methods FMINBFGS, FMINNCG or EXTERNE, this keyword makes it possible to indicate to Code_Aster the way of computing the gradients (non-dimensionalised or not), or else not to compute them. Note: for the algorithms which use the gradients, the latter may be computed by finite differences automatically by Code_Aster , or else computed in the slave file by using, for example, sensitivity analyses (keyword LIST_DERIV). 5 Precautions of use Here is a set of pieces of advice indispensable to the proper use of the recalibration. - The experimental curves are defined as arrays with two columns: one for the abscissae and one for the ordinates. - The experimental curves must be functions: only one ordinate must correspond to an abscissa. If an experimental curve contains cycles (for example stress as a function of strain in loading–unloading), one must then split this parameterised curve into two curves, expressing on the one hand the abscissae and on the other hand the ordinates of the cyclic curve as a function of the parameter (for example strain as a function of time and stress as a function of time). - One must recalibrate N computed curves on N experimental curves. - The first computed curve will be recalibrated on the first experimental curve, the second computed curve will be recalibrated on the second experimental curve, and so on in the order supplied for the operands RESU_EXP and RESU_CALC. - The computed quantities supplied under the operand RESU_CALC must come from POST_RELEVE_T (except for dynamics, where one may have tables coming from CREA_TABLE and MAC_MODES). - The recalibration parameters must be declared as a block at the beginning of the slave command file. For example: DEBUT() DSDE__ = 200. YOUN__ = 8.E4 SIGY__ = 10. ...... - The initial values of the recalibration parameters are those supplied for the operand LIST_PARA and not those present in the user's slave file. - At each recalibration iteration, the analyses defined in the slave file must converge. In the context of the recalibration of non-linear analyses, it is therefore strongly recommended to use the automatic cutting of the time step. - In the context of the recalibration of non-linear analyses with automatic cutting of the time step, it is indispensable to define an archiving list under the operand LIST_ARCH. - The recalibration is a powerful means of obtaining parameter values from tests. It is however not miraculous: the experimental curves must contain enough information to identify the parameters. It is for example impossible to identify elastoplastic parameters with a test remaining in the elastic domain. The experimental tests must therefore excite the parameters to be identified. - In the same logic, it is desirable that the experimental curves contain a sufficient number of points to describe properly the action of the parameters to be identified. - Finally, in the case of the use of several experimental curves, the fact that they have the same number of points balances the information that they provide. 6 Examples of use 6.1 Identification of the parameters of an elastoplastic constitutive law on a tensile test This example is treated by the test ZZZZ159A V1.01.159. 6.1.1 Statement of the problem One has the results of a tensile test. They are the evolution of the stress {\sigma}_{yy} in the course of time as well as the evolution of the cumulative plastic strain p in the course of time. | Stress SIYY | Cumulative plastic strain | | --- | --- | One wishes to recalibrate, on these tests, Young's modulus, the yield stress and the hardening slope of an elastoplastic constitutive law with linear isotropic hardening. 6.1.2 Data setup 6.1.2.1 Experiment One begins first by defining our test results. They consist of two curves which one defines as follows. exper1 = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA='INST', NOM_RESU='SIYY', VALE=(0.00000E+00 , 0.00000E+00 , 5.00000E-02 , 5.00000E+01 , ... 9.50000E-01 , 2.07500E+02 , 1.00000E+00 , 2.08000E+02 ),) exper2 = DEFI_FONCTION( NOM_PARA='INST', NOM_RESU='V1', VALE=(0.00000E+00 , 0.00000E+00 , 5.00000E-02 , 0.00000E+00 , ... 9.50000E-01 , 3.71250E-03 , 1.00000E+00 , 3.96000E-03 ),) exper1 and exper2 are therefore functions which represent respectively the stress {\sigma}_{yy} and the cumulative plastic strain p . 6.1.2.2 Analysis One then writes the Code_Aster slave command file modelling this tensile test, in which our 3 parameters will appear as well as the two curves to be recalibrated.
