Identification of the parameters of a dynamic model by exploiting the sensitivity of the eigenmodes This example is treated by the test SDLS121A V2.03.121. One wishes to recalibrate the thickness of a plate and the value of a discrete mass which is located on it, by using experimental measurements of eigenmodes. 6.2.1 Data setup In the master file one first supplies the names of the tables which will contain both the computed results and the numerical results: calcul = [["REPONSE1", "NUME_ORDRE", "FREQ"], ["REPONSE2", "NUME_ORDRE", "MAC"]] experience = [["REPEXP1", "NUME_ORDRE", "FREQ"], ["REPEXP2", "NUME_ORDRE", "MAC_EXP"]] It is important to note here that, for the computed results, REPONSE2 is given by the diagonal of the MAC matrix coming from the command MAC_MODES, as one will see a little later in this paragraph. The name of the parameter 'MAC' is therefore a reserved name, chosen as such in the Fortran, and it can therefore no longer be used afterwards (for the corresponding experimental response one has chosen 'MAC_EXP'). The options retained in the command MACR_RECAL, still in the master file, are: RESU = MACR_RECAL( UNITE_ESCL=3, RESU_EXP=experience, LIST_PARA=parametres, RESU_CALC=calcul, POIDS=poids, METHODE="HYBRIDE", ITER_FONC_MAXI=500, NB_PARENTS=10, NB_FILS=5, ECART_TYPE=10.0, ITER_ALGO_GENE=2, DYNAMIQUE=_F(MODE_EXP="MODMES", MODE_CALC="MODNUM", APPARIEMENT_MANUEL="NON"), ) One has therefore chosen to launch the recalibration by using the HYBRIDE method with two iterations for the evolutionary algorithm. Finally one defines the following profile for the study: 6.2.2 Slave analysis The main particularity of the slave analysis is the presence in the command file (unit 3) of two models: the experimental model and the numerical one. Below one presents, for this test case, the slave command file with the necessary explanations. - reading of the experimental mesh (the mesh of the sensors): PRE_GIBI(UNITE_GIBI=23) MAILEXP1 = LIRE_MAILLAGE() - creation of a node group which will later serve to define a discrete mass element: MAILEXP1 = DEFI_GROUP( reuse=MAILEXP1, MAILLAGE=MAILEXP1, CREA_GROUP_NO=_F(NOM="NO_MA", OPTION="ENV_SPHERE", POINT=(2.0, 3.0), RAYON=0.1, PRECISION=0.1), ) - creation of the node group in order to define the boundary conditions: MAILEXP1 = DEFI_GROUP( reuse=MAILEXP1, MAILLAGE=MAILEXP1, CREA_GROUP_NO=_F(GROUP_MA="BORDS", NOM="BORDS") ) - creation of a POI1 element in order to introduce the discrete mass: MAILEXP2 = CREA_MAILLAGE(MAILLAGE=MAILEXP1, CREA_POI1=(_F(NOM_GROUP_MA="MASS", GROUP_NO="NO_MA"),)) - assignment of the experimental model: MODEXP = AFFE_MODELE( MAILLAGE=MAILEXP2, AFFE=( _F(GROUP_MA="TOUT_ELT", PHENOMENE="MECANIQUE", MODELISATION="DST"), _F(GROUP_MA="MASS", PHENOMENE="MECANIQUE", MODELISATION="DIS_T"), ), ) - definition of the elementary characteristics, material, etc. CAREXP=AFFE_CARA_ELEM(...) ACIER=DEFI_MATERIAU(...) MATEX=AFFE_MATERIAU(...) - elementary analyses and assembly of the matrices. KELEXP=CALC_MATR_ELEM(OPTION='RIGI_MECA', ...) MELEXP=CALC_MATR_ELEM(OPTION='MASS_MECA', ...) NUMEXP=NUME_DDL(...) KASSEXP=ASSE_MATRICE(...) MASSEXP=ASSE_MATRICE(...) - creation of the sd_mode_meca with the experimental eigenmodes: MODMES = LIRE_RESU( TYPE_RESU="MODE_MECA", FORMAT="IDEAS", MODELE=MODEXP, UNITE=21, NOM_CHAM="DEPL", MATR_RIGI=KASSEXP, MATR_MASS=MASSEXP, FORMAT_IDEAS=_F( NOM_CHAM="DEPL", NUME_DATASET=55, RECORD_6=(1, 2, 3, 8, 2, 6), POSI_ORDRE=(7, 4), POSI_NUME_MODE=(7, 4), POSI_FREQ=(8, 1), POSI_MASS_GENE=(8, 2), POSI_AMOR_GENE=(8, 3), NOM_CMP=("DX", "DY", "DZ", "DRX", "DRY", "DRZ"), ), TOUT_ORDRE="OUI", ) And one continues with the numerical model, the same steps. The parameters to be recalibrated are EP__ (the thickness) and MP__ (the mass): EP__ = 0.5 MP__ = 50000.0 PRE_GIBI(UNITE_GIBI=22) # nombre de fréquences NF = 8 MODES = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI=M_AS_RIG, MATR_MASS=M_AS_MAS, OPTION="PLUS_PETITE", CALC_FREQ=_F(NMAX_FREQ=NF), SOLVEUR_MODAL=_F(METHODE="SORENSEN"), VERI_MODE=_F(STOP_ERREUR="NON"), ) The experimental mesh is always coarser than the mesh of the numerical model, so one must project the numerical result onto the experimental mesh: MODNUM = PROJ_CHAMP(RESULTAT=MODES, MODELE_1=MODEL, MODELE_2=MODEXP, NUME_DDL=NUMEXP) One recovers the table of the experimental frequencies REPEXP1 = RECU_TABLE(CO=MODMES, NOM_PARA="FREQ") One builds the table of the experimental MAC — in fact the ideal MAC, which is 1.0 liste_mac = [1.0] NF REPEXP2 = CREA_TABLE( LISTE=(_F(PARA="NUME_ORDRE", LISTE_I=range(1, NF + 1)), _F(PARA="MAC_EXP", LISTE_R=liste_mac)) ) And finally the tables with the computed responses: REPONSE1 = RECU_TABLE(CO=MODES, NOM_PARA="FREQ") REPONSE2 = MAC_MODES(BASE_1=MODNUM, BASE_2=MODMES) The results (the recalibrated values of the parameters) are then computed in a similar way to the classical case of recalibration presented in the preceding paragraph. 6.3 Parametric identification of a conservative system by exploiting the orthogonality of the eigenmodes This example is treated by modelling D of the test case SDLS121 V2.03.121. One wishes to recalibrate the thickness of a plate and the value of a discrete mass which is located on it, by using experimental measurements of eigenmodes. From the mode shapes recorded at the observation points, one carries out an expansion onto the supporting numerical model. One then tries to recover the parameters of the model such that the generalised mass and stiffness matrices relative to the modes identified experimentally are diagonal and that the discrepancy between the measured natural circular frequency and the computed natural circular frequency is minimal. 6.3.1 Data setup The technique illustrated here exploits the identified mode shapes extended onto the supporting numerical model. This mode shape can be obtained by means of an independent analysis by depositing the extended shapes in a file which will later be read by the slave file. For practical reasons, one carries out the expansion in the driving file. It is thus easier to recover the support model which will be used in the slave file. In the master file one supplies both the target values (experimental values) and the names of the tables which contain the results coming from the numerical analysis carried out in the slave file. The different steps are recalled below. - Creation of an experimental model in order to be able to define the location of the measurement points. The nodes of the mesh may be linked to one another by discrete elements in order to facilitate the visualisation of the measured information. The mechanical characteristics that one assigns to this model do not influence the results; they allow the model to receive the identified eigenmodes - Reading of the identified eigenmodes - Creation of the supporting numerical model for the expansion of the measurement - Definition of the expansion basis (here, a modal basis) - Computation of the coordinates of the identified modes in the expansion basis - Expansion of the measured information onto the support model - Writing of the extended modes in a file in order to be able to use it in the slave analysis - Definition of the target values The target values are deposited in two lists. The first list contains the off-diagonal terms which should be zero and the second list contains the identified natural frequencies. - Definition of the recalibration parameters - Launching of the optimisation procedure 6.3.2 Slave analysis The slave analysis creates the tables which will contain the values computed from the input parameters. The different analysis steps are described below: - Creation of the support model (same numbering of the degrees of freedom as that which served for the expansion of the measurement) - Reading of the extended mode shapes - Computation of the generalised mass and stiffness matrices via MAC_MODES - Creation of the tables which contain the off-diagonal terms of the generalised matrices - Creation of the table which contains the natural frequencies estimated by means of the generalised matrices 6.4 Parametric identification of a dissipative system by exploiting the norm relations of the mode shapes This example is treated by modelling E of the test case SDLS121 V2.03.121. One wishes to recalibrate the thickness of a plate, the value of a point mass on the plate and the discrete dampings distributed over the plate. From the complex mode shapes recorded at the observation points, one carries out an expansion onto the supporting numerical model. One then tries to recover the parameters of the model in such a way that the eigenmodes identified experimentally satisfy the norm relations associated with the numerical model. One focuses only on the diagonal terms of the normalisation matrix. 6.4.1 Data setup The data setup resembles that presented in the previous chapter (6.3). The difference lies in the expansion of the mode shape. The mode shapes are complex here. One carries out the expansion by processing the real part and the imaginary part independently. The extended complex shape is obtained after assembly of the extended real shape and of the extended imaginary shape. The different steps are described below: - Creation of the experimental model - Reading of the identified (experimental) eigenmodes - Expansion of the measurement - Definition of the target values (the target values are zero vectors here) - Definition of the recalibration parameters - Launching of the optimisation procedure 6.4.2 Slave analysis The slave analysis creates the tables which will contain the diagonal terms of the normalisation matrix. The different analysis steps are described below: - Creation of the support model (same numbering of the degrees of freedom as that which served for the expansion of the measurement) - Reading of the extended mode shapes - Reading of the natural frequencies and of the reduced damping ratios - Computation of the matrix–vector products by PROD_MATR_CHAM - creation of the table which contains the terms relating to damping and mass: \frac{{y}_{\nu}^{T}B\bar{{y}_{\nu}}+2\Re ({s}_{\nu}){y}_{\nu}^{T}M\bar{{y}_{\nu}}}{\mid {n}_{\nu}\mid }={z}_{1\nu } - creation of the table which contains the terms relating to stiffness and mass: \frac{{s}_{\nu}\bar{{s}_{\nu}}{y}_{\nu}^{T}M\bar{{y}_{\nu}}-{y}_{\nu}^{T}K\bar{{y}_{\nu}}}{\mid {n}_{\nu}{s}_{\nu}\mid }={z}_{2\nu } - creation of the table which contains the terms relating to mass, stiffness and damping: \frac{{s}_{\nu}^{2}{y}_{\nu}^{T}{\mathit{My}}_{\nu}+{s}_{\nu}{y}_{\nu}^{T}{\mathit{By}}_{\nu}+{y}_{\nu}^{T}{\mathit{Ky}}_{\nu}}{{n}_{\nu}{s}_{\nu}}={z}_{3\nu } 7 Use of mode EXTERNE 7.1 Warning We draw attention to the fact that this mode of operation is to be reserved for advanced use. Most cases should be treated with the algorithms supplied in the command MACR_RECAL, and in particular the Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm, which is the best suited to problems of parameter recalibration. This mode of operation requires external software in order to carry out the optimisation (Python code, Matlab, Scilab, black-box type software, etc.). Moreover, it is necessary to have some Python skills. Finally, the use of mode EXTERNE falls outside the quality-assurance scope of Aster , and should not be used for safety-important studies (IPS). 7.2 Methodology 7.2.1 Principle In this mode of use, Code_Aster is used only for the evaluation of the functional for an optimisation software which is completely external to Code_Aster . Figure 7.2.1-a : MACR_RECAL “External algorithm” Generally, optimisation software packages ask the user to write a procedure for the computation of the functional: f = F(param). If the software allows the reading/writing of files and the execution of external code (“system” command or others), then it is potentially usable with MACR_RECAL. One will encapsulate the call to the Python procedure recal.py as well as the writing of the parameter file and the re-reading of the file of the value of the functional in the routine for the computation of F. Figure 7.2.1-b : MACR_RECAL “Principle of mode EXTERNE”, example Matlab The optimisation software launches Code_Aster at each evaluation of the functional. The functional-evaluation routine goes through text files in order to send to Code_Aster the parameters to be used and in order to recover the value of the functional. The Python routine recal.py can therefore be called independently of Aster and makes the link between the optimisation software and Code_Aster (recovery of the parameter file, reformatting of the slave file, launching of Aster, recovery of the functional). In practice, one must have a classical Astk profile of the slave study (and not the profile of one use of MACR_RECAL). This profile must be completely functional. Under this EXTERNE mode, the mode of operation is the following: the routine recal.py takes care of recovering the parameters from the command line or from an input.txt file, will replace these parameters in the slave profile, then will launch the execution of the slave study for the new parameters, and finally will return in a text file output.txt the values of the functional. To date, this mode of operation has been tested with several optimisation software packages (the optimisation toolbox of Matlab, the Tomlab toolbox for Matlab, and the optimisation module of Python-Scipy), but it is possible to use almost any software provided that this software allows the external execution of a script. One thinks in particular of Zopt (Zebulon), SiDoLo. 7.2.2 Use of the external launching file recal.py The file recal.py can be executed autonomously with a few optional parameters on the command line: Usage: /aster/NEW10/bibpyt/Macro/recal.py fichier_export [options] Options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --input=INPUT Text string containing the parameters --input_step=INPUT_STEP Text string containing the discretisation steps of the finite differences --input_file=INPUT_FILE File containing the parameters --input_step_file=INPUT_STEP_FILE File containing the discretisation steps of the finite differences --output=OUTPUT file containing the functional --output_grad=OUTPUT_GRAD file containing the gradient --aster_root=ASTER_ROOT Aster installation path --as_run=as_run Path to as_run --resudir=RESUDIR Default path of the temporary Aster executions --noclean Erase temporary Code_Aster execution directory --info=INFO message level (0, 1, 2) --sources_root=SOURCES_ROOT Default path of the Python overloads --objective=OBJECTIVE Functional ([fcalc]/[error]) --objective_type=OBJECTIVE_TYPE type of the functional (float/[vector]) --gradient_type=GRADIENT_TYPE computation of the gradient by Code_Aster ([no]/normal/adim) --mr_parameters=MR_PARAMETERS MACR_RECAL parameter file: parameters, analysis, experiment --study_parameters=STUDY_PARAMETERS Study parameter file: export --parameters=PARAMETERS Parameter file This procedure needs: 1. the .export file of the Astk study defined previously (the standard MACR_RECAL study) 2. a text file containing the list of the parameters From these two files, it launches a Code_Aster analysis for the specified parameters (or two Code_Aster analyses, see above) and generates a text file containing only the value of the functional (scalar or vector). This procedure can be launched without an argument. It will then look in the current directory for default files: 1. if there is only one .export file in the current directory, it will be used (otherwise the procedure stops in error) 2. the default input file will be looked for under the name “input.txt” 3. the output file will be generated with the name “output.txt” The arguments –i (--input) and -o (--output) make it possible to specify the files. The argument –g (--output_grad) makes it possible to specify the text file in which the gradient will be written, if the latter is requested (argument -G). Other arguments are available: 1. --info: defines the message level; 0=silent, 1 or 2; 2. --objective: makes it possible to specify whether the functional must be returned in vector or scalar form; 3. --gradient: makes it possible to specify whether one does not want Aster to compute and return the gradients (no), and, if one wants the gradients, to specify whether one wants them non-dimensionalised or not; By default, a Code_Aster .output file is created in the execution directory of the procedure, making it possible to have access to the output of the last Code_Aster analysis. Finally, one must configure the environment variable ASTER_ROOT (the base path of Aster) in order to be able to launch the file recal.py in Python, or else use the argument --aster_root. The proper operation of the procedure recal.py can be checked manually, by generating an input file with parameter values and by launching the procedure manually. Example on the Code_Aster machine: cd directory export ASTER_ROOT=/aster echo “10., 20., 30. ” >input.txt Python ASTER_ROOT/NEW10/bibpyt/Macro/recal.py etude.export –-info=2 cat ouput.txt The Code_Aster analysis should launch and finish properly. An output.txt file must be generated in the current directory. The test case zzzz159f illustrates the external use of MACR_RECAL: in this Code_Aster test, one defines a function f and one calls Code_Aster once again in order to simulate a recalibration iteration. 7.3 Example: optimisation module of Matlab© If one takes up the principle again and applies it to an optimisation algorithm which would be written in Matlab, one must write two files go.m and fonction.m which carry out the actions described below: Figure 7.3-a : MACR_RECAL “Principle of mode EXTERNE” applied to Matlab© The following example uses the optimisation module of Matlab and carries out the Code_Aster analyses on the local server. File go.m (initialisation and launching of the optimisation) clear all; format long; system('rm -f fort.91'); options = optimset('Display', 'iter', 'LevenbergMarquardt', 'on', 'TolFun', 1e-8, 'MaxFunEvals', 1000, 'MaxIter', 100); % Params : DSDE__, SIGY__, YOUN__ x0 = [:ref: 1000., 30., 100000. ]; lb = [:ref: 500., 5., 50000. ]; ub = [:ref: 10000., 500., 500000. ]; % vecteur [x,resnorm,residual,exitflag,output,lambda,jacobian] = lsqnonlin(@fonction,x0,lb,ub,options) % scalaire %[x,fval,exitflag,output] = fmincon(@fonction,x0,[],[],[],[],lb,ub,[],options) File fonction.m (computation of F(param)) / Linux version function f = fonction(x) system('rm -f input.txt'); system('rm -f output.txt'); % Ecriture des parametres dlmwrite('input.txt', x, 'precision', '%.20f'); % Local iret = system('export ASTER_ROOT=/opt/aster ; Python ASTER_ROOT/NEW10/bibpyt/Macro/recal.py etude.export --objective_type=vector'); f = dlmread('output.txt', ',', 0, 0); % relit un scalaire ou un vecteur In go.m, one gives two examples of algorithms. The algorithm lsqnonlin minimises a vector functional and one must therefore uncomment the first line “iret=”. This algorithm is based on Levenberg–Marquardt with active constraints, and is therefore similar to the one implemented in Code_Aster . Note: It is important to note the presence of the command format long and of the argument precision for the command dlmwrite. This makes it possible to work with a sufficient number of significant digits and not to stop if the tolerance on the function is no longer satisfied. Note 2: When the optimisation software is not capable of handling the return codes of the external execution, one must take care to stop the procedure cleanly in the event of an abnormal stop of the Code_Aster analysis. This is the reason why one deletes the files input.txt and output.txt just after their use, so as not to fall into endless loops.

u4.74.01 Operator MODI_REPERE u4.74.01 Operator MODI_REPERE This operator makes it possible to modify the reference frame in which fields carried by continuum elements and by structural elements (shells, plates, beams, ...) are expressed. The call to MODI_REPERE generally produces a new result concept: RESUOUT = MODI_REPERE(RESULTAT= RESUIN … ) The result concept in output is of the same type as the concept in input. For the changes of reference frame COQUE_INTR_UTIL, COQUE_UTIL_INTR and UTILISATEUR for the beams, it is possible (although not recommended) to use the same result concept in input and in output. In all the other cases, this mode of operation is forbidden. It is strongly recommended not to use the concept produced by MODI_REPERE as input to another analysis command. It is moreover necessary to take care to comply properly with the rules of paragraph §3. 1 Contents

u4.75.01 Macro-command CALC_THERMECA_MULT u4.75.01 Macro-command CALC_THERMECA_MULT Purpose : The macro-command CALC_THERMECA_MULT makes it possible to produce the thermal and linear mechanical results of an arbitrary thermal shock without systematically projecting the fields from a linear mesh onto a quadratic mesh, thanks to the multiplication of a single unit analysis. It implements a methodology for thermo-mechanical analyses in the linear domain. This macro-command produces, as chosen, a concept of type evol_elas or evol_ther . 1 Syntax / evol_elas / evol_ther = CALC_THERMECA_MULT( ◆ TEMP_FIN = float, ◆ TEMP_INIT = float, ◆ RESU_MECA_UNIT = evol_elas, ◆ RESU_SUPL_THER = / "OUI", / "NON", # Si: equal_to('RESU_SUPL_THER', 'OUI') ◆ RESU_THER_UNIT = evol_ther, ◆ RESU_THER = co, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 2 General points The objective of this macro-command is to determine the thermal and mechanical state of a structure following a thermal shock. By using linearity properties, it is possible to determine the solution of an arbitrary shock from an “other” shock, most often a unit shock. This approach has the advantage of computing the finite-element solutions only once for the unit shock, then of generating the solutions for the other shocks. Since linearity properties are used, this operator is valid only for thermo-mechanical analyses in which the thermal analysis and the mechanical analysis are linear. 3 Operands and keywords 3.1 Operand TEMP_FIN TEMP_CIBLE is a real giving the value of the temperature, different from the rest temperature, which creates the thermal shock. Typically, in the case where one studies a pipe periodically and rapidly traversed by a fluid at a non-ambient temperature, TEMP_FIN corresponds to the difference between the temperature of the fluid and the reference temperature TEMP_INIT of the pipe. 3.2 Operand TEMP_INIT This is the reference temperature of the solid under study. In the model of this macro-command, it is also the temperature of the system before the thermal shock. 3.3 Operand RESU_SUPL_THER Operand to be supplied as ‘OUI’ when the user wishes also to produce the linear thermal analysis of the thermal shock under study. The concept is then produced on the right-hand side of the macro-command in the keyword RESU_THER. 3.4 Operands RESU_MECA_UNIT and RESU_THER_UNIT These are the result concepts of the unit analyses, mechanical and thermal respectively. RESU_THER_UNIT is to be supplied only when one asks the macro-command for a thermal result (i.e. RESU_SUPL_THER = ‘OUI’). 3.5 Keyword RESU_THER Contains the result concept produced on the right-hand side by the macro-command when one asks for it. 4 Examples An example of use of the macro-command for an analysis of a thermal shock of 50°C on the surface of a cube of reference temperature 20°C is found in the test case hslv303a.

u4.81.03 Operator CALC_CHAM_ELEM u4.81.03 Operator CALC_CHAM_ELEM 1 Purpose Compute an elementary field at the Gauss points containing the coordinates and the weight of the Gauss points. Compute an elementary field of heat flux and of acoustic pressure, from already computed fields of type cham_no_ . Put into the format of a field at the nodes by element the values of certain material parameters and of certain beam characteristics. 2 Syntax cham_elem = CALC_CHAM_ELEM( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ INST = float, ◇ MODE_FOURIER = int, ◆ OPTION = / "FLUX_ELGA", / "FLUX_ELNO", / "PRAC_ELNO", / "COOR_ELGA", / "ROCH_ELNO", # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'ROCH_ELNO') ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, # Si: not equal_to("OPTION", 'ROCH_ELNO') ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, # Si: is_in("OPTION", ('FLUX_ELNO','FLUX_ELGA',)) ◆ TEMP = cham_no, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, # Si: is_in("OPTION", ('PRAC_ELNO',)) ◆ PRES = cham_no, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands MODELE / CARA_ELEM / CHAM_MATER ♦ MODELE= mo, Name of the model on which the option is computed. ◊ CARA_ELEM= carac, Elementary characteristics associated with the model mo, if it contains structural elements or if the isoparametric elements are assigned a local anisotropy reference frame. Only for the option ROCH_ELNO: ♦ CHAM_MATER= chmat, Material field. Must contain the elastic data and the material POST_ROCHE. 3.2 Selection of the mesh cells concerned by the analysis The keywords TOUT = 'OUI' and GROUP_MA allow the user to choose the mesh cells on which he or she wishes to carry out the elementary post-processing analyses. / TOUT = 'OUI' All the mesh cells (carrying finite elements) will be processed. This is the default value. / GROUP_MA = l_grma Only the mesh cells included in l_grma will be processed. 3.3 Operand INST ◊ INST Value of the time instant making it possible to evaluate possible functions in the material parameters for the computation of the heat flux. 3.4 Thermal options The elementary thermal computation options can be computed from a temperature field: ♦ TEMP= temp For these analyses one needs the material field associated with the model mo: ♦ CHAM_MATER= chmater, The options available are: | 'FLUX_ELGA', | 'FLUX_ELNO', Their meaning is given in U4.81.04. In the case of the modellings AXIS_FOURIER and PLAN_FOURIER, one can specify the harmonic number by the keyword: MODE_FOURIER. 3.5 Acoustic options The elementary acoustic computation options can be computed from a complex pressure field: ♦ PRES= pres The option available is: | 'PRAC_ELNO' Computation of the real and imaginary parts of the pressure field per element at the nodes. 3.6 Option COOR_ELGA Computation of the coordinates and of the weights of the Gauss points of each element. 3.7 Option ROCH_ELNO This option puts into the form of a field at the nodes by element the values of certain material parameters and of certain beam characteristics. The output field has 10 components described in the following table: | Components | Correspondence | | --- | --- | | E | Young's modulus | | K_FACT | Parameter FACTEUR of POST_ROCHE | | N_EXPO | Parameter EXPOSANT of POST_ROCHE | | A | Area of the (circular) beam cross-section | | I | Inertia of the (circular) beam cross-section | | R | Outer radius of the (circular) beam cross-section | | EP | Pipe thickness | | I2 | Value of the inertia at the other node of the same mesh cell | | R2 | Value of the radius at the other node of the same mesh cell | | EP2 | Value of the thickness at the other node of the same mesh cell | This option is used for the specific needs of the macro-command POST_ROCHE. Caution, the parameter E must not be a function. 4 Examples of analyses with CALC_CHAM_ELEM epsno = CALC_CHAM_ELEM ( MODELE= moaxfour, TEMP= temp, CHAM_MATER= chmater, OPTION= 'FLUX_ELNO', MODE_FOURIER= 1, );

Si: is_type("RESULTAT") in (evol_sech,) | SECHAGE = / "DIFF_ELGA", / "DIFF_ELNO", / "DIFF_NOEU", / "FLUX_ELGA", / "FLUX_ELNO", / "FLUX_NOEU", / "GRAT_ELGA", / "GRAT_ELNO", / "GRAT_NOEU", / "HYGR_ELGA", / "HYGR_ELNO", / "HYGR_NOEU", ◆ | CHAM_UTIL = _F( ◆ NOM_CHAM = text, ◆ / FORMULE = list[formule], / CRITERE = / "INVA_2", / "TRACE", / "VMIS", / NORME = / "FROBENIUS", / "L2", ◆ NUME_CHAM_RESU = int, ), ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_ther / char_ther, ◇ / FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, / COEF_MULT = float, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), # Si: is_type("RESULTAT") in (acou_harmo,mode_acou,tran_gene,harm_gene) | ACOUSTIQUE = / "INTE_ELNO", / "INTE_NOEU", / "PRAC_ELNO", / "PRAC_NOEU", / "PRME_ELNO", ◆ | CHAM_UTIL = _F( ◆ NOM_CHAM = text, ◆ / FORMULE = list[formule], / CRITERE = / "INVA_2", / "TRACE", / "VMIS", / NORME = / "FROBENIUS", / "L2", ◆ NUME_CHAM_RESU = int, ), ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◆ CHARGE = char_cine_meca / char_meca, ◇ PHAS_DEG = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ PUIS_PULS = int (défaut: 0), ◇ FONC_MULT_C = fonction_c / formule_c, ◇ COEF_MULT_C = complex, ◇ / FONC_MULT = fonction / formule / nappe, / COEF_MULT = float, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, / 3, ◇ PARALLELISME_TEMPS = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands RESULTAT/MODELE/CHAM_MATER/CARA_ELEM/EXCIT 3.1 Operands RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT= resu Name of the result data structure to be enriched. This argument may be the same as that used for the concept enriched by the operator, or a different name, which will create a new result data structure. Notes In the majority of situations, the data structure resu contains all the information required for the computation of the options: the model, the material field, the elementary characteristics, the loadings. The keywords MODELE, CHAM_MATER, CARA_ELEM and EXCIT are therefore useless; A notable exception, however, concerns the dynamic data structures produced by DYNA_VIBRA, for which the user must himself ensure the consistency of the keywords between the analysis operator and CALC_CHAMP. An alarm warns him of this. 3.2 Operands MODELE / CHAM_MATER / CARA_ELEM. ◊ MODELE= mo Name of the model on which the forces, the stresses, the strains, and so on, are computed. It is optional because it can be extracted from the result. ◊ CHAM_MATER= chmater Material field associated with the model mo. This keyword is optional and must be supplied only in exceptional cases (deliberate modification of the material, for example). ◊ CARA_ELEM= carac Elementary characteristics associated with the model mo if it contains structural elements or if the isoparametric elements are affected by a local anisotropy frame. This keyword is optional because it can be extracted from the result. 3.3 Keyword EXCIT This factor keyword (optional) makes it possible to specify the thermal or mechanical loadings to be used for the computation of the options, in place of those which were used in the analysis of the data structure specified under the keyword RESULTAT. The definition of this keyword is identical to that of the commands which built the data structure resu: see the commands MECA_STATIQUE U4.51.01, STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03, DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. 4 Selection of the mesh cells concerned by the analysis The keywords TOUT and GROUP_MA allow the user to choose the mesh cells on which he wishes to perform his elementary post-processing computations. / TOUT = 'OUI' All the mesh cells (carrying finite elements) will be processed. This is the default value. / GROUP_MA = l_grma Only the mesh cells included in l_grma will be processed. 5 Selection of the order numbers The use of the keywords TOUT_ORDRE, NUM_ORDRE, INST, FREQ is described in the document U4.71.00. In the case where there are many order numbers, it may be more efficient (in memory in particular) to call the command several times on sub-lists of the order numbers. 6 Localisation of the fields In the remainder of the document one will not state explicitly the localisation of the fields. Indeed, the localisation is given in the name of the field (and therefore of the option): - Field by element: x_ELEM - Field at the Gauss points by element: x_ELGA - Field at the nodes by element: x_ELNO - Field at the nodes: x_NOEU The fields are, for the most part, computed natively at the Gauss points ( x_ELGA). The fields at the nodes by element ( x_ELNO) are obtained by extrapolation from the field at the Gauss points (method detailed in R3.06.03). The fields at the nodes ( x_NOEU) are obtained from the fields at the nodes by element by taking a simple arithmetic mean (not weighted by the size of the mesh cells) of the values encountered on the elements at a given node. Note 1 For the computation of the equivalents, the fields at the nodes by element ( x_ELNO) are not obtained by extrapolation from the field at the Gauss points. The extrapolation is done on the stress or strain field and then one computes the equivalent field. Note 2 The averages at the nodes of fields computed in local frames are licit only if the angles between these frames are small. Otherwise, they have no meaning. Note 3 When the keyword GROUP_MA is filled in for the computation of an option x_NOEU, the arithmetic mean is taken over the selected mesh cells. Thus this result is different from that obtained by performing a global computation and then restricting it to the selected mesh cells only. Example: One considers a structure whose shear stress {\sigma}_{xy} is: In the global computation, {\sigma}_{xy} is zero on \mathit{M1}\cap \mathit{M2} as the average of two opposite values. These values are far from being zero, as the computation on \mathit{M1} alone shows. The values on the boundary of the requested domain must therefore be interpreted with care. For the structural elements which have sub-points (plates, shells, multi-fibre beams, pipes), the fields of type x_ELGA and x_ELNO are computed on all the sub-points. In order to obtain a field on a single sub-point (one layer and one level, for example), one must perform an extraction via the operator POST_CHAMP (options EXTR_COQUE, EXTR_PMF and EXTR_TUYAU). Moreover this intermediate operation is indispensable in order to compute a field of type x_NOEU for these structural elements: the fields of type x_NOEU indeed never have a sub-point. Finally the energy-computation options never produce fields with sub-points. Indeed, for the structural elements, the field is integrated through the thickness (integration carried out on the sub-points). 7 Dependence of the fields The computation of a field may require the prior computation of one or more other fields. Thus, for example, in order to compute a field x_NOEU it is necessary to have available the same field by element at the nodes x_ELNO and at the Gauss points x_ELGA. This dependence is resolved by the operator CALC_CHAMP, which automatically carries out the computation of the intermediate fields. It is therefore not necessary for the user to know the dependence tree of the options. Only the fields explicitly requested by the user are saved in the result data structure. 8 Operands for the mechanical options 8.1 Options for the computation of the stresses (Operand CONTRAINTE) The components of the stress fields and of the generalised forces are detailed in the document U2.01.05. | 'EFGE_ELGA' | 'EFGE_ELNO' | 'EFGE_NOEU' Computation of the generalised forces (structural elements). List of the components of the field: | DX DY DZ | Nodal forces | | --- | --- | Additional components for the thermo-hydro-mechanical modellings: | PRE1 PRE2 TEMP | Nodal forces (hydraulic / thermal) | | --- | --- | Additional components for the structural elements: | DRX DRY DRZ | Nodal forces (moments) | | --- | --- | The nodal forces correspond, in the finite-element sense, to the internal forces taking part in the equilibrium equations. The computation of the generalised nodal forces {F}_{K} is done in the following way: \sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}={\int}_{\Omega}\sigma .\epsilon ({\mathrm{v}}_{K})d\Omega =\sum_{K}\underset{K}{\int}{\sigma}^{K}.\epsilon ({\mathrm{v}}_{K})\mathit{dK}=\sum_{K}\underset{K}{\int}{\sigma}^{K}.\mathrm{B}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}\mathit{dK} With: - {\sigma}^{K} stresses at the Gauss points of the element K ; - \mathrm{B} the finite-element operator of generalised strains (matrix relating the first-order strains to the generalised displacements); - {\mathrm{v}}_{K} generalised unit elementary displacement. Hence: {\mathrm{F}}_{K}=\left\lbrace \underset{K}{\int}{}^{t}\mathrm{B}.{\sigma}^{K}\mathit{dK}\right\rbrace The dimension of the nodal forces is dual to that of the {v}_{K} so as to give a work (in joules). For the solid elements (3D, 2D and bars), the FORC_NODA in general have the dimension of a force. It is a field on the nodes of the mesh in which the value at a node is obtained from the stresses computed on the elements meeting at that node; their values therefore vary when the mesh changes. In the absence of a distributed loading, equilibrium imposes that they be zero at an interior node, whereas they correspond to the reaction on the supports where a kinematic relation is imposed (the case of an imposed displacement). Two-dimensional case For the axisymmetric elements, the integration in \theta is done over a sector of 1\mathit{radian} . If one wants the integral of the surface force over the whole disc one must therefore multiply by 2\pi . For the plane-strain elements, the computation is done on a strip of unit width. The computed nodal forces are therefore in fact forces per unit length. If one wants to compute the nodal forces acting on a structure of width l , one must multiply the result in D_PLAN by l , except that the plane-strain assumption is not valid near the two faces. One will therefore have an approximate result. Case of the structural elements For the beam elements and the discrete elements, the stresses at the Gauss points are in fact the generalised nodal forces in the frame of the element (obtained by the product of the stiffness matrix of the element by the displacement and taking into account the forces of thermal origin and the distributed forces). The computation of the nodal forces is done by projecting the nodal forces contained in the field of symbolic name 'SIEF_ELGA' into the global frame. The summation above over the elements is then applied. The components DX, DY and DZ give the forces and DRX, DRY and DRZ the moments. In the case of the shells, the components DX, DY and DZ give the FORC_NODA (of the dimension of a force) in the global frame of the mesh. These components are built with the normal and shear forces in the shell. The components DRX, DRY and DRZ give the FORC_NODA (of the dimension of a moment) in the global frame of the mesh, built with the bending moments in the shell. In the case of homogenised shell constitutive behaviours of type ELAS_COQUE, it is preferable to look at EFGE_NOEU. Case of thermo-hydro-mechanics (THM) In thermo-hydro-mechanics, cf. §8, R7.01.10, the generalised nodal forces associated with each component correspond to the mechanical forces and to the fluxes. If one denotes by {Q}^{T}{\sigma}_{0} the result of FORC_NODA, for the hydraulic equations, then for a time step \Delta t , one has: \int_\Omega Q^T\sigma_0\cdot p^ d\Omega =-\int_\Omega \Delta m p^ d\Omega + \Delta t\int_\Omega M^+\cdot \nabla {p}^ d\Omega. The fluxes are taken at the time instant t^+=t^-+\Delta t . If one denotes by q the thermal flux, Q the heat supply, M_w , M_{vp} , M_{as} and M_{ad} the hydraulic fluxes of liquid water, of vapour, of dry air (or any other component) and of dissolved air, and by m_w , m_{vp} , m_{as} and m_{ad} their respective mass supply R7.01.10, then the expression of FORC_NODA is the following: - with the degree of freedom PRE1 is associated the water flux -\int_\Omega (\Delta m_w + \Delta m_{vp}) p^ d\Omega +\Delta t\int_\Omega (M_w^++{M}_{vp}^+)\cdot\nabla {p}^ d\Omega - with the degree of freedom PRE2 is associated the flux of the gaseous component -\int_\Omega (\Delta m_{as} + \Delta m_{ad}) p^ d\Omega+\Delta t\int_\Omega(M_{as}^++M_{ad}^+)\cdot\nabla {p}^ d\Omega - with the degree of freedom TEMP is associated the thermal flux -\int_\Omega \Delta Q T^ d\Omega+\Delta t\int_\Omega q^+\cdot \nabla {T}^{ }d\Omega | 'REAC_NODA' Computation of the generalised nodal reaction forces at the nodes, from the stresses at the Gauss points and the loadings. List of the components of the field: | DX DY DZ | Nodal reactions | | --- | --- | | Additional components for the structural elements: | | | DRX DRY DRZ | Nodal reactions (moments) | The generalised nodal reactions correspond, in the finite-element sense, to the forces exerted on the supports (boundary conditions) taking part in the equilibrium equations. Case of statics In statics, for the result concepts of type evol_elas, mult_elas, fourier_elas or evol_noli, the computation of the generalised nodal reactions {R}_{K} is done by: \sum_{K}{\mathrm{R}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}=\sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}-\mathrm{L}({\mathrm{v}}_{K}) With: - \sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K} the expression of the nodal forces (option FORC_NODA, see () and ()); - {v}_{K} generalised unit elementary displacement. And one therefore has: L({v}_{K})=\underset{\Omega}{\int}f\cdot {v}_{K}d\Omega +\underset{\Gamma}{\int}{F}_{s}\cdot {v}_{K}d\Gamma +\sum_{i}{F}_{i}\cdot {{v}_{K}}_{i} With: - f are the body forces; - {F}_{s} the generalised surface forces; - {F}_{i} the generalised point forces at the node i . The vector of the generalised nodal reactions on the element K is therefore obtained from the generalised nodal forces: {\mathrm{R}}_{K}={\mathrm{F}}_{K}-\underset{K}{\int}\mathrm{f}\mathit{dK}-\underset{\partial K}{\int}\mathrm{F}\partial K-\sum_{i}{{\mathrm{F}}_{i}}_{K} in other words, one subtracts from the nodal forces the generalised external forces applied to the element K . Note It is to be noted that the temperature loading does not appear in the external forces: it enters the expression of the stresses via the constitutive law. Case of non-linear transient dynamics For the result concepts of type evol_noli coming from non-linear transient dynamic analyses, in order to obtain the nodal reactions, one must in addition remove the inertia forces (acceleration) and the damping forces linked to the velocity: \sum_{K}{\mathrm{R}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}=\sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}+(\mathrm{M}\ddot{\mathrm{u}})\cdot {\mathrm{v}}_{K}-\mathrm{L}({\mathrm{v}}_{K}) Where: - \sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K} the expression of the nodal forces (option FORC_NODA, see () and ()); - {v}_{K} generalised unit elementary displacement. - M is the mass matrix; - \ddot{u} the generalised acceleration field; - L the vector of the applied generalised external forces (equation ()). Notes The contributions of the damping linked directly to the velocity on the nodal reactions are neglected; The computation of the inertia forces requires the presence of the acceleration field ACCE in the data structure resultat. In the case of a structure of type evol_noli, it is not possible for the code to check its presence; one must therefore take care. Case of modal dynamics For the result concepts of type mode_meca (coming from modal analyses) the formula is: \sum_{K}{R}_{K}.{v}_{K}=\underset{\Omega}{\int}\sigma (\varepsilon (u)).\varepsilon ({v}_{K})d\Omega -{\omega}^{2}(M\cdot u)\cdot {v}_{K} Where: - \sigma (\varepsilon (u)) are the generalised modal stresses; - M is the mass matrix; - \omega the eigen angular frequency; - u the generalised displacement field of the mode; - {v}_{K} generalised unit elementary displacement. Case of linear transient dynamics For the result concepts of type dyna_trans coming from linear transient dynamic analyses (DYNA_VIBRA/TYPE_CALCUL='TRAN') or of type dyna_harmo coming from harmonic analyses (DYNA_VIBRA/TYPE_CALCUL='HARM') the expression of the generalised nodal reactions is obtained by: \sum_{K}{\mathrm{R}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}=\sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K}+(\mathrm{M}\ddot{\mathrm{u}})\cdot {\mathrm{v}}_{K}-\mathrm{L}({\mathrm{v}}_{K}) Where: - \sum_{K}{\mathrm{F}}_{K}.{\mathrm{v}}_{K} the expression of the nodal forces (option FORC_NODA, see () and ()); - {v}_{K} generalised unit elementary displacement. - M is the mass matrix; - \ddot{u} the generalised acceleration field; - L the vector of the applied generalised external forces (equation ()). Use of GROUP_MA in FORC_NODA and REAC_NODA If the keyword GROUP_MA is filled in, {F}_{K} (option FORC_NODA) is computed only on the requested elements and then assembled. The result is different from a global computation over the whole domain then reduced to the requested elements. The implemented method makes it possible to measure the reaction of one piece of the model on another. Caution! The computation of 'REAC_NODA' on a subset of the model (via the keyword GROUP_MA) must be done with care. Example 4 below illustrates this type of computation. For results of type dyna_harmo, 'REAC_NODA' is computed only on the model as a whole. The computation on a subset of the model can be carried out manually by performing a computation of 'FORC_NODA' on the mesh-cell group in question and then subtracting the external force from the results obtained. Notes The nodal reactions are zero at every interior point of the model and are not zero a priori at a point of the boundary subjected to a kinematic boundary condition (or to contact forces); Neglecting the contribution of the damping in dynamics may create a slight discrepancy with respect to the exact result; Only the resultant of the forces or of the nodal reactions on a node group has a physical meaning (this group must correspond to at least one element of the model, for example a boundary subjected to a boundary condition). It may be computed with POST_RELEVE_T [U4.81.21]. Locally, the field FORC_NODA or REAC_NODA must not be interpreted, because the value at a node is directly linked to the fineness of the mesh. Moreover the sign of these forces on the nodes of one and the same element may be counter-intuitive, whereas it is perfectly in agreement with the theory of finite elements (for example on QUAD8 mesh cells located at the interface of a zone in pure compression, the signs of the nodal forces at the vertices and at the mid-sides are opposite); The computation of REAC_NODA takes into account the distributed loadings on the beams. As soon as one varies this loading over a non-linear analysis (change of EXCIT from one time step to the next), the computation of REAC_NODA is forbidden. It is necessary to divide one's post-processing into «batches» of order numbers, for which the loading is constant (that is, it uses the same AFFE_CHAR_MECA concept in EXCIT). Some loadings are not taken into account during the computation of this option; they are: INTE_ELEC, FORCE_SOL and RELA_CINE_BP. Case of the HHO modellings In the case of the HHO modellings, the fields FORC_NODA and REAC_NODA are not forces but stresses. Moreover, this field is not defined at the nodes and is continuous. 12.2 Example 1: structure loaded with a nodal force (2 QUAD4 elements) In this example, the reactions at the nodes (2) are indeed equal to the nodal forces (1) minus the loading. They represent the reactions at the supports of the structure. If one restricts the computation to the mesh cell \mathit{M1} , the forces (3) at the nodes belonging to the boundary between \mathit{M1} and \mathit{M2} are different. They represent the reaction of the model formed by \mathit{M1} on the model formed by \mathit{M2} . It is to be noted that the nodal loading is divided by two because the two mesh cells contribute to it. The nodal reactions (4) are again equal to the nodal forces minus the loading. On the computation restricted to the mesh cell \mathit{M2} , the nodal forces (5) along \mathit{OX} are of opposite sign to the computation restricted to the mesh cell \mathit{M1} , illustrating the principle of action and reaction. 12.3 Example 2: structure with a temperature loading Data: > E={1.10}^{9}\text{Pa} > \nu =0.3 > \alpha ={1.10}^{-6} Results: > {F}_{y}=-{3.410}^{4}N > {F}_{\mathrm{1x}}=7.8{10}^{3}N > {F}_{\mathrm{2x}}=-1.2{10}^{3}N In this example, the nodal forces and the nodal reactions coincide because the only loading is a temperature loading. If one restricts the computation to the mesh cell \mathit{M2} , the forces along \mathit{OY} remain the same but are different along \mathit{OX} . 12.4 Example 3: structure under distributed loading (beam) One considers a structure of beam type, clamped and subjected to a gravity loading on its upper half. There may be several occurrences of CHAM_UTIL in order to chain the computation of several fields. The processing being carried out at the end of the command CALC_CHAMP, the fields computed by the preceding keywords (CONTRAINTE, DEFORMATION...) are available here. Either one requests the computation of a predefined criterion, or one applies one or more formulae in order to compute another field. 13.1 Operand NOM_CHAM This is the field from which one performs the computations. The field produced will have the same type: ELGA, ELNO or NOEU. 13.2 Operand CRITERE Requests the computation of a predefined criterion. The criteria are (paragraph 2.6.5 provides the expressions of each criterion): - VMIS (for the stress fields), - INVA_2 (for the strain fields), - TRACE (for the stress or strain fields). Each of these criteria produces one component (named X1). One of the advantages is to be able to compute INVA_2 of any strain field. 13.3 Operand FORMULE This makes it possible to compute any expression as a function of the components of the field supplied for NOM_CHAM. The field produced will contain as many components as formulae supplied: the component X1 will correspond to the first formula, X2 to the second, and so on. Up to 30 components may thus be created. The output field is systematically extended by zero on the other components and where the input field is not defined. Examples of formulae making it possible to recover the criteria VMIS and INVA_2 can be found in the second part of the test sslv104a. 13.4 Operand NORME Requests the computation of a predefined norm. The norms are: - L2: norm {L}_{2} of a tensor - FROBENIUS: Frobenius norm of a tensor The computed norm is a quantity integrated (in the weak sense) over an element {\Omega}_{e} . For a tensor A , the {L}_{2} norm is: {N}_{{L}_{2}}={\int}_{{\Omega}_{e}}\sqrt{(A:A)}.d{\Omega}_{e} The Frobenius norm on the components {A}_{ij} of a tensor A : {N}_{F}={\int}_{{\Omega}_{e}}{\sum}_{i,j}∣{A}_{ij}∣.∣{A}_{ij}∣.d{\Omega}_{e} Each of these norms produces one component (named X1) on an element. It is therefore an ELEM field. It is to be noted that the difference between the two norms comes from the cross terms (off-diagonal). 13.5 Operand NUME_CHAM_RESU The field produced must be stored, in a unique way, in the result concept. By default, when MPI parallelism is activated 1 (cf. U2.08.06), the computation options generally benefit here from a so-called «in space» parallelism . That is, the computations are distributed over the parallel processes by batches of mesh cells. An MPI process will handle, for all the time steps, the elementary computations required by a given mesh-cell group. But, besides the fact that this parallelism is not very efficient for the options involving directly few or no elementary computations (such as the options REAC/FORC_NODA and xxx_NOEU), it also gives rise to large and repeated MPI communications 2. For the options mentioned above, one therefore prefers the so-called «in time» parallelism , which, for its part, distributes, for all the mesh cells, the computations (elementary or not) required by a batch of time steps. The communications are therefore less costly 3 and the parallelism is extended to portions of code beyond the elementary computations. With this parallelism, the speed-ups may range from X5 to X50 depending on the configuration of the analyses. The activation of this parallelism is carried out in a given CALC_CHAMP 4 and it concerns all the computation options liable to benefit from it: REAC/FORC_NODA and xxx_NOEU and all the underlying computation options 5. On a costly CALC_CHAMP, comprising REAC/FORC_NODA or xxx_NOEU computations on long transients and/or on large models, one therefore advises activating this parallelism in time: PARALLELISME_TEMPS='OUI'. And, unlike the one in space, it does not need a minimum granularity 6 in order to be effective. From about ten time steps per MPI process, the speed-up provided by the parallelism in time may be significant 7 . The type of active parallelism (in space, in time or none) is stated, option by option, in the message file. For more details one may consult the user's guide of parallelism U2.08.06. CALC_CHAMP(EFGE_ELGA, REAC_NODA, ETOT_ELGA, EPSI_NOEU, PARALLELISME_TEMPS='OUI') CALC_CHAMP(EFGE_ELGA, ETOT_ELGA) CALC_CHAMP(REAC_NODA, EPSI_NOEU, PARALLELISME_TEMPS='OUI') Notes on parallelism The parallelism in time, when it is activated in the operator, concerns all the data-processing treatments liable to benefit from it. To this end, one «switches off», behind the scenes and locally, option by option, the parallelism in space. The latter is then reactivated, «as if nothing had happened», in the following options if those are not, in their turn, concerned by the parallelism in time. Thus the call will activate the parallelism in space for options no. 1 and no. 3 and that in time for the others. It is equivalent, from the point of view of parallelism, to the sequence of calls: In order to simplify the programming 8 and not to look needlessly for minor gains, when the number of time steps is not a multiple of the number of MPI processes, the remainder of the time steps is carried out by all the processes. And of course, no communication is organised between them. In certain situations, the parallelism in time does not work. Depending on the case, the analysis stops or issues an alarm: option not yet covered (CHAM_UTIL), analysis context varying during the transient (MODELE...), analysis impossible in sequential mode, not enough time steps... MPI version of the code + Astk menu Options/mpi_nbcpu>1. On all the components of the field and at each time step. On vectors only and every mpi_nbcpu time steps. It is therefore no longer active in a following CALC_CHAMP. If necessary, it will have to be reactivated. Called if necessary, behind the scenes, by these computation options. A few tens of thousands of degrees of freedom per MPI process for the parallelism in space. Obviously, all the more so as the unit computation of a time step is costly. Hence the maintenance and the capacity for evolution of the operator.

points When an sd_resultat (resu) contains fields «with sub-points» (the case of multi-layer shells, of pipe elements or of multi-fibre beam elements), the command POST_CHAMP makes it possible to create another sd_resultat (resu2) which will contain the restriction of the fields with sub-points to a single sub-point. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = resu Name of a result concept of type resultat. 4.2 Selection of the order numbers The use of the keywords TOUT_ORDRE, NUME_ORDRE, INST, ... is described in the document U4.71.00. 4.3 Selection of the elements concerned By means of the keywords TOUT='OUI', and GROUP_MA, the user can select the elements on which the computations will take place. Note : if the user selects elements which are not structural elements, they are ignored. 4.4 Keyword EXTR_COQUE This keyword is used to extract a field on a single sub-point for shell elements. 4.4.1 Operand NOM_CHAM The keyword NOM_CHAM makes it possible to designate the fields to be extracted in the result resu. The following are permitted: | SIGM_ELGA | SIGM_ELNO | SIEQ_ELGA | SIEQ_ELNO | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | EPSI_ELGA | EPSI_ELNO | EPEQ_ELGA | EPEQ_ELNO | | SIEF_ELGA | SIEF_ELNO | VARI_ELGA | VARI_ELNO | 4.4.2 Operand NUME_COUCHE > ♦ NUME_COUCHE = nucou, [I] Number of the layer containing the sub-point to be extracted. By convention, layer 1 is the lower layer (in the direction of the normal) of the shell elements. 4.4.3 Operand NIVE_COUCHE > ♦ NIVE_COUCHE= For the layer nucou defined by NUME_COUCHE, makes it possible to specify the ordinate of the sub-point: | 'INF' | lower ordinate of the layer | (inner skin), | | --- | --- | --- | | 'SUP' | upper ordinate of the layer | (outer skin), | | 'MOY' | mean ordinate of the layer | (middle surface). | 4.5 Keyword EXTR_TUYAU This keyword is used to extract a field on a single sub-point for pipe elements. 4.5.1 Operand NOM_CHAM The keyword NOM_CHAM makes it possible to designate the fields to be extracted in the result resu. The following are permitted: (see 4.4.1 ) 4.5.2 Operand NUME_COUCHE > ♦ NUME_COUCHE = nucou, [I] Number of the layer containing the sub-point to be extracted. By convention, layer 1 is the inner layer of a TUYAU element. 4.5.3 Operand NIVE_COUCHE > ♦ NIVE_COUCHE= For the layer nucou defined by NUME_COUCHE, makes it possible to specify the ordinate of the sub-point: | 'INF' | lower ordinate of the layer | (inner skin), | | --- | --- | --- | | 'SUP' | upper ordinate of the layer | (outer skin), | | 'MOY' | mean ordinate of the layer | (middle surface). | 4.5.4 Operand ANGLE ♦ ANGLE = delta, [I] delta: angle in degrees (integer value), counted from the position of the generatrix of the pipe element. Note : The sub-points of the pipes are spaced regularly through the thickness of the pipe and also in azimuth. When the user indicates an angle which does not correspond geometrically to a sub-point (in azimuth), a linear interpolation is performed between the 2 sub-points which «bracket» the specified angle. 4.6 Keyword EXTR_PMF This keyword is used to extract a field on a single sub-point for multi-fibre beam elements. 4.6.1 Operand NOM_CHAM The keyword NOM_CHAM makes it possible to designate the fields to be extracted in the result resu. The following are permitted: (see 4.4.1 ) 4.6.2 Operand NUME_FIBRE > ♦ NUME_FIBRE = nufib, [I] Number of the fibre corresponding to the sub-point to be extracted. 4.7 Keyword MIN_MAX_SP This keyword is used to compute the «maximum» (or minimum) value of a component of a field. The «max» is taken over all the sub-points. If the input field is for example an ELGA stress field on the sub-points of a multi-layer shell, the output field will be an ELGA field (without sub-points) containing, for each Gauss point, the «max» value of the stress. In addition to the «max» value, one also extracts the information making it possible to locate the sub-point which has reached the «max». In the end, on each «point», one computes 6 components: | VAL | The value of the «max» | | --- | --- | | NUCOU | Number of the layer if the element is a multi-layer shell or a pipe | | NUSECT | Number of the angular sector if the element is a pipe | | NUFIBR | Number of the fibre if the element is a multi-fibre beam | | POSIC | «Position» in the layer: -1. : position «INF» 0. : position «MOY» +1. : position «SUP» | | POSIS | «Position» in the sector: -1. : «start» of the sector (in the direction of increasing azimuths) 0. : «middle» of the sector (in the direction of increasing azimuths) +1. : «end» of the sector (in the direction of increasing azimuths) | 4.7.1 Operand NOM_CHAM The keyword NOM_CHAM makes it possible to designate the field to be extracted in the result resu. The following are permitted: (see 4.4.1 ) 4.7.2 Operands NOM_CMP/NOM_VARI > ◊ NOM_CMP = nocmp, [Kn] > Name of the component for which one wishes to compute the «max». > ◊ NOM_VARI= novari, [Kn] For the fields of internal variables (VARI_ ), one may give the name of the internal variable for which one wishes to compute the «max» (see U4.51.11 for the naming rules of the internal variables). 4.7.3 Operand TYPE_MAXI This keyword is used to choose the «type» of maximum sought: | 'MAXI' | One extracts the maximum value of the component taking its sign into account | | --- | --- | | 'MINI' | One extracts the minimum value of the component taking its sign into account | | 'MAXI_ABS' | One extracts the maximum value of the absolute value of the component | | 'MINI_ABS' | One extracts the minimum value of the absolute value of the component | 4.7.4 Operand NUME_CHAM_RESU > ♦ NUME_CHAM_RESU = nuch, [I] The number nuch is used to name the field produced. If, for example, NOM_CHAM = 'SIEF_ELGA' and NUME_CHAM_RESU = 7, in the result data structure produced, the field will be accessible by NOM_CHAM = 'UT07_ELGA'. It is the 7th ELGA «user» field in the data structure. Note: nuch is limited to 20. 4.8 Keyword COQU_EXCENT This keyword is used to modify the «plane» of computation of the generalised forces in the offset plates. The field found under the name NOM_CHAM in the input sd_resultat (resu) contains forces computed in the «plane» of the mesh. Account is taken of the offset of the elements in order to modify the computation of the moments (they are computed in the mean «plane» of the offset plate). 4.8.1 Operand NOM_CHAM The keyword NOM_CHAM makes it possible to designate the field to be extracted in the result resu. The following are permitted: 'EFGE_ELNO' and 'EFGE_ELGA'. 4.8.2 Operand MODI_PLAN = 'OUI' This keyword is used to confirm that one wishes to modify the «plane» of computation for the forces in the offset plates. 5 Examples 5.1 Extraction of the stresses on 1 sub-point for pipe elements U2 = POST_CHAMP(RESULTAT = U1, TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', TOUT = 'OUI', EXTR_TUYAU =_F(NOM_CHAM = 'SIGM_ELGA', > NUME_COUCHE = 3, NIVE_COUCHE = 'SUP', ANGLE = 90 ),); 5.2 Extraction of the maximum (and minimum) Von Mises stress for pipe elements U2 = POST_CHAMP(RESULTAT = U1, TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', GROUP_MA = 'TUYAU', MIN_MAX_SP =( _F(NOM_CHAM = 'SIEQ_ELGA', NOM_CMP='VMIS', > TYPE_MAXI = 'MAXI', NUME_CHAM_RESU=1), _F(NOM_CHAM = 'SIEQ_ELGA', NOM_CMP='VMIS', > TYPE_MAXI = 'MINI', NUME_CHAM_RESU=2), ));
