u4.81.07 Operator POST_ERREUR u4.81.07 Operator POST_ERREUR 1 Purpose Compute the relative error between a solution obtained by a finite-element analysis and a reference analytical solution in terms of a given norm, with the aim of assessing the convergence of the finite elements. The norms currently available are: - the energy norm, - the {L}^{2} norm of the displacement, - the {L}^{2} norm of the contact pressure. The concept returned is a table. 2 Syntax table = POST_ERREUR( ◆ OPTION = / "DEPL_RELA", / "ENER_RELA", / "LAGR_RELA", ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'DEPL_RELA') ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ CHAM_GD = cham_no, ◇ DX = formule, ◇ DY = formule, ◇ DZ = formule, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'ENER_RELA') ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ DEFORMATION = "PETIT" (ou non renseigné), ◆ CHAM_GD = cham_elem, ◇ SIXX = formule, ◇ SIYY = formule, ◇ SIZZ = formule, ◇ SIXY = formule, ◇ SIXZ = formule, ◇ SIYZ = formule, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'LAGR_RELA') ◆ CHAM_GD = cham_no, ◇ LAGS_C = formule, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 General operands 3.1.1 Keyword OPTION > This keyword makes it possible to determine the type of norm to be used: - 'ENER_RELA' for the energy norm (FEM and X-FEM). - 'DEPL_RELA' for the {L}^{2} norm of the displacement (FEM and X-FEM). - 'LAGR_RELA' for the {L}^{2} norm of the contact pressure (FEM only). This keyword also determines the type of field corresponding to the keyword CHAM_GD: - the stress field at the Gauss points in the case OPTION='ENER_RELA'. - The displacement field at the nodes in the cases OPTION='DEPL_RELA' and OPTION='LAGR_RELA'. 3.1.2 Operand MODELE Name of the model on which the option is computed. It must be the same model as the one which was used to carry out the mechanical analysis from which the field given by the keyword CHAM_GD comes. 3.1.3 Operand GROUP_MA The operand GROUP_MA makes it possible to specify the mesh-cell groups for which the computations of energy or of {L}^{2} norms will be carried out. 3.2 Operands for OPTION = 'ENER_RELA' The option 'ENER_RELA' makes it possible to estimate the difference between the stress field obtained by the finite-element analysis {\sigma}_{h} and the reference stress field \sigma . For each mesh-cell group of the list given by the operand GROUP_MA, the macro-command POST_ERREUR computes: - The elastic energy of the difference field {\sigma}_{h}-\sigma \frac{1}{2}{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}({\sigma}_{h}-\sigma ):{D}^{-1}:({\sigma}_{h}-\sigma )\mathit{dV} , where {\Omega}_{i} is the domain obtained by concatenating all the mesh cells of the mesh-cell group under consideration and D is the Hooke tensor. - The elastic energy of the reference stress field \sigma \frac{1}{2}{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}\sigma :{D}^{-1}:\sigma \mathit{dV} . Finally, the relative error in terms of the energy norm is obtained by: e=\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i}\frac{1}{2}{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}({\sigma}_{h}-\sigma ):{D}^{-1}:({\sigma}_{h}-\sigma )\mathit{dV}}{\sum_{i}\frac{1}{2}{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}\sigma :{D}^{-1}:\sigma \mathit{dV}}} , where the sum is taken over all the mesh-cell groups. 3.2.1 Operand CHAM_GD The stress field {\sigma}_{h} extracted from a finite-element analysis result. 3.2.2 Operand CHAM_MATER Name of the material field to be used for the energy computations. It is recommended that it be the same model as the one which was used to carry out the mechanical analysis from which the field given by the keyword CHAM_GD comes. 3.2.3 Operand DEFORMATION This keyword makes it possible to define the assumptions used for the computation of the strains (cf. U4.51.11, §4.5). The only permitted value is 'PETIT', which corresponds to small displacements and small strains. 3.2.4 Operands SIXX, SIYY, SIZZ, SIXY, SIXZ and SIYZ These keywords make it possible to define the components of the reference stress field \sigma in the form of formula objects. These operands are optional because all the components which are not specified are set to zero. The value of each keyword is a list of formulae to be matched with the list of mesh-cell groups specified by the operand GROUP_MA. A frequent source of error is not to fill in SIZZ for a plane problem, forgetting that, in the general case ( i.e. non-zero Poisson's ratio), the component {\sigma}_{zz} of the stress tensor \sigma is zero only in the case of plane stresses (C_PLAN). 3.2.5 Example Computation of the error in terms of the energy norm for a crack opening in pure mode I, for a plane problem. It is to be noted that the component {\sigma}_{zz} is zero for this problem and is therefore not specified. # extraction du champ de contraintes de la structure de données résultat Scal=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='ELGA_SIEF_R', RESULTAT=UTOT, NOM_CHAM='SIEF_ELGA', NUME_ORDRE=1) # calcul de l'erreur en termes de la norme en énergie tabNRJ=POST_ERREUR(OPTION='ENER_RELA', CHAM_GD=Scal, MODELE=MODELK, DEFORMATION='PETIT', CHAM_MATER=CHMA, GROUP_MA='SURF', SIXX=SXX, SIYY=SYY, SIXY=SXY, ) ) 3.2.6 Table produced > The table produced contains, for each mesh cell of the mesh-cell group, the energy of the difference field {\sigma}_{h}-\sigma and the energy of the reference field \sigma . It also contains the sum over all the mesh-cell groups of the energy of the difference field {\sigma}_{h}-\sigma , the sum over all the mesh-cell groups of the energy of the reference field \sigma and the relative error in terms of the energy norm. | GROUP_MA | DIFFERENCE | REFERENCE | ERREUR RELATIVE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SURF | 1.53608E-09 | 3.50518E-06 | | | TOTAL | 1.53608E-09 | 3.50518E-06 | 2.09340E-02 | 3.3 Operands for OPTION = 'DEPL_RELA' The option 'DEPL_RELA' makes it possible to estimate the difference between the displacement field obtained by the finite-element analysis {u}_{h} and the reference displacement field u . For each mesh-cell group of the list given by the operand GROUP_MA, the macro-command POST_ERREUR computes: - The {L}^{2} norm of the difference field {u}_{h}-u \sqrt{{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}{\parallel {u}_{h}-u\parallel }^{2}\mathit{dV}} , where {\Omega}_{i} is the domain obtained by concatenating all the mesh cells of the mesh-cell group under consideration. - The {L}^{2} norm of the reference displacement field u \sqrt{{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}{\parallel u\parallel }^{2}\mathit{dV}} . Finally, the relative error in terms of the {L}^{2} norm of the displacement is obtained by: e=\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i}{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}{\parallel {u}_{h}-u\parallel }^{2}\mathit{dV}}{\sum_{i}{\int}_{{\Omega}_{i}}{\parallel u\parallel }^{2}\mathit{dV}}} , where the sum is taken over all the mesh-cell groups. 3.3.1 Operand CHAM_GD The displacement field {u}_{h} extracted from a finite-element analysis result. 3.3.2 Operands DX, DY and DZ These keywords make it possible to define the components of the reference displacement field u in the form of formula objects. These operands are optional because all the components which are not specified are set to zero. The value of each keyword is a list of formulae to be matched with the list of mesh-cell groups specified by the operand GROUP_MA. 3.3.3 Example Computation of the error in terms of the {L}^{2} norm of the displacement for a crack opening in pure mode I, for a plane problem. # extraction du champ de déplacements de la structure de données résultat Ucal=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', RESULTAT=UTOT, NOM_CHAM='DEPL', NUME_ORDRE=1) # calcul de l'erreur en termes de la norme L2 du déplacement tabL2=POST_ERREUR(OPTION='DEPL_RELA', CHAM_GD=Ucal, MODELE=MODELK, GROUP_MA='SURF', DX=U1, DY=U2) 3.3.4 Table produced > The table produced contains, for each mesh cell of the mesh-cell group, the {L}^{2} norm of the difference field {u}_{h}-u and the {L}^{2} norm of the reference field u . It also contains the sum over all the mesh-cell groups of the {L}^{2} norm of the difference field {u}_{h}-u , the sum over all the mesh-cell groups of the {L}^{2} norm of the reference field u and the relative error in terms of the {L}^{2} norm of the displacement. | GROUP_MA | DIFFERENCE | REFERENCE | ERREUR RELATIVE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SURF | 1.14688E-09 | 7.60569E-06 | | | TOTAL | 1.14688E-09 | 7.60569E-06 | 1.50793E-04 | 3.4 Operands for OPTION = 'LAGR_RELA' The option 'DEPL_RELA' makes it possible to estimate the difference between the contact pressure obtained by the finite-element analysis {\lambda}_{h} and the reference pressure field \lambda . For each mesh-cell group of the list given by the operand GROUP_MA, the macro-command POST_ERREUR computes: - The {L}^{2} norm of the difference field {\lambda}_{h}-\lambda \sqrt{{\int}_{{\Gamma}_{i}}{({\lambda}_{h}-\lambda )}^{2}\mathit{dS}} , where {\Gamma}_{i} is the domain obtained by concatenating all the mesh cells of the mesh-cell group under consideration. - The {L}^{2} norm of the reference displacement field \lambda \sqrt{{\int}_{{\Gamma}_{i}}{\lambda}^{2}\mathit{dS}} . Finally, the relative error in terms of the {L}^{2} norm of the contact pressure is obtained by: e=\sqrt{\frac{\sum_{i}{\int}_{{\Gamma}_{i}}{({\lambda}_{h}-\lambda )}^{2}\mathit{dS}}{\sum_{i}{\int}_{{\Gamma}_{i}}{\lambda}^{2}\mathit{dS}}} , where the sum is taken over all the mesh-cell groups. 3.4.1 Operand CHAM_GD The contact-pressure field {\lambda}_{h} extracted from a finite-element analysis result. 3.4.2 Operand LAGS_C This keyword makes it possible to define the reference contact pressure \lambda in the form of a formula object. The value of the keyword is a list of formulae to be matched with the list of mesh-cell groups specified by the operand GROUP_MA. 3.4.3 Example Computation of the error in terms of the {L}^{2} norm of the pressure for the case of the inclusion of two crowns. # définition de la pression de contact analytique PRES=FORMULE(NOM_PARA=('X','Y'),VALE='-pres_cont EXP(0.1)') # extraction du champ de déplacements de la structure de données résultat Ucal=CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='EXTR', TYPE_CHAM='NOEU_DEPL_R', RESULTAT=RESU1, NOM_CHAM='DEPL', NUME_ORDRE=1) # calcul de l'erreur en termes de la norme L2 de la pression de contact tabL2=POST_ERREUR(OPTION='LAGR_RELA', CHAM_GD=Ucal, MODELE=MO, GROUP_MA='S2R2', LAGS_C=PRES) 3.4.4 Table produced > The table produced contains, for each mesh cell of the mesh-cell group, the {L}^{2} norm of the difference field {\lambda}_{h}-\lambda and the {L}^{2} norm of the reference field \lambda . It also contains the sum over all the mesh-cell groups of the {L}^{2} norm of the difference field {\lambda}_{h}-\lambda , the sum over all the mesh-cell groups of the {L}^{2} norm of the reference field \lambda and the relative error in terms of the {L}^{2} norm of the contact pressure. | GROUP_MA | DIFFERENCE | REFERENCE | ERREUR RELATIVE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | S2R2 | 1.24905E+03 | 1.79688E+05 | | | TOTAL | 1.24905E+03 | 1.79688E+05 | 6.95124E-03 |

u4.81.08 Operator POST_BEREMIN u4.81.08 Operator POST_BEREMIN 1 Purpose The purpose of this command is to compute, in post-processing of a non-linear elastoplastic mechanical analysis: - the Weibull stress and the probability of cleavage coming from the Beremin model. - the surface density of Weibull stress coming from the industrial version of the Beremin model. This command returns a table and a MED file (optional). The macro-command works in D_PLAN, C_PLAN, AXIS or in 3D. The Beremin model and its industrial version are described in more detail in the reference documentation R7.02.04. Advice on the use of this model is given in the documentation U2.05.08. A test case of the use of POST_BEREMIN is available in V1.01.163. 2 Syntax / table = POST_BEREMIN( ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli, ◆ DEFORMATION = / "GDEF_LOG", / "PETIT", / "PETIT_REAC", ◆ FILTRE_SIGM = / "SIGM_CORR", / "SIGM_ELGA", / "SIGM_ELMOY", ◇ NUME_VARI = int (défaut: 0), # Si: equal_to("DEFORMATION", 'GDEF_LOG') ◆ LIST_NUME_SIEF = list[int], ◇ HIST_MAXI = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ SIGM_MAXI = co, ◇ COEF_MULT = float (défaut: 1.0), # Si: equal_to("FILTRE_SIGM", 'SIGM_CORR') ◆ SIGM_CORR = evol_noli, ◆ / WEIBULL = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ M = list[float], ◆ VOLU_REFE = float, ◇ SIGM_REFE = list[float] (défaut: 0.0), ◇ SIGM_SEUIL = list[float] (défaut: 0.0), ◇ TYPE_SEUIL = / "REDUIT" (par défaut), / "RESTREINT", ), / WEIBULL_FO = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ M = list[float], ◆ VOLU_REFE = float, ◇ SIGM_CNV = float (défaut: 0.0), ◇ SIGM_REFE = cham_elem / cham_no / fonction, ◇ SIGM_SEUIL = cham_elem / cham_no / fonction, ◇ TYPE_SEUIL = / "REDUIT" (par défaut), / "RESTREINT", ), ◇ METHODE_2D = _F( ◇ / MAILLAGE_PLAN = list[maillage], ◇ / NOM_MAIL_MED = list[text], / GROUP_NO_PLAN = list[grno], ◇ / FISSURE = fond_fissure, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ UNITE_RESU = int (défaut: 0), ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT Designates the result of the mechanical analysis for which one computes the Beremin quantities (Weibull stress and probability of failure, or surface density of Weibull stress). 3.2 Operand DEFORMATION Defines the assumptions for the computation of the strains. - In small strains (DEFORMATION = 'PETIT' or DEFORMATION = 'PETIT_REAC'), the computation is carried out from the Cauchy stress field SIEF_ELGA - In large logarithmic strains (DEFORMATION = 'GDEF_LOG'), the computation is carried out from the specific stress field T close to the Kirchhoff stress defined in the logarithmic space R5.03.24. Note 1: in large multiplicative strains (DEFORMATION='SIMO_MIEHE' or DEFORMATION='GREEN_LAGRANGE'), the macro-command is not available. Note 2: in order to minimise the effects linked to incompressibility (volumetric locking) it is possible to carry out the post-processing of the fracture mechanics of cleavage with the incompressible elements (GRAD_INCO) with POST_BEREMIN. 3.3 Operand FILTRE_SIGM With 'SIGM_ELGA', the elementary stress fields are used in their representations at the Gauss points. With 'SIGM_ELMOY', the elementary stress fields are determined from the average weighted by the Gauss weights. With 'SIGM_CORR', the Weibull stress is computed by integrating a user field \sigma_I^ given under the keyword SIGM_CORR. This functionality allows the user to consider corrected stress fields, with as a typical application the taking into account of the plastic correction (see R7.02.04). 3.4 Operand SIGM_CORR User stress field \sigma_I^ corresponding to the integrand in the computation of the Weibull stress: {{\sigma}}_{W} = {\left[\underset{{\Omega}}{\int}{({{\sigma}}_{I}^{ })}^{m}\frac{{\delta}V}{{V}_{0}}\right]}^{\frac{1}{m}} A typical application is the taking into account of the plastic correction (see R7.02.04). It is incumbent on the user to define the field \sigma_I^ . The following formalism must be respected: - SIGM_CORR must be a concept of type evol_noli containing at each time instant the field \sigma_I^ to be integrated; - the field \sigma_I^ must be a "utility" field of type UT01_ELGA; - the value of the corrected stress must be carried by the component X1 of this field. The test cases ssna108c to ssna108g provide examples of use. The field \sigma_I^ there is a function of the fields of principal stresses, of internal variables and of principal strains (total or plastic). In particular, the test case ssna108e gives the implementation of the following standard plastic-correction model: {{\sigma}}_{I}^{\star}={{\sigma}}_{I}\exp\left(-\frac{{{\varepsilon}}_{1}^{p}}{2}\right) where \sigma_I is the maximum principal stress and \epsilon_1^p the maximum principal plastic strain. 3.5 Operand NUME_VARI Gives the index of the internal variable of the plasticity indicator, usually named INDIPLAS in code_aster. If this parameter is not filled in, the filter on active plasticity is not activated, and all the volume mesh cells of the GROUP_MA are taken into account in the computation of the Weibull stress. See R7.02.04. 3.6 Operand LIST_NUME_SIEF If DEFORMATION='GDEF_LOG', gives the indices of the logarithmic stresses T close to the Kirchhoff stresses defined in the logarithmic space R5.03.24 taken instead of the Cauchy stress tensor if DEFORMATION='PETIT' or 'PETIT_REAC' (cf [LO17]) 3.7 Operand HIST_MAXI If HIST_MAXI='NON' (default value), the maximum principal stress is instantaneous. If HIST_MAXI='OUI', the maximum principal stress is computed by considering the temporal maximum over the whole history (historical Beremin model). 3.8 Operand COEF_MULT The default value of this coefficient is 1.0. For the Beremin model, the following table, in which the thickness is denoted e , indicates typical values of the coefficient C as a function of the type of symmetry: - simple symmetry : the plane of symmetry of the mesh passes through the plane of the defect and the defect is entirely meshed, - double symmetry : the plane of symmetry of the mesh also passes through the plane of the defect but only one half of the defect is meshed. | | 3D and 3D_SI | AXIS and AXIS_SI | D_PLAN and D_PLAN_SI | C_PLAN | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SIMPLE | 2 | 4\pi | 2e | 2e | | DOUBLE | 4 | not applicable | not applicable | not applicable | | NONE | 1 | 2\pi | e | e | Table 3.5-1 : Values of the symmetry-thickness multiplier coefficient for the Weibull stress Caution, this table is valid only for the Beremin model (computation of the Weibull stress). In the case of the industrial version of the Beremin model, this table is no longer valid and one cannot reason in terms of simple or double symmetries. Indeed, the value of COEFF_MULT depends only on the portion of the integration plane represented in the model. If one represents the whole integration plane, then COEF\_ MULT = 1 . If one represents only half of the plane, then COEF\_ MULT = 2 . 3.9 Operand SIGM_MAXI Makes it possible to print a post-processing result file in MED format. This field will contain two components: the integrand of the Weibull stress before and after raising to the power m. Caution, this keyword cannot be used if several material parameters are given as input or if several projection planes are requested (in the case METHODE_2D). 3.10 Factor keyword WEIBULL or WEIBULL_FO Weibull parameters (see R7.02.04). In the case WEIBULL, the parameters M, SIGM_REFE and SIGM_SEUIL may be lists of parameters. All the combinations of material parameters are computed if lists of parameters are supplied by the user. WEIBULL = _F(GROUP_MA = group_ma, M = m, SIGM_REFE = sigmu, VOLU_REFE = V0, SIGM_SEUIL = sigth, TYPE_SEUIL = type_seuil) In the case WEIBULL_FO, the parameters SIGM_REFE and SIGM_SEUIL may be: - functions, and only of the temperature or of the coordinates X, Y or Z; - fields at the Gauss points or fields at the nodes. In this latter case, the intended application is to define material parameters depending on the temperature or on the position in a more complex way than by going through functions of T, X, Y or Z. One may for example define these parameters as formula fields evaluated at one or more parameters, such as the temperature or the coordinates of the position. In the case WEIBULL_FO, the parameters SIGM_REFE and SIGM_SEUIL may be: - functions, and only of the temperature or of the coordinates X, Y or Z; - fields at the Gauss points or fields at the nodes. Note that it is expected that the field given for the parameter SIGM_REFE (resp. SIGM_SEUIL) has the component X1 corresponding to the value of the parameter. Such a field is typically obtained by defining a field of type ELGA_NEUT_F or NOEU_NEUT_F (formula field) and then evaluating it at one or more parameters in order to obtain a field ELGA_NEUT_R or NOEU_NEUT_R. An example of use is given in the test case zzzz163g. A single function or a single field may be assigned to SIGM_REFE (resp. SIGM_SEUIL). Only M may be a list of parameters. WEIBULL_FO = _F(GROUP_MA = group_ma, M = m, SIGM_REFE = sigmu, SIGM_CNV = sigm0u, VOLU_REFE = V0, SIGM_SEUIL = sigth, TYPE_SEUIL = type_seuil) All the combinations of material parameters are computed if lists of parameters are supplied by the user. The keyword WEIBULL(_FO) may be repeated as many times as desired, for example in order to perform the post-processing on different GROUP_MA. In this case the result tables are concatenated successively. 3.10.1 Operand GROUP_MA Mesh-cell group on which the integrand of the Weibull stress will be computed. 3.10.2 Operand VOLU_REFE Reference volume V_0 . 3.10.3 Operand M Parameter m characterising the scatter of the material. 3.10.4 Operand SIGM_REFE Cleavage stress \sigma_u . If this parameter is not filled in, the probability of failure is not computed. 3.10.5 Operand SIGM_CNV Case WEIBULL_FO only. Stress \sigma_u^0 in the presence of a cleavage stress depending on the temperature (see R7.02.04). 3.10.6 Operand SIGM_SEUIL Threshold stress \sigma_{th} . Default value: 0.0. 3.10.7 Operand TYPE_SEUIL Type of threshold used. May take the values "REDUIT" or "RESTREINT". In the case "REDUIT", the Weibull stress is computed from max (0 , \sigma_I - \sigma_{th}) In the case "RESTREINT", the Weibull stress is computed from \sigma_I restricted to the zone where \sigma_I > \sigma_{th} Default value: "REDUIT". 3.11 Keyword METHODE_2D Makes it possible to use the industrial version of the Beremin model (see R7.02.04). It can be used only with a 3D model. The integrand of the Weibull stress is computed on the basis of the options (threshold stress? filter on active plasticity? maximum over the history? average on the stresses?) specified by the user, in a manner identical to the usual Beremin model. This integrand is then projected onto one or more planes filled in by the user by means of node groups present in the 3D mesh (operand GROUP_NO) or by plane meshes (operand MAILLAGE_PLAN). The integral is then computed in each of these planes. Examples of syntax are given in the section Examples of use. 3.11.1 Operand GROUP_NO_PLAN Makes it possible to specify the name of the node groups onto which the integrand of the Weibull stress will be projected. It may take as input one or more group names. 3.11.2 Operand FISSURE Mandatory if GROUP_NO_PLAN is present. Makes it possible to define the crack front. It takes as input an object fond_fiss defined by the command DEFI_FOND_FISS. In the case where GROUP_NO_PLAN corresponds to a single node group, one may omit this parameter FISSURE. 3.11.3 Operand MAILLAGE_PLAN Makes it possible to define the integration planes of the Weibull stress by means of 2D meshes, distinct from the 3D mesh. 3.11.4 Operand NOM_MAIL_MED Mandatory if MAILLAGE_PLAN is present. Makes it possible to define the name under which the MAILLAGE_PLAN will appear in the output table of POST_BEREMIN. 3.11.5 Operand UNITE_RESU Makes it possible to define optionally the logical unit in which will be printed, in .med format, the integrand of the Weibull stress projected into a plane, for the purpose of checking the computation of this Weibull stress. Requires that only a single integration plane be given. 3.11.6 Operand PRECISION Makes it possible to define the relative precision of the projection from 3D to 2D. This relative precision is defined with respect to the minimum size of the volume mesh cells of the GROUP_MA defined by the user. By default, this relative precision is 10^{-6} . See R7.02.04. 4 Examples of use Examples will be found in the test cases zzzz163 and sslv101. Advice on the use of this model is given in the documentation U2.05.08. 4.1 Example of use for the Beremin model - Stress averaged by element - Filter on active plasticity, on the basis of the internal variable V2 - Maximum of the stresses over the history (HIST_MAXI = "OUI" by default) In the case below, the Weibull stress is computed on the mesh-cell group "CT", by applying the following options: BERE = POST_BEREMIN( RESULTAT=U, COEF_MULT=1, DEFORMATION="PETIT", FILTRE_SIGM="SIGM_ELMOY", NUME_VARI=2, WEIBULL=_F(GROUP_MA="CT", M=8.0, VOLU_REFE=1.25e-4, SIGM_REFE=2630.0e0), ) In the example below in large logarithmic strains, the Weibull stress is computed from the components of the tensor T stored in the internal variables 4 to 9 (it is for the user to adapt the numbers of the internal variables as a function of the constitutive law used, for example) BERE = POST_BEREMIN( RESULTAT=U, COEF_MULT=1, DEFORMATION="GDEF_LOG", LIST_NUME_SIEF=[4,5,6,7,8,9], FILTRE_SIGM="SIGM_ELMOY", NUME_VARI=2, WEIBULL=_F(GROUP_MA="CT", M=8.0, VOLU_REFE=1.25e-4, SIGM_REFE=2630.0e0), ) 4.2 Example of use for the industrial version of Beremin In the case of planes defined by node groups: fiss = DEFI_FOND_FISS( MAILLAGE=mail_meca, FOND_FISS=_F( GROUP_MA="FRONT0", TYPE_FOND="OUVERT", ), LEVRE_SUP=_F(GROUP_MA="LEVRE"), SYME="OUI", ) liste_plans = ["Plan_" + str(i) for i in range(0, 51)] beremin_2D = POST_BEREMIN( COEF_MULT=2.0, DEFORMATION="PETIT", FILTRE_SIGM="SIGM_ELMOY", HIST_MAXI="NON", RESULTAT=evol_meca, WEIBULL=_F( GROUP_MA="TORE_COMPLET", M=3, SIGM_SEUIL=1300.0, VOLU_REFE=0.000125, ), METHODE_2D=_F(GROUP_NO_PLAN=liste_plans , FISSURE = fiss), ) In the example above, one defines a crack front by means of the command DEFI_FOND_FISS and then one applies the Beremin post-processing on 51 planes defined by node groups named "Plan_i", with i ranging from 0 to 50. In the case of a plane defined by a 2D mesh, for which one also requests printing the result of the projection in a .med file: mesh_2D_tore_c0 = LIRE_MAILLAGE(FORMAT="MED", UNITE=22) beremin_2d_c0_tore = POST_BEREMIN( RESULTAT=resu_elas, COEF_MULT=2, DEFORMATION="PETIT", FILTRE_SIGM="SIGM_ELMOY", WEIBULL=_F(GROUP_MA="CT", M=18.0, VOLU_REFE=1.25e-4, SIGM_REFE=2630.0e0), METHODE_2D=_F( MAILLAGE_PLAN=mesh_2D_tore_c0, NOM_MAIL_MED="Couche_0_TORE", UNITE_RESU = 80), )

u4.81.13 Operator MACR_LIGN_COUPE u4.81.13 Operator MACR_LIGN_COUPE 1 Purpose Extraction into a table of the values of a result on section lines defined by two points and an interval or by node groups. The result may be mechanical (evol_elas, evol_noli, mode_meca, comb_fourier, mult_elas, fourier_elas, dyna_trans) or thermal (evol_ther). Principle: This macro-command creates a mesh which may be: - straight, defined by the data of its end points and of a number of intervals making it up; - curved, defined by the data of the centre and of the angle of a circle, of the first point of the section line, of the number of points desired, and possibly of a vector normal to the plane containing the section line (in 3D only); - arbitrary, when the section line constitutes a path linking the nodes of a node group. The fields of the result supplied (by default displacement or temperature) are projected onto this mesh by means of the command PROJ_CHAMP. The nodal values on the section line of the field to be post-processed are then recovered in a table by POST_RELEVE_T. It is this table which is produced by the macro-command. 2 Syntax table = MACR_LIGN_COUPE( ◆ / RESULTAT = dyna_trans / comb_fourier / mult_elas / fourier_elas / evol_noli / evol_elas / evol_ther / mode_meca, evol_ther, comb_fourier, mult_elas, fourier_elas, dyna_trans] Name of the result concept of type evol containing the field to be post-processed. Name of the concept of the field to be post-processed. The optional keyword MODELE must be supplied as soon as CHAM_GD is present. 3.2 Operands NUME_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / LIST_ORDRE / INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE See documentation U4.71.00 ? 3.3 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM = / 'SIGM_NOEU', [DEFAUT si mécanique] / 'TEMP', [DEFAUT si thermique] / champ, [:ref: K16 ] Name of the field of the result resu whose values one wishes to record on a section line. If this keyword is not supplied, the stress field at the nodes computed from the displacements is projected by default for a result of mechanical type and the temperature for a result of thermal type. Note: The macro-command processes all types of field: NOEUD, ELEM, ELNO. It is not recommended to use the field type ELNO, because the result of the projection of an ELNO field by PROJ_CHAMP is sometimes a little disconcerting. For a node, its value is recovered in one of the mesh cells which contain this node. More detail in Chapter 3.13 u4.72.05. 3.4 Operand REPERE_INIT ◊ REPERE_INIT = / 'GLOBAL', / 'LOCAL' Frame in which the base field is expressed (necessary when at least one change of frame is requested for a field on the elements). MACR_LIGN_COUPE cannot process changes of frame for fields defined in the local frame. This argument makes it possible to check that one is not in this configuration. 3.5 Operand MODELE ◊ MODELE = modele, [modele] Name of the model associated with the result concept evol_xxx. The model is necessary during the projection of the field by PROJ_CHAMP. 3.6 Operand UNITE_MAILLAGE ◊ UNITE_MAILLAGE = 25, [DEFAUT] Specifies the logical unit number in which the line mesh of the section line is created. This unit is 25 by default; the user is offered the possibility of modifying it in case unit 25 is already assigned to another use in the study. 3.7 Operand UNITE_RESU ◊ UNITE_RESU = uniteres, Optional keyword; if a logical unit is defined, a file in med format will be generated. This MED file presents the results extracted at the section lines; it also presents, when they are known, the frames in which these results are expressed. The med file can be visualised in ParaVis (a dedicated macro, "macr_lign_coupe", is available there to simplify the visualisation). 3.8 Operands VIS_A_VIS ◊ VIS_A_VIS = _F( ♦ GROUP_MA_1 = gma, [:ref: l_K8 ]) ) This factor keyword is used by the operator PROJ_CHAMP and makes it possible, with its operand GROUP_MA_1, to restrict the extent of the field to be projected. The user is invited to consult the documentation U4.72.05 for further information. 3.9 keyword LIGN_COUPE ♦ LIGN_COUPE = _F( repeatable keyword making it possible to define one or several section lines. A section line is composed of segments with 2 nodes which can describe: - either a straight line, - or an arc of a circle or a circle, - or an arbitrary broken line. In the first case, the section line is composed of a straight segment, defined by its two end points and a number of regular intervals cutting it up. In the second case, the section line is composed of homogeneous straight segments, whose union forms an arc of a circle, or, as a particular case, a circle. In the third case, the section line is defined from node groups or mesh-cell groups of the mesh: the section line is then the path defined by the succession of the nodes of the group. 3.9.1 Operand INTITULE ♦ INTITULE = txt, [Kn] Heading label in the table making it possible to distinguish the different section lines. If this keyword is not supplied, the heading label is equal to ‘l.coupe(n)’ where (n) is the occurrence number of the section line. 3.9.2 Operand TYPE This keyword makes it possible to define the type of section line that one wishes to create. It can be identified with SEGMENT, GROUP_NO, GROUP_MA or ARC. 3.9.2.1 TYPE='SEGMENT' The section line is identified with a straight segment, defined by its two end points and a number of regular intervals cutting it up. 3.9.2.2 TYPE='GROUP_NO' The section line is defined by the data of node groups in the mesh supporting the fields: the section line is then the path defined by the succession of the nodes of these groups. 3.9.2.3 TYPE='GROUP_MA' The section line is built from the nodes of a mesh-cell group made up of mesh cells of type SEG. The section line is then the path defined by the succession of the reordered nodes of this group. If the line is closed, this must be specified by designating the origin and end nodes (for example with the keywords GROUP_NO_ORIG and GROUP_NO_EXTR). These 2 nodes must be identical. To impose the orientation of the line, the keyword VECT_ORIE can be used. For more details concerning these keywords, consult the documentation of the keyword NOEUD_ORDO of the command DEFI_GROUP. 3.9.2.4 TYPE='ARC' The section line amounts to an arc of a circle or to a complete circle. It is defined by the following data: - a first point corresponding to the origin of the circular section line, - a second point corresponding to the centre of the circle, - an angle (expressed in degrees) making it possible to determine the end of the section line, - a number of points constituting the section line, - a vector normal to the plane containing the section line in 3D only. 3.9.3 Operand NB_POINTS ♦ NB_POINTS = nb, [I] Number of points of the section line. 3.9.4 Operand COOR_ORIG ♦ COOR_ORIG = (x1,y1,[z1]), [l_R] Coordinates of the first point of the section line: 2 reals in the plane, 3 in space. This keyword is used for TYPE='SEGMENT' or TYPE='ARC'. 3.9.5 Operand GROUP_NO_ORIG ♦ GROUP_NO_ORIG = gnoA, [group_no] Name of the node group defining the first point of the section line. This group must contain only one node. This keyword is used for TYPE='SEGMENT'. 3.9.6 Operand COOR_EXTR ♦ COOR_EXTR = (x2,y2,[z2]), [l_R] Coordinates of the last point of the section line: 2 reals in the plane, 3 in space. This keyword is used for TYPE='SEGMENT'. 3.9.7 Operand GROUP_NO_EXTR ♦ GROUP_NO_EXTR = gnoB, [group_no] Name of the node group defining the last point of the section line. This group must contain only one node. This keyword is used for TYPE='SEGMENT'. 3.9.8 Operand GROUP_NO ♦ GROUP_NO = gno, [grno] This keyword makes it possible to extract the values on a given node group. In the case of the processing of fields at the nodes, this is perfectly analogous to POST_RELEVE_T. This keyword is used only for TYPE='GROUP_NO'. 3.9.9 Operands GROUP_MA and MAILLAGE ♦ GROUP_MA = grma, [l_grma] This keyword makes it possible to pass the mesh-cell group of type SEG used in order to extract the nodes from it so as to reorder them before the post-processing. ♦ MAILLAGE = mail, [maillage] mail is the mesh concept containing the mesh-cell group grma. These keywords are used for TYPE='GROUP_MA'. 3.9.10 Operand DNOR ◊ DNOR = (xa,ya,[za]), [l_R] The vector to be transmitted to this keyword must be normal to the plane containing the circular section line. In 2D: it is unnecessary (DNOR = vector Z of the global frame) In 3D: it makes it possible to define the direction of travel of the section line (direct sense). This keyword is used for TYPE = 'ARC'. 3.9.11 Operand CENTRE ♦ CENTRE = (x0,y0,[z0]), [l_R] Coordinates of the point corresponding to the centre of the circle supporting the circular section line. This keyword is used for TYPE ='ARC'. 3.9.12 Operand ANGLE ♦ ANGLE = theta , [R] It corresponds to the angle of the circle supporting the circular section line (expressed in degrees) which, from its centre, from the origin point and from the plane containing the section line, determines the end of the section line. This keyword is used for TYPE = 'ARC'. 3.9.13 Operands DISTANCE_MAX and DISTANCE_ALARME ◊ DISTANCE_MAX = distmax, [R] ◊ DISTANCE_ALARME = distala, [R] These keywords are useful to the operator PROJ_CHAMP (a single PROJ_CHAMP for the whole command). If the distance between a node of the section line and the cut mesh is greater than distmax, then this node will be ignored (no recording of a value on this node). If the distance between a node of the section line and the cut mesh is greater than distala, an alarm will be issued. The minimum values of DISTANCE_ALARME and DISTANCE_MAX are retained over all the occurrences of LIGN_COUPE. If no value is supplied for all the LIGN_COUPE, 0 is taken by default. The user is invited to consult the documentation U4.72.05 for further information. 3.9.14 Operands REPERE ◇ REPERE = / "INITIAL" (par défaut), / "LOCAL", / "POLAIRE", / "UTILISATEUR", / "CYLINDRIQUE", Makes it possible to define the frame in which one wishes to express the result produced. INITIAL makes it possible to keep the frame of the original field. The other options are valid only for fields expressed in the global frame. For more details, see documentation U4.81.21. 3.9.15 Operands INVARIANT / ELEM_PRINCIPAUX / RESULTANTE / OPERATION / NOM_CMP / TRAC_NOR / TRAC_DIR / DIRECTION / VECT_Y/ REPERE See documentation U4.81.21. Note: VECT_Y is useful only in 3D. For sections of segment type in 2D, the tangent vector is obtained automatically by a rotation of -\pi /2 in the plane. 4 Example resu = STAT_NON_LINE (...); tab1 = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(RESULTAT = resu, LIGN_COUPE =( _F(TYPE= ‘SEGMENT’, NB_POINTS = 17, COOR_ORIG = (0.,0.,0.), COOR_EXTR = (10.,0.,0.), INTITULE = ‘ligne1’, ), _F(TYPE= ‘SEGMENT’, NB_POINTS = 25, COOR_ORIG = (-10.,0.,0.), COOR_EXTR = (0.,20.,0.), INTITULE = ‘ligne2’,), ) ); IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=tab1) In this example, the values of the displacement obtained in the result resu are recorded at all the analysis time instants on two section lines. The table tab1 contains the order numbers, the curvilinear abscissae, the coordinates of the points and finally the values of the nodal quantity (grandeur) (on the nodes of the line) of the field processed, here by default the displacement. 5 Visualisation 5.1 Output file For results of extraction type, the user has the possibility of producing a file in MED format by supplying the keyword UNITE_RESU. The fields contained in this file are the following: CUT_AXE_X Vector X of the frame in which the results are expressed. CUT_AXE_Y Vector Y of the frame in which the results are expressed. CUT_AXE_Z Vector Z of the frame in which the results are expressed. CUT_AXE_MASK Field equal to 1.0 at the end nodes of the sections and 0.0 elsewhere (makes it possible to filter these nodes). CUT_XXXX Field of the quantity (grandeur) post-processed in MACR_LIGN_COUPE. For each section, a group named "CUT_" followed by the heading of the section is generated. It can be used to filter the sections. - It is not possible to write in continuation of an existing file (the .med file is reinitialised at each call of MACR_LIGN_COUPE) - The frames of the results are printed only when they are known with certainty (see keyword REPERE_INIT) 5.2 ParaView macro In ParaVis, the macro macr_lign_coupe facilitates the visualisation of the results as well as of the labels associated with each section line. This macro is also available in the sources of Code_Aster. A documentation of this macro is available here: [SV1.01.01].

/ 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Principles of use of POST_RELEVE_T: operand ACTION The post-processing carried out by POST_RELEVE_T requires the data of three pieces of information: - location, - object, - nature. Each occurrence of the factor keyword ACTION defines this triplet. The location of the post-processing designates a geometric figure linking the post-processing points. This location is defined by means of the keyword GROUP_NO. The object of the post-processing is defined by the choice of a field of a quantity (grandeur), of components and possibly of associated quantities chosen by various keywords. The fields of quantities (grandeurs) are chosen by one of the keywords: RESULTAT and the keywords making it possible to choose the fields at the nodes or the fields on the elements of the data structure resultat. CHAM_GD field of a quantity (grandeur) produced by an elementary operator, or extracted from a result concept by CREA_CHAMP U4.72.04. the components by: TOUT_CMP NOM_CMP and the associated quantities by: INVARIANT ELEM_PRINCIPAUX TRAC_NOR TRAC_DIR and DIRECTION RESULTANTE and, optionally, MOMENT and POINT The nature of the post-processing corresponds to the operations: keyword OPERATION - extraction of values: 'EXTRACTION' - computation of means (in the sense of integration), of the minimum and of the maximum on an ordered group of nodes: 'MOYENNE' - computation of the minimum and of the maximum on groups or entities: 'EXTREMA' - computation of means in the arithmetic sense on groups or entities: 'MOYENNE_ARITH' 4 Choice of the location of the post-processing 4.1 OPERATION = 'EXTRACTION' or 'MOYENNE' 4.1.1 Syntax ♦ GROUP_NO = lgrno, [l_gr_noeud] ◊ / TOUT= 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgrma, [l_gr_maille] 4.1.2 Operands GROUP_NO / TOUT / GROUP_MA - The argument of GROUP_NO is a list of node groups. The nodes are processed in the order supplied by the user. To reorder the nodes of a list, the command DEFI_GROUP/OPTION =‘NOEUD_ORDO’ U4.22.01 must be used - The keyword GROUP_MA makes it possible to limit the post-processing to a list of mesh-cell groups. TOUT= 'OUI' amounts to the standard case (all the mesh cells are considered). These keywords can be used only with GROUP_NO. Notes: It is not recommended to use GROUP_MA with the operation MOYENNE unless the elements are segments. Recall that the operation MOYENNE computes quantities along a length L. For further information, refer to the paragraph devoted to the keyword OPERATION where the quantities computed by means of this option are presented. The keyword TOUT='OUI' means “all the mesh cells of the mesh”. The nodal elements assigned directly on the nodes of the mesh ( AFFE_MODELE / NOEUD ), which are moreover not recommended, are ignored by the post-processing. 4.1.3 Notions of post-processing points and examples The post-processing points are the points of \Omega where the components (or derived quantities) are evaluated. The extraction operation carries out this evaluation. 4.1.4 Example of post-processing points specified by the keyword GROUP_NO Figure 4.3.3-a This figure visualises a post-processing location built from a list of nodes. The post-processing points are the nodes shown, the post-processing location is the broken line linking them in the order supplied by the user, which makes it possible to define a curvilinear abscissa. The value extracted on these lines is interpolated linearly between the values recorded on the nodes. Thus it must be noted that if the post-processing operation is a computation of a mean, everything happens as if the segment [{N}_{\mathrm{47 }}{N}_{61}] were contained entirely in \Omega . In this case, the curvilinear abscissa is computed from the path of the nodes, as defined in the list of nodes. 4.2 OPERATION = 'EXTREMA' or 'MOYENNE_ARITH' 4.2.1 Syntax ♦ | TOUT= 'OUI', | GROUP_NO = lgrno, [l_gr_noeud] | GROUP_MA = lgrma, [l_gr_maille] 4.2.2 Operands TOUT/ GROUP_NO / GROUP_MA - The argument of GROUP_NO is a list of node groups. The nodes are not ordered. - The keyword GROUP_MA makes it possible to limit the post-processing to a list of mesh-cell groups. - TOUT= 'OUI' amounts to the standard case (all the mesh cells are considered). 5 Choice of the object of the post-processing These keywords make it possible to define the object of the post-processing. They designate: - a field of a quantity (grandeur): keywords CHAM_GD, RESULTAT (and its associated keywords), - a quantity associated with the components of the field: keywords TOUT_CMP, NOM_CMP, INVARIANT, ELEM_PRINCIPAUX, TRAC_NOR, TRAC_DIR, DIRECTION, REPERE, SOMME, RESULTANTE, MOMENT, POINT. 5.1 Field of a quantity (grandeur) 5.1.1 Syntax ♦ / CHAM_GD = chpgd, / RESULTAT = resu, ♦ NOM_CHAM = chpsymbo, [:ref: K16 ] ♦ / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI', / NUME_ORDRE = lordre, [l_I] / LIST_ORDRE = lenti, [listis] / NUME_MODE = lmode, [l_I] / LIST_MODE = lenti, [listis] / NOM_CAS = nomcas, [:ref: K24 ] / / FREQ = lfreq, [l_R] / LIST_FREQ = lreel, listr8 / INST = linst, [l_R] / LIST_INST = lreel, listr8 ◊ | PRECISION= / prec, [R] / 1.D–6, [DEFAUT] ◊ | CRITERE= / 'RELATIF', [DEFAUT] / 'ABSOLU' , ◊ FORMAT_C= / 'MODULE', [DEFAUT] / 'REEL' , / 'IMAG' , 5.1.2 Operand CHAM_GD The argument of CHAM_GD is the name of a concept of type cham_no_ or cham_elem_ . 5.1.3 Operands RESULTAT / NOM_CHAM / TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / LIST_MODE / NOM_CAS / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE See U4.71.00. 5.1.4 Operand FORMAT_C In the case of complex fields, one can extract: / 'MODULE' le module / 'REEL' la partie réelle / 'IMAG' la partie imaginaire 5.2 Components of the field and derived quantities For vectors and tensors of order 2, it is possible to request the evaluation of the components in a frame and to derive quantities obtained by contracted product. The keywords REPERE, TRAC_NOR, TRAC_DIR and DIRECTION make it possible to define these quantities. 5.2.1 Syntax ♦ / TOUT_CMP = 'OUI', / NOM_CMP = lcmp, [:ref: l_K8 ] ◊ / REPERE = / 'GLOBAL' , [DEFAUT] / 'POLAIRE', / 'LOCAL' , ◊ VECT_Y=(oy1,oy2,oy3), [l_R] / 'UTILISATEUR', ♦ ANGL_NAUT= (a,b,c),[l_R] / 'CYLINDRIQUE', ♦ ORIGINE= (x,y,z), [l_R] ♦ AXE_Z=(oz1,oz2,oz3),[l_R] ◊ / TRAC_NOR = 'OUI', / TRAC_DIR = 'OUI', ♦ DIRECTION = (x,y,[z]), [l_R] / INVARIANT = 'OUI', / ELEM_PRINCIPAUX= 'OUI', / RESULTANTE = lcmp, [:ref: l_K8 ] ◊ MOMENT = lcmp, [:ref: l_K8 ] ♦ POINT = (x,y,[z]), [l_R] 5.2.2 Operand TOUT_CMP / TOUT_CMP This keyword admits as argument only the text 'OUI' and selects all the components defined in the catalogue of quantities (grandeurs) for the quantity (grandeur) relating to the fields specified by the keywords RESULTAT and CHAM_GD. 5.2.3 Operands NOM_CMP Makes it possible to define the components of the quantity (grandeur) of the field processed: / NOM_CMP : les composantes sont introduites par nom 5.2.4 Operand REPERE / REPERE Makes it possible to choose a frame from among the following frames: - GLOBAL frame: Cartesian frame of definition of the mesh, - POLAIRE frame: standard polar frame of the plane (\mathit{OXY}) (order of the components: (r,\theta ) , - LOCAL frame: frame of the plane made up of the tangent and normal vectors (in that order) to the post-processing location. The normal vector is defined at each post-processing point as the mean of the normals to the right and to the left. Definition of the normal to the post-processing location. At each post-processing point the normal is defined as the mean of the normals to the right and to the left. Figure 5.2.4-a The tangent vector is obtained by a rotation of -\pi /2 from the normal vector. In the case of the LOCAL frame and of a 3D line, one will have to supply: VECT_Y = (oy1,oy2,oy3) The coordinates of a vector whose projection onto the plane orthogonal to the directing axis of the line will be taken as the normal to the line. The order of the components in a local frame is (t,n,k) . Example of use: O Figure 5.2.4-b One wants to carry out an extraction on the line \mathit{ABC} in the local frame defined above (local axis y in the global direction \mathit{OX} ). Here, one can find a vector constant at every point of the line in order to define the vector VECT_Y=(1.,0.,0.). This is possible because at every point this vector is already in the plane orthogonal to the line. Figure 5.2.4-c If, on the other hand, one wishes to have the local axis z in the global direction \mathit{OX} [Figure 5.2.4-c], the vector VECT_Y will depend on the point considered: (0.,0.,1.) is suitable except at A (where (0.,-1.,0.) is suitable) (0.,-\mathrm{1.0.}) is suitable except at C (where (0.,0.,1.) is suitable) One will therefore have in this case to cut the line into two pieces ( \mathit{AB} and \mathit{BC} ) and to define a different VECT_Y on each piece. - UTILISATEUR frame: defined by the data of 3 nautical angles (in degrees): ANGL_NAUT= (a, b, c) - CYLINDRIQUE frame defined by: | ORIGINE= (x,y,z) | the coordinates of the origin O of the frame | | --- | --- | | AXE_Z=(oz1,oz2,oz3) | the coordinates of a vector defining the axis \mathit{Oz} (axis of the cylinder). The order of the components in a cylindrical frame is (r,z,\theta ) . | 5.2.5 Operand TRAC_NOR / TRAC_NOR: uniquement pour les modélisations 2D et 3D. Determination of the normal trace of a vector or of a tensor of order 2: this is the particular case of the directional trace obtained when the direction u is identified with the normal n to the post-processing location. 5.2.6 Operands TRAC_DIR / DIRECTION / TRAC_DIR : uniquement pour les modélisations 2D et 3D. ♦ DIRECTION Determination of the directional trace of a vector v=({v}_{i}) or of a tensor of order 2 \sigma =({\sigma}_{i}) in the direction u=({u}_{i}) ; that is, of the scalar {v}_{k}{u}_{k} or of the vector {\sigma}_{\mathit{ik}}{u}_{k} . The direction u is defined by means of the keyword DIRECTION whose arguments are the components of the vector u given in the order X,Y,Z and evaluated in the global frame. If this list contains only two values then, by convention, the component along Z of the vector u is considered to be zero. 5.2.7 Operand INVARIANT Post-processing of a stress or strain tensor of order 2 associated with the principal directions of the tensor: TRACE \mathrm{Tr}(\sigma )=\sum_{i=1}^{2\mathrm{ou}3}{\sigma}_{ii} VON_MIS \mathrm{VM}(\sigma )=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{2\mathrm{ou}3}\frac{3}{2}{({\sigma}_{ij}-\frac{1}{3}\mathrm{Tr}(\sigma ){\delta}_{ij})}^{2}} TRESCA \mathrm{TR}(\sigma )=\max(∣{\lambda}_{i}-{\lambda}_{j}∣) with {\lambda}_{i} eigenvalues of \sigma DETER \mathrm{DET}(\sigma )=\mathrm{déterminant}\mathrm{de}\sigma 5.2.8 Operand ELEM_PRINCIPAUX / ELEM_PRINCIPAUX Determination of the principal values of a tensor 2\times 2 or 3\times 3 of order 2. They are arranged in increasing order of their values. 5.2.9 Operands RESULTANTE / MOMENT / POINT Determination of the resultant and of the moment of a torsor field on the post-processing location. RESULTANTE can be used only if OPERATION='EXTRACTION'. From the software point of view, these keywords can be applied to any field of a quantity (grandeur) but, for the results to have a physical meaning, one must restrict oneself to the fields of nodal forces and nodal reactions. In this latter case, 2 possibilities arise: - the user wants to compute the resultant of certain components of the field: behind the keyword RESULTANTE a list of components will be entered, to be taken from among \lbrace 'DX', 'DY', 'PRE1', 'PRE2', 'TEMP' \rbrace in 2D and \lbrace 'DX', 'DY', 'DZ', 'PRE1', 'PRE2', 'TEMP' \rbrace in 3D or for structural elements (the resultant of rotation components having no physical meaning), - the user wants to compute the resultant and the moment of certain components of the field: behind the keywords RESULTANTE and MOMENT 2 lists of components of the same length will be entered, to be taken from among | formula \lbrace 'DX', 'DY', 'DZ' \rbrace | behind the keyword RESULTANTE | | --- | --- | | formula \lbrace 'DRX', 'DRY', 'DRZ' \rbrace | behind the keyword MOMENT | In addition, behind the keyword POINT the list of the coordinates of the point with respect to which the moment is evaluated will be introduced. If one denotes by P this point and by M_{i} the post-processing points, the quantities evaluated will be: - Resultant: F=\sum_{i}{F}_{i}=\sum_{i}(FX_{M_i},FY_{M_i},FZ_{M_i}, PRE1_{M_i},PRE2_{M_i},TEMP_{M_i}) - Moment: m=\sum_{i}(\overrightarrow{PM}_i\wedge F_i)+\sum_{i}m_i^c where m_i^c designates the list of the concentrated moments corresponding to the rotation components introduced by the keyword MOMENT, relevant only in the case of structural elements (beams, shells, discrete elements). 1. In continuous media, one must not introduce behind MOMENT translation components which would be considered as concentrated moments and therefore summed with the true moments. 1. The computation of RESULTANTE and/or of MOMENT is carried out by a sum over a set of nodes. This sum has a meaning only if all the nodal forces (or moments) are expressed in the same frame. This means that the keyword REPERE can take as value only 'GLOBAL' or 'UTILISATEUR'. 1. The components 'PRE1', 'PRE2' and 'TEMP' of the keyword RESULTANTE are accessible only in thermo-hydro-mechanical modelling. Notes 6 Nature of the post-processing 6.1 Operand OPERATION ♦ OPERATION = | 'EXTRACTION' The operation of extraction of a field of a quantity (grandeur) makes it possible to recover the values of one or several components or of quantities derived from these components at the points of the post-processing location. In the case of an extraction on a cham_elem, the values of the components extracted from this field are computed as follows: - If the post-processing location is determined by the keyword GROUP_NO, for each node the components are averaged over all the elements meeting at this node. In the case of the extraction of a field of type ELNO, the same values are obtained by giving the field of type NOEU. Note: The averagings at the nodes of fields computed in local frames are licit only if the angles between these frames are small. Otherwise, they have no meaning. If the post-processing location is defined by GROUP_NO = (\mathit{GN}1,\mathit{GN}2,\mathit{GN}3,\mathit{GN}4,\mathit{GN}5) , the values are averaged over all the elements of the mesh above. If the post-processing location is defined as being the segment of origin \mathit{N1} and of end \mathit{N5} , the values will be averaged over the hatched elements. In the case of quadratic elements (presence of mid-side nodes), the mean at the vertex nodes can lead to greater weights of certain elements (depending on the subdivision) with respect to the mid-side nodes which average over 2 elements (hence of the same weight). One can therefore find oneself in the presence of oscillations between the values at the vertices and at the mid-sides. | 'MOYENNE' This operation is limited to 6 field components at a time. Given a scalar field U (typically a component of a quantity (grandeur)), the operation 'MOYENNE' computes the following quantities ( L designating the length of the post-processing location C considered): MOMENT_0 = \frac{1}{L}{\int}_{c}U(s)\mathrm{ds} MOMENT_1 = \frac{12}{{L}^{2}}{\int}_{c}U(s)(s-\frac{L}{2})\mathrm{ds} MINIMUM = \underset{c}{\mathrm{Min}}U MAXIMUM = \underset{c}{\mathrm{Max}}U MOYE_INT = MOMENT_0 - ½ MOMENT_1 MOYE_EXT = MOMENT_0 + ½ MOMENT_1 It is important that the post-processing location be traversed in one direction. If a node group is used, care will be taken to reorder the nodes, by using the command DEFI_GROUP option 'NOEUD_ORDO', U4.22.01. Thus, the curvilinear abscissa is defined from the origin node of the group, following the broken line made up of the nodes. The integrals above are evaluated by assuming U linear between two nodes. Thus, denoting by {U}_{i} the values of the field at the nodes (numbered by i=1,\mathrm{...},N ) of abscissa {s}_{i} , one has: \text{MOMENT\_0}=\frac{1}{2({s}_{N}-{s}_{1})}\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}({s}_{i+1}-{s}_{i})({U}_{i}+{U}_{i+1}) \begin{array}{}\text{MOMENT\_1}=\frac{2}{{({s}_{N}-{s}_{1})}^{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}({s}_{i+1}-{s}_{i})({U}_{i}({s}_{i+1}+{\mathrm{2s}}_{i})+{U}_{i+1}({\mathrm{2s}}_{i+1}+{s}_{i}))\\ -\frac{3}{({s}_{N}-{s}_{1})}\sum_{i=1}^{N-1}({s}_{i+1}-{s}_{i})({U}_{i}+{U}_{i+1})\end{array} | 'EXTREMA' calcule les MIN, MAX, MINI_ABS, MAXI_ABSd'un champ réduit éventuellement sur une liste de nœuds ou de mailles, sur toutes les composantes ou une liste de composantes. 6.2 Operand MOYE_NOEUD Keyword making it possible to choose a detailed or averaged printout at a point. This keyword is significant only for quantities (grandeurs) of type cham_elem and for the operation EXTRACTION. MOYE_NOEUD = 'OUI' For each post-processing point, the displayed value of a component or of a deduced quantity is obtained as the mean of the values given by each mesh cell meeting at this point. The way of taking the mean is the same as for the fields XXXX_NOEU computed by CALC_CHAMP U4.81.04. MOYE_NOEUD = 'NON' The list of the values obtained for each mesh cell meeting at the post-processing point is displayed. 7 Operands for access to and printout of the content of the tables created by POST_RELEVE_T 7.1 Principles of addressing the content of the tables The records of values are stored in concepts of type table. It concerns all the occurrences of the factor keyword ACTION. Two groups of checks are distinguished. The first group is common to the arguments of the keywords CHAM_GD and RESULTAT (which are mutually exclusive) and reduces to the following checks: - acceptability of the components: one checks that the components requested are indeed present in the catalogue of description of the quantity (grandeur) to be processed, The second group is specific to the keyword RESULTAT, and reduces to the checks: - check of the acceptability of the symbolic field: one makes sure that the symbolic field argument of the keyword NOM_CHAM does indeed exist for the type of concept resultat argument of the keyword RESULTAT, - existence of at least one data structure for the symbolic field to be processed. At the end of the verification phase, in the execution phase the following alternative arises: - all the occurrences of ACTION are correct and the operations are launched, - at least one occurrence of ACTION is incorrect, then a fatal error message is produced with a stop of the command. Information is given on the nature of the errors and the means of correcting them. 8.2 During processing A new verification filter arises but never causes the command to stop. This filter reduces to the following checks: - existence of the data structure designated by CHAM_GD or RESULTAT and one of the keywords allowing access in a RESULTAT data structure. In the event of failure a message is issued and the following occurrence is processed, - in the case of a computation of tensor invariants, one checks that the object of the processing does indeed designate a tensor of order 2, - in the case of a computation of a mean or of a request for extraction of values, one checks that the components to be processed have indeed been computed on the post-processing location. In the event of failure of this check, a message details the components not available as a function of the mesh cells or nodes of the post-processing location. In the case where this last filter detects no impossibility of computation, the post-processing is launched and the results are inserted in the table. 9 Examples The examples which follow apply to the same physical problem (test case SHLV100G). 9.1 Keywords 'EXTRACTION''MOYENNE' 'EXTREMA' 'MOYENNE_ARITH' 9.1.1 'EXTRACTION' 9.1.1.1 Commands # extraction des CMP du tenseur des contraintes sur une liste de noeuds # t2 = POST_RELEVE_T( ACTION = _F ( INTITULE = 'ex_2', GROUP_NO= ('GN1','GN347','GN21','GN432','GN39','GN229'), CHAM_GD = SIGMA, NOM_CMP = ('SIXX','SIYY','SIZZ','SIXY'), OPERATION = 'EXTRACTION' ) ) 9.1.1.2 Result --- POST_TRAITEMENT NUMERO : 1 - u4.81.22 Operator POST_ELEM u4.81.22 Operator POST_ELEM 1 Purpose Calculate quantities on the whole or on part of the structure. The quantities calculated correspond to particular computation options of the assigned modelling. The options currently available are: - calculation of the mass, of the inertias and of the position of the centre of gravity, - calculation of the potential energy, - calculation of the kinetic energy, - calculation of the dissipation energy (DKTG elements), - calculation of the work of the external forces, - calculation of the indicators of loss of proportionality of the loading in elastoplasticity, - calculation of the limit load, - calculation of the Weibull stress, - calculation of the growth rate of a spherical cavity (Rice - Tracey), - calculation of the elastic energy and of the total energy, - calculation of the area of a hole in a 2D mesh, - calculation of the integral and of the mean of a field, - calculation of the surface/volume distribution of the value of a component of a field, - calculation of the spatial extrema of a list of components of a field, - calculation of the norm of a field. The concept returned is a table. 2 Syntax / table / table_container = POST_ELEM( ◆ / MASS_INER = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ ORIG_INER = float, ), / ENER_POT = _F( ◆ given. 3.1 Operand MODELE ◊ MODELE = mo, Name of the model on which the option is calculated. The name of the model is optional because it is contained in the resultat data structure. 3.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater, Material field associated with the model mo, optional because it is contained in the resultat data structure. 3.3 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, The elementary characteristics carac are necessary if structural elements (beam, plate, shell or discrete elements) exist in the model, optional because they are contained in the resultat data structure. 3.4 Operands NUME_COUCHE / NIVE_COUCHE ◊ NUME_COUCHE = nume, In the case of a multilayer material, integer value lying between 1 and the number of layers, necessary to specify the layer where one wishes to carry out the elementary computation. By convention, layer 1 is the lower layer (in the direction of the normal to the element) in the case of mechanical shell elements or thermal shell elements. ◊ NIVE_COUCHE = For the layer nume defined by NUME_COUCHE, makes it possible to specify the ordinate where one wishes to carry out the elementary computation: | 'INF' lower ordinate of the layer | (inner skin), | | --- | --- | | 'SUP' upper ordinate of the layer | (outer skin), | | 'MOY' mean ordinate of the layer | (mean ply by default). | 3.5 Operand MODE_FOURIER ◊ MODE_FOURIER = Number of the Fourier harmonic: positive or zero integer (default = 0). 3.6 Operand GEOMETRIE ♦ GEOMETRIE = / 'INITIALE', [DEFAUT] / 'DEFORMEE', Indicates whether one is working on the initial geometry or on the deformed geometry. In the latter case, a displacement field must be supplied by CHAM_GD or RESULTAT. 3.7 Operands CHAM_GD / RESULTAT The options ENER_POT and ENER_CIN are calculated from a field at the nodes or an element-wise field, existing or extracted from a resultat. 3.7.1 Operand CHAM_GD ♦ / CHAM_GD = cham, Name of a field (for the options ENER_POT and ENER_CIN). For the option ENER_POT, a displacement field or a temperature field must be supplied (see [§3.9]). For the option ENER_CIN, a velocity field must be supplied (without supplying a frequency), or else a displacement field and a frequency (see [§3.9]). 3.7.2 Operand RESULTAT / RESULTAT = resu, Name of a result concept of type evol_elas, evol_ther, mode_meca, evol_noli, mult_elas, fourier_elas or dyna_trans. | Option ENER_POT: | evol_elas, evol_ther, mode_meca, mult_elas, fourier_elas, evol_noli or dyna_trans. | | --- | --- | | Option ENER_CIN: | mode_meca, evol_elas, evol_ther, evol_noli, or dyna_trans. | | Option ENER_ELAS and ENER_TOTALE: | evol_noli, evol_elas | 3.7.2.1 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / LIST_ORDRE / NOEUD_CMP / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE See U4.71.00. 3.8 Keyword MASS_INER 3.8.1 Purpose Factor keyword making it possible to calculate the mass, the inertias and the centre of gravity. This option allows the computation, on each element, of the following characteristics: ( \rho denoting the density defined in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 by ELAS or ELAS_FO). Mass: m=\underset{v}{\int}\rho \mathrm{dv} Centre of gravity: {x}_{G}=\frac{1}{m}\underset{v}{\int}x\rho \mathit{dv};{y}_{G}=\frac{1}{m}\underset{v}{\int}y\rho \mathit{dv};{z}_{G}=\frac{1}{m}\underset{v}{\int}z\rho \mathit{dv} Inertia tensor at the centre of gravity G in the global frame of description of the mesh: \begin{array}{cc}{I}_{xx}(G)=\underset{v}{\int}({(y-{y}_{G})}^{2}+{(z-{z}_{G})}^{2})\rho \mathit{dv}& {I}_{xy}(G)=\underset{v}{\int}(x-{x}_{G})(y-{y}_{G})\rho \mathit{dv}\\ {I}_{yy}(G)=\underset{v}{\int}({(x-{x}_{G})}^{2}+{(z-{z}_{G})}^{2})\rho \mathit{dv}& {I}_{xz}(G)=\underset{v}{\int}(x-{x}_{G})(z-{z}_{G})\rho \mathit{dv}\\ {I}_{zz}(G)=\underset{v}{\int}({(x-{x}_{G})}^{2}+{(y-{y}_{G})}^{2})\rho \mathit{dv}& {I}_{yz}(G)=\underset{v}{\int}(y-{y}_{G})(z-{z}_{G})\rho \mathit{dv}\end{array} It then calculates by "summation" the quantities relating to the global structure. The principal inertia tensor, made up of the eigenvalues of the inertia matrix, is calculated, as well as the 3 Euler angles associated with the principal frame of inertia. These components are denoted in the table: IX_PRIN_G IY_PRIN_G IZ_PRIN_G ALPHA BETA GAMMA. 3.8.2 Syntax | MASS_INER =_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA= lgrma, [l_gr_maille] ◊ ORIG_INER= (xp, yp [,zp]), [l_R] ), Simple keywords: (see [§2]) ◊ MODELE = mo, [modele] ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater, [cham_mater] ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, [cara_elem] ◊ | NUME_COUCHE = | NIVE_COUCHE = ◊ MODE_FOURIER = ◊ GEOMETRIE = ♦ / CHAM_GD = / RESULTAT = Note For the factor keyword MASS_INER, the model and the material field are mandatory if RESULTAT and CHAM_GD are absent. 3.8.3 Operands ♦ GEOMETRIE = / 'INTIALE', [DEFAUT] / 'DEFORMEE', Indicates whether one is working on the initial geometry or on the deformed geometry. In the latter case, one must supply a displacement field by CHAM_GD or RESULTAT. ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', Over the whole structure. / GROUP_MA = lgrma, On a list of mesh-cell groups. If there is more than one mesh-cell group in the list, then a row is added to the output table which is the result on the union of the mesh cells of the groups given, in addition to the result per group. This new row corresponds to the mesh-cell group ‘UNION_GROUP_MA’. ◊ ORIG_INER= (xp, yp [,zp]), [l_R] Point with respect to which the inertia tensor will be calculated. The inertia tensor at the point P of coordinates (xp, yp, zp) is obtained from the inertia tensor at the centre of gravity G , from the mass m of the structure and from the coordinates of G by the formulae: \begin{array}{}{I}_{xx}(P)={I}_{xx}(G)+m{x}_{\mathrm{PG}}^{2}\\ {I}_{yy}(P)={I}_{yy}(G)+m{y}_{\mathrm{PG}}^{2}\\ {I}_{zz}(P)={I}_{zz}(G)+m{z}_{\mathrm{PG}}^{2}\\ {I}_{xy}(P)={I}_{xy}(G)+m{x}_{\mathrm{PG}}{y}_{\mathrm{PG}}\\ {I}_{xz}(P)={I}_{xz}(G)+m{x}_{\mathrm{PG}}{z}_{\mathrm{PG}}\\ {I}_{yz}(P)={I}_{yz}(G)+m{y}_{\mathrm{PG}}{z}_{\mathrm{PG}}\end{array} with \begin{array}{}{x}_{\mathrm{PG}}={x}_{G}-{x}_{P}\\ {y}_{\mathrm{PG}}={y}_{G}-{y}_{P}\\ {z}_{\mathrm{PG}}={z}_{G}-{z}_{P}\end{array} 3.9 Keyword ENER_POT 3.9.1 Purpose Factor keyword making it possible to calculate: - the potential strain energy at equilibrium from the displacements, in linear continuum mechanics (2D and 3D thermoelasticity): \mathit{EPOT}=\frac{1}{2}\underset{\mathit{élément}}{\int}\varepsilon (\mathrm{U})\cdot \mathrm{A}\varepsilon (\mathrm{U})\mathit{dv}-\underset{\mathit{élément}}{\int}\varepsilon (\mathrm{U})\cdot \mathrm{A}{\varepsilon}^{\mathit{th}}(\mathrm{T})\mathit{dv}+\frac{1}{2}\underset{\mathit{élément}}{\int}{\varepsilon}^{\mathit{th}}(\mathrm{T})\cdot \mathrm{A}{\varepsilon}^{\mathit{th}}(\mathrm{T})\mathit{dv} where A denotes the elasticity tensor, - the potential strain energy at equilibrium from the displacements, in linear mechanics for structural elements: \mathrm{EPOT}=\frac{1}{2}{U}^{T}{K}_{e}U-{U}^{T}{B}^{T}A{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}+\frac{1}{2}{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}A{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}} where K denotes the stiffness matrix Note: Strictly speaking, the potential energy of a structure is the opposite of these quantities. - the thermally dissipated energy at equilibrium in linear thermal analysis from the temperatures (cham_no_TEMP_R): {W}_{\mathit{th}}=-\frac{1}{2}\underset{\Omega}{\int}\nabla T\cdot \mathrm{K}\cdot \nabla Td\Omega Note: In the first two cases, one must give a displacement field under the operand RESULTAT or CHAM_GD. In the last case a temperature field. Note: In the case of the computation of the option on a temperature field the dependence of the material parameters on the temperature is taken into account via the command variables defined in AFFE_MATERIAU . 3.9.2 Syntax | ENER_POT =_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgrma, [l_gr_maille] ) Simple keywords: (see [§2]) ◊ MODELE = mo, [modele] ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater, [cham_mater] ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, [cara_elem] ◊ | NUME_COUCHE = | NIVE_COUCHE = ◊ MODE_FOURIER = ♦ / CHAM_GD = / RESULTAT = Note For the factor keyword ENER_POT, the model, the material field and, where applicable, the field of structural-element characteristics are mandatory (except if RESULTAT is supplied) in order to determine beforehand the energy fields by element. 3.9.3 Operands ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', Over the whole structure. / GROUP_MA = lgrma, On a list of mesh-cell groups. 3.9.4 Produced table The table contains, for each time instant, the values of the energy and of the percentage on the geometric locus concerned: | INST | LIEU | ENTITE | TOTALE | POUR_CENT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 5.50000E+00 | MA | TOUT | 4.00093E+12 | 1.00000E+02 | | 5.50000E+00 | GMA1 | GROUP_MA | 2.71323E+11 | 6.78151E+00 | 3.10 Keyword ENER_CIN 3.10.1 Purpose Factor keyword making it possible to calculate the kinetic energy from a velocity field or from a displacement field and a frequency. The user may carry out this post-processing from a result concept of type evol_noli or evol_elas. In the case of an evol_noli concept, the computation carried out depends on the choice of strain formulation made during the analysis. - In small strains (DEFORMATION = PETIT or DEFORMATION = PETIT_REAC), the computation is carried out from the Cauchy stress field SIEF_ELGA by Hooke's expression: {E}^{e}(t)=\frac{1}{2}{\int}_{v}^{t}\sigma (t){D}^{-1}\sigma (t)\mathit{dv} where D represents the elasticity operator. - in multiplicative large strains (DEFORMATION = SIMO_MIEHE), the computation is carried out from the Jacobian J of the transformation gradient and from the specific measure of elastic strain {\overline{\mathrm{b}}}^{\mathrm{e}} of SIMO_MIEHE (see R5.03.21): {E}^{e}(t)={\int}_{v}^{t}\left[\frac{1}{2}\frac{E}{3\left(1-2\nu \right)}\left(\frac{1}{2}\left({J}^{2}(t)-1\right)-\lnJ(t)\right)+\frac{1}{2}\mu \left(\mathit{tr}{\overline{\mathrm{b}}}^{\mathrm{e}}(t)-3\right)\right]\mathit{dv} In the presence of thermal effects, a specific correction is carried out in order to remove, as well as possible, the effects of the latter on the Jacobian. This specific correction is detailed in R5.03.21. - in logarithmic large strains (DEFORMATION = GDEF_LOG), the computation is carried out from the specific stress field T (see R5.03.24) by the expression: {E}^{e}(t)=\frac{1}{2}{\int}_{v}^{t}T(t){D}^{-1}T(t)\mathit{dv} 3.11.2 Syntax | ENER_ELAS=_F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgrma, [l_gr_maille] ) Simple keywords: (see [§2]) ◊ MODELE = mo, [modele] ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater, [cham_mater] ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, [cara_elem] ◊ | NUME_COUCHE = | NIVE_COUCHE = ◊ MODE_FOURIER = ♦ RESULTAT = 3.11.3 Operands ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', Over the whole structure. / GROUP_MA = lgrma, On a list of mesh-cell groups. The material parameters m , {V}_{\mathrm{ref}} and the plasticity threshold are defined in DEFI_MATERIAU by the constitutive relation WEIBULL (cf. R7.02.06). Once this elementary field has been determined, the option calculates by "summation" the Weibull stress of a domain D for each defined time instant: {\sigma}_{w}(D)={(C\underset{K\in D}{\Sigma}{\sigma}_{w}^{m}(K))}^{\frac{1}{m}} where is a coefficient intended to take into account the symmetries (two- and three-dimensional case) and the thickness (in the two-dimensional case) of the structure containing the domain (keyword COEF_MULT). The failure probability of the domain D is then calculated by: {P}_{w}(D)=1-\exp(-\frac{{\sigma}_{w}^{m}}{{\sigma}_{u}^{m}}) The parameter "cleavage stress" {\sigma}_{\mu} is, likewise, defined in the constitutive relation WEIBULL. Finally, the preceding expressions of the Weibull stress and of the failure probability are valid only in the case of a monotonic loading path. This type of post-processing may nevertheless also be applied to a more general loading path, including when the cleavage stress depends on the temperature (constitutive relation WEIBULL_FO). The expressions of the Weibull stress and of the failure probability are then different (cf R7.02.06). Note: For the factor keyword WEIBULL, the model and the material field are mandatory (except if RESULTAT is present). Advice on the use of this model is given in the documentation U2.05.08. Only the time instants defined by the user by means of the keywords INST / NUME_ORDRE are taken into account in the computation of the maximum of the stresses over the history. In order to take all the time instants into account, utiliser TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI". 3.14.2 Syntax | WEIBULL = _F ( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', / GROUP_MA = lgrma, [l_gr_maille] ◊OPTION = / 'SIGM_ELGA', [DEFAUT] / 'SIGM_ELMOY', ◊ CORR_PLAST = / 'OUI', / 'NON', [DEFAUT] ◊COEF_MULT = / coef, [R] / 1., [DEFAUT] ) Simple keywords: (see [§2]) ◊MODELE = mo, [modele] ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater, [cham_mater] ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, [cara_elem] ◊ | NUME_COUCHE = | NIVE_COUCHE = ◊ MODE_FOURIER = ♦ / CHAM_GD = / RESULTAT = 3.14.3 Operands 3.14.3.1 Operand OPTION ◊ / OPTION = 'SIGM_ELGA', The value of the elementary field associated with the mesh cell K is obtained by integration by quadrature at the Gauss points of the expression \frac{1}{{V}_{p}}{\int}_{{K}_{p}}{\sigma}_{1}^{m}\mathrm{dK} . / OPTION = 'SIGM_ELMOY', The value of the elementary field associated with the mesh cell K is obtained from the maximum principal value of the tensor \frac{1}{{V}_{p}}{\int}_{{K}_{p}}\sigma \mathrm{dK} , whose value is approximated by quadrature at the Gauss points. 3.14.3.2 Operand CORR_PLAST ◊ / CORR_PLAST = 'OUI', The Weibull stress field is evaluated taking the plastic strain into account. / CORR_PLAST = 'NON', The Weibull stress field is evaluated without taking the plastic strain into account. 3.14.3.3 Operand COEF_MULT / COEF_MULT = valeur, The default value of this coefficient is 1.0 . This indicator is described in detail in the document R4.20.01. Its function and its expression are recalled here. This indicator is intended to detect whether, in the course of the history of the structure and up to the current time instant t, and for a zone of the structure chosen by the modeller, there has been a loss of proportionality of the loading (i.e. it is a matter of having a global measure of the change in the principal directions of the stress tensor for each point of the zone defined by the user). This indicator can be used only for models whose material exhibits isotropic hardening and whose elements are 2D or 3D isoparametric elements.
