u }} - 'MODE_I': This combination is available in 2D and in 3D and is written: \Delta \mathit{K1} 3.6 Operands for the operation 'COMPTAGE_CYCLES' L'opération 'COMPTAGE_CYCLES' permet de calculer les cycles liés à l'évolution d'une (ou plusieurs) quantité(s). Cette opération créée une nouvelle table, avec une colonne CYCLES et une colonne correspondant à la variation de la quantité comptée par cycle. La table en entrée peut comporter plusieurs fonds de fissure. 3.6.1 Operand NOM_PARA ♦ NOM_PARA = / nom_para, [TXT] This operand makes it possible to choose the name of the quantity on which the cycle counting is carried out. The counting may possibly be carried out on several quantities (for example \mathit{K1} , \mathit{K2} and \mathit{K3} ), provided that the same number of cycles is found for each quantity. 3.6.2 Operand COMPTAGE ♦ COMPTAGE = / 'RAINFLOW', / 'RCCM', / 'NATUREL', / 'UNITAIRE' This operand makes it possible to choose the cycle-counting method. Except for UNITAIRE counting, the command POST_FATIGUE is called. For further information on the counting methods, see the documentation R7.04.01. The input table may contain one or several time instants, but corresponding to the same crack front. UNITAIRE counting is a particular case for linear elastic analyses. In this case, the input table must contain only a single time instant and the variation of the quantity will then be determined by the operands COEF_MULT_MINI and COEF_MULT_MAXI. 3.6.3 Operand DELTA_OSCI ◊ DELTA_OSCI = / 0. [DEFAUT] / delta, [R] see documentation U4.83.01 3.6.4 Operands COEF_MULT_MINI and COEF_MULT_MAXI ♦ COEF_MULT_MINI = cmini [R] ♦ COEF_MULT_MAXI = cmaxi [R] For unit counting, the variation of the quantity to be counted is the following: \Delta q={q}_{u}(\mathit{cmaxi}-\mathit{cmini}) where q is the quantity to be counted, and {q}_{u} the unit value of this quantity (the only value contained in the input table). 3.7 Operands for the operation 'LOI_PROPA' The operation 'LOI_PROPA' creates a new column in the output table, corresponding to the unit advance (that is, for one cycle) of a crack given a fatigue propagation law. The input table may comprise several crack fronts. It may contain one or several time instants for each of the crack fronts. 3.7.1 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA = / 'DELTA_A' [DEFAUT] / nom_da, [TXT] This operand makes it possible to choose the name of the new column created. 3.7.2 Operands LOI, C, M, NOM_DELTA_K_EQ ♦ / LOI = / 'PARIS' [DEFAUT] / C = c , [R] / m = m, [R] ◊ DELTA_K_SEUIL = / 0. [DEFAUT] / val_seuil, [R] ◊ NOM_DELTA_K_EQ = / 'DELTA_K_EQ' [DEFAUT] / nom_dkeq [TXT] The operand LOI makes it possible to specify the fatigue propagation law chosen. For the moment, only Paris's law is available. This law is written:  rac{\mathit{da}}{\mathit{dN}}=\mathit{C.}{(\Delta {K}_{\mathit{eq}}-\Delta {K}_{\mathit{seuil}})}^{m} where C and m are material coefficients, supplied by the operands C and M. \Delta {K}_{\mathit{seuil}} is the propagation threshold, which can be set by the optional parameter DELTA_K_SEUIL, whose default value is 0. If \Delta {K}_{\mathit{eq}}\le \Delta {K}_{\mathit{seuil}} , then the advance is zero. The column in the input table corresponding to \Delta {K}_{\mathit{eq}} is specified by the operand NOM_DELTA_K_EQ. The unit advance is then computed ( \Delta N=1 implicitly): \Delta a=\mathit{C.}{(\Delta {K}_{\mathit{eq}}-\Delta {K}_{\mathit{seuil}})}^{m} Note: In pure mode I : \Delta {K}_{\mathit{eq}} is equal to \Delta {K}_{I} . In mixed mode, \Delta {K}_{\mathit{eq}} may be written {(\Delta K)}_{\mathit{eq}} or else \Delta ({K}_{\mathit{eq}}) , according to the conventions. These two quantities are generally different. There are, however, situations in which these two quantities are identical: - in pure mode 1 if \mathit{K1} is always positive, - in mixed mode, linearly, for a cycle (0-max) . 3.8 Operands for the operation 'CUMUL_CYCLES' The operation 'CUMUL_CYCLES' makes it possible to accumulate a quantity previously counted for each cycle by computing the mean over all the cycles. The table created contains all the columns of the initial table, except the column CYCLE. Caution: at a point of the front, the other columns of the table must not vary over the cycles. The name of the column corresponding to the quantity to be accumulated does not change. The input table may comprise several crack fronts. 3.8.1 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA = / 'DELTA_A' [DEFAUT] / nom_da, [TXT] This operand makes it possible to specify the name of the parameter on which the accumulation is carried out. By default, the accumulation is carried out on 'DELTA_A'. 3.8.2 Operand CUMUL ◊ CUMUL = 'lineaire' [DEFAUT] This operand is of no use for the moment, because the only accumulation allowed is the linear accumulation (arithmetic mean over the cycles): {q}_{\mathit{cumul}}= rac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}{q}_{i} where {q}_{i} corresponds to the value for cycle i of the quantity to be accumulated. 3.9 Operands for the operation 'PILO_PROPA' The operation 'PILO_PROPA' makes it possible to drive the propagation of several crack fronts (for the moment, limited to a single crack). The driving is done: - either by imposing the increment of the number of cycles (driving in cycles); - or by imposing the increment of maximum advance of the crack front (driving in advance). This driving takes into account all the points of all the fronts of all the cracks. The input table must contain the parameter DELTA_A. 3.9.1 Operands delta_A_max and DELTA_N ♦ / delta_A_max = da, [R] / delta_n = dn, [R] To drive the propagation in cycles, delta_n is used. This has the effect of multiplying the value of the (unit) advance by a factor \mathit{dn} for all the points of all the fronts of all the cracks. The other driving mode consists in fixing the increment of maximum advance \mathit{da} via the operand delta_A_maX. First, the point of all the fronts of all the cracks that has the greatest advance is determined. Let \mathit{damax} denote this advance. The number of cycles applied will then be  rac{\mathit{da}}{\mathit{damax}} . 3.10 Operands for the operation 'K1_NEGATIF' The operation 'K1_NEGATIF' is intended to treat the points of the front for which the stress intensity factor \mathit{K1} is negative. For these points where the values of \mathit{K1} are negative, \mathit{K1} is set to zero and the energy release rates G and/or {G}_{\mathit{IRWIN}} are recomputed by Irwin's formula. If at least one of the two energy release rates is present in the input table, the latter must also contain the parameter \mathit{K2} (and \mathit{K3} in 3D). The input table may comprise several analysis time instants and several crack fronts. 3.10.1 Operand mODELISATION ♦ MODELISATION = / '3D' / 'C_PLAN' / 'D_PLAN' / 'AXIS' This operand makes it possible to choose Irwin's formula suited to the type of modelling used. When mathit{K1} is zero, Irwin's formula is: In 3D: G= rac{1-
u \mathrm{²}}{E}\mathit{K2²}+ rac{1+
u }{E}\mathit{K3}\mathrm{²} In plane strain and for axisymmetry about the Y axis: G= rac{1-
u \mathrm{²}}{E}\mathit{K2²} In plane stress: G= rac{\mathit{K2²}}{E} where E is Young's modulus and 
u Poisson's ratio. 3.10.2 Operand mATER ♦ MATER = mat, [materiau] This operand recovers the name of the material used for the analyses. The material parameters are then used in Irwin's formula in order to recompute the energy release rate or rates. Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio must be defined as constant in time.

u4.82.05 Operator POST_K1_K2_K3 u4.82.05 Operator POST_K1_K2_K3 1 Purpose Compute the stress intensity factors in 2D and in 3D. This operator makes it possible to compute \mathit{K1} , \mathit{K2} in 2D (modellings 'D_PLAN', 'C_PLAN' and 'AXIS') and \mathit{K3} in 3D (modelling '3D') by extrapolation of the displacement jumps on the lips of the crack, cf. R7.02.08. This method is applicable only for homogeneous and isotropic materials. This operator can be used for a meshed crack as well as for an unmeshed crack (X-FEM method). In the case of a meshed crack, the latter must necessarily be plane. The method used is theoretically less accurate and more sensitive to the mesh than the computation from the bilinear form of the energy release rate and from the singular displacements, which can be used in 2D and in 3D with the option CALC_K_G of the operator CALC_G U4.82.03. It does, however, make it possible to obtain easily a good estimate of the stress intensity factors. Produces a concept of type table. 2 Syntax table = POST_K1_K2_K3( ◆ / FOND_FISS = fond_fissure, / FISSURE = fiss_xfem, ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli / evol_elas / mode_meca, ◇ MATER = mater, ◇ NB_NOEUD_COUPE = int (défaut: 5), # Si: exists("FOND_FISS") # Si: is_type("RESULTAT")!= mode_meca ◇ TYPE_MAILLAGE = / "LIBRE", / "REGLE" (par défaut), # Si: is_type("RESULTAT")== mode_meca ◇ TYPE_MAILLAGE = "REGLE", ◇ GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ SANS_GROUP_NO = grno, ◇ TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ ABSC_CURV_MAXI = float, # Si: exists("FISSURE") ◇ NB_POINT_FOND = int, ◇ NUME_FOND = int (défaut: 1), ◇ ABSC_CURV_MAXI = float, ◇ PREC_VIS_A_VIS = float (défaut: 0.1), # Si: is_type("RESULTAT")== mode_meca ◇ TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ LIST_ORDRE = listis, ◇ TOUT_MODE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ NUME_MODE = int, ◇ LIST_MODE = listis, ◇ FREQ = float, ◇ LIST_FREQ = listr8, # Si: (exists("FREQ")) or (exists("LIST_FREQ")) ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, # Si: is_type("RESULTAT")!= mode_meca ◇ TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ LIST_ORDRE = listis, ◇ INST = float, ◇ LIST_INST = listr8, # Si: (exists("INST"))or(exists("LIST_INST")) ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Case in which the operand FOND_FISS is supplied This case corresponds to an analysis on a meshed crack, defined for the post-processing with the operator DEFI_FOND_FISS. By default, the analysis is carried out automatically for all the nodes of the crack front. 3.1.1 Operands FOND_FISS / PREC_VIS_A_VIS / GROUP_NO / SANS_GROUP_NO ◊ FOND_FISS = fond, [fond_fiss] ◊ PREC_VIS_A_VIS = / 1.D-1, [DEFAUT] / epsi, [R] ◊ / TOUT = ‘OUI’, / GROUP_NO = gr_noeu, [l_gr_noeud] / SANS_GROUP_NO = gr_noeu, [l_gr_noeud] The operand FOND_FISS makes it possible to supply the concept fond_fiss (created by the command DEFI_FOND_FISS) in which the information required for the automatic search for the nodes of the two lips lying on segments normal to the crack front is stored. Caution: the concept fond_fiss must necessarily be defined such that the lips of the crack are initially stuck together (CONFIG_INIT='COLLEE' in DEFI_FOND_FISS U4.82.01). In 3D, by default, the computation of the stress intensity factors is carried out only on the vertex nodes of the mesh cells making up the crack front (hence all the nodes for the linear elements, and one node out of two for the quadratic elements). The user has the possibility of: - selecting certain vertex nodes of the crack front (keyword GROUP_NO); - excluding nodes of the crack front (keyword SANS_GROUP_NO); - carrying out the analysis on all the mid-side nodes and vertex nodes of the crack front (keyword TOUT). ◊ ABSC_CURV_MAXI = dmax [R] Maximum distance for the computation of the stress intensity factors from the crack front. In practice, the accuracy of the results is poorer if one is situated very far from the crack front R7.02.08. It is therefore advisable to choose \mathit{dmax} as small as possible (of the order of 3 to 4 elements, or else of the order of the radius of the radiating mesh, where applicable). In the case where, at a point N of the crack front, this distance is greater than the distance from the crack front at this point to the edge of the lips, the values of the stress intensity factors at the point N are obtained by constant extension. The value retained is that of the point of the crack front that is closest and for which the analysis could be carried out. The operand ABSC_CURV_MAXI is optional. When this operand is not indicated, the value of ABSC_CURV_MAXI is computed automatically from the maximum h of the sizes of the mesh cells connected to the nodes of the crack front. These mesh-cell sizes at each node of the front are computed in the command DEFI_FOND_FISS and are present in the concept fond_fiss D4.10.01. It has been chosen to take ABSC_CURV_MAXI equal to 4h . If the automatically computed value is chosen for ABSC_CURV_MAXI, one should nevertheless make sure that its value (displayed in the .mess file) is consistent with the dimensions of the structure. During the automatic search for each node of the crack front, the operator selects the nodes satisfying the following conditions: - distance R from the crack front: R ◊ ABSC_CURV_MAXI = dmax [R] Maximum distance for the computation of the stress intensity factors from the crack front. In practice, the accuracy of the results is poorer if one is situated very far from the crack front R7.02.08. It is therefore advisable to choose \mathit{dmax} as small as possible (of the order of 4 to 5 elements). In the case where, at a point N of the crack front, this distance is greater than the distance from the crack front at this point to the edge of the lips, the values of the stress intensity factors at the point N are obtained by constant extension. The value retained is that of the point of the crack front that is closest and for which the analysis could be carried out. The operand ABSC_CURV_MAXI is optional. When this operand is not indicated, the value of ABSC_CURV_MAXI is computed automatically from the maximum h of the sizes of the mesh cells connected to the nodes of the crack front. These mesh-cell sizes at each node of the front are computed in the command DEFI_FOND_FISS and are present in the concept fiss_xfem D4.10.02. It has been chosen to take ABSC_CURV_MAXI equal to 5h . If the automatically computed value is chosen for ABSC_CURV_MAXI, one should nevertheless make sure that its value (displayed in the .mess file) is consistent with the dimensions of the structure. 3.2.4 Operand NUME_FOND ◊ NUME_FOND = / 1, [DEFAUT] / numfon, [I] Several crack fronts may be defined in a single data structure of type fiss_xfem. This operand makes it possible to select the number of the front on which the analysis must be carried out. By default, only the first front is considered. 3.2.5 Operand NB_NOEUD_COUPE ◊ NB_NOEUD_COUPE = / 5, [DEFAUT] / n, [I] This operand makes it possible to define the number of nodes for projection of the displacement of the lips on each of the normal directions. The projection nodes are evenly distributed between the crack front and the distance ABSC_CURV_MAXI. 3.2.6 Operand NB_POINT_FOND ◊ NB_POINT_FOND = / nbnofo, [I] By default for an X-FEM crack, the analysis is carried out on all the points of the crack front, i.e. all the points of intersection between the crack front and the edges of the mesh. The operand NB_POINT_FOND makes it possible to fix a priori the number of post-processing points, in order to limit the run times. The nbnofo points are evenly distributed along the crack front. 3.3 Operand MATER ◊ MATER = mat, [mater] Concept of type materiau containing the elastic characteristics of the cracked material. If this optional keyword is supplied, the material mat will replace, during the execution of the command, the material used for the solution of the mechanical problem and present in the cham_mater contained in the sd_resultat (datum under the keyword RESULTAT). The material mat must be homogeneous, isotropic and linear elastic. This material must be constant (mandatory use of DEFI_MATERIAU/ELAS). The keyword MATER is to be used with caution. 3.4 Operands INST, LIST_INST, FREQ, LIST_FREQ, TOUT_ORDRE, NUME_ORDRE, LIST_ORDRE, TOUT_MODE, NUME_MODE, LIST_MODE Cf. U4.71.00. 3.5 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1, [DEFAUT] / 2, Level of messages in the message file: if INFO is equal to 2, the list of all the values computed for all the nodes treated is supplied. 3.6 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre, Title that one wishes to give to the result of the command. 4 Precautions and advice on use 4.1 Assumptions relating to the material used for the computation of the displacements The computation of the stress intensity factors by extrapolation of the displacement jumps assumes that the linear elastic characteristics of the cracked material that was used for the solution of the mechanical problem (computation of the displacement field) are known. In practice, the command POST_K1_K2_K3 automatically recovers the material concept assigned to a set of mesh cells neighbouring the crack front (for a meshed crack or for X-FEM). The material must be homogeneous, isotropic and linear elastic. This material may be constant (use of DEFI_MATERIAU/ELAS) or a function (use of DEFI_MATERIAU/ELAS_FO). The only command variables that may be used for the computation of the stress intensity factors in the case of a function material are 'TEMP' (temperature) and 'NEUT1' . Furthermore, these variables must necessarily be assigned (in AFFE_MATERIAU/AFFE_VARC) from nodal fields (cham_no). In the case of a function material, the elastic parameters are evaluated at the computation points of the crack front: - for a meshed crack (operand FOND_FISS supplied) these points are the nodes of the crack front; - for an X-FEM crack (operand FISSURE supplied), these points are either those contained in the object .FONDFISS of the data structure fiss_xfem, or those deduced from it by the use of the keyword NB_POINT_FOND. 4.2 Reminder of the various methods used for the extrapolation of the displacement jumps R7.02.08 At each node of the crack front, 3 methods (variants) are used to determine {K}_{I} , {K}_{\mathit{II}} (and {K}_{\mathit{III}} in 3D). - Method 1: for each node of the interpolation segment, the jump of the displacement field squared is computed and divided by r . Various values of \mathrm{K1} (resp. \mathrm{K2} , \mathrm{K3} ) are obtained (to within a multiplicative factor) by extrapolation at r=0 of the straight-line segments thus obtained. - Method 2: the jump of the displacement field squared is plotted as a function of r . The approximations of \mathrm{K1} are (still to within a multiplicative factor) equal to the slope of the segments connecting the origin to the various points of the curve. - Method 3: linear regression. At each node of the crack front, each method supplies a MAX value and a MIN value. At each node of the crack front, there are therefore 6 values for {K}_{I} , 6 values for {K}_{\mathit{II}} and 6 values for {K}_{\mathit{III}} (for method 3, the MIN and MAX values coincide). These values are denoted as follows, the exponent j corresponding to the number of the method: - for {K}_{I} (mode I or opening mode): {K}_{I}^{j,\mathit{MAX}},{K}_{I}^{j,\mathit{MIN}},j=1,2,3 - for {K}_{\mathit{II}} (mode \mathit{II} or in-plane shear): {K}_{\mathit{II}}^{j,\mathit{MAX}},{K}_{\mathit{II}}^{j,\mathit{MIN}},j=1,2,3 - and for {K}_{\mathit{III}} (mode \mathit{III} or anti-plane shear): {K}_{\mathit{III}}^{j,\mathit{MAX}},{K}_{\mathit{III}}^{j,\mathit{MIN}},j=1,2,3 . 4.3 Table produced The command POST_K1_K2_K3 produces a concept of type table. The table may be printed by IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. It contains, for each node of the crack front: - the values of the corresponding stress intensity factors: K1, K2 (and K3 if 3D) - the value of the energy release rate: G - estimates of the error on the stress intensity factors: ERR_K1, ERR_K2 (and ERR_K3 if 3D). The following paragraphs detail these quantities. 4.3.1 Values of the stress intensity factors The table produced contains, for each node (or point) of the crack front, the values of the stress intensity factors corresponding to the MAX values of method no. 1 (see § 4.2): \mathit{K1} ( \text{}={K}_{I}^{1,\mathit{MAX}} ), \mathit{K2} ( \text{}={K}_{\mathit{II}}^{1,\mathit{MAX}} ) In 3D, one has in addition \mathit{K3} ( \text{}={K}_{\mathit{III}}^{1,\mathit{MAX}} ) A single value of \mathit{K1} , \mathit{K2} (and \mathit{K3} if 3D) is therefore printed per node of the crack front. 4.3.2 Values of the energy release rate The table produced contains, for each node (or point) of the crack front, the value of the energy release rate G computed from the stress intensity factors by Irwin's formula. 4.3.3 Estimate of the error made on the stress intensity factors In order to evaluate the error made on the stress intensity factors at each node of the front, the discrepancy between the 6 values given by the 3 methods is evaluated (see § 4.2). This gives an absolute discrepancy concerning \mathit{K1} , \mathit{K2} (and \mathit{K3} if 3D). In order to obtain a relative discrepancy that is easier to interpret, the absolute discrepancies are normalised by a value K which is the maximum value of all the K at this node of the crack front. More precisely, the error made on {K}_{i}(i=1,2,3) , i being the loading mode of the crack and j the number of the method, is defined in the following manner: \mathit{erreur}({K}_{i})=\frac{\underset{j=1,2,3}{max}({K}_{i}^{j,\mathit{MAX}}-{K}_{i}^{j,\mathit{MIN}})}{K} , with K=\underset{j=1,2,3}{max}({K}_{I}^{j,\mathit{MAX}},{K}_{\mathit{II}}^{j,\mathit{MAX}},{K}_{\mathit{III}}^{j,\mathit{MAX}}) The errors on \mathit{K1} , \mathit{K2} (and \mathit{K3} if 3D) are printed in the table: ERR_K1, ERR_K2 (and ERR_K3 if 3D) for each node of the crack front. 4.4 Additional printouts If INFO is equal to 2, all the intermediate computations are displayed in the message file. It is pointed out that the column entitled SAUT_DX (resp. SAUT_DY and SAUT_DZ) in the tables of the message file corresponds to the displacement jump along the axis \mathit{X1} (respectively \mathit{X2} and \mathit{X3} ), multiplied by a coefficient depending on the material, the whole squared R7.02.08. 4.5 Precautions and advice The assumptions necessary for the validity of this method are: 1. the crack must be sufficiently regular (that is, the front and the lips do not present a geometric singularity); 2. the constitutive behaviour must be elastic, linear, isotropic and homogeneous; 3. the structure must be isothermal (or, at the very least, the temperature gradients on the lips may be neglected in the interpolation zone). The method used is theoretically less accurate and more sensitive to the mesh than the singular-displacement method R7.02.05. In general, one may advise comparing, in the studies, the results of POST_K1_K2_K3 and those of CALC_G U4.82.03, which is a good indicator of the quality of the result obtained. Advice in the case of a meshed crack: the mesh should preferably be quadratic and comprise enough nodes perpendicularly to the crack front. Furthermore, the results are markedly improved if, in the case where the mesh is composed of quadratic elements, the mid-side nodes (of the edges that touch the crack front) are moved to the quarter of these edges, bringing them closer to the crack front. This is made possible by the keyword MODI_MAILLE (option 'NOEUD_QUART') of the command MODI_MAILLAGE U4.23.04. The computation by interpolation of the displacement jumps requires at least 3 nodes on the normal to the crack front. If the number of nodes is not sufficient, an alarm is issued and the rows corresponding to this node of the front are set to 0 in the result table. The analysis then continues, where applicable, for the next node of the crack front. In this case one may: - either increase the maximum curvilinear abscissa ABSC_CURV_MAXI in order to look for nodes further from the crack front; - or increase the parameter PREC_VIS_A_VIS (and possibly PREC_NORM in DEFI_FOND_FISS), which amounts to being less demanding in the selection of the nodes for the analysis. Advice in the case of an unmeshed crack: the accuracy of the method is sensitive to the choice of the enrichment zone of the X-FEM method (parameter RAYON_ENRI of DEFI_FISS_XFEM). Ideally, the enrichment radius and the maximum curvilinear abscissa ABSC_CURV_MAXI are of the order of three times the size of the smallest edge of the mesh. Analyses are possible on a non-plane crack, but the user must make sure that it remains sufficiently regular for the analysis assumptions to be valid: there must not be a geometric singularity on the front or on the lips. Typically, the analysis is admissible for an axisymmetric crack, but not for a corner. The computation by interpolation of the displacement jumps requires at least 3 nodes on the normal to the crack front. The number of interpolation points is normally equal to NB_NOEUD_COUPE but may be smaller in one case: - if the geometry of the front and of the structure is such that part of the interpolation points leaves the material. In this case ABSC_CURV_MAXI must be reduced (while remaining consistent with the fineness of the mesh) and/or NB_NOEUD_COUPE increased. The analyses are fairly demanding in time and in memory if there are many points on the crack front. The use of the keyword NB_POINT_FOND makes it possible to limit the post-processing to a certain number of points evenly distributed along the front (for example some twenty points is often sufficient). 5 Example 1: ruled mesh Circular crack in a 3D block (test SSLV134D). MA = LIRE_MAILLAGE() LEVINF1, LEVINFS are the groups containing the surface mesh cells located on the upper and lower lips of the crack. The associated node groups are created: MA = DEFI_GROUP ( MAILLAGE = MA, CREA_GROUP_NO =_F( GROUP_MA=( 'LEVINF1', 'LEVINFS',) ) Displacement of the nodes to the quarter of the edges: MA = MODI_MAILLAGE( MAILLAGE = MA, reuse = MA, MODI_MAILLE =_F( OPTION = 'NOEUD_QUART', GROUP_MA_FOND = 'LFF1', ) ) Analysis with MECA_STATIQUE... FISS = DEFI_FOND_FISS ( MAILLAGE = MA, FOND_FISS = _F ( GROUP_MA = 'LFF1', GROUP_NO_ORIG = 'NFF1', GROUP_NO_EXTR = 'NFF2', ), LEVRE_SUP = _F ( GROUP_MA = 'LEVINFS' ), LEVRE_INF = _F ( GROUP_MA = 'LEVINF1' ), DTAN_ORIG = ( 1. , 0. , 0. ), DTAN_EXTR = ( 0. , 1. ,0. ) PREC_NORM = 0.1, ) TABK1K3 = POST_K1_K2_K3 ( INFO=2, FOND_FISS = FISS, RESULTAT = RESU1, ABSC_CURV_MAXI = 0.539, PREC_VIS_A_VIS = 0.1, ) 6 Example 2: free mesh In 3D, if the mesh is not ruled at the crack front, there may not be enough nodes on directions normal to the front for the interpolation. In this case, the option TYPE_MAILLAGE=’LIBRE’ must be used. With this option, the principle of the analysis is the following 1. determination of the directions normal to the crack front for each node of the front, 2. definition, on each of these directions, of NB_NOEUD_COUPE points, evenly distributed between the front and the distance ABSC_CURV_MAXI, 3. projection of the displacement of each lip onto these nodes and interpolation of the displacement jump. The option TYPE_MAILLAGE=’LIBRE’ is not available in 2D. The only case in which it could be of use is the case of nodes that do not coincide between the two lips. Figure 6a: Free mesh of the crack lips – Definition of the projection points TABK = POST_K1_K2_K3 ( INFO=2, TYPE_MAILLAGE = ‘LIBRE’, FOND_FISS = FISS, RESULTAT = RESU_MECA, ABSC_CURV_MAXI = 0.539, NB_NOEUD_COUPE = 5, )

u4.82.06 Operator RECA_WEIBULL u4.82.06 Operator RECA_WEIBULL 1 Purpose Calibrate the parameters of the WEIBULL model on experimental data. These data consist of one (or several) list(s) of failure time instants determined experimentally, associated with one (or several) result concept(s) of STAT_NON_LINE modelling the tests at these various time instants. The WEIBULL modulus, or the cleavage stress (possibly depending on the temperature), or else both of these parameters, may be calibrated. The maximum-likelihood method or linear regression R7.02.09 is used for this calibration. Produces a data structure of type table. 2 Syntax table = RECA_WEIBULL( ◆ LIST_PARA = / "SIGM_REFE", / "M", ◆ RESU = _F( ◆ EVOL_NOLI = evol_noli, ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ TEMPE = float, ◆ LIST_INST_RUPT = float, ◇ / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = int, / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, # Si: exists("INST") or exists("LIST_INST") ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF') ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU') ◆ PRECISION = float, ◆ | TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), | GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ COEF_MULT = float (défaut: 1.0), ), ◇ OPTION = / "SIGM_ELGA" (par défaut), / "SIGM_ELMOY", ◇ CORR_PLAST = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ METHODE = / "MAXI_VRAI" (par défaut), / "REGR_LINE", ◇ INCO_GLOB_RELA = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ ITER_GLOB_MAXI = int (défaut: 10), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand LIST_PARA ♦ LIST_PARA / 'M', / 'SIGM_REFE', List of the parameters of the Weibull model for which calibration is requested ( m , {\sigma}_{u} or both). 3.2 Keyword RESU 3.2.1 Operand EVOL_NOLI ♦ EVOL_NOLI = resu, Name of a result concept of type evol_noli. 3.2.2 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo, Name of the model on which the calibration is carried out. 3.2.3 Operand CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER = chmat, Name of the material field assigned to the model. It must necessarily contain the initial value of the parameters of the Weibull method (keyword WEIBULL of DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01), namely: | {V}_{0} | : reference volume | | --- | --- | | m | : exponent of the Weibull statistical law | | {\sigma}_{u} | : cleavage stress | 3.2.4 Operand TEMPE ◊ TEMPE = temp, Temperature associated with the result resu. If it is supplied, the cleavage stress {\sigma}_{u} will be calibrated for each result. 3.2.5 Operand LIST_INST_RUPT ♦ LIST_INST_RUPT = lreel, List of the failure time instants of the result database resu at which the Weibull stresses will be computed (these time instants are interpolated if they do not coincide with the time instants of the result resu). This list of time instants must be strictly increasing and contain at least two time instants. The minimum time instant (respectively maximum) of this list must of course necessarily be greater (resp. smaller) than the minimum time instant (resp. maximum) of the list of time instants of the result resu. 3.2.6 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA The analysis domain or domains are specified by: ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', A single domain is defined and it coincides with the whole structure. / GROUP_MA = lgrma, Each mesh-cell group of the list lgrma defines an analysis domain. 3.2.7 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE selection of the analysis time instants at which the Weibull stresses are to be interpolated at the time instants given by LIST_INST_RUPT see TOUT_ORDRE, NUME_ORDRE, LIST_ORDRE, INST, LIST_INST in U4.71.00 Aster first computes the Weibull stresses for all the time instants given by TOUT_ORDRE/ NUME_ORDRE/ INST/LIST_INST; it then interpolates the Weibull stresses at the time instants given by LIST_INST_RUPT. 3.2.8 Operand COEF_MULT ◊ COEF_MULT = coef, Multiplicative coefficient of the m-th power of the Weibull stress, intended to take symmetries of the domain into account (the default value is 1. cf. POST_ELEM U4.81.22). 3.3 Operand OPTION / OPTION = 'SIGM_ELGA', The elementary field of the maximum principal stress is computed from the representation of the stress field at the Gauss points. / OPTION = 'SIGM_ELMOY', The elementary field of the maximum principal stress is computed from the representation of the stress field averaged with respect to the Gauss points. 3.4 Operand CORR_PLAST / CORR_PLAST = 'OUI', The Weibull stress field is evaluated with the plastic correction. / CORR_PLAST = 'NON', The Weibull stress field is evaluated without plastic correction. 3.5 Operand METHODE / METHODE = 'MAXI_VRAI', The calibration method used is that of maximum likelihood. / METHODE = 'REGR_LINE', The calibration method used is that of linear regression. 3.6 Keyword INCO_GLOB_RELA ◊ INCO_GLOB_RELA = / increl, [R] / 1.E-3, [DEFAUT] The calibration algorithm continues the iterations if: \max(∣\frac{{m}_{k+1}-{m}_{k}}{{m}_{k}}∣;\underset{T}{\max}(∣\frac{{\sigma}_{u(k+1)}(T)-{\sigma}_{u(k)}(T)}{{\sigma}_{u(k)}(T)}∣))>\mathrm{increl} 3.7 Keyword ITER_GLOB_MAXI ◊ ITER_GLOB_MAXI = / maglob, [R] / 10, [DEFAUT] Maximum number of calibration iterations carried out. 3.8 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Indicates the printout level of the results of the operator, | 1: | no printout, | | --- | --- | | 2: | printout of the information relating to the calibration. | The printouts are made in the file 'MESSAGE'. 4 Example of use For the use of RECA_WEIBULL, one may refer to the test case SSNA103 V6.01.103. u4.82.07 Operator POST_KCP correction β u4.82.07 Operator POST_KCP correction β 1 Purpose Harmfulness assessment of a defect by the Kcp β-correction method for a semi-elliptical defect located under the cladding of pressurised-water reactor vessels. The objective of this method is to evaluate, on a sound mesh (without a meshed defect) and in post-processing of a mechanical study (axisymmetric or 3D) in linear elasticity, the elastic-plastic stress intensity factor at each of the two tips of the defect, that is at the tip on the cladding side and at the tip on the base-metal side. The quantities obtained as output of this method can then be used to determine subsequently the margin factors with respect to fracture, by comparison with the critical toughness of the fracture mode considered at the defect tip under consideration. POST_KCP first computes the elastic stress intensity factors at the two tips of the defect, using the stresses at the nodes obtained from the mechanical solution and the residual stresses given by the user. Then, in a second step, the operator computes the plastically corrected stress intensity factor from its elastic equivalent by the so-called “β correction” method. This method is specific to underclad defects stuck to the interface and makes it possible to take into account the influence on the defect of the plastification phenomenon occurring at the tip on the cladding side and at the tip on the base-metal side R7.02.10. Produces a concept of type table_sdaster. 2 Syntax table = POST_KCP( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ MATER_REV = mater, ◆ EPAIS_REV = float, ◆ MATER_MDB = mater, ◆ EPAIS_MDB = float, ◆ UNITE_LONGUEUR = / "M" (par défaut), / "MM", ◆ FISSURE = _F( ◇ FORM_FISS = / "SEMI_ELLIPTIQUE", / "BANDE", # Si: equal_to("FORM_FISS", 'SEMI_ELLIPTIQUE') ◆ LONGUEUR = float, ◆ CORRECTION = / "BETA_3D" (par défaut), / "BETA_2D", ◆ PROFONDEUR = float, ◆ ORIENTATION = / "CIRC", / "LONGI", ), ◆ K1D = _F( ◆ TABL_MECA= table, ◆ TABL_THER = table, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands The operator POST_KCP may be used within axisymmetric or three-dimensional modellings. In the figure below we present a schematic of a vessel slice with a semi-elliptical defect present. Semi-elliptical defect located under the cladding 3.1 Operand MODELE Concept of type modele. 3.2 Operand MATER_REV Name of the concept of type materiau defining the material that constitutes the cladding. Required in order to recover: - Young's modulus, for the computation of the influence coefficients (semi-elliptical defect), - the elastic limits, for the plastic correction of the stress intensity factors. 3.3 Operand EPAIS_REV Thickness of the cladding. Required for: - the computation of the stress intensity factors in the case of the influence-coefficient method (semi-elliptical defect) - the plastic correction. 3.4 Operand MATER_MDB Name of the concept of type materiau defining the material that constitutes the base metal. Required in order to recover Young's modulus, for the computation of the influence coefficients (semi-elliptical defect). 3.5 Operand EPAIS_MDB Thickness of the base metal, required for the correction of the stress intensity factors by the influence-coefficient method (semi-elliptical defect). 3.6 Operand UNITE_LONGUEUR Makes it possible to use the millimetre as the unit of length. If the user specifies UNITE_LONGUEUR = “MM” in the command POST_KCP, this means that the user wishes to handle length units in millimetres, and the command POST_KCP carries out the transformation of the units. 3.7 Keyword FISSURE Factor keyword for the geometric characterisation of the defect. It can be used only once. 3.7.1 Operand FORM_FISS | Shape of the defect: | 'BANDE' for a band defect a/c = 0, | | --- | --- | | | 'SEMI_ELLIPTIQUE' for a semi-elliptical defect, | 3.7.2 Operand CORRECTION | CORRECTION: | 'beta_2d' for a band defect, | | --- | --- | | | 'beta_3d' for a semi-elliptical defect, | 3.7.3 Operand LONGUEUR Second dimension of the defect (axial or circumferential according to the orientation of the defect) in SI units. 3.7.4 Operand PROFONDEUR Radial dimension of the defect in SI units. 3.7.5 Operand ORIENTATION | Characterisation of the orientation of the defect: | 'CIRC' for a circumferential defect, | | --- | --- | | | 'LONGI' for a longitudinal defect. | 3.8 Keyword K1D Factor keyword for the characterisation of the thermomechanical transient. This keyword may be repeated. 3.8.1 Operands TABL_MECA The table TABL_MECA is mandatory. It supplies the transient of the stresses undergone by the vessel during the loading history, respectively on the cladding side (of tip A of the defect: interface between the cladding and the base metal) and on the base-metal side (at tip B of the defect). The parameters common to these tables that are required are: - 'INST'[R], - 'ABSC_CURV'[R] - 'COOR_X'[R], - 'COOR_Y'[R] - 'COOR_Z'[R] (in 3D) - 'SIXX'[R] (in 3D with 'LONGI'), - 'SIYY'[R] (in 3D with 'LONGI' or in 2D with 'CIRC'), - 'SIXY'[R] (in 3D with 'LONGI'), - 'SIZZ'[R] (in 2D with 'LONGI' or in 3D with 'CIRC'). The reader is invited to consult the documentation of the commands POST_RELEVE_T U4.81.21 and MACR_LIGN_COUPE [U4.81,13] for further information on the meaning of the parameters. The macro-command MACR_LIGN_COUPE must be used with the keywords TYPE='SEGMENT' and NB_POINTS=5. The influence-coefficient method requires the evaluation of a polynomial of degree 5 representing the evolution of the stress normal to the segment representing the crack R7.02.10. The macro-command MACR_LIGN_COUPE allows the user to define the locations at which the stress is recorded, independently of the mesh used during the thermomechanical study. 3.8.2 Operand TABL_THER Table supplying the thermal transient in the vessel during the loading history from tip A to tip B. The required parameters of this table are: - 'INST'[R], - 'ABSC_CURV'[R], - 'TEMP'[R]. The reader is invited to consult the documentation of the commands POST_RELEVE_T U4.81.21 and MACR_LIGN_COUPE U4.81.13 for further information on the meaning of the parameters. 4 Table produced The u4.82.08 Operator DEFI_FISS_XFEM u4.82.08 Operator DEFI_FISS_XFEM 1 Purpose Define a 2D or 3D crack or interface by means of level-set functions. For cracks, two level-set functions are defined, making it possible to characterise an arbitrary crack (plane or not). For interfaces, a single level set is necessary. The level sets may be defined in four different ways: - either from two mesh-cell groups (the mesh-cell group of the crack and the mesh-cell group of the crack front); - or from two analytical functions. - or from a catalogue of predefined shapes. - or by rereading already existing nodal fields. For the 2D case, the mesh cells of the crack front are POI mesh cells; they must not be given as a node group but as a mesh-cell group. For the 3D case, the crack front is oriented automatically. The ordered list of the points of the front is displayed automatically in the message file, when the command DEFI_FISS_XFEM is passed through. The orientation method, and the specific case in which it does not work, are described in the documentation R7.02.12. This operator does not make it possible to define a crack coinciding with an edge of the structure. The characteristics linked to contact on the lips of the crack are not given here but in a specific contact load with the operator DEFI_CONTACT. Cohesive forces between the lips of the crack may also be defined, by this same operator. The crack is then generally declared as being of type COHESIF. The theoretical aspect of the X-FEM method is dealt with in R7.02.12, and the user who is not familiar with the use of level sets is advised to read the few explanatory lines relating to the representation of surfaces by the level-set method. Furthermore, this operator is also used with meshed cracks, prior to the computation of the stress intensity factors in 3D by the operator CALC_G U4.82.03 with the option CALC_K_G. The operator produces a concept of type fiss_xfem. 2 Syntax fiss_xfem = DEFI_FISS_XFEM( ◇ TYPE_DISCONTINUITE = / "FISSURE" (par défaut), / "INTERFACE", / "COHESIF", ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ / MAILLAGE_GRILLE = maillage, / FISS_GRILLE = fiss_xfem, #
