Si: (not exists("RAYON_ENRI")) ◇ NB_COUCHES = int (défaut: 2), # Si: (not exists("MAILLAGE_GRILLE")) and (not exists("FISS_GRILLE")) ◇ JONCTION = _F( ◆ FISSURE = fiss_xfem, ◆ POINT = float, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, / 3, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE ♦ MAILLAGE = ma ma: name of the mesh on which the crack is to be defined. This mesh is necessarily a 2D or 3D mesh. Caution: the quadratic X-FEM elements lack robustness (especially in 3D); it is advisable to use linear X-FEM elements. It is therefore preferable that ma be a linear mesh. 3.2 Definition of a grid to be associated with the crack An auxiliary grid may be associated with the crack: - either by giving a grid mesh (see § 3.2.1), - or by giving a crack already associated with a previous grid (see § 3.2.2), In the case of use of the upwind method in PROPA_FISS (document U4.82.11), its use is almost mandatory. This keyword is typically used following a refinement by Homard of the mesh on which the crack was defined. 3.2.1 Operand MAILLAGE_GRILLE ◊ MAILLAGE_GRILLE = magri [maillage] magri: name of the grid mesh to be associated with the crack This operand is used to associate the grid mesh magri with the crack. The two level-set functions and their gradients are computed both on the mesh ma given by MAILLAGE (see § 3.1) and on the mesh magri according to the method chosen by DEFI_FISS (see § 3.4), and they are stored with the crack. Several cracks may therefore be defined on the same grid magri. The mesh magri is created by the operator DEFI_GRILLE U4.24.02. The auxiliary grid used must extend only over the zone planned for propagation of the crack, so as to be able to represent the crack front correctly throughout the propagation simulation. It may lie partly outside the mesh ma (keyword MAILLAGE, see § 3.1) and no relationship exists between this mesh and that of the grid magri. In the presence of several cracks and with a different grid used for each, the grids are independent and may overlap partly or totally. In this case a single grid could also be used for all the cracks. 3.2.2 Operand FISS_GRILLE In the case where a crack has been defined on a mesh with an associated grid and where one wishes to redefine it on another mesh without changing the grid, computing time can be saved by avoiding recomputing the level-set functions on the grid. Indeed, in this case the level-set functions defined on the grid do not change. This is always the case when Homard is used on the mesh on which the crack was defined, because the grid is not affected by the modifications of Homard and the level-set functions defined initially do not change. The same crack can therefore be redefined on the refined mesh with the same associated grid, by computing the level-set functions only on the mesh and keeping them identical on the grid. ◊ FISS_GRILLE = fiss_orig, [fiss_xfem] The crack fiss_orig that was defined previously is specified. The grid already present is associated with the new crack and the computed nodal fields that define the level-set functions and their gradients are copied onto the grid for the new crack. This is equivalent to defining the crack fiss_orig on the new mesh while still using the same grid. Note: No check can be made of the consistency between the crack that is going to be defined by DEFI_FISS (see § 3.4 ) and that which was defined on the grid of fiss_orig. 3.3 Operand TYPE_DISCONTINUITE ◊ TYPE_DISCONTINUITE = / 'FISSURE', [DEFAUT] / 'COHESIF' / 'INTERFACE' By default, a crack is defined. It is however possible to define an interface (in order to treat the case of 2 solids in contact, or of under-thicknesses, …). In the case where TYPE_DISCONTINUITE = 'FISSURE', the data structure produced is enriched with two tables named 'FOND_FISS' and 'NB_FOND_FISS', which can be recovered using the command RECU_TABLE. The table 'NB_FOND_FISS' contains a single value corresponding to the number of crack fronts. The table therefore contains a single column (named NOMBRE) and a single row. The table 'FOND_FISS' contains the list of the coordinates of the points of all the crack fronts. This table has 6 columns: - the first column ('NUME_FOND') corresponds to the number of the crack front, - the next column ('NUM_PT') corresponds to the number of the point of the crack front; this number is local to the current crack front, - the next column ('ABSC_CURV') corresponds to the value of the curvilinear abscissa along the current crack front, - the next 3 columns ('COOR_X', 'COOR_Y' and 'COOR_Z') correspond to the coordinates of the point. The discontinuity type COHESIF makes it possible to have information on the propagation front (because of the data mentioned previously and the second level-set function) in order to transmit it to algorithms for propagation or for tracking of the cracked surface. On the other hand, unlike the type FISSURE, it does not contain information linked to a tip enrichment, since the latter has no reason to exist in the presence of cohesive forces. Indeed, it is important to note that for the discontinuity type COHESIF, the propagation front does not coincide with the end of the Heaviside enrichment, which may cross the whole structure. The initial front must therefore be given independently, by the keyword GROUP_MA_BORD. 3.4 Keyword DEFI_FISS ♦ DEFI_FISS = _F The factor keyword DEFI_FISS makes it possible to define a crack or an interface in 4 different ways: - either from two mesh-cell groups (see § 3.4.1); - or from two analytical functions (see § 3.4.2); - or from a catalogue of predefined shapes (see § 3.4.3); - or from existing fields (see § 3.4.4). 3.4.1 Definition of the crack by mesh-cell groups If one has a crack (or an interface) that is already meshed, then the crack can be defined by giving two mesh-cell groups: GROUP_MA_FISS and GROUP_MA_FOND. This mesh may be independent of the mesh of the structure. > / ♦ GROUP_MA_FISS = grma . with grma a single mesh-cell group. This mesh-cell group corresponds to only one of the lips of the crack (lower or upper lip). This mesh-cell group must be oriented. In the case of lips that would not be perfectly stuck together, favouring one side will have a slight influence on the local basis of the crack front, an influence that is all the greater as the angle between the two lips is large. For the 2D case, the program sorts the mesh cells of GROUP_MA_FISS so as to have a group of contiguous mesh cells whatever the starting group. It is therefore not necessary to give a mesh-cell group whose members follow one another. > ◊ GROUP_MA_FOND = grma with grma a single mesh-cell group. This operand serves to define the crack front. For interfaces, GROUP_MA_FOND is not to be supplied. In 2D, GROUP_MA_FOND is a group of point mesh cells. 3.4.2 Definition of the crack by analytical functions The main interest of this operator is the possibility of defining a crack without the latter necessarily being meshed. In this case, the crack is defined by means of two level-set functions. The first level set (called the “normal” level set) is the one that makes it possible to characterise the surface of the crack. FONC_LN is therefore supplied with a real function of X , Y and Z defined beforehand by the operator FORMULE. The surface of the crack will then be the zero iso-value of this function. The second level set (called the “tangent” level set) is the one that makes it possible to characterise the crack front. FONC_LT is therefore supplied with a real function of X , Y and Z defined beforehand by the operator FORMULE. The trace of the zero iso-value of FONC_LT in the cracking plane is the crack front. The points of the crack are then characterised by FONC_LN = 0 and FONC_LT / ♦ FONC_LN = fonc, . with fonc a function or a formula defined beforehand. > ◊ FONC_LT = fonc, . with fonc a function or a formula defined beforehand. Note: For a crack, it is essential that the level sets be the true distance functions; one therefore cannot define an elliptical crack by: LN=FORMULE(NOM_PARA=('X','Y','Z'),VALE=’Z-H’) LT=FORMULE(NOM_PARA=('X','Y','Z'),VALE=’(X/a)²+(Y/b)²-1’) where a and b would be the semi-major axis and the semi-minor axis of the ellipse. Indeed, the function LT is not the distance to the ellipse. The distance function to an ellipse cannot be expressed by means of the usual functions. In order to introduce such a crack, the 3rd method must be used: the predefined shapes. For interfaces, any level-set function is possible, and it is not useful to introduce the true distance function. Note: To date nothing would forbid having a level set that defines several closed crack fronts (for example several cracks of “penny-shaped” type). Under these conditions, a call to DEFI_FISS_XFEM could then define several cracks. This possibility is forbidden: each command DEFI_FISS_XFEM defines only a single crack. It is therefore not possible to define several closed fronts OR one closed front plus one or several open fronts. Note: Beware of the sign of FONC_LT; always remember that the crack is defined on the side FONC_LT / N, [I] If RAYON_ENRI is not supplied (and TYPE_ENRI_FOND = ‘GEOMETRIQUE’), then NB_COUCHES is the number of layers of elements to be enriched (2 by default). The use of a large number of layers affects only the computing cost, particularly in 3D. 3.8 Operand JONCTION # Si MAILLAGE_GRILLE = None, ◊ JONCTION = _F ( ♦ FISSURE = (fiss1, fiss2, …,fissi), [l_fiss_xfem] ♦ POINT = (Px , Py , Pz), [l_R] This operand makes it possible to define one or several junctions between a crack and other already existing cracks. These other cracks are then considered as mother cracks: they must already have been defined beforehand by calls to DEFI_FISS_XFEM. A list of mother cracks is supplied in the keyword FISSURE. All these mother cracks will be taken into account when the current crack is defined. The keyword POINT must be given in the domain in which one wishes the crack to be defined. An example is provided in figure 3.7-a. It is considered in this figure that crack 3 was defined initially so as to cut the domain vertically. The keyword JONCTION is introduced in order to connect it to cracks 1 and 2. The three configurations of the figure can be obtained according to the choice of the position given in the keyword POINT. Figure 3.8-1: Example of definition of the crack fiss3, for the mother cracks \mathit{fiss1} and \mathit{fiss2} , as a function of the point (\mathit{px},\mathit{py}) chosen. Care must be taken when the operand JONCTION is used: the crack will then no longer be represented only by its normal and tangent level sets, but it will also depend on the mother cracks. This may pose a problem if one wishes to use operators such as RAFF_XFEM, which accept only the definition of a crack by level sets. Likewise the graphical representation of the zero iso-value of the level sets is not sufficient; it is preferable to go through the post-processing operations via the operator POST_MAIL_XFEM. An example of configuration is presented. In this example the cracks onto which another crack connects are identified. Thus for the crack N=3 , one has K=2 where K is the set of the cracks onto which 3 connects. Likewise for the crack N=5 , one deduces K=[3,4] . Crack 5 is therefore defined from the operand jonction and from the two cracks 3 and 4. Crack 3 is itself defined beforehand from the operand jonction acting on crack 2, itself defined from the operand jonction acting on crack 1. The hierarchy tree therefore serves to establish the order of definition of the various cracks (2 from 1, 3 from 2, 4 from 1 and 5 from 3 and 4). Figure 3.8-2 : Network of cracks on the left, hierarchy tree on the right indicating what connects to what and making it possible to establish the order relations for the crack definitions and the use of the operand JONCTION . The junction operator makes it possible to establish an order relation for a mesh cell that sees N cracks. The two hierarchy trees on the right will thus be distinguished. In the rightmost tree, cracks 1 and 2 are close enough for a mesh cell seeing crack 3 also to see cracks 1 and 2: it is therefore decided to connect crack 3 to cracks 2 and 1, but also to use the operand junction to indicate that crack 2 is connected to crack 1. For the other tree, a mesh cell sees at most 2 cracks (no mesh cell then sees cracks 1, 2 and 3 at the same time) and in this case crack 3 simply connects to cracks 2 and 1, which are no longer connected to each other. Figure 3.8-3 : Network of cracks on the left, hierarchy trees on the right. The rightmost hierarchy tree indicates that crack 2 cannot be defined independently of crack 1 because it is too close to the latter (a mesh cell seeing crack 3 then also sees cracks 1 and 2). 3.9 Operand INFO | / 1 : | printout in the file 'MESSAGE' 1. of the number of points of the crack front; 2. of the number of crack fronts; 3. of the ordered list of the coordinates of the points of the front as well as their curvilinear abscissa, for each crack front. | | --- | --- | | / 2 : | same printouts as 1 + printouts 1. of the number of level sets readjusted; 2. of the number of mesh cells of the crack zone; 3. of the number of mesh cells containing the crack front 4. of the number of mesh cells of Heaviside, Crack-tip and Heaviside Crack-tip type. | | / 3 : | same printout as 2 + printouts 1. of the steps of the analysis; 2. of the level-set fields and of their gradients; 3. of the status of the nodes; 4. of the numbers of the enriched mesh cells. | 4 Examples 4.1 With analytical formulae LN = FORMULE ( NOM_PARA=('X','Y','Z'),VALE= ’Z-12.5’) LT = FORMULE ( NOM_PARA=('X','Y','Z'),VALE= ’X-10’.) FISS= DEFI_FISS_XFEM ( MAILLAGE = MAILLAIN, DEFI_FISS =_F( FONC_LT = LT, FONC_LN = LN, ), GROUP_MA_ENRI = 'VOL', INFO=2, ) 4.2 With mesh-cell groups FISS= DEFI_FISS_XFEM ( MAILLAGE = MAILLAIN, DEFI_FISS =_F( GROUP_MA_FISS = ’LEVSUP’, GROUP_MA_FOND = ’FONFIS’,), GROUP_MA_ENRI = 'VOL', INFO=3, ) 4.3 With the catalogue of predefined shapes Case of a cylindrical crack: FISS=DEFI_FISS_XFEM(MAILLAGE = MAILLAIN, DEFI_FISS=_F( FORM_FISS = 'CYLINDRE', DEMI_GRAND_AXE = r, DEMI_PETIT_AXE = r, CENTRE = (0., l_fiss ,0.), VECT_X = (0., 0. ,1.), VECT_Y = (1., 0. ,0.), ), GROUP_MA_ENRI='VOL', INFO=1, ); Case of a crack defined by a half-plane: FISS=DEFI_FISS_XFEM(MAILLAGE = MAILLAIN, INFO=1, DEFI_FISS=_F( FORM_FISS = 'DEMI_PLAN', PFON =(0. , 5. ,15.), NORMALE =(0. , 0. , 1.), DTAN =(0. ,-1. , 0.)), GROUP_MA_ENRI='VOL');

u4.82.09 Macro-command CALC_GP u4.82.09 Macro-command CALC_GP 1 Purpose The purpose of this macro-command is to compute, in post-processing of a non-linear elastoplastic mechanical analysis, the energetic fracture-mechanics parameter called {G}_{P} . The energy approach based on this criterion is detailed in the document R7.02.16. This macro-command can be used in 2D and in 3D. In 2D, it makes it possible to use the approach with a specific mesh dedicated to the approach (presence of groups of elements forming particular zones called chips) or a sufficiently fine free mesh in which the zones are built by the macro-command. It is important to point out that In 3D, only a specific mesh dedicated to the approach, comprising groups of elements forming slices of several chips, can be used. The macro-command returns a table containing, for each requested analysis time instant: - the name of the analysis zone (chip) ZONE - the elastic energy, modified or not, in the zone (ENER_ELTR for a chip mesh or ENER_ELAS for a free mesh), - the length of the zone (or the area in 3D) DELTA_L - the parameter GP - an indicator specifying the location of the maximum at each time instant MAX_INST The user may also request a reduced table in which only the rows corresponding to the maximum at each time instant are given. In the case where the user has used the automatic construction of the chip zones, a field may be requested as output, making it possible to visualise the zones and to check that they are correctly defined. 2 Syntax / cham_elem / table = CALC_GP( ◆ RESULTAT = resultat, ◆ LIST_INST = listr8, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF", / "ABSOLU" (par défaut), ◆ / TRANCHE_2D = _F( ◆ ZONE_MAIL = / "NON", / "OUI", # Si: equal_to("ZONE_MAIL", 'OUI') ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ TAILLE = listr8, # Si: equal_to("ZONE_MAIL", 'NON') ◆ CENTRE = float, ◆ RAYON = float, ◆ ANGLE = float, ◆ TAILLE = float, ◆ NB_ZONE = int, ◇ CHAMP_VISU = co, ), / TRANCHE_3D = _F( ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ), # Si: exists("TRANCHE_2D") ◆ SYME = / "NON", / "OUI", # Si: exists("TRANCHE_3D") ◆ FOND_FISS = fond_fissure, ◇ GPMAX = co, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Energetic elastoplastic fracture model Gp The energetic model for predicting fracture in elastoplasticity is described in more detail in the reference documentation R7.02.16. The aim of this model is to estimate the critical loading for cleavage initiation in an elastoplastic structure; it therefore represents a deterministic alternative to the models based on principal-stress levels, namely Beremin or Bordet (also available in Code_Aster ). The model is based on a representation of the defect by a notch; the principle of minimising the potential energy of the structure with respect to the advance of the defect alone finally leads to a criterion on the mean elastic energy present in particular zones C(l) downstream of the notch and commonly called chips. The Figure presents a definition of these zones, which are therefore measured from the notch root up to a distance l ; {L}_{C} here represents the diameter of the notch. Figure 3-1- Definition of the zone of interest. The cleavage criterion is then written: (\exists l>0)\tilde{{G}_{P}}(l)\ge {G}_{\mathit{PC}} with \tilde{{G}_{P}}\left(l\right)=\frac{{\int}_{C\left(l\right)}{\Phi}_{\mathit{el}}^{\mathit{traction}}d\Omega }{l} , where {\Phi}_{\mathit{el}}^{\mathit{traction}}=\frac{\lambda}{2}H(\mathit{tr}(ϵ))\mathit{tr}{(ϵ)}^{2}+\mu \sum_{i=1}^{3}H({ϵ}_{i}){ϵ}_{i}^{2} , H represents the Heaviside function, ϵ represents the elastic strain tensor, {ϵ}_{i} represents the principal elastic strains.and {G}_{\mathrm{PC}} is a material parameter to be determined. In 3D, the distance l is replaced by the area of the chip in the propagation plane of the notch. In order to carry out the computation of the elastic energy in these zones called chips, two solutions exist in 2D: - having defined these zones in the mesh {\Phi}_{\mathit{el}}^{\mathit{traction}}=\frac{\lambda}{2}H(\mathit{tr}(ϵ))\mathit{tr}{(ϵ)}^{2}+\mu \sum_{i=1}^{3}H({ϵ}_{i}){ϵ}_{i}^{2} - defining these zones a posteriori in the free mesh {\Phi}_{\mathit{el}}=\frac{1}{2}\sigma {A}^{-1}\sigma Figure 3-2- Classical mesh with definition of the chips. In the first case, the Figure presents a view of the mesh to be used. This mesh comprises 95 chips of small size (each meshed by 8 quadrilateral finite elements), then a coarsening zone. A mesh-cell group must then be associated with each chip. In the second case, the Figure presents one possible mesh around the notch. This mesh must be sufficiently fine in this zone in order to allow a reliable computation of the parameter of the energy method. Figure 3-3- Free mesh without definition of the chips. In 3D, the notion of a slice is introduced, each slice containing several chips. The slices follow one another along the defect front, which is a line. In 2D, there is only one slice, the defect tip being reduced to 1 point. The chips of the 1st slice are defined in the same way as in 2D, with the difference that the mesh cells are solid and must be hexahedral; the list is continued by adding the chips of the 2nd slice in the same way; one finally obtains a list of {\mathrm{nb}}_{\mathrm{copeaux}}\times {\mathrm{nb}}_{\mathrm{tranches}} mesh-cell groups. Slice no. 1 Slice no. 2 Figure 3-4 Definition of the slices 4 Operands CALC_GP is a macro-command and therefore calls other commands of Code_Aster internally. Most of the keywords are passed as they are to the other commands. It will be indicated below in which command(s) the keywords are used. 4.1 Operand RESULTAT > ♦ RESULTAT = resumeca, [resultat] Denotes the result of the thermomechanical analysis for which the parameter {G}_{P} is computed. Used by POST_ELEM and CALC_CHAMP. 4.2 Operand LIST_INST > ♦ LIST_INST = instant, [l_R] List of time instants at which the parameter will be computed. Warning : the quantities from which the parameter {G}_{P} is computed being non-linear, no temporal extrapolation is allowed; if a time instant is specified, it must belong to the list of archiving time instants of the thermomechanical analysis. Used by POST_ELEM, CREA_CHAMP and CALC_CHAMP. 4.3 Operand PRECISION > ◊ PRECISION = /prec, [R] [DEFAUT] Accuracy with which the list of time instants must be considered. 4.4 Operand CRITERE > ◊ CRITERE = /'ABSOLU' [DEFAUT] > /'RELATIF' Denotes the type of accuracy for the determination of the list of time instants. 4.5 Operand GP_MAX > ◊ GPMAX = CO('TABGPMAX') [CO] Indicates whether the user wishes to obtain as a result a second table, a restriction of the mandatory complete table containing only the row of the location of the maximum of the parameter {G}_{P} for each analysis time instant. 4.6 Operand TRANCHE_2D > ◊ TRANCHE_2D =_F( > ♦ ZONE_MAIL = /'NON' > = /'OUI' > #Si ZONE_MAIL = 'OUI' : > ♦ GROUP_MA = l_group [l_group_ma] > ♦ TAILLE = l_taille [l_R] > #Si ZONE_MAIL = 'NON' : > ♦ TAILLE = taille [R] > ♦ CENTRE = centre [R,R,R] > ♦ RAYON = R [R] > ♦ ANGLE = \theta [R] > ♦ NB_ZONE = n [I] > ◊ CHAMP_VISU = CO('CHAMP') [CO] Denotes the set of geometric parameters required for the computation of the energy parameter. 4.6.1 Keyword ZONE_MAIL > ♦ ZONE_MAIL = /'NON' > = /'OUI' Indicates whether the mesh represents the geometry of the chip zones. If 'OUI', one is in the case of a mesh such as that in the Figure. 4.6.2 Case ZONE_MAIL = 'OUI' 4.6.2.1 Keyword GROUP_MA > ♦ GROUP_MA = l_group [l_group_ma] List of the mesh-cell groups on which the computations will be carried out. Each mesh-cell group must correspond to a chip zone. Used by POST_ELEM. 4.6.2.2 Keyword TAILLE > ♦ TAILLE = l_taille [l_R] List of the sizes of the zones. This list must be of the same size as the list of mesh-cell groups. 4.6.3 Case ZONE_MAIL = 'NON' In this case, a geometric analysis zone is built by the macro-command. The following parameters make it possible to define it. The Figure presents the parameters defining these zones; it represents a notch of centre {C}_{\mathit{ent}} , of radius R ; the third zone {C}_{3}(l) of length 3\times {l}_{C} is hatched. Figure 4-1- Geometric definition of the zones in the unmeshed case. 4.6.3.1 Keyword TAILLE > ♦ TAILLE = {l}_{C} [R] Increment of the size of the zones. Zone n is therefore of size n {l}_{C} . Used by FORMULE. 4.6.3.2 Keyword CENTRE > ♦ CENTRE = centre [R,R,R] Denotes the coordinates of the centre of the notch {C}_{\mathrm{ent}} in the global frame. Used by FORMULE. 4.6.3.3 Keyword RAYON > ♦ RAYON = R [R] Denotes the radius of the notch. Used by FORMULE. 4.6.3.4 Keyword ANGLE > ♦ ANGLE = \theta [R] Denotes the angle formed between the direction of the notch and the axis \overrightarrow{X} of the global frame. The angle must be given in degrees and measured in the trigonometric sense. Used by FORMULE 4.6.3.5 Keyword NB_ZONE > ♦ NB_ZONE = n [I] Denotes the number of zones (chips) considered in the analysis. 4.6.3.6 Keyword CHAMP_VISU > ◊ CHAMP_VISU = CO('CHAMP') [CO] If the user so wishes, the output of a field at the Gauss points representing the chips may be requested. The value of this field is 1 in the chip zone and 0 elsewhere. The Figure presents a visualisation of this field for the mesh presented in the Figure. Figure 4-2- Field for visualisation of the chips. 4.7 Operand TRANCHE_3D > ◊ TRANCHE_3D =_F( > ♦ GROUP_MA = l_group [l_group_ma] > ) 4.7.1 Keyword GROUP_MA > ♦ GROUP_MA = l_group [l_group_ma] List of the mesh-cell groups on which the computations will be carried out. Each mesh-cell group must correspond to a chip zone. Each list of mesh-cell groups corresponds to a given slice; the mesh-cell groups inside each list must correspond to the chips and be ordered from the closest to the defect front to the furthest. Used by POST_ELEM. 4.8 Operand SYME > #Dans le cas 2D > ♦ SYME = /'OUI' > /'NON' States whether a symmetry of the structure with respect to the notch has made it possible to mesh only half of the structure. In figures and , only the part of the structure above the notch is defined; in this case, the user will supply SYME='OUI' and the result indicated in the table will take the symmetry into account (multiplied by two). 4.9 Operand FOND_FISS > #Si TRANCHE_3D : > ♦ FOND_FISS = fond [fond] In 3D, the user must previously define a crack front, with separated lips (since the defect is represented by a notch). This crack front makes it possible in particular to compute the areas (denominator of the computation of {G}_{p} ). 5 Examples of use Examples will be found in the test cases SSNV218a, SSNP131a and SSNP131b.

u4.82.10 Operator CALC_G_XFEM u4.82.10 Operator CALC_G_XFEM 1 Purpose This operator computes the following fracture-mechanics quantities, in 2D and in 3D, for unmeshed cracks (X-FEM method): - the energy release rate by the theta method in the case of a linear or non-linear thermoelastic problem R7.02.01 and R7.02.03, in statics or in dynamics R7.02.02, and in elastoplasticity R7.02.07; - the stress intensity factors \mathrm{K1} , \mathrm{K2} and \mathrm{K3} by the singular-displacement method in the case of a linear thermoelastic problem R7.02.05; - the maximisation of G and of \mathrm{K1} under bound constraints. Before a first use, it is advisable to refer to the corresponding reference documents and user's guides, in particular the document U2.05.01. This operator generates a concept of type table_sdaster. 2 Syntax table_container = CALC_G_XFEM( ◇ CHAM_THETA = co, ◆ THETA = _F( ◆ FISSURE = fiss_xfem, ◇ NB_POINT_FOND = int, ◇ NUME_FOND = int (défaut: 1), ◇ & R_INF = float, & R_SUP = float, ◇ & R_INF_FO = formule / nappe / fonction, & R_SUP_FO = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ DIRECTION = float, ), ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli / dyna_trans / evol_elas / mode_meca, ◇ / TOUT_ORDRE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_ORDRE = int, / LIST_ORDRE = listis, / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, / TOUT_MODE = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / NUME_MODE = int, / LIST_MODE = listis, / FREQ = float, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, # Si: (exists("INST"))or(exists("LIST_INST"))or(exists("FREQ"))or(exists("LIST_FREQ")) ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ◇ EXCIT = _F( ◇ CHARGE = char_meca / char_cine_meca, ◇ FONC_MULT = formule / nappe / fonction, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = "FIXE_CSTE", ), ◇ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◆ RELATION = / "ELAS", / "ELAS_VMIS_LINE", / "ELAS_VMIS_TRAC", / "ELAS_VMIS_PUIS", ◇ DEFORMATION = / "PETIT" (par défaut), / "PETIT_REAC", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / | GROUP_MA = grma, ), ◇ ETAT_INIT = _F( ◆ SIGM = cham_elem / cham_no, ), ⟐ LISSAGE = _F( ◇ LISSAGE_THETA = / "LEGENDRE" (par défaut), / "LAGRANGE", ◇ LISSAGE_G = / "LEGENDRE" (par défaut), / "LAGRANGE", / "LAGRANGE_NO_NO", # Si: (equal_to("LISSAGE_THETA", 'LEGENDRE')) or (equal_to("LISSAGE_G", 'LEGENDRE')) ◇ DEGRE = / 0, / 1, / 2, / 3, / 4, / 5 (par défaut), / 6, / 7, ), ◇ OPTION = / "CALC_G" (par défaut), / "CALC_K_G", # Si: (exists("COMPORTEMENT") and (equal_to("OPTION", 'CALC_G'))) ◇ CALCUL_CONTRAINTE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT / RESULTAT = resu Name of a result concept of type evol_elas, evol_noli, dyna_trans or mode_meca. This operand makes it possible to recover the displacement field (and the velocity and acceleration fields for a dynamic analysis). The model and the material field, which are required for the analysis, are also extracted from the result data structure. The analysis options available for each type of modelling are recalled in the table below. | | Computation of G | Computation of K | | --- | --- | --- | | D_PLAN / C_PLAN | CALC_G | CALC_K_G | | AXIS | CALC_G | CALC_K_G | | 3D | CALC_G | CALC_K_G | Table 3.1: Availability, by modelling, of the analysis options. Notes on the material properties: The characteristics of the material, recovered in the data structure resu, are the following: - Young's modulus E, - Poisson's ratio NU, - thermal expansion coefficient ALPHA (for a thermomechanical problem), - yield stress SY (for a non-linear elastic problem), - slope of the tension curve D_SIGM_EPSI (for a non-linear elastic problem with linear isotropic hardening). For the computation of the energy release rate, these characteristics may depend on the geometry (option ‘CALC_G’) and on the temperature (option ‘CALC_G’). They must be independent of the temperature for the computation of the stress intensity factors. The characteristics SY and D_SIGM_EPSI are treated only for a non-linear elastic problem with Von Mises hardening. The computation of the stress intensity factors is treated only in linear elasticity. > Note: For the computation of the stress intensity factors (option 'CALC_K_G' ), the characteristics must be defined on all the materials, including on the edge elements, because of the computation method R7.02.05. To make sure of this, it is advisable to do an AFFE = _F (TOUT = 'OUI') in the command AFFE_MATERIAU U4.43.03, even if the overloading rule is used afterwards. The stress intensity factors obtained with the option CALC_K_G are computed by evaluating the bilinear form of G with a purely mechanical singular solution (Westergaard asymptotic solution). If a thermomechanical problem is solved, the singularity due to the thermal field is then not taken into account. An indicator of the error due to this approximation can be obtained by evaluating the difference between G and G_IRWIN. In practice, the quantity \frac{∣G-{G}_{\mathit{irwin}}∣}{∣G∣} is evaluated at every point of the crack front, and the arithmetic mean of it is then taken. If this mean exceeds 50%, it is considered that one is outside the domain of validity of the approach, and an alarm message is issued. Bimaterial problem: 1st case : one has a bimaterial but the crack tip is in a single material, cf. Figure 3.1-a. If one is assured that the crown, defined between the lower radius R_INF and the upper radius R_SUP, is supported by elements of the same material, the analysis is possible whichever option is chosen. Otherwise only the option 'CALC_G' is possible. Figure 3.1-a: Bimaterial: 1st case 2nd case : one has a bimaterial in which the crack tip is at the interface, cf. Figure 3.1-b. To date, only the option for computing the energy release rate (option 'CALC_G') is available. The computation of stress intensity factors is not possible in this case. Figure 3.1-b: Bimaterial: 2nd case Computation of equivalent stress intensity factors of a model with cohesive forces: For studies of crack propagation in the presence of cohesive forces, one may be led to compute equivalent stress intensity factors, according to a very specific procedure of surface integrals over the cohesive zone, detailed in the reference documentation R7.02.19. A few adjustments of the syntax are then necessary: - the keywords R_INF/R_SUP must not be supplied, because it is not necessary to define a torus for the field \theta ; - the keyword COMPORTEMENT must not be supplied; all the information is extracted from the result; - only the smoothings LAGRANGE and LAGRANGE_NO_NO are available; - only the option CALC_K_G is available. A typical syntax is proposed at the end of this documentation. 3.2 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / INST / LIST_INST / TOUT_MODE / NUME_MODE / LIST_MODE / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / PRECISION / CRITERE These operands are used with the operand RESULTAT. The operands TOUT_ORDRE, NUME_ORDRE, LIST_ORDRE, INST, LIST_INST are associated with results of type evol_elas, evol_noli or dyna_trans. See U4.71.00. The operands TOUT_MODE, NUME_MODE, LIST_MODE, FREQ, LIST_FREQ are associated with results of type mode_meca. 3.3 Keyword EXCIT and operands CHARGE/FONC_MULT ◊ EXCIT = _F( ♦ CHARGE = charge ◊ FONC_MULT = fmult ) The keyword EXCIT makes it possible to recover a list of loadings charge, coming from the commands AFFE_CHAR_MECA or AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01, and the possible associated multiplicative coefficients fmult. The keyword EXCIT is optional and must not be supplied in the general case. If the keyword EXCIT is absent from the command, the loading taken into account is that extracted from resu. If the loading is supplied via EXCIT, then it is this loading that will be used in CALC_G_XFEM. If the loading supplied in EXCIT is different from that present in resu (consistency of the name and of the number of loads, of the load–function pairs), an alarm is issued and the analysis continues with the loadings indicated by the user. Caution: this use is valid only when the result is created via the operator CREA_RESU. Indeed, CREA_RESU makes it possible to define a result with or without application of loads. In the latter case, EXCIT gives the possibility of defining the loading directly in CALC_G_XFEM. The loadings currently supported by the various modellings and that may have a meaning in fracture mechanics are the following: - Body force: ROTATION, FORCE_INTERNE, PESANTEUR. - Surface force on the lips of the crack: FORCE_CONTOUR (2D), FORCE_FACE (3D), PRES_REP. - Thermal expansion: the temperature is transmitted via AFFE_MATERIAU/AFFE_VARC - In the case of a thermomechanical problem, the temperature is transmitted via the material properties (AFFE_MATERIAU / AFFE_VARC / EVOL). The thermal expansion is therefore automatically taken into account in the analysis with CALC_G. Note: The loadings not supported by an option are ignored . To date, the following loadings, which may have a meaning in fracture mechanics, are not treated: - FORCE_NODALE - FORCE_ARETE - DDL_IMPO on the lips of the crack - FACE_IMPO - PRE_EPSI It is important to note that the only loadings taken into account in a fracture-mechanics analysis with the method \theta are those supported by the elements inside the crown, where the theta vector field is non-zero (between R_INF and R_SUP [R7.02.01 §3.3]). The only types of load liable to influence the computation of G are therefore the body loadings (gravity, rotation), a non-uniform temperature field or forces applied on the lips of the crack. Warning: - If several loadings of the same kind (for example a body force) appear in the analysis, they are combined with one another for the post-processing. It is not, however, possible to date to carry out this combination if loadings of type FORMULE are present : the analysis then ends in error. - An exclusion rule is also applied when a pre-strain field (via 'PRE_EPSI' ) and an initial-stress field are present simultaneously. - It is not possible to date to associate a load defined from a FORMULE and a multiplicative coefficient ( FONC_MULT ). In this case, the analysis ends in error. - The kinematic loads ( AFFE_CHAR_CINE and AFFE_CHAR_CINE_F ) cannot be taken into account in the analysis. - For the option CALC_K_G , if a loading is imposed on the lips of the crack ( PRES_REP or FORCE_CONTOUR ), then the mesh cells of the lips must necessarily be oriented correctly (using ORIE_PEAU_2D or ORIE_PEAU_3D ) prior to the computation of K (meshed-crack case only). - If an analysis is carried out in large transformations (keyword DEFORMATION = 'GROT_GDEP' or 'PETIT_REAC'), the loadings supported in the vicinity of the crack front (more precisely in the integration torus) must be dead loads, typically an imposed force and not a pressure [R7.02.03§2.4]; these loads must have been declared as non-follower in STAT_NON_LINE . Nevertheless, follower loads may be defined far from the crack, because they then do not take part in the computation of G. - It is noted that the computation of CALC_G_XFEM with the modelling AXIS is not available for the results of thermomechanical analyses in large strain and large rotation. 3.4 Keyword THETA The theta field is computed in CALC_G_XFEM from the keywords R_INF/R_INF_FO, R_SUP/R_SUP_FO and FISSURE. The various cases are described in the table below according to the analysis option, the modelling (2D or 3D) and the type of crack (meshed crack or not). | | CALC_G | CALC_K_G | | --- | --- | --- | | 2D | ◊ R_INF, R_SUP... ♦ FISSURE | ◊ R_INF, R_SUP... ♦ FISSURE | | 3D | ◊ R_INF, R_SUP... ♦ FISSURE | ◊ R_INF, R_SUP... ♦ FISSURE | Advice on the choice of the crowns (in CALC_G_XFEM): - Avoid using a theta field defined with a lower radius R_INF equal to zero. The displacement fields are singular at the crack front and introduce inaccurate results in fracture-mechanics post-processing. - It is advisable to use the command CALC_G_XFEM successively with at least three theta fields of different crowns in order to make sure of the stability of the results. In the event of a significant variation (greater than 5–10%) one must question whether the whole modelling has been properly taken into account. - For the option CALC_K_G in 2D-axisymmetric conditions, the radius of the crowns must be small compared with the radius of the crack front in order to have the best possible accuracy. It is forbidden to have crowns of radius greater than the radius of the crack front. 3.4.1 Operand FISSURE ♦ FISSURE = fiss, This operand makes it possible to supply the information relating to the crack defined by the command DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08. This keyword is mandatory. In the few cases where a propagation study is carried out with cohesive elements, this crack is of type COHESIF (keyword TYPE_DISCONTINUITE in DEFI_FISS_XFEM), and the operator then automatically carries out a computation of equivalent stress intensity factors by a specific method of surface integrals over the cohesive zone, detailed in R7.02.19, §6.3. 3.4.2 Operands R_INF, R_INF_FO, R_SUP, R_SUP_FO These operands make it possible to compute the theta field when it has not been determined beforehand. They correspond respectively to the lower and upper radii of the crowns (a scalar or, in 3D, a function of the curvilinear abscissa). The two radii may be introduced either by constant real values, which are arguments of the simple keywords R_INF and R_SUP, or by functions of the curvilinear abscissa on the oriented crack front, which are arguments of the simple keywords R_INF_FO and R_SUP_FO. Some advice is given below. In 3D, when the radii are not a function of the curvilinear abscissa, the operands R_INF and R_SUP are optional. If they are not indicated, they are computed automatically from the maximum h of the sizes of the mesh cells connected to the nodes of the crack front. These mesh-cell sizes at each node of the front are computed in the command DEFI_FISS_XFEM and are present in the concept or fiss_xfem D4.10.01. It has been chosen to set R_SUP = 4h and R_INF = 2h. If the automatically computed value is chosen for R_SUP and R_INF, one should nevertheless make sure that these values (displayed in the .mess file) are consistent with the dimensions of the structure. In the case of a defect that is initially open and whose front is not plane, it is not at present possible to compute the energy release rate. 3.4.3 Operand NUME_FOND ◊ NUME_FOND = n, This keyword is optional. It may happen, for certain structures, that the crack front is discontinuous. In the case of a crack defined by DEFI_FISS_XFEM the crack front is then cut into several parts. The operand NUME_FOND makes it possible to indicate on which of these sub-parts of the crack front one wishes to carry out the analysis. By default, the analysis is carried out on the first crack front. 3.4.4 Operand NB_POINT_FOND ◊ NB_POINT_FOND = nbnofo, This keyword is optional. By default, the analysis is carried out on all the points of the crack front, that is all the points of intersection between the crack front and the edges of the mesh, for an unmeshed crack. The points of the crack front may be very irregularly spaced, which may lead to troublesome oscillations in the parameters G(s) or K(s) computed. The operand NB_POINT_FOND makes it possible to fix a priori the number of post-processing points, in order to improve the regularity of the results. The \mathit{nbnofo} points are evenly distributed along the crack front. Some advice is given in § 3.7. This keyword can be used only for a LAGRANGE-LAGRANGE smoothing. 3.5 Keyword COMPORTEMENT ◊ COMPORTEMENT = _F( This factor keyword makes it possible to redefine the constitutive behaviour of the material. But the use of this keyword must not be systematic : indeed, by default, the constitutive law used in CALC_G_XFEM is identical to that used for the mechanical analysis (via MECA_STATIQUE or STAT_NON_LINE). Supplying the keyword comportement creates an alarm, but the analysis continues; it is up to the user to check that the constitutive behaviours during the mechanical solution and during the computation of G are identical. The computation of the energy release rate G has a meaning only in linear or non-linear elasticity . Finally, the only command variable (see U4.43.03: operator AFFE_MATERIAU, keyword AFFE_VARC) allowed for the computation of the energy release rate is the temperature 'TEMP'. Notes: - Nothing forbids assigning a different constitutive behaviour when computing the displacements (for example elastoplastic) and then carrying out this post-processing with another relation (for example non-linear elastic). A consistency check is carried out on the constitutive behaviours used for the analysis and for the post-processing, and an alarm message is issued if there is a difference; the user is responsible for the interpretation of the results obtained R7.02.03. - For example, if the loading is perfectly radial and monotonic, the analyses in non-linear elasticity and in elastoplasticity lead to the same results. For further details, refer to U2.05.01. 3.5.1 Operand RELATION for the elastic constitutive laws - RELATION = The possible elastic constitutive relations ('ELAS', 'ELAS_VMIS_LINE', 'ELAS_VMIS_TRAC', 'ELAS_VMIS_PUIS') are detailed in U4.51.11. / 'ELAS' Linear elastic constitutive relation, that is the relation between the strains and the stresses considered is linear [R7.02.01 §1.1]. It is possible to define a non-zero initial stress state (see keyword ETAT_INIT), which leads to considering the elastic constitutive behaviour as incremental. / 'ELAS_VMIS_LINE' Non-linear elastic constitutive relation, of Von Mises type with linear isotropic hardening. The necessary material data of the material field are supplied in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU (cf. [R7.02.03 §1.1] and R5.03.20). / 'ELAS_VMIS_TRAC' Non-linear elastic constitutive relation, of Von Mises type with non-linear isotropic hardening. The necessary material data of the material field are supplied in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU (cf. [R7.02.03 §1.1] and R5.03.20). / 'ELAS_VMIS_PUIS' Non-linear elastic constitutive relation, of Von Mises type with non-linear isotropic hardening defined by a power law. The necessary material data of the material field are supplied in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU (cf. [R7.02.03 §1.1] and R5.03.20). 3.5.2 Operand ETAT_INIT ◊ ETAT_INIT=_F(SIGM = siefelga) In the case of an incremental elastic constitutive relation, it is possible to define a non-zero initial stress state. The use of this keyword requires beforehand the definition of an initial state in the operator STAT_NON_LINE when solving the analysis to be post-processed by CALC_G_XFEM. STAT_NON_LINE allows this definition in two ways (see u4.51.03): - with an initial state of result type, supplied under the keyword EVOL_NOLI of the factor keyword ETAT_INIT - with an initial state of field type, supplied under the keywords SIGM/DEPL/VARI/STRX/COHE of the factor keyword ETAT_INIT To date, post-processing with CALC_G_XFEM of analyses using the keywords EVOL_NOLI/DEPL/VARI/STRX/COHE is not possible. Only post-processing with CALC_G_XFEM of analyses using the keyword SIGM is possible. The initial stress field supplied may be of type SIEF_ELGA only (with the possibility of creating them from CREA_CHAMP in particular). In every case, this initial stress field must be self-equilibrated , in the absence of a crack, with the boundary conditions alone. The user must check that the initial stress field is admissible by applying it in the keyword ETAT_INIT of the operator STAT_NON_LINE, with a linear elastic constitutive behaviour (RELATION = 'ELAS'), with the boundary conditions alone; the mechanical result must be the same stress field without additional strains (see ). Figure 3.1: Check of the validity of the initial stress field. Given the difficulty of validating the formulation that has been implemented, it is not at present admissible to combine a pre-strain ( via the keyword PRE_EPSI of the operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA) and an initial stress. 3.5.3 Operand DEFORMATION This keyword makes it possible to define the assumptions used for the computation of the strains. For further details on the strain formalisms, see the paragraph DEFORMATION of [U4.51,11]. To begin with, the quantities computed by CALC_G_XFEM are defined only in small strains. It is therefore not possible to use for CALC_G_XFEM a formalism other than PETIT, GROT_GDEP or PETIT_REAC. If this is the case, the analysis stops in error. Next, there must in theory be consistency between the strain formalisms used for the mechanical analysis itself and the post-processing in question here. This would therefore mean that the mechanical analyses themselves must be carried out with the formalisms PETIT, GROT_GDEP or PETIT_REAC only. However, the possibility is left of carrying out the post-processing in small strains (PETIT) from the result of a mechanical analysis carried out with another formalism (for example GDEF_LOG). In this case, an alarm is issued, and it is up to the user to decide whether the result supplied has a meaning or not. In order to carry out a more reliable computation of the energy release rate in large strains, it is advisable to use the crack-opening equivalence method presented briefly in U2.05.01. ◊ DEFORMATION = / 'PETIT' : les déformations utilisées dans la relation de comportement sont les relations linéarisées. Cela signifie que l'on reste en Hypothèse de Petites Perturbations: petits déplacements, petites rotations et petites déformations. Dans ce cas, les calculs des grandeurs sont licites et validés. Cette option est la seule possible pour les fissures non maillées. / 'GROT_GDEP' : Permet de traiter les grandes rotations et les grands déplacements, mais en restant en petites déformations / 'PETIT_REAC' : disponible uniquement en comportement incrémental, c'est une approximation des grandes déformations pour laquelle les incréments de déformations sont calculés dans la géométrie actuelle (réactualisée). Elle n'est valable que pour de petits incréments et pour des rotations faibles [:ref: U4.51.11 ]. 3.5.4 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA ◊ / TOUT = 'OUI' , / GROUP_MA = lgrma , Specifies the mesh cells or the nodes on which the constitutive relation is used. 3.5.5 Constitutive relation available for each option | | | 'CALC_G' | 'CALC_K_G' | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | COMPORTEMENT | 'ELAS' | 'PETIT' 'GROT_GDEP' | 'PETIT' | | | 'ELAS_VMIS_LINE' 'ELAS_VMIS_TRAC' 'ELAS_VMIS_PUIS' | 'PETIT' 'GROT_GDEP' | not avail. | Table 3.6.4-a: Availability, by option, of the constitutive relations. 3.6 Operand OPTION ♦ OPTION = / 'CALC_G' , / 'CALC_K_G', 3.6.1 OPTION = 'CALC_G' R7.02.01 and R7.02.03 It makes it possible to compute the energy release rate G by the theta method in 2D or in local 3D for a linear or non-linear thermoelastic problem. In 2D, for the AXIS modelling, the result obtained must be divided by the radius at the crack front, cf. § 4.2. 3.6.2 OPTION = 'CALC_K_G' R7.02.05 This option computes in 2D and in 3D the energy release rate G and the stress intensity factors {K}_{1} , {K}_{2} and {K}_{3} in plane linear thermoelasticity by the singular-field method (use of the bilinear form of G , R7.02.05). Notes: - For this option, only linear elastic analyses without an initial state, or linear elastic analyses with an initial stress, are available. - For this option in 2D, if INFO is equal to 2, the computation and the printout (in the file MESSAGE) of the propagation angle of the crack are generated. This angle, computed according to 3 criteria ( \mathrm{K1} or G maximum, \mathrm{K2} minimum) according to the formulae of AMESTOY, BUI and DANG-VAN [R7.02.05 §2.5], is given to within 10 degrees. 3.7 Keyword LISSAGE > The domain of application of this keyword is limited to the local 3D case. 3.7.1 Operand LISSAGE_THETA ◊ LISSAGE_THETA= / 'LEGENDRE' [DEFAUT] / 'LAGRANGE' The trace of the theta field on the crack front may be discretised either according to the basis of the N first Legendre polynomials ('LEGENDRE'), or according to the shape functions associated with the discretisation of the crack front ('LAGRANGE') R7.02.01. The command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03 makes it possible to print the results in the desired format. 4 Normalisation of the energy release rate G 4.1 2D plane stress and plane strain In dimension 2 (plane stress and plane strain), the crack front is reduced to a point and the value G(\theta ) coming from the command CALC_G_XFEM is independent of the choice of the field \theta : > G=G(\theta )\forall \theta \in \Theta 4.2 Axisymmetry In axisymmetric conditions the value G(\theta ) obtained with Aster for the option CALC_G must be normalised: > G=\frac{1}{R}G(\theta ) where R is the distance from the crack front to the axis of symmetry [R7.02.01 §2.4.4]. For the option CALC_K_G, the values of G and of K supplied in the result table are directly the local values; they must therefore not be normalised. 4.3 Symmetry of the model If only half of the solid is modelled with respect to the crack: - either specify the keyword SYME='OUI' in the commands concerned; - or do not forget to multiply by 2 the values of the energy release rate G or G(s) , and by 4 those of {G}_{\mathrm{Irwin}} . In addition the values of the stress intensity factors corresponding to the symmetry mode must also be multiplied by 2. 5 Examples Let us take the case of an unmeshed crack, and of a computation of equivalent stress intensity factors in the presence of cohesive forces. The crack was defined by: fiss=DEFI_FISS_XFEM(MODELE=MO, TYPE_DISCONTINUITE = 'COHESIF', > DEFI_FISS=_F(FONC_LN = fonc1, FONC_LT = fonc2, GROUP_MA_BORD = group_ma,), > ); After the mechanical analysis that has given a result res, the post-processing in order to obtain the equivalent stress intensity factors is carried out by: table_k=CALC_G(OPTION='CALC_K_G', RESULTAT = res, INST = inst_fin, THETA =_F(FISSURE = fiss, NB_POINT_FOND = nb_pts,), LISSAGE = F(LISSAGE_THETA = 'LAGRANGE', LISSAGE_G = 'LAGRANGE_NO_NO'), > )

u4.82.11 Operator PROPA_FISS u4.82.11 Operator PROPA_FISS 1 Purpose The purpose of the operator PROPA_FISS is to propagate a crack, this crack being defined with the X-FEM method. Three types of method are available: - a method based on a fast marching algorithm (METHODE_PROPA='SIMPLEXE', 'UPWIND'): this method is available in 2D and in 3D for all types of finite element. The initial crack may be defined on the mesh of the model or on an auxiliary mesh. - a purely geometric method by computation of distances to the crack front (METHODE_PROPA='GEOMETRIQUE') - a method using an intermediate surface mesh of the lip of the crack (METHODE_PROPA='MAILLAGE'): this method is available in 2D and in 3D for all types of finite element. The initial crack must itself also be defined by means of a mesh. The operator PROPA_FISS thus computes the crack resulting from a fatigue propagation according to a local Paris law, from the previous crack and from the table of stress intensity factors coming from CALC_G or from POST_K1_K2_K3. For half-line cracks (in 2D) or plane cracks with a straight front (in 3D), the surface mesh of the initial crack may be created by the operator PROPA_FISS (METHODE_PROPA = 'INITIALISATION'). The operator produces: - either a concept of type fiss_xfem defining the propagated crack (case METHODE_PROPA='SIMPLEXE', 'UPWIND' or 'GEOMETRIQUE'); - or the mesh of the initial crack (case METHODE_PROPA='INITIALISATION'); - or the mesh of the propagated crack (case METHODE_PROPA='MAILLAGE'). - The theoretical aspect of the propagation of the level sets for the X-FEM method is dealt with in R7.02.12. 2 Syntax / fiss_xfem / maillage = PROPA_FISS( ◆ METHODE_PROPA = / "SIMPLEXE", / "MAILLAGE", / "INITIALISATION", / "GEOMETRIQUE", / "UPWIND", ◇ OPERATION = / "RIEN" (par défaut), / "DETECT_COHESIF", / "PROPA_COHESIF", #
