This option is available only for TYPE_RESU_MECA= B3200, ZE200a or ZE200b - VALE_MAX: only the maximum values are given; these maxima are not, however, necessarily reached at the same analysis time instant. 3.2 Operand TITRE ♦ TITRE = titre Character string describing the title of the table of values created, which appears in the printout of this table by IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. 3.3 Operand INFO ♦ INFO = /1 /2 Allows a more or less detailed display in the message file. 3.4 Result types: keyword TYPE_RESU_MECA Five types of post-processing are available in POST_RCCM: these post-processings follow the rules of different paragraphs of the RCC-M: B3600, B3200, ZE200. Results of RCC-M type B3600 for piping: 'B3600' With the option FATIGUE, this type of result is dedicated to the post-processing of mechanical analyses ( MECA_STATIQUE , STAT_NON_LINE , COMB_SISM_MODAL ) on a piping line. The fatigue analysis is carried out according to the rules of paragraph B3600. Several situations may be defined, but in a single group. Seismic situations may be taken into account. With the option MOMENT_EQUIVALENT, this type of result is dedicated to the post-processing of mechanical analyses ( MECA_STATIQUE , STAT_NON_LINE , DYNA_VIBRA, DYNA_NON_LINE ) on a piping line. This option allows the analysis of the maximum equivalent moments on the line. According to the formula of paragraph B3600: MEQ=\sqrt{({MT}^{2}+{MFY}^{2}+{MFZ}^{2})} The table produced contains the temporal maxima of the components MT, MFY, MFZ and MEQ as well as the value of the curvilinear abscissa of the node in question. Results of RCC-M type B3200: 'EVOLUTION' and 'B3200' 'EVOLUTION' is dedicated to the post-processing of one or more thermomechanical analyses (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE) on a 2D or 3D modelling. The results are transmitted via stress tables, extracted on the analysis segment or segments. The accessible criteria are: - for the current zones (away from a geometric singularity): the level 0 criteria (option PM_PB), the level A criteria excluding fatigue (option SN) and the fatigue criteria (option FATIGUE_ZH210) on segments; - for the geometric singularities: analysis of the crack-initiation factor (option AMORCAGE) on a circular cutting line around the singularity. This option is well suited to cases where there are few situations to study, or to cases where it is necessary to determine the crack-initiation factor. 'B3200' is, by contrast, well suited to analyses on a component subjected to numerous situations, possibly distributed among several operating groups. An earthquake may be taken into account, as well as passage situations and sharing groups. One may also assess the environmental fatigue resistance with this option. The loadings may be entered in several forms. This type of result may therefore require the prior analysis: - of the stresses associated with the thermal transients considered, which must be extracted on the analysis segment ( RESU_THER ) , - of the stresses associated with the pressure loadings: in the form of a transient ( RESU_PRES ) or in the form of a unit loading with two pressures for the stabilised states ( RESU_MECA_UNIT, PRES_A and PRES_B ), - of the stresses associated with the loadings due to the forces and to the moments: - in the form of a transient ( RESU_MECA ) - for unit loadings (unit global forces and moments applied at the boundaries of the model) with two torsors for the stabilised states (CHAR_ETAT_A and CHAR_ETAT_B). These forces may either be computed with code_aster, or come from the OAR database, - for unit loadings to which one applies a torsor, this torsor is computed by interpolation between two torsors ( CHAR_ETAT_A and CHAR_ETAT_B ) which correspond to the temperatures TEMP_A , and TEMP_B and by means of the temperature during the situation TABL_TEMP. The accessible criteria are the level 0 criteria (option PM_PB ), the level A criteria excluding fatigue (option SN ), the fatigue criteria (option FATIGUE ) and the environmental fatigue criteria (option EFAT) on segments. Results of RCC-M type ZE200: 'ZE200a' and 'ZE200b' The ZE200 method of the RCC-M is a mixed method which combines B3200 and B3600. This type of result is therefore dedicated to the post-processing of mechanical analyses on a piping line according to B3600, combined with the thermal transients, for 'ZE200a'. The method 'ZE200b' in addition treats the stresses due to the pressure in the form of a transient. These options are well suited to analyses on piping subjected to numerous situations, possibly distributed among several operating groups. An earthquake may be taken into account, as well as passage situations and sharing groups. One may also assess the environmental fatigue resistance with this option. 3.5 Table produced The command POST_RCCM generates a concept of type table. The command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03 makes it possible to print the content of the table. For further information, one may refer to the document U2.09.03. 3.6 Operand AXIS ◊ AXIS = / ‘NON’ [DEFAUT] / ‘OUI’ Indicator making it possible to declare the axisymmetry of the modelling. For TYPE_RESU_MECA='EVOLUTION', if this operand takes the value ‘OUI’, the analysis of the equivalent membrane stresses Pm and bending stresses Pb will be carried out by an algorithm specially designed for axisymmetric models. Given the inhomogeneous distribution of the mass in the radial direction, this algorithm introduces a corrective shift of the mean line into the stress linearisation formulation. For the other values of TYPE_RESU_MECA, if this operand takes the value ‘OUI’, the analysis will stop with an error message because no specific treatment has been implemented. 4 Operands specific to results of type B3200 4.1 Preliminaries From several results of mechanical analyses on a component, one computes level 0 and level A criteria of the RCC-M. The loadings may be entered in several forms. This type of result may therefore require the prior analysis: - of the stresses associated with the thermal transients considered, which must be extracted on the analysis segment ( RESU_THER ) , - of the stresses associated with the pressure loadings: in the form of a transient ( RESU_PRES ) or in the form of a unit loading with two pressures for the stabilised states ( RESU_MECA_UNIT, PRES_A and PRES_B ), - of the stresses associated with the loadings due to the forces and to the moments: - in the form of a transient ( RESU_MECA ) - for unit loadings (unit global forces and moments applied at the boundaries of the model) with two torsors for the stabilised states (CHAR_ETAT_A and CHAR_ETAT_B). These forces may either be computed with code_aster, or come from the OAR database. The frame used for the 2D or 3D analysis must be consistent with the one in which the global forces coming from the beam analysis are expressed. - for unit loadings to which one applies a torsor, this torsor is computed by interpolation between two torsors ( CHAR_ETAT_A and CHAR_ETAT_B ) which correspond to the temperatures TEMP_A , and TEMP_B and by means of the temperature during the situation TABL_TEMP. 4.1.1 Option PM_PB Option making it possible to compute the level 0 criteria, which aim to protect the equipment against the damage of excessive deformation, of plastic instability and of elastic and elastoplastic instability. These criteria require the analysis of the equivalent stresses of membrane Pm , of local membrane Pl , of bending Pb and of membrane plus bending Pm+Pb . 4.1.2 Option SN Option making it possible to compute the level A criteria (excluding fatigue), which aim to protect the equipment against the damage of progressive deformation. They require the analysis of the range of variation of the linearised stress at a point, denoted Sn . Under certain conditions, this option also allows the analysis of Sn\ and of the thermal ratcheting (if the factor keyword RESU_THER is present). Note: With the option ‘SN’, the analysis is carried out without combination between the situations defined: each situation will be processed in succession. In order to have the quantities (grandeurs) with combination between each situation, one must use the option ‘FATIGUE’. 4.1.3 Option FATIGUE The fatigue analyses are carried out in the sense of the RCCM B3200 on the analysis segment. Two fictitious transients are thus identified in order to combine two situations with each other R7.04.03. 4.1.4 Option EFAT The environmental fatigue analyses (option ‘EFAT’) are carried out in the sense of the RCCM B3200 on the analysis segment. Two fictitious transients are thus identified in order to combine two situations with each other. The effects of the PWR environment on the usage factor are then taken into account. One must add the factor keyword 'ENVIRONNEMENT' and the keywords 'O_ETOILE' and 'TABL_TEMP' under each occurrence of the factor keyword 'SITUATION' R7.04.03. 4.2 Operand MATER ♦ MATER = mat Name of the material containing, for the analysed segment, the characteristics defined under the keywords ELAS and RCCM of DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 (E,NU, ALPHA, WOHLER, E_REFE, M_KE, N_KE, SM) Note on the fatigue curves: The question of the extension of the fatigue curve and the notion of endurance limit are discussed in §9.1.1 . 4.3 Operand SY_MAX ◊ SY_MAX = symax, Conventional yield limit for the maximum temperature reached during the cycle. This operand is used only for the analysis of the thermal ratcheting. If the yield limit SY_MAX is not defined, one takes the value defined under the operand SY_02 of the keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01; if this operand is not defined either, the analysis of the thermal ratcheting is impossible. 4.4 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE = / ‘TRESCA’, [DEFAUT] / ‘TOUT_INST’ There are two methods for selecting the time instants when analysing Sn or Sp: - the method 'TRESCA' carries out a pre-selection of the time instants based on the signed Tresca stress of each transient; it is the faster of the two methods and it is therefore taken by default if the user specifies nothing. It is nevertheless less robust than the second method R7.04.03 - the method 'TOUT_INST' combines all the possibilities of time instants and may be more costly in run time. 4.5 Operand TYPE_KE ◊ TYPE_KE = / ‘KE_MECA’, [DEFAUT] / ‘KE_MIXTE’ The elastoplastic correction factor Ke may be computed in two ways R7.04.03: - KE_MECA: this is the original method, the only one available in versions earlier than version 7.2; - KE_MIXTE: this method decomposes the range of variation of the alternating stresses into a thermal part and a mechanical part. It has been authorised since the 1997 modification of the RCC-M. 4.6 Operand SOUS_CYCL ◊ SOUS_CYCL = / ‘NON’, [DEFAUT] / ‘OUI’ The usage factor due to the sub-cycles of all the situations may or may not be taken into account. 4.7 Keyword FACT_SIGM ◊ FACT_SIGM=_F( ◊ KT_SN = ktsn, [R] ◊ KT_SP = ktsp, [R] ), Values of the stress concentration KT_SN and KT_SP to be applied to Sn and/or to Sp. Enters only into the fatigue analysis. 4.8 Keyword INDI_SIGM ◊ INDI_SIGM=_F( ... ), Values of the stress indices to be used in the fatigue analysis (values codified in the RCC-M B3683). The user supplies, for the analysis segment, the values of C1, C2, C3, K1, K2, K3. This keyword makes it possible to compare results coming from the method which follows paragraph ZE200 or paragraph B3600. 4.9 Keyword RESU_THER This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the thermal analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different thermal analyses. 4.9.1 Operand NUME_RESU_THER ♦ NUME_RESU_THER = numtran [I] Number of the thermal transients. This number is used to identify the thermal transient associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 4.9.2 Operand TABL_RESU_THER ♦ TABL_RESU_THER = table [tabl_post_releve] Table produced by POST_RELEVE_T, containing, for each transient thermal analysis, the record of the stresses due to the thermal loading on the section of the 2D or 3D mesh chosen by the user at different time instants of the transient. 4.10 Keyword RESU_PRES This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the pressure analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different pressure analyses. It may be used if RESU_MECA_UNIT and CHAR_MECA are not used. 4.10.1 Operand NUME_RESU_PRES ♦ NUME_RESU_PRES = numtran [I] Number of the pressure transients. This number is used to identify the pressure transient associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 4.10.2 Operand TABL_RESU_PRES ♦ TABL_RESU_PRES = table [tabl_post_releve] Table produced by POST_RELEVE_T, containing, for each transient pressure analysis, the record of the stresses due to the pressure loading on the section of the 2D or 3D mesh chosen by the user at different time instants of the transient. It is specified that the columns SXZ and SYZ must be present even in 2D. It is therefore in particular necessary to add them (with zero values) to the tables produced by POST_RELEVE_T which do not contain them. 4.11 Keyword RESU_MECA This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the analyses of mechanical origin. It is repeatable as many times as there are different analyses of mechanical origin. This keyword is necessary if the keywords CHAR_MECA and RESU_MECA_UNIT have not been supplied. 4.11.1 Operand NUME_RESU_MECA ♦ NUME_RESU_MECA = numtran [I] Number of the transients of mechanical origin. This number is used to identify the mechanical transient associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 4.11.2 Operand TABL_RESU_MECA ♦ TABL_RESU_MECA = table [tabl_post_releve] Table produced by POST_RELEVE_T, containing, for each transient mechanical analysis, the record of the stresses due to the loading of mechanical origin on the section of the 2D or 3D mesh chosen by the user at different time instants of the transient. It is specified that the columns SXZ and SYZ must be present even in 2D. It is therefore in particular necessary to add them (with zero values) to the tables produced by POST_RELEVE_T which do not contain them. 4.12 Keyword CHAR_MECA This factor keyword makes it possible to define, for each mechanical loading appearing in the situations, the torsors applied at the boundaries of the model, coming from beam-type analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different mechanical loadings in the set of situations. It may be used if RESU_MECA and RESU_PRES are not used. 4.12.1 Operand NUME_CHAR Number of the mechanical loading. This number is used to define the loadings associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 4.12.2 Operand NOM_CHAR Name of the mechanical loading (optional). 4.12.3 Operands MX / MY / MZ / FX / FY / FZ Generalised forces coming from analyses of the piping line, of beam type, for each loading, to be applied to the stress profiles supplied under RESU_MECA_UNIT, by linear combination. Warning: this assumes that these values are supplied in a frame consistent with the one used for the 2D or 3D modelling of the component. 4.12.4 Operands MX_CORP / MX_TUBU, MY_CORP / MY_TUBU, … ♦ MX_CORP = mxc , [R] ♦ MY_CORP = myc , [R] ♦ MZ_CORP = mzc , [R] ◊ FX_CORP = fxc , [R] ◊ FY_CORP = fyc , [R] ◊ FZ_CORP = fzc , [R] ♦ MX_TUBU = mxt , [R] ♦ MY_TUBU = myt , [R] ♦ MZ_TUBU = mzt , [R] ◊ FX_TUBU = fxt , [R] ◊ FY_TUBU = fyt , [R] ◊ FZ_TUBU = fzt , [R] Generalised forces applied to the body and the nozzle of a branch connection. Their meaning is identical to that of the operands MX, MY, … used for the piping lines. If these operands are used, the corresponding result tables (TABL_MX_TUBU, TABL_MX_CORP, …) must be specified under the keyword RESU_MECA_UNIT. 4.13 Keyword RESU_MECA_UNIT ◊ RESU_MECA_UNIT=_F( ... ) This factor keyword makes it possible to supply the stress profiles on the chosen segment, coming from the unit mechanical analyses either on the piping line (TABL_MX, TABL_MY…), or on the branch connection (TABL_MX_CORP, TABL_MX_TUBU…). It may be used if RESU_MECA and RESU_PRES are not used. For carrying out these analyses, it is recommended to apply, at the boundaries of the 3D model, connections of 3D–beam type with point discrete elements. One of these elements is clamped, and on the other one applies unit generalised forces. In the case of a branch connection, one of the ends of the body is fixed, the generalised forces being applied to the other end of the body and to the end of the nozzle. It is noted that it is customary in RCCM analyses of piping type to consider only the moments, which is why the keywords of type TABL_FX, TABL_FY, TABL_FZ are optional. TABL_PRES corresponds to an analysis under unit internal pressure, without forgetting the closed-end effect. 4.14 Keyword SEISME A single loading of type SEISME may be defined per group of situations. 4.14.1 Operands NUME_SITU / NOM_SITU / NB_OCCUR / NB_CYCL_SEISME ♦ NUME_SITU = numsitu, [I] ◊ NOM_SITU = nomsitu, [Kn] ♦ NB_OCCUR = nbocc , [I] ♦ NB_CYCL_SEISME = nbsss, [I] Number, name (optional) and number of occurrences of the seismic situation. NB_CYCL_SEISME is the number of cycles associated with each occurrence of the earthquake, regarded as sub-cycles in the analysis of the usage factor. 4.14.2 Operands CHAR_ETAT ♦ CHAR_ETAT = num_char_meca , [I] Number of the mechanical loading (corresponding to the keyword NUME_CHAR of the factor keyword CHAR_MECA) associated with the seismic situation. 4.14.3 Operands TABL_FX, TABL_FY, ..., TABL_MZ Stress profiles associated with the seismic situation; this keyword is necessary if the keyword CHAR_ETAT is not supplied. It is specified that the columns SXZ and SYZ must be present even in 2D. It is therefore in particular necessary to add them (with zero values) to the tables produced by POST_RELEVE_T which do not contain them. 4.15 Keyword SITUATION This factor keyword makes it possible to define the situations. It is repeatable as many times as there are situations. 4.15.1 Operands NUME_SITU / NOM_SITU / NB_OCCUR ♦ NUME_SITU = numsitu, [I] ◊ NOM_SITU = nomsitu, [Kn] ♦ NB_OCCUR = nbocc, [I] Number, name (optional) and number of occurrences of the situation. 4.15.2 Operand NUME_GROUPE / NUME_PASSAGE /NUME_PARTAGE ♦ NUME_GROUPE = (numgroup1, numgroup2, ...) , [L_I] ◊ NUME_PASSAGE= (num1, num2, ...), [L_I] ◊ NUME_PARTAGE= num1 [I] One indicates under NUME_GROUPE the group number or numbers to which the situation belongs. If the situation is a passage situation, one indicates under NUME_PASSAGE the numbers of the various groups which it links (20 groups at most). When a situation provides the passage between n groups, it necessarily belongs to these n groups (the numbers under NUME_PASSAGE must appear under NUME_GROUPE ). Note: Conversely, a situation may belong to different groups without being a passage situation between these groups (the numbers under NUME_GROUPE are not necessarily under NUME_PASSAGE) If the situation belongs to a sharing group, one indicates under NUME_PARTAGE the number of this sharing group. Notes: No relation exists between the number of an operating group (NUME_GROUPE) and the number of a sharing group (NUME_PARTAGE) A situation may belong to at most one sharing group 4.15.3 Operand COMBINABLE ♦ COMBINABLE = /'OUI', [DEFAUT] /'NON', [Kn] This keyword indicates whether a situation is combinable with the others inside its group (general case). In the case where COMBINABLE='NON', this means that the situation is a sub-cycle. 4.15.4 Operands PRES_A / PRES_B ◊ PRES_A = presa , [R] ◊ PRES_B = presb , [R] Pressures associated with each of the two stabilised states of the situation. 4.15.5 Operand NUME_RESU_PRES ◊ NUME_RESU_PRES = num_tran [I] Number of the pressure transient associated with the situation. There may be 0 or 1 transient per line section (which corresponds to mesh-cell groups) for each situation. This number corresponds to the keyword NUME_RESU_PRES of the factor keyword RESU_PRES. 4.15.6 Operand NUME_RESU_THER ◊ NUME_RESU_THER = num_tran [I] Number of the thermal transient associated with the situation. There may be 0 or 1 transient per line section (which corresponds to mesh-cell groups) for each situation. This number corresponds to the keyword NUME_RESU_THER of the factor keyword RESU_THER. In the case where, for a given situation, there are physically two transients for one section, such as heat-up–cool-down for example, it is customary to combine these two transients into a single one. 4.15.7 Operands CHAR_ETAT_A / CHAR_ETAT_B / TEMP_A / TEMP_B ♦ CHAR_ETAT_A = num_char_meca , [I] ♦ CHAR_ETAT_B = num_char_meca , [I] ♦ TEMP_A = tempa , [R] ♦ TEMP_B = tempb , [R] Numbers of the mechanical loadings associated with each stabilised state. These numbers correspond to the keyword NUME_CHAR of the factor keyword CHAR_MECA. If the keywords TEMP_A and TEMP_B are supplied, then the keyword TABL_TEMP must be supplied as well. The moments and forces will be interpolated as a function of the temperature. 4.15.8 Operand NUME_RESU_MECA ♦ NUME_RESU_MECA = num_tran [I] Number of the transient of mechanical origin associated with the situation. There must be 1 transient per line section (which corresponds to mesh-cell groups) for each situation. This number corresponds to the keyword NUME_RESU_MECA of the factor keyword RESU_MECA. This keyword is necessary if the keywords CHAR_ETAT_A and CHAR_ETAT_B have not been supplied. 4.15.9 Operands O_ETOILE / TABL_TEMP ◊ O_ETOILE = oet , [R] ◊ TABL_TEMP = tabtemp, [table] These two operands are necessary for the analysis of the environmental fatigue and therefore when calling the option 'EFAT'. For each situation, O_ETOILE represents the oxygen content (it is regarded here as constant) and TABL_TEMP is the table of the temperatures as a function of time during the transient. Note: The table under the keyword TABL_TEMP must be defined at the same time instants as the thermal transient of the situation under TABL_RESU_THER. 4.16 Keyword ENVIRONNEMENT This factor keyword makes it possible to compute the environmental fatigue resistance. It is not repeatable because it lists the data required for the analysis but common to all the situations. 4.16.1 Operand FEN_INTEGRE ♦ FEN_INTEGRE = fenint, [R] Integrated Fen, which enters into the analysis of the environmental factor. 4.16.2 Operand CRIT_EPSI ♦ CRIT_EPSI = epsilim, [R] Strain threshold from which the environmental factor does not come into play. 4.16.3 Operands TABL_YOUNG ♦ TABL_YOUNG = tabyoung, [table] Table supplying Young's modulus (column YOUNG) as a function of the temperature (column TEMP). A linear interpolation is carried out from this table in order to evaluate Young's modulus, which enters into the analysis of the environmental factor. 4.16.4 Operands S_ETOILE ♦ S_ETOILE = set , [R] Sulphur content of the metal analysed (therefore common to all the situations), equal to a constant. 4.16.5 Operands SEUIL_EPSI_INF / SEUIL_EPSI_SUP ♦ SEUIL_EPSI_INF = epsimin , [R] ♦ SEUIL_EPSI_SUP = epsimax , [R] Thresholds which enter into the analysis of the strain rate. 4.16.6 Operands A_ENV / B_ENV / C_ENV ♦ A_ENV = aenv , [R] ♦ B_ENV = benv , [R] ♦ C_ENV = cenv , [R] Constants which enter into the general expression of the environmental factor. 4.16.7 Operands SEUIL_T_INF / SEUIL_T_SUP / VALE_T_INF / VALE_T_SUP / VALE_T_MOY_NUM / VALE_T_MOY_DEN ♦ SEUIL_T_INF = tempmin , [R] ♦ SEUIL_T_SUP = tempmax , [R] ♦ VALE_T_INF = valmin , [R] ♦ VALE_T_SUP = valmax , [R] ♦ VALE_T_MOY_NUM = valmoynum , [R] ♦ VALE_T_MOY_DEN = valmoyden , [R] Thresholds which enter into the analysis of the temperature T . 4.17 Table produced and example The table produced by POST_RCCM depends on the analysis OPTION and on the type of result requested under the operand TYPE_RESU: - if TYPE_RESU=’VALE_MAX’ (default option): the table is simple and contains only the maximum parameters of the various quantities (grandeurs) (Pm, Pb, Pmpb, Sn, Sn , Sp, Salt, Fu, Fen, integrated Fen, Fu_environnement and the quantities (grandeurs) related to ratcheting) at the two ends - if TYPE_RESU=’DETAILS’: the table is much richer. It contains the maximum parameters mentioned previously (row 'MAXI') plus all the parameters computed, for each situation (rows of type 'SITU') and each combination of situations (rows of type 'COMB'), with or without earthquake, and the combinations which actually entered into the analysis of the usage factor (row 'FACT'). It is then strongly recommended to print the table with successive filters so that it is easy to use. - If TYPE_RESU=’SYSTUS’ : the table contains all the parameters computed for all the situations and combinations which actually entered into the analysis of the usage factor (row ' FACT '). - Printout of the maxima: if TYPE_RESU=’VALE_MAX’ or with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=_F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='MAXI'), the table produced may contain, depending on the option requested, the following parameters: PM_MAX, PB_MAX, PMPB_MAX, SN_MAX, SN _MAX, SIGM_M_PRES, SN_THER_MAX, CRIT_LINE_MAX , SP_THER_MAX, CRIT_PARA_MAX, SP_MAX, SALT_MAX, FU_TOTAL, FEN_TOTAL, FEN_INTEGRE and FUEN_TOTAL. - Printout of the quantities (grandeurs) of each situation: with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=(_F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='SITU' ), _F(NOM_PARA='SEISME', VALE_K='AVEC' ou ‘ SANS’) ), the table produced contains, depending on the option requested, the following parameters for each of the situations (with or without earthquake): PM, PB, PMPB, SN, INST_SN_1, INST_SN_2, SN , INST_SN _1,INST_SN _2, SIG_PRES_MOY, SN_THER, CRIT_LINE, SP_THER, CRIT_PARAB, SP1(MECA), INST_SALT_1, INST_SALT_2, SALT and FU_UNIT . - Printout of the quantities (grandeurs) of each combination of situations: with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=( _F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='COMB' ), _F(NOM_PARA='SEISME', VALE_K='AVEC' ou ‘ SANS’) ), the table produced contains, depending on the option requested, the following parameters for each of the combinations of situations (with or without earthquake): SN, INST_SN_1, INST_SN_2, SN , INST_SN _1,INST_SN _2, SIG_PRES_MOY, SN_THER, CRIT_LINE, SP_THER, CRIT_PARAB, SP1(MECA), INST_SALT_1, INST_SALT_2, SALT and FU_UNIT . - Printout of the combinations of situations which entered into the analysis of the usage factor: with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=( _F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='FACT' ), ), the table produced contains, depending on the option requested, the following parameters for each of the combinations of situations which entered into the analysis of the usage factor FU_TOTAL : SN, INST_SN_1, INST_SN_2, SN , INST_SN _1,INST_SN _2, INST_SALT_1, INST_SALT_2, SALT, FU_UNIT, NOCC_PRIS, FU_PARTIEL. If the option ‘ EFAT ’ is called, the following quantities (grandeurs) are added to the maxima relative to the option 'FATIGUE': FEN_TOTAL, FEN_INTEGRE and FUEN_TOTAL. In addition, if TYPE_RESU=’DETAILS’ , two quantities (grandeurs) are added to the rows of type 'FACT': FEN and FUEN_PARTIEL. For monitoring the analyses, additional information may be found in the message file, in particular for the option FATIGUE. One can thus follow, at the origin and then at the end of the segment: the processing of each of the situations and then of the combinations of situations, and the display of FU_TOTAL (including the part related to the sub-cycles and the part related to the seismic sub-cycles) The test cases rccm01a, rccm01b, rccm01c, rccm01d, rccm01e and rccm07 provide in particular complete examples of use. For further information, one may also refer to the document U2.09.03. 5 Operands common to results of type B3600 5.1 Keyword ZONE_ANALYSE This keyword makes it possible to limit the analysis to mesh cells or mesh-cell groups of the piping line. 5.1.1 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA ◊ / TOUT = 'OUI' , / GROUP_MA = gma1 , [groupma] Par défaut le calcul est fait pour tous les nœuds du modèle. Ces mot-clés permettent de restreindre l’analyse à des groupes de mailles, ce qui permet d’économiser du temps de calcul. 5.2 Keyword OPTION This keyword makes it possible to define the type of analysis requested. If OPTION = ‘FATIGUE’, one computes fatigue criteria from several results of mechanical analyses (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, COMB_SISM_MODAL) on a piping line. If OPTION = ‘MOMENT_EQUIVALENT’, one computes, for a mechanical result (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, DYNA_VIBRA, DYNA_NON_LINE), the temporal maxima of the components MT, MFY and MFZ of the field EFGE_ELNO as well as the temporal maxima of the equivalent moment (MEQ) at each point. In addition to the names of the mesh cell and of the node, each node is located in the table by its curvilinear abscissa along the piping line if the information exists. In order to compute these curvilinear abscissae, one must use beforehand the command MODI_MAILLAGE/ABSC_CURV. 6 Operands specific to the option FATIGUE of type B3600 6.1 Preliminary notes concerning the steps prior to this post-processing From several results of mechanical analyses (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE, COMB_SISM_MODAL) on a piping line, one computes fatigue criteria by the option FATIGUE. The data required for the post-processing are summarised here (and detailed in the following paragraph): - The geometry of the piping line. - The material field: it is the map of the materials assigned to the mesh-cell groups of the mesh by AFFE_MATERIAU, to which one must add the fatigue curve, E_REFE, M_KE and N_KE (keywords RCCM). - AFFE_CARA_ELEM makes it possible to assign the elementary characteristics. - Stress indices (at each node of the mesh). - The operating scenario containing the list of situations: - For each situation: 1. Numbers of occurrences of each situation (therefore of each stabilised state). 2. Pressure and mean temperature of each stabilised state. 3. List of the mechanical loadings of each stabilised state. 4. The group to which the situation belongs. 5. The associated thermal transient. - The results of the analyses for each mechanical loading (including the earthquake), identified by its number, with, for information, the name of the load case: element field at nodes of generalised forces, for each loading (EFGE_ELNO, or SIEF_ELNO). - For each node, a reference to a thermal result defined below. - Results of the thermal analyses: the 2D or 3D finite-element analyses which give this information depend both on the geometry and on the transient. One therefore has one thermal analysis per type of junction, and per type of transient. In practice one carries out two POST_RELEVE_T per transient and per different type of thickness or of geometry: one POST_RELEVE_T with the option EXTRACTION, and a second with the option MOYENNE The preliminary analyses to be carried out are therefore: - Beam-type analyses (elastic analysis) for each loading (one uses only the moments, expressed in a frame local to each element, a frame assumed identical for all the results) making up each of the two stabilised states of each situation. - A seismic analysis (inertial response and anchor displacements) (a single type of earthquake taken into account). - The analysis of each thermal transient, on as many 2D or 3D meshes as there are different thicknesses or components. The operands and keywords of the option FATIGUE have been chosen so as to allow a later use in connection with the OAR tool. They are therefore inspired by the specifications of the OAR database [3]. 6.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER = chmat It is the material field containing, for all the mesh cells of the model, the material characteristics useful to FATIGUE and defined under the keywords ELAS_FO, FATIGUE and RCCM of DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 (E, NU, ALPHA, WOHLER, E_REFE, M_KE, N_KE, SM). Note on the fatigue curves: For small stress amplitudes, the problem of extending the fatigue curve may arise: for example, for the RCCM fatigue curves beyond 106 cycles, the corresponding stress, 180 MPa, is regarded as an endurance limit, that is, any stress lower than 180 MPa must produce a zero usage factor, or an infinite allowable number of cycles. The method adopted here corresponds to this notion of endurance limit: if the stress amplitude is lower than the first abscissa of the fatigue curve, a zero usage factor is taken. 6.3 Operand CARA_ELEM ♦ CARA_ELEM = cara It is the field of characteristics of the beam elements (external radius and thickness, angle and radius of curvature of the elbows) defined by AFFE_CARA_ELEM. 6.4 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = modele It is the model (beam finite elements) on which the analyses of the mechanical loadings were carried out. 6.5 Operand TYPE_KE ◊ TYPE_KE = / ‘KE_MECA’, [DEFAUT] / ‘KE_MIXTE’ The elastoplastic correction factor Ke may be computed in two ways R7.04.03: - KE_MECA: this is the original method, the only one available in versions earlier than version 7.2; - KE_MIXTE: this method decomposes the range of variation of the alternating stresses into a thermal part and a mechanical part. It has been authorised since the 1997 modification of the RCC-M. 6.6 Keyword RESU_MECA This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the mechanical analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different mechanical loadings in the set of situations. 6.6.1 Operand NUME_CHAR Number of the mechanical loading. This number is used to define the loadings associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 6.6.2 Operand NOM_CHAR Name (optional) of the mechanical loading. 6.6.3 Operand RESULTAT / CHAM_GD / ♦ CHAM_GD = cham_effo , [cham_elem] / ♦ RESULTAT = resu, / [evol_elas] / [evol_noli] / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' , / NUME_ORDRE = lordre , [l_I] / LIST_ORDRE = lordre , [listIs] / INST = linst , [l_R] / NOEUD_CMP = lnoecmp, [:ref: l_K16 ] / LIST_INST = linst , listr8 ♦ NOM_CHAM = / 'EFGE_ELNO', / 'SIEF_ELNO', The results of the analyses for each loading (element fields at nodes of generalised forces) may be defined: - either an element field: cham_effo, which is of type EFGE_ELNO, or SIEF_ELNO, - or a data structure resultat (produced by MECA_STATIQUE or STAT_NON_LINE) with extraction parameters: time instant, NOM_CHAM='EFGE_ELNO', or 'SIEF_ELNO'…) or else produced by COMB_SISM_MODAL or MODE_STATIQUE with the additional extraction parameter NOEUD_CMP. For the latter, the force fields relating to the earthquake are the moments for each component of each earthquake, resulting from a quadratic combination NOEUD_CMP=('COMBI','QUAD') for the inertial response; and of the nodes and of the directions (for example NOEUD_CMP=('N1','DX')) for the anchor displacements. 6.7 Operand INDI_SIGM ♦ INDI_SIGM =_F( ... ) Values of the stress indices to be used in the fatigue analysis (values codified in the RCC-M B3683, varying according to the type of junction). The user supplies, for each mesh-cell group, or each node of each mesh cell, the values of C1, C2, C3, K1, K2, K3, it being known that the default values are those which correspond to the straight parts of the piping, which makes the input of the data easier. One may have, for example: INDI_SIGM= _F( GROUP_MA='GMA1'), (affectation des valeurs par défaut pour tous les nœuds de toutes les mailles de GMA1 ) TYPE_ELEM_STANDARD est un mot-clé optionnel, purement informatif, permettant d’afficher plus clairement dans la table les résultats selon le type d’éléments et de jonctions. On pourra donner, comme dans OAR, [:ref: 3 ] un descriptif du type: - DRO: for a straight part, - COU: for an elbow, - TRN: for a thickness transition, - TEE: for a tee. 6.8 Keyword RESU_THER This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the thermal analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different thermal analyses and geometric or material discontinuities. As an indication, there may be: (number of discontinuities) (number of thermal transients). 6.8.1 Operand NUME_RESU_THER ♦ NUME_RESU_THER = numtran [I] Number of the thermal transients. This number is used to identify the thermal transient associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 6.8.2 Operand TABL_RESU_THER ♦ TABL_RESU_THER = table [table] Table produced for example by POST_RELEVE_T, containing, for each transient thermal analysis, the record of the temperatures on a section (chosen by the user) of the 2D or 3D mesh of a junction or of a straight part at different time instants of the transient. The origin of the section must be the inner skin. ♦ TABL_MOYE_THER = table [table] Table produced for example by POST_RELEVE_T (OPERATION='MOYENNE'), containing, for each transient thermal analysis, the averages of order 0 and 1 of the temperatures on the chosen section (consistently with TABL_RESU_THER) at different time instants of the transient. These quantities are used to compute the values of \Delta {T}_{1} , \Delta {T}_{2} , {T}_{a} and {T}_{b} R7.04.03. 6.8.3 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA / MAILLE / GROUP_NO / NOEUD ◊ / TOUT = 'OUI' , / GROUP_MA = gma1 , [groupma] ◊ GROUP_NO = gno1 , [groupno] The table and the transient are associated either with a mesh-cell group (in general this group contains all the straight parts which see the same thermal transient), or with a mesh cell and a node of this mesh cell (which in general corresponds to a junction). One may have, for example: RESU_THER =_F(NUME_RESU_THER = 1, TABL_RESU_THER = tabl1, TABL_MOYE_THER = tabl11, GROUP_MA='gma1'), _F(NUME_RESU_THER = 1, TABL_RESU_THER = tabl2, TABL_MOYE_THER = tabl22, GROUP_MA = 'gma2' , GROUP_NO = 'gno1' ) 6.9 Keyword SEISME This factor keyword makes it possible to define the seismic situations. There can be only one earthquake per group of situations. 6.9.1 Operands NUME_SITU / NOM_SITU / NB_OCCUR / NB_CYCL_SEISME / NUME_GROUPE / TEMP_REF ♦ NUME_SITU = numsitu , [I] ◊ NOM_SITU = nomsitu , [Kn] ♦ NB_OCCUR = nbocc [I] ♦ NB_CYCL_SEISME = nbsss , [I] ◊ NUME_GROUPE = numgroup , [I] ◊ TEMP_REF = temp, [R] Number of the situation, and name (indicative). NB_OCCUR corresponds to the keyword OCCURRENCE of the OAR file and indicates the number of occurrences of the situation. NB_CYCL_SEISME supplies the number of sub-cycles for each occurrence of the earthquake, regarded as sub-cycles in the analysis of the usage factor. NUME_GROUPE makes it possible to define the number of the group to which the situation belongs. There can be only one earthquake per group of situations. The reference temperature TEMP_REF of the seismic situation is useful only if the material properties depend on the temperature (operand RCCM_FO of DEFI_MATERIAU). 6.9.2 Operand CHAR_ETAT ♦ CHAR_ETAT = (list_num_char_meca) , [L_I] CHAR_ETAT makes it possible to define the list of the numbers of the mechanical loadings associated with the seismic situation. These numbers correspond to the keyword NUME_CHAR of the factor keyword CHAR_MECA. They must correspond to the results of the inertial analysis by means of COMB_SISM_MODAL, and of each anchor displacement under earthquake, obtained either by means of MODE_STATIQUE, or case by case. 6.10 Keyword SITUATION This factor keyword makes it possible to define the definitions of the situations. It is repeatable as many times as there are situations. 6.10.1 Operands NUME_SITU / NOM_SITU / NB_OCCUR ♦ NUME_SITU = numsitu , [I] ◊ NOM_SITU = nomsitu , [Kn] ♦ NB_OCCUR = nbocc , [I] Number of the situation, and name (indicative). NB_OCCUR corresponds to the keyword OCCURRENCE of the OAR file and indicates the number of occurrences of the situation. NUME_GROUPE makes it possible to define the number of the group to which the situation belongs. For results of type B3600, it is for the moment not possible to combine situations of different groups linked by a passage situation. 6.10.2 Operand NUME_GROUPE / NUME_PASSAGE ♦ NUME_GROUPE = numgroup , [I] ◊ NUME_PASSAGE = (num1, num2), [L_I] Situation group number for each situation. The situations of two different groups cannot be combined with each other, unless a passage situation exists. For the passage situations, num1 and num2 indicate the two group numbers linked by this situation. 6.10.3 Operands PRES_A / PRES_B / TEMP_REF_A / TEMP_REF_B ♦ PRES_A = pressa , [R] ♦ PRES_B = pressb , [R] ◊ TEMP_REF_A = tempa, [R] ◊ TEMP_REF_B = tempb, [R] Temperatures (stabilised) and pressures associated with each of the two stabilised states of the situation. The temperatures are used for the analysis of the material properties at the two stabilised states; the operands TEMP_REF_A and TEMP_REF_B are therefore useful only if the material properties depend on the temperature (operand RCCM_FO of DEFI_MATERIAU). 6.10.4 Operands CHAR_ETAT_A / CHAR_ETAT_B ♦ CHAR_ETAT_A = (list_num_char_meca) , [L_I] ♦ CHAR_ETAT_B = (list_num_char_meca) , [L_I] List of the numbers of the mechanical loadings associated with each stabilised state. These numbers correspond to the keyword NUME_CHAR of the factor keyword CHAR_MECA. In the general case, a single mechanical loading is associated with each stabilised state. 6.10.5 Operand NUME_RESU_THER ◊ NUME_RESU_THER = list_num_tran [L_I] List of numbers of tables produced by thermal analyses associated with the situation. With each situation is associated a thermal transient (or several in the case of different line sections). In the case where, for a given situation, there are physically two transients, such as heat-up–cool-down for example, it is customary in B3600 to combine these two transients into a single one. For each situation, one supplies n tables which represent the analysis of the same thermal transient at different locations on the line (for each thickness or each discontinuity). These numbers must belong to the list of numbers supplied under the keyword NUME_RESU_THER of the factor keyword RESU_THER. 6.10.6 Operand COMBINABLE ♦ COMBINABLE = /'OUI', [DEFAUT] /'NON', [Kn] This keyword indicates whether a situation is combinable with the others inside its group (general case). In the case where COMBINABLE='NON', this means that the situation is a sub-cycle. 6.11 Example of use The test case rccm02 provides a complete example of use. For further information, one may refer to the document U2.09.03. 7 Operands specific to the option MOMENT_EQUIVALENT of type B3600 This factor keyword makes it possible to define a mechanical analysis result. 7.1 Operand RESULTAT / CHAM_GD / ♦ CHAM_GD = cham_effo , [cham_elem] / ♦ RESULTAT = resu, / [evol_elas] / [evol_noli] / TOUT_ORDRE = 'OUI' , / NUME_ORDRE = lordre , [l_I] / INST = linst , [l_R] ◊ NOM_CHAM = 'EFGE_ELNO', [DEFAUT] The analysis result (element fields at nodes of generalised forces) may be defined: - either an element field: cham_effo, which is of type EFGE_ELNO. The operator then computes the equivalent moment at each node. - or a data structure resultat for which the symbolic field EFGE_ELNO has been computed beforehand (CALC_CHAMP). The operator then computes the equivalent moment at each node and for each time instant defined by the user, then, on the model of CREA_CHAMP/EXTR/TYPE_MAXI=’MAXI_ABS’, it computes the temporal maxima (in absolute value) of the 4 components MT, MFY, MFZ and MEQ. 8 Operands specific to results of type ZE200a and ZE200b 8.1 Preliminaries From several results of mechanical analyses on a piping line, one computes only level A criteria of the RCC-M (therefore no option 'PM_PB'). The methods 'ZE200a' and 'ZE200b' are very similar. Indeed only the name ZE200 exists in the RCC-M (and not ZE200a and ZE200b). The difference between the two methods lies in the definition of the pressure loading. In 'ZE200b', the pressure loading is in the form of a transient and therefore requires an analysis on the 2D or 3D mesh in order to extract on the segment the stresses due to the pressure, whereas in 'ZE200a' the pressure enters into the equations of type B3600. Preliminary analyses to be carried out in code_aster or to be extracted from the OAR database (if available): - Analysis of each thermal transient, on the 2D or 3D mesh. - Beam-type analyses (elastic analysis) for each loading (one uses only the moments, expressed in a frame local to each element, a frame assumed identical for all the results) making up each of the two stabilised states of each situation. The data required for the post-processing are summarised here: - The material (assumed unique at first) which the segment under study passes through: isotropic elastic material to which one must add the fatigue curve, E_REFE, M_KE and N_KE. - The geometry of the piping line. - Stress indices - The operating scenario (available in OAR) containing the list of situations: - For each situation: - Numbers of occurrences of each situation. - Pressure and mean temperature of each stabilised state if 'ZE200a'. - Associated pressure transient if 'ZE200b'. - List of the mechanical loadings of each stabilised state. - The group to which the situation belongs. - The associated thermal transient. The temperature during the situation if one wishes to assess the environmental fatigue resistance. - The definition of each mechanical loading (including the earthquake), identified by its number, with, for information, the name of the load case, and the torsor of generalised moments corresponding to this loading, to be applied at the boundaries of the model. - The results of the thermal analyses: extraction of the stresses on a segment of the 2D or 3D finite-element model. One therefore has one thermal analysis per transient. 8.1.1 Option SN Option making it possible to compute the level A criteria (excluding fatigue), which aim to protect the equipment against the damage of progressive deformation. They require the analysis of the range of variation of the linearised stress at a point, denoted Sn, and of the amplitude Sn . Note: With the option ‘SN’, the analysis is carried out without combination between the situations defined: each situation will be processed in succession. In order to have the quantities (grandeurs) with combination between each situation, one must use the option ‘FATIGUE’ or 'EFAT'. 8.1.2 Option FATIGUE The fatigue analyses (option ‘FATIGUE’) are carried out in the sense of the RCCM ZE200 on the analysis segment. Two fictitious transients are thus identified in order to combine two situations with each other R7.04.03. 8.1.3 Option EFAT The environmental fatigue analyses (option ‘EFAT’) are carried out on the analysis segment. Two fictitious transients are thus identified in order to combine two situations with each other. The effects of the PWR environment on the usage factor are then taken into account. One must add the factor keyword 'ENVIRONNEMENT' and the keywords 'O_ETOILE' and 'TABL_TEMP' under each occurrence of the factor keyword 'SITUATION' R7.04.03. 8.2 Operand MATER ♦ MATER = mat Name of the material containing, for the analysed segment, the characteristics defined under the keywords ELAS and RCCM of DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 (E, NU, ALPHA, WOHLER, E_REFE, M_KE, N_KE, SM) Note on the fatigue curves: The question of the extension of the fatigue curve and the notion of endurance limit are discussed in §9.1.1 . 8.3 Operand SY_MAX ◊ SY_MAX = symax, Conventional yield limit for the maximum temperature reached during the cycle. This operand is used only for the analysis of the thermal ratcheting. If the yield limit SY_MAX is not defined, one takes the value defined under the operand SY_02 of the keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. 8.4 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE = / ‘TRESCA’, [DEFAUT] / ‘TOUT_INST’ There are two methods for selecting the time instants when analysing Sn or Sp: - the method 'TRESCA' carries out a pre-selection of the time instants based on the signed Tresca stress of each transient; it is the faster of the two methods and it is therefore taken by default if the user specifies nothing. It is nevertheless less robust than the second method R7.04.03 - the method 'TOUT_INST' combines all the possibilities of time instants and may be more costly in run time, especially when an earthquake is taken into account. 8.5 Operand TYPE_KE ◊ TYPE_KE = / ‘KE_MECA’, [DEFAUT] / ‘KE_MIXTE’ The elastoplastic correction factor Ke may be computed in two ways R7.04.03: - KE_MECA: this is the original method, the only one available in versions earlier than version 7.2; - KE_MIXTE: this method decomposes the range of variation of the alternating stresses into a thermal part and a mechanical part. It has been authorised since the 1997 modification of the RCC-M. 8.6 Operand SOUS_CYCL ◊ SOUS_CYCL = / ‘NON’, [DEFAUT] / ‘OUI’ The usage factor due to the sub-cycles of all the situations may or may not be taken into account. 8.7 Keyword INDI_SIGM ♦ INDI_SIGM=_F( ... ), Values of the stress indices to be used in the fatigue analysis (values codified in the RCC-M B3683). The user supplies, for the analysis segment, the values of C1, C2, C3, K1, K2, K3. For a piping junction, the user then enters only the values of K2 and of C2 which correspond to the body and to the nozzle. 8.8 Keyword TUYAU ♦ TUYAU =_F( ♦ R = r, [R] ♦ EP = ep, [R] / ♦ I = i, [R] / ♦ R_TUBU = rt, [R] ♦ R_CORP = rc, [R] ♦ I_TUBU = it, [R] ♦ I_CORP = ic, [R] ), Geometric characteristics of the piping: thickness EP, radius R and moment of inertia I. In the case of a piping junction, one also enters the radius of the body and of the nozzle and one substitutes for the inertia I the inertias of the body and of the nozzle (I_TUBU and I_CORP). 8.9 Keyword CHAR_MECA This factor keyword makes it possible to define, for each mechanical loading appearing in the situations, the torsors applied at the boundaries of the model, coming from beam-type analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different mechanical loadings in the set of situations. 8.9.1 Operand NUME_CHAR Number of the mechanical loading. This number is used to define the loadings associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 8.9.2 Operand NOM_CHAR Name of the mechanical loading (optional). 8.9.3 Operands MX / MY / MZ ♦ MX = mx, [R] ♦ MY = my, [R] ♦ MZ = mz, [R] Generalised moments coming from analyses of the piping line, of beam type, for each loading. Warning: this assumes that these values are supplied in a frame consistent with the one used for the 2D or 3D modelling of the component. 8.9.4 Operands MX_CORP / MX_TUBU, MY_CORP / MY_TUBU, … ♦ MX_CORP = mxc, [R] ♦ MY_CORP = myc, [R] ♦ MZ_CORP = mzc, [R] ♦ MX_TUBU = mxt, [R] ♦ MY_TUBU = myt, [R] ♦ MZ_TUBU = mzt, [R] Generalised moments applied to the body and the nozzle of a branch connection. Their meaning is identical to that of the operands MX, MY, … used for the piping lines. 8.10 Keyword RESU_THER This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the thermal analyses. It is repeatable as many times as there are different thermal analyses. 8.10.1 Operand NUME_RESU_THER ♦ NUME_RESU_THER = numtran [I] Number of the thermal transients. This number is used to identify the thermal transient associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 8.10.2 Operand TABL_RESU_THER ♦ TABL_RESU_THER = table [tabl_post_releve] Table produced by POST_RELEVE_T, containing, for each transient thermal analysis, the record of the stresses due to the thermal loading on the section of the 2D or 3D mesh chosen by the user at different time instants of the transient. The origin of the section must be the inner skin. 8.11 Keyword RESU_PRES (if 'ZE200b') This factor keyword makes it possible to define the results of the pressure analyses in the form of a transient. It is repeatable as many times as there are different pressure analyses when one uses the method 'ZE200b'. 8.11.1 Operand NUME_RESU_PRES ♦ NUME_RESU_PRES = numtran [I] Number of the pressure transients. This number is used to identify the pressure transient associated with each situation (see keyword SITUATION). 8.11.2 Operand TABL_RESU_PRES ♦ TABL_RESU_PRES = table [tabl_post_releve] Table produced by POST_RELEVE_T, containing, for each transient pressure analysis, the record of the stresses due to the pressure loading on the section of the 2D or 3D mesh chosen by the user at different time instants of the transient. 8.12 Keyword SEISME A single loading of type SEISME may be defined for all the groups of situations. 8.12.1 Operands NUME_SITU / NOM_SITU / NB_OCCUR / NB_CYCL_SEISME ♦ NUME_SITU = numsitu, [I] ◊ NOM_SITU = nomsitu, [Kn] ♦ NB_OCCUR = nbocc, [I] ♦ NB_CYCL_SEISME = nbsss, [I] Number, name and number of occurrences of the seismic situation. NB_CYCL_SEISME is the number of cycles associated with each occurrence of the earthquake, regarded as sub-cycles in the analysis of the usage factor. 8.12.2 Operands CHAR_ETAT ♦ CHAR_ETAT = num_char_meca , [L_I] Number of the mechanical loading (corresponding to the keyword NUME_CHAR of the factor keyword CHAR_MECA) associated with the seismic situation. 8.13 Keyword SITUATION This factor keyword makes it possible to define the situations. It is repeatable as many times as there are situations. 8.13.1 Operands NUME_SITU / NOM_SITU / NB_OCCUR ♦ NUME_SITU = numsitu, [I] ◊ NOM_SITU = nomsitu, [Kn] ♦ NB_OCCUR = nbocc, [I] Number, name and number of occurrences of the situation. 8.13.2 Operand NUME_GROUPE / NUME_PASSAGE /NUME_PARTAGE ♦ NUME_GROUPE = (numgroup1, numgroup2, ...) , [L_I] ◊ NUME_PASSAGE= (num1, num2, ...), [L_I] ◊ NUME_PARTAGE= num1 [I] One indicates under NUME_GROUPE the group number or numbers to which the situation belongs. If the situation is a passage situation, one indicates under NUME_PASSAGE the numbers of the various groups which it links (20 groups at most). When a situation provides the passage between n groups, it necessarily belongs to these n groups (the numbers under NUME_PASSAGE must appear under NUME_GROUPE ). Note: Conversely, a situation may belong to different groups without being a passage situation between these groups (the numbers under NUME_GROUPE are not necessarily under NUME_PASSAGE) If the situation belongs to a sharing group, one indicates under NUME_PARTAGE the number of this sharing group. Notes: No relation exists between the number of an operating group (NUME_GROUPE) and the number of a sharing group (NUME_PARTAGE) A situation may belong to at most one sharing group 8.13.3 Operand COMBINABLE ◊ COMBINABLE = /'OUI , [DEFAUT] /'NON', [Kn] This keyword indicates whether a situation is combinable with the others inside its group (general case). In the case where COMBINABLE='NON', this means that the situation is a sub-cycle. 8.13.4 Operands PRES_A / PRES_B (if 'ZE200a') ♦ PRES_A = presa , [R] ♦ PRES_B = presb , [R] Pressures associated with each of the two stabilised states of the situation in the method 'ZE200a'. 8.13.5 Operands CHAR_ETAT_A / CHAR_ETAT_B ♦ CHAR_ETAT_A = num_char_meca , [I] ♦ CHAR_ETAT_B = num_char_meca , [I] Number of the mechanical loading associated with each stabilised state. This number corresponds to the keyword NUME_CHAR of the factor keyword CHAR_MECA. A single mechanical loading is associated with each stabilised state. 8.13.6 Operand NUME_RESU_THER ◊ NUME_RESU_THER = num_tran [I] Number of the thermal transient associated with the situation. There may be 0 or 1 transient per line section (which corresponds to mesh-cell groups) for each situation. This number corresponds to the keyword NUME_RESU_THER of the factor keyword RESU_THER. In the case where, for a given situation, there are physically two transients for one section, such as heat-up–cool-down for example, it is customary to combine these two transients into a single one. 8.13.7 Operand NUME_RESU_PRES (if 'ZE200b') ◊ NUME_RESU_PRES = num_tran [I] Number of the pressure transient associated with the situation if the method is 'ZE200b'. There may be 0 or 1 transient per line section (which corresponds to mesh-cell groups) for each situation. These numbers correspond to the keyword NUME_RESU_PRES of the factor keyword RESU_PRES. 8.13.8 Operands O_ETOILE / TABL_TEMP ◊ O_ETOILE = oet , [R] ◊ TABL_TEMP = tabtemp, [table] These two operands are necessary for the analysis of the environmental fatigue and therefore when calling the option 'EFAT'. For each situation, O_ETOILE represents the oxygen content (it is regarded here as constant) and TABL_TEMP is the table of the temperatures as a function of time during the transient. Note: The table under the keyword TABL_TEMP must be defined at the same time instants as the thermal transient of the situation under TABL_RESU_THER. The temperature must imperatively be defined on the nodes of the analysis segment considered (a column ABSC_CURV is therefore required). 8.14 Keyword ENVIRONNEMENT This factor keyword makes it possible to compute the environmental fatigue resistance. It is not repeatable because it lists the data required for the analysis but common to all the situations. 8.14.1 Operand FEN_INTEGRE ♦ FEN_INTEGRE = fenint, [R] Integrated Fen, which enters into the analysis of the environmental factor. 8.14.2 Operand CRIT_EPSI ♦ CRIT_EPSI = epsilim, [R] Strain threshold from which the environmental factor does not come into play. 8.14.3 Operands TABL_YOUNG ♦ TABL_YOUNG = tabyoung, [table] Young's modulus as a function of the temperature. A linear interpolation is carried out from this table in order to evaluate Young's modulus, which enters into the analysis of the environmental factor. This table must necessarily contain the parameters named 'TEMP' and 'YOUNG'. 8.14.4 Operands S_ETOILE ♦ S_ETOILE = set, [R] Sulphur content of the metal analysed (therefore common to all the situations), equal to a constant. 8.14.5 Operands SEUIL_EPSI_INF / SEUIL_EPSI_SUP ♦ SEUIL_EPSI_INF = epsimin , [R] ♦ SEUIL_EPSI_SUP = epsimax , [R] Thresholds which enter into the analysis of the strain rate. 8.14.6 Operands A_ENV / B_ENV / C_ENV ♦ A_ENV = aenv , [R] ♦ B_ENV = benv , [R] ♦ C_ENV = cenv , [R] Constants which enter into the general expression of the environmental factor. 8.14.7 Operands SEUIL_T_INF / SEUIL_T_SUP / VALE_T_INF / VALE_T_SUP / VALE_T_MOY_NUM / VALE_T_MOY_DEN ♦ SEUIL_T_INF = tempmin , [R] ♦ SEUIL_T_SUP = tempmax , [R] ♦ VALE_T_INF = valmin , [R] ♦ VALE_T_SUP = valmax , [R] ♦ VALE_T_MOY_NUM = valmoynum , [R] ♦ VALE_T_MOY_DEN = valmoyden , [R] Thresholds which enter into the analysis of the temperature T . 8.15 Table produced and example The table produced by POST_RCCM depends on the analysis OPTION and on the type of result requested under the operand TYPE_RESU: - if TYPE_RESU=’VALE_MAX’ (default option): the table is simple and contains only the maximum parameters of the various quantities (grandeurs) (Sn, Sn , Sp, Salt, Fu, Fu_environnement and the quantities (grandeurs) related to ratcheting) at the two ends - if TYPE_RESU=’DETAILS’: the table is much richer. It contains the maximum parameters mentioned previously (row 'MAXI') plus all the parameters computed, for each situation (rows of type 'SITU') and each combination of situations (rows of type 'COMB'), with or without earthquake, and the combinations which actually entered into the analysis of the usage factor (row 'FACT'). It is then strongly recommended to print the table with successive filters so that it is easy to use. - If TYPE_RESU=’SYSTUS’ : the table contains all the parameters computed for all the situations and combinations which actually entered into the analysis of the usage factor (row ' FACT '). - Printout of the maxima: if TYPE_RESU=’VALE_MAX’ or with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=_F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='MAXI'), the table produced may contain, depending on the option requested, the following parameters: SN_MAX, SN _MAX, SIGM_M_PRES, SN_THER_MAX, CRIT_LINE_MAX , SP_THER_MAX, CRIT_PARA_MAX, SP_MAX, SALT_MAX, FU_TOTAL , FEN_TOTAL, FEN_INTEGRE and FUEN_TOTAL. - Printout of the quantities (grandeurs) of each situation: with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=(_F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='SITU' ), _F(NOM_PARA='SEISME', VALE_K='AVEC' ou ‘ SANS’) ), the table produced contains, depending on the option requested, the following parameters for each of the situations (with or without earthquake): SN, INST_SN_1, INST_SN_2, SN , INST_SN _1,INST_SN _2, SIG_PRES_MOY, SN_THER, CRIT_LINE, SP_THER, CRIT_PARAB, SP1(MECA), INST_SALT_1, INST_SALT_2, SALT and FU_UNIT . - Printout of the quantities (grandeurs) of each combination of situations: with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=( _F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='COMB' ), _F(NOM_PARA='SEISME', VALE_K='AVEC' ou ‘ SANS’) ), the table produced contains, depending on the option requested, the following parameters for each of the combinations of situations (with or without earthquake): SN, INST_SN_1, INST_SN_2, SN , INST_SN _1,INST_SN _2, SIG_PRES_MOY, SN_THER, CRIT_LINE, SP_THER, CRIT_PARAB, SP1(MECA), INST_SALT_1, INST_SALT_2, SALT and FU_UNIT . - Printout of the combinations of situations which entered into the analysis of the usage factor: with a filter in IMPR_TABLE: FILTRE=( _F(NOM_PARA='TYPE', VALE_K='FACT' ), ), the table produced contains, depending on the option requested, the following parameters for each of the combinations of situations which entered into the analysis of the usage factor FU_TOTAL : SN, INST_SN_1, INST_SN_2, SN , INST_SN _1,INST_SN _2, INST_SALT_1, INST_SALT_2, SALT, FU_UNIT, NOCC_PRIS, FU_PARTIEL. If the option ‘ EFAT ’ is called, the following quantities (grandeurs) are added to the maxima relative to the option 'FATIGUE': FEN_TOTAL, FEN_INTEGRE and FUEN_TOTAL. In addition, if TYPE_RESU=’DETAILS’ , two quantities (grandeurs) are added to the rows of type 'FACT': FEN and FUEN_PARTIEL. For monitoring the analyses, additional information may be found in the message file, in particular for the option FATIGUE. One can thus follow, at the origin and then at the end of the segment: the processing of each of the situations and then of the combinations of situations, and the display of FU_TOTAL (including the part related to the sub-cycles and the part related to the seismic sub-cycles) The test cases rccm13a ('ZE200a') and rccm13b ('ZE200b') provide complete examples of use. For further information, one may also refer to the document U2.09.03. 9 Operands specific to results of type EVOLUTION For a precise description of the analyses carried out by these options, one may consult the document R7.04.03 and the user's guide U2.09.03. The material characteristics required for the analysis of the criteria are to be defined by the command DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. The computed values and the limit values are stored in the table tabl_post_rccm, which one prints by means of the command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. Note on the use of the material characteristics as a function of the temperature: For the post-processing, the RCC-M B rules require the use of the material characteristics, such as Sm, at the maximum temperature of the transients. The operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 nevertheless allows the definition of the material characteristics as a function of the temperature (factor keyword RCCM_FO). With the option 'EVOLUTION', the user must define the material characteristics, for the post-processing, only by the factor keyword RCCM of the command DEFI_MATERIAU. Indeed, in order to use this option 'EVOLUTION', the user has to supply as input data only stresses, the thermal evolution being ignored even in the case where it exists in the previous analysis steps. With the option 'EVOLUTION', the use of the characteristics as a function of the temperature therefore leads to an execution error. The analysis is carried out in post-processing of one or more thermomechanical analyses (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE) on a 2D or 3D modelling. The results are transmitted via stress tables, extracted on the analysis segment or segments. These stress tables may be created by the commands POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE. The possible analysis options are: 1. level 0 criteria by the option PM_PB; 2. level A criteria (excluding fatigue) by the option SN; 3. fatigue criteria (also of level A) by the option FATIGUE_ZH210; 4. crack-initiation criteria in singular zones by the option AMORCAGE. The first three options may be called alone or simultaneously. The last option may be called only alone: it indeed requires a record of the stresses on a circular cutting line around the geometric singularity, whereas the other options are dedicated to segments crossing the structure. This option is well suited to cases where there are few situations to study. It is not possible to take seismic situations into account. 9.1 Operand MATER ♦ MATER = mat It is the material containing the characteristics useful to POST_RCCM and defined under the keyword RCCM of DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. Note on the fatigue curves: For small stress amplitudes, the problem of extending the fatigue curve may arise: for example, for the RCCM fatigue curves beyond 106 cycles, the corresponding stress, 180 MPa, is regarded as an endurance limit, that is, any stress lower than 180 MPa must produce a zero usage factor, or an infinite allowable number of cycles. One recalls that the fatigue curve is defined in the material properties (keyword FATIGUE / WOHLER) as being the number of cycles to failure as a function of the half-amplitude of the stress Salt. The small stress amplitudes therefore correspond to the extension to the left of the curve. Several situations may arise, according to the type of extension adopted in DEFI_FONCTION: - if PROL_GAUCHE = 'EXCLU' or 'CONSTANT', the analysis is carried out by assuming that the first value of the Wöhler curve supplied is the endurance limit of the material. In other words, any alternating stress smaller than the first value indicated in the DEFI_FONCTION will correspond to a zero usage factor. The method adopted here therefore does correspond to the notion of endurance limit; - if PROL_GAUCHE = 'LINEAIRE', the curve is extended in a linear manner. Warning: the extension is not carried out in logarithmic coordinates, so one may have non-negligible usage factors even for low values of Salt. In order to return to the notion of endurance limit, it is then recommended to add, in the definition of the curve, the allowable number of cycles for a very low value of Salt (computed by hand, for example by interpolation with a power law). 9.2 Operand SY_MAX ◊ SY_MAX = symax, Conventional yield limit for the maximum temperature reached during the cycle. This operand is used only for the analysis of the thermal ratcheting (cf. § 9.1.4.2). If the yield limit SY_MAX is not defined, one takes the value defined under the operand SY_02 of the keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. If this operand is not defined either, the analysis of the thermal ratcheting is impossible. 9.3 Operand RAYON_MOYEN ◊ RHO_MOYEN = rho, (défaut : -1.) Topological curvature of the mean line at the intersection with the extraction segment in the XOY plane of the axisymmetric model. The default value -1 implies that the segment being processed is locally straight. Otherwise, the curvature must be strictly positive. This operand will be taken into account if the operand AXIS = ‘OUI’. 9.4 Option PM_PB Option making it possible to compute the level 0 criteria, which aim to protect the equipment against the damage of excessive deformation, of plastic instability and of elastic and elastoplastic instability. These criteria require the analysis of the equivalent stresses of membrane Pm , of local membrane Pl , of bending Pb and of membrane plus bending Pm+Pb . The necessary operands are MATER, the stress table TABL_RESU_MECA (built by POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE after the mechanical analysis at the post-processing location) and possibly the stress table TABL_SIGM_THER built from an analysis with the thermal loading alone. The analysis points are the two ends of the analysis segment. If several extraction segments have been used to define one and the same stress table, the analysis is carried out in succession for each of them. This option makes it possible to obtain the peak stress F in the output table of the operator, which is useful for the fatigue and progressive-deformation analyses. The limit values are Sm and 1.5 Sm, Sm being the allowable stress as a function of the material and of the temperature, given by the keyword SM of the keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. Notes: The analysis of PM and PMPB is carried out from the primary stresses only, therefore excluding stresses of thermal origin. If TABL_SIGM_THER is supplied, one assumes that the result indicated in TABL_RESU_MECA corresponds to a thermomechanical analysis and one therefore subtracts the thermal stresses from it. If only TABL_RESU_MECA is supplied, the analysis is carried out directly from the stresses indicated in the table. Note: For the option PM_PB in EVOLUTION , one recovers in the output table of the operator the peak stresses F which are defined by F = \sigma_{\text{totale}} - (\text{Pm\_Pb} + Q) where Q is the thermal secondary stress defined by Q = Pm_{\text{thermique}} + Pb_{\text{thermique}} . 9.5 Option SN Option making it possible to compute the level A criteria (excluding fatigue), which aim to protect the equipment against the damage of progressive deformation. They require the analysis of the range of variation of the linearised stress at a point, denoted Sn . If the user requests it (presence of the operand TABL_SIGM_THER) one also carries out the analysis of Sn . If the user requests it (presence of the operands TABL_SIGM_THER and TABL_RESU_PRES) one also carries out the analysis of the thermal ratcheting. The necessary operands are MATER and the stress table TABL_RESU_MECA (built by POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE after the mechanical analysis at the post-processing location) to be supplied in the keyword TRANSITOIRE. The analysis points are the two ends of the analysis segment. If several extraction segments have been used to define one and the same stress table, the analysis is carried out in succession for each of them. The limit value of Sn is 3 Sm, Sm being the allowable stress as a function of the material and of the temperature, given by the keyword SM of the factor keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. Note: The keyword TABL_RESU_MECA may be repeated several times under a single keyword TRANSITOIRE. For the analysis of Sn and Sn\ , there will nevertheless be no combination between the situations thus defined: each stress table will be processed in succession. 9.5.1 Computation of Sn If the operand TABL_SIGM_THER of the factor keyword TRANSITOIRE is present, one also carries out the analysis of Sn\ . In order for the analysis to be consistent and in accordance with the RCC-M, the stresses supplied in TABL_SIGM_THER must have been obtained with a thermal loading alone, it being known that the result given by TABL_RESU_MECA may be due to a combination of this thermal loading with other loadings. The time instants of the table TABL_SIGM_THER must therefore correspond to those of the table TABL_RESU_MECA. 9.5.2 Computation of the thermal ratcheting If the operands TABL_SIGM_THER and TABL_RESU_PRES of the factor keyword TRANSITOIRE are present, one also carries out the analysis of the thermal ratcheting. For this, one must also have previously defined the conventional yield limit for the maximum temperature reached during the cycle, either by the operand SY_MAX of POST_RCCM, or by the operand SY_02 of the keyword RCCM in DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. If no yield limit is defined, the analysis of the thermal ratcheting is impossible. In order for the analysis to be consistent and in accordance with the RCC-M, the stresses supplied in TABL_RESU_PRES must have been obtained with a pressure loading alone. In the result table there appear, for each end of each analysis segment, the yield limit SY, the range of variation of the stress of thermal origin SP_THER, the maximum of the general membrane stress due to the pressure SIGM_M_PRES and two allowable maximum values of the range of variation of the thermal stress, computed either by assuming a linear temperature variation in the wall (VALE_MAXI_LINE), or by assuming a parabolic temperature variation in the wall (VALE_MAXI_PARAB). 9.6 Option FATIGUE_ZH210 Option making it possible to compute the usage factor resulting from the combination of one or more transients, according to the method of RCC-M appendix ZH210. The range of variation of the stress at each end of the analysis segment is computed from the stress tables TABL_RESU_MECA, for each combination of time instants belonging to the transient or transients defined by the user. One then applies a combination and cumulation method in order to obtain the total usage factor, cf. R7.04.03. The time instants corresponding to the extreme states must be specified by the user by the operands NUME_ORDRE, INST or LIST_INST. Notes: The keyword TABL_RESU_MECA may be repeated several times under a single keyword TRANSITOIRE. For the fatigue analysis, the results contained in each stress table will be combined with one another. For the operands NUME_ORDRE, INST or LIST_INST, a possible confusion is the use of the list of time instants of the thermomechanical analyses (MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE) instead of the list of time instants corresponding to the extreme states expected by the operator POST_RCCM. In the first case, all the analysis time instants are then regarded as stress extrema and lead to run times which may be large. 9.7 Option AMORCAGE Option making it possible to compute the crack-initiation factor at a singular zone. For this option, the stresses are to be supplied as input in the table TABL_SIGM_THETA and must correspond to the extraction of the stresses, in the local frame, on a circular cutting line of diameter D_AMORC (material parameter defined in the RCC-M) around the geometric singularity. The stress tables may be created by using the operator MACR_LIGN_COUPE(TYPE=’ARC’). For this option, it is also mandatory to define in the material properties (keyword RCCM) the coefficients of the crack-initiation law (A_AMORC and B_AMORC), the diameter of the circle on which the stresses are extracted (D_AMORC) and the coefficient between stress and effective stress (R_AMORC). 9.8 Operand TYPE_KE ◊ TYPE_KE = / ‘KE_MECA’, [DEFAUT] / ‘KE_MIXTE’ The elastoplastic correction factor Ke may be computed in two ways R7.04.03: - KE_MECA: this is the original method, the only one available in versions earlier than version 7.2; - KE_MIXTE: this method decomposes the range of variation of the alternating stresses into a thermal part and a mechanical part. It has been authorised since the 1997 modification of the RCC-M. 9.9 Keyword TRANSITOIRE This factor keyword makes it possible to define the transient or transients to be studied. 9.9.1 Operand TABL_RESU_MECA ◊ TABL_RESU_MECA = tabmeca Table of the stresses on the analysis segment, built for example by POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE from mechanical results of type evol_elas and evol_noli. 9.9.2 Operand TABL_SIGM_THER ◊ TABL_SIGM_THER= tabth Table of the stresses on the analysis segment, built for example by POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE on a result obtained with a thermal loading alone. This keyword allows in particular the analysis of Sn [§9.1.4.1]. 9.9.3 Operand TABL_SIGM_THETA ◊ TABL_SIGM_THETA= sigt This operand is to be used only in the case of the option AMORCAGE [§9.1.6]. It corresponds to the table of the stresses, in the local frame, on a circular cutting line around the geometric singularity. The table must necessarily contain the columns ANGLE, ABSC_CURV, INST and SIZZ, where SIZZ corresponds to the stress sigma_theta_theta in the local frame of the cutting line. The diameter of the circle on which the stresses are extracted is a material parameter (operand D_AMORC of DEFI_MATERIAU / RCCM) Such a table may be built by means of the operator MACR_LIGN_COUPE (TYPE='ARC', REPERE='CYLINDRIQUE'). 9.9.4 Operand TABL_RESU_PRES ◊ TABL_RESU_PRES= tabpres Table of the stresses on the analysis segment, built for example by POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE on a result obtained with the pressure loading alone. This keyword allows the analysis of the thermal ratcheting [§9.1.4.2]. 9.9.5 Operand NB_OCCUR ◊ NB_OCCUR = / nocc, / 1, [DEFAUT] Number of occurrences for the analysis of the usage factor. 9.10 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / TOUT_INST / INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ TOUT_ORDRE, TOUT_INST, INST, LIST_INST These keywords allow the selection of the time instants corresponding to the fields grouped in the stress tables tabmeca, tabth and/or sigp under the symbolic names previously specified. ◊ PRECISION, CRITERE Keywords (optional) defining the precision (10-6 by default in relative terms) and the search criterion (RELATIF by default) of an order number from a time-instant value. 9.10.1 Warning on the list of analysis time instants In the post-processing of the stress analyses in order to check the criteria of RCC-M B3200, one must distinguish two lists of analyses. In the stress analysis, it is the user's responsibility to supply a first list of analysis time instants with a time-step subdivision fine enough to ensure that all the extreme values of the stresses during the transient are computed. For the post-processing with the operator POST_RCCM, a second list of time instants to be supplied by the user, via the operands TOUT_ORDRE, TOUT_INST, INST or LIST_INST and distinct from the previous list of computed time instants, indicates the time instants corresponding to the extreme states expected by the operator POST_RCCM. The confusion of these two lists is a frequent error. By supplying the same list of time instants, all the analysis time instants are then regarded as stress extrema . This leads to run times which may be large and to excessive values of usage factors. 9.11 Execution phase One checks that the analysis time instants of the table tabth are identical to those of the table tabmeca. On the other hand, one cannot check that the thermal transients which contributed to the mechanical results tabth and tabmeca are identical. It is up to the user to ensure consistency (including the material data). > Note: If the various tables supplied as input contain the coordinates of the points, consistency checks are carried out: alignment of the points (for the options PM_PB, SN and FATIGUE_ZH210) or diameter of the circular cutting line (option AMORCAGE); check of the consistency between the various situations. It is therefore strongly recommended not to delete the coordinates of the points in the stress-extraction tables. 9.12 Example of use An example of use of the operator POST_RCCM with results of type EVOLUTION may be found in the test case rccm01 . An analysis of the RCCM criteria proceeds in the following manner: 1. definition of the material parameters and of the fatigue curve, 2. definitions of the mechanical and thermal loadings, 3. linear or non-linear thermomechanical analysis, 4. (if analysis of Sn ) mechanical analysis with the thermal loading alone, 5. (if analysis of the thermal ratcheting) mechanical analysis with the pressure alone, 6. definition of the analysis segment and extraction of the results with POST_RELEVE_T or MACR_LIGN_COUPE, then (possibly in restart): SN1=POST_RCCM(MATER=MAT, TYPE_RESU='VALE_MAX', TYPE_RESU_MECA='EVOLUTION', OPTION='SN', TITRE='SN, RESULTAT: RESU2b AVEC RESUTH', TRANSITOIRE=_F(TABL_RESU_MECA = T_RESU2b, TABL_SIGM_THER = T_RESUTHb, ) ) IMPR_TABLE ( TABLE = sn1 ) An example of use of the operator POST_RCCM with results of type EVOLUTION for the option AMORCAGE may be found in the test case rccm09 . For further information, one may refer to the documents U2.09.03 and R7.04.03. 10 Bibliography 1. «RCC-M: Design and Construction Rules for the mechanical equipment of PWR nuclear islands. 1993 edition» Published by the AFCEN: French association for the design and construction rules for the equipment of electro-nuclear boilers. 1.
