u4.83.31 Operator COMB_FOURIER u4.83.31 Operator COMB_FOURIER 1 Purpose Recombine the FOURIER modes of a resultat data structure in particular directions. The modes are produced for an 'AXIS_FOURIER' model by the macro-command MACRO_ELAS_MULT U4.51.02. This is possible for the displacements, the reactions, the strain and stress fields in elasticity and for the temperature and flux fields in thermal analysis. The data structure produced is of type comb_fourier. 2 Syntax comb_fourier = COMB_FOURIER( ◆ RESULTAT = fourier_elas / fourier_ther, ◆ ANGLE = float, ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL", / "REAC_NODA", / "SIEF_ELGA", / "EPSI_ELNO", / "SIGM_ELNO", / "TEMP", / "FLUX_ELNO", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands Reminder: The FOURIER recombination on the displacements is written: u(\theta )=\sum_{l=0}^{N}\left[\underset{{A}^{s}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{(\begin{array}{ccc}\cosl\theta & 0& 0\\ 0& \cosl\theta & 0\\ 0& 0& -\sinl\theta \end{array})}}{u}_{l}^{s}+\underset{{A}^{a}}{\underset{\underbrace{}}{(\begin{array}{ccc}\sinl\theta & 0& 0\\ 0& \sinl\theta & 0\\ 0& 0& \cosl\theta \end{array})}}{u}_{l}^{a}\right] A symmetrical harmonic is therefore recombined with the matrix {A}^{s} , an antisymmetrical harmonic with the matrix {A}^{a} . The FOURIER recombination on the strains and the stresses is written: \varepsilon (\theta )=\sum_{l=0}^{N}(\left[\begin{array}{cc}\cosl\theta {I}_{4}& {0}_{4,2}\\ {0}_{2,4}& -\sinl\theta {I}_{2}\end{array}\right]{\varepsilon}_{l}^{s}+\left[\begin{array}{cc}\sinl\theta {I}_{4}& {0}_{4,2}\\ {0}_{2,4}& \cosl\theta {I}_{2}\end{array}\right]{\varepsilon}_{l}^{a}) 3.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = resu, Name of the concept of type fourier_elas or fourier_ther from which the modes will be recombined. 3.2 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM = nomsymb, Symbolic name of the recombined field or fields. 3.3 Operand ANGLE ♦ ANGLE = langl, Angle(s) in degrees of the section(s) where the FOURIER recombination takes place. 4 Example The example below carries out an analysis on 2 Fourier harmonics with MACRO_ELAS_MULT, enriches the concept of type RESULTAT with CALC_CHAMP, then recombines the computed fields with COMB_FOURIER. Calcul Fourier sur les deux premières harmoniques symétriques resu = MACRO_ELAS_MULT( MODELE = mo, CHAM_MATER = cm, CHAR_MECA_GLOBAL= bloqu, CAS_CHARGE= ( _F (MODE_FOURIER = 1, TYPE_MODE = 'SYME' , CHAR_MECA = ch, SOUS_TITRE = 'mode fourier 1 SYME'), _F (MODE_FOURIER = 2, TYPE_MODE = 'SYME' , CHAR_MECA = ch, SOUS_TITRE = 'mode fourier 2 SYME'),), ) Calcul des contraintes et des réactions nodales par CALC_CHAMP resu = CALC_CHAMP(reuse = resu, RESULTAT = resu, CONTRAINTE = 'SIGM_ELNO', FORCE = 'REAC_NODA', Recombinaison de Fourier sur les déplacements, réactions et contraintes pour 45° et 135° angl1 = 45. angl2 = 135. co_four = COMB_FOURIER( RESULTAT = resu, NOM_CHAM = ('DEPL','REAC_NODA','SIGM_ELNO'), ANGLE = (angl1,angl2),);

u4.84.01 Operator COMB_SISM_MODAL u4.84.01 Operator COMB_SISM_MODAL 1 Purpose Compute the response to a seismic loading, by the spectral modal approach, based on the combination of the modal responses, under the assumption of linear elastic constitutive behaviour. (Spectral response = response resulting from the combinations) The seismic loading consists of two parts: - the static deformation motion of the structure under the effect of the displacements imposed at the supports (driving motion), represented by the seismic differential displacements DDS; - the deformation motion relative to the static deflected shape (inertial), represented by the oscillator response spectrum SRO. The analysis is either single-support (identical excitation of all the supports by the same SRO) or multi-support (excitations differentiated according to the supports). In the multi-support case, the excitations are either all correlated with one another, or related to (uncorrelated) groups of correlated supports. The spectral modal approach makes it possible to estimate the probable mean maximum absolute values of the quantities of interest, obtained from the quadratic sum of the response to the DDS and of the inertial response. The spectral modal method is strictly limited to the evaluation of quantities depending linearly on the displacements: strains, stresses (excluding equivalent quantities), generalised forces, nodal forces, support reactions. Produces a concept of type mult_elas. 2 Syntax mode_meca = COMB_SISM_MODAL( ◆ MODE_MECA = mode_meca, ◇ / TOUT_ORDRE = / "OUI", / "NON", / NUME_ORDRE = int, / FREQ = float, / NUME_MODE = int, / LIST_FREQ = listr8, / LIST_ORDRE = listis, # Si: exists("FREQ") or exists("LIST_FREQ") ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◆ / AMOR_REDUIT = float, / LIST_AMOR = listr8, / AMOR_GENE = matr_asse_gene_r, ◇ MODE_CORR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("MODE_CORR", 'OUI') ◆ PSEUDO_MODE = mode_meca, ◇ FREQ_COUP = float, ◇ TYPE_ANALYSE = / "MONO_APPUI" (par défaut), / "MULT_APPUI", / "ENVELOPPE" # Si: is_in("TYPE_ANALYSE", ('MULT_APPUI', 'ENVELOPPE')) ◆ APPUIS = _F( ◆ NOM = text, ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ), # Si: equal_to("TYPE_ANALYSE", 'MONO_APPUI') ◆ SPECTRE = _F( ◆ LIST_AXE = / "X", / "Y", / "Z", ◆ SPEC_OSCI = formule / nappe, ◇ ECHELLE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ NATURE = / "ACCE" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "DEPL", ◇ CORR_FREQ = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ), # By default \mathit{prec}=\mathrm{1.0D}-3 . According to the value of the keyword CRITERE: 'RELATIF': the search interval is: > [\mathit{inst}(1-\mathit{prec}),\mathit{inst}(1+\mathit{prec})] 'ABSOLU': the search interval is: > [\mathit{inst}-\mathit{prec},\mathit{inst}+\mathit{prec}] 3.2 Modal damping Three possibilities exist for defining the modal damping: a list of reduced damping values supplied by the user in the form of a list of reals (l_R) or of a concept of type listr8 built by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01, or a generalised damping matrix (damping matrix projected onto the basis of the real eigenmodes). 3.2.1 Operand AMOR_REDUIT / AMOR_REDUIT = amor This operand makes it possible to supply the list of reduced damping values in the form of a list of reals (l_R). If the number of coefficients supplied is smaller than the number of eigenmodes taken into account, the last coefficient is assigned to the corresponding mode and to the following modes. 3.2.2 Operand LIST_AMOR / LIST_AMOR = lamor This operand makes it possible to supply the list of reduced damping values in the form of a concept of type listr8. If the number of reduced damping values is smaller than the number of eigenmodes taken into account, the last coefficient is assigned to the corresponding mode and to the following modes. Example: LIST_AMOR =(‘0.01’, ‘0.02’) first mode \xi =\text{0.01} and, for all the other modes, \xi =\text{0.02} 3.2.3 Operand AMOR_GENE / AMOR_GENE= amogene The name of the generalised damping matrix amogène produced by the operator PROJ_MATR_BASE U4.63.12 or PROJ_BASE U4.63.11 is given. Note For theoretical reasons (framework of COMB_SISM_MODAL restricted to “classical” damping) the damping matrix must be diagonal. 3.3 Corrections by pseudo-mode: operand MODE_CORR The modal basis used is in general incomplete. The evaluation of the probable mean upper bound of the response to a seismic excitation therefore requires a correction by a term representing the contribution of the neglected eigenmodes, in each earthquake direction, called pseudo-mode correction or static correction. For each earthquake direction, this correction is carried out by adding to the modal basis a pseudo-mode \Psi obtained from a static mode \varphi , the displacement field of the nodes of the structure subjected to a uniform acceleration in the direction considered , defined by: K\varphi =M\delta - K stiffness matrix of the structure - M mass matrix of the structure - \delta unit field in the earthquake direction The pseudo-mode \Psi is obtained by subtracting the static contributions of the modes taken into account: \Psi =\varphi -\sum_{r=1}^{\mathrm{nmod}}\frac{{p}_{r}}{{\omega}_{r}^{2}}{\Phi}_{r} with: - {\Phi}_{r} eigenmode of index r - {p}_{r} participation factor in the direction \delta In this direction \delta , for each quantity, the contribution of the neglected modes is given by: {R}_{t}={R}_{s}-\sum_{r=1}^{\mathrm{nmod}}{R}_{r} {R}_{s} is the quantity associated with the static mode The definition of the pseudo-mode correction is as follows: ◊ MODE_CORR = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT] Uniquement si MODE_CORR = 'OUI': ♦ PSEUDO_MODE = acce [mode_stat_acce] ◊ FREQ_COUP = freq [R] Compulsory if MODE_CORR = 'OUI', this keyword makes it possible to supply the displacement field(s) \phi of the nodes of the structure subjected to a uniform acceleration in one (or more) direction(s), field(s) computed by the operator MODE_STATIQUE with the keyword PSEUDO_MODE U4.52.14. For specific needs, it is also possible to supply a concept produced by CREA_RESU, by choosing TYPE_RESU='MODE_MECA' and by entering the keyword AXE of AFFE in order to indicate the direction corresponding to each field (defined by its order number) U4.44.12. For every earthquake direction in which the response is computed, a pseudo-mode is computed if acce is supplied. For the other quantities of interest (see the options u4.84.01-option-calcul) other than the displacement, it is important to compute these quantities mode by mode via CALC_CHAMP from the displacement fields \varphi coming from the operator MODE_STATIQUE/PSEUDO_MODE. By the very principle of the static analysis of the displacement fields \phi at the nodes of the structure subjected to a uniform acceleration via MODE_STATIQUE/PSEUDO_MODE, it is therefore impossible to deduce from them fields of the responses in relative velocity or in absolute acceleration. Thus, it is impossible to take the static correction by pseudo-mode into account for the options 'VITE', 'ACCE_ABSOLU' (see the options u4.84.01-option-calcul), with the exception of the absolute-acceleration response in the single-support case, where the absolute-acceleration field 'ACCE_ABSOLU' of the structure subjected to a uniform acceleration is known analytically. This is the unit field of the absolute acceleration at the translational degrees of freedom. This correction is carried out automatically whatever the value entered for the keyword MODE_CORR. Warning: selection of the pseudo-modes When the concept supplied to PSEUDO_MODE contains several definitions of pseudo-modes (with both AXE and GROUP_NO), only the part compatible with the current TYPE_ANALYSE is used: - In MONO_APPUI, only the pseudo-modes defined with AXE/DIRECTION are considered; - In MULT_APPUI, only the pseudo-modes defined with NOEUD or GROUP_NO are used. In order to guarantee a clear use, it is recommended to supply to COMB_SISM_MODAL a MODE_STATIQUE concept specific to each analysis configuration. ◊ FREQ_COUP = fcoup This keyword makes it possible to supply the frequency at which one reads, on the SRO, the value which will be used for the level of the pseudo-mode correction. This frequency normally corresponds to the cut-off frequency of the seismic signal, i.e. the frequency at which the SRO reaches (in absolute pseudo-acceleration) an asymptote. This keyword is particularly useful when the last frequency of the modal basis does not reach the cut-off frequency of the seismic signal, although it is nevertheless sufficient to take into account all the modes which predominate in the response of the structure (a practice which is not recommended). The value entered in FREQ_COUP is applied for all the earthquake directions taken into account in the analysis. If this keyword is absent, the last frequency existing in the modal basis MODE_MECA is used as soon as the pseudo-mode correction is activated (MODE_CORR = 'OUI'). In addition, the spectral value read on the spectrum corresponds to the smallest value of the damping. 3.4 Type of the excitation (single-support or multi-support) Three configurations are possible: - single-support: the structure is studied with the same driving motion at all the supports - multi-support: the structure is studied with several different driving motions at the supports and, possibly, differential displacements of the supports (DDS) - envelope: the structure is studied with several different driving motions at the supports, as in the multi-support case. For a given direction, only the maximum value of the spectra read at the desired frequency is used. Differential displacements of the supports (DDS) are not taken into account in this configuration. The treatment of the three types of excitation is different. The type of analysis is defined appropriately by the user via the operand TYPE_ANALYSE ♦ TYPE_ANALYSE = / 'MONO_APPUI' [DEFAUT] / 'MULT_APPUI' / 'ENVELOPPE' 3.5 Description of the loading The seismic loading is defined by: - one or more oscillator spectra - differential displacements of the support, only in the multi-support case 3.5.1 Single-support Only the oscillator spectra are defined for the single-support case. ♦ SPECTRE =_F( ♦ LIST_AXE = l_axe [l_axe] ♦ SPEC_OSCI = spec [nappe] ◊ ECHELLE = echel [R] ◊ CORR_FREQ = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT] ◊ NATURE = / 'ACCE' [DEFAUT] / 'VITE' / 'DEPL' ) 3.5.1.1 Oscillator spectrum > ♦ SPEC_OSCI = spec A single layer of oscillator spectra, where spec is the name of the layer to be used (oscillator spectra parameterised by the value of the reduced damping). This spectrum is computed beforehand by the command CALC_FONCTION U4.32.04 or read from a file by the command LIRE_FONCTION U4.32.02. In both cases, the concept produced is of type function of two variables (nappe). > ◊ ECHELLE = echel A scale factor echel to be applied to all the points of the spectrum spec. ◊ NATURE = 'ACCE' [DEFAUT] Quantity of the oscillator spectrum. By default, a spectrum in absolute pseudo-acceleration 'ACCE' is used. It is possible, more rarely, to use other quantities: velocity 'VITE' (relative pseudo-velocity) or displacement 'DEPL' (relative displacement). ♦ LIST_AXE = ( | 'X', | 'Y', | 'Z', ) At each occurrence of the factor keyword, the axes concerned by the excitation described are specified via a list composed of 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'. ◊ CORR_FREQ = / 'OUI' / 'NON' [DEFAUT] In fact, in order to compute the displacement response components from an oscillator spectrum in absolute pseudo-acceleration (NATURE = ‘ACCE’) or relative pseudo-velocity (NATURE = 'VITE'), one is led to divide each value once or twice by {\omega}_{r} , the angular frequency of the real eigenmode (undamped oscillator). Strictly speaking, the oscillator r is damped and its natural angular frequency is {\omega}_{r}\sqrt{1-{\xi}^{2}} , and {\omega}_{r} is only the natural pseudo-angular frequency. The operand CORR_FREQ = 'OUI' makes it possible to correct these values in order to take the damping of the eigenmode into account: \begin{array}{ccccc}{\mathit{vite}}_{max}& =& {\omega}_{r}\sqrt{1-{\xi}^{2}}{\mathit{depl}}_{\mathit{lu}}& =& \mathit{vitesse}\hfill \\ {\mathit{acce}}_{max}& =& {\omega}_{r}^{2}\left(1-{\xi}^{2}\right){\mathit{depl}}_{\mathit{lu}}& =& \mathit{accélération}\hfill \end{array} If a response spectrum in relative pseudo-velocity is supplied (NATURE = 'VITE'), the operand CORR_FREQ will be necessary in order to correct {\mathrm{depl}}_{\max} and {\mathrm{acce}}_{\max} if required. Likewise for a response spectrum in absolute pseudo-acceleration (NATURE = 'ACCE'), in order to correct {\mathit{depl}}_{max} and {\mathit{vite}}_{max} . Example: For a ground spectrum in absolute pseudo-acceleration sol_0_1 scaled to 0.1m/{s}^{2} and a scale factor making it possible to simulate a spectrum scaled to 0.25m/{s}^{2} , applied to the three global directions, and without taking the frequency correction into account: ♦ SPECTRE =_F( SPEC_OSCI = sol_0_1, ECHELLE = 2.5, NATURE = 'ACCE', LIST_AXE = ('X','Y','Z',), CORR_FREQ = 'NON', ) 3.5.2 Multi-support In the multi-support case, the structure is studied with several different motions at the supports. There are two configurations: - Correlated multi-support: all the supports are correlated with one another; - Uncorrelated multi-support: one can exhibit groups which are perfectly uncorrelated with one another, the excitations within one and the same group of supports being assumed to be correlated with one another. Thus, the steps for defining the loading are as follows: - Definition of the supports via the operand APPUIS - Definition of the groups of correlated supports via the operand GROUP_APPUI_CORRELE - Definition of the oscillator spectra (SRO) for each support via the operand SPECTRE - Definition of the Seismic Differential Displacements (DDS) for each support via the operand DEPL_MULT_APPUI 3.5.2.1 Operand APPUIS ♦ APPUIS =_F( ♦ NOM = nom_appui ♦ GROUP_NO = lgrno [l_gr_noeud] ) where: ♦ NOM = nom_appui Character string (limited to 4 characters at most) defined by the user to designate the name of the support. ♦ GROUP_NO = lgrno List of the GROUP_NO which constitute the support. 3.5.2.2 Group of correlated supports in multi-support analysis: operand GROUP_APPUI_CORRELE ♦ GROUP_APPUI_CORRELE =_F( ♦ NOM = nom_group_appui ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' [DEFAUT] / LIST_APPUI = l_appui ) where: ♦ NOM = nom_group_appui Character string (limited to 8 characters at most) defined by the user to designate the name of the group of correlated supports. ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI' [DEFAUT] All the supports are correlated with one another and gathered into a single group of correlated supports. This case corresponds to the correlated multi-support configuration. ♦ / LIST_APPUI = l_appui List of the supports correlated with one another and gathered into the group of correlated supports. The user must take care to define the groups of supports for all the supports defined by the operand APPUIS (see u4.84.01-operande-appuis); a support can belong to only one group of supports. And all the groups of correlated supports defined by the factor keyword GROUP_APPUI_CORRELE are uncorrelated with one another. If all the supports form a single group of supports, this is the correlated multi-support case. Conversely, the case where there are at least two occurrences of the factor GROUP_APPUI_CORRELE, that is two groups of correlated supports, corresponds to the uncorrelated multi-support configuration. 3.5.2.3 Operand SPECTRE The spectra are defined for each support via the factor SPECTRE, as in the single-support case, with, in addition: > ♦ NOM_APPUI = nom_appui : the name of the support concerned 3.5.2.4 Operand DEPL_MULT_APPUI Since the driving motion of the structure is not uniform, this keyword makes it possible to define the contribution to the global response of a list of supports or of groups of supports. This contribution is established from the static modes with imposed displacements of the structure: {R}_{\mathrm{ei}}={\Phi}_{\mathrm{si}}{\delta}_{i\max} with: | {\Phi}_{\mathrm{si}} | static mode for support i | | --- | --- | | {\delta}_{i\max} | maximum displacement of support i relative to a reference support (for which {\delta}_{imax}=0 ) | If this keyword is not entered, then the contribution of the static modes of the structure is zero. In other words, this is equivalent to entering {\delta}_{i\max}=0 . The DDS are defined by the occurrences of the factor DEPL_MULT_APPUI: ◊ DEPL_MULT_APPUI=_F( ♦ NOM_APPUI = nom_appui ◊ GROUP_NO_REFE = lgrno [l_gr_noeud] ♦ MODE_STAT = stat [mode_stat_depl] ♦ GROUP_NO = lgrno [l_gr_noeud] ♦ | DX = dx [R] | DY = dy [R] | DZ = dz [R] ) ♦ NOM_APPUI = nom_appui Name of the support concerned ◊ MODE_STAT = stat Name of the static modes {\Phi}_{\mathit{si}} , concept of type mode_stat produced by the operator MODE_STATIQUE, keyword MODE_STAT U4.52.14. ◊ GROUP_NO_REFE = grno Group containing the reference node with respect to which the relative displacements of the supports are defined (the group given must contain only one node). If this operand is present, the maximum displacement applied to support i is equal to {\delta}_{imax}-\Delta where \Delta is the displacement assigned to the reference node noeu in the direction considered. ♦ GROUP_NO = lgrno List of the names of the node groups corresponding to the supports concerned by the occurrence of the factor keyword DEPL_MULT_APPUI. ♦ I DX = dx I DY = dy I DZ = dz Value of the maximum relative displacement of the supports concerned, direction by direction. By the very principle of the static analysis of the displacement fields \phi at the nodes of the structure subjected to a displacement imposed at a given support via MODE_STATIQUE, it is impossible to deduce from them fields of the responses in relative velocity or in absolute acceleration. Thus, it is impossible to take the DDS into account for the options VITE, ACCE_ABSOLU (see the options u4.84.01-option-calcul). Example: A line of piping is fixed to two distinct floors via different supports. Two supports (sup1 and sup2) are located on floor level 1, while (sup3 and sup4) are located on floor level 2. Four different spectra are defined. The motions of floors 1 and 2 are considered to be uncorrelated, while all the spectra of the same floor are considered to be correlated. APPUIS=( _F(NOM="sup1", GROUP_NO="NO1"), _F(NOM="sup2", GROUP_NO="NO2"), _F(NOM="sup3", GROUP_NO="NO3"), _F(NOM="sup4", GROUP_NO="NO4"), ), GROUP_APPUI_CORRELE=( _F(LIST_APPUI=("sup1","sup2",), NOM="planc_1"), _F(LIST_APPUI=("sup3","sup4",), NOM="planc_2"), ), SPECTRE=( _F(NOM_APPUI="sup1", LIST_AXE=("X"), SPEC_OSCI=SRO1_NO1,), _F(NOM_APPUI="sup2", LIST_AXE=("X"), SPEC_OSCI=SRO1_NO2,), _F(NOM_APPUI="sup3", LIST_AXE=("X"), SPEC_OSCI=SRO2_NO1,), _F(NOM_APPUI="sup4", LIST_AXE=("X"), SPEC_OSCI=SRO2_NO2,), ), DEPL_MULT_APPUI=( _F(MODE_STAT=MODE_STA, NOM_APPUI="sup1", DX=DDS1), _F(MODE_STAT=MODE_STA, NOM_APPUI="sup2", DX=DDS2), _F(MODE_STAT=MODE_STA, NOM_APPUI="sup3", DX=DDS3), _F(MODE_STAT=MODE_STA, NOM_APPUI="sup4", DX=DDS4), ), 3.5.3 Envelope The idea of this complementary type of analysis is to supply the envelope response of a multi-support analysis with a minimum of modifications in the command file. 3.5.3.1 Selected envelope spectrum For a given direction, only the maximum value of the spectra coming from different groups of correlated supports, read at an eigenfrequency of the structure, is retained in order to compute the modal response. Suppose that there exist nbGr groups of supports; the retained value of the spectra (in this example, the pseudo-acceleration) is: PSA_{retenu} = \max(PSA_1, PSA_2, ..., PSA_{nbGr}) This envelope value is applied to all of the supports. The combinations remain identical to those used in the single-support analysis case. 3.5.3.2 Static corrections by pseudo-mode If the static correction by pseudo-mode is activated in the multi-support analysis, it must be replaced by a MODE_STATIQUE result, computed under the assumption that the structure is treated as single-support. When MODE_CORR = 'OUI', the result supplied with the compulsory keyword PSEUDO_MODE corresponds to the displacement field \phi of the nodes of the structure, subjected to a uniform acceleration in one or more directions. These displacements are computed by the operator MODE_STATIQUE with the keyword PSEUDO_MODE U4.52.14. More concretely, in multi-support analysis, the static mode is computed with the following command: mode_meca_mult = MODE_STATIQUE( PSEUDO_MODE = _F( GROUP_NO = grno, # Si: exists("TOUT") or exists("NOEUD") or exists("GROUP_NO") ◆ / TOUT_CMP = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / AVEC_CMP = text, / SANS_CMP = text, ), ) It is necessary to modify this command in order to supply the static correction in the case of a single-support analysis, by using the operands AXE or DIRECTION, for example as below: mode_meca_mono = MODE_STATIQUE( PSEUDO_MODE = _F( ◆ / AXE = / "X", / "Y", / "Z", ), ) The last result, mode_meca_mono , is entered in COMB_SISM_MODAL as follows: reponse_env = COMB_SISM_MODAL( TYPE_ANALYSE = "ENVELOPPE", MODE_CORR = "OUI", PSEUDO_MODE = mode_meca_mono, ... ) 3.5.3.3 Differential displacements of the supports (DDS) In the case where differential displacements of the supports (DDS) are taken into account in the multi-support analysis, they will not be considered when the envelope option is used. 3.6 Combination rules One reasons quantity by quantity (displacement, velocity or acceleration, internal forces, stresses) from the modal values associated with the eigenmodes taken into consideration. For each quantity, each degree of freedom (nodal fields of displacement, velocity or acceleration), or each component of a wrench (internal forces) or of stress, will be treated independently . This is what we call the response R in the statement of the combination rules. Several levels of combination are necessary: - combination of the eigenmodes, - static correction by pseudo-mode, - combination along the earthquake directions. In the case of a multi-support analysis, the combination rules are modified in order to take into account the different excitations applied to groups of supports. It is also possible to compute separately the inertial components of the response and those due to the DDS. 3.6.1 Single-support The analysis of the total response resulting from the combinations of the modal responses and then of the directional responses is presented in u4.84.01-fig-calcul-spectral-mono-appui. Single-support spectral analysis (Ref. [6]) The total response of the structure R is obtained by combination of the directional responses {R}_{X} where X represents one of the directions of the GLOBAL frame of definition of the mesh (X,Y,Z) . The directional response is given by: {R}_{X}=\sqrt{{R}_{d}^{2}+{({R}_{t}+{R}_{\mathit{qs}})}^{2}} - {R}_{d} combined dynamic response of the modal oscillators established by the combination of the modes with the rule defined by the keyword COMB_MODE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-modes-propres) - {R}_{t} correction of the static effects of the neglected modes (pseudo-mode) (see u4.84.01-spectre-oscillateur) - {R}_{\mathit{qs}} combined quasi-static response of the modal oscillators established by the combination of the modes only with the GUPTA rule by the keyword COMB_MODE (TYPE ='GUPTA') (see u4.84.01-combinaison-gupta) The rule for combining the directional responses is defined by the keyword COMB_DIRECTION (see u4.84.01-combinaison-suivant-directions). In summary, for the single-support case, the rule for combining the modes is defined by the keyword COMB_MODE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-modes-propres) and that of the directions by the keyword COMB_DIRECTION (see u4.84.01-combinaison-suivant-directions). 3.6.2 Multi-support For the total response of the multi-support case, the sequence of the combinations is presented in u4.84.01-fig-calcul-spectral-multi-appui. Multi-support spectral analysis (Ref. [6]) The total response of the structure R is obtained by combination of the directional responses {R}_{X} where X represents one of the directions of the GLOBAL frame of definition of the mesh (X,Y,Z) . The directional response is given by: {R}_{X}=\sqrt{{R}_{d}^{2}+{R}_{t}^{2}+{R}_{e}^{2}} - {R}_{d} combined dynamic response of the modal oscillators established by the combination of the modes with the rule defined by the keyword COMB_MODE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-modes-propres) - {R}_{t} correction of the static effects of the neglected modes (pseudo-mode) (see u4.84.01-corrections-pseudo-mode) - {R}_{e} response to the driving motion (see u4.84.01-operande-depl-mult-appui) For the combined dynamic response {R}_{d} by direction, by default , one combines quadratically the combined dynamic responses of the different groups of correlated supports: {R}_{d}=\sqrt{\sum_{m=1}^{\mathit{nbG}}{R}_{d,m}^{2}} - {R}_{d,m} combined dynamic response of the modal oscillators for the m-th group of correlated supports - \mathit{nbG} total number of groups of correlated supports The user may choose other rules for combining the responses between the groups of supports (LINE, ABS), defined by the keyword CUMUL_INTER (see u4.84.01-mot-cle-cumul-inter). Warning: These combinations can return very conservative results. For the combined dynamic response of the m-th group of supports {R}_{d,m} , one combines the responses of the modes of the m-th group of correlated supports with the combination rule defined by the keyword COMB_MODE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-modes-propres) (illustration example for the SRSS rule): {R}_{d,m}=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{\mathit{nbM}}{R}_{d,m,i}^{2}} - {R}_{d,m,i} combined dynamic response of the i-th mode for the m-th group of correlated supports - \mathit{nbM} total number of modes For the combined dynamic response of the i-th mode of the m-th group of supports {R}_{d,m,i} , by default , one combines linearly the responses of the i-th mode of the correlated supports in the m-th group of correlated supports: {R}_{d,m,i}=\sum_{n=1}^{{\mathit{nbA}}_{m}}{R}_{d,m,i,n} - {R}_{d,m,i,n} dynamic response of the i-th mode due to the SRO at the n-th support in the m-th group of correlated supports - {\mathit{nbA}}_{m} total number of correlated supports constituting the m-th group of correlated supports The user may also choose other rules for combining the responses of the supports within one and the same group of supports (QUAD, ABS), defined by the keyword CUMUL_INTRA (see u4.84.01-mot-cle-cumul-intra). Warning: These combinations can return very conservative results. In summary, the combined dynamic response {R}_{d} of the direction considered results from the linear combination of the correlated supports, then from the combination of the modes by the rule defined by the keyword COMB_MODE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-modes-propres) and finally from the quadratic combination of the groups of supports. For the combined correction of the static effects of the neglected modes (pseudo-mode) {R}_{t} by direction, one combines linearly the corrections of the correlated supports within a group of supports and then quadratically the corrections of the groups of supports (no choice is left to the user for these combinations): {R}_{t}=\sqrt{\sum_{m=1}^{\mathit{nbG}}{R}_{t,m}^{2}} {R}_{t,m}=\sum_{m=1}^{{\mathit{nbA}}_{m}}{R}_{t,m,n} - {R}_{t,m,n} correction due to the SRO at the n-th support in the m-th group of correlated supports - {\mathit{nbA}}_{m} total number of correlated supports constituting the m-th group of correlated supports - {R}_{t,m} correction of the m-th group of correlated supports - \mathit{nbG} total number of groups of correlated supports For the response to the driving motion {R}_{e} by direction, one combines the responses of the correlated supports within a group of supports by the rule defined in COMB_DDS_CORRELE (see u4.84.01-mot-cle-comb-dds-correle) and then quadratically the responses of the groups of supports (no choice is left to the user for this inter-group combination). For this component, the rule for combining the DDS of the correlated supports is in absolute value, by default (illustration formula with the absolute rule): {R}_{e}=\sqrt{\sum_{m=1}^{\mathit{nbG}}{R}_{e,m}^{2}} {R}_{e,m}=\sum_{m=1}^{{\mathit{nbA}}_{m}}\left|{R}_{e,m,n}\right| - {R}_{e,m,n} response due to the DDS at the n-th support in the m-th group of correlated supports - {\mathit{nbA}}_{m} total number of correlated supports constituting the m-th group of correlated supports - {R}_{e,m} combined response of the m-th group of correlated supports - \mathit{nbG} total number of groups of correlated supports In summary, for the multi-support case, the first combination, being linear, is carried out between the different nodes (NOEUD) of one and the same support for all the components, with no choice left to the user. Then, the intra-group combination rule (responses between correlated supports within one and the same group) is linear for the responses of the oscillators and of the pseudo-mode (no choice is left to the user), whereas for the response to the DDS the rule is defined in COMB_DDS_CORRELE (see u4.84.01-mot-cle-comb-dds-correle). Then, the combination of the modes is defined by the keyword COMB_MODE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-modes-propres), then the quadratic combination of the groups of supports (quadratic inter-group combination with no choice for the user). Finally, the combination of the directions is defined by the keyword COMB_DIRECTION (see u4.84.01-combinaison-suivant-directions). 3.6.3 Combination of the eigenmodes: keyword COMB_MODE ♦ COMB_MODE The response of the structure {R}_{d} , in one earthquake direction , is obtained by one of the possible combinations (defined by the operand TYPE) of the contributions of each of the eigenmodes taken into account. Each eigenmode is considered as an independent oscillator of response {R}_{r} defined by ({\omega}_{r},{\xi}_{r}) . The response is read by interpolation in the oscillator spectrum of the excitation signal in this direction. For a single-support excitation, the response {R}_{r} of the oscillator r is given by: {R}_{r}=\frac{{p}_{r}}{{\omega}_{r}^{2}}{S}_{r}{\Phi}_{r} | {\Phi}_{r} | modal quantity (displacement, generalised force, reaction) associated with the eigenmode of index r | | --- | --- | | {P}_{r} | modal participation factor associated with mode r in the direction studied | | {S}_{r} | value of the response spectrum, for example in pseudo-acceleration, for the oscillator r , for the specified damping value | Several rules for combining the eigenmodes are available. They are chosen by the operand TYPE. The rule for combining the eigenmodes is common to all the directions considered. 3.6.3.1 Quadratic combination TYPE = ‘SRSS’ This combination (Square Root of Sum of Squares) corresponds to the assumption of strict independence of the oscillators associated with each eigenmode: {R}_{d}=\sqrt{\sum_{r=1}^{\mathit{nmod}}{R}_{r}^{2}} Note that this combination rule, although very commonly used, may be ill-suited when the independence assumption is not satisfied for neighbouring eigenmodes or for strongly damped modes. 3.6.3.2 Complete quadratic combination TYPE = ‘CQC’ The quadratic combination (established by DER KIUREGHIAN) provides a correction to the previous rule by introducing correlation coefficients depending on the damping ratios and on the distances between neighbouring eigenmodes (see R4.05.03): {R}_{d}=\sqrt{\sum_{{r}_{1}}\sum_{{r}_{2}}{\rho}_{{r}_{1}{r}_{2}}{R}_{{r}_{1}}{R}_{{r}_{2}}} with the correlation coefficient: {\rho}_{ij}=\frac{8\sqrt{{\xi}_{i}{\xi}_{j}{\omega}_{i}{\omega}_{j}}({\xi}_{i}{\omega}_{i}+{\xi}_{j}{\omega}_{j}){\omega}_{i}{\omega}_{j}}{{({\omega}_{i}^{2}-{\omega}_{j}^{2})}^{2}+4{\xi}_{i}{\xi}_{j}{\omega}_{i}{\omega}_{j}({\omega}_{i}^{2}+{\omega}_{j}^{2})+4({\xi}_{i}^{2}+{\xi}_{j}^{2}){\omega}_{i}^{2}{\omega}_{j}^{2}} 3.6.3.3 Sum of the absolute values TYPE = ‘ABS’ This combination corresponds to an assumption of complete dependence of the oscillators associated with each eigenmode: {R}_{d}=\sum_{r=1}^{\mathit{nmod}}\left|{R}_{r}\right| Note that this combination rule is to be discouraged, because it is far too conservative and leads to systematic over-design. 3.6.3.4 Combination with the 10% rule TYPE = ‘DPC’ Neighbouring modes (whose frequencies differ by less than 10%) are first combined by summation of the absolute values. The values resulting from this first combination are then combined quadratically. This method was proposed by the American regulations of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (Regulatory Guide 1.92 – February 1976) in order to lessen the conservatism of the previous method. It remains inadequate for structures with a high modal density. The modes i and i+1 are neighbours when: 2\frac{({f}_{i+1}-{f}_{i})}{({f}_{i+1}+{f}_{i})}\le 10\text{\%} 3.6.3.5 Combination with the "Grouping" method TYPE = ‘NRC_GROUPING’ This method is similar to the "DPC" method (10% rule). It is also proposed by the American regulations of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC 1.92 Rev. 1). Important: it is recommended to use this method only in PipingMaster. For a given direction I (I = X, Y, Z), the periodic response is: R_{mode, I} = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{nmode} R_{i, I}^2 + 2 \sum_{j>i}^{nmode} \varepsilon_{i, j} |R_{i, I} R_{j, I}|} The modes are grouped according to the following rule: 1. Start a new group by adding the lowest eigenmode k (in frequency) which has not yet been grouped. 2. Increase the eigenfrequencies starting from k. 3. As long as \frac{({f}_{i}-{f}_{k})}{{f}_{k}} \le 10\text{\%} , add mode i to the group. 4. Return to step 1. The correlation coefficient: - \varepsilon_{i, j} = 1 if modes i, j belong to one and the same group - \varepsilon_{i, j} = 0 otherwise. 3.6.3.6 Combination with the "Ten Percent" method TYPE = ‘NRC_TEN_PERCENT’ This method is very similar to the "NRC_GROUPING" method. It is also proposed by the American regulations of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC 1.92 Rev. 1). For a given direction I (I = X, Y, Z), the periodic response is: R_{mode, I} = \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^{nmode} R_{i, I}^2 + 2 \sum_{j>i}^{nmode} \varepsilon_{i, j} |R_{i, I} R_{j, I}|} There is no notion of "group" in this method. The two modes are considered to be "close" when the gap between the two associated frequencies is less than or equal to 10%. In other words, the two modes i , j are close if: \frac{({f}_{j}-{f}_{i})}{{f}_{i}} \le 10\text{\%}, \; f_i Warning: - The number entered must correspond to the mode number (NUME_MODE) and not to the order number (NUME_ORDRE), which is linked to the computational design of the data. After a mode filtering (by the command EXTR_MODE, for example), the order numbers may be modified whereas the mode numbers remain unchanged. - The modal shapes being defined up to a multiplicative factor. In other words, {\phi} and {-\phi} represent physically and mathematically the same eigenmode. Depending on the desired orientation, it is sometimes necessary to use suitable filters in order to select the reference modal shape. - The CQC_SIGNE combination can be used only with the directional combination type 'NEWMARK'. The modal quantities requested with the operand OPTION (see u4.84.01-option-calcul) as well as their associated signature field are listed in the following table: | Computed field | Signature field | | --- | --- | | DEPL | DEPL | | VITE | DEPL | | ACCE_ABSOLU | DEPL | | EFGE_ELNO | EFGE_ELNO | | SIGM_ELNO | SIGM_ELNO | | SIPO_ELNO | SIPO_ELNO | | EGRU_ELNO | EGRU_ELNO | | REAC_NODA | REAC_NODA | | FORC_NODA | FORC_NODA | | SIEF_ELGA | SIEF_ELGA | | SIEF_ELNO | SIEF_ELNO | 3.6.4 Combination along the directions: keyword COMB_DIRECTION ◊ COMB_DIRECTION = / 'QUAD' / 'NEWMARK' [DEFAUT] / 'ABS' Three rules for combining the directional responses are available. This operand is not compulsory. If more than one direction is entered in the operand SPECTRE, the rule COMB_DIRECTION = NEWMARK is applied by default. If only one direction is entered in the operand SPECTRE, no directional combination is carried out. 3.6.4.1 Quadratic combination: COMB_DIRECTION = ‘QUAD’ This combination corresponds to the assumption of strict independence of the responses in each direction: R=\sqrt{{R}_{X}^{2}+{R}_{Y}^{2}+{R}_{Z}^{2}} 3.6.4.2 NEWMARK combination: COMB_DIRECTION = ‘NEWMARK’ For each of the directions i(X,Y,Z) , one computes the 8 values: {R}_{i}=\pm {R}_{X}\pm 0,4{R}_{Y}\pm 0,4{R}_{Z} Which leads, by circular permutation, to 24 (respectively 8 and 2) values if 3 (respectively 2 and 1) directional excitations are defined {R}_{max}=max({R}_{i}) 3.6.4.3 Absolute combination: COMB_DIRECTION = ‘ABS’ This combination corresponds to the assumption of correlation of the responses in each direction: R= |{R}_{X}| + |{R}_{Y}|+|{R}_{Z}| It should be noted that this assumption is very conservative. 3.6.5 Keyword COMB_DDS_CORRELE ◊ COMB_DDS_CORRELE = / 'ABS' [DEFAUT] / 'QUAD' / 'LINE' This keyword defines the rule for combining the responses to the driving motions of the correlated supports. 3.6.5.1 Quadratic combination COMB_DDS_CORRELE = ‘QUAD’ {R}_{e}=\sqrt{\sum{R}_{\mathit{ej}}^{2}} 3.6.5.2 Linear combination COMB_DDS_CORRELE = ‘LINE’ {R}_{e}=\sum_{j=1}^{\mathit{nbA}}{R}_{\mathit{ej}} 3.6.5.3 Absolute-value combination COMB_DDS_CORRELE = ‘ABS’ {R}_{e}=\sum_{j=1}^{\mathit{nbA}}\left|{R}_{\mathit{ej}}\right| 3.6.6 Keyword CUMUL_INTRA ◊ CUMUL_INTRA = / 'LINE' [DEFAUT] / 'ABS' / 'QUAD' This keyword defines the rule for combining the modal responses corresponding to mode i . Let nbAm be the number of supports in the m-th group of supports; the modal response of mode i for the group of correlated supports m is obtained by the following combination rules: 3.6.6.1 Linear combination CUMUL_INTRA = ‘LINE’ R_{d, m, i}=\sum_{n=1}^{nbAm} R_{d, m, i, n} 3.6.6.2 Absolute-value combination CUMUL_INTRA = ‘ABS’ R_{d, m, i}=\sum_{n=1}^{nbAm} \left| R_{d, m, i, n} \right| 3.6.6.3 Quadratic combination CUMUL_INTRA = ‘QUAD’ R_{d, m, i}=\sqrt{\sum_{n=1}^{nbAm} R_{d, m, i, n}^2} 3.6.7 Keyword CUMUL_INTER ◊ CUMUL_INTER = / 'QUAD' [DEFAUT] / 'LINE' / 'ABS' This keyword defines the rule for combining the modal responses between the groups of supports. Let nbG be the number of groups of supports and d the direction (d = X, Y, Z); the directional modal response is obtained by the following combination rules: 3.6.7.1 Quadratic combination CUMUL_INTER = ‘QUAD’ R_{d}=\sqrt{\sum_{m=1}^{nbG} R_{d, m}^2} 3.6.7.2 Linear combination CUMUL_INTER = ‘LINE’ R_{d}= \sum_{m=1}^{nbG} R_{d, m} 3.6.7.3 Absolute-value combination CUMUL_INTER = ‘ABS’ R_{d}= \sum_{m=1}^{nbG} \left| R_{d, m} \right| 3.7 Analysis option: operand OPTION ♦ OPTION List of the modal quantities (analysis options) for which one wishes to determine the combined response: | 'DEPL' | relative displacement | | --- | --- | | 'VITE' | relative velocity | | 'ACCE_ABSOLU' | absolute acceleration = relative acceleration + driving acceleration | | 'SIGM_ELNO' | stresses by finite element at the nodes | | 'SIEF_ELGA' | stresses by finite element at the integration points | | 'SIPO_ELNO' | stresses in the beam cross-section split into the contributions of each generalised force | | 'EFGE_ELNO', 'SIEF_ELNO' | generalised forces by finite element at the nodes | | 'EGRU_ELNO' U4.74.01 | generalised forces by finite element at the nodes in the user's frame | | 'REAC_NODA' | reactions at the supports | | 'FORC_NODA' | internal forces | Note For the analysis of the force or stress options on a part of the model defined by mesh-cell groups, it is possible to chain an analysis on the mode concept produced by the operator CALC_CHAMP. 3.8 Type of output result: operand TYPE_RESU It is possible to output several results by the occurrence of the operand ♦ TYPE_RESU=_F( TYPE = /'VALE_XXX', ... ), Depending on the type of result defined by the keyword TYPE, several keywords are possibly necessary in order to filter the output results: - It is possible to output these components for each direction as well as their combination by the rule COMB_DIRECTION = 'QUAD' (and only that). # Si TYPE = 'VALE_INER', 'VALE_DDS': ♦ LIST_AXE = l_axe List of the axes concerned by the excitation described via a list composed of 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'. 3.8.4.1 Inertial component: TYPE = 'VALE_INER' For the direction X , the directional inertial component is defined as follows: {R}_{I,X}=\sqrt{{R}_{d,X}^{2}+{R}_{t,X}^{2}} - {R}_{d,X} combined modal response of the modal oscillators for the direction X (see u4.84.01-regles-combinaison) - {R}_{t,X} contribution of the static correction of the neglected modes (pseudo-mode) (see u4.84.01-regles-combinaison) The inertial component is the result of the quadratic combination of the three directional inertial responses: {R}_{I,\mathit{tot}}=\sqrt{{R}_{I,X}^{2}+{R}_{I,Y}^{2}+{R}_{I,Z}^{2}} 3.8.4.2 Component due to the DDS: TYPE = 'VALE_DDS' This is the static response induced by the seismic differential displacements of the anchorages (driving motion), only in the multi-support case. For the single-support case, this component is considered to be zero. For the direction X , the directional component of the response due to the DDS is defined as presented in u4.84.01-multi-appui. The component due to the DDS is the result of the quadratic combination of the three directions: {R}_{E,\mathit{tot}}=\sqrt{{R}_{e,X}^{2}+{R}_{e,Y}^{2}+{R}_{e,Z}^{2}} It is recalled that the intra-group combination of the responses to the DDS is carried out according to the rule defined by the user via COMB_DDS_CORRELE (see u4.84.01-combinaison-valeur-absolue), whereas the inter-group combination is quadratic, with no choice left to the user. 3.8.5 Partition of the dynamic and quasi-static contributions It is possible to output these parts for each direction as well as their combination by the rule COMB_DIRECTION = 'QUAD' (and only that). # Si TYPE = 'VALE_DYNA', 'VALE_QS': ♦ LIST_AXE = l_axe List of the axes concerned by the excitation described via a list composed of 'X', 'Y' and 'Z'. 3.8.5.1 Dynamic part: TYPE = 'VALE_DYNA' For the direction X , the directional dynamic part {R}_{d,X} is defined as the combined modal response of the modal oscillators for the direction X (see u4.84.01-regles-combinaison). The dynamic part is the result of the quadratic combination of the three directional dynamic responses: {R}_{d,\mathit{tot}}=\sqrt{{R}_{d,X}^{2}+{R}_{d,Y}^{2}+{R}_{d,Z}^{2}} 3.8.5.2 Quasi-static part: TYPE = 'VALE_QS' For the direction X , the directional quasi-static part {R}_{t,X} is defined as the contribution of the static correction of the neglected modes (pseudo-mode) (see u4.84.01-regles-combinaison). The quasi-static part is the result of the quadratic combination of the three directional quasi-static responses: {R}_{t,\mathit{tot}}=\sqrt{{R}_{t,X}^{2}+{R}_{t,Y}^{2}+{R}_{t,Z}^{2}} 3.9 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = t Title attached to the concept produced by this operator U4.03.01. 3.10 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 [DEFAUT] = / 2 | /1: | printout in the “message” file of the following information: | | --- | --- | General information: - name of the modal basis used, - number of eigenvectors retained, - modal combination rule chosen, - analysis options requested. u4.84.02 Operator POST_DYNA_MODA_T u4.84.02 Operator POST_DYNA_MODA_T 1 Purpose Post-process the results in generalised coordinates produced by DYNA_VIBRA. Two options are available: post-processing of the shock non-linearities or of the force–displacement relations. In the first case, one chooses a wear diagnosis or a better knowledge of the shocks that occurred during the transient analysis. The content of the table produced can be printed in the RESULTAT file by the command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. 2 Syntax table = POST_DYNA_MODA_T( ◆ RESU_GENE = tran_gene, ◆ / CHOC = _F( ◇ INST_INIT = float (défaut: -1.0), ◇ INST_FIN = float (défaut: 999.0), ◇ NB_BLOC = int (défaut: 1), ◇ SEUIL_FORCE = float, ◇ DUREE_REPOS = float, ◇ OPTION = / "IMPACT", / "USURE" (par défaut), ◇ NB_CLASSE = int (défaut: 10), ), / RELA_EFFO_DEPL = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESU_GENE ♦ RESU_GENE = tg Result of a transient analysis by modal recombination, produced by the operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. 3.2 Keyword CHOC ◊ CHOC Factor keyword making it possible to specify that one wishes an analysis of the shock non-linearities taken into account in the modal transient analysis. 3.2.1 Operand INST_INIT ◊ INST_INIT = t0 Start time instant of the averaging of the signals and of the shock analysis. By default t0 corresponds to the first time instant of the transient analysis by modal recombination. 3.2.2 Operand INST_FIN ◊ INST_FIN = t1 End time instant of the averaging of the signals and of the shock analysis. (t1 = 999. default value), 3.2.3 Operand NB_BLOC ◊ NB_BLOC = nb Number of time blocks into which the interval [t0, t1] is split for the averaging of the signals (1 by default). The keyword is not used for the option 'IMPACT'. 3.2.4 Operand SEUIL_FORCE ◊ SEUIL_FORCE = s Threshold characterising a contact phase, ( \mid {f}_{n}\mid >s\Rightarrow \text{contact établi} ) (s = 0. default value). 3.2.5 Operand DUREE_REPOS ◊ DUREE_REPOS = d Avec d la durée minimale de repos caractérisant la fin d'un choc. Si on désigne par tc la fin du choc alors \forall t\in \left[{t}_{c},{t}_{c}+d\right]\to \mid {f}_{n}\mid The parameters of the table produced are described in the following table: | PARAMETRES | TYPE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | --- | | RELATION | K8 | name of the relation at the observed node | | NOEUD | K8 | name of the node processed | | GROUP_NO | K8 | Name of the node group containing the node to be processed | | CMP | K8 | name of the component | | PHASE | I | number of the phase | | INST_INIT | R | initial time instant of the interval of the non-linear phase | | INST_FIN | R | final time instant of the interval of the non-linear phase | | MAXI | R | maximum reached | | INST_MAXI | R | time instant associated with the maximum reached | 3.3.1 Operand GROUP _ NO ♦ GROUP _ NO = grnoeu, Name of the node group containing the node of the structure on which the non-linear relation to be processed was defined. 3.3.2 Operand NOM_CMP ♦ NOM_CMP = noncmp Name of the component processed at the node noeu. 3.4 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = imp, niveau des impressions / 1 no printout in the message file (everything is stored in the table produced) / 2 printout of the number of analysis time steps 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre titre is the title of the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results. It is stored in the table concept. 4 Checking — Execution 4.1 For the factor keyword CHOC The value of INST_FIN is compared with the final time instant {t}_{f} of the tran_gene result. The value of INST_FIN retained is \min({t}_{f},{t}_{1}) . If the value of INST_INIT {t}_{0} is greater than the value of INST_FIN, the analysis stops in error. 4.1.1 Execution with the option 'IMPACT' For each shock non-linearity, the following are computed and stored in the result table: - the shocks and the associated quantities: for each shock, one has the value of the time instant at which the force is maximum, the value of the maximum force and of the impulse, the duration of the shock, the impact velocity and the number of rebounds, - the global shock data: over the set of shocks observed, one specifies: the absolute maximum of the shock force, the mean value of the maxima of the shock forces and the standard deviation of the extrema of the shock force, - the histogram describing the maxima of the impact forces: one has the number of classes of the histogram, the values of its abscissae (minimum and maximum force of each class) and the probability density of the maximum force of each class. 4.1.2 Execution with the option 'USURE' For each shock non-linearity, the following are computed and stored in the result table: - the mean, minimum, maximum, standard-deviation and RMS values of the relative displacements of the shock nodes in their global frame, - the mean and RMS values (over the shock time and the total time) as well as the minimum and maximum of the normal and tangential shock forces, - the mean number of shocks on each shock connection, the mean shock time, the mean rebound time, - the mean wear power computed in the sense of ARCHARD [bib1]: {P}_{\text{usure}}=\frac{1}{T}.{\int}_{0}^{T}{F}_{N}(t).{V}_{T}(t).\text{dt} 4.2 For the factor keyword RELA_EFFO_DEPL One checks that the node noeu corresponds to a non-linear relation. One prints, using the command IMPR_TABLE: --------------------------------------------------------------------------- ASTER 4.03.15 CONCEPT TABLE CALCULE LE 03/02/98 A 12:08:19 DE TYPE TABLE_SDASTER RELATION NOEUD CMP PHASE INST_INIT INST_FIN MAXI INST_MAXI NON_LIN N100 DRY 1 1.24000E+00 1.26600E+00 1.80716E-05 1.25200E+00 NON_LIN N100 DRY 2 2.02600E+00 2.09000E+00 -2.00433E-05 2.05800E+00 NON_LIN N100 DRY 3 3.00000E+00 3.04000E+00 -1.89110E-05 3.02200E+00 NON_LIN N100 DRY 4 3.10400E+00 3.20400E+00 3.50715E-05 3.15400E+00 NON_LIN N100 DRY 5 3.26000E+00 3.33600E+00 -2.91359E-05 3.30000E+00 NON_LIN N100 DRY 6 3.41400E+00 3.43200E+00 1.73099E-05 3.42400E+00 . 5 Examples of use The test SDND101 is presented here. The aim is to compute the response of a mass–spring system with a non-zero initial velocity {V}_{0} , which may impact a shock stop. The initial gap is zero. The values of the time instants of maximum force, the value of the maximum force, the duration of the shock time, the value of the impulse and of the impact velocity, and the number of elementary impacts for the first two oscillations of the system are compared with the analytical values. 6 Bibliography 1. ARCHARD : The wear of metals under unlubrificated conditions Proc-Roy-Soc. (1956).

u4.84.03 Operator POST_FATI_ALEA u4.84.03 Operator POST_FATI_ALEA 1 Purpose Compute the fatigue damage undergone by a structure subjected to a random loading. To this end POST_FATI_ALEA makes it possible, from the spectral moments which fully characterise the random signal: - to extract, by a statistical cycle-counting method (stress-peak counting method or level-crossing counting method), the number of elementary loading cycles undergone by the structure, - to determine the elementary damage associated with each elementary cycle using the Wöhler curve of the material, - to determine the mean damage over the duration of the signal. It is also possible to take into account the influence of the elasto-plastic concentration coefficient. The mean damage is stored in a table of type table_sdaster. 2 Syntax table = POST_FATI_ALEA( ◆ / MOMENT_SPEC_0 = float, ◇ & MOMENT_SPEC_2 = float, ◇ & MOMENT_SPEC_4 = float, / TABL_POST_ALEA = table, ◆ COMPTAGE = / "PIC", / "NIVEAU", ◇ DUREE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ CORR_KE = "RCCM" (ou non renseigné), ◆ DOMMAGE = "WOHLER" (ou non renseigné), ◆ MATER = mater, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands TABL_POST_ALEA / MOMENT_SPEC_0 / MOMENT_SPEC_2 / MOMENT_SPEC_4 These operands make it possible to introduce the value of the three spectral moments of orders 0, 2 and 4, which may have been determined by the command POST_DYNA_ALEA U4.84.04. These values fully characterise the random signal for the statistical cycle-counting methods: - stress-peak counting method, which uses 0, 2 and 4, - level-crossing counting method, which requires only 0 and 2. ♦ / ♦ MOMENT_SPEC_0 = 0 , [R] ♦ MOMENT_SPEC_2 = 2 , [R] ◊ MOMENT_SPEC_4 = 4 , [R] The value of the spectral moment is supplied after the corresponding operand. ♦ / TABL_POST_ALEA = table , [tabl_post_alea] Makes it possible to specify the name of a table created by POST_DYNA_ALEA U4.84.04, in which values of the spectral moments 0, 2, 4) are stored, for various modes or various nodes. The values are read back and a mean-damage value is computed for each triplet of spectral moments encountered in the table. However, since the method for computing the mean damage is valid only for loadings homogeneous with stresses, an alarm is issued when the computation of the mean damage does not correspond to power spectral densities homogeneous with stresses (DSP_CONT). 3.2 Operand COMPTAGE ♦ COMPTAGE = In order to compute the damage undergone by a structure, the elementary cycles of the loading history must first be extracted. / 'PIC' , Makes it possible to choose the stress-peak counting method to determine the elementary cycles of the random loading R7.04.02. / 'NIVEAU' , Makes it possible to choose the level-crossing counting method to determine the elementary cycles of the random loading R7.04.02. 3.3 Operand DUREE ◊ DUREE = / duree , [R] / 1. , [DEFAUT] Makes it possible to introduce the duration of the signal, which appears in the expression of the mean damage R7.04.02. 3.4 Operand CORR_KE ◊ CORR_KE = 'RCCM' , This operand makes it possible to take into account an elasto-plastic concentration coefficient {K}_{e} , which is defined by the RCC-M as the ratio of the real strain amplitude to the strain amplitude determined by an elastic analysis. \lbrace \begin{array}{ccccccccc}{K}_{e}& =& 1& \text{si}& & & \Delta \sigma & \text{<}& 3{S}_{m}\\ {K}_{e}& =& 1+\frac{(1-n)(\Delta \sigma /3{S}_{m}-1)}{n(m-1)}& \text{si}& 3{S}_{m}& \text{<}& \Delta \sigma & \text{<}& 3m{S}_{m}\\ {K}_{e}& =& 1& \text{si}& 3m{S}_{m}& \text{<}& \Delta \sigma & & \end{array} where {S}_{m} is the maximum allowable stress, and n and m are two constants depending on the material. The values of {S}_{m} , n and m are introduced in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 under the keyword FATIGUE and the operands SM_KE_RCCM, N_KE_RCCM and M_KE_RCCM. 3.5 Operand DOMMAGE ♦ DOMMAGE = 'WOHLER' , This operand makes it possible to specify the damage-computation method, which, for a random loading, is the Wöhler method. To compute the damage, the user must introduce in the operator DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01 the Wöhler curve of the material, which may be given in three distinct mathematical forms R7.04.02: - function discretised point by point (keyword FATIGUE, operand WOHLER), - analytical Basquin form (keyword FATIGUE, operands A_BASQUIN and BETA_BASQUIN), - “current-zone” form (keyword FATIGUE, operands E_REFE, A0, A1, A2, A3 and SL, and keyword ELAS, operand E). Note on the fatigue curves: For small amplitudes, the problem of extending the fatigue curve may arise: for example, for the RCC-M fatigue curves beyond 106 cycles, the corresponding stress, 180 MPa, is regarded as an endurance limit, that is, any stress lower than 180 MPa must produce a zero usage factor or an infinite allowable number of cycles. The method adopted here corresponds to this notion of endurance limit: if the stress amplitude is lower than the first abscissa of the fatigue curve, a zero usage factor is taken, that is, an infinite allowable number of cycles. 3.6 Operand MATER ♦ MATER = mater , Makes it possible to specify the name of the material mater created by DEFI_MATERIAU U4.43.01. The material mater must contain at least the definition of the Wöhler curve of the material R7.04.02. If one wishes to take into account an elasto-plastic concentration coefficient {K}_{e} , the material data (N, M and SM) required for the computation of {K}_{e} must also have been specified. 3.7 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre , Title associated with the table. 3.8 Table produced The operator POST_FATI_ALEA creates a table, tabl_post_f_alea, which comprises 1 parameter: DOMMAGE: value of the mean damage over the duration of the signal. Note: In the case where the operand TABL_POST_ALEA has been used to introduce the values of the spectral moments, the value of the mean damage over the duration of the signal is stored in the table, for each triplet of spectral moments present in the table. The command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03 makes it possible to print the table produced. 4 Example mate = DEFI_MATERIAU ( FATIGUE = _F (A_BASQUIN = 1.001730939 E–14 , BETA_BASQUIN = 4.065 ) ) table = POST_FATI_ALEA ( MOMENT_SPEC_0 = 182.5984664 , MOMENT_SPEC_2 = 96098024.76 , MOMENT_SPEC_4 = 6.346193569E+13 , COMPTAGE = 'PIC' , DOMMAGE = 'WOHLER' , MATER = mate , )

u4.84.04 Operator POST_DYNA_ALEA u4.84.04 Operator POST_DYNA_ALEA 1 Purpose POST_DYNA_ALEA makes it possible to carry out two types of post-processing after a stochastic dynamics analysis: Analysis of fragility curves from a table containing the results of a Monte Carlo simulation From a table [table_sdaster] containing the information on the excitation levels (in a seismic analysis, the PGA is generally chosen) and the variable of interest characterising whether or not the structure fails, POST_DYNA_ALEA makes it possible to determine the parameters of a fragility curve according to the log-normal model and to compute values of this curve. The reader may consult [U2.08.05] for a more detailed description. Statistical post-processing of results of type interspectre. POST_DYNA_ALEA makes it possible, on functions selected in a concept of type [interspectre], to compute statistical parameters: spectral moments, standard deviation, peak distribution, central frequency. The cross-spectral matrix may be obtained by various operators: lire_inte_spec U4.36.01, calc_inte_spec U4.36.03, defi_inte_spec U4.36.02, dyna_alea_modal U4.53.22, DYNA_SPEC_MODAL U4.53.23 or REST_SPEC_PHYS U4.63.22. One should refer to R7.10.01 for the description of the processing carried out. This operator produces a table of type table_sdaster which can be printed by IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. 2 Syntax table = POST_DYNA_ALEA( ◆ / FRAGILITE = _F( ◆ TABL_RESU = table, ◆ / VALE = float, / LIST_PARA = listr8, ◆ METHODE = / "EMV", / "REGRESSION", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'REGRESSION') ◆ SEUIL = float, # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'EMV') ◇ SEUIL = float, ◆ AM_INI = float, ◇ BETA_INI = float (défaut: 0.3), ◇ FRACTILE = float, # Si: exists("FRACTILE") ◇ NB_TIRAGE = int, ), / INTERSPECTRE = _F( ◆ INTE_SPEC = interspectre, ◆ / NUME_ORDRE_I = int, / NOEUD_I = no, / OPTION = / "DIAG", / "TOUT", # Si: exists("NUME_ORDRE_I") ◆ NUME_ORDRE_J = int, # Si: exists("NOEUD_I") ◆ NOEUD_J = no, ◆ NOM_CMP_I = text, ◆ NOM_CMP_J = text, ◇ FRACTILE = float (défaut: 0.5), ◇ MOMENT = int, ◇ DUREE = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword FRAGILITE FRAGILITE = The keyword FRAGILITE makes it possible to determine the parameters {A}_{m} and \beta (median and logarithmic standard deviation) of a fragility curve according to the log-normal model [U2.08.05]: {P}_{f\mid a}=\Phi (\frac{\ln(a/{A}_{m})}{\beta}) One may also compute the values of the curve for the values of the parameters Am and \beta obtained. The option FRACTILES (optional) also makes it possible to determine fractiles for the curve by a resampling method applied to the original sample supplied in TABL_RESU. 3.1.1 Operand TABL_RESU ♦TAB_RESU = tabres [table_sdaster] One gives the name of the table [table_sdaster] which must have been created beforehand using CREA_TABLE [U4.33.02] . This table must have at least two columns with access keys (column label name): PARA_NOCI (this is the indicator characterising the level of the excitation) and DEFA (the values of this column are 0 if no failure has been observed or 1 if there has been a failure) or DEMANDE (the values of the real variable of interest characterising failure or damage, also called seismic demand in the literature). 3.1.2 Operand METHODE > ♦ METHODE=/ 'EMV' / 'REGRESSION' One chooses between the two methods for the analysis of the log-normal fragility curve: EMV for maximum-likelihood estimation or REGRESSION for linear regression. Further details on these two methods are given in the documentation [U2,08.05]. If one chooses REGRESSION, then the table tabres must contain a column DEMANDE giving the seismic demand (variable of interest such as the drift, a maximum stress, ...) and the failure threshold must be supplied via the keyword SEUIL. 3.1.3 Operand SEUIL ◊ SEUIL= seuil [R] Si la table TAB_RESU contient une colonneDEMANDE, alors il faut renseigner le seuil de cette variable à partir duquel la structure est considérée défaillante. 3.1.4 Operands LIST_PARA and VALE One may give a list of reals, values for which the fragility curve is evaluated. This may be done in the form of a list containing the analysis values ({a}_{1,}{a}_{2,}\mathrm{...},{a}_{n}) : ◊VALE =liste [l_R] or by giving the name of the concept of type listr8 containing the list of values: ◊LIST_PARA =liste listr8 3.1.5 Operands AM_INI and BETA_INI ♦ AM_INI ◊ BETA_INI If one has chosen METHODE='EMV', then it is essential to give an initial value for the estimation of the parameter {A}_{m} and it is advisable to give an initial estimate for \beta (starting points for the optimisation algorithm). 3.1.6 Operands FRACTILES and NB_TIRAGE These operands must be supplied if one wishes to determine confidence intervals or, more precisely, fractiles for the fragility curve estimated by the maximum-likelihood method ('EMV'). The resampling method (also called “bootstrap” in the English-language literature) is used for this purpose. The operand FRACTILES makes it possible to give the fractiles that one wishes to compute. ◊FRACTILES = fract listr8 By default, as many “bootstrap” samples are drawn as there are data available (this is the number N of Monte Carlo simulations carried out beforehand and whose results are stored in the table TABL_RESU). The command NB_TIRAGE nevertheless makes it possible to reduce the number of draws to be carried out: ◊NB_TIRAGE = nbt [I] nbt must be less than or equal to the number of values in TABL_RESU ( \mathrm{nbt}\le N ). This feature makes it possible to reduce the analysis time but is not recommended in the general case because the results are not very reliable. 3.2 Keyword INTERSPECTRE 3.2.1 Operand INTE_SPEC ♦ INTE_SPEC = inter inter is the user name of the cross-spectral matrix. The cross-spectral matrix may be obtained by various operators: lire_inte_spec U4.36.01, calc_inte_spec U4.36.03, defi_inte_spec U4.36.02, dyna_alea_modal U4.53.22, DYNA_SPEC_MODAL U4.53.23 or REST_SPEC_PHYS U4.63.22. Note : The spectral moments are defined as integrals of the power spectral density (PSD): {\lambda}_{i}=\underset{-\infty }{\overset{+\infty }{\int}}{\mid \omega \mid }^{i}{S}_{\text{XX}}(\omega )d\omega =2\underset{0}{\overset{+\infty }{\int}}{\omega}^{i}{S}_{\text{XX}}(\omega )d\omega Thus, if the PSD is given for the positive frequencies only, POST_DYNA_ALEA multiplies by 2 the integrals of the PSDs computed for \omega >0 . Furthermore, the PSDs are defined as a function of the natural frequency f=2\pi \omega ( \mathit{Hz} ) in POST_DYNA_ALEA . The following formulae are used [cf. R7.010.01]: \begin{array}{}{S}_{\text{XX}}(f)=\underset{-\infty }{\overset{+\infty }{\int}}{R}_{\text{XX}}(\tau ){e}^{-\mathrm{2i}\pi f\tau }d\tau ;\\ S{'}_{\text{XX}}(\omega )=\frac{1}{2\pi }{S}_{\text{XX}}(f)\end{array} The reader is invited to consult the documentation of the command DYNA_ALEA_MODAL U4.53.22 for further information on the meaning of the parameters of the keyword. 3.2.2 Operands NUME_ORDRE_I, NUME_ORDRE_J ♦ / ♦ NUME_ORDRE_I = lnumi ♦ NUME_ORDRE_J = lnumj These keywords make it possible to define the terms of the matrix whose functions will undergo the processing. When the auto-spectra or the cross-spectra are computed on the modes : - lnumi is the list of the order numbers of the modes 'i'. Example: (2,3,1). - lnumj is the list of the order numbers of the modes 'j'. Example: (2,1,4) The indices are paired according to the same rank. - (2,2) corresponds to the auto-spectrum on mode 2, - (3,1) corresponds to the cross-spectrum between mode 3 and mode 1. lnumi and lnumj must contain the same number of terms. 3.2.3 Operands NOEUD_I, NOEUD_J, NOM_CMP_I, NOM_CMP_J ♦ / ♦ NOEUD_I = lnoeudi ♦ NOEUD_J = lnoeudj ♦ NOM_CMP_I = lcmpi ♦ NOM_CMP_J = lcmpj When the auto-spectra or the cross-spectra are computed on the nodes in a given direction: - lnoeudi is the list of the nodes along "i": (\mathit{NO92},\mathit{NO95},\mathit{NO98}) - lnoeudj is the list of the nodes along "j": (\mathit{NO92},\mathit{NO92},\mathit{NO92}) - lcmpi is the list of the components along "i": (\mathit{DX},\mathit{DX},\mathit{DY}) - lcmpj is the list of the components along "j": (\mathit{DX},\mathit{DX},\mathit{DX}) The nodes and components are paired according to the same rank: - (\mathit{NO92}\mathit{DX},\mathit{NO92}\mathit{DX}) corresponds to the auto-spectrum at the node \mathit{NO92} in the direction \mathit{DX} , - (\mathit{NO98}\mathit{DY},\mathit{NO92}\mathit{DX}) corresponds to the cross-spectrum between the node \mathit{NO92} in the direction \mathit{DX} and the node \mathit{NO95} in the direction \mathit{DY} . lnoeudi, lnoeudj, lcmpi and lcpmj must contain the same number of terms. 3.2.4 Operand OPTION ♦ / OPTION = 'TOUT' The analyses are carried out on all the cross-spectra of the matrix. / OPTION = 'DIAG' The analyses are carried out on all the auto-spectra of the matrix and only on those. fract = 0.5 3.2.5 Keywords DUREE and FRACTILE ◊ DUREE = duree Si le mot-clé duree est renseigné, alors on détermine le maximum médian ou tout autre fractile ainsi que le facteur de pic du processus stochastique stationnaire Gaussien selon les formules de Vanmarcke. duree désigne alors l'intervalle du temps considéré pour estimer ces quantités. A titre d'exemple, dans le cadre d'une analyse sismique, duree peut être pris égal à la durée de la phase forte du signal sismique. ◊ FRACTILE = /frac [R] /0.5 [DEFAUT] Permet de définir le fractile considéré pour les calculs du maximum. Par défaut, on prend fract = 0.5, ce qui correspond à la médiane des maxima. 3.2.6 Operand MOMENT ◊ MOMENT = lmom lmom is the list of the orders of the spectral moments which will be computed. By default, the spectral moments of orders 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 are always computed. The moments of order higher than 4 should therefore be mentioned in this list. Example: (5,7,8). 3.3 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= | 1 | printout of the requested results. | | --- | --- | | 2 | as 1 but with more detail. | 3.4 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre titre is the title of the analysis. It will be printed at the head of the results. See U4.03.01. 4 Results supplied 4.1 Keyword FRAGILITE The parameters of the output table are: | PARAMETRES | TYPE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | --- | | TITRE | TXM | Title of the table | | AM | R | Parameter {A}_{m} estimated by maximum likelihood from the original sample | | BETA | R | Parameter \beta estimated by maximum likelihood from the original sample | | PARA_NOCI | R | Values of the harmfulness parameter for which the curves are evaluated | | PFA | R | Values of the fragility curve (parameters AM and BETA) | | FRACTILES | R | Values of the curves for the fractile f | 4.2 Keyword INTE_SPEC For each function chosen in the interspectrum, POST_DYNA_ALEA stores in a table accessible by IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03 - the spectral moments - statistical parameters (to be used if it is an auto-spectrum): - standard deviation, - irregularity factor, - mean number of extrema per second, - number of zero crossings per second, - central frequency - the peak factor according to Vanmarcke's formula - the mean maximum according to Vanmarcke's formula The parameters of this table are: | PARAMETRES | TYPE | DESCRIPTION | | --- | --- | --- | | NUME_ORDRE_I | I | order number of the modes i | | NUME_ORDRE_J | I | order number of the modes j | | NOEUD_I | NO | Node i | | NOEUD_J | NO | Node j | | NOM_CMP_I | TXM | Name of the component at node i (\mathit{DX},\mathit{DY},\mathit{DY}) | | NOM_CMP_J | TXM | Name of the component at node j (\mathit{DX},\mathit{DY},\mathit{DY}) | | LAMBDA_00 | R | spectral moment of order 0 | | LAMBDA_01 | R | spectral moment of order 1 | | LAMBDA_02 | R | spectral moment of order 2 | | LAMBDA_03 | R | spectral moment of order 3 | | LAMBDA_04 | R | spectral moment of order 4 | | ECART | R | standard deviation | | NB_EXTREMA_P_S | R | mean number of extrema per second | | NB_PASS_ZERO_P_S | R | number of zero crossings per second | | FREQ_APPAR | R | central frequency | | FACT_IRRE | R | irregularity factor | | MAX_MOY | R | Mean maximum | | FACT_PIC | R | Peak factor | If INFO = 1 one prints in the file MESSAGE - the user name of the table, - the two indices (the 2 nodes or the 2 modes) of the selected function, - the type of result computed, - the analysis options chosen or taken by default, - the values of the selected functions. 5 Example 5.1 Keyword FRAGILITE Example of a table generated beforehand, by calling CALC_TABLE, during the Monte Carlo simulation (see also U2.08.05): #TABLE_SDASTER PARA_NOCI DEFA 5.00000E-01 1 4.50000E-01 0 3.00000E-01 0 3.00000E-01 1 1.50000E-01 0 2.50000E-01 0 9.00000E-01 1 4.00000E-01 1 > \mathrm{⋮} ⋮ Example of the analysis of a fragility curve: TAB_POST=POST_DYNA_ALEA( FRAGILITE=(_F(TABL_RESU=TAB1, LIST_PARA=lr, > AM_INI =0.3 , BETA_INI=0.1 , FRACTILE = (0.0,0.05,0.5,0.95,1.0), NB_TIRAGE =50, ),), TITRE = 'courbe 1', INFO=2,); In this example, a resampling is carried out ( N=\mathit{nbtr}=50 ) in order to estimate the 5%, 50% (median) and 95% fractiles of the curve, and the envelopes (100% and 0%) are determined. 5.2 Keyword INTERSPECTRE First example: POSTALEA =POST_DYNA_ALEA( INTERSPECTRE = _F( INTE_SPEC= INTERS, OPTION='DIAG' ) ) Second example: POSTALEA=POST_DYNA_ALEA(INTERSPECTRE = _F( INTE_SPEC=INTERS, NOEUD_I='N1', NOM_CMP_I='DX', NOEUD_J='N1', NOM_CMP_J='DX', ) )

u4.84.05 Operator POST_USURE u4.84.05 Operator POST_USURE 1 Purpose Compute the worn volume and the wear depth from the wear power. The wear power is given or computed by the operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. A wear law, a contact geometry and a list of time instants must be supplied. Si: equal_to("LOI_USURE", 'EDF_MZ') ◆ / MOBILE = _F( ◇ COEF_USURE = float (défaut: 1e-13), ◇ COEF_B = float (défaut: 1.2), ◇ COEF_N = float (défaut: 2.44e-08), ◇ COEF_S = float (défaut: 1.14e-16), ), / MATER_USURE = text, ◇ / USURE_OBST = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ / OBSTACLE = _F( ◇ COEF_USURE = float (défaut: 1e-13), ◇ COEF_B = float (défaut: 1.2), ◇ COEF_N = float (défaut: 2.44e-08), ◇ COEF_S = float (défaut: 1.14e-16), ), # Si: not exists("TUBE_NEUF") ◇ INST_INIT = float (défaut: -1.0), ◇ NB_BLOC = int (défaut: 1), ◇ COEF_INST = float (défaut: 1.0), ◆ / INST = float, / LIST_INST = listr8, # Si: exists("TUBE_NEUF") ◇ INST = float, ◆ TABL_USURE = table, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ TITRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands Attention is drawn here to a few delicate points in the use of POST_USURE. 1. The result of POST_USURE does not depend on the final mechanical state of the analysis but on the whole history of the shocks. It is therefore very important to take into account all the analysis time instants, that is, not to request selective archiving in DYNA_VIBRA. 2. The result of POST_USURE is very sensitive to the analysis parameters, in particular to the richness of the modal basis and to the time step. It is therefore strongly recommended to test different modal bases (increasingly rich) and different time steps (increasingly small). For example, for the time step, one may test different values spaced by a factor of 10, then of 2, in order to determine a range of time steps over which the result is stable. 3. In the case of a vibratory analysis, one may obtain a result which is not representative of the real wear if the experiment is not long enough. Likewise, in the case of randomly generated excitations, it is recommended to carry out several draws before drawing sizing conclusions. 3.1 Case PUIS_USURE or RESU_GENE 3.1.1 Operand PUIS_USURE ♦ PUIS_USURE = pu The wear power is: - taken from the result of a transient analysis by modal recombination, produced by the operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03 (following operands), - or given by the user, who then uses the operand PUIS_USURE. 3.1.2 Operand RESU_GENE ♦ RESU_GENE = tg Result of a transient analysis by modal recombination, produced by the operator DYNA_VIBRA U4.53.03. 3.1.3 Operand GROUP _ NO ♦ GROUP _ NO = grnoeu, Definition of the shock node to be post-processed. 3.1.4 Operand INST_INIT ◊ INST_INIT = t0 Start time instant of the averaging of the signals (cf. [§4]). (t0 = 0. default value). 3.1.5 Operand INST_FIN ◊ INST_FIN = t1 End time instant of the averaging of the signals. 3.1.6 Operand NB_BLOC ◊ NB_BLOC = nb Number of time blocks into which the interval [t0, t1] is split for the averaging of the signals (1 by default). 3.2 Case TUBE_NEUF For the processing of the wear of the control-rod clusters, the user may take into account the replacement of a tube by a new tube by supplying the keyword TUBE_NEUF = 'OUI' 3.2.1 Operand TUBE_NEUF ◊ TUBE_NEUF = 'OUI' If the user supplies this keyword, the operator modifies the wear values of the tube (V_USUR_TUBE, P_USUR_TUBE, V_USUR_TUBE_SECT, P_USUR_TUBE_SECT, V_USUR_TUBE_CUMU = 0) in the table produced by POST_USURE for the time instants later than the time instant at which the new tube is loaded. 3.2.2 Operand TABL_USURE ♦ TABL_USURE = tresu If the user supplies the keyword TUBE_NEUF = 'OUI', the name of the table to be updated must be entered.
