géom Definition of the contact geometry. Depending on the type of contact, different geometrical relations between the worn volumes and the worn depths. 3.6.1 Operand CONTACT = 'GRAPPE_ALESAGE' The cluster is centred in a bore. The wear scar has a lune-shaped cross-section. The worn volume is reduced to a worn area in a cross-section. 3.6.2 Operand CONTACT = 'GRAPPE_1_ENCO' The cluster is centred with respect to the obstacle. The guide card is formed of one notch. The worn volume is reduced to a worn area in a cross-section. The coefficients are based both on the experimental results and on those from operating experience. They apply only to the control-rod clusters. 3.6.3 Operand CONTACT = 'GRAPPE_2_ENCO' The cluster is centred with respect to the obstacle. The guide card is formed of two diametrically opposite notches. The worn volume is reduced to a worn area in a cross-section. The coefficients are based both on the experimental results and on those from operating experience. They apply only to the control-rod clusters. 3.6.4 Operand CONTACT = 'TUBE_BAV' Case 1: The tube is vertical, the bar impacts perpendicularly to the tube, and it is assumed that the bar does not wear. Case 2: The bar is inclined (operand ANGL_INCLI) with respect to the tube, the bar impacts perpendicularly to the tube, and it is assumed that the bar does not wear. Case 3: The tube is vertical, the bar impacts perpendicularly to the tube, and the wear of the bar is taken into account. Case 4: The bar is inclined (operand ANGL_INCLI) with respect to the tube, the bar impacts perpendicularly to the tube, and the wear of the bar is taken into account. 3.6.5 Operand CONTACT = 'TUBE_ALESAGE' Case 1: The tube is perfectly centred in a bore animated by a pure orbital motion and wears uniformly over the whole periphery in contact with the obstacle. Case 2: The tube is centred in a bore animated by an elliptical impact-sliding motion which leads to the formation of cylindrical wear scars, diametrically opposite on the tube and having a lune-shaped cross-section. Case 3: The tube, animated by an impact-sliding motion, this time has an inclination with respect to the support (operand ANGL_INCLI). Two symmetrical V-shaped wear scars are obtained on the tube. 3.6.6 Operand CONTACT = 'TUBE_3_ENCO' Case 1: The initial contact takes place against an edge of one of the isthmuses of a trefoil bore. The tube is assumed to be perfectly centred with respect to its obstacle. The wear scar does not extend over the whole isthmus. The wear of the obstacle is not taken into account. Case 2: Same assumptions as for case 1 except for the position of the tube with respect to the obstacle. It is assumed this time that the tube has an angle of inclination (operand ANGL_INCLI). 3.6.7 Operand CONTACT = 'TUBE_4_ENCO' Case 1: The initial contact takes place against an edge of one of the isthmuses of the quatrefoil bore. The tube is assumed to be perfectly centred with respect to its obstacle. The wear scar does not extend over the whole isthmus. The wear of the obstacle is not taken into account. Case 2: Same assumptions as for case 1 except for the position of the tube with respect to the obstacle. It is assumed this time that the tube has an angle of inclination (operand ANGL_INCLI). 3.6.8 Operand CONTACT = 'TUBE_TUBE' Following the rupture of a plugged tube, there may be contact between this tube and one of its neighbours. The wear of the two tubes by accommodation of the surfaces in contact leads to the creation of two plane surfaces. 3.7 Description of the obstacle 3.7.1 Operand RAYON_MOBILE ♦ RAYON_MOBILE = r_t Definition of the radius of the moving body (mandatory parameter). 3.7.2 Operand RAYON_OBST ♦ RAYON_OBST = r_o Definition of the radius of the obstacle (mandatory parameter if the wear of the obstacle is taken into account). 3.7.3 Operand LARGEUR_OBST ♦ LARGEUR_OBST = l_o Definition of the width of the obstacle (mandatory parameter for the operands TUBE_ ). 3.7.4 Operand ANGL_INCLI ◊ ANGL_INCLI = angl Definition of the angle of inclination of the moving body with respect to the obstacle (optional parameter = the value 0. is taken by default). 3.7.5 Operand ANGL_ISTHME ♦ ANGL_ISTHME = angli Definition of the angle of the isthmus of the contact geometry (mandatory parameter for the operands TUBE_3_ENCO and TUBE_4_ENCO). 3.8 Definition of the analysis time instants 3.8.1 Case PUIS_USURE or RESU_GENE 3.8.1.1 Operands INST / LIST_INST / COEF_INST ♦ INST = l_inst Definition of the analysis time instants in the form of a list of values. ♦ LIST_INST = linst Definition of the analysis time instants in the form of a concept of type listr8. ◊ COEF_INST = coef The time instants given are to be multiplied by a given coefficient coef, which makes it easy to pass from SI units to the natural units for a wear analysis (the month of the year). 3.8.2 Case TUBE_NEUF If TUBE_NEUF = 'OUI', the loading time instant may be entered. 3.8.2.1 Operand INST ◊ INST = inst Loading time instant of a new tube. The wear values of the tube (V_USUR_TUBE, P_USUR_TUBE, V_USUR_TUBE_SECT, P_USUR_TUBE_SECT, V_USUR_TUBE_CUMU) are set to 0 for the time instants later than the loading time instant of the new tube. By default, the wear values of the last time instant of the table are set to 0 if TUBE_NEUF = 'OUI'. 3.9 Operand ETAT_INIT 3.9.1 Keyword TABL_USURE ♦ TABL_USURE= tresu [table_sdaster] Definition of the table that one wishes to update. 3.9.2 Keyword INST_INIT ◊ INST_INIT= tt [R] Definition of the time instant from which one wishes to update the table. 3.10 Operands TITRE / INFO ◊ TITRE = ’montitre’ Title that one wishes to give to the result U4.03.01. ◊ INFO = / 1 / 2 Printout level | 1 | no printout. | | --- | --- | | 2 | printout of the worn volumes and wear depths at the specified time instants | 3.11 Table produced The command POST_USURE generates a concept of type table, whose content is: | INST: | time instants at which the user wishes to know the worn volume and the wear depth, | | --- | --- | | V_usur_tube: | worn volume at the tube (for each time instant specified by the user), | | V_usur_obst: | worn volume at the obstacle (for each time instant specified by the user), | | P_usur_tube: | wear depth at the tube (for each time instant specified by the user). | The command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03 makes it possible to print the results. 4 Checking — Execution 4.1 Operand MATER_USURE One checks that the pair of materials supplied by the user is present in the database. 4.2 Operands RESU_GENE / INST_INIT / INST_FIN / NB_BLOC The value of INST_FIN is compared with the final time instant {t}_{f} of the tran_gene result. The value of INST_FIN retained is \min({t}_{f},{t}_{1}) . If the value of INST_INIT {t}_{0} is greater than the value of INST_FIN, the analysis stops in error. 5 Example dateu = DEFI_LIST_REEL(DEBUT = 0.25, INTERVALLE = _F(JUSQU_A = 1., NOMBRE = 20 ), _F(JUSQU_A = 5., NOMBRE = 10 ), _F(JUSQU_A = 10., NOMBRE = 5 ) ) # us1 = POST_USURE ( PUIS_USURE = 0.312, LOI_USURE = 'ARCHARD', NB_BLOC = 4, MOBILE = _F(COEF_USURE = 30.e-15 ), OBSTACLE = _F(COEF_USURE = 20.e-15), CONTACT = 'GRAPPE_1_ENCO', RAYON_MOBILE = 0.00485, RAYON_OBST = 0.00545, LIST_INST = dateu, COEF_INST = 31557600., TITRE = 'NO1 = Usure par années', INFO = 2 ) # us2 = POST_USURE ( RESU_GENE = dynamoda, GROUP_NO = ’GNO1’, LOI_USURE = 'EDF_MZ', MOBILE = _F( COEF_USURE = 1.e-13, COEF_B = 1.2, COEF_N = 2.44e-08, COEF_S = 1.14e-16, ), OBSTACLE = _F( COEF_USURE = 1.e-13, COEF_B = 1.2, COEF_N = 2.44e-08, COEF_S = 1.14e-16 ), USURE_OBST = 'OUI', CONTACT = 'GRAPPE_1_ENCO', RAYON_MOBILE = 0.00485, RAYON_OBST = 0.00545, LIST_INST = dateu, COEF_INST = 31557600., TITRE = 'NO1 = Usure par année', INFO = 2 )

| : plusieurs choix possibles 2 Operands 2.1 Operand RESULTAT Simple keyword making it possible to retrieve the result data structure of type evol_noli which contains, among other things, the displacement field on the surface of the raft at the various time instants. 2.2 Operand NOM_CHAM Simple keyword making it possible to collect the name of the field. By default it is 'DEPL', the displacement field. 2.3 Operand NOM_CMP Simple keyword making it possible to supply the name of the component of the displacement field which shows the lift-off. By default, it is 'DZ'. 2.4 Operand GROUP_MA Simple keyword making it possible to retrieve the group of surface mesh cells of the raft. 2.5 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = /1, [DEFAUT] /2, Level of messages in the file 'MESSAGE'. > If INFO = 2, then the table produced by this operator is printed in the file 'MESSAGE'. 3 Principle of the macro-command The operator POST_DECOLLEMENT carries out the following actions: - computes the total area of the raft: it calls the command POST_ELEM/INTEGRALE to determine the area of the mesh-cell group supplied to the operand GROUP_MA. This analysis requires the creation of a 2D model reduced to the mesh-cell group GROUP_MA and the creation of a unit field at the nodes of this group before it is integrated. - loops over the time instants of the result data structure supplied to the operand RESULTAT in order to: - extract from it the component NOM_CMP of the displacement field NOM_CHAM at the current time instant, - define a nodal field whose values are 0 at the negative values of NOM_CMP of the field NOM_CHAM, and 1 at the strictly positive values, - determine the area of the raft for which the values of the previous field are equal to 1, - compute the ratio of the areas in order to obtain the raft/soil lift-off percentage. Although this operator was developed to compute the lift-off area of a raft on the soil in soil–structure interaction analyses, it may be used for other purposes, on fields other than a displacement field. 4 Example This example is taken from the test case zzzz200d: one is interested in the lift-off percentage along the Z axis of the mesh-cell group 'SRADIER' corresponding to the surface of the raft. choix possibles 3 Operands The command makes it possible to compute the complement of internal forces due to the non-linearities of the constitutive behaviour. This analysis concerns the constitutive laws in which the internal forces depend essentially on the kinematic fields (displacements, velocities, accelerations); it therefore concerns above all the localised non-linearities, for example penalised contact between discrete elements. The terms computed at the nodes are obtained by the difference between the integrated residual of internal forces (depending both on the kinematic fields and on the parameters of the constitutive law) and the internal force that would be obtained from the same kinematic fields by considering a linear constitutive behaviour for the structure. Note 1: The name of the result concept created, of type dyna_trans, must be different from the name of the result concept of type dyna_trans used as input under the operand RESULTAT, and it constitutes an evolution of fields of type ‘ DEPL’. This new result of complementary nodal forces is used under the keyword EXCIT_RESU in the command DYNA_VIBRA with TYPE_RESU='HARM' (in this case after transformation by the operator REST_SPEC_TEMP U4.63.34) and DYNA_VIBRA or DYNA_VIBRA and TYPE_RESU='TRAN'. An example is supplied in the test case SDLS119A. Note 2: In the specific case of the analysis with the relation ‘DIS_CHOC’ assigned to discrete elements, it is then necessary always to orient the discrete contact element in the direction from the structure towards the stop. Whether with POI1 elements, as always by means of the keyword ORIENTATION of AFFE_CARA_ELEM, but also with SEG2 elements, where one must properly define the element in the sense from the structure that is a candidate for contact, associated with node 1, towards the stop, associated with node 2. 3.1 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / NUME_MODE/ NOEUD_CMP / NOM_CAS / INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / PRECISION / CRITERE See U4.71.00 for the description of these operands. 3.1.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo, Name of the model, which it is necessary to enter 3.1.2 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmater, Name of the material field in which the material characteristics of the elements are defined. This argument is necessary for the analysis because the constitutive laws defined in the keywords COMPORTEMENT always require a material field. 3.1.3 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac, The concept of the elementary characteristics of type cara_elem is necessary for the analysis if structural elements exist in the model. 3.1.4 Operand COMPORTEMENT ◊ COMPORTEMENT = _F Factor keyword making it possible to assign constitutive laws to mesh cells or to mesh-cell groups of the mesh. One defines one assignment per occurrence of the keyword COMPORTEMENT. 3.1.4.1 Operand RELATION ◊ RELATION, Name of a constitutive-law relation in text format. The relations accepted are those in which the internal forces depend essentially on the kinematic fields (displacements, velocities, accelerations); besides the relation ‘ELAS’, the first relation provided for is the relation ‘DIS_CHOC’ assigned to discrete elements. 3.1.4.2 Operand DEFORMATION ◊ DEFORMATION, Name of the type of strain in text format, compatible with the type of the elements assigned the constitutive law. 3.1.4.3 Operands TOUT/GROUP_MA/MAILLE ◊ TOUT = 'OUI' , The relation is assigned over the whole mesh. > ◊ GROUP_MA = lgma , The relation is assigned on the mesh-cell groups contained in the list lgma. > ◊ MAILLE = lma , The relation is assigned on the mesh cells contained in the list lma.

u4.84.31 Command DEFI_SOL_EQUI u4.84.31 Command DEFI_SOL_EQUI 1 Purpose Characterise the variation of the mechanical characteristics of layers of stratified soil in the course of an earthquake from their level of shear strain. For this, one determines by an iterative procedure, for each of these soil layers, equivalent linear characteristics recalibrated from the curves of reduction of the shear modulus and of increase of the hysteretic damping as a function of the shear strain. This procedure generally relies on a model of a column of stratified soil with two different types of modelling: - 2D in plane strain, meshed by horizontal layers, subjected to a driving acceleration with a periodicity condition between the left-hand face and the right-hand face and an absorbing condition at the base. This modelling also allows the simplified taking into account of the water pressures by the Byrne method. - 3D, meshed by horizontal layers and subjected to a driving acceleration in the 3 directions X, Y and Z, with penalisation stiffnesses on the lateral edges in order to ensure the same dynamic behaviour in the two horizontal directions and an absorbing condition at the base. The command DEFI_SOL_EQUI makes it possible to produce a table containing the information necessary for the description of a soil file for the software MISS3D. 2 Syntax table = DEFI_SOL_EQUI( ◇ LIEU_SIGNAL = / "AFFLEURANT" (par défaut), / "CHAMP_LIBRE", ◇ CHARGEMENT = / "MONO_APPUI" (par défaut), / "ONDE_PLANE", # Si: equal_to("CHARGEMENT", 'ONDE_PLANE') ◆ / FONC_SIGNAL = fonction, / UNITE_TRAN_INIT = unit, / FONC_SIGNAL_X = fonction, ◇ & FONC_SIGNAL_Y = fonction, & FONC_SIGNAL_Z = fonction, & GROUP_MA_ARRETE_1 = grma, & GROUP_MA_ARRETE_2 = grma, ◇ TOUT_CHAM = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ / LIAISON = / "PERIODIQUE", / "SANS", ◇ MASS_PENA = float, ◇ LONG_CARA = float, ◇ NOM_CMP = / "DX" (par défaut), / "DY", # Si: exists("FONC_SIGNAL_X") ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: not exists("FONC_SIGNAL_X") ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: not exists("GROUP_MA_ARRETE_1") ◇ CORRECTION = / "BYRNE", / "SANS" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("CORRECTION", 'BYRNE') ◇ COEF_KSI = float (défaut: 0.666666667), # Si: equal_to("CHARGEMENT", 'MONO_APPUI') ◆ / FONC_SIGNAL = fonction, / DSP = fonction, / FONC_SIGNAL_X = fonction, ◇ & FONC_SIGNAL_Y = fonction, & FONC_SIGNAL_Z = fonction, & GROUP_MA_ARRETE_1 = grma, & GROUP_MA_ARRETE_2 = grma, # Si: exists('DSP') ◆ DUREE = float, ◆ UNITE_RESU_DSP = unit, ◇ NOM_CMP = / "DX" (par défaut), / "DY", ◇ TOUT_CHAM = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: exists("FONC_SIGNAL_X") ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: not exists("FONC_SIGNAL_X") ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, # Si: not exists("GROUP_MA_ARRETE_1") ◇ CORRECTION = / "BYRNE", / "SANS" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("CORRECTION", 'BYRNE') ◇ COEF_KSI = float (défaut: 0.666666667), ◇ CORR_AMOR = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ LIST_FREQ_SPEC_OSCI = listr8, ◇ LIST_FREQ = listr8, ◇ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ & GROUP_MA_DROITE = grma, & GROUP_MA_GAUCHE = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_SUBSTR = grma, ◆ GROUP_MA_COL = grma, ◇ COEF_VARI_MATE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ COEF_AMPL_ACCE = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ COEF_GAMMA = float (défaut: 0.65), ◇ NMAX_ITER = int (défaut: 10), ◇ RESI_RELA = float (défaut: 0.05), ◇ FREQ_COUP = float, ◇ FREQ_FILTRE = float, ◇ INTEGRATION = / "TEMPS" (par défaut), / "FREQUENCE", ◇ SURF = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("SURF", 'NON') ◆ NIVE_COUCH_ENFO = int, ◇ NB_RECEPTEUR = / 2 (par défaut), / 4, ◇ UNITE_TABLE_RESU = unit, ◇ UNITE_RESU_TRAN = unit (défaut: 40), ◇ UNITE_RESU_SPEC = unit (défaut: 55), ◇ & TABLE_MATER_ELAS = table, & TABLE_GEQUI_GMAX = table, & TABLE_AMOR_EQUI = table, ◇ SEPARATEUR = text (défaut: " "), ◇ LIST_EPSI = listr8, # Si: not exists("TABLE_MATER_ELAS") ◇ MATERIAU = _F( ◆ GAMMA = float, ◆ G_GMAX = float, ◆ D = float, ), ◇ COUCHE = _F( ◆ EPAIS = float, ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ E = float, ◆ NU = float, ◆ RHO = float, ◆ AMOR_HYST = float, ◆ NUME_MATE = int, ◇ N1 = float, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand CHARGEMENT ◊ CHARGEMENT = / 'MONO_APPUI', [DEFAUT] / 'ONDE_PLANE', Indicates the nature of the loading imposing the motion: CHARGEMENT = 'MONO_APPUI': loading in the form of a single-support driving acceleration imposed on the soil column. CHARGEMENT = 'ONDE_PLANE': loading in the form of a vertically propagating plane wave in velocity imposed on the soil column, a shear wave if the excitation motion is horizontal, a pressure wave if the excitation motion is vertical. 3.2 Operand FONC_SIGNAL ♦ FONC_SIGNAL = foncs Makes it possible to define a time function defining the acceleration signal for a 1D modelling – 1 component: a driving acceleration if the loading is single-support, or else a loading by a vertically propagating plane wave, imposed on the column model representative of the soil stratification. From this model one characterises the variation of the mechanical characteristics of layers of stratified soil as a function of their level of shear strain. Note 1 It is necessary that the initial time instant of the signal be zero and that the time step \mathit{dt} be constant. If one uses a number of time steps which is a power of two, then the final time will necessarily be equal to ({2}^{N}-1)\mathit{dt} . Note 2 In the case of a plane-wave loading, this option is an alternative to the supply of a table of the transient evolutions of the accelerations, and possibly of the velocities and displacements obtained by a previous call to DEFI_SOL_EQUI. This table is supplied by the keyword UNITE_TRAN_INIT. 3.3 Operands FONC_SIGNAL_X/FONC_SIGNAL_Y/FONC_SIGNAL_Z ♦ FONC_SIGNAL _X = foncs ♦ FONC_SIGNAL _Y = foncs ♦ FONC_SIGNAL _Z = foncs Makes it possible to define the time functions defining the acceleration signal for a 1D modelling – 3 components: a driving acceleration if the loading is single-support, or else a loading by a vertically propagating plane wave, imposed on the column model representative of the soil stratification. Note It is necessary that the initial time instant of the signal be zero and that the time step \mathit{dt} be constant. If one uses a number of time steps which is a power of two, then the final time will necessarily be equal to ({2}^{N}-1)\mathit{dt} . 3.4 Operand DSP ◊ DSP = dsp [FONCTION] The operand makes it possible to define a spectral density function (DSP) imposed on the column model representative of the soil stratification. This keyword is compatible only with a single-support loading. If the keyword DSP is present, then one calls on the tools of the RVT ( Random Vibration Theory ) for the (de)convolution and the computation of the degraded soil profiles. The DSP equivalent to a spectrum (SRO) is obtained beforehand by CALC_FONCTION/SPEC_OSCI. This approach, which does not require a passage into the time domain for the computation of the maximum responses and of the response spectra, is also called spectrum transfer. 3.5 Operand LIEU_SIGNAL ◊ LIEU_SIGNAL = / 'AFFLEURANT', [DEFAUT] / 'CHAMP_LIBRE', Indicates the place of imposition of the signal with respect to the soil column: LIEU_SIGNAL = 'AFFLEURANT': signal imposed at the base of the column (at the outcropping bedrock). LIEU_SIGNAL = 'CHAMP_LIBRE': signal imposed at the top of the column (in the free field). 3.6 Operand DUREE ◊ DUREE = T [R] This keyword is to be supplied only in the presence of the keyword DSP. Cf. U4.32.04 for the meaning of this keyword. 3.7 Operand NOM_CMP ◊ NOM_CMP = / 'DX', [DEFAUT] / 'DY', Indicates the direction of the signal imposed on the soil column: NOM_CMP = 'DX': horizontal imposed signal. This is the usual case, in which one determines the variation of the mechanical characteristics of the layers of stratified soil in the course of the earthquake from their level of shear strain. NOM_CMP = 'DY': vertical imposed signal. In this case, the mechanical characteristics of the layers of stratified soil do not vary in the course of the earthquake. The only point of interest is to supply as a result the transient evolutions and the acceleration spectra obtained at the bottom of each soil layer. 3.8 Operand FREQ_COUP ◊ FREQ_COUP = freqc Cut-off frequency making it possible to filter the input signal. By default, one takes a maximum value corresponding to half the inverse of the time step of the input signal. 3.9 Operand INTEGRATION ◊ INTEGRATION = / 'TEMPS', [DEFAUT] / 'FREQUENCE', Makes it possible to choose the method of integration in post-processing of the motion signals in displacement or velocity. By default, one keeps the time method by the value 'TEMPS', which implements the call to the option INTEGRE of CALC_FONCTION. Otherwise one may choose the frequency method by the value 'FREQUENCE', which implements the call to the option INTEGRE_FREQ of CALC_FONCTION. 3.10 Operand FREQ_FILTRE ◊ FREQ_FILTRE = / 0.0 , [DEFAUT] / freqf Frequency making it possible to filter the input signal from below if one has chosen the frequency integration method. By default, one takes a zero value, which cancels the filtering from below. 3.11 Operand MAILLAGE ◊ MAILLAGE = ma If the modelling is of type 1D – 1 component, makes it possible to define the name of the concept of the global surface mesh of the column representative of the soil stratification. A plane-strain model ('D_PLAN') will be assigned to it. If the operand is not supplied, one will fill, from the names of mesh-cell groups supplied in the operands GROUP_MA, the contents of a mesh file in 'ASTER' format printed in the file RESULTAT. If the modelling is of type 1D – 3 components, makes it possible to define the name of the concept of the volume mesh of the column representative of the stratification of the soil, to which a 3D modelling will be assigned. In this case, this keyword is mandatory. 3.12 Operand GROUP_MA_COL ♦ GROUP_MA_COL = gmco Makes it possible to define, in the previous mesh (if it exists), the name of the surface mesh-cell group comprising the whole of the column representative of the soil stratification. If the modelling is 1D – 1 component and the previous mesh does not exist, this group will be created in the mesh file in 'ASTER' format filled by the operator. 3.13 Operands GROUP_MA_DROITE/GROUP_MA_GAUCHE ♦ GROUP_MA_DROITE = gmda ♦ GROUP_MA_GAUCHE = gmga For a 1D – 1 component simulation, make it possible to define respectively, in the previous mesh (if it exists), the names of the line mesh-cell groups to which a periodicity relation will be assigned between the right-hand edge and the left-hand edge of the column representative of the soil stratification. If the previous mesh does not exist, these groups will be created in the mesh file in 'ASTER' format filled by the operator. For a 1D – 3 component simulation, make it possible to define respectively, in the previous mesh, the names of the surface mesh-cell groups on the facing faces of the column to which a periodicity relation will be assigned. 3.14 Operands GROUP_MA_ARRETE_1 and GROUP_MA_ARRETE_2 ♦ GROUP_MA_ARRETE_1= gmda ♦ GROUP_MA_ARRETE_2= gmda Only for a 1D – 3 component simulation, makes it possible to define the name of the line mesh-cell groups defining the edges over the whole length of the column, both belonging to the same face defined either by GROUP_MA_GAUCHE or by GROUP_MA_DROITE, to which a periodicity relation will be assigned. 3.15 Operand GROUP_MA_SUBSTR ♦ GROUP_MA_SUBSTR = gmdr For a 1D – 1 component modelling, makes it possible to define, in the previous mesh (if it exists), the name of the line mesh-cell group to which an absorbing-boundary modelling will be assigned. If the previous mesh does not exist, this group will be created in the mesh file in 'ASTER' format filled by the operator. For a 1D – 3 component modelling, makes it possible to define, in the previous mesh, the name of the surface mesh-cell group to which an absorbing-boundary modelling will be assigned. 3.16 Operand CORRECTION ◊ CORRECTION = / 'SANS', [DEFAUT] / 'BYRNE', For a 1D – 1 component modelling, makes it possible to activate the taking into account of the water pressures in a simplified manner by the Byrne model. In this case, the evaluation of the degraded value of the shear modulus is corrected by a factor depending on the rise of effective water pressure computed. 3.17 Operand COEF_KSI ◊ COEF_KSI = / 0.666666667 [ DEFAUT ] /coef_ksi, [R] Parameter making it possible to define the value of the weighting coefficient which makes it possible to modulate the impact of {r}_{\mathit{umax}} on the effective strain for a 1D – 1 component modelling with the Byrne model. 3.18 Operand SURF ◊ SURF = / 'NON', [DEFAUT] / 'OUI', Indicates whether or not one wishes to have certain layers of the soil modelled in the column above an embedded foundation, which one finds in the soil table usable by MISS3D: SURF = 'OUI': shallow foundation with respect to the soil layers. SURF = 'NON': embedment of the foundation in the soil. 3.19 Operand NIVE_COUCH_ENFO ◊ NIVE_COUCH_ENFO = ncoue If SURF = 'NON', this keyword becomes mandatory: it then gives the number of soil layers above the embedded foundation. 3.20 Operand NB_RECEPTEUR ◊ NB_RECEPTEUR = / 2, [DEFAUT] / 4, This keyword has a meaning only if SURF = 'NON': it makes it possible to define the number of receivers per layer of element embedded in the stratified soil: it also corresponds to the number of sub-layers generated for each layer of embedded element in the soil table produced. 3.21 Keyword MATERIAU ♦ MATERIAU = _F ( Repeatable factor keyword allowing the description of the characteristics of families of non-linear materials, material by material, defined by curves of reduction of the shear modulus and of increase of the hysteretic damping as a function of the shear strain. These materials constitute groups of layers of the stratified soil. Each group is generally associated with a geological zone (clay, rock...). 3.21.1 Operand GAMMA ♦ GAMMA = lgamma Makes it possible to define the ordered increasing list of reals of the abscissae of the shear strain for each family of non-linear material defined in the column. 3.21.2 Operands G_GMAX/D ♦ G_GMAX = lggma, ♦ D = lisd, Make it possible to define respectively the lists of real values of reduction of the shear modulus and of increase of the internal damping D, half of the hysteretic damping, as a function of the shear strain for each current non-linear material. Each of the terms of these lists corresponds to a value of the list supplied by the operand GAMMA. All these lists must therefore have the same cardinality for the same material. Note 1 It is necessary to define a non-linear material for the last soil layer corresponding to the substratum, which will have, for the operand G_GMAX, constant values of 1 (no reduction) and, for the operand D, constant values of the half-value of the hysteretic damping of the substratum. Note 2 The functions thus created are extended to the left and to the right with the option 'CONSTANT' and interpolated with an option ('LOG','LIN'). Note 3 If the lists of the abscissae of the shear strain of the families of non-linear material differ from one another, one will use as a common reference list, in order to define by interpolation the description of the characteristics of the non-linear materials, material by material, the list of the non-linear material for the last soil layer corresponding to the substratum. One may nevertheless force the supply of the common reference list by the operand LIST_EPSI. 3.22 Operand LIST_EPSI ◊ LIST_EPSI = lepsi Makes it possible to force the supply of the common reference list of the abscissae of the shear strain for interpolation of the characteristics of the families of non-linear material. 3.23 Keyword COUCHE ♦ COUCHE = _F ( Repeatable factor keyword allowing the geometrical description of the layers of a stratified soil, that of the characteristics of the materials constituting these layers, and the assignment, layer by layer, of the non-linear materials defined previously by the keyword MATERIAU. 3.23.1 Operands EPAIS/E/NU/RHO/AMOR_HYST/N1 Make it possible to define respectively the real values of the thickness, of Young's modulus, of Poisson's ratio, of the density and of the initial hysteretic damping of each layer; as a reminder, twice the value of the internal damping D (to be supplied in absolute value and not as a percentage). For the modelling with the Byrne model, the user must also supply the value {N1}_{60} of the SPT of the layer. This value is used to obtain the parameters of the Byrne model via the following expression: {C}_{1}=\frac{8,7}{{({N}_{1})}_{60}^{1,25}} {C}_{2}=\frac{0,4}{{C}_{1}} Note A special treatment is applied so that the value N1=0 supplies the same result as for a modelling CORRECTION = 'SANS' (cf. test case zzzz412e). 3.23.2 Operand NUME_MATE ♦ NUME_MATE = numat Number of the non-linear material in the order of description of the occurrences of the keyword MATERIAU to be assigned to the current layer. 3.23.3 Operand GROUP_MA ♦ GROUP_MA = gmaco Makes it possible to define the name of the surface mesh-cell group of the current layer. The last occurrence corresponds to a substratum layer. If the latter is not meshed in the column model, then one assigns to it the name of the line mesh-cell group of the substratum already supplied by the keyword GROUP_MA_SUBSTR. If the operand MAILLAGE is not supplied, this group will be created in the mesh file in 'ASTER' format filled by the operator. 3.24 Operand COEF_VARI_MATE ◊ COEF_VARI_MATE = / 1.0, [DEFAUT] / coevm Gives a global amplification factor of Young's moduli defined initially in the keyword COUCHE. Besides the default unit value, one also generally uses in sizing studies the values 1.5 and 0.67. 3.25 Operand COEF_AMPL_ACCE ◊ COEF_AMPL_ACCE = / 1.0, [DEFAUT] / coeaa Gives an amplification factor of the acceleration signal defined initially by the operand FONC_SIGNAL. 3.26 Operand COEF_GAMMA ◊ COEF_GAMMA = / 0.65, [DEFAUT] / coega Gives a factor, less than 1, used to compute the effective strain from the maximum strain obtained in each of the soil layers during the signal. The value obtained will give the level from which one will determine the variation of the characteristics of the non-linear material constituting the layer, by reading on the curves given by the operands D and G_GAMMA of the keyword MATERIAU. 3.27 Operand CORR_AMOR ◊ CORR_AMOR = / 'NON', [DEFAUT] / 'OUI', Indicates whether or not one wishes to correct the datum of the hysteretic damping given by material by introducing a new formulation of the shear modulus G which corrects the real modulus G by the formulation of LYSMER, namely that G is written: {G}^{\text{ }}=G[(1-{2\xi }^{2})+2\xi j\sqrt{1-{\xi}^{2}}] This formulation makes it possible to obtain the equality between the real value of G and the modulus of the complex G . This is done by adding the keyword CORR_AMOR equal to 'OUI'. 3.28 Operand LIST_FREQ Allows the user to introduce a list of frequencies for the computation of the harmonic evolution launched by the operator. By default, the operator imposes one bounded by the cut-off frequency (operand FREQ_COUP). 3.29 Operand LIST_FREQ_SPEC_OSCI Allows the user to introduce a list of frequencies different from the one used by default in the computation of the oscillator response spectra (or SRO) by the option SPEC_OSCI of CALC_FONCTION. 3.30 Operands NMAX_ITER/RESI_RELA Give the parameters of the iterative process of variation of the characteristics of the materials constituting the layers. Respectively the maximum number of iterations and the stopping criterion on the maximum relative variation, between two successive iterations, of Young's modulus over the set of soil layers. “Iteration” here has the meaning “analysis stage”. At least some are needed in order to compute the possible degradations and to establish the stopping criterion with respect to the initial state. Therefore NMAX_ITER is greater than or equal to 1. 3.31 Operands TABLE_GEQUI_GMAX/TABLE_AMOR_EQUI Represent an alternative to the description of the characteristics of the non-linear materials, material by material, defined by the factor keyword MATERIAU. One may then give directly tables of values resulting from an initial definition by this keyword. For example, one will be able respectively to read the contents of these tables produced by a first pass of DEFI_SOL_EQUI in the test case SDNX100E: - the table supplied by TABLE_GEQUI_GMAX will contain the following information on the variation of the reduction of the shear modulus by material: | | | --- | - the table supplied by TABLE_AMOR_EQUI will contain the following information on the variation of the increase of the hysteretic damping by material: | | | --- | One specifies that the damping values must be given in absolute value and not as a percentage. 3.32 Operand TABLE_MATER_ELAS Represents an alternative to the geometrical description of the layers of stratified soil and that of the characteristics of the materials constituting these layers, defined by the factor keyword COUCHE. As for the factor keyword COUCHE, if the operand MAILLAGE is not supplied, the groups given in the table supplied by the operand TABLE_MATER_ELAS will be created in the mesh file in 'ASTER' format filled by the operator. One may then give directly, by the operand TABLE_MATER_ELAS, a table of values resulting from an initial definition by the factor keyword COUCHE. For example, one will be able to read the contents of this table produced by a first pass of DEFI_SOL_EQUI in the test case SDNX100E: - the table supplied by TABLE_MATER_ELAS will contain the following information on the geometrical description of the layers of stratified soil and that of the initial characteristics of the materials constituting these layers, layer by layer: | | | --- | Note The names of the columns given on the first line correspond to the names of the access parameters of the table. They must be kept as they are. 3.33 Operand UNITE_TABLE_RESU Supplies the logical unit for writing the table containing the result of the iterative process of DEFI_SOL_EQUI, including the evolution in the course of the analysis iterations of the characteristics of the materials constituting the stratified soil layers. One also prints, once convergence has been reached, the variation with depth, that is layer by layer, from top to bottom, of the maximum accelerations and strains in the course of time. 3.34 Operand SEPARATEUR Makes it possible to define the separator character (blank by default) making it possible to space the columns of the results constituting the table entered by the operand UNITE_TABLE_RESU containing the result of the iterative process of DEFI_SOL_EQUI. This operand plays the same role as in the operators LIRE_TABLE or IMPR_TABLE. 3.35 Operand UNITE_RESU_TRAN Supplies the logical unit for writing, in 'TABLEAU' format, the transient evolutions of the accelerations, then of the strains and then of the shear stresses, obtained at the end of the iterative process of DEFI_SOL_EQUI. These evolutions are printed, column by column, successively: in the free field, at the outcropping bedrock, then at the bottom of each layer of stratified soil, from top to bottom. 3.36 Operand UNITE_RESU_SPEC Supplies the logical unit for writing, in 'TABLEAU' format, the frequency evolutions of the response spectra (SRO) in acceleration obtained at the end of the iterative process of DEFI_SOL_EQUI. The spectra are computed for a damping level of 5% and normalised by 9.81 m/s2. These evolutions are printed, column by column, successively: in the free field, at the outcropping bedrock, then at the bottom of each layer of stratified soil, from top to bottom. 3.37 Operand UNITE_RESU_DSP Supplies the logical unit for writing, in 'TABLEAU' format, the spectral densities (DSP) in acceleration obtained at the end of the iterative process of DEFI_SOL_EQUI. These evolutions are printed, column by column, successively: in the free field, at the outcropping bedrock, then at the bottom of each layer of stratified soil, from top to bottom. 3.38 Operand TOUT_CHAM Indicates whether or not one prints, in the file given by UNITE_RESU_ , the transient evolutions of the fields 'VITE' and 'DEPL' as well as the nodal-force fields 'FORC_NODA' at each of the levels of the column of stratified soil. This is necessary in particular for a later use by the operator DEFI_CHAR_SOL U4.84.32. Note It is strongly advised, in successive calls to DEFI_SOL_EQUI, to distinguish the logical-unit numbers of UNITE_RESU_xxx because, by using the same numbers, one risks creating shifts in the table number to be read, especially when one has used the option TOUT_CHAM='OUI'. 3.39 Operand TOUT_ACCE ◊ TOUT_ACCE = / 'OUI', [DEFAUT] / 'NON', Makes it possible to restrict the printout in the file given by UNITE_RESU_TRAN to the acceleration evolutions only, at the following points of the soil column: free field, outcropping bedrock, borehole if TOUT_ACCE='NON'. Use the keyword ACCE_LIST in order to obtain the acceleration signals at other positions in the soil column. 3.40 Operand ACCE_LIST ◊ ACCE_LIST = / alist, Together with the use of TOUT_ACCE='NON', makes it possible to supply the list of additional GROUP_MA for printout of the acceleration signals in the file UNITE_RESU_TRAN. Note 1 The signals obtained for each element defined in the list alist are positioned at the lower nodes of the mesh-cell groups of the layers of the soil column (whose name has been defined either by the operand GROUP_MA of the keyword couche, or via column M of the table supplied as input via the keyword TABLE_MATER_ELAS). Note 2 The command ignores the terms of the list which are not equal to a layer name. 3.41 Operand LIAISON ◊ LIAISON = / 'PERIODIQUE', / 'SANS', Indicates, in the case of a plane-wave loading, whether the periodicity relation between the right-hand edge and the left-hand edge of the column representative of the soil stratification is active. If the modelling is of type 1D – 3 components, one must imperatively set LIAISON ='PERIODIQUE'. 3.42 Operand LONG_CARA Indicates, in the case of a plane-wave loading, the value of the characteristic length defined in DEFI_MATERIAU, keyword ELAS, making it possible to compute the added stiffness on the absorbing boundary constituted by the right-hand and left-hand edges of the soil column. 3.43 Operand UNITE_TRAN_INIT In the case of a plane-wave loading and of a 1D – 1 component modelling, supplies the logical unit for writing, in 'TABLEAU' format, the transient evolutions at each of the levels of the column of stratified soil obtained during a previous call to DEFI_SOL_EQUI. During this previous call, the evolutions are created by means of the keyword UNITE_RESU_TRAN. 3.44 Operand MASS_PENA Indicates, in the case of a plane-wave loading and of a supply of input signals by UNITE_TRAN_INIT, the value of penalised mass assigned at each point of the edges of the soil column in order to impose the acceleration evolutions at these points. 3.45 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Allows the user to define a title for the soil table. 3.46 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1, [DEFAUT] / 2, Indicates a printout level for information in the file "MESSAGE": INFO = 1: no printout INFO = 2: printout of the soil table

u4.84.32 Command DEFI_CHAR_SOL u4.84.32 Command DEFI_CHAR_SOL 1 Purpose Produce a load usable in the dynamic solution operators DYNA_VIBRA and DYNA_NON_LINE in order to be able to take into account seismic loads on the boundaries of 2D or 3D soil domains. The loads created potentially come from two sources: either loads of “plane wave” type deduced from motions imposed on the lateral boundaries in the direction of propagation, or right-hand-side complements of “nodal force” type imposed on the lateral boundaries in the directions transverse to the propagation. The imposed-motion data or the force fields may likewise come from two sources: either a result file of transient evolutions coming from an auxiliary analysis of a 2D soil column by DEFI_SOL_EQUI, or an evolution of result type computed on an auxiliary model and projected onto the boundaries of the domain. It takes into account the concomitance of these alternative choices: - source of the transient data of motions or forces on the boundaries: either a unit of transient results obtained by DEFI_SOL_EQUI for the auxiliary analysis of a 2D soil column, behind the keyword UNITE_TRAN_UNIT, and in this case one supplies data consistent with DEFI_SOL_EQUI; or a result of transient evolutions on the boundaries of the basin computed on an auxiliary 2D or 3D model, entered behind the keyword RESU_INIT and consistent with the new syntax of CREA_RESU. In both cases, one must specify the type of load, plane wave or imposed force, by the keyword CHARGEMENT. 2 Syntax char_meca = DEFI_CHAR_SOL( ◇ CHARGEMENT = / "FORCE" (par défaut), / "ONDE_PLANE", ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ / UNITE_TRAN_INIT = unit, / RESU_INIT = evol_noli / dyna_trans / evol_char, # Si: exists("UNITE_TRAN_INIT") ◇ LONG_CARA = float, ◇ AXE = / "X", / "Y", / "Z", ◇ NOM_PARA = / "Y", / "Z" (par défaut), ◇ Z0 = float, ◇ NOM_CMP = / "DX" (par défaut), / "DY", ◆ | GROUP_MA_DROITE = grma, | GROUP_MA_GAUCHE = grma, ◆ TABLE_MATER_ELAS = table, # Si: exists("RESU_INIT") ◇ MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ COEF = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ NOM_CHAM_INIT = / "ACCE", / "FORC_NODA" (par défaut), / "REAC_NODA", ◇ DDL_EXCLUS = / "DX", / "DY", / "DZ", / "DRX", / "DRY", / "DRZ", ◇ MATR_AMOR = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◆ LIST_INST = listr8, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE = mo Makes it possible to define the name of the model to which the load will be assigned. Depending on the dimension of the problem, it must be, in 2D, a plane-strain model ('D_PLAN'), or, in 3D, a volume model with a modelling '3D'. 3.2 Operand CHARGEMENT ◊ CHARGEMENT = / 'ONDE_PLANE', / 'FORCE', Indicates the nature of the imposed loading: - CHARGEMENT = 'ONDE_PLANE': loading in the form of a vertically propagating plane wave imposed on the model and deduced from the plane-wave motion imposed on a 2D soil column or on another auxiliary model. The wave is a shear wave if one has a horizontal excitation motion, and a pressure wave if one has a vertical excitation motion. - CHARGEMENT = 'FORCE': loading in the form of opposing forces imposed on the lateral edges of the model. 3.3 Operand UNITE_TRAN_INIT Supplies the logical unit for writing, in 'TABLEAU' format, the transient evolutions at each of the levels of a 2D column of stratified soil obtained during a previous call to DEFI_SOL_EQUI. During this previous call, the evolutions are created by means of the keyword UNITE_RESU_TRAN. The loads imposed on the model are extracted in the form of force distributions depending on time and on the elevation of the stratification, from the file corresponding to this unit. 3.3.1 Operand NOM_CMP ◊ NOM_CMP = / 'DX', [DEFAUT] / 'DY', Indicates the direction of the signal imposed on the 2D soil column that was used to supply the results of the transient evolutions to be imposed as boundary conditions: - NOM_CMP = 'DX': the imposed signal is horizontal (corresponds to a vertically propagating shear wave); - NOM_CMP = 'DY': the imposed signal is vertical (corresponds to a vertical pressure wave). 3.3.2 Operand AXE ◊ AXE = / 'X', / 'Y', / 'Z', Indicates the direction of the load imposed on the model. This parameter is necessary in 3D and, by its presence, makes it possible to activate this loading case. Note: this keyword is not necessary in 2D because the direction of the load depends on the type of loading and on the direction of the signal: for NOM_CMP = 'DX', one has 'X' for CHARGEMENT = 'ONDE_PLANE' and 'Y' for CHARGEMENT = 'FORCE'. The converse holds for NOM_CMP = 'DY'. 3.3.3 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA= / 'Y', / 'Z', [DEFAUT] Makes it possible to specify, in 3D only, the direction of propagation of the plane-wave signal generating the force to be applied and corresponding to the vertical direction of the model. This operand is not necessary in most cases because it is generally deduced from the direction of the signal imposed on the soil column by NOM_CMP and from the direction of the load imposed on the model by AXE. But for NOM_CMP = 'DY', and AXE = 'X', for example, one may have a propagation parameter for a loading of type 'FORCE' equally well in the direction 'Y' as in the direction 'Z'. And for NOM_CMP = 'DX', and AXE = 'X', for a loading of type 'ONDE_PLANE', one may equally well have an SH wave in the direction 'Y' as an SV wave in the direction 'Z'. One nevertheless considers a default value ' Z' as the vertical direction for a 3D problem. 3.3.4 Operands GROUP_MA_DROITE/GROUP_MA_GAUCHE ♦ | ◊ GROUP_MA_DROITE = gmda | ◊ GROUP_MA_GAUCHE = gmga Make it possible to define respectively the names of the mesh-cell groups representative of the right-hand edge and of the left-hand edge of the model to which the load will be assigned. One must supply at least one of these operands. These mesh-cell groups are line groups in 2D and surface groups in 3D, except in the case of a loading of type 'FORCE' in 3D, where one must define line mesh-cell groups encircling the edges of the model. 3.3.5 Operand TABLE_MATER_ELAS Indicates the table which contains the information on the geometrical description of the layers of stratified soil and that of the initial characteristics of the materials constituting these layers, layer by layer. It corresponds to the table produced by the call to DEFI_SOL_EQUI which also produced the file entered by UNITE_TRAN_INIT. 3.3.6 Operand Z0 Indicates the elevation of the free surface, zero by default, of the model with which to make the zero elevation of the 2D soil-column model correspond geometrically. 3.3.7 Operand LONG_CARA Indicates, in the case of a plane-wave loading, the value of the characteristic length defined in DEFI_MATERIAU, keyword ELAS, making it possible to compute the added stiffness on the absorbing boundary constituted by the right-hand and left-hand edges of the soil column. 3.4 Operand RESU_INIT Supplies the name of the result of the transient evolution computed on an auxiliary model, from which one must extract the velocity, displacement or nodal-force fields necessary for the generation of the right-hand-side evolutions to be applied as boundary conditions on the edges of the model. 3.4.1 Operand COEF ◊ COEF = / 1,0, [DEFAUT] > / coef Gives the combination factor to be applied in the case of a loading of type 'FORCE'. It may be necessary to apply factors -1 in the case of a pressure wave P or in the case of a shear wave S on the nodal-force fields computed on the auxiliary model of the original result entered behind the keyword RESU_INIT. 3.4.2 Operands MATR_AMOR / MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_AMOR= matr_a ◊ MATR_RIGI= matr_k, In the case of a loading of type 'ONDE_PLANE', names of the assembled damping and stiffness matrices (the latter optional) that one uses in the products KU+CV constituting the right-hand-side evolution produced, from which one can create the load to be applied on the model. 3.4.3 Operands NUME_DDL / MATR_RIGI ◊ / MATR_RIGI= matr_k / NUME_DDL = nume, In the case of a loading of type 'FORCE', entries from which one can obtain the reference numbering, or conversion, of the right-hand-side evolution produced, from which one can create the load to be applied on the model. 3.4.4 Operands INST / LIST_INST / PRECISION / CRITERE ◊ INST= litps List of real values of the analysis time instants of the original result. ◊ LIST_INST= litps List of reals produced by DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01 of the analysis time instants of the evolutions produced. ◊ PRECISION = / prec [R] /1.0D-6 [DEFAUT] Precision used to search for the time instant specified in the original result. ◊ CRITERE = / 'RELATIF', / 'ABSOLU,' Criterion used to search for the time instant specified in the original result. 3.4.5 Operand NOM_CHAM_INIT ♦ NOM_CHAM_INIT= / 'ACCE', / 'FORC_NODA', / 'REAC_NODA', Name of the field of the result of the starting evolution, computed of type evol_char or dyna_trans, which one then converts into the field of the result of the right-hand-side evolution of type evol_char transformed into a load. 3.4.6 Operand DDL_EXCLUS ◊ DDL_EXCLUS = nom_cmp [TXM] Name of the component to be excluded on the field of the result of the starting evolution computed of type evol_char or dyna_trans, which one then converts into the field of the result of the right-hand-side evolution of type evol_char transformed into a load. It applies in general to a field 'FORC_NODA'. One takes the whole field if the keyword is not supplied. 3.5 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titre Allows the user to define a title for the loading. 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = Indicates a printout level for information in the file "MESSAGE": INFO = 1: no printout INFO = 2: printout of information on the loading. _

u4.84.44 Operator POST_LIQUEFACTION u4.84.44 Operator POST_LIQUEFACTION 1 Purpose This command makes it possible to compute the value of a criterion {r}_{u} evaluating the liquefaction zones in a geotechnical structure, modelled by a saturated porous medium. Four formulae are available to compute this criterion: - DP_SIGV_REF: the criterion is based on the values, at every material point, of the pore pressure at the time instant considered, of the pore pressure at the reference time instant and of the component of the effective-stress field at the reference time instant, in the direction of gravity, associated with the weight of the soil. It is accepted that when the value of the criterion exceeds 0.8, one deduces from it a risk of local liquefaction. - DP_SIGM_REF: the criterion is computed from the values, at every material point, of the pore pressure at the time instant considered, of the pore pressure at the reference time instant and of the mean effective stress at the reference time instant. - DP: it is a difference of pore pressure between a time instant t and a reference time instant. - P_SIGM: the criterion is computed from the pore pressure and the mean effective stress at the time instant t . This post-processing analysis is independent of the mechanical constitutive model of the porous medium considered. As input, one gives: - the result concept EVOL_NOLI of the simulation of the structure at the time instant considered; - the axis along which gravity is applied; - For the criteria DP_SIGV_REF/DP_SIGM_REF/DP: - a “reference” result concept EVOL_NOLI of the simulation of the structure; - the reference time instant. As output, one obtains a result concept EVOL_NOLI which contains, in a field at the Gauss points of type 'ELGA_SIEF_R', the value of the criterion, in the variable SIPXX or SIPYY or SIPZZ according to the direction of gravity in the mesh. 2 Syntax evol_noli = POST_LIQUEFACTION( ◆ AXE = / "X", / "Y", / "Z", ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli, ◆ CRITERE = / "DP_SIGV_REF", / "DP_SIGM_REF", / "DP", / "P_SIGM", # Si: equal_to('CRITERE', 'DP_SIGV_REF') ◆ RESU_REF = evol_noli, ◆ INST_REF = float, # Si: equal_to('CRITERE', 'DP_SIGM_REF') ◆ RESU_REF = evol_noli, ◆ INST_REF = float, # Si: equal_to('CRITERE', 'DP') ◆ RESU_REF = evol_noli, ◆ INST_REF = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Description The command POST_LIQUEFACTION makes it possible to compute the value of a criterion evaluating the liquefaction zones in a geotechnical structure, modelled by a saturated porous medium. Four formulae are available to compute this criterion: - DP_SIGV_REF: the criterion is based on the values, at every material point, of the pore pressure {p}_{h} at the time instant t , of the pore pressure at the reference time instant {t}_{\mathrm{réf}} , of the component of the effective-stress field {\sigma}_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}} at the reference time instant, in the direction of gravity, associated with the weight of the soil. It is accepted that when the value of the criterion exceeds 0.8, one deduces from it a risk of local liquefaction: consult for example the document DGPR, «Risque sismique et sécurité des ouvrages hydrauliques», final version of October 2014. Its expression is the following, at the time instant t and at the point x : {r}_{u}(t,\mathrm{x})=\frac{{p}_{h}(t,\mathrm{x})–{p}_{h}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})}{{\sigma}_{v}^{\mathit{eff}}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})} - DP_SIGM_REF: the criterion is computed from the values, at every material point, of the pore pressure {p}_{h} at the time instant t , of the pore pressure at the reference time instant {t}_{\mathit{réf}} and of the mean effective stress {\sigma}_{m}^{\mathit{eff}} at the reference time instant. Its expression is the following, at the time instant t and at the point x : {r}_{u}(t,\mathrm{x})=\frac{{p}_{h}(t,\mathrm{x})–{p}_{h}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})}{{\sigma}_{m}^{\mathit{eff}}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})} with the mean stress defined by {\sigma}_{m}^{\mathit{eff}}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})=\frac{({\sigma}_{xx}^{\mathit{eff}}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})+{\sigma}_{yy}^{\mathit{eff}}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x})+{\sigma}_{zz}^{\mathit{eff}}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x}))}{3} - DP: it is a difference of pore pressure {p}_{h} between a time instant t and a reference time instant {t}_{\mathit{réf}} . Its expression is the following, at the time instant t and at the point \mathrm{x} : {r}_{u}(t,\mathrm{x})={p}_{h}(t,\mathrm{x})–{p}_{h}({t}_{\mathit{réf}},\mathrm{x}) - P_SIGM: the criterion is computed from the pore pressure {p}_{h} and the mean effective stress at the time instant t . Its expression is the following, at the time instant t and at the point x : {r}_{u}(t,\mathrm{x})=\frac{{p}_{h}(t,\mathrm{x})}{{\sigma}_{m}^{\mathit{eff}}(t,\mathrm{x})} avec la contrainte moyenne définie par {\sigma}_{m}^{\mathit{eff}}(t,\mathrm{x})=\frac{({\sigma}_{xx}^{\mathit{eff}}(t,\mathrm{x})+{\sigma}_{yy}^{\mathit{eff}}(t,\mathrm{x})+{\sigma}_{zz}^{\mathit{eff}}(t,\mathrm{x}))}{3} This post-processing analysis is independent of the mechanical constitutive model of the porous medium considered. Let us make it clear that only one formula may be associated with the command. If the user wishes to compute several criteria, he or she must use the command several times. The test case zzzz403a V1.01.403 illustrates an implementation of the command on a fictitious case, and the documentation U2.04.09 presents the liquefaction analyses. 4 Keywords 4.1 Concept created by the command This command creates as output a concept of type resultat EVOL_NOLI, from which one will extract the field 'SIEF_ELGA', then the component SIPXX, or SIPYY or SIPZZ according to the direction of gravity in the mesh (see §4.4). 4.2 Keyword CRITERE > This keyword makes it possible to choose the formula for computing the criterion. ♦ CRITERE = 'DP_SIGV_REF'ou'DP_SIGM_REF'ou'DP'ou'P_SIGM' 4.3 Keywords RESU_REF and RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = resu This mandatory keyword makes it possible to supply the name of the concept of type resultat, for which the analysis of the structure has been carried out, from which one recovers the pore pressure at the time instant considered, in the form of a field 'SIEF_ELGA'. Pour les critères 'DP_SIGV_REF'/'DP_SIGM_REF'/'DP': ♦ RESU_REF = resu_ref Cet opérande obligatoire pour les critères 'DP_SIGV_REF'/'DP_SIGM_REF'/'DP'permet de renseigner le nom du concept de type resultat, pour lequel le calcul de l'ouvrage a été mené, dans lequel on récupère la pression interstitielle à l'instant de référence, sous forme d'un champ 'SIEF_ELGA'. Note: Only a result structure of type evol_noli can be supplied in these keywords. 4.4 Keyword INST_REF Pour les critères 'DP_SIGV_REF'/'DP_SIGM_REF'/'DP'. ♦ INST_REF = inst_ref This keyword is mandatory for the criteria 'DP_SIGV_REF'/'DP_SIGM_REF'/'DP'. It makes it possible to supply the reference time instant at which the value of the component of the effective-stress field {\sigma}_{v}^{\mathrm{eff}} and of the pore pressure {p}_{h} is taken. 4.5 Keyword AXE ♦ AXE = /'X' /'Y' /'Z' This mandatory keyword makes it possible to supply the direction x , y or z of the mesh along which gravity acts.

u4.84.45 Macro-command POST_NEWMARK u4.84.45 Macro-command POST_NEWMARK 1 Purpose Check the stability of a 2D embankment structure (dyke/dam) according to the criterion of maximum admissible horizontal displacement under seismic loading, via the Newmark method [1]. The procedure depends, as input, on the result concept of a linear or non-linear transient dynamic analysis, as well as on the position of the potential slip circle and on the associated seismic coefficient. The macro-command also makes it possible to estimate the static and dynamic factor of safety from a stress field coming from the application of self-weight to the structure, as well as during the dynamic transient. Depending on the options requested by the user, the macro-command supplies as output a table containing the mean horizontal acceleration of the sliding mass, the horizontal displacement, the factor of safety and the seismic coefficient. 2 Syntax table = POST_NEWMARK( ◆ / MAILLAGE_GLIS = maillage, / RAYON = float, # Si: exists("RAYON") ◆ CENTRE_X = float, ◆ CENTRE_Y = float, ◇ RAFF_CERCLE = int, # Si: exists("MAILLAGE_GLIS") ◇ GROUP_MA_GLIS = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_LIGNE = grma, ◇ POSITION = / "AMONT", / "AVAL" (par défaut), ◆ | RESULTAT = dyna_trans / evol_noli, | RESULTAT_PESANTEUR = evol_noli / evol_elas, # Si: exists("RESULTAT") ◇ VERI_MASSE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("VERI_MASSE", 'OUI') ◇ RESI_RELA = float, ◇ ITER_MAXI = int, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, # Si: exists("RESULTAT_PESANTEUR") ◆ CHAM_PHI = cham_no, ◆ CHAM_COHESION = cham_no, ◇ CHAM_FS = co, ◇ METHODE = / "ECLA_PG" (par défaut), / "COLLOCATION", ◇ KY = float, ◆ GROUP_MA_CALC = grma, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Description of the macro-command The macro-command POST_NEWMARK makes it possible to obtain an estimate of the irreversible lateral displacement of a potentially sliding zone of an embankment structure (dam/dyke) via the Newmark method bib1. The Newmark method is based on the idea that the potentially sliding zone of the structure can be approximated by a block sliding on an inclined plane. During the earthquake, this block slides along the inclined plane when the mean acceleration ( {a}_{m} ) of the block exceeds a fixed value, called the critical acceleration ( {a}_{y} ). The method considers that the residual displacement of the sliding block can be obtained by integrating twice the time instants of the mean acceleration exceeding the critical acceleration. This operation is carried out in the following manner: - obtaining the velocity signal by integration of the mean acceleration exceeding the critical acceleration, - clipping of the velocity signal at v>0 and then integration in order to obtain the displacement signal. From a dynamic analysis of finite-element type, the mean acceleration of a potentially sliding zone is defined as the quotient of the resultant of the lateral forces {F}_{L} along the interface between the potentially sliding zone and the rest of the structure and the mass m of this zone: {a}_{m}=\frac{{F}_{L}}{m} The critical acceleration is defined as the acceleration which leads to a factor of safety of value 1.0 for the potentially sliding zone. From the critical acceleration, one defines the seismic coefficient {k}_{y} by relating the critical acceleration to the value of the acceleration of gravity g : {k}_{y}=\frac{{a}_{y}}{g} The macro-command POST_NEWMARK accepts only 2D meshes and two types of slip zone: - a simple circular shape, whose position is supplied by the user. In this case, the resultant of the lateral forces is computed from the mesh cells of the mesh on which the dynamic analysis was carried out and of which a part belongs to the circle defined by the user. - a shape defined from an auxiliary mesh, which must be positioned on the geometrical locus of the mass that slides. In this case, one computes the resultant of the lateral forces on the mesh cells corresponding to the geometrical locus of the auxiliary mesh. The seismic coefficient {k}_{y} may be supplied by the user as input to the macro-command, if obtained for example from a pseudo-static stability analysis with a non-linear constitutive law incorporating a failure criterion, or by a methodology of limit-analysis type. The user may also not supply the seismic coefficient {k}_{y} . In this case, it is estimated from the evolution of the factor of safety with the mean acceleration (cf. test case sdlp200). The regression is carried out for a range lying between 0.8 and 1.2 of the value of the factor of safety, and the critical-acceleration value is retained by default conservatively because it is at −3 standard deviations from the mean of the regression. 3.1 Computation of the factor of safety in statics and in dynamics The macro-command POST_NEWMARK makes it possible to estimate the static and dynamic factor of safety of a potentially sliding zone defined from: - an auxiliary mesh defining the potentially sliding zone, or directly from the data supplied by the user on the position of the slip circle. In this latter case, the macro-command builds the auxiliary mesh directly, - a static stress field coming from gravity. For this one uses the definition of the global factor of safety {F}_{s}^{g} of Kulhawy bib2: {F}_{s}^{g}=\frac{\sum_{i}^{N}(c'+\sigma {'}_{n,s}\tan(\varphi '))\Delta L}{\sum_{i}^{N}{\sigma}_{t,s}.\Delta L} where c' and \varphi ' are the effective cohesion and the effective friction angle of the material, \sigma {'}_{n,s} is the normal stress and {\sigma}_{t} the tangential stress on the slip line, both obtained from a static gravity analysis, N the spatial discretisation of the slip line and \Delta L the length of each discretised element. For a dynamic analysis, the estimate of the factor of safety takes into account the variations of the normal and tangential stresses along the slip line, via the following formula: {F}_{s}^{g}=\frac{\sum_{i}^{N}(c'+\sigma {'}_{n,s}\tan(\varphi '))\Delta L+\sum_{i}^{N}(\sigma {'}_{n,d}\tan(\varphi '))\Delta L}{\sum_{i}^{N}{\sigma}_{t,s}.\Delta L+\sum_{i}^{N}{\sigma}_{t,d}.\Delta L} where \sigma {'}_{n,d} is the normal stress and {\sigma}_{t,d} the tangential stress on the slip line for the dynamic analysis. The user must therefore supply the static stress field coming from an application of self-weight. The macro-command carries out the estimate of the factor of safety for each time step. 3.2 Test cases sslp119 V3.02.119 Computation of the static factor of safety for a homogeneous embankment. zzzz402 V1.01.402 Dynamic response of an embankment structure under earthquake. sdlp200 V2.03.200 Comparison of the seismic resistance of a homogeneous embankment between POST_NEWMARK and GeoSlope 3.3 Bibliography Newmark, N.M. 1965. Effects of earthquakes on dams and embankments. Géotechnique, 15(2): 139-160. Kulhawy. F.H. 19,69. Finite element analysis of the behavior of embankments .PhD. Thesis, the Universiry of Califomia, at. Berkley, California. U,S.A. 4 Operands 4.1 Operands RAYON, CENTRE_X, CENTRE_Y ◊ RAYON = rayon Radius of the slip circle for which the structure must be checked ♦ CENTRE_X = posx Position along the coordinate X of the centre of the slip circle ♦ CENTRE_Y = posy Position along the coordinate Y of the centre of the slip circle Note 1: The command POST_NEWMARK handles only structures modelled according to a 2D geometry. The command stops with a fatal error if the mesh used is 3D. Note 2: The user must check the suitability of the position supplied for the slip circle and of the mesh on which the dynamic analysis was carried out. 4.2 Operand RAFF_CERCLE ◊ RAFF_CERCLE = n, [I] This operand makes it possible to choose the level of refinement of the mesh of the slip circle which will be used for the computation of the factor of safety. The refinement is controlled by the integer value n, which controls the size of the angular sector \alpha [°] of the mesh cells in the following manner: \alpha =\frac{45}{{2}^{n}} . 4.3 Operand RESULTAT ◊ RESULTAT = resultat This operand makes it possible to supply the result concept incorporating the seismic response of the structure. Note: In the case of a result of type dyna_trans, the user must beforehand compute the stress field of type SIEF_ELGA. This operation is carried out with the command CALC_CHAMP (see test case zzzz402a). 4.4 Operand KY ◊ KY = ky This operand makes it possible to supply the value of the seismic coefficient obtained for the slip circle from a static stability analysis (e.g. limit analysis) and for which the structure must be checked. If it is not supplied, the macro-command will compute it automatically and the value will be displayed in a column of the table at the output of the macro-command. 4.5 Operand POSITION ◊ POSITION = /’AVAL’, [DEFAUT] /’AMONT’ This operand makes it possible to distinguish a slip circle on the downstream face or on the upstream face. The macro-command considers by convention the upstream face to the left of the structure and the downstream face to the right. This information makes it possible to compute the factor of safety correctly, because the sign of the shear stresses along the slip circle depends on whether the circle is on the upstream face or on the downstream face. Note: The user may consult the test case sslp119 for the use of this operand. 4.6 Operand GROUP_MA_CALC ♦ GROUP_MA_CALC = grma This mandatory operand makes it possible to supply the set of mesh-cell groups on which the dynamic analysis was carried out. These mesh-cell groups are used in order to determine the mesh cells belonging to the slip circle. The use of this operand makes it possible to speed up appreciably the projection stages if the factor of safety is computed by the macro-command. 4.7 Operand MAILLAGE_GLIS ◊ MAILLAGE_GLIS = mail This operand makes it possible to supply the auxiliary mesh which will be used as a “patch” for the stability analysis. This mesh must be positioned geometrically on the zone that slides and must have SEG2 or SEG3 mesh cells for the slip line. 4.8 Operand GROUP_MA_GLIS ◊ GROUP_MA_GLIS = grma_gls This operand allows the user to supply the surface mesh-cell group grma_gls of the mesh mail on which he or she wishes to define the patch. If the keyword is not supplied, the patch is constituted of all the surface mesh cells of the mesh mail. 4.9 Operand GROUP_MA_LIGNE ◊ GROUP_MA_LIGNE = grma_lgn This operand allows the user to supply the line mesh-cell group grma_lgn of the mesh mail defining the slip line. If the keyword is not supplied, the slip line is constituted of all the line mesh cells of type SEG2 and SEG3 of the mesh mail. 4.10 Operand RESULTAT_PESANTEUR ◊ RESULTAT_PESANTEUR = resu_pes This mandatory operand makes it possible to supply the result concept incorporating the response of the structure to gravity (static stresses). Note: In the case of a result of type evol_elas, the user must beforehand compute the stress field of type SIEF_ELGA. This operation is carried out with the command CALC_CHAMP (see test case zzzz402a). 4.11 Operands CHAM_PHI and CHAM_COHESION ♦ CHAM_PHI = cham_phi ♦ CHAM_COHESION = cham_coh These operands, mandatory if RESULTAT_PESANTEUR is supplied, allow the user to supply the fields at the nodes of type NOEU_NEUT_R which define the material properties ( \varphi ' and c' ) necessary for the evaluation of the factor of safety. \varphi ' must be stored in the variable X1 and c' in the variable X2. Note 1: The user may take inspiration from the test case sslp119a in order to see the sequence of commands to be used for the definition of CHAM_PHI and CHAM_COHESION. Note 2: The value of \varphi ' must be supplied by the user in degrees [°]. The value of c' must be consistent with the modelling carried out. 4.12 Operand CHAM_FS ◊ CHAM_FS = CO(cham_fs) This operand makes it possible to produce, at the output of the macro-command, the field of the local static factor of safety. 4.13 Operand NB_ECART_TYPE ◊ NB_ECART_TYPE = nb_ecart_type, [R] In the case where the critical acceleration is estimated by the macro-command, this operand makes it possible to take into account conservatively the variance of its estimate by subtracting nb_ecart_type standard deviation from the estimator of the mean of the critical acceleration. Note: Choosing NB_ECART_TYPE=0 amounts to not taking the variance into account in the estimate of the critical acceleration. 4.14 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE = /‘ECLA_PG‘, [DEFAUT] /‘COLLOCATION‘ This operand makes it possible to choose the type of projection of the operator PROJ_CHAMP in order to obtain the stresses in the support mesh of the zone that slides, necessary for the computation of the factor of safety (in statics and in dynamics). The default method ‘ECLA_PG’ is more accurate, but nevertheless more costly for large models than the approach via the method ‘COLLOCATION’. Note: The choice of the projection method by COLLOCATION implies having beforehand computed the stress field of type SIEF_NOEU. This operation is carried out with the command CALC_CHAMP (see test case zzzz402c) 4.15 Operand VERI_MASSE ◊ VERI_MASSE = /‘NON‘, [DEFAUT] /‘OUI‘ This operand makes it possible to activate the option of checking the computation of the mass of the potentially sliding zone. For this, the macro-command carries out successive refinements via MACR_ADAP_MAIL, so as to estimate the mass of this zone better. For this, two refinement strategies are deployed: - If the option RAYON is used, one refines a circular zone with a radius 20% larger than that defining the slip circle, - If the option MAILLAGE_GLISS is used, uniform refinement of the whole mesh (which may potentially be costly). 4.16 Operands RESI_RELA and ITER_MAXI ◊ RESI_RELA = resi, [R] ◊ ITER_MAXI = iter, [I] In the case where VERI_MASSE=’OUI’, these operands make it possible to control the mesh-refinement process via two criteria: - RESI_RELA: maximum relative residual between two verification iterations. - ITER_MAXI: maximum number of iterations. One stops the process as soon as one of the two criteria is reached. 4.17 Operand CHAM_MATER ◊ CHAM_MATER = cham_mat, [cham_mater] In the case where the dynamic analysis was carried out directly from the mass, stiffness and damping matrices, this operand allows the user to supply a material field if VERI_MASSE=’OUI’. 4.18 Keyword MAILLAGE ◊ MAILLAGE = _F( Factor keyword making it possible to supply the name of the mesh objects that the user may have available at the output of the macro-command. 4.18.1 Operands MAILLAGE, NOM_GROUPE ◊ MAILLAGE = CO(mesh_out), ◊ NOM_GROUPE = grpma_out, Operand for recovering as output the mesh mesh_out, equal to the mesh given in resultat enriched with the mesh-cell group grpma_out on which the computation of the irreversible displacements was carried out. 4.18.2 Operand MAILLAGE_MASSE ◊ MAILLAGE_MASSE = CO(mesh_mass_out), Operand for recovering, at the output of the macro-command, the refined mesh used for checking the estimate of the mass (operand VERI_MASSE).

u4.84.46 Macro-command POST_ROCHE u4.84.46 Macro-command POST_ROCHE 1 Purpose and description The objective of this macro-command is to carry out post-processings of linear elastic analyses, accounting for the elastoplastic behaviour of piping lines under earthquake and permanent loadings, according to the simplified Roche method. It takes as input values of moments (components MT, MFY and MFZ) coming from previous analyses corresponding to different types of loading (inertial earthquake, self-weight, thermal expansion, imposed non-seismic displacement, seismic differential displacement DDS) on piping lines (POU_D_T elements only). These moments are supplied either in the form of fields at the nodes by element (ELNO) or else of results containing the field EFGE_ELNO. The internal pressure is taken into account directly, without a previous linear analysis (impossible with POU_D_T elements). This macro-command handles the cases in which all the loadings are independent of time (factor keyword RESU_MECA). The output concept is two fields at the nodes by element of quantity (grandeur) NEUT_R: a principal field ROC1_ELNO and a complementary field ROC2_ELNO. Two variants are proposed: RCC_MRX, based on the codification, and ASNR, in accordance with the file supplied to the ASNR in 2024. One distinguishes the loadings depending on the displacements (dynamic inertial earthquake, thermal expansion, imposed non-seismic displacement DINS, seismic differential displacement DDS) from the loadings depending on the forces (self-weight, quasi-static inertial earthquake). The 17 components Xi of the principal field ROC1_ELNO relate to the reference linear elastic stresses, to the abatement coefficients, and to the abated quantities (equivalent stress and moment). They correspond to the following characteristics, quantities directly usable in an industrial framework: | X1 | Reference elastic stress due to the displacements (DINS, DDS) and to the thermal expansion, excluding the abated-moment computation of ASNR form (B2) | | --- | --- | | X2 | Reference elastic stress due to the displacements and to the thermal expansion, for the abated-moment computation of ASNR form (B2=1) | | X3 | Reference elastic stress due to the inertial earthquake, excluding the abated-moment computation of ASNR form (B2) | | X4 | Reference elastic stress due to the inertial earthquake, for the abated-moment computation (B2=1) | | X5 | Optimised monotonic abatement coefficient, excluding the abated-moment computation of ASNR form (B2) | | X6 | Optimised monotonic abatement coefficient, for the abated-moment computation (B2=1) | | X7 | Optimised seismic abatement coefficient, excluding the abated-moment computation of ASNR form (B2) | | X8 | Optimised seismic abatement coefficient, for the abated-moment computation (B2=1) | | X9 | Optimised abated equivalent stress | | X10 | Optimised abated moment, permanent resultant: torsion component | | X11 | Optimised abated moment, permanent resultant: bending component in the plane of the elbow | | X12 | Optimised abated moment, permanent resultant: bending component out of the plane of the elbow | | X13 | Optimised abated moment, permanent resultant: norm | | X14 | Optimised abated moment, seismic resultant: torsion component | | X15 | Optimised abated moment, seismic resultant: bending component in the plane of the elbow | | X16 | Optimised abated moment, seismic resultant: bending component out of the plane of the elbow | | X17 | Optimised abated moment, seismic resultant: norm | The 28 components Xi of the complementary field ROC2_ELNO relate to intermediate quantities (local and total reversibilities, spring-effect factors, true stress and true strain) and to verification tests. They correspond to the following characteristics: | X1 | Local reversibility due to the displacements and to the thermal expansion, excluding the abated-moment computation of ASNR form (B2) | | --- |
