X23, X24 are verifications. These 4 components are equal to 0 or 1. The value 1 means that, during the analysis, one obtained a value for the true stress lower than the pressure stress. In this case, this induces an abatement coefficient equal to 1. For the variant RCC_MRX, one specifies that, in the case where SIGM_LIM=’OUI’, the components X17 to X28 are not used and are left at 0. The printout in the “result” file of the fields and results computed is carried out via the commands IMPR_RESU U4.91.01 or POST_RELEVE_T U4.81.21 (by specifying the appropriate order numbers in the case of result concepts). 2 Syntax evol_noli = POST_ROCHE( ◇ VARIANTE = / "ASNR", / "RCC_MRX" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("VARIANTE", "RCC_MRX") ◇ SIGM_LIM = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ SIGM_ABAT = / "CODE" (par défaut), / "REFE_ELAS", # Si: equal_to("SIGM_LIM", "NON") ◇ TRAC_EPSI = fonction, # Si: equal_to("VARIANTE", "ASNR") ◇ TRAC_EPSI = fonction, ◆ ZONE_ANALYSE = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ GROUP_NO_ORIG = grno, ), ◇ COUDE = _F( ◇ GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ ANGLE = float, ◆ RCOURB = float, ), ◇ MODELE = modele, ◇ CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◇ INST_TEMP = float (défaut: 0.0), ◆ RESU_MECA = _F( ◆ TYPE_CHAR = / "DDS", / "DILAT_THERM", / "DINS", / "POIDS", / "SISM_INER_SPEC", # Si: equal_to("TYPE_CHAR", 'SISM_INER_SPEC') ◆ RESULTAT = mode_meca / mult_elas, ◇ DIRECTION = / "COMBI" (par défaut), / "X", / "Y", / "Z", ◆ TYPE_RESU = / "DYN", / "QS", # Si: not equal_to("TYPE_CHAR", 'SISM_INER_SPEC') ◆ / CHAM_GD = cham_elem, / RESULTAT = evol_elas, ◆ / NUME_ORDRE = int, / INST = float, # Si: exists("INST") ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ), ◇ PRESSION = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = list[grma], ◆ VALE = float, ), ◇ TOUT_CHAM = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), # Si: not exists("TOUT_CHAM") ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "ROC1_ELNO" (par défaut), / "ROC2_ELNO", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand VARIANTE Makes it possible to define the variant of the Roche method: 'RCC_MRX' is for the most part in accordance with the RCC-MRx codification; 'ASNR' denotes the variant relating to the file accepted by the ASNR in 2024. ◊ VARIANTE = / ‘RCC_MRX’ [DEFAUT] / ‘ASNR’ 3.2 Operand SIGM_LIM ◊ SIGM_LIM = / ‘OUI’ [DEFAUT] / ‘NON’ Operand to be supplied only if FORME= 'RCC_MRX'. Makes it possible to define the method of computation of the true stress and of the true strain. If this parameter is equal to ‘OUI’ (by default), the true stress is computed from an allowable stress level, itself computed from the material data of the material POST_ROCHE (See R7.10.04), in accordance with the RCC-MRx codification. If this parameter is equal to ‘NON’, the true stress is obtained by solution of a system of non-linear equations, representing the projection of the reference linear elastic stress onto the tension curve of the material. If VARIANTE= 'ASNR', the method of computation of the true stress corresponds to the case SIGM_LIM = 'NON'. 3.2.1 Operand SIGM_ABAT Operand to be supplied only if VARIANTE= 'RCC_MRX'. The keyword makes it possible to indicate which formulation is chosen for the computation of the optimised abated stress. ◊ SIGM_ABAT = / ’CODE’ [DEFAUT] / ‘REFE_ELAS ‘ The value 'CODE' refers to the formulation of the RCC-MRx. The value 'REFE_ELAS' relates to a formulation based on the formulation of the reference elastic stress, and taking the pressure stress into account in addition. It is in fact the formulation of the variant 'ASNR'. 3.3 Operand TRAC_EPSI ♦ TRAC_EPSI = traction, [fonction] Makes it possible to define the tension curve of the material (strain as a function of the stress) onto which the reference linear elastic stress is projected. 3.4 Operand INST_TEMP ◊ INST_TEMP = inst In order to define the various material parameters necessary for the operator, the user may use the keyword POST_ROCHE_FO of DEFI_MATERIAU instead of POST_ROCHE if he or she wishes these parameters to be functions depending on a temperature field. This temperature field is then to be supplied in AFFE_MATERIAU/AFFE_VARC. To do this, the user is strongly encouraged to use the keyword CHAM_GD to declare the temperature field, rather than the keyword EVOL to which a result is to be supplied. However, it may happen that the user is constrained to use EVOL because other previous analyses impose it. In this case, the operand INST_TEMP makes it possible to indicate which time instant of the result data structure supplied is to be taken into account for the computation of the material parameters. 3.5 Factor keyword ZONE_ANALYSE ♦ ZONE_ANALYSE=_F( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', [DEFAUT] / GROUP_MA = gma1, [groupma] ♦ GROUP_NO_ORIG = gno1, [groupno] This keyword makes it possible to define the different zones (or runs) to be analysed. Each zone must be a contiguous line. For example, for the analysis of a “T”, one must define at least two zones (the “branch” and the “run”). 3.5.1 Keywords TOUT and GROUP_MA Declaration of the mesh cells of the zone. Only the modelling POU_D_T is accepted on the mesh cells declared. 3.5.2 Keyword GROUP_NO_ORIG Definition of a node placed at one of the ends of the run. 3.6 Factor keyword COUDE ◊ COUDE=_F( ♦ GROUP_MA = gma1, [groupma] ♦ ANGLE = ang, [R] ♦ RCOURB = rc, [R] This keyword makes it possible to locate the elbows in the piping and to assign certain parameters to these mesh cells. On the parts declared as an elbow, it is necessary to define in the properties of the material POST_ROCHE the optional parameter RP02_MIN. Furthermore, in order to comply with the codification, the user must define in AFFE_CARA_ELEM/ORIENTATION the local reference frame in the bent parts so as to take the bending moments correctly into account (in the plane of the elbow and out of plane). An example is given in the test case sdll157a. 3.6.1 Keywords GROUP_MA Declaration of the mesh cells belonging to an elbow 3.6.2 Keywords ANGLE, RCOURB ♦ ANGLE Defines the angle, in degrees, of the elbow to which the mesh cells belong. ♦ RCOURB Defines the radius of curvature of the elbow to which the mesh cells belong. 3.7 Operands MODELE, CARA_ELEM and CHAM_MATER ◊ MODELE = modele Makes it possible to define the model in the case where it cannot be recovered directly from the field by element or from the result supplied in the first occurrence of RESU_MECA. ◊ CARA_ELEM = cara Makes it possible to define the elementary beam characteristics in the case where they cannot be recovered directly because only fields by element have been supplied in the occurrences of RESU_MECA. ◊ CHAM_MATER = chmat Makes it possible to define the material field in the case where it cannot be recovered directly because only fields by element have been supplied in the occurrences of RESU_MECA. 3.8 Factor keyword PRESSION ◊ PRESSION=_F( ♦ / TOUT = 'OUI', [DEFAUT] / GROUP_MA = gma1, [groupma] ♦ VALE = press, [R] This keyword makes it possible to define the values of the internal pressure of the piping. 3.8.1 Keywords GROUP_MA Definition of the mesh cells to which a pressure value is to be assigned. 3.8.2 Keyword VALE ♦ VALE Defines the value of the pressure. 3.9 Factor keyword RESU_MECA ♦ RESU_MECA This keyword makes it possible to define the different loadings to be taken into account for the analysis by the Roche method. The loadings do not depend on time; the output concept is a field at the nodes by element (ELNO). 3.9.1 Operand TYPE_CHAR This operand makes it possible to indicate the type of loading declared so that it is processed correctly during the classification. ♦ TYPE_CHAR = ‘SISM_INER_SPEC’, ‘DDS’, ‘DINS’, ‘DILAT_THERM’, ‘POIDS’ There may be several occurrences with the same type of loading for the types 'DDS', ‘DINS’, ‘DILAT_THERM’ and ‘POIDS’. The value ‘SISM_INER_SPEC’ makes it possible to declare a spectral modal inertial seismic response. The value ‘DDS’ makes it possible to declare a loading of seismic differential displacements of the anchors. The value ‘DINS’ makes it possible to declare a loading of imposed non-seismic displacements. The value ‘DILAT_THERM’ makes it possible to declare a loading due to thermal expansion. The value ‘POIDS’ makes it possible to declare a self-weight loading. 3.9.2 Operands RESULTAT, DIRECTION and TYPE_RESU For TYPE_CHAR = ‘SISM_INER_SPEC’, the loading is defined by the following keywords: ♦ RESULTAT = resu , [mode_meca / mult_elas] The results supplied here must come from the command COMB_SISM_MODAL and possess the field EFGE_ELNO. ◊ DIRECTION = ‘COMBI’, [DEFAUT] ‘X’, ‘Y’, ‘Z’, This keyword makes it possible to indicate the excitation to be taken into account among the three directions of space and their combination. ◊ TYPE_RESU = ‘DYN’, ‘QS’, In the case of an inertial seismic loading TYPE_CHAR = ‘SISM_INER_SPEC’, this keyword makes it possible to indicate whether the inertial seismic response is dynamic or quasi-static. There must be exactly two occurrences, one with TYPE_RESU equal to ‘DYN’, the other with TYPE_RESU equal to ‘QS’. The processing of two distinct previous spectral modal analyses relates to the so-called historical Roche method: the quasi-static part (‘QS’) is therein the result of a spectral modal inertial analysis at a damping ratio of 100%; the dynamic part ('DYN') is then defined as the difference between the spectral modal response at the desired damping ratio and this quasi-static part ('QS') thus determined. The computation of the part 'DYN' is described in the test case SDLL157a. 3.9.3 Operands RESULTAT and CHAM_GD One may supply a result coming from the command MECA_STATIQUE, from which one will extract the field EFGE_ELNO (computed beforehand) at the analysis time instant indicated, or directly a field at the nodes by element EFGE_ELNO containing the components MT, MFY and MFZ. ♦ / RESULTAT = resu , [evol_elas] / CHAM_GD = cham , [cham_elem] 3.9.4 Operands NUME_ORDRE, INST, CRITERE and PRECISION These keywords serve to indicate the analysis time instants to be taken into account when one uses the keyword RESULTAT for all the types of loading except SISM_INER_SPEC, for which one uses DIRECTION and TYPE_RESU. ♦ / NUME_ORDRE = ordre, [I] / INST = inst, [R] # Si INST : ◊ CRITERE = 'RELATIF', [DEFAUT] 'ABSOLU' , ◊ PRECISION = prec, [R] 1.E-6, [DEFAUT] The keywords CRITERE and PRECISION are used to parameterise the search for the analysis time instants in the data structure from the time instant supplied to INST. 3.9.5 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM These keywords make it possible to indicate the type of output field (principal ROC1_ELNO and complementary ROC2_ELNO). u4.84.47 Macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE u4.84.47 Macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE 1 Purpose Check the static stability of embankment structures modelled in 2D, such as embankment dams, slopes and the dykes around reservoirs, etc . The macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE makes it possible to compute the factor of safety representing the available stability margin, defined by the ratio between the shear resistance force and the driving force induced by the loadings applied. CALC_STAB_PENTE groups two categories of methods, thus making it possible to equip oneself with the means of verification, and to adapt to the practices of the hydraulic industry in the different regions of the world. - The first type of analysis ( METHODE_STAB = "SRM" ) is carried out by progressive reduction of the shear-strength parameters (“ strength reduction method ” in English, called SRM) until divergence of the finite-element analysis. This divergence reflects the instant of failure of the global structure. By the definition of an SRM zone , it is possible to indicate directly the slope to be analysed, if several exist in the model. - The second type of analysis ( METHODE_STAB = "LEM" ) is based on the limit-equilibrium theory (LEM). One computes the factor of safety by solution of the balance of the forces and of the moments of the soil slices considered as rigid solids. Under seismic conditions, it is also possible to solve for the critical-acceleration coefficient instead of the FS by activating ACCE/CALC_KC . The result is therefore useful in the macro-command POST_NEWMARK (U4.84.45) in order to evaluate the irreversible displacement caused by the earthquake. The macro has optimisation algorithms in order to locate the failure surface. 4 LEM methods are available: - "FELLENIUS" and "BISHOP" simplified for the circular failure surfaces. - "SPENCER" and "MORGENSTERN-PRICE" for the non-circular failure surfaces. The macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE supplies as output a table containing the factors of safety (FS) tested and the information about the geometry of the failure surface. choix possibles 3 Description of the macro-command According to the recommendations, the justification of the stability of embankment dams and dykes, the verification of the stability of the slopes are indispensable both at the design stage and during operation of this kind of structure. This analysis has the objective of preventing the sudden failure of the slope by evaluating quantitatively the risk of failure, i.e. the factor of safety. The stability of the slopes depends at once on the geometry, on the mechanical properties of the embankment, and on the mechanical and hydraulic loadings such as gravity, the hydrostatic pressure and the pore pressure generated by the infiltration of water within the structure. The macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE makes it possible to compute the factor of safety via two approaches: 1. SRM method : the method of progressive reduction of the parameters linked to the shear strength of the material (named the SRM method). This method was proposed by Griffiths [1] in 1999. The SRM method implemented has been validated only on slopes modelled in 2D. Use on 3D models is also possible but the relevance of the result must be checked by the user. 2. LEM method : a series of methods based on the limit-equilibrium theory (named the LEM method), including the simplified Bishop, Fellenius, Spencer and Morgenstern-Price procedures [2]. These methods cut the slope into several slices considered as rigid bodies. Given a potential failure surface, the computation of the factor of safety is done by solution of the balance of the forces and of the moments of the set of slices. The factor of safety is defined by the ratio between the resistance force and the driving force along the failure surface. CALC_STAB_PENTE is also equipped with optimisation algorithms in order to locate the failure surfaces minimising the factor of safety. The SRM method takes advantage of the relevance and of the fidelity of the finite-element method in order to analyse the stability of the slopes without needing to assume in advance the slip circles. Indeed, by using the failure criterion of Mohr-Coulomb type, the SRM method defines the factor of safety as being the ratio between the initial material parameters and those reduced leading to the divergence of the non-linear analysis under the loadings applied: \mathit{FS}=\dfrac{c}{{c}_{i}}=\dfrac{\tan(\varphi )}{\tan({\varphi}_{i})}=\dfrac{\tan(\psi )}{\tan({\psi}_{i})} where - \psi is the dilatancy angle of the material, - c and \varphi represent respectively the cohesion force and the friction angle of the embankment. CALC_STAB_PENTE makes it possible to define the SRM zone by an independent mesh-cell group. The advantages of the SRM method are the following: - Possibility of applying various types of mechanical loading, such as the hydrostatic pressure and the inertia force under seismic conditions (pseudo-static). - Computation of a stress field faithful to reality without the necessity of presupposing the failure surfaces, which leads to an FS result more relevant than that of the LEM method. - Natural visualisation of the failure surface characterised by the high plastic strain. If the user is not sufficiently experienced, the SRM method will generally take more analysis time and the relevance of the result is not guaranteed because of a poorly configured FEM analysis. Unlike the SRM method, the LEM method is, for its part, independent of the FEM analysis. Nevertheless, the LEM method requires one to presuppose the potential failure surfaces and makes an assumption on the interaction forces between the slices. Given the simplicity and the efficiency of the analysis, the LEM method has become the most popular in the hydraulic industry and is recommended by the regulations for the design and verification of embankment structures. At the output of the macro-command one recovers a table to the left of the equals sign, whose contents depend on the analysis method chosen: - In the case of SRM : the table contains the factors of safety tested during the iterations, as well as the values of the maximum total displacement in the SRM zone. This table facilitates both the recovery of the stability result and the verification of its relevance. Indeed, the factor of safety is found in the last line of the table. The convergence of the algorithm is checked by a progressively “flattened” plot of the factor of safety as a function of the maximum displacement. - In the case of LEM : the table contains the factors of safety of the critical surface in the course of the mesh refinement, as well as the geometrical parameters of the failure surface. With the detailed output mode activated ( INFO_TABLE=2 ), the table also contains the statistics of the potential surfaces visited, which make it possible to justify the result and to check the convergence of the optimisation algorithm. - For the Bishop and Fellenius procedures, the failure surface is described by the abscissae of the entry and exit points, the radius and the coordinates of the centre of the circle. - For the Spencer and Morgenstern-Price procedures, the failure surface is described by the abscissae of the entry and exit points, and the ordinates of the intermediate points describing the multi-linear surface. The macro-command supplies the option of visualising the slip surface. If requested, a concept of type evol_noli will be produced for this purpose. 4 Operands 4.1 Operands CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER= cham_mater Name of the material field assigned on the model mo. One must make sure that the chmat has been created using the same mesh as that of the model modele . Otherwise, a fatal error will occur. 4.2 Operand METHODE_STAB = 'SRM' ♦ METHODE_STAB= 'SRM' By choosing the SRM method, the slope-stability analysis is based on the non-linear solver STAT_NON_LINE with a view to seeking iteratively the factor of safety until the analysis diverges. Consequently, the inputs of this latter command are also required by the macro-command. 4.2.1 Operand MODELE ♦ MODELE= modele Name of the model whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis. With the THM model (see R7.01.11), the macro-command takes into account the hydraulic effect during the stability analysis, which favours above all the evaluation of the stability of dams and dykes. On the other hand, the models requiring the definition of elementary characteristics via the command AFFE_CARA_ELEM are not authorised by the macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE. 4.2.2 Operand GROUP_MA/TOUT ♦ /GROUP_MA = grma /TOUT = 'OUI' List of the mesh-cell groups defining the zone where the SRM algorithm applies. If one analyses the stability of the whole model, one sets the operand TOUT = 'OUI'. In the case where the mesh-cell groups differ from those which are used in the assignment of the material to the mesh, the macro-command will identify the materials affecting the SRM zone on the basis of the material field chmat as input, and computes the mesh-cell groups of intersection between the SRM zone and the zone of assignment of the material in question with a view to assigning the degraded material in the SRM zone by the overloading principle. 4.2.3 Keyword EXCIT ♦ EXCIT = _F() Factor keyword making it possible to describe at each occurrence a load (excitation and boundary condition), and possibly a multiplying coefficient and/or a type of load. The configuration of this factor keyword is identical to that of the command STAT_NON_LINE (see u4.51.03), except that the types of load are limited to 'FIXE_CSTE', 'SUIV' and 'DIDI' . The types of load linked to the PILOTAGE functionality have been eliminated in the macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE since they are in contradiction with the SRM algorithm. 4.2.4 Keywords INCREMENT, CONVERGENCE and COMPORTEMENT ♦ INCREMENT= _F() Factor keyword defining the time intervals taken in the incremental method (see STAT_NON_LINE u4.51.03) ♦ CONVERGENCE= _F() Factor keyword making it possible to control the convergence criteria during the non-linear analysis carried out by the command STAT_NON_LINE (u4.51.03). ♦ COMPORTEMENT= _F() Factor keyword defining the constitutive relations. It is a keyword common to several commands. Its syntaxes are described in the document U4.51.11. 1. The use of the option of automatic cutting of the time steps defined by the command DEFI_LIST_INST with the operand ECHEC/ACTION = 'DECOUPE' (in the factor keyword INCREMENT ) is strongly recommended. Indeed, the splitting of the increment over several levels makes it possible to avoid the stopping of CALC_STAB_PENTE because of the divergence of the Newtonian algorithm before the formation of a through-going plastified surface marking the true failure of the slope. Likewise, increasing ITER_GLOG_MAXI in the keyword CONVERGENCE also favours the capture of the exact instant of collapse of the slope. 2. In the factor keyword COMPORTEMENT it is possible to define different constitutive relations on the different parts of the model. However, similarly to the processing of the material field in the SRM zone, the program checks that there exists one and only one constitutive behaviour among MOHR_COULOMB and DRUCKER_PRAGER in the SRM zone. Otherwise, a fatal error will be produced. Furthermore, the definition of constitutive relations on the mesh cells is not authorised by the macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE. 4.2.5 Keyword FS ◊ FS= _F() Factor keyword defining the parameters of the SRM algorithm, including the initial value of the factor of safety, the initial increment and the refinement method. 4.2.5.1 Operand FS_INIT ◊ FS_INIT = f0 This operand makes it possible to supply the initial value of the factor of safety. 1. It is the reduction coefficient of the shear-strength properties for the first SRM iteration. Therefore, the closer this initial value is to the real factor of safety, the shorter the analysis will last. This value is often obtained by an empirical method or by previous tests, but can never exceed the real value, otherwise the analysis will diverge at the first SRM iteration and a fatal error will be produced. f0 must be strictly positive and the default value is 1.0. 2. In the case of the fatal error informing that f0 is too small, one must not intuitively increase it and relaunch the SRM analysis. It is preferable first to examine the configuration of the non-linear analysis, since it is probable that the divergence of the analysis at the first SRM iteration is due to a poor configuration of the solver STAT_NON_LINE. 4.2.5.2 Operand INCR_INIT ◊ INCR_INIT= p0 This operand makes it possible to define the initial increment of the factor of safety. 4.2.5.3 Operand RESI_MAXI ◊ RESI_MAXI= pfin This operand makes it possible to define the maximum residual of the factor of safety. The factor of safety finally obtained is within pfin of its real value. This operand therefore defines the precision of the stability analysis. Its default value is fixed at 0.01 according to the practice of the hydraulic profession. The large gap between p0 and pfin will lead to a long analysis duration if one does not impose the number of refinements via the keyword ITER_RAFF_LINE. 4.2.5.4 Operand ITER_MAXI ◊ ITER_MAXI = iter_max This operand defines the maximum number of SRM iterations. It serves to avoid an inefficient analysis because of the inappropriate configuration of the keyword FS. The analysis stops with the fatal error if iter_max is reached without the algorithm having converged. 4.2.5.5 Operand METHODE ◊ METHODE= /'EXPONENTIELLE' /'LINEAIRE' This operand defines the law of variation of the increment of the factor of safety. Two options are available: 1. 'EXPONENTIELLE' : Exponential variation The increment of the factor of safety approaches the maximum residual in an exponential manner. At the nth refinement, the increment is computed by: {p}_{n}={p}_{0}{2}^{-n} until {p}_{N}<{p}_{\mathit{fin}} . 2. 'LINEAIRE' : Linear variation The increment of the factor of safety approaches the maximum residual in a linear manner. In that case an additional operand ITER_RAFF_LINE is necessary. At the nth refinement, the increment is computed by: {p}_{n}={p}_{0}-n\dfrac{{p}_{0}-{p}_{\mathit{fin}}}{N} until {p}_{N}={p}_{\mathit{fin}} . The advantage of the exponential method is that the analysis converges more rapidly, whereas the linear method controls the precision of the result better. The exponential variation of the increment is suited above all to the analysis with a large INCR_INIT. The following method would simplify the choice between the two laws of variation of the increment. Let N be the number of refinements desired; one chooses the linear law if: \dfrac{{p}_{0}-{p}_{\mathit{fin}}}{{\log}_{2}({p}_{0})-{\log}_{2}({p}_{\mathit{fin}})}<N and one chooses the exponential law otherwise. 4.2.5.6 Operand ITER_RAFF_LINE ◊ ITER_RAFF_LINE= nbpas This operand makes it possible to define the number of refinements of the increment if the linear law of variation is selected. 4.3 Operand METHODE_STAB = 'LEM' ♦ METHODE_STAB= 'LEM' By choosing the LEM method, the computation of the factor of safety no longer relies on the finite-element method; nevertheless it still relies on the mesh with a view to dividing the slope into slices and to computing the mass of the slices via the operator POST_ELEM. 4.3.1 Operand CRITERE ◊ CRITERE = /'MOHR_COULOMB' /'DRUCK_PRAGER' This operand makes it possible to indicate the failure criterion to be used in order to compute the tangential resistance force. In all cases one converts the parameters of the Mohr-Coulomb or Drucker-Prager criterion into the friction angle and the cohesion in order to inject them into the formulations of the computation of the factor of safety according to the procedure METHODE_LEM selected. 4.3.2 Operand GROUP_MA ♦ GROUP_MA= profil_pente This operand defines the group of line mesh cells representing the profile of the slope. It is mandatory to indicate it in order to: - Estimate the ordinates of the entry and exit points. - Check the potential failure surface so that it lies within the model but never too close to the profile of the slope. - Estimate the slope rate at the ends of the failure surface in order to determine the direction of the interaction force between the slices. The way in which the profile of the slope intervenes in the various algorithms is explained in more detail in R7.05.02. The user must make sure that the profile of the slope supplied includes the search bands of the entry and exit points, and that it satisfies the needs mentioned above. It is advised to choose a profile of the slope which contains the entire slope as well as a part of the flattened surfaces upstream and downstream. An example of the profile of the slope is shown in fig1-geom-lem. Illustration of the LEM geometrical parameters 4.3.3 Operand NB_TRANCHE ◊ NB_TRANCHE = / 10 / Nt This operand defines the number of slices dividing the slope. One must note that the LEM analysis will be all the slower as one increases the number of slices. However, one must increase the number of slices if one analyses the stability of stratified structures whose failure surface is probably non-circular. 4.3.4 Operands X1_MINI, X1_MAXI, X2_MINI and X2_MAXI ♦ X1_MINI = x1_min ♦ X1_MAXI = x1_max ♦ X2_MINI = x2_min ♦ X2_MAXI = x2_max These operands define the search bands of the abscissae of the entry and exit points of the potential failure surface. By convention, x1_min and x2_min must be less than x1_max and x2_max respectively. An example of the definition of X1 and X2 is shown in fig1-geom-lem. 4.3.5 Keyword RAFF_MAIL RAFF_MAIL = _F( ◊ NB_RAFF_MAXI = / 4 / N_raff ◊ RAFF_CRIT_STAB = / 1e-3 / raff_crit_stab ) Factor keyword defining the parameters linked to the algorithm of refinement of the mesh on the contour of the slices. The refinement via the macro-command MACR_ADAP_MAIL is driven by the proximity field measuring the distance between the nodes and the contour of the slices. The complete procedure is illustrated in R7.05.02. The operand NB_RAFF_MAXI defines the maximum number of refinements. This operand makes it possible to limit the number of refinements in order to be able to consult the FS result more rapidly, at the expense of the precision of the analysis, if the FS convergence criterion is not satisfied. The operand RAFF_CRIT_STAB defines the criterion of stabilisation of the factor of safety in the course of the mesh refinement. The algorithm stops if the absolute value of the variation of FS is less than raff_crit_stab. 4.3.6 Keyword CHAM_PRES ◇ CHAM_PRES = _F( ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli, ◆ / INST = float, / NUME_ORDRE = int, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ ALGO_PRES = / "INVERSE", / "PROJECTION" (par défaut), ), Factor keyword making it possible to couple the hydraulic pressure field coming from the THM model with the stability analysis. The field DEPL in the evol_noli result entered in the operand RESULTAT must comprise the component PRE1 and possibly PRE2 for the unsaturated models. In the absence of PRE2, the air pressure is assumed zero. The pressure field corresponding to the time instant indicated by the operand INST or NUME_ORDRE will intervene in the evaluation of the shear strength along the failure surface. Two interpolation methods are available in the operand ALGO_PRES : - INVERSE : Inverse-distance-weighted interpolation (IDW). The power value is fixed at 2. It is a simple and efficient method. However, the weighting of the distant nodes decreasing rapidly as a function of the distance, only the nodes in the immediate neighbourhood influence the interpolation result. This method is therefore suited rather to a fine mesh. - PROJECTION : The interpolation is done by PROJ_CHAMP U4.72.05 by means of the shape functions of the finite elements. This method is more reassuring than the IDW. 4.3.7 Keyword LIGN_PHREA ◇ LIGN_PHREA = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ INDIC_PIEZO = (int, ), ◆ TABLE = table, ◇ PRES_MAX = float, ), Factor keyword defining the phreatic lines for the whole model or by zone in the form of an aster_table entered in the operand TABLE . The operand INDIC_PIEZO makes it possible to indicate the two indices of the columns in the table which will define respectively the abscissa and the pressure head. One determines the capillary pressure at the point with the coordinates (x, y) such that: P_c(x, y) = \rho_W g \left[y - y_w(x)\right]cos^2A(x) where A(x) is the local angle of inclination of the phreatic line with respect to the horizontal. The air pressure is assumed zero. One observes that the capillary pressure is positive above the phreatic line and proportional to y . This will become problematic if one computes the strength due to the matric suction by the simple parameter PHI_B , because this additional strength term will tend towards infinity, which is inconsistent with reality. Therefore the operand PRES_MAX makes it possible to limit the positive capillary pressure in order to avoid obtaining an unrealistic result. 4.3.8 Keyword COEF_RU ◇ COEF_RU = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ VALE = float, ), Factor keyword defining by zone the pore-pressure coefficient. This parameter R_u is defined by the ratio between the pore-water pressure and the overburden stress applied on the base of the slices: R_u = \frac{u}{\rho_s g H_s} This simplest approach for considering the hydraulic effect was proposed for the first time by Bishop and Morgenstern in 1960 [3]. However, this ratio R_u may vary in the slope if the real phreatic line is not parallel to the surface of the slope. One must therefore use it with caution. It is advised to measure R_u at several points in the structure and to compute the mean value in order to avoid an erroneous result. 4.3.9 Operand SUCCION ◇ SUCCION = "OUI" The operand SUCCION makes it possible to take into account the shear strength due to the matric suction in the unsaturated soil above the phreatic line, with the aim of obtaining a less conservative stability result. There exist two options for computing the strength with matric suction: Option 1 One defines a constant angle \varphi_b expressing the increase of the strength as a function of the suction. One determines the strength such that: S = c' + (\sigma_n - p_a)\tan\varphi' + p_c \tan\varphi_b Option 2 One computes the strength according to the hydraulic constitutive behaviour supplied by the user in DEFI_MATERIAU/THM_DIFFU . As proposed by Vanapalli et al[4], the strength is expressed by: S = c' + (\sigma_n - p_a)\tan\varphi' + p_c \left(\frac{\theta_w - \theta_r}{\theta_s - \theta_r}\right) \tan\varphi' where \theta_w , \theta_s , \theta_r represent respectively the water saturation, the saturation in the saturated state and the residual saturation. According to the properties supplied in the cham_mater as input, one determines the effective saturation, which is expressed by: S_{we} = \frac{\theta_w - \theta_r}{\theta_s - \theta_r} either by the parameters of the Van-Genuchten model, or by the function \theta_{w}(p_c) defined via the operand SATU_PRES in DEFI_MATERIAU/THM_DIFFU . In the second case, \theta_s and \theta_r take the value of the first and of the last element in the list defining the function. 4.3.10 Keyword PHI_B ◇ PHI_B = _F( ◆ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ VALE = float, ), Factor keyword defining the value of the matric-suction angle \varphi_b by zone, on condition of having activated SUCCION . 4.3.11 Operand INFO_TABLE ◇ INFO_TABLE = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, By default one supplies as output the simplified result containing only the factors of safety / critical-acceleration coefficient at each iteration of the mesh refinement, as well as the geometrical parameters of the critical surface. By setting INFO_TABLE=2 , one adds furthermore in the output table the statistics of these parameters and the intermediate results of the optimisation algorithm. The detailed explanation of each column in the output table is found in table-1 and table-2. - For the Bishop and Fellenius methods (circular surface) | Result | Meaning | | --- | --- | | NUME_RAFF | Iteration number of the mesh refinement. | | FS/KC | Factor of safety or critical-acceleration coefficient. | | X_ENTRE | Abscissa of the left-hand end of the failure surface. | | Y_ENTRE | Ordinate of the left-hand end of the failure surface. | | X_SORTIE | Abscissa of the right-hand end of the failure surface. | | Y_SORTIE | Ordinate of the right-hand end of the failure surface. | | CENTRE_X | Abscissa of the centre of the failure surface. | | CENTRE_Y | Ordinate of the centre of the failure surface. | | RAYON | Radius of the failure surface. | | NB_SURF_TEST | Number of potential surfaces tested. | | EXT_CENTRE_X | Extremum X of the centres. | | EXT_CENTRE_Y | Extremum Y of the centres. | | EXT_RAYON | Extremum of the radii. | | HIST_RAYON | History of the radii in increasing order. | | HIST_CENTRE_X | History of the abscissa of the centres. | | HIST_CENTRE_Y | History of the ordinate of the centres. | | HIST_FS/KC | History of the FS/KC. | Additional results when INFO_TABLE=2 . - For the Morgenstern-Price and Spencer methods (non-circular surface) | Result | Meaning | | --- | --- | | NUME_RAFF | Iteration number of the mesh refinement. | | FS/KC | Factor of safety or critical-acceleration coefficient. | | NUME_POINT | Number of points on the failure surface (= number of slices + 1). | | COOR_X | Abscissa of the points defining the critical surface. | | COOR_Y | Ordinate of the points defining the critical surface. | | MIN_X | Minima in X. | | MAX_X | Maxima in X. | | MIN_Y | Minima in Y. | | MAX_Y | Maxima in Y. | | NUME_ITER | EFWA iteration number. | | HIST_FS/KC | History of the FS/KC minima during the EFWA iterations. | Additional results when INFO_TABLE=2 . Owing to the limitations of the optimisation algorithm and to an incorrect search zone, the result of the stability analysis by LEM may be erroneous without a software error. However, the output table makes it possible to check and to justify the result manually. More precisely, it is advised to examine the following points: 1. Convergence of FS/KC : Plot FS/KC against NUME_RAFF in order to check whether the number of refinements is sufficient. In the case of non-convergence because NUME_RAFF_MAXI has been reached, increase the maximum number of refinements or adjust the input mesh. 2. Convergence of the optimisation algorithm : With INFO_TABLE = 2 , one easily justifies the configuration of the optimisation algorithm. For the Bishop and Fellenius methods, one checks that the minimum of HIST_FS/KC lies right in the middle of the band of radii tested for each combination of the entry and exit points. For the Morgenstern and Spencer methods, one plots HIST_FS/KC as a function of NUME_ITER so as to check the convergence graphically. In the case of non-convergence, one examines the extrema of the geometrical parameters of the potential surfaces visited and then corrects the configuration of the optimisation algorithm. 4.3.12 Operands PHI_C_EQUI and TOLE_DIST ◇ PHI_C_EQUI = "OUI", ◇ TOLE_DIST = float, The operand PHI_C_EQUI makes it possible to activate the computation of the equivalent cohesion and friction angle on the base of the slices which cross several materials: c_{eq} = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N_c}c_kl_k}{L}, \quad \tan\varphi_{eq} = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N_c}\tan\varphi_kl_k}{L} where N_c is the number of materials on the base of the slices, l_k is the base length in material k, L is the total length of the base. The operand TOLE_DIST defines the distance tolerance for distinguishing two different materials. If this value is sufficiently high, PHI_C_EQUI will become ineffective. In the contrary case, one manages to identify the soil layers of very small thickness, at the expense of the analysis time. By default, this parameter is adaptive and equal to 5% of the base length. 4.3.13 Operand FONC_PRES ◇ FONC_PRES = fonction / formule The operand FONC_PRES makes it possible to apply a distributed pressure on the surface of the slope defined in the operand GROUP_MA in the form of a pressure function or formula with the coordinates X and Y as variables. One evaluates the nodal force at the nodes of the 1D elements constituting the slope profile. One thus computes the force and the moment applied on the soil slices by trapezoidal integration. 4.3.14 Keyword ACCE ◇ ACCE = _F( ◆ / CALC_KC = "OUI" , / COEF_ACCE = float, ◇ DIRECTION = float, ), Factor keyword defining the inertia force caused by the earthquake. By the principle of pseudo-static analysis, one models the seismic effect by the inertia force computed from the acceleration coefficient k_a defined via COEF_ACCE and the direction vector \overrightarrow{r} defined via DIRECTION such that: F_{i} = \rho_s g k_a \frac{\overrightarrow{r}}{\Vert \overrightarrow{r} \Vert_2} It is also possible to solve for the critical-acceleration coefficient denoted k_c and the associated critical surface, which may then be used as input to the macro-command POST_NEWMARK U4.84.45 in order to compute the irreversible displacement of the slope at the end of the earthquake. To do this, one simply has to activate the operand CALC_KC , which then excludes the two other operands. 4.3.15 Operand METHODE_LEM = 'BISHOP' or 'FELLENIUS' ◊ METHODE_LEM= /'BISHOP' /'FELLENIUS' The operand METHODE_LEM makes it possible to switch between the different procedures for the stability analysis by the LEM method. This operand determines at the same time the objective function of the optimisation algorithm. When METHODE_LEM = 'BISHOP' or 'FELLENIUS', one makes the assumption that the failure surface is circular and one computes the factor of safety by assuming that the interaction forces between the slices are horizontal (BISHOP) or zero (FELLENIUS). The surface being circular, one seeks the critical surface by visiting all the combinations of entry and exit points. For each combination, one automatically computes the radius minimising FS. Two approaches are available for determining the trial bands of the radius: - Option 1 : One visits all the radii which form a kinematically admissible failure surface. - Option 2 : One defines manually the trial band by defining the horizontal straight lines tangential to the failure surfaces. This search option speeds up the analysis if the experienced user foresees a reduced zone in which the failure surface probably lies. One also takes advantage of this option in order to examine the surfaces in the neighbourhood of the one given by the result. The document R7.05.02 explains in more detail the optimisation algorithm for the simplified Bishop and Fellenius procedures. 4.3.15.1 Operands NB_POINT_1 and NB_POINT_2 ◊ NB_POINT_1 = / 5 / nb_point_1 ◊ NB_POINT_2 = / 5 / nb_point_2 The operands NB_POINT_1 and NB_POINT_2 define the number of intermediate points between the search bands of the entry and exit points respectively. For example, one tests all the points x1: {x}_{1}^{i}={x}_{1min}+({x}_{1max}-{x}_{min})/({N}_{1}-1)\ast i \quad \text{} \forall i=0,1,\mathrm{...},{N}_{1}-1 If X1/2_MINI and X1/2_MAXI are equal, NB_POINT_1/2 will systematically be reset to 1. 4.3.15.2 Operands Y_MINI and Y_MAXI ◊ Y_MINI = y_min ◊ Y_MAXI = y_max The operands Y_MINI and Y_MAXI define the minimum and maximum ordinates of the horizontal straight lines tangential to the failure surfaces tested. These operands will be necessary if one controls manually the search for the radius (option 2 mentioned in section 4.3.6 ). An example of the configuration of Y_MINI and Y_MAXI is shown in fig1-geom-lem. One must make sure that y_min is less than min\lbrace x{1}_{max},x{2}_{min}\rbrace . Indeed, if the entry and exit points lie on the two sides of the tangential straight line, this combination will be ignored since it will be impossible to create a tangential failure surface which crosses its tangent line. 4.3.15.3 Operand NB_RAYON ◊ NB_RAYON = / 15 / nb_r The operand NB_RAYON defines the number of surfaces to be tested for each combination of the entry and exit points. For the Bishop and Fellenius methods, the circles are generated in the manner illustrated in illus-circ-gene. From the two ends, a third point on the circle is determined by drawing the perpendicular straight line passing through the middle of the segment X1-X2. The operand NB_RAYON controls the number of discretisations of the distance between the segment X1-X2 and the intersection of this straight line with the circle: d_n = d_{min} + \frac{d_{max} - d_{min}}{N_r - 1}(n-1) where the minimum value d_{min} is determined automatically in the following two situations: 1. If there is no intersection between the segment X1-X2 and the slope profile, d_{min} is computed simply as d_{min} = \frac{d_{max}}{N_r} . 2. Otherwise, one chooses the circle whose radius is maximum among those which satisfy the following conditions in order to avoid the failure of creation of the mesh-cell groups of the slices: - The circle is included in the model between X1 and X2. - The distance between the circle and the slope profile is greater than the minimum size of the mesh cells in the vertical direction. - All the intermediate points move away from the slope profile by a vertical distance greater than the size of the mesh cell just below the slope at the same abscissa. Generation of the circles in the Bishop and Fellenius methods. 4.3.16 Operand METHODE_LEM = ‘SPENCER’ or ‘MORGENSTERN_PRICE’ ◊ METHODE_LEM= /'SPENCER' /'MOGENSTERN-PRICE' When METHODE_LEM = 'SPENCER' or 'MORGENSTERN_PRICE', one makes the assumption that the failure surface is multi-linear and one computes the factor of safety by solving at the same time the complete balance of the forces and of the moments of the set of slices. The search for the critical surface relies on the enhanced fireworks algorithm (Enhanced Fireworks Algorithm, EFWA), which is part of the swarm-intelligence algorithms (Swarm Intelligence Algorithm), and therefore requires additional parameters in order to configure the EFWA algorithm. The document R7.05.02 explains the EFWA algorithm in detail. During the evaluation of the FS of the potential failure surfaces generated by the EFWA, it is possible that the surface is physically illegal and that the condition of convergence of the fixed-point iterations is not satisfied, which does not prevent the location of the global critical surface. Therefore in that case one assigns to this illegal surface a very large FS (with the issuing of an information message) and continues to test the other failure surfaces. In order to avoid the EFWA generating this type of illegal surface, it is better to increase the number of slices so that the surfaces are smooth. However, one must check at the same time that the mesh is fine enough, which ensures the existence of mesh cells all of whose nodes are included in a slice of reduced size. 4.3.16.1 Keyword INIT_ALEA ◇ INIT_ALEA = int, If the keyword INIT_ALEA is supplied, one initialises the seed of the random sequences by this value. Two consecutive analyses with the same initialisation then produce the same results. If the keyword is not supplied, then the seed used is displayed in the message file. 4.3.16.2 Keyword ALGO_EFWA ⟐ ALGO_EFWA = _F( ◇ ETAT_INIT = table, ◇ ITER_MAXI = int (défaut: 50), ◆ A = float, ◇ A_INIT = float, ◇ A_FINAL = float, ◇ N = int (défaut: 5), ◇ M = int (défaut: 40), ◇ MG = int (défaut: 5), ◇ SA = float (défaut: 0.04), ◇ SB = float (défaut: 0.8), ◇ NB_STAB_MAXI = int (défaut: 10), ◇ CRIT_STAB = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ MARGE_PENTE = float, ), Factor keyword defining the parameters linked to the EFWA optimisation algorithm. ◊ ETAT_INIT = tabfs This operand takes as input the table at the output of the macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE, which makes it possible to initialise the EFWA algorithm by adding to the first generation of fireworks the position of the critical surface coming from the previous analysis. This operand is useful in the following two circumstances: 1. Since the EFWA is a probabilistic algorithm, the reaching of the global optimum is not mathematically guaranteed at the end of a limited number of iterations. Therefore CALC_STAB_PENTE offers the possibility of recovering the result before the true optimum is reached and of restarting the analysis if necessary. 2. In order to reduce the number of iterations, one may take the result coming from the Bishop or Fellenius method as the initial state. In general, this initial state is already a perfect approximation of the exact solution. ◊ ITER_MAXI = / 1e2 / iter_max The operand ITER_MAXI defines the maximum number of iterations of the EFWA. At the end of iter_max iterations, the algorithm stops even if the minimum value of FS has not yet been obtained. ◆ A = float, ◇ A_INIT = float, ◇ A_FINAL = float, ◇ N = int (défaut: 5), ◇ M = int (défaut: 40), ◇ MG = int (défaut: 5), ◇ SA = float (défaut: 0.04), ◇ SB = float (défaut: 0.8), The operands A, A_INIT, A_FINAL, N, M, MG, SA, SB define the parameters linked to the generation of the ordinary and Gaussian sparks in the EFWA. The meaning of these operands is the following: - The operand A : the total amplitude of the explosion of the fireworks. It depends on the characteristic dimension of the slope. For example, let H be the height of the slope; it is reasonable to estimate approximately the value of A as: A=\frac{m}{\mathit{nb}\text{\_}\mathit{tranches}}H - The operands A_INIT and A_FINAL : the initial and final minimum amplitude which is involved in the computation of the lower bound of the explosion amplitude. This minimum amplitude makes it possible to maintain the local search capacity around the optimal solution. By default, the initial and final amplitudes are equal to 100% and 10% of the width of the soil slices. One adopts the non-linear decreasing function: A_{min}(N) = A_{init} - \frac{A_{init} - A_{fina}}{N_{max}}\sqrt{(2N_{max} - N)N} - The operand N : number of fireworks in each generation. - The operand M : total number of ordinary sparks generated during the explosion of all the fireworks. - The operand MG : number of Gaussian sparks generated during the explosion of the fireworks. The generation of the Gaussian sparks has the purpose of improving the diversity of the sparks distributed in the space of the state variables, which is the main advantage of the EFWA with respect to the other swarm algorithms. - The operand SA : multiplying coefficient determining the lower limit of the number of sparks generated during the explosion of a firework. - The operand SB : multiplying coefficient determining the upper limit of the number of sparks generated during the explosion of a firework. ◇ NB_STAB_MAXI = int (défaut: 10), ◇ CRIT_STAB = float (défaut: 0.001), The operand NB_STAB_MAXI defines the number of consecutive iterations giving an FS/KC whose variation is less than the threshold defined via the operand CRIT_STAB before the analysis is considered to have converged. ◇ MARGE_PENTE = float, The operand MARGE_PENTE imposes a vertical margin between the failure surfaces tested and the slope profile, in order to ensure the possibility of creating the mesh-cell groups for the soil slices. It is not always necessary to impose manually a margin between the failure surface and the slope profile, except if one is confronted with the failure of creation of the mesh-cell groups followed by the error messages of the operator DEFI_GROUP . Indeed, the program evaluates this margin automatically by analysing the mesh contained in the cham_mater as input. One attempts to choose a margin as small as possible in order to widen the search zone. Furthermore, the potential surfaces being generated recursively, too large a margin will have an impact on the efficiency of the EFWA and even risks causing the failure of generation of the initial surfaces. Therefore, in the case of failure of DEFI_GROUP or of non-convergence, it is advised first to improve the mesh used before imposing a vertical margin manually. 4.4 Operand CHAM_DEFO ◊ CHAM_DEFO=CO(chamdef) Name of the evol_noli concept containing the field visualising the failure surface. 1. In the case where METHODE_STAB = 'SRM': The result chamdef contains the cumulative plastic-strain field (component V1 of the field VARI_NOEU) to be produced by the macro-command. It is possible to print this field via the command IMPR_RESU at the end of the execution of the macro-command in order to visualise the slip surface, which corresponds to the zone where the cumulative plastic strain is large. 1. In the case where METHODE_STAB = 'LEM': The result chamdef contains the indicative displacement field (NOEU_DEPL) visualising the sliding part of the slope. One assigns to the component DX the value 1 if the node is part of the sliding part, and 0 otherwise. 5 Example of use The stability analysis of a dam or of a dyke proceeds in 5 stages: 1. Definition of the model and of the material field. 2. Computation of the pore-pressure field by the model D_PLAN_H (static) or D_PLAN_HH (transient). 3. Definition of the mechanical loadings (hydrostatic pressure and acceleration coefficient). 4. SRM method: introduction of the hydraulic pressure into a new material field via the factor keyword AFFE_VARC. LEM method: introduce the hydraulic pressure field via CHAM_PRES. One has the option of taking the matric suction into account by activating SUCCION. 5. Computation of the stability factor via the macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE. 5.1 Example of an analysis with the SRM method An example of use for the static analysis with the SRM method is shown below. More details are found in the test case V1.01.135. CMPTOT = AFFE_MATERIAU( AFFE=( _F(GROUP_MA=("fondation",), MATER=(FOND,)), _F(GROUP_MA=("fond_fill",), MATER=(ROCK,)), _F(GROUP_MA=("rockfill_down", "rockfill_up"), MATER=(Remblai,)), _F(GROUP_MA=("core",), MATER=(CLAY,)), ), AFFE_VARC=_F(EVOL=REPTOT, NOM_VARC="PTOT", TOUT="OUI"), MAILLAGE=MAILME, ) TABFS1 = CALC_STAB_PENTE( MODELE=modME, CHAM_MATER=CMPTOT, GROUP_MA=("ZONE_SRM"), EXCIT=( _F(CHARGE=DIRI), _F(CHARGE=Gravity, FONC_MULT=multi), _F(CHARGE=Presrep, FONC_MULT=multi), ), INCREMENT=_F(LIST_INST=LTr), CONVERGENCE=_F(ITER_GLOB_MAXI=10), COMPORTEMENT=(_F(RELATION="MOHR_COULOMB"), _F(RELATION="ELAS", GROUP_MA=("rockfill_down"))), FS=_F(FS_INIT=1.84, INCR_INIT=0.04, RESI_MAXI=0.02), CHAM_DEFO=CO("chamdef"), ) IMPR_TABLE(TABLE=TABFS1, UNITE=8) IMPR_RESU(RESU = _F(RESULTAT = chamdef), UNITE= 2) The transient hydraulic analysis makes it possible to evaluate the stability of a hydraulic embankment structure under transient loadings, such as flooding for the dykes and the rapid drawdown of the reservoir. The macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE is nevertheless not capable of processing the transient loadings directly, with the exception of the quasi-static loadings with a multiplying function which serves to improve the convergence of the analysis. However, the evaluation of the stability of the structure under transient hydraulic loading can possibly be carried out with CALC_STAB_PENTE by checking, at each transient analysis step, the static stability of the structure. With this method one will obtain the tables as a result whose total number is equal to the number of physical time instants. It is therefore possible to plot the variation of the factor of safety as a function of time. 5.2 Example of an analysis with the LEM method An example of use for the stability analysis by the simplified Bishop method is shown below. RESTAB = CALC_STAB_PENTE(CHAM_MATER = CHMAT, METHODE_STAB = 'LEM', METHODE_LEM = 'BISHOP', GROUP_MA = 'range_pente', NB_TRANCHE = nb_tranche, NB_RAYON = 15, SUCCION = 'OUI', PHI_B = _F(TOUT = 'OUI', VALE = 10.), LIGN_PHREA = _F(INDIC_PIEZO = [1, 2], TABLE = TABPIEZO, TOUT = 'OUI', ), FONC_PRES = f_pres, RAFF_MAIL = _F(NB_RAFF_MAXI = nb_raff_maxi, RAFF_CRIT_STAB = raff_crit_stab), X1_MINI = x1_mini, X1_MAXI = x1_maxi, X2_MINI = x2_mini, X2_MAXI = x2_maxi, NB_POINT_1 = nb_point_1, NB_POINT_2 = nb_point_2, INFO_TABLE = 2, ) An example of use for the stability analysis by the Morgenstern-Price method is shown below. TABFS = CALC_STAB_PENTE( CHAM_MATER=CHMAT, METHODE_STAB="LEM", METHODE_LEM="MORGENSTERN_PRICE", CRITERE="MOHR_COULOMB", GROUP_MA=("range_pente",), NB_TRANCHE=5, CHAM_PRES=_F(RESULTAT=CHPROJ, INST=CHPROJ.LIST_VARI_ACCES()["INST"][-1], ALGO_PRES="INVERSE"), RAFF_MAIL=_F(NB_RAFF_MAXI=1), X1_MINI=3.0, X1_MAXI=3.0, X2_MINI=13.2, X2_MAXI=13.2, ALGO_EFWA=_F(ETAT_INIT=TAB_INIT, ITER_MAXI=1, A=50, N=1, M=1, MG=0, MARGE_PENTE=0.8), CHAM_DEFO=CO("chamdef"), ) More details are found in the test case V1.01.146. 6 Bibliography 1. Griffiths, D. V., & Lane, P. A. (1999). Slope Stability Analysis by Finite Elements . Geotechnique, 49, 387–403. doi:10.1680/geot.1999.49.3.387 1. Duncan, J. M., Wright, S. G., & Brandon, T. L. (2014). Soil Strength and Slope Stability (2nd ed.). Wiley. 1. A. W. Bishop and N. Morgenstern, (1960). Stability Coefficients for Earth Slopes , Geotechnique, 10(4): 129-153 1. S. K. Vanapalli, D. G. Fredlund, D. E. Pufahl, and A. W. Clifton , (1996), Model for the Prediction of Shear Strength With Respect To Soil Suction , Can. Geotech. J., 33(3): 379-392

u4.85.01 Operator CALC_META u4.85.01 Operator CALC_META 1 Purpose Computes the metallurgical evolution associated with a thermal history. The operator operates as a post-processing of the result of the thermal analysis in the sense that the latter is an “incoming” datum of the metallurgical analysis and that there is no coupling between the metallurgy and the thermal analysis. Two evolution models are available: - a model dedicated to the austenite–ferrite transformations of steel, - a model dedicated to the transformations of zirconium alloys. It is furthermore possible to apply a model in order to compute the tempering phases of the steel. The analysis is carried out at the nodes (field META_ELNO). The result obtained may subsequently be used as a loading datum of a thermomechanical analysis with account taken of the metallurgy. One may also, at the end of a metallurgy analysis, carry out a hardness post-processing analysis. Re-entrant operator; it enriches a data structure evol_ther . 2 Syntax evol_ther = CALC_META( ◆ reuse = , ◇ MODELE = modele, ◇ CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, ◆ RESULTAT = evol_ther, ◆ OPTION = / "DURT_ELNO", / "DURT_NOEU", / "META_ELNO", / "META_NOEU", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, # Si: is_in('OPTION', ('META_ELNO','META_NOEU')) ◆ ETAT_INIT = _F( ◆ / EVOL_THER = evol_ther, / META_INIT_ELNO = carte, # Si: exists("EVOL_THER") ◆ / NUME_INIT = int, / INST_INIT = float, # Si: exists("INST_INIT") ◇ CRITERE = / "ABSOLU", / "RELATIF" (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'RELATIF')) ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 1e-06), # Si: (equal_to("CRITERE", 'ABSOLU')) ◆ PRECISION = float, ), ◆ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◆ RELATION = / "ACIER", / "ACIER_REVENU", / "ZIRC", # Si: equal_to("RELATION", 'ACIER') ◇ LOI_META = "WAECKEL", # Si: equal_to("RELATION", 'ZIRC') ◇ LOI_META = "EDGAR", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / | GROUP_MA = grma, ), ◇ REVENU = _F( ◆ RELATION = "ACIER_REVENU" (ou non renseigné), # Si: equal_to("RELATION", 'ACIER_REVENU') ◇ LOI_META = "JMA", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / | GROUP_MA = grma, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keywords MODELE and CHAM_MATER Name of the model MODELE and of the assigned material field CHAM_MATER whose elements are the subject of the metallurgical analysis. 3.2 Keyword RESULTAT RESULTAT is the name of the result of type evol_ther coming from a thermal analysis from which one carries out a metallurgy analysis. At the end of the analysis this result will be enriched with the evolution of the metallurgical field, fields of internal variables whose number and meaning depend on the transformation model used. 3.3 Selection of the mesh cells concerned by the analysis The keywords TOUT (all the mesh cells carrying finite elements will be processed) and GROUP_MA allow the user to choose the mesh cells on which he or she wishes to carry out the elementary post-processing analyses. 3.4 Factor keyword COMPORTEMENT ◆ COMPORTEMENT = _F( ◆ RELATION = / "ACIER", / "ZIRC", # Si: equal_to("RELATION", 'ACIER') ◇ LOI_META = "WAECKEL", # Si: equal_to("RELATION", 'ZIRC') ◇ LOI_META = "EDGAR", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / | GROUP_MA = grma, ) The factor keyword COMPORTEMENT supplies the metallurgical evolution model used. One may use only one evolution model per analysis. 3.4.1 Keyword RELATION The keyword RELATION, which is equal to "ACIER" , serves to specify the execution of the analysis of the metallurgical transformations of the steel, in the vicinity of 800°C , from a ferritic phase (ferrite, pearlite, bainite, martensite) to an austenitic phase (and conversely on cooling). The model on heating and on cooling are different (the selection of this model is made according to the keyword LOI_META). Steel gives six phases as internal variables. | Variable | Quantity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | \mathrm{V1} | {Z_1} | proportion of ferrite | | \mathrm{V2} | {Z_2} | proportion of pearlite | | \mathrm{V3} | {Z_3} | proportion of bainite | | \mathrm{V4} | {Z_4} | proportion of martensite | | \mathrm{V5} | {Z_\gamma} | proportion of austenite (hot phase) | | \mathrm{V6} | {Z_c} | proportion of the cold phases | The sum of all the phases must be equal to 1.0. If this is not the case (to within 1%), an alarm is issued. The necessary material data must be supplied in DEFI_MATERIAU, under the keyword META_ACIER. The keyword RELATION, which is equal to "ZIRC" , serves to specify the execution of the analysis for the metallurgical transformation (on cooling) of zirconium alloys, from a hexagonal close-packed phase to a body-centred cubic phase in the vicinity of 800°C (the selection of this model is made according to the keyword LOI_META). Zircaloy gives three phases as internal variables: | Variable | Quantity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | \mathrm{V1} | {Z_\alpha} | proportion of the cold phase | | \mathrm{V2} | {Z_2} | initially without meaning and obligatorily zero; for a post-processing, the fraction of phase \alpha is given by V1+V2 ; | | \mathrm{V3} | {Z_\beta} | proportion of the hot phase | The sum of all the phases must be equal to 1.0. If this is not the case (to within 1%), an alarm is issued. The necessary material data must be supplied in DEFI_MATERIAU, under the factor keyword META_ZIRC. 3.4.2 Keyword LOI_META The keyword LOI_META serves to specify the metallurgical model used: - For steel, LOI_META equal to "WAECKEL" uses the Waeckel model r4.04.01 - For Zircaloy, LOI_META equal to "EDGAR" uses the Edgar model r4.04.02 The Waeckel model adds three internal variables to those describing the phases of the steel. | Variable | Quantity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | \mathrm{V7} | d | austenitic grain size | | \mathrm{V8} | T_g | temperature at the Gauss points | | \mathrm{V9} | {M}_{s} | martensitic transformation temperature | The Edgar model adds two internal variables to those describing the phases of Zircaloy. | Variable | Description | | --- | --- | | \mathrm{V4} | The temperature at the nodes | | \mathrm{V5} | The time corresponding either to the equilibrium transformation start temperature if the fraction of phase \alpha is equal to 1 initially, or to the equilibrium transformation end temperature if the fraction of phase \alpha is equal to 0 initially. This variable is used to compute the rate on heating, respectively on cooling (sliding-secant method), which serves to determine the transformation start temperatures on heating or on cooling. | 3.4.3 Keywords TOUT and GROUP_MA The keywords TOUT and GROUP_MA specify the mesh cells on which the model is used and make it possible to assign the analysis only on a sub-part of the total mesh. 3.5 Factor keyword ETAT_INIT The factor keyword ETAT_INIT describes the initial metallurgical state. 3.5.1 Keyword META_INIT_ELNO The keyword META_INIT_ELNO defines the assignment of the initial internal-variable field, constant per element, from a map defined by CREA_CHAMP. Only the variables whose initial assignment has a meaning are to be supplied. One therefore supplies only the variables corresponding to a phase proportion, plus possibly the one corresponding to the austenitic grain size if it is not zero. In the case of the steel, one obligatorily supplies all the phases and the grain size, otherwise the code stops with a fatal error. If the user has not supplied correctly the sum of the cold phases, it is the code which will replace it by the sum computed from the data. An alarm will then be issued. In the case of Zircaloy, one obligatorily supplies all the phases and the time corresponding to the equilibrium transformation start temperature, otherwise the code stops with a fatal error. 3.5.2 Keywords EVOL_THER, NUME_INIT, INST_INIT, PRECISION and CRITERE The keyword EVOL_THER defines the concept of type evol_ther from which one will extract the initial state from which the analysis will be carried out. This concept must contain metallurgical quantities (grandeur) (fields META_ELNO) The definition of the initial state may be made by stored order number or by the time instant associated with the analysis. NUME_INIT allows the definition from the stored order number and INST_INIT allows the definition from the analysis time instant. In this latter case, PRECISION and CRITERE make it possible to define the precision and the criterion according to which the extraction will be carried out. If "ABSOLU" is chosen, it is mandatory to supply the field PRECISION; if CRITERE is equal to "RELATIF" , a precision of 1.E-6 is given by default, and may possibly be modified by supplying the keyword PRECISION. 3.6 Keyword OPTION The keyword OPTION specifies the quantities to be computed: - If OPTION is equal to "DURT_ELNO" , one computes the hardness at the nodes by element from the metallurgical phases (cf. R4.04.01) - If OPTION is equal to "DURT_NOEU" , one computes the hardness at the nodes from the metallurgical phases (cf. R4.04.01) - If OPTION is equal to "META_ELNO" , one computes the proportion of metallurgical phase at the nodes by element. - If OPTION is equal to "META_NOEU" , one computes the proportion of metallurgical phase at the nodes 3.7 Factor keyword REVENU ◆ REVENU = _F( ◆ RELATION = / "ACIER_REVENU", (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("RELATION", 'ACIER_REVENU') ◇ LOI_META = "JMA", ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / | GROUP_MA = grma, ), The factor keyword REVENU makes it possible to activate the computation of the tempering phases for steel (cf. R4.04.01). It is possible to restrict the analysis to a sub-part of the mesh by means of the keyword GROUP_MA. A check is made in order to prevent the use of this tempering model on anything other than an analysis on steel. The necessary material data must be supplied in DEFI_MATERIAU, under the keyword META_ACIER_REVENU. This analysis enriches the field META_ELNO and modifies its internal variables, now 12 in number (instead of 9 in the case without tempering). | Variable | Quantity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | \mathrm{V1} | {Z_1} | proportion of ferrite | | \mathrm{V2} | {Z_2} | proportion of pearlite | | \mathrm{V3} | {Z^b_3} | proportion of bainite (as-quenched phase) | | \mathrm{V4} | {Z^r_3} | proportion of bainite (tempered phase) | | \mathrm{V5} | {Z^b_4} | proportion of martensite (as-quenched phase) | | \mathrm{V6} | {Z^r_4} | proportion of bainite (tempered phase) | | \mathrm{V7} | {Z_\gamma} | proportion of austenite (hot phase) | | \mathrm{V8} | {Z_c} | proportion of the cold phases | | \mathrm{V9} | d | austenitic grain size | | \mathrm{V10} | T_g | temperature at the Gauss points | | \mathrm{V11} | {M}_{s} | martensitic transformation temperature | | \mathrm{V12} | {I}^{th} | thermal-cycle indicator | Note These metallurgical phases are not usable as input to a mechanical analysis. 4 Example in the case of a steel One presents an example of creation of the initial internal-variable field (with 70% ferrite, 30% bainite and the rest at zero). phasinit = CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION ='AFFE', TYPE_CHAM = 'CART_VAR2_R', MAILLAGE = mail, AFFE =_F( TOUT = 'OUI', NOM_CMP = ('V1','V2','V3','V4','V5','V6','V7'), VALE = (0.7,0.0,0.3,0.0,0,1.,0.))), Then one computes the thermal evolution: tempe = THER_LINEAIRE(MODELE = moth, CHAM_MATER = chmat , EXCIT = _F(CHARGE = chth1), INCREMENT = (LIST_INST= lr8), TEMP_INIT =(VALE = 700),) Finally one computes the evolution of the metallurgical phases: tempe = CALC_META (reuse = tempe, MODELE = moth, CHAM_MATER = chmat, RESULTAT = tempe, ETAT_INIT =_F(META_INIT_ELNO = phasinit), COMPORTEMENT =_F(RELATION ='ACIER',TOUT = 'OUI'))

u4.86.01 Procedure POST_ENDO_FISS u4.86.01 Procedure POST_ENDO_FISS 1 Purpose The command POST_ENDO_FISS carries out a post-processing on a result coming from continuum mechanics. The aim is to find the curve which represents the crack from a representative field, and the crack opening. The field may be the damage or another scalar field. As input, the command uses an evol_noli or cham_gd concept, containing the field to be post-processed. The latter must be a field at the nodes. As output, the command returns a mesh of the crack (constituted by SEG2 elements), as well as a table containing the coordinates of the nodes of the crack and the value of the opening on each node. The procedure applies to 2D studies. 2 Syntax / table / maillage = POST_ENDO_FISS( ◆ TABLE = co, ◇ OUVERTURE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: exists("RESULTAT") ◆ / NUME_ORDRE = int, / INST = float, ◆ / CHAM_GD = cham_gd, / RESULTAT = evol_noli, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ◆ NOM_CHAM = text, ◆ RECHERCHE = _F( ◆ LONG_ORTH = float, ◇ NB_POINT = int (défaut: 500), ◆ PAS = float, ◆ LONG_REG = float, ◇ BORNE_MIN = float (défaut: 0.5), ◇ ANGL_MAX = float (défaut: 120.0), ◇ / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), / GROUP_MA = grma, ◇ BORNE_MAX = float, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TABLE ♦ TABLE = CO('table') This operand (mandatory) makes it possible to give the name of the concept output by the command. The table at the output contains the information on the cracking path and the crack opening. In the case where only the path is sought (option OUVERTURE='NON'), the table has 4 columns, in which, for each node of the crack, are displayed: the name of the crack of which the node is part, its coordinate X , its coordinate Y , the value of the post-processed field. If the crack opening is also requested (OUVERTURE='OUI'), it will be entered in the table in a 5th column. 3.2 Operands RESULTAT / CHAM_GD / ♦ RESULTAT = evol_noli ♦ CHAM_GD = cham_gd Name of the result concept containing the field to be post-processed (RESULTAT), or field of quantities (grandeur) (CHAM_GD). One must obligatorily choose one of the two. The field to be post-processed must obligatorily be a field at the nodes. 3.3 Operands INST / NUME_ORDRE / ♦INST = inst ♦ NUME_ORDRE = nume_ordre These operands must be supplied only in the presence of the operand RESULTAT. They are used to select the time instant to be post-processed. One must obligatorily choose one of the two. 3.4 Operand NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM = nom_cham This operand is mandatory. One gives here the name of the field to be post-processed and on which the procedure for searching for the cracking paths is then applied, for example VARI_NOEU. 3.5 Operand NOM_CMP ♦ NOM_CMP = nom_cmp This operand is mandatory. It makes it possible to choose the component to be post-processed in the field supplied, for example V1. Indeed, the procedure is applicable only to a scalar field. 3.6 Operand OUVERTURE ♦ OUVERTURE = /NON /OUI Under this operand, one supplies the type of operation carried out by the command. By default, one seeks only the cracking path (OUVERTURE='NON). If OUVERTURE='OUI', the crack opening is also computed. 3.7 Keyword RECHERCHE One supplies here the parameters for the search for the cracks and for the corresponding openings. The call to this keyword is repeatable in order to allow the search for several cracks which lie on distinct mesh-cell groups. 3.7.1 Operands TOUT / GROUP_MA ◊ / TOUT = "OUI" [DEFAUT] / GROUP_MA = group_ma Under the operand GROUP_MA, one may supply the mesh-cell group on which to search for the cracking path. If this operand is absent, the search is carried out over the whole geometrical domain defined by the mesh. 3.7.2 Operands LONG_ORTH / LONG_REG ♦ LONG_ORTH= long_orth ♦ LONG_REG = long_reg Under the operand LONG_ORTH, one supplies the length of the profile orthogonal to the search direction, used by the procedure at each analysis step. On this profile, one keeps the point where the value of the field (projected and smoothed) is maximum, which gives the new point of the crack trace. LONG_ORTH must normally be equal to or greater than the width of the damaged band. The projection of the field onto this profile is smoothed by means of another length, LONG_REG, in order to avoid the new point lying on the edge of a finite element. For the method to work properly, LONG_REG must lie in the range 0.5 to 2 times the size of the mesh cells which lie in the damaged band. It shows a diagram of the search for the cracking path; one will consult the document R7.02.17 for a more detailed explanation of the operation of the command. Figure 3.7.2-a : diagram of the search for the cracking path. 3.7.3 Operand PAS ♦ PAS = pas This is the advance step of the search procedure. There is no recommended value; the procedure is fairly robust with respect to the choice of this parameter. On the other hand, if the advance step is too large, one risks not detecting the portions of the crack characterised by strong curvatures. A small step (of the order of magnitude of the size of the finite element) may be recommended if one seeks to have many points in order to discretise the crack. 3.7.4 Operand BORNE_MIN ◊BORNE_MIN = seuil Value of the field in correspondence with which one stops the search for the path of the crack. 3.7.5 Operand BORNE_MAX ♦BORNE_MAX = lfpz This quantity defines the width of the damaged band, on which the crack opening is computed. It is to be supplied only with the option OUVERTURE='OUI'. 3.7.6 Operand ANGL_MAX ◊ANGL_MAX = / 120. / angle_max The search on the orthogonal profile may be restricted to a central piece defined by means of an angle (in degrees) equal to angle_max, symmetric with respect to the prediction point (see the ). 3.7.7 Operand NB_POINTS > ◊ NB_POINT = nb_points This keyword makes it possible to define the number of points on half of the orthogonal profile, which defines the precision on the latter. By default, this parameter is equal to 500. 4 Example of use See the test case zzzz264 (document V1.01.264).

u4.86.02 Macro-command POST_CZM_FISS u4.86.02 Macro-command POST_CZM_FISS 1 Purpose This macro-command makes it possible to carry out the following two types of post-processing: - supply, at each loading increment, information on the length of a straight 2D cohesive crack (positions of the crack tip and of the cohesive tip). More precisely, the macro supplies the distance between an origin point POINT_ORIG and each of the two tips in the direction and the sense of the direction vector VECT_TANG, as well as the distance between the two tips (size of the cohesive zone); - compute and store in a map the stress triaxiality in the solid elements directly neighbouring the cohesive elements. 2 Syntax / carte / table = POST_CZM_FISS( ◆ OPTION = / "LONGUEUR", / "TRIAXIALITE", ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli, # Si: equal_to("OPTION", 'LONGUEUR') ◆ GROUP_MA = grma, ◆ POINT_ORIG = float, ◆ VECT_TANG = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = resu Name of the result concept of a non-linear analysis with cohesive elements. 3.2 Operand OPTION ♦ OPTION = /'LONGUEUR' /'TRIAXIALITE' Choice of the type of post-processing carried out by the macro-command 3.3 Operand GROUP_MA ♦ GROUP_MA = group_ma Name of the group of cohesive mesh cells with the modellings PLAN_JOINT, PLAN_INTERFACE, AXIS_JOINT or AXIS_INTERFACE. And having one of the cohesive constitutive behaviours: CZM_OUV_MIX, CZM_TAC_MIX, CZM_LIN_REG, CZM_EXP_REG. This operand is possible only when OPTION = 'LONGUEUR'. 3.4 Operand POINT_ORIG ♦ POINT_ORIG = point Point initial de la fissure cohésive: deux composantes réelles dans le plan (X,Y) (voir figures ci-dessous) This operand is possible only when OPTION = 'LONGUEUR'. 3.5 Operand VECT_TANG ♦ VECT_TANG = vecteur Vecteur directeur: deux composantes réelles dans le plan (X,Y) (voir figures ci-dessous). This operand is possible only when OPTION = 'LONGUEUR'. 4 Concept produced 4.1 Case OPTION = 'LONGUEUR' As output one creates a table of type table_sdaster containing four columns: INST: the time instant of the analysis LONG_FIS: distance between the crack tip and the reference point (LF see figure2). LONG_TOT: total length (LF + LZC see figure2) LONG_COH: size of the cohesive zone (LZC see figure2) 4.2 Case OPTION = 'TRIAXIALITE' The macro-command produces in this case a map (of NEUT_R with one component X1) sized to the number of mesh cells carrying cohesive elements. For each mesh cell, the value stored is that of the stress triaxiality, read and averaged in the elements of the solid directly neighbouring (by edge in 2D or by face in 3D) this mesh cell. The stress field used for this post-processing is the one which corresponds to the last archived time step in the evol_noli supplied under the keyword RESULTAT. 5 Scope of use 5.1 Case OPTION = 'LONGUEUR' The evol_noli supplied under the keyword RESULTAT must be the result of a 2D non-linear analysis with cohesive elements. The crack must furthermore be straight. The command issues an error or alarm message if the user goes outside the scope of use: - The user is required to define properly the half-line from the point POINT_ORIG (aligned with the GPs) and the direction vector VECT_TANG (collinear with the line of the GPs). One checks these conditions but also that there do indeed exist GPs on the half-line in question (sense of the vector properly chosen). - In the case where one of these three conditions is not satisfied, one displays an error message indicating the problem encountered as well as the extrema of the coordinates of the GPs in order to help the user define the half-line properly. - As defined, the lengths are valid only if the cohesive zone is connected. If this is not the case, an alarm message is displayed. - If one observes that the cohesive zone is composed of only three GPs or fewer, one displays an alarm message stating that the mesh does not seem fine enough to capture this zone correctly (see doc U2.05.07, advice on the use of cohesive models). 5.2 Case OPTION = 'TRIAXIALITE' This post-processing is available in 2D and in 3D. The modellings supported in the solid and on the cohesive interface are summarised in the table below. | Modellings supported in the solid | Modellings supported on the cohesive interface | | --- | --- | | 'D_PLAN', 'C_PLAN', 'AXIS', '3D' | 'PLAN_JOINT', 'AXIS_JOINT', '3D_JOINT' | | 'PLAN_INTERFACE', 'AXIS_INTERFACE', '3D_INTERFACE' | | | 'PLAN_INTERFACE_S', 'AXIS_INTERFACE_S', '3D_INTERFACE_S' | | 6 Details of the command 6.1 Case OPTION = 'LONGUEUR' The cohesive crack is represented in figure 1; it is assumed straight, and it is decomposed into three distinct zones: sound, cohesive (or damaged) and free surface (or cracked). One represents respectively in red, green and blue the Gauss points (GPs) of these zones. From these zones one defines a cohesive tip (white point) and a crack tip (black point). The macro gives the distance between the origin point POINT_ORIG (red point) and each of the two tips in the direction and the sense of the direction vector VECT_TANG (red vector) as well as the distance between the two tips. Figure1 : Diagram of the cohesive crack and of its Gauss points. In order to define the position of the tips (see figure2) one relies on the geometrical coordinates of the GPs and on the field of the internal variable VARI_ELGA, component V3 of the CZM laws, which takes the value 0 if the GP is sound, 1 if the GP is damaged and 2 if the GP is cracked. For each of these three states one defines Dmin and Dmax corresponding to the minimum and maximum distances with respect to the origin point. The crack tip is positioned between the broken GPs and the damaged GPs, the cohesive tip is positioned between the damaged GPs and the sound GPs.
