Figure2 : Diagram of the GP field of a straight 2D cohesive crack with the position of the tips (as an example one draws Dmin and Dmax for the damaged GPs). 6.2 Case OPTION = 'TRIAXIALITE' For this option, the operation of the macro-command is as follows. 1. Detection of the presence of cohesive elements (see the modellings supported in the paragraph “scope of use”) in the model which was used to produce the evol_noli supplied under the keyword RESULTAT. If no cohesive element is detected, a fatal error message is issued. 2. Recovery of the stress field corresponding to the last archived time step. 3. Carrying out of a loop over the mesh cells assigned cohesive elements. During this loop, for each cohesive mesh cell, one identifies the mesh cells of the solid which are directly neighbouring it (by face in 3D, and by edge in 2D) by means of the data structure sd_voisinage. One makes sure that this cohesive mesh cell has only one or two neighbouring mesh cells of this type (the zone of the mesh assigned the cohesive elements must therefore: either cross the structure completely, or lie on a part of the boundary, as is for example the case when one models a symmetry condition). Once these neighbouring mesh cells have been identified, one computes the stress-triaxiality ratio at all the Gauss points of these neighbouring elements. One then carries out the arithmetic mean of the triaxiality at the Gauss points: by element and then over the number of neighbours if the current cohesive mesh cell has 2 neighbours in the solid. Finally, in the map produced by the macro-command, one stores for the current cohesive mesh cell the value of this averaged triaxiality. The map produced by the macro-command may then be used as a command variable in the operator AFFE_MATERIAU (AFFE_VARC / CHAM_GD) U4.43.03 in order to make the parameters of the cohesive law vary with the triaxiality. 7 Example of use For OPTION = 'LONGUEUR': see the test case ssnp139 V6.03.139. For OPTION = 'TRIAXIALITE': see the test case zzzz359 V1.01.359

u4.90.01 Macro-command CALC_ESSAI u4.90.01 Macro-command CALC_ESSAI 1 Purpose Launching of the macro-command CALC_ESSAI, which makes it possible to launch identification and expansion analyses on wire structures and to launch structural-modification analyses: - expansion of experimental data on a basis of numerical mode shapes, using the macro-command MACRO_EXPANS (which carries out the elementary operations EXTR_MODE, PROJ_MESU_MODAL, REST_GENE_PHYS and PROJ_CHAMP), - identification of forces on an arbitrary structure, with decomposition of the motion on a modal basis and a priori localisation of the loadings, - structural modification: assess the effect of a modification, knowing the experimental modal model of the initial structure and the finite-element model of the modification introduced 2 Syntax / matr_asse_depl_r / macr_elem_stat / mode_gene / modele / maillage / nume_ddl / interspectre / mode_meca = CALC_ESSAI( ◇ RESU_IDENTIFICATION = _F( ◇ TABLE = co, ), ◇ RESU_MODIFSTRU = _F( ◇ MODELE = co, ◇ MODE_MECA = co, ◇ MAILLAGE = co, ◇ NUME_DDL = co, ◇ MASS_MECA = co, ◇ RIGI_MECA = co, ◇ AMOR_MECA = co, ◇ MACR_ELEM = co, ◇ PROJ_MESU = co, ◇ BASE_ES = co, ◇ BASE_LMME = co, ◇ MODE_STA = co, ), ◇ EXPANSION = _F( ◆ CALCUL = mode_meca, ◇ NUME_MODE_CALCUL = int, ◆ MESURE = mode_meca, ◇ NUME_MODE_MESURE = int, ◇ RESOLUTION = / "SVD" (par défaut), / "LU", # Si: equal_to("RESOLUTION", 'SVD') ◇ EPS = float, ), ◇ IDENTIFICATION = _F( ◇ ALPHA = float, ◇ EPS = float, ◆ OBSERVABILITE = mode_meca, ◆ COMMANDABILITE = mode_meca, ◆ INTE_SPEC = interspectre, ◆ BASE = mode_meca, ), ◇ MODIFSTRUCT = _F( ◆ MESURE = mode_meca, ◆ MODELE_SUP = modele, ◆ MATR_RIGI = matr_asse_depl_r, ◇ RESOLUTION = / "ES" (par défaut), / "LMME", # Si: equal_to("RESOLUTION", 'LMME') ◆ MATR_MASS = matr_asse_depl_r, ◆ NUME_MODE_MESU = int, ◆ NUME_MODE_CALCUL = int, ◆ MODELE_MODIF = modele, ), # Si: exists("MODIFSTRUCT") ◇ GROUP_NO_CAPTEURS = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ), ◇ GROUP_NO_EXTERIEUR = _F( ◆ GROUP_NO = grno, ◆ NOM_CMP = text, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Introduction The macro-command CALC_ESSAI makes it possible to carry out identification analyses from measured data: expansion of experimental data onto a numerical model, force identification, and structural modification. 4 Use of modal expansion (EXPANSION) The way this option is used is not very relevant; it is mainly useful for validation. If one wishes to carry out a modal expansion, it is preferable to use the command MACRO_EXPANS directly, or the sequence PROJ_MESU_MODAL, REST_GENE_PHYS and PROJ_CHAMP. 4.1 Keywords MESURE and NUME_MODE_MESURE ♦ MESURE = mesure, Concept sd_resultat of type mode_meca or dyna_harmo which contains the modes to be expanded onto the numerical model. ♦ NUME_MODE_MESURE = L_I, Makes it possible to select the order numbers of the modes that one wishes to expand. 4.2 Keyword CALCUL ♦ CALCUL = calcul, Concept sd_resultat of type mode_meca which will be the expansion basis. The choice of the expansion basis is important for the quality of the results. ♦ NUME_MODE_CALCUL = L_I, Makes it possible to select the order numbers of the modes that one wishes to use in the expansion basis. It is more useful to keep only the modes that «resemble» the shapes to be expanded, the resemblance criterion being obtainable by a MAC analysis. 4.3 Keywords RESOLUTION and EPS The expansion consists in solving an inverse problem in order to determine the generalised coefficients of PROJ_MESU_MODAL. The inversion methods and regularisation coefficients are detailed in the user's documentation of this operator (cf U4.73.01). 5 Structural modification (MODIFSTRUCT) This structural-modification technique is based on the substructuring method. The first substructure corresponds to the initial structure and the second substructure corresponds to the modification introduced. The initial structure is modelled from the eigenmodes identified experimentally. The second substructure is modelled numerically by finite elements. Except in very particular cases, the measurement points are not located at the interface between the initial structure and the modification. It is therefore necessary to go through an intermediate step which consists in carrying out an expansion of the measurement onto the interface degrees of freedom. This expansion is done via the supporting numerical model. The following paragraphs describe the keywords required in CALC_ESSAI for this functionality. More details on the method and on the principles of its implementation in Code_Aster are given in the documentation U2.07.03. 5.1 Keyword MESURE ♦ MESURE = mesure [mode_meca] mesure is the name of the concept which contains the identified eigenmodes. 5.2 Keyword MODELE_SUP ♦ MODELE_SUP = modele [modele] Name of the supporting model on which the expansion basis is built. 5.3 Keyword MODELE_MODIF ♦ MODELE_MODIF = modele [modele] Name of the model of the modification introduced into the initial structure. 5.4 Keyword MATR_RIGI ♦ MATR_RIGI = matrice, [matr_asse] Stiffness matrix defined on the supporting model, required for the analysis of the static modes. 5.5 Keyword RESOLUTION ♦ RESOLUTION = /’ES’, [DEFAUT] /'LMME' This keyword makes it possible to choose the method used for the analysis of the expansion basis. ES corresponds to static expansion and LMME corresponds to «Local Model Modeshapes Expansion». 5.6 Keyword NUME_MODE_MESU ♦ NUME_MODE_MESU = L_I, [l_I] This keyword makes it possible to select the numbers of the modes to be used among the identified eigenmodes. By default, all the eigenmodes of the concept mesure are taken into account. 5.7 Keyword NUME_MODE_CALCUL ♦ NUME_MODE_CALCUL = L_I, [l_I] This keyword makes it possible to select the numbers of the modes to be used among the vectors of the expansion basis. By default, all the vectors of the expansion basis are taken into account. 5.8 Keyword GROUP_NO_CAPTEURS ◊ GROUP_NO_CAPTEURS = _F( ♦ GROUP_NO = gr_no, [mode_meca] ♦ NOM_CMP = nom_cmp, [matr_asse] This factor keyword makes it possible to select the list of node groups that will be used for the analysis of the static modes associated with the measurement points. These node groups are defined on the supporting model. 5.9 Keyword GROUP_NO_EXTERIEUR ◊ GROUP_NO_EXTERIEUR = _F ( ♦ GROUP_NO = gr_no, [mode_meca] ♦ NOM_CMP = nom_cmp, [matr_asse] This factor keyword makes it possible to define the «external» node groups on which the measured information will be condensed. These node groups must contain at least the interface between the supporting model and the model of the modification. 5.9.1 The concepts produced The user may specify the names of the concepts produced by the interface by filling in the factor keyword RESU_MODIFSTRU. These concepts can then be used for subsequent analyses. ◊ MODE_MECA = mode, [mode_meca] mode will be the name of the concept which contains the eigenmodes of the modified structure. ◊ MODELE = modele, [modele] modele will be the name associated with the model of the modified structure. ◊ MAILLAGE = maillage, [maillage] maillage will be the name of the mesh associated with the modified structure. ◊ NUME_DDL= nume, [nume_ddl] nume will be the name of the nume_ddl concept associated with the modified structure. ◊ MASS_MECA = masse, [matr_asse] masse will be the name of the concept which contains the assembled mass matrix of the modified structure. ◊ RIGI_MECA = raid, [matr_asse] raid will be the name of the concept which contains the assembled stiffness matrix of the modified structure. ◊ AMOR_MECA = amor, [matr_asse] amor will be the name of the concept which contains the assembled damping matrix of the modified structure. ◊ MACR_ELEM = macrel, [macr_elem_stat] macrel will be the name of the concept which contains the macro-element in which the measurement is condensed. ◊ PROJ_MESU = proj, [mode_gene] proj will be the name of the concept which contains the generalised coordinates of the identified modes with respect to the expansion basis. ◊ BASE_LMME = balmme, [mode_meca] balmme will be the name of the expansion basis obtained from the LMME method. ◊ BASE_ES = baes, [mode_meca] baes will be the name of the expansion basis obtained from static expansion (ES method). ◊ MODE_STAT = modest, [mode_stat_force] modest will be the name of the concept which contains the static modes associated with the measurement points. 6 Identification of forces localised a priori (IDENTIFICATION) 6.1 Keyword INTE_SPEC ♦ INTE_SPEC = intsp Cross-spectrum that will be used as displacements, in order to recover the associated forces. 6.2 Keywords OBSERVABILITE and COMMANDABILITE ♦ OBSERVABILITE = observ ♦ COMMANDABILITE = command Concept of type mode_meca. They correspond respectively to the objects C\Phi and {\Phi}^{T}B described in section 6.4 . One may either choose a raw mode_meca, or build it with the operator OBSERVATION (U4.90.03). 6.3 Keywords ALPHA and EPS ♦ ALPHA = reel ♦ EPS = reel Regularisation parameters. More details in section 6.5 . 6.4 Reminder of the theoretical principles Force identification assumes that the motion of the structure under study can be decomposed on a modal basis: y(\omega )=\left[C\Phi \right].{\left[Z(\omega )\right]}^{-1.}\left[{\Phi}^{T}B\right].f(\omega ) In the following equations, the dependence on \omega will be omitted. \Phi is a basis of modal shapes associated with the structure under study. In theory, it is the basis of the continuous mode shapes. In practice, one generally uses a basis defined on a numerical model with a relatively fine discretisation. This basis may be computed numerically, or be the result of a modal expansion. The operator C makes it possible to project this basis of mode shapes onto the subspace of the observable degrees of freedom. The operator B makes it possible to project the basis of mode shapes onto a set of degrees of freedom called actuators: one finds here one of the fundamental assumptions of the identification: the identified forces are localised on degrees of freedom declared a priori by the user, as was done to declare the measurement degrees of freedom (use of the operator OBSERVATION). The aim is to reduce as far as possible the number of unknowns to be determined, which makes it possible to avoid the problems of under-determination of the problem. Identifying the forces amounts to inverting the system above: NB: the basis \Phi may be different on the right and on the left of Z : this is the case when the available measurements are strains. The equation relating the force to the measurement is then written: f={\left[{\Phi}^{T}B\right]}^{-1.}\left[Z\right].{\left[C\Psi \right]}^{-1.}\epsilon ( 8-2) where the matrix \Psi is the data of the modes in strain. Warning, however: writing this last equation is an abuse of language, because the passage from displacements to strains should normally be written in the projection operator (which, let us recall, is linear in the case of small strains), and not by replacing \Phi by \Psi . But in practice, one often imports a basis of modes \Psi directly from the measurement software. 6.5 The concepts to be used Observability and controllability: The computation of \left[C\Phi \right] is carried out in the panel «Definition of the observability concept», in which one gives the mode basis \Phi , and an experimental model that contains the degrees of freedom onto which it is projected. One chooses, among the degrees of freedom of the experimental model (grouped by node groups and mesh-cell groups), the degrees of freedom corresponding to the measurement. One can thus choose only a single direction if single-axis sensors were used during the measurement. It is also possible to carry out a change of frame. For more detail, refer to the documentation of the operator OBSERVATION (U4.90.03). - It is important that the nodes and the components declared in the cross-spectrum be consistent with the degrees of freedom of the observability concept . In the case where the cross-spectrum is read by LIRE_INTE_SPEC (FORMAT = ‘IDEAS’), the nodes are defined in the header of each dataset; the table then created by this operator keeps the notations of that file. The computation of \left[{\Phi}^{T}B\right] is carried out in the panel «Definition of the controllability concept». The choice of the degrees of freedom and the potential changes of frame are made according to the same rule. Each tab has a basis-selection button, which makes it possible, as for equation 8-2, to use two different bases. Regularisation: The inversion of the transfer function is carried out in two steps: - inversion of \left[C\Phi \right].{\left[Z\right]}^{-1} , which makes it possible to compute the modal forces, - inversion of \left[{\Phi}^{T}B\right] , which makes it possible to compute the forces on the physical basis. These two steps are carried out by SVD (SVD of LinearAlgebra, a Python module, which calls a lapack_lite library, in the numpy package). It is possible to regularise the inversion in three ways: 1. truncation of the SVD (parameter \varepsilon ), 2. Tikhonov regularisation (parameter \alpha ), 3. slope control: it is possible to multiply the parameter \alpha by {(\omega -{\omega}_{i})}^{m} , where {\omega}_{i} is the natural circular frequency of the mode and m a parameter to be determined; this makes it possible to control the slope of the curve obtained for the high frequencies, when the measured signal is strongly noisy at high frequency.

u4.90.02 Macro-command MACRO_EXPANS u4.90.02 Macro-command MACRO_EXPANS 1 Purpose The macro-command MACRO_EXPANS makes it possible to carry out the expansion of experimental data onto a numerical model from an expansion basis. It consists of the succession of the operators EXTR_MODE, PROJ_MESU_MODAL, REST_GENE_PHYS and PROJ_CHAMP. 2 Syntax / dyna_harmo / mode_meca = MACRO_EXPANS( ◆ MODELE_CALCUL = _F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ BASE = mode_meca, ◇ NUME_MODE = int, ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ), ◆ MODELE_MESURE = _F( ◆ MODELE = modele, ◆ MESURE = mode_meca_c / dyna_trans / dyna_harmo / mode_meca, ◇ NOM_CHAM = / "DEPL" (par défaut), / "VITE", / "ACCE", / "SIEF_NOEU", / "EPSI_NOEU", ◇ NUME_MODE = int, ◇ NUME_ORDRE = int, ), ◇ NUME_DDL = nume_ddl, ◇ RESU_NX = co / dyna_harmo / mode_meca, ◇ RESU_EX = co / dyna_harmo / mode_meca, ◇ RESU_ET = co / dyna_harmo / mode_meca, ◇ RESU_RD = co / dyna_harmo / mode_meca, ◇ RESOLUTION = _F( ◇ METHODE = / "LU" (par défaut), / "SVD", # Si: equal_to("METHODE", 'SVD') ◇ EPS = float, ◇ REGUL = / "NON" (par défaut), / "NORM_MIN", / "TIK_RELA", # Si: not equal_to("REGUL", 'NON') ◇ / COEF_PONDER = float, / COEF_PONDER_F = formule / nappe / fonction, ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword MODELE_CALCUL ♦ MODELE_CALCUL Factor keyword gathering all the keywords relating to the expansion basis, generally obtained by analysis (hence the name). 3.1.1 Keyword MODELE ♦ MODELE = modelnum modele_sdaster denoting the model onto which the measurement will be expanded 3.1.2 Keyword BASE ♦ BASE = base mode_meca serving as the basis for the expansion. The basis must not contain collinear vectors, and the number of modes used must be smaller than the number of measurement degrees of freedom (preferably, nmodes << nmes); otherwise, the system to be solved is under-determined, which may lead to a fatal error and a stop of the code. 3.1.3 Keyword NUME_ORDRE/NUME_MODE List of the order numbers or of the modal positions of the modes that one wishes to use for the expansion. 3.2 Keyword MODELE_MESURE ♦ MODELE_MESURE Factor keyword gathering all the keywords relating to the experimental basis that one wishes to expand 3.2.1 Keyword MODELE ♦ MODELE = modelexp modele_sdaster denoting the model associated with the experimental mesh. Knowledge of the nodes is in general sufficient to determine an experimental mesh. The associated model can then be defined as follows: MODELEXP = AFFE_MODELE( MAILLAGE = MAIEXP, AFFE = _F( GROUP_MA = 'CAPTEURS', PHENOMENE = 'MECANIQUE', MODELISATION = 'DIS_T',),); CAREXP = AFFE_CARA_ELEM( MODELE = MODELEXP, DISCRET = _F( GROUP_MA = 'CAPTEURS', REPERE = 'GLOBAL', CARA = 'K_T_D_N', VALE = (100.0,100.0,100.0,), ),); The stiffness values given are arbitrary; they are not used in the analysis. NB: in order to use the operator PROJ_CHAMP in the macro, one needs to generate a nume_ddl associated with this mesh. To do so, one must in addition assign a material to the model, compute the elementary matrices (stiffness, for example) and create the numbering with NUME_DDL. 3.2.2 Keyword MESURE ♦ MESURE = mes dyna_harmo or mode_meca to be expanded. These data are in general imported from a measurement result (.unv file) with the operator LIRE_RESU. 3.2.3 Keyword NUME_ORDRE/NUME_MODE List of integers. Makes it possible to select the modes that one wishes to expand. 3.2.4 Keyword NOM_CHAM ♦NOM_CHAM = ‘DEPL’… Experimental quantity to be expanded. 3.3 Keyword RESOLUTION Two solution techniques are proposed for the inverse problem: truncated SVD, LU method. For the SVD, one may choose to truncate the smallest singular values in order to improve the conditioning of the problem (choice of 'eps'), or use a Tikhonov-type regularisation. One may refer to the documents U4.73.01 (documentation of PROJ_MESU_MODAL) and R6.03.01 (reference document on the singular-value decomposition). 3.4 Keyword NUME_DDL Makes it possible to impose the numbering to be used for the operator PROJ_CHAMP. For more detail, refer to the documentation of PROJ_CHAMP U4.72.05. 3.5 Keywords RESU_XX The keywords RESU_XX make it possible to pre-declare the names of the output concepts: - RESU_NX is the truncation of the numerical basis (keyword BASE under the factor keyword MODELE_CALCUL) to the modes chosen in NUME_MODE, - RESU_EX is the truncation of the experimental basis (keyword MESURE under the factor keyword MODELE_MESURE) to the modes chosen in NUME_MODE, - RESU_ET is the result of the expansion, - RESU_RD is the reprojection onto the experimental model of the expanded basis: it is useful to check whether the reprojection of the expanded result is comparable to the initial experimental data.

u4.90.03 Macro-command OBSERVATION u4.90.03 Macro-command OBSERVATION 1 Purpose The macro-command OBSERVATION uses the operators PROJ_CHAMP, CREA_CHAMP, CREA_RESU, MODI_REPERE and POST_RELEVE_T in order to: - project a field from a numerical model onto an experimental model, - modify the local frames, - select the «measurement» degrees of freedom, - compute the mean value of a strain field in order to obtain the equivalent of the information delivered by a strain gauge This macro-command accepts as input a concept evol_elas, dyna_trans, dyna_harmo or a mode_meca. The concept produced is of the same type as the input concept. Warning: Code_Aster does not store the frames in which the fields are written. The result of this macro-command must therefore not be used in subsequent Code-Aster analyses. It can be used for post-processing in Python, or for visualisations. 2 Syntax / dyna_trans / dyna_harmo / evol_elas / mode_meca = OBSERVATION( ◆ MODELE_1 = modele, ◆ MODELE_2 = modele, ◆ RESULTAT = dyna_trans / dyna_harmo / evol_elas / mode_meca, ◆ NOM_CHAM = / "ACCE", / "ACCE_ABSOLU", / "COEF_H", / "COHE_ELEM", / "COMPORTEMENT", / "COMPORTHER", / "CONT_ELEM", / "CONT_NOEU", / "DEGE_ELGA", / DDL_ACTIF = text, ), ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands The first simple keywords are those used in the operator PROJ_CHAMP. Some of these concepts are however reused in the following phases of the macro-command (modification of the frames and filtering of the degrees of freedom). In the macro-command, the operator PROJ_CHAMP is used by default with the method 'COLOCATION' (cf U4.72.04). But one can explicitly use the point-cloud method by adding the necessary keywords detailed in the documentation of this operator. The concept produced is of the same type as the input concept, defined by the keyword RESULTAT. 3.1 Keyword RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT Data structure that one wishes to manipulate. At present, only structures of type evol_elas, dyna_trans, dyna_harmo and mode_meca can be given as input. 3.2 Keyword MODELE_1 ♦ MODELE_1 Structure of type modele_sdaster associated with the result concept. It is in general the supporting numerical model. 3.3 Keyword MODELE_2 ♦ MODELE_2 Structure of type modele_sdaster. It is in general the model associated with the experiment. Warning: PROJ_CHAMP works only if the degrees of freedom of the nodes of model 1 are the same as those of model 2. For example, if model 1 is 3D, and therefore has only translational degrees of freedom, one cannot take a POU_D_T modelling (Timoshenko beam, with translational and rotational degrees of freedom) for model 2. One will choose in this case a modelling of type BARRE. 3.4 Keyword PROJECTION ◊ PROJECTION = / 'OUI' [DEFAUT] / 'NON' This keyword makes it possible to carry out, or not, the projection of the results of the processing onto model 2. If no projection is carried out, the results of the processing overload the results already present on model 1. 3.5 Operand CAS_FIGURE This keyword (optional) is used to direct the program towards one of the following 4 cases: - "3D" The only mesh cells of mesh "1" that will be used for the projection are the volume mesh cells: hexahedra, pentahedra, tetrahedra and pyramids. The nodes have 3 coordinates (X,Y,Z) . - "2D" The only mesh cells of mesh "1" that will be used for the projection are the surface mesh cells: quadrilaterals and triangles. The mesh is assumed to be plane. The nodes have 2 coordinates (X,Y) . - "2.5D" The only mesh cells of mesh "1" that will be used for the projection are the surface mesh cells: quadrilaterals and triangles. The mesh is 3D. The nodes have 3 coordinates (X,Y,Z) . This is the case of "shells" immersed in 3D. - "1.5D" The only mesh cells of mesh "1" that will be used for the projection are the line mesh cells: segments. The mesh may be 2D or 3D. The nodes have 2 or 3 coordinates (X,Y,Z) . 3.6 Keyword VIS_A_VIS One may refer to U4.72.04 (documentation of the operator PROJ_CHAMP) for the use of this optional keyword, which makes it possible to declare explicitly the links between entities of model 1 and of model 2 for the projection. There is nevertheless a specificity to the use of VIS_A_VIS in this command: the mesh-cell groups placed face to face must bear the same name in the two models. Otherwise, an error is issued. 3.7 Operand TYPE_CHAM = 'NOEU' This keyword is used to force the projected fields to be fields «at the nodes». This keyword is used systematically (for example) by the command MACR_LIGN_COUPE because one does not know how to create fields by elements on the «fictitious» beam model created by this visualisation macro-command. 3.8 Selection of the field names The keyword NOM_CHAM = l_noch makes it possible to choose which fields of the data structure RESULTAT one wants to project. This keyword is mandatory. One can also project the fields by elements "ELNO" and "ELEM" (but not "ELGA"). 3.9 Operands MATR_RIGI, MATR_MASS These 2 keywords make it possible to associate (for a data structure of type «mode») their matr_asse with the data structure produced. They also make it possible to recover the numbering of the degrees of freedom. They are necessary if one wishes to use the result of the command in subsequent analyses (commands REST_GENE_PHYS, PROJ_BASE, MAC_MODES, …). 3.10 Selection of the order numbers See U4.71.00. 3.11 Operand MODI_REPERE ◊ MODI_REPERE = _F( Mot-clé facteur permettant de définir un repère local pour les entités (nœuds ou mailles) du modèle 2 sélectionnées. 3.11.1 Keywords TYPE_CHAM/NOM_CMP The operator MODI_REPERE must know the components to be transformed. One generally uses a displacement field as input, which is why the entries 'VECT_3D' and ('DX','DY','DZ') are proposed by default. But if one wishes, for example, to treat the case of a strain field (measured by means of strain gauges), one will write TYP_CHAM ='TENS_3D' and NOM_CMP=('EXX','EYY'…) 3.11.2 Keywords REPERE/VECT_X/VECT_Y/ANGL_NAUT/ORIGINE/AXE_Z - REPERE = 'UTILISATEUR' The user may himself define the local frame associated with a node by giving the three nautical angles. A definition of the nautical angles will be found in [U4.42.01-I1], U4 documentation of AFFE_CARA_ELEM, paragraph 10.4. - REPERE = 'CYLINDRIQUE' To define a cylindrical frame, one must give the origin (keyword ORIGINE) and the direction of the vertical axis (keyword AXE_Z). - REPERE = 'NORMALE' The axes of the local frame are denoted (\mathrm{X1},\mathrm{Y1},\mathrm{Z1}) . In general, the sensors, for a measurement, have the axis \mathrm{Z1} along the normal to the wall of this structure. This option makes it possible to compute a frame associated with this normal: - computation of the field of vectors normal to model 1 (the most accurate); these vectors will be the axes \mathrm{Z1} of the local frame, - projection of this field onto the selected entities of model 2, - explicit data of the second vector of the frame; if one wishes the vector \mathrm{Y1} to be the same vector as Y in the global frame, one writes VECT_Y = (0.0,1.0,0.0) - One therefore needs two equations to compute the local frame: one of them is given by the normal vector, the other is given by the keyword VECT_X or VECT_Y, according to whether the additional condition concerns the vector \mathrm{X1} or \mathrm{Y1} of the local frame. - REPERE = 'DIR_JAUGE' The user may define the local frame associated with the strain gauge by filling in VECT_X and/or VECT_Y. These two vectors correspond to the first two basis vectors of the local frame. 3.12 Operand FILTRE ◊ FILTRE = _F( Keyword describing, for all the entities (nodes, mesh cells, node groups, …), the degrees of freedom to be kept. 3.12.1 Keyword DDL_ACTIF ◊ DDL_ACTIF = liste_ddl List of the degrees of freedom to be kept for the result. 3.12.2 Keywords GROUP_NO/GROUP_MA Each degree-of-freedom filter corresponds to a topological entity to be chosen (by default, the whole structure is selected). 3.12.3 Keyword NOM_CHAM ♦ NOM_CHAM = noch Symbolic name of the field to be filtered. This keyword is mandatory. It makes it possible, among other things, to distinguish the component DX of the displacement field from the component DX of the velocity field. 3.13 Operand EPSI_MOYENNE ◊ EPSI_MOYENNE = _F( Factor keyword making it possible to compute the mean value of the strain field on a given topological entity. This mean value of the strain field can be seen as the information that a strain gauge bonded onto the surface considered would have delivered. This is valid if the field is not too variable over the surface onto which the gauge is bonded. The user is warned if the fluctuation of the strain field is too large. Each occurrence of this keyword corresponds to a computation of the mean on the designated entities. The values computed are then projected onto model 2, unless the user explicitly specifies PROJECTION = 'NON'. In that case, one overloads the input concept resu_in and one stores the results of the analysis in resu_out. 3.13.1 Keywords GROUP_NO/GROUP_MA This keyword indicates the topological entity on which one wants to compute the mean. 3.13.2 Keyword MASQUE ◊MASQUE = lcmp This keyword makes it possible to list unmeasured components of the strain field. 3.13.3 Keyword SEUIL_VARI ◊ SEUIL_VARI = seuil One gives here a relative threshold value above which the user is warned if the fluctuation of one of the components of the field, not masked, departs too far from the computed mean value. The value taken by default is equal to 0.1 . 3.14 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = titr, Title that one wishes to give to the result concept.

u4.90.11 Operator CALC_MAC3COEUR u4.90.11 Operator CALC_MAC3COEUR 1 Purpose Macro-command dedicated to fuel assemblies. The aim is to evaluate: - either the deformation of the fuel assemblies subjected to thermal, hydraulic and neutronic loadings; - or the inter-assembly water gaps at the beginning or at the end of a reactor cycle. 2 Syntax evol_noli = CALC_MAC3COEUR( ◆ TYPE_COEUR = / "MONO", / "MONO_FROID", / "TEST", / "900", / "1300", / "N4", / "LIGNE900", / "LIGNE1300", / "LIGNEN4", # Si: is_in("TYPE_COEUR", ("LIGNE900","LIGNE1300","LIGNEN4")) ◆ NB_ASSEMBLAGE = int, ◆ TABLE_N = table, ◇ MAILLAGE_N = maillage, ◇ RESU_DEF = co, ◇ FLUENCE_CYCLE = float, ◇ TYPE_DEFORMATION = "RIGI_GEOM", ◇ ETAT_INITIAL = _F( ◇ UNITE_THYC = unit, ◆ NIVE_FLUENCE = float, ◇ TYPE_MAINTIEN = "DEPL_PSC", ◇ MAINTIEN_GRILLE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ ARCHIMEDE = "OUI", ), ◇ LAME = _F( ◆ UNITE_THYC = unit, ◇ COEF_MULT_THV = float (défaut: 1.0), ◇ COEF_MULT_THT = float (défaut: 1.0), ), # Si: exists("TYPE_COEUR") and TYPE_COEUR.startswith('MONO') ◇ DEFORMATION = _F( ◇ RESU_INIT = resultat, ◆ NIVE_FLUENCE = float, ◆ UNITE_THYC = unit, ◇ MAINTIEN_GRILLE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◆ TYPE_MAINTIEN = / "FORCE", / "DEPL_PSC", # Si: equal_to("TYPE_MAINTIEN", 'FORCE') ◆ FORCE_MAINTIEN = float, ◆ ARCHIMEDE = / "OUI", / "NON", ), # Si: exists("TYPE_COEUR") and not TYPE_COEUR.startswith('MONO') ◇ DEFORMATION = _F( ◇ RESU_INIT = resultat, ◇ TEMP_IMPO = float, ◆ NIVE_FLUENCE = float, ◆ UNITE_THYC = unit, ◇ MAINTIEN_GRILLE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ TYPE_MAINTIEN = "DEPL_PSC", ◇ ARCHIMEDE = "OUI", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TYPE_COEUR Name of the type of core to be processed. The case 'TEST' represents a fictitious core with five fuel assemblies, arranged in a cross. The case 'MONO' represents a single assembly (that is, a fictitious single-assembly core, without taking into account contact with the reactor-vessel internals) at «hot core» temperature. The case 'MONO_FROID' represents a single assembly (that is, a fictitious single-assembly core, without taking into account contact with the reactor-vessel internals) at ambient temperature. The cases 'LIGNEXXX' (with XXX='900','1300' or 'N4') represent a row analysis for each plant-series design. One should refer to the reference documentation R7.06.01, in particular for everything concerning the loadings and the various frames used. 3.2 Operand NB_ASSEMBLAGE In the case of a core of type 'LIGNEXXX' (with XXX='900','1300', 'N4' or 'EPR'), this keyword makes it possible to specify the length of the line. 3.3 Operand TABLE_N Table (in DAMAC format) containing the assembly information (mainly position, design and deformation). For a 'DEFORMATION' analysis, this is the composition of the core of the simulated cycle. For a 'LAME' analysis, this is the DAMAC from which one wants to compute the water gaps. For an 'ETAT_INITIAL' analysis, this is the DAMAC that one seeks to reproduce. 3.4 Operand MAILLAGE_N Mesh corresponding to the description of the core: the design of the assemblies in the mesh must correspond to the design supplied in 'TABLE_N'. 3.5 Operand FLUENCE_CYCLE «Flat-rate» fluence used to take into account the initial irradiation of the assemblies: the initial irradiation of each assembly is taken equal to N times 'FLUENCE_CYCLE', with N the number of cycles already undergone by the assembly, given in 'TABLE_N'. With a value of FLUENCE_CYCLE=0, all the assemblies will therefore have a zero initial irradiation. Note: this keyword is not taken into account for a DEFORMATION analysis with RESU_INIT, because in that case the initial irradiation of each assembly comes from the result given in RESU_INIT. 3.6 Operand TYPE_DEFORMATION Makes it possible to choose how the kinematics are taken into account. The only option available is 'RIGI_GEOM', which corresponds to an analysis in PETIT with the option RIGI_GEOM='OUI'. 3.7 Operand DEFORMATION Factor keyword which specifies that the macro-command is used here to compute the deformations of the fuel assemblies in the core configuration. 3.7.1 Operand RESU_INIT Possibility of giving a result as the initial state. This keyword is useful when several irradiation cycles are carried out. 3.7.2 Operand UNITE_THYC Logical unit in which the THYC file is supplied as input to CALC_MAC3COEUR, containing the axial and transverse hydraulic loadings. 3.7.3 Operand TEMP_IMPO Value of the constant temperature. Activates the analysis of the simple thermal expansion of the reactor (without contact/friction or hydraulic loadings). 3.7.4 Operand NIVE_FLUENCE Value of the fluence received by the assemblies during the cycle (in {10}^{24}\mathit{neutrons}/{m}^{2} ). 3.7.5 Operand MAINTIEN_GRILLE Makes it possible to activate the option of locking the grids 3.7.6 Operand TYPE_MAINTIEN For multi-assembly cores (other than 'MONO' or 'MONO_FROID'), this keyword is optional and allows only the value 'DEPL_PSC' (default value) explained below. The hold-down force is then produced by the displacement imposed by the Upper Core Plate (PSC) on the hold-down system of each assembly. The value of this displacement is given in the geometric data file (datg) of each of the cores considered. In the single-assembly case ('MONO' or 'MONO_FROID'), the keyword TYPE_MAINTIEN is mandatory, with no default value, and may take the values 'DEPL_PSC' or 'FORCE': - 'DEPL_PSC': the hold-down force is then produced by an imposed displacement as described above; in this case the keyword FORCE_MAINTIEN is not expected; - 'FORCE': the hold-down force is then introduced by a fixed imposed force whose value is given by the keyword FORCE_MAINTIEN. This option makes it possible to reproduce faithfully the experimental tests that are used in particular to recalibrate the model. 3.7.7 Operand FORCE_MAINTIEN In the single-assembly case ('MONO' or 'MONO_FROID'), this keyword makes it possible to supply the value (in Newtons) of the hold-down force in the case TYPE_MAINTIEN='FORCE'. 3.7.8 Operand ARCHIMEDE In the single-assembly case, the keyword ARCHIMEDE is mandatory, with no default value, and may take the values 'OUI' or 'NON'. This keyword makes it possible to choose whether Archimedes' buoyancy is activated or not. For multi-assembly cores (other than 'MONO' or 'MONO_FROID'), this keyword is optional and allows only the value 'OUI' (default value): Archimedes' buoyancy is always activated. 3.8 Operand LAME Factor keyword which specifies that the macro-command is used here to determine the water gaps from a core made up of deformed assemblies. For an end-of-cycle water-gap analysis (EOC in English), it is sufficient to supply the measured DAMAC in 'TABLE_N'. For a beginning-of-cycle water-gap analysis (BOC in English), one must supply a «reconstructed» DAMAC from the known DAMACs and from the core loading pattern; this «reconstructed» DAMAC is the user's responsibility, and must be supplied in 'TABLE_N'. The hydraulic forces are taken into account by the loading defined in 'UNITE_THYC'. 3.8.1 Operand UNITE_THYC Logical unit in which the THYC file is supplied as input to CALC_MAC3COEUR, containing the axial and transverse hydraulic loadings. 3.8.2 Operands COEF_MULT_THV and COEF_MULT_THT Multiplicative coefficients for the axial and transverse hydraulic loadings. 3.9 Operand ETAT_INITIAL Factor keyword which specifies that the macro-command is used here to reconstruct the mechanical state from the observation of the deformations at the end of the cycle: this mechanical state can then be used as the initial state in a later analysis. 3.9.1 Operand UNITE_THYC Same use as in § 3.8.1 3.9.2 Operand NIVE_FLUENCE Same use as in § 3.7.4 . 3.9.3 Operand TYPE_MAINTIEN Same use as in § 3.7.6 in the case other than 'MONO'. 3.9.4 Operand ARCHIMEDE Same use as in § 3.7.8 in the case other than 'MONO'. 3.10 Operand RESU_DEF When the operand 'LAME' is used, the result is supplied on the mesh initially deformed by the given deformations (see R7.06.01 for the details of this operation): the displacements supplied by the result concept are therefore to be understood as the displacement relative to this deformed mesh and as the displacement relative to the mesh supplied with the «straight» assemblies. In practice, it is therefore complicated to use such displacements. CALC_MAC3COEUR / LAME therefore provides the operand 'RESU_DEF', which makes it possible to recover a result concept that contains the displacement on the initial undeformed mesh, which makes it easy to post-process the displacements. On the other hand, for post-processing of the «water gap» type, the results supplied by the result concept of CALC_MAC3COEUR are perfectly usable. The recommendation for a water-gap analysis is therefore to proceed as follows: RESU = CALC_MAC3COEUR( > […] > RESU_DEF = CO('RESUDEPL'), > LAME=_F( > […] > ) > ) post-processing of the water gaps on RESU POST_MAC3COEUR( > RESULTAT = RESU , > […] > LAME =_F( > […] > ), > ) post-processing of the displacements on RESUDEPL POST_MAC3COEUR( > RESULTAT = RESUDEPL , > […] > DEFORMATION =_F( > […] > ), > )

u4.90.12 Operator POST_MAC3COEUR u4.90.12 Operator POST_MAC3COEUR 1 Purpose Macro-command dedicated to the post-processing of CALC_MAC3COEUR, in order to extract, in table format, the values or analyses of the result. 2 Syntax table = POST_MAC3COEUR( ◆ TYPE_COEUR = / "MONO", / "MONO_FROID", / "TEST", / "900", / "1300", / "N4", / "LIGNE900", / "LIGNE1300", / "LIGNEN4", # Si: is_in("TYPE_COEUR", ("LIGNE900","LIGNE1300","LIGNEN4")) ◆ NB_ASSEMBLAGE = int, ◆ RESULTAT = evol_noli, ◆ TABLE = table, ◆ INST = float, ◆ TYPE_CALCUL = / "LAME", / "DEFORMATION", / "FORCE_CONTACT", ◇ OPERATION = / "EXTRACTION" (par défaut), / "ANALYSE", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TYPE_COEUR Name of the type of core to be processed. See u4.90.11 CALC_MAC3COEUR. 3.2 Operand NB_ASSEMBLAGE In the case of a core of type 'LIGNEXXX' (with XXX='900','1300', 'N4' or 'EPR'), makes it possible to specify the length of the line 3.3 Operand RESULTAT Name of the result data structure to be post-processed. 3.4 Operand TABLE Table (in DAMAC format) containing the assembly information. 3.5 Operand INST Time instant of the desired post-processing. Only one time instant is possible at a time. 3.6 Operand TYPE_CALCUL Nature of the result to be post-processed: water gaps, deformations or contact forces. 3.7 Operand OPERATION Nature of the post-processing: extraction or analysis of values.

u4.90.13 Macro-command PERM_MAC3COEUR u4.90.13 Macro-command PERM_MAC3COEUR 1 Purpose Macro-command making it possible to define the loading of a core from previous results. 2 Syntax evol_noli = PERM_MAC3COEUR( ◆ TYPE_COEUR_N = / "MONO", / "MONO_FROID", / "TEST", / "900", / "1300", / "N4", / "LIGNE900", / "LIGNE1300", / "LIGNEN4", # Si: is_in("TYPE_COEUR_N", ("LIGNE900","LIGNE1300","LIGNEN4")) ◆ NB_ASSEMBLAGE_N = int, ◆ TYPE_COEUR_NP1 = / "MONO", / "MONO_FROID", / "TEST", / "900", / "1300", / "N4", / "LIGNE900", / "LIGNE1300", / "LIGNEN4", # Si: is_in("TYPE_COEUR_NP1", ("LIGNE900","LIGNE1300","LIGNEN4")) ◆ NB_ASSEMBLAGE_NP1 = int, ◆ TABLE_N = table, ◆ RESU_N = evol_noli, ◆ TABLE_NP1 = table, ◆ MAILLAGE_NP1 = maillage, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Principle The command makes it possible to start an analysis of a cycle (CALC_MAC3COEUR / DEFORMATION) from previous results, taking into account the loading pattern and the names of the assemblies. It is thus possible to chain the cycle analyses: for example - from the results of the analyses of CHO101 (starting core), one can start the analysis of CHO102 (arrival core) with fresh assemblies and assemblies coming from CHO101, - after the analysis of CHO101 and CHO102 (starting cores), one can start the analysis of CHO103 (arrival core) from fresh assemblies, assemblies coming from CHO101 and assemblies coming from CHO102 - it is also possible to start a core analysis of any type (say 'N4' to take an example) from a set of results of core analyses of arbitrary types (say 'MONO' to take an example): it is sufficient that the names of the assemblies correspond between the arrival core and the starting cores. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand TYPE_COEUR_N Name of the type of the starting core. 4.2 Operand NB_ASSEMBLAGE_N In the case of a starting core of type 'LIGNEXXX' (with XXX='900','1300', 'N4' or 'EPR'), makes it possible to specify the length of the starting line 4.3 Operand TYPE_COEUR_NP1 Name of the type of the arrival core. 4.4 Operand NB_ASSEMBLAGE_NP1 In the case of an arrival core of type 'LIGNEXXX' (with XXX='900','1300' or 'N4'), makes it possible to specify the length of the arrival line 4.5 Operand TABLE_N Ordered list of tables containing the assembly information (mainly name, position and design) in the starting cores. If an assembly (identified by its name) appears in several tables, the result used will be the last one that appears in the list. The lists TABLE_N and RESU_N must therefore be ordered from the oldest to the most recent. For example > TABLE_N = (tab_CHO101, tab_CHO102), > RESU_N = (resu_CHO101,resu_CHO102) 4.6 Operand RESU_N Ordered list of results on the starting cores (the list must be of the same length as TABLE_N, and TABLE_N and RESU_N must be in the same order) 4.7 Operand TABLE_NP1 Table containing the assembly information in the arrival core Warning: it is essential that the information concerning an assembly be consistent in the starting and arrival tables (for example, an assembly of the same name in the starting and arrival tables must also have the same design in those tables) 4.8 Operand MAILLAGE_NP1 Mesh corresponding to the description of the arrival core.

= / "SINUSOIDAL" (par défaut), / "TRIANGULAIRE", ), | ESSAI_ISOT_DR_C_F = _F( ◆ PRES_CONF = float, ◆ SIGM_IMPOSE = float, ◆ SIGM_DECH = float, ◇ NB_INST = int (défaut: 25), ◇ TABLE_RESU = co, ◇ GRAPHIQUE = text (défaut: "P-EPS_VOL"), ◇ PREFIXE_FICHIER = text, ◇ TABLE_REF = table, ◇ NOM_CMP = text, ◇ COULEUR = int, ◇ MARQUEUR = int, ◇ STYLE = int, ◇ TYPE_CHARGE = / "SINUSOIDAL" (par défaut), / "TRIANGULAIRE", ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MATER ♦ MATER = mat [mater] This keyword makes it possible to give the name of the material defined by DEFI_MATERIAU [U4.43.01], in which the parameters required for the chosen constitutive behaviour are supplied. 3.2 Keyword COMPORTEMENT The syntax of this keyword is described in the document U4.51.11. Within this macro-command, the use of the operand RELATION of the keyword COMPORTEMENT is restricted to the following elastoplastic soil constitutive laws: - 'MOHR_COULOMB' - 'MohrCoulombAS' - 'CAM_CLAY' - 'CJS' - 'DRUCK_PRAGER' - 'DRUCK_PRAG_N_A' - 'HUJEUX' - 'Iwan' - 'MFRONT' - 'NLH_CSRM' - 'MCC' - 'CSSM' 3.3 Keyword CONVERGENCE ◊CONVERGENCE= _F() If neither of the following two operands is present, then everything proceeds as if: RESI_GLOB_RELA = 1.E-6 3.3.1 Operand RESI_GLOB_RELA/RESI_GLOB_MAXI ◊| RESI_GLOB_RELA = resi_rela [R] The algorithm continues the global iterations as long as: \underset{i=1,\mathit{nbddl}}{max}|{F}_{i}^{n}|\phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}>\phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\text{resi\_rela}\times max|L| where {F}^{n} is the residual of iteration n and L the vector of the imposed loading and of the support reactions (see R5.03.01 for more details). When the loading and the support reactions become zero, that is when L is zero (for example in the case of a total unloading), an attempt is made to switch from the relative convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_RELA to the absolute convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_MAXI. This operation is transparent for the user (alarm message issued in the .mess file). When the vector L becomes non-zero again, one automatically returns to the relative convergence criterion RESI_GLOB_RELA. However, this switching mechanism cannot work at the first time step. Indeed, in order to find a reasonable value of RESI_GLOB_MAXI automatically (since the user has not supplied one), one needs to have had at least one converged step in RESI_GLOB_RELA mode. Consequently, if the loading is zero from the first time instant, the analysis stops. The user must then first check that the zero loading is normal from the point of view of the modelling being carried out, and if that is the case, find another convergence criterion (RESI_GLOB_MAXI for example). If this operand is absent, the test is carried out with the default value, unless RESI_GLOB_MAXI is present. ◊| RESI_GLOB_MAXI = resi_maxi [R] The algorithm continues the global iterations as long as: \underset{i=1,\mathit{nbddl}}{max}|{F}_{i}^{n}|\phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}>\phantom{\rule{2em}{0ex}}\text{resi\_maxi} where {F}^{n} is the residual of iteration n (see R5.03.01 for more details). If this operand is absent, the test is not carried out. If RESI_GLOB_RELA and RESI_GLOB_MAXI are both present, both tests are carried out. 3.3.2 Operand ITER_GLOB_MAXI ◊ITER_GLOB_MAXI = | 10 [DEFAUT] | nb_iter Maximum number of iterations carried out to solve the global problem at each time instant. 3.4 Keyword ESSAI_TRIA_DR_M_D This repeatable factor keyword makes it possible to carry out a series of simulations of the same monotonic drained triaxial test at imposed strain, for which the loading parameters are varied (confining pressure and imposed axial strain), to post-process the results obtained and to write them in the form of plots (in xmgrace format) and/or tables. 3.4.1 Sign convention for the inputs and the outputs The sign convention of geomechanics applies to the input parameters in imposed stresses or strains, that is, the values are positive in compression. This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables, the complete list of which for this test is as follows: - INST: time instant - EPS_AXI: axial strain - EPS_LAT: lateral strain - EPS_VOL: volumetric strain - SIG_AXI: axial effective stress - SIG_LAT: lateral effective stress - P: mean effective stress - Q: stress deviator On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.4.6 ). 3.4.2 Operands PRES_CONF, EPSI_IMPOSE, NB_INST ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ EPSI_IMPOSE = l_epsi_impo [l_R] ◊NB_INST = | 100 [DEFAUT] | nbinst [I] The operand PRES_CONF makes it possible to define the list of confining pressures that will be maintained during each test. Likewise, the operand EPSI_IMPOSE makes it possible to define the list of the final values of the compression loading (imposed axial-strain ramp). For this test, each confining pressure is associated with a final value of the axial-strain ramp (see the figure): the lists PRES_CONF and EPSI_IMPOSE must therefore have the same cardinality. This cardinality corresponds to the number of simulations that will be run under this factor keyword. Stresses and strains being counted positive in compression, the values supplied for PRES_CONF must be strictly positive. The values supplied in EPSI_IMPOSE are strictly positive or negative, a negative value indicating a loading in extension. The operand NB_INST makes it possible to define the time discretisation of the loading (see the figure), with a default value of 100 loading steps during the ramp. .. image:: images/Cadre5.gif .. _RefSchema_Cadre5.gif: Figure 3.4.2-a: discrétisation et allure du chargement pour les mots-clés ESSAI_TD et ESSAI_TND 3.4.3 Operand KZERO ◊KZERO = | 1 [DEFAUT] Value of the coefficient of earth pressure at rest; it makes it possible to define an anisotropic confinement state: {\sigma}_{xx}={\sigma}_{yy}={K}_{0}{\sigma}_{zz}={K}_{0}\times \text{PRES\_CONF} Note: When the value of KZERO is set different from 1, the real confining pressure of the test is no longer PRES_CONF; it becomes: {P}_{c}=\frac{1+2{K}_{0}}{3}\times \text{PRES\_CONF} 3.4.4 Operand TABLE_RESU ◊TABLE_RESU= l_tabres [l_CO] This optional operand makes it possible to give the list of the names of the concepts produced by the macro-command, which will then be of type [table]. Each table produced contains the raw and post-processed results of one test simulation: the list TABLE_RESU must therefore have the same cardinality as the lists PRES_CONF and EPSI_IMPOSE. The title of each table produced is completed by the macro-command; it comprises: - the name of the factor keyword (here ESSAI_TRIA_DR_M_D) and its occurrence number (this keyword being repeatable); - the pair of values (PRES_CONF, EPSI_IMPOSE) characterising the loading of the test; Example : TABRES1=CO('TRES1') TABRES2=CO('TRES2') TABRES3=CO('TRES3') CALC_ESSAI_GEOMECA( ... ESSAI_TRIA_DR_M_D = _F( PRES_CONF = (-1.E4, -1.5E4, -2.E4 ), EPSI_IMPOSE = (-1.E-2, -1.E-2, -1.E-2), TABLE_RESU = (TABRES1, TABRES2, TABRES3),), ); TABRES1, TABRES2 and TABRES3 are filled successively according to the order of the lists PRES_CONF and EPSI_IMPOSE; the table below specifies the test results contained in each table. | EPSI_IMPOSE ® | -1.0E-2 | -1.0E-2 | -1.0E-2 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | PRES_CONF | | | | | -1.0E4 | TABRES1 | | | | -1.5E4 | | TABRES2 | | | -2.0E4 | | | TABRES3 | 3.4.5 Operand GRAPHIQUE, PREFIXE_FICHIER ◊GRAPHIQUE = | ('P-Q', 'EPS_AXI-Q', 'EPS_AXI-EPS_VOL', 'P-EPS_VOL') [DEFAUT] | l_graphique [l_Kn] This operand makes it possible to specify the types of plots produced by the macro-command. These plots summarise the results of the simulations run under the current factor keyword. A default list is proposed. However, it is possible to produce any plot by giving the desired combinations of components existing in l_graphique, of the form: ABSCISSA-ORDINATE. The dash «-» separates the component requested on the abscissa from the one requested on the ordinate. Example : l_graphique = ('P-Q', 'EPS_AXI-Q', 'INST-EPS_VOL', 'INST-V23') The non-predefined component V23 (corresponding to the plastic volumetric strain of the Hujeux constitutive law R7.01.23) must be declared in NOM_CMP ( § 3.4.6 ) in order to be taken into account. Otherwise, the requested plot is not produced. As for the predefined components, the complete list of which is given in § 3.4.1 , they will be displayed, where relevant, with the sign convention of geomechanics, that is with positive values in compression. Furthermore, all the components requested for the construction of the plots will be displayed in the output tables ( § 3.4.4 ). The files containing these plots are written in xmgrace format in one and the same directory specified by the user (type repe as a result in astk), and are named as follows: 'prefix'_'test_name'_'occurrence_number'_'abscissa-ordinate'.agr A prefix may be added to the name of the output file by means of the optional keyword: ◊PREFIXE_FICHIER= prefix [Kn] 3.4.6 Operand NOM_CMP ◊NOM_CMP= l_composante [l_Kn] liste des composantes non-prédéfinies demandées en sortie. Il s'agit de toutes les composantes existantes contenues dans les champs SIGM, EPSI et VARI produits par le calcul. Ces composantes non-prédéfinies seront produites avec la convention de signe par défaut, c'est-à-dire avec des valeurs négatives en compression. Les composantes non existantes sont ignorées. 3.4.7 Operand TABLE_REF ◊ TABLE_REF = l_tabref [l_table] This operand makes it possible to supply reference curves (for example experimental ones), tabulated and stored in the form of tables, in order to superimpose them on the curves coming from the simulations run under the current factor keyword. These reference curves are then included in the files produced by the keyword GRAPHIQUE. Each table contained in the list TABLE_REF must be created beforehand by means of the operator CREA_TABLE U4.33.02, and formatted as follows: tabref = CREA_TABLE( LISTE = ( _F(PARA = 'TYPE', LISTE_K = [typgraph,]), _F(PARA = 'LEGENDE', LISTE_K = [malegend,]), _F(PARA = 'ABSCISSE', LISTE_R = l_absc), _F(PARA = 'ORDONNEE', LISTE_R = l_ordo),),); with: - typgraph a character string whose value must belong to the list of default values of the keyword GRAPHIQUE. This value makes it possible to identify the type of plot (and therefore the file) to which the reference curve must be added. - malegend a character string which contains the legend associated with the reference curve - l_absc and l_ordo are Python lists of reals containing respectively the abscissae and the ordinates of the points of the reference curve. These lists must therefore have the same cardinality 3.4.8 Operands COULEUR, MARQUEUR, STYLE ◊ COULEUR= l_couleur [l_I] ◊MARQUEUR= l_marqueur [l_I] ◊STYLE = l_style [l_I] These operands accept a list of integers making it possible to define respectively the colour, the marker type and the style of the curves displayed in the plots. The information coded by each integer is given in the XMGRACE documentation U2.51.01. The length of the list must be equal to that of PRES_CONF. 3.5 Keyword ESSAI_TRIA_ND_M_D This repeatable factor keyword makes it possible to carry out a series of simulations of the same monotonic undrained triaxial test at imposed strain (total saturation is assumed), for which the loading parameters are varied (confining pressure and imposed axial strain), to post-process the results obtained and to write them in the form of plots (in xmgrace format) and/or tables. 3.5.1 Sign convention for the inputs and the outputs The sign convention of geomechanics applies to the input parameters in imposed stresses or strains, that is, the values are positive in compression. This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables, the complete list of which is as follows: - INST: time instant - EPS_AXI: axial strain - EPS_LAT: lateral strain - EPS_VOL: volumetric strain - SIG_AXI: axial effective stress - SIG_LAT: lateral effective stress - P: mean effective stress - Q: stress deviator - PRE_EAU: pore pressure On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.5.7 ). 3.5.2 Operands PRES_CONF, EPSI_IMPOSE, NB_INST ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ EPSI_IMPOSE = l_epsi_impo [l_R] ◊NB_INST = | 100 [DEFAUT] | nbinst [I] Same as in § 3.4.2 . 3.5.3 Operand BIOT_COEF ◊BIOT_COEF = | 1 [DEFAUT] | biot [R] Value of the Biot coefficient. 3.5.4 Operand KZERO ◊KZERO = | 1 [DEFAUT] Same as in § 3.4.3 . 3.5.5 Operand TABLE_RESU ◊TABLE_RESU= l_tabres [l_CO] Same as in § 3.4.4 . 3.5.6 Operand GRAPHIQUE, PREFIXE_FICHIER ◊GRAPHIQUE = |('P-Q', 'EPS_AXI-Q', 'EPS_AXI-PRE_EAU') [DEFAUT] | l_graphique [l_Kn] ◊PREFIXE_FICHIER = préfixe [Kn] Same as in § 3.4.5 . 3.5.7 Operand NOM_CMP ◊NOM_CMP= l_composante [l_Kn] Same as in § 3.4.6 . 3.5.8 Operand TABLE_REF ◊ TABLE_REF = l_tabref [l_table] Same as in § 3.4.7 . 3.5.9 Operands COULEUR, MARQUEUR, STYLE ◊ COULEUR= l_couleur [l_I] ◊MARQUEUR= l_marqueur [l_I] ◊STYLE = l_style [l_I] Same as in § 3.4.8 . 3.6 Keyword ESSAI_CISA_DR_C_D This repeatable factor keyword makes it possible to carry out a series of simulations of the same drained cyclic shear test at imposed shear strain, for which the loading parameters are varied (confining pressure, shear-strain amplitude and number of cycles), to post-process the results obtained and to write them in the form of plots (in xmgrace format) and/or tables. 3.6.1 Sign convention for the inputs and the outputs The sign convention of geomechanics applies to the input parameters in imposed stresses or strains, that is, the values are positive in compression. This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables. On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.6.7 ). In this test, one distinguishes the predefined level-2 output variables, which correspond to the variables produced by the test, the complete list of which is as follows: - INST: time instant - GAMMA: shear strain \gamma =2{{\varepsilon}}_{xy} - SIG_XY: shear stress And the predefined level-1 output variables, which correspond to curves whose points represent the result of a test (for example the curve \frac{G}{{G}_{\max}}-\gamma ). The complete list of the level-1 variables is as follows: - G_SUR_GMAX: \frac{G}{{G}_{\max}} - DAMPING: hysteretic damping \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} 3.6.2 Operands PRES_CONF, GAMMA_IMPOSE, NB_CYCLE, NB_INST, TYPE_CHARGE ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ GAMMA_IMPOSE = l_gamma_impo [l_R] ♦ NB_CYCLE = nbcyc [I] ◊ NB_INST = | 25 [DEFAUT] |nbinst [I] ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = | 'SINUSOIDAL' [DEFAUT] |'TRIANGULAIRE' [Kn] These operands make it possible to define the loading of each of the simulations to be run under the current factor keyword, as well as its discretisation. Their meaning is summarised in the figure and detailed below: - PRES_CONF makes it possible to define the list of confining pressures (strictly positive) that will be maintained during each test; - GAMMA_IMPOSE makes it possible to define the list of the amplitudes (strictly positive) of the shear strain \gamma =2{\epsilon}_{xy} of the imposed cyclic loading; - NB_CYCLE corresponds to the number of cycles, fixed for all the simulations. - NB_INST makes it possible to define the time discretisation of the loading, and corresponds to the number of loading steps per quarter-cycle - TYPE_CHARGE indicates the type of loading requested: sinusoidal or triangular; For each confining pressure PRES_CONF, as many simulations are carried out as there are entries in the list GAMMA_IMPOSE. Unlike the tests TRIA_DR_M_D and TRIA_ND_M_D (see respectively § 3.4 and § 3.5 ), these lists are not in one-to-one correspondence and there are in total: \mathit{card}(\text{PRES\_CONF})\times \mathit{card}(\text{GAMMA\_IMPOSE}) simulations run. Figure 3.6.2-a : discretisation and shape of the loading of triangular type for the keyword ESSAI_CISA_DR_C_D for 3 loading cycles 3.6.3 Operand GAMMA_ELAS ◊GAMMA_ELAS = | 1.E-7 [DEFAUT] |gamma_elas [R] For each confining pressure, the maximum secant shear modulus (that is, of the intact material) is determined by simulating an imposed shear-strain ramp (in terms of distortion) whose final value is GAMMA_ELAS. This value must be such that the material remains in its elasticity domain (linear or not, according to the constitutive relation used). GAMMA_ELAS is equal to 1.E-7 by default, and any value supplied by the user must be smaller than it. If the value supplied does not make it possible to remain in the elasticity domain, the code stops with a fatal error. 3.6.4 Operand KZERO ◊KZERO = | 1 [DEFAUT] Same as in § 3.4.3 . 3.6.5 Operand TABLE_RESU ◊TABLE_RESU= l_tabres [l_CO] This optional operand makes it possible to give the list of the names of the concepts produced by the macro-command, which will then be of type [table]. The size of this list must satisfy: \mathit{card}(\text{TABLE\_RESU})=\mathit{card}(\text{PRES\_CONF})+1 Indeed, each table produced gathers the raw results of all the simulations run for one and the same confining pressure (PRES_CONF), in which each simulation corresponds to a bundle of contiguous columns whose titles are all indexed by the same integer (index of the value considered in the list GAMMA_IMPOSE). An additional table summarising the post-processing carried out at the end of all the simulations is also produced. This table contains, for each confining pressure (PRES_CONF), the values of the normalised secant shear modulus \frac{G}{{G}_{max}} and of the hysteretic damping ratio \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} set against the imposed distortion amplitudes (GAMMA_IMPOSE). The hysteretic damping \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} for the last simulated cycle is computed according to Kohusho [] as follows (Figure ): - \Delta W={\int}_{C}\delta {\sigma}_{xy}\delta \gamma the area of the last hysteresis loop; - W=\Delta {\sigma}_{xy}\Delta \gamma the associated elastic energy This table corresponds to the concept name given in the last position in the list TABLE_RESU. This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables. On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.7.9 ). In this test, one distinguishes the predefined level-2 output variables, which correspond to the variables produced by the test, the complete list of which is as follows: - INST: time instant - EPS_AXI: axial strain - EPS_LAT: lateral strain - EPS_VOL: volumetric strain - SIG_AXI: axial effective stress - SIG_LAT: lateral effective stress - P: mean effective stress - Q: stress deviator - PRE_EAU: pore pressure - RU: pore-pressure coefficient equal to {r}_{u}=\frac{3}{1+2{K}_{0}}\frac{\Delta {u}_{w}}{\sigma {'}_{v,0}} And the predefined level-1 output variables, which correspond to curves whose points represent the result of a test (for example the curve \mathit{CRR}-{N}_{\mathit{cyc}} ). The complete list of the level-1 variables is as follows: - NCYCL: number of loading cycles to liquefaction - DSIGM: maximum imposed stress normalised by the initial mean effective stress \mathit{DSIGM}=\mathit{CRR}=\frac{{Q}_{\max}}{P{'}_{0}} 3.7.2 Operands PRES_CONF, SIGM_IMPOSE, NB_CYCLE, NB_INST, NB_INST_MONO, TYPE_CHARGE ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ SIGM_IMPOSE = l_sigma_impo [l_R] ♦ NB_CYCLE = nbcyc [I] ◊NB_INST = | 25 [DEFAUT] | nbinst [I] ◊NB_INST_MONO= | 400 [DEFAUT] | nbinst_mono [I] ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = | 'SINUSOIDAL' [DEFAUT] |'TRIANGULAIRE' [Kn] These operands make it possible to define the loading of each of the simulations to be run under the current factor keyword, as well as its discretisation. Their meaning is summarised in the figure and detailed below: - PRES_CONF makes it possible to define the list of confining pressures (strictly positive) that will be maintained during each test; - SIGM_IMPOSE makes it possible to define the list of the amplitudes of axial effective stress of the imposed cyclic loading (with PRES_CONF the mean stress). A strictly positive value indicates a first loading in compression, a strictly negative value a first loading in extension; - NB_CYCLE corresponds to the number of cycles, fixed for all the simulations; - NB_INST makes it possible to define the time discretisation of the loading, and corresponds to the number of loading steps per quarter-cycle; - NB_INST_MONO makes it possible to define the time discretisation of the monotonic loadings at imposed strain after detection of an instability, and corresponds to the number of loading steps per quarter-cycle. The number of time instants must be large enough (>100) for a sufficiently accurate detection of the attainment of the force target; - TYPE_CHARGE indicates the type of loading requested: sinusoidal or triangular; For each confining pressure PRES_CONF, as many simulations are carried out as there are entries in the list SIGM_IMPOSE. Unlike the tests TRIA_DR_M_D and TRIA_ND_M_D (see respectively § 3.4 and § 3.5 ), these lists are not in one-to-one correspondence and there are in total: \mathit{card}(\text{PRES\_CONF})\times \mathit{card}(\text{SIGM\_IMPOSE}) simulations run. Figure 3.7.2-a: discretisation and shape of the triangular loading for the keyword ESSAI_TRIA_ND_C_D for 3 loading cycles Note: For loose sands, stress control of the test raises difficulties when crossing the two instability lines, shown in blue on the Figure . Indeed, imposing a maximum-stress target greater than the maximum admissible stress on the instability line leads either to divergence or to a false solution (a sudden stress jump, visible on the Figure ). Indeed, the instability line represents the locus of all the admissible stress maxima of a monotonic TRIA_ND_M_D test for various values of the initial consolidation (black curve). The problem does not arise for a dense sand, because there is no stress maximum in that case, as can be seen on the black curve of the Figure . For this test, there is therefore an automatic procedure for handling unstable situations. It consists in detecting the instability and in continuing the test under strain control. The detection criteria are the following: non-convergence of the analysis \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta P} 10 One continues over the remaining number of cycles by a sequence of monotonic strain-controlled TRIA_ND_M_D tests, at the rate of two tests per cycle ( \pm {{\varepsilon}}_{max} in order to reach \pm {\sigma}_{max} ). The maximum strain target {{\varepsilon}}_{max} imposed is 4%, or 12% if the previous target was insufficient. The list of time instants for these TRIA_ND_M_D tests runs from 0 to 100 seconds with a time step of 0.2 seconds (or of 0.1 seconds if the target is {{\varepsilon}}_{max}=12\text{\%} ). The chaining of one strain-controlled TRIA_ND_M_D test to the next is carried out by a restart of the analysis from the last time instant at which the stress target \pm {\sigma}_{max} is reached. On the Figure , one shows, on an example of loose sand (test case comp012c), the solution obtained with or without the instability-handling procedure. Figure 3.7.2-c : Result of the tests TRIA_ND_M_D (black) and TRIA_ND_C_F (pink) for a loose sand. The failure state is represented by the purple line, and the instability lines are blue. The order of the criteria must correspond to the order of the numerical values. If several criteria are chosen, liquefaction is stipulated to occur when all the criteria have been reached successively. The analysis is stopped at the last cycle at which the last criterion is reached, if that is possible, if ARRET_LIQUEFACTION = 'OUI'. If ARRET_LIQUEFACTION = 'NON', the test is continued up to the number of cycles given in NB_CYCLE. This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables. On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.8.7 ). In this test, one distinguishes the predefined level-2 output variables, which correspond to the variables produced by the test, the complete list of which is as follows: - INST: time instant - EPS_AXI: axial strain - EPS_LAT: lateral strain - EPS_VOL: volumetric strain - SIG_AXI: axial effective stress - SIG_LAT: lateral effective stress - P: mean effective stress - Q: stress deviator And the predefined level-1 output variables, which correspond to curves whose points represent the result of a test (for example the curve \frac{E\text{ }}{E{\text{ }}_{\max}}-\Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v} ). The complete list of the level-1 variables is as follows: - E_SUR_EMAX: \frac{E\text{ }}{E{\text{ }}_{\max}} with E\text{ }=\frac{|\Delta ({\sigma}_{v}-{\sigma}_{h})|}{|\Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}|} the apparent modulus of the test; - DAMPING: hysteretic damping \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} 3.8.2 Operands PRES_CONF, EPSI_MAXI, EPSI_MINI, NB_CYCLE, NB_INST ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ EPSI_MAXI = l_epsi_maxi_impo [l_R] ♦ EPSI_MINI = l_epsi_mini_impo [l_R] ♦ NB_CYCLE = nbcyc [I] ◊ NB_INST = | 25 [DEFAUT] |nbinst [I] ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = | 'SINUSOIDAL' [DEFAUT] These operands make it possible to define the loading of each of the simulations to be run under the current factor keyword, as well as its discretisation. Their meaning is summarised in the figure and detailed below: - PRES_CONF makes it possible to define the list of confining pressures (strictly positive) that will be maintained during each test; - EPSI_MAXI and EPSI_MINI make it possible to define the list of the maximum and minimum axial strains, respectively, of the imposed cyclic loading. The cardinality of EPSI_MAXI must be equal to that of EPSI_MINI. The condition \Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}=\mathit{EPSI}\text{\_}\mathit{MAXI}–\mathit{EPSI}\text{\_}\mathit{MINI}>0 must be satisfied term by term; - NB_CYCLE corresponds to the number of cycles, fixed for all the simulations. - NB_INST makes it possible to define the time discretisation of the loading, and corresponds to the number of loading steps per quarter-cycle - TYPE_CHARGE indicates the type of loading requested: sinusoidal or triangular; For each confining pressure PRES_CONF, as many simulations are carried out as there are entries in the list GAMMA_IMPOSE. Unlike the tests TRIA_DR_M_D and TRIA_ND_M_D (see respectively § 3.4 and § 3.5 ), these lists are not in one-to-one correspondence and there are in total: \mathit{card}(\text{PRES\_CONF})\times \mathit{card}(\text{EPSI\_MAXI}) simulations run. This value must be such that the material remains in its elasticity domain (linear or not, according to the constitutive relation used). EPSI_ELAS is equal to 1.E-7 by default, and any value supplied by the user must be smaller than it. If the value supplied does not make it possible to remain in the elasticity domain, the code stops with a fatal error. 3.8.4 Operand KZERO ◊KZERO = | 1 [DEFAUT] Same as in § 3.4.3 . 3.8.5 Operand TABLE_RESU ◊TABLE_RESU = l_tabres [l_CO] This optional operand makes it possible to give the list of the names of the concepts produced by the macro-command, which will then be of type [table]. An additional table summarising the post-processing carried out at the end of all the simulations is also produced. This table contains, for each confining pressure (PRES_CONF), the values of: - normalised equivalent cyclic apparent modulus \frac{E\text{ }}{E{\text{ }}_{\max}} for the last simulated cycle, set against the imposed strain amplitudes (EPSI_MAXI). E\text{ } and E{\text{ }}_{max} are computed as follows: E\text{ }=\frac{|\Delta ({\sigma}_{v}-{\sigma}_{h})|}{|\Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}|} with \Delta \sigma ={\sigma}_{max}-{\sigma}_{min} and \Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}={{\varepsilon}}_{v,max}-{{\varepsilon}}_{v,min} ; - the hysteretic damping \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} for the last simulated cycle, set against the imposed strain amplitudes (EPSI_MAXI). This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables. On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.9.10 ). In this test, one distinguishes the predefined level-2 output variables, which correspond to the variables produced by the test, the complete list of which is as follows: - INST: time instant - EPS_AXI: axial strain - EPS_LAT: lateral strain - EPS_VOL: volumetric strain - SIG_AXI: axial effective stress - SIG_LAT: lateral effective stress - P: mean effective stress - Q: stress deviator - PRE_EAU: pore pressure - RU: pore-pressure coefficient equal to {r}_{u}=\frac{3}{1+2{K}_{0}}\frac{\Delta {u}_{w}}{\sigma {'}_{v,0}} And the predefined level-1 output variables, which correspond to curves whose points represent the result of a test (for example the curve \mathit{CRR}-{N}_{\mathit{cyc}} ). The complete list of the level-1 variables is as follows: - NCYCL: number of loading cycles to liquefaction - DEPSI: imposed axial-strain amplitude \Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}=\text{EPSI\_MAX}-\text{EPSI\_MIN} - RU_MAX: maximum of RU - E_SUR_EMAX: \frac{E\text{ }}{E{\text{ }}_{\max}} with E\text{ }=\frac{|\Delta ({\sigma}_{v}-{\sigma}_{h})|}{|\Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}|} - DAMPING: hysteretic damping \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} 3.9.2 Operands PRES_CONF, EPSI_MAXI, EPSI_MINI, NB_CYCLE, NB_INST ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ EPSI_MAXI = l_epsi_maxi_impo [l_R] ♦ EPSI_MINI = l_epsi_mini_impo [l_R] ♦ NB_CYCLE = nbcyc [I] ◊ NB_INST = | 25 [DEFAUT] |nbinst [I] ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = | 'SINUSOIDAL' [DEFAUT] Same as in § 3.8.2 . 3.9.3 Operand EPSI_ELAS ◊EPSI_ELAS = | 1.E-7 [DEFAUT] |epsi_elas [R] Same as in § 3.9.3 . 3.9.4 Operand BIOT_COEF ◊BIOT_COEF = | 1 [DEFAUT] | biot [R] Value of the Biot coefficient. 3.9.5 Operand KZERO ◊KZERO = | 1 [DEFAUT] Same as in § 3.4.3 . 3.9.6 Operand UN_SUR_K ♦UN_SUR_K = unsurk [R] Value of the inverse of the compressibility modulus of water. 3.9.7 Operand RU_MAX ◊RU_MAX = | 0.8 [DEFAUT] Value of the liquefaction criterion in RU. 3.9.8 Operand TABLE_RESU ◊ TABLE_RESU = l_tabres, [l_CO] This optional operand makes it possible to give the list of the names of the concepts produced by the macro-command, which will then be of type [table]. The size of this list must satisfy: \mathit{card}(\text{TABLE\_RESU})=\mathit{card}(\text{PRES\_CONF})+1 Indeed, each table produced gathers the raw results of all the simulations run for one and the same confining pressure (PRES_CONF), in which each simulation corresponds to a bundle of contiguous columns whose titles are all indexed by the same integer (index of the value considered in the list EPSI_MAXI). An additional table summarising the post-processing carried out at the end of all the simulations is also produced. This table contains, for each confining pressure (PRES_CONF), the values of: - normalised equivalent cyclic apparent modulus \frac{E\text{ }}{E{\text{ }}_{\max}} for the last simulated cycle, set against the imposed strain amplitudes (EPSI_MAXI). E\text{ } and E{\text{ }}_{max} are computed as follows: E\text{ }=\frac{|\Delta ({\sigma}_{v}-{\sigma}_{h})|}{|\Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}|} with \Delta \sigma ={\sigma}_{max}-{\sigma}_{min} and \Delta {{\varepsilon}}_{v}={{\varepsilon}}_{v,max}-{{\varepsilon}}_{v,min} ; - the hysteretic damping \frac{\Delta W}{\pi W} for the last simulated cycle, set against the imposed strain amplitudes (EPSI_MAXI). W is computed as follows: \Delta W={\int}_{C}\delta ({\sigma}_{v}-{\sigma}_{h}).\delta ({{\varepsilon}}_{v}-{{\varepsilon}}_{h}) the area of the last hysteresis loop W=\Delta ({\sigma}_{v}-{\sigma}_{h}).\Delta ({{\varepsilon}}_{v}-{{\varepsilon}}_{h}) the associated elastic energy - number of cycles to liquefaction NCYCL This table corresponds to the concept name given in the last position in the list TABLE_RESU. 3.9.9 Operand GRAPHIQUE, PREFIXE_FICHIER ◊GRAPHIQUE = |('NCYCL-DEPSI', 'DEPSI-RU_MAX', 'DEPSI-E_SUR_EMAX', 'DEPSI-DAMPING', 'P-Q', 'EPS_AXI-EPS_VOL' 'EPS_AXI-Q', 'P-EPS_VOL', 'EPS_AXI-PRE_EAU', 'EPS_AXI-RU', 'P-PRE_EAU') [DEFAUT] | l_graphique [l_Kn] ◊PREFIXE_FICHIER= prefix [Kn] Same as in § 3.4.5, except that, unlike the level-2 plots, which may be arbitrary, the level-1 plots are to be selected from the list: 'NCYCL-DEPSI' 'DEPSI-RU_MAX' 'DEPSI-E_SUR_EMAX' 'DEPSI-DAMPING' 3.9.10 Operand NOM_CMP ◊NOM_CMP= l_composante [l_Kn] Same as in § 3.4.6 . 3.9.11 Operand TABLE_REF ◊ TABLE_REF = l_tabref [l_table] Same as in § 3.4.7 . 3.9.12 Operands COULEUR_NIV1, MARQUEUR_NIV1, STYLE_NIV1, COULEUR_NIV2, MARQUEUR_NIV2, STYLE_NIV2 ◊ COULEUR_NIV1= l_couleur_niv1 [l_I] ◊MARQUEUR_NIV1= l_marqueur_niv1 [l_I] ◊STYLE_NIV1= l_style_niv1 [l_I] ◊ COULEUR_NIV2= l_couleur_niv2 [l_I] ◊MARQUEUR_NIV2= l_marqueur_niv2 [l_I] ◊STYLE_NIV2= l_style_niv2 [l_I] Same as in § 3.4.8 . 3.10 Keyword ESSAI_OEDO_DR_C_F This repeatable factor keyword makes it possible to carry out a series of simulations of the same drained cyclic oedometric test at imposed force, for which the loading parameters are varied (initial isotropic consolidation pressure, amplitude of the imposed axial effective stress, and amplitude of the axial effective stress at the end of unloading), to post-process the results obtained and to write them in the form of plots (in xmgrace format) and/or tables. 3.10.1 Sign convention for the inputs and the outputs The sign convention of geomechanics applies to the input parameters in imposed stresses or strains, that is, the values are positive in compression. This convention likewise applies to the predefined output variables, the complete list of which for this test is as follows: - INST: time instant - EPS_VOL: volumetric strain - SIG_AXI: axial effective stress - SIG_LAT: lateral effective stress - P: mean effective stress On the other hand, this convention does not apply to the non-predefined variables requested as output in NOM_CMP(§ 3.10.6 ). 3.10.2 Operands PRES_CONF, SIGM_IMPOSE, SIGM_DECH, NB_CYCLE, NB_INST, TYPE_CHARGE ♦ PRES_CONF = l_sigma_conf [l_R] ♦ SIGM_IMPOSE = l_sigma_impo [l_R] ♦ SIGM_DECH = l_sigma_décharge [l_R] ♦ NB_CYCLE = nbcyc [I] ◊NB_INST = | 25 [DEFAUT] | nbinst [I] ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = | 'SINUSOIDAL' [DEFAUT] |'TRIANGULAIRE' [Kn] These operands make it possible to define the loading of each of the simulations to be run under the current factor keyword, as well as its discretisation. Their meaning is summarised in the figure and detailed below: - PRES_CONF makes it possible to define the list of the initial vertical consolidation pressures (strictly positive). The initial mean stress will therefore be equal to \frac{1+2{K}_{0}}{3}\times \text{PRES\_CONF} ; - SIGM_IMPOSE makes it possible to define the list of the imposed axial-stress values (strictly positive and greater than SIGM_DECH); - SIGM_DECH makes it possible to define the list of the (strictly positive) values of the unloading axial stress, fixed for all the loading cycles, at a given initial consolidation pressure. The lists PRES_CONF and SIGM_DECH must have the same cardinality; - NB_INST makes it possible to define the time discretisation of the loading, and corresponds to the number of loading steps per half-cycle; - TYPE_CHARGE indicates the type of loading requested: sinusoidal or triangular; For each initial consolidation pressure PRES_CONF, and each unloading stress SIGM_DECH, as many cycles are carried out as there are entries in the list SIGM_IMPOSE.
