u4.91.01 Procedure IMPR_RESU in the 'RESULTAT' and 'ASTER' formats u4.91.01 Procedure IMPR_RESU in the 'RESULTAT' and 'ASTER' formats 1 Purpose Write the mesh or the results of an analysis to a file in the 'RESULTAT' format, or the mesh in the 'ASTER' format. At present this procedure makes it possible to write, as one chooses: - a mesh, - fields at the nodes (of displacements, of temperatures, of eigenmodes, of static modes, …), - fields by element at the nodes or at the Gauss points (of stresses, of generalised forces, of internal variables…). The procedure IMPR_RESU also makes it possible to write a mesh and/or results to a file with a view, in particular, to their graphical visualisation (cf. documents U7.05.01 (format 'IDEAS'), U7.05.21 (format 'MED') and U7.05.32 (format 'GMSH')). For concepts of type resultat, one can print only part of the information, by selecting the fields and the order numbers that one wishes to exploit. For the printouts in the 'RESULTAT' format, it is possible to select the topological entities (node groups and mesh-cell groups) on which one wants to print the results. One can also reduce the number of pieces of information printed by requesting only the printout of certain components, of values lying in an interval chosen by the user or of extreme values. One can combine all the possibilities, for example in order to obtain the maximum value of a given component, on a particular topological entity and in an interval of values chosen by the user. The 'RESULTAT' format must not be used as a basis for storing or exchanging results; its format is not fixed. 2 Syntax IMPR_RESU( ◇ FORMAT = / "RESULTAT", / "IDEAS", / "ASTER", / "MED" (par défaut), / "GMSH", ◇ PROC0 = / "OUI", / "NON", # Si: not equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ◇ MODELE = modele, # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'RESULTAT') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'IDEAS') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 30), ◇ VERSION = / 4, / 5 (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'ASTER') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 26), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 80), ◇ VERSION_MED = / "3.3.1" (par défaut), / "4.0.0", / "4.1.0", ◇ FICHIER_UNIQUE = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'GMSH') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 37), ◇ VERSION = / 1.0, / 1.2 (par défaut), # Si: 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Typography in the IMPR_RESU documentation In order to understand the documentation of IMPR_RESU properly, one must note that the term 'RESULTAT' covers in Code_Aster three rather different notions: - a type of concept, - a type of file, - a write format. Indeed, on the one hand, one designates as a result the quantities produced by an Aster analysis operator producing several fields (evolutionary analysis, eigenmode analysis, etc...). These data (results) are contained in an Aster data structure of generic type called resultat. This generic type is subdivided into subtypes, for example mode_meca, evol_elas, etc., whose storage mode differs somewhat. A concept of type resultat has only one subtype. In the Aster documentation the names of the concept types are in lower-case Courier. On the other hand, the results intended for printout, in particular those coming from IMPR_RESU, are placed in a file designated as the RESULTAT file (associated with unit 8, type resu in astk). The write format associated with this file intended for printout is itself also named RESULTAT. In summary : | résultat | data coming from the solution of the system, | | --- | --- | | resultat | generic designation of the concept type (of the data structure) which contains the result, | | evol_ther mode_meca | name of the subtype of the result of type resultat, | | FICHIER | (without quotes) designation of the file which contains the results, independently of the format of its content, | | 'RESULTAT' | (with quotes) designation of the format ( Aster ) of the file which contains the results. | 4 Results that can be printed with IMPR_RESU The operator IMPR_RESU makes it possible to print various types of results according to the format chosen ( RESULTAT , MED , IDEAS , GMSH , etc.). The types of results handled depend on the write format, but always rest on a concept of generic type resultat (see Typography). The main results currently supported are the following: - Static or quasi-static results - EVOL_ELAS : evolutionary elastic analyses (time evolution of the fields), - STAT_NON_LINE : results of static non-linear analyses, - THER_NON_LINE : results of static non-linear thermal analyses, - MULT_ELAS : linear combinations of elastic fields. - Modal or harmonic results - MODE_MECA : results of a mechanical modal analysis, - MODE_THER : results of a thermal modal analysis, - DYNA_HARMO : results of a dynamic harmonic analysis, - ACOU_HARMO : results of a harmonic acoustic analysis. - Other types supported - EVOL_THER : transient thermal evolution, - EVOL_CHAR : parameterised evolution of characteristic type, - DYNA_NON_LINE : non-linear dynamic results, - SIMU_POINT_MAT : results of a simulation at the material point, - REST_GLOBALE : global results coming from the recovery of quantities (grandeurs), - CHAM_GD : fields of computed quantities (grandeurs) independently of a RESULTAT concept. The results of type _GENE (for example MODE_MECA_GENE or DYNA_HARMO_GENE ) cannot be printed with IMPR_RESU. They must be handled with the aid of the operator IMPR_GENE, specifically designed for generalised results. In summary: | Type of result | Formats supported | | --- | --- | | EVOL_ELAS | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | STAT_NON_LINE | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | THER_NON_LINE | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | MULT_ELAS | RESULTAT, MED ( + TYPE_NOM=NOM_CAS ), IDEAS, GMSH | | MODE_MECA | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | MODE_THER | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | DYNA_HARMO | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH ( PARTIE mandatory in MED/GMSH ) | | ACOU_HARMO | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH ( PARTIE mandatory in MED/GMSH ) | | EVOL_THER | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | EVOL_CHAR | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | DYNA_NON_LINE | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | SIMU_POINT_MAT | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | REST_GLOBALE | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | CHAM_GD | RESULTAT, MED, IDEAS, GMSH | | _GENE | (Not supported) → use IMPR_GENE [U4.91.02] | 5 Operands FORMAT, PROC0, UNITE and INFO The procedure IMPR_RESU makes it possible to write a mesh and/or result values in various formats with a view, in particular, to a graphical visualisation U7.05.01, U7.05.11, U7.05.21 and U7.05.31. The operand FORMAT makes it possible to specify the print format of a result. The default format is 'MED' ( cf. U7.05.21). It makes it possible to print the mesh and/or the results in the form of a listing. The operand PROC0, whose default value is 'OUI', makes it possible to restrict the printout to the processor of rank 0. If one assigns it the value 'NON', the printouts will be carried out on all the processors. One specifies in which file the data will be written via the keyword UNITE (cf. command DEFI_FICHIER). By default, one uses the file of logical unit 8 in the 'RESULTAT' format and 26 in the 'ASTER' format. The keyword INFO, when it is equal to 2, makes it possible to obtain information on the printouts carried out by the command. 6 Keyword RESU This factor keyword makes it possible to specify the results to be printed and the format according to which one wants to print them. 7 Operands CHAM_GD and RESULTAT The values of the computed fields are stored in data structures called fields of quantities (grandeurs). These fields of quantities (grandeurs) may be directly accessible (concept cham_gd) or be found in a data structure grouping several fields of quantities (grandeurs) (concept resultat). - a field of a quantity (grandeur) is a data structure which makes it possible to store fields defined at the nodes (cham_no_ ) or fields defined by element (cham_elem_ ). For the fields by element, one distinguishes the fields defined at the nodes of the elements and the fields defined at the Gauss points of the elements, - a result concept is composed of one or more fields of quantities (grandeurs). For example, at each analysis step one stores in the resultat data structure the field of the quantity (grandeur) displacement. This structure is therefore indexed by a matrix structure of order 2, one index of which is, for example, the list of the analysis time instants and the other the set of the computed fields (displacements, stresses, strains, ...). One accesses in this case a field of a quantity (grandeur) by specifying the value of an access variable (order number, time instant, frequency, mode number ...) and a field name ('DEPL', 'SIGM_ELNO', ...). There exist several types of result concept: evol_elas, evol_noli, mode_meca, .... To each one corresponds a list of fields and a list of licit access variables. On the other hand, with a result concept is also associated a certain number of complementary results (for example the generalised mass or the modal participation factors in a modal analysis (result concept of type mode_meca)), different for each value of the access variable. These complementary results are called parameters. Given the resultat data structure, one easily understands that the printout possibilities available are those of the fields of quantities (grandeurs), supplemented by specific possibilities: - information on the data structure (for example: list of the access variables, list of the fields actually computed, ...), - selective access to a field of a quantity (grandeur) (for example, printout of the displacement field at the time instant t=15. ), - printout of the parameter values. The operand RESULTAT makes it possible to print the fields contained in a result concept. One can for example choose to print only certain fields (see the following keyword: NOM_CHAM) on certain components of certain nodes (cf. NOEUD_CMP). 8 Extraction of a field of a quantity (grandeur) 8.1 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM Cf. document U4.71.00. 8.2 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / NOEUD_CMP / NOM_CAS / ANGLE / PRECISION / CRITERE Cf. document U4.71.00. 9 Parameters 9.1 Operand TOUT_PARA This keyword indicates whether or not one wants to print all the values of the parameters attached to the concept of type resultat. Example: IMPR_RESU(RESU=_F(RESULTAT=resu, TOUT_PARA='OUI', NUME_ORDRE=3)) One prints in the RESULTAT file the values of all the parameters, but only for the third analysis step of a resultat concept of type mode_meca : Printout of the parameters of the concept resu for order number 3: NOM_MODE 3 FREQ 1.09787E+4 OMEGA2 4.75843E+09 AMOR_REDUIT 0.00000E+00 ERREUR 2.76853E-10 MASS_GENE 1.50009E-07 RIGI_GENE 7.13806E+02 ........ ........ NORME SANS_CMP: LAGR 9.2 Operand NOM_PARA This keyword makes it possible to choose a list of symbolic parameter names from among all the possible ones. The keywords TOUT_PARA and NOM_PARA cannot be used simultaneously. Example: IMPR_RESU(RESU=_F(RESULTAT=resu, NOM_PARA=('NORME',), NUME_ORDRE=3)) One prints in the RESULTAT file the value of the parameter of name NORME , but only for the third analysis step of a resultat concept of type mode_meca : Printout of the parameters of the concept resu for order number 3: NORME SANS_CMP: LAGR 9.3 Operand FORM_TABL This keyword makes it possible to choose the print format of the parameter values. Either in the form of a table each line of which is limited to 80 characters ( FORM_TABL='OUI' ), or in the form of a table each line of which can reach 2000 characters ( FORM_TABL='EXCEL' ), or in the form of a list (one parameter per line) ( FORM_TABL='NON' ). By default, the parameters are printed in the form of a table. Example: 1. FORM_TABL = 'OUI' NUME_ORDRE NUME_MODE ITER_QR ITER_BATHE FREQ OMEGA2 AMOR_REDUIT MASS_GENE RIGI_GENE AMOR_GENE MASS_EFFE_DY MASS_EFFE_DZ FACT_PARTICI_DX FACT_PARTICI_DZ MASS_EFFE_UN_DX MASS_EFFE_UN_DY NORME METHODE 2. FORM_TABL = 'EXCEL' NUME_ORDRE NUME_MODE ITER_QR ITER_BATHE 10 Selection on the components Another way of reducing the volume of the printouts is to print only the values of certain components (for example only the displacement along the axis X: component DX). Note: the selection of the components does not work for the fields with sub-points. 10.1 Operand TOUT_CMP This keyword makes it possible to indicate that one wishes to print all the components of the field. 10.2 Operand NOM_CMP This keyword makes it possible to choose the list of the components of the cham_gd or of all the fields of the result concept that one wishes to print. The keywords TOUT_CMP and NOM_CMP cannot be used simultaneously. These components are described in the specific documentation of the elements. 11 Selection of the topological entities In order to reduce the volume of the printouts, it is sometimes necessary to print only part of the result. To do this one can print a field at the nodes only at certain nodes, or a field by element only on certain elements. Note: the selection of the topological entities does not work for the fields with sub-points. 11.1 Operand TOUT This keyword indicates that one wishes to print the field over the whole structure (all the nodes for a field at the nodes, all the elements for a field by element). 11.2 Operand GROUP_NO This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the node groups on which one wishes to print a cham_no. If this keyword is used in the case of the printout of a cham_elem, it is ignored, and the cham_elem is printed on all the mesh cells, specified elsewhere. 11.3 Operand GROUP_MA This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the mesh-cell groups on which one wishes to print a cham_elem. For a cham_no, it makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes, vertices of the mesh cells, at which one wishes to print the cham_no. 12 Selection on the values It is also of interest to print only the extreme values of all or certain components, over all or part of the structure. 12.1 Operand VALE_MAX This keyword indicates that one wishes to print the maximum value of each component of the field, possibly in a given interval specified by the arguments BORNE_SUP and/or BORNE_INF. 12.2 Operand VALE_MIN This keyword indicates that one wishes to print the minimum value of each component of the field, possibly in a given interval specified by the arguments BORNE_SUP and/or BORNE_INF. 12.3 Operand BORNE_SUP This keyword indicates the upper bound of the interval over which one wishes to print the field. One prints all the values of the field lower than this upper bound. 12.4 Operand BORNE_INF This keyword indicates the lower bound of the interval over which one wishes to print the field. One prints the values of the field greater than this lower bound. 13 Printout of the coordinates: operand IMPR_COOR This keyword makes it possible to specify whether one wishes to print the coordinates of a node when writing a cham_no in the 'RESULTAT' format. 14 Operand FORMAT_R ◊ FORMAT_R = / FORM, / ’1PE21.14’ [DEFAUT] Makes it possible to specify the write format of the real values in the 'RESULTAT' format. Note: the choice of the write format of the real values does not work for the fields with sub-points. 15 Operand PARTIE > ◊ PARTIE = / ‘REEL’, / ‘IMAG’, / ‘MODULE’, / ‘PHASE’, Makes it possible to specify the print format of the complex numbers. If one specifies nothing, one will print the complex number. Otherwise one can print the real part (PARTIE='REEL'), the imaginary part (PARTIE='IMAG'), the modulus (PARTIE='MODULE') or the phase (PARTIE='PHASE'). 16 Note concerning the fields with sub-points In Aster , there exist cham_elem with sub-points (both for cham_elem at the nodes and for cham_elem at the Gauss points). In the 'RESULTAT' format, IMPR_RESU allows the printout of the cham_elem with sub-points. If the same cham_elem has sub-points on certain mesh cells and not on others, the printout of the cham_elem will be done in two stages: - first the printout of the cham_elem on all the mesh cells on which there are no sub-points, - then the printout of the cham_elem on all the mesh cells on which there are sub-points. A specific format is used for each of these printouts. The printout of the fields with sub-points is "basic": one systematically prints all the geometric entities, all the components and all the sub-points (one line per sub-point). The real numbers are always printed with 10 significant digits. A trick for printing more significant digits for a field with sub-points consists in calling the command POST_CHAMP in order to extract the field on a particular sub-point and then in printing the new data structure with the keyword FORMAT_R. 17 Printout of the mesh: operands MAILLAGE / MODELE This argument makes it possible to print the mesh with FORMAT='ASTER' or 'RESULTAT'. One then finds the format used for LIRE_MAILLAGE U4.21.01 and defined in U3.01.00. By default, one prints the whole mesh. The concept of type modele is optional in the majority of the printouts. However, it can be used in the case of the printout of a mesh in the 'ASTER' or 'RESULTAT' formats, in order to print only the part of the mesh whose mesh cells are assigned in the model. If one chooses the 'ASTER' format, the mesh is written in a file of type .mail which can then be re-read by LIRE_MAILLAGE. If one chooses the 'RESULTAT' format, the mesh is written, by default, in the .resu file and cannot be re-read by LIRE_MAILLAGE as it stands, because the .resu file also contains titles, subtitles and possibly other information. 18 Operand SOUS_TITRE This argument makes it possible to print a comment subtitle; for more details consult the document U4.03.01. The default SOUS_TITRE is: - for a cham_gd - for a cham_no SOUS_TITRE = (’CHAMP AUX NOEUDS’ ) - for a cham_elem SOUS_TITRE = (’CHAMP PAR ELEMENT &LOC(cham_elem)’ ) Example: "CHAMP PAR ELEMENT AUX POINTS DE GAUSS" - for a resultat - for a cham_no SOUS_TITRE = ( ’CHAMP AUX NOEUDS DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE &NOM_SYMB(Resultat cham_no)&RL NUMERO D’’ORDRE &NUM_ORDRE(Resultat cham_no) &ACCES(Resultat cham_no) ’) Example of printout: CHAMP AUX NOEUDS DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE DEPL NUMERO D’ORDRE 2 NUME_MODE 3 FREQ 5.52739E+00 - for a cham_elem SOUS_TITRE = ( ’CHAMP PAR ELEMENT &LOC(Resultat cham_elem) DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE &NOM_SYMB(Resultat cham_elem)&RL NUMERO D’’ORDRE &NUM_ORDRE(Resultat cham_elem) &ACCES(Resultat cham_elem) ’) Example of printout: CHAMP PAR ELEMENT AUX NOEUDS DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE EPSI_ELNO NUMERO D’ORDRE 1 INST 0.00000E+00

u4.91.02 Procedure IMPR_GENE u4.91.02 Procedure IMPR_GENE 1 Purpose Write the result of a dynamic analysis in generalised variables to a file, in the 'RESULTAT' format. INFO_CMP_GENE = / "OUI", / "NON", ◇ INFO_GENE = / "OUI", / "NON", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Keyword GENE This factor keyword makes it possible to specify the results to be printed. At least one factor block of the keyword is necessary for each result that one wishes to print. 4 Operand RESU_GENE This keyword makes it possible to specify the user name of the concept of type tran_gene, vect_asse_gene, harm_gene or mode_gene to be printed. 5 Access variables if the concept is of type vect_asse_gene The keyword TOUT_CMP_GENE indicates that one wants or does not want to print the fields for all the numbers of generalised components (except those which correspond to Lagrange degrees of freedom). The keyword NUME_CMP_GENE indicates that one wants to print the fields which correspond to a list of numbers of generalised components. 6 Access variables if the concept is of type mode_gene or harm_gene 6.1 Extraction of a result field: operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM The keyword TOUT_CHAM indicates that one wants to print all the fields actually computed. The keyword NOM_CHAM makes it possible to choose a list of symbolic field names from among all the possible ones. 6.2 Extraction of a parameter: operands TOUT_PARA / NOM_PARA The keyword TOUT_PARA indicates that one wants or does not want to print all the values of the parameters attached to the concept considered. The keyword NOM_PARA makes it possible to choose a list of symbolic parameter names from among all the possible ones. These keywords are available only for the concept of type mode_gene. 6.3 Operands TOUT_CMP_GENE / NUME_CMP_GENE The keyword TOUT_CMP_GENE indicates that one wants to print the fields for all the numbers of generalised components (except those which correspond to Lagrange degrees of freedom). The keyword NUME_CMP_GENE indicates that one wants to print the fields which correspond to a list of numbers of generalised components. 6.4 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE The keyword TOUT_ORDRE indicates that one wants to print the fields for all the order numbers. The keywords NUME_ORDRE and LIST_ORDRE make it possible to print only the fields corresponding to a list of order numbers lordre or lent defined by DEFI_LIST_ENTI U4.34.02 (lent is therefore a concept of type listis). 6.5 Operands TOUT_MODE / NUME_MODE The keyword TOUT_MODE indicates that one wants to print the fields for all the mode numbers. The keyword NUME_MODE indicates that one wants to print the fields corresponding to a list of mode numbers lmode. These numbers are those assigned by the analysis algorithm. This keyword can be used only for a concept of type mode_gene. 6.6 Operands FREQ / LIST_FREQ The keyword FREQ indicates that one wants to print the fields corresponding to a list of frequencies lfreq. The keyword LIST_FREQ indicates that one wants to print the fields corresponding to a list of frequencies lreel, defined by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01 (lreel is therefore a concept of type listr8). This keyword can be used for a concept of type harm_gene, and possibly mode_gene. 6.7 Operands CRITERE / PRECISION The keyword PRECISION indicates with what precision one must carry out the search for the analysis frequency. The keyword CRITERE indicates with what type of precision interval the search for the interpolation frequency must be carried out: | 'ABSOLU': | search interval [fr-prec, fr+prec] | | --- | --- | | 'RELATIF': | search interval [(1-prec)fr, (1+prec)fr] | 7 Access variables if the concept is of type tran_gene 7.1 Extraction of a result field - Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM See [§6.1]. - Operands TOUT_CMP_GENE / NUME_CMP_GENE See [§6.3] - Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE See [§6.4]. 7.2 Operands INST / LIST_INST / CRITERE / PRECISION The keyword INST indicates that one wants to print the fields corresponding to a list of time instants linst. The keyword LIST_INST indicates that one wants to print the fields corresponding to a list of time instants lreel, defined by the operator DEFI_LIST_REEL U4.34.01 (lreel is therefore a concept of type listr8). For CRITERE / PRECISION see [§6.7] (replacing frequency by time instant). 8 Parameters for the printout of the results 8.1 Operand SOUS_TITRE This argument makes it possible to print a comment title. 8.2 Operand FORMAT Print format of the results in the output file. For the moment only the RESULTAT format is available. 8.3 Operand INFO_GENE When printing a generalised concept, one may have forgotten the exact content of the data structure. The operand INFO_GENE makes it possible to print this content (number of order numbers, list of the symbolic names of the fields actually computed, list of the symbolic names of the parameters actually computed, ...). 8.4 Extraction of a genealogy of the generalised model: operand INFO_CMP_GENE This keyword indicates that one wants or does not want to print, for each generalised component, the name of the base_modale or mode_meca concept from which the mode corresponding to this component comes, its type (eigen or constrained), its frequency and the node of application of this mode if it is constrained. 8.5 Execution phase For the concepts tran_gene and harm_gene, one checks that the time instants (frequencies) of extraction requested by the operands NUME_ORDRE, LIST_ORDRE, INST, LIST_INST, (FREQ, LIST_FREQ) are in the domain of definition of the concept. One also checks that the fields stipulated by the keywords TOUT_CHAM, NOM_CHAM have indeed been computed. For the concept mode_gene, one checks that the names of the parameters specified by the keyword NOM_PARA are indeed admissible. If the mode number is selected by the operand NUME_MODE, one checks that this number is smaller than the total number of modes which define the mode_gene. 9 Examples 9.1 Printout of a vect_asse_gene IMPR_GENE ( GENE = _F( RESU_GENE = fgen, NUME_CMP_GENE = ‘OUI’ ), _F( RESU_GENE = fgen, INFO_CMP_GENE = ‘NON’, NUME_CMP_GENE = 1 ) ) One obtains the following printout: CONCEPT FGEN DE TYPE VECT_ASSE_GENE NUME_CMP VALEUR BASE_MODALE TYPE_MODE FREQUENCE APPLICATION 1 1.00000E+00 BAM01_CL PROPRE 2.25079E-01 2 5.00000E-01 BAM01_CL CONTRAINT 0.00000E+00 N03 DX 3 0.00000E+00 BAM02_CL PROPRE 2.25079E-01 4 0.00000E+00 BAM02_CL CONTRAINT 0.00000E+00 N01 DX CONCEPT FGEN DE TYPE VECT_ASSE_GENE NUME_CMP VALEUR 1 1.00000E+00 9.2 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = / unit, [I] / 8, [DEFAUT] The results are written, by default, to the file of logical unit 8. The user can define another output file whose logical unit he or she indicates. 9.3 Printout of a mode_gene IMPR_GENE ( GENE = _F( RESU_GENE = resgen, INFO_GENE = ’OUI’, NUME_ORDRE = 1, NOM_PARA = (‘FREQ’,‘MASS_GENE’,‘RIGI_GENE’), INFO_CMP_GENE = ‘NON’ ), _F( RESU_GENE = resgen, NUME_CMP_GENE = (1, 3), NUME_ORDRE = 1, NOM_PARA = (‘FREQ’,‘MASS_GENE’,‘RIGI_GENE’), INFO_CMP_GENE = ‘OUI’ ) ) The results are written, by default, to the file associated with logical unit 8. But the user can define another output file whose logical unit he or she indicates. U4.12.01.

u4.91.03 Procedure IMPR_TABLE u4.91.03 Procedure IMPR_TABLE 1 Purpose Print the content of a table in a file. The command makes it possible to print a subset of the table in various formats. The default format (TABLEAU) is convenient for processing by spreadsheet-type software; other formats allow direct visualisation with a curve plotter (for example xmgrace). 2 Syntax IMPR_TABLE( ◆ TABLE = table, ◇ FORMAT = / "TABLEAU" (par défaut), / "ASTER", / "TABLEAU_CROISE", / "AGRAF", / "XMGRACE", / "NUMPY", # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'XMGRACE') ◇ PILOTE = / "" (par défaut), / "POSTSCRIPT", / "EPS", / "MIF", / "SVG", / "PNM", / "PNG", / "JPEG", / "PDF", / "INTERACTIF", / "INTERACTIF_BG", ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 29), # Si: not equal_to("FORMAT", 'XMGRACE') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), ◇ FILTRE = _F( ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ CRIT_COMP = / "EQ" (par défaut), / "LT", / "GT", / "NE", / "LE", / "GE", / "VIDE", / "NON_VIDE", / "MAXI", / "MAXI_ABS", / "MINI", / "MINI_ABS", # Si: (is_in("CRIT_COMP", ('EQ','NE','GT','LT','GE','LE'))) ◆ / VALE = float, / VALE_I = int, / VALE_K = text, / VALE_C = complex, # Si: is_in("CRIT_COMP", ('EQ','NE')) ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ), ◇ TRI = _F( ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ ORDRE = / "CROISSANT" (par défaut), / "DECROISSANT", ), ◇ PAGINATION = text, ◇ FORMAT_R = text (défaut: "E12.5"), ◇ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ IMPR_FONCTION = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'TABLEAU') ◇ DEBUT_TABLE = text, ◇ FIN_TABLE = text, ◇ SEPARATEUR = text (défaut: " "), ◇ COMMENTAIRE = text (défaut: "#"), ◇ COMM_PARA = text, ◇ DEBUT_LIGNE = text, ◇ FIN_LIGNE = text (défaut: " "), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'XMGRACE') ◇ LEGENDE = text, ◇ STYLE = int, ◇ COULEUR = int, ◇ MARQUEUR = int, ◇ FREQ_MARQUEUR = int, ◇ BORNE_X = float, ◇ BORNE_Y = float, ◇ ECHELLE_X = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ ECHELLE_Y = / "LIN" (par défaut), / "LOG", ◇ GRILLE_X = float, ◇ GRILLE_Y = float, ◇ LEGENDE_X = text, ◇ LEGENDE_Y = text, ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 What is a table? A table is a data structure of a computing nature making it possible to store a set of integer, real, complex or character-string values. A table is comparable to the worksheet of a spreadsheet, that is to say that one can see it as a list of columns side by side. Each column has a field name, which we call a parameter , and contains similar data of type: I, R, C, K8, K16, K24 or K32. Example: | NUME_ORDRE | INST | NOEUD | G | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 10 | N1 | 5 | | 1 | 10 | N2 | 6 | | 1 | 10 | N3 | 7 | | 1 | 10 | N4 | 8 | | 2 | 20 | N1 | 9 | | 2 | 20 | N2 | 9 | | 2 | 20 | N3 | 8 | | 2 | 20 | N4 | 8 | | 3 | 30 | N1 | 7 | | 3 | 30 | N2 | 6 | | 3 | 30 | N3 | 5 | One can also see the table as a sequence of records (which we shall call lines ). Not all the lines necessarily have the same structure (that is to say the same parameters). For example: | ACTION | NUME_ORDRE | INST | NOEUD | DX | DY | MAILLE | SIXX | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | INTITULE 1 | 1 | 10 | N1 | 3 | 5 | | | | INTITULE 1 | 1 | 10 | N2 | 6 | 7 | | | | INTITULE 1 | 1 | 10 | N3 | 8 | 9 | | | | INTITULE 1 | 2 | 20 | N1 | 11 | 12 | | | | INTITULE 1 | 2 | 20 | N2 | 15 | 13 | | | | INTITULE 1 | 2 | 20 | N3 | 19 | 18 | | | | INTITULE 2 | 2 | 20 | | | | MA1 | -12. | | INTITULE 2 | 2 | 20 | | | | MA2 | -14. | To print the content of a table, the user will be able to: - select the columns and the lines that he or she wants to print [§3.6] - choose a criterion for the print order of the lines [§3.7] - choose the print "format": in lines, in tables, ... [§3.8] 3.2 Operand TABLE ♦ TABLE= matable Name of the table that one wants to print 3.3 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE= titre Character string which will be printed before the table (and before the title possibly attached to the table). This string can make it possible to distinguish better the printouts of tables placed one after another in the same file. 3.4 Selecting what one wants to print: the keywords FILTRE and NOM_PARA, TOUT_PARA The user chooses the columns to print by means of the keywords NOM_PARA and TOUT_PARA. He or she chooses the lines to print by means of the factor keyword (repeatable at will) FILTRE. 3.4.1 Keyword FILTRE The factor keyword FILTRE makes it possible to retain in the table only the lines satisfying certain criteria imposed by the user. The occurrences of the keyword are added to one another as successive filters ("AND" filters). For each occurrence of this keyword, one specifies the name of the parameter for which one imposes a condition, the type of condition (equality, non-equality, smaller than, ...) as well as the value associated with the condition. 3.4.1.1 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA= para para is the name of the parameter to which the filtering constraint applies. 3.4.1.2 Operand CRIT_COMP ◊ CRIT_COMP= crit crit is the type of the filtering constraint. | EQ | 'equality' for the integers, the texts, the reals or the complexes. For the floating-point numbers (reals or complexes), this equality is evaluated with a certain tolerance given by the keywords PRECISION and CRITERE. | | --- | --- | | NE | 'non-equality' (see EQ) | | LT | 'smaller than' Order relations: - natural for the integers and the reals - alphabetical for the texts - invalid for the complexes | | GT | 'greater than' (see LT) | | LE | 'smaller than or equal to' (see LT) | | GE | 'greater than or equal to' (see LT) | | VIDE | empty cell | | NON_VIDE | non-empty cell | | MAXI | the line retained will be the one which has the maximum value | | MAXI_ABS | the line retained will be the one which has the maximum absolute value | | MINI | the line retained will be the one which has the minimum value | | MINI_ABS | the line retained will be the one which has the minimum absolute value | | REGEXP | checks the regular expression supplied by VALE_K | Warning In the extraction commands EXTR_TABLE/RECU_FONCTION , the criteria MINI/MAXI (and MINI_ABS/MAXI_ABS ) select a single line satisfying the criterion, the last one. Whereas in the commands which handle the tables CALC_TABLE/IMPR_TABLE , all the lines satisfying these criteria are retained. The filter by regular expression is available only in CALC_TABLE . 3.4.1.3 Operands VALE / VALE_I / VALE_C / VALE_K These various keywords are used according to the type of the column associated with the parameter to which the constraint applies: integer, real, complex or text. One gives as argument the value associated with the constraint; for example 12 if one is interested only in order number 12. One can supply several values (valid for the equality or inequality tests) in order to apply an "OR" filter (cf. example below). This operand is useless when one uses the constraint types: 'VIDE', 'NON_VIDE', 'MAXI', 'MINI', … VALE_K is also used to supply the regular expression to be checked (CRIT_COMP='REGEXP'). Example: VALE_K='^N[MP]' in order to retain only the lines where, for the chosen parameter, the cell contains a character string which begins with an N (upper case) followed by an M or a P, then possibly by other characters (See the Python re module for more details on regular expressions). 3.4.1.4 Operands CRITERE / PRECISION When the constrained parameter is of floating type (real or complex) and the constraint type is equality (or non-equality), this equality is evaluated with a certain tolerance. PRECISION = eps, eps est la tolérance CRITERE= /'RELATIF' , |x-xref| COMM_PARA = comp Character inserted in order to comment out the line of the labels (by default, no character is inserted). ◊ DEBUT_LIGNE = deb String inserted at the start of each line (empty by default). ◊ FIN_LIGNE = fin String inserted at the end of the line ('\n' by default). 3.6.3 FORMAT = 'ASTER' The difference between the 'ASTER' format and the 'TABLEAU' format is the header of the table and its last line. This difference is justified by the fact that a table printed in the 'ASTER' format can be re-read by Code_Aster (command LIRE_TABLE U7.02.03). Example: #DEBUT_TABLE #TITRE ASTER 6.03.11 CONCEPT TAB_REAC CALCULE LE 12/07/2002 #TITRE TABL_POST_RELE INTITULE RESU NOM_CHAM NUME_ORD INST DY K8 K8 K16 I R R MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 1 2.50000E-01 -2.25146E+00 MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 2 5.00000E-01 -4.44089E+00 MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 3 7.50000E-01 -6.59515E+00 MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 4 1.00000E+00 -8.65972E+00 MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 5 1.25000E+00 -1.06742E+01 MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 6 1.50000E+00 -1.26438E+01 MESSAGE RESU REAC_NODA 7 1.75000E+00 -1.45569E+01 #FIN_TABLE 3.6.4 FORMAT='NUMPY' Numpy is a Python module for handling arrays. The printout in this format produces a file which can be re-read by the function numpy.load(). Only the real and integer parameters (columns) (automatically converted into reals) are printed. The other parameters are ignored. Finally, the topology of the table is preserved: one finds a numpy array which has as many lines as the table and as many columns as there are real or integer parameters. Note In the case of a parametric analysis, one expects a single line in the printed table. Use CALC_TABLE to filter the lines if need be. 3.6.5 FORMAT = 'TABLEAU_CROISE' The 'TABLEAU_CROISE' format is reserved for double-entry tables. The printout is made in the form of a table whose column names and line names have been documented. This printout concerns tables having 3 parameters. One represents the values of one of the 3 parameters as a function of the other 2. Example: DX as a function of NOEUD and INST: | DX FONCTION DE NOEUD ET DE INST | | 4 | 8 | 20 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | NOEUD/INST | N7 | 3.4 | 3.4 | 3.4 | | | N4 | 2.4 | 2.4 | 2.4 | | | N2 | 1.4 | 1.4 | 1.4 | NOM_PARA = ('INST', 'NOEUD', 'DX') The parameter "filling" the table is the 3rd of the list indicated by the simple keyword NOM_PARA. The "abscissa" parameter is the 2nd of the list indicated by the simple keyword NOM_PARA. The "ordinate" parameter is the 1st of the list indicated by the simple keyword NOM_PARA. Note: If the table contains more than 3 parameters, one can use the keyword PAGINATION to "enumerate" the values taken by the other parameters (see example 3). 3.6.6 FORMAT = 'XMGRACE' This format makes it possible to produce a file that can be visualised directly in xmgrace in the form of a curve. One has the same formatting functionalities as in IMPR_FONCTION. If PILOTE is not specified, one produces a data file for xmgrace; if PILOTE is supplied and if the chosen driver is actually available on the machine, one can produce directly a postscript, png, … file. Keywords for formatting the graph: see IMPR_FONCTION U4.33.01. 3.6.7 Operand PAGINATION This keyword is used to print a table in pieces (as a set of smaller tables). One gives a list of parameters (lpagi) which will be enumerated and printed as titles of the small tables. The list of the pagination parameters (lpagi) must be included in the complete list of the parameters that one wants to print (lpara). If one wants to use pagination and the 'TABLEAU_CROISE' format, the list lpara, once the parameters of lpagi have been removed from it, must be formed of 3 residual parameters. These 3 parameters will be used for the presentation as a table [§3.4.3]. Example: FORMAT='TABLEAU', PAGINATION='NOEUD' NOEUD: N7 | NUME_ORDRE | INST | DX | DY | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 4 | 3.4 | 3.8 | | 4 | 8 | 3.4 | 3.8 | | 7 | 20 | 3.4 | 3.8 | NOEUD: N4 | NUME_ORDRE | INST | DX | DY | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 4 | 2.4 | 2.8 | | 4 | 8 | 2.4 | 2.8 | | 7 | 20 | 2.4 | 2.8 | NOEUD: N2 | NUME_ORDRE | INST | DX | DY | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 4 | 1.4 | 1.8 | | 4 | 8 | 1.4 | 1.8 | | 7 | 20 | 1.4 | 1.8 | 3.6.8 Operand FORMAT_C For the complexes, two print formats are available (modulus/phase by default or real part/imaginary part). 3.6.9 Operand FORMAT_R This keyword makes it possible to choose the number of decimal places printed for each floating-point number: (real or complex). One uses for this the FORTRAN syntax. For example, for the default value: 'E12.5', one will print each floating-point number on 12 characters, with 5 decimal places and in scientific notation (with an exponent). 3.6.10 Operand IMPR_FONCTION For tables containing in their cells names of functions, this keyword makes it possible to indicate that one also wants to print the content of the functions referenced in the table. One first prints the table (as has been seen above) then one "loops" over all the functions contained in the printed part of the table and one prints these functions (as the command IMPR_FONCTION does). 3.7 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = inf Prints in the "message" file additional information if inf=2. Nothing happens if inf=1. 4 Examples Example 1: to discover the structure of a table IMPR_TABLE(TABLE= post_rel) Example 2: print a few parameters with filter and sorting IMPR_TABLE(TABLE= post_rel, FILTRE=_F(NOM_PARA='inst', VALE= 0., CRITERE= 'absolu'), TRI=_F(NOM_PARA=('absC_curv','coor_x'),ORDRE=('croissant'), NOM_PARA= ('coor_x', 'temp'), ) Example 3: use pagination and the tableau_CROISE format IMPR_TABLE(TABLE= post_rel, NOM_PARA= ('coor_x', 'temp', 'absC_curv', 'inst', 'coor_y'), PAGINATION= ('inst','coor_x'), FORMAT= 'tableau_CROISE', ) 4.1 Operand UNITE Makes it possible to choose the file in which one prints the table. By default, the printout is carried out on the file associated with logical unit 8. In the 'XMGRACE' format, the default value is 29, type dat in astk.

u4.91.04 Procedure IMPR_CONCEPT u4.91.04 Procedure IMPR_CONCEPT 1 Purpose Print, in a form that can be visualised, "data" fields from concepts assigned by the user with the commands AFFE_MATERIAU, AFFE_CARA_ELEM and AFFE_CHAR_MECA. 2 Syntax IMPR_CONCEPT( ◇ FORMAT = / "MED" (par défaut), / "RESULTAT", ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 80), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'MED') ◇ VERSION_MED = / "3.3.1" (par défaut), / "4.0.0", / "4.1.0", ◆ CONCEPT = _F( ◆ / CHAM_MATER = cham_mater, / CARA_ELEM = cara_elem, / CHARGE = char_meca, # Si: exists("CARA_ELEM") ◇ REPERE_LOCAL = / "NON" (par défaut), / "ELEM", / "ELNO", # Si: not equal_to("REPERE_LOCAL", 'NON') ◆ MODELE = modele, ), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Typography in the IMPR_CONCEPT documentation The procedure IMPR_CONCEPT makes it possible to print, in a form that can be visualised, the quantities assigned by the user with the commands AFFE_MATERIAU, AFFE_CARA_ELEM and AFFE_CHAR_MECA. This makes it possible to check that the overloading rules of the code lead to the desired assignments. For example: IMPR_CONCEPT( FORMAT=’MED’, CONCEPT=( _F(CHAM_MATER = CHAMPMAT), _F(CARA_ELEM = CARA_ELE), _F(CHARGE = CHARG1),), ) The fields contained in these data structures are printed in two very different forms: - Form "A" (the easiest to interpret graphically): each component is printed separately as a real number. For example, the thickness of the shell elements can be visualised as a scalar field (scalar map in Salomé). - Form "B": one assigns to each mesh cell an integer code: 1, 2, 3, ... n. The mesh cells assigned the same code then have ALL their components identical. The "definition" of the codes, that is to say the values of these components, is printed in the message file. One can visualise the "codes" as a scalar field, which makes it possible to "see" the zones where "everything is constant". Form "A" is used systematically for the "MED" format, except for the material field because this field contains the name of the material assigned on the mesh cells and this name is not a number. Form "A" is not programmed in the "RESULTAT" format. Form "B" is used systematically for the "RESULTAT" format and for the material field. For form "B", the correspondence between the assigned quantities and the code is given in the .mess file. For example, for the material field: IMPRESSION D’UN CHAMP DE CONCEPT: Champ de MATERIAUX NOM DU CHAMP: CHAMPMAT_CHAMP_MAT CORRESPONDANCE VALEUR CONTENU: VALEUR = 1. X1 = MAT_1 VALEUR = 2. X1 = MAT_2 VALEUR = 3. X1 = MAT_3 4 Operands FORMAT and UNITE and INFO 4.1 Operand FORMAT The operand FORMAT makes it possible to specify the format of the file in which to write the result. Two formats 'MED' and 'RESULTAT' are available. The 'MED' format is the default write format. 4.2 Operand UNITE Defines the unit in which one writes the med file. By default, UNITE = 80 and corresponds to the default unit of type rmed in astk. 4.3 Operand INFO The keyword INFO, when it is equal to 2, makes it possible to obtain information on the printouts carried out by the command. 4.4 Operand VERSION_MED ◊ VERSION_MED = /’3.3.1’, [DEFAUT] /’4.0.0’, /’4.1.0’, When a new file is created in med format, the printout is made in med format 3.3.1. If the file already exists, the med format level is retained. One can change the MED file version with the keyword VERSION_MED. 5 Factor keyword CONCEPT 5.1 Operand REPERE_LOCAL If REPERE_LOCAL has the value 'ELEM' or 'ELNO', the keyword MODELE is mandatory. If REPERE_LOCAL has the value 'ELEM', the 3 vectors constituting the local frame of each element are printed, so that they can be visualised with the aid of ParaVis. If REPERE_LOCAL has the value 'ELNO', the 3 vectors constituting the local frame of each element are stored in the form of a field at the nodes, so that they can then be used in the ParaVis calculator in combination with other fields at the nodes. In this case no other information coming from the concept CARA_ELEM is stored in the file. When REPERE_LOCAL='ELNO' it is therefore possible to combine the local vectors with the components of the internal-force fields. This makes it possible to visualise the force vectors in 3D, and also to produce an animation of their evolution over the time instants of the analysis. To carry out this action several elementary operations are to be performed in ParaVis: - Open the MED file containing the frames: on the REPE-> Filter "ELNO Points"-> Filter "Merge blocs" - Open the MED file containing the fields: on the EFGE_ELNO-> Filter "ELNO Points"-> Filter "Merge blocs" - selection of the 2 "Merge blocs" then "Append Attributes" In "Calculator" one has access to the REPE vectors and to the field components. The computation of the force vector (N, Vy, Vz) is done in the following way: \begin{array}{c}\mathit{Fint}=\\ \\ \end{array}\begin{array}{c}\text{CAREL\_\_\_.REPLC\_1}\ast \text{xxxxxxxxEFGE\_ELNO\_N +}\\ \text{CAREL\_\_\_.REPLC\_2}\ast \text{xxxxxxxxEFGE\_ELNO\_VY +}\\ \text{CAREL\_\_\_.REPLC\_3}\ast \text{xxxxxxxxEFGE\_ELNO\_VZ}\end{array} where 'xxxxxxxx' denotes the name of the result concept, produced by Code_Aster . The computation of the Moment vector (Mt, My, Mz) is done in the following way: \begin{array}{c}\mathit{Mint}=\\ \\ \end{array}\begin{array}{c}\text{CAREL\_\_\_.REPLC\_1}\ast \text{xxxxxxxxEFGE\_ELNO\_MT +}\\ \text{CAREL\_\_\_.REPLC\_2}\ast \text{xxxxxxxxEFGE\_ELNO\_MFY +}\\ \text{CAREL\_\_\_.REPLC\_3}\ast \text{xxxxxxxxEFGE\_ELNO\_MFZ}\end{array} where 'xxxxxxxx' denotes the name of the result concept, produced by Code_Aster . 5.2 Fields that can be visualised CHAM_MATER: Material field CARA_ELEM: General characteristics of the bars Geometric characteristics of the bars General characteristics of the beams Geometric characteristics of the beams Characteristics of the cables Characteristics of the curved beams Characteristics of the "fluid" beams Characteristics of the discrete elements K_ Characteristics of the discrete elements M_ Characteristics of the discrete elements A_ Geometric characteristics of the shells Orientation of the 2D and 3D elements Orientation of the shells and of the beams CHARGE: PESANTEUR loading ROTATION loading PRES_REP loading Loading of volume forces in 3D Loading of surface forces in 3D Loading of line forces in 3D Loading of surface forces in 2D Loading of line forces in 2D Loading of distributed forces for the shells PRE_EPSI loading FORCE_ELEC loading FLUX_THM_REP loading IMPE_FACE loading ONDE_FLUI loading

u4.91.11 Procedure IMPR_CO u4.91.11 Procedure IMPR_CO 1 Purpose Print all the JEVEUX objects which constitute an existing concept. This command is intended above all for "debugging". The content of the JEVEUX objects that one prints is in principle understandable only by developers equipped with their D documentation. In particular, the format of these objects can change without consultation with the users. It is therefore very risky to use these writings in "post-processing" or in "chaining" to other codes. 2 Syntax IMPR_CO( ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), ◇ NIVEAU = / -1, / 0, / 1, / 2 (par défaut), ◇ ATTRIBUT = / "NON" (par défaut), / "OUI", ◇ CONTENU = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ◇ BASE = / " ", / "G" (par défaut), / "V", / "L", ◆ / CONCEPT = _F( ◆ NOM = datastructure, ), / CHAINE = text, / TOUT = "OUI" (ou non renseigné), ◇ POSITION = int (défaut: 1), # Si: equal_to("NIVEAU", -1) ◇ PERMUTATION = / "NON", / "OUI" (par défaut), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Factor keyword CONCEPT L'utilisateur indique derrière le mot clé NOM, la liste des concepts qu'il veut imprimer. 3.2 Operand TOUT = 'OUI' Permet d'imprimer tous les objets présents sur une base (ou sur toutes les bases). Attention, ces impressions peuvent être très volumineuses. 3.3 Operands CHAINE / POSITION / ♦ CHAINE The user can give a text (between "quotes") of length less than 24 characters: the command will then print all the objects having in their name the character string chain in position ipos (see keyword POSITION). Examples: 1) CHAINE= 'TOTO1234' , POSITION= 1 is equivalent to CO = TOTO1234 2) CHAINE= '.DESC' , POSITION= 20 , makes it possible to print all the objects whose name ends with '.DESC'. ◊ POSITION= ipos , This integer specifies the position of the start of the string to be sought in the name of the existing objects. 3.4 Operand ATTRIBUT ◊ ATTRIBUT= One can choose to print (or not) the attributes of the selected JEVEUX objects. 3.5 Operand CONTENU ◊ CONTENU= One can choose to print (or not) the content of the selected objects. 3.6 Operand BASE ◊ BASE= base One will print only the JEVEUX objects found on the base base. If one wants to obtain the objects located on the set of the bases ('G' and 'V'), one will use BASE = ' ' ("blank" character). 3.7 Operand NIVEAU ◊ NIVEAU= 0: only the names of the objects are printed, 1: one prints only the first 5 objects of each collection of JEVEUX objects, 2: one prints everything. -1: One prints for each object a single line containing: - the name of the object - a few characteristics: LONMAX, LONUTI, TYPE - a number (SOMMI or SOMMR) which "summarises" the whole of the object. These printouts make it possible for example to help compare 2 different versions of the code. For this: - Add at the end of the command file: IMPR_CO(TOUT='OUI', NIVEAU=-1) - "run" the 2 versions of the code with this set of commands - do a "diff" of the 2 result files produced. 3.8 Operand PERMUTATION ◊ PERMUTATION= / 'OUI', [DEFAUT] / 'NON' This keyword can be present only when NIVEAU = -1. It makes it possible to make the numbers SOMMI or SOMMR (mentioned in the paragraph of the operand NIVEAU) depend on the order in which the elements of the object are arranged. - 'OUI': SOMMI or SOMMR will depend on this order - 'NON': SOMMI or SOMMR will not depend on this order 3.9 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE= Logical unit number associated with the file on which the selected objects must be printed. By default, the printout is carried out on the unit which is associated with the file fort.8. 4 Examples Example 1 IMPR_CO (CONCEPT= _F(NOM=(ma, mo, ch1 ))) Printout of the concepts: ma, mo, ch1. The attributes of the objects will not be written. Example 2 IMPR_CO(CHAINE= '&', POSITION= 1, NIVEAU= 0, BASE= ‘V’, ) Printout of the names of the objects of the volatile database beginning with '&'.

u4.91.12 Procedure INFO_RESU u4.91.12 Procedure INFO_RESU 1 Purpose Print the list of the fields and of the components of those fields present in a result data structure. 2 Syntax INFO_RESU( ◇ RESULTAT = resultat, ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 8), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand RESULTAT ♦ RESULTAT = RESU, It is with this keyword that the user specifies the result data structure for which he or she wishes to have the fields and the components present printed. 3.2 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = Logical unit number associated with the file on which the result data structure must be printed. By default, the printout is carried out on logical unit 8. 4 Example RESUTRQU=MECA_STATIQUE( … ) INFO_RESU(RESULTAT=RESUTRQU) This command will cause the following printout in the message file: ----------------------------------------------------------- COMPOSANTES DES CHAMPS PRESENTS DANS LE RESULTAT : RESUTRQU - CHAMP DEPL : DX DY - CHAMP SIEF_ELGA : SIXX SIYY SIZZ SIXY -----------------------------------------------------------

u4.91.21 Procedure IMPR_JEVEUX u4.91.21 Procedure IMPR_JEVEUX 1 Purpose Print the content of the objects created by the JEVEUX memory manager. Useful for the maintenance and the debugging of new developments. Print the content of the JEVEUX objects, access the JEVEUX system objects, print the directory of the objects associated with a database, print the memory segmentation or access the content of a database stored on disk. 2 Syntax IMPR_JEVEUX( ◆ ENTITE = / "DISQUE", / "MEMOIRE", / "REPERTOIRE", / "OBJET", / "ATTRIBUT", / "SYSTEME", / "ENREGISTREMENT", # Si: (equal_to("ENTITE", 'OBJET')) ◇ NOMOBJ = text, ◇ NUMOC = int, ◇ NOMOC = text, # Si: (equal_to("ENTITE", 'ATTRIBUT')) ◇ NOMOBJ = text, ◇ NOMATR = / " DESO", / " IADD", / " IADM", / " NOM", / " LONG", / " LONO", / " LUTI", / " NUM", # Si: (equal_to("ENTITE", 'SYSTEME')) ◆ CLASSE = / "G", / "V", ◇ NOMATR = / " CARA", / " IADD", / " GENR", / " TYPE", / " MARQ", / " DOCU", / " ORIG", / " RNOM", / " LTYP", / " LONG", / " LONO", / " DATE", / " LUTI", / " HCOD", / " INDX", / " TLEC", / " TECR", / " IADM", / " ACCE", / " USADI", # Si: (equal_to("ENTITE", 'REPERTOIRE')) ◇ CLASSE = / "G", / "V", / " " (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("ENTITE", 'DISQUE')) ◇ CLASSE = / "G", / "V", / " " (par défaut), # Si: (equal_to("ENTITE", 'ENREGISTREMENT')) ◇ CLASSE = / "G" (par défaut), / "V", ◆ NUMERO = int, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ◇ IMPRESSION = _F( ◇ NOM = text, ◇ UNITE = unit, ), ◇ COMMENTAIRE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand ENTITE The possible values of ENTITE are: - 'OBJET': Call to JEIMPO, JEPRAT (values of an object, ...), - 'ATTRIBUT': Call to JEIMPA (attributes of an object or of a collection), - 'SYSTEME': Call to JEPRAT (attributes of a collection or system objects), - 'MEMOIRE': Call to JEIMPM (state of the memory), - 'REPERTOIRE': Call to JEIMPR (directory of one or more classes), - 'DISQUE': Call to JEIMPD (objects written to disk), - 'ENREGISTREMENT': Call to JEPREN (content of the records of the file associated with the database). The possibilities offered by the various print routines are described in the booklet: JEVEUX memory management D6.02.01. If ENTITE='OBJET': - NOMOBJ: Name of a simple object or name of a collection. - NOMOC: Name of a collection object. - NUMOC: Number of a collection object. If ENTITE='ATTRIBUT': - NOMOBJ: Name of a simple object or of a collection. - NOMATR: Attribute name on 8 characters for: - a collection: DESO, IADD, IADM, NOM, LONG, LONO, LUTI, NUM. If ENTITE='SYSTEME': - NOMATR: Attribute name on 8 characters for: - the system: CARA, IADD, GENR, TYPE, MARQ, DOCU, ORIG, RNOM, LTYP, LONG, LONO, DATE, LUTI, HCOD, INDX, TLEC, TECR, IADM, ACCE, USADI. - CLASSE: Name of the class associated with one or more databases of values ('G', 'V'). For the entity 'SYSTEME' this keyword is mandatory. For the entities 'REPERTOIRE' and 'DISQUE', one prints by default what concerns all the open databases. 3.2 Operand NUMERO Makes it possible to specify the number of the record whose content must be examined. 3.3 Operand INFO Makes it possible to specify the level of the printouts to be carried out. INFO=1 one merely prints the list of the names of the JEVEUX objects present on the record. INFO=2 one prints in addition the content of the record. This printout is carried out in integer format; the storage of the image of the JEVEUX memory being carried out under this type, it is therefore impossible to interpret the other types. 3.4 Operands IMPRESSION and UNITE The factor keyword IMPRESSION makes it possible to choose the file or the logical unit for the printout of the information. - NOM: Internal file name; it equals 'MESSAGE' or 'RESULTAT'. - UNITE: Logical unit number. 3.5 Operand COMMENTAIRE Text appearing as the title of the printouts requested. 4 Example of use IMPR_JEVEUX(ENTITE="OBJET", NOMOBJ="00000001.NOMMAI") # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Commande #0003, ligne 1 IMPR_JEVEUX(ENTITE='OBJET', NOMOBJ='00000001.NOMMAI') ECRITURE DE L'OBJET : "00000001.NOMMAI " JEIMPA IMPRESSION DES ATTRIBUTS DE >00000001.NOMMAI 00000001.NOMMAI >>>> 1 - >M1 <>M2 <>M3 <>M4 <>M5 <>M6 <>M7 M8 <>M9 <>M10 <>M11 <>M12 <>M13 <>M14 M15 <>M16 <>M17 <>M18 <>M19 < FIN DE L'OBJET : "00000001.NOMMAI " # Mémoire (Mo) : 974.18 / 913.89 / 209.19 / 185.02 (VmPeak / VmSize / Optimum / Minimum) # Fin commande #0003 user+syst: 0.00s (syst: 0.00s, elaps: 0.00s) # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

u4.92.01 Procedure TEST_RESU u4.92.01 Procedure TEST_RESU 1 Purpose Compare a value extracted from a data structure with a reference value supplied by the user. This command makes it possible to test a numerical value: integer, real or complex extracted from an already computed concept. Today, one can test a component of a cham_no or of a cham_elem, a component of a field extracted from a resultat, a parameter of a resultat, a 'global' value extracted from a field, or else the content of an arbitrary object of a user concept. The procedure then writes a conventional message: - "OK" (if it is good), - "NOOK" (otherwise). followed by the value found, the reference value and the percentage of error. Systematically, one checks a non-regression value, and when this is possible, an analytical reference value, coming from an external source or from another analysis with Code_Aster. The commands TEST_FONCTION U4.92.02 and TEST_TABLE U4.92.03 make it possible to test the values extracted from the functions and from the tables. 2 Syntax TEST_RESU( ◆ | CHAM_NO = _F( ◆ CHAM_GD = cham_no, ◇ & GROUP_NO = grno, & NOM_CMP = text, # Si: True ◆ / VALE_CALC_I = int, / VALE_CALC = float, / VALE_CALC_C = complex, ◇ VALE_ABS = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ TYPE_TEST = / "SOMM_ABS", / "SOMM", / "MAX", / "MIN", ◇ TOLE_MACHINE = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: exists("REFERENCE") ◆ / VALE_REFE_I = int, / VALE_REFE = float, / VALE_REFE_C = complex, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ REFERENCE = / "ANALYTIQUE", / "SOURCE_EXTERNE", / "AUTRE_ASTER", / "NON_DEFINI", # Si: exists("VALE_CALC") and abs(VALE_CALC if type(VALE_CALC) not in (list, tuple) else VALE_CALC[0]) ◊ LEGENDE = > Character string of at most 16 characters describing the test performed. > The user therefore has the possibility of commenting on the test. 4.9 Keyword TEST_NAN | TEST_NAN = / ‘NON’ , [DEFAUT] / ‘OUI’ , This keyword is used to validate the operation of the \mathit{NaN} ( Not-a-Number ) of Code_Aster. This keyword is to be used only with a view to carrying out tests. Its use must cause a fatal error in \mathit{FPE} ( Floating Point Exception ) in debug mode in TEST_RESU. 5 Examples TEST_RESU( CHAM_NO= _F ( CHAM_GD = f, GROUP_NO = 'GN2', NOM_CMP = 'DX' , REFERENCE= 'ANALYTIQUE' , VALE_CALC = 1.1999996845E-5 , VALE_REFE = 1.2E-5 , PRECISION= 1D-4 ,)) TEST_RESU( CARTE =_F ( CHAM_GD = CART1, GROUP_MA = 'GM3', NOM_CMP = 'X4' , REFERENCE= 'AUTRE_ASTER', VALE_CALC_I = 3, VALE_REFE_I = 3,)) TEST_RESU( CHAM_ELEM=(_F ( CHAM_GD = SIGGA, GROUP_MA = 'GM3', POINT = 3, NOM_CMP = 'SIXX' , VALE_CALC = 3.4E6, ), _F ( CHAM_GD = SIGNO, GROUP_MA = 'GM5', GROUP_NO = 'GN1', NOM_CMP = 'SIXX' , VALE_CALC = 3.4E6 , ),)) TEST_RESU ( RESU=(_F ( RESULTAT = evolth, NOM_CHAM = 'FLUX_ELGA' , TYPE_TEST= 'MAX' , REFERENCE = 'ANALYTIQUE', VALE_CALC = 154.35000201404, VALE_REFE = 154.35),)) TEST_RESU ( OBJET= _F ( NOM= 'CH1 .CHME.LIGREL.LIEL' , VALE_CALC_I= 1278484 ,)) TEST_RESU ( MAILLAGE=( _F ( MAILLAGE= ma , CARA= 'NB_MAILLE' VALE_CALC_I= 1000 ,), _F ( MAILLAGE= ma , CARA= 'NB_GROUP_NO' VALE_CALC_I= 12 ,), _F ( MAILLAGE= ma , CARA= 'EXI_GROUP_MA' NOM_GROUP_MA='GAUCHE', VALE_CALC_I= 25 ,), ))

u4.92.02 Procedure TEST_FONCTION u4.92.02 Procedure TEST_FONCTION 1 Purpose Extract a numerical value or an attribute of a function for comparison with a reference value. The function is a data structure of type fonction or nappe. This procedure then writes a conventional message "OK" (if it is good) or "NOOK" (otherwise). It does not stop the execution if the test is not satisfied; this makes it possible to use it either systematically for the validation tests, or to extract and print a value of a function or of a nappe for a particular value of a parameter. This command is used essentially by the test cases in order to validate the non-regression of the results. 2 Syntax TEST_FONCTION( ◇ VALEUR = _F( ◆ FONCTION = formule / fonction_c / fonction / nappe, ◇ NOM_PARA = text, ◆ / VALE_PARA = float, / INTERVALLE = float, # Si: True ◆ / VALE_CALC_C = complex, / VALE_CALC = float, ◇ VALE_ABS = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ TYPE_TEST = / "SOMM_ABS", / "SOMM", / "MAX", / "MIN", ◇ TOLE_MACHINE = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: exists("REFERENCE") ◆ / VALE_REFE_C = complex, / VALE_REFE = float, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ REFERENCE = / "ANALYTIQUE", / "SOURCE_EXTERNE", / "AUTRE_ASTER", / "NON_DEFINI", # Si: exists("VALE_CALC") and abs(VALE_CALC if type(VALE_CALC) not in (list, tuple) else VALE_CALC[0]) < 1.e-16 ◇ ORDRE_GRANDEUR = float, ◇ LEGENDE = text, ), ◇ ATTRIBUT = _F( ◆ FONCTION = formule / fonction_c / fonction / nappe, ◇ PARA = float, ◇ CRIT_PARA = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ PREC_PARA = float (défaut: 0.001), ◆ ATTR = / "NOM_PARA", / "NOM_RESU", / "PROL_DROITE", / "PROL_GAUCHE", / "INTERPOL", / "PROL_GAUCHE_FONC", / "PROL_DROITE_FONC", / "INTERPOL_FONC", / "NOM_PARA_FONC", ◆ ATTR_REFE = text, ◇ REFERENCE = / "ANALYTIQUE", / "SOURCE_EXTERNE", / "AUTRE_ASTER", ), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Keyword VALEUR ♦ VALEUR = Factor keyword for testing a value of a function or of a nappe. 3.1.1 Operand FONCTION ♦ FONCTION = f Name of the function (with one parameter) or of the nappe (with two parameters) on which the operation is performed. 3.1.2 Operand NOM_PARA ◊ NOM_PARA = lnom In the case of a function, this keyword is not processed. In the case of a nappe, the user will give 2 parameter names: the first defining the parameter of the nappe, the second defining the parameter of the function that one wants to test (see the command DEFI_NAPPE U4.31.03). 3.1.3 Operand VALE_PARA ♦ VALE_PARA = lpara In the case of a function, the user gives the value of the parameter for which the value of the function is tested. In the case of a nappe, the user gives the 2 values corresponding to the names of the two parameters (that of the nappe and that of the function). 3.1.4 Keywords common to the commands TEST_XXX The definition of the non-regression and reference values, as well as of the allowable tolerances and of the comparison criteria, is detailed in the documentation u4.92.01 of the command TEST_RESU. The specific features of TEST_FONCTION are: - no integer values or character strings, - no tolerance on the value of the parameter (TOLE_MACHINE and CRITERE take only a single value). 3.2 Keyword ATTRIBUT / ATTRIBUT= Factor keyword for testing an attribute of a function or of a nappe. 3.2.1 Operand FONCTION ♦ FONCTION = f Name of the function or of the nappe on which the operation is performed. 3.2.2 Operand PARA ◊ PARA = reel In the case of a function, this keyword is not necessary. In the case of a nappe, the user gives the value of the parameter in order to retrieve the function so as to test the attribute. 3.2.3 Operands PREC_PARA / CRIT_PARA ◊ PREC_PARA = prec One searches for the function defined by the value of the parameter in an interval defined by the absolute or relative position: "inst ± prec" (cf. CRITERE[§3.2.3]). By default prec = 1.0D-3. ◊ CRIT_PARA = 'RELATIF': the search interval is: [inst(1-prec),inst(1+prec)] 'ABSOLU': the search interval is: [inst-prec,inst+prec] 3.2.4 Operand ATTR ♦ ATTR = Name of the attribute to be tested. For the meaning of the attributes refer to DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02 or to DEFI_NAPPE U4.31.03. 3.2.5 Operand ATTR_REFE ♦ ATTR_REFE = attr Reference attribute. For the meaning of the attributes refer to DEFI_FONCTION U4.31.02 or to DEFI_NAPPE U4.31.03. 4 Examples 4.1 Checking of a nappe df1 = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = 'INST', NOM_RESU = 'DEPL', VALE = (0.,0.,1.,1.,2.,2.,3.,3.,4.,4. ) ) df2 = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = 'INST', NOM_RESU = 'DEPL', VALE = (3., 3., 4., 4., 5., 5. ) ) dn1 = DEFI_NAPPE ( NOM_PARA = 'AMOR', NOM_RESU = 'DEPL', VALE = (0.01, 0.02), FONCTION = ( df1, df2 )) TEST_FONCTION ( one checks the attribute 'NOM_PARA' of the function df1 in the nappe dn1 ATTRIBUT = ( _F( FONCTION = dn1 , PARA = 0.01, # 0.01 atteint df1 ATTR = 'NOM_PARA_FONC', ATTR_REFE = 'INST' ), one checks the attribute 'NOM_PARA' of the nappe dn1 _F( FONCTION = dn1 , ATTR = 'NOM_PARA', ATTR_REFE = 'AMOR' )), one checks a value of the nappe dn1 (in practice on the function df1) VALEUR = _F( FONCTION = dn1, NOM_PARA = ('AMOR', 'INST' ), VALE_PARA = ( 0.01, 1. ), VALE_REFE = 1. ) ) 4.2 Checking of a function li1=DEFI_LIST_REEL( DEBUT=0., INTERVALLE=_F(JUSQU_A=2 pi, PAS=2 pi/20), ) f1=FORMULE( NOM_PARA=’INST’, VALE=’sin(INST) + cos(INST)’, ) fonc=CALC_FONC_INTERP ( FONCTION=f1, LIST_PARA=li1, NOM_RESU=’DEPL’, INTERPOL=’LIN’, ) TEST_FONCTION( # on teste un attribut de la fonction ATTRIBUT=_F( FONCTION=fonc, ATTR=’INTERPOL’, ATTR_REFE=’LIN LIN’,), # on teste une valeur de la fonction VALEUR=_F ( FONCTION=fonc, VALE_PARA=pi, REFERENCE='ANALYTIQUE', VALE_CALC=-1., VALE_REFE=sin(pi)+cos(pi), ), )

u4.92.03 Procedure TEST_TABLE u4.92.03 Procedure TEST_TABLE 1 Purpose Test a "cell" (or a whole column) of a concept of type table. Prints OK if the value found in the cell is identical to the value given as reference, NOOK otherwise. This command is used essentially by the test cases in order to validate the non-regression of the results. 2 Syntax TEST_TABLE( ◆ TABLE = table, ◇ FILTRE = _F( ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ CRIT_COMP = / "EQ" (par défaut), / "LT", / "GT", / "NE", / "LE", / "GE", / "VIDE", / "NON_VIDE", / "MAXI", / "MAXI_ABS", / "MINI", / "MINI_ABS", # Si: (is_in("CRIT_COMP", ('EQ','NE','GT','LT','GE','LE'))) ◆ / VALE = float, / VALE_I = int, / VALE_K = text, / VALE_C = complex, ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ), ◆ NOM_PARA = text, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, # Si: True ◆ / VALE_CALC_I = int, / VALE_CALC = float, / VALE_CALC_C = complex, / VALE_CALC_K = text, ◇ VALE_ABS = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ TYPE_TEST = / "SOMM_ABS", / "SOMM", / "MAX", / "MIN", ◇ TOLE_MACHINE = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", # Si: exists("REFERENCE") ◆ / VALE_REFE_I = int, / VALE_REFE = float, / VALE_REFE_C = complex, / VALE_REFE_K = text, ◇ PRECISION = float (défaut: 0.001), ◇ REFERENCE = / "ANALYTIQUE", / "SOURCE_EXTERNE", / "AUTRE_ASTER", / "NON_DEFINI", # Si: exists("VALE_CALC") and abs(VALE_CALC if type(VALE_CALC) not in (list, tuple) else VALE_CALC[0]) < 1.e-16 ◇ ORDRE_GRANDEUR = float, ◇ LEGENDE = text, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TABLE One gives the name of the table that one wants to test. 3.2 Operand NOM_PARA One gives the name of the parameter identifying the column to be tested. 3.3 Testing a cell; keyword FILTRE This factor keyword (repeatable at will) is used to select the line containing the cell to be tested. The use of this keyword is described in the command IMPR_TABLE U4.91.03. The only difference with respect to IMPR_TABLE is that the inequality comparison criteria (CRIT_COMP) are not available. Note: It is often necessary to repeat this keyword in order to select a single line, which is why the command TEST_TABLE makes it possible to test only one value at a time. If one wants to test 3 values in a table, one must call the command 3 times. 3.4 Testing a whole column / TYPE_TEST= ‘SOMM_ABS’ The sum of the absolute values of the whole column of the table. / TYPE_TEST= ‘SOMM’ The sum of the values of the whole column of the table. / TYPE_TEST= ‘MAX’ The maximum of the values of the whole column of the table. / TYPE_TEST= ‘MIN’ The minimum of the values of the whole column of the table. 3.5 Keywords common to the commands TEST_XXX The definition of the non-regression and reference values, as well as of the allowable tolerances and of the comparison criteria, is detailed in the documentation u4.92.01 of the command TEST_RESU. 3.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = inf Prints additional information in the "message" file if inf=2. Prints nothing if inf=1. 4 Example To test the table maxFchoc: TEST_TABLE ( TABLE= maxFchoc , NOM_PARA= 'MAXI', FILTRE = ( _F(NOM_PARA= 'FONCTION', VALE_K= 'effochoc'), _F(NOM_PARA= 'INST' , VALE= 3.76E-1),) REFERENCE= 'ANALYTIQUE', VALE_CALC= –6,298299978E2 VALE_REFE = -6.2983E2,)

u4.92.04 Procedure TEST_FICHIER u4.92.04 Procedure TEST_FICHIER 1 Purpose This macro-command makes it possible to test the non-regression of files produced by the Code_Aster commands, principally IMPR_RESU, but one can use it on any text file. To test a file, one extracts the list of the real and integer numbers present in the file, the cardinality of this list, and the whole of the remaining text (once the numbers have been extracted). For the numbers, one checks the non-regression of the sum, of the absolute sum or of the min/max of the values to within a given accuracy. For testing the text of the file, one uses the Python module md5, which provides a "signature" of the text (called md5sum). Returns OK if the file is identical to the file that served as the reference, NOOK otherwise. This command is used essentially by the test cases in order to validate the non-regression of the results. 2 Syntax TEST_FICHIER( ◆ FICHIER = text, ◇ EXPR_IGNORE = text, ◆ NB_VALE = int, ◇ NB_VALE_I = int, ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, # Si: True ◇ VALE_CALC_I = int, ◇ VALE_CALC_K = text, ◇ TYPE_TEST = / "SOMM_ABS", / "SOMM", / "MAX", / "MIN", ◇ TOLE_MACHINE = float (défaut: 1e-06), ◇ CRITERE = / "RELATIF" (par défaut), / "ABSOLU", ◇ VALE_CALC = float, # Si: exists("VALE_CALC") and abs(VALE_CALC if type(VALE_CALC) not in (list, tuple) else VALE_CALC[0]) iret, sum = test_file( filename='nom_fichier', > type_test='SOMM', > verbose=True) Note 3 For the integer numbers, the value tested on the integers is truncated to the largest integer that can be represented in 32 bits (about 2.e9) . 4 Operands 4.1 Operand FICHIER ♦ FICHIER = fich, One supplies here the name of the file to be analysed, with its access path relative to the execution directory or absolute. Examples: 'fort.37' or './REPE_OUT/resultats.pos'. 4.2 Operand EXPR_IGNORE ◊ EXPR_IGNORE = regexp The lines of the file satisfying the regular expressions given under this keyword will be ignored in the analysis of the file. Exemple: EXPR_IGNORE = ( 'DATE=[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{2}/[0-9]{4}', '^VERSION' ) Here the lines containing DATE=jj/mm/aaaa where j , m , a are digits or starting with VERSION are ignored. 4.3 Operand TYPE_TEST Type of the test performed on the real and integer values of the file. The possible values are: - SOMM: sum of the values - SOMM_ABS: sum of the absolute values - MAXI: maximum value - MINI: minimum value - MAXI_ABS: maximum of the absolute values - MINI_ABS: minimum of the absolute values 4.4 Operands NB_VALE and NB_VALE_I NB_VALE is the number of real values expected in the file. It is the only compulsory test. NB_VALE_I is the number of integer values expected in the file. 4.5 Keywords common to the commands TEST_XXX The definition of the non-regression and reference values, as well as of the allowable tolerances and of the comparison criteria, is detailed in the documentation u4.92.01 of the command TEST_RESU. The specific features of TEST_FICHIER are: - no complex values, - no test in absolute value (except with TYPE_TEST), - VALE_CALC, VALE_CALC_I and VALE_CALC_K may be supplied together, - no tolerance on the value of the parameter (TOLE_MACHINE and CRITERE take only a single value). - VALE_CALC supplies the expected reference value for the test on the real values (the sum or the maximum or...). - VALE_CALC_I supplies the expected reference value for the test on the integer values (the sum or the maximum or...). - VALE_CALC_K supplies the md5 signature of the text of the file after all the real and integer values have been removed. To obtain the value on the reference file, it is enough to launch the command TEST_FICHIER and to note the displayed value (it is a sequence of 32 hexadecimal characters). 4.6 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = inf Specifies the detail of the information printed in the message file. If inf=1, one has the following summary: (extract from ssls108a) File name: ./REPE_OUT/DEP12.pos Computed Reference Integers: Number of values: 176 176 Sum of the values: 878 878 Reals: Number of values: 10375 10375 Sum of the values: 1.5553683808e+04 1.5553683808e+04 Checksum: e5050b2a3517728c4cc0e23af2b16ba5 not_tested If inf=2, one has the list of all the values recorded in the file, read by block (5897 real values and 118 integer values in the 3rd block of this example): Real numbers: 5897 ['2.1774365E-003', '2.4554530E-003', '2.4552944E-003', '7.0000000E+000', ...] Integer numbers: 118 ['1', '0', '0', '0', '0', '0', '0', '144', '0', '0', '0', '0', '0', '0', ...] as well as the whole of the remaining text once all the numbers have been extracted: Text: EndView ViewDEFZ_DRX
