& : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Description of a mesh adaptation 3.1 General scheme of an adaptation The general principle of an analysis with mesh adaptation is the following: | Phase 1: | Reading of the initial mesh, M0 Definition of the materials | | --- | --- | | Phase 2: | definition of the model, of the loadings on this mesh M0 analysis producing a result RESU0 analysis, where appropriate, of a field driving the refinement, CHAMP0 | | This initial phase is the standard phase of any analysis | | | Phase 3: | Adaptation of the mesh M0. One obtains a new mesh, M1 | | Phase 4: | definition of the model, of the loadings on the mesh M1, analysis producing a result RESU1, analysis, where appropriate, of a field driving the refinement, CHAMP1. | Phase 4 is similar to phase 2. The only thing which has changed is the mesh. Because of this, all the concepts which depend on it must be rebuilt. Today, there is no possibility either of reusing the old concepts, or of destroying them automatically. Then, one may continue, as many times as one wishes, the phase 3/phase 4 pair. This is done either by duplicating the instructions, or by writing a Python loop. See reference [bib1] for a general presentation of mesh adaptation and of HOMARD, accompanied by examples. 3.2 Operation of the macro-command Phase 3 carries out the adaptation of the mesh. It is activated by the macro-command MACR_ADAP_MAIL, described in this document. Its essential argument is the name of the concept of the current mesh and the name which will be given to the concept of the future mesh. The other mandatory datum is the type of adaptation which one wishes: free refinement or coarsening, that is to say according to the values taken by a field on the mesh cells of the mesh, or according to a geometric zone, or uniform refinement or coarsening, that is to say that all the mesh cells are treated in the same way. The other data then depend on the options retained. In addition to the adaptation, HOMARD can supply on request reports on the quality or the diameter of the mesh cells of the mesh, the connectivity of the analysis domain, the characteristic sizes, the over-constrained elements or a check of the non-interpenetration of the mesh cells. This information is obtained by activating the associated keywords. One will profitably look at the command MACR_INFO_MAIL U7.03.02, which makes it possible to obtain all this information, independently of any analysis. 3.3 Some comments The adapted mesh contains the same groups as the input mesh, with the following rule: a group defines the same geometric location in the two meshes. - Using a node group amounts to defining point locations. The group in the adapted mesh will be the list of the same nodes, neither more nor less, in order to represent the same points; only their numbers may have changed. - Using a group of segments amounts to defining lines. The group in the adapted mesh will be the list of the segments which represent the same lines. Depending on the adaptation mode, these segments will be either the same, up to the numbering, or the halves of the initial segments. - Using a group of triangles and/or quadrangles amounts to defining surfaces. The group in the adapted mesh will be the list of the triangles and/or quadrangles which represent the same surfaces. Depending on the adaptation mode, these mesh cells will be either the same, up to the numbering, or the fractions of the initial 2D mesh cells. - Likewise, using a group of 3D mesh cells amounts to defining volumes. The group in the adapted mesh will be the list of the 3D mesh cells which represent the same volumes. Depending on the adaptation mode, these mesh cells will be either the same, up to the numbering, or the fractions of the initial 3D mesh cells. The consequence is the following. The loadings of the mechanical or thermal analysis must exclusively be defined by groups of the dimension consistent with the phenomenon which one wants to model. Any other operation will lead to an error in the analysis on the adapted mesh. Using mesh cells defined by their number is impossible because the numbering will change. Using node groups or mesh-cell groups of the wrong dimension will not completely describe the location. For a more detailed and illustrated explanation, see: https://www.code-aster.org/outils/homard/usage/regles.fr.htm#CL When one wants to adapt a mesh several times in succession, it is fundamental to respect the chain of meshes properly. At the first iteration, the input mesh of MACR_ADAP_MAIL is the initial mesh of the case which one is treating. Then, the input mesh of a MACR_ADAP_MAIL must be the output mesh of the previous MACR_ADAP_MAIL. Warning: it is not enough to give a mesh which is formally the same, following a copy for example. It is imperative to supply the same concept (see also IDENTIFICATION). If one does not proceed in this way, one will lose the refinement history of the mesh cells and it will be impossible to coarsen later. More seriously, HOMARD no longer having knowledge of the additional cuttings which were introduced in order to ensure conformity, one will be led to cut mesh cells while strongly degrading their quality. If this bad data setup appears, an alarm is emitted. Mesh adaptation is possible in POURSUITE mode. The data necessary for the restart are automatically archived and then re-read in the storage directory of the database necessary to Code_Aster . Using HOMARD in restart is therefore done in the same way as using Code_Aster in restart. In general, the essential printouts supplied by HOMARD are inserted into the "mess" file in the course of the execution. In the event of an error or in information mode 3 or 4, more detailed printouts take place. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand ADAPTATION ♦ ADAPTATION= / 'RAFF_DERA' / 'RAFFINEMENT' / 'DERAFFINEMENT' / 'RAFF_DERA_ZONE' / 'RAFFINEMENT_UNIFORME' / 'DERAFFINEMENT_UNIFORME' / 'RIEN' / 'MODIFICATION' / 'LECTURE' This operand makes it possible to define the type of adaptation wished for. In the first place, one finds the adaptation modes which are driven by a field. In other words, the decision to refine or coarsen a mesh cell is taken according to the value of a field computed beforehand on this mesh cell. The choice may be made between three variants: - 'RAFF_DERA': the mesh is refined and coarsened according to the field. This is the recommended option. - 'RAFFINEMENT': only the refinement function is activated. No mesh cell will be coarsened. - 'DERAFFINEMENT': it is the opposite; only the coarsening function is activated. No mesh cell will be refined. In the second place, one may decide to adapt the mesh in geometric zones defined by boxes. All the mesh cells of which at least two nodes are present in one of these boxes will be retained. This makes it possible to carry out refinements or coarsenings a priori , without having performed an analysis. - 'RAFF_DERA_ZONE': the mesh cells of each of the boxes defined are refined or coarsened. Finally, one may activate a uniform adaptation of a mesh. In other words, all the mesh cells of the mesh are treated in the same way. The choice may be made between three variants: - 'RAFFINEMENT_UNIFORME': all the mesh cells are refined, - 'DERAFFINEMENT_UNIFORME': all the mesh cells are coarsened, - 'RIEN': all the mesh cells are kept; the mesh is the same on output as on input. Notes: When one applies a coarsening option, one only goes back on earlier refinements. This option must be understood as de-refinement. In particular, one will never be able to obtain a mesh coarser than the initial mesh. The refinement or coarsening options may apply only to part of the mesh. This is obtained by the filtering option GROUP_MA or GROUP_NO . Two complementary options exist: The first makes it possible to modify the mesh, in order to change the degree of the mesh: - 'MODIFICATION': the mesh is modified globally. The second makes it possible to read fields at the Gauss points which have been updated on the new mesh: - 'LECTURE': the fields at the Gauss points are read. 4.2 Operand MAILLAGE_N ♦ MAILLAGE_N = man The mesh of type [maillage] to be adapted or modified. Warning, the adaptation can bear only on the following mesh cells: point mesh cells, segments, triangles, quadrangles, tetrahedra, hexahedra or pentahedra. If one supplies a mesh comprising other mesh cells, for example pyramids, two situations are possible: either a stop in error, or an adaptation on the authorised zone and an unchanged restitution of the rest of the mesh. The choice between these two modes of operation is made by the keyword ELEMENTS_NON_HOMARD. The mesh is of degree 1 or 2, but it is not possible to mix the two. In all cases, the presence of enriched HEXA27 mesh cells is forbidden. When the choice has been made to read fields at the Gauss points, one gives here the mesh on which they lie. 4.3 Operand MAILLAGE_NP1 ◊ MAILLAGE_NP1 = co (manp1) The name of the concept of type [maillage] which will contain the mesh resulting from the adaptation. This name must respect the usual constraints on concept names (8 characters at most) and must not already have been used. 4.4 Operand MAILLAGE_NP1_ANNEXE ♦ MAILLAGE_NP1_ANNEXE = co (manp1ann) This operand makes it possible to produce a mesh analogous to the mesh obtained by the operand MAILLAGE_NP1, but of different degree. This is useful in thermo-mechanics, where the thermal analysis takes place on the mesh in degree 1 and the mechanics on the same mesh but in degree 2. This name must respect the usual constraints on concept names (8 characters at most) and must not already have been used. 4.5 Operand IDENTIFICATION ◊ IDENTIFICATION = refmesh Suppose that the mesh resulting from an adaptation (M1) is then slightly modified (into M1bis). If one adapts this modified mesh, one will naturally not be able to benefit from coarsening. In this situation, it is possible to indicate that the modified mesh (MAILLAGE_N=M1bis) may be considered of the same lineage as M1 by indicating IDENTIFICATION=M1. Thus, the history of M1 will be able to serve to coarsen M1bis. Of course, it is essential that the meshes be very close and that the result of the adaptation be checked carefully. 4.6 Choice of the field driving the adaptation In the case of a free adaptation, the driving of the mesh cells to be refined or coarsened is carried out by a field. This field is contained either in a result data structure, or in a field of quantities (grandeurs). This field may be an error-indicator field in the numerical sense of the term (QIRE_ELEM for example) but this is not mandatory; any field may be used. One may for example drive the adaptation by the stress field or by a field built on purpose such as a distance or a damage criterion. It is enough that this field be defined by its name as described in the documents U4.81.01, U4.81.02 or U4.81.03. If the field is a field at the nodes, the refinement/coarsening decision will be taken on each edge according to the values of the field on its nodes. If the field is a field constant per element, it is this value which will drive the refinement/coarsening of the mesh cell. If the field is a field at the nodes per element or at the Gauss points, the algorithm will rely on the maximum value in the mesh cell in order to decide on the refinement/coarsening. 4.6.1 Operand RESULTAT_N / ◊ RESULTAT_N = resun This operand makes it possible to designate the concept of type [resultat] which contains the field to be used for free adaptation. 4.6.1.1 Operand NOM_CHAM ◊ NOM_CHAM = nomsymb One specifies here which field is used to drive the adaptation. Warning: The field must be present in the result; if it is absent, it is not computed automatically. 4.6.2 Operand CHAM_GD / ◊ CHAM_GD = cham_gd_i This operand makes it possible to designate the concept of type [cham_gd] which contains the field to be used to drive the free adaptation. 4.6.3 Operand NOM_CMP ◊ NOM_CMP = l_cmp Name of the component of the field which must be used to drive the mesh adaptation. If several components are wished for, give the list here. If no component is defined here, the command will take all those which exist in the field transmitted. The type of taking into account of the component or components is driven by USAGE_CMP. 4.6.4 Selection of the time parameter of the field If the result data structure contains the required field for only a single order number, nothing is to be specified. It is the values of the field at this order number which will be used. Otherwise, one must specify which number is involved. This is done by the designation of an order number or of a value of time instant. Refer to the document U4.71.00 for the details on these keywords. 4.6.5 Operand USAGE_CMP ◊ USAGE_CMP = / 'NORME_L2' [DEFAUT] / 'NORME_INFINIE' / 'ABSOLU' / 'RELATIF' One specifies here how to treat the various components of the field driving the adaptation. One starts from the principle that the refinement bears on the large values examined and, symmetrically, the coarsening bears on the small values. By default, one will filter the refinement and the coarsening by examining the L2 norm of the components of the field on the mesh cells (or the nodes), that is to say the square root of the sum of the squares of the values of the components (the so-called Euclidean norm). If several components have been retained, one may choose between two types of norm: either the L2 norm, the default choice, or the infinity norm, that is to say the greatest of the absolute values of the components. If a single component is retained to drive the adaptation, the choices NORME_L2, NORME_INFINIE and ABSOLU are equivalent: one will examine the absolute value of the field. An alternative is possible: using RELATIF makes it possible to drive the adaptation with the raw values of the field. In that case, for a field whose values are negative, the refinement bearing on the maximum values, it will be the zones where the value is close to 0 which will be refined; symmetrically, the coarsening will bear on the zones where the value is very large and negative. 4.6.6 Operand USAGE_CHAMP ◊ USAGE_CHAMP= /'MAILLE' [DEFAUT] /'SAUT' By default, the driving of the adaptation is done by sorting the values of the field transmitted, mesh cell by mesh cell or node by node. With the SAUT variant, HOMARD will sort on the jump of the field between mesh cells, according to the following procedure. For each mesh cell, HOMARD begins by computing the maximum of the absolute difference between the value of the field on the current mesh cell and its value on each of the neighbouring mesh cells. This maximum is assigned to the current mesh cell. Then, one sorts the mesh cells on these maximum differences according to the usual criteria. In 2D, the neighbours examined are the triangles/quadrangles which share an edge with the mesh cell in progress. In 3D, they are the volume mesh cells which share a triangular or quadrangular face with the current mesh cell. If the field is defined by node, the neighbours are the nodes which share an edge with the current node. Note: This option makes it possible to adapt the mesh easily, setting oneself the objective of a regular variation of a field from one mesh cell to the next. Thus, choosing the type SAUT and the field SIEF_ELGA makes it possible to obtain a mesh in which the strong variations of stresses from a mesh cell to its neighbour will be reduced. 4.6.7 Operand ADAP_INIT ◊ ADAP_INIT = / 'GARDER' [DEFAUT] / 'RAFFINER' / 'DERAFFINER' When the field driving the adaptation is defined over the whole mesh, this option has no effect. Otherwise, it makes it possible to specify how the regions where this field is not defined are treated. With the GARDER variant, the mesh cells of the regions where the indicator is not defined are a priori kept as they are. This is the default option. With the RAFFINER variant, the mesh cells of the regions where the indicator is not defined are a priori cut. With the DERAFFINER variant, the mesh cells of the regions where the indicator is not defined are a priori reactivated. Obviously, this is only an initialisation and these decisions may evolve in order to ensure the conformity of the mesh, taking into account the decisions applied to the neighbouring mesh cells. Note: This option is particularly useful when one uses an indicator built from a field. For example, one uses the damage computed in a given region whereas elsewhere it is not defined. One will be able to choose not to touch the other mesh cells or to attempt to coarsen them. For example: in excavation analyses, mesh cells are removed from the model in order to simulate the digging; those mesh cells no longer carry an indicator value. If one does nothing, they remain in the mesh. If one chooses the DERAFFINER variant, they will be coarsened as the excavation progresses. 4.7 Operand CRIT_RAFF_xxxx In the case of free adaptation involving mesh refinement, one must define a high refinement criterion. All the mesh cells for which the field is greater than this criterion will be refined. It is important to look afterwards at the shape of the distribution of the field. This is possible thanks to the printouts produced by HOMARD in the mess file. One will find there in particular a table presenting this distribution in the form of a histogram; see chapter 5 for a commented example. For the choice of the criterion, four variants are possible: 4.7.1 Operand CRIT_RAFF_PE ◊ /CRIT_RAFF_PE= crp The criterion is defined by a proportion of mesh cells to be refined. It is a real number lying between 0 and 1. The process is the following: - computation of the number of mesh cells n corresponding to the proportion defined by crp, that is n=crp x total number of mesh cells - refinement of the n mesh cells with the highest value of the field. 4.7.2 Operand CRIT_RAFF_ABS /CRIT_RAFF_ABS= cra The criterion is defined by an absolute value of the field. All the mesh cells with a value greater than this value will be refined. 4.7.3 Operand CRIT_RAFF_REL /CRIT_RAFF_REL= crr The criterion is defined by a relative value of the field. It is a number lying between 0 and 1. The process is the following: - computation of the minimum and maximum values of the indicator, - computation of the value corresponding to the required proportion: v= vmin + crr(vmax-vmin), - refinement of all the mesh cells where the field is greater than this value. 4.7.4 Operand CRIT_RAFF_MS ◊ /CRIT_RAFF_MS= crms The criterion is defined by an absolute value of the field, computed as a function of the mean and of the standard deviation of this field. All the mesh cells with a value greater than this value will be refined. The criterion equals: mean + n sigma, where n is the coefficient supplied, strictly positive. 4.8 Operand CRIT_DERA_xxxx In the case of free adaptation involving coarsening, one must define a low coarsening criterion. All the mesh cells where the field is less than this criterion will be coarsened. Three variants are possible. 4.8.1 Operand CRIT_DERA_PE ◊ /CRIT_DERA_PE= cdp The criterion is defined by a proportion of mesh cells to be coarsened. It is a number lying between 0 and 1. The process is the following: - computation of the number of mesh cells n corresponding to the proportion defined by cdp, that is n=cdp x - coarsening of the n mesh cells with the lowest field value. 4.8.2 Operand CRIT_DERA_ABS /CRIT_DERA_ABS= cda The criterion is defined by an absolute value of the field. All the mesh cells with a field value less than this value will be coarsened. 4.8.3 Operand CRIT_DERA_REL /CRIT_DERA_REL= cdr The criterion is defined by a relative value of the field. It is a number lying between 0 and 1. The process is the following: - computation of the minimum and maximum values of the indicator, - computation of the error value v corresponding to the proportion cdr such that: v= vmin + cdr(vmax-vmin), - coarsening of all the mesh cells where the field is less than this value. 4.8.4 Operand CRIT_DERA_MS ◊ /CRIT_DERA_MS= cdms The criterion is defined by an absolute value of the field, computed as a function of the mean and of the standard deviation of this field. All the mesh cells with a value less than this value will be coarsened. The criterion equals: mean - n sigma, where n is the coefficient supplied, strictly positive. 4.9 Keyword ZONE ♦ ZONE=_F ( In the case of a request for adaptation by zone, one must define at least one zone. This keyword is to be used as many times as one wants to define adaptation zones. The principle is the following: one defines a zone by coordinates, then each mesh cell of which at least one of the edges lies in this zone will be selected. One has the choice between several types of zone. Warning: For an analysis which would be 2D, the zone types are in fact rectangles or circles. But as the notion of a strictly 2D mesh is unknown in Code_Aster at the time of the creation of the commands, one will assume that the 3rd coordinate z is zero. 4.9.1 Type of the zone ♦ TYPE= / 'RECTANGLE' / 'BOITE' / 'DISQUE' / 'SPHERE' / 'CYLINDRE' / 'DISQUE_PERCE' / 'TUYAU' This operand makes it possible to define the type of zone wished for. 4.9.2 Use of the zone ♦ USAGE= / 'RAFFINEMENT' [DEFAUT] 'DERAFFINEMENT' This operand makes it possible to define the use assigned to the zone. With the choice 'RAFFINEMENT', all the edges both of whose ends belong to the zone will be cut. With the choice 'DERAFFINEMENT', all the edges both of whose ends belong to the zone will be reactivated. 4.9.3 Case of the rectangle 4.9.3.1 Operands X_MINI, X_MAXI, Y_MINI, Y_MAXI ♦ X_MINI = x_mini ♦ X_MAXI = x_maxi ♦ Y_MINI = y_mini ♦ Y_MAXI = y_maxi These are the extreme values of the coordinates of the rectangle bounding the mesh cells to be refined. 4.9.4 Case of the parallelepiped box 4.9.4.1 Operands X_MINI, X_MAXI, Y_MINI, Y_MAXI, Z_MINI, Z_MAXI ♦ X_MINI = x_mini ♦ X_MAXI = x_maxi ♦ Y_MINI = y_mini ♦ Y_MAXI = y_maxi ♦ Z_MINI = z_mini ♦ Z_MAXI = z_maxi These are the extreme values of the coordinates of the box bounding the mesh cells to be refined. 4.9.5 Case of the disc 4.9.5.1 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre These are the coordinates of the centre of the disc. 4.9.5.2 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of the disc. 4.9.6 Case of the sphere 4.9.6.1 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE, Z_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre ♦ Z_CENTRE = z_centre These are the coordinates of the centre of the sphere. 4.9.6.2 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of the sphere. 4.9.7 Case of the cylinder The cylinder is defined by an axis and a radius. It is bounded by two planes perpendicular to the axis. The first plane is positioned by a point on the axis. The second plane is at a distance of one height from the first, in the direction of the axial vector defined. 4.9.7.1 Operands X_AXE, Y_AXE, Z_AXE ♦ X_AXE = x_axe ♦ Y_AXE = y_axe ♦ Z_AXE = z_axe These are the coordinates of the direction vector of the axis of the cylinder. The orientation is of no importance. The vector is not necessarily normalised. 4.9.7.2 Operands X_BASE, Y_BASE, Z_BASE ♦ X_BASE = x_base ♦ Y_BASE = y_base ♦ Z_BASE = z_base These are the coordinates of a point at the base of the cylinder and lying on the axis. 4.9.7.3 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of the cylinder. 4.9.7.4 Operand HAUTEUR ♦ HAUTEUR = hauteur It is the height of the cylinder. 4.9.8 Case of a pierced disc 4.9.8.1 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre These are the coordinates of the centre of the disc. 4.9.8.2 Operands RAYON_INT, RAYON_EXT ♦ RAYON_INT = rayon_int ♦ RAYON_EXT = rayon_ext These are the inner and outer radii of the pierced disc. 4.9.9 Case of the pipe The pipe is defined by an axis and its inner and outer radii. It is bounded by two planes perpendicular to the axis. The first plane is positioned by a point on the axis. The second plane is at a distance of one height from the first, in the direction of the axial vector defined. 4.9.9.1 Operands X_AXE, Y_AXE, Z_AXE ♦ X_AXE = x_axe ♦ Y_AXE = y_axe ♦ Z_AXE = z_axe These are the coordinates of the direction vector of the axis of the pipe. The orientation is of no importance. The vector is not necessarily normalised. 4.9.9.2 Operands X_BASE, Y_BASE, Z_BASE ♦ X_BASE = x_base ♦ Y_BASE = y_base ♦ Z_BASE = z_base These are the coordinates of a point at the base of the pipe and lying on the axis. 4.9.9.3 Operands RAYON_INT, RAYON_EXT ♦ RAYON_INT = rayon_int ♦ RAYON_EXT = rayon_ext These are the inner and outer radii of the pipe. 4.9.9.4 Operand HAUTEUR ♦ HAUTEUR = hauteur It is the height of the pipe. 4.10 Operands GROUP_MA / GROUPE_NO ◊ GROUP_MA = l_grma ◊ GROUP_NO = l_grno If this option is absent, the driving of the adaptation applies to the whole mesh. If one wishes to restrict this driving to part of the mesh, one gives here the list of the groups which define this part. Example 1, in order to refine a region of the mesh uniformly: one requests uniform refinement and one gives the list of the mesh-cell groups forming this region. Example 2, in order to apply the field driving the adaptation only on certain regions: one requests refinement/coarsening with the field and one supplies the list of the mesh-cell groups forming this region. Notes: For all the 1D, 2D or 3D mesh cells contained in the groups of the list, there is refinement according to the criteria retained. For the 0D mesh cells or the nodes contained in the groups, one retains the edges both of whose ends are in these lists. The mesh cells retained are adapted, but the adaptation will certainly go a little further in order to be able to supply a conformal mesh on output. 4.11 Operand DIAM_MIN ◊ DIAM_MIN= diamin One recalls that the diameter of a mesh cell is the length of the longest segment which it is possible to draw inside it. For a triangle or a tetrahedron, the diameter is the length of the longest side. For a quadrangle, a hexahedron or a pentahedron, the diameter is the length of the longest diagonal. Giving a value to diamin makes it possible not to make a mesh extremely fine. A mesh cell which would be selected as having to be refined because of the driving field or of the geometric zone, but whose diameter is already less than this minimum value diamin, will not be cut; it will be kept as it is. Warning: it is nevertheless possible that in the end it will be cut all the same if its neighbours are, in order to respect the conformity of the final mesh. By default, no limit is given: one may obtain mesh cells as small as one wishes. 4.12 Operand NIVE_MAX ◊ NIVE_MAX= nivmax It is the maximum level of refinement of the mesh. In other words a mesh cell of the initial mesh will not be able to be divided more than nivmax times in the whole of the process. This makes it possible to ensure that the mesh will not become extremely fine in the neighbourhood of a singularity: the minimum size of an edge will be its initial size divided by 2nivmax. By default, no limit is given: one may cut as much as one wishes. 4.13 Operand NIVE_MIN ◊ NIVE_MIN= nivmin It is the minimum level of coarsening of the mesh. That is to say that only the mesh cells resulting from at least nivmin mesh cuttings may be coarsened. This makes it possible to ensure that one will not go back up too far in the coarsening: one thus keeps a minimum fineness in the mesh. By default, no limit is given: one may coarsen until the initial mesh is recovered. 4.14 Keyword MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE ◊ MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE= maf The choice of this option allows the adaptation process to follow the curvature of the boundaries of the mesh. The option applies exclusively to 1D boundaries. For 2D boundaries, one must use the option FRONTIERE_ANALYTIQUE. One supplies here a Code_Aster concept of mesh type which contains a fine mesh of the one-dimensional boundaries of the geometry. This mesh is therefore formed a priori only of segments. Their lengths are very much smaller than those of the boundary segments of the mesh to be adapted. If the adaptation process is led to cut a boundary segment, the new node will be placed on the mesh of the boundary. Thus the angles will be smoothed as the adaptations proceed. The identification of the various boundaries is done by the groups, with the following rules: - the boundaries are described by groups of segments; - a boundary is described by the same group name in the analysis mesh and in the mesh of the boundary; - a boundary can have only zero or two ends; - it is neither indispensable nor inadvisable to include the straight boundaries; - the boundary may just as well be external, the most common case, as internal, in order to separate two materials. - the boundary is not necessarily plane; it may be a curve in 3D space such as the intersection of two cylinders for example. Put another way, a group of boundary segments must comprise a list of segments forming a line. Note: One will look at the test cases zzzz121d, zzzz175a, zzzz175c and zzzz259a for examples of driving the boundary following, as well as the HOMARD web site for a graphical illustration of the result obtained. Example: | Let us consider a two-dimensional object whose boundary is not always straight. This boundary will have been meshed by SEG2 or SEG3 elements both in the analysis mesh and in the auxiliary mesh. These boundary mesh cells are placed in the same groups. | | | --- | --- | | The wrong solution is this one: locate the mesh cells of the curved boundaries and store them all in the same group. HOMARD does not know how to handle a split boundary; there will be a stop with a message meaning that the line is in several pieces. | | | A first good way of proceeding consists in creating as many groups as there are zones of interest. | | | Another acceptable solution consists in grouping by section. Between the two methods, there is no difference for HOMARD: the essential point is not to go all the way round (otherwise, no end) and not to cut (otherwise, too many ends!). One will choose the method which is easiest to carry out in the mesher. | | 4.14.1 Operand GROUP_MA_FRONT ◊ GROUP_MA_FRONT= l_grma If this option is absent, the following of the boundary is done for all the groups defined in the mesh of the boundary. If one wishes to restrict this following to part of the boundary, one gives here the list of the groups of segments which define this part of the boundary. 4.15 Keyword FRONTIERE_ANALYTIQUE ◊ FRONTIERE_ANALYTIQUE= _F ( This keyword is to be entered as many times as one wants to define analytical boundaries. The choice of this option allows the adaptation process to follow the curvature of the boundaries of the mesh. The option applies exclusively to 2D boundaries. For 1D boundaries, one must use the option MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE. One supplies here the analytical description of each boundary to be followed. If the adaptation process is led to cut a boundary mesh cell, the new node will be positioned on the boundary, via its description. Thus the angles will be smoothed as the adaptations proceed. Note: One will look at the test cases zzzz175a, zzzz175c and zzzz259a for an example of analytical boundary following. When one launches the adaptation several times in succession, it is indispensable that each analytical boundary be defined in the same way at each invocation of MACR_ADAP_MAIL : name, type, list of groups, geometric characteristics. 4.15.1 Name of the boundary ♦ NOM = nom [K] This operand makes it possible to define the name associated with the boundary. The choice of this name is free. 4.15.2 Type of the boundary ♦ TYPE = / 'SPHERE' / 'CYLINDRE' / 'CONE_A' / 'CONE_R' / 'TORE' This operand makes it possible to define the type of boundary wished for: sphere, cylinder. 4.15.3 Operand GROUP_MA ♦ GROUP_MA = l_grma One gives here the list of the mesh-cell groups which define the part of the boundary represented by this analytical definition. 4.15.4 Case of the sphere 4.15.4.1 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE, Z_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre ♦ Z_CENTRE = z_centre These are the coordinates of the centre of the sphere. 4.15.4.2 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of the sphere. 4.15.5 Case of the cylinder The cylinder is defined by an axis, a point on the axis and a radius. 4.15.5.1 Operands X_AXE, Y_AXE, Z_AXE ♦ X_AXE = x_axe ♦ Y_AXE = y_axe ♦ Z_AXE = z_axe These are the coordinates of the direction vector of the axis of the cylinder. The orientation is of no importance. The vector is not necessarily normalised. 4.15.5.2 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE, Z_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre ♦ Z_CENTRE = z_centre These are the coordinates of a point lying on the axis of the cylinder. 4.15.5.3 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of the cylinder. 4.15.6 Case of the cone defined by an angle The cone is defined by an axis, a centre on the axis and an angle. 4.15.6.1 Operands X_AXE, Y_AXE, Z_AXE ♦ X_AXE = x_axe ♦ Y_AXE = y_axe ♦ Z_AXE = z_axe These are the coordinates of the direction vector of the axis of the cone. The orientation is of no importance. The vector is not necessarily normalised. 4.15.6.2 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE, Z_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre ♦ Z_CENTRE = z_centre These are the coordinates of the centre on the axis of the cone. 4.15.6.3 Operand ANGLE ♦ ANGLE = angle It is the angle in degrees of the cone. 4.15.7 Case of the cone defined by radii The cone is defined by two points on its axis and the two radii corresponding to these positions. 4.15.7.1 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE, Z_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre ♦ Z_CENTRE = z_centre These are the coordinates of the first point lying on the axis of the cylinder. 4.15.7.2 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of the cone for this first position on the axis. 4.15.7.3 Operands X_CENTRE2, Y_CENTRE2, Z_CENTRE2 ♦ X_CENTRE2 = x_centre2 ♦ Y_CENTRE2 = y_centre2 ♦ Z_CENTRE2 = z_centre2 These are the coordinates of the second point lying on the axis of the cylinder. 4.15.7.4 Operand RAYON2 ♦ RAYON2 = rayon2 It is the radius of the cone for this second position on the axis. 4.15.8 Case of the torus The torus is defined by an axis, a centre and the two radii. 4.15.8.1 Operands X_AXE, Y_AXE, Z_AXE ♦ X_AXE = x_axe ♦ Y_AXE = y_axe ♦ Z_AXE = z_axe These are the coordinates of the direction vector of the axis of the torus. The orientation is of no importance. The vector is not necessarily normalised. 4.15.8.2 Operands X_CENTRE, Y_CENTRE, Z_CENTRE ♦ X_CENTRE = x_centre ♦ Y_CENTRE = y_centre ♦ Z_CENTRE = z_centre These are the coordinates of the centre of the torus. 4.15.8.3 Operand RAYON ♦ RAYON = rayon It is the radius of revolution of the torus. 4.15.8.4 Operand RAYON2 ♦ RAYON2 = rayon2 It is the radius of the primary circle which revolves about the axis of the torus. 4.16 Keyword MAJ_CHAM ◊ MAJ_CHAM= _F ( This keyword is to be used as many times as one has fields to be updated from the old mesh onto the adapted mesh. This field is contained either in a result data structure, or in a field of quantities (grandeurs). Note: One must make sure that the field is defined on a mesh identical to the mesh entered under the operand MAILLAGE_N . 4.16.1 Operand RESULTAT / ◊ RESULTAT=resu Name of the [resultat] concept containing the field to be updated. 4.16.1.1 Operand NOM_CHAM ◊ NOM_CHAM=nomsymb [:ref: K16 ] Symbolic name of the field which one wishes to express on the new mesh. 4.16.2 Operand CHAM_GD / ◊ CHAM_GD= cham_gd Name of the [cham_gd] concept containing the field to be updated. 4.16.3 Operand NOM_CMP ◊ NOM_CMP = l_cmp Name of the component of the field which must be updated. If several components are wished for, give the list here. If no component is defined here, the command will take all those which exist in the field transmitted. 4.16.4 Selection of the time parameter of the field to be updated The selection of the order number associated with the field to be interpolated is done by the designation of an order number or of a value of time instant. Refer to the document U4.71.00 for the details on these keywords. 4.16.5 Operand TYPE_MAJ ◊ TYPE_MAJ = / 'AUTO' [DEFAUT] / 'ISOP2' One specifies here the type of update wished for. By default, the 'AUTO' operation is ... automatic: the interpolation is carried out according to the nature of the field. For a field constant per element, if a mesh cell is cut, the value of the field is carried over as it is onto the child mesh cells. For a field at the nodes, the interpolation takes place with the P1 or P2 shape functions according to the support of the field. A variant is possible for fields at the nodes expressed on a mesh of degree 2. By specifying 'ISOP2', the interpolation is carried out by P1 shape functions expressed on the sub-mesh-cells of the element. This technique guarantees that the interpolated field respects the extreme values of the initial field on a mesh cell. For a field at the Gauss points, the update takes place only in the cases where the mesh-cell types are homogeneous between the input and the output: triangle or tetrahedron. For the quadrangles, the hexahedra or the pentahedra, nothing is done because one does not know how to define the families of Gauss points on the triangles or tetrahedra produced. For a mesh of triangles, one proceeds thus: - for a triangle unchanged after the adaptation, the values at the Gauss points are carried over identically. - for a triangle cut, into 2 or into 4, one computes the mean value of the field over all the Gauss points and this value is assigned to all the Gauss points of all the child triangles. - for a triangle which disappears (in the case of coarsening), one computes the mean of the field over all the Gauss points of this triangle and of its siblings and this value is assigned to all the Gauss points of the parent triangle which reappears. This mechanism makes it possible to guarantee that the extreme bounds are not crossed. The same technique is applied to the tetrahedra. Warning: There can be no consistency check between the type requested and the true type of the field to be interpolated. 4.16.6 Operand CHAM_MAJ ♦ CHAM_MAJ = co(chpmaj) [:ref: K8 ] Name of the concept which will contain the field expressed on the new mesh. This concept must not exist. It will be created automatically. A field at the nodes or at the elements will be read automatically by the macro-command which requests the adaptation or the modification of the mesh. It will be available in the analysis as soon as the execution of the macro-command is finished. On the other hand, this is not possible for a field expressed at the Gauss points because Code_Aster needs to know the model in order to read. For that, one must proceed in 3 stages. The field is computed by the macro-command which requested the adaptation or the modification of the mesh, as for a field at the nodes. Then, a new model must be applied to the new mesh by the command AFFE_MODELE. Finally, the reading will be done by a new invocation of MACR_ADAP_MAIL by means of the parameter ADAPTATION = 'LECTURE' and the supply of the mesh and of the model. Note: One will look at the test case zzzz175b for an example of updating and reading of fields of different types. 4.16.7 Operand TYPE_CHAM ♦ TYPE_CHAM= /'NOEU_DEPL_R' /'NOEU_TEMP_R' /'ELGA_SIEF_R' /etc ... One designates here the type of the concept to be updated on the new mesh. The name of this type is built with the usual logic of Code_Aster . The first 4 characters are 'NOEU', 'ELEM' or 'ELGA'. One then finds '_'. The following sequence defines the type of field: 'TEMP', 'DEPL', etc. The name ends with '_R' for a real field. Example: 'NOEU_TEMP_R', 'NOEU_DEPL_R', etc. Warning: There can be no consistency check between the type requested and the true type of the field to be interpolated. 4.17 Keyword ADD_CHAM ◊ ADD_CHAM= _F ( This keyword is to be used in order to produce particular fields on the adapted mesh. 4.17.1 Operand CHAM_GD ♦ CHAM_GD= co(chpmaj) [:ref: K8 ] Name of the concept which will contain the field expressed on the new mesh. This concept must not exist. It will be created automatically. Note: One will look at the test cases zzzz121b and zzzz121f for an example of additions of fields of different types. 4.17.2 Operand CHAM_CAT ♦ CHAM_CAT= /'NIVEAU' /'QUALITE' /'DIAMETRE' One designates here the category of the field which one wants to produce. With 'NIVEAU ', the field produced will contain for each mesh cell its level. One recalls that a mesh cell of the initial level is of level 0. Then a mesh cell resulting from n standard cuttings of an initial mesh cell will carry the level n . A mesh cell which ensures the conformity transition between level n and level n+1 will carry the level n+0.5 . With 'QUALITE ', the field produced will contain the value of the quality for each mesh cell. With 'DIAMETRE ', the field produced will contain the value of the diameter for each mesh cell. 4.18 Operand MODELE ◊ MODELE= modele [modele] Warning: This operand is active only when one has chosen ' LECTURE ' as the type of adaptation. This operand makes it possible to specify the model which has been assigned to the mesh on which the update of fields expressed at the Gauss points took place. Note: One will look at the test case zzzz175b for an example of updating and reading of fields at the Gauss points. 4.19 Operand DEGRE ◊ DEGRE= /'OUI' Warning: This operand is active only when one has chosen ' MODIFICATION ' as the type of adaptation. If the choice is 'OUI', the degree of the mesh is changed globally. Note: Combined with MAJ_CHAM, the operand DEGRE can be used for example for the post-processing of the pressure in THM (cf. doc U2.04.05). For certain 3D studies with large meshes, it can sometimes prove more efficient than PROJ_CHAMP. 4.20 Operand NOMBRE Note: One will consult the document U7.03.02 describing the command MACR_INFO_MAIL for comments on the outputs of the operands QUALITE, INTERPENETRATION, NOMBRE, CONNEXITE and TAILLE. ◊ NOMBRE= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] / 'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a report of the numbers of nodes and of mesh cells is printed on the message file. 4.21 Operand QUALITE ◊ QUALITE = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] / 'OUI' If the choice is 'OUI', a report of the quality of the mesh cells is printed on the message file. The quality of a triangle is defined as being the ratio between the length of the longest side and the radius of the inscribed circle. The quality of a quadrangle is defined as the quotient of the product of the greatest length and of the averages over the sides and the diagonals by the smallest of the areas of the triangles internal to the quadrangles. Likewise, the quality of a tetrahedron is defined as being the ratio between the length of the longest side and the radius of the inscribed sphere. These ratios are normalised so as to equal 1 in the case of an equilateral triangle, of a square, of an equilateral tetrahedron or of an equilateral hexahedron. For any non-equilateral element, the quality is greater than 1. See reference [bib1] for detailed explanations. The result is presented in the form of tables, with the extreme values. The interpretation of the values produced depends on the numerical method employed for the analysis. Depending on whether the problem is isotropic or not, depending on the rapidity of the spatial variation of the data, depending on the analysis technique, one and the same mesh cell may lead to a good Jacobian or not. The essential point in a first stage is to locate the frankly bad mesh cells. If one observes that the maximum of quality exceeds 100, or even 1,000 or 100,000, one must be concerned: one or several mesh cells are very distorted and the mesh is certainly to be redone. In a second stage, this quality information must make it possible to compare two a priori correct meshes, without a large value. If the problem is isotropic, one will have an interest in using the mesh with the quality distribution closest to 1. One will find illustrations of quality values of various mesh cells in [Ref.5]. 4.22 Operand DIAMETRE ◊ DIAMTRE = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] / 'OUI' If the choice is 'OUI', a report of the diameters of the mesh cells is printed on the message file. The diameter of a mesh cell is defined as the length of the longest segment which it is possible to insert into the mesh cell. For a triangle or a tetrahedron, the diameter corresponds to the length of the longest side. For a quadrangle, a hexahedron, a pentahedron or a pyramid, the diameter is the maximum between the length of the longest side and the length of the longest diagonal. The result is presented in the form of tables, with the extreme values. 4.23 Operand INTERPENETRATION ◊ INTERPENETRATION = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] / 'OUI' If the choice is 'OUI', one checks that the mesh is correct from the point of view of overlap: no mesh cell enters another. 4.24 Operand TAILLE ◊ TAILLE = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] / 'OUI' If the choice is 'OUI', a report of the sizes of the subdomains is printed on the message file. A subdomain is defined as a set of mesh cells of the same dimension and belonging to the same groups. 4.25 Operand CONNEXITE ◊ CONNEXITE = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] / 'OUI' If the choice is 'OUI', a report of the connectivities is printed on the message file. One will then know whether the segments, the 2D elements (triangles and quadrangles taken together) or the 3D mesh cells (tetrahedra, hexahedra, pentahedra and pyramids taken together) are in a single piece or distributed in several blocks. One will also know the number of holes in the structure: the through-holes or the internal holes. 4.26 Operand PROP_CALCUL ◊ PROP_CALCUL = / 'NON' [DEFAUT] / 'OUI' If the choice is 'OUI', a diagnosis of the properties of the mesh cells as elements for the analysis is printed on the message file. One counts the number of over-constrained elements: the elements all of whose vertices lie on the boundary. One counts the volume mesh cells (resp. surface mesh cells) which touch the boundary of the domain but which are not bordered by surface mesh cells (resp. line mesh cells). 4.27 The histories It must be carefully noted that the mesh will be able to be coarsened only within one and the same study. If one executes a new analysis (use of DEBUT and not POURSUITE), the refinement history will be lost. 4.28 Operand LANGUE ◊ LANGUE = / 'FRANCAIS' [DEFAUT] / 'FRENCH' / 'ANGLAIS' / 'ENGLISH' This operand specifies the language in which the messages coming from HOMARD are printed. 4.29 Operand VERSION_HOMARD ◊ VERSION_HOMARD = / 'V11_10' [DEFAUT] / 'V11_N' / 'V11_N_PERSO' This operand makes it possible to select the version of HOMARD which is used for the adaptation. By default, HOMARD 11.10 is launched. This is the reference version. The choice 'V11_N' activates version 11.n of HOMARD, which is the development version. The choice 'V11_N_PERSO' activates a development version specific to the user. This option allows the HOMARD development team to develop new functionalities. It also makes it possible to let the user benefit from an innovation in HOMARD before it is put into service in Code_Aster . 4.30 Operand LOGICIEL ◊ LOGICIEL= logiciel [K] This option proposes to use another coupling interface between Code_Aster and HOMARD than the one supplied by default in the directory of the tools associated with Code_Aster . This option is in fact reserved for the HOMARD development team in order to develop new functionalities. It makes it possible to test new features before having modified the driving macro-command. 4.31 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = unite [I] This option is possible only if one has activated the development version of HOMARD, 11.n. The data file transmitted by the user under this logical unit number will be transmitted directly as a complement to the HOMARD configuration file. This option is in fact intended for the HOMARD development team in order to develop new functionalities. It makes it possible to test new features before having modified the driving macro-command. 4.32 Operand ELEMENTS_ACCEPTES ◊ ELEMENTS_ACCEPTES = / 'HOMARD' [DEFAUT] / 'IGNORE_PYRA' In its current version, HOMARD knows how to read all the types of mesh cells but makes the adaptation bear only on certain ones: point mesh cells, segments, triangles, quadrangles, tetrahedra, hexahedra or pentahedra. The mesh is of degree 1 or 2, but it is not possible to mix the two. By retaining the option 'HOMARD', the transmission of a mesh containing something other than these types of mesh cells will lead to a stop in error. This is the default option. By choosing the option 'IGNORE_PYRA', one will be able to transmit a mesh comprising pyramids. The adaptation will bear only on the zones authorised by HOMARD. If, as a consequence of the propagation of the refinement, a forbidden zone comes to be touched, there will be a stop in error. Otherwise, when the refinement is limited to the authorised zone, the other mesh cells are returned without change. In all cases, the presence of enriched HEXA27 mesh cells is forbidden. 4.33 Operand INFO ◊ INFO = / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 If INFO equals 1, the printouts are minimal; one obtains only those which have explicitly been requested, the quality of the mesh cells for example, and the possible error messages. If INFO equals 2, one will obtain the messages emitted by the commands underlying the macro-command: IMPR_RESU, LIRE_MAILLAGE, LIRE_RESU. If INFO equals 3, one will have the standard messages of HOMARD, summarising the execution. If INFO equals 4, one will have all the messages emitted by HOMARD, for the purpose of debugging. 5 Example One will profitably look at the command files associated with the test cases zzzz121a, b, c, d, e, f and zzzz175a, b. They express the mesh-adaptation processes either by chaining of the commands or in the form of a loop in the Python language. Here is an example of parameter setting of the macro-command. MACR_ADAP_MAIL ( ADAPTATION= 'RAFF_DERA', MAILLAGE_N= mun, MAILLAGE_NP1= CO ("mdeux"), RESULTAT_N= remeun, NOM_CHAM= 'QIRE_ELEM', NOM_CMP= 'ERREST' NUME_ORDRE= 3, CRIT_RAFF_PE= 0.01, CRIT_DERA_PE= 0.25, NIVE_MAX= 5 MAJ_CHAM = _F ( RESULTAT= rethun, NOM_CHAM= 'TEMP', TYPE_CHAM= 'NOEU_TEMP_R', INST= 12.5, CHAM_MAJ= CO ("tempdeux") ), QUALITE= 'OUI', ) This sequence will adapt the mesh contained in the concept mun and return a mesh concept of name mdeux. The adaptation is done by free refinement and coarsening, according to the field contained in the field QIRE_ELEM of the result remeun, at the 3rd time instant; the component used is ERREST. The mesh cells will be classified according to their decreasing error level. The first % will be refined; the last 25% will be candidates for coarsening. No mesh cell of the final mesh must result from more than 5 refinements. The field TEMP of the result rethun at time instant 12.5 is expressed on the mesh mun. It will be expressed on the mesh mdeux in the form of the nodal temperature field tempdeux. A summary of the quality of the mesh cells of the new mesh is produced. One does not check the interpenetration of the mesh cells. Here is an example of the table presenting the distribution of the field driving the adaptation of the mesh. The diagnosis of the distribution of the field driving the mesh adaptation first recalls the extreme values encountered in the current analysis. Here the minimum is 0.353585x10-5 and the maximum is 0.33395x10-3. The mean value, 0.66371x10-4, and the standard deviation, 0.51323x10-4, are given. Then the distribution by equidistant interval starting from the optimum value, 0, is presented. One sees that for 880 triangles, the value of the field is less than 1.70x10-4, that is 94.02 % of the total number of triangles. Then, for 21 triangles the value of the field lies between 1.70x10-4 and 1.87x10-4, that is 2.24 % of the total number of triangles. Cumulatively, one therefore observes that for 901 = 880 + 21 triangles, the value of the field is less than 1.87x10-4, that is 96.26 % of the total. And so on. For example, for 99.79 % of the mesh cells, the value of the field is less than 2.55x10-4. On the previous figure, one can see the representation, in the form of a histogram, of the percentages of mesh cells in each of the value ranges concerned. As one could also observe in the previous table, one observes that very few mesh cells concentrate the high values. By displaying a representation of the cumulative percentage of mesh cells in a given value range, one has the following figure. From this distribution of the values, one can deduce two consequences for the refinement strategies. If one requests a refinement on a relative criterion of the value of the field, keyword CRIT_RAFF_REL, this amounts to selecting the mesh cells which lie to the right of the vertical line passing through this criterion. For example if one requests CRIT_RAFF_REL = 0.77, one will select all the mesh cells whose error is greater than 0.35358x10-5 + 0.77x(0.33395x10-3-0.35358x10-5), that is 2.58x10-3. One observes that this corresponds to very few mesh cells: only 2 exceed this value, that is 0.21% of the total. One had the impression of requesting an important refinement, 0.77 that is roughly a quarter, but in fact one refines almost nothing. If one requests a refinement on a percentage of mesh cells, keyword CRIT_RAFF_PE, this amounts to selecting the mesh cells which lie above the horizontal line passing through this criterion. For example if one requests CRIT_RAFF_PE = 0.10, one will select the 10% worst mesh cells, that is 93 mesh cells. This is the horizontal line at 90%. Among those mesh cells, the «least bad» ones carry a value less than 1.36x10-4, that is 40% of the maximum value. This is fairly effective since one will have trapped the large discrepancies. The consequence of these notes is that it is appropriate to carry out a first analysis of the distribution of the values of the field before choosing the type and the values of the refinement criteria. It is indeed useless, or even costly in terms of increase of the mesh size, to refine in zones where the field is not very strong. The adaptation will be all the more efficient if one has been able to reduce the mesh cells with a high value until a balance is obtained in the mesh. 6 Bibliography 1. u7.03.02 Macro-command MACR_INFO_MAIL u7.03.02 Macro-command MACR_INFO_MAIL 1 Purpose Provide information on the quality of a mesh. This macro-command makes it possible to obtain information on a mesh, of degree 1 or 2, containing point mesh cells, segments, triangles, quadrangles, tetrahedra, hexahedra or pentahedra. The printout is directed to the message file. One first finds an overall summary of the mesh: dimension, degree, number of nodes, number of mesh cells, extreme dimensions. Then six items of information are available: - a summary of the quality of the mesh cells, - a summary of the diameter of the mesh cells, - a check of the non-interpenetration of the mesh cells, - a summary of the connectivity of the mesh - a summary of the size of the various subdomains - the number of over-constrained elements This analysis is performed by the mesh-adaptation software HOMARD. For further details, see: https://www.code-aster.org/outils/homard or refer to the documents cited in the bibliography. 2 Syntax MACR_INFO_MAIL( ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, / 3, / 4, ◆ MAILLAGE = maillage, ◇ MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE = maillage, # Si: exists("MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE") ◇ GROUP_MA_FRONT = grma, ◇ NOMBRE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ QUALITE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ CONNEXITE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ TAILLE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ INTERPENETRATION = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ◇ PROP_CALCUL = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ DIAMETRE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ LANGUE = / "FRANCAIS" (par défaut), / "FRENCH", / "ANGLAIS", / "ENGLISH", ◇ ELEMENTS_ACCEPTES = / "HOMARD" (par défaut), / "IGNORE_PYRA", ◇ VERSION_HOMARD = / "V11_10" (par défaut), / "V11_N", / "V11_N_PERSO", ◇ LOGICIEL = text, # Si: is_in("VERSION_HOMARD", ('V11_N','V11_N_PERSO')) ◇ UNITE = unit, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE ♦ MAILLAGE = ma The mesh of type [maillage] to be analysed. Caution: the analysis will cover only the nodes, the point mesh cells, the segments, the triangles, the quadrangles, the tetrahedra, the hexahedra or the pentahedra. If one supplies a mesh containing other mesh cells, for example pyramids, two cases are possible: either an error stop, or information on the authorised zone, the rest of the mesh being ignored. The choice between these two modes of operation is made by the keyword ELEMENTS_NON_HOMARD. The mesh is of degree 1 or 2, but it is not possible to mix the two. In all cases, the presence of enriched HEXA27 mesh cells is forbidden. 3.2 Operand NOMBRE ◊ NOMBRE= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] /'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a summary of the numbers of nodes and of mesh cells is printed to the message file. 3.3 Operand QUALITE ◊ QUALITE= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] /'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a summary of the quality of the mesh cells is printed to the message file. The quality of a triangle is defined as the ratio between the length of the longest side and the radius of the inscribed circle. The quality of a quadrangle is defined as the quotient of the product of the greatest length and of the averages over the sides and the diagonals by the smallest of the areas of the triangles internal to the quadrangles. Likewise, the quality of a tetrahedron is defined as the ratio between the length of the longest side and the radius of the inscribed sphere. The quality of a hexahedron is defined as the worst of the qualities of the inscribed tetrahedra. All these quality measures are normalised so as to equal 1 in the case of an equilateral triangle, a square, an equilateral tetrahedron or a cube. For any non-equilateral mesh cell, the quality is greater than 1. See reference [bib1]_ for detailed explanations. The result is presented in the form of tables, with the extreme values. The interpretation of the values produced depends on the numerical method employed for the analysis. Depending on whether the problem is isotropic or not, on the rapidity of the spatial variation of the data, and on the analysis technique, one and the same mesh cell may or may not lead to a good Jacobian. The essential point, in a first stage, is to identify the frankly bad mesh cells. If one observes that the maximum quality exceeds 100, or even 1,000 or 100,000, one must be concerned: one or more mesh cells are very distorted and the mesh certainly needs to be redone. In a second stage, this quality information should make it possible to compare two a priori correct meshes, without a large value. If the problem is isotropic, it will be advantageous to use the mesh with the quality distribution closest to 1. Illustrations of quality values for various mesh cells will be found in [bib2]_. 3.4 Operand DIAMETRE ◊ DIAMETRE= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] /'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a summary of the diameters of the mesh cells is printed to the message file. The diameter of a mesh cell is defined as the length of the longest segment that it is possible to insert into the mesh cell. For a triangle or a tetrahedron, the diameter corresponds to the length of the longest side. For a quadrangle, a hexahedron, a pentahedron or a pyramid, the diameter is the maximum between the length of the longest side and the length of the longest diagonal. The result is presented in the form of tables, with the extreme values. 3.5 Operand CONNEXITE ◊ CONNEXITE= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] /'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a summary of the connectivities is printed to the message file. One will then know whether the segments, the 2D mesh cells (triangles and quadrangles taken together) or the 3D mesh cells (tetrahedra, hexahedra, pentahedra and pyramids taken together) are in a single piece or distributed over several blocks. One will also know the number of holes in the structure: the through-holes or the internal holes. 3.6 Operand TAILLE ◊ TAILLE= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] /'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a summary of the sizes of the subdomains is printed to the message file. A subdomain is defined as a set of mesh cells of the same dimension and belonging to the same groups. 3.7 Operand PROP_CALCUL ◊ PROP_CALCUL= /'OUI' [DEFAUT] /'NON' If the choice is 'OUI', a diagnostic on the properties of the mesh cells as elements for the analysis is printed to the message file. One counts the number of over-constrained elements: the elements all of whose vertices lie on the boundary. One counts the volume mesh cells (respectively surface mesh cells) which touch the boundary of the domain but which are not bordered by surface mesh cells (respectively line mesh cells). 3.8 Operand INTERPENETRATION ◊ INTERPENETRATION= /'OUI' /'NON' [DEFAUT] If the choice is 'OUI', one checks that the mesh is correct from the point of view of overlap: no mesh cell has one of its vertices inside another mesh cell. Caution: this operation may prove costly for large meshes, hence the default choice ‘NON’. 3.9 Operand MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE ◊ MAILLAGE_FRONTIERE=maf The choice of this option means that the segments forming the boundary of the analysis mesh or an internal boundary are attached to a fine description of this boundary. This fine mesh is transmitted here. The link is made by the segments belonging to the same groups. 3.10 Operand GROUP_MA_FRONT ◊ GROUP_MA_FRONT=l_grma If this option is absent, the link between the segments is made for all the groups present in the boundary mesh. If the link is made only for a few groups, they are designated here. 3.11 Operand ELEMENTS_ACCEPTES ◊ ELEMENTS_ACCEPTES= /'HOMARD' [DEFAUT] /'IGNORE_PYRA' In its current version, HOMARD only applies the information to certain mesh cells: point mesh cells, segments, triangles, quadrangles, tetrahedra, hexahedra, pentahedra of degree 1 or 2. By retaining the option 'HOMARD', the transmission of a mesh containing something other than these types of mesh cells will lead to an error stop. This is the default option. By choosing the option 'IGNORE_PYRA', one will be able to analyse a mesh containing pyramids. The information will cover only the zones authorised by HOMARD; the rest of the mesh will be ignored. In all cases, the presence of enriched HEXA27 mesh cells is forbidden. 3.12 Operand VERSION_HOMARD ◊ VERSION_HOMARD= /'V11_10' [DEFAUT] /'V11_N' /'V11_N_PERSO' This operand makes it possible to select the version of HOMARD which is used for the adaptation. By default, HOMARD 11.10 is launched. This is the reference version. The choice 'V11_N' activates version 11.n of HOMARD, which is the development version. The choice 'V11_N_PERSO' activates a development version specific to the user. This option allows the HOMARD development team to develop new functionalities. It also allows the user to benefit from an innovation in HOMARD before it is put into service in Code_Aster . 3.13 Operand LANGUE ◊ LANGUE= /'FRANCAIS' [DEFAUT] /'FRENCH' /'ANGLAIS' /'ENGLISH' This operand specifies the language in which the messages issued by HOMARD are printed. 3.14 Operand LOGICIEL ◊ LOGICIEL= logiciel [K] This option proposes using a coupling interface between Code_Aster and HOMARD other than the one supplied by default in the directory of the tools associated with Code_Aster . This option is in fact reserved for the HOMARD development team in order to develop new functionalities. It makes it possible to test new features before having modified the driving macro-command. 3.15 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE= unite [I] This option is possible only if one has activated the development version of HOMARD, 11.n. The data file transmitted by the user under this logical unit number will be transmitted directly as a complement to the HOMARD configuration file. This option is in fact reserved for the HOMARD development team in order to develop new functionalities. It makes it possible to test new features before having modified the driving macro-command. 3.16 Operand INFO ◊ INFO= /1 /2 /3 /4 If INFO is equal to 1, the printouts are minimal; one obtains only those which have explicitly been requested, the quality of the mesh cells for example, and any error messages. If INFO is equal to 2, one will obtain the messages issued by the commands underlying the macro-command: IMPR_RESU, LIRE_MAILLAGE, LIRE_RESU. If INFO is equal to 3, one will have the standard messages of HOMARD, summarising the execution. If INFO is equal to 4, one will have all the messages issued by HOMARD, for debugging purposes. 4 Example MACR_INFO_MAIL(MAILLAGE=MARTEAU, TAILLE='OUI', CONNEXITE='OUI', INTERPENETRATION='OUI', DIAMETRE='OUI', QUALITE='OUI') This sequence will write the general information (dimension, degree, number of nodes and of mesh cells, ...) then a diagnostic on the quality, the diameters and the interpenetration of the mesh cells used in the mesh MARTEAU, as well as the size and the connectivity of the various subdomains. The default version of HOMARD is used. Maillage a analyser MARTEAU Date de creation : lundi 15 fevrier 2010 a 15 h 59 mn 22 s Dimension : 2 Degre : 1 C'est un maillage de depart. u7.03.03 Python methods for driving GMSH u7.03.03 Python methods for driving GMSH Summary: This document presents the supervisor that makes it possible to drive GMSH from Python, and therefore from the Aster command file. This supervisor produces any type of 2D mesh using the GMSH software (https://gmsh.info). It is used in particular in Aster by the interactive post-processing tool STANLEY in order to generate mesh elements for the post-processing, but it can be extended to other applications: parametric meshing, remeshing, etc. 1 Directions for use There are four steps to follow in order to produce a mesh with the GMSH supervisor: 1. Definition of the geometry; 2. Definition of the discretisations; 3. Creation of the GMSH mesh and of the associated GROUP_MA and «Physical» objects; 4. Import of the GMSH mesh into Aster. Simple example of use: In the following example, the functionalities of the supervisor are used to generate the mesh of a rectangular plate: Geometry from Utilitai.sup_gmsh import larg = 5. H_beton = 3. H_S1 = 4. t_beton = 25. prog_S1 = 1.1 The module is imported and a few parameters are defined. Geometry O = Point(0 , 0 ) A = Point(larg, 0 ) B = Point(larg, H_beton) C = Point(0 , H_beton) D = Point(0 , -H_S1 ) E = Point(larg, -H_S1 ) OA = Line(O,A) AB = Line(A,B) BC = Line(B,C) OC = Line(O,C) OD = Line(O,D) DE = Line(D,E) AE = Line(A,E) S2 = Surface(OA,AB,BC,OC) S1 = Surface(OD,DE,AE,OA) Points are created, lines between the points, and surfaces from the lines. Discretisation OA.Transfinite(1) BC.Transfinite(1) DE.Transfinite(1) N_beton = int(H_beton/t_beton + 0.5) AB.Transfinite(N_beton) OC.Transfinite(N_beton) N_S1 = Progress(H_S1, r=prog_S1, h=t_beton) OD.Transfinite(N_S1,prog_S1) AE.Transfinite(N_S1,prog_S1) S2.Transfinite() S1.Transfinite() The discretisation of the lines and of the surfaces is defined. Mesh mesh = Mesh() mesh.Physical('FOND',DE) mesh.Physical('LAT_G',OC,OD) mesh.Physical('LAT_D',AB,AE) mesh.Physical('INTERFAC',OA) mesh.Physical('HAUT',BC) mesh.Physical('S2',S2) mesh.Physical('S1',S1) The mesh object is created and the mesh-cell groups are defined, which will be GROUP_MA in the Aster maillage data structure and « Physical» in GMSH (the latter will be named \mathit{GM1} , \mathit{GM2} , etc...). MA = mesh.LIRE_GMSH( MODI_QUAD = 'OUI' ) Import of the mesh into Aster: \mathit{MA} is an Aster mesh. 2 List of the available functions The list of functions is extracted directly from the source, sup_gmsh.py, which explains why it is in English. 2.1 Generic class for the geometric objects class Geometric : private attribute parameters : dictionnary of the attributes (except relation and parameters itself) see __getattr__ and __setattr__ Attributes num : index among gmsh objects md : mesh descriptor mesh : related mesh object relation : model object in case of coincidence Public methods Is_point : return true is the object inherits of the Point class Is_line : return true is the object inherits of the Line class Is_surface : return true is the object inherits of the Surface class Is_volume : return true is the object inherits of the Volume class Is_same_dimension : return true is both objects are of the same dimension (point, line, surface or volume) in -> object to compare to self Duplicate : duplicate an object and base its mesh_descriptor on the mesh_descriptor of the model Coincide : assert that an object is coincident with a model one All the attributes are then automatically read from the model object (see __setattr__ and __getattr__). in -> model object Private method Root : Provides the root object of an object, ie the object itself if there is no relation or the deepest model in case of relation. Geometric_coincide : check if a geometrical coincidence is possible return information about the coincidence, false else. in -> model object Deep_coincide : proceed recursively to ensure coincidence of the relevant sub-objects in -> model object in -> correspond (information returned by Geometric_coincide) __setattr__ : distinguish two sets of attributes relation (to express a relation with a model object in case of coincidence) all the other attributes which are stored in the dictionnary parameters instead of the usual __dict__ if there is no relation (see Coincide) and in the model object if there is a coincidence __getattr__ : if the object is related (relation <> None) the attribute is read in the model object. Else, it is read in the current object, actually in the dictionnary parameters (see __setattr__) Thanks to these two overloaded methods, the access to the attributes is usual if there is no relation whereas the attributes of the model object are accessed transparently if there is a relation. __cmp__ : The comparison of two objects involves possible coincidence. It is no more the object ids that are compared but the object roots (.relation if any). Gmsh : produce the source code for Gmsh in -> mesh Gmsh_send : send a line code to the gmsh interpreter in -> line_code (string) Intermediate_meshing : produce the source code for the intermediate u7.03.04 Macro-command CREA_LIB_MFRONT u7.03.04 Macro-command CREA_LIB_MFRONT 1 Purpose Build a constitutive-law library from a .mfront file. The object produced is then used under the keyword COMPORTEMENT/COMPOR_MFRONT. One will find more information on the MFront format in the dedicated user's guide. 2 Syntax compor_mgis = CREA_LIB_MFRONT( ◆ NOM_COMPOR = text, ◆ | UNITE_MFRONT = unit, | UNITE_LIBRAIRIE = unit, ◇ DEBUG = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand NOM_COMPOR ◆ NOM_COMPOR = nom, Name of the constitutive behaviour to be used, as defined in the .mfront file (directive @Behaviour ). 3.2 Operand UNITE_MFRONT UNITE_MFRONT = unit_mfront, Logical unit number of the .mfront file containing the constitutive law in MFront format. The file supplied will be compiled using the mfront executable. If UNITE_MFRONT is not filled in, one must indicate UNITE_LIBRAIRIE in order to specify which library to use. If both keywords are filled in, the library built will be copied onto the file corresponding to UNITE_LIBRAIRIE. The version of code_aster used (since 16.3.13) must be compiled with support for MGIS and for MFront in order for the compilation to work. 3.3 Operand UNITE_LIBRAIRIE UNITE_LIBRAIRIE = unit_lib, If both keywords UNITE_MFRONT and UNITE_LIBRAIRIE are filled in, UNITE_LIBRAIRIE indicates the logical unit on which the compiled library will be written (it is a result). If only UNITE_LIBRAIRIE is filled in, it indicates the library to be used (it is an input). 3.4 Operand DEBUG ◊ DEBUG = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut) By using DEBUG="OUI", one activates the --debug option of MFront, which displays the input and output data.

u7.03.12 Operator CALC_MISS u7.03.12 Operator CALC_MISS 1 Purpose The purpose of this command is to prepare the data, to run the Miss3D software, then to post-process its results in order to produce concepts that can be used in code_aster. Depending on the input arguments of the command, one obtains the harmonic or transient response of the structure, or evolutions of the displacements, velocities and accelerations at certain locations, or else concepts of transient nodal seismic-force load. This operator can also be used together with DYNA_NON_LINE for non-linear transient analyses, by the Laplace-time method (test case miss03 and its associated documentation v1.10.122). Advice on the implementation of soil-structure interaction analyses is given in u2.06.07 and u2.06.05. 2 Syntax / tran_gene / harm_gene / table / char_meca = CALC_MISS( ◆ TYPE_RESU = / "HARM_GENE", / "TRAN_GENE", / "TABLE", / "TABLE_CONTROL", / "FICHIER", / "FICHIER_TEMPS", / "CHARGE", ◇ PROJET = text (défaut: "MODELE"), ◇ REPERTOIRE = text, ◇ VERSION = / "V6.7" (par défaut), / "V6.6", / "V6.5", / TABLE_SOL = table, ◇ / MATER_SOL = _F( ◆ E = float, ◆ NU = float, ◆ RHO = float, ◇ AMOR_HYST = float, ), ◇ MATER_FLUIDE = _F( ◆ RHO = float, ◆ CELE = float, ◇ AMOR_BETA = float, ◇ DEMI_ESPACE = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ), ◇ ISSF = / "OUI", / "NON" (par défaut), #
