Si: equal_to("TYPE", "MITA_LUCO") ◇ VITE_ONDE = float (défaut: 600.0), ◇ PARA_ALPHA = float (défaut: 0.5), ), ◇ UNITE_RESU_IMPE = unit, ◇ TYPE = / "BINAIRE", / "ASCII" (par défaut), ◇ INFO = / 1 (par défaut), / 2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operating principle Depending on its input arguments, CALC_MISS produces a concept whose type varies, or else does not produce a concept: - If TYPE_RESU is equal to 'FICHIER' or 'FICHIER_TEMPS', no concept is produced. Only the execution of Miss3D is launched. The results (dynamic soil stiffness and seismic forces) are then written in the files identified by the logical units such as UNITE_RESU_IMPE, UNITE_RESU_FORC, UNITE_RESU_MASS, UNITE_RESU_RIGI or UNITE_RESU_AMOR. There is no post-processing of the results coming from Miss3D - If TYPE_RESU is equal to 'CHARGE', a mechanical load is produced in the form of a nodal force - If TYPE_RESU is equal to 'TABLE_CONTROL', the Miss3D analysis is the same as for FICHIER. A table is produced containing a point-wise post-processing of the Miss3D results - Otherwise (TYPE_RESU is equal to 'HARM_GENE', 'TRAN_GENE' or 'TABLE'), one runs Miss3D only if the logical units UNITE_RESU_IMPE and UNITE_RESU_FORC are not supplied. Otherwise, one uses the files supplied as input. Post-processing is then carried out and the requested concept is returned to the user. Les calculs MISS3D sur de gros modèles (ou avec beaucoup de fréquences) peuvent être longs et coûteux en mémoire. Heureusement ceux-ci peuvent être accélérés en activant un ou deux niveaux de parallélisme. La valeur TYPE_RESU = ’FICHIER_TEMPS’ permet d’en activer deux, les autres valeurs, un seul. Pour plus d’informations on pourra consulter les documentations :ref: u2.06.07 et :ref: u2.08.06 CALC_MISS produit un concept tran_gene ou harm_gene, incluant les champs d'accélération et de déplacements absolus (exception faite pour le cas de chargement EXCIT_MONO). Dans ce cas, les accélérations sont directement employées pour le calcul du spectre de plancher ; inversement, la déduction des déplacements de sol est obligatoire (à lire avec la commande LIRE_FONCTION (:ref: u4.32.02 ) depuis un fichier spécifique donné par son unité logique) pour obtenir les déplacements relatifs Dans le cadre d'un calcul avec l'option EXCIT_MONO, un chargement mono-appui est appliqué au calcul harmonique. Les résultats sont donc fournis en repère relatif Lors de l'exécution de Miss3D, si le mot-clé MACR_ELEM_DYNA est renseigné, on l'utilise. Sinon, il est créé par CALC_MISS à partir des opérandes BASE_MODALE, MATR_RIGI et MATR_MASS Dans le cas où TYPE_RESU vaut FICHIER_TEMPS, on fait un appel à Miss3D pour chaque fréquence de calcul. Ces appels peuvent être faits en parallèle. Pour cela, il suffit d'exécuter la version parallèle MPI de Code_Aster et demander plusieurs processeurs (pas de mot-clé supplémentaire nécessaire) In the figure Schema-Miss, one shows a schematic flow chart of the operation of the macro-command CALC_MISS. Flow chart of the operation of CALC_MISS 4 Definition of the model 4.1 Keyword TYPE_RESU Defines the type of analysis to be performed. Five values are allowed: - FICHIER: only the execution of Miss3D is carried out. One recovers directly the files produced by Miss3D in the files identified by the logical units UNITE_RESU_IMPE and UNITE_RESU_FORC. CALC_MISS does not return a concept (nothing to the left of the «=» sign) - FICHIER_TEMPS: only the execution of Miss3D is carried out. One recovers directly the files produced by Miss3D in the files identified by the logical units UNITE_RESU_RIGI, UNITE_RESU_MASS, UNITE_RESU_AMOR and UNITE_RESU_FORC. CALC_MISS does not return a concept (nothing to the left of the «=» sign). This option is specific to the Laplace-time method (r4.05.07) - CHARGE: one computes a mechanical load from the seismic-force file - HARM_GENE: one computes the harmonic response of the structure (of type harm_gene) after having run Miss3D or from the files coming from a previous solution (TYPE_RESU='FICHIER') - TRAN_GENE: one computes the harmonic response of the structure and then one returns to the time domain via the inverse Fourier transform (one obtains a concept of type tran_gene) after having run Miss3D or from the files coming from a previous solution (TYPE_RESU='FICHIER') - TABLE: one computes the harmonic response of the structure to a unit excitation at certain points, and one returns a concept of type table which contains the response functions in displacement, velocity, acceleration and oscillator spectrum recombined over the loading cases - TABLE_CONTROL: one recovers from the Miss3D analysis the transfer functions at certain control points and the harmonic and transient responses to a supplied acceleration. One produces a concept of type table 4.2 Operands PROJET/REPERTOIRE The keyword REPERTOIRE makes it possible to define a directory (entered by its full path on the execution machine) in which the Miss3D analysis will be run. One will be able to find there all the Miss3D data and result files (for debugging, for example). These files will begin with a root name given by the operand PROJET (which is equal to MODELE by default). Si REPERTOIRE n'est pas défini, l'exécution aura lieu dans un répertoire temporaire qui sera détruit en fin de calcul. 4.3 Operand MACR_ELEM_DYNA This is the dynamic macro-element of the structure (type macr_elem_dyna) produced by the command of the same name (u4.65.01). 4.4 Operand BASE_MODALE Basis of the modes of the structure. If MACR_ELEM_DYNA is not supplied, this modal basis is used to determine it. Quand on n'effectue que le calcul Miss3D (TYPE_RESU='FICHIER'), on fournit soit MACR_ELEM_DYNA, soit BASE_MODALE Quand on demande le post-traitement, il est nécessaire de renseigner le mot-clé BASE_MODALE (utilisé pour le calcul harmonique). On peut malgré tout fournir un macro-élément spécifique en cas de besoin 4.5 Operands MATR_RIGI and MATR_MASS These keywords make it possible to supply the stiffness and mass matrices of the structure. They will be used during the harmonic analysis and, where applicable, to create the dynamic macro-element. 4.6 Operand MATR_AMOR This keyword makes it possible to supply a damping matrix of the structure used during the harmonic analysis, alternating with the use of modal damping with the keyword AMOR_REDUIT. 4.7 Operand UNITE_IMPR_ASTER Logical unit number on which one can recover the file produced by the operator IMPR_MACR_ELEM, format 'MISS_3D', called internally by CALC_MISS. The default value is 25. 4.8 Operands UNITE_RESU_IMPE, UNITE_RESU_RIGI, UNITE_RESU_MASS, UNITE_RESU_AMOR, UNITE_RESU_FORC Logical unit numbers of the files containing the dynamic soil stiffness (or its decomposition into stiffness, mass and damping) and the seismic forces by frequency. Si on ne demande que le calcul Miss3D, UNITE_RESU_IMPE, UNITE_RESU_RIGI, UNITE_RESU_MASS, UNITE_RESU_AMOR et UNITE_RESU_FORC sont utilisés suivant les cas pour stocker les fichiers résultats Si on demande un post-traitement, il ne faut utiliser ces arguments que si le calcul Miss3D a été exécuté auparavant (les fichiers sont alors des données pour CALC_MISS) Les opérandes UNITE_RESU_RIGI, UNITE_RESU_MASS, UNITE_RESU_AMOR sont d'un usage spécifique à la méthode Laplace-temps (cas TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS') et la présence de UNITE_RESU_AMOR ou de UNITE_RESU_MASS rend obligatoire le mot-clé facteur MATR_GENE Dans l'exécution de Miss3D, le post-traitement de la rigidité dynamique (respectivement des forces sismiques) n'est effectué que si le mot-clé UNITE_RESU_IMPE (respectivement UNITE_RESU_FORC) est renseigné. Ceci permet de réduire un petit peu le temps de calcul 4.9 Operand GROUP_MA_INTERF This keyword makes it possible to define the list of surface mesh-cell groups constituting the soil-structure interface, passed internally to the operator IMPR_MACR_ELEM (u7.04.33). 4.10 Operands GROUP_MA_FLU_STR/GROUP_MA_FLU_SOL/GROUP_MA_SOL_SOL In the case of a soil-fluid-structure interaction, these keywords make it possible to complete the list of surface mesh-cell groups made up respectively of the fluid-structure, fluid-soil and free-soil interfaces (passed internally to the operator IMPR_MACR_ELEM (u7.04.33). Le mot-clé GROUP_MA_SOL_SOL pour l'interface sol libre peut être aussi présent optionnellement en interaction sol-structure, afin de modéliser les liaisons imparfaites entre le sol et la structure le long de l'enfoncement de la fondation. 4.11 Operand TABLE_SOL The data describing the soil stratifications are supplied in the form of a table produced by the command DEFI_SOL_MISS (u7.02.34). Cette donnée est à fournir exclusivement dans le cas ou la macro-commande CALC_MISS fait appel à Miss3D. 4.12 Operand MATER_SOL For a homogeneous soil, one supplies the soil properties: - E is Young's modulus - NU Poisson's ratio - RHO the density Cette donnée est à fournir exclusivement dans le cas ou la macro-commande CALC_MISS fait appel à Miss3D. 4.13 Operand MATER_FLUIDE In the case of a soil-fluid-structure interaction analysis (ISSF='OUI'), one supplies the fluid properties: - RHO is the density - CELE the wave celerity - AMOR_BETA the damping. One also indicates whether or not the domain represents a fluid half-space, according to the definition of Miss3D. Cette donnée est à fournir exclusivement dans le cas ou la macro-commande CALC_MISS fait appel à Miss3D. 4.14 Operand SOURCE_SOL Factor keyword defining the loads arising from point sources in the soil domain, given by their direction and the coordinates of the source. Cette donnée est à fournir exclusivement dans le cas TYPE_RESU='FICHIER' Le vecteur DIRECTION est automatiquement normé à 1 par Miss3D 4.15 Operand SOURCE_FLUIDE Factor keyword defining the loads arising from point pressure sources in the fluid domain, given by the coordinates of the source. Cette donnée est à fournir exclusivement dans le cas TYPE_RESU='FICHIER' 4.16 Operand AMOR_REDUIT List of the reduced dampings passed internally to DYNA_VIBRA (u4.53.03). Let nb_{mode} be the number of dynamic modes defined in the modal basis and nb_{amor} the number of reduced dampings supplied: - If nb_{amor}<nb_{mode} , then one completes the list of dampings up to nb_{mode} with the last damping in the list - One then adds a zero damping, which will be applied to the static modes present 4.17 Operand SURF This operand indicates whether or not one has a shallow foundation. 4.17.1 Operand ISSF This operand indicates whether or not one has a fluid domain and therefore also fluid-structure, soil-fluid and free-soil interfaces supplied by the operands GROUP_MA_FLU_STR, GROUP_MA_FLU_SOL and GROUP_MA_SOL_SOL in the operand PARAMETRE. 5 Miss3D analysis – factor keyword PARAMETRE This factor keyword makes it possible to enter the parameters of the Miss3D analysis: interface type, foundation type, analysis frequencies, spectral and spatial discretisation, which complete the soil description data. These data are necessary as soon as Miss3D must be run . The mode AUTO='OUI' makes it possible to define automatically the value of certain parameters, in accordance with the advice in the documents u2.06.07 and u2.06.05. This concerns the parameters OFFSET_MAX, OFFSET_NB, DREF, RFIC and SPEC_MAX. 5.1 Operands FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX, FREQ_PAS These operands supply the bounds and the frequency step of the Miss3D analysis in the frequency-domain solution (thus one excludes TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS'). 5.2 Operand LIST_FREQ, FREQ These operands supply the list of real frequencies of the Miss3D analysis. This datum is mutually exclusive with the keywords FREQ_xxx. On utilise FREQ dans le cas où on crée la liste de fréquences à la main et LIST_FREQ dans le cas où on utilise une liste de réels produite par code_aster via DEFI_LIST_REEL. L'utilisation de LIST_FREQ (ou FREQ) n'est possible que si on fait le calcul Miss3D seul ou bien si on cherche la réponse à une excitation harmonique (Présence d'EXCIT_GENE). Dans les autres cas, il est nécessaire de fournir une liste de fréquences à pas constant en utilisant les mots-clés FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX, FREQ_PAS. 5.3 Operand FREQ_IMAG This operand is to be used only in the mode TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS' (which corresponds to the Laplace-time method). Indeed, this keyword serves to define the imaginary part of the complex frequency when one places oneself in the Laplace domain. In all the other types of analysis, one is in the frequency domain and the frequency is then always purely real. On ne peut utiliser qu'un seul mot-clé à la fois parmi FREQ_IMAG, FREQ_MIN, LIST_FREQ et FREQ. 5.4 Operand Z0 This operand gives the elevation of the free surface of the soil. 5.5 Operand RFIC This operand indicates the value of the parameter, homogeneous to a characteristic distance, necessary in order to eliminate the fictitious resonances. Il s'agit d'une option disponible exclusivement dans le cadre d'une fondation enfoncée. 5.6 Operand DREF This operand indicates the value of the parameter, homogeneous to a characteristic distance, which makes it possible to eliminate the vertical slope of the impedance for a zero frequency. 5.7 Operand ALLU This operand indicates the value of the absorption coefficient, between 0 and 1, at the soil-fluid interface. Valid if ISSF='OUI'. 5.8 Operands OFFSET_MAX, OFFSET_NB These operands supply the maximum bound and the subdivision of the spatial discretisation for the computation of the dynamic stiffness by Miss3D from the soil data. 5.9 Operands SPEC_MAX, SPEC_NB These operands supply the maximum bound and the subdivision of the spectral discretisation for the computation of the dynamic stiffness by Miss3D from the soil data. 5.10 Operand TYPE This operand makes it possible to store the frequency-dependent dynamic stiffness matrix in a file of binary or ascii format. If one wants to exploit them with the command LIRE_IMPE_MISS (U7.02.32), one must then take care to use the same type of file. 5.11 Operand AUTO This operand makes it possible to trigger the automatic mode for defining the value of certain Miss3D parameters, in accordance with the advice in the documents u2.06.07 and u2.06.05. This concerns the parameters OFFSET_MAX, OFFSET_NB, DREF, RFIC and SPEC_MAX. These automatic values are displayed in the message file. A noter que si avec ce mode automatique, l'utilisateur donne quand même la valeur de tout ou partie de ces paramètres, ces valeurs viennent surcharger les valeurs calculées automatiquement. 5.12 Operand OPTION_DREF This operand makes it possible to specify, with the mode AUTO='OUI', whether one must use the DREF option. If so, then the code automatically computes the value to give it. 5.13 Operand OPTION_RFIC This operand makes it possible to specify, with the mode AUTO='OUI', whether one must use the RFIC option. If so, then the code automatically computes the value to give it. 5.14 Operand COEF_OFFSET This operand makes it possible to define the oversampling coefficient for the automatic computation of the parameter OFFSET_NB (documents u2.06.05 and u2.06.07). By default it is equal to the recommended value of 12 (12 points per element). 6 Post-processing In the case where TYPE_RESU is different from 'FICHIER', 'FICHIER_TEMPS' and 'TABLE_CONTROL', the Miss3D result files are post-processed by CALC_MISS in order to supply the harmonic or transient response of the structure, or evolutions of the characteristic quantities (displacement, velocity, acceleration, oscillator spectrum) at certain post-processing points. 6.1 Definition of the loading There are three different ways of imposing the loading by means of CALC_MISS: - One can apply the equivalent seismic force evaluated beforehand with Miss3D by multiplying this force by a multiplier function. This is the option EXCIT_FORC - One can apply a generic loading on the model which was produced beforehand with AFFE_CHAR_MECA by means of the option EXCIT_GENE - Finally, one can impose a single-support loading at the base of the model via the option EXCIT_MONO Compte-tenu de la différente nature des chargements, on ne peut imposer qu'un seul type pour calcul: En effet, l'option EXCIT_FORC produit un résultat en repère absolu, tandis que EXCIT_MONO produit un résultat en repère relatif. Le mélange de chargement n'est donc pas raisonnable De l'autre coté, l'option EXCIT_GENE permet de produit un chargement générique (que ça soit un déplacement imposé dans le repère absolu ou un chargement type mono-appui) 6.1.1 Operand TYPE_EXCIT If a loading EXCIT_MONO or EXCIT_FORC is present, one must declare the nature of the loading supplied by the user. Two choices are possible: - 'INST' for a time-domain loading - 'FREQ' for a frequency-domain loading 6.1.2 Operands INTERPOL, PAS_INST, INST_FIN In the case where the user supplies a time-domain loading (TYPE_EXCIT='INST'), one has the possibility of re-interpolating this loading (INTERPOL = 'OUI', by default 'NON'). One must then supply two additional parameters: - PAS_INST, that is the interpolation time step - INST_FIN, that is the final time instant of the loading Dans tous les cas, INST_FIN ne peut pas être plus grand que l'instant final de la fonction initiale. En ne connaissant pas la nature du chargement, on ne choisit pas la nature d'un éventuel prolongement. INST_FIN a donc plutôt un fonction de coupure du signal d'entrée . Operand MODELEe This is the model of the structure (passed to DYNA_VIBRA). 6.2 Analysis of the harmonic or transient response of the structure One is in the case TYPE_RESU='HARM_GENE' (harmonic response) or 'TRAN_GENE' (transient response). One then computes the harmonic response of the structure to the loading supplied (EXCIT_GENE, EXCIT_MONO or EXCIT_FORC). Dans le cas 'TRAN_GENE', on effectue la restitution temporelle en utilisant l'opérateur REST_SPEC_TEMP (option PROL_ZERO). 6.2.1 Operands EXCIT_FORC, ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z, DEPL_X, DEPL_Y, DEPL_Z The option EXCIT_FORC is used to impose the loading via the equivalent seismic forces computed beforehand with Miss3D. In this case one will supply: - Either an accelerogram in one or more directions (ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z) - Or imposed displacements in one or more directions (DEPL_X, DEPL_Y, DEPL_Z) En fonction de la nature du chargement il faut fournir soit des fonctions réelles (TYPE_EXCIT='INST') soit des fonctions complexes (TYPE_EXCIT='FREQ'). 6.2.2 Operands EXCIT_HARMO, VECT_ASSE, FONC_MULT, COEF_MULT, FONC_MULT_C, COEF_MULT_C, PHAS_DEG=SIMP, PUIS_PULS EXCIT_HARMO makes it possible to define a generic load in CALC_MISS, a load which will be supplied as input to DYNA_VIBRA. For more details on the definition of a generic load in DYNA_VIBRA one may refer to the option EXCIT in the documentation u4.53.03. 6.2.3 Operands EXCIT_MONO, DIRECTION, ACCE EXCIT_MONO makes it possible to define a single-support loading at the base of the model. For this, one must specify: - The direction (keyword DIRECTION) of the entrainment motion ('X', 'Y' or 'Z') - The multiplier function (keyword ACCE). This multiplier function may be real (TYPE_EXCIT='INST') or complex (TYPE_EXCIT='FREQ') 6.3 Analysis of the evolutions at certain points One is thus in the case TYPE_RESU='TABLE'. In this case, one computes the harmonic response of the structure to a unit acceleration (in the direction or directions requested). Then, for each loading, one recombines at each post-processing location M the unit frequency contributions (equation :eq: eq-recombinaison ): {u}_{M}(f)={u}_{x}\times FFT(a_x)+{u}_{y}\times FFT(a_y)+{u}_{z}\times FFT(a_z) One also computes the FFT of this response and the oscillator spectrum supplied by CALC_FONCTION/SPEC_OSCI. One does the same for {\dot{u}}_{M} and {\ddot{u}}_{M} . All these functions are stored in a table. One thus finds, for each loading case (for the first NUME_CAS = 0): - On the first line, the «loading functions», that is the accelerograms of the excitation (time-domain, NOM_PARA='INST') in the 3 directions: FONC_X, FONC_Y, FONC_Z - On the second line, the FFT of these signals (NOM_PARA='FREQ') - Then for each point, the evolution of the displacement, velocity and acceleration. With, for each, the signal, its FFT and the oscillator spectrum 6.3.1 Operands EXCIT_FORC, ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z The option EXCIT_FORC is used to impose the loading via the equivalent seismic forces computed beforehand with Miss3D. In this case one will supply an accelerogram in one or more directions (ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z). 6.3.2 Operand NORME, AMOR_SPEC_OSCI, LIST_FREQ_SPEC_OSCI These parameters are passed to CALC_FONCTION for the option SPEC_OSCI (u4.32.04), where AMOR_REDUIT has been renamed AMOR_SPEC_OSCI so as not to confuse it with the list of dampings used for the harmonic analysis. Likewise, LIST_FREQ has also been renamed here LIST_FREQ_SPEC_OSCI in order to avoid confusion with the keyword LIST_FREQ. 6.4 Post-processing of the results at the control points One is thus in the case TYPE_RESU='TABLE_CONTROL'. 6.4.1 Operand GROUP_MA_CONTROL This is the group of point mesh cells locating the control points (passed to IMPR_MACR_ELEM). During post-processing, response functions are created for each of the points, which are taken in the order of definition of this mesh-cell group. Thus, in the table, the point designated PC1 does not in general correspond to a node or node group named PC1. It is the first point mesh cell of GROUP_MA_CONTROL. 6.4.2 Operand TOUT_CHAM If this operand is absent, one post-processes in time only the accelerations at the control points. If it is present with the value TOUT_CHAM='OUI', one will also post-process in time the velocity and displacement fields. 6.4.3 Operands ACCE_X, ACCE_Y, ACCE_Z, NORME, AMOR_SPEC_OSCI, LIST_FREQ_SPEC_OSCI Identical to the paragraphs of the option TYPE_RESU='TABLE'. 6.4.4 Table produced The loading applied in the Miss3D analysis is a unit harmonic acceleration. The first two lines correspond to the accelerations ACCE_X/Y/Z supplied by the user, interpolated with the time step supplied, and its FFT : - At each control point, one recovers the transfer function in the three directions for this excitation. These are the lines with TRANSFERT/FREQ - Then, one has the combination {a}_{Mx}(f)={ft}_{x}(f)\times FFT({a}_{x}) and the same thing in y and z depending on the loading applied - One also computes the FFT of this response and the oscillator spectrum supplied by CALC_FONCTION/SPEC_OSCI - All these functions are stored in the table produced Le paramètre de la table désignant le point de contrôle est nommé GROUP_NO pour être homogène au cas TABLE. Comme on l'a vu plus haut, il s'agit simplement d'un numéro de point dans le groupe de mailles des points de contrôle. 6.5 Definition of the list of analysis frequencies - the operand LIST_FREQ_CALC The definition of the list of frequencies for the frequency-domain analysis is handled automatically in the case where TYPE_RESU is equal to 'TRAN_GENE'. In the case where the load is supplied in the time domain (TYPE_EXCIT='INST') one would have: - A frequency step \Delta f=\frac{1}{n_{pas}\cdot\Delta t} - A maximum analysis frequency f_{max}=\frac{1}{2\Delta t} where: - n_{pas} is the number of time steps of the list of time instants - \Delta t is the time step In the case where the load is supplied in the frequency domain (TYPE_EXCIT='FREQ'), the frequency range used is that of the harmonic signal. In the case where TYPE_RESU is equal to 'HARM_GENE','TABLE' or 'TABLE_CONTROL' one can define the list of frequencies via the keyword LIST_FREQ_CALC. Le mot-clé LIST_FREQ_CALC n'est pas à renseigner si TYPE_RESU vaut 'TRAN_GENE'. 6.5.1 The parameters AUTO, FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX, FREQ_PAS, FREQ and LIST_FREQ If AUTO is equal to 'OUI', the frequency list is handled automatically as in the case where TYPE_RESU is equal to 'TRAAN_GENE'. If AUTO is equal to 'NON', the user can define the frequency list: - Either one uses FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX and FREQ_PAS to supply respectively the minimum frequency, the maximum frequency and the frequency step - Or one uses FREQ to supply a list of frequencies by hand - Or one uses LIST_FREQ to supply a frequency list built with DEFI_LIST_REEL 7 Analysis of a seismic-force load In the case where TYPE_RESU is equal to 'CHARGE', the result file of the frequency-domain seismic forces of MISS3D is post-processed by CALC_MISS in order to supply the transient excitation of seismic forces in one direction of space applied on the soil-(fluid-)structure interface. 7.1 Operand MODELE This is the model of the structure to which one adds a super-element comprising a macro-element obtained from the transient or frequency-domain evolution of the impedance of the soil domain (and possibly of the fluid domain) obtained by means of the code_aster-MISS3D chain through the option TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS' or TYPE_RESU='FICHIER' of CALC_MISS. 7.2 Operand FONC_SIGNAL Time-domain imposed-displacement signal, generally obtained by double time integration of an accelerogram. The latter generally corresponds, in the data of the code_aster-MISS3D chain, to an acceleration imposed at the surface of the soil in the far field. The integrations can be obtained directly in the transient domain or in the frequency domain by means of the operator CALC_FONCTION (u4.32.04). 7.3 Operand UNITE_RESU_FORC Makes it possible to define the logical unit of the generated file which will contain the frequency-domain seismic forces computed with the option TYPE_RESU='FICHIER' of CALC_MISS. 7.4 Operand FREQ_MAX This operand supplies the value of the cut-off frequency for the computation of the transient seismic force obtained by the combination of the frequency-domain seismic forces (supplied by UNITE_RESU_FORC) and of the imposed-displacement signal supplied by FONC_SIGNAL. 7.5 Operand NOM_CMP This operand supplies the component (to be chosen among 'DX', 'DY' and 'DZ') giving the direction of the seismic excitation. On calcule une charge pour une seule direction à la fois Dans le cas de sollicitations simultanées dans plusieurs directions, il faut alors créer autant de charges différentes avec l'option TYPE_RESU='CHARGE' de CALC_MISS 7.6 Operand GROUP_NO_AFFE This operand supplies the list of node groups on which the seismic load is imposed. These nodes may be real, for example the central node of a foundation made rigid by a LIAISON_SOLIDE relation, or else fictitious, corresponding to modal coordinates linked to the physical coordinates of the dynamic interface of the soil macro-element by a LIAISON_INTERF relation. 7.7 Operand ISSF This operand indicates whether or not one has a fluid domain. 7.8 Operand VARI This operand makes it possible to activate or not the spatial-variability functionalities, as in the operator DYNA_ISS_VARI (u4.53.31). 7.9 Operand UNITE_RESU_IMPE Makes it possible to define the logical unit of the generated file which will contain the frequency-domain impedances computed with the option TYPE_RESU='FICHIER' of CALC_MISS. 7.10 Keyword INTERF 7.10.1 Operand MODE_INTERF ♦ MODE_INTERF = / 'TOUT', / 'CORP_RIGI' / 'QUELCONQUE' This operand makes it possible to characterise the type of interface modes of the model. Three types of interface modes are possible: if one chooses a modelling based on the six rigid-body modes, one must supply 'CORP_RIGI'; if one works with all the interface modes (finite-element unit modes), one supplies 'TOUT'. For all the other foundation cases (embedded geometry, arbitrary representation modes for a flexible foundation, case ISSF='OUI'), one supplies 'QUELCONQUE'. 7.10.2 Operand GROUP_NO_INTERF With this keyword, one defines the node group based on the surface mesh cells constituting the soil-structure interface. 7.11 Keyword MATR_COHE 7.11.1 Operands TYPE, VITE_ONDE and PARA_ALPHA These are the same parameters used in the operator DYNA_ISS_VARI (u4.53.31). 7.12 Keyword MATR_GENE 7.12.1 Operand BASE Name of the concept of the basis of the interface modes. 7.12.2 Operand NUME_DDL_GENE Name of the generalised numbering concept based on the previous modal basis. In general with full storage 7.13 Operand PRECISION This is the same parameter used in the operator DYNA_ISS_VARI (u4.53.31). 8 Analysis of the dynamic stiffness in the time domain In this paragraph one will detail the options specific to the Laplace-Time method (r4.05.07), that is in the case TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS' 8.1 Operand PRECISION Precision parameter of the Laplace-time computation method (TYPE_RESU='FICHIER_TEMPS'). On conseille fortement de laisser la valeur par défaut. 8.2 Operand COEF_SURECH Parameter for imposing the oversampling coefficient for the Laplace-time method. On recommande de garder la valeur par défaut afin de garantir un bon résultat sur toute la fenêtre de calcul: En effet, lorsque cet opérande vaut 1.0 (pas de suréchantillonnage), l'impédance transitoire est valide uniquement sur 70% environ de la fenêtre de calcul. Ainsi, si l'utilisateur augmente ce coefficient, la précision de calcul sera améliorée, mais avec un surcoût de calcul proportionnel à cette valeur 8.3 Operand FACTEUR_INTERPOL It gives the value of the interpolation step and therefore of the factor of reduction of the run time. 8.4 Operand PCENT_FREQ_CALCUL It gives, as a percentage, the ratio between the number of samples without interpolating and the total number of samples. 8.5 Operand COEF_MULT It makes it possible to assign a multiplicative factor to the transient impedances. Useful, for example, for conversions to 2D models by dividing the 3D impedance results by a domain thickness. 8.6 Operand TYPE_FICHIER_TEMPS Parameter which makes it possible to specify the format of the output time-domain file, between 'ASCII' (default) and 'BINAIRE'. The binary format makes it possible to save space and a little time but is not readable by the user. The format thus defined must be consistent with the format specified with the keyword TYPE under the option FORCE_SOL of AFFE_CHAR_MECA. 8.7 Operands INST_FIN, PAS_INST and INST_ECRI_FIN - The keywords PAS_INST and INST_FIN are mandatory with the Laplace-time analysis method in order to give the time step and the final time instant of the integration analysis of the method. - The keyword INST_ECRI_FIN (optional) makes it possible to limit the storage size of the transient impedances sufficient for the analysis of the seismic forces. Otherwise, this size is determined from INST_FIN. 8.8 Operand MATR_GENE This parameter makes it possible to specify all the options relating to the dynamic-stiffness analyses (test case miss03 and its associated documentation v1.10.122). If this optional factor keyword is used, then one must also define the values of the operands UNITE_RESU_AMOR and UNITE_RESU_MASS. 8.8.1 Operand DECOMP_IMPE This keyword makes it possible to specify the method of decomposition of the impedance. On recommande de laisser la valeur par défaut ('PRODUIT'). 8.8.2 Operand AMOR_HYST This keyword makes it possible to specify the way in which the hysteretic damping in the soil will be taken into account. There are two possible choices: - 'DANS_MATR_AMOR': The damping matrix given by the user (via MATR_AMOR under MATR_GENE) takes the hysteretic damping of the soil into account - 'DANS_IMPEDANCE': This is the opposite case of the previous one 8.8.3 Operands MATR_MASS, MATR_RIGI and MATR_AMOR These arguments serve to define the mass, stiffness and damping matrices which can be used by the decomposition of the impedance: - If one has AMOR_HYST='DANS_MATR_AMOR', then one must mandatorily supply, at least, MATR_AMOR - Conversely, AMOR_HYST='DANS_IMPEDANCE', then it is enough, as a minimum, to give one of the three matrices for the decomposition. 8.9 Operand EXCIT_SOL This optional factor keyword serves to characterise the excitation transmitted by the soil: definition of the seismic forces. If one wishes to compute only the dynamic stiffness, this keyword is unnecessary. 8.9.1 Operands NOM_CHAM, CHAM_X, CHAM_Y and CHAM_Z These arguments serve to specify the input signal. Its nature (displacement, velocity or acceleration signal) is indicated by the value of NOM_CHAM (by default one expects an imposed displacement). This signal may have from one to three components, along X , Y and Z and, for each direction, one can give the corresponding function: CHAM_X, CHAM_Y and CHAM_Z. 8.9.2 Operand UNITE_RESU_FORC Makes it possible to define the logical unit of the generated file which will contain the seismic forces, which will be reusable in DYNA_NON_LINE via a loading of type FORCE_SOL in AFFE_CHAR_MECA (test case miss03c and its associated documentation v1.10.122). 9 Miscellaneous Level of detail of the printout of the command. With INFO=2, a great deal of information on the sequence of the analysis steps is displayed.

u7.03.41 Procedure MACR_ECREVISSE u7.03.41 Procedure MACR_ECREVISSE Summary: The purpose of the macro-command MACR_ECREVISSE is to compute the flow rate of fluid (air/steam/liquid) through one (or several) through-crack(s) in a structure modelled in 2 dimensions. To do this, at each time step, it carries out the chaining of two codes: - Code_Aster which makes it possible to know the thermo-mechanical state of the structure - Ecrevisse which carries out the thermo-hydraulic analysis of the flow through the crack. In practice, the macro-command takes care of carrying out successively, for all the time steps: - a linear thermal analysis - a quasi-static mechanical analysis - calling the macro-command CALC_ECREVISSE, which will be in charge of: - recovering the crack profile - calling a third macro-command MACR_ECRE_CALC which will generate the command file and launch Ecrevisse - extracting and copying the results - checking that the imposed criteria are satisfied and, if necessary, subdividing the time step. The main output concept is the result data structure of the mechanical analysis (evol_noli). It is also possible to obtain the result data structure of the thermal analysis, as well as 2 tables, one containing the flow rates at each time instant, the other summarising the data concerning the cracks. By creating an output directory in the study profile, one will be able to recover there all the outputs concerning Ecrevisse. It is possible to perform restarts of the analysis. Note It is necessary to specify the keyword DEBUG=_F(HIST_ETAPE='OUI') in DEBUT or POURSUITE in order to use MACR_ECREVISSE . 1 Purpose This command makes it possible to chain Code_Aster with the ECREVISSE software. The principle is based, for each time step, on a successive call to: - THER_LINEAIRE in order to obtain the thermal state of the structure - STAT_NON_LINE in order to obtain the mechanical state of the structure - the ECREVISSE code in order to know the flow conditions of the fluid. Note It is necessary to specify the keyword DEBUG=_F(HIST_ETAPE='OUI') in DEBUT or POURSUITE in order to use MACR_ECREVISSE . 2 Syntax / evol_noli / evol_ther / table = MACR_ECREVISSE( ◇ reuse = , ◇ défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operands TABLE / TEMPER / DEBIT ◊ TEMPER = CO('temp') ◊ TABLE = CO('table') ◊ DEBIT = CO('debit') These keywords make it possible to give the name of the concepts coming out of the macro-command, namely - TABLE : a table of 7 columns giving for each time step: the coordinate z , the flux, the total pressure ( \mathrm{Pa} ), the temperature of the fluid ( °C ), the convective heat-exchange coefficient ( {\mathit{W.m}}^{-2.}°{C}^{-1} ), the name of the crack. - TEMPER : the result data structure of the thermal analysis - DEBIT : the value of the flow rate ( {\mathit{kg.s}}^{-1} ) at each time step and for each crack Notes: | all the output concepts are optional; it is nevertheless strongly recommended to specify at least TEMPER , otherwise it is impossible to check the temperature fields in the structure and to perform a restart if the concept is re-entrant, the keyword TEMPER must not be specified here but under the keyword ETAT_INIT , operand EVOL_THER . | | --- | 3.2 Keyword ETAT_INIT ◊ ETAT_INIT = _F ( ♦ EVOL_NOLI = evol_noli ♦ EVOL_THER = evol_ther ♦ NUME_ORDRE = nume_ordre Keyword making it possible to define the initial state in the framework of a restart of the macro-command. 3.2.1 Operand EVOL_NOLI Name of the concept of type evol_noli from which the mechanical state will be extracted. 3.2.2 Operand EVOL_THER Name of the concept of type evol_ther from which the thermal state will be extracted. This concept will be enriched in the course of the analysis. 3.2.3 Operand NUME_ORDRE The initial state in order to restart the analysis will be defined from the archiving order number NUME_ORDRE for evol_noli and for evol_ther. 3.3 Operands MODELE_MECA / MODELE_THER ♦ MODELE_MECA = m_meca ♦ MODELE_THER = m_ther These keywords make it possible to specify the name of the model (m_meca) whose elements are the subject of the mechanical analysis and the name of the model (m_ther) whose elements are the subject of the thermal analysis. 3.4 Operand LIST_INST ♦LIST_INST = list_inst List of the time steps which correspond to the imposed analysis time instants. In the event of subdivision, the time instants are inserted into this list. 3.5 Operand CHAM_MATER ♦ CHAM_MATER = chmat Name of the material field assigned to the mesh. Caution, this field must include the data associated with the mechanical constitutive behaviour and with the thermal constitutive behaviour (keyword THER of DEFI_MATERIAU). 3.6 Operand TEMP_INIT ♦ TEMP_INIT = temp_init Value of the initial temperature over the whole domain. 3.7 Operand CARA_ELEM ◊ CARA_ELEM = carac This keyword makes it possible to specify the characteristics of the beam, bar, shell, pipe and discrete elements, when they are present in the model. Caution, this keyword is used only for the mechanical analysis and is not transmitted to the thermal operator (in order to avoid any problem with the bars). 3.8 Keyword EXCIT_MECA ♦ EXCIT_MECA = _F ( ♦ CHARGE = chi ◊ FONC_MULT = fi ◊ TYPE_CHARGE = / "FIXE_CSTE" / "SUIV" / "DIDI" ) The aim here is to specify the boundary conditions of the mechanical problem, as well as any mechanical loadings which apply to the structure. The syntax is identical to that of the keyword EXCIT of STAT_NON_LINE but it is not possible to pilot a loading. See the document U4.51.03. 3.9 Keyword CONTACT ♦ CONTACT = char_contact One specifies here the contact conditions between the lips of the crack, which may close again during the analysis. The purpose of this keyword is to avoid the interpenetration of the lips which may occur under the effect of the flow of the fluid. 3.10 Keyword EXCIT_THER ♦ EXCIT_THER = _F ( ♦ CHARGE = chi ◊ FONC_MULT = fi ) The aim here is to specify the boundary conditions of the thermal problem as well as any thermal loadings. The syntax is identical to that of the keyword EXCIT of THER_LINEAIRE. See the document U4.54.01. 3.11 Keyword COMPORTEMENT The aim here is to specify the constitutive law which will be used to solve the mechanical problem. See the document U4.51.03. 3.12 Keyword NEWTON The aim here is to specify the parameters of the Newton algorithm in order to solve the mechanical problem. This keyword is identical to that of STAT_NON_LINE; one should therefore refer to the document U4.51.03. 3.13 Keyword CONVERGENCE The aim here is to specify the convergence criteria for the mechanical analysis. The syntax corresponds to that of STAT_NON_LINE (see the document U4.51.03). Note: | It may be necessary to use RESI_GLOB_MAXI rather than RESI_GLOB_RELA , when there is no mechanical loading (otherwise, zero force, hence RESI_GLOB_RELA undefined). | | --- | 3.14 Keyword ENERGIE This keyword makes it possible to activate the computation of the energy balance and its display in the course of the mechanical analysis (see the document R4.09.01). This balance is stored in the table named PARA_CALC, from which it can be extracted by means of the command RECU_TABLE U4.71.02. 3.15 Keyword FISSURE ♦ FISSURE This keyword makes it possible to define all the parameters relating to a crack. Several occurrences of this keyword are possible if there are several cracks. 3.15.1 Operand GROUP_MA ♦ GROUP_MA = gma Groups of mesh cells defining the lip or the lips of the crack. One gives the group of the lower lip and of the upper lip. 3.15.2 Operands GROUP_NO_ORIG and GROUP_NO_EXTR ♦ GROUP_NO_ORIG = ogno ♦ GROUP_NO_EXTR = egno Makes it possible to define the two node groups which define the two ends of the crack in order to orient it. 3.15.3 Operand SECTION ♦ SECTION = /"ELLIPSE" /"RECTANGLE" The aim here is to define the flow passage section (plane perpendicular to the modelling plane). This may be elliptical or rectangular. One of the dimensions of this section corresponds to the size of the crack in the modelling plane. This is determined at each time instant by the macro-command. The other dimension corresponds to the size of the crack out of the modelling plane. This is fixed throughout the analysis and must be specified by means of the operands LISTE_COTES_BL and LIST_VAL_BL. 3.15.4 Operand RUGOSITE ♦ RUGOSITE = eps Absolute roughness of the wall (in metres). This value influences the result only if the friction is computed by Ecrevisse (operand FROTTEMENT >0) and if the flow is no longer laminar. For the friction options 21,22,23,24 it is the diameter of the largest aggregate (flow in a crack in concrete). 3.15.5 Operands LISTE_COTES_BL / LISTE_VAL_BL ◊ LISTE_COTES_BL = lcbl ♦ LISTE_VAL_BL = lvbl Figure 3.2.5-1: Representation of the crack In order to characterise the size of the crack in the non-modelled plane, one must supply the value of the «small» axis of the elliptical section or the width of the rectangular section at a minimum of 2 points. LISTE_COTES_BL makes it possible to specify the curvilinear abscissae at which one gives the dimension of the crack and LIST_VAL_BL makes it possible to give the dimension. If LISTE_COTES_BL is not specified, LISTE_VAL_BL must contain the width of the crack at the inlet and at the outlet of the crack. 3.15.6 Operand ZETA ♦ ZETA = zeta Coefficient of singular pressure loss at the inlet (dimensionless). 3.15.7 Operand OUVERT_REMANENTE ♦ OUVERT_REMANENTE = ouv_rem Value of the residual opening (in metres) for the Ecrevisse analysis corresponding to the actual hydraulic opening of the crack when the two lips are in contact. This expresses the fact that, even when the crack is closed, a small quantity of fluid will pass through, in particular because of the roughness. This parameter depends on the material: for example, it is of the order of 10\mu m for concrete. This keyword is therefore taken into account during the hydraulic analysis (Ecrevisse), but not by Code_Aster : it may therefore well happen that the hydraulic analysis is carried out with the residual opening, and that contact is activated in the mechanical analysis. 3.15.8 Operand TORTUOSITE ◊ TORTUOSITE = tort If the crack is tortuous, one may accept that, as seen by the fluid, the length of the crack is greater than the thickness of the wall crossed. This coefficient, which by default is equal to 1, makes it possible to take this phenomenon into account. The length of the crack will therefore be equal to \frac{L}{\mathit{tort}} with \mathit{tort}\le 1 3.15.9 Operand PREFIXE_FICHIER ◊ PREFIXE_FICHIER = prefix Makes it possible to define the name of the Ecrevisse output files in the directory REPE_OUT (curves and text files), and thus to distinguish the files associated with each crack. 3.16 Keyword ECOULEMENT ♦ ECOULEMENT In this keyword one defines the nature of the fluid and its characteristics. 3.16.1 Operands PRES_ENTREE / PRES_ENTREE_FO ♦ / PRES_ENTREE = pe / PRES_ENTREE_FO = fpe This operand makes it possible to give the total pressure ( \mathit{Pa} ) or its evolution in the course of time, upstream of the crack. It must lie between 215.{10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} and {10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} . 3.16.2 Operands PRES_SORTIE / PRES_SORTIE_FO ♦ / PRES_SORTIE = pe / PRES_SORTIE_FO = fpe This operand makes it possible to give the total pressure ( \mathit{Pa} ) or its evolution in the course of time, at the outlet of the crack. It must lie between 215.{10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} and 800\mathit{Pa} and be lower than the inlet pressure (otherwise, there is no flow and the analysis stops). 3.16.3 Operand FLUIDE_ENTREE ♦ FLUIDE_ENTREE = 1,2,3,4,5 ou 6 This operand makes it possible to define the state of the fluid at the inlet of the crack: > 1 : Subcooled or saturated water; > 2 : Two-phase fluid; > 3 : Saturated or superheated steam; > 4 : Air + superheated steam; > 5 : Air + saturated steam; > 6 : Air alone. Depending on the state of the fluid, only some of the following characteristics are to be specified. 3.16.4 Operands TEMP_ENTREE / TEMP_ENTREE_FO ♦ / TEMP_ENTREE = te / TEMP_ENTREE_FO = fte This operand makes it possible to specify the temperature ( °C ) or its evolution in the course of time, upstream of the crack. It must be specified if the fluid at the inlet is «Subcooled or saturated water», «Saturated or superheated steam», «Air + superheated steam» or «Air alone». (operand FLUIDE_ENTREE = 1,3,4,or 6). 3.16.5 Operands TITR_MASS / TITR_MASS_FO ♦ / TITR_MASS = xe / TITR_MASS_FO = fxe This operand makes it possible to specify the vapour mass fraction, or its evolution in the course of time, upstream of the crack. It corresponds to the ratio between the mass of vapour and the mass of liquid water and vapour. It must be specified if the fluid at the inlet is «Two-phase fluid» or «Air + saturated steam» (operand FLUIDE_ENTREE = 2 or 5). 3.16.6 Operands PRES_PART / PRES_PART_FO ♦ / PRES_PART = pae / PRES_PART_FO = fpae This operand makes it possible to specify the partial pressure of air ( \mathit{Pa} ) or its evolution in the course of time, upstream of the crack. It must be specified if the fluid at the inlet is «Air + superheated steam» or «Air + saturated steam» (operand FLUIDE_ENTREE=4 or 5). 3.17 Keyword MODELE_ECRE ♦ MODELE_ECRE This keyword makes it possible to specify the models which will be used by Ecrevisse to compute the flow of the fluid. 3.17.1 Operand IVENAC ◊ IVENAC = 0 ou 1, When this operand is activated (IVENAC=1), the ECREVISSE analysis is carried out taking the vena contracta into account (pressure loss at the inlet). Otherwise (default case), the analysis will be carried out without this modelling option. 3.17.2 Operand ECOULEMENT ♦ ECOULEMENT = / 'SATURATION', / 'GELE' In the absence of air and in the presence of water (operand FLUIDE_ENTREE=1 or 2), this operand makes it possible to choose between the homogeneous equilibrium model and the «GELE» flow model characterised by a non-zero fraction of metastable liquid. 3.17.3 Operand PRESS_EBULLITION Boiling pressure ( \mathit{Pa} ) to be supplied only for the frozen-flow model. 3.17.4 Operand FROTTEMENT The aim here is to define how the friction is computed. The valid values are: -14,-12,-11,-4,-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,11,12,14,21,22,23,24 . The value 0 corresponds to an analysis without friction. For the negative values, the user fixes the value of the friction coefficient for the turbulent flows. For the positive values, the friction in turbulent flow is computed from the roughness coefficient. In particular, the options 21,22,23,24 correspond to the friction relation of Greiner and Ramm [Bib.6] for the flow in a crack in concrete; the roughness is in this case the diameter of the largest aggregate. Moreover, for the values greater than 10 , the law used for laminar flow (friction proportional to the inverse of the Reynolds number) is connected with that in turbulent flow (constant value of the friction coefficient). Otherwise, a discontinuity is present. The second digit (1,2,3,4) of each option (units) determines the option for computing the dynamic viscosity for the two-phase flows, cf. Ecrevisse documentation [Bib.1] [Bib.2] [Bib.3] [Bib.4] [Bib.5] . 3.17.5 Operands REYNOLDS_LIM / FROTTEMENT_LIM Limit Reynolds coefficient and imposed friction coefficient for a Reynolds number greater than the limit Reynolds number. To be supplied only if FROTTEMENT ELLIPSE : List of the values of the points defining the major axis of the section; > RECTANGLE : List of the values of the points defining the length of the section. 7.4.2 Keyword TEMPERATURE 7.4.2.1 Operand GRADIENT Model of the temperature gradient: > Supplied : Supplied temperature distribution; > Imposed : Imposed temperature distribution; > Computed : Computed temperature profile; 7.4.2.2 Operand LISTE_COTES_TEMP List of the coordinates for the temperatures. 7.4.2.3 Operand LISTE_VAL_TEMP List of the temperature values. 7.4.2.4 Operand TEMP1 Temperature gradient of the wall along the flow. 7.4.2.5 Operand TEMP2 Wall temperature at the inlet. 7.4.2.6 Operand EPAISSEUR_PAROI Thickness of the wall. 7.4.2.7 Operand CONVECTION_AMONT Convection coefficient at the surface of the wall on the upstream side. 7.4.2.8 Operand CONVECTION_AVAL Convection coefficient at the surface of the wall on the downstream side. 7.4.2.9 Operand LAMBDA Thermal conduction of the wall. 7.4.2.10 Operand TEMP_FLUIDE_AVAL Temperature of the fluid on the downstream side.

u7.03.51 Macro-command RAFF_XFEM u7.03.51 Macro-command RAFF_XFEM 1 Purpose Perform the computation of the error criterion prior to a mesh refinement for cracks and interfaces modelled by the X-FEM method. The command produces a data structure cham_no. 2 Syntax / carte / cham_no = RAFF_XFEM( ◇ TYPE = / "DISTANCE" (par défaut), / "ZONE", ◆ FISSURE = fiss_xfem, # Si: equal_to("TYPE", 'ZONE') ◆ RAYON = float, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 General operation The operator RAFF_XFEM makes it possible to create a field in anticipation of a mesh refinement in the framework of cracks represented by the X-FEM method. The idea is to characterise the nodes or the mesh cells located in a zone around the crack front (zone of interest). This will make it possible to refine subsequently the mesh cells close to the crack front, for example in order to improve the computation of the energy release rate. The field created by RAFF_XFEM may be qualified as an a priori “error” field (or indicator). The indicator created may be of 2 types (TYPE = 'DISTANCE' or 'ZONE'). 3.1 Distance indicator By choosing this type of indicator, the operator RAFF_XFEM creates an a priori “error” field at the nodes. This error at each node reflects the minimum of the distances to the crack fronts (or to the surface for the interfaces). Thus, the nodes close to the X-FEM crack fronts (or to the X-FEM surfaces for the interfaces) will have a high “error”. Conversely, the further away the node is, the smaller the “error” will be. This criterion is used for the mesh-refinement software used subsequently (see for example sslp317a,b). The nodes closest to the crack fronts will be refined as a priority. More precisely, if one denotes by \mathrm{lsn} the normal level set and by \mathrm{lst} the tangential level set, the nodal field created has the formula: \mathrm{erreur}=-r where r is the distance: - to the crack front for the cracks: r=\sqrt{({\mathrm{lsn}}^{2}+{\mathrm{lst}}^{2})} - to the interface for the interfaces: r=\sqrt{({\mathrm{lsn}}^{2})} The values of the field are therefore all negative. Very distant nodes ( r large) will have negative error values very far from 0 and close nodes ( r small) will have negative error values close to 0. It will suffice to tell Homard (MACR_ADAP_MAIL) to refine the mesh cells where the value is the largest (mathematically speaking). To do this, it will be necessary to specify in MACR_ADAP_MAIL: USAGE_CMP = 'RELATIF' One may either refine a given percentage of the mesh cells closest to the front (CRIT_RAFF_PE), or give a value of the distance (more precisely the opposite of the distance) below which the mesh cells will be refined (CRIT_RAFF_ABS). For further advice, consult the documentation U2.05.02. This distance indicator may pose problems which will not be discussed here. That is why a second, more robust, indicator has been developed. 3.2 Zone indicator (binary indicator) This is the recommended indicator. By choosing this indicator, the operator RAFF_XFEM creates a field by mesh cell (field of type carte) of binary nature. The principle of this indicator is to be equal to 1 in the zone to be refined (zone of interest) and 0 everywhere else. The zone of interest is in 2D a disc around the crack front and in 3D a torus around the crack front, characterised by the datum of a radius {R}_{\mathit{raff}} . For the interfaces, the zone of interest is a band around the interface. More precisely: The field is initialised to 0. The field is set to 1 if the mesh cell contains: - the crack front (for the cracks), - the interface (for the interfaces). In addition, the field is set to 1 if the mesh cell has at least one node located at a distance from the front (or from the interface) less than {R}_{\mathit{raff}} . This distance is determined in the same way as that appearing in the distance indicator (see § 3.1 ). This indicator is easier to handle than the distance indicator. It is used with the default keywords of MACR_ADAP_MAIL, but exclusively with a criterion in absolute value (CRIT_RAFF_ABS). The value of the criterion does not matter (between 0 and 1), but for reasons of readability it is recommended to choose CRIT_RAFF_ABS= 0,5. Examples of use will be found in the tests sslv155[b,c] , sslv110f , sslp317c . For further advice, consult the documentation U2.05.02. 3.3 Note common to the 2 types of indicator It must be noted that the 2 indicators are based on the level sets. At the present time, the level sets are computed over the whole mesh, but one may limit the potential enrichment zone to only part of the mesh (keyword GROUP_MA_ENRI of the command DEFI_FISS_XFEM). In the case where the level sets are liable to define a crack outside the zone delimited by GROUP_MA_ENRI 1 , the indicator computed by RAFF_XFEM, being based on the level sets, does not take the restriction of the crack into account. This means that certain nodes or certain mesh cells (outside GROUP_MA_ENRI) may have high error values without however being close to the crack front. In order to prevent these nodes from causing an unnecessary refinement in this zone, it is also recommended to limit the refinement zone in MACR_ADAP_MAIL, by means of the keyword GROUP_MA (supply the same mesh-cell group as the one given under GROUP_MA_ENRI). See the documentation of DEFI_FISS_XFEM [U4.82.08] for an illustrated example of such a case. 4 Operands 4.1 Operand TYPE ◊ TYPE = / 'DISTANCE', [DEFAUT] / 'ZONE' Permet de choisir le type d'indicateur. Par défaut, c'est indicateur en distance qui est choisi. :ref: 3 Voir la description du fonctionnement des 2 types d'indicateur au §. 4.2 Operand FISSURE FISSURE = (fiss1, fiss2) (fiss1, fiss2): list of the names of the cracks (or interfaces) defined beforehand by the operator DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08. The number of cracks (or interfaces) is not limited. 4.3 Operand RAYON Makes it possible to supply the value of the radius of the zone of interest (see § 3.2 ). This operand is possible only for the zone indicator.

u7.03.71 Macro-command RAFF_GP u7.03.71 Macro-command RAFF_GP 1 Purpose The purpose of this macro-command is to refine a two-dimensional mesh containing a defect represented by a notch; the refinement is carried out in the zone downstream of the notch. This macro-command may in particular be used upstream of the mechanical analysis from which a fracture-mechanics post-processing by CALC_GP will be performed. The macro returns a mesh. 2 Syntax maillage = RAFF_GP( ◆ MAILLAGE_N = maillage, ◆ TRANCHE_2D = _F( ◆ CENTRE = float, ◆ RAYON = float, ◆ ANGLE = float, ◆ TAILLE = float, ◆ NB_ZONE = int, ), ◇ NB_RAFF = int (défaut: 4), ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands RAFF_GP is a macro-command and therefore calls other commands of Code_Aster internally. Most of the keywords are passed as they are to the other commands. It will be indicated below in which command(s) the keywords are used. 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE_N > ♦ MAILLAGE_N = ma_n, [sd_maillage] Denotes the initial mesh on which the refinement will take place. It must contain a notch represented finely enough (at least 5 elements on the contour of the half-notch) and the elements that compose it must not be distorted (refinement reducing the quality of the mesh, it is important that the initial mesh be as clean as possible). Used by MACR_ADAP_MAIL. 3.2 Operand TRANCHE_2D > ♦ TRANCHE_2D =_F( > ♦ TAILLE = {l}_{C} [R] > ♦ CENTRE = centre [R,R,R] > ♦ RAYON = R [R] > ♦ ANGLE = \theta [R] > ♦ NB_ZONE = n [I] > ) Denotes the set of geometric parameters required for the definition of the geometric refinement zone. The syntax is identical to that used by the operator CALC_GP. The Figure presents the parameters defining these zones; it represents a notch of centre {C}_{\mathrm{ent}} , of radius R ; the third zone {C}_{3}(l) of length 3\ast {l}_{C} is hatched. Figure 4.2-a : Definition of the geometric refinement zone. 3.2.1 Keyword TAILLE > ♦ TAILLE = {l}_{C} [R] Increment of the size of the zones. Zone n is therefore of size n {l}_{C} . Used by FORMULE. 3.2.2 Keyword CENTRE > ♦ CENTRE = centre [R,R,R] Denotes the coordinates of the centre of the notch {C}_{\mathrm{ent}} in the global frame. Used by FORMULE. 3.2.3 Keyword RAYON > ♦ RAYON = R [R] Denotes the radius of the notch. Used by FORMULE. 3.2.4 Keyword ANGLE > ♦ ANGLE = \theta [R] Denotes the angle formed between the direction of the notch and the axis \overrightarrow{X} of the global frame. The angle must be given in degrees and measured in the trigonometric sense. Used by FORMULE, 3.2.5 Keyword NB_ZONE > ♦ NB_ZONE = n [I] Denotes the number of zones (chips) considered. 3.3 Operand NB_RAFF ◊ NB_RAFF = nombre [R] Denotes the number of refinements carried out from the initial mesh. By default, this number is 4. Used by MACR_ADAP_MAIL. 4 Example of use Examples will be found in the test cases zzzz356 and ssnp131. Figure 5-a : Initial mesh and mesh after refinement of case zzzz356,

u7.04.33 Procedure IMPR_MACR_ELEM u7.04.33 Procedure IMPR_MACR_ELEM 1 Purpose Print a data structure macr_elem_dyna in the IDEAS and MISS_3D formats. One prints: - the definition of a connection interface between a macro-structure and its external environment, - a modal basis (dynamic modes of the macro-structure and static modes resulting either from unit displacements imposed at the interface, or from unit forces imposed at the interface), - the mass and stiffness matrices of the macro-structure projected onto the preceding modal basis. 2 Syntax IMPR_MACR_ELEM( ◆ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = macr_elem_dyna, ◇ FORMAT = / "MISS_3D", / "IDEAS" (par défaut), # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'IDEAS') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 30), ◇ VERSION = 5, # Si: equal_to("FORMAT", 'MISS_3D') ◇ UNITE = unit (défaut: 26), ◇ SOUS_TITRE = text, ◇ / AMOR_REDUIT = float, / LIST_AMOR = listr8, ◆ GROUP_MA_INTERF = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_FLU_STR = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_FLU_SOL = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_SOL_SOL = grma, ◇ GROUP_MA_CONTROL = grma, ◇ FORMAT_R = / "1PE12.5" (par défaut), / "1PE16.9", ◇ IMPR_MODE_MECA = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ◇ IMPR_MODE_STAT = / "OUI" (par défaut), / "NON", ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand MACR_ELEM_DYNA ♦ MACR_ELEM_DYNA = melem [macr_elem_dyna] Name of the concept of type macr_elem_dyna which one wishes to print in the file. 3.2 FORMAT = 'IDEAS' ◊ FORMAT = / ‘IDEAS’ [DEFAUT] Makes it possible to specify the print format. The format ‘IDEAS’ is taken by default. Currently only the printout is carried out according to the specifications of version 5. Upward compatibility with the versions of IDEAS is therefore ensured. 3.2.1 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = / 30, [DEFAUT] / unit [I] This keyword makes it possible to define the logical unit for printing in the ‘IDEAS’ format (30 by default). 3.2.2 Operand VERSION ◊ VERSION = / 5, [DEFAUT] This keyword makes it possible to define the print version in the ‘IDEAS’ format (5 by default). 3.3 FORMAT = 'MISS_3D' ◊ FORMAT = / 'MISS_3D' The format ‘MISS_3D’ is used by the soil-dynamics code MISS3D to import structural data coming from Code_Aster (content of the dynamic macro-element which corresponds to the terms of the contribution of the structure to the impedance of the global soil-structure interaction problem). One also prints the mesh of the soil-structure interface in its local numbering and, possibly, the dynamic and static modes reduced to this interface. For this format one must supply the operand GROUP_MA_INTERF and five operands are optional: UNITE, SOUS_TITRE, AMOR_REDUIT, IMPR_MODE_STAT and IMPR_MODE_MECA. 3.3.1 Operand UNITE ◊ UNITE = / 26, [DEFAUT] / unit [I] This keyword makes it possible to define the logical unit for printing in the ‘MISS_3D’ format (26 by default). 3.3.2 Operand SOUS_TITRE ◊ SOUS_TITRE = l_st [l_Kn] Allows the user to give a name to the data transferred into the MISS3D code. 3.3.3 Operand AMOR_REDUIT ◊ / AMOR_REDUIT = lam [l_R] / LIST_AMOR = l_amor listr8 These keywords make it possible to enter a list of dampings for the dynamic modes. One can thus complete the terms of the dynamic macro-element. 3.3.4 Operand GROUP_MA_INTERF ♦ GROUP_MA_INTERF = gr_inter [l_group_ma] This keyword makes it possible to define the list of surface mesh-cell groups constituting the soil-structure interface. One prints the coordinates of the “Nb_nœuds” nodes of the set of interfaces, then the “Nb_elem” elements with their connectivities in the local numbering of the set of interfaces (1 to “Nb_nœuds”). 3.3.5 Operand IMPR_MODE_STAT ◊ IMPR_MODE_STAT = / ‘OUI’ [DEFAUT] / ‘NON’ This keyword makes it possible, optionally (if ‘OUI’), to print the static modes reduced to the interface. This proves necessary for the 6 rigid-body modes. In this case, the macro-element is based on a dynamic interface of type CRAIGB reduced to one point with a rigid link of the interface (keyword LIAISON_SOLIDE of AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01). 3.3.6 Operand IMPR_MODE_MECA ◊ IMPR_MODE_MECA = / ‘OUI’ [DEFAUT] / ‘NON’ This keyword makes it possible, optionally (if ‘OUI’), to print the dynamic modes reduced to the interface. 3.3.7 Operand FORMAT_R ◊ FORMAT_R = / ‘1PE12.5’ [DEFAUT] / ‘1PE16.9’ This keyword gives the print format of the real numbers used when printing the structural impedances which one assembles with the soil impedances in MISS3D. 3.3.8 Operands GROUP_MA_FLU_STR/GROUP_MA_FLU_SOL/GROUP_MA_SOL_SOL ◊ GROUP_MA_FLU_STR= gr_flustr [l_group_ma] ◊ GROUP_MA_FLU_SOL= gr_flusol [l_group_ma] ◊ GROUP_MA_SOL_SOL= gr_solsol [l_group_ma] In the case of a soil-fluid-structure interaction, these keywords make it possible to complete the list of surface mesh-cell groups made up respectively of the fluid-structure, fluid-soil and free-soil interfaces. In this case, one completes the printing of their elements with their connectivities in the local numbering of the set of interfaces (1 to "Nb-nœuds") (including the soil-structure interface). 3.3.9 Operand GROUP_MA_CONTROL ◊ GROUP_MA_CONTROL= gr_control [l_group_ma] This keyword makes it possible to introduce groups of point mesh cells POI1 in order to model, with Code_Aster , control points in the part of the soil modelled by MISS3D. This then makes it possible to carry out any post-processing on their nodes with Code_Aster operators after recovery of the evolution computed by CALC_MISS. This therefore requires, for these control points: - to introduce them into the mesh as isolated nodes, - to assign them a DIS_T modelling with AFFE_MODELE, - to impose on them blockings in ‘DX’, ‘DY’, ‘DZ’ with AFFE_CHAR_MECA, > An illustrative example is given in the test case ZZZZ108C. In this case, one completes the printing of these point elements with their connectivity to a single node in the local numbering of the set of interfaces (1 to "Nb-nœuds") (including the nodes of the modelled control points). 4 Example of printing data in the MISS3D format In the example below, the main commands are given which allow the chaining between Code_Aster and the MISS3D code, and which illustrate the use of the command IMPR_MACR_ELEM in this context. # # calcul des modes # mode = CALC_MODES( MATR_RIGI= rigidite, MATR_MASS= masse, CALC_FREQ=_F( NMAX_FREQ= 30 ), ); # # calcul du macro-élément dynamique # interdyn = DEFI_INTERF_DYNA ( NUME_DDL= nume_ddl, INTERFACE= ( NOM = ‘DROITE’, TYPE = ‘CRAIGB’, NOEUD= 'N98' ) ); bamo = DEFI_BASE_MODALE ( CLASSIQUE=_F ( INTERF_DYNA = interdyn, MODE_MECA = mode, NMAX_MODE = 30 ) ); mael = MACR_ELEM_DYNA ( BASE_MODALE= bamo, OPTION= ‘CLASSIQUE’ ); fo1 = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA= ‘FREQ’, VALE= (0., 1., 100., 1. ) ); # # lecture de l’accélérogramme de sol acce # ACCE = DEFI_FONCTION ( NOM_PARA = 'INST', VALE = ( 0.00000E+00, 1.1940E-03, - - - - - - - - - - - )); # # pré-traitement de MISS3D # # (maillage et impédances d’interface) IMPR_MACR_ELEM ( MACR_ELEM_DYNA = mael, FORMAT = ‘MISS_3D’, SOUS_TITRE = ‘CIVAUX RIGIDE’, IMPR_MODE_STAT = ‘OUI’, IMPR_MODE_MECA = ‘NON’, AMOR_REDUIT = ( 0.07 ), GROUP_MA_INTERF = ('SRADIER') );

u7.04.51 Operator IMPR_OAR u7.04.51 Operator IMPR_OAR 1 Purpose Write the result of an ASTER mechanical or thermomechanical analysis in the OAR format. The OAR (Rapid Analysis Tool) makes it possible to carry out brittle-fracture analyses according to the codified methods of the RSE-M. The stress field along the ligament in line with the defect enters into the input data necessary for the application of these methods. This field may be computed by an ASTER mechanical or thermomechanical analysis. In this case, the operator IMPR_OAR prints the stress tables obtained by ASTER in a format readable by OAR. 2 Syntax IMPR_OAR( ◆ / TABL_MECA = _F( ◇ PRESSION = table, ◇ FLEXION_P = table, ◇ FLEXION_HP = table, ◇ TORSION = table, ), / TABL_THER = _F( ◆ | TEMP = table, | CONTRAINTE = table, ), ◆ UNITE = unit, ◇ TITRE = text, ◇ MODELE = modele, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands 3.1 Operand TABL_MECA ♦ / TABL_MECA This factor keyword makes it possible to supply the stress table or tables, results of a mechanical analysis, to be printed in OAR format. The tables are to be created via the command MACR_LIGN_COUP. In the case where several time instants are computed, the mechanical tables must contain only a single time instant. | PRESSION = tab1 Name of the aster table giving the stresses due to the pressure. | FLEXION_P = tab2 Name of the aster table giving the stresses due to in-plane bending. | FLEXION_HP = tab3 Name of the aster table giving the stresses due to out-of-plane bending. | TORSION = tab4 Name of the aster table giving the stresses due to torsion. 3.2 Operand TABL_THER ♦ / TABL_THER This factor keyword makes it possible to supply the temperature and thermal-stress tables, results of a thermomechanical analysis, to be printed in the OAR format. The tables are to be created via the command MACR_LIGN_COUP. | TEMP = tab1 Name of the aster table giving the temperature as a function of time. | CONTRAINTE = tab2 Name of the aster table giving the thermal stresses as a function of time. Note: in the case where the number of mechanical time instants is smaller than the number of thermal time instants, only the mechanical time instants are printed, so as not to print empty mechanical time instants. 3.3 Operand UNITE ♦ UNITE = unite Logical unit number of the output file. 3.4 Operand TITRE ◊ TITRE = ‘titre’ Keyword making it possible to add a title in the table printed in the OAR format. 3.5 Operand MODELE ◊ MODELE = modele Mandatory keyword in the case of printing of a stress table coming from a thermal analysis (operand TABL_THER). The model to be supplied is the mechanical model . In the case of a thermomechanical analysis (operand TABL_THER) the stresses are printed in the order: - PLAN model: SIXX, SIZZ, SIXZ, SIYY, SIXY, SIYZ, - axisymmetric model: SIXX, SIYY, SIXY, SIZZ, SIXZ, SIYZ, - 3D model: SIXX, SIYY, SIZZ, SIXY, SIXZ, SIYZ. In the case of a mechanical analysis (operand TABL_MECA) the stresses are always printed in the order SIXX, SIYY, SIZZ, SIXY, SIXZ, SIYZ. The operand MODELE is therefore optional, as it has no impact on the stress print format. 4 Examples of use 4.1 Mechanical analysis At the end of the analysis, the user produces the tables necessary for the generation of the OAR file using the command MACR_LIGN_COUPE. The command MACR_LIGN_COUPE must be called as many times as necessary in order to obtain the tables used by IMPR_OAR, namely one command per loading (Pressure, In-plane bending, Out-of-plane bending, Torsion). The command MACR_LIGN_COUPE may contain one or several azimuths. creation of the tables in the aster format, here on two azimuths tableP = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(LIGN_COUPE=(_F(COOR_EXTR=(0.2032, 1.8904, 0.0), COOR_ORIG=(0.1818, 1.8904, 0.0), NB_POINTS=40), _F(COOR_EXTR=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.2032), COOR_ORIG=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.1818), NB_POINTS=40)), NOM_CHAM='SIGM_NOEU', RESULTAT=resulP) tableFP = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(LIGN_COUPE=(_F(COOR_EXTR=(0.2032, 1.8904, 0.0), COOR_ORIG=(0.1818, 1.8904, 0.0), NB_POINTS=40), _F(COOR_EXTR=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.2032), COOR_ORIG=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.1818), NB_POINTS=40)), NOM_CHAM='SIGM_NOEU', RESULTAT=resulFP) tableHFP = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(LIGN_COUPE=(_F(COOR_EXTR=(0.2032, 1.8904, 0.0), COOR_ORIG=(0.1818, 1.8904, 0.0), NB_POINTS=40), _F(COOR_EXTR=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.2032), COOR_ORIG=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.1818), NB_POINTS=40)), NOM_CHAM='SIGM_NOEU', RESULTAT=resulHFP) tableT = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(LIGN_COUPE=(_F(COOR_EXTR=(0.2032, 1.8904, 0.0), COOR_ORIG=(0.1818, 1.8904, 0.0), NB_POINTS=40), _F(COOR_EXTR=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.2032), COOR_ORIG=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.1818), NB_POINTS=40)), NOM_CHAM='SIGM_NOEU', RESULTAT=resulT) printing of the tables in the OAR format IMPR_OAR(TABL_MECA=_F(PRESSION = tableP, FLEXION_P = tableFP, FLEXION_HP = tableHFP, TORSION = tableT,), UNITE = 38, TITRE = 'Resultats mecaniques') 4.2 Thermomechanical analysis The thermomechanical analysis produces two result fields, a thermal field and a stress field, respectively TEMPE and RESU in the example below. At the end of the analysis, the user produces the tables necessary for the generation of the OAR file using the MACR_LIGN_COUPE commands. The MACR_LIGN_COUPE commands may contain one or several azimuths. 1. creation of the thermal results table from the command MACR_LIGN_COUPE tableTEMP = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(LIGN_COUPE=(_F(COOR_EXTR=(0.2032, 1.8904, 0.0), COOR_ORIG=(0.1818, 1.8904, 0.0), NB_POINTS=40), _F(COOR_EXTR=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.2032), COOR_ORIG=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.1818), NB_POINTS=40)), NOM_CHAM='TEMP', RESULTAT=TEMPE) 2. creation of the mechanical results table from the command MACR_LIGN_COUPE tableTEMPSIG = MACR_LIGN_COUPE(LIGN_COUPE=(_F(COOR_EXTR=(0.2032, 1.8904, 0.0), COOR_ORIG=(0.1818, 1.8904, 0.0), NB_POINTS=40), _F(COOR_EXTR=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.2032), COOR_ORIG=(0.0, 1.8904, 0.1818), NB_POINTS=40)), NOM_CHAM='SIGM_NOEU', RESULTAT=RESU) 3. Printing in the OAR format IMPR_OAR(TABL_THER=_F(TEMP= tableTEMP, CONTRAINTE = tableTEMPSIG), UNITE = 38, TITRE = 'Choc thermique 300 70', MODELE = modele_MECA) 5 Precautions Supplying the OAR program requires the conventions specific to this program to be respected, in particular: - the coordinate system in which the component is computed, - the value of the imposed unit forces. The command IMPR_OAR does not handle these points. They remain the responsibility of the user.

The use of this format is not recommended because it only handles simple cases.
