2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Write formats The procedure IMPR_RESU makes it possible to write values to a file in the I-DEAS™ format, software marketed by the company EDS / UGS, with a view to graphical visualisation. 3.1 Operands FORMAT / VERSION The operand FORMAT makes it possible to specify the print format and is mandatory in the case of a printout in the I-DEAS™ format. The operand FORMAT makes it possible to request the creation of an ASCII file, called a "universal file" (of type .unv or .msup), which can be re-read by I‑DEAS™. The universal file used by the I-DEAS™ software has a different computer structure depending on the version of the I-DEAS™ software. The operand VERSION makes it possible to specify the version of I-DEAS™ that one wishes to use. This operand is therefore licit only when the operand FORMAT is equal to 'IDEAS'. The authorised versions are version 4 and version 5 of I-DEAS™. By default, the printout is done in version 5. Example: IMPR_RESU ( RESU= (_F ( FORMAT= 'IDEAS', > VERSION= 4, .........) )) Upward compatibility of the versions of I-DEAS™ is ensured from version 5 onwards. One can therefore use versions later than version 5 of I-DEAS™ with files written in version 5 (because any version N of I-DEAS™ can re-read the files created by version N–1). 3.2 Operand UNITE Logical unit of the written file (30 by default, which corresponds to the default number of the mesh files of type .unv in ASTK). 4 Keyword RESU This factor keyword makes it possible to specify the results to be printed and the format according to which one wants to print them. 5 Printing the mesh: operands MAILLAGE / MODELE The operand ‘MAILLAGE’ makes it possible to print the mesh in the I-DEAS™ format. Printing the mesh can be requested only once and before any other result. By default one prints the whole mesh. One can nevertheless reduce the printing of the mesh to only those mesh cells of the mesh that support a finite element, by defining the operand MODELE. As a result, the concept of type modele is optional in the majority of the printouts. However, it can be used to print only the part of the mesh whose mesh cells are assigned in the model. Furthermore, in the 'IDEAS' format, when the keyword MODELE is supplied one looks for the I‑DEAS™ finite-element type closest to that of Code_Aster , otherwise a default finite-element type is assigned in the I-DEAS™ universal file. In the 'IDEAS' format, the numbering of the nodes is that of Code_Aster except when the mesh comes from the I-DEAS™ software (one checks for the presence of the character string AUTEUR=INTERFACE_IDEAS in the first line of the mesh title and from the tenth position); in this case one restores the I-DEAS™ numbering. Notes: 1. The 3D mesh cells of type PYRAM5 and PYRAM13 are not available in I-DEAS. These mesh cells are therefore not written in the universal file created by the command IMPR_RESU in the format IDEAS. 2. The 3D mesh cell of type HEXA27 is not available in I-DEAS. Aster mesh cells of this type are converted into mesh cells of type HEXA20 in the universal file created by the command IMPR_RESU in the format IDEAS. 6 Operands CHAM_GD and RESULTAT The values of the computed fields are stored in data structures called fields of quantities (grandeurs). These fields of quantities (grandeurs) may be directly accessible (concept CHAM_GD) or be found in a data structure grouping several fields of quantities (grandeurs) (concept resultat). - A field of a quantity (grandeur) is a data structure which makes it possible to store fields defined at the nodes (cham_no_ ) or fields defined by element (cham_elem_ ). For the fields by element, one distinguishes the fields defined at the nodes of the elements and the fields defined at the Gauss points of the elements. - A result concept is composed of one or more fields of quantities (grandeurs). For example, at each analysis step one stores in the resultat data structure the field of the quantity (grandeur) displacement. This structure is therefore a matrix structure of order 2, one index of which is, for example, the list of the analysis time instants and the other the set of the computed fields (displacements, stresses, strains, ...). One accesses in this case a field of a quantity (grandeur) by specifying a value of an access variable (order number, time instant, frequency, mode number, ...) and a field name ('DEPL', 'SIGM_ELNO',...). There exist several types of result concept: evol_elas, evol_noli, mode_meca,.... To each one corresponds a list of fields and a list of licit access variables. Given the resultat data structure, one easily understands that the printout possibilities available are those of the fields of quantities (grandeurs), supplemented by specific possibilities. Notes: 1. The 3D mesh cells of type PYRAM5 and PYRAM13 are not available in I-DEAS. The values of the Aster fields associated with these mesh cells are therefore not written in the universal file created by the command IMPR_RESU in the format IDEAS. 2. The 3D mesh cell of type HEXA27 is not available in I-DEAS. The values of the Aster fields computed on this type of mesh cell are written on mesh cells of type HEXA20; that is, one transfers only the values of the Aster fields on the first 20 nodes. 6.1 Operand CHAM_GD The values of the fields of quantities (grandeurs) are written in one or more datasets of the universal file: | dataset 55 | for the fields at the nodes, | | --- | --- | | dataset 57 | for the fields by element at the nodes, | | dataset 56 | for the fields by element at the Gauss points (in fact, one writes constant fields per element by averaging over the Gauss points). | In I-DEAS™, certain datasets are typed: displacements, stresses, strains, temperature, pressure. One therefore groups the components so as to write the typed datasets, then one writes the other components in datasets of type “UNKNOWN”. Datasets of type “UNKNOWN” contain at most six components; for a field of a quantity (grandeur) of n components one therefore writes n/6 datasets. 6.2 Operand RESULTAT The operand RESULTAT makes it possible to print the fields contained in a result concept. One can for example choose to print only certain fields (Cf. the keyword: NOM_CHAM). The result concept is written field of a quantity (grandeur) by field of a quantity (grandeur) in datasets 55, 56 or 57. 7 Extraction of a field of a quantity (grandeur) 7.1 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM Cf. document U4.71.00. 7.2 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / NOEUD_CMP / NOM_CAS / ANGLE / PRECISION / CRITERE Cf. document U4.71.00. 8 Selection on the components In order to reduce the volume of the printouts and the size of the «universal» I-DEAS™ file, the user can print only the values of certain components (for example only the displacement along the axis X: component DX or only the stress XX: component SIXX). 8.1 Operand TOUT_CMP This keyword makes it possible to indicate that one wishes to print all the components of the field. This is the default value. 8.2 Operand NOM_CMP This keyword makes it possible to choose the list of the components of the CHAM_GD or of all the fields of the result concept that one wishes to print. The keywords TOUT_CMP and NOM_CMP cannot be used simultaneously. When the user specifies the keyword NOM_CMP, the datasets created in the universal file are typed UNKNOWN, which will prevent the user from plotting deformed shapes (even if the dataset contains the components DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY, DRZ) and from computing the Von Mises and/or Tresca criteria (even if the dataset contains the components SIXX, SIYY, … SIXZ). This functionality makes it possible to choose the components, both for cham_no and for cham_elem with real values. The operand NOM_CMP is not programmed for the cham_no and cham_elem with complex values. 9 Selection of the topological entities In order to reduce the volume of the printouts and the size of the «universal» I-DEAS™ file, it is sometimes necessary to print only part of the result. To do this one may wish to print a field at the nodes only at certain nodes, or a field by element only on certain elements. This selection, which will be denoted "selection on topological entities", is possible in the 'IDEAS' format. 9.1 Operand TOUT This keyword indicates that one wishes to print the field over the whole structure (all the nodes for a field at the nodes, all the elements for a field by element). 9.2 Operand NOEUD This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes on which one wishes to print a cham_no. If this keyword is used in the case of the printout of a cham_elem, it is ignored, and the cham_elem is printed on all the mesh cells specified elsewhere. 9.3 Operand GROUP_NO This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the node groups on which one wishes to print a cham_no. If this keyword is used in the case of the printout of a cham_elem, it is ignored, and the cham_elem is printed on all the mesh cells, specified elsewhere. 9.4 Operand MAILLE This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the mesh cells on which one wishes to print a cham_elem. For a cham_no, it makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes, vertices of the mesh cells, at which one wishes to print the cham_no. 9.5 Operand GROUP_MA This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the mesh-cell groups on which one wishes to print a cham_elem. For a cham_no, it makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes, vertices of the mesh cells, at which one wishes to print the cham_no. 10 Operand SOUS_TITRE This argument makes it possible to print a comment subtitle; for more details consult the document U4.03.01. The default SOUS_TITRE is: - for a cham_gd - for a cham_no SOUS_TITRE = ('CHAMP AUX NOEUDS' ) - for a cham_elem SOUS_TITRE = ('CHAMP PAR ELEMENT &LOC(cham_elem)') Example: CHAMP PAR ELEMENT AUX POINTS DE GAUSS - for a resultat - for a cham_no SOUS_TITRE = ( 'CHAMP AUX NOEUDS', 'DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE &NOM_SYMB(Resultat cham_no)&RL', 'NUMERO D''ORDRE &NUM_ORDRE(Resultat cham_no)', '&ACCES(Resultat cham_no) ') Example of printout: CHAMP AUX NOEUDS DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE DEPL NUMERO D'ORDRE: 2 NUME_MODE: 3 FREQ : 5.52739E+00 - for a cham_elem SOUS_TITRE = ( 'CHAMP PAR ELEMENT &LOC(Resultat cham_elem)', 'DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE &NOM_SYMB(Resultat cham_elem)&RL', 'NUMERO D''ORDRE &NUM_ORDRE(Resultat cham_elem) ', '&ACCES(Resultat cham_elem) ') Example of printout: CHAMP PAR ELEMENT AUX NOEUDS DE NOM SYMBOLIQUE EPSI_ELNO NUMERO D'ORDRE: 1 INST : 0.00000E+00 11 Note In Aster, there exist fields by element with sub-points (both for fields by element at the nodes and for fields by element at the Gauss points). In the 'IDEAS' format, IMPR_RESU does not allow the printout of these fields by element with sub-points.

u7.05.21 Procedure IMPR_RESU in 'MED' format u7.05.21 Procedure IMPR_RESU in 'MED' format 1 Purpose Write the result of an analysis to a file in MED format. One describes all the keywords of the command IMPR_RESU U4.91.01 as regards this output format only. One can write, as one chooses, to a file in MED format: - a mesh, - fields at the nodes, - fields at the elements. When writing the fields by element at the Gauss points, one also writes the localisation of the reference elements (coordinates and weights of the Gauss points). MED (Modelling and Exchange of Data) is a neutral data format developed by EDF R&D and the CEA for the exchange of data between analysis codes. The data that one can exchange according to this format are the meshes and the result fields at the nodes and by element. The MED files are binary and portable files (relying on the HDF5 library, Hierarchical Data Format). Writing results to a MED file allows any other analysis code interfaced with MED to read the results produced by Code_Aster via the command IMPR_RESU. 2 Syntax IMPR_RESU( ◇ FORMAT = / "ASTER", / : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Operands FORMAT, UNITE, PROC0, VERSION_MED and INFO 3.1 Operand FORMAT The operand FORMAT makes it possible to specify the format of the file in which to write the result. The format ’MED’ indicates to the procedure IMPR_RESU that the result must be written to a file in MED format. It is the default write format. When a new file is created in MED format, the printout is made in MED format 3.3.1. If the file already exists, the MED format level is retained. 3.2 Operand UNITE Defines the unit in which one writes the med file. By default, UNITE = 80 and corresponds to the default unit of type rmed in astk. 3.3 Operand PROC0 The operand PROC0, whose default value is 'OUI', makes it possible to restrict the printout to the processor of rank 0. If one assigns it the value 'NON', the printouts will be carried out on all the processors. 3.4 Operand INFO The keyword INFO, when it is equal to 2, makes it possible to obtain information on the printouts carried out by the command. 3.5 Operand VERSION_MED ◊ VERSION_MED = /’3.3.1’, [DEFAUT] /’4.0.0’, /’4.1.0’, When a new file is created in med format, the printout is made in med format 3.3.1. If the file already exists, the med format level is retained. One can change the MED file version with the keyword VERSION_MED. 4 Factor keyword RESU This factor keyword makes it possible to specify the results and the fields to be printed. 4.1 Operand MAILLAGE If the result is a mesh (operand maillage U4.91.01), the data reported in the result file in MED format are: | the list of nodes | number, name, coordinates, | | --- | --- | | the list of mesh cells | number, name, type, name of the nodes, | | the list of node groups | number, name, number of nodes, names of the nodes, | | the list of mesh-cell groups | number, name, number of mesh cells, names of the mesh cells. | Note: In a MED file, there is a partition of the nodes and of the mesh cells according to the groups. A partition corresponds to a MED family. In a MED file, the groups are distributed within the families: one therefore finds families of nodes and families of elements. 4.2 Operand RESULTAT The operand RESULTAT makes it possible to print, in a MED file, fields contained in a resultat concept. One writes the following information to the ’MESSAGE’ file: - operand ’RESULTAT’, - operand ’NOM_CHAM’, - operand ’NUME_ORDRE’, - name of the field stored in the MED file: concatenation of the three preceding operands. If INFO_MAILLAGE = = ‘OUI’, more detailed information is printed in the ‘MESSAGE’ file when the MED mesh is written. One may for example obtain the types of mesh cells printed, the names of the MED families that are created, etc. 4.3 Operand CARA_ELEM The operand CARA_ELEM is used for the printout of the fields with sub-points. When CARA_ELEM is supplied, the fields with sub-points are printed by adding information to the MED file that makes it possible to position the sub-points, taking into account the information contained in the sd_cara_elem (thickness of a shell, twist angle of a multi-fibre beam, …). 4.4 Operand CHAM_GD The operand CHAM_GD makes it possible to print in the file a data structure of type cham_gd. Concretely, one can therefore print with this keyword a carte, a field by element or a field at the nodes. 4.5 Operand NOM_CHAM_MED The operand NOM_CHAM_MED makes it possible to define the name of the MED field. It is a string of 64 characters. This can be used in particular when one wishes to print certain components of the field as several fields in the same MED file (for example for the visualisation of SIRO_ELEM). 4.6 Operand NOM_RESU_MED The operand NOM_RESU_MED is an alternative to NOM_CHAM_MED concerning the terminology of the MED fields. Its use will make it possible to no longer name the MED fields explicitly, which means that all the fields contained in the result will be printed. Each MED field name will be constructed from: - the character string supplied to NOM_RESU_MED (a string of at most 8 characters) , - the symbolic name of the Aster field. For example: IMPR_RESU = ( FORMAT = ’MED’, RESU = _F( RESULTAT = U, NOM_RESU_MED = ’U_HAUT’, GROUP_MA = ’HAUT’, NUME_ORDRE = 1, ) ) If the result U contains the fields DEPL and SIEF_ELGA, then the command above will produce the MED fields: - ’U_HAUT__DEPL’ , - ’U_HAUT__SIEF_ELGA’ , This can be used in particular when one wishes to print, in the same MED file, the same field on different mesh-cell groups. 4.7 Operand IMPR_NOM_VARI This keyword is useful in the case of the internal variables. When it is used and the printout of a field VARI_ has been requested, it is in fact a field VARI_ _NOMME that will be printed. This field will have components whose name will be based on the catalogue of the constitutive laws used in the analysis. If two constitutive laws have common internal variables, these will be merged into a single component. 4.8 Operand PARTIE It is not possible to write complex fields. That is why one must choose between the real part (PARTIE=’REEL’) , the complex part (PARTIE=’IMAG’), the modulus (PARTIE='MODULE') or the phase (PARTIE='PHASE'). 4.9 Operand TYPE_NOM In the case where the type of result is a MULT_ELAS (result of MACRO_ELAS_MULT). One must specify how the results will be written to the MED file. The default value taken by TYPE_NOM is "NUME_ORDRE". Thus, each load case is saved on a time instant of the result. The other value that TYPE_NOM can take is "NOM_CAS"; in this case, each case will be stored in a different result whose result name in the MED file will be: "NOM_CAS_NOM_CHAM" For example, if the result contains two load cases FX and FY , each containing the fields DEPL and SIEF_ELGA, the following MED fields will be produced: - 'FX______DEPL' - 'FX______SIEF_ELGA' - 'FY______DEPL' - 'FY______SIEF_ELGA' 4.10 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / NOEUD_CMP / NOM_CAS / ANGLE / PRECISION / CRITERE Cf. document U4.91.01. 5 Selection on the components Another way of reducing the volume of the printouts is to print only the values of certain components (for example only the displacement along the axis X: component DX). Note: the selection of the components does not work for the fields with sub-points. 5.1 Operand TOUT_CMP This keyword makes it possible to indicate that one wishes to print all the components of the field. 5.2 Operand NOM_CMP This keyword makes it possible to choose the list of the components of the cham_gd or of all the fields of the result concept that one wishes to print. The keywords TOUT_CMP and NOM_CMP cannot be used simultaneously. These components are described in the specific documentation of the elements. 6 Selection of the topological entities In order to reduce the volume of the printouts, it is sometimes necessary to print only part of the result. To do this one can print a field at the nodes only at certain nodes, or a field by element only on certain elements. Note: the selection of the topological entities does not work for the fields with sub-points. 6.1 Operand TOUT This keyword indicates that one wishes to print the field over the whole structure (all the nodes for a field at the nodes, all the elements for a field by element). 6.2 Operand GROUP_NO This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the node groups on which one wishes to print a cham_no. If this keyword is used in the case of the printout of a cham_elem, it is ignored, and the cham_elem is printed on all the mesh cells, specified elsewhere. 6.3 Operand GROUP_MA This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the mesh-cell groups on which one wishes to print a cham_elem. For a cham_no, it makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes, vertices of the mesh cells, at which one wishes to print the cham_no. 7 Example IMPR_RESU = ( FORMAT = ’MED’, RESU = _F( RESULTAT = REMEZERO, NOM_CHAM = ’ERME_ELEM’, NUME_ORDRE = 3, ) ) Execution of the command IMPR_RESU will produce the following display in the ’MESSAGE’ file: RESULTAT : REMEZERO CHAMP : ERME_ELEM NUME_ORDRE : 3 ==> NOM MED : REMEZEROERME_ELEM #Exemple d’utilisation de NOM_CHAM_MED pour l’impression de SIRO_ELEM: IMPR_RESU(FORMAT=’MED’, RESU=( _F(RESULTAT=RESUNL, NOM_CHAM=(’SIRO_ELEM’,), NOM_CHAM_MED=(’RESUNL__SIRO_ELEM_NORMAL’), NOM_CMP=(’SIG_NX’,’SIG_NY’,’SIG_NZ’,’SIG_N’,), GROUP_MA=’PRES’,), _F(RESULTAT=RESUNL, NOM_CHAM=(’SIRO_ELEM’,), NOM_CHAM_MED=(’RESUNL__SIRO_ELEM_TANGENT’), NOM_CMP=(’SIG_TX’,’SIG_TY’,’SIG_TZ’,), GROUP_MA=’PRES’,), _F(RESULTAT=RESUNL, NOM_CHAM=(’SIRO_ELEM’,), NOM_CHAM_MED=(’RESUNL__SIRO_ELEM_T1’), NOM_CMP=(’SIG_T1X’,’SIG_T1Y’,’SIG_T1Z’,’SIG_T1’,), GROUP_MA=’PRES’,), _F(RESULTAT=RESUNL, NOM_CHAM=(’SIRO_ELEM’,), NOM_CHAM_MED=(’RESUNL__SIRO_ELEM_T2’), NOM_CMP=(’SIG_T2X’,’SIG_T2Y’,’SIG_T2Z’,’SIG_T2’,), GROUP_MA=’PRES’,), ),);

2, ) ◆ : obligatoire ◇ : optionnel ⟐ : présent par défaut & : ensemble / : un seul parmi | : plusieurs choix possibles 3 Keyword RESU This factor keyword makes it possible to specify the results to be printed and the format according to which one wants to print them. 3.1 Operand MAILLAGE This operand makes it possible to choose the mesh that one wishes to print. The simultaneous printout of the mesh and of fields is impossible. 3.2 Selection of the data to be printed The values of the computed fields are stored in data structures called fields of quantities (grandeurs). These fields of quantities (grandeurs) may be directly accessible (concept CHAM_GD) or be found in a data structure grouping several fields of quantities (grandeurs) (concept resultat). - A field of a quantity (grandeur) is a data structure which makes it possible to store fields defined at the nodes (cham_no_ ) or fields defined by element (cham_elem_ ). For the fields by element, one distinguishes the fields defined at the nodes of the elements and the fields defined at the Gauss points of the elements. - A result concept is composed of one or more fields of quantities (grandeurs). For example, at each analysis step one stores in the resultat data structure the field of the quantity (grandeur) displacement. This structure is therefore a matrix structure of order 2, one index of which is, for example, the list of the analysis time instants and the other the set of the computed fields (displacements, stresses, strains, ...). One accesses in this case a field of a quantity (grandeur) by specifying a value of an access variable (order number, time instant, frequency, mode number, ...) and a field name ('DEPL', 'SIGM_ELNO',...). There exist several types of result concept: evol_elas, evol_noli, mode_meca,.... To each one corresponds a list of fields and a list of licit access variables. Given the resultat data structure, one easily understands that the printout possibilities available are those of the fields of quantities (grandeurs), supplemented by specific possibilities. Warning One cannot print in the same file the MAILLAGE and the RESULTAT/CHAM_GD, GMSH does not know how to read such a file. The command therefore stops if the two keywords are present. 3.2.1 Operand CHAM_GD For the CHAM_NO, the components of the field at the nodes are split into a vector field grouping the components DX, DY, DZ and into as many scalar fields as there are other components. Example : In the case of a field at the nodes of quantity (grandeur) DEPL and whose modelling is of beam type, one writes: - 1 vector field (grouping the set of the translation components), - 3 scalar fields (one field per degree of rotation). For the CHAM_ELEM, one prints only the fields by element at the nodes (_ELNO_). A field by element at the nodes is split into as many scalar fields as there are components. Note When one writes a result in the GMSH format, the title of the fields, which appears in GMSH, consists of the name of the Aster result + the name of the field + the component. Example: RESU_DEPL_DX: the component 'DX' of the field 'DEPL' of the result 'RESU' If one writes a derived field, one inserts the name of the sensitivity parameter with respect to which one differentiates, between the name of the result and the name of the field. Example: RESU_PS1_DEPL_DX: the derivative with respect to 'PS1' of the component 'DX' of the field 'DEPL' of the result 'RESU'. 3.2.2 Operand RESULTAT The operand RESULTAT makes it possible to print the fields contained in a result concept. One can for example choose to print only certain fields (Cf. the keyword: NOM_CHAM). The result concept is written field of quantity (grandeur) by field of quantity (grandeur) as described in [§4.1]. 4 Choice of the fields to be printed 4.1 Operands TOUT_CHAM / NOM_CHAM Cf. document U4.71.00. 4.2 Operands TOUT_ORDRE / NUME_ORDRE / LIST_ORDRE / NUME_MODE / INST / LIST_INST / FREQ / LIST_FREQ / NOEUD_CMP / NOM_CAS / ANGLE / PRECISION / CRITERE Cf. document U4.71.00. 5 Selection of the geometrical zones and of the components In order to reduce the volume of the printouts, it is sometimes necessary to print only part of the result. To do this one can print a field at the nodes or a field by element only on certain elements. This selection, which one will denote "selection on topological entities", is possible in the 'GMSH' format. 5.1 Operand MAILLE This keyword makes it possible to indicate the list of the mesh cells on which one wishes to print a cham_elem. For a cham_no, it makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes, vertices of the mesh cells, at which one wishes to print the cham_no. 5.2 Operand GROUP_MA This operand makes it possible to indicate the list of the mesh-cell groups on which one wishes to print a cham_elem. For a cham_no, it makes it possible to indicate the list of the nodes, vertices of the mesh cells, at which one wishes to print the cham_no. 5.3 Operand TYPE_CHAM GMSH because it is capable of visualising vectors and tensors; it is thus possible to visualise things other than each of the components independently. This operand makes it possible to choose the type of field to be printed ('VECT_2D', 'VECT_3D', 'SCALAIRE', 'TENS_2D' or 'TENS_3D'). The default value is 'SCALAIRE'. 5.4 Operand NOM_CMP This operand makes it possible to choose the list of the components that one wishes to print according to the type of field chosen. If one has chosen to print scalar fields it is not necessary to supply NOM_CMP; in this case, each of the components will be printed independently of one another. 5.5 Operand PARTIE One cannot print complex fields in the GMSH format; one must therefore, for such fields, select the REEL (real) part or the IMAG (imaginary) part to be printed. 6 Operand VERSION The mesh cells accepted by GMSH (in post-processing) are, since version 1.35, the mesh cells of type POI1, SEG2, TRIA3, QUAD4, TETRA4, HEXA8, PENTA6, PYRAM5, which corresponds to: VERSION = ‘1.2’ which is the default value If one needs to visualise the fields with an old version of GMSH or if one wishes to cut all the mesh cells into POI1, SEG2, TRIA3 and TETRA4, one uses VERSION = ‘1.0’. In order to be able to visualise the views with GMSH, the mesh is modified so as to have only GMSH mesh cells. At present, the PYRAM13 mesh cells are not processed. - the SEG3 is decomposed into 2 SEG2, - the SEG4 is decomposed into 3 SEG2, - the TRIA6 is decomposed into 4 TRIA3, - the TRIA7 is decomposed into 4 TRIA3, - the QUAD4 is decomposed into 2 TRIA3 (cut only if VERSION=’1.0’), - the QUAD8 is decomposed into 6 TRIA3, - the QUAD9 is decomposed into 6 TRIA3, - the TETRA10 is decomposed into 8 TETRA4, - the PENTA6 is decomposed into 3 TETRA4 (cut only if VERSION=’1.0’), - the PENTA15 is decomposed into 16 TETRA4, - the PYRAM5 is decomposed into 2 TETRA4 (cut only if VERSION=’1.0’), - the HEXA8 is decomposed into 6 TETRA4 (cut only if VERSION=’1.0’), - the HEXA20 is decomposed into 24 TETRA4, - the HEXA27 is decomposed into 48 TETRA4. Note 1 The TRIA7 (respectively QUAD9) is cut like the TRIA6 (resp. QUAD8) because the central node does not carry a displacement degree of freedom in modelling COQUES_3D. Note 2 With the recent versions of GMSH ( >1.60 ), one could avoid cutting the elements. The choice is not available in Code_Aster because it is possible to read the MED format in GMSH since version 2.0. 7 Operand UNITE UNITE makes it possible to choose on which file the results will be written. By default, UNITE = 37 in the 'GMSH' format. One can thus print results on different files at each IMPR_RESU command. The natural suffix of the GMSH post-processing files is .pos and the usual logical unit (by default in astk) is 37. 8 Operand PROC0 The operand PROC0, whose default value is 'OUI', makes it possible to restrict the printout to the processor of rank 0. If one assigns it the value 'NON', the printouts will be carried out on all the processors.

v0.00.000 Classification of Validation Documentation v0.00.000 Classification of Validation Documentation Summary: The Validation Manual consolidates the tests used to ensure the non-regression of the features available in Code_Aster . These tests are offered and maintained by the respective functionality managers. This document presents the classification of the tests. 1 Reminder of documentation management principles The Validation Manual consolidates the code validation documentation. The validation sheets it contains specify the area of guaranteed use and give confidence in the use of the code. They illustrate the use of different modelling options and are an essential complement to learning about structural calculations. 1.1 Identification of validation and codification manual fascicles Each booklet is identified by a key on all pages. This key allows for the progressive management of documentation as it is written. The manual is divided into ten parts . The parts of the manual are materialized by cardboard interlayers, delivered with the binder. They are numbered from 0 to 9 . The parts of the manual are made up of fascicles , software notes under A.Q. which comply with the rules for the presentation of D.E.R. technical notes (notes HI, HP, ...); a note may contain one or more fascicles. Each part of the manual may contain a priori one hundred booklets. Each specification is identified by a specification number between 00 and 99 . A booklet can be cut, as required, into documents numbered from 0 . Key: Manual Part.Fascicle number[.Document number] | V1.01 | Validation Manual / Organization of Validation / | | --- | --- | | V3.04.004 | Validation Manual / Linear Mechanics / Linear Static of Volumetric Structures / SSLV004 | Each validation test is accompanied by a coded reference which is unique to it (see attached table). This coding, taken from the VPCS guide, consists of eight alphanumeric characters: - takes into account the type of problem dealt with by the test (4 alphabetical characters), - the serial number of the test in the list of tests of the same type (2 or 3 numeric characters). The four alphabetical characters indicate in order: | 1er | character | : | the scope, | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 2nd | character | : | the type of analysis, | | 3rd | character | : | the type of behaviour, | | 4th | character | : | the type of model. | Example : SDLA04 will be the 4th SDLA test Document numbers between 01 and 99 correspond to tests from the VPCS guide. The numbers between 100 and 299 correspond to the tests offered by the developers. The numbers between 300 and 399 are reserved for tests resulting from the independent validation of version 3, between 400 and 499 to that of version 4,... For tests resulting from independent validation, only those included in the list of non-regression of Code_Aster are documented in the Validation Manual. A test can be associated with several modellings. Each model is also coded by itself and is composed of eight characters. The first six or seven are made up of the coded reference of the test, the last character indicates the order number of the model in the list of modellings associated with the test. By convention, the numbers will be taken in the following order: A, B, C, ……, Y, Z Example : SDLA04C will be the coding relative to the 3rd model studied in the SDLA04 test. If only one model is studied in a test, it will be indicated A. Example : SDLA04A, SSLV101A. By convention YYYY tests are performance tests and ZZZZ tests are tests to validate computer features. Other names not corresponding to the nomenclature exist. These tests are generally linked to trade tools. In particular, it is a test of the different possibilities of the commands DEFI_FONCTION, DEFI_NAPPE, CALC_FONCTION, INFO_FONCTION, LIRE_FONCTION, IMPR_FONCTION, DEFI_PROP_ALEA. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.102 ZZZZ102 - Read accelerogram and oscillator spectrum v1.01.102 ZZZZ102 - Read accelerogram and oscillator spectrum Summary: This test concerns: 1. reading in different formats of an accelerogram on an external file (LIRE_FONCTION U4.21.08) and testing the attributes of the function and the maximum value, 2. verification of the calculation of the oscillator spectrum by CALC_FONCTION U4.62.04 and the high frequency acceleration value ( >35.5\mathrm{Hz} ) as a function of the max value of the accelerogram, 3. playing a spectrum of free-format oscillators on an external file (LIRE_FONCTION U4.21.08). In this example, the frequency list must therefore be modified at the operator's input. It is therefore necessary to be careful about the spectral content of the signal and not to trust blindly the default values (the default list is well suited to the regulatory signals that are usually encountered in France with a lower cut-off frequency: from the order of 20 to 30\mathrm{Hz} ). v1.01.103 ZZZZ103 – Jeveux memory manager core function unit tests v1.01.103 ZZZZ103 – Jeveux memory manager core function unit tests Summary: This test allows you to check the operation of basic JEVEUX memory manager utilities. Model A prints values associated with platform-dependent numerical constants. In particular, the lengths and extremal values of integer numbers and floating numbers, some particular mathematical constants, and certain parameters related to the use of memory and files. The values are accessible using the ENVIMA functions described in D6.01.01. Model B checks that the base extension functionality is triggered (on a volatile basis) in case of lack of memory and space in the previous database. Modelling C checks the extension functionality of the bases on the global basis, as well as the retassing. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.104 ZZZZ104 – Validation of command variables in split commands with macro-elements v1.01.104 ZZZZ104 – Validation of command variables in split commands with macro-elements Summary: This test is designed to validate the consideration of the command variables with macro-elements in split commands and also in monolithic commands. In both modellings, it is a beam (D_PLAN) half of which is a macro-element and the other one consists of finished elements. A temperature load is affected throughout the beam. References are obtained by the same calculation without macro-elements. Modelization A: The calculation is done with STAT_NON_LINE. The beam is bi-clamped. We check that the stresses are the same as those in the reference calculation. Modelling B: The calculation is done in burst control. The beam is clamped at one end and blocked according to X at the other. It is checked that the movements are the same as those of the reference calculation. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.108 ZZZZ108 - Code_Aster-MISS3D Interface Test v1.01.108 ZZZZ108 - Code_Aster-MISS3D Interface Test Summary: This test allows the Modelling of a structure of model-type building skewer (elements discrete and beams) in linear harmonic and transient dynamics, supplemented at its elements density and superfacial base. Its interest is to test the Code_Aster commands specific to the soil-structure interaction for interfacing with MISS3D software (ECP-LMSSM at). In this test, post-processing also tests the displacement of the control points located in the ground and added to the structure Modelling by Code_Aster . Finally, it is verified that the accelerograms can be given directly on a frequency basis by reproducing the calculation for which they are given on a time basis. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A skewer model of the building is used with a radier that is modelled by a layer of 136 mesh cells TRIA3 superfacial and 6 degrees of freedom is assigned to its lower side. The Modelling presented is a simplified model for which the building is represented by a flat structure. Four substructures are represented by four non-heavy vertical beams, of variable bending inertia and bearing nodal masses and inertias representing civil engineering and equipment. Discreet elastic restraintss connect these beams at different levels. The four beams are clamped on a general radier of great bending inertia. 1.2 Material properties E=4.0{10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} \rho =2500\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} (elements heavy only) \nu =0.15 - features of point weights ('M_TR_D_N') and restraints node-node ('K_TR_D_L'). 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Restraints solid on the top and bottom of the radier (LIAISON_SOLIDE on the nodes \mathit{HRADIER} and \mathit{SRADIER} groups). - Blocking of the node centre ( \mathit{N98} ) of the lower side (6 degrees of freedom) to calculate the rigid body modes, - {10}^{4}\mathit{Newtons} nodal force applied to node \mathit{N1500} , - Or transient acceleration \mathit{EUR} spectrum in X direction of amplitude 0.25g , - Or unit harmonic acceleration in the X and Y directions 1.4 Initial conditions Zero displacements, speeds and acceleration. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The resolution in the projection modal base (constituted by eigenmodes with blocked interface and static modes forced calculated by the Code_Aster ) performed by MISS3D in the frequency range on the elements border finished. There is also the possibility to perform this resolution by Code_Aster using the harmonic resolution operator after recovering the ground impedances and seismic forces variable according to frequency from MISS3D. MISS3D post-processed time return by Fourier reverse transformation. Return to the physical basis of a harmonic or transient evolution resulting from Code_Aster . 2.2 Baseline Harmonic responses to the upper nodes (N800, N1500 and N2700) at frequencies close to resonances. Maximum transient accelerations at these same points for EUR spectrum of 0.25g . 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution Digital solution. 2.4 Bibliographical references - MISS3D User Manual and Reference - (version 5.6) (D. CLOUTEAU - MSSM-ECP Laboratory). - Interface Aster -MISS3D: principle and use (G. DEVESA - Technical Note HP‐62/95/038/B. 3 Modelling C 3.1 Modelling characteristics 25 elements beam POU_D_T, 5 elements de restraint node-node (DIS_TR_L), 26 elements POI1 point mass (DIS_TR_N), 2 elements POI1 point zero mass (DIS_T) for modelling control points in the post-treating ground, 136 elements density ('3D' model) for radiating and 136 elements DST for its lower face. 1st harmonic calculation: in the (0,10\mathit{Hz}) step by step interval of 0.1\mathit{Hz} , 2nd harmonic calculation: in the (0,10\mathit{Hz}) step by step interval of 0.1\mathit{Hz} , 3rd transient calculation: in the (0,10s) interval by step of {10}^{-2}s . This Modelling is characterized by the presence of soil control points to model the deconvolution of a vertical sinusoidal signal imposed on the soil surface. 3 elements POI1 point zero mass (DIS_T) are introduced to model control points in the soil to be treated. They correspond to 3 levels in depth of homogeneous soil: surface and shifted respectively from one quarter and half a flat wave of pressure with vertical impact. This soil is a homogeneous soil, the characteristics of which are summarized in the following table: | Size | Size ( m ) | \rho ( \mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} ) | \nu | E ( \mathit{MPa} ) |  | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Layer 1 | 35 | 2400 | 0.4 | 70 | 0.1 | Table 6.1-1: Caractéristiques mécaniques du sol homogène These values induce a pressure wave speed {V}_{P}=250m/s , which gives a pressure wave length of 50 meters for an excitation frequency of 5\mathit{Hz} . The second and third control points are therefore depressed from 12.5m and 25m respectively in the vertical direction. A transient (0,4s) stepwise calculation of {10}^{-2}s is performed with a sinusoidal 5\mathit{Hz} frequency acceleration imposed on the ground surface in the vertical direction Z . 3.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes : 190 Number of mesh cells and type: 136 PENTA6, 136 TRIA3, 30 SEG2, 28 POI1 3.3 reference solution For sinusoidal frequency f stress in C wave speed and \beta hysteretic damping ground, analytically, the Z depth amplitude factor is: \mathit{Az}=\mathit{sh}(\beta \pi fZ/C)\sin(2\pi fZ/C)+\mathit{ch}(\beta \pi fZ/C)\sin(2\pi fZ/C) The corresponding amplitude in speed will then be: \mathit{Vz}=\mathit{Az}/(2\pi f) And the corresponding amplitude on the move will be: \mathit{Dz}=-\mathit{Az}/{(2\pi f)}^{2} It can only be seen from comparison that the peaks of harmonic responses correspond well to the resonance frequencies obtained with an equivalent soil spring model. On the other hand, for the resolution in the frequency domain of the harmonic problem projected on a modal basis consisting of eigenmodes with blocked interface and static modes forced, the same results are obtained by Code_Aster and by MISS3D. 3.4 Tested quantities and results Transitional calculation (actual), resolution by MISS3D and post-processing at control points. v1.01.111 ZZZZ111 - Validation of the DEFI_CABLE_BP operator v1.01.111 ZZZZ111 - Validation of the DEFI_CABLE_BP operator Summary: The purpose of this test case is to validate the DEFI_CABLE_BP operator, which calculates the voltage profiles in prestressing cables of a concrete structure, in accordance with BPEL rules: these allow for the loss of tension by contact between cables and concrete, by recoiling at anchors, by removing and creeping concrete and by relaxing steel, the material constituting the cables. For modellings A and B, the structure is a semi-cylindrical veil, containing four prestressed cables in its thickness. The cables each describe a half circle in a horizontal plane, and thus travel the sail along its length. Two cables have an eccentricity compared to the average radius of the sail. The results obtained are validated by comparison with those theoretically expected. The voltage profiles can be explained analytically outside the areas where the losses by recoil apply to the anchors. This calculation is made for the modellings DKT (modelization A) and Q4GG (modelization B). Modellings C and D can validate the operation of the PROJKM routine in cases where the projection can only be made on an node. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The concrete veil has a semi-cylindrical shape: the height is H=10m and the average radius is R=\mathrm{10 }m . The thickness of the sail is e=0,6m . The "equivalent average radius", in the sense of BPEL on the vertical section of the sail is therefore {r}_{m}=0,283m , knowing that: {r}_{m}=\frac{\mathit{eH}}{2(e+H)} (reference BPEL 2.1.5) The cables each describe a half circle in a horizontal plane, and thus travel the sail along its length. The dimensions of the planes containing the cables are: - for cable number 1: {z}_{1}=1m ; - for cable 2: {z}_{2}=3,5m ; - for cable 3: {z}_{3}=6m ; - for cable #4: {z}_{4}=8,5m . Cables 3 and 4 are eccentric to the average beam of the sail, respectively: - {\mathrm{ex}}_{3}=0,05m ; - {\mathrm{ex}}_{4}=0,1m . The right section of each cable is {S}_{a}=1,5{.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} . 1.2 Material properties 1.2.1 Concrete material constituting the veil Elastic properties: | Young's modulus | {E}_{b}={3.10}^{10}\mathrm{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio | {\nu}_{b}=0,2 | Characteristic parameters for estimating voltage loss: | Flat rate of stress loss by concrete creep | {x}_{\mathrm{flu}}=0,07 | | --- | --- | | Flat rate of tension loss by removal of concrete | {x}_{\mathrm{ret}}=0,08 | 1.2.2 Steel material constituting cables Elastic properties: | Young's modulus | {E}_{a}=2,1{.10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio | {\nu}_{a}=0,3 | | Characteristic parameters for estimating voltage loss: | | | --- | --- | | Steel relaxation at 1000 hours | {\rho}_{1000}=2\text{\%} | | Adimensional relaxation coefficient of prestressed steel | {\mu}_{0}=0,3 | | Steel elastic limit constraint | {f}_{\mathit{prg}}=1,77{.10}^{9}\mathit{Pa} | | Curved friction coefficient | f=0,2{\mathrm{rad}}^{-1} | | Voltage loss coefficient per unit length | \varphi ={3.10}^{-3}{m}^{-1} | 1.3 Loading A normal tensile force is applied to both ends of each cable. The applied voltage value is {F}_{0}={2.10}^{5}N . The following relationships are used to assess the loss of tension by relaxation of cables over time: | \Delta {\sigma}_{\mathit{pj}}=\Delta {\sigma}_{p}(x)r(j) | (reference BPEL 3.3.24) | | --- | --- | | \Delta {\sigma}_{p}=\frac{6}{100}{\rho}_{1000}(\frac{{\sigma}_{pi}(x)}{{f}_{\mathit{prg}}}-{\mu}_{0}){\sigma}_{pi}(x) | (reference BPEL 3.3.23) | | r(j)=\frac{j}{j+9\times {r}_{m}} | (reference BPEL 3.3.24 and 2.1.51) | | {\sigma}_{pi}(x) | called initial voltage, the point voltage d-abscisse x , after instant voltage loss. | | --- | --- | | j | assessment moment, day | | {r}_{m} | equivalent average radius, \mathit{cm} | The characteristics are evaluated on the j=10 day. The test results shall be carried out in accordance with the requirements of the Annex to Regulation (EU) No 1303/2013. Note: This problem ignores the equilibrium resolution of the complete steel-beton structure and is limited to the determination of prestress in the cables according to BPEL. 2 reference solution 2.1 Curvilinear abscess and cumulative angular deviation The cables each describe a semi-circle path in a horizontal plane. As a result, the curvilinear abscisse s and the cumulative angular deviation \alpha very simply express: \left\{ \begin{array}{c}s={R}_{c}\theta \\ \alpha =\theta \end{array}\right. where {R}_{c} is the radius of the half circle described by the cable, and \theta l-azimut is the radius of the half circle described by the cable, and \theta l-azimut is the radius of the half circle described by the cable. The reference values for the tests are estimated using these expressions. 2.2 Normal effort in cables A cable describing a horizontal half circle of {R}_{c} radius is considered. {\theta}_{0} l-azimut is noted to be the end of the area where the voltage losses by reverse apply to the first anchorage; \pi -{\theta}_{0} is the beginning of the area where the voltage losses by reverse apply to the second anchorage. Taking into account the previous expressions of curvilinear abscisse and the cumulative angular deviation, the tension profile along the cable can be set by the \theta l-azimut, outside areas where the losses by recoil apply to anchors: F(\theta )=-{F}_{0}({x}_{\mathit{flu}}+{x}_{\mathit{ret}}) +{F}_{0}\left[1+r(j)\times \frac{5}{100}{\rho}_{1000}\times {\mu}_{0}\right]\exp(-(f+\varphi {R}_{c})\theta ) -{F}_{0}\times r(j)\times \frac{5}{100}{\rho}_{1000}\times \frac{{F}_{0}}{{S}_{a}{f}_{\mathit{prg}}}\times \exp(-2(f+\varphi {R}_{c})\theta ) on the \left[{\theta}_{0};\frac{\pi}{2}\right] interval F(\theta )=-{F}_{0}({x}_{\mathit{flu}}+{x}_{\mathit{ret}}) +{F}_{0}\left[1+r(j)\times \frac{5}{100}{\rho}_{1000}\times {\mu}_{0}\right]\exp(-(f+\varphi {R}_{c})(\pi -\theta )) -{F}_{0}\times r(j)\times \frac{5}{100}{\rho}_{1000}\times \frac{{F}_{0}}{{S}_{a}{f}_{\mathit{prg}}}\times \exp(-2(f+\varphi {R}_{c})(\pi -\theta )) on the \left[\frac{\pi}{2};\pi -{\theta}_{0}\right] interval The reference values for the tests are estimated using these expressions, which define a voltage profile symmetrical to the central node. 2.3 Projection index The projection of node from one of the cables on a mesh cell of the concrete veil results in the assignment of a \mathit{IPROJ} projection index according to the following rule: Projection on mesh cell triangle nodes \mathit{N1} peaks , \mathit{N2} and \mathit{N3} : | \mathit{IPROJ}=0 | the point projected is within the triangle; | | --- | --- | | \mathit{IPROJ}=11,12 ou 13 | if the point projected belongs to the [\mathit{N1};\mathit{N2}] , [\mathrm{N2};\mathrm{N3}] or [\mathrm{N3};\mathrm{N1}] edge respectively; | | \mathit{IPROJ}=2 | if there is coincidence of point projected with a node summit. | Projection on mesh cell quadrangle nodes \mathit{N1},\mathit{N2}\mathit{N3} and \mathrm{N4} peaks: | \mathit{IPROJ}=0 | if the point projected is within the quadrangle; | | --- | --- | | \mathit{IPROJ}=11,12,13 ou 14 | if the point projected belongs respectively to the [\mathrm{N1};\mathrm{N2}] , [\mathrm{N2};\mathrm{N3}] , [\mathrm{N3};\mathrm{N4}] or [\mathrm{N4};\mathrm{N1}] edge; | | \mathrm{IPROJ}=2 | if there is coincidence of point projected with a node summit. | The reference values for the tests are estimated by predicting the locations of the cable projection, taking into account their position with respect to the sail and the arrangement of the mesh cells on the sail. 2.4 Excentricity The eccentricity of an node belonging to one of the cables is defined as the distance from this node to the mesh cell of the concrete veil on which it is projected. Viewed in a horizontal plane, the mesh cell trace is a rope on the R radius half circle. \alpha is noted as the angular sector covered by the mesh cell. The node of the cable, noted \mathit{NC} , is located on the {R}_{c} radius half circle. Its relative position relative to the mesh cell is spotted by the \beta zilimut. The (\cos\frac{\alpha}{2};\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}) vector is normal to the rope, which passes through the point (R;0) . The equation of the rope is therefore \cos\frac{\alpha}{2}x+\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}y-R\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}=0 The distance from point to one right in the plane is given by: d=\frac{∣a{x}_{0}+b{x}_{0}+c∣}{\sqrt{{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}}} where ({x}_{\mathrm{0 }};{y}_{0}) is the coordinates of point and \mathit{ax}+\mathit{by}+c=0 is the equation of the right. The node \mathit{NC} of the cable has ({R}_{c}\cos\beta ;{R}_{c}\sin\beta ) coordinates. Its eccentricity compared to the mesh cell of the sail on which it is projected is therefore worth: {\mathit{ex}}_{c}=∣{R}_{c}\cos(\frac{\alpha}{2}-\beta )-R\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}∣ The reference values for the tests are estimated using this expression. 3 Modelization A and B 3.1 Features of modellings The concrete veil is represented by elements DKT for Modelling A and elements Q4GG for Modelling B, supported in both cases by mesh cells quadrangles at 4 nodes: there are 10 mesh cells on a vertical generator and 32 on a horizontal half circle. With this arrangement, the mesh cells have dimensions close to those of a square of 1m on the side. All of the following is common to modellings A and B. e=0,6m thickness is assigned to all mesh cells of the sail, as well as a concrete material for which ELAS and BPEL_BETON behaviors are defined: the parameters take the values given previously in v1.01.111-materiaau-beton-voile. Each cable is represented by 128 elements MECA_BARRE, supported by mesh cells segments at 2 nodes. On a horizontal half circle, there are 4 times more mesh cells on a cable than on the concrete veil. A straight section area {S}_{a}=1,5{.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} is assigned to all mesh cells cables, as well as a steel material for which the ELAS and BPEL_ACIER behaviors are defined: the parameters take the values given previously in v1.01.111-material-steel-cables. The {F}_{0}={2.10}^{5}N voltage is applied to the two nodes ends of each cable. The value of this voltage is consistent with the values of section and elastic limit stress, for twisted prestress cables. The evaluation of the tension losses by relaxation and recoil at anchors is carried out according to the BPEL rules. Since the same voltage is applied to both ends of each cable, and since the anchors are placed on the same step, the voltage profiles obtained must be symmetrical with respect to the nodes cable media. Given the geometrical characteristics and the mesh, the nodes of cables 1 and 2 project on the top nodes and edges of the mesh cells of the concrete veil. For the nodes of these two cables, the projection indices obtained must be in accordance with the following sequence: 2 for the first node, then 13-13-13-2 until the last node. The nodes of cables 3 and 4 are projected on the edges and inside the mesh cells of the concrete veil. For the nodes of these two cables, the projection indices obtained must be in accordance with the following sequence: 14 for the first node, then 0-0-0-12 until the last node. The projection index allocation rule is defined in v1.01.111-projection index. Based on Mesh characteristics, nodes eccentricities of the cables are evaluated using v1.01.111-eccentricite expression with \alpha =\frac{\pi}{32} and \beta =0,\frac{\alpha}{4},\frac{\alpha}{2},\frac{3\alpha }{4} . 3.2 Tested quantities and results 3.2.1 Curvilinear abscess The tested component is ABS_CURV. | Identification (node) | Reference type | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 1,090035.10–1 | 0.10% | 3.3 Remarks Relative differences are obtained for the cumulative angular deviation of an order of quantity significantly higher than those obtained for curvilinear abscisse, which is calculated with very good accuracy. The cause is inherent in the cubic spline interpolation method used to interpolate the cable trajectories. This method consists of interpolating the trajectory over each sub-range by a polynomial of order 3, ensuring continuity of the first and second derivatives at the sub-interval terminals. The interpolation of a circular trajectory by order 3 polynomials is an approximation, the effects of which are more sensitive on the second derivatives than on the first derivatives. Therefore, the accuracy obtained for the curvilinear abscisse, calculated using the first derivative of the trajectory, is significantly better than that obtained for the cumulative angular deviation, calculated using cross products between the first and second derivatives. To improve the accuracy on the cumulative angular deviation, the mesh should be significantly refined: this approach is not valid a priori, as it would lead to very substantial additional calculation costs for a small gain in accuracy. The differences by default on the curvilinear abscisse and the cumulative angular deviation induce differences by excess on the calculated voltage values, but the accuracy remains satisfactory: this validates the calculation method. The projection indices obtained are consistent with those expected, and the eccentricities are calculated with very good accuracy: this validates the projection operations. 4 Modelling C The objective of this Modelling is to validate the PROJKM routine in case the projections on the mesh cells and then on the sides are impossible. 4.1 Modelling characteristics et mesh A geometry with double "coupole" curvature is used for concrete. The command file is based on Modelling A with a minimum modification to fit the mesh and tests of this model; all other parameters are identical: Modelling, materials, loadings, ... 4.2 Tested quantities and results The projection index for the 3 nodes cable is tested and the eccentricity of the central point, the projection of which was calculated by the PROJKN routine. | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | N101 - INDICE_PROJECTION | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 0 | 1.0E-03 | | N105 - INDICE_PROJECTION | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 2 | 1.0E-03 | | N109 - INDICE_PROJECTION | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 0 | 1.0E-03 | | N105 - EXCENTRICITE | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 0.1 | 1.0E-10 | 5 Modelling D This Modelling is the same as C Modelling. v1.01.112 ZZZZ112 - Cylinder under variable pressure. Validation of LIRE_PLEXUS v1.01.112 ZZZZ112 - Cylinder under variable pressure. Validation of LIRE_PLEXUS Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the operation of the LIRE_PLEXUS command. This allows reading pressure fields calculated by PLEXUS on a wired mesh, and to apply these pressures to a mesh composed of wired hulls or d-elements. This test has an analytical solution: it is a cylinder subjected to pressure that varies linearly according to its axis. Three modellings are proposed: - Modelization A: The cylinder is meshed in elements DKT / POU_D_E; - Modelization B: The cylinder is meshed in elements COQUE_3D / POU_D_E; - Modelization C: The cylinder is meshed in elements COQUE_3D / TUYAU_3M / POU_D_T. The results differ from reference solution only because of the lack of refinement of the mesh hulls (especially for Modelling A). This test therefore validates the LIRE_PLEXUS command. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry X axis cylinder, L length, R medium radius, e thickness. v1.01.115 ZZZZ115 - Validation of the CALC_COUPURE command v1.01.115 ZZZZ115 - Validation of the CALC_COUPURE command Summary: This test case is used to validate the CALC_COUPURE command. For more information see U4.81.24 > Contents 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry and mesh A rectangular plate is considered at the L=12 m and H=3 m height. L-thickness is B=0.3 m. The mesh is set, each element is square on the 0.3 m side. The geometry in the Figure is tested, but also the same geometry that has rotated 150°. Figure 1.1-1: Géométrie et maillage de la plaque testée. 1.2 Cuts made Three cuts are made: - The first at the clamped support level and is expressed in the global benchmark. - The second at 3m to the right of the boundary condition and is expressed in the global marker. - The third is identical to the first but is expressed in the local reference as described in the figure above. The torsos are evaluated at the middle of the cut. 1.3 Material properties The plate is made of concrete, characterised by the following elastic properties: - Young's modulus: 30 GPA - Poisson's ratio: 0,2 The calculation is linear elastic. 1.4 modellings CALC_COUPURE applies to plate elements. Modelling of type DKT (modelization A) and type DST (modelization B) will be used. 1.5 Boundary conditions and loads The plate is loaded statically or dynamically (spectral method) according to the model. 1.5.1 Static loadings The plate is clamped on the left side. Two loads are tested: - CH1 : shear on the right side of the plate and normal force. Both are applied as forces distributed on the right side of the plate. - CH2 : Off-plane shear applied as a load distributed on the right side of the plate. The forces applied are: - {F}_{X}=100\mathit{kN} - {F}_{Y}=6000\mathit{kN} - {F}_{Z}=600\mathit{kN} 1.5.2 Dynamic loadings The plate is in simple support on the left and right sides. A constant response spectrum is provided with reduced frequency and damping. The acceleration spectrum is 5000 mm/s in the x direction. 1.6 Quantities and reference results The quantities extracted by the CALC_COUPURE command is tested for the 3 cuts performed. The tests are analytical. 1.6.1 Static loadings If the plate is represented as an clamped beam at its end, it is simple to calculate the internal forces in the static case. The results shall be looked at at the d distance from the clamped support, for a cut parallel to the right and left sides. In the case where the torso is expressed in the global marker, the analytical results shall be: CH 1: - {R}_{1}=0 - {R}_{2}={F}_{Y} - {R}_{3}={F}_{Z} - {M}_{1}={F}_{Z}(L-d) - {M}_{2}={M}_{3}=0 CH 2 : - {R}_{1}={F}_{X} - {R}_{2}={R}_{3}={M}_{1}={M}_{2}={M}_{3}=0 In the local benchmark, the results are: CH 1: - {R}_{1}={F}_{Y} - {R}_{2}={F}_{Z} - {R}_{3}=0 - {M}_{1}={M}_{2}=0 - {M}_{3}={F}_{Z}(L-d) CH 2 : - {R}_{3}={F}_{X} - {R}_{1}={R}_{2}={M}_{1}={M}_{2}={M}_{3}=0 1.6.2 Dynamic loadings The acceleration response spectrum refers to an earthquake in the X direction, normal at the plate plane, which is therefore required to flex and shear out of the plane. The objective of the tests carried out is to check the proper functioning of the modal combinations. Several configurations are studied: - Calculation of the torso associated with the modal contribution of the first mode, - Calculation of the torso taking into account the contribution of the first 2 modes (combination CQC). - Signature of the contribution of the first modal on unit acceleration. - Calculation of the quadratic combination of the contribution of the 3 earthquake directions, - Calculation of Newmark combinations related to the 3 earthquake directions. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Type of finite element Elements DKT will be used for this modelling. 2.2 Boundary conditions and loading The static loads are those described in paragraph 1.5.1. 2.3 Quantities and reference results The analytical results are checked with an accuracy of less than {10}^{-5} , except for certain theoretically zero moments for which a tolerance of 1N.m, corresponding to a lever arm shift of less than 1mm is accepted. 3 Modelling B 3.1 Type of finite element Elements DST will be used for this modelling. The geometry is the same as model A but has been rotated by 150°. 3.2 Boundary conditions and loading The static loads are those described in § 1.5.1 , after 150° rotation. 3.3 Quantities and reference results The analytical results are checked with an accuracy of less than {10}^{-5} , except for certain theoretically zero moments for which a tolerance of 1N.m, corresponding to a lever arm shift of less than 1mm is accepted. 4 Modelling C 4.1 Type of finite element Elements DKT will be used for this modelling. 4.2 Boundary conditions and loading The seismic loads with response spectrum are those described in § 1.5.2. 4.3 Quantities and reference results The analytical results are verified with an accuracy less than the {10}^{-2} . 5 References 1. R.W. Clough, J. Penzien, Dynamics of Structures , CBS Publishers and Distributors, second edition, 2015

v1.01.121 ZZZZ121 - mesh adaptation with HOMARD v1.01.121 ZZZZ121 - mesh adaptation with HOMARD Summary This series of validated computer-based case-tests of mesh adaptation with HOMARD. On a single mesh, either in 2D or 3D, a static mechanics or thermal calculation is launched, with the production of an error indicator. From there, a call to the HOMARD software will result in a modification of the mesh. On this new mesh, a new calculation is activated, corresponding to the same physical problem. These test cases are not examples of the relevance of mesh adaptation and have no physical significance. They are only used as non-regression tests of functionality in the various possible configurations. 1 General 1.1 Background The objective is only to test the non-regression of future evolutions of Code_Aster and HOMARD. Even if the test cases are realistic of the physical point to represent real studies, it is not necessary to attach importance to the value of the results. In particular, there is no need to infer from this the performance of the mesh error/adaptation indicator torque. These test cases validate the operation of the two MACR_INFO_MAIL and MACR_ADAP_MAIL macro-commands that drive the entire process. Specifically, the functions tested are: - mesh and MED format fields and readings. These are IMPR_RESU, LIRE_CHAMP and LIRE_MAILLAGE commands with keyword MED as format, - writing the data file for HOMARD, - start the HOMARD execution procedure. This is the EXEC_LOGICIEL command; it calls a script with a variable number of arguments, - control of the entire process by the python: macr_adap_mail_ops.py. The process is a priori insensitive to the Modelling envisaged. The important points that cause different processing in the data exchange between HOMARD and Code_Aster are the types d-elements, the adaptation control and the updating of fields on the new mesh. We thus envisage 4 modellings which are distributed as follows: | Modelling | Dimension | Update of fields | | --- | --- | --- | | A | 2D, triangles | No | | C | 2D, triangles | Yes | | D | 2D, quadrangles | Yes | | E | 3D, hexahedrons | Yes | | F | 3D, pentahedrons | No | The non-regression is tested on the value of the displacement, stress or temperature field in a free node. The test takes place for several resolutions, those with meshes from the first and at least another adaptation. Indeed, the data transmissions and the control of HOMARD are not the same for the first adaptation and the following ones. Therefore, we must test at least two passages. 1.2 Material Two separate materials are used to ensure that the subdomains are well reconstituted after the mesh has been adapted. | Material 1 | E=180000\mathit{Pa} | | --- | --- | | | \nu =0,3\mathit{S.I.} | | | \alpha =1,5{10}^{-5}\mathit{S.I.} | | | \rho =7700{\mathit{kg.m}}^{-3} | | | \lambda =400{\mathit{W.K}}^{-1}.{m}^{-1} | | | \rho {C}_{p}=1.\mathit{S.I.} | | Material 2 | E=220\mathrm{000Pa} | | --- | --- | | | \nu =0,33\mathit{S.I.} | | | \alpha =1,6{10}^{-5}\mathit{S.I.} | | | \rho =8300{\mathit{kg.m}}^{-3} | | | \lambda =600{\mathit{W.K}}^{-1}.{m}^{-1} | | | \rho {C}_{p}=1.\mathit{S.I.} | In each case of modellings A and C, material 1 is assigned to half 1 and material 2 is assigned to half 2. It is not necessary to provide traction curves, as the test does not make elements calculation finished. quantities such as temperature and energy restitution rates are directly extracted from tables. v1.01.135 ZZZZ135 - Computer validation of SRM methods in CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command v1.01.135 ZZZZ135 - Computer validation of SRM methods in CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the computer features of the CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command. In this test case the stability of a dam in embankment with water infiltration is studied. This test is a non-regression test to validate the use of the macro-command, and therefore has no physical meaning or scientific reference solution. There are 2 modellings available for this test case: - Model A : Calculation of the upstream slope safety factor with Mohr-Coulomb law. This Modelling validates the following features: - Using command variables in the input cam_mater. - Checking the constitutive law in the SRM area. - The use of Mohr-Coulomb law in SRM algorithm. - The GROUP_MA keyword for defining the SRM area by independent mesh cells groups. - The CHAM_DEFO key word for the glide surface. - The keyword METHODE = 'EXPONENTIELLE' - Model B : Calculation of the safety factor of the entire model with Drucker-Prager law. This Modelling validates the following features: - The use of Drucker-Prager law in SRM algorithm. - Le keyword METHODE = 'LINEAIRE' - Le keyword TOUT = 'OUI' 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry and mesh Geometry and mesh of the dam in embankment A dam in embankment with clay core, composed of the foundation, is considered to be a dam in embankment with clay core, of the gravel between the foundation and the body of the dam, a clay core characterized by a relatively low permeability coefficient, and fills upstream and downstream. The mesh is shown in fig1-geom-mail, where the different components of the dam are represented by different colors. 1.2 Material properties Table 1 : Ownership of Dam Materials | | Foundation | Gravier | Nome | Recharge | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Density \rho (kg/m3) | 2250 | 2450 | 1900 | 2450 | | Young's modulus E (MPa) | 250 | 250 | 250 | 250 | | Poisson's ratio \nu | 0.3 | 0.3 | 0.3 | 0.3 | | Permeability k (cm/s) | 1e-5 | 1e-3 | 2e-6 | 1e-3 | | Cohesion Force c (kPa) | 40 | 40 | 44.5 | 40 | | Friction angle \varphi (deg) | 35 | 20 | 23.3 | 20 | The mechanical and hydraulic properties of the model materials are presented in Table 1. For Mohr-Coulomb law, the hypothesis of the associated plastic flow law is made. The parameters of the Drucker-Prager Act were obtained by the following formulae: A=\frac{2\sin(\varphi )}{3-\sin(\varphi )},{\sigma}_{y}=\frac{6c\cos(\varphi )}{3-\sin(\varphi )} where the cohesion force and friction angle take the values in Table 1. The dilatance angle is equal to the friction angle in the Drucker-Prager law. To simplify the calculation, the ultimate cumulative plastic deformation {p}_{\mathit{ultm}} is considered null (= 0). The porosity is uniform in the model and equals 0.672. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The boundary conditions applied to the model are as follows: - Bottom of the clamped foundation, and the vertical sides normally blocked. - Hydraulic pressure from the upstream side of 77.19m (peak elevation = 94.2m). - Hydraulic pressure defined from the level of the downstream table, which is 43m. The dam is modeled in D_PLAN_HS for hydraulic calculation and D_PLAN for stability analysis. To test the constitutive law verification in the SRM area, the elastic behavioral relationship on downstream charging. This demonstrates the possibility of assigning other behavioral relationships Mohr-Coulomb and Drucker-Prager outside the SRM zone. The law of exponential variation of the increment of safety factor is used, with INCR_INIT = 0,04 and RESI_MAXI = 0,02 , or 1 refinement in total before the convergence of the algorithm. The sliding surface is visualized via the evol_noli concept produced. 2.2 Tested quantities and results The safety factor and the maximum total displacement at each SRM iteration shall be tested. v1.01.146 ZZZZ146 - Computer validation of LEM methods in CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command v1.01.146 ZZZZ146 - Computer validation of LEM methods in CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the computer functions of stability analysis of the gradients by methods based on the equilibrium limit theory (LEM) of the macro-command CALC_STAB_PENTE. In this test case the stability of a homogeneous slope is analysed considering Water infiltration into the soil. This test case has no physical sense or solution Scientific reference. - Model A : Calculation of the safety factor according to the Drucker-Prager criterion using Bishop method. This Modelling validates the following features: - Calculation of the safety factor by the simplified Bishop method. - Recovery of shear strength properties from the constitutive law Drucker-Prager. - Adaptation of the mesh with circular fracture surfaces. - Consideration of water infiltration into the structure. - Optimization algorithm for circular surfaces with limited radius terminals. - Model B : Calculation of the safety factor according to Mohr-Coulomb criterion by method Morgenstern-Price. This Modelling validates the following features: - Calculation of safety factor by Morgenstern-Price method. - Recovery of shear strength properties from the constitutive law Mohr-Coulomb. - Adaptation of mesh with non-circular fracture surfaces. - Consideration of water infiltration into the structure. - Optimization algorithm EFWA. - Resumption of the EFWA calculation by defining the initial state. - Model C : Calculation of the safety factor according to the Druck-Prager criterion by the Fellenius method. This Modelling is identical with Modelling A apart from the method of calculating the FS. - Modelling D : Calculation of safety factor according to Mohr-Coulomb by the Spencer method. This Modelling is identical with Modelling B apart from the method of calculating the MSDS. - Modelling E : Definition of the pore pressure field by COEF_RU . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry and mesh Geometry and mesh of the homogeneous slope A slope (slope 1:2) consisting of the homogeneous material of height 4.5m is considered. The model is 18m wide and 6.5m high. The right side is defined as the upstream surface in contact with water (river or water reservoir), and slope as the surface swallows. The mesh is shown in fig1-geom-mail. This is the same model used in the test case ssnp006 (V6.03.006) but with a rough mesh to speed up the calculation. 1.2 Material properties The same material properties are adopted as the test case ssnp006, i.e.: - Unit mass of soil: {\gamma}_{\mathit{sol}}=16\mathit{kN} - Ground friction angle: \varphi =20deg - Soil Cohesion: c=5\mathit{kN}/{m}^{2} - Soil permeability: k=1e-7m/s - Biot coefficient: b=1.0 For Mohr_Coulomb law, the associated plastic flow law is assumed. The parameters of the Drucker-Prager Act were obtained by the following formulae: A=\dfrac{2\sin(\varphi )}{3-\sin(\varphi )},{\sigma}_{y}=\dfrac{6c\cos(\varphi )}{3-\sin(\varphi )} - The dilatance angle is equal to the friction angle in the Drucker-Prager law. In order to simplify the calculation, the cumulative plastic deformation ultimate {p}_{\mathit{ultm}} is considered to be null (= 0). - The porosity is uniform in the model and equals 0.62. 1.3 boundary conditions The hydraulic boundary conditions applied to the model are as follows: - The bottom of the model is waterproof. - Hydraulic pressure from the upstream side of 4m (peak elevation = 6.5m). - Hydraulic pressure defined from the level of the downstream table, which is 2m. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Modelling characteristics The slope stability factor is calculated according to the Druck-Prager criterion. taking into account water infiltration into the soil. Before analysing the stability, the calculation of the pore pressure field (PRE1) is therefore performed. using D_PLAN_HS model. The boundary conditions hydraulics are used in PRE1 This will result in a reasonable line of water in spite of the positive pore pressure above the water line. Indeed, it generates underpressure below the slices of earth that reduces the force This makes the slope less stable than the state without infiltration. The pore pressure field is introduced via keyword CHAM_PRES of the CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command. In this model, the fracture surface is assumed to be circular and the analyses stability by the Simplified Bishop method ( METHODE_LEM ='BISHOP' ). The preliminary study showed that the area of search for the fracture surface was reduced to setting X1_MINI = X1_MAXI = 3,0 and X2_MINI = X2_MAXI = 13,2 . In order to speed up the calculation, manually control the ray search strip by putting Y_MINI = 1,2 et Y_MAXI = 1,6 . The boundary order of the tangential line being less than the order of the slope foot, ensure that the supposed fracture surfaces are kinematically permissible. 2.2 Tested quantities and results In the evol_noli object at macro-command output the value of the slide indicator is tested (DX field DEPL_NOEU) on the node N391 near the breaking surface and located in the part The result is shown in Table 1. v1.01.147 ZZZZ147 – Validation of POST_COMBINAISON operation on simple geometry v1.01.147 ZZZZ147 – Validation of POST_COMBINAISON operation on simple geometry Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate the correct functioning of POST_COMBINAISON on a simple geometry incorporating different types of d-element. It validates a correction to the management of the lagranges. 1 Presentation of the test case 1.1 Geometry The geometry, realized under CIVIL_MASTER, is on 3 levels. It consists of 6 sails, 3 floors, 4 columns and an opening located in a sail. It is illustrated by the following figure: Figure 1.1-1: Géométrie 1.2 Mesh The mesh is as follows: Figure 1.2-1: Maillage 1.3 Material & Geometric Properties Concrete material is applied to the whole structure. - The Young E=30000\mathit{MPa} module - Le Poisson's ratio \nu =0,2 The thicknesses of the sails and floors are 200\mathit{mm} and the beams have a square cross section on the side 200\mathit{mm} . 1.4 Loading The load is: - The base is clamped. - The weight is applied throughout the structure, - F=-10\mathit{kN}/m\mathrm{²} over-fact pressure is applied to the roof of the structure and to a lower sail (Fig 1). Two load cases are defined and correspond respectively to Weight (Cas G) and Pressure (Cas Q). Then POST_COMBINAISON is used to sum up the loads. 1.5 Validation The node displacement of the intermediate floor is extracted following the calculations of the load cases and then POST_COMBINAISON by ensuring that the sum of the load cases (Case G : \mathit{DZ}=-0,0107m , Case Q \mathit{DZ}=-0,0153m ) is the displacement from POST_COMBINAISON \mathit{DZ}=-0,026m . This documentation is deliberately succinct.

This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.151 ZZZZ151 – Validating the EXEC_LOGICIEL Operator when calling mesh Tools v1.01.151 ZZZZ151 – Validating the EXEC_LOGICIEL Operator when calling mesh Tools Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate calls to system base commands and to the various tools of mesh (gmsh, salome, gibi) from EXEC_LOGICIEL macro-command: - call to the basic commands unixlset pwdfrom the command file, - construction of an mesh in 'GMSH' format by using the gmsh tool, - construction of mesh in 'MED' format by call to salome, - construction of mesh in 'GIBI' format by using the gibi tool. v1.01.154 ZZZZ154 – Verification of composite types v1.01.154 ZZZZ154 – Verification of composite types Summary It is a purely computer-based test of the so-called "composites" data structures. 1 Reference problem Not applicable. 2 reference solution This is a functioning test.
