v1.01.155 ZZZZ155 – mesh cutting machine verification v1.01.155 ZZZZ155 – mesh cutting machine verification Summary It is a purely computer test of the mesh cutter. 1 Reference problem Not applicable. 2 reference solution This is a functioning test. There is no uncertainty about the expected behavior. 3 Modelling A In this Modelling, the basic operation of the cutter and the CommGraph and ObjectBalancer objects is checked. The meshes checked and cut are checked from mesh purely sequential (Mesh) or from IncompleteMesh. The call to PtScoch is also checked from the python space and the cut into broken commands. The parallel connections of the meshes produced are checked. 4 Modelling B This Modelling tests the same as A but on one of the larger grids. 5 Modelling C This Modelling testes the re-reading and cutting of meshes and fields from MED files in relation to a reference that corresponds to the MED file medump. The nodes and elements fields are tested using the python splitMeshAndFieldsFromMedFile function. 6 Modelling D This Modelling tests the cutting and rereading of meshes and fields by producing a Result (ie: NonLinearResult) with splitMedFileToResults. It also demonstrates the possibilities offered by the python interface to an med file in terms of creating fields with changing type or component names. Comparison of results is made with a pre-cut and re-read file by LIRE_RESU. 7 Modelling E This Modelling tests the proper functioning of the partitioner and the following calculation in the presence of local communicators. 8 Modelling F This Modelling testes the creation and existence of mesh cells and nodes groups after partitioning mesh. 9 Modelling G This Modelling tests the serialization of the MedField object. 10 Modelling H This Modelling tests the rebalancing of the result sd load (Object MeshBalancer). This Modelling checks consistency by reconstructing the sequential fields and comparing them to the starting field. 11 Modelling I This Modelling tests partitioning with ParMetis. 12 Modelling J This Modelling tests the order of med file rereading type of mesh cells by type of mesh cells. 13 Modelling K This Modelling tests the partitioning of mesh with mesh cells ghost layers with a number of more than 1 over 2 processors. MECA_STATIQUE calculation is performed and its results are verified. 14 Modelling L This Modelling tests the partitioning of mesh with mesh cells ghost layers with a number of more than 1 over 4 processors. A 3D MECA_STATIQUE calculation is performed and its results are verified. 15 Modelling M This Modelling tests convergence and residue calculation in a parallel calculation on 4 processors. A 3D STAT_NON_LINE calculation is performed and its results are verified.

v1.01.161 ZZZZ161 - MED format exchange, computer control v1.01.161 ZZZZ161 - MED format exchange, computer control Summary: This test case controls the MED format field writings and their ASTER rereading. It validates in particular the writing of undefined fields on the full domain or defined on several types of d的elements. It also controls the exchange of quantity fields. It should be noted that mechanical calculation is only a pretext and has no ambition of validation per se. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The domain is a 10\times 20 size rectangle, separated into 4 slices of 10\times 5 . 3 points are associated with this rectangle: M , N and O . OPPOSE J 11 O D C B A 6 N 1 M ORIGINE I 22 17 12 7 2 0 1.2 Material properties Two materials are used: The material 1 has the following characteristics: E=180000{\mathit{N.m}}^{-2} \nu =0,3 \alpha =1,5{10}^{-7} \rho =7700{\mathit{kg.m}}^{-3} It is applied in A and B slices. The second material has the following characteristics: E=220000{\mathit{N.m}}^{-2} \nu =0,3 \alpha =1,6{10}^{-7} \rho =8300{\mathit{kg.m}}^{-3} It is applied in C and D slices. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads At point \mathit{ORIGINE} , the displacement is zero according to y . On the whole left edge, i.e. between the \mathit{ORIGINE} and J points, normal displacement is zero. On the upper edge, i.e. between the J and \mathit{OPPOSE} points, the pressure is imposed on 1000 . 1.4 Initial conditions Not applicable. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solutions The calculation is in static mechanics. It is only a pretext to provide a result. 2.2 Baseline At node \mathit{OPPOSE} , the displacement has the following values: {u}_{x}=0,4183044 2.3 Uncertainty about solutions Not applicable. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The calculation is made of two-dimensional static mechanics, in flat deformation. 3.2 Mesh characteristics A and B slices are gridded with 8 TRIA3 triangles. They form the mesh-cell group named 'TRIA'. C and D slices are gridded with 4 QUAD4 quadrangles. They form the mesh-cell group named 'QUAD'. The 4 triangles of the B slice and the 2 quadrangles of the C slice are assembled in the 'MILIEU' group. The external border segments are gridded with 12 SEG2 segments. They are grouped into 4 groups called \text{BORD\_INF} , \text{BORD\_DRO} , \text{BORD\_SUP} and \text{BORD\_GAU} . 'J' 'OPPOSE' 11 'O' 6 'N' 1 'M' 'ORIGINE' 'I' 22 17 12 7 2 0 3.3 Tested Features This case tests the different options of writing in 'MED' format via the IMPR_RESU command. To do this we calculate various additional options of the single displacement and create a field of quantity equivalent to the field of moving to nodes. The impressions are successively these: - the nodes displacement field and the Gauss point stress field, expressed throughout the mesh. This triggers the creation of a profile for displacement because it is not defined everywhere: the three nodes M , N and O do not have any value, - quantity field. It uses the same profile as the displacement field of the standard result, - 'SIXY' and 'SIYY' components of the nodes stress field by element 'SIGM_ELNO', - l , error indicator 'ERRE_ELGA_NORE' on mesh cells group \mathit{MILIEU} . This triggers the creation of two profiles because the values written are not on all mesh cells. The first profile concerns the 4 triangles out of the 8 of the total; the second one concerns the 2 quadrangles out of the 4 of the total. The rereading from the 'MED' format is that of the nodes field in the quantity field. 4 Modelling results A Comparison is made on the node 'OPPOSE' displacement value with a relative {10}^{-4}\text{\%} tolerance. | Identification | Value | difference relative in % | | --- | --- | --- | | {u}_{x} | 0,4183044 | 1,55 10–7 | | {u}_{y} | –1,639849 | 2,71 10–5 | 5 Summary of the results No specific comments are to be made on this test case. v1.01.164 ZZZZ164 - Validation of keywords DEFORME, TRANSLATION, ROTATION, MODI_BASE and ECHELLE of the MODI_MAILLAGE command v1.01.164 ZZZZ164 - Validation of keywords DEFORME, TRANSLATION, ROTATION, MODI_BASE and ECHELLE of the MODI_MAILLAGE command Summary: This test validates TRANSLATION, ROTATION, MODI_BASE and ECHELLE keywords. To this end, two key words are required to be combined, one 3D and the other 2D. The first one consists of a translation, two rotations, and a scale-up. The two possibilities of definition of the rotation axis are tested: either by two points or by an point and the direction. The second one will combine a basic change and a scale-up. Thus, all cases of figures allowed by these key words will be tested. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The problem is 3D, it is a parallelepiped rectangle: We'll be working this volume with a massive element HEXA8. A 2D Modelling is derived, meshed with a solid element QUAD4: 1.2 Material properties There's no reason to be here. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Not defined. 1.4 Initial conditions Not defined. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference solution is an analytical. M(x,y,z) is a space point, and is required to have T translation of the (\mathit{tx},\mathit{ty},\mathit{tz}) vector, and R rotation of \alpha angle (in radians) with P(\mathit{px},\mathit{py},\mathit{pz}) axis and D(\mathit{dx},\mathit{dy},\mathit{dz}) direction. Then M becomes {M}_{T} after translation: {M}_{T}(x+\mathit{tx},y+\mathit{ty},z+\mathit{tz}) . {M}_{T} becomes {M}_{\mathit{TR}} after rotation: {M}_{\mathit{TR}}=P+\cos\alpha \cdot P{M}_{T}+(1-\cos\alpha )\cdot ({\mathit{PM}}_{T}\cdot D)\cdot D+\sin\alpha \cdot (D\mathrm{\wedge }{\mathit{PM}}_{T}) with {M}_{T}=M+T The scale of a factor of the Ech, gives: {M}_{\mathit{TRE}}=\mathit{ech}\cdot {M}_{\mathit{TR}} The basic change functionality is expected to be inputted by the user of two orthogonal vectors in 3D (one vector in 2D). This data is supplemented to generate a direct orthogonal database, in 3D or 2D. Tests are carried out to verify whether the input data will allow the definition of a direct orthogonal base. A normalization of the vectors of the database is then carried out. In 3D, we therefore expect the data of U and V , the first two vectors of the new database: W(x,y,z)=U(x,y,z)\mathrm{\wedge }V(x,y,z) \mathrm{\Rightarrow }B=(U,V,W) : matrix formed by the basic vectors M(U,V,W)={B}^{T}M(x,y,z) In 2D, the second vector of the base is generated by a 90° rotation of the vector entered by the user. This basic change can be combined with scaling and translation, for example. Programming of these transformations is done differently in 3D and 2D, in order to optimize each of these two cases. 2.2 Quantities and reference results We will control the new coordinates of point \mathit{P1} , \mathit{P7} and \mathit{P8} in 3D ( \mathit{P1} , \mathit{P3} and \mathit{P4} in 2D). 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution Uncertainties arise from the numerical accuracy in Code_Aster (platform dependence) and in the calculation of the analytical solution reference. v1.01.175 ZZZZ175 - Aster-Homard pairing on a STAT_NON_LINE calculation v1.01.175 ZZZZ175 - Aster-Homard pairing on a STAT_NON_LINE calculation Summary: This series of validated computer case-tests of mesh adaptation with HOMARD with STAT_NON_LINE use. On a single mesh, either in 2D or 3D, a nonlinear mechanical calculation is launched, with the production of an error indicator. From there, a call to HOMARD software will result in a modification of the mesh. On this new mesh, a new calculation is activated, corresponding to the same physical problem. These test cases are not examples of the relevance of mesh adaptation and have no physical significance. They are only used as non-regression tests of functionality in the various possible configurations. 1 General 1.1 Background The objective is only to test the non-regression of future evolutions of Code_Aster and HOMARD. Even if the test cases are realistic of the physical point to represent real studies, it is not necessary to attach importance to the value of the results. In particular, there is no need to infer from this the performance of the mesh error/adaptation indicator torque. These test cases validate the operation of the two MACR_INFO_MAIL and MACR_ADAP_MAIL macro-commands that drive the entire process. Specifically, the functions tested are: - mesh and MED format fields and readings. These are IMPR_RESU, LIRE_CHAMP and LIRE_MAILLAGE commands with keyword MED as format, - writing the data file for HOMARD, - start the HOMARD execution procedure. This is the EXEC_LOGICIEL command; it calls a script with a variable number of arguments, - control of the entire process by the python: macr_adap_mail_ops.py. The process is a priori insensitive to the Modelling envisaged. The important points that cause different processing in the data exchange between HOMARD and Code_Aster are the d-types, the adaptation control and the updating of fields on the new mesh. The non-regression is tested on the value of the displacement, stress or temperature field in a free node. The test takes place for several resolutions, those with meshes from the first and at least another adaptation. Indeed, the data transmissions and the control of HOMARD are not the same for the first adaptation and the following ones. Therefore, we must test at least two passages. 1.2 Calculation method used for reference solution These test cases are non-regression test cases. The reference solution is the one obtained with a Code_Aster calculation. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Geometry 2.2 Material properties Material with elasto-plastic behavior with linear nutring: Elasticity: - E=2.1x{10}^{5}\mathrm{Pa} Young's modulus - \nu =0.3 Poisson's ratio Plasticity: - Tensile curve pent in plastic \frac{\partial \sigma }{\partial \varepsilon }=2.\times {10}^{\mathrm{3 }}\mathrm{Pa} - Elastic limit {\sigma}_{e}=235.\mathrm{Pa} 2.3 Boundary conditions and loads The calculation is in nonlinear mechanics. The part is clamped on its left side. Pressure is exerted on the lower horizontal part of the second hole (zone \mathrm{PRES1} on the sketch). This pressure varies over time. The evolution of the displacement will be looked at on a node of the base. Border ENCASTR : blocking of movements by blocking degrees of freedom: DX = DY = 0. v1.01.185 ZZZZ185 - Validation of MODI_MAILLAGE command associated with SYMETRIE and PROJ_CHAMP command associated with DISTANCE_MAX v1.01.185 ZZZZ185 - Validation of MODI_MAILLAGE command associated with SYMETRIE and PROJ_CHAMP command associated with DISTANCE_MAX Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate the MODI_MAILLAGE command with the SYMETRIE keyword and the PROJ_CHAMP command with the DISTANCE_MAX keyword. - MODI_MAILLAGE command, with the keyword SYMETRIE allows you to take the symmetrical of a mesh \mathrm{2D} or \mathrm{3D} , - PROJ_CHAMP command with the DISTANCE_MAX keyword allows you not to project the field to nodes that does not meet the following 2 criteria: 1. nodes is not in a element of the 1st mesh, 2. nodes is beyond DISTANCE_MAX. The test case consists of: - a thermal study on 1/8th structure, - the construction of the thermal field on 1/4 of structure by projection of the results obtained on the 1/8th structure, with the consideration of a plane of symmetry, - 1/4 thermal study of structure, - comparison of the temperature field obtained by projection and a 1/4 structural study. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure is obtained by rotation around the Z axis, from the section shown in [Figure]. Figure 1.1-a: Coupe de la structure 1.2 Material properties The study is carried out in linear thermal, only thermal characteristics are necessary for the definition of materials. Isotropic thermal conductivity: \lambda =15.0W/\mathrm{m.k} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The study is performed in linear thermal, the conditions on the imposed temperatures are represented in [Figure], the flow conditions and the thermal exchange are shown in [Figure]. Figure 1.3-a: Vue de dessus, avec les conditions en température imposée. Figure 1.3-b: Vue en coupe, avec les conditions de flux et les échanges thermiques. Flow conditions: {\phi }_{1}=10.0W/{m}^{2} {\phi }_{2}=0.0W/{m}^{2} {\phi }_{3}=30.0W/{m}^{2} Convection exchange conditions: {h}_{1}=350.0W/{m}^{2}k {\mathrm{tf}}_{1}=300.0°C {h}_{2}=400.0W/{m}^{2}k {\mathrm{tf}}_{2}=275.0°C {h}_{3}=600.0W/{m}^{2}k {\mathrm{tf}}_{3}=310.0°C Temperature conditions imposed: {\mathrm{Temp}}_{1}=250.0°C {\mathrm{Temp}}_{2}=160.0°C 1.4 Initial conditions Not applicable. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation For this test case, 2 studies are carried out. - The first study is carried out on 1/8th of the structure. The calculation is a linear thermal analysis, with the boundary conditions described in [§1.2]. - The second study is carried out on 1/4 of structure. The calculation is a linear thermal analysis, with the boundary conditions described in [§1.2]. Figure 2.1-a: Maillage de 1/8ème de structure. 2.2 Quantities and reference results The reference result is the temperature field. The results of the 1/8th structure study and its mesh are saved in a file in the format [Figure] gives the temperature field obtained on 1/8th of the structure. Figure 2.2-a: Champ de température calculé sur 1/8ème de la structure. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution No meaning in this case. The purpose of the test case is to verify that the mesh symmetry and temperature field projections are correctly made. 2.4 Bibliographical references No use. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The purpose of this Modelling is to obtain the solution to the thermal problem from the calculation performed on 1/8th of the structure. The test case is as follows: - mesh, 1/8th structure, from file in - reading the temperature field from the file in 的MED - create a result from the previously read field, command CREA_RESU. - creating a model from the previously read mesh, command AFFE_MODELE. - creating a model for mesh cells groups that belong to the symmetry plane, command AFFE_MODELE (see note #1). - mesh read, 1/8th structure, from the file in 的MED-format and mesh change by symmetry to the plane ( {\pi}_{\mathrm{sym}} ) defined by: - AXE_1= (\mathrm{1.0,}1.0,0.0) , AXE_2= (0.0,0.0,-1.0) , POINT= (0.0,0.0,0.0) LIRE_MAILLAGE and MODI_MAILLAGE commands. - reading the temperature field from the file in 的MED - create a result from the previously read field, command CREA_RESU. - creating a model from the symmetrical mesh, AFFE_MODELE command. - read mesh representing 1/4 of the structure, command LIRE_MAILLAGE. - creating a model from the previously read mesh, command AFFE_MODELE. - projection of the 3 results created from the solution calculated on 1/8th of structure, command PROJ_CHAMP with the keyword DISTANCE_MAX. - Extracting the temperature fields from the 3 results from the projection, CREA_CHAMP command. - creating a zero field on the model built on 1/4 of the structure, command CREA_CHAMP (see note #2). - combination of all fields, command CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION= - create a result from the field combination, CREA_RESU. Note 1: In this test case, nodes of mesh, [Figure ], belong to the symmetry plane {\pi}_{\mathrm{sym}} . For these nodes, the temperature field projection will be counted twice. To avoid cumulating the temperature field too much, one solution is to create a model containing only these nodes and to make the projection on the complete mesh. This projected field will then be subtracted using the command CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION=WASSE. Note No. 2: The projection of fields using the command PROJ_CHAMP and the keyword DISTANCE_MAX allows you to avoid creating a field on the nodes that is not contained in one of the elements's original mesh and that is at a distance greater than DISTANCE_MAX from the nearest element. When you combine fields using the command CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION=的ASSE, it is the first field to be taken as a reference. If the field is incomplete, as in our case, the combination will not give the desired result. The solution is therefore to create a null field over the entire model and use it as a reference field. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The temperature field projection calculated on 1/8th structure (mesh of [Figure1.1-a]) is projected on the model constructed from the mesh of the 1/4 structure [Figure3.2-a]). | | | | --- | --- | Figure 3.2-a: Maillage du 1/4 de la structure. 3.3 Tested quantities and results The test is performed on the temperature field. From the result obtained by projection and combination on 1/4 of structure is extracted the temperature field TEMP1. From the result calculated on 1/4 of structure is extracted the 2nd temperature field TEMP2. These 2 fields are subtracted using the command CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='ASSE', and the test is performed on the maximum and minimum value of the resulting field. At all points of the structure, one must have TEMP1=TEMP2, the field resulting from the command CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='ASSE' must be zero at all points. | Values tested | Reference | Code_Aster | Creative decision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Maximum | 0.0 | 2.694E-05 | 1.0E-4 | | Minimum | 0.0 | -1.808E-05 | 1.0E-4 | The [Figure] shows the differences between the two temperature fields obtained during this test case. Figure 3.3-a: Carte des différences de température. 4 Summary of the results This test case validates: - MODI_MAILLAGE command associated with the SYMETRIE keyword, - PROJ_CHAMP command associated with the DISTANCE_MAX keyword. Validation is done on the whole temperature field and not just on a few points. When the 2 commands are associated, it must be taken into account that the fields supported by nodes that belong to the symmetry plane can be counted twice. When combining the fields using the CREA_CHAMP/OPERATION='ASSE' command, it is the structure of the first CHAM_NO that serves as a reference structure. If the structure is incomplete, then you must create a reference CHAM_NO.

v1.01.186 ZZZZ186 - Validation of the IMPR_OAR Operator v1.01.186 ZZZZ186 - Validation of the IMPR_OAR Operator Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate the IMPR_OAR operator. v1.01.189 ZZZZ189 – Circumferential orientation by a Python loop v1.01.189 ZZZZ189 – Circumferential orientation by a Python loop Summary: The case of a concrete hemisphere with orthoradial reinforcements under pressure in linear elasticity is treated. The aim is to circumferentially orient the reinforcements. This operation can be carried out in two ways. In the modellings (A) and (C) , a Python function is offered to perform this action, orienting the mesh cells one by one. In modellings (B) and (D) , AXE command of GRILLE option is used, which allows a much simpler data set of the command file to direct all frames with a single command. The (B) Modelling results are then compared to (A) Modelling, and those of (D) Modelling to (C) Modelling. In modellings (A) and (B) , the reference axis is (0,0,1) . In modellings (C) and (D) , the reference axis is (0,1,0) . The last two modellings have been added in order to have non-zero \beta nautical angle values. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry | Ray | R=10.m | | --- | --- | | Thickness | t=0.04 | Point contact details: | | A | B | C | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | x | | | | | y | | | | | z | | | | 1.2 Material properties The hemisphere is composed of concrete reinforced by grids. Since the objective is only to test controls, the same properties are given to concrete and grids. E=200000\mathit{Pa} , \nu =0.3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Over a quarter of the hemisphere: | Point C | no displacement in z | | --- | --- | | Side \mathrm{AC} | symmetry with xz plane | | Side \mathrm{BC} | symmetry with yz plane | | Side \mathrm{AB} | free | Internal pressure: P=10.\mathit{Pa} 1.4 Policy issues The reinforcement grids are intended to be circumferentially oriented in relation to the given axis. However, given the hemispheric shape considered, a Python function is proposed to achieve it. The principle is: 1. Hemispheric axis is noted Z 2. for each mesh cell, the vector indicating the direction of the V=Z\mathrm{\wedge }N ciconference where N is normal at the mesh cell is calculated. V=[\mathit{Vx},\mathit{Vy},\mathit{Vz}] is noted and its projection on the (\mathit{XOY}) plane is defined by W=[\mathit{Vx},\mathit{Vy},0] 3. calculates the values of ANGL_REP to be assigned to the current mesh cell by \alpha =\arctan(\mathrm{Vy}/\mathrm{Vx}) and \beta =-\arctan(\mathit{Vz}/\mathit{norm}(W)) The function called LIST_CARA_CIRCONF loops on all mesh cells grids, calculates \alpha and \beta and creates the keywords: _F(SECTION=20.0, > Mesh cell=Name_Size_Current, > EXCENTREMENT=0.0, ANGL_REP=(,)), > COEF_RIGI_DRZ=1.E-10 ), and it adds them to a list. This list is then provided to AFFE_CARA_ELEM. So we get the commands: LIST_GRI=LIST_CARA_CIRCONF( > GROUP_MA='GRILLE', > AXE=(0.,0.,1.), > MODELE=MODEL, > GRILLE=_F(SECTION=20.,EXCENTREMENT=0.,) ) CARA_COQ=AFFE_CARA_ELEM( > MODELE=MODEL, > COEF_RIGI_DRZ=0.,), > GRILLE=LIST_GRI, ) Finally, it should be noted that LIST_CARA_CIRCONF formally follows the following catalogue: LIST_CARA_CIRCONF( > GROUP_MA =SIMP(statut='o',typ=grma,max=' '), > AXE =SIMP(statut='o',typ='R',max=3,min=3), > MODE =SIMP(statut='o',typ=model_sdaster), > GRILLE =FACT(statut='f',max=1, > SECTION =SIMP(statut='o',typ='R'), > EXCENTREMENT =SIMP(statut='f',typ='R'), > COEF_RIGI_DRZ =SIMP(statut='f',typ='R'), > ), ) 2 Modelling A 2.1 Modelling characteristics 1373 elements shell DKT 1373 elements grid GRILLE_MEMBRANE Modelling of a quarter of the hemisphere in TRIA3. 2.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes : 734 Number of mesh cells and types : 2746 TRIA3 2.3 Tested quantities and results Non-regression values calculated with \mathit{V7.03.30.} version are tested | Identification | Reference type | Reference values | | --- | --- | --- | | Node 30, \mathit{DX} displacement | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 0 | | Node 30, \mathrm{DY} displacement | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 3.139397E-05 | | Node 30, \mathit{DZ} displacement | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 1.533531E-05 | | Node 700, \mathrm{DX} displacement | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 4.487504E-06 | | Node 700, \mathrm{DY} displacement | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 3.321124E-05 | | Node 700, \mathrm{DZ} displacement | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 1.515258E-05 | 3 Modelling B Modelling B tests AXE functionality of GRILLE option AFFE_CARA_ELEM which allows you to direct the frames directly by Code_Aster. The principle of validation is to do the same nonlinear calculation in two different ways: - STAT_NON_LINE with dualised (regular) loads created via the AFFE_CHAR_MECA(keyword DDL_IMPO) operator, - STAT_NON_LINE with kinematic loads created via the AFFE_CHAR_CINE(keyword MECA_IMPO) operator, For each calculation the calculation resume (wrong) is checked. v1.01.208 ZZZZ208 – Validation of Generalized Terms Extraction and Recovery Methods v1.01.208 ZZZZ208 – Validation of Generalized Terms Extraction and Recovery Methods Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the EXTR_MATR_GENE, EXTR_VECT_GENE, RECU_MATR_GENE and RECU_VECT_GENE methods. General terms are extracted, a change is made in the python environment and a cross-validation is made by comparing the results obtained with the library nullsy and those obtained with the generic commands. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A slender structure of 0.25m length and 0.05m\ast 0.03m section is considered. 1.2 Material properties The material is elastic isotropic with properties of: - Young's modulus E=2.1{10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} - Poisson's ratio \nu =0.3 - Density \rho =7800\mathit{kg}/\mathit{m³} - Hysteretic damping \eta =0.01 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads We place a zero displacement on the y=0.25m abscisse face For the calculation of the harmonic response, a vertical (1+\mathrm{0.5j})/2 amplitude point excitation is applied to the point coordinates (0m,0.1375m,0.03m) . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation Two types of calculation are performed to test the methods for handling generalised quantities. The first Modelling performs a modal calculation and a harmonic response calculation on the generalised quantities. The second model performs a modal calculation using the dynamic substructure technique. 2.2 Quantities and reference results Cross validation is performed by comparing results from standard operators and calculations with the library nully. The obtained eigenfrequencies and the displacement field for the harmonic response calculation shall be checked. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution Regression is considered to occur if the results obtained are not identical. 2.4 Bibliographical references Not applicable 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics A modal calculation and harmonic response calculation is performed on a basis composed of 10 modes. v1.01.215 ZZZZ215 – 3D chaining code_saturne-code_aster v1.01.215 ZZZZ215 – 3D chaining code_saturne-code_aster Summary: This test validates the 3D link code_saturne -code_aster . Different features are affected by this validation: - reading a pressure field in a MED file - creating a data structure EVOL_CHAR result - the spatial projection of one field of one mesh on another - the temporal interpolation of the load induced by fluid pressure from fluid to solid time discretization For example, various types of input fields are used - a pressure field produced by code_saturne - pressure fields artificially created by code_aster 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry of the problem is that of a 200-side cube with faces called \mathit{Face1} , \mathit{Face2} , \mathit{Face3} , \mathit{Face4} , \mathit{Face5} and \mathit{Face6} . 1.2 Material properties It is a linear isotropic elastic material of Young's modulus 1. and Poisson's ratio 0.3 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The cube is clamped on its \mathit{Face1} face while all the others are subject to fluid pressure. 1.4 Initial conditions The initial conditions are blank of any displacement and constraint. 2 reference solution Not applicable. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Here we define 2 pressure fields on the fluid mesh which is associated with 2 moments, 0 and 1 . Then we assemble them in a data structure of type loading. To apply this load to the solid mesh, the loading data structure is projected on the solid mesh. The solid calculation is performed at 0.2 , 0.4 , 0.6 , 0.8 and 1 moments which validates the time interpolation of the load. 3.2 Mesh characteristics Not important 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics A pressure field is defined on the time- and space-dependent fluid mesh depending on the 1.E-4\times \mathit{INST}\times (X+Y+Z) function. It is then associated with the 0 , 1 moment list in a load-type data structure. To apply this load to the solid mesh, the loading data structure is projected on the solid mesh. The solid calculation is performed at 0.2 , 0.4 , 0.6 , 0.8 and 1 moments which validates the time interpolation of the load. 4.2 Mesh characteristics Not important 5 Modelling C 5.1 Modelling characteristics Here we read a true Code_Saturn constant pressure result by element at 0.25 , 0.5 , 0.75 and 1 moments, which is defined as a load-type data structure. To apply this load to the solid mesh, the loading data structure is projected on the solid mesh. The solid calculation is performed at 0.333 , 0.6666 and 0.9999 moments which validates the time interpolation of the load. 5.2 Mesh characteristics Not important 6 Modelling D This test is very close to Modelling B. It allows testing the code coupling in MPI replacing the fluid-mechanical chaining with a low coupling (without pressure dependence on displacement). Note: this test would be close to a coupling to make fluid-strucutre interaction (IFS) if the pressure had a dependence The main reason for this is that the system is not yet fully integrated into the system. 6.1 Modelling characteristics A pressure field on the fluid mesh is defined here depending on time and space depending on the 1.E-4\times \mathit{INST}\times (X+Y+Z) function. This pressure field will be interpolated on the solid mesh to serve as an input load. Solid calculation is performed at 0.2 , 0.4 , 0.6 , 0.8 and 1 moments. 6.2 Mesh characteristics Not important 7 Summary of the results The results are quite the expected results.

v1.01.216 ZZZZ216 – Low 3D coupling code_saturne-code_aster v1.01.216 ZZZZ216 – Low 3D coupling code_saturne-code_aster Summary: This test validates the low 3D coupling code_saturne - code_aster . The aim is to model a mechanical calculation with a following pressure coming from a fluid calculation. Here is what the different modellingss test: - A: purely mechanical reference calculation, - B and C: coupling code_aster - code_aster with interface-compliant meshes on 2 and 4 MPI, - D and E: coupling code_aster - code_aster with non-conform meshes at interface on 2 and 4 MPI, - F: coupling code_saturne - code_aster with interface-compliant meshes on 4 MPI, - G: coupling code_saturne - code_aster with non-conform meshes at the interface on 4 MPI, - I: dynamic code_aster - code_aster coupling with interface-compliant meshes on 2 MPI, - J: dynamic code_aster - code_aster coupling with non-conform meshes at the interface on 2 MPI, - K: dynamic code_saturne - code_aster coupling with interface-compliant meshes on 2 MPI, - L: dynamic code_saturne - code_aster coupling with non-conform meshes at interface on 2 MPI, - M: like F but with nodal projection for forces. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry of the problem is that of a cube on the side 200 whose faces are called \mathit{Face1} , \mathit{Face2} , \mathit{Face3} , \mathit{Face4} , \mathit{Face5} et \mathit{Face6} . 1.2 Material properties It is a linear isotropic elastic material of Young's modulus 1. and Poisson's ratio 0.3 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The cube is clamped on its \mathit{Face1} face while all the others are subject to fluid pressure. The fluid pressure is defined here as a pressure field on the fluid mesh depending on time and space depending on the function 10^{-4} \times \mathrm{INST} \times (X_f+Y_f+Z_f) , where (X_f,Y_f,Z_f) is the coordinate on the distorted configuration. For this purpose, fluid pressure is considered to be a follower. 1.4 Modelling characteristics Solid calculation is performed at 0.2 , 0.4 , 0.6 , 0.8 and 1 moments. For low coupling cases, a relative residue on the displacement increment of 10^{-6} is required to switch to the next time step. 1.5 Initial conditions The initial conditions are blank of any displacement and constraint. 2 reference solution The reference solution is the Modelling A where the calculation is mechanically and without coupling. 3 Summary of the results The results are quite the expected results.

v1.01.218 ZZZZ218 – Validation of the MACR_ECREVISSE command v1.01.218 ZZZZ218 – Validation of the MACR_ECREVISSE command Summary: This test case enables the validation of Code_Aster's chaining with Ecrevisse, done via MACR_ECREVISSE macro-command, to estimate fluid flows (air/water/vapor) that can pass through a crack. Three modellings are proposed, the first and second of which are non-regression. In the first model, a horizontal crack is found in a structure; in the second one has two vertical cracks that interact; in the third one tests the macro-command in relation to a rotation-translation. 1 Reference problem This test is based on the SIMIBE test performed at CEA. Three different modellings are described. The material and flow characteristics are the same for the three modellings, and they are described in section §1. Geometry changes slightly for the three modellings. A geometry diagram for Modelling A is shown in §1.1; for the other modellings the differences will be described. 1.1 Geometry and material The overall geometry is presented on the . The crack characteristics are given at the bottom. Note that the units are expressed in the international system S.I. As also specified in the U7.03.41 user documentation, this is made mandatory by the software Crevisse , which contains formulas that are not adimensionalized. Figure 1.1-a : test case geometry Crack Details: - section: RECTANGLE - flow direction: X , positive - solid roughness of the wall: 0,5{.10}^{-6}m - singular load loss coefficient at input: none (ZETA = 0) - dimension of crack in normal direction at plane ( z ): 0.5m (LIST_VAL_BL = (0.5.0.05) - Remanent opening fixed to 30\mu m Flow: - Stabilizing pressure at inlet: {10.10}^{5}\mathrm{Pa} - Stabilization pressure at outlet: {10}^{5}\mathrm{Pa} - Inlet fluid condition: air alone (FLUIDE_ENTREE = 6) - Inlet temperature: 140°C Model: - SATURATION flow model - friction calculated directly from the absolute roughness of the wall (FROTTEMENT = 1) - heat transfer with a laminar monophase Sieder & Tate correlation and Mac Adams correlation in other regimes. In the case of gas/liquid mixture, calculation either in the gas or in the liquid or via Chen correlation as a function of gas mass titre and vacuum rate (TRANSFERT_CHAL = 1). 1.2 Material properties The values chosen are representative of a concrete. E=35000\mathrm{MPa} \nu =0.25 \alpha =10-5/°C \lambda =2.3J/{m}^{2}s°C/m \rho {C}_{p}=2500000J/{m}^{3}°C 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading The upper and lower parts are clamped. It is assumed that the crack cannot be closed completely. Thus, the standing opening is fixed to 30\mu m to leave a minimum fluid flow not zero. At l-extrados, the temperature is always {T}_{\mathrm{ext}}=20°C and the pressure {P}_{\mathrm{ext}}=1.105\mathrm{Pa} . On the internal and external sides, it is assumed that the exchanges with the ambient medium take place with the following exchange coefficients: {h}_{int}=\mathrm{8W}/{m}^{2} and {h}_{\mathit{ext}}=\mathrm{4W}/{m}^{2} Hot air is injected under pressure either {T}_{int}=140°C and {P}_{int}={10.10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} . 1.4 Initial conditions The concrete is at rest, at 20°C , with a 140\mu m opening crack. 2 reference solution Modellings A and B are non-regression tests. Model C checks the macro-command behavior for an oblique crack, and the macro is robust compared to a rotation-translation. The structure's response to a reference position is compared with that of the same tow and translatate structure. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The MACR_ECREVISSE control behavior is validated in the presence of a horizontal through crack. A flat deformation model for D_PLAN mechanics is chosen, and a thermal model PLAN_DIAG, with a diagonized mass matrix for thermal. Flow characteristics were described with geometry in §1.1. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh used is presented: Figure 3.2-a : mesh complete The dimensions are the same as for geometry. Number of nodes : 1260 Number of mesh cells : 1156 QUAD4 The growth parameters used to achieve the mesh are: from 0.002m (intrados) to 0.05m (extrados), and idem from BFISH and BFISB to ENCASTRE. 3.3 Quantities and results The significant quantities of this calculation is tested: flow rate, displacement and temperature at crack inlet and outlet. Two moments are tested. A t=500s : | Identification | Tolerance | | --- | --- | | Moving \mathit{DY} to node {E}_{\mathit{HD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Material temperature node {E}_{\mathit{HD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | Moving \mathit{DY} to node {I}_{\mathit{HD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Temperature at node {I}_{\mathit{HD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | Flow | 1.0E-06 | A t=10000s : | Identification | Tolerance | | --- | --- | | Moving \mathit{DY} to node {E}_{\mathit{HD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Material temperature node {E}_{\mathit{HD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | Moving \mathit{DY} to node {I}_{\mathit{HD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Temperature at node {I}_{\mathit{HD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | Flow | 1.0E-06 | 3.4 Remarks At t=10000s , the node I_HD moved about -70\mu m , (notably due to thermal expansion) which corresponds to the half opening of the crack. This means that the lips are in contact (keyword DEFI_CONTACT activated) and the crack closed. However, for the hydraulic part (managed by Crevisus ), a remanent opening is fixed, so that the flow is never zero. 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling, the use of MACR_ECREVISSE macro-command is validated in the presence of 2 vertical cracks. The geometry is slightly different from that of Modelling A. It is described with mesh in . The flow and material characteristics were described in §1. As for Modelling A, we work in flat deformations for mechanics (D_PLAN), and with a matrix of diagonized mass for thermal (PLAN_DIAG). 4.2 mesh et boundary conditions The mesh used is presented: Figure 4.2-a : mesh complete The dimensions of each of the three blocks are 0.50m high and 0.25m wide. Number of nodes : 2275 Number of mesh cells : 2108 QUAD4 The mesh cells size growth parameters used to produce the mesh are: from 0.002m (intrados) to 0.05m (extrados), and idem from BFISG1/BFISD2 to ENCASTRE; from 0.025m to MILIEU to 0.002m on BFISM1/BFISM2. The cracks are named with the name of the lips: BFISG1-BFISM1 (FISSURE 1), (FISSURE 2). The boundary conditions: 1. The quotes named ENCASTRE are clamped ( \mathit{DX}=0 , \mathit{DY}=0 ). 2. On the MILIEU side (symmetry line) the displacement is blocked in the direction X ( \mathit{DX}=0 ). 3. A contact condition is defined between the lip BFISG1-BFISM1 and BFISM2-BFISD2 (DEFI_CONTACT). 4. The pressure and temperature on the INTRADOS intrados are greater than on the EXTRADOS extrados ( 1.E6\mathrm{Pa} and 140°C versus 1.E6\mathrm{Pa} and 20°C ), which causes the flow of the intrados to the extrados. 5. The material is considered, at the beginning of the calculation, at the temperature atmosphere 20°C , which is the reference temperature. 4.3 Quantities and results The movement and temperature of the left crack and the exit of the right crack are tested at 2 different moments. Finally, the flow of the right crack at t=500s and the left crack at t=10000s is tested. A t=500s : | Identification | Tolerance | | --- | --- | | Moving \mathit{DX} to node {E}_{\mathit{MD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Material temperature node {E}_{\mathit{MD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | Moving \mathit{DX} node {I}_{\mathit{GD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Material temperature node {I}_{\mathit{GD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | BFISG1-BFISM1 Fissure, Flow | 1.0E-06 | A t=10000s : | Identification | Tolerance | | --- | --- | | Moving \mathit{DX} to node {E}_{\mathit{MD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Material temperature node {E}_{\mathit{MD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | Moving \mathit{DX} to node {I}_{\mathit{GD}} [m] | 1.0E-06 | | Material temperature node {I}_{\mathit{GD}} [°C] | 1.0E-06 | | BFISM2-BFISD2 Fissure, Flow | 1.0E-06 | 4.4 Remarks The opening of the t=10000s crack is of the order of {10}^{-9} , so is almost closed due to the thermal expansion due to the high temperature at the intrados. In this case also, it is the residual opening that is retained for the calculation of the flow. 5 Modelling C 5.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling, the use of MACR_ECREVISSE macro-command is validated in relation to rotation and translation, so this is not a non-regression test. The results of Ecrevisse depend only on the characteristics of the crack, including the direction of the crack. This is influenced by gravity. Thus, cracks with the same characteristics and having a symmetrical direction in relation to the vertical must give the same flows. The mesh is also the same (material, crack flow) as in Modelling A (§ 1.1). The mesh is also the same, except that it is turned and translated. v1.01.219 ZZZZ219 - AFFE_CHAR_MECA: keyword FACE_IMPO validation v1.01.219 ZZZZ219 - AFFE_CHAR_MECA: keyword FACE_IMPO validation Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate the FACE_IMPO key word for the AFFE_CHAR_MECA operator. This keyword allows you to impose on all nodes on one side on superfacial or volume elements, one or more degree of freedom values. In this test case FACE_IMPO is checked under the following conditions: - FACE_IMPO/SANS_GROUP_MA - FACE_IMPO/SANS_NOEUD - FACE_IMPO/SANS_GROUP_NO In this very simple test case (MODELISATION='C_PLAN'), all the movements of the mesh 6 nodes are imposed. It is therefore easy to check that the boundary conditions are being respected. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.221 ZZZZ221 – Validation of a thermo-hydration chaining calculation v1.01.221 ZZZZ221 – Validation of a thermo-hydration chaining calculation Summary: The objective of this test case axisymmetric is to verify the calculation of a thermo-hydration chaining. The concrete structure studied is composed of two levees. The main steps in the chaining are as follows: - Step 1: Thermo-Hydratation calculation on the first lift with operators: - DEFI_MATERIAU(THER_HYDR), - THER_NON_LINE(COMPORTEMENT='THER_HYDR'), - Step 2: Defnition of initial conditions on both lifts from the first lift results and initial values for the second lift. - CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE',NOM_CMP='TEMP') - CREA_CHAMP(OPERATION='AFFE',NOM_CMP='HYDR_NOEU') - Step 3: Thermo-Hydratation calculation on both lifts with operators: - DEFI_MATERIAU(THER_HYDR), - THER_NON_LINE(COMPORTEMENT='THER_HYDR'), Non-regression tests are performed on temperature and hydration. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.235 PLEXU01 – Basic CALC_EUROPLEXUS command validation v1.01.235 PLEXU01 – Basic CALC_EUROPLEXUS command validation Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the CALC_EUROPLEXUS command which initiates a EUROPLEXUS calculation (fast dynamic code) from a data set of the calculation in Code_Aster. It is verified that the results recovered by Code_Aster following the EUROPLEXUS calculation are those calculated by EUROPLEXUS alone. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A model structure consisting of a horizontal square slab 0.5m of thickness and side 3m , four vertical poles of length 3m planted in four corners of the slab and four horizontal beams (of the same length) connecting the upper ends of the poles and thus forming a closed contour is considered. All posts and beams have a rectangular cross section 0.4m\times 0.6m . 1.2 Material properties The material of the slab is elastic isotropic corresponding to a concrete whose properties are: - E=30000\mathit{MPa} - \nu =0.3 - \rho =2500\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} The material of the poles and beams is elastic isotropic corresponding to a steel whose properties are: - E=200000\mathit{MPa} - \nu =0.3 - \rho =7500\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The slab is based on a carpet of springs whose stiffness is calculated by the RIGI_PARASOL command from 6 specified values. A carpet of ground shock absorbers is also defined, of the A_T_D_N type, whose values are chosen voluntarily low in order to remain close to the reference solution, calculated, it, neglecting this damping. The slab is loaded by a pressure overfacial whose time-likeness is given by a function. 1.4 Initial conditions None. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference solution comes from the EUROPLEXUS calculation launched outside of Code_Aster. 2.2 Quantities and reference results The displacement, speed and acceleration values reread by Code_Aster are tested at the final moment and compared with the values from a single EUROPLEXUS calculation. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution None. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Q4GG Modelling is used for slab and POU_D_E for beams and poles. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh of the slab contains 36 elements of type QUAD4. Each beam and pole is discretized with 6 mesh cells SEG2. 3.3 Tested quantities and results The displacement, speed and acceleration values reread by Code_Aster are tested at the final moment and compared with the values from a single EUROPLEXUS calculation. | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Point \mathit{N1} - \mathit{DZ} | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 5.56E-03 | 0.011% | | Point \mathit{N49} - \mathit{VRZ} | 'NON_REGRESSION' | -1.718E-04 | 0.016% | | Point \mathit{N1} - \mathit{ARX} | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 5.56E-03 | 0.0004% |

v1.01.239 ZZZZ239 - Validation of the calculation of the non-symmetric matrix for elements DKT v1.01.239 ZZZZ239 - Validation of the calculation of the non-symmetric matrix for elements DKT Summary: This test validates the calculation of non-symmetric matrices for elements DKT (application with ENDO_LOCA_TC law). The number of iterations for convergence is comparable to the equivalent 3D case.

v1.01.257 ZZZZ257 - Error Estimator in Interest Quantity for Breaking Mechanics v1.01.257 ZZZZ257 - Error Estimator in Interest Quantity for Breaking Mechanics Summary: This test validates the error estimate in quantity of interest for the break mechanics. Thus, the 3 methods available in Code_Aster (residues, smoothing \mathrm{ZZ1} and smoothing \mathrm{ZZ2} ) are tested. In addition, the command files give a pattern for the implementation of the error estimate in quantity of interest and more specifically the definition of the load for the dual problem. There are 3 modellings that have 3 different problems: - Modelization A: cracked plate subjected to a uniform tensile force; - Modelization B: cantilever beam subjected to shearing effort; - Modelization C: plate with an inclined crack, subjected to a tensile force. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry In this test, three cracked plate configurations are considered. The first problem is a cracked plate subjected to a uniform tensile force (solicitation in I mode). The second problem is a cantilever beam subjected to shearing effort (solicitation in I mode and \mathrm{II} mode). Finally, the third problem is a plate with an inclined crack, subject to tensile force (solicitation in I mode and \mathrm{II} mode). v1.01.258 ZZZZ258 - STAT_NON_LINE ETAT_INIT Keyword Validation v1.01.258 ZZZZ258 - STAT_NON_LINE ETAT_INIT Keyword Validation Summary: This test validates the behavior of the code when a nonlinear calculation is "pursued" by imposing an initial state (keyword ETAT_INIT). In particular, it is checked that certain alarms are issued when changing behavior on some elements. Note: The code must also cause a fatal error when the behavior change is prohibited. This is verified in error test07 (v1.01.260). 1 Test principle This test is a computer test. It is used to validate the programming of the ETAT_INIT keyword processing and more specifically the routine vrcomp.f To define the initial state of a nonlinear calculation, the user has two options: - either it indicates an evol_noli data structure and a "minute" in this evol_noli (keywords EVOL_NOLI + INST) - or it gives 3 "isolated" displacement fields, constraints and internal variables (keywords DEPL, SIGM and VARI) Programming is different to deal with both cases, which is why we both test them. The difficulty we are trying to test here is that of a pursuit for which one or more elements of the "change" behavior model. Specifically, the following situations are tested: - adding new elements to the model - removal of elements in the model - the following possibilities for changing behaviour: - 'vmis_cine_line' -> 'vmis_cine_line' - 'vmis_cine_line' -> 'nothing' (deletion of elements) - 'vmis_cine_line' -> 'vmis_cine_line' - 'vmis_isot_trac' -> 'vmis_isot_line' - 'vmis_isot_trac' -> 'elas' - 'vmis_isot_line' -> 'vmis_isot_trac' - 'elas' -> 'vmis_cine_line' - 'nothing' -> 'vmis_cine_line' (add elements) - 'nothing' -> 'vmis_cine_line' (add elements)

v1.01.259 ZZZZ259 - mesh Adaptation and 2D Border Tracking v1.01.259 ZZZZ259 - mesh Adaptation and 2D Border Tracking Summary: This case tests the border tracking functionality during mesh adaptation with HOMARD. It contains 2D borders that are described analytically and 1D borders that are described by a fine mesh. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The field studied is a pricking: two pipes join together to form a connection. In the chosen example, one aims at generality by taking different diameters and non-scathing axes. The geometry is built by Salome. Groups of all edge faces are created. The groups of sharp edges are also created. With each adaptation of the mesh, nodes will be created on the edge. If you do nothing, the geometry remains facetted. Here you test the ability of HOMARD to replace the new nodes on the curved border. For 2D borders, surfaces are described analytically, as is the case with the internal and external faces of both pipes. For 1D boundaries, lines are described by a very fine mesh annex. This is the case of the complex curve which represents the intersection of the two pipes. For the ends of the cylinders, two cases of appearance occur. For the large pipe, the cutting planes are perpendicular to the axis. It is unnecessary to specify the shape of the intersection because the projection on the cylinder is made in the plane. However, the outer plane of the small pipe is not perpendicular to its axis. Therefore, the curve must be described by a fine annex mesh. The test results in the following two errors: !---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------! ! ! ! ! ! incompatible behaviors: VMIS_CINE_LINE and VMIS_ISOT_TRAC for the mesh cell M1! !---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------! !----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------! ! ! ! ! v1.01.261 ZZZZ261 - Validation of PROJ_CHAMP in 2D for nodes fields v1.01.261 ZZZZ261 - Validation of PROJ_CHAMP in 2D for nodes fields Summary: This test validates the different projection methods of the PROJ_CHAMP command ('ELEM', 'NUAG_DEG_0/1') for a mesh 2D. 1 Test principle The field studied is a square [0,1]\times [0,1] It is meshed in quadrangles in two different ways: MA1: Cut the square into 9\times 9 QUAD4 MA2: Cut the square into 12\times 12 QUAD4 On the mesh MA1, a thermal evolution is created by assigning to each node the temperature obtained by the formula: T=t\ast (1+2{(x-0,5)}^{2}+3{(y-0,25)}^{2}) where t,x,y represents the value of the moment and the 2 coordinates of the nodes. v1.01.264 ZZZZ264 – Validation of the POST_ENDO_FISS command v1.01.264 ZZZZ264 – Validation of the POST_ENDO_FISS command Summary: This test case allows you to validate the POST_ENDO_FISS command, which allows you to search for a crack path and open cracks from a mechanical damage calculation. Three test cases are offered: - the cracking path over an analytical field, - crack opening on study calculated with the ENDO_SCALAIRE / GRAD_VARI law, - crack opening on study calculated with MAZARS law. 1 Reference problem: Searching for cracking path on an analytical result 1.1 Field Generation In this first test, the cracking path is sought on an artificial field, that is, created analytically and not from a mechanical calculation. The advantage is that the cracking path is known a priori , so it can be compared with the path resulting from the command. With the , we show the artificial field on which we will test the command, on the domain x,y . Figure 1.1-1 : discretized post-treating field on mesh. For the field generation, the crack path was first fixed, then the field is given by a function defined on the orthogonal profile at the crack at each of its points. The cracking path is the polynomial of degree 4 which passes through the points: \mathit{P1}=(10.,0.) , \mathit{P2}=(35.,20.) , \mathit{P3}=(60.,0.) , \mathit{P4}=(85.,20.) , \mathit{P5}=(110.,0.) On the orthogonal profile of the r curvilinear abscisse, a z=-{a}_{1}{r}^{2}+{a}_{2} parabolic profile is defined that is bounded below the minimum \mathrm{valmin} value of the field (here, {10}^{-6} ). The resulting field is everywhere equal to \mathrm{valmin} , except in the vicinity of the crack, creating an artificial "damaged" zone. The width of the damaged area and the value of the field are variable along the crack: {a}_{1}=-0.04\cos(0.1(x-{x}_{{P}_{1}}))+0.0667 éq 1.1-1 {a}_{2}=(\cos(0.3(x-{x}_{{P}_{1}}))+2)/3 éq 1.1-2 The field described was discretized on a mesh to mesh cells rectangular size \mathit{dx}=2.45 , \mathit{dy}=1 , on a 120\times 40 domain. In the test case, the MED file containing the post-processing field, contained in a given structure of the result type (evol_noli), is given directly and created previously using the CREA_CHAMP and CREA_RESU commands, in order to make the test case faster. As the command only processes nodes fields, the analytical field is stored in the field at DEPL nodes, under the DX component (the VARI_NOEU field, which normally contains the damage, is not available in CREA_CHAMP). 1.2 Command Settings The parameters used to search for the crack path are as follows: LONG_ORTH= 20, PAS= 2, LONG_REG= 4, SEUIL= {10}^{-3} ANGL_MAX= 180 2 Modelling A 2.1 Cracking path found The crack path found by the command is given in . In the , the crack is superimposed on the field map. Figure 2.1-1 : Theoretical cracking (black) trajectories compared to the one provided by the command. Figure 2.1-2 : Overlay cracking path to post-treated field. 2.2 Tested quantities and results The distance between the points found by the algorithm and the theoretical curve is tested. This distance, stored in the test case command file in the TAB_FISS table, represents the absolute error in each point. We then check that the maximum error is less than a certain accuracy. The test is done in absolute terms, as we compare ourselves to a zero distance. The precision requested is 0.05, the test case is analytical. 2.3 Remarks The route found is very satisfactory. The procedure reproduces the strong curvatures of the journey, as well as the variations in the value of the field. The accuracy is related to the width of the damaged strip, as seen on the right side of the strip: the error is greater where the width of the damaged strip is small. That said, normally the damage resulting from a mechanical calculation is extended to several elements, so that convergence with refinement is verified, which limits this type of error. 3 Reference problem: crack opening on a study with damage law In this test case, POST_ENDO_FISS searches both the crack path and the crack opening on a mechanical test case. The mechanical study is done beforehand which consists of a tensile test piece calculated with the ENDO_SCALAIRE damage law and then MAZARS. This mechanical calculation is not included in the test case due to the significant time required for calculation. Thus, a MED file containing the mechanical results is read, and then the post-processing control is applied. Finally, the crack opening is compared to the displacement imposed on the free edge. 3.1 Geometry, mesh and loading. This is a two-fold tensile test piece. The dimensions of the test piece are 1m\times 2m ; the radius of the (semi-circular) slat is 6\mathrm{cm} . At one end of the test piece, a displacement is imposed until rupture, when the resulting force applied is zero. The displacements of the other end are blocked in the direction of application of the load. Figure 3.1-1: géométrie, maillage et conditions aux limites de l'éprouvette en traction. 3.2 Material properties and models of advance mechanical calculations 3.2.1 Law ENDO_SCALAIRE ENDO_SCALAIRE R5.03.25 law is used, with gradient adjustment of R5.04.01 internal variables and flat deformations: D_PLAN_GRAD_VARI Modelling. - Elastic parameters: E=40000\mathrm{MPa} Young's modulus \nu =0,25 Poisson's ratio Damage parameters : D=0.1m Half-width of the damaged strip {G}_{f}=100N/m Breaking energy \mathrm{SY}=2.8\mathrm{MPa} Tensile strength 3.2.2 Law MAZARS MAZARS R7.01.08 is used. - Elastic parameters: E=40000\mathrm{MPa} Young's modulus \nu =0,25 Poisson's ratio MAZARS (modelization B): {\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{d0}}=\mathrm{SY}/E=7E-5 Damage Threshold {A}_{t}=1 Traction parameter {B}_{t}=13000 Traction parameter {A}_{c}=1.09 Compression parameter {B}_{c}=1600 Compression parameter \beta =1.06 Parameter to improve shear response \mathrm{NON}\mathrm{LOCAL}=0.1m Characteristic length of non-local model 3.3 Post-processing POST_ENDO_FISS Settings The crack path is searched for on the damage field. We therefore use the \mathit{V1} component of the VARI_NOEU field (because the command only takes in fields to the nodes). The average size of the mesh cell in the damaged area is 0.02m . The parameters used: LONG_ORTH = 2m PAS = 0.02m LONG_REG = 0.02m SEUIL = 0.5 LIM_FPZ = 0.8 All other parameters have the default value. It is also possible to use the VARI component of the DEPL field, which also stores the damage variable and is a nodal field (so it can be used directly by the command). It is also necessary to project this field on a linear mesh, which will be given to it as an input to POST_ENDO_FISS, to make the interpolation of the VARI component consistent with that of the mesh (so linear). The command file gives an example of how the VARI_NOEU/V1 field and DEPL/VARI field are used. As regards Modelling C, the search for the cracking path is carried out on the equivalent deformation, as the damage field does not allow to identify a true maximum (it is too "flat"). We therefore use the \mathit{V4} component of the VARI_NOEU field. The parameters used in POST_ENDO_FISS are the same as in B Modelling, except for the following: SEUIL = 0.0001 LIM_FPZ = 0.0001 4 Modelling B 4.1 Mechanical results The elastic prediction steering method (PRED_ELAS) is used. The force-moving curve obtained is in . The test piece at the moment C is completely broken, the residual force being close to zero. It is at this moment that the crack opening will be calculated. The appearance of displacement and damage are given in Figures and . Figure 4.1-1: Courbe force-déplacement, éprouvette bi-entaillée (loi ENDO_SCALAIRE). Figure 4.1-2: Déplacements sur l'axe longitudinal de l'éprouvette (loi ENDO_SCALAIRE). Figure 4.1-3: Endommagement sur l'axe longitudinal de l'éprouvette (loi ENDO_SCALAIRE). 4.2 Tested quantities and results The crack path found at the instant C is shown in the VARI component of the DEPL field. The path found with the VARI_NOEU field is similar. Figure 4.2-1: trajet de fissuration dans l'éprouvette bi-entaillée (loi ENDO_SCALAIRE). At the end of the calculation, either the cracking path or the crack opening are tested. Pour ce qui concerne le trajet de fissuration, celui ci doit à priori se trouver sur l'axe de symétrie de l'éprouvette, sur l'axe x . On teste alors que la distance maximale à cet axe des points trouvés par la commande soit inférieure à une certaine précision. Un cas-test analytique est prévu, avec précision (absolue) égale à 1.5\times \mathit{taille}\mathit{élément}=0.03m . For crack openings, the crack must be equal to the required displacement. Therefore, an analytical test case, with a relative accuracy of 10%, and an test case of non-regression with precision of 5%, are proposed. In summary, if you use the VARI_NOEU field, component \mathit{V1} for searching for the crack path: | Quantity tested | Type of test | Creative action requested | test case precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} | Analysis | 0.03m | 0.0129m | | Opening | Analysis | 10 % | 4.69 % | | Opening | non-regression | 5 % | 4.69 % | If DEPL, component VARI is used to search for the crack path: | Quantity tested | Type of test | Creative action requested | test case precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} | Analysis | 0.03m | 0.0128m | | Opening | Analysis | 10 % | 4.97 % | | Opening | non-regression | 5 % | 4.97 % | 4.3 Remarks The found cracking path is satisfactory, however the accuracy recovered is at the limit of the permissible accuracy for the test case analytical. This is because the ENDO_SCALAIRE law locates the damage much when approaching the breakage (damage=1). According to the analytical solutions in fact, the damage is 1 as on the crack. This requires very fine meshes in the localization band. In the , a more precise cracking path could have been obtained following a mechanical calculation using a finer mesh. For the crack opening, the error source is related to: 1. cracking path not perfectly straight, 2. residual force on the test piece close to but not equal to zero. 5 Modelling C 5.1 Mechanical results Figure 5.1-1: Courbe force-déplacement, éprouvette bi-entaillée (loi MAZARS). No steering method is used. The force-moving curve obtained is in . The test piece at the moment C is completely broken, the residual force being close to zero. It is at this moment that the crack opening will be calculated. The appearance of displacements, damage and equivalent deformation are given in the Figures, and . Figure 5.1-2: Déplacement sur l'axe longitudinal de l'éprouvette (loi MAZARS). Figure 5.1-3: Endommagement sur l'axe longitudinal de l'éprouvette (loi MAZARS). Figure 5.1-4: Déformation équivalente sur l'axe longitudinal de l'éprouvette (loi MAZARS). 5.2 Tested quantities and results The cracking path found at the instant C is similar to that of the . The quantities tested are the same as in model B. In summary: | Quantity tested | Type of test | Creative action requested | test case precision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} | Analysis | 0.03m | 2.58\cdot {10}^{-3}m | | Opening | Analysis | 10 % | 0.683 % | | \mathit{DY} | non-regression | 0.01m | 2.58\cdot {10}^{-3}m | | Opening | non-regression | 1 % | 0.683 % | 5.3 Remarks The cracking path found is more accurate than for model B. This is due to the damage law used, which is less localized at breakage.

v1.01.268 ZZZZ268 - Validation of POST_BORDET in 2D and 3D v1.01.268 ZZZZ268 - Validation of POST_BORDET in 2D and 3D Summary: This test validates Bordet's two-dimensional and three-dimensional stress and probability calculation, with thermal evolution, on cases in which the mechanical fields are uniform (which allows an analytical calculation of these quantities); this test case is intended to test numerical developments and not to conduct a realistic case study. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry of modelling A A axisymmetric \mathrm{1mm} radius and \mathrm{10mm} height bar is considered to be subject to a single (imposed displacement) traction test. This test is chosen as it allows uniform mechanical fields to be obtained. Figure 1.1: axisymmetric Bar. 1.2 Modelling Geometry B Here we consider a \mathrm{1mm} side cube subject to traction. The front face is blocked in the direction \text{X} , the left face in the direction \text{Y} , the bottom face in the direction \text{Z} and an incremental traction of 0,001\text{mm} is applied on the upper face. 1.3 Material properties The material is perfect for elastoplastics with Young's modulus from 300000\text{MPa} , Poisson's ratio from 0 and 300\text{MPa} elastic limit. 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads For Modelling A, 5 0,01\text{mm} traction increments are performed, so that the total deformation increment is 1.0\text{E-3} and the elastic limit is reached at the first step. For Modelling B, the front face is blocked according to the \text{X} direction, the left face according to the \text{Y} direction, the bottom face according to the \text{Z} axis and an incremental 0,001\text{mm} traction is applied on the upper face. Temperature varies linearly in the bar from \text{O°C} to \text{5O°C} on the 5 time step. In order to test the various possibilities offered by the CALC_BORDET macro-command, the parameters of the temperature and the plastic deformation speed are used, where possible. The list of parameters used is presented in the table below. | Parameter | Type | Value | | --- | --- | --- | | M | Scalar | 22 | | SIG_CRIT | Scalar | 250 | | VOLU_REFE | Scalar | 1 | | SIGM_REFE | Function | 200+\text{T} | | SEUIL_CALC | Tablet | \lbrace \begin{array}{cc}10T& \text{si}{\dot{\stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon}}}^{p}=0,0005\\ 5T& \text{si}{\dot{\stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon}}}^{p}=0,001\end{array} | | DEF_PLAS_REFE | Scalar | 0 | Table 1.1 : Bordet parameters used 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation In both cases, due to the uniform nature of the mechanical fields, the analytical calculation can be performed both of Bordet's constraints and of probability. This is done by using the equations of the Bordet model presented in the R7.02.06 documentation: Models of Beremin, Bordet and Rice and Tracey. 2.2 Quantities and reference results Both Bordet stress and associated probability are tested for 0-5 times. For Modelling A, the following reference results are obtained: | Instant | Bordet's Continuity | Probability of Bordet | | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | 0 | 0.0000 | | 1 | 0 | 0.0000 | | 2 | 247.67 | 0.9999 | | 3 | 252.23 | 0.9995 | | 4 | 254.1 | 0.9701 | | 5 | 254.7 | 0.7780 | Table 2.1: Résultats analytiques pour la modélisation A For model B, the following reference results are obtained: | Instant | Bordet's Continuity | Probability of Bordet | | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | 0 | 0.0000 | | 1 | 0 | 0.0000 | | 2 | 211.75 | 0.3500 | | 3 | 215.64 | 0.2150 | | 4 | 217.24 | 0.11 | | 5 | 217.75 | 0.0467 | Table 2.2: Résultats analytiques pour la modélisation B 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution Because of the analytical character, the reference solution is accurate. v1.01.269 PYNL02 - STAT_NON_LINE in split commands for elasto-plastic calculation v1.01.269 PYNL02 - STAT_NON_LINE in split commands for elasto-plastic calculation Summary: This document is intended to validate the methodology for solving a nonlinear problem (here a problem of elasto-plasticity) in broken commands, without using the STAT_NON_LINE command. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry We consider a unitary cube. 1.2 Material properties A material with a Von constitutive law Mixed-nuting (VMIS_ECMI_TRAC) bets is considered. The elastic properties are as follows: - Young's modulus: E=221300\mathrm{MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu =0,3 The Prager constant is C=2200\mathrm{MPa} . The traction curve considered is given on the . Figure 1.2-1: Courbe de traction 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The lower face (in the z=0 plane) is clamped. The upper face (in the z=1 plane) is subjected to a vertical \mathrm{dz}={10}^{-2}[m] displacement. 2 reference solution The reference solution is obtained by numerical resolution of the problem using the STAT_NON_LINE command. This gives the constraint field and the field of internal variables. The charge increment is discretized in 2 moments between 0 and 1. An elastic prediction is made, and the tangential matrix is re-re-actualized with each iteration and increment. The convergence table is shown below: Figure 2-1: Tableau de convergence de référence 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling, the STAT_NON_LINE command is replaced by broken commands. boundary conditions are applied by dualization (Lagranges) 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh is composed of a single mesh cell HEXA8. 3.3 Tested quantities and results The difference between the stress field (respectively internal variables) calculated by STAT_NON_LINE and the CALCUL command, at last moment, is tested. | Identification | Reference | \text{\%} difference | | --- | --- | --- | | \min(\Delta \sigma ) | 0 | 0 | | \max(\Delta \sigma ) | 0 | 0 | | \min(\Delta v) | 0 | 0 | | \max(\Delta v) | 0 | 0 | The convergence table is also identical to the reference table: Figure 3.3-1: Tableau de convergence obtenue via la commande CALCUL 4 Summary of the results This test validated the methodology for solving a nonlinear problem (here a problem of elasto-plasticity) in broken commands, without using the STAT_NON_LINE command. In this test, the scope of the methodology is limited: - no external forces (loading imposed via Lagranges) - no temperature loading (control variables) - no pilotage, - no linear search, - no contact, - the NUME_DDL does not change during the time step (notably, the nodes whose displacement is imposed does not vary).

v1.01.277 ERREU03 - Simple singularity detection in MECA_STATIQUE v1.01.277 ERREU03 - Simple singularity detection in MECA_STATIQUE Summary: This test validates the emission of an error message when a single singularity is detected (absence or overabundance) by direct linear solvers (MUMPS, LDLT and MULT_FRONT) in MECA_STATIQUE. 1 Test principle This test is used to validate the emission of a few messages by MECA_STATIQUE in the case of a symmetrical matrix: - First case: there is a blockage missing. v1.01.278 ERREU04 - Simple singularity detection in broken commands v1.01.278 ERREU04 - Simple singularity detection in broken commands Summary: This test validates the issuance of an error message when a simple singularity is detected (absence or overabundance of blocks) by direct linear solvers (MUMPS, LDLT and MULT_FRONT) used in split commands (FACTORISER, RESOUDRE). 1 Test principle This test is used to validate the sending of a few messages by FACTORISER or RESOUDRE commands in the case of a symmetrical matrix: - First case: there is a blockage missing. In this case, you get FACTOR_20/77 for LDLT, MULT_FRONT and MUMPS when \mathrm{NPREC}>0 and FACTOR_57 for MUMPS when \mathrm{NPREC} 0 and FACTOR_42 for MUMPS when \mathrm{NPREC}<0 . - Last case: Check that the FACTOR_80 message is sent when using the TYPE_RESOL='SYMDEF' parameter of the MUMPS solver, while the matrix to be reversed is not symmetrically defined as positive.

v1.01.279 ERREU05 - Checking for Recovery of Fatal Errors in STAT_NON_LINE v1.01.279 ERREU05 - Checking for Recovery of Fatal Errors in STAT_NON_LINE Summary: This test validates recovery of fatal errors in STAT_NON_LINE and the possibility of pursuing a base obtained from the exit of a study that stopped in error. 1 Test principle This test is a computer test and is conducted in two phases: - The test case initially performs a first STAT_NON_LINE during which an error occurs (interpolation problem of a function). This error is intercepted and the test base is properly closed. - In a second step, an POURSUITE is performed using the database produced during the first calculation.

v1.01.280 ERREU06 - Checking the operation of the NaN in Code_Aster v1.01.280 ERREU06 - Checking the operation of the NaN in Code_Aster Summary: This test validates the fact that in debug version on the central server Aster4, Code_Aster stops in error when attempting to manipulate a NaN (Not-a-Number) type SNaN (Signalling NaN). 1 Test principle This test is a computer test.
