v1.01.344 ZZZZ344 – Validation of the calculation of angular deviations in DEFI_CABLE_BP v1.01.344 ZZZZ344 – Validation of the calculation of angular deviations in DEFI_CABLE_BP Summary: Calculation of the angular deviations in the DEFI_CABLE_BP operator is done using cubic spline interpolations. However, sometimes this method fails when the mesh is too irregular. In this case, an interpolation-free method is used for calculating angular deviations. The objective of this test is to validate the calculation of angular deviations by this method. To this end, we compare the calculation of angular deviations by spline and without interpolation for the same geometry. The meshes for which spline interpolation fails are derived from different meshes of the Vercors enclosure. The mesh for which it is correct was created from the equation of the circle to be as close as possible to the other meshes. 1 Reference problem A horizontal and circular cable is considered to be contained in concrete. The mesh of the concrete part is the same for each model. But the mesh of the cable changes. Model A: the cable was built from the circle equation; it has 100 mesh cells of type SEG2. It is very regular, the spline interpolation is correct. This Modelling serves as a reference for the other two. Model B: the cable (like concrete) is from a mesh from the Vercors enclosure. The discretization of the cable is identical to the model A(100 mesh cells). Model C: the cable (like concrete) is from a finer mesh from the Vercors enclosure, it has 302 mesh cells. 2 reference solution Modelling A. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics The mesh of the cable is generated from the circle equation. v1.01.346 ZZZZ346 – Bifurcation of a right XFEM interface with quadratic elements 2D v1.01.346 ZZZZ346 – Bifurcation of a right XFEM interface with quadratic elements 2D Summary The purpose of this test is to validate the XFEM sub-cut algorithm with quadratic elements 2D. The general sub-cut algorithm is described in the R7.02.12 reference documentation. Moreover, the sub-cut is mainly used when calling the MODI_MODELE_XFEM U4.41.11 operator. In this test, one is interested in a particular cutting situation: the bifurcation of an interface along a ridge, within the element. Depending on the position of the point fork on the edge, two R7.02.12 cutting configurations are available. These configurations correspond to two regularizations of the level-set shape. Four modellings are envisaged: 1. A Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{2D} with elements TRIA6, the interface fork before the mid point on the bifurcation edge. 2. B Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{2D} with elements QUAD8, the interface fork before the mid point on the bifurcation edge. 3. C Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{2D} with elements TRIA6, the interface fork after the mid point on the bifurcation edge. 4. D Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{2D} with elements QUAD8, the interface fork after the mid point on the bifurcation edge. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The \mathrm{2D} structure is a square unit plate ( \mathit{LX}=0,1 , \mathit{LY}=0,1 ). A "right" interface cuts the domain into 2 subdomains. The interface bifurcates near the centre of the (0,0.5) square with an \theta =67,5° angle relative to the horizontal. Figure 1.1-1 : Geometry of cracked plate The interface is defined analytically by the union of 2 segments on the right, the respective equations of which are: - X=0 for the vertical segment. - Y=2x+0.55 for the oblique segment. The point intersection of the 2 segments on the right is calculated to be located on the edge where the bifurcated interface: - (0,0.55) for modellings A and B , or - (0,0.6) for modellings C and D , or Figure 1.1-2: «zoom» au voisinage du point de bifurcation Figure 1.1-3: «zoom» au voisinage du point de bifurcation 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus: E=210{10}^{9}\mathrm{Pa} Poisson's ratio: \nu =0 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Modelling A : The interface breaks the domain into 2 subdomains. The moving solution is imposed on each subdomain, thanks to the conditions of Dirichlet on the edges: - on the \mathit{LIG2} edge: \mathit{DX}=-1 and \mathit{DY}=0 - on the \mathit{LIG4} edge: \mathit{DX}=+1 and \mathit{DY}=0 There is no contact at the interface level. We are just interested in the movements of the 2 blocks, which can interpenetrate. The imposed Dirichlet conditions also block the rigid body movements of the 2 subdomains. modellings B , C et D : Same load as in A Modelling. 1.4 reference solution Modelling A : By construction, the displacement field is uniform on each sub-block. - On the subdomain on the right, we have: \mathit{DX}=-1 and \mathit{DY}=0 - On the left-hand subdomain, we have: \mathit{DX}=+1 and \mathit{DY}=0 Modelling B : Same analytical solution as A Modelling Modelling C : Same analytical solution as A Modelling Modelling D : Same analytical solution as A Modelling 1.5 Bibliographical references 1. v1.01.347 ZZZZ347 – Validation of the CABLE_GAINE rubbing cables v1.01.347 ZZZZ347 – Validation of the CABLE_GAINE rubbing cables Summary: The objective of this test is to validate CABLE_GAINE prestress cable modelling. Modelling A is used to validate the use of DEFI_CABLE_BP/CALC_PRECONT with elements BARRE in the absence of friction in curved cases, and serves as a reference to validate the CABLE_GAINE Modelling in the ADHERENT case, tested in Modelling B. Modelling C validates CABLE_GAINE Modelling in the GLISSANT case. The D Modelling validates the use of DEFI_CABLE_BP/CALC_PRECONT with elements BARRE in the presence of friction. It also serves as a reference to Modelling E, which validates the CABLE_GAINE Modelling in the case of FROTTANT, with consideration for linear and curved friction, in the case of only one or both active anchors, and finally, with and without anchoring back. Modellings F and G are copies of the E Modelling with the inshell modeled concrete (DKT and Q4GG), and are used to validate the new prestressing procedure with the hull elements. Finally, H Modelling tests PETIT_REAC kinematics in comparison with elements BARRE. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 1.1.1 modellings A à G A square sectional concrete half-ring with a cable in the centre of the section is considered. The half ring is r=5m radius, from the centre of the origin, in a (xy) plane and half of the ring is y positive. A section of the ring in the y=0 plane is given by the following two points of the diagonal (4.5;\mathrm{0 };-0.5) and (5.5;\mathrm{0 };0,5) (i.e. a 1m surface by 1m ). The section of the cable is 2,5\times {10}^{-3}m . For modellings A to E, concrete modelling is volume-intensive, for modellings F and G, the Modelling is flat. Figure 1-1: vue du maillage béton utilisé (modélisations A à E) Figure 1-2: vue du maillage béton utilisé (modélisations F et G) Figure 1-3: vue du câble de précontrainte noyé dans le béton 1.1.2 Modelling H A 10m length concrete beam, with a square cross section of 1m on the side with a cable in the centre of the section, is considered. The cross section of the cable is 2,5\times {10}^{-3}{m}^{2} . Figure 1-4: vue du maillage du béton de la modélisation H 1.2 Material properties Concrete is elastic isotropic, its properties are: - E=45000\mathit{MPa} - \nu =0 The steel is elastic isotropic, its properties are: - E=185000\mathit{MPa} - \nu =0 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads 1.3.1 modellings A à G The y=0 and x<0 section of the ring is clamped (sided containing ANCR2). 1.3.2 Modelling H The face in the x=0 plane is clamped and the lower side of the beam ( z=-0,5 ) is pressured to a value of {10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} . There is no prestressing in this test. 1.4 Initial conditions None. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation In the case of a slippery cable without friction (modelling C), with concrete and cable sheath clamped (only the slip of the cable is then allowed), the following analytical solution is displayed. The imposed slip is noted \stackrel{̃}{g} , the length of the cable L , its section A The deformation of the cable is uniform (no friction) and is then \frac{\tilde{g}}{L} , the E\frac{\tilde{g}}{L} stress and the T=AE\frac{\tilde{g}}{L} voltage . The reaction on the whole concrete is R=\mathrm{2T} . On a cable section, the reaction is S=T\Delta \alpha with \Delta \alpha the angular deviation. If the cable is discretized in n elements of the same size, we have S=T\frac{\pi}{n} . For BPEL voltage calculations, analytical references are obtained using the formulae given in R7.01.02. 2.2 Quantities and reference results 2.2.1 Voltage and reactions for Modelling C Taking \tilde{g}=0.1 , L=r\pi , A=2.5e-3 , E=185000\mathit{MPa} , we find: - T=2.9443664{10}^{6}N voltage - reaction on all R=5.888734{10}^{6}N concrete and S=462500N cable cross section with n=20 . 2.2.2 BPEL voltage for modellings E, F and G The Gauss points tested are the Gauss 1 points of the mesh cells 105 and 96 for Modelling E corresponding to the mesh cells 59 and 50 for the modellings F and G. All point P owned by the cable can be defined by the a=\stackrel{ˆ}{\overrightarrow{({\mathit{OA}}_{1},\mathit{OP})}} or b=\stackrel{ˆ}{\overrightarrow{({\mathit{OA}}_{2},\mathit{OP})}} angle value where O is the center of the semi-circle, {A}_{1} is ANCR1 and {A}_{2} is ANCR2. The first node of the mesh cell 96 is defined by a=67,5 or b=112,5 . The first point of the mesh cell 96 is then defined by {a}_{96}=67,5+\frac{4,5}{\sqrt{(3)}} or {b}_{96}=112,5-\frac{4,5}{\sqrt{(3)}} . The first node of the mesh cell 105 is defined by a=148,5 or b=31,5 . The first point of the mesh cell 105 is then defined by {a}_{96}=148,5+\frac{4,5}{\sqrt{(3)}} or {b}_{96}=31,5-\frac{4,5}{\sqrt{(3)}} . The cumulative angular deviation \alpha of these points is required to be calculated and used for the calculation of voltages. The cumulative angular deviation used in the BPEL formula of the voltage must be calculated from the nearest active anchor. In the E Modelling, two calculations are made: one with passive ANCR1 and active ANCR2 and the other with both active anchors. The mesh cell 105 is closer to ANCR2, which is still active, so we have both: {\alpha}_{105}={b}_{105}\mathrm{\ast }\pi /180 . We note that in our case the cumulative angular deviation is equal to the angles a or b , we only pass in radians. The mesh cell 96 is closer to ANCR1 so we have two different values: {\alpha}_{96}={b}_{96}\mathrm{\ast }\pi /180 for PASSIF/ACTIF {\alpha}_{96}={a}_{96}\mathrm{\ast }\pi /180 for ACTIF/ACTIF The curvilinear abscisses of these points are also necessary for the calculation of the voltage, they are also given in relation to the nearest active anchor. We then have: {s}_{105}={\alpha}_{105}\mathrm{\ast }r and {s}_{96}={\alpha}_{96}\mathrm{\ast }r . For the case without anchoring back, the formula {F}_{c}={F}_{0}\exp(-f\alpha -\phi s) is used, with {F}_{0}={10}^{6}N , \phi =0,01 ; f=0,03 , we obtain: - for PASSIF/ACTIF: {F}_{105}=960448.709086365N and {F}_{96}=857741.905702382N - for ACTIF/ACTIF: {F}_{105}=960448.709086365N ; {F}_{96}=906761.8988894981N The EPSI_ELGA deformation field is tested in Modelling E in the case PASSIF/ACTIF, on the same Gauss points as the N voltage. The calculation is elastic, therefore: {\mathit{EPXX}}_{105}={F}_{105}/E/A {\mathit{EPXX}}_{96}={F}_{96}/E/A For the case with the anchoring rearrangement, with the ratings of R7.01.02, the distance d on which the anchoring rearrangement acts is shown to be: d=\frac{-1}{f}\ln(1-\sqrt{(f\ast {E}_{a}\ast {S}_{a}\ast \Delta /{F}_{0})}) With an \Delta =5.{10}^{4} anchoring step, you get here d=3.9222 . By keeping the ratings defined above, this means that an point is affected if a<44,94 or b<44,94 . The mesh cell 105 is therefore affected by the modification due to the anchoring step, but not the mesh cell 96. Using {F}_{c}=\frac{{(F(d))}^{2}}{{F}_{0}}\exp(-f\alpha -\phi s) for mesh cell 105 and {F}_{c}={F}_{0}\exp(-f\alpha -\phi s) for mesh cell 96, we obtain: {F}_{105}=918367.3641803192 ; {F}_{96}=906761.8988894981 2.2.3 Reference for Modelling H Due to the load imposed, DEFORMATION = 'PETIT' would not have any constraints in the cable. However, DEFORMATION = 'PETIT_REAC' will have to show constraints. The reference solution in this case is obtained by calculating with elements BARRE. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution None 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The Modelling is 3D for the concrete ring and BARRE for the cable. v1.01.348 ZZZZ348 – Coupling of the Aster Code and Python Python Solver commands for time integration used in LEGOS tool v1.01.348 ZZZZ348 – Coupling of the Aster Code and Python Python Solver commands for time integration used in LEGOS tool Summary: In the context of the development of the rotating machine calculation tool in the LEGOS code which uses a C++-written solver and has a API python, the possibility of coupling via the aster control file is simpler and no longer requires the passage complicated by YACS. Thus, this possibility of coupling the aster controls and the python time integration solver used in the LEGOS code is demonstrated through a simple mechanical calculation of a shaft line subjected to harmonic loading. This test case is broken down into two parts: - Aster controls to construct the modal base and mass, damping, gyroscopy and stiffness matrices of the tree line studied; - Python solver to achieve the time integration of the dynamic system that allows to pair the dynamics of the tree line with the lubrication code of the LEGOS code. The result of this test case is compared with the reference calculation of the old procedure for calculating rotating machines using the DYNA_VIBRA operator. It is therefore test case non-regression. The comparison shows an excellent consistency between the two results. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry For purely demonstrative purposes, this test case is studied with a "non-real" tree line of a total length of 0.4m and a circular cross-section full of the external diameter of 0.02m, supported by three bearings. This tree line has a disc positioned 130mm from the left end. Figure 1.1-1 > The coordinates of the points shown in the figure above are: | Nœud | X(m) | Y(m) | Z(m) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | N1Z1 | 0.000000E+00 | 0.000000E+00 | 0.000000E+00 | | N2Z1 | 0.000000E+00 | 0.000000E+00 | 1.333340E-01 | | N3Z1 | 0.000000E+00 | 0.000000E+00 | 2.666670E-01 | | N4Z1 | 0.000000E+00 | 0.000000E+00 | 4.000000E-01 | | AP1 | 1.000000E-05 | 0.000000E+00 | 0.000000E+00 | | P1 | 1.000000E-05 | 0.000000E+00 | 2.666670E-01 | | AP2 | 1.000000E-05 | 0.000000E+00 | 4.000000E-01 | Table 1.1-1 1.2 Material properties The material made of the shaft line has the following elastic characteristics: - density: ρ = 7800kg/m3 - Poisson's ratio: ν = 0.3 - Young's modulus: E = 200GPa Stiffness restraint Modelling the node N1Z1 bearing: {k}_{x}={k}_{Y}={10}^{12}N/m ; Stiffness restraint Modelling the node N3Z1 bearing: {k}_{x}=2.0\times {10}^{5}N/m and {k}_{Y}=5.0\times {10}^{5}N/m ; Stiffness restraint Modelling the node N4Z1 bearing: {k}_{x}={k}_{Y}={10}^{12}N/m ; Point mass of rotor: m=16.47\mathit{kg} The rotor's inertia tensor relative to the node N2Z1 is: {I}_{\mathit{XX}}=0.1861{\mathit{kgm}}^{2} ; {I}_{\mathit{YY}}={I}_{\mathit{ZZ}}=0.09427{\mathit{kgm}}^{2} and coupling terms as well as the terms of the de-centering are zero. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions : Nodes belonging to the shaft line are blocked at the vertical displacement and rotation around this axis: \mathit{dz}=\mathit{drz}=0 The nodes \mathit{AP}1 , P1 and \mathit{AP}2 are clamped: \mathit{dx}=\mathit{dy}=\mathit{dz}=\mathit{drx}=\mathit{dry}=\mathit{drz}=0 . Charge : The structure is subjected to a point N2Z1 bald with A=15 amplitude g.mm with zero phase. The rotation speed is 2500 rpm. 1.4 Initial conditions The system is at rest. 2 Coupling procedure 2.1 Dynamic fundamental equation of the rotating system > The dynamic equation of the rotating system shall be written as follows (without taking into account the prestress): > K\ddot{U}+(C+G)\dot{U}+(K+\mathit{KG})U=F > où: - M,C,K : the conventional mass, damping and rigidity matrices of the discretized system, respectively - G\mathit{et}\mathit{KG} : Coriolis and stiffness centrifugal coupling matrices, respectively. - \ddot{U},\dot{U},U : vectors in acceleration, speed and displacement - F : external loading vector 2.2 Part 1: Aster Commands The aster commands are used to construct the modal base. The mass, damping, gyroscopy and stiffness matrices are then projected on this basis. The following diagram shows the sequence of these orders: Figure 2.2-1 The matrices are extracted and stored as python objects via the EXTR_MATR_GENE() command. 2.3 Part 2: Python Time Integration Solver The python time integration solver uses the β-Newmark diagram with γ = 0.5 and β=0.25. The architecture of the python solver is shown in the figure below: Figure 2.3-1 The classes are defined as follows: - Base(): Convert Aster modal bases to python objects. This class converts vectors of results from the generalized base to physical base and vice versa; - Load(): generic class representing a load; - LinearBearing(): Allows linear bearings to be treated as an external load. - HamonicLoad(): Integrator Harmonic Loading: Generic class represents a temporal integration scheme. - NewmarkIntegrator(): Integrator using the Newmark schema. - TransitSimulation(): Controls integration by building the load vector and archiving results. The result is the maximum displacement value in node N2Z1 as a function of time. 3 reference solution The reference solution is done by the old procedure for calculating rotating machines with the DYNA_VIBRA operator's transition with the data of the problem described above. > The maximum displacement in node N2Z1 is 2.6473318845597886e-05 (m). 4 Modelling 4.1 Mesh characteristics The mesh consists of 13 nodes, 12 mesh cells SEG2 and 1 mesh cell POI1. 4.2 Modelling characteristics With regard to the mesh, the tree line is modelled by elements beam type (POU_D_T) on linear segments (SEG2). The three bearings (supports) are modelled by discrete elements (DIS_TR). The disc is modeled by a nodal mass (element discreet DIS_TR) with moments of inertia in rotation. 5 Modelling results > The maximum displacement obtained by the test case is compared with the reference solution (test non-regression): | Max displacement | Reference | Code_Aster | Ratio error (%) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 2.647331884559E-05 | 2.64636281607E-05 | -0,0355 | Table 5-1 6 Summary of the results Perfectly accords the results Code_Aster with the reference values.

v1.01.351 ZZZZ351 – Validation of the ELIM_LAGR command v1.01.351 ZZZZ351 – Validation of the ELIM_LAGR command Summary: This test validates the ELIM_LAGR command, which allows the equations corresponding to dualised linear relationships to be removed in a matrix. v1.01.352 ZZZZ352 – Keyword validation SOLVEUR / ELIM_LAGR = 'OUI' v1.01.352 ZZZZ352 – Keyword validation SOLVEUR / ELIM_LAGR = 'OUI' Summary This test validates the keyword SOLVEUR / ELIM_LAGR = 'OUI' which allows the equations corresponding to the dualised linear relationships to be removed in a matrix, which sometimes makes the matrix defined positive. There are four modellings (A,B,C,D). 1 Test principle The problem is some very simple mechanical elastic problem. The kinematic boundary conditions are not trivial: there are relationships between several degrees of freedom. The reference calculation is obtained with the MUMPS solver and using ELIM_LAGR='NON' (default). The same calculation is done with ELIM_LAGR='OUI' and we check that we get the same result. The method of removing the Lagrange equations is described in R5.03.05 The validation is complete: - The method is checked for the correcting of the solution: MUMPS, LDLT and PETSC - The method is checked for non-homogenous linear relationships - It is checked that the solution is well reconstituted on all degrees of freedom, including the Lagrange degrees of freedom (use of the STAT_NON_LINE command). - The method is checked for operation on multiple processors (modellings C and D) 2 Summary of results The results are very good.

v1.01.359 ZZZZ359 – Validation of POST_CZM_FISS / OPTION macro-command = 'TRIAXIALITE' v1.01.359 ZZZZ359 – Validation of POST_CZM_FISS / OPTION macro-command = 'TRIAXIALITE' Summary This test validates the functionality available under keyword OPTION = 'TRIAXIALITE' of POST_CZM_FISS U4.86.02 Macro Command. In this case, the macro command provides a sized card with mesh cells number bearing cohesive elements (joint or interface), containing the value of the average triaxiality rate in the elements of the mass directly connected to each of these mesh cells. The objective is then to use this card as a control variable in the AFFE_MATERIAU (AFFE_VARC / CHAM_GD) U4.43.03 operator to vary the parameters of the cohesive law with triaxiality. This feature is valid on a simple uniaxial traction problem, for which one has a analytical solution: it is a linear elastic bar pressed in traction, at the center of which is arranged a discontinuity governed by cohesive behavior. For this material a zero Poisson's ratio is chosen to maintain a uniaxial state since the modellings of this test is performed in dimension 2 and 3. The two modellings of this test have the following characteristics: - Modelling A: 3D Modelling for the massif, 3D_INTERFACE Modelling for the cohesive interface, the bar is fully modelled; - Modelling B: D_PLAN Modelling for the massif, PLAN_JOINT Modelling for the cohesive interface, only half of the bar (symmetry condition) is modelled. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A one-dimensional \mathrm{2L}=199\mathit{mm} length bar is considered, at the centre of which is a discontinuity governed by cohesive behaviour. Figure 1.1-a : One-dimensional tensile bar The space variable is noted \widehat{x} , and the center of the bar is located by \widehat{x}=0 . 1.2 Material properties The behaviour of the massif is linear elastic: - Young's modulus: E=30000\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu =0 The cohesive behaviour is described by a softening affine law (CZM_TAC_MIX for interface elements used in Modelling A, and CZM_LIN_REG for joint elements used in Modelling B), with the following parameters: - Critical constraint: {\sigma}_{c}=3\mathit{MPa} - Breaking energy: {G}_{c}=0.1N/\mathit{mm} The values of the additional numerical parameters are as follows: - \text{PENA\_LAGR}=45000 for Modelling A (CZM_TAC_MIX) - \text{PENA\_ADHERENCE}={10}^{-4} for Modelling B (CZM_LIN_REG) Note: When only half the bar (as is the case for model B) is modelled by imposing a symmetry condition, the value of the breaking energy is divided by 2. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The problem is one-dimensional. The bar is pressed in traction, imposing the same U intensity displacement at each end. The displacement is increased by a ramp from U=0 to {U}_{\mathit{test}}=2L\frac{{\sigma}_{c}}{E}=0.0199\mathit{mm} 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation Notes: > u : displacement; > \sigma : constraint; > \epsilon : deformation; > \delta =⟦u⟧ : displacement jump through the cohesive discontinuity; > {\delta}_{c}=\frac{2{G}_{c}}{{\sigma}_{c}} : displacement jump corresponding to the breakage of the bar (zero stress). This is a analytical solution. The problem is one-dimensional, all the quantities are scalar and the constraint is constant in space. The problem is symmetrical and can therefore be restricted to the [0,L] interval. The following set of equations is available: In the bar: > \sigma =E\epsilon (eq1) > \frac{\mathit{du}}{d\widehat{x}}=\epsilon (eq2) In terms of discontinuity (cohesive affine law in softening regime): > \delta ={\delta}_{c}(1-\frac{\sigma}{{\sigma}_{c}}) (eq3) By integrating (eq2) on the [0,L] interval and using (eq1), the following relationship is obtained: > u(\widehat{x}=L)-u(\widehat{x}=0)=L\epsilon , i.e. U-\frac{\delta}{2}=L\frac{\sigma}{E} (eq4) {U}_{c} and {U}_{f} are noted as the required displacements corresponding to the stress levels {\sigma}_{c} (break-off threshold) and 0 (break-up material), respectively. > {U}_{c}=L\frac{{\sigma}_{c}}{E} et {U}_{f}=\frac{{\delta}_{c}}{2} (eq5) The values chosen for the material parameters E , {\sigma}_{c} and {G}_{c} , and for the length of the L bar, are assumed to lead to a stable response of the bar (no "snap-backs"). In addition, the hypothesis of a monotonous loading is increased, so {U}_{c}⩽U⩽{U}_{f} is in nonlinear mode. The values of the material and geometric parameters must therefore verify the following inequality: > L\frac{{\sigma}_{c}}{E} \sigma =\frac{\frac{{\delta}_{c}}{2}-U}{\frac{{\delta}_{c}}{2{\sigma}_{c}}-\frac{L}{E}},\forall U\in [\frac{L{\sigma}_{c}}{E},\frac{{\delta}_{c}}{2}] (eq7) 2.2 Quantities and reference results At the moment corresponding to the {U}_{\mathit{test}}=0.0199\mathit{mm} displacement, the \sigma (space constant) constraint and the u displacement to the point \widehat{x}={0}^{+} (half displacement jump) are tested. > \sigma =\frac{\frac{{\delta}_{c}}{2}-\mathrm{2L}\frac{{\sigma}_{c}}{E}}{\frac{{\delta}_{c}}{2{\sigma}_{c}}-\frac{L}{E}} digital application: \sigma =1.72344975053\mathit{MPa} > u(\widehat{x}={0}^{+})=2{\delta}_{c}(1-\frac{\sigma}{{\sigma}_{c}}) digital application: u(\widehat{x}={0}^{+})=0.0141838916607\mathit{mm} | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | | --- | --- | --- | | Under load {U}_{\mathit{test}}=0.0199\mathit{mm} , in total point: \sigma | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 1.72344975053\mathit{MPa} | | Under load {U}_{\mathit{test}}=0.0199\mathit{mm} , in \widehat{x}={0}^{+} : u | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 0.0141838916607\mathit{mm} | 3 Test principle The test consists of defining two \mathit{MAT1} and \mathit{MAT2} materials: - For \mathit{MAT1} , constant cohesive parameters are defined via DEFI_MATERIAU / RUPT_FRAG: \text{GC}={G}_{c} and \text{SIGM\_C}={G}_{c} ; - For \mathit{MAT2} , it is defined via DEFI_MATERIAU / RUPT_FRAG_FO that are cohesive parameters that are functions of triaxiality (noted \alpha ): \text{GC}=f(\alpha ).{G}_{c} and \text{SIGM\_C}=f(\alpha ).{G}_{c} ; In uniaxial traction the triaxiality is \alpha =1/3 , so we choose to define for \mathit{MAT2} a linear dependence on triaxiality with a slope of 3 : f(\alpha )=3\alpha . In this way: the values of the parameters of the cohesive law in \mathit{MAT2} must remain constant and identical to those chosen in \mathit{MAT1} throughout the load history. The test shall then be conducted as follows: 1. \mathit{MAT1} material definition; 2. first call to STAT_NON_LINE with \mathit{MAT1} up to a required displacement level below {U}_{\mathit{test}} ; 3. call POST_CZM_FISS on the mechanical result previously obtained; 4. \mathit{MAT2} material definition by using the triaxiality board obtained with POST_CZM_FISS as the control variable; 5. with the material \mathit{MAT1} , further calculation with STAT_NON_LINE from the mechanical state obtained at point 2 to the loading {U}_{\mathit{test}} ; 6. with the material \mathit{MAT2} , further calculation with STAT_NON_LINE from the mechanical state obtained at point 2 to the loading {U}_{\mathit{test}} . v1.01.360 ZZZZ360 - Validation of the MODI_MAILLAGE / ABSC_CURV command v1.01.360 ZZZZ360 - Validation of the MODI_MAILLAGE / ABSC_CURV command Summary: This computer test validates the programming of the ABSC_CURV keyword of the MODI_MAILLAGE command. The mesh forms an "open" line (with 2 ends: N1 and N13). The nodes are all in the XOY plan. There are 13 nodes. nodes N2, N3, ..., N12 are located on a portion (270 degrees) of the O-centered 1-ray circle. They are not equidistant. The mesh is made up of 2 SEG2, 2 SEG3, 2 SEG4 and 3 POI1. The orientation of certain segments is voluntarily "turned". Since nodes is almost all located on the same circle, it is easy to calculate their curvilinear abscisses by hand. This allows the TOUS curvilinear abscisses to be validated as nodes as TOUS as elements (POI1, SEG2, SEG3 and SEG4). This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.361 ZZZZ361 - Degenerate cutting case for elements XFEM 3D quadratic v1.01.361 ZZZZ361 - Degenerate cutting case for elements XFEM 3D quadratic Summary: In this test case, it is proposed to check the smoothness of the specific volume cutting cases in the quadratic XFEM frame. In three-dimensional XFEM, the finished elements "parents" through the crack are cut into "children" tetrahedrons which are then re-cut into sub-tetrahedras to be consistent with discontinuity. There are in total five configurations of the "children" tetrahedrons cut into subtetrahedras ( cf. R7.02.12), distinguished by the number of nodes apex of the child tetrahedron for which the "lsn cancels (npts) and the number of intersection points between the surface lsn =0 and the edges of the child tetrahedron. However, degenerate "scratch" configurations exist. These degenerate configurations are easily resembled to the classical cutting configurations. The six degenerate configurations (modellings A to F) for which the surface lsn=0 shaves the surface of the child tetrahedron are examined and which occur only in quadratic XFEM. These situations occur when one or more edges of the child tetrahedron have exactly 2 points such as lsn=0 (necessarily one end and the mid-node based on the adjustment of the level set in the quadratic case). Finally, in model G, the case of undegenerated cutting for which the surface lsn=0 shaves one of the edges of the tetrahedron is studied. 1 Reference problem A unique reference element tetraedric is being worked on in Figure . v1.01.362 ZZZZ362 - Checking the consistency of the fields produced by the X-FEM sub-cut v1.01.362 ZZZZ362 - Checking the consistency of the fields produced by the X-FEM sub-cut Summary This test has no physical significance, it is a computer test. The fields produced by the X-FEM sub-cut correspond to the cam_elem produced by the TOPOSE and TOPOFA calculation options, and stored in the D4.10.02 sd_modele_xfem. The size of these cam_elems must be done in the same way for all elements X-FEM belonging to the same category "topological". v1.01.363 ZZZZ363 – Dynamic damage to AXIS-cut test piece v1.01.363 ZZZZ363 – Dynamic damage to AXIS-cut test piece Summary: This test represents a dynamic damage calculation of a cut-out test piece. It allows the validation of GRAD_VARI Modelling to axisymmetric, which allows for the calculation of damage regulated by the gradient of damage, taking into account degrees of freedom displacement and damage to nodes. GRAD_VARI Modelling performs a local resolution, Gauss points by Gauss points. AXIS_GRAD_VARI Modelling is valid for constitutive law ENDO_SCALAIRE. Modelling and constitutive laws Endoming Tested: - Model A : AXIS_GRAD_VARI Modelling with constitutive law ENDO_SCALAIRE 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A 10\mathit{dm} height cut test piece is considered. 3\mathit{dm} width and 1\mathit{dm} radius of ENT. Figure 1: Promotion of the problem 1.2 Common properties of the material The material is assimilated to concrete (decipemetric scale is used): Elastic characteristics: > E=3.E10\text{Pa}=3.E8{\text{N/dm}}^{2} > \nu =0.2 Tensile strength of the damage law: > \mathit{SY}=3.E4{\text{N/dm}}^{2}=3.E6\text{Pa} Energy restitution rate per crack surface (Griffith constant): > {G}_{f}=10\text{N/dm}=100{\text{J/m}}^{2} Density: > \mathit{Rho}=2300\mathit{Kg}/{m}^{3}=2.3\mathit{Kg}/{\mathit{dm}}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Block : \mathrm{DX}=0 on nodes that belong to the symmetry axis ( x=0. ), to ensure the structure is maintained (in red on Figure 1). Loading : The upper and lower parts of the cut test piece are moved (in green on Figure 1). 2 reference solution This test case is a case of non-regression. This is a study, which quickly changes from a weakly damaged state to a state of rupture (damage equal to 1). The loads are not analytical. The values of the imposed displacements are simply empirical. Similarly, associated damage values are found which are not exact values. With no reference value for this type of Modelling, this test case is checked only for non-regression of the code. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics A model of damage GRAD_VARI, which is a mixed Lagrangian formulation of damage regulated by the gradient of damage, is considered. It takes into account in addition the degrees of freedom of displacement and damage to the nodes, the coeficients of Lagrange. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains 1034 elements TRIA6 and 462 elements QUAD8. The mesh at the centre of the test piece is oriented out of symmetry. Figure 2 : Representation of mesh 3.3 Damage law: material ENDO_SCALAIRE Standard concrete characteristics are defined above. Characteristics related to the non-local damage law: c=1.875\text{N};p=1.5;m=10 which corresponds to the damage area \mathrm{1D} equal to D=0.5\text{dm} The correspondence with physical parameters is as follows: c=3/8D{G}_{f};m=\frac{3E{G}_{f}}{2D\cdot {\mathit{SY}}^{2}};p=m/4-1; 3.4 Boundary conditions and loads Charge : A normal -5\mathit{SY}/E=-5E-04 displacement speed is imposed on the upper part and +5\mathit{SY}/E=5e-04 on the lower part of the cut-out swab so that the test piece works in compression. The load on the required displacement is applied during 1.2\mathit{sec} . 3.5 Tested quantities and results This test case is only validated in non-regression: - Non-regression on the point \text{P\_HAUT} move test. - Non-regression test on point stress field of gauss 1 of mesh cell \mathit{M160} . - Non-regression test on the point forced field of gauss 1 of the mesh cell \mathit{M1324} . - Non-regression test on maximum stress in test piece. - Non-regression test on the nodal reaction to point \text{P\_HAUT} . 4 Summary of the results This test allows to check in non-regression: - AXIS_GRAD_VARI Modelling with constitutive law ENDO_SCALAIRE dynamic.

v1.01.364 ZZZZ364 - Validation of large rotations v1.01.364 ZZZZ364 - Validation of large rotations Summary: This test allows you to check the correct consideration of large rotations by some modellings Code_Aster that can take them into account: '3D', 'COQUE_3D', 'POU_D_T_GD', 'POU_D_EM', 'POU_D_TGM'. 1 Test principle The model (consisting of mesh cells 3D, or mesh cells hull or mesh cells beam) is subject to a shift imposed on a part of its edge (there is no load of "force" type). Since the required displacement corresponds to a simple rotation of the edge, the complete solution is also the imposed rotation. The structure does not deform, its state of constraint is zero. The modellings tested are those that accept large rotations: 3D, COQUE_3D, POU_D_T_GD, POU_D_EM et POU_D_TGM For the three modellings structure (which have rotation ddls), it is It is interesting to see how large rotations "compose". rotations are not additive quantities. For this, the required displacement is broken down into 4 steps: - a phi0 angle rotation around Oz between 0 and 1. - a phi0 angle rotation around Oy between moments 1. and 2. - a phi0 angle rotation around Ox between moments 2. and 3. - rotation to return to the initial position. 1.1 Baseline, validation The displacement solution is known: it is the forced rotation. The stress solution is known: a zero stress state. For displacement, the U - Uref field is checked for a maximum and a minimum of zero. 2 Observations - It is difficult to converge this calculation for all modellings and for a large phi0 angle. That's why the phi0 angle and the time step cutting are chosen differently for each model. - The modellings POU_D_EM and POU_D_TGM are frankly put into default on this test (error > 100%). This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.365 ZZZZ365 - Validation of SIEF_R(3D) to SIEF_R(DKT) v1.01.365 ZZZZ365 - Validation of SIEF_R(3D) to SIEF_R(DKT) Summary: This test validates the transformation of an SIEF_R field of type ELNO or NOEU calculated on elements density to superfacial elements. The SIEF_R(3D) is passed to the SIEF_R(DKT) by 2 commands: - PROJ_CHAMP: SIEF_R(3D) field projection on subpoints of the overfacial elements, without changing the reference point of the input field. - MODI_REPERE with GLOBAL_UTIL option: change of reference from the input field. The field moves from the global reference to the local reference point linked to the superfacial elements. The orientation of the superfacial elements is given by AFFE_CARA_ELEM with ORIENTATION option. 1 Test principle Validation shall consist of: - define a field of SIEF_R using linear formulae depending on space. - affect the SIEF_R field on a mesh d的elements density. - Use PROJ_CHAMP to project the SIEF_R(3D) field to obtain a global SIEF_R(DKT_) field on the subpoints of the superfacial elements. Be careful that this field is in the same reference as the initial field (so the global reference), so it does not correspond to a superfacial SIEF_Rd-element field that must be expressed in the local reference. - compare the SIEF_R(DKT_ global) field to a field calculated at subpoints using the formulae previously defined, these 2 fields are expressed in the same reference. - use MODI_REPERE to change the reference to the SIEF_R(DKT_) field, by placing it in the local elements superfacial marker and getting a real SIEF_R(DKT). - compare the SIEF_R(DKT) field to a field calculated at subpoints using formulae previously defined but expressed in the local elements surfacic benchmark. 2 Modelling A The results are analytical. Tests are performed on all components of the SIEF_R fields, on the greater absolute value of the differences between the solution calculated by Code_Aster and the one calculated in the command file. In theory the difference must be zero, in practice the default value is retained.

v1.01.368 PLEXU08 - Validation of new CALC_EUROPLEXUS features v1.01.368 PLEXU08 - Validation of new CALC_EUROPLEXUS features Summary: During the CALC_EUROPLEXUS redesign project new features were added to the macro-command. The list of these additions is as follows: - new constitutive law: VMIS_ISOT_TRAC(modelization A), - new load: required displacements (DDL_IMPO) other than blockages (modelling B), - new Modelling: 3D on mesh cells HEXA8 and TETRA4 support. v1.01.370 PLEXU10 - Validation of slippery and rubbing cables in CALC_EUROPLEXUS v1.01.370 PLEXU10 - Validation of slippery and rubbing cables in CALC_EUROPLEXUS Summary: Mechanisms to model slippery and rubbing cables have been added to EUROPLEXUS. This series of tests validates the call of CALC_EUROPLEXUS to these prestressed features calculated in Code_Aster or not, but also directly participates in their validations in EUROPLEXUS. Slippering cables: The Modelling of slippery cables is done only by a restraint ( LCAB GLIS ). This restraint, inspired by RELA_CINE_BP loading, calculates the kinematic relationships between concrete and cable by leaving the movement of each node cable in the tangent direction to the trajectory of the cable. To take into account the large deformations and slippages, this restraint is updated to each time step. Rubbing cables: The Modelling of the rubbing cables is done using the same restraint as for slippery cables. Specific discrete elements are used to model friction. restraints should also be made on the nodes of the non-common discrete elements with elements cables. This restraint is enabled by the LCAB FROT syntax . Model A: Validation of the call to restraint EPX LCAB GLIS (reproduction of the test bm_str_lcab_glis). Model B: Validation of the correct consideration of an initial prestress status with the restraint LCAB GLIS . Model C: Tensioning of a slippery cable in EPX (reference Code_Aster). Modelling D: Validation of the call to restraint EPX LCAB FROT , (reproduction of the test bm_str_lcab_frot_amor). This test is part of the validation of LCAB FROT in EPX, it provides a reference value for a tensioning of a rubbing cable with an anchoring rearward. Modelling E: Reproduction of the test bm_str_lcab_frot Model F: Validation of Code_Aster/EPX chaining with rubbing cables. 1 Description 1.1 Geometry, mesh and model The design of the study is a portion of H=2m R=10m R=10m \mathit{ep}=1m \mathit{ep}=1m \mathit{ep}=1m R=10m R=10m \mathit{ep}=1m \mathit{ep}=1m \mathit{ep}=1m x>0 x>0 x>0 x>0 x>0 x>0 3m 3m 3m x>0 x>0 3m 3m 3m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m \mathit{ex}=0,4m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m 3m Xk4 The concrete is modeled in shell (element Q4GG). From this field at Gauss points (SIEF_ELGA) the field was calculated at the corresponding nodes (SIEF_NOEU). The first node cable from the node ANCR2 with the updated Y coordinate was then detected in the 0.06s time field of movement, and the first node cable from the node ANCR2 was physically not removed from the concrete during this voltage phase. The value of the voltage to be applied in Code_Aster is the nodes field of stress at this node. Contrary to what one might think, the anchoring step to apply in Code_Aster is not 0.2m but 0.116m. Indeed, the anchoring step should not be calculated from the node ANCR2 but from the last node still included in the concrete following the initial phase. The value of 0.116m is then obtained. 5.3 Comparison of voltage profiles The analysis in EPX is given here: In the initial phase of tensioning, we see that the curves are almost perfectly superimposed for curvilinear abscisses greater than about 20.0 m. By printing the value of curvatures in each node calculated in EPX, we found that some values in the middle of the cable were quite different from the others, whereas in the circular part the curvature must be the same in each point. This is probably the result of very slight impreciseness in the mesh at this level. Code_Aster does not see it because it uses a spline method that interpolates the trajectory of the cable globally while in EPX one simply interpolates the trajectory locally. Concerning the anchoring step, there are slightly larger differences but the curves are parallel on this part. The differences can arise from a consideration of friction on nodes normally removed from concrete or from the interpretation of the node reference for determining the anchoring step to be applied in Code_Aster. 5.4 Tested quantities and results Maximum the difference voltage profiles of Code_Aster and EPX are tested at the end of the initial voltage and anchoring phases. | Instant | Maximum difference | | --- | --- | | 0.06 | 0.0447086123078 | | 0.12 | 0.0605346658829 | 6 Modelling E This test reproduces the EPX bm_str_lcab_frot bench. v1.01.380 ZZZZ380 - Adding fictitious degrees of freedom for multigrill solvers v1.01.380 ZZZZ380 - Adding fictitious degrees of freedom for multigrill solvers Summary: This test shows the value of adding fictitious degrees of freedom when using PETS c multigrill solvers and dualized kinematic conditions requiring the use of the ELIM_LAGR='OUI' keyword. 1 Test principle: A simple mechanical problem with boundary conditions type LIAISON_MAIL is solved. The dualization of these boundary conditions prevents the use of multigrill solvers of PETS c (because of the degrees of freedom of Lagrange). So you have to use the ELIM_LAGR='OUI' feature. But the code, to eliminate each degree of freedom from Lagrange is forced to eliminate a physical degree of freedom. Ultimately, some nodes have less degrees of freedom than others, which theoretically prevents the efficient use of multigrill solvers. In this case, the code adds fictitious degrees of freedoms so that all nodess in the model have the same number of degrees of freedoms and can be used more efficiently with 'GAMG', 'BOOMER' and 'ML' solvers. This test shows that this strategy is interesting: the number of iterations to converge is very much reduced by adding fictitious degrees of freedom: | Solver | BOOMER | ML | GAMG | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Without degrees of freedom | 375 | 38 | 478 | | With degrees of fictitious freedom | 50 | 24 | 41 | This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.391 PLEXU09 – Validation of VMIS_JOHN_COOK in CALC_EUROPLEXUS v1.01.391 PLEXU09 – Validation of VMIS_JOHN_COOK in CALC_EUROPLEXUS Summary: This test validates the use of constitutive law VMIS_JOHN_COOK in CALC_EUROPLEXUS. It also validates VARI_INT ='OUI' functionality of ETAT_INIT and the use outside CALC_EUROPLEXUS of LIRE_EUROPLEXUS macro-command. Modelling A: Reproducing the EPX test bm_ini_med_ecro_vmjc that validates the inclusion of internal variables in the initial state (from Code_Aster) for VMIS_JOHN_COOK law (VMJC from EPX). Modelling B: non-regression test to validate the correct translation of material parameters. 1 Details on Internal Variable Transformations for VMIS_JOHN_COOK Law 1.1 Description Internal variables of Code_Aster are noted with the suffix V and internal variables of EPX with the suffix ECR followed by the component number. 1.1.1 Code_Aster VMIS_JOHN_COOK law in Code_Aster has 5 internal variables. | V1 | EPSPEQ | Cumulative equivalent plastic deformation (deviatoric) | | --- | --- | --- | | V2 | INDIPLAS | Plasticity indicator (0: threshold not reached, 1 or > 1: threshold reached) | | V3 | DEPSPEQ | Equal plastic deformation increment | | V4 | DINSTM | Time increment | | V5 | DDISSM | Mechanical dissipation speed | 1.1.2 EPX EPX VMJC Law has 8 internal variables. Here is the information from the EPX documentation: | ECR1 | current hydrostatic pressure | | --- | --- | | ECR2 | current equivalent stress (Von Mises) | | ECR3 | current equivalent plastic train | | ECR4 | current yield stress | | ECR5 | sound speed | | ECR6 | equivalent train rate (Von Mises) | | ECR7 | failure flag (0=virgin Gauss Point, 1=failed Gauss Point) | | ECR8 | damage parameter for the Johnson-Cook criteria | 1.2 Code_Aster to EPX 1.2.1 ECR1 The stress matrix trace is calculated using CALC_CHAMP/CHAM_UTIL/CRITERE = 'TRACE' on the SIEF_ELGA field. The value obtained for each Gauss point is then divided by 3 to obtain \mathit{ECR1} . 1.2.2 ECR2 \mathit{ECR2} corresponds to the \mathit{VMIS} component of the SIEQ_ELGA field. 1.2.3 ECR3 \mathit{ECR3} corresponds to the \mathit{V1} component of the VARI_ELGA field. 1.2.4 ECR4 \mathit{ECR4} corresponds to the \mathit{VMIS} component of the SIEQ_ELGA field, which is added to the epsilon equal to 10E-6 . This choice was made as part of Emricka Julan's thesis. It allows calculations with VMJC law to work with the given initial state. 1.2.5 ECR5 \mathit{ECR5} : value set to 0. because calculated entirely by EPX at each moment. 1.2.6 ECR6 This value corresponds to a deformation speed that is still zero at the end of a static calculation, so it is set to 0. because it is not intended to give an initial state from a dynamic calculation to CALC_EUROPLEXUS. 1.2.7 ECR7 et ECR8 These two variables are only for the breaker mechanics. They are set to 0. . 1.3 EPX to Code_Aster Transformations during this passage can only be made from values present in the field of internal variables from EPX. For this law, the transformation consists only of putting the \mathit{ECR3} component into \mathit{V1} and putting the other 4 components into 0. . 2 Modelling A 2.1 Purpose The purpose of this test is to validate the sending and transformation (for VMIS_JOHN_COOK law) of an internal variable field in the initial state of an EPX calculation via CALC_EUROPLEXUS. It also validates the transformation of internal variables in the EPX direction to Code_Aster for VMIS_JOHN_COOK law and the use of LIRE_EUROPLEXUS outside of CALC_EUROPLEXUS. 2.2 Description This test is the equivalent of the EPX bm_ini_med_ecro_vmjc "bench". It is a single element cube. The bottom side is clamped and a load (displaced on X) is applied to the top side. This calculation is done with the STAT_NON_LINE operator to produce an initial state for EPX calculation. CALC_EUROPLEXUS is then launched with this initial state (movements + stresses + internal variables) and without additional loading than those that were able to obtain the initial state. It is then checked that the internal variables in the initial and final state are the same as in bm_ini_med_ecro_vmjc with the keyword COURBE (and TEST_TABLE) and that the internal variables recovered by Code_Aster at the end of the calculation are the ones expected. Internal variables should not normally evolve since no additional loading has been added. However, some components that do not depend on calculated values are recalculated completely by EPX at each iteration. This is the case with ECR5. 2.3 Validation principle Comparison with test case EPX or analytical references. 2.4 Test values In this first table of internal variable numbers are those of EPX. | mesh cell | Instant | Component | Point | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | M1 | | \mathit{V1}=\mathit{ECR1} | 1 | 4.078819E+2 | 1E-4 | | M1 | | \mathit{V2}=\mathit{ECR2} | 2 | 1.420337E+2 | 1E-4 | | M1 | | \mathit{V3}=\mathit{ECR3} | 3 | 5.773488E-3 | 1E-4 | | M1 | | \mathit{V4}=\mathit{ECR4} | 4 | 1.561430E+2 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V1}=\mathit{ECR1} | 1 | 4.078819E+2 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V2}=\mathit{ECR2} | 2 | 1.420337E+2 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V3}=\mathit{ECR3} | 3 | 5.773488E-3 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V4}=\mathit{ECR4} | 4 | 1.561430E+2 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V5}=\mathit{ECR5} | 5 | 4019.1847623425019 | 1E-4 | The value of the internal variables in the Aster output result of CALC_EUROPLEXUS is then tested. | mesh cell | Instant | Component | Point | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | M1 | | \mathit{V1} | 3 | 5.773488E-3 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V1} | 3 | 5.773488E-3 | 1E-4 | Finally, the value of the internal variables is tested in the Aster output result of LIRE_EUROPLEXUS. | mesh cell | Instant | Component | Point | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | M1 | | \mathit{V1} | 3 | 5.773488E-3 | 1E-4 | | M1 | 0.004 | \mathit{V1} | 3 | 5.773488E-3 | 1E-4 | 3 Modelling B 3.1 Purpose Modelling A does not ensure that the material parameters have been correctly translated. v1.01.392 ZZZZ392 – Validation of the CREA_RESU-based mode_meca concept for COMB_SISM_MODAL/MODE_CORR v1.01.392 ZZZZ392 – Validation of the CREA_RESU-based mode_meca concept for COMB_SISM_MODAL/MODE_CORR Summary: This test has no physical meaning, it is essentially a computer test. It is designed to validate keyword AXE from CREA_RESU/AFFE. This keyword is designed to provide MODE_CORR's COMB_SISM_MODAL operating unit with a mode_meca concept from CREA_RESU instead of a mode_meca concept from MODE_STATIQUE. Modelization A: The test principle is as follows: using the CREA_CHAMP operator, we extract the moving field of a MODE_STATIQUE mode_mecassusin concept(there are 3 order numbers each corresponding to a direction of space). We create a mode_meca concept from the extracted field with CREA_RESU, by telling keyword AXE of AFFE. It takes the valueX for the first order number, Yfor the second and Zfor the third. For the 3 directions of space, the COMB_SISM_MODAL operator is called twice, the first time by telling the concept from MODE_STATIQUE to MODE_CORR, this calculation being used as a reference and a second time with the concept from CREA_RESU. We check that we get the same results as in the first. It is specified that the second calculations do not work without providing keyword AXE CREA_RESU/AFFE. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.01.394 ZZZZ394 – PRE_EPSI Check v1.01.394 ZZZZ394 – PRE_EPSI Check Summary: This test has no physical meaning, it is essentially a computer test. It aims to validate PRE_EPSI loading for 3 possible types of assignments: - by direct assignment under keyword PRE_EPSI (via EPXX, EPYY, ...) - creating a card via CREA_CHAMP, taken into account via keyword EPSI from PRE_ESPI - by providing a deformation field from another calculation (via EPSI also) The principle is the following, a PRE_EPSI load is applied to an mesh cell whose only rigid body movements are blocked. v1.01.399 ZZZZ399 – Frequency of a quantum harmonic oscillator to one dimension v1.01.399 ZZZZ399 – Frequency of a quantum harmonic oscillator to one dimension Summary: The objective of this test is to calculate the frequencies of a quantum harmonic oscillator 1 one dimension, for the stationary solution. https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscillateur_harmonique_quantique 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The problem, while one-dimensional, is modelled in two dimensions (there is currently no 1D Modelling for Code_Aster thermic). For reasons of scale, the Atomic Units System 2 is used. https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syst%C3%A8me_d%27unit%C3%A9s_atomiques . A L=10,0{a}_{0} length and L/100{a}_{0} thickness band, centred at the origin of the axes, are considered to represent space. A charged particle (in this case, an electron), subject to a potential, can assume only specific energy values, which can be obtained by resolution of the Schroedinger equation: -\frac{{\hslash }^{2}}{\mathrm{2m}}\frac{{d}^{2}}{{\mathit{dx}}^{2}}{\psi}_{n}(x)+\frac{1}{2}{\mathit{kx}}^{2}{\psi}_{n}(x)={E}_{n}{\psi}_{n}(x) n=0,1,\cdots \omega =\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} This is a problem with its own functions. https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fonction_propre : you must find the values {E}_{n} (autovalues). The equation is diffusion-like (in analogy to the calculation of thermal equilibrium), the resolution of the functions of the individual will be done by a modal calculation. 1.2 Materials The test uses two materials: one for the resolution of the diffusion equation ( \lambda =1,{\rho}_{\mathit{cp}}=1 ) and the other for the potential, with {\rho}_{\mathit{cp}} variable depending on a value of a field, calculated with the potential formula. 1.3 boundary conditions The zero value is imposed on the domain's extremes. There is no real need for this condition, which is set to test this data set as well but which can be removed without modification. 1.4 Initial conditions None. None None 2 reference solution An exact solution is known for this problem: {E}_{n}=(n+\frac{1}{2})\hslash \omega 2.1 Bibliographical references 1. ATKINS P.W. Molecular Quantum Mechanics 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics PLAN modelling is used. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains 212 elements of type TRIA8. 3.3 Tested quantities and results Energy values calculated from the modal calculation "frequency" are tested in relation to the exact solution. | Location | Reference type | VALE_REFE | P decision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Difference between analytical solution () and calculation | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 0 | 5.0E-4 | 4 Summary of the results Here is a visualization of the actual part of the calculated clean functions. The SIEF_ELGA stress field is recovered at Gauss points in the 'EVOL_NOLI' data structure read in MED format. The direction of the gravity is y . We select a particular moment. v1.01.418 ZZZZ418 – Multilayer and multifibre elements: verification of values at subpoints v1.01.418 ZZZZ418 – Multilayer and multifibre elements: verification of values at subpoints Summary: This test validates the values extracted from the integration subpoints. All subpoint values are tested. 1 Reference problem A SEG3 between the nodes P0, P1. the node mid P2. P0=(0.0;0.0;0.0) P1=(3.0;0.0;0.0) P2=(1.5;0.0;0.0) 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The elements pipe supports are SEG3. - The position of the integration points along the SEG3 is given in R3.01.01 # Coordonnées des Points de Gauss sur l'axe X long_poutre = 3.0 xpg = (1.0 / 3.0) 0.5 points_gauss = (long_poutre (1.0 + xpg) 0.5, long_poutre (1.0 - xpg) 0.5) - The coordinates of the integration subpoints are based on the number of layers, the number of sectors and of course the diameter and thickness of the pipe. # Coordonnées des Sous-Points !!! def coord_fibre(ifib): Rint = Rext - Ep # index des coordonnées numAng = ((ifib - 1) % (2 Nsect + 1)) / (2.0 Nsect) numCou = ((ifib - 1) // (2 Nsect + 1)) / (2.0 Ncou) y = (Rint + Ep numCou) np.cos(2.0 np.pi numAng) z = -(Rint + Ep numCou) np.sin(2.0 np.pi numAng) if abs(y) < 1.0e-08: y = 0.0 if abs(z) < 1.0e-08: z = 0.0 return y, z où : - Rext and Ep are the external radius and the pipe thickness, indicated in the AFFE_CARA_ELEM control, respectively. - Nsect and Ncou are the number of sectors and layers, respectively, specified in the AFFE_CARA_ELEM command. CAREL = AFFE_CARA_ELEM( MODELE=MODELE, POUTRE=( _F( SECTION="CERCLE", GROUP_MA="TUBE", CARA=("R", "EP"), VALE=(Rext, Ep), TUYAU_NSEC=Nsect, TUYAU_NCOU=Ncou, ), ), ORIENTATION=_F(CARA="GENE_TUYAU", GROUP_NO="ENC", VALE=(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)), ) For P0P1 hose the (x,y,z) coordinates of ifib fiber for point ipt are given by: xx = points_gauss[ipt] yy, zz = coord_fibre(ifib) 2.2 Quantities and reference results The values are assigned to the sub-points by: - CALC_CHAM_ELEM: calculation of the coordinates of subpoints. - CREA_CHAMP, option AFFE: create a function field. - CREA_CHAMP, option EVAL: function evaluation at subpoint coordinates. - CREA_CHAMP, option ASSE: definition of the constraint field. - CREA_RESU: Create a result containing the constraint field. Quantities are then tested using TEST_TABLE. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution None, exact solution. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics The mesh of the pipes is composed of an mesh cell type SEG3. 3.2 Modelling characteristics Definition of the model: MODELE = AFFE_MODELE( MAILLAGE=MAIL, AFFE=_F(GROUP_MA="TUBE", PHENOMENE="MECANIQUE", MODELISATION="TUYAU_3M") ) Assignment of characteristics: - Strip and thickness of pipe - Number of sectors and number of layers CAREL = AFFE_CARA_ELEM( MODELE=MODELE, POUTRE=( _F( SECTION="CERCLE", GROUP_MA="TUBE", CARA=("R", "EP"), VALE=(Rext, Ep), TUYAU_NSEC=Nsect, TUYAU_NCOU=Ncou, ), ), ORIENTATION=_F(CARA="GENE_TUYAU", GROUP_NO="ENC", VALE=(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)), ) 3.3 Test values and results All values assigned to subpoints are tested. A extraction is performed in a particular point using POST_CHAMP and recorded in a table using CREA_TABLE. The value of all components is tested including the coordinates. 4 Summary of the results This test is to verify that quantities at the TUYAU_3M model integration subpoints are extracted well.

v1.02.101 SSEP001 - Limit load calculation of a tube with sub-thickness v1.02.101 SSEP001 - Limit load calculation of a tube with sub-thickness Summary In this test, the limit load of a tube with sub-thickness is calculated. The limit load is calculated in two different ways: 1. By a static approach that allows the calculation of the load that corresponds to the solution of free plastic flow. This approach allows to calculate from inside a minor of the limit load. Simply raise the value of ETA_PILOTAGE from the moment this value stabilizes. 2. By a kinematic approach regulated by the Norton-Hoff-Friaâ method, which uses incompressible elements. It is based on a static linear resolution and parametric control. An post-processing with the POST_ELEM command allows to obtain the upper and lower terminal estimates of the limit load. This test case is used to check the validity of the command files corresponding to the lower and upper limit load of both cases of a tube with sub-thickness. The sub-thickness is defined from the measurement points recorded on site. Modelling A: - Calculation of the lower limit load. Modelling B: - Calculation of the upper limit load. This documentation is deliberately succinct.

v1.02.202 RTOOL01 – Release of DDL s on SMART with Rtool v1.02.202 RTOOL01 – Release of DDL s on SMART with Rtool Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the kinematic relationships produced by the Rtool tool of salome_meca. This tool, allows to easily release rotational degrees of freedom (DDL) between two elements structures. The modal analysis of the model of the reinforced concrete building carried out during the SMART2013 (Seismic design and best-estimate Methods Assessment of Reinforced concrete buildings subject to Torsion and non-linear effects) campaign conducted by the CEA and EDF. This campaign focuses on the seismic study of irregular reinforced concrete buildings whose response is strongly affected by the torsion movements of the whole. The model represents an electric concrete building reinforced with three floors on a 1/4 scale. It is carried out in the law of similarity of Cauchy-Froud (i.e. the eigenfrequencies increased by a ratio 2). The objective is to perform modal analysis under different release and orientation configurations, and to compare the first three eigenfrequencies obtained. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The model model model is modeled at the 1/4th scale of a typical nuclear facility building. It consists of three V01/02 V03 and V04 U-shaped sails and three trapezoidal floors. Openings are pierced in the V01/02 and V03 sails. Each floor is supported by a horizontal beam as well as a vertical pole. The model is asymmetrical to facilitate twisting movements. The geometrical characteristics of the model are presented on the and on the. Figure 1.1-1: Dimensions de la maquette Smart 2013 (High elevation view – Dimensions in mm) Figure 1.1-2: Dimensions de la maquette Smart 2013 (Plan view – Dimensions in mm) 1.2 Material properties The material is elastic isotropic with the following properties: - E=30000\mathit{MPa} - \nu =0.3 - \rho =2500\mathit{kg}/m\mathrm{³} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Boundary conditions are clamped supports at the base of the model (including the pole). By comparing different modellings, you just need to make sure that these boundary conditions are equal in all modellings. For this reason, the representation of the vibrating table is not necessary and you can simplify the model with a clamped support under the base. 1.4 Initial conditions None. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation This analysis consists of 5 modellings: • Modelization A : In this Modelling the first three frequencies are calculated on the original mesh. These values are used as a reference to verify the operation of the Rtool tool; • Modelization B : In this Modelling the first three eigenfrequencies will be calculated on a modified mesh. Rotation will be released on an internal node of the pole. It will be released node/node; • Modelization C : In this Modelling the first three frequencies are calculated on a modified mesh. Rotation on the three restraintss between poles and floors will be released. It will be node/plane release; • Modelization D : In this Modelling the first three frequencies are calculated on a modified mesh. Rotation will be released on the common stops between sails and floors. It will be a plan/plan release; • Modelling E : In this Modelling, before releasing DDL as in D Modelling, a rigid rotation of mesh is made according to the global axes X, Y and Z. Then, the operations performed in the Modelling D are repeated. This last study will confirm the correct writing of kinematic relations by the Rtool tool. 2.2 Quantities and reference results As already mentioned, A Modelling gives us a reference for modellings B, C, D . The simple release of DDL results in a change of stiffness, which causes a change in the model's eigenmodes and frequencies. Furthermore, the relaxation is done in directions parallel to the global axes, this allows to verify the kinematic relationships produced by the Rtool tool. In order to test the tool in a more complex case, a rotation of the model is performed for the model E . Once the rotation is carried out on the three main axes (rotation of 35° around the X axis, 50° around the Y axis and 65° around the Z axis), a new calculation of the eigenfrequencies is made, after having released the DDL sails/floors. In this case, the verification of the kinematic relations produced by Rtool is much more complex, but a simple comparison with the D Modelling is sufficient to verify the writing of the kinematic relations produced by the Rtool tool. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution Completely digital solutions and comparison. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The reinforced concrete walls and floors are modeled by elements plates DKT. The reinforced concrete is modeled with a simple elastic law. The beams and poles are modeled by elements POU_D_E. These are considered elastic. The sole is modeled by elements 3D and is considered elastic. Depreciation is not considered in modelling. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains about 2600 mesh cells and 2700 nodes (without considering the sole). The mesh is the SMART model. Figure 3.2-1: Maillage de la maquette SMART 3.3 Tested quantities and results The first three frequencies are calculated from modal analysis. A simple non-regression test is done. | Frequences | Reference values | | --- | --- | | First eigenfrequency | 29,1856 Hz | | 2nd eigenfrequency | 37,2940Hz | | 3rd eigenfrequency | 66,3803 Hz | 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics The reinforced concrete walls and floors are modeled by elements plates DKT. The reinforced concrete is modeled with a simple elastic law. The beams and poles are modeled by elements POU_D_E. These are considered elastic. The sole is modeled by elements 3D and is considered elastic. Depreciation is not considered in modelling. In this Modelling a rotational DDL is released on a node of the pole (relay node/node). 4.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains about 2600 mesh cells and 2700 nodes (without considering the sole). The mesh is the SMART model. 4.3 Tested quantities and results The first three frequencies are calculated from modal analysis. A simple non-regression test is done. 4.4 Remarks The release causes a slight change in the values of the eigenfrequencies. 5 Modelling C 5.1 Modelling characteristics The reinforced concrete walls and floors are modeled by elements plates DKT. The reinforced concrete is modeled with a simple elastic law. The beams and poles are modeled by elements POU_D_E. These are considered elastic. The sole is modeled by elements 3D and is considered elastic. Depreciation is not considered in modelling. In this Modelling rotational DDLs are released to the nodes common between poles and floors (relay node/plane). 5.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains about 2600 mesh cells and 2700 nodes (without considering the sole). The mesh is the SMART model. 5.3 Tested quantities and results The first three frequencies are calculated from modal analysis. A simple non-regression test is done. 5.4 Remarks The release causes a slight change in the values of the eigenfrequencies. 6 Modelling D 6.1 Modelling characteristics The reinforced concrete walls and floors are modeled by elements plates DKT. The reinforced concrete is modeled with a simple elastic law. The beams and poles are modeled by elements POU_D_E. These are considered elastic. The sole is modeled by elements 3D and is considered elastic. Depreciation is not considered in modelling. In this Modelling the rotational DDLs are released on the common edges between the sails and the floors (planar/planar re-lay). 6.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains about 2600 mesh cells and 2700 nodes (without considering the sole). The mesh is the SMART model. 6.3 Tested quantities and results The first three frequencies are calculated from modal analysis. A simple non-regression test is done. 6.4 Remarks The release causes a slight change in the values of the eigenfrequencies. 7 Modelling E 7.1 Modelling characteristics The reinforced concrete walls and floors are modeled by elements plates DKT. The reinforced concrete is modeled with a simple elastic law. The beams and poles are modeled by elements POU_D_E. These are considered elastic. The sole is modeled by elements 3D and is considered elastic. Depreciation is not considered in modelling. In this Modelling the rotational DDL is released on the common edges between the sails and the floors (planar/planar re-lay). However, before doing this operation, a rotation is applied to the mesh of the model according to the three global axes. 7.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains about 2600 mesh cells and 2700 nodes (without considering the sole). The mesh is the SMART model. 7.3 Tested quantities and results The first three frequencies are calculated from modal analysis, which are compared with the results obtained with the D Modelling. | Frequences | Reference values (modelization D) | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | | First eigenfrequency | 24.7734Hz | 0,1% | | 2nd eigenfrequency | 36.3761Hz | 0,1% | | 3rd eigenfrequency | 65.1450Hz | 0,1% | 7.4 Remarks The exact same values are obtained as with D Modelling. This method validates the writing of kinematic relationships produced by the Rtool tool. 8 Summary of the results The SMART model allows the testing of different modellings created using the Rtool tool for the release of DDL rotation between elements structure. Through these modal analyses we test different types of release using Rtool, as well as writing the kinematic restraints produced by the tool.

v1.03.129 MFRON04 – Code_Aster-MFront interface test for anisotropic constitutive laws v1.03.129 MFRON04 – Code_Aster-MFront interface test for anisotropic constitutive laws Summary: This test validates the implementation of constitutive laws elastic and orthotropic elasto-plastics defined using MFront on uniaxial loads. Modellings A and B consider an orthotropic linear elastic model, in modellings 3D and AXIS respectively. Modellings C and D consider an elastoplastic model associated with linear elasticity isotropic and Hill's orthotropic plasticity criterion, modellings 3D and AXIS respectively. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 1.1.1 modellings A et C It is a cube of unitary dimension. Height: h=1 m, width: l=1 m, thickness: e=1 m. 1.1.2 modellings B et D It is a square of unitary dimension. Height: h=1 m, width: l=1 m. 1.2 boundary conditions 1.2.1 modellings A et C - On the x=e side, the displacement is blocked in DX . - On the y=0 side, the displacement is blocked in DY . - On the z=0 side, the displacement is blocked in DZ . - On the z=h side, the displacement is driven in DZ from 0 to 0.01 m in a growing way. 1.2.2 modellings B et D - On the x=0 edge, the displacement is blocked in DX . - On the y=0 edge, the displacement is blocked in DY . - On the y=h edge, the displacement is driven in DY from 0 to 0.01 m in a growing way. 1.3 Material properties 1.3.1 modellings A et B These modellings consider an orthotropic linear elastic model. In the orthotropy marker, the stress-deformation relationship can be written: with \poissonCoef_{ij}/\youngModulus_i=\poissonCoef_{ji}/\youngModulus_j . The relationship depends on nine elastic constants: - Young's modulus \youngModulus_1 in direction 1. - The Young's modulus \youngModulus_2 in direction 2. - Young's modulus \youngModulus_3 in direction 3. - Poisson's ratio \poissonCoef_{12} in direction 2 under loading in direction 1. - Poisson's ratio \poissonCoef_{23} in direction 3 under loading in direction 2. - Poisson's ratio \poissonCoef_{13} in direction 3 under loading in direction 1. - \shearModulus_{12} shear module in plane 1-2. - The \shearModulus_{23} shear module in plane 2-3. - The \shearModulus_{13} shear module in plane 1-3. 1.3.2 modellings C et D These modellings consider an associated elasto-plastic model, with linear elasticity isotropic and Hill's orthotropic plasticity criterion. The elasticity depends on two parameters, the Young's modulus \youngModulus and the Poisson's ratio \poissonCoef (or equivalently the \bulkModulus compressibility module and the \shearModulus shear module). Hill's orthotropic plasticity criterion is based on seven constants (six anisotropic parameters and a limit of elasticity). When F=G=H and L=M=N=3F , Hill's orthotropic criterion is reduced to von Mises' isotropic criterion with \sigma_0 as the yield strength. 2 reference solution All modellings are considered to have a parallel loading axis to an \tensTwo{e}_1, \tensTwo{e}_2 or \tensTwo{e}_3 anisotropy marker axis. The local model is described by the following equations: with the following parameters: - \youngModulus : Young's modulus - \poissonCoef : Poisson's ratio - \stressCmp_{0} : initial tensile strength/compression - H : isotropic nutring module 1.3.2 Non-local model The formulation of the non-local model is based on the framework of the gradient models of internal variables as presented by r5.04.01. In this case, the internal variable regulated is the cumulative plastic deformation p . The behavior equations are then unchanged, with the exception of the expression of the thermodynamic force R , which becomes: with the newly introduced parameters: - C : Offshoring parameter - r : Penalization coefficient r5.04.01 will be available for a detailed presentation of the non-local models with gradients of internal variables and their numerical implementation. 1.4 Material properties The characteristics used in the non-local von Mises law are: - Young's modulus \youngModulus = 200 MPa - Poisson's ratio \poissonCoef = 0.3 - Initial yield strength \sigma_0 = 1 MPa - H = -20 MPa isotropic nutring module - C = \sigma_0 (\delta/\pi)^2 offshoring parameter with \delta = 0.6 m - Penalization coefficient r = -H 2 reference solution A one-dimensional solution with the field location of deformations in the softened plasticization regime is being sought.
