v1.04.118 PETSC03- Validation of the PETS c solver with a second level preconditioner v1.04.118 PETSC03- Validation of the PETS c solver with a second level preconditioner Summary: This test case allows the GMRES_LMP algorithm to be validated. This algorithm is used to use the GMRES iterative solver with a first-level preconditioner (here LDLT_SP) and a second-level preconditioner, called the Limited Memory Conditioner. Reference documentation R6.01.02 is referred to for more details on the second-level preconditioner, as well as the U4.50.01 operating documentation. The test is derived from the test case mumps02 described in the V1.04.112 validation documentation. It has two modellingss, which can be used to check the correct functioning of the solver on 1 and 2 processors respectively. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A rectangular plate of 100m length and 50m width is considered. D C A B Contact details of (m) points: A:(0.,0.,0.) B:(100.,0.,0.) C:(100.,50.,0.) D:(0.,50.,0.) 1.2 Material properties E=1.0\mathit{E2}N/{m}^{2} \nu =0.4999 1.3 boundary conditions We're imposing \mathit{DX}=1,\mathit{DY}=2 on the whole mesh 2 Solution The reference quantity used is the displacement according to the x axis and the y axis to the node C. 3 Modelling A Modelling D_PLAN_INCO_UPG Number of nodes: 341 Number of mesh cells: 140 ( 40 SEG3 and 100 QUAD8). Modelling A uses the GMRES_LMP algorithm of the PETSC solver. The solver parameters are chosen to trigger the construction of the second level preconditioner (this is not an example to follow). 4 Modelling B Model B is identical to model A, but the calculation is performed on 2 processors. 5 Summary of the results This test case shows the GMRES_LMP algorithm of the PETSC solver on 1 and 2 processors.

v1.04.119 PETSC04- FIELDSPLIT pre-conditioner validation c v1.04.119 PETSC04- FIELDSPLIT pre-conditioner validation c Summary: This test case allows you to validate the FIELDSPLIT pre-conditioner operation of the PETSC solver. It is a very general framework for dynamically defining block preconditioners. keyword SOLVEUR, U4.50.01 operating documentation. The test consists of 4 modellings, which allows to check the correct functioning of the solver: - petsc04a, Stokes problem sequentially - petsc04b, Stokes problem in parallel - petsc04c, sequential THM problem - petsc04d, sequential THM problem - petsc04b, Stokes problem hpc - petsc04d, THM problem in hpc This is a brief documentation. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A cube of size 0.5x0.5x0.5 is considered 1.2 Material properties See each of the modellings. 1.3 boundary conditions See each of the modellings. 2 Solution The reference quantity used is the x-axis displacement to node 165. 3 Modelling A 3D_INCO_UP Modelling Young's modulus 1, Poisson's ratio 0,4999 A Stokes problem is modelled. A 2-level preconditioner is defined that collectively treats the DX, DY, DZ components on the one hand and the PRES component on the other. A pressure approximation of the Schur supplement is used, which is preconditioned by a Jacobi method and a multigrill method is used for displacement. 4 Modelling B Model B is identical to model A, but the calculation is performed on 2 processors. 5 Modelling C 3D_THM modelling A thermo-hydro-mechanical problem is modelled. A 3-level preconditioner is defined that collectively treats the components DX, DY, DZ, PRE1 component and TEMP component. Several preconditioning levels are defined: an external Gauss-Seidel preconditioner, an iterative GMRES method preconditioned by Jacobi for temperature, a Schur-type preconditioner based on an approximation of the Schur supplement to pressure that is preconditioned by a Jacobi method and a multigrill method for displacement. 6 Modelling D Modelling D is identical to Modelling C, but the calculation is performed on 2 processors. 7 Modelling E Modelling E is identical to Modelling B, but the calculation is performed in hpc on 2 processors. 8 Modelling F Modelling F is identical to Modelling C, but the calculation is performed in hpc on 2 processors. 9 Summary of the results This test case shows the FIELDSPLIT functionality of the PETSC solver on 1 and 2 processors.

v1.04.120 PETSC05 – Use of user solver with petsc4py v1.04.120 PETSC05 – Use of user solver with petsc4py Summary: This test case validates the definition and use of a user solver with PETS c. The solver is defined by the Python user as a petsc4py.PETS c.KSP object and is then used in the MECA_STATIQUE or STAT_NON_LINE calculation operator. In model A, the preconditioner is trivial. The test is purely computer-based. In model B, the preconditioner is an implantation of the Reverse Constrained Enhanced Preconditioner developed by Franceschini et al. and published in https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2111.05599. This is a brief documentation.

v1.04.417 PYNL04 – Validation of CALCUL command with elements plates and shells v1.04.417 PYNL04 – Validation of CALCUL command with elements plates and shells Summary: This test is intended to validate the CALCUL command for elements DKT and COQUE_3D by comparing with the STAT_NON_LINE command. 1 Description 1.1 Geometry The study model is a square plate on the side c=\mathrm{1m} and \mathit{ep}=\mathrm{0.05m} thickness. 1.2 Material properties The properties of the steel for the plate are given in the following table. | Material | Storage | | --- | --- | | Young's modulus | 2\times {10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | | Poisson's ratio | 0.2 | | Volume size | 7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads 1.3.1 boundary conditions The side defined by the \mathit{AB} segment of the plate is blocked at 0 for \mathit{DX} , \mathit{DZ} and \mathit{DRY} components, and the \mathit{DY} component is blocked in A . 1.3.2 Loading: The load consists of applying a linear force according to Z on both points C and D , going from 0 to 50000N/m in one step (1.0 s). 2 reference solution The reference solution is obtained by numerical problem resolution (behaviour integration) using the STAT_NON_LINE command. The stress field, the nodal force vector, is obtained for comparison. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The mesh is composed of a single mesh cell QUAD4 modeled in DKT. In modelling, one single iteration is required in the STAT_NON_LINE command to compare with the CALCUL results. The Modelling is under the linear elastic behavior relationship with DEFORMATION = ‘PETIT', as well as DEFORMATION = ‘GROT_GDEP'. 3.2 Comparisons and results The difference between the stress field and the nodal force vector calculated by STAT_NON_LINE is tested and those calculated by the CALCUL command. 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics The mesh is composed of a single mesh cell QUAD9 modeled in COQUE_3D. In modelling, a single iteration is required in the STAT_NON_LINE command under the linear elastic behavior relationship only with DEFORMATION = ‘PETIT 4.2 Comparisons and results The difference between the stress field and the nodal force vector calculated by STAT_NON_LINE is tested and those calculated by the CALCUL command. Note: A significant difference is observed under the DEFORMATION = ‘GROT_GDEP' behavior for COQUE_3D. This difference is due to the non-taking into account of the change in normal in the CALCUL command. 5 Executive summary This test validated the CALCUL command for the integration of the constitutive law elastic for elements plates and shells.

v2.01.001 SDLD01 - degree of freedom mass-spring system v2.01.001 SDLD01 - degree of freedom mass-spring system Summary: This one-dimensional problem consists in making a transient dynamic calculation on a physical basis of a mechanical structure consisting of a mass and two springs subjected to multi-support loading. This test allows for a complete validation of the options for calculating the displacement fields in the absolute marker. Three different modellings are proposed: one test the classic multi-support approach in the trained marker, and two other test the direct approach in the absolute marker. The results are compared to the analytical solution from an oscillator to an degree of freedom (1 ddl). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry In MassSpring_System, one mass and two spring Modelling is shown. One-dimensional system with one mass and two springs 1.2 Material properties Both springs represent two beams with stiffness equal to k=EA/L , where: - E = 35 GPa is the Young's modulus - A = 0.016 m^2 is the surface of the beam section - L = 4 m is the length of the beam The concentrated mass is equivalent to m = 4000 t . A Rayleigh damping is re-applied around the basic frequency of the \omega_0=\sqrt{k_{eq}/m} system, where k_{eq}=2EA/L . The reduced damping is taken equal to \xi=0.05 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The following limit conditions are imposed: - DX = DY = DZ = 0 on nodes A and B - DY = DZ = 0 on the mass The following loads are required: - On the node A you will require a u_A = u_{0,A}sin(\omega_At + \alpha_A) displacement, where: - u_{0,A} = 2 mm - \omega_A = \pi - \alpha_A = 0 - On the node B you will require a u_B = u_{0,B}sin(\omega_Bt + \alpha_B) displacement, where: - u_{0,B} = 4.5 mm - \omega_B = 2\pi - \alpha_B = 0 1.4 Initial conditions In this test case, we propose two ways to impose the load: - Through a multi-support load in trained frame, in this case there is no need to impose initial conditions - Two shifts on the nodes A and B are required in this case to impose the initial speed and acceleration fields which are not zero 2 reference solution The reference solution is well known in literature. It is an oscillator with an degree of freedom (1 ddl) subjected to harmonic loading (). 3 Modelling A In this model, a multi-support load is tested in the -trained marker . The DEPL field at the end of this calculation is, of course, the field in the driven marker. The field in the absolute marker is stored in DEPL_ABSOLU. The field value at the moment t=0.268 s , which corresponds to the first peak of the displacement, is tested. The results are compared to the analytical solution. 4 Modelling B In this Modelling, a multi-support load is tested in the absolute mark using the DYNA_VIBRA operator. The DEPL field at the end of this calculation is therefore the field in the absolute marker. The field value at the moment t=0.268 s is tested, which corresponds to the first peak of displacement. The results are compared to the numerical solution of Modelling A. 5 Modelling C In this Modelling, a multi-support load is tested in the absolute mark using the DYNA_NON_LINE operator. The DEPL field at the end of this calculation is therefore the field in the absolute marker. The field value at the moment t=0.268 s is tested, which corresponds to the first peak of displacement. The results are compared to the numerical solution of Modelling A. 6 Bibliography Kramer, S. L. (1996). Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering. Prentice-Hall.

v2.01.004 SDLD04 - Transitional response of a mass-spring system subject to an accelerated requirement v2.01.004 SDLD04 - Transitional response of a mass-spring system subject to an accelerated requirement Summary This test consists of calculating the undisturbed transient response of a linear clamped-free mass-spring system subject to an accelerated requirement. The discrete traction-compression element, the calculation of eigenmodes, static modes, and the calculation of the transient response of a system subject to an accelerated requirement are tested. The direct calculation of the response is compared with its calculation by modal recombination. This test case comes from the VPCS guide. The reference solution is an analytical calculation. Errors on the results obtained are normal given the time step chosen for digital integration. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The response of a linear system consisting of three masses and three springs is calculated to an acceleration imposed on the point sound of (A) anchor: 1.2 Material properties - restraint stiffeners: k={k}_{1}={k}_{2}={k}_{3}=1000N/m ; - point masses: m={m}_{1}={m}_{2}={m}_{3}=1\mathrm{kg} . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions The only travels allowed are x -axis translations. The point A is clamped: \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dy}=\mathrm{dz}=\mathrm{drx}=\mathrm{dry}=\mathrm{drz}=0 . Charge The point anchor A is subject to an acceleration, a growing time function, according to the x direction: \gamma (t)=2.{10}^{5}.{t}^{2} ( t varies from 0 to 0,1s ). 1.4 Initial conditions The system is initially at rest: t=0 , \mathrm{dx}(0)=0 and \mathrm{dx}/\mathrm{dt}(0)=0 in all point. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution {f}_{i} eigenfrequencies and associated {\phi }_{\text{Ni}} own vectors are first calculated, standardized to the mass matrix. The generalised response of the single-excise system is then calculated by the analytically-solvented integral of Duhamel [bib1]. Finally, the relative displacement of point D is restored on the physical basis. Calculation of eigenfrequencies The mass and stiffness matrices are as follows: M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}m& 0& 0\\ 0& m& 0\\ 0& 0& m\end{array}\right] , K=k\left[\begin{array}{ccc}2& -1& 0\\ -1& 2& -1\\ 0& -1& 1\end{array}\right] \omega eigenfrequencies are solution of the \det[K-{\lambda}^{2}M]=0 equation, i.e. {\lambda}^{3}-5{\lambda}^{2}+6\lambda -1=0 where \lambda =\frac{\omega}{{\omega}_{0}} and \omega =\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} . Calculation of the generalised response of the mono-excise system \gamma (t)={\mathrm{a.t}}^{2} with a={2.10}^{5} . In the absolute benchmark, the fundamental equation of the undisturbed mass-spring system dynamics is written: M\ddot{{X}_{a}}+K{X}_{a}=0 . The {X}_{a} absolute displacement is broken down into a uniform drive displacement in {X}_{e} translation and a relative {X}_{r} displacement: {X}_{a}={X}_{r}+{X}_{e} . The equation of motion in the relative marker is written: M\ddot{{X}_{r}}+K{X}_{r}=-M\Psi \ddot{{X}_{s}}=Q with \ddot{{X}_{s}}=\gamma (t)={\mathrm{a.t}}^{2} and \Psi =\left[\begin{array}{}1\\ 1\\ 1\end{array}\right] and therefore Q={\mathrm{a.t}}^{2}m\left[\begin{array}{}1\\ 1\\ 1\end{array}\right] . The equation of the projected motion based on the dynamic modes standardized with the mass matrix sss written: \ddot{{\alpha}_{i}}(t)+{\omega}_{i}^{2}{\alpha}_{i}(t)=\frac{{\Phi}_{i}^{T}.M.\Psi }{{\Phi}_{i}^{T}.M.{\Phi}_{i}}\gamma (t)=-{p}_{i}(t)\gamma (t) . The response of this linear system, at a moment t is given by Duhamel's integral: \ddot{{\alpha}_{i}}(t)=\frac{1}{{\omega}_{i}}{\int}_{0}^{t}-{p}_{i}(t)\gamma (t).\sin{\omega}_{i}(t-\tau )d\tau =-\frac{{p}_{i}(t)}{{\omega}_{i}}{\int}_{0}^{t}{\mathrm{a.t}}^{2}\sin{\omega}_{i}(t-\tau )d\tau . However, after [bib1], {\int}_{0}^{t}a.{t}^{2}\sin{\omega}_{i}(t-\tau )d\tau =\frac{\alpha}{{\omega}_{i}}\left[{t}^{2}+\frac{2}{{\omega}_{i}}(\cos{\omega}_{i}t-1)\right] . So {X}_{r}={\Phi}_{i}\cdot {\alpha}_{i}=-\underset{i}{\Sigma}\frac{a.{p}_{i}(t).{\Phi}_{i}}{{\omega}_{i}^{2}}\left[{t}^{2}+\frac{2}{{\omega}_{i}}(\cos{\omega}_{i}t-1)\right] . 2.2 Baseline The reference results are the three specific frequencies of the system and the relative displacement {x}_{r} to point D , for different moments between 0 and 0,1s . 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution None if Duhamel's integral is calculated analytically [bib1], [bib2]. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. J.S. PRZEMIENIECKI: Theory of matrix structural analysis. New York, MacGraw-Hill, 1968, pp. 351-357 2. S.P. TIMOSHENKO, D.H. YOUNG and W. WEAVER : Vibration problems in engineering 4th edition, New York, Wiley & Sons, 1974, pp. 284-321 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The springs and point weights are modelled by discrete elements at 3 degrees of freedom DIS_T: The node \mathit{NO1} is clamped and is subject to an acceleration imposed \gamma (t) . The relative displacement of the node \mathit{NO4} is calculated . Modal synthesis calculus The full basis of the eigenmodes is considered. Temporal integration is performed with the algorithms of Newmark, d的Euler and Devogelaere with an time step of 0,001s . Calculations are archived all time step. A reduced {\xi}_{i} depreciation is considered to be zero for all calculated modes. The load is taken into account as a projected vector on the EXCIT:(VECT_GENE) modal basis or as a EXCIT:(NUME_MODE) modal component or both. Direct calculations The time integration is performed either with the Newmark algorithm or with the explicit algorithm of the time step-centered differences. The calculations are archived every ten time step. Note: As the diagram of the centered differences can only be used with a diagonal mass matrix, the elementary matrices are calculated with the option MASS_MECA_DIAG in the operator CALC_MATR_ELEM. Account for an initial state In both types of calculation, the relative displacement obtained from a one-time calculation is verified to be identical to that obtained in several times, i.e. by considering as the initial state, the result of the last time step calculated: ETAT_INIT=_F (RESULTAT ...) pour un calcul par synthèse modale; ETAT_INIT=_F (DEPL ... VITE ..) pour un calcul direct. Considered of modes neglected by static correction: A modal base consisting of the first two eigenmodes is considered and is completed by a mode corresponding to the static response of the system v2.01.023 SDLD23 - Random Excitation Mass and Spring System v2.01.023 SDLD23 - Random Excitation Mass and Spring System Summary: This test was part of the dynamic test set planned for VPCS, which officially failed but served as the basis for many Code_Aster dynamic test cases. It has a set of eight point masses and nine springs excited by a random force imposed on one of the masses. The excitement is of the white noise type. It is given by the spectral density of power of the excitatory force. The excited mass movement is calculated by a stochastic approach using different frequency discretizations for the response. The spectral moments of the response are also calculated in post-processing. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Excitation is a seismic force-type movement applied to point \mathrm{P4} in the \mathrm{dx} direction. We're interested in DSP moving node \mathrm{P4} . 1.2 Material properties | Point mass: | m=10\mathrm{Kg} | | --- | --- | | Elastic springs: | k={10}^{5}N/m | | Amortizers: | c=50N/(m/s) | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The problem is one-dimensional in the direction x (1 degree of freedom per mass). The excitation is a constant DSP force level 1, between 3 and 13 \mathrm{Hz} . 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The solution taken for reference is derived from the SDLD23 test of the VPCS [bib1] guide. 2.2 Baseline Pick of the response to the first eigenfrequency. Values of the first spectral moments for different discretizations. 2.3 Reference [bib1] VPCS Guide. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Discrete element in translation DIS_T Modelling respects geometry. The user can choose the step: the frequency band is then evenly discretized and the peak(s) may be misrepresented: this is the case with 40 steps of 0.25\mathrm{Hz} , which results in an error of more than \text{40\%} on spectral moments. The more discretization is refined, the better the result. To avoid unnecessary refinement away from peaks, a fairly wide default discretization is proposed, supplemented by a refinement of 50 discretization points around each peak. In the case of this test, which includes only one peak, this default discretization allows to estimate the spectral moments with precision of the order of \text{2\%} .

v2.01.027 SDLD27 - 8 degrees of freedom spring mass-system with non-proportional viscous shock absorber (modal analysis) v2.01.027 SDLD27 - 8 degrees of freedom spring mass-system with non-proportional viscous shock absorber (modal analysis) Summary: This two-dimensional problem consists in searching for the frequencies, vibration modes and damping of a mechanical structure composed of viscous masses, springs and shock absorbers. This test case Structure Mechanics corresponds to a dynamic analysis of a discrete model with linear behavior. This test allows for a complete validation of the discrete modelling options of rigidity, viscous damping and mass (without elements finished) offered by the AFFE_CARA_ELEM command. Five different modellings are offered: the Modelling of the discrete elements is either translational, translational/rotational and is written either as a global benchmark or as a local benchmark. Furthermore, different features of the CALC_MODES commands (search for clean values) and NORME_MODE (definition of the standard of a clean vector) are tested for this quadratic problem. This test refers to an VPCS test, but it has been modified. Indeed, the test directs the mechanical system on an \mathrm{3y}=\mathrm{4x} axis, which allows the data entry to be validated as a local reference. The results obtained are in good agreement with the reference results. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry | Point mass: | {m}_{{P}_{1}}={m}_{{P}_{2}}={m}_{{P}_{3}}=\dots \dots ={m}_{{P}_{8}}=m | | --- | --- | | Restraint Riders: | {k}_{\mathit{AP1}}={k}_{\mathit{P1P2}}={k}_{\mathit{P2P3}}=\dots \dots ={k}_{\mathit{P8B}}=k | | Viscous damping: | {c}_{\mathit{P1P2}}={c}_{\mathit{P2P3}}=\dots \dots ={c}_{\mathit{P7P8}}=c {c}_{\mathit{AP1}}=\mathit{cc} {c}_{\mathit{P8B}}=\mathit{cd} | 1.2 Material properties | Linear elastic translation spring | k={10}^{5}N/m | | --- | --- | | Point mass | m=10\mathit{kg} | | Single-directional viscous dampers | c=50N/(m/s) | | | \mathit{cc}=250N/(m/s) | | | \mathit{cd}=25N/(m/s) | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads A and B clamped points: u=0 . 1.4 Initial conditions Not applicable for modal analysis. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is the one given in the SDLD27 plug in the VPCS guide. The problem leads to the search for the clean values and proper vectors of the following dissipative system: M\ddot{u}+C\dot{u}+Ku=0 with M mass matrix, C damping matrix, K stiffness matrix. The problem is associated with this dissipative problem, the conservative problem: Ku+M\ddot{u}=0 . In harmonic form, it spells K-{\omega}^{2}M=0 . \Lambda =[{\omega}_{v}^{2}] is the spectral diagonal matrix of the values of this conservative system and \phi =[{\varphi}_{v}] is the corresponding matrix of the own vectors. {\varphi}_{v} are standardized such as: {\phi }^{T}M\phi =\mathit{Id} {\phi }^{T}K\phi =\Lambda . The solutions of the dissipative system are in the form of: u={u}_{0}{e}^{\mathit{st}} d’où (M{s}^{2}+Cs+K){u}_{0}=0 . {u}_{0} is broken down into the {\varphi}_{v} base. {u}_{0}=\phi q is then available, where: (I{s}^{2}+\gamma s+\Lambda )q=0 with \gamma ={\phi }^{T}C\phi (full matrix) This problem with clean values is solved by a reverse power method by taking as initial estimate {s}_{v}=j{\omega}_{v} . 2.2 Baseline The 8 system-specific damping and frequencies, as well as the 1st and 8th mode (complexes). 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution Semi-analytic solution. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. v2.01.031 SDLD31 - Basic validation of dynamic time schemas v2.01.031 SDLD31 - Basic validation of dynamic time schemas Summary: This test case validates the programming of the time-input schemas in DYNA_NON_LINE and DYNA_VIBRA. More specifically, the following implicit diagrams are tested for DYNA_NON_LINE: 1. Average acceleration (keyword NEWMARK) with resolution in motion and acceleration; 2. modified average acceleration (keyword HHT with MODI_EQUI='NON'); 3. HHT complete (keyword HHT with MODI_EQUI='OUI'); With the complete HHT schema, we also test the pursuits because this schema requires a particular initialization. Similarly, we also validate the pursuits for the average acceleration with acceleration resolution because it is not tested in other cases. DYNA_VIBRA is tested for constant time step schemas, i.e.: 1. explicit order scheme 1 says EULER; 2. NEWMARK implicit order 2 schema; 3. explicit order 4 scheme says DEVOGELAERE The aim is to study the behaviour of the patterns in time, so the problem chosen is deliberately very simple: it is a linear system 1 degree of freedom spring mass which is subjected to sinusoidal force. The reference solution is obtained by reprogramming the integration diagrams in Matlab and by calculating the analytical solution. 1 Reference problems 1.1 Geometry | | The 1 degree of freedom system is of the M mass type at the end of a stiffness K spring oriented in the vertical direction z . | | --- | --- | 1.2 Material properties Stiffness spring K : 36.{\pi}^{2}N/m Point mass M : 1\mathit{kg} The values shall be selected so as to have a specific pulse of the {\omega}_{0} mass-spring system such as: {\omega}_{0}=6.\pi \mathit{rad}/s because {{\omega}_{0}}^{2}=K/M . 1.3 Geometrical characteristics The displacement is done in vertical direction z . 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads The spring base is clamped, so the only degree of freedom is the following z displacement of the point mass M which is fixed to the other end of the spring. The load is a vertical F(t) sinusoidal force imposed on the point mass M: F(t)=\sin(1,1.{\omega}_{0}.t) . 1.5 Initial conditions The system is initially at rest. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation With this test case we want to study the behavior of the various implicit time integration schemes of the DYNA_NON_LINE operator. Therefore, it is not a question of trying to reproduce as closely as possible an analytical solution. So we choose a time step \mathit{dt}={10}^{-2}s , small enough compared to the system's own pulse and we will solve the linear transient problem with the DYNA_NON_LINE operator. For the non-dissipative scheme of the average acceleration (keyword NEWMARK) it would be possible to calculate the analytical solution to compare it. The resolution in motion or acceleration is tested which must obviously give the same results. The HHT scheme uses an ALPHA=-0.3 coefficient. For other schemes that are wanted to be tested and dissipative, obtaining an analytical solution is not easy. So we chose to compare all calculations with a numerical solution obtained with the Matlab code. To do this, the different schemas were programmed in Matlab. The result is several transient calculations in one step: with the average acceleration diagram, the modified average acceleration diagram, the complete HHT diagram and the Krenk diagram. For this latter dissipative diagram (with the selected parameter values), the displacement resolution and speed are validated. Then we test the calculation resume with the complete HHT schema, to validate the tracking mechanism with this schema (we do two pursuits, the first at 0,2s and the second at 0,35s ). 2.2 Quantities and reference results Comparisons will be made on the displacement and acceleration of the M point mass at the following moments: 0,5s , 0,7s and 1s . 3 Modelling A - DYNA_NON_LINE The quantities tested are the M point mass displacements and accelerations. | Schedule in time | Type of field | Instant | Values of Reference | tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | NEWMARK | DEPL | 0,5 s | 1.0804500210685E-02 | 1.E-5% | | Resolved while moving or accelerating (with and without continuation) | | 0,7 s | -4.0671779495390E-03 | 1.E-5% | | | 1,0 s | -1.3026189840935E-02 | 1.E-5% | | | ACCE | 0,5 s | -4.6479181362891E+00 | 1.E-5% | | | | 0,7 s | 2.3748682319566E+00 | 1.E-5% | | | | | 1,0 s | 5.5793367773016E+00 | 1.E-5% | | HHT | DEPL | 0,5 s | 9.0224842641940E-03 | 1.E-5% | | MODI_EQUI='NON' | | 0,7 s | -2.0242152707660E-03 | 1.E-5% | | | | 1,0 s | -9.074477606657E-03 | 1.E-5% | | | ACCE | 0,5 s | -4.0147576088701E+00 | 1.E-5% | | | | 0,7 s | 1.6489918279122E+00 | 1.E-5% | | | | 1,0 s | 4.022313059734449E+00 | 1.E-5% | | HHT | DEPL | 0,5 s | 1.0775515187707E-02 | 1.E-5% | | MODI_EQUI='OUI' | | 0,7 s | -4.1787420850760E-03 | 1.E-5% | | With or without prosecution | | 1,0 s | -1.3121050364360E-02 | 1.E-5% | | | ACCE | 0,5 s | -4.6864764249454E+00 | 1.E-5% | | | | 0,7 s | 2.7540329873126E+00 | 1.E-5% | | | | 1,0 s | 5.9586276847714E+00 | 1.E-5% | 4 modellings B et C - DYNA_VIBRA In the tests on the DYNA_VIBRA diagrams a slight viscous damping of one per thousand is introduced. This validates the correct treatment of the damping. It is also an opportunity to validate the quadratic modal calculation. Modelling B is done with elements DIS_T and Modelling C with elements 2D_DIS_T (the Z axis therefore corresponds to Y for this Modelling). 4.1 analytical solution William Weaver Jr. Stephen P. Timoshenko and Donovan H. Young provide in Chapter 1.9 of "Vibration Problems in Engineering" the solution to the problem of a mass/spring system with viscous damping subject to harmonic excitation. The equation to be solved is a second order equation in time on a single degree of freedom space: \ddot{x}+2\eta \dot{x}+{\omega}_{0}^{2}x=\frac{F}{m}\sin({\omega}_{e}t) where x is the shift of the mass, \dot{x} its speed and \ddot{x} its acceleration. {\omega}_{0}^{2}=\frac{k}{m} is the system's own pulse, m being its mass and k its stiffness. \eta is the reduced depreciation. Finally F is the amplitude of the excitation force while {\omega}_{e} is its pulsation. 4.2 Tested quantities and results | Calculated | Type of field | Instant (or modal method) | Values of Reference | tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | CALC_MODES | | 'SORENSEN' | | | | | FREQ | | 3 Hz | 1.E-4% | | AMOR_REDUIT | | 1E-03 | 1.E-4% | | | | 'TRI_DIAG' | | | | | FREQ | | 3 Hz | 1.E-4% | | | | AMOR_REDUIT | | 1E-03 | 1.E-4% | | EULER | DEPL | 0,5 s | 0.010785 | 1.E-2% | | with and without REST_GENE_PHYS | | 0,7 s | -3.745074E-03 | 1.E-1% | | | | 1,0 s | -0.0125639 | 1.E-1% | | NEWMARK | DEPL | 0,5 s | 0.010785 | 1.E-2% | | | | 0,7 s | -3.745074E-03 | 1.E-1% | | | | 1,0 s | -0.0125639 | 1.E-1% | | DEVOG | DEPL | 0,5 s | 0.010785 | 1.E-2% | | | | 0,7 s | -3.745074E-03 | 1.E-1% | | | | 1,0 s | -0.0125639 | 1.E-1% | 5 Summary of the results This test case allows the validation, in linear form, of the implicit time diagrams (average acceleration, modified average acceleration and complete HHT) of the DYNA_NON_LINE operator, in the case of a variable load, for resolutions on the move, speed or acceleration depending on the case. v2.01.032 SDLD32 - Basic Schema Validation in Time HHT v2.01.032 SDLD32 - Basic Schema Validation in Time HHT Summary: This test case validates the programming of the HHT time integration scheme (Hilber-Hughes-Taylor) in DYNA_NON_LINE ( SCHEMA='HHT' with MODI_EQUI='OUI' ). It involves a simple problem, i.e. a system with a degree of freedom. Two schematic schemes are tested, namely the classic HHT schema initially introduced in [bib1] ( SCHEMA='HHT' with MODI_EQUI='OUI' ), and the proposed HHT schema without overshooting in [bib2] ( SCHEMA='NOHHT' ). 1 Reference problems 1.1 Geometry A degree of freedom system consisting of a point mass m is considered, stiffness k spring oriented to x axis, and shock absorber. The displacement is made according to the x axis. > Figure 1: Schéma du système masse-ressort-amortisseur. 1.2 Basic characteristics The mass is assumed to be equal to m=1 \ \text{kg} . The system's own period is assumed to be equal T=1 \ \text{s} , which corresponds to a clean pulse \omega_0 = 2\pi/T , and therefore to a stiffness k = m \omega_0^2 = 2\pi \ \text{N}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} . c = 2 \xi \omega_0 depreciation is considered, where \xi \in [0, 1[ is the reduced depreciation The system. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The spring base is clamped, so the only degree of freedom is the x displacement of the m point mass that is attached to the other end of the spring. 1.4 Initial conditions Initial u_0 = 1.0 \ \text{m} displacement and initial v_0 = 1.0 \ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} speed are considered. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The numerical solution of the problem is calculated via HHT and NOHHT schemas of DYNA_NON_LINE , considering a time step \Delta t = 5\cdot 10^{-3} \ \text{s} . \alpha=-0.3 coefficient for these diagrams. The two formulations available for these diagrams, i.e. the formulations on the move and in acceleration are tested. 2.2 reference solution The problem is a analytical solution. Indeed, the displacement of the point mass subjected to the analytical solution initial conditions on the move and speed u_0, v_0 \in \mathbb{R} may be written as follows: for all t \ge 0 , with \omega_d = \omega_0 \sqrt{1-\xi^2} . Solutions obtained with Code_Aster are also compared with results obtained with Python implantation HHT and NOHHT diagrams. 2.3 Quantities and reference results Comparisons will be made on the displacement, speed and acceleration of the m point mass at several moments. 3 Modelling A The case is considered here without depreciation, i.e. , \xi = 0 . 3.1 Tested quantities and results The quantities tested are the m point mass displacements, speeds and accelerations. 4 Modelling B This is considered with reduced depreciation \xi = 0.5 . 4.1 Tested quantities and results The quantities tested are the m point mass displacements, speeds and accelerations. 5 Summary of the results This test case allows you to validate the HHT (full) schema of the DYNA_NON_LINE operator in linear mode, in the case of initial conditions on the move and in non-zero speed, for resolutions in the moving and accelerating. 6 Bibliography H.M. v2.01.034 SDLD34 – Dropping a single mass/spring v2.01.034 SDLD34 – Dropping a single mass/spring Summary: A simple oscillator, consisting of a mass connected to a support by a spring, is subjected to a release from the strained spring. It is checked that Code_Aster calculates the oscillation response to the initial conditions without external forces. The linear transient calculation features on physical and modal basis of the DYNA_VIBRA operator are tested. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry We're interested in the m mass movement. 1.2 Material properties | Point mass: | m=1\mathrm{kg} | | --- | --- | | Elastic spring: | k={\pi}^{2}N/m | Case 1 : system of conservative (without depreciation) Cas 2 : c=0,2\pi \mathrm{N.s}/m dissipative system 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The problem is one-dimensional in the x direction, and at a degree of freedom: the m mass displacement. The mass is left free, without external excitement. Initially it is out of balance: the spring is tense with a 1 metre elongation. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is analytical. In the absence of damping, it is a simple sinusoid whose period is equal to the proper pulse of the oscillator, {\omega}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} , and whose amplitude is the initial ({x}_{0}) extension of the spring. The x(t) position of the mass is given by the equation: > x(t)={x}_{0}\cos({\omega}_{0}t) (1) The speed of the mass is therefore: > v(t)=-{\omega}_{0}{x}_{0}\sin({\omega}_{0}t) (2) In the presence of ({c}_{[\mathrm{N.s}/m]}) viscous damping, the oscillations become damped and the x(t) position is written: > x(t)={x}_{0}{e}^{-\zeta {\omega}_{0}t}[\cos(\omega t)+(\frac{\zeta}{\sqrt{1-{\zeta}^{2}}})\sin(\omega t)] (3) where \zeta is the reduced damping given by \zeta =\frac{c}{2{\omega}_{0}m} . \zeta is considered to be less than 1 to keep the oscillations. Pulsation is given by the formula \omega ={\omega}_{0}\sqrt{(1-{\zeta}^{2})} . It is therefore different from the system's own ({\omega}_{0}) pulse. 2.2 Results Case 1 : system of conservative (without depreciation) For this system, the clean pulse {\omega}_{0}=\pi \mathrm{rad}/s . The eigenfrequency is therefore {f}_{0}={\omega}_{0}/2\pi =0,5\mathrm{Hz} . The displacement (m) and speed (m/s) of the mass given by Eqs.1 and 2 respectively are: > x(t)=\cos(\pi t) et v(t)=-\pi \sin(\pi t) Cas 2 : viscous dissipative system The reduced damping is \zeta =0,1 . The pulse is \omega =0,995\pi \mathrm{rad}/s and the frequency is f=\omega /2\pi =0,4975\mathrm{Hz} . The displacement (m) can then be calculated according to Eq.3. 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution analytical solution. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Discrete element in translation DIS_T Features of elements: Nodes \mathrm{P1} and \mathrm{P2} : M_T_D_N mass matrices with m=100\mathrm{kg} . v2.01.104 SDLD104 - Extrapolation of local measurements on a complete model (discreet) v2.01.104 SDLD104 - Extrapolation of local measurements on a complete model (discreet) Summary: It is a discrete linear dynamic test. The aim is to test the PROJ_MESU_MODAL command in the case of a discrete system. This command allows to project dynamic dynamic transient responses at a number of points on a numerical Modelling modal basis. This test contains 2 modellings where the projection is made on a concept of type [mode_meca], the difference being given by the way this concept is made. For the 2 modellings, the experimental measurements provided are identical and allow testing of nodes searches against nodes, taking into account local orientation and processing of sampling in constant or non-constant time for measurements on the move. In both cases, the reference solution is determined analytically (by Maple); the projection is made in the favorable configuration where the number of modes is equal to the number of measurements. The displacement responses obtained after projection are identical to the reference displacements provided in data. The values of the speeds and accelerations derived from the movements obtained after projection are similar to those obtained analytically. The low differences observed are due to the approximation errors generated by the determination via a linear schematic in time of the speeds and accelerations. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Description of the system We consider the system represented by the following diagram: 1.2 Masses and rigidity The three springs are of identical rigidity: k=1000N/m . Both masses are equal to m=10\mathrm{kg} . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading Both ends are clamped. The load is an axial tensile force applied to the \mathrm{m1} mass, sinusoidal as a function of time, of \omega pulse. 2 Reference solutions 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The analytical solution of this problem is presented below. - Vibration modes and frequencies: The following system characterizes the dynamics of the masses: > \lbrace \begin{array}{}m(\ddot{{x}_{1}}+\ddot{{x}_{2}})+k({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})=0\\ m(\ddot{{x}_{1}}-\ddot{{x}_{2}})+\mathrm{3k}({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})=0\end{array} éq 2.1-2 The system's 2 frequencies are therefore given by: {\omega}_{1}=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}} et {\omega}_{2}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{3k}}{m}} éq 2.1-3 and the associated modal deformations are: {\Phi}_{1}=(\begin{array}{}1\\ 1\end{array}) et {\Phi}_{2}=(\begin{array}{}1\\ -1\end{array}) éq 2.1-4 The generalised matrices are: \stackrel{ˉ}{M}={\Phi}^{T}M\Phi =(\begin{array}{cc}1& 1\\ 1& -1\end{array})(\begin{array}{cc}m& 0\\ 0& v2.01.105 SDLD105 - Transition response from a mass-spring system to a mono-support earthquake with static correction v2.01.105 SDLD105 - Transition response from a mass-spring system to a mono-support earthquake with static correction Summary This test case, inspired by test case VPCS SDLD04, is the calculation of the unamortized transient response of a linear clamped-free mass-spring system, subject to a mono-support required acceleration. Its objective is to show the value of static correction, whether it is done "a priori" by adding static modes at the basis of dynamic modes, or a posteriori . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The response of a linear system consisting of three masses and three springs is calculated to an acceleration imposed on the point sound of (A) anchor: 1.2 Material properties - restraint stiffeners: {k}_{1}=1000N/m and {k}_{2}={k}_{3}=100N/m ; - point masses: m={m}_{1}={m}_{2}={m}_{3}=1\mathrm{kg} . - \text{5 \%} modal damping for all modes 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions The only travels allowed are x -axis translations. The point A is clamped: \mathit{dx}=\mathit{dy}=\mathit{dz}=\mathit{drx}=\mathit{dry}=\mathit{drz}=0 . Charge The point anchor A is subjected to a harmonic acceleration of frequency {f}_{\mathrm{ex}} . The calculation is made from 0 to 20s . 1.4 Initial conditions The system is initially at rest: t=0 , \mathrm{dx}(0)=0 and \mathrm{dx}/\mathrm{dt}(0)=0 in all point. 2 reference solution The objective of the test case is to show the modal truncation effect on a very simple example of seismic calculation and to illustrate the value of static correction, whether it is done a priori by adding static modes at the basis of dynamic modes, or a posteriori . The reference solution is the complete modal-based transitional calculation performed with the DYNA_VIBRA operator. The mass-spring system has three degrees of freedoms. It is therefore associated with three modes whose calculated frequencies are: {f}_{1}=0,946\mathrm{Hz} , {f}_{2}=2,533\mathrm{Hz} et {f}_{3}=5,305\mathrm{Hz} . The frequency of the harmonic seismic signal was chosen at {f}_{\mathrm{ex}}=2\mathrm{Hz} to keep only the first two modes in the modal base. The rule of holding modes up to twice the maximum frequency of excitement is respected. The table of unit effective modal masses gives interesting information: | Unit effective mass | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | NUME_MODE | FREQUENCE | MASS_EFFE_UN_DX | CUMUL_DX | | 1 | 9.48538E-01 | 6.82972E-01 | 6.82972E-01 | | 2 | 2.53344E+00 | 5.03369E-02 | 7.33309E-01 | | 3 | 5.30513E+00 | 2.66691E-01 | 1.00000E+00 | It is observed that the third mode will have a negligible dynamic response because its eigenfrequency is {f}_{3}=5,305\mathit{Hz} , beyond 2\times {f}_{\mathit{ex}}=4,0\mathit{Hz} . However, its effective unit modal mass in the x direction is \text{26,7 \%} . It is not negligible and this mode can influence the response of the mass-spring system by its quasi-static contribution. It is the purpose of the static correction that it should be taken into account. v2.01.106 SDLD106 – Spring mass system with harmonic oscillation damping v2.01.106 SDLD106 – Spring mass system with harmonic oscillation damping Summary This test case validates the elemental matrix of a discrete element. The proper frequency of an oscillator to an degree of freedom (mass – spring system), the transient response due to sinusoidal excitation and the forced response due to harmonic excitation is calculated. The reference results are obtained analytically. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The diagram of the system is shown in the following figure: 1.2 Material properties The Material properties are: stiffness K:4{\pi}^{2}N/m mass M:100\mathit{kg} C=0.4\pi \mathit{Ns}/m damping 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The spring is clamped at one of its ends and subjected to F force at the free end. The point mass can only move according to the x direction. 1.4 Initial conditions At the initial moment, the mass is still and is in its equilibrium position. x(0)=0m v(0)=0m/s 2 reference solution The purpose is to calculate the proper frequency of the oscillator, the response due to sinusoidal excitation, and the response due to harmonic excitation. 2.1 Calculation of the eigenfrequency For the validation of the calculation of the eigenfrequency, we consider the system without damping. Thus, the displacement of the free end of the spring is governed by the following relationship: M\ddot{x}+Kx=F (1) The frequency of this oscillator is: {f}_{0}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\sqrt{\frac{K}{M}}=\frac{{\omega}_{0}}{2\pi } ( {f}_{0} : eigenfrequency, {\omega}_{0} : clean pulse) 2.2 Calculation of the transitional response For the validation of the calculation of the transient response, we consider the system without damping. With the initial condition x(0)=0 and \dot{x}(0)=0 , if a sinusoidal force F(t)=F\sin(\Omega t) is applied to the free end of the spring, the differential equation solution (1) is: x(t)=\frac{F(\sin\Omega t-\frac{\Omega}{{\omega}_{0}}\sin{\omega}_{0}t)}{M({\omega}_{0}^{2}-{\Omega}^{2})} For this response calculation to sinusoidal excitation, we chose: \Omega =1\mathit{rd}/s and F=1N . 2.3 Calculation of the harmonic response The purpose of this calculation is to calculate the amortized oscillator response due to harmonic excitation. The free end of the spring is moved by the following relationship: M\ddot{x}+C\dot{x}+Kx=F (2) Applying a sinusoidal force F(t)=F\sin(\Omega t) , at the free end of the spring, and adopting the complex notation, obtains the forced response: \stackrel{ˆ}{x}(\Omega )=\frac{F}{K-{\Omega}^{2}M+jC} For this calculation of the harmonic forced response, we chose: 0.5{\omega}_{0}\le \Omega \le 1.5{\omega}_{0} 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics L-oscillator is modelled using d-d-elements 2D_DIS_TR. 3.2 Mesh characteristics Mesh cells number and type: 1 element of SEG2 type and 1 element of POI1 type. 3.3 Tested quantities and results Eigenfrequency: | quantity tested | Reference | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | | {f}_{0}=\frac{{\omega}_{0}}{2\pi } | 0.1\mathit{Hz} | 1.E-4 | | | | | | | | | | Sine response at instant {t}_{1}=1s : | | | | quantity tested | Reference | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | | x({t}_{1}=1s) | 1.55346{10}^{-3}m | 5.E-4 | | | | | | | | | | Harmonic response at {\Omega}_{1}=1.5{\omega}_{0} frequency: | | | | quantity tested | Reference | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | | \stackrel{ˆ}{x}(\Omega )=1.5{\omega}_{0} | -2.022511{10}^{-2} –5.15690{10}^{-4}im | 5.E-3 | The three tests are doubled by non-regression tests with a tolerance of 1.E-6. 4 Summary of the results The results obtained are in good agreement with the theoretical solution.

v2.01.107 SDLD107 - Minimization of an energy function of error type in relation to dynamic behaviour of structures v2.01.107 SDLD107 - Minimization of an energy function of error type in relation to dynamic behaviour of structures Summary: The application field of this test is for structural dynamics. It allows to validate the CALC_ERC_DYN u4.53.41 computing operator, which allows to obtain fields solution of a problem of minimizing an energy function of error-like behavioral type (ERC) under a modal formulation. The solution is to solve the problem of ERC for a system composed of 3 masses and 4 springs, clamped at its ends in free vibration. Springs and masses are modelled by elements type 'DIS_T'. The results of the audit for the case studied were obtained semi-analytically. Its resolution, which serves as a reference, was carried out using the Matlab software. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The system studied is composed of 3 masses ( m ) and 4 springs ( k ). The whole is clamped at its ends. Image 1.1-a : Geometry of the system studied 1.2 Material properties Stiffness springs: k=\mathrm{1 }N/m . Point mass: m=\mathrm{1 }\mathrm{kg} . 1.3 boundary conditions A and B clamped points. 1.4 Initial conditions Structure initially at rest. 1.5 Observation The two translation x1 and x2 are considered to be perfectly observed. The first two modes are considered to be: - For the first mode of its own, the two translation x1 and x2 are assumed, as well as its perfectly observed own pulse ( \widehat{{\omega}_{1}}={\omega}_{1} ). - For the second mode of the same, the two perfectly observed x1 and x2 translations are considered, while the information on the own pulse is assumed to be tainted by an error of 25% ( \widehat{{\omega}_{2}}=1,25\ast {\omega}_{2} ). 1.6 Error function The error of energy function error in relation to the following behaviour is minimized: {e}_{\omega}^{2}(u,v,w)=\frac{\gamma}{2}{(u-v)}^{T}K+\frac{1-\gamma }{2}{(u-w)}^{T}{\omega}^{2}M+\frac{1-\alpha }{\alpha}{(\mathit{Hu}-\widehat{u})}^{T}\text{}\mathit{Gr} 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution 2.1.1 Reference model For the reference model the following displacement vector is assumed: x=\left(\begin{array}{c}{x}_{1}\\ {x}_{2}\\ {x}_{3}\end{array}\right) Thus, the structural mass matrices (M) and stiffness (K) are: M=\left(\begin{array}{ccc}1& 0& 0\\ 0& 1& 0\\ 0& 0& 1\end{array}\right) K=\left(\begin{array}{ccc}2& -1& 0\\ -1& 2& -1\\ 0& -1& 2\end{array}\right) The proper pulses of the mass-spring system are: {\omega}_{1}^{2}=(2-\sqrt{2}) {\omega}_{2}^{2}=2 {\omega}_{3}^{2}=(2+\sqrt{2}) of the respective modal deformities (standardized at 1 at the greatest amplitude): {\varphi}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\begin{array}{c}\sqrt{2}\\ 2\\ \sqrt{2}\end{array}\right) {\varphi}_{2}=\left(\begin{array}{c}-1\\ 0\\ 1\end{array}\right) {\varphi}_{3}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\begin{array}{c}-\sqrt{2}\\ 2\\ -\sqrt{2}\end{array}\right) The matrix for the perfect observation of x1 and x2 is: H=\left(\begin{array}{ccc}1& 0& 0\\ 0& 1& 0\end{array}\right) In addition, the standard matrix (Gr) is chosen by combining the reduced Guyan mass and stiffness matrices. For their construction, the static modes associated with x1 and x2 are: {\psi}_{1}=\left(\begin{array}{c}1\\ 0\\ 0\end{array}\right) {\psi}_{2}=\left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ 1\\ 0.5\end{array}\right) Forming the \psi =\left[{\psi}_{1}{\psi}_{2}\right] static mode base. This leads to: {G}_{r}={\psi}^{T}[K+M]\psi ; \mathit{Gr}=\left(\begin{array}{cc}3& -1\\ -1& 2.75\end{array}\right) The weighting parameters of {e}_{\omega}^{2}(u,v,w) are selected \alpha =0.5 and \gamma =0.5 . 2.1.2 Construction of linear system associated with problem of error function in relation to behaviour. The problem of finding fields associated with the behavioral error-like function leads to the resolution of the following linear matrix system: Al=b with, for each individual pulse {\omega}_{i} : {A}_{i}=\left(\begin{array}{cc}\gamma (K+\gamma /(1-\gamma ){\omega}_{i}^{2}M)& -\gamma (K-{\omega}_{i}^{2}M)\\ -\gamma (K-{\omega}_{i}^{2}M)& (-2\alpha /(1-\alpha )){H}^{T}{G}_{r}H\end{array}\right) et {b}_{i}=\left(\begin{array}{c}{0}_{3}\\ (-2\alpha /(1-\alpha )){H}^{T}{G}_{r}\widehat{{u}_{i}}\end{array}\right) where \widehat{{u}_{i}} represents the observation of the {\varphi}_{i} mode associated with the estimated {\omega}_{i} own pulse. \alpha and \gamma are the weighting parameters associated with the error function. Finally, the l solution vector is the concatenation of two fields associated with the error function in such a way that: l=\left(\begin{array}{c}u-v\\ u\end{array}\right) 2.2 Baseline Two reference cases are tested: 1. First eigenmode, perfect observations: \widehat{{u}_{1}}=\left(\begin{array}{c}\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\\ 1\end{array}\right) ; \widehat{{\omega}_{1}}=(2-\sqrt{2}) In this case, the result is trivial as it must lead to a perfectly zero error functional result associated with: (u-v)=\left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ 0\\ 0\end{array}\right) ; u=\frac{1}{2}\left(\begin{array}{c}\sqrt{2}\\ 2\\ \sqrt{2}\end{array}\right) 1. Second eigenmode, perfect moves, and clean pulse tainted with error: \widehat{{u}_{2}}=\left(\begin{array}{c}-1\\ 0\end{array}\right) ; \widehat{{\omega}_{2}}=1.25\ast 2 In this case, the construction of the Al=b matrix problem leads to: A=\left(\begin{array}{cccccc}1+{1.25}^{2}& -0.5& 0& -1+{1.25}^{2}& 0.5& 0\\ -0.5& 1+{1.25}^{2}& -0.5& 0.5& -1+{1.25}^{2}& 0.5\\ 0& -0.5& 1+{1.25}^{2}& 0& 0.5& -1+{1.25}^{2}\\ -1+{1.25}^{2}& 0.5& 0& -6& 2& 0\\ 0.5& -1+{1.25}^{2}& 0.5& 2& -5.5& 0\\ 0& 0.5& -1+{1.25}^{2}& 0& 0& 0\end{array}\right) b=\left(\begin{array}{c}0\\ 0\\ 0\\ 6\\ -2\\ 0\end{array}\right) This system of equations was solved using the Matlab software, leading to the solution: l=\left(\begin{array}{c}0.223608826207038\\ 0.107013222975753\\ -0.095122864867336\\ -0.957415448053491\\ 0.038110367724860\\ 0.494584477951991\end{array}\right) In this case, the value of the function is: {e}_{{\omega}_{2}}^{2}(u,v,w)=0.089643288114668 the part associated with the error fields is: \frac{\gamma}{2}{(u-v)}^{T}K+\frac{1-\gamma }{2}{(u-w)}^{T}{\omega}^{2}M=0.083454681437031 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution First case: analytical solution. Second case: semi-analytic solution. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes: 5 of which 2 clamped Number of mesh cells and types: 4 SEG2 3.2 Tested quantities and results Calculation of the solution fields and the functional value with the CALC_ERC_DYN operator. | Identification | Reference | | --- | --- | | Formulation: MODALE | | | First case | | | Value of {e}_{{\omega}_{1}}^{2}(u,v,w) Function | 0.0 | | Second case | | | Value of {e}_{{\omega}_{2}}^{2}(u,v,w) Function | 0.089643288114668 | | Value of {e}_{{\omega}_{2}}^{2}(u,v,w) Function | 0.083454681437031 | | | | | {u}_{1} ( m ) | -0.957415448053491 | | {u}_{2} ( m ) | 0.038110367724860 | | {u}_{3} ( m ) | 0.494584477951991 | | {(u-v)}_{1} ( m ) | 0.223608826207038 | | {(u-v)}_{2} ( m ) | 0.107013222975753 | | {(u-v)}_{3} ( m ) | -0.095122864867336 | Table 3.2-1 : quantities and tested results 4 Summary of the results The accuracy of the optimum fields (u) and (u-v) and the functional value is very good (errors in the order of 1E-12 to 1E-14) This test therefore validates the CALC_ERC_DYN operator for the search calculation of eligible fields associated with an error-like energy functional problem in relation to dynamic behavior under a modal formulation.

v2.01.301 SDLD301 - Spectral seismic response of a 2 masses and 3 multi-supported springs system (corresponding or decorreal excitation) v2.01.301 SDLD301 - Spectral seismic response of a 2 masses and 3 multi-supported springs system (corresponding or decorreal excitation) Summary: The problem is to calculate the spectral response of a system 2 masses - 3 springs subjected to multiple seismic excitation. Excitations are considered either decorrellated and independent or correlated with each other. The element is tested in traction, the calculation of eigenmodes, static modes and spectral response by modal superposition via COMB_SISM_MODAL operator. Different cumulations are tested when calculating the support responses. It is verified that, in the case of excitation equal to the support, the single-tension calculation and the correlated multi-tension calculation provide the same result. The proper operation of the depreciation input is also verified as a damping matrix (modelling C). v2.01.313 SDLD313 - Spring mass system with 2 degrees of freedom hysteretic damping v2.01.313 SDLD313 - Spring mass system with 2 degrees of freedom hysteretic damping Summary: This unidirectional problem consists of a harmonic analysis of a mechanical structure composed of a set of spring masses with hysteretic damping and subjected to sinusoidal excitation. This mechanical test of the structures corresponds to a dynamic analysis of a discrete model with linear behavior. It consists of three modellings. The elements discrete translation (mass, spring) options AMOR_HYST are tested through Modelling A. Through Modelling B, elements beam (POU_D_T) and AMOR_HYST options are tested, Through Modelling C, the complex modal calculation (CALC_MODES) is tested. The results obtained for the first two modellings (moving field for different excitation frequencies) are in good agreement with the results of the VPCS guide. The results obtained for the third model are in good agreement with the semi-analytic results. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry We consider the system represented by the following diagram: | Point mass: | {m}_{1} et {m}_{2} | | --- | --- | | Restraint Riders: | {k}_{1} et {k}_{2} | | Hysteretic damping: | {\eta}_{1} et {\eta}_{2} | 1.2 Material properties | Linear elastic translation spring | {K}_{1}=28000N/m | | --- | --- | | | {K}_{2}=28000N/m | | Point mass | {M}_{1}=10\mathit{kg} | | | {M}_{2}=5\mathit{kg} | | Hysteretic damping | {\eta}_{1}=0.1 | | | {\eta}_{2}=0.0 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions : A , B , C clamped in \mathit{DY} and \mathit{DZ} A points: clamped (\mathit{DX}=0) . Through this problem, the various algorithms of the DYNA_VIBRA U4.54.03 command are tested and their ability to deal with extreme damping problems is tested. The results are compared with the exact analytical solutions. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The system consists of a mass, spring and shock absorber. v2.02.001 SDLL01 - Short beam on single supports v2.02.001 SDLL01 - Short beam on single supports Summary: This two-dimensional problem consists in searching for vibration frequencies of a mechanical structure composed of a beam in single support at both ends. This test case of Structure Mechanics corresponds to a dynamic analysis of a linear model with linear behavior. The influence of the position of the points considered as support points (points on neutral fiber or points excentrated at the base of the beam) in relation to the neutral fiber of a thick beam is studied. This test allows testing some of the features that concern Timoshenko beams, rigid restraintss and searching for eigenfrequencies by inverse iterations. The results obtained with the support points on the neutral fibre, i.e. with the support points excentric, are compared with the analytical calculations on the beams of TImoshenko. The results obtained with the support points excentric are compared with the results of non-regression. When the support points are eccentric, there is a coupling between the different traction-compression and bending modes. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Retangular straight section: | height: | h=0.2m | | --- | --- | | width: | b=0.1m | | Area: | A={2.10}^{-2}{m}^{2} | | inertia: | \mathrm{Iz}=6.667{10}^{-5} | | shearing: | \mathrm{Ay}=\mathrm{Az}=1.17692 | | twist: | \mathit{Jx}=0.45776042{10}^{-4} | Length of beam L=1.m Point coordinates ( m ) : | | A | B | C | D | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | x | | | | | | y | | | – 0.1 | – 0.1 | 1.2 Material properties E={2.10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} \nu =0.3 \rho =7800.\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads | Problem 1: | Point A | u=v=0. | Point B | v=0. | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Problem 2: | Point C | u=v=0. | Point D | v=0. | 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is the one given in Timoshenko's book on the theory of vibrations of beams and plates ([1]): Problem 1: Analytical calculation The bending equation of the unslender beams gives the Timoshenko formulation, superimposing the effects of simple bending, shear force deformations and rotation inertia. v2.02.002 SDLL02 - slender beam, clamped-free, folded on itself v2.02.002 SDLL02 - slender beam, clamped-free, folded on itself Summary: This two-dimensional problem consists in searching for the frequencies and vibration modes of a mechanical structure, composed of a free slender beam, clamped and folded on itself. The problem does not have physical significance, but it allows to validate the search for the own multiple bending frequencies and the search for double modes in a subspace of order 2. In this test, three different modellingss are performed: - in the first model, boundary conditions is imposed using Lagrange parameters (command AFFE_CHAR_MECA) and the own values and vectors are calculated by the Lanczos method (command CALC_MODES, METHODE='TRI_DIAG' under the factor keyword SOLVEUR_MODAL), - in the second model, boundary conditions is imposed by removing degrees of freedom in the mass and stiffness matrices (command AFFE_CHAR_CINE) and the own values and vectors are calculated by the Bathe and Wilson method (command CALC_MODES, METHODE='JACOBI' under the factor keyword SOLVEUR_MODAL) 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry B The geometrical characteristics of the beam forming the mechanical model are as follows: Length: L=0.5m Rectangular straight section: | Height: | h=0.005m | | --- | --- | | Width: | b=0.050m | | Area: | A=2.5{10}^{-4}{m}^{2} | | Inertial moment: | {I}_{z}=5.208{10}^{-10}{m}^{4} | The coordinates (in metres) of the characteristic points of all beams are: | | A | B | C | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | x | | 0.5 | | | y | | | | 1.2 Material properties The Material properties making up the beam are: E=2.1{10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} \nu =0.3 \rho =7800.\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The boundary condition that characterizes this problem is the clamped support of point A and is written: u=v=0. , \theta =0 . 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is the one given in the SDLL02/89 form of the VPCS guide which presents the calculation method as follows: By dynamic stiffness method, the folded beam is shown to allow double frequencies, a solution of: \begin{array}{ccc}\cos(\lambda )=0& \mathrm{\Rightarrow }& {\lambda}_{i}=(\mathrm{2i}-1)\frac{\pi}{2}\\ {f}_{i}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\frac{{\lambda}_{i}^{2}}{{L}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{{\mathit{EI}}_{z}}{\rho A}}& & i=1,2,\mathrm{...}\end{array} For a rectangular section, we obtain: {f}_{i}={(\mathrm{2i}-1)}^{2}\pi \frac{R}{{\mathrm{8L}}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{E}{12\rho }} i=1,2,\mathrm{...} This formulation neglects the deformations of shear force and rotation inertia (Euler-Bernoulli beam). v2.02.006 SDLL06 - Transient Response of a clamped-Free Post v2.02.006 SDLL06 - Transient Response of a clamped-Free Post Summary In this test case, the transient response of an unabated clamped-free beam, modelled by a spring mass system and subjected to any dynamic loading, is analyzed. The discrete flexion element, the calculation of the eigenmodes by the Lanczos method, and the calculation of the transient response by modal recombination of the structure subjected either to an accelerogram (modelization A) or to an equivalent imposed force (modelization B) are tested. The scheme d The results obtained are in good agreement with the reference results (analytical results). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry This is an issue originally proposed in the reference [bib1] and included in [bib2]. - \mathrm{AB} beam: slender beam without mass of length \mathrm{AB} , l=\mathrm{10 }m and {I}_{Z}=0,3285{m}^{4} inertial moment . - B point mass: m=43,8{10}^{\mathrm{3 }}\mathrm{kg} 1.2 Material properties | Young's modulus: | E=4.{10}^{10}\mathrm{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Density: | \rho =0\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions: The only travels allowed are x -axis translations. The point A is clamped: \mathrm{dx}=\mathrm{dy}=\mathrm{dz}=\mathrm{drx}=\mathrm{dry}=\mathrm{drz}=0 . Charges: - Modelling A: transverse acceleration to point A: \gamma (t) - Modelling B: point B transverse force: \mathrm{Fx}(t) with \mathrm{Fx}(t)=–\mathrm{m.}\gamma (t) 1.4 Initial conditions The system is at rest: t=0 , \mathrm{dx}(0)=0 , \mathrm{dx}/\mathrm{dt}(0)=0 in all point. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The problem is treated by a model with an degree of freedom. The pole is considered an unabated and non-heavy beam slender with k=3E{I}_{Z}/{l}^{\mathrm{3 }}=3,942{.10}^{\mathrm{7 }}N/m rigidity. The superstructure at the top of the pole is modelled by a point mass m=43,8{10}^{\mathrm{3 }}\mathrm{kg} . Both load cases lead to the calculation of the system response to an degree of freedom subject to \gamma (t) acceleration of any shape: \ddot{{x}_{r}}+{\omega}^{2}{x}_{r}=-\gamma (t) with \omega =\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{3E{I}_{z}}{m{l}^{3}}} the system's eigenfrequency and {x}_{r} the relative displacement of point B from point A . The solution is obtained by integration of Duhamel's integral [bib3]: {x}_{r}(t)=-\frac{m}{\omega}\underset{0}{\overset{t}{\int}}\gamma (t)\sin\omega (t-\tau )d\tau 2.2 Baseline Movement related to point B . For an imposed triangular acceleration, Duhamel's integral can be calculated analytically [bib3]: t<{t}_{0} : {x}_{r}=-\frac{{P}_{0}}{{\omega}^{2}{t}_{0}}(t-\frac{\sin\omega t}{\omega}) {t}_{0}<t<2{t}_{0} : {x}_{r}=-\frac{{P}_{0}}{{\omega}^{2}{t}_{0}}(2{t}_{0}-t-\frac{2\sin\omega (t-{t}_{0})}{\omega}-\frac{\sin\omega t}{\omega}) {t}_{0}<t<2{t}_{0} : {x}_{r}=-\frac{{P}_{0}}{{\omega}^{3}{t}_{0}}(2\sin\omega (t-{t}_{0})-\sin\omega (t-2{t}_{0})-\sin\omega t) 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution None if Duhamel's integral is calculated analytically [bib3]. In the order of the accuracy of the numerical integration method used to calculate Duhamel's integral ([bib1], [bib2]): Simpson's method with 40 points per period. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. R.W. Clough and J. Penzien: Dynamics of structures New York, Mac Graw-Hill, 1975, pp. 102-105 2. VPCS AFNOR Technical Guide - 1990 3. J.S. Przemieniecki: Theory of matrix structural analysis New York, MacGraw-Hill, 1968, pp. 351-357 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Elements are modeled by discrete elements at 6 degrees of freedom DIS_TR. v2.02.014 SDLL14 - Vibration modes of a thin pipe elbow v2.02.014 SDLL14 - Vibration modes of a thin pipe elbow Summary: This test is to search for the eigenfrequencies and associated vibration modes of a bent pipe. It allows to validate modellings elements finished TUYAU_3M (SEG3 and SEG4) and TUYAU_6M (SEG3). It also validates the option of calculating the largest frequencies of a structure. The results obtained are compared to an analytical reference solution. In addition, it validates modellings elements finished POU_D_T by comparing the results obtained with the reference results found in the reference as well as those obtained by Pipestress software. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Reference problem 1.2 Material properties The Material properties that make up the plate are: | E=2.1 \cdot {10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} | Young's modulus | | --- | --- | | \nu =0.3 | Poisson's ratio | | \rho =7800.\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} | Density | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads - boundary conditions: - C and D clamped sections - Point A : Next y and z moves null - Point B : Next x and z moves null 1.4 Initial conditions Not applicable 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The Rayleigh method applied to slender straight beam elements and a thin curved element beam allows the determination of parameters such as: - bending in the plane: {f}_{i}=\frac{{\lambda}_{i}^{2}}{2\pi {R}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{E{I}_{z}}{\rho A}} i=1,2 ; - transverse bending: {f}_{i}=\frac{{\mu}_{i}^{2}}{2\pi {R}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{G{I}_{p}}{\rho A}} i=1,2 ; The {\lambda}_{i}^{2} and {\mu}_{i}^{2} values are taken from a bib2 abacus. Bib2 abacus for \lambda_i and \mu_i In the modellings presented, the \frac{L}{R} ratio is 0 , 0.6 or 2 . The values taken in bib1 are: - \lambda_1^2 = 22.5 ; - \lambda_2^2 = 43 ; - \mu_1^2 = 9.5 ; - \mu_2^2 = 26.9 ; For \frac{L}{R} = 0 : - \lambda_1^2 = 17.8 ; - \lambda_2^2 = 34 ; - \mu_1^2 = 7.2 ; - \mu_2^2 = 21.5 ; For \frac{L}{R} = 0.6 : - \lambda_1^2 = 4.8 ; - \lambda_2^2 = 5.1 ; - \mu_1^2 = 3.85 ; - \mu_2^2 = 5.3 ; For \frac{L}{R} = 2 : This formulation is only suitable for very slender pipes: - Launch of straight parts above \frac{l}{{d}_{e}}>20 - Thin head such as \alpha R>100\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{z}}{A}} with \alpha , radian central angle. In addition, the values of the frequencies for transverse bending are not valid only for Poisson's ratio \nu = 0.3 after bib2. A coefficient of elbow flexibility is not necessary here. v2.02.015 SDLL15 - slender beam, clamped-free, with excreted mass or inertia v2.02.015 SDLL15 - slender beam, clamped-free, with excreted mass or inertia Summary: This three-dimensional problem consists in calculating the frequencies and vibration modes of a mechanical structure composed of a slender straight beam, clamped-free, tubular cross section and an excreted mass attached to the free end of the beam. This Structures Mechanics test corresponds to a dynamic analysis of a linear model with linear behavior. It consists of a single model. This problem allows testing the Euler Bernouilli beam element, the point mass model and the modal calculation by the Lanczos method. The results obtained are in good agreement with those of the VPCS guide. The two calculations performed (excentricity of the point mass zero or different from zero) allow to highlight the coupling of the different modes when the point mass is excreted. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Point coordinates (in m ): | | A | B | C | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | x | | | | | y | | | \mathit{yc} | | z | | | | length of beam: \mathit{AB}=L=10m C point mass: {m}_{c}=1000\mathit{kg} Tubular section: | outer diameter | \mathrm{de}=0.350m | | --- | --- | | inner diameter | \mathit{di}=0.320m | | Area | A=1.57865{10}^{-2}{m}^{2} | | inertia | \mathrm{Iy}=\mathrm{Iz}=2.21899{10}^{-4}{m}^{4} | | Polar inertia | \mathit{Ip}=4.43798{10}^{-4}{m}^{4} | | 2 cases studied: | \mathrm{yc}=0. | | --- | --- | | | \mathit{yc}=1.m | 1.2 Material properties E=2.1{10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} \rho =7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Point A clamped : ( u=v=w=0 , {\theta}_{x}={\theta}_{y}={\theta}_{z}=0 ). 1.4 Initial conditions Not applicable for modal analysis. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is the one given in the SDLL15/89 form of the VPCS guide which presents the calculation method as follows: The problem with non-excise mass leads to decoupled modes: - traction-compression (mass-only effect), - torsion (effect of inertia around the neutral fibre), - bending in planes x,y and x,z (mass effect). The different frequencies are determined with a model by elements finished beam d-Euler (slender beam). For the first mode with an excreted mass, a Rayleigh method gives the approach formula: {f}_{1}=\frac{1}{2\pi }\sqrt{\frac{3E{I}_{z}}{{L}^{3}({m}_{c}+0.24M)}} with M = total beam mass. When the mass is out of reach, (x,z) bending and twist modes are coupled, as well as (x,y) bending and traction-compression modes. For the proper mode, point B components are used to calculate the components at the centre of gravity of the mass (point C ) by: \left[\begin{array}{c}{u}_{c}\\ {v}_{c}\\ {w}_{c}\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{c}{u}_{B}\\ {v}_{B}\\ {w}_{B}\end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{ccc}0& {z}_{c}& -{y}_{c}\\ -{z}_{c}& 0& +{x}_{c}\\ +{y}_{c}& -{x}_{c}& 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}{\theta}_{\mathit{xB}}\\ {\theta}_{\mathit{yB}}\\ {\theta}_{\mathit{zB}}\end{array}\right] {u}_{c}={u}_{B}=-{\theta}_{\mathit{zB}} For this test: \begin{array}{c}{v}_{c}={v}_{B}\\ {w}_{c}={w}_{B}+{\theta}_{\mathit{xB}}\end{array} 2.2 Baseline Case 1: Top 10 eigenmodes. International Journal of Mechanical Sciences. 2016 May 1;110:116-26. 3 Post treatment of pipe model results import numpy as np def toroidal_to_cartesien(array_in:np.ndarray): """ Convert toroidal coordinates to Cartesian coordinates. This function takes an array of points in toroidal coordinates and converts them to Cartesian coordinates. The toroidal coordinates are expected to be in the format [u, v, w, phi], where: - u is the axial coordinate, - v is the orthoradial coordinate, - w is the radial coordinate, - phi is the angle described by v w.r.t. the Cartesien coordinates. The conversion formulas are: - X = u - Y = w cos(phi) - v sin(phi) - Z = w sin(phi) + v cos(phi) Parameters: array_in (np.ndarray): A 2D array where each row represents a point in toroidal coordinates [u, v, w, phi]. Returns: np.ndarray: A 2D array where each row represents a point in Cartesian coordinates [X, Y, Z]. """ # Extract data orthor = array_in[:, 1] radial = array_in[:, 2] cos_phi = np.cos(array_in[:, 3]) sin_phi = np.sin(array_in[:, 3]) array_out = np.copy(array_in) # array_out[:, 0] = array_in[:, 0] array_out[:, 1] = radial cos_phi - orthor sin_phi array_out[:, 2] = radial sin_phi + orthor cos_phi return array_out[:, :3] # Return only X Y Z def postprocess_shell_displacement(U_s:np.ndarray, nb_modes:int, angles:np.ndarray): """ Postprocess the shell displacement data to extract axial, ortho-radial, and radial displacements as a function of azimuthal angle and radial position. The input array U_s is expected to be an array containing the displacement components of the middle surface of a shell structure. The structure of U_s is as follows: - For each Fourier mode (from 1 to nb_modes ), the displacements are listed in the order: [u^i_m, v^i_m, w^i_m, u^o_m, v^o_m, w^o_m] - The displacement for mode 0 are listed at the end in the following order: [w^o, w^i_1, w^o_1] Here, i denotes the in-plane Fourier displacement and o denotes the out-plane Fourier displacement, and m denotes the Fourier mode. The number of modes, also called nb_modes , is either 3 or 6. The angles array contains the azimuthal angles at which the displacements are evaluated. The function returns a 2D array where each row corresponds to a different angle. The first three columns are the axial, ortho-radial, and radial displacements, respectively. """ displacement = np.array([[0, 0, 0, phi] for phi in angles]) for i, phi in enumerate(angles): block_list = [] for m in range(2, nb_modes+1): block = np.array([ [np.cos(m phi), 0, 0], [0, np.sin(m phi), 0], [0, 0, np.cos(m phi)] ]) block_list.append(block) for m in range(2, nb_modes+1): block = np.array([ [np.sin(m phi), 0, 0], [0, np.cos(m phi), 0], [0, 0, np.sin(m phi)] ]) block_list.append(block) block = np.array([ [0, 0, 0], [0, np.sin(phi), -np.cos(phi)], [1, np.cos(phi), np.sin(phi)], ]) block_list.append(block) displacement[i, :-1] = np.block(block_list) @ U_s return displacement def postprocess_beam_displacement(U_p:np.ndarray, radius:float, angles:np.ndarray): """ Postprocess the beam displacement data to extract axial, ortho-radial, and radial displacements as a function of azimuthal angle and radial position. The input array U_p is expected to be an array containing the displacement components of the section of a beam structure. The structure of U_p is as follows: - The beam displacements [DX, DY, DZ] are the first three components of U_p, - The beam rotations [RX, RY, RZ] are the last three components of U_p. The angles array contains the azimuthal angles at which the displacements are evaluated. The radius float is the value of the middle radius of the cylindrical shell. The function returns a 2D array where each row corresponds to a different angle. The first three columns are the axial, ortho-radial, and radial displacements, respectively. """ displacement = np.array([[0, 0, 0, phi] for phi in angles]) for i, phi in enumerate(angles): displacement[i, 0] = U_p[0] + U_p[5] radius np.sin(phi) - U_p[4] radius np.cos(phi) displacement[i, 1] = U_p[2] np.sin(phi) - U_p[1] np.cos(phi) - U_p[3] radius displacement[i, 2] = -(U_p[2] np.cos(phi) + U_p[1] np.sin(phi)) return displacement def sum_toroidal_coords(array_list:list): """ Sum an arbitrary number of arrays of toroidal coordinates. This function takes a list of arrays, each representing toroidal coordinates, and returns a single array containing the sum of the input arrays. The input arrays are expected to have the same shape, with the last axis representing the angle values. Parameters: array_list (list): A list of arrays, where each array represents a set of toroidal coordinates. Returns: np.ndarray: A single array containing the sum of the input arrays, with the same shape as the individual arrays. """ assert len(array_list) > 0, "At least one array" array_out = np.copy(array_list[0]) if len(array_list) > 1: for array in array_list[1:]: array_out[..., :-1] += array[..., :-1] return array_out # Define global variables # For importing and exporting import os SUFIX = '6m' # '3m' or '6m' DIRPATH = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) COORDS = np.load(f"{DIRPATH}/output/coords_{SUFIX}.npy") DEPLS = np.load(f"{DIRPATH}/output/displacements_{SUFIX}.npy") # For post-processing RADIUS = 1 ANGLES = np.linspace(0, 2 np.pi, 120) # For plotting OFFSET = 2.5 VMIN, VMAX = 0, 2 NBTICKS = 11 NBCOLORS = 2 NBTICKS-1 # Loop through each frequency from matplotlib import colors, cm, gridspec, pyplot as plt nb_freqs, nb_coords = np.shape(DEPLS)[:2] nb_freqs = np.min([nb_freqs, 18]) for ii in range(nb_freqs): fig = plt.figure(figsize=(9, 4)) gs = gridspec.GridSpec(1, 2, width_ratios=[1, 2.5], figure=fig) ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0]) ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1], projection='3d') # Loop through each coordinate XX_all, YY_all, ZZ_all, VV_all = [], [], [], [] for jj in range(nb_coords): # Compute the total displacement beam_disp = postprocess_beam_displacement(U_p=DEPLS[ii, jj, :6], radius=RADIUS, angles=ANGLES) shell_disp = postprocess_shell_displacement(U_s=DEPLS[ii, jj, 6:], nb_modes=int(SUFIX[0]), angles=ANGLES) total_disp cylinder in cartesien coordinates new_cylinder = toroidal_to_cartesien(sum_toroidal_coords([old_cylinder, total_disp])) # Collect the data for later plotting XX_all.append(new_cylinder[:, 0]) np.array(XX_all) YY_all = np.array(YY_all) ZZ_all = np.array(ZZ_all) VV_all = np.array(VV_all) # Create the scatter plot for this frequency ax1.scatter(YY_all, ZZ_all, c=VV_all, OFFSET]) ax1.set_aspect('equal') sc = ax2.scatter(XX_all, YY_all, ZZ_all, c=VV_all, norm=colors.Normalize(vmin=VMIN, vmax=VMAX), cmap=cm.get_cmap('viridis', NBCOLORS)) ax2.grid(False) v2.02.023 SDLL23 - clamped-free earthquake beam (spectral response) v2.02.023 SDLL23 - clamped-free earthquake beam (spectral response) Summary This unidirectional problem consists of performing a spectral seismic analysis of a clamped-free beam, equipped with two localized masses, subjected to a three-dimensional excitation provided as a pseudoacceleration oscillator spectrum. Through this problem, COMB_SISM_MODAL operator's DPC, SRSS, CQC and DSC modal combinations are tested. The SRSS combination is tested with consideration of neglected modes. In addition, CALC_MODES, NORM_MODE, MODE_STATIQUE, DEFI_FONCTION and DEFI_NAPPE operators are tested. The results obtained for Modelling A, relating to Euler beams, are in agreement with the results of other codes, for cases without taking into account the pseudomode. The differences with the reference results in the case where the pseudomode is taken into account are explained by a different calculation hypothesis for the determination of this pseudomode. The Modelling B, in Euler beams, is relative to a more refined mesh than that of Modelling A.
