The total cross section of the top steels is {3.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} and the lower steels is {4.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} . 1.2 Material properties - concrete: E=2.{10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} ; \nu =0.2 ; \rho =2400{\mathit{kg.m}}^{-3} ; \alpha =10-5{K}^{-1} - steel: E=2,1.{10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} ; \nu =0.33 ; \rho =7800{\mathit{kg.m}}^{-3} ; \alpha =10-5{K}^{-1} 1.3 boundary conditions Simple support in B : \mathit{dy}=0 "Double" support in A : \mathit{dx}=\mathit{dy}=\mathit{dz}=0 as well as \mathit{rx}=\mathit{ry}=0 . 1.4 Loading Three load cases are tested successively: - Loading 1: concentrated effort in beam media, F=10000N - Loading 2: own beam weight, g=9,8{\mathit{m.s}}^{-2} - Loading 3: Uniform heating of the \Delta T=100K beam 2 reference solution The reference calculations are based on a simple elastic calculation in RdM. 2.1 Elastic centre In simple bending, for elastic behaviour, the neutral axis passes through the elastic centre (barycentre of sections weighted by the material modules): C such as {\int}_{S}E\overrightarrow{\mathit{CM}}\mathit{dS}=\overrightarrow{0} The position of the centres of gravity of the concrete alone is determined first and steel alone relative to point O . \begin{array}{c}{y}_{{G}_{b}}=\frac{0.125\times 0.3\times 0.05-0.125\times 0.2\times 0.05}{0.2\times 0.05+0.1\times 0.2+0.3\times 0.05}=1.38888{10}^{-2}m\\ {y}_{{G}_{a}}=\frac{0.125\times 3-0.125\times 4}{3+4}=-1.78571{10}^{-2}m\\ {z}_{{G}_{a}}={z}_{{G}_{b}}=0m\end{array} The position of the C elastic centre can then be determined. \overrightarrow{\mathit{OC}}=\frac{{E}_{a}{S}_{a}\overrightarrow{{\mathit{OG}}_{a}}+{E}_{b}{S}_{b}\overrightarrow{{\mathit{OG}}_{b}}}{{E}_{a}{S}_{a}+{E}_{b}{S}_{b}} The {S}_{b} concrete section is 0,045{m}^{2} and the {S}_{a} steel section is {7.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} . The Young's modulus of the concrete is {2.10}^{10}\mathit{MPa} and the {21.10}^{10}\mathit{MPa} steel section is {21.10}^{10}\mathit{MPa} . \begin{array}{c}{y}_{c}=\frac{2\times 0.045\times 1.38888-21\times 7{10}^{-4}\times 1.78571}{2\times 0.045+21\times 7{10}^{-4}}=0.94317{10}^{-2}m\\ {z}_{c}=0m\end{array} 2.2 Quadratic times The quadratic moments of rectangular concrete sections are calculated by the following formula: \frac{b{h}^{3}}{12}+b\times h\times {d}^{2} Where, b represents the width, h the height and distance from the centre of gravity of the section from the axis for which the moment is calculated. The quadratic moment of the concrete cross section is then obtained in relation to the z axis through the elastic centre: \begin{array}{cc}{I}_{\mathit{béton}}& =\frac{0.3\times {0.05}^{3}}{12}+(0.3\times 0.05)\cdot {(0.125-0.94317\cdot {10}^{-2})}^{2}+\frac{0.1\times {0.2}^{3}}{12}+(0.1\times 0.2)\cdot {(0.94317\cdot {10}^{-2})}^{2}\\ & +\frac{0.2\times {0.05}^{3}}{12}+(0.2\times 0.05)\cdot {(0.125+0.94317\cdot {10}^{-2})}^{2}=0.4547\cdot {10}^{-3}{m}^{4}\end{array} Inertials of steels are calculated by the following formula: \frac{\pi {\phi }^{4}}{64}+S\times {d}^{2}\approx S\times {d}^{2} Where, \phi represents the diameter of the steel, S the cross section of steel and the distance from the centre of gravity of the cross section to the axis for which the moment is calculated. The diameter of the steels being small, the first term is neglected. The quadratic moment of the steel sections is obtained from the z axis through the elastic centre: 3{10}^{-4}\times {(0.125-0.94317{10}^{-2})}^{2}+4{10}^{-4}\times {(0.125+0.94317{10}^{-2})}^{2}=0.1124{10}^{-4}{m}^{4} For the complete section of the beam, the quadratic moment weighted by the d-Young modules of the material is: \mathit{EI}=2{10}^{10}\times 0.4547{10}^{-3}+21{10}^{10}\times 0.1124{10}^{-4}=11.4544{10}^{6}\mathit{Pa}.{m}^{4} 2.3 Load case 1 For load 1 (concentrated load in the middle of the beam), the deflection is calculated by the following RDM formula: f=\frac{F\times {l}^{3}}{48\mathit{EI}} Which gives the deflection: f=\frac{10000\times {5}^{3}}{48\times 11.4544{10}^{6}}=2.2735{10}^{-3}m The following generalised efforts can also be calculated: - l-shear force at the beginning of the beam (left part) is \frac{F}{2}=5000N , - the bending moment in the middle of the beam is \frac{F\times l}{4}=1.25{10}^{4}\mathit{N.m} . 2.4 Load case 2 For load case 2 (clean beam weight), the deflection is calculated by the strength formula of the following materials: f=\frac{5\times p\times {l}^{4}}{384\mathit{EI}} where p is the linear load due to the weight of the materials: p=g({\rho}_{a}{S}_{a}+{\rho}_{b}{S}_{b})=9.8\times (2800\times 7{10}^{-4}+2400\times 0.045)=1111.9{\mathit{N.m}}^{-1} Which gives the deflection: f=\frac{5\times 1111.9\times {5}^{4}}{384\times 11.4544{10}^{6}}=7.9{10}^{-4}m 2.5 Load case 3 For load 3 (homogeneous temperature rise), the beam being isostatic and the coefficients of expansion of concrete and steel being identical, the solution is simple: The general constraints and efforts are zero. The lengthening of the beam is: \Delta l=\alpha \times l\times \Delta T This gives with the values of our case: \Delta l={10}^{-5}\times 5\times 100=5.{10}^{-3}m 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics POU_D_EM modelling is used. 3.2 Mesh characteristics Longitudinal mesh of the beam: We have 3 nodes and 2 elements (POU_D_EM). The concrete part of the cross-section of the beam is meshed (DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE / SECT) while the steels are given directly as 4 point fibers in DEFI_GEOM_FIBRE / FIBRE. Two meshes of the concrete part are tested for the load case 1. The fine mesh is made of 120 fibres and the coarse mesh consists of 16 fibres: Note: The problem being \mathrm{2D} , only one fiber in width might seem sufficient (multilayers), but this would lead to zero terms in the rigidity matrix (the own inertia of the fibres not being taken into account) and to an error in the resolution of the equations system. 3.3 Tested quantities and results 3.3.1 Load case 1 | | Reference | | --- | --- | | deflection | | | (mesh fin) | 2,2735 10–3 | | deflection | | | (mesh coarse) | 2,2735 10–3 | | shear force | | | ( A support ) | 5000 | | bending moment | | | (Middle) | 1,25 104 | | | The calculations are made without taking into account the specific inertia of each fibre. Note: The moments on the beams are affected by AFFE_CHAR_MECA and AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F, FORCE_POUTRE operand, MX, MY, MZ, MT, MFY and MFZ key words. They are applicable to constant-character straight beams. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A 1m length beam is considered to be X -oriented or Z -oriented according to modellings. 1.2 Loading 1.2.1 boundary conditions In each case, the node A is clamped. Then depending on the type of moment tested, the node B can either be left free or supported in a given direction. 1.2.2 Time distribution The MX, MY, MZ, MT, MFY and MFZ key words are applied in turn. To test distributed moments affected by the AFFE_CHAR_MECA command, this list is supplemented by constant loadings. 2 reference solution 2.1 Torsion time A analytical solution for the twist moment is easily found by a Material Resistance calculation. Either \mathit{AB} beam length L , clamped in A , if you apply a \mathit{mt} twist moment to point C from [\mathit{AB}] then the resulting A moment is \mathit{mt} . The reaction depending on the moment is -\mathit{mt} . v3.01.121 SSLL121 – Pressures: Calculation of nodes SIPO_ELNO stress v3.01.121 SSLL121 – Pressures: Calculation of nodes SIPO_ELNO stress Summary: The objective of this test is to verify the calculation of SIPO_ELNO stresses in the presence of specification of coefficients of flexibility and stress intensification on beams. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry studied is a straight cylindrical section of 10m long according to the Ox axis, of 500mm external radius and 100mm thickness. 1.2 Characteristics and materials The Young's modulus of the beam is E=200 GPa. The pipe segment has: - two coefficients of flexibility cflex, depending on the Y axis and the Z axis, - Two coefficients of intensification of the isigm stresses, according to the Y axis and the Z axis. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The section is anchored in (0.0), node group FIXA. A force of 1e6 N is applied to the free end of the section, to the group of node TIPA. The force is either on the Oy axis or on the Oz axis. 1.4 Purpose The correct calculation of SIPO_ELNO stresses is checked by taking into account flexibilities and stress intensification coefficients. 2 reference solution 2.1 Inertia moment of tubular section By defining: - d_{ext} = 2R : outer diameter, - d_{int} = d_{ext} - 2e_p : inner diameter, the inertia moment of a hollow circular cross section is given by: I = \frac{\pi}{64} \left( d_{ext}^4 - d_{int}^4 \right) . 2.2 Calculation of the deflection The deflection at the end of a clamped tubular beam subjected to F-force is given by: \delta = \frac{F \cdot L^3}{3 \cdot E \cdot I} Note: in the presence of a Timoshenko beam, this solution is approximate, as the deflection depends not only on the bending moment but also on shearing effort. In the presence of a {c_{flex}} flexibility coefficient, the deflection is amplified as follows: I_{c_{flex}} = \frac{I}{c_{flex}}, \delta = \frac{F \cdot L^3}{3 \cdot E \cdot I_{c_{flex}}}. 2.3 Calculation of SIPO constraints SIPO constraints due to bending moment M_f = -F \cdot L are defined by: \sigma = \frac{M_f}{I} \cdot R, With R the outer radius of the tubular beam. They are amplified where appropriate by the stress intensification coefficient sif . \sigma = sif \cdot \frac{M_f}{I} \cdot R Note: The stress calculation is done with the "real" inertia moment, not modified by the flexibility coefficient. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics The mesh consists of two mesh cells SEG2 of equal length. 3.2 Modelling characteristics The beam is modelled by Timoshenko beams with elements POU_D_T. 3.3 Boundary conditions and loads The beam is clamped at the node FIXA group with DDL_IMPO. The force is applied at the other end of the beam at the node TIPA group with FORCE_NODALE. 3.4 Tested quantities and results The values tested are SIPO_NOEU stresses at the anchor level (group of node FIXA) and deflections at the free end (group of node TIPA). The analytical expressions are in the command file and are used to test all calculated values and all reference values in the TEST_RESU. 4 Summary of the results For each model processed, the results are analytical solution. Note that the accuracy in terms of deflection has been slightly relaxed, the deflection of the Timoshenko beams also depending on shearing efforts, neglected here.

v3.01.403 SSLL403 - Flaming of a beam under the effect of its own weight v3.01.403 SSLL403 - Flaming of a beam under the effect of its own weight Summary: This test allows linear elasticity to validate the load due to gravity forces for straight beam Modelling of Euler (POU_D_E). It also allows the implementation and validation of the geometric stiffness matrix calculation. The reference solution is analytical and the results are considered satisfactory. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Figure 1.1-a : Vertical beam. Rectangular section : {H}_{y}=0.01m , {H}_{z}=0.01m Length: L=1m 1.2 Material properties | Young's modulus : | E=2.{10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio : | \nu =0,3 | | Density: | \rho =7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading boundary condition : Clamped (0) End: \mathit{DX}=\mathit{DY}=\mathit{DZ}=\mathit{DRX}=\mathit{DRY}=\mathit{DRZ}=0 . Charge: Gravity force: p weight per unit length with g=(0,0,-9.81) (data as a global benchmark). 2 Reference solutions 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solutions As a local reference, x along the \mathit{OA} axis of the beam, the bending moment, at the x abscisse, is expressed as follows: {M}_{{F}_{y}}(x)=p{\int}_{x}^{L}\left[v(\xi )-v(x)\right]d\xi . The deflection v(x) therefore satisfies the equation: E{I}_{z}=\frac{{d}^{2}v}{{\mathrm{dx}}^{2}}=p{\int}_{x}^{L}\left[v(\xi )-v(x)\right]d\xi =-p\left[{\int}_{x}^{L}v(\xi )d\xi +(L-x)v(x)\right] By drifting the two members, the differential equation is obtained: \frac{{d}^{3}v}{{\mathrm{dx}}^{3}}+\frac{p}{E{I}_{z}}(L-x)\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}}=0 The v'(x)=\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{dx}} function satisfies the linear and homogeneous differential equation of the second order: \frac{{d}^{\mathrm{2v}}'}{{\mathrm{dx}}^{2}}+\frac{p}{E{I}_{z}}(L-x)v'=0 , which can be solved using the functions of Bessel. The value of the critical linear weight is then equal to: {p}_{c}=7,837\frac{E{I}_{z}}{{L}^{3}} . The analytical solution gives numerically: {p}_{c}=7,8372{10}^{11}\cdot \frac{{10}^{-8}}{12}=1,3061667{10}^{3} . 2.2 Baseline The critical value of the \lambda multiplier: {\lambda}_{c}=\frac{{P}_{c}}{\rho Sg} 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution analytical solution. 2.4 Bibliographical references [1] Report No 2314/A of the Aerotechnical Institute "Proposal and implementation of new test cases missing at the validation of beams Aster " 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The model is composed of 10 elements straight beam d 3.2 Mesh characteristics It consists of 10 elements POU_D_E. 3.3 Tested quantities and results System own value ( K+\lambda {K}_{G} ) X=0 : | | Reference | Error | | --- | --- | --- | | \lambda | 170.701 | 0.01 | 3.4 Note Since {p}_{c}=\lambda \rho Sg , ( \rho Sg represents the linear prestress), we have as a critical load: {p}_{c}=1300,84{\mathrm{N.m}}^{-1} . 4 Summary of the results The results are very close to the analytical solution (difference: \text{1\%} for 10 elements). This difference is a function of the discretization finesse being given the assumptions used for geometric rigidity (cf.[R3.08.01]). This therefore validates this type of load for the d-Euler flaming.

v3.02.108 SSLP108 - clamped Arche in elasticity v3.02.108 SSLP108 - clamped Arche in elasticity Summary: The objective of this test is to check D_PLAN_MIX_STA Modelling on clamped arch problem in elasticity. This problem allows to test the application of symmetry conditions to the generalised displacement components corresponding to deformations. 1 Reference problem The problem is derived from article [1]. 1.1 Geometry The geometry can be viewed in the figure below and will be used for all modellings. Figure 1.1-1: Géométrie de la membrane We're taking t=1\mathit{mm} and R=10\mathit{mm} . We represent only the right half of the ark, so to exploit the symmetries of the problem. 1.2 Material properties The material is elastic. - Elasticity module: E=200\mathit{\;MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu = 0,3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The segment is embedded at the bottom of the arch ( \mathit{DX}=\mathit{DY}=0 ). Vertical surface force applied to the centre section such as \mathit{FY}=-1 \mathit{kN}/\mathit{mm}\mathrm{²} The right half of the arch is modeled only. v3.02.109 SSLP109 - Validation of a feature of the DDL_STAB option v3.02.109 SSLP109 - Validation of a feature of the DDL_STAB option Summary: This test allows validation of a feature of DDL_STAB option CRIT_STAB, which evaluates the stability of steady state found by numerical simulation of non-conservative problems such as damage problems. This requires the application of an optimization algorithm under unequal constraints. The option can be applied to a list containing any degree of freedom available in Code_Aster. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Theoretical framework In the case of a conservative problem, the stability of the equilibrium state is defined by the strict positivity of all the tangential operator's own values. This is written, in the case of a tangential K symmetric operator: \underset{x}{\mathit{Min}}(\frac{{x}^{T}.\mathit{Kx}}{{x}^{T}.x})>0 In the case of non-conservative problems, unilateral conditions of irreversibility are imposed on certain components of the x vector. The previous inequality becomes sufficient but not necessary to deduce the stability of a state of equilibrium. One of the features developed in the stress optimization algorithm is limited to the calculation of the smallest own value (quantity that is accessed quickly), when this is a positive sign. In this case, the reference value for the stability criterion is exactly that of the smallest own value, recalculated from the power method. No additional projection steps are performed to determine the exact value of the minimum under unequal constraints. This allows for a calculation time gain. The test case presented here is an interest in a uniform tensile bar, whose behavior is purely elastic. The elastic character is conservative and ensures the strict positivity of the smallest tangential operator's own value. Therefore, we are in the precise case where the function described above is triggered. 1.2 Geometry A \mathrm{2D} bar of length L=4m is considered to be h=0.5m height Figure 1 : Problem Representation 1.3 Material properties 1.3.1 Elastic Law: material ELAS Characteristics : E=1\text{Pa} , \nu =0. 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads clamped support : Impaired \mathit{DY}=0m displacements . on all nodes and \mathit{DX}=0m . on the left side ( x=0. ). See Figure 1. Load 1 : Linear displacement imposed {U}_{1} on right side ( x=4. ): {U}_{1}=t\cdot {10}^{-6}\text{m} 2 reference solution The smallest tangential operator's own value, calculated by the CRIT_STAB operator, is 0.146447 . 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics D_PLAN modelling is used. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains 4 elements QUAD4. 3.3 Tested quantities and results | NUMERO | TYPE_REFERENCE | VALE_REF | TOLERANCE | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 0.14644700 | 5.0E-04% | Table 1: Comparaison de l'estimation du critère de stabilité avec la valeur de référence 4 Summary of the results The DDL_STAB option has a value of the stability criterion equal to the smallest own value calculated by CRIT_STAB. The algorithm developed for the specified functionality is therefore validated.

v3.02.111 FORMA05 - Practical work of the "Rupture Mechanics" training: Traction cracked plate (SENT) v3.02.111 FORMA05 - Practical work of the "Rupture Mechanics" training: Traction cracked plate (SENT) Summary: This \mathrm{2D} test (plane deformations) models a cracked plate (pure mode I) into a quasi-static form. This is a Modelling of the SENT test piece (Single Edge Notched Specimen in Voltage). This test is used in the "Mechanics of the Rupture" formation because of the speed of the execution time and the existence of an analytical solution. It allows to become familiar with the post-processings in linear elastic break mechanics (operators CALC_G , and POST_K1_K2_K3 ) for FEM and X-FEM modelling. The educational objectives are the illustration of the influence of mesh (mesh with linear / quadratic / quadratic elements + Barsium) and the illustration of independence to the coronas of integration for the G-theta method. This test case has 4 modellings: - Modelling A: FEM, whole plate (without symmetry condition), mesh free - Modelling B: FEM, (half-)plate with symmetry condition, mesh free - Modelling C: X-FEM, whole plate (without symmetry condition), mesh set - Modelling D: FEM, whole plate (without symmetry condition), mesh radiating Only Modelling A is the subject of a TP session as part of the training. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A rectangular H=2\,\mathrm{m} height plate, W=1\,\mathrm{m} width, with flat deformation, with a horizontal crack leading to depth a=0,1\,\mathrm{m} is considered. This geometry is presented on the v3.02.111-fig-geom. : Schematic of the cracked plate 1.2 Material properties A homogeneous isotropic material with linear elasticity is considered to have the following characteristics: - Young's modulus : E=210000\,\mathrm{MPa} - Poisson's ratio : \nu=0,3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The plate is loaded in traction: \sigma=10\,\mathrm{MPa} . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method used for reference solution The reference solution for the stress factor of the I K_I mode is expressed as follows [1]: K_I=\sigma \sqrt{\pi a}F\left(\frac{a}{W}\right) with F\left(\frac{a}{W}\right)=1,122-0,231\left(\frac{a}{W}\right)+10,550{\left(\frac{a}{W}\right)}^{2}-21,710{\left(\frac{a}{W}\right)}^{3}+30,382{\left(\frac{a}{W}\right)}^{4} This expression of F is derived from a least square regression (Gross 1964; Brown 1966). The announced accuracy of this formula is 0.5% for \frac{a}{W}{\le}0,6 . Note: in [1] are given other formulas for F\left(a/W\right) , e.g. a formula due to Tada (1973) that shows a precision of less than 0.5% for any a/W ratio. The G energy return rate is obtained using the formula d-Irwin: G=\frac{1-{\nu}^2}{E} K_I^2 . The expected accuracy for the G reference value will be less than 1%. 2.2 Baseline With the numerical values of the statement, we find: F\left(a/W\right)\approx 1,186 {K}_{I}\approx 6,646 \,\mathrm{MPa.\sqrt{m}} G\approx 191,4 \,\mathrm{J.m^{-2}} Note : Using the alternative formula of Tada 1973, F\left(a/W\right)\approx 1,196 is obtained, i.e. an difference between the 2 references of approximately 0.8%. Considering the details announced for each reference, it is inferred that the theoretical value lies between these 2 references. It would therefore certainly be more wise to choose the average value F\left(a/W\right)\approx 1,191 as a reference value. However, in the next few years, reference solution is considered to be the one from the regression by least squares (Gross 1964; Brown 1966). 2.3 Bibliographical references 1. Tada, P. Paris, G. Irwin, The stress analysis of cracks manual, 3rd edition, 2000 3 Modelling A: FEM, whole plate (without symmetry condition), mesh free 3.1 TP procedure For this TP, two possibilities are offered to obtain the mesh of the cracked plate: - you can recover the cracked mesh directly: see the instructions given in § v3.02.111-section-recup-mesh - you can create it yourself: see the instructions given in § v3.02.111-section-creation-mesh 3.1.1 Recovery of mesh with Salome-Meca For this TP, you can recover the mesh forma05a.mmed directly. It is a mesh with the mesh cells linear. The groups are described on the v3.02.111-fig-mail: : mesh forma05a with its groups The groups defined are: | Nodes groups | FRONT | This group contains a single node: the node corresponding to the crack front. This node will also be used to block certain rigid modes | | --- | --- | --- | | | C | This group contains a single node: the node located in the middle of the right side of the plate, used to block rigid modes | | Mesh cells 1d groups | HAUT | Top of plate | | | BAS | Lower plate line | | | LEV_SUP | Upper lip of crack | | | LEV_INF | Lower lip of crack | As a reminder, the aim is to apply a pressure equal to 10 MPa on the HAUT line and on the BAS line. This is to check whether the XFEM Modelling accurately represents the analytical solution, the mechanics of the break. This analytical field is the exact solution for the I opening problem of a flat crack. The domain is a square plate, cut to the middle by a horizontal crack. A load is imposed on the 4 edges to ensure a strict opening in I mode, conforming to the analytical solution. Limit conditions of type "moving" on the unfungible edges, and of type "force" on the edge cut by the crack. To validate this approach, we are considering 3 modellings: - Modelling A: A simple calculation is performed from linear elements (TRIA3) for a horizontal crack - Modelling B: a simple calculation is performed from quadratic elements (TRIA6) for a horizontal crack - Modelling C: The crack is tilted to change the reference of analytical formulas. To keep the opening in I mode, the fields (stress and displacement) imposed on the edges are tilted. On the one hand, the impact of the form of the domain on the results is evaluated, since in theory, asymptotic equations do not depend on the geometry of the domain in the reference of the crack. On the other hand, the robustness of the calculation with the degradation of the conditioning is evaluated. - Modelling D: A simple calculation is performed from linear elements (TRIA3) for a horizontal crack, in flat stresses - Modelling E: A simple calculation is performed from quadratic elements (TRIA6) for a horizontal crack, in flat stresses The stress intensity factors \mathrm{KI} , \mathrm{KII} are tested. For I mode, \mathrm{KII}=0 and \mathit{KI}

In paragraph [ 19 ], the evolution of the displacement field was restored to a wide angle of inclination, thus demonstrating that the calculated displacement field remains invariant in the local crack-related repository: the asymptotic field "suits" the crack movement, according to theory. Therefore, the geometry of the domain in the crack repository, the regularity and "directionality" of the mesh, have no influence on the accuracy of the test case calculations, with linear elements. Furthermore, there is no evidence of a transition zone between the boundary conditions of Dirichlet and Neumann. For example, in model C, the \mathit{L2} test of the error on the move is performed on the corner of the Neumann loading and Dirichlet condition. The displacement calculated by Aster "paste" to the analytical solution. Should it also be ensured that the same is true for the stress field? Developments in the code_Aster should put in place a calculation of the standard in energy to confirm these observations. In model C, the angle of inclination is between -135° and 135° because of the limit condition of Dirichlet on one of the edges of the domain. Given the symmetry of the problem, continuing this study on the rest of the trigonometric circle does not seem relevant. - On the other hand, model B shows that validation is possible with quadratic elementss. v3.02.115 SSLP115 - Calculation of the energy return rate of a cracked disc in the presence of initial stresses v3.02.115 SSLP115 - Calculation of the energy return rate of a cracked disc in the presence of initial stresses Summary This test validates the calculation of the energy return rate by the theta method in the presence of a state of initial stress. Model A: a clamped disc and cracked is subjected to an initial stress field opening the crack. This initial stress field is identical to that generated by a thermal gradient. The solution is identical to that obtained in the case of thermal loading alone, validating the consideration of an initial stress state. Modelling B: it is similar to Modelling A with a non-grided crack (X-FEM). Modelling C: it is similar to Modelling A. Material coefficients are defined by constant temperature functions. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A \mathrm{100mm} ray disc, clamped on its edges, containing a horizontal crack of \mathrm{23mm} , one of which is at the centre of the disc, is considered. Figure 1.1: Géométrie du disque. . 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus: E=210000\mathrm{MPa} Poisson's ratio: \nu =0,3 Thermal expansion coefficient: \alpha ={10}^{-5}{K}^{-1} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The disc is totally clamped on its edge. It is subjected to an initial stress field obtained by applying a thermal load with a strong gradient in the horizontal direction (see and ). Figure 1.2: Gradient de température appliqué au disque encastré. Figure 1.3: Création du champ de contraintes initiales. 1.4 reference solution The reference solution is the one obtained by applying the thermal load directly to the cracked disc without initial condition. Indeed, since the behaviour is elastic, the superposition principle applies and the results in the presence of thermal loading without initial stresses and in the absence of thermal stresses with initial stresses are equivalent, as summarized in . Figure 1.4: Équivalence des chargements. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Mesh characteristics The mesh is quadratic radiating around the crack; it consists of 27670 nodes forming 9519 mesh cells, 100 triangles allowing de-refining. The mesh cells are quadratic. elements type "Barsium" are used at both bottoms of the crack. The mesh used and have the mesh. Figure 2.1: Maillage du disque. Figure 2.2: Maillage : zoom sur la fissure. From the mesh, several crowns are defined which will be used later, during the post-processing in the break-up mechanics. Each crown is characterized by the data of a lower radius (R_INF) and a higher radius (R_SUP). The correspondence is also given in terms of the number of layers d | | Value of R_INF (mm) | Value of R_SUP (mm) | Number of layers correspondence d | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Crown No. 1 | 1,009 | 2,05 | 2h-4h | | Crown No. 2 | 2,05 | 4,228 | 4h-8h | | Crown No. 3 | 4,228 | 9,0 | 8h-16h | 2.2 Calculations It is recalled that the principle of this test to verify equivalence between the consideration of an initial state and an equivalent thermal load, when post-processing of the mechanical failure is used. The quantities of interest is the energy return rate (G) and stress intensity factors (limited here to KI because configuration only requires mode I due to symmetry). Paragraph 2.3.1 details the different ways to post-treat those quantities that are used and tested. Modelization : The configuration is bidimental. Mechanical calculations are performed under the hypothesis of Planes Deformations. Reference scale: Since analytical solution is not known, the first step is to generate the calculation as the reference: i.e. the thermo-linear elasticity calculation. The creation of the temperature field is followed by the thermo-elastic bonding calculation, following which two types of post-processings are made: - a post-processing in breaking mechanics to determine the reference values of the quantities of interest, - extraction of the stress field, which will serve as the initial stress field. Calculum with initial constraints: An incremental linear elasticity calculation with an initial state given as an initial stress field, with the presence of the crack, is performed. It is important to note that l-initial state is specified via an initial stress field , not by the result type (EVOL_NOLI) concept data in the resolution operator. Then, post-processings in breaker mechanics are made. To test the different possibilities offered by the CALC_G command, several configurations are implemented, which differ by the type of initial stress field provided to the CALC_G command: at Gauss points, nodes by element or nodes. 2.3 Tested quantities and results 2.3.1 Quantities tested The values of the energy return rate (G) from: - CALC_G operator, option G. The values of the stress intensity factor in mode I (KI) obtained from: - CALC_G operator, option K, - POST_K1_K2_K3 operator. For post-processings with CALC_G operator, the 3 previously defined crowns are systematically tested. Finally, each time, the values from the reference calculation were compared to the values from the initial state calculation, with iso-condition (the same representation of the initial stress field, v3.02.119 SSLP119 – Calculation of the static safety factor of a homogeneous embankment with POST_NEWMARK v3.02.119 SSLP119 – Calculation of the static safety factor of a homogeneous embankment with POST_NEWMARK Summary: This test compares the static safety factor estimates for a homogeneous embankment by POST_NEWMARK to other methods used by other geotechnical computing software. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A homogeneous embankment of 15 m high and slope 1:2 (26.6°) is considered. A sliding circle joining the top and bottom of the embankment is considered, the centre of which is positioned at (6.08, 49.6). (-30,15) (0,0) Figure 1- Configuration du remblai et positionnement du cercle de glissement. 1.2 Material properties 1.2.1 Elastic properties of the material The mechanical characteristics of the material constituting the embankment are summarised in the table below: | | E(\mathit{MPa}) | \rho (\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{\mathrm{²}}) | \nu | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SLOPE | 90 | 1936 | 0.3 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and mechanical loadings 1.3.1 boundary condition The boundary conditions applied to the model are: - Bas e : zero displacement in vertical direction (DY) - Right and left sides : zero displacement according to horizontal direction (DX) 1.3.2 Loading Gravity type loading applied to the model. 1.4 Initial conditions The displacement is zero throughout the model at the initial moment. 1.5 Position of sliding circle A mesh of the sliding circle is provided, the centre of which is positioned at (\mathrm{6.08,}49.6) , with a radius of 50m . 2 reference solution The POST_NEWMARK macrocommand result is compared with other safety factor estimation methods, based on the Potgieter results [1]: - Band method by SLOPE/W software - Enhanced Limit Equilibrium by SIGMA/W and SLOPE/W software - C-phi reduction by PLAXIS 2D software. The approach chosen by the POST_NEWMARK macro-command is similar to the Enhanced Limit Equilibrium method and the results must be as close to this method. The reference values obtained by Potgieter [1] for these three methods are as follows: - Band method: FS = 1.73 - Enhanced Limit Equilibrium : FS = 1.82 - Reduction c-phi: FS = 1.72 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Model A uses a behavior model for the linear type dam, the calculation is based on operator MECA_STATIQUE. The safety factor assessment is performed: - from a 2D auxiliary mesh sufficiently refined sliding circle. - from mesh of the sliding circle built directly by the macro-command 3.2 Tested quantities and results The value of the overall static safety factor estimated by the Newmark method is tested, comparing it with the result of the Enhanced Limit Equilibrium (ELE) method. | Identification | Reference type | ELE | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | FS | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | 1,82 | 0.2% | 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics Model B uses a behavior model for the linear type dam, the calculation is performed from the MECA_STATIQUE operator. A mesh and a sliding circle are tested on the upstream trim (symmetric to model A). The safety factor is evaluated from a sufficiently refined 2D auxiliary mesh of the sliding circle. 4.2 Tested quantities and results The value of the overall static safety factor estimated by the Newmark method is tested, comparing it with the result of the Enhanced Limit Equilibrium (ELE) method. | Identification | Reference type | ELE | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | FS | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | 1,82 | 0.2% | 5 Bibliography [1] Potgieter, J.-T. v3.02.313 SSLP313 - Stitched in unlimited plate, subjected to uniform tensile infinity v3.02.313 SSLP313 - Stitched in unlimited plate, subjected to uniform tensile infinity Summary: This test is based on independent validation of Code_Aster 3 in breakage mechanics. {K}_{I} , {K}_{\mathrm{II}} and the energy return rate for a straight crack, inclined at an b angle, are calculated in a large plate with uniform traction. This \mathrm{2D} reference test allows the separability of {K}_{I} and {K}_{\mathrm{II}} to be verified in a mixed mode. The reference solution, given for a theoretically unlimited domain, is analytical. In addition to the energy method (CALC_G), the method of calculating stress intensity factors by extrapolation of displacement (POST_K1_K2_K3) is tested. B modelling allows testing this latter method with a recommended mesh type (nodes media per quarter) to obtain a precise solution. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Any value is assigned to the inclination, \beta =37\mathit{degrés} . We choose a=1.E-3m . 1.2 Material properties The material is isotropic linear elastic, Young's modulus E=2.E11\mathrm{Pa} and Poisson's ratio \nu =0.3 . The traction curve is defined as: - the slope is equal to 3. - the yield strength is equal to 1.88\mathrm{GPa} . The flat stress hypothesis is applied. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads - Arbitrary limits of the mesh domain: -{x}_{\max}\le x\le {x}_{\max} with {x}_{\max}=\mathrm{10a} -{y}_{\max}\le y\le {y}_{\max} with {y}_{\max}=\mathrm{20a} - boundary conditions : In order to block only the 3 rigid plane modes. \mathrm{UX}=\mathrm{UY}=0 at the bottom left corner of the complete model. \mathrm{UY}=0 at the bottom right corner of the complete model. The whole consists of two elastic materials, linear and isotropic, the material 1 being located in the upper half plane. The crack is defined by two branches. The first branch is located horizontally at the interface of both materials, and is characterized by its length c . The second is in the extension of the first and is inclined to 45° in relation to the horizontal, in the hourly direction (characteristic length a ). v3.02.315 SSLP315 - Propagation of crack opening in a 2D hole plate of finished width with XFEM v3.02.315 SSLP315 - Propagation of crack opening in a 2D hole plate of finished width with XFEM Summary: The purpose of this test is to verify that the four propagation methods available in the PROPA_FISS operator (mesh, simplex, upwind, geometric) give the same result for a mixed-mode \mathrm{2D} propagation. v3.02.317 SSLP317- Validation of RAFF_XFEM macro-command on multi-fissed plate v3.02.317 SSLP317- Validation of RAFF_XFEM macro-command on multi-fissed plate Summary: This document is intended to validate the RAFF_XFEM U7.03.51 command macro that allows you to obtain an error field a priori to power a mesh refinement process. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A square \mathrm{2D} plate is considered to be of the unit side, originally centered. This plate has 2 cracks and 2 inclusions (interfaces): - an inclusion of {L}_{e}=0,6 length and {R}_{e}=0,05 radius type, centred in E(0;-0,3) , - a circular {R}_{c}=0,05 radius inclusion centred at the origin, - a horizontal straight-line non-emitting crack of {L}_{A}=0,2 length centred in A(\mathrm{0,3 };0,25) , - a horizontal straight-line non-escaper crack of {L}_{B}=0,2 length centred in B(-\mathrm{0,2 };0,25) . Figure 1.1-1 : multi-cracked plate diagram 1.2 Material properties The material has the following properties: - Young's modulus: E=205000\mathrm{MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu =0,3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Mechanical calculation does not matter in this test because it is only a test of the refinement criterion a priori . Mechanical calculation is given only as an illustrative example in Modelling A. p=1\mathit{MPa} traction load is considered on the left, right and upper sides of the plate. The lower side is clamped. 1.4 Brief description of the different modellings All modellings are part of the representation of cracks and interfaces by the X-FEM method associated with the level sets. Modelling A calculates a remote indicator (fields to nodes). The test will focus on the value of this indicator in different nodes. The mesh refinement methodology used is the simplest (criterion in percentage of refined mesh cells), but is not necessarily optimal in terms of number of mesh cells. Model B calculates a remote indicator (fields to nodes). The value of this Modelling is to show a more optimal methodology in terms of number of mesh cells. The test will focus on the size of mesh cells in the refined area. Model C calculates one indicator per zone (by mesh cells). The methodology presented is the most complete and robust, and this indicator and methodology is recommended. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution 2.1.1 Modelling A The test is for the value of the error indicator output of RAFF_XFEM. I(M) is noted for the value of this indicator at any point M . At the point {P}_{1} at the bottom left of the structure, the indicator is the opposite of the distance to the point of the nearest pitch, i.e. I({P}_{1})=-({\mathit{CP}}_{1}-{R}_{e}) . At the point {P}_{2} at the bottom right of the structure, the indicator is the opposite of the distance to the point of the nearest pitch, i.e. I({P}_{2})=-({\mathit{DP}}_{2}-{R}_{e}) . At the point {P}_{3} at the top right of the structure, the indicator is the opposite of the distance at the right end of the crack to the right, I({P}_{3})=-A'{P}_{3} where A'=A+\frac{{L}_{A}}{2}\overrightarrow{x} . At the point {P}_{4} at the top left of the structure, the indicator is the opposite of the distance at the left end of the leftmost crack, I({P}_{4})=-B'{P}_{4} where B'=B-\frac{{L}_{B}}{2}\overrightarrow{x} . 2.1.2 modellings B et C The test is about the diameter value of the smallest mesh cell. If {h}_{0} is the initial size of the mesh cells, {h}_{c} the target size of the mesh cells after refinement, then the minimum number of calls to Homard to reach {h}_{c} is \text{nb\_raff}=E(n)+1 , with n=\frac{\ln({h}_{0})-\ln({h}_{c})}{\ln(2)} . v3.02.320 SSLP320 - Propagation of a X-FEM crack for the requested outlet in Mode I v3.02.320 SSLP320 - Propagation of a X-FEM crack for the requested outlet in Mode I Summary The purpose of this test is to validate the calculation of stress intensity factors ( {K}_{I} and {K}_{\mathrm{II}} ) and the crack propagation path with X-FEM in 2D, within the framework of the linear elasticity. This test involves a rectangular plate with an opening crack, and is subject to a tensile charge on the lower and upper edges of the plate. Three methods to manage the propagation of X-FEM cracks are available, each of which is modeled. Three modellings are considered: - Modelling A: mesh method, - Model B: simplex method, - Modelling C: upwind method, - Modelling D: geometric method, The relevance of the results is assessed by comparing stress intensity factors with analytical values. There is a difference between {K}_{I} and {K}_{I} theoretically less than 1.13% for the mesh method, 1.12% for the simplex method, 1.13% for the upwind method, 1.1% for the geometric method and 1.1% for the upwind & FMM method. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The 2d structure is a rectangular plate ( \mathrm{LX}=10m , \mathrm{LY}=30m ), with an opening crack (see v3.02.320-fig-geometrie-plate-fissuree). The initial crack length is a=5m . The line in y=0 and the line in y=\mathrm{Ly} is called "lower line". v3.02.321 SSLP321 - Propagation of a X-FEM crack in a 3-point bending plate v3.02.321 SSLP321 - Propagation of a X-FEM crack in a 3-point bending plate Summary This test is intended to validate the crack propagation path with \text{X-FEM} in \mathrm{2D} , as part of the linear elasticity. This test involves a rectangular plate with a crack opening, and subjected to a 3 point bending as in the article by Mariani and Perego . Five methods to manage the propagation of \text{X-FEM} cracks are available, each of which is modeled. - A Modelling: mesh method - B Modelling: simplex method - C Modelling: upwind method - D Modelling: geometric method Comparisons are made with the values given by the mesh method. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Geometry, dimensions and materials are taken identical to those of Mariani et al. The \mathrm{2D} structure is a rectangular plate ( 230\mathrm{mm}\times 75\mathrm{mm} ), with an opening crack (see v3.02.321-fig-geometry-plate-fissuree). The initial crack length is a=19\mathrm{mm} . The nodes rated \mathrm{P1} , \mathrm{P2} and \mathrm{P3} are used to impose the boundary conditions, which is explained to the v3.02.321-conditions-limits-loads. Geometry of cracked plate 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus: E=31,37{10}^{9}\mathrm{Pa} Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.2 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The load consists of applying a single nodal force in \mathrm{P3} . In order to block rigid modes, the nodes \mathrm{P1} and \mathrm{P2} movements are blocked as follows: - {\mathrm{DY}}^{\mathrm{P1}}={\mathrm{DY}}^{\mathrm{P2}}=0 ; - {\mathrm{DX}}^{\mathrm{P1}}=0 . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The study of this case is entirely based on Mariani and Perego's article. Three initial crack configurations are selected: \chi =0,25 and 50 . In this test case we chose only \chi =50 . Thus, the propagation path compared to the experimental path of the bib1 article is compared. The reference expressions of the stress factors {K}_{I} and {K}_{\mathit{II}} are those of the mesh method. Thus, the values of the simplex, upwind and geometric methods will be compared to the values given by the mesh method. For the spread of the crack, we use the Paris law: \begin{array}{c}\frac{\mathit{da}}{\mathit{dN}}=C\Delta {K}^{m}\end{array} where a is crack length, C and m are material constants, \begin{array}{}\Delta K\end{array} is the difference between two consecutive \mathrm{FIC s} and N is the number of cycles. v3.02.326 FORMA01 - Practical work of the "Initiation" training: Modelling of a linear elasticity hole plate and adaptation of mesh v3.02.326 FORMA01 - Practical work of the "Initiation" training: Modelling of a linear elasticity hole plate and adaptation of mesh Summary: This 2D test in near-static plane stresses allows a grip of the Salome-Meca platform on a single case in linear elasticity. It is a homogeneous rectangular plate, holed in its centre, which is subject to traction at its ends. Initially (modelization A) the method of constructing the geometry and then the mesh and how to data the study is indicated. In a second stage (modelization B and C), the mesh will be adapted. Finally (modelization D), an alternative solution is presented using the X-FEM method. The Practical Work of Training statements (TP1) are included in this document (see modellings A, B and C). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is a rectangular plate, with a hole, modelled in \mathrm{2D} flat stresses. Only a quarter of the plate is modelled with symmetries. Dimensions are given in millimetres. y y P A B D G G B D L=100 H=150 a=10 F F A x x 1.2 Boundary conditions and loads Conditions of symmetry: The plate is blocked following \mathit{Ox} along the \mathrm{AG} side and following \mathrm{Oy} along the \mathrm{BD} side. Conditional loading imposed: It is subjected to P=100\mathit{MPa} traction following \mathit{Oy} distributed on the \mathrm{FG} side. 1.3 Material properties The characteristics are: - Young's modulus E=200000\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio \nu =0,3 - Elasticity limit: 200\mathit{MPa} 2 reference solution 2.1 Elastic solution In elasticity, for an infinite plate, with a a diameter hole, subject to P loading on y infinitely, the analytical solution in flat stresses and polar coordinates (r,\theta ) is [bib1]: {\sigma}_{\mathit{rr}}=\frac{P}{2}\left[(1-{(\frac{a}{r})}^{2})-(1-4{(\frac{a}{r})}^{2}+3{(\frac{a}{r})}^{4})\cos2\theta \right] {\sigma}_{\theta \theta }=\frac{P}{2}\left[(1+{(\frac{a}{r})}^{2})+(1+3{(\frac{a}{r})}^{4})\cos2\theta \right] {\sigma}_{r\theta }=\frac{P}{2}\left[(1+2{(\frac{a}{r})}^{2}-3{(\frac{a}{r})}^{4})\sin2\theta \right] In particular, at the edge of the hole ( r=a ) : {\sigma}_{\theta \theta }=P[(1+2\cos2\theta )] And along the x axis: {\sigma}_{\theta \theta }={\sigma}_{yy}=\frac{P}{2}\left[(1+{(\frac{a}{r})}^{2})+(1+3{(\frac{a}{r})}^{4})\right] Digitally, for P=1\mathit{MPa} , and for an infinite plate , we have: | Point | Component | Calculation | \mathrm{MPa} | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | \mathit{SIXX} | {\sigma}_{\theta \theta }(r=a,\theta =\pi /2) | –1 | | B | \mathit{SIYY} | {\sigma}_{\theta \theta }(r=a,\theta =0) | 3 | For a -finished plate, the abacus [bib1] allows to obtain the stress concentration coefficient, and it is found that for a traction of 1\mathrm{MPa} , the maximum \mathit{SIYY} is about 3.03\mathit{MPa} at point B . 2.2 Bibliographical references 1. Limit analysis of cracked structures and resistance criteria. F. VOLDOIRE: Note EDF/DER/HI/74/95/26 1995 2. Stress concentration factors. R.E. PETERSON Ed. J. WILEY p150 3 Modelling A 3.1 TP procedure The purpose is to complete the elastic calculation by generating geometry, mesh and command file AsterStudy using the Salome-Meca platform. The Modelling is C_PLAN elastic. A quarter of the plate is modelled. The controls required for counting (curve tracks and post-processings graphics) will also be defined. 3.1.1 Geometry The flat surface of the upper right quarter of the plate will be created. Launch the Geometry module. The main steps to build this geometry are as follows: - To define the contours of the plate, you can, for example, use the "Sketcher" tool (Menu New Entity → Basic→2D Sketch). It is easier to start with the point B of (10,0) coordinates. Starting from B , for circle arc, use Element Type(Arc) and Destination(Direction/Perpendicular), and set the radius 10 and angle and the 90° radius. You get the point A . Then use Element Type(Line) and give the other points ( G , F , D ) by their absolute coordinates. Finish with Sketch Close. - A closed contour (Sketch_1) is then obtained on which one must build a face (Menu New Entity →Build →Face). The geometry of the plate is then complete. - Build useful groups for calculation. Here we build the 3 groups of edges on which the boundary conditions (symmetries and loading) will be based: left for the \mathit{AG} edge, top for the \mathit{GF} edge and bottom for the \mathit{BD} edge. Menu New Entity →Group →Create Group: Select the geometric entity type (here the line, edge) and select the edge directly from the graphic window, then click Add, then an object number must appear. We can change the name of the group before validating by Apply. 3.1.2 Mesh A mesh plane of the upper right quarter of the plate, in elements order 2, will be created to ensure sufficient accuracy. Run the Mesh module. The main steps to generate the mesh are as follows: - Build the mail (Menu Mesh→ Create Mesh). Select the geometry to be knit Face_1, then choose Algorithm → NETGEN 1D-2D by addingHypothesis → NETGEN 2D Parameters. In this case, selectFineness→ Fine and check the box Second Order before Apply. - Calculate themail(MenuMesh→ Compute). A window of mesh information must appear, and then you get a free mesh. - Create the corresponding mail groups for the geometric groups(Menu Mesh→Create Groups from Geometry).Select all 3 groups of edges under Geometry module and then Apply. We get 3 groups of edges on the mesh. - To obtain better accuracy, we will move the mesh from linear to quadratic, thanks to the tool "Modification -> Convert to/from quadratic". The most curious can compare the differences in results between the two types d - (Optional) Exportmailing in MED format: select Mesh_1 and right click, then choose Export / MED file. Notes: This mesh is fine enough (with quadratic elements) to have a good approximation of the elasticity solution: for example, if you compare {\sigma}_{\theta \theta } on the edge of the hole with the analytical solution, you get a difference of less than 5%. The geometry and parameters of mesh are defined in the file forma01a.datg associated with the test. The mesh produced is stored in the file forma01a.mmed . 3.2 Creation and launch of the calculation case (via AsterStudy) Launch the AsterStudy module. Then in the left column, click on the Case View tab. In the Data Settings box, click on the right at CurrentCase and choose Add Stage. C Note:Search for orders by Menu Commands→ Show All gold by the 10 calculation categories: Mesh, Model Definition, Material, Functions and Lists, BC and Load, Pre Analysis, Post Processing, Fracture and Fatigue, Output. The main steps for creating and launching the calculation case are: - Read mesh in MED format: Mesh Category / LIRE_MAILLAGE Command.The mesh in the MESH module is available in the list. Otherwise the button behind allows you to choose an mesh in the directories. - Orient the normal edge on which the traction load will be applied: Mesh Category / MODI_MAILLAGE / ORIE_PEAU_2D command by affecting the group high in GROUP_MA.We keep the same name of the mesh using weer. - Set the finished elements used: Category Model Definition / AFFE_MODELE command for 2D flat stress Modelling (C_PLAN). Add a term in AFFE. In this term, assign OUI to TOUT elements, and choose the MECANIQUE phenomenon, and add the 2D flat stress term ( C_PLAN ) in the Modelling - Define material: Material Category / DEFI_MATERIAU Command.Choose ELAS and enter the values of Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio. - Assign material: Material Category / AFFE_MATERIAU Command.Definite at least one option between mesh and MODELE.Add a term in AFFE, and assign the material defined to TOUT. - Mechanical boundary conditions Assignments and Loading: Category BC and Load / AFFE_CHAR_MECA Command: - for symmetry on the plate quarter: DDL_IMPO. For left, DX=0, and for bottom, DY=0. - for traction: PRES_REP. For the top, grab traction at PRES (so negative). - Solve the static linear mechanical problem: Category Analysis / MECA_STATIQUE control by giving material (CHAM_MATER), Modelling (MODELE), boundary conditions and loading (EXCIT). - Calculate the field: Post Processing Category / CALC_CHAMP command by enabling activating (to keep the same name of the input object in the command). That is, we will enrich the MECA_STATIQUE concept by taking the same name. - for the calculation of the stress field: CONTRAINTE / SIGM_ELNO (contraints by elements to nodes), SIGM_NOEU (contraints overall to nodes). - for the calculation of the equivalent stress field: CRITERES / SIEQ_ELNO (by elements to nodes), SIEQ_ELGA (by elements to Gauss points), SIEQ_NOEU (overall to nodes). - Print the results of a calculation in MED format: Category Output / Command IMPR_RESU.Add a term in RESU, and choose the results to print. Set the output file (.rmed) by UNITE. - To start the calculation case, in the left column, click on the History View tab.You must save the study first, and select CurrentCase. Add Stage_1 by selecting run (green cross). Before running, check the desired calculation parameters in the Run Parameters box: time limit of calculation, memory, code_aster version etc. 3.3 Post-processing of the results To view the results, two choices are currently available: Results tab in AsterStudy, and ParaViS module. For this purpose, the concept of interface (limiting the hole) is used, with an interface being seen as an "infinite" crack (no crack front). The interface is then represented by a single Level Set (Level Set Normal), separating two solids, without contact on the interface. Thus, a hole (empty) is modelled because the solid inside is isolated from the rest of the structure on which the pressure load is applied. Geometry and mesh and command file AsterStudy will be generated using the Salome-Meca platform. The Modelling is C_PLAN elastic. A quarter of the plate is modelled. 6.1.1 Geometry The geometry is the upper right quarter of the rectangular plate, without holes. Launch the Geometry module. The main steps to build this geometry are as follows: - To create the face, one can, for example, use the "rectangle" tool (MenuNew Entity / Primitives / Rectangle), and possibly translater (Menu Operations / Transformation / Translation). - Build the groups of edges on which the boundary conditions (symmetries and loading) (Menu New Entity →Group →Create Group) will be based. Select the type of geometric entity (here the line, edge) and select the edge directly from the graphic window. Then click Add. An object number must then appear. The name of the group can be changed before validating by Apply. Build the 3 groups of edge useful for calculation: left for the \mathit{AG} edge, top for the \mathit{GF} edge and bottom for the \mathit{BD} edge. 6.1.2 Mesh A mesh plane of the upper right quarter of the plate, in elements order 2, will be created to ensure sufficient accuracy. Run the Mesh module. The main steps to generate the mesh are as follows: - Build the mesh (Menu Mesh→ Create Mesh). Select the mesh geometry, then the NetGEN 1D-2D algorithm with the Netgen 2D Parameters hypothesis. In this case, selectFineness→ Fine and check the Second Order box. - Calculate themail(MenuMesh→ Compute). - Create the corresponding mesh groups for the geometric groups (Menu Mesh→Create Groups from Geometry).Select all the geometric groups. You get 3 groups of edges on the mesh. - Export mail in MED format. 6.2 Creation and launch of the calculation case (via AsterStudy) Launch the AsterStudy module. Then in the left column, click on the Case View tab. The command file of the calculation case is defined. Note: To add commands: Commands Menu→ Show All. The main steps for creating and launching the calculation case are: - Read mesh in MED format: LIRE_MAILLAGE command. - Orient the mesh on the edge affected by the load: Command MODI_MAILLAGE / ORIE_PEAU_2D using the top group. - Set the finished elements used: AFFE_MODELE command for 2D flat stress Modelling (C_PLAN). - Set interface: DEFI_FISS_XFEM with crack shape (FORM_FISS / ELLIPSE) and discontinuity type. - Create enriched finished elements (MODI_MODELE_XFEM). And name a new name for the X-FEM model. - Set the material: DEFI_MATERIAU command. - Assign material: AFFE_MATERIAU command on X-FEM model. - Assign mechanical boundary conditions and loading: AFFE_CHAR_MECA to X-FEM: - for symmetry on the plate quarter: Force DOF (DDL_IMPO), - for traction: FORCE_CONTOUR. - Solve the static linear mechanical problem: MECA_STATIQUE control on the X-FEM model. - Createmail: POST_MAIL_XFEM command. And name a new name for the mesh. - Set the finished elements used: AFFE_MODELE command for 2D flat stress Modelling (C_PLAN). And name a new model name. - Createoutput of visualization: POST_CHAM_XFEM command. And name a new name of the result. - Calculate field: CALC_CHAMP command. > The POST_CHAM_XFEM concept will be enriched by the same concept name. - for the calculation of the stress field by elements to nodes: CONTRAINTE / SIGM_ELNO. - for the calculation of the stress field equivalent to elements to nodes: CRITERES / SIEQ_ELNO. - for the calculation of the equivalent stress field by elements at Gauss points: CRITERES/ SIEQ_ELGA. - Print the results of a calculation in MED format: IMPR_RESU command. - To start the calculation case, in the left column, click on the History View tab. Note: The rigid modes of the hole are blocked by the symmetry conditions applied. In the case of a Modelling of the entire plate, the rigid modes of the plate and also of the hole should have been blocked. 6.3 Post-processing of the results Run ParaViS module. The distortion of the plate will be visualized and the stresses at the edge of the hole compared with the reference solution. - Import the result file (Data Files Tab → Open in ParaVis with the GenerateVectors option). - View the deformed plate (Menu Filters → Common → Warp By Vector). An automatic mesh refinement step can be added to improve the accuracy of the results. Note: The rigid modes of the hole are blocked by the symmetry conditions applied. In the case of a Modelling of the entire plate, the rigid modes of the plate and also of the hole should have been blocked. 6.4 Tested quantities and results Value of stress components at points A and B: For this reason, the SIGM_NOEU field is calculated. Attention, the SIGM_NOEU concept is special for X-FEM because the elements generated for visualization (by POST_CHAM_XFEM) have double nodes not connected. Therefore, we have several values for a node position. In this case, we have two nodes located at point A (plate-cotted) and two nodes located at point B (plate-cotted). So we test the min and max for each point. | Location | Identification | Reference (Analytic) | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Nœud A | Constraint \mathit{SIXX} | -100.0 | 5.0% | | Nœud B | Constraint \mathit{SIYY} | 303.0 | 5.0% | These tests on analytical values are doubled by non-regression tests. 7 Summary of the results This test shows how to conduct the calculation of an elastic structure and how to extract post-processing of interest. It also highlights the benefit of using mesh adaptation to improve the accuracy of results.

v3.03.011 SSLS11 - Combination of static loads on a plate v3.03.011 SSLS11 - Combination of static loads on a plate Summary This test is intended to validate the operation of the POST_COMBINAISON command. This allows for the combination of different physical quantitiess following calculations to the elements finished upstream. This command will only perform post-processings by manipulating results in the form of fields or tables from previous calculations. This test involves a rectangular plate, which is submitted to its own weight and three cases of loads. The test saves the results obtained during the call to the POST_COMBINAISON command, and checks its operation in the following situations: - Data structures of the sd_result type to be combined. - Data structures of the sd_table type to be combined. The tables are of type ‘RESULTANTE - Data structures of the sd_table type to be combined. The tables are of type ‘EXTRACTION 1 Reference problem The POST_COMBINAISON command calculates linear combinations of different calculation results associated with user-defined coefficients. {C}_{i}\text{}\text{}\text{}=\text{}\text{}\text{}({\alpha}_{i,1}\times {Q}_{1})\text{}\text{}\text{}+\text{}\text{}\text{}({\alpha}_{i,2}\times {Q}_{2}) Où : - is the number of the combination - Q1 is the result/table resulting from a first calculation at the finished elements - Q2 is the result/table resulting from a first calculation at the finished elements - αi,1is the coefficient associated with Q1 - αi,2is the coefficient associated with Q2 - This is the result of the combination performed. 1.1 Geometry The structure is a straight parallelepipeda with rectangular base. The dimensions of the block are: L=12,0m , H=3,0m and B=0,3m [ Figure 1.1-1 ]. Figure 1.1-1 : Geometry of the structure 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus : E=30000\mathit{MPa} . Poisson's ratio : \nu =0,3 . Density: \rho =2500\mathit{kg}/m\mathrm{³} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The left side is clamped. Charge 1: The right side is subject to three cases of loads: - Force distributed according to x axis: FX = 100 kN - Force distributed according to y axis: FY = 6000 kN - Force distributed according to z axis: FZ = 600 kN Charge 2: The structure is subject to its own weight. 1.4 Bibliography 2 Modelling A: simple case 2.1 Mesh characteristics The structure is modelled by a regular mesh ‘2D' composed of 2\times 2 QUA4(see ). This campaign focuses on the seismic study of irregular reinforced concrete buildings whose response is strongly affected by the torsion movements of the whole. The model represents an electrical reinforced concrete building of three floors on a scale of 1/4; it is carried out in the law of similarity of Cauchy-Froude (i.e. the eigenfrequencies increased by a ratio of 2). v3.03.110 SSLS110 - Stability of a compressed square plate v3.03.110 SSLS110 - Stability of a compressed square plate Summary: A homogeneous isotropic square elastic plate simply leaning on its four sides is subjected to a linear compression force acting on two sides. Critical loads leading to the elastic blazing of the plate are calculated. The geometric rigidity matrix used in solving the problem to the specific values is that due to the initial stresses. - linear elastic mechanics, - a shell flashing, - test value: calculation of the geometric rigidity matrix of elements DKT, DKTG and COQUE_3D, - 6 modellings. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Due to the geometric and physical symmetry of the problem, only one quarter of the plate is modelled. Taking into account the symmetry conditions, only symmetrical flaming modes can be captured. 1.2 Material properties E=2.1E5\mathrm{Mpa} . \nu =0.3 The transverse shear coefficient for the plate is {A}_{\mathrm{CIS}}=5/6 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads | boundary conditions : | \mathrm{P2P3} : | | \mathrm{DZ}=0. | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | \mathrm{P3P4} : | | \mathrm{DZ}=0. | | | | Symmetry | \mathrm{P1P2} : | \mathrm{DY}=0. | | \mathrm{DRX}=\mathrm{0 }. | \mathrm{DRZ}=0. | | | \mathrm{P4P1} : | \mathrm{DX}=0. | | \mathrm{DRY}=\mathrm{0 }. | \mathrm{DRZ}=0. | Loading: q compression linear force on \mathrm{P2P3} 1.4 Remarks It is not possible to solve the compression deformation problem without introducing the symmetry conditions. Indeed, imposing boundary conditions symmetry for a quarter of a plate is to eliminate the rigid body modes for the complete plate. 2 reference solution 2.1 reference solution - Critical loads The analytical solution obtained with a isotropic homogeneous linear elasticity thin plate theory [bib1] without consideration of transverse shear energy determines the rd critical load: {q}_{\mathit{cr}I}=\frac{D{\pi}^{2}}{{L}^{2}}{(i+\frac{1}{i})}^{2} with: D=\frac{E{h}^{3}}{12(1-{\nu}^{2})} : the coefficient of bending rigidity of the hull h : thickness L : the length on the side of the square plate. - Membrane deformation The analytical expression of membrane deformation along the X axis is as follows: > {e}_{xx}=\frac{q\times L}{(h\times L\times E)} The reference result was calculated with q=1.N/\mathit{mm} 2.2 Baseline Some modes corresponding to the critical loads of the analytical solution are not symmetrical and cannot be captured with symmetry conditions for a quarter of a plate. The values of the critical loads obtained correspond to the first 3 symmetrical flaming modes: - Mode 1 of the plate quarter = Mode 1 of the whole plate - Mode 2 of the plate quarter = Mode 3 of the whole plate - Mode 3 of the plate quarter = Mode 5 of the whole plate 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution The exact solution for a plate theory without transverse shear. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. The modellings used are: > Modelling A - DST, DSTQ(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > Modelling B - DKT, DKTG(TRIA3)+MECA_STATIQUE > D Modelling - Q4G , Q4G(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > E Modelling - Q4G , Q4G(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > Modelling F - DKT, DKTG(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > Modelling G - DST,DSQ(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > Modelling H - DKTG,DKTG(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > Modelling I - Q4G, Q4G(QUAD4)+MECA_STATIQUE > Modelling J - DKT, DKT(QUAD4)+STAT_NON_LINE > Modelling K - DKTG, DKTG(QUAD4)+STAT_NON_LINE > Modelling M - Q4GG, Q4GG(QUAD4)+ STAT_NON_LINE > N Modelling - DKTG, DKTG(QUAD4)+STAT_NON_LINE – GLRC_DAMAGE > O Modelling - DKT. DKT(QUAD4)+STAT_NON_LINE Modellings A and B : Two plates are modelled out of the average plane and the results are compared to an analytical solution. Between D and E Modelling, the fineness of the mesh is changed. O Modelling: A single plate is modelled off the average plane to validate the calculation of the SIXZ and SIYZ stress components. Two calculations are performed, the first in monolayer, which is used as a reference to the second in multilayer. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A4 A3 5 subdivisions > z y > A1 GRN011 A2 0.2 m > 0.2 m > 10 subdivisions x The coordinates of the points are given in metres ( m ): | \mathrm{A1}(0,0,0) | \mathrm{A3}(10,5,0) | | --- | --- | | \mathrm{A2}(10,0,0) | \mathrm{A4}(0,5,0) | 1.2 Material properties 1.2.1 modellings A à O The material has an isotropic elastic behavior: > Young's modulus : E=\mathrm{200000.MPa} > Poisson's ratio: \nu =0. > Density: \rho =\mathrm{1000.Kg}/{m}^{3} 1.2.2 For Modelling N, the material is GLRC_DAMAGE with equivalent elastic properties (no steel module). 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads 1.3.1 modellings A et B The A1A4 edge is clamped.The plate is 0,8m thick. The plate is excreted from e=0,4m . A nodal force \mathit{Fz}=–1000\text{N} is applied to the A1A2 edge. 1.3.2 Modelization D, E, F, G , H, I, J, K, M and N The A1A4 edge is clamped. The plate is 0,8m thick. The plate is excreted from e=0,4m . A {F}_{z}=–1000N/m transverse distributed nodal force is applied to the A2A3 edge and a distributed nodal force of {F}_{x}=4000N/m traction is applied to the same A2A3 edge. 1.3.3 Modelling O The A1A4 edge is clamped. The plate is 0,8m thick. The plate is excreted from e=0,4m . A nodal force \mathit{Fz}=–1000\text{N} is applied to the A1A2 edge. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution 2.1.1 modellings A et B The deflection \mathrm{fl} is given by the formula: \mathrm{fl}={\mathrm{FlL}}^{3}/\mathrm{3EI} where l is the width, L the length of the plate, and I={\mathrm{lh}}^{3}/12 , h being the thickness. 2.2 Baseline 2.2.1 modellings A et B They consist of the \mathrm{DZ} displacement field values at \mathrm{A3} and point \mathrm{A1} forces. On the other hand, the 4 smallest frequencies of the structure are calculated. 2.2.2 Modelization C to N In this case, only one ex-entry plate is represented (ex-center e=0,4m , h/2=0,4m thickness ). The deflection w at the free end is given by the expression: w=\left(2{F}_{z}L-3{F}_{x}e\right)\ell {L}^{2}/6\mathit{EI}+{F}_{z}L/(6\mathit{Gh5}/6) . The overall stresses on the clamped \mathrm{A1A4} edge , of \ell =5m length are: {N}_{x}={F}_{x} and {V}_{z}=-{F}_{z} . 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution For modellings A and B , the reference solution is analytical, so there is no uncertainty. For other modellings, another solution is used as reference solution for the eigenfrequency from an unexccentric calculation. v3.03.115 SSLS115 - Square composite plate under uniform pressure v3.03.115 SSLS115 - Square composite plate under uniform pressure Summary: The case of a three-layer square plate, simply supported and subjected to uniform pressure, is treated. The skins consist of homogeneous orthotropic material, as well as the heart (same axis of orthotropy).The E and G modules of the heart are ten times weaker than those of the skins. The displacement at the centre and the stresses at the lower and upper interfaces of the skin are calculated. The test consists of eight modellings: for the first four, the results obtained are compared for triangular and quadrangular superfacial mesh cells in two different user markers. The last four modellings allow the sensitivity of the results to the orientation of triangular mesh cells in both user markers. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Due to the geometric and physical symmetry of the problem, only one quarter of the plate is modelled. v3.03.117 SSLS117 - Non-symmetric plate excentering v3.03.117 SSLS117 - Non-symmetric plate excentering Summary: This test validates the excentre of single plates not symmetrical with the plane of the mesh or plane of the depur (keyword EXCENTREMENT of the AFFE_CARA_ELEM command). The reference is given by a first resolution in which a two-layered layer of two layers of different thicknesses and two materials is modelled. It is used to validate a second calculation where two layers are modelled out of the mesh plane. It differs from the SSLS111 test only in that the 2 layers are different thicknesses. Four modellings implement the elements DKT, DKQ. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 10m 5m 0.4m \mathrm{A4} \mathrm{A3} 0.2m \mathrm{A1} \mathrm{m3} \mathrm{m1} \mathrm{m2} \mathrm{A2} z y x 1.2 Material properties 1.2.1 modellings A et B The material has an isotropic elastic behavior: > Young's modulus : E=20000\mathrm{MPa} > Poisson's ratio: \nu =0. > Density: \rho =1000\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads 1.3.1 modellings A et B The \mathit{A1A4} edge is clamped. A distributed force {F}_{z}=–1000N/m is applied to the \mathit{A2A3} edge. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The calculation with the two-layer material (DEFI_COMPOSITE command) is used as a reference. The non-regression in relation to the results obtained by this first calculation is verified. The two plates of the second model are out of the middle plane of the two-layer. 2.2 Baseline 2.2.1 modellings A et B They consist of the \mathrm{DZ} displacement field values at \mathrm{A3} point and the generalised node \mathrm{A1} forces. On the other hand, the 4 smallest frequencies of the structure are calculated. 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution For modellings A and B , the reference solution is analytical, so there is no uncertainty. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. R3.07.03: elements plate DKT,DST,DKQ,DSQ and Q4G. 2. The displacement at the centre, \sigma_{xx}, \sigma_{yy}, \sigma_{xy}, \sigma_{xz}, \sigma_{yz} stresses at the lower middle and upper interfaces, N_{xx}, N_{yy}, N_{xy} membrane forces, shear forces T_{x}, T_{y} and M_{xx}, M_{yy}, M_{xy} moments are calculated. The test consists of 14 modellings: for modellings A to F, the results obtained are compared for modellings DKQ, DSQ, DKT, DST, COQUE_3D with triangular mesh cells and COQUE_3D with rectangular mesh cells. The modellings G and H test results in a different user benchmark from the global benchmark. Modellings I and J measure the sensitivity of the results to the fineness of the mesh, for the DSQ configuration. The modellings K to N are for the multilayer plate, for the modellings DST and DSQ, as a global and user benchmark, and allow the distribution of flat stresses and transverse shear within the plate to be estimated. This is explained by the order of rotation approximations that is quadratic for DSQ and bilinear for Q4G, - The stress estimate is more accurate with DKT modelling (<2%) compared to DST modelling (<3.5%). However, L-shear force is better estimated by DST (<10% for DST and <20% for DKT), - for COQUE_3D triangle or quadrangle configurations, the estimate of the transverse shear stress is constant in plate thickness, according to the Modelling assumptions, - the results expressed in the user mark for the DST and COQUE_3D configurations are identical to those expressed in the global mark, - mesh refinement for DSQ configuration improves the estimation of stresses, shear forces and moments; the reverse trend in displacement, - The multilayer configuration allows the visualization of the distribution of flat and transverse shear stresses in the plate thickness, and confirms the theory, namely a linear distribution for flat and parabolic stresses for shear stresses; on the other hand, the rotation of the reference does not affect the values of the stresses, - In general, at nodes where the expected stresses or analytically zero forces are expected, the numerical results obtained are not correct because the estimates are made mesh cell by mesh cell and then extrapolated to nodes. Even the averaged values for the nodes in question are not necessarily zero.
