v3.03.130 SSLS130 - Structural Zoom: hole plate subjected to normal stress on a edge v3.03.130 SSLS130 - Structural Zoom: hole plate subjected to normal stress on a edge Summary: This test represents the static calculation of a free clamped hole plate bending by a normal effort applied to its free edge. This is a process of applying the so-called structural zoom method, which improves the quality of a result obtained on an mesh which is too coarse or insufficiently detailed. The particular feature of the method is that the solution is calculated on an mesh located around the area of interest (patch), by applying as a load on the contour of the patch the movements (or forces) from the original model. In this test, solutions obtained on a fine mesh and a coarse mesh after using structural zoom are compared. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is a rectangular plate, holed in the centre: Thickness: \mathrm{0.001m} 1.2 Material properties Classic homogeneous material on the whole structure: E=7.1{10}^{10} , \nu =0.3 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Clamped support on the 6 degrees of freedom on the left side of the plate. Nodal force on right side of \mathrm{100N} amplitude plate in X and \mathrm{1N} direction in Z . 2 reference solution The reference solution is obtained by Modelling A. This is the same calculation obtained on an mesh with a degree of refinement similar to that of Modelling B after using the structural modification method. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics 3.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes: 1944 Number of mesh cells and type: 620 TRIA3 and 1532 QUAD4 3.3 Tested quantities and results - The non-regression of the SIXX, SIYY and mesh cell M1533 maximum component values are tested. - The shear stresses of DKT are also tested. | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Creative decision | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SIXZ \mathit{M1533},\mathit{P1},\mathit{SP1} | 'AUTRE_ASTER' | 7.9745E+04 | 1% | | SIYZ \mathit{M1533},\mathit{P1},\mathit{SP1} | 'AUTRE_ASTER' | 14377.0954 | 1% | | EPXZ \mathit{M1533},\mathit{P1},\mathit{SP1} | 'AUTRE_ASTER' | 1.1681E-06 | 1% | | EPXZ \mathit{M1533},\mathit{P1},\mathit{SP1} | 'AUTRE_ASTER' | 2.1060E-07 | | We visualize the constraint of Von Bets around the hole: Figure 3.3-a : Baseline 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics Below the original coarse mesh: Below the mesh fine says patch: 4.2 Mesh characteristics The coarse Mesh characteristics are: Number of nodes: 754 Mesh cells number and type: 160 TRIA3 > 612 QUAD4 The Mesh characteristics fin are: Number of mesh cells and type : 620 TRIA3 > 580 QUAD4 4.3 Tested quantities and results This is a test against the values obtained on Modelling A | Identification | Reference | Tolerance ( \text{\%} ) | | --- | --- | --- | | SIXX max | 6.019E+06 | 2.0 | | SIXX min | -2.486E+05 | 2.0 | | SIYY max | 9.782E+05 | 2.0 | | SIYY min | -2.092E+06 | 2.0 | We visualize the constraint of Von Bets around the hole: Figure 4.3-a : Initial result on coarse model Figure 4.3-b : Result obtained after structural zoom 5 Summary of the results The very good match between the two modellings results validates the structural zoom method.

v3.03.131 SSLS131 – Optimization of curvature radius of a bent pipe v3.03.131 SSLS131 – Optimization of curvature radius of a bent pipe Summary: This demonstration test illustrates the use of python in Code_Aster . The objective of this test case is to optimize the value of the radius of curvature of a pipe via a python loop. The radius of curvature is changed iteratively. The optimal value is obtained when the maximum stress of Von Bets is below a threshold. The python language in this test case allows for: - modify the file describing the elbow geometry, - to launch GMSH in order to knit the elbow, - to recover the maximum stress of Von Bets, - d - to launch GMSH to perform an interactive post-processing. This test case takes up the problem of the test case forma01f: bent piping, consisting of a linear elastic material, subjected to a force applied at its end, modelled by elements shells DKT. Note: To have interactive visualization functions, set interactive = 1 at the beginning of the command file. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The study concerns a pipe with two straight pipes and one elbow [Figure 1.1-a]. The geometrical data of the problem are as follows: - the {L}_{G} length of both straight pipes is 3m , - the initial \mathrm{Rc} radius of the elbow is 0.3m , - the angle \theta of the elbow is 90 degrees, - the thickness of the straight pipes and elbow is 0.02m , - and the \text{Re} outer radius of the straight pipes and elbow is 0.2m . Figure 1.1-a Note: The geometry of the problem shows a symmetry with the plane (A,X,Y) . 1.2 Material properties Isotropic linear elastic material. Material properties are those of \mathrm{A42} steel: | le Young's modulus: | E=1.8{10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} | | --- | --- | | le Poisson's ratio: | \nu =0.3 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads - Boundary conditions : clamped support at A section , - Loading: constant force \mathrm{FY} directed on the Y axis and applied on the B section. The value of \mathrm{FY} shall be calculated from: - of the average radius: \mathrm{RMOY}=0.19 , - of the total force applied: \mathrm{FTOT}=500000N/{m}^{2} , The expression is as follows: \mathrm{FY}=\mathrm{FTOT}/(2\pi \mathrm{RMOY})(\simeq 418828.8) - The constraint of Von Bets limit is 2.0E+09N/{m}^{2} 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is obtained numerically, so it is only a non-regression test. 2.2 Modelling results The optimum value of the radius of curvature, respecting the criterion {\sigma}_{\mathrm{mises}} TUYAU # GM28 EFOND # GM31 A1 # GM27 ENCAST # GM29 SYMETRIE - Definition of the finished elements used (AFFE_MODELE). Straight pipes and elbow are modeled by elements hull (DKT). - Normal elements reorientations: MODI_MAILLAGE is used to orient all elements in the same way, with a normal inward-facing orientation. - Definition and allocation of the material (DEFI_MATERIAU and AFFE_MATERIAU). The mechanical characteristics are identical throughout the structure. Python buckle for optimization of curvature radius - Assignment of elements hull characteristics (AFFE_CARA_ELEM): thickness, V vector defining the counting mark (keyword ANGL_REP) - Definition of boundary conditions and loading (AFFE_CHAR_MECA). - The pipe is clamped at its base, on all nodes located in plane Y=0. The pipe shows a plane of symmetry Z=0 . - A \mathrm{FY} distributed force is calculated, directed to the Y axis and applied to the B section (the distributed force is such that the 2\pi .\mathrm{RMOY.}\mathrm{FY}=\mathrm{FTOT} result, \mathrm{FTOT} being the total force that you want to apply). To apply the force on section B, FORCE_ARETE will be used. - Resolution of the linear elastic problem (MECA_STATIQUE). - Calculation of the stress field by elements to nodes for each load case (option 'SIGM_ELNO'). The stresses are calculated in the local benchmark defined for each element using the V vector (previous ANG_REP keyword). Use NIVE_COUCHE to set the calculation level in thickness. - Calculation of the equivalent stress field by elements to nodes calculated from the stress field (option 'SIEQ_ELNO'). - Calculation of the previous fields to nodes (options 'SIGM_NOEU', 'SIEQ_NOEU') - Printing results (IMPR_RESU). - Determination of a table containing the calculation of the stress field averages equivalent to nodes.(‘POST_RELEVE_T') - Extract the VMIS component from the previous table via python. - Stop test: - If VMIS is greater than CRIT, then repeat with \mathrm{Rc}=\mathrm{Rc}+0.2 - Otherwise we'll get out of the python loop. 4 Modelling results A | Iterations | Curvature test | Max. v3.03.132 SSLS132 – Reinforced concrete console plate under bending loading, elastic v3.03.132 SSLS132 – Reinforced concrete console plate under bending loading, elastic Summary This quasi-static test is part of the validation of elements GRILLE_EXCENTRE, GRILLE_MEMBRANE and MEMBRANE. A concrete plate (modified by COQUE if necessary) is covered with two rebar panels on its upper and lower sides, each excreted from the same quantity. The loads are of three types: 1. clamped edge and plate bending 2. effect of gravity and own weight 3. pre-deformations in both rebars to compress the plate The results of the simulation are compared with analytical solutions. v3.03.135 SSLS135 - Ferry of a square tank according to the method of Capra and Maury v3.03.135 SSLS135 - Ferry of a square tank according to the method of Capra and Maury Summary: This test is for the study of the square tank used as an example in the descriptive document of the Capra and Maury method. The aim is to calculate longitudinal and transverse ferrailage densities for elements Plate or Coque. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A square concrete tank of L\times l\times h=10m\times 10m\times 5m (medium to medium sheet) and 0.4m thickness is considered. 1.2 Material properties Isotropic linear elastic material: Young's modulus: E={3.10}^{4}\mathit{MPa} , Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.15 , Density: \mu =2500\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The density of stiffness soil applied under the tank is 50\mathit{kN}/{m}^{3} . The integral of this density on the basis of the tank is therefore 5{10}^{6}\mathit{kN}/m . This amount is then distributed over the nodes of the base. The load consists of: - of the tank's own weight - the water thrust of the filled tank (constant push on the bottom and gradual push on the edges) - an overload spread over the contour at the top of the tank ( 20\mathit{kN}/m ) 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The density of longitudinal steels is calculated using the Capra and Maury method, for the \text{X} and \text{Y} directions of each element and on both sides, \text{I} (Inferior) and \text{S} (Superior), defined by their position following the normal \text{Z} elemental. The cross-sectional steel density is also calculated as described in the article entitled "Automatic calculation of the optimum ironing of reinforced concrete plates or hulls" by Alain CAPRA and Jean-Francis MAURY. 2.2 Baseline The different results are published in the article by Capra and Maury in the form of graphs (for a quarter model only) are: - the deformed tank, - \text{Mxx} and \text{Myy} iso-moments, - Ferry densities in the \text{X} and \text{Y} directions above and below. Below is the extract of the article for the distorted and the \text{Mx} moments, \text{My} . Below is the extract from the article for the ferrage density. For better legibility, colors were associated with the different density values of ferrage. 2.3 Bibliographical references > [1] Annales of the Technical Institute of Building and Public Works N° 367 December 1978 – Series: INFORMATIQUE APPLIQUEE – Article entitled "Automatic calculation of the optimal ironing of reinforced concrete plates or hulls" by Alain CAPRA and Jean-Francis MAURY. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics We use DKT Modelling. We model only a quarter of the tank. 3.2 Mesh characteristics Elements are quadrangles. elements DKT are oriented to have their normal output. 3.3 Other parameters of the calculation The acceleration of the gravity is 9.81m/{s}^{2} . The distance between the steel axis and the surface of a element (coated) is 0.04m . The equivalence coefficient is 15.0 . The maximum permissible stress of the steel is 2.8{10}^{8}\mathit{Pa} . v3.03.137 SSLS137 - Prestressed concrete plate with a flexion cable v3.03.137 SSLS137 - Prestressed concrete plate with a flexion cable Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the CALC_PRECONT macro-command for elements hulls. The reference solution is based on beam theory. The first Modelling is done with elements \mathrm{3D} and is designed to validate the use of beam theory as a reference. Two modellings hulls are then proposed (DKT and Q4GG) as well as two different mesh cells types (TRIA3, QUAD4) for each Modelling. Finally, the F Modelling resumes the D Modelling by replacing the constitutive law concrete elastic with the constitutive law nonlinear GLRC_DAMAGE. 1 Description 1.1 Geometry The design of the study is a rectangular plate of length L=\mathrm{4m} , width l=\mathrm{0.5m} and thickness t=\mathrm{0.2m} . A bending rail composed of a single frame, crosses the plate at its half and is eccentricated by a distance {e}_{z}=\mathrm{0.075m} from the median plane of the plate following the z axis . D-un point geometrically visible, only the area of the right section of the A={\mathrm{0.00015m}}^{2} bar is known . The figure below illustrates the position of the cable for the study model . The median plane of the plate is defined by the \mathit{ABCD} rectangle and the cable by the \mathit{EF} segment . 1.2 Material properties The properties of concrete for plate and steel for cable are listed in the table next. | Material | Beton | Storage | | --- | --- | --- | | Young's modulus | 4\times {10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} | 1.93\times {10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | | Poisson's ratio | 0.0 | 0.0 | | Volume size | 2500\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | 7850\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | | Elastic limit tension | n/a | 1.94\times {10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | It is subsequently justified that the study model can be assimilated to a beam and that a Poisson's ratio for concrete equal to 0.0 will be taken. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The AB segment of the plate is clamped, all degrees of freedom on this side are blocked and the other edges are left free to allow it a beam-type configuration. The order of application of the loads is defined as follows. 1.3.1 Loading 1: It corresponds to the cable voltage setting. We charge a tension in the cable equal to 3.75\times {10}^{5}N , and only the node F of the cable located at the free edge of the plate is active. Voltage losses due to steel relaxation and back anchoring are neglected. 1.3.2 Loading 2: The second load applies a pressure {P}_{0}={10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} , carried by the -z axis , to the entire plate. 1.4 Key steps in testing DEFI_CABLE_BP macro-command is used to obtain kinematic relationships between the plate and cable as well as the voltage-related load in the cable. Only the node F of the cable is considered active. The CALC_PRECONT macro-command is then launched to prestress the plate from the voltage of the given cable. The STAT_NON_LINE control is also used to apply the pressure load to the plate. The maximum value of the displacement on the free edge of the plate is then extracted at node D , to compare them with the reference values and thus validate the voltage setting of the prestress cables for elements hulls. 2 reference solution For each model, the objective is to recover the correct initial prestress voltage of the cable after the application of CALC_PRECONT, but also to determine the maximum displacement of the plate to node D following the z axis after the application of the pressure. 2.1 Baseline For determining maximum displacement, the theory of bending beams is used. For one clamped beam at one end and free of the other under distributed load, the maximum displacement at the free end called deflection is given by: f=-\frac{{\mathit{qL}}^{4}}{\mathrm{8EI}} q : the force distributed in N/m . L : the length of the beam in m . E : the Young's modulus of the plate, so concrete in \mathit{Pa} . I=\frac{{t}^{3}l}{12} : the quadratic moment of the beam relative to the y axis in {m}^{4} . For pressure force: Thanks to its excentre, the cable contributes to the rigidity of the model: {(\mathit{EI})}_{\mathit{eq}}={E}_{b}\frac{{t}^{3}l}{12}+{E}_{a}{a}_{x}l\times {e}_{z}^{2} {a}_{x}=\frac{A}{\mathit{dx}} : is the rate of railing. {(\mathit{EI})}_{\mathit{eq}}=13.50{\mathit{MN.m}}^{2} The deflection under pressure loading is calculated as follows: {f}_{p}=\frac{-{P}_{0}l\times {L}^{4}}{8{(\mathit{EI})}_{\mathit{eq}}} Then: {f}_{p}=-\mathrm{0.118552m} For the voltage setting of the prestress cable: The energized cable then applies an -{F}_{0} compression force and an bending moment -{e}_{z}{F}_{0} to the free end of the plate. With the principle of superposition, the expression of normal stress is: {\sigma}_{x}=\frac{-{F}_{0}}{\mathit{tl}}(1+\frac{12{e}_{z}z}{{t}^{2}}) If the effects of Poisson's ratio are ignored, the displacement field is given by: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}u(x,y,z)=\frac{-{F}_{0}}{{E}_{b}\mathit{tl}}(1+\frac{12{e}_{z}z}{{t}^{2}})x\\ v(x,y,z)=0\\ w(x,y,z)=\frac{{F}_{0}}{{E}_{b}\mathit{tl}}(\frac{6{e}_{z}}{{t}^{2}}{x}^{2})\end{array} The movements are given at the free end of the beam to node D , i.e. in (4,0.5,0) : \lbrace \begin{array}{c}u(x,y,z)=-\mathrm{0.375mm}\\ v(x,y,z)=0\\ w(x,y,z)=\mathrm{16.875mm}\end{array} By superimposition, the theoretical maximum displacement of the prestressed plate under the pressure force is: {f}_{\mathit{tot}}={f}_{p}+w {f}_{\mathit{tot}}=-\mathrm{0.101677m} 2.2 Uncertainty about the solution analytical solution. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics - Modelling: 3D - Finished elements type: Hexahedron (HEXA8), \mathrm{0.05m} height dimension and \mathrm{0.04m} length dimension and \mathrm{0.04m} maximum width. The plate is cut in 13 elements on its width, 100 on its length and 4 on its thickness. The steel frame is modeled by elements BARRE. The test case also validates the calculation of the elastic matrix (RIGI_MECA) when the reference axis is not confused with the elastic centre line (excenter). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A L=1m length console beam (see Figure 1). v3.03.145 SSLS145 - Calculation of the securing of a flat plate loaded in its plane v3.03.145 SSLS145 - Calculation of the securing of a flat plate loaded in its plane Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the COMBINAISON_FERRAILLAGE macro command which calculates the dimensioning ferrage density between several loading cases. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A rectangular plate of dimensions is considered: - thickness B=30\mathit{cm} - length H=3m - height L=12m Figure 1. Géométrie de la plaque rectangulaire. 1.2 Material properties The beton is isotropic elastic with the following material properties: - E=30000N/{\mathit{mm}}^{2} - \nu =0.3 For the calculation of the railing (at Eurocode 2), the following set of properties shall be considered: - Lower and upper coating {c}_{inf}={c}_{\sup}=20\mathit{mm} - Characteristic resistance to compression of {f}_{\mathit{ck}}=35\mathit{MPa} concrete - Nutring limit characteristic of steel {f}_{\mathit{yk}}=450\mathit{MPa} - Type of diagram (ε-ε): ‘B1' - Safety coefficient of steel with the ELU (Fondamental and Accidental) {\gamma}_{s}=1,15 - Concrete safety coefficient at the ELU (Fondamental and Accidental) {\gamma}_{c}=1,5 - Limiting stress of concrete to l-ELS Feature {\sigma}_{\text{c,lim}}=1,0\times 35=35\mathit{MPa} - Limiting steel constraint to the ELS Feature {\sigma}_{\text{s,lim}}=1,0\times 450=450\mathit{MPa} - Limiting stress of concrete to l-ELS Quasi Permanent {\sigma}_{\text{c,lim,qp}}=1,0\times 35=35\mathit{MPa} - Coefficient of equivalence steel-beton to l-ELS {\alpha}_{E}=15,0 - Steel class: ‘B - \mathit{FERR}\text{\_}\mathit{SYME}='\mathit{NON}' / \mathit{FERR}\text{\_}\mathit{COMP}='\mathit{OUI}' / \mathit{EPURE}\text{\_}\mathit{CISA}='\mathit{NON}' - Volumetric mass of steel {\rho}_{\mathit{acier}}=7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} - Maximum crack opening permitted in front of lower than l-l-ELS QP {w}_{\text{max,inf}}=0,25\mathit{mm} - Maximum crack opening permitted in the upper face of the ELS QP {w}_{\text{max,sup}}=0,3\mathit{mm} - Load time coefficient for calculation at l-ELS QP {K}_{T}=0,4 - Diameter of the following bars ‘X' for calculation at l-l-ELS QP {\varphi}_{X}=20,0\mathit{mm} - Diameter of the following bars ‘Y' for calculation at l-l-ELS QP {\varphi}_{Y}=25,0\mathit{mm} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The plate is loaded in its plane by a {F}_{Z}=-1,5\cdot {10}^{6}N shear force in the first load case (nodal loading " shearLd1 " in the command file). This load case will be tested at the ELS QUASI PERMANENT. A second load case (nodal loading " shearLd2 " in the command file) is obtained by applying double the load, {F}_{Z}=-3\cdot {10}^{6}N . This load case will be tested at the ELS CARACTERISTIQUE. A third load case (nodal loading " shearLd3 " in the command file) is obtained by applying the triple of this force, i.e. {F}_{Z}=-4,5\cdot {10}^{6}N . This load case will be tested at l-l-ELU. The plate is then loaded into its plane by a traction force {F}_{Y}=1\cdot {10}^{6}N (nodal loading " tractLd1 " in the control file). This load case will be tested at the ELS QUASI PERMANENT. A second load case (nodal loading " tractLd2 " in the command file) is obtained by applying double this force, {F}_{Y}=2\cdot {10}^{6}N . This load case will be tested at the ELS CARACTERISTIQUE. A third load case (nodal loading " tractLd3 " in the command file) is obtained by applying the triple of this force, {F}_{Y}=3\cdot {10}^{6}N . This load case will be tested at l-ELU. The plate is finally loaded into its plane by a compression force {F}_{Y}=-1,5\cdot {10}^{6}N in a seventh load case (nodal loading " comprLd1 " in the command file). This load case will be tested at the ELS CARACTERISTIQUE. A last load case (nodal loading " comprLd2 " in the command file) is obtained by applying double the load, {F}_{Y}=-3\cdot {10}^{6}N . v3.03.311 SSLA311 – Circular fissure subject to an annular charge v3.03.311 SSLA311 – Circular fissure subject to an annular charge Summary: This test case deals with the case of an internal crack located in the centre of a circular bar, in axisymmetric mode. The particularity of the load is that the linear load applies to a ring very close to the crack bottom. The fixed parameter is the radius of the a crack, and the parameter to be explored is the application radius of the c charge. The medium is elastic, linear, homogeneous and isotropic. The geometric domain is assumed to be unlimited in r and z . The meshes must therefore take into account the proximity of the load in such a way as to respect the load application deck. Since the load is normal at the crack, we calculate the characteristic coefficient of the K breaker mechanics in pure I mode. Then we use the Irwin formula in flat deformation to deduce G from it. This is of course an approximation. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Figure 1.1Géométrie du problème 1.2 Material properties | Young's modulus | E=2\times {10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio | \nu =0.3 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The point \mathit{PB} is used for the application of {F}_{Y} force. The position of the point \mathit{PB} is different depending on the modellings, and is managed by the C parameter. The distance a separating the \mathit{P8} and \mathit{P0} points is a constant parameter ( a=0,1 ). In the different models, the c/a ratio is modified. The lip of the crack is the \mathit{P8P0} straight. \mathit{P0} is therefore the crack front. The differences point-based, which is shown at the tested points, notably the point D , appears to be due to experimental uncertainty, probably reinforced by uncertainty about the graphical sampling. On the other hand, the solutions proposed by Batoz in deep hull theory are well verified by the four modellings, with relative errors of less than 5% for the long cylinder. It appears that: - modellings TRIA3 and QUAD4 are substantially equivalent for this problem, - the relative errors are much lower for the long cylinder (modellings C and D) than for the short cylinder (modellings A and B): at point F , the error is reduced by a factor 10 compared to the Batoz reference solution, - mesh refinement does not significantly minimize relative differences, both with TRIA3 and QUAD4. It is therefore found that the results degrade when the ratio of length to diameter decreases, in fact the geometric effects become important with this type of Modelling. It would be desirable to be able to perform a calculation in elements finished shells in orthotropic medium, in order to better take into account curvature, the plates constituting a case limit.

The problem is implemented: - in 3D in Modelling A - in C_PLAN in Modelling B 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is an elastic cube (or squared in 2D), 1,000 mm side and crossed by an oblique interface at 45°. The cube is positioned so that 0\le x\le 1000 , 0\le y\le 1000 and 0\le z\le 1000 . | | | --- | Figure 1.1-a: géométrie de la structure étudiée 1.2 Material properties The material of the volume follows an elastic law and interface to the CZM_ELAS_MIX law. u =0.2 | Poisson's ratio | | {k}_{n}=20	ext{MPa/mm} | Stiffness of the interface in the normal direction | | {k}_{t}=40	ext{MPa/mm} | Stiffness of the interface in the tangent direction | Furthermore, the increase coefficient of the Lagrangian (PENA_LAGR_ABSO), without impact here because the solution is homogeneous, is fixed to r=600	ext{MPa/mm} . Finally, we examine the six possible adhesion combinations: normal elastic, unilateral or perfect adhesion and tangential elastic or perfect adhesion. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The cube is subjected to \sigma ={\sigma}_{0}	ext{}{e}_{x}\otimes {e}_{x} constraint. More precisely: - x=0 face is blocked in {u}_{x}=0 - y=0 face is blocked in {u}_{y}=0 - z=0 face is blocked in {u}_{z}=0 - The x=1000	ext{mm} face is subjected to T={\sigma}_{0}{e}_{x} overfacial force These conditions also allow to block rigid body movements. The stress intensity {\sigma}_{0} successively takes the values +2 MPa and -2 MPa. 1.4 Initial conditions As this is an elastic problem, there is no need for initial conditions. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution This problem admits an analytical solution that is exposed in this part. v3.04.101 SSLV101 - Application of the industrial declination of the Beremin model to a CT test piece v3.04.101 SSLV101 - Application of the industrial declination of the Beremin model to a CT test piece Summary: This test validates the use of the POST_BEREMIN command to calculate Weibull stress overfacial density (use of keyword METHODE_2D). For this, a CT test piece is considered and this stress density of Weibull is calculated. in both planes at the end of the crack front. Here it is simply a question of checking the post-processing with POST_BEREMIN. How to get the concept result given at the command input So we choose an elastic behavior, so we keep a reasonable calculation time. Two modellingss are present in this test: - Modelling A: separate mesh density plane meshes (use of keyword MAILLAGE_PLAN), with elements 3D/3D_SI finished - B Modelling: plans defined through nodes groups in mesh volume (use of keyword GROUP_NO_PLAN), with elements 3D/3D_SI finished - Modelling C: plans defined through nodes groups in the mesh volume (use of keyword GROUP_NO_PLAN), with elements finished 3D_GRAD_INCO 1 Problem considered 1.1 Mesh This CT25 test piece is deliberately coarsely meshed, so that it can be stored a test case with a reasonable calculation time. Only a quarter of the test piece is represented. The crack front is discretized by 4 elements, and a mesh set to hexahedrons is present around this crack front. The mesh contains 10,879 nodes and 3,092 elements quadratic volume. 1.2 Behaviour and modelling For modellings A and B, the elements hexahedrons are assigned to 3D_SI modelling, the other elements to 3D modelling. The behavior is linear elastic, in small deformations. The Young's modulus retained is 210 GPa and the Poisson's ratio 0.3. For Modelling C, all elements are assigned 3D_GRAD_INCO modelling. v3.04.105 SSLV105 - Centrifugal raid of a rotating beam v3.04.105 SSLV105 - Centrifugal raid of a rotating beam Summary: Test of Mechanical structures in linear static analysis. The geometry is that of an slender beam that is rotated around one of its ends. Five modellings are considered: elements 3D (HEXA20), multifibre Timoshenko beams (POU_D_TGM), d-Euler beams (POU_D_E) and Timoshenko beams (POU_D_T) with constant or variable cross-section. The rotational inertia forces (such as the SSLV104 test) are tested here with centrifugal stiffening. The reference solutions (analytical and numerical) take into account the additional rigidity term due to rotation. The results are identical to those corresponding to the reference solutions. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure is composed of a space-oriented slender beam that is carried by the (1,1,1) vector axis. As regards the section of the beam, two cases are considered: - Constant square section, dØaire 4.0{10}^{-4}{m}^{2} (modellings A, B, C and D), - Circular cross section with homothetic variation, initial 2.0{10}^{-2}m radius and final 4.0{10}^{-2}m radius (modelization E). In all the above cases, the length of the beam is 0.5m . 1.2 Material properties E=2.{10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} \nu =0 \rho =7800\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Clamped beam, free in rotation around an axis perpendicular to its largest dimension and passing through the centre of the clamped face. Contact details of the rotation vector: (1,0,–1) . Rotation speed: \omega =3000\mathrm{rd}/s . The important value of the rotation speed is nothing physical. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation methods used for reference solutions In the beam local marker, the equation for displacement {U}_{x} (without neglecting elongation) is given by: \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(ES(x)\frac{\partial {U}_{x}}{\partial x}\right)+\rho S\left(x\right){\omega}^{2}\left(x+{U}_{x}\right)=0.\text{ } The boundary conditions associated with this equation sew: \begin{array}{}{U}_{x}(0)=0\\ \frac{\partial {U}_{x}}{\partial x}(L)={\sigma}_{xx}(L)=0\end{array} . 2.1.1 Case of a constant cross-section – analytical solution In the case of a constant cross-section (modellings A, B, C and D), the above equation may be simplified as follows: \frac{{\partial}^{2}{U}_{x}}{\partial {x}^{2}}+\frac{\rho}{E}{\omega}^{2}(x+{U}_{x})=0 . \alpha =\sqrt{\frac{\rho {\omega}^{2}}{E}} is installed. By integrating the previous differential equation, the beam marker is obtained: {U}_{x}(x)=\frac{\sin(\alpha x)}{\alpha \cos(\alpha L)}-x {U}_{y}={U}_{z}=0 In the global marker, the total point displacement of the beam is therefore written: \begin{array}{}{U}_{x}(X,Y,Z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\frac{\sin(\alpha r)}{\alpha \cos(\alpha L)}-r)\\ {U}_{y}(X,Y,Z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\frac{\sin(\alpha r)}{\alpha \cos(\alpha L)}-r)\\ {U}_{z}(X,Y,Z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(\frac{\sin(\alpha r)}{\alpha \cos(\alpha L)}-r)\end{array} , with r=\sqrt{{X}^{2}+{Y}^{2}+{Z}^{2}} . 2.1.2 Case of a variable section – Digital solution In the case of the variable section beam of model E, the reference solution is derived from an Aster calculation with a 3D model with a quadratic 19268 elements (TETRA10) and 29122 nodes. 2.2 Baseline Values of the three movements in the centre of the section furthest from the axis of rotation. 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution Analytical solution for modellings A, B, C and D. v3.04.115 SSLV115 - element prestressed concrete compression and gravity v3.04.115 SSLV115 - element prestressed concrete compression and gravity Summary: This test allows simple verification of gravity calculations for elements concrete with prestress cables, in static linear structures mechanics. Concrete L-element is volumetric, and prestress cable elements are elements BARRE or elements CABLE_GAINE with a adhering law. The modellings A , B and C test the application of gravity on elements BARRE or elements CABLE_GAINE, for two directions of the gravity. The values tested are the result of the reactions on the supports equal to the total weight of the model. This test case also validates the CALC_PRECONT command for different types of elements \mathrm{3D} (parallelepiped, pyramid and tetrahedral). To do this, we check the values of the calculated stresses. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A rectangle parallelepiped Modelling concrete, and a line included in this volume Modelling the prestress cable: All dimensions are in meters. L-sections of the cable is A=0.00015{m}^{2} The cable is parallel to the x axis. Its intersection with the (\mathrm{Oyz}) plane is defined by the point (1.,0.3) . 1.2 Material properties E=2.1{10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} for cable, and E={3.10}^{10}\mathrm{Pa} for concrete. {\rho}_{c}=2{10}^{4}\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} for cable and concrete {\rho}_{b}=3\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} (non-physical values to make the weight of the cable predominant) 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads \mathrm{DY}=0 to point 1001 , \mathrm{DZ}=0 to all nodes to z=0 , and \mathrm{DX}=0 to all nodes to x=0 face . Only one load is applied: the gravity, with g=10m/{s}^{2} , successively in the direction –z and then –x . There is also an initial voltage in the N=2.{10}^{5}N cable. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution > The problem is solved in an analytical way. The result of the effort (equal to the total weight) is: - weight of concrete: \mathrm{Pb}=V{\rho}_{b}g - Cable weight: \mathrm{Pc}=AL{\rho}_{c}g in the direction where the gravity is applied. The structure is isostatic. Prestressing forces are self-balanced. {S}_{b} is the concrete area in a plane perpendicular to the {S}_{b}=(2\times 0,6){m}^{2} cable, {E}_{a} and {E}_{b} are the modules of steel and concrete, {N}_{a} the tension in the cable and {\sigma}_{b} and the stress in the concrete after tensioning. The balance of the concrete and cable assembly is written: {N}_{a}+{\sigma}_{b}{S}_{b}=0 so {\sigma}_{b}=-\frac{{N}_{a}}{{S}_{b}} Since CALC_PRECONT is used, and there is no friction or loss in the cable, the tension in the cable is equal to the initial voltage, unlike the case where RELA_CINE_BP is used, which is subject to prestress losses due to shortening of the concrete (see SSNP108, V6.03.108 test). > The deformation of the concrete is: {\varepsilon}_{b}=\frac{{\sigma}_{b}}{{E}_{b}} 2.2 Baseline - Resulting from the efforts: R=132N - Constraint in concrete: {\sigma}_{b}=-1,66666667{10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} - Normal effort in steel: {N}_{a}=2{10}^{5}\mathit{Pa} - Deformation in concrete: {\varepsilon}_{b}=-5,555555555{10}^{-6} 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution This is a analytical solution. The solution gives the average stress in the concrete. When there are several elements (modellings B and C ) you must make an average of the values of the mesh cells. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The concrete volume is modelled by a single hexaedric element. The prestress cable is modeled first by 4 BARRE elements, then by 4 elements CABLE_GAINE. 3.2 Mesh characteristics With BARRE model cable: 4 mesh cells SEG2, mesh cell HEXA8 With CABLE_GAINE model cable: 4 mesh cells SEG3, mesh cell HEXA8 x y z 3.3 Test values and modelling results A The calculations are done for the first time with BARRE Modelling and a second time with CABLE_GAINE Modelling using the CABLE_GAINE_FROT law-enforced case. The prestress cable is modeled by 4 BARRE elements. 5.2 Mesh characteristics 4 mesh cells SEG2, 5 mesh cells TETRA4 x z 5.3 Modelling results C | Identification | Reference type | Reference | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Gravity next –z | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 132 | {10}^{\text{-8}}\text{\%} | | Gravity next –x | 'ANALYTIQUE' | 132 | {10}^{\text{-8}}\text{\%} | | Constraint in concrete SIXX | 'ANALYTIQUE' | -1,66666667{10}^{5} | {10}^{\text{-6}}\text{\%} | | Deformation in concrete: EPXX | 'ANALYTIQUE' | -5,555555555{10}^{\text{-4}} | {10}^{\text{-6}}\text{\%} | 6 Summary of the results This very simple test allows you to check the gravity in the elements for the correct operation of the elements, which allows you to model the prestress, i.e. BARRE and CABLE_GAINE, which is verified by the perfect coincidence of the results with the analytical solution. v3.04.140 SSLV140 - Calculation of actual modules by Python method v3.04.140 SSLV140 - Calculation of actual modules by Python method Summary: A test with an analytical reference is presented here. The geometry treated is a set of two cubes with different elastic properties. The aim is to find the Young's modulus of the mixture made up of these two cubes in two directions. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The following surfaces are defined: - \mathrm{YZ1} face: containing nodes \mathrm{P1},\mathrm{P3},\mathrm{P5} and \mathrm{P7} . - \mathrm{YZ2} face: containing nodes \mathrm{P9},\mathrm{P10},\mathrm{P11} and \mathrm{P12} . - \mathrm{XY1} face: containing nodes \mathrm{P1},\mathrm{P2},\mathrm{P9},\mathrm{P3},\mathrm{P4} and \mathrm{P10} . - \mathrm{XY2} face: containing nodes \mathrm{P5},\mathrm{P6},\mathrm{P11},\mathrm{P7},\mathrm{P8} and \mathrm{P12} . - \mathrm{XZ1} face: containing nodes \mathrm{P3},\mathrm{P4},\mathrm{P10},\mathrm{P7},\mathrm{P8} and \mathrm{P12} . - \mathrm{XZ2} face: containing nodes \mathrm{P1},\mathrm{P2},\mathrm{P9},\mathrm{P5},\mathrm{P6} and \mathrm{P11} . and the following elements: - \mathrm{M1} element: containing nodes \mathrm{P1},\mathrm{P2},\mathrm{P3},\mathrm{P4},\mathrm{P5},\mathrm{P6},\mathrm{P7} and \mathrm{P8} . - \mathrm{M2} element: containing nodes \mathrm{P2},\mathrm{P9},\mathrm{P4},\mathrm{P10},\mathrm{P6},\mathrm{P11},\mathrm{P8} and \mathrm{P12} . 1.2 Material properties Two materials are used: - Material \mathit{MAT1} assigned to the element \mathrm{M1} : Young's modulus : \mathit{E1}=200000\mathit{MPa} Poisson's ratio : {\nu}_{1}=0.3 - Material \mathit{MAT2} assigned to the element \mathrm{M2} : Young's modulus : \mathrm{E2}=100000\mathrm{MPa} Poisson's ratio : {\nu}_{2}=0.3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads First calculation: It is a simple tensile calculation according to the X direction: - A linear {\varepsilon}_{xx}=1 elastic deformation is imposed on the \mathrm{YZ2} surface. - The \mathrm{YZ1} surface does not move in the direction X . Second calculation: It is a simple tensile calculation according to the Y direction: - A linear {\varepsilon}_{yy}=1 elastic deformation is imposed on the \mathrm{XZ2} surface. - The \mathrm{XZ1} surface does not move in the direction Y . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation According to the general theory of homogenization of composite materials [bib1], the effective {E}_{xx}^{\mathit{eff}} and {E}_{yy}^{\mathit{eff}} modules in X and Y directions of a mixture of the above-mentioned shape are given by the following formulae: \frac{1}{{E}_{xx}^{\mathit{eff}}}=\frac{{f}_{1}}{{E}_{1}}+\frac{{f}_{2}}{{E}_{2}} {E}_{yy}^{\mathit{eff}}={f}_{1}{E}_{1}+{f}_{2}{E}_{2} {f}_{1} and {f}_{2} are the density fractions of each material, in our case: {f}_{1}={f}_{2}=0.5 2.2 Bibliographical references 1. BORNET, T. BRETHEAU and P. GILORMINI: Homogenization in Materials Mechanics (T1). Hermes Science Publications - 2001. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes: 12. 3D Modelling: 2 elements quadratic volume: HEXA8. 3.2 Tested Features Python commands are inserted directly into the command file ASTER. These commands are used to write post-processing functions on the result fields, such as averages, trace of a strain or strain tensor, etc. The result fields are recovered by the EXTR_COMP command. 3.3 Test values First calculation: The Young's modulus in this case following the X direction is the average of the {\sigma}_{xx} stresses: {E}_{xx}^{\mathit{eff}}=\langle {\sigma}_{xx}\rangle Second calculation: The Young's modulus in this case following the Y direction is the average of the {\sigma}_{yy} stresses: {E}_{yy}^{\mathit{eff}}=\langle {\sigma}_{yy}\rangle | Identification | Reference | Aster | \text{\%} difference | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \langle {\sigma}_{xx}\rangle | 133333 | 134134 | 1.00 | | \langle {\sigma}_{yy}\rangle | 150000 | 150000 | 0.00 | 4 Summary of the results The results are in perfect agreement with the reference solution.

v3.04.147 RCCM09 - POST_RCCM Operator: Calculation of the boot factor v3.04.147 RCCM09 - POST_RCCM Operator: Calculation of the boot factor Summary: This static linear thermomechanical test validates the calculation of the boot factor with the POST_RCCM command (option AMORCAGE, EVOLUTION results). The analytical solution is simple, and allows you to test the post-processing in the sense of the RCC_M. Test case Model A consists of a set of unit tests, where stresses are directly supplied and not calculated, to verify the correct functioning of the initiation factor calculation. Model B is the complete resolution (modelization, stress calculation and initiation factor estimation) of an Reference problem presented below. 1 Reference problem of Modelling B 1.1 Geometry The Reference problem is flat. A rectangular plate, W wide, with an opening crack of a length is considered. The starting factor related to the geometric singularity in P is investigated, with the structure being subjected to several transient mechanical loads. Definition of Reference problem and local reference 1.2 Material properties The material properties selected are as follows: 1. Young's modulus: E=2.E+05\mathrm{MPa} ; 2. Poisson's ratio : \nu =0,3 . The characteristics of the RCC-Mcorrespond to the \text{Ni-Cr-Fe} alloy (inconel): 1. parameters of the boot law: A_AMORC = 7091 and B_AMORC = -0.1823; 2. Effective stress parameter: R_AMORC = 1.63; 3. distance d to singularity: D_AMORC = 0,046\mathrm{mm} . v3.04.153 SSLV153 - Error indicators – mesh cells volumetrics and functions v3.04.153 SSLV153 - Error indicators – mesh cells volumetrics and functions Summary: This case tests the calculation of error indicators per residue and in amount of interest on a very simple mesh: 4 mesh cells volumetrics of each possible type, tetrahedron, pentahedron, hexahedron and pyramid. Compared to other test cases, this one allows to test the non-regression on two functions: - the consideration of all types of edges for mesh cells 3D, - the load expressed by functions. This case is not a validation of error indicators, but it can be used as an example for their use. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The field studied is a volume with facets, the only interest of which is to be an assembly of mesh cells different. The starting point is a cube on the side 100. The front side of this cube is the base of a pyramid; the contiguous side is the base of a pentahedron. Between the pentahedron and the pyramid, there is a tetrahedron. Figure 1.1-1 .: Breaking view of the field of calculation 1.2 Material properties The material is defined with: Young's modulus =400000 Poisson's ratio =0.3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The upper side of the block is subjected to a pressure of 13, 14, 15 and 16 respectively, for the upper side of the tetrahedron, pyramid, pentahedron and hexahedron, respectively. The outer triangular side of the pentahedron and the rear side of the hexahedron are clamped. The other external sides are free. A zero normal stress value is voluntarily imposed to ensure correct calculation of error indicators. 2 reference solution There is no analytical solution. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The calculation is a linear mechanical resolution. A residual error indicator is then calculated. The surfacial terms are then tested. The following dual calculation is defined to optimize the \mathrm{DZ} component of the displacement field. This modifies the load by cancelling external pressures and adding an internal, unitary volume force according to Z . The same calculation is done twice. The first calculation is performed with loads expressed as real constants. The second calculation is done with loads in the form of functions. The results are strictly identical. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The original mesh was created "hand-made", in MED format. It is in degree 1. It is passed in degree 2 by the MODI_MAILLAGE command. Each volume form corresponds to a unique mesh cell 3D. The hexahedron is in contact on one of its sides with the pentahedron and on one side close to the pyramid. The tetrahedron is located between the pentahedron and the pyramid. v3.04.159 SSLV159 - Cantilever beam subject to static deflection loading v3.04.159 SSLV159 - Cantilever beam subject to static deflection loading Summary: This test validates the connection between 1D and 3D models, in the Arlequin frame (3D_POU_ARLEQUIN) [1]. It is a cantilever beam model, clamped at one end and subjected to a static deflection loading at the other end. The results of the calculations are compared with those obtained by Code_aster with a 1D reference model and a 1D-3D mixed model connected with the 3D_POU option. The results coincide perfectly with the reference solutions. 1 Reference problem The objective of this test case is to validate the Arlequin 3-D beam connection in Code_Aster. The results obtained are compared with those obtained from two modellings in Code_Aster: - 1D reference mono-modelization - 1D-3D mixed reference model with 3D_POU connection 1.1 Geometry A beam of length 0.35 m on the X axis, clamped on the left end and charged with a concentrated force F at its right end. The cross section of the beam is a rectangle of width b and height h (in this case: b = h = 0.02 m). Image 1.1-1 : Rotor Geometry 1.2 Material properties The cantilever beam has a density of \rho =7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} . The Young's modulus is E=2.{10}^{11}N{m}^{-2} and the Poisson's ratio is \nu =0,3 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The left end of the beam (X = 0.15 m) is fixed, and the right end (X = 0.5 m) is subjected to a concentrated load that is vertically directed downwards at 500 N. 2 reference solution The reference solution is derived from a 1D calculation with Code_Aster (see Model B). The latter is itself validated in relation to the RDM solution for a cantilever beam. The analytical solution is equal to: w=\frac{F.{L}^{3}}{3.E.J} where F is the concentrated force applied, L is the length of the beam, E is the Young's modulus of the material, J=\frac{b.{h}^{3}}{12} is the moment of inertia of the cross section of the beam. 1. The stresses are not calculated but extracted from tables. This test consists of two modellings, which differ by taking into account thermal transients: - the first one calculates the two thermal transients on two axisymmetric sections of the same diameter and thickness as the straight pipes and elbow, - the second reads directly the values from a temperature reading on the thermal calculation of the elbow, previously modelled in \mathrm{3D} by the MMC department. v3.04.312 SSLV312 – Semi-elliptic fissure perpendicular to the interface of a bi-material v3.04.312 SSLV312 – Semi-elliptic fissure perpendicular to the interface of a bi-material Summary: This test case studies the influence of a semi-elliptic crack perpendicular to the interface of two elastic materials. The first model represents a circular crack (modelization A) and the second a large axis-to-small axis-to-axis elliptical crack equal to 2. The models are massive three-dimensional with a uniform load by pressure on the lip of the crack. The objective of the study is to calculate local G along the crack bottom and to evaluate the mean quadratic the difference between the geometric correction factor {F}_{I} along the crack bottom and an article reference value. {F}_{I} is calculated from the local G using the Irwin formula in flat deformations. Because cracks are located in an infinite medium, the finite element model limits were selected based on the feedback gained during pre-validation of the cracked block. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Figure 1.1 Geometry of the problem The massif consists of two materials, VMAT1 for the upper part and VMAT2 for the lower part. v3.04.316 SSLV316 – Spread crack imposed with X-FEM v3.04.316 SSLV316 – Spread crack imposed with X-FEM Summary: The purpose of this test is to verify that the simplex, upwind and geometrical methods of the PROPA_FISS operator correctly calculate the position of the bottom of a 3D crack that propagates in mixed mode. Several propagations of a crack are simulated by imposing a given advance and propagation direction. The position of the crack after each propagation is therefore known and it can be verified whether the bottom position calculated by the operator PROPA_FISS is correct. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Figure 1.1-a : geometry of cracked plate Geometrical dimensions of the cracked plate: | width | L=\mathrm{8m} | | --- | --- | | thickness | E=\mathrm{1m} | | height | H=\mathrm{18m} | Initial length of flat crack: {a}_{0}=\mathrm{2m} The crack is positioned in the middle of the plate height ( H/2 ). 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus E=205000\mathrm{MPa} Poisson's ratio \nu =0.3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Figure 1.3-a : boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions: > Point P : \Delta X=\Delta Y=\Delta Z=0 > Points on the \mathrm{AB} segment: \Delta X=\Delta Z=0 > Surface points \text{INF} : \Delta Z=0 Loading: > Surface pressure \text{SUP} : P=-1\mathrm{MPa} The load is constant during propagation. Three calls to the operator PROPA_FISS are made to simulate a propagation of the initial crack already present in the structure. At each call the advance and the propagation direction of each point of the crack bottom are imposed: > Point forward from background: \Delta a=0.4m > Transmission angle: \beta =30° The positive direction of the \beta angle is visible on the . The bottom of the crack remains always straight throughout the spread. The motivation for this choice will be explained in paragraph 4. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation It is intended to verify that the position of the bottom after propagation, calculated by the operator PROPA_FISS, is correct. Therefore, the theoretical position determined by the advance and the propagation direction imposed must be calculated. As already noted, the crack bottom remains straight throughout the spread. The bottom is always perpendicular to the two surfaces of the plate parallel to the \mathit{YZ} plane, as shown. The bottom position can therefore be indicated using only the Y and Z coordinates. The initial position is as follows: > {y}_{0}={a}_{0}=2.0 > {z}_{0}=9.0 After propagation i , the new background position can be calculated as follows: > {y}_{i}={y}_{i-1}+\Delta a\cdot \cos(i\cdot \beta ) > {z}_{i}={z}_{i-1}+\Delta a\cdot \sin(i\cdot \beta ) 2.2 Quantities and reference results For the three propagations calculated in the tests, the background position is as follows: | Propagation | Coord {y}_{i} | Coord {z}_{i} | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 2.34641 | 9.19999 | | 2 | 2.54642 | 9.54640 | | 3 | 2.54644 | 9.94640 | Table 2.1 In the current version of Code_Aster, the coordinates of the crack bottom points are only available in the .mess file and therefore they cannot be verified directly in the command file. However, for this test case, we know the theoretical position and the shape (a segment) of the crack bottom. In fact the bottom is always coincide with the edge that connects the two (0,{y}_{i},{z}_{i}) and (1,{y}_{i},{z}_{i}) points. Using MACR_LIGN_COUPE, we can record the values of the level set at the intersection points between this edge and the faces of the elements of the mesh. If the position of the bottom after propagation is correctly calculated by PROPA_FISS, the value of the two level set must be equal to zero for all intersection points found because, by definition, the crack bottom is formed by all points where the level set tangent and normal are equal to zero. This explains why it was decided to give the same advance and direction of propagation at all points of the crack bottom. Even if the crack bottom is located by only two coordinates, the propagation is 3D and the algorithms implemented in PROPA_FISS calculate a 3D propagation. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The upwind method is used by PROPA_FISS to solve crack propagation equations. No auxiliary grid is used. This is possible because the mesh of the structure is very regular. The calculation field is located around the bottom of the crack. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The structure is modelled by a mesh composed of 6720 elements HEXA8 (see ). Figure 3.2-a : mesh of the structure The mesh is not very refined to reduce the calculation time. The size of the elements is uniform and equal to 0.29x0.33x0.25m . 3.3 Tested quantities and results The intersection points between the edge giving the theoretical background position and the faces of elements mesh are calculated using MACR_LIGN_COUPE (see ). For each of these points, the value of the normal ( \mathrm{LSN} ) and tangent ( \mathrm{LST} ) level set is calculated using the POST_RELEVE_T operator and the maximum and minimum values are verified to be almost zero: | Propag. i | Max {\mathit{LSN}}_{i} | Min {\mathit{LSN}}_{i} | Max LST_ i | Min {\mathit{LST}}_{i} | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | -2.64E-16 | -8.40E-16 | 9,71E-16 | -4,16E-17 | | 2 | -3.30E-04 | -3.30E-04 | -2.23E-06 | -2.25E-06 | | 3 | -3.44E-03 | -3.53E-03 | -2.20E-04 | -2.22E-04 | The values obtained are calculated from the nodes values of mesh using the elements shape functions. Therefore, these values are expected to be affected by an error that depends on the size of the elements of mesh. Indeed, the level set representation accuracy is itself related to the size of the elements. Therefore, a tolerance is used to check if the calculated level sets are almost zero. Considering that the mesh is coarse, a tolerance equal to 15% of the length of the largest mesh edge in the propagation zone is affected: Tolerance used = 0.15\times 0.33=0.05m 3.4 Remarks All tested values respect the tolerance used. This means that the crack bottom position calculated by the upwind method is correct and that the domain location works well for the upwind method without auxiliary grid. It should be noted that after the three simulated propagations, the crack deviated from 90 . However, the total advance is small. Therefore, a very severe mixed mode propagation was simulated. v3.04.319 SSLV319 - Flat spread of semi-elliptic crack v3.04.319 SSLV319 - Flat spread of semi-elliptic crack Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the flat propagation of a crack by observing the displacement of the crack bottom during propagation. This test involves a paved stone with a flat semi-elliptic crack, subjected to a tensile force. The crack is represented by the X-FEM method and the simulated propagation using the PROPA_FISS command. We will compare the results with an experimental solution. This test contains four modellings: Modelling A uses mesh method from the PROPA_FISS operator. Modelling B uses GEOMETRIQUE method from the PROPA_FISS operator. Modelling C uses GEOMETRIQUE method of PROPA_FISS operator, with cohesive elements. Operation DETECT_COHESIF is used to determine front advance. Modelling D uses SIMPLEXE method of the PROPA_FISS operator. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A three-dimensional bar shall be considered to have the following dimensions: - height: \mathit{LZ} = 4 mm, - side: \mathit{LX} = \mathit{LY} = 1 mm. The bar has a flat, semi-elliptic crack. The crack is located in the \mathit{Oxy} plane. The crack characteristics are as follows: - half-large axis: a = 119 μm - half-small axis: b = 100 μm. ● A ● B ● C Figure 1.1-1: Géométrie de la fissure initiale 1.2 Material properties The material is elastic isotropic with properties of: E=200000\mathit{MPa} \nu =0,3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads 1.3.1 Cyclic loading for fatigue study The structure is subjected to a constant amplitude fatigue load: traction {\sigma}_{max}=220\mathit{MPa} and a ratio R=0,1 . Temperature is the ambient temperature. The loading frequency is 40\mathit{Hz} . A load of 4000 cycles is applied. The traction force is applied to the upper and lower surfaces. Blocking of rigid modes shall be carried out as follows: - the point A is blocked in the \mathit{Oy} and \mathit{Oz} directions, - the point B is blocked in the \mathit{Oy} and \mathit{Oz} directions, - point C is blocked in \mathit{Ox} and \mathit{Oz} directions. 1.3.2 Modelling with cohesive zones: monotonous loading For this model, the load is monotonous instead of cyclic: the structure is subjected to {\sigma}_{max}=220\mathit{MPa} traction. Blocking of rigid modes shall be carried out as follows: - the point A is blocked in the \mathit{Oy} and \mathit{Oz} directions, - the point B is blocked in the \mathit{Oy} and \mathit{Oz} directions, - point C is blocked in \mathit{Ox} and \mathit{Oz} directions. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution was obtained by experimental method 4 . v3.04.320 SSLV320 - Flat spread of a 3D crack dividing and merging with X-FEM v3.04.320 SSLV320 - Flat spread of a 3D crack dividing and merging with X-FEM Summary: The objective of this test is to verify that the different crack propagation methods available in PROPA_FISS correctly manage a 3D crack bottom that is divided into several bottoms and several bottoms that merge into a single bottom during propagation. In addition, this test gives an example of how mesh (Homard) refinement is used with the PROPA_FISS operator. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A 30\times 30\times 10\mathit{mm} size parallelepiped with three holes and a crack on one side is considered (Figure ). Figure 1.1-a : geometry of the structure considered 1.2 Material properties No material is defined because the elements model is not solved. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads No boundary condition is defined because the elements model is not solved. Two propagations in mode I of the existing crack with constant displacement are calculated along the bottom. The crack remains flat during propagation. Every step of propagation requires an advance equal to \Delta a=12\mathit{mm} . The bottom of the crack spreads while remaining always straight. 1.4 Initial conditions The initial crack is a half-plane. Its length is equal to {a}_{0}=4\mathit{mm} . The bottom of the crack is straight. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation At each propagation step the following two quantitiess will be calculated: - the number of pieces that make up the bottom of the crack, - the position of the crack. The problem is that of a 3D block cut by an XFEM interface. Multiaxial compression is applied to the entire block surface, including the XFEM interface. The expected analytical solution is a {P}_{1} displacement within the domain. This solution is naturally captured by elements {P}_{1} and {P}_{2} Code_Aster. v3.05.100 SSLX100 - 3D Mix - Cover - Bend beam v3.05.100 SSLX100 - 3D Mix - Cover - Bend beam Summary: This test allows to validate for a linear elastic calculation: - a mixture of different mechanical models: 3D model (element HEXA20), shell models (elements DKT, or elements COQUE_3D) and beam model (elements POU_D_E), - linear relationships between degrees of freedom, built especially with R3.03.03 and R3.03.06 connections. v3.05.101 SSLX101 - Straight pipe modeled in shell and beams v3.05.101 SSLX101 - Straight pipe modeled in shell and beams Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the restraint beam hull. The hose is clamped at one end, and subjected to 4 successive forces (traction and 3 moments) on the other end. Half of the pipe is mesh in shell, the other is mesh in beams. The clamped support and the connection between the shell and the beam are made by an restraint beam shell, in particular allowing only the torsor to transmit to the shell the forces of the beam type, without causing any harmful stresses. The reference solution is analytical (material resistance). the difference with the digital solution (3 to 5%) is explained by the fact that the mesh in shell is actually made up of element planes (facets). The geometry of the pipe is therefore approached. The solution obtained makes it possible to verify that the connection between the elements hull and the element beam is correct. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 80m straight hose, modeled in inshells between 0 and \mathrm{40m} , and in beams between 40 and \mathrm{80m} . Outside radius: \mathrm{2m} , thickness: \mathrm{0.1m} . The hose axis is in the \mathrm{Oxy} plane, inclined 30 degrees from \mathrm{Ox} . 1.2 Material properties E={2.10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} \nu =0.3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Clamped support "beam type" in x=y=0 , made by a restraint beam shell between the \mathrm{C1} edge of the hull and an point \mathrm{P1} (located in O ). This point is blocked. 4 unit load cases applied to point \mathit{P2}(80\times \mathit{cos30},80\times \mathit{sin30},0) \mathrm{Fx1}=\mathrm{1N} Traction on \mathrm{Ox1} axis, i.e. \mathrm{Fx}=\mathrm{cos30.Fx} and \mathrm{Fy}=\mathrm{sin30.Fx1} \mathrm{Mx1}=\mathrm{1Nm} twisting moment around \mathrm{Ox1} , i.e. \mathrm{Mx}=\mathrm{cos30.Mx1} and \mathrm{My}=\mathrm{sin30.Mx1} Bending moment \mathrm{My1}=\mathrm{1Nm} around \mathrm{Oy1} i.e. \mathrm{Mx}=-\mathrm{sin30.My1} and \mathrm{My}=\mathrm{cos30.My1} Bending moment around \mathrm{Oz} , i.e. \mathrm{Mz}=\mathrm{1Nm} 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution Analytical solution for each of the 4 loading cases: In beam theory, in the context of the Euler-Bernouilli hypothesis, the solution of Reference problem is that of an straight beam subjected to effort and moments at one end and clamped at the other end: Traction : \boldsymbol{u}_{x_1} = F_{x_1} \frac{x}{ES} \boldsymbol{e}_{x1} Torsion : \boldsymbol{\theta}_{x_1} = M_{x_1} \frac{x}{GJ} \boldsymbol{e}_{x1} Flexion around O_{y1} : \boldsymbol{u}_{z} & &= - M_{y} \frac{x^2}{2 EI_{y_1}} \boldsymbol{e}_{z} \\ \boldsymbol{\theta}_{y_1} & = (-\partial_x \boldsymbol{u}_{z} \cdot \boldsymbol{e}_{z} ) \boldsymbol{e}_{y_1} & = M_{y} \frac{x}{EI_{y_1}} \boldsymbol{e}_{y1} \\ Flexion around O_{z} : \boldsymbol{u}_{y_1} & & = M_{z} \frac{x^2}{2 EI_{z}} \boldsymbol{e}_{y_1} \\ \boldsymbol{\theta}_{z} & = (\partial_x \boldsymbol{u}_{y_1} \cdot \boldsymbol{e}_{y_1} ) \boldsymbol{e}_{z} & = M_{z} \frac{x}{EI_{z}} \boldsymbol{e}_{z} \\ No loading involves shear force, loading cases bending being in bending pure . The reference solutions are also valid for the cinematic of the Timoshenko (in addition to Euler-Bernouilli's cinematic), as indicated in V3.01.102. This implies that the same reference solutions can be used for elements POU_D_E and TUYAU_3M . 2.2 Baseline Traction : u_{x1}(P_2) = F_{x_1} \frac{L}{ES} So \begin{cases} u_{x}(P_2) & = F_{x_1} \frac{L}{ES} \cos(30)\\ u_{y}(P_2) & = F_{x_1} \frac{L}{ES} \sin(30)\\ \end{cases} Torsion : \theta_{x1}(P_2) = M_{x_1} \frac{L}{GJ} So \begin{cases} \theta_{x}(P_2) & = M_{x_1} \frac{L}{GJ} \cos(30)\\ \theta_{y}(P_2) & = M_{x_1} \frac{L}{GJ} \sin(30)\\ \end{cases} Flexion around O_{y_1} : \theta_{y_1}(P_2) = M_{y_1} \frac{L}{EI_{y_1}} So \begin{cases} \theta_{x}(P_2) & = - M_{y_1} \frac{L}{EI_{y_1}} \sin(30)\\ \theta_{y}(P_2) & = M_{y_1} \frac{L}{EI_{y_1}} \cos(30)\\ u_z(P_2) & = - M_{y_1} \frac{L^2}{2EI_{y_1}} \end{cases} Flexion around O_{z} : u_{y_1} = M_{z} \frac{L^2}{2 EI_{z}} So \begin{cases} u_x(P_2) & = - M_{z} \frac{L^2}{2 EI_{z}} \sin(30) \\ u_y(P_2) & = M_{z} \frac{L^2}{2 EI_{z}} \cos(30) \\ \theta_{z}(P_2) & = M_{z} \frac{L}{EI_{z}} \\ \end{cases} Note: Using the restraint beam hulls for the clamped support and for the loadings allows you to stay within the framework of the hypothesis of Euler-Bernouilli (cf. R3.03.06). v3.05.102 SSLX102 - bended bending hose v3.05.102 SSLX102 - bended bending hose Summary: This test validates the Modelling of the ovalization phenomena in the pipes: an elbow, extended by straight pipes, is subjected to an bending moment. This causes in the elbow an ovalization that spreads and simmers in the straight parts, and which alters the rigidity of the entire pipe. To verify the accuracy of the results, the flexibility of the entire pipe (value of displacement at the end for a moment imposed) and elements hulls DKT is tested. The test case has six modellings: - For Modelling A, the elbow is mesh in shell (modelling DKT), the pipe Modelling is used for straight parts, the restraint is provided by an COQUE_TUYAU connection. - For modellings B and C, TUYAU Modelling is assigned to the entire piping: TUYAU_3M for B and TUYAU_6M for C ( M = Fourier modes). - In Modelling D, the piping is mesh in shell (elements COQUE_3D), the ends are gridded in beams to apply the loads. - Modelling E: TUYAU Modelling (3 modes of Fourier) is assigned to the entire piping. - For Modelling F, the elbow is meshed in mesh cells density, the straight parts in elements TUYAU and the restraint is provided by a 3D_TUYAU connection. Modelling A validates the correct transfer of the ovalization (mode 2) between elements TUYAU, and validates the COQUE_TUYAU connection, both modellings B and C validate the elements TUYAU (with 3 and 6 modes of Fourier) in linear elasticity, and the latest model validates the correct transmission of the ovalization (mode 2) between elements TUYAU, and validates the 3D_TUYAU connection. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Coved pipework in the \mathrm{XY} plane . The straight parts are L=1200\mathrm{mm} length . The displacement due to thermal expansion in the axis of the element is: The stress displacement in the axis of the element is: - For beams: U_p =\frac{F L}{E S} - For the discreet: U_d =\frac{F}{K_x} The stiffness of the discreet is chosen so that the movements of beams and discrete ones are identical: K_x = \frac{E S}{L} . When loading is both temperature and effort: - The total displacement is: U_{total} = U_{th} + U_{d} = U_{th} + U_{p} . - The internal effort is: F_{normal} = F . - The supportive reactions are: - For elements following AB : F_x = F - For elements following AC : \left[ F_x, F_y, F_z \right] = -F \left[ \cos(\beta) cos(\alpha), \cos(\beta) sin(\alpha), \sin(\beta) \right] 2.2 Uncertainties about solutions None 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The modelling consists of: - POUTA : a SEG2 between nodes A and B assigned to an POU_D_E model. - POUTB : a SEG2 between nodes A and C assigned to an POU_D_E model. - DISCA : a SEG2 between nodes A and B assigned to an DIS_TR model. - DISCB : a SEG2 between nodes A and C assigned to an DIS_TR model. characteristics It is a functional test case and computer non-regression of the thermal-imposed ex post error indicator calculation (see R4.10.03). It exhumes a spatial error mapping on which will be supported, in a Python loop, the HOMARD refinement/derefining tool encapsulated in MACR_ADAP_MAIL (see U7.03.01). The calculation of this error indicator card is performed, via the ERTH_ELEM option of the post-processing CALC_ERREUR operator, on an EVOL_THER (provided to keyword RESULTAT) from an earlier thermal calculation (linear or non-linear, transient or stationary, isotropic or orthotropic, via THER_LINEAIRE or THER_NON_LINE, cf. necessary environment, parameterization and usage area R4.10.03 §6.2/4). This calculation requires the prior use of the CALC_CHAMP ‘FLUX_ELNO' option which determines the values of the heat flow vector at nodes (see example of R4.10.03 §6.5). The indicator is made up of fifteen components by element and for a given moment. In this test case the fifteen components are calculated but the refinement/derefining procedure is based only on the ERTABS component which represents absolute total spatial error (see R4.10.03 §6.3). In order to be able to post-process via POST_RELEVE or GIBI, we need to extrapolate fields by element to nodes fields by element. The addition of the option ‘ERTH_ELNO_ELEM' (after the call to ‘ERTH_ELEM_TEMP') allows this purely computer-based transformation to be performed. For a moment and a given finite element, it only duplicates the fifteen components of the indicator on each node of the element. This Modelling is therefore an example of the use in a PYTHON loop of possible "indicator calculation"/"mesh refining/derefining" couplings, as well as of test case non-regression options ‘ERTH_ELEM_TEMP' and ‘ERTH_ELNO_ELEM' and their adhesion to the re-mailing process. v4.04.007 TPLV07 - Cube orthotrope v4.04.007 TPLV07 - Cube orthotrope Summary: This test is based on independent validation of version 3 in linear steady-state thermal analysis. It validates the elements thermal volume under conditions of imposed flux, convection but also linear variation of the outside temperature. The results are compared with an analytical solution (VPCS). In this test, we also check the integral calculation on the edge of a thermal domain and the calculation of the thermal energy with orthotropic material on 3D elements. For this latter point two calculations are made in addition to that with orthotropic material: - a calculation with isotropic material (keyword THER of DEFI_MATERIAU ) as reference - a calculation with isotropic material but using keyword THER_ORTH from DEFI_MATERIAU validated by the first calculation. v4.04.106 TPLV106 - Stationary nonlinear thermal in mobile marker v4.04.106 TPLV106 - Stationary nonlinear thermal in mobile marker Summary: This elementary test allows a three-dimensional example to be treated as a problem with a variable of space in nonlinear stationary thermal as a moving marker (convection-diffusion problem). It also allows to check the account of a solid/liquid phase change by Code_Aster . The reference solution is analytical and the differences with the results of Code_Aster are less than 1%. The problem is modelled in the plane case. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Either a bar moving at V speed to the right of temperature conditions imposed in X=0 and X=L expressed in a fixed reference (relative to the moving bar). 1.2 Material properties - the thermal conductivity is constant: K=150W/m°C - the enthalpy function is such that: \beta (T)=\lbrace \begin{array}{cc}{C}_{S}T& ;T\le {T}_{1}\\ {C}_{S}T+{C}_{\mathrm{Sl}}(T-{T}_{1})& ;{T}_{1}\le T\le {T}_{2}\\ {C}_{S}T+{C}_{\mathrm{Sl}}({T}_{2}-{T}_{1})+{C}_{l}(T-{T}_{2})& ;{T}_{1}\le T\le {T}_{2}\end{array} with the following values: \begin{array}{}{C}_{S}={C}_{l}=1/3.{10}^{7}J/{m}^{3}°C\\ {C}_{\mathrm{Sl}}=8.333{10}^{7}J/{m}^{3}°C\\ {T}_{1}=585.°C\\ {T}_{2}=615°C\end{array} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Temperatures imposed on the ends {T}_{0}=200°C for x=0 {T}_{L}=1000°C for x=L=\mathrm{1m} Solid moving speed: V={10}^{-4}m/s 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference result is of the semi-analytic type. The 1D equation to be solved is as follows: \lbrace \begin{array}{}V\beta {(T)}_{,x}-K{T}_{,xx}=0\\ \text{avec}{T}_{(x=0)}={T}_{0}\text{et}{T}_{(x=L)}={T}_{L}\end{array} éq 2.1-1 By integrating the equation [eq 2.1-1-o]: \frac{V}{K}\beta (T)-\frac{\mathrm{dT}}{\mathrm{dx}}=A éq 2.1-2 where A is a boundary conditions-dependent constant, \frac{V}{K} -speed, and \beta (T) -enthalpy function. This constant will be determined analytically. The equation [eq 2.1-2] leads to: x={\int}_{{T}_{0}}^{T(x)}\frac{\mathrm{dT}}{A+\frac{V}{K}\beta (T)} éq 2.1-3 who must verify: L={\int}_{{T}_{0}}^{{T}_{L}}\frac{\mathrm{dT}}{A+\frac{V}{K}\beta (T)} éq 2.1-4 Knowing {T}_{0,}{T}_{L},L,V,t and \beta (T) , the equation [eq 2.1-4] shall give the value of the A integration constant . However, it is difficult (or even impossible) to determine this constant analytically, hence the use of a numerical resolution of the equation [eq 2.1-4] to determine A . With the ({T}_{0,}{T}_{L},{T}_{1,}{T}_{2,}{C}_{S}={C}_{l},{C}_{\mathrm{Sl}}...) problem data, we got the (physical) solution of A that takes the A=-294.9117 value. From this constant, the analytical solution of the problem [eq 2.1-1-o] is analytical. 2.2 Baseline | Abscisse | Temperature | | --- | --- | | 0.6 | 387.98514 | | 0.7 | 451.51001 | | 0.725 | 469.72232 | | 0.750 | 488.97505 | | 0.775 | 509.32766 | | 0.80 | 530.84296 | | 0.825 | 553.58738 | | 0.85 | 577.63114 | | 0.9 | 683.71269 | | 0.9125 | 719.51615 | | 0.925 | 756.32221 | | 0.9375 | 794.16795 | | 0.95 | 833.07971 | | 0.9625 | 873.08751 | | 0.9750 | 914.22222 | | 0.9875 | 956.51557 | 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics 2D modelling 3.2 Mesh characteristics 80 QUAD8 3.3 Test values | Identification Temperature | Reference | | --- | --- | | \mathrm{N80}(X=0.9875) | 956.515 | | \mathrm{N79}(X=0.9750) | 914.222 | | \mathrm{N78}(X=0.9625) | 873.087 | | \mathrm{N77}(X=0.9500) | 833.079 | | \mathrm{N76}(X=0.9375) | 794.167 | | \mathrm{N75}(X=0.9250) | 756.322 | | \mathrm{N74}(X=0.9125) | 719.516 | | \mathrm{N73}(X=0.9000) | 683.712 | | \mathrm{N69}(X=0.8500) | 577.631 | | \mathrm{N67}(X=0.8250) | 553.587 | | \mathrm{N65}(X=0.8000) | 530.842 | | \mathrm{N63}(X=0.7750) | 509.327 | | \mathrm{N61}(X=0.7500) | 488.975 | | \mathrm{N59}(X=0.7250) | 469.722 | | \mathrm{N57}(X=0.7000) | 451.510 | | \mathrm{N44}(X=0.6000) | 387.985 | 4 Summary of the results The results are very satisfactory with differences at reference solution below 1%.

Since the interface is adiabatic, two thermally insulated solids are on both sides of the interface. Each solid sees a temperature imposed on a part of its edge, and a zero flow on the rest of its edge. The problem being linear and stationary, the temperature is constant in each part of the bar (and equal to the corresponding imposed temperature), and discontinus through the interface: en 3D: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}T(x,y,z)=\text{}\stackrel{̄}{T}{\rbrace ^{\inf}=10°C,\text{}\forall \text{}(x,y,z)\text{}\in \text{}\left[\frac{-\mathit{Lx}}{2},\frac{\mathit{Lx}}{2}\right]\times \left[\frac{-\mathit{Ly}}{2},\frac{\mathit{Ly}}{2}\right]\times \left[\frac{-\mathit{Lz}}{2},0\right[\\ T(x,y,z)=\text{}\stackrel{̄}{T}{\rbrace ^{\sup}=20°C,\text{}\forall \text{}(x,y,z)\text{}\in \text{}\left[\frac{-\mathit{Lx}}{2},\frac{\mathit{Lx}}{2}\right]\times \left[\frac{-\mathit{Ly}}{2},\frac{\mathit{Ly}}{2}\right]\times \left]0,\frac{\mathit{Lz}}{2}\right]\end{array} en 2D: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}T(x,y)=\text{}\stackrel{̄}{T}{\rbrace ^{\inf}=10°C,\text{}\forall \text{}(x,y)\text{}\in \text{}\left[\frac{-\mathit{Lx}}{2},\frac{\mathit{Lx}}{2}\right]\times \left[\frac{-\mathit{Ly}}{2},0\right[\\ T(x,y)=\text{}\stackrel{̄}{T}{\rbrace ^{\sup}=20°C,\text{}\forall \text{}(x,y)\text{}\in \text{}\left[\frac{-\mathit{Lx}}{2},\frac{\mathit{Lx}}{2}\right]\times \left]0,\frac{\mathit{Ly}}{2}\right]\end{array} In the modellings presented in the following paragraphs, the temperature field approximation is enriched by a Heaviside function to represent the introduced discontinuity. nodes with support through the interface carry "classical" and "Heaviside" degrees of freedoms: then, they cannot be compared directly with the analytical values obtained above. In order to test the values of these degrees of freedom, one can set up in case the mesh of the bar is made up of 5 regular \mathrm{1m} side hexahedrons, so the central mesh cell is cut in its middle by the interface. The solution being constant in the x and y directions, one can simply consider the equivalent one-dimensional element represented in Figure . v4.19.203 TTLA203 - Cylinder with temperature imposed with adiabatic crack v4.19.203 TTLA203 - Cylinder with temperature imposed with adiabatic crack Summary The objective of this test is to validate elements axisymmetric X-FEM thermal thermal transient. A full cylinder, cracked at the section at mid-height, is considered. The crack is a crown of radius inside the half radius of the cylinder, and the radius of the cylinder is external. The load is transient and consists of a temperature gradient imposed by the application of Dirichlet conditions to the two ends of the cylinder. It is assumed that an adiabatic crack (zero flow on the lips of the crack and discontinuous temperature through the crack) Four modellings are considered: - A Modelling: \text{FEM AXIS} (mesh crack) - B Modelling: \text{X-FEM AXIS} , crack in the middle of elements - C Modelling: \text{FEM 3D} (mesh crack) - D Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{3D} , crack in the middle of elements 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure, shown in Figure , is a R=1m radius and H=2m height cylinder with a flat crack on the section at mid height.(included in the y=H/2 equation plane ). The crack is opening, and has as geometric support the inner R/2 radius crown and external R radius crown (red filled in Figure ). The disk included in the y=0 equation plane is called "lower disc", and the disk included in the y=H equation plane is called "upper disc". Figure 1.1-1: Géométrie du problème Finally, {P}^{+}(\theta ) is noted with point coordinates (located on the upper lip), and {P}^{-}(\theta ) with \left(R\cos\theta ,{H}^{-}/2,R\sin\theta \right) coordinates (located on the lower lip) 1.2 Material properties Thermal conductivity: \lambda =1{\mathit{W.m}}^{\text{-1}}.{K}^{\text{-1}} Volumetric heating capacity: \rho {C}_{p}=2\mathit{J.m}-{\mathrm{3.K}}^{-1} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The problem is solved on the time interval \left[0.s,1.s\right] discretized in 5 time step equal (of duration \Delta t=0.2s ). v4.22.002 TTNL02 - Thermal transition with phase change v4.22.002 TTNL02 - Thermal transition with phase change Summary: This elementary test allows to treat a unidirectional problem in nonlinear transient thermal analysis and to verify the consideration of a liquid/solid phase change by Code_Aster by introducing via the volume enthalpy the latent fusion heat. The solution is analytical and involves the error functions \mathrm{erf} and \mathrm{erfc} . The problem is treated in both plane and volume cases. v4.22.003 TTNL03 - Thermo-hydration. Simulation of an adiabatic trial v4.22.003 TTNL03 - Thermo-hydration. Simulation of an adiabatic trial Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the thermo-hydratant behaviour THER_HYDR, simulating an adiabatic test: A sample of fresh concrete is immersed in a calorimeter, the intake being operated with heat release, it is to recover the field of temperature and hydration over time. The temperature and degree of hydration are uniform in the sample. The temperature measured in the calorimeter will therefore be reference solution, the hydration being determined by analytical integration of the law of evolution. 2 modellings are proposed: three-dimensional and axisymmetric. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 1.2 Material properties The material has the following thermal characteristics: Heat conductivity: {k}_{s}=6\mathrm{kJ}/h/m/°K variation of enthalpivolumic: \Delta H=2.4105\mathrm{kJ}/{m}^{3} , and the following characteristics relating to moisturizing behaviour: Heat per degree of hydration: {Q}_{0}=1.4904105\mathrm{kJ}/{m}^{3} Constant of Arrhenius: \mathrm{Ar}=4000/°K . Note: The constant d-Arrhenius is always expressed in Kelvin degree. Temperatures are expressed in °C .
