Figure 1.3-a: a ac_s2_c_1 ccelerogram imposed on the structure 2 reference solution The tests performed are only of non-regression type. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Longitudinal mesh of the beam: It is composed of 17 nodes and 16 pairs d-elements POU_D_EM (16 elements for concrete and 16 for steel). Cross section of the beam: Concrete is modelled by an mesh composed of 2\times 20 quadrilateral (40 fibres). The steel is modelled by 4 point fibers. The coefficients \alpha and \beta for depreciation shall be calculated using the following formula: \left[\begin{array}{c}\alpha \\ \beta \end{array}\right]=2\frac{{\omega}_{1}{\omega}_{2}}{{\omega}_{2}^{2}-{\omega}_{1}^{2}}\left[\begin{array}{cc}\frac{-1}{{\omega}_{2}}& \frac{1}{{\omega}_{1}}\\ {\omega}_{2}& -{\omega}_{1}\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}{\xi}_{1}\\ {\xi}_{2}\end{array}\right] where {\omega}_{1} and {\omega}_{2} are the first two clean pulses (\omega =2\pi f) and {\xi}_{1} and {\xi}_{2} are the desired dampings on the first two modes. With {f}_{1}=39.9\mathrm{Hz} and {f}_{2}=157.6\mathrm{Hz} (calculated with Code_Aster ), for \text{5\%} modal depreciation, we find: \alpha ={8.10}^{-5} and \beta =20 . The time step chosen is 0,01s . v5.02.133 SDNL133 – Rotor rotating cracked, subjected to bending effort v5.02.133 SDNL133 – Rotor rotating cracked, subjected to bending effort Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the Modelling of a 1D crack in a rotor. This feature is available via ROTOR_FISS option of the DYNA_VIBRA operator. The test case involves a slow rotating beam subjected to a constant bending moment. The solution is compared with a 3D calculation made with STAT_NON_LINE for the extreme closed crack and open crack positions. 1 Reference problem The objective of this test case is to validate the 1D Modelling of a cracked rotor (ROTOR_FISS option of DYNA_VIBRA) which simulates the behaviour of a crack in a shaft line by an equivalent law. The law is established by 3D calculations made in quasi-static (see model D). The results obtained by the beam model and the crack element are compared with the 3D calculation for the extreme positions: closed crack and fully cracked at the maximum. 1.1 Geometry For the cracked rotor, a simple cylindrical straight beam of \mathrm{2L}=4m length and D=0,8m diameter is considered. The crack is in the middle of the beam and has a straight bottom. The crack depth is 65%. Figure 1: Géométrie du rotor fissuré 1.2 Material properties The rotor has a density of \rho =7800\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} . The Young's modulus is E=210{10}^{9}N{m}^{-2} and the Poisson's ratio is \nu =0,3 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads For modellings A, B and C, the beam is clamped on the left and is subjected to bending moment of unit amplitude on Y on its right end. The crack is considered to be running relatively slowly at 5 revolutions per second ( 300\text{rpm} ). For Modelling D, the boundary conditions imposed are, on the one hand, an clamped support in the sense of the beam theory of one of the ends of the cylinder by means of a 3D-POU connection, and on the other hand, a unilateral contact without friction between the lips of the cracks. The imposed load is a bending moment unit of ({M}_{x},{M}_{y}) components applied at the free end. The orientation of this moment evolves according to the moment of calculation. 1.4 Initial conditions In the initial state, t=0 , the crack is closed. It is gradually opened by a linear ramp spread over 0.2s leading to the moment on Y from 0 to 1\mathrm{Nm} . 2 reference solution The reference solution is a 3D calculation performed with STA_NON_LINE. The post-processing deformed neutral fiber is recovered. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The rotor is modeled by elements Euler beam (POU_D_E). The crack is modelled by ROTOR_FISS functionality of DYNA_VIBRA. The constitutive law crack is input by a function, itself determined on a bar of unit diameter, independent of rotor geometry (see Modelling D). DYNA_VIBRA calculates the transient on a modal basis. v5.02.138 SDNL138 - Frequency and clean vibration modes of a self-contraning frame v5.02.138 SDNL138 - Frequency and clean vibration modes of a self-contraning frame Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the calculation of the frequencies and vibration modes of a self-contraning frame. The forces in the structure are generated only by the tensioning of the cables. The principle of the test case is: - perform a nonlinear calculation, - recover the different fields at a given moment, - calculate the stiffness and mass matrices, - calculate the vibration frequencies and modes. Several modellings are made: - calculation with STAT_NON_LINE, use of CALC_MATR_ELEM, ASSE_MATRICE and COMB_MATR_ASSE operators for the assembly of matrices. Then calculation of the frequencies and vibration modes with CALC_MODES operator. - calculation with DYNA_NON_LINE and MODE_VIBR option. - STAT_NON_LINE calculation, stiffness matrix determination using CALCUL operator. Then calculation of the vibration frequencies and modes with CALC_MODES operator. The results are compared to a theoretical solution. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A frame consisting of 2 bars and 4 cables is considered. 1.2 Material properties The materials are elastic, their properties are: - For bars: E=2.1E+11 \alpha =0.0 \rho =7800.0 - For cables: E=2.1E+11 \alpha =1.0E-05 \rho =7800.0 1.3 Mechanical characteristics The only features required are the sections of the different elements. - for bars: A=1.0E-04 - for cables: A=5.026E-05 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads On the move: - node \mathit{N3} , all moves are blocked : \mathit{DX}=\mathit{DY}=\mathit{DZ}=0.0 - node \mathit{N4} , blocked moves following Y and Z : \mathit{DY}=\mathit{DZ}=0.0 - nodes \mathit{N1} , \mathit{N2} : blocked moves following Z : \mathit{DZ}=0.0 The load is applied by the tensioning of the cables. A fictitious temperature of -200°C, is imposed on the elements cables in 20 steps of loading. 1.5 Initial conditions Not applicable. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference solution chosen is the one obtained by solving the vibrating string equation: The equation of vibrating strings is: \frac{{\partial}^{2}y}{\partial {t}^{2}}=\frac{{F}_{0}}{\rho S}\frac{{\partial}^{2}y}{\partial {x}^{2}} with: {F}_{0} : tension in the rope, \rho : density, S : section of the rope. For a L length rope, fixed to these 2 ends, the nth proper vibration frequency is: f=\frac{n}{2L}\sqrt{\frac{{F}_{0}}{\rho S}} 2.2 Quantities and reference results The quantities tested are the clean vibration frequencies of the cables for 2 calculation moments, which correspond to 2 different voltages. | Not | Cable Tension | Frequency | | --- | --- | --- | | 10 | 6171.050459855N | 62.73227096292042\mathit{Hz} | | 20 | 12345.2954376N | 88.72830898253936\mathit{Hz} | 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution The vibrating string equation solution is obtained under the following assumptions: - the movements of the rope around its equilibrium position remain small. - \alpha angle variations remain small. - The variation in tension of the moving rope remains small. Under these assumptions, the reference solution is unsure. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Modelling with elements BARRE and CABLE. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains: - 2 elements type BARRE. - 60 elements CABLE type. The calculation of the frequencies and vibration modes is done with the CALC_MODES operator. 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics Modelling with elements BARRE and CABLE. 4.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains: - 2 elements type BARRE. - 60 elements CABLE type. (15 elements per cable). 4.3 Tested quantities and results The first eigenfrequency of vibration of the cables is tested. L is only one frequency that is displayed in the message file and stored in the FREQ parameter of the data structure produced by the operator. Therefore, this is a test of non-regression. 5 Modelling C 5.1 Modelling characteristics Modelling with elements BARRE and CABLE. 5.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains: - 2 elements type BARRE. - 60 elements CABLE type. (15 elements per cable). 5.3 Tested quantities and results The first frequency of the cables vibration is tested at the last step of the calculation, PAS=20. As the 4 cables have the same voltage, so there are multiple vibration modes. Six multiple modes are tested. It is a test of non-regression. | Frequency | Reference type | Calculated value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 88.5312 | default | | 2 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 88.8603 | default | | 3 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 88.9670 | default | | 4 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 89.0146 | default | | 5 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 89.0146 | default | | 6 | 'NON_REGRESSION' | 89.0146 | default | Note: For memory the reference frequency is 88.728308982\mathit{Hz} . 5.4 Remarks The first calculation is done with the STAT_NON_LINE operator. The CALCUL operator, which has the input fields of displacement, constraint, internal variables and an increment of displacements, allows you to know the stiffness matrix of the system. The calculation of the frequencies and vibration modes is done with the CALC_MODES operator using the stiffness matrix which comes from the CALCUL operator. The CALCUL operator assumes that the fields are linear as a function of the increment of the movements. However, in the case of cables this hypothesis is not quite right. This displacement increment should allow to approximate the matrix the tangent, so it must be small. It is determined by a sensitivity study. That is why this Modelling is a test of non-regression. 6 Summary of the results The results of modellings A, B and C are in good match with the reference solution. The results of Modelling C (only for educational purposes) require a sensitivity study to find the displacement increment that allows to approximate the tangent matrix and to stow the reference solution. This is due to the linearity hypothesis of the CALCUL operator.

v5.02.140 SDNL140 – Shrinking vibration of two contact-frost beams v5.02.140 SDNL140 – Shrinking vibration of two contact-frost beams Summary: This test modeled the nonlinear vibration response of two contact-frotting beams, subjected to the effect of a concentrated force at one of the ends of the beam. v5.02.141 SDNL141 – Oscillating submerged beam subject to wave field v5.02.141 SDNL141 – Oscillating submerged beam subject to wave field Summary: This test modeled the response of a submerged oscillating beam subjected to Morison's hydraulic forces (trail and inertial forces) in a fluid at rest or in the presence of a regular wave field. The reference solution comes from a comparison with the EDF-R&DCALHYPSO code. The proposed modellings are as follows: - Modelling A: In this Modelling, the calculation of drag forces for an oscillating beam in a resting fluid is tested. - Modelling B: In this Modelling, the calculation of drag forces and the weight added for an oscillating beam in a resting fluid is tested. - Modelling C: In this Modelling, the calculation of drag and inertia forces for an oscillating beam in a regular wave field is tested. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry and boundary conditions The figure below shows the Reference problem: a hollow cylindrical beam of length L=1m , external radius R=0.5m and thickness \mathit{ep}=0.01m . This one is immersed at 2.1m under the free surface in a column of water of height h=30m . The ends of the beam ss- press on two identical springs, themselves clamped at their ends. {S}_{w}=\pi {R}^{2} is noted the hydraulic cross section (seen by the fluid) transversal to the beam and S=\pi (2.R.\mathit{ep}-{\mathit{ep}}^{2}) the actual cross section. 1.2 Material properties The material has an isotropic elastic behavior: | Young's modulus | 200\mathit{GPa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio | 0,3 | | Density of beam \rho | 7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | | Volumetric mass {\rho}_{w} | 1000\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | | Rigidity of springs following z | 50.0N/m | | Trail coefficient {C}_{d} | 1.0 | | {C}_{a} added mass coefficient | 0.9 | 1.3 Swell Cinematic A single-directional, single-directional, single-directional swell is considered to be in the direction of +y, of order 1 (d-Airy) height, H-period, T-period, and \lambda wavelength, see diagram below. The free surface \eta depending on y space and t time is expressed: \eta (y,t)=\frac{H}{2}\cos(ky-\omega t) with k=\frac{2\pi }{\lambda} the number of wave and \omega =\frac{2\pi }{T} the pulse. The speed of the fluid {V}_{w}=(u,v,w) is as follows: \begin{array}{c}u(y,z,t)=0\\ v(y,z,t)=\frac{H}{2}\omega \frac{\sinh(k(h+z))}{\sinh(\mathit{kh})}\sin(k.y-\omega t)\\ w(y,z,t)=\frac{H}{2}\omega \frac{\sinh(k(h+z))}{\sinh(kh)}\sin(k.y-\omega t)\end{array} L-acceleration of the fluid is noted {a}_{w}=\frac{\partial {v}_{w}}{\partial t} . 1.4 Loading The initial equilibrium position of the problem is, starting from the reference position described in Geometry , to apply a translational displacement of the 1m beam in the +z direction. This imposed displacement is then released leading the beam to adopt a dynamic oscillatory motion. Note that Archimedes' weight and thrust are not taken into account in this problem. Model A The oscillating beam is subjected to Morison's (trailer term only) efforts in a resting fluid. {F}_{\text{mor}}=\frac{1}{2}{C}_{d}{\rho}_{w}{S}_{w}({v}_{w}^{\text{ortho}}-{v}_{s}^{\text{ortho}})({v}_{w}^{\text{ortho}}-{v}_{s}^{\text{ortho}}) where {v}_{w} and {v}_{s} respectively refer to the fluid speed (nil here) and solid speed (inlet parameter of mechanical loading FORCE_POUTRE). The symbol \text{ortho} represents the projection in the normal direction at the neutral fibre of beam 1 It is noted that these are linear forces which are applied in a distributed way on the beam. Model B The oscillating beam is subjected to the forces of Morison (trailer term and inertia terms) in a resting fluid {F}_{\text{mor}}=\frac{1}{2}{C}_{d}{\rho}_{w}{S}_{w}({v}_{w}^{\text{ortho}}-{v}_{s}^{\text{ortho}})({v}_{w}^{\text{ortho}}-{v}_{s}^{\text{ortho}})+{\rho}_{w}{S}_{w}{a}_{w}^{\text{ortho}}+{C}_{a}{\rho}_{w}{S}_{w}({a}_{w}^{\text{ortho}}-{a}_{s}^{\text{ortho}}) The first term (corresponding to drag) is identical to model A, the second and third correspond to the terms of inertia. The acceleration of the fluid being zero, the latter reduce to the term of solid added mass {-C}_{a}{\rho}_{w}{S}_{w}{a}_{s}^{\text{ortho}} . This is taken into account in the system mass matrix by changing the density of the beam: {\rho}^{\text{ }}=\rho +{C}_{a}{\rho}_{w}\frac{{S}_{w}}{S} Note: Note that this change in density must be accompanied by a suitable change in gravity to properly reflect the weight of the beam. However, it is recalled that this force is not taken into account in our problem. Model C The oscillating beam is subjected to the forces of Morison (see model B) in a fluid subjected to a wave of height H=3m and period T=12s . The fluid speed and acceleration are defined in Swell Cinematic. The term solid added mass is taken into account in the mass matrix in the same way as for model B by changing the density of the beam. General note: Morison's forces depend on the position of the beam, they must be mentioned as follow-up loads in the calculations. This projection also requires switching to the input parameter of FORCE_POUTRE l-beam orientation. 2 reference solution The reference solution is based on the results of the CALHYPSO (internal EDF R&D) calculation code dedicated to wave-structure interactions. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics et mesh - Beam: POU_D_E Modelling (one mesh cell SEG2) - Springs: DIS_TR Modelling (two mesh cells SEG2) - Relationship of linear elastic behavior. 3.2 Tested quantities and results The non-regression of the node NO2 of the beam is tested. v5.03.106 SDNV106 – Analysis with DYNA_NON_LINE own values (stability and vibration modes) v5.03.106 SDNV106 – Analysis with DYNA_NON_LINE own values (stability and vibration modes) Summary: This test case allows to validate the flaming analysis, as well as vibrational modal analysis in DYNA_NON_LINE. Only one model is used: \mathrm{3D} massive A Modelling composed of mesh cells HEXA8. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A 2m length side cube with uniform tensile strength in the vertical direction Z is considered: | | | --- | For symmetry reasons, only one eighth of the structure will be considered, which will be meshed by a single cubic linear element volume. 1.2 Material properties The structure is assumed to be homogeneous, composed of an isotropic elastoplastic material, with linear isotropic hardening: - E={2.10}^{4}\mathrm{MPa} - \nu =0.49999 - \rho =7900\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} - {\sigma}_{y}=0,1\mathrm{Mpa} (SY elastic threshold) - {E}_{T}=200\mathrm{Mpa} (module tangential plastic D_SIGM_EPSI) So we choose a material that is still almost incompressible, whether we are in elastic or plastic regimes. In addition, we impose a 100 ratio between the elastic stiffness and the plastic tangent stiffness. 1.3 boundary conditions A uniform tensile load is imposed following Z on the top of the cube. This force, initially zero, increases linearly over time. The other boundary conditions are Dirichlet type and reflect the symmetry conditions of the problem (following the 3 orthogonal planes (\mathrm{xOy}) , (\mathrm{xOz}) and (\mathrm{yOz}) ). These boundary conditions are sufficient to block all rigid body movements in the system. 1.4 Initial conditions The first calculation being quasistatic, we just impose a zero initial displacement. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation We want to check two types of quantities: - the first critical blazing charge, - the first proper frequency of the vibration system. The reference value of the critical load sought is obtained by a quasistatic calculation (CRIT_STAB key word of STAT_NON_LINE). This value is taken from the last step of quasistatic calculation, which corresponds to the instant t=1s . The number stored under CHAR_CRIT in the result data structure (this is the minimum multiplier coefficient of the load imposed to obtain the blazing load) being proportional to the imposed load which is monotonous increasing linearly over time, it is corrected to have the true value at the first moment of the transient dynamic calculation, i.e. 1,001s . The multiplier coefficient CHAR_CRIT is defined as: {F}_{\mathrm{critique}}=\text{CHAR\_CRIT}({t}_{i}).{F}_{\mathrm{ext}}({t}_{i}) The external force is proportional to the time: {F}_{\mathrm{ext}}({t}_{i})={F}_{\mathrm{ext}}.{t}_{i} , so {F}_{\mathrm{critique}}=\text{CHAR\_CRIT}({t}_{i}).{F}_{\mathrm{ext}}.{t}_{i} . It is assumed that on one step the load is moving very slowly and therefore the result of the dynamic calculation can be assimilated to a quasistatic evolution during this step. For the first dynamic step, which follows the quasistatic calculation, we can write: \begin{array}{c}{F}_{\mathit{critique}}={\text{CHAR\_CRIT}}_{\text{STAT\_NON\_LINE}}({t}_{i}).{F}_{\mathit{ext}}.{t}_{i}\approx {F}_{\mathit{critique}}={\text{CHAR\_CRIT}}_{\text{DYNA\_NON\_LINE}}({t}_{i}).{F}_{\mathit{ext}}.{t}_{i}\\ \mathrm{\Rightarrow }\\ {\text{CHAR\_CRIT}}_{\text{DYNA\_NON\_LINE}}({t}_{i+1})\approx {\text{CHAR\_CRIT}}_{\text{STAT\_NON\_LINE}}({t}_{i}).\frac{{t}_{i}}{{t}_{i+1}}={\text{CHAR\_CRIT}}_{\text{STAT\_NON\_LINE}}({t}_{i}).\frac{1}{1,001}\end{array} For the vibration analysis, we will do two tests: - using the stiffness elastic matrix, - using stiffness matrix tangent plastic. Both reference values are obtained by two linear modal calculations conducted with the CALC_MODES operator. To obtain the first proper frequency corresponding to the elastic case, a linear elastic calculation is made with CALC_MODES and the original material defined above (of Young's modulus valant {2.10}^{4}\mathrm{Mpa} ). To obtain the first eigenfrequency corresponding to the tangential plastic case, a linear elastic calculation is made with CALC_MODES and a fictitious elastic material whose Young's modulus is worth the plastic tangent module defined above: 200\mathrm{Mpa} , 100 times less than the actual elastic module. So we will have a eigenfrequency 10 times lower than the previous one. We also know the analytical solution of our problem (length 1 cup consisting of a single linear finite element) which is reduced to a 1D case of compression traction: \omega =\sqrt{2E/\rho }\approx \lbrace \begin{array}{}0,358128\mathrm{rad}/s:\text{matériau élastique}\\ 0,0358128\mathrm{rad}/s:\text{matériau plastique}\end{array} 2.2 Quantities and reference results | quantities | Values | Unit | | --- | --- | --- | | Multiplier coefficient of the first critical flaming load | -2.85714E+01 / 1.001 | | | First frequency own elastic | 3.58128E-01 | \mathrm{Hz} | | First frequency own plastic | 3.58128E-02 | \mathrm{Hz} | 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics Number of mesh cells: 1 HEXA8 Number of nodes: 8 3.2 Tested quantities and results | Identification | Reference | Aster | % difference | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Frequency of own vibratory plastic | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.01 | 3.58128E-02 | 3.5812661359567D-02 | -3.87E-04 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.06 | 3.58128E-02 | 3.5812661359997D-02 | -3.87E-04 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.25 | 3.58128E-02 | 3.5812661358541D-02 | -3.87E-04 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.49 | 3.58128E-02 | 3.5812661355801D-02 | -3.87E-04 | | Elastic vibration frequency of its own | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.51 | 3.58128E-01 | 3.5812779545194D-01 | -5.71E-05 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.52 | 3.58128E-01 | 3.5812779545194D-01 | -5.71E-05 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.56 | 3.58128E-01 | 3.5812779545194D-01 | -5.71E-05 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.75 | 3.58128E-01 | 3.5812779545194D-01 | -5.71E-05 | | | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.99 | 3.58128E-01 | 3.5812779545194D-01 | -5.71E-05 | | The first critical load coefficient | \mathrm{Tps} = 1.001 | -2.854285714E+01 | -2.85701899729E+01 | 0.096 | These tests are completed by two tests on the DEPL_VIBR vibratory mode calculated with MODE_VIBR. v5.05.101 SDNX101 - MISS3D‐Code_Aster Chain Verification for ISS Dynamic Foundation Detachment v5.05.101 SDNX101 - MISS3D‐Code_Aster Chain Verification for ISS Dynamic Foundation Detachment Summary: This non-regression test uses a Code_Aster mode of use to treat the nonlinear foundation detachment problem of a building with consideration of a soil-structure interaction (ISS) in dynamic analysis. L的ISS is then modelled by a recalated floor spring mat from the soil impedance determined by the Code_Aster chaining with the MISS3D software. The standard case of a seismically excitation-treated building with a flexible foundation representation is presented as an application case, resulting in the total consideration of the radier deformation modes associated with RIGI_MISS_3D-type characteristics. The maximum displacements obtained at the foundation edge by dynamic calculation with DYNA_NON_LINE are a first reference result. In a second model, the same problem is addressed by using a dynamic building condensation method, which is then represented by a dynamic substructure macro‐element. The soil is represented directly by a soil impedance determined by the Code_Aster chaining with MISS3D software and also considered as a dynamic macro‐element. The dynamic problem resolution with DYNA_NON_LINE ss-oper on a mixed model consisting of macro‐elements and a physical model reduced to nonlinear contact springs. However, this method is more accurate and cost-effective than the previous one provides fairly close values for the maximum displacements obtained at the foundation edge. In a third model, the same condensation method is used as in the second model, but the dynamic problem is solved in a linear calculation loop with transient dynamic operators where the nodal forces complement is recalculated over the entire time range, due to the nonlinearity of the delamination, which is even more economical than the previous one and provides satisfactory values for the maximum displacements obtained at the foundation edge. In a fourth model, the same condensation method is always used, but only for the soil macro-element, keeping the physical model of the structure. The modes for the soil-structure interface are reduced modes to represent the flexibility of the foundation by a LIAISON_INTERF relationship. Only the proper modes of the structure-ground system are tested. A fifth model uses a physical model of building and point ground springs of RIGI_PARASOL characteristics where the dynamic problem is solved in a linear calculation loop with transient dynamic operators where the nodal forces complement is recalculated over the entire time range, due to the nonlinearity of the delamination. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The software Code_Aster -MISS3D uses the frequent coupling method to account for the soil-structure interaction. This method, based on dynamic substructure, consists of cutting the field of study into three sub-domains: - soil, - the foundation, - the building. Figure 1.3-a: Accelerogram acc1.c2 2 The flexible foundation method Representing the flexible foundation hypothesis is tantamount to considering the limit condition for calculating the foundation modes. The following method is used for modelling test case A. 2.1 Description of the method The flexible foundation condition is obtained by representing the static foundation modes by forced modes associated with all degrees of freedom foundation translation. Therefore, for the calculation of the own blocked mode, all degrees of freedom translation ( \mathrm{DX}=\mathrm{DY}=\mathrm{DZ}=0 ) of the node group \mathrm{BRADIER} [Figure 3.1-a] of the foundation in the AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01 command will be blocked. For the calculation of the static foundation modes, the forced modes associated with each of the degrees of freedom blocked in these nodes will be obtained. The number of static modes to be calculated then amounts to the number of nodes on the foundation multiplied by 3, the number of degrees of freedom translation associated. Then, once the impedances dependent on the frequency by FICHIER option of the CALC_MISS command are calculated, we can then affect the aggregate reclagged characteristics of the foundation using AFFE_CARA_ELEM U4.42.01 option RIGI_MISS_3D. 2.2 Summary of impedance calculation The calculation of soil impedances requires the following steps to sequence the commands of Code_Aster : - Calculation of eigenmodes on blocked basis with block limit conditions compatible with foundation hypothesis by CALC_MODES U4.52.02 command, - Definition of the dynamic interface, producing the type (CRAIGB (pre-set) or MCNEAL) and the mesh of the ground-structure interface, by the DEFI_INTERF_DYNA U4.64.01 command, - Definition of a complete modal base by the DEFI_BASE_MODALE U4.64.02 command which calculates the static modes of the previously defined dynamic interface and completes the eigenmode base with the complete modal base of the CLASSIQUE type, - Assembling the dynamic macro‐element by the MACR_ELEM_DYNA U4.65.01 command, from the previously defined modal base. The data to be transferred from Code_Aster to MISS3D is obtained by using a specific command: - IMPR_MACR_ELEM U7.04.33 allows the mesh of the soil-structure interface to be produced and the static and dynamic modes reduced to this interface. The terms of the dynamic macro-element are used to determine the structure's contribution to impedance. - Then we get the ground impedance calculation by launching MISS3D by CALC_MISS U7.03.12 option FICHIER. In this command data, in addition to the file produced by IMPR_MACR_ELEM, it is necessary to provide a calculation parameter file as well as a file of soil data as described in the [bib3] document. 3 Modelling of the delamination with ground springs Simultaneous modelling of the delamination and the ISS by discrete elements requires combining the use of linear springs representing the ground with nonlinear springs working only in compression to represent contact by penalization. An example of Modelling adapted to the Modelling of a seismically-sustained building is described below. 3.1 Matching between ground springs and contact springs In the case of a building subjected to seismic excitation whose soil-structure interaction (ISS) is to be studied, the foundation base must be geometrically represented by superfacial mesh cells, grouped here in \mathrm{SRADIER} , which may not be modelled in the soft foundation hypothesis when they rely on density elements. In the case of linear behavior, nodes \mathrm{SRADIER} can be directly affected by stiffness characteristics calculated by AFFE_CARA_ELEM, RIGI_MISS_3D, for the soft foundation hypothesis. However, to represent the detachment, these soil characteristics must only be active when the ground is compressed and they must be cancelled in the event of traction. A classic means is to intercalate, between each point of the \mathrm{SRADIER} foundation and a point spring affected by soil characteristics in this point, a nonlinear spring in series meshed by a segment supporting a rigid foundation DIS_TR Modelling or DIS_T in the case of a soft foundation. This group of discrete segments is called here \mathrm{LIGRAD} . The characteristics of these contact springs are very high in compression ( {10}^{15} in this test) and zero in tensile. They are indicated with a material DIS_CONTACT behavior and then affected with the constitutive law DIS_CHOC in the last ground compression process (which is formed by the tensile X-type and therefore the last-typed by the ground-type X-typed by the ground-typed by the ground-typed by the ground- To calculate the characteristics of the punctual ground springs grouped here in \mathrm{BRADIER} , the nodes of this group must belong to the superfacial mesh cells of the same geometry as \mathrm{SRADIER} . Or, \mathrm{SRADIER} no longer contains nodes of \mathrm{BRADIER} because the segments of \mathrm{LIGRAD} are intercalated. Therefore, in the mesh a superfacial mesh-cell group called here \mathrm{SRADIE2} is created by translating \mathrm{SRADIER} with a very small distance value equal to the size of the segments of \mathrm{LIGRAD} ( 2.E-2 in this test). This distance value is then used as a game in the material characteristics of DIS_CONTACT so that the ground and foundation are joined at the initial time. mesh-cell group superfacial \mathrm{SRADIE2} does not need to be modelled by finished elements. All modellings ground and contact springs are schematized as follows [Figure3.1-a]: Figure 3.1-a: Soil interface model – connecting contact springs and ground springs 3.2 Calculation of the modes on floor spring mats The calculation of the modes on floor springs mats is desirable. It is even necessary if modal damping is to be taken into account later in the dynamic calculation. In advance, it is necessary to calculate the soil characteristics with the option of AFFE_CARA_ELEM, RIGI_MISS_3D, for the soft foundation hypothesis. These new characteristics will be assigned instead of the previous ones and associated with the limit condition of blocking both for the calculation of modes on floor mats but also in the calculation operators d-evolution. For RIGI_MISS_3D, the mesh-cell group \mathrm{BRADIER} point is entered on GROUP_MA_POI1. Simply enter the logical unit number of the soil impedance matrix calculated by MISS3D that has already been given in CALC_MISS option MISS_IMPE. 3.3 Dynamic calculation of the de-lamination Before calculating the dynamic evolution of the de-lamination, it is necessary to calculate the static de-lamination due to the gravity. The following modelling steps are therefore taken: - Definition of the vertical gravity load and horizontal gravity unit loads for seismic loading, - Definition of the dynamic calculation moment list, - Calculation of the static position under gravity by STAT_NON_LINE U4.51.03 command: the discrete segments \mathrm{LIGRAD} are affected by the DIS_CHOC behavioral relationship. The rest of the structure has linear behavior in our case but the interest of this Modelling is also to be able to affect other behavioral relationships, - Calculation of dynamic evolution, with recovery as the initial state of the previous static result, under the effect of the gravity always and also seismic loads by the DYNA_NON_LINE U4.53.01 control. Discrete segments \mathrm{LIGRAD} are also affected by the DIS_CHOC behavioral relationship. It is at this level that modal damping can be introduced associated with each of the previously calculated ground spring mat modes. 4 Dynamic condensation decollation modelling A second active alternative model for modellings B and C test case is to treat the same problem using a dynamic building condensation method, which is then represented by a dynamic substructure macro-element. The building is condensed by its interface modes with the foundation and nonlinear contact springs. The soil is represented directly by the previous soil impedance also considered as a dynamic macro-element instead of the assignment of ground springs by AFFE_CARA_ELEM, and option RIGI_MISS_3D or RIGI_PARASOL. Figure 5.1-a: mesh of the building foundation 6.1.2 Mesh of the building The building consists of a circular drum topped by a dome and can be modeled by 756 elements DKT 1,4 m shell thickness. Figure 5.1-b: Semi-mesh of the vertical-cut building 6.2 Mesh characteristics The model is composed of 1057 nodes (5784 degrees of freedom), 1797 elements (998 elements plates and 799 elements discreet). 6.3 Calculation parameters The dynamic calculation is conducted over a 0.4 seconds interval by time step of 0.01 seconds with a modal damping calculated by CALC_AMOR_MODAL, different for each mode with a frequency of less than 20\mathrm{Hz} and including a 5% material damping contribution for the building structure and a representative contribution of the radiative damping of the soil extracted from the imaginary part of the soil impedance. 6.4 Modelling results A Non-regression tests are performed on the displacement values (vertical and horizontal) of the nodes top and centre of the radier, at the beginning of the transient and at the end. 7 Modelling B 7.1 Modelling characteristics This Modelling implements the dynamic condensation method of structure and soil. The mixed model is used consisting of their macro‐elements and a physical model reduced to nonlinear contact springs. The Modelling ss is based on the same elements and the same mesh as the previous model unlike the \mathit{BRADIER} soil springs replaced by the macro‐element directly consisting of the soil impedance calculated by MISS3D. This Modelling also allows testing the two modes of transient loading condensation in a macro-element from the VECT_ASSE_GENE and RESU_GENE operands in the CAS_CHARGE factor keyword CAS_CHARGE of MACR_ELEM_DYNA. 7.2 Mesh characteristics The model is composed of 1057 nodes (5784 degrees of freedom), 1184 elements (998 elements plates and 186 elements discreet). 7.3 Calculation parameters The dynamic calculation is conducted over a 3 seconds interval by time step of 0.01 seconds with a 5 % damping for each of the structural modes with a frequency of less than 20\mathrm{Hz} combined with a damping matrix extracted from the ground macro-element and representative of radiative damping, which is equivalent to the modal damping of the previous model. 7.4 Modelling results B A test of non-regression is performed on the vertical displacement value at the top node at the beginning of the transient. 8 Modelling C 8.1 Modelling characteristics This Modelling uses exactly the same mixed model consisting of macro-elements and a physical model reduced to nonlinear contact springs as in the second model. The difference lies only in the resolution method in a linear calculation loop with the transient calculation operators where the nodal force complement due to the nonlinearity of the delamination is recalculated each time using the CALC_FORC_NONL operator. 6 iterations of linear calculations are performed here. 8.2 Mesh characteristics The model is composed of 1057 nodes (5784 degrees of freedom), 1184 elements (998 elements plates and 186 elements discreet). 8.3 Calculation parameters The dynamic calculation is conducted over a 5 seconds interval by time step of 0.01 second with a 5 % damping for each of the structural modes with a frequency of less than 20\mathit{Hz} combined with a damping matrix extracted from the ground macro-element and representative of radiative damping, which is equivalent to the modal damping of the first model. 8.4 Modelling results C Non-regression tests are performed on the displacement values (vertical and horizontal) of the nodes top and centre of the radier, at the beginning of the transient and at the end. 9 Modelling D 9.1 Modelling characteristics This Modelling always uses a mixed model, but only consisting of the soil macro-element and a physical model comprising both the restraint linear springs of the modellings B and C and the building model of Modelling A. The difference also lies in the calculation of modes to represent a flexible restraint at the ground-structure interface. The restraint between soil impedance and the structure at this interface is represented by an restraint type LIAISON_INTERF. 9.2 Mesh characteristics The model is composed of 1057 nodes (5784 degrees of freedom), 1184 elements (998 elements plates and 186 elements discreet). 9.3 Modelling results D The first eigenfrequencies of the soil-structure system are tested very close to those obtained with the other modellings. 10 Modelling E 10.1 Modelling characteristics This Modelling uses the physical building model of model A and a model of point ground springs distributed by RIGI_PARASOL under the foundation of \mathit{RADIER} . As with model C, the resolution method is used in a linear calculation loop with the transient calculation operators where the nodal forces complement due to the nonlinearity of the delamination is recalculated each time using the CALC_FORC_NONL operator. 3 linear calculations iterations are performed here. 10.2 Mesh characteristics The model is composed of 1057 nodes (5784 degrees of freedom), 1184 elements (998 elements plates and 186 elements discreet). 10.3 Calculation parameters The dynamic calculation is conducted over a 5-second interval by time step of 0.01 second with a material damping of Rayleigh equivalent to 5% of modal damping for each of the structural modes with a frequency of less than 20\mathit{Hz} combined with amortization characteristics of ground springs distributed by RIGI_PARASOL and representative of radiative damping, which is equivalent to the modal damping of the first model. 10.4 Modelling results E Non-regression tests are performed on the displacement values (vertical and horizontal) of the nodes top and centre of the radier, at the beginning of the transient and at the end. 11 Summary of the results The ISS representation method by a carpet of soil springs used in model A provides non-regression results in terms of maximum displacements obtained at the foundation edge at the initial moment and during a de-lamination. An alternative method of representation of the ISS and dynamic condensation structure is used in model B. This method is more accurate (as it uses all the terms of soil impedance) and more economical (because of dynamic condensation) than the previous method, however, provides fairly close values for the maximum displacements obtained at the foundation edge. It is therefore the first priority to use in dynamic de-lamination studies. It is also used in model C where the dynamic problem resolution sseries in a linear calculation loop with the transient calculation operators where the nodal forces complement is recalculated over the entire time range, each time due to the nonlinearity of the delamination. This resolution method is even more cost-effective than the previous one and provides satisfactory values for the maximum displacements obtained on the foundation edge.

v5.05.102 SDNX102 - Verification of Miss3D-code_aster Chaining for a rigid foundation beam v5.05.102 SDNX102 - Verification of Miss3D-code_aster Chaining for a rigid foundation beam Summary: This non-regression test implements the different options of Miss3D-code_aster chaining to deal with the linear problem of a beam placed on a rigid foundation with consideration of a soil-structure interaction (ISS) in dynamic analysis. L的ISS is then modelled through the frequency coupling from the CALC_MISS macro-command. Different modellings are presented: - In modelization A CALC_MISS is used to use Miss3D and estimate the dynamic rigidity matrix of the interface - In modelization B frequent coupling is tested via a single-support load using EXCIT_GENE option CALC_MISS - In the modelization C frequency coupling is tested via a single-support load using EXCIT_MONO option CALC_MISS - In modelization D frequency coupling is tested by loading equivalent seismic forces using CALC_MISS EXCIT_FORC option 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry taken into account is that of a beam with a concentrated head mass placed on a square rigid foundation on the H=1m side. The characteristics of the beam are as follows: - One length L=12m - A square section on the B=0.4m side 1.2 Material properties This paragraph presents the material characteristics of the soil and structure. 1.2.1 Soil properties A homogeneous soil is considered with the following characteristics: - Un Young's modulus de E=200MPa - Un Poisson's ratio de \nu=0.33 - A density density of \rho=1610kg/m^3 1.2.2 The properties of the beam A beam with the following characteristics shall be considered: - Un Young's modulus de E=30GPa - Un Poisson's ratio de \nu=0.2 - A concentrated mass in the head of m=2000kg The beam is modelled as a discrete element by providing the following stiffnesses: - Horizontal Rigidity K_h=12EI/L^3 - Vertical Rigidity K_h=EA/L where I=B^4/12 is the inertia of the beam and A=B^2 is the surface of the section. 1.3 Boundary conditions and dynamic loadings The foundation is placed on a macro-element of soil defined using CALC_MISS through the material properties of the soil. The imposed load is a Ricker wavelet with the following shape: a(t)=(1-2\pi f(t-t_0)^2)e^{-(\pi f(t-t_0))^2} where t_0=1.24s is the time of phase of the wavelet and f=2Hz is the main frequency. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling the dynamic rigidity of the interface will be calculated using CALC_MISS. 2.2 Modelling results A The value of static horizontal and vertical rigidity (i.e. zero frequency) will be compared with analytical values. 3 Modelling B 3.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling a single-support load is imposed through EXCIT_GENE option CALC_MISS. 3.2 Modelling results C A non-regression test is performed on the X , Y and Z spectra at the top of the beam at the f_1=2.37Hz frequency. 4 Modelling C 4.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling a single-support load is imposed through EXCIT_MONO option CALC_MISS. 4.2 Modelling results B A non-regression test is performed on the X , Y and Z spectra at the top of the beam at the f_1=2.37Hz frequency. In addition, the results of Modelling are compared with the B. 5 Modelling D 5.1 Modelling characteristics In this Modelling, an equivalent seismic load is imposed through CALC_MISS EXCIT_FORC option. 5.2 Modelling results D A non-regression test is performed on the X , Y and Z spectra at the top of the beam at the f_1=2.37Hz frequency. v5.06.107 SDNS107 – Transitional Response of a reinforced concrete slab: model with GRILLE_EXCENTRE v5.06.107 SDNS107 – Transitional Response of a reinforced concrete slab: model with GRILLE_EXCENTRE Summary: This test validates in linear transient dynamics the Modelling of square reinforced concrete plate using for concrete a model of plate DKT and for reinforcements elements of grid-membrane GRILLE_EXCENTRE. We check the frequencies of eigenmodes, temporal responses on the move, reactions, and kinetic energy, for a sinusoidal loading. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry used in this test case is a reinforced concrete plate of e=0.1\text{m} thickness and l=1\text{m} length. Figure 1.1-a : Geometry studied The characteristics of the steel sheets of the reinforced concrete plate are: - Upper tablecloth: section per linear metre =0.05{m}^{\mathrm{²}}/\mathrm{ml} ; de-centrement compared to average sheet: +0.03m , - Lower tablecloth: section per linear meter =0.05{m}^{\mathrm{²}}/\mathrm{ml} ; excentered from average sheet: –0.03m . 1.2 Material properties The material characteristics for multilayer concrete modelling with steel reinforcements (DKT and GRILLE_EXCENTRE) are summarized in the following table. | Modelling | Young's modulus N/{m}^{\mathrm{²}} | Poisson's ratio | Density \mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Concrete (plate DKT) | 1010 | 0.0 | 2500 | | Steel (GRILLE_EXCENTRE) | 1011 | 0.0 | 7800 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads On the A ( \mathrm{B0X} ) side of the plate the {u}_{x}={u}_{y}={u}_{z}=0 moves are embedded, as well as {\theta}_{x}={\theta}_{y}={\theta}_{z}=0 rotations. During the modal calculation, the {u}_{y}=0 displacement is blocked everywhere on the plate. A linear force is applied to the \mathrm{B1X} side (opposed to \mathrm{B0X} ) in the (0.0,0.0,1,0) direction and depends on {F}_{0}={10}^{6}N value. In the case of dynamic calculation, a sinusoidal linear force is applied to the \mathrm{B1X} side in the (0.0,0.0,1.0) direction. The frequency of the sinusoidal is 20\mathrm{Hz} . The duration of the stress is 0,1s . 1.4 Initial conditions In the initial state, the movements and speeds are zero everywhere. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation It is possible to calculate the frequencies of the first and second modes of bending vibration of the plate as it functions as a beam-console. The {f}_{1} frequency of the first eigenmode is written: {f}_{1}=\frac{3,5156}{2\pi {L}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{EI}}{\rho}} with L the length of the console (1 m here), \mathrm{EI} l e produces bending inertia by the Young's modulus for the complete structure and \rho the mass of the structure per unit of length. Similarly, the {f}_{2} frequency of the second mode ssss: {f}_{2}=\frac{22,0336}{2\pi {L}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{EI}}{\rho}} To calculate {f}_{1} and {f}_{2} , the concrete and reinforcing parts are broken down: (\mathrm{EI})={(\mathrm{EI})}_{\mathrm{beton}}+{(\mathrm{EI})}_{\mathrm{acier}} où {(\mathrm{EI})}_{\mathrm{acier}}=2{E}_{\mathrm{acier}}({\mathrm{sL}}_{2}){e}_{\mathrm{exc}}^{2} with {E}_{\mathrm{acier}} the Young's modulus of steel, s the section of the frames per linear meter and {e}_{\mathrm{exc}} the excentre of the rebar sheets in relation to the average sheet, and: {(\mathrm{EI})}_{\mathrm{beton}}={E}_{\mathrm{beton}}{L}_{2}\frac{{e}^{3}}{12} where {E}_{\mathrm{beton}} is the Young's modulus of the concrete. For mass per unit length, the concrete mass and the steel mass shall be broken down. Using the previous equations, it becomes possible to calculate the frequency of the modes considered. The results are: | Frequency | Reference | | --- | --- | | First bending mode | 54,67\mathrm{Hz} | | Second bending mode | 342,64\mathrm{Hz} | The centre of gravity is located at the centre of the console, so its coordinates are: (0.5,0.05,0) . L-inertia according to the y axis of the complete structure is: {I}_{yy}(G)={\int}_{V}({(x-{x}_{G})}^{2}+{(z-{z}_{G})}^{2})\rho \mathrm{dv} ({x}_{G},{y}_{G},{z}_{G}) the coordinates of the centre of gravity, V the volume of the structure and \rho its density. It is considered reasonable and the results are considered satisfactory. Although this test was designed to approach Code_Aster Modelling as closely as possible to that of Europlexus code, one is aware, among other things, of the difference in the calculation of the mass matrix. The mass matrix implemented in Europlexus follows the method proposed in [1], which is better suited for an explicit fast dynamic calculation software. Code_Aster uses a more standard approach, explained in [2]. The difference concerns, in particular, the calculation of inertias (components of the mass matrix corresponding to the degrees of freedom rotation), which are not important in the case of slow dynamics. However, in fast dynamics, they are the most influential influence of the critical time step. For example, neglecting them the mass matrix becomes singular and explicit integration becomes unconditionally unstable. The various simulations proposed validate the use of GRILLE_EXCENTRE Modelling for modal calculations, explicit dynamics and implicit dynamics. The values obtained are consistent with analytical solutions, when available.

v5.06.110 PLEXU06 – Validation of the Code_Aster chaining - Europlexus v5.06.110 PLEXU06 – Validation of the Code_Aster chaining - Europlexus Summary: This test is intended to validate the chaining of a nonlinear transient calculation where the first part of the resolution is conducted by Europlexus via the CALC_EUROPLEXUS command, then continues in Code_Aster with the use of the DYNA_NON_LINE operator, with an explicit rebalancing step to implicit MACRO_BASCULE_SCHEMA command. More specifically, the model implemented includes the following specific features: - elements finished beam type ( POU_D_E ), - elements Q4GG finished on triangular or quadrangular mesh cells, - floor springs carpets to model the soil under the foundation, - load of pressure type imposed variable in time, - linear zone, - nonlinear zone with constitutive law GLRC_DAMAGE . 1 Description 1.1 General description The structure is of the square reinforced concrete portico type of 10m side and 2m top with the 4 poles connected to their base to a radier of the same size and resting on a carpet of ground springs. The radier and roof are represented in elements Q4GG hulls. Only the toe can be nonlinear (constitutive law GLRC_DAMAGE) and it is subjected to variable pressure in time. The objective of this type of study is to process the fast dynamic part of the response in Europlexus, then switch to Code_Aster (implicitly) for the induced shake phase, which is too long in time to allow a resolution in a reasonable time by remaining explicitly in Europlexus. In post-processing, the displacement, acceleration and oscillator response spectrum (SRO) will be analyzed at the point \mathit{PP2} that is in the middle of the upper slab. 1.2 Material properties The slabs are made of reinforced concrete and steel poles. | Material | Concrete | Steel | | --- | --- | --- | | Young's modulus | {E}_{b}=42824,5\mathit{MPa} | {E}_{a}={2.10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | | Poisson's ratio | {\nu}_{b}=0 | {\nu}_{a}=0.3 | | Density | {m}_{b}=2500\mathit{Kg}/{m}^{3} | {m}_{a}=7800\mathit{Kg}/{m}^{3} | | D_SIGM_EPSI | 0 | 0 | | SYT | 4,2{.10}^{5}\mathit{MPa} | Not applicable | | SYC | -{35.10}^{5}\mathit{MPa} | Not applicable | | SY | Not applicable | {5.10}^{7}\mathit{MPa} | The linear part of the slabs is affected by the linear characteristics of the concrete defined above. The additional part is characterized by a behaviour of type GLRC_DAMAGE ., whose concrete phase and steel reinforcements also have the above characteristics. The specific parameters of the GLRC_DAMAGE law are specified with the DEFI_GLRC operator. | BETON | NAPPE | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | EPAIS | 1,3 | OMX | 5,027{.10}^{-3} | | GAMMA | 0 | OMY | 5,027{.10}^{-3} | | QP1 | 0,152 | RX | 0,877 | | QP2 | 0,152 | RY | 0,877 | | OMT | {5.10}^{-3} | | | | EAT | {2.10}^{11} | | | | C1N1=C1N2=C1N3 =C2N1=C2N2=C2N3 | 87,3{.10}^{6} | | | | C 1M1 =C1M2=C1M3 =C2 M 1=C2M2=C2M3 | 14,8{.10}^{6} | | | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading The pressure on the top slab follows this in time: The radier is based on a floor spring mat (K_TR_D_N type) defined with keyword RIGI_PARASOL from AFFE_CARA_ELEM . The six components of the global stiffness input are: \begin{array}{c}\mathit{Kx}=0,13572{.10}^{12}\mathit{Pa}\\ \mathit{Ky}=0,13428{.10}^{12}\mathit{Pa}\\ \mathit{Kz}=0,13467{.10}^{12}\mathit{Pa}\\ \mathit{Krx}=0,24722{.10}^{15}\mathit{Pa}\\ \mathit{Kry}=0,22386{.10}^{15}\mathit{Pa}\\ \mathit{Krz}=0,30600{.10}^{15}\mathit{Pa}\end{array} 1.4 Time limitations CPU For reasons purely related to a short CPU time for this test case, the total duration that will be simulated numerically during the transient resolution will be deliberately shortened. This will also induce a moment of tilting between the codes that will be located too "at a time": the initial fast dynamic response regime will not have turned into an overall shake mode. The test case will therefore have the disadvantage of tipping from schema to time at an unfavourable moment when non-linearities will still be in the propagation phase, which should not be the case for a real industrial study where the phase of shake-up treated as implicit should remain linear. Logically, the switch should therefore occur after the return to 0 of the pressure imposed (failure to be in the throttle speed) , so after 0,0171s . The CFL condition imposing an explicit time step of the order of 5\mu s , the number of time step would be prohibitive for an test case . To reduce the time CPU, you place the switch much earlier, to 0,007s , so when the pressure imposed is on its maximum tray . In implicit the time step will be 50\mu s . 1.5 Europlexus to Code_Aster transition strategy In this chapter we will discuss two problems: - rereading and building fields to move from Europlexus resolution (via CALC_EUROPLEXUS) to DYNA_NON_LINE: this step will be validated by comparing calculations explicitly (it remains schematic in similar time between codes), - the switch from an explicit schema to an implicit schema. 1.5.1 Construction of fields for prosecution The model has a linear zone and a nonlinear zone. On the linear zone, the fields that we will recover at the last moment calculated with Europlexus are kinematic fields, so only fields to nodes. The constraints will be recalculated in Code_Aster . On the nonlinear zone, two fields at additional Gauss points should be read again for the constraint and internal variables related to the material law used: GLRC_DAMAGE . The nonlinear zone only contains elements type Q4GG on triangular or quadrangular mesh cells. All fields generated by Europlexus will be re-read from an MED file. For the continuation with DYNA_NON_LINE (or MACRO_BASCULE_SCHEMA) the following fields are defined as initial state: displacement, speed, acceleration, stress (over the entire model) and internal variables. 1.5.2 Diagram switch The transient resolution, following Europlexus, is continued in Code_Aster starting with the explicit pattern of centered differences, with molten mass matrix, in order to remain in the same assumptions as the Europlexus calculation. Then the transition to an implicit resolution is made with a specific phase of rebalancing within the MACRO_BASCULE_SCHEMA operator. The transient resolution ends in implicit with a consistent mass matrix and for a time step ten times larger than explicit. 2 reference solution The results obtained with a diagram shift will be compared with the results obtained when one diagram is kept in time. In order to quantify the differences between the codes, we will therefore build two reference solutions: the first calculated with Europlexus, the second with Code_Aster explicitly. 2.1 Baseline The point \mathit{PP2} is compared to the SRO (with a 5% damping factor) reference solutions in terms of displacement, acceleration and SRO (with a 5% damping factor) in the middle of the top slab. The SRO also compares the results obtained using the OBSERVATION tables, particularly the CALC_EUROPLEXUS generated with the ARCHIVAGE data. 2.2 Uncertainty about the solution Differences due to the schema shift will be compared to differences between the two reference solutions (one obtained with Europlexus, the other with Code_Aster ). Ideally, the switch should not amplify these differences between the reference solutions, which cannot be reduced. 3 Modelling A The concrete slabs are modeled in elements Q4GG, on quadrangular or triangular mesh cells. The poles are modeled in elements type POU_D_E. The ground springs are, on the other hand, of the K_TR_D_N type. 3.1 Analysis of results In this chapter, we will trace the vertical evolutions of the displacement and acceleration of the point \mathit{PP2} (in the middle of the top slab). Each time, we will superimpose the different responses obtained: 1. resolution with CALC_EUROPLEXUS then continuation with DYNA_NON_LINE explicitly, 2. resolution with CALC_EUROPLEXUS over the entire study interval, 3. resolution with DYNA_NON_LINE explicit over the entire study interval, 4. switch CALC_EUROPLEXUS to DYNA_NON_LINE implicit, 5. DYNA_NON_LINE is explicitly switched to implicit. This will allow the quantification of: - accuracy when rereading MED data between codes and good model concordance (curve 1), - the model differences between Europlexus and Code_Aster (curves 2 and 3) with identical timing, - differences between explicit solution and solution with diagram shift (curves 4 and 5). Acceleration analysis is expected to amplify the differences, compared to the differences in calculated displacement. For the following graphs, the simulated time duration was deliberately increased to provide a more relevant analysis. In the test case command file, this simulation time is much shorter to reduce the time CPU. 3.1.1 Comparison of calculated displacements The response is oscillating and the differences are weak. There is only a very slight phase shift between explicit and implicit responses, which is due to time patterns. the difference amplitude is negligible. To complete the analysis we will zoom in on the rocking moment at the moment 0.0075 s: The tipping generates a slight disturbance, but the responses remain the same, whether you switch from Europlexus to Code_Aster (black curve) or whether all resolution is in Code_Aster (brown curve). It is important to note that this difference due to the switch does not go by amplifying itself and that the answers remain very close to the reference solutions (without tipping). 3.1.2 Comparison of calculated accelerations Accelerations have much more chahutized appearances than displacements, but differences between numerical solutions remain moderate. More precisely, we can see the influence of the schema in implicit time that smoothes the response (dissipative pattern type HHT). By zooming in on the rocking moment, significant disturbances of acceleration occur. These numerical oscillations cannot be totally annihilated, even by playing on the parameters of the diagram-turning method (choose of the diagram during the balancing phase, parameter of this diagram, choice of the diagram before and after the rocking...). In fact, we have been able to verify that these oscillations are very largely caused by the change in mass matrix: in fact, in explicit use is made of a flambed mass matrix, whereas by implicit it is the consistent mass matrix that is chosen. When the rocking is made, one passes abruptly from one mass matrix to the other and this disturbs the solution. The rebalancing strategy does not completely succeed in eliminating this jump. A parade could be to gradually switch from one mass matrix to another, using on some time step a variable mass matrix that would be a linear combination of the two matrices (light and consistent). The interest of this algorithmic evolution will still be quantified on this test case, for example. 3.2 Test values We will test the values obtained (movements and accelerations) at the final moment: 0,007s . Each tested value will in fact be the absolute value of the relative difference between the result to be tested and the reference solution considered. This formula must tend to 0 and it is directly a relative value, which explains that in the TEST_FONCTION operator it is specified CRITERE='ABSOLU'car, otherwise it would be sought to render the value relative a second time. In practice, these tested values can only be set to 0 if the difference between the same calculation with Code_Aster or Europlexus is zero, which is not the case. More precisely, the differences for time-shift solutions can only be less than the differences between the two reference solutions (complete calculation with Europlexus and complete calculation with Code_Aster explicitly). So we start by measuring the relative differences between the two reference solutions. On the move, we have: 2,656188{.10}^{-3} and acceleration: 0,016270437 Then we will analyze the relative differences induced by the calculation resume between Europlexus and Code_Aster (explicit, so no rocking). On the move, we have: 4,93101{.10}^{-04} and acceleration: 0,0380 . Differences induced by the time shift should be of the same order as quantity. Indeed, the switch cannot correct these differences inherent in the differences between the codes. First, we compare the Europlexus to Code_Aster implicit. On the move, we have a relative difference from: 5,02195{.10}^{-04} and in acceleration: 0,019848325 . Finally, the relative differences is given with the solution obtained by explicit toggle to implicit, but always remaining in Code_Aster . On the move, we have a relative difference of : 0,011460178 and acceleration: 0,045500117 . It is noted that the acceleration differences is larger than the displacement differences, which is logical because the displacements are more regular than the accelerations, as can be verified on the graphs of the v5.06.110-comparison-deplacement-calculated and v5.06.110-comparison-acceleration-calculated. Then, it is found that on the movements, the rocking introduces very little disturbance, while on the accelerations, oscillations, albeit damped, appear. After analysis, it turns out that they are mainly due to the abrupt passage of a mass matrix fused to a consistent matrix. For the calculation of SRO, the difference relative maximum (over the entire frequency range and for an equivalent damping of 5%) will be calculated with reference solution, whether for SRO obtained from OBSERVATION and ARCHIVAGE. These relative differences are in the order of 5 to 8% and are attributable to the time step tilt and differences where the SRO input data are archived. 4 Executive summary This test case validates the continuation of calculations by switching from Europlexus to code_aster , on a reinforced concrete building model. Specifically, we begin by validating the field rereading to nodes or Gauss points to continue with an explicit calculation with DYNA_NON_LINE . Then we validate this pursuit by tilting to an implicit time schema. The observed differences are satisfactory and consistent with the differences in Modelling between the codes (mainly at the level of the mass matrix that can be consistent or fused). post-processings SRO is also valid for ARCHIVAGE or OBSERVATION data.

v6.01.103 SSNA103 - Calibration of Weibull Model Parameters v6.01.103 SSNA103 - Calibration of Weibull Model Parameters Summary: This test validates the RECA_WEIBULL command allowing the identification of m and {\sigma}_{u} parameters of the Weibull model. The identification is made using a database consisting of 45 tests, all of which are performed on smooth cylindrical test pieces at three different temperatures, -150°C , -100°C and –50°C . This database is obtained by random drawing of a sample representative of the statistical law of Weibull corresponding to values of m and {\sigma}_{u} arbitrarily fixed. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Each test is performed on a smooth cylindrical test piece. For obvious symmetry reasons, a 2D axisymmetric model of the quarter of the structure is sufficient. 1.2 Material properties The behaviour of the material studied by an elasto-plastic law of Von Linear isotropic hardening devices, ‘VMIS_ISOT_LINE The Poisson's ratio is not temperature dependent, \nu =0,3 . The values of Young's modulus E , {E}_{t} tangential module and yield limit are given in the following table: | Temperature [°C] | –150 | –100 | –50 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | E[\mathrm{MPa}] | 200000 | 200000 | 200000 | | \mathrm{Et}[\mathrm{MPa}] | 2000 | 2000 | 2000 | | {\sigma}_{Y}[\mathrm{MPa}] | 750 | 700 | 650 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads In relation to the figure of the v6.01.103-geometrie, the boundary conditions and loads are as follows: On the segment \mathrm{BC} ( Y={L}_{0} ), the displacement imposed in the direction \mathrm{OY} : | T[°C] | Movement ( l-{l}_{0} ) at break for reference length {l}_{0} of 203.5\mathrm{mm} [\mathrm{mm}] The results for each temperature are ranked in ascending order | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | -50 | 10,68 | 28,78 | 30,31 | 31,66 | 32,53 | 33,90 | 34,38 | 35,82 | 36,69 | 37,09 | 37,37 | 37,49 | 38,45 | 39,77 | 44,39 | | -100 | 20,57 | 21,68 | 23,32 | 24,37 | 24,66 | 25,59 | 25,84 | 27,51 | 28,44 | 29,30 | 29,68 | 30,16 | 30,18 | 30,20 | 30,95 | | -150 | 11,33 | 14,70 | 14,79 | 14,90 | 18,62 | 18,87 | 19,00 | 19,37 | 19,61 | 20,07 | 21,19 | 22,79 | 23,28 | 24,17 | 24,41 | On the segment \mathrm{OA} ( Y=0 ) blocked moves in the direction \mathrm{OY} . On the segment \mathrm{OB} ( X=0 ) blocked moves in the direction \mathrm{OX} . 1.4 Initial conditions No stress and deformation. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation No calculation is required to obtain the reference solution. The m and {\sigma}_{u} (M and SIGM_REFE in WEIBULL option of DEFI_MATERIAU) values that are being identified are known and allow the database to be generated. Thus, break elongations are determined as follows: For each m and {\sigma}_{u} torque associated with a d-test temperature, a sample of 15 stress values of Weibull at rupture was determined by random drawing, taking into account the following statistical law: {P}_{f}({\sigma}_{w})=1-\exp[-{(\frac{{\sigma}_{w}}{{\sigma}_{u}})}^{m}] The Weibull constraint is defined by: {\sigma}_{w}=\sqrt[m]{\sum_{i}{({\sigma}_{I}^{i})}^{m}\frac{{V}_{i}}{{V}_{0}}} The summation covers the volumes of plasticized {V}_{i} material, {\sigma}_{I}^{i} designating the maximum main stress in each of these volumes (the volume {V}_{0} (VOLU_REFE in WEIBULL option) is equal to (50\mu {m}^{3}) ). In the case of single tensile stress with the hypothesis of small deformations, the stress of Weibull, {\sigma}_{W} , is expressed as a function of (l-{l}_{0})/{l}_{0} break elongation, depending on: {\sigma}_{w}=[{E}_{t}(\frac{l-{l}_{0}}{{l}_{0}})+(1-\frac{{E}_{t}}{E}){\sigma}_{Y}]\sqrt[m]{\frac{V}{{V}_{0}}} The values of the break elongations carried forward in the table of the v6.01.103-conditions-limits-loads are therefore derived from this expression and from the previous random drawing. 2.2 Quantities and reference results The quantities reference m and {\sigma}_{u} used to create the experimental test bases are: | Temperature [°C] | –50 | –100 | –150 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | m | 24 | 24 | 24 | | {\sigma}_{u} [\mathrm{MPa}] | 2800 | 2700 | 2600 | 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution The uncertainty of the solution cannot be determined precisely, but it can be quite high. Indeed, the reference values can only be found if we consider experimental populations composed of an infinite number of samples. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes: 149 Number of mesh cells and types: 40 elements QUAD8 3.2 Tested quantities and results Identification of a m common to the three experimental bases and a {\sigma}_{u} per base. | Temperature [°C] | Reference | Values calculated | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | MAXI_VRAI | REGR_LINE | | | | | | | | m | {\sigma}_{u} [\mathrm{MPa}] | m | {\sigma}_{u} [\mathit{MPa}] | m | {\sigma}_{u} [\mathit{MPa}] | | –50 | 24 | 2800 | 26,7 | 2536 | 16,1 | 4983 | | –100 | 24 | 2700 | 26,7 | 2428 | 16,1 | 4642 | | –150 | 24 | 2600 | 26,7 | 2372 | 16,1 | 4555 | 3.3 Remarks Using the maximum likelihood method, although the difference between the values of ( m , {\sigma}_{u} ) obtained with RECA_WEIBULL and their reference values remains significant, it is consistent with the result sought given the relatively small number of samples used for the re-scaling (15 per temperature). To obtain the reference values, the number of samples per temperature ( N>1000 ) would have to be significantly increased. However, the difference found remains reasonable (about 10%). Furthermore, the growth of {\sigma}_{u} according to temperature is respected. With the linear regression method, the difference is more important. 4 Summary of the results The results obtained show that the automatic setting procedure for the parameters of the Weibull models works and gives results consistent with the expected theoretical results.

The Modelling of the test piece is carried out with elements 2D (QUA8). In particular, this test proposes the use of plastic corrections for the calculation of the stress of Weibull R7.02.04 The modellings studied are the following (unless otherwise stated, all calculations are in HPP): - Modelling A: - Weibull stress calculation without plastic correction, SIGM_ELGA and SIGM_ELMOY options with POST_ELEM / WEIBULL ET POST_BEREMIN. - calculation of Bordet stress with POST_BORDET and triaxiality rate with POST_ELEM / RICE_TRACEY - Modelling B: Idem than Modelling A, but the calculation is done in parallel - Modelling C: test of a plastic correction formulation for the calculation of the stress of Weibull, option SIGM_ELGA - Modelling D: test of the same plastic correction formulation for the calculation of the stress of Weibull, option SIGM_ELMOY - Modelling E: test of a second formulation of plastic correction for the calculation of the stress of Weibull, option SIGM_ELGA - Modelization F: calculation of the stress of Weibull with the large deformation kinetics SIMO_MIEHE and GDEF_LOG. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The model is to model a cylindrical, cut-out test piece. The interested reader will also be able to refer to it for a more in-depth study of this test case. 1 Reference problem Either a hollow cylinder of length L , internal radius {R}_{f} and external radius R . Or a rigid frame of circular section {R}_{f} clamped radius in its centre. {\Gamma}_{i} and {\Gamma}_{e} are noted the inner and outer surfaces of the hollow cylinder (see [Figure 1.1-a]). The load consists of applying a {U}^{i}{e}_{z} ( {U}^{i}>0 ) displacement on the rigid frame as well as zero displacement on the outer edge {\Gamma}_{e} . Figure 1.1-a: Schéma du domaine et chargement The axisymmetric solution is assumed to allow us to restrict our study to a rectangular 2D domain \Omega . The dimensions of the domain are as follows: . The load on the rigid frame will be taken into account by applying the displacement required all the way over \mathrm{2D} domain and zero side displacement to take into account the clamped support of the cylinder. Finally, a zero radial displacement is imposed on the lower and upper faces of the domain in order to avoid a singularity due to a change of boundary condition at the points and A' (see [Figure 1.1-a]). These boundary conditions will lead to an anti-plane solution (independent of ) which allows to obtain more simply an analytical solution. 2 reference solution The reference solution is an analytical solution from [bib3], itself inspired by a one-dimensional study proposed in [bib1] and more generally based on the energy approach of the break proposed by G. v6.01.119 SSNA119 – Damage to AXIS-cut test piece v6.01.119 SSNA119 – Damage to AXIS-cut test piece Summary: This test represents a calculation of damage to a cut-out test piece. It allows the validation of GRAD_VARI Modelling to axisymmetric, for AXIS_GRAD_VARI modelling, allowing for damage calculations to be performed regularized by the damage gradient, taking into account degrees of freedom displacement and damage to nodes. GRAD_VARI Modelling is based on a local resolution, with each Gauss point. The test validates two constitutive laws: ENDO_SCALAIRE and ENDO_FISS_EXP. The different modellings and constitutive laws damaging are tested: - Model B : GRAD_VARI Modelling with constitutive law ENDO_SCALAIRE - Model C : GRAD_VARI Modelling with constitutive law ENDO_FISS_EXP 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A 10\mathit{dm} high-cut plate is considered. 3\mathit{dm} wide and 1\mathit{dm} nick radius. Figure 1: Promotion of the problem 1.2 Common properties of the material The material is assimilated to concrete (decipemetric scale is used): Elastic characteristics: > E=3.E10\text{Pa}=3.E8{\text{N/dm}}^{2} > \nu =0.2 Tensile strength of the damage law: > \mathit{SY}=3.E4{\text{N/dm}}^{2}=3.E6\text{Pa} Energy restitution rate per crack surface (Griffith constant): > {G}_{f}=10\text{N/dm}=100{\text{J/m}}^{2} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Block : \mathrm{DX}=0 on an node group located in the middle of the axis ( x=0. ), to ensure the maintenance of the structure. Charge : Forced or controlled displacement (variety depending on model) in the traction direction. 2 reference solution This test case is a case of non-regression. This is a particularly unstable study, which quickly changes from a weakly damaged state to a state of rupture (damage equal to 1). A complete snap-back calculation is made with the elastic prediction steering technique for GRAD_VARI Modelling. 3 Modelling B 3.1 Modelling characteristics A model of damage GRAD_VARI, which is a mixed Lagrangian formulation of damage regulated by the gradient of damage, is considered. It takes into account in addition the degrees of freedom of displacement and damage to the nodes, the coeficients of Lagrange. This model accepts loading control by elastic prediction. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains 1034 elements TRIA6 and 462 elements QUAD8. The mesh at the centre of the test piece is oriented out of symmetry. 3.3 Damage law: material ENDO_SCALAIRE Standard concrete characteristics are defined above. Characteristics related to the non-local damage law: c=1.875\text{N};p=1.5;m=10 which corresponds to the damage area \mathrm{1D} equal to D=0.5\text{dm} The correspondence with physical parameters is as follows: c=3/8D{G}_{f};m=\frac{3E{G}_{f}}{2D\cdot {\mathit{SY}}^{2}};p=m/4-1; 3.4 Boundary conditions and loads Charge : The calculation is done by elastically predicting control until the test piece is completely broken, thanks to the projection on the predefined terminals. 3.5 Tested quantities and results Non-regression test on point \text{P\_HAUT} displacement, point \text{P\_HAUT} nodal force and point Gauss 1 mesh cell \mathit{M160} stress field. 4 Modelling C 4.1 Modelling characteristics A model of damage GRAD_VARI, which is a mixed Lagrangian formulation of damage regulated by the gradient of damage, is considered. It takes into account in addition the degrees of freedom of displacement and damage to the nodes, the coeficients of Lagrange. This model accepts loading control by elastic prediction. 4.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh contains 1034 elements TRIA6 and 462 elements QUAD8. The mesh at the centre of the test piece is oriented out of symmetry. 4.3 Damage law: material ENDO_FISS_EXP In addition to the concrete characteristics defined in §1.2, a compression limit of fc=30.E6 Pa, a shape parameter of the cohesive model p=1.5 and a half width of D=0.5 dm is introduced. 4.4 Boundary conditions and loads Charge : The calculation is done by elastically predicting control until the test piece is completely broken, thanks to the projection on the predefined terminals. 4.5 Tested quantities and results Non-regression test on point \text{P\_HAUT} displacement, point \text{P\_HAUT} nodal force and the overall stress field (absolute sum). 5 Summary of the results This test allows you to check in non-regression: - GRAD_VARI Modelling with constitutive law ENDO_SCALAIRE - GRAD_VARI Modelling with constitutive law ENDO_FISS_EXP

v6.01.121 SSNA121 - Concrete tube subjected to internal pressure with model BETON_UMLV v6.01.121 SSNA121 - Concrete tube subjected to internal pressure with model BETON_UMLV Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the correct treatment of tensile states to treat the creep of concrete, model BETON_UMLV, under these tensile stress states. The test consists of applying internal pressure to a concrete tube modelled in axisymmetric conditions. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry An infinite tube of \mathrm{20m} internal radius and \mathrm{21m} external radius is considered. The length of the tube is not involved in the evaluation of the reference solution, but this length is fixed to \mathrm{10m} for the physical modelling of the problem (illustration). Figure 1.1.1: Geometry of 1m thick concrete tube with internal radius 20m 1.2 Material properties The concrete material is elastic isotropic with properties of: - E=31000\mathrm{MPa} - 
u =0.2 The properties of clean-flow concrete (model ULMV_FP) are given below: - K_RS = 2.0e11\mathrm{Pa} , - ETA_RS = 4.0e16\mathrm{Pa.s} , - K_IS = 5.0e10\mathrm{Pa} , - ETA_IS = 1.0e17\mathrm{Pa.s} , - K_RD = 5.0e11\mathrm{Pa} , - ETA_RD = 1.0e16 , - ETA_ID = 1.0e17 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads On the \mathrm{AB} edge, vertical displacements are blocked along the Y axis. On the \mathrm{AD} edge, a containment pressure of \mathrm{1MPa} is imposed. On the \mathrm{BC} edge, a uniform restraint is imposed for all nodes in the X direction. On the \mathrm{CD} edge, a uniform restraint is imposed for all nodes in the Y direction. The boundary conditions type restraint uniform ensures that an infinite cylinder is modeled, not a finished cylinder. 1.4 Initial conditions None 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation 2.1.1 Elastic solution The analytical solution is established on an infinite cylinder in the direction Z , with an internal {R}_{int} radius , with an external {R}_{	ext{ext}} radius , subjected to internal pressure. A particular solution of this model of delayed deformations for constant loading and relative humidity is examined here. The focus is on the spherical part of deformations.
