v6.01.122 SSNA122 – Contact Validation Benchmark NAFEMS 2: punch (rounded edges) v6.01.122 SSNA122 – Contact Validation Benchmark NAFEMS 2: punch (rounded edges) Summary: This is the second test case in a NAFEMS benchmark for the validation of contact and frangling. Benchmark references are obtained with Abaqus and MARC codes. This test modeled a contact between a rounded edge punch (off) and a solid axisymmetric. This test case validates the axisymmetric contact and allows to observe the positive effect of a discharge on the singularity of the contact pressure in the vicinity of a sharp angle. This test includes 4 modellings for testing: - linear and quadratic elementss, - ‘CONTINUE' contact treatment formulations without and with friction. - contact treatment formulations ‘DISCRETE 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure is modeled in axisymmetric. M is the point of the foundation located in the upper face on the axis of revolution. 1.2 Material properties Foundation : Poisson's ratio: 0,3 Young's modulus: 70000{\mathit{N.mm}}^{-2} Poin : Poisson's ratio: 0,3 Young's modulus: 210000{\mathit{N.mm}}^{-2} The friction coefficient between the block and the cylinder is \mu =0,1 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Since the structure is axisymmetric and is subject to a load respecting the revolution symmetry, only one slice is represented. \mathit{DX}=0 is applied to the revolution axis. The foundation is clamped at its base: - \mathit{DX}=0 - \mathit{DY}=0 The punch shall be subjected to uniform pressure on its upper face: - P=100\mathit{Mpa} 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference solution is derived from results obtained with Abaqus and MARC codes in a NAFEMS benchmark for the [bib1] contact-frost validation. 2.2 Quantities and reference results Vertical displacement of point M (according to y ) (external reference). Contact pressure at point M (external reference). The raised contact pressure is that extrapolated from the stresses in the volume. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution Important (average code). 2.4 Bibliographic reference [1] A. KONTER. Advanced Finish Element Contact Benchmarks . NAFEMS, 2006. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The Modelling is AXIS, the contact formulation is CONTINUE, cases with and without friction are treated. 3.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes: 743 Number of mesh cells and types: 671 QUAD4. 3.3 Tested quantities and results First calculation (without friction) | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -0,13073410182805 | 0,18% | | \mathit{SIYY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -91,100555673515 | 0, 09% | Second calculation (with friction) | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -0,12858017574262 | 0,18% | | \mathit{SIYY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -88,665240835356 | 0, 05% | 3.4 Remarks Figure 1: Comparison of the tangential constraint between Abaqus, MARC and Code_Aster The results obtained by the continuous formulation in Code_Aster with as without friction are in very good agreement with those of the reference codes. It should be noted, however, that the contact pressure given by the degree of freedom LAGS_C for the point M (located on the revolution axis) is disturbed in continuous formulation. Indeed, the jacobian is zero for the points of the revolution axis. However, for linear elements, the default integration scheme (and recommended) is trapeze (so nodes). This test illustrates the value of the specific features of continuous formulation that allow for the initial contact (to block rigid body movements) and exclude nodes from friction only (to avoid incompatibilities between boundary conditions and contact-frost conditions). 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics The Modelling is AXIS, the contact formulation is CONTINUE, cases with and without friction are treated. 4.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes: 2155 Number of mesh cells and types: 671 QUAD8. 4.3 Tested quantities and results First calculation (without friction) | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -0,13294119101090 | 0, 2% | | \mathit{SIYY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -94,122096406847 | 0,1% | Second calculation (with friction) | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | \mathit{DY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -0,13079352874552 | 0,19% | | \mathit{SIYY} au point M | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | -95,473963617887 | 0, 08% | 4.4 Remarks The results on a quadratic mesh change very little compared to the A model (mesh linear) and are as close to the references. 5 Modelling C 5.1 Modelling characteristics Modelling is AXIS, the contact formulation is DISCRETE, only the case without friction is processed. v6.01.129 SSNA129 - Elastoplastic tubes subjected to internal/external pressures axisymmetric v6.01.129 SSNA129 - Elastoplastic tubes subjected to internal/external pressures axisymmetric Summary: This test case allows a comparison of finished elements plates and hulls (cinematics, integration methods in thickness) and pipes to model homogenous elastoplastic cylindrical tubes subjected to static axisymmetric pressure loading paths, producing a solution independent of the axial direction of the tube. Three tube geometries are processed: - \mathit{h}/\mathit{R} = \mathrm{0.05}= \mathrm{1/20} , - \mathit{h}/\mathit{R} = \mathrm{0.10}= \mathrm{1/10} , - \mathit{h}/\mathit{R} = \mathrm{0.20}= \mathrm{1/5} The axisymmetric pressure loading routes are: - internal/external asynchronous pressures alternated to complete discharge of the isotropic hardening elastoplastic tube, - Internal monotonous pressure increasing to the ruin limit, with radial steering of the elastoplastic tube without nutring. The reference solutions are obtained by elements solid finished axisymmetric Modelling on a very refined mesh in thickness: see Modelling A. These solutions are also confronted with partial analytical results. The elements finished plates and shells tested are: - Modelling B: DKT r3.07.03 plates, - Modelling C: COQUE_3D r3.07.04 density hulls. - Modelling D: solid COQUE_SOLIDE r3.07.10 hulls, - Modelling E: TUYAU_3M r3.08.06 pipes, with their ability to treat swelling (radial). The following are compared respectively: - radial displacement over time, - axial displacement over time, - circumferential and radial constraints in thickness at certain moments, - the plastic deformations accumulated in thickness at certain moments. 1 Reference problem The reference problem is the study presented in and . The material of the tube is supposed to be elastoplastic with isotropic hardening and Von Mises criterion, described by a tensile curve with plastic tray. A complicated pressure loading path is chosen, showing phases of the expansion or contraction of the tube (low pinch) and phases of the "rolling" type (strong pinching), such as entering the plastic domain. The residual state is also considered. Schedema of the tube under internal/external pressure - Route 1: Asynchronous internal/external pressures alternated to complete discharge of the isotropic-nutted elastoplastic tube. This route is inspired by the tube's dudgeoning in a tube plate. - path 2: Internal monotonous pressure increasing to the ruin limit, with radial steering of the isotropic hardening elastoplastic tube. The progression of the plastic flow area in the thickness is decisive to describe the fate of the ruin. The first plasticization appears, in any case, in the internal wall. This path is inspired by a test of tube burst pressure. Two different axisymmetric pressure loading routes are envisaged: 1.1 Geometry Three geometries of variable thinner tubes are treated: Table 1-1: Tube dimensions. | Tube | 1 | 2 | 3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Average radius R ( \mathit{mm} ) | 10 | 10 | 10 | | Thickness h ( \mathit{mm} ) | 0.5 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 1.2 Material and behaviour - Young's modulus : E=165000\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio : \nu=\mathrm{0.3} - Elastic limit: {\sigma}_{y}=330\mathit{MPa} - Ultimate limit: {\sigma}_{u}=820\mathit{MPa} The material parameters are as follows: The tensile curve is as follows: Table 1-2: Monotonous traction curve. | Deformation | Constraint ( \mathit{MPa} ) | | --- | --- | | 0.002 | 330 | | 0.0024 | 340 | | 0.005 | 347 | | 0.010 | 362 | | 0.0198 | 404 | | 0.0296 | 446 | | 0.0392 | 484 | | 0.0583 | 549 | | 0.0770 | 609 | | 0.1044 | 689 | | 0.1222 | 742 | | 0.1484 | 819 | | 0.5000 | 820 | Elastoplastic monotonous traction curve It is decided to model the elastoplastic behavior of Von Isotropic hardening devices, with this tensile curve. 1.3 Loading conditions journey 1 The axial displacement of the tube is blocked on the lower side of the model, and it is uniform and free on the upper side (unblocked tube). Il y a 74 nodes. 4.2 Modelling characteristics and Loading Conditions There are 5 layers in the thickness, each with 3 subpoints for the calculation of stress fields and internal variables. The lower edge is affected by a total blockage in Oz axial direction; the upper edge is assigned a uniform restraint on the axial direction translation to simulate a kinematic identical to that of a tube of very long length. The applied pressure values are corrected to meet the exact internal and external wall metrics, so that they are identical to those applied in model A. The factor keyword used in AFFE_CHAR_MECA is FORCE_COQUE=_F(PRES=) . 4.3 Non-linear static Modelling characteristics The time step chosen is 0.5 , fixed for all nonlinear calculation steps; however, a cut is allowed in the event of convergence failure, the RESI_GLOB_RELA criterion being fixed to 10^{-6} . The precision required for the fulfilment of the flat stress condition is: RESI_CPLAN_RELA=1e-06 . The Newton method uses the MATRICE='TANGENTE' otion. For the calculation of the limit pressure, a load control is used by radial displacement of an node from the outer wall. (For plotting curves, a calculation is used with a maximum time step of 0.1 .) 4.4 post-processing The post-processing of the radial displacement is made at any time in a node on the Oy=0 axis. In this model, cf. r3.08.06, kinematics represents axial, circumferential, tangential and transverse distortion deformations in the section plane, but not radial deformation or orthogonal transverse distortion in the section plane. The behavior relationship produces axial, circumferential, plane shears tangential and transverse stresses in the section plane. The MODI_METRIQUE = OUI option is chosen to express gradients in thickness with the local metric (not the average metric as in the elements of ordinary cockurs). There are 16 sectors on the circumference, each with 3 subpoints for the calculation of the stress fields and internal variables. There are 5 layers in the thickness, each with 3 subpoints for the calculation of the stress fields and internal variables. This makes 4 \times 2 + 3 = 11 subpoints in the thickness and 15 \times 2 + 3 = 33 subpoints in the circumference, hence 363 subpoints in total. 7.3 Loading conditions The lower edge is affected by a total blockage of all 6 degrees of freedom beam; the upper edge is affected by a total blockage of 5 degrees of freedom beam other than translational Oz axial direction. The degrees of freedom of Fourier "out-of-plane" modes: UO2, UO3, VO2, VO3, WO2, WO3 are also blocked on the lower and upper edges. This simulates a kinematic identical to that of a tube of very long length. The applied pressure values are corrected to meet the exact internal and external wall metrics, so that they are identical to those applied in model A. The factor keyword used in AFFE_CHAR_MECA is FORCE_TUYAU=_F(PRES=) . Since this model only accepts pressures on the inner surface of the pipe, the application of external pressure is simulated by negative internal pressure, so that its effect on the normal circumferential stress is identical: p_i^{éq}=-p_e \times {R_e}/{R_i} . 7.4 Non-linear static Modelling characteristics The time step chosen is 0.5 , fixed for all non-linear calculation steps; however, a cut is allowed in the event of convergence failure, the RESI_GLOB_RELA criterion being fixed to 10^{-6} . For the calculation of the limit pressure, a load control is used by the radial displacement WO of the node of the lower edge. (For plotting curves, a calculation is used with a maximum time step of 0.1 .) 7.5 post-processing The post-processing of the radial displacement is made in a node on the z=0. plane at any moment. The post-processing of the axial displacement is made in a node on the z=1. plane at any moment. The generalized forces (beam theory) are produced at nodes of elements: N, VY, VZ, MT, MFY, MFZ. By introducing internal and external pressures with a corrected value that correctly represents the true area of the internal and external walls (metric correction according to thickness), the results are corrected significantly, but this is not enough to get close enough to the reference calculation; COQUE_3D Modelling produces results very similar to DKT Modelling, since these fine elements membranes, in a homogeneous situation, must give the same results as DKT with mesh cells planees; TUYAU_3M Modelling ( TUYAU_6M Modelling would give the same result) provides very close results to DKT Modelling. - for stresses: The residual radial and circumferential stresses are very well evaluated by COQUE_SOLIDE modelling using the clamping in reference to the 2D axisymmetric calculation; DKT modelling with behavior model expressed in flat stresses deviates significantly from the 2D axisymmetric calculation even after internal and external pressures have been used with a corrected value. While in DKT and COQUE_3D modelling produce constant circumferential stresses in thickness, TUYAU_3M modelling produces variable stresses in thickness, but does not overlap the reference model values. - for internal variables: COQUE_SOLIDE Modelling using the clamping system is very good at evaluating the nutrification variable, while modellings in flat stresses ( DKT , COQUE_3D , TUYAU_3M ) are very disappointing. - for a monotonous loading journey to the internal pressure ruin: - The COQUE_SOLIDE Modelling capacity is observed to correctly reproduce the evolution of plasticization in thickness and to provide the boundary load with high accuracy. - DKT Modelling with behavior model expressed in flat stresses deviates significantly from the 2D axisymmetric calculation, even after having corrected the internal pressure with the true area of the internal wall. It is apparent, as expected, that this Modelling without pinching leaves no margin between first plasticization and ruin of the structure. - The evolution of radial displacement during loading corroborates these observations. - However, in terms of plastic ruin limit load, modellings COQUE_SOLIDE , COQUE_3D , DKT , TUYAU_3M provide conservative values to within 10%. For example, for these types of problems: - The hypothesis of the flat constraints appearing in the writing of the constitutive law is too restrictive and enrichment in clamping constraints is decisive; - The correction of metrics according to thickness is also necessary. For this reason, COQUE_SOLIDE r3.07.04 inshell modelling allows the reproduction of completely satisfactory results, with reference to the calculation with solid finished elements, cf. v6.01.129-Modelization_A. v6.02.100 SSNL100 - Laying of a double-gauge line township v6.02.100 SSNL100 - Laying of a double-gauge line township Summary: This test simulates the operation of a two-stranded cable. The cable is attached to one end of the cable, passes on a fixed pulley towards the other end and rests in its middle on a pulley at the bottom of a mobile suspension. The deflection of the ranges is adjusted by "giving" more or less cable at the level of the fixed pulley. The interest is to test the elements cable and pulley cable and their operation in the STAT_NON_LINE operator. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry | | O | {P}_{1} | {P}_{2} | {R}_{2} | C | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | x | | | | | | | z | | | | | | Table 1.1-a : Point coordinates (in m ) Names and position of nodes (mid-range before installation): - left hand range: \mathrm{N6} and x=48.50m - right hand range: \mathrm{N19} and x=160.50m 1.2 Material properties Linear weight of cable : 30N/m Axial rigidity of the cable (produced from Young's modulus by the area of the right section): 5.{10}^{7}N 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The O , C and {P}_{2} points are fixed. The cable, fixed in O , is supported by two pulleys. The first is attached to the lower end of the {P}_{1} suspension fixed in C . The second is attached to {P}_{2} . The cable is subject to its weight and is given deflection by moving its right end from \mathrm{10 }m from {R}_{2} to {R}_{2}' . The position of the {Q}_{1} , {R}_{1} and {Q}_{2} points is not imposed, but it is necessary to ensure that during the installation the {P}_{1} pulley remains on the {Q}_{1}{R}_{1} cable segment. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference deflection is relative to an inextensible 105m cable over a range of 100m . It is obtained by solving a transcendent equation [bib2]. 2.2 Baseline The deflection reference is 13.93m , equal for each range. 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution Semi-analytic solution. 2.4 Bibliographical references | [1] | AUFAURE, 'Un finite element de cable-polli', Document R3.08.05 (1996). | | --- | --- | | [2] | MAX IRVINE, 'Cable Structures', The MIT Press (1981). | 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics | 10 elements cable | MECABL2 between O and {Q}_{1} , carried by mesh cells SEG2; | | --- | --- | | 1 element | MEPOULI via {P}_{1} pulley and carried by mesh cell SEG3 {Q}_{1}{P}_{1}{R}_{1} ; | | 9 elements | MECABL2 between {R}_{1} and {Q}_{2} ; | | 1 element | MEPOULI on {Q}_{2}{P}_{2}{R}_{2} ; | | 1 element | MECABL2 on the {P}_{1}C suspension. | 3.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes : 25 Number of mesh cells and types: 20 mesh cells SEG2 and 2 mesh cells SEG3 3.3 Remarks Starting from a horizontal straight line cable in weighting, gravity is applied while increasing the length of the cable between O and {P}_{2} from 10m by moving {R}_{2} to {R}_{2}' ( {R}_{\mathrm{2 }}{R}_{2}'=10m ). Since straight untrenched cables do not have stiffness for transverse loads, the previous load case cannot be applied immediately as a system of singular equations would be achieved. The calculation is therefore done in 2 stages: - The cables are pre-voltageed by applying a voltage to the cable itself in {R}_{2} and to the suspension in {P}_{1} (it is suggested to take 10000N voltages). - The gravity load will be declared SUIV type, because of elements MEPOULI with both parts of variable length. 3.4 Tested quantities and results | Identification | Reference | | --- | --- | | Deflection left-hand range \mathrm{N6} | -1.3930E+001 | | Deflection of the right-hand range \mathit{N19} | -1.3930E+001 | 4 Modelling B Model B is identical to model A. It is just used to validate the fact that thermal loading is not taken into account. For this reason a constant temperature is imposed. The results are identical to model A. 5 Summary of the results This test ensures that Code_Aster evolutions do not cause regressions for elements cable and pulley cable, as well as for the following loads of the STAT_NON_LINE command.

v6.02.101 SSNL101 - Non-linear behavior of a line arming element v6.02.101 SSNL101 - Non-linear behavior of a line arming element Summary: This test considers 1 element discrete to 2 nodes subjected to a transverse stress in nonlinear static analysis. v6.02.112 SSNL112 - Bar subjected to a cyclic thermal charge v6.02.112 SSNL112 - Bar subjected to a cyclic thermal charge Summary: This test case is part of the validation of the elements bar elastoplasticity behavior relationships for quasi-static structural mechanics. A clamped bar at both ends undergoes a cyclic thermal loading that induces traction-compression forces. Each model allows validation of one of the introduced nonlinear behavior relationships: linear isotropic hardening with von Mises criterion (modelization A), linear kinematic hardening with von Mises criterion (modelization B). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry | Length of the bar: | 1m | | --- | --- | | Section of the bar: | 5{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} | 1.2 Material properties 1.2.1 Isotropic and linear kinematics | Young's modulus : | E=2.{10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Nuts: | {E}_{t}={2.10}^{9}\mathrm{Pa} | | Limit of elasticity: | \sigma ={2.10}^{8}\mathrm{Pa} | | Poisson's ratio : | \nu =0,3 | | Thermal expansion coefficient: | \alpha ={1.10}^{-5}{K}^{-1} | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading boundary conditions : The bar is clamped. The movements are therefore blocked in all three directions. En \mathrm{N1} et \mathrm{N2} : \mathrm{DX}=\mathrm{DY}=\mathrm{DZ}=0 Charge: The loading path is described by the temperature evolution, uniform in the bar: | t | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | T(°C) | 50 | –50 | –300 | –100 | 50 | –150 | –350 | –200 | The reference temperature is 0°C . 2 Reference solutions 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solutions 2.1.1 Linear scrubbing Isotropic scrubbing For uniaxial traction, the plasticity criterion ssss: ∣{\sigma}_{L}∣-R(p)\le 0 , where p is the cumulative plastic deformation. The expression of R(p) is given by the relation: R(p)=R'p+{\sigma}^{y} et R'=\frac{E{E}_{1}}{E-{E}_{1}} . The criterion then reads: ∣{\sigma}_{L}∣-R'p-{\sigma}^{y}\le 0 . The stress tensor is obtained by: \sigma =A.(\varepsilon (u)-{\varepsilon}^{p})-\mathrm{3K}\alpha (T-{T}^{\mathrm{ref}})\mathrm{Id} . The expression of {\sigma}_{L} is derived from this: {\sigma}_{L}=E(\varepsilon -\alpha T)-E{\varepsilon}^{p} . ({T}^{\mathrm{ref}}=0) . In our case, \varepsilon =0 so: {\sigma}_{L}=E{\varepsilon}_{L}-E{\varepsilon}^{p} , with {\varepsilon}_{L}=-\alpha T . So: - Si ∣{\sigma}_{L}∣-R(p)<0 : p=0 et {\sigma}_{L}=E{\varepsilon}_{L} , - Si ∣{\sigma}_{L}∣-R(p)=0 : p=(\frac{∣\sigma ∣-{\sigma}^{y}}{R'}) et {\sigma}_{L}=E{\varepsilon}_{L}-E{\varepsilon}^{p} . Application to the loading journey Instant 1: \sigma =E\varepsilon =\mathrm{200MPa} and R(p)=R'p+{\sigma}^{y}=\mathrm{100MPa} , because p=0 . We have {\sigma}_{L}-R(p)\le 0 . The criterion is not met, the evolution is elastic: {\sigma}_{L}=\mathrm{100MPa} and N=\mathrm{100kN} . Instant 2: The criterion is met: {\sigma}_{L}=\frac{E}{E+R'}(R'{\varepsilon}_{L}+{\sigma}^{y})=\frac{2\cdot {10}^{11}}{2\cdot {10}^{11}+2.02\cdot \mathrm{10⁹}}(2.02\cdot \mathrm{10⁹}\times 3.5\cdot {10}^{-3}+2\cdot \mathrm{10⁸})=\mathrm{205MPa} . With N=\mathrm{102.5kN} , and p=2.475\cdot {10}^{-3} . Instant 3: Elastically discharged: {\sigma}_{L}=E{\varepsilon}_{L}-E{\varepsilon}^{p}=2\cdot {10}^{11}(1.5\cdot {10}^{-3}-2.475\cdot {10}^{-3})=-195\mathrm{MPa} . With N=-97.5\mathrm{kN} . Instant 4: We plasticize again: The criterion s's written: \mid \sigma \mid -R'p-{\sigma}^{y}=0 with p={p}_{1}+{p}_{2} where {p}_{1}=2.475\cdot {10}^{-3} Thus, we obtain: {p}_{2}=\frac{\mid \sigma \mid -{\sigma}^{y}}{R'}-{p}_{1} , \sigma =-E{\varepsilon}^{p}=-E({p}_{1}-{p}_{2}) , \sigma =(\frac{R'}{R'+E})(-2E{p}_{1}-\frac{E{\sigma}^{y}}{R'})=-\mathrm{207.9MPa} , And so N=-\mathrm{103.95kN} . It is clamped at the O and B ends, which are themselves distant from \mathrm{2L} . Initially, 2{l}_{0}=2L=\mathrm{325m} The area of the cable section is: 2.2783E-04{m}^{2} 1.2 Material properties E=5.70E+10\mathrm{Pa} \nu =0.3 (modelization B only) \mathrm{ALPHA}:2.3E-5{K}^{-1} \mathrm{RHO}:2.844230E+03\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads clamped support en O et B gravity: (9.81,0.0,0.0,-1.0) The temperature in the cable varies with time, the reference temperature is 0.°C . - Instant: 0. Temperature T=0.°C - Instant: 1.Temperature T=39.26°C The following are therefore dealt with: - at instant 0, a cable subject to its own weight only - at moment 1, a heavy cable subjected to thermal expansion. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution analytical solution : For an extendable (elastic) cable, subject to its own weight, the displacement is equal to: x(s)=a\mathit{Argsh}\left(\frac{s}{a}\right)+\frac{\rho g}{E}as z(x)=a\sqrt{1+\frac{{s}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}+\frac{\rho g}{E}\frac{{s}^{2}}{2}-a\sqrt{1+\frac{{l}_{0}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}-\frac{\rho g}{E}\frac{{l}_{0}^{2}}{2} a solution of equation L=a\mathrm{Argsh}(\frac{{l}_{0}}{a})+\frac{\rho g}{E}a{l}_{0}=f(a) With s abscisse curvilinear, s\in [-{l}_{o},{l}_{o}] . Here we are interested in the deflection in the center (point C ) : z(C)=a-a\sqrt{1+\frac{{l}_{0}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}-\frac{\rho g}{E}\frac{{l}_{0}^{2}}{2} a solution of equation L=a\mathrm{Argsh}(\frac{{l}_{0}}{a})+\frac{\rho g}{E}a{l}_{0}=f(a) The only difficulty in calculating this solution is the resolution of the L=f(a) equation. This resolution was numerically made (fortran program using the routine search for zero d-Aster ZEROFO). Note: In the case of thermal expansion, the solution is the same as before, considering that the initial length 2{l}_{0} is equal to its initial length \mathrm{2L} increased linear expansion: {l}_{0}=L(1+\alpha T) 2.2 Baseline Moving Z to point C 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution Semi-analytical solution: The numerical resolution of the L=f(a) equation gives a value to the {10}^{-3} . 2.4 Bibliographical references [1] C.CONEIM "On the approximation of the equations of the static of aerial cables in the presence of electromagnetic forces fields." v6.02.118 SSNL118 - Wind speed field bar v6.02.118 SSNL118 - Wind speed field bar Summary: This test is for the validation of the application of wind loads on linear elements. The load is described by wind speed fields. This problem allows testing: - Linear finished elements (bars, cables, beams (except curved beams)) with following loads of a kind - Loads representing wind speeds: - reading wind field data, - projection of the wind fields attached to the dot cloud on the distorted mesh of the structure, - calculation of the relative speed, - the function giving the force distributed according to the relative speed of the structure, - the updating of geometry to take account of large movements and large rotations. v6.02.120 SSNL120 - Cyclical Response of 1D Concrete Behaviour Laws v6.02.120 SSNL120 - Cyclical Response of 1D Concrete Behaviour Laws Summary: In this example, the concrete behaviour model of Mazars R7.01.08 in their 1D version is tested using element multifibre beam R3.08.08 axially-suspension. - For Modelling A, the load consists of traction with loading and unloading followed by compression also with loading and unloading. It allows to test tensile and compression resistance, to highlight crack closing phenomena and to test anelastic deformations. - For model B, the material parameters all depend on temperature. The load is composed of traction with loading and unloading followed by compression also with loading and unloading. The temperature changes during the loading of traction and compression. 1 General characteristics 1.1 Geometry Console beam of unit length, square section of unit side. 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus concrete: E=3,7272{10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} Tensile strength of concrete: {F}_{\mathit{tj}}=4.{10}^{6}\mathit{Pa} Concrete compression strength: {F}_{\mathit{cj}}=40.{10}^{6}\mathit{Pa} 1.3 boundary conditions clamped support en A : \mathit{dx}=\mathit{dy}=\mathit{dz}=0 et \mathit{drx}=\mathit{dry}=\mathit{drz}=0 . 1.4 Loading The axial deformation is increased and decreased by imposing a B displacement in the x direction. v6.02.125 SSNL125 - Traction of a fragile bar: gradient damage v6.02.125 SSNL125 - Traction of a fragile bar: gradient damage Summary: This test allows verification of fragile damage laws with gradient ENDO_SCALAIRE Modelling A) and ENDO_FISS_EXP (Modelling B) in a one-dimensional, non-homogeneous situation. Because of its 1D character, this problem admits an analytical solution that displays two regimes of boundary layers: one of finite length (existence of a free boundary between the damaged zone and the healthy zone) and the other of infinite length (extension to the boundary of the part). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure studied is a long 375\mathrm{mm} bar. The problem being purely \mathrm{1D} , its section is without influence. 1.2 Material properties In model A, the material follows a fragile elastic constitutive law (ENDO_SCALAIRE) with a gradient of damage (modelization _GRAD_VARI). | ELAS | ENDO_SCALAIRE | NON_LOCAL | | --- | --- | --- | | E= 30000\mathrm{MPa} NU = 0 | SY= 3\mathrm{MPa} GAMMA= 4 | C_GRAD_VARI= 1.875N PENA_LAGR= 1.5 | In model B, the material is governed by an ENDO_FISS_EXP law for which the following parameters are given: E = 30,000 MPa, NU = 0, ft = 3 MPa, fc = 30 MPa (not affecting 1D), Gf = 0.1 N/mm, p=1.5, D=50 mm. 1.3 Loading conditions The left part of the bar ( 125\mathrm{mm} long) is required to remain rigid (locking the degrees of freedom displacement). The right part of the bar is subject to uniform {\varepsilon}_{0} axial deformation, i.e. a forced displacement with linear spatial distribution. So only one parameter controls the load intensity: the required {\varepsilon}_{0} deformation level. In the perpendicular directions to the axis of the bar, the movements are blocked: the problem is purely \mathrm{1D} . Moreover, since the Poisson's ratio is zero, no flange stress develops in these directions. 2 reference solution We consider one of the constitutive laws gradient damage R5.04.01 with a free energy density in the form of: \Phi (\varepsilon ,a)=A(a)w(\varepsilon )+\omega (a)+c/2{(\nabla a)}^{2} , where 0\le a\le 1 refers to the damage variable and w(\varepsilon ) to the elastic strain energy. For ENDO_SCALAIRE law, \omega (a)=\mathrm{ka} and the damage prefactor is written as A(a)={(\frac{1-a}{1+\gamma a})}^{2} . The solution then depends on three material parameters \gamma , c , and k (see R5.03.25). In the general case, two partial derivative equations must be solved: the equilibrium equation ( \delta \Phi (\varepsilon ,a)/\delta \varepsilon =0 ) and the \delta \Phi (\varepsilon ,a)/\delta a=0 behavior equation. Getting an analytical solution s is generally delicate, even for one-dimensional structures. To validate this model, however, one attaches to a simpler problem for which the equilibrium equation does not need to be solved, i.e. the displacement field is fixed everywhere. The behavior equation is then controlled by the strain energy elastic w known in all point space. In this case, the semi-analytic solution is obtained by numerical integration of a differential equation with the initial Cauchy conditions. The ENDO_FISS_EXP law is totally equivalent to the ENDO_SCALAIRE law in a uniaxial traction situation. The analytical solution is therefore identical to the ENDO_SCALAIRE law. 2.1 Characterization of the solution More specifically, a bar with one part of the bar being forced to remain free of deformation is considered, while the other is subject to homogeneous deformation. The damage limit layer that develops at the interface of these two zones is studied. The differential equation of behaviour is as follows in areas where the criterion is met, i.e. where damage is developed: c\frac{{\partial}^{2}a}{\partial {x}^{2}}-\frac{\partial A}{\partial a}w-k=0 , où \frac{\partial A}{\partial a}(a)=-2(1+\gamma )\frac{(1-a)}{{(1+\gamma a)}^{3}} , éq 2.1-1 where x is the space variable. The strain energy elastic w is known in both parts of the bar: w=0 on the left and w({\varepsilon}_{0})=\mathrm{const} on the right. The solution is given by a continuous a\in {C}^{1}(-{L}_{0,}{L}_{1}) detrievable function. Three boundary conditionss are available: \frac{da}{dx}(-{L}_{0})=\frac{da}{dx}({L}_{1})=0 et a(-{L}_{0})=0 éq 2.1-2 as well as two interface conditions: {\left[\mid a\mid \right]}_{x=0}=0{\left[∣\frac{da}{dx}∣\right]}_{x=0}=0 éq 2.1-3 In total, we have five boundary conditions for five unknowns. Despite this fact, the problem is "unsure" to be solved numerically, because the boundary conditions are defined at the different points in the space. We proceed in the next process to identify unknowns using the boundary conditions and finally to obtain an ordinary differential equation of type Cauchy-Lipschitz. 2.2 Problem resolution in the unloaded area It is assumed that the left end of the x=-{L}_{0} bar is sufficiently far from the x=0 interface to maintain the validity of the hypothesis of a finite length limit layer in the unloaded area. Note then {b}_{0}>0 the length ( a priori dependent on the {\varepsilon}_{0} deformation level in the loaded area) on which this boundary layer develops. In part x\in \left[{L}_{0},-{b}_{0}\right] damage does not change and remains null: a(x)=0 on \left[-{L}_{0},-{b}_{0}\right] eq 2.2-1 In the x\in \left[-{b}_{0},0\right] part, the criterion is reached and the damage field is evolving according to the equation [eq 2.1-1], which is considerably simplified in this part of the bar since the elastic strain energy is zero: c\frac{{d}^{2}a}{{\mathrm{dx}}^{2}}=k on \left[-{b}_{0},0\right] eq 2.2-2 By definition of {b}_{0} , the following conditions are available: a(-{b}_{0})=0 et \frac{\mathrm{da}}{\mathrm{dx}}(-{b}_{0})=0 éq 2.2-4 The damage variable can then be expressed analytically by integrating [eq 2.2-2]: a(x)=\frac{k}{\mathrm{2c}}{(x+{b}_{0})}^{2} on \left[-{b}_{0},0\right] eq 2.2-5 The values of damage and its derivative at the x=0 interface are then known, depending on the unknown {b}_{0} : a({0}^{-})=\frac{{\mathrm{kb}}_{0}^{2}}{2c} et a'({0}^{-})=\frac{{\mathrm{kb}}_{0}}{c} éq 2.2-6 and damage to the {a}_{0} interface being strictly between 0 and 1 , the following frame is derived from the {b}_{0} length : 0 0 deformation associated with an strain energy elastic {w}_{0} . In this area, the boundary layer is no longer bounded and extends asymptotically towards the homogeneous response. It will therefore be assumed that the right end of the x={L}_{1} bar is sufficiently far from the x=0 interface to allow for the approximation of a zero derivative for the "infinite" damage field. In the vicinity of the right end of the bar, the behavior equation [eq 2.1-1-o] then reduces to: \frac{-\partial A}{\partial a}({a}_{\infty}){w}_{0}=k éq 2.3-1 where {a}_{\infty} is the asymptotic value of the damage field. Considering the expression of \partial A/\partial a ( cf. [eq 2.1-1]), the loading level can then be set by the {a}_{\infty} value only: for {a}_{\infty}\in \left]0,1\right[,{w}_{0}=\frac{k}{2(1+\gamma )}\frac{{(1+\gamma {a}_{\infty})}^{3}}{(1-{a}_{\infty})} eq 2.3-2 On the other hand, the nonlinear differential equation [eq 2.1-1-o] can be written as follows: \frac{c}{2}2a'a''=a'(A'(a)w-k) éq 2.3-3 It therefore admits a first integral: \forall x\in \left[0,{L}_{1}\right],{\left[\frac{c}{2}{(\frac{\mathrm{da}}{\mathrm{dx}}(s))}^{2}\right]}_{0}^{x}={\left[A(a(s))+ka(s)\right]}_{0}^{x} éq 2.3-4 It is recalled that the interface condition [eq 2.1-3] imposes an {C}^{1} connection in x=0 , taking into account the expressions linking a({0}^{+}) and a'({0}^{+}) to the {b}_{0} length of the boundary layer, it is possible to write: {a}_{0}=a({0}^{+})=\frac{{\mathrm{kb}}_{0}^{2}}{2c} et a{'}_{0}=a'({0}^{+})=\sqrt{\frac{2k}{c}{a}_{0}} éq 2.3-5 In addition, the boundary conditions [eq 2.1-2] ensures the nullity of the x={L}_{1} damage derivative, by making the a({L}_{1})={a}_{\infty} approximation, the first integral [eq 2.3-4] evaluated in x={L}_{1} is: A({a}_{0}){w}_{0}+k{a}_{0}-\frac{c}{2}a{'}_{0}^{2}=A({a}_{\infty}){w}_{0}+k{a}_{\infty} éq 2.3-6 The equation [eq 2.3-6] is simplified by [eq 2.3-5], and then reduced to the trinomal of the following second degree of unknown {a}_{0} : (f({a}_{\infty}){\gamma}^{2}-1){a}_{0}^{2}+2(f({a}_{\infty})\gamma +1){a}_{0}+(f({a}_{\infty})-1)=0 où f({a}_{\infty})=A({a}_{\infty})+\frac{k{a}_{\infty}}{{w}_{0}} éq 2.3-7 This provides a simple relationship between the {a}_{\infty} loading parameter and the {a}_{0} value of the damage and its a{'}_{0} derivative at the interface. The resolution of the nonlinear EDO [eq 2.1-1-o] on \left[0,{L}_{1}\right] was achieved by bringing it back to a differential order 1 system, numerically integrated with a Runge-Kutta schema in order 4 (space). The implementation of this schema requires only knowledge of the initial ({a}_{0,}a{'}_{0}) conditions associated with each {a}_{\infty} load parameter, which is ensured by the [eq 2.3-o] relationship. 2.4 Problem solving in the entire bar To calculate the reference solution on the entire bar, the following diagram is used: - choice of a loading parameter {a}_{\infty}\in \left]0,1\right[ - Resolution in the section concerned: - determination with [eq 2.3-2] of the strain energy elastic {w}_{0} associated - determination with [eq 2.3-7] of the boundary conditions ({a}_{0,}a{'}_{0}) game - digital integration with a Runge-Kutta schema in order 4 - Resolution in the unloaded part: - determination with [eq 2.3-7] and [eq 2.3-5] of the size {b}_{0} of the boundary layer in the unloaded area - obtain a(x) analytical field in this area with [eq 2.2-5] 2.5 Digital application For elasticity, hardening and non-local parameter, the following characteristics are adopted: \begin{array}{cc}E={3.10}^{4}\mathrm{MPa}& {\sigma}^{y}=3.\mathrm{MPa}\\ \nu =0.& \gamma =4.\end{array}c=1.875N éq 2.5-1 These choices lead to a strain energy elastic threshold: {w}_{y}=1.5{10}^{-4}\mathrm{MPa} éq 2.5-2 2.6 Baseline The reference solution is obtained by taking a -{L}_{0}=-125\mathrm{mm} and {L}_{1}=250\mathrm{mm} length bar. v6.02.130 SSNL130 – Unformable plate on a spring mat v6.02.130 SSNL130 – Unformable plate on a spring mat Summary: The objective is to test and validate the possibilities of the AFFE_CARA_ELEM command, option RIGI_PARASOL in \mathrm{2D} and \mathrm{3D} and affected by DIS_CHOC or DIS_CONTACT behavior. This test case modeled a plate, considered unformable, placed on a carpet of springs. - The springs are modeled by DIS_T ( K_T_D_L ), which allows to impose boundary conditions at the ends of the springs that are not tied to the solid. - DIS_CHOC or DIS_CONTACT behaviors allow for unilateral spring behaviour, leaving a possibility of plate release from the spring mat. The same problem can also be modelled by elements d-interfaces with the CZM_ELAS_MIX behavioral relationship, which then represent a continuous distribution of springs (modelization E). The F Modelling allows to validate the grid method, option RIGI_GRILLE. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A rectangular plate of a width and b length, supported by a carpet of springs. : Schematic of the plate and springs in the (y,z) plane. Dimensions: a = 1.00 m , b = 2.00 m , ep = 0.30 m 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus : 2.0E+11 Pa Poisson's ratio : 0.3 Stiffness overall spring mat : K = 10000.0 N/m Stiffness density of the spring mat: k = \frac{K}{a.b} = 5000 N/{m}^{2} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The loading is a pressure of the P = {p.(y-b)^{2}} shape, with p = {5N /{m}^{4}} Displacements imposed on the ends of springs not connected to the plate: - In the time interval [0,1] the displacement is imposed to 0.0 following {DX} , {DY} and {DZ} , - In the time interval [1,2] the displacement is imposed to 0.0 following {DX} and {DY} . - Next {DZ} it is imposed by the {Dz} = (t-1.0) 0.5E-02 function. 1.4 Initial conditions Not applicable for static analysis. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation of the continuous problem : Plate and springs after loading. The problem solving is to calculate the vertical displacements of the corners of the plate and the position of the point of the delamination vis-à-vis the spring mat. The equilibrium equations are as follows: - Effort resulting from loading: {Fp} = \underset{s}{\iint }{P.ds} ={p.a.}\frac{{b}^{3}}{3} - The point A due to loading: {{Mp}_{A}} = \underset{s}{\iint }{P.y.ds} = {a.p.}\frac{{b}^{4}}{12} The plate is considered rigid, its displacement is of the form z(y)={U}_{a}(1-\frac{y}{{y}_{0}}) . With {U}_{a} the vertical displacement of the point A and {y}_{0} the position of the detachment. - Spring reaction effort: {Fr}=\underset{s}{\iint }\frac{K}{a.b}{U}_{a}(1-\frac{y}{{y}_{0}}) ds =K.{U}_{a}\frac{{y}_{0}}{2b} - Point A spring reaction time: {{Mr}}_{A}=\underset{s}{\iint }\frac{K}{a.b}{U}_{a}(1-\frac{y}{{y}_{0}})y{ds}=K.{U}_{a}\frac{{y}_{0}^{2}}{6b} The equations (balance of effort and moments) are solved by the following result: {y}_{0}=\frac{3b}{4} , {U}_{a}=-\frac{8p.a.{b}^{3}}{9K} is derived from {U}_{b}=-\frac{{U}_{a}}{3} 2.2 Method of calculating the discretized problem In this analysis the spring mat is no longer considered continuous. Springs are regularly distributed. As previously the vertical displacements of the corners of the plate and the position of the stripping line vis-à-vis the spring mat will be calculated. : Schematic of the plate and springs after loading. : Discretization of the plate in the (x,y) plane The v6.02.130-fig-Place DiscreteRessortPlan identifies the springs according to their stiffness. This stiffness is calculated by the RIGI_PARASOL option of the AFFE_CARA_ELEM command. The allocation of the values is based on the area of the area they affect. If K is the overall stiffness of the spring mat, we have: {k4}=\frac{{K}}{{nx}{ny}} , {k2}={k3}=\frac{{k4}}{2}=\frac{{K}}{2{nx}{ny}} , {k1}=\frac{{k4}}{4}=\frac{{K}}{4{nx}{ny}} The equilibrium equations are as follows: - Spring reaction effort: {\mathit{Fr}}_{(j)}={U}_{a}\cdot \left[{K}_{x}^{'}+{K}_{x}^{''}\cdot \sum_{j=1}^{n}\left(1-j\frac{b}{\mathit{ny}{y}_{0}}\right)\right] - Spring reaction time along line {AB} : {{Mr}}_{(j)}={U}_{a}\cdot {K}_{x}^{''}\cdot \sum_{j=1}^{n}(1-j\frac{b}{{ny}{y}_{0}})\cdot j\frac{b}{{ny}} with: - {K}_{x}^{'}=(2{k1}+{k2}({nx}-1)) - {K}_{x}^{"}=(2{k3}+{k4}({nx}-1)) - n \frac{b}{ny} \le {y}_{0} \le (n+1)\frac{b}{ny} The solution of equations (balance of effort and moments) gives the solution of balance: \left \lbrace \begin{array}{l} {U}_{a}=\frac{p.a.{b}^{3}.{ny}.(3.ny-8.n-4)}{6.K.(1+n+{n}^{2})} \\ {y}_{0}=\frac{b.n.(1+n).(3.ny-8.n-4)}{3.ny.(ny+2.n.(ny-2)-4.{n}^{2})} \end{array} \right. where n and {y}_{0} must meet the following conditions: - {n}\frac{b}{ny} \le {y}_{0} \le (n+1)\frac{b}{{ny}} - 0 \le {y}_{0} \le b - Integer n 2.3 Quantities and reference results The quantities tested will be vertical displacements at the 4 corners of the plate. 2.4 Uncertainties about the solution None, the solution is analytical. 3 modellings A, C 3.1 Features of modellings The plate is modelled by elements DKT . In {2D} as in {3D} , using the RIGI_PARASOL keyword of the AFFE_CARA_ELEM command allows you to assign to the springs stiffeners proportional to the length or surface of the elements to which they are connected. Since the behaviour is unilateral, it is necessary to make several iterations to find the position of equilibrium. It is also possible to encounter convergence problems related to a loss of precision, due to poor conditioning of the matrix of stiffness during iterations. The stiffness springs can be canceled from one iteration to the other. With regard to elements d'interface modelling, the continuous solution is obtained without error. Here too, several iterations are necessary to find the point plate detachment. Ideally, we should also guard against the energy-free mode in which the plate takes off everywhere (it could lead to a non-invertible matrix, even if it was not observed because in the natural state, the compression stiffness, not zero, is preferred).

v6.02.134 SSNL134 - Elasto-plastic Ruin of Lee's Gate v6.02.134 SSNL134 - Elasto-plastic Ruin of Lee's Gate Summary This test is intended to validate simultaneously the nonlinear material and geometric possibilities of element multifibre beam POU_D_TGM . L的element is implemented on a test case commonly treated in the literature with respect to elastic behavior as it presents a complex response with snap-back and snap-through : cs Lee's portal. The elastoplastic behavior of the portal is assumed here, which allows the correct integration of the constitutive law of the multifibre elements to be tested, as well as the correct treatment of large movements. The results obtained are compared with the results from the literature and non-regression tests. The current case contains only one model. However, in the Summary of the results, further analysis of the results is provided to help the reader understand the actual dataset. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The portico of Lee is a two-armed portico, articulated at its ends: Geometry and dimensions of Lee's portal Contact details of points (in \mathrm{cm} ): | | A | B | C | X | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | x | 0 | 0 | 120 | 24 | | y | 0 | 120 | 120 | 120 | 1.2 Section characteristics The arms are rectangular cross-section of 3\mathrm{cm} by 2\mathrm{cm} . The cross-section is oriented in such a way that the lowest inertia axis is perpendicular to the gantry plane. | A=6{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} | | --- | | {I}_{y}=2.0{\mathrm{cm}}^{4} | | {I}_{z}=4.5{\mathrm{cm}}^{4} | | {A}_{y}=1.2 | | {A}_{z}=1.2 | 1.3 Material properties | E=720N/{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} | | --- | | \nu =0.3 | | {E}_{t}=72N/{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} | | {\sigma}_{e}=10.44N/{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} | 1.4 Boundary conditions and loading | | Boundary conditions are imposed on A and C points (articulation around \mathrm{Oz} ): \mathrm{DX}=\mathrm{DY}=\mathrm{DZ}=\mathrm{DRX}=\mathrm{DRY}=0 | | --- | --- | | | Point X is charged with F vertical loading: \mathrm{FY}=C\times t . The C constant is the steering coefficient determined for example by a d-arc length method. Indeed, this structure has a complex response under non-monoton loading. | 2 reference solution 2.1 Method used for the calculation of the reference solution This portal was first studied in 1968 by Lee bib1, who proposed an analytical solution in the elastic case and neglecting the strain energy due to normal effort. v6.02.135 SSNL135 – Determination of MEKELEC console ruin loads v6.02.135 SSNL135 – Determination of MEKELEC console ruin loads Summary In this test, we are looking to validate in the nonlinear geometrical field and multifibre Timoshenko beam material l-element, available in Code_Astervia POU_D_TGM Modelling. To illustrate the possibilities offered by this element, we propose to numerically determine the ruin loads of the MEKELEC pylon console and compare them with test results. The MEKELEC console is subjected to different load cases and for each case the predicted ruin load and the predicted ruin mode are compared to those observed in the tests. The results show a very good prediction of the ruin modes with, however, a disparity in the loads that is explained more by the simplified Modelling adopted for the console than by the gaps in the finite element used. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Structure geometry The MEKELEC console is studied. It is a P4T pylons console, whose dimensions have been reduced to facilitate the instrumentation of the tests while maintaining a structure whose ruin modes can be varied and cover those encountered in a real lattice tower. The structure consists of 10 horns assembled on their wings with bolts, or via pods. Reference can be made to [3] for detailed plans of the console. 1.2 Characteristics of the angles used The MEKELEC console is a standard metal construction profile. v6.02.141 SSNL141 - Multifibre and multimaterial P-rings v6.02.141 SSNL141 - Multifibre and multimaterial P-rings Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the use of multimaterial cross section for multifibre beams. The beam consists of two materials. Two types of calculation are made: - a static calculation - two modal calculations, one with the MASS_MECA option and the other with the MASS_MECA_DIAG option The reference solutions are derived from Euler's beam theory. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A 2m length beam is considered to be X oriented. 1.2 Section characteristics 1.2.1 Geometry and fibre The section under consideration is a square of 10\mathit{cm} side. It is composed of 16 fibres, themselves squared. 1.2.2 Materials The section has two different materials, as described in the following table. | Material | Beton | Storage | | --- | --- | --- | | Young's modulus | 3\times {10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} | 2\times {10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | | Poisson's ratio | 0.2 | 0.0 | | Volume size | 2500\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | 7850\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} | | Symbol on figure | B | A | Materials are affected on fibres as shown in the figure below: The advantage of this structure is to keep the centres of rigidity, gravity, torsion, which are the origin of the local section marker, and to be symmetrical with respect to its centre and with respect to the Y and Z axes. 1.3 Loading 1.3.1 boundary conditions Static calculus: The node A is clamped and the node B is left free. modal calculus: The node A moves are blocked and the rotation around the beam axis is blocked. Y and Z moves of node B are blocked as well as rotation around the beam axis. 1.3.2 Forced Static calculus: A constant distributed force of -1.0E+04N/m according to Z is applied to the beam. modal calculus: None. 2 reference solution 2.1 Static calculation: clamped beam The theory of bending beams provides a reference value for maximum displacement. For one clamped beam at one end and free of the other under distributed load, the maximum displacement at the free end called deflection is given by: f=\frac{-{\mathit{qL}}^{4}}{{\mathrm{8EI}}_{\mathit{eq}}} - q : the force distributed in N/m . - L : the length of the beam in m . - {\mathit{EI}}_{\mathit{eq}} : in the case of single-materials, it is the product of Young's modulus and quadratic moment. In the multimaterial case, and with the configuration described above, {\mathit{EI}}_{\mathit{eq}} is calculated as follows: {\mathit{EI}}_{\mathit{eq}}={\int}_{S}E(s){z(s)}^{2}\mathit{ds} In Code_Aster this calculation is approached by a sum on the fibres: {\mathit{EI}}_{\mathit{eq}}={\sum}_{i=1}^{{\mathit{nb}}_{\mathit{fibres}}}{E}_{i}{{z}_{i}}^{2}{A}_{i} where {z}_{i} is the Z coordinates of the centre of i fiber and where {A}_{i} is its surface. 2.2 Modal calculation: single support beam For a single support beam, as defined in paragraph 1.3.1. , the beam theory provided with reference values for the modal calculation's eigenfrequency. The first eigenfrequency is: {f}_{1}=\frac{\pi}{2{L}^{2}}\sqrt{\frac{{\mathit{EI}}_{\mathit{eq}}}{m}} . where L is the length of the beam and m is the linear mass of the beam. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution None. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The elements beams are modeled by POU_D_TGM. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh is made up of 10 mesh cells SEG2 of the same length. 3.3 Tested quantities and results 3.3.1 Static calculation: clamped beam deflection au node B . | Nœud | Field | Component | Reference value | Tolerance (%) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | B | DEPL | DZ | -6.64935064935E-2 | 0.5 | 3.3.2 Modal calculation: single-screw beam Calculation of the first frequency of its own. | NUME_ORDRE | PARA | Reference value | Tolerance (%) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | FREQ | 34.7665079762 | 0.5 | 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics The elements beams are modeled by POU_D_EM. 4.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh is made up of 10 mesh cells SEG2 of the same length. 4.3 Tested quantities and results 4.3.1 Static calculation: clamped beam deflection au node B . | Nœud | Field | Component | Reference value | Tolerance (%) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | B | DEPL | DZ | -6.64935064935E-2 | 0.1 | 4.3.2 Modal calculation: single-screw beam Calculation of the first frequency of its own. | NUME_ORDRE | PARA | Reference value | Tolerance (%) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | FREQ | 34.7665079762 | 0.1 | 5 Summary of the results The calculated results are extremely theoretical solution for static calculation and modal calculation. v6.02.504 SSNL504 – Assembling skeleton element v6.02.504 SSNL504 – Assembling skeleton element Summary: This test validates the element skeleton assembly described with multifibre beams. A first calculation is made using a ten-beam mesh, where boundary conditions equivalent to the kinematic assembly is applied and a load is imposed while moving. This solution is considered as the reference one. v6.03.009 SSNP009 - Stability of a homogeneous slope with suction evaluated by the water retention curve v6.03.009 SSNP009 - Stability of a homogeneous slope with suction evaluated by the water retention curve Summary: This test case is part of the tutorials of the commercial software Geostudio SLOPE/W, designed with the aim of demonstrating and validating methods to take into account matrix suction in slope stability analysis in the presence of hydraulic pressure[1]. In this test case the SLOPE/W results are reproduced with the CALC_STAB_PENTE macro-command using the Simplified Bishop method. This test case allows you to validate the following features: - Definition of hydraulic pressure field by the result of THM calculation. - Consideration of matrix suction with pressure field defined via LIGN_PHREA and CHAM_PRES . - Evaluation of suction resistance by the Van-Genuchten model or water retention curve in the keyword THM_DIFFU . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Geometry of the slope with horizontal waterline[1]. The stability of a homogeneous slope with the horizontal water line at the foot of the slope is studied. The slope geometry is shown in geom-ssnp009. 1.2 Material properties The mechanical properties of the soil are as follows: - Density: 2000kg/m^3 - Friction angle: 20^{\circ} - Cohesion : 5kPa The water retention curve of the limousine clay forming the slope is recovered from the SLOPE/W software, which is shown in Fig-1. Water retention curve of the limousine clay. The saturated water saturation and the residual saturation are \theta_s = 0.5 and \theta_r = 0.25 respectively. Effective saturation is estimated by the formula: S_{we} = \frac{\theta - \theta_r}{\theta_s - \theta_r} This allows the Van-Genuchten model to be calibrated: Pr = 19.79kPa and n = 2.32 . However, as shown in Fig-2, the Van-Genuchten model cannot reproduce the negative effective saturation. So we define the same Van-Genuchten parameters in SLOPE/W to generate the reference results for the modellings A and C. In addition, when the water retention curve is defined via the SATU_PRES operand in THM_DIFFU , \theta_s and \theta_r automatically take the values of the first and last sample on the curve. So we slice the curve in Fig-1 to p_c = 74kPa corresponding to S_w = \theta_r = 0.25 to generate the reference result in the B Modelling. Calibration of the Van-Genuchten model. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The following loads shall be applied: - The gravity with g=9,81m/{s}^{2} The hydraulic pressure field is defined by the horizontal water line corresponding to the 10m rating. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation Calculations with the same configuration in the different modellings of this test case are done with the software Geostudio SLOPE/W version 2024.1.0. v6.03.108 SSNP108 - element prestressed concrete in compression v6.03.108 SSNP108 - element prestressed concrete in compression Summary: An elementary structure consisting of a square concrete plate crossed by a prestress cable whose neutral fiber is confused with the horizontal symmetry axis of the plate. The vertical left edge of the plate is fixed. The cable is pulled at both ends in order to prestress the plate in compression. The tension losses along the cable are neglected. The purpose of this test case is to validate, on a simple configuration, the method of calculating the equilibrium state of a prestressed concrete structure. The results are validated by comparison with an analytical solution. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The concrete plate is square; the sides have the same length L=H=2m . The thickness of the plate is e=0,6m . The cable crosses the plate horizontally, at mid-height, without eccentricity in thickness. L-section of the right section of the cable is {S}_{a}=1,5{.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} . 1.2 Material properties | Concrete material constituting the plate: | Young's modulus {E}_{b}={3.10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Steel material constituting the cable: | Young's modulus {E}_{a}=2,1{.10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | The Poisson's ratio is taken equal to 0 for both materials, thus favouring the direction of application of the normal effort (direction x ). The loss of tension is neglected, and the various parameters used for their estimation are set at 0. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The bottom top of the left edge of the plate, i.e. the node origin (0;0) , is clamped: all translation and rotation degrees of freedom are blocked. The top top of the same left edge, i.e. the node (0;2) , is supported bi-laterally: the blocked degrees of freedom translation is \mathit{DX} and \mathit{DZ} . At both ends of the cable (which are attached to the concrete in A and B ) a normal tensile force is applied: (–{F}_{0};0) to node A (0;1) and ({F}_{0};0) to node B (2;1) , with {F}_{0}={2.10}^{5}N . 2 reference solution 2.1 Formal solution The movements in the cable and concrete are continuous and homogeneous. Thus the horizontal displacement on the [0;L] interval is u(x)=\frac{{u}_{L}}{L}x The normal stresses in the concrete plate and the steel cable are described respectively (elasticity hypothesis): \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{\sigma}_{b}={E}_{b}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}={E}_{b}\frac{{u}_{L}}{L}\\ {\sigma}_{a}={E}_{a}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+{\sigma}_{0}={E}_{a}\frac{{u}_{L}}{L}+{\sigma}_{0}\end{array} where {\sigma}_{0}=\frac{{F}_{0}}{{S}_{a}} is the initial prestress in the cable and {u}_{L} is the horizontal displacement to L abscisse. The balance of the plate and cable set writes: {\sigma}_{b}{S}_{b}+{\sigma}_{a}{S}_{a}=0\mathrm{\Rightarrow }{u}_{L}=\frac{-L{F}_{0}}{{E}_{b}eH+{E}_{a}{S}_{a}} Normal stress in the cable is: {N}_{a}={E}_{a}{S}_{a}\frac{{u}_{L}}{F}+{F}_{0}={F}_{0}\frac{{E}_{b}eH}{{E}_{b}eH+{E}_{a}{S}_{a}} The total effort on the vertical section of the concrete plate is: {N}_{b}={E}_{b}eH\frac{{u}_{L}}{L}=-{F}_{0}\frac{{E}_{b}eH}{{E}_{b}eH+{E}_{a}{S}_{a}} The normal stress linear density is derived from the concrete plate {N}_{xx}=-{F}_{0}\frac{{E}_{b}e}{{E}_{b}eH+{E}_{a}{S}_{a}} 2.2 Reference numerical values The numerical reference values are: | {u}_{L}=–1,11013974{.10}^{-5}m | | --- | | {N}_{a}=1,99825153{.10}^{5}N | | {N}_{b}=–1,99825153{.10}^{5}N | | {N}_{xx}=–9,99125765{.10}^{4}N/m | 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The figure below gives a simplified representation of the mesh. The concrete plate is represented by an element DKT, supported by a 4 nodes quadrangle mesh cell. A thickness e=0,6m is affected, as well as a concrete material for which the ELAS (Young's modulus {E}_{b}={3.10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} ) and BPEL_BETON behaviors are defined: the characteristic parameters of this relationship are fixed to 0 because the voltage losses along the prestress cable are neglected. The node \mathit{NB001001} is clamped: DX, DY, DZ, DRX, DRY and DRZ are blocked. The node \mathit{NB002001} is supported bilaterally: DX and DZ are blocked. The cable is represented by 4 elements MECA_BARRE, supported by 4 mesh cells segments at 2 nodes. A straight section area {S}_{a}=1,5{.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} is affected, as well as a steel material for which the ELAS (Young's modulus {E}_{a}=2,1{.10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} ) and BPEL_ACIER behaviors are defined: the characteristic parameters of this relationship are set to 0 (loss of neglected voltage), with the exception of the elastic limit stress for which a null value is unlawful ( {f}_{\mathit{prg}}=1,77{.10}^{9}\mathit{Pa} ). The {F}_{0}={2.10}^{5}N voltage is applied to nodes \mathit{NC001001} and \mathit{NC001005} . This voltage value is consistent with the section and elastic limit values for a prestressed toron cable. The equilibrium state of the plate and cable assembly is calculated in one step, the behaviour being elastic. 3.2 Calculation steps and tested functionalities The main steps in calculation correspond to the features that one wishes to validate: - DEFI_MATERIAU operator: definition of BPEL_BETON and BPEL_ACIER behavior relationships, in the particular case where voltage losses along the prestress cable are neglected (default values of parameters); - DEFI_CABLE_BP operator: determination of a constant voltage profile along the prestress cable, with losses neglected; calculation of the coefficients of kinematic relationships between degrees of freedom of the nodes of the cable and degrees of freedom of the nodes "neighbors" of the concrete plate; - AFFE_CHAR_MECA operator: definition of a RELA_CINE_BP load; - STAT_NON_LINE operator, option COMPORTEMENT: calculation of the equilibrium state taking into account the RELA_CINE_BP type loading. 4 Modelling results A 4.1 Test values 4.1.1 Lineic density of normal stress on vertical section of concrete plate The SIEF_ELNO field values derived from STAT_NON_LINE are compared to the theoretical reference values. The mesh cell \mathit{QD001001} representing the concrete plate is extracted from the SIEF_ELNO field. The component that the tests are about is \mathit{NXX} . v6.03.109 SSNP109 - Prestress cable excreted in a concrete straight beam v6.03.109 SSNP109 - Prestress cable excreted in a concrete straight beam Summary A rectangular straight beam is considered to be concrete, crossed along its length by a steel prestress cable. The cable is straight, parallel to the average fibre of the beam, and passes halfway up the section of the beam, being out of the middle plane. The left section of the beam and the left end of the cable are fixed. The cable is pulled to its right end, in order to prestress the bending-compression beam. The tension losses along the cable are neglected. The purpose of this test case is to validate the equilibrium state calculation method of a prestressed concrete structure compared to an analytical reference solution. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The concrete beam is straight, rectangular section. Its dimensions are: L\times h\times p=10m\times 0,4m\times 0,2m ( y=h/2 ). The cable crosses the beam parallel to the average beam fiber, at mid height. Its eccentricity compared to the average plane is e=0,05m ( z=e ). The right section of the cable is {S}_{a}=1,5{.10}^{-4}{m}^{2} . 1.2 Material properties | Concrete material constituting the beam: | Young's modulus {E}_{b}={3.10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} | | --- | --- | | Steel material constituting the cable: | Young's modulus {E}_{a}=2,1{.10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} | The Poisson's ratio is taken equal to 0 for both materials. So the Poisson effects are cancelled in the y and z directions. The displacements only have components in the (x,z) plane. The loss of tension in the cable is neglected, and the various parameters used for their estimation are set at 0. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The point A located at the bottom of the left edge of the beam, of (\mathrm{0 };–h/\mathrm{2 };0) coordinates, is blocked in translation in all three directions and in rotation around the y axis. The degree of freedom rotational \mathit{DRY} lock involves a zero slope of the average fiber deformity to x=0 . The left end of the cable, (\mathrm{0 };\mathrm{0 };e) coordinates, is blocked in translation in all three directions. At the right end of the cable, (L;\mathrm{0 };e) coordinates, a normal ({F}_{\mathrm{0 }};\mathrm{0 };0) traction force is applied where {F}_{0}={2.10}^{5}N . 2 reference solution The analytical solution reference is determined by beam theory. The clamped-free beam is considered. Geometrical characteristics are those defined in paragraph [§2.1]. The prestressed cable applies a normal (-F;\mathrm{0 };0) compression force and a bending moment (\mathrm{0 };–\mathit{eF};0) to the free end. v6.03.110 SSNP110 - Edge crack in a rectangular, finished elastoplastic plate v6.03.110 SSNP110 - Edge crack in a rectangular, finished elastoplastic plate Summary: This test is a test case in nonlinear fracture mechanics. A finished rectangular plate is considered, cracked and subjected to traction loading. The constitutive law used is an elastoplastic law of Von Mises. This test case includes five modellings in \mathrm{2D} : - A Modelling, in flat stress, under the hypothesis of small deformations (DEFORMATION= 'PETIT' in the STAT_NON_LINE operator); - Model B, removed in V15, allowed, in flat stresses, to study the influence of the consideration of the second order terms of deformations (DEFORMATION= 'GREEN' in STAT_NON_LINE operator) on the calculation of energy release rate G ; - modellings C and D, in flat stress, are designed to test the X-FEM method (non-meshed crack) in non-linear elasticity and elastoplasticity for the calculation of the displacement field; - Modelling E, in flat deformations, validates the calculation of G for the different methods of definition of the hardening curve; - F Modelling is identical to C with quadratic elements. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry C D B A | Length | L=50\mathrm{mm} | | --- | --- | | Width | W=16\mathrm{mm} | | Crack depth | a=6\mathrm{mm} | 1.2 Material properties The material is elastoplastic Von-type. For modellings A to D, there is no hardening. For Modelling E, different hardening laws are compared (linear hardening or power). The Material properties are the following: | Young's modulus | E=2,0601{10}^{5}\mathrm{MPa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio | \nu =0.3 | | Elastic limit | {\sigma}_{y}=808,34\mathrm{MPa} | | Nutrient module | H=0 (modelling A to D) or H=6,867{10}^{4}\mathrm{MPa} (modelling E) | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading For modellings A, B and E, the model is limited to half the structure, with the vertical crack plane being a plane of symmetry. v6.03.112 FORMA10 - Practical work of Advanced Use Training: Loading route v6.03.112 FORMA10 - Practical work of Advanced Use Training: Loading route Summary: This test illustrates, on a material point, the influence of loading path on the response of an elastoplastic behavior. It highlights the effects of discretization in time. It is inspired by the SSNP15 test: a material point, made of a plastic material with linear isotropic nutrification, is subjected to both tensile and shearing effort. The main interest of this test lies in the non-radial character of the load. Model A is the force-based calculation with VMIS_ISOT_LINE behavior and illustrates the influence of coarse-time discretization compared to the solution obtained with a finer time step. From this test we can remember some ideas: - Even outside of perfect elasto-plastic behavior, there may be a limit load. This is the case with all the actual traction curves. The resolution method must then be adapted to the mechanical solution and for example use steering; - Cutting into small load increments is often necessary to properly integrate the behavioral relationship. This can also help convergence, so it is advisable to use the automatic redistribution of the time step; - Linear search can be used to help convergence, as well as automatic subdivision of time step. In case of discharge, elastic prediction is an effective solution.

MACR_ADAP_MAIL does not have regularization processes, so a bad initial mesh will produce, even coupled with an indicator, probably a bad adapted mesh! As in mechanical engineering, l-chaining "thermal operators/MACR_ADAP_MAIL OPTION ‘LIBRE" allows optimal convergence of the mesh . In addition, "jongler" with the components of the thermal indicator and boundary conditions, whether "fictive" or not, may be used to orient the construction of a refined or de-refined mesh by zones (see [§6.3] R4.10.03). 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics The mesh thermal (mechanical) is made with elements type TRIA3 (resp.TRIA6). A isotropic stationary linear thermal calculation (via THER_LINEAIRE in PLAN_DIAG Modelling) is carried out and a linear elasticity calculation (via STAT_NON_LINE in C_PLAN Modelling). Spatial error maps of the indicators are calculated as pure thermal and mechanical residue (ERTH_ELEM and ERME_ELEM). Before this time, the thermal flux and stress field of the Gauss points must be smoothed at nodes (FLUX_ELNO and SIEF_ELNO) and, to post-treat the error card, it must be converted from CHAM_ELEM to element to CHAM_ELEM to nodes to element. The value of the potential deformation energy (POST_ELEM) is also determined. The whole is placed in a loop PYTHON allowing the setting up of a free refinement procedure in nb_calc=2 levels (via MACR_ADAP_MAIL option LIBRE=的RAFF_DERA) coupled on the previously exhumed error card. This process is piloted: - ERTREL component of ERTH_ELEM (relative component of the residual indicator) for the thermal mesh, - NUEST component of ERME_ELEM (relative component of the residual indicator) for the mechanical mesh. With CRIT_RAFF_PE=0.2 and CRIT_DERA_PE=0.1 (we refine 20% of the worst elements and de-refine 10% of the best). After each thermal calculation the temperature field of the thermal mesh is projected to the mechanical mesh (via PROJ_CHAMP). This can be seen in the convergence of energy, the increase in its relative error compared to the errors provided by the indicators (both relative and overall), the variations in the indicators' efficiency indices and their correct verification of the saturation hypothesis. 4.2 Mesh characteristics mesh thermal Initially: 1619 TRIA3, 102 SEG2, 911 nodes After a free refinement: 3088 TRIA3, 134 SEG2, 1681 nodes After two free refinements: 6105 TRIA3, 180 SEG2, 3253 nodes mesh mechanical Initially: 1619 TRIA6, 102 SEG3, 3443 nodes After a free refinement: 2881 TRIA6, 152 SEG3, 6065 nodes After two free refinements: 5319 TRIA6, 180 SEG3, 11097 nodes 4.3 Tested quantities and results The relative error values in potential energy of deformation are tested in relation to reference solution (see [§2.2]). This is done on the initial mesh and after two free refinements. The tests must be multi-platform, the relative tolerance, which is on the initial errors fixed at 10–6%, is voluntarily released on the errors after two refinements: 10–4%. These tests are performed on PYTHON variables (via TEST_FONCTION) previously inserted into ASTER functions (via FORMULE). | Identification | Values Code_Aster | Values of reference | Tolerance | Ratio ratio (in %) | Variable ASTER | Variable PYTHON | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | {E}_{p}(0) | 10.077761% | Idem | 10–6% | 4.79–12 ~ 0% | ERREEN0 | eren0 | | {E}_{p}(2) | 0.459330 % | Idem | 10–4% | –1.03 10–12 ~ 0% | ERREEN2 | eren2 | 4.4 Remarks In thermo-mechanical, different adaptation strategies of mesh offer to the user: - n-adapt the mesh only to a thermal criterion, - idem according to a mechanical criterion, - First adapt according to a thermal criterion, then according to a mechanical criterion (two separate adjustment loops). - adapt together according to a thermal and then mechanical criterion (a loop as in this test case), - adapt according to a thermo-mechanical criterion. In Code_Aster there is no access to explicitly thermomechanical indicators, although mechanical indicators may incidentally have thermal dependence. Depending on the study needs (rather thermal or rather mechanical, converge a mesh overall, better account for some boundary conditions ...) one can put in place in the code, one of the first four strategies. The good practice in a thermo-mechanical calculation is to use the elements {P}_{1} heat-lights and the {P}_{2} mechanically, this leads to the use of two meshes and interpolation of the linear thermal field solution on the quadratic mechanical mesh (via PROJ_CHAMP). However, if you want to work with only one mesh, you can easily decline one of the first four strategies via MACR_ADAP_MAIL's MAJ_CHAM option. This allows, while adapting the mesh to a thermal (mechanical) criterion, to update the complementary, mechanical (thermal) field on the new mesh adapted. 5 Summary of the results A thermo-elastic calculation is made on a cracked metal head in flat stress Modelling (for the mechanical part) and lighted (for the thermal part). In accordance with the "good practices" of the quality of the studies, two distinct meshes are used: linear in thermal and quadratic in mechanical. The thermal calculation on which the mesh {P}_{1} is freely converged with a spatial error d-indicator map coupling (CALC_ERREUR + ‘ERTH_ELEM)/refining/defining (MACR_ADAP_MAIL ‘RAFF_DERA) is performed first (modelization A). In the second model (B), the two meshes are adapted in conjunction with the same process during a chained thermo-mechanical calculation. For the free adaptation of the mechanical mesh, the pure residue indicator ‘ERME_ELEM' is used. The objectives of this test case are multiple, they are: - familiarise yourself and put into practice the two dual problems: calculation of the map d'indicator d'error and adaptation strategies of mesh. On standard cases, but also on pathological cases and for calculation links, - detail the various parameters of the operators involved (CALC_ERREUR, MACR_ADAP_MAIL) and related operators that may be particularly interesting for these issues (INFO_MAILLAGE, MACR_INFO_MAIL, PROJ_CHAMP...), - The aim is to provide "good practice" advice for the quality of studies and the use of tools already available on the subject. The only focus is on the mesh geometry aspects, mesh proper and the d-type of elements finished. The problems of time step, the calibration of numerical parameters and the sensitivity aspects to the data are not discussed here, - d--to illustrate the tremendous potential and facilities that the ASTER/PYTHON coupling allows in the command file of a study (test, loop, display, calculation, personal macro-command, interactivity...).The official test cases being calibrated to work in batch, some of these aspects have therefore been "commentarized" in the command file. D-a-point view computer validation , this test case allows of course to test the non-regression of different mapping couplings d-errors/process refinement-derefining in thermo-mechanical, but also the options of "pre and post-processings" of these calculations (smoothing of stresses and thermal fluxes to nodes, switching from an error by element to an error at nodes by element).

This technique aims to reduce the magnitude of contact pressure. In the case studied here, the pressure is constant over the entire contact surface (note that the Poisson's ratio is zero). Thus, with the discrete formulations ‘CONTRAINTE' and ‘PENALISATION', the solution has non-physical oscillations of the order of 6-7 %.
