v6.04.126 SSNV126 - Anisothermal traction-relaxation test with VENDOCHAB v6.04.126 SSNV126 - Anisothermal traction-relaxation test with VENDOCHAB Summary: The VENDOCHAB model, is based on a formulation proposed by Chaboche. It is a coupled formulation that covers an elasto-viscoplastic law with multiplicative isotropic hardening and isotropic damage kinetics. This law was originally developed to predict the life and cracking of turboreactors' blades and more generally to predict the ruin time of the structures being pressed at high temperatures. This non-linear quasi-static mechanical test validates the VENDOCHAB \mathrm{3D} model in the case of a test piece subjected to an anisothermal uniaxial tensile test. The stress and deformation states are homogeneous in the test piece. This test also validates the explicit and implicit integration of this model. The equations of this coupled formulation are described in the R5.03.15 reference booklet. Two modellings of the test piece are tested with one single element \mathrm{3D} at 8 nodes (HEXA8), the other with a quadrangle at 8 nodes (QUAD8) at AXIS. 1 Reference problem The mechanical problem is the load at the required displacement (in the case of relaxation) of an anisotherm axisymmetric test piece. 1.1 Geometry The geometry of the cylindrical test piece is defined by: - radius: r = 3 mm; - length: l = 60 mm. v6.04.127 SSNV127 - Cylinder in a contact and friction bore v6.04.127 SSNV127 - Cylinder in a contact and friction bore Summary: This problem corresponds to a quasi-static analysis of a mechanical problem with contact and friction. A cylinder is compressed in a cylindrical bore of slightly larger diameter by a concentrated force applied to its axis. This test, called "Klang problem", is widely used in the literature to validate friction contact modellings and has been used by P. Alart and A. Curnier [bib1] to validate their contact and friction finished elements. Three modellings 2D are proposed (D and H with linear elements and F with quadratic elements): The D Modelling test the algorithm of the "PENALISATION" method with master-slave pairing, the penalization is about contact and friction. Modellings F and H test the algorithm of the CONTINUE method with elements quadratic (SEG3) and linear (SEG2) contact, respectively. The results are compared with an analytical solution given by Klang [bib2]. Instead of reproducing this relatively complicated analytical solution we will use the values of pressures obtained from it [bib1]. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry | | | | | --- | --- | --- | Cylinder radius: r=5.999\mathrm{cm} . Rim of the bore: R=6.\mathrm{cm} . Position of reference points on the contact surface: one point every three degrees d-angle from the bottom, up to 60°. 1.2 Material properties Cylinder and bore: | Young's modulus: | E=2.1{10}^{11}N/{m}^{2} | | | --- | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio: | \nu =0.3 | | | Friction coefficient: | \mu =0.4 | | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The massif containing the bore is supposed to be infinite, its movements will be blocked (following x and y) on a concentric circle with the bore. The cylinder is subjected to a Q distributed force according to the (z) thickness: Q=–1875{10}^{3}N/m . This force is applied in one increment. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is analytical [bib2]. 2.2 Baseline Prediction on contact area: 60 degrees. Prediction on the beginning of the slip zone: 26.2 degrees. On A , B , C and D , a relative error is less than 1% compared to the GRECO results. On the other hand, for point E , the relative error of about 2.5% remains acceptable. The method of penalisation is rather rapid, as the use of point is not obvious, since the convergence and quality of the results obtained are conditioned by the coefficient of penalisation. Qualitatively visible point: - in 2D, there was a positive effect on the results of the quadratic mesh compared to the linear mesh (see modellings A and B), - In 3D, we find that calculations with mesh quadratic do not improve the results. This is explained by the fact that we have reduced the number of mesh cells from the linear mesh by 50% to have an equivalent number of nodes. In all cases only the use of mesh cells TETRA10 or HEXA27 is recommended in discrete formulation, the mesh cells HEXA20 need to be linearized (they lose their interest). In the case of L-modelling, inclined plate, there is good convergence and satisfactory results. The ADAPTATION='CYCLAGE' or ADAPTATION='TOUT' method allows for a better convergence of the cases of razing pressures. Finally, for the continuous method (modellings M, N, P, Q, R, V, W and X), results are obtained in 3D with relative errors slightly greater than those obtained by the penalized methods. These errors are derived from the blocking in the direction DZ which is not complete in continuous formulation in modellings which do not use the SANS_GROUP_NO_FR feature of excluding the friction nodes.

v6.04.133 SSNV133 - Uniaxial compression-traction. Mixed scrubbing v6.04.133 SSNV133 - Uniaxial compression-traction. Mixed scrubbing Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the VMIS_ECMI_TRAC and VMIS_ECMI_LINE elastoplastic behaviors, which combine isotropic (linear or given by a tensile curve) hardening with linear kinematic hardening. Geometric and mechanical data allow to be in a uniaxial situation (uniform constraints, a single non-zero component). The reference solution is simple, analytical. This test simply allows to verify that the integration of the behavior model is correct. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 1.2 Material properties Constitutive law elastoplastic with mixed nutrification (linear isotrop and linear kinematic). 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The plate is blocked next along the side [3,4], following along the side [1.3] while being subject to a displacement imposed in y : along the side [1,2]. The loading route is as follows: | t | (\mathrm{mm}) | | --- | --- | | 1 | 10–3 | | 2 | 4.5d–3 | | 3 | 0.1d–3 | | 4 | –2. 10–3 | 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is obtained by analytical calculation. The {u}_{y}^{D} displacement is immediately used to provide {\epsilon}_{yy}=\frac{{u}_{y}^{D}}{1} deformation. Only this component (corresponding to the non-zero component of the stress tensor) is of interest to us here. v6.04.137 SSNV137 - Prestress cable in a concrete straight beam v6.04.137 SSNV137 - Prestress cable in a concrete straight beam Summary A square cross sectioned straight beam is considered to be concrete, crossed along its length by a steel prestress cable. In the resting state, the cable is parallel to the average fiber of the beam and out of the center of the two main planes. The beam and cable are clamped-free. The cable is pulled at its free end, in order to prestress the beam in bending-compression. The tension losses along the cable are neglected. The purpose of this test case is to validate the equilibrium state calculation method of a prestressed concrete structure, when this structure is modelled by elements 3D, associated with the base elements representing the prestress cable. The specific features to be tested are: - DEFI_CABLE_BP operator: determination of kinematic relationships between degrees of freedom of nodes of a cable and degrees of freedom of nodes "neighbors" of a concrete structure modelled by elements 3D; - STAT_NON_LINE operator, option COMPORTEMENT: calculation of the equilibrium state. The results obtained are validated by comparison with a reference analytical solution. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The concrete beam is straight, square section. Its dimensions are L\times a\times a=3m\times 0,4m\times 0,4m . The cable crosses the beam parallel to the medium fiber and is eccentricated from the two main planes. The eccentricities in the y and z directions are valid respectively {e}_{y}=-0,12m et {e}_{z}=-0,16m . The right section of the cable is {S}_{a}=2,5{.10}^{-3}{m}^{2} . z y a x a L z ey y ez a a 1.2 Material properties Concrete material forming beam: Young's modulus {E}_{b}=4,5{.10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} Steel material making up cable: Young's modulus {E}_{a}=1,85{.10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} The Poisson's ratio is taken equal to 0 for both materials, so the Poisson effects are cancelled in the y and z directions. The loss of tension in the cable is neglected, and the various parameters used for their estimation are set at 0. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The nodes of the beam on the x=0 side is blocked in translation in three directions. Among these nodes are the "neighbors" of the node left end of the cable, which is therefore blocked in translation by kinematic relations. Therefore, you should not impose additional boundary conditions in this node, which would be redundant with kinematic relations and make it impossible to resolve in motion (synthetic matrix). The node right end of the cable is applied a normal ({F}_{\mathrm{0 }};\mathrm{0 };0) traction force, with {F}_{0}={10}^{6}N . 2 reference solution The analytical solution reference is determined by beam theory. Interest: Test the elements non-linear geometric finished COQUE_3D (modellings A and C), DKT (modellings E and F), DKTG (modellings G and H) and POU_D_T_GD (modelization B) using the \mathrm{3D} GROT_GDEP large rotation update algorithm in STAT_NON_LINE. Also compare the results to POU_D_TGM multifibre beam POU_D_TGM which allows to process large rotations under the hypothesis of small loading increments. Note: This test is the test case plate version of the SSNL103 beam . The mechanical characteristics have been modified to support superfacial modelling. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Clamped rectangular plate in {P}_{1}{P}_{4} and {P}_{1}{P}_{4} subjected to a linear torque in {P}_{2}{P}_{3} : m=-{\mathrm{me}}_{y};m>0 1.2 Material properties and section characteristics Elastic behaviour: E=12\times {10}^{6}\text{Pa};\nu =0 The fact that the Poisson's ratio ( \nu ) is zero makes the plate solution identical to the beam solution. {I}_{y} is the inertia of the section with a beam model: {I}_{y}=\frac{b{h}^{3}}{12}=\frac{1}{12}\times {10}^{-3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading Clamped support {P}_{1}{P}_{4} . The successive states of equilibrium under the load of the {P}_{2}{P}_{3} linear torque are investigated: m(t)=100t ; t pseudo-time. Particular attention is paid to horizontal and vertical displacements and rotation of the {P}_{2}{P}_{3} line. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution With a beam kinematic and a model in resulting effort, the curvature (in large rotations) of the cantilever submitted to bending moment M=\text{mb} is, with the previous numerical data: \frac{d\theta }{\text{dx}}=\frac{\text{mb}}{{\text{EI}}_{y}}=\frac{t}{L} This is the solution of Euler. 2.2 Baseline Depending on the solution d-Euler, the deformed is a circle arc. At {P}_{2}{P}_{3} (x=L) section, the rotation is: \theta (x=L)=t. The value of the angle of rotation reached is 86 degrees. 12 Summary of the results - modellings COQUE_3D, POU_D_T_GD et POU_D_TGM There are convergence difficulties which disappear by multiplying the thickness by 3 or 4. It is necessary to increase the value of the COEF_RIGI_DRZ which attributes stiffness around the normal elements shell which is by default {10}^{-5} (the smallest bending rigidity around the directions in the hull plane) so that it can increase the value of the angle of rotation that can be reached. Values of this coefficient up to {10}^{-3} remain lawful. During Newton iterations, membrane deformations appear and cancel at convergence. The convergence speeds of NEWTON algorithms are comparable for modellings POU_D_T_GD and COQUE_3D. The convergence rate of NEWTON algorithm in the case of POU_D_TGM Modelling is much lower than the other two because this Modelling requires in this case very small loading increments to describe the geometric transformation well and remain in the hypothesis of small deformations. The time cost \text{CPU} sss is felt since the calculation is about 10 times longer than that of POU_D_T_GD Modelling. Of course the multifibre element has the advantage of being able to treat several types of behavior and not only an elastic behavior like the element POU_D_T_GD. If the required precision is not of the order of 1%, one can afford to use less time step. Moreover, it is important for a problem like this, where the inertia of the section plays a leading role, to ensure that the section is discretized with enough fibers when POU_D_TGM is used, to obtain inertia as close to the theoretical value as possible (which is why we have meshed with nearly 40 fibers in thickness). - modellings DKT et DKTG DKT Modelling allows to reach a large 300° rotation angle , more important than that obtained with DKTG 86° Modelling . Compared to the analytical solution, the difference maximum on the move is 2% for modellings DKT and DKTG

v6.04.139 SSNV139 - Bias plate v6.04.139 SSNV139 - Bias plate Summary: Almost static calculation of a horizontal clamped elastic plate on one side and subjected to a vertical concentrated force. The results are compared with those of SAMCEF software. The advantage is to test COQUE_3D's finite element in non-linear geometric COQUE_3D using the GROT_GDEP large 3D rotation update algorithm in STAT_NON_LINE. Rotations are 3D and slightly above 1 radian. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Clamped {P}_{1}{P}_{2} -shaped and P -concentrated vertical force: f=-F{e}_{z} ; F>0 1.2 Material properties Elastic behaviour: E=2100000 ; \nu =\frac{1}{3} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Clamped support in {P}_{1}{P}_{2} . The successive states of equilibrium under load consisting of force are sought: F(t)=t P , t being the pseudo time. Particular attention is paid to horizontal and vertical P displacements. 2 reference solution This [bib4] solution is the one obtained with SAMCEF [bib1] software. The Modelling is based on a resulting stress hull theory with a corotational [bib3] formulation and DSQ [bib2] discretization. v6.04.143 SSNV143 - Biaxial Traction with constitutive law BETON_DOUBLE_DP v6.04.143 SSNV143 - Biaxial Traction with constitutive law BETON_DOUBLE_DP Summary: This validation case is intended to verify the \mathrm{3D} BETON_DOUBLE_DP model of behaviour formulated in the thermoplasticity framework, for the description of the nonlinear behaviour of concrete, in traction, and in compression, with the consideration of irreversible variations in the thermal and mechanical characteristics of concrete, particularly sensitive at high temperature. The description of cracking is treated in the plasticity framework, using energy equivalence, by identifying the density of cracking energy in I mode, with the plastic work of an equivalent homogeneous medium, where plastic deformation is evenly distributed, in an "elementary" zone. This approach preserves the continuity of model formulation, over the whole of its behavior, and helps to avoid the possible numerical difficulties when changing the material's condition. The pathological sensitivity of the digital solution to spatial discretization (mesh), generated by the introduction of a softening behaviour of concrete in traction and compression, is partially resolved by introducing a cracking or breaking energy, depending on a characteristic length {l}_{c} , related to the size of the elements. The test case consists of two modellings 3D, the load consists of a load followed by a discharge. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is a cube with 8 nodes, two sides of which have a normal zero displacement, and the two opposite sides have a normal imposed displacement, different from each other from a coefficient 2. The cube makes 1\mathrm{mm} sidewise. The test cases are composed of a load, followed by a discharge. In Modelling A, the cube is oriented according to the \mathit{Oxyz} marker. In Modelling B, it is turned from 30° around the \mathrm{Oy} axis. Model A Model B {U}_{2}={\mathrm{2.U}}_{1} 1.2 Material properties In order to test the evolution of mechanical characteristics irreversibly with temperature, a decreasing temperature field is applied. Some variables depend on temperature, others on drying. The thermal deformations will thus be equal and opposed to the deformations of desiccation withdrawal. The following load involves changes in the linearised equation system. The equation system solved by NEWTON method is non-symmetric. The stiffness tangent matrix (internal forces) and the contribution of pressure forces following the deformed structure are nonsymmetric. This Modelling allows testing COQUE_3D finite geometric nonlinear objects using the update algorithm of the large 3D rotations GROT_GDEP in STAT_NON_LINE in the presence of a following type pressure. The reference solution is obtained by elements finished SAMCEF software. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry L = 10 Lengths are given in metres. Torispheric tank Summary This test enables operators to qualify for regularised limit analysis. The limit load is calculated by a kinematic approach regulated by the Norton-Hoff-Friaâ method. Compared to the A index of this document, it should be noted that the calculation method has been modified in the Code_Aster which no longer uses Norton-Hoff material but uses the more general resolution with incompressible elements. The Reference problem is the result of a European benchmark carried out in the framework of a Brite EuRam BE97-4547 project "LISA" in 1998. A axisymmetric tank with a torispheric background is considered. The constituent material checks the vonMises criterion and the structure is subjected to internal pressure. The structure is modelled by incompressible elements. The resolution by the regularised method of Norton-Hoff-Friaâ is performed in the STAT_NON_LINE command. An post-processing in the POST_ELEM command allows the upper and lower terminal estimates of the limit load to be obtained. The reference solution is digital and the results are in perfect agreement with the reference values. Some implementation details of this test case are presented in the u2.05.04 Help Use document. 1 Reference problem The test is the test case LA6 of a benchmark of the European project Brite EuRam BE97-4547 "LISA" studied by three bodies: - EDF (former Norton-Hoff method with three values of the regularization parameter: Norton-Hoff n coefficient); - LTAS in Liège (the regularised kinematic method of the university software dedicated " ELSA "; - ForschungZentrum by Jülich (static method approached by elements finished on displacement, reduced representation of auto-contraint fields and algorithm of optimization of code Permas ). An axisymmetric tank with a torispheric background subject to internal pressure is considered. The same mesh is used by the three participating organisms. It contains two elements Q8 in thickness, and in all there are 34 elements, and 141 nodes. The constituent material is homogeneous and checks the von Mises criterion with the {\sigma}_{y} yield limit ( {\sigma}_{y} ) for the threshold. EDF LISA results: mesh initial and deformed Norton-Hoff coefficient n =31 The calculation of the limit load by the Norton-Hoff-Friaâ method is detailed in reference document r7.07.01. Let us briefly remember that the aim is to look for the {\lambda}_{\lim} limit load, for which the structure, consisting of a material of the perfect elastoplastic type at the threshold of von Mises, can support {\lambda}_{\lim}F surface loads and {\lambda}_{\lim}f volume loads to which one can possibly add constant loads ( {F}_{0} and {f}_{0} ). Code_aster allows two parameters to be calculated for each moment of the calculation, i.e. for increasingly low regularizations: - An estimate of an upper limit of the load: {\widehat{\lambda}}_{m}=\underset{\Omega}{\int}{\sigma}_{y}\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}\epsilon ({u}_{m})\cdot \epsilon ({u}_{m})}d\Omega -{L}_{0}({u}_{m}) - and, in the absence of constant loading, an estimate of a lower terminal {\underline{\lambda}}_{m} : {\underline{\lambda}}_{m}=\underset{\Omega}{\int}\frac{A(m)}{m}\cdot {(\sqrt{\varepsilon ({u}_{m})\cdot \varepsilon ({u}_{m})})}^{m}d\Omega \cdot {(\underset{x\in \Omega }{\text{Sup}}(\sqrt{\frac{\frac{3}{2}{\sigma}^{D}({u}_{m})\cdot {\sigma}^{D}({u}_{m})}{{\sigma}_{y}}}))}^{-1}\le {\stackrel{ˆ}{\lambda}}_{m} If a constant load is present, the constant load power is provided in the speed field solution of the problem. The stress deviator checks the behavioral relationship of Norton-Hoff: {\sigma}^{D}(u)=A(m).{(\sqrt{{\epsilon}^{D}(u).{\epsilon}^{D}(u)})}^{m-2}.{\epsilon}^{D}(u) with \text{tr}\varepsilon (u)=0 , and A(m)={k}^{1-m}{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)}^{m/2}{{\sigma}_{y}}^{m} . 1.1 Data for modelling | Geometry | The axisymmetric tank with a torispheric background has the following characteristics: internal radius of the cylindrical part: 49\mathrm{mm} ; thickness: 2\mathrm{mm} ; radius of the spherical part with l-apex: 98\mathrm{mm} ; radius of the connecting torus: 20\mathrm{mm} . | | --- | --- | | Material properties | Elasticity limit: {\sigma}_{y}=100\mathrm{MPa} | | boundary conditions | \mathrm{DY} zero axial displacement on the {\mathrm{BORD}}_{\mathrm{INF}} end of the cylindrical part (symmetry conditions) | | Charges | 1\mathrm{MPa} internal pressure applied to internal wall {B}_{D} | 1.2 Baseline For this test case, no analytical results are available, but only numerical values from the LISA benchmark calculations and v6.04.146-tab-results-benchmark-lisa. | Modelling | Estimated higher value | Estimated lower value | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | EDF | m=1,0476 | n=21 | t=2,3222 | 3,9514 | 3,6049 | | m=1,0322 | n=31 | t=2,4914 | 3,9456 | 3,7090 | | | m=1,0141 | n=71 | t=2,8513 | 3,9404 | 3,8372 | | | m=1,0099 | n=101 1 | t=3,0043 2 | 3,9396 | 3,8673 | | | Univ. of Liège/LTAS | 3,931 | None | | | | | FZJ Research Centre | None | 3,997 | | | | The Law Regularization Coefficient of Norton-Hoff n={(m-1)}^{-1} (former method d m=1+{10}^{1-t} , the ‘snapshots' parameter t was not explicit in this old method, and here we add to compare with calculations in sections 4.2 and 4.3. 2 Modelling A The moment list is used to control the Norton-Hoff regularization method via an t coefficient ( m=1+{10}^{1-t} ), not the loading evolution as in an ordinary calculation. To perform a calculation in code_aster in limit analysis with the Norton-Hoff-Friaâ regularization method with the vonMises resistance criterion, it is necessary to: - define the 2D (plane or axis) or 3D model with the elements near-incompressible finished, modellings 3D_INCO_UPG, D_PLAN_INCO_UPG, or AXIS_INCO_UPG; - ensure the incompressibility condition: GONF=0 in AFFE_CHAR_MECA; - define only the material characteristic {s}_{y} , the limit load being independent of E and \nu ; - define the permanent load and the one that is set by \lambda ; - define the time-based discretization (in practice between {t}_{min}=1 and {t}_{max}=2 to 5 ); - perform a nonlinear calculation with the NORTON_HOFF behavioral relationship with the STAT_NON_LINE u4.51.03 command, and the ANA_LIM control. The calculation was conducted up to the instant t=2s . The regularised kinematic methods of EDF and the University of Liège give very similar results (difference less than 1% at t=2s ). v6.04.150 SSNV150 - Triaxial Traction with constitutive law BETON_DOUBLE_DP v6.04.150 SSNV150 - Triaxial Traction with constitutive law BETON_DOUBLE_DP Summary This validation case is intended to verify the 3D BETON_DOUBLE_DP behavior model formulated in the thermoplasticity framework, for the description of the nonlinear behaviour of concrete, in traction, and in compression, with consideration for irreversible variations in the thermal and mechanical characteristics of concrete, particularly sensitive at high temperature. The description of cracking is treated in the plasticity framework, using energy equivalence, by identifying the density of cracking energy in I mode, with the plastic work of an equivalent homogeneous medium, where plastic deformation is evenly distributed, in an "elementary" zone. This approach preserves the continuity of model formulation, over the whole of its behavior, and helps to avoid the possible numerical difficulties when changing the material's condition. The pathological sensitivity of the numerical solution to spatial discretization (mesh), generated by the introduction of a softening behaviour of concrete in traction and compression, is partially resolved by introducing a cracking or breaking energy, depending on a characteristic length {l}_{c} , related to the size of the elements. The resolution of the model's constituent equations is performed by an implicit schema. This is a cube with 8 nodes subjected to a triaxial traction, while on the required displacement. This load leads to the particular case of a hydrostatic stress state, solved by projection at the top of the tensile cone, when placed in an equivalent stress/hydrostatic stress diagram. It is a test case with analytical solution. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is a cube with 8 nodes, three sides of which have a normal zero displacement and the three opposite sides a normal imposed and identical displacement. The cube is 1\mathit{mm} sidewise. In Modelling A, the cube is oriented according to the \mathit{Oxyz} marker. Model A {U}_{2}={U}_{1}={U}_{3} 1.2 Material properties To test the irreversible evolution of mechanical characteristics with temperature, a decreasing temperature field is applied. Some variables depend on temperature, others on drying. Finally, a non-zero desiccation removal coefficient, equal to the coefficient of thermal expansion, is applied to test the "computer" operation. The thermal deformations will thus be equal and opposed to the desiccation withdrawal deformations. These dependencies only occur for purely computer-based verifications, the mechanical characteristics can be considered constant. v6.04.151 SSNV151 - Traction / Compression with constitutive law BETON_DOUBLE_DP v6.04.151 SSNV151 - Traction / Compression with constitutive law BETON_DOUBLE_DP Summary This validation case is intended to verify the \mathrm{3D} BETON_DOUBLE_DP behavior model formulated in the thermoplasticity framework, for the description of the nonlinear behaviour of concrete in traction and compression, with consideration given to irreversible variations in the thermal and mechanical characteristics of concrete, particularly sensitive at high temperature. The description of cracking is treated as part of plasticity, using an energy equivalence, by identifying the density of cracking energy in I mode, with the plastic work of an equivalent homogeneous medium, where plastic deformation is evenly distributed in an "elementary" zone. This approach preserves the continuity of model formulation, over the whole of its behavior, and helps to avoid possible numerical difficulties when changing the material's condition. The pathological sensitivity of the digital solution to spatial discretization (mesh), generated by the introduction of a softening behaviour of concrete in traction and compression, is partially resolved by introducing a cracking or breaking energy, depending on a characteristic length {l}_{c} , related to the size of the elements. The solution of the model's constituent equations is made by an implicit schema. This is a cube with 8 nodes subjected to uniaxial compression, while on the move imposed, to which is added a two-axial traction when a high tensile hardening has been achieved. This load leads to the particular case of a state of hydrostatic stress, solved by projection at the top of the tensile cone, when placed in an equivalent stress diagram/hydrostatic stress. It is a test case non-regression. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is a cube with 8 nodes, three faces of which have a normal zero displacement, and the three opposite sides have a normal imposed and identical displacement. The cube is 1\mathrm{mm} sidewise. In Modelling A, the cube is oriented according to the \mathrm{Oxyz} marker. Model A 1.2 Material properties To test the implantation of thermal expansion and desiccation removal, a variable temperature field and drying field are imposed so that the deformations generated by both phenomena are compensated, while considering that the coefficients of thermal expansion and desiccation removal are equal. The values related to drying have no physical meaning, the test is of this point of view, purely computer-based. Normal changes from one mesh cell to another. This discontinuity causes pairing problems that have a great influence on the calculation. Among these problems, we find the problem of dissymmetrization, i.e. finding results that do not respect the symmetry of the problem. For this test case, the problem is perfectly symmetrical (geometrics, boundary conditions and loading) on the y axis. Without normal regularization a dissymmetry appears on the x axis. Indeed, the horizontal displacements of the A , B and C points on the y axis then have nonzero values that do not respect the overall symmetry of the problem. With normal adjustment, the solution obtained using the continuous method, respects perfectly the symmetry. It should be noted, however, that the gibi mesh, used in this test case, does not give a perfectly symmetrical mesh and that rounding problems very slightly damage the quality of the solution. In Modelling A, the problem is dealt with with the CONTINUE method (use of DEFI_CONTACT ). Integration is done at the nodes level of the mesh. Particular attention should be paid to the choice of potential contact areas in these problems of non-plane surfaces. In model B, the problem is treated with an increased Lagrangian approach (use of DEFI_CONT ).

This test involves a cube with a flat central circular crack, subjected to an inclined force relative to the crack plane. For each model, SIF s are evaluated by CALC_G option G and K. The numerical values are compared with the analytical values. In Modelling A, the mesh used is a free mesh generated with ZCracks. In Modelling B, the mesh is set (raising around the crack front). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The crack is circular (penny shape crack) of a=0,2m radius in the \mathit{OXY} plane. The side of the cube is L=2m=10a length. Thus, the crack is considered to be in an infinite medium. Modelling C: Clean creep test with BETON_UMLV model and C_PLAN Modelling. Modelling D: Clean creep test with BETON_BURGER and 3D Modelling. Modelling E: Clean creep test with BETON_BURGER model and AXIS Modelling. v6.04.164 SSNV164 - Tensioning of prestress cables in a 3D beam v6.04.164 SSNV164 - Tensioning of prestress cables in a 3D beam Summary A reinforced concrete beam of square cross section, consisting of two 10 metre long sections, having one and four square metres of cross section respectively, is considered. The beam is vertical, the lowest section at the bottom. It is clamped at its base, and contains 5 straight prestress cables. The phase of prestressing, i.e. the successive tensioning of the various cables, is tested here. The specific features to be tested are: - DEFI_CABLE_BP operator: determination of kinematic relationships between degrees of freedom of nodes of a cable and degrees of freedom of nodes "neighbors" of a concrete structure modelled by elements \mathrm{3D} and calculation of voltages in a cable under friction effect and recoil anchoring, - AFFE_CHAR_MECA operator associated with keyword RELA_CINE_BP, - CALC_PRECONT operator: powering prestress cables with the standard NEWTON method or with the IMPLEX method. - CALC_PRECONT operator: tensioning prestress cables modelled by elements BARRE with elements CABLE_GAINE in the model and vice versa (modelling C and D). The results obtained are validated by comparison with the CASTEM 2000 calculation code. B Modelling allows more specific validation of the use of keyword CONE in DEFI_CABLE_BP. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A reinforced concrete beam of square cross section, consisting of two 10 metre long sections, having one and four square metres of cross section respectively, is considered. The beam is vertical, the lowest section at the bottom. It is clamped at its base, and contains 5 straight prestress cables. The five cables that cross the length of the beam are located as shown below: 2 Figure 1.1-a: Positioning of cables in beam The section of each cable is 25{\mathrm{cm}}^{2} . 1.2 Material properties Concrete material constituting the beam: | Young's modulus : | {E}_{b}=4.{10}^{5}\mathrm{MPa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio : | \nu =0,2 | | density: | \rho =2500\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} | | Tensile limit | {\sigma}_{Y}=\mathrm{3MPa} | | Nutrient module | {E}_{\mathrm{bT}}=-10000\mathrm{MPa} | Steel material constituting the cable: | Young's modulus : | {E}_{c}=1,93{10}^{5}\mathrm{MPa} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio : | \nu =0,3 | | density: | \rho =7850\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} | | Tensile limit | {\sigma}_{Y}=\mathrm{19400MPa} | | Nutrient module | {E}_{\mathrm{bT}}=10E-3\mathrm{MPa} | Characteristics concerning the tensioning of cables: - anchoring back: 1\mathrm{mm} - linear friction coefficient: 0,0015{m}^{-1} - tension force at the end of a cable: 3,75{10}^{6}N - Age of de-offrage 150 days - first cable voltageing age: 300 days 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The base of the beam is blocked in the Z direction. The two translation movements relative to \mathrm{OX} and \mathrm{OY} are blocked as well as the rotational movement around \mathrm{OZ} . The loading sequence is as follows: - 300 days, tensioning of 2 cables (1 and 2) at the lower end, - 450 days, tensioning of 2 additional cables (3 and 4) at the lower end, - 600 days, the last cable (5) is energized by both ends. The beam is obviously subject to gravity. 2 reference solution The reference solution was obtained by the CEA with CASTEM 2000, with a mesh containing 2080 elements cubics with 20 nodes and 100 elements cable. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The concrete beam is represented by 2080 elements MECA_HEXA8, supported by as many mesh cells hexahedrons at 8 nodes. The non-zero values for BPEL_ACIER concern friction ( \mathrm{FROT}\text{\_}\mathrm{LINE}=1,5{10}^{-3}{m}^{-1} ) and the yield limit since a zero value is unlawful ( \mathrm{SY}=1,94{10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} ). The cable radius is 2,8209{10}^{-2}m . The blocked degrees of freedom are: \mathrm{DZ} for the lower side \mathrm{DX} and \mathrm{DY} for points on the beam symmetry axis \mathrm{DX} for point (0.50.0.) and \mathrm{DY} for point (–0.50.0.) v6.04.165 FORMA42 - Practical work of the Civil Engineering training: tensioning a variable section prestressed beam v6.04.165 FORMA42 - Practical work of the Civil Engineering training: tensioning a variable section prestressed beam Summary: The \mathrm{3D} test is designed to implement the two techniques for tensioning prestress cables and compare the solutions thus obtained. In A Modelling all cables are energized simultaneously from the beginning of the calculation using simply the STAT_NON_LINE operator. In modellings B and C the idea is to use the CALC_PRECONT operator. In the first case, all cables are energized simultaneously, in the second case, the phase of prestressing is modelled. The objective of the TP is to implement these different strategies and to compare the differences in results achieved in each case. In all cases, restraints conditions between the cable and the concrete and the BPEL91 voltage calculation are performed using the DEFI_CABLE_BP operator. When the TP is done in limited time, it can be wise to start from A Modelling, and only to achieve modellings B and C . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A reinforced concrete beam of square cross section, consisting of two 10 metre long sections, having one and four square metres of cross section respectively, is considered. The beam is vertical, the lowest section at the bottom. It is clamped at its base, and contains 5 straight prestressed cables. Furthermore, when combining this calculation of the tension of the cable with a nonlinear calculation, it is important not to accumulate losses. Thus, if concrete is modelled by means of a visco-elastic law, it is not necessary to take into account the losses by creep of concrete in the calculation of the tension of the cable. v6.04.166 SSNV166 – Cylinder cracked under multiple loadings v6.04.166 SSNV166 – Cylinder cracked under multiple loadings Summary The purpose of this test is to calculate stress intensity factors along the crack bottom for a cylinder with axisymmetric crack. The influence of the degree of elements and the type of the method is studied through various modellings. 1. A Modelling tests \mathrm{K1} and \mathrm{K3} with a mesh linear \mathrm{3D} and a elements classic finished method ( \mathrm{FEM} ). 2. B Modelling tests \mathrm{K1} and \mathrm{K3} with a mesh quadratic \mathrm{3D} (elements from Barsium) around the crack bottom and an \mathrm{FEM} . 3. C Modelling tests \mathrm{K1} and \mathrm{K3} with a mesh linear \mathrm{3D} with a classic resolution but intensity factor extraction based on energy calculation. In addition, for each model, various cases of loadings are studied: - traction (solicitation in I mode); - twist (solicitation in \mathrm{III} mode); - flexion (opening one side, closing the other) with and without taking into account the contact. Tensile and twisting cases do not involve contact. Although symmetries exist in some cases (axisymetry for case 1, plane symmetry for the 2nd) the representation is made in \mathrm{3D} to make the test generalizable under multiple loading. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The crack is a circular crown in an orthogonal plane at the cylinder axis [Figure 1.1-a None None ]. The parameters a and b determine the radius of the cylinder and the depth of the crack. [Figure 1.1-b] is a cut of the cylinder in the crack plane (plane \mathrm{Oyz} ). To make the medium considered infinite, the height of the cylinder is h=10b . The load 1 test \mathrm{K1} and \mathrm{K3} . The load 2 test \mathrm{K2} without taking into account the contact. The 3 load tests \mathrm{K2} with the contact factor. \mathrm{K1} and \mathrm{K3} are expected to be constant along the crack bottom and \mathrm{K2} to vary. Case 1: Traction and Torsion Tensile induces an opening in mode 1. \mathrm{K1} is given by the following formula: {K}_{I}=\frac{P}{\pi {a}^{2}}\sqrt{\pi a}{F}_{1}(a/b) where P is the force applied to the upper and lower faces and {F}_{1} is a given function [Figure 2.1-a]. v6.04.173 SSNV173 – Bar cracked with X-FEM v6.04.173 SSNV173 – Bar cracked with X-FEM Summary The purpose of this test is to validate two aspects of the elementary calculation in the X-FEM R7.02.12: - integration of a discontinuous quantity by sub-cutting of the element, - The enrichment of form functions by the Heaviside function. This test involves a parallelepipedic bar cracked all over its section (we will then speak of an interface), subject to a forced displacement, which results in the separation of both parts of the structure. The influence of mesh and boundary conditions is also studied. \mathrm{2D} also studies the case of a plate. 1 Reference problem 1.1 3D geometry The structure is a straight parallelepipeda with square base. The dimensions of the bar (see []) are: \mathit{LX}=5m , \mathit{LY}=5m and \mathit{LZ}=25m . The crack (or rather the interface) is introduced by level set functions directly into the command file using DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08 operator. The interface is present in the middle of the structure through its representation by a level set \mathit{LSN} (see []) equation: \mathrm{LSN} (for interface plane): Z-\frac{\mathit{LZ}}{2} Figure 1.1-b Figure 1.1-a : Bar Geometry and Interface Positioning 1.2 2D geometry The structure is a rectangle. The dimensions of the bar (see []) are: \mathrm{LX}=1m , \mathrm{LY}=5m . The interface is introduced by a level set function directly into the command file using the DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08 operator. The interface is present in the middle of the structure through its representation by a level set \mathrm{LSN} (see []) equation: \mathrm{LSN} (for interface layout): Y-\frac{\mathrm{LY}}{2} Figure 1.2-a : Plate Geometry and Interface Positioning 1.3 Material properties Young's modulus: E=205000\mathit{MPa} Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.3 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads The nodes on the lower side of the bar is clamped and a displacement is imposed on the upper side. Here we want to show the possibility of separating a finite element in half with X-FEM. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Mesh characteristics The structure is meshed by a single mesh cell of the HEXA8 type. The interface is present within this element via the level sets. 2.2 boundary conditions Remember that moving under X-FEM is the sum of continuous displacement and discontinuous displacement. In the case of an interface, without crack bottom, the displacement approximation is written as follows: {u}^{h}(x)=\sum_{i\in {N}_{n}(x)}{a}_{i}{\varphi}_{i}(x)+\sum_{j\in {N}_{n}(x)\cap {K}_{+}}{b}_{j}{\varphi}_{j}(x)\left(\text{-2}{\chi }_{-}\left(\mathit{lsn}(x)\right)\right)+\sum_{j\in {N}_{n}(x)\cap {K}_{-}}{b}_{j}{\varphi}_{j}(x)\left(2{\chi }_{+}\left(\mathit{lsn}(x)\right)\right) Où: {a}_{i} and {b}_{i} are the degrees of freedom moving node i , {\phi }_{i} the form functions associated with node i , {N}_{n}(x) is all nodes with point x in its support, {K}_{-} is all nodes located in the \mathit{lsn}(x) 0 domain, and the support is completely cut by the interface, {\chi }_{-}(x) is a domain characteristic function defined by {\chi }_{-}(x)=\lbrace \begin{array}{c}1\text{si}x<0\\ 0\text{si}x\ge 0\end{array} , {\chi }_{+}(x) is a domain characteristic function defined by {\chi }_{+}(x)=\lbrace \begin{array}{c}0\text{si}x<0\\ 1\text{si}x\ge 0\end{array} , \mathit{lsn}(x) is the normal level-set value at point x For more details, refer to the X-FEM R7.02.12 reference documentation. Since nodes near the interface, i.e. the 8 nodes of mesh are enriched by additional degrees of freedom, boundary conditions write a little differently. This is related to the enrichment of R7.02.12 classic form functions by {\chi }_{-}(x) and {\chi }_{+}(x) domain characteristic functions. Imposing a zero displacement on the nodes of the lower side is like writing a linear relationship between the degrees of freedom. For each node, you impose {a}_{\mathit{ix}}=0 (idem following y and z ) when the interface is not in line with the nodes of the mesh. However, if the interface was nodes compliant, imposing zero displacement on the interface, also underlies a hypothesis regarding the displacement jump through the interface. This introduces an additional relationship due to the continuity/saut displacement. The following condition should be imposed on degrees of freedom discontinuity {\mathrm{2b}}_{\mathit{ix}}=\Delta u=0 . For the nodes on the top side, a z displacement is required, and zero in the other two directions, i.e. {a}_{\mathit{ix}}=0 , {a}_{\mathit{iy}}=0 and {a}_{\mathit{iz}}={10}^{-6} . These relationships are imposed automatically when keyword DDL_IMPO is used on a node X-FEM. For example, the taxation of the X zero displacement of node X-FEM \mathit{N1} is therefore done in the classic way: DDL_IMPO=_F(node='N1',DX=0) 2.3 Analytical resolution The solution to such a problem is of course obvious. It is clear that mechanically speaking, the two parts of the structure will detach: the lower part will have a zero displacement and the upper part will have a whole movement equal to the required displacement (see []). Figure 2.3-a : Initial and final status of the structure The analytical solution is then the following: all the following x and y moves are zero, all the following z moves below the level set are zero and all the following z moves above the level set are equal to the {u}_{z} displacement at the top of the structure. 2.4 Tested quantities and results The POST_MAIL_XFEM operator allows the cracks to be broken by the X-FEM method. The POST_CHAM_XFEM operator then allows the X-FEM results to be exported to this new mesh. Both operators are only to be used after the calculation at post-processing views. They allow the nodes to be generated just below and above the interface and to display their movements. The values of the displacement are therefore tested just below and above the interface after convergence of the iterations of the STAT_NON_LINE operator. v6.04.176 SSNV176 – Law Identification ENDO_ORTH_BETON v6.04.176 SSNV176 – Law Identification ENDO_ORTH_BETON Summary: The ENDO_ORTH_BETON law tests are presented here on a single element to identify the model parameters. Since there is no empirical formula for calibrating the parameters, the user can use some of the test cases presented here to adjust his parameters. The study of the model parameters is in the R7.01.09 documentation. The 5 tests proposed are as follows: 1. single traction 2. single traction with steering 3. simple compression 4. simple compression with control 5. single traction, simple compression and a biaxial test 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry and boundary conditions L的element used is a tetrahedron to a gauss point. There is therefore no problem of homogeneity of the fields in the element. The blocking conditions and linear relationships between the nodes to be applied are summarized in [Figure 1.1-a]. The \mathrm{N0N1} , \mathrm{N0N2} and \mathrm{N0N3} edges are of length 1. Given the geometry of the element, blocking conditions and linear relationships, deformation is directly related to the displacements of the nodes: {\varepsilon}_{xx}=\mathit{DX}(\mathit{N1}) {\varepsilon}_{yy}=\mathit{DY}(\mathit{N2}) {\varepsilon}_{zz}=\mathrm{DZ}(\mathrm{N3}) {\varepsilon}_{xy}=\mathit{DX}(\mathit{N2})=\mathit{DY}(\mathit{N1}) {\varepsilon}_{xz}=\mathit{DX}(\mathit{N3})=\mathit{DZ}(\mathit{N1}) {\varepsilon}_{yz}=\mathit{DY}(\mathit{N3})=\mathit{DZ}(\mathit{N2}) If we work with imposed deformation, we need only impose the appropriate nodes displacements. If you want to work forcefully, as is the case for Modelling E, you must impose the following loads (see [Figure 1.1-a] for the definition of the \mathrm{F1} , \mathrm{F2} , \mathrm{F3} and \mathrm{F4} faces ): {\sigma}_{xx}>0 : \mathrm{FX} on \mathrm{F1} and -1/\sqrt{3}\mathrm{FX} on \mathrm{F4} , \mathrm{FX} 0 : \mathrm{FY} on \mathrm{F2} and -1/\sqrt{3}\mathrm{FY} on \mathrm{F4} , \mathrm{FY} 0 : \mathrm{FZ} on \mathrm{F3} and -1/\sqrt{3}\mathrm{FZ} on \mathrm{F4} , \mathrm{FZ} 0 (Compression) - {U}_{3} : \mathrm{FX} on \mathrm{F1} , -1/\sqrt{3}\mathrm{FX} on \mathrm{F4} , \mathrm{FX}>0 (Compression on x axis ); \mathrm{FY} on \mathrm{F2} , -1/\sqrt{3}\mathrm{FY} on \mathrm{F4} , with \mathit{FY}=-0,2\mathit{FX} (Traction on y axis ). 7.5 Test values | Instant | Result | Name of field | Component | Location | Aster | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 42 | \mathrm{U1} | SIEF_ELGA | \mathrm{SIXX} | VOLUME, point 1 | 3.20684E+00 | | 76 | \mathrm{U2} | SIEF_ELGA | \mathrm{SIXX} | VOLUME, point 1 | -3.18000E+01 | | 74 | \mathrm{U3} | SIEF_ELGA | \mathrm{SIXX} | VOLUME, point 1 | -1.42038E+01 | The maximum value (in absolute value) of the {\sigma}_{xx} stress is tested for each calculation. The tensile fracture stress ( \mathrm{U1} ), in compression ( \mathrm{U2} ), is then obtained and the tensile stress in the biaxial test ( \mathrm{U3} ) is verified to be less than the single tensile fracture stress ( \mathit{U1} ): 1. \mathit{U1} : {\sigma}_{\mathit{rupture}}^{\mathit{traction}}=3.20684\mathit{MPa} 2. \mathrm{U2} : {\sigma}_{\mathit{rupture}}^{\mathit{compression}}=-31.8\mathit{MPa} 3. \mathrm{U3} : {\sigma}_{\mathit{U3}}^{\mathit{traction}}=-0.2{\sigma}_{\mathit{U3}}^{\mathit{compression}}=0.2\times 14.2038\mathit{Mpa} et {\sigma}_{\mathit{U3}}^{\mathit{traction}}<{\sigma}_{\mathit{rupture}}^{\mathit{traction}} Warning 1 : The number of time step may not be sufficient to reach the softening phase. Therefore, the user will verify that for \mathit{U1} and \mathrm{U2} calculations, the \mathrm{U3} calculation is subject to an additional warning (see Warning 2 ), it is well in the softening phase (decrease of the steering parameter). The maximum absolute stress should not be reached for the last time step. Otherwise, the calculation should continue until the softening phase. Warning2 : For some sets of parameters, it is possible to observe convergence difficulties for \mathrm{U3} calculation during the softening phase. Indeed, the constitutive law ensures the existence and uniqueness of the imposed deformation solution, but not in imposed force. These convergence problems only appear in the softening phase, the user can consider the highest value of the control parameter reached, equal to the greatest compression stress This is true only in the case of convergence problems. If there is no convergence problem for \mathrm{U3} calculation, and the maximum absolute stress is reached for the last time step, then the calculation must be continued. 8 Summary of the results The objective of the modellings presented in this document is to identify the parameters of the ENDO_ORTH_BETON law. As there is no empirical formula for the values of the parameters to be used, the user will have to calibrate his parameters step by step on the various tests proposed. The method for calibrating the parameters, which is contained in the R7.01.09 document, can be summarized as follows: 1. \mathrm{ALPHA} choice: (0.85 to 0.9), 2. Calibration of \mathrm{K0} , \mathrm{ECROB} on modellings A, C or E (calculation \mathrm{U1} ). Once these parameters are calibrated, they should not be changed in the calibration phase of the other parameters, 3. \mathrm{K1} , \mathrm{K2} and \mathrm{ECROD} calibration on modellings B (or D) and E. In fact, E Modelling ( \mathrm{U2} and \mathrm{U3} calculations) is sufficient. It allows to verify the value of the single compression break stress, and to ensure that the break envelope for biaxial tests does not inflate. It is not necessary to calibrate the \mathit{K2} parameter in a very fine way because it results from a qualitative argument, and no experimental data is ever available to identify it.

v6.04.177 SSNV177 - Willam Test with ENDO_ORTH_BETON Law v6.04.177 SSNV177 - Willam Test with ENDO_ORTH_BETON Law Summary: The Willam test applied to the constitutive law anisotropic unilateral for the behaviour of ENDO_ORTH_BETON concrete (see R7.01.09) developed in [Bib 1] is presented here. It is a tensile-switch test that allows the rotation of the clean damage marker in the case of an unproportional load. 1 Presentation of Willam's test The objective of the test proposed by Willam et al. (see [Bib 2]) is to observe the model's response when the proper load marker turns. This test is purely theoretical and it is unlikely that experimental results will ever be available for this test, given the difficulties associated with the study of the fracture of the tensile concrete. Its major interest is to compare the influence of the description of damage anisotropy on the material response to the isotropic models. This test is the succession of two loading phases: - First phase: single traction. \Delta {\varepsilon}_{xx} is imposed up to nonlinearity, i.e. the beginning of traction damage. - Second phase: starting from the deformation state at the end of the first phase, two tensile loads and one shear load are imposed in the tensile loading plane with the following proportionality coefficients: (\Delta {\varepsilon}_{xx},\Delta {\varepsilon}_{yy},\Delta {\varepsilon}_{xy})=(0.5,0.75,0.5) . Figure 1-a shows the evolution of the different stress components as a function of {\varepsilon}_{xx} deformation. Four phases can be distinguished in the behaviour: 1. Phase 1 is the elastic phase under uniaxial loading. 2. Phase 2 is the growth of damage in a particular direction. The stress {\sigma}_{xx} decreases as damage first becomes less on the x axis. The stress {\sigma}_{yy} does not increase linearly, indicating that the proper damage marker turns. 3. Phase 3 begins when the damage is total in one direction. The proper damage marker is then blocked as shown in Figure 1-b, which shows the evolution of the angle between the clean damage marker and the initial mark (as well as the angle between the proper deformation mark and the initial mark). 4. Phase 4 then begins when damage in the orthogonal direction to the senitiated blocked direction is observed, and the stress of the growth of damage is softened. Figure 1-a Strengthening constraints for Willam test Figure 1-b also shows that the proper damage marker does not rotate in the same way as the proper deformity marker. This is due to the fact that the law of evolution of damage is not written in relation to deformations but in relation to thermodynamic forces, which depend on both the state of deformation and damage. Since the Willam test is a theoretical test, it is difficult to make a precise judgement on this prediction of the ENDO_ORTH_BETON model. Figure 1-b Evolution of angles of proper markers of deformations and damage from the initial mark The behaviour obtained with our model for the Willam test appears to be characteristic of what can be expected from anisotropic models (see [Bib 3]). The main difference, compared to Carol's results [1999], is the blocking of the clean marker which is observed with the ENDO_ORTH_BETON model when damage is complete in a direction, which does not appear in [Bib 3]. 2 Reference problem 2.1 Geometry and boundary conditions L的element used is a tetrahedron to a gauss point. There is therefore no problem of homogeneity of the fields in the element. The blocking conditions and linear relationships between the nodes to be applied are summarized in [Figure 3]. The \mathit{N0N1} , \mathit{N0N2} , and \mathit{N0N3} edges are 1. v6.04.178 SSNV178 – Cylinder with pressure-reinforced frame v6.04.178 SSNV178 – Cylinder with pressure-reinforced frame Summary: A cylinder with pressure-rebar is considered. More precisely, a 3d hollow cylinder is completed on its outer face with a circumferential frame. This structure is charged by an internal pressure. The calculation is elastic linear. The simulation is compared with an analytical solution to validate modellings of the grid_membrane-type frame structure. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The cylinder has an internal a=10m radius, an external b=20m radius, a height of h=\mathrm{0.02m} The circumferential frame, positioned on the outer surface of the cylinder, has one section per unit length of s=0.1{m}^{2}/\mathit{ml} . The main direction of the frame is vertical. This allows verification that the desiccation creep remains stable during this phase. The degree of hydration varies linearly from 0 to 1 between the initial moment and the 28th day. The reference temperature is 20°C . The thermal loading corresponds to a temperature rise varying from 20°C and 40°C between the initial and final moments. The mechanical load corresponds to a one-way compression in the vertical direction ( z in \mathrm{3D} ); its intensity is 12[\mathrm{MPa}] . The load is applied in \mathrm{1s} and is kept constant for 100 days. 1.4 Initial conditions The beginning of the calculation is assumed at the moment –1 . Also, the reference solution is obtained numerically using the software Scilab 2.7.2 for BETON_UMLV or python for BETON_BURGER. Each deformation component is calculated separately. - The endogenous withdrawal deformations are determined from the e_{re} = k_{re} \beta relationship where \beta is the degree of hydration of the material. - The desiccation removal deformations are determined from the e_{rd} = k_{rd} C relationship where the moisture content of the material is defined. - The thermal expansion deformations are determined from the e_{th} = \alpha (T-T_{ref}) relationship where T and T_{ref} refer to the current temperature and the material reference temperature, respectively - The own creep deformations are calculated numerically using a discretization identical to that of BETON_UMLV and an implantation following an explicit scheme for BETON_BURGER. The temporal discretization is then necessarily finer for the explicit scheme. - The creep deformations of desiccation are calculated analytically. BETON_UMLV law still uses the old relationship: \dot{e_{th}} = \frac{|\dot{h}|\sigma}{\eta_{fd}} where h=f(C) means the moisture of the material. v6.04.182 SSNV182 – Block with frictional contact interface with X-FEM v6.04.182 SSNV182 – Block with frictional contact interface with X-FEM Summary The purpose of this test is to validate the consideration of contact on the lips of the crack, limiting itself to the case where the crack completely crosses the structure. The contact is taken into account by the continuous method [bib1] adapted to the framework of the X-FEM [bib2] method. Two contact algorithms are tested: the Lagrangian augmented method and the penalised method [bib2]. This test involves a parallelepipedic block in compression modelled in \mathrm{2D} and \mathrm{3D} . The interface through it is represented by a level-set as part of the X-FEM method. Several angular positions of the interface are taken into account: the interface follows the faces of the elements ( \theta =0° ) and the interface cuts elements ( \theta =26.56° in \mathrm{3D} and \theta =30° in \mathrm{2D} ). By taking a friction coefficient of Coulomb high enough to be gripped, we find the solution of the same problem without interface. The modellings d, e and f enable the method to be validated also in \mathrm{2D} . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure is a straight parallelepipeda with a square and healthy base. The dimensions of the block (see[ Figure -1.1-a ]) are: \mathrm{LX}=5m , \mathrm{LY}=20m and \mathrm{LZ}=20m . It does not have cracks. The interface is introduced by level set functions directly in the command file using the DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08 operator. The interface is present in the middle of the structure through its representation by the level set. The normal level set ( \mathrm{LSN} ) allows to define a flat interface making an \theta angle with the \mathrm{Oxy} plane by the following equation: \mathrm{LSN}=Z-(\mathrm{aY}+b) éq 1.1-1 where a is the slope of the interface, i.e. a=-\tan(\theta ) and b=\frac{\mathrm{LZ}}{2}-a\frac{\mathrm{LY}}{2} . Figure ‐ 1.1-a : Bar Geometry and Interface Positioning In \mathrm{2D} , we have an equivalent structure. Figure 1.1-b : Geometry and positioning of the interface in \mathrm{2D} 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus : E=100\mathrm{MPa} Poisson's ratio : \nu =0 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The nodes of the lower side of the bar is clamped and a \mathrm{UZ}=-{10}^{-6}m displacement is imposed on those of the upper side which corresponds to a pressure load following the z axis. The displacements along the x and y axes are blocked for the nodes of the upper surface. In \mathrm{2D} , the displacement is carried out on the y axis. 1.4 Mesh characteristics The structure is modelled in \mathrm{3D} by a regular mesh composed of 5\times 20\times 20 HEXA8 [Figure 1.4-a]. Figure ‐ 1.4-a : mesh \mathrm{3D} This mesh is composed of linear finished d-elements. However, as part of the continuous method [bib1] with X-FEM [bib2], it is necessary to switch to a somewhat special linear elements. These elements have linear shape functions and a quadratic mesh cell support. On these elements, the top nodes carry the unknowns of the displacement, and the middle nodes carry the unknowns related to the contact. Moreover, when the interface follows the border of element, the top nodes of the element also carry the unknowns of contact. For test case \mathrm{2D} , the structure is modelled by a regular mesh made up of 20\times 20 QUAD4. Figure ‐ 1.4-b : mesh \mathrm{2D} 1.5 Bibliography 1. MASSIN P., BEN DHIA H., ZARROUG M.: elements contacts derived from a continuous hybrid formulation, Reference Manual of Code_Aster , R5.03.52 1. MASSIN P., GENIAUT S.: X-FEM Method, Code_Aster Reference Manual , R7.02.12 1. TARDIEU N., VAUTIER I., LORENTZ E.: Non-linear quasi-static algorithm, Code_Aster Reference Manual, R5.03.01 2. DHATT G., TOUZOT G.: A presentation of the elements method finished, Maloine Ed., PARIS 2 Modelization A: straight interface, Lagrangian method increased In this Modelling, one represents a straight interface, the \theta angle is then 0. The interface coincides with the faces of some finished elements. The increased Lagrangian method is used for the treatment of contact / friction. 2.1 Analytical resolution When the adhering contact is taken into account on the interface, the problem is equivalent to that of a healthy bar in pure compression. The solution to the problem is that of the same problem without interface. The constraint in the structure is: {\sigma}_{zz}=E\frac{\mathit{UZ}}{\mathit{LZ}} éq 2.1-1 and the value of the contact pressure on the interface is: \lambda ={\sigma}_{zz} éq 2.1-2 With the numerical values previously introduced, \lambda =-5.0\mathit{Pa} . 2.2 Tested Features As indicated in the previous paragraph, friction must be activated. In the DEFI_CONTACT operator, FROTTEMENT=的COULOMB is specified, and the coefficient of friction is chosen equal to 1. In addition, from the first iteration of active stresses, it is assumed that contact points have contact status. This is possible by specifying CONTACT_INIT= Otherwise, at the end of the first iteration, the contact being not activated, the upper block enters the lower block but the two blocks have not deformed. Their stress state is therefore zero, and a global criterion (RESI_GLOB_MAXI) for the convergence of the Newton-Raphson algorithm [bib3] must be chosen, which may be inappropriate in the further calculations when the contact is activated. To avoid this, and to have a relative criterion, it takes a non-zero state of stress from the first iteration, and therefore activate contact from the beginning. The algorithm of the active stresses thus converges into an iteration. 2.3 Tested quantities and results The values of the normal contact pressure after convergence of the iterations of the STAT_NON_LINE operator and the loop on the active stresses are tested. All contact points, corresponding to the nodes of the mesh on the interface, are tested. v6.04.183 SSNV183 - Fluid test with VENDOCHAB v6.04.183 SSNV183 - Fluid test with VENDOCHAB Summary: The VENDOCHAB model, is based on a formulation proposed by Chaboche. It is a coupled formulation that covers an elasto-viscoplastic law with multiplicative isotropic hardening and isotropic damage kinetics. This law was originally developed to predict the life and cracking of turboreactors' blades and more generally to predict the ruin time of the structures being pressed at high temperatures. This non-linear quasi-static mechanical test validates the VENDOCHAB \mathrm{3D} model in the case of a test piece subjected to an isothermal uniaxial creep test. The stress and deformation states are homogeneous in the test piece. This test validates the explicit integration of this model. The equations of this coupled formulation are described in the R5.03.15 reference booklet. The Modelling of the test piece is done with an element \mathrm{3D} at 8 nodes (HEXA8). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry is chosen voluntarily simple, to translate a homogeneous state of stress and deformation, as is the case in uniaxial creep. It is here a volume element represented by a side cube 3\mathrm{mm} . The Modelling is volume volume and the creep is done at stress imposed. 1.2 Material properties The characteristics are as follows: Keyword ELAS: - \mathit{YOUNG}=150000.0\mathit{MPa} - \mathrm{NU}=0.30 Keyword VENDOCHAB: - {S}_{\mathrm{VP}}=0. - \mathrm{SEDVP1}=0. - \mathrm{SEDVP2}=0. - {N}_{\mathrm{VP}}=12. - {M}_{\mathrm{VP}}=9. - {K}_{\mathrm{VP}}=2110. - {A}_{D}=3191. - {R}_{D}=6.3 - {K}_{D}=14 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads \mathrm{DZ}=0 on the lower side ( Z=0 ) \mathrm{DY}=0 on the left side ( Y=0 ) \mathrm{DX}=0 on the rear side ( X=0 ) 200\mathrm{MPa} pressure on the upper surface, such as: P=0 à t=\mathrm{0s} P=200\mathrm{MPa} à t=\mathrm{0.1s} P=200\mathrm{MPa} up to t=2.5{10}^{6}s This corresponds to a uniaxial creep test under a constant load of 200\mathit{MPa} . 1.4 Initial conditions No stress and deformation. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation Analytical solution for the damage variable D : D(t)=1-{(1-(1+k){(\frac{{\sigma}_{0}}{A})}^{R}t)}^{\frac{1}{1+k}} Analytical solution for the viscoplastic isotropic hardening variable, r , in the case of a zero {\sigma}_{Y} threshold: r(t)={\left[\frac{(M+N)}{M(1+k-N)}{(\frac{{\sigma}_{0}}{A})}^{-R}{(\frac{{\sigma}_{0}}{K})}^{N}(1-{(1-(1+k){(\frac{{\sigma}_{0}}{A})}^{R}t)}^{\frac{1+k-N}{1+k}})\right]}^{\frac{M}{M+N}} In previous expressions, D is the damage variable corresponding to the internal variable \mathit{V9} and r is the multiplicative viscoplastic hardening variable corresponding to the internal variable \mathit{V8} . The following correspondence is also available in relation to the parameters of the keyword VENDOCHAB: N={N}_{\mathit{VP}} M={M}_{\mathit{VP}} K={K}_{\mathit{VP}} A={A}_{D} R={R}_{D} k={K}_{D} 2.2 Quantities and reference results Evolution of the damage variable, D , depending on the time. v6.04.186 SSNV186 – LBB condition and frictional contact with X-FEM v6.04.186 SSNV186 – LBB condition and frictional contact with X-FEM Summary The purpose of this test is to validate the consideration of contact (by the continuous [bib1] method) on the crack lips in the X-FEM [bib2] method, when the LBB condition [bib3] [bib4] is not met. Contact/frost is processed by an increased Lagrangian algorithm for modellings A to H and by a penalised algorithm for modellings I to K. This test involves a parallelepipedic block in compression. The interface through it is represented by a level set. The interface is straight, unspinned and completely crosses the elements. 1 Reference problem In some cases, oscillations of contact pressures may occur, particularly for structures where the interface cuts pentahedrons under a non-uniform load. This is due to the non-compliance with the LBB condition [bib3] [bib4]. This d-oscillation phenomenon is comparable to that encountered in incompressibility [bib5]. Physically, in the case of contact, this amounts to wanting to impose contact in excess of interface points (over-stressed), making the hyperstatic system. To release it, it is necessary to restrict the space of Lagrange multipliers, as is done in [bib6] for Dirichlet conditions with X-FEM. Such algorithms have P0 segments, which slow the convergence. A good algorithm must minimize the appearance of such segments. L-algorithm proposed by Moës [bib6] to reduce oscillations is adapted to the 3D case (algorithm version 1). This algorithm has been improved to make it more physical and effective (algorithm version 2). A comparison of both versions is made. It should be noted that these parasitic oscillations are not reproducible in the current version of Code_Aster: one of the two algorithms is systematically chosen (the 2 is used by default), and even an overload of the code to not use any one would bring a zero pivot. We illustrate them in this documentation by results from another formulation (formulation to the edges [bib7]), which is now being resolved. For hexahedrons or quadrangles cut horizontally, there are no P0 segments. 1.1 Geometry The structure is a straight parallelepipeda with a square and healthy base. The dimensions of the block are: \mathrm{LX}=5m , \mathrm{LY}=20m and \mathrm{LZ}=20m . It does not have cracks [ Figure 1.1-1 ]. The interface is introduced by level set functions directly into the command file using the DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08 operator. The interface is present within the structure through its representation by the level set. The normal level set ( \mathrm{LSN} ) allows to define a flat, unpaved interface that completely crosses the elements, by the following equation: \mathrm{LSN}=Z-17.5 éq 1.1-1 Figure 1.1-1: Géométrie et positionnement de l’interface 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus : E=100\mathit{GPa} . Poisson's ratio : \nu =0 . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The lower side is clamped. The upper side is subjected to a parabolic pressure which means: \mathrm{pression}=(100-\frac{{(Y-10)}^{2}}{2})\frac{E}{{10}^{6}}\mathrm{Pa} éq 1.3-1 Movements along the x and y axes are blocked for the nodes of the upper surface. 1.4 Bibliography 1. Massin P., Ben Dhia H., Zarroug M.: elements from contacts derived from a continuous hybrid formulation, Reference Manual of Code_Aster , R5.03.52 1. Chapel D., Bathe K. J.: The Inf-sup test, Computers & Structures 47 (4/5), 537-545, 1993 2. Indeed, in the case of hexahedrons cut by a parallel interface to the faces, the number of contact pressures (one per cut edge) is compatible with the discretization of the displacement field [bib1] [bib2]. 2.1 Mesh characteristics The problem is invariant along the \mathit{Ox} axis. To limit the calculation time, the mesh here is composed of only one element on this axis. The structure is then modelled by a regular mesh composed of 1\times 20\times 20 HEXA8 see [ Figure 2.1-1 ]. As part of the continuous method [bib1] with X-FEM [bib2], contact unknowns are carried by the nodes peaks. 2.2 Tested Features The integration scheme is reduced to 4 Gauss points per contact facet. Contact is active from the first iteration of active stresses but friction is not taken into account The algorithm to restrict the space of Lagrange multipliers is the #1. 6.4 Tested quantities and results The value of the contact pressures for all interface points is tested. v6.04.191 SSNV191 – Validation of Neumann conditions with X-FEM in 2D and 3D v6.04.191 SSNV191 – Validation of Neumann conditions with X-FEM in 2D and 3D Summary The purpose of this test is to validate the consideration of boundary conditions Neumann type on elements skin in 2D and 3D. This test involves a 3D structure or a 2D equivalent with a horizontal flat interface cutting the structure into two parts (a "higher part above the interface, and a "lower part" below the interface). The interface is represented by level sets. The loads applied are of several types: a constant pressure load on the side faces of the structure, a load with positive pressure on the upper side faces and a negative pressure on the lower side faces. The same problem is also addressed by replacing the pressures with 3D surfactic forces and 2D linear forces. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The 3D structure of dimensions \mathit{LX}=\mathrm{1m} , \mathit{LY}=\mathrm{2m} and \mathit{LZ}=\mathrm{3m} has a horizontal flat interface at mid-height (see [ Figure 1.1-1 ]). The interface is not meshed, and geometry is actually a healthy structure without interface. The interface is then introduced by level set functions directly into the command file using DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08 operator. Figure 1.1-1 : Geometry of the 3D structure The A , B , C , D , E and F points are defined to block rigid modes. | | x | y | z | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A | LX | \mathrm{LY}/2 | 0 | | B | 0 | \mathrm{LY}/2 | 0 | | C | \mathrm{LX} | \mathrm{LY} | 0 | | D | \mathrm{LX} | \mathrm{LY}/2 | LZ | | E | 0 | \mathrm{LY}/2 | LZ | | F | \mathrm{LX} | \mathrm{LY} | LZ | Table 1.1-1 : Coordinates of 3D blocking points The equivalent structure in 2D, of dimensions \mathrm{LX}=\mathrm{2m} , \mathrm{LY}=\mathrm{3m} with a horizontal flat interface at mid-height (see [ Figure 1.1-2], is also defined. Figure 1.1-2 : Geometry of the 2D structure The A , B , C and D points are set to block rigid modes. | | x | y | | --- | --- | --- | | A | \mathrm{LX}/2 | 0 | | B | \mathrm{LX} | 0 | | C | \mathrm{LX}/2 | \mathrm{LY} | | D | \mathrm{LX} | \mathrm{LY} | Table 1.1-2 : Coordinates of 2D blocking points 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus : E=10000\mathrm{MPa} Poisson's ratio : \nu =0 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads In 3D, rigid modes are blocked as follows: | The A and D points are blocked in 3 directions: | \lbrace \begin{array}{}{\mathrm{DX}}^{A}={\mathrm{DX}}^{D}=0\\ {\mathrm{DY}}^{A}={\mathrm{DY}}^{D}=0\\ {\mathrm{DZ}}^{A}={\mathrm{DZ}}^{D}=0\end{array} | | --- | --- | | B and E points are blocked along the \mathrm{Oz} axis: | {\mathrm{DZ}}^{B}={\mathrm{DZ}}^{E}=0 | | The C and F points are blocked along the \mathrm{Ox} and \mathrm{Oz} axes: | \lbrace \begin{array}{}{\mathrm{DX}}^{C}={\mathrm{DX}}^{F}=0\\ {\mathrm{DZ}}^{C}={\mathrm{DZ}}^{F}=0\end{array} | In 2D, rigid modes are blocked as follows: | The A and C points are blocked in both directions: | \lbrace \begin{array}{}{\mathrm{DX}}^{A}={\mathrm{DX}}^{C}=0\\ {\mathrm{DY}}^{A}={\mathrm{DY}}^{C}=0\end{array} | | --- | --- | | B and D points are blocked along the \mathrm{Oy} axis: | {\mathrm{DY}}^{B}={\mathrm{DY}}^{D}=0 | In 3D, two loads are envisaged: - Constant distributed pressure ( p=10000\mathrm{Pa} ) on the side surfaces (planes y=0 and y=\mathrm{LY} ), corresponding to a compression case on the \mathrm{Oy} axis. - Positive pressure ( p=10000\mathrm{Pa} ) on the upper side and negative pressure ( p=-10000\mathrm{Pa} ) on the lower side, corresponding to a compression case on the upper solid and a tensile case on the lower solid In 2D, two loads are envisaged: - Constant distributed pressure ( p=10000\mathrm{Pa} ) on the side segments ( x=0 and x=\mathrm{LX} ) corresponding to a compression case on the \mathrm{Ox} axis. - Positive pressure ( p=10000\mathrm{Pa} ) on the upper side edges and negative pressure ( p=-10000\mathrm{Pa} ) on the lower side edges, corresponding to a compression case on the upper solid and a tensile case on the lower solid Figure 1.3-1 : Pressure loading 1.4 Problem solutions The solution of the 3D problem is presented. The solution of the 2D problem is obtained by replacing y with x . 1.4.1 Pure compression loading La structure est en compression pure, la solution en déplacement est triviale. Pour les nœuds de la face latérale de gauche, le déplacement solution est: {u}_{y}=-\frac{\mathit{LY}}{2}{\varepsilon}_{yy}=-\frac{\mathit{LY}}{2}\frac{{\sigma}_{yy}}{E}=\frac{\mathit{LY}}{2}\frac{p}{E}=\frac{{2.10}^{4}}{{2.10}^{10}}={10}^{-6}m Pour les nœuds de la face latérale de droite, le déplacement solution est: {u}_{y}=\frac{\mathit{LY}}{2}{\varepsilon}_{yy}=\frac{\mathit{LY}}{2}\frac{{\sigma}_{yy}}{E}=\frac{-\mathit{LY}}{2}\frac{p}{E}=-\frac{{2.10}^{4}}{{2.10}^{10}}=-{10}^{-6}m Lorsqu’un nœud du bord est enrichi par la fonction Heaviside, son déplacement s’écrit comme une combinaison d’un terme continu et d’un terme discontinu. Pour ce cas de chargement, il n’y a pas de discontinuité au travers de l’interface, donc les degrés de liberté enrichis sont tous nuls. 1.4.2 Charge in compression / traction La structure supérieure est en compression pure et les déplacements des nœuds de la face latérale supérieure sont les mêmes que ceux du cas de chargement précédent. La structure inférieure est en traction pure. Seuls les signes des valeurs de déplacement changent. Pour les nœuds de la face latérale inférieure de gauche, le déplacement solution est: {u}_{y}=-\frac{\mathrm{LY}}{2}{\varepsilon}_{yy}=\frac{\mathrm{LY}}{2}\frac{p}{E}=-\frac{{2.10}^{4}}{{2.10}^{10}}=-{10}^{-6}m Pour les nœuds de la face latérale inférieure de droite, le déplacement solution est: {u}_{y}=\frac{\mathrm{LY}}{2}{\varepsilon}_{yy}=\frac{\mathrm{LY}}{2}\frac{p}{E}=\frac{{2.10}^{4}}{{2.10}^{10}}={10}^{-6}m In this case, the displacement is discontinuous through the interface. The values of the degrees of freedom discontinuous can be easily determined (refer to the similar case treated in V6.04.173). 2 Modelling A In this model, for the pressure load, the load is applied using a constant distributed pressure or constant superfacial forces for load 1 and distributed pressure or distributed forces z functions for load 2 . In this model, for the load load in the surface, the load is applied using constant overfacial forces for load number 1, and z function superfacial forces for load number 2. 2.1 Mesh characteristics The structure is meshed with 8 nodes hexahedrons. The number d-elements is the smallest possible, i.e. a element on the \mathrm{Ox} axis, 2 elements on the \mathrm{Oy} axis (to be able to define nodes in the y=\mathrm{LY}/2 midplane), and 5 elements on the \mathrm{Oz} axis. On the \mathrm{Oz} axis, the number d-elements is odd so that the interface does not coincide with the faces of the elements; the 3 central d-elements layers use elements X-FEM, and the 2 d-elements layers at the top and bottom use classic elements. Figure 2.1-1 : mesh 3D 2.2 Tested Features Keyword PRES_REP from AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01 allows for constant distributed pressure to be applied to mesh cells skin. When the pressure is a function or formula, keyword PRES_REP from AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01 is used. This feature is tested with #2 loading, because with X-FEM, you cannot define a higher and lower lateral surface as mesh-cell group. In this case, only one mesh-cell group with all side-facing mesh cells is defined, and z is applied to this mesh-cell group. Keyword FORCE_FACE operator AFFE_CHAR_MECA U4.44.01 allows you to apply a constant overfacial force to mesh cells skin. When the overfacial force is a function or formula, keyword FORCE_FACE AFFE_CHAR_MECA_F U4.44.01 is used. 2.3 Tested quantities and results The POST_MAIL_XFEM operator allows the cracks to be broken by the X-FEM method. The POST_CHAM_XFEM operator then allows the X-FEM results to be exported to this new mesh. Both operators are only to be used after the calculation at post-processing views. They allow the nodes to be generated just below and above the interface and to display their movements.
