v6.04.231 SSNV231 – Internal pressure hollow sphere in large deformations v6.04.231 SSNV231 – Internal pressure hollow sphere in large deformations Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the different incompressible formulations in large deformations. The advantage of this test case is that one has an analytical solution. Five modellings are used to validate formulations regardless of the type of finite element: Modelling A: 3D mesh Quadratic HEXA20 (INCO_UPG, INCO_UP) Modelling B: 3D mesh Quadratic TETRA10 (INCO_UPG, INCO_UP) Modelling C: 3D mesh Quadratic PENTA15 (INCO_UPG, INCO_UP) Modelling D: AXIS mesh Quadratic QUAD8 (INCO_UPG, INCO_UP) Modelling E: AXIS mesh Quadratic TRIA6 (INCO_UPG, INCO_UP) Modelling F: 3D mesh Quadratic HEXA20 (HHO) 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A hollow sphere of 1m external radius and 0.2m internal radius is considered. Figure 1.1-a : Cut of the sphere studied 1.2 Material properties The material has a perfectly plastic elastoplastic behavior. Its loading surface is defined by the criterion of von Mises. The material properties are: - E=200000\mathit{MPa} - \nu =0.3 - {\sigma}_{y}=150\mathit{MPa} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Internal pressure is applied until the entire sphere is plastified. The outer surface is free of effort. 1.4 Initial conditions None 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation In the following, all quantities defined in the initial configuration will be written in capital letters. quantities defined in the distorted configuration will be written in lowercase. To establish the analytical solution, one considers an inner \text{A} and outer \text{B} ray sphere. The material is elastoplastic with perfect plasticity. The plastic flow is normal and associated with the criterion of von Mises, yield limit {\sigma}_{y} . The elasticity is isotropic defined by the compressibility and shearing modules, K and \mu . The sphere is subjected to internal pressure P . Given the spherical symmetry of geometry and loading, a solution is sought that has the same invariance properties, which excludes the search for bifurcated solutions. The solution depends only on the distance at the center of the sphere noted R in the initial configuration and r in the distorted configuration. The displacement is purely radial: \vec{u}(r)=u(r){\vec{e}}_{r} , where ({\vec{e}}_{r},{\vec{e}}_{\theta},{\vec{e}}_{\phi }) is the orthonormized base associated with the spherical coordinate system. Therefore, the definition of the operators \text{grad} , div , ... adequate. The stress tensor is expressed as follows: \sigma ={\sigma}_{\mathit{rr}}(r){\vec{e}}_{r}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{r}+{\sigma}_{\theta \theta }(r)({\vec{e}}_{\theta}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\theta}{\vec{e}}_{\phi }\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\phi }) As for displacement, its expression in the reference configuration is: \vec{u}(\vec{X})=U(r){\vec{e}}_{r} . It can be noted that, by definition, we have the relationships: r=R+U(R) et u(r)=U(R) The following formula for derivatives is derived from this formula: \frac{\partial U}{\partial R}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\frac{\partial r}{\partial R}=\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\left(1+\frac{\partial U}{\partial R}\right)\Rightarrow \frac{\partial U}{\partial R}=\frac{\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}}{\left(1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\right)} The transformation gradient shall be calculated: F=\left(1+\frac{\partial U}{\partial R}\right){\vec{e}}_{r}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{r}+\left(1+\frac{U}{R}\right)({\vec{e}}_{\theta}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\theta}{\vec{e}}_{\phi }\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\phi }) Note: F admits constant clean directions during transformation. Logarithmic deformation then simply admits as expression: E=\ln\left(1+\frac{\partial U}{\partial R}\right){\vec{e}}_{r}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{r}+\ln\left(1+\frac{U}{R}\right)({\vec{e}}_{\theta}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\theta}{\vec{e}}_{\phi }\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\phi }) Note: In this particular case, the deformation rate \dot{E} coincids with the Eulerian D deformation rate, so that the stress tensor T associated with the logarithmic deformations is equal to the Kirchhoff \tau content. It is a favorable situation to display an analytical solution. In the distorted configuration, the e(\vec{x})=E(\vec{X}) deformation is expressed: e=-\ln\left(1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\right){\vec{e}}_{r}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{r}+\left(\lnr-\ln\left(r-u\right)\right)({\vec{e}}_{\theta}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\theta}{\vec{e}}_{\phi }\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\phi }) It is also useful to express the Jacobian of the transformation and its logarithm in the distorted configuration: j=\detF=\frac{1}{\left(1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\right)}{\left(\frac{r}{r-u}\right)}^{2} The equilibrium equations can also be expressed in the deformed configuration as a function of the Kirchhoff \tau =j\sigma tensor: {div}_{x}\left(\frac{\tau}{j}\right)=0\iff \frac{\partial {\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}}{\partial r}-{\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}\frac{\partial \lnj}{\partial r}+\frac{2}{r}({\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}-{\tau}_{\theta \theta })=0 Besides, we have the boundary conditions: {\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}(b)=0 Where a and b are the internal and external rays of the distorted sphere. Due to the spherical symmetry, it is equivalent to imposing internal pressure or radial displacement on the inner skin. It is preferable to pilot the calculation while moving, so that the second boundary condition is replaced by: u(a)={U}^{\mathit{imp}} The hydrostatic part of the behaviour is purely elastic: \text{tr}\tau =3K\text{tr}e\iff 3K\lnj={\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}+2{\tau}_{\theta \theta } For the deviatoric part, we have the classical relations of the plasticity of von Mises: {\tau}_{\mathit{eq}}\le {\sigma}_{y};\dot{p}\ge 0;\dot{p}({\tau}_{\mathit{eq}}-{\sigma}_{y})=0 {\tau}^{D}=2\mu ({e}^{D}+{e}^{p}) When it comes to the response of the structure, it is expected that the plastic zone will gradually develop from the inside to the outside of the sphere. When it reaches the outer wall, all points of the sphere are in a plastic regime either: {\tau}_{\mathit{eq}}={\sigma}_{y}\iff {\tau}_{\theta \theta }-{\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}={\sigma}_{y} In addition, at the moment when the outer wall is reached, the plastic deformation is still zero. {e}^{D}(b)=\frac{1}{2\mu }{\tau}^{D}(b)\iff \frac{({\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}(b)-{\tau}_{\theta \theta }(b))}{2\mu }={\ln\left(\frac{1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}}{r-u}\right)\mid }_{b}+\lnb When the plastic zone leads to the outer wall, one of the two components of the stress tensor is known in all point via (13). The equilibrium relationship (7) and the spherical part of the behavior (10) allow the entire determination of the stress field, as well as the Jacobian of the transformation. In fact, unlike the case of small deformations, these two equations are coupled. They are written: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}\frac{\partial {\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}}{\partial r}-{\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}\frac{\partial \lnj}{\partial r}+\frac{2}{r}({\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}-{\tau}_{\theta \theta })=0\\ \mathrm{3K}\lnj={\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}+2{\tau}_{\theta \theta }\end{array} Substitute the definition of \lnj in the first equation of (15) and obtain: \frac{\partial}{\partial r}\left({\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}-\frac{{\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}^{2}}{\mathrm{2K}}\right)=\frac{2}{r}{\sigma}_{y} This equation is easily integrated by taking into account the boundary condition (8) {\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}-\frac{{\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}^{2}}{\mathrm{2K}}=2{\sigma}_{y}\ln\left(\frac{r}{b}\right) The stress field can be deduced by solving this second-order equation. The root choice is fixed by the fact that it is a compression stress, therefore negative. The \lnj volume change field is deduced from it through (15): \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{\tau}_{\mathit{rr}}(r)=K-\sqrt{{K}^{2}-\mathrm{4K}{\sigma}_{y}\ln\left(\frac{r}{b}\right)}\\ \lnj(r)=1-\sqrt{1-4\frac{{\sigma}_{y}}{K}\ln\left(\frac{r}{b}\right)}+\frac{2{\sigma}_{y}}{\mathrm{3K}}\end{array} The kinematic relationship (6) may also be rewritten: \frac{\partial}{\partial r}\left({(r-u)}^{3}\right)=\frac{3{r}^{2}}{\exp\lnj} Taking into account the b-u(b)=B definition, this is derived by integration: {(r-u)}^{3}={B}^{2}-{\int}_{r}^{b}\frac{3{\rho}^{2}}{\exp\lnj(\rho )}d\rho The primitive in (20) will have to be calculated numerically. One can also rely on the relationship (19) to simply express the distorted radius in b . Indeed, in r=b , the volume change is: \lnj(b)=\frac{2{\sigma}_{y}}{\mathrm{3K}} The equation (19) is written in r=b : \left(1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\right)=\frac{{b}^{2}}{{B}^{2}}\exp\left(-\frac{2{\sigma}_{y}}{\mathrm{3K}}\right) The condition of continuity (14) allows the radius of the distorted sphere to be fixed, as it is expressed again: \left(1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}\right)={\left(\frac{b}{B}\right)}^{-1}\exp\left(\frac{{\sigma}_{y}}{2\mu }\right) From (22) and (23), the deformed outer radius is deduced: \frac{b}{B}=\exp\left(\frac{{\sigma}_{y}}{3}\left(\frac{1}{2\mu }+\frac{2}{\mathrm{3K}}\right)\right) The knowledge of deformation and stress allows the determination of the cumulative plastic deformation field p , Indeed, its evolution is governed by the tensor equation (12). Specifically, it turns out that the {\tau}^{D}/{\tau}_{\mathit{eq}} direction is constant which allows the plastic deformation to be integrated simply: {e}^{p}=p\left({\vec{e}}_{r}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{r}-\frac{1}{2}{\vec{e}}_{\theta}\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\theta}-\frac{1}{2}{\vec{e}}_{\phi }\otimes {\vec{e}}_{\phi }\right) Then by substituting this expression in the first equation of (12), we deduce: p(r)=\frac{2}{3}({e}_{\theta \theta }-{e}_{\mathit{rr}})-\frac{{\sigma}_{y}}{3\mu }=\frac{2}{3}\left(\lnr-\frac{{\sigma}_{y}}{2\mu }+\ln\frac{1-\frac{\partial u}{\partial r}}{r-u}\right) Where the expression of the field of displacement is now known as appres (20). Finally, the inner boundary condition allows to determine the critical loading level for which the plastic zone reaches the outer wall. Indeed, the inner radius decompressed is given implicitly by the relationship (20) expressed precisely in r=a : {\int}_{r}^{b}\frac{3{\rho}^{2}}{\exp\lnj(\rho )}d\rho ={B}^{3}-{A}^{3} 2.2 Quantities and reference results The reference quantitiess are the stress trace and the cumulative plastic deformation in distorted configuration for the points of Gauss with the smallest and largest r. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution The solution being analytical, we have no uncertainty. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. v6.04.232 SSNV232 – Triaxial drained test with MOHR_COULOMB and MohrCoulombAS laws v6.04.232 SSNV232 – Triaxial drained test with MOHR_COULOMB and MohrCoulombAS laws Summary A triaxial calculation in pure mechanics (equivalent to drained hydraulic conditions) is performed with the MOHR_COULOMB (modellings A and B) and MohrCoulombAS (modellings C and D) laws. The calculated solutions are compared to an analytical solution. This test consists of four modellings: - A: Modelling on point hardware (SIMU_POINT_MAT) with MOHR_COULOMB law; - B: 3D Modelling (STAT_NON_LINE) with MOHR_COULOMB law; - C: Modelling on point hardware (SIMU_POINT_MAT) with MohrCoulombAS law; - D: 3D Modelling (STAT_NON_LINE) with MohrCoulombAS law. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The triaxial test is performed on a single finite element isoparametric cubic \mathit{CUB}8 . The length of each edge is 1 . The different facets of this cube are mesh cells groups named \mathit{HAUT} , \mathit{BAS} , \mathit{DEVANT} , \mathit{DERRIERE} , \mathit{DROIT} and \mathit{GAUCHE} . The mesh-cell group SYM also contains the mesh cells \mathit{BAS} , \mathit{DEVANT} and \mathit{GAUCHE} groups; the mesh-cell group \mathit{COTE} groups of mesh cells \mathit{DERRIERE} and \mathit{DROIT} . 1.2 Material properties The elastic properties are: - isotropic compressibility module: K=516,2\mathit{MPa} - shear module: \mu =238,2\mathit{MPa} The common parameters of the MOHR_COULOMB and MohrCoulombAS laws are: - Friction angle (Friction Angle): \mathrm{\phi }=33° - Dilatancy Angle: \psi =27° - Cohesion (Cohesion): {c}_{0}=1\mathit{kPa} The parameters specific to MohrCoulombAS are: - Transition angle (Transition Angle): {\theta}_{T}=29.9° - TensionCutOff: a=0.25C/\tan(\varphi ) - Hardening Hardening Parameter (HardeningCoef): {h}_{C}=0 The {\theta}_{T}=29.9° parameter was selected to approximate the original (single) criterion of Mohr-Coulomb ( {\theta}_{T}=30° ); and by ensuring that convergence was not too degraded. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads A triaxial test consists of imposing a vertical load variation on the test piece while maintaining the constant lateral pressure. It can be drained (the fluid pore pressure does not vary during the test) or undrained (the valve is closed: the fluid pore pressure evolves in the sample). Here, we are interested in the drained case, simpler, because it does not involve the influence of the fluid pore pressure and modelisable by this pure mechanical calculation . In the model considered (cases of models B and D), cubic l-element represents one eighth of the sample. The limit conditions are therefore as follows: - The symmetry conditions: - {u}_{z}=0 on mesh cell \mathit{BAS} group - {u}_{x}=0 on mesh cell \mathit{GAUCHE} group - {u}_{y}=0 on mesh cell \mathit{DEVANT} group - Side pressure conditions: - {P}_{n}=1 on mesh cell \mathit{COTE} group - The loading conditions: - {P}_{n}=1 on mesh cell \mathit{HAUT} Group (phase 1) - {u}_{z}=-1 on mesh cell \mathit{HAUT} Group (Phase 2) The load is carried out in two phases: - Initiation . Isotropic loading between t\in \left[-2;0\right]s : the pressure p on the mesh cells \mathit{COTE} and \mathit{HAUT} groups varies from 0 to p={P}_{0}=50\mathit{kPa} , the isotropic preconsolidation pressure in the intial state; - triaxial test : displacement imposed on mesh-cell group \mathrm{HAUT} with t varying between t\in \left[0-30\right]s and {u}_{z} varying between {u}_{z}\in \left[0;-0,3\right]\mathit{mm} . The total vertical {\epsilon}_{zz} deformation is 0,03\text{\%} ; 1.4 analytical solution The loads applied to the cubic sample are shown below: - {\epsilon}_{1}=F\left(t\right) - {\sigma}_{2}={\sigma}_{3}={\sigma}_{0} The behaviour of the sample is governed by Mohr-Coulomb law, which states: \left\{\begin{array}{c}f\left({\sigma}_{1},{\sigma}_{3}\right)=\mid {\sigma}_{1}-{\sigma}_{3}\mid +\left({\sigma}_{1}+{\sigma}_{3}\right)\sin\varphi -{\mathrm{2c}}_{0}\cos\varphi \le 0\\ {\sigma}_{1}\ge {\sigma}_{2}={\sigma}_{3}\end{array}\right. It is associated with the plastic flow potential: g\left({\sigma}_{1},{\sigma}_{3}\right)=\mid {\sigma}_{1}-{\sigma}_{3}\mid +\left({\sigma}_{1}+{\sigma}_{3}\right)\sin\psi -{\mathrm{2c}}_{0}\cos\psi so that, by noting t=\sin\psi and \xi =\mathit{signe}\left({\sigma}_{1}-{\sigma}_{3}\right) , the flow law is written: \left\{\begin{array}{c}f({\sigma}_{1},{\sigma}_{3})\ge 0\\ \frac{\partial g}{\partial {\sigma}_{1}}=\dot{{\varepsilon}_{1}^{p}}=\dot{\lambda}(t+\xi )\\ \frac{\partial g}{\partial {\sigma}_{2}}=\dot{{\varepsilon}_{2}^{p}}=\dot{{\varepsilon}_{3}^{p}}=\dot{\lambda}(t-\xi )\end{array}\right. where \dot{\lambda} represents the plastic multiplier. So the two unknowns of the problem are {\sigma}_{1} (or {\varepsilon}_{3} ) and \dot{\lambda} . 1.4.1 Elastically adjusted resolution The equation is satisfied. \left\{ \begin{array}{l} \sigma_1 = \underbrace{(K + \tfrac{4}{3}G)}_{E}\varepsilon_1^{e} + 2\Bigl(K - \tfrac{2}{3}G\Bigr)\varepsilon_3^{e} \\ \sigma_3 = \Bigl(K - \tfrac{2}{3}G\Bigr)\varepsilon_1^{e} + \Bigl(K - \tfrac{2}{3}G\Bigr)\varepsilon_3^{e} + \Bigl(K + \tfrac{4}{3}G\Bigr)\varepsilon_3^{e} \\ \phantom{\sigma_3 =}\ = \underbrace{\Bigl(K - \tfrac{2}{3}G\Bigr)}_{C}\,\varepsilon_1^{e} + \underbrace{2\Bigl(K + \tfrac{1}{3}G\Bigr)}_{D}\varepsilon_3^{e} \end{array} \right. Knowing that {\sigma}_{3}={\sigma}_{0} , it is directly deduced from that: \dot{{\varepsilon}_{3}^{e}}=-\frac{C}{D}\dot{{\varepsilon}_{1}^{e}} 1.4.2 Resolution in plastic mode The equation is satisfied. Either {\sigma}^{p}={\sigma}^{e} the elastic prediction given by the equations , the final stress {\sigma}^{+} is written: {\sigma}^{+}=\mathrm{ℂ}.{\varepsilon}^{+}={\sigma}^{p}-\dot{\lambda}\mathrm{ℂ}.\overrightarrow{{n}_{g}} where \mathrm{ℂ}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}E& \mathrm{2C}\\ C& D\end{array}\right] represents the linear elasticity and \overrightarrow{{n}_{g}}=(t+\xi ,t-\xi ) tensor. The plastic multiplier is calculated by writing f({\sigma}^{+})=0 , i.e.: \begin{array}{cc}(s+\xi )(K+\frac{4}{3}G){\varepsilon}_{1}^{+}+2(s+\xi )(K-\frac{2}{3}G){\varepsilon}_{3}^{+}& +\\ (s-\xi )(K-\frac{2}{3}G){\varepsilon}_{1}^{+}+2(s-\xi )(K+\frac{G}{3}){\varepsilon}_{3}^{+}& =2{c}_{0}\cos\phi \end{array} \mathrm{\iff}\ \underbrace{2\bigl(Ks + G(\xi + \tfrac{s}{3})\bigr)}_{A}\,\varepsilon_1^{+} + \underbrace{2\bigl(2Ks - G(\xi + \tfrac{s}{3})\bigr)}_{B}\,\varepsilon_3^{+} = 2c_0\cos\phi which gives, by replacing: \left\{ \begin{array}{c}{\varepsilon}_{1}^{+}={\varepsilon}_{1}^{e}-\dot{\lambda}(t+\xi )\\ {\varepsilon}_{3}^{+}={\varepsilon}_{3}^{e}-\dot{\lambda}(t-\xi )\end{array}\right. in , we get: \dot{\lambda}\,\underbrace{ \left[A(t+\xi) + B(t-\xi)\right] }_{\mathit{BB}}= -2c_0\cos\phi + A\,\varepsilon_1^{e} + B\,\varepsilon_3^{e}= f(\sigma^{e}) , either: \dot{\lambda}=\frac{f({\sigma}^{e})}{\mathit{BB}} 1.4.3 Correction of imbalance {\sigma}_{3}^{+}={\sigma}_{0} should be checked. A small \delta virtual variation of the solution is assumed. \delta {\sigma}_{3}^{+} is sought, i.e.: \delta {\sigma}_{3}^{+}=C\delta {\epsilon}_{1}^{e}+E\delta {\epsilon}_{3}^{e}-\delta \dot{\lambda}C\left(t+\xi \right)-\delta \dot{\lambda}E\left(t-\xi \right) Knowing that \dot{\lambda} is given by , we have: \delta \dot{\lambda}=\frac{A}{\mathit{BB}}\delta {\epsilon}_{1}^{e}+\frac{B}{\mathit{BB}}\delta {\epsilon}_{3}^{e} that we report in . In addition to the equation, the following expression is also obtained for \delta {\sigma}_{1}^{+} : \delta {\sigma}_{1}^{+}=\left[E-A\frac{E\left(t+\xi \right)+C\left(t-\xi \right)}{\mathit{BB}}\right]\delta {\epsilon}_{1}^{e}+\left[C-B\frac{E\left(t+\xi \right)+C\left(t-\xi \right)}{\mathit{BB}}\right]\delta {\epsilon}_{3}^{e} The expression of the coherent tangent matrix \mathit{DSDE} is therefore written: \mathit{DSDE}=\left[\begin{array}{cc}E-A\frac{E(t+\xi )+C(t-\xi )}{\mathit{BB}}& C-B\frac{E(t+\xi )+C(t-\xi )}{\mathit{BB}}\\ C-A\frac{C(t+\xi )+E(t-\xi )}{\mathit{BB}}& E-B\frac{C(t+\xi )+E(t-\xi )}{\mathit{BB}}\end{array}\right] 1.5 Results The solutions are post-treated with point C for {\sigma}_{zz} vertical and horizontal stresses, as well as {\epsilon}_{v}^{p} plastic density deformation and \mid {\epsilon}_{d}^{p}\mid =\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}\left(\epsilon -\frac{{\epsilon}_{v}^{p}}{3}I\right):\left(\epsilon -\frac{{\epsilon}_{v}^{p}}{3}I\right)} plastic deviator deformation. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Modelling characteristics The A Modelling is performed on a hardware point using SIMU_POINT_MAT. v6.04.233 SSNV233 – Torsion test with Mohr-Coulomb law v6.04.233 SSNV233 – Torsion test with Mohr-Coulomb law Summary: A twist test is performed with Mohr-Coulomb law. The objective of the test is to check the correct convergence of the model in the presence of rotation of the main stresses. The calculated tangent matrix is compared to that obtained by disturbance. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A torsion test is repeated on a hollow cylinder subjected to {P}_{i} internal and external containment pressures, {P}_{e} vertical force, and M twist moment. This test is schematized by a cubic sample (a material point) subjected to {\sigma}_{z} , {\sigma}_{r} and {\sigma}_{\theta} containment stresses, and {\epsilon}_{z\theta }=M(t) shear deformation ( Figure ). If {P}_{i}={P}_{e}={\sigma}_{0} and F=\frac{2{\sigma}_{0}}{\pi} , the following containment values shall be obtained: - {\sigma}_{\theta}={\sigma}_{r}={\sigma}_{0} - {\sigma}_{z}=3{\sigma}_{0} The following values of the main constraints are then used: - {\sigma}_{1}=2{\sigma}_{0}+\mid {\sigma}_{z\theta }\mid - {\sigma}_{2}={\sigma}_{0} - {\sigma}_{3}=2{\sigma}_{0}-\mid {\sigma}_{z\theta }\mid But above all, the main axes rotate at an \alpha angle equal to [:ref: 1 ]: \alpha (t)=\frac{1}{2}\arctan\left(\frac{2{\sigma}_{z\theta }(t)}{{\sigma}_{z}-{\sigma}_{\theta}}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\arctan\left(\frac{{\sigma}_{z\theta }(t)}{{\sigma}_{0}}\right) Figure 1.1-a: Schématisation de l'essai de torsion sur un cylindre creux 1.2 Sample properties The elastic parameters are: - isotropic compressibility module: K=516,2\mathit{MPa} - shear module: \mu =238,2\mathit{MPa} The Mohr-Coulomb Law parameters are: - friction angle: \phi =33° - characteristic angle: \Psi =27° - Cohesion: {c}_{0}=1\mathit{kPa} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The torsion test presented here is performed on a material point with the SIMU_POINT_MAT command. The following constraints are imposed: - {\sigma}_{xx}={\sigma}_{yy}=-50\mathit{kPa} - {\sigma}_{zz}=-150\mathit{kPa} The shear deformation imposed {\epsilon}_{yz} varies linearly between t=0 and 100\mathit{sec} from 0 to 0,01\text{\%} to N=10 time step. 2 reference solution We're checking that {N}^{\mathit{num}}<{N}^{\mathit{per}} is on every time step. The calculated tangent matrix is therefore better than that obtained by disturbance, as shown in paragraph § 4, by better taking into account the multiple mechanisms of constitutive law. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The Modelling is performed on a hardware point with SIMU_POINT_MAT. Redistribution of the time step is active. The convergence criterion is RESI_GLOB_RELA = {10}^{-10} . 3.2 Tested quantities and results The difference is measured at each moment between the number of iterations of Newton given by the calculated tangent matrix \mathit{NB}\text{\_}\mathit{ITER}\text{\_}1 and that given by the tangent matrix by \mathit{NB}\text{\_}\mathit{ITER}\text{\_}2 disturbance. The test is to verify that \mathit{NB}\text{\_}\mathit{ITER}\text{\_}1-\mathit{NB}\text{\_}\mathit{ITER}\text{\_}2\le 0 at each moment: | t\left[\mathit{sec}\right] | \mathit{NB}\text{\_}\mathit{ITER}\text{\_}1-\mathit{NB}\text{\_}\mathit{ITER}\text{\_}2 | Reference value | Tolerance \left[\text{\%}\right] | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 10 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | 20 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | 30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | 40 | 0 | 0 | 0 | | 50 | -8 | 0 | 0 | | 60 | -11 | 0 | 0 | | 70 | -11 | 0 | 0 | | 80 | -11 | 0 | 0 | | 90 | -11 | 0 | 0 | | 100 | -11 | 0 | 0 | 4 Summary of the results The figure below presents a comparison of the iterations of Newton between the case of the calculated tangent matrix and that of the perturbation tangent matrix. v6.04.234 SSNV234 - Basic ENDO_FISS_EXP Law and PRED_ELAS Modelling Pilotage Validation v6.04.234 SSNV234 - Basic ENDO_FISS_EXP Law and PRED_ELAS Modelling Pilotage Validation Summary: The purpose of this test is to validate the integration algorithm of the constitutive law ENDO_FISS_EXP with gradient of internal variables and the PRED_ELAS control available for this law. The problem studied is a homogeneous strained stress imposed for which an analytical solution can be obtained. The different modellings processed are: - Modelling A ( \mathrm{2D} ): D_PLAN_GRAD_VARI Modelling is used. - Model B ( \mathrm{3D} ): 3D_GRAD_VARI modelling is used. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry According to \mathrm{2D} or \mathrm{3D} Modelling, one considers a square or a cube on the side 2 \text{mm} respectively. 1.2 Material properties The material obeys the constitutive law fragile elastic ENDO_FISS_EXP gradient damage (D_PLAN_GRAD_VARI and 3D_GRAD_VARI). The macroscopic data correspond to: | E=30000\text{MPa} | Young's modulus | | --- | --- | | \nu =0.2 | Poisson's ratio | | {G}_{f}=0.1{\text{N/mm}}^{2} | Cracking energy | | p=5 | Parameter of shape | | {f}_{t}=2.986\text{MPa} | Tensile limit | | {f}_{c}=29.86\text{MPa} | Compression limit | | | | | D=50\text{mm} | Half width of the damage strip | The choice of these values of ft and fc in relation to the François criterion in ENDO_FISS_EXP corresponds to a confined tensile limit of s c = 3 MPa. Furthermore, the internal parameters of the model that intervene in the analytical solution are equal to: k=1.5\times {10}^{-3}\text{MPa} ; m=11.111 ; \gamma =9.534\times {10}^{3} In the test, they are calculated by the DEFI_MATER_GC macro-command. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The displacements are imposed in all nodes of the structure, so as to match the desired homogeneous deformation. Specifically, the displacement in one node of X coordinates is valid: u(x)=\epsilon \cdot x . First, a uniaxial tensile deformation is imposed and then a compression deformation is discharged until a compression deformation is imposed to verify the effect of the restoration of rigidity in compression. 1.4 Initial conditions None. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution This problem admits an analytical solution. During the tensile phase, the relationship that to the imposed deformation \varepsilon combines the homogeneous damage level a is determined. Here we adopt a uniaxial deformation of the form: \epsilon =\epsilon n\otimes n\text{où}∥n∥=1\text{et}\epsilon >0 This is therefore a problem in confined uniaxial traction. The problem being homogeneous, damage (laden) and deformation are linked by the consistency relationship: A'(a)\Gamma (\epsilon )+\omega '(a)=0 with \omega (a)=\mathit{ka},A(a)=\frac{{(1-a)}^{2}}{{(1-a)}^{2}+\mathit{ma}(1+\mathit{pa})} The G function is based on the form of the criterion that defines the elasticity domain, cf. R5.03.28 or, in more detail, [Lorentz, 2016]. In the present case of a confined uniaxial traction / compression, it is simply written: \Gamma (\epsilon )=\frac{1}{2}{E}_{c}{\epsilon}^{2} où {E}_{c}=\lambda +2\mu This is why we simply deduce the relationship between \epsilon and a : \epsilon =\sqrt{\frac{-2k}{{E}_{c}A'(a)}} For the test case, the deformation will increase to such a level as the level of a=0.2 zero damage and it will be tested that the damage is well at its target value. In a second step, the deformation is released and then compression is imposed to an {\epsilon}_{\mathit{comp}}=-2{\sigma}^{c}/{E}_{c} level. Damage is no longer evolving. The stress-deformation relationship is written: \sigma =A(a){E}_{c}\epsilon +\frac{1}{2}(1-A(a)){E}_{c}S'(\epsilon ) où S(\epsilon )={\langle -\epsilon \rangle }^{2}\exp(\frac{1}{\gamma \epsilon }) The discharge is therefore performed linearly with a A(a){E}_{c} splintering rigidity module. Then, in the compression phase, the model gradually restores the rigidity according to the above relationship. The test checks that the stress level is the one corresponding to the analytical relationship. In practice, rather than projecting the stress tensor to the direction of the stress, we ensure that the strain energy obtained via the POST_ELEM command (factor keyword TRAV_EXT component TRAV_ELAS) is well equal to the expected value, i.e.: \frac{\mathit{vol}(\Omega )}{2}\sigma :ϵ=\frac{\mathit{vol}(\Omega )}{2}\sigma ϵ where \mathit{vol}(\Omega ) is the volume of the element (4 mm2 or 8 mm3) 2.2 Baseline In flat deformations, one adopts a direction of n=(1/\sqrt{5,}2/\sqrt{5}) solicitation. In 3D, it is equal to n=(1/\sqrt{14,}2/\sqrt{14,}3/\sqrt{14}) . One attaches as target a damage a=0.2 ; this corresponds to a intensity of \epsilon =2.86\times {10}^{-4} solicitation after the reference solution above. The load is applied by PRED_ELAS control technique, in which the maximum terminal is fixed to achieve the above \varepsilon deformation level. It will be checked that the corresponding damage reaches 0.2. In compression, the required deformation level is {\epsilon}_{\mathit{comp}}=-1.8\times {10}^{-4} for a stress of {\sigma}_{\mathit{comp}}=-4.537\text{MPa} . 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution None. 2.4 Bibliographical references Lorentz E. (2016) A nonlocal damage model for plain concrete consist with cohesive fracture. Submitted to J. Mech. Phys. Solids. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics D_PLAN_GRAD_VARI Modelling with a single mesh cell, element QUAD8. Loading in direction n=(1/\sqrt{5,}2/\sqrt{5}) . 3.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes : 8 Number and types of mesh cells: 1 QUAD8, 4 SEG3 3.3 Tested quantities and results of Modelling A The damage to the mesh cell is tested in three nodes, the nodes value being obtained by extrapolation (CHAM_NO ‘VARI_NOEU, component V1) and the strain energy after compression. | Identification | Reference | Type | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | V1( X=2 , Y=0 ) | 0.2 | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | | V1( X=2 , Y=1 ) | 0.2 | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | | V1( X=2 , Y=2 ) | 0.2 | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | | TRAV_ELAS | 1.633\times {10}^{-3} | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics A 3D_GRAD_VARI model with a single mesh cell, element HEXA20. Loading in direction n=(1/\sqrt{14,}2/\sqrt{14,}3/\sqrt{14}) . 4.2 Mesh characteristics Number of nodes : 20 Number and types of mesh cells: 1 HEXA20, 6 QUAD8, 8 SEG3 4.3 Tested quantities and results of Modelling B The damage to the mesh cell is tested in three nodes, the nodes value being obtained by extrapolation (CHAM_NO ‘VARI_NOEU, component V1) and the strain energy after compression. | Identification | Reference | Type | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | V1 ( X=2 , Y=0 ) | 0.6 | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | | V1 ( X=2 , Y=1 ) | 0.6 | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | | V1 ( X=2 , Y=2 ) | 0.6 | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | | TRAV_ELAS | 3.267\times {10}^{-3} | ANALYTIQUE | RELATIF– 0,1% | 5 Summary of the results This test case is made on a single mesh cell, therefore it is the homogeneous damage response that is recovered numerically. The reference solution is obtained by placing itself on the damage threshold. There is a very good agreement between the Modelling and the reference solution. In compression, the rigidity restoration is tested, also satisfactorily. However, the non-local part of the law is not tested here.

v6.04.246 SSNV246 - Application of a pressure distributed over the lips of a XFEM curved interface through a column v6.04.246 SSNV246 - Application of a pressure distributed over the lips of a XFEM curved interface through a column Summary: This is a test to validate the contact facets of XFEM integration elements. The contact facets used by default are not from the integration elements subs and do not give the possibility to have quadratic 3D contact facets. It is possible to enable the recovery of contact facets from the integration elements subs into the MODI_MODELE_XFEM operator with the DECOUPE_FACETTE='SOUS_ELEMENTS' key word. Linear and quadratic facets in 2D as well as in 3D have the advantage of being in line with the integration elements subs since they are chosen from the sides of the elements subs of the 2D integration and the faces of the elements subs of the 3D integration. This recovery mode also has the following advantage: the nodes coordinates of these facets are not recalculated as is the case by default, since these nodes are recovered during the cutting that is performed in TOPOSE. In this test, the correct operation of the recovery of these facets is ensured when mechanical pressure is applied to the lips of the interface. The results obtained are compared to an analytical solution. The geometry is two-dimensional, an example of the use of the contact facets from the integration elements subs for a 3D geometry is presented in the test case ssnv247 v6.04.247. A "lsn" curve is chosen voluntarily representing the interface to appreciate the performance gain brought by quadratic "facetization". 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry of the problem This is a square on the L=10m side. This bar has an interface type discontinuity (unmesh interface which is introduced into the model via the level-sets thanks to the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator). The square is thus completely crossed by discontinuity (at the approximation of the field of displacement, only Heaviside enrichment is taken into account). The discontinuity is circular of center O(0,-2) and radius R=9m . The geometry of the problem is represented on the Figure. The contact facets used by default are not from the integration elements subs and do not give the possibility to have quadratic 3D contact facets. It is possible to enable the recovery of contact facets from the integration elements subs into the MODI_MODELE_XFEM operator with the DECOUPE_FACETTE='SOUS_ELEMENTS' key word. Linear and quadratic facets in 2D as well as in 3D have the advantage of being in line with the integration elements subs since they are chosen from the sides of the elements subs of the 2D integration and the faces of the elements subs of the 3D integration. This recovery mode also has the following advantage: the nodes coordinates of these facets are not recalculated as is the case by default, since these nodes are recovered during the cutting that is performed in TOPOSE. In this test, the correct operation of the recovery of these facets is ensured when mechanical pressure is applied to the lips of an interface for a three-dimensional geometry. The results obtained are compared to an analytical solution. A iso-zero "lsn" curve representing the interface is chosen voluntarily to appreciate the performance gain brought by quadratic "facetization". 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry of the problem This is an eighth of {R}_{i}=1m inner ray sphere, {R}_{e}=2m outer ray sphere and O(0,0,0) cente. This part of the sphere is crossed by an interface-type discontinuity (unmesh interface that is introduced into the model via the level-set via the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator), R=\mathrm{1.5m} concentric radius. The Figure shows the geometry of the column. 1.2 Material properties The parameters given in the Table correspond to the parameters used for the 4 modellings. The behavior is elastic ('ELAS'). | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | Elastic parameters | Young's modulus E(\mathit{en}\mathit{MPa}) Poisson's ratio \nu Thermal expansion coefficient \alpha (\mathit{en}{K}^{\text{-1}}) | 5800 0 0 | Table 1.2-1 : Material properties 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading The following Dirichlet conditions shall be applied: - on the lower face [ABDC], the following z moves are blocked {u}_{\text{z}}=0 , - on the face [ABFE], the following y moves are blocked {u}_{\text{y}}=0 , - on the face [CDFE], the following x moves are blocked {u}_{\text{x}}=0 , - on the BDF outer cap and the ACE inner cap, the movements are blocked in all directions ( {u}_{\text{x}}=0 , {u}_{\text{y}}=0 and {u}_{\text{z}}=0 ). The load is as follows: - On each of the lips of the interface to r=R a uniform distributed pressure p=10\mathit{MPa} is imposed via AFFE_CHAR_MECA and the keywordFISSURE dePRES_REP. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation This is an analytical solution. Taking into account the boundary conditions, the displacements can be obtained from the analytical resolution of the motion quantity conservation equation. By neglecting the gravity, the equation is written (in total constraints): \text{Div}(\sigma )=0 The Poisson \nu module being zero, and being elastic in the case, we have \sigma =Eϵ . The volume studied is spherical symmetry, made up of homogeneous and isotropic material; the boundary conditions also possess spherical symmetry. Therefore, a solution of the problem is sought in a system of (r,\theta ,\varphi ) spherical coordinates such that the fields of displacement, stress and deformation are respectively of the form: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{u}_{\text{r}}=h(r)\\ {u}_{\theta}={u}_{\varphi}=0\end{array} \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{\sigma}_{\text{rr}}={f}_{1}(r)\\ \begin{array}{c}{\sigma}_{\theta \theta }={\sigma}_{\varphi \varphi }={g}_{1}(r)\\ {\sigma}_{r\theta }={\sigma}_{r\varphi }={\sigma}_{\theta \varphi }=0\end{array}\end{array} \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{ϵ}_{\text{rr}}={f}_{2}(r)\\ \begin{array}{c}{ϵ}_{\theta \theta }={ϵ}_{\varphi \varphi }={g}_{2}(r)\\ {ϵ}_{r\theta }={ϵ}_{r\varphi }={ϵ}_{\theta \varphi }=0\end{array}\end{array} The \text{Div}(\sigma )=0 equilibrium equation is then reduced to: \frac{d{\sigma}_{\text{rr}}}{\mathit{dr}}+\frac{2}{r}\ast ({\sigma}_{\text{rr}}-{\sigma}_{\theta \theta })=0 The static boundary conditions are of the shape: {\sigma}_{\text{rr}}(R)=-p The kinematic equations have the form: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{ϵ}_{\text{rr}}=\frac{{\mathit{du}}_{\text{r}}}{\mathit{dr}}\\ {ϵ}_{\theta \theta }=\frac{{u}_{\text{r}}}{r}\end{array} is finally: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{\sigma}_{\text{rr}}=E\ast \frac{{\mathit{du}}_{\text{r}}}{\mathit{dr}}\\ {\sigma}_{\theta \theta }=E\ast \frac{{u}_{\text{r}}}{r}\end{array} By replacing these two relationships in the equilibrium equation we obtain: \frac{\mathit{d²}{u}_{\text{r}}}{\mathit{dr²}}+\frac{2}{r}\ast (\frac{{\mathit{du}}_{\text{r}}}{\mathit{dr}}-\frac{{u}_{\text{r}}}{r})=0 i.e. \frac{d}{\mathit{dr}}(\frac{1}{\mathit{r²}}\frac{d({\mathit{r²u}}_{r})}{\mathit{dr}})=0 The solution of this differential equation is: {u}_{r}(r)={C}_{1}r+\frac{{C}_{2}}{\mathit{r²}} . The solution sought is discontinuous in R , and this equation is solved separately on both [{R}_{i},R] and [R,{R}_{e}] domains . Finally: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{u}_{\text{r}}(r)={C}_{1}r+\frac{{C}_{2}}{\mathit{r²}}\text{}\mathit{sur}[{R}_{i},R]\\ {u}_{r}(r)={C}_{3}r+\frac{{C}_{4}}{\mathit{r²}}\text{}\mathit{sur}[R,{R}_{e}]\end{array} Based on the kinematic boundary conditions, {u}_{r}({R}_{i})={u}_{r}({R}_{e})=0 so \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{C}_{1}{R}_{i}+\frac{{C}_{2}}{{R}_{i}\mathrm{²}}=0\\ {C}_{3}{R}_{e}+\frac{{C}_{4}}{{R}_{e}\mathrm{²}}=0\end{array} In addition {\sigma}_{\text{rr}}=E\ast \frac{{\mathit{du}}_{\text{r}}}{\mathit{dr}}=\lbrace \begin{array}{c}E\ast {C}_{1}-2E\ast \frac{{C}_{2}}{\mathit{r³}}\text{}\mathit{sur}[{R}_{i},R]\\ E\ast {C}_{3}-2E\ast \frac{{C}_{4}}{\mathit{r³}}\text{}\mathit{sur}[R,{R}_{e}]\end{array} therefore according to the static boundary conditions: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{C}_{1}-2\ast \frac{{C}_{2}}{\mathit{R³}}=-\frac{p}{E}\\ {C}_{3}-2\ast \frac{{C}_{4}}{\mathit{R³}}=-\frac{p}{E}\end{array} . v6.04.259 SSNV259– Circular crack in a solid cylinder under tension v6.04.259 SSNV259– Circular crack in a solid cylinder under tension Summary : The aim of this test is to verify all keywords of the POST_JMOD macro_command except for ETAT_INIT. The testcase allows the computation of J-integrals in the presence of an initial stress state, within the framework of linear elasticity. 1 Reference problem 2.1 Geometry As shown in Figure 1, the structure under investigation is a cylinders (of radius b=10mm) containing a circulating penny-shaped crack subjected to a uniform tensile loading condition. The crack is circulating (penny shape crack) of radius a=2mm, as shown in Figure 1. The cubes length is L=10a. They write: - z=H top edge: T={\sigma}_{zz}{e}_{z}+{\sigma}_{\mathit{rz}}{e}_{r} - z=0 lower edge: T=-{\sigma}_{zz}{e}_{z}-{\sigma}_{\mathit{rz}}{e}_{r} - r={R}_{i} inner wall: T=-{\sigma}_{\mathit{rr}}{e}_{r}-{\sigma}_{\mathit{rz}}{e}_{z} - r={R}_{e} exterior wall: T={\sigma}_{\mathit{rr}}{e}_{r}+{\sigma}_{\mathit{rz}}{e}_{z} The stress field is then at balance with the load imposed. A purely deviatoric loading allows the porosity due to the growth of cavities to be cancelled, which allows the display of analytical solutions. The problem is implemented at the scale of the material point (SIMU_POINT_MAT): it is directly the stress T that is imposed by ensuring that it remains in a positive hardening regime. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The problem is dealt with at the point hardware scale. 1.2 Material properties The material obeys constitutive law GTN, enabling germination modelling, considering linear isotropic hardening and not introducing any coalescence. Since the stress trace is zero, the traces of the elastic, plastic and total deformations are also zero. And the Jacobian of J transformation remains equal to 1. By noting d={q}_{1}f and {d}_{0}={q}_{1}{f}_{0} , one can express the equivalent stress of GTN: {T}_{\text{ }}=\frac{{T}_{\mathit{eq}}}{1-d} In plastic conditions, the consistency condition establishes the link between the stress and the hardening variable: {T}_{\mathit{eq}}=(1-d)({R}_{0}+{R}_{H}\kappa ) The elastic deformation is the same as the shear module with \mu : {E}^{e}=\frac{{T}_{\mathit{eq}}}{2\mu }{D}^{0} The law of plastic evolution is reduced to: \dot{{E}^{p}}=\frac{3}{2}\frac{\dot{\kappa}}{1-d}{D}^{0} In particular, the equivalent plastic deformation shall be: {\dot{E}}_{\mathit{eq}}^{p}=\frac{\dot{\kappa}}{1-d} And finally, the evolution of porosity writes: \dot{f}=B(\kappa )\dot{\kappa}+{b}_{0}\frac{\dot{\kappa}}{1-{q}_{1}f}{\mathrm{\chi }}_{[{E}_{\mathit{eq}0}^{p};+\infty ]}({E}_{\mathit{eq}});\dot{d}={q}_{1}B(\kappa )\dot{\kappa}+{q}_{1}{b}_{0}\frac{\dot{\kappa}}{1-d}{\mathrm{\chi }}_{[{E}_{\mathit{eq}0}^{p};+\infty ]}({E}_{\mathit{eq}}) In general, the above differential equation does not allow simple analytical solution. Therefore, two cases are distinguished, which will correspond to the A and B versions of the test case. 2.1.1 Case A: {b}_{0}=0 In this case, porosity simply states: f(\kappa )={f}_{0}+\underset{0}{\overset{\kappa}{\int}}B(u)\mathit{du};d(\kappa )={d}_{0}+{q}_{1}\underset{0}{\overset{\kappa}{\int}}B(u)\mathit{du} And plastic deformation is obtained by integration of (): {E}^{p}(\kappa )=\frac{3}{2}\underset{0}{\overset{\kappa}{\int}}\frac{\mathit{du}}{1-d(u)}{D}^{0} 2.1.2 Case B: B(\kappa )=0 In this case, the differential equation () is with separable variables, easily integrating and leading to: {\left(1-d(\kappa )\right)}^{2}={\left(1-{q}_{1}{f}_{0}\right)}^{2}-2{q}_{1}{b}_{0}⟨\kappa -{\kappa}_{0}⟩;{\kappa}_{0}={E}_{\mathit{eq}0}^{p}(1-{q}_{1}{f}_{0}) And plastic deformation is again obtained via (). 2.2 Baseline The \kappa values used to obtain the reference results in the A and B cases are chosen so as to remain in the positive hardening field of the model (otherwise, the stress control is not feasible). For the test case A, \kappa =0.148 is chosen; for the test case B, \kappa =0.180 . An increasing stress is then imposed up to the {T}_{\mathit{eq}}(\kappa ) value according to (). 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution The reference results are obtained very precisely by calculating the integrals which appear in the analytical solution using a trapezoid method, the step of which is very fine. 2.4 Bibliographical references None 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics This is The problem studied corresponds to a material point. The results are compared with those obtained with the VMIS_CINE_LINE law for a particular load. The problem is implemented only in 3D (modelization A) as the programming of the behavior relationship does not depend on the spatial dimension and there is no specific formulation for either flat or 1D constraints. 1 Reference problem The problem is detailed in the reference [1], in particular the loading path. Here, it is only a brief description of its main features. It is now clear that only the elastoplastic branch of the KICHENIN_NL behavior model is mobilized; the viscoelastic branch is cancelled by the introduction of a Young's modulus {E}^{v} null. Validation of this second branch is carried out in V6.04.267. Both branches are parallel, so there is no coupling other than the sum of the stresses and the tangent operators, which justifies this validation choice. The model is reduced in this case to an elastoplastic law with linear kinematic nutrification, quite similar to the VMIS_CINE_LINE model; the latter will then serve as a reference. 1.1 Geometry This is a "point hardware" test. v6.04.301 SSNV301 - Rotating cylindrical ring subjected to thermal shock and internal pressure – Von Mises (isotropic scrubbing) v6.04.301 SSNV301 - Rotating cylindrical ring subjected to thermal shock and internal pressure – Von Mises (isotropic scrubbing) Summary: This \mathrm{3D} quasi-static nonlinear mechanical test concerns the modelling of a cylindrical ring piece and checks for the resumption of a deformation field after a transient linear thermal calculation (thermal shock: application of a thermal flux inside the cylindrical ring). Then, the calculation is repeated and the transfer of the deformation field of thermal origin is checked and the use of a follower load (centrifugal force) is used. Then, the calculation is repeated by applying an internal pressure (change of the boundary conditions). The Von Mises criterion with isotropic hardening defined by a function that depends on temperature. Comparison with numerical results of Modelling with Samcef V7.0 (module THERNL for the calculation of the transient temperature field and recapture with the MECANL module for the geometrical and material nonlinear mechanical calculation). Modelling with elements \mathrm{3D} HEXA20 and elements axisymmetric of the meaxtr6 type. A fine mesh is used to check the robustness and performance of Code_Aster. In both modellings A and B, the applied pressure is not monitored. The results obtained by SAMCEF are provided with and without following pressure. In addition, Modelling A is used to validate the use of the 'ERME_ELEM' mechanical residual error indicator on 3D modelling in the presence of rotations. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Cylinder with: | Internal radius | {R}_{i}=0.04m | | --- | --- | | Outside radius | {R}_{e}=0.08m | | Height | L=0.04m | 1.2 Material properties The material is homogeneous isotropic, linear thermoelastic. The mechanical properties of materials depend on temperature. The properties vary linearly between the 2 extreme temperatures: 0°C and 100°C . Constitutive law with linear isotropic hardening: Thermal properties and density: \lambda = 72\,\frac{J}{\mathrm{m\,s\,K}} \rho = 7860\,\frac{\mathrm{kg}}{\mathrm{m}^3} C_p = 452\,\frac{J}{\mathrm{kg\,K}} \alpha = 12\cdot 10^{-6}\,\frac{1}{K} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The thermal shock is modelled by a thermal flow of 300000W/{m}^{\mathrm{2s}} inside the cylinder. The thermal calculation and mechanical calculation are performed with 50 time step identical. A quarter of the cylinder is modelled by attaching the transverse components of the displacements to the two cross-sections of the cylinder. v6.04.401 SSNV401 – constitutive law BETON_RAG and BETON_BURGER verification: creep phenomenon v6.04.401 SSNV401 – constitutive law BETON_RAG and BETON_BURGER verification: creep phenomenon Summary: These tests validate the constitutive law BETON_RAG on a compression-supplied cube with either a stress or a deformation. The model's response is compared to solutions obtained by analytically resolving the equations that govern the R7.01.26 behavior and identical modellings made with the BETON_BÜRGER r7.01.35 behavior model. Four modellings are proposed: - Modelization A: compression creep test with a stress imposed on a cube free to deform in the direction perpendicular to the load. - Modelization B: compression creep test with deformation imposed on a cube free to deform in the direction perpendicular to the load. - Modelization C: compression creep test with a stress imposed on a confined cube (blocked transverse deformations). - Modelization D: compression creep test with deformation imposed on a confined cube (blocked transverse deformations). - Modellings E, F, G and H: the same as A, B, C and D respectively, but using a nonlinear irreversible viscosity model. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Geometry is a cube of 1\,m on the side. Geometry adopted 1.2 Mesh The mesh is made with 1 HEXA8. 1.3 Materials The material is of type BETON_RAG. The necessary characteristics are those related to the damage and creep phenomena. The material characteristics of "BETON_RAG" of this test case should not be used for studies. These parameters are not physical and are used only for mathematical verification. The material parameters used in this test case are given in v6.04.401-paramsBRAG. Note: In modellings C, D, F and H, the FLUA_SPH_KR parameter was double-folded to prevent the stresses or displacements from changing signs, making it easier to compare the numerical model to analytical solutions. A second calculation is made with the BETON_BURGER r7.01.35 model for programming quality verification purposes. The numerical resolution of the differential equation system by Laplace transforms shows a perfect coincidence with the results of code_aster. As regards non-linearly viscous simulations, the agreement between BETON_RAG and BETON_BÜRGER is satisfactory, despite a slight loss of precision of BETON_BÜRGER results due to too coarse temporal discretization. 11 Annexes This annex lists the codes that generated the analytical solutions of modellings [A], [B], [C], and [D]. The Python libraries that are used to obtain analytical solutions and calculate them are: numpy , sympy and inspect . The constant parameters used are defined in the following section of the code: Note: For C and D test cases, the k_r_sph rigidity module must be multiplied by two. The Analytical Solutions are based on Laplace transforms of the sympy module. To do this, you have to define the variables of Laplace, and the symbols used: The test case ssnv401a [Mod_lization_A] is simple enough to obtain the analytical solution can be obtained by hand. Under constant \sigma_0 uniaxial stress, deformation is the superposition of elastic solutions and transient solutions due to creep. Elastic solutions are given to the equation. {\varepsilon}^{él}_{sph} = \frac{E}{1-2\nu}\frac{{\sigma}_0}{3} {\varepsilon}^{él}_{dev,\,x} = -\frac{E}{1+\nu}\frac{{\sigma}_0}{3} {\varepsilon}^{él}_{dev,\,y} = -\frac{E}{1+\nu}\frac{{\sigma}_0}{3} {\varepsilon}^{él}_{dev,\,z} = \frac{E}{1+\nu}\frac{2{\sigma}_0}{3} Transitional solutions are given to the equation {\varepsilon}_{sph}^{f}(t)=\sigma_0\left(\frac{t}{\eta_{sph,\,irr}} - \frac{1}{k_{sph,\,r}}\left[exp\left(-\frac{k_{sph,\,r}t}{\eta_{sph,\,r}}\right)-1\right]\right) {\varepsilon}_{dev,\,x}^{f}(t)=\frac{-\sigma_0}{3}\left(\frac{t}{\eta_{dev,\,irr}} - \frac{1}{k_{dev,\,r}}\left[exp\left(-\frac{k_{dev,\,r}t}{\eta_{dev,\,r}}\right)-1\right]\right) {\varepsilon}_{dev,\,y}^{f}(t)=\frac{-\sigma_0}{3}\left(\frac{t}{\eta_{dev,\,irr}} - \frac{1}{k_{dev,\,r}}\left[exp\left(-\frac{k_{dev,\,r}t}{\eta_{dev,\,r}}\right)-1\right]\right) {\varepsilon}_{dev,\,z}^{f}(t)=\frac{2\sigma_0}{3}\left(\frac{t}{\eta_{dev,\,irr}} - \frac{1}{k_{dev,\,r}}\left[exp\left(-\frac{k_{dev,\,r}t}{\eta_{dev,\,r}}\right)-1\right]\right) To obtain the analytical solution on an i\in\lbrace{x,y,z}\rbrace component, you need only sum the i spherical and deviatoric components of the elastic participations of the equation and transients of the equation. For modellings [B], [C], and [D] analytical solutions, boundary conditions, the partition of the partly spherical and deviatoric creep and the application of a constant deformation load complicate the search for a analytical solution by hand. To remove this problem, the sympy package is used. This involves writing transfer functions in the Laplace domain, and reverse processing of Laplace. For B Modelling, the v6.04.401-ssnv401b_soluanaly allows you to calculate and display a function that allows you to calculate the analytical solution. Similarly, the v6.04.401-ssnv401c_soluanaly and v6.04.401-ssnv401d_soluanaly allow the analytical solution code of the Modelling [C] and [D].

The objective of this test is to enable the calculation of the Coulomb criterion and the correct transmission of pressure to be validated in a certain way. v6.04.509 SSNV509 – frictional contact chain with quadratic X- FEM v6.04.509 SSNV509 – frictional contact chain with quadratic X- FEM Summary: This test is intended to validate the consideration of the contact on the lips of a curved crack, limiting itself to the case where the crack completely crosses the structure (interface). The continuous method adapted to the X-FEM method with resolution by increased Lagrangien. This test involves a parallelepipedic block in compression. The interface is represented by a circular level set cutting elements with variable angles. It involves elements X-FEM \text{P2} on the move and \text{P1} on the pressure that have degrees of freedom moving in each node and degrees of freedom contact-frost on the nodes peaks. 1 Reference problem en 2D 1.1 Geometry The structure is a healthy square plate on the L=10\text{m} side. The interface is represented by a circular level set inserted into the command file using the DEFI_FISS_XFEM U4.82.08 operator given in its analytical form: {(x-5)}^{2}+{(y-11,77)}^{2}=64,27 . It was chosen to go through the structure completely but does not identify with an V6.04.507 inclusion. The position of the reference points is: | | x | y | | --- | --- | --- | | A | 0 | 5,5 | | B | 5 | 3,75 | | C | 10 | 5,5 | 1.2 Material properties Poisson's ratio: 0 Young's modulus : 1.{10}^{6}N/{m}^{2} Coulomb coefficient: 2.0 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The lower side is blocked by an clamped support and a {u}_{y}=-{1.10}^{-6}m displacement is imposed on the upper side. Figure 1.3‑a: Géométrie de la structure et positionnement de l’interface et chargements 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation Normal at the interface is noted n and the tangential vector is noted \tau : n=(\begin{array}{}\cos\theta \\ \sin\theta \end{array}) , \tau =(\begin{array}{}-\sin\theta \\ \cos\theta \end{array}) éq 2.1-1 with \theta =\arctan\frac{y-11,77}{x-5} eq 2.1-2 In this Modelling, the hypothesis of flat stresses is considered (although the Poisson's ratio is zero here, there are no differences between flat stresses and deformations). The increased Lagrangian method is used for contact/frotting treatment. The interface has a slope that varies from end to end of the plate. However, where the inclination is highest, near the side edges, it may be slipped. To avoid this, we increase the adhesion via the coefficient of friction of Coulomb: we take \mu =2 . The value of the contact pressure on the interface is a function of the normal n : \lambda =n.\sigma .n={n}_{y}{\sigma}_{yy}{n}_{y} éq .2.1-3 - where {n}_{y} is the following y component of n - where {\sigma}_{yy} is the following y constraint in the normal {e}_{y} plane in the interfaceless structure: {\sigma}_{yy}=E\frac{{u}_{y}}{{L}_{y}} The \Lambda friction semi-multiplier is defined by: {r}_{\tau}=\lambda \mu \Lambda éq 2.1.1-4 With the tangential force density, which reads as follows: {r}_{\tau}=(\tau .\sigma .n)\tau éq 2.1-5 D’où: \Lambda =(\frac{1}{\mu}\frac{\tau .\sigma .n}{n.\sigma .n})\tau =(\frac{1}{\mu}\frac{{\tau}_{y}}{{n}_{y}})\tau éq 2.1-6 With the numerical values previously introduced: \lambda (x,y)=\frac{-1}{10}{\sin}^{2}(\arctan\frac{11,77-y}{5-x})\mathrm{Pa} éq 2.1-7 \Lambda (x,y)=\Lambda .\tau =\frac{x-5}{2(y-11,77)} éq 2.1-8 2.2 Quantities and reference results Minimum contact pressure LAGS_C on the interface (in points A and C): -0.1 Maximum contact pressure LAGS_C on the interface (to point B): -0.06110 Minimum of LAGS_F1 tangential stress density on the interface (at point A): 0.39894 Maximum tangential LAGS_F1 stress density on the interface (to point B): 0 2.3 Uncertainties of the solution None (analytical solution). 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Modelling: C_PLAN. v6.04.510 SSNV510 - Uniaxial compression of a multi-fissed block v6.04.510 SSNV510 - Uniaxial compression of a multi-fissed block Summary: This test validates the multi-Heaviside approach for elements X-FEM. It is a test case where several laterally compressed interfaces are introduced. The mesh is quite rough so that mesh cells see several cracks. Some nodes also see several cracks. These nodes then contain several Heaviside enrichments. It is verified that these different enrichments are well taken into account at the kinematic level and that the stiffness matrices associated with each area between two interfaces allow to obtain the correct distorted ones. The approach is tested with and without contact. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure is a healthy rectangle in which four horizontal cracks are introduced, in red in Figure 1.1.a. The dimensions of the structure and the position of the cracks are given in metres. The level function equations for horizontal and vertical interfaces are as follows: 	ext{LN}1=Y éq 3.1-1 	ext{LN}2=X éq 3.1-2 The horizontal interface is defined in a classic way using the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator with the normal level set 	ext{LN1} . To define the vertical interface, the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator is first called DEFI_FISS_XFEM with the normal 	ext{LN2} level set, defining an point "top" of the horizontal crack for the JONCTION keyword (the point is not necessarily on the level set). This step allows to define the top part of the vertical interface (see Figure 3.1-a in the centre). A second time the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator is called the same way, but defining an point "below" of the crack (see Figure 3.1-a to the right). So we called DEFI_FISS_XFEM (creation of 3 crack objects) in total 3 times to define the two interfaces that intersect. From a theoretical point, each crack object adds an enrichment of the Heaviside type. This makes a total of three degrees of freedom Heaviside in addition to the classic degrees of freedom. So we have 4 degree of freedom at the intersection level, allowing to move independently the 4 zones generated by the 2 interfaces. v6.04.513 SSNV513 – Block cut by three interfaces sequentially plugging with X-FEM v6.04.513 SSNV513 – Block cut by three interfaces sequentially plugging with X-FEM Summary: This test validates the approach to join with \text{X-FEM} . This is an test case where three cracks are introduced. The first crack completely breaks the domain. The second plugs in on the first via the JONCTION key word of the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator. The third plugs in on the second. The approach is tested with and without contact. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure is a healthy square in which three interfaces are inserted, in red in Figure 1.1-a. The first one is oblique and completely cuts the domain. The second one is vertical. The third one is horizontal. It connects to the second one. The dimensions of the structure and the position of the interfaces are given in Figure 1.1-a and are expressed in meters, \text{[m]} . Figure 1.1-a: Géométrie de la structure et positionnement des interfaces. 1.2 Material properties The material has an isotropic elastic behaviour defined by the following material parameters: Young's modulus : 100\text{MPa} Poisson's ratio : 0.3 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads In the case of contactless (modellings A to D), conditions are applied on the left and right edges of the structure, so that each of the 4 zones has a different displacement from the others according to \text{X} . This load is shown in figure 1.3-a. The displacements in \text{Y} (and in \text{Z} for modellings 3D) are blocked on the same edges. Figure 1.3-a : Illustration des conditions aux limites et des chargements, cas sans contact. In the case of contact (modellings E to H), roll conditions are imposed on the left and lower edges and a homogeneous pressure is applied on the right and upper edges of \text{1 MPa} . This load is shown in Figure 1.3-b. Each block is then compressed uniformly according to X and Y . Figure 1.3-b : Illustration des conditions aux limites et des chargements, cas avec contact. 2 reference solution Without contact, each area shall undergo a rigid body movement corresponding to the limit condition imposed on its edge (right or left). With contact, the 4 blocks undergo a uniform compression following \text{X} and \text{Y} . The structure can be expressed as follows: > {\mathrm{Depl}}_{X}(X)=-(5+X)\frac{\mathrm{Press}}{E} éq 2.1-1 > {\mathrm{Depl}}_{Y}(Y)=-(5+Y)\frac{\mathrm{Press}}{E} éq 2.1-2 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics This is a \text{X-FEM} model, in flat deformations (D_PLAN). Interfaces are defined by level functions (normal level sets rated \text{LN} ). The level function equations for slant, horizontal and vertical interfaces are as follows: \text{LN}1=Y-1-\frac{X}{2} éq 3.1-1 \text{LN}2=Y éq 3.1-2 \text{LN}3=X éq 3.1-3 The oblique interface is defined in a classic way using the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator with the normal \text{LN1} level set. To define the vertical interface, the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator is called with the normal \text{LN2} level set, defining a connection with the oblique crack via the JONCTION key word, and choosing an point "below" the oblique interface in the POINT operand. This step allows you to define the crack 2 in the domain below the first (see Figure 3.1-a in the centre). To define the horizontal interface, the DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator is called with the normal \text{LN3} level set , defining a connection with the vertical crack via the JONCTION keyword, and choosing a point "right" in the POINT operand. This step allows you to define the 3 crack in the domain to the right of the second crack (see Figure 3.1-a to the right). Figure 3.1-a : Étapes de construction de l'intersection. 3.2 Mesh characteristics The mesh with 25 mesh cells of QUAD4 type is shown in Figure 3.2-a. This figure shows that the central mesh cell is cut by the three interfaces. This test allows you to validate the multiple cutting. The nodes of this mesh cell is enriched 3 times: they therefore have the degrees of freedom DX, DY, H1X, H1Y, H2X, H2Y, H3X and H3Y. Figure 3.2-a: Le maillage de la modélisation A. The advantage of this test is to verify that the addition of 3 discontinuity functions to the standard form function for each node of the central mesh cell allows the displacement kinematics of the 4 domains generated by the two connections (see Figure 3.2-b). Figure 3.2-b : nœuds multi-heaviside et domaines de discontinuité représentés. 3.3 Tested Features The DEFI_FISS_XFEM operator is tested using the JONCTION key word, which allows the definition of crack connections in \text{X-FEM} . The MODI_MODELE_XFEM operator is also tested for mesh cells which is cut by several cracks. The multi-Heaviside and multi-stocking of the data structures ( \text{SD} ) \text{X-FEM} is of course activated. The assignment of Heaviside functions is verified in the elements sub-integration of the horizontal crack support (in blue in Figure 3.2-b). The assembly of Heaviside ddegrades of freedom at the matrix and second member level of elements connected to the intersection for COMPORTEMENT option in STAT_NON_LINE is tested. The post-processing \text{X-FEM} is also valid for multi-cutting, with POST_MAIL_XFEM and POST_CHAM_XFEM operators. 3.4 Tested quantities and results The lip displacements of cracks are tested after post-processings operations relative to \text{X-FEM} (POST_MAIL_XFEM and POST_CHAM_XFEM). The DX displacement must correspond to the load imposed in Figure 1.3-a on each area and DY must be zero. v6.04.518 SSNV518 - Modelling a relaxation trial with visco-hyperelastic law (ELAS_HYPER_VISC) v6.04.518 SSNV518 - Modelling a relaxation trial with visco-hyperelastic law (ELAS_HYPER_VISC) Summary: This test consists of simulating the relaxation of a single element volume-finished, uniaxially tensile, and is designed to validate the constitutive law ELAS_HYPER_VISC. The results obtained are compared and validated with results provided by the Abaqus software. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is a test on a cubic mesh cell of 1 mm side. 1.2 Material properties The material obeys the visco-hyperelastic constitutive law. The hyperelastic behavior is of the Neo-Hookean type. The visco-elastic behavior is given by a series of Prony order 3 . The parameters of the law are: | {\nu}=0.495 | Poisson's ratio | | --- | --- | | {\mathrm{C_{10}}}=0.30,{\mathrm{C_{01}}}=\mathrm{C_{02}}=\mathrm{C_{20}}=0 | Long-term Mooney-Rivlin material parameters, i.e., for infinite behavior (MPa) | | {\mathrm{G}}=[1.33, 0.66, 0.33] | Long-term shear module list of Prony Series 3 (MPa) | | {\tau}=[100, 10000, 1000000] | List of values of the relaxation time of the Prony series of order 3 (s) | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Symmetric conditions are imposed on the 3 orthogonal faces in the 3 direction of the marker. A displacement of 0.2 mm is imposed on the 1 s stress surface to generate a nominal stress state of the order of 1 MPa. The load is held for 10 million seconds. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The test is based on the results of the Abaqus calculation code. It is noted that the viscous flow in the Abaqus calculation code is modelled by introducing a decomposed coefficient in Prony series on the The isochore and volumetric parts of the second Piola Kirchoff tensor. In the case of the ELAS_HYPER_VISC law, the viscous scoop only concerns the isochore part of the tensor of the stresses. This implementation difference should not impact the results of the two codes given the very low compressibility of the material. 2.2 Baseline The equivalent deformation and stress of Von Mises is ensured to correspond well with the values obtained from the calculation to within 1\% at two different moments. 2.3 Bibliographical references EC2 Modelling Report, RAP-EC2-02112-2-A.pdf (06/02/24) - Simulation of mechanical behaviour of an elastomer joint - Study of integration of a viscoelastic constitutive law 3 Modelling A 3D modelling. 3.1 Mesh characteristics One cubic mesh cell. 3.2 Tested quantities and results The equivalent deformation and stress of Von Platings at the end of the load shall be tested. | Identification | Reference | Test | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | MAX_INVA_2 à t=1 s | 0.201664 | External | 0.1\% | | MAX_INVA_2 à t=1.e7 s | 0.202054 | External | 0.1\% | | MAX_VMIS à t=1 s | 1.203393 | External | 0.1\% | | MAX_VMIS à t=1.e7 s | 0.36333 | External | 0.1\% | The Von Lays stress curves in the element are presented below as a function of time: Illustration 1: Comparison of results between Abaqus and Code_Aster. 4 Summary of the results The results of the two codes are highly correlated.

The reinforced concrete model is subjected to a load of displacements imposed: ddl_impo. The nonlinear behavior of the rebar arrays is modelled by grid_isot_line for isotropic plasticity. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A reinforced concrete cube is considered L=1m side. The rebar arrays belong to the plane defined by the four nodes \mathit{N05}-\mathit{N02}-\mathit{N03}-\mathit{N08} . Two rebar panels are defined: one according to the X local direction and one according to the Y local direction. The rate of ironing for each rebar is 0.1{m}^{2}/\mathit{ml} (Section per linear metre). 1.2 Features of modellings The mesh cell concrete is modeled with a element hexa8. The modellings considered for reinforcing sheeting are: - Modelling A (§3): use of Membrane_grid with mesh cells tria3 support - Modelling B (§4): use of Membrane_Grate with quad4 support mesh cells - Modelling C (§5): use of excentre grid with mesh cells tria3 support 1.3 Material properties Concrete material is elastic isotropic with properties of: - {E}_{b}=20000\mathrm{MPa} - \nu =0.2 The constitutive law of the frame follows an elastoplastic model with properties: - {E}_{a}=200000\mathrm{MPa} - \nu =0 - {E}_{\mathrm{ecr}}^{\mathrm{acier}}=20000\mathrm{MPa} - {\sigma}_{e}^{\mathrm{acier}}=200000\mathrm{MPa} The grid_isot_line model for isotropic hardening plasticity is used in stat_non_line. 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads boundary conditions: - clamped support en \mathit{A1} - \mathit{DX}=0 on the \mathit{A1}-\mathit{A4} edge - \mathit{DY}=0 on the \mathit{A1}-\mathit{A2} edge - \mathrm{DZ}=0 on the lower surface of the cube (N01-N02-N03-N04) Loading by required travel: - \mathrm{DX}=1 on the \mathit{A2}-\mathit{A3} edge - \mathit{DY}=1t on the \mathit{A3}-\mathit{A4} edge where t is the pseudo-time parameter. 1.5 Initial conditions Initially, displacement and stress are zero everywhere. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference results are obtained by another Aster calculation. 2.2 Quantities and reference results The displacements, reaction forces to different nodes of mesh are evaluated, as well as the local stress values for different mesh cells. v6.05.107 SSNS107 – Cylinder with pressure-rebar v6.05.107 SSNS107 – Cylinder with pressure-rebar Summary: A cylinder with pressure-reinforced frames is considered. More precisely, a hollow cylinder, 3D, is completed on its outer face with a circumferential frame (skin 2D). This structure is charged with an internal pressure. The calculation is elastic linear. The simulation is compared with an analytical solution to validate modellings GRILLE_MEMBRANE reinforcements on a structure. All numeric values are given in SI unit. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The cylinder has an internal {R}_{1}=10m radius, an external {R}_{2}=20m radius, a height h=1m . The circumferential frame has a section per unit length of e=1{m}^{2}/\mathrm{ml} . 1.2 Material properties The concrete (drain cylinder) is E=2E+10\mathrm{Pa} and \nu =0.2 ; the steel (circumferential frame) E=2E+11\mathrm{Pa} , \nu =0 , {E}_{t}=2.E+09 (dangerous module), {\sigma}_{y}=2.E+11\mathrm{Pa} (very large plasticity constraint to stay in the elastic range). The rebar is in its vertical main direction and a cross section per linear meter of 1m . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loading Only one section of the cylinder is interested. The following conditions are imposed: 1. a normal zero displacement on the side faces of the cylinder angular section ( \mathrm{SG} and \mathrm{SD} on the schematic figure) (zero ortho-radial displacement) 2. a zero vertical displacement on the lower side of the cylinder section (single support) 3. a pressure imposed by {10}^{6}\mathrm{Pa} on the inner side of the cylinder section ( \mathrm{SI} ) on the schematic figure (internal pressure) Schedule designation of cylinder surfaces 2 Reference solutions For the solution without reinforcement, and seen the symmetries of the problem, the displacement can be written in the form: U(r,z)=g(r){u}_{r}+h(z){u}_{z} With: The boundary conditions then allows to explain the constants: with {R}_{2} the radius at the interface level between concrete and the circumferential reinforcements. Here we give the solution with {P}_{2} not null because it will be useful in the next. In the case of circumferential reinforcement on the outer side of the cylinder, this reinforcement exerts pressure. This pressure (movement function) must be determined and the previous results applied. The "boilermakers formula" (presence of reinforcements) is applied: To link the stress to the displacement solution, deformation is used (the deformation of the reinforcements being the deformation of the cylinder): Applying the previous results with {P}_{2}=P , you get the desired solution. 3 Modelling A Modelling only concerns one angular sector of the cylinder, one element in the section, one element in the height, 100 elements between {R}_{1} and {R}_{2} In this Modelling, the local circumferential frame marker is defined in four different ways in AFFE_CARA_ELEM: VECT_1/ VECT_2/ ANGL_REP_1 and ANGL_REP_2. 3.1 Test values The radial displacement values of the points on the inner face of the concrete cylinder ( \mathrm{N6} in the figure below) and on the outer face of the concrete cylinder ( \mathrm{N17} in the figure below) are tested and compared with the analytical solution. v6.05.108 SSNS108 – Simulation of SAFE Test by Progressive Push v6.05.108 SSNS108 – Simulation of SAFE Test by Progressive Push Summary: This test represents a simplified Modelling of a SAFE (Slowly-Raised Armed Structure) study under static monotonous progressive pushover loading. The objective of this test is to validate the DEBORST calculation option on NEWTON. This test is delicate because it considers a problem not posed, without one-sided solution, due to the softening material related to the damage. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry studied is that of the T5 structure of the SAFE [bib1] program. The geometrical characteristics of reinforced concrete parts are illustrated by the []. They are composed of a veil and two return walls (or recasts). The structure is also equipped with metal parts related to its loading. These parts will not be modelled in this study. Figure 1.1-a : Geometry of the T5 model Figure 1.1-b : Illustration of the railing The model's railing consists of horizontal and vertical reinforcements on each side of the central wall, as well as in the returns []. In both horizontal and vertical directions, the corrosion rates {r}_{h} and {r}_{v} (the rebar quantity per linear metre of the sail) are identical and equal to \text{0,8\%} , i.e.: \frac{{S}_{\mathrm{armatures}\mathrm{horizontales}}}{\mathrm{ml}(\mathrm{vertical})}={r}_{h}e=\frac{0,8}{100}.20\mathrm{cm}=16{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}/\mathrm{ml} \frac{{S}_{\mathrm{armatures}\mathrm{verticales}}}{\mathrm{ml}(\mathrm{horizontale})}={r}_{v}e=\frac{0,8}{100}.20\mathrm{cm}=16{\mathrm{cm}}^{2}/\mathrm{ml} And this for all the two tables facing North and South. Either 8\mathit{cm²}/\mathit{ml} per tablecloth and direction (horizontal and vertical, or \mathrm{2x8}=16\mathit{cm²}/\mathit{ml} ). 1.2 Material properties The behaviour of concrete is modelled by damaging elasto-plastic behaviour ENDO_ISOT_BETON [bib2]. v6.05.110 SSNS110 – Extraction of a rebar table represented by a membrane v6.05.110 SSNS110 – Extraction of a rebar table represented by a membrane Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the Modelling of the decohesion of a rebar sheet, which is represented by a membrane, connected to the surrounding volume by an interface law. This Modelling is compared to a reference model in which the steel bars are modelled in 3D. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A reinforced concrete plate, with two straight-line reinforcing sheets, is considered to be held at one end and a force is applied to the cross-section of the steel bars at the other end. Figure 1: Extraction d'une nappe d'armature hors d'une plaque en béton armé. To limit the cost of calculation, only one section of the plate is modelled, at which edges periodicity conditions are imposed. The dimensions of the plate and the reinforcements are shown in the Figure. Figure 2: Dimensions du tronçon de plaque modélisé. (a) Vue générale; (b) vue longitudinale; (c) coupe du tronçon modélisé. The two rebar panels are represented by a membrane model connected to the concrete volume by an interface law. This allows for a considerable limitation of the cost of calculation (see Figure). Figure 3: Représentation des nappes d'armature par une membrane 1.2 Material properties Concrete has a homogeneous isotropic elastic behaviour, characterized by the Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio indicated below: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{E}_{B}=30\text{GPa}\\ {\nu}_{B}=0.22\end{array} The Young's modulus of the steel is {E}_{A}=200\text{GPa} , the spacing between the e=20\text{cm} steel bars and the diameter of the d=2\text{cm} bars . The restraint steel-beton is of the CZM_LAB_MIX type, with the following parameters: | quantity | Value | | --- | --- | | {\sigma}_{C} | 10\text{MPa} | | {\delta}_{C} | 1\text{mm} | | \alpha | 0.7 | | \beta | 1 | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The limit conditions applied to the plate are indicated below, corresponding to the limit conditions at the end of the plate, the periodicity conditions and the force exerted on the frames: \lbrace \begin{array}{c}{u}_{Y}=0\text{sur}\text{A\_FOND et B\_FOND}\\ {u}_{Z}=0\text{sur}\text{A\_FOND}\\ {u}_{X}=0\text{sur}\text{A\_GAUC et B\_GAUC}\\ {u}_{X}=0\text{sur}\text{A\_DROI et B\_DROI}\\ {F}_{Y}=-\frac{9810.T}{e}\text{sur}\text{BOUT}\end{array} 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation This problem does not allow for exact analytical solution. The reference solution is therefore obtained by fine three-dimensional modelling, detailed in the reference [1] . 2.2 Quantities and reference results The horizontal displacement of the steel measured at the end of the plate is specified below for two different loading levels. | quantity | Component | Instant | reference solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DEPL – BOUT | DY | 5 | -140.367141312E-6 | | | | 10 | -318.457920376E-6 | 2.3 Bibliographical references 1. DAVID M., Multi-scale approach to the mechanical behaviour of reinforced concrete structures – Application to containment enclosures of nuclear power plants. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics A model called "decohesion grid model" is used to represent the rebar table (see reference [1] ). The mechanical behaviour of the sheet is represented by a membrane model, the coefficients of which are calculated analytically: {M}_{\mathit{LLLL}}={M}_{\mathit{TTTT}}={E}_{A}\frac{\pi {d}^{2}}{4e} The other coefficients of rigidity of the membrane are all zero. v6.05.112 SSNS112 – Compression test and alternating traction of a reinforced concrete pole v6.05.112 SSNS112 – Compression test and alternating traction of a reinforced concrete pole Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the alternating uniaxial response of a reinforced concrete beam, based on experimental tests, modelled by laws: - GLRC_DM, R7.01.32, generalised reinforced concrete law used with elements DKTG - MAZARS_UNIL,[R5.03.09], 1D Concrete Law, combined with a nonlinear law for VMIS_CINE_GC steel on a POU_D_EM Multifibre beam model - DHRC, R7.01.37, homogenized reinforced concrete law used with elements DKTG. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A reinforced concrete pole of 0,7m length , on \mathrm{Ox} axis , of square cross-section of height and width equal to 0,15m is considered. Figure 1: section du poteau en béton armé. The longitudinal frames are four \mathit{HA14} . Cross-sectional frames are not included in the modellings below. Two X and Y reinforcing beds are used for Modelling A. For Modelling B, one steel fibre of 6,15{\mathit{mm}}^{2} section is used. 1.2 Material properties GLRC_DM constitutive law has the following parameters for concrete: - Young's modulus: E=28500\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.2 - Maximum compression stress: {\sigma}_{c}=25\mathrm{MPa} - Compression peak deformation: {ϵ}_{c}=2,25.\text{}{10}^{-3} - Maximum tensile stress: {\sigma}_{t}=2,94\mathit{MPa} The parameters for steel are: - Young's modulus: E=195000\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.3 - Elasticity limit: {\sigma}_{y}=610\mathrm{MPa} - Tangent module (plastics): {E}_{t}=19,5\mathit{MPa} DEFI_GLRC is used to obtain the parameters of GLRC_DM law. The stress of the concrete has been reduced to {\sigma}_{t}=1,6\mathit{MPa} . In addition, the parameters {\gamma}_{c}=0,35 and {\alpha}_{c}=60 are also fixed for nonlinear compression behavior. The equivalent membrane elastic module, cf.[R7.01.32], is valid with this material data: {E}_{\mathrm{eq}}^{m}=34021.0\mathrm{MPa} , i.e. a stiffness membrane according to the \mathrm{Ox} direction: {E}_{\mathrm{eq}}^{m}\ast S=765.393\mathrm{MN} . The DEFI_MATER_GC operator was used to determine the parameters of the MAZARS_UNIL and VMIS_CINE_GC laws. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads One end of the beam, edge A , is blocked and the other end, edge B , is imposed a distributed effort of result \mathit{FX}=1\mathit{kN} in the direction X .
