v6.05.114 1 v6.05.114 SSNS114 – Degradation of a reinforced concrete plate under various stresses with BETON_REGLE_PR law l l 1 v6.05.114 SSNS114 – Degradation of a reinforced concrete plate under various stresses with BETON_REGLE_PR law Summary: This test validates the constitutive law nonlinear concrete BETON_REGLE_PR (see R7.01.27) for various cyclic loads: traction/compression, alternating bending, shear in the plane and their combinations. Multilayer modelling is used, in which the steels of the rebars are represented by GRILLE_EXCENTRE. The analyses are done in static (STAT_NON_LINE). The results are compared with those of modelling with the ENDO_ISOT_BETON behavior model (see R7.01.04). Modelling H tests thermomechanical processes. In this Modelling, it is verified that the two thermal expansion loads (homogeneous temperature in thickness and constant temperature gradient in thickness) lead to the same stress state as two simple mechanical loads: Ox extension and flexion around Oy. The modellings E to G correspond to the modellings A to C for higher levels of stress. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry | e | | | --- | --- | Figure 1.1-a : geometry of square reinforced concrete plate Length: L=1.0m ; Plate thickness: e=0.1m . Steel diameter: 0.01m . Coating of the lower and upper rebar sheets of the steels according to the z axis : 0.01m . The Modelling is based on a semi-global multilayer plate Modelling. Concrete and reinforcements are modeled separately. For each rebar sheet, one considers a layer that behaves only in the longitudinal direction of the reinforcements. So one will have 4 layers for the rebar. On the same mesh 5 models representing reinforced concrete plate are defined: 1 DKT model for concrete and 4 GRILLE models for reinforcements (2 in X direction, 2 in Y direction for lower and upper parts). The rate of ironing for each rebar table is 8.0\times {10}^{-4}{m}^{2}/m . The position of the frames (lower or higher) is defined by the key word EXCENTREMENT under the key word factor GRILLE in the AFFE_CARA_ELEM operator, which is \pm 0.04m : so it is assumed here that the steels in X and Y are in the same position, which is the usual approximation of the multilayer models. 1.2 Material properties Concrete cracking is modelled by constitutive law BETON_REGLE_PR, while steel modeled by GRILLE_ISOT_LINE. Beton (model BETON_REGLE_PR) : Young's modulus: {E}_{b}=32308.0\mathrm{MPa} Poisson's ratio: {\nu}_{b}=0.20 Threshold of single traction damage {\sigma}_{y}^{t} : 3.4\mathrm{MPa} Softening pent: {E}_{T}=-0.2{E}_{b} Threshold of damage in single compression {\sigma}_{y}^{c} : 32.308\mathit{MPa} Deformation at {\varepsilon}_{c} compression threshold: 0.002 > Exposing the law of compression hardening n : 2 Steel : Young's modulus : {E}_{a}=200000.0\mathrm{MPa} Linearity limit {\sigma}_{e}^{\text{acier}} : 570.0\mathrm{MPa} Post-elastic pent {E}_{\text{écrouis}}^{\text{acier}} : \text{}=0.0015{E}_{a}=300\mathrm{MPa} . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Different modellings A to H are considered for different types of characteristic loads and different plate behaviors. The elements of the reference literature was also used to implant the element membrane in large deformations in code_aster, so the correct placement of the element in the screw code against the sources used is checked. v6.06.102 SSNX102 - element 3D_INTERF_POU Calculation Options v6.06.102 SSNX102 - element 3D_INTERF_POU Calculation Options Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the different calculation options of the 3D_INTERF_POU R7.01.49 interaction element. This test is purely numerical. It is a question of checking that the programming is correct. Movements are imposed in different nodes of the element. It is then checked that the nodal forces, as well as the linear forces of interest and relative displacement, at the integration points and nodes, are in line with expectations. The different modellings check: - the orientation of the reinforcement axis : MODI_MAILLAGE( ORIE_INTERF_POU ) - the orientation of the reinforcement section : AFFE_CARA_ELEM( ORIENTATION ) - the section type of reinforcement : AFFE_CARA_ELEM( POUTRE( _F(SECTION) )) - the behavior type : STAT_NON_LINE( COMPORTEMENT( _F(RELATION) )) - calculation options related to linear and nonlinear static resolution: MECA_STATIQUE, STAT_NON_LINE - CALC_CHAMP post-processing calculation options: FORC_NODA, SIEF_ELGA, SIEF_ELNO, SIEF_NOEU, SAUT_ELGA, SAUT_ELNO - other calculation options: COOR_ELGA 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 3D_INTERF_POU modeled the interaction between a beam element, representing a reinforcement section, with an element HEXA8, representing the surrounding matrix. The domain of interaction considered (l-interface) is a line confused with the field of beam. L-L-element 3D_INTERF_POU incorporates in its Gauss points a phenomenological law 1 returning the interaction efforts between matrix and reinforcement according to their relative displacement. The element is carried by an mesh cell HEXA27, but only the first 8 nodes (corresponding to the HEXA8 of the matrix) and the nodes 23 and 25 (corresponding to the SEG2 of the reinforcement) are assigned to degrees of freedom (ddl). On the nodes of the matrix only the translation ddls are affected, while the nodes of the reinforcement carry translation and rotation ddls. In this test case, the mesh cell is a parallelepiped 2 \times 3 \times 7 \, m ( X \times Y \times Z ) dimensional device. The load is chosen so that it is identical at each of the Gauss points. The outputs of the digital integration are checked at the scale of the Gauss point. The effort and the tangent matrix returned by the constitutive law are checked. The law is only verified in 3D, because it is only compatible with the element 3D_INTERF_POU. Two constitutive laws are tested. v6.06.201 CONT201 - Projection-intersection for 3D linear mesh cells beam matching v6.06.201 CONT201 - Projection-intersection for 3D linear mesh cells beam matching Summary: The objective of this test is to verify the projection-intersection procedure in the case of beam-launch matching (mortar approach). Specifically, this test is limited to the case of linear 3D mesh cells (so mesh cells skin type QUAD4 or TRIA3). 1 Reference problem 1.1 General formalism adopted The focus here is on the matching procedure and the construction of the mortar integrals for the calculation of contact. In this case, it is limited to elementary cases in 3D. As a reminder, pairing and projection-intersection decomposes in several stages: 1. projection of the nodes slaves on the master mesh cell, 2. calculation of an intersection on the master mesh cell, 3. Inverse projection and expression of intersection points on the slave mesh cell. Then, a quadrature law is built by re-mailing the polygon obtained from the barycentre (using triangles). The associated documentation can be consulted for more information. v6.07.101 COMP001 – Test for elasto-plastic behavior. Simulation in one point hardware v6.07.101 COMP001 – Test for elasto-plastic behavior. Simulation in one point hardware Summary: This test uses a simulation of a loading path in stress or deformation in a material point, i.e. on a model such that the stress and deformation states are homogeneous at any time. It thus allows testing a number of models of elastoplastic behaviour, with the aim of verifying the robustness of their numerical integration, their insensitivity to a change in units, the correct consideration of the control variables on which the coefficients of the model depend, the invariance with an overall rotation applied to the problem, the accuracy of the tangential matrix. Modelling A: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ISOT_LINE model in 3D and C_PLAN. Modelling B: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ISOT_TRAC model in 3D and C_PLAN. Modelling C: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CINE_LINE model in 3D. Modelling D: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ECMI_LINE model in 3D and C_PLAN. Modelling E: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ECMI_TRAC model in 3D and C_PLAN. Modelling F: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CIN1_CHAB model in 3D. Modelling G: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CIN2_CHAB model in 3D. H Modelling: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ISOT_PUIS model in 3D. Modelling J: This Modelling allows to validate the MOHR_COULOMB model in 3D. Modelling K: This model allows to validate the MohrCoulombAS model in 3D. The exploitation is concerned with the invariants of the stress tensor: tensor trace, Von-Mises stress and internal variables of a scalar nature: usually it is the cumulative plasticity. The overall convergence criteria are the default values for ASTER. (RESI_GLOB_RELA=10-6, ITER_GLOB_MAXI=10) A common Newton schema for the re-update of the tangent matrix was adopted: with each converged increment (REAC_INC=1) and with every 1 iteration (REAC_ITER=1). 2.2 Equivalent problem studies For rough discretization of the journeys: 1 time step for each segment of the journey, the solution obtained for each law is compared to 3 strictly equivalent problems for the condition of the material point: - \mathit{Tpa} , same route with a change of unit, substitutes \mathrm{Pa} for \mathrm{MPa} in material data and possible law parameters, - \mathit{Trot} , route by imposing the same \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon} tensor after rotation: {brace ^{t}R\cdot \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon}\cdot R where R is a rotation matrix. For the 2D case, the rotation angle will be \alpha =0.9\mathit{rad} , for the 3D configuration, the angles d-Euler were chosen with arbitrary values { \Psi =0.9\mathit{rad} , 	heta =0.7\mathit{rad} , and \mathrm{\phi }=0.4\mathit{rad} }, - \mathit{Tsym} , path by imposing the \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon} tensor after symmetry: x and y axis permutation to 2D, x to y , y to z and z to x to 3D. For each of these problems, the solution (invariants in stresses, cumulative equivalent plastic deformation) must be identical to the basic solution, obtained with the same discretization in time. The reference value of the difference is therefore 0. This means in practice that the difference found must be of the order of machine precision is about 1.E-15 . 2.3 Test of the tangent matrix The tangential matrix is also tested for each behavior, by difference with the matrix obtained by disturbance. Here again, the reference value is 0. 2.4 Study of time step discretization (A2) The behavior of the integration of laws in relation to discretization is studied. For the same Modelling, therefore a given behavior, several discretizations are studied in different times, multiplying by 5 the number of steps of the loading path. In the reference [1], the discretization is pushed up to 3125 increments per segment on the same principle. Here, to limit the duration of the tests, we limit ourselves to three successive refinements. v6.07.102 COMP002 – Visco-elastic-plastic behavior test. Simulation in one point hardware v6.07.102 COMP002 – Visco-elastic-plastic behavior test. Simulation in one point hardware Summary: This test uses a simulation of a loading path in stresses or deformations in a material point, i.e. on a model such that the stress and deformation states are homogeneous at any time. It thus allows to test a number of models of visco-elastic-plastic behavior, with the aim of checking the robustness of their numerical integration, their insensitivity to a change in units, the correct consideration of the control variables on which the coefficients of the model depend, the invariance with an overall rotation applied to the problem, the accuracy of the tangent matrix. Modelling A: This Modelling allows to validate the LEMAITRE model in 3D. Modelling B: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_CIN1_CHAB model in 3D. Modelling C: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_CIN2_CHAB model in 3D. Modelling D: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_ENDO_LEMA model in 3D. Modelling E: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_TAHERI model in 3D. Modelling F: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_ISOT_LINE model in 3D. Modelling G: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_ISOT_TRAC model in 3D. H Modelling: This Modelling allows to validate the VISC_CIN2_MEMO model in 3D. Modelling I: This Modelling allows to validate the VISCOCHAB model in 3D. Modelling J: This Modelling allows to validate the MONOCRISTAL model in CPLAN and 3D. K Modelling: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_JOHN_COOK model in 3D. The exploitation is concerned with the invariants of the stress tensor: tensor trace, Von-Mises stress and internal variables of a scalar nature: usually it is the cumulative plasticity. The overall convergence criteria are the default values for Code_Aster. (RESI_GLOB_RELA=10-6, ITER_GLOB_MAXI=10) A common Newton schema for the re-update of the tangent matrix was adopted: - calculation of the prediction tangent matrix at each converged increment (REAC_INC=1) - calculation of the coherent tangent matrix at each Newton iteration (REAC_ITER=1). 2.2 Studies of equivalent problems For rough discretization of the journeys: 1 time step for each segment of the journey, the solution obtained for each law is compared to 3 strictly equivalent problems for the condition of the material point: - \mathrm{Tpa} , same route with a unit change, substitutes \mathrm{Pa} for \mathrm{MPa} in material data and possible law parameters, - Trot, route by imposing the same \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon} tensor after rotation: R\stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon}{R}^{T} where R is a rotation matrix. For \mathrm{2D} case, the rotation angle will be \alpha =0.9 radian, for \mathrm{3D} configuration, we chose the angles d-Euler with arbitrary values { \psi =0.9 radian 	heta =0.7 radian and \phi =0.4 radian }, - Tsym, route by imposing the \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon} tensor after a symmetry: x and y to \mathrm{2D} rotation, x to y rotation, y to z and z to x to 3D. For each of these problems, the solution (invariants in stresses, cumulative equivalent plastic deformation) must be identical to the basic solution, obtained with the same discretization in time. The reference value of the difference is therefore 0. This means in practice that the difference found must be of the order of machine precision is about 1.E-15. 2.3 Test of the tangent matrix The tangential matrix is also tested for each behavior, by difference with the matrix obtained by disturbance. Here again, the reference value is 0. 2.4 Study of time step discretization The behavior of the integration of laws in relation to discretization is studied. For the same Modelling, therefore a given behavior, several discretizations are studied in different times, multiplying by 5 the number of steps of the loading path. In the reference [1], the discretization is pushed up to 3125 increments per segment on the same principle. Here, to limit the duration of the tests, we limit ourselves to three successive refinements. v6.07.103 COMP003 – Test of concrete-specific behaviors. Simulation in one point hardware v6.07.103 COMP003 – Test of concrete-specific behaviors. Simulation in one point hardware Summary: This test involves a simulation of a loading path in stress or deformation in a material point, i.e. on a model such that the stress and deformation states are homogeneous at any time. It allows testing a number of concrete-specific behaviour models, with the aim of verifying the robustness of their digital integration, their insensitivity to a change in units, the correct consideration of the control variables on which the coefficients of the model depend, l-invariance with an overall rotation applied to the problem. Modelling A: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_RAG model in \mathrm{3D} . Modelling B: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_UMLV model in \mathrm{3D} . Modelling C: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_BURGER model in \mathrm{3D} . Modelling D: This Modelling allows to validate the ENDO_LOCA_EXP model in \mathrm{3D} . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry generated automatically in the SIMU_POINT_MAT[U4.51.12] macro-command is unique and simple: it is a tetrahedron on side 1, to which nodes linear relationships are applied to obtain a homogeneous state of stress and deformation. 1.2 Material properties The material characteristics are defined by the DEFI_MATERIAU command. The exploitation is concerned with the invariants of the stress tensor: tensor trace, Von-Mises stress and internal variables of a scalar nature. The overall convergence criteria are the default values for Code_Aster. (RESI_GLOB_RELA=10-6, ITER_GLOB_MAXI=10) A common Newton schema for the re-update of the tangent matrix was adopted: - calculation of the prediction tangent matrix at each converged increment (REAC_INC=1) - calculation of the coherent tangent matrix at each Newton iteration (REAC_ITER=1). 2.2 Equivalent problem studies For rough discretization of the journeys: 1 time step for each segment of the journey, the solution obtained for each law is compared to 2 strictly equivalent problems for the material point state: - \mathrm{Tpa} , same route with a unit change, substitutes \mathrm{Pa} for \mathit{MPa} in material data and possible law parameters, - \mathrm{Trot} , route by imposing the same \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon} tensor after rotation: {t}^{}R\cdot \stackrel{ˉ}{\varepsilon}\cdot R where R is a rotation matrix, corresponding to a rotation of 30 degrees around the \mathit{Oz} axis. For each of these problems, the solution (invariants in the stresses, scalar internal variable) must be identical to the basic solution, obtained with the same discretization in time. v6.07.104 COMP004 - constitutive law VISC_ISOT_PLAS applied to a hardware point v6.07.104 COMP004 - constitutive law VISC_ISOT_PLAS applied to a hardware point Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the constitutive law elasto-viscoplastic isotropic mechanical VISC_ISOT_PLAS described in R5.03.38. The problem is implemented at the point material scale (SIMU_POINT_MAT) by imposing the (total) deformation over time. The numerically obtained solution is compared to a reference analytical solution as well as to non-regression values. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The problem is handled at the point hardware scale using SIMU_POINT_MAT macro-command. 1.2 Material properties The material is governed by the constitutive law VISC_ISOT_PLAS which is explicitly temperature dependent. The model parameters include the elastic mechanical characteristics and the microstructure of the material. The Material properties used for this test are: | T | -20.0 \text{ °C} | Constant temperature expressed in degrees Celsius | | --- | --- | --- | | E | \left( 2.6\text{e}6 \text{ Pa} \right) \left( 78821.0 - 23.721 \frac{T}{1.0 \text{ °C}} \right) | Young's modulus explicitly dependent on the T temperature defined above and expressed in Pascal | | \nu | 0.3 | Poisson's ratio (no unit) | | TAILLE_GRAIN | 5.0\text{e}6 \text{ m} | Grain size for non-irradiated state expressed in metres | | D_DISLOC | 1.4\text{e}14 \text{ m}^{-2} | Initial dislocation density expressed in reverse of square meter | | C_AMAS | 1.6\text{e}23 \text{ m}^{-3} | Concentration of solute clusters expressed in reverse from meter to cubic | | TAILLE_AMAS | 3.0\text{e-}9 \text{ m} | Size of solute clusters expressed in metres | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Total deformation is imposed over the moments by taking the one obtained for the reference solution analytical of this test. This is a growing function of time, linear as long as the constitutive law remains in the elastic domain. 1.4 Initial conditions The initial conditions correspond to those taken naturally: internal variables zero and zero deformations. 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation A number of quantities described in the VISC_ISOT_PLAS R5.03.38 model are first explicitly calculated: \begin{array}{l} \mu := \dfrac{E}{ 2 \left( 1 + \nu \right) } \\ \\ \sigma_{HP} := \mu \sqrt{ \dfrac{ 3.3090\text{e-}11 }{ \text{TAILLE_GRAIN} } } \\ \\ \sigma_{VD} := 2.5\text{e}7 \, \text{min} \left[ \text{max} \left( 0, 0.01 \, T - 2 \right), 1 \right] \\ \\ \sigma_{VS0} := 8\text{e}7 - 2\text{e}5 \left( 150 + T \right) \\ L := \dfrac{1}{ 2.222222222\text{e-}4 + 6.7925\text{e-}6 \, \sqrt{ 1\text{e-}22 \, \text{C_AMAS} } } \\ \\ f := \text{min} \left( 1.178 + 0.019 \, T, 6.8 \right) \\ \\ H := \dfrac{ \mu^{2} }{ 4 \, L \, f } \\ \\ H_{0} := \mu^{2} \, 1.5376\text{e-}20 \, \text{D_DISLOC} \\ \\ \sigma_{I} := \sqrt{ \mu^{2} \, 3.35\text{e-}8 \, \left( 1\text{e}9 \, \text{TAILLE_AMAS} \right)^{2.3} \, \left( 1\text{e-}22 \, \text{C_AMAS} \right)^{1.142857} } \\ \\ \sigma_{C0} := \sigma_{HP} + \sigma_{VD} + \sigma_{VS0} + \sqrt{\left( \sigma_{I} \right)^{2} + 4 \, H_{0} } \\ \\ \sigma_{E} := 900\text{e}6 \, \left[ 1 - \left( T + 273.15 \right) \dfrac{19.3289}{9744} \right]^{2} \\ \\ \sigma_{D} := 5\text{e}6 \, \left( 1 \text{e}6 \right)^{0.1} \\ \end{array} Then, a list of 1001 moments (noted t ) describing the \left[ 0; 1 \right] interval with a constant discretization step (equal to 0.001 ). It is recalled that when simulating an constitutive law on a material point, the \varepsilon^{tot} total deformation tensor can be assimilated to a scalar and the same for the \sigma stress tensor. The total required \varepsilon^{tot}_{ref} reference deformation is then initially assimilated to this list of moments while the reference stress is initialized as if the behavior were elastic i.e. as if \varepsilon^{elas}_{ref} = \varepsilon^{tot}_{ref} . In other words, \sigma_{ref}(t) := E t and \varepsilon^{tot}_{ref}(t) = t are installed. Then, we look at the moment from which the (visco-)plastic regime begins, i.e. from when \sigma exceeds the \sigma_{C0} threshold already calculated: this is when \varepsilon^{tot}_{ref} > \frac{\sigma_{C0}}{E} . We then follow the evolution of the cumulative plastic deformation, noted here p and equal to the (visco-)plastic deformation \varepsilon^{vp}_{ref} in the case of a material point. In other words, when t > \frac{\sigma_{C0}}{E} is imposed p(t):= t - \frac{\sigma_{C0}}{E} . This results in a number of evaluations that allow new reference values for \sigma_{ref} and \varepsilon^{tot}_{ref} at these t moments of the (visco-)plastic regime: \begin{array}{l} \sigma_{VS} : = \sigma_{VS0} \text{exp} \left( -200 p \right) \\ \\ \sigma_{auto} := \sqrt{ H_{0} \text{exp} \left( -3 f p \right) + H \left[ 4 - \text{exp} \left( - 3 f p \right) - 3 \text{exp} \left( -p \right) \right] } \\ \\ \sigma_{LT} : = \text{max} \left[ 0, \sqrt{ 3 \left(\sigma_{auto} \right)^{2} } - \sigma_{E} \right] \\ \\ \sigma_{ref} := \sigma_{D} + \sigma_{E} + \sigma_{HP} + \sigma_{VD} + \sigma_{VS} + \sqrt{\left( \sigma_{I} \right)^{2} + \left( \sigma_{auto} \right)^2 + \left(\sigma_{LT} \right)^{2} } \\ \\ \varepsilon^{tot}_{ref} := p + \dfrac{\sigma_{ref}}{E} \\ \\ \end{array} 2.2 Quantities and reference results This resulted in \varepsilon_{ref}^{tot} reference values for total deformation that will be imposed at the test input in the SIMU_POINT_MAT macro-command via EPXX operand of factor keyword EPSI_IMPOSE. A second identical test is also performed by changing the length and stress units via UNITE_LONGUEUR = 'MM' and UNITE_CONTRAINTE = 'MPa' of keyword VISC_ISOT_PLAS_FO in DEFI_MATERIAU macro-command. This test is also used to verify that the VISC_ISOT_PLAS behavioral relationship works in the non-scalar case by defining the material parameters with DEFI_CONSTANTE macro-command and adapting the values to the new units (millimeter and MegaPascal). For both tests, the 1001 reference values obtained for total stress and deformation (as 'SIXX' and 'EPXX' in the table returned by SIMU_POINT_MAT respectively) will be compared with those previously calculated ( \sigma_{ref} and \varepsilon_{ref}^{tot} ), as well as with non-regression values explicitly stored in a python list of the comp004.comm file associated with the test. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution The reference results are obtained very precisely and the time step is chosen very fine. Both total deformation and stress are tolerated by 10^{-10} on relative the difference between the non-regression values and those calculated by the test. For total deformation, 10^{-10} is also tolerated between the reference and test values. As for stress, 10^{-7} is tolerated between the reference and test values except for a few moments when the criterion is somewhat released and corresponds to the transition between elastic and (visco-)plastic regime: | Instant | PRECISION (for 'SIXX') | | --- | --- | | 0.000 | 1.0\text{e-}7 | | 0.001 | 1.0\text{e-}7 | | 0.002 | 1.0\text{e-}7 | | 0.003 | 4.41\text{e-}2 | | 0.004 | 5.35\text{e-}3 | | 0.005 | 6.06\text{e-}4 | | 0.006 | 6.72\text{e-}5 | | 0.007 | 7.20\text{e-}6 | | 0.008 | 7.06\text{e-}7 | | 0.009 | 1.0\text{e-}7 | | 0.010 | 1.0\text{e-}7 | | \ldots | 1.0\text{e-}7 | 2.4 Bibliographical references None 3 Summary of the results There is a good agreement between the Modelling and the reference analytical solution (less than 5%) for this test which lasts about 15 seconds.

v6.07.105 COMP005 – Validation of GRAD_VARI formulations with ENDO_ISOT_BETON law v6.07.105 COMP005 – Validation of GRAD_VARI formulations with ENDO_ISOT_BETON law Summary: This test validates the ENDO_ISOT_BETON damage law, in 2D and 3D GRAD_VARI Modelling, defined under COMPORTEMENT. This is an elementary test of an mesh cell (cube), subjected to a temperature loading with dirichlet conditions on the faces. A comparison of the stresses is made on the calculation with GRAD_VARI and without GRAD_VARI. It allows to check the numerical equivalence between two formulations of the same behavior problem concrete damage: the formulation gradient of internal variables ( _GRAD_VARI ) and formulation local (D_PLAN, AXIS, 3D). It is ensured that, for the same load and the same boundary conditions, the fields (contraints, deformations) extracts are equivalent and the quantity comparison DIFF is zero to the expected accuracy. The 3 modellings validated are: - B Modelling: comparison D_PLAN_GRAD_VARI vs D_PLAN , - C Modelling: comparison AXIS_GRAD_VARI vs AXIS , - D Modelling: comparison 3D_GRAD_VARI vs 3D . 1 Methodology The protocol is based on a double simulation for each model: 1. Simulation 1 – GRAD_VARI The calculation is performed with a Modelling with a grade of internal variables ( _GRAD_VARI ). The constitutive law used is ENDO_ISOT_BETON (isotropic damage to concrete). 2. Simulation 2 – Without GRAD_VARI (reference) The same problem is solved with the corresponding GRAD_VARI ( D_PLAN , AXIS or 3D ) free Modelling, with the same behavior law ( ENDO_ISOT_BETON ), the same load and the same conditions for limits . At the end of the two calculations, the same quantities (contraints, deformations, internal variables, etc.) and A comparison table is being constructed. The quantity DIFF represents the difference (absolute max) between the fields from the two simulations, evaluated at the same time. point hardware / on the same set. Validation criteria : DIFF ≃ 0 at a specified accuracy (see section Tested quantities and results of Each model). 2 Interpretation of results For each model, TEST_TABLE compares the quantity DIFF to a zero reference value. The test is passed if the absolute maximum value of DIFF is less than the required tolerance (or accuracy). 3 Modelling B 3.1 Description This is a transient thermomechanical test with deformations imposed on the x and y axes. v6.07.107 COMP007 – Thermomechanical validation of nonlinear elastic laws (COMPORTEMENT) v6.07.107 COMP007 – Thermomechanical validation of nonlinear elastic laws (COMPORTEMENT) Summary This test validates the thermo-elastic constitutive laws defined in COMPORTEMENT. It allows you to check the following points: - Thermal expansion is well calculated (with consideration of the variation of thermal expansion with temperature) - The variation of the material coefficients with temperature is correct. The 4 validated laws of behaviour are as follows: - A Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ELAS model, - B Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ELAS_VMIS_LINE model, - C Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ELAS_VMIS_PUIS model, - D Modelling: This Modelling allows to validate the ELAS_VMIS_TRAC model. 1 Methodology It is a double simulation, the first in thermomechanical, the second in pure mechanics. The first will be validated in comparison with the second, assuming of course that the behaviour tested provides a correct solution in pure mechanics. The first simulation (solution that is being validated) is to apply a temperature variation to a material point, for example by blocking the following x deformations: {\varepsilon}_{xx}=0 . The temperature imposed is increasing linearly with time. The second simulation (which must be equivalent to the first) consists of applying to the same material point a deformation imposed following x : {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) , in pure mechanics. Indeed, for any behavior (assuming additive decomposition of deformations): {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)({\varepsilon}_{xx}-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) in the first case, {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(0-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) , and in the second: {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(\varepsilon -{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) . Therefore, at every moment, you can apply {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) for mechanical calculation. In addition, to obtain the same results in both cases, it is necessary, at each time step of the second simulation, to perform the pure mechanical calculation with coefficients whose values are interpolated according to the temperature at the current moment. This interpolation is performed in the command file of the test, in a loop in outside time at STAT_NON_LINE. 2 Interpretation of results The purpose is to verify with TEST_TABLE that the result obtained at each moment of the thermomechanical transient of the first simulation is identical to the result obtained with the second simulation. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Simulation 1 This is a thermomechanical test with a zero-imposed deformation on the x axis. The test is performed on a material point with the SIMU_POINT_MAT control. The temperature varies from {T}_{0}=20°C to {T}_{\max}=500°C . The material is elastic. The transient is made of NCAL not. The reference temperature is {T}_{\mathrm{Ref}}=20°C . 3.2 Simulation 2 The purpose is to perform a loop on NCAL mechanical calculations. Each i calculation, the load imposed is made up of the {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)({T}_{i}-{T}_{\mathrm{Ref}}) thermal deformation. The initial load consists of the deformations, stresses and internal variables of the previous mechanical calculation. 3.3 Constitutive law and material parameters The constitutive law tested is 'ELAS' documented in the R4.01.02 documentation. v6.07.108 COMP008 – Thermo-mechanical validation of elasto-plastic laws v6.07.108 COMP008 – Thermo-mechanical validation of elasto-plastic laws Summary This test validates the temperature variation in the elastoplastic constitutive laws. These tests allow to check the following two points: - Thermal expansion is well calculated (with consideration of the variation of thermal expansion with temperature) - The variation of material coefficients with temperature is correct, especially in incremental behavior resolution, The validated laws of behaviour are as follows: - A Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ELAS model with isotropic material - B Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ELAS model with orthotropic material, - C Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ISOT_LINE model, - D Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CINE_LINE model, - E Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VENDOCHAB model, - F Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ECMI_LINE model, - G Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CIN1_CHAB model, - H Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CIN2_CHAB model, - I Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CIN2_MEMO model, - J Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VISC_CIN1_CHAB model, - K Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VISC_CIN2_CHAB model, - L Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VISC_CIN2_MEMO model, - M modelling: this model validates the transverse isotropic elasticity, - N Modelling: This Modelling allows to validate the ROUSS_PR model. - O Modelling: This Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_JOHN_COOK model. 1 Methodology It is a double simulation, the first in thermo-mechanical, the second in pure mechanics. The first will be validated in comparison with the second, assuming of course that the behaviour tested provides a correct solution in pure mechanics. 1.1 Simulation 1 The first simulation (solution that is being validated) is to apply a temperature variation to a material point, blocking the deformations following x : {\varepsilon}_{xx}=0 . The temperature imposed is increasing linearly with time. Unless otherwise stated, the temperature varies from {T}_{0}=20°C to {T}_{\max}=500°C . Material parameters are chosen for part of the transient to be in the nonlinear domain of the constitutive law, except in elasticity. The transient is made up of NCAL not. The reference temperature is {T}_{\mathrm{Ref}}={T}_{0} . 1.2 Simulation 2 The second simulation (which must be equivalent to the first) consists of applying, in pure mechanics, without thermal, and at each moment, a deformation imposed according to x equivalent to the thermal deformation of the first simulation: This is therefore to perform a loop on NCAL mechanical calculations. At each i calculation, the imposed load consists of the thermal deformation {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}_{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)({T}_{i}-{T}_{\mathrm{Ref}}) . The initial load consists of the deformations, stresses and internal variables of the previous mechanical calculation. > Indeed, for any behavior (assuming the additive decomposition of deformations): {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)({\varepsilon}_{xx}-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) in the first case, {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(0-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) , and in the second: {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(\varepsilon -{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) . Therefore, at every moment, you can apply {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) for mechanical calculation. In addition, to obtain the same results in both cases, it is necessary, at each time step of the second simulation, to perform the pure mechanical calculation with coefficients whose values are interpolated according to the temperature at the current moment. This interpolation is performed in the command file of the test, in a loop in outside time at STAT_NON_LINE. 2 Interpretation of results The purpose of this test is to verify that the result obtained at each moment of the thermomechanical transient of the first simulation is identical to the result obtained with the second simulation: - the value to be tested is the component of the extracted field at a given moment i of the first thermo-mechanical simulation performed on NCAL moments. - the reference value is that obtained for the mechanical calculation 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics The constitutive law tested is 'ELAS'. v6.07.109 COMP009 – Thermomechanical validation of BARRE Modelling v6.07.109 COMP009 – Thermomechanical validation of BARRE Modelling Summary This test validates the temperature variation in the constitutive laws available with BARRE Modelling. These tests allow you to check the following points: - Thermal expansion is well calculated (with consideration of the variation of thermal expansion with temperature) - The variation of material coefficients with temperature is correct, especially in incremental behavior resolution, The validated laws of behaviour are as follows: - A Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ELAS model, - B Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ISOT_LINE model, - C Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_ISOT_TRAC model, - D Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VMIS_CINE_LINE model, 1 Methodology The mesh used is composed of a single mesh cell SEG2, on which BARRE Modelling is assigned. The ends of the bar are clamped, no axial deformation is possible. nodes N3 et N7 : \mathrm{DX}=\mathrm{DY}=\mathrm{DZ}=0. Section : A=1. It is a double simulation, the first in thermomechanical, the second in pure mechanics. The first will be validated in comparison with the second, assuming of course that the behaviour tested provides a correct solution in pure mechanics. The first simulation (solution that is being validated) is to apply a temperature variation to the element BARRE, for example by blocking movements along the local x axis: {\varepsilon}_{xx}=0 . The temperature imposed is increasing linearly with time. The second simulation (which must be equivalent to the first) consists of applying to the element a deformation imposed in the direction x : {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) , pure mechanics. Indeed, for any behavior (assuming the additive decomposition of the deformations) one has: {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)({\varepsilon}_{xx}-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) with normal N=A{\sigma}_{xx} effort in the first case, {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(0-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) , and in the second: {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)({\varepsilon}_{xx}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) . Therefore, at every moment, you can apply {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) for mechanical calculation. In addition, to obtain the same results in both cases, it is necessary, at each time step of the second simulation, to perform the pure mechanical calculation with coefficients whose values are interpolated according to the temperature at the current moment. This interpolation is performed in the command file of the test, in a loop in outside time at STAT_NON_LINE. 2 Interpretation of results The purpose is to verify with TEST_TABLE that the result obtained at each moment of the thermomechanical transient of the first simulation is identical to the result obtained with the second simulation. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics 3.1.1 Simulation 1 This is a thermomechanical test with zero deformation imposed on the local x axis. v6.07.110 COMP010 – Thermomechanical validation of elastoviscoplastic laws v6.07.110 COMP010 – Thermomechanical validation of elastoviscoplastic laws Summary This test validates the temperature variation in the elastoviscoplastic constitutive laws. These tests allow to check the following two points: - Thermal expansion is well calculated (with consideration of the variation of thermal expansion with temperature) - The variation of material coefficients with temperature is correct, especially in incremental behavior resolution, The validated laws of behaviour are as follows: - A Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the GRAN_IRRA_LOG model - B Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the LEMAITRE model - C Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the LEMA_SEUIL model - E Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the LEMAITRE_IRRA model - F Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VISC_IRRA_LOG model - G Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the VISC_TAHERI model - H Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the ROUSS_VISC model - I Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the model - J Modelling: this Modelling allows to validate the META_LEMA_ANI model 1 Methodology It is a double simulation, the first in thermomechanical, the second in pure mechanics. The first will be validated in comparison with the second, assuming of course that the behaviour tested provides a correct solution in pure mechanics. The first simulation (thermo-mechanical solution that l-on is seeking to validate) consists of applying a temperature variation on a material point, with a deformation imposed zero on the x axis {\epsilon}_{xx}^{1}=0 The temperature imposed is increasing linearly as a function of time. The transient is made up of NCAL not.According to the modellings: - Modellings A , C , E , F : temperature varies from {T}_{0}=0°C to {T}_{max}=500°C and reference temperature is {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=0°C . - Modellings B , G : temperature varies from {T}_{0}=20°C to {T}_{max}=500°C and the reference temperature is {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=20°C . - H Modelling: temperature varies from {T}_{0}=20°C to {T}_{max}=800°C and reference temperature is {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=20°C . - I Modelling: temperature varies from {T}_{0}=20°C to {T}_{max}=200°C and reference temperature is {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=20°C . - J Modelling: temperature varies from {T}_{0}=700°C to {T}_{max}=1000°C and reference temperature is {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=700°C . The second simulation (which must be equivalent to the first) consists of applying to the same material point a deformation imposed following x such as: {\epsilon}_{xx}^{2}=-{\epsilon}^{\mathit{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}}) In pure mechanical design on NCAL moments of thermomechanical calculations. Each i calculation, the load is made of thermal deformation. {\epsilon}_{xx}^{2}=-{\epsilon}^{\mathit{th}}=-\alpha ({T}_{i})({T}_{i}-{T}_{\mathit{ref}}) The initial load consists of the deformations, stresses and internal variables of the previous mechanical calculation, the stresses being corrected for the variation of the Young's modulus Indeed, for any behavior (assuming the additive decomposition of deformations): {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)({\varepsilon}_{xx}-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) In the first case: {\sigma}_{xx}^{1}=E(T)(0-{\epsilon}^{\mathit{th}}-{\epsilon}_{xx}^{p}) In the second case: {\sigma}_{xx}^{2}=E(T)(\epsilon -{\epsilon}_{xx}^{p}) Therefore, at every moment, you can apply {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) for mechanical calculation. In addition, in order to obtain the same results in both cases, it is necessary, at each time step of the second simulation, to perform the pure mechanical calculation with coefficients whose values are interpolated according to the temperature at the current moment. v6.07.111 COMP011 – Thermomechanical validation of concrete laws v6.07.111 COMP011 – Thermomechanical validation of concrete laws Summary This test validates the temperature variation in the constitutive laws for concrete. These tests allow to verify the following two points: - The thermal expansion is well calculated (with consideration of the variation of thermal expansion with temperature). - The variation of material coefficients with temperature is correct, especially in incremental behavior resolution. The validated laws of behaviour are as follows: - Modelling A: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_REGLE_PR model. - Modelling B: This Modelling allows to validate the MAZARS model. - Modelling C: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_UMLV model. - Modelling D: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_DOUBLE_DP model. - Modelling E: This Modelling allows to validate the ENDO_ISOT_BETON model. - Modelling F: This Modelling allows to validate the BETON_BURGER model. - Modelling G: This Modelling allows to validate the MAZARS_UNIL model. - H Modelling: This Modelling validates the Leverett isotherm hygrometry calculation (BETON_DESORP/LEVERETT='OUI'). 1 Methodology It is a double simulation, the first in thermo-mechanical, the second in pure mechanics. The first will be validated in comparison with the second, assuming of course that the behaviour tested provides a correct solution in pure mechanics. 1.1 Simulation 1 The first simulation (the thermo-mechanical solution that is being validated) consists of applying a temperature variation to a material point, blocking deformations according to the x {\varepsilon}_{xx}=0 direction. The temperature imposed is increasing linearly as a function of time.The temperature varies from {T}_{0}=20°C to {T}_{max}=500°C .The transient is constituted byNCAL not.The reference temperature is {T}_{\mathit{réf}}=20°C . 1.2 Simulation 2 The second simulation (which must be equivalent to the first) consists of applying to the same point material a deformation imposed following x : {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathit{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}}) , in pure mechanics. Each i calculation, the load imposed consists of the thermal deformation {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}_{\mathit{th}}=-\alpha (T)({T}_{i}-{T}_{\mathit{réf}}) . The initial load consists of the deformations, stresses and internal variables of the previous mechanical calculation. Indeed, for any behavior (assuming the additive decomposition of deformations): {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)({\varepsilon}_{xx}-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) in the first case, {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(0-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}-{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) , and in the second: {\sigma}_{xx}=E(T)(\varepsilon -{\varepsilon}_{xx}^{p}) . Therefore, at every moment, you can apply {\varepsilon}_{xx}=-{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{th}}=-\alpha (T)(T-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}) for mechanical calculation. In addition, to obtain the same results in both cases, it is necessary, at each time step of the second simulation, to perform the pure mechanical calculation with coefficients whose values are interpolated according to the temperature at the current moment. This interpolation is performed in the command file of the test, in a loop in outside time at STAT_NON_LINE. 2 Interpretation of results The purpose is to verify that the result obtained at each moment of the thermo-mechanical transient of the first simulation is identical to the result obtained with the second simulation. The validation is done by comparing the fields calculated at each step of the transient on the one hand with the result of a mechanical calculation on the other, the reference value being the component of the field extracted at a given moment i from the first thermo-mechanical simulation performed on NCAL moments. The calculated value is that obtained at the end of the mechanical calculation i+1 of the loop on the NCAL. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Constitutive law and material parameters The constitutive law tested is The elastic parameters are as follows: E(T) ,

In model A, these nine tests are simulated with Hujeux's law. For the ESSAI_ISOT_DR_C_F test, the calculated solutions are compared with those of the test case ssnv204a. Finally, for the last test, the solutions are controlled by non-regression tests. In model B, a drained monotonous triaxial test with imposed displacement is simulated with MOHR_COULOMB law. The solution is compared to an analytical solution. In model C, a non-drained cyclic triaxial test with imposed force is simulated on a sand modelled with Hujeux's law. It validates the detection of instability specific to this test and the change of the test in controlled deformation. In model D, a cyclic shear test drained with Iwan's law is simulated. In model E, a non-drained cyclic triaxial test with force imposed is simulated on the same sand as model C and modelled with Hujeux's law. It allows testing the crossovers of the new liquefaction criteria and illustrates the use of new keywords introduced by the recasting of the macro-command in Code_Aster version 14.2. In F Modelling, a monotonous drained triaxial test with imposed displacement is simulated with MohrCoulombAS law. The solution is compared to an analytical solution. In G Modelling, a drained monotonous triaxial test with imposed displacement is simulated with NLH_CSRM law. A non-regression test validates the robustness of the model. Indeed, the Q stress deviator has a maximum value on this value line below the maximum stress set {Q}_{max}=110\mathit{kPa} . Therefore, the stress control of the test is not possible at this location, and generally leads either to a divergence of the calculation or to a perfectly unstable false result (high stress and deformation, see the red curve of the Figure). The calculation of the exact solution passes through the tilting of the test in controlled deformation when the instability is detected (blue curve). v6.07.113 COMP013 – incremental isotropic and hyperelastic elasticity v6.07.113 COMP013 – incremental isotropic and hyperelastic elasticity This test aims to test constitutive laws incremental isotropic elasticity ELAS_ISOT_INCR and isotropic hyperelasticity ELAS_ISOT_ENER in 3D and 1D, in the presence of command variables. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The problem is homogeneous. We rely on the SIMU_POINT_MAT command for 3D tests. As for 1D tests, a slash is passed through the (Oxy) plane, the original coordinates of which are (2,1,0) , (4,2,0) end and the cross section is S=5 mm^2 . 1.2 Material properties The material is elastic. The Poisson's ratio is set to 0.3 but this value does not affect the results because the load is uniaxial. The Young's modulus depends on the temperature affinely. The coefficients of thermal expansion, desiccation removal and endogenous withdrawal are constant. The values are given in the table below. Note that these values are not representative of a specific material. | Poisson's ratio | \nu=0.3 | | --- | --- | | Young's modulus | T= 20 °C \quad E = 10^5 MPA | | T= 120 °C \quad E = 2 \times 10^5 MPA | | | Thermal dilation | \alpha = 10^{-5}°C^{-1} \quad T_{ref}=0°C | | Withdrawal of desiccation | k=10^{-5}m^3/l \quad C_{ref}=500l/m^3 | | Endogenous withdrawal | \beta= 10^{-5} | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads In the 3D case, the \varepsilon uniaxial deformation is imposed by leaving zero stresses in the normal directions at loading. In the 1D case, the following displacement is imposed on all nodes of the bar, where \varepsilon again designates the uniaxial deformation level: The deformation changes from \varepsilon_0=10^{-3} to \varepsilon_1=3 \times 10^{-3} . In general, index 0 will refer to the values at the beginning of loading and index 1 will refer to the end of loading. There are no forces imposed but it is considered that there is an initial stress \sigma_0=100 MPa . Finally, the material is subject to an evolution of the control variables: - Temperature changes from T_0=20°C to T_1=120°C - Water concentration changes from C_0=500L/m^3 to C_1=300L/m^3 - The degree of hydration changes from \xi_0=0 to \xi_1=1 - The anelastic (external) deformation changes from \varepsilon_0^a=10^{-3} to \varepsilon_1^a=3 \times 10^{-3} . Note that \varepsilon_1^a=3 \times 10^{-3} is (temporarily) not applied to 3D situations, due to a bug in SIMU_POINT_MAT. 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution In view of the control variables, mechanical deformation is written as follows: \varepsilon^m=\varepsilon-\alpha(T-T_{ref})-k(C-C_{ref})+\beta\xi-\varepsilon^a In the case of hyperelastic behaviour (ELAS_ISOT_ENER), the stress at the end of loading then simply expresses itself as a function of the current mechanical deformation, without history effect: \sigma_1=E(T_1)\varepsilon_1^m The case of incremental elastic behaviour (ELAS_ISOT_INCR) is more complicated, as the constitutive law is written in function of an intermediate deformation a : \begin{aligned} \sigma &=E a ; \\ \dot a &= \dot\varepsilon_m \end{aligned} The initial value of this intermediate deformation is determined by the knowledge of the initial state, i.e. a_0=\sigma_0/E(T_0) . v6.08.101 SSND101 – constitutive law for viscous shock absorbers on discreet elements v6.08.101 SSND101 – constitutive law for viscous shock absorbers on discreet elements Summary: The response of the DIS_VISC nonlinear viscous shock absorber model, of the generalised 的Zener type, cf. R5.03.17, formulated on discrete elements for mesh cells SEG2 or POI1, is tested. Although it is a viscous law, it is the STAT_NON_LINE operator that is used for validation. The discrete d的elements response is analyzed for a nonlinear viscous constitutive law under a harmonic load. The modellings are: 1. static non-linear cycle, 1. static linear cyclic and dissipation calculation, 1. static non-linear creep, 1. static nonlinear, Modelling a shock absorber of type MAXWELL. The discrete modellings and elements tested are in \mathrm{3D} with modellings DIS_T and DIS_TR and the basic features: (K_T_D_L, K_TR_D_L, K_T_D_N, K_TR_D_N, A_T_D_L, M_T_D_L), depending on the type of mesh cell and d的element. This behavior is also validated for dynamic stresses in test case SDND107 V5.01.107 with DYNA_VIBRA and DYNA_NON_LINE operators. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Description of the device L-slipper is represented by the rheological model below. Figure 1.1-a: Rheological model of viscous shock absorber. The values of the different {E}_{1} , {E}_{2} , {E}_{3} and the characteristics of the nonlinear viscous part {C}_{3} , {\alpha}_{3} are derived from tests. The equations governing the behaviour are R5.03.17: {\dot{F}}_{1}\left(\frac{1}{{E}_{1}}+\frac{1}{{E}_{3}}+\frac{{E}_{2}}{\left({E}_{1}.{E}_{3}\right)}\right)=\left({\dot{U}}_{2}-{\dot{U}}_{1}\right)\left(1+\frac{{E}_{2}}{{E}_{3}}\right)-{\langle \langle \frac{{F}_{1}}{{C}_{3}}\left(1+\frac{{E}_{2}}{{E}_{1}}\right)-\frac{{E}_{2}}{{C}_{3}}\left({U}_{2}-{U}_{1}\right)\rangle \rangle }^{1/{\alpha}_{3}} with \begin{array}{cc}{\langle \langle x\rangle \rangle }^{a}={x}^{a}& \mathit{si}x\ge 0\\ {\langle \langle x\rangle \rangle }^{a}=-{∣x∣}^{a}& \mathit{si}x\le 0\end{array} The dissipation increment is: \Delta D={C}_{3}.{∣\frac{{F}_{1}}{{C}_{3}}\left(1+\frac{{E}_{2}}{{E}_{1}}\right)-\frac{{E}_{2}}{{C}_{3}}\left({U}_{2}-{U}_{1}\right)∣}^{1+1/{\alpha}_{3}} 1.2 modellings The modellings tested are on elements DIS_T then DIS_TR, mesh cells SEG2 then mesh cells POI1. The stiffness features of the discreet elements, which are used for predicting nonlinear algorithm, are therefore of the type: K_T_D_L, K_TR_D_L, K_T_D_N, K_TR_D_N, depending on the type of d的element. Note: The units of the parameters must be in accordance with the unit of forces, length unit and time unit of the R5.03.17 problem. For all modellings units are homogeneous to [N], [m], [s]. 1.2.1 Modelling A This Modelling allows testing the static nonlinear cyclic behaviour of the law. 1.2.2 Modelling B This nonlinear static model allows the dissipation of a stabilized cyclic load to be tested in addition to the constitutive law. Dissipation is compared to a theoretical value obtained in the particular case {\alpha}_{3}=1.0 . For a cyclic load with {\alpha}_{3}\ne 1 the theoretical calculation of dissipation is not accessible. 1.2.3 Modelling C This nonlinear static Modelling allows testing of constitutive law during a creep test. The displacement is imposed and remains constant. The response of constitutive law and dissipation are compared to the theoretical values obtained in the particular case {\alpha}_{3}=0.5 . 1.2.4 Modelling D This Modelling validates the fact that it is possible to model a Maxwell type shock absorber by affecting the suitable material characteristics. It is possible to make the stiffeners to the infinite by using the UNSUR_K key words when defining the material. In this particular case \mathit{K1}=120.0 , \mathit{K2}=0 , \mathit{K3}\to \infty or \mathit{UNSUR}\text{\_}\mathit{K3}=0 . The modeled shock absorber is shown in the following figure. v6.08.103 SSND103 - Validation of a bilinear constitutive law on a discreet element (application to bolted assemblies) v6.08.103 SSND103 - Validation of a bilinear constitutive law on a discreet element (application to bolted assemblies) Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate a bilinear constitutive law on a discreet element. This constitutive law was developed in a study in which the behaviour of the screw d-a bolted assembly is modelled by a discrete element affected by the same behavior. The constitutive law DIS_BILI_ELAS requires in argument the two apparent screw stiffeners (elements of the contact assembly or not) as well as the value of the pre-locking force imposed on the screw. It is verified that the gradients of the load curves obtained when the discrete is applied correspond to the apparent stiffeners for different temperatures and direction of stress and that the slope break corresponds to the pre-stressed force imposed. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry \stackrel{ˉ}{U} In theory, a load (force or displacement) is being imposed on a discrete element represented by a node as in Figure a . In practice, a blocking condition must be introduced on this node to avoid any movement of solid body and give a physical meaning to its stiffness. Therefore, the mesh will be composed of two nodes, with the stiffness assigned to the segment formed by their junction (see Figure b ). N.B. : If this segment has a nonzero length (i.e. both nodes are not confused), its direction sets the direction of the discrete. - \mathrm{N1} is called the node to which the blocking conditions will be applied. - \mathrm{N2} is the node on which mechanical loadings will be imposed. - \mathrm{Disc} l的element is called discrete SEG2 type, which is affected by the constitutive law to be validated. 1.2 Material properties The material data of an elastic steel: E={2.10}^{11}\mathrm{Pa} , \nu =0.3 is arbitrarily chosen to assign to the discreet element . 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads A d-condition is imposed on the node \mathrm{N1} . It is considered that the discreet element can only work in translation, and is assigned DIS_T Modelling. 2 reference solution The discrete element is assigned, via the bilinear constitutive law, two {K}_{1} and {K}_{2} stiffeners, which are the temperature functions of the {K}_{i}={\alpha}_{i}-{\beta}_{i}\dot{T} shape. v6.08.104 SSND104 - Validation of the DRUCK_PRAG_N_A behavior v6.08.104 SSND104 - Validation of the DRUCK_PRAG_N_A behavior Summary: This test concerns the case of a single mesh cell for both modellings A and B to compare the Drucker-Prager behaviors in the associated and non-associated version. In Modelling A, the idea is to choose a P_ULTM parameter large enough for both laws to be assimilated to perfect plasticity. Therefore, a cross validation of these two behaviors is undertaken. In Modelling B, the material parameters are more common and the goal is to have a validation in NON-REGRESSION. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Figure 1.1-a The geometry refers to a single square isoparametric finite element, the length of each edge is 1. 1.2 Material properties The massif consists of elasto-plastic material modelled by a Drucker Prager constitutive law, associated or not. The material elasticities parameters are as follows: - Young's modulus isotropic elasticity: E={10}^{9}\mathrm{Pa} - Poisson's ratio : \nu =0,3 - Actual constant density: \rho =2764\mathit{kg}.{m}^{-3} - Isotropic thermal expansion coefficient: \alpha =0 The nut-work characteristics are then given by: - Pressure dependency coefficient: \alpha =0,328 - Elasticity limit: {\sigma}_{y}=2.11\times {10}^{6} - Ultimate Constraint: {\sigma}_{\mathit{ULTM}}=1.0\times {10}^{6} For modelling A: Ultimate cumulative plastic deformation: {P}_{\mathrm{ULT}}=2 For modelling B: Ultimate cumulative plastic deformation: {P}_{\mathit{ULT}}=1.225\times {10}^{-2} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads A unit displacement is imposed on the y axis on the \mathrm{CD} segment, zero on the y axis on the \mathrm{AB} segment and zero on the x segment on the \mathrm{AD} segment. v6.08.119 SSND119 - Validation of DASHPOT Relationship for Discreet elements v6.08.119 SSND119 - Validation of DASHPOT Relationship for Discreet elements Summary: The objective of this test case is to validate the constitutive law DASHPOT available for discreet elements by an analytical test. 1 reference solution The constitutive law DASHPOT binds, at each {t}_{i} calculation moment, the nodal force F({t}_{i}) to the {\Delta}_{x}({t}_{i}) displacement increment as follows: F({t}_{i})=K{\Delta}_{x}({t}_{i}) where K is a stiffness parameter provided by the user. In this test, the following moving load is required: U(t)=\sin(\omega t) . The analytical solution for force is thus expressed as follows: F(t)=K\omega {\Delta}_{t}\cos(t) where {\Delta}_{t} is the time-increment. 2 Modelling A 2.1 Geometry and modelling The model has 4 discreet elements, 2 based on mesh cells POI1 and 2 based on mesh cells SEG2. For each mesh cells type, the first vector of the local marker is oriented according to the X vector (global) for one mesh cell and according to Y for the other. For POI1, the keyword ORIENTATION is used to impose this, for SEG2, this is imposed by geometry. This allows to verify the correct consideration of the keyword REPERE that can take the GLOBAL or LOCAL values. 2.2 Parameters The parameters are as follows: - \omega =2\pi f with f=50\mathit{Hz} - K=(\mathrm{1,0,0}) , only a longitudinal stiffness (according to the local x vector) is imposed - The orientation is chosen: (30.30.30.30) to validate unidirectional behavior in a quelcquonque repere; - Two {\Delta}_{t} values are considered, a low for the first 1E-4 calculation, leading to low displacement increments and therefore low forces, and a higher for the second 1E-3 calculation, leading to larger displacement increments and therefore greater forces. 2.3 Results For both calculations and for the 4 elements, the maximum difference between the analytical value and the calculated value shall be tested at each moment of calculation. This maximum shall be close to 0. For each calculation, this value is identical for the 4 elements. Moreover, as can be expected, the lower the time increment the closer one is to the analytical solution. | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Calculation {\Delta}_{t}=1E-4 | «ANALYTIQUE» | | 1E-5 | | Calculation {\Delta}_{t}=1E-3 | «ANALYTIQUE» | | 2E-3 | The following figure compares the calculated results with the analytical solutions for the two calculations performed. 3 Conclusion The DASHPOT relationship has the behavior expected.

v7.01.100 HPLA100 - Hollow thermoelastic cylinder with uniform rotation v7.01.100 HPLA100 - Hollow thermoelastic cylinder with uniform rotation Summary The purpose of this test is to test the second members corresponding to the effects of gravity, thermal expansion and acceleration due to uniform rotation. For modellings C and D ( \mathrm{3D} hull), a chain thermo-elastic calculation and a thermoelastical calculation without plastic evolution were performed. The results for modellings are presented: - \mathrm{2D} axisymmetric: elements isoparametric finished axisymmetric on mesh cells QUAD8, - axisymmetric hulls: elements axisymmetric isoparametric finished on mesh cells SEG3 (mesh meridian section linear), - \mathrm{3D} hulls: elements finished MEC3QU9H, MEC3TR7H on mesh cells QUAD9 and TRIA7, respectively, - \mathrm{DKT} plates: elements finished DKQ planes, DKT on mesh cells QUAD4 and TRIA3 respectively. DEFI_COMPOSITE orthotropic shells are also tested for two layers of the same isotropic material and ELAS_COQU key word for the assignment of homogenized plate characteristics. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry > (m) cylinder geometry: | Internal radius | {R}_{i}=19.5 | | --- | --- | | Outside radius | {R}_{e}=20.5 | | Point F | R=20.0 | | Thickness | h=1.0 | | Height | L=10.0 | 1.2 Material properties The material is homogeneous isotropic, linear thermoelastic, the initial state is virgin. | Young's modulus | E=2.0E-5{\mathrm{N.mm}}^{-2} | | --- | --- | | Poisson's ratio | \nu =0.3 | | Density by volume | \rho =8.0{E}^{-6}{\mathrm{kg.mm}}^{-3} | | Dilation coefficient | \alpha =1.0{E}^{-5}°{C}^{-1} | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads - Displacement: - \Omega =1.0{s}^{-1} according to \mathrm{OZ} axis - Charge imposed: - gravity, g=10.0{\mathit{m.s}}^{-2} according to \mathrm{OZ} axis - traction force on the upper side: -160.0{E}^{-4}N equivalent to a force distributed over \mathrm{CD} of -8.0{E}^{-4}{\mathrm{N.mm}}^{-1} - Thermal dilation: T(\rho )-{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}(\rho )=\frac{({T}_{s}+{T}_{i})}{2}+\frac{({T}_{s}-{T}_{i}).(r-R)}{h} with: - case 1: {T}_{s}=0.5°C,{T}_{i}=-0.5°C,{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}=0.0°C - case 2: {T}_{s}=0.1°C,{T}_{i}=0.1°C,{T}_{\mathrm{ref}}=0.0°C These temperature fields are calculated with THER_LINEAIRE, using a stationary calculation on the same mesh, but with a PLAN model to have a solution affine in thickness. The boundary conditions on the move (and rotation) being different according to the model considered, they will be described later (in the paragraphs relating to modellings). 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The calculation method used for reference solution was determined by F. Voldoire (EDF R&D / AMA) and is presented in the Appendix. The analytical reference results are: - movements and rotations, - axial stress, generalized forces (in hull theory), in internal and external skins on \mathrm{AB} and \mathrm{CD} sections. v7.14.103 EPICU03 - Validation of the POST_KCP command correction β in the case of a semi-elliptic defect. v7.14.103 EPICU03 - Validation of the POST_KCP command correction β in the case of a semi-elliptic defect. Summary: The POST_KCP control calculates the elastic stress intensity factor and the elasto-plastic stress intensity factor (also known as "plasticly corrected") using the nodes stress counting from mechanical resolution respectively via the influence coefficient method and the so-called β correction method described in the RSE-M annex 5.4. This test validates the determination of stress intensity factors of a semi-elliptic defect under longitudinal orientation coating at first and circumferential orientation in a second stage at the point of the defect at the base metal side. The thermo-mechanical transient considered to be spatially uniform at each moment and the thermal and mechanical properties of the coating as well as of the base metal being also spatially invariant, the absence of an effective defect in the mesh of the core zone of the tank, which is inherent in this simplified method of defect harmfulness analysis, allows this test to be carried out by using axisymmetric Modelling of the core zone of the tank. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The geometry studied is that of the core zone of a generic 1300 MWe tank. 1.2 Defect In the simplified fault-harm analysis methodology, the method of calculating the stress strength factor elastic via the influence coefficient method assumes inherently the absence of effective fault modelling in the mesh. In fact, the mesh allows the stress to be calculated initially at the nodes and a post-processing is then applied to calculate the stress intensity factor elastic by the influence coefficient method from these stresses at the nodes (the method is detailed in R7.02.10). For this test, the under-coating defect considered is semi-elliptic and longitudinal orientation in the first stage and circumferential orientation in a second stage. Its surface-side tip is strictly based on the interface between the coating and the base metal. Its dimensions are as follows (see figure below): - depth: {\mathit{prof}}_{\text{def}}=\mathrm{5mm} - length: \mathrm{2c}\mathrm{=}\mathrm{25mm} 1.3 General description of thermomechanical coupling The study consists of a thermo-mechanical chaining. The thermal calculation and the mechanical calculation are performed on the same mesh. The mesh used for these two calculations consists only of 2nd order d-elements (mesh called "quadratic"). Given the invariances of the problem, the chosen Modelling is axisymmetric and only one mesh cell is used in the direction of the height of the vessel. 1.4 Material properties For thermal calculation: Two properties are indicated, namely: - LAMBDA: isotropic temperature function thermal conductivity, expressed in {\mathit{W.m}}^{-1}.{K}^{-1} , - BETA: enthalpy volume as a function of temperature, expressed in {\mathit{J.m}}^{-3} . v7.14.303 HSLV303 – CALC_THERMECA_MULT operator verification on a hollow cylinder subjected to thermal shock v7.14.303 HSLV303 – CALC_THERMECA_MULT operator verification on a hollow cylinder subjected to thermal shock Summary: To reduce the time required to set up thermomechanic calculations in the linear domain, a new methodology is proposed. This methodology consists of determining the temperature in a structure from the calculation of a unit thermal shock using the CALC_THERMECA_MULT macro-command. The objective of this test case is to validate this methodology on the one hand and to verify its ease of implementation on the other. In this test case, one models a tube in which a fluid carrying a thermal shock circulates. Then the mechanical response is calculated using the same methodology. The four modellingss performed are as follows: - Modelization A : Volume modelling which calculates the transient thermal analysis response and the associated mechanical response for \Delta T=50°C thermal shock from (\Delta {T}_{U}=1°C) unit thermal shock via CALC_THERMECA_MULT. - Modelling B : axisymmetric Modelling or transient thermal analysis response and associated mechanical response for \Delta T=50°C thermal shock from (\Delta {T}_{U}=1°C) unit heat shock via CALC_THERMECA_MULT. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The structure consists of a tube in which a fluid carrying the thermal shock flows. - Straight tube section - Length of tube: L=0.1m - Outer tube diameter: {\varphi}_{\mathit{ext}}=0.048m - Tube thickness: e=0.006m 1.2 Material properties - \lambda =15W/m°C Thermal conductivity coefficient - {C}_{P}=500J/\mathit{Kg}°C Specific heat - a=3.8x{10}^{-6}{m}^{2}/s Thermal diffusivity - E=200000\mathit{MPa} Young's modulus - \nu =0.3 Poisson's ratio - \alpha =15x{10}^{-6}/°C Thermal expansion coefficient 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Thermal shock is transmitted to the tube by the fluid via convective exchange. Two thermal shocks are studied: | Thermal shock | Intrados | Extrados | | --- | --- | --- | | \Delta T=1°C | {T}_{\mathit{fluide}}=21°C h=20000W/{m}^{2}/°C | {T}_{\mathit{imposée}}=20°C | | \Delta T=50°C | {T}_{\mathit{fluide}}=70°C h=20000W/{m}^{2}/°C | {T}_{\mathit{imposée}}=20°C | The thermal shock corresponds to the difference between the initial temperature of the tube and that of the fluid. The flow is zero in the axial direction of the tube ( \frac{\partial T(x,t)}{\partial z}=0 ). For mechanical analysis the tube is blocked at its base in the axial direction. 1.4 Initial conditions - T(x,t=0)=20°C for \Delta T=50°C impact - T(x,t=0)=20°C for \Delta {T}_{U}=1°C unit impact 1.5 Details concerning modellings To define the time discretization the time constant \tau =\frac{{e}^{2}}{(a{\pi}^{2})}=1s is used which gives us in the case of a thermal shock the moment beyond which the thermal behavior becomes almost stationary in the tube. The duration of the thermal shock is fixed to {10.}^{-1}s . We chose the discretization in the following time: | 5 | not for | [0.0,0.1] | either | \Delta t=0.01s | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | not for | [0.1,0.5] | either | \Delta t=0.04s | | 4 | not for | [0.5,3.0] | either | \Delta t=0.25s | | 1 | not for | [3.0,5.0] | either | \Delta t=0.4s | | 1 | not for | [5.0,10.] | either | \Delta t=2.5s | 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution To reduce the time required to implement thermal calculations in the linear field, a new methodology is proposed. A \Omega structure is considered. A thermal shock is imposed on part of the \partial \Omega structure. The following figure presents an example. Thermal shock is defined as a significant and instantaneous temperature increment. Figure 2 shows an example of several consecutive thermal shocks. Fourrier's law describing the thermal exchange applied to this thermally shocked structure may be written in this form: T(x,t)=\lbrace \begin{array}{c}T(x,{t}_{0})\text{pour t }{t}_{c}\end{array} In addition, considering that the \beta scalar is time independent, which is consistent with a thermal shock, we have: \underset{{t}_{c}}{\overset{t}{\int}}a\beta \frac{{\partial}^{2}\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t)}{\partial {x}^{2}}\mathit{dt}=\beta \underset{{t}_{c}}{\overset{t}{\int}}a\frac{{\partial}^{2}\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t)}{\partial {x}^{2}}\mathit{dt} The integral present in this problem equation is in reality the solution previously obtained for the unit shock: \underset{{t}_{c}}{\overset{t}{\int}}a\frac{{\partial}^{2}\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t)}{\partial {x}^{2}}\mathit{dt}=\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t)\text{}\mathit{pour}t\ge {t}_{c} The solution to the problem of any thermal shock on \partial \Omega solution obtained for unit thermal shock: \stackrel{̃}{{T}_{\beta}}(x,t)=\beta .\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t) Here it is considered that unit heat shock occurs at the same time as thermal shock \Delta {t}_{c} . If the shock occurs at another time, simply shift the solution: \stackrel{̃}{{T}_{\beta}}(x,t)=\beta .\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t-({t}_{c}-{t}_{\mathit{c2}})) Where {t}_{\mathit{c2}} is the moment of the unit shock. Therefore, by choosing the unit shock so that {t}_{\mathit{c2}} is at the moment t=\mathrm{0s} , the solution becomes: \stackrel{̃}{{T}_{\beta}}(x,t)=\beta .\stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t-{t}_{c}) The temperature range of the structure can therefore be determined by following the following steps: - Set a uniform initial temperature field on the {T}_{\beta}(x,{t}_{0}) structure - Set up a thermal analysis of a unit shock at t=\mathrm{0s} time on the structure and get the solution of the unit problem and determine \stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t) . It may be wise to impose an initial temperature zero so that \stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t)={T}_{U}(x,t) . - Calculate the solution (space and time) from a linear combination of the initial T(x,{t}_{0}) situation, the intensity of the \beta shock and the solution of the \stackrel{̃}{{T}_{U}}(x,t) shock problem. 2.2 Baseline 2.2.1 Thermal analyses The thermal behavior is axisymmetric. Several points through the thickness and two moments are chosen to test the temperature response. The reference results were obtained by Code_Aster and with a linear mesh axisymmetric four times finer.
