v7.15.100 FORMA02 - Practical work of the "Initiation" training: thermomechanical and dynamically-sold pipe v7.15.100 FORMA02 - Practical work of the "Initiation" training: thermomechanical and dynamically-sold pipe Summary: This test corresponds to the practical work of the basic training when using Code_Aster . It is a bent pipe, consisting of a linear elastic material, subjected to various loads: internal pressure, thermal transient, transient force. The modellings used are: - Modelling A: 3D modelling, thermomechanical calculation, - Modelling B: 3D modelling, dynamic calculation, modal and transient, - Modelling C: elements DKT hulls, mechanical calculation under internal pressure loading, - D Modelling: elements beams (POU_D_T), dynamic calculation. Chapter 1 "Reference problem" presents the problem to be processed and the data common to all modellings; the statements of the Training Practical Work are included in this document: - TP2: "3D thermo-elastic" see model A, - TP2:"3D dynamic" see model B. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The study concerns a pipe with two straight pipes and one elbow [Figure 1.1-a]. The geometrical data of the problem are as follows: - the {L}_{G} length of both straight pipes is 3m , - the \mathit{Rc} radius of the elbow is 0.6m , - \theta angle of the elbow is 90° , - \text{e} thickness of straight pipes and elbow is 0.02m , - and the \text{Re} outer radius of the straight pipes and elbow is 0.2m . Figure 1.1-a Note: The geometry of the problem shows a symmetry with the plane (A,X,Y) . 1.2 Material properties For all modellings A, B, C and D: Isotropic elastic material. Material properties are those of \mathrm{A42} steel to 20°C : - le Young's modulus E=204000.\times {10}^{+6}N/{m}^{2} , - le Poisson's ratio \nu =0.3 . For thermo-elastic calculation (modelization A): - the thermal expansion coefficient \alpha =1.096\times {10}^{–5}/°C , - \lambda =54.6W/m°C thermal conduction, - \rho \mathit{Cp}=3.71\times {10}^{6}J/{m}^{3}°C volumetric heat, For dynamic calculation (modellings B, D): - \rho =7800\mathrm{kg}/{m}^{3} density , - The mode damping will be taken at \text{5\%} for modes. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The boundary conditions for all modellings are as follows: - clamped support at A section level, - when loading static clamped support at A section and B section . For static calculations, the loads applied are of three types: - internal pressure (on the inner side) P={15.10}^{+6}N/{m}^{2} (shell Modelling or 3D), - thermomechanical loading with a temperature transient imposed on the inner surface of the piping (mounting from 20°C to 70°C in \mathrm{10s} ) and a zero exchange condition on the outer surface of the piping (calori-refuge) (modelling A only). For dynamic calculation, the load applied is a transient force (in Newton): \mathit{FY}(t)=10000000.\sin(2\pi \mathit{Freq}1.t) directed on Y axis and applied on B section with \mathit{Freq}1=20\mathit{Hz} . 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is obtained numerically, so it is only non-regression tests. 2.2 Results of the different modellings: 2.2.1 Static calculation The values tested are: - for pressure loading (modellings A and C), the displacement at the upper elbow outlet at the mean surface (as in the figure below in white, DX at -4.52e-4 m) - for thermomechanical loading (modelization A), internal wall temperature at the foot of the tube (70°C) and maximum stress Von Loads of the order of 200 MPa. 2.2.2 Dynamic calculation The values tested are: - For 3D modelling (modelization B), the first eigenfrequency of the order of 9Hz and the displacement component DYdu point P at the end of the pipework at the mean surface (as in the figure below in white) of the order of -0.128m at instant 1s. - for 1D Modelling (modelization D), equivalent tube foot stresses. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Glossary: in Salomé: - vertex points useful for the construction of geometry; - edge lines (right); - arcs of circles; - wire lines composed of edge and arc; - face of the surfaces bounded by a wire; - shell a set of faces intended to be meshed or delimiting a volume; - Compounds a set of geometric entities. Straight pipes and elbow are modelled by isoparametric quadratic massive elementss. The piping has a Z=0 symmetry plane. One mesh cell only has half volume. Boundary conditions and loading: see Chapter 1.3. 3.2 Geometry Launch the Geometry module of the Salome-Meca platform. Two methods to create geometry (recommend the second): - Extrusion of a base surface on a path: 1. Create \mathit{Ae1} points , \mathit{Ai1} , \mathit{Ae2} , \mathit{Ai2} , \mathit{Pe1} , Pi1 , then L1 and L2 circle arcs , d1 and d2 segments (Menu New Entity → Basic → Point / arc / Line). 2. Creation of the contour (wire) bounded by L1 , d1 , l2 , d2 and then the surface (object type " Face ") from this contour (Menu New Entity → Build → wireless / Face ). 3. Creating the wire path: A,C,D,B,O points, then the two \mathit{AC} and \mathit{DB} lines, and \mathit{CD} circle arch, finally the total \mathit{ACDB} path in wire. 4. This surface is then extruded by the New Entity menu → Generation → Extrusion Along Path. - Use of basic volumetric objects: - Build a straight Z hose (default option), using two 3 -height elementary cylinders and 0.2 and 0.18 (Menu New Entity → Primitives → Cylinder), and a Boolean operation (Menu Operations → Boolean → Cut). Rename the object created in \mathit{TUY}1 . - Apply a rotation to \mathit{TUY}1 around X to make it d-axis Y (Menu Operations → Transformation → Rotation): Angle = -90° and disable Create a copy. - Select the top side by creating a group: New Entity Menu → Group → Create Group. This side allows you to generate the elbow through the New Entity menu → Generation → Revolution (Angle = -90°). This requires creating the revolution axis (a Z steering vector via the point O (\mathrm{0.6,}\mathrm{3.0,}0.0) ): creating (\mathrm{0.6,}\mathrm{3.0,}0.0) and (\mathrm{0.6,}\mathrm{3.0,}1.0) points and then creating the vector (Menu New Entity → Basic → Vector). - Then create the second straight pipe \mathit{TUY}2 in the same way: select the upper side of the elbow by creating a group, and generate the right pipe by the New Entity menu → Generation → Extrusion following X . - The remaining half of the piping located in the Z>0 plane is selected. For this you can first create a plan (Menu New Entity → Basic → Plane, for example, the 5th choice of Plane (creation from the local coordinate system), with the option OXY and size 8). Then cut using the partition (Menu Operations → Sheet) by selecting the 3 parts of the piping as Object and the plan as Tool Objects. - Create a volume group by selecting the parts located in Z>0 (Menu New Entity → Group → Create Group)., and finally with this group create a "comound" (Menu New Entity → Build → Compound). Preparation of geometry for mesh in hexahedrons : The pipe is intended to be meshed with hexahedrons, i.e. set (the number d-elements is identical on two opposite sides). Before proceeding with the mesh, it is necessary to check that the geometry is topologically equivalent to a hexahedron (6 sides). To do so, you must use the menu Inspection → Check Compound of Blocks. Depending on the construction mode (the first process), it may be necessary to make a partition by two planes of the sections in and out of elbow in order to obtain a geometry topologically equivalent to a hexahedron (6 faces).To create both planes, menu New Entity → Basic → Plane: point + Vector so C + AC / D + BD).For the partition, menu Operations → Partition. If you want to make a mesh with tetrahedrons, this condition is not necessary. However, if you want to knit in hexahedron, it is essential for the algorithms of the mafers. Group creation : Then we will create the groups of faces where we want to put limit conditions: Base, Symetrie, Efond, Surfint and Surfext (Menu New Entity → Group → Create Group). The group will also be created with a thickness edge ( d1 ) and another group of board with a circumference edge ( L1 ) to allow a different refinement on these edges. The other mode of using the Geometry / Mesh module, consisting of producing, possibly modifying, and rereading a python file, which contains all the instructions necessary for the construction of geometry, is tested. This file is created by the File → Dump Study menu. This python file can be read by the File → Load Script menu. This allows in particular to modify the dimensions of geometry. For example, you can examine the contents of the file forma02a.datg, and read it in Salome-Meca. 3.3 Mesh Launch the Salome-Meca Platform Mesh module. The mesh is defined by the Mesh → Create Mesh menu. Select the geometry to be meshed, then the algorithm and the dimensional discretization hypothesis: - 3D Hexahedron(i,j,k). - 2D Quadrangle:Mapping. - 1D Wire Discretion with the basic hypothesis Number of Segments (15 segments per edge). - Then calculate the mesh(Menu Mesh → Compute). To allow a different refinement according to the edge, we will create submails by the menu Mesh → Create Sub-mesh: - A sub-mesh defining the number of segments in d1 thickness. For example, the basic number of segments hypothesis with 2 segments on d1 and the additional hypothesis "Propagation of 1D hypothesis on Opposite Edges". - A sub-mesh defining the number of segments on the L1 circumference. For example, 10 segments on L1 and the additional hypothesis "Propagation of 1D hypothesis on Opposite Edges". - Then calculate the mesh(Menu Mesh → Compute). Create the groups of meshes corresponding to the geometric groups (Menu Mesh→Create Groups from Geometry). Export mail in MED format. To obtain better accuracy, we will move the mesh from linear to quadratic, thanks to the tool "Modification -> Convert to/from quadratic". The most curious can compare the differences in results between the two types d Notes : With another fineness of mesh, it is possible to obtain substantially different results. In particular, to obtain a correct solution, it is desirable to use quadratic elements. 3.4 Creation and launch of the calculation case (via AsterStudy) Launch the AsterStudy module of the Salome-Meca platform. Then in the left column, click on the Case View tab, right click CurrentCase to add a new internship where you set commands of the calculation case. Note: add commands from the Commands→ Show All menu. The study requires a first transient thermal analysis calculation followed by a mechanical calculation. The main steps for creating and launching the calculation case are: - Read mesh in MED format: LIRE_MAILLAGE command. - Set the material: DEFI_MATERIAU( E,\nu ,\alpha ) command in ELAS, \lambda ,\rho \mathit{Cp} in THER). Thermical calculus: - Set the finished elements used: AFFE_MODELE command to assign the THERMIQUE phenomenon and 3D Modelling to TOUT. - Assign material to all: AFFE_MATERIAU command. - Assign boundary conditions thermal and loading: - The temperature transient is imposed on the internal surfaceSurf of the piping. This rise from 20°C to 70°C to \mathrm{10s} is defined with the DEFI_FONCTION command: set the data in VALE and NOM_PARA = INST. - This temperature transient is imposed with the AFFE_CHAR_THER_F command: option TEMP_IMPO, with Overfint as GROUP_MA, and the function defined as the temperature imposed TEMP) - The piping is considered to be calorifuged and no conditions are specified on the outside surface (which is a zero flow). - Set the calculation moments, 0 s, 5 s, 10 s: DEFI_LIST_REEL command. - Solve the linear thermal problem: THER_LINEAIRE control, by defining an initial uniform temperature state equal to 20°C (ETAT_INIT / VALE), and by affecting MODELE, CHAM_MATER (materials), EXCIT (loading), INCREMENT (score list). Thermomechanical calculus: - Set the finished elements used: AFFE_MODELE command to affect the MECANIQUE phenomenon and 3D Modelling. - Assign material: AFFE_MATERIAU control. The result of the thermal calculation will be applied to all as variable controlling the behavior of the mechanical material by EVOL in the AFFE_VARC option with reference temperature NOM_VARC = TEMP at 20°. - Mechanical boundary conditions Assigning and Loading: AFFE_CHAR_MECA Command: - The piping is clamped at both ends and has a symmetry plane: DDL_IMPO. - Ona an internal surface pressure of 15\mathit{MPa} : PRES_REP (check the direction of normal to the internal surface in AsterStudy). - Solve the static linear mechanical problem: MECA_STATIQUE control with the calculation of the above temperature field and the same list of moments as thermal calculation. - Calculate field: CALC_CHAMP command with drill. - for the calculation of the stress field by elements extrapolated to nodes: CONTRAINTE / SIEF_ELNO. - for the calculation of the equivalent stress field of Von Bets: CRITERES/ SIEQ_ELNO. - Print the maximum SIEQ_ELNO stress tensor values in Result format (RESULTAT) and print the temperature field, displacements, and stress fields in MED format: IMPR_RESU command. - To start the calculation case, in the left column, click on the History View tab. 3.5 Post-processing of the results 3.5.1 With Salomeet Results View the fields and the mesh deformed with a few clicks in the Results tab d的AsterStudy. To do so, you must use the menu Inspection → Check Compound of Blocks. Depending on the construction mode (the first process), it may be necessary to make a partition by planes of the inlet and outlet sections in order to obtain a geometry topologically equivalent to a hexahedron (6 faces). For geometry generated following the first process, several planes must be created to partition the piping: a plane Y=3, a plane X=0.6(Menu New Entity →Basic →Plane: point + Vector soC + AC /D + BD), and a curved surface from the ACDB path created(Wire_1): menu New Entity → Generation →Extrusion following the Z axis, then Operations / Transformation / Translation so that the curved surface completely cuts the piping. If you want to make a mesh with tetrahedrons, this condition is not necessary. However, if you want to knit in hexahedron, it is essential for the algorithms of the mafers. Group creation : Then we will create the groups of faces where we want to put limit conditions: Base (surface below to recess), Efond (pipe tip to apply dynamic force): New Entity Menu → Group → Create Group. The group will also be created with a thickness edge ( \mathit{d1} ) and another group of board with a circumference edge ( \mathit{L1} ) to allow a different refinement on these edges. For the post-processing it is convenient to create a group on an point where one can follow the evolutions. So the point B group located on the bottom section of the inner surface of the pipe will be created. 4.2 Mesh Launch the Salome-Meca Platform Mesh module. The mesh is defined by the Mesh → Create Mesh menu. Select the geometry to be meshed, then the algorithm and the dimensional discretization hypothesis: - 3D Hexahedron(i,j,k). - 2D Quadrangle: Mapping. - 1D Wire Discretion with the basic hypothesis Number of Segment (15 segments per edge. - Then calculate the mesh(Menu Mesh → Compute). To allow a different refinement according to the edge, we will create submails by the menu Mesh → Create Sub-mesh: - A sub-mesh defining the number of segments in d1 thickness. For example, the basic number of segments hypothesis with 2 segments on d1 and the additional hypothesis "Propagation of 1D hypothesis on Opposite Edges". - A sub-mesh defining the number of segments on the L1 circumference. For example, 20 segments on L1 and the additional hypothesis "Propagation of 1D hypothesis on Opposite Edges". - Then calculate the mesh(Menu Mesh → Compute). Create the corresponding mesh groups for the geometric groups (Menu Mesh→Create Groups from Geometry). Export mail in MED format. To obtain better accuracy, we will move the mesh from linear to quadratic, thanks to the tool "Modification -> Convert to/from quadratic". The most curious can compare the differences in results between the two types d Notes : - With another fineness of mesh, it is possible to obtain substantially different results. In particular, to obtain a correct solution, it is desirable to use quadratic elements. 4.3 Creation and launch of the calculation case The main steps of the calculation with AsterStudy will be: - Data preparation and modal analysis: - Read mesh by LIRE_MAILLAGE - Assign type d - Define and affect the material by DEFI_MATERIAU and AFFE_MATERIAU - Set boundary conditions by AFFE_CHAR_MECA: option DDL_IMPO to recess base. - Assemble the system mass and rigidity matrices by ASSEMBLAGE: ASSEMBLAGE(MODELE=… , CHAM_MATER= … , CHARGE=… , Numbering of unknowns of a system d-linear equations NUME_DDL=CO(' … '), MATR_ASSE=(_F(MATRICE=CO(' … '), OPTION='RIGI_MECA',), _F(MATRICE=CO(' … '), OPTION='MASS_MECA',),),); - Calculate the first 10 eigenmodes by CALC_MODES CALC_MODES(MATR_RIGI= … , MATR_MASS= … , OPTION='PLUS_PETITE', CALC_FREQ=_F(NMAX_FREQ= 10 ,),) - Extract and view eigenmodes by IMPR_RESU. Then the calculation will be started in the AsterStudy module. It is recommended to view the animations in the Results tab of the Asterstudy. Modes can also be viewed in Paravis by "deforming" them: - Right click the results file in the Case View → Data Files tab, and click Open In Paravis to load results by choosing the mode format instead of time, then click Apply to validate - Apply filter in Filters → Mechanics → Normal animation modes (real), and validate - Show the Animation View window (menu View → Windows → Animation View), and add an animation for the filter above by clicking + next to Normalmodesanimationreal - Select the mode to view (Array Selection mode) in the Properties window on the left and validate, then click the Play button (►) to view the mode movement - Transitional analysis For the transient analysis from the calculated modes, the "wizard" below will be used. The necessary commands will be added following the analysis. - Continue calculation in a new internship with the POURSUITE command - Definition of temporal discretization using DEFI_LIST_REEL: from 0s to 2.0s with an time step of 0.0001s. Construction of point force - Definition of unit load (value at 1) "force on B section" (AFFE_CHAR_MECA / FORCE_FACE). - Calculation of the elementary force vectors (CALC_VECT_ELEM / OPTION= - Assembly of the force vector (ASSE_VECTEUR). - Definition of the function evolved over time by FORMULE: VALE for \mathit{FY}(t)=10000000.\sin(2\pi \mathit{Freq1}.t) expression directed on Y axis and applied on B section, where \mathit{Freq}1=20\mathit{Hz} . First, the variables used in the formula must be reported. - Evolve the function by CALC_FONC_INTERP according to the defined moment list. With PROL_GAUCHE/DROITE = CONSTANT to set the curve out of the moment list. Transitional on modal basis - Projection of the problem assembled on the basis of eigenmodes - PROJ_BASE(BASE= … , - MATR_ASSE_GENE= ( - # For the mass matrix > _F( MATR_ASSE = … ), - # For the rigidity matrix - _F( MATR_ASSE = … ), - # For dynamic force - VECT_ASSE_GENE= _F( TYPE_VECT = ‘FORC’, - VECT_ASSE = … ), )). - Transitional calculation by modal recombination (DYNA_VIBRA) - DYNA_VIBRA(TYPE_CALCUL=’TRAN’, BASE_CALCUL=’GENE’, SCHEMA_TEMPS= _F(SCHEMA = 'DIFF_CENTRE'), - AMOR_MODAL = … , MATR_MASS = … , MATR_RIGI = … , EXCIT = … , INCREMENT = …, … ). - Recovery of Y moves to point B (RECU_FONCTION): RESU_GENE, GROUPE_NO, NOM_CHAM=DEPL, NOM_CMP=DY. - Printing of these functions in XMGRACE (IMPR_FONCTION): FORMAT, UNITE, COURBE, etc. - View moving fields: - REST_GENE_PHYS command: because the type of results generated (physical basis) directly by DYNA_VIBRA cannot print in MED format by IMPR_RESU, you must restore results in the physical base in general coordinate by giving LIST_INST, NOM_CHAM, RESU_GENE. Warning: the many time step drives the MED file very heavy, and you recommend redefining a list of moments, for example with a time step 0.01s. - IMPR_RESU command: print in MED format 4.4 Post-processing of the results The DY displacement curve can be directly visualized at point B as a function of time after IMPR_FONCTION in XMGRACE format. Import the transient results into the Results tab, and check the DY displacement on an point at the end of the hose (see Chapter 2.2.2). 5 Modelling C In the case of elements hull Modelling, the mesh consists of the discretization of the average surface of the piping. The geometry being symmetrical with the (A,X,Y) plane, one mesh cell is only half a surface. Boundary conditions and loading: clamped support at both ends of the piping, and pressure at the internal surface. A1 P 5.1 Geometry This geometry can be created by defining the A1 , P and \mathrm{A2} points , then the \mathit{Base} circle arc (Menu New Entity → Basic → Point / Arc).Then you just create the first straight pipe \mathrm{AC} from the \mathrm{Base} circle arc by the New Entity menu → Generation → Extrusion: Vector = OY, Height = 3. To create the elbow, you must recover the end of the \mathrm{AC} hose by applying the NewEntity→Explode menu, then create a vector parallel to the Z axis and passing the point O (\mathrm{0.6,}\mathrm{3.0,}0.) . Then generate the geometry of the elbow by the New Entity → Generation → Revolution menu. Finally, apply the same approach for the \mathrm{DB} hose (explode and then Extrusion). Create a "comound" (Menu New Entity → Build → Compound) by selecting the three parts of the pipe. We will then create the groups desmailles where we want to put limit conditions: Base, Symetrie, Efond et surface du pipe (Menu New Entity → Group → Create Group). We will also create the point \mathrm{A1} group. 5.2 Mesh Launch the Salome-Meca Platform Mesh module. The mesh is defined by the Mesh → Create Mesh menu. Select the geometry to be meshed, then the algorithm and the dimensional discretization hypothesis: - 2D Quadrangle: Mapping. - 1D Wire Discretion with Basic Numerial of Segment hypothesis(15 segments per edge. Then calculate the mesh(Menu Mesh → Compute). To allow a different refinement according to the edges, a sub-mesh (Menu Mesh → Create Sub-mesh) will be created defining the basic number of segment hypothesis on the circumference, for example 10 segments on \mathit{base} and the additional hypothesis "Propagation of 1D hypothesis on Opposite Edges". Then calculate the mesh(Menu Mesh → Compute). Create the corresponding mesh groups for the geometric groups (Menu Mesh→Create Groups from Geometry). Export mail in MED format. 5.3 Creation and launch of the calculation case (via AsterStudy) Launch the AsterStudy module of the Salome-Meca platform. Then in the left column, click on the Case View tab. The command file of the calculation case is defined. Note: add commands from the Commands→ Show All menu. The main steps in this mechanical calculation for the creation and initiation of the calculation case are: - Read mesh in MED format: LIRE_MAILLAGE command. - Set the finished elements used: AFFE_MODELE command. The piping will be modelled by elements hull (DKT). - Orient normals to elements: MODI_MAILLAGE / ORIE_NORM_COQUE command to steer all elements in the same way, with normal turning inside the pipe (given the pressure sign convention) to give a positive value to the pressure (use the surface group). - Set Material: DEFI_MATERIAU Command: E, NU, ALPHA - Assign material: AFFE_MATERIAU control. The mechanical characteristics are identical throughout the structure. - Assign the features of the elements hulls: AFFE_CARA_ELEM / COQUE command to define the thickness. - Assign mechanical boundary conditions and loads: AFFE_CHAR_MECA command: - There is a clamped support on the mesh-cell group \mathrm{Base} and \mathrm{Efond} , and symmetry conditions (normal displacement \mathrm{DZ} null and \mathrm{DRX} and \mathrm{DRY} null rotations) on the mesh-cell group \mathrm{Symetrie} : DDL_IMPO. - Internal pressure P : PRES_REP. The P pressure at the internal surface must be converted to the pressure at the average surface. - Solve elastic problem: MECA_STATIQUE control: CARA_ELEM, CHAM_MATER, EXCIT, MODELE. - Print displacements and constraints to MED format: IMPR_RESU command.. - To start the calculation case, in the left column, click on the History View tab. 6 Modelling D 6.1 Geometry Geometry can be created by defining A,C,D,B points, then the two \mathrm{AC} and \mathrm{DB} lines, and the \mathrm{CD} circle arch. This can be done in several ways: - By defining the coordinates of each point, including the point mid-arc \mathit{CD} (Menu New Entity → Basic → ...); - Simpler using the "Sketcher" tool (Menu New Entity → Basic→2D Sketch). After building the entire line, you have to define the groups under this "Wire": it will be enough for these practical works to create the groups A , B , \mathrm{AC} , \mathrm{CD} , and \mathrm{DB} ( Menu New Entity → Group → Create Group ). 6.2 Mesh Launch the Salome-Meca Platform Mesh module. The mesh is defined by the Mesh → Create Mesh menu. Select the geometry to be meshed, then the algorithm and the dimensional discretization hypothesis: 1D Wire Discretization with the 15 segment hypothesis per edge. 6.3 Creation and launch of the calculation case (via AsterStudy) Launch the AsterStudy module of the Salome-Meca platform. Then in the left column, click on the Case View tab. The command file of the calculation case is defined. Note: add commands from the Commands→ Show All menu. The study requires a first transient thermal analysis calculation followed by a mechanical calculation. The main steps for creating and launching the calculation case are: - Read mesh in MED format: LIRE_MAILLAGE command. - Set the finished elements used: AFFE_MODELE command. - Set the material: DEFI_MATERIAU command. - Assign Material: AFFE_MATERIAU command. - Assign the features of elements beams: AFFE_CARA_ELEM command. - Assign mechanical boundary conditions and loading: AFFE_CHAR_MECA/ Force DOF (DDL_IMPO) command. The point A is clamped. - Set the elastic problem matrices: HASSING/MASS_MECA and RIGI_MECA. - Calculate the first 5 eigenmodes: CALC_MODES command. - Print MED-specific modes: IMPR_RESU-command. The mesh and the modes will be printed. To start the calculation case, in the left column, click on the History View tab. Transient analysis: - Construction of the point force - Assign the load "force to point B ": Command AFFE_CHAR_MECA/ FORCE_NODALE. - Calculate the elementary force vectors: CALC_VECT_ELEM command. - Build a field at nodes by joining the force vector: ASSE_VECTEUR command. - Define the time evolution function: FORM CONTROL. - Modal base transitory 1. Projection of the problem assembled on the basis of the eigenmodes: PROJ_BASE command. 2. Calculate the transient by modal recombination: DYNA_VIBRA command. 3. Extract Y displacements in B : RECU_FONCTION command. 4. Print these functions in TABLEAU format: IMPR_FONCTION command.

v7.20.100 HSNA100 - Drying of a concrete enclosure wall v7.20.100 HSNA100 - Drying of a concrete enclosure wall Summary: This test case is designed to validate the calculation of concrete drying, developed in operator SECH_NON_LINE. The case studied corresponds to the simulated drying of the Flamanville enclosure. Geometric data and material characteristics are derived from Laurent Granger's thesis "Distorted behaviour of concrete in nuclear power plant enclosures" published by the Central Laboratory of Bridges and Chaussées (1996, pages 185 to 204). Drying is done by exchange with the outside, on the internal and external walls of the wall, in model axisymmetric \mathrm{2D} . It is carried out over a period of 54 years. The diffusion coefficient of the drying dependent on temperature, the analysis consists of the chaining of a thermal calculation and a drying calculation. A mechanical calculation of the removal of linear elasticity and Von Misès plasticity is then carried out with an isotropic hardening. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The enclosure is modelled on a height \text{Lint}=\text{Lext}=1m Outside radius of enclosure: \mathit{Rext}=23,5m Internal radius of the enclosure: \mathrm{Rint}=22,5m 1.2 Material properties For thermal calculation: Thermal diffusion coefficient: \lambda =80J/(\mathit{h.cm.}°C)=2.22W/(\mathit{m.}°C) Volumetric heat: \rho {C}_{p}=2.4{10}^{6}J/{m}^{3}/°C For the calculation of drying: In the drying equation: \frac{\mathrm{dC}}{\mathrm{dt}}-div\left[D(C,T)\mathrm{grad}C\right]=0 the D scattering coefficient shall be of the form recommended by Granger [bib1], [bib2] for modellings A to C: D(C,T)=A\exp(\mathrm{BC})\frac{T}{{T}_{0}}\exp\left[-\frac{{Q}_{S}}{R}(\frac{1}{T}-\frac{1}{{T}_{0}})\right] A=3.8{10}^{-13}{m}^{2}/s B=0.05 {T}_{0}=0°C \frac{{Q}_{S}}{R}=4700{K}^{-1} For modellings D and E using SECH_RFT law, the parameters are given in each modellings. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads For thermal calculation: Thermal exchange is imposed on the inside and outside walls of the wall of the enclosure (groups of mesh cells {l}_{int} and {l}_{\text{ext}} ). For the first five years, the outside temperature is 15°C on each wall: {T}_{int}={T}_{\text{ext}}=15°C From the fifth year onwards, the internal outside temperature is changed to 35°C : {T}_{int}=35°C et {T}_{\text{ext}}=15°C The internal wall is considered unventilated and its exchange coefficient is {h}_{int}=4\frac{W}{\mathit{m².}°C} . The outer wall is considered to be ventilated and its exchange coefficient is {h}_{\text{ext}}=6\frac{W}{\mathit{m².}°C} . (page 136 in [bib1]). In practice, the drying time scales are much higher than those of the thermal one can be considered to be almost immediate. The calculation is made in linear thermal. For the calculation of drying: Boundary conditions is expressed in terms of normal moisture flow on the inner and outer walls of the enclosure (groups of mesh cells {l}_{int} and {l}_{\text{ext}} ). FLUX_NL is used as the AFFE_CHAR_SECH_F operator's option. The normal flow is expressed in general terms, in a drying calculation, based on the initial concentration {C}_{0} , the concentration at 50% {C}_{50} humidity and the external concentration {C}_{\mathit{ext}} , in the form of: w=-D\left(C,T\right)\frac{\partial C}{\partial n}=\frac{0.5\beta }{{\left({C}_{0}-{C}_{50}\right)}^{2}}\left[C-\left(2{C}_{0}-{C}_{\mathit{ext}}\right)\right]\left(C-{C}_{\mathit{ext}}\right) with \beta ={\mathrm{3.41557.10}}^{–6}\frac{l}{\mathit{m².s}} (page 181 in [bib1]) The data used for the Flamanville compound are as follows: {C}_{0}=105.7l/{m}^{3} and {C}_{50}=57.5l/{m}^{3} (page 194 in [bib1]) On the inside side: | 0-5 years , | {C}_{\mathit{ext}}=69.1l/{m}^{3} Value for 60% humidity | | --- | --- | | 5 to 54 years, | {C}_{\mathit{ext}}=51.6l/{m}^{3} Value for 45% humidity | On the outside face: {C}_{\mathit{ext}}=69.1l/{m}^{3} The drying calculation is performed in nonlinear thermal, by linking with the linear thermal calculation. 1.4 Initial conditions Initial conditions consist of the initial temperature, which is taken at 15°C , and the initial water concentration, which is {C}_{0}=105.7l/{m}^{3} 2 reference solution This section only applies to modellings A and C using the Granger Law. For modellings D and E using SECH_RFT, the reference solutions are obtained by calculations using the SECH_NAPPE behavior to which an equivalent python function has been provided. 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The reference solution is made up of calculations made with a similar model by L. Granger, as part of his thesis [bib1]. The test case concerns the calculation made with the experimental data corresponding to the Flamanville enclosure. The implementation and results are described in it pages 185 to 204. Drying is done over 54 years, taking into account the change in boundary conditions in the fifth year. 2.2 Baseline Water concentration in the enclosure thickness after 5, 15, and 54 years. Figure 1: Concentration en eau suivant une coupe pour différents instants (page 204 [bib1]) 2.3 Uncertainty about the solution Only water concentrations calculated in the framework of Laurent Granger's thesis are available, without precise numerical data. Reference results are directly extracted from Figure 1. The uncertainty of the solution is more impotent in skin (where the points overlap) than at heart. 2.4 Bibliographical references 1. GRANGER: "Delayed behaviour of concrete in nuclear power plant enclosures" published by the Central Laboratory of Bridges and Chaussées (1996). 1. DEBRUYNE, B. CIREE: "Modelling of thermo-hydration, drying and concrete removal", Reference Manual Code_Aster , R7.01.12 (2001). 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics This is a model axisymmetric. Temp | 126.314 | 126.314 | 0 | Note : This Modelling includes only one non-regression test. It is the starting point of the TP, designed to improve Modelling (see Model B). On the evolution of temperature in the middle of the cylinder as a function of time, and the temperature distribution at t=\mathrm{4s} . It is evident (see red curves, with square marker on the following figure), that the temperature of 100°C is exceeded, which is not physical. This characterizes a non-compliance with the principle of maximum. 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics This Modelling is in line with the TP correction. It implements all the calculations proposed, commenting on the results obtained. Figure 5.1-a Figure 5.1-b 4.1.1 Thermal calculation To improve the results of Modelling A, thus to overcome these exceedances of the maximum temperature (see R3.06.07), several solutions are possible: - time step can be increased, which is not always compatible with the correct apprehension of the speed of the transient (as in the present case), - or refine the mesh, which is a good solution, but expensive in time calculation, - The diagonalization of thermal mass matrices, i.e. AXIS_DIAG Modelling, can be used. The curves marked with circles on the figures [Figure 5.1-a] and [Figure 5.1-b] above are obtained. The temperature is always below 100°C . It is the simplest solution. If an explicit diagram ( \mathit{THETA}=0 ) is used, there is a clear instability for large time step (cross-marking curve in Figure 5.1-a above). In conclusion, for thermal calculation, an \mathit{THETA} greater than or equal to 0.5 must be used to have a stable diagram whatever the time step. In addition, a time step small enough to grasp the transient must be used, but not too small to avoid oscillations. If they appear, either the mesh must be refined or the AXIS_DIAG Modelling (or PLAN_DIAG, or 3D_DIAG) used. 4.1.2 Free expansion thermoelastic calculation The calculation is performed with MECA_STATIQUE, using thermal expansion as the only load. With boundary conditions of the unbridled case: zero displacement following \mathit{Oy} along the \mathit{AB} side. For mechanical calculation, it will be enough to calculate at t=\mathrm{0s} , and t=\mathrm{11s} for example. The t=\mathrm{0s} -time stresses are zero, as the temperature field is uniform ( T=200°C ) and remains compatible. However, the resulting deformations are not zero since the reference temperature is equal to 200°C . At t=\mathrm{11s} , or any other positive mechanical moment, we see the so-called thermal compatibility stresses. Indeed, the temperature field is no longer uniform but varies according to r . This produces incompatible deformations, which therefore generate stresses, even for an unbridled cylinder. This situation occurs even for a linear temperature field relative to the radius. On the other hand (see exposed) a linear temperature field relative to the global coordinates does not produce a constraint for an unbridled structure. 4.1.3 Thermoelastic calculation with flange The calculation with MECA_STATIQUE of the bride case shows the contribution of the flange to the stresses ( \mathit{SIYY} in particular): at the moment t=\mathrm{0s} , the reference temperature being equal to 0°C , the uniform temperature field causes a uniform stress state \mathit{SIYY} of \mathrm{200MPa} , and at t=\mathrm{11s} , the stress state is different from the unbridled case. This Modelling is correct, but is limited to linear behaviors. 4.1.4 Thermoplastic calculation with flange We are looking to do the same calculation as before, but this time with STAT_NON_LINE, with COMPORTEMENT=_F(RELATION=的ELAS) so as not to complicate the problem (another behavior would lead to the same observations).The list of moments provided to STAT_NON_LINE is: t=\mathrm{0s} and t=\mathrm{11s} . Since the calculation is incremental, the 0-minute moment is considered as the initial moment. It is therefore not calculated, and at the next moment ( t=\mathrm{11s} ) the solution due to the increase in load (thermal here) between \mathrm{0s} and \mathrm{11s} is calculated. It is then found that the solution obtained (movements, stresses) is different from the calculation with MECA_STATIQUE. It is logical and consistent with the definition of the incremental calculation, but it is a trap for use. To be remembered: implicitly, STAT_NON_LINE in increment assumes that at the initial moment, the structure is non-stressed, not distorted. This implies that the temperature field must be uniform and equal to the reference temperature. This is not the case here: at t=\mathrm{0s} , \mathit{TREF}=0°C , and T=200°C . By not calculating this thermal expansion, we assume here that at t=\mathrm{0s} , there is no deformation, and no stress. 4.1.5 Thermoplastic calculation with flange and addition of initial conditions The list of moments is changed: for example, a preliminary moment is added t=–\mathrm{1s} . At this moment, a uniform temperature field is defined, equal to the reference temperature. For this purpose, CREA_CHAMP commands are used, then CREA_RESU to enrich the thermal results data structure with this uniform field. The mechanical calculation is then performed, providing the list of moments: t=–\mathrm{1s} , t=\mathrm{0s} , and t=\mathrm{11s} It is then found that the t=\mathrm{0s} moment is well calculated, and that the stresses are identical to the case calculated with MECA_STATIQUE. 4.2 Mesh characteristics Same mesh as for Modelling A. 4.3 Quantities tested and values Modelling AXIS_DIAG | Temperature | moment | Identification | Reference | Aster | % difference | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | maximum | 4 | Max. v7.20.102 HSNA102 - Validation of drying laws on a concrete cylindrical test piece v7.20.102 HSNA102 - Validation of drying laws on a concrete cylindrical test piece Summary: This test case is designed to validate the calculation of concrete drying, developed in the SECH_NON_LINE operator. Here we test the various available diffusion laws, namely SECH_GRANGER, SECH_MENSI, SECH_BAZANT, SECH_NAPPE and SECH_RFT. However, the possible dependence on the temperature of the models is not tested. This is a test case axisymmetric where the water concentration is applied directly to the outer wall. The results are compared with a numerical resolution of the equations using Scilab except for SECH_RFT whose reference solution is given by a calculation with SECH_NAPPE to which an equivalent python formula is provided. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry A cylindrical test piece of diameter 160\mathit{mm} is modelled. 1.2 Material properties Each model allows validation of a D diffusion coefficient, namely: - Modelling A and E: Mensi law D(C) = A \exp(BC) - Modelling B: Granger's law D(C,T)=A\exp(\mathrm{BC})\frac{T}{{T}_{0}}\exp\left[-\frac{{Q}_{S}}{R}(\frac{1}{T}-\frac{1}{{T}_{0}})\right] - Modelling C: definition of D as a tablecloth - Modelling D: Bazant law - Modelling F: SECH_RFT law The expression of D\left(C,T\right) for this law is quite complex, it is presented in detail in R7.01.12. The coefficients used are those recommended by Granger in his thesis [bib1]: | SECH_MENSI: | A=0.74{10}^{-13}{m}^{2}/s B=0.05 | | --- | --- | | SECH_GRANGER | A=0.74{10}^{-13}{m}^{2}/s B=0.05 {T}_{0}=293°K {Q}_{s}/R=4700{K}^{-1} | | SECH_NAPPE | The law of Mensi is in the form of a tablecloth | | SECH_BAZANT | \mathit{D1}=3.0{10}^{-10}{m}^{2}/s \alpha =0.04 n=6 with {C}_{0}=128.8l/{m}^{3} and {C}_{\mathit{eq}}=58.8l/{m}^{3} | | SECH_RFT | Parameters are given in model F. | 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The drying calculation is carried out over a period of 5 years - the temperature remains uniform and is 20°C - apply to \mathit{FE} : {C}_{\mathit{eq}}=58.8l/{m}^{3} 1.4 Initial conditions The initial conditions are the initial temperature, which is taken at 20°C , and the initial water concentration, which is 128.8l/m^3 . 2 reference solution 2.1 Calculation method used for reference solution The 2 reference solutions are obtained by solving the finite difference drying equation using Scilab. v7.20.105 HSNA105 - Expansion of an infinite hollow cylinder with consideration of thermal dissipations due to mechanical deformations v7.20.105 HSNA105 - Expansion of an infinite hollow cylinder with consideration of thermal dissipations due to mechanical deformations Summary: The objective of this test is to validate the setting up of a thermomechanical coupling with consideration of thermal dissipations due to mechanical deformations as a source of heat in the thermal equation. The coupling is carried out by the classical method of the so-called isothermal staggered schematic literature. This test case has two modellingss that correspond to two distinct physical transients described in the literature [2]: - Modelling A: Thermoelastic case where the expansion of a cylinder causes its cooling; - Model B: Thermoelastoplastic case where the plastic dissipation effect compensates for the previous effect and causes the overall warming of the cylinder. The results obtained are in good correlation. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry An infinite hollow cylinder is considered. Figure 1: Géométrie du cylindre creux Model A: Geometrical properties are: - {R}_{i}=10\mathit{mm} internal radius - External radius {R}_{e}=20\mathit{mm} Model B: Geometrical properties are: - {R}_{i}=100\mathit{mm} internal radius - External radius {R}_{e}=200\mathit{mm} 1.2 Material properties The materials used in the calculations use the constitutive law VMIS_JOHN_COOK. Its nutring function is written as follows [1]: R(p,\dot{p},T)=(A+B{p}^{n})(1+C\ln(\frac{\dot{p}}{\dot{{p}_{0}}}))(1-(\frac{T-{T}_{\mathit{room}}}{{T}_{\mathit{melt}}-{T}_{\mathit{room}}})) We will not use the terms related to the dependence on temperature and the plastic deformation rate. We will then work with: R(p)=A+B{p}^{n} Model A: An elastic constitutive law is modelled. The following mechanical and thermal parameters are used: - Young's modulus E=206900\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio \nu =0.29 - Elasticity limit A=5{.10}^{100}\mathit{Pa} - Post-elastic pen B=2{.10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} - Post-elastic power n=1 - Density \rho =7800\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} - \alpha =1,5{.10}^{-5}{K}^{-1} expansion coefficient - \lambda =45W/(\mathit{m.K}) conductivity - Heat capacity {C}_{p}=460J/(\mathit{kg.K}) - Reference temperature {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=293K Model B: A constitutive law elastoplastic is modelled equivalent to an VMIS_ISOT_LINE law. The following mechanical and thermal parameters are used: - Young's modulus E=70000\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio \nu =0.3 - Temperature-dependent yield limit A(T)=A({T}_{\mathit{ref}})(1-w(T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}})) - Elasticity limit at reference temperature A({T}_{\mathit{ref}})=70\mathit{MPa} - Linear softening coefficient w=3{.10}^{-4}{K}^{-1} - Post-elastic pen B=210\mathit{MPa} - Post-elastic power n=1 - Density \rho =2700\mathit{kg}/{m}^{3} - \alpha =2,38{.10}^{-5}{K}^{-1} expansion coefficient - \lambda =150W/(\mathit{m.K}) conductivity - Heat capacity {C}_{p}=900J/(\mathit{kg.K}) - Reference temperature {T}_{\mathit{ref}}=293K 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads Model A: 20\mathit{mm} radial displacement is imposed on the inner side of the cylinder at the speed of \mathrm{1mm}/s . The temperature of the outer face is imposed on {T}_{\mathit{ref}} . The other sides of the cylinder are considered thermally isolated. The behaviour is thermoelastic and the expansion of a cylinder causes its cooling. Model B: The cylinder surface is considered thermally insulated. The displacement of the cylinder's inner face is 130\mathit{mm} applied in 1,3s . The behaviour is thermoelastoplastic and the plastic dissipation effect compensates for the previous thermo-elastic cooling effect to cause the cylinder to warm up overall. 1.4 Initial conditions The cylinder temperature is equal to {T}_{\mathit{ref}} . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference solutions for each of the two problems are derived from the curves presented in the thesis of L. ADAM. These results were obtained using the METAFOR software developed by the University of Liège. 2.2 Bibliographical references 1. U4.43.01 Document, DEFI_MATERIAU Operator, Code_Aster User Manual. 1. ADAM, "Modulating the thermo-elasto-viscoplastic behaviour of metals subjected to large deformations. Application to superplastic forming." PhD Thesis, University of Liège, 2003. 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics AXIS_DIAG Modelling for thermal and AXIS_SI Modelling for mechanics are used. The test introducing large deformations, GDEF_LOG formalism is used. 3.2 Characteristics of meshes Two meshes are used (one for each phenomenon). For thermal purposes, a linear mesh elements is used: - 100 elements type QUAD4 . - 121 nodes . For mechanics, a mesh of elements is used with quadratic interpolation: - 100 elements type QUAD8 . - 341 nodes . 3.3 Tested quantities and results The temperature on the inner cylinder wall is tested at the moment t=\mathrm{6s} , which corresponds to the cylinder cooling peak. | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Internal wall temperature | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | 261,5 | 0,2% | We traced the temperature evolution of the cylinder's inner face during the calculation and compared it with the result of L. ADAM. We can see that we find the same results. 3.4 Remarks The results obtained with the coupling introduced in Code_Aster give good results. 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics AXIS_DIAG Modelling for thermal and AXIS_SI Modelling for mechanics are used. The test introducing large deformations, GDEF_LOG formalism is used. 4.2 Characteristics of meshes Two meshes are used (one for each phenomenon). For thermal purposes, a linear mesh elements is used: - 22 elements type QUAD4 . - 22 nodes . For mechanics, a mesh of elements is used with quadratic interpolation: - 22 elements type QUAD8 . - 53 nodes . 4.3 Tested quantities and results The temperature is tested on the inner wall of the cylinder at the end of the transient. | Identification | Reference type | Reference value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Internal wall temperature | 'SOURCE_EXTERNE' | 341,44 | 0,1% | We have the temperature in the cylinder thickness at the end of the calculation and compared it with the result of L. ADAM. We can see that we find the same results. 4.4 Remarks The results obtained with the coupling introduced in Code_Aster give good results. 5 Summary of the results The thermomechanical coupling method implanted in the test cases of Code_Aster allows to find results consistent with those of the literature. The approach developed in these tests is sufficiently generic to be applied to any situation.

v7.20.106 HSNA106 – Model META_LEMA_ANI: full single-trail cylinder with variable temperature v7.20.106 HSNA106 – Model META_LEMA_ANI: full single-trail cylinder with variable temperature Summary: This quasi-static thermomechanical test consists of uniformly heating a cylindrical bar ( \mathrm{2D} axisymmetric) and then tensile. The bar is represented by a element axisymmetric quadrangular QUAD4. It is modelled in two different but equivalent ways: either with the META_LEMA_ANI model that is "degenerated" into a Norton law by judiciously choosing coefficients (modelization A), or with a Norton law itself (modelization B). The META_LEMA_ANI model has two different thermal expansion coefficients for the cold a phase and the hot b phase. In the most general case, the expansion is calculated by a law of the mixtures. Here, one takes place in the case of 100% phase b and the calculation of the thermal expansion is tested. The thermomechanical load is done on the required displacement and by imposing a rising temperature. The same response must then be obtained for both modellings A and B. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 1.2 Material properties The material obeys a viscoplastic constitutive law of Norton (special case of Lemaître law, where the UN_SUR_M parameter is null, confir R5.03.08), with the parameters: - Young's modulus: E=80000\mathit{MPa} - Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.35 - n=4.39 - K=253.5497\mathit{MPa}.{s}^{-1} - \alpha =0.00004 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The bar, of initial length , blocked in the direction on the face [1,2] is subjected to a uniform temperature and a mechanical displacement of traction u on the [3,4] face. v7.22.100 HSNV100 - Thermoplasticity in single traction v7.22.100 HSNV100 - Thermoplasticity in single traction Summary: This test treats Von Mises thermoplasticity with isotropic hardening on a three-dimensional ( A axisymmetric Modelling) and two-dimensional ( B Modelling in flat stresses). The value of the test is the dependence of the yield limit on temperature. It also allows testing the thermo-elasticity orthotropy as it applies to an isotropic material and then to an isotropic material declared orthotropic. The calculation of the strain energy is also tested. Two modellings ( C with element TUYAU, D with element TUYAU_6M) are added to test thermoplasticity in these elements. E Modelling is used to test the correct consideration of the variation of the coefficients of the VMIS_CINE_LINE behavior with temperature (axisymmetric). F Modelling is used to test the calculation of the thermoelastic l-strain energy in beams (POU_D_T Modelling). G Modelling allows testing the same features as modellings A and B , but with 3D Modelling. The modellings H and I allow the testing of an initial field loading of anelastic deformations in 3D Modelling and flat stress. This is equivalent to thermal deformation. J Modelling is a product of G Modelling, and allows to validate SIMU_POINT_MAT's functions in thermoplasticity. K Modelling is a result of A Modelling, and allows the AFFE_CHAR_TEMP_R option of AXIS_INCO_UPG Modelling to be validated with DEFORMATION='PETIT'. The same applies to modellings L and M but to 3D_INCO_UPG with DEFORMATION='PETIT'. N Modelling is the result of A Modelling, and allows to validate AFFE_CHAR_TEMP_R option of AXIS_INCO_UP Modelling. The same applies to modellings O and P but to 3D_INCO_UP. Q Modelling is a result of A Modelling, and allows the AFFE_CHAR_TEMP_R option of AXIS_INCO_UPG Modelling to be validated with DEFORMATION='SIMO_MIEHE'. The same applies to modellings R and S but to 3D_INCO_UPG with DEFORMATION='SIMO_MIEHE'. T Modelling is a result of A Modelling, and allows the AFFE_CHAR_TEMP_R option of AXIS_INCO_UPG Modelling to be validated with DEFORMATION='GDEF_LOG'. The same applies to modellings U and V but to 3D_INCO_UPG with DEFORMATION='GDEF_LOG'. W Modelling is the result of A Modelling, and allows to validate AFFE_CHAR_TEMP_R option of AXIS_INCO_UP Modelling. The same applies to modellings X and Y but to 3D_INCO_UP. Z Modelling is based on A Modelling, and allows the validation of MPI code coupling. v7.22.132 HSNV132 - X-FEM thermal elasticity v7.22.132 HSNV132 - X-FEM thermal elasticity Summary The purpose of this test is to validate the consideration of a thermal load for a cracking calculation by the X-FEM [bib1] method on an academic case \mathrm{2D}/\mathrm{3D} . This test involves a square plate with a straight crack opening, clamped on the lower edge, and subjected to a horizontal temperature gradient. This load opens the crack. The displacement for the node end at the top right, for FEM and X-FEM, is compared. This test includes a call to THER_LINEAIRE, then MECA_STATIQUE. Four modellings are considered: - A Modelling: \text{FEM}\mathrm{2D} (as reference), - B Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{2D} , crack in the middle of elements, - C Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{3D} (the following z moves are blocked), cracking in the middle of elements, - D Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{3D} , real \mathrm{3d} Modelling, without putting \mathit{DZ}=0 , to validate the G calculation to \mathrm{3D} . - E Modelling: \text{X-FEM}\mathrm{3D} , true \mathrm{3d} Modelling, without putting \mathrm{DZ}=0 , to validate G calculation to \mathrm{3D} . Similar to D Modelling except that the top and bottom surfaces were clamped to induce significant stresses. There is a difference less than \text{1\%} for moving, and a difference of \text{3,5\%} on {K}_{I} and \text{1,4 \%} on {K}_{\mathit{II}} . 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry The \mathrm{2d} structure is a unit square ( \mathrm{LX}=1m , \mathrm{LY}=1m ), with a straight crack opening to the right, located at mid-height. [ Figure 1.1-1 ]. The left line is called the x=0 line , the right line is called the x=\mathrm{LX} line and the bottom line is called the y=0 line . Figure 1.1-1 : geometry of cracked square plate 1.2 Material properties Young's modulus: E=205000\mathit{MPa} Poisson's ratio: \nu =0.3 Thermal expansion coefficient: \alpha =1,282{10}^{-5} Thermal conductivity: \lambda =1{\mathit{W.m}}^{\text{-1}}.{K}^{\text{-1}} Volumetric heating capacity: \rho {C}_{p}=0\mathit{J.m}-{\mathrm{3.K}}^{-1} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads 1.3.1 For the thermal part The thermal loading consists of applying an imposed temperature T=20°C to the nodes of the left line and an imposed temperature T=220°C to the nodes of the right line. The temperature gradient is uniform and opens the crack in mixed mode. 1.3.2 For the mechanical part The nodes of the lower line is clamped. 1.4 Bibliography 1. GENIAUT S., MASSIN P.: eXtended Finish Element Method, Reference Manual of Code_Code_Aster , R7.02.12 2. GALENNE E.,PROIX J.M.: Calculation of stress intensity factors, R7.02.08. 2 Modelization A: dimension 2 mesh crack In this Modelling, the \mathrm{2D} structure is considered. The classic elements method is used. v7.22.133 HSNV133 - Thermoplastic Traction in Large Deformities VMIS_ISOT_PUIS v7.22.133 HSNV133 - Thermoplastic Traction in Large Deformities VMIS_ISOT_PUIS Summary: This quasi-static thermomechanical test consists of uniformly heating a rectangular section bar (strain and homogeneous deformation states) and then tensile. Similarly, in the HSNV121 V7.22.121 test, the kinematics of the large elasto-plasticity deformations are validated for a Von-type behavioral relationship. Isotropic hardening bets defined either by a given traction curve point by point (VMIS_ISOT_TRAC); or by a power law (VMIS_ISOT_PUIS). The bar is modeled by a volume element. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry 1.2 Material properties The material obeys a constitutive law in large plastic deformations with isotropic hardening defined by a tensile curve (point by point or power law). The tensile curve is given in the logarithmic deformation plane - rational stress. | \sigma =\frac{F}{S}=\frac{F}{{S}_{o}}\cdot \frac{l}{{l}_{o}} | R(p)={\sigma}_{y}+{\sigma}_{y}{(\frac{E}{a{\sigma}_{y}}p)}^{1/n} | | --- | --- | | | \begin{array}{cc}\nu & =0.3\\ \alpha & ={10}^{-4}{K}^{-1}\\ {\sigma}_{y}& =1000\mathrm{MPa}\\ E& =200000\mathrm{MPa}\\ n& =7\\ a& =1\end{array} | {l}_{o} and l are, respectively, the initial and current length of the useful part of the test piece. {S}_{o} and S are the initial and current surfaces, respectively. Between the 20°C and 120°C temperatures, the characteristics are interpolated linearly. 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads The bar, of initial length {l}_{o} , blocked in the direction \mathrm{Ox} on the face [1,2] is subjected to a uniform temperature T and a mechanical displacement of traction {u}^{\text{meca}} on the face [3, 4]. The loading sequences are as follows: y x Reference temperature: {T}_{\text{réf}}=20°C . Note: Mechanical displacement is measured from the thermal loading deformed configuration ( t=\mathrm{1s} ). To achieve total displacement, the thermal displacement obtained over time must be added t=\mathrm{1s} . 2 reference solution 2.1 Baseline Reference results will be taken from the displacements, the stress of Cauchy \sigma and the cumulative plastic deformation p obtained with the VMIS_ISOT_TRAC behavior (also valid with DEFORMATION=的SIMO_MIEHE and 的GDEF_LOG). v7.22.137 FORMA41 - Practical work of the Civil Engineering training: taking into account withdrawals in the study of a 3 point bending beam v7.22.137 FORMA41 - Practical work of the Civil Engineering training: taking into account withdrawals in the study of a 3 point bending beam Summary: This \mathrm{3D} test illustrates the questions of modelling the removals in concrete on a simple case basis, and highlights the effect of drying and temperature on stress distribution. It is a reinforced concrete beam subjected to a 3-point bending to which is added thermal and drying stress. The objective of the test is to show the possibilities of Modelling withdrawals by thermal (THER_NON_LINE) and drying (SECH_NON_LINE) and mechanical MECA_STATIQUE. Model A is the calculation of the elasticity bending. It is used as a comparison for the other modellings. Model B is the calculation with regard to desiccation removal, endogenous withdrawal and thermal expansion. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry It is an armed 5m beam of a length of which only one quarter is modelled thanks to symmetries. Dimensions are given in millimetres. | | | --- | 1.2 Initial condition and thermal loading The initial temperature is uniform to 20°C . Concrete is subjected to thermo-hydration. The temperature is imposed on 20°C on the \mathrm{EFGH} face, which is HAUT in the mesh. The temperature is constant at 20°C for up to 10 days and then varies linearly from 20\mathrm{°}\mathrm{C} to 40\mathrm{°}\mathrm{C} for 10 days to 30 days, then is constant at 40\mathrm{°}\mathrm{C} on the \mathrm{ABCD} face, rated BAS in the mesh. 1.3 Initial condition and drying loads The initial water concentration is uniform at 120l/{m}^{3} . The water concentration is imposed on 50l/{m}^{3} on the \mathrm{EFGH} face, which is HAUT. The water concentration is imposed on 70l/{m}^{3} on the \mathrm{ABCD} side. 1.4 Boundary conditions and mechanical loadings Conditions of symmetry The plate is blocked following \mathrm{Ox} on the \mathrm{BCGF} side noted SYME_X and following \mathrm{Oz} on the \mathrm{ABFE} side noted SYME_Z . Limited The plate is blocked following \mathrm{Oy} on the \mathrm{HE} side rated APPUI. Charge It is subjected to \frac{F}{4}=3840N force following \mathrm{Oy} distributed on the \mathrm{BC} side, which is equivalent to a total F=15360N force on the entire beam. The force is applied at the final moment of each calculation (in Modelling A to time step performed only and in Modelling B to t=100\mathit{jours} ). 1.5 Thermal properties of materials The characteristics of the concrete are: - \rho {C}_{p}=2.4{e}^{6}J/{m}^{3}/°C thermal capacity; - \lambda =1W/m/°C conductivity; and the following characteristics relating to moisturizing behaviour: - heat per degree of hydration: {Q}_{0}={1.14e}^{8}J/{m}^{3} - affinity function of hydration (polynomial evaluation of known function by point) and temperature (naple): A(\xi ,T)=(50.12{\xi}^{6}-190.76{\xi}^{5}+258.38{\xi}^{4}-123.71{\xi}^{3}-11.82{\xi}^{2}+15.37\xi +2.43)\exp(\frac{-{\mathit{QSR}}_{K}}{(273.15+T)}) - with constant d-Arrhenius: {\mathit{QSR}}_{K}=4000K . Note: The constant d-Arrhenius is always expressed in Kelvin degree. Temperatures are expressed in °C . 1.6 Properties of drying materials The SECH_GRANGER scattering law is used: D(C,T)=A\cdot \exp(\mathit{BC})\frac{T}{{T}_{0}}\exp\left[-\frac{{Q}_{s}}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T}-\frac{1}{{T}_{0}}\right)\right] - A=3.3e-13{m}^{2}/s ; - B=0.05 ; - \mathit{QSR}=4000K - {T}_{0}=293°K=20°C 1.7 Mechanical properties of materials The behavior is elastic. The characteristics of steels are: - Young's modulus {E}_{a}=200000\mathrm{MPa} ; - Poisson's ratio \nu =0.3 ; The characteristics of the concrete are: - Young's modulus {E}_{b}=32000\mathit{MPa} for Modelling A. In Modelling B, it varies linearly according to the temperature from {E}_{b}=30000\mathrm{MPa} for T=0°C to {E}_{b}=40000\mathit{MPa} for T=100°C ; - Poisson's ratio \nu =0.2 ; - \alpha =1.2e-6 thermal dilation at the reference temperature of {T}_{\mathrm{ref}}=20°C - {K}_{\mathit{des}}=8e-6 Desiccation Removal Coefficient - Endogenous withdrawal coefficient {B}_{\mathit{endo}}=9e-5 2 reference solution 2.1 Elastic solution without withdrawal The following assumptions are made: - sections of the beams remain flat - there is perfect adhesion between concrete and steel - the behavior is linear elastic The position of the {y}_{n} beam neutral axis can therefore be evaluated by the position of the steels. The following equation must be solved: {y}_{n}\left(2\frac{n}{b}\left({A}_{s}+{A}_{S}'\right)+2h\right)-\left(2\frac{n}{b}\left({A}_{S}'c'+{A}_{s}\left(h-c\right)\right)+{h}^{2}\right)=0 With: {A}_{s} and {A}_{s}' : steel surfaces, tensioned and compressed respectively in section c' and c' : concrete coating below the tensioned steels and above the compressed steels, respectively b and h : width and height of beam section respectively n=\frac{{E}_{a}}{{E}_{b}} : ratio between concrete and steel Young's modulus The {\sigma}_{\mathit{xxC}} longitudinal compression stress as a function of the bending moment and the neutral axis position. {\sigma}_{\mathit{xxC}}=\frac{\mathit{Mf}}{\left({A}_{s}n\frac{{\left(h-c-{y}_{n}\right)}^{2}}{{y}_{n}}+{A}_{s}'n\frac{{\left({y}_{n}-c'\right)}^{2}}{{y}_{n}}+\frac{{\mathit{by}}_{n}^{2}}{3}+b\frac{{\left(h-{y}_{n}\right)}^{3}}{{y}_{n}}\right)} \mathit{Mf}(x)=\frac{\mathit{Fx}}{2} The digital application gives: {y}_{n}=0.2674 And in x=2.5m and y=0,25m , the maximum compression stress is: {\sigma}_{\mathit{xxC}}=-2.05\mathit{MPa} Using the linearity of the stresses in the section, the maximum tensile stress is {\sigma}_{\mathit{xxT}}=1.78\mathit{MPa} 2.2 Solution with withdrawals Deformities due to desiccation removal and thermal expansion can easily be assessed where water concentration and temperature values are known. For endogenous withdrawal, the degree of hydration is estimated from the interpolation used to define hydration parameters. - en G à t>30j : T=20°C so {\epsilon}_{\mathit{th}}=\alpha (T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}})=0 C=50l/{m}^{3} so {\epsilon}_{\mathit{sec}}=-{K}_{\mathit{des}}({C}_{0}-C)=-5.6e-4 \xi =0,95 so {\epsilon}_{\mathit{endo}}=-{B}_{\mathit{endo}}\xi =-\mathrm{8,55e-5} - en G à t>30j : T=40°C so {\epsilon}_{\mathit{th}}=\alpha (T-{T}_{\mathit{ref}})=2.4e-5 C=70l/{m}^{3} so {\epsilon}_{\mathit{sec}}=-{K}_{\mathit{des}}({C}_{0}-C)=-4e-4 \xi =0,95 so {\epsilon}_{\mathit{endo}}=-{B}_{\mathit{endo}}\xi =-\mathrm{8,55e-5} G stresses are not calculated analytically but are calculated on a very fine mesh (32000 HEXA20 and 155369 nodes). 3 Modelling A 3.1 Modelling characteristics Elastic calculation on a volume model (3D). The load is defined in § 1.4 . 3.2 Mesh characteristics A mesh with 4000 HEXA20 and 22965 nodes is used. 3.3 Tested quantities and results The longitudinal stress value is tested: | Component | Reference type | Value | Tolerance | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SIGM_NOEU– \mathrm{SIXX} en G | ANALYTIQUE | 1.78\mathrm{MPa} | 2,00% | | SIGM_NOEU– \mathrm{SIXX} en G | NON_REGRESSION | 1.75388\mathrm{MPa} | 0,1% | 4 Modelling B 4.1 Modelling characteristics Three successive calculations are made: - Thermal calculation as described in 1.2 in 3D_DIAG modelling; - Drying calculation as described in 1.3 in 3D_SECH_DIAG Modelling; - Elastic calculation as in Modelling A. 4.2 Mesh characteristics The same mesh Modelling as A, which includes 4000 HEXA20 and 22965 nodes for elastic calculation, is used for thermal and drying calculations, but is linear. This TP allows: - implement thermal and drying calculation in Code_Aster: management of loading, materials, behaviour and parameters of THER_NON_LINE and SECH_NON_LINE; - understand and implement the concept of command variable; - define parameters of an constitutive law that depend on command variables; 5.2 Geometry and mesh Geometry and mesh (quadratic) are provided. v7.23.102 HSNS102 - Reinforced concrete plate with thermal loading v7.23.102 HSNS102 - Reinforced concrete plate with thermal loading Summary: The main purpose of this test is to verify the Modelling of elements reinforced concrete under thermal loading using three techniques: - Modelling A: Model shell: DKT + GRILLE_EXCENTREE - Modelling B: Solid model: Volumic + GRILLE_MEMBRANE - Modelling C: Solid model: Volumic + MEMBRANE The objective is to check the mechanical response compared with an analytically obtained reference solution. In addition, it tests MATRICE=ELASTIQUE functionality for STAT_NON_LINE GRILLE_MEMBRANE GRILLE_MEMBRANE EPVC_ELGA, EPVC_ELGA, EPME_ELGA and EPSP_ELGA in B Modelling. In Modelling C, the calculation of EFGE_ELGA and EFGE_ELNO options is also tested on MEMBRANE elements (linear and nonlinear). 1 Reference problem 1.1 Geometry Z A Y C B X | Square plate: | Weapons: | | --- | --- | | Length: l=1.0m | Section : {S}_{a}=0.01{m}^{2} | | Thickness: \mathit{ep}=0.2m | Excentering: e=-0.01m | 1.2 Material properties Béton: Young's modulus, E=3{10}^{10}\mathit{Pa} Poisson's ratio, \nu =0.0 Thermal expansion coefficient, \alpha ={10}^{-5}{K}^{-1} Storage: Young's modulus, E=2{10}^{11}\mathit{Pa} Poisson's ratio, \nu =0.0 Thermal expansion coefficient, \alpha ={10}^{-5}{K}^{-1} 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads On the A side, the X and Z moves are blocked and the rotation around Y is blocked: > {U}_{x}=0.0;{U}_{z}=0.0;{R}_{y}=0.0 On the B edge the displacement is blocked according to Y : > {U}_{Y}=0.0 The initial temperature is 20°C for steel and concrete. We increase the temperature of the steel to reach 120°C . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The total deformations in steel and concrete are: > {\epsilon}_{a}^{t}={\epsilon}_{a}^{m}+{\epsilon}_{a}^{\mathit{th}} and {\epsilon}_{b}^{t}={\epsilon}_{b}^{m} with {\epsilon}_{a}^{\mathit{th}}=\alpha \Delta T \epsilon is the deformation of the average plane of the plate and \chi the curvature of the plate, the two unknowns to be found. By respecting the kinematics (the sections remain flat), the steel being perfectly bound to the concrete, we have: > {\epsilon}_{a}^{t}=\epsilon -e\chi et {\epsilon}_{b}^{t}=\epsilon -y\chi The normal effort imposed on the plate is zero: > N={N}_{a}+{N}_{b}={E}_{a}{S}_{a}{\epsilon}_{a}^{m}+{E}_{b}\int{\epsilon}_{b}^{m}\text{}={E}_{a}{S}_{a}(\epsilon -e\chi -{\epsilon}_{a}^{\mathit{th}})+{E}_{b}{S}_{b}\epsilon =0 Similarly, the bending moment imposed on the plate is zero: > M={M}_{a}+{M}_{b}=e{E}_{a}{S}_{a}{\epsilon}_{a}^{m}+{E}_{b}\inty{\epsilon}_{b}^{m}\text{}={E}_{a}{S}_{a}(e\epsilon -{e}^{2}\chi -e{\epsilon}_{a}^{\mathrm{th}})+{E}_{b}{I}_{b}\chi =0 Two equations are obtained to determine the two unknowns: > \begin{array}{c}({E}_{a}{S}_{a}+{E}_{b}{S}_{b})\epsilon -{E}_{a}{S}_{a}e\chi ={E}_{a}{S}_{a}{\epsilon}_{a}^{\mathit{th}}\\ {E}_{a}{S}_{a}e\epsilon +({E}_{b}{I}_{b}-{E}_{a}{S}_{a}{e}^{2})\chi ={E}_{a}{S}_{a}e{\epsilon}_{a}^{\mathit{th}}\end{array} We get: > \epsilon =\frac{\alpha \Delta T}{A} et \chi =\frac{-\alpha \Delta T}{B} with: > A=1+\frac{{E}_{b}{S}_{b}}{{E}_{a}{S}_{a}}+\frac{{S}_{b}{e}^{2}}{{I}_{b}} et B=e+(\frac{1}{{E}_{a}{S}_{a}}+\frac{1}{{E}_{b}{S}_{b}})+\frac{{E}_{b}{I}_{b}}{e} From these values one can calculate: - elongation of the plate: \Delta L=\epsilon L - the rotation of the plate: {R}_{y}=\chi L - deflection at the end of the plate: f=-\chi \frac{{L}^{2}}{2} or in the middle of the plate f=-\chi \frac{{L}^{2}}{8} - It uses the "GonfElas" model that was originally developed by Dashnor Hoxha. It is a nonlinear elastic model dependent on suction and describing the swelling behaviour of certain types of clay. This model is written according to the following couple of variables: net stress and suction (suction is the capillary pressure). It can be considered as the elastic part of the Barcelona model. v7.31.109 WTNV109 - Water and mechanical loading of saturated porous medium v7.31.109 WTNV109 - Water and mechanical loading of saturated porous medium Summary: A three-dimensional problem of thermo-hydro-mechanical coupling of a saturated porous medium is considered. The test consists of studying the effect of mechanics and hydraulics on the thermal. The element is stretched by imposing a shift in the direction z , hydraulic pressure is imposed on the whole domain and the effect of these loads on the temperature of the model is studied. The aim is to look at the very low coupling of poromechanical to the thermal. The first time step is limited. The models studied are \mathrm{2D} planes (DPQ8 and DPTR6) and \mathrm{3D} density (HEXA20) with linear behavior for hydraulics and thermals. 1 Reference problem 1.1 Introduction The test case study examines the thermo-hydro-mechanical behavior of a saturated porous medium consisting of a single fluid: water in its liquid phase. It is used in THM Modelling in Code_Aster . The constitutive law of the associated fluid is LIQU_SATU type. 1.2 Geometry A 1m cube is considered to be centred on the centre of the (-0,5\le x\le 0,5;-0,5\le y\le 0,5;-0,5\le z\le 0,5;) axis. 1.3 Material properties | solid | Density ({\mathrm{kg.m}}^{-3}) Young's modulus drained E(\mathrm{Pa}) Poisson's ratio Thermal expansion coefficient of solid ({K}^{-1}) | 2.\times {10}^{3} 225.\times {10}^{6} 0. 8.\times {10}^{-6} | | --- | --- | --- | | Fluid | Volumetric mass ({\mathrm{kg.m}}^{-3}) Constant pressure heat ({\mathrm{J.K}}^{-1}) Thermal expansion coefficient of the liquid ({K}^{-1}) Derivated from fluid conductivity relative to temperature | {10}^{3} 2.85\times {10}^{6} {10}^{-4} 0. | | Thermal | Homogenized conductivity ({\mathrm{W.K}}^{-1}{m}^{-1}) Derivated from homogenized conductivity relative to temperature | 1.7 0. | | Coefficients of homogenization | \mathrm{Biot} coefficient Porosity | {10}^{-12} 0.4 | | Homogenized coefficients | Density ({\mathrm{kg.m}}^{-3}) Constant stress heat ({\mathrm{J.K}}^{-1}) | 1.6\times {10}^{3} 2.85\times {10}^{6} | 1.4 Boundary conditions and loads - Element complete: fluid pressure \mathrm{PRE1}=500.0\mathrm{Pa} (no flow or variation in water mass) - Lower side: {u}_{x}=0.0m,{u}_{y}=0.0m,{u}_{z}=0.0\mathrm{m.} displacements - Upper side: {u}_{z}={10}^{-3}m displacement 1.5 Initial conditions The fields of movement, pressure, temperature are all initially zero, the reference temperature is {T}_{0}=273°K . 2 reference solution 2.1 Method of calculation The reference solution is one-dimensional because it depends only on the vertical coordinate. Therefore, we will reason on a linear axis according to z. If gravity is neglected and there is no external heat source, the thermal equation is given by the following expression: {h}_{l}^{m}\frac{d{m}_{l}}{\mathrm{dt}}+\frac{\delta Q'}{\mathrm{dt}}D{M}_{l}+\mathrm{divq}=0 Where {h}_{l}^{m} is the water mass enthalpy, {m}_{l} its mass, {M}_{l} its flux, q the heat flux and Q' the unconvected heat. The mass conservation equation is as follows: \frac{d{m}_{l}}{\mathrm{dt}}+D{M}_{l}=0 In the absence of water flow, the equation is simplified to become: \frac{\delta Q'}{\mathrm{dt}}+\mathrm{divq}=0 In this equation, the quantity Q' represents the heat received by the system in a transformation for which there are no heat inputs by fluid input. Low pressure variation and parameters are chosen so that the temperature varies little and therefore: \frac{dQ'}{T}=\frac{dQ'}{{T}_{0}} \mathrm{dQ}' therefore has this expression: \mathrm{dQ}'=3{\alpha}_{0}{K}_{0}{T}_{0}d{\varepsilon}_{v}+{C}_{0}^{\varepsilon}\mathrm{dT}-3{\alpha}_{l}^{m}{T}_{0}{\mathrm{dp}}_{l} with: - {\alpha}_{0} the homogenized thermal expansion coefficient equivalent to that of solid {\alpha}_{s} . - {K}_{0} the drained coefficient of elasticity. - {C}_{0}^{\varepsilon} heat has constant deformation which has as expression {C}_{0}^{\varepsilon}={C}_{0}^{\sigma}-9{T}_{0}{K}_{0}{\alpha}_{0}^{2} and {C}_{0}^{\sigma} heat at constant stress. - {\alpha}_{l}^{m} The relative thermal expansion coefficient of the liquid relative to the skeleton, it is expressed as: {\alpha}_{l}^{m}=(b-\phi ){\alpha}_{s}+\phi {\alpha}_{l} with b the coefficient of Biot, \phi the porosity and {\alpha}_{l} the coefficient of expansion of the liquid. - d{\varepsilon}_{v} The variation of density deformation. - {\mathrm{dp}}_{l} The fluid pressure variation. In addition, the heat flow has the following expression: q=-{\lambda}_{T}\partial \frac{T}{\partial z} where {\lambda}_{T} is the coefficient of thermal conductivity. By replacing \mathrm{dQ}' and q with their value in the equation and limiting itself to time step \Delta t , we obtain: 3{\alpha}_{0}{K}_{0}{T}_{0}\Delta {\varepsilon}_{v}-3{\alpha}_{l}^{m}{T}_{0}\Delta {p}_{l}+{C}_{0}^{\varepsilon}\Delta T=-\Delta tdq={\lambda}_{l}\Delta t\frac{{\partial}^{2}T}{\partial {z}^{2}} Considering temperatures and initially zero movements, we can write: \Delta T=T(t)-T(0)=T et \Delta \varepsilon =\varepsilon (t)-\varepsilon (0)=\varepsilon et \Delta {p}_{l}={p}_{l}(t)-{p}_{l}(0)={p}_{l} So at the first time step, we'll have: T-a\frac{{\partial}^{2}T}{\partial {z}^{2}}=b with a=\frac{{\lambda}_{l}\Delta T}{{C}_{0}^{\varepsilon}} and b=-\frac{3{\alpha}_{0}{K}_{0}{T}_{0}\varepsilon -3{\alpha}_{l}^{m}{T}_{0}{p}_{l}}{{C}_{0}^{\varepsilon}} The variational formulation of this expression (in the one-dimensional case) is then as follows: {\int}_{\Omega}T.\stackrel{ˆ}{T}\mathrm{dz}+a{\int}_{\Omega}\frac{\partial T}{\partial z}\frac{\partial \stackrel{ˆ}{T}}{\partial z}\mathrm{dz}-a{\int}_{\partial \Omega }\frac{\partial T}{\partial z}\stackrel{ˆ}{T}\mathrm{dz}={\int}_{\Omega}b.\stackrel{ˆ}{T}\mathrm{dz} To establish the analytical solution one considers a single element of degree 1 since in Modelling THM the thermo-hydraulic part is treated with linear elements. Modellings I and J are selective and light Modelling variants of G, they have results that differ from the proposed analytical solution (integration is different), and are therefore non-regression. At each step n+1 of the installation, a model containing strictly the n+1 layers placed is combined. The states of stress, displacement and internal variables at the end of the previous step are transferred to the next step by field transfer operations. The initial field of displacement of the laid floor layer must vary linearly from bottom to top, because it varies between the value of the settlement of the lower layers and the geometrical rib to be respected, combined with a zero initial displacement. 2.2 Quantities and reference results The solutions are post-treated in terms of settlement. However, the use of the multi-model method does not give direct access to the settlement of the column: the vertical displacement of the last layer laid is the sum of the actual settlement that it has undergone and the settlement that it has already achieved when it was not there: it is the latter component that must be removed. Consider, for example, layer 4 (see figure below). This layer is placed at the moment n=4 . The settlement n-y makes sense only for n\ge 4 . \delta {u}_{4}^{n} the settlement increment between n and n+1 moments above layer 4. The settlement of layer 4 at the moment n : \Delta {u}_{4}^{n} , is defined as the accumulation of the settlement increments experienced by the layer during the overall process of construction of the soil column, i.e. by laying the successive layers above it ( n\ge 5 ). Thus: \Delta {u}^{n\ge 4}=\sum_{i=4}^{n}\delta {u}_{4}^{i} with \delta {u}_{4}^{n}={u}_{4}^{n}-{u}_{4}^{n-1} Thus, by decomposition of the iterative process, the settlement is easily rewritten as: \Delta {u}_{4}^{n\ge 4}={u}_{4}^{n}-{u}_{4}^{0} . i.e. the movement above the 4th layer at the moment n (under the influence of the layers above it), minus its displacement when placed ( n=4 ). The validation is performed by comparison with GEFDYN solutions provided by the École Centrale Paris. At the moment n\ge 4 : \begin{array}{c}\Delta {u}_{4}^{n\ge 4}=\sum_{i=4}^{n}\delta {u}_{4}^{i}\\ =\sum_{i=4}^{n}{u}_{4}^{i}-{u}_{4}^{i-1}\\ ={u}_{4}^{n}-{u}_{4}^{4}={u}_{4}^{n}-{u}_{4,0}\end{array} For Modelling C, the PDIL_ELGA elemental option calculation is also performed to validate the numerical developments for modellings HM. The values obtained are tested in non-regression. 2.3 Uncertainties about the solution The results obtained during the modelling with the Finements GEFD yn software of the Ecole Centrale Paris are precise according to the convergence criteria used in this software. The definition of convergence criteria is specified in the software user manual []. The value of the criteria for displacement and hydraulic pressure is equal to {10}^{-3} and the value of the criteria for mechanical (force) and hydraulic (flux) imbalances is equal to {10}^{-2} . 2.4 Bibliographical references [bib1] D.
